title: Majlis 2 |  Khuloos (Sincerity) | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 2023 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound concept of Khuloos (sincerity) as the foundation of spiritual life and faith. The speaker emphasizes the importance of performing actions solely for the pleasure of Allah, warning against the pitfalls of Riya (showmanship) and the misuse of predestination to evade personal accountability. By drawing parallels between the teachings of the Ahlulbayt and the tragic events of Karbala, the lecture highlights how true devotion requires absolute reliance on God and the recognition of the Imam of the time.
content:
Are you my Hussain? Removing the stones from the body, are you my Hussain? How is your body lying here, are you my Hussain? Alas, alas, my poor brother's body is trampled by horses in the wilderness. How do I recognize you? The head is severed from the body. Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab called out, 'Are you my Hussain?' I will recognize you, in the eyes of your sister now... Removing the stones from the corpse, are you my Hussain? Are you my Hussain? Recognizing me has also become difficult for you. I have come, please tell me quickly, are you my Hussain? Raise your voice... Alhamdulillah. ... La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azim. ... Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is my... La hawla wa la quwwata... a part of your life keeps decreasing. A human's life decreases daily, in fact, every moment and every second. If a human understands this reality, if they pay a little attention to how precious each second of theirs is, they will value every single minute, value every single second, and think about doing as much as possible in this time, and completely... They are working against the clock and will absolutely not waste their time, unlike how we usually do in worldly things that are of no use to us—which are of no use at all, neither useful in this world nor in the hereafter. Playing video games, etc.—there is no benefit to anyone in playing these video games. Except for the game creators, there isn't a single penny of benefit. Similarly, there are other things that people watch, in which only their time is wasted and nothing else; it's just a waste of time, but they don't understand. Will that thing be of any use in this world? Always ask this question to yourself, to your intellect. Ask your intellect. If you are thinking about worldly matters, let's see from the worldly perspective: are we going to get some money, are we going to get some assets, or from the perspective of the hereafter, will we get some reward in the hereafter? Ask this question to yourself, question yourself. That is why the Quran has repeatedly, time and again, told humans to use their intellect. The Quran has used so many words, so many times... if you read the Quran, how many words has it used just for contemplation (fikr)? Use it, and the internet, use your brains. Is this thing going to be of use to you? Are you going to get anything from these games? Nothing. Except that in gaming, competitions are held, and if money is involved in that, then if you ask any jurist (faqih), they will tell you that even that earning is not permissible (halal). You can ask, I won't say it, you ask them: is this kind of earning permissible? Please recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. How should a person develop their personality? Yesterday, in your presence, what I submitted was about hard work. But before that, the greatest thing is faith (iman) and good deeds. These two things have appeared repeatedly, 50 times. 50 times the Quran has said that their faith, their beliefs must be correct, and they should keep doing good deeds, meaning performing acts of worship, and getting as close to Allah as possible. Insha'Allah, today, what should be the second aspect of a person's personality? That whatever work they do, there must be sincerity (ikhlas) in it. Do not do it so that people recognize you or your name is praised, like, 'Yes, I am giving money, but my name should appear on the board.' Doing things for show, for showing off (riya), is completely the cause of the destruction of all of a person's deeds. Except when we want others to follow us, at that time you show that action, and even that should not be ostentation. Let me give an example so that our point becomes clear. For example, we don't pray at home at all—for instance, we don't pray at home, not at all. But when we are with friends, we think, 'Let's show them I'm a religious man, my friend.' So, with friends, we say 'Allahu Akbar' and pray. This is not right. We are praying regularly. Third, a third example: we pray regularly, and now we want to show our son, or a friend's son, or someone else, that 'Look, we pray, and prayers are performed like this.' For example, any action—not just prayers, any action: fasting, prayers, coming to a majlis, anything. Look, it happens like this: we should do it ourselves, regularly, and if someone says, 'Brother, teach them, show them,' then to show them, we perform it: 'Look, this is how this work is done.' And there is also a hadith of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself: 'Sallu...' (Pray as you see me pray)... ...is also there: 'Sallu kama ra'aytumuni usalli' (Pray as you have seen me pray). 'As I pray, as you see me praying, you should pray like that.' The book is there, both are there. 'Sallu kama ra'aytumuni usalli'—pray as you see me praying. Can there be such a clear order? Can there be an order clearer than this? Despite this, today there is so much difference of opinion among Muslims about how prayers should be performed. Today, Muslims have not been able to decide how to pray—where to fold hands, what to do, how to do it—there is a lot of debate on that. Anyway, this ikhlas and sincerity is a very important thing. This word has been used 31 times in the Quran. Today, this word is there 31 times: ikhlas, khalsa, ikhlas. Alaykum assalam. Okay? And this khuloos (sincerity) is the enemy of Iblis, the enemy of Satan. The hardest thing for Satan to bear is when a person does something with sincerity. That is why you don't need the whole story of Satan. When Allah created Hazrat Adam (a.s.), He told Satan, 'Prostrate.' He said, 'I won't.' Allah said, 'Get out of here, get out of My presence.' Okay? 'Get out of My presence.' Okay, friends, but whose head did he place the blame of his bad deed on? Allah's. You must know, all those in the world who are determinists (Jabriyyah), who say 'Whatever we do, Allah does it all,' they are following Satan in this matter by saying, 'We didn't do it, Allah does it, Allah does it, Allah did everything, it was pre-written, Allah did it.' You know, many people hold this belief that we do nothing, everything is pre-written. There was a Persian poet, his couplet goes: 'My drinking of wine was already known to Allah beforehand; if I do not drink wine today, Allah's knowledge would become incorrect, therefore I must drink wine.' Brother, Allah's knowledge must not be proven wrong! So there are people of this kind as well, who put all their bad deeds on Allah's head. Who are they following? Iblis. 'Rabbi bima aghwaytani'—'My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely mislead all of Your servants...' I will mislead all Your servants, all of Adam's descendants. How will I mislead them? Satan explained that too, laying out his entire strategy. Just think about how much confidence he had in himself, thinking, 'I will tell them everything, yet they will follow me and I will mislead them.' So he said beforehand, clearly specifying, 'On the earth, whatever wrong deeds they do, I will present them so beautifully, I will decorate them so much.' And 'If I don't do it, someone else would'—completely decorating it. Now, let's move a bit forward so that 'I will mislead'... ...mislead, I will mislead everyone. In Surah number 16, these three verses are found. Allah says, 'Fa-iza qara'tal Qur'an...' [When you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast]. Whenever you read the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Satan, the accursed Satan, the rejected Satan. And then Allah stated two verses, 99 and 100. From here, Satan's authority does not work on those who believe—there must be faith—and who trust in their Lord. Satan only has authority over those who accept his mastership... ...who accept his mastership, who make Satan their guardian (wali). If someone says, 'Brother, I am Satan, follow me,' would anyone follow? Would anyone follow? What he did was select some people among the crowd and tell them, 'Brother, take my agency.' People said, 'We will take it 100%, why wouldn't we?' When they get worldly wealth, authority, money, fame, and power, they walk on Satan's path. He says, 'If I do right, follow me...' ...'If I do right, follow me; if I do wrong, correct me.' That is why, after that, most Muslims throughout history said, 'We didn't do it, Allah did it.' Thus, those who came to fight in the Battle of Jamal were asked, 'You knew the virtues of Ali (a.s.).' They asked her, 'O Lady, when you knew this Hadith, why did you go to fight? Why did you go to fight against Ali (a.s.)?' She replied, 'I did not go to fight, Allah had already decreed the fighting. It was written in destiny, so it had to happen.' 'Why was Ali (a.s.) removed? We didn't remove him, it was written in destiny.' 'Why did this happen? It was written in destiny.' Someone asked, 'Why did you kill Husayn (a.s.)?' 'I didn't kill him, it was written in destiny.' 'It was written in destiny, this had to happen, I didn't kill him.' In this way, Muslims kept justifying all their deeds. Man is 100% responsible for his actions. 100%. If Allah were involved even 1%, then Allah would have to bear that 1% of the punishment. Allah is not involved even 1%. We are reading the verses of the Qur'an before you, Surah [Hijr], verses 39, 40, and now we will read 41. It is a bit dangerous, but it is a verse of the Qur'an. Anyone who wants can go and check the Qur'an, it is dangerous. After that, Allah replied when Satan said, 'I will do this.' Allah said, 'No problem, this is a straight path to Me (Aliyyun Mustaqeem)'—if you put the diacritics correctly... ...'This is a straight path to Me' (Aliyyun Mustaqeem). If you put the diacritics correctly... Then the Muslims realized, 'Oh, this is a problem.' Let me tell you another point from the history of the Qur'an, for those who are familiar with it. You know that when the Qur'an was compiled, initially the Arabs did not use 'I'rab' (diacritical marks like Zabar, Zer, Pesh). These diacritics were introduced by a disciple of the Master of the Universe (a.s.) named [Abul Aswad] under his guidance. 'This path of Ali is the straight path' is the translation of 'Aliyyun Mustaqeem'. So they changed the diacritics of the Qur'an. What did they do? Actually, it should be read like this... Even today, we ask Muslims—how many years have passed? 1300, 1400 years have passed, right? 1400 years. Even today we ask this question, 'Brother, you have read the Qur'an, now translate it a bit and tell us.' Do you understand up to this point? 'This path is upon Me...' Allah is saying 'upon Me' (alayya)—this path goes over Allah, and it is straight. If it were for Allah, in Arabic it should be 'to Me' (ilayya), not 'upon Me' (alayya). And the Qur'an says that a spider's web is very weak. The spider's web is extremely weak; if you just sweep it with a thin broom, the entire web is destroyed. If you strike one argument against them, their entire building collapses, the way they read it. Is it 'Mustaqeem'? Let's look at it step by step quickly... ...Let's look at it step by step quickly because time is running out. So, the first condition of this class, the first condition of sincerity, is that a person does not stretch their hand before anyone except Allah. If they have something, they give it in the way of Allah. This refers to the 'Muhsineen'. But the level of the 'Mukhliseen' is such that they give away what they have even before using it themselves. And they gave in such a way that an entire Surah of the Qur'an was revealed. Allah revealed a Surah of the Qur'an in their honor. It says that these are the ones who give in the way of Allah, and they neither want any reward nor demand anything from anyone. So here He says, meaning Allah Himself says to Jibra'eel... When a person does not stretch their hand before any creation, they are demonstrating and confessing that they are a servant of Allah, asking only from Allah. Just then, [Jibra'eel asked], 'O Ibrahim, do you need any help?' 'I don't need help.' It was not that he did not need help, but 'I will not ask you. I will ask Him for whose sake I am going into the fire today.' This friendship (khullah) was so pleasing to Allah that He said, 'O my Khalil, O my friend Ibrahim.' Thus, it is known that whoever dedicates their life, time, wealth, and everything in His way, this is the standard of their friendship and intimacy. This is why the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) called Sheikh Mufid 'my brother'... ...called him 'brother'. God willing, go and see, just outside the shrine, as soon as you exit the Haram, the graves of Sheikh Mufid and Ibn Qulawayh (who wrote Kamil al-Ziyarat) are side by side. There, the elegy (marsiya) of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) is written, which the Imam of the Time recited for Sheikh Mufid's grave: 'Your absence is deeply felt.' What a level that must befitting level that must be! When he is pleased with Allah and Allah is pleased with him, then perhaps you haven't fully grasped it yet. When I tell you this much, you should understand the rest—whenever the pleasure of 'mardi' (will/pleasure) is mentioned in the Quran. 'And among mankind is he who sells his soul to seek the pleasure of Allah.' There are some among the servants of Allah who give their lives solely to attain the pleasure of Allah, to attain Allah's will. With great effort, I have to make this one point: keep recognizing Ali (a.s.). He is that Ali who took Allah's pleasure and kept it with him. Now, if anyone wants Allah's pleasure from Allah, they must come through Ali. And to acquire the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Ali was made the gate. Now, whoever wants to go there... ...made him the gate. Now, whoever wants to go there must first go through him. Now it must be known that whoever makes a deal with Allah and the Messenger must first make a deal with Ali. Until a deal is made with Ali, and until Ali is pleased, Allah's pleasure cannot be obtained. So no matter how much you keep saying 'Razi Allah, Razi Allah', until Ali is pleased, Allah is not pleased. [Music] Now, wherever the word of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (a.s.), is present, that is where the truth lies. Bravo! It will be either 'Ya Ali' or the progeny of Ali (a.s.). Leaving that aside, whatever remains will be either ignorance or theft. Why was the plural used? So that all the pleasure is included. Lest someone says, 'Yes, Ali was given 10%, and 90% was with us.' [Applause] Whatever pleasure there was, whatever stock there was, it all went over there. Now we have nothing; whatever you want, get it from there. Allah did this: 'We have given our thing, now let Allah decide.' Similarly, the Prophet went and decided: 'I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate.' That is the end of the matter. Whose decision is this? If anyone wants it, they must come through the gate, simple. Who decided this? Did we decide? Did you decide? Experience is experience, remember that. Experience is experience, remember that. Experience is a great teacher. [Some might say] 'Ali is the son-in-law, that's why he gave it to Ali and made him the gate.' Brother, what kind of Muslim would think like this? Who knows. That is why Allah gave a guarantee beforehand: 'Wa ma yantiqu 'anil-hawa' (Nor does he speak from his own desire). This Prophet does not speak of his own accord. Whatever he speaks is only revelation sent down to him. 'He speaks when We command, otherwise he does not speak at all.' If anyone wants to argue, let them go and argue with Allah. Now, how to reach Allah is another discussion, God willing, some other time. So Allah gave His pleasure from there... And if someone gives everything in the way of Allah, then 'He is sufficient for me.' He is at the extreme level of reliance, having extreme trust in Allah. His total reliance is at a level no one can even imagine. No one can conceive it. Extreme reliance is at that level where you... Extreme reliance is at that level where you give up everything. Now, when we began to search history, when we began to explore history, we did not find anyone who gave up everything, absolutely everything, except the one whose name was Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). That is why Allah said, that is why Allah said: 'Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul-mutma'innah' (O reassured soul!), the last verses of Surah al-Fajr. O soul that is at the level of peace, at the level of absolute contentment and satisfaction! Absolute satisfaction, absolute contentment. At that level of total reliance on Allah, where there is no reliance on anyone else. The Quran is addressing this. It has come in the Quran, in Surah ar-Ra'd, Surah number 13 of the Quran: 'Ala bi-dhikrillahi tatma'innul-qulub' (Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured). Those who believe love Allah intensely. Only by the remembrance of Allah, only on Allah... Only through the remembrance of Allah and by relying solely on Allah does the heart find peace. Husayn (a.s.) showed that, 'Look, my father bought the pleasure of the Lord, and I have kept peace (itminan) with me.' [As the Quran says:] '...well-pleased and well-pleasing.' This complete level of trust is the level of Ikhlas (sincerity). So, if anyone wants to learn Ikhlas, it is at the doorstep of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.); they should go and present themselves at their doorstep. Then, the narrator says, 'I heard Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) say...' If one does not recognize the Imam, the Imam of his time, he will die the death of disbelief, hypocrisy, and misguidance. [The Imam said:] '...and submit completely before us.' That is 'Tasleem' (submission). These are the three conditions. What is the first condition? To refer to them, meaning to obtain all knowledge from them. The third thing is to submit before them. If a person does not do these three things, even if he fasts, he is a polytheist, he is not a Muslim. And with complete sincerity—this 'Ikhlas' means no showing off, absolutely not. Whatever work you are doing, whether it is worldly work or work for the hereafter, do not do it for 'Riya' (showing off), do not do it to show people. If someone says to you, 'Brother, give this much money and we will make you the chief guest,' [you should think] we are already cheap enough, why do you want to make us even cheaper? Taking money from there and saying, 'Yes, write my name as Fakhr-e-Millat, so-and-so...' You know, right? Just these big titles are given. And do you know what the problem with this is? When a person gets used to having their name highlighted, when their name stops appearing, they get frustrated and go into depression. And they feel, 'What is this life? No one asks about me anymore.' For sincerity, whenever you do any work, always think that you are not going to get any recognition at all. Go with this mindset. Otherwise, it means your trust in Allah is less, and your trust in that [recognition] is more. What will he do? In Surah Al-Qasas—which is Chapter number 28 of the Quran—'Qasas' is the plural of 'Qissah' (story/narrative). In it, there is a story of Prophet Musa (a.s.) himself. When Prophet Musa (a.s.) killed [the Copt], someone advised him to leave from there because Pharaoh and his chiefs were searching for him and would kill him, so he should leave and get out of there. So when he reached Madyan, at a place where people usually go to get water near a well, when he arrived at the well to drink water, he saw a large crowd there. People were watering [their flocks]. These are all Quranic verses, I am just speaking very briefly, otherwise it will take too much time... ...that those girls were unable to go [to the well], right? Unlike how women today mingle among men, women back then had modesty (ghayrah). And men too were somewhat... anyway... He was deeply embarrassed and asked, 'Where did your veil go?' They replied, 'A veil has fallen over our intellect.' That is why men are doing this. And the second couplet is absolutely amazing. It says, 'By the grace of God, both husband and wife are... Thank God, both are highly educated and very cultured. She has no modesty, and he doesn't get angry.' That is, the woman... [praise] ...was given water. Then [she said], 'I will take him.' She told her father, 'This is what happened, this is the story.' He said, 'Call him. Where was he?' She said, 'He was near the water.' Prophet Musa (a.s.) was sitting under the tree. So, now look at the lesson here. See what Islam's question, the Quran, and what we are connecting here. [She said], 'You walk ahead.' Musa (a.s.) said, 'No, I will walk ahead. You give me directions from behind. I will walk ahead, you give me directions from behind.' 'I will walk ahead, give me directions from behind. You tell me from behind whether to go right or left.' He replied, 'We belong to a family [of prophets/modesty]...' What did Western culture introduce? 'Ladies first'. Prophet Shuaib (a.s.) said, 'My friend, you did a good deed for my daughters. I want to reward you, please have some food.' [Musa (a.s.) replied], 'Lest it be that I did this good deed and I receive this reward in return for it. My good deed must not be ruined; I did it for the Hereafter.' [Shuaib (a.s.) said], 'This food is out of hospitality, you are correct in your stance.' You are right in your own place, but we too—and that too from the Prophet—are such that when a guest comes to us, we do not let them leave without feeding them. And the most important thing to show in this is that one should abstain from every kind of sin. Whatever sin it is, abstain from it; it is not to be done, it is wrong, it is not to be done, Allah has forbidden it, it is not to be done. Look, it is not easy. It is easy to say, but very difficult to practice. The perfection is that a person distances themselves from sins... meaning what is the reality of sensitivity? Inshallah tomorrow... there is not much time left today. Inshallah, to completely submit before Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). If you want to see an example in history... If you want to see an example in history, do you know the incident of Siffin? In the battle, [Maula Ali said], 'Muhammad, you attack,' and he properly explained how to do it: 'Keep your eyes on the furthest row, clench your teeth tightly, clench your teeth firmly, and attack with all your strength.' He explained everything to him. But as soon as Muhammad attacked, they immediately rained arrows down on him and started attacking instantly. So many arrows came that Muhammad turned back. Then Hazrat... then Muhammad went again, and they rained arrows again, and he returned again. This is all fully recorded in the historical texts. So when Maula sent him for the third time, and Muhammad returned again, Maula took the sword and struck him on his back with the flat side of the sword—not to hurt him, but as a gentle nudge... ...and not to hurt him, but as a gentle nudge, [saying], 'This is the effect of your mother's milk that you are retreating and coming back like this. Step aside, I will show you how battle is fought. I will show you how battle is fought.' Ali [went out] like a lion, but his age was only 18 years or even less, even less than that. And when a warrior from Muawiyah's army emerged, who was a very tall and broad warrior, and he said, 'Send the bravest person in your army,' Ali said, 'Fine, I am sending someone, you come forward to fight.' Whoever came forward to fight... he said, 'No, my sons are enough for your entire army.' He had seven or eight sons. 'My sons are enough for your army.' How did it happen? His first son came, the youngest son came. The one who was his youngest son, as soon as his neck was severed, the father flew into a rage. He sent the second son. He came, and before a single round was completed, his neck was also severed. And imagine what the father's state must have been. He sent the third son. He had seven or eight sons; everyone's neck was chopped off in a single round. Now, he came out in anger to fight himself. As soon as he came, the warrior made another round, and within one round, his neck was also severed. Now when all this happened, everyone became terrified. If this is Ali, then who is that? So when Abbas returned, the Master of the Universe said, 'Abbas, remove the veil from your face.' As soon as Abbas... this is Ali, this is called bravery. Such was the renown of Abbas that when he sat on a horse—and the speaker is not just exaggerating, do not think that some orator is just pleasing you with rhetoric, I am telling you from history books—that when he sat on a horse, his feet would drag on the ground. And he was such a brave warrior who was repeatedly saying, 'Master, grant me permission.' People were terrified of the name of Abbas. They had already experienced it; they feared his name. That prince, that brave one, that courageous one! But no, Abbas, even up to his martyrdom... What, brother, the army is calling you now, that commander of the army... What, brother, the army is calling you now, that commander of the army is calling you, 'O Commander of the Army', the one whose standard-bearer I am. Now that army is no more, that commander is no more. Hussain said, 'Alright, Abbas, go and bring water for the children. Just bring water for the children.' Abbas came to the entrance of the tent and called out, 'Sakeena, Sakeena!' As soon as Sakeena heard Abbas's voice, she said, 'Uncle, how did you remember me?' He said, 'Daughter, bring your water-skin.' She asked, 'What will we do with the water-skin, Uncle?' He said, 'The Master has ordered me to bring water from the Euphrates, to bring water from the river. Bring it, I will bring water.' Now Sakeena went to get the water-skin. As she was carrying it, small children gathered around Sakeena, saying, 'O lady, this water-skin is going, where are you taking it?' She said, 'My uncle has promised. Father told Uncle to bring water, my uncle is going to get water. My uncle will surely bring it.' The children's hope grew, Sakeena's hope was rekindled, and Sakeena gave the water-skin. Abbas, the generous, took Sakeena's water-skin and set off. Pushing back the army, he rode his horse into the Euphrates. After entering the Euphrates, Abbas dismounted, dipped the water-skin, filled it, and then took a little water in his palm and said, 'O oppressors, do not think I am helpless, I can drink water...' ...do not think I am helpless, I can drink water. But the children are thirsty, that is why I am not drinking water.' Saying this, he threw the water away and set off with the water-skin. Now, with the water-skin in one hand and the standard in the other, as Abbas began to move, a wretched person attacked from behind such that Abbas's right arm was severed. Abbas recited epic verses. After that, another wretched person made such an attack that his left arm was also severed, and the standard also fell. Abbas again recited verses and held the water-skin with his teeth. Now as he was carrying the water-skin, both his hands having been severed, Abbas had not gone very far when an arrow of oppression was shot, which struck the water-skin. As soon as it struck the water-skin, the water began to flow out. As soon as the water flowed out, Abbas bowed his head, he bowed his neck, thinking, 'What will I do now when I go back to the tents? How will Abbas go back?' It is written in the books of tragedy that as soon as Abbas bowed his head, a wretched person struck him with a mace. Do you know what a mace is? A mace is a very large iron weapon, like a ball with spikes on it... ...like a ball with spikes on it, large iron spikes. He struck so hard that Abbas fell down from his horse. Whenever a person falls from a height, they put their hands forward, but Abbas had no hands. Abbas fell onto the sands of Karbala, calling out, 'My last salutations to you!' As soon as this voice reached Hussain's ears, Hussain held his back, held his waist, and cried, 'Now my strength is shattered, O Allah! Now my back is broken! Now my back is broken!' And today his strength was shattered... 'O Abbas, I cannot see anything, I cannot see anything.' At that moment, the enemy was taunting, the enemy was taunting, 'Your protector has been killed, your protector has been killed!' Abbas... the enemy was taunting. Hussain reached Abbas. He placed Abbas's head on his lap. The brothers spoke for a short while, and then Abbas's eyes closed forever. Hussain then recited an elegy, 'Now, the enemies who are yours... children, do not sleep...' And the enemies who are yours... the children could not sleep, how will they sleep now so late into the night? Abbas went taking the water-skin. He came to the door, Sakina saw the water-skin but Uncle was not there. He just... and three times... Late Ghulam Ali family [Music]
Sincerity (Ikhlas) is the essential condition for any deed to be accepted by Allah.
Human beings must take full responsibility for their actions rather than blaming destiny or Satan.
Riya (performing deeds for public recognition) destroys the spiritual value of one's worship.
Imam Ali (a.s.) serves as the gateway to understanding the pleasure of Allah and the Prophet.
True faith is defined by total reliance on God and avoiding dependence on worldly validation.
The sacrifice of Hazrat Abbas at Karbala serves as the ultimate example of loyalty and sincerity.
Recognizing the Imam of the time is a fundamental requirement for spiritual perfection.

title: Sunni Kitab Mein Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s) Ki Wilaadat Ka Tazkera
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical documentation of Imam Mahdi's (a.t.f.s) birth as recorded in the Sunni scholarly work 'Wafayat al-A'yan' by Ibn Khallikan. The speaker highlights how this prominent biographical dictionary confirms the lineage and birth date of the 12th Imam. By citing this non-Shia source, the lecture provides evidence of the historical recognition of Imam Mahdi's existence among Sunni scholars.
content:
Wafayat al-A'yan wa Anba' Abna' az-Zaman, which is famously known as Wafayat al-A'yan, is an important book by Ibn Khallikan. This book was written between 654 AH and 671 AH. In this book, the author has narrated the life stories of about 850 scholars, rulers, ministers, and famous individuals. And in this book, regarding these individuals, the personalities described, their dates of birth and other details have also been mentioned. In this book, regarding Imam Mahdi (a.s.), he writes that Abul Qasim M-H-M-D (Muhammad) ibn al-Hasan al-Askari ibn al-Hadi ibn Muhammad al-Jawad is the 12th Imam of the Shias, and he is famously known as Al-Hujjah. His birth took place on Friday, the 15th of Shaban, 255 AH. When his father was martyred, his age was 5 years. Peace be upon him [Music]

The discourse emphasizes the emotional weight of these historical injustices and the importance of maintaining mourning rituals (Maatamdaari) to honor the sacrifices of the Prophet's household.
content:
The sehra (wedding garland) is adorned, the sehra is adorned, the enemies have brought it. In Karbala, there is no support for the Master (Sarwar), no support at all. My Master, I say, you are like a father, it is very dark. The mother was looted, the tyrant went to the court, I remained barren. Zainab has gone, Sakina has gone, my master. Those who have come having lost everything, to Medina, to the tents, to bow down. I, an old person, from door to door, of Raza, pulled, pulled, weeping. When it came upon my hand.

title: EP#7: Khalifa Ka Afsos | Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses a historical account found in Tarikh Tabari regarding the regrets of the first caliph of the Sunni tradition. The speaker highlights three specific actions the caliph wished he had not taken, with a primary focus on the raid on the house of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.). The lecture emphasizes the gravity of this event by referencing the caliph's own admission of remorse.
content:
There were three things that the first caliph of the Ahl-e-Tasanun (Sunnis) regretted. In the famous book of Ahl-e-Tasanun, Tarikh Tabari: 'I do not regret anything of this world except three things that I did, but I wish I had not done them; three things that I did not do, but I wish I had done them; and three things that I did not ask the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) which I should have asked. Of the three things I wish I had not done, the first is: I wish I had not raided the house of Fatima, even if they had locked it from inside to prepare for war against me. Second: I wish I had not burned Fuja'ah al-Sulami, and instead had either just killed him or set him free. And third: I wish on the day of Saqifah Bani Sa'idah, I had handed over the caliphate to Umar or Abu Ubaidah al-Jarrah, and remained only their minister.' That is, out of these three actions, the very first thing for which regret was expressed was the raiding of the house of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.). Does anything more remain to be said?
