title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 10 | Duties of Shias during Ghaibat (Occultation) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture explores the essential duties of Shias during the period of the Imam's Occultation (Ghaibat), emphasizing the spiritual necessity of constant remembrance and sincere supplication. It highlights the Imamate as a divine position and explains how the Occultation serves as a critical trial of faith for believers. The session provides practical guidance on maintaining a connection with Imam al-Mahdi through specific prayers, intellectual defense of the faith, and the cultivation of Taqwa. Ultimately, it encourages believers to actively prepare for the reappearance by aligning their lives with the teachings of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
And hasten their reappearance and destroy their enemies from among the jinn and mankind, from the first to the last. I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Lord of Majesty and Honor, and I turn to Him in repentance. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Hassan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an observer, until You make him dwell on Your earth in obedience and cause him to live in it for a long time. O Allah, hasten the reappearance of Your representative and make us among his helpers, his assistants, his followers, and his servants. And do not make us among his enemies. Grant us success in that which You love and are pleased with. And do not leave us to ourselves for even a blink of an eye, ever. And do not replace us with others. By the right of Muhammad and his purified family. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their reappearance, and curse all their enemies. Respected viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. This is special in Karbala because the one who is the support of the religion of God has arrived. Everyone is coming and saying, 'Congratulations, O Hussain, the one who will take your revenge has arrived.' On behalf of The Strong Rope team, to all our viewers, this night, which is the night of the birth of the Imam of our time—the Imam with whom we are to be resurrected on the Day of Judgment—the Flower of Narcissus, the coolness of the eyes of Hassan al-Askari, the Seal of the Successors, the Joseph of Zahra, the Avenger of Karbala, the Guardian of the Era, the Master of the Time, Hazrat Baqiyatullah al-A'zam, Hujjat ibn al-Hassan al-Askari—may Allah hasten his noble reappearance—a very happy birth night to you all. By the grace of God and the bounty of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), today is the tenth and final session of this Mahdism webinar. In this era filled with hardships and difficulties, where the whole world is facing a pandemic for which no cure has been found to date, at the time of organizing this unique webinar, we did not know how successful it would be. However, relying on Allah and His Proof (Hujjah), we took the initiative for this program, and by the grace and mercy of God, the blessings of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), and the prayers of all you viewers, this program has been successful. Thank you for your prayers and your love. Through this webinar, under the topic of the belief in Mahdaviyat, in the light of the Holy Quran and Hadith, various subjects related to Hazrat-e-Wali-e-Asr (ajtfs) were discussed. Such as the necessity of the Proof of God, the characteristics of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), the Imam's mother Hazrat-e-Nargis (s.a.), the birth of the Imam, the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra), the Four Deputies (Nawab-e-Arba), the Major Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Kubra), and Taqlid. Finally, we will continue today with the topic that began yesterday, which is the responsibilities of the Shia during the Occultation. Yesterday's discussion reached the point that to understand our responsibilities during the Occultation, it is essential to first understand the value and status of the Imam and Imamate. First, we saw that the Imam we are waiting for is 'faqid', meaning he is hidden, he is absent. He is 'tareed', meaning the one whose door people have closed upon themselves, and he is 'ghareeb', meaning he is unknown in his worth, whose value, status, and position people are unaware of, and he is a stranger in the land. Then, a brief review was taken of a lengthy Hadith of Imam-e-Riza (a.s.), in which the rank of the Imam and Imamate was described, stating that this is a divine position where the selection of the Imam is solely in the hands of Allah. Imamate is the status of the Prophets. It is the position of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and it is beyond the intellect of people to reach the importance, value, and status of this position of Imamate. When it came to responsibilities, the most important responsibility mentioned was that we should thank God and the Proof of God, from whose grace and bounty we are receiving all blessings, the greatest of which is that we have received existence and life. After this, another important responsibility is to pray for our Imam, during which it was also mentioned that Ayatollah Sayyid Abul Qasim al-Khoei (r.a.) used to recite the Dua 'Allahumma Kulli Waliyyik' in the Qunut of his obligatory prayers. Now, let us move from here to our final discussion today and listen to our other responsibilities, which will be explained to us by the honorable Dr. Shabib Rizvi, InshaAllah. Assalamu Alaikum, Sir. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Many congratulations to you and all your family and relatives on this night. Congratulations to you, your entire team, and all the Momineen. Especially, we should all present a gift of congratulations in the court of Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.) that the chain of Imamate, the chain of Imamate, has reached its final link today in this world, and he has stepped into it. Congratulations to everyone. Viewers, in this final session of the first Mahdaviyat webinar, I request you one last time to keep sending your questions to 'The Strong Rope' WhatsApp number, which is +91, the code is [number removed], [number removed], [number removed]. However, as always, please keep in mind that those questions should not be related to any specific person or personality, but should be related to our topic and discussion. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and Ale Muhammad: Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum wal'an A'da-ahum Ajma'in. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, curse the first oppressor who oppressed the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) and the last one who followed him in that. O Allah, curse them all. O Allah, reform Your servant and Your Caliph with that which You reformed Your Prophets and Your Messengers, and surround him with Your angels, and support him with the Holy Spirit from Yourself, and appoint guards before him and behind him. They protect him from every evil, and replace his fear with security. He worships You, not associating anything with You, and do not grant anyone from Your creation authority over Your Wali, and grant him strength in the struggle against Your enemy and his enemy, and make me among his helpers. Indeed, You are capable of all things. By the status of Muhammad and his pure family. Furthermore, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala has said in His Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'And say, Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to perish.' Salawat upon Muhammad and Ale Muhammad. The verse of the Quran that I have had the honor of reciting, that verse of... An announcement is being made in the world. O Prophet, say: 'Wa qul ja'al haq' (And say, the truth has come). It is the night of the birth of Hazrat Wali-e-Asr (a.s.), may Allah hasten his noble reappearance. O Prophet, say the truth has come. 'Wa zahaqal batil' (And falsehood has perished), and falsehood has vanished. 'Innal batila kana zahooqa' (Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to perish). There is no doubt that falsehood was destined to be erased. This blessed night is the night of the birth of that personality who will eradicate oppression and tyranny from the world, and justice and fairness will prevail throughout the world. Oppression and tyranny will be completely wiped out, and the flag of Tawheed and the flag of Wilayat will wave everywhere. So, on this blessed night, let us all together present a gift of salutation to Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and all the believers, with a loud voice, Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. The discussion was about responsibilities, the first important point of which was that there must be Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Imam. When there is Ma'rifat, then a human being will thank that Imam through whose medium, through whose means, this entire world, this entire universe, this entire cosmos, and the entire galaxy—everything—was created. Everything has been created, everything through his medium. But continuing the discussion, we see that this is not the case. People have not valued the Imam, nor are they doing so. Very few, 'illal qaleel' (except a few). And the Quran has also announced this scarcity, very few, 'illal qaleel'. 'Wa qaleel', this is the announcement of the Quran. 'Wa qaleelun min ibadi yashkur' (And few of My servants are grateful). This occultation is a very severe test. And there are abundant narrations regarding this occultation. Fazl bin Shazan wrote a book, 'Isbat al-Ghaybah'. After that, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nu'mani wrote 'Al-Ghaybah'. Sheikh al-Tusi wrote 'Al-Ghaybah'. Thus, books were written on the occultation 1100, 1200 years ago, in which this narration is recorded: this occultation is a very severe test. And one effect of this test is that the majority will forget their Imam. The majority will forget. And very few people will remember their Imam. And that is why these individuals in whose hearts the remembrance of the Imam remains are called 'Mu'minoon' (believers) in the Hadith. That is, the people of faith, believers, those who are truly Mu'min. Only he will be a Mu'min who remembers his Imam. That is why you see, Sheikh al-Saduq, may Allah be pleased with him—everyone knows him, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh al-Qummi—is a famous Muhaddith (traditionist), the leader of the traditionists. His book is 'Kamal al-Din wa Tamam al-Ni'mah'. In that book, Volume 2, page 368, Hadith number 2, he has recorded a narration. And the name of the narrator is Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi. He says that I asked my master and leader, the seventh Imam, Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s.), about this verse of the Quran. And which verse is that? 'Wa asbagha alaykum ni'amahu zahiratan wa batinah' (And He has bestowed upon you His bounties, both apparent and hidden). And Allah has given you many blessings. 'Asbagha alaykum ni'amahu'. Many blessings, 'asbagha' means very much, abundant, excessive. He has conferred bounties upon you. And these blessings are of two types. There are apparent ones that everyone sees, and there are hidden ones that people do not see—'al-zahir'. What is the meaning of this verse? Azdi asked the Imam, what is the meaning of this verse, what is the concept, what is the interpretation? The Imam (a.s.) replied in response, 'Al-ni'matu al-zahiratu al-imamu al-zahir' (The apparent bounty is the apparent Imam). And what is meant by the hidden—that is, the concealed—bounty? 'Al-Imam al-Ghaib' (The hidden Imam). That Imam who will be concealed, who will be hidden, who will be veiled from the eyes of the people. Whom people cannot see. As soon as Azdi heard this, he asked, 'Wa yakunu fil-a'immati man yaghib?' (And among the Imams, will there be one who will be hidden?) 'Qala alayhi-s-salam' (He said, peace be upon him), the seventh Imam said—look, this is about the time of the seventh Imam, right? The seventh Imam said, 'Na'am' (Yes). 'Yaghibu an absari-n-nasi shakhsuhu' (His person will be hidden from the eyes of the people). This will be the Imam whose personality—that is, physically—will be hidden from the eyes of the people. People will not be able to see him, physically. But 'wa la yaghibu an qulubi-l-mu'minina dhikruhu' (But his remembrance will not be hidden from the hearts of the believers). His remembrance, his memory will never be extinguished from the hearts of the people, it will never be erased. It will never disappear. People who are truly Mu'min will remember him day and night. As I submitted to you yesterday, in every Qunut, they will remember him. They will remember him before prayer, they will remember him after prayer. They will remember him during the day, they will remember him at night. 'Ya Sahib al-Zaman, Ya Sahib al-Zaman'. And then the Imam explained, who will this be? 'Wa huwa thani ashar minna' (And he is the twelfth from us). The twelfth Imam will be that one. Similarly, a Hadith is also found from the sixth Imam. And the narrator of this Hadith is Mufaddal. He is a very famous narrator. 'Tawhid al-Mufaddal' is famous. And this narration is found in 'Al-Kafi'. Yesterday, the importance of the book 'Al-Kafi' was mentioned to you. Volume 1, page 336, Hadith number 3, page number 336. It is Hadith number 3, 'Kitab al-Hujjah'. In this, Mufaddal says that I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). I heard from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) that the Imam is saying, 'Iyyakum wa-t-tanwiha'. What does 'tanwiha' mean? To forget the remembrance, to let the memory fade. Look, the Imam says, refrain from forgetting the remembrance. Don't forget the remembrance, Imam. He is saying to Mufaddal. Rather, he was saying to all the other Shias who were sitting there, that do not forget the remembrance. Whose remembrance? The Imam clarifies, explains it. 'Ama wallah' (By Allah), 'la-yaghibanna imamukum' (your Imam will surely be hidden from you). Not one day, two days, one year, one month, two months, one year, two years. The Imam said, 'sinin min dahrikum' (for many years of your time). That is, a long period. This period of occultation will be long. And will this be easy? No. The Imam explains it, 'wa la-tumahassana' (And you will be tested). In which you will be severely tested, that is, you will be sifted. Sifted, that is, you will be tested in which very few people will remain on faith. 'Hatta yuqal' (Until it will be said), some people will say, 'mata' (He has died). Some people will say, 'qutila' (He has been killed). Some people will say, 'halaka' (He has perished). Some people will say, 'bi-ayyi wadin salaka' (I don't know in which valley he has gone). He is not here now. The Imam is no longer in this world. The test will be such that people's belief in the very existence of the Imam and the remembrance of the Imam—that is, the belief in the existence of the Imam—will be removed, whether the Imam exists or not. And they will forget the remembrance of the Imam. And then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) said a strange sentence. He says, "Wa latadma'unna alayhi uyunu-l-mu'minin" (And the eyes of the believers will surely shed tears for him). Meaning, there will be a small group who will have full certainty that the Imam exists, they will just keep weeping in the remembrance of the Imam. Eyes will weep. The eyes of the believers who will keep remembering the Imam will weep. This is that group. When they wake up in the darkness of the night for Namaz-e-Shab (night prayer), they will pray, "Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyika-l-faraj" (O Allah, hasten the reappearance of Your Wali). After Namaz-e-Shab, they will pray, before Namaz-e-Subh (morning prayer) they will pray, after Namaz-e-Subh they will pray, in Namaz-e-Subh they will pray, in all prayers they will pray, "Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyika-l-faraj". O Lord, I give You the intercession of Ali ibn Abi Talib, "Alladhi ma ashraka bika tarfata 'aynin abada" (Who never associated partners with You for the blinking of an eye, ever). That Ali who never committed Shirk in Your worship, never. "An tu'ajjila faraja waliyyika-l-mahdi" (That You hasten the reappearance of Your Wali, the Mahdi). In this way, they will remember their Imam. They will weep day and night. They will call upon their Imam. They will pray to Allah. This is the remembrance of the Imam. This is the remembrance of the Beloved. For whom the believers will keep remembering day and night. Now look here, now we come to another responsibility, which means, and that responsibility is Dua (supplication). Look, usually, it has been seen nowadays that some ignorant individuals make fun of Dua. About Dua, you people just do Dua, just Dua. Brother, look, go and read the narrations, the Hadiths. "Ad-du'au silahu-l-anbiya" (Dua is the weapon of the Prophets). Dua used to be the weapon of the Prophets. There is such an effect in Dua that there is no effect in anything else in the world. In narrations, in Hadiths. So never consider this Dua light. And it is the command of the Imam himself, "Wa akthiru-d-du'a bi-ta'jili-l-faraji fa-inna dhalika farajukum" (And pray abundantly for the hastening of the reappearance, for in that is your relief). Look, for the reappearance, for the Faraj, that is, for respite, for ease, pray abundantly. Because in this, in this Dua, is your relief. In this Dua is the remembrance of the Imam, and in the remembrance of the Imam himself is relief, is respite. Do not consider it light. It has great worth and value, great value. But unfortunately, some people consider it light, some people make fun of it. They cannot understand what they are saying. So come, let's see, that is, there is a sentence of Dua which is present in Mafatih al-Jinan and has been taken from 'Kamal al-Din'. It is Sheikh Saduq's book 'Kamal al-Din', and many other scholars have also recorded it in their books. For example, Sayyid ibn Tawus has recorded it, who was a very great Marja-e-Taqlid of his time, of the seventh century Hijri. That is, his passing was in 664 Hijri, so in that same year, that is, in that same century, Sayyid ibn Tawus was a very great Marja-e-Taqlid, who was by lineage from the progeny of Sheikh al-Tusi. That is, he was his grandson in terms of relationship. And Sheikh al-Tusi passed away in 461 Hijri. Sayyid ibn Tawus passed away in 664 Hijri, that is, about 200 years later. And he was a Marja-e-Taqlid of his time and possessed great greatness, he had a very great position. He had a great status. So he wrote the book 'Jamal al-Usbu', that is, prayers for the whole week. In it, he has recorded this Dua. Allama Majlisi has recorded this Dua in 'Bihar al-Anwar'. Look at the sentence of the Dua, what it is. "Allahumma" (O Allah), they are reading the Dua, "la wa la taslubna-l-yaqina li-tuli-l-amadi fi ghaybatihi" (O Lord, do not take away from our hearts the certainty, the conviction, due to the long duration of his occultation). May it not be that we become doubtful about the Imam. Because what is the opposite of certainty (yaqin)? Doubt (shak). God forbid, it should not happen that due to the prolonged and extended nature of the occultation (ghaybat), we start wondering whether the reappearance (zuhur) has actually happened or not. We don't know if the Imam exists or not, or if he is truly the Imam. Is it not possible that, God forbid, God forbid, some sect is saying the Imam has come, or some people are saying the Imam has come? Are those people correct? These kinds of doubts, these kinds of suspicions, Satan puts into the heart. Because it is Satan's job to put doubts into the heart. To create doubt in the heart is the work of Satan. So here we are praying. The Imam has taught us: "Lā taslubnāl-yaqīna li-ṭūlil-amadi fī ghaybatihi" (Do not deprive us of certainty due to the length of time in his occultation). May it not be that due to the prolonged and extended occultation, You take away our certainty, because Satan has put doubt in our hearts. "Wa-inqiṭāʿi khabarihi ʿannā" (And the cessation of news from him to us). And what is the second reason? One is the prolonged occultation, which is a cause for the loss of certainty, and the second is that no news from the Imam is reaching us. There is no news, it is the occultation, right? So there is no news, no information. So, O Lord, do not take away this certainty, due to these two reasons. And after that, the Imam says to pray like this: "Wa-lā tunsīnā dhikrahu wa-in-tiẓārahu" (And do not make us forget his remembrance and his waiting). O Lord, do not make us forget his remembrance, do not make us forget his memory. "Wa-in-tiẓārahu" (And his waiting). And may we never forget waiting for him. Never forget waiting for him. Wait day and night, as is the command of the Imams, that wait day and night. "Tawaqqaʿ amra ṣāḥibika laylaka wa-nahārak" (Expect the affair of your Master day and night). Keep waiting day and night, O Lord, never let us forget this thing from our hearts. "Wal-īmāna bihi" (And faith in him). And may it not be that we forget the faith we have in him. Allahu Akbar. What strange sentences of supplication you see. Because it is found in traditions that the era will be so intense that it will be as if a man goes to sleep at night and by morning his faith will be gone. He will wake up in the morning with faith, and by evening his faith will be gone. This era of occultation is very difficult. And then after that, we pray: "Wa-quwwatal-yaqīni fī ẓuhūrihi" (And give us strong certainty regarding his reappearance). "Wad-duʿā'a lahu" (And grant us the success to pray for him). Because this success (tawfiq) is also from Allah. The one who gives success is Allah, not the servant. What success will a servant give? He himself is a beggar, what will he give to others? Success is given only by Allah. It is written in the Quran as well: "Wa-mā tawfīqī illā billāh" (And my success is only through Allah). And whatever success I have, the Prophet is saying, whatever success there is, it is only from the side of Allah. So no servant can take away success from anyone. Pharaoh could not take it away from Lady Asiya. So then what will these ordinary servants take away? So "Wad-duʿā'a lahu waṣ-ṣalāta ʿalayhi" (And praying for him and sending blessings upon him), meaning I should continuously send blessings (durud) upon him. "Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa-āli Muḥammad wa-ʿajjil farajahum" (O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief). Meaning, how many things are we asking for? In this sentence, one is faith in him, second is certainty in his reappearance, third is praying for him, fourth is continuously sending blessings upon him. Meaning whenever you send salawat, "Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa-āli Muḥammad wa-ʿajjil farajahum wal-ʿan aʿdā'ahum ajmaʿīn" (O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their relief, and curse all their enemies). This blessing is a complete blessing. Send blessings in this way. "Waṣ-ṣalāta ʿalayhi ḥattā lā yuqanniṭanā ṭūlu ghaybatihi min ẓuhūrihi wa-qiyāmihi" (And blessings upon him so that the length of his occultation does not make us despair of his reappearance and his uprising). Meaning, make the faith so strong that despair never finds a way. May there never be despair, never any qunut, meaning despair. And what thing should make us despair? Despair, meaning this length of occultation, the prolongation of the occultation, should not make us despair. That we should not despair of what? Of the Imam's reappearance and the Imam's uprising, his re-appearance. Never despair. Never in the mind, because it is Iblis's job to put doubt. Emphasize that, it is Iblis's job to put doubt. Iblis puts doubt and it is our responsibility to immediately remove the doubt. As soon as a doubt comes to mind like, 'I don't know if the Imam exists or not,' then immediately say: "Aʿūdhu billāhi minash-shayṭānir-rajīm" (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan), "Aʿūdhu billāhil-qawiyyi minash-shayṭānil-ghawiyyi" (I seek refuge in Allah the Powerful from the misguided Satan), "Wa-aʿūdhu bi-Muḥammadir-raḍiyyi" (And I seek refuge in Muhammad the Pleasing). This isti'adha (seeking refuge) that I am telling you, it is present in the traditions. Who is this... Saying A'udhubillah is called isti'adha. This teaching was given by the Master of the Universe, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), to Kumayl ibn Ziyad al-Nakha'i. He gave this teaching of isti'adha to Kumayl: Aʿūdhu billāhil-qawiyyi minash-shayṭānil-ghawiyyi, wa-aʿūdhu bi-Muḥammadir-raḍiyyi, min sharri mā quddira wa-quḍiya, wa-aʿūdhu bi-ālihit-ṭayyibīna min sharril-jinnati wannāsi ajmaʿīn. So take refuge in this era of occultation. In what? Take refuge in Allah. Take refuge in the sacred essence of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And take refuge in the essence of the Ahlul-Bayt of the Messenger (a.s.). This isti'adha is formally present in the books of hadith where the Master of the Universe gave advice to Kumayl, and one of them is this. So how should the method of supplication be? How should the remembrance of the Imam be? How should one pray for the Imam? There are many things in this, there are many in the traditions, but I will present only a few points for your service because, in any case, there is not enough room in the span of time. Just a few points for your service. The first thing is that in supplication, whenever you ask Allah for something, keep in mind that the one who fulfills supplications, meaning the one who answers them, is only Allah. There is no one besides the Essence of Truth. Servants can do nothing. Servants are beggars. Meaning, be completely hopeless of whatever is in the hands of people. Whatever is in the hands of people, and trust and reliance should be only on the Essence of Allah. That is why it is found in a Hadith Qudsi. This Hadith Qudsi is present in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 90, page 341, and this Hadith Qudsi is present there. And that Hadith Qudsi is like this—you know what Hadith Qudsi is, those things that came directly from Allah to the Prophet but did not become part of the Quran or other heavenly books. So, in any case, Allah revealed this revelation to Prophet Isa (a.s.): "Yā ʿĪsā udʿūnī duʿā'al-gharīq" (O Isa, look, pray to Me like this when you pray to Me). Not for Me, excuse me, meaning when you pray to Me, pray like someone who is drowning is praying. Dua al-Ghariq (The supplication of the drowning). The one who is drowning is praying. Al-hazin, who is sorrowful, whose heart is broken. He is praying. Whose heart is broken. "Alladhī laysa lahu mughīth" (The one who has no other helper). Pray like this. The refuge is only Allah. It is the Essence of Truth, that's all. Pray to the Essence of Truth. Just ask for supplication, O Lord. "Allāhumma ʿajjil li-waliyyikal-faraj" (O Allah, hasten the relief of Your Wali). Morning, evening, afternoon, night, always. As much as possible. And here I will present one point for your service, that never let the thought come to your mind that we pray a lot. This is something that no matter how much we do, it is less. No matter how much we do, it is less. No matter how much we serve the Ahlul-Bayt, it is less. Never let it come to your mind that we are doing a lot, our service is great, we have done this much. This is the work we are doing, this is the work we are running, this institution we are running, this thing we are doing. Do not let this come to your mind. This is an Iblisi (Satanic) whisper. This is a whisper of Satan. Remove this from your mind. If anyone in the world is getting even a tiny opportunity to serve the family of Muhammad (a.s.), then this is only success from Allah, and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) is giving them permission, that is why they are doing it. And this is the honor of the doer, the servant. It is not the honor of the family of Muhammad. It is an honor for the servant that he is serving them. Whether it is a small service or a big service. Time is very short, but I will give you a small example for your service. Our great scholars, who were truly scholars, used to sit near the door in the gathering of Sayyid al-Shuhada (Imam Husayn) and fix the shoes. They used to say these are the guests of the Imam and we are the servants of the Imam. Today, we do a little bit of work and start attributing it to ourselves. And these are the people who have truly served, and I have seen one or two examples with my own eyes. It is not a hearsay story. I have truly seen people fixing shoes. So pray like someone who has no other refuge. Only Allah, and be hopeless of whatever is in the hands of people. Let other people of the world say these are beggars, what will they give? Just only that Essence of Truth. The second thing is very important. It holds great importance, and that is that whenever you pray, do it with full attention. There should be 100% attention. And you are remembering your Imam, right? The heart should be filled. The heart should be sorrowful. "Allāhumma ʿajjil li-waliyyikal-faraj". "Yā Bāsiṭ" (O Expander). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time. With full attention, with full focus. There is a tradition in Usul al-Kafi in Kitab al-Dua, in Volume 2. Kitab al-Dua. There is a hadith on page 473, and this hadith is from the Master of the Pious, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). What does he say? "Lā yaqballullāhu ʿazza wajalla duʿā'a qalbin lāhin" (Allah will never accept the supplication of a heart that is not attentive). Not attentive. Not attentive, their attention is wandering here and there, thinking of something else, doing something else. Or as seen nowadays, checking the mobile and praying. No, no. That is fine if Allah gives reward, that is a different thing. But what is the actual value of that supplication? The Master himself says that Allah will not accept it. Ask as much as you want. The attention is here and there. You are praying only and only for the reappearance of the Imam, right? Just the heart should be filled. For example, reciting this supplication: "Allāhumma kun li-waliyyikal-ḥujjati-bnil-Ḥasan" (O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of al-Hasan). So as it is present in the traditions, it is highly recommended to raise the hands. Raf' al-yadayn, meaning raising the hands, is highly recommended. It has been emphasized a lot. Although there are other methods of supplication that are in the traditions, but there is no time for that now. But there is a tradition in Kafi and it is present in other books that raf' al-yadayn, meaning by raising the hands. Meaning this is a way to gather your focus, this is a way to gather your attention. That brother, pray in this manner. And the third thing is that the heart should be so full, so full, and so tender that the hardness of the heart diminishes. The hardness of the heart should decrease and the heart should become so soft that tears come to the eyes automatically. However, this state is not achieved very easily. That is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said in a very famous hadith. This tradition is present in Bihar al-Anwar. It is in Bihar, volume 90, in Kitab al-Dua, page number 313. Bihar al-Anwar volume 90, page number 313, hadith number 17. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Ightanimu al-du'a 'inda al-riqqah' (Seize the opportunity for supplication when the heart is tender). Look, when the heart is soft, that is, when tears come to your eyes, consider that time as a blessing for supplication. That is, pray at that time. It is the best time. The heart has become soft. For example, in the state of prostration, if the remembrance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) comes to mind, or 'Ya Sahib al-Zaman, Ya Sahib al-Zaman'—write the example in prostration. So the Prophet says, consider this a blessing. Why is it so high up to here? Ya Sahib al-Zaman. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyika al-faraj. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyika al-faraj. If tears come to the eyes, then understand that 'fa-innaha rahma' (for it is a mercy). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is saying that when this opportunity arises and your state changes like this, understand that the Mercy of Allah is descending upon you. Allahu Akbar. This is the tradition. The Mercy of Allah is descending. And then, the fourth condition for supplication—although there are many conditions, but briefly, moving quickly towards our destination—is that one should continue to pray constantly. Do not get tired of praying. Usually, when we pray in the morning, we think in the evening, 'I already prayed in the morning.' When we pray in the evening, we think, 'I prayed in the morning or afternoon, so what is the need to pray again at night?' No, this is a satanic whisper. Look, be very cautious of Satan. Satan attacks continuously because you are on the right path. Because you are on the Sirat al-Mustaqim. You are on the path of the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Therefore, Satan will continue to attack. Beware of this attack. He has different ways of attacking. So Satan will continue to attack, and that attack—meaning, look at what is found in the traditions—is that one should never get tired. The tradition is such that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said in this hadith—the reference for this is Bihar al-Anwar, volume 90, Kitab al-Dua, page number 364, hadith number 8, and this hadith is narrated from Amali al-Shaykh al-Tusi. Shaykh al-Tusi, the Shaykh al-Ta'ifa, a high-ranking Mujtahid of his time whose title was Shaykh al-Ta'ifa, who established the Hawza Ilmiyya of Najaf al-Ashraf, laid its foundation. He was the founder, Shaykh al-Tusi, do you know? Shaykh al-Tusi was the founder of the Hawza Ilmiyya of Najaf. In his Amali, this hadith is present that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Ma futiha li-ahadin babu du'a' (The door of supplication is not opened for anyone), except that when the door of supplication is opened, the door to having that supplication answered is also opened. Here, 'the door of supplication is opened' means Allah has given the servant permission and the opportunity to pray, and along with that, Allah opens the door of 'istijabat' (the answering of that prayer), meaning the door for the fulfillment of that prayer. In other words, whenever a servant prays with a sincere heart for lawful and religious matters, Allah answers his prayer. It is not possible that Allah does not answer the prayer. Yes, of course, there is a delay. It is not that we prayed here and it was answered there; it is not like that. If someone thinks like this, for example, he cannot be a wise person. A wise person knows that when it is Allah's wisdom, then Allah will answer that prayer. Allah will fulfill that prayer. This is in Allah's control, in Allah's hands. But He will definitely fulfill it. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says—meaning the first sentence was that when Allah opens the door of supplication for someone, He also opens the door of 'istijabat' (the fulfillment of the prayer)—and then he says, when Allah opens the door of supplication for any one of you, he should pray with full effort. That is, do not get tired, struggle. 'Falyajhad' (He should strive). The sentence in Arabic is 'Falyajhad', strive. 'Fa-innallaha 'azza wa-jalla la yamallu hatta tamullu' (For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not get tired until you get tired). What a strange sentence! Meaning, put in full effort. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, put in full effort, work hard in supplication. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, work hard in supplication. Why? Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not get tired until you get tired. Obviously, does Allah get tired? No, Allah does not get tired. Allah never gets tired. But here the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wants to explain a point, that is, Allah's mercy will continue to descend upon you until you yourself get tired. Until you yourself give up. And Allama Majlisi has narrated this same sentence from Abu Tayyib, that what is meant by a human getting tired is that the human gets tired, becomes worried, becomes impatient, that 'it is enough, what more can I do?' But from Allah's side, the meaning of Allah getting tired is that Allah stops sending His Divine Mercy. 'Tarkun lil-fi'li minallah' (Abandonment of the action from Allah). Allah's action here is His mercy. Allah is sending His mercy. As long as the servant is praying, the Divine Mercy is continuously descending upon him. When the servant gets tired, the chain of mercy stops. So, this supplication is also a mercy from the Lord. Allah does not give this opportunity to everyone. So those who raise fingers at supplication should understand that they are raising fingers at the Mercy of the Lord. Just don't get tired. Keep praying as much as you can. Pray morning and evening. Different supplications have been introduced. For example, when you send Salawat: 'Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa-ali Muhammad', then after every Salawat, do not forget: 'wa-'ajjil farajahum' (and hasten their relief). And hasten the relief of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, that is, hasten their reappearance. 'Wa-la'ana a'da'ahum' (And curse their enemies). So whenever you send Salawat, definitely keep these two sentences, these two phrases in mind. Do not be shy about this. These are very powerful supplication phrases. Understand their importance, understand their value. Then, besides that, there is the Dua-e-Ahad which should be recited every morning. It is found in the traditions that whoever recites Dua-e-Ahad continuously for 40 days will not leave this world until he has the Ziyarat of the Imam. And if he dies before the reappearance, he will be raised from his grave after the reappearance. So that he may be counted among the Imam's helpers and supporters. His name should be among the helpers. Because he used to remember his Imam every morning. And one phrase of this supplication is: 'Allahumma in hala bayni wa-baynahu al-mawt' (O Allah, if death comes between me and him), O Lord, if death comes between me and him, if I die, if I die before his reappearance. 'Allahumma in hala bayni wa-baynahu al-mawt'—which death? 'Alladhi ja'altahu 'ala 'ibadika hatman maqdiyya' (Which You have made a certain and decreed matter for Your servants), meaning everyone has to die. Everyone has to die. No one is going to live forever in this world. 'Fa-akhrijni min qabri mu'taziran kafani shahiran sayfi mujarradan qanati' (Then bring me out of my grave, wearing my shroud, with my sword drawn, my spear ready). Bring me out of my grave. Raise me from the grave, wearing my shroud, in that same state. 'Shahiran sayfi' (With my sword drawn), and in my hand should be my sword, a naked sword. 'Shahiran sayfi mujarradan qanati' (With my sword drawn and my spear ready). 'Mulabbiyan da'wata al-da'i fi al-hadiri wa-al-badi' (Responding to the call of the caller, whether in the city or the desert). And when my Imam calls me, I should say 'Labbayk' to his invitation. Wherever I am. Whether I am in the cities or in the wilderness. Wherever I am, or wherever my Imam calls me, I should immediately say 'Labbayk' to his voice. Labbayk ya Sahib al-Zaman. Labbayk ya Sahib al-Zaman. Labbayk ya Mahdi. This spirit of 'Labbayk' should be there. However, is just supplication enough? No. Then it is also not just empty supplication. Along with supplication, our important responsibility is, as I just mentioned in your service, to have the 'Ma'rifat' (recognition) of the Imam—what is Imamate? What is the Imam? And then, along with that, acquire so much knowledge that you can defend Imamate. Defend Imamate. That if any person writes a book on the Imam or the subject of Imamate, writes an article, in newspapers or publishes a book, then we should immediately be ready to give an answer. In our India, a man wrote a book 150 years ago, 200 years ago, 150 years ago, 'Tuhfa-e-Ithna Ashariya', against the Shias. Muhaddith-e-Dehlavi was his name. You know that just that one book, it was a minor book which had 14 chapters, just 14 chapters. 53 answers were written by our scholars at that time; they were so sensitive about how these things were being said about the Imam. 53 answers were written, 53. And they were not minor answers. Among which one answer alone was 'Abaqat al-Anwar', and this book 'Abaqat al-Anwar', which has now been printed in its summary, meaning it is being printed. Ayatollah Milani is printing it as a summary in Qom, and it is currently going up to 90 volumes. The summary is up to 90 volumes. You understand that this book 'Abaqat al-Anwar' was an answer to only one chapter of that book by Muhaddith-e-Dehlavi, 'Tuhfa-e-Ithna Ashariya'. In which Muhaddith-e-Dehlavi has said that the Shias' claim that these verses and traditions in the honor of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) are wrong. He rejected eight verses and rejected five hadiths. So they proved those eight verses and those five traditions from their own books, that these were revealed in the honor of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And for that, how many references—you understand that today, there is continuous research on one book. So this much knowledge—these are the scholars who defend. Now, here, knowledge is very important. Very important. Now, here is a hadith for your service, just that. No more than that. And you see this hadith, it is present in 'Ehtijaj-e-Tabarsi', who was a scholar of the 6th century, he passed away in the 6th century. The late Tabarsi, Abu Mansur Tabarsi, and besides that, it is in the Tafsir attributed to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Besides that, this hadith is present in 'Bihar al-Anwar', volume 2, 'Bab al-Thawab', 'Bab al-Thawab al-Hidayat wa-al-Ta'lim'. In it, this hadith is present. Hadith number 12. You see, the tradition is very powerful—meaning three references I have presented in your service. The Imam says from his noble father, meaning Imam al-Hadi (a.s.), Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) narrates the hadith from his noble father Imam al-Hadi (a.s.) that 'Lawla man yabqa ba'da ghaybatihi' (If there were not those who remain after his occultation), and then he takes that special name for whom it is recommended to stand, although facing the Qibla and placing a hand on the head—that in his occultation, just for ease here, it is the Imam, right? Meaning, in his occultation, if such individuals did not exist... Which individuals? 'Min al-Ulama' (from the scholars), if there were no scholars. Who are the people of knowledge? What are the characteristics of these scholars? First, 'Al-Da'ina lahu' (those who invite to him). The first characteristic is that they invite people towards the Imam. Meaning, in every speech of theirs, there should be a mention of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). These are not just individuals. No matter how much he is mentioned, it is less. He is in every speech, every gathering, every class; the Imam must be mentioned. 'Wal-dallina alayhi' (and those who provide evidence for him), and they present proofs for the existence of the Imam. If someone does not have the proof, they provide it to them. 'Wal-dhabina 'an dinihi' (and those who defend his religion), and they protect the Imam's religion. Protect it. 'Dhabina' means those who protect. Protect the Imam's religion. Through what? 'Bi-hujajillah' (through the proofs of Allah). And then, an important point comes here: 'Wal-munqidhina li-du'afa' ibadillah' (and those who rescue the weak servants of Allah), and they save the weak servants of Allah, they liberate them. They get them freed. Through whose hands should they be freed? 'Min shibak Iblis wa maradatihi' (from the nets of Iblis and his rebels), they should take them out of the net of Iblis and his rebels. 'Shibak' means net. Take them out of it. 'Wa min fikhakh al-nawasib' (and from the traps of the Nawasib), and the traps laid by the Nawasib—the traps, meaning that which is set to catch prey. Who are the Nawasib? The plural of Nasibi. Who is a Nasibi? The Imam said that a Nasibi is not someone who is our enemy, an enemy of us Ahlulbayt. Because—we are saying this in our own words just to explain—no one has the courage to say, 'I am an enemy of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' The Imam says no one has the audacity to say, 'I am an enemy of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Rather, a Nasibi is one who holds enmity towards you Shias. Because you love us. You have the love of Ali and the children of Ali in your hearts. That is why he holds enmity towards you. So, these scholars—if these scholars did not exist, who take people out of the nets of Iblis and the traps of the Nawasib—if these scholars, these educated individuals, these insightful individuals did not exist, then 'Lama baqiya ahad illa irtadda 'an dinillah' (no one would remain except that they would have apostatized from the religion of Allah). They would have left the religion. 'Wa lakinahum' (but they), these scholars, who are they? 'Yumsikuna azimata qulubi du'afa' al-shia' (they hold the reins of the hearts of the weak Shias). These are the people who are firmly holding the reins of the Shias who are weak in terms of their faith. The reins of the hearts. In other words, these scholars are those who stay in touch with the weak Shias, they remain connected to them, those whose faith is weak. They support them in every way. Meaning, through their speeches, through their books, and in whatever way possible. And how do they support them? 'Kama yumsiku sahib al-safinati sukkannaha' (just as the captain of a ship holds its rudder). Just as the captain of a ship holds the steering or the sails—in the old days there were sails, so how he manages them. In today's era, how he manages the steering so that the vehicle or the ship does not go astray. It keeps moving on the straight path. This is the job of the scholars, to keep them steady. And then the Imam says, 'Hum ula'ika hum al-afdaluna 'inda Allah 'azza wa jall' (they are the ones who are the most excellent in the sight of Allah, the Almighty). These are the people whose status and rank in the sight of Allah are the highest. There is no one more excellent than them. The highest level. This was an important point. For instance, Ibn Khaldun was a very great historian. He raised an objection. His objection was that the belief in Imam Mahdi is not correct. It is not correct. Why? He brought three or four objections, saying it is not in Bukhari or Muslim, it came from Iran, and it is a Shia belief. The scholars gave him the answer. They named who—meaning from the Ahl-e-Sunnah, because Ibn Khaldun was also from the Ahl-e-Sunnah—which scholars wrote that he is Imam Mahdi (a.s.). They wrote books on the belief of Mahdism and narrated hadiths. Bukhari's teacher, Tayalisi, who died 51 years before the birth of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), wrote his book. Meaning, he brought hadiths about Imam-e-Zamana. After that, Abdur Razzaq San'ani, who was also a teacher of Bukhari, wrote 'Musannaf' in 15 volumes. He brought a whole chapter in his book titled 'Bab al-Mahdi', and in this way, there is a whole list of scholars who wrote books on Imam-e-Zamana. They wrote them before the birth of Imam-e-Zamana. This is a matter of wonder. Meaning, this was the belief. One should have enough knowledge to defend it, so that if another Ibn Khaldun is born today or any false claimant arises, they can be refuted. In this way, we must constantly have enough knowledge so that we can defend. At the very least, Shias can keep their belief intact so that no one can attack it. So, let us all, in this sacred night, pray together for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Especially, as per the instruction of Ayatollah Vahid Khorasani for tonight, when it strikes 12:00 in India, everyone together... Recite 'Allahumma li-waliyyik', and after that, other things you might have heard, and gift it to Janabe Narjis Khatun. 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyik' and Salawat, recite all of this together while sitting in your homes and gift it to Janabe Narjis Khatun. Gift it to the noble mother of Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajah al-sharif). Insha'Allah, pray to Allah that for the sake of this blessed and sacred night, hasten the reappearance of our Imam. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, forgive our shortcomings, our mistakes, and our sins, and purify us in a way that only You can, as it is within Your power, so that we may be counted among the helpers of our Imam. 'Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin'. Thank you very much, Sir. Sir, we have received a few questions. The first question is, Sir, because 'Dua-e-Ahad' was mentioned, in which a person prays that even if he dies before the Imam's reappearance, Allah should raise him from his grave—the question is related to that: What is the meaning of 'Raj'at'? What is the meaning of Raj'at and when will it happen? Actually, these were two separate questions, but since both were related to Raj'at, I have combined them into one. What is the meaning of Raj'at and when will it happen? And will the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) also be back in Raj'at? The topic of Raj'at is very vast. The connection with Dua-e-Ahad is that when the Imam reappears, we will be raised from our graves. This is about the time of reappearance. As far as Raj'at is concerned, there are various narrations, and the topic is very vast. It is that after Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) leaves this world, a whole sequence of the Masumin (a.s.) will begin again, and the Masumin (a.s.) will arrive. I will just quote one sentence from a hadith for you: 'Raj'at is only for pure faith and pure disbelief.' Meaning, those with pure faith will be raised, and those who are pure disbelievers will be raised. Meaning, Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) and their very special companions (a.s.), and the enemies of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad who are pure, staunch Nasibi enemies, they will be raised. And then the Masumin (a.s.) will rule. It is a very vast topic, which we are discussing briefly here; it requires a full discussion. Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the opportunity, we will discuss it. Yes. Insha'Allah. The second question, Sir, is to some extent—this discussion came up during the talk... But perhaps for further clarification: If Dua is our responsibility, what precautions must we take while praying for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.)? See, first of all, as far as precautions are concerned, Dua is one of the responsibilities, and the most important thing is that Taqwa (piety) is very important. One should have religion. A person should have faith, Taqwa, be pious, and be insightful. These are all things, and along with that, one should have Ma'rifat (gnosis). Because Dua or any action without Ma'rifat is useless. So, all these things are very necessary. And after that, everything through which we prepare the ground for the Imam's reappearance. You prepare the ground for the reappearance. And, of course, adherence to Sharia, as I have mentioned many times in my speeches before, for example, the orders of the Maraje, what is written in the 'Tawzih al-Masail'—from the chapter of Taharat (purity) to the chapter of Diyat (blood money), and besides that, in matters, in everything—in acts of worship and dealings, whatever is present, follow them, obey them in whatever they have ordered. Meaning, in Sharia rulings and in dealings, whatever is the scope of Taqlid, act upon it. Be pious, be God-fearing, be insightful, and then, whatever their command is, act upon it accordingly. This is our Sharia responsibility in the era of Ghaybah (occultation), because as you have heard in the discussion of Taqlid, it is also the Imam's command. Yes. Sir, the third question is: Salam, as we live in a society of different cultures. Yes. To prove from the Holy Quran the reality that there are Imams and they are appointed by Allah. So, with the help of which verses can we prove? And even our belief becomes more strong, and God forbid, we do not have any doubts regarding Imamate in our lives. See, if the question becomes a little clearer, it would be better—meaning, who is our addressee that we want to invite towards Shi'ism, towards the Imams? If they are non-Muslim, first invite them towards Islam, let them understand Islam, meaning understand Tawhid (monotheism). Because Tawhid is the foundation, Adl (justice) is the foundation. So, first explain Tawhid to them. If they are a believer in multiple gods, tell them, 'Brother, there are not multiple gods.' Just as the Prophet announced, 'I invite you, I call you to say this, to accept that there is no god except Allah, and renounce all these idols.' Or whoever is of any religion, through rational arguments—see, the Shia religion is entirely based on rational arguments. So, prove it to them through rational arguments. And if they become Muslim, then it is easy to introduce Imamate after Prophethood. If they are not Shia, they are Muslim but belong to another school of thought, another religion, another sect—not on the religion of Ahlulbayt—then start from the original: 'Did the Messenger of Allah appoint a successor or not? If he did, who did he appoint? In whose favor are the verses and narrations? How many hadiths, how many verses are there? What are the historical evidences? You look at them, as I mentioned to you yesterday, look at their knowledge and look at the knowledge of the enemies. Just compare. For example, there are so many sermons in Nahj al-Balagha, so many sermons about Tawhid, the sermons of the Master of the Universe—bring one or two sermons in comparison, or rather, not a sermon, but a paragraph of a sermon that can match Nahj al-Balagha in terms of meaning and concept. It is simple, very simple. See, there should be intellect, and there should be a willingness in a person to accept the truth. There is no question of stubbornness. to accept the truth. The second thing is supplications (duas). Bring one dua from Sahifa-e-Sajjadiya. Just one dua that is in Sahifa-e-Sajjadiya—not the entire Sahifa-e-Sajjadiya, that is a very great thing. Do not bring the entire Mafatih al-Jinan, but bring something that matches the concepts available in it. We are presenting to you things that have not been taken from here. Interestingly, many times the duas found among them are actually originally found right here. So, in this way, show them the truth, that this is the truth. Because the majority are those who are not aware of the truth. Their only slogan is—this is the Quran's slogan. The Quran says, what was the slogan of the Kuffar (disbelievers) when the Prophets would call them? They would say, 'Inna wajadna 'alayha aba'ana' (We found our forefathers doing this). So we are doing it, that's the end of it. So they just have to follow that. If they don't follow the religion of their forefathers, the Quran asks this very question. Oh, they talk about following their forefathers, even though their forefathers were neither guided nor did they use their intellect. Still, they will follow their forefathers. These people are strange. Meaning, the Quran is questioning them. So, in the same way, awaken their intellects, awaken their nature through the teachings of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.), and there is also a tradition that you should convey our hadiths to the people, because if people see the beauty of our speech, our hadiths, and our duas, if they become aware of them, then surely 100% they will follow us. The only exception is if someone is stubborn and possesses the emotion of stubbornness, saying, 'No, we will not do it.' Just as many people are stubborn themselves, so stubborn people exist everywhere. Yes. The last question, sir, is related to Dua-e-Ahad: 'What about women? If they pray Dua-e-Ahad for 40 days, will they also rise from their graves with a sword?' In the traditions that exist regarding the support of the Imam, women are also mentioned. But of course, not for swords; the responsibility is according to their capacity. Just as in the time of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), there were nurses, women who used to serve. If someone—like their duty—it is found even about Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the Princess of the Worlds, that she was present in battles. So it is found, but how? According to their duty, not in terms of fighting, because Jihad is exempted for women. Jihad is not permissible for women. This is very clear, a Sharia ruling. But other duties, for example, as I mentioned, it is present that, for instance, as a nurse, for example, whoever it may be. So now, whatever will happen in the time of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), after his reappearance when there will be wars—and there will be wars, because here, incidentally, let me mention one thing to you—some people say, 'No, no, Imam-e-Zamana will only deal with love and affection.' God forbid, is Imam-e-Zamana a bloodthirsty tyrant? No, no, Astaghfirullah, who is called a bloodthirsty tyrant? One who kills the innocent is a bloodthirsty tyrant. Imam-e-Zamana is not a bloodthirsty tyrant, God forbid, God forbid. But yes, whoever is a tyrant and an oppressor, if he does not understand through arguments, does not understand through intellect, does not understand through rational matters, then he cannot live in the world, he cannot remain in the government of Imam-e-Zamana. And that is why the government of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will be different from other Infallibles (a.s.). Other Infallibles (a.s.) were 'Ma'murun biz-zahir' (commanded by the apparent). Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will be 'Ma'murun bil-batin' (commanded by the inner/hidden). Look, it is a very simple thing. I mean, some people ask, 'Will Imam-e-Zamana commit mass murder?' He will not kill everyone, like a man who started cutting everyone down. No, no, the meaning is that those who persist in their oppression, their force, their enmity—look, it is simple. When a farmer farms, what does he do? Before farming, he levels the land. How does he do it? The hard things, like stones and such, he removes and throws them away so that the land becomes soft. This is the farmer's job. So, do you ask any farmer, 'Oh brother, why are you being cruel to these stones? Why are you removing and throwing away the stones?' Do you ask that? You don't. That is one thing. The second thing is that if you see that, for example, if someone establishes a government, then obviously, in this government, first, whatever oppression and force needs to be eradicated, one must explain to them. If they do not understand, then the Imam will put an end to them, will annihilate them. Otherwise, oppression and force will remain. Let me present a small example to you, as many people say, 'Oh no, Imam-e-Zamana will not kill.' ISIS attacked Iraq and Syria. So, was force used to eradicate ISIS or not? Were the soldiers of ISIS killed or not? Was there bombing on them or not? Were they annihilated or not? Why did we fight them? I mean, whoever the Iraqis were, or whoever the individuals were who went to fight them, whoever the soldiers of the religion were, they all went to Iraq, Iran, Syria, whatever Mujahideen there were, from wherever, they all went to fight, and they went and—how many believers were martyred in this, how many? In this path, to eradicate ISIS. So, should one say to them, 'Brother, why are you killing them? You should have gone and hugged ISIS, because the religion of Muhammad is this: treat everyone with love.' No, no. When a tyrant and oppressor is in front, then one is treated in that same way, and this is the Sunnah of Allah. Allah's Sunnah is also this. Allah explains first. When the matter is not understood, then He destroys them in the world through various punishments. Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is a proof of Allah, a means of Allah, to eradicate the enemies of Allah. For them, Imam-e-Zamana is a punishment. And in this way, oppression and force will be eradicated. This is one method. So, anyway, women will also have a role. There is a tradition in this regard that a narrator came to the Imam and said, 'When will the government of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) be? And we see that the government is in the hands of others in this way.' He complained to the Imam, weeping, about how the situation is. The Imam said to him, 'The state you are in right now is better for you. Because you are living a life of comfort. Meaning, you are wearing soft clothes, sleeping on good carpets, and eating good food. But when our Mahdi reappears, those who will be his helpers and supporters, those who will be his companions, they will eat hard food, wear rough clothes, sleep on stones, stay awake at nights, perform worship, and keep traveling all day long.' These are all the qualities of his helpers and supporters. Right now, individuals like us only talk verbally, but actually, to qualify for that, a lot of criteria are needed. Yes. We are grateful to you, sir, that you made us aware of our responsibilities in the light of the traditions of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). And once again, we are grateful to all the viewers. Especially those gentlemen who made this webinar successful through their questions. InshaAllah, as we have received feedback from the believers, Alhamdulillah, regarding this webinar, that they liked this series and this format very much, and more such programs should be held. Pray that God gives us the ability to organize more such programs. One piece of good news that needs to be conveyed to you is that, InshaAllah, we will continue such programs in the light of the teachings of Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad (a.s.), and this Friday, meaning this Friday, InshaAllah, a series of discussions and speeches on some important topics will be continued, InshaAllah. It will start this Friday, April 10, 2020. InshaAllah, InshaAllah. And on Friday, there will be a speech by the honorable Syed Mehdi Modarresi. His speech will take place. The details of this will be conveyed to you, InshaAllah. Stay in touch with us through our social media. Subscribe to our YouTube channel, 'The Strong Rope', and press the bell icon so that its details reach you through YouTube. Apart from this, our Twitter, Facebook, Instagram account, WhatsApp number, Telegram—stay connected through these as well so that the details keep reaching you, InshaAllah. May God help us all to be with our Imam of the time... Will his speech be in English? Yes, yes, his speech will be in English, InshaAllah. May God grant us all the ability to pray for the reappearance of our Imam of the time. In closing, listen to a few verses regarding the wait for the reappearance, in which a waiter for the Imam is praying to his Imam for something. The human himself is praying to his Imam in these verses. Listen: 'O most sacred flower of the garden of Askari, O Kaaba of the light of vision, Qibla of principles, take from us the tribute of heart and soul, Master, without you, this paradise is not acceptable. Not for the world, not for wealth and gold, not for ministry, not for the world, not for wealth and gold, not for ministry, we are living for the sake of your vision.' And our final prayer is praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Hassan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience, and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, hasten the reappearance of Your representative, and make us among his helpers, his supporters, his Shia, and his servants, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance and curse their enemies all.

title: Qabron Se Inteqaam Kyun? | Aah Jannatul Baqi | Demolition of Jannatul Baqi | #YoutubeShorts
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and spiritual motivations behind the demolition of Jannat al-Baqi. It argues that the destruction of these sacred graves is an extension of the historical envy and oppression faced by the Progeny of Muhammad (Ahlulbayt). The speaker highlights that despite attempts to diminish their status, the glory of the Prophet's family remains protected by Allah.
content:
In the Holy Quran, Allah (SWT) states: 'Do people envy what Allah has bestowed upon them—meaning the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)—from His bounty? We have certainly given the Progeny of Ibrahim the Book and wisdom, and We have given them a great kingdom.' Since all these virtues and merits are bestowed by Allah (SWT), when the envious could not snatch the status of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them) from them, they chose the path of oppression. They usurped their rights, broke the allegiance pledged to them, waged war against them, and martyred them with poison or the sword. It reached the point where, when the oppressors saw that despite all their efforts, the status and glory of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them) remained intact, they began to take revenge on their graves. The demolition of Jannat al-Baqi is the result of that same envy and hatred.
Allah bestowed great wisdom and kingdom upon the Progeny of Ibrahim and Muhammad.
Envy toward the Ahlulbayt led to the usurpation of their rights and martyrdom.
Oppressors failed to diminish the status of the Progeny of Muhammad through direct conflict.
The demolition of Jannat al-Baqi is framed as an act of revenge against the Prophet's family.
Hatred and envy are identified as the primary drivers behind the destruction of sacred sites.
The glory of the Ahlulbayt remains intact despite physical attacks on their resting places.

title: Jaan Nisaar e Wilayat - Hurr Ibn Yazid Riyaahi (a.r.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of 'Jabr' (determinism) and how it has been historically misused to justify atrocities, specifically by the enemies of Imam Husayn (a.s.). It highlights the transformation of Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi, who rejected this false narrative to repent and sacrifice his life for the truth on the day of Ashura. The talk concludes by honoring Hurr's elevated status as the first martyr of Karbala and his legacy, which continues through his descendants like Sheikh Hurr al-Amili.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And Assalamu Alaikum, Assalamu Alaikum, Assalamu Alaikum. Mourners, it is true that 'destiny' (taqdeer) is a word that has been highly misused in the past and is still being misused today. Many went astray, who, in order to cleanse the skirt of their deeds from sins, took refuge in this word 'destiny' and tried to justify their sins by saying, 'It was written in destiny.' Blaming destiny for one's sins is called 'Jabr' (determinism), and those who believe in this creed are called Mujabbirah. The enemies of the Household of Muhammad (a.s.) also misused this creed of Jabr to unsuccessfully justify all their evil deeds and atrocities. And unknowingly, their followers and extremist individuals, based on the outcome of that same belief in Jabr, still support accursed ones like Yazid and Muawiyah. Even Shimr the accursed was asked, 'When you knew who Imam Husayn (a.s.) was and what his status was, why did you still murder Husayn?' That accursed one, to save himself from this sin, took refuge in this same creed of Jabr and said, 'This was written in destiny.' Taking [this] and saying, "This was written in my destiny," using the word of change... And the one who unmasked the face of those oppressors wearing the mask of tyranny through his actions, his name was Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi. On the morning of Ashura, Hurr found himself between Heaven and Hell. Seeing this hesitation, one of his companions said, "O Hurr, if we were asked who is the bravest warrior of Kufa, we would surely name you." But it had become clear to Hurr that the family of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had been made strangers in their own land, and despite the massive army of Yazid, they refused to submit. In this, the correction lies in sacrificing one's life for the sake of truth and in support of the Son of the Messenger. Although at that moment, Hurr's sin was grave, he knew very well that he was going to Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), who is the lamp of guidance and the son of Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.). This was the greatness of Janabe Zahra (s.a.)'s upbringing and the passion to abandon falsehood and return to the truth, due to which Imam Husayn (a.s.) accepted Hurr's repentance and said to him, "You are free as your mother named you, free in this world and..." ...and free in the hereafter, and achieved martyrdom. And this proved that when a person acts in this world according to the will of Allah and His Proof (Hujjah), then in the end, he attains the pleasure of Allah. In return for this repentance, the status that Allah and Imam Husayn (a.s.) bestowed upon Janabe Hurr-e-Riyahi is narrated in Al-Khisaal: 'The first to be martyred with Imam Husayn (a.s.) in the battlefield was Janabe Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi.' Not only was he the first martyr, but among all the martyrs, Janabe Hurr holds an elevated status. Imam Husayn (a.s.) tied the handkerchief of Hazrat Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.) on Hurr's forehead. Apart from this, the distinction that Shias hold worldwide today, backed by our eminent scholars, includes the great scholar and Muhaddith whom we know as Sheikh Hurr al-Amili (Rizwanullah Alaih), who wrote the monumental book 'Wasail al-Shia', which is a source of guidance for Shias today. Sheikh Hurr al-Amili was also from the lineage of Janabe Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi. The team of the 12th Imam (a.s.), on behalf of all of you, pays tribute to the first martyred warrior of Husayn, the brave Janabe Hurr... ...the martyred warrior, the brave Janabe Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi (r.a.), and presents salutations in his presence. And along with this, we also pray that Almighty Allah may hasten the reappearance of His last Proof, Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), and like Hurr, grant us the grace to distinguish truth from falsehood and to sacrifice our lives for the sake of our Imam of the Time in his presence. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

title: EP#3: Saqifah – Karbala Ki Buniyaad | Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological connection between the event of Saqifah and the tragedy of Karbala. It highlights the perspective of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), who identifies the events following the Prophet's passing as the root cause of the suffering endured by the Ahlulbayt. The discourse emphasizes that the martyrdom of Hazrat Muhsin and the attack on the house of Bibi Fatima (s.a.) served as the foundational calamity that led to the eventual tragedy at Karbala.
content:
The foundation of Karbala was laid in Saqifah. Hazrat Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said: "There is no day of greater calamity for us than Karbala. Although the day of Saqifah and the day when the door of the house of Ali Amir al-Mu'minin, Fatima, Hasan, Husayn, Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, and Fizza (a.s.) was burned, and Hazrat Muhsin ibn Ali (a.s.) was martyred by a kick, that day is even more calamitous and bitter for us, because that very day laid the foundation for the Day of Calamity (Yawm al-Azab), which is the day of Karbala."

title: Har Saal Azadaari Kyun? | Tajdeed-e-Azaa: Ek Vaada
excerpt: This lecture explains the spiritual significance and historical continuity of Azadari (mourning for Imam Hussain). It highlights that the practice is a fulfillment of the Prophet Muhammad's promise and Janab-e-Zahra's desire for her son to be remembered. The speaker emphasizes that the annual tradition of mourning serves as a guarantee for intercession and entry into Paradise on the Day of Judgment.
content:
What is this Azadari (mourning) that we perform, this Azadari of the Master of Martyrs (Sayyid-al-Shuhada) that we observe? In reality, it is an expression of love for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It is not just an expression of love for Hussain (a.s.)—though it certainly is that—but fundamentally, it is an expression of love for the Prophet. And we can never stop this expression; it can never diminish. Because the Prophet himself gave us its importance and the Prophet himself gave us its guarantee. There is that famous Hadith where, upon the birth of Hussain (a.s.), when the Prophet informed his daughter of the martyrdom of her son, Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.) wept. And after weeping, the question Janab-e-Sayyeda asked was, 'Ya Aba, O Father, faman yabki 'alay?' (O Father, who will weep for my child?) And then look at the following sentence, 'Wa man yantazimu bi-iqamatil aza-e lahu?' (And who will establish the Azadari for my child?) Establishing this Azadari was the desire of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.); it was her wish. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'Ya Fatima, O my daughter Fatima, inna nisa-a ummati yabkuna 'ala nisa-e ahl-e-bayti' (The women of my Ummah will weep for the women of my Ahl-e-Bayt). Wa rijaluhum yabkuna 'ala rijal-e ahl-e-bayti (And the men of my Ummah will weep for the men of my Ahl-e-Bayt). And then, when we are asked every year, 'You have come again? You perform Azadari every year, you weep so much every year, why do you do it? That event happened 1400 years ago, it ended 1400 years ago. How long will you mourn it?' The answer has been given by the Prophet, the guarantee has been given by the Prophet. The Prophet says, 'These people—meaning the women will weep for the women, the men will weep for the men—wa yujaddidunal aza-a (they will renew this mourning), they will keep doing it repeatedly. Jeelan ba'da jeelin (generation after generation), they will continue it. It will remain established in every era, Azadari will continue in every era. Fi kull-e sanatin (and it will happen every year). This Azadari will continue every year. This is not just about our destiny; it is the Prophet's guarantee upon which we perform Azadari. It was Janab-e-Zahra's (s.a.) desire upon which we perform Azadari. And when this Azadari takes place—meaning those who establish this mourning—what did the Prophet say next in this Hadith? Fa-idha kana yawmal qiyamati (When the Day of Judgment comes), what will happen? 'My daughter, you will intercede for the women, and I will intercede for the men. Wa kullu man baka minhum 'ala musab-e Hussain (And whoever among them has wept over the tragedy of Hussain), akhadhna bi-yadihi wa adkhalnal jannata (we will take them by the hand and lead them into Paradise).' The Prophet has given the guarantee; who can stop the Azadari? 'Ya Fatima, kullu 'aynin bakiyatun yawmal qiyamati (O Fatima, every eye will weep on the Day of Judgment), illa 'aynun bakat 'ala musab-e Hussain (except for the eye that has wept over the tragedy of Hussain).' Because that eye which has wept for Hussain in this world, when it goes to the hereafter and sees the reward of this weeping with its own eyes—with those very eyes, the eyes that it purified through weeping—then what will happen? Fa-innaha dahikatun mustabshira, bin-na'imil jannati (Then it will be smiling and rejoicing at the blessings of Paradise).

title: 13.20 Crore People Forgiven on Shab of Eid-ul-Fitr
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense mercy of Allah during the month of Ramadan as described by Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.). It details the specific numbers of individuals granted freedom from Hell throughout the month, culminating in a massive act of forgiveness on the night of Eid-ul-Fitr. The speaker encourages believers to spend this holy night in prayer and spiritual striving to attain these divine blessings.
content:
No human can estimate the mercy and forgiveness of the Lord of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.) said, 'Indeed, Allah (Jalla wa 'Azza wa 'Ala) frees 600,000 people from Hell on the first night of the month of Ramadan. Then, in the last ten nights, He frees the same number of people every night as He freed in those previous twenty nights.' That is, in the last ten nights, 12 million people receive freedom from Hell every night. And when the night of Eid-ul-Fitr arrives, Allah frees the same number of people as He has freed throughout the entire month of Ramadan. That is, on the night of Eid-ul-Fitr, 132 million people receive freedom from Hell. Now, Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.) commands his followers to remain awake on the night of Eid-ul-Fitr, pray, and continue to strive and make great efforts.

title: Zuhoor Achaanak Hoga | ⛅IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture explains that the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is unpredictable and sudden, much like the arrival of the Day of Judgment. Citing the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), the speaker emphasizes that only Allah knows the timing of this event. Believers are encouraged to maintain a state of constant readiness and anticipation for the Imam's arrival. The talk highlights that the divine preparation for his manifestation can occur in a single night.
content:
They asked, 'Ya Rasool Allah, when will the Sahib al-Ism al-Khas appear? When will Imam Mahdi (a.s.) reappear?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) likened the time of the Imam's reappearance to the time of the Day of Judgment. He said, 'Mathaluhu mathalus sa'ah'—the example of his reappearance is like the example of the Hour. Meaning, just as no one can fix a time for the Day of Judgment, no one can fix a time for the reappearance. 'La yujalliha li waqtiha illa hu'—only Allah knows its time. 'Thaqulat fis samawati wal ard'—it will be heavy upon the heavens and the earth. 'La ta'tikum illa baghtan'—it will come upon you suddenly. Just as the word 'baghtan' is used for the Day of Judgment, meaning it will come suddenly, the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) will be unexpected; it will happen suddenly. Therefore, we have been commanded in the traditions to wait for the reappearance day and night. In one night, the Lord of the Worlds will gather his affairs in such a way that He will bring about his reappearance.
