title: JASHN  |  AALAMI JASHN E ELAAN E WILAYAT
excerpt: This lecture celebrates the significance of Ghadir Khumm and the declaration of Wilayah, emphasizing the spiritual and historical importance of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). It explores the intersection of faith and literature, providing detailed insights into the technical structure of religious poetry such as Qasida and Marsiya. The program concludes by honoring participants of poetry and quiz competitions while encouraging believers to maintain the tradition of mourning for Imam Husain (a.s.) during Ayyam-e-Aza.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance, and curse their enemies... There is no god but Allah... My respected listeners, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. The famous companion of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Jabir bin Abdullah al-Ansari, himself narrates this tradition from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), stating that... ...stating that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Adorn your gatherings with the remembrance of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).' Decorate your gatherings, your assemblies, with the remembrance of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Under this very title and with this very purpose, today this International Celebration of Elan-e-Wilayat has been organized, in which I, on behalf of the entire team of 'The Strong Rope', welcome all of you. By the grace of Allah, the journey of 'Faizan-e-Wilayat' which was started in the year 1440 AH has reached its completion. And the gathering that was organized under the title of 'Elan-e-Wilayat', in which two poetic lines (misra) were presented to you, and poets, reciters, and respected personalities were requested to support us in this propagation of Wilayat, so that we all together could... ...support us so that we all together could propagate the Wilayat of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), this unique Wilayat, and spread this program as much as possible across the world. For this reason, this International Celebration of Elan-e-Wilayat was organized. Today, although this celebration has reached its destination, the propagation of Wilayat will never end. We pray to the Lord of the worlds that until the Day of Judgment, as long as we breathe, the remembrance of Ali remains on our tongues, because after all, this is the propagation of Wilayat whose command was given to us by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the field of Ghadir. chapters.title: Introduction to the International Elan-e-Wilayat Celebration
chapters.summary: The event organizers welcome participants to the International Celebration of Elan-e-Wilayat, highlighting the importance of propagating the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

chapters.title: Poetry Contest and Scholarly Insights
chapters.summary: The program features a poetry competition regarding the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and introduces Maulana Mohsin to deliver a lecture on the significance of this divine leadership.

chapters.title: The Essence of Love and Obedience to Allah
chapters.summary: Maulana Mohsin discusses the Quranic requirement of following the Prophet to attain Allah's love and defines the importance of rejoicing in the Greatest Eid (Eid-e-Akbar).

chapters.title: The Foundation of Wilayah and the Best of Deeds
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is the core of faith, referencing the historical significance of the proclamation at Ghadir and the meaning of 'Hayya 'ala khayril 'amal'.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ghadir and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker draws a parallel between the congregational prayer standing order and the declaration of Imam Ali's leadership at Ghadir Khumm.

chapters.title: The Meaning of Khatam and Divine Appointment
chapters.summary: An explanation of the term 'Khatam' as a seal and its symbolic connection to the finality of the Prophet's mission and the appointment of Ali.

chapters.title: Poetry Competition and Evaluation Criteria
chapters.summary: The organizers introduce the judges and explain the criteria for evaluating the Qasida submissions for the Jashn-e-Wilayah event.

chapters.title: Historical Impact of Ghadir
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the enduring historical significance of Ghadir and the joy it brings to believers, leading into the announcement of the competition results.

chapters.title: Literary Standards in Religious Poetry
chapters.summary: The discussion highlights the importance of maintaining literary quality, historical accuracy, and proper technique in Nohas and religious poetry, cautioning against the dilution of these art forms by untrained individuals.

chapters.title: Technical Components of Qasida and Marsiya
chapters.summary: The speakers define the structural components of a Qasida, such as Tashbeeb, Gureiz, and Madah, while distinguishing them from other genres like Marsiya, Salam, and Qita.

chapters.title: Evolution and Purpose of Salam and Noha
chapters.summary: This section explores the transition of Salam from an introductory piece to a medium for grief, and defines the essential characteristics of a Noha as a form of lamentation that balances praise and sorrow.

chapters.title: The Art of Gureiz and Proper Praise
chapters.summary: The discussion focuses on the necessity of maintaining artistic integrity in Qasidas, specifically emphasizing the role of Gureiz as a graceful transition to the praise of the Mamdooh, while rejecting vulgar or irrelevant content.

chapters.summary: The speaker explains the importance of the Tashbeeb (prelude) and Gurez (transition) in a Qasida, emphasizing that they should be used to build a logical and emotional connection to the praise of the Imam.

chapters.title: Composition and Flow in Manqabat
chapters.summary: The speaker demonstrates how to construct a Manqabat by linking the prelude to the praise of the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring the verses resonate with the audience.

chapters.title: Length and Meter in Modern Poetry
chapters.summary: The discussion covers the evolution of Qasida length, suggesting that modern compositions should be concise, ideally around twelve verses, while maintaining strict adherence to poetic meter.

chapters.title: Structure of Religious Qasidas
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the essential components of a Qasida, including the prelude (Tashbeeb), the transition (gurez), and the importance of concluding with supplication (dua).

chapters.title: Wilayah and Human Effort
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the beauty of destiny and Wilayah, emphasizing that while God is the Sustainer, human effort remains a necessary component of life.

chapters.title: Poetry Competition Results
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with the announcement of winners for a poetry competition, providing feedback on technical prosody and the importance of preserving the Urdu language.

chapters.title: Announcement of Competition Winners
chapters.summary: The program announces the winners of the social media engagement contest and conducts a lucky draw for participating poets.

chapters.title: Ghadir Quiz Results and Conclusion
chapters.summary: Winners of the 'Objections on Ghadir' quiz are announced, followed by concluding remarks and a transition into the mourning period for Imam Husain.

chapters.title: Observing Ayyam-e-Aza
chapters.summary: The speaker encourages viewers to maintain mourning rituals for Imam Husain at home during the upcoming Ayyam-e-Aza period.

title: Khatm -e- Qur'an aur Eesaal e Sawaab Majlis-e-Azaa | Baraaye Marhoom Abulhasan Ibne Ibnehasan Sayed
excerpt: This lecture serves as a Khatm-e-Qur'an and Eesaal-e-Sawaab for the late Abulhasan Ibne Ibnehasan Sayed, blending Quranic recitation with the theological significance of death and the afterlife in Shia Islam. The speaker explores the certainty of resurrection, the vital role of Wilayah (allegiance to the Ahlulbayt) in the grave, and the promise of salvation for those who hold fast to the love of the Prophet's household. Through the lens of Karbala and the sacrifices of figures like Hazrat Abbas (a.s.), the discourse emphasizes that true faith requires both devotion to the righteous and disassociation from their enemies.
content:
Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance and destroy their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ya-Sin. By the wise Quran. Indeed you, [O Muhammad], are from among the messengers, on a straight path. [This is a] revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware. Already the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe. Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to the chins, so they are with heads raised. And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see. And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward. Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register. And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it. When We sent to them two but they denied both, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, 'Indeed, we are messengers to you.' They said, 'You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies.' They said, 'Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you, and there is not upon us except the clear notification.' They said, 'Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment.' They said, 'Your omen is with yourselves. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people.' And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, 'O my people, follow the messengers. Follow those who do not ask of you any payment, and they are [rightly] guided. And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned? Should I take other than Him [false] deities while, if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me? Indeed, I would then be in manifest error. Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.' It was said, 'Enter Paradise.' He said, 'I wish my people could know of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored.' And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have been senders. It was but one shout, and behold, they were extinguished. Alas for the servants! There comes not to them any messenger except that they used to mock him. Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—that they will not return to them? And all of them will all be brought before Us. And a sign for them is the dead earth; We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat. And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused springs to gush forth therein, that they may eat of its fruit and what their hands have produced. Will they not then be grateful? Exalted is He who created all pairs from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know. And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs its course toward a stopping point; that is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. And the moon—We have determined for it phases, until it returns like the old date stalk. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each, in an orbit, is swimming. And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers in the laden ship. And We created for them from that which is similar, that which they ride. And if We should will, We could drown them; then no one would respond to their cry, nor would they be saved, except by mercy from Us and provision for a time. And when it is said to them, 'Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, that you may receive mercy,' [they turn away]. And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it. And when it is said to them, 'Spend from that which Allah has provided for you.' And it is said by those who disbelieve to those who believe, 'Should we feed those whom, if Allah willed, He could have fed? You are not but in clear error.' And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?' They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor will they return to their people. And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, 'O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?' [The angels will say], 'This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.' It will not be but one blast, and at once they are all brought present before Us. So today, no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do. Indeed the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be amused in [joyful] occupation - They and their spouses, in shade, reclining on adorned couches. For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they request [or wish]. [And] 'Peace,' a word from a Merciful Lord. 'But stand apart today, O criminals. Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - [for] indeed, to you he is a clear enemy - And that you worship [only] Me? This is a straight path. But he had already led astray many of you, so did you not use reason? This is the Hell, which you were promised. [Enter to] burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve.' That Day, We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn. And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to [find] the path, and how could they see? And if We willed, We could have deformed them, [paralyzing them] in their places so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return. And he whom We grant long life - We reverse him in creation; so will they not understand? And We did not give Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) knowledge of poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a message and a clear Qur'an - To give warning to whoever is alive and justify the word against the disbelievers. Do they not see that We created for them from what Our hands have made, grazing livestock, and [then] they are their owners? And We tamed them for them, so some of them they ride, and some they eat. And for them therein are [other] benefits and drinks, so will they not be grateful? But they have taken besides Allah [other] deities that perhaps they would be helped. They are not able to help them, and they [themselves] are for them soldiers in attendance. So do not let their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare. Does man not consider that We created him from a [mere] sperm-drop - then at once he is a clear adversary? And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, 'Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?' Say, 'He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.' [It is] He who made for you from the green tree, fire, and then from it you ignite. Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them? Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator. His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is. So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned. Sadaqallahul Aliyyul Azeem. Innallaha wa malaikatahu yusalluna alan-nabi, ya ayyuhalladhina amanu sallu alaihi wa sallimu taslima. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Ashfa'een. The Azadari of the oppressed Imam of Karbala. That we are sitting in this court today. For the Majlis of our brother Abul Hasan's Salimun. And surely... it is hard to believe that just a few days ago, in the gathering of Ghadir, our brother Abul Hasan was with us. Right here. And now, he is performing Azadari with the Mawla. And when his funeral rites were being performed, I want to tell you that when his children were standing there, people were placing hands of compassion on them, whether it was his son or his daughter. And there is another daughter found in history, whose father passed away and that daughter received nothing but slaps. No one offered her consolation. And these tears and this condolence have reached the court of the Imam for brother Abul Hasan, and may he receive the reward for it. Think of Zahra (s.a.). Sakina (s.a.) was persecuted. Sakina (s.a.) was made to weep at every step. Oh, that wound is still fresh today. From the back of the camel—alas, she did not fall; she was made to fall, Sakina (s.a.). Sakina (s.a.) would cry out from the prison, 'My ribs are broken just like my grandmother's. Oh father, how they made me fall while walking, my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's. Oh, Sakina (s.a.) has become like Zahra (s.a.) at only four years of age, my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's. Oh, she kept hiding her side from her grandfather, I too cannot bear to see Ali's (a.s.) tears, I too cannot bear to see Ali's (a.s.) tears. Oh, while alive, I did not let anyone see my wound, brother, my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's.' O Azadars, listen to the scene of the Day of Judgment. 'Oh, how I have come after passing through the bazaar, father, they threw stones at this wound of mine, father. I kept crying, yet no one listened, my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's. Alas, now I can understand how she must have slept, how she must have writhed in pain while keeping her hand on her side. I too cannot even turn due to the pain, my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's.' And the lady who is made to walk for 1000 miles until the evening under the soles of feet, her condition becomes such that: 'Exactly like Fatima Zahra (s.a.), old age descended, wrinkles appeared on the face, and whiteness in the hair.' One deficiency remained, and that too was fulfilled, father; my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's. Alas, she fell to the dust, neither beating her face nor her chest, another calamity occurred in the prison, Akbar. Oh, taking the father's head, the little girl said while weeping, 'My ribs are broken just like my grandmother's. Oh father, how they made me fall while walking, my ribs are broken just like my grandmother's.' Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. It is good, Sughra, it is good, Sughra, it is good, Sughra, that you were not with me. Zainab's (s.a.) lament was, 'We were looted, Sughra, it is good, Sughra, that you were not with me.' I offer a prostration of gratitude for this, that at least someone's veil among us remained intact. And how should I tell you how my heart is bursting? Oh, the honor of the Sadaat did not demand it, Sughra. I only say this much, everyone's veil was snatched; it is good, Sughra, that you were not with me. It is good, Sughra, that you were not with me. You ask why this shawl of yours is red; come, let me tell you, daughter of my oppressed one. When the corpse of Ali Akbar (a.s.) was in the tent, I fell beside the corpse, writhing in pain. This shawl became red with Akbar's blood; it is good, Sughra, that you were not with me. Bi-Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad, recite a loud Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. This is just a condolence poem: Why should the world not shed tears over their separation? Abul Hasan is dear to the people of the heart, and Abul Hasan reached Paradise to perform Ashura with Zahra (s.a.), Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), Ali (a.s.), and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The wound of the heart will remain fresh, Abul Hasan. How can one bear the shock of separation, Abul Hasan? And why should we not mourn your grief? Your name was in every deed, Abul Hasan. As long as we live, we will keep mentioning you. Your character was such, Abul Hasan, that as long as this series of 18 Majalis lasts, your mention will remain fresh, Abul Hasan. And it is a truth that if there is no mention of the King of Karbala, then when is there a remedy for your grief, Abul Hasan? That even in the calamities of the world, with what dignity you used to mention Fatima Zahra (s.a.), Abul Hasan. And the reference of 18 Majalis will be enough for your intercession, Abul Hasan, and where will we find a dear friend like you who supports us in joy and sorrow, Abul Hasan? He emerged from the dust and settled in our hearts, Abul Hasan is alive among us. With a loud voice, Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Nara-e-Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Rahim Allah man qara'a al-Fatiha. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil adheem. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man nasir. Alhamdulillahir Rabbil Alamin, wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqin, wal yaqin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashrafil ambiya'i wal mursalin, habibi ilahil alamin, Abil Qasimi Muhammad. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi al-ma'sumin, alladhina adh-haba Allahu 'anhumur-rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum, siyyama Baqiyatillahi fil ardi, Imam-e-Zamanina wa waliyyi amrina wa sahibina wa mawlana wa habibina wa tabibina wa anisina wa munisina, al-kahfil hasin wa ghiyathil mudtarril mustaqim, ruhu wa arwahul 'alamina lahul fida. Amma ba'd, faqad qala mawlana wa sayyiduna Ja'far ibn Muhammad alayhimus-salam: 'Lam yakhluqillahu 'azza wa jalla yaqinan la shakka fihi ashbaha bi-shakkin la yaqina fihi minal mawt.' Sadaqa mawlana Ja'far ibn Muhammad alayhimus-salam. Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Before starting the Majlis, I request you all to recite one Surah Fatiha and three times Qul Huwallahu Ahad and gift it to the soul of the late Abul Hasan ibn Sayyid Hasan. Recite one more Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in this Hadith, which I have made the title of this Majlis, says: 'Allah has not created any such certain thing in which there is no doubt, that resembles a doubt in which there is no certainty, more than death.' That is, this is a thing that is so certain that no one can deny it. But the attitude of every human being towards it is as if it is not for us, but for others. And that is why we are urged to remember death as much as possible. There are many narrations; I do not have to read all the narrations now. Recite one Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. 'Akyasul naas man ashadda zikral lil maut' (The smartest person is the one who remembers death the most). 'Aksaru zikra hadimul lazzat' (Remember the destroyer of pleasures often). There are many traditions regarding the remembrance of death, but the Shia's relationship with death is different compared to others. That is why Allama Majlisi (R.A.), in the seventh volume of Bihar al-Anwar—or perhaps the sixth—has a chapter titled 'Bab Hubb Liqa Allah' (The Chapter of Love for Meeting Allah). This chapter is about the love of death and the condemnation of fleeing from it. It is a strange relationship. Before we proceed, let us look at the context to make it clear. Harith Hamdani, a great lover of Maula Ali (a.s.), became severely ill—to the point where his death was imminent. Maula Ali (a.s.) went to visit him. Allahu Akbar, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is going to visit the sick. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Now Harith Hamdani began to list his troubles to Maula. He spoke of his worries, his great troubles, and said, 'I have reached this stage, and now death is standing before me.' Maula (a.s.) said, 'Why are you mentioning death? You still have to live.' The hadith is long, but Himyari presented it in the form of a poem, which is easier to recite. In the poem, it is said that Maula (a.s.) replied, 'O Harith Hamdani, man yamut yarani, min muminin au munafiqin qubla' (O Harith Hamdani, whoever dies will see me, whether they are a believer or a hypocrite, before they die). 'Wa ana arifuhu bi ismihi wa na'tihi wa ma amila' (And I will recognize them by their name, their attributes, and their deeds). Now, there is a question here. Harith is in front of Maula, he is looking at Maula. Are you paying attention? Harith is looking at Maula. Maula has come to visit him, and Harith is talking about death, saying he is about to die. And Maula is saying, 'Harith, do not worry. When you die, you will see me.' Is this a conversation? He is seeing him face-to-face right now, and Maula is talking about after death? Harith should have said this, but it is not found in the tradition. The tradition says that as soon as Harith heard this, he became very happy. Why? To understand this, one must read the Quran. Read the Quran, Surah Qaf, verse 22: 'Laqad kunta fi ghaflatin min haza, fakashafna anka ghita'aka fabasarukal yauma hadid' (You were heedless of this, so We have removed your veil, and your sight today is sharp). Until now, you were in the world, and because of the veils of the world, you were in heedlessness. Now that death has come, 'We have removed your veil,' and 'your sight today is sharp.' Meaning, Maula is saying, 'Harith, the manifestation that I will have then...' Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Subhan Allah! That will be a different manifestation. Until now, you were seeing Ali ibn Abi Talib through the veils of the world. Now, when these veils are removed, you will see. That is the 'Ma'rifat bin Nuraniya' (Knowledge through Light) in which Salman and Abu Dharr were astonished in this world. Salman and Abu Dharr went and asked, 'Maula, what is your Ma'rifat bin Nuraniya?' First, Abu Dharr asked Salman, and Salman said, 'I do not know either, let us go and ask Maula.' So they both went. Think about it, these are not ordinary men. Salman is at the tenth level of faith, Abu Dharr at the ninth. They are 'Min Ahlulbayt' (from the Household). When they asked, 'Maula, what is your Ma'rifat bin Nuraniya?', Maula (a.s.) said—the hadith is long, but he said the first sentence: 'Ya Salmanu ya Jundab, ma'rifati bin nuraniyati ma'rifatullah' (O Salman, O Jundab, my knowledge through light is the knowledge of Allah). Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! 'Wa ma'rifatullahi, ma'rifati bin nuraniya' (And the knowledge of Allah is my knowledge through light). This is the first sentence of the Hadith al-Nuraniya, which Allama Majlisi recorded in the 26th volume of Bihar al-Anwar. It is the first hadith. So, the connection a Shia has with death is a different kind of relationship. A Shia is never afraid of death. As Sibte Jafar says, 'Death does not come to his lovers; even if it comes, it does not leave without them.' And this is a fact. It is not just a poet's imagination; it is a tradition. It is clear. This is not just Sibte Jafar's thought; it is the truth. Now, let me read a few traditions to you about where this love and connection will be useful, because if I am feeling anyone's presence, it is Abu al-Hasan's. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, narrating from his ancestors, that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Hubbi wa hubbu Ahlulbayti nafi'un fi sab'ati mawaatin' (My love and the love of my Ahlulbayt will be useful in seven places). 'Fi sab'ati mawaatin' (In seven places). What are those seven places? The Prophet says, 'Ahwalu hunna azima' (Their terrors are great). These are seven stations where the terror is immense. But for the one who has the love of Muhammad and Aali Muhammad in their heart, there is no fear at all. The first one is 'Indal wafaat' (At the time of death), when the Angel of Death comes to take the soul. Intercession. Just the arrival of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is enough. It is over. A great Ayatollah saw in a dream—or rather, his son saw him in a dream—and asked, 'How was your journey of death?' He said, 'It was very difficult. But there was a person next to me who was not educated at all. He was buried in Karbala, and his state was very good. When the angels went to him, they asked him questions in the grave, and he kept saying, "Wallahi la arifu, la arifu illa sahib hazil qubba" (By God, I know nothing except the Master of this Dome). I do not know anything else, ask Imam Hussain (a.s.). I only know him.' Then they said, 'This is the best answer.' This is the best answer. So when the angels asked him, he said, 'La arifu illa sahib hazil qubba.' Even though he was a great scholar, he realized at that moment that nothing would be useful except the knowledge of the Master of this Dome. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Subhan Allah! 'I only know him, nothing else.' 'Indal wafaat' (At the time of death), 'Wa fil qabr' (And in the grave). Regarding the grave, what do you read in Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali? 'Fama li la abki' (Why should I not weep?). 'Abki li khuruji nafsi' (I weep for the time my soul is taken from my body). 'Abki li diqi lahdi' (I weep for the narrowness of my grave). 'Abki li wahshati qabri' (I weep for the loneliness of my grave). 'Abki li su'ali' (I weep for the questioning). Munkar and Nakir... I weep for the pressure of the grave, the loneliness of the grave, and the questioning of Munkar and Nakir. It is very dangerous, but the intercession you are carrying—the love of Muhammad and Aali Muhammad—we will read the hadith for you. I am just reading quickly. I am only saying that you should connect yourself to this door as much as possible, because this is the only thing that will be useful. Nothing else will be of any use. If we think our skills or our deeds will help, they will not be as useful as this love. And then the grave, and 'Inda nushur' (At the time of resurrection). The Prophet says 'Nushur'—the state of rising. The second station. The first will be the gathering (Hashr), the second will be the resurrection (Nushur). This is the third station; the first is the rising from the grave. There will be a station (mawqif) lasting 1000 years. That is, out of 1000 years, a person will sit in their grave for 500 years. They will remain in a sitting position for 500 years and then rise from the grave after 500 years. Such fear will overwhelm them, and then the second station will be the 'Nash' (resurrection). People will emerge from their graves and run here and there; this 'Nash' is the second stage. And then the third will be the 'Hashr' (gathering), where angels will gather everyone in the field of Qiyamah. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that when you are taken out of the grave and people are running here and there, the one who is a Shia of Muhammad and Ale Muhammad will be completely at peace. Completely at peace. There will be no need to run anywhere at all. Is this clear? We usually give this example to the youth just to explain the point: suppose a situation arises where, for instance, there is a raid somewhere, and the police or whoever comes and starts a lathi charge, and the main police officer turns out to be someone you know. So, how at ease you remain! He is even talking to you with a smile. Now, others are being lathi-charged, but he is talking to you with a smile. You understand, right? So, there will be a severe lathi charge on them. But anyway, that is for another time, and its mention is at the time of 'Nashur' (resurrection), and at the time of the 'Kitab' (book of deeds) when the record of deeds is presented, and at the time of 'Hisab' (reckoning) when the account is taken, and at the time of 'Mizan' (the scale) when deeds are weighed. These are all very difficult stages. Each stage lasts a thousand years. There are 50 stations of Qiyamah. A person has to stay in Qiyamah for 50,000 years. 50,000 years. One of the stations is 'Mizan-ul-A'mal' (the scale of deeds) when deeds are weighed. But you recite in the Ziyarat, 'Assalamu alayka ya Mizan-ul-A'mal.' So, when you are regularly reciting this Ziyarat here, when you reach the Mizan, it will say, 'Oh, you used to greet me regularly, come this way.' And it is found in the traditions, God willing, we will read the Hadith if there is time. In short, as soon as the love of Ale Muhammad is placed on the scale, it will be so high—meaning this side will be so heavy—and the other side, the sins, will go so high up, with a distance like that between the sky and the earth. It will be so heavy. God willing, we will read the Hadith for you. And at the 'Sirat' (the bridge), and you know the Sirat: 'Ahaddum minas-sayf wa adaqqu minash-sha'ar' (sharper than a sword and thinner than a hair). But if the love of Ale Muhammad is in the heart, one will pass with great ease. What is the phrase in the tradition? Like someone riding on Buraq, they will pass through. Very fast, instantly. They will reach the Hawdh (the Pond) immediately. Nothing happened; in a single moment. And some whose Wilayah is weak, who have many questions but still have Wilayah, they will crawl across; there will be some trouble, this will happen, but they are Shias, just a little less. And those who used to say, 'What is this, why do you say Ali, Ali, Ali in everything? What are you doing like the Punjabis?' So, anyway, all these things... this is a prayer of the Mawla of the universe, you know. It is a prayer of the Mawla of the universe. Listen to this tradition; this is recorded in 'Ta'wil al-Ayat al-Zahira' by Sayyid Abul Hasan Astarabadi. And this tradition is strange. It is from Harith al-Hamdani. He says: 'Dakhaltu ala Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) wa huwa sajidun yabki' (I entered upon Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) while he was in prostration and weeping). 'Hatta ala najibuhu wa irtafa sawtuhu bil buka' (Until his shoulders shook and his voice rose with weeping). He was weeping loudly, the Mawla's voice was raised as he wept. We asked, 'Ya Amirul Momineen, we are becoming ill seeing your weeping. We are troubled that you are weeping like this. We have never seen you do this, we have never seen you act like this before, not in all these days.' The Mawla replied, 'I was in prostration.' I was supplicating to my Lord with a prayer of goodness in my prostration. Then my eyes closed. I saw a dream that was very terrifying. And it frightened me. I saw the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—send blessings upon him and his family—standing, and he was saying, 'Ya Abul Hasan, your absence from me has been long.' Since the martyrdom of the Prophet was in 11 Hijri, and this incident is in Kufa, it had been about 30 years. 'I am longing to see you. And my Lord has fulfilled what He promised me regarding you.' This is what the Prophet is saying to Amirul Momineen (a.s.). I asked, 'Ya Rasulullah, what were the promises that Allah fulfilled regarding me?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'He fulfilled regarding you, your wife, your two sons, and your progeny, that you will be with me in the highest degree in Illiyin.' Allah promised that you, your wife, your two sons, and your progeny will all be with me in the highest degree of Paradise, in Illiyin. 'With me.' This was Allah's promise, and Allah said this promise is firm. I said—the Mawla says I asked in front of the Messenger of Allah—'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, Ya Rasulullah, what about our Shias? We are in Illiyin, but what about our Shias?' He said (s.a.w.a.), 'Our Shias will be with us.' Allah, our Shias will be with us. Their palaces will be in front of our palaces. They will be facing them. And their dwellings will be opposite our dwellings. Subhan Allah. I said, 'Ya Rasulullah, what is for our Shias in this world?' He said (s.a.w.a.), 'Security and well-being.' Meaning they will remain firm on their religion, on their belief. Even if the world turns upside down, the Shias will remain very firm. Wow! They will remain in security and well-being; nothing will happen to their belief. Wow! The world will shake, the world's belief will waver, but our Shias will remain in security and well-being. I said, 'And what about them at the time of death, Ya Rasulullah?' He said (s.a.w.a.)—it is a strange sentence, listen carefully, it is a strange sentence—the Prophet says, 'The man will be the judge of his own soul.' Wow! Whatever he wants, that is how he will die. 'And the Angel of Death will be commanded to obey him.' Wow! Once, Haydari! Ya Ali! 'And in whatever state of death he wishes, he will die.' It is not your choice; it is the Shia's choice. Wow! May Allah have mercy on the one who knows his own worth. Know your own worth. Know your own worth. 'And our Shias,' the Prophet says, 'will not die except according to the extent of their love for us.' Wow! The more love they have, the more peaceful their death will be. Wow! Now we will stop the Hadith here. Now we will tell you what Dr. Abbas Wakeel said. You know Dr. Abbas Wakeel; he is about 59 years old. His life has been spent in this field. It has been more than 30 years, right? More than 30 years. He has been a doctor since '87. You can calculate, 35 years, 36 years he has been practicing. Now, after seeing him, he said, 'My life has passed, I have never seen a patient on a ventilator sleeping with such peace until today.' Those who are put on a ventilator, they have an uneasiness. The one I saw, he was sleeping so peacefully, there was nothing to it. These are the words of Dr. Abbas Wakeel. If you want, you can ask him. You might have his number, if not, take it from us. He was completely at peace. And very comfortable. When we saw him ourselves, we were also surprised at how he was lying there so peacefully. Completely at ease, as if there was nothing. We felt like he might just get up and sit down. That was his condition; it didn't even look like this man was a brain hemorrhage patient. Whose reports showed that all the veins in the back of the brain were completely damaged. They were completely ruptured. But he was completely at peace, completely calm. The incident is strange. But we are not saying this from ourselves; you ask him, ask him, he is a doctor. He is saying, 'I have never seen it until today. I have never seen it.' Anyway. 'They will not die except according to the extent of their love for us.' I asked, 'So how is this limit known?' The Mawla is asking the Messenger of Allah; in reality, such Hadiths are called 'Masri' (hidden/symbolic). 'Masri' means the Mawla knows everything, but this is being stated to explain it to some people. So the Mawla asked, 'So how is this limit recognized, what is his level, what is it?' So the Prophet says, 'Yes, the Shia who is most intense in our love, who is deeply drowned in our love, when his soul is taken out, when the Angel of Death takes it out, how will it be? Like one of you drinking cold water on a hot summer day, how much pleasure does he get? In the same way, when the Angel of Death is taking his soul, he will be feeling pleasure.' Wow! He will feel that pleasure. That pain, that suffering, nothing. Rather, he will feel pleasure, and the Angel... in another Hadith, not this one, but another, it is said that the Angel of Death will hold his soul with great respect and take it... They will be taken in silk, in silk garments, just as a bride is taken. Wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah. To this extent, whatever you see, just remain attached to this door, stay connected to it, stick to it. Keep saying 'Ali Ali'. Love, Wilayah, Bara'ah. Get drowned in it. This is the only thing that will be of use. Look, worldly life has no value, I submit to your service. It has no value. It is here today and gone tomorrow. Today we are talking to you, it is possible that after 5 minutes we might not be here. There is no guarantee for anyone. There is no guarantee for anyone. The only thing that will be of use is this. And some fools—I am choosing my words very carefully, thinking very thoughtfully—with full responsibility, I say: no fool should ever be proud of their worship. Wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah. We are not saying do not worship, no, certainly worship is obligatory, whatever Allah's command is. But what are we and what is our worship? Wah, wah, wah. The only thing that matters is this love. 'La arifu illa sahib hazil qubba' (I do not know anyone except the one in this dome, I only recognize him, I do not recognize anyone else besides him). 'Allazi yantafiu minhul qalb' (When he drinks cold water on a hot day, how his heart finds peace, how he likes it, that is how it is at the time of death). 'Wa in sa'erahum' (And the rest of them, the Shias who will be lower in rank, their level will be lower). 'La yamutu kama yamutu ahadukum ala firashihi' (They do not die as one of you dies on his bed). 'Ka akrama kana aynahu bimautihi' (The other Shias will have lower ranks, but for them too, how will death be? Just like turning over on one's side. Just turning over on the bed, and it is done, yes, it is finished like that. No pain, no trouble, Insha'Allah, nothing. Just keep one thing in the heart: keep the thought of Wilayah and Bara'ah. Do not separate from this. Subhan Allah. If, God forbid, God forbid, God forbid, it should not happen that if Bara'ah is happening or Tabarra is being done, we make a face, 'What is happening?' And call the enemies of Amir al-Mu'minin with respect. Countless. It is clear for you. 'Ka akrama kana aynahu bimautihi'. It is clear for you. Very, very calmly. Just get drowned in Wilayah. Completely, Wilayah and Bara'ah. These two things. Now, I present another Hadith for your service. Look, it is a strange and wonderful Hadith. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. This Hadith is from the Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Look, just as there was the Tafsir of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, likewise there is the Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). The subject of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi's Tafsir was Raj'ah. You will find many Hadiths about Raj'ah in it. Meaning, the Tafsir was completely destroyed, later the scholars collected it. All the Hadiths from Jabir ibn Yazid. And after that, this Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), its subject is Bara'ah and Wilayah. Wah, wah, wah. You did not notice. I said Bara'ah first. Wah, wah, wah, wah, wah. Bara'ah and Wilayah. Wah, wah, wah. Because when you recite the Kalima, you say 'La ilaha illallah'. After that, you say 'illallah'. Wah, wah, wah. Now we habitually say 'Tawalla Tabarra'. It is a different thing. But 'La yuqbalul wilayatu illa bil bara'ah, illa bil bara'ah' (Wilayah is not accepted except with Bara'ah, except with Bara'ah). First Bara'ah, then Wilayah. The rest are all things to be said, just to be said. Right? So, the main subject of this Tafsir is Bara'ah and Wilayah. You read it. Actually, this Tafsir was in 120 volumes. And for 7 years, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) was dictating it, for 7 years. Now, what we have left is only one volume. A small one. Nothing else. Everything was destroyed. But anyway, its subject is this. You can check it. If you read the Hadith in it now, you will be amazed after hearing the Hadith. I do not have to read it, but now I will read a small one. Just a four-word one. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. It is said that the Imam says, 'Sawabussalat, la azuma sawabussalat, la azuma'. You know 'azuma', right? 'Azuma' means 'azim' (great). 'Sawabussalat' (the reward of prayer). 'Lil musalli fi salatihi' (for the one praying in his prayer). You know Arabic, right? The reward of the one praying in prayer will be exactly that, meaning directly proportionate to how much, how much he mentions the excellence of Muhammad and Ali. Wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Wah, wah. These are traditions, you can check. If anyone wants the reference, I can show it. It is in the Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and it is properly narrated. Anyway, there are many traditions, but this tradition here is strange and wonderful that 'Inna Allaha yab'athu yawmal qiyamati aqwaman' (Allah will raise some Shias from the grave on the Day of Judgment). 'Yamtal'u min jihatis sayyi'ati wa mawazinuhum' (Their record of deeds, the scales that will be given, the side will be filled with sins). 'Yam tali' means filled. It will be filled. 'Fayuqalu lahum' (Then the angels will say to them), 'Hazihi sayyi'at' (These are all your sins). 'Fa aynal hasanat?' (Where are your good deeds?). Look, that is why I tell you one thing before moving forward, I am saying a very important thing. That even if a lover of Ali, even if he is a sinner, still you should respect him if he loves Ali in the end. Because you do not know when a turn might come in his life that he repents for his sins and all his sins are forgiven. He might do one small deed and all his sins are forgiven, and we who were proud of our religion, our worship, and our piety—those will all go away. It turns out nothing is of use. Why? He did one small deed such that its result was this. Anyway, so it will be asked, 'Aynal hasanat?' (Where are the good deeds?). 'Wa illa faqad asaytum' (Otherwise you have only committed sins). 'Fayaquluna' (These Shias will say), 'Ya Rabbana ma na'rifu lana hasanat' (O our Lord, we do not remember any good deeds, meaning we did not do good deeds in life). Meaning, worship, piety—all this is nothing. 'Fa iza nida'un min qibillahi' (Then a call from Allah). Look, I am reading the Hadith for you. If anyone has a doubt, I will give the reference. Yes? Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 7, Page 248, Hadith number 1; Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), Page number 139. Look, I even gave you the reference, yes? So that no one says I am reading from my own side, yes? And if anyone doubts whether the Hadith is weak or what, then they can go to a doctor, no problem. Recite one more Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. 'Fa iza nida'un min qibillahi azza wa jalla' (Then a call will come from Allah, directly Allah). Here the angels are asking, 'Where are the good deeds? Yes, only committed sins.' The voice will come from the Boss. It will come from above. 'La'illam ta'arifu li-anfusikum ibadil hasanat' (Are you not finding good deeds for yourselves? No). Allah will say, 'Okay. Fa-inni arifuha lakum' (Then I know them for you). 'Wa uwwafiru alaykum' (And I will fill your entire Mizan, the scale, with these good deeds). 'Uwwafiru' (I will fill it, completely fill it). 'Summa ya'ti bi-sahifatin saghiratin' (Then a small scroll will be brought). A small paper which 'saghiratun yatrawu fi kaffati hasanatihim' (which will be placed in the scale of their good deeds). The one that was empty, the scale of good deeds. That was the one above, this scale of sins was all the way down. The angels will bring it and put it in there. 'Take this small paper, brother. Yes. Okay, right?'. What will happen? 'Fa-turajjihu bi-sayyi'atihim' (Immediately this scale will come down and the sins will go up so much that the sentence of the Hadith is) 'bi-aksara mimma baynas sama'i wal ard' (more than what is between the heaven and the earth). This one small paper, and sins of a lifetime. Evils, whatever they are. 'Fa-qalu li-ahadihim' (And then it will be said to each of them), 'Khuz bi-yadi abika wa ummika wa ikhwanika wa akhwatika wa khassatika wa qarabatika wa akhnadika wa ma'arifika'. Take everyone by the hand. Mother, father, brother, sister, special people of yours, relatives, servants, acquaintances, friends, loved ones, take everyone and 'fa-adkhilhumul jannah' (enter them all into Paradise). Is it clear? Now here some fools, those fools, ask, 'Oh, they are selling Paradise, distributing Paradise.' We are not distributing it, the Messenger of Allah is distributing it. 'Hay re Ali!' And believe me, whoever objects to these Hadiths, on the Day of Judgment, he will keep looking with regret. That, 'If only this paper had been placed in my scale too.' 'Fayaqulu ahlul mahshar' (The people of the gathering will say), 'Ya Rabba, amma zunubu faqad arafnaha' (O Lord, we know his sins, he was a great sinner, O Creator). 'Famadha kanat hasanatuhum?' (What good deed did he do that this happened?). 'Fayaqulu Allahu azza wa jalla, ya ibadi' (Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say, 'O My servants, these people did this work that a Shia was in debt, was in debt. So one of them said to this Shia, 'Whatever I have, you take it.' For what? 'Bi-hubbi Ali ibn Abi Talib' (For the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib). Whatever I have, you take it. And the other one from whom he had taken the loan, he will say, 'Taraktuha laka' (I have forgiven the debt). 'Bi-hubbika Aliyan' (Because you love Ali, therefore I have forgiven it). 'Wa laka min mali ma shi'ta' (And from my wealth, whatever you want, take it. I gave you a loan, and if you want more, take more). 'Fa-shakara Allahu ta'ala dhalika lahuma' (Allah will reward them for that, how? 'Fa-hatta bihima khatayahuma' (He will forgive all their sins). 'Wa ja'ala dhalika fi hashwi sahifatihima wa mawazinihima' (And in their record of deeds and in their weight, in the Mizan, all the good deeds). 'Wa awjaba lahuma wa li-walidayhima al-jannah' (For them, for their parents, for everyone, Paradise). Everyone in Paradise. Only for this good deed. Here one example of a loan has been given. In this Hadith, one example. Any thing, you have helped a Shia in any way, from any perspective, for him... Why only favor? Love for Ali ibn Abi Talib. He loves Ali ibn Abi Talib. He holds enmity towards his enemies. Yes, that is enough. Okay, let it be, that's fine. It doesn't matter. But these two things are necessary, yes. Not just one. If only love were enough, then those who fill the water skins (for the thirsty) would have had a lot of trouble with that. Subhan Allah. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Buraydah.' O Buraydah, when did the Messenger state this hadith? When Buraydah came to the Messenger of Allah with a complaint about the Master of the Universe (Ali). At that time, the Prophet said to Buraydah: 'Yadkhulu an-nara bi-bughdi Aliyyin aktharu mimma hasala al-khadfu alladhi yurma 'inda al-jamarat' (Those who will enter Hell due to hatred of Ali are more numerous than the pebbles thrown at the Jamarat). There are many who are good, but they harbor hatred for Ali. There is malice in the heart. There is hatred and enmity towards Ali ibn Abi Talib. There is malice in the heart. That is why, look, they are celebrating in Muharram. Why are they celebrating? They are saying 'Happy New Year.' In reality, it is not 'Happy New Year.' They are happy because Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred. There is no other reason. This is the reason. 'Fa-iyyaka an takuna minhum' (So beware of being among them). O Buraydah, look, never be among these people. Never be among these people. This is the message of today's gathering: Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib and Bara'ah (disassociation from his enemies). This is a gathering for the Isal-e-Sawab (transfer of merit) of a believer, a lover, and an Azadari (mourner) who truly loved the Ahlulbayt. You all often know him better than we do. And our acquaintance with him in the last four or five years was only that much. But the one thing we saw, and you must have seen it too, is that he had great devotion to Hazrat Abbas (a.s.). He had great devotion. And that is why he used to sweep outside the shrine of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.). That is, the opportunity to serve. When he went for Ziyarat. He used to go for Ziyarat. Service. This is a very great thing. It is not strange that Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) might have come to welcome him. Because the family of Muhammad (a.s.) does not keep anyone's debt unpaid. The principle of the household of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad is that they do not keep anyone's debt. They give more than what anyone does. That is why I presented the hadith for your service. Whoever does more, gets more. And Abbas is that personality about whom what can be said? Just read the phrases of Ziyarat and you will attain Ma'rifat (gnosis). 'A'immati ma'sumina 'alayhimu as-salam' have sent blessings upon him. Just think, what a status, what a position. This is that Abbas. On the day of Ashura, he is continuously asking for permission, but the Imam is not giving permission. 'You are the standard-bearer of my army.' Abbas said, 'Where is that army left for me to lead?' Abbas, if you want to go, then go. Bring water for the children. The children are thirsty. That was all that was needed; he came to the door of the tent and called out, 'Sakina, my daughter, bring the water skin.' Sakina asked, 'Uncle, what will you do with the water skin?' He said, 'The Master has ordered me to bring water for the children. So bring your water skin.' Now, it is written in the Maqtal (chronicle of martyrdom) that when Sakina went with the water skin, the children followed her and were asking, 'Bibi, what is this water skin for? Where are you taking it?' She said, 'Father has ordered Uncle to bring water. Now my uncle will bring water. Children, now be assured that if my uncle goes, he will definitely bring water.' Now Abbas left and went, mounted his horse, and went to the bank of the Euphrates, pushing back the armies. The armies began to flee here and there. Seeing Abbas, such awe was cast that the armies began to flee here and there. Abbas put his horse into the Euphrates. He dismounted, and after dismounting, he took a little water in his cupped hands, just to tell them, 'O oppressors, do not consider me helpless.' I am just not drinking the water. It is because the children are thirsty. The ladies are thirsty. Saying this, Abbas filled the water skin, and after filling it, Abbas walked with the water skin. How does he walk? In one hand is the standard, in the other is the water skin. As he walks, a wretch struck such a blow that his right hand was severed. Abbas still recited Rajaz (heroic poetry) that even if you have severed my right hand, I will still continue to support my Imam. Then another struck a second blow. Abbas's second hand was severed, the left hand was severed. Abbas held the water skin in his mouth, held it with his teeth. Now, holding it with his teeth, Abbas is moving rapidly towards the tents when suddenly a wretch struck such an arrow of oppression that it hit the water skin. The water fell. Now, the falling of the water... Abbas bowed his head. 'What will I do when I go to the tent? What face will I show Sakina now? What face will I show the children now?' Just as Abbas bowed his head, it is written in the Maqtal that a wretch struck him from behind with a mace. Such a mace that Abbas fell from the back of his horse to the ground. Mourners, when someone falls from a height, naturally they put their hands forward. Abbas had no hands. He fell face-first. He called out, 'Master!' As soon as the voice reached Hussain's ears, Hussain went towards the Maqtal of the Euphrates and began to recite a dirge: 'Al-ana inkasara zahri' (Now my back is broken). 'Al-ana inkasara zahri wa qallat hilati' (Now my back is broken and my stratagem has diminished). 'Wa shamata bi 'aduwwi' (And my enemy is mocking me). Abbas, the enemy is mocking me. The enemy is laughing. Your standard-bearer has been killed. Hussain came to Abbas. He placed his head on his lap. There was some conversation between the brothers. Just once, Abbas gave some advice. One of them was, 'Do not take my corpse to the tent.' Now I do not know the reason for that. One reason could be that the Imam would not be able to lift Abbas's corpse, and the other reason was, 'How can I show my face to Sakina? I am very ashamed.' While giving his last will, Abbas's eyes closed once. Hussain recited a dirge, 'Abbas, the eyes that used to sleep, now they will wake, and those that used to wake out of fear for you, now they will sleep in peace. Abbas. Alas, Abbas.' 'Sa-ya'lamu alladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun' (And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned). 'Ala la'natu Allahi 'ala al-qawmi az-zalimin' (The curse of Allah be upon the oppressive people). O Sustainer. O Sustainer. Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Protect the scholars of the world and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Whoever protects them, protect them. O Sustainer, bless us with the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Recite one Surah Al-Fatiha and three times Qul Huwallahu Ahad and dedicate it to the deceased. Shukr kiya Hussain, Shukr kiya Hussain.
