chapters.title: Recitation of Surah Ya-Sin
chapters.summary: The speaker recites Surah Ya-Sin, emphasizing the message of the prophets, the signs of Allah in creation, and the reality of the afterlife.

chapters.title: Commemoration and Azadari
chapters.summary: The speaker transitions to a memorial for the deceased brother, Abul Hasan, connecting his passing to the broader tradition of Azadari.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Sakina (s.a.)
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with a heart-wrenching account of the suffering of Sakina (s.a.) after the tragedy of Karbala, drawing parallels to the grief of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Lament of the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the suffering of the Ahlulbayt, specifically focusing on the pain and trials faced by the children of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the sorrow of Bibi Zainab (s.a.).

chapters.title: The Certainty of Death
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the inevitability of death as described by Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and highlights the importance of remembering it as a spiritual practice.

chapters.title: The Shia Perspective on Death
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the unique relationship between a believer and death, emphasizing that for a Shia, death is a transition to witnessing the true light of Maula Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: The Benefit of Loving Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by citing a tradition from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) regarding the seven stations where the love of the Ahlulbayt provides protection and comfort, starting with the moment of death.

chapters.title: The Significance of Wilayah in the Grave
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the love and recognition of the Ahlulbayt is the only source of salvation and peace during the trials of the grave and the afterlife.

chapters.title: The Stages of Qiyamah and the Status of Shias
chapters.summary: An explanation of the various stations of the Day of Judgment, highlighting that the Shias of Muhammad and Ale Muhammad will be at peace while others face severe reckoning.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Promise to the Shias
chapters.summary: A narration describing a vision of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) promising that the Shias will reside near the Ahlulbayt in Paradise and receive divine protection and ease at the time of death.

chapters.title: The Peaceful Death of a Believer
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with a personal account of a peaceful death, illustrating the reality of the Prophet's promise regarding the tranquility of those who hold deep love for the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Ease of Death for the Shia
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that for a true Shia, the experience of death is pleasurable and peaceful, likened to drinking cold water on a hot day.

chapters.title: The Primacy of Wilayah and Bara'ah
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that the core of faith is the combination of Wilayah (love for the Ahlulbayt) and Bara'ah (disassociation from their enemies), which are essential for salvation.

chapters.title: The Weight of Love and the Mercy of Allah
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates a Hadith from the Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari regarding how Allah rewards the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib, even for those who have committed many sins.

chapters.title: The Virtue of Helping Believers and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the immense spiritual rewards for helping fellow believers and emphasizes that true faith requires both love for Ali ibn Abi Talib and disassociation from his enemies.

chapters.title: Commemorating the Deceased and Devotion to Abbas
chapters.summary: The lecture honors the deceased's devotion to Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) and highlights the importance of serving the Ahlulbayt through acts of service and mourning.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.)
chapters.summary: A detailed account of the tragic martyrdom of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) at the Euphrates, focusing on his sacrifice to bring water to the children of Imam Hussain (a.s.).

chapters.title: Closing Supplications and Prayers
chapters.summary: The session concludes with prayers for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), the relief of the believers, and the transfer of merit to the deceased.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 4 | History of Compilation of Holy Quran - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture provides a critical examination of the historical compilation of the Holy Quran from a Shia perspective. It contrasts the traditional Sunni narrative of the Quranic collection under the early caliphs with the belief that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) personally dictated the Quran to Imam Ali (a.s.). The session explores the significance of the Mushaf of Ali, the rejection of the doctrine of companion justice, and the role of the Ahlulbayt in preserving the authentic text and its esoteric interpretation.
content:
Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wa ahlik 'aduwwahum min al-jinni wal-insi min al-awwalina wal-akhirin. Astaghfirullaha alladhi la ilaha illa huwal-hayyul-qayyumu ar-rahmanu ar-rahimu dhul-jalali wal-ikrami wa atubu ilayh. A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alimi min ash-shaytani ar-rajim. Bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyika al-hujjati ibni al-hasani salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi fi hadhihi as-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma 'ajjil li-waliyyika al-faraja waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi wa waffiqna lima tuhibbu wa tarda wa la takilna ila anfusina tarfata 'aynin abadan wa la tastabdil bina ghayrana bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa alihi at-tahirin. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal-'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Welcome to the fourth session of this webinar on the Holy Quran. This webinar has completed its initial stages, and now we will continue our discussion from yesterday, the subject of which was the history of the compilation of the Holy Quran, Insha'Allah. In yesterday's discussion, it became clear to us that there are different perspectives among the Sunnis regarding whether the writing and compilation of the Holy Quran took place after the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) or was completed during his lifetime. The Sunnis believe that this writing continued during the era of their Caliphs, and various companions gathered the verses of the Quran together and attempted to organize them. However, one thing that is absolutely clear to all Muslims is that the order in which the Quran and the Mushaf exist among us today is not the order in which it was revealed to the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.). In the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, which all Muslims consider mutawatir (widely transmitted), the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) himself made it clear by commanding adherence to the Book of God and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) that the Quran existed in the form of a book and a Mushaf. It is the belief of us Shias, and evidence for this was also presented yesterday, that no verse was revealed to the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) except that the Prophet of God had it dictated to the Master of the Universe, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). So, let us begin today's session with the recitation of the Holy Quran, and for this, I request the respected Maulana Azadar Abbas Khan. Assalamu Alaikum, Maulana Sahib. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. Viewers, I request you all to welcome the aforementioned Maulana with a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 'And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our Servant [Muhammad], then produce a surah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful. But if you do not - and you will never be able to - then fear the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers. And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before," and it is given to them in likeness. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally. Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. And those who have believed know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. And He misleads not except the defiantly disobedient, who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth. It is those who are the losers.' 'How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you [back] to life, and then to Him you will be returned. It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed [His attention] to the heaven, and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.' Sadaq Allahu al-Aliyyul Azeem. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Sadaq Allahu al-Aliyyul Azeem. Indeed, Allah the Great and Exalted has spoken the truth. Viewers, the Hadith I have chosen for you today regarding Bismillah is a frightening and alarming one. It is often seen that people are oblivious to the importance and greatness of Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Why have people forgotten Bismillah? In Tafsir al-Burhan, Volume 1, page 219, Hadith number 244, it is found that news reached the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), that people had completely removed Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. The Mawla replied: 'It is a verse from the Book of Allah. Satan has made them forget it.' One meaning of this is that any work done without Bismillah, Satan definitely participates in that work. Sadaq Maulana Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Indeed, my Mawla Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) has spoken the truth. From here, let us move towards today's discussion, which is connected to yesterday's conversation. Today's discussion is even more interesting because, Insha'Allah, we will mention that personality to whom the Lord of the Worlds not only granted the knowledge of the entire Book, but there was no verse of the Quran whose revelation, whose ta'wil (esoteric interpretation), and whose tafsir (exegesis) was not with that personality. Who is the Imam Mubin (Manifest Imam) in the Quran and the Commander of the Faithful in both worlds, namely the sacred personality of Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), who performed the compilation of the Holy Quran in a way that no one else could do, nor can they. To shed more light on this topic, I respectfully request the respected Maulana Syed Sibtain Abbas Rizvi. Assalamu Alaikum, Aqa. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Viewers, before today's speech begins, I would like to remind you again to keep sending your questions to the 'The Strong Group' WhatsApp number, which is [number removed], so that after the speech, Insha'Allah, the Maulana can answer those questions. Send Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless our master and Mawla Abul Qasim Muhammad, Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad, and his pure, immaculate, infallible, and chosen family. Through them, we take guardianship, and from their enemies, we dissociate ourselves before Allah Almighty from now until the Day of Judgment. Allah the Almighty said in His glorious Book, In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, 'Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most suitable.' Respected attendees, scholars, people of virtue, possessors of Wilayah, Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. May your worship and obedience in the blessed month of Ramadan be accepted in the court of the Almighty. May Allah Almighty grant you a long life, and may we all together find the success to go and answer the heavenly call to assist the Proof of the Worlds, Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), from our respective places. This topic relates to the protection of the Quran. This topic relates to the sanctity of the Quran. This topic leaves a circle of questions for all future generations: the Holy Quran, which was a heavenly book and which Allah Almighty gave to His Prophet—the verse I recited, 'Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most suitable'—the very purpose of its coming is that it is a book that guides to the most upright, the purest, and the most correct path, i.e., the Straight Path (Sirat-e-Mustaqim). Now, if the people who come after are aware of the virtues of Islam, whether it be the Noble Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) or occasionally the chosen and selected companions—meaning, not all companions are considered righteous by us Shias, nor do we believe in the absolute justice of all companions. Because believing in the absolute justice of all companions means justifying every crime they committed. We correct those crimes that, God forbid, some companions occasionally committed. Therefore, we can only say what the angle Imam Sajjad (a.s.) created: 'O Allah, send blessings upon his companions who were good companions during his life and after his death.' Blessings and peace upon those companions who gave the right of companionship, both during the life of the Prophet of God and after the death of the Prophet of God. During the life of the Prophet of God, in his wars and his trials, how many remained steadfast, how many fled, how many acted against the Prophet of God, rejected his instructions, etc., from the sins. And after the death of the Prophet of God, it is very clear what crimes some people committed. This is a narration in Sahih Bukhari: 'A group of my companions will come to me.' In the chapter of 'Bab al-Fitan wal-Hawadith' (Chapter of Tribulations and Events), the narration says, 'A group of my companions will come to me at the Hawd (the Pond).' At the Hawd-e-Kawthar. And the angels will push them and drive them away from the Hawd with force and severity. 'So I will extend my hand towards them and say, O Lord, these are my companions.' The voice will come, 'O My Beloved, you do not know what they innovated after you.' My Beloved, this is apparently a mode of address, and the Prophet of God is aware of souls and is present in all worlds. Because 'Allah and His Messenger will see your deeds.' But the reality of the meaning is that the voice says, 'O Messenger of Allah, O Allah, these are my companions.' The voice will come, 'You do not know what they innovated after you.' What do you know, my Beloved, how many innovations they created after you? Therefore, giving a 'clean chit' to all companions is not in our religion, nor can we give it. Yes, we can say, 'His chosen companions, his noble companions, his learned companions, upon them be thousands of greetings and peace.' But those who were not like that, then upon them is what is upon them. Their account is upon them. But any new Muslim who comes will ask: 'Do all the companions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Infallible Imams (a.s.), all the sciences of the general religion, jurisprudence, recitation, ethics, lawful and unlawful, mathematics, and all the chapters of jurisprudence related to Islam—whether it be gnosis or ethics—all relate back to the Quran?' First and foremost, they will debate the dignity and authenticity of the Quran, asking whether, God forbid, the Quran is authentic or not, and whether it is reliable or not. Look at all the Orientalists; about six months ago, I collected about 1,500 research papers by Orientalists, written in Arabic, dating back to the 8th or 9th century in Holland and France. There are 1,500 research papers that condemn the Quran, God forbid, and their sole means of attacking the Quran is by bringing up the issue of the compilation and collection of the Quran. The problem is that 'Nahnu nabni baytan wa nukharibu biladan' (We build a house and destroy a country). Our Sunni brothers destroy an entire city just to build one house. They shake the entire foundation just to place one brick. For instance, to prove that 'Jam' al-Quran wa tadwinuhu min fada'il' (The collection and compilation of the Quran is a virtue). If collecting the Quran is a virtue, why shouldn't this virtue be at the house of Abu Bakr? If collecting the Quran is a virtue, why shouldn't it be at the house of Umar? Presenting the Quran to us in its current form is a virtue; why shouldn't it be in the name of Uthman? They are oblivious to the fact that when one investigates the details of this, the status of their actions is a later matter. What is the status of the act they performed, which is called the Quran itself? I mentioned yesterday as well, although this topic requires at least 10 sessions, dear ones, for a comprehensive discussion. Therefore, within a brief 40-45 minutes, only the headings can be stated; a debate cannot be held. Umar ibn al-Khattab says that Abu Bakr said to Zayd ibn Thabit, 'Anta shabun la nattahimuka' (You are a young man, we do not suspect you). The question is, 'Ama kana fi'... Were there not companions present, men, nobles, scholars, and virtuous people? Were there no men of the field among the companions of the Messenger of Allah that you gave the task of collecting the Quran to an 18-19-year-old boy? 'Ama kana fihim Aliyyun salamullahi alayh? Ama kana fihim Abdullahi bni Mas'ud? Ama kana fihim Ammar? Ama kana fihim Salman? Ama kana fihim Abu Dharr ridwanullahi ta'ala alayhim? Ama kana fihim Abbas? Ama kana fihim Abdullahi bni Abbas?' Was Ali (a.s.) not among them? Was Abbas (a.s.) not among them? Was Salman not among them? Was Abu Dharr not among them? Was Miqdad not among them? Was Zayd ibn Arqam not present? Were Umm Salama and Abi Salama not present? Was Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari not present? The virtuous companions were neglected, and the responsibility of collecting the Quran was given to a boy. 'Alaysa hiya muhinatan lil-Islami wa ghayrihi?' (Is this not a cause of disgrace for Islam and others?) Do you consider this a virtue? Furthermore, who is this Zayd ibn Thabit? Why do we raise fingers at these issues, saying that collecting the Quran was beyond their capacity? 'Zaydu bnu Thabitin huwa min rijalil-lati hamalu wa hajamu ala bayti Fatimataz-Zahra'i salamullahi alayha.' (Zayd ibn Thabit is one of the men who carried out and attacked the house of Fatima al-Zahra (a.s.)). This Zayd ibn Thabit ibn Shimas ibn Qays al-Ansari is the same person who was the first among the Ansar at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah to pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr. And this same Zayd ibn Thabit is the one who advised the killing of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). The late Sheikh Saduq mentions it, and the author of 'Yanabi al-Mawaddah' also mentions it. They said, 'Bring the Quran.' They said if Ali presents his Quran, 'Fama baqiya li wa li-amali qimatun' (Then nothing remains of value for me or my work). They said, 'Famal-hilatu? Fanaqtuluhum' (What is the trick? Let us kill them). After that, they told Khalid ibn Walid to kill Ali during the prayer when Ali (a.s.) would be present. The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) would not attend the prayers of the companions because if he stood up, everyone's prayers would be invalidated. We are told when going for Ziyarat, do not face the Imam (a.s.), do not turn your back to the Imam, or your prayer will be invalidated. That day, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) went by the command of Allah to see how much strength they had. He arrived, and after that, the decision was delayed for a long time. They say, 'Khifna hatta tulu'ish-shamsi wa khifnal-qada'a' (We feared that the sun would rise and we would miss the prayer). After that, Ibn Abi Quhafa said, 'Ya Khalid ibn Abdurrahman, Khalid ibn Walid, la taf'al ma amartuka, assalamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu.' They say, 'Fa-akhadha Amirul-Mu'minina talabibahu.' (The Commander of the Faithful grabbed him by his collar). What did he command you, and what did he forbid you from? So he said, 'Bi-qatlika' (To kill you). He said, 'By Allah.' 'Fa-akhadha bi-talabibihi wa raja'a alal-ardi.' (He grabbed him by his collar and threw him to the ground), and he let out a scream. After that, Ibn al-Khattab came, and he threw him to the ground too. After that, Qays ibn Thabit ibn Shimas al-Ansari, he threw him to the ground as well. People understood. Abu Bakr said, 'Ya Aliyyu alayka bi-haqqi hadha sahibil-qabri wa huwa rahimun warham bina.' (O Ali, by the right of the owner of this grave, he is merciful, so have mercy on us). The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) removed his hand because when the name of the Messenger was mentioned, Ali (a.s.) stopped. This is the reality; what is the status of this Zayd ibn Thabit that we should consider him the collector of the Quran? But anyway, Umar says that Zayd ibn Thabit made a law that every man should bring verses of the Quran and bring two witnesses for every verse. Now, whoever brings two witnesses, in such a case, the Quran would be recorded. Umar regretted until his death that his verse was not registered because I was alone, there was no other witness. 'Ash-shaykhu wash-shaykhatu idha zanata fajliduhuma thamaniyata jaldatin.' (If an old man and an old woman commit adultery, lash them eighty times). Umar says, 'Alas, I could not include the verse in the Quran.' Do you understand the meaning of this? It means that the Quran, which is a reliable and perfect book, should not be debated based on this. It is a book sent by Allah, present from Allah, and proven. But if one looks at the collection of the Quran, then in this case, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Bakr, and Umar made a mockery of the Quran. After that, the third point mentioned about Uthman is that Uthman collected the Quran. Now the question is that Uthman collected this Quran in the last period of his caliphate, in the last 5 years. That is, the Messenger of the Universe passed away in 11 AH. His martyrdom—keep a seminar on this sometime to discuss it. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was martyred. After the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the first caliph remained caliph for 2 years, then the second caliph remained for 10 years. How much is that? 12, 12, 10, 22, 23 years, and Uthman was caliph for 13 years. So it is about 25, 24, 25 years. So, about 20 years after the passing and martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, the Muslims came to their senses. They say that Salim and Hudhayfah (ridwanullahi ta'ala alayh) came from the Battle of Azerbaijan and saw that people were reading different Qurans. He said, 'Adrik ya khalifata Rasulillahi ummata Rasulillahi qabla an yahliku wa qabla an yuharrifu kitabahum.' (Hurry, O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, to the Ummah of the Messenger of Allah before they perish and before they distort their book). Anyway, they collected the Quran. After collecting it, a group was formed, which I mentioned yesterday, consisting of three Qurayshis and three Ansaris. Among those three Qurayshis, one man was acceptable, and that was Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who was among the students of the Family of Muhammad and among those 12 men who protested against Abu Bakr, and the Commander of the Faithful says, 'Anta sayyidul-qurra'i fil-ummah.' (You are the master of the reciters in the Ummah). So, he was the master of the reciters in the Ummah of the Messenger of Allah; he was a proper man. Now, it is a separate matter that when Uthman did not collect the Quran, he performed 'Tawhid al-Masahif' (unification of the codices). He took the codices of the companions, and after taking them, he burned them or buried them. History says he actually burned them and soaked them in hot water. Now, who will determine the punishment for this crime? Obviously, when the police chief himself has drunk, what is there to fear? Now, when the caliph himself is doing this, what can others do? This should have been asked of the caliph himself: why did you burn them? You could have kept them safe as references for the Quran. What was the need to burn them? It was because he burned the Quran of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud himself, he burned the Quran of Aisha himself. Aisha herself said, 'Uqtulun-na'thala innahu ghayyara sunnata Rasulillahi wa ma ghayyara kafanahu wa ma ghayyara jismahu wa ma ghayyara libasahu.' (Kill the Na'thal, for he has changed the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, and he has not changed his shroud, nor his body, nor his clothes). Your clothes have not even become dirty yet, and so-and-so has changed the religion, and so on and so forth. But in the time of Uthman, these codices were taken away. A book was written, which is called 'Nuskha-bardari' (copying). The reality of the word is that the truth was that this copy was the same copy that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had prepared through Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And the one that the Commander of the Faithful prepared again, I will mention its details shortly. He had it prepared, and according to that same Quran, many people completed the recitation of the Quran. Abdullah ibn Abbas completed the recitation, Ubayy completed the recitation, Ammar-e-Yasir completed the recitation. In the same way, Zayd ibn Thabit ibn Zayd says, 'I also completed the recitation of the Quran,' and many other companions of the Messenger of Allah were present who completed the recitation of the Quran. And the Messenger said, 'Inni tarikun fikumuth-thaqalaini kitaballahi.' (I am leaving among you the two weighty things, the Book of Allah). The unification of the codices was a political issue. They wanted to eliminate the margins of the Quran, to eliminate the hadiths written by the companions so that the Quran—because when Umar ibn al-Khattab sent his representatives, the author of 'Iqd al-Farid' and 'Jawahir al-Iqdayn' writes that when Abu Umar sent his governors, Umar ibn al-Khattab came out of the city to see them off. After coming out of Medina, he says to all of them, 'Atadruna limadha kharajtu min baladi?' Do you know why I came out? They said, 'Bi-mathabati annana sahabatu Rasulillahi.' (Because we are the companions of the Messenger of Allah, so you came out to welcome us here). He said, 'No, no, no.' Not for that reason. 'La tashghalu-nnasa an hadithi Muhammadin wa ashabihi.' (Do not occupy the people with the hadith of Muhammad and his companions). He said Muhammad, I cannot say it. Do not occupy the people with the Prophetic hadiths and the Prophetic Sunnah. They should only have the Quran. 'Waqra'u fihimul-qur'ana wa allimul-qur'ana bi-qira'atihi.' (Read the Quran to them and teach them the Quran with its recitation). Do not tell them anything about the Quran. Why? Because he says that if you tell them, people will leave the Quran and get busy with the Sunnah and hadiths of the Messenger of Allah. 'Sallu kama ra'aytumuni usalli.' (Pray as you have seen me pray). Allah said, 'Aqimussalah.' (Establish prayer). Everyone knows 'Aqimussalah', but how to establish prayer? No one knows. The Ummah of Muslims differs on whether to place hands here after Takbirat al-Ihram, or here, or here. Because it was omitted, [the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said] 'Sallu kama ra'aitumuni usalli' (Pray as you have seen me praying). Insha'Allah, I will discuss on another topic that the only sect whose hadith are connected and authentic is the Shia sect. All others do not have hadith; they are legends, myths, and fiction. Because this fiction was created 91 years after the passing of the Messenger of Allah, collecting the forgotten, scattered memories of old women—it is not hadith. But 'Ma qamat Shia wa ma tarak wa ma zala yaktubu wa yantashirul ulum' (The Shia, from the passing of the Messenger of Allah, have been writing and spreading knowledge). Regarding Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), it is written: 'Kana Aliyun Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) yu'alliqu kitabud diyat ma hilbate saife' (Amir al-Mu'minin, to break the law that writing hadith is forbidden and not permissible, used to keep the Book of Diyat tied to the hilt of his sword). He used to say, 'Haza ma katabtu an Rasulillah (s.a.w.a.)' (This is what I have written from the Messenger of Allah). There are thousands of sorrows, my dear friends, but the subject is limited. Why? Because now there is no room on the pulpits to express these things. There is no one to listen. That taste for research is gone, the spirit of investigation is gone. Pray for the day when those truths are expressed from our pulpits that Zainab (s.a.) used to uproot the Umayyad dynasty. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) has made the angels astonished from the earth to the heavens through his knowledge and excellence. In short, my dear friends, during the time of Uthman, this Quranic 'Tauhid al-Masahif' (unification of manuscripts) took place, and all those manuscripts were taken and burned. After that, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, 'I used to write, and people would dictate.' Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, 'Kunnama kunto arizu ala Aliyin (a.s.) fil laila ila tamami' (Whatever I wrote, I would present to Mawla Ali (a.s.) at night). If a 'waw' was missing, Amir al-Mu'minin would have it added; if an 'alif' was missing, he would have it added. Amir al-Mu'minin did not come to the forefront, but in the preparation of that manuscript—even though it was not a complete collection, just a manuscript made to take the companions' manuscripts away from them—even in that, nothing could be done without Ali. Amir al-Mu'minin himself says, 'Kana Uthmanu yushawiruni' (Uthman used to consult me), and people used to refer to me. Siddiq Hasan Khan, the Nawab of Bhopal, writes: 'Kullus Sahaba yuraji'una ila Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)' (All the companions used to refer to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)), 'Wa huwa la yuraji'u ila ahad' (And he did not go to anyone to learn). After that, the Mufti, the Nawab of Bhopal—although he was from the Sadat-e-Razviya, he was influenced by his maternal family and married the sister or daughter of Hamidullah Khan, which is why he later became a Salafi—writes: 'Wa sha'nul mustaftiyin an yastaftu ila muftihim' (It is the way of the followers to learn knowledge from their Mufti). This narration of Abi Darda al-Ansari has also been quoted by Ibn Taymiyyah. It has been quoted by Musannif Ibn Abi Shaybah that Abi Darda al-Ansari says, 'Al-ulama'u salathun' (There are only three scholars in the Islamic world, there is no scholar other than them). He says, 'Am al-alim bisham, alim bil Iraq, alim bil Hijaz' (One is the teacher of the people of Sham, one of Iraq, and one of Hijaz). 'Ana Abi Darda al-Ansari' (I am Abi Darda al-Ansari, I have taught the people of Sham the Quran and the lawful and unlawful). Abi Darda al-Ansari says, 'Alim bisham yuraji'u ila alim-e-ahl-e-Iraq' (The scholar of Sham refers to the teacher of the people of Iraq), 'Wa huwa Abdullah ibn Mas'ud' (Abdullah ibn Mas'ud is the scholar of the people of Iraq). Then he says, 'Wa alimul Hijaz' (And the scholar of Hijaz), 'Alimul Iraq wal Hijaz kulluhum yuraji'una ila alam-e-Hijaz' (The scholar of Kufa and Iraq and the teacher of Sham, all of them refer to the one from Hijaz, they are students of the one from Hijaz). 'Wa huwa Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)'. Regarding Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili says, 'Kullul ulum yantahi ila Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)' (All sciences return to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)). Whether it is the collection and compilation of the Quran, it returns to Ali ibn Abi Talib. The recitation of the Quran follows this chain: Hafs bin Ghiyas, from Abi, from Asim bin Abi al-Nujud, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abi Asad al-Du'ali, from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Today, all the Qurans in the world are according to the recitation of Ali (a.s.). Besides recitation, the science of linguistics, the science of exegesis, the science of lawful and unlawful—Amir al-Mu'minin. Ibn Abi al-Hadid says that 'Al-fuqaha-e-arba kulluhum ayalun ala Ali (a.s.)' (All four jurists are dependents of Ali (a.s.)). Why? 'Anna Malik yaqulu' (Because Malik says), 'Sa'alu anil Malik anna laka hazal ilm' (They asked Malik, where did you get this knowledge?), 'Min ikhtilaf-e-dar-e-Ja'far ibn Muhammad Sadiq' (We kept visiting the threshold of Ja'far ibn Muhammad Sadiq, hence we became scholars). After that, Malik is the teacher of Abu Hanifa. Abu Hanifa says, 'Ma ra'at ainun wala sami'at uzunun wala khatara ala qalb-e-basharin' (No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has crossed the heart of any human) that there would be an Imam, a scholar, or a jurist superior to Ja'far ibn Muhammad in knowledge, piety, devotion, and jurisprudence. Ahmad ibn Hanbal is a student of Malik, Ahmad ibn Hanbal is a student of the teachers and students of Abu Hanifa, and Imam al-Shafi'i openly says, 'Mat Shafi'i wa lam yadri Aliyan rabbuhu am Allahu rabba' (Shafi'i died without knowing whether Ali was his Lord or Allah was his Lord). I don't know what this means; Shafi'i will answer that. Sometimes he says, 'Aliyan hubbuhu junna qasim-un-nar wal jannat wasiyul Mustafa haqqan' (The love of Ali is a shield, the divider of Hell and Paradise, the true successor of the Chosen One). So these Shafi'is and all these people are bowing at the threshold of Amir al-Mu'minin. All the Sufis are bowing at the threshold of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). The chain of Sufis goes from the Prophetic Medina to Ibn Arabi, and Ibn Arabi and Bayazid Bastami. For Bayazid Bastami, Fakhruddin Umar ibn Bahr al-Razi, the author of Tafsir al-Kabir, writes in 'Ihya-ul-Ulum' that 'Ma kana jalalati fil qawm' (Although Bayazid Bastami was very great among the Muslims), 'Kana sakha-an lidar-e-Ja'far ibn Muhammad Sadiq' (He used to stand at the threshold of Ja'far ibn Muhammad Sadiq and serve water). Therefore, the culmination of all sciences was with Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Thus, the collection of the Quran was done solely by Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Yes, it is true that during the time of Umar, there was an effort to ensure that the copy which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had made could be copied. During the time of Uthman, it happened that all the companions' manuscripts were taken and copied. But in reality, if the companions collected it, there is a possibility of error, a possibility of mistake, a possibility of unreliability. Because not all companions had the knowledge. The Quran says that when you used to speak, they would sleep and 'Yatasallalun liwadhan' (would slip away secretly, taking cover behind others), and some would sleep and say, 'Maza qala anifan?' (What did the Messenger of Allah just say?). But Amir al-Mu'minin used to say, 'Liya Rasulillahi dakhalatan' (I had two entries to the Messenger of Allah). One was that I stayed with the Messenger of Allah all day, 'Wa huwa yatkallumuni wa huwa yaqulu wa yubayyinu wa yu'allimuni' (And he would speak to me, tell me, explain to me, and teach me). After that, I would ask, and he would keep answering. When he would fall silent, I would ask questions. After that, at night, 'Kana li dakhalatan la yadkhulu ahadun ghairi' (I had an entry where no one else would enter except me), and for hours I would be with the Messenger of Allah, 'Wa huwa allamani alfan wa inni qad ta'allaftu minal alf-e-alfa' (If the Prophet taught me one point, I converted that one point into a thousand points). Umar says, 'Lawla Umar lahalaka, lawla Aliyun lahalaka Umar' (If it weren't for Ali, Umar would have perished). All scholars say, 'Ali alam-un-nas, afzal-un-nas, akram-un-nas' (Ali is the most knowledgeable of people, the most excellent of people, the most noble of people). Ali is 'Alam-un-nas bil Quran wa sunnat-e-Rasulillah (s.a.w.a.)'. Thus, this matter is settled that the collection of the Quran was only a political act, and the manuscripts were unified; the Quran was not [originally] collected [by them]. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Now, let me complete my point: the first manuscript of Islamic history, the Mushaf of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), the Mushaf meaning the Quran. A Mushaf in which there was no doubt, no suspicion, no error, no possibility of mistake. A Mushaf that was in the era of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The instruction and the method of writing was the dictation of the Messenger of Allah. That is, the Messenger of Allah would speak, and Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) would write it down. The fourth issue is that this Mushaf was with the order of revelation, the occasion of revelation, the interpretation (ta'wil), and the exegesis (tafsir). It contained the explanation of the concise, the explanation of the detailed, the explanation of the absolute verses, the explanation of the restricted, the explanation of the firm verses, the explanation of the ambiguous verses, the abrogating, and the abrogated. Therefore, in terms of compilation, this Quran is a masterpiece. During my speech, I will say one more thing: Amir al-Mu'minin collected this Quran twice. Once, he collected it according to the instruction of the Messenger of Allah, which relates to the revelation of the Quran. That is, just as the Prophet had the Surah placed, had the verse placed, he collected it exactly like that and handed it over to the Messenger of Allah. The Prophet of the Universe used to say, 'Haza al-Quran, inni tarikun fikum al-thaqalain' (This is the Quran, I am leaving among you the two weighty things). The second compilation that Amir al-Mu'minin did was with the ta'wil (esoteric interpretation). Ta'wil means that not everything is the Quran, but the Quran is everything. The Quranic revelation is the revelation that is the Book of Allah, but there are many other inspirations and revelations that descended upon the Messenger of Allah which related to the Quran but were not the Quran itself, and their relation to the exegesis of the Quran is called ta'wil. Amir al-Mu'minin says that I called all the Muslims, 'Uhaziru' (I brought them), and placed that book in front of them. Hello. Yes, the voice is coming. A brother called in between. Anyway. So the ta'wil related to the exegesis, to the lawful, to the unlawful. This second compilation of Amir al-Mu'minin is a special compilation, but the compilation that is called the collection and compilation of the Quran was done in the time of the Messenger of Allah. You see, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says, 'Ma nazalat ayatul ala Rasulillahi (s.a.w.a.) illa aqra'aniha' (No verse descended upon the Messenger of Allah except that he made me read it). 'Wa amlaha alayya' (And he dictated it to me). After making me read it, he dictated it to me, had it written. That is, he had it written letter by letter. 'Fa-aktubuha bi-khatti' (And I kept writing it with my own hand). 'Wa allamani ta'wilaha' (And he taught me its ta'wil, meaning the reality of the exegesis). He explained those exegeses and their clarifications, explained the abrogating, the abrogated, the firm, and the ambiguous. After that, he says when he had finished dictating, he said, 'Wa da'allahu li' (And the Messenger of Allah prayed for me), 'An yu'allimani fahman wa-hifza fahmaha wa-hifzaha fa-ma nasiyatu ayatan min kitabillah' (That may He teach me understanding and the memorization of its understanding and its preservation, so I never forgot a verse from the Book of Allah). And he prayed, 'O Sustainer, increase Ali in understanding, increase Ali in memorization,' that Ali was already a master of understanding and memorization, but even more so, beyond our imagination. 'Wa-la ilman amlaha alayya' (And whatever the Messenger of Allah dictated to me). The Messenger prayed that all those things remain preserved in my being. 'Fa-katabtu-hu munzu da'a li ma da'a' (So I wrote it down since he prayed for me). After that, I did not forget it; it is present with me. This is the characteristic of the Quran collected by the school of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Tafsir al-Quran, Volume 16, Hadith number 14. Talha ibn Abdullah said to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) during the time of Uthman, 'Ya Abul Hasan! Ma yamnu'uka an takhruja kitaballahi ilannas?' (O Abul Hasan! What prevents you from bringing out the Book of Allah to the people?). It was famous among the companions that, 'Ali, the Book of Allah that you have, why don't you give it?' Today people are worried. Amir al-Mu'minin did not answer. One day Talha said, 'Why don't you answer me?' Am I saying something bad? He said, "O Talha! I deliberately did not answer your question. The reason is that what I have written will not be digested by the Muslims. Therefore, they will not accept my words. So, read the original Quran, that is enough. The interpretation (ta'wil) and commentary (tafsir) of the Quran are beyond their capacity." After that, he said, "Tell me about what the people have written." What is your opinion about the Quran that the people have written and sent to every city? "Is it all Quran, or is there something in it, God forbid, that is less or more?" Talha said, "Yes, it is all Quran." Whatever it is, it is the Quran-e-Majeed. The Imam said, "If you hold onto what is in it, you will be saved." If you act upon it and take it and follow it, you will be saved from Hell and will enter Paradise. Kitab-e-Sulaym ibn-e-Qays, page number 82, and Ehtejaj-e-Tabarsi, page number 82. This Mushaf, which was the Mushaf of Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.), this Mushaf was likely, with strong probability, rather certainly, with the Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ibn-e-Sirin says that I kept searching for this Mushaf in Medina for years. I had heard that it is with the family of Ja'far, Ja'far bin Abi Talib (a.s.) or the family of the Imam-e-Mustafa (a.s.), "But I could not find it; if I had found it, there would have been a great deal of beneficial knowledge in it for the Ummah." It is said that Umar ibn-e-Khattab, during his caliphate, said to Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.), "O Abul Hasan! Bring the Quran that you presented to Abu Bakr." The Quran that you placed before Abu Bakr, give it. Imam Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) said, "I only brought it to complete the proof (itmam-e-hujjat) so that on the Day of Judgment you do not recite this verse before God: 'We were unaware of this.' We did not know that the Quran was with Ali. We brought this Quran only for the sake of proof." After that, he said, "None can touch this Quran except the purified ones." Access to this Quran is impossible, except for those who are pure, meaning it is for the Masumeen (a.s.). Because it has a ta'wil, "And none knows its ta'wil except those who are firmly rooted in knowledge." The knowledge of the teaching of the Quran and the ta'wil of the Quran is only with the Imams, and that source which was the ta'wil of the Quran was the marginalia and the appendix of Mawla (a.s.) that he had added after the life of the Messenger of God to the original manuscript that he himself had written. Peace of Allah be upon him and upon him be thousands of greetings and peace. After that, he said, "The successors (Awsiya) from my progeny." The successors who will come from my progeny, who are pure and purified, this will be with them. I searched a lot to find a trace of this Quran, so I am also handing it over to you. Where will this Quran be found? It is in the tradition, in Ehtejaj-e-Tabarsi, Volume 1, page number 360, that Imam Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) says in response to Umar that, "When the Qaim from my progeny rises." And when Hazrat-e-Qaim (a.s.) from my progeny will rise, "He will bring it forth." And he will make people ready to act upon its contents and concepts. In reality, Amir-ul-Momineen had compiled the Quran twice. Once the tanzil, meaning those verses that are present in the Quran today, and the second time the ta'wil, which was related to the heavens, to inspiration, and to the hadiths of the Prophet, which were written in the margins of every verse, just as an appendix or commentary is written today. After that, the confirmation of Imam Muhammad-e-Baqir (a.s.) says, "No one from this Ummah has compiled the Quran except the successor of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)." If anyone in this Ummah says they compiled the Quran, they are a liar. No one except Ali (a.s.) compiled the Quran. Tafsir-e-Qummi, Volume 2, page number 451. In another hadith, Imam Muhammad-e-Baqir (a.s.) says, "If anyone claimed that he compiled the Quran." He has compiled the Quran just as "Allah revealed it, he is a liar." No one has compiled and preserved the Quran "as it was revealed except Ali ibn-e-Abi Talib (a.s.)." Except for Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.), when he memorized and preserved it, it was his pure progeny. Basair-ud-Darajat, page number 103. Ali (a.s.) says, So the Sunnis praise their own sources. If this prayer mat of mine is spread out, if the seat of knowledge is set up, then I will bring out a Mushaf that I have written and the Messenger of God dictated its dictation to me. I will write that Quran and present it before you. Manaqib-e-Aale Abi Talib, Volume 2, page number 41. Sayyid Mohsin Amin, in A'yan al-Shia, quoting Ehtejaj-e-Tabarsi and other Usul-e-Kism Sitta Ashar, says that it is stated that the Prophet ordered Ali (a.s.) to compile the Quran, and he compiled it. Thus, Amir-ul-Momineen compiled it the first time, and Amir-ul-Momineen compiled it the second time. The first time he compiled it, it was generally with the Muslims. Let me point to one more point. Zayd bin Thabit says that we compiled the Quran from scraps and wood, but he never says that we took this Quran from the Messenger of God, the House of the Messenger of God, Amir-ul-Momineen, or Fatima. They compiled what was scattered among them. They avoided taking what was with the Messenger of God. But it is obvious that there is no choice for Muslims except the Ahlulbayt. Enmity is not shown towards Ali. One cannot be hostile to the reality of Ali. If you are hostile to Ali, you will be deprived of the Quran as well. Because the Quran that exists in the world today is Hafs from Asim, from Abdurrahman, from Abi Aswad, from Ali (a.s.); this is the current recitation. Later, Saudi Arabia added Uthman's name to it. Regarding Uthman, Qadi Ayyad Misri says he did not know how to recite, did not know the Book, and did not know the lawful and the unlawful. He did not have knowledge of the lawful and the unlawful, did not know how to write the Quran, and did not know how to read the Quran. In his time, the Mushafs were unified, but it is just like a book being written in Modi's time and Modi sahib saying that I have written it. In Uthman's time, the Mushafs were unified for political reasons, and a copy of every sect was sent everywhere. They had no scholarly contribution to this. In reality, it was the same Quran that Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) had written. After that, they took the companions' Quran and put it aside, and by rewriting it clearly and cleanly, it was sent to all Islamic lands. In short, the summary is that I have searched for you, and the gift of my talk today is: where is that Quran? I have seen this tradition in Uyun Akhbar al-Rida and other traditions. I was very happy after reading this tradition. They say that apparently, this Mushaf is the same Mushaf that was with Imam Abul Hasan Ali ibn-e-Musa al-Rida (a.s.), which Imam Ali ibn-e-Musa al-Rida (a.s.) had given as a trust to his noble companion Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, and you had said to take care that it does not get lost or misplaced. After that, Abi Nasr al-Bazanti says that with the permission of Mawla, I opened only one page, and when I opened it, I read this verse: "And those who were among the disbelievers..." and below that, Mawla Ali had made a list. In it, I found a list of seventy men's names, their names, their fathers' names, and their tribes' names in the margin. Now, it is obvious that when Amir-ul-Momineen, after compiling the Quran, added the knowledge of the Quran around the pages of that Quran or on separate pages, then tell me, what use was Ali's Quran to the Caliph? Therefore, they did not take Ali (a.s.)'s Quran. Still, that same Quran was demanded in every era and was made the basis of action. Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) says in Ehtejaj-e-Tabarsi that the book was presented before them which was complete and contained the tanzil. The summary of the discussion, my friends and dear ones, is that I was listening with great interest, but we fell asleep while telling the story. Neither the topic is complete nor has the conversation reached its conclusion. Just understand this much that no one has a share or part in the Quran except Amir-ul-Momineen. Where the sun of Wilayat rises, there is no room for fake candles. The companions are students; the incompetent goes before the master, not the competent. Ali is the master of masters. Finally, all praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance and curse the enemies of the purified ones. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. This is a very comprehensive discussion, meaning we forced you, because the topic is so vast, but to cover this topic in two sessions, we need at least five sessions. Insha'Allah, this is such a topic, this is such a topic that how wudu is done, how fasting is done, finish this and do at least five sessions on this. Insha'Allah, may God give us all the ability. And really, what you stated during the speech is very important, that nowadays such topics, as they say in English, "it has no takers," meaning there are no appreciators to listen to such topics. Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah, may Allah give us the ability to have more such discussions.

title: His Name Will Be ALI - Uska Naam ALI Hoga | A Monk's Prophecy | Kull-e-Imaan (a.s.) GRAND QUIZ 2022
excerpt: This lecture recounts a historical prophecy made by a monk to Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) regarding the birth of Imam Ali (a.s.). The monk recognizes Abu Talib as a Wali of Allah and foretells that his future son will be the Imam of the pious and the true successor to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The narrative emphasizes the divine appointment of Ali (a.s.) and the monk's request for his salutations to be conveyed to the future Imam.
content:
And the monk says, 'All praise is due to Allah, Who did not grant me death until He let me meet one of His Wali.' This means Abu Talib (a.s.) is the Wali of Allah. Now, this monk, what did he do? He said to Abu Talib (a.s.), 'O Abu Talib, I give you glad tidings. The One Who is the Most High (Ali al-A'la), Who is Allah, He inspired me.' And what was that inspiration? 'That I give you this glad tiding.' Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) asks, 'Which glad tiding?' The monk says, 'A son will be born from your loins who will be the Wali of Allah. He will be the Imam of the pious (Imam al-Muttaqin), and he will be the successor (Wasi) of the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds. Your son is the delight of the heart. If you see him, if you find him, if you reach his era, then what should you do? Convey my salutations to him. Convey my salam to your son.' Convey my Salaam to your son, and tell your son that Mastar has sent you Salaam, Mastar has greeted you, and has greeted you in this state. What is Mastar's belief? [Music] ...upon His Messenger, and then he gives the third testimony: 'And I bear witness that you, Ali, are the successor (Wasi) of Muhammad, and the true successor appointed by Allah through Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and through you, and you are his successor, through you the successorship (Wasiyyat) will be completed, you are his successor.' And after that, he also gave glad tidings to Abu Talib (a.s.) that the child's name is Ali.
The monk identifies Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) as a Wali of Allah.
A prophecy was given to Abu Talib regarding the birth of a son who would be the Imam of the pious.
The son is explicitly identified as the Wasi (successor) of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).
The monk asks Abu Talib to convey his salutations to the future Imam.
The name of the child is revealed to be Ali by the monk.
The testimony of faith includes the recognition of Ali as the divinely appointed successor.

title: Jab Muawiyah Ne Kaha "Bataao Ali (a.s.) Kaise Thay" | Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Ali (a.s.) | Maahe #ramazan
excerpt: This lecture reflects on the profound grief felt by the Muslim Ummah following the martyrdom of Imam Ali (a.s.) on the 21st of Ramadan. It highlights the deep connection between the Imam and his followers, specifically through the account of Zirar ibn Zamra al-Nahshali, who described the Imam's character to Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. The narrative emphasizes the Imam's humility, his awe-inspiring presence, his devotion to worship, and his detachment from worldly temptations.
content:
Haydar, Haydar, Haydar... [repeated]. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. 'The pillars of guidance have collapsed.' When an elder passes away, especially if a father passes away in a house, the grief of that father is immense for the children, for that person's friends, and for his loved ones. The closer that person was to his loved ones, the greater the grief of his departure. Whether it is a father, his friends, or relatives, whenever they remember him after he has passed from this world, whenever they remember his virtues, their hearts fill with sorrow and their grief is renewed. When the passing of an ordinary father has such an effect on people in this world, we cannot even imagine what the Muslim Ummah, especially the Shias of Haydar-e-Karrar (a.s.), must have gone through on the 21st of Ramadan, 40 AH, when the shadow of the father of the Ummah was lifted. Regarding the Master of the Universe, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself had said, 'I and Ali are the two fathers of this Ummah.' When the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) occurred, the shadow of a father was lifted from the head of the Ummah, but the Mawla was still present. After the martyrdom of the Mawla in 40 AH, the Ummah became orphaned again. And that too, an Ali who treated his subjects and his followers with such love, especially the orphans. It is said that when the news spread in Kufa that if anything would prove effective in easing the pain of Ali (a.s.)'s head wound, it would be milk, then the children of Kufa came to the Mawla's door with small pitchers, bringing milk so that it might provide some relief to the Mawla's head wound. Such was the love for the Mawla in the hearts of those people. And who was this Mawla? Who was Ali ibn Abi Talib? He himself stated in a narration: 'Mingle with people in such a way that if you depart from among them, they will weep for you, and if you remain among them, they will desire to be with you.' When this Ali ibn Abi Talib left the world, how great must his grief have been for his followers! There is an incident after the Mawla's martyrdom. Asbagh ibn Nubata narrates that one of the Mawla's companions was Zirar ibn Zamra al-Nahshali. Asbagh states that Zirar once entered the court of Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan. Muawiya said to Zirar—this was after the martyrdom of Ali (a.s.)—'Describe Ali to me. Tell me, how was Ali? Describe Ali.' At first, Zirar said, 'Excuse me from this; I will not be able to do it. I will not be able to describe how Ali was.' Muawiya insisted, 'No, you must tell.' So now Zirar, who is a lover of the Mawla, is describing to Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan how the Mawla was. Now look, this is the grief of a lover that flowed from Zirar's tongue in these words. Zirar says, 'Alright, if you insist, then listen: May Allah have mercy on Ali. By God, Ali was among us as one of us.' He lived exactly like us, meaning he did not differentiate among people, whether he was the Imam or the others were his followers and believers. Therefore, he did not keep any distance between them; rather, he kept people close to him. Then Zirar says, 'He would draw us near when we came to him, and he would answer us when we asked him. He would bring us close when we visited him. No door was ever closed to us; his door was always open for us. And there was no gatekeeper to stop us from reaching him.' We used to come and go to him without fear. This is what Zirar says. After that, Zirar says a strange sentence: 'Despite this closeness, despite being so near to the Mawla, by God, even with his closeness to us and our closeness to him, we would not speak to him out of awe.' The awe of the Master of the Universe was such, the awe of our Mawla was such, that we did not have the courage to speak to him, to have a conversation with him face-to-face. His awe was such, and we would refrain from initiating any conversation due to his greatness, lest—Zirar's point is—lest we say something that might appear disrespectful. The greatness of the Mawla was such in our eyes that we considered it disrespectful to speak to him. Then, after that, Zirar continues to describe his Mawla. When our Mawla smiled, his blessed teeth shone like pearls on a string. Such was the smile of the Mawla. Hearing this, Muawiyah said, 'Tell me more about his attributes, Zirar.' Zirar replied, 'May Allah have mercy on Ali. By Allah, he was a man of long vigils and little sleep. He slept very little. He would spend the night in worship until the late hours, reciting the Book of Allah throughout the night and the day. When it came to generosity in the path of Allah, he did not care for his own life. Our Mawla, Ali ibn Abi Talib, was such that when he stood before Allah, he did so with tearful eyes. He kept no curtains between himself and the people; he met them openly. And he never hid the moon from us.' This is a strange and wonderful phrase. Literally, it means he never hid the moon from us—meaning he never hid his radiant, shining knowledge, which was manifest to the people. When the Mawla spoke, his knowledge was revealed; he did not conceal it. He did not seek comfort; he was not fond of ease, but was a man of hard work and struggle. He never treated anyone with harshness or bad manners; he was soft-tempered. He met people with such grace. It must have been a strange state for Zirar as he described this. Zirar then said, 'If you had seen him when he stood in his prayer niche (mihrab), when the night had spread its curtains and the stars had faded, he would go to his mihrab, holding his blessed beard with his hands, writhing like a wounded person, restless and in agony on his prayer mat. He would weep like a grief-stricken person, saying, "O world, are you trying to entice me? Are you showing me your charms? Alas, alas! I have no need of you. I have divorced you three times." And I have divorced you in such a way that there is no room for reconciliation. Ali has no need of you.' Then the Mawla would say, 'Alas, alas! How long is the journey, and how little is the provision!' We often worry about how long the journey of the Hereafter is. What lesson is the Mawla giving us? The journey of the Hereafter is long; prepare your provisions in this world. 'And the path is rugged.' Prepare for it here in this world. This was our Mawla, this was Ali ibn Abi Talib. The implication of Zirar's words is that upon hearing this, Muawiyah began to weep. Muawiyah could not bear it. Even a hard-hearted man like Muawiyah, who was an open enemy of the Master of the Universe—to the point that he even waged war against him—could not hold back his tears after hearing this. He said, 'Enough, Zirar, enough.' Muawiyah could no longer bear to hear how such a man, how Ali ibn Abi Talib, how such a Mawla had been lost by the world. 'By Allah, Ali was indeed like that.' Muawiyah said that the world and the universe had lost such a compassionate father. And all these things that Zirar described about the Master of the Universe—that the Mawla was such that he would draw people close to him. He would keep them close, especially his followers, whom he kept near to himself. The son of the Master of the Universe, the Imam of our time, Hazrat Hujjat ibn al-Hasan al-Askari (a.j.t.f.s.), possesses all these attributes. We pray to the Almighty Allah to give us some realization of that closeness and to hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time. May He count us all among his sincere servants. And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

title: Religion and Science  |  Episode #3  |  Maulana Sayed Abu Talib Tabatabai Sahab
excerpt: This lecture explores the complex relationship between scientific inquiry and religious truth, emphasizing that while science relies on empirical data and physical observation, it remains subject to change and human error. Maulana Sayed Abu Talib Tabatabai argues that the Quran and the Ahlul Bayt provide an absolute, divine framework that transcends the limitations of the five senses. The discussion highlights the necessity of integrating intellect, knowledge, and Wilayah to achieve a holistic understanding of existence, warning against the pitfalls of forcing scientific theories onto scripture.
content:
...was born. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad and hasten their appearance. [Arabic prayer] O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. In this final lecture on 'Religion and Science', the Strongroom team welcomes you with a Salawat: 'Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin Wa Ali Muhammad'. We hope that all our viewers have gained a lot of information regarding religion and science from the previous two lectures of this series. Viewers, religion is that rational and eternal law of Allah which the Lord of the worlds sent to the earth through His infallible guides... ...sent to the earth through His infallible guides. Before departing, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) handed over two Qurans to us: one is the silent Quran (Quran-e-Samit) which does not speak, and the other is the speaking Quran (Quran-e-Natiq) which is seen speaking even in silence. The Quran did not come just to be kept, but it came for reflection, it came for contemplation, and it came for guidance. This is because the Quran is both art and miracle, and it is also a guide for you and me. The Quran is proof, the Quran is eloquence, and the Quran is wisdom. If the Quran is spread out, it becomes a book of 30 parts (Paras), and if it is condensed into a dot, it becomes Abu Turab (Imam Ali). Viewers, whether it is the silent Quran or the speaking Quran, the nature of both is the same, seeming to encompass everything. 'Neither wet nor dry, but it is in a clear Book'. When the Quran has claimed that everything is present in it, then rest assured, whether it is science or medicine, you will find all of them within the Quran. And on the other hand, with the same confidence, the speaking Quran claimed: 'Saluni, Saluni, qabla an tafqiduni' (Ask me, ask me, before you lose me). Ask whatever you want to ask. This astonishing... ...'Ask whatever you want to ask.' This astonishing and challenging claim of 'Saluni, Saluni' has never been made by any messenger or prophet from the day of creation until today. World history bears witness that this claim was made solely and exclusively by the one who is known as the Gate of the City of Knowledge. Viewers, it is a proven fact that all Muslims agree that the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and his descendants are the source. So it is certain that we do not take religion from science, rather we take religion from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). Whoever follows religion through the Quran and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), a mountain may move from its place, but that person will not waver from his stance. The Hadith also says: 'Whoever takes his religion from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah...' The steadfastness of such people is such that if a person takes his religion from the Book and the Sunnah, from the Book and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), a mountain will move from its place, but that person will not waver. Now, let us move towards today's program of this series. The summary of the previous lectures is that trying to prove most religious matters through science, or keeping religion out of science, or comparing the miracles of religion to modern gadgets, is a futile effort. So, viewers, to gain more information on religion and science, let us once again... ...to gain more information, we once again turn to Hujjatul Islam Ali Janab Maulana Abu Talib Tajalli Saheb, and request him to shed more light on this topic through his speech. Please welcome him with a Salawat: 'Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin Wa Ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum'. [Music] ...In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful... [Music] ...In this matter, according to that calculation, many... ...in this matter, according to that calculation, many things were discussed, and the conclusion that was reached is that we should not make unnecessary attempts to say that whatever religion says is what science says, or whatever science says is what religion says. There can certainly be a dialogue between science and religion, but up to a certain point where they align with each other. In places where science and religion speak against each other, in many places science might say something and religion might say something else. In such cases, we say that science can be wrong, but religion cannot be wrong. This does not mean that... when we talk about religion, we are talking about something greater. But if an Infallible (Masoom) says... religion can say in that place, 'I have its knowledge...' This means... ...'I have its knowledge.' This means those who claim to have knowledge of religion, those who possess religious knowledge, and those who become scholars today just by acquiring bookish knowledge, or by gaining some superficial knowledge, leaving aside traditional knowledge... which is scientifically proven... it can be said, if science is religious, it can be said. Okay, now the question is that if religion came from the Almighty, Who knows everything, the Almighty... Has our Quran explained everything? If the Almighty has explained everything, then why did He keep certain things hidden in His knowledge, and here... ...does it, meaning... it proves that... indeed, all of it is with Him. We have not yet... this is wrong, that we forcefully fit some scientific thing into the Quran. Our scholars have proven this. Once, a person was traveling on the back of a mount, and he met an astrologer who was reading... ...and now... for the sake of Muslims, let me tell you my point, which will remain true till the last breath... He sat down and started arguing with an astrologer. Now, Imam Ali (a.s.) explained in his own words... Imam Ali (a.s.) was riding... Why am I saying these things? I am saying this because the problem of both is that our Imams (a.s.) always... on the basis of their knowledge... the Imams (a.s.) who are the source of knowledge... when the astrologer said, 'Do not go at this hour, because the stars indicate...' then Imam Ali (a.s.) asked him, 'Do you know about the nine planets and their positions?' He started questioning him. I am saying this because it is possible that... due to this, it won't happen. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Tell me your answer here.' Then he started explaining... 'Did you see the two stars meeting?' ...'Did you see the two stars meeting? Tell me, did you see them meeting? And listen to this, did you see them colliding? And look, these are some strange things.' In this way, he questioned him... Why does it seem that the word of Allah is true? The concept of miracles and the laws of nature, which the astrologer was presenting, the Imam refuted them. The Imam (a.s.) wanted to show... He stopped him... 'The army is with me, but upon my followers...' I am giving you the answer. If we go out to fight here, then naturally... when the thoughts of the Imam are discussed, you will find the answer. The Imam (a.s.) asked him, 'Tell me about those ten or twelve stars, did you see them in their orbits? The one which is at the fourteenth station, which is the planet... its position and house...' All these things are before us in the words of the Imam. It happens... do not wait for us... we are all going... our intellect... we walk... we don't even know where... when we manage to understand... what has been discovered today, look at that. Okay, you will note that science—when we learn science and understand science—basically, our intellectual achievement... What does intellect mean? I won't give a long list. Intellect means you have the power of pattern recognition, the power of data processing. Data processing is not just the power to drive socially, you have the power to solve things through data processing. Okay, intellect is... my question is, is intellect sufficient today for everything? If you say yes, your answer is absolutely wrong. Intellect alone is not sufficient. Along with intellect, you need knowledge (ilm). Look, along with intellect, you need knowledge. For example, if a 20-year-old youth comes to me and says, 'Sir, you are wise, please tell me how to fix this car.' I would say, 'Son, the car will be fixed like this: spend six months, a year, or two years with me...' If intellect alone were sufficient, why would an 18 or 12-year-old child come to me to get the car fixed? If intellect was enough, why did he come to me? Think about it. Intellect is a rider, and knowledge is its ride. If you have intellect but no knowledge, you won't understand what guidance is, what love is. Along with intellect, there must also be knowledge so that you can understand things that are not obvious. If you only have intellect... ...just showing off, or cooking biryani, or doing your duty, or showing quality. If you have intellect, now acquire knowledge. Intellect is the rider, and what is the horse of this rider? It is knowledge, on which it rides forward. Until intellect and knowledge are combined, things cannot progress. You cannot understand the Quran and Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) with intellect alone, you cannot wait for the Imam (a.t.f.s.) with intellect alone. Let me give an example of this. How are they connected? Just like winter is connected to the month of December. As soon as intellect and knowledge come together, your understanding begins. So, what we understand is that we want everything... ...we want everything... Look at this example of data processing. What does knowledge do? What is data? What is data analysis? In business, how much profit came, how much was spent on marketing, how much was launched, how much was sold, what is our profit, how much time will it take... all of this is told to you. You are given data. If you give me data, I will analyze it and tell you. But the knowledge of the unseen is not with me. Has the Maulana been given a contract? You have intellect, you have knowledge, you have been given data, and you can progress. If you have intellect and knowledge, and you are given data, you can progress. If you look at big companies, they work from morning to night on data. This is understood. So, you proceed with intellect and knowledge... This is understood. So, you proceed with intellect and knowledge. Science and all these things are understood. But when it comes to matters of religion, what do we say? We say that only what is within the five senses is rational, otherwise how can we accept it? For example, the issue of Hijab, or the command to do something. We say, 'What is this? We have cleaned our body, we have used sanitizer.' Sanitizer cleans outwardly, but what about spiritual cleanliness? I cannot say, because the One who commanded us has not given us the complete data, He has only given us the command. He didn't give us the data that 'if you do this for two weeks, this will happen.' You don't have the data to process. How will your intellect work there? It is like a computer. If a software is not installed in your computer, how will it run? That software is with the 14 Infallibles (a.s.). That software is with the 14 Infallibles (a.s.). Because when we talk about science, our research is based on data, on physical reality, on data collection. Botany, zoology—we go to the laboratory and prove things. But about many things, science has not told us anything. For example, removing ritual impurity (najasat). You might clean it with spirit or sanitizer, but Islam says it becomes pure (pak) with water. When you iron clothes, the high temperature kills all bacteria and viruses. If we talk about science, science would say everything is gone, but is it ritually pure (pak)? Now, what is the view of Shariah? Shariah says that even if the bacteria are gone, it is not ritually pure unless washed with water. If science was everything, then why did Allah command us to ponder? You use science, you do research in laboratories, you search for elements. But do you understand the depth of religion? Why was a command given? Understand it. I am not rejecting science... I am not rejecting science, but even children understand this. I am talking as a professional. You use your intellect, but have you understood everything? No. The Quran itself tells you to use your intellect. Where does it say to use your intellect? In understanding the creation, the alternation of night and day, and the signs of Allah. Allah invites us to use our intellect. But we... ...how the sun rises, how the mountains are set... look at all of this. Ponder upon it. It is not a big deal to look at a tree, but look at how a virus, which might have originated in China, transfers from one person to another, how every human becomes a carrier, and how the virus spreads... ...use your intellect. People say science, science, science... but the knowledge of science is just a drop compared to the knowledge of the Quran. The same spirit, the same light (Noor) of God... title: EP#17: Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) Kis Se Naraaz Thin?
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical account of the displeasure of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) towards the first two caliphs following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the narrative from Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinawari regarding the confrontation at her house and the dispute over the inheritance of Fadak. The speaker emphasizes the Prophet's explicit statement that Fatima's pleasure is his pleasure and her anger is his anger. The lecture concludes by urging listeners to reflect on the spiritual implications of this historical event.
content:
[Music] Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) said, "I will complain about you to my father." In the book *Al-Imamah wa al-Siyasah*, the famous Sunni scholar Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinawari has narrated that Abu Bakr and Umar came to the house of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) to appease her anger. The Lady stood behind a door. Both of them greeted her with Salam, but the Lady did not reply to their Salam. Then Abu Bakr said, "O beloved daughter of the Prophet! By God, the relatives of the Messenger of Allah are dearer to me than my own relatives, and you are dearer to me than my daughter Aisha. I wish I had died on the day your father departed from this world. I recognize your status and I acknowledge your honor and excellence. I did not deny you your right and your inheritance except because I heard your father saying, 'We do not leave inheritance; whatever we leave behind is charity.'" The Lady said, "I ask you both in the name of Allah, did you not hear my father saying, 'Fatima's pleasure is my pleasure, and Fatima's anger is my anger'?" Both of them said, "Yes." Then the Lady said, "I take Allah and His angels as witnesses that you both have angered me. When I meet the Prophet, I will complain about both of you." Now, let every Muslim decide for themselves... ...with whom they would prefer to be on the Day of Judgment: with the Messenger, or with those who angered the Messenger? [Music]
