title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 17 | Tafseer of Surah al-Kafirun (109)
excerpt: This lecture provides an exegesis of Surah al-Kafirun, focusing on its historical context and spiritual significance. The speaker explains that the Surah serves as a firm declaration of dissociation from polytheism and a refusal to compromise on Islamic principles. Additionally, the lecture highlights the virtues of reciting this Surah, including protection from shirk and spiritual rewards in this life and the hereafter.
content:
Masha'Allah. [Arabic prayers: Wa ma tawfiqi illa billah... A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'Alamin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Sayyidil-Mursalin... Muhammadin wa Alihit-Tayyibinat-Tahirin... Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun, la a'budu ma ta'budun, wa la antum 'abiduna ma a'bud, wa la ana 'abidum ma 'abattum, wa la antum 'abiduna ma a'bud, lakum dinukum wa liya din. Sadaqallahul-'Aliyul-'Azim.] Salam Alaykum. Once again, I am present today with the exegesis (tafsir) and themes of Surah al-Kafirun. My previous talk was regarding Surah an-Nas and Surah al-Falaq, and it must have been well-received by the audience, explaining how the Lord of the worlds, in Surah an-Nas and Surah... ...how the Lord of the worlds has commanded us through Surah an-Nas and Surah al-Falaq, and what the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the other Imams (a.s.) have taught us about what we should and should not do. Let us begin Surah al-Kafirun, and what Allah has stated in this Surah. Respected viewers, this is from Tafsir al-Mizan, the last volume, volume 9, page 402. In this Surah, Allah has given a program to His Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to speak clearly to those people and tell them: 'Your paths are different, our paths are different, and your paths are completely separate from ours.' This is a model for the Islamic world, showing that they should not compromise with the enemy under any circumstances regarding Islamic principles. Let me first mention the virtue of its recitation. In the book 'Thawab al-A'mal', Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Whoever recites Surah al-Kafirun and Surah al-Tawhid in their obligatory prayers, Allah will forgive him, his parents, and his children, even if they were among the wretched (shaqi)...' ...and his name will be erased from the register of the wretched (ashqiya) and written in the register of the martyrs (shuhada). As long as he lives, he will live happily, and when death comes to him, he will die as a martyr, and on the Day of Judgment, he will be resurrected as a martyr. In 'Majma' al-Bayan', it is narrated that whoever recites Surah al-Kafirun, it is as if he has recited one-fourth of the Quran. Rebellious devils (shayatin) will stay away from him, he will be purified from polytheism (shirk), and he will remain safe from every kind of fear on the terrifying Day of Judgment. Who wouldn't want to be safe on the Day of Judgment? Every person wants this. If you want this, then recite Surah al-Kafirun. Jubayr ibn Mut'im narrates that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to him: 'O Jubayr, when you go on a journey, do you wish to be superior to your companions in appearance and provisions?' He replied: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, may my parents be sacrificed for you, I indeed desire that.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Then recite these five Surahs...' He said: 'Recite these five Surahs: Surah al-Kafirun, Surah an-Nasr, Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq, and Surah an-Nas, starting each of these Surahs with Bismillah.' Jubayr says: 'I acted upon the command of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and became wealthy, whereas previously my financial condition was not good.' Someone requested the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.): 'Teach me something to recite when I go to sleep.' He said: 'When you go to bed, recite Surah al-Kafirun and then sleep, because in this Surah there is a declaration of dissociation from polytheism (shirk), meaning you will remain safe from shirk.' Now, viewers, let me present the translation and its exegesis. The translation is: 'Say: O disbelievers! I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship. Nor will I worship what you worship, nor will you worship what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.' Regarding the context of revelation (Shan-e-Nuzul), it is narrated in our Tafsir that this Surah was revealed concerning a group of Quraysh: Walid bin Mughirah, 'As bin Wa'il, Harith bin Qays, and Umayyah... ...bin Khalaf and others. They said to you: 'O Muhammad, come, follow our religion and we will follow your religion. We will share all our affairs with you. For one year, you worship our gods, and the next year, we will worship your God. If your religion is better, we will join in it and take our share from it; and if our religion is better, you join in our religion and take your share from it.' At that time, this Surah was revealed. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) does not speak of his own accord, but only by the will of the Lord. Without divine revelation (Wahy), the Prophet does not take any step; when revelation comes, he acts upon it. Therefore, since this was a major issue, the Prophet remained silent—whether it was a small matter or a big one, he would remain silent until the revelation of the Lord arrived. When the revelation came, you recited these verses to the disbelievers. Upon hearing them, the disbelievers were disappointed and became even more hostile than before, increasing their enmity and wanting to cause you even more harm. The reason given is that since the disbelievers had presented their proposal repeatedly, the response to them was also delivered with repetition, meaning... Therefore, in response to them, there is also repetition. The reason for the repetition twice in this Surah is that the proposal they presented to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was also a repetitive proposal. Since their proposal was repetitive, the Lord of the Worlds also responded using the same style. Repetition was used in response to them, and it is also said that this was done for emphasis in response to the disbelievers' denial, so that they might realize their misunderstanding. So, this was the brief commentary (Tafseer) of Surah Al-Kafirun. Tomorrow, I will present myself before you with a new Surah and its commentary. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, take care of yourselves. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

content:
When Imam Mahdi (a.s.) reappears, he will deliver his very first sermon in the Holy Kaaba between Rukn and Maqam, in which he will raise five calls. Among those calls, three are regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.). He says, 'I am the avenging sword, I am the chosen one whom Allah has selected.' After that, the Imam says, 'O people of the world! Indeed, my grandfather Hussain was killed thirsty.' Then the Imam says, 'O people of the world! Indeed, they left my grandfather Hussain's body without ghusl (ritual bath) and shroud.' And at the end, the Imam says, 'O people of the world...'

title: Aashura Ki Wajah Se Ummat-e-Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) Bani Israel Se Afzal [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores a Hadith Qudsi in which Prophet Musa (a.s.) asks Allah why the Ummah of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is superior to the Children of Israel. Allah lists ten specific qualities, with Ashura—defined as mourning and weeping for Imam Hussain (a.s.)—being a central factor. The speaker emphasizes that this act of devotion guarantees Paradise for the believers who participate in the remembrance of the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Waliyul Asr, assist us. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. It is found in the supplications of Prophet Musa (a.s.) that he asked, 'O Lord! Why have You given superiority to the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) over other nations?' Allah replied, 'I have given them superiority based on ten qualities.' Musa (a.s.) asked, 'What are those qualities that they practice, so that I may command the Children of Israel to practice them?' Allah replied, 'Prayer, Zakat, Fasting, Hajj, Jihad, Friday prayers, congregational prayers, the Quran, knowledge, and Ashura.' Musa (a.s.) asked, 'O Lord! What is this Ashura?' Allah replied, 'Weeping for the grandson of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), Imam Hussain (a.s.), or feigning to weep, reciting elegies, and mourning the calamities inflicted upon the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).' O Musa! There will be no servant of Mine in that era who weeps, or feigns to weep, or offers condolences to the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), but that Paradise is guaranteed for him.' In this Hadith Qudsi, the Lord of the Worlds is clarifying that the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has been given superiority over other nations because they weep and mourn over the calamities of Imam Hussain (a.s.). O Lord! Include us among those who weep and mourn for Imam Hussain (a.s.). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Aisi Faqeeri Ameeri Se Behtar Hai - Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) Ki Naseehat
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual perspective on poverty as experienced by the followers of the Ahlulbayt. It highlights a correspondence between a believer and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) regarding financial hardship. The Imam explains that poverty can serve as a means of purification for sins and reaffirms that a life of hardship with the Imams is superior to a life of luxury with their enemies.
content:
Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Maymun says, 'I wrote a letter to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) complaining about my poverty. Then it crossed my mind that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) had said: "Living a life of poverty and hardship with us is better than living a life of wealth and affluence with our enemy. And being martyred in our path is better than living with our enemy." In response, the Imam (a.s.) said: "When Allah sees many sins of our lovers, He sends them poverty and destitution, while Allah forgives most of the sins. Just as you thought, indeed, living a life of poverty with us is better than living a life of wealth and affluence with our enemy. We are a sanctuary for whoever seeks refuge in us. We are a protection for whoever connects with us. We are a light for whoever takes light from us. Whoever loves us will attain a high status with us, and whoever distances themselves from us, their abode is Hell."'

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 24 | Tafseer of Surah al-Kawthar (108)
excerpt: This lecture provides an exegesis of Surah al-Kawthar, explaining its revelation as a divine response to those who insulted the Prophet Muhammad by calling him 'abtar' (lineageless). The speaker discusses the spiritual rewards of reciting this Surah, the nature of the Kawthar river in Paradise, and the necessity of following the commandments of the Ahl al-Bayt to attain proximity to them in the afterlife. The session emphasizes the importance of combining love for the Infallibles with righteous action and adherence to the Quran.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and peace and blessings be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the seal of prophets, Muhammad, and his pure and immaculate progeny. May Allah's curse be upon all their enemies. Today, I have presented myself in your service with a discourse on the exegesis of Surah al-Kauthar. As our discussion was ongoing regarding this Surah, today we clarify that the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) was commanded... because this entire Surah was revealed in honor of the greatness of the Prophet, addressing the accusation that was being leveled against the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) when his enemies called him 'abtar' (lineageless) and many people had started saying so. The enemy called him 'abtar' (without progeny), and in response to the enemy, Allah revealed this Surah. It was said, 'O Messenger, your enemy will remain abtar, not you.' Thus, the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) was given the glad tidings: 'Indeed, We have granted you Kauthar.' In the end, the command for prayer and sacrifice was given in the Surah. Let me present the reward and blessings of reciting it. It is narrated in Sawaab al-A'maal that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Whoever recites this Surah in his obligatory and supererogatory prayers, Allah will quench his thirst from the Pond of Kauthar on the Day of Judgment.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Whoever recites Surah al-Kauthar, Allah will quench his thirst from the rivers of Paradise and will grant him a reward ten times greater than the number of those who offer sacrifices on the day of Eid.' Allahu Akbar! Ten times more reward than the number of those offering sacrifices on the day of Eid! Whoever recites this Surah a hundred times on Friday will be blessed with the visitation of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in a dream, whether they are a man or a woman. It is narrated in Misbah al-Kaf'ami: 'If an animal has a stomach ache, recite this Surah three times into its right ear and blow...' ...recite it three times into its right ear and blow, Bismillah, it will get well and stand up. Think, if an animal can be cured, will a human not be cured if a human... Let us now move towards the translation of the Surah: 'Indeed, We have granted you Kauthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.' 'Inna a'tainaka al-Kauthar'—We have granted you Kauthar. The commentators of the Quran have presented various opinions in the exegesis of Kauthar. In a narration, it is narrated from Hazrat Ibn Abbas that when this Surah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) ascended the pulpit and recited this Surah. When he descended from the pulpit, people asked him, 'What is this Kauthar that Allah has granted you?' He said: 'It is a river in Paradise, whiter than milk, its two banks made of pearls and rubies.' It is narrated in the book al-Khisal that Imam al-Rida (a.s.) and Imam Ali (a.s.) said: 'When the Day of Judgment comes, I will be with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), my progeny ('itrat) will be with me, and we will all be at the Pond of Kauthar. Whoever wishes to reside with us in Paradise must act upon our commandments.' Respected viewers, we do pray at someone's passing... ...we do pray at someone's passing. When we receive news of someone's demise and go to offer condolences, we say, 'May Allah drown them in His mercy and grant them a place in the vicinity of the Infallibles (a.s.).' When we depart, people will pray the same for us; this is generally said for everyone. So my point is that we should also act in such a way, we should act upon the commandments of the Infallibles (a.s.). Since this clarification has been made absolutely clear by the Master, the Master of the Universe explicitly stated that whoever wishes to reside with us in Paradise must act upon our commandments. Whoever merely claims love—even if it is me claiming the love of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), saying I love them, I am their follower, their Shia, their adherent, but I do not act upon their commandments—then I am not worthy of residing with them in Paradise. As for what their status will be, only Allah and the pure Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) know. But intellect also says something; Allah has granted intellect, He has granted sound intellect to every human. From this, we must also think that if the Infallibles (a.s.) have emphasized action so much, there must be some reason, some cause; we need to pay attention to this. Once, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was present in the Prophet's Mosque, and the companions were gathered around him. During that time, he dozed off, his eyes closed... ...during that time, you dozed off, your eyes closed. When your eyes opened, you smiled and said: 'Just now, a Surah has been revealed to me.' Then, you recited Surah al-Kauthar. You asked: 'Do you know what Kauthar is?' Everyone submitted: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a river in Paradise, on whose banks cups are placed in the number of the stars in the sky, and the people of my Ummah will arrive there to meet me. When some of those people are being driven away from me, at that time I will say: "O my Lord, O my Sustainer, O my Allah, my Master and Chief, these are from my Ummah." Then the reply will be: "You do not know what innovations (bid'ah) they introduced after you; they are innovators."' When Ibn Jubayr inquired about Surah al-Kauthar, he said that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Kauthar is a river in Paradise that Allah has granted me.' When Imam Ali (a.s.) sought further clarification, he said: 'This river flows from beneath the Throne ('Arsh). Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, softer than butter, and in it are chrysolite...' ...softer than butter, containing pebbles of chrysolite, ruby, and coral, and the grass on its banks is saffron, and its soil is musk. Then, placing his hand on Ali's shoulder, he said: 'This river is for me, for you, and for your friends.' In another narration, it is mentioned that its depth is equal to seventy thousand farsakhs. Allahu Akbar! Respected viewers, all these glad tidings that have been mentioned are for the believer—the believer who loves the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and acts upon their commandments. Let us perform such deeds that please the pure Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), let us perform such deeds that please Allah. Let us pledge, on the occasion of the martyrdom of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), let us pledge that we will act upon these commandments of the Master of the Universe. We will remain connected to the Quran, and even outside of the blessed month of Ramadan, we will remain connected to the Holy Quran. Even if we recite only one verse daily, but God willing, we will surely do so, and also read its translation and exegesis so that our lives become better and better. Anyway, viewers, I conclude my talk here. God willing, tomorrow we will continue from here. Until then, I seek your leave. Khuda Hafiz. And our final prayer is that all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

title: Jab Maula Ali (a.s.) Aur Bibi Zahra (s.a.) Muskuraaye | 1st Zilhajj
excerpt: This lecture discusses the significance of the month of Dhul-Hijjah, highlighting the marriage of Imam Ali (a.s.) and Lady Fatimah (s.a.) and the revelation of Surah Ad-Dahr. It recounts a tradition from Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.) describing how the smiles of Imam Ali and Lady Zahra illuminate Paradise. The speaker emphasizes that seeking their pleasure through prayers for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is the most virtuous act for believers.
content:
The month of Dhul-Hijjah has begun, a month that starts with the marriage of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and Lady Zahra (s.a.). This entire month is the month of Wilayah. During this month, at various times, different virtues of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were revealed, such as Ghadir and Mubahila. Among all these virtues and perfections of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), one special virtue of this month is that Allah revealed Surah Ad-Dahr in it. Yes, Surah Ad-Dahr, which is known as Surah Al-Insan, Surah number 76. Its interpretation is very strange and wonderful. Let me present a tradition to you regarding the Commander of the Faithful and Lady Zahra (s.a.). In a tradition, the sixth Imam, Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.), says that one day in Paradise, suddenly the light of the sun will shine. The people of Paradise will be worried and surprised, wondering where the sunlight is coming from in Paradise. They will cry out to the Lord of the Worlds, 'O Lord, You said in Your Book'—and this is the verse from Surah Ad-Dahr: 'La yarawna fiha shamsan' (They will not see therein any sun)—'there will be no sun in Paradise, there will be no sunlight, so what is this? What is the matter? Why is all of Paradise illuminated by sunlight?' Then Allah the Almighty will send Jibra'il (a.s.) to the people of Paradise. He will deliver this message. Jibra'il will say to them, 'Laysa hadhihi bishams'—this is not sunlight. It is not the sunlight you think it is; rather, it is the smile of Ali and Fatimah. It is the smile of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and Lady Zahra (s.a.) in Paradise, because of which all of Paradise has become illuminated like the light of the sun. Meaning, when the Commander of the Faithful and Lady Zahra (s.a.) are happy, the entire Paradise becomes illuminated because of their happiness. So, if someone makes them happy in this world, imagine how illuminated our lives could be. And the best deed among these, by which they will always be pleased and happy, is that we pray as much as possible for the reappearance of their son, Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Our prayer to the Lord of the Worlds is: O Allah, for the sake of the pleasure of Ali and Fatimah, illuminate this entire universe and this world through the soon-to-come, radiant reappearance of their son, our Imam of the time, may our souls be sacrificed for him, and count us among his sincere servants. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Kaabe Mein Wiladat - Ek Azeem Amr e Ilaahi
excerpt: This lecture discusses the miraculous birth of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) inside the Holy Kaaba, an event considered unique in history. The speaker highlights the divine significance of this occurrence, citing both historical accounts and scholarly references from various Islamic traditions. Additionally, the talk touches upon Imam Ali's upbringing under the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), his early acceptance of Islam, and his exalted status as the successor to the Messenger of Allah.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. It is a great status... and it is the exaltation of the religion of Islam when that great, luminous personality arrived in the world, who has no equal. The special grace of Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, was upon Hazrat Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), and Allah Almighty granted him such a son, like whom no other newborn exists in the world, nor is there any parallel to this birth found in the world. On this very day, ten years before the proclamation of the prophethood of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the wall of the Kaaba split open for Hazrat Fatima bint Asad (a.s.) and she entered inside. This event left the people of Mecca astonished, but at the same time, they also realized that this indicated a momentous event. Three days later, when Hazrat Fatima bint Asad (a.s.) emerged from that same place, in her merciful embrace was that newborn... ...in her merciful embrace was that newborn for whom Allah Himself chose the name 'Ali'. If a human praises someone, they do so based on their limited intellect. But the Creator of the universe, Who is the Most High (Ali) and the Most Great (Azeem), if He calls someone 'Ali', then estimating the greatness and majesty of that personality is not only impossible but also beyond the ultimate reach of our intellect. If the birth of the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), in the Kaaba is its greatest proof, then the wall of the Kaaba where it split open, even today that mark remains exactly as it was. And every person who goes for the Hajj of the House of Allah or Umrah can see that mark near the Rukn al-Yamani with their own eyes. The mention of the arrival of the successor of the Messenger of Allah, Ali al-Murtaza, the Leader of the Pious, the Commander of the Faithful, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in the Kaaba is recorded in the books of both schools of thought. Hakim al-Nishapuri, in his famous book 'Al-Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn', has acknowledged this fact on page 483 of the third volume. In this regard, the narrations have reached the level of tawatur (consecutive transmission). Regardless of all those narrations... ...regardless of all those narrations, we will mention just one reference. There was a famous Sunni scholar and author of the 13th century Hijri named Sheikh Mumin ibn Hasan Mumin al-Shablanji. He belonged to a town in Egypt called Shablanja. At the age of 10, he memorized the Quran, and later, his education and training began at Egypt's famous Al-Azhar University. He was a student of the famous Sunni scholar... He wrote a book named 'Nur al-Absar fi Manaqib Al-i Bayt al-Nabi al-Mukhtar'. In this book, from the beginning to page 108, he has mentioned the biography of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and from page 109 to 175, he has referred to the first three caliphates. And then, from page 156 to 220, he has written solely about the biography of the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). He mentions the birth of Imam Ali (a.s.) in this manner: 'And he in whom is our Master and Chief, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), who is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah and the Wali of Allah...' ...cousin of the Messenger of Allah and the Wali of Allah, and it is well-known that this is a mention of his virtues. Right at the beginning of this book, he writes about Imam Ali (a.s.) that his birth took place inside the Kaaba in Mecca. According to one opinion, on Friday, the 13th of Rajab, thirty years before the proclamation of prophethood (Be'sat), or according to another opinion, twenty-five years before, or twelve years before Be'sat, or according to one opinion, ten years before. And other than you, no one before you was born inside the Kaaba. On page 157 of this very book, the virtues of the Master of the Universe, Imam Ali (a.s.), that have been described, if we cast a brief glance at them, the summary is as follows: that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) requested his uncle, Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), to let him take Imam Ali (a.s.) into his guardianship. And then, Imam Ali (a.s.) was brought up by the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). After the proclamation of prophethood, the first person who publicly accepted Islam and testified to following the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was indeed Imam Ali (a.s.), and at that time his blessed age was only 10 years. And you never... Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was never separated from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and was always with him, except on the occasion of the Battle of Tabuk, because the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had entrusted Imam (a.s.) with the responsibility of looking after his family. When the reason for this was asked, this was the very occasion where the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) narrated that famous Hadith to Imam Ali (a.s.) and declared the vicegerency of Imam Ali (a.s.): 'Are you not pleased that you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me?' Your position to me is like that of Aaron to Moses, except that there will be no prophet after me. This is just one page. Apart from this, even before saying 'Whomsoever I am his master (mawla), this Ali is his master', if a person is fair-minded, he would be left amazed, because no one can encompass the virtues and merits of Imam Ali (a.s.), nor can anyone equal them. These virtues cannot remain hidden due to anyone's inattention, negligence, or attempts to conceal them. No one can deny the arrival (birth) of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) inside the Kaaba. It was the will of Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and... ...It was the will of Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and His grand command that He arranged His own House for the arrival into this world of His most superior creation after the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Despite this, if someone deliberately denies those virtues, we simply overlook it and invite them to reflect. Today, on this joyous occasion, we present our congratulations to the entire Islamic world, and we pray to Allah the Almighty to keep us steadfast on the path of the guardianship (wilayah) of Imam Ali (a.s.) until our last moments, and to hasten the reappearance of His last Proof and heir, the 12th successor of the Holy Prophet, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), so that he may arrive and fill this world with justice and equity, just as it would be filled with oppression and tyranny. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Zaair-e-Husain (a.s.) Jannat mein Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ka Padosi Hoga | Arbaeen 2025
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual rewards and divine protection granted to the pilgrims of Imam Hussain (a.s.). It details how angels are appointed to cleanse the sins and increase the good deeds of those who visit the grave of the Imam. The discourse concludes with the promise that these pilgrims will be neighbors to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in Paradise and receive the guardianship of Imam Ali (a.s.).
content:
The pilgrim of Hussain (a.s.) will be the neighbor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in Paradise. Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.) said that indeed, Allah has certain angels appointed at the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.). When a person intends to visit Imam Hussain (a.s.), Allah entrusts his sins to those angels. When that person takes one step, the angels erase his sins. Then, with the second step, they begin to increase his good deeds, and this process of increasing his good deeds continues until Paradise becomes mandatory for him. Then the angels surround him and begin to sanctify him, that is, praise him, and then they call out to the angels of the heavens, saying: 'An qaddisu zuwwara habibi habibillah'—'Sanctify the pilgrims of the beloved of the beloved of Allah.' When those pilgrims perform Ghusl, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says to them: 'Ya wafdallahi abshiru bimurafaqati fil jannah'—'Rejoice in being my neighbors in Paradise.' Then the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) says to those pilgrims: 'Ana daminun liqada'i hawa'ijikum wa daf'il bala'i 'ankum fid-dunya wal akhirah'—'I guarantee to fulfill your needs and ward off calamities from you in this world and the hereafter.' Then those angels surround the pilgrims from the right and the left until they return to their families.

title: EP04 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ke Ehsaanaat | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2025 🎁🎉 #ImamMahdi
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual and protective role of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the source of divine mercy and security for the world. It highlights how the Imam continuously watches over his followers, averts calamities, and intercedes for them both in this life and the hereafter. The session also integrates a competitive mega quiz series aimed at fostering deeper knowledge of the Ahlulbayt and strengthening the bond between the Imam and his Shias.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat (proof), son of Al-Hassan (a.s.), Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, as a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye. If you have not yet subscribed to our channel... If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, please subscribe now and do not forget to click the bell icon. The quiz link is now live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered already, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All questions must be answered, and you must provide the correct answers. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all questions must be answered correctly. Winners will be selected from those who answer correctly, but if your name does not appear among today's winners or if you missed an episode, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have answered all questions correctly in all episodes. That is, even if someone is not among the daily winners but has answered correctly in all episodes, even if they were not a daily winner but have answered correctly in all episodes, all such people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. A'udhu billahi samii'il 'aleem minash shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alaika ya waliyyal 'asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. All praise is for Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, who blessed us with the invaluable bounty of the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), because the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the Ark of Salvation and the guiding lights. These are the noble personalities whose generosity and benevolence cannot even be described. The Creator bestowed this great favor upon His creation by sending such personalities for the guidance and salvation of His creation, who are themselves the cause of creation, and the existence of the universe depends upon their noble existence. Countless favors of theirs are upon us due to their noble existence, and today, in this era, regarding the favors of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) that are upon us, regarding the favors of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) that are upon us, let us turn to our brother to shed more light on this topic. A'udhu billahi samii'il 'aleem minash shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Sallallahu 'alaika ya waliyyal 'asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Respected viewers, today we will discuss how the existence of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is beneficial for the earth. Just as there is a verse in the Quran where Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala states: 'I'lamu annallaha yuhyil arda ba'da mawtiha' (Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death). Here, Allah's intention is not the apparent death of the earth, that He makes barren land fertile again through water, rain, or by providing other things. Here, Allah's... To make it fertile again; here, Allah's intention is that through the Imam, He should refill this world—which was crushed under the oppression of tyrannical rulers—with the Imam's justice and fairness, and revive it once again. This is the meaning derived here. Similarly, there is a narration from Ibn Abbas in the book 'Al-Muhajja' regarding the verse 'Know that Allah will revive the earth again,' which means that Allah will establish justice and fairness in the world through Mahdi-e-Aale-Muhammad (A.J.T.F.S.), and Allah has given this as an example of reviving it. The 'death' of the earth refers to it being filled with the oppression of tyrannical rulers, which is likened to its death. We have explained to you the signs of Mahdi-e-Aale-Muhammad (A.J.T.F.S.) so that you may understand. It is narrated from Imam Kazim (a.s.) that the meaning of reviving the earth after its death is not that Allah, through His grace and mercy, or through rain or other means, will revive the earth again, or revive the earth through other means, but rather, Allah's intention here is that He will establish justice and fairness in the world through His Mahdi-e-Aale-Muhammad (a.s.) and revive it. The 'death' of the earth means that the tyrannical rulers had filled this world with their oppression and cruelty; that is what is meant by its death. The Imam (a.s.) says that the establishment of justice and fairness in the world is more beneficial for the world than forty days of rain. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. As you have just heard the discussion presented before you regarding the favors of the Masumeen (a.s.), especially Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), which are upon us, the first discussion you heard was that the survival of this world is due to his blessed existence, and because of his existence, Allah grants life to this world again. As we have read in the sentences of the supplications, 'Bi-baqaihi baqiyatid-dunya' (By his survival, the world remains), that Allah keeps the world alive through his survival, Allah keeps the world alive through his survival, and it is through his blessings that Allah grants sustenance to all of humanity. So, it is a settled fact that Allah (T.W.T.) sent the Masumeen (a.s.) into this world as a blessing for us. This is our second topic to present before you: that the apparent blessing is due to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and the source of the inner blessing is also the noble personality of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). As we present in a sentence of Ziyarat to the Masumeen (a.s.), the phrase: 'Assalamu ala ni'matillahil-abrar' (Peace be upon you, the blessing of Allah upon the righteous). Meaning, the blessing of Allah upon the Momineen (believers) who are righteous. So, through that blessing of Allah—which is the noble personality of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—they become the means for a human to attain worldly and hereafter perfections. Now, what are the things through which a human attains perfection? Such as Ma'rifat (recognition), worship, and guidance. As Ahsan Bhai presented very beautifully in the first episode: 'Bikum budiallahu wa bikum...' (Through you, Allah is worshipped, and through you...) Through you, Allah is worshipped; through you, the recognition of Allah is attained. In the same way, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the source of knowledge and wisdom. The Mawla himself said, 'You will not attain true knowledge from anywhere except our door.' Besides this, whatever other worldly and hereafter perfections a human tries to achieve in this world, sustenance is also reached to the human through you. Patience and strength are also attained by the human through this blessing. If you look at all other blessings, they are being received by humans due to your blessed existence. Now, the first point to present before you is regarding 'Bala' (calamity), that calamity is averted through you. Regarding calamity, I will present two or three points: the arrival of calamity, trouble, and suffering in a human's life—these trials that descend are due to our own deeds, our actions, and our sins. As we mention in Dua-e-Kumayl, which we recite every Thursday night, what do we say in the presence of Allah? 'Allahummaghfirli-dhunuballati tahbisud-du'a' (O Allah, forgive those sins of mine that cause the descent of calamities). So, on one hand, calamities descend due to our sins; on the other hand, it is a test, that Allah... On the other hand, it is a test, that Allah tests His servants to check their patience, to check their gratitude, and to check their faith. As the Quranic verse says, 'Nabtali-ka basira' (We test you so that you may see/understand). That We have created you for a test, and We have made you hearing and seeing—meaning We have granted you intellect. So, certainly, this calamity is a trial that occurs in every human's life. If a human comes to know that there is a sacred personality in this world through whom calamity can be averted, then surely that personality will be a blessing for the human. Let us turn to the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in which they have introduced themselves, that through us, Allah averts calamities. In one Hadith, which Janab Qutubuddin Rawandi has recorded in his book 'Al-Khara'ij', it is mentioned that Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is present in the cradle and is speaking from there to his follower. The Mawla asked for something, and the follower who was present there in the service of the Mawla brought that thing to Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). After that, the Mawla asks, 'Do you know me?' The follower says, 'Yes, Mawla, I know you.' After that, the Mawla asks him, 'Who am I?' Then he says, 'Anta Sayyidi...' Who am I? Then he says, 'Anta Sayyidi, ibn Sayyidi' (You are my master, son of my master), O Mawla, you are our Sayyid and the son of a Sayyid. Mawla, after that, Mawla says, 'I did not ask you this.' Then he asks, Mawla inquires in the presence of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), 'Mawla, may my life be sacrificed for you, please enlighten me, what do you wish to know?' Then the Imam (a.s.) says, and then Mawla himself introduces himself, 'Ana al-Sasiya' (I am from the Sasiya), 'I am the last one, wa bi-dhalika yadhfa'u Allahu al-bala' 'an ahli bayti' (and it is through me that Allah, the Exalted, removes calamities from my family and my Shias). So, this first hadith makes it clear that due to the existence of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), because of his blessed presence, as narrated by Furat al-Kufi in his book 'Tafsir Furat', in which Mawla says, 'Wa bina yustajabu al-du'a' (And it is through us that Allah accepts prayers, prayers are accepted), and then you say, 'Wa yadhfa'u al-bala'' (And it is our being through which Allah removes calamities), 'Wa bina yunazzalu min al-sama' (And because of us, because of us, rain...) And because of us, because of us, rain descends. So here, viewers, we saw that regarding the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and specifically Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), we saw this hadith that calamities are removed because of you, and every human being is afflicted with calamities. Whether one is rich or poor, if everyone analyzes their life, reflects, and contemplates, they find that they are surrounded by calamities. One comes out of one calamity and enters another, from the second to the third; they are afflicted with some problem or another. So, if a person presents the love of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) and his intercession (waseela) in their prayers before the Almighty, then surely Allah will keep them safe from calamities. Now, what are the other favors of the Imam (a.s.)? One is the removal of calamities, the second aspect is that this world exists because of the Imam. And we present this hadith before you, which is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in which he says, 'Al-nujumu amanun li-ahli al-sama'' (The stars are a source of security for the inhabitants of the heavens), and then he says, 'Fa-idha dhahabat al-nujumu, dhahaba ahlu al-sama'' (And when these stars disappear or are destroyed, the inhabitants of the heavens will also be destroyed). And then after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Li-ahli bayti amanun li...' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Li-ahli bayti amanun li-ahli al-ard' (And my Ahlulbayt are a security for the inhabitants of the earth), and then he says, 'Fa-idha dhahaba ahlu bayti, dhahaba ahlu al-ard' (If the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were to leave from among the inhabitants of this earth, if they were to leave, then the inhabitants of the earth would also be destroyed). So what is the conclusion? That the presence of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), their remaining in this world, is the cause of our security. If they are, then we are. Just as we presented the opening sentence before you, 'Bi-baqa'ihi baqiyat al-dunya' (By his remaining, the world remains), in the same style, this hadith has also been presented before you. So, viewers, we saw here that the existence of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is a cause of security for us and for all of humanity. Conversely, if you look, we find that because of the existence of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), punishment is not descending upon us. And if we turn towards the Quranic verse, the Lord of Majesty is saying, 'Wa ma kana Allahu li-yu'adhibahum wa anta fihim' (And Allah would not punish them while you are among them). Now, viewers, reflect a little on whom this verse is being revealed for. It is regarding your and our last... It is being revealed regarding your and our last Messenger, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), and what is its central point, the discussion? That because of your existence, Allah is not sending punishment upon this earth. Now, our question to the entire Muslim Ummah is for them to answer our question. First, listen to the question carefully and then answer it. Tell us, do they believe in this verse or not, in which Allah, the Exalted, is saying that as long as you are there, my beloved, we will not send down punishment? So, answer us this: the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), who has left this world, so now punishment is not coming? So, does this mean that someone like the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is present in this world, due to whose blessed existence punishment is not descending upon us, upon this humanity? And this hadith of the Messenger of Allah itself confirms this, in which he said, 'Law annallaha rafa'a hujjatahu...' (If Allah were to remove His proof from this world for even a moment, this world would perish along with its inhabitants). So, this non-arrival of punishment, if we look at this verse of punishment in the background of this hadith, then it becomes clear... If we look at this verse of punishment, it becomes clear that there is some individual present from the house of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) whose survival is the reason this world is finding security and punishment is not descending upon this world. It is narrated from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) that once the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to Amirul Momineen (a.s.), 'Write what I am dictating to you.' Amirul Momineen (a.s.) said to the Messenger of Allah, 'O Prophet of Allah, do you fear that I might forget?' He said, meaning the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'No, I do not fear your forgetting at all, and I pray to Allah that He keeps you in His protection and security, and that you do not forget anything. I want to have it written for your successors.' Amirul Momineen (a.s.) said to the Messenger of Allah, 'O Prophet of Allah, who are my successors?' He said, 'Your...' Who are my successors? He said, 'Those who share in your affair, those who help you in your affair, all those people are your successors, and the Imams from your progeny. It is through them that rain will fall for my Ummah, through them prayers will be accepted, through them calamities and troubles will be removed from them, and through them, mercy will descend from the heavens.' And then, pointing with his hand towards Imam Hasan (a.s.), he said, 'And this is the first of them,' and after that, pointing towards Imam Hussain (a.s.), he said, 'The remaining Imams are from their progeny.' In the same way, today, the rain falling on this earth, the blessings descending from Allah, the prayers of ours being accepted in the court of Allah, and the troubles and calamities being averted from us, there is only one cause for all of this, and that is the presence of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), due to which Allah is blessing us with His mercy. So, viewers, we just saw that the discussion that Shabeel Hasan Sahab was presenting before you here... The discussion that Shabeel Hasan Sahab was presenting before you here, that our prayers are accepted through Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), and we had also presented this hadith before you in the discussion we had before that, that 'Wa bina yustajabu al-du'a' (We are the ones through whom Allah accepts your prayers, or accepts our prayers). Now, the next topic we have here regarding the favors of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is how he prays for us. So, respected audience, it is not just that our prayers are accepted because of you, but Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is constantly watching over us every moment, every time, and the Imam (a.s.) is continuously praying. Let us see from a sentence how Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) prays for us, in which Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) himself says to his Shias, 'O my Shias, inna ghayru muhmilina li-mura'atikum' (Indeed, we are not negligent in watching over you), 'wa la nasina li-dhikrikum' (and we do not forget you). And then after that, Mawla says, 'Lawla dhalika' (If it were not so, O my Shias, if it were that we had forgotten you, what would be your state?), Mawla says, 'lanazala bikum al-la'wa' (then calamity would have befallen you, you would have fallen into trouble), and then Mawla says, 'wastadh'afa...' And then Mawla says, 'wastadh'afa...' (and the enemy would have surrounded you from all sides). Respected audience, it is very clear from this sentence that when we reflect on the turbulent times of today, and when we look at the world—whether it is Syria, whether it is Iraq, or various parts of the world—when we reflect and see, we find that we are present in this whole world in a very small number, and our enemies are present everywhere, and in every respect, they possess more power than us. So, surely, it is the prayer of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) because of which we are saved in this world today. Today, the fact that we are found, today the ease with which we are performing Azadari, holding gatherings and majalis, performing Azadari for Aba Abdillah (a.s.), this is only and only due to your glance of favor, because of which we are so easily, especially in our country, very easily holding the gatherings of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), performing the majalis of Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Surely, this is the prayer of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), otherwise, this is very, very difficult, because you see how much this world holds enmity towards us, and in various regions, we have visualized this, we have observed it. So come, respected audience, an incident in which how... Respected audience, an incident in which how Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) prays for his followers and how he helps them, provides them aid. This incident is such that there is a person whose name is Yaqoot, found in history, and this incident is not from any ordinary book but in 'Jannatul Ma'wa', which Mirza Hussain Noori, who was the 'Khatim al-Muhaddithin' (Seal of the Narrators), whose title was 'Khatim al-Muhaddithin', recorded in this book of his. And the specialty of this book is that he has recorded the mention of various people's meetings with Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). So, in this book, he mentions a religious scholar whose name is Sheikh Ali Rashti, and he was a great scholar and a respectable scholar, and he was a person possessing all good qualities and excellent characteristics, and he was also a true Sayyid. And this Sheikh Ali Rashti, his teacher was Hujjatul Islam Mirza Buzurg Shirazi, who were very high-ranking Maraje (authorities). So, he was also his student in that era. So, Sheikh Ali Rashti was present among his students. Some people come to the service of Buzurg Shirazi and request him regarding their region that we need a religious scholar here. And when they insist a lot, then Agha Buzurg Shirazi... Insist, then Agha Buzurg Shirazi requests Sheikh Ali Rashti, 'O man of faith, I request you to go to that region and teach the people of that region the religion, make them familiar with the teachings of Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' Now, at their request, Sheikh Ali Rashti goes to that region and lives his life there, and continuously teaches the teachings of Ahlulbayt (a.s.). He went towards Karbala-e-Mualla for the Ziyarat of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and when he was returning to his region, he boarded a boat. And after boarding the boat, he sees a strange scene. The scene was that some young men were present there who were joking around a lot, and one young man was sitting quietly in a corner or on one side. Now, these people who were mocking were also taunting him from time to time, and were taunting him regarding his religion. I mean, they were attacking his personality, and they were also attacking his religion, that he belongs to the Shia sect, and they were attacking him in that regard. Now, when the boat reached the shore and Sheikh Ali Rashti got off that boat and started walking with that person, now when he stays with him, he asks that person named Yaqoot... When asked about the man, the young man named Yaqut explains what happened and who those people were. He says that they were actually from the opposing group and were his relatives. His father also belonged to that opposing group, while his mother was a follower of the Ahl al-Tashayyu, meaning she was a follower of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). He then mentions that now, through the intercession of the Hujjat (a.s.), he has changed. When Sheikh Ali Rashti hears the name of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), he is a bit surprised and wants to know the story behind this, as to how he moved from his father's sect to his mother's. He asks the young man to explain how he came to adopt the Shia faith. The young man explains that his business was in oil—a small trade—and he used to conduct it under a bridge. He often traveled far from his city, Hilla, to buy and sell oil before returning home. Once, he set out with his caravan for business and, after finishing his work, began his return journey. After finishing the work, I began my return journey. Night fell, and I spent the night in the desert with my caravan companions. When morning came, at the time of Subh-e-Sadiq, I woke up to find that my companions were gone; they had left. I was extremely anxious and terrified because I knew my city, Hilla, was about six to seven farsakhs away, and the path was very difficult and dangerous. The area was full of predators that could attack and destroy a lone traveler at any moment. Having no other choice, I moved forward. After traveling for a while, I realized I had strayed from the true path. Despite many attempts, I could not find the right way in the desert and sat down, exhausted. Overwhelmed by thirst and gripped by fear, I felt that an attack could happen at any moment. I saw the final moments of my life before my eyes. At that time, I invoked the intercession of all those I believed in and prayed to the Almighty. I prayed to the Almighty, saying, 'O Lord, for their sake, save me from this calamity.' After much prayer and weeping, when nothing happened, I remembered my mother's words. She had said, 'Son, if you ever find yourself in such a stage or difficulty in your life, or if you are trapped in a sea where you see no way out and it seems impossible to escape, then invoke the intercession of this Imam before the Almighty, and you will surely find that Allah will save you from that difficulty.' Since I had already invoked the intercession of everyone I believed in and had seen the result—that despite my efforts, Allah had not cleared a path—I began to act upon my mother's advice. I started presenting the intercession of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) before Allah and began to weep and cry out. After weeping for a short while before the Almighty, I saw a person wearing a green turban come to me, lift me up, and begin to take me with him. Then, as we spoke, that person... As we spoke, the person who was with me said, 'Why don't you adopt your mother's religion?' After that, he showed me a path and said, 'Travel from here, and you will soon reach your city, Hilla.' I then requested him, 'Why don't you come to my city? Why don't you come with us?' To this, he replied, 'At this moment, thousands of Shias from different regions are calling out to me, seeking my help, and I must reach out to assist all the Shias.' Saying this, he left. When I returned to my city, Hilla, I found that the caravan that had left before me had not yet entered the city. I had arrived before them, even though I had spent a long time wandering in the desert and they had left much earlier. After all this, I went to the Shia scholar of that time, Sayyid Mahdi Qazwini, and presented my entire story to him. Here, Sayyid Mahdi Qazwini explains that this was none other than our Mawla, Hazrat Sahib al-Zaman, Wali al-Asr, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (ajtf). After this, Yaqut requests Mahdi Qazwini to teach him his religion. He then teaches him the entire faith and all its laws. The man then makes another request to Mahdi Qazwini: 'Can I not meet my Imam again? Is there any solution through which I can meet my Imam again?' To this, Mahdi Qazwini says, 'There is one way: if you go to the shrine of Aba Abdillah (a.s.) in Karbala for forty Friday nights, then surely, definitely, you will meet Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.).' As soon as I heard this, the love for his Ziyarat was born in my heart again, and I started acting upon it consistently. When I reached there on the 40th Friday night, I saw that there was very strict security. The tyrant king of that time was demanding permits from everyone—asking if they had brought a permit from their city or if they were just coming—and there was very tight... There was very tight security. No matter how many times I tried, through different groups or caravans entering the city of Karbala, I could not find a way to get entry. Exhausted, I sat outside and again began to seek the help and assistance of my Imam. I then saw Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) appearing to me again, this time wearing a white turban. Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) took the man's hand and entered Karbala, after which he departed from him. From this incident, we learn—this young man named Yaqut teaches us—that Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) does not just pray for the Shias. As we have just seen, 'We never forget you'—he does not just pray; rather, when Shias are trapped in calamity, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) himself is present at that place to assist and help that Shia, or he provides aid through some means. This is quite clear. It is quite clear that the Imam (a.s.) loves us more than a compassionate father. To maintain this love, we also have certain responsibilities: to obey Allah and refrain from His disobedience. If we do this, the compassion of both the Imam and Allah will be upon us. But God forbid, if we do not do this, it should not happen that our love turns into enmity toward the progeny of Muhammad. Just as there is a tradition in the book Al-Kafi from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that Allah (azz wa jal) is so merciful and kind to His servants that He has protected His righteous servants with 40 shields. In this world, as one commits major sins, one shield after another is removed. When his sins... When his sins increase to the point that these 40 shields are removed, Allah says to His angels, 'O angels, protect this believer; cover him with your wings.' Even after committing 40 major sins, Allah assigns angels to protect His servant. But God forbid, we become so stubborn and so occupied in sin that we do not even receive protection from the wings of the angels. We keep sinning to such an extent that at one point, the angels cry out to Allah, 'O Lord, whom have You assigned me to protect? He is sinning openly!' After that, Allah says to the angels, 'Remove your wings from him, for I have torn all the veils of the sky for him.' In this way, when even the angels remove their protection and there is no way left for him to be saved, he becomes ready for enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt. Imam Baqir (a.s.) says that whoever obeys Allah is our friend, our Wali, and whoever disobeys Allah is our enemy. Whoever obeys Allah is our friend, our Wali, and whoever disobeys Allah is our enemy. Viewers, MashaAllah, Shabeel Hassan Sahab has presented these points in a very excellent manner, explaining how the Masumeen (a.s.) love their Shia followers and how they play the role of a pained father, a pained brother, or a kind father. The next topic we have to present before you is that the love found among the Momineen is actually because of the Imam (a.s.). As you have just heard, the role of the Imam (a.s.) is like that of a pained father or brother—like a kind father. A father would never want there to be conflict among his children; he will always try to ensure that the hearts of his followers, his children, or his loved ones are united. Therefore, the Imam will always be engaged in the effort that there should be no conflict among his followers. There should be no conflict among his followers. Now, we observe this here; this is something worth contemplating. All Shia brothers can understand this well: when we go from one region or city to another, and in that unfamiliar city we find a Momin—someone who loves the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), specifically a follower of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)—we don't know his name, his lineage, his identity, or his background. But as soon as we hear that he is a follower of Ali (a.s.), a follower of the Hujjat, or a follower of the Princess (s.a.), love for that individual is automatically born in our hearts. Everyone watching this has observed this at some place or time. The best example is when we go for Ziyarat; we don't know the people there, and we have no connection with them. But when we go there, even if they don't speak our language and we are not familiar with their tongue, when we see them, love for those Momineen is automatically born in our hearts. When we see those Momineen (believers) who have love for them in their hearts, love for them is born in our hearts too. Respected viewers, the cause of this love is Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). This coolness of love that we feel in our hearts for our Momineen—if this mercy is not born, then it is not right. But it is the miracle and excellence of the Masumeen (a.s.) that when their Shias meet, even without knowing each other, they treat one another with gentleness, which is a very difficult task. Allama Majlisi, in his book Bihar al-Anwar, has presented this point through this Hadith. In this part of the Hadith, the Masumeen (a.s.) state that the one who will create affection between different hearts is the work of the Masumeen (a.s.). The hearts are different, they are separate, but the work of creating affection within them is being done by Hazrat Hujjat (a.s.). Similarly, if you look at the phrases of Dua-e-Nudba, where you plead to Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) with a broken heart, saying: 'Ayna al-shaml al-ma'luf' (Where is the one who will gather the scattered people?), which translates to: 'Where is the one who will gather the scattered people and reform them and make them pleased?' This work belongs only to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This part we have presented to you is from before the reappearance (Zuhur). This is from before the reappearance. After the reappearance, when the government of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is established, surely the whole world that accepts the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will have hearts that are united. Everyone will love each other, everyone will consider each other brothers, no difference will be seen, no dispute will be seen. So, this is a very great task of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), to create affection in the hearts of the Momineen while being in occultation. Now, viewers, the culmination of this love is that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) love us, pray for us so much, and express so much love for us. Since we came into this world and as long as we are living our lives, in every matter and at every place, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are seen helping us. And we witness this; we find that the Imam (a.s.) brought us out of difficult conditions and situations when no solution was visible. Yet, some arrangement was made from the unseen, and we came out of that difficult position. We will see the culmination of this love on the Day of Judgment, where the Imam (a.s.) will forgive the Shias regarding his own rights. These are the words of the Hadith in which Imam Ali (a.s.) is seen pointing towards this point. Imam (a.s.) is seen pointing towards this point, saying: 'Idha kana yawm al-qiyamah' (When the Day of Judgment comes), 'My Shias, my followers, O those who believe in me, when the Day of Judgment comes, Allah will place the accounting of our Shias in our hands.' Meaning, we will account for our Shias; no one else will. We will question them, and their responsibility will be ours. And then the Mawla says, 'As for the matters between our Shias and Allah,'—the Imam (a.s.) has stated three separate points here. So, the first point regarding the matters between the servant and Allah, the Mawla says: 'Istashfa'u bi Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) min Allah' (Seek intercession through Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) from Allah), and Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) will request forgiveness from Allah, and Allah will forgive our Shias. SubhanAllah! Regarding the shortcomings we have had in our lives in the worship of Allah, the recognition of Allah, and all the obligations He placed upon us—there is no human who has not had some deficiency in their life. When all those matters are presented before Allah, and we find ourselves alone and... And when we find ourselves alone and solitary, and no helper or supporter is visible to answer for the obligations Allah had imposed upon us, at that time, the Masumeen (a.s.) will help us and, by using the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), will get our sins forgiven. This is the first thing. The second thing, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'As for the matters between our Shias and the people,'—if our Shia has usurped any right or, for some reason, has committed an injustice against any person, then the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Adda Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) 'anhu' (Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) will pay it on his behalf). So here, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) will pay the rights of the people. Meaning, in the first stage, who is becoming the intercessor? Our and your Messenger. In the second matter, when our affair is with the people, even then, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) will become the intercessor. Meaning, this Messenger and his progeny are not only helping and supporting us in this world, but in the hereafter, in the most critical matter, they will not leave their Shias alone. In the most critical matter, they will not leave their Shias alone. The Mawla will be seen helping and supporting us there too. Now, the final matter—they will save us in two stages. In the final stage, the Mawla says, 'And as for what is between us and them,'—meaning the matters between the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and their Shias—the Mawla says, 'Wa nahnu na'fu 'anhum' (And we will forgive them). Ya Ali, Ya Ali, Ya Ali! Meaning, by saving us from all three matters, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will take us towards Paradise. And then the final sentence is the same: 'Hatta yadkhulu al-jannah bi ghayr hisab' (Until they enter Paradise without reckoning). This is a sentence that our intellects cannot understand—that Shias will be forgiven for all the sins they committed without reckoning, and they will be taken to Paradise without account. In the narrations, it is stated very clearly that the Imam (a.s.) even comes to participate in the funerals of his followers. On this topic, a narration... On this topic, a narration is found in Bihar al-Anwar that there is a city in Iran called Nishapur. The people there selected a person named Muhammad ibn Ali to go to Medina. They collected the Khums money or other gifts for the Imam and said to Muhammad ibn Ali, 'Go to Medina and present these gifts to the Imam on our behalf.' They had collected about 30,000 dinars, 50,000 dirhams, and 12,000 garments, and sent Muhammad ibn Ali on the journey to meet the Imam. They had some questions prepared in the form of a folder containing 70 pages, with one question on each page and space left below for the Imam to write his answer. They had tied this folder from three places so that no one could open it. They believed that the one who correctly identifies the Imam, opens the folder, and answers the questions is the true Imam, because that era was very... Because that era was very turbulent; many people claimed to be the Imam. That is why these people took this precaution. Among those Momineen in Nishapur, there was a Mominah (believing woman) named Bibi Shatita. She was poor but had immense love for the Imam. Her Khums money was about one dinar, and a garment she had woven from wool was worth four dirhams. She also made a small bundle and gave it to Muhammad ibn Ali, saying, 'Give my Salam to the Imam and present this gift on my behalf.' Now, Muhammad Ali reached Medina with all this. Since they did not know the true Imam, they reached the door of Abdullah Aftah. They tested Abdullah in their own way, and Abdullah failed. Disappointed, they left the door of Abdullah Aftah, praying, 'O Lord, show me the right path, lead me to the door of the Ahlulbayt.' In this state of confusion... In this state of confusion, a small child came and said to him, 'The one you are looking for, come with me, I will take you to him.' And he took them to Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.) in Masjid-e-Nabawi. As soon as the Imam saw Muhammad ibn Ali, he said, 'Abu Ja'far, what confusion were you in? Did you not know the door of Masjid-e-Nabawi? You could have come here. Like the Jews and Christians, you were worried. As for the questions you brought, I answered them yesterday. And Muhammad ibn Ali, from the gifts and money you brought, bring me only Bibi Shatita's one dirham and the garment given as a gift.' Now, because Muhammad Ali did not remember where he had kept Bibi Shatita's dirham and gift, the Imam told him the exact place, the weight of the dirham, and the weight of the garment. He went and very easily brought Bibi Shatita's garment and that dirham to the Imam (a.s.). He brought the garment and the dirham to the Imam (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) said to Muhammad ibn Ali, 'O Abu Ja'far, convey my Salam to Bibi Shatita.' What a status for Janab-e-Bibi Shatita that the Imam is sending her Salam! And he gave him an envelope containing 40 dirhams and a piece of his own shroud, saying, 'Look, this is from the region of my grandmother, Janab-e-Fatima (s.a.), and it has been woven by my own sister, Janab-e-Halima. Give this to her and tell her that it contains 40 dirhams; she should spend 16 dirhams on herself and keep 24 dirhams for her burial and charity. And 19 days from today, she will pass away, and I myself will come to lead her funeral prayer.' What a destiny Janab-e-Bibi Shatita attained that the Imam is coming to lead her funeral prayer! And he said to Muhammad ibn Ali, 'As for the rest...' And he said to Muhammad ibn Ali, 'As for the remaining money, take it and return it to its owners; I do not need it.' The Imam accepted only Bibi Shatita's one dirham and the piece of cloth she sent; the Imam returned all the rest of the money. And it happened exactly as predicted. When Muhammad ibn Ali returned to Nishapur, he saw that those who had sent the Khums money to the Imam had all turned to the religion of Abdullah Aftah and had adopted the Fathi religion. Only Bibi Shatita was the Mominah who remained steadfast on the Imam's true religion. And it happened exactly as predicted: 19 days later, Bibi Shatita passed away, and the Imam came riding on a camel to lead her funeral prayer himself. The Imam sent a message for all the Shias, conveyed his Salam to all the Shias, and said to them, 'If you remain steadfast on the obedience of Allah and our love, we will participate even in your funeral prayers.' How fortunate is that person! How fortunate is the person whose funeral prayer is led by the Imam (a.s.) himself; how easy the paths of the hereafter will become for him. This incident makes it absolutely clear that in the eyes of the Imam, the amount of money sent does not matter. Even if the amount is small, if it is accompanied by our sincerity and love for the Imam, the Imam accepts it. His love for us is such that he is even ready to attend our funerals. What a life that person has, in whose funeral the Imam participates; all the paths until the Day of Judgment become easy for him, and his life becomes a successful one. The garden of Paradise becomes a gift for the grave; what is death when one meets Ali (a.s.)? Yes, respected viewers, we are very grateful to Allah (S.W.T.) that He has blessed us with such an Imam, under whose love and compassion we are not only living our lives, but even after our death, his mercy and grace will continue to be upon us. We are grateful to our brother who mentioned a few favors of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). We pray to the Almighty that He keeps us steadfast on his recognition (Ma'rifat) and that our end comes upon his Wilayat. Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad. And the Master of the Era, the one who establishes the truth, the one who commands what is right and forbids what is wrong. I believe in Allah, He has no partner, and I bear witness to the truth. Ameen, Ameen. [Music] A'udhu billahi samil 'alim minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alaika ya Wali al-Asr, adrikna. chapters.title: Quiz Guidelines and Program Overview
chapters.summary: The speakers explain the rules for the mega quiz, emphasizing that all questions must be answered correctly across all episodes to qualify for the grand prize of Ziyarat.

chapters.title: The Role of Imam Mahdi in Reviving the Earth
chapters.summary: The lecture interprets the Quranic verse about reviving the earth as the establishment of justice and fairness by Imam Mahdi, which is more beneficial than rain.

chapters.title: Ahlulbayt as the Source of Divine Blessings
chapters.summary: The Ahlulbayt are described as the source of all worldly and spiritual perfections, including knowledge, guidance, and sustenance for humanity.

chapters.title: Averting Calamities through the Imam
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss how human calamities are often the result of sins or tests, and explain that the existence of Imam Mahdi serves as a shield that averts these calamities from the Shias.

chapters.title: Imam Mahdi as the Security of the World
chapters.summary: The existence of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) serves as a divine security for the earth, preventing calamities and ensuring the world's continued existence.

chapters.title: The Role of Ahlulbayt in Divine Mercy
chapters.summary: The Imams from the progeny of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) are the conduits through which rain, mercy, and the acceptance of prayers reach the Ummah.

chapters.title: The Constant Vigilance and Prayers of the Imam
chapters.summary: Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) actively watches over his Shias and prays for them, protecting them from enemies and enabling the practice of their faith.

chapters.title: Historical Accounts of Imam's Divine Aid
chapters.summary: The lecture recounts historical narratives, such as the story of Sheikh Ali Rashti, to illustrate how the Imam provides guidance and support to his followers.

chapters.title: The Story of Yaqut and Imam Mahdi
chapters.summary: A young man named Yaqut recounts how he was saved from a dangerous desert ordeal by invoking Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), leading to his conversion to the Shia faith.

chapters.title: Imam Mahdi's Constant Support and Protection
chapters.summary: The narrative highlights that Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) actively assists his followers in times of distress, demonstrating a love greater than that of a compassionate father.

chapters.title: The Consequences of Sin and Divine Protection
chapters.summary: The lecture warns against persistent sinning, which removes the spiritual shields of protection provided by Allah and the angels, potentially leading to enmity against the Ahl al-Bayt.

chapters.title: Unity Among Believers Through the Imam
chapters.summary: The natural affection felt between Shia believers, even strangers, is attributed to the spiritual influence and unifying role of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).

chapters.title: Intercession and Salvation of Shias
chapters.summary: The lecture explains how the Ahlulbayt will intercede for their followers on the Day of Judgment, covering sins against Allah, rights of people, and matters between the Imam and the Shia.

chapters.title: The Story of Bibi Shatita
chapters.summary: The account of Bibi Shatita from Nishapur illustrates that the Imam values sincere love and faith over material wealth, even promising to attend the funerals of his faithful followers.

chapters.title: The Imam's Mercy and Conclusion
chapters.summary: Reflecting on the Imam's compassion, the speaker emphasizes that the Imam's presence at a funeral ensures an easy path to the hereafter, followed by the concluding Ziyarat.

chapters.title: Salutations to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)
chapters.summary: The session begins with traditional salutations and Ziyarat addressed to the Master of the Era, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
