title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Ka Haakim-e-Shaam Ko Jawaab | Ek Dilchasp Waaqeah | SIBT E AKBAR (a.s.) GRAND QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture highlights a historical confrontation between Imam Hasan (a.s.) and the ruler of Sham, who attempted to claim superiority based on the size of his following. Imam Hasan (a.s.) rejects this false logic, clarifying that numerical majority does not equate to virtue or divine approval. The Imam exposes the nature of the ruler's supporters, distinguishing between those oppressed by tyranny and those who willingly disobey Allah. Ultimately, the lecture emphasizes that true status is defined by purity and submission to Allah rather than worldly power.
content:
'As far as I am concerned, Allah has kept me pure and free from all vices, which are the worst of things, and Allah has kept you far away from all virtues.' This was an audacity against the status of Imam (a.s.)—when an earthly being displays his false superiority and false pomp before a being of light. He was committing such audacity in front of Imam Hasan (a.s.). Now, where are those people who say that the Imams remained silent? See, they did not remain silent. As soon as he spoke, Imam Hasan (a.s.) immediately replied to him, 'How is this possible? What are you talking about?' To this, he replied, 'I am saying this because I am better than you, I am superior to you, because people have gathered around me, whereas you have no one.' This means he was trying... ...He was trying to subdue Imam Hasan (a.s.) by arguing that since the majority was with him, he was therefore better. He was trying to measure virtues by the number of people. And here, indeed, is a very important point: despite the fact that the people were on his side, Imam Hasan (a.s.) confronting him and replying with such bravery and courage is highly significant. 'The majority is with me, and you have no one.' 'A small group overcame a much larger group by Allah's permission.' Thus, in Islam, numbers have no significance, and the majority has no value. If anything has value, it is solely whether one submits before the Proof of Allah. So, to this, he said, 'I have people with me, while you have no one.' Now listen to the reply of Imam Hasan (a.s.). The Imam said, 'Far from it! Far from it!' He did not remain silent; he gave a jaw-breaking reply to the oppressor... He did not remain silent; he gave a jaw-breaking reply to the oppressor: 'O offspring of the liver-eater! Alas, alas for your intellect, that you mistake such baseness for loftiness! Those who have gathered around you... there are two types of people with you. One type are those who are obedient to you, and the other are those who are with you out of compulsion because they have no other choice. They are poor, oppressed people whom you are tyrannizing; they have no shelter, no means. Therefore, at heart, they are not with you, but since you rule over them, they are outwardly living under your rule. They are the oppressed (mustad'afin), just as the Quran has called them oppressed. The Quran has excused them, and the Quran will accept their excuse. But those who are obeying you...' Now the Imam is clarifying about both groups: 'Those who are obedient and submissive to you are disobedient to Allah.' After this, Imam Hasan (a.s.) says, 'Far be it from Allah! Allah forbid that it should ever happen that I say...' Allah forbid that it should ever happen that I say, 'I am better than you' (ana khayrun minka), that I am superior to you. Allah forbid that such a day should ever come when I have to say that I am superior to you. Why? Because there is no goodness in you at all; Allah has kept no goodness in you. As far as I am concerned, Allah has kept me pure and free from all vices and the worst of things, whereas Allah has kept you far away from all virtues.
The ruler of Sham used the size of his following to claim superiority over Imam Hasan (a.s.).
Imam Hasan (a.s.) immediately countered the ruler's arrogance rather than remaining silent.
Numerical majority has no inherent value in Islam; truth is determined by submission to Allah.
The Imam distinguished between the oppressed people forced to follow the ruler and those who willingly disobey Allah.

The Imam refused to equate himself with the ruler, as the ruler lacked any goodness or virtue.

title: EP#9 | Imam Mahdi (atfs) Ka Zuhoor - Qayamat Ki Laazmi Shart | IMAM MAHDI (ATFS): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT
excerpt: This lecture discusses the essential role of Imam Mahdi (atfs) in the timeline of the universe, emphasizing that the Day of Judgment cannot occur without his reappearance. The speaker cites authentic Hadith from Sunni sources, such as Ahmad bin Hanbal and Abu Dawud, to confirm that the Mahdi will be from the progeny of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The session concludes with a call to prayer for the hastening of his reappearance and instructions for a related educational quiz.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. The method to participate in the mega quiz based on this entire video series is as follows: First, you need to register for the quiz at account.dawngroup.com. The registration link is provided in the comments and description of this video. Open this link, and if the link does not open, copy this link, open the Google Chrome browser on your phone, tablet, laptop, or computer, and paste the link there so that it opens. Once the link is open, click on the Google 'G' icon that appears and select the Gmail ID through which you wish to participate in this quiz. As soon as you select your Gmail ID, your registration will be complete. On the registration page, you will see your token number and your details. At the end of that same page, there will be an 'Edit Profile' button; click on it and edit your details, especially your name, WhatsApp number, and area details. It is very important for these details to be correct because through these details... ...is very important because the quiz winners will be contacted using these details. I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. In Ahmad bin Hanbal, Volume 3, Page 376, and Volume 4, Page 52, Hadith number 2231: It is narrated by Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'The Day of Judgment cannot come until a man from my Ahl al-Bayt, who will be my namesake, rises (performs Qiyam).' In addition, Abu Dawud, in his book, page... 325, 326, Hadith number 575, has also narrated it in a similar manner. Once, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was describing the events of the Day of Judgment in a sermon. Then, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Even if only a single day remains before the end of this world, Allah will prolong that day until He sends a man from my progeny whose name will be my name.' Then, Hazrat Salman stood up and inquired, 'O Messenger of Allah! From the progeny of which of your sons will he be?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), placing his hand on the shoulder of Imam Husayn (a.s.), said, 'He will be from his progeny.' Every Muslim performs good deeds in this world in the hope of receiving the reward for their deeds on the Day of Judgment. But in both of these Hadiths, you observed that the reappearance of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is such a divine decree without which the Day of Judgment cannot occur, even if only a single day remains before the end of the world. In other words, when even the Day of Judgment is waiting for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s)... ...is waiting. O Lord of the Universe! Hasten the reappearance of the hope of humanity, the heir of Imam Husayn (a.s.), Hazrat Wali al-Asr Imam Mahdi (a.s.), and grant us the grace to remain steadfast in our belief in his support and guardianship (wilayah). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Today's quiz questions are: 1. What is the name of Ahmad bin Hanbal's book? 2. Whose namesake is Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)? To answer, click on the quiz link provided in the description and comments of this video, and submit the correct answers to these questions as soon as possible for a chance to win various prizes in this quiz.

Hadith from Ahmad bin Hanbal confirm the Mahdi will be the namesake of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).

title: Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course  (With LIVE Demo) - Session # 3
excerpt: This session of the Surah Al-Hamd recitation course focuses on refining the articulation and Tajweed of verses 4 and beyond. The instructor provides a live demonstration, emphasizing the importance of correct makhraj (articulation points) for letters like 'Ain', 'Waw', and the emphatic 'thick' letters. Participants are encouraged to prioritize slow, deliberate recitation over speed to ensure the integrity of the Quranic text is maintained during prayer.
content:
All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and peace and blessings be upon the noble Messenger and upon his pure and purified family, and the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies. After that, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Allah the Blessed has said in the Holy Book, and He is the most truthful of the truthful, and His word is the truth. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. "And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?" Respected viewers, peace be upon you all and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Once again, you are welcome to the Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course program, and Alhamdulillah, we presented the program related to Surah Mubarak Al-Hamd for two days, and you all saw and heard it. Our only purpose from this program is that we correct our Surah Al-Hamd so that, especially in prayer and otherwise, whenever we recite it, we can recite it with the correct letters from their points of articulation and with the correct Arabic pronunciation. Yesterday, I requested you that when you sit here, try to remain in wudu, and the second thing is to keep a pen and notebook in your hands. There might be some things worth noting for you, and today I request you that if you are not sitting with the Quran in front of you, open the Quran or any Juz, the first Juz, or any primer that contains Surah Mubarak Al-Hamd. If it is in front of you, then when I spell it out or say a word or say that this word has a big 'He' or a small 'He', it will be in front of you, before your eyes. Try to have the Taj Company Lahore or Farid Book Depot Quran, meaning the one with the Urdu font, the Urdu script. The Uthman Taha one, the Uthman Taha script which has 604 pages, 15 lines on each page, and the verse ends on the same page, try not to have that for now. Because its handwriting, its script is a bit heavy, difficult for us Urdu-speaking people. So if you don't have the Quran with you right now, take the trouble to get up and open the Quran and keep Surah Al-Hamd in front of you. Today I will state that now we have only three nights, three days, three nights, three hours, three programs, whatever you call it. Friday will be our last program. Today is Wednesday, tomorrow Thursday, day after tomorrow Friday. So in these three days, we have to complete this Surah, Insha'Allah, and without talking about other things, I come directly to the lesson on Surah Mubarak Al-Hamd. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. We have completed three verses, understood their correct and incorrect meanings, and learned their correct Arabic pronunciation. I will read the Bismillah, the first, second, and third verses once, and then go directly to verse number 4. I request you all not to sit completely silent when I read. This is because this subject is something that will come through repeated practice, not just by listening. When you are asked to recite, that is a different matter, but even in between, wherever I read, try to repeat it to yourself in a low voice, even if it is just to yourself, and try to compare how much difference there is between how it is being read and your own reading and pronunciation. For now, we have to read it simply, and on the last day, I will practice the 'Lahn' (melodic recitation), Insha'Allah. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. For now, we have to learn simple pronunciation. In 'Rahman-ur-Rahim', we learned that since there is a 'Zabar' (Fatha) on the 'Ra', we will pronounce it with a full mouth (thick), and the 'Ha' will be articulated from the middle of the throat—from this bone that protrudes here—and the 'Ain' will also be articulated from there. Therefore, we will say 'Rahman-ur-Rahim'. We have also read verse number one, two, and three of the blessed Surah Al-Hamd. We learned to read the first verse like this: Al-Hamdu lillah, lillah, Al-Hamdu lillah. 'Rabbil', since there is a 'Zabar' on the 'Ra', we will pronounce it with a full mouth. 'Rabbil', we have to read every letter with a 'Tashdeed' with a little bit of emphasis. This is what I explained in some detail yesterday. A 'Tashdeed' comes on a letter where one letter is actually two, but it is written as one. We have to read both, but not separately. We will not read it like 'Rabb-bil', we will not read the 'Ba' twice like that. We will read it only once but with emphasis. Similarly, throughout the entire Quran, in supplications (Duas), in prayers (Namaz), in religious recitations (Wazaif), and even in Arabic literature, wherever we read a 'Mushaddad' (emphasized) letter, we will read it with emphasis. Therefore, we will say it like this: Al-Hamdu lillah-i Rabbil-Alamin. Although a reader might read it however they like and move on, if we want to read it according to the Qaris, if we want to observe the rules of Tajweed, if we want to read it the way the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself read it and taught the 'Qira'at-e-Ashra', and the way our Imams (a.s.) read it and emphasized it, then we must observe these rules. No matter how we read, there are few people in our society who point out, stop, explain, and teach the rules of Tajweed. But when scholars, Qaris, Huffaz, and teachers of the Quran are present, it is not easy for everyone to just read and move on. So, for now, we must learn to the extent that no one says after hearing our Surah Al-Hamd that so-and-so read it incorrectly. It is fine if the 'Lahn' is not very good, but at least the mistakes should be removed. So, we must emphasize the 'Mushaddad' letter. Al-Hamdu lillah. After that, 'Rabbil', 'Rabbil Alamin', 'Ar-Rahman-ur-Rahim'. Regarding 'Ma', I also mentioned that when you write the name 'Meem', two Alifs come, and everywhere in Arabic, especially in recitation, wherever an Alif comes, we have to read it short. Like this: Rabbil-Alamin, Al-Hamdu lillah. Look, I am deliberately repeating these words, reading them again and again, and Alhamdulillah, in 20 years of experience, I have seen that many children, girls, ladies, and gentlemen who come to our classes do not have the time to sit and practice. Even scholars, Imams of the congregation, and students who come to the classes do not get time; there is too much work and too many preoccupations. That is why I read again and again, and as a result of this reading, Alhamdulillah, because this sound falls into their hearing repeatedly, they benefit from it and learn. And anyway, there is an Arabic proverb: 'Ad-darsu harfun wat-tikraru alfun' (The lesson is one letter, but the repetition is a thousand). If we have received only one letter or one lesson in class, if the teacher has taught only one letter in class, then read that same thing thousands of times. This is a common thing, but for Tajweed and Qira'at, we should read it millions of times. And the double benefit is that every time we read, we will get reward, and our recitation will improve. So, you who are sitting, wherever you are, whatever place you are in, do not sit silent for these three days. Let your blessed lips move, listen to what I read, try to tally it, and see what the difference is between your reading and mine. I do not say that I read very well or that I am a very good Qari, no. We are trying to improve our recitation a little bit and ensure this Surah is correct for us. I am reading it: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Al-Hamdu lillah-i Rabbil-Alamin. Al-Hamdu lillah-i Rabbil-Alamin. Ar-Rahman-ur-Rahim. Ar-Rahman-ur-Rahim. Maliki yawmid-din. Maliki yawmid-din. These three verses are done. Now after that, verse number 4: Iyyaka. Look at the 'Ya' after the Alif in 'Iyya', which I hope you have the Quran in front of you, you must have opened Surah Al-Hamd. Look at it, in verse number 4, there is a 'Tashdeed' on the 'Ya' after the Alif. 'Tashdeed' means that we have to... read it with emphasis. Leave aside how people are reading or what kind of recitation they are presenting. We have to pay attention to what the law says and how we should read according to the rules of Tajweed. We have to read it like this: 'Iyyaka', 'Iyyaka', not 'Iyya ka', but 'Iyyaka'. This is what emphasis means. 'Iyyaka', now the word I am reading repeatedly, you are listening to it, so read it in your place. 'Iyyaka', look, 'Iyya ka' is different. 'Iyyaka', you have to put a little emphasis on the 'Ya'. 'Iyyaka', 'Na'budu', 'Nun' 'Ain' 'Zabar' 'Na', 'Ba' 'Pesh' 'Bu', 'Na'bu', 'Dal' 'Pesh' 'Du', 'Na'budu'. There is an 'Ain' after the 'Nun'. If we say 'Na'budu', which is derived from 'Ibadat' (worship), it will mean that 'O Allah, we 'Iyyaka' (only You), only You, only You, O God, O my Lord, we worship only You'. When will this meaning be correct? When we read the 'Ain' after the 'Nun' from the middle of the throat, dark, with a thick sound. We will say 'Na', 'Na'. We will combine it 'Na', 'Na', 'Na'. Not 'Na abudu'. 'Na abudu' has a different meaning. When we say 'Iyyaka na'budu', then it will mean that we worship only You. If we said, God forbid, 'Iyyaka na abudu', 'na abudu', with the sound of an Alif or Hamza, then it would mean that it is derived from the word 'Abad' (eternity). Its root would be considered the word 'Abad', and its meaning would be that we are eternal. Whereas you know that nothing in this world is eternal, except for God. So the meanings become incorrect. So we have to read the 'Ain' after the 'Nun' and produce the sound of 'Ain'. 'Na'budu', 'Na', 'Na', 'Ain', 'Ain', 'Na'budu', 'Na'budu', 'Na'budu'. Not 'Na abudu'. 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu'. After that, there is the letter 'Waw'. If we go towards the authentic, eloquent Arabic pronunciation, then those who have participated in our classes or any correct teacher of the Quran know that the letter 'Waw' is read with the rounding of both lips. They are 'Huroof-e-Shafawi', meaning letters articulated from the lips. I pointed this out that day; one is 'Ba', one is 'Meem'. 'Ba' is articulated from the inner lips, the wet parts of both lips, and the upper part also, both will meet like this: 'Ba', 'Ba', 'Na'budu', 'Al-Hamdu lillah-i Rabbil', 'Rabbil'. And the letter 'Meem', the wet part ends, then the dry part that appears, where the dry part starts after the wet part, both parts of the lips will touch, and 'Meem' will come out from that. Meem, but we will not do it like this, we will not do it like that. Meem, normal, Meem, Meem, Maliki, Maliki. So the letter 'Ba' and 'Meem' will both come out from the lips. 'Meem', 'Ba' from the inner lips and 'Meem' from the outer lips. Which part it is, I have explained. After that, the inner wet part of the lower lip touches the edges of the two large front teeth, right in the front. Meaning, like this. We won't keep it pressed all the time, I am just telling you for the sake of explanation. We will read it like this: 'Fa', 'Fa'. Since these letters are here in this Surah, that is why I am mentioning these letters. So the inner part of the lower lip touches the edges of the two large front teeth, the letter 'Fa' will be articulated. 'Fa', 'Fa', 'Fa', 'Fa', 'Falaq', 'Qul a'udhu birabbil falaq'. That is done. And the fourth letter that is articulated from the lips is 'Waw'. 'Waw' is articulated with the rounding of both lips. In Urdu, when we read the name of 'Waw' to learn the Urdu language, we say 'Waw', 'Waw', 'Waw', with the sound of 'O'. But when you learn the Quranic rules and learn the alphabet, the teacher teaching the Quran, the teacher teaching the rules, it is their responsibility to show the students the authentic sound that 'Waw' has in Arabic, like this: 'Wau', 'Wau', 'Wau', 'Wau', this is the Urdu accent, 'Wau', this is the Arabic pronunciation. So this 'Wau' that we say, you saw it is articulated with the rounding of both lips. 'Wau', 'Wau', 'Wau', 'Wau'. These four letters are called 'Huroof-e-Shafawi'. In the Arabic language, since both lips are called 'Shafatain', for that same reason, these four letters are called 'Huroof-e-Shafawi'. All such letters have names, they are all divided into different categories. Letters articulated from the throat are called 'Huroof-e-Halqi', similarly, the six letters that come out from the beginning are 'Ghain', 'Kha', and from the middle come 'Ain' and 'Ha', which is being used a lot in Surah Al-Hamd, and Hamza, and from the end, from the end of the throat, the hollow part, the beginning of the chest, the hollow part, from here 'Ha' (small Ha) and Hamza are articulated. These six letters are called 'Huroof-e-Halqi', and there are three points of articulation in the throat out of 17; there are 17 total points of articulation, three of which are here in the throat. Similarly, these four letters are called 'Huroof-e-Shafawi': 'Ba', 'Meem', 'Fa', and 'Waw'. These four letters are called 'Huroof-e-Shafawi'. You understood, now let's move on. If you want to learn the recitation of Surah Al-Hamd like the great Qaris and teachers of the Quran read, then pay attention, or leave them all aside, if you want to read your Surah Al-Hamd correctly, then pay attention to this thing that I am saying. Especially those who teach the Quran to others, it is obligatory, it is their duty to learn these correct things in this way so that they can teach correctly. We will read 'Iyyaka na'budu wa', now we will not say 'wa', 'Iyyaka na'budu wa Iyyaka', not this, 'Iyyaka na'budu wa wa wa wa Iyyaka', because there is a 'Ya' in the second word 'Iyyaka' as well. So in the first word 'Iyyaka', there is a 'Ya-e-Mushaddad', we will emphasize it, and we will articulate the 'Waw' with rounded lips, this sound that I produced, this is the eloquent Arabic pronunciation. After that, in the second word 'Iyyaka' as well, at the beginning, after the Alif, there is a 'Tashdeed' on the 'Ya', so we have to read both with emphasis, with intensity. 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu'. Now how will you read this in prayer, I will practice that later, I will tell you later. For now, pay attention to the authentic pronunciation. 'Iyyaka na'budu', 'Iyyaka na'budu', then 'wa Iyyaka', not 'wa', like 'wa wa wa wa Iyyaka nasta'in'. There is an 'Ain' in 'Nasta'een'. If we say 'Nasta'een' with an 'Ain', it means, 'O my Lord, we worship only You and we seek help only from You.' We seek help only from You, 'Wa Iyyaka Nasta'een'. 'Iyyaka Na'budu wa Iyyaka Nasta'een'. If we say 'Nasta'een' (with a different sound), it has a very crude meaning; it is incorrect. I will tell you later. We must say 'Nasta'een' with an 'Ain'. So, in verse number 4, we have observed that we need to pay attention to two things. Number one, the word 'Iyyaka' appears twice in this verse. At the beginning of this 'Iyyaka', after the Alif, there is a 'Ya', and in both places, there is a 'Tashdeed' on the 'Ya'. We must emphasize the letter with the Tashdeed. Tashdeed means to give intensity, to stress. Once I placed my finger on my right hand here and just left it, and another time I placed it and pressed it; this is called Tashdeed, intensity. Observing the quality of 'Shiddah' (intensity). If you read 'Iyyaka' once, you have read it, but according to the rules, you have not read it correctly until you stress the 'Ya'. We will read it as 'Iyyaka', like this. I think the point is clear. It is the same in the second one, 'wa Iyyaka'. So, there are two words of 'Iyyaka' in verse number 4, and the 'Ain' has appeared in two words. First, we have to read it like this: 'Iyyaka Na'budu', O Allah, we worship only You. If we read it with the 'Ain', it will mean, 'wa Iyyaka Nasta'een', and we seek help only from You. The point is clear. Verse number 4. Let us move towards verse number 5. There is an Alif, then a 'Ha'. Please observe where the Surah is written in front of you, after the Alif, We have joined it with the 'Ha'. For the 'Ha', I have said that it will be articulated from the bottom of the throat. 'Ha', 'Ha'. In most Qurans, this verse, verse number 5, which is 'Ihdinas-Siratal Mustaqeem', the 'Ha' is written in the form of a 'do-chashmi Ha' (two-eyed Ha). Actually, the letter 'Ha' is the same. title: Adl Meezan Hai | Justice is the Criterion | Kalaam e Noor # 06
excerpt: This lecture focuses on the profound statement of Imam Ali (a.s.) regarding the nature of justice. It highlights that justice is not merely a social construct but the divine balance established by Allah for all creation. The discourse emphasizes the foundational role of justice in maintaining order and righteousness within the universe.
content:
Imam Ali (a.s.) said: "Indeed, justice is the balance of Allah, the Glorified, which He has placed among the creation." Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) stated: "Indeed, justice is the balance of Allah, the Glorified, which He has placed among the creation."
Justice is defined as the balance of Allah.
The concept of Adl (justice) is fundamental to the creation.
Imam Ali (a.s.) serves as the primary source for this spiritual insight.
Divine justice is placed among the creation to maintain equilibrium.
Justice is a reflection of the Glorified nature of Allah.

title: Majlis 3 | Mohabbat-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.): Paakeezgi Ki Alaamat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound connection between the love for the Ahlulbayt and the purity of one's lineage and character. He emphasizes that true devotion to Imam Ali (a.s.) manifests through the practice of modesty, protective jealousy (ghairat), and the active fulfillment of the duty to forbid evil. The discourse further highlights the deceptive nature of the material world and the necessity of acquiring spiritual knowledge early in life to secure one's eternal salvation. Ultimately, the speaker underscores that Wilayah and the recognition of the Imams are essential for navigating life's trials and ensuring the Imam's presence at the time of death.

Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the righteous and certainty. And peace and blessings be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abu al-Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And upon his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The Master of the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our guardian of authority, our master, our patron, our beloved, our physician, our intimate friend, our companion, the Sufficient, the Reckoner, the succor of the distressed and the helpless; may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has said in His Glorious Book—and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'Allah has not made for any man two hearts in his chest.' Allah, the Exalted, the Almighty, has spoken the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance. In the fourth verse of Surah Al-Ahzab, Allah the Almighty declares that Allah has not given any human being two hearts; He has given only one. The discussion was ongoing regarding the core topic of Wilayah and Bara'ah and its sub-topics. Please recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance. One thing that is absolutely certain, and which the Shia believe in, is that no one born of a lawful union (halal-zada) will ever harbor hatred or enmity toward Ali (a.s.). If there is even an iota of hatred or enmity in someone's heart against Ali and the progeny of Ali—that is, the Infallible Imams (a.s.)—then this is a sign of the impurity of their birth. That is why the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance—said to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.): 'O Ali, none shall love you except one who is of pure birth (tabat wiladatuhu). One whose birth is pure, who is born of a lawful union. And none shall hate you except one whose birth is impure (khabuthat wiladatuhu), and whose birth is not pure. None shall accept your Wilayah except a believer, and none shall show enmity toward you except a disbeliever.' Look, the Prophet is establishing fundamental principles here. It is a fundamental principle that whoever harbors hatred for Ali, know that there is a flaw in their birth. I am repeatedly presenting this to you, regardless of who they are. Yes, in this regard, no rank, status, position, wealth, riches, worldly status, or importance matters. As soon as a word against the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) comes out of their mouth and they manifest their enmity and hostility, you can immediately judge that there is some flaw there. Otherwise, a human being would never harbor hatred against Ali (a.s.). There are many other traditions in this regard. Anyway, I must proceed quickly to cover more hadith, if Allah grants the ability. The hadith I just read to you is narrated from 'Al-Ihtijaj' by Tabarsi. The late Tabarsi (may Allah be pleased with him)—this is the late Tabarsi, and his book 'Al-Ihtijaj'—was a scholar of the sixth century. Abu Mansur al-Tabarsi was a very famous scholar and a tremendous personality; he was a great devotee of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The entire first sermon of Ghadir, which is narrated as a mursal (unbroken chain) report, is recorded in his book. It was the first time it was recorded in his book as a mursal report, and regardless, the entire sermon is recorded there. The second hadith is from 'Qurb al-Isnad', which we have discussed before, by Abdullah ibn Ja'far (a.s.). Look, I mention the names of the scholars, the authors, and the writers because they have done us a favor by writing these books. And today they are in Barzakh. If we all gather here today and remember them kindly, then Insha'Allah, we all have to go to Barzakh. So, they should realize that these people remembered us. That is why we should remember them, and because these are individuals who have a very high status and a great position in Barzakh. It is not a common position like that of ordinary people. They have a very high status. These are those individuals. Similarly, Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, as I mentioned to you, was a companion of three Imams. He wrote 'Qurb al-Isnad'. He narrates a hadith from Imam Baqir and Imam Sadiq (a.s.)—O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance—and he narrates from Imam Baqir (a.s.), and he narrates it as a mursal report that: 'A man came to Ali (a.s.).' Listen to this hadith; it is a very strange hadith. A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and said, 'May Allah make me your sacrifice, I love you, Ahlulbayt.' It is said that there was softness in him. The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) treated him with some gentleness. It is said that several people who were sitting there also praised him greatly. Now, 'there was softness in him' could also refer to the man, that his tone was very soft and he was showing great sincerity. Now, if we see someone like that and they come and say this, we would immediately say, 'Friend,' and if four other people testify and say he is a great believer, we would say, 'Brother, everyone is saying he is a great believer.' But the Commander of the Faithful is the Commander of the Faithful. Whoever entered his presence, he would immediately look at their forehead and understand what they were—whether they were destined for Paradise or Hell. Now, no matter how much four people say something in front of him, as soon as he spoke and others supported him, and he expressed it with great sincerity, the Master of the Universe said, 'You are lying. You are lying.' And then the Master of the Universe explained who will never love us. We, the Ahlulbayt, will never be loved by certain categories. There are several categories that are not appropriate to mention here. I have just quickly read the Arabic; the rest is fine. The Master said, 'A mukhannath (effeminate man) will not love us,' meaning one who possesses the traits of women. There are such people, and all those things. 'And a dayyuth will not love us.' This is important. A dayyuth is one who acts as a pimp. So, a person who walks on the street with a non-mahram woman, even if she is his own mahram, if she is unveiled, then he is performing this act for that woman. He is a dayyuth. He is shameless; he has no sense of honor. He is a dayyuth. And similarly, when the Master of the Universe came to Kufa, he saw a strange atmosphere in Kufa. And what was that atmosphere of Kufa like? The atmosphere of Kufa was such that women would walk on the streets shoulder-to-shoulder with men. Well, in that era, such a thing was not common; this is not about today. You might say, 'That is common everywhere today. What are you talking about Kufa? Today it is quite common, right?' You understand, right? Meaning, nowadays the situation is such. So, the Master of the Universe said that when he came to Kufa and saw this condition, he immediately went to the pulpit and said, 'O people of Iraq! O people of Iraq! "And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively." "And fear a trial." "And fear a trial." I have been informed that your women walk shoulder-to-shoulder with men. "Do you not feel shame?" Do you not feel shy? "Allah curses the one who has no sense of honor (ghayrah)." Look, how much the Master of the Universe cares about the veil, hijab, and honor. May Allah's curse be upon the one who is a dayyuth, who is shameless. Meaning, a dayyuth is one who acts as a pimp—that is certainly true—but also one who walks on the street with a woman, walks alongside her, even if she is his own mahram. If someone's mahram is unveiled and does not observe the veil, then if that person has honor, he should say, 'I will not walk with you on the street. I will not talk to you; I will not be on the street. You are without hijab, you are unveiled.' If he does not do that, and walks alongside her like that, saying, 'Oh no, she is our relative, this is that, that is this,' whatever it may be—your relationship does not matter here; the religion matters here. The religion matters here. No matter what it is like. Do not walk. It is found in the tradition. It is in the tradition that the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance—was passing through Medina and what did he see? That a man was standing on the street talking to a woman. The Prophet said to that man, 'Come here, what are you doing?' Nahy an al-munkar (forbidding evil). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is forbidding evil. If it were us, we would say, 'Brother, what do we have to do with this? Why should we get involved? It's not my business.' No, no, it is our business. Nahy an al-munkar is a much bigger responsibility than Amr-bil-Ma'ruf (enjoining good). So, what is the situation in today's age? 'It's not my business, why should I interfere?' Why should we meddle? 'Oh, she is unveiled, what does that have to do with me?' No. You must do it. You must do it because indecency has many consequences. There are many consequences of indecency. And that effect does not only impact the indecent man or woman, it affects others as well. Because human actions, human deeds, have effects that exist in the realm of creation (takwiniyat). And if one person commits an act, it affects others too. The Quran says, 'Fear that punishment' (la tusibanna alladhina zalamu minkum khassah) (wattaqu fitnah). By 'fitnah' here, it means punishment. Avoid that punishment, which will not descend only upon those among you who are oppressors. When the punishment comes, it will descend upon everyone. When a fire breaks out, all houses will burn. Fire does not burn by looking at whose house it is. All houses will burn. The divine punishment is the same. So, Nahy an al-munkar is obligatory. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) called someone and asked, 'What are you doing? Standing on the road talking like this?' He said, 'She is my mother.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'She is your mother? Talk at home, not on the road. This is not the way.' Look at how they were taught Islam. Look at the Prophet's sense of honor (ghairat). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) does not tolerate that he should be overly free with his mother on the road. No, not on the road. Or similarly, for example, 'She is my wife,' or whoever it may be. Whatever you have to do, do it at home, not here, not on the road. Not in the middle of the public square. Therefore, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) says, 'La yuhibbuna mukhannathun wa la dayyuth' (A man who lacks honor or is a pimp will not love us). And how will a dayyuth (a man who lacks protective jealousy over his family) ever love us? Meaning, if he is going out on the road with his mother, sister, daughter, or anyone else in an unveiled state, it means his love for Ali (a.s.) is somewhat lacking. There is no love for Ali (a.s.). He made a claim, and look, he made it in a very soft tone, and many people even supported him. 'No, Maulana, he is one of our own.' You understand, right? 'He is one of our own.' But the Maulana said, 'No, it was a lie, you are lying.' You are lying. 'Walad al-zina' (a child of adultery). And the one who is a child of adultery, the offspring of immorality, will never love us. He will never love us. And then, after that, the Maulana mentioned one or two more things, and then the sentence of the hadith is this. Now look, the Maulana said it. He even gave a prediction: 'You do not love us, you are not our follower. This claim of yours is false.' Now listen to the sentence of the hadith: 'Fadhahaba al-rajulu' (The man got up and left). He got up and left. 'Falamma kana yawmu Siffin' (When the Battle of Siffin took place), then 'faqutila ma'a Mu'awiyah' (he was killed fighting alongside Mu'awiyah). He came to fight against the Master of the Universe (a.s.) and was killed. He was sent to Hell there. Killed at the hands of the believers. Is it clear? And then, the next hadith I am presenting to you, this hadith is from the book 'Kitab-us-Sara'ir'. Actually, the name of the book is 'Mustatrafat-us-Sara'ir'. And it belongs to the late Ibn Idris al-Hilli. Ibn Idris al-Hilli (ridwanullah-e-ta'ala alaih) was also a scholar of the sixth century. Now, let me tell you about him; these are people whose stature is unknown. People do not know about them, and they are not spoken about. He was a tremendous scholar. He was from Hilla. He was from Hilla. And just as Sayyid ibn Tawus was from Hilla, just as Allama Hilli was from Hilla. Whoever is from Hilla is called 'Hilli'. So, his name was Ibn Idris al-Hilli. Ibn Idris al-Hilli, from Hilla, was a scholar of the sixth century. When he used to give lessons, 400 mujtahids in Hilla would attend his lectures. 400 mujtahids in that era. In the late scholar's class, 400 mujtahids. And he was from the lineage of Sheikh Tusi. He was from the lineage of Sheikh Tusi. Meaning, Ibn Idris al-Hilli was not an ordinary personality. So, he narrates this tradition that 'Inna afdala fada'ili shi'atina' (The greatest virtue of our Shias is this). Look at the tradition, what it is. It is a strange and wonderful tradition. The greatest virtue of our Shias is that no immoral woman will ever give birth to them. Wah, wah, subhanAllah, say subhanAllah, wah, wah. Meaning, every Shia's mother is pure and chaste. No immoral woman will give birth to them. 'Anna al-'awahira lam yalidnahum' (Indeed, the immoral women did not give birth to them), 'fi jahiliyyatin wa la islam' (neither in the Age of Ignorance nor in Islam). 'Wa annahum ahl al-buyutat wa al-sharaf wa al-ma'adin wa al-hasab al-sahih' (And they are people of noble houses, honor, treasures, and authentic lineage). Our Shias are from noble families. They are from the honorable ones. And they are keepers of treasures. Keepers of treasures means of knowledge, ethics, and all such things. And they are people of noble lineage. Who is called a Shia? Shia does not mean just anyone can do anything, no. The Master (a.s.) says they are 'Ahl-ul-Buyutat', they are from noble families. In the Arab world, it was asked like this: 'To which family do you belong?' So he would say, 'I belong to such and such family.' Ahl-ul-Buyutat. And they were people of honor, they were mines (of virtue), and they had authentic lineage. And then, the strange and wonderful hadith on this topic is this: that whoever used to come close to the Master (a.s.), then this closeness... Why did this closeness—this intense closeness—exist? It was because the Imams (a.s.), and clearly Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), are superior to all the infallible Imams; they are superior to all the Imams. The most superior is Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). They were the guides, the leaders, and the mentors of the people. And observe how they provided guidance. At every stage, every moment, and in every matter, they opened a door. Now, look here, I am narrating a tradition in your presence that reveals how the infallible Imams (a.s.) guided their followers at every single step. The only condition is this: that we must seek guidance. We must ask for it. We must keep asking at every moment and every instant. That is, we should pray to Allah that it never happens that we go a minute without asking, or for instance, without seeking, and start relying on ourselves, thinking, 'I can accomplish this task on my own.' Now, look at the tradition here; it is as follows: Harith al-Hamdani is a famous personality, and if time permits today, we will read another hadith about him. He is a very famous personality, from the Hamdan tribe of Yemen. See, Hamdan was a tribe in Yemen. And this was a very 'Mowla-loving' tribe, a powerful one. They possessed great Wilayah. They had strong Wilayah. All those Hamdanis—this is not the Hamadan of Iran, that is called Hamadan, it is different. This is the one from Yemen. So, this Harith al-Awar al-Hamdani (Ridwanullah Ta'ala Alaih) says that I went out with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) towards Hira. Hira, meaning a little distance from Kufa. A little distance from Kufa. For a journey, for a stroll. I requested—Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.) went out for a stroll. Look, what a blessing that was. Well, obviously, Hazrat-e-Amir did not take just anyone with him. Whenever you see such traditions where one says, 'I went out for a stroll with him,' it is either Kumayl ibn Ziyad al-Nakha'i, or Harith al-Hamdani, or Habbah al-Arani. These were the individuals who were extremely close to the Imam. So, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) went out with them. 'Baynama ana asiru ma'a Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib alayhimas-salam fil-Hira' (While I was walking with Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in Hira), and they went quite far. Where did we reach? We reached a monastery (Dayr). A monastery, meaning where the Christians—those whom they call Nasrani—where their monks, their 'popes' as they call them, lived; their Sufis lived there. So, we reached there, right by the church. So, what did he do? That Nasrani priest started ringing the bell. Of the church. Which is called 'Naqus' in Arabic. It is called Naqus. 'Faqala Ali ibn Abi Talib alayhimas-salam' (Then Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said), the Mawla said, 'Ya Harith, atadri ma yaqul' (O Harith, do you know what it is saying?) Now tell me, does a bell say anything? The Mawla reached there, 'Atadri ma yaqul hadhan-naqus' (Do you know what this bell is saying?) 'Qultu' (I said), I requested—now look at the faith of Harith—'Allahu wa rasuluhu wabnu ammi rasulihi a'lam' (Allah, His Messenger, and the cousin of His Messenger know best). And no one else knows. The Mawla said, 'Innahu yadribu mathalad-dunya wa kharabiha' (It is striking a parable of the world and its ruin). This bell is giving an example, a proverb, of what the world and its end are going to be. This world and its end, its 'kharab'—meaning destruction. 'Ruins'. 'Mathalad-dunya wa kharabiha'. Now, this bell that is ringing, it is saying, 'La ilaha illallah haqqan haqqan' (There is no god but Allah, truly, truly). This bell is saying it. The Christian is ringing it, but the bell is saying, 'La ilaha illallah haqqan haqqan, sidqan sidqan' (There is no god but Allah, truly, truly, sincerely, sincerely). There is no god but Allah, and this is the truth, and this is a true statement. 'Innad-dunya qad gharratna wa shaghalatna wastahwatna wastaghwatna' (Indeed, the world has deceived us, occupied us, seduced us, and led us astray). What is this world doing? It is deceiving us. The world is deceiving us and keeping us occupied, keeping us busy all the time. That is, either in the forbidden, and if not forbidden, then in useless permissible things. Or before that, either the forbidden or play and amusement, those things that have no purpose—meaning they will not help in the hereafter in any way. They will be of no use; rather, one will be questioned severely about them. You wasted so much of your time in the world—and he is addressing the youth specifically. See, once a person reaches a certain age, they cannot perform the same deeds. Certainly, Allah accepts everyone's worship, but the real service is the service done in youth and early adulthood. That is the true service to the religion. And their worth is greater, their value is higher, and their effects are also longer-lasting. That is, it is an everlasting impression. That is why the Mawla says that acquiring knowledge in youth is like carving on stone. And acquiring knowledge in old age is like writing on water. On waves. Have you ever tried writing on waves? Will anything written on a wave last? No. We think, 'I will study later.' When later? That 'later' is never going to come. Then, at that time, when a person crosses 40, their memory also weakens, they have less strength, they lack the courage, and then the whispers of Satan increase, saying, 'What will you study now? At this old age, what will you study? Forget it.' Satan also whispers this. There are very few individuals who are blessed with the fortune of saying, 'No, no, even if I am old, so what? I must study.' When you wake up, that is your morning; it is never too late. That is one point. The second point is that there is no guarantee of anyone's life. We say we will do this later, but has anyone seen the 'later'? No one has. You see how many young people are dying before your eyes. And this has always been the order of the world. Can anyone say that 40 years, 50 years, or any age is fixed? No. Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says, "Gharatna" (it deceives us)—this world deceives. "Shaghalatna"—it keeps man busy. Look, the deception of the world is strange, isn't it? Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says, "Ya dunya ghurri ghayri" (O world, deceive someone other than me). "Qad tallaqtuki thalathan" (I have divorced you three times). "Irji'i zawjan ghayri" (Go find another husband besides me). Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says, "Irji'i watlubi zawjan ghayri"—go back, and seek another husband besides me. I have no interest in you. The Quran says, "Ya ayyuhal-insanu ma gharraka birabbikal-karim" (O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?). In what deception are you living your life in this world? In what deception? You are continuously disobeying Allah, committing sin after sin, sin after sin. And if not sin, then the other thing is, for example, 'lahw-o-laib' (play and amusement), all those things that "Alhakumut-takathur"—takathur, meaning Allah gave you so much worldly wealth, Allah gave you children, Allah gave you all these things, and all these things have "Alha"—that is, distracted you, meaning they kept you busy with other things. Even if you say these things are not entirely 'haram' (forbidden), at the very least, they distance a person from Allah and the Hereafter. Mawla (a.s.) says this, it is a saying of Mawla (a.s.). And Mawla (a.s.) expects this trust and hope from his Shias. So no one can say, 'No, I am a lover of Ali (a.s.) but I will not listen to this; talk about something else.' If you are a lover of Ali (a.s.), you have to listen to everything that Ali (a.s.) has said. 'Wastahwatna'—wastahwatna means desires, carnal desires. This world pulls a person into its desires. 'Come here.' 'Wastaghwatna'—and this world makes a person 'ghawi' (rebellious). That is, a tyrant, a disobedient one. 'Istaghwatna'—it distances one from Allah. A person becomes so disobedient that they stand up against Allah. Look at the phrases in the supplications. Look at the phrases in Dua-e-Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Look at the phrases in Dua-e-Arafah. What does Imam Hussain (a.s.) say in Dua-e-Arafah? 'O Lord, You bestowed so many favors upon me, but how did I repay Your favors? By disobeying.' Obviously, Imam Hussain (a.s.) is not speaking for himself; he is speaking for us. This is for us. This is the Imam's teaching for us. Because if the Imam (a.s.) does not teach us, then who will? I disobeyed. Anyway, Mawla (a.s.) says that this 'naqus' (bell) is saying: 'Yabnad-dunya mahlan mahlan' (O son of the world, slowly, slowly). You are moving towards the world so fast. 'Yabnad-dunya daqqan daqqa' (O son of the world, with precision). This church bell is saying: O son of the world, with precision, think about what you are doing. 'Yabnad-dunya jaman jamma, tafnad-dunya qarnan qarna' (O son of the world, you collect the world, and the world perishes century by century). We have seen the generation before us; they are gone. Many of our own generation are gone. Some of our children are gone. Now it is our turn; we are fully prepared to leave. But is there really preparation? To what extent is the preparation? 'Jaman jamma, tafnad-dunya qarnan qarna'. Look at what Mawla (a.s.) is saying, that this bell is saying: 'Yafnad-dunya mahlan mahlan, yafnad-dunya daqqan daqqa, yafnad-dunya jaman jamma, tafnad-dunya qarnan qarna. Ma min yawmin yamdi 'anna illa wahiya awha, minna ruknan qad dayya'na daran baqa.' Every day that passes, we become weaker than the day before. We have wasted the eternal home. From the first day, our condition becomes worse. And time is being wasted, it is ending, it is going away. And for that house where we have to go forever, what preparation have we made? 'Daran baqa'—the house that is to remain. The house that will never end. You travel by train, flight, or bus; in any mode of transport, have you ever seen a passenger get off at a bus stop or station and start building a house, collecting goods there? If people ask, 'Brother, why are you doing this?', he says, 'I am just doing it.' 'But brother, the train is moving, you have to go.' 'So what? Stay for 15 minutes, let's at least look around.' Have you ever seen that? When you travel by flight, do you start building a house at the airport? You don't. Man cannot understand this. That this world is meant to be left behind. This world is transient. This world is going to end, and what will remain is in the Hereafter. What does Mawla (a.s.) say? It is strange that a man is about to leave this world, yet he does not spend his wealth. He is a 'bakhil' (miser), he does not spend his wealth. So when he dies, his wealth goes into the hands of his heirs. Now, when it goes to the heirs, the heir will either be obedient to Allah or a sinner. Since he himself did not spend it—he didn't spend it for 'majlis', for 'matam', for 'azadari', for the path of religion, for the mosque, for the 'Imambargah', for helping the 'muminin'—no, none of that. 'I have to save money.' Save for whom? We don't even have the concept of who to save for. Allah is the Provider. Now what will happen? There will be two types of heirs: either obedient or sinful. Now, if the heir is obedient and he takes the money and spends it well, he spends the same money that the deceased left behind. The deceased didn't spend it, but who spent it? On the Day of Judgment, it will be written in his account. So he will say, 'Brother, the money was mine.' It will be said, 'It wasn't yours; it went into his account. You left it for him, so that happened.' Now he will get the reward. So he will be regretful. 'I was a miser in the world. I should have spent it; I would have received the reward in my account.' And the second chance? That the heir is a sinner. And mostly it happens like this, that the children are sinners. It happens very often. Now, what is that child spending it on? On sin. He is using it for sin. Now, on the Day of Judgment, it is seen that you took the money and gave it to him, and he used it for sin. Now you will also get the punishment for this. If you had spent it yourself, you would have received the reward for it. You gave this thing into the hands of a 'fasiq' (transgressor) and 'fajir' (wicked) servant of Allah. For example, if Yazid did whatever he did, will only Yazid get the sin? No. Whoever created Yazid will also get the sin. Not just one; whoever created him, and then whoever created him, and so on. As far as the chain goes. Then he cannot say, 'What can I do? Saqifah created it.' No, no, they will have already received a good beating. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Anyway, Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) explained the whole detail to Harith al-Hamdani. So Harith asked, 'Ya Amir al-Mu'minin, do the Christians know this which you are describing?' He (a.s.) said, 'If they had heard this and known what this bell is saying, they would have stopped taking Christ as a god besides Allah Azza-wa-Jall.' They would have stopped. Anyway, 'Fadhhab ilad-dairani wa qul lahu bihaqqil masihi 'alaika lamma darabta min naqus alal jihatil lati tadribuha.' Harith al-Hamdani went to the main priest there and spoke to him. And he said to him, 'Do you know what this bell says? By the right of Christ upon you, you have to tell me.' So he said, 'No, I don't know.' So Harith says, 'I told him word by word, letter by letter, what Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) had said.' Until Mawla (a.s.) said, 'Qad mitna' (we have died). As soon as he heard it, that Christian priest said, 'By the right of your Prophet, who told you this?' I said, 'The man who was with me yesterday.' He asked, 'And is there any relationship between him and your Prophet?' I said, 'Yes, he is the cousin of our Prophet.' He said, 'By the right of your Prophet, did you hear this from your Prophet?' I said, 'Yes, I heard it from the Prophet.' So that Christian priest embraced Islam. Then he said, 'By God, I have found in the Torah that in the end times there will be a Prophet who will explain what the bell says.' Subhan Allah. What a thing. Recite a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Hazrat Amir (a.s.) in this way... and this was just one example. But for this closeness, for this proximity, it is necessary that we remain connected to Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.), and especially our Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Maintain such a bond, such a connection. And this bond, this connection, should not be merely a formal one—like just reciting it in Qunut, and that's it. No, recite it in Qunut, by all means, do recite it. But along with that, keep remembering your Imam constantly, throughout the day. Look, this Wilayah that we are talking about is a very strange and extraordinary thing. And why is this world a 'Dar-e-Ehtijab' (House of Veils)? What is the name of this world? Dar-e-Ehtijab. Meaning, it is full of veils. In this world, many things are hidden from us. We do not know the reality of things. We do not know, except for those whom Allah has granted Ilm-e-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen). Except for them, no one knows the reality of things. So, this world is a house of veils, and Allah has intentionally made it a house of veils to test people. Now, this state is known only to Allah. The reality of things is known either to Allah or to the Sufara-e-Ilahi (Divine Ambassadors). That is, the envoys of Allah, the ambassadors, they know. Those whom Allah sends into this world as Prophets, Messengers, or successors (Wasi), they know. They possess the knowledge of the unseen, and no one else does. This is for the sake of the test. If the question paper were given in advance, and it were said, 'Here is the answer key, now write it down,' then it would not be a test. A test is when you are given the question paper, but the key is not provided. The key is hidden from you. Similarly, this matter is hidden. This Wilayah is so important that every single breath you take—every single breath—that you take in favor of Wilayah will be of use to you. Believe me. Every single breath. Every single time you say 'Ya Ali', 'Ya Sahib-e-Zaman', 'Ya Mawla-e-Adrikni', every single thing will be of use. Believe me. In other words, if I may submit to your service, immerse yourself in the Wilayah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, because this is what will be of use to you. It will be of use in this world too, but this world is passing anyway. It will be of use in this world as well. It is not that people think Wilayah will only be useful in the hereafter. No, no. It is useful in this world too. And every time you say 'Ya Ali Madad', that many times Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), and especially Hazrat Amir (a.s.), come to your aid. Every time you say 'Ya Baqiyatullah', 'Ya Sahib-e-Zaman', believe me, the Imam-e-Zaman hears you, and the Imam-e-Zaman helps. But this does not mean we should expect the Imam-e-Zaman to just appear and stand before us right now. No. Anyway, this world is passing. People often ask this question—though it is not the topic, I am just mentioning it—that if this is the case, then why did such-and-such Momin face difficulties? Why did such-and-such Imam face difficulties? Why did such-and-such scholar face difficulties? Oh brother, this world is a house of trial. And the Momin, the scholar, and the Imam all know that the more difficulties one faces in this world, the higher their status will be there. Because 'Ad-dunya sijnul Momin wa jannatul kafir' (The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever). And this is our topic today. The second topic was actually a Hadith, let me quickly present it to you so that this matter becomes clear to you. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Allama Majlisi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alaih) has brought an entire chapter in Bihar al-Anwar on this topic: 'Ma yanfa'uhukum minal mawaatin' (In which places will the love of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad be of use). And that they (a.s.) will definitely come at the time of death and thereafter. And that one will be questioned about Wilayah in the grave. Obviously, the one who gets stuck on 'Allah' and 'Rabbi' and doesn't know, well, that's a different matter. So, let's move on. That person is gone. The one who does not recognize the Messenger, well, there is no point in talking about them. The one who does not recognize the Quran, there is no point in talking about them. But the issue will start after that. Just keep the recognition (Ma'rifat) of your Imam as much as possible. As much as possible. And keep performing the Ziyarat of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada. If you don't have the opportunity to go to Karbala, or don't have the time, or due to any difficulty, just remember this one sentence: 'La arifu illal Hussain' (I recognize no one except Hussain). I only recognize Hussain, that's it. 'La arifu illal Hussain'. 'La arifu illa Sahib-e-hazal qubba' (I recognize no one except the owner of this dome). I only know the owner of this dome, I don't recognize anyone else. Believe me. Do not think that these things have no value. This is not a ritual that you are participating in gatherings, mourning; this is not a ritual. Rather, this is a great act of worship and a cause for intercession. Now look at what the Mawla says. Harith al-Hamdani. Amirul Momineen (a.s.)—this Hadith is a very long one, but I have shortened it for your service because time has passed. Let me quickly present two or three sentences of the Hadith to you. He came to the service of the Mawla of the universe, and he was so old that people were supporting him. Harith al-Hamdani, the same one whose Hadith we just mentioned. He came, very old, unable to walk, people were supporting him. The Mawla of the universe asked, 'O Harith, what has brought you here?' Harith, how did you come? Meaning, you are unable to walk, unable to stand, and yet you have come, how did you come? I submitted, 'Hubbi laka ya Amirul Momineen' (My love for you, O Amirul Momineen). Your love has drawn me here. This is your love. He said, 'O Harith, do you love me?' I said, 'Yes, by Allah, O Amirul Momineen, I love you.' The Mawla (a.s.) said, 'Amma Allahu balaghat nafsukal hulqum' (O Harith, when your soul reaches your throat)... When the soul is departing, 'Ra'aitani' (you will see me), 'haisu tuhib' (in the state you desire). You will see me in the state you wish to meet Ali. 'Wa law ra'aitani wa ana azudul rijala anil hauze, tawda gharibatil ibil' (And if you see me driving people away from the Hawd-e-Kawthar, just as stray camels are driven away). 'La ilaha illallah'. 'Law ra'aitani wa ana marrun alas sirat' (If you see me passing over the Sirat). And how I will be passing, 'biliwail hamd baina yaday Rasulillah sallallahu alaihi wa alihi' (with the flag of praise in my hand, walking ahead of the Messenger of Allah). 'Ra'aitani haisu tuhib' (You will see me in the state you desire). O Harith, this thing will truly be of use there. Insha'Allah, the remaining narrations will be presented to you tomorrow. But this gathering, this mourning, this Azadari, this is what will be of great use to you, believe me. This is a sign of love. It is a sign, a sign of love. The people of the world are busy in all the worldly pleasures, but you are wearing black clothes and mourning for Hussain. You are saying 'Ya Hussain, Ya Hussain'. You are beating your chests. You are performing Azadari in various ways. You are reviving the command of Hussain. You are keeping the command of Hussain alive. Although Hussain does not need us, but anyway, since we have been given the opportunity. This is a great honor. So yes, O mourners, it was the 28th of Rajab, and Imam Hussain (a.s.) intended to leave Medina on the 28th of Rajab. Abdullah ibn Sinan, the narrator, says that I happened to reach Medina that same day. When I reached Medina, I saw sadness all around, despair all around, people were worried. I asked, 'O brother, tell me, why are all these people in despair?' Someone replied, 'Are you a traveler?' He said, 'I am a resident of Kufa, I don't know the reason.' So he said, 'Don't you know that the beloved of Medina is leaving Medina? The life of Medina is leaving Medina. Medina is about to become desolate, Medina is about to be ruined.' Abdullah ibn Sinan says that I thought I should also go and see how the people of Medina are leaving, how they are bidding farewell to Medina. I went and stood near the house. I hadn't stood there for long when two youths of Banu Hashim came out and cleared the crowd, saying, 'Move away, move away. The ladies are about to mount, the camels are coming.' The crowd moved away. One by one, the camels came, the ladies mounted, until I saw a sturdy youth come forward, and a lady emerged from the house. That sturdy youth helped her mount. I asked, 'Who is this sturdy youth?' He said, 'This is the orphan of Hassan, Qasim.' And the one he helped mount was his mother, Umm Farwa. Not long after, another lady emerged. A youth came and helped her mount. I asked, 'Who is this youth?' He said, 'This is the son of Hussain, the likeness of the Prophet, Ali Akbar, and he is helping his mother, Umm Laila, mount.' Then another lady emerged, and a youth helped her mount. I asked, 'Who is this youth?' He said, 'This is Abbas, the son of Ali, and Ali's daughter, Umm Kulthum, was mounting.' By now, all the youths of Banu Hashim were busy with the arrangements. Hussain was sitting on a chair, overseeing everything, when suddenly, the curtain of the house was drawn, and a lady emerged. Hussain stood up from his chair. The youths of Banu Hashim came forward. Someone held the camel, someone lifted the curtain of the howdah, someone held the stirrups, and together they helped her mount. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is Bibi Zainab, Ali's eldest daughter Zainab.' When all the ladies had boarded and the caravan of camels began to move, Hussain stood up once and said, 'Ya Abbas, Abbas, steady your feet. O Abbas, now bring my mount, now bring my ride.' The obedient brother brought the mount and helped Imam Hussain (a.s.) to mount. The Imam mounted, the ride moved forward, the horse moved forward. I will say with folded hands, 'O Abbas-e-Alamdar, this is 28th Rajab and this is Medina; you have helped him mount, but on the day of Ashura, when Hussain will turn towards the camp and say, "Hayya-e-Baqi-ul-Khattam-o-Jawadi, ya Afzal-e-Safar, wa ya Fursan-e-Hijaz, O my lions, O my brave ones, Ali-o-Baqi-ul-Khattam-o-Jawadi, who among you will help me mount?" But there will be no answer from the side of the tents. Yes, the curtain of the tent will be pulled back, Zainab will come out. "Brother, do not worry, Zainab is still alive, Zainab will help you mount again." Now Hussain will mount, but this was the time for riding. When Hussain falls slightly, at that moment Fatima-e-Zahra will come to the battlefield of Karbala.' 'Come my son, come my son, I have arrived.' 'Wah Hussainah, wah Mazlumah, wah Shahidah.' 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant righteous and virtuous children to those who are childless. Grant complete and swift recovery to those who are ill. O Lord, return those who are far from their homeland to their homes safe and sound. O Lord, protect the Ulema, the high-ranking scholars, and the Maraje-e-Izam. Protect the Atabat-e-Aliyat and the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. O Lord, grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and Aali-Muhammad in this world and their intercession in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.
