chapters.title: The Purity of Birth and Love for Ali
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the fundamental Shia belief that love for Imam Ali (a.s.) is a definitive sign of pure birth, while hatred toward him indicates impurity.

chapters.title: Signs of Those Who Cannot Love Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: Imam Ali (a.s.) identifies specific character traits, such as lack of honor (ghayrah), that prevent individuals from truly loving the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Importance of Hijab and Ghayrah
chapters.summary: Imam Ali (a.s.) emphasizes the necessity of modesty and honor, condemning those who lack the sense of shame regarding the public display of their womenfolk.

chapters.title: The Obligation of Nahy an al-Munkar
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the duty of forbidding evil, explaining that indecency has collective consequences and that true followers of the Ahl al-Bayt must maintain modesty and honor.

chapters.title: The Noble Lineage of the Shia
chapters.summary: Citing Ibn Idris al-Hilli, the lecture highlights that a defining virtue of the Shia is their pure and noble lineage, free from the influence of immorality.

chapters.title: The Parable of the World
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates an incident where Imam Ali (a.s.) explains to Harith al-Hamdani that the ringing of a church bell serves as a reminder of the world's deceptive and transient nature.

chapters.title: The Urgency of Seeking Knowledge
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that acquiring knowledge in youth is permanent, while delaying it leads to missed opportunities and spiritual deception.

chapters.title: The Deceptive Nature of the World
chapters.summary: Drawing on the teachings of Imam Ali (a.s.), the lecture warns against being distracted by worldly wealth and the false sense of security regarding one's lifespan.

chapters.title: The Consequences of Worldly Attachment
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the folly of hoarding wealth instead of spending it in the path of Allah, noting how heirs may use it for either good or sin.

chapters.title: The Symbolic Meaning of the Church Bell
chapters.summary: A historical account of Imam Ali (a.s.) explaining the true meaning of a church bell's toll leads a Christian priest to embrace Islam.

chapters.title: The Significance of Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that Wilayah is a hidden test and a vital source of spiritual support in this world and the hereafter.

chapters.title: The Value of Ma'rifat and Azadari
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the importance of recognizing the Imam and the intercessory power of mourning for Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Promise of Amirul Momineen
chapters.summary: A narration of Harith al-Hamdani illustrates that Imam Ali will be present to assist his followers at the time of death and on the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: The Departure from Medina
chapters.summary: A historical account of Imam Hussain's departure from Medina, highlighting the devotion of his family and the tragic foreshadowing of Karbala.

title: EP02 | Ghadeer Aur Quran | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 2024💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound connection between the event of Ghadir Khumm and the Holy Quran, emphasizing that the appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the successor was a divine command rather than a personal choice. It examines the behavior of hypocrites who outwardly pledged allegiance while harboring internal opposition, drawing parallels to Quranic verses regarding spiritual disease and the rejection of divine authority. The session also highlights the metaphysical status of the Imam, including his Wilayah al-Takwiniyyah, and underscores the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt as established by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).
content:
TSR presents. [Music] ... In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. "O Allah, be for Your representative, [the Hujjah], son of Al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian..." ... [Music] I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O our master, help us. If you haven't subscribed to our channel yet, subscribe now and don't forget to press the bell icon. The quiz link is now live, which is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you haven't registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are present in the discussion. You only need to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the series. Therefore, do not rush to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. For the quiz... ...there is no prize. To win the quiz prize, it is only necessary that all the answers to the questions must be correct. From among all those who answer all the questions correctly, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names do not appear in today's winners, or if they missed any episode, do not need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the pilgrimage (Ziyarat) of Iraq, will be chosen from those who have answered all the questions correctly in all four episodes, and that mega winner will be selected in our special episode, Insha'Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O my master, help us, do not leave us. Respected listeners and esteemed viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Praise be to Allah Who made us among those who hold fast to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). We are once again present in your service with the second episode of 'Ghadir: The Divine Covenant', and we welcome you all to today's episode. ...welcome you all to today's episode. Respected brothers, the topic of today's episode is a highly important one, which is related to Ghadir and the Quran. Respected brothers, the proclamation of Ghadir is such a Quranic reality that to command its proclamation, a Quranic verse was revealed to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), which is famously known as the Verse of Tabligh (Ayat al-Tabligh), in which the Lord of Honor says: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people.' [Quran 5:67] Not only this, but when the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) conveyed the proclamation of Ghadir, after that, the verse of the completion of religion was revealed, in which the Lord of Honor says: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.' [Quran 5:3] And respected brothers, if anyone denied this proclamation of Ghadir or objected to it, then... ...denied it or objected to it, a Quranic verse was revealed for them as well. A Quranic verse was revealed in condemnation, in which the Lord of Honor says: 'A petitioner asked for a punishment as bound to happen.' [Quran 70:1] So, respected viewers, these are the well-known verses that we repeatedly hear in our gatherings (Majalis) and lectures. So, are these the only verses related to Ghadir, or has Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, revealed other verses in the Holy Quran that relate to Ghadir? Our topic today, 'Ghadir and the Quran', is about this very subject, where we will see whether there are other verses in the Holy Quran regarding Ghadir or not. For this, we have in our gathering our dear brother, Janab Muhammad Abbas Patel Sahab. Let us request him to shed more light on this topic. Abbas Bhai, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. / Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah, Gulzar Bhai. First of all, I congratulate you. Many congratulations on Eid al-Akbar (Eid al-Ghadir), and I congratulate all the viewers on Eid al-Akbar, and present these congratulations to the Imam of our Time (a.t.f.s.). Gulzar Bhai, as far as the Quranic verses are concerned, it is not just these three verses; rather, there are many other verses in the Holy Quran related to Ghadir. One group or category of these verses is the one that the Holy Prophet himself... ...one category of verses is the one that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself included in the Sermon of Ghadir. These are about more than 100 verses that are present in the Sermon of Ghadir. That is, in the sermon that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) delivered at Ghadir, he recited more than 100 verses; more than 100 verses are present in it. So, this is one group of verses which are present in the Sermon of Ghadir itself. Apart from this, the core subject of Ghadir, which is the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)—there are numerous verses in the Holy Quran regarding the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). But today, we will only discuss those verses that directly relate to the incident of Ghadir and the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Our topic today is also the same: which verses in the Holy Quran relate directly to the event of Ghadir and also to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)? We will examine those verses, Insha'Allah. The first set of verses is from Surah al-Baqarah, verses 8 to 16, which are regarding the hypocrites (Munafiqeen). Baqarah 8 to 16, yes, 8 to 16, which are about the hypocrites. These verses begin like this: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.' [Quran 2:8] It starts from here and the sequence continues. That is, the translation of these verses... ...the sequence continues. That is, the translation of these verses is like this: 'Among the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but Allah says they are not believers.' They are not believers, and what they are expressing with their tongues is contrary to the belief that lies in their hearts. Meaning, they were absolute hypocrites; they did not believe from their hearts. They would testify with their tongues that they believed, but in their hearts, they had hatred (bughz) for the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Yes, there was hatred in their hearts, while they expressed belief with their tongues. They were called hypocrites. Anyway, in the commentary (Tafsir) of these verses, in Tafsir al-Imam (a.s.), there is a narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) raised the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) on his hands at Ghadir—that famous and well-known occasion of Ghadir where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) raised the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) on his hands—at that time, the Prophet asked the people, 'State my lineage (nasab).' That is, the Prophet asked the crowd to state his lineage. So, the people said, 'You are Muhammad, son of Abdullah, son of Abdul Muttalib, son of Hashim, son of Abd Manaf,' thus stating his lineage. Then the Prophet took a testimony from them, asking, 'Do I not have more authority (Wilayah) over you than your own selves?' ...'Do I not have more authority over you than your own selves?' Yes. Everyone said, 'Qalu Bala' (They said, 'Yes, indeed'). Everyone said, 'Why not, indeed, O Messenger of Allah!' Then the Prophet looked towards the sky and said, 'O Allah, bear witness,' and the Prophet repeated this three times—taking this testimony and making Allah a witness, 'O Allah, bear witness to their testimony.' And after that, the Prophet recited 'Man Kuntu Mawlahu fa hadha Aliyyun Mawlahu' and prayed to Allah. After that, the Prophet made the hypocrites stand up one by one, saying, 'Come and pledge allegiance (Bay'ah) to the Commander of the Faithful. Address Ali (a.s.) as "Amirul Mu'minin" (Commander of the Faithful) and pledge allegiance to him.' Under this title, one by one, the first hypocrite came and pledged allegiance. The second hypocrite came and pledged allegiance. The third hypocrite came and pledged allegiance. And after that, the entire group of hypocrites, which included nine other people, were made to stand by the Prophet, and one by one, he made everyone pledge allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), addressing him as 'Amirul Mu'minin'. And when this allegiance was completed, these hypocrites gathered together. They harbored hatred in their hearts against the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). They firmly resolved that they would rebel against the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and would not let this Imamate remain with Ali (a.s.). They thought, 'As soon as the Prophet closes his eyes (passes away), we will not let this Imamate reach Ali (a.s.).' ...'As soon as he passes away, we will not let this Imamate reach Ali (a.s.).' Meaning, 'We will not let this Imamate go to its rightful place.' These people were planning this at Ghadir. Yes, this was their firm resolve. And regarding this resolve of theirs, Allah said in the Holy Quran: '...but they are not believers.' They are saying 'We believe,' but they are not believers. That is, regarding the allegiance they pledged, Allah is saying in this verse that these people are hypocrites; they do not believe from within. Yes. Indeed, the verse is like this: 'O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah," Who commanded you to appoint Ali as the Imam and leader...' They do not believe in that command, in that belief. The Messenger of Allah also knew. Yes, the Messenger of Allah knew. Then after this, Allah says in the next verse: 'They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive [it] not.' [Quran 2:9] They want to deceive Allah and the believers by outwardly declaring their acceptance of the Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) with their tongues. ...to the believers. Allah says that they are not deceiving anyone but themselves, and they do not even realize that they are deceiving themselves by outwardly showing faith while their hearts are filled with hypocrisy. Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s.) says: 'So Allah informed the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) about what they plotted against Ali (a.s.) and their evil plans.' Allah informed the Prophet about what was in their hearts regarding Ali (a.s.) and what they were uttering with their tongues. Whatever was in their hearts, Allah told the Messenger of Allah. Allah informed the Prophet of this, and the Messenger of Allah called them and reprimanded them severely, saying, 'What you are doing is only deceiving yourselves, and you do not even realize that you are deceiving yourselves.' Then, one after another, they began to express false faith, and the words they used are noteworthy. The first one said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not believe in anything else the way I believe in this allegiance (Bay'ah). And I hope that because of this allegiance, Allah will admit me into Paradise.' ...will do, and Allah will grant me the best abode in Paradise on account of this allegiance (bay'ah). That is, they are describing the actual importance of Wilayah. Even though these hypocrites are saying this hypocritically, it is the reality of Wilayah; it is the truth that they have uttered with their tongues out of hypocrisy, but Allah made manifest through their tongues the status and glory of Wilayah. And the second one said, 'O Messenger of Allah, may my parents be sacrificed for you! O Messenger of Allah, I do not believe that I can enter Paradise and find salvation from the fire of Hell except through this allegiance.' That is, without this allegiance, I cannot enter Paradise, and without this allegiance, I cannot escape the fire of Hell. 'By Allah, if I break it...' meaning, 'By Allah, if I break this allegiance, I will never be happy.' These were the words of the second one. 'And even if the space from the earth to the Throne (Arsh) were filled with gold for me, even then I would not be pleased with this wealth to break it.' These are the words of the second one. And the third one is saying, 'O Messenger of Allah, I became so happy after pledging this allegiance, my joy and delight knew no bounds. And I hope that Allah... That is, 'I hope that Allah will admit me into Paradise. I will attain Allah's pleasure on account of this allegiance. And even if...'—this is a very astonishing sentence—'...even if the sins of the entire universe were laden upon my shoulders, all these sins would still be forgiven if I acknowledge this allegiance.' What a statement! 'This is what my belief says,' whereas that was not his belief. And they began to swear oaths and invoke curses, saying, 'Accursed be whoever brought this news to you; they have brought you false news.' In this way, these people were trying to deceive. Brother, even if they were uttering these sentences in hypocrisy, when someone speaks to another in hypocrisy, they say things that will please the other person. In hypocrisy, only those things are said that would make the person pleased and happy. This means that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was indeed pleased with all these statements, and they were repeating those very sentences before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in hypocrisy. This shows that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had made manifest to them the status of Wilayah—that is, the status of accepting this Wilayah. They knew which words pleased the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Yes, indeed. But they did not know that Allah had informed the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) about what was in their hearts, and this... ...is what is in their hearts. The Quranic verse points to this: 'In their hearts is a disease' [2:10]—meaning a sickness in their souls—'so Allah has increased their disease, and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie.' On this basis, because they were denying the Imamah and the position of Imamah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), planning to prevent this position from reaching Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Allah has promised a painful punishment for them. The Imam (a.s.) says that when these people related this to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and spoke these words before him, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left them to their outward appearance and left their inner state to Allah. But Jibra'il was not pleased with this, or rather, Allah was not pleased with this. But Jibra'il came to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'O Muhammad, indeed Allah sends peace upon you and says: Expel them, these sick ones...' ...saying, 'Expel them, these sick ones'—meaning these rebellious people, expel them. And those about whom you have been informed regarding what is hidden in their hearts concerning this announcement about Ali (a.s.), expel them and manifest before them the glory and greatness of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). They have no idea of the Wilayah that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) has been granted, to what level this Wilayah reaches—what we call Wilayah al-Takwiniyyah (existential/cosmic authority). They have no idea of its status. Manifest to them what kind of Wilayah this is that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) has been granted.' So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and explained the entire matter to him, and then said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, when we reach such-and-such mountain, pray to Allah by invoking the sake of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). And on account of your prayer, Allah will transform these mountains. They will change in whatever way you wish.' And the hadith continues: when they reached the outskirts of Medina, [the Prophet said], 'O Ali, indeed Allah has commanded them to aid and assist you...' 'Indeed, Allah has commanded these mountains to aid you, assist you, become obedient to you, and enter your service.' Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) brought these hypocrites out. He took them towards the mountains outside Medina and said, 'If you obey Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and accept this Wilayah, it is better for you. But if you oppose this Wilayah and Imamah, then an eternal punishment in Hell is prepared for you. Very soon, you will be shown a glimpse of it.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to them, and then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Ali, ask your Lord through the sake of Muhammad and his pure, immaculate Progeny.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) called upon Allah through this sake, and the mountains began to respond. The mountains called out, 'O Ali, O Successor (Wasi) of the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds!' These hypocrites were watching the mountain respond to Amir al-Mu'minin's call in this manner, saying, 'O Ali, O Successor of the Messenger!' The very thing these people were denying, the mountain was acknowledging and bearing witness to. It was not just this... ...bearing witness to it. It wasn't just that an announcement was made to them; they were also being shown through miracles what the status of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is. Yes, indeed. And this mountain was saying, 'O Ali, Allah has prepared us for you, and whenever you wish to spend, call upon us, we are at your service.' That is, these mountains were not just stone; as they went forward, one after another, their substance was transformed. It turned entirely into gold. That is, it was made of stone, but Allah gave Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) such Wilayah that he could change the substance of this mountain from stone to gold. The mountain turned into gold. And before that, it had turned into silver. The silver mountain said, as in the sentence above, 'Spend us however you wish. Whenever you command, we are ready.' Then it turned into gold, and the golden mountain said the same: 'Spend us however you wish. Call upon us, we are at your service.' What authority Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) possesses! He can change whatever he wants, however he wants. This is Wilayah al-Takwiniyyah. Allah gave them this Wilayah to change the substance of any object. Then this mountain turned into musk and ambergris... ...then this mountain turned into musk, ambergris, and various other fragrances, and into jewels, gems, and rubies. Every time its substance changed into a new form, it repeated the same testimony that the previous mountain had repeated. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) addressed Ali (a.s.) saying, 'O Ali, now call upon these trees around these mountains, change their substance, and command them, and they will be transformed.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) prayed to Allah, and when he prayed and all these things were transformed, the hadith describes these soldiers: each tree that transformed into a soldier was stronger than ten thousand men. Then all these things—the entire mountain—became filled with soldiers, lions, leopards, and dragons, and those soldiers were extremely powerful and fully armed. Brother, at the time of Ghadir... ...fully armed. Brother, these miracles were being shown at the event of Ghadir. Yes, these miracles and this power were being shown in response to the denial of Ghadir. Several miracles occurred around Ghadir, like the stone that fell from the sky upon Harith, which was also a miracle. That was also a miracle. And viewers must indeed be hearing about this miracle for the very first time, as it is rarely mentioned that these miracles were shown at the location of Ghadir. And the miracle does not end here. After that, the entire mountain was filled with these things. Surely, that group of hypocrites must have been terrified and shaken upon seeing this power. But it does not end here. All of them—the lions, leopards, dragons, and soldiers—began to bear witness and call out to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), 'O Ali, O Successor of the Messenger, we are all subjugated to you, ready for you. Just command us, we are ready. Whenever you command, we will arrive to assist you.' Then these things spoke further with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and said, 'O Ali, O Successor of the Messenger, indeed you have a magnificent status near Allah... ...such that if you command this entire universe to turn into a single bag, and this bag be filled with jewels, Allah would do it. That is, He would gather the entire universe into a bag for you. And if you command the sky, it will come down for you; the sky would do this. And if you command the earth, it will carry you up to the sky; it would do this for you. And if you command the salty water of the entire ocean, it will turn into sweet water and into various kinds of syrups, or into oil. Today, major powers take pride in their oil, but the Imam (a.s.) can change all these things if he wishes—he can turn the entire ocean's water into oil if he wishes. And if you command this ocean to freeze and stop, it will freeze and turn into land. Then these things—the mountain and the creations of Allah around it—began to reassure Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), saying, 'Do not let the rebellion of these rebels grieve you... ...'Do not let the rebellion of these rebels grieve you, nor let their opposition sadden you, O Amir al-Mu'minin. Very soon, the world will slip from their hands as if they were never in the world at all. This is how they will depart from the world. And when they enter the Hereafter, they will feel as if they never possessed anything at all. O Ali, the One Who has given them respite despite their disbelief, transgression, and rebellion against your obedience, is the same One Who gave respite to Pharaoh the tyrant, and to Nimrod who claimed divinity, and to the leader of them all, Iblis, the leader of misguidance. This same God has given respite to Iblis as well.' Brother Abbas, this is indeed a very important point here, that when this conversation is taking place, Allah knows about the hypocrites and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) also knows that they are acting in this manner. The Messenger of Allah also knows that they are planning in this manner, harboring hatred for Hazrat Ali (a.s.) in their hearts, and they are planning that they will never let him become the Caliph. And despite this, they are still on the earth, remaining. So it is being stated that this is a respite from Allah, which He also gave to Pharaoh, and before him, to the oppressive Satan. Indeed. So in this way, there is a respite, and as was also stated later, in the Hereafter, it will be for them as if the world never existed for them. Correct. And for the believers, this is a place of admonition here, as you stated: 'Ma khalaqtum lil-fana' (You were not created for annihilation), neither you nor these people were created for this transient world, 'bal khalaqtum lil-baqa' (but you were created for the eternal abode), you were created for the eternal abode, 'wa innama tantaqiluna min darin ila darin' (and you will only migrate from one abode to another), moving from one house to another. Yes, but after seeing all this, it will only increase their disease. The verse of Surah Al-Baqarah states: 'Fazada...' (He increased...). They did not just harbor hatred for Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.); that is, their issue was not just with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), but they also could not tolerate the merits of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) mentioned in the Quran. '...and indeed, Allah has made Himself a surety over you.' 'Indeed, Allah knows what you do.' This will be the status of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) on the Sirat, on the Sirat. That is, when you asked if this is from Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger guaranteed that indeed, this is from Allah and His Messenger, after that, do not break your covenant once you have known where this command is coming from. Let us move to the next verse, which is verses 79 and 80 of Surah Az-Zukhruf: 'Or have they devised a plan? But indeed, We are planning.' Surah Az-Zukhruf, verses 79 and 80, yes. 'Yes, and Our messengers are with them writing them down.' They record everything. They thought—meaning, the hypocrites thought that... ...they thought—meaning, the hypocrites thought that Allah is not aware of the whispering they do, whereas even Allah's angels record it. The meaning of the verses is that if you make any plans, Allah knows how to plan better than that, and whatever whispering you do among yourselves, whispering in each other's ears, Allah is aware of that too. Correct, Allah is aware of that too. And these things they were discussing were plans against the Wilayah. They were planning to usurp this Wilayah from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). So, Brother Gulzar, in the exegesis of this verse, it is narrated by Abdullah ibn Abbas from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that the Prophet took the pledge of the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) from us twice. The first time was when the Prophet asked, 'Do you know who my caliph is after me?' The people replied, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Surah al-Nasr, which according to the order of revelation is considered to be the last Surah revealed. The very last Surah that was revealed is Surah al-Nasr. And this entire Surah was revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wida). Under this Surah, regarding its first verse, the narration we find says: 'It was revealed during Hajjat al-Wida.' This Surah was revealed in Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'My soul has been forewarned of my death' (meaning, 'I have been informed of my departure'). And then, in Masjid al-Khaif, the Prophet gathered the people and began to advise them. And then the Prophet said, 'I am not gesturing like this (joining the index and middle finger, where one is longer than the other), but rather like this (joining the two index fingers).' excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological significance of Fadak, framing it as a pivotal struggle for the rights and legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt. And the Imam wanted to show that actually these boundaries were the boundaries of the Islamic government of that time. Yes. So, in fact, the Imam wanted to say that the position you are sitting on is usurped. And the Imam came and demanded not just Fadak, but Wilayah and Imamat. Whoever—as the sentence here goes—whoever snatched Fadak initiated an innovation (bid'ah) in the prophetic law. Right? Because Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) presented many verses in the Quran as evidence that prophets do leave inheritance. So, we do not understand this stance of Muslims: that the one who snatches the right is also 'rightly guided', the one who returns the right is also 'rightly guided', and the one whose right was snatched is also 'rightly guided'. One thing is certain from this: these protests that kept happening had an impact on the oppressors of every era, but this has to end somewhere, and not just in this world, but it is certain that on the Day of Judgment, this will be decided. Indeed. So now the question arises: where does an ordinary Muslim find themselves standing on this issue on the Day of Judgment? I seek refuge... ...with Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. Yes, viewers, today in this final episode, the topic of our discussion is 'Fadak and Our Responsibility', to discuss which in detail, our dear brother, Janab Kazim Sahib, is present with us. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. Kazim Bhai, when it is proven that this is the right of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and it is the right of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and this right was usurped from them in an oppressive manner, did the governments that came later—the Umayyads, the Abbasids—ever realize that this was the right of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) which was usurped from them? If you look at history after the martyrdom of Ali (a.s.) or the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), you will see that from that era, protests regarding Fadak were continuously happening. The Princess herself protested regarding Fadak, other Infallibles (a.s.) made demands regarding this, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) himself, in that era, in the very beginning after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah... ...in the early period after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, when the Princess made this demand, probably even before that, yes, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) himself demanded Fadak from the ruler of that time, stating that 'this is our right and this is the right of the Princess (s.a.)'. Now, because of that embarrassment—since we will explain and present to the viewers how Ali (a.s.) demanded Fadak before the ruler of Medina and how he embarrassed him—because of that embarrassment, in the subsequent periods, whether it was the Umayyad era or the Abbasid era, its effects were continuously visible in every age. The demand made by Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) and the other proofs she presented regarding this land, regarding this Fadak, its effects were continuously seen in every era. Yes. So, to present to the viewers, now that the topic has come up, let us connect it a bit from the early era and move towards the rulers of the Umayyads and Abbasids. Yes. So, in the very beginning, when the usurpers usurped Fadak from Hazrat Zahra (s.a.), Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)—this incident is fully present in our books. And in the book 'Al-Ihtijaj', Allamah Tabarsi narrates this incident. This tradition is narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that when the ruler of Medina refused to give Fadak to Hazrat Zahra (s.a.)... ...refused to give Fadak to Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) at that time, and her appointed administrators who were present in Fadak were removed. At that time, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) himself personally entered the mosque. The ruler of the time was present, and a crowd of Muhajirun had gathered there, and a crowd of Ansar was also formally present inside that mosque, the Prophet's Mosque, when Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) went to present this demand. Yes, and then Ali (a.s.) took his name and asked him, 'Why did you deprive the Princess of her right?' And then the sentence after that, in which Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says, '...which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had granted to her.' This means it was the property of the Princess, the proof of which is shown here by the action of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had given it to Hazrat Zahra. So, if you—alright, that property which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself had given—if you are taking that thing back, then you are directly contradicting the action of the Prophet. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) immediately stated this sentence here, and then said, '...and it has been in her possession for two years.' Alright, it is not that it was just a few moments or a few days ago, but for two years... ...for two years, Hazrat Zahra's (s.a.) administrators and servants were present there. After this, the ruler of the time says, 'This property, this Fadak, is the property of the Muslims, and if Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) brings just witnesses for her claim, then she has a right to this. She has a right to this Fadak. Otherwise, she has no right to it.' Meaning, what was he demanding from Janabe Zahra (s.a.) there? Proof of her ownership. 'Claim' meaning, if it is your property, then prove your claim. On that, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says to him, taking his name, 'You do not judge in our case as you judge in the case of other Muslims.' Now, he says nervously, 'No, no, it is not like that.' Alright. On that, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) corners him and says, 'Tell me, if the Muslims possess something, and I claim that thing—if the Muslims have something in their possession and I come and tell you that this is my thing—from whom will you demand the proof, the evidence, the argument? Will you ask me, or will you ask the Muslims? If it is in the possession of the Muslims, from whom will you ask?' To which the ruler of the time immediately says, 'No, O Ali, we would ask you.' Ali, they will ask you for it. Right? Because you are presenting a claim. Yes, you are presenting a claim, and it is the property of Muslims. Now, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) then says to him, 'Fa-dhalika fi yadi shay'un...' [So if something is in my possession...] '...fi Muslim' [among Muslims], right, 'and Muslims claim it, would you ask me for proof of that property?' Now, here Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) completed the entire argument (hujjah) with this sentence. Because here, if the viewers remember, and if you also remember, in the previous episode, Brother Ahsan discussed the 'Rule of Possession' (Qaydah-e-Yad) in great detail. Regarding that, it is the responsibility of the claimant (mudda'i) to present proof of their claim, correct? 'Aimmat al-dalalah', those who are the leaders of misguidance. 'Wa qa'adat al-jawr', and those who were the leaders and guides of oppression and tyranny—dissociation from them is obligatory. Disassociation (Bara'at) is also obligatory from those who were the leaders and guides of oppression and tyranny. Disassociation is obligatory from all of them, from the first to the last. To express this is the responsibility of the Shias; this is the responsibility of the Shias in this era, the era of Occultation (Ghaybah). Right? That disassociation is obligatory from all those people who unleashed mountains of oppression upon the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). And then, the Mawla does not remain silent here. Then Mawla says, 'and from the most wretched of the first and the last' (wa ashqa al-awwalina wal-akhirin), and disassociation is also obligatory from the most wretched person of both eras. And among them, he names the one who killed the she-camel of the nation of Thamud. And who was the second? The killer of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), that wretched person, that wretched person who killed Hazrat Amir (a.s.); disassociation from them is also obligatory. Meaning, the Imam (a.s.) is mentioning them one by one in this Hadith, stating that you must disassociate from this one, disassociate from that one, and disassociate from them. And then Mawla states, 'and from all the killers of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)' (wa jami' qatalat Ahl al-Bayt), disassociation is also obligatory from all the killers of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Now, this first part was where Mawla is urging the Shias of the time towards Tabarra (disassociation), that there should never be any corner of love in a person's heart for those who showed enmity towards them (a.s.). Now here, the Imam (a.s.) states, 'And the love (Wilayah) of those believers is obligatory who did not change...' He states, 'And the love (Wilayah) of those believers is obligatory who did not change [the teachings of] the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).' And now we are talking about those believers who are the embodiment of 'peace to those who are at peace with you' (silmun liman salamakum), indeed, right? That friendship/allegiance (Wilayah) is obligatory with those believers, Mawla is saying, who did not alter or change the religion after their Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Yes, friendship with those who did not change the religion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Or if we explain it this way: those who did not anger Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) or those who stood against the foundation of oppression—those who laid the foundation of oppression upon the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Yes, their list is now coming up here, who they are. Now, in that, Mawla says that loving them is obligatory (wajibatun). Yes, right. And then Mawla names them one by one, and here Mawla lists the names of 13 individuals, saying, 'such as...' Who are they? Salman al-Farsi. Here, Janab-e-Salman al-Muhammadi is being mentioned. And after that, Janab-e-Abu Dharr al-Ghifari was mentioned. And after that, whose name was taken? Miqdad al-Kindi. The name of Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi was taken. And after that, Ammar ibn Yasir was mentioned. After that, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari was mentioned. After that, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman al-Yamani was mentioned. After that, Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan... ...narrated. After that, he mentioned Abu'l-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan. After that, he mentioned Sahl ibn Hunayf. After that, the Mawla (a.s.) said, 'and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari', okay. After that, the Mawla (a.s.) said, 'and Abdullah ibn Samit', and then after that, the Mawla (a.s.) mentioned Ubadah ibn al-Samit. And then after that, Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, who was 'Dhu'sh-Shahadatayn' (the possessor of two testimonies). The Mawla (a.s.) mentioned Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. And then after that, the Mawla (a.s.) says, after naming these 13 individuals who were very steadfast in their love for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)—after taking their names, the Mawla (a.s.) reaches the final part of this narration, the narration of al-Khisal, and the Mawla (a.s.) says: 'Wa man nahaja nahjahum wa fa'ala mithla fi'lihim' (And whoever follows their path—meaning the path of these 13 individuals—and acts like them, and performs actions like theirs), 'Wilayatuhu li-atba'ihim wal-muhtadina bi-hudahum wajibah' (then the Wilayah for their followers and those guided by their guidance is obligatory), okay, and to obtain guidance from them and friendship with them is what? It is obligatory, obligatory. Meaning, here the Mawla (a.s.) has explained both aspects in this Hadith: that Bara'at (disassociation) is highly obligatory, and Wilayah (allegiance) is also obligatory, and loving those who are the friends of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) is also obligatory. So, our responsibility as a Shia is a very big responsibility... ...as a Shia, it is a very big responsibility regarding Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) that we express Bara'at (disassociation) from those who perpetrated oppressions against the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and especially those who inflicted calamities and oppressions upon Hazrat Zahra (s.a.). Absolutely. And I am reminded of a couplet which I would like to present to the viewers: 'Whatever oppressions were committed against the Prophet's daughter, we will not let the people of the world forget them.' This is a couplet by Jamdabadi: 'We will not let the people of the world forget.' Whosoever was involved in the oppression of Hazrat Zahra (s.a.), we will expose those oppressions, and we will unveil the faces of those who perpetrated the oppression, Insha'Allah. Thank you very much, Brother Kazim. And finally, a few questions that every Muslim must answer for themselves individually: Number one: Have I done any such deed due to which Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.) would become angry with me, making it impossible for me to attain Paradise? Number two: Do I support those individuals who angered Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.)? And number three: What can I do to please Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.)? May Allah make us among those... What can I do for her? May Allah include us among those who cause the pleasure of Hazrat Fatima-tuz-Zahra (s.a.) and not her anger. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Quran-e-Majeed Ki Ta'weel Kaun Jaanta Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the interpretation of the Quranic verse regarding 'Muhkamat' (fundamental) and 'Mutashabihat' (allegorical) verses. He highlights how the placement of a mandatory pause (waqf-e-lazim) by later scholars has been used to exclude the Ahlulbayt from possessing the true knowledge of the Quran. The lecture emphasizes that, according to the traditions of the Imams, the Ahlulbayt are indeed those 'firmly grounded in knowledge' who possess the interpretation of the allegorical verses.
content:
Allah says: {He it is Who has sent down to thee the Book: In it are verses basic or fundamental (of established meaning); they are the foundation of the Book: others are allegorical.} Meaning, He is the One who revealed the Book to you, in which some verses are 'Muhkamat' (fundamental), which are the Mother of the Book, and others are 'Mutashabihat' (allegorical). {But those in whose hearts is perversity}—perversity in interpretation means doubt; those whose hearts contain doubt, they lack certainty and faith—{they follow that part thereof that is allegorical}, seeking to create discord and seeking to interpret them according to their own desires. Yet Allah says regarding their interpretation: {But no one knows its true meanings except Allah and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge.} Now, observe here: the enemies performed a great act of distortion. They placed a small 'meem' (م) above the word 'Allah', indicating a 'waqf-e-lazim' (mandatory pause), implying that no one knows the interpretation except Allah, and then they separated {and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge} from Allah. They claimed this 'waw' (and) is 'istinaf' (the start of a new sentence). They did not connect it to Allah, suggesting that no one knows the interpretation except Allah, and then separately, those grounded in knowledge... This 'meem' was not in the original revelation; it was added later. {And those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in the Book; the whole of it is from our Lord.'} This is not part of the Quran; it was added in the 'qira'at' (recitation style). Remember, this is not about the distortion of the Quran itself, but about the style of recitation. There should be no misunderstanding that we are talking about 'tahrif' (alteration of the text). This was a change made by the enemies in the style of reading, which is why I am repeating it so the matter is clear: {No one knows its interpretation except Allah} and then they added {and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say...}. Firstly, there is no apparent connection between these two, and secondly, who placed this 'meem' (mandatory pause) there? When did this come about? And thirdly, when we refer to the traditions of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) regarding the interpretation of this verse, we see that there are at least ten to fifteen hadiths where, when the Imam (a.s.) recited this verse, he recited it as: {And no one knows its interpretation except Allah and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge}. The Imam says: 'By God, we are those firmly grounded in knowledge. We are those who are immersed in knowledge, we are those who are deeply rooted in it. We know its interpretation; we are aware of the interpretation of the allegorical verses of the Quran.'
The Quran contains both fundamental (Muhkamat) and allegorical (Mutashabihat) verses.
The placement of a 'meem' (mandatory pause) in the verse 3:7 is a later addition that alters the intended meaning.
The pause was used to separate 'Allah' from 'those firmly grounded in knowledge'.
The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the ones who are truly 'firmly grounded in knowledge'.
Imams have explicitly stated in multiple traditions that they know the interpretation of the allegorical verses.
The discussion focuses on the style of recitation and interpretation, not the alteration of the Quranic text itself.

title: Ep#3: Kya Janasheen-e-Rasool (s.a.w.a ) Ka Hona Zaroori Hai?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the theological necessity of a successor (Janasheen) to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), arguing that divine guidance must remain continuous and infallible. Drawing from Quranic history, such as the appointment of Aaron as Moses's successor, the speaker demonstrates that the selection of a divine guide is exclusively Allah's prerogative. The lecture highlights logical contradictions in historical caliphate successions and references Sunni sources to validate the early designation of Imam Ali. Ultimately, it asserts that adhering to the covenant of Ghadir Khumm and recognizing a divinely appointed leader is essential to resolving theological disputes and maintaining unity within the Ummah.
content:
The initial part contains some unclear audio transcription noise. ... Therefore, it is better to address the issue that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed Amir [al-Mu'minin] Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as his successor (wasi), whereas the view of the majority of Muslims today is that they do not believe the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed any successor. They say that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... ...they say that after the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), they do not feel the need for anything other than the Quran. And this is the very topic that is most important to understand among all Muslims. It should be seen whether the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), before leaving this world, appointed his successor or not. Let us look into this; our program today is: Is it necessary to have a successor to the Prophet? To discuss this topic further, I would request our respected guest, Janab-e-Akram Sahab, to throw light on this topic through Quranic verses and narrations. Brother, Assalamu Alaykum. 'Wa Alaykum Assalam wa Rahmatullah.' 'Respected brother, the topic is: Is it necessary to have a successor to the Prophet? We would like you to present further details on this topic for our viewers.' 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.' 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Brother Gulzar, regarding the question of what is the necessity of a successor to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), I would like to present a few points before the viewers. In view of His supreme grace, even before the creation of humanity, mankind, and human beings, Allah appointed infallible guides for guidance, so that not a single human being breathing on this earth could say that they were deprived of the guidance of an infallible guide even for a single moment. On the Day of Judgment, no individual should have the opportunity to present this excuse: "O Lord, we went astray because there was no infallible guide for our guidance, no divinely appointed (mansoos minallah) guide for our direction." If that were the case, then for however long the guide arrived late, the blame for the misguidance of that period would fall upon the Divine Himself. And if blame were to be cast upon His justice, His purity would not remain intact.' '...if blame were to be cast, His purity would not remain intact. And if His essence were not pure even for a single moment, then His guidance would fail. Therefore, He made this arrangement: "Before the creation of the first human in this universe, We will make a guide, We will send a guide." That guide would be infallible, divinely appointed (mansoos minallah), and aided by Allah. The one who accepts him would be like an angel, and the one who rejects him would be like Satan (Iblees). The guide would arrive on earth first, and those seeking guidance would come later, so that not even for a single moment would this earth be devoid of divine guidance, from Adam (a.s.) to the Day of Judgment. This is the established path, that Allah never left any human without a guide. In connection with this chain, He announced: "We are going to appoint a vicegerent (Khalifah) on this earth." Reflect on this: God said, "Indeed, I am going to appoint a vicegerent on the earth." He is announcing this in the Quran. Right? And not only did Allah first designate the guide, but...' '...Allah first designated the guide. Moreover, if you look at this entire chain of prophethood, all the prophets who are mentioned, if anyone examines the history of Islam, they will not find a single guide whose selection was made by the people of that time. Let me present a few verses before you in this regard and provide proofs from the Quran. Allah, the Almighty, states in the Holy Quran: "And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, each of them We guided. And Noah We guided before; and of his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good." Similarly, if we reflect on other verses, it will be clear from them as well that Allah Himself chose the guides, not the humans. "O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth..." This is regarding Janab-e-Dawud (a.s.), that "We have appointed you as a successor on this earth." Similarly, Allah says in the Quran: "Indeed, I will make you a leader (Imam) for the people." All these verses point to the fact that this guide and leader must be divinely appointed (mansoos minallah). We want to ask only one question to the entire Muslim Ummah: that God...' '...We want to ask only one question: How could that God, who considers it against His dignity and wisdom to send even the very first human on this earth without an infallible guide, leave billions of humans without a guide until the Day of Judgment after the departure of the Seal of Prophets, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.)? This is the first point. As we have seen, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not send anyone into this world until a guide was first designated. So that is the first point. The second point is: Why would God give every human the authority to choose their guide? If you reflect on both of these things, they are not found in the Sunnah (way) of Allah. Neither did Allah ever allow or give authority to humans before this to choose their guide, nor did Allah ever leave any human without a guide in the world even for a single moment. If you look at both of these, they are not found in the Sunnah of Allah. And we would like to provide proof of this from the Quran, as the Quranic verse itself declares: "And you will never find in the way (Sunnah) of Allah any change." There is never any change in the Sunnah of Allah. So this makes it clear that the Sunnah of Allah, which He established from day one, is that He will first send a guide, and after that...' '...He will send a guide first, and after that, He will send humans. He Himself will select the guide, and He will not leave humans without a guide even for a single moment. These are all the arguments from which it can be concluded: How could the divine Sunnah (Sunnat-e-Ilahiyyah) that has been ongoing since Janab-e-Adam (a.s.) change? It is clear from these verses that choosing a guide, choosing an Imam, or choosing a successor is solely the prerogative of Allah, and no one else has any say in it. Yes, and this is Allah's Sunnah; from the very beginning, it was Allah's Sunnah that Allah alone makes the selection, and He did not allow any human interference in this. I would also like to present another instance before you, which is regarding Janab-e-Musa (a.s.). Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) did not choose Janab-e-Harun (a.s.) himself. Rather, he, the Messenger of Allah, prayed in the court of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and that prayer is recorded in the Quran. It is mentioned in these verses. What is it? It is a very famous prayer: "My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a minister from my family, Aaron, my brother. Increase through him my strength..." Here, Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) is praying: "O Lord, expand my breast..."' '..."O Lord, expand my breast, and ease my task for me, and untie the knot from my tongue so that they may understand my speech." And after this, the prayer that follows in the Quran is the most important part. Here, Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) is praying in the court of God: "And appoint for me a minister (wazir) from my family." Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) requests in the court of God regarding his brother: "Aaron, my brother, appoint him as my minister." And after that, Musa (a.s.) prays in the court of God: "Increase through him my strength," meaning grant me strength through my brother Aaron. And then he says: "And make him associate in my affair," so that he may be a partner in my work of prophethood and guidance. Now, Brother Gulzar, I want to present a very important point before you from the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, who is a very prominent and highly respected scholar among them, narrates in his book of exegesis, Tafsir al-Kabir, regarding this prayer—although that exegesis of the verse is in relation to the Verse of Wilayah (Ayat al-Wilayah)...' '...in relation to that, he has presented this prayer in that exegesis. He narrates the tradition from Janab-e-Abu Dharr (r.a.) that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was praying in the mosque, a beggar entered the mosque and asked for charity, but none of the people present in the mosque gave him anything. He then prayed to Allah, "O Lord, bear witness that I am returning empty-handed from the mosque of Your Prophet." As soon as he made this prayer, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) gestured with his finger, and the beggar came and took the ring off the finger of Imam Ali (a.s.). Now, the important point here is that Janab-e-Abu Dharr narrates that as soon as this event occurred, the Messenger of Allah immediately prayed in the court of the Lord of the Worlds, and he made the exact same prayer that Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) had made for Janab-e-Harun (a.s.): "My Lord, expand for me my breast..." The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited the exact same prayer, and then prayed to the Lord of the Worlds: "O Lord, just as You appointed Janab-e-Harun as the minister to help Janab-e-Musa, in the same way, appoint Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as my..."' '"...appoint Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as my minister to help me and assist me." And Fakhr al-Din al-Razi writes in this narration that the Messenger of Allah said, "O Allah, appoint Ali as my minister, just as Aaron was to Moses." Here, Fakhr al-Din al-Razi writes that the Prophet prayed specifically taking the name of Ali (a.s.) in the court of Allah. And after that, it is written in the narration that the Messenger of Allah had not even finished his prayer when immediately Janab-e-Jibra'il (a.s.) arrived before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) with this verse: "Your ally (wali) is none other than Allah, His Messenger, and those who have believed—those who establish prayer and give zakat while they bow [in worship]." What conclusion do we draw from this? Just as Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) prayed and Allah appointed Janab-e-Harun as his minister to help him, in the same way, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, appointed Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) as the successor and minister to help and assist the Messenger of Allah. Now, the question is: when Janab-e-Musa prayed, Allah did not reject his prayer. So when the Prophet, who is greater than Musa, prays, how could Allah reject his prayer?' '...how could Allah reject his prayer? Therefore, this clearly leads to the conclusion that if there is anyone who is the successor after the Messenger of Allah, it is the master of the universe, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). One thing is clear from this: the Prophet appointed his minister. And the second thing is, since he became the minister, why did people choose someone else? That is the point; we are presenting proofs from their own books, showing that it is written in their books. It is not that we are presenting proofs from our own books. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi is a very prominent name among the Ahl al-Sunnah, and he has recorded this in his book. Let us also look at other books of the Ahl al-Sunnah. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith number 7898, it is clearly written that Allah never sent any prophet who did not have a successor (Khalifah). This is also present there: "Allah never sent a prophet but he had a successor..." meaning that if there is a prophet, it is necessary for him to have a successor.' '..."He did not send [a prophet] without a successor," meaning if there is a prophet, it is necessary for him to have a successor, a vicegerent. This is present in Sahih al-Bukhari. So, from this Hadith, it becomes clear that it is necessary for the Messenger of Allah to have a successor. Similarly, if you look at other narrations found among the Ahl al-Sunnah, there is the book Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal. In it, there is a narration mentioning the "Da'wat dhu al-'Ashirah" (Invitation of the Close Kinsfolk), and he has mentioned this under Hadith number 883. In the mention of Da'wat dhu al-'Ashirah, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) very clearly announced the Wilayah, Imamat, leadership, and ministership of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) during the Da'wat dhu al-'Ashirah. This is present in that book. Brother Gulzar, our third point is—and this is a strange tragedy—that those who usurped the caliphate of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called themselves the "successor of the Messenger" (Khalifat al-Rasul) during their lifetimes, even though their belief was that the Prophet did not leave behind any successor. This is the first thing: if the Messenger of Allah did not leave a successor, how could they call themselves the successor of the Messenger?' Firstly, how are they calling themselves the successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? And secondly, they selected their successor in the final phase of their life. When the Messenger of Allah did not appoint one, who gave these people the right or permission to choose their successor in the final phase of their life? In a way, they tried to show that the Messenger of Allah did not care about the Ummah, but these people cared about the Ummah, so they appointed their successor before leaving this world. Yes, this is indeed a sign of falsehood, that it acts against its own claims. Yes, absolutely. By presenting this excellent point to the viewers, let us guide our friends towards this topic: among the key responsibilities of the Prophets, if there is one most important task, it is that of the deputy (successor), and its need exists in every era. Whether it was the era before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) or the era after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Meaning, guidance is one of the most vital needs of human beings in every era, without which man cannot lead his life in this world. So now, the question arises here that... ...the question arises here that among all the divine guides before the Messenger of Allah, you will not find any disagreement over even a single name among them. Look, is there any disagreement over the name of Prophet Noah (a.s.)? No. Is there any disagreement over the name of Prophet Moses (a.s.)? No. Is there any disagreement over the name of Prophet Jesus (a.s.)? No. Over Prophet Abraham (a.s.)? No. Whichever Prophet came, you will not find any disagreement over their names. Where do you find disagreement? It is over the guides whom the Messenger of Allah entrusted to the Muslim Ummah; you will find disagreement within the Muslim Ummah over their names. Now, two types of groups appear before us, before our eyes. The first group is the one that says the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint his successor or did not announce a successor—this is the first group—and then they call themselves the Caliph or the Caliph of the Prophet, and in the final phase of their lives, they also appoint their own successor. This is the first group. The second group is the one that holds the view that the Messenger of Allah announced his successors, and not just one successor, but twelve successors until the Day of Judgment... ...announced twelve successors until the Day of Judgment. This is the second group, and this is the group of truth. And viewers, this perspective, which is the perspective of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.), is a divine perspective, which we presented before you in our previous discussion: what is the Sunnah of Allah? 'And you will never find in the Sunnah of Allah any change.' Allah never leaves His servants without a guide. So, after the life of the Messenger of Allah, why would Allah leave humanity without a guide? Thus, our perspective aligns with the divine perspective. Regarding this very disagreement, a Syrian man once came to the presence of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) and wanted to debate the Imam (a.s.) on this matter. At that moment, our Imam (a.s.) called Hisham ibn al-Hakam, and Hisham ibn al-Hakam arrived there. When Hisham arrived, the Imam (a.s.) said to the Syrian, 'O Syrian, whatever you want to ask, ask Hisham. He will answer you.' After that, the Syrian addressed Hisham and asked, 'On what topic do you want to debate me?' The Syrian, representing his stance against Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), said, 'I want to debate regarding his Imamate.' As soon as Hisham heard this topic... ...as soon as Hisham heard this topic, his face turned pale, he became angry, and Hisham asked him, 'O Syrian, tell me, is Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, more concerned about the guidance of His creation, or is creation itself more concerned about its own guidance?' Look, man himself is not as concerned about his own guidance. This is the first question-and-answer session Hisham has with the Syrian, and the Syrian replies, 'Indeed, Allah is more concerned about the guidance of His creation.' Now, Hisham asks the second question, 'What arrangement has Allah made for that guidance?' The Syrian replies, 'For guidance, Allah appointed the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' Then Hisham asks, 'After the Messenger of Allah, what arrangement has Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made for guidance?' The Syrian replies, 'After the Messenger of Allah, Allah has placed the Quran and the Sunnah for the guidance of His creation.' Now Hisham asks him, 'Are the Quran and the Sunnah sufficient for human guidance?' He replies, 'Yes, they are absolutely sufficient.' Here, Hisham says, 'If they are sufficient, then why is there a disagreement between you and me? You also believe in this Quran...' ...why is there a disagreement? You are a believer in this Quran, and I am also a believer in this Quran. You are a follower of the Sunnah, and I am also a follower of the Sunnah. If the Quran and Sunnah are sufficient, then why this disagreement? Today, you have traveled all the way from Syria to Medina; why this disagreement? When you also accept this Quran and you also accept this Sunnah, why is there a disagreement?' Now, he looks at the Imam (a.s.) with great despair, and the Imam (a.s.) says to him, 'Why do you not speak?' The Syrian replies, 'If I say that the Quran and Sunnah are sufficient, my argument will be refuted, and I will be proven wrong. And if I say that the Quran and Sunnah are not sufficient, then what is the benefit of such a Quran and Sunnah? So, the situation is that I am asking Hisham this very question.' The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Ask Hisham.' Then Hisham asks the same question that the Syrian had asked: 'Is Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, more concerned about the guidance of His creation, or is creation itself more concerned about its own guidance?' To this, Hisham says, 'Indeed, Allah is more concerned.' Then his question is, 'What arrangement has Allah made for this guidance? And if there is a disagreement among people regarding something, how should that disagreement be resolved?' ...how should that disagreement be resolved? Here, Hisham says, 'If one speaks of the past era, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made the arrangement through the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And if one speaks of today's era, then pointing towards the resolver of disagreements, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), Hisham says, 'In today's era, if anyone can resolve the disagreements of the Muslim Ummah, it is your personality, meaning Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.).' Now, the conclusion of this entire debate is that the divine proof or the successor of the Prophet has the most important task of guidance, and to resolve the disagreements among the people. The Quran is the same, the verses of the Quran are the same; the task of the true successor is to resolve the disagreements among the people through that Quran, and if different ideologies are being formed among the people, to turn those ideologies back to the correct ideology, which is the divine ideology. Now, the final point is that if the Muslim Ummah had recognized the true successor in the field of Ghadir, and upheld the allegiance that the Messenger of Allah had taken, then today in this Muslim Ummah, or among this Muslim Ummah, there wouldn't be so many... ...so many disagreements would not be seen among this Muslim Ummah today. I wish to conclude my speech with these four poetic lines: 'You once made a covenant of Wilayah with Ali, which all your tribes have forgotten. You memorized the entire Quran of thirty parts, but forgot the four-letter word Ghadir. You forgot the four-letter word Ghadir.' [Host speaking] We hope you liked this episode, and you must have benefited from the points presented to you. Along with this, let me also inform you that during the broadcast of this episode, a link will be provided in our description. You are requested to answer the questions in it correctly as soon as possible so that you may also be included among the fastest 100 people. God willing, we will meet you in the next episode. Until then, subscribe...

And many such losses are remembered which, because of Yazid and people like him, were presented to the people and established for acceptance. And whoever accepted him as caliph and pledged allegiance to him has committed a grave injustice. And when Imam Hussain (a.s.) faced the initial oppression, they targeted him. If the history of Bani Umayya is examined, it is because in his view, neither did any news come, nor did any revelation descend, nor was there any religion. ...will start again, and whoever... let's see how these people, the way they said to control him... title: Maula Ali (a.s.) Ki Sab Se Badi Fazeelat Kya Hai? | Eid-e-Mubaahelah Mubaarak
excerpt: This lecture discusses the supreme merit of Imam Ali (a.s.) as highlighted by Imam Reza (a.s.) during a dialogue with Ma'mun. The speaker focuses on the Quranic event of Mubahala, where Imam Ali (a.s.) is identified as the 'nafs' or 'self' of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). This designation establishes Imam Ali's unparalleled status and superiority among all of Allah's creation, secondary only to the Prophet himself.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless you, O Wali... Sayyid Murtaza (a.r.) narrates from his teacher Sheikh Mufid (a.r.) that once Ma'mun asked Imam Reza (a.s.) to mention a great merit of the Master of the Universe, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), which is mentioned in the Quran. Imam Reza (a.s.) replied that Allah, the Glorious and Majestic, states this merit in the event of Mubahala: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Then whoever argues with you about it after [this] knowledge has come to you - say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then supplicate earnestly and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars."' Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called Imam Hasan and Imam Hussain (a.s.), who were his sons, and Janabe Fatima-tuz-Zahra (s.a.), who was representing the women at this place, and called Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), who, according to Allah's command... ...was declared as the 'self' (nafs) of the Messenger of Allah. It is proven that among Allah's creation, there is no one more glorious and superior than the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Therefore, it also became clear that by Allah's command, there is no one superior to the 'self' of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), i.e., Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Before the truthfulness of Sayyida (s.a.), the Christians were clever and saved themselves from the curse...

title: EP#4 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ke Wujood Par Shak Karna | IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT
excerpt: This lecture discusses the spiritual dangers of doubting the existence and reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). By referencing a narration from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) regarding Surah Ash-Shu'ara, the speaker explains that questioning the Imam's birth or location is equivalent to questioning the divine power and decree of Allah. The lecture emphasizes that the Imam's role is a fixed divine plan, and skepticism in this matter leads to loss in both this world and the hereafter.
content:
O sight, O sight, O hidden desire in longing. My life is a pretext, my bond of servitude is a testament. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance, assist us and do not let us perish. In the book 'Yanabi al-Mawadda', the Sunni scholar Sheikh Sulaiman Qunduzi, in Chapter 71, page 485, narrates this hadith from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.). Mufaddal bin Umar asked Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) about verse 18 of Surah Ash-Shu'ara: {Those who doubt the Hour are indeed in a far-reaching error}. When asked about those who doubt the Hour, the Imam (a.s.) replied: 'The doubters are those who say: When was Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) born? Who has seen him?' Where is he at this time? When will he reappear? All these questions are like doubting the decree and power of Allah. These are the people who will suffer loss in this world and the hereafter. In short, it is clear from this verse of the Holy Quran and the narration of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that people will doubt the existence of Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif). They will doubt themselves and sow doubt in the hearts of others. In the light of this hadith, doubting the existence of Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) is like doubting the decree and power of Allah. Sending 124,000 prophets, establishing Islam as the final religion, and bringing about the Day of Judgment—all these are divine decrees. Allah has decided these things, and no one can interfere in His decisions. Allah has made them absolute. Similarly, this entire universe was created by divine power. Allah can do whatever He wills, whenever He wills. He is the Master of 'Be, and it is'. He has power over all things. One who doubts the decree and power of Allah is, in fact, doubting Allah Himself. Similarly, the existence, reappearance, and government of Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) are also divine decrees and power. Therefore, whoever doubts Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) has considered the power of Allah to be insignificant. That is why such a person will suffer loss in this world and the hereafter. In the end, we pray that the Lord hastens the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) and protects us from the evil of the doubters. Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Ilm Haasil Karne Ke liye Umr Ki Qaid Nahin | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the importance of lifelong learning and overcoming the ego or shame associated with acquiring knowledge at any age. He emphasizes that one should be willing to learn from anyone, regardless of their status or age, citing the humility of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the ultimate example. The lecture includes an inspiring anecdote about a student of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari who, through spiritual intercession and sincere prayer, transformed from a mocked, struggling student into a brilliant scholar capable of correcting his teacher.
content:
So now if someone says, 'Learn now,' they say, 'Is this some Congress? What will we learn now? At the last moment, won't you all be... if you are, then be it, otherwise if you die the death of disbelief (kufr), you will be severely punished. And there should never be any shame felt in this, like "We won't learn from him, how can we learn from him, he is just a child in front of us, he is like this and we are like that, he is like that," right? This should never come in the way of acquiring knowledge. If this thing comes in the way, then remember, the Master of the Universe, Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)... if one has reached such an age, then even their knowledge will feel ashamed. Therefore, one should never feel ashamed while acquiring knowledge, no matter who they are or who they are learning from. Now, let me present a short incident to you about a very great... ...in the era of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, you know Sheikh Ansari was a very great jurist (faqih). What is his title? 'Khatim al-Fuqaha'. He passed away in 1281 AH. Sheikh Ansari's books, like 'Rasa'il' and 'Makasib', are taught in the seminaries, and indeed Sheikh Murtaza Ansari holds a very, very high status. Among his students, in the class, there was a student... ...personality, and people don't know about him. Let me tell you a short incident about him. One of his students in the class was someone whom everyone used to make fun of and mock. A classroom environment often has someone who becomes the scapegoat whom everyone makes fun of. So, that boy was very weak academically, but he felt very bad when they mocked him. So, what did he do? He sought intercession (tawassul) and prayed intensely, 'O Master, I am so weak, they make fun of me. I will study, or else I will leave studying altogether.' When this happened, by the grace of Allah, he received spiritual assistance, and he was told, 'Take this, drink a drop of water, and God willing, your problem will be solved.' He drank that single drop of water, and then went and sat in the class of the great scholar (Sheikh). As soon as the Sheikh started teaching, before he could even read two sentences, the student spoke up and said, 'You have made a mistake.' The whole class started laughing that he was correcting the Sheikh. The Sheikh asked, 'What is it?' He said, 'You said this, but actually it is not like this, it is like that.' title: Roz-e-Arafah Kiske Aamaal Barbaad Ho Jaayenge?
excerpt: This lecture discusses a critical warning regarding the Day of Arafah and the spiritual consequences of harboring hatred toward the Ahl al-Bayt. Citing a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker explains that enmity toward the Prophet's progeny and their followers renders all of a person's good deeds void. The lecture emphasizes that such hatred acts as a spiritual barrier that turns one's efforts into dispersed dust.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless you... Respected viewers, people gather in the plain of Arafat to attain the mercy of Allah, but there is one deed due to which, let alone receiving Allah's mercy, all of a person's deeds will be wasted and ruined. Sulayman ibn Khalid says, 'I heard Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) say: Indeed, the deeds of the servants are presented before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) every Thursday night (Shab-e-Juma), and on the Day of Arafah, a call comes from Allah, which is His saying: "And We will regard what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed." (Quran 25:23)' The narrator says, 'I said to the Imam, "May my life be sacrificed for you, what is this deed due to which all of people's deeds will be wasted?"' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'This is the hatred (bughz) towards us, the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and hatred towards our lovers, due to which all of a person's deeds will be made like dispersed dust.' ...all these good deeds will be made like dispersed dust. That is, enmity towards the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and enmity towards their lovers is the deed due to which all of a person's deeds will be ruined and wasted. Whatever good deeds they have performed will be rendered like dispersed particles of dust. Meaning, they will be left with nothing in their hands; all their deeds will be wasted. Blessings be upon Muhammad and his infallible progeny.
