excerpt: The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) describes a group of people who will exist in the end times and whom he refers to as his 'brothers.' Unlike his companions, these individuals will possess faith in him without ever having seen him. The Prophet emphasizes their immense virtue, noting that they will remain steadfast in their religion despite facing extreme hardships and trials. These believers are described as lamps of light who will be protected by Allah from the dark tribulations of the future.
content:
One day, some companions were present with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). He said, "O Allah, let me meet my brothers," twice. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) uttered these words, the companions sitting near him asked, "Are we not your brothers, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah replied, "No, you are my companions. My brothers are a people in the end times." Then the Messenger of Allah described their virtue: "They will believe without having seen me." Allah has told me their names and the names of their forefathers while they were still in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers. They have not yet come into this world. Each one of them will remain steadfast on their religion with such intensity that it will be more difficult than walking on thorns in a dark night or holding hot coals in one's hands. They are the lamps of light. Allah will save them from all the tribulations that are like dark storms.

excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical confrontation between Imam Ali (a.s.) and the ruling authority regarding the land of Fadak. Imam Ali (a.s.) utilizes logical arguments and legal principles to challenge the double standards applied to Lady Fatima (s.a.). The discourse highlights the Imam's defense of the rights of the Ahlulbayt and his appeal to the Quranic status of the Prophet's household.
content:
Then Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) asked, 'Then tell me, if something is in the possession of a Muslim and I claim it, would you demand proof from me?' The ruler said, 'Yes.' Imam Ali (a.s.) said, 'Then if something is in my possession and the Muslims are claiming it, why are you demanding proof from me?' Hearing this reply, the ruler fell silent. [Imam Ali (a.s.)] entered the mosque where the ruler was sitting on the throne among the people. He (a.s.) asked the ruler, 'Why did you [deprive] Fatima...' He (a.s.) asked the ruler, 'Why did you snatch away that thing from Fatima (s.a.) which was in her possession during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah?' The ruler said, 'This is the property (fai') of the Muslims; if she presents witnesses, then fine, otherwise she has no right to it.' He (a.s.) said, 'Will you decide against us contrary to the decision you would make for other Muslims? Why are you demanding proof from me?' Hearing this reply, the ruler fell silent. But his advisor said, 'This is the property of Muslims, and we will not give any answer to these words of yours.' Upon this, Amir [al-Mu'minin] (a.s.) asked the ruler again, 'Do you believe in the Holy Quran?' He said, 'Of course.' Imam Ali (a.s.) said, 'Then tell me about this verse of Allah, the Almighty: "Innama yureedullah..."' 'Was this verse revealed about us or about others?' The ruler said, 'Of course, about you.' Upon this, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), continuing his words, asked the ruler, 'If two Muslims testify against Fatima (s.a.), what judgment would you pass?' The ruler said, 'I would establish the legal punishment (hadd) on her just like other ordinary Muslim women.'

O avenger of the blood of the prophets and the children of the prophets. Where is the one who will take revenge for the killing of the prophets and the children of the prophets? title: EP12 | Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) Ki Teen (3) Wasiyyatein | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture details the final moments and testamentary wishes of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) as she prepared to depart from this world. It highlights her specific instructions to Imam Ali (a.s.) regarding her funeral, burial, and the protection of her children. The speaker contrasts her final requests with the subsequent suffering endured by her progeny at the hands of the Ummah.
content:
...that do not let those people participate in my funeral who oppressed me and snatched my right from me. Indeed, they are my enemies and the enemies of the Messenger of Allah. Neither they nor their followers should pray over me. Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had built a place indeed named 'Bayt al-Huzn' (House of Sorrows). She used to go there during the day with her children, and after spending the day there mourning her father (a.s.), she would return home. He was returning home after Zuhr when on the way he met the maidservant weeping. She said, 'We fear that by the time you reach, it might be too late.' Mawla (a.s.) rushed very quickly towards the house. When he reached the Lady's chamber, he saw that the Lady was lying on a floor covered with a thin Egyptian sheet, sometimes turning to the right side, sometimes to the left. Mawla (a.s.) took off his cloak from his shoulders, removed the turban from his head, placed the Lady's head on his lap, and called out to her. The Lady did not give any reply. Then he said, 'O you who used to take out from your own food and distribute it to the poor!' There was no reply. There was no reply, and then both began to weep. Then Mawla (a.s.) asked, 'How are you feeling? I am Ali.' She replied, 'There is no escape from death, and I know that after me you will be left alone. Even so, please take care of my children,' and she made her final testament. And she addressed [Maula Ali (a.s.)] saying, 'O Abul Hasan, I fell asleep for a short while, and I saw my beloved, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in a magnificent palace made of white pearls. He said, "My child, come to me, for I am eager to meet you." I replied, "By Allah, I am eager to meet you as well." And I know that my father is true to his promise and fulfills his covenant. When [I pass away], sit by my side and recite Surah Yasin, and know that I have bid farewell to this world. Then, wash me with my clothes on...' ...keep only the close members of my family and only those [whom I approve] for my burial, and then bury me in the darkness of the night. My beloved, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), told me these things. In another Hadith, it is narrated that she willed, 'Arrange a coffin (taboot) for my funeral.' It is narrated that the first funeral in the world to be carried in a coffin was hers. 'O Maula Ali, I make a will to you that you must not allow those who oppressed me and usurped my right to participate in my funeral. Indeed, they are my enemies and the enemies of the Messenger of Allah. Neither they nor their followers should pray over me, and then bury me in the darkness of the night.' If we reflect upon this will of the Princess (a.s.), some specific points come to light. If we reflect, some specific points come to light. Maula [Ali (a.s.)] acted upon that will, but how did the Ummah ignore the Lady's will after her martyrdom? The Lady had willed to love her children and take special care of them, but after her, the Ummah expressed its 'love' for her children sometimes with arrows, sometimes with swords, and sometimes with poison. The Lady's funeral was carried in a coffin to preserve her veil, but alas, after her, her daughters were paraded through the markets of Sham. Her final will was not to let the oppressors participate in her funeral prayer; those oppressors retaliated in such a way that sometimes they showered arrows on the funeral of her elder son, Imam Hasan (a.s.), and sometimes in Karbala, they left the body of her beloved son, Imam Hussain (a.s.), without a shroud on the sands of Karbala. O Lord of Fatima, by the right of Fatima, accept this...

title: EP04 | Noor Sirf Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ke Paas Hai | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2026
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the ultimate source of divine light and guidance for humanity. It emphasizes that true faith requires absolute submission (Taslim) to the Ahlul-Bayt, distinguishing the light of Wilayah from the darkness of personal opinion and disbelief. The session also provides guidance on maintaining a steadfast connection with the Imam during his occultation through prayer, remembrance, and the practice of Bara'at.

TSR presents. Ya, ya, O hidden desire in the longing of my eyes, O, O comfort of my heart. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, then subscribe now and do not forget to click the bell icon. The quiz link is now live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered before, then click on the quiz link and register. Then on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all the answers must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear in today's winners or if an episode was missed, they do not need to be disappointed, because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the winner of the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all the questions in all the episodes. That is, even if someone is not among the daily winners, but has given correct answers in all episodes, then all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-hujjati-bnil-hasani, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aabaihi, fi hadhihis-saa'ati wa fi kulli saa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. A'udhu billahi sami-il-alim minash-shaytan-nir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya Wali-al-Asr adriknah wala tuhliknah. What is most necessary for success in this world and the hereafter? Correct guidance. If the guide is not correct, then a human wanders into misguidance and cannot reach their destination. If the path is dark and one cannot see anything, then the most necessary thing for guidance is light (Noor). So, just as one who does not have light cannot reach their destination by traveling the path of darkness, in the same way, one who has light but does not use it correctly, they also cannot reach their destination. Related to this is today's 'Panah-e-Kainat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu Sharif' mega quiz, where in this final episode, it will be stated regarding the Khutbah-e-Ghadir that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said regarding Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu Sharif, 'Wa la noora illa indahu' (And there is no light except with him). Let us remind you that to know the surprise question, watch this episode carefully and get a chance to be included in the daily prize and mega prize lucky draw by giving correct answers to all the questions. Let us now begin the final episode. A'udhu billahi sami-il-alim minash-shaytan-nir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya Wali-al-Asr adriknah wala tuhliknah. Respected listeners, our topic today is from that sentence of the Khutbah-e-Ghadir in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said regarding Imam-e-Zamana Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu Sharif, 'Wa la noora illa indahu' (And there is no light except that which is with him), meaning with Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Let us begin the discussion with reference to this. From the Ziyarat of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) which is recited on Friday, in which we recite these sentences: 'Assalamu alayka ya Noorallahi alladhi yahtadi bihil-mohtadun' (Peace be upon you, O light of Allah through whom the guided ones receive guidance). Meaning, those who are in search of guidance receive guidance through Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). 'Wa yufarriju bihi anil-muminun' (And through whom the believers find relief). Respected audience, the Imam is that light which Allah has sent down. If you look, in Al-Kafi, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) has brought a chapter in which he has collected about six hadiths which are on this very topic, in which he is stating that the Imams (a.s.) are the light of Allah which He has sent down. Like the name of that chapter is 'Bab-u-annal-aimmata alayhimussalam Noorullahi Azza-wa-Jall' (The chapter in which it is stated that the Imams (a.s.) are the light of Allah). Now there is a hadith in this that he has brought. The narration is from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli that he asked Imam Baqir (a.s.) regarding verse number 8 of Surah Taghabun. What is the verse? The verse is: 'Fa-aaminoo billahi wa rasoolihi wan-noorilladhi anzalna' (So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down). Meaning, in verse number 8 of Surah Taghabun, Allah is commanding to believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the light which I have sent down. In the context of this verse, when Abu Khalid al-Kabuli asked regarding this verse, the fifth Imam said in its interpretation: 'Ya Aba Khalid, O Aba Khalid, an-nooru wallahi al-aimma' (O Abu Khalid, by Allah, the light is the Imams (a.s.)) 'min aali Muhammad s.a.w.a.' (who are from the family of Muhammad). The Imams (a.s.) who are from the family of Muhammad are the ones meant by this light. Then he further says, 'ila yawmil qiyama' (until the Day of Judgment). Until the Day of Judgment, these are the Imams (a.s.), and after that he says, 'wa hum wallahi Noorullahi alladhi anzala' (And by Allah, they are the light of Allah which Allah has sent down). 'Wa hum wallahi Noorullahi fis-samawati wal-ard' (And by Allah, they are the light of Allah in the heavens and the earth). 'Wallahi ya Aba Khalid' (And by Allah, O Abu Khalid) 'la-noorul-imami fi quloobil-muminina anwaru minash-shams al-mujiyyati bin-nahar' (And by Allah, the Imam swears that O Abu Khalid, these are definitely the light that is brighter in the hearts of the believers than the sun shining in the day). The light of the Imams (a.s.) which is in the hearts of the believers is brighter than the sun that shines in the day. And he further says, 'wa hum wallahi yunawwiruna quloob-al-muminin' (And by Allah, it is through them that Allah illuminates the hearts of the believers). 'Wa yahjubullahu Azza-wa-Jall noorahum amman yashao fa-tuzlimu quloobuhum' (And Allah veils/hides their light from whom He wills, and makes their hearts dark). 'Wallahi ya Aba Khalid' (And O Abu Khalid, by Allah) 'la yuhibbuna abdun wa yatwallana hatta yutahhirallahu qalbahu' (No servant can love us and accept our Wilayah until Allah purifies his heart). Meaning, to keep their love in the heart, to keep their Wilayah in the heart, the heart must be pure, and Allah also purifies the heart, Allah also makes the heart pure, and apart from this, their love and their Wilayah cannot enter the heart. The heart must be pure. 'Wa la yutahhirullahu qalba abdin hatta yusallima lana' (And Allah does not purify the heart of any servant unless he submits to the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), submits to the Imams (a.s.)). Unless he submits to the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). If he does not submit, then Allah does not purify his heart, and if He does not purify the heart, then their Wilayah and their love cannot enter his heart. He further says, 'wa yakoon silman lana' (And he is in peace with us). 'Fa-idha kana silman lana, sallamahullahu min shadidil-hisab' (And when he is in peace with us, Allah also grants him safety from the severity of the reckoning, from the severity of the account that is going to happen to him, Allah gives him peace from that too). And after that he says, 'wa amanahu min faza'i yawmil-qiyamatil-akbar' (And He gives him safety from the fear of the Day of Judgment, the fear of the Day of Judgment, Allah gives him safety from that fear too when he is in peace with the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.)). Meaning, the Imam is the light of Allah. In this regard, there is another verse in the Holy Quran which is Surah Zumar, Surah number 39, verse number 69. What does Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala say in this verse? 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa ashraqatil-ardu binoori rabbiha wa wuzi'al-kitabu wa ji'a bin-nabiyyina wa shuhada wa qudiya bainahum bil-haqqi wahum la yuzlamun' (And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the book will be placed, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be passed between them with truth, and they will not be wronged). And the earth will shine, through what will it shine? It will shine with the light of its Lord. 'Wa wudi'al kitabu'—the book will be placed, meaning the record of deeds will be established. 'Wa ji'a bin-nabiyyina wa shuhada'—the prophets will be brought, the witnesses will be brought. 'Wa quziya bainahum bil-haqqi'—judgment will be passed between them with truth, and they will not be wronged on that day. The interesting point here is the beginning of the verse: 'The earth will shine with the light of its Lord.' What is the commentary on this? Janab Mufazzal ibn Umar, a prominent companion of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), asks the Imam about this very verse, saying, 'Mawla, what is meant by "wa ashraqatil ardu binuri rabbiha"—the earth will shine with the light of its Lord?' The Imam replies, 'Rabbul-ard yu'na Imamul-ard'—the Lord of the earth means the Imam of the earth. The Imam of the earth is whom Allah calls the Lord. He is the Lord, the Sustainer of this earth. Therefore, the use of the word 'Rabb' for the Imam is further proof that in this verse of the Holy Quran, 'Rabb' does not mean the Worshipped One (Allah), but rather the one responsible for the entire upbringing of the earth. The one by whose command the earth thrives, and by whose light the earth will shine, is the Imam of the earth. I asked, 'Fa-idha kharaja yakunu madha?'—Janab Mufazzal asks, 'When the Imam (a.s.) comes, meaning when the Imam of the earth comes'—referring to Hazrat Hujjat (a.s.)—'what will happen when he arrives, when he appears?' The Imam replies, 'Idha yastaghni-nnasu an daw'ish-shams'—people will become independent of the light of the sun. 'Wa nuril-qamar'—and the light of the moon, there will be no need for that either. 'Wa yajtazi'una binuril-imam'—and the light of the Imam will be sufficient for them. Meaning, the light of the sun and moon will fade when the Imam's light shines across the whole world, the whole universe. When the Imam (a.s.) appears, after that. The Imam says people will become independent of the sun's light. And look, what does 'Noor' (light) mean? Noor means light, brightness, illumination. What is the function of light? It is the job of light to remove every darkness, every gloom. Light removes it. For example, in a dark room, if there is no light at all, a person will never know the reality of what is kept where in that room. If there is no light in that room, if it is completely dark. As soon as light enters that room, the reality of every single thing—what is kept where—will become clear. Similarly, the function of light is to clarify the reality of everything. In the same way, Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) is that light; when he arrives, when his reappearance occurs, through him the realities of all other things—the reality of every person, the reality of their faith, the reality of every matter—will become clear when the Imam (a.s.) comes. And whoever is with the Imam, who believes in his Imamate—this is very important, to be with the Imam, to be a believer in his Imamate—whoever submits to his command, whoever is waiting for him, will attain guidance. They will benefit from that light. But whoever is not with the Imam will go astray. Why? Because the Imam is the only light, and apart from the light, a person will gain nothing but misguidance and darkness. Because the Imam is light, and the function of light is to guide, and every human being is in need of guidance; they are dependent on guidance, no matter what the matter is. A child going to school needs guidance. A young person stepping into their career needs guidance, and a businessman doing business also needs guidance. If a person takes guidance from the right person, they succeed. But if they do not get the right guidance, or try to take guidance from someone who does not know themselves, that person goes astray and suffers a loss. And this is about the world, where if a person suffers a loss, they still have a chance to compensate for it. But the question of the Hereafter, which is the final destination—if a person does not take guidance from the right guide in that arena and goes astray, and because of not receiving the right guidance from that guide, they enter Hell, then returning from there is impossible. Therefore, we must choose a guide who leads us to Allah and grants us success in this world and the Hereafter. On this topic, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) brings a chapter in Kitab al-Kafi in which he narrates five hadiths. The name of the chapter is 'Chapter regarding the one who takes his religion from someone other than the Imam appointed by Allah (Jalla Jalaluhu).' In this chapter, we find a hadith, and this hadith is a commentary on a verse. The verse is Surah Al-Qasas, the 28th Surah, verse number 50, in which Allah says: 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa man adallu mimmanittaba'a hawahu bighayri hudam-minallah'—And who is more astray than the one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah? Regarding this verse, the Imam (a.s.) says that here it means, 'Manittakhadha dinahu ra'yahu bighayri imamin min aimmatil-huda'—this refers to the person who took his religion from his own opinion, from his own guesswork, from his own calculations, and did not take it from the Imam whom Allah had sent as a guide. And even if a person performs good deeds based on their own guesswork or opinion, they will not receive the reward for it. Because whatever they are performing, whatever deeds they are doing, even if they are virtuous, they are doing them according to their own opinion, and if a person follows their own opinion, follows their own desires, follows their own opinions, then they are following everything except that which Allah has sent as religion. Now, viewers, one should not be impressed by the good deeds of such people and make the mistake of considering them 'Deendar' (religious). Now, let us present a hadith in this regard which is narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, and he presents similar matters before Imam Sadiq (a.s.). He states that, 'Mawla, when I reach the service of the Imam (a.s.)...' After arriving, he states, 'Mawla, I live among people. And when I move among people, I see a very strange scene. Mawla, there are some people who acknowledge your Wilayah (guardianship). But along with acknowledging it, neither trustworthiness is found in them, nor loyalty, nor truthfulness. And on the contrary, Mawla, I also meet a group similar to them who do not hold your Wilayah, but trustworthiness is found in them, truthfulness is found in them, and loyalty is found in them.' When Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur presents this to the Imam (a.s.), the Mawla was sitting leaning back. The words of the hadith are: 'Fastawa Abu Abdillah (a.s.) jalisan'—the Mawla sat up straight. And then the sentence of the narration is: 'Wa aqbala alayya kal-ghadban'—and with anger, Ibn Abi Ya'fur says, he turned towards me with anger. Meaning, why did the Imam adopt this tone of anger and severity? It means the Imam wants to show that this is not a common stage, not a common issue, but a fundamental issue of belief, which the Imam (a.s.) will now address and clarify before Ibn Abi Ya'fur. Meaning, this change in posture was a sign that the Imam (a.s.) was displeased with what Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur had stated. Now the Imam (a.s.) is going to give the explanation here. The Imam immediately declares, 'La dina liman dana-llaha biwilayati imamin ja'irin laysa minallah'—O Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, that person has no religion who adopts a religion based on the Wilayah of a tyrannical Imam who is not appointed by Allah. And then, the Imam delivers a definitive verdict here. A person does not become 'Deendar' just by good deeds or good character; rather, a person becomes 'Deendar' when they accept the Wilayah of the Imam or Wali appointed by Allah. After that, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Wa la adba 'ala man dana biwilayati imamin adilin minallah'—and there is no blame on the one who accepts the Wilayah of a just Imam from Allah. Here too, the Imam (a.s.) is trying to say that if a person is on the Wilayah of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) and is acting upon the teachings given by the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), and some deficiency or weakness is found in their character, their path will still be the path of truth. They will not be considered outside of religion; they will be 'Deendar'. Now, when the Mawla presents this explanation before Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, Abdullah ibn Ya'fur asks in a very surprised manner, 'La dina li-ula'ika?'—then they have no religion? Meaning those people who do not hold your Wilayah, okay, but their character is excellent, they are trustworthy, loyal, and all good character traits are found in them, so do they have no religion? And then he submits to the Mawla, 'Wa la adba 'ala ha'ula'i?'—and these people who are treading on your Wilayah, they will have no blame, Mawla? Now, Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur expresses this surprise before the Imam (a.s.). Now, the Mawla clarifies the confusion in his companion's mind in the light of the Quran and tries to remove that doubt. The Mawla says, 'Thumma qala ala tasma'u qawlallahi azza wa jall'—O Abdullah ibn Ya'fur, have you not heard this saying of Allah? Then the Mawla recites that verse of the Quran which is very famous and well-known: 'Allahu waliyyulladhina amanu yukhrijuhum minaz-zulumati ilan-nur'—Allah is the Wali of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into the light. After presenting this verse, the Imam (a.s.) says in explanation: 'Min zulumatidh-dhunubi ilan-nurit-tawbati awil-maghfira'—meaning He will bring them out of the darkness of sins into the light of repentance and forgiveness. Now, the reason why Allah is bringing them out of darkness into the light, the Imam (a.s.) explains: 'Liwilayatihim kulla imamin adilin minallah'—because they accepted the Wilayah of that Imam from Allah who is a just Imam. If that person does not accept the Wilayah of the Imam of the time (a.s.) or these 12 Imams, then Allah leaves them in darkness, and Allah would never bring them out of darkness into brightness or light. Then the Imam (a.s.) states, 'Qala walladhina kafaru awliya'uhumut-taghutu yukhrijunahum minan-nuri ilaz-zulumat'—and those who disbelieved, their allies are the Taghut (tyrants); they bring them out of the light into the darkness. Then what will be their state? 'Yukhrijunahum minan-nuri ilaz-zulumat'—these Taghut will bring them out of the light into the darkness. And then in explanation, the Imam (a.s.) states, 'Fa-ayyu nurin yakunu lil-kafiri fayukhraju minhu'—so for the one who disbelieved, what light is there from which he would be brought out? Then the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Innama ana bihadha annahum kanu 'ala nuril-islam'—it means they were on the light of Islam. Then, when they adopted the Wilayah of that tyrannical Imam who was not from Allah, then the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Kharaju biwilayatihim iyyahum min nuril-islami ila zulumatil-kufr'—then because of their Wilayah, meaning because of the Wilayah of the Taghut, they will move from the light of Islam into the darkness of disbelief. And then after that, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'فَأَوْجَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُمُ النَّارَ مَعَ الْكُفَّارِ' (Allah has made Hell mandatory for them along with the disbelievers). Allah has made Hell mandatory for those people along with those who had adopted disbelief earlier. 'فَقَالَ أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ' (He said, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally). The Imam (a.s.) completes this verse, stating that these people are the people of Hell and will remain in Hell forever. Respected brothers, that is why it is necessary for us to remain firm in our belief in the Imamate of Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), and may no one ever, ever lead us away from this belief, otherwise, its result is only misguidance and destruction. Because the Occultation (Ghaybah) is a test for the special Shias, as the Occultation is such an era that we find in traditions that even those who believe in Imamate, those who are convinced of the belief of Imamate, will also go astray in this era of Occultation. In another hadith, it is said that people will deny his birth. Just as the seventh Imam, Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), states: 'صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ مَنْ يَقُولُ النَّاسُ لَمْ يُولَدْ' (The master of this affair is the one about whom people will say that he was not born). Meaning, regarding the master of this affair, Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), they are those about whom people will say that he was not even born, his birth did not even take place. That is, people will deny his birth. Respected brothers, now those who deny the birth of Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), those who deny his birth, they are so ignorant that they do not even know that if the Imam were not on this earth, this earth would sink along with its inhabitants. The remaining of this earth indicates that he is present on this earth. And respected brothers, the second point is that by saying this, by denying the birth of Imam-e-Zamana, they are not just expressing their ignorance, but they are—God forbid, God forbid—accusing Allah of leaving this earth empty without a Proof (Hujjah). Meaning that He has left the people wandering. He has left the people just like that to go astray; He has not left any Proof or evidence of His on this earth. Now, to clarify this point further, we will take the help of the hadith that we mentioned in the previous episode. The hadith was from Ahmad ibn Ishaq when he came to the 11th Imam, and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) showed Ahmad ibn Ishaq the Ziyarat of Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), and when he saw him and asked the Imam more to increase his certainty, the Imam said, 'Ahmad ibn Ishaq, when you have seen with your own eyes, do not look for anything else.' When he heard these words from Imam-e-Zamana, he further says, Ahmad ibn Ishaq, that I left from there with great joy and happiness. I left there very happily, and then the next day I returned to Imam-e-Zamana, and when I returned, he further says that I asked him a question. 'يَا ابْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَدُومَ سُرُورِي بِمَا مَنَنْتَ بِهِ عَلَيَّ' (O Son of the Messenger of Allah, my joy has increased greatly due to the favor you have bestowed upon me). O my Master, O Son of the Messenger, my happiness, my joy, my delight has increased greatly. The favor you have done upon me has increased my happiness significantly. And then he asks further: 'فَمَا سُنَّةُ الْجَارِيَةِ فِيهِ مِنَ الْخَضِرِ وَذِي الْقَرْنَيْنِ' (What is the ongoing tradition in him from Khidr and Dhu al-Qarnayn?). He asked about what the Imam had said in the previous episode, asking: 'O my Master, tell me, what is that ongoing tradition (Sunnah)? What is that...' ...what is that ongoing tradition that is found in Imam-e-Zaman from Khidr (a.s.) and Dhu al-Qarnayn (a.s.)? What is that ongoing tradition? So the Imam replied, saying: 'Faqala tulul-ghaybah' (He said, the length of the Occultation). That the long Occultation that Imam-e-Zaman will have, it bears a resemblance to them, to Khidr (a.s.) and Dhu al-Qarnayn (a.s.). He further says that he asked the Imam again, 'O Son of the Messenger! Will his Occultation really be long?' Meaning he himself is thinking about the Occultation and asking the Imam if his Occultation will really be long. So the Imam replied, 'Ay, wa Rabbi!' (Yes, by my Lord!). Yes, by my Lord, 'Hatta yarja'a an hadhal amre aksarul-kalina bihi' (Until those who believe in this affair will turn back). The Imam says, yes, to the extent that those who believe in this affair, who are convinced of this affair—meaning those who are convinced of Imam-e-Zaman, convinced of his Occultation, convinced of his Imamate—they will turn back. The Occultation will be so long that in this long Occultation, they will turn away from the Imamate, from the Imam, and from his Occultation. 'Wala yabqa' (And no one will remain) 'illa man akhadhallahu azza-wa-jall ahdahu le-wilayatina' (Except for those from whom Allah has taken a covenant for our Wilayah). No one else will be saved except them; only they will be saved. Meaning, how firmly we must hold onto the rope of Wilayah in this era of Occultation, otherwise, the Imam says no one else will be saved. ...from whom Allah has taken a covenant for our Wilayah. Then he further says, 'Wa kataba fi qalbihil-iman' (And in whose heart Allah has written faith), and those on whose hearts Allah has written faith, they—meaning we should also keep praying to Allah in this era of Occultation that He keeps us firm on this belief of Imamate in this era of Occultation—and he says, 'Wa ayyadahu be-ruhin-minhu' (And supported them with a spirit from Him), and those whose faith Allah has strengthened through the Spirit. The Imam further states, 'Ya Ahmad ibn Ishaq!' (O Ahmad ibn Ishaq!). 'Haza amrum-min-amrillah' (This affair is from the affair of Allah), this matter is from the matters of Allah. 'Wa sirrum-min-sirrillah' (And this secret is from the secret of Allah). Meaning regarding Imam-e-Zamana. He further says, 'Wa gaybum-min-gaybillah' (And this Occultation is from the Occultation of Allah). 'Fa-khuz ma ataytuka' (So take what I have given you), so take what we are giving you. 'Wa-ktum hu wa-kum minash-shakirin' (And hide it and be among the grateful). Meaning, take what the Imam is giving, and not everything is such that you announce it to the people; keep everything. The belief you have, keep it safe with yourself. Keep the secrets of the Imam hidden from people and be among the grateful. And the Imam states a very beautiful sentence further, which every Shia should understand, that whoever keeps himself, his faith, and his belief firmly connected to Imam-e-Zaman during the Occultation, the Imam says to him—the Imam said to Ahmad ibn Ishaq—'Takum ma'ana ghadan fi illiyyin' (You will be with us tomorrow in Illiyyin, the highest heaven). Respected brothers! Many things have been presented before you regarding the Light (Noor). Regarding the hadiths of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), that the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) are Light. In this era, especially Imam-e-Zaman is Light, and just before this, our brother stated that this era, which is the era of Occultation, is an era of testing. When it is an era of testing, then obviously, we have some responsibilities in this era of testing, and among those responsibilities, I want to present one responsibility to you, which is 'Taslim' (submission). Now, to explain this submission, we take the help of the Book of God, that Allah (s.w.t.) is stating in Surah an-Nisa, verse number 65, that 'Fala wa rabbika' (But no, by your Lord), 'la yuminuna hatta' (they will not believe until), 'yuhakkimuka fi ma shajara bainahum' (they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves), they make you the judge, the ruler, in the disputes that arise between them. 'Summa la yajidu fi anfusihim harajan mimma qazayta' (Then they find no discomfort within themselves from what you have decided), then whatever decision you make, they do not feel any constriction in their hearts about it. 'Wa yusallimu taslima' (And submit in full submission). Now, regarding this verse, let us take the help of the traditions of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) as to what the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) have stated in the interpretation of this verse. So we go to the door of Imam as-Sadiq (a.s.), and after going to the door of the Imam (a.s.), we ask the Imam (a.s.) to clarify this verse a little. So when we look at the traditions of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), we find what the Master has stated regarding this verse. So in one hadith, the Imam (a.s.) states: 'Law anna qawman abadullaha wahdahu la sharika lah' (If some people worship Allah alone, having no partner), and acknowledge His Oneness and consider Him without a partner, 'wa aqamus-salata wa atuz-zakat' (and establish prayer and give Zakat), and establish prayer and pay Zakat, 'wa hajjul-baita wa samu shahra-ramazan' (and perform Hajj and fast the month of Ramadan), and perform Hajj and keep the fasts of Ramadan, then regarding any matter of Allah or regarding any matter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they say, 'I wish something else had been done against this' or some other things had come. Just as he thinks, 'Aw wajadu dhalika fi qulubihim' (Or they find that in their hearts), and as soon as they bring this thought into their hearts, 'la-kanu bi-dhalika mushrikin' (they immediately become polytheists). Then the Imam (a.s.) recited this same verse: 'Fala wa rabbika la yuminuna hatta yuhakkimuka fi ma shajara bainahum summa la yajidu fi anfusihim harajan mimma qazayta wa yusallimu taslima' (But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves, then they find no discomfort within themselves from what you have decided, and submit in full submission). And after that, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Alaikum bi-taslim' (It is incumbent upon you to adopt submission). Meaning the result here is that whatever things the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) have stated, and especially the things that Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) stated, from Asir to Ghadir, and especially the things emphasized in the sermon of Ghadir—meaning from the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to the Wilayah of Hazrat-e-Hujjah (a.j.t.f.s.)—a person should submit to everything. Submit to the Wilayah of the Imamate of all 12 Imams from the first to the last, and humans have no authority to present any opinion against the decision made by Allah and His Messenger. Submission. It has different levels. Every human, based on their capacity, as much as they can do, submits to Allah and the Imam accordingly. But let us see what the Imam's expectation is of us. There is a person named Mansur, who asks our sixth Imam, Imam as-Sadiq (a.s.): 'Ma aksara ma asma'u minka sayyidi dhikra Salman al-Farsi' (How often I hear from you, my master, the mention of Salman al-Farsi). He says, 'O my Master! I hear you mentioning Salman al-Farsi so frequently.' Meaning, if the Imam can mention Salman al-Farsi frequently, then why shouldn't we frequently mention Imam Ali (a.s.)? However, the Imam does not answer him, but rather rebukes him, corrects him. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'La taqul Salman al-Farsi walakin qul Salman al-Muhammadi' (Do not say Salman al-Farsi, but say Salman al-Muhammadi). 'Do you know why we remember Salman so much?' Mansur says, 'No, Master.' The Imam (a.s.) now states three qualities of Salman al-Muhammadi. First: 'Isarahu hawa Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) ala hawa nafsihi' (His preferring the desire of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) over his own desire). The first one, which is related to our topic, is that Salman al-Muhammadi always preferred the desires of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) over his own desires. Meaning, if he saw what Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) wanted, he never looked at what he himself wanted. He always preferred Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and did not prefer himself. Do we, in this era today, prefer Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) and his desires over ourselves and our own desires? The Imam (a.s.) now moves forward. The second quality that the Imam (a.s.) states: Salman al-Muhammadi liked to sit with the poor, rather than spending his time with those who are wealthy and powerful. Do we also, in this era today, spend our time with those who are counted among the poor, or do we like to spend our time with those who are rich and famous? And the last thing that the Imam... Salutations are very dear to Janab Salman. This is because of 'Hubbul lil ilmi wal ulama' (love for knowledge and the scholars), and this point is especially for the youth: Janab Salman-e-Mohammadi loved knowledge and used to sit in the gatherings of scholars. Therefore, it is necessary for us to acquire knowledge from the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). We should turn to the scholars so that we can acquire the knowledge of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) from them. When the Imam (a.s.) states these three characteristics, he then gives evidence of Janab Salman's faith, saying, "Inna Salman-a kana 'abdan salihan" (Indeed, Salman was a righteous servant), that Janab Salman is an 'Abd-e-Saleh, a good servant. "Hanifan musliman" (inclined to truth, a Muslim), that he is upon the Deen-e-Hanif and is a true Muslim. "Wa ma kana minal mushrikin" (and he was not of the polytheists). Let us examine ourselves against this hadith to see if we meet this standard or not. To be 'Tasleem' (submissive) before the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Another aspect of this submission is to submit before their statements—what they have stated—and not to deny them. In this regard, there is a tradition from the fourth Imam, Hazrat Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.), and Sheikh Saduq (ar) brings this tradition in Kamaluddin. Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) says, "Inna deenallahi 'azza wa jall" (Indeed, the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic) "la yusabu bil-'uqulin-naqisah" (cannot be attained through deficient intellects), meaning that this religion cannot be attained through imperfect intellect. Meaning, if a person, due to their limited thinking or crooked thinking, thinks that they can attain the religion, they will not be able to do so. It is impossible; this thing is impossible. "Wal-ara'il batilah" (and false opinions), and if they think they can attain the religion based on their own false opinions, they will not be able to. "Wal-maqayisil fasidah" (and corrupt scales/standards), and if they follow corrupt scales—'maqayis' meaning those scales or the 'mizan' (balance) that determines what is right and what is wrong. If their scale itself is wrong—for example, if a person wants to measure a fever, and the thermometer is fraudulent, meaning the thermometer itself is corrupt and not working correctly—they will never be able to measure the fever correctly. Similarly, the Imam says that if the scale to measure the religion is corrupt, is not correct, then the person will not be able to reach the religion. "Wa la yusabu illa bit-taslim" (and it cannot be attained except through submission). Only when a person totally and completely submits themselves before the statements and commands of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will they be able to understand the religion, and only then will they be able to attain it. In other words, if it is said, the Imam (a.s.) is saying that my opinion and my heart's desire have no place in the religion. If you want to understand the religion, then understand it through those who are the people of the religion, the people of the Reminder (Ahl-e-Zikr), the Infallible Imams (a.s.), and their statements. Then the Imam says, "Faman sallama lana" (So whoever submits to us), whoever submits before us, "salima" (will be safe). In reality, they will be safe and sound. "Wa maniqtada bina" (and whoever follows us), whoever follows us, "hudiya" (will be guided). Meaning they will receive guidance. "Wa man kana ya'malu bil-qiyasi war-ra'yi halaka" (And whoever acts according to analogy and opinion will perish). And if someone tries to act according to their own analogy, their own guesswork—that 'my heart says so'—and tries to act on their own opinion without looking at the perspective of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) want in every matter—if they try to move forward according to their own will, then what will happen? What will be the result? 'Halaka' (perish), they will perish. "Wa man wajada fi nafsihi" (And whoever finds within themselves) — this is a very important thing. The Imam says, "Wa man wajada fi nafsihi" — if someone finds this thing within themselves, what thing? "Shay'an mimma naqulu aw naqdi bihi harajan" (something of what we say or judge, a difficulty/doubt). If we have made a decision on something or stated something, and if they have even the slightest doubt or the slightest difficulty in their heart regarding our decision or our hadith—you know, if it is becoming difficult for them to accept our hadith. They feel that 'No, the Imam could not have said this. This is against the temperament of the Messenger of Allah.' As if they have understood the entire temperament of the Messenger of Allah. They are aware of everything regarding the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). So, they are trying to understand the hadiths based on their own intellect and their own scales, rather than accepting what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have stated as it is. So what will happen? "Kafara billadhi anzalas-sab'al mathani wal-qur'anal 'azim" (They have disbelieved in the One who revealed the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses and the Great Quran). They have denied all those things. They have denied that Being, that God, who revealed the Sab-e-Mathani (Surah Fatiha) and this Great Quran. They will deny that Allah. Meaning, denying the Ahlulbayt is denying Allah. Denying the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt is denying Allah. And then, in the end, the Imam says, and in what state will this denial happen? "Wa huwa la ya'lam" (and they do not even know). They won't even know when they went outside the circle of the religion. When they denied Allah. This is such a grave and heavy matter; it is such a tough thing. A person should not take this lightly. Because if a person does not submit before the command of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), before their word, before their action, then what will happen? They will perish. Come, viewers, let us also mention the second responsibility, which is love, and in this regard, many hadiths and traditions are found in the teachings of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). We want to present a hadith here that is being narrated from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), in which he says, "Likulli shay'in asas" (For everything, there is a foundation), and then he says, "Wa asasul-islam" (And the foundation of Islam is) "hubbuna Ahlulbayt" (our love, the Ahlulbayt). Meaning, the love of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) is the foundation of Islam. Here, the Infallible Imams, or Imam al-Baqir (a.s.), presented a universal rule to the entire Muslim Ummah that everything has a base. Right? There is nothing in the world that does not have a base. A building has a foundation; knowledge has a foundation, principles, and rules. Action has a foundation, which is intention. Similarly, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) is stating here that Islam also has a foundation, and that foundation is our love. And if one wants to see the practical application of this love—the love of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.)—what is meant by love? Is just taking their name enough? No, rather, it is acquiring their 'Ma'rifat' (recognition), submitting before them—which was our first point—and turning to them for everything. Let us present another hadith in which the Imam (a.s.) is stating—this hadith is narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)—that he says, "Inna fawqa kulli 'ibadatin 'ibadah" (Indeed, above every act of worship is another act of worship). "Wa hubbuna Ahlulbayt afdalul-'ibadah" (And our love, the Ahlulbayt, is the most excellent act of worship). In this hadith, the Imam (a.s.) is stating a scale, a hierarchy, that there are many different acts of worship, and they have different degrees. But if there is any most excellent act of worship in the sight of Allah, it is our love. Now, let us present a hadith regarding the requirements of love, in which the Imam (a.s.) says, "Tuba li-shi'atina" (Glad tidings for our Shias), "al-mutamassikina bi-hablina fi ghaybati qa'imina" (those who hold firmly to our rope during the occultation of our Qa'im), those who hold firmly to our rope, especially in that era which is the era of occultation, in the era of the occultation of our Mahdi, and who remain steadfast with us and are walking upon our Wilayat. And then, the most important sentence is coming here: "Wal-bara'ati min a'da'ina" (and disassociation from our enemies). So, the requirement of love is not just love—that their praise and glorification be done—but also that disassociation and 'Bara'at' (repudiation) be expressed from their enemies. Here, the Imam (a.s.) is pointing towards that, that they keep 'Bara'at' from our enemies. Who will these Shias be? Who will be our lovers who are expressing love for us? These will be the people who will not just announce their love for us but will also express 'Bara'at' from our enemies. Upon that, the Imam (a.s.) says, "Ula'ika minna wa nahnu minhum" (Those are from us, and we are from them). "Qad radu bina a'immatan" (They have accepted us as Imams and chosen contentment). Now, when they have accepted us as Imams, the Imam (a.s.) states, "Wa radina bihim shi'atan" (And we are pleased that they are our Shias). Then the Imam (a.s.) gives glad tidings twice: "Fa tuba lahum thumma tuba lahum" (So glad tidings for them, then glad tidings for them), "wa hum wallahi ma'ana fi darajatina yawmal qiyamah" (and by Allah, they will be with us at our station on the Day of Judgment). This hadith shows that love alone is not enough, Wilayat alone is not enough; along with Wilayat, a person must... Especially the one who loves the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), that they should express 'Bara'at' and express hatred for their enemies, everywhere, at all times, every moment. One requirement of love is also that the one we love, the one who is our beloved, we remember them, feel their absence, and weep for them. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) asks his companion Fudayl, "Tajlisuna wa tuhaddisuna?" (Do you sit and have discussions?). Fudayl says, "Qala, na'am, ju'iltu fidak" (Yes, may I be sacrificed for you, my Mawla). Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) says, "Inna tilkal majalis uhibbuha fa ahyu amrana" (Indeed, I love those gatherings, so revive our affairs), O Fudayl, we love such gatherings, so revive our affairs. "Fa rahimallahu man ahya amrana" (May Allah have mercy on those who revive our affairs), and after that, the Imam prays for those who organize such gatherings, that may Allah have mercy on them, may He send His mercy upon those who revive our affairs. After that, the Imam (a.s.) says, "Ya Fudayl, man dhakarana aw dhukirna 'indahu fa kharaja min 'aynihi mithlu janahis-dhubabi ghafarallahu lahu dhunubahu wa law kanat akthara min zabadil-bahr" (O Fudayl, if someone remembers us or we are mentioned in their presence, and from their eye comes a tear equal to the wing of a fly, Allah will forgive their sins, even if they were more than the foam of the sea). So, this is that separation from Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) due to which a person remembers them, weeps, and bears all hardships in their separation. Even if a tear comes from their eye in the separation of the Imam, they will become the recipient of this hadith, and Allah will forgive all their sins. Apart from this, we should recite those supplications and Ziyarat in the Imam's occultation that are attributed to the Imam (a.s.), some of which have been mentioned in our 'Panah-e-Kainat' series. Another supplication attributed to Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is Dua-e-Ahad. We should recite Dua-e-Ahad every morning for the Imam because, in this supplication, we are renewing our allegiance (Tajdid-e-Bay'at) with the Imam, renewing our oath that 'O Imam, we will spend our lives in your service, and even if we die, by the permission of Allah, we will rise from our graves to help you.' So, we should recite this supplication repeatedly. Another famous supplication attributed to the Imam (a.s.) is Dua-e-Nudba. Dua-e-Nudba is the supplication that has been emphasized to be recited on four Eids. Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Eid-e-Ghadir, and Friday. These are four such days that are attributed to the Imam (a.s.). Therefore, we should definitely recite this supplication on these days because, in this supplication, we remember the Imam (a.s.), feel their absence, and weep for them. There are sentences in this Dua-e-Nudba where we call the Imam with these titles: "Aynat-talibu bi-damil-maqtuli bi-Karbala" (Where is the seeker of the blood of the one killed in Karbala?), and after that, remembering the Imam, we say, "Layta shi'ri aynastaqarat bikannawa" (I wish I knew where you are residing). And we also express this separation from the Imam by saying, "'Azizun 'alayya an aral-khalqa wa la tura" (It is difficult for me to see all the people but not see you, O my Mawla). "'Azizun 'alayya an abkiyaaka wa yajriyo lakal wara" (It is difficult for me that I weep for you, but some people disappoint you). After that, we also say, "Hal ilayka ya ibna Ahmad sabilun fa tulqa" (Is there any way to reach you, O Son of Ahmad, so that I may meet you?). "Unzur ilaina nazratan rahima, unzur ilaina nazratan rahima" (Look upon us with a merciful gaze, look upon us with a merciful gaze). A person can remember the Imam in two ways. One is individual, as we have just seen; a person can recite Dua-e-Ahad, Dua-e-Nudba, and other supplications, or recite Ziyarat. The second method is collective remembrance. Invite people towards the remembrance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), and this has a distinct importance. Jamil ibn Darraj narrates from Mu'attib, who was a servant of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), that Mu'attib said, "Sami'atuhu yaqul" (I heard him saying). Mu'attib says I heard Imam Sadiq (a.s.) saying this, and to whom? To one of his companions, another companion named Dawud ibn Sirhan. The Imam says, "Ya Dawud" (O Dawud), the Imam is giving a message through this hadith. This is a message for all of us. The Imam (a.s.) says, "Ya Dawud, ablih mawaliyya anni salam" (O Dawud, convey my greetings to my followers). "Wa anni aqul" (And tell them that I have said this), meaning Sadiq-e-Aale Muhammad (a.s.) is saying this, "Rahimallahu abdan ijtama'a ma'a akhar" (May Allah have mercy on a servant who meets with another servant), meaning two people gather, "Fa tazakara amrana" (and discuss our affair, narrate our hadiths). Meaning they remember, discuss our hadiths, discuss our affair, and converse regarding Wilayah. "Fa inna salisuhuma malakun" (For the third among them is an angel). So when these two people are sitting together and conversing, the third one who joins them is an angel, and what does that angel do? "Yastaghfiru lahuma" (He seeks forgiveness for both of them). An angel is seeking forgiveness; look, angels are infallible (Ma'sum). Allah never rejects the prayer of an infallible. This means if we discuss the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and narrate their virtues, angels will come there and pray for those who discuss the virtues of the Ahlulbayt, who invite one another towards their Imam of the time. Angels will pray and seek forgiveness for such people. And then the Imam says, "Wa ma ijtama'a ithnani 'ala dhikrina" (And no two people gather for our remembrance) except that what happens? "Illa bahallahu ta'ala bihima al-mala'ikata" (Except that Allah the Almighty boasts about them to the angels). Allah takes pride. Allah expresses pride before His angels for those two servants who gathered, what are they doing? They are remembering the Ahlulbayt, remembering their Imam, and calling people towards the Imam. "Fa idha ijtama'tum" (So when you gather), then the Imam says, giving an order, "Fashtaghilu bidh-dhikr" (then busy yourselves with remembrance). Meaning, narrate this remembrance, narrate our hadiths to one another, that is all. There is no need to do any other work, just narrate our hadiths. Whenever you meet, what should be the purpose of your meeting? The remembrance of Ahlulbayt. This should not be for other worldly things, from which no reward will be gained, and in which nothing will be achieved except wasting time. If you are gathering, then remember the Ahlulbayt. Then the Imam says, "Fa inna fi ijtima'ikum wa mujakaratikum ahya'ana" (For in your gathering and your discussion is the revival of our affair). This meeting of yours and remembering us, narrating these hadiths to one another, is the cause of our life. Meaning, it keeps us alive. In a way, since the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are light (Nur), therefore, a person receives life from this. The affair of the Ahlulbayt, their hadiths, and their Wilayah become alive. Then the Imam says, "Wa khayrun-nasi min ba'dina man dhakara bi-amrina" (And the best of people after us are those who discuss our affair). They narrate them, and invite others towards our remembrance. Therefore, these are the best of people. So try, and this is the Imam's command, see, it is the Imam's command for all of us. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) expects this from his Shias, that when our Shias gather, they will not talk about this and that. When our Shias gather, they will only talk about us. Therefore, this is one of the most important responsibilities during the occultation (Ghaybah) that we ourselves remember the Ahlulbayt and bring others towards the remembrance of the Ahlulbayt. Remember your Imam yourself, and encourage others to remember their Imam, encourage them. And in this regard, among the supplications of the occultation, among the supplications of this era of occultation, there is one important supplication which is called Dua dar Ghaybat (Supplication during Occultation). This is a supplication that begins like this: "Allahumma arrifni nafsak" (O Allah, make me know Yourself), it begins in this way. Let us, through that supplication, through one of the phrases of that supplication, conclude this final episode of our series and this series. In which a believing servant, in this era of occultation, prays to his Lord regarding his Imam: "Allahumma wala taslubnal yaqina lituli amadi fi ghaybatihi" (O Allah, do not take away our certainty due to the long duration of his occultation), O Lord, do not snatch away the certainty we have in our hearts regarding the Imam-e-Zaman due to his prolonged occultation. May it not happen that because the occultation is long, our certainty in him fades away. Do not snatch that certainty from us. "Wa inqita'i khabarihi anna" (And the cutting off of his news from us), and since no news of him is reaching us, no one is bringing us news of where he is, in what state he is, how he is. Because this news is not reaching us, therefore, O Lord, still keep our certainty in him intact. Do not snatch it from us. "Wala tunsina dhikrahu wa intizara" (And do not make us forget his remembrance and his waiting). May it never happen that we forget our Imam, our Imam of the time, and forget his waiting. Always spend every moment in his waiting. "Wal imana wa quwwatal yaqini fi zuhuri" (And keep our faith and the strength of our certainty in his reappearance). May faith never leave our hearts. And the certainty in his reappearance, the strength of our certainty, we have complete and intense certainty that he will definitely come. Do not make us forget our certainty in his coming. That this thing, this matter, should always be in our memory that the Imam will come. "Wa du'a lahu" (And praying for him), and never let us forget to pray for him. O Lord, may every day that passes, every night that passes, we remain in a state of prayer for our Imam of the time, for our Imam-e-Asr (a.s.). Keep praying for him, keep reciting Salawat for him, keep reciting the Dua "Allahumma kun li-waliyyika" for him. Keep reciting the Dua "Allahumma aslih abdaka" for him. Keep reciting supplications for him, keep working on his behalf. Keep reciting the Tasbih of Salawat. May we keep performing all these recommended acts (Mustahabbat) for our Imam so that his remembrance is always with us. May we never forget his remembrance. "Wassalata 'alayhi" (And sending blessings upon him), O Lord, grant us the ability to send blessings upon him. May his Salawat never leave our tongues. Until when? "Hatta la yuqannitana tulu ghaybatihi min zuhurihi wa qiyamihi" (Until the length of his occultation does not make us despair of his reappearance and his uprising). Until it never happens, O Lord, do not let it happen that because his occultation is long, there is time in his reappearance, there is time in his uprising, and it is taking time, so because of that, never let us fall prey to despair. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum wa la'na a'da'ahum ajma'in. O God! By the sake of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time. May You grant acceptance to this small effort of ours in Your presence. May You make our Imam pleased and satisfied with us. Keep our Imam away from every calamity and evil. And O Lord, in the end, this is the only prayer that count us all among the true servants and helpers of our Imam and grant us the ability to always keep remembering our Imam. Amin Ya Rabbal Alamin. You are requested to pay attention to the Ziyarat because immediately after the Ziyarat, our daily winners will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Insha Allah. Assalamu 'alayka ayyuhal 'alamul mansubu wal 'ilmul masbubu, wal ghawthu war-rahmatul wasi'atu wa'dan ghayra makdubin. Assalamu 'alayka hina taqumu. Assalamu 'alayka hina ta'cudu. Assalamu 'alayka ayyuhal muqaddamul ma'mul. Assalamu 'alayka bi-jawami'is-salam. Ashhadu ya Mawlaya anni ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lahu wa anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluhu la habiba illa huwa wa ahluhu. Wa ushhiduka ya Mawlaya anna 'Aliyan Amirul Mu'minina hujjatu, wal Hasana hujjatu, wal Husayna hujjatu, wa 'Aliyyabnal Husayni hujjatu, wa Muhammadabna 'Aliyan hujjatu, wa Ja'farabna Muhammadin hujjatu, wa Musabna Ja'farin hujjatu, wa 'Aliyyabna Musa hujjatu, wa Muhammadabna 'Aliyan hujjatu, wa 'Aliyyabna Muhammadin hujjatu, wal Hasanabna 'Aliyan hujjatu, wa ashhadu annaka Hujjatullahi. The beginning and the end, and that your return is a truth in which there is no doubt. On the day when a soul's faith will not benefit it if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith. And that death is a truth, and Munkar and Nakir are a truth, and I bear witness that the resurrection is a truth, and the rising is a truth, and the path (Sirat) is a truth, and the observation point (Mirsad) is a truth, and the scale (Mizan) is a truth, and the gathering (Hashr) is a truth, and the reckoning (Hisab) is a truth, and Paradise and Hell are a truth, and the promise and the threat regarding them are a truth. chapters.title: Quiz Instructions and Introduction
chapters.summary: The speaker provides instructions for the mega quiz, emphasizing the importance of correct answers for the lucky draw and introduces the topic of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the light of Allah.

chapters.title: Imams as the Light of Allah
chapters.summary: This section explores the theological concept that the Imams are the 'Noor' (light) of Allah, referencing Ziyarat and Al-Kafi to explain their role in guiding believers.

chapters.title: Quranic Interpretation of Noor
chapters.summary: The speaker analyzes Surah Taghabun verse 8 and Surah Zumar verse 69, explaining that the 'light' mentioned in the Quran refers to the Imams of the Ahlul-Bayt.

chapters.title: The Imam as the Light of the World
chapters.summary: The Imam (a.s.) is described as the ultimate source of light that clarifies all realities, rendering the physical sun and moon unnecessary upon his reappearance.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Divine Guidance
chapters.summary: Humanity requires guidance for both worldly and spiritual success, and following anyone other than the divinely appointed Imam leads to misguidance.

chapters.title: Wilayah as the Foundation of Religion
chapters.summary: Imam Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that true religion is defined by the Wilayah of the divinely appointed Imams, not merely by external good deeds or character traits.

chapters.title: Darkness vs. Light in Divine Wilayah
chapters.summary: The Imam explains that Allah brings the believers from darkness into light through the Wilayah of the just Imams, while those who follow Taghut are led from the light of Islam into the darkness of disbelief.

chapters.title: The Test of Occultation and Denial of Birth
chapters.summary: The lecture warns that denying the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is a grave error that leads to misguidance, as the Imam's presence is essential for the earth's existence.

chapters.title: The Long Occultation and Divine Covenant
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) explains that the long Occultation of the 12th Imam is a divine secret and a test, where only those with a firm covenant of Wilayah and faith will remain steadfast.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Total Submission (Taslim)
chapters.summary: True faith requires absolute submission to the decisions of Allah and His Messenger, as any internal resistance to their commands is equated to polytheism.

chapters.title: Qualities of Salman al-Muhammadi
chapters.summary: The Imam explains that Salman al-Muhammadi is a model of faith due to his preference for the Imam's desires, his humility with the poor, and his dedication to seeking knowledge.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Submission to Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: True religion cannot be attained through personal opinion or analogy, but only through total submission to the teachings of the Infallible Imams.

chapters.title: Love and Disassociation as Foundations
chapters.summary: The foundation of Islam is the love of the Ahlulbayt, which must be accompanied by adherence to their guidance and disassociation from their enemies.

chapters.title: True Shias and the Virtue of Remembrance
chapters.summary: True Shias are defined by their love, Bara'at from enemies, and the act of remembering the Ahlulbayt, which leads to divine forgiveness and high status.

chapters.title: Supplications During Occultation
chapters.summary: Reciting specific supplications like Dua-e-Ahad and Dua-e-Nudba helps believers maintain their connection and renew their allegiance to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).

chapters.title: Collective Remembrance and Its Rewards

title: Tabarra Ki Wajah Se Shia Maare Jaate Hain? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the theological necessity of Tabarra (disassociation from the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt) within the Shia faith. It emphasizes that while practicing Tabarra may lead to persecution or martyrdom, it is considered an essential component of Wilayah. The speaker references a narration from Imam Reza (a.s.) to illustrate that such sacrifice is viewed as a high honor rather than a reason to abandon one's beliefs.
content:
...gave their lives in this path. Did they practice Tabarra? Yes, indeed they did, because they knew that Wilayah is incomplete without Tabarra. But to them, Allah's religion was more precious than their lives, especially the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). When someone complained to Imam Reza (a.s.), 'You sit here and say these things, while over there, the blood of the Shias is dripping from the swords of the enemies,' Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Indeed, Allah has a valley of gold which is guarded by Allah's weak creatures like ants, but even the powerful cannot reach there despite wanting to. Therefore, if someone attains martyrdom because of Tabarra, it is a great honor for them.'
Tabarra is an essential requirement for the completeness of Wilayah.
