title: 28 Safar 1442 | Majlis e Aza | Shahadate Hazrat Rasool e Akram & Imam Hasan (as) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi commemorates the martyrdom of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Hasan (a.s.), focusing on the moral and spiritual foundations of Islam. The discourse emphasizes the Prophet's mission to perfect human character, the necessity of truthfulness, and the importance of maintaining trusts despite societal pressures. It further explores the historical conspiracies faced by the Prophet and his family, highlighting the significance of Wilayah and the profound sacrifices made by the Ahlulbayt.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah... There is no power nor strength except with Allah... Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best disposer of affairs. Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds. Peace be upon you, [O Ahl al-Bayt]... May Allah's blessings be upon him and his immaculate progeny. O Allah, hasten the reappearance of our master... From here... [garbled Arabic/Urdu phrases]... Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)... Amma ba'd (furthermore)... Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala... this noble verse... in that noble verse, addressing [the Prophet], He says: 'Indeed, you... ...addressing [the Prophet], He says: 'Indeed, you are of a great moral character' (Quran 68:4). Indeed, you possess such morals and character that... the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself said: 'I was sent only to perfect noble character.' I was sent so that I may take moral heights to their completion, to the stage of perfection, to complete it... and this is the martyrdom of... This is very amazing. Inshallah, if Allah grants the opportunity... the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared the aim and purpose of his life to be reforming the morals of the people. He explained the purpose of being sent, and made it his goal. In whichever society he lived, his concern was to reform the people. One must keep in mind among what kind of people the Prophet was. When we describe it, first of all... What was your condition before Islam? You were on the worst religion, and you lived in the worst manner. In this life, there was idol worship, shedding each other's blood, and no respect for women or honor. In such an environment and among such people, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came, and the Prophet began to transform such people. When you look at how the Prophet taught people everyday small things... Before moving forward, please understand that Allah... has mentioned morals in about 12 traditions... ...Let's begin with the testaments of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), where he advised about certain things to keep in mind. Look at Hazrat Abu Dharr or Hazrat Salman (r.a.). This means that... and we should also... 'My Lord commanded me...' In all these things in the world... 'My Lord commanded me...' in all these things in the world, that I should only look at those who are below me [in worldly status], and not look at those who are above me. When I look at those who are below me—for instance, if Allah gave me a thousand and another person less—in worldly matters, we should look at those below us... But this should not be the case for the Hereafter. For the Hereafter, we must look at those who are above us, so that we can make them our role models and exemplars. Even the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... ...to follow the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). After that, he says: 'And He advised me to love the destitute, the poor, the needy, those who are helpless, homeless, and have no worldly wealth.' It was not just to help them, but to love them. And what is the first requirement of love? To meet them; a person wants to meet the one they love as much as possible. The second requirement of love is that one should improve the condition of the beloved, remove their shortcomings, improve their situation, and bring about such reform in their life that, at the very least, they come on par with me. So here he says... ...'Love the destitute, and as for your relatives, prioritize their rights.' 'And He commanded me to speak the truth, even if it is bitter.' No matter how bitter it may be... but since our vision is very limited, we try to achieve this in the world... But when we look at history, the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) from the first Imam to the last have been such that they always acted with truthfulness in the way of Allah, spoke the truth, even if they had to make great sacrifices for it. There are many such examples, but a person should always focus on the will of Allah. He advised me to practice Silah al-Rahm (maintaining family ties), to take the initiative yourself and maintain relations with your relatives, even if they turn their faces away. It is our responsibility to greet them; if they do not respond, that is their action, they will have to answer for it. Honor and humiliation are in the hands of Allah. If you look at the Holy Quran, what does Allah say? 'Say, O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will...' We need a good leader... 'You honor whom You will, and You humiliate whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are powerful over all things.' So when all honor is in the hands of Allah, why do we think like this? If we obey the commands of Allah and His Messenger, we will not be diminished; rather, the more we obey, the more we will shine, and people's love for us will increase. Allah has promised in the Quran that whoever has faith... and they do not fear the blame of any critic in the way of Allah. ...the blame of any critic. We often think, 'If we speak this truth, we might lose our status or resources.' We think like this. But if we hide this truth, have we ever thought about the consequences? Have we considered that if we do not convey that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appointed [his successor], Allah will be displeased? If you conceal this reality, have you ever thought about it? Some people say that speaking about these things will cause division. But our duty is to convey the truth to the people, to recognize the truth, and not to care about the world, nor care about what others say, and in the way of Allah... ...not to care about the blame of any critic in the way of Allah, even if they criticize, speak ill, or accuse us. We should never care about any of that. The only thing that is always most important is the pleasure of Allah. That is why, look at the status of Abu Dharr (r.a.). When the third caliph asked him, 'Which place do you hate the most?' Abu Dharr replied, 'Rabadhah,' because it was a place of ignorance and disbelief. The caliph said, 'Fine, then you shall be exiled there.' Look at this! He is a companion of the Prophet, and the one sitting on the Prophet's pulpit is sending a companion of the Prophet to a place he hates the most. And we are told to respect all companions! If so, who is disrespecting whom? When you reveal these historical facts... ...who is disrespecting whom? When you state these facts, people say, 'This is a dispute between two companions, it was an error of judgment (ijtihadi mistake).' Allahu Akbar! They call it an ijtihadi mistake! This is a matter of truth and falsehood. Is truth and falsehood just an ijtihadi mistake? If everything is just an ijtihadi mistake, then why do we have any disputes? If Yazid's actions were also an ijtihadi mistake, then why do we condemn him? Even Allah should not condemn him then! If Cain killed Abel, was that also an ijtihadi mistake? If all the crimes in history are labeled as ijtihadi mistakes, then the entire concept of truth and falsehood disappears, and there would be no dispute left. Anyway, when Abu Dharr was being exiled to Rabadhah, a decree was issued that no one should go with him to bid him farewell. Look at this! In Medina, there were thousands of Muslims, but because of this decree, no one came to bid farewell to this great companion of the Prophet, except for Commander of the Faithful [Imam Ali (a.s.)]... ...except for Commander of the Faithful [Imam Ali (a.s.)], Imam Hasan (a.s.), Imam Husayn (a.s.), Aqeel, and Salman (r.a.). They came to bid farewell to Abu Dharr. And what an extraordinary sentence the Master [Imam Ali (a.s.)] uttered while bidding him farewell! He said, 'O Abu Dharr, these people fear you because of your faith. Since you are a religious man, they fear you. They are worshippers of this world, and they fear a religious man. They are anxious because of you, and you fear them only for the sake of your religion, lest their love for this world corrupts your faith.' ...lest their love for this world corrupts your faith. In any case, Abu Dharr did not care about anyone. This is why when Ka'b al-Ahbar—whom many Muslims highly revere, who entered Islam in the 9th or 10th Hijri, and after the martyrdom of the Holy Prophet, was trying to interpret Islam according to his own whims—Abu Dharr hit him on the head with his staff, not caring that Ka'b was close to the ruling power and could get him punished. And similarly, in the court of Syria, in front of everyone, he did not fear the blame of any critic in the way of Allah. He used to frequently recite: 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'Aliyyil 'Azim' (There is no power nor strength except by Allah, the All-High, the Almighty). He kept repeating this phrase, which means there is no power or strength except through Allah, the All-High. And whatever happens in this world, whatever change occurs, is only through Allah. This phrase is 'a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.' When someone makes this treasure of Paradise a part of their life, they themselves become heavenly. That is why Abu Dharr used to repeat this constantly. Furthermore, in another Hadith, the Imam clearly states that the most beloved person to Allah is the one who... ...the most beloved person to Allah is the one who guards his prayers, is punctual in his prayers, never abandons them, and strives to perform them properly. This is the obligatory duty that Allah loves the most. He performs everything that Allah has made obligatory upon him, and he returns the trust. If he holds a trust, he does not commit treachery in it. If someone leaves some money or an item with him, his intention does not waver even slightly to use it or replace it later. He does not touch the trust at all. Look at how, after the Imam... Look at how the Imam explains the reason behind this. When someone is entrusted with something, Iblis immediately appoints his devils over him. And who are these devils? They are the rebellious, arrogant ones among his followers who commit transgressions against God and stand in opposition to Him. Iblis appoints these devils to go after him. So, do not ask about the state of that person! He is alone, and these devils are set upon him. What do they do? They mislead people and whisper to them, 'Go ahead, use a little bit of it...' They say, 'Use a little bit of it, use a little bit, take the money from where you need it,' and they keep compromising, to the extent that if one does not seek refuge in Allah, they get compromised. Then, Satan keeps misleading them until he ruins them and makes them commit a breach of trust, except for those individuals whom Allah protects. And upon whom does Allah descend His mercy? Allah protects those who constantly seek refuge in Him. They keep reciting supplications like: 'A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim' (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan). 'I seek refuge in Allah, the Almighty, from the accursed Satan, from the evil of Satan...' 'I seek refuge in the Lord of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and in Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)...' ...in Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) from all those things that are evil, which have been decreed and punished. And I seek refuge in Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) from the hands of those humans who committed such acts. It is not just about our own honor; the honor of others also exists. We have the honor of others to protect, and therefore we must take great care of it. God forbid, we should not violate others' honor. Asad al-Ghabah, volume 5, page 295, and four Majalis, and in this... ...Asad al-Ghabah, volume 5, page 295, and four Majalis, and in this way to his followers. All these things will bear fruit only when a person's beliefs (Aqeedah) are correct. A person has beliefs about God, about the Prophets, about the Imams, and most importantly, about faith (Iman) and Wilayah. The most important thing is Wilayah, about which the Prophet constantly emphasized to the people—the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). He emphasized that it is through this Wilayah that we have received everything in our beliefs, in our Monotheism (Tawheed), in our ethics (Akhlaq)... That is why at Ghadir Khumm, the Prophet announced: 'Man kunto mawlahu fa haza Aliyun mawlahu' (Whomsoever I am his master, this Ali is his master). Those who accept me as their Mawla, it is obligatory upon them to also accept Ali as their Mawla. ...obligatory upon them to accept Ali as their Mawla. When the Prophet announced the Wilayah, guardianship, and immediate Caliphate of the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) at Ghadir, those people who loved the world, who loved status and position, became restless. They started talking among themselves, 'Look, he has appointed Ali. He has made Ali his successor. Now, after him, Ali will become the leader, and this lineage will continue. Why don't we remove Ali from the way? But how long will we wait? The longer we wait, the more the Prophet will reinforce Ali's Wilayah and Caliphate. So let's do one thing: let's remove the Prophet himself from the way.' And this was not the first time they tried to remove the Prophet. Even before this, during his final days, they tried to remove him. When those attempts came to light—like when the Prophet was on the mountain, they tried to push him off the mountain so that he would be martyred, but they failed in that attempt. So then they made another attempt. After this, meaning after 18th Dhu al-Hijjah... what comes after Dhu al-Hijjah? Muharram. And what comes after Muharram? Safar. What comes after Muharram? Safar. An attempt was made to poison the Prophet. This conspiracy was hatched, and the Prophet was poisoned. During this time, verses like this were revealed: 'Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is slain, will you turn back on your heels?' Did Allah not know that the Prophet would be killed or die? This was a test for them. So this was the first time it became clear... 'If he dies or is slain...' meaning he would not just die a natural death, but rather his martyrdom would be brought about. The Prophet was martyred. And the second proof... The Prophet was martyred. And the second proof is the famous saying: 'There is none among us except that he is either killed by the sword or poisoned.' This was indeed done; he was poisoned. Now, when the Prophet was on his deathbed, on that day which is called 'Raziyyat al-Yoom al-Khamis' (The Tragedy of Thursday). 'Raziyyah' means tragedy, a great calamity. The Prophet said, 'Bring me a pen and paper (inkwell) so that I may write something for you after which you will never go astray.' But those individuals who were present there started creating a commotion, saying that the pen and paper should not be given, claiming (God forbid) that the Prophet... ...that the pen and paper should not be given, claiming (God forbid) that the Prophet is talking deliriously. When Muslims describe this betrayal, it is indeed a tragedy. They stopped the pen and paper from being given to the Prophet, saying (God forbid) that he is not in his right mind. But think about how painful this was, that the Prophet had to say, 'Get up and leave from here, leave my presence.' The Prophet knew what was going to happen after him. And Lady Zahra (a.s.) came and clung to the Prophet, weeping. She kept crying, 'O father, O father!' The Prophet held her to his chest, and Lady Zahra's tears flowed even more... ...and her tears flowed even more, falling upon the Prophet's body. The Prophet felt those tears and held her close to his chest. Then, the Prophet whispered something in Lady Zahra's (a.s.) ear, and her tears stopped, and she began to smile. Later, when someone asked, 'O Lady, when you were crying at that moment, why did you stop crying, and what was the reason for your smile?' She replied, 'My father told me, "Zahra, I am leaving this world very soon," which is why I was weeping. But then my father told me, "Zahra, from among my family, you will be the first to join me." So, out of the joy of this reunion, I smiled, knowing that I would not live long after the Prophet's departure.' O Princess of Grief! You were weeping while clinging to your father, and no one stopped you. But alas, when Sakina (a.s.) wept for her father, this four-year-old child—it is clearly written in several places... ...this child—it is clearly written in several places, some say a three-year-old child, some say a four-year-old child—she was slapped in the caravan. Whenever she wept, she was slapped. The executioners of Yazid slapped her so hard... Today is indeed like the evening of Qiyamah. This is the night of 28th Safar, the night of the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the martyrdom of the second Ma'sum [Imam Hasan (a.s.)]. Heart-wrenching tragedies (Masaib) are narrated about them. Let me describe it completely... ...Let me describe it completely. When Imam Hasan (a.s.) would vomit, pieces of his liver would come out with the vomit. The poison was tearing his body apart from the inside, because of which his face and his entire body had turned green. It was such a state that pieces of his liver were falling out, causing him immense pain. In this great calamity, Imam Hasan (a.s.) called for Imam Husayn (a.s.). Imam Husayn (a.s.) asked, 'O brother, why are you weeping?' And this King (Shah) is departing from the world. At that time, Imam Hussain... and there will be another... people will gather in thousands who will claim to be Muslims, but instead of helping us, they will fight against you, Hussain, and they will not show mercy, but rather they will [capture] your women... O Hussain, what will be your state then? Hussain is crying out to his Lord at that very moment... At that time, the heavens will weep blood for you, Hussain, and the wild beasts of the wilderness will weep for you, and even the fish in the depths of the sea will weep for you. O Hussain, the entire universe has mourned and is mourning for this, and will continue to mourn. Therefore, weep abundantly! Whoever wants to lament, whoever wants to mourn, whoever wants to weep loudly, let them weep and say: 'O Hussain! O Hussain!'... O Lord, relieve the worries of those who are distressed, and pay off the debts of those who are in debt... Those who are in debt, pay off their debts; those who are sick, grant them recovery. Wherever in the world believers are, protect their lives, wealth, and honor. O Lord, protect us from this epidemic that has spread throughout the world. O Lord, protect those who worship day and night, protect our scholars. O Lord of the worlds, grant us the visitation (Ziyarah) of Hussain in this world, and the intercession (Shafa'at) of Hussain and Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) in the hereafter...

title: Hajj Ko Mukammal Kaise Karein? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual necessity of concluding the Hajj pilgrimage with a Ziyarah to the Ahl al-Bayt. Citing a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker emphasizes that the visitation to the shrines of the Prophet's family is essential for the completion of the Hajj. The talk concludes with a prayer for the audience to be granted the opportunity to perform both the Hajj and the Ziyarah.
content:
It is narrated that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'When any of you performs Hajj, he should conclude his Hajj with our Ziyarah (visitation), for indeed this completes the Hajj.' May Almighty God grant us all the opportunity to perform the Hajj of the House of Allah and the Ziyarah of the shrines of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.
Hajj is considered incomplete without the Ziyarah of the Ahl al-Bayt.

title: Majlis 9 | Ma'refat-e-Imam (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the critical importance of Ma'refat (recognition) of the Imam as the foundation of faith and spiritual growth. The discourse emphasizes that true piety and worship are inseparable from the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, highlighting that divine guidance is channeled through these divinely appointed leaders. The session concludes with a poignant reflection on the tragedy of Karbala, specifically the sacrifice of Ali Asghar (a.s.), and underscores the parental duty to preserve the history and core beliefs of the Ahlulbayt for future generations.
content:
Hussain (A.S.) makes a small grave in the battlefield. Hussain (A.S.) makes a small grave in the battlefield. Hussain (A.S.) hides the second Mohsin in the dust. Hussain (A.S.) hides the second Mohsin in the dust. Hussain (A.S.) makes a small grave in the battlefield. He keeps putting soil on Asghar's body. He keeps putting soil on Asghar's body. And Hussain (A.S.) keeps looking towards the tents. Hussain (A.S.) makes a small grave in the battlefield. At the time of death, the small hands that had held on. At the time of death, the small hands that had held on. Now Hussain (A.S.) is pulling that hem away from Ali Asghar. Hussain (A.S.) makes a small grave in the battlefield. Hussain (A.S.) hides the second Mohsin in the dust. Hussain (A.S.) hides the second Mohsin in the dust. Hussain (A.S.) makes a small grave in the battlefield. For Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs. The best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. And the end is for the pious and those with certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of the prophets and messengers. The beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. May Allah bless him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, the Imam of the Age, the Master of our affair, our Master, our Mawla, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate friend, the protector of the fortress, and the relief for the distressed and the upright. May the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has said in the Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers. So race to [all that is] good. Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. May Allah bless you, O Aba Abdillah. May Allah bless you, O Aba Abdillah. May Allah bless you, O Aba Abdillah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The verse of the Quran that I had the honor of reciting, which I selected for these gatherings—of which today is the final gathering—this verse states: Allah the Almighty says, 'Fastabiqul Khairat' (So race to all that is good). Compete with one another, try to take the lead over one another in good deeds, in righteousness. Allah the Almighty repeatedly invites man in the Holy Quran towards felicity, that is, eternal bliss. That come towards Paradise. Allah continuously—if you study the verses of the Quran—just read verses 133 to 136 of Surah Al-e-Imran. See how Allah says in the Quran, 'Sari'u ila maghfiratin'. 'Sari'u' means run quickly, 'Sari'u' come quickly. Go quickly, 'Sari'u', towards what? 'Ila maghfiratin min Rabbikum' (Towards forgiveness from your Lord). Forgiveness, 'Maghfirah' means forgiveness. That you go quickly, right? Allah is inviting, Allah is calling. That come, come to the banquet of My forgiveness so that I may forgive you all. 'Maghfiratin min Rabbikum wa Jannatin' (Forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise), and come towards that Paradise, the width of which is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the pious. That Paradise whose width is the distance between the heavens and the earth. That is its width, which no one can estimate. 'U'iddat lil-Muttaqin' (Prepared for the pious). Allah has prepared this for the people of piety. In the light of traditions, the first instance of the people of piety, the very first example, is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Meaning, who is the Muttaqi (pious)? The one in whom Wilayah is found. Without Wilayah, there can be no Taqwa. And after that, the Quran says, 'Alladhina yunfiquna fis-sarra'i waz-darra'—those who spend in the way of Allah, in times of ease and in times of hardship. 'Wal-kaziminal-ghayz'—and those who... And they control it, they restrain it. 'Wal-'afina 'anin-nas'—and they pardon people, they forgive them, they forgive them. 'Wallahu yuhibbul-muhsinin'—and Allah loves those who do good. Insha'Allah, if there is no time today, we will try to explain this in the light of traditions; we will explain what is meant by 'Muhsinin'. What is meant by those who do good? 'Wallahu yuhibbul-muhsinin'. And further, Allah says, 'Walladhina idha fa'alu fahishatan aw zalamu anfusahum'—and those who, if they commit an indecent act or wrong themselves, 'fahisha' meaning very bad deeds or any other sin, 'zalamu anfusahum'—meaning if any sin is committed by them, then what do they do? 'Dhakarullaha'—they remember Allah. Yesterday, I submitted to you what the meaning of 'Dhikr-e-Khuda' (remembrance of God) is. They remember Allah, and after that, what do they do? 'Fastaghfiru lidhunubihim'—they seek forgiveness and pardon from Allah for their sins. 'Fastaghfiru lidhunubihim'—O Lord, a mistake has been made. And then Allah asks, 'Wa man yaghfirudh-dhunuba illallah'—and who forgives sins except Allah? Meaning, come to the court of Allah. In the court of Allah, of course—meaning before moving forward, before completing this verse—there is also an emphasis in the Quran that if you want to seek forgiveness from Allah, what is the best means (Waseela)? It is the Waseela of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny. Ya Ali. What does the Quran say? There is a verse of the Quran: 'Alladhina idha zalamu anfusahum ja'uka'—when these people commit sins against their souls, when they commit sins, when they wrong their souls, they come to you. O Prophet, they come to you. 'Ja'uka'—this is a verse of the Quran, a verse of Surah An-Nisa. 'Fastaghfirullaha'—and they seek forgiveness from Allah, meaning they come to you and seek forgiveness from whom? They seek forgiveness from Allah. So, if there is no need for a Waseela, then what is the need to come to the Prophet? They could have done it sitting at home on their prayer mat. But coming to the Prophet means that if you go by making him a Waseela, then this seeking of forgiveness of yours will be accepted. 'Ja'uka fastaghfirullaha wastaghfara'—and after that, the Messenger seeks forgiveness for them. 'Rasulu la-wajadullaha tawwaba'—then surely they will find Allah as the Acceptor of Repentance. Allah turns towards them, Allah looks towards them, He turns to them—meaning Allah forgives their sins. So this is a verse of the Quran, so now, going to his court and seeking [forgiveness], 'yaghfirudh-dhunuba illallah', and they do not persist in what they have done while they know. And the sin they have committed, they will not repeat it. They will not repeat it. If they are seeking forgiveness, if they are repenting, then they will not repeat the sin. If someone repeats it again and again, then he is mocking himself. Not anyone else. This is present in the Hadith that if someone, after seeking forgiveness, repeats the same thing again and again, then 'faqat istahza'a binafsihi'—he has mocked himself. He has not mocked anyone else. He has mocked himself. And then Allah says, 'Ula'ika jaza'uhum maghfiratum mir rabbihim'—the reward of these people is that Allah forgives them. Their reward is that Allah forgives them. 'Jaza'uhum maghfiratum mir rabbihim wa jannatun tajri min tahtihal-anhar'—and they will get such gardens beneath which rivers flow. 'Khalidina fiha'—and they will live in it forever. They will live in it forever and ever. 'Wa ni'ma ajrul-'amilin'—and how excellent is the reward of the doers of deeds. How beautiful is the reward of the doers of deeds. Look, having knowledge alone is not enough. Rather, action must accompany it. There is a very famous tradition of the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali a.s.). 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu i'lamu'—O believers, know. 'Annakamalad-dini talabul-ilmi wal-'amalu bihi'—know that the religion is complete when you acquire knowledge and act upon it. The religion is perfect at that time. Meaning, if there is only knowledge, it is of no use. If there is only action, it is also of no use. If both things are individual, if they are alone, there is no benefit. If they are together, there is benefit. This is the statement of the Master of the Universe. See, pay attention to the statement of the Master of the Universe. So, it is very necessary that a person should 'raft'—meaning run fast towards Allah's mercy and forgiveness. This speed does not mean physical speed. It means what we have been discussing in so many gatherings—that a person should always look for the opportunity to receive Allah's mercy. At every moment, he should look for when—meaning whatever opportunity to serve the religion, to serve Allah, to serve the Imam of the Time (a.s.) comes, whenever he gets time, whatever opportunity he gets, he should not let that opportunity slip from his hands. This is the important thing. So when this is the case, then I submitted to you, what is the tradition? 'Man arada Allahu bihil-khayra qadhafa fi qalbihi hubbal-Husayni wa hubba ziyaratihi'—the one for whom Allah wants good, Allah puts the love of Husayn and the love of his Ziyarat in his heart. And the one for whom He wants evil, 'wa man arada bihi ash-shar'—wanting evil means Allah leaves him to his own state. He does not care in which valley he perishes; Allah does not care. He abandons him. So Allah puts the hatred of Husayn in his heart. He starts hating Husayn. And he starts hating the Ziyarat of Husayn. And do you know what is one sign of hatred? One sign, if you want to know, I am just giving one indicator; you yourselves understand the other indicators. That when a person starts objecting to Azadari, wow, wow, wow. Then you understand that something is definitely wrong somewhere. Why this part, why this part? Instead of this, if we build hospitals, build schools—build them, look, you should build them, hospitals should also be built, schools should also be built, but build them from your own budget, not from Imam Husayn's budget. Spend from your own money. Why is your eye on Imam Husayn's budget, brother? And any government in the world, every government has its own separate allotment of budget. Similarly, this is a separate... Those who do not have 'Marifat' (gnosis), they worship a lot, tremendously. And its best example, or rather, worst example, in history is the Khawarij, the Kharijites. They used to worship tremendously. But they did not have Marifat. When the Quran was lifted from the front in the Battle of Siffin, when they were being defeated, they immediately lifted the Quran. That, Quran, choose. Amr ibn al-Aas gave a suggestion to Muawiyah. That look, if you want to be saved from Ali at this time, then do this. Because Malik al-Ashtar had reached there, fighting. You know the Battle of Siffin lasted 18 months. Not one or two days. 18 months, it was a fierce battle. It was a very fierce battle. Now when Malik al-Ashtar, he was one of the commanders of Amir al-Mu'minin, he was a commander. When he reached there, reached near, then Muawiyah understood this. Look, we are reading history, we are not saying anything hidden or covered. And all this that the historians wrote in their books, we are reading that. Right? So there is no need to panic. So don't panic at all. So as soon as Malik al-Ashtar reached near, Muawiyah understood. That now there is no chance. He said to Amr ibn al-Aas, quick, any suggestion, tell me a quick suggestion, what to do? Because Amr ibn al-Aas had a very tremendous, he had a very devilish mind. Meaning, 'wastasa'. You know when the Master of the Universe chased him, what he did, there is no need to tell. Right? He did such an act that the Master turned his face away. Now you understand what he did. That the Master turned his face away. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. And what did you? So he said, look, there is only one chance to be saved now, and that is to lift the Quran on spears. The Quran was lifted on spears. Now all these Khawarij, they surrounded Amir al-Mu'minin. That why are you fighting them? They read the Quran, they believe in the Quran. Look, like us, they also read the Quran. They believe in the Quran. Ali (a.s.) explained that this is not the Quran. This is just a book. The Quran is this. Look at me, I am the Quran. This is not the Quran. He was explaining. But why? Because they did not have Marifat. They were not able to understand this matter. Therefore, they said, 'Ali, call the master back, otherwise we will kill you right now.' These people were such worshippers that it is written in history books that the mark of prostration on their foreheads was like the knee of a camel. You have seen how a camel's knee becomes, right? From sitting so much. So, there was a mark like that, a deep indentation. But they could not recognize him. They lacked the 'Marifat' (gnosis) of the Imam. The Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says, 'These people broke my back.' And this holds true even today. Therefore, the Marifat of the Imam is very necessary. And even today, this is essential. If there is no correct Marifat, then you will start calling anyone your Imam. This one is also an Imam, that one is also an Imam. Is it clear to you? So, yesterday I presented some things for your service. Now, today, I will present two sentences and one or two hadiths for your service. Since this is the final Majlis, I will try to cover as much material as possible, though I won't be able to explain it in great detail. 'Nahnu-lladhina anqal-allahu an-nasa bina min-al-dalala' (We are those through whom Allah saves people from misguidance). Through us, meaning if someone has not held onto the mantle of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), they cannot be saved from misguidance. It is impossible. It is impossible. And holding onto the mantle means not just saying, 'We believe in Ali.' That is not it. The meaning is complete—we will present that to you as well. 'Wa bassarahum bin-al-ama' (And Allah saves them from blindness, He grants them insight). If someone holds onto the mantle of the Ahlulbayt, Allah gives them eyes. Meaning spiritual eyes. Meaning divine eyes, so that they can see things. 'Wa Allahu bina min-al-jahl' (And Allah brings them out of ignorance through our knowledge). This is important. There must be the knowledge of the Ahlulbayt. Meaning their teachings, their knowledge, meaning the knowledge of their hadiths. It is verse number 16 of Surah Jinn, right? What is verse number 16 of Surah Jinn? Read it, brother, is there anyone here? 'Wa an law-istaqamu 'ala al-tariqati la-asqaynahum ma'an ghadaqa' (If they had remained steadfast on the path, We would have surely given them abundant water to drink). Now, what is the meaning of this verse? Look, what is the joy in this? If it were the days of Adhan, we would have read the Tafsir of the Muslims to you. But there is a lot of laughter in that, so we do not recite it. Otherwise, the Tafsir they have done, if you heard it, you would find it amusing. It would be like listening to a joke. 'Wa an law-istaqamu 'ala al-tariqati la-asqaynahum ma'an ghadaqa.' If they had remained steadfast on the path, We would have given them sweet, abundant, and pleasant water. But we recite the Tafsir of the Ahlulbayt. If they had remained steadfast on the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib, we would have acquainted them with our teachings. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. Did you notice? So, remaining steadfast on Wilayah is a very important thing. On the Wilayah of the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). The Quran has announced their Wilayah. Not in one verse, but in many verses. Verse number 55 of Surah Ma'idah is the easiest to remember. 'Innama waliyyukumullahu wa rasuluhu walladhina amanu.' Your Wali, your Mawla, is only Allah. And 'Innama' is used; Allah has restricted it. 'Inhisar' means restricted. Limitation, there is no one beyond this, no one besides them. Who is it? Only Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe. Meaning the Momineen. Now, which Momineen? Which Momineen? There should be clarification of the Momineen, right? The Quran has also clarified that in the same verse. 'Alladhina yuqimunas-salata wa yu'tunas-zakata wa hum raki'un.' Those who establish prayer and give Zakat while in the state of Ruku. In the state of Ruku. Now, search through history. Who was it in whose honor this verse was revealed? Then you will know that there was only one personality in whose honor this verse was revealed, and that is the sacred personality of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). 'Ati'ullaha wa ati'ur-rasula wa ulil-amri minkum.' Obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and obey the Ulil-Amr from among you. Who is the Ulil-Amr? Who is the Ulil-Amr? Who is the Wali-e-Amr? This is very significant, and that is why it was submitted in the 12 Majalis that the best thing is to instill the love of Hussain in the hearts of your children. Bring the children to these Majalis. Bring them to the gatherings; if it is a day of happiness, bring them to the celebrations, if it is a day of grief, bring them to the Majalis. So that they understand how grief is observed, so that they know how Matam (mourning) is performed. Not just by watching others. They should know how Ziyarat is recited, how it is read, how it is taught. All these things they must know, this culture they must know. And Imam Hussain (a.s.) brought such individuals to Karbala that there was a representation for every age. There was a deputy for every age. To the extent that the time came in Karbala when Imam Hussain (a.s.) called out once, 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna? Hal min mugithin yugithuna? Hal min dhabbin yadhubbu 'an harami rasulillahi?' Is there anyone who will help us? Is there anyone who will give us refuge? Is there anyone who will defend the Haram of the Messenger of Allah? Is there anyone to defend the Ahl-e-Haram? Just as Hussain raised the cry for help, a commotion broke out in the tents. Imam Hussain came to the door of the tent, 'Sister Zainab, what is this commotion?' She said, 'Brother, you raised the cry for help, and Asghar threw himself out of the cradle.' He said, 'Sister, bring Asghar to me.' Princess Zainab said, 'No, he is not going into anyone's lap. You come too, you also talk to him.' Hussain came to the cradle, and the phrase from the Maqtal is, 'Hussain bowed down.' And what the father said and what the son understood, no one knows. It is only written that Asghar rushed into Hussain's lap. Perhaps Asghar was saying, 'Father, everyone had feet, they were walking, but I do not have feet, but I will come through you, I will also be sacrificed for you.' Now Hussain takes Asghar and walks. As soon as he reaches the door of the tent, he sees that Rubab is standing there. He said, 'Rubab, why are you standing here?' Rubab replied, 'I am seeing that whoever went to the battlefield since morning, they did not return alive. So I want to see my son one last time.' Hussain explained, 'Rubab, whoever went to the battlefield until now, the enemy thought they came to fight, that is why they martyred them, they killed them. Oh, six-month-old babies do not wage Jihad. I will see, I will take Asghar, and if possible, I will bring him back after giving him water.' A mother's heart is a mother's heart, Hussain walked, came to an elevated place, and came and showed Asghar to the army of the wretched and asked, 'Hal feekum muslim?' Is there any Muslim among you? You know that Islam commands to give water to the thirsty. No one answered. Hussain asked the second question, 'Oh, even if you are not Muslims, is there no one among you who has children?' Even then, no one gave any answer. Hussain said one sentence, 'Do you not see what the condition of my child is? Thirst, the intensity of thirst, 'Kaifa yatalazza', do you see how he is writhing in thirst? Sometimes he opens his lips, sometimes he closes his lips.' Now, hearing these words of Hussain, the wretched ones started turning their faces away and weeping. It was near that signs of revolution would appear, when the son of Sa'ad called out, 'Ayna ayna Hurmala?' Where is Hurmala? The cursed Hurmala came forward. The son of Sa'ad said, 'Ehda kalam al-Hussain, cut off the speech of Hussain, silence the voice of Hussain.' That cursed one took the bow from the quiver, took an arrow from the quiver, filled the arrow, aimed such a shot, into the throat of the six-month-old Asghar, from one corner, from one side to the other, it pierced into Hussain's arm. Asghar's neck bent, the child turned over in the father's lap. Now when Hussain looked down, there was a smile on Asghar's face. Now Hussain wants to take Asghar to the tents, for the final farewell. Now as he gets closer, the thought comes to his heart, I don't know if the mother will be able to bear it or not. Thinking this, Hussain comes back, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un', 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. Seven times Hussain performed this action. Then finally this thought came that now the child has left this world, so why deprive the mother of the final Ziyarat? Now Hussain comes to the door of the tent, called out, 'Rubab.' Now how he called out to Rubab, it is written in the Maqtal, from one side Rubab came, from the other side Sakina came running. 'Father, I have to give water to my brother. Father, is my brother not thirsty?' Hussain could not say anything, could not answer. As soon as Rubab arrived, Hussain only moved his cloak, his cloak, Rubab saw that scene, which may Allah not show to any mother. A six-month-old child, an arrow pierced through. Ya Bunayya, now listen to this lament, 'Oh my son, are children like you also slaughtered?' Wa saya'lamulladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. 'Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, those who are troubled, remove their troubles. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Those who are away from their homeland, return them to their homeland safe and sound. O Lord, protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Those who are protecting them, You protect them. O Lord, grant us the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Accept this small mourning of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Jannat Mein Jaane Ki Shart [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses a profound narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq regarding the significance of Wilayah (guardianship) in Islam. It addresses the common confusion regarding the morality of non-believers versus the shortcomings of some believers, clarifying that true religion is contingent upon following an Imam appointed by Allah. The speaker emphasizes that while good deeds are important, they are only accepted within the framework of divine guardianship, which ultimately leads to salvation.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. It is narrated by the highly esteemed Abdullah bin Abi Ya'fur (r.a.): 'I submitted to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that when I meet people, I am greatly surprised to see that those who do not hold your Wilayah (guardianship) and follow so-and-so as their leader are trustworthy, speak the truth, and keep their promises. But those who accept you as their guardian are neither trustworthy, nor do they keep promises, nor do they speak the truth. Hearing this, the Imam (a.s.) sat up, addressed me in a serious manner, and said: "There is no religion for the one who believes in an Imam whom Allah has not appointed, and there is no punishment for the person who believes in a just Imam appointed by Allah." I asked in surprise: "They have no religion, and these have no punishment?" The Imam (a.s.) replied: "Yes, have you not heard the saying of Allah, the Almighty and Majestic: 'Allah is the guardian of those who believe, He...'"' Have you not heard: 'Allah is the guardian of those who believe, He brings them out of darkness into light' (Quran 2:257)? That is, He brings them out of the darkness of sins into the light of repentance, because they accepted the just Imam appointed by Him. 'And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the Taghut, who bring them out of light into darkness.' So, what light were the disbelievers in, from which they were taken out and cast into darkness? Indeed, this refers to those who were in the light of Islam, but when they accepted those as their leaders who were not appointed by Allah, they departed from the light of Islam and entered the darkness of disbelief. Allah made the fire of Hell mandatory for them along with the disbelievers. 'They are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.' Often it happens that people are impressed by the good deeds of the enemies of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and begin to consider them good, and they even advise Shias to become like them. And they even advise Shias to become like them. But it is proven from this Hadith of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) that whoever does not accept the Imam appointed by Allah as their guardian, no matter how many good deeds they perform, not only will Allah not accept any of their good deeds, but He will also send them to Hell. However, this Hadith does not mean that one who holds the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) should oppose the Shariah. Through this Hadith, the Imam (a.s.) has only explained that even if someone is a sinner, by virtue of accepting the Imamah and Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), they are eligible for salvation, provided they seek forgiveness and do not persist in sins. But for those without their Wilayah, there is no way to enter Paradise. May Almighty God grant us the opportunity to remain steadfast upon the Imamah of His appointed infallible Imams until our last breath, and especially upon the Imamah of the Imam of our time (a.t.f.s.). Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Majlis-e-Aza (Urdu) for Esaal e Sawaab of Marhoom Ansar Ali Rajab Ali Damani
excerpt: This Majlis-e-Aza serves as a spiritual reflection on the qualities of a true Shia, emphasizing the necessity of prayer, moral integrity, and the avoidance of forbidden environments. The lecture highlights the importance of Namaz-e-Shab and the rejection of worldly greed or flattery in favor of devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt. It concludes by connecting the act of mourning for Imam Hussain to the spiritual path of the Imam of our Time, urging believers to maintain the legacy of Karbala.
content:
There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Almighty, the All-High. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Faithful. Peace be upon you, O Fatimah al-Zahra, the leader of the women of the worlds. Peace be upon you, O Hasan and Hussain, the masters of the youths of Paradise. May Allah bless him and his infallible progeny, the oppressed ones... ...upon them and their infallible progeny, the oppressed ones... [Poetic recitation of elegies/Nauha regarding the tragedy of Karbala, mentioning the sorrowful state of Lady Laila...] ...the miserable state of Lady Laila... [Poetic recitation of elegies...] For the reward and elevation of the soul of the deceased Rajab Ali Dani, please recite Surah al-Fatiha. ...We have narrated this Hadith for this brief gathering. In this Hadith, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Innama Shi'atuna yu'rafuna bi-khisal...' In Arabic, 'Innama' is used for restriction (hasr), meaning 'only'. In English, it means 'only'. 'Innama Shi'atuna yu'rafuna bi-khisal...'—there are a few traits or characteristics. If you want to recognize our Shia, look whether these traits, these characteristics, are found in them or not. And then the Imam began to explain... ...and then the Imam began to explain. Before this, let us look at the explanation of the Imam's statement. Our Shia are those who are generous, who are open-handed, who treat their brothers with generosity. Here, the Imam has described this trait: they are very generous towards their brothers, their Mu'min brothers. They do not act with miserliness, they do not show stinginess, but rather they act with generosity. When they see any brother in distress, they immediately step forward to help him. It is not possible for a Shia to see his Mu'min brother in pain and not feel it in his heart. A person cannot be a Shia if he is tight-fisted, miserly, or hoards money. A miserly person cannot be a Shia. A Shia will always be generous, open-handed, and will help his needy brothers. When he sees a needy Shia, he will help him. Needy, meaning our poor (miskeen) who do not have financial means... ...our poor (miskeen) who do not have financial means, who do not possess the wealth of this world, they will always help them so that their standard of living remains at a good level, so that the people of the world look at them with respect, so that the world understands that Shia always help one another. The Imam first explained this social aspect; the very first thing is that Shia will always help their brothers with generosity. Generosity means helping with lawful (halal) things, not in unlawful (haram) things... helping them with things that are basic necessities to fulfill their needs. But nowadays, there are people whom Allah has given worldly wealth, but they spend it for show, for fame, so that they are given titles in their social circle. But when a needy Mu'min is in need, they say, 'No, currently the conditions are not good, there is some trouble,' making some excuse and they do not help him. ...'the conditions are not good, there is some trouble,' making some excuse and they do not help him. Believe me, there is so much emphasis in the narrations, though there is no time to mention all of them. This one Hadith is sufficient to show how much importance the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have placed on helping the poor and needy among the Shia, helping a Mu'min. 'Innama Shi'atuna yu'rafuna bi-khisal...'—this is the first thing. It must be like this; a Shia can never be a miser. [The next trait is] one who prays 51 rak'ahs day and night. Therefore, 51 rak'ahs, and there is so much emphasis to pray as much as possible... ...It is narrated that when a Mu'min prays his prayer at its prime time (awwal-e-waqt), the Angel of Death (Malakul Maut) treats him with ease. Therefore, give great importance to prayer, immense importance. However, some people often start saying that Wilayah is everything, and deeds are nothing without Wilayah, so prayer has no value. Of course, the prayer that is accepted is the one prayed with the Wilayah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.), there is no doubt about that. But at the same time, one who abandons prayer (tarik-us-salat) is not a Shia. How can someone be a Shia who does not pray? The Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have... ...The Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have called the one who abandons prayer (tarik-us-salat) their enemy. 'He is our enemy.' And this is very clear: 'Man kana lillahi muti'an fahuwa lana waliyyun'—our follower is only the one who is obedient to Allah. 'Wa man kana lillahi 'asiyan fahuwa lana 'aduwwun'—and whoever disobeys Allah is our enemy. So how can someone who abandons prayer claim to be a Shia? In the narrations, abandoning prayer is condemned to such an extent that it is said: 'Whoever feeds a tarik-us-salat (one who abandons prayer) is as if he participated in the killing of the Prophets.' He has participated in killing Allah's Prophets. This narration exists. So how can anyone make such a claim, claiming to love the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and Imam Ali (a.s.) while abandoning prayer? This is a deception; it cannot even be conceived. Here we are talking about praying on time, not even about abandoning it altogether... ...This is about praying on time. And Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's (a.s.) final testament was: 'Inna shafa'atana la tanalu man istakhaffa bis-salat' (Our intercession will not reach the one who takes prayer lightly). When the Imam (a.s.) was martyred, he said, 'Convey my Salaam to my followers and deliver my message to them: tell our people that whoever takes prayer lightly will not receive our intercession.' This is about taking it lightly, let alone abandoning it. The Imam (a.s.) said that whoever takes prayer lightly... as the Quran says in Surah al-Ma'un: 'Fawaylun lil-musallin, alladhina hum 'an salatihim sahun' (Woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer). This 'wayl' is a valley in Hell for those people... ...This 'wayl' is a valley in Hell for those people who take prayer lightly. Therefore, we must take prayer very seriously. Now, that was about prayer. The next thing is praying on time. Regarding prayer, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Allah has made prayer the delight of my eyes.' It brings comfort to my eyes. It is something I love. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) loved prayer. You know that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not sleep continuously through the night. When the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) slept at night, he would wake up every little while, pray two rak'ahs of prayer, and then go back to sleep. Every little while. The Prophet's sleep was not like our heedless sleep, where we sleep soundly and only wake up in the morning, forgetting about night prayers and letting morning prayers get delayed. No, it wasn't like that. The Prophet was very vigilant, very awake. He would wake up and... ...He would wake up, pray two rak'ahs of prayer, and then go back to sleep. If we cannot do that because it is difficult, no problem, but at least whenever we get time, we must pray the Nafilah (supererogatory prayers). Great emphasis has been placed on Nafilah prayers. Now people say that the time for Nafilah is before the obligatory prayer, and they cannot pray it due to some excuse. But in the narrations, it is very clear. Regarding Nafilah, it is said that Nafilah is like a gift. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Whenever a gift is presented, Allah accepts it.' A gift is accepted whenever it is given. Therefore, whenever you get the opportunity, never abandon prayer, and pray Nafilah as much as possible. The Imam (a.s.) said: 'Our Shia are those who pray 51 rak'ahs [day and night].' That is, their attention is always towards prayer, and they keep praying. See how much emphasis there is. This is the sign of our Shia, and a Shia is one who follows the footsteps of the Imams (a.s.). So he says: 'Innama Shi'atuna yu'rafuna bi-khisal...' ...'yu'rafuna bi-khisal... [praying 51 rak'ahs] day and night.' They pray 51 rak'ahs in 24 hours. And here, there is great emphasis on the Night Prayer (Namaz-e-Shab). But many of our people say, 'We cannot wake up [at night].' Fine, if you cannot wake up, then pray it before sleeping. If you cannot pray it before sleeping, no problem, when you wake up in the morning and the time has passed, pray its Qada (make-up prayer). Pray it after sunrise, pray it after Dhuhr, pray it after Maghrib, pray it after Isha. It is narrated that when a Mu'min prays the Qada of Namaz-e-Shab, Allah boasts to the angels, saying: 'O My angels, look at this servant of Mine whose prayer was missed, yet he is praying its Qada, even though I did not make this prayer obligatory upon him.' Allah boasts about him. How blessed is that servant for whom Allah boasts to the angels! There is so much emphasis to pray Namaz-e-Shab. Please try not to miss it under any circumstances. If not on time, pray its Qada... If you cannot pray Namaz-e-Shab at its prime time, pray it as Qaza in the morning or afternoon, but do pray it. If you can pray it, no matter the reason—whether it is due to holidays, or someone is sick, or there is weakness, absolutely any illness, weakness, or any reason—then pray at least three Rak'ahs, or even two Rak'ahs, and as brief as possible, there is no issue, but do pray it. And if a person is so weak that they cannot pray standing, it is fine, pray sitting down, but do pray it. What is the most important thing here? It is the intention. I am talking about Namaz-e-Shab, and there are many benefits of it, among which is physical health. The one who is regular in Namaz-e-Shab is protected from many physical illnesses. Yes, indeed, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Our Shia will never drink wine.' God forbid, God forbid... ...if anyone ever... In Islam, there is a curse on drinking wine, on those who drink it, on those who trade in it, on those who transport it, on those who buy it, on those who serve it, on those who drink it, and on those who sit in a gathering where wine is being consumed. Many people say, 'Our friends drink but we don't, we just sit with them.' Attending a gathering where wine is served, even if you don't drink, participating in that gathering is forbidden (haram), staying there is forbidden, you cannot remain there. Now, many people say, 'But we have to do it for business, we have to attend parties.' Why do you have to? If someone leaves Allah and considers someone else as their guardian, then Allah leaves them to that person, and the one who is left to them does not succeed. The one who is left to them does not succeed. Sometimes people complain that their prayers are not answered. Why would they be answered when Allah has given you good circumstances, yet you attend such parties and go to places where wine is served, which is forbidden? And look, wine is not something that only harms the one who drinks it; rather, wine is something whose effect reaches up to seven generations. Now, how it affects them, Allah knows best, but it does have an effect. One must stay away from it. Do not go to places where wine is consumed. There is no need to make excuses. Our religion is our religion. When you stand firm, people will respect you for prioritizing Allah over your desires, your profile, or your profit. Allah will always... ...and Allah will always support you. Our Shia will never flatter anyone or make groveling sounds. Just as a dog makes a specific sound when it flatters someone, a Shia will never do that. Our Shia will never beg or grovel before anyone, nor will they ever flatter anyone. Here, flattery is only appropriate before Allah, begging and crying before Allah, or before those whom Allah has appointed as His means (Wasilah), the Ma'sumeen (a.s.), about whom Allah said in the Quran: 'Seek a means of approach to Him' (Wabtaghu ilayhil-wasilah). If you want to seek, then find the Wasilah. Finding it is the human's responsibility. And who are our Wasilah? If we ask them, go to their doorstep, and ask Allah through them, making them the intermediary. What is the point of begging before others? Our Shia will never be greedy like a crow. Greed for the world is something that makes a person do things that lead to their humiliation and downfall. This greed is called 'Hirs' in Arabic. It stems from the hope that one will get something from the people of the world, so they run after it greedily, thinking that... ...running after it and being greedy, thinking, 'If I get this, so-and-so will give me that.' He goes to him, sits with him, and flatters him, even if that person is an enemy of Allah. Out of greed for this world, he is ready to do anything. For a political post or status, he is ready to do anything just because he is getting a position. Sometimes, in the pursuit of politics, some of our own people go to such lengths that one would never expect or explain. This is what greed does. Whatever Allah has destined, He will give. But greed makes a person never content, always wanting more and more. There is a very profound narration about this. The narration says that the love of this world is like a silkworm. What does this silkworm do? What does this silkworm do? It spins silk around itself. It spins so much silk around itself that it cannot escape from its own cocoon. It thinks, 'A little more, a little more,' and spins so much silk that it gets trapped inside. Even if it tries, it cannot get out, until it dies of suffocation inside. When it dies, people take it, throw it into boiling water, and extract the silk. So, who did the hard work? The silkworm did. And who benefited? The silk merchant or the person who makes silk benefited after its death. The example of a person who has the love of the world in their heart is just like this. Out of greed for the world, they work so hard, put in so much effort, and accumulate so much... ...and works so hard that they get trapped in it and cannot get out. In the end, they build properties and wealth, but they gain nothing of real value. They lose in this world and the hereafter. What was the result? They died, and their soul went into the boiling water of hellfire, while the people of the world began distributing their wealth. Who benefited? Their heirs and others benefited, while they spent their life enslaved to the world. This is the example of those who run after the world. Therefore, our Shia is never greedy. And then the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Our Shia will never stretch their hand before our enemies, even if they die of hunger.' Look at this high status of a Shia! Look at this high status of a Shia! Our Shia will never stretch their hand before our enemies, even if they die of hunger. This is the honor of our Shia. When someone asked Imam Ali (a.s.), 'Where can we find such Shia?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'You will find them on the mountain peaks and in remote corners of the cities.' You will find such Shia there. These were the people whom Janab-e-Abu Dharr (r.a.) had guided and made Shia in those mountainous regions. And look at their upbringing. Today, that entire region... Janab-e-Abu Dharr was exiled so that he would not go to Medina, but rather... ...he was sent to Syria (Sham). But from this, we get a lesson: no matter what corner of the world we are in, we must continue to propagate the message (Tableeg). We should not complain about the circumstances, but rather continue our propagation. And the best propagation is to stand by the truth, even if it costs one's life. And that is why, when someone among us passes away, we do not just mourn our elders, but we mourn the martyrs of Karbala, so that their memory remains alive forever. A believer always does this. Once, a person had a great desire in his heart to meet the Imam of our Time (a.t.f.s.), but he was not able to. He tried hard. Once, while praying, he fell asleep... Once, while praying, he fell asleep. As soon as he closed his eyes, he saw the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in his dream. Now, remember one thing: if anyone sees an Infallible (Ma'soom) in a dream—any of the 14 Infallibles—that dream can never be false; it is a true dream. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked him the reason for his weeping. He submitted, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have been weeping and reciting supplications for so many days to be blessed with the visitation (ziyarat) of my Imam, but I am not being granted the visitation of the Imam.' The Prophet said, 'If you want to be close to us, the best way is to recite the tragedies (Masaib) of Imam Hussain (a.s.) more often. Allahu Akbar! Mourn the tragedies of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Because it is a fact that my son, Mehdi (a.t.f.s.), weeps for Imam Hussain (a.s.) morning and evening.' So, if anyone wants to connect with the Imam of our Time (a.t.f.s.), the best way is to cry for Imam Hussain (a.s.) morning and evening, even if just for two minutes, only two minutes, or three minutes daily. Yes, my friends... Our friend, Ansar Bhai, had a deep love, he loved immensely... When Imam Hussain (a.s.) came for the final farewell, when everyone had been martyred, even Janabe Ali Asghar (a.s.) was martyred, and everyone else was martyred, and only this lone warrior was left, Imam Hussain (a.s.) once called out... 'O Zainab, O Umme Kulthum, O Ruqayya, O Sakina, peace be upon you all, my final salam to you.' Her heart broke, and she asked, 'O brother, are you prepared for death? Are you going to die?' Hussain (a.s.) replied, 'How can one not be prepared for death when he has no helper or supporter left?' She said, 'O brother, then go to Sajjad (a.s.).' He went to Sajjad (a.s.). As he leaned over, Sajjad (a.s.) was so weak and exhausted that he could not recognize him at first and asked, 'Where is my father?' Hussain (a.s.) pressed him to his chest... ...and said, 'O my son, how would you recognize me? Your father's body is riddled with wounds.' 'O father, you are in this state, and I am lying here like this. Father, I will help you.' Hussain (a.s.) said, 'No, Sajjad, this is not your time, this is not your battlefield. Your battlefield is Kufa and Shaam. Convey my salam to my followers (Shias), and tell them that whenever they drink cold water, or see a traveler or a martyr, they should remember my thirst.' Sajjad (a.s.) wept bitterly, and the Imam bid him farewell. Now Hussain (a.s.) went towards the battlefield for the final time. He stood outside the tents, calling out for help when there was no helper left. He called out, 'O heroes of Safa, O brave lions! What has happened to you that I call you but you do not answer my call?' They did not answer, but a voice seemed to come from the martyrs' bodies, 'O Master, we are helpless (constrained by death).' Now Imam Hussain (a.s.) stood before them... 'O my brother, O my Hussain, do not be distressed...' Then Zainab (a.s.) asked Hussain (a.s.)... ...asked him, 'Are you distressed, my mother?' Hussain (a.s.) launched a second attack towards the enemy... The plunderers reached, and they reached the banks of the Euphrates (Furat)... But as soon as Hussain (a.s.) launched the third attack, after a short while, a voice came from the heavens... Hussain (a.s.) sheathed his sword. As soon as he put his sword in the scabbard, the wretched army attacked him. Someone threw stones, someone shot arrows, someone attacked with a sword. Suddenly, Hussain (a.s.) fell from his horse onto the sands of Karbala. He did not just fall, but his body was so filled with arrows that they held him up like a cradle. When Zainab (a.s.) could not see her brother, she came out of the tent calling, 'O brother Hussain, O Hussain!' She could not see him clearly. Then she saw a sight that no sister should ever have to see—Shimr was sitting on Hussain's chest and was severing his head from his body. ...severing his head. Hussain (a.s.) gestured during his last moments... As soon as this tragedy occurred, a voice echoed, 'Hussain has been slaughtered in Karbala!' The sun was eclipsed, a dark storm began to blow, and the sky turned black. Sakina (a.s.) cried out, 'O Sajjad, what am I hearing?' ... 'Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah... Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah. This is my final salam to you.' ...My final salam to the son of the Messenger of Allah. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of our Imam. Relieve the troubles of all those who are distressed. Deliver the entire world and humanity from this calamity. Protect the lives, wealth, and honor of the Shias wherever they are in the world. For the sake of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.), accept the prayers of those who worship. O Lord, grant us the visitation (ziyarat) of Hussain (a.s.) and Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in this world, and their intercession (shafa'at) in the hereafter. Recite Salawat three times...

title: Maqtal-e-Janabe Ali Asghar (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture recounts the tragic martyrdom of the six-month-old infant, Janabe Ali Asghar (a.s.), on the day of Ashura. It describes Imam Hussain's (a.s.) desperate plea to the enemy army for water for his suffering child. The narrative culminates in the brutal act of Hurmala ibn Kahil, who killed the innocent infant with an arrow. The lecture serves as a poignant reflection on the immense sacrifice made by the Ahlulbayt at Karbala.
content:
'Thirst is on your lips, and this weeping is divine...' On the day of Ashura, when Imam Hussain (a.s.) brought his six-month-old child, Janabe Ali Asghar (a.s.), to get some water, he pleaded with the oppressive army, 'O people! You have killed my brothers, my sons, and my companions. And now, no one is left except this child. See how this child is writhing in the intensity of thirst, even though he has committed no sin. I have brought him before you; if possible, give him a little water.' While Mawla Hussain (a.s.) was still making this plea, the cursed Hurmala ibn Kahil al-Asadi shot an arrow that pierced through one ear of Janabe Ali Asghar (a.s.) and came out the other side. Salam... Alas, Asghar! Alas, Asghar!...

title: Kis Paigham Ki Tableegh Sabse Zyada Zaroori Hai? | 20 days to go for Ghadeer
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the critical importance of propagating the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib as commanded by Allah in the Quran. The speaker highlights that the Prophet Muhammad was instructed to deliver this specific message at Ghadir, noting that failure to do so would render his mission incomplete. The talk argues that if the Muslim Ummah had maintained this focus on Wilayah after the Prophet's passing, the current sectarian divisions within Islam would not exist.
content:
Right? We do not show any undue leniency; there is no compromise on the household of the 14 (Infallibles). It is a very straightforward matter that some people do not like my Master, and some people I do not like because their character is incomplete. 'O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you...' [Quran 5:67]. Here, Allah, the Lord of the Universe, addresses His Messenger, His Beloved, by his designation. In various contexts, He addressed His Messenger with different titles—sometimes calling him 'Taha', sometimes 'Muzzammil', sometimes 'Muddassir', sometimes 'Sirajum Muneer', and also gave him the name 'Rasool Allah' and 'Rahmatul lil 'Alameen', who is the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family. But this is an occasion where Allah, the Lord of the Universe, addresses His Beloved Messenger by his designation, commanding him to deliver the message to the Muslim Ummah. And after that, if you look, it immediately commands: '...and if you do not do it, then you have not delivered His message' [Quran 5:67], which refers to the Wilayah (guardianship) of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). ...commanding the propagation regarding the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Right? So, if the Muslim Ummah, in the same way that the Messenger of Allah established the Wilayah of Maula Ali (a.s.) in the field of Ghadir—if after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, the Muslim Ummah had continued to present this propagation to the world, then surely, the division and differences we see today among the sects would not have existed in Islam. [Music]

title: Imamat Ko Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Nasl Mein Hi Kyun Rakha Gaya? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological reasoning behind why the lineage of Imamah was established specifically through Imam Husayn (a.s.) rather than Imam Hasan (a.s.). Using the teachings of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker explains that Imamah is a divine appointment determined by Allah's absolute wisdom. Ultimately, the lecture emphasizes that human intellect cannot fully comprehend divine decrees, and believers are obligated to accept these decisions as part of their faith.
content:
[Music] I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Wali of Allah. Imamah is a great position and office which is certified by the Holy Quran, and Allah has placed it in the progeny and descendants of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), as stated in verse 124 of Surah al-Baqarah. Allah made Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) an Imam for mankind, and then Ibrahim (a.s.) requested the Lord of the Universe for this position to continue in his descendants. If we look, the Holy Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is also from the progeny of Ibrahim (a.s.), and we, the Ithna Ashari Shi'as, believe in that very chain of Imamah, meaning the lineage of the 12 Imams connects to Ibrahim (a.s.). But a unique aspect of this chain is that after Imam Ali (a.s.), Imam Hasan (a.s.) and then Imam Husayn (a.s.) are our first three Imams. After this, the lineage of Imamah continued through Imam Husayn (a.s.). ...the lineage of Imamah continued through Imam Husayn (a.s.) and not through Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). Why is that? The famous companion, Janab-e-Mufaddal ibn Umar (r.a.), approached the 'Ahl al-Dhikr' (People of the Remembrance), i.e., the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), in accordance with Allah's command, with this very question and asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). Mufaddal submitted, 'O son of the Messenger, tell me about this saying of Allah, the Almighty: "And He made it a word remaining among his descendants" [Quran 43:28].' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'By this word, Imamah is meant, which Allah has placed in the progeny of Imam Husayn (a.s.) until the Day of Judgment.' Mufaddal says, 'I asked again: O son of the Messenger, why did this happen? Why was Imamah placed in the progeny of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and not in the progeny of Imam Hasan (a.s.), when both of them are the sons of the Holy Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)...' ...both are the sons of the Holy Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), his grandsons, and the leaders of the youths of Paradise?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Prophet Musa (a.s.) and Prophet Harun (a.s.) were both prophets, messengers, and brothers, but Allah placed the prophethood in the lineage of Prophet Harun (a.s.) and not in the lineage of Prophet Musa (a.s.). And it is not permissible for anyone to say why Allah did so. Indeed, Imamah is the vicegerency (Khilafah) of Allah, the Almighty. No one has the right to say why Allah placed it in the lineage of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and not in the lineage of Imam Hasan (a.s.), because Allah acts with wisdom in His actions.' Then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) recited the 23rd verse of Surah al-Anbiya: 'He cannot be questioned about what He does...' '...but they will be questioned.' [Quran 21:23] By reciting this verse, the Imam (a.s.) answered every question raised by opponents regarding the issue of Imamah. Imamah is a divine, guided office which Allah has declared as a remaining word that will persist until the Day of Judgment. Allah bestows this guided office upon whomever He wills; no one else has any say in it. Behind every action of Allah, there is some wisdom. It is not necessary that His wisdom is understood by everyone. A human cannot comprehend a divine, guided office with their own intellect; the matter of Imamah has been kept far beyond human intellect and understanding. Our responsibility is to accept the decisions made by Allah without any ifs and buts, because people are accountable for their actions, not Allah. People will be questioned... ...people will be questioned about how they treated the Imam appointed by Allah. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Universe to hasten the reappearance of Hazrat Baqiyatullah, the heir of the Quran, the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), so that we too may learn the true religion of God and the knowledge of the Quran from the blessed tongue of the final light of that lineage of Imamah which continued from Imam Husayn (a.s.). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Shareeftareen Aamaal Kya Hain? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the definition of true nobility according to a hadith from Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). It emphasizes that a believer's most noble deeds are sending Salawat upon the Prophet and his progeny, praying for the pious Shia, and distancing oneself from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt. The speaker clarifies that nobility is not a self-proclaimed title but a status earned through these specific spiritual actions in the sight of Allah.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider. A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alim min ash-shaytani ar-rajim. Bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. Wa salla Allahu 'alayka ya waliyyal 'asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. The noble saying of Hazrat Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) is: Inna ashrafa a'malil mu'minina fi maratibihimullati qad rutribu fiha minath-thara ilal 'arsh. Indeed, the most noble deeds of the believers, by virtue of which they will attain ranks from the earth to the Divine Throne, are: As-salatu 'ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibin. Sending blessings (Salawat) upon Muhammad and his pure and purified progeny (s.a.w.a.). Wastid'au rahmatillahi wa ridwanihi lishi'atihimul muttaqin. Praying for the mercy and pleasure of Allah for their pious and God-fearing Shia. Wal-la'nu lilmutabi'ina li-a'daihimul mujahirinal munafiqin. And sending curses upon those who follow their open and hypocritical enemies. Nobility is a status and 'Sharif' (noble) is a title that people love for themselves, but one does not become noble just by calling oneself by this name or by people considering someone noble. The one who is noble in the light of the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and according to their teachings is the one who will truly be considered noble in the sight of Allah, and their rank will be determined accordingly. That is, according to this hadith, true nobility is sending blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), praying for their pious Shia, and cursing those who follow their enemies. May the Almighty grant us the ability to act according to the teachings of the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and hasten the luminous reappearance of the last heir of the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Amen, O Lord of the worlds.
