title: Suwwar Ke Gosht Se Zyaada Haraam Kya Hai?
excerpt: This lecture discusses a profound warning attributed to Imam Sajjad (a.s.) regarding the misuse of titles and names associated with the Ahlulbayt. The speaker highlights that attributing the sacred titles of the Imams or Maula Ali (a.s.) to undeserving individuals is considered more forbidden than the consumption of pork. The talk emphasizes the gravity of misusing these holy designations and the spiritual consequences of such actions.
content:
A very strict stance is reported from Imam Sajjad (a.s.). The Imam says that the Messenger of Allah said: 'It is more forbidden (haram) than eating pork to use the names or titles of the Imams (a.s.) or Maula Ali (a.s.) for someone who is not deserving of them.' The Imam has given the example of swine here, i.e., pork. I often have discussions with Muslims. Once I asked a cleric, 'Muslims consider usury (interest) to be highly forbidden.' He replied, 'No, you are wrong; they consider pork to be more forbidden.' The Imam is saying that it is more forbidden than pork to use our titles and our names for someone who is not worthy of them—whether someone else gives it to them, it is forbidden, or for oneself... [Music]
Imam Sajjad (a.s.) stated that misusing the titles of the Imams is more forbidden than eating pork.
The prohibition applies to both those who bestow these titles and those who accept them.
Sacred titles belong exclusively to the Ahlulbayt and should not be used for others.
The comparison to pork is used to illustrate the extreme level of spiritual impurity associated with this act.
Muslims often prioritize the prohibition of pork, but this teaching elevates the sanctity of the Imams' names.
Using these titles for undeserving people is a serious transgression in Islamic ethics.

title: Tafseer-e-Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) Ki Tareekh | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the historical context and authenticity of the Tafsir attributed to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). He narrates the story of a Shia family from Astarabad who sought refuge with the Imam to escape persecution, leading to the Imam teaching them the Tafsir over seven years. The lecture addresses common doubts regarding the authenticity of the work and explains the tragic loss of the majority of its volumes during historical unrest in Baghdad.
content:
Now, as soon as we mention this Tafsir (exegesis), many people say, 'Oh, that Tafsir is not authentic.' Look, before saying anything, think about what we are saying. Is the Tafsir of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) not authentic? No. A few people said, 'Brother, according to us, this is not authentic.' A few people, but the number of those who accepted it and the stature of those people is so great that there is no possibility of denying it. The Tafsir of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.). The background of this Tafsir is that there is a place in Iran called Astarabad. People from there are called Astarabadi. There was a Zaydi government there at one time. The people of this government, meaning the minister of the king, used to incite the king against the Shia. So the king used to oppress the Shia a lot. The result was that the Shia were just suffering. So a Shia family fled from there and came to Samarra, and after coming to Samarra, they took refuge with Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) and said, 'Master, our king oppresses us a lot, so we have fled from there and come here.' Master Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) said to them, he told them, 'Go back to Astarabad, your problem has been solved.' They said, 'Master, we have just come from there.' He said, 'I am telling you, go. Your problem has been solved. When you arrive, you will get the news that your problem has been solved, in fact, you will get the news before that.' So the poor people were hesitant; there was a hesitation in their hearts. Now they could not disobey the Master, and they were also afraid to go back. This whole family fled from there. Well, at that time, Astarabad was not a small place, news used to reach everyone that the whole family had fled. Anyway, the summary is that to reassure them, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) said, 'Do one thing, keep your two young men here, and I will teach them the Tafsir. I will teach them the Tafsir, you go, and when you get the news that your problem is solved, send me the news, and then I will teach these children the Tafsir until they understand it.' I will teach them until then. They were happy, 'Okay.' They went back. They had only reached halfway to Astarabad when a man met them and said that the king, the minister who used to incite the king, was found dead one morning. His head was separated from his body. Someone had killed him, and the problem was solved, and the king became completely normal. Now there was no one left to incite, no one left to provoke. So their problem was solved. The Imam taught these people the Tafsir for 7 years. 7 years, and it was not like that, he taught them daily. And he said, 'I will keep teaching as long as you have the capacity, as long as you have the ability, you keep writing, I will keep teaching.' That is why Ibn Shahr Ashub says that this Tafsir was in 110 volumes or 120 volumes, it was in 120 volumes. But when the events in Baghdad happened, this entire Tafsir was burned, only one volume of it survived.
The Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) is considered authentic by many prominent scholars despite some modern skepticism.
The work originated from the Imam teaching two young men from a persecuted family from Astarabad.
The Imam predicted the end of the persecution in Astarabad before the family returned.
The teaching process lasted for seven years, focusing on the capacity and understanding of the students.

title: SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024-25 | 29-Dec-2024 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture provides a profound theological exploration of the status and luminous nature of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.) within Islamic tradition. It details her central role in the creation of the universe, her divine origin from the light of majesty, and her significance as a source of guidance and intercession. The session also serves as the concluding event for the Shahzaadi-e-Kaunain Grand Quiz, blending spiritual discourse with community recognition and prize distribution.
content:
Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. [Music] Wali... A'udhu billahi samil 'alim minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alaika ya Wali al-Asr, adrikna. Wala likna al-hamd parh ke madad-e-Zahra sunaunga. Wala likna al-hamd parh ke madad-e-Zahra sunaunga. Al-hamd parh ke madad-e-Zahra sunaunga. Surah ki peshwai mein surah sunaunga, aur Kausar ki aayatein hain parhunga namaz mein. Kausar ki aayatein hain parhunga namaz mein, Khaliq ko Syeda ka qasida sunaunga. Khaliq ko Syeda ka qasida sunaunga. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. All praise is for that Almighty God, for that Creator of the universe, who created the creation to attain His recognition (Ma'rifat), and for the attainment of that recognition, He created that 'Noor-e-Anwar' (Radiant Light) by seeing whose greatness and majesty, the angels learned the etiquette of worshipping God by witnessing their glorification, praise, and sanctification. And this is that light beyond the description of God, for whose sake Adam and Eve, the paradise, hell, and the vast oceans were created, and the expanse of the sky, decorated with stars, was created, in whose witness the sentences of Hadith-e-Kisa are speaking. Bismillahir-Rahman... Kisa are speaking: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Inni ma khalaqtu sama'an mabniya, wala ardan madhiya, wala qamaran munira, wala shamsan mudhiya, wala falakan yadur, wala bahran yajri, wala fulkan yasri, illa fi mahabbati ha'ula'il khamsati alladhina hum tahtal kisa. It is being declared by the Lord of Majesty: Verily, I have not raised these canopies of the heavens, nor spread this floor of the earth, nor made the moon luminous, nor the sun radiant, nor caused the sky to rotate, nor the oceans to flow, nor the ships to sail, except for the love of these five who are under this cloak. Worthy of blessings and peace is this embodied radiant cloak, and specifically that luminous personality who became the center of the light of the Kisa, that is, Sayyidatun Nisa, Siddiqa Tahira, Radiya Mardiya, Hurratul Insiyah, Batul-e-Azra, Fatima Zahra (s.a.), on the occasion of whose auspicious birth, the TSR team is once again present to serve you with the 'Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz'. Let us first offer congratulations on this auspicious birth. First, we offer our congratulations for this blessed birth to the court of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and specifically to the court of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), through a Salawat. We also extend our congratulations to all of you, and we welcome you all to the 'Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz.' So, viewers, before we begin our discussion, let us look at the rules of our quiz. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. The link for the 'Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz' is now live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, please click the quiz link to register. You will then see questions related to this discussion on that same link. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion; you just need to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not rush to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is no prize for answering first. The only condition for the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. Among those who provide correct answers to all questions, winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, and they will be given these prizes. Let us move forward to today's discussion. As you heard the phrases of the Hadith-e-Kisa, Allah (s.w.t.) announced that He created the universe. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'Ya Rabbe, wa man tahtal Kisa?' (O Lord, who is under this cloak?). Allah (s.w.t.) replied, 'Hum Fatimatu wa abuha wa ba'luha wa banuha' (They are Fatima, her father, her husband, and her sons). This means that in the As-hab al-Kisa, the center of introduction was declared to be Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.). Or, as I would say: 'Listen to the introduction from God under the Kisa; it is the limit that the reference for Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) is Fatima (s.a.).' It is the limit that the reference for Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) is Fatima (s.a.). Yes, viewers, this centrality is not limited to the Hadith-e-Kisa; rather, from the beginning of creation until the Day of Judgment, and in the division of Paradise and Hell, the personality of the Shahzadi (s.a.) is the central figure. Regarding this centrality, our brothers, Mr. Mohammad Abbas Patel and Gulzar Haider Naqvi, are with us for further discussion on this 'Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz.' Mohammad Abbas bhai, Gulzar bhai, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. The centrality of the personality of the Shahzadi (s.a.) is indeed visible from the beginning of creation to the end of creation, as you said. It does not end here; her centrality is also clearly visible in the division of Paradise and Hell. Yes, when Allah (s.w.t.) commanded the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to marry the Shahzadi to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), the phrases of the narration are: 'Qad zawwajtu Fatimata min Ali...' ...Qad zawwajtu Fatimata min Ali. Allah is saying to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that He has indeed performed the marriage of Fatima (s.a.) to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). This means, where did this happen? Is this about the heavens or Paradise? Allah performed the marriage of the Shahzadi in Paradise first, and then commanded the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to perform this marriage on earth. The Hadith continues: 'Wa qad amartu shajarat-e-Tuba an tal-dar wal yaqut wal marjan.' Then Allah says that He commanded the tree of Tuba—which is the tree spread throughout Paradise, where a branch of this tree reaches every house in Paradise—to decorate itself with pearls, rubies, and coral for the occasion of the Shahzadi's marriage. This is the arrangement for the Shahzadi's (s.a.) marriage in Paradise; the situation on this earth is different. In Paradise, Allah is arranging the marriage, and the entire Paradise is being decorated with rubies, pearls, and coral spread in every house. And the people of the heavens... ...and the people of the heavens were happy to see this sight. Based on this sight and this marriage, the people of the heavens appear happy. Then the Hadith continues: 'Wa sayuladu minhuma waladan, sayyida shabab-e-ahlil jannah' (And soon, two sons will be born from her, who will be the leaders of the youth of Paradise), 'wa yuzayyanu bihim ahlul jannah' (and the people of Paradise will be adorned through them). O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), give glad tidings, for you are the best of the first and the last. Now, what is the dowry (Mahr) of this marriage that was decided in the heavens and performed on earth? When we turn our attention to this Mahr, we will understand how the Shahzadi's centrality is visible in the division of Paradise and Hell, or from the beginning of creation to the end. Yes, the narration is found in Amali of Sheikh Tusi. Sheikh Tusi (r.a.) narrates through his chain of transmission from Abu Basir, who narrates from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.): 'Qala al-salam, Innallaha tabarak wa ta'ala...' ...Innallaha tabarak wa ta'ala ja'ala mahr-e-Fatima al-salam rub'a al-dunya. The Imam (a.s.) is saying that Allah (s.w.t.) has declared one-fourth of the world as the dowry of Fatima (s.a.). Allah has made one-fourth of the world her dowry. The word 'world' is used here; it is not just about the earth. The entire world—if a person reflects on what is included in the entire world, how many planets and galaxies are included—and one-fourth of it! And people were talking about a small piece of land (Fadak) saying it is not yours, while Allah is giving one-fourth of the entire world to the Shahzadi as her dowry. The Hadith continues: 'Wa ja'ala al-jannata mahr-e-ha' (And He has made Paradise her dowry). The entire Paradise is her dowry. 'Wa al-nara' (And Hell is also included in her dowry) in the sense that 'tudkhilina al-nara' (you will admit your enemies into Hell); Hell is completely obedient to you. 'Wa tudkhilina awliya'a ahlil jannah' (And you will admit your followers into Paradise). And she is the Siddiqa al-Kubra... ...and she is the Siddiqa al-Kubra. The term 'Siddiqa al-Kubra' is used, not just 'Siddiqa.' The greatest of all those who speak the truth. 'Wa Siddiqa al-Kubra, la ma'rifat-e-ha dar-o-madar-e-qurun-e-ula.' And the foundation of the recognition of the eras before this world, or the eras that are higher in rank than this world, depends on her recognition. What is meant by this? Which world is being referred to, and how is the foundation of the recognition of those worlds dependent on her? Abbas bhai, could you please explain this part about the recognition of the Shahzadi being the foundation of the 'Qurun-e-Ula'? Certainly, Kamyab bhai. If we turn to Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira, we learn that along with this world and the hereafter, another realm or several realms are mentioned, which are called 'Ula.' For example, in the Ziyarat of the Imams (a.s.), we read in Ziyarat-e-Jamia: 'Hujjatullah ala al-dunya wal akhirat wal ula.' You are the proof of Allah... ...upon the people of the world, the hereafter, and the 'Ula.' Or, those who are beyond this, beyond the world and the hereafter in rank. If we change the phrasing, it would not be wrong to say that this refers to the realms that existed before this world—that is, those included in the realm of Malakut, such as Alam-e-Zarr, Alam-e-Arwah, Alam-e-Ajbah, and Alam-e-Ajlah. All these realms are higher in rank than this world. The foundation of the recognition of all these realms depends on the recognition of the Shahzadi (s.a.), based on this narration. That is, it depends on acknowledging her recognition. Mashallah, according to the phrases of this Hadith, just as we acknowledged the recognition of Allah, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the Imams (a.s.) in the 'Ula' (the realms before coming to this world), the recognition of the Shahzadi (s.a.) was also acknowledged there. In fact, it was not just an acknowledgment; the foundation in those realms was based on this recognition. That is, the center of recognition for all these realms... ...is the Shahzadi herself. Yes, it was incumbent upon the father of humanity, Adam (a.s.), to have the recognition of Zahra (s.a.), and the personality of Fatima (s.a.) cannot be compared with any other woman, whether it is Maryam (s.a.), the daughter of Imran, or Kulthum (s.a.), or Asiya (s.a.), or even the mother of the Shahzadi (s.a.) herself, Ummul Momineen Khadija (s.a.). Just as it was incumbent upon all the Prophets (a.s.) who passed to acknowledge the recognition of the status of Wilayat of the Seal of Prophets (s.a.w.a.), the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and all the Imams (a.s.), it was similarly incumbent upon all creation to acknowledge the recognition of Fatima (s.a.), because without the recognition of the Shahzadi (s.a.), recognition cannot be complete. Gulzar bhai, we would like you to express something for our viewers regarding this centrality of the Shahzadi (s.a.). Yes, thank you Kamyab bhai. I will start my point from where Abbas bhai finished, that in the... ...realms before this world, that is, the 'Qurun-e-Ula' (the eras before this world), the central point was the recognition of the Shahzadi (s.a.). All the angels or whoever was there, their foundation depended on the recognition of the Shahzadi (s.a.). Now, I will present a Hadith before you from Bihar al-Anwar, where Allama Majlisi has brought a chapter regarding the Shahzadi (s.a.) and her names—why her name is Fatima, and similarly, the Hadith regarding why she is called 'Zahra.' This relates to the entire luminous personality of the Shahzadi. Regarding 'Zahra,' there are other Hadiths as well. One Hadith implies that she is called 'Zahra' because when she was on the prayer mat, a light would radiate from her, and it would shine for the people of the heavens just as the stars shine for the people of the earth. It is stated in one place that she is called 'Zahra' because her light would shine for the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) three times a day; her face would become illuminated. Regarding this, it is also said that the light radiating from the Shahzadi at the time of Fajr was white, and at the time of Maghrib... Its color used to be white, and at the time of Maghrib, it would turn red. This light was so intense that it would spread throughout all of Medina; that is, the light would spread so much that people would come to the service of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and ask, 'O Messenger of Allah, what kind of light is this?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would reply, 'My daughter is on her prayer mat.' Subhan Allah! That is why the Princess is called 'Zahra'. Now, regarding this Zahra, there is a hadith that Allama Majlisi has brought in Bihar al-Anwar. This narration describes the luminous personality of the Princess in such a way that the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is decorated, and in that gathering, Janab-e-Salman Mohammadi is present. He narrates that in that gathering, Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib asked, 'What is the reason that Allah has given Ali (a.s.) superiority over us?' So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) began to explain why he has superiority. He started by saying that Allah created my light and Ali's light before He created the heavens, the earth, the Pen, or the Throne. He had not created the Pen, nor the Throne, nor anything else. First of all, He created my light and Ali's light. The hadith continues, and then it is stated that after that, the light of Imam Hassan (a.s.) was created, through which the sun and the moon were created, and the light of Imam Hussain (a.s.) was created, through which Paradise was created. The hadith proceeds in this manner, and then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states that when Allah willed to test the angels—that is, to involve them in a trial—the words of the hadith are: 'Arsala alayhim sahaban muzliman' (He sent dark clouds over them). Allah sent dark clouds over the angels. What happened was that one angel could not see the other, and the other could not see the first. Complete darkness prevailed. Because of those dark clouds, this was the test for the angels. The light was removed; the light was completely hidden. It was pitch black; no one could see anyone else. And when this situation arose, the angels became terrified because it was total darkness and no one could see anyone else, so the angels cried out to Allah. The angels cried out to Allah, crying out, 'O our Lord, O our Creator, O our God! Since the time You created us, we have never seen such an environment before. What is this?' The angels were terrified, bewildered, and distressed, praying in the court of Allah, saying, 'Since You created us, we have never seen such an environment until today. What is this?' And they continue to cry out, 'Fawassalna ilayka bi-hadhihi al-anwar' (We beseech You through these lights)—which I just presented to you, meaning the light of Hazrat Ali (a.s.), the light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the lights of Imam Hassan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.) were all present. So the angels said, 'We beseech You through these lights to remove this from us.' This darkness, remove it from us. So, Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala, Allah Azza wa Jalla, swore by His Honor and Majesty, saying, 'I swear by My Honor and Majesty, I will surely, surely do what you have prayed for, O angels. I will surely do it.' So what did Allah do? Allah created the light of Fatima Zahra (s.a.). What did Allah do? He created the light of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) in the form of a lantern. That day, in the darkness, just as we have lamps or candles, Allah created the light of the Princess (s.a.) in the form of a lantern and hung it on the edge of the Throne. Because of it, the seven heavens and the seven earths were illuminated by its radiance. The light spread all around, and the angels' test was resolved through this light; they were saved from this calamity. And look, this is about the angels, and angels are luminous beings created by Allah, very honorable beings. Even when calamities, troubles, and difficulties come upon them, they pray to the Lord by beseeching through these lights, and Allah removes their distress. When they beseech through these lights, through whom does Allah remove it? Through the Princess (s.a.). That is, for the inhabitants of the heavens, Janab-e-Fatima Zahra (s.a.)... For the inhabitants of the heavens, Janab-e-Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is the 'Mushkil Kusha' (the remover of difficulties). Their difficulties are removed because of her light, just as the Master of the Universe, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), is the Mushkil Kusha for us in this world. The Princess is the Mushkil Kusha for the angels and for those beings who existed before. Now, what happened after that? When the trouble was removed, the angels immediately began to glorify and sanctify Allah. They began to praise and sanctify Allah. When Allah heard their glorification and sanctification, Allah swore by His Honor and Majesty again and said, 'I will surely, surely, definitely establish this.' What will I establish? These glorifications. These praises that the angels are reciting, I will establish them for the lovers of this Lady, her father, her husband, and her sons until the Day of Judgment. The glorification and sanctification that these angels will perform until the Day of Judgment, Allah will grant the reward of it to their lovers. chapters.title: Centrality of Fatima (s.a.) in Creation
chapters.summary: The discussion explores the Hadith-e-Kisa, establishing Fatima (s.a.) as the central figure of creation and the link between the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the universe.

chapters.title: Marriage and Dowry of the Shahzadi
chapters.summary: The speakers detail the heavenly marriage of Fatima (s.a.) and Ali (a.s.), noting that her dowry includes one-fourth of the world and authority over Paradise and Hell.

chapters.title: The Centrality of Fatima Zahra (s.a.)
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the recognition of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is a fundamental requirement for all creation, including Prophets and angels.

chapters.title: The Luminous Nature of Zahra (s.a.)
chapters.summary: This section explores the meaning of the title 'Zahra' and describes the radiant light that emanated from her during her prayers.

chapters.title: The Creation of Light and the Angels' Trial
chapters.summary: A Hadith from Bihar al-Anwar explains how the light of the Ahlulbayt was created and how the light of Fatima (s.a.) saved the angels from darkness.

chapters.title: The Light of Majesty and Divine Knowledge
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the meaning of 'Light of Majesty,' explaining that Fatima (s.a.) was created directly from this divine source, representing God's knowledge and power.

chapters.title: The Luminous Origin of Lady Fatimah
chapters.summary: The lecture describes the creation of Lady Fatimah's light from the Divine Majesty, which dazzled the angels and led to the manifestation of the Imams.

chapters.title: Angelic Devotion to the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The angels, including Gabriel and Michael, recognized the superiority of the Ahlulbayt and prayed to become their servants, a status granted by Allah.

chapters.title: Angelic Service and the Day of Judgment
chapters.summary: Traditions illustrate how angels served Lady Fatimah in her home and the grand, luminous arrangements prepared for her resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: The Centrality of Lady Fatima (s.a.) in Mahshar
chapters.summary: The lecture describes the unique, exalted status of Lady Fatima (s.a.) on the Day of Judgment, where she is carried on a she-camel of light while other noble figures walk on foot.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Verse of Light
chapters.summary: Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) interprets the Verse of Light (Surah An-Nur 24:35), identifying Lady Fatima (s.a.) as the niche, Imam Hasan (a.s.) as the lamp, and Imam Husayn (a.s.) as the glass.

chapters.title: Dua-e-Noor and Seeking Intercession
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces Dua-e-Noor, a prayer taught by Lady Fatima (s.a.) to Salman (r.a.) for protection against fever and as a means of seeking intercession.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Ziyarat
chapters.summary: The session concludes with the recitation of the Ziyarat of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.) following the announcement of the quiz details.

chapters.title: Salutations to Lady Fatima (s.a.)
chapters.summary: The session begins with traditional salutations and Ziyarat, emphasizing the spiritual connection between the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his daughter, Lady Fatima (s.a.).

chapters.title: Grand Quiz Lucky Draw Results
chapters.summary: The organizers announce the lucky draw winners for the Shahzadi-e-Konain Grand Quiz, listing recipients of the fourth, third, second, and first-place prizes.

title: 🎁🎉 KULL-E-IMAAN (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2026 🎁🎉 | 11-JAN-2026 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive exploration of the philosophy of worship as exemplified by Imam Ali (a.s.), serving as the foundation for the Kull-e-Imaan Grand Quiz 2026. It examines the three levels of worship—merchant, slave, and the free—while highlighting the Imam's unparalleled devotion, sincerity, and absolute certainty in his faith. The session emphasizes the necessity of Wilayah as a prerequisite for the acceptance of deeds and explores the Imam's practice of Namaz-e-Shab even amidst the intensity of battle.
content:
DSR Presents: Ali, Ali, Ali, Ali [Music] Ali, Ali. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 'O Allah, be for Your representative, Al-Hujjah, the son of Al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him dwell on Your earth...' I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon you, O Wali of the Age, assist us and do not leave us. Respected listeners and honorable viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Whose uniqueness is the limit of self-sufficiency, the sign of the Eternal... The limit of self-sufficiency, the sign of the Eternal (As-Samad); in His house is the birth of the beloved, the heir of 'He begets not, nor is He begotten' (Lam yalid wa lam yulad). Subhan Allah! Respected audience, on the occasion of the auspicious birth of the Commander of the Faithful, the Leader of the Pious, the Soul of the Master of Messengers, the Slayer of the Infidels and Polytheists, the Leader of the Bright-faced ones, the Victorious Lion of Allah, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), on this 13th of Rajab al-Murajjab, we are once again present before you with the 'Kull-e-Imaan (a.s.) Grand Quiz'. On behalf of the entire TSR team, we welcome you all to this episode. Before we begin this episode, let us first present our congratulations on this auspicious day of birth to the presence of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.), and we also offer our special congratulations and greetings to all of you on this day. Respected audience, the virtues and merits of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), are like an ocean, a deep sea, where everyone can dive as much as they want based on their knowledge and recognition (ma'rifah), but no matter how hard they try, they cannot reach its depth. That is, human intellect... ...that is, human intellect seems unable to comprehend it, the tongue unable to describe it, and the pen unable to write it. Numerous narrations have been recorded in this regard, and the honorable poets have also penned this down beautifully. I recall four poetic lines (misras) which I present before you: 'The pen says, what kind of miracle of every historian of the world do I see? I have been writing the virtues of Ali for centuries, yet the page always appears blank. I have been writing the virtues of Ali for centuries, yet the page always appears blank.' Respected audience, among these countless virtues and merits of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (a.s.), such as the knowledge of Ali, the courage of Ali, and the status and station of Ali, an important aspect is also the worship ('ibadah) of Ali. This is such an important aspect that it would require several episodes to describe, and in itself, in terms of its depth and vastness, it is a very broad topic. And another point worthy of consideration, Brother Gulzar, is that sometimes it happens that a person makes a failed attempt to understand these virtues of Mawla Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) through the limited flight of their intellect, and when they fail to comprehend these virtues... ...when they fail to comprehend these virtues, they deny them and become a 'Mukassir' (one who diminishes their status). On the other hand, there are also individuals who, upon reading or hearing about the lofty status, station, and virtues of Ali (a.s.), fall into exaggeration (Ghuluw) and, God forbid, make the mistake of considering him God. However, by ignoring such a great aspect as the worship ('ibadah) of Ali (a.s.), they too will be called 'Mukassir'. Jazak'Allah, Brother Ehsan! Your sentence reminds me of four poetic lines: 'The Messenger of Truth has raised Haidar in such a way, as if a Quran has been placed upon another Quran. And the Nusayri is also a Mukassir at the door of Haidar... Yes, the Nusayri is also a Mukassir at the door of Haidar, for they have reduced worship from his virtues.' Ah! Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah! 'They have reduced worship from his virtues.' Yes, indeed, indeed. So with this, dear friends, we begin today's 'Kull-e-Imaan (a.s.) Grand Quiz', the topic of which is 'Mawla Ali (a.s.) and Worship', and we will try to have a brief discussion on this. But before that, we request you all to take a look at the rules and regulations of this quiz. The link for the quiz is now live, which... ...the quiz link is live, which is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you haven't registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all questions are present in the discussion. You just need to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not rush to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. The only condition for winning the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. Among all those who answer all questions correctly, 18 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, who will be given these prizes. So, viewers, let us begin our quiz and our discussion. But before that, an important announcement: the quiz link, which is live, is also pinned in the live chat. You can access the link from there. When you open the link, you will see all the quiz questions. Among all those questions, there will be one question labeled 'Special Question' with four options. Only one of the four options is correct, and the other three, as always, are incorrect... ...option is correct, and the other three, as always, are incorrect. However, instead of the question itself, it only says 'Special Question'. What is this Special Question? This Special Question will be announced for you at any point during our discussion. Therefore, you are requested to listen to the discussion carefully and wait for that Special Question, because the question is not written on the quiz link. To know the question, you must listen to this discussion. So, keep listening to the discussion. Whenever that Special Question is mentioned, pay attention to it, and then choose the correct option from the answer choices provided there based on that Special Question. So, with this, let us begin today's quiz. Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad: 'Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad'. Respected viewers, as you might have noticed, our topic for today is 'Mawla Ali (a.s.) and Worship'. Before we proceed with this discussion, we want to first look at what worship actually is in the eyes of the Master of the Universe (a.s.) and what he has stated regarding it. There is a narration found in Nahj al-Balagha, in which the Master of the Universe (a.s.) states: 'Inna qawman 'abadullaha raghbatan...' He states that indeed, there is a group of people who worship Allah out of desire... ...who worship Allah out of greed, for the sake of reward. For the sake of reward, thinking that if they worship, they will gain something through it; that whatever worship they perform, Allah will grant them something. With this intention, they worship based on greed. He states: 'Fa tilka 'ibadatut-tujjar'—that worship is the worship of merchants. It is the worship of a merchant; they are engaged in a trade with Allah, expecting something in return. Yes. Then he further states: 'Wa inna qawman 'abadullaha rahbatan'—and indeed, there is a group that worships Allah out of fear. That is, if they do not worship, Allah will punish them. Indeed, so to escape that punishment, they worship Allah. This means that in the first case too, their goal is not to reach Allah, but to gain something through worship. The second is the one who worships Allah out of fear, to escape punishment. In one place, there is a desire for Paradise, and in the other, there is the desire to escape Hell. Then he states: 'Fa tilka 'ibadatul-'abeed'—and this worship is the worship of slaves. Then he states: 'Wa inna qawman 'abadullaha shukran'—and indeed, there is a group that worships Allah to express gratitude, to thank Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon them. So the Mawla states: 'Fa tilka 'ibadatul-ahrar'—that this is the worship of the free. Wow, wow! That is, Brother Gulzar, if we look at it... ...that is, Brother Gulzar, if we look at it, all three are worship. Yes, it is not that the Mawla excluded any of these three methods from being worship. All three are worship. The state/quality of all three types of worship is different. This one is worshipping in freedom because he is worshipping Allah with the intention of gratitude, to thank Him for the blessings He has bestowed. And in another place, there is another narration in which the Master of the Universe (a.s.) states: 'Ilahi ma 'abadtuka...' He states: 'O my Lord, O my God, I do not worship You because I fear Your punishment.' Ah! 'That I fear Your punishment, that if You punish me, I will not worship You.' He states: 'Wa la tama'an fi thawabiq'—'nor do I desire that I should receive any reward through worship. I have no desire for the blessings You might give me in return for worship.' He states: 'Wa lakin wajadtuka ahlan lil-'ibadah fa 'abadtuka'—'but I found You worthy of worship, so I worshipped You.' Ah, Subhan Allah! 'I found that You are worthy of being worshipped, therefore I worship You.' What a beautiful statement! Subhan Allah! This is worship in the eyes of the Master of the Universe, and how worship should be performed. And the Mawla explained this. Moving forward, there is a narration in which a Jewish scholar came to the Master of the Universe (a.s.) and asked a question. He asked... ...he asked, and his question was: 'O Commander of the Faithful, when you worship Allah, your Lord, have you seen your Lord? At that time when you worship Allah, when you worship your Lord, have you seen your Lord?' This is exactly the kind of question asked by worldly people, ordinary people who worship in such a way that they have a physical concept of a Lord, a Creator, in their minds. He is understanding it in that way, thinking that the Master of the Universe (a.s.) must also be worshipping with some physical concept of a Creator in his mind. Therefore, he asks further: 'Have you seen your Lord?' Now look, this is also a stage of recognition (ma'rifah). Here we will also discuss the level of recognition of the Master of the Universe (a.s.). This is also for the people to understand that a person's worship is connected to their recognition (ma'rifah). Indeed, the value of one's worship depends on their recognition. The more recognition one has while worshipping, the more the value of their worship will increase. Now, the conversation is with the Master of the Universe (a.s.). He is asking the Master of the Universe (a.s.). And see, recognition itself means knowing one's Lord. Indeed. Now, how the Master of the Universe (a.s.) recognizes Him is what he will explain here. He is asking: 'When you worship, have you seen your Lord at that time of worship?' ...seen your Lord. The Mawla said to him: 'Waylaka! Ma 'abadtuka Rabban lam arah.' Woe to you! I do not worship a Lord whom I have not seen. This is the statement of recognition (ma'rifah). 'I do not worship a Lord whom I have not seen.' So he asked: 'How? How did you see Him?' He too thought that when the Master of the Universe (a.s.) was stating this, because of his limited intellect, he thought he was talking about physical eyes. Also, look, he might have been asking sarcastically, taunting that 'Your Lord is not visible, so how do you worship Him?' But he forgot whom he was questioning. So the Mawla states... He asked: 'How then did you see Him?' The Mawla replied: 'Woe to you! Eyes cannot perceive Him with physical sight...' That is, He cannot be observed with these physical eyes. '...but hearts see Him through the realities of faith (wa lakin tarahul-qulubu bi-haqa'iqil-iman).' That is, the heart sees Him, not the eyes. The heart sees Him through the realities of faith. This means the heart is completely certain of His existence. Yes, it is not in a dilemma of whether God exists or does not exist. ...exists or does not exist. It does not need arguments to prove whether God exists or not. That heart is completely content and certain that God exists. And with those eyes, the Mawla states, 'I have found my Lord whom I worship. I have seen Him.' That is, the Mawla states, 'I have seen Him. I do not worship one whom I have not seen.' This is the stage of worship of the Master of the Universe (a.s.), his stage of recognition (ma'rifah). And look, this is the Master of the Universe (a.s.). How can anyone estimate his recognition? There are statements like: the Mawla states, 'Even if the veils were removed, it would not increase my certainty.' That is, even if the veil of the unseen is removed, my faith and certainty are at such a stage that they cannot be increased further; my faith is at the peak of perfection, and there can be no further increase in certainty. This is what is called faith, and this is what is called 'Kull-e-Imaan' (the totality of faith). Wow, wow! That is, the Mawla is describing the limit of his faith, where he does not need physical sight or arguments to believe in God. And when we talk about the worship of the Master of the Universe (a.s.), let us first ask the Holy Quran, because the Holy Quran is the book in which Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has concealed the attributes of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.). The attributes of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have been kept hidden. In fact, the Holy Quran is seen reciting the praises of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Indeed, O Quran, tell us what secrets of the worship of the Master of the Universe (a.s.) you have kept hidden within you. In this regard, Allama Majlisi (a.r.) narrates in Bihar al-Anwar from the Amali of Sheikh Saduq, referencing Surah az-Zumar, which is Surah number 39, verse number 9. What does the verse say? 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord...'—that is, is the one who spends the entire night, in the moments of the night, in the state of prostration and standing, in what state? Fearing the Hereafter, worshipping God, and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, spending the entire night in worship? Regarding this verse, it is mentioned in a narration that a person says, 'I came to Ali (a.s.)'—for what purpose? This is an interesting thing—'so that I may observe his worship (*li-anzura ila ibadatihi*).' Wow, I just want to see his worship, how the Mawla worships. So, that person came to the Mawla and then says, 'I swear by Allah, I now bear witness to this...' ...by Allah, I swear by God, I am now a witness to this, I bear witness to what I saw. What did I see? That I came to him at the time of Maghrib, and then what did the Mawla do? The Mawla offered the Maghrib prayer with his companions, meaning his companions and friends offered the Maghrib prayer in congregation behind the Mawla. When he finished the Maghrib prayer, the Mawla became occupied with *ta'qibat* (post-prayer supplications). He recited the *ta'qibat*, and immediately after the *ta'qibat*, he offered the Isha prayer. The Isha prayer was offered with the companions, and then the Isha prayer ended here. That is, the obligatory prayer in congregation was finished. After this, that person says, '*Thumma dakhala manzilah* (then he entered his house)'. Then the Mawla returned to his home. Yes, meaning this proves another thing: congregational prayer is for obligatory prayers, which can be performed in congregation. As for recommended (*mustahab*) prayers, they are performed individually (*furada*). If a person wants to pray their recommended prayers, they cannot be done in congregation. They should go home and perform them individually. So then, the Mawla returned home. He says, 'I also followed the Mawla to his house.' There, that night, he was blessed with the opportunity to stay at the Mawla's house. So now he says, 'I saw how the Mawla spent the entire night.' He says, '*Zalla yusalli* (he continued to pray)'—the entire night he was either praying or reciting the Quran (*wal-Quran*). And until when? *Ila fajr* (until Fajr). Until the Fajr prayer, the Mawla spent the night in this state, either in prayer or... ...the Mawla spent the night, either in the state of prayer or reciting the Quran. Okay, here, for us, especially for the youth, if one has to stay awake at night, then the worship of God should be the purpose for which a person stays awake, not just to waste time. This should be the way of the followers of the Master of the Universe. Then after that, this person says, '*Thumma jaddada wudu'a*' (then he renewed his wudu). He performed ablution again and then returned to the mosque. He came out of the house, went towards the mosque, and once again, the Fajr prayer was offered in congregation with the people. The Mawla led the Fajr prayer. Then, after offering the Fajr prayer, the Mawla remained sitting there. He was occupied with *ta'qibat* until sunrise (*hatta tala'at ash-shams*). The sun rose. After sunrise, the Mawla is still sitting there, present in the mosque. People are coming to the Mawla, one after another. First, two men came. There was some dispute between them; they were quarreling. They had a dispute over something. The Mawla reconciled them. Then, when these two left, another two men came. And all of this was being observed by the person who had come. He is narrating all this, saying, 'I saw two men leave, and two other men came. They also had a dispute between them, and they too came to the Master of the Universe for reconciliation. The Mawla also resolved their...' ...had come to the Master of the Universe. The Mawla decided their matter as well. And this process continued until Zuhr. Yes, it went on until Zuhr. Then, when the time for Zuhr came, the Mawla renewed his wudu again for the Zuhr prayer. Even though he was already in a state of wudu, this is also recommended (*mustahab*). Our jurists (*maraji'*) say that one should renew their wudu. Even if a person is in a state of wudu, it is still a recommended act to perform wudu again before prayer. So, the Mawla renewed his wudu, and the Zuhr prayer was offered, and after that, similarly, *ta'qibat* were recited, and after the *ta'qibat*, the Asr prayer was offered. That is, Zuhr and Asr were performed together, one after the other. After performing the Asr prayer, the Mawla sat in the mosque again. Yes, then some people started coming. They were bringing their issues, and the Mawla was resolving their problems. And it is also written in the narration, '*wa yufti*' (and he was giving rulings), meaning the Mawla was also issuing decrees/fatwas for them. And how long did this continue? *Ila an ghabat ash-shams* (until the sun set). That is, he was blessed with the opportunity to spend an entire day with the Mawla. Yes. So, what did he see throughout the day? That the Mawla was in a state of worship. Yes. And then at the end he says, '*Fa-kharajtu*' (so I left). 'Now I left from there, and as I left, I was saying, *wa ana aqul* (and I was saying), I was leaving while bearing witness: I swear by Allah, I...' ...I was leaving while saying, 'I swear by Allah, I bear witness that *annaha hazihil-ayah nazalat fihi* (indeed, this verse was revealed concerning him).' This verse of the Quran was revealed only for the Master of the Universe. I bear witness to this. Yes, Hasan Bhai, you were just discussing wudu and the renewal of wudu. Let us start from here, as worship also begins with wudu. Indeed, the wudu of the Master of the Universe. Wow, let us start the discussion from here. Since there are acts of worship, let us begin with this. It is mentioned in a narration, meaning the sixth Imam (a.s.) says, that when Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) went to perform wudu, he would not allow anyone to pour water for him. He would not give permission to anyone else even for the water. He would fetch his own water and perform wudu himself. And when he was asked, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, why do you not allow anyone to pour water for you?'—and since he was Amir al-Mu'minin, people would step forward out of respect to pour water, but he would refuse. He would refuse the water. So when asked, 'Why do you not allow anyone? You should let them,' the Imam replied, '*faqala: la uhibbu an ushrika fi salati ahada* (he said: I do not like to associate anyone in my prayer).' Wow, Subhan Allah! This is the standard of worship. Meaning, Gulzar Bhai, in the worship of the One Who has no partner, the Mawla does not want anyone to be associated with him in that worship while he is performing it. ...anyone to be associated with him. This is the faith of the complete faith (Kull-e-Iman)—not to associate anyone even by an atom's weight anywhere. As for our worship, even when we pray the entire prayer, we look to see who is watching our prayer or who is not, and we wish someone would do this or that for us. The Master of the Universe—meaning we too should learn many things from this and put them into practice. That is, there is sincerity (*khuloos*) in this, showing how pure worship is performed. Indeed, indeed. Further, there is another narration in which it is stated: '*kana amirul-mu'minina (a.s.) iza tawadda'a...*'—the reason being that when the Master of the Universe went for wudu, his face would change color. Allahu Akbar! This is the fear of God, meaning it would change out of the fear of God. This is recognition (*ma'rifat*), this is witnessing (*mushahadah*). He does not worship the One whom he has not seen. So that is it, he is the complete faith; when he goes for worship, his face changes color. Further, it is mentioned not only for Amir al-Mu'minin, but also for Janabe Zahra (s.a.) that when she went for worship, her face would similarly change color. After that, it is mentioned about Imam Hasan (a.s.) that when Imam Hasan (a.s.) went for wudu, his face also changed color. He was also asked, 'Why does your condition become like this when you go for wudu?' The Mawla replied, '*faqala: haqqun 'ala man arada...*' The Mawla said, '*faqala: haqqun 'ala man arada an yadkhula 'ala dhi-l-'arsh...*' He says that it is the right of the one who is going for worship, it is his right that when he enters, he is going before the Lord of the Throne. Wow, so his state should be such; why shouldn't his face change color, a face like that? And along with this, in the same narration, it is mentioned similarly about the fourth Imam (a.s.) that when he went just for wudu, his face would change color. Now, who knows what his state would be during worship, if this is the condition during wudu! And if you see, Hasan Bhai, there is also a narration from the sixth Imam (a.s.) where he says—meaning, this is just about wudu, the discussion hasn't even reached worship yet, but we cannot even comprehend it. Whether we call it a miracle or what, this is something beyond human comprehension, that this is the state just during wudu, before worship. So, these are the extraordinary merits (*faza'il*) of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and they must be narrated. Their worship must be described, showing how they used to worship. Now look here, this is a small matter, but look at the aspect of worship: Ali (a.s.) had arranged a small chamber (*hujrah*) in his own house specifically for worship. Subhan Allah! This is the arrangement for worship in his own home. This is how a person progresses. And most of their (a.s.) actions were performed so that people would see them and prepare and ready themselves. ...prepare and ready themselves. That is, the manner of worship—they established this manner even in their home. While people usually think about whether to go to the mosque or not, he had a separate place for worship even in his home. It is mentioned in a narration where the sixth Imam (a.s.) states: '*kana 'aliyyun (a.s.) qad attakhadha baytan fi darihi laysa bil-kabiri wa la bis-saghir...*' He says that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had made a chamber in his house that was neither too big nor too small, meaning it was not so cramped that a person could not worship freely. And then it is mentioned that whenever he intended to pray, he would go into that chamber. Now, this preparation for worship—wudu and arranging a room—this is the preparation. Regarding this, we find accounts of Amir al-Mu'minin's prayers and fasting. We are mentioning all this briefly. Because we have already said that if we were to discuss only his worship, it would require several episodes; even one or two would not suffice. Indeed, indeed, we are speaking briefly here. Here, in this narration found in Bihar al-Anwar, it says: '*kana yasumu naharahu wa yusalli laylahu alfa rak'ah*' (he used to fast during his day and pray a thousand rak'ahs during his night). Wow! It is mentioned that he would fast during the day and pray all night, offering a thousand rak'ahs of prayer in a single night—every single night. That is, fasting during the day and praying a thousand rak'ahs every night. This is just the night-long worship of a thousand rak'ahs... ...this is just the night-long worship of praying a thousand rak'ahs every night—1,000 rak'ahs of prayer every night, and that too after fasting all day. Wow, alright. Now, this is the night prayer, but separate from this is the Night Prayer (Namaz-e-Shab). Wow! Apart from this thousand-rak'ah prayer, there is Namaz-e-Shab. It is mentioned in a narration that the Master of the Universe himself says: '*ma taraktu salat al-layl mundhu sami'tu an-nabiyya (s.a.w.a.) [yaqulu] salat al-layl nur*' (I have never missed the night prayer since I heard the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say: 'The night prayer is light'). Wow! Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says, 'I have never abandoned the Night Prayer since I heard from the blessed tongue of the Messenger of Allah that the Night Prayer is light.' Wow, Subhan Allah! title: Ahkaam | Session # 2 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture provides a detailed overview of the Islamic rulings (Ahkaam) regarding fasting during travel and the definition of 'watan' (homeland). Maulana Zulfiqar Mehdi explains the conditions under which a traveler is exempt from fasting, the specific distance requirements, and the rules for frequent travelers. Additionally, the session clarifies the three categories of 'watan' according to Ayatollah Sistani, helping viewers understand their obligations for prayer and fasting in different residential contexts.
content:
...that this love... speak to me... wound on the heart [music]... La ilaha illallah... Rahman's songs... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. In the second episode of this wonderful program, we welcome all of our viewers. Alhamdulillah, in the first episode, we saw how the intention (niyyah) for this blessed month of Ramadan should be made, regarding a person's... ...how the intention (niyyah) for Ramadan should be made, regarding a person, and regarding the recitation of the Quran... will be before us. So dear friends, the blessed month of Ramadan is before you. We wait for this blessed month so that this month comes and we can perform maximum worship (a'maal) in it. The best worship regarding this month is that we seek forgiveness for our sins in the court of the Almighty. Friends, the real purpose of the blessed month of Ramadan is not just to remain hungry and thirsty, or to consume delicious dishes at the time of Sahar and Iftar, but its purpose is far more sublime. The Holy Quran itself states in this regard, in Surah al-Baqarah, verse 183: 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu kutiba alaykumus-siyam kama kutiba alalladhina min qablikum...' (O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you...). And this is what we have discussed in detail in the episodes of this program... and we request all the viewers who have questions regarding Ramadan... Keep sending your questions regarding Ramadan to this WhatsApp number, [number removed]..., the answers to which we will keep conveying to you through the scholars of religion. Come, viewers, with some of today's questions, let us once again present ourselves in the presence of the highly learned Maulana Zulfiqar Mehdi Saheb Qibla and seek answers from him. Salam Alaykum wa Rahmatullahi... Wa Alaykum Assalam. Alhamdulillah... In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Praise be to Allah... A traveler (musafir) is defined as one who intends to travel a total distance of 44 kilometers (including both going and returning). If such a person intends to travel from the night itself and leaves in the morning, and travels up to this distance, then after crossing the limit of Tarakhkhus (hadd-e-tarakhkhus), he can break his fast; he cannot keep the fast. If all the conditions are met... Now, the conditions of travel are, for example, that the travel must not be for a sinful purpose, okay? One should go for a permissible (halal) work. The total distance of going and returning, as I just said, should be 44 kilometers. There shouldn't be his home or any such thing on the way. So, if all these conditions are met and a person is traveling, he cannot fast. His fast automatically breaks once he crosses the limit of Tarakhkhus. Therefore, after that, he can eat or drink. ...before that, he cannot eat. Secondly, if someone's travel meets the Shariah conditions, and the travel is not for a sinful purpose, then that person cannot fast. But a person whose profession itself involves traveling, like a driver, or a tour operator, etc., and they travel for 16 or 17 days in a month... for all such people, they must fast, and their prayers will not be qasr (shortened). This is for those who are frequent travelers (kaseer-us-safar) or whose job involves traveling, and they do not have to travel continuously otherwise. But if someone travels not for a permissible purpose, but to commit a sin, like to kill someone, or for example, going to dance, or going to steal, then their fast is not excused. They must fast during their journey, and if they deliberately do not fast, they must perform qaza. This is the rule for drivers whose job is traveling. Otherwise, if they are regular Shariah travelers (shar'i musafir), they cannot fast; fasting is forbidden for them, and they must make up for it after the blessed month. Thank you very much, Maulana... Thank you very much, Maulana. You explained it very well. Regarding the limit of Tarakhkhus (hadd-e-tarakhkhus), if someone travels a certain distance, it is not that as soon as he leaves his house and completes the kilometers, he can break his fast. No. Tarakhkhus is that place where the city's boundary ends. For example, if someone lives in Mumbai, Mira Road, when they leave home, until they cross Borivali, they cannot eat or drink anything, nor can they shorten their prayers. Once they reach that point, they can. If someone travels more than 16 days in a month, then he must keep his fast... ...keep it away from his home. Look, you have addressed this question of ours here. The second question was regarding frequent travelers, about what the ruling is for them regarding fasting, which you have clearly explained—that they must fast. The third major question, which often arises for people, is regarding 'watan' (homeland). Maulana, what is meant by 'watan'? Is it just the birthplace, or does it include other things as well? If you could shed some light on 'watan', it would clarify things. Yes, look, Ayatollah Sistani says that a person can have three types of 'watan'. Listen carefully, viewers, this is a ruling of Ayatollah Sistani. First, 'watan' refers to the place, the house, the property, or land where your parents lived or live, where you were born, and after birth, you intend to keep it as your original homeland (watan-e-asli), where you reside and where your life's main center is. ...and where a person spends the main part of his life. The second is the home that a person adopts by choice. For example, your original home is in Azamgarh, but by choice, you have made Mumbai your home. What does this mean? It doesn't matter whether you live there permanently or for a few days, but by choice, you consider it your homeland, you live there, and you wish to spend the rest of your life there. This is the second type, a home chosen by yourself. The third type of home is one that a person chooses temporarily due to some necessity. For example, you got a job in Chandigarh. You went there, and you don't know how long you will stay—you know it might be 1, 2, or 3 years, but you don't know what will happen after that. So, if you go there for a job, for example... ...or if you went there to study, say for a 3-year course, and you live there and blend in with the local community. For example, you live in Mumbai but go to Pune to study, staying there for 5 days a week and returning on Saturday and Sunday. Now, when you stay there for 5 days, regardless of whether you intend to stay there for ten days at a stretch or not, if it accumulates to two weeks in a month, then you must pray full (tamam) prayers there, and you must fast. This will continue until you leave that place. If you leave it, then a new intention will be required. So, these are the three types of 'watan' (homeland) that have been explained. This is 'watan', and the rules of 'watan' will apply to it. Yes. Thank you very much, Maulana, for explaining the definition of 'watan' so clearly and easily, and how prayers, fasting, and other Shariah rulings applicable to us should be performed in relation to 'watan'. Insha'Allah, in the next episode, we will benefit from your presence again. Viewers, you too can send your questions to this WhatsApp number: [number removed].
Fasting is not permitted for a traveler who meets the Shariah conditions of travel (44km round trip, non-sinful purpose).
A traveler must cross the 'hadd-e-tarakhkhus' (city boundary) before they are allowed to break their fast.
People whose profession requires constant travel, such as drivers, must fast and perform full prayers.
Travel for sinful purposes does not grant an exemption from fasting; such fasts remain obligatory.
Ayatollah Sistani defines three types of 'watan': original homeland, chosen homeland, and temporary residence.
A temporary residence can become a place where full prayers and fasting are required if one stays there for specific durations.

title: EP14 | Saqalain Mein Afzal Kaun? Sawaalon Ke Jawaabaat | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological necessity of the Ahlulbayt as inseparable guides to the Quran, emphasizing the concept of Itmaam-e-Hujjat. The discussion addresses common doubts regarding the infallibility of Imams and the behavior of their deputies, clarifying that divine leaders operate based on outward manifestations rather than hidden knowledge. The session concludes by establishing the historical and scriptural foundation for the twelve successors of the Prophet, drawing parallels between the twelve Nuqaba of Bani Isra'il and the twelve Imams using Sunni source material.
content:
They do. I have the greatest right and authority over them. That is, whatever they do is in accordance with the Quran. This is what they have written. And then they say that the reason for keeping the Quran with the Ahlulbayt is that the love of the Ahlulbayt has been made obligatory by the Quran and the Prophetic traditions. (Qul la as'alukum 'alayhi ajran illal-mawaddata fil-qurba) - under verse 23 of Surah Ash-Shura, this love is obligatory. This is the reward of the Risalah (Prophethood). And if someone does not love the Ahlulbayt and does not follow them as stated in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, (Ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abada) - 'If you hold fast to both of them, you will never go astray after me.' These two will never separate from each other until they reach me at the Pond of Kawthar. That is, one individual from the Quran and the Ahlulbayt will always remain until the Day of Judgment. Therefore, some traditions say it is the Quran, and some say it is the Ahlulbayt. For example, there is a very famous tradition: (La yaghru al-Qur'anu hujjatan illa bi-qayyim) - 'The Quran cannot be a proof except with a guardian (Qayyim).' There must be a guardian. Just as the Quran itself says in Surah Bani Isra'il, (Inna hadhal-Qur'ana yahdi lillati hiya aqwam) - 'Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.' Now, who is this 'Aqwam'? That is the Imam. This 'Aqwam' and what is in the tradition (La yakunu al-Qur'anu hujjatan illa bi-qayyim) - look, both are tallying with each other. In the same way, every... Tabari has explicitly explained that this refers to the Imams of the Ahlulbayt. So, this is the Greater Weight (Thaqal al-Akbar) and the Lesser Weight (Thaqal al-Asghar). Now, play the next question. Assalamu Alaikum. My question was that our Imams are infallible, and according to our belief, an infallible person cannot make a mistake. Then what is the matter with the deputies who collected Khums on behalf of our Imams? In history, there are countless instances where our Infallibles appointed someone to collect Khums, and they deceived the people. Like the case of Ali Hamza al-Bataini. Yes, so he is asking that the Na'ibeen (deputies) and Wukala (agents) were appointed by the Imams, yet they went astray. Does this mean the Imams do not have knowledge of the unseen? If they have knowledge of the unseen, how did they appoint the wrong people? Does this not cast doubt on their infallibility? So, see, understand this well: when not just the Imams, but for example, the story of Prophet Musa (a.s.) which I presented in the previous episode—that he selected 7,000 out of 70,000, then 700 out of 7,000, and then 70 out of those 700, and after that, those 70 all became apostates. So, does this cast a shadow on the infallibility (Ismah) of Prophet Musa (a.s.)? Does it cast a slur on his infallibility? No. This does not affect his infallibility. It does not affect it because Prophet Musa (a.s.) was outwardly dealing with the people. As I just submitted to you, all the Prophets, Messengers, and divine representatives were tasked with dealing with the outward aspect. They dealt with people according to the outward appearance. In exactly the same way, the Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) also dealt with people outwardly, and no slur was cast upon their infallibility. Is that right? So, as you mentioned regarding Ali ibn Abi Hamza al-Bataini, he was initially a good companion, but later he became a ghali (extremist) and deviated, becoming a follower of Abul Khattab. Abul Khattab was also a companion, but he too became a ghali. His name was Abul Khattab. Actually, his name was Muhammad ibn Abi Zaynab, who was famous by the name Abul Khattab. So that was the case. Take the next question. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We have some non-Shia friends who tell us, 'You say your Imams are Shia, but on the other hand, we see that they get provoked by others.' For example, the Hadith al-Manzilat that you narrate—what is in it? You say that Imam Ali (a.s.) went to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked Imam Ali (a.s.), 'Are you not happy with the position you have?'—the whole narration and event you know. They point out three things in it. First, that Imam Ali (a.s.), God forbid, was not satisfied—meaning he was not happy—with the decision of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to leave him behind in Medina, and he only agreed after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) explained it to him. Before that, he was sad. This proves that the decisions of Mawla Ali (a.s.) and other Imams (a.s.) are not the same as the decisions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and their planning is not the same. The second thing this proves—leave aside that they are infallible—is that your Imams, God forbid, are easily provoked by others. Meaning, they were told that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is leaving you behind, so they became sad and went to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the whole event followed. At the same time, you also say that your Imams are the Hujjah (proof) of Allah on this earth. How can it be that the Hujjah of Allah is provoked by common people and gets deceived by them? So please answer this. Khuda Hafiz. So, look, these two questions about Hadith al-Manzilat—we will have a separate topic for that, Insha'Allah, and there will be a full episode on Hadith al-Manzilat, Insha'Allah. The second question is: why was Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) so easily provoked by people? When people provoked him, he went and complained to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), saying 'Ama tarza' (Are you not pleased?), because the Prophet had said, 'You have left me among women and children.' That the Prophet had to explain the Hadith al-Manzilat. So, the answer is very simple. Let me first present a sentence of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to you: Mawla-e-Kainat says, '(Law kushifal ghita'u ma zdadtu yaqina) - If the veils of the unseen were removed from before me, my certainty would not increase.' Ali has such certainty. Now the question is, why did Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) say this? The hypocrites were spreading this propaganda. The hypocrites were spreading propaganda all over Medina that 'He left Ali among women and children.' To break this propaganda, to end it, Mawla-e-Kainat went to the Prophet and said this, so that the Prophet himself would say it. If Ali (a.s.) had said it himself, it would not have mattered. But when the Prophet said, '(Ama tarda an takuna minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa) - Are you not pleased that you are to me as Harun was to Musa?', such things are called 'Masrahi' (theatrical/demonstrative). 'Masrahi' means sometimes a question is asked so that the answer becomes manifest for others. And there are many examples of this in the Quran. We will give just one example, and the matter will become clear to you. This example is in Surah Taha, verse number 17. Allah asks Prophet Musa (a.s.), '(Wa ma tilka bi-yaminika ya Musa) - And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?' Did Allah not know what it was? So why was Allah asking the question? He was asking so that the matter would be clear to others—meaning, what is its use? What is its reality? What is the reality of this staff? So Prophet Musa (a.s.) replied, '(Qala hiya 'asaya) - He said, this is my staff. (Atawakka'u 'alayha) - I lean upon it. (Wa ahushu biha 'ala ghanami) - I use it to drive my sheep. I use this wooden staff for this purpose. (Wa liya fiha ma'aribu ukhra).' And it has other uses. Prophet Musa (a.s.) answered exactly as Allah asked, so that everyone would know that the reality of the staff Musa had until then was the same as any other piece of wood. But then, when the divine permission came, this same staff turned into a snake, into a dragon, which ate the snakes of the magicians. Their snakes were imaginary; they were not real. As the Quran said, 'Yukhayyalu ilayhi'—meaning 'bi-sihrihim' (by their magic). They were imagining it. People thought—people were imagining that these were snakes. And Allah commanded Prophet Musa (a.s.), 'Alqi 'asaka' (Throw your staff). First, He took the guarantee, explained the reality of the staff, and then, by the permission of the Creator, it happened. So it is known that Allah is showing that when we command, a simple staff can turn into a 'Bayyina' (clear proof). It can turn into a miracle of Allah. So, when a staff can change, then if the Hujjah of Allah wants to show a miracle by the permission of Allah, why do you wonder at it? So this question is 'Masrahi'. Masrahi means for the clarity of others, to explain to others, for the elucidation of others. So no one deceived the Imam, and it was not the case that the Mawla-e-Kainat fell for their words. No, do not use such sentences that Mawla-e-Kainat was deceived by them or fell for their words. No. Did Mawla-e-Kainat take any action, like 'Since they did this, I will do that'? No. He only submitted to the Prophet that 'These hypocrites are spreading this propaganda.' The Prophet clarified it, saying, 'It does not matter. Are you not pleased with this?' The Prophet explained that you are to me as Harun was to Musa. And then that question—if it is regarding Hadith al-Manzilat, we will discuss it in the chapter of Hadith al-Manzilat, Insha'Allah. There are no further questions. So let us move to today's topic. Let's see how much we can cover in this episode, otherwise, we will deal with the rest in the next episode, Insha'Allah. This next topic is, I believe, the last discussion on 'Imamat-e-Amma' (General Imamate). This is the last discussion of General Imamate. And after that, we will come to 'Imamat-e-Khassa' (Specific Imamate), so that the proof is complete, in which we will prove the Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) from the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni) so that no doubt or suspicion remains for anyone. Before moving forward, see, the most important rule of 'Jidal-e-Ahsan' (best argumentation) is that one should always provide references from the opponent's book. So, if anyone has any objection to these things, they should provide references from Shia books, and we will answer them. Otherwise, the references we will provide will all be from the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun when we discuss the Imamate of the 12 Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Insha'Allah. So this was a very important point that I had to submit to you. So now let us see that the last topic of this subject is that there are 12 Imams. Now, let me present some narrations to you. The Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, '(Inna hadhal amra la yanqadi hatta yamdiya fihimu ithna 'ashara khalifa) - This affair, meaning Islam, this religion, will not end until 12 Caliphs pass through them.' 12 successors of the Messenger of Allah. What is the emphasis on? On 12, 12. Now look at another Hadith: '(La yazalu amrul nasi madiya ma waliyahumu ithna 'ashara rajulan) - The affair of the people will not end until 12 men, meaning their guardians and Imams, are in charge of them.' And then he said, '(Kulluhum min Quraish) - All of them are from Quraish.' And in Sahih Muslim, this is as you know, the Sahih of Muslim ibn Hajjaj al-Nishapuri, and among the Ahl-e-Tasannun, Bukhari and Muslim are considered the top Sahih books—meaning among the Sihah al-Sittah, the position they hold is the highest. And there are many such narrations. Is that right? So refer to Sahih Muslim, Volume 3, Page 1451, Kitab al-Imara. You will find such narrations. And let me present one more Hadith to you: The Prophet says, '(Inna 'iddatal khulafa'i ba'di 'iddatu nuqaba'i bani Isra'il) - The number of Caliphs after me will be equal to the number of Nuqaba (leaders) of Bani Isra'il, or Nuqaba-e-Musa.' The narration is like this: Nuqaba-e-Musa, equal to the Nuqaba of Musa—meaning the Nuqaba of Bani Isra'il, whose number is said to be how many in the Quran? 12. Their number is stated as 12 in the Quran. And its reference is Kanz al-Ummal, Muttaqi al-Hindi, Hadith number 14971. So this is absolutely clear. Now, when we have seen that it is like this, let us see who these 12 are. We will discuss this in the next episode, Insha'Allah. Wa Sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi al-tayyibina al-tahirin al-ma'sumin al-mazlumin, wa la'natullahi da'ima ala a'daihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri faza'ilihim wa manaqibihim.
