title: EP13 | Shahaadat-e-Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) | Masaaib | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn | 3rd Jamadi al-Saani
excerpt: This lecture commemorates the martyrdom of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), focusing on the profound grief of the Ahlulbayt and the historical significance of mourning her. The speaker recounts the final moments of the Lady of Light, her preparations for her children, and the immense sorrow experienced by Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Hasnain (a.s.). The discourse emphasizes the importance of keeping the tradition of mourning alive as a testament to the Prophet's teachings.
content:
TSR presents. Imam-e-Raza (a.s.) says: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum wa sahhil makhrajahum. 'Inna yawmal Husayn'—indeed, the day of Husayn has wounded our eyelids. And it is not just for one day; this grief of ours continues in this manner until the Day of Judgment. Oh sir, that is for Imam-e-Husayn (a.s.). That is for Imam-e-Husayn (a.s.). In the same hadith, Imam-e-Raza (a.s.) says: 'Fa'ala mithlil Husayni falyabkil bakoon'—and for the likes of Husayn, the weepers should weep. For the likes of Husayn. Only these 14 are like Husayn. That is all. Should one go for that personality, or for the mourning of Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.)? Regarding this, Allama Iqbal said: 'Let us salute such a threshold, which gave the cradle of Husayn to the world.' His grief, or the grief of that Lady. Brother, the Majlis is growing. There used to be one Majlis, now there are ten. What is your problem? That famous hadith: 'Who will weep for my son?' If you look at the original text, what did the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) say to the Princess (s.a.)? What did he say? 'Inna nisaa-a ummati yabkeena ala nisaa-i ahli bayti wa rijaluhum yabkoona ala rijal-i ahli bayti'—Indeed, the women of my Ummah will weep for the women of my Ahlulbayt, and their men will weep for the men of my Ahlulbayt. The next sentence is your answer: 'Wa yujaddidoonal azaa jeelan ba'da jeelin fee kulli sanah'—And they will renew the mourning generation after generation every year. It is increasing every year. Why? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has said so. Indeed. The Prophet had already told us that they would continue to renew this mourning year after year. Now do you understand whose enemy is the one who wants to reduce this mourning? In reality, he is an enemy of the Prophet. Indeed. Indeed. He is not trying to reduce the mourning; he is actually trying to deny the word of the Prophet (na'uzubillah). The Prophet has already stated that they will continue to renew this mourning year after year. And how much do we weep, and how much should we weep for that Lady who became frail at the age of 18? Whose face became wrinkled? Whose hair turned white? It is the anniversary of Mir Anees. One of his stanzas. You gentlemen are listening, from the bed. Sarkar-e-Anees says that when the fire was lit or gathered, it said while shedding tears: 'Why do you burn my house? What have I done?' Why should we not weep? A person committed this atrocity, what a tragedy. They kicked the door and made it fall upon her. They kicked the door and made it fall upon her. Which house is that? It is the house whose roof is the Throne of Allah. For this, the Quran said: 'Ya ayyuhallatheena amanoo la tadkhuloo buyootan-nabiyyi illa an yu'thana lakum'—O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you. The Quran is saying do not enter the houses of the Prophet without permission. And what is happening here? They kicked the door and made it fall upon her. The weight fell on the side of the daughter of the Prophet, the benefactor. The martyr was in the womb of Batool. Dear ones, your voices have risen. May God shower mercy upon your voices. Listen. This is a special request for Masaib. That day came. When Sayyeda (s.a.) departed from this world. She prepared the Hasnain (a.s.). Then I remembered this stanza of the elegy. Keep listening, from the bed. 'Har hara ke uthi tham kar asar'—What is the state in this verse? Now think. Only 18 years old. This is the condition, from the bed. 'Har hara ke uthi tham kar asar'—She recited the final Fatiha upon her Prophet. She went to the neighbors' houses to say goodbye. 'O people, bid me farewell. Now is my departure. It was a burden, it was a burden, it was a burden for all of you, my noise and lamentation. Tomorrow Fatima will not be there. You sleep in peace. Tomorrow Fatima will not be there. You sleep in peace.' Listen to the final sentences, I am concluding the Majlis. Dear ones, Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.) prepared the Hasnain (a.s.). She prepared them and sent them to the mosque. 'My children, there is a special request, a special order. I am fulfilling it.' It is an order. She sent the children: 'Go to the mosque. Pray near your grandmother.' The Hasnain (a.s.) headed towards the mosque. Sayyeda (s.a.) called Asma. She called Asma and said, 'I see that the coffins made here do not have the level of modesty that Fatima requires.' Asma said, 'Lady, a coffin is made here. If you permit, I will make that coffin.' Sayyeda (s.a.) gave permission. Asma made a coffin out of palm wood. Please tell me with your hand on your heart. You are mourners. You are lovers of the Mawla. You are weepers for the Princess. Who in the world would be happy to see their own coffin? Tell me. Who in the world would be happy to see their own coffin? God knows what they did to my Lady. That Fatima, who had not smiled since the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) passed away. She saw the coffin. Ah, it is written that the Lady lay down in the coffin happily. She raised her hands: 'O God, just as she has protected my modesty, You also protect her modesty.' I would say, Lady, today there is so much concern for Asma's modesty. Come, let us go to the courts of the King of Kufa. Listen, dear ones. Look, the coffin is ready. Sayyeda (s.a.) came near Asma. She called Asma. 'Asma, now I am going into the chamber. Look, as long as the sound of Tasbih and Tahlil continues,' Understand that Fatima is alive. If the sound stops, understand that Sayyeda has gone to her father. I am narrating this faithfully. Asma was standing at the door of the chamber. For a while, the sound of Tasbih continued. For a while, I recited and you listened. Ask Zainab's (s.a.) heart. Ask Husayn's (a.s.) heart. Ask the heart of the Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). This sentence is on their hearts. For a while, the sound of Tasbih continued. And the Tasbih was not like how you and I recite it. When you and I recite Tasbih, the beads are in our hands. Why? Because we raise our hands. Alas for that Fatima, whose arm was struck with such a lash. Not just a lash, but a blow was struck with the hilt of a sword, such that now Fatima cannot even raise her hand for Tasbih. The sound of Tasbih and Tahlil continued. Asma kept listening. After a while, the sound stopped. Asma entered the chamber. She saw. What is the state? The Princess is covered with a sheet. She had said, 'Look, when the Hasnain come, do not bring them to my funeral first.' First, feed them something. My children will be hungry. Where in the universe will one find a mother like Fatima? The Hasnain (a.s.) entered the house. Asma saw the Hasnain. Seeing her, the Hasnain asked, 'Where is my mother?' Asma said, 'Children, go to the dining cloth, eat something first. I will take you to your mother shortly.' The Hasnain said a sentence, 'Asma, have you ever seen us eat without our mother?' She fell down, seeing Asma, seeing the Hasnain. She came into that chamber. Now, the request, listen. The Hasnain entered the chamber. They removed the sheet from their mother's face. The tradition says that Husayn came to her side. Hasan came to bathe her. They said one sentence: 'Mother, speak to us. Mother, speak to us. Otherwise, our souls will depart from our bodies.' The sound of falling from the chamber rose. Asma said, 'Princes, go and inform your father first.' Now listen, how great is the blow for Ali (a.s.). For Ali, God, the Commander of the Faithful, says: 'My life had two aspects. One aspect collapsed when the Prophet was martyred. The second aspect collapsed when the Prophet was martyred.' Ali, dear ones, the Hasnain came to the mosque, and now they come back. What I am about to say will shake the foundations of the Day of Judgment and has reached you gentlemen. When the Commander of the Faithful saw the Hasnain coming, crying and wailing, just saw them, 'Fabaqa Ali alayhis-salam ala wajh'—the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, who was so patient, Ali who was the conqueror of Khaybar, Ali who was the Lion of God, when he saw the Hasnain coming, Ali fell face down on the ground. Just the final sentences, I have reached the state. The Commander of the Faithful, face down, Allahu Akbar, fell face down on the ground. Just the final sentences. Alas, now look towards me, but Masaib is more about imagining than reciting. Whenever it is remembered, whenever we weep. The Commander of the Faithful went to the chamber, entered the chamber, removed the sheet from Sayyeda's face. What did he see? Fatima, with one hand on her cheek—God knows what Fatima is saying to Ali—with one hand on her cheek, Fatima is resting. Ali waited for the night as per her will. The night came, he prepared Fatima's coffin, laid Zahra in the coffin. Sayyeda's funeral, Sayyeda's corpse was in the coffin. We are saying it was a corpse, otherwise, you read the differences, 'Sarat kal khayal'—the body was not a body, it looked like a shadow that was in the coffin. Just the final sentences, dear ones. Surely, those of you whose mothers are alive, may God keep them safe. Those who have departed from this world, may God grant them the neighborhood of the Masoomeen (a.s.). The Commander of the Faithful said to the children once, 'Come, have the final look at your mother.' What a tragedy. To take the shadow of Fatima from their heads. Zainab, who was five years old—God knows what they do. When Khadija (s.a.) departed from the world, Zahra was five years old. Today, when Zahra is departing from the world, Zainab is five years old. Tomorrow, when Husayn (a.s.) departs from the world, Sakina (s.a.) will be five years old. Alas, what happens to Zainab's daughters? Zainab clung to her mother's funeral, but there was a father like Ali. He must have consoled her, and after consoling her, separated her from her mother's funeral. This is the way, this is the way. Children are separated from their parents' funerals like this. I wish someone had done this in Karbala, in Karbala. May God grant the reward of perfection. The daughters were separated from their mother's funeral. Sheikh Abbas-e-Qummi writes in 'Bayt-ul-Aza', both sons were standing. Ali said, 'Come, have the final look at your mother. Until Mother calls, we will not come.' Two hands emerged from the coffin, two hands emerged, as if Zahra was saying, 'Come my children, embrace my chest.' And then Husayn said, 'Mother, today you have called, we have come. Tomorrow you will call, there will be the chaos of the Resurrection, there will be the scene of Sham-e-Ghariban. This will be the same mother, the fear of Zahra.' Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. Allahumma ajjil liwaliyyikal faraj. Fatallal ayyami feehi ma lana lijar.

title: Hadees-e-Saqalain Mein Tamassuk Ka Kya Matlab Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the significance of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, emphasizing the Prophet's command to hold fast to the Quran and the Ahlul Bayt. He clarifies that the authentic narration specifies the Ahlul Bayt, refuting attempts to replace them with the Sunnah. The lecture defines 'Tamassuk' as a firm, life-saving commitment to these two weighty things and stresses the importance of educating the next generation in these teachings.
content:
This refers to Hadith al-Thaqalayn: 'I am leaving behind two weighty things among you: the Book of Allah and my progeny (Ahlul Bayt). If you hold fast to them, you will never go astray after me.' Hold fast to them, and you will never go astray. 'They will never separate from each other until they reach me at the Pond (of Kauthar).' This is fully established in the narrations. Now, some people have made alterations and replaced 'Ahlul Bayt' with 'Sunnah', repeating it over and over. But the authentic reference is 'Ahlul Bayt'. No one can change this, and any other version is not reliable. If they say 'my Sunnah', it is a weak narration. Therefore, the authentic path is the path of the Ahlul Bayt, and no one else can take their place. It is necessary for us, if we follow the narrations, to hold fast to the Ahlul Bayt. Another thing is that we must teach these narrations to our children and create an environment where children are educated in the teachings of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Today, the environment has become such that people are moving away from the Quran and Hadith. What does 'Tamassuk' (holding fast) mean? 'Tamassuk' means holding onto something with all your strength. For example, if there is a strong current of water and you are holding onto something to save yourself, you hold onto it not half-heartedly, but with all your life and strength. That is 'Tamassuk'—holding fast, because you know there is no other way of salvation... ...and if you leave it, there is destruction and loss everywhere.

title: Religion and Science  |  Episode #2  |  Maulana Sayed Abu Talib Tabatabai Sahab
excerpt: This lecture explores the complex relationship between Islamic faith and scientific inquiry, arguing that religion and science operate in distinct domains. Maulana Sayed Abu Talib Tabatabai Sahab emphasizes that while Islam encourages intellectual reflection, it is a category error to demand empirical scientific proof for spiritual truths. The discussion highlights the limitations of science as a fluid, changing discipline compared to the unchanging nature of divine revelation and devotional submission.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance. I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful... [recitation of prayers] ...O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Respected viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Viewers, it is very clear in our religion that the divine religion is a constitution that never changes, in which no alteration is ever found. The times keep changing, moving from depths to heights... Times keep changing, moving from depths to heights, but there will be no change in Allah's religion and law. Time is a moving caravan, but religion is an unalterable reality. Viewers, some people hold the view that 1400-year-old laws cannot work in this glittering modern world. Therefore, if you want to call yourself progressive, do not look back, otherwise you will find yourself trapped in a grip. We must clearly understand how to tear away this veil of deception, to know what changes in our times and what does not. Those religions where there is often a conflict between religion and science—like the tyrannical system of the Church that used to impose restrictions on thought, forbidding research—when that system could not succeed and the true face of the Church's religion began to fade, they started imprisoning people. Obviously, the body can be imprisoned, but intellect and thought cannot be chained in iron fetters. Alhamdulillah, Islam has neither... ...imprisoned nor has Islam placed blindfolds on the eyes, nor has it ordered to shut one's vision. chapters.title: Religion as an Unchanging Constitution
chapters.summary: The speaker asserts that while time is a moving caravan, the divine laws of religion are unalterable and do not conflict with true intellect.

chapters.title: Science, Religion, and the Limits of Proof
chapters.summary: Science relies on observation and physical laws, but it cannot be the sole metric for evaluating spiritual realities or devotional matters.

chapters.title: Refuting the Gadget Theory of Miracles
chapters.summary: The speaker rejects the modern attempt to explain miracles as advanced technology, emphasizing that they are divine acts beyond physical science.

chapters.title: The Fallacy of Proving Religion via Science
chapters.summary: The speaker argues against the trend of validating religious practices solely through scientific proof, noting that science is constantly changing and unreliable as a foundation for faith.

chapters.title: Limitations of Human Knowledge and Divine Power
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights that many aspects of creation, such as the biological processes within animals, remain beyond the scope of current scientific explanation, pointing instead to the power of God.

title: Majlis 1 | Amr Bil Ma'roof: Ma'roof Kya Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the Quranic command of 'Amr bil-Ma'roof' (enjoining good) through the lens of Surah Al-A'raf, verse 199. He emphasizes that true 'Ma'roof' is defined by sound intellect and spiritual satisfaction rather than mere ritualistic adherence. The discussion highlights the necessity of establishing 'Ma'rifat' (recognition) of the Creator and the Wilayat of Imam Ali as the foundation for all religious practice, while also reflecting on the profound sacrifices made by the youth of the Prophet's household in Karbala.

Peace be upon him who is a prisoner and also ill. Peace be upon him who is a prisoner and also ill. There are blisters on his feet, and there are thorns in the blisters. Peace be upon him. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. La hawla wala quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azim. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil. Ni'mal mawla wa ni'man nasir. Alhamdulillahir rabbil alamin. Wal aqibatu lil muttaqin wal yaqin. Wassalatu wassalamu ala ashrafil ambiya'i wal mursalin. Habibe rahil alamin Abil Qasim Muhammad. Sallallahu alayhi wa alihil masumin. Huwa waliyyi amrina wa sahibana wa mawlana wa habibana wa tabibana wa anisana wa munisana al kahfil hasin wa giyasul muztaril mustaqim. Ruhi wa arwahul alamin lahul fida. Amma ba'd faqad qalallahu tabaraka wa ta'ala fi kitabihil majid wa qawluhul haq wa huwa asdaqul qa'ilin. 'Khudh al-'afwa wa'mur bil-'urfi wa a'rid 'anil jahilin'. Sadaqallahul aliyyul azim. Salawat. The verse I have chosen for this discussion is from Surah Al-A'raf, which is the seventh chapter of the Quran. In this chapter, which is named Surah Al-A'raf, it is verse number 199. Allah Tabaraka wa Ta'ala is saying, giving an order to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Allah is ordering the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and actually, this is not just for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), but for all of us. Meaning, before translating, I am telling you that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says. The Imam (a.s.) says that 'Ma anzalallahu al-qur'ana illa bi-iyyak a'ni wasma'i ya jara'. This is the saying of the sixth Imam (a.s.). Allah did not reveal the Quran except with this motto, with this proverb, the Imam (a.s.) says with this proverb 'Iyyak a'ni wasma'i ya jara'. Meaning, I am talking to you, but listen, O neighbor. Meaning, it is addressing Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.) in many places, it happens like this. But actually, Allah's intent is other people. So this is a very important verse of the Quran, which was recited before you just now, that Allah says 'Khudh al-'afwa'. The very first thing. There are three commands in this verse. It is a small verse, see, actually there are only six words. But there are three main commands. And what is that command? The first is 'Khudh al-'afwa'. Meaning, what is its apparent meaning? You make forgiving your motto, your habit. That you forgive people. Whoever makes a mistake, forgive him. Whoever does a wrong thing, forgive him. 'Khudh al-'afwa', just keep forgiving. This is actually, we will explain it further, Insha'Allah. First, let me translate the verse. And then the second part says 'Wa'mur bil-'urf'. Wa-amur, meaning command, and give orders to the people. For what? Bil-urf (with what is known/customary). This portion, 'wa-amur bil-urf', is what we will discuss for the next five days, Insha'Allah. These two words. If Allah grants the ability and life, then we will discuss these two words. What does 'wa-amur bil-urf' mean? Command with 'urf'. 'Urf'. Insha'Allah, we will clarify that. Wa-arid 'anil-jahilin, the third order. And when the ignorant (jahil) addresses you, when the ignorant begins to speak, then turn away. There is no benefit in talking to the ignorant. Here, 'ignorant' does not mean someone who does not know. See, when the word 'jahil' is used in Arabic, it has two opposites. One word has two opposites. One opposite of 'jahil' is 'alim' (learned), and the other opposite of 'jahil' is 'aqil' (wise). Meaning, if a 'jahil' is someone who does not know, then it is fine; many people do not know many things. In that sense, only Allah, His Messenger, and the Imams are 'alim'. But the second type of 'jahil' is one who acts against intellect (aql). That intellect which Allah has given to everyone. Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the ability, we will discuss that a bit. So, there are three commands in this verse. First of all, forgive the people. Forgive them. Meaning, we hold onto a matter, and it happened 10 or 20 years ago, and in many places, it happens that the feud continues through generations. 'Their grandfather did this to our grandfather, so today we will not speak to them.' It is clear, right? Here, Allah is commanding: Khudh-il-'afwa. So, 'afw' means to forgive. And there is another meaning of 'afw', which is to treat with gentleness. 'Afw' means to treat with kindness and softness. And Allah has commanded the Prophet regarding this in the Quran as well. In another verse, verse number 159 of Surah Al-e-Imran, Allah says: 'Fabi-ma rahmatin minallahi linta lahum' (It is by the mercy of Allah that you are gentle with them). This is Allah's mercy upon you that you are treating them with such gentleness. You treat them so politely, so softly. This is the mercy of the Lord, because what was the Prophet? He was Rahmatul-lil-'Alamin (Mercy to the Worlds). The Prophet was a mercy for everyone, that is why the Prophet spoke with gentleness. The Prophet spoke softly. This was the Prophet's way. And from this, it is known who follows the Prophet and who does not. From a person's way of speaking, it becomes clear who is actually a Muslim and who is not. A person whose nature is to shout and scream and use abusive language in every conversation, understand that they are a Muslim only by name. But in terms of deeds, they are nothing. They are zero. Because the actual meaning of a Muslim is one who submits completely. That is called a Muslim. One who not only verbally but also adopts the Seerah (biography) and character of the Messenger of Allah. So now look at what Allah is saying in the Quran: 'Fabi-ma rahmatin minallahi linta lahum'. 'Linta' in Arabic is derived from 'layn', meaning very soft. Something that is very soft is called 'layyin' in Arabic. Meaning, the Prophet was very, very soft. So soft that Allah has given an example elsewhere in the Quran that even when you people act insolently towards the Prophet, the Prophet still feels shy to say anything to you. Meaning, Allah says in the Quran about the Prophet that he feels shy, but I will not. Allah says I will rebuke you on his behalf. Did you notice? So look at what the verse is: 'Fabi-ma rahmatin minallahi linta lahum; wa-law kunta fazzan ghalizal-qalbi la-naffaddu min hawlik'. O Prophet! If you were 'fazz', 'fazz' means rude, which is called rude in English. If you were rude and foul-mouthed, your tongue was bad, 'fazz' and 'ghalizal-qalbi' (hard-hearted), and if your heart was filled with malice, enmity, and all these things, then 'la-naffaddu min hawlik' (they would have dispersed from around you). The first part is for the Messenger of Allah, that he was very soft and that is why people came around him. And the second part, 'fazzan ghalizal-qalbi', in our exegesis, this was for that other 'big gentleman' who always walked around with a stick in his hand. So look, this verse that we just read, 'Khudh-il-'afwa', meaning forgive the people. 'Wa-amur bil-'urf', and command with 'urf'. What does 'urf' mean? 'Urf' means 'ma'ruf'. You say 'Amr-bil-Ma'ruf', right? So Allah is commanding the Prophet. There are many verses in the Quran that are about 'Amr-bil-Ma'ruf'. Many, for example, in Surah Tawbah, the signs of the believers are mentioned: 'Al-amiruna bil-ma'rufi wan-nahuna 'anil-munkar'. What is the sign of the believers? That they do 'Amr-bil-Ma'ruf', meaning they always command people to do good and forbid them from evil. This is the sign of the believers. And when the hypocrites are mentioned, what does the Quran say about them? That these are the people who command evil and forbid people from good. So if someone does this, understand that they are a hypocrite. These are the verses of Surah Tawbah. Or for example, the verse of Surah Luqman, Hazrat Luqman, who was a very great sage, said to his son: 'Ya bunayya' (O my son!), 'Aqimis-salah' (Establish prayer), look, pray, pray. 'Wa-mur bil-ma'ruf' (And command with good). 'Wan-ha 'anil-munkar' (And forbid from evil), forbid people from evil. 'Wasbir 'ala ma asabak' (And be patient over what befalls you). And then after that, Hazrat Luqman says, 'Inna dhalika min 'azmil-umur' (Indeed, these are matters of great resolve). These four tasks are very tough tasks, very difficult tasks, not easy. Prayer is also a difficult task, 'Amr-bil-Ma'ruf' is also difficult, 'Nah-e-'anil-munkar' is also difficult, and being patient over calamities is also difficult. This is what Hazrat Luqman says, the Quran has said it. 'Wasbir 'ala ma asabak'. Now, to understand what 'urf' is called. See, 'urf' means 'ma'ruf'. Generally, 'urf' means 'ma'ruf'. But in Urdu, for those who are familiar with Urdu, what is 'urf' called? That thing which is customary. That thing which people recognize. It is called 'urf-e-aam'. For example, in Urdu, a word is used, 'urf-e-aam'. Actually, in Bombay, the biggest problem in speaking is the language. Bombay people do not understand any one language. Meaning, they understand a mix of everything. That is why one has to speak a bit mixed here. Then when you speak mixed and this video goes somewhere else, they say, 'What language were you using?' For example, if we go somewhere else and speak, they say, 'We saw your video, what language were you speaking?' We said, 'Brother, for those we are addressing, that is the language.' Now, what does 'urf' mean? 'Ma'ruf', which is said, see, now we are bringing you to a point. What is 'ma'ruf' called? See, 'ma'ruf', the first thing is that 'ma'ruf' is that which a human accepts, meaning his intellect accepts it. His intellect says, 'Yes, this is the right thing.' This is the first. His intellect accepts it, his intellect says, 'Yes, this is right.' We will give you an example. And what is its second condition? That the person who does it, enjoys doing it. When he does that work, he should enjoy it. We will give an example. See, the intellect must accept it. For example, there is a thing that is intellect. See, when we say intellect, remember, that thing which everyone accepts, yes? Whether he is a Hindu, a Muslim, a Christian, a Sikh, anyone, that thing should be acceptable. He will accept it. For example, speaking the truth. Is there any religion in the world that says, 'Tell lies'? Is there any religion that says, 'Tell lies'? No religion says to tell lies. After that, people justify it, the liar justifies it. But actually, if you look, see, meaning in any law in the world, there is a common law, and it is called 'perjury'. What does 'perjury' mean? Lying in court. It is considered a very big sin. And whenever a witness is brought, before that, it is said, right, he places his hand on whatever his religious book is and says that I will say, 'I will tell the truth.' No, 'I will tell the truth and nothing but the truth.' That is why the witness is brought. And in the same way, he gives testimony. Have you heard anywhere in the world that there is any court where it is said you can lie? It is nowhere. Whatever religion it may be in the world. So what is the definition of 'urf'? The definition of 'urf' is, 'urf' is that which the intellect accepts, one. And it is any religion. And the second thing is, the person doing it should like it. For example, a child, he did mischief. He did something in the house, for example, he broke this glass. He was playing cricket, the glass broke, he was playing with a ball. Now the father came, came into the house, Daddy came. Daddy asked, 'Who broke this glass?' He says, 'Daddy, it happened by me.' He is afraid, he is afraid, but the parents have raised him such that, 'Son, no matter how big a sin you commit, never tell a lie.' So now when he speaks, he speaks the truth. 'Daddy, it happened by me, I made a mistake.' Now look, the truth he is speaking, his father is also accepting it, this boy is also accepting it, he is also liking it, and the father is also liking it that my son tells the truth. No matter what happens. Or let us give another example, that in any company, if there is an employee, if anything happens, meaning if the owner or manager sees that something went wrong, he asks, 'Brother, who did this?' If that employee says, 'Sir, I did it, I made a mistake,' then his credibility increases. He is very honest, he never lies and always owns up that 'Yes, I made a mistake.' So what is 'ma'ruf' called? First thing, what the intellect accepts, and the second thing, he should get pleasure in doing it. He should like it. That is why, that is why in the light of traditions, 'ma'ruf', meaning among all 'ma'ruf', what is the most important 'ma'ruf'? What is the best 'ma'ruf'? It is 'Ma'rifatullah'. It is the recognition of Allah. It is to recognize Allah. That is why they say this 'ma'rifat' is 'alladh-lazzat' (the ultimate pleasure). You don't get more pleasure than this in anything else. And what is its example? Like a man who is, for example, very thirsty. Understand, you fast in the month of Ramadan in the summer season and you are extremely thirsty. One feels very thirsty. Now, when the time to break the fast comes, at the moment you break your fast and you are dying of thirst, the water you drink—that which is neither too cold nor too hot, which is called 'Aab-e-Gawara', meaning pleasant water—the pleasure you get when you drink it is immense. In the same way, a person who recognizes Allah, as is His right to be recognized, gets the same pleasure from the 'Marifat' (gnosis) of Allah. They get the same pleasure from recognizing the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). They get the same pleasure from recognizing their Imam (a.s.). And that is why whoever recognized the Imam, whoever truly recognized him, did so to the extent that they were ready to give their life. That is why you see, during the era of Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi—may Allah's curse be upon him—you know he was a very wicked man. It was his era, his time, and he used to hunt for Shias to kill them. So, he asked his man, 'Is there any lover of Ali (a.s.) here at this time? I am in the mood to kill one today. Is there anyone?' He said, 'There is one who was a very staunch companion of Ali (a.s.) and a very old companion.' He asked, 'Who?' He said, 'Qambar.' He said, 'Bring him to me.' Now, Janab-e-Qambar had become very old and frail at that time. But look, if a person's faith is young, they never grow old. It is clear, right? That is why Maula (a.s.) used to say—let me recite this Hadith—'When a wise person grows old, their intellect becomes young.' The one who is wise, the one who has faith—because being wise means being a person of faith—when they grow old, their intellect becomes young. 'Wal jahilo iza shaba shabba jahlo'—and when an ignorant person grows old, their ignorance becomes young. So, he called Janab-e-Qambar. After calling him, when he was summoned, Janab-e-Qambar came, very old and frail, but his faith was solid. He asked, 'Is your name Abu Hamdan?' Abu Hamdan was the kunya (patronymic) of Janab-e-Qambar. So Janab-e-Qambar said, 'Na'am' (Yes). He asked, 'Are you the slave of Maula Ali ibn Abi Talib?' 'Maula' means slave. Look, in Arabic, 'Maula' has two meanings. 'Maula' also means master, and 'Maula' also means slave. Do you understand? That is why when you translate Hadith-e-Ghadir, translate it correctly. We usually translate it incorrectly. 'Allahumma wali man wala'—'whoever keeps Ali as a friend, keep him as a friend'—this is a wrong translation. If you translate it this way, then those people are right in saying that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was only announcing friendship. This translation is wrong. Its translation should be: 'Allahumma wali man wala'—'O Lord, take him as Your slave who takes Ali as his Master.' Subhan Allah. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. 'Whoever takes Ali as his Master, You take him as Your slave.' Allahumma wali man wala. This is it. Otherwise, if you say 'friend', then they will say, 'This is exactly what we were saying; we have been debating this for so long, and in the end, you give the same translation.' Therefore, translate very carefully. Anyway, what question did he ask? 'Are you the slave of Maula Ali ibn Abi Talib?' Janab-e-Qambar replied—look, one who lives at Ali's doorstep is educated. Subhan Allah. They are possessors of Marifat. Those who are at the doorstep of Ali and the progeny of Ali are not in a state of ignorance. They are not ignorant; they are educated, eloquent, and brave. They are not afraid of anyone. So, at such an old age, Janab-e-Qambar did not think, 'Let's see, I only have a few days left, let me live in peace, live comfortably.' No, what was his reply? Now listen, listen to the reply. The reply of a person of Marifat. He said, 'Allahu Maula-ya' (Allah is my Master). 'Wa Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib waliyu ni'mati' (And Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib is the guardian of my blessings). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. 'My God is Allah, but the blessings He gave me, He gave through Ali.' Look at the Marifat. 'He gave me blessings through Ali.' Now he flared up, because he used to get very angry, and especially when Hajjaj did all this, he used to do it under the influence of alcohol, very much so. He would get very angry at that. When he heard this reply—what was the habit of these people? You know, they were all big rulers; what was their habit? To hear 'Yes sir'. Now, if someone gives a retort like this, they were not used to hearing it. So he gave the order, saying, 'Tabarra min deen-e-Ali' (Dissociate from the religion of Ali). 'Dissociate from the religion of Ali, do Tabarra, show that you hate Ali.' So Qambar replied, 'I will.' Now listen to the reply, yes, 'I will, if you can bring a religion better than Ali's.' Subhan Allah. What can I say, Subhan Allah. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. A religion better than Ali's—look, a comparative study. It happened, didn't it? A complete comparative study in one sentence. 'Bring a religion better than Ali's.' The Quran says, 'Fabuhitallazi kafar' (The disbeliever was stunned). He was dumbfounded. He did not know what hit him. He said, 'Fine, then get ready to be killed.' He said, 'No problem.' Now, with that, look at the arrogance—arrogance was at its peak. 'In what way do you want to die?' He said, 'I have left that to you. Kill me in whatever way you want.' He asked, 'Why?' He said, 'My Master said, Ali said that your killer is Qambar; in the Raj'at (return), you will kill him in the same way he kills you.' Subhan Allah. It is clear, right? Look at the level of faith. He said, 'Fine, I will slaughter you the way sheep and goats are slaughtered.' Qambar said, 'No problem.' So it is written in the Hadith, 'Fazabahaha' (He slaughtered him), and just like one cuts into pieces, he cut Qambar into pieces. He was already intoxicated, anyway. So this is the level. This is what is called Marifat. But you see, until the last moment, Qambar remained steadfast on his religion. Until the last moment. And not even a little bit—in fact, he was enjoying that Allah gave him this opportunity to be martyred for the sake of Ali. You see, this is the level of faith. For instance, if someone threatens a person among us today, they say, 'No brother, whatever I said, I am doing Taqiyya.' Brother, there are five rulings of Taqiyya, five laws that apply to everything. I am not saying this; Sheikh Murtaza Ansari has written it in his book. Taqiyya is Wajib (obligatory), Taqiyya is Mustahab (recommended), Taqiyya is Makruh (disliked), Taqiyya is Haram (forbidden), Taqiyya is Mubah (permissible). If there is a fear of losing the religion, then Taqiyya is Haram. And if there is a danger of the destruction of the lineage, then Taqiyya is Haram. Taqiyya is Haram in such cases, otherwise, all our great scholars who were martyred—why were they all martyred? They were all martyred precisely because they knew that if we do Taqiyya today, generations will be ruined. The religion of generations will be lost. Shaheed-e-Awwal, Sheikh Muhammad Makki; Shaheed-e-Thani, Sheikh Zainuddin Amili; Shaheed-e-Salis, Qazi Nurullah Shustari; Shaheed-e-Rabi, Mirza Muhammad Kamil Kashmiri in Delhi. InshaAllah, I will tell you their story too. All these people gave their lives, and they gave their lives knowingly; it's not that they were killed by deception, no. So, therefore, you see, now the definition of Ma'ruf has become clear, so that when we discuss further, InshaAllah, we will continue accordingly. So now, the definition of Ma'ruf is that thing which the intellect accepts and in doing which a person finds pleasure. Therefore, now listen, a very important point is currently in service. In the Quran, in the Hadith, in the Fatawa, in the rulings of the scholars and jurists, have you ever seen 'Amr-bil-Ma'ruf' (Enjoining the good)? Have you heard 'Nahi-anil-Haram' (Forbidding the forbidden)? Have you heard it anywhere? What is written? 'Amr-bil-Ma'ruf, Nahi-anil-Munkar.' Meaning that... Enjoin that which the intellect accepts and in doing which one finds pleasure. And forbid that which is against the intellect and which one does not like to do. Meaning, what is against the intellect, yes? That is why when we preach the religion, this is a very important point. Look, why do people run away from religion? Why are they annoyed by religion? Look, do not look at their excessive prayers, do not look at their excessive fasting, do not look at their excessive Hajj, do not look at their excessive good deeds, and their recitation at night. Look, do not look at their excessive prayers, the Imam says. Do not look at excessive prayers, do not look at excessive fasting, do not look at excessive Hajj. We can give you examples for each one. An example for each. The best example of prayer and fasting was that of the Khawarij. It is written in history that the Khawarij used to prostrate so much that their foreheads became like a camel's knee; they used to pray so much, they used to fast so much. In this amulet, you will find the solution to your problem. As soon as Qasim opened the amulet, it was written inside: 'Bunayya Qasim, adrik ammakal Hussain.' (My son Qasim, go to the aid of your uncle Hussain). 'Son Qasim, help your uncle Hussain when he is all alone in Karbala, and if he does not grant you permission, keep insisting until your uncle gives you permission.' It is the night of Ashura. Qasim brought the amulet and showed his father's writing to Hussain. As soon as Hussain saw his brother's writing, he said, 'Son Qasim, this is not your father's writing; you have brought a message of your own death.' Qasim said, 'Uncle, what can I do? It is my father's command.' Hussain... Oh, my Qasim, you have been comforted; tomorrow everyone is to die. And Qasim, I did not just take your name; otherwise, your name was also in the list of martyrs, and not just yours, but your brother Ali Asghar's as well. So, while on one hand, Qasim was happy that his name was among the martyrs, on the other hand, the honorable child of Bani Hashim was restless and began to ask, 'Uncle, will the wicked ones enter the tents? ﴿هَلْ يَصِلُونَ إِلَى الْخِيَامِ﴾' Then I would say, 'Oh honorable child of Bani Hashim, you could not hear that they will enter the tents.' Now imagine, Imam Zainul Abideen, Sayyid-e-Sajjad, is watching the evening of Ashura; the tents are on fire, and the wicked are entering the tents, and Sayyid-e-Sajjad is watching the whole scene—veils are being snatched from the heads of the ladies, and whips are being used. The day of Ashura arrived, the series of martyrdoms began, until the moment came when the martyrdoms of the Bani Hashim began. Once, when the martyrdom of the children of Hasan began, Qasim came again and stood before Hussain, 'Uncle, please grant me permission.' Uncle, grant me permission. Now listen to the sentence from the Maqtal (chronicle of martyrdom). It is written in the Maqtal that Hussain is standing silently; Hussain is unable to grant permission, he is standing silently. So, Qasim took both of Hussain's hands and began to rub his eyes, 'Uncle, grant me permission, uncle, grant me permission,' until Hussain said, 'Go Qasim, I grant you permission.' Now that he had granted permission, Hussain prepared Qasim, adorned him. Before putting him on the horse, he embraced Qasim once. Both uncle and nephew wept so much, so much that they fainted. Mourners, when someone faints, water is sprinkled to bring them back to consciousness. But alas, the helplessness of Zainab! It was the noon of Ashura, and there was no arrangement for water. They sprinkled tears. When, somehow, the uncle and nephew regained consciousness, he said, 'Brother, do not stop Qasim now, grant him permission.' Hussain mounted Qasim. As he was leaving, he tore his collar once. He said, 'Uncle, what is this?' He said, 'This is the sign of orphans.' 'Qasim, go now.' You went, and he remembered his brother, that is why he tore the collar. And it is possible that Hussain tore it so that the enemy, seeing an orphan, might perhaps show mercy. But what happened was that when Qasim, after fighting, sent many of the wicked to Hell, a wicked man struck such a blow that Qasim began to stagger. Now, when he fell from the horse, his foot got stuck in the horse's saddle. Now that it was stuck, Qasim fell in such a way that half his body was on this side and half on that side. The horse took Qasim and ran among the wicked. The wicked began to tear Qasim's body into pieces. By the time Hussain reached, Qasim's body had been torn into pieces. It is written in the Maqtal that when Hussain reached, he spread his cloak. He gathered the pieces of Qasim's body in such a way that it became like a bundle, and bringing that bundle, he placed it in the tent. Then there was mourning: 'Wa Qasima, Wa Hussaina, Wa Mazluma.' ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنقَلَبٍ يَنقَلِبُونَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, fulfill their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and pious children. Those who are far from their homes, return them to their homes safe and sound. Grant complete and immediate healing to all the sick. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the holy shrines and sacred places. Whoever protects them, You protect them. Especially protect the shrine of Janabe Zainab. O Lord, grant us the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the hereafter. By reciting one Surah Fatiha and three times Surah Tawheed, grant peace to the souls of all the deceased, men and women, of the families of Ghulam Ali Ibn Abdul Aziz Lakhani, the late Zarina Binte Shivji Rupani, the late Shahnaz Binte Amir Ali Rupani, the late Khadija Binte Natha Lakhani, the Lakhani family, Rupani family, Himani family, Lada family, and the Narsi family.

title: Ghadeer Mein Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ka Tazkera
excerpt: This lecture highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) declaration at Ghadeer regarding the succession of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the subsequent Imams. It emphasizes that the line of leadership, culminating in Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), was divinely ordained. The speaker underscores the significance of the Imam's future role in establishing absolute truth and justice upon his reappearance.
content:
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Know that the lawful and the unlawful are more than I can count here in one place, telling you how many are lawful and how many are unlawful. Therefore, I have been commanded to take an oath of allegiance from you all. Accept what I have brought from Allah (Azzawajal) regarding Ali, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), that he is the Commander of the Faithful, and the Imams after him who are from me and from him. Among them will be the Mahdi. This chain will continue until the Day of Judgment. He who will judge with truth.' That is, the decision that Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) will make will be the truth. May Allah grant us that day, Insha'Allah, and hasten the reappearance of the Imam.

Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is the final link in this chain of leadership.

title: New Video Series  |  Marefat-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) – Sawaalon Ke Jawaabaat
excerpt: This lecture introduces a new video series titled 'Ma'rifat-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.): Answers to Questions,' which aims to address common queries regarding the 12th Imam. The speaker cites Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' to highlight the universal Muslim belief in the arrival of Imam Mahdi and the establishment of global justice. The series intends to provide logical, Quranic, and Hadith-based responses to doubts about the Imam's birth, longevity, and occultation. Additionally, the program includes an interactive component with a quiz and a lucky draw for participants.
content:
Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim. Ibn Khaldun, the famous scholar, in the 53rd chapter of the first part of his book 'Muqaddimah', has described the government of the progeny of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (a.s.) in this manner: 'It is well-known among all Muslims in every era that in the end of times, a man will surely appear from the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) who will be the helper of the religion, Allah will spread justice through him, Muslims will follow him, and he will gain control over all Islamic lands. He will be called al-Mahdi, and his name will be Mahdi.' On this very page, Ibn Khaldun has written that the traditions regarding Imam Mahdi (a.s.) are authentic, and the prominent scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah, such as Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Bazzar, Ibn Majah, Hakim, Tabarani, and Abu Ya'la, have narrated traditions on the authority of companions like Anas bin Malik, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, and... ...Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, Anas bin Malik, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Umm Salama (a.s.), and others. The question arises that when all Muslims, regardless of which sect they belong to, believe in the arrival of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) in the end of times, his government, and the spread of justice throughout the world at his hands, then where do the differences lie, and what is the reason for these differences? These differences began when people made failed attempts to diminish the infallibility and greatness of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and in this regard, they went to such an extent that they forgot they were actually denying the authority and power of Allah. That is why such questions were raised in the past and are still being raised today: 'Has Imam Mahdi (a.s.) not been born yet?', 'How can a human being have such a long life?', 'Why has the Imam hidden himself from the community?' Today, to answer these very questions, the team of 'The Strongroom' is presenting its new series before you, titled 'Ma'rifat-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.): Answers to Questions', in which we will try to provide brief, authentic, and logical answers to these and many other questions in the light of the Quran and Hadith, Inshallah. ...answers, in which we will try to provide brief, authentic, and logical answers to these and many other questions in the light of the Quran and Hadith, Inshallah. And one more thing, in every episode of this entire series, a question based on that episode will be asked, the link to which will be in the comment section of that video. You have to watch the video and give the correct answer to the question related to that video. From those who give the correct answer to the question of each episode in this series, two winners will be selected through a lucky draw. This draw will take place in our event, which will be announced after the 15th of Sha'ban, Inshallah. Stay connected with us for its details, and do not forget to watch our new series 'Ma'rifat-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.): Answers to Questions'. And our final prayer is: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

title: Majlis 5 |  Zohd | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | #Muharram 2026 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this fifth session of the Khamsa-e-Majaalis, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual concept of Zuhd (asceticism) and its practical application in the life of a believer. The lecture emphasizes the necessity of prioritizing the Hereafter over worldly attachments, the importance of following religious authority, and the spiritual lessons derived from the Ahlul-Bayt. The discourse culminates in a poignant reflection on the tragedy of Karbala, highlighting the ultimate sacrifice of Imam Hussain and the endurance of Janabe Zainab.
content:
Imam-e-Zamana, he is the guardian of our affairs, our master, our leader, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate, the strong shelter, the relief for the distressed and the upright. May my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. After praising Allah, our master and our leader, Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.), said: 'Know that 'Ma'ruf' (goodness) is something that earns you praise and brings a reward. If you were to see 'Ma'ruf' as a person, you would see him as beautiful and handsome, pleasing to the onlookers and excelling over all the worlds.' Truth spoke our master Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. In this hadith of the Master of Martyrs, which I have chosen for this discussion, for this series of five Majlis, the Master of Martyrs says: 'Know that Ma'ruf, meaning goodness—which we have already explained—is something through which you will earn praise. People will praise you if Ma'ruf becomes your habit, if Ma'ruf becomes your profession, then people will praise you and Allah will also give its reward. If you see Ma'ruf—and God willing, people will see it on the Day of Judgment, as I submitted to you in the first Majlis—on the Day of Judgment, people will see Ma'ruf in the form of a human. You will see that he is extremely beautiful, 'Hassanun Jamila.' 'Hassanun Jamila' means there will be no flaw in him, not even an atom's worth; he will be very beautiful, so beautiful that those who see him will be delighted, they will feel joy upon seeing Ma'ruf, and he will encompass the entire universe, meaning he will excel over everything. So, Ma'ruf—I just submitted to you—what is Ma'ruf? 'Fal-Ma'rufo' is a sentence from Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin: 'Ma amartum bihi wal-munkaro ma nahaytum an.' Ma'ruf is what you have commanded, and Munkar is what you forbid.' In another hadith, when the Imam asked in a debate with Abu Hanifa what Ma'ruf is, he started counting various good deeds. The Imam said, 'No, the first instance of Ma'ruf is the Wilayat of Amir-ul-Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib.' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. And similarly, who is Munkar? The Imam asked, 'Who is Munkar?' So he said, 'Now you tell me, since you said this.' So the Imam said that Munkar are those people who usurped the right of Amir-ul-Momineen. So, Amr-bil-Ma'ruf and Nahy-anil-Munkar are explained by this. In any case, to convey the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt to people as much as possible is Ma'ruf, and this is everyone's responsibility, so much so that the Imams have prayed for those who revive the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt. 'Rahimal-lahu abdan ahya amrana.' May Allah shower mercy on the servant who revives our affair. In one hadith, it says, 'Rahimal-lahu abdan ahayana.' Meaning, whoever revives us. So the narrator asked, 'Kaifa yuhya amrukum?' How is your affair revived? The Imam said, 'Yata'allamu ulumana wa yu'allimuhun-nas.' They should learn our sciences, our hadiths. It is necessary for everyone to learn and then convey them to people. As much as one's capacity is—if someone has the capacity for five hadiths, they should learn five; whoever learns ten, should learn ten; whoever learns fifty, should learn fifty; whoever learns a hundred, should learn a hundred. But the focus should always be on the hadith; this is a very important topic. Anyway, our topic was that Hazrat Jibraeel (a.s.) came to the Prophet and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah Almighty has sent me to you with a gift, and this gift is such that Allah has neither given it to anyone before you nor will He give it to anyone after you.' The Prophet asked, 'What is it?' He said, 'Patience (Sabr) is the first thing.' And what is better than that? He said, 'Contentment (Rida) is better than that.' And what is better than that? He said, 'Asceticism (Zuhd) is better than that.' And what is better than that? He said, 'Sincerity (Ikhlas) is better than that.' And what is better than that? He said, 'Certainty (Yaqeen) is better than that.' And what is better than that? The Prophet asked, 'Jibraeel, what could be better than this?' He said, 'The peak, the height of all these things, in which everything is gathered, is called Tawakkul (Trust in Allah).' So we covered Tawakkul in the first Majlis, and after that, we covered two topics, meaning Sabr and Qaza (being content with Allah's decree). But there was a question in it, as asked today, that brother, I mentioned two points yesterday—what does being content mean? One is what Allah does with us, and two is what we do ourselves, meaning the commands Allah has given us—'pray, fast, don't do this, don't do that'—those two things. And remember, one should have patience on both of these things. Like the last verse of Surah Ale-Imran in the Quran: 'Ya ayyuhal-lazina amanus-biru wa sabiru wa rabitu wattaqullaha la'allakum tuflihun.' O believers, have patience, and encourage one another to have patience, and 'Rabitu.' And look, 'Rabitu'—usually people translate it as 'keep a connection' (rabt). No, that is not the translation. Do you know the beauty of Arabic grammar? That every scale of grammar carries a different meaning. Like 'Nasara' means to help, but 'Intasara' means to win. The word changes, its meaning changes. Similarly, this 'Rabitu,' so the Imam said, 'Rabitu Imamakum.' Be 'Murabit' for your Imam. Now, if you go and look in an Arabic dictionary, you will see that 'Murabita' does not mean 'keep a connection,' but rather 'Murabit'—even in the Quran it appears, 'Ribatal-khail'—meaning defend your Imam. Defend your Imam, and how can you defend him in today's age? The best way is through these teachings, because nowadays it is cultural defense. What is the most important thing? Cultural defense. Anyway, whatever happens in the world, whether Allah does it to us or we did it ourselves—anyhow, if Allah has done something, first of all, the Quran says that whatever calamity befalls you, whatever trouble comes, it is the result of your own actions. Indeed. 'Zaharal-fasadu fil-barre wal-bahre.' It is a verse of the Quran, right? I didn't make it up just now, did I? It is a verse of the Quran: 'Zaharal-fasadu fil-barre wal-bahre bima kasabat aidin-nas.' Come forward, son, come here a little. Make space, recite one more Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. It is found in ethics that whenever someone comes to any gathering—this is ethics, meaning a tradition, a hadith—that when someone comes to a gathering, the other believers sitting there should make space for them. This is a verse of the Quran regarding ethics, a verse of Surah Mujadila: 'Ya ayyuhal-lazina amanu,' the Quran says, 'Ya ayyuhal-lazina amanu iza qila lakum tafassahu fil-majalis-i fafsahu yafsahillahu lakum.' O believers, when you are told to make space, then make space; Allah will make space for you. This is a verse of Surah Mujadila. Allah will make space for you; you make space for others. And if we do not move, if we do not make space for others, then Allah will not make space for us either. Recite one Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. So there are two things, see, for example, if someone gets sick, now look, in sickness, a person is not responsible for it, so what should they do? If someone gets high blood pressure, someone gets diabetes, someone has a heart attack, anything can happen, anything can happen to a human being, look. Always, because what is a human? A human is between the two fingers of Allah. I submitted to your service yesterday, right? Allah keeps reminding him, telling him that you are a servant, I am the Creator. Never consider yourself the Creator. Please understand. Do not consider yourself God. And I had just submitted to your service before this as well that Pharaoh was also like this. He used to say, 'Ana Rabbukumul A'la' (I am your Lord, the Most High). I am your God, and the greatest God. But he used to say this during the day. At night, he would tie himself up and say, 'O Lord, You know that my claim is false. So, please, just preserve my honor.' And once, he was bathing, and Satan entered inside. Pharaoh was in the hammam (bathhouse). So Satan hit him hard, slapped him hard. So he said, 'Who is it that slapped me?' We are narrating a tradition, brother, not telling a story. He said, Pharaoh asked, 'Who are you?' So Satan replied, 'How ignorant and how helpless—helpless meaning powerless—you are, that you claim to be God while being both. Ignorant, that you don't know who I am, that you are asking who I am? And helpless, that I am coming in and you cannot stop me.' So before Allah, Allah always wants to show the human—they say 'taskhir', Allah keeps everything under His control. Let us finish the topic by speaking, as I submitted to your service that the Imam used 22 arguments before Ibn Abi al-Awja, who was an atheist. He gave 22 arguments on how you remain under Allah's control. So, one thing Allah has done is that one must have patience (Sabr) over it. One must remain content with Allah's decree (Qada). Alhamdulillah for whatever Allah has done. If He made you sick, as I submitted to your service. If He gave a son, then be grateful; if He didn't, then be grateful. So that is why I tell the youth to keep a time for supplications in your daily schedule. Read it a little. Just presenting the Hadith of the Master of the Universe (a.s.) for your service. Just finishing the topic quickly because time is short. The Master (a.s.) says that people are of three types regarding the world. Regarding the world, yes. With regards to the world, people are of three types. Which three types? Zahidun, Raghibun, Sabirun. Who is a Zahid? 'Fa-amma az-zahid.' Who is the Zahid? The one who is the interpretation of the Quran. 'La yafrahu bi-shay'in minad-dunya.' If he gets something of the world, if Allah gives it to him, he does not become arrogant. 'I have so much wealth, I have so much treasure, I have this, I have so much property, I have this.' It doesn't go straight to his head. You know, right? A little money comes and they start shaking a bit, isn't it? The Quran is there, the Quran says in Surah Bani Israil. In Surah Bani Israil, what does Allah say? 'La tamshi fil-ardi maraha' (Do not walk on the earth exultantly). Because by walking like this, neither will the earth split, nor will you reach the height of the mountains. This is a verse of the Quran. A verse of Surah Bani Israil. What is the arrogance for? 'Don't you recognize me?' Yes, he doesn't recognize you, but the angels will make him recognize you. They will make him recognize you on the very first night. It is clear, right? It often happens, right? This phrase is 'la minad-dunya wa la yahzanu 'ala shay'in minha fat' (not of the world, and he does not grieve over anything of it that is missed). And if there is any loss, he does not feel sorrow or grief. Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah. And there are examples before you, examples. See, we don't have time now, otherwise, I would give you one or two examples recently. Then the Master (a.s.) says, and who is the Sabir? Look at the phrase of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). He calls the Sabir, the Master defined the Zahid first. Now he says the Sabir is the one who has the desire for the world in his heart. He has the desire for the world in his heart, that he should get the world. But when the world comes before him, he turns his face away because he knows that its end is bad. This is forbidden, I will not accept this. He turns his face away. 'This is not permissible, I will not accept this.' Even if it looks very attractive, but no, not this. And who is the third? Raghib. The Master (a.s.) says this is the one who 'fala yubali' (he does not care). 'Min ayyi asbaha aw min haramiha' (Whether it comes from a lawful source or a forbidden one). Whether it comes through forbidden means or lawful means, no problem. Whatever wealth comes, let it come, I will repent later. I mean, he is so careless. Like that companion of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), right? What was he doing? He used to steal. He used to steal and from that, he would take an amount and give it in the way of Allah. So the Imam (a.s.) got the news. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Brother, what are you doing? This is forbidden.' He said, 'The Quran says that if you do one good deed, you get 10 rewards, and if you do one sin, you get one sin, one punishment. So I am doing one sin, so I will get one punishment. Here I got 10 rewards. So 10 - 1 = 9. So I am in profit, right?' You don't think that such clever people are only today, yes? In the time of the Imams (a.s.) too, there were such people. What did the Imam (a.s.) say in reply? 'This 10 is for when you give from your own wealth. Not from stolen wealth. Not from such forbidden wealth. Allah does not accept forbidden wealth at all. Allah does not accept it.' So if a person, see, it is a very strange incident of a man. He came to the service of the Imam (a.s.), the sixth Imam (a.s.), and started saying, 'I love you.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'If you love me, first tell me what you do for a living?' He said, 'I am a courtier, a courtier.' 'What do you do as a courtier?' He said, 'I take money from people for the king, I do this, I do that, whatever, all things, forbidden ones.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Do you know that this is your forbidden earning?' He said, 'Yes.' 'And all the property you have made so far is all forbidden?' He said, 'Yes, all of it is forbidden. Total, it all came like this.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'You cannot be our Shia until you distance yourself from all that wealth. Give up everything.' See, today is the last Majlis, I am taking a little more time. Please forgive me. Just recite a Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Just this, very quickly, let me present it to you. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'If you love us, then relinquish everything. Leave everything.' He said, 'Okay. If you say so, then okay.' 'And if you do this, then I promise you that you will not leave this world until you see Paradise with your own eyes.' When he reached back immediately, he was a resident of Kufa. Immediately, the first thing he did was resign. He resigned from his job, whatever job he had. He said, 'I do not want to do this.' After that, he started selling all the wealth he possessed, until he was left with nothing. Not even the clothes on his body, because even those were bought with unlawful (haram) money. So, he said, 'Even this is not mine, what should I do now?' People gave him a garment to cover himself. Now he had nothing left. Nothing to eat, not even a morsel. Eventually, he became bedridden. His condition became extremely critical. He was in the throes of death (sakratul maut). In this state, one of the Imam's companions came to visit him. When he came to visit, do you know what he said? He said, 'Tell my Master that I have acted upon what you commanded, and you have fulfilled your promise.' Believe me, if the Imams make a promise, they will never leave you alone. We mentioned this in yesterday's gathering as well. Therefore, in life, whenever you face situations, options will keep appearing. This is the last hadith I will share with you; I will not read further because there is no time. Options will always appear, and I am not saying this; the Imam has stated it. Listen carefully. The Imam says that two options will come before you: one is the world, and the other is the Hereafter. If these two ever clash, always prefer the Hereafter, not the world. For example, if you have some important work of the Imam to do, and there is a worldly meeting that is optional for you—yes, if it is not optional for someone, that is a different matter—but if it is optional, then prefer the Imam's service, not the world. Remember this; God willing, we will discuss this another time. The second option: honor with haram or humiliation with halal. These two options will come. Many people who take bribes justify it, don't they? You see it in government departments. 'No, this is goodwill.' Goodwill? What kind of goodwill? Ask the heart of the one giving it, how much 'will' is there. Did you notice? Bribery is haram, but in any case, it is absolutely not permissible in Islam. Honor and humiliation—if it is humiliation, then accept it, as long as it is halal. Leave the honor that comes with haram. Then the Imam says: halal, meaning struggle and hard work in the service of the Imam, choose that. Endure hardship. Leave ease. For instance, if a believer comes to you and says, 'Please do this work for me,' you will have to work hard for it. Do you know how much reward there is in this? It is greater than performing I'tikaf in the Holy Kaaba during the month of Ramadan. Fulfilling a believer's need, or if you cannot fulfill it, at least trying to go with them and saying, 'Let's try.' The definition of a believer is that they put themselves in hardship so that others may remain in comfort. This is the definition of a believer. They put themselves in trouble. And next, the Imam says, they will remain hungry. If it is halal and one has to stay hungry, and the alternative is to fill the stomach with haram, they will not fill their stomach with haram. They will not fill it with haram. They will walk hungry. They know this thing is impure (najis), so they will not eat it. It's okay. We will stay hungry. No problem, no issue, but it is impure, so we will not eat it. This happens many times. You go, and you know about 'dhabihah' (slaughtered meat), people do this, 'Oh, such and such airline is allowed.' No, no, it is not allowed, brother. Dhabihah, meaning non-veg food, is not allowed unless you are certain that it has been slaughtered in a halal manner. And the 'halal' sticker they put on it does not make it halal, brother. Because if you go to many Muslim countries, it is written 'Lahmul Khanzir Halal' (Pork is Halal). For them, they slaughtered the pig in a halal way, so that doesn't count. We will stay hungry, that is fine. And let me tell you one thing: see what happens? No one dies. You fast for 12-14 hours in the month of Ramadan, does anyone die? Have you ever heard of anyone dying? People fast through great difficulties, no one dies. But what does Satan say? 'Oh, it's a 6-hour journey from here to Iraq, what will happen if you don't eat?' Nothing will happen. Nothing will happen, believe me. And if you are in so much trouble, then cook something from home and take it with you. But eating there and saying, 'No, this is halal'—no, it is not halal, brother. It is not religiously permissible. Pick up and read the 'Tawdih al-Masa'il'. Any Marja's Tawdih—Khoei's, Agha Sistani's, anyone's—read it. For dhabihah, it is necessary to be certain that it is halal. Next, the Imam says, and what does he do? His focus is always on the Hereafter. He removes the love of the world from his heart. He is always in remembrance of Allah. He is not heedless of Allah. And the last sentence the Mawla says is: 'His body is in the world, but his heart is in the Hereafter.' Now, you just go home and read Nahj al-Balagha, Sermon number 193, 'Sifat al-Muttaqin' (Attributes of the Pious). Just one sentence from the Master of the Universe. Listen to what it is. He says: 'Were it not for the fixed time of death that Allah has written for everyone, their souls would not remain in their bodies for even the blink of an eye.' These pious ones are such that their souls would not stay in their bodies for even a second if there were no fear of God. Why? Meaning, if Allah had not written the time of death. Why? The Mawla says, 'out of longing for the reward.' Why would their souls not stay in their bodies? They have such a longing for the reward and fear of the punishment—the fear of Hell. 'The Creator is so great in their souls that everything else appears small in their eyes.' Allah is so great in their sight that all other things become small in their eyes. Now, we, generally—because I am talking about ourselves, not you—are so drowned in the world that we don't understand these things. We think they are just saying this. But the Ahlulbayt used to give such training to their children that they would experience this while living. The tragedies of Karbala that you hear about are not just like that. When Janab-e-Ali Akbar said, 'Idhan la nubali bil mawt' (Then we do not care about death). Imam Hussain (a.s.) recited the verse of Istirja: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' Janab-e-Ali Akbar asked, 'Father, what is the reason for reciting this verse of Istirja?' The Imam said, 'I just saw in a dream that someone is announcing that this caravan is moving, and death is walking ahead of them.' Janab-e-Ali Akbar asked, see, what is the training? Look at the incredible upbringing. He asked, 'Alastu 'ala al-haqq?' (Are we not on the truth?) Obviously, Ali Akbar knew, but he was giving a lesson for us. This lesson was for us. 'Alastu 'ala al-haqq?' So he said, 'Certainly.' 'Ajal' (Yes). The Imam said, 'Ajal.' So he said, 'Idhan la nubali bil mawt.' Then what do we care about death? Whether death comes upon us or we go upon death. What do we care? This was Janab-e-Ali Akbar. Now, Janab-e-Qasim was only 13 years old. But Imam Hussain (a.s.) asks, when he insists so much on the night of Ashura, he just asks, 'Kayfal mawt indakum ya bunayya?' (How is death to you, my son?) He said, 'Ahla minal asal' (Sweeter than honey). Qasim had already tasted it, that's why he was saying it. Now think, if the children of a house are like this, then the one who trained them, Hussain ibn Ali, how must he be? 'Tarak-tul khalqa kullahan fi tarak.' The poet says in Arabic, Imam Hussain said—this is a poem—that Imam Hussain said, 'O Lord, I have left everything, only for the sake of Your love.' 'Wa aytam-tul al-ayala likay ara.' I have orphaned my children so that I may meet You. Hussain, when he saw that no one was left, even Hazrat Ali Asghar was martyred. So he comes to the door of the tent and says for the final farewell, 'Ya Zaynab, ya Umm Kulthum, ya Sakina, ya Fizza, alaykunna minni as-salam.' O Zaynab, O Umm Kulthum, O Sakina, O Fizza, my final peace be upon you all. As soon as he said this, Janab-e-Zaynab was devastated. She came and started saying, 'Ya akhi, O my brother, a-istaslamta lil mawt?' Have you become ready for death? The Imam said, 'How can he not be ready for death, who has no helper and no supporter left?' Zaynab said, 'Brother, do not say that, Zaynab is still alive.' He said, 'Sister, then take me to Sayyid-e-Sajjad.' Janab-e-Zaynab held Imam Hussain's arm and brought him. Janab-e-Zaynab said, 'Son Sayyid-e-Sajjad, wake up, see, Father has come.' Janab Imam Zayn al-Abidin opened his eyes. Can you hear the sentence from the Maqtal? The Imam could not recognize him. Where is Father? Hussain was so wounded, from morning until the afternoon of Ashura, lifting bodies, Hussain had become so wounded. Sayyid-e-Sajjad asked, 'Aunt, where is Father?' Hussain hugged him, 'Son, how will you recognize me when all the blood from my body has drained, covered in wounds?' 'Oh Father, is this your condition? Aunt, bring my sword, I will defend my Father.' The Imam said, 'No son, Karbala is not your battlefield; your battlefield is the markets of Kufa and Sham. Son Sayyid-e-Sajjad, you have to endure great tragedies, be patient, son, be patient. And when you are released from captivity, go to Medina and convey our greetings to our Shias and say: O my followers, when you drink cold water, remember my thirst, remember my thirst, and when you see someone helpless, remember the helplessness of Hussain.' Hussain departed, came, and once looked towards the battlefield. He saw the bodies of his loved ones, bodies drenched in blood. Hussain called out, Hussain called out, 'Ya aftal as-safa, wa ya fursan al-hayja.' O my lions, O my brave ones, O my knights, 'Ma lakum unadikum fala tujibuni.' What has happened to you? Your Imam is calling you, and you are not answering? 'Ayyukum yuqaddimu jawadi?' Which of you will now help me mount my horse? On the 28th of Rajab, Hussain had said, 'Abbas, qaddim jawadi.' Bring my mount. Janab-e-Abbas had helped Hussain mount on the 28th of Rajab. It is no wonder that an answer came immediately, 'Master, death has forced us.' Hussain's address had not even finished when suddenly the 'Sani-e-Zahra' (Zaynab) came out of the tent, 'Brother, do not worry, Zaynab is still alive, Zaynab will help you mount.' On the afternoon of Ashura, Zaynab helped Hussain mount. I will ask with folded hands, O Sani-e-Zahra (Zainab), you have helped him mount, but when the time comes to descend or fall from the horse, it would not be strange if Zainab replies, 'Oh, my mother has arrived in the plains of Karbala.' Hussain came to the battlefield to complete the argument (Hujjat). Hussain launched three attacks. When Hussain launched the first attack, the armies were pushed back to the walls of Qadisiyah. When Hussain launched the second attack, he moved towards the Euphrates, and the attack was so swift that the armies began to scatter here and there. Hussain reached the banks of the Euphrates. It would not be strange if his heart called out, 'Abbas, rise, wake up and see, brother.' Now Hussain came, and as soon as he launched the third attack, while in the midst of it, Hussain paused for a moment to rest, to stop for a second, when the heavenly call came: 'Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul mutma'inna, irji'i ila rabbiki radiyatan mardiyya, fadkhuli fi 'ibadi wadkhuli jannati.' O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, and enter among My servants and enter My Paradise. Come, enter among My servants, come, enter My Paradise. As soon as Hussain heard this call—now listen to the words of Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.), who says that as soon as the divine call came, Hussain (my father) put the sword back into the scabbard. As soon as my father did this, someone threw a stone, someone a spear, someone pierced him with a spear, and a rain of arrows began from there. Hussain was no longer able to steady himself on the horse. When Hussain began to fall from the horse, what happened then? I will not recite much more, just listen to what the Imam of the Age says in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah. The Imam says, 'Wa Shimrun jalisun 'ala sadri' (And Shimr was sitting on my chest). He was sitting on your chest, wanting to quench the thirst of his dagger with your blood. He took your noble beard in his hands and began to run the dagger. When Janabe Zainab saw that Zuljanah had returned without a rider, she went in search of Imam Hussain. It is written in the Maqtal that a voice was echoing in the atmosphere of Karbala, 'Ya Hussain.' Zainab could not see Hussain anywhere. Janabe Zainab came to the place known as Tila-e-Zainabia. She stood there, and when she arrived, what a scene she witnessed: Shimr was sitting on his chest. When Zainab could do nothing, Then she said, 'O son of Sa'd, you are watching while my brother is being slaughtered?' As soon as Zainab's voice reached Hussain's ears, Hussain signaled, 'Sister Zainab, go back to the tent.' It was the Imam's command. Janabe Zainab returned to the tent. As soon as she stepped inside, the sky turned dark, an eclipse occurred, the water of the Euphrates began to surge, and a voice echoed in the atmosphere of Karbala: 'Ala qutilal Hussain, ala dhubiha al-Hussain' (Behold, Hussain is killed; behold, Hussain is slaughtered). Zainab asked, 'Son, Sayyid-e-Sajjad, what am I hearing?' He said, 'Aunt, please lift the curtain of the tent.' Now, when she lifted the curtain, what did she see? On the nine-nine spears, the father's head is raised high. Assalamu alaika ya Aba Abdillah, Father, you have been martyred. Wa sa'ya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Ala la'natullahi 'ala qawmin zalimin. O Lord, O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Age (a.s.) and count us among his helpers. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are troubled, pay off the debts of those who are in debt, grant righteous and virtuous children to those who are childless, grant complete and swift healing to those who are ill, grant righteous and virtuous children to those who are childless, return those who are far from their homeland safely and soundly. Protect the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. O Lord, O Lord, protect the scholars of the world and the Maraje-e-Izam. Protect the sacred sanctities. Protect those who are protecting them.
