title: Majlis #3: Bulandi -e- Darajaat | Ahle Bait (a.s.): Daawate Husnaa | Muharram 1443
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual elevation of the believer through the teachings and examples of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.). It emphasizes the importance of the Hadith al-Kisa, the practice of Islamic etiquette, and the transformative power of Azadari and Namaz-e-Shab. The discourse concludes with the profound sacrifices made at Karbala, highlighting the unwavering devotion of figures like Wahab and the emotional legacy of the tragedy.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. [Recitation of a tradition/supplication]: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... and he called upon... and he said to Abbas... and he said... and then... and indeed... the Prophet of Allah... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Indeed, I feel weakness in my body.' I said to him: 'I seek refuge in Allah, O father, from weakness.' He said: 'O Fatima, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it.' So I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it. Then my son Al-Hasan (a.s.) approached and said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O delight of my eye and fruit of my heart.' He said: 'O mother, indeed I smell a beautiful fragrance near you, as if it is the fragrance of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, indeed your grandfather is under the cloak.' So Hasan approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah! Do you permit me to enter with you under the cloak?' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my son and the companion of my pool, I have permitted you.' So he entered with him under the cloak. Then my son Al-Hussain (a.s.) approached... ...and said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my son, O delight of my eye and fruit of my heart.' He said: 'O mother, indeed I smell a beautiful fragrance near you, as if it is the fragrance of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, indeed your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak.' So Hussain approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah! Do you permit me to enter with you under the cloak?' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my son and the intercessor of my nation, I have permitted you.' So he entered with them under the cloak. Then Abul Hasan, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) approached and said: 'Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O Abul Hasan and O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'O Fatima, indeed I smell a beautiful fragrance near you, as if it is the fragrance of my brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah.' I said: 'Yes, there he is with your two sons under the cloak.' So Ali approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, do you permit me to be with you under the cloak?'... ...He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my brother, O my successor, O my vicegerent, and my standard-bearer, I have permitted you.' So Ali entered with them under the cloak. Then I approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O my father, O Messenger of Allah! Do you permit me to be with you under the cloak?' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my daughter and my flesh, I have permitted you.' So I entered with them under the cloak. When we were all gathered under the cloak, my father, the Messenger of Allah, took the two ends of the cloak and pointed with his right hand to the heavens and said: 'O Allah, these are the people of my household, my confidants, and my supporters. Then Allah, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: 'O My angels and O inhabitants of My heavens, indeed I have not created a constructed heaven, nor a stretched earth, nor a shining moon, nor a radiating sun, nor a rotating planet, nor a flowing ocean, nor a sailing ship, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak.' The trustworthy Gabriel asked: 'O Lord, and who is under the cloak?' The Almighty replied: 'They are the household of the Prophethood and the source of the Message; they are Fatima, her father, her husband, and her sons.' Gabriel said: 'O Lord, do you permit me to descend to the earth to be the sixth among them?' Allah said: 'Yes, I have permitted you.' Allah Tabaraka wa Ta'ala says in His firm Book: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice...' The Almighty is saying: 'Invite to the path of your Lord with wisdom'—meaning wise words and logical discourse—'and with good advice'—meaning the best exhortation and counseling. So friends, the point was that among the preachers of religion, when we study about the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), one of the titles of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) is 'Da'wat-e-Husna' (the beautiful invitation)—meaning the best invitation. The way they invite towards the religion of Allah, no one can invite to Allah's religion in a better or more beautiful way than them. And the reason for this, the secret behind it, is that all the speech of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) is in accordance with human nature (fitrah). Yesterday, I also submitted that even if we present a point without explicitly stating it as a Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), if that point is stated, it will be completely in line with human nature, absolutely in accordance with their nature. The only condition is that their nature should not be covered by sins. If it is covered by sins, and their nature is veiled by faults, then that is a different matter—where a person pretends to be ignorant despite knowing the truth, which is a wrong thing. But if a person, with absolute justice and fairness, has a discussion presented before them, and they are asked whether this... ...is presented to people and they are asked whether this is in accordance with their intellect or not, they will immediately say, 'Absolutely, you are speaking completely rationally.' However, there are levels in this as well, as was presented yesterday, that as a human being becomes closer to Islam, their intellect and their intellectual decisions become refined, and they begin to see things that an ordinary person does not see. That is why we find the narration: 'Beware of the discernment of the believer, for he sees with the light of Allah.' And there is another very powerful narration: 'Beware of the conjectures of the believers,' because Allah loves the believer so much that whatever conjecture they make, Allah makes reality conform to their conjecture. This is how much Allah loves a believer. Anyway, let us move forward today to another topic. That topic is about what things make a person... there is a mention of four things in a Hadith, and this Hadith is from our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) [or Imam (a.s.)], where he says... Our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that there are a total of 12 things mentioned in this. Let us know these 12 things, which are easy and not difficult. If you try, and if Allah grants the opportunity (tawfeeq), I will mention these points very quickly. The rest you all understand, there is no need to go into details. So there are 12 things. He says that three things raise a person's ranks (darajaat), three things are the expiation (kaffarah) for a person's sins, three things ruin and destroy a person, and three things—which are the last ones—become the cause of salvation (najaat) for a person. Yes, so in total, there are 12 things. In a hadith, the Imam (a.s.) has mentioned these 12 things. Inshallah, instead of going into deep details, we will briefly touch upon them. What are the three things that increase a person's ranks, which elevate a person's status? First is 'Ifsha-us-Salam', meaning greeting with Salam, always greeting, spreading Salam, making Salam common. Second is 'It'am-ut-Ta'am', feeding food to others. Third is 'Namaz bil-layl wan-nasu niyam', praying at night while people are asleep. And the things that are expiations (kaffarah), what are they? One is performing Wudu perfectly even in difficult conditions. And second is walking on foot to the mosque or center for prayers—what we call the center... ...going to the center, what we call centers. If you have to go to the center, you should go on foot. Walking on foot to places of worship has been highly emphasized. If this is understood, we can relate it to why people walk on foot from Najaf to Karbala. And what is this? Some people who don't know things say, 'Why do they do this? Is it some kind of festival or custom from Najaf to Karbala?' They make such absurd remarks. Don't they feel ashamed sitting on the pulpit (minbar) of Hussain (a.s.) and making such absurd remarks? Today, anyone says anything. And the second thing (among expiations) is safeguarding the congregational prayers (Namaz-e-Jama'at), waiting for the next prayer after one prayer. Then, after that, the three things that ruin a person, what are they? One is extreme greed and miserliness (shuh-un muta'), about which we have discussed a lot. Second is that a person follows their carnal desires (hawa-un muttaba'), following their own desires. And the third thing that ruins a person is self-conceit (ujb), that is, a person admires themselves, thinking 'I am so amazing, look what I have achieved,' and pats their own back. And then, after that, the three things that grant salvation (najaat) to a person... ...the three things that grant salvation (najaat) to a person. In this hadith, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) mentions them. The things that grant salvation are: first, fearing Allah (khashyatullah) in private and in public, both privately and publicly. We should fear Allah in both states. And moderation (qasd) in spending, whether one's economic condition is good or bad, always maintain moderation. It shouldn't be that if dollars come, one loses their senses, wastes money, and spends extravagantly. And if conditions are bad, then taking loans to maintain that status, selling land or property just to maintain status. And after that, the third thing that grants salvation is that in every situation, a person speaks with justice, whether they are pleased with someone or angry with them, they must speak with justice. So these are the 12 things that should be the roadmap and perspective of a person's life. And you will see that these things are small, but they elevate a person's life. If you look at them individually and at the family level, they build an exemplary individual and family. And if this is implemented in society... ...family level, and if this is made common in society, then the society will become an Islamic society, a pure society, which is in accordance with the teachings of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.). And then, the biggest problem we face today, do you know what the biggest issue is? It is that we get influenced by others, others affect us and influence us. While the way (seerah) of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) is that they influence others and do not get influenced by others, no matter what the circumstances are. And the best example of this is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) [Salawat on Muhammad and Aal-e-Muhammad]... Yes, although these are not obligatory (wajib) acts, they elevate a person's ranks and a person progresses spiritually. Among them is 'Ifsha-us-Salam'—spread Salam. But why? Because you have seen that nowadays, even when people greet, they either say 'Hi', 'Hello', or 'How's it going?' because they are influenced by others. On the other hand, the proper way is to say 'Assalamu Alaikum, Assalamu Alaikum, Assalamu Alaikum'. And if the person is a believer (momin), then add 'wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh', otherwise if they are not a believer, suffice with 'Assalamu Alaikum'. If a non-believer says 'Assalamu Alaikum', then do not say 'Wa Alaikumus Salam wa Rahmatullah'. We shouldn't say 'wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh' to just anyone. 'Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh' is only for believers, not for others. So, spread Salam. Zurarah is also mentioned here. I will give a brief introduction about Zurarah, because these things have reached us through them. So let us mention Zurarah. Who is Zurarah? It is narrated about Zurarah that on the Day of Judgment, when a call will be made, 'Where are the companions of the fifth and sixth Imams?' then first of all... Where is the fifth or sixth story? First of all, this name was taken, which involves Ju'dah. And do you know the secret of Ju'dah, what the background is? Secondly, these were eleven brothers, six of whom died during their own time. Out of those six, the names of two have appeared in the hadith... Yajuj and Majuj, these two brothers... they were non-Muslims. And Ju'dah's grandfather was a non-Muslim. But what happened was that Ju'dah's sister, Umm-e-Farwah, went to seek guidance, became a savior there, and guided all eleven brothers. Look, if a single woman becomes religious—we were talking about goodness, walking on the right path—if a woman becomes religious, she transforms the entire family. And it was the effect of Ju'dah's upbringing that up to five or six generations of theirs—we have read this ourselves in a book, we have read the history, we are not talking about hearsay. Whatever we say... ...not talking about hearsay. Whatever we say, for four, five, or six generations, in their lineage, they used to append 'Ju'dari' to their names, meaning they were associated with Ju'dah. So much so, that once someone was asked, 'Are you Ju'dari?' 'Yes.' 'Whose descendant are you?' Then they explained they were from the lineage of Ju'dah's brother, but they still wrote 'Ju'dari'. Look how great the status of Ju'dah was! Indeed, Allah loves two things: feeding people and spreading peace (greetings). Spread greetings. The next point is to greet with Salaam. How to make this a habit? As soon as you enter the house, greet your family members: 'Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah.' After greeting, what should you focus on? We do many things after greeting, but what is in the heart should come out; it should be manifest on the outside, and true faith should be on the inside. It should be manifest on the outside, and true faith should be on the inside. If true faith is on the inside, many problems will be resolved. If there is someone in the house, greet them with Salaam. And even if there is no one in the house, still greet with Salaam. Why? Because even if the house is empty, there are angels in it. Therefore, when you greet, if there is no one in the house, say: 'Assalamu alayna wa 'ala 'ibadillahis-salihin' (Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah). Some people open the door with a key and just say 'Assalamu Alaikum'. No, say 'Assalamu alayna...', meaning peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah from Allah's side. What a beautiful teaching this is! Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah from our Lord. This is the manner, the etiquette. This is in Bihar al-Anwar, volume 76, page 7, hadith 25. Now, what are the etiquettes of Salaam? I am telling you quickly. In Bihar al-Anwar, it is narrated that the Imam (a.s.) said: 'The younger one should always greet the elder one first.' The younger one should always greet the elder one first. But if the younger one does not do it, the elder one should greet them first. Why? So that the elder teaches the child, giving practical training, showing that initiating the Salaam holds a higher reward. Should we always wait for others to greet us? No, if they don't, you should greet them: 'Assalamu Alaikum'. This is the way. If you teach practically, they will understand that this is the correct manner. Secondly, the one who is passing by—whether in a car, on a bicycle, a scooter, a bike, or walking—should greet those who are sitting. And the smaller group of people should greet the larger group. For example, in our gatherings, when someone enters, they sit down silently. But in Arab countries, it is not like that. In good religious gatherings, whenever someone enters, they greet the entire gathering: 'Assalamu Alaikum', and then everyone replies. ...'Walaikum Assalam'. Everyone will reply. Although one person's reply is sufficient, everyone replying 'Walaikum Assalam' is the Islamic way. And if there are many people in a gathering, but two specific people are present, greet them individually: a father and a teacher. If the teacher is there, greet them separately: 'Assalamu Alaikum', and greet the rest separately. These are all Islamic etiquettes. And since we are talking about this, let me tell you: never walk ahead of your father; always walk behind him, unless it is dark and your father does not know the way, in which case you can walk ahead and guide him. This is the etiquette. If you are sitting and your father enters the room, stand up immediately. It shouldn't be that the son remains seated while the father is standing. Just think for a moment: even if you are a king, you must stand up for your father. This is how much respect and honor is due to a father. Do not speak in a loud voice in front of your father, and do not argue with him, even if... ...even if he is completely wrong, remain silent. If you must speak, present your point with great respect. Some might think, 'My father has passed away, what should I do?' If you remember being disrespectful or rude to him, go to his grave if possible. If you cannot go to his grave, then from wherever you are sitting, ask your father for forgiveness. Say, 'Father, I am sorry for my mistakes.' And recite Surah al-Ikhlas three times and gift the reward to him. He is still your father. These are all etiquettes. And who should we not greet with Salaam? This is also mentioned in the hadiths. Nowadays, people greet everyone without considering who they should or shouldn't greet. First of all, non-Muslims are outside this circle. If they do not believe in 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.)'... If they do not believe, then do not greet them. But if they do, then greet them. Now, who else should we not greet? Non-Muslims aside, among Muslims, who should we not greet? Someone who drinks alcohol at the dining table, or a habitual drinker. Do not greet them. Why? Because greeting them honors them, and why should we honor someone who drinks alcohol? Or a sinner, so they realize why we are treating them this way. Our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has forbidden us from meeting sinners with a cheerful face. We should meet them with a stern face. Why? Because they are committing sins. And it is in the hadith: 'Indeed, Allah dislikes a weak believer...' ...'Indeed, Allah dislikes a weak believer.' What is the explanation? Allah dislikes a believer who is weak, powerless, and has no faith. Physical weakness is one thing, but having no faith is another. People asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, who is the believer who has no faith?' He replied, 'The one who does not forbid evil.' One who sees evil and remains silent, thinking, 'What do I have to do with it?' No, we must act. So this was the first thing about Salaam. The second thing is that if someone is playing chess or gambling, do not greet them. There are such hadiths about chess that we cannot even describe. There are such narrations. Nowhere is it written that chess is only forbidden if played with gambling; chess itself is forbidden, and gambling too. ...and gambling too. And if someone has effeminate behavior or habits—acting like women—do not greet them, otherwise the whole society will become like that if we do not draw a line. And after that, do not greet someone who is praying, because they cannot reply in their normal voice. Although they can reply with 'Salamun Alaikum', it is better not to greet them so they don't have to reply. And if someone consumes usury (interest), do not greet them. If someone is earning through usury, do not greet them. This has become so common among us now, and no one stops it. As long as they give us donations, we say, 'It's okay, Allah will forgive.' And if someone is in the washroom, do not greet them, because speaking in the washroom is Makruh (disliked). If you greet them, they will be obliged to reply. And in public matters too, this is emphasized. And the last point is that a sinner who sins openly... ...a sinner who sins openly, do not greet them. When they ask, 'Why aren't you greeting me?' you can say, 'Because you are committing sins openly.' This is how an Islamic society is formed. See how an Islamic society is structured. The second thing is to feed people as much as possible. Since you are followers of Islam, and the Quran says: 'Wa yut'imunat-ta'ama 'ala hubbihi...' This is Surah al-Dahr, verse number 8, you can see. So, what the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) are feeding... See the connection: the nourishment of the body is eating food, while the strength of the soul is feeding others. The strength of the body is eating food, and the strength of the soul is feeding others. This is connected to spending. A person spends and feeds people, and especially, what is it for? If this feeding of food is for the sake of Allah—for example, you went for Hajj, and there are other pilgrims with you, and you said, 'Today's food is on me,' and you fed the pilgrims. This is a very big question. And remember one thing: the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) do not keep anyone's debt. We do not narrate these incidents without reason; it is not our habit. These incidents are recorded in books of Hadith, in what we call literature, which people collected over the passage of time. But the greatest work done in this regard was by a very great scholar in Qom, Iran, whose name was Allama Majlisi. He worked extensively on this... ...Allama Majlisi, he worked a lot on this, and compiled Bihar al-Anwar. He gathered books from here and there, put in immense effort. These are not just stories we have heard; the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) have preserved them so that we can remove any doubts. I am telling you this briefly. Ayatullah Mar'ashi Najafi's son heard this. Ayatullah Mar'ashi Najafi said, 'Do not worry, it will be arranged. Somehow, Mashallah, even if you have to take a loan... you have worked for the cause of the Mawla (a.s.), and the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) do not keep anyone's debt.' Ayatullah Mar'ashi Najafi then narrated a short incident to him... ...he narrated a short incident. I am telling it quickly, not going into too much detail, but I will tell you the essence. He said, 'Do you know Al-Masi?' He said, 'No, I don't.' 'Al-Mas' means diamond. So, Al-Masi was a gentleman in Isfahan whose financial condition was not very good. He had only two rooms in his house. He told his wife, 'Let's do one thing: we will raise some animals like chickens or goats in one of the two rooms, so we can have some income and run our household.' His wife agreed, saying, 'Okay, no problem, we will live in one room.' Both husband and wife agreed on this. And after that, what happened? They started preparing the second room for the animals. As they began digging it, a large diamond was found. This diamond was found... let me tell you, it was about a hundred years ago. When the diamond was found, this gentleman, Al-Masi—at that time he wasn't called Al-Masi, he was called something else—took this diamond to Isfahan... ...he took this diamond to all the jewelers in Isfahan. People said, 'Brother, this is a very huge diamond, we don't have the capacity to buy it. If you want a good price for it, go to Baghdad. You will find a buyer in the jewelry market of Baghdad.' So he decided to go to Iraq. But before going to Baghdad, he thought, 'Since I have the opportunity to visit the holy shrines, let me perform the Ziyarah first. I will visit Najaf, Karbala, Kazmain, Samarra, and then go to Baghdad.' So he reached Najaf. When he reached Najaf, he first went to the Haram of Imam Ali (a.s.) for Ziyarah. As soon as he arrived for Ziyarah, he was reciting the Ziyarah supplications. Meanwhile, the Mutawalli (custodian) of the shrine was calling out, 'O lovers of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)! You see that the Zarih (shrine grille) of Ali (a.s.) is made of wood, and the kings of the world do not care that his Zarih is made of wood. If you give some donations, we can make a beautiful Zarih for this shrine, a steel Zarih.' Now, this man... ...this touched his heart deeply. He quickly said, 'I have nothing else but this diamond. Take this diamond, and whatever money comes from it, use it to make the Zarih.' It is said that the first silver Zarih made after the wooden one was funded by Al-Masi's money. He gave it, but then he started thinking, 'What do I do now? I have nothing left in this world. This was my only hope, based on which I had borrowed money from people, promising to go to Baghdad, sell it, and return their money. Now I don't even have money to go back, and how will I repay people?' He was very worried. Meanwhile, someone knocked on his door. 'Please come, you have been summoned. Is your name this?' He said, 'Yes.' 'We have been tracking you all the way from Isfahan. You had a relative in India who died, leaving no children or heirs...' ...he died, leaving no children or heirs, so he has willed all his land to your name. And a representative is saying, 'Either you take the land, or I will buy it from you for this huge amount of money.' He agreed. 'Okay, this draft/money is in your name, this is for you.' He started crying and couldn't even sleep. He went to the guest house and slept. In his dream, he saw the Imam (a.s.) saying, 'Remember, we Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) do not keep anyone's debt.' So, practice this tradition of feeding others as much as possible, especially in Azadari, in the month of Ramadan, wherever possible. And look, especially in Azadari, we emphasize this because Azadari is our lifeline. Never think about how much was spent on it. Sometimes we shouldn't repeat things, but repeating is necessary because the audience keeps changing... ...because the audience keeps changing, it is necessary to say this: Azadari is our lifeline. So never think that too much was spent on it. This is Imam Hussain's (a.s.) budget that came to your share. And if you spend on Imam Hussain's (a.s.) path, remember that Imam Hussain (a.s.) repays it in other ways. And there are satanic whispers on our WhatsApp, people sitting and saying, 'Oh, what is this Azadari? Why spend on food? Why spend on Niyaz? Why do Tabarruk? Build a hospital instead, build a school instead.' Well, brother, who has stopped you from building hospitals and schools? How many schools have you built? We have seen that wherever people spend generously on Nazr and Niyaz, those communities also have hospitals, schools, and all other facilities. Remember, no matter how wealthy a person is, if their heart is small, they will never spend. But even if they have very little, if their heart is big and they love Imam Hussain (a.s.), they will say, 'Take whatever I have,' just like the incident of Al-Masi. Whatever I can do for the path of the Mawla (a.s.), that is everything for me. Just keep this in mind, Inshallah. And the third thing that increases sustenance (rizq) is the night prayer (Namaz-e-Shab/Tahajjud). What is the verse of the Quran? Let's read Surah Bani Isra'il, verse 79: 'Wa minal layli fa tahajjad bihi nafilatal lak...' ('And from [part of] the night, pray with it as additional [worship] for you...'). When a part of the night passes, stand up and pray. Tahajjud in Arabic means to wake up and worship. Going and worshipping in the night... 'Tahajjud' is a word that has two opposite meanings. 'Hajada' (or Tahajjud) means both to sleep and to wake up. But keep in mind, for worship, 'Tahajjud' is used. 'Wa minallaili fatahajjad bihi nafilatal lak' (And pray Tahajjud in the night as an additional prayer for you). Wake up and pray. These are 8 rak'ahs of Nafilah, then 2 rak'ahs of Shafi', and 1 rak'ah of Witr. Some call it 'Witr', but in Arabic, it is called 'Witr'. So, these 11 rak'ahs are very easy, very simple. But Satan whispers so much: 'Don't do it, don't do it. Look how tired you are. You were watching the match for so long, how can you pray now?' Satan whispers to the youngsters, and they sleep. Look, wake up and pray. It has a very high status. If these same youngsters have to go to the gym, they will wake up, lift heavy weights, endure it, and spend one or two hours in the gym. This prayer takes at most 10 minutes, 10 to 12 minutes. But Satan distances them from it. So what is written? 'Wake up and pray Namaz-e-Tahajjud as a Nafilah.' 'Asa anyab'asaka rabbuka maqamam mahmuda' (Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station [Maqam-e-Mahmud]). Your Lord will elevate you to Maqam-e-Mahmud. Elevate you to Maqam-e-Mahmud. What is Maqam-e-Mahmud? Maqam-e-Mahmud is a station where whoever reaches it can intercede (do Shafa'at) for people through Namaz-e-Shab, and can take you along with them. That is what Maqam-e-Mahmud is. And on page number 90, it is narrated that Jibrail (a.s.) advised me so much, gave me so much counsel regarding Namaz-e-Shab, that I began to think the best people of my Ummah do not sleep at all. In Arabic, the phrase used is 'La yanamoon'—they do not sleep at all. Jibrail (a.s.) advised and counselled me so much about Namaz-e-Shab. These narrations are such, volume 84, page number 13, and hadith number 26. And after this, when a youth stands up to pray Namaz-e-Shab, Satan whispers. What does he do? He sets an alarm, and when the alarm rings, he thinks, 'I should wake up, but I'll sleep a bit more.' Try this and see, if you experience this, then tell me. Just a little while before... Just a little while before Fajr, 12 to 15 minutes before Fajr, pray Namaz-e-Tahajjud (Shab), then pray Namaz-e-Fajr, and sit on the prayer mat until sunrise. If there is no rain of sustenance (Rizq), then tell me that Allah did not give it. You can become so wealthy. Allah promises in the Quran: 'Wa man yattaqillaha yaj'al lahu makhraja' (And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him a way out) 'Wa yarzuqhu min haithu la yahtasib' (And He will provide for him from where he does not expect). He will give him sustenance from sources he cannot even imagine, he will remain in shock. So when this youth prays, what happens? When this youth prays Namaz-e-Shab, Allah says to the angels: 'Thumma yaqoolu Azza wa Jall li-malaikatihi' (Then Allah, the Almighty, says to His angels), 'O My angels, look at My servant! He has stood up in the darkness of the night to whisper secrets to Me, worshipping Me, while the people of falsehood and negligence are asleep or watching matches.' They are sleeping, they are heedless of Namaz-e-Shab. They have no care for Namaz-e-Shab. Why are they so immersed in falsehood? They do not pay attention to this side. And those who are in a state of negligence are sleeping, they have no care, they are busy in play and amusement. Look at this, I have witnessed it with my own eyes, that until 3:00, 3:30, or 4:00 in the morning, they sit at the crossroads talking about useless, worldly things. They sit at the crossroads until 3:30 or 4:00 AM, and then as soon as it's 4:00, they say, 'Okay brother, Khuda Hafiz, Shabba Khair, Khuda Hafiz,' go home, and sleep. Forget Namaz-e-Shab, they even miss Namaz-e-Fajr! And when they sleep, they wake up at 2:00 PM. Then at 2:00 PM, they complain, 'O Allah, my sustenance is blocked.' Their sustenance is bound to be blocked! Allah does give them sustenance, but He reduces its blessings (Barakah)... Allah created the angels, created them and said, 'Glorify Me (Tasbih) and praise Me (Taqdis).' They said, 'We cannot carry this burden.' So He said, 'Okay, do one thing, send Salawat upon Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his Progeny (a.s.).' And they did so. Do you know that in this Salawat that you send, Tasbih is present, Taqdis is present, everything is present. Then after that, Allah says, 'O angels, look, everyone is asleep in negligence, but this youth is worshipping Me. Bear witness that I have forgiven all his sins.' Bear witness that I have forgiven all his sins. That is why when someone asks, 'I pray, but my prayers are not answered, my prayers are blocked...' This means they must have committed some sin. And among the greatest sins, what is it? Lying. Lying is among them. And attributing a lie to someone is an even bigger sin. And if you attribute a lie to Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.) or the Imams (a.s.), it is one hundred percent Haram. Do not fabricate any Hadith on your own. Nowadays, fabricating Hadiths has become a huge problem. Understand this, it is very dangerous. People fabricate Hadiths on their own, saying 'Imam Hussain (a.s.) said this or that...' or attributing things to Yazid's character, making up stories. Do not write anything on your own. And my request to WhatsApp users is that unless there is a complete reference, do not forward it. No matter who sends it to you, unless a proper book reference is given, do not share it. Otherwise, it is a major sin (Gunah-e-Kabirah). It is a sin that even breaks the fast. Attributing a lie to Allah and His... It breaks the fast—attributing a lie to Allah, His Messenger (s.a.w.a.), and the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.). If the reference is known and verified, only then mention it, otherwise it is not permissible. These were the things. Insha'Allah, the remaining points will be discussed very soon tomorrow. These are the things that elevate a person's spirit. Among them, the most important thing is to submit completely before the Almighty. When one submits completely before the Almighty, their spiritual stations are automatically elevated. You know the famous saying: 'Agar zarre par Abu Turab ki nazar pad jaye, toh yeh zarra aasman tak jayega aur suraj ka kaam karega' (If the gaze of Abu Turab [Imam Ali (a.s.)] falls upon a speck of dust, that speck will rise to the heavens and act as a sun). And that is why in history, you will see people who, just a short time before their martyrdom, accepted Islam and guidance. Let us give an example. If anyone has a doubt, let us give an example. The magicians of Pharaoh. They stood before Prophet Musa (a.s.). And as soon as they threw their staffs and ropes, they became snakes. You know the story of Pharaoh, it is present in the Quran, the entire account of Prophet Musa (a.s.). Prophet Musa (a.s.) cast his staff. As soon as they saw Prophet Musa's staff, it became a giant serpent and swallowed their magic. At that very moment, those magicians attained the recognition (Ma'rifah) of the Almighty. And as soon as they attained the recognition of the Almighty, and the merciful gaze of Prophet Musa (a.s.) fell upon them, they were instantly transformed. Their faith suddenly soared to such a level that when Pharaoh threatened them, 'How dare you believe in him without my permission? I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all,' they did not waver. Their faith had reached the highest peak. Their faith had reached the highest peak. A believer (Mu'min) does not fear death. Only he fears death who is attached to this world. Now look at what they replied to Pharaoh, as quoted in the Quran: 'La daira' (No harm/No problem). 'Do whatever you want to do, cut our hands and feet, crucify us, "Inna ila Rabbina munqaliboon" (Indeed, to our Lord we will return).' This is the status when the merciful gaze falls upon someone. Therefore, always pray for the Imam of our time (a.t.f.s.), always pray. And this is what happened... those who remained in Mecca and Medina did not come to help the Imam (a.s.); they were only giving advice. No one came to help. But on the way, there was a youth, Wahab (Wahab bin Abdullah Kalbi), who was a Christian, but through the merciful gaze of the Imam, he became a true follower. Why use the word 'follower'? Because just as we follow the Imam of our time, he also followed the Imam of his time, and by chance, he joined them. Now, on the day of Ashura, as the companions began to be martyred one after another, his mother started telling him, 'O my son, go and sacrifice your life for the Imam of your time...' ...started saying, 'Go and sacrifice your life for the Imam of your time.' What courage his mother had! Now he came and requested the Imam, 'O Master, grant me permission.' He is pleading with the Imam, requesting him with folded hands, 'O Master, grant me permission.' Now the entire scene is before you: he is a youth, his wife has just been married for seventeen days, leaving her father's house. She does not want him to go, and he is the only support of his mother, with no other support. How could the Imam grant him permission? The Imam stood silent. Suddenly, a voice came from behind the curtain, 'O Master, grant him permission. I have only this one son, I have no other sacrifice to offer. I have only this one sacrifice, please accept it and grant him permission.' What incredible courage! He went to the battlefield, fought bravely, and when his body was riddled with wounds, Wahab came back to his mother and said, 'Mother, are you pleased with me now?' What a historic reply his mother gave: 'My son, I sent you to die, not to return alive! Go and sacrifice your life there!' If it remains, they do not want it, and they wanted it, and then doubt... so ask your heart... [garbled text] ...so much victory. May I be sacrificed, may I be ruined, may I be ruined... wherever they are in the world, their honor was plundered... The mourning of Hussain... This was the solace of Bano, Sakina. Come back, Sakina, come back, Sakina. They say, this was the solace of Bano, Sakina. Come back, Sakina, come back, Sakina, come back... Come back, Sakina, come back, Sakina... Those who are not with you make you weep. Qasim and Akbar have already left us, and Asghar is no longer in this world to return to us. In this state of exile, we were separated from you. Do not torment us with your separation, Sakina. Come back, Sakina... Why are you upset with us, beloved of Shabbir? Come to my lap, my darling. In the battlefield, your Abbas is distressed; the helpless ones wander around searching for you in every direction. Do not torment us any further, Sakina... Where is Asghar now to swing you in the cradle? Where is Asghar now to swing you in the cradle? Have patience, come into my lap for a moment. In this foreign land, those with guardians do not survive. Your earrings have been snatched away... Come and hide in my lap, Sakina. Come back, Sakina... This dark night, this scene of Doomsday, a smoke of grief is cast over the atmosphere. Without water, weeping is now justified in the desert. I only desire you, I do not care about thirst. Do not be stubborn, come back, Sakina... Granted that some more oppressors will inflict tyranny, do not be despondent, the womenfolk of the household are still with you. Do not despair, we are now with you to comfort you, brother. You have to sleep in the prison... For a long time... today it could be... they will not be able to say 'Syria' when your name is taken, they will sigh. The sun of the Haram will mourn. When the people of our homeland ask, we will tell them, we will tell them. For God's sake, tell me, will they be able to...? Come, come, come, come, come, come, everything was declared... How much was declared?

title: Majlis 2 | Marefat-e-Nooraaniyyah | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound theological concept of Ma'rifat-e-Nooraniyyah, or the recognition of the luminous status of the Ahl al-Bayt. The discourse bridges the historical events of Imam Hussain's arrival in Karbala with deep philosophical inquiries into the nature of creation, divine authority, and the dangers of human arrogance. Dr. Rizvi emphasizes that true faith requires moving beyond superficial understanding to recognize the spiritual light of the Imams, while carefully navigating the balance between reverence and theological extremes.
content:
Presenting the Marsiya of Mir Anis: When the King of Religion entered Karbala, the desert of calamity became a model of the sublime Paradise. The sky bowed its head, touching the earth. The sun became captivated by the beauty of the beautiful Hussain (a.s.). The world gained splendor from his manifestation; the wilderness was adorned with moons by the light of his face. Because of Zahra's (s.a.) son, the earth became like heaven. Wherever the Ghazi (a.s.) walked, that land became a galaxy. All the pure land became the envy of the gardens of Paradise. It found such an inhabitant that its status became highly exalted. The skirt of the battlefield, which was pure and clean, the Kaaba bound its Ihram to circumambulate it. An unseen voice proclaimed, 'How glorious is the status of Karbala! The Master of the Universe is the guest of Karbala.' Today, the lap of Karbala is filled with flowers... Today, the lap of Karbala is filled with flowers; it is as if the garden of Karbala is Paradise itself. What honors were received through the grace of the Sun of Religion! The Pearl of Najaf, by whom the Throne is illuminated, was found. Every garden blossomed, spring came close. Giving peace to the garden of the world, this is a wondrous season. The nightingale, separated from its nest, said, 'The flower of the garden of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has arrived, how fortunate!' It is the pride of the earth, around which humans and jinn revolve. Behold the glory of God, the days of the wilderness have turned for the better. The earth, which is like heaven, was saying to the sky, 'Who is higher in status today, you or I? Upon me are the footsteps of the one who was on the Seal of Prophethood. Before my particles, your sun and moon are insignificant. Now even this humble dust is like the Kaaba... all the ornaments of the Throne are now with me.' Stopping his horse, the King of heavenly dignity said, 'We have reached our destination, by the grace of the Creator. Let no one advance their steed from here...' Let no one advance their steed from here. This is the land for which the heart is restless. May I be sacrificed for this place, O Lord, my ultimate desire is fulfilled. Saying this, the captain of the ship of the Ummah dismounted. All those who were riding dismounted and became on foot. The Holy Imam (a.s.) smiled and said to everyone, 'Look at this lush land, look at the atmosphere of the canal!' Akbar (a.s.) became delighted upon seeing the desert, Abbas (a.s.) began to sway with joy upon seeing the river. The renowned Abbas (a.s.) said with folded hands, 'Where should we pitch the tents, O King of land and sea? The heat is intense for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and the children are more delicate than flowers. For how long have the curtains of the litters been drawn? Due to the heat, everyone's breath is suffocated.' After thinking for a moment, the Imam (a.s.) of both worlds said, 'Wherever Zainab (s.a.) says, pitch the tents there.' Hearing this, the loyal Abbas (a.s.) stepped back, went near the litter of Zainab (s.a.), and called out, 'The devoted servant of the Imam is present...' At the litter of Zainab, a voice called out, 'The devoted ones are present.' Where should the holy tent of the honorable Imam be pitched? Hearing this, the sorrow-stricken Lady of the Era (Zainab) said, 'What say do I have in this matter, I who am devoted? Whether it be dry land or a valley, a garden or a thousand greens, everywhere, the protector and helper of travelers is the Master of the Universe. You are the light of the universe, pitch the tents where my brother finds peace.' The Crown-wearer of the two worlds was silent in thought. Abbas, the possessor of dignity, was getting the tents unpacked. Suddenly, a black and red dust cloud rose from the north, and three or four riders appeared. Turning around, Habib said, 'The situation seems different.' Someone said, 'This is the manner of the Syrian army.' The loyal Abbas said to the attendants, 'Go find out what their intention is. What kind of behavior is this for rebels upon arrival? Tell them that this is the place for the tents of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). It is obligatory...' ...that this is the place for the tents of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Respect for the ladies is obligatory; they should camp elsewhere, as this is a place of respect. The piece of the heart of the Master of Mankind (the Prophet) is seated here. Are they not aware of the manners of travel? The dust raised by the hooves of their horses is flying this way. Why do they not hold back the reins of their horses? They have forgotten who we are; perhaps these oppressors are riding the horses of wind. The commander of that army came forward and spoke, 'This is the command of the commander, that the Syrian army shall camp here. We will occupy the place of comfort. You should pitch your camp away from the river. An army is marching against the King of the Universe. Tomorrow, the army's positions will be on the Euphrates. We have come here to block the riverbanks. Today, everyone has news of Shimr's arrival.' Hearing this, that brave lion (Abbas) roared in the valley. Frowning, his gaze fell upon the hilt of his sword. Was he not the Lion of God? He emerged... Was he not the Lion of God? He emerged roaring like a lion from its lair. Placing his lightning-like sword on his shoulder in anger, the Lion (Abbas) raised a battle cry, 'Will we retreat before you? Even if the victorious army arrives, what is the grief? The head that stands firm is severed right there. When this lion is enraged, no one dares to come before him. This is an eye in which no one can fit (none can withstand his gaze). Even if the whole world is on one side, in my thoughts, my sword has run through millions in battle. They will be destroyed and left without a trace if I enter into wrath. On all sides, there is the grace of the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). What is this river that this lion would leave and retreat, when [my father] made a bridge by breaking the gate of Khaybar? Who are you? Hussain is the chosen master. Who else is the Emperor of land and sea? Look, there will be conflict if you advance. Is this the place for lions, do you not know? We do not show leniency to anyone in battle.' We do not show leniency to anyone in battle. I have said it: do not set foot in the valley. We can turn the earth and sky upside down right now. Whoever rebels, we can crush them right now. We can turn this land into a river of blood right now. If anyone speaks, we will sever their head from their body. If the day of judgment does not occur, we will bring it about right now.' Hazrat Qasim rolled up his sleeves. The handsome Akbar advanced, placing his hand on the hilt of his sword. The moon-faced youths of Hazrat Zainab said in anger, 'Will these lowlifes take the valley from lions? Tell the spearmen that we will deal with them. If anyone glares at us, we will gouge their eyes out.' As that brave lion (Abbas) advanced, swaying with majesty, some fell here out of fear, and some fell there. When the sword was drawn, there was commotion and clamor, and the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) became anxious. When the sword was drawn, there was commotion and clamor, and the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) became anxious. In the lap of her aunt, Sakina trembled with fear. A clamor arose that swords had been drawn at the riverbank. The sorrowful and unfortunate Zainab cried out weeping, 'Go find out with whom this conflict has occurred! What is the reason for this clamor against those stricken by exile? Let someone see where the good-natured King (Hussain) is. O people, sacrifice yourselves for the Imam of the nations, and pray for the moon-faced Akbar.' Saying this, the sister of the Imam began to weep. On the other side, Abbas, in great anger, advanced towards the Syrian army. Rising quickly from his seat, the King of Mankind (Imam Hussain) called out, 'Brother, by my head, I swear to you, stop! In our view, there is no place for rage and anger on the path of truth. Come, I swear to you by Hazrat Amir (a.s.), do not get angry at the rebellion of this wicked army. The daughters of the Prophet are with us, and this is the destination of a dervish.' The daughters of the Prophet are with us, and this is the destination of a dervish. Is the desert not enough for those who are patient and grateful? Why all this arrangement for a traveler?' When the master swore by his holy head, that generous soul (Abbas) trembled. His anger, which could shatter stones, did not lessen, but he became quiet as soon as the King of the Nations arrived. He bowed his head so that there would be no breach of respect, but tears of blood fell from his eyes. He bowed his head so that there would be no breach of respect, but tears of blood fell from his eyes. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the outcast. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power nor strength except by Allah, the High, the Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Patron, and the best Helper. Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the ultimate end is for the pious. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of the Prophets and Messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad, and his purified progeny. ...the Imam of the Time, the Guardian, the Proof... and may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. As for what follows, our master and leader, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) said: Our master, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.)—blessings be upon him and his pure family—in this noble Hadith, which we have made the theme of this series of lectures, states: 'Indeed, the day of Hussain—that is, the grief of Hussain—has severely wounded our eyelids.' Through weeping, the Imam's eyelids are wounded; through crying, the Imam's eyelids are wounded. 'And our tears flow continuously. Therefore, if anyone is to weep, let him weep for someone like Hussain; weep for Hussain.' '...weep for someone like Hussain; weep for Hussain.' And there are many such narrations from Imam al-Rida (a.s.). For instance, during the days of Muharram, when Rayyan ibn Shabib came to the Imam, the Imam said to him, 'O Ibn Shabib, if you must weep for anything, weep for my grandfather Hussain.' Why? The Imam explains the reason: 'Because he was slaughtered just as a ram is slaughtered.' This is a profound comparison, the details of which we will discuss some other time, Inshallah. So, this is a sign of a Shia, as I submitted to you. Now, we often see that there are differences among Shias on certain matters. If these differences are over minor, worldly matters, then it is not a major issue; that is natural. However, when differences arise in matters of belief (Aqaid), then it becomes a significant matter. Similarly, a narrator came and asked the Imam a question. The narrator's name is Muhammad ibn Sinan, who says, 'I was with Abu Ja'far al-Thani (a.s.)...' My name is Muhammad ibn Sinan. He says: I presented myself in the service of Abu Ja'far al-Thani, i.e., Imam al-Jawad (a.s.), and I asked a question, I discussed why there are differences among the Shi'as. Then he (a.s.) said... Now look, what was the narrator's question? That there are differences among the Shi'as. Obviously, the differences he is talking about here are differences in beliefs (Aqa'id). Meaning, not differences over worldly monetary transactions, or differences over some land, or differences over anything else, but rather regarding beliefs. The Imam says, addressing him, 'O Muhammad' or 'O Muhammad ibn Sinan: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, was unique in His oneness...' Now look, the Imam is discussing something else. Why is there a difference? Is it this reason or that reason? Or that one's belief is lesser, another's is... one's belief is wrong, another's is correct, one has less, one has more? No. The Imam states what the reason is. The Imam says: Allah was alone and solitary, He had not created anything, there was no object, no creation; Allah was completely alone. Then He created Muhammad, Ali, and Fatima (a.s.). Meaning, the Imam wants to convey that the differences that arise among the Shi'as, the differences in their beliefs, the reason for this is that they have not understood the discussion on creation, they have not understood the discussion on the original source (mabda). ...they have not understood the discussion on the original source (mabda), they have not understood the concept of original creation, which is why there are differences in their beliefs. Insha'Allah, we will explain this. You will see, Insha'Allah, how these things [affect] a person's belief... Now look, 'Dahr' (time/epoch)—its details have not been mentioned in the narrations, and scholars have explained different things about it. Recite a Salawat. Scholars have explained different things. Look, we do not even say that this thing is right and that thing is wrong; we are just presenting a perspective. Allah knows best whether it is right or wrong. The word 'Dahr' has appeared in the Quran, in the first verse of Surah al-Insan. The first verse of Surah al-Insan: 'Has there not come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing even mentioned?' Meaning, 'Dahr' is that time when he was not even worthy of mention. That time came upon man. Usually, people translate it as 'time' or when man was nothing. That is why in Urdu, the idiom is used: 'your status/worth'... ...the idiom is used: 'Do not forget your status (auqat).' Not forgetting your status means: remember that time when you were nothing. Today, you have become something, so you have started walking with arrogance; at that time, you were nothing. The Quran says: 'Indeed, We created man from a mixed drop... and We made him hearing and seeing (intellectual).' 'Indeed, We guided him to the way...' And after making him intellectual, We also showed him the way, 'whether he be grateful or ungrateful.' That is within his choice; Allah has given him free will. Look, the word 'Insan' (man) has been used many times in the Quran. Right now, that is not our topic. Insha'Allah, if Allah ever grants the opportunity, that will be the topic. The word 'Insan', humanity, and related things—there is such a deep discussion on this in the Quran and narrations. The Quran says: 'O...' ...The Quran says: 'O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?' Where did this pride come from? In Arabic, 'ghurur' means deception. How were you deceived? How were you deceived before Allah? What does deception mean here? The verse explains further, but we will just speak briefly and move forward so as not to deviate from the topic. What does deception mean here? Deception here means: how did you start considering yourself to be something? How did you start thinking highly of yourself? Now connect this verse with that other verse. Do you not remember the time when you were nothing? That is, the word the Quran used: you were not even worthy of mention. What does 'not worthy of mention' mean? Mir Damad—and Western authors have also discussed this quite a bit, let me tell you this too... ...have discussed this quite a bit. Zaman is time, meaning from when Allah created time until time runs its course and ends—if we calculate that entire span of time, one second of it is 'Dahr'. Dahr is one second. One second... the entire span of time is one second of Dahr. The entire span of time is one second of Dahr. Now you can understand what Dahr is. Anyway, that is not the topic. Allah kept whom for this long? He kept the light (Noor) of Muhammad, Ali, and Fatima (a.s.). Then He created all other things. Another point is that when the word 'fawwada' (delegated) appears here—'He delegated the affairs to them'—'fawwada' means to delegate, to hand over completely, to delegate all affairs to them. So, many of our people have a disease—just like the flu comes, they have the disease of 'Ghuluww' (exaggeration). Anything they cannot digest, they say, 'This is Ghuluww, this is Ghuluww.' Ghuluww occurs—and we will explain this too, Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the opportunity and time—Ghuluww occurs when a person elevates the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) to the level of Allah. If one is not bringing them to the level of Allah... ...if one is not bringing them to the level of Allah, but placing them vertically below Allah, that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) do everything with Allah's permission, by Allah's leave, then there is no harm in it, just as all the Prophets did. Now, obviously, all these things do not easily fit into human intellect. Can they? No. For example, if someone tells you that a she-camel will emerge from this wall right now and drink up all the rainwater that is falling, would you believe it? You would say, 'Brother, take him to a good doctor.' Would you believe it? No. But that she-camel is mentioned in the Quran. If we say we have a staff, and if we just go to Carter Road and wave it like this, the sea at Carter Road will split into two parts, would you believe it? Now, indeed, this would be considered a gone case. But Hazrat Musa (a.s.) is mentioned in the Quran, that Hazrat Musa did this. Similarly, Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) slaughtered birds—four of them—scattered them on different mountains, and then called them, and the birds joined back together, came to life, and returned. Who did this? It happened by the Prophet's order, but it was by the leave of the Lord (bi-idhnillah), by the permission of the Lord. Therefore, there is nothing surprising in these actions; everywhere it is 'by Allah's leave, by Allah's leave'. So, if the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) perform any action by Allah's leave, then why is the label of... ...if the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) perform any action by Allah's leave, why is the label of Ghuluww stamped on it? They did not readily narrate the virtues (fada'il) of the Ahl al-Bayt, and when the Shi'as did, they said, 'Brother, this is Ghuluww, this is exaggeration, this is exaggeration, and these are Ghali (exaggerators), and Ghali.' Meaning, in the world of creation, Allah has given them power, He has given them power such that, for example, whatever they wish, even raising the dead... The Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) possess this power, given to them by Allah, but only with Allah's permission, with Allah's permission. Similarly, Allah has given them another power: whatever the Ahlul Bayt do, they are the standard of Halal and Haram. This is why in Ziyarat Al-e-Yasin, you recite: 'The truth is that with which you are pleased, and falsehood is that with which you are displeased; the good is that which you have commanded, and the evil is that which you have forbidden.' Now, whatever the Ahlul Bayt have declared is the truth, and whatever they forbade is falsehood. If Imam Hasan (a.s.) made peace, it was right, and if Imam Husayn (a.s.) waged war, that was also right. Every Imam acts according to his circumstances, in line with the wisdom, the command of the Lord, and the will of the Lord. Therefore, whatever they wish, they make Halal, and whatever they wish, they make Haram. Recite a Salawat. And they do not wish for anything unless Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, wishes it. The Ahlul Bayt do not wish for anything unless Allah wishes it. After that, the Imam said, 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad ibn Sinan'—the Imam, Imam al-Jawad (a.s.), addresses the narrator—'O Muhammad, this is our religion. Look, this is the religion, the actual religion, this is religiousness, this is our religion. The one who went ahead became deviated, and the one who lagged behind—meaning the one who committed 'ghuluww' (exaggeration) became deviated, and the one who lagged behind, the 'muqassir', was destroyed and ruined. And whoever remains on this path and this belief will reach the right destination. 'Khudhha ya Muhammad' (Take it, O Muhammad), O Muhammad ibn Sinan, hold fast to this religion, hold fast to it. This is the reason why there are differences among people, why there are differences, because they did not understand the actual... Why are there differences? Because they did not understand the reality of creation. If they had understood the reality of creation, no one would ever argue or dispute, they would never dispute. And we sometimes give an example of this: generally, those who go against the Ahlul Bayt—or rather, when we do not appreciate their value, the reason is that there is no actual Ma'rifat (recognition). We do not think about all this. Now, let us look at a short Hadith in your service, and after that, we will return to Ma'rifat bin-Nooraniyyah. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (r.a.), as you know, is a very great personality, a companion of the Messenger, who attained the ninth level, the ninth grade of faith. What was the actual content, the matter in it? The Prophet gave the entire answer in just one or two lines. He said, 'They were entirely lessons.' The Scrolls of Moses contained nothing but lessons. And what are they? The Prophet gives two or three examples of this, which we will mention quickly. Allah says in a Hadith al-Qudsi, 'I am amazed at the person who is certain of death, yet he is arrogant in this world.' He is certain of death, that everyone has to die and go there. (Inshallah, that is a different topic). 'And I am amazed at the one who is certain of the Fire, how does he laugh? How can he laugh?' And after that, 'And the one who observes the world and how it turns against its people...' ...and how it turns against its people, how does he feel secure in it?' A person is observing the world, seeing how the world turns, how the world turns its back, observing its instability and its turning, so how can he feel secure in this world? Does this world belong to anyone? Anyone with a little experience in life will say, 'No, the world belongs to no one.' A perfectly healthy, walking person departs from this world in a minute. A well-spoken person becomes a victim of paralysis in a moment, suffers a paralytic attack, cannot speak, cannot convey his thoughts. A perfectly fine person ends up in the hospital ICU in a moment. We cannot say anything about anyone, we cannot say anything about ourselves. This is what the world is, this is the law of the world, this is the way and manner of the world. What is there to be proud of? 'O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?' What has made you so arrogant? Where is this pride coming from? Anyway... Now, when Ma'rifat bin-Nooraniyyah is so important, why are we distant from Ma'rifat bin-Nooraniyyah? This is the reason: firstly, we do not have certainty in the Ahlul Bayt, we do not have certainty in their creation. Sir, before calling a Hadith weak, look at yourself, think, and understand what we are saying. If there is even a 1% chance out of 100—we say this to those who very quickly issue decrees of a Hadith being weak—if there is a 1% chance that the Hadith is authentic and not weak, then whose saying does it become? It becomes the saying of an Infallible (Ma'sum). If it is the saying of an Infallible, it means that the Imam is saying something, and we say, 'No, we do not accept your word, your saying is weak.' Anyway, this proof is sufficient that Allamah Majlisi narrated this Hadith in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 26, and he said that his respected father—his father himself was a very great scholar of Hadith, Sheikh Muhammad Taqi Majlisi, and his... ...was a Muhaddith, Sheikh Muhammad Taqi Majlisi. One day Abu Dharr, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, came to Janab-e-Salman. Now, pay attention to the Hadith. 'Jundab' is used when you address someone younger, just as a father does not address his son by his kunya, right? And 'Abu Dharr' is used when addressing an elder, when a younger person addresses an elder. For example, if we address Janab-e-Abu Dharr, what will we say? 'O Aba Dharr, O Aba Dharr.' When we address him, we will not say 'O Jundab'. Just like you do not address your father inappropriately. A gentleman, in trying to speak Urdu, addressed his father inappropriately—it does not work like that. Learn Urdu well, then speak Urdu. You should speak Urdu, you should learn Urdu, but learn it first and then practice; do not practice while learning, especially with elders. Yes, elders are addressed respectfully. Anyway, 'O Jundab'—that is why I mentioned in the explanation that Hazrat Janab-e-Salman addressed Abu Dharr as a younger... ...brother, treating him as a younger brother, and is not calling him Abu Dharr here. He says, 'O Jundab, let us go so that we both can ask Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) ourselves.' We went, but we did not find him; we saw that Mawla was not there. So we waited for him until he arrived. 'By my life, by my life!'—Mawla is swearing an oath—'By my life, indeed this is a duty upon every believing man and believing woman.' How many of us know it? How many are familiar with it? We neither read it, nor do we have a desire to learn, nor any interest. It is obligatory upon men to tell women about these things. He has become an 'Arif (gnostic); he has reached the highest stage of Irfan (gnosis), a stage about which we... ...cannot even imagine. Now, who is the Master (a.s.) addressing? Think about this a little, brothers. You are not paying attention; if you were thinking, you wouldn't be sitting so silently. These are all Arabic terms. What can I say? To explain each of these, an entire sermon (Majlis) is required. Do you know what it means to become an 'Arif? Or 'Mustabsir'? One needs a whole sermon for this. 'Mustabsir' in Arabic means one who has insight. In Arabic, two words are used: [Wa alaykum assalam] one is 'Basar' (sight) and the other is 'Basirat' (insight). 'Basar' means physical sight—we see you, you see us, this is 'Basar'. Anyone with eyes who can see things has 'Basar'. And there is... ...and there is 'Basirat'. 'Basirat' is—just to give an example—not just that we see you or you see us, but when you look at us, you are able to assess our personality: how deep this person is, how genuine he is, how much truth there is in his words, and how much is not true, and other such aspects. In other words, 'Basirat' is—to put it in very simple terms—when a person sees with the light of Allah, that is called 'Basirat'. That is why it is mentioned in the narrations: 'Beware of the foresight (Firasat) of the believer, for he sees with the light of Allah.' He sees with the light of Allah. No one can deceive a believer. Once, in good faith, a believer might trust someone and get deceived; that is possible, generally speaking. But it is mentioned in the narrations that 'juhr' refers to a hole, like a mouse hole, or for example, any such... ...hole, or for example, a small animal that makes a small pit or hole, that is called a 'bil' (burrow/hole) in Urdu. Not the English word 'bill', but the Urdu word 'bil'. Now, when I say 'bil', people here might not even understand it. 'Bil' means a small pit—understand it in Mumbai slang if you will. In Urdu, a small pit is called a 'bil', alright? So, just as a person might stumble over it while walking, they say a believer is never stung from the same hole twice. If it happens once, that too because of trusting someone in good faith, that is a narration. He will never be deceived twice. Therefore, 'Mustabsir' is the one who has the special light of the Lord upon him. The light of the Lord. So here the Imam (a.s.) says, 'The Ma'rifat of this...' Now, pay attention to this. Now look, let's discuss word by word. 'Shakk' means doubt, and 'Murtab' is derived from 'Rayb' (doubt). You read the Quran, don't you? When you read the Quran, what is the very first verse of Surah al-Baqarah? 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alif Lam Mim. Dhalikal kitabu la rayba fih.' See, at least you remember one verse, Alhamdu lillah. Recite a Salawat... 'That is the Book.' It does not say, 'This is the Book.' ...'That is the Book.' It does not say, 'This is the Book.' If it were referring to the physical Quran, Allah should have said, 'This is the Book.' 'That is the Book'—'Dhalika' in Arabic means 'that'. You can ask any Arabic scholar what 'Dhalika' means. To anyone who knows Arabic, 'Hadha' means 'this' and 'Dhalika' means 'that'. This means it is talking about some other Book. Now, obviously, it is not talking about the Torah or the Gospel, nor do we want to name any other book, so it's not talking about that either, right? So, this means that it is talking about the 'Kitab-e-Mubeen' (the Manifest Book), Ameer al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). 'Dhalikal kitabu la rayba fih.' Here, the Master (a.s.) is saying that if someone is not aware of the Ma'rifat-e-Nooraniyyah, he is a victim of doubt. The disease of doubt is within him; he is afflicted with the disease of 'Rayb' (skepticism). 'Rayb' is found in him; he has no religion. If someone says—if you say this is the Quran, and if someone says, 'We have doubts about this Quran, we have doubts, we don't understand whether to believe in it or not'—would you call him a Muslim? You would not call him a Muslim. You would say he is not a Muslim at all. This is regarding the Quran... ...you would say he is not a Muslim at all. If this is the case regarding the Quran—when this is the case regarding the silent Quran (Quran-e-Samit), then what judgment will you pass regarding the speaking Quran (Quran-e-Natiq)? 'La rayba fih.' The Master (a.s.) says, 'He is a doubter and a skeptic (shakkun wa murtab). O Salman, O Jundab!' Both said, 'Labbayk ya Ameer al-Mu'minin!' This was the issue. The issue was this. That is why, in what I submitted to you yesterday as an introduction, and today as we came to the actual Ma'rifat bi-Nuraniyyah—if people only knew where this issue started. It started with Satan. When Satan argued, when he argued with Allah, 'I will not prostrate to Adam, I will not prostrate before Adam. Why? You created Adam from clay, and me from fire.' And Satan was a great philosopher too, wasn't he? He knew logic very well, tremendously. Satan was the first to use analogy (Qiyas). Before anyone else, the one who used analogy was Satan. He said, 'Khalaqtani min narin...'—'You created me from fire and created Adam from clay. I am better than Adam. I am superior, superior to Adam.' Satan refused. Did he speak the truth or falsehood? Tell me. Was this justification of Satan, this argument of Satan, correct? There is no doubt that fire is superior to clay; any wise person would say, 'Yes, that is correct, what did he say wrong?' But the Imam (a.s.) says, if Satan had known that our lights (Anwar) were in the loins of Adam—Haidari ya Ali!—Allah ordered the prostration because Allah wanted the prostration of respect to be for our lights. He could not have said otherwise. If prostrating to a clay statue is not polytheism (shirk), then how can prostrating to the Light (Noor) be polytheism? Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and his family. He (Satan) refused to prostrate. [Allah said,] 'Go away from here, indeed you are rejected (rajeem), you are accursed.' So it became known that the issue which started from the very first day was due to the lack of recognition (ma'rifat) of the Light. And that is why the calamities inflicted upon the Family of Muhammad (a.s.) were because people were unaware of their spiritual recognition (ma'rifat-e-noorani); they were kept away from the Hadith. ...they were not aware of the spiritual light, they were kept away from the Hadith. They were not acquainted; they did not even know who the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) were. They had no idea who the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) were. If they had been acquainted, if they had recognized them, if they had their recognition (ma'rifat), then no person possessing even a little intellect and understanding would ever accept the words of others, and would say, 'How can we bring anyone in comparison to those for whose sake the entire universe was created?' And this was the reason why allegiance (bay'ah) was demanded from the Chief of Martyrs (a.s.), and the Chief of Martyrs refused. Now the Chief of Martyrs, Imam Hussain (a.s.), understood that Medina was no longer a place to live. Now, coming to Medina, he said to Janabe Zainab (s.a.), 'Sister Zainab, Medina is no longer a place to live. Now we must leave Medina.' And the preparations began. Abdullah ibn Sinan says, 'I, Abdullah ibn Sinan al-Kufi, who was a resident of Kufa, say that when I reached Medina, it was the 28th of Rajab. I saw that there was an atmosphere of great grief in Medina; sadness was cast over everyone's face. I asked, what is the cause of this sadness?' People... ...asked, 'What is the cause of this sadness?' People said, 'Do you not know? Are you a traveler?' He said, 'I am a resident of Kufa.' So those people said, 'The soul of Medina is leaving Medina; Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) is leaving Medina.' Abdullah said, 'I thought, let me also see how the people of Medina bid farewell to Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). Now I came and stood outside the noble house, where a large crowd had gathered. Suddenly, I saw two young men come out of the noble house and push the crowd back, saying, "Move back, move back! The ladies are coming, the mount of the ladies is coming, the ladies are about to mount, move back!" They cleared everyone away. The mounts began to arrive. When one mount came, I saw a young boy of thirteen years; he helped a lady mount. I asked, "Who is this?" They said, "This is Qasim, the orphan of Hasan (a.s.); he is helping Umm Farwa mount." After a short while, what did I see? I saw another lady emerge, and another young man assisted her. I asked, "Who is this?" They said, "This is the likeness of the Prophet, Ali al-Akbar (a.s.), helping his mother Umm Layla mount." He helped Umm Layla mount. After a short while, another lady emerged—to keep the narration very brief—another lady emerged. I asked, "Who is this?" ...another lady emerged. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is Umm Kulthum, the younger daughter of Ali (a.s.) and Fatima (s.a.).' And who was helping her mount? They said, 'This is Abul Fazl al-Abbas (a.s.).' Until now, the ladies who were mounting, the revered ladies who were mounting, all the young men were busy with the arrangements, and Hussain (a.s.) was sitting on a chair in one place. Suddenly, when all the ladies had mounted, I saw—I saw that as soon as one lady emerged, Hussain (a.s.) stood up from his place. Someone held her arm, someone held the stirrup, someone... I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'Ali's eldest daughter, Zainab (s.a.).' I would say, O honorable youths of Bani Hashim, today you are all engaged in helping Zainab (s.a.) mount. Oh, if only you had come to Karbala on the 11th of Muharram and seen how Zainab (s.a.) was being whipped! Janabe Zainab (s.a.) mounted, the camels moved forward. Suddenly Hussain (a.s.) came forward and said, 'Abbas, bring my mount, Zuljanah...' ...forward and said, 'Abbas, bring my mount, bring my horse.' Abbas (a.s.) brought the Imam's horse and helped the Imam mount. Hussain (a.s.) mounted. I, folding both my hands, would say, 'O Master Abbas, today you have helped him mount with great respect. Oh, but come on the afternoon of Ashura, and see there when Hussain (a.s.) is all alone, and Hussain (a.s.) calls out, "Is there anyone among you who will bring my mount?"' It is not surprising that no answer came from the Euphrates, but my heart says that perhaps the soul of Abbas (a.s.) replied, 'O Master, death has made me helpless.' Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Who is there among you who will help me mount?' Zainab (s.a.) came out of the tent, 'Brother, Zainab is still alive, Zainab will help you mount.' Zainab (s.a.) helped Hussain (a.s.) mount on the afternoon of Ashura, 'Brother, farewell, I have fulfilled my duty. Now, when the time came to fall from the horse...' When it came to the point of falling, Fatima herself came... O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and companions. O Lord, alleviate the difficulties of those who are distressed. Help those who are in debt to pay off their debts. Grant righteous and pious offspring to those who are childless. Grant complete and speedy recovery to those who are sick. Return those who are away from their homeland safely. Wherever the Shias are in prisons, decree their release this very night. O Lord, protect the lives, wealth, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar (a.s.) wherever they are in the world. Protect them from the evil of their enemies. O Lord, protect the high scholars and religious authorities. O Lord, protect the sacred shrines. And those who are protecting them... ...protect them. Honor us with the visitation (Ziyarah) of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) in this world, and their intercession (Shafa'ah) in the Hereafter. Mourning for Husayn (a.s.).

title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Ke Nazdeek Duniyaawi Daulat Ki Qeemat | From Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz 2023
excerpt: This lecture recounts a profound incident involving Imam Hasan (a.s.) during his visit to Syria. When the ruler of Syria attempted to bribe or honor him with a vast treasure of jewels and wealth, the Imam showed complete indifference toward the material offering. Instead, he gifted the entire fortune to a servant who simply straightened his shoes, illustrating that the worldly wealth of a ruler holds less value than the footwear of the Imam.
content:
This is a very interesting incident. Once, when Imam Hasan (a.s.) went to Syria (Sham), upon his arrival, what did the ruler of Syria do? The ruler of Syria prepared a huge tray for Imam Hasan (a.s.) containing many things—diamonds, jewels, money, dinars, and dirhams—a very long list is mentioned in the narrations. He placed it before Imam Hasan (a.s.) and offered, 'All this wealth is for you, please accept it.' But Imam Hasan (a.s.) did not even turn to look at it. As he was about to leave, a servant stepped forward and straightened Imam Hasan's (a.s.) shoes (na'layn). He simply straightened the Imam's (a.s.) shoes. So, what did Imam Hasan (a.s.) do? All that wealth that was offered to Imam Hasan (a.s.)—that entire wealth and treasure—the Imam gave to the one who straightened his shoes. In other words, what is the actual value of all that immense wealth of the ruler of Syria? It is not even equal to the shoes of Imam Hasan (a.s.).

excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive analysis of the Khutba-e-Ghadir, focusing on the divine appointment and supreme status of Imam Ali (a.s.). It explores the theological necessity of Wilayah, the inseparability of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, and the spiritual consequences of rejecting this leadership. The session emphasizes that the perfection of religion is intrinsically linked to the acceptance of Imam Ali's authority as the successor to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).
content:
Hadith of the Prophet, the light of God, the Prophet of Khuda... Ali is the proof of God... Ali is the sign... O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjat, son of Al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until... until You make him reside on Your earth.
