But those whose names did not appear in today's winners or if an episode was missed, there is no need to be disappointed, because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the winner of the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those... who have given correct answers to all questions in all episodes. That is, even if someone was not among the daily winners but gave correct answers in all episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. This matter is very clear from this phrase... Imam Mahdi (a.s.)'s Mahdawiyat, his Imamate, and those who are skeptical about his occultation, how he is, where he is—it is clear from this phrase that the Quran is present today, in this era. So the heir of that Quran, its teacher, its instructor, the Qayyum of the Quran, he must also be present. The greatest responsibility of every Shia should be to give priority to Ali (a.s.) in all their affairs, otherwise, be prepared for this curse of the Messenger of God: 'May Allah abandon you.' So, if there is anything we should consider the most important in our lives, it is the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.). A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. First of all, on behalf of the entire TSR team, we present our congratulations to all the Momineen on the occasion of Eid-e-Ghadir, Eid-e-Akbar, with a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Respected audience, a few things need to be presented regarding Ghadir, and especially that part of the Khutbah-e-Ghadir in which the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) spoke the most about the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in the field of Ghadir. And because time is very short and there are many points to present, we move directly to our topic: what things the Messenger of God said in that field and what he explained to the Muslim Ummah regarding the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). First, the things the Messenger of God presented regarding the virtues of Ali (a.s.), we want to present the first phrase here, in which he says: 'Ma'ashar-an-nas, faddilu Aliyan' (O people, give preference to Ali), 'innahu afdalu ba'di min zakarin wa untha' (because he will be the most virtuous among men and women after me). Now, two words are coming here: 'fazl'... will be. Now, two words are appearing here: 'faza' and 'ba'di', and both words are pointing towards the Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.). The word 'ba'di' clarifies that the chain of Prophethood is coming to an end here. And since this chain of Prophethood is concluding, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is introducing his successor in that field, saying that if there is anyone who is the best and most excellent person in the Muslim Ummah after me, then it is he whom I am going to introduce to you. And he stated that Ali (a.s.) is the most excellent. And after that, he also mentioned 'afzal-un-nas', and the meaning of 'afzal-un-nas' here proves the superiority of Ali (a.s.) among all humans. And this excellence is not restricted to any specific task or time, as if he were trying to prove the excellence of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) only in relation to a certain task. For example, in the battlefield, the bravery of Ali (a.s.) is the most excellent, or in the field of generosity, Ali (a.s.) is the most excellent—no, in a general sense, in every field, in every field of excellence, the Commander of the Faithful is the most excellent of people. So, it was not restricted to any... So, it was not restricted to any one task or any one time that the Messenger of Allah stated here; rather, he uttered a comprehensive sentence. The Messenger of Allah said, 'afzal-un-nas-i ba'di'—among all men and all women, if there is anyone who is the most excellent person, then it is my brother, my Wasi, my successor, this Ali. And after that, he stated, 'bima anzala Allahu'—he is uttering a strange sentence, that immediately after the excellence of Ali (a.s.), he is telling the Muslim Ummah that all the sustenance (rizq) you receive is being granted to you because of our existence. Which we also see in the phrases of supplications, like if you look at Dua-e-Adila, we keep reading in it: 'bi-baqa'ihi baqiyat-ud-dunya'—that O Mawla, because of your survival, this world remains. 'Wa bi-yumnihi ruziqal-wara'—and O Mawla, by the blessing of your existence, we are receiving sustenance. 'Wujudihi sabab-us-sama'—and because of your presence, this earth and sky are established. So here, the Messenger of Allah, immediately after the excellence of the Commander of the Faithful, is presenting a sentence to the Muslim Ummah regarding sustenance, that because of us you receive sustenance. But not just grain and water, rather all sustenance—you read Dua-e-Tawfiq, in which 'Allahumma tawfiq...' and all those sentences that are coming in it, they are... they are pointing towards that sustenance. Right? Right? So, sustenance is not just money, wealth, or riches, but all the things that a human consumes, which is his spiritual food and physical food, all these things fall into the category of sustenance. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) immediately says after that, 'wa bi-hi baqiyal-khalq'—and because of us, the existence of the creation remains. O my followers, O my lovers, in the field of Ghadir, I am telling you that because of me, and because of my brother Ali (a.s.), and because of their children, you remain. After that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) moves to the second phrase, which is a very terrifying phrase, that immediately after this sentence, the Messenger of Allah states, 'mal'un, mal'un, maghdubun, majnun'—that the Messenger of Allah cursed, called him accursed, called him one upon whom wrath has descended, and then said that whoever rejects this statement of mine—meaning the excellence of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) that I am talking about, or the sustenance I am talking about, or the survival of the world I am talking about—if this statement of mine is rejected, then he is the most accursed person, and the wrath of Allah will descend upon him, whoever rejects these words of mine, 'wa man lam yuwafiq'—and whoever does not agree with it, he is accursed. And then after that, the Messenger of Allah... he is accursed. And then after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) does not stop there; he confirms it through the news of Jibra'il (a.s.) and says that Jibra'il (a.s.) informed me that Allah (t.b.t.) is stating that whoever 'man ada Aliyan'—so the word 'ada' (enmity) is coming here, and then the word 'lam yatawallahu' is coming. Right? Meaning, whoever shows enmity towards Ali (a.s.) outwardly, he is also deserving of a curse. And whoever denies the Wilayah, even if outward enmity is not being shown—meaning he is not showing outward enmity, but in his heart, he is denying the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Right? So, whoever denies it in his heart and whoever shows outward enmity, both are under the curse of God. 'La'nati wa ghadabi'—so here, the Messenger of Allah presented the message of Jibra'il (a.s.) to the Muslim Ummah that I am not just saying this, but Allah is sending this message through Jibra'il (a.s.) that whoever shows enmity towards Ali (a.s.), whether outwardly or inwardly, in both ways he will be deserving of a curse and will be a victim of Allah's wrath. Now, respected listeners, the two phrases I presented to you, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated the excellence of Ali (a.s.) to the Muslim Ummah, and then he also said that whoever... and then he also said that whoever rejects this statement of mine will be deserving of a curse and my wrath, deserving of Allah's wrath. Now, immediately after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) presents this verse of the Quran to the Muslim Ummah: 'Faltanzur nafsun ma qaddamat li-ghadin'—that every person should see what he has sent for tomorrow, i.e., the Hereafter, and fear Allah. Meaning, here every person should take account and review his deeds, what he is sending for the Hereafter. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is also stating the fear of Allah, that fear Allah regarding 'an tukhalifu'—lest you oppose Ali (a.s.). Right? So, the fear of Allah should be within you. If you oppose Ali (a.s.), then you should fear Allah. And then after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) presents the next sentence to the Muslim Ummah. It is: 'Fatazilla qadamun ba'da thubutiha'—lest your feet slip after they were firm. Meaning, this is a metaphor; intentional misguidance is being talked about, that you should not intentionally go towards misguidance while you were firm before, understanding the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). But you turned your face away from the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), so lest you go astray. Here, the Messenger of Allah is pointing towards this... is pointing towards this. And this is a metaphor, in a way, that beware, do not go astray regarding the Imamate of Ali (a.s.). And then after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) again presents a sentence or a phrase from the Quran: 'Inna Allaha khabirun bima ta'malun'—that indeed Allah is aware of all your deeds. And after that, he is again presenting this phrase to the Muslim Ummah regarding the excellence of Ali (a.s.): 'Ma'asharan-nas, innahu janbullahi alladhi nazala fi kitabihi, ya hasrata 'ala ma farrattu fi janbilla'—O people, pointing towards the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), the Messenger of Allah is stating this. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is stating that Ali (a.s.) is the 'Janbullah' (the side/proximity of Allah), and regarding whom He has revealed in His Book. What has He revealed? Now, the Messenger of Allah quotes the verse of the Quran: 'Ya hasrata'—O regret, when people reach the field of Judgment, they will say with regret, 'ala ma farrattu fi janbilla'—that I was negligent regarding the side of Allah. This is a sentence from the 56th verse of Surah Az-Zumar, in which this person who will be—the negligent ones, those who are negligent regarding the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), those who have abandoned the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), those who have turned their faces away from his obedience, those... those who have turned their faces away from his obedience, those who have not recognized his status, everything is coming under 'tafritu fi janbilla'. After that, here again, the Messenger of Allah is encouraging his Ummah: 'Ma'asharan-nas', now he is encouraging them through the Quran, 'tadabbaru al-Qur'ana wa ayatihi wa muhkamatihi wa la tattabi'u mutashabihi'—O people, reflect on the Quran, understand its verses, look towards its 'muhkamat' (clear and definitive commands), and do not follow the 'mutashabihat' (ambiguous verses). Here, the Messenger of Allah is emphasizing four things to the Muslim Ummah regarding the Quran: 'Tadabbur'—reflect deeply on it; 'Fahm'—understand it; reflect and think upon it; pay attention to the 'muhkamat'; and do not act upon the 'mutashabihat' on your own. Now, in this connection, I want to present another Hadith for your clarification, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has stated: 'Laisa ashadda quluban... tafsir al-Qur'an'—that there is nothing more distant and hidden from human hearts or human intellects than the interpretation of the Quran. 'Wa fi dhalika khala'iqu ajma'un'—for this reason, all the creation is bewildered regarding the interpretation of the Quran. They are in a state of confusion. And then after that, the Messenger of Allah says, 'illa man sha'a Allah'—except those whom Allah willed. except those whom Allah willed, that they should not be bewildered. Now look, on one hand, he is encouraging them towards Ali (a.s.), and on the other hand, he is encouraging them towards the Quran, that the Quran is such a book that no individual of the Muslim Ummah can understand its reality regarding its interpretation. So, it is obvious that just as the Quran is, in the same way, Ali (a.s.) or other members of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) should also be. So, if the entire Muslim Ummah is bewildered regarding the interpretation of the Quran or regarding understanding the Quran, then the Muslim Ummah should also be bewildered regarding understanding the reality of Ali (a.s.). And my Mawla was saying from the pulpit of Kufa: 'Saluni qabla an tafqiduni'—that a flood of knowledge is flowing from my chest, and the bird of intellect does not have enough strength to understand the reality of Ali. So here you see that on one hand, the reality of the Quran cannot be understood; human intellect cannot understand the interpretation of the Quran, cannot grasp it. In the same way, Ali (a.s.) is also stating that you cannot understand my reality either. Your intellects cannot reach that far, what the reality of Ali (a.s.) is. So here, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is encouraging people to reflect on the Quran, to understand it. Look... to reflect on the Quran, to understand it. Look towards the 'muhkamat' verses, and do not act upon the 'mutashabihat' verses on your own. Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Fawallahi'—and by Allah, here the Messenger of Allah is seen taking an oath, 'lam yubayyin lakum tafsirahu'—that the things that stop you from the Quran have not been clarified to you, and then he says, 'wa la yubayyin lakum tafsirahu'—and its interpretation will not be explained to you, and then after that, he states, 'illa 'ala alladhi ana akhidhu bi-yadihi'—except for this person whose hand I have held. Meaning, if anyone can explain the Quran after me, then it is only and only the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And then after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) lifts his arm and states, 'wa ukhbirukum'—that I am telling you that he will give you the knowledge of the Quran—meaning, pointing towards Ali (a.s.), he is saying that he is the only person in this Ummah, in this Muslim Ummah, after me, who will clarify things to you regarding the knowledge of the Quran. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'wa ukhbirukum'—and I am informing you of this, 'man kuntu mawlahu fa-Aliyun mawlahu'—that of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla. And then he stated... this Ali is his Mawla. And then he stated, 'wa Aliyun ibnu Abi Talib (a.s.) akhi wa wasiyyi'—and this brother of mine, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), is my brother and my Wasi. And then he stated, 'wa muwalatuhu wa wilayatuhu anzala Allahu 'alayya'—and the command for his 'muwalat' (friendship) and his 'wilayah' (guardianship) has been revealed to me by Allah. Meaning, here the Messenger of Allah is repeatedly saying that this announcement I am making is 'mansus min Allah' (ordained by Allah). It is not that I am making this announcement or presenting this announcement to you people out of my own love for Ali (a.s.). No, this is 'mansus min Allah', this is Allah's order, Jibra'il (a.s.) is bringing this message. Repeatedly within his sermon, the Messenger of Allah is emphasizing this point. Right? After that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) mentions the 'Thaqalayn'. He is mentioning the Hadith al-Thaqalayn here, that 'Ma'asharan-nas'—O people, 'inna Aliyan wa tayyiba min wuldi al-asghar wa al-Qur'an al-akbar'—O people, he did not just mention Ali (a.s.) here, but here he also mentioned the remaining 11 Imams to the Muslim Ummah, 'wa tayyiba min wuldi'—that my progeny who are pure and clean, who are 'tayyib'—meaning these 11 Imams who are to come after the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), he is also mentioning them here, that they are... He is stating, 'What is this Thiqal al-Asghar (the lesser weight)?' What is this? This is also a part of the Thaqalayn (the two weights). That 11 is also a part of the Thaqalayn, and then the Quran. Okay, now I want to draw your attention to one point here. The term 'Thiqal al-Asghar' or 'Thiqal al-Akbar' here does not imply 'greater' or 'smaller' in terms of status. Rather, since the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) mentioned the Hadith al-Thaqalayn in many places—'Inni tarikun feekum al-thaqalayn: Kitab Allah wa itrati'—the first thing he mentioned was the Book of Allah. Because it was mentioned first, it is the 'Thiqal al-Akbar' (the greater weight), and because his Itrah (progeny) was mentioned after it, it is the 'Thiqal al-Asghar' (the lesser weight). Furthermore, the Messenger of Allah has stated in many hadiths, narrated through various chains—and it has reached us in a mutawatir (consecutive) manner, presented to the Muslim Ummah—that the Messenger of Allah repeatedly said that both the Book of Allah (the Quran) and my Itrah (Ahlulbayt) are equal. Both are from Allah. With a gesture of his finger, the Messenger of Allah showed the Muslim Ummah that both are from Allah. It is not that the Quran is superior and greater, and my Itrah is smaller, or that the Itrah is greater and the Quran is smaller. No, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) declared both to be from Allah. He declared both to be from Allah, and then he stated, 'Wa kullu wahidin munabbi'un 'an sahibih' (and each one of them informs about the other). This means the first points towards the second; the Quran points towards the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and shows that these Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the guides, and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) present the interpretation of the Quran to the world, confirming that this is the Word of Allah. So, both will come pointing towards each other. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Wa muwafiqun lahu' (and they are in agreement with each other). It is not that the Book of the Messenger says one thing and my Ahlulbayt will say something else. No, both will remain in agreement. And then he states, 'Lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayya al-hawd' (they will never separate from each other until they meet me at the Pond). This means as long as the Quran is present in this Muslim Ummah, it is necessary that a member of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) must also be present in this Ummah. This fact is made clear by this phrase. Regarding the Mahdawiyyah of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), his Imamate, and those who are skeptical about his occultation—asking how he is or where he is—this phrase clarifies that since the Quran is present today, in this era, then the heir of that Quran, its teacher, its instructor, the Qayyum al-Quran (the Sustainer of the Quran), must also be present. Then the heir of that Quran, its teacher, its instructor, the one who teaches it, the Qayyum al-Quran, must also be present. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Ala innahum umanau Allah fi khalqihi' (Be aware, O my Ummah, these people, meaning the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), are the trustees of Allah among all His creation). And then he states, 'Wa hukkamuhu fi ardihi' (and they are His rulers upon this earth). Here, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is establishing the proof (hujjah) of the Imam, and he is stating, 'Ala hal ballaghtu? Ala hal ballaghtu? Ala hal ballaghtu?' (Be aware, O my Ummah, have I conveyed the message? Have I fulfilled it? Listen, I have fulfilled the duty of tabligh (conveyance). Be warned, I have made you hear). This means he has conveyed the message regarding the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and know that I have clarified everything before you. 'Ala wa qad awda'tu' (Be aware, I have deposited/presented everything that will come before you after me). I have presented all the things that will come before you after me, how you are to live your lives. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Ala wa innallaha 'azza wa jalla qala' (Be aware, and surely Allah the Almighty has said), and I am saying... Allah the Almighty has said, and what I am saying, I am saying from Allah. Again, he is pointing towards the same thing. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is saying, 'I am not saying this from myself, but it is ordained by Allah.' This message of the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) that I am conveying at Ghadir, and in all the places before this where I was seen propagating for Ali (a.s.)—from the beginning to Ghadir, in all the places where I was introducing Ali (a.s.) and telling you who my Wasi (successor), my heir, and my Caliph would be after me—it was not my personal decision, but it was ordained by Allah. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is repeatedly emphasizing this. And then he points towards this special title of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), which is exclusively attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), meaning Ali (a.s.). 'Ala innahu laysa amir al-mu'minin ghayru hadha' (Be aware, there is no Amir al-Mu'minin other than this brother of mine). Now, if you call someone else Amir al-Mu'minin in any era, then what are you doing? You are opposing my declaration. You are opposing Allah's declaration. You are opposing the command that is beloved to Allah, or... The command that is beloved to Allah, or the beloved title that is attributed to Ali (a.s.). And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Wa la tahillu imrati ba'di li ahadin ghayrihi' (And this title is not lawful for anyone after me except for this brother of mine). This means he has made this title exclusive. And in our traditions, it is found that this title cannot be used for any other Imam. A person asked, 'When your last descendant comes...'—generally, it was asked to the sixth Imam, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.)—'Can we call your last descendant by the title of Amir al-Mu'minin?' Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) forbade it and said, 'No, Amir al-Mu'minin is exclusively for Ali (a.s.).' So, the one who is to come should be called Baqiyatullah. Now, after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) placed his hand on the arm of Ali (a.s.) and raised his hand. And when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself was on the pulpit, Ali (a.s.) was present one step below. So, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) took the hand of Ali (a.s.) and raised it, and Ali (a.s.) brought his hand to the blessed face of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) raised Ali (a.s.) so high, so high, that the blessed feet of Ali (a.s.) reached the level of the knees of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). It means he raised him to a great height. It wasn't just that he raised his hands; he actually raised him so that the feet of Ali (a.s.) reached the level of the knees of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'Hadha 'Aliyyun Wasiyyi' (This is Ali, my brother and my Wasi), introducing him again. 'Wa khazin 'ilmi' (And the one who holds the treasure of my knowledge is this person). And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Wa khalifati 'ala ummati' (And if there is any Caliph over my Ummah, it is him). And then he states, 'Wa 'ala tafsir Kitab Allah 'azza wa jalla' (And if anyone is responsible for the interpretation of the Book of Allah, it is this brother of mine). And then he states, 'Wa al-da'i ila Allah' (And he is the one who calls to Allah). And then he states, 'Wa al-'amilu bima yarzahu' (And he is the one who acts according to what pleases Allah). And then he states, 'Wa al-muharibu li a'da'ihi' (And if there was, is, or will be anyone who fights the enemies of Allah, it is this brother of mine). And after that, he states, 'Wa al-muwali 'ala...' After that, he states, 'Wa al-muwali 'ala ta'atihi' (And the one who is most loyal in His obedience and the one who does not disobey Him is my brother). After that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Khalifatu Rasulillah (s.a.w.a.) wa Amir al-Mu'minin wa al-Imam al-Hadi' (The Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, the Commander of the Faithful, and the Guiding Imam). And after that, he states, 'Wa qatilu al-nakithin wa al-qasitin wa al-mariqin' (And he is the fighter of the Nakithin, Qasitin, and Mariqin). This means those who broke the allegiance, who will fight them? Ali (a.s.) will fight them. And those who are oppressors (al-qasitin)—what is meant by al-qasitin here? The oppressors. So, who will fight the oppressors? My brother will. And the Mariqin (those who deviated)—if anyone fights those who went out of the religion, by the command of Allah, it will be my brother. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'Aqulu ma qultu 'an amri Rabbi' (I am saying what I am saying by the command of my Lord). I am stating that I do not have the authority to change this matter. This means the Wilayah that I am introducing, this message that I am conveying, I cannot change it. I have no authority in this. All of this is from my Lord... I have no authority. All of this is by the command of my Lord. If you look at every phrase, dear viewers, the Messenger of Allah is drawing attention, pointing out that these things I am conveying are from Allah. I am not committing any betrayal in this. So, beware, do not cause corruption regarding my position after me, do not cause corruption regarding my succession, do not seat anyone else in the place of Ali (a.s.) after me, do not seat anyone else in my place. Now, after this, viewers, I present to you the last phrase of this part of the sermon, which is the Du'a of Ghadir, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Allahumma wali man walahu wa 'adi man 'adahu' (O Allah, befriend those who consider Ali (a.s.) their Wali, those who acknowledge the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and be an enemy to those who are enemies to Ali (a.s.)). This means here the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is not only announcing Wilayah but also announcing Bara'ah (disassociation). Within this sermon of Ghadir, I want to present one phrase that comes in the second part, where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Ma shar al-nas, innahu sayakun ba'di a'immatan' (O people, there will be some leaders after me)... There will be some leaders after me. This means immediately after me, some people will come. He is pointing towards that too. 'Yad'una ila al-nar' (They will invite to the Fire), 'Wa yawm al-qiyamati la yunsarun' (And on the Day of Judgment, they will not be helped). 'Ma shar al-nas, innallaha wa ana bari'un minhum' (O people, surely Allah and I are free and disassociated from all those people; we have no responsibility regarding them). And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Ma shar al-nas, inna... wa ansaruhum' (O people, those who usurp the Caliphate of Ali (a.s.), if anyone does so, and their helpers, supporters, followers, and those who follow them and agree with them, 'fahum fi dark al-asfal min al-nar' (they will be in the lowest part of the Fire/Hell)). This means here the Messenger of Allah is warning. He is not just conveying Wilayah, but also warning people about Bara'ah and enmity towards Ali (a.s.), saying, 'Beware, let no one show enmity towards Ali (a.s.). If anyone shows enmity towards Ali (a.s.), their abode will be the lowest part of Hell.' Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Wa la'ana Allahu man jahadahu' (And may the curse of Allah be upon the one who denies Ali), 'Wa ghadiba Allahu 'ala man jahada haqqahu' (And may the wrath of Allah be upon the one who denies his right)... May the wrath of Allah be upon the one who denies his right. The one who denies his right—here the Messenger of Allah is sending curses and praying to Allah. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is one whose prayers are answered (mustajab al-da'wat). This means if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has prayed something in the court of Allah, it is impossible for Allah not to accept his prayer. So, if the Messenger of Allah is saying here, 'Whoever considers Ali his Wali, O Allah, You also befriend him, and whoever is an enemy to Ali, O Allah, You be an enemy to him,' and then in the second part, if you look at the different parts of the Du'a of Ghadir, what is there? 'Wansur man nasarahu' (O Allah, help the one who helps Ali), meaning help him in the world, in every worldly matter, in every religious matter, help the one who is loyal to Ali. 'Wakhdhul man khadhalahu' (And O Allah, abandon the one who abandons Ali). This means if someone does not give preference to Ali (a.s.) in their life, does not give importance to his Wilayah in their life, then O Lord, abandon him to his state. This means our greatest responsibility, the responsibility of every Shia, of every follower, should be to give the highest importance to Ali (a.s.) in all their affairs, otherwise the Messenger... Give the utmost importance to these matters, otherwise, be prepared for the curse of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—'Wul-man jafa'—that Allah may abandon those who do not show loyalty to Ali (a.s.). And Allah does not accept any deeds of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) if he had not conveyed the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) at the plain of Ghadir. If there is anything in our lives that we should consider the most important, it is to understand the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). The propagation of his loyalty and his Imamate is our core; this is what we must prioritize above all else. And then, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Allahumma innaka anzalta alayya annal-imamata Ali-yun wali'—O Allah, You revealed to me regarding the Imamate of Ali (a.s.) that he is Your Wali. 'Idha tibyani dhalika al-ahd'—and when I declared and manifested this to the people, 'wa nasabi iyyahu'—and I appointed Ali (a.s.) and established his Imamate before the people, 'bima akmalta li-ibadika dini'—it was because You had perfected the religion for Your servants. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'wa tamammta ala ni'matika wa' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'wa tamammta ala ni'matika wa radhita al-Islama dina'—and You completed Your blessings upon them and chose Islam as a religion for them. And then, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) presented this verse of the Quran, saying, 'wa man yabtaghi ghayra al-Islami dina'—and whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, 'falan yuqbala minhu'—it will not be accepted from him, 'wa huwa fil-akhirati minal-khasirin'—and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter. Meaning, if any person follows someone other than Ali (a.s.), then no matter how hard they try or how many deeds they perform, Allah will not accept any of those deeds. If a person wants their deeds to be accepted, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has indicated the straightest path here, and the only path is to accept the Wilayah and Imamate of Ali (a.s.). If they do not do this, Allah will render all their deeds void. And respected audience, this was the part of the sermon that was the longest. And you saw in this sermon that from the very beginning to the very end, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) From the beginning to the end, the things the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) emphasized the most to the people were the virtues of Ali (a.s.). This was the longest part of the sermon, and the most frequent mention was regarding the virtues of Ali (a.s.). So, respected audience, we also need to realize that these are the days of Ghadir. Therefore, it is our responsibility to propagate the virtues of Ali (a.s.) and convey the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to the people, just as the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) conveyed them at the plain of Ghadir. Come, viewers, let us conclude this program with this prayer: Alhamdulillah, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Assalamu alaika ya amina Allahi fi ardihi wa hujjatahu ala ibadihi, assalamu alaika ya Amir al-Mu'minin, ashhadu annaka jahadta I bear witness that you strove with the striving due to Him, and followed the Sunnah of His Prophet (s.a.w.a.), until Allah called you to His neighborhood, and He chose you to be the proof over all His creation, and He made you the master over yourself, capable of patience, and a lover of the friends of Allah, beloved in His sight, and a listener to His command... A seeker of His pleasure, a practitioner of His piety, a day of reward, a follower of the Sunnah of the friends of Allah, a refiner of character, a renouncer of the world... [prayers continue]... and the doors of His guidance are open, and the path is clear. And the path is clear, the one who seeks your help, the one who seeks your intercession, the one who seeks your refuge, the one who is your servant, the one who is your follower, the one who is your beloved, and the one who hopes for your intercession in the eternal abode... And we ask for your intercession, and we gather with your friends, and we follow Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn. You are our Wali and our guide, and our love for you is in our hearts... and you are our guide to the friends of Allah, and our protection against the enemies... Against the enemies, and the word of piety, and the firmest handle, and Allah is capable of all things. And may Allah bless Muhammad, the master of the messengers, and his pure and purified progeny. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, respected viewers. Imam Ali (a.s.) is the most excellent human being after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the only rightful Amir al-Mu'minin.
The sustenance of the universe and the acceptance of religious deeds are dependent upon the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt.
The Quran and the Ahlulbayt are inseparable, with the Imam serving as the only divinely appointed interpreter of the Quran.
The Ghadir sermon establishes both the affirmation of Wilayah and the necessity of Bara'ah (disassociation from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt).
Rejecting the leadership of Imam Ali (a.s.) leads to spiritual misguidance and divine wrath.
Believers have a religious duty to propagate the virtues of Imam Ali (a.s.) to the world.
The perfection of Islam was finalized through the public proclamation of Ali's Imamate at Ghadir Khumm.

title: Who are the Batris?  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explains the historical and linguistic origins of the 'Batriyya' sect during the time of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.). The term 'Batri' is derived from the Arabic word 'Abtar', meaning cut off or incomplete, and was used to describe those who held contradictory allegiances. The lecture highlights the Imam's condemnation of individuals who claimed to love the Ahlulbayt while simultaneously maintaining affection for the enemies of Imam Ali (a.s.).
content:
At that time, a new sect had started called the 'Batriyya'. This sect did not consist of entirely new people; they were from the previous ones, and this name became associated with them. Why was this name given? What does 'Batri' mean? It is very important to understand this. 'Batri' comes from 'Abtar' (cut off), and its meanings are Arabic. For instance, someone whose foundation is weak... and 'Abtar' is famously used for a man who has no offspring, he is called 'Abtar'. Or an animal whose tail is cut off is also called 'Abtar'. Such are the meanings. But these people... who gave them this name? In the era of Imam Baqir (a.s.), some people came before him and said, 'We love you, and we love those who love you...' ...and we love those who love us. And regarding those who are the enemies of Ali (a.s.), we love them too, and we also love their enemies. Well, if you love Ali (a.s.) and also love his enemies, what does that mean? The Imam said, 'You are Batri (cut off).' He told them, 'You have cut off your own faith. May Allah cut you off in the same way.' The Imam then remained silent. This is how they got the name 'Batri' or 'Batriyya'. Anyway, this... I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
The term 'Batri' is derived from the Arabic word 'Abtar', meaning cut off or incomplete.
Historically, 'Abtar' refers to someone without offspring or an animal with a severed tail.

The sect was characterized by a contradictory belief system of loving both the Ahlulbayt and their enemies.
Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) explicitly rejected this group, stating they had cut off their own faith.
The name 'Batri' serves as a theological warning against compromising one's allegiance to the truth.

title: Qibla Kyun Badla Gaya?
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and spiritual significance of the change of the Qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah. Citing Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), the speaker explains that the change was a divine test designed to distinguish true followers of the Prophet from those driven by personal desires. The talk emphasizes the necessity of prioritizing divine commands over human inclinations to achieve true submission to Allah.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless him and his family. We all know that before the Khana-e-Ka'bah, the first Qibla (Qibla-e-Awwal) of the Muslims was Bayt al-Maqdis, which we also know as Bayt al-Muqaddas. Just as today Muslims pray facing the Khana-e-Ka'bah, before the Ka'bah, Muslims used to pray facing towards Bayt al-Maqdis. So why did the Lord of the worlds change that previous Qibla of the Muslims and make the Khana-e-Ka'bah the Qibla of the Muslims? And if it had to be changed, why did Allah make Bayt al-Maqdis [the Qibla in the first place]? When this very question was asked to our 11th Imam, Hazrat Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), the Imam (a.s.) replied by first reciting the 143rd verse of Surah al-Baqarah from the Holy Quran, which says: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa ma ja'alnal-qiblatallati kunta 'alayha illa lina'lama may-yattabi'ur-Rasula mimman yaqalibu 'ala 'aqibayh...' (And We did not make the Qibla which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger...) ...except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. The Imam (a.s.) stated that the people of Mecca wanted to worship facing the Khana-e-Ka'bah, but Allah, contrary to their desires, commanded them to pray facing towards Bayt al-Maqdis. Similarly, the people of Medina wished to worship facing Bayt al-Maqdis, so Allah, contrary to their desires, commanded them to pray facing the Khana-e-Ka'bah. And this was done so that it would become clear who follows their own desires and wishes, and who, without giving preference to their own desires, obeys the commands of the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And then, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) recited the next part of this verse, saying: 'Wa in kanat lakabiratan illa 'alalladhina hadallah' (And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah guided). Indeed, this change of Qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Khana-e-Ka'bah was very difficult for those who followed their own desires. It was very difficult for those who followed their own desires, compared to those who only followed their Prophet. Now, the point that becomes clear to all of us from this narration is that if we want to act as true servants of God, want to submit ourselves before God, and want to follow and obey the Messenger of God, Hazrat Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), then we must never prefer our own desires over the command of Allah and His Prophet, but rather sacrifice our desires for the command of God and the Messenger. May the Lord of the worlds hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and may Allah grant us the grace to be among his helpers and companions, and grant us the passion and ability to sacrifice our desires for all his commands. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds.

excerpt: This lecture, part of the Khamsa-e-Majaalis series, explores the profound spiritual significance of Wudu and its role as a fortress for the believer. The speaker emphasizes the necessity of lifelong learning, humility, and the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt. Through the lens of Karbala and the sacrifice of Ali Asghar, the discourse highlights the importance of maintaining sincerity, performing prayers on time, and upholding justice in all aspects of life. The session concludes with reflections on spiritual nourishment, the virtues of Namaz-e-Shab, and the dangers of arrogance.
content:
Mother used to say, clinging to the swinging cradle, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar. Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' The tyrant took you out of the grave in such a way, oh, when the spear pierced your chest, son. Seeing your corpse, Akbar's head said, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Mother used to say, clinging to the swinging cradle, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Oh, if I could find your killer, I would ask him myself, tell me, what was the crime of a six-month-old child? He didn't even call me mother, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' That scene still does not leave my eyes, blood kept dripping from your neck, son. I couldn't even tie a handkerchief around your throat, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Oh, the arrow with which they bring down a camel to the ground, that arrow struck your tiny throat. You kept spitting blood while clinging to your father, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Oh, you have died, she still does not believe this, she insists, 'I will feed my brother water.' That tyrant is standing in the battlefield for your sake, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Oh, the oppressor has slapped Sakina, like Ghazi, she cannot bear to see you either. You are crying with closed eyes on the tip of the spear, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Oh, I was helpless, there was no water in the house, otherwise, I would have washed this beautiful face. Do not complain to your grandmother when you go, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Oh, is that why you drop your head from the spear, perhaps you want to come into my lap, son? But my hands are tied, I cannot lift them, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' Mother used to say, clinging to the swinging cradle, 'Alas, alas, Ali Asghar.' May Allah have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; the best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome belongs to the people of piety and certainty. May peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. May peace be upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Especially, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, the Imam of our time, the Master of our affair, our Master, and our Mawla. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their relief, and curse their enemies. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says in this hadith: 'He lies who claims that he knows us, that he has our recognition (marifah), that he knows us, but he holds onto the rope of others.' Meaning, he does not come to us to acquire knowledge, he does not attend our threshold, but goes to the thresholds of others and asks from others. He leaves our threshold and goes to the thresholds of others. Whereas the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had clearly stated that I am leaving behind two weighty things among you: one is the Book of Allah and the other is my Ahlulbayt. As long as you hold onto them, you will remain on the straight path. 'Indeed, as long as you hold onto them, you will never go astray after me, for they will never separate until they return to me at the Pond (Hawd).' And this Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Pond of Kawthar. Meaning, until the Day of Judgment, they will be together; the Quran and the Ahlulbayt will remain with each other. So, if someone is a Shia, they will neither leave the Quran nor the Ahlulbayt. One cannot be a Shia who says that we only believe in the Ahlulbayt but do not read the Quran, are not familiar with the Quran, and are not acquainted with the Quran. That is simply impossible. Because the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'For they will never separate,' and what is the phrase in the hadith? It is written in the hadith that the Prophet said these two will be joined together like this. They will never be separated from each other; they will be perfectly joined. So, if a person holds onto one, then surely the other will also be with them. It is impossible that one remains with one and the other is not there. This is impossible. So, one cannot be a Shia who does not know how to recite the Quran, who does not know the rules of Quranic recitation, who does not know the etiquette of the Quran, who is not familiar with the interpretation (tafsir) of the Quran. Meaning, one must take both together to hold onto the Quran and the Itrat (progeny). And this is the means of salvation; there is no other means of salvation besides this. Now, before moving forward, let me present a point to you, and that is that regarding these things, especially regarding the Quran and the sciences of the family of Muhammad (a.s.), it is not like that. Meaning, regarding the hadith of the family of Muhammad as well, but especially regarding the Quran, what we have seen and experienced with our own eyes is that there are many people who waste their youth in such a way that they do not know how to read the Quran. But when they realize at a certain age that they do not know how to read the Quran, and if someone says, 'Learn it now,' they say, 'Is this an age to learn? What will I learn now? What kind of Muslim will I be in my final days?' You will not be a 'useless' Muslim; even in your final days, if you become one, then become one. Otherwise, if you die in a state of disbelief, you will face severe punishment. Therefore, it is better that whenever you realize, 'When you wake up, it is morning.' And one should never feel ashamed in this, that 'I will not learn from this person, how should I learn from them? This is just a child in front of me, this is that, and I am like this and they are like that,' and such things should never come in between. If this comes in the way of acquiring knowledge, then remember that the Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their relief, and curse their enemies. Whoever is shy in their face (i.e., too proud/shy to ask), their knowledge will be thin.' If someone is shy to acquire knowledge, is shy—'How should I read now?' Now that I have reached this age, then their knowledge will also be thin. Therefore, one should never feel ashamed in acquiring knowledge, from anyone and for anything. Let me present a small incident for you: there was a great teacher of ethics who was in the time of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, Mulla Ali Quli Hamadani. Mulla Ali, you know Sheikh Murtaza Ansari was a very great jurist (faqih), what is his title? Khatam al-Fuqaha (The Seal of Jurists), may Allah be pleased with him. In 1282, 1282 Hijri, sorry, excuse me, he passed away in 1281 Hijri. In 1281 Hijri, Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, meaning the greatest of the 13th century, in fact, his title today is Khatam al-Fuqaha. Even today, his books 'Rasa'il' and 'Makasib' are taught in the Hawza, and truly Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, Khatam al-Fuqaha, a very great philosopher, a very high status. Among his students, in his class, students would sit—and when we say students, do not think they were small children. Meaning, they were all elderly, white-bearded, all kinds of people. Among them sat Janab Mulla Ali Quli Hamadani. Mulla Quli Hamadani, Mulla Ali Quli Hamadani, remember the name. He was a teacher of ethics. He used to sit in Sheikh Murtaza's jurisprudence (fiqh) class, in the class of fiqh and usul (principles of jurisprudence). And Sheikh Murtaza Ansari used to go and sit in his ethics class. Just think, he was such a tremendous teacher of ethics. A man like Sheikh Murtaza Ansari—now children will not understand who Sheikh Murtaza Ansari is. Let me tell you who Sheikh Murtaza Ansari is. Sheikh Murtaza Ansari is someone—just one incident for your service, although his entire biography is a tremendous personality, and people of great stature do not know about him. Let me just tell you a small incident: he had a student in his class who was very weak, everyone used to make fun of him, everyone used to mock him. Everyone in the class used to make fun of him; it happens, it happens in every class. There is always someone who is, in our language, the 'goat' (the target). Everyone keeps mocking him. So, in Sheikh Murtaza Ansari's class, there was a boy who was very weak, but he felt very bad when people made fun of him. So what did he do? He performed tawassul (intercession) to the Master (a.s.), he performed a lot of tawassul, 'O Mawla, I am so weak, people make fun of me, please help me, otherwise I will stop studying.' I will stop studying. So when this happened, well, Alhamdulillah, a manifestation occurred, and he was told, 'Just drink this one drop of water, Insha'Allah your problem will be solved.' He drank just one drop of water, and after that, he went and sat in the class. Whose class? Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, who was the Marja and the Scholar of the Age. He was the Scholar of the Age. And as soon as Sheikh Murtaza came to the pulpit to teach, he hadn't even taught two sentences when he said, 'Master, there is a mistake. Master, I made a mistake.' So the whole class started laughing loudly. Meaning, now he started interrupting the Sheikh. So the Sheikh asked, 'What is this?' He said, 'You said this, actually it is not like this, it is like this.' So the Sheikh said, 'You are correct, you are saying it right.' You are saying it right. Everyone was amazed. Amazed, what is this? Then Sheikh Murtaza was teaching for a little longer when he interrupted again. Then the Sheikh said, 'Now what?' He said, 'It is not like this, it is like this.' So the Sheikh said, 'Yes, you are saying it right.' But now what happened, for the third time he interrupted the Sheikh again. So the Sheikh said, 'Son, sit down. The one who gave you...' 'And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.' Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, then Allah—meaning, who are these people? They are those who are with the ones upon whom Allah's blessings are. With the Siddiqin (truthful), Shuhada (martyrs), and Salihin (righteous)—what an excellent company this is. There cannot be a better company than this. Prophets, Siddiqin, Shuhada, Salihin. 'And excellent are those as companions.' The Quran says, 'And excellent are those as companions.' Then after that, when it was asked in the service of the Master (a.s.), the Master (a.s.) asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what are these 40 hadiths?' So he said, in the service of the Prophet, it was asked, and the Prophet said, 'This is the very first thing: Tawheed (Monotheism).' Therefore, in the service of the discourse, I have only spoken about one point regarding Tawheed, yes. Do not think that the discussion on Tawheed is complete. No, no, the discussion on Tawheed is very detailed. For that, two years are required. That is also where all the students are who are capable of understanding, who understand the meaning. It goes on there for two years. It is clear, isn't it? And that too, only by indication. Meaning, not complete. Tawheed, after all, is obviously something that no one can understand completely except the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). We only speak of the apparent meanings that we understand. Otherwise, the things that are understandable to us are clear, aren't they? After that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says the second sentence. Now look at the second sentence. First, what is the first topic? Tawheed. Now the second topic, 'wa tuqimussalata bi wudu-in sabighin fi mawaqitiha' (and establish prayer with a perfect wudu at its appointed times). And pray. Pray, but two conditions were set for prayer, pay attention. Two conditions were set. One, 'bi wudu-in sabighin'. Meaning, perform wudu properly and pray at its time, 'fi mawaqitiha'. Insha'Allah, we will discuss that later. For now, let's just complete the sentence. 'Wa la tu'akhirha' (and do not delay it). Look, do not delay the prayer. Iblis says, 'We will pray later, there is still time.' What time is it now? Okay, there is still plenty of time. And especially for the morning prayer. If you wake up, God forbid, yes. If you wake up at the beginning of the time, you think there is still plenty of time. This qada (missed prayer), what time does it become qada? Let's talk about youngsters; these things happen among youngsters, and then they see, 'Okay, even if I pray, then... oh, for example, it becomes qada at 6:15, okay, I will wake up at 6:10 and pray.' But who knows if you will wake up or not? If you don't wake up, the prayer is gone. The flight has taken off. The flight is gone. Now what to do? This is qada. But qada is a sin. I mean, you prayed the qada, that was just fulfilling an obligation, it is qada. You had to do the obligation anyway. But because the prayer was missed intentionally, missing it intentionally is a sin. And when something is a sin and an expiation (kaffara) is given, one does not know whether Allah accepts that expiation or not. Now let me give an example of this. The example is this, right, that when you are on a flight, it happens that when it takes off, I gave the same example before, that when you go for a flight, what is written on it? 'Boarding gates will be closed 20 minutes before departure.' The boarding gate will close 20 minutes before departure. Boarding gate closed, then they won't take you. Now we think, 'I have already taken the boarding pass. Now the flight won't leave without me.' Understand? Now how much will it go? Understood? Yes. Now, thinking this, they go and sit in the restaurant and eat. Now there is an announcement there repeatedly, 'Final call, final call, final call.' It turns out that when they arrived, there were 10 minutes left and the flight door was closed. Now they say, 'Hey, I have a boarding pass.' But man, you have to reach 20 minutes before departure. So what if you have a boarding pass? Will the flight stop taking off just because you are late? Exactly, the sequence of qada prayer is just like this. That the angels wait, 'Okay, fine, you didn't pray at the beginning of the time, no problem. A little delay, delay, delay.' But where it becomes qada, now whether the angel accepts it or not, whether he takes it up or not, that is in the hands of the angels. Now no one has the authority to complain. He will say, 'O Lord, I did pray, didn't I?' He will say, 'No, you did pray, but you prayed it as qada.' Anyway, Allah is Ghafoor-ur-Raheem (Forgiving and Merciful), Insha'Allah Allah forgives, and if it happens to someone by mistake, then it's no problem. Meaning, if he fell asleep, for example, he slept late at night and didn't wake up in the morning, no problem. Then he can pray qada, but intentionally... so that is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says here, 'wa la tu'akhirha' (and do not delay it). Look, do not delay it, 'fa inna fi ta'khiriha min ghayri 'illatin' (for in delaying it without a reason) because delaying it without a reason, what is in delaying it? 'ghadabu ghadabullahi 'azza wa jall' (the wrath of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic). It is the wrath of Allah. Wrath means punishment. Allah sends punishment for delaying it intentionally. 'min ghayri 'illatin' (without any reason). Anyway, so what was the first condition? Wudu-e-sabigh. Now understand wudu-e-sabigh, meaning what it is. Wudu-e-sabigh is a phrase, 'sabigh' is an attribute, a quality, an adjective for wudu. Meaning, the wudu should be such that the wudu itself should be acceptable. We just did wudu like this, took water. You are not looking. Did wudu like this, then did this, did this, and left quickly. Meaning, no care for the right, no care for the left. No, this is not called wudu-e-sabigh. And this will not be accepted either. Wudu-e-sabigh means that a person should perform wudu properly, nicely. And that is, at the very least, if one is not doing the recommended acts (mustahabbat), one is doing the obligatory ones, then one should do the obligatory ones as written in the Tawdih al-Masa'il. Take care of that, and then the best thing is to recite the supplications (duas) for it because there are strange and wonderful supplications and there is strange reward for this. One thing, if someone doesn't remember that supplication, then I will tell you a shortcut for it. You don't have to do anything, just keep reciting Inna Anzalna. There is tremendous reward. You know Inna Anzalna, right? Inna Anzalna, just that much. This is for the youth; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Al-wudu nisf al-iman' (Wudu is half of faith). Now, think about why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that? Wudu, just Wudu. Look, Wudu itself is not inherently obligatory. Wudu is not obligatory in itself. Only if you have to perform an obligatory act for which Wudu is a condition, like prayer, touching the pages of the Quran, or performing Tawaf and other rites of Hajj where Wudu is a condition, then Wudu becomes obligatory. Otherwise, Wudu is not obligatory in itself. Wudu is Mustahab (recommended). Wudu is not obligatory, it is recommended. Despite that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says—look, when someone sneezes, it is the duty of others to say 'Yarhamukumullah' (May Allah have mercy on you). But a man was sitting near Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Look, a sneeze... 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum'. He sneezed and said 'Alhamdulillah'. The Imam was silent; the Imam said nothing. So he said, 'You did not say Yarhamukumullah.' The Imam replied, 'Have you fulfilled our right?' He said, 'I did say Alhamdulillah.' So the Imam said—we are just speaking in brackets—'Others say that too. So what is the difference between them and you? You did not fulfill our right. Just as others do not, you did not either.' So he asked, 'Then what should I say, Mawla?' He said, when you sneeze, after saying 'Alhamdulillah', say: 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum'. So when they sneeze, they should recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) after saying 'Alhamdulillah'. This is the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Why? Listen to the reason too. Why? Because every sneeze increases one's lifespan slightly. But this does not apply to those who are ill. Right? We are talking about a regular sneeze, not about illness. Because some people have allergies, and that is a different matter, they don't stop. So how long would we keep saying 'Yarhamukumullah'? So we are not talking about them. Every sneeze increases one's lifespan. When one's lifespan increases, this increase in age is... To the Wali-e-Nimat, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Muhammad-o-Aale-Muhammad, Salawat! Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-o-Aale-Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum. He said, 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-o-Aale-Muhammad'. The Imam said, 'Yarhamukumullah'. As he fulfilled the right, the Imam fulfilled his right. Therefore, whenever you sit with your people, tell them that this is the right of the family of Muhammad. Do not waste this right. This Salawat is a very great right. Especially from Thursday night until Friday, until sunset on Friday, there is no better deed than this. And I also submit to you that if you do not remember any other Dua during Wudu, or even if you do not remember Surah al-Qadr, if you do not remember anything at all—there are some poor souls who don't know anything. Well, if you don't know anything, you hear Salawat in the Majlis, right? Just recite that. Subhan Allah. Wah wah wah. And let me tell you, there is no better Dua than this. Wah wah, indeed, indeed, wah wah. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-o-Aale-Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum. So the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Al-wudu nisf al-iman'. Wudu is half of faith. Why half of faith? Wudu is recommended because Wudu acts as insurance. When a person remains in a state of Wudu, Allah insures them against the whispers of Satan. Now, the devils cannot easily approach them. When they remain in a state of Wudu, the devils say, 'They are in Wudu, how can we approach them? There is a fortress all around them.' This Wudu acts as insurance. That is why it is so important. That is why it was said, look at the Hadith. I present another Hadith for you. Mawla-e-Kainat, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-o-Aale-Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum. He says, 'Man ahsanat-tahur'—'ahsan' means to do it well, 'tahur' means Wudu. Or Wudu or Ghusl. Both are called Tahur. Wudu for minor impurity (Hadath-e-Asghar), Ghusl for major impurity (Hadath-e-Akbar), and Tayammum if water is not available. These three things are for Tahur. Okay? We don't need to explain the rulings in detail here, but just briefly. So this is called Tahur. So, whoever performs Tahur well, performs Wudu well, 'Summa masha ilal masjid', then walks towards the mosque, walks on foot to the mosque, 'Fahuwa fi salatin ma lam yuhdis'—as soon as they start walking after performing Wudu, prayer starts being written in their record of deeds, as long as their Wudu is not broken. Subhan Allah. Until then, pray, pray, pray. Meaning they are not doing anything, they are just walking. They are praying, they are not doing Zikr. But because they left in a state of Wudu, the angels are busy. They are writing prayer in their record of deeds, prayer, prayer. The sign of prayer, if Allah grants the opportunity, we will discuss it tomorrow. Not today. So the angels are writing prayer, prayer, prayer, prayer. Because they are not praying, but because they have performed Wudu with the intention of praying. Now, for as long as—for example, even if they are at home. They performed Wudu at home, it is not time for prayer yet. But they have performed Wudu. For example, prayer is at 12:45, and they performed Wudu at 12:30 and are doing other tasks. They are not praying. But the reward of prayer is being written in their record of deeds. They are walking around the house, doing other work, but the reward of prayer is being written. Subhan Allah. 'Ma lam yuhdis', the Mawla says, as long as a Hadath (breaking of Wudu) does not occur. As long as that does not happen, it is fine. As long as the Wudu is not broken, until then. Now after that, I present another Hadith for you. This Hadith is a bit long. But anyway, I will just translate it; there is no time to explain. But the Hadith is amazing. Just pay attention and try to remember it. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Ya Ali', I submit to you again. Who is the addressee? And who is the one being addressed? That is, the addressee is the City of Knowledge. Who is the addressee? The Gate of the City of Knowledge. You cannot find a better combination than this. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Ya Ali', he says, 'Salasun darajatun, salasun kaffaratun, salasun muhlikatun, wa salasun munjiatun'. O Ali, there are three things that elevate ranks. There are three things that become a cause for the expiation of sins. There are three things that destroy a person. And there are three things that save a person. Meaning the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) mentioned 12 things in one Hadith. Three of each. One that elevates ranks. 'Fa ammal darajat', the things that elevate ranks, 'Fasbagul wudu fis-sabarati'. The first thing. What elevates the rank is 'Isbagul wudu'. What is Isbagul wudu? To perform Wudu well. And especially when? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) specifically mentioned one season in this Hadith. 'Fis-sabarati'. Sabarat means when it is freezing cold. Cold water, and at that time there were no heaters, right? That you turn on the geyser, hot from the left, cold from the right, or whatever. It didn't exist in that era. In that era, they would just go straight to the well, draw water, and perform Wudu. It's clear, right? In such cold weather, people wouldn't even get up. That they would have to perform Wudu. This Abu Ali Sina, who at the age of 18 was the champion of all the sciences of that time. And his students, one of the jobs of students is to flatter the teacher. What they call 'pumping' in Bombay language. The students said, 'Teacher, why don't you claim prophethood? You have so much knowledge, you give an opinion on everything. So why don't you claim prophethood?' Abu Ali Sina remained silent. This was—meaning when he had reached that age, this is about that time. Meaning at the age of 18 he had become a master. So at 40-50, imagine what he must have been like, at 40. Yes? Then the student said. He remained silent. He started traveling with the same student in the desert. When he was traveling in the desert, the Muezzin called out, 'Allahu Akbar'. Abu Ali Sina said—Abu Ali Sina didn't really pray, because he was a Batini. Meaning he was an Ismaili. So he didn't pray. He said, 'Brother, okay, at least for whatever reason the Muezzin said Allahu Akbar.' So he said to his student, 'Brother, give me some water, man.' Morning, meaning, now he said, 'Wow.' Prayer, Azan, desert, cold—you know it is very cold in the desert. I told you, right, it is very cold in the desert. It is hot during the day, cold at night. So he said, 'Brother, give me some water.' So he pulled the blanket even tighter. And started saying, 'I am very sleepy. I will give it to you after a while.' Abu Ali Sina says, 'You were the one saying claim prophethood. Look at Muhammad, it has been 400 years since he died. Even today, his follower, standing in this cold, is saying Allahu Akbar. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-o-Aale-Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum. 'Isbagul wudu fis-sabarati'. When... meaning two words are used in Arabic. One is 'Shita' for cold, when it is the winter season, cold. And 'Sabarat' means it is extremely cold. In which the body shivers, in which a person trembles, as they say, right? That a person is completely shivering. That cold is called that. Like, for example, there is cold in Bombay, there is, is there any season in Bombay, like the rain? Otherwise, for 8-9 months, it's all the same weather. And if you want to see cold, then go to UP, go to Bihar, go to Kashmir, look there, especially that is called cold. This is especially for them. So, whoever performs Wudu well in extreme cold, meaning they get up and perform Wudu properly. Or when they go to Iran, etc. So I have seen with my own eyes. That some people, meaning they came out of the toilet, didn't even perform Wudu. And went straight to the Arab. The water was so cold, because they didn't have the courage. To perform Wudu. So the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, "فَإِسْبَاغُ الْوُضُوءِ عَلَى الْمَكَارِهِ" (performing Wudu thoroughly despite difficulties), and then two other things that elevate one's status: "وَانْتِظَارُ الصَّلَاةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ" (waiting for the next prayer after finishing one). Subhan Allah. Meaning, there is great virtue in waiting for the prayer. "وَانْتِظَارُ الصَّلَاةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ" and the third is walking to join the congregational prayer, which increases one's status. "أَمَّا الْكَفَّارَاتُ" (as for the expiations), the things that become an expiation for sins, "فَإِفْشَاءُ السَّلَامِ" (spreading the greeting of peace), meaning always be the first to say Salam. No. "إِفْشَاءُ السَّلَامِ"—it is in the traditions that a believer is one who greets first, and a hypocrite is one who waits for the other person to greet them. Not eating at your own time, but feeding others. Feeding others. That is why, what is in the tradition regarding Salam? What is the Hadith, what are the words? He says, listen, "الطَّعَامُ قُوتُ الْجَسَدِ" (food is the nourishment of the body). Is this a very big deal? No. It is not a big deal. But listen to the second sentence: "الطَّعَامُ قُوتُ الْجَسَدِ" (food is the nourishment of the body), "وَالْإِطْعَامُ قُوتُ الرُّوحِ" (and feeding others is the nourishment of the soul). Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! And feeding others is the nourishment of the soul. Ya Ali! This is the nourishment of the soul, "إِطْعَامُ الطَّعَامِ". And do not wait, saying, 'When they feed us, then we will feed them.' No, no. You be the first. Do not wait for them to feed you before you feed them. Why didn't you leave the house? They thought you were a fool. Recite a Salawat. "اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ". And what is the third thing that is an expiation? "وَالتَّهَجُّدُ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ" (and performing Tahajjud at night while people are asleep). "وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَكَ" (and in the night, perform Tahajjud as an additional prayer for you). And rise in the last part of the night, "وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ" and perform Tahajjud. "نَافِلَةً لَكَ" (an additional prayer for you), Nafila, Nafila. "نَافِلَةً لَكَ" "عَسَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا" (it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station). If you do this, your Lord will elevate you to the Maqam-e-Mahmud. You will be under the Liwa-ul-Hamd (Banner of Praise) with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) on the Day of Judgment. What is the Liwa-ul-Hamd? The Liwa-ul-Hamd is the banner that Ali (a.s.) will be holding. Do you want to be under the banner of Ali ibn Abi Talib on the Day of Judgment? Then perform Namaz-e-Shab (Night Prayer). Because Ali was a man of prayer and Ali was constant in his Namaz-e-Shab. So, whoever claims to be a follower of Ali must also be constant in Namaz-e-Shab while the people of the world are sleeping. "وَالتَّهَجُّدُ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالتَّهَجُّدُ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ" "وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَكَ". Now, can I add something in brackets here? People object, 'Why do you recite Tabarra? Why do you curse? You shouldn't do all this. It doesn't look good coming from your mouth.' In Ziyarat-e-Ashura, we say, 'O Lord, You have given me the sustenance of Bara'ah (disassociation).' Wah! Wah! Wah! Bara'ah, meaning performing Tabarra, is a sustenance from Allah. Not every Tom, Dick, and Harry gets it. Indeed! Wah! Wah! Wah! Countless curses. Isn't it? The third thing the Imam said, "Nafila, Nafila, Nafila", Nafila, meaning perform Nafila-e-Shab, Nafila-e-Shab. It is eight Rakats. Eight Rakats, youngsters, it takes 5 minutes.
