When you wake up, perform it. If you wake up at 7:00 or 8:00, perform it. It is written in the Hadith that when a youngster performs Qaza of Namaz-e-Shab, Allah takes pride before the angels. 'O My angels, look at this youngster, this was a recommended act, yet he is performing its Qaza.' Wah! Wah! Wah! Is it clear to you? There is so much emphasis. So what does this do? Expiation. And three things that destroy a person, destroy them. One, Bakhil (stinginess). Stinginess. A believer can never be stingy. If he is stingy, he cannot be a believer. Subhan Allah. If he is stingy, he cannot be a believer. If he is a believer, he cannot be stingy. A believer is one who is generous, whose hands are open. That is called a believer. And the third thing that destroys is when a person considers himself better than others, considers his own deeds to be good. "إِعْجَابُ الْمَرْءِ بِنَفْسِهِ" (self-admiration). To be amazed, 'Wow, look at me.' Patting one's own back. A believer is not like that. A believer is one who, no matter how much he does, always thinks, 'I have done nothing.' "إِعْجَابُ الْمَرْءِ بِنَفْسِهِ"—arrogance is not found in him. The problem with Satan was exactly this. Pride and arrogance. He thought, 'I have performed so many acts of worship. So many acts of worship.' He was amazed by his own worship. 'How can I prostrate to him whom Allah has just created?' "خَلَقَنِي مِنْ نَارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ" (You created me from fire and created him from clay). 'You created me from fire and him from clay. Can clay ever bow before fire? Fire is superior.' The Imam says if he had been aware of the light of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) in the loins of Adam, he would never have refused. Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! He was not aware of the light of Ale-Muhammad. He was ignorant. His duty was—it was his duty to be immediately obedient and submissive before Allah's command; he should have bowed down. Or he could have asked the Lord, 'O Lord, tell me, why are You saying this?' At least he could have asked. Then Allah would have told him that in the loins of Adam is such a light before which the entire world will bow. Subhan Allah. Therefore, whenever you go to the Haram, do not go with the intention of prostrating to Allah—there is no harm in bowing your head with the intention of kissing the threshold of the Mawla. Indeed! Wah! Wah! Wah! If we don't bow at the Mawla's door, where will we bow? Where else? And remember, I will tell you one more thing. That whoever refuses to bow there, he bows everywhere else. Indeed! Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah! Then Allah makes him bow everywhere, and he keeps bowing. Whoever does not bow at the door of Ale-Muhammad. Then the fourth thing—three things save a person. This is the fourth thing. Three things save a person. One, fear of Allah, fear Allah. Then in private and in public, even when you are alone, fear Him, and when you are in public, fear Him. Wah! Wah! The sentence of the Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.). "اتَّقُوا فِي اللَّهِ" (Fear Allah). Recite a Salawat. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum. Mawlana Ya Ali, the Mawla says that in solitude, fear disobeying Allah. Fear Allah when you are alone, because the One who is the Witness is also the Judge. He is not in need of any witness. Is it clear to you? And moderation in spending, whether Allah makes you rich or poor, always keep your economic life normal, live a moderate life. Stay moderate. Not too much, no extravagance, no stinginess, nothing. Live a completely normal life. Allah likes this. Moderation in everything, Allah likes moderation in everything. Economy. And the last thing, "وَلْكَلِمَةُ الْعَدْلِ فِي الرِّضَا وَالسَّخَطِ" (and the word of justice in pleasure and anger), meaning always speak the truth, whether you are pleased with the person or angry. If someone you have enmity with comes to you and says, 'Look, so-and-so did injustice to me,' if he is speaking the truth, support him. Even if he is your enemy, support him. And if a friend says something wrong, you should tell him, 'You are doing wrong, you are saying the wrong thing.' Not that, 'He is our friend, what can we do? We have to support him, we have to do this.' No, this is wrong. And that is why when people advised Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) and asked Sayyid-ush-Shuhada to somehow agree, what sentence did Sayyid-ush-Shuhada say? Two sentences of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada are very famous. You must have heard them. One, 'A person like me cannot pledge allegiance to a person like Yazid.' And what was the second sentence? The second sentence was this: on the day of Ashura, in his sermon, 'The son of the illegitimate one, the son of the illegitimate one.' These are the sentences of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, and everyone reads this in the Maqtal. Those who object also read this. 'The son of the illegitimate one, the son of the illegitimate one, he has left me with only two options: either I take up the sword or I live a life of disgrace.' 'Haihata minna-dh-dhilla' (Disgrace is far from us, the Ahlulbayt). Sayyid-ush-Shuhada sacrificed everyone, sacrificed everyone. No one was left, no one was left. Now, once Sayyid-ush-Shuhada came, and after coming, Sayyid-ush-Shuhada gave a call. It is called the 'Sada-e-Istighasa' (call for help). Sayyid-ush-Shuhada said, 'Is there any helper to help us? Is there any rescuer to rescue us? Is there any defender to defend the Haram of the Messenger of Allah?' No one answered from the battlefield. Just a commotion arose in the tents. Sayyid-ush-Shuhada came near the tents. Sister Zainab also cried out, 'Brother, you raised the call for help, and Asghar threw himself out of the cradle.' She said, 'Brother, bring Asghar, give him to me.' She said, 'Brother, he is not going into anyone's lap. Now, Hussain, you also bring him.' Imam Hussain came to the tent, came near the tent. Now, it is not written what the father said and what the son understood. It is just written in the Maqtal that Asghar came into the lap of the father of Asghar. Hussain took him and started walking. Now when he came to the door of the tent, the mother was standing there. He said, 'Rubab, why are you standing?' Rubab said, 'I am seeing that whoever has gone to the battlefield since morning has not returned alive. I thought I would see my child once.' Hussain consoled her, 'Rubab, whoever has gone so far has gone on their own feet. This enemy thought perhaps he has come to fight. Oh, does a lion's cub fight? A mother's heart, Hussain took him and came to a height and called out, 'O people, is there any Muslim? My child has been thirsty for three days, and Islam says to give water to the thirsty.' No one answered. Then Hussain said the second sentence, 'If you are not Muslims, then at least you are parents. You are parents. You can see that my child is dying of thirst, he is gasping, closing his mouth, opening his mouth, closing his mouth.' Once, a commotion arose in the tents, a commotion arose among the wretched ones. They started crying in hiding. It was near an uprising, the atmosphere was such that Ibn Sa'd called out, 'Where, where is the archer?' And Hussain came in front. 'Fa-inn-al-kalam...' Hussain stopped the speech. Now it is written in the Maqtal that Hurmala took out an arrow, fixed it to the bow, and aimed at Asghar's throat. The arrow hit Asghar's throat. The child was martyred. There is a smile on the child's face. There is a smile on the child's face. 'Father, do not worry, do not worry.' Now Hussain is walking with the child towards the tent. Now Hussain... He took a few steps, reciting 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. He went a little further, but then the thought occurred to him: how will I show the child to his mother in this condition? He turned back, again reciting 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. Seven times Husayn (a.s.) performed this act. Finally, he thought that now that the child has departed from this world, the mother should not be deprived of a final glimpse. He came near the tent and called out, 'Rabab!' As soon as Husayn (a.s.) called out, it is written in the Maqtal that Rabab came from one side and Sakina came from the other. The little girl reached first, 'Father, give water to my brother, my brother is no longer thirsty.' When Husayn (a.s.) saw this, he struck his own face. Oh my son, will I be left behind after a child like you? O Allah, grant us peace and prosperity in our homeland. O Allah, keep us away from the troubles and hardships of this world. O Allah, for those who are in debt, grant them the means to repay their debts. O Allah, for those who are childless, grant them righteous offspring. O Allah, for those who are far from their homeland, return them safely and soundly. O Allah, for those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Allah, for those who are suffering from illness and have asked for prayers, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Allah, protect the life, wealth, honor, and dignity of all the Shi'a of Haydar-e-Karrar wherever they may be in the world. O Allah, protect the great scholars and the Maraji-e-Izam. O Allah, protect the holy shrines and sacred places. Grant us the pilgrimage of Husayn in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. O Allah, accept this Fatiha and prayer. 'Wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil adheem'. Bestow the reward upon the souls of the Lada Khani, Bayani, Hasrani families, and all the believing men and women.

title: Majlis-e-Azaa: Court of Inquiry | Watch 👆 Full Video | Majlis 05 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi emphasizes that a Majlis-e-Aza should function as a serious court of inquiry rather than a mere ritual. He highlights that Janabe Zainab (s.a.) established this precedent by challenging the authorities in the courts of Ibn Ziyad and Yazid. The lecture encourages believers to critically examine the historical chain of events, including the political legitimacy of the Umayyad rulers, to truly understand the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
And we have said this many times before. This Majlis-e-Aza (mourning gathering) is a court of inquiry. And it should be exactly that. If this court of inquiry does not do its job, it means the right is not being fulfilled. Look, let me give you a common example. You take your case to court. You take your case to court, and the lawyer or judge there talks about other things instead of your case and does not discuss the actual subject. So if there is no discussion on the actual subject, you will say, 'Brother, what is happening? I have come with my case.' The first person who filed this case in court was Janabe Zainab (s.a.). This court was established by Janabe Zainab (s.a.). When she gave a sermon in the court of Ibn Ziyad and Yazid and established this court, established this Majlis-e-Aza, and after that, it is the responsibility of all of us to ask, 'Who killed Imam Hussain (a.s.)? Who killed him? Why was he killed?' This is the first question. Well, everyone has answered this question. Everyone knows who killed him and why he was killed, and the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) himself gave the answer. The second thing is, if that man was like that, then who made him Caliph? So the father thought that the government should go to the son. So the father made him. Then the third question arises, 'Who made the father?' Discuss that, brother.
A Majlis-e-Aza is a court of inquiry, not just a mourning gathering.
Janabe Zainab (s.a.) established the precedent of challenging injustice in the courts of Yazid.
The primary duty of the mourner is to investigate the 'who' and 'why' of the tragedy of Karbala.
Historical inquiry must go beyond the immediate perpetrators to identify the systemic causes.
The legitimacy of the Umayyad Caliphate is a central subject for critical historical analysis.
Failure to discuss the actual subject of the tragedy is a failure to fulfill the purpose of the Majlis.

title: Eesaal-e-Sawaab Majlis-e-Azaa Baraaye Marhoom Syed Mahdi Hasan Ibn Sayed Sibte Hasan
excerpt: This lecture, delivered as an Eesaal-e-Sawaab for the late Syed Mahdi Hasan, explores the theological significance of the Ahl al-Bayt through the lens of Hadith al-Kisa and Ayat al-Tathir. The speaker emphasizes the unique status of the Prophet Muhammad and the infallibility of the members gathered under the cloak. The session concludes by connecting these foundational Islamic concepts to the emotional legacy of mourning for Bibi Zahra (s.a.) and the broader tradition of Majlis-e-Azaa.
content:
Assalamu Alaykum. I am Noha Khawan Ali Zamin from Pakistan. Please recite Surah al-Hamd once and Surah al-Tawheed three times to send the reward (Isal-e-Sawab) to the soul of the late Syed Mehdi Hasan from India, who was very pious. And may the Lord, through the blessings of this Noha that I am about to recite, forgive his soul. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! Your daughter was made to weep... Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! Today, your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! And I was writhing in pain... And I was writhing in pain... Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! With the whip of this accursed one... grabbing her... Your daughter was made to weep with slaps... Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! And I was writhing in pain... Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! Your daughter was made to weep with slaps, O father! Your daughter was made to weep with slaps... The writer wrote that she was beaten severely... They took... They took her veil... Shedding blood upon it, and passed from here... Her son was trampled... Where your veil fell, O Hussain... The mother wrote with so much consolation... The sister cries out, remembers her brother, and weeps bitterly. She cannot see anything now, she cannot see anything... blood was spilled on him, and [the horses] passed over him, her son was trampled... Reciting Surah al-Ikhlas, Syed... ...meaning, reciting Surah al-Ikhlas, Syed Mehdi Hasan, for the esal-e-sawab of the late Sibte Hasan Sahab, and all Muslim men and women... I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah Who... ...peace be upon... our master, our prophet, our guardian, our master of the two worlds, the grandfather of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, Abul Qasim Muhammad... O Allah, Amen, Amen, Amen... Amma ba'd (now then), indeed Allah, the Glorified, the Blessed and Exalted, has said... ...indeed Allah, the Glorified, the Blessed and Exalted, has said in His firm Book: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, Allah only wishes...' This verse of Surah al-Ahzab, which you know as the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tathir), in this verse, the divine proclamation is made: 'Indeed, Allah only wishes to remove all impurity from you, O Ahl al-Bayt, and to purify you with a thorough purification.' For the sake of guidance, Allah sent 124,000 prophets. In the Quran, Allah mentioned some prophets by name, and some without mentioning their names. And there are some prophets in whom believing and having faith... ...is necessary for us because the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) stated this number, that Allah sent 124,000 prophets to the world. But the Prophet did not mention all of their names, nor their parentage, nor their locations, nor their lineages. But because the Prophet said that Allah sent 124,000 prophets, believing and having faith in 124,000 is necessary for us. And we exercise such caution in this matter that if someone accidentally or mistakenly says in front of another that Allah sent 124,000 prophets, the other person immediately corrects him, saying, 'Not 124,000, but 124,000 prophets were sent to this world.' If someone says 125,000 were sent, people cannot tolerate even this addition of 1,000, and correction is immediately made that it is not 125,000, but 124,000 prophets were sent to the world. What the Prophet said is final, and everyone believes in it. Neither an addition of one prophet is tolerated, nor is a reduction of one prophet tolerated by anyone. Now, you tell me in all fairness, even though the Prophet did not mention their names, parentage, or lineages... ...did not mention, yet if we deny even one of them, our Islam is put in danger. Then what about those twelve whose names were told, whose lineages were told, and whose attributes were told? In the Holy Quran, Allah mentioned those prophets with great respect and high manners. But the level of respect and manners Allah used for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in the Quran, was never used for anyone else. Apart from this, Allah gave the Prophet a unique status. For instance, Allah called Prophet Musa (a.s.) to the sacred valley of Tuwa, saying, 'Come here and take the Book.' This was to show the importance of the Book... ...'Come and take the Book.' This was to show the importance of the Book, that this Book will not come to you on its own; you have to come to receive it. Prophet Musa (a.s.) went to receive the Torah. Allah called him for thirty days, and then, to test the nation, extended it by ten days. (Recite a Salawat). And when those ten days were added—even though before this, these people themselves were demanding, 'Bring us a Book from Allah so we can live our lives according to it'—but when Prophet Musa went to receive it, and instead of 30 days it became 40 days, people here went astray. A person named Samiri made a golden calf out of gold and silver, and performed some magic... and within those few days, people's faith deviated, and they started worshipping the calf. I would like to mention a special point here: Musa (a.s.) had to go to receive the Torah, but Allah did not call the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to give him the Quran... ...did not call him, did not summon him. Now, if a person has even a little intellect, they can understand the status of the Prophet from this. He was never summoned anywhere. If the Prophet is in Mecca, the Quran is being revealed in Mecca. If the Prophet is in Medina, the Quran is being revealed in Medina. (Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad). The Prophet of Islam migrated from Mecca to Medina, but you will find that due to the necessity of revelation, there are Meccan chapters and Medinan chapters... ...Medina, Medina. If the Prophet is in the battlefield, the Quran is being revealed in the battlefield. If the Prophet is traveling, the Quran is being revealed during the journey. If the Prophet is... the Quran is still being revealed. Allah never summoned the Prophet for any revelation, saying, 'Since you are inside the cave, come out so we can reveal the Quran,' or 'You are on the camel's back, please dismount so we can reveal the Quran,' or 'You are riding, please halt so we can reveal the Quran,' or 'You are fighting a battle, please... ...'You are fighting a battle, please rest a bit so we can reveal the Quran,' or 'You are busy, please find some free time so we can reveal the Quran,' or 'You are lying down, please sit up so we can reveal the Quran.' No! In whatever state the Prophet was, Allah revealed the Quran to him in that very state. Allah never summoned the Prophet anywhere for the revelation of any verse or Surah. In the entire Quran, out of 114 Surahs and more than 6,000 verses, there is only one event of purification (Tathir) for which the Prophet was at home... I will share with you the significance of Hadith al-Kisa (Hadith of the Cloak). Such an elaborate arrangement was never made for anyone else as was made for this event. And it is this very arrangement of Hadith al-Kisa that people have a problem with, which is related to... if you perform mourning (matam), they have a problem... If we perform your mourning (matam), there is problem after problem. Now, because of all these things, there is nothing but problems. Let us look at some people's perspective. Now you tell me, Hadith al-Kisa has been recited among us for a very long time. If there is a wedding, Hadith al-Kisa is recited; if someone builds a house, Hadith al-Kisa is recited; if there is a shop, Hadith al-Kisa is recited. So, Hadith al-Kisa is recited for what? For blessings, for prosperity, Hadith al-Kisa is recited. Now, I will tell you that some people consider it authentic, while others do not. Ayatollah Reyshahri in his book claimed that the commonly known Hadith al-Kisa is not authentic. Its style is somewhat different. If you feel it, you will realize, and those who are watching online will also realize what I am going to present today. Since online lectures are heard far and wide nowadays, we should speak in a way that the message reaches far and wide. Just reflect on these things, there, Hadith al-Kisa... ...reflect on these things. There, Hadith al-Kisa is narrated in various books. In those narrations, they describe how the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) came to my house, and brought Moula Ali (a.s.), Bibi Zahra (s.a.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), and Imam Husayn (a.s.). After coming, he sat on a platform, seated Moula Ali (a.s.) on one side, Bibi Zahra (s.a.) on the other side, and Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Husayn (a.s.) as well. Then he placed a cloak over all of them. When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) placed the cloak over them, at that very moment, Jibra'il al-Amin descended and said to the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) that Allah declares from His Throne... ...and recited Ayah al-Tathir. Some narrations state that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) came to our house, stood up, gathered Moula Ali (a.s.), Bibi Zahra (s.a.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), and Imam Husayn (a.s.) close to him, placed the cloak over everyone's heads, and then recited Ayah al-Tathir. However, there are many differences; some narrate they were standing, some say they were sitting, some say they were lying down. But in all these narrations, what is common to our understanding? First, the common element is that the cloak was placed over them. Second... Second, there is no doubt in any narration about this. The second thing is that in every narration, in one way or another, Ayah al-Tathir is mentioned, that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited it. No matter the style of recitation, it must be accepted that Ayah al-Tathir is related only to those who came under the cloak. Send blessings (salawat) upon them. The third point is... ...thirdly, first of all, Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, in their books of Hadith, have narrated this. But they made a claim and an addition which is not read in our version of Hadith al-Kisa. They wrote that when everyone was gathered under the cloak, Umme Salama was watching this. In some narrations, there are 9, 10, 11, or 12 versions... ...no one came without permission. Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Husayn (a.s.) came with permission, and Moula Ali (a.s.) also came with permission. Then, Umme Salama also came and asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the same manner, 'May I also enter the cloak?' Look, this does not disrespect Umme Salama. She was watching this scene. But except for Umme Salama, no other wife had the courage to come near the cloak. Umme Salama is not infallible (masoomah), but she is among the righteous companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and holds a very high status. But when she came near the cloak, there is a sentence... ...but when she came near the cloak, we can say that although Umme Salama is not infallible, she is close to the boundaries of infallibility. She came and asked the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), 'May I also enter?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'No,' but he also said, 'You are upon goodness, you are in your place.' I believe Umme Salama did this so the world would know the boundary of the Ahlul Bayt. If even Umme Salama is not included under the cloak, then who is? Inside the cloak, there is only Moula Ali (a.s.), Bibi Zahra (s.a.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), and Imam Husayn (a.s.). Now, there is one more point regarding the narration of Hadith al-Kisa... ...whose word should we accept? The one who was watching from afar, or the lady who was actually inside the cloak? The Hadith al-Kisa we recite is narrated by Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.) herself. Bibi Zahra (s.a.) narrates it. Who else would understand it better? She is not like ordinary women who get angry when a needy person comes to their door... ...so this means they are seen close to the Ahlul Bayt. I often say that if someone appears close to the Ahlul Bayt, it is a matter of time. Even if Hurr was in Yazid's army, he eventually came to Imam Husayn (a.s.). One cannot remain distant from the Ahlul Bayt. And Allah's will (irada) is above everything... ...everything in the world changes, but when Allah wills something, no change occurs to it. So as long as Allah's will remains, the Ahlul Bayt will remain purified. They have been made the center of guidance. People ask why Bibi Zahra (s.a.) is the pivot. There is a difference between perfection (kamal) and status. Status is achieved due to perfection; perfection is not achieved due to status. If someone does a PhD, they get the title of professor... Support of Wilayat... but Ismat (infallibility) is the name of perfection. Perfection is attained through... If the Master (Maula) is giving testimony, it is being said that a husband's testimony is not acceptable. Regarding Imam Hasan and Husayn, it is being said that they are children, and that their mother still keeps weeping. ...always in our tradition... when the ruler banned the majalis... Or look closely, the daughter of the Prophet... is being snatched from everyone. 'O Hasan, last night I saw a dream that my father arrived and said, "Now you will not have to face these calamities for many more days..."' And his... who wanted to show... two hands emerged from the grave to take her in... when the Shahzadi was before me... but when... is becoming Muslim... and this is the day when even in the funeral... I am presenting the proofs... Today, Maula Ali is performing the ghusl... The way... 'May Allah preserve your veil (hijab).' But Zahra (a.s.) had to go to the courts... Salutations upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)... May Allah accept this mourning for Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad... Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. Who else besides you looks after a helpless one? Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. Whenever she stands before the mirror, she asks, 'Where is the pain and grief?' Let someone go and see... Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. I sigh and weep, I have departed from my own self, let me reach you... Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. Since childhood, you pampered me... Karbala... always weeping... it makes me weep a lot... Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. Tell me, do you know... Ali Akbar... Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me. At this moment, she weeps, voices are raised, we also always bring the standard (Alam) of martyrdom. Should I call you 'Father'? Come and speak to me.

title: Mukammal Imaan Kya Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #YouTubeShorts
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explains the criteria for achieving perfect faith according to a tradition found in Usul al-Kafi. He highlights the concept of 'Bab al-Taslim,' which emphasizes total submission to the beliefs and teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The lecture stresses that true belief requires accepting everything declared or hidden by the Progeny of Muhammad, regardless of whether it has reached the individual.
content:
There is a hadith in Usul al-Kafi, in the first volume. The chapter is named 'Bab al-Taslim'—the chapter of submission and the excellence of those who submit. In its sixth hadith, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'If anyone wants their faith to be completely perfect, without any defect, they should say: "My belief in all matters is the same as the belief of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). I believe in what they have declared, and I believe in what they have kept hidden. I believe in what has reached me, and I believe in what has not reached me."' This means total submission, without any reservation, solely for the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and no one else.
Perfect faith requires total submission to the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.).
The concept of 'Bab al-Taslim' refers to the excellence of those who submit completely.
True believers accept both what is declared and what is kept hidden by the Imams.
Faith encompasses both the knowledge that has reached us and what has not.
Submission must be absolute and without any personal reservation or doubt.
The source of this teaching is the first volume of Usul al-Kafi.

In short, the reality of the Quran is Zahra (a.s.). The secret in its recitation that gladdens the heart is that the entire eulogy is for my Princess (a.s.). Wah! Wah! Subhan Allah! What of one language, even if all the languages of the world were to describe her glory... I present a couplet to the lovers of Mawla... The reality of languages is that we know that so far, perhaps enough words have not even come into existence for human nature itself to wrap its every emotion in the envelope of words. The Quran cannot leave, the Quran can never leave the hem of... The Quran can never leave the hem of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.). What happens if the letters of Muhammad are hidden? ... What happens if Muhammad is displeased? Is the Kalima (testimony of faith) ever separated from its meaning? Their speech in the Messenger's... Their speech is highly esteemed by the Messenger, their character itself is the asset of Monotheism (Tawheed). Their speech is highly esteemed by the Messenger, their character itself is the asset of Monotheism. The couplet is: By God, her cloak has cast a shadow... a shadow that has no equal, so it seems. Subhan Allah! The one who is the daughter, is also the mother of her own father (Umm Abiha). Who can comprehend where her high status lies? The one who is the daughter is the mother of her own father. Lady Zahra (a.s.)! Who has the power to... ...comprehend where her high status lies? The one who is the daughter is the mother of her own father. Who has the power to describe your veil (hijab/purdah)? May Mawla Hussain (a.s.) keep you in remembrance. Who has the power to describe your veil? The couplet is: Who has the power to describe your veil? ... ...The Creator sent down the picture of guidance in the darkness, but He passed that light through every pure forehead. But those who were the requirements of the veil, she did not lessen them. He passed that light through every pure forehead, but those who were the requirements of the veil, she did not lessen them... ...She did not even make the Messenger a confidant to the veil of Zahra (a.s.). Hadith al-Kisa (the Tradition of the Cloak) lifts the veil, it reveals the secret. Hadith al-Kisa imparts divine gnosis (Irfan) to the world. Hadith al-Kisa awakens... It tells the entire universe, it tells the entire universe that because of Hadith al-Kisa, he is the Prophet of Prophets, and He is the Lord of the worlds. If she were not there, the universe would not exist... ...We are alive! You thought we would die, but we are alive. You thought we would die, so listen to this secret as to why we are alive. You thought we would die, but we are alive because the one whose cloak itself cures Prophethood... We are alive! You thought we would die. Such a Lady prays for our life... Such a Lady prays for our life.

title: Speak The Truth Even If You Perish | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound wisdom of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) regarding the necessity of speaking the truth. It emphasizes that while honesty may appear dangerous or destructive in the short term, it is the ultimate path to salvation. Conversely, the speaker warns that falsehood, despite its perceived benefits, leads to inevitable ruin.
content:
A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alim min ash-shaytani ar-rajim. Bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. Wa salla Allahu 'alayka ya waliyyal 'asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. The saying of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) is: 'Speak the truth. Speak the truth even if it seems like your destruction lies in it, because in reality, your salvation lies in it.' After that, he says: 'And abandon falsehood, even if it seems like your salvation lies in it, because in reality, your destruction lies in it.' Allah says: 'That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness.' And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
Speak the truth regardless of the perceived consequences.
True salvation is found in honesty, not in avoiding temporary hardship.
Falsehood is deceptive and leads to ultimate destruction.
Do not prioritize worldly safety over moral integrity.
Allah rewards those who remain truthful in their speech and actions.
The teachings of the Ahlulbayt provide a roadmap for spiritual success.

content:

title: EP10 | Zuhoor Ka Intezaar Kaise Karein? | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉 #ImamMahdiعج
excerpt: This lecture, part of the Panaah-e-Kainaat series, explores the true essence of awaiting (Intizar) the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). It emphasizes that awaiting is not about physical migration, but rather about spiritual readiness built upon three pillars: acquiring recognition (Ma'rifah), practicing piety (Taqwa), and maintaining steadfast beliefs (Aqeedah). The discussion highlights the importance of Tawalla, Tabarra, and remaining loyal to the Wilayah of the Ahlul Bayt during the major occultation. Additionally, the episode features details on the Panaah-e-Kainaat Mega Quiz, including the grand prize of a Ziyarat pilgrimage to Iraq.
content:
[Music] I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the outcast. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon... The quiz link is now live, which is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you haven't registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just need to watch the discussion carefully and answer the quiz questions correctly. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not rush to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. The only condition for the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. From all those who answer all questions correctly, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names do not appear in today's winners, or if they missed any episode, do not need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the pilgrimage (Ziyarat) to Iraq, will be selected from those who have answered all questions correctly in 7 out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone is not among the daily winners, but in 7 out of 12... Even if they didn't [answer all], but have given correct answers in seven out of twelve episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the pilgrimage (Ziyarat) to Iraq. Allahumma Kulli Waliyyikal... [Music] ... [Music] I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr (Guardian of the Age), assist us and do not let us perish. Respected listeners, in the previous episode, we saw two examples regarding the importance and history of awaiting (Intizar). In which we saw that regarding the Jews' awaiting of the Messenger, after the Prophet's arrival, they rejected him solely on the grounds that the Messenger was not from their tribe. The Messenger was from the Arabs, not from the Bani Israel. Meaning, here their personal desires overcame their awaiting, and they ended up denying the one they were awaiting. The second example you saw was of a companion of the Messenger who had heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that his grandson, Imam Hussain (a.s.) would be martyred in the land of Karbala after being kept hungry and thirsty for three days; so, with this desire, he went and settled in Karbala, and later he was also blessed with martyrdom. So, now let us... ...he was also blessed with martyrdom. So, let us now try to see what the state of our awaiting (intizar) should be, so that we do not deny him like those Jews, but await him with the spirit of sacrificing everything for the Imam of our time. We all know that the reappearance (zuhoor) of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) will take place from the Kaaba. So, should we migrate towards the Kaaba? Does awaiting mean leaving our homes and migrating towards Mecca? As you saw in the previous examples, one of the two migrations succeeded. The Jews' migration failed, while that of Anas ibn al-Harith succeeded. Thus, it becomes clear that merely migrating is not proof of awaiting. So, let us try to see what the state of our awaiting should be, so that we do not become like those Jews, but await him with the spirit of sacrificing everything for the Imam of our time, just as the Imam has commanded us to await him. In this regard, let us consider a few points on how the Imam has commanded us to... ...how he has commanded us to await the Imam. The first of these is to acquire recognition (ma'rifah)—that is, to acquire the recognition of the Imam of our time. In this regard, it is narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.): 'Know your Imam (Ar: I'rif Imamaka). When you recognize your Imam, it does not matter or cause any harm whether the reappearance of the Imam happens early or is delayed.' The second point is to adhere to piety (taqwa) and devoutness (wara'). Abu Basir narrates from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). Abu Basir was a companion of the Imam who was physically blind, but he could recognize the Imam by his scent. Abu Basir's level of recognition (ma'rifah) was so high that he recognized the Imam by his scent. The Imam says: 'There will be a government for us, and when Allah wills, that time will come. Whoever wishes to be among the companions of the Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) should await, and await in such a way that he practices devoutness (wara')...' ...and await in such a way that he practices devoutness (wara') and behaves with good morals (husn al-akhlaq). Even if that person passes away, and the Imam's reappearance occurs after his death, he will receive exactly the same reward as the person in whose lifetime the Imam reappears and who is included among the Imam's helpers. Therefore, we must strive and work very hard. There is glad tidings for you in awaiting, O group upon whom the mercy of God has descended! And the third point, which the Imam has emphasized greatly, is that we must remain steadfast on the correct belief (aqeedah). This is the most important matter, and we must pay the utmost attention to how our religion and our belief are. In this regard, let me share an incident narrated from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.). It is narrated from Hakam ibn Utaibah: 'Once, I was at the house of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), and his entire...' ...Baqir's (a.s.) house, and his entire courtyard was filled with the companions of the Imam. Then we saw an elderly, old man, leaning on a small staff, arrive at the Imam's door and salute the Imam: "Assalamu alaika ya bna Rasoolillah wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh" (Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings). And after that, the phrase is "thumma sakata" (then he became silent), and he fell silent. The Imam (a.s.) replied to his greeting. Then this man saluted all the companions present in the courtyard of the Imam and became silent again. They too replied to the old man's greeting. Then he turned towards Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, may my parents be sacrificed for you, I request permission to come close to you.' This was the manner of the companions of the Imams when speaking to the Imams. That elderly man went close to the Imam and declared his belief. And whatever he declared to the Imam, it is our wish too: 'If only our Imam...' ...it is our wish too: 'If only our Imam were before us, and we could declare our belief before him, and the Imam would validate our belief, Inshallah.' That person said to the Imam, 'Wallahi, inni la-uhibbukum' (By Allah, indeed I love you), 'By Allah, I love you, and I also love those who love you. And this love is not based on any worldly greed—it is not for worldly greed that I love you or your Shias.' Let me tell you a small thing: who is a Nasibi? Often, we think that the enemies of the Ahlul Bayt are called Nasibi. When the Imam was asked this very question, the Imam said, 'No, whoever harbors enmity towards our lovers, towards our Shias, is called a Nasibi.' So, this elderly man is affirming both things: 'I love you, and I also love those who love you. This love is solely and exclusively based on the love for the Ahlul Bayt.' And that person said to the Imam, 'And from your enemies...' ...'that I harbor hatred and enmity towards your enemies, and I disassociate myself from them (izhar-e-bara'at).' That is, 'I also practice Tabarra. And by God, I do not harbor enmity or practice Tabarra against your enemies because of any personal dispute.' This means the standard of friendship and enmity is the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.). And this is our responsibility. If we have a dispute or disagreement with any Shia, we have no right to curse or condemn them based on our personal differences. As long as they remain on the Shia path and have not opposed the Ahlul Bayt in any way, we have no right to curse them or backbite about them. Conversely, no matter how good our worldly relations with someone may be, if they are an opponent of the Ahlul Bayt, or a usurper of their rights, or a follower of their usurpers, then we must not have even an atom's weight of love for them in our hearts. From this... ...we must not have love. This is Tawalla and Tabarra—loving the Imam and those who love the Imam, and disassociating (bara'at) from the enemies of the Imam and the enemies of those who love them. Anyway, that person further says, 'By God, I consider lawful (halal) what you have made lawful, and I consider unlawful (haram) all those things you have declared unlawful. Wa muntazirun li-amrikum (And I am awaiting your affair/government).' Then that person asks the Imam, 'Is there any hope of reward for this belief of mine? May my life be sacrificed for you!' Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) said, 'Come close to me.' Then he sat the old man next to him and said, 'O man, a person once came to my father, Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.), and asked him the very same question you have asked me. My noble father replied to him: "If death comes to you—that is, if you depart from this world with this belief that you have just declared...' ...depart from this world with this belief that you have just declared, then rest assured that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Maula Ali (a.s.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), Imam Husayn (a.s.), and Ali ibn al-Husayn—Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) is narrating this incident from his noble father's time to that man—you will be presented before all these personalities, and that too in a state where your heart (qalb) will be at peace, there will be coolness in your heart, and your eyes will find comfort. You will be welcomed in the gardens of Paradise, along with the Kiraman Katibin (noble scribes). Even if your soul reaches here'—saying this, the Imam (a.s.) pointed towards his throat—'and if you remain alive, meaning you witness our government, then you will see that this world itself has become Paradise for you, and Allah will show you scenes that will bring coolness to your eyes, and you will be with us in the highest station.' ...'and you will be with us in the highest station.' Hearing this, the man said to the Master, 'O Master, what are you saying? A man like me will behold the Messenger of Allah? Will behold the Master of the Universe (Maula-e-Kainat)?' He asked the Imam, 'Please say it again.' The Imam repeated the entire reward for him. That is, if a person dies with this belief, Paradise is for him. If someone passes away, departing from this world on these four or five points mentioned to you, Paradise is guaranteed for him. And if he remains alive and witnesses the Imam's government, then this very world is Paradise for him. Then that man raised the slogan of 'Allahu Akbar'. Tears flowed from his eyes, and three times he cried, 'Allah, Allah, Allah,' and fell unconscious. Seeing his state—seeing the state of this old man—all the companions of the Imam present in the courtyard began to weep. Then the Imam himself rubbed his blessed hand over his face, wiped the tears from his eyes, and then he recovered from his unconsciousness... ...wiped the tears from his eyes, and then he recovered from his unconsciousness. Then the old man raised his head and requested Imam al-Baqir (a.s.), 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, stretch forth your hand. May my life be sacrificed for you.' Then the Imam stretched forth his hand, and he kissed the Imam's hand. This in itself is a great fortune, that the Imam is permitting someone to kiss his hand. With utmost affection, he took the Imam's hand—the very hand of the Imam that had touched his face and wiped his tears a moment ago—and rubbed it on his face, placed it on his eyes, touched it to his chest, and touched it to his stomach. Then he stood up from there and left, saluting everyone. When he had gone, the Imam (a.s.) said to all those present, 'Whoever wishes to look at one of the people of Paradise, let him look at this old man.' Hakam ibn Utaibah states, 'I have never seen such a sight before or after this.' In this incident, the most important thing for us... ...the most important thing for us is that if a person wants to go to Paradise, they must protect this belief of theirs. How? The first condition is to love the Ahlul Bayt and to love the Shias of the Ahlul Bayt. Second, to harbor hatred (bughz) towards the enemies of the Ahlul Bayt, and also to harbor hatred towards those who harbor hatred towards the lovers of the Ahlul Bayt. The third point is to consider lawful (halal) what they have made lawful, and to consider unlawful (haram) what they have declared unlawful. And the fourth is to await the government of the Ahlul Bayt—the government that will be established after the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.), Inshallah. These four beliefs alone bestowed such a status upon that old man that the son of Zahra (a.s.) rubbed his face with his blessed hand, wiped his tears, and he kissed the Imam's hands. To... ...and he kissed the Imam's hands. Concluding my talk, let me share a Hadith with you. Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman says: 'I asked Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), "Are you the one who will rise with the truth?" The Imam replied, "Indeed, I will rise with the truth, but the one you are talking about will be the fifth son from my lineage, who will fill the earth with justice and equity just as it would be filled with oppression and tyranny. For him, there is a lengthy occultation (ghaybah) during which many nations will go astray, wondering how anyone could have such a long life. However, there will be some who will remain steadfast. Blessed are those people." The Imam says, "Glad tidings and the promise of Paradise are for those of our Shias who hold fast to our rope during the occultation of our Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)."' They hold fast to our rope. They remain steadfast in our Wilayah and in disassociation (Bara'at) from our enemies. They are from us and we are from them. They are pleased that we are their Imams, and we are pleased that they are our Shias. So, glad tidings (Tooba) be to them, glad tidings be to them! By God, on the Day of Judgment, they will be with us in our station. So, the only supplication to the Lord of the Worlds is that He may hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our Time (a.t.f.s.) to establish the government of the Ahlul Bayt (a.s.) in the world, and grant us the grace (tawfeeq) to remain safe from the tribulations of this era, to attain the recognition (Ma'rifah) of the Imam of our time, and to remain steadfast on our true religion. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim. A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Now the time has come to announce the daily lucky draw winners of the 'Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Panaah-e-Kayanat Mega Quiz', which is being conducted through our computerized lucky draw system. They will receive a prize of Indian ₹1000, and their names are on your screen: Wasi Palsania from Thane, Syeda Adeeba Zahra from Rustampura, Syeda Tasneef Ruhullah from Alipur, Rida Zahra from Kashmir, Shahr Bano from Jamshedpur, and Fayez Rizvi from Mumbai. Many congratulations to all the winners! If anyone's name did not appear in today's winners, there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series, and out of the 12, whoever has given all correct answers in the quizzes of at least seven episodes will be included in the lucky draw for the Mega Prize, which is the pilgrimage (Ziyarat) to Iraq. We thank all of you once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time with another new video. Until then, Khuda... ...with a new video. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Those who remain steadfast in the Wilayah of the Ahlul Bayt during the occultation are promised the highest stations in Paradise.

title: EP11 | Ahle Madina Ki Ahle Bait (a.s.) Se Kinaarakashi | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound isolation faced by Imam Ali (a.s.) and Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) in Medina following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It highlights the betrayal of the Ansar and the people of Medina, who prioritized political opportunism over the Prophet's explicit testament at Ghadir. The narrative focuses on the grief of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.), her establishment of Bayt al-Ahzan, and the enduring lesson of loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt.
content:
On one hand was this loneliness of the Master (a.s.), and on the other hand was the weeping of the Princess (s.a.) over the separation from her father. Today, those who cannot tolerate tears for the grandson of the Prophet, yesterday they could not tolerate the tears of the Prophet's daughter. The Princess (s.a.) used to go and remind the Ansar of the Sunnah and the testament of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), inviting them to support the truth and assist Ali (a.s.). But the Ansar refused, saying, 'We have already pledged allegiance to the first ruler, and you...' So we have already spoken about the ruler, and you two should have come first for the allegiance (bay'ah). In response, he said, 'Should I have left the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in his house without burying him, just to come to you to debate the issue of the Caliphate?' And Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) said, 'After Ghadir, Allah will not accept any excuse or justification from anyone.' This means the Mawla made it clear that for him, at that time, nothing was greater than the respect and burial of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). He was not like those opportunists who took unfair advantage of this opportunity, forced allegiance from the people, and seated themselves on the seat of the Caliph of the Messenger. Grieved by this indifference and disloyalty of the people, Mawla would often weep alone in his city. When asked for the reason, he pointed to the deviation of the people, showing how much the people of Medina had reverted to the era of ignorance (jahiliyyah) and left the true successor of the Messenger alone. And had left the true successor of the Messenger alone. On one hand was this loneliness of Mawla, and on the other hand was the weeping of the Princess (s.a.) over the separation from her father. Today, those who cannot tolerate tears for the grandson of the Messenger, yesterday they could not bear the tears of his daughter. They would come and request Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), 'O Abu al-Hasan, Fatima weeps day and night, and because of her weeping, we can neither sleep peacefully at night nor can we work during the day without disturbance. Please request her to either weep during the day or at night.' The Mawla of the Universe came to the Princess and said, 'O daughter of the Messenger, the people of Medina came to me and asked me to tell you to either weep during the day or at night.' Upon this, the Princess replied, 'O Abu al-Hasan, I am not going to remain among them for many more days, and very soon I will depart. But by God, I will neither remain silent during the day nor at night until I meet my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' On this, Mawla replied, 'Very well...' ...do so.' On this, Mawla replied, 'Very well, O daughter of the Messenger, as you wish.' So, Ali (a.s.) built a room (hujrah) for the Princess (s.a.) in Baqi, which was named Bayt al-Ahzan (House of Sorrows). The Princess (s.a.) would go there every day taking Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (a.s.) with her, and after weeping all day, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) would bring them back home at night. No one could have ever imagined that the people of Medina, who recited the creed (Kalimah) of the Messenger, would distance themselves from the family of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) so quickly and in this manner. Yesterday they abandoned the funeral of the Messenger, then did... O Ali (a.s.), we implore You by the loneliness of Ali (a.s.) and the weeping of Zahra (s.a.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the opportunity to avenge every single tear shed from the eyes of the Princess (s.a.) alongside him. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.
The people of Medina failed to support Imam Ali (a.s.) despite the clear declaration at Ghadir.
Imam Ali (a.s.) prioritized the funeral rites of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) over political power struggles.
Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) refused to be silenced in her mourning for the Prophet.
The people of Medina complained about the grief of the Prophet's daughter, showing their lack of empathy.
Bayt al-Ahzan was built as a place for the Princess (s.a.) to mourn away from the public eye.

The session concludes with a supplication for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).

excerpt: This lecture discusses the primordial covenant known as Aalam-e-Zarr, where all human souls were asked to testify to the Lordship of Allah, the Prophethood of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). content:
Thus, the Lord said, 'Am I not your Lord? And is Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) not your Prophet? And is Ali (a.s.) not your Wali and Imam? And are the purified Imams from his progeny not your Imams, who are the guides and the guided ones?' At that time, all of them said, 'Yes, we bear witness.' In this way...

title: Jung-e-Jamal Kaise Jeeti Gayi? | Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz 2022
excerpt: This lecture recounts the pivotal moment during the Battle of Jamal when Imam Ali (a.s.) commanded the fall of the camel to secure victory. It details the initial attempt by Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah to reach the camel, which was thwarted by the enemy's dense defensive circle. Ultimately, Imam Hasan (a.s.) stepped in, successfully broke through the enemy lines, and brought down the camel, effectively ending the conflict.
content:
O Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, go and attack that camel directly and bring it down. This was the place where the enemy was riding a camel, and the litter (howdah) of that camel was not made of wood but of iron. A plan was made, and the one she was riding was acting as a focal point, and they wouldn't let anyone enter the battle. As I said, you all know that if they... they had initiated this battle from Medina, which was another front to fight... they supported the people of Medina... and as I said, they surrounded the camel from all sides so that no one could get close to it, because if the camel was brought down, it would mean those who came to fight... ...were brought down, it meant those who had come to fight against Mawla would be defeated. If the camel was killed, the enemy would be defeated. The fall of the camel was the sign of the enemy's defeat. Now, what happened in this battle was that the standard-bearer of the army was Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah. Mawla made him the vanguard. Mawla said, 'O Muhammad, go and attack that camel directly and bring it down.' So, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah took his spear and went to attack, tearing through the army. But as history records, the enemy had surrounded the camel so densely that they did not let Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah get close to the circle surrounding it. History records that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah was a very brave and courageous person, which is why Mawla had given him the standard. But the enemy's defense was so strong that they did not allow him to break through that circle. So, he was returning with his spear, and as he was turning back... ...returning with his spear, as he was turning back, Imam Hasan (a.s.) immediately stepped forward, took the spear from his hand, and rushed towards the camel. He advanced in such a way that the obstacles in front of him were cleared away, and Imam Hasan (a.s.), spear in hand, broke through the enemy's circle and launched a direct attack on the camel, bringing it down. Imam Hasan (a.s.) returned with the spear in such a state that drops of the camel's blood were still dripping from the tip of his spear.
The camel served as the central hub and symbol of the enemy's resistance at the Battle of Jamal.
Imam Ali (a.s.) identified the fall of the camel as the key to defeating the opposing army.
Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah was tasked with the mission but faced an impenetrable defensive circle.
Imam Hasan (a.s.) demonstrated exceptional courage and skill by breaking through the enemy lines.
The successful strike by Imam Hasan (a.s.) resulted in the immediate collapse of the enemy's morale and battle formation.
The blood on Imam Hasan's spear served as historical evidence of his direct role in ending the battle.

title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 2 | Characteristics of Imam Mahdi (peace be upon him) - Part 1
excerpt: This lecture provides an in-depth examination of the theological and historical foundations of Mahdaviyyat, focusing on the characteristics and necessity of Imam Mahdi. It explores the concept of the Imam as the divine Proof and the Prophet's successor, emphasizing his role in establishing global justice. The session further validates the lineage of the twelve Imams through both Shia and Sunni sources, contrasting their divine authority with the historical conduct of Umayyad and Abbasid rulers.
content:
May Allah hasten his reappearance and destroy his enemies from among the Jinn and mankind, from the first to the last. I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful, Lord of Majesty and Honor, and I turn to Him in repentance. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, hasten his reappearance and make us among his helpers, supporters, servants, and Shi'a. Do not make us among his enemies. Grant us success in what You love and are pleased with. Do not leave us to ourselves even for a blink of an eye. Do not replace us with others, by the right of Muhammad and his pure progeny. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad, hasten their reappearance, and curse their enemies all together. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Praise be to Allah, our first session under the title 'The Doctrine of Mahdism in the Light of the Holy Quran and Hadith' was very successful, in which the topic of the necessity of the Proof of God was discussed. And if I try to summarize that entire discussion into five points briefly, the five important points that emerged from the first session are these: In the Holy Quran, in Surah Ar-Ra'd, which is the thirteenth chapter of the Holy Quran, in the seventh verse, the Lord of the Worlds says to His beloved, Hazrat Ahmad Mustafa Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), 'Innama anta mundhirun wa likulli qawmin hadin' (You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide). The second point that emerged was that in the exegesis of this verse, traditions exist in both Sunni and Shi'a books, which clarify that 'warner' refers to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and 'guide' refers to Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). The third point that emerged was that this earth can never remain empty of the Proof of God. Whether that Proof is manifest or hidden and concealed. From Hazrat Adam (a.s.) to the Imam of the time, Hazrat Hujjat ibn al-Hasan al-Askari (a.j.t.f.). And if there is no Proof of God, then Allah will not be worshipped, and the earth will be destroyed along with its inhabitants. The fourth point that emerged was that it is because of the existence of the Proof of God that this entire universe remains. This entire universe is receiving its sustenance, and it is only because of belief in the Proof of God and his recognition that Allah will accept people's worship. The fifth and final point that was in yesterday's discussion was the incident of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar Ahwazi, who had performed twenty Hajj pilgrimages with the desire to meet the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.). He narrated the incident of his father, in which his father had willed to fear Allah in spending the Khums money. And how in this incident we also saw how the Proof of God, i.e., the Imam of the Time, manifested his knowledge of the unseen and sent his Tawqi (signed letter) to Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar Ahwazi. And through that Tawqi, it was clarified that whenever one Imam leaves the world, another takes his place. And until the Day of Judgment, Allah will keep His Proof on earth. That is, until the Day of Judgment, the Proof of Allah will remain established and eternal on earth. In this context, the poet has said beautifully: 'The Proof remains only because of the Qa'im, the claim remains only because of the Qa'im. O greatness of the Qa'im, because of you, the Truth is established entirely. He will come, he will surely come and bring the trust of Truth. Why would the Sharia not be established when its very name is Qa'im? O patients of the heart, look, think, understand.' O patients of the heart, look, think, understand. The Messiah of the world is Isa (a.s.), and the Messiah of Isa is the Qa'im. The beginning of the world is Muhammad, look, this has been derived from the hadith 'Awwaluna Muhammad'. This verse touches upon that hadith. Keep in mind: 'O patients of the heart, look, think, understand. The Messiah of the world is Isa (a.s.), and the Messiah of Isa is the Qa'im. And the beginning of the world is Muhammad, the end of creation is Muhammad, our first is the Qa'im, our last is the Qa'im.' With this, let us move towards the second session of this Mahdism webinar, the topic of which you all must have read well on social media by now. The topic of this second session is 'Characteristics of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.)', and today again we have with us the respected Dr. Shabib Rizvi, who will shed more light on this topic. Assalamu Alaikum, Sir. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Viewers, once again, all viewers are requested to send their questions via The Strong Rope's WhatsApp number or through the Q&A and chat in Zoom. But keep in mind that the questions should only be related to the topic and the discussion. So, let us move towards our second topic, which is 'Characteristics of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.)'. Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, for us and for the oppressors who oppressed the right of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and their hereafter, may Allah curse them all. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, reform Your servant and Your Caliph with what You reformed Your prophets and messengers, surround him with Your angels, support him with the Holy Spirit from Yourself, and place guards before him and behind him. They protect him from every evil, and replace his fear with security. He worships You, not associating anything with You, and do not grant anyone from Your creation authority over Your representative. And strengthen him in the jihad against Your enemy and his enemy, and make me among his helpers. Indeed, You are powerful over all things. Furthermore, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'The Mahdi is from us, the Ahlulbayt.' Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Today, the topic of our discussion is the characteristics of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.). Before starting this discussion, one or two introductions are necessary to present to you, and that is that Shi'a... Our belief is this, our belief is this that the Imam is the 'Adl-e-Nabi' (the equivalent of the Prophet), meaning 'Adna al-Ma'rifat' (the minimum recognition). What is the minimum recognition? But before that, it is necessary to state this hadith, why did we bring this discussion of characteristics? We brought the characteristics because there is a famous and well-known tradition that both sects have narrated, i.e., both Shi'a and Sunni, that 'Whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time, dies the death of ignorance.' It is a famous tradition, everyone is aware of it, that whoever dies and does not recognize his Imam of the time, dies the death of ignorance. Ignorance means the death of disbelief, the death of hypocrisy, and the death of misguidance. The tradition exists in this regard. So it is very important that every person recognizes the Imam of his time. Now, when the question was asked, what is the minimum recognition of the Imam? 'Adna' means minimum. So in response, it was said that the Imam said that the minimum recognition is that he is the 'Adl-e-Nabi'. The Imam is equal to the Prophet, except for the degree of Prophethood, because no prophet came after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). There is no prophet after the Messenger of Allah, and as the famous Hadith al-Manzilah states: 'O Ali, your position to me is like that of Aaron to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me.' All these traditions are famous. Now, our belief—the belief of the Shias—is that because the Imam is the successor (qaim-maqam) of the Prophet, he must possess all the characteristics of the Prophet, excluding Prophethood. This includes Wilayat-e-Takwini (universal authority), meaning authority over the entire universe—a status of 'Kun fa-yakun' (Be, and it is). Then there is Wilayat-e-Tashri'i (legislative authority) from Allah, that 'yuhilluna halaluhu wa yuharrimuna haramuhu' (they make His lawful things lawful and His forbidden things forbidden). Allah has given them authority just as He gave it to the Prophet, along with Tayy al-Ard (traversing the earth instantly) and Ilm al-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen). These are the things, these are the characteristics that are common to all the Imams (a.s.). They are common to all. But when we talk about Imam-e-Zamana, that is, Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), some additional characteristics are mentioned. The reason for this is the position that Allah has given him—that he will fill the world with justice and equity and establish a divine government. There are traditions from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) which both sects (Sunni and Shia) have narrated regarding Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.). Besides that, there are numerous traditions, and each thing being described is such that Imam Mahdi is the one who will fill the world with justice and equity just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. In this discussion, we will try to discuss those characteristics that specifically pertain to Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.). Let us take a bird's-eye view first, so that the viewers get an idea of how our discussion will proceed, what the topics will be, and then we will see how much success Allah grants us to speak on this. Wama tawfiqi illa billah (And my success is only by Allah). The first characteristic is that Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.) is from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). No one else can ever claim this. An important reason for stating this characteristic is that anyone who is aware of these traits will never fall into the trap of a false claimant. No one can cheat him, no one can deceive him, because we have seen that throughout history, many people have risen who claimed to be Imam Mahdi, and many people were deceived. So, if one is aware of the characteristics, one will never be deceived. He is from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), meaning he is a Sayyid, the leader of the Sayyids. Insha'Allah, I will try to provide details for each, reading one or two traditions on every topic. He is from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), is the namesake of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and is the final link in the chain of Imamate. He is the son of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), the eleventh Imam of the Shias. His mother was a noble lady, a princess who came in the guise of a slave girl to Iraq, whose marriage took place with Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), and whom we remember by the name of Janab-e-Narjis Khatun. Furthermore, his birth will be hidden and secret, such that people will not be aware of it. Another important characteristic is that for Imam-e-Zamana, there will be two occultations (Ghaybah): a minor occultation and a major occultation, which is called Ghaybah al-Kubra, while the minor one is called Ghaybah al-Sughra. This occultation will be so long that, due to its length, the hearts or beliefs of even good people will be shaken. Another important characteristic is that Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.) will never bow before any tyrant, nor will he give allegiance (bay'ah). Because he will be in occultation, no tyrant can find the Imam, catch him, force him to give allegiance, oppress him, put him in prison, or kill him. Moreover, the Imam himself will have a long life. We will discuss this, Insha'Allah, and when the Imam reappears, although his age will be very long, his appearance will be that of a young man. When he comes, he will appear as a very young, beautiful, and handsome man. The next characteristic is that the Imam will prevail over every tyrant and oppressive king or government in the world, and there is no one who will prevail over the Imam. The Imam will uproot oppression and tyranny; he will end oppression such that no trace of it will remain. 'Yamla'ul-arda qistan wa 'adlan ba'dama muli'at zulman wa jawra' (He will fill the earth with justice and equity after it has been filled with oppression and tyranny). The Imam will possess all the perfections, miracles, and heritage of all the Prophets (a.s.). He will have everything. And furthermore, Allah has arranged and will arrange his guidance and leadership in such a way that an ordinary person in the world cannot even imagine it. These were a few points that were a bird's-eye view of this discussion. Now, let us briefly discuss each topic to see how much we can complete. The first thing is that Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), the Mahdi-e-Maw'ud (the Promised Mahdi), whom the Quran and Hadith have promised, will be only and only from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). That is why both sects have narrated the tradition that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Al-Mahdi min wuldi' (The Mahdi is from my children). Look and reflect; there is a kind of pride in this sentence. The Prophet is saying it with pride, announcing it proudly, that the Mahdi is from my progeny. 'Al-Mahdi min wuldi.' And in another Hadith, he says, 'Al-Mahdi minna Ahl al-Bayt' (The Mahdi is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt). And he said, 'Huwa al-rajulu min 'itrati' (He is the man who will be from my progeny). Once, in a state of intoxication, when the Adhan was called, people said, 'O Commander of the Faithful'—in their terminology—'O Commander of the Faithful, it is time for prayer.' So he told the slave girl who was with him at that time, 'Go, you lead the prayer today.' This was a mockery of Islam. This is what was done to the religion. And in his drunken state, he would say, 'Did I not lead too many prayers today?' This was the state of the Banu Umayya and the Banu Marwan. Then some people made another attempt: the kings of the Banu Abbas. Now, if you count them, their number exceeds 12. And among them, there were one tyrant and oppressor after another. Who killed 70,000 of the Sadat-e-Alawi, and the walls of Baghdad were plastered with their blood. These were the people, these were the Muslims. If we use Allama Iqbal's terminology, 'These are the Muslims, seeing whom even the Jews would be ashamed.' Yes. I think this is enough. Yes, thank you, sir. I think our time is also up. Therefore, there is no room for more questions today. We are grateful to all the listeners and viewers for joining us today in this second session of the religious webinar. Sir, we are deeply grateful to you for discussing this topic. God willing, we take leave from all the viewers, and tomorrow, God willing, at this same time, 10:30 PM India time, we will meet you all. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in.
The existence of a divine Proof (Imam) is essential for the earth's continuity at all times.
Imam Mahdi is the twelfth Imam and the ninth descendant of Imam Husayn, serving as the promised restorer of justice.
The Prophet Muhammad's succession is defined by twelve infallible Imams, a concept supported by numerous Sunni and Shia historical sources.
Recognizing the Imam of the time is a religious obligation to avoid the 'death of ignorance' and ensure spiritual guidance.
The Imam possesses both universal (Takwini) and legislative (Tashri'i) authority, acting as the equivalent of the Prophet in status, excluding prophethood.
The occultation of the Imam (Ghaybah) is a divine test, and his eventual return will restore the original teachings of Islam.
Historical dynasties like the Umayyads and Abbasids are critiqued for their betrayal of the Prophet's legacy and systemic oppression.
