chapters.title: Review of Previous Session on Mahdism
chapters.summary: The speaker summarizes five key points from the first session, emphasizing the necessity of a divine Proof (Imam) on earth for the universe's existence.

chapters.title: Introduction to Imam Mahdi's Characteristics
chapters.summary: The lecture transitions to the characteristics of Imam Mahdi, highlighting the importance of recognizing the Imam to avoid dying in a state of ignorance.

chapters.title: The Imam as the Successor to the Prophet
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the Shia belief that the Imam possesses all the attributes of the Prophet, excluding Prophethood, including universal authority and knowledge of the unseen.

chapters.title: Characteristics of Imam Mahdi
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces the foundational traits of Imam Mahdi, emphasizing his lineage from the Prophet Muhammad and the importance of this knowledge in avoiding false claimants.

chapters.title: Occultation and Divine Leadership
chapters.summary: This section covers the two stages of the Imam's occultation, his long life, and his eventual role in eradicating tyranny to establish global justice.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Pride in the Mahdi
chapters.summary: The speaker explores traditions where the Prophet Muhammad proudly identifies the Mahdi as his descendant and the promised restorer of the original Prophetic Sunnah.

chapters.title: The Certainty of the Mahdi's Arrival
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the Prophet's emphatic oaths regarding the necessity of the Mahdi's appearance and his status as a pure member of the Ahl al-Bayt.

chapters.title: The Promised Mahdi and His Lineage
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the Mahdi is a promised figure from the Prophet's family, whose arrival is divinely guaranteed.

chapters.title: The Twelve Successors of the Prophet
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the famous tradition of the twelve Imams, noting that only the Shia school correctly identifies them.

chapters.title: The Authority and Knowledge of the Imams
chapters.summary: The Prophet described the twelve Imams as having knowledge equal to his own and commanded the Ummah to follow them.

chapters.title: Holding Fast to the Two Weighty Things
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the importance of holding fast to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, noting the historical scarcity of those who remained steadfast.

chapters.title: The Twelve Imams and the Mahdi
chapters.summary: The Prophet identified twelve successors from the lineage of Imam Husayn, culminating in the Mahdi who will establish global justice.

chapters.title: Sunni Hadith Sources on Twelve Imams
chapters.summary: Prominent Sunni scholars and books like Musnad Ahmad and Sahih Muslim confirm the prophecy of twelve successors, emphasizing their necessity for the world's existence.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Imamate
chapters.summary: The lineage of Imamate is traced back to Prophet Ibrahim, clarifying that the covenant is reserved for the infallible descendants.

chapters.title: Critique of Alternative Interpretations
chapters.summary: The speaker refutes attempts by some scholars to include figures like Muawiya and Yazid among the twelve Caliphs, citing their historical crimes against Islam.

chapters.title: Critique of Umayyad and Abbasid Leadership
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the moral corruption and tyranny of the Umayyad and Abbasid rulers, contrasting their actions with true Islamic leadership.

chapters.title: Conclusion of the Webinar Session
chapters.summary: The session concludes with a reflection on historical atrocities against the Sadat-e-Alawi and a formal closing of the webinar.

title: Muharram 1442 Urdu Majlis #08: Takabbur (Arrogance) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual dangers of arrogance (Takabbur) and the necessity of humility in the life of a believer. Drawing on the Hadith of the Cloak and the historical example of Mufaddal ibn Umar, the speaker emphasizes that true guidance requires an inclusive approach rather than elitism or judgment. The session concludes by contrasting the destructive nature of pride with the ultimate sacrifice of Ali Akbar, illustrating that submission to Allah is the only path to spiritual growth.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. 'Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet; O you who believe, send blessings upon him and salute him with a worthy salutation.' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. It is narrated from Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), she said: 'One day, my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), entered upon me and said: "Peace be upon you, O Fatima." I replied: "And upon you be peace." He said: "I feel some weakness in my body." I said to him: "I seek refuge with Allah, O father, from your weakness." He said: "O Fatima, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it." So I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it. Then I looked at him and saw his face shining like the full moon on the night of its completion...' ...Then my son, Hasan (a.s.), approached and said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O light of my eyes and the fruit of my heart.' He said: 'O mother, I smell a beautiful fragrance near you, as if it is the fragrance of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, indeed, your grandfather is under the cloak.' So Hasan went towards the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah. Will you permit me to enter with you under the cloak?' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my son and the companion of my fountain (Kauthar), I permit you.' So he entered with him under the cloak. Then my son, Husayn (a.s.), approached... ...and said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O light of my eyes and the fruit of my heart.' He said: 'O mother, I smell a beautiful fragrance near you, as if it is the fragrance of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, indeed, your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak.' So Husayn went towards them and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather... Will you permit me to enter with you?' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my son and the intercessor of my nation, I permit you.' So he entered with them under the cloak. Then came Abu al-Hasan, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and said: 'Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O Abu al-Hasan, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'O Fatima, I smell a beautiful fragrance, as if it is the fragrance of my brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, he is there under the cloak with your two sons.' So Ali went towards the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Will you permit me to be with you under the cloak?' He replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my brother, my successor, my vicegerent, and the bearer of my banner, I permit you.' So Ali entered with them under the cloak. Then I, Fatima, approached...' Peace be upon her (s.a.)... but when we say 'Ya Rasulullah'... [reciting Hadith al-Kisa]: 'When the gathering under the cloak was complete, Allah, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: O My angels and the inhabitants of My heavens, indeed I have not created a built heaven, nor a stretched earth, nor a shining moon, nor a glowing sun, nor a rotating planet, nor a flowing ocean, nor a sailing ship, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak.' Then the trustworthy Jibra'il (a.s.) said: 'O my Lord, and who is under the cloak?' Allah, the Almighty, the Majestic, replied: 'They are the household of the Prophet...' ...[reciting Hadith al-Kisa]: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and peace be upon you, O mine of the Message...' 'Allah, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: Indeed, I have not created a built heaven, nor a stretched earth, nor a shining moon, nor a glowing sun, nor a rotating planet, nor a flowing ocean, nor a sailing ship, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak.' Then Jibra'il said: 'O Lord, do You permit me to descend to the earth to be with them as a sixth under the cloak?' Allah said: 'Yes, I have permitted you.' So the trustworthy Jibra'il descended and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah...' Then Jibra'il said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you permit me to enter with you under the cloak?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) replied: 'And upon you be peace, O trustee of Allah's revelation. Yes, I permit you.' So Jibra'il entered with them under the cloak and said: 'Indeed, Allah desires to remove all impurity from you, O Ahlul Bayt, and purify you with a thorough purification.' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad... [Music] Even if the sun hides, or the rotation of the universe stops, chanting your name is my life's work. As long as there is a heart in my chest, I will speak your name. Your door is the helper of the helpless, this is my prayer. Yes, your door is the helper of the helpless. As long as there is a heart in my chest, I will speak your name. And what is that? From your door, the flag of victory would come waving to the helpless... ...it would come waving to the helpless. When hands rise in prayer, as long as there is a heart in my chest, I will speak your name. When the coffin is lifted... as long as there is a heart in my chest, I will speak your name. In prostration... There is a special pain of the heart... As long as the heart is in the chest... I am yours... Do not forget... As we say, my heart is in my chest... despite everything, you are still in my breaths... Despite everything, you are still in my breaths... O people of Shaam (Damascus), recognize! O people of... Neither is there now [Abbas], nor is there now [Akbar]... Who is there to protect the veil of the sisters of the Wali (Guardian)? A mother is... supplication... This is Sayyida (s.a.)... In the school of... remember us... even stones... the destination of every tyranny... ...the looted house, the bazaar of the shameless... hiding [her face] with her hair... how will she leave this homeland... How will she leave this homeland... Neither is there now... weeping bitterly near the grave... now she has to bear... Without you, my life is incomplete... O people of Shaam (Syria), recognize us! O people of Kufa, recognize us! This is the son of Mina, this is the son of Haram... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the High, the Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Patron, and the best Helper. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the most noble of Prophets and Messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad, and upon his purified and immaculate Ahl al-Bayt... ...the infallible, the purified, the Imams of guidance... O Allah, bless... ...Imam Husayn (a.s.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)...' [The Prophet said] 'Indeed, you have a status that you cannot reach except through martyrdom...' 'Peace be upon you, O Aba 'Abdillah...' The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had stated in this Hadith, and our elders narrated it on the day of Ashura. My respected father told me: 'O my son Husayn, soon you will be taken to a land where you and a group of your companions will be martyred.' In this regard, various personalities are being forgotten. Those people who, out of love for Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), made efforts, should be mentioned—those who are forgotten or whose life stories people are not well-acquainted with, whom people do not know as they should. That is, their sacrifices are such that we must appreciate them. One of them was Janab Mufaddal, who was a companion of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). His book 'Tawhid al-Mufaddal' is famous, but beyond that book, people do not know much about him. Who was Mufaddal in reality? Mufaddal was a great jurist (faqih) of his time, deeply immersed in the love of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). He had a unique quality; just as every flower has its own unique fragrance, he was like a beautiful bouquet. He was like a beautiful bouquet. And apart from Hadith, Mufaddal had a unique characteristic. Do you know what his unique characteristic was? His quality was that in society, the class of people who are considered completely irreligious, in whom no piety is found—for example, those who fly pigeons, play chess, or engage in other such activities—religious people usually avoid them, saying, 'They are not right, they are sinners, they are lowly, we are destined for Paradise and they are destined for Hell.' They look down upon others with contempt and look at themselves with pride, thinking the other is nothing and they are pious. But Mufaddal's unique quality was that he would keep all of them close. He kept them in his circle so that he could gradually teach them about religion and guide them. This is a wonderful method of propagation (tabligh). But what happened was that since Janab-e-Mufaddal was a great jurist (faqih) and a great scholar of his time, many other... ...scholars of his time, his contemporaries, did not like this. Because they were contemporaries, the jurists and scholars of that time felt that he was spoiling his reputation by associating with such people. Although they were prominent people, sometimes jealousy (hasad) creeps in. This is a factor. Anyway, these people, the jurists of Kufa, did something. They wrote a letter to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) saying, 'You respect Mufaddal so much, he is such an educated man, but look at his company! Look at who he sits with. This tarnishes our reputation, the reputation of our religion, the reputation of the jurists, and ruins our environment. Therefore, you should warn him, reprimand him, and tell him to stop.' They wrote that he associates with people of bad character. After that, the Imam took a step and wrote a reply. It is written in the books... ...It is written in the books that the Imam (a.s.) started writing the reply with his own hands. He wrote the letter but sealed it. After sealing it, the Imam told his messenger, 'Take this and gather all those prominent jurists who wrote the letter, and tell them that the Truthful of the Progeny of Muhammad (Imam Sadiq a.s.) has sent this letter. Tell them they do not have permission to open it. This letter must be handed over to Mufaddal, and Mufaddal must open this letter in front of you.' These people were happy, thinking, 'Now he will be severely punished or reprimanded.' The messenger went and delivered the letter. Mufaddal, being a respectful companion, accepted it. Then, in front of everyone, he opened it and began to read. It was written: 'We need certain things...' ...'We need certain things.' This sentence was written. 'We need some things, so tell those friends of yours with whom you sit and spend time to fulfill these needs.' When Mufaddal read this, the letter ended. The jurists were shocked. The Imam was asking for help, writing to Mufaddal, and specifically asking those friends about whom they had complained to fulfill the Imam's needs! Mufaddal turned to these prominent scholars and said, 'Now you may leave.' He sat them down and told his servant, 'Arrange for refreshments.' One servant got busy with the arrangements, and he told another servant... ...He got busy with the arrangements, and he told the other servant, 'Go and quickly call all those friends of ours—the pigeon-flyers, the game-players, the Ludo-players.' They were all summoned. They came quickly, asking, 'Why has Mufaddal called us today?' Mufaddal said, 'Our Master (a.s.) needs these things. How quickly can you arrange them?' Some went and came back immediately, some went and brought whatever they had. They brought even more than what the Imam had requested. They said, 'Here, the Imam's requirement is fulfilled.' Meanwhile, the prominent scholars sat there, utterly stunned. This is how it is. Sometimes, in these matters, even good religious people hesitate. If someone asks us for something, we think, 'If we have spare, we will give,' but these people pooled all their money and immediately fulfilled the need. And after that, the speaker gathered everyone. Inshallah, Maulana Sahib keeps us in his thoughts. Then, roaring like these people, he began to say, 'Do you think Allah needs your prayers and fasting?' Just because we have come—our prayers, our fasting, our circumambulation (tawaf), our piety—in the light of this, we look down upon everyone else with contempt. No, it is not like that. This approach needs to change. We must take along those people who are generally not religiously inclined in society. They live in a completely different world; they have a different world. So we have to bring them towards religion. Unless we befriend them, how will we bring them towards religion? Of course, they will be influenced by this. Look, a sign of a believer (momin) is that he influences others; he does not get influenced. He does not get affected. This is the sign of a believer. So when we do Tarbiyah (nurturing), we should establish a connection in this manner. Tarbiyah means to convey the message and the model to those who are not religious individuals. Generally, the approach of us religious people is that if someone is irreligious, if they are on the wrong path, avoid them, boycott them. If they are on the wrong path, avoid them, boycott them. No, it is not like that. Befriending them is necessary. Anyway, one more thing, at least they have something in them, and there are no major problems. Anyway, so this is an important thing. Now we come to the actual Hadith, which is about 'Usul al-Kufri al-Thalatha' (The Three Roots of Disbelief). But before reading that Hadith and before explaining it, I request you all to recite Surah al-Fatihah for the demise of Maulana... Syed Raza... [names of deceased scholars/individuals]... He was a pious soul who passed away... came from afar... May Allah have mercy on him, Inshallah. So, this topic is about 'Usul al-Kufri al-Thalatha'. There are three roots. Yesterday, there was a discussion, Inshallah... the whole point was not covered. Let's complete the Hadith. The whole point was not covered, let's complete the Hadith. It is narrated about this that the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Manhumani la yashba'an'—two hungry people are such whose stomachs are never filled: one is the seeker of knowledge (talib al-ilm), and the second is the seeker of wealth (talib al-mal). The seeker of wealth never gets satisfied, no matter how much he earns—he wants more, and more, and more. And whose mention is made in this regard? Qarun. His story is in Surah [Al-Qasas], verse 76 onwards. Qarun had immense wealth, it wasn't just a little. He was so wealthy... people would pray, 'O Qarun, please pray for us, how can we manage without you?' It is said that the keys to his treasures were so heavy that a group of strong men had to carry them... ...the keys were carried by a group of strong men (like 70 men or so). This is about the keys of the treasures, not the treasures themselves. He didn't give charity and kept moving forward. His mind became corrupted due to this wealth. He became arrogant and started disobeying. He started opposing Prophet Musa (a.s.). He thought, 'Musa has become a thorn in my side, I must do something about him.' But what to do? So he spoke to a woman of ill repute (a prostitute) and said, 'Do this...' ...he said to that woman of bad profession, 'Do this: when Musa stands up to preach in public, stand up and say that Musa did a wrong deed with me.' He offered her a lot of money. She agreed, saying, 'No problem.' So when Prophet Musa (a.s.) stood up in the market to preach, Qarun gestured to her to speak. Qarun started challenging Musa, saying, 'Musa, what are you preaching? Look at your own conduct first. This woman...' But the woman got nervous and couldn't speak at first. Then she said, 'O Musa, Qarun gave me money to accuse you falsely, but I fear Allah and cannot falsely accuse a Prophet.' Thus, it was revealed that Qarun's plot failed. This is how greed ruins a person... ...So this is the thing that never fills a person's stomach. Anyway, you know the end of Qarun—how the earth swallowed him up. He was so proud of his wealth, but he was sunk into the earth along with his treasures. He died and became a dweller of Hell. Those who yesterday wished to be like Qarun started saying, 'Indeed, Allah gives sustenance to whom He wills.' If we are believers, we will realize in Paradise that whatever Allah did not give us in the world was actually better for us. Anyway, so this is important. Now, there is a question: how can a person cure this greed? How to cure this disease of greed? Abu Basir asked this question to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam replied that its cure is, first of all, to remember death (maut) always. If you remember death, you will never be greedy. Remember that you will be alone in the grave very soon. You will be completely alone, no one will be with you. And remember when you are laid in the grave, and when the body decomposes... ...and when the body decomposes, the first thing that comes out of the body is the eye. This is the first thing to come out. The Imam says, 'O son of Adam, your eyes will flow out...' A person will feel this. Do not think that since we won't be there, we won't feel anything. No, the human soul (ruh) is there, so the person will feel it. These eyes will flow out, and you will see your own state. All these things will start coming out. Then the bones will start breaking, and after that, only the flesh remains. The Imam says that insects and worms of the grave will come and start eating your flesh. Remember, if a mosquito bites us while we are asleep, we wake up and try to get rid of it. But there, you will feel it, yet you won't be able to do anything. You will feel it but won't be able to do anything. But those who spent their lives in the way of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his Progeny (a.s.)... and this is not a myth, this is still available on YouTube. You know when the Syrian uprising started, some terrorists said they would dig up the graves of the companions of the Prophet and Ahlul Bayt. Those enemies who dug up the graves saw that the bodies of these pious personalities, even after 1,000 or 1,400 years, were completely fresh, like a sleeping child. Normally, if you bury someone, within a few years the body decomposes completely. But for people like Hurr or Sheikh Saduq... when there was a flood in Tehran and the graves were filled with water, they had to move the body of Sheikh Saduq. His body was completely fresh even after 800 or 900 years (he passed away in 381 AH, which is about 1,000 years ago). But the body was completely fresh. Anyway, the Imams say to remember all this—how the worms and insects of the grave will eat your flesh, and your body will decay, decompose, and turn to dust, and you will be completely cut off from the world. No one will be yours, you will go to your final destination. If you remember this daily and continuously, it will direct you towards good deeds for the hereafter. Keep performing deeds for the hereafter, not for this world. This remembrance will prevent you from being greedy for the world. However, greed (desire to acquire more) is allowed in three things: First, in spiritual progress and the hereafter—we should strive to move forward, even compete with each other in good deeds. If someone is doing good, we should try to do even better and constantly improve ourselves daily. Second, greed is allowed in acquiring knowledge (ilm). The more you can study, the more greedy you are for knowledge, the better. Third, in performing obligatory acts (wajibaat) and good deeds—the more eager and greedy a person is in performing them, the better. ...especially in guiding others, because there is nothing greater or better in this world than guiding others. Guiding others is superior to all optional acts of worship. Guiding others, teaching them, and showing them the right path is the best deed. That is why Allama Majlisi, in his book Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 2, has a chapter titled 'Thawab al-Ta'lim wa al-Hidayah' (The Reward of Teaching and Guiding). In it, Allama Majlisi has compiled more than a hundred Hadiths. If you read even one Hadith, you will see how much reward there is for a person who guides others. Therefore, this is the best thing; there is nothing better than this. The more greedy you are for this, the better. Teach as much as you can. But if you teach just to build your worldly life—thinking you will get money, fame, or prestige—then if that is your intention, it is all in vain; nothing will be of use. So these are the things... One thing is that there is so much reward for reciting Salawat. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The second thing, which is today's topic, is arrogance (Takabbur) and pride (Istikbar). What is arrogance? It is to consider oneself better than others. It is condemned in every form. Iblis had said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.' When Allah commanded all the angels to prostrate to Adam (a.s.), everyone prostrated except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant (*wastakbara wa kana minal kafireen*). Because of this arrogance, he became a disbeliever and was expelled from the court of Allah. Allah said, 'Get out of here, for you are rejected (Rajim), and indeed, my curse is upon you.' Even when you look at... Our Imams (a.s.) state in the light of the Holy Quran that one must stay away from arrogance (Takabbur). Because this arrogance is the greatest sin, and there is no sin greater than this. This is a defect, a human defect, which causes the most suffering in this world and the hereafter. In this world, human nature is such that people get irritated by an arrogant person. You can ask anyone. It might be that someone flatters him to his face, praises him, and says, 'You are exceptional,' lifting him up, but as soon as he leaves, he despises him. Because people hate those who show arrogance. Whenever he speaks, he says, 'I...' He says, 'This work was done by me.' For example, a person built a mosque, and his name is written on it. If someone asks, 'Who built this mosque?' and his name is removed, he gets upset. Did you build the mosque for yourself or for Allah? If you built it for Allah, then whether your name is there or not shouldn't matter. But he says, 'The money I gave, the land was mine, so my name should be there.' This means he is doing it for his own name, so that his name is glorified. If you are doing it for your own name, then it is not for Allah. If you built the mosque for yourself, then your name is there. But if you built it for Allah, then erase your name. He erased his name... Instead of his name, write: *Haza min fadli Rabbi* (This is by the grace of my Lord). After that, a person does not act this way. And in the hereafter, his end is terrible. This is the guise of Iblis, the clothing of arrogance. When Iblis was expelled from the court of Allah, Allah said, 'Get out of here.' He was expelled. Why? Because sometimes a person has knowledge, but arrogance comes in, and that knowledge becomes useless. Knowledge is there, but when arrogance comes, it becomes useless. Now, look at Iblis. He worshipped for 6,000 years. And we do not know—this is said to make us understand—whether these were the years of this world or the years of the hereafter. 6,000 years, because you know what the calculation is. Because the life of this world compared to the hereafter is like a single second. If you calculate, Iblis worshipped Allah for 6,000 years. Leave aside 6,000 years; Islam has only been here for 1,400 years in total. How many years have we lived? 50 years, 60 years, 70 years? The youngsters have lived only 20 or 25 years, and some have already grown old. Yes, some have grown old, and some are still young. 6,000 years! But there was one flaw in him, one evil trait that completely cast him out. In Iblis, there was no spirit of submission (Tasleem); it was mixed with arrogance, and that is what cast him out. Look at how he recognized Allah. Look at his dialogue. He said, 'You are my God.' He said, 'You created me from fire.' He did not deny that Allah is the Creator. Pharaoh was worse than Iblis; Pharaoh said, 'I am your supreme lord' (*Ana Rabbukum al-A'la*). And today's self-proclaimed godmen, who have 'god' attached to their names, are worse than Iblis. They have misled people and set up many partners against Allah. But look at what Iblis is saying. The second thing he says is, 'Because You have expelled me...' Because You have expelled me from Your court, what will I do? 'I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path' (*la-aq'udanna lahum sirataka al-mustaqeem*). So, Iblis even knew what the straight path (Sirat al-Mustaqeem) was, which many Muslims today do not even know. People are searching for where the straight path is. Is it in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, India, Pakistan, or Bangladesh? Where is it? When it comes to misleading people, he says, 'I will mislead them.' This means he has this arrogance and overconfidence that 'I will do it.' Look at how much he understood. Now, look at how Iblis went astray. There is a Hadith that Iblis used to visit the Prophets (a.s.). He had a special hat with him, but he would take it off in front of the Prophets. A Prophet asked him, 'Why do you have this hat?' He replied, 'Through this, I trap and hunt people.' (In Mumbai, 'wearing a hat' has become a slang for fooling someone). Recite a Salawat. He said, 'Since you spared me, I will give you three pieces of advice. Listen to me.' This narration is recorded in books. There is a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) about this. But despite his high level, because of one flaw—arrogance—he was expelled from the court of Allah. In the world, you might know of many scholars... you know of scholars who were very knowledgeable, but in the end... ...very knowledgeable, but in the end, he went astray. In the old days, there was a person who used to guide people, a leader. His name was Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He used to visit the Imam (a.s.) and study under him. He studied so much that he became a great scholar. But when the time of trial came, he could not withstand it. When the Imam passed away, he said... He went astray. He was a great scholar in the time of the Imam, but he became misguided. He went astray in his knowledge, in his actions, and in society. Now, he came to the Imam of the time... He came to the Imam of the time and sat before him. He said, 'O Imam...' He knew the secrets, he knew that the Imam was superior, but he still showed arrogance. Look at how a person falls from such a high level. That is why there is a very significant Hadith. It is narrated that people work hard, perform worship, gain knowledge, and reach a very high spiritual station. But when they reach there, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Either he will fall from there, or he will go even higher.' And then the Imam (a.s.) says... And then he condemns it. 'Most of them are low' (aktsaruhum yasfalun). This is the state after falling from above. Therefore, one should always pray: 'O Allah, do not leave us to ourselves for even the blink of an eye.' If You leave us to ourselves for even a single moment, we are ruined. Ayatullah Sayyid Mujtaba Musavi Lari (r.a.), who passed away a few years ago, was a highly responsible scholar. Why am I saying this? Because we should not steal others' intellectual property. Whoever said it, we must credit them. What has been stated here is his sentence: 'If my deeds do not take me to Hell, at least they are not good enough to take me to Heaven either.' If you ask why I hope for Heaven, it is because of this love for Hussain (a.s.), these tears I shed for Hussain (a.s.), and the complete trust in him that he will not let these tears go to waste. What amazing scholars we have had! There are even videos of this short speech of his. Anyway, this is his saying. Then, Imam Ali (a.s.) says regarding pride (takabbur)... ...regarding pride (takabbur), what does it do? Look at Iblis and his efforts. Compared to his efforts, we are nothing. He worshipped Allah for six thousand years—whether of this world or the hereafter, only Allah knows. And because of his pride of a single moment, Allah destroyed all his worship of six thousand years. When Allah dealt with him like that for a single moment of pride, what is the standing of others? Then, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Cleanse your hearts of the diseases of ignorance and malice.' Remove these spiritual diseases from your hearts and cure them. Otherwise, these are all satanic whispers. All these spiritual diseases of the heart are Satan's whispers. Satan is putting them in your heart, blowing them into you. That is why we are instructed: 'Seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the outcast.' I seek refuge in Allah from the rebellious, misleading Satan. After this, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Adopt humility (tawadu) and put it in your minds.' Keep telling yourself: 'I am nothing, my worship is nothing, my knowledge is nothing. Everyone else is better than me because they do not know my sins, but I know my own sins. I do not know their hidden deeds, but looking at my own inner state, I am the worst.' Keep telling yourself this constantly. And crush any desire for self-importance or false pride in your heart under your feet. My honor, my self-respect... 'He stood up so rudely, he didn't even greet me!' If someone doesn't greet us, we get upset. We should take the initiative in greeting (salam). If elders do not practice the religion, how will the children learn? The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Crush this ego of yours under your feet.' There was a very famous scholar, Ayatullah Tehrani (r.a.). Despite writing many books and being highly advanced in the field of knowledge, whenever he wrote a book, he would not put his name on it. His students insisted, but he refused. He was an incredibly great scholar, yet so humble. He was a great scholar, but he didn't want his name published. People said, 'If we don't write the author's name, how will people know who wrote it?' He said, 'Okay, just write "G. Tehrani" (or "J. Tehrani").' Writing just 'J' or 'G' doesn't reveal the full name. His students started publishing it like that. What a great personality! The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Crush this desire for fame and honor under your feet.' And then he says: 'Remove the collar of pride that you have tied around your neck and put it aside.' Put aside this collar of pride. And adopt humility (tawadu). Use humility as a weapon against Iblis. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Use your humility as a weapon.' This is from Sermon 192 (Khutbah al-Qasi'ah) of Nahj al-Balagha. In this narration, it is mentioned that as a person's pride increases, their intellect decreases. Allah diminishes their intellect, and they lose their manners. It's not that they can excuse themselves by saying they lacked manners. What is pride? It is when a person thinks they are something. But the opposite is true. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'If someone praises you, it is as if they are slaying you.' We should be like those who do not care about the blame of any blamer in the way of Allah. Then he says: 'We do not seek superiority over others.' Our intention should not be to seek high status. Prophet Sulayman (a.s.) prayed for a kingdom, but Imam Ali (a.s.) said: 'O world, I have divorced you three times.' 'I have divorced you three times.' Allah has praised those who do not seek loftiness or corruption on earth, and the ultimate good end is for the righteous. Those who are actually small try to show off that they are big. Those who lack capacity try to project greatness. But the righteous are those who do not possess these negative traits. Their focus is solely on the Hereafter and Paradise, and their focus in this world is on performing good deeds so they may attain Paradise. There are many such narrations. Pride (kibriya) belongs only to Allah. No one else in the world is great; everyone is insignificant before Allah. ...everyone is insignificant before Allah. In a Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Allah says: 'Pride (kibriya) is My cloak, and greatness is My robe. Whoever tries to snatch them from Me, I will cast him into the Fire.' Therefore, pride is a dangerous thing. It leads a person to a point where they start questioning the commands of Allah, rejecting religion, and abandoning worship. They might say, 'How can this be? We are in the 21st century, why are we talking about old things?' This is a sign of arrogance—thinking that one's own intellect is so great that they can question Allah's laws. If we want to submit to Allah, we must understand what true humility is. He asked, "What is the definition of pride (takabbur)?" One is to look down upon others, to consider them inferior to oneself—"I am great, they are small," "I am highly educated, they are less educated," "I am this, they are that." And the second is to stand in opposition to the truth, to confront it. This is the definition of pride. One is egoism (ana'iyyah), which I explained to you from the beginning: "I am better than others." And the second is to stand in opposition to the truth. Imam (a.s.) was asked, "Why does a person become arrogant? What is the reason?" The Imam (a.s.) replied, "Because of a deficiency he finds within himself." In psychology, there is an interesting topic: to hide an inferiority complex, they try to show how great they are. Let's take a simple example. Since there are children here, let's give them a sports example, like cricket, so they understand. A child who plays cricket at school or is a cricket expert at home, he won't sit outside boasting to people, "I am a great cricketer." But the one who is truly a great cricketer will never sit around showing off that he is a great cricketer. However, the one who only scores 22 runs at home will sit outside boasting because no one knows him in the match, so he wants to show off. And the one who is truly great in any field, you see, he will never try to show off. The one who is truly great will never show off that "I am great," just like... ...will never show off that "I am great." Just like... [unclear]. My friends, what can I say about the character of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)? The discussion remained incomplete. If possible, tomorrow we will cover these points, if Allah gives us the opportunity and life, because life and death are in the hands of Allah. Today, let us go to Karbala and remember that youth about whom Imam Hussain (a.s.) did not even wait until he was martyred. "O my son, now you have come forward." When the turn of Bani Hashim came, the replica of the Prophet, Ali Akbar (a.s.), came forward. Hussain (a.s.) said, "Go, my son, go and be martyred." For Ali Akbar, there was perhaps no greater joy than this. He prepared himself. First, he went to his father to ask for permission. In such a situation, the father said, "Why are you asking me, my son? Go and ask your mother, who raised you with such love and care for 18 years." What a strange scene of Karbala! What strange mothers they were! "Go and take permission from your mother." He came and stood before Umme Layla. He said, "Mother, give me permission." The mother said, "My son, did I raise you for any other reason than to sacrifice your life for Hussain?" Ali Akbar said, "Mother, give me permission, but if I am asked on the Day of Judgment who was dearer to you, my Hussain or Ali Akbar, what will you answer? What will you answer?" She said, "My son, go..." ..."what will you answer?" She said, "My son, go. If it is a matter of my brother, go and be martyred." Ali Akbar set out. Historians write that as Ali Akbar was about to leave, someone grabbed his cloak and pulled it. When Ali Akbar tried to move forward, someone pulled his cloak. It is not explicitly written in the books, but it is understood that if an elder had stopped Ali Akbar, they would have held his arms. But grabbing the cloak means it was a small child who was stopping him. And it was Sakina (a.s.) who was stopping him, saying, "Ali Akbar, have mercy on our state, have mercy on our loneliness. You are leaving, but my father... my father..." Akbar set out for the battlefield. Hussain (a.s.) looked towards the heavens and said, "O Lord, bear witness against these people. A youth is going towards them who, in his appearance, character, and speech, resembles Your Messenger the most. O Lord, whenever we yearned to see the Prophet, we would look at Akbar..." ...who, in his appearance, character, and speech, resembles Your Messenger the most. O Lord, whenever we yearned to see the Prophet, we would look at Akbar. Hussain (a.s.) said, "My son is coming back in a short while." Oh, what a moment for a father! If you are a parent, you would understand the pain of a son's departure. Ali Akbar went and fought. Until now, whoever went to the battlefield never returned alive, but Ali Akbar returned. Why? Because a mother's heart was restless. She was standing at the door of the tent. Her face had turned pale. She was praying, "O Lord, return my Akbar to me..." ...She was praying, "O Lord, return my Akbar to me." Umme Layla went inside the tent and prayed, "O Savior of Yusuf, return my Akbar to me." The prayer of the mother was answered, and Ali Akbar returned. But in what state? He was severely wounded, and his chest was pierced. He said, "Father, is there a drop of water? The weight of the armor and thirst are killing me." Hussain (a.s.) said, "My son, put your tongue in my mouth." When Ali Akbar did so, he felt that his father's tongue was even drier, like a piece of wood. Hussain (a.s.) said, "My son, go back. Soon your grandfather, the Messenger of Allah, will quench your thirst." Ali Akbar returned to the battlefield. Suddenly, a cry arose, "O father, accept my last salutation!" "O father, do not trouble yourself." Hussain (a.s.) reached the battlefield. He pulled the spearhead from Ali Akbar's chest. Blood gushed out. Hussain (a.s.) cried out, "O my son, after you, dust be upon this world! You have been relieved of the sorrows of this world, but your father is left alone and friendless among the enemies." O Ali Akbar! O Allah, for the sake of Ali Akbar, ease our difficulties. O Allah, resolve the problems of those who are distressed. Cure those who are sick. Grant debt relief to those in debt. chapters.title: The Hadith of the Cloak

chapters.title: Lamentations and Historical Context
chapters.summary: The lecture transitions into poetic lamentations regarding the tragedy of Karbala and the suffering of the Ahlul Bayt.

chapters.title: The Character of Mufaddal ibn Umar

chapters.title: Criticism and Jealousy Among Scholars
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how contemporary jurists criticized Mufaddal for associating with sinners, illustrating the dangers of arrogance and jealousy.

chapters.title: The Imam's Lesson on Inclusivity

chapters.summary: While worldly greed is discouraged, the speaker highlights that greed is encouraged in spiritual progress, seeking knowledge, and guiding others.

title: KULL-E-IMAAN (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2023 🎁🎉 | 11-Feb-2023 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture presents the Kulle Iman Grand Quiz 2023, organized to celebrate the birth of Imam Ali (a.s.) on the 13th of Rajab. The session explores the divine titles, virtues, and Quranic status of Imam Ali, emphasizing his role as the 'Speaking Quran' and the sole custodian of the Prophet's true teachings. Through historical traditions and theological discourse, the speakers highlight the necessity of Wilayah and the spiritual dangers of denying the status of the Ahlul-Bayt.
content:
TSR presents 'Kulle Iman (a.s.) Grand Quiz'. Bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasani salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alim min ash-shaytani ar-rajim. Bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. Wa salla Allahu 'alayka ya waliyyal 'asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. Dear ones, I begin my speech with four lines by Janab Nazir Turabi. 'Whose oneness is called Ahad, the limit of independence, the sign of Samad. Whose oneness is called Ahad, the limit of independence, the sign of Samad. In His house, the birth of the beloved, outside, He begets not, nor is He begotten, praise without limit.' For that All-Knowing, Wise, Merciful, and Generous God, who adorned His own house with the birth of Ali (a.s.), and no matter how much gratitude is expressed, no matter how many prostrations of gratitude are offered in His court, it is less, for He kept us all attached to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and the Imams (a.s.) from his progeny, and along with this, granted the ability, the fortune, and the honor that we adorn every gathering of ours with their remembrance. And if the talk is about the 13th of Rajab, then its luminosity increases even more. Yes, dear ones, today we are present once again with our 'Kulle Iman Grand Quiz' on the occasion of the 13th of Rajab al-Murajjab, the blessed birth of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). First of all, we offer our heartfelt congratulations to all of you on the 13th of Rajab and all the births that take place in the month of Rajab al-Murajjab, and we welcome you all to our gathering. Before we begin our discussion today, let us tell you what the rules of our quiz are today. The quiz rules are on your screen. A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alim min ash-shaytani ar-rajim. Bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. Wa salla Allahu 'alayka ya waliyyal 'asr adrikna. Rules of the Kulle Iman (a.s.) Grand Quiz. The quiz link is live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link and register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You only need to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in any hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who provide the correct answers to all questions, 14 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, and they will be given these prizes. Respected viewers, if we talk about the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), human intellect cannot reach its depth. That is, the intellect is incapable of contemplating it, and the tongue is incapable of describing his virtues. A poet has rightly said: The pen of every historian in the world says, The pen of every historian in the world says, What kind of miracle is this that I see? I have been writing about the virtues of Ali for centuries, But the page still appears blank. I have been writing about the virtues of Ali for centuries, But the page still appears blank. Yes, respected viewers, just as we presented a few aspects of the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) in your service last year, in which we discussed the arrival of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) in the House of Kaaba and the names given to him by his parents and by Allah. So, let us continue this series this year as well and present to you a discussion on how the names of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) have been revealed in the Holy Quran. Yes, respected viewers, just as when a child is born in someone's house, they try to give the child the best possible name, and when it comes to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), his parents must have surely chosen his name in the best possible way. For instance, his noble father, Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.), named him Zaid, and his noble mother, Janab-e-Fatima bint Asad, named him Haidar. The name through which Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) introduced himself in front of Marhab, and when he was born in the House of Kaaba—that is, born in the House of Allah—Allah Himself stepped forward and gave His own name to Ali (a.s.); Allah Himself named him Ali. So, let us begin today's discussion on what other names Allah has given to Hazrat Ali (a.s.) in the Holy Quran. Continuing our discussion on this, we have with us in our gathering today Janab Shabiul Hasan Sahab and Janab Ahsan Jafri Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We welcome you both to our gathering from the bottom of our hearts. Let us begin our discussion today. So, Ahsan Bhai, I would like to start the discussion with you; regarding our topic today, which is the names of Hazrat Ali (a.s.) that appear in the Holy Quran, we would like you to shed more light on it. Certainly, Insha'Allah, I will try. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim, Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim, wa salla Allahu 'alaika ya Wali al-'Asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. First of all, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the viewers and to you on the occasion of the 13th of Rajab, with the hope that this small effort of ours will be accepted in the court of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), Insha'Allah. Insha'Allah. And as you have asked about the mention of Mawla-e-Kainat in the Holy Quran in this regard. Now, although we keep hearing many discussions about Mawla-e-Kainat in our various gatherings and Majalis, there is a very interesting Hadith here, which is not just a Hadith but an entire sermon. The Mawla himself has delivered the entire sermon in which he is introducing himself, and in it, the Mawla himself, with his own noble tongue, is—in a way—stating the attributes of Ali by the tongue of Ali. Yes, Subhan Allah. That the Mawla himself is mentioning in his sermon those names that Allah has specified for him in the Holy Quran. Subhan Allah. The incident is such that after the Battle of Nahrawan, as you know, and all the viewers know, the Battle of Nahrawan was the last battle of the Mawla's apparent life. After returning from the Battle of Nahrawan, when he came back to Kufa, having won the Battle of Nahrawan and defeated the Khawarij, after that, when he returned to Kufa. When the Mawla reached Kufa, he received the news that Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan was insulting the Mawla and was selectively killing the Mawla's companions. title: EP16 | 12 Khalifa - Eteraazaat Ke Jawaabaat | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines the Prophetic tradition regarding the twelve Caliphs, arguing that the Shia doctrine of the twelve Imams is the only interpretation that aligns with historical and theological consistency. The speaker refutes common objections regarding the terminology used in these narrations, specifically addressing the Prophet's use of 'Khalifatayn' to link the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt. By citing authentic Sunni and Shia sources, the lecture establishes the divine status of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Ahl-e-Bayt as the rightful guides of the Muslim community.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... (repeated). I bear witness that Ali is the Wali of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjah son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and allow him to enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his supporters, his Shia, his servants, and his followers, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. The discussion was that the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'La yazalu hadhad-dinu ya'nil-Islamu qa'iman 'azizan mani'an' (This religion, meaning Islam, will remain established, honored, and invincible). There are different wordings in different narrations. This Islam will be honored, exalted, and strong as long as 'hatta yakuna fihi ithna 'ashara khalifah' (as long as there are 12 Caliphs in it). All of them... then the narrator, Jabir ibn Samura, says that when the Prophet said this, people started making noise, so I could not hear what the Prophet said next. I later asked my father, who was close to the Prophet, what the Prophet had said. My father replied that the Prophet said: 'Kulluhum min Quraish' (All of them will be from Quraish). After that, I submitted to you that many people tried to somehow arrive at this figure of 12. In this figure of 12, the scholars of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni scholars) included Yazid ibn Mu'awiya, Marwan, and such people who were drunkards and had no connection or link to the religion. They mentioned them just to somehow fit the number 12, but it was not working. Some said there would be some after the Mahdi, as Ibn al-Jawzi said, that they would be after the Mahdi, not now. Whereas the Prophet was talking about the time after himself. These were all their justifications; there was nothing to them. Now, when they saw that the Shia were explaining it in such a way that the 12 are all from the Prophet's lineage, all from Banu Hashim, and one after another, the sequence fits perfectly, and all of them, Alhamdulillah, are 'A'lamun-nasi afdalun-nasi' (the most knowledgeable of people, the most virtuous of people). They possessed all perfections, were the most knowledgeable, and were superior to people in every respect. When they saw this, some extremist Nasibi scholars of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, who truly hated the Shia and the Ahl al-Bayt, began to attack viciously, among whom two names can be specifically mentioned, such as Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Jawzi. They attacked very viciously, saying that the Shia are ignorant, and so on. They raised some objections to the Shia explanation, asking why the 12 Imams of the Shia do not fit this Hadith. They raised objections. Actually, if you look at them, the objections are completely childish; they have no substance. But regardless, because they made them, and especially since they are present on Arabic websites on the internet—and perhaps we haven't gone through English websites, but they are present on Arabic websites—I thought I should provide a response so that people's hearts may be satisfied. Even though you will see that they are completely childish objections, there is an Urdu proverb for this: 'Khisyani billi khamba noche' (A frustrated cat scratches the pillar). When one doesn't understand anything, when a cat gets frustrated and doesn't know what to do, it starts scratching the pillar. That is exactly the situation; when they didn't understand anything, they made such objections. Now, listen to the first objection. They say that the Hadith says: 'La yazalu hadhad-dinu 'azizan qa'iman hatta yakuna fihi ithna 'ashara khalifah'. It is written 'Caliph', nowhere is 'Imam' written. The Prophet did not say 'Imam', he said 'Caliph'. Whereas the Shia have Imams. Now look at how childish this is. While the 12 Imams are the Caliphs of the Prophet, the successors of the Prophet. When Allah appointed His Hujjah, the first Hujjah, Prophet Adam (a.s.), He said: 'Inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah' (Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority). Allah has the authority to appoint a Caliph. The Quran says: 'Wa ma kana limu'minin wa la mu'minatin idha qadallahu wa rasuluhu amran an yakuna lahumul-khiyaratun fi amrihim' (It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair). This is a verse from Surah al-Ahzab. When Allah and His Messenger have made a decision, people have no choice. No believing man or woman has the choice to select someone of their own choosing. When Allah has selected, the matter is settled. But regardless, they say 'Caliph'. Now, they say 'Caliph', but the Prophet has used the word 'Caliph' for the Ahl al-Bayt in other narrations. For example, the very famous Hadith, you must have heard the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. In the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, the Prophet said: 'Inni tarikun fikum al-thaqalayn' (I am leaving among you two weighty things). One is the Book of Allah and the other is my Ahl al-Bayt. And the Hadith is long, you know the full Hadith: 'Inni tarikun fikum al-thaqalayn kitaba Allahi wa 'itrati ahla bayti. Ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abada' (I am leaving among you two weighty things, the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt. As long as you hold fast to them, you will never go astray after me). 'Fa-innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayyal-hawd' (And they will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Pond [of Kawthar]). Now here the Prophet said: 'Fanzuru kayfa takhlufuni fihima' (Look at how you treat them after me). 'Takhlufuni' is derived from 'Khilafah'. Look at how you treat them after me. But they say, 'No, where is 'Caliph' written in this?' Okay, fine, brother, let us complete the argument on that too. Now, for example, the very famous scholar of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, Nuruddin al-Samhudi. Nuruddin al-Samhudi narrates from Zayd ibn Thabit that the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Inni tarikun fikum khalifatayn' (I am leaving among you two Caliphs). Now, is there anything left after this? I am leaving two Caliphs among you. 'Kitabullahi 'azza wajall', one is the Book of Allah, the Book of Allah 'azza wajall, which is 'hablun mamdudun ma baynas-sama'i ilal-ard' (a rope extended between the heaven and the earth), the Book of Allah. 'Wa 'itrati ahla bayti' (And my progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt). 'Wa innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayyal-hawd' (And they will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Pond). This is Samhudi's narration. Similarly, Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrates in his Musnad: 'Inni tarikun fikum khalifatayn'. Ahmad ibn Hanbal writes that Aswad ibn Amir narrated this from Sharik. Sharik narrated from Rakin, and Rakin narrated from Qasim ibn Hassan, and Qasim ibn Hassan narrates from Zayd ibn Thabit. This is a complete chain of narration. Ahmad ibn Hanbal has provided the full chain because the name of his book is 'Musnad'. Musnad means he narrated the Hadith with its chain of authority, and with this full chain, he says that Zayd ibn Thabit says the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, and then the Hadith is: 'Inni tarikun fikum khalifatayn. Khalifatayni kitaba Allahi 'azza wajall hablun mamdudun ma baynas-sama'i wal-ard'. This is the same narration as Ahmad ibn Hanbal's. So, this is exactly the narration of 'Khalifatayn', and this is not one or two; for example, Ahmad ibn Hanbal himself is an Imam, Ahmad ibn Hanbal is called 'Imam al-Muhaddithin'. He has narrated it in his Musnad. If you are not satisfied with this, then write down more references. For example, al-Hammu'i, Imam al-Juwayni al-Hammu'i, yes, he writes in 'Fara'id al-Simtayn'. Al-Sakhawi, who was the teacher of al-Suyuti, al-Sakhawi in Egypt, al-Sakhawi was the teacher of al-Suyuti. He wrote a book called 'Istijlab Irtiqa' al-Ghuraf'. In that, Volume 1, page 371, Hadith number 74, and Chapter 1, and he has narrated this narration from Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Then al-Suyuti himself, in his book 'Ihya' al-Mayyit', page 30, Hadith number 56, he has narrated from two people, al-Suyuti, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal and also from al-Tabarani. Al-Tabarani, who is a famous author of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, is a very great scholar who wrote three Ma'ajim (plural of Mu'jam), his are famous. Ma'ajim, meaning Mu'jam: Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, and Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir. These three Ma'ajim of al-Tabarani are famous. Right? After that, 'Al-Budur al-Safirah 'an Umur al-Akhirah'. Right? Here, he has page number 248, Hadith number 625, and has narrated the narration from Ibn Abi Asim. This is al-Suyuti's book, and al-Suyuti has also in 'Al-Durr al-Manthur', his Tafsir, this is his Tafsir. Al-Suyuti's Tafsir is 'Al-Durr al-Manthur', Volume 2, page 60, and where did he narrate this Hadith? Under verse number 103 of Surah Ali 'Imran: 'Wa'tasimu bihablillahi jami'an wa la tafarraqu' (And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided). Look, hold firmly to the rope of Allah and look, do not cause division. Hold firmly to the rope of Allah. What is the rope of Allah? The Quran. And the Ahl al-Bayt. Now, whoever has left the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt has left the rope of Allah. And after that, al-Suyuti has also narrated it in 'Jami' al-Saghir', Volume 1, page 157, Hadith number 2631, under the alphabet 'Alif'. And he has narrated it here too from Ahmad and al-Tabarani. And after that, which is what I told you about al-Suyuti in response to the objection, then Mulla Ali Qari, Mulla Ali Qari has narrated this Hadith in 'Sharh Mishkat', Volume 5, page 601, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal and al-Tabarani. Al-Shaykhani has narrated it in 'Al-Sirat al-Sawi' from Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Azizi has narrated it in 'Al-Siraj al-Munir fi Sharh Jami' al-Saghir', 'Al-Siraj al-Munir' is the commentary on al-Suyuti's 'Jami' al-Saghir'. This commentary was written by al-Azizi. He has narrated this Hadith from Ibn Abi Asim, from Abu Bakr Shaybah, and from al-Tabarani. Then al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir, al-Tha'labi, the name of the Tafsir is 'Al-Kashf wal-Bayan'. In the commentary of which verse? In the commentary of verse number 103 of Surah Ali 'Imran: 'Wa'tasimu bihablillahi jami'an wa la tafarraqu. Wadhkuru ni'mata Allahi 'alaykum idh kuntum a'da'an fa'allafa bayna qulubikum fa'asbahtum bini'matihi ikhwana'. This is from Surah Ali 'Imran, right? Hold firmly to the rope of Allah and look, do not cause division. Now, in so many places, these people have used the word 'Khalifatayn'. The Prophet used 'Khalifatayn'. The companions used 'Khalifatayn'. The narrators used 'Khalifatayn'. The scholars used 'Khalifatayn'. Even after that, people like Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Jawzi have an objection as to why 'Khalifatayn' was used. This is childish, brother, just like why did the Prophet say 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa 'Aliyyun mawlahu'? 'Man kuntu khalifatahu fa 'Aliyyun khalifatahu'? Is this any point? These kinds of objections, why wasn't 'Caliph' used? Like a horseman of the Caliph. No, there are different words in different places. This is one objection, for which we see there are enough references. There is no need for more references than this. And if even after this, someone does not agree, then that is their problem. Now, what is the second objection? That the Shia were not believers in the 12 Imams at all. They became believers later. And what proof do they bring for this? Now look at what the proof is. They say the proof is that the Shia formed many sects. Some became Zaydi, some became this, some became that. Therefore, the different Imams—some have 6 Imams, some have 8, some have 7. The 12-Imam ones came later, they were formed later. If this is the proof, if this is the reasoning, then this means Islam has been ruined. You have ruined Islam itself. Because there are many more sects among other Muslims than among the Shia. They simply do not accept it. They do not accept any Imam. Except for a few hadiths from the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.), there is nothing else. Nothing at all. So, this is their sectarian objection, which is absolutely childish, infantile, baseless, and nonsensical. I will not present many more objections for your consideration because, look, they are all of this same nature. Right? They say that the Prophet said, 'All of them will be from the Quraish.' If it was truly intended to appoint Ali (a.s.) and his progeny, then what should have been said? It should have been said, 'After me, all of them will be Ali and his progeny.' Now, there are many answers to this, but to be very brief, I say: where the Prophet did say 'Ali', did you accept it? Even there, you played with words, saying, 'No, the meaning of Mawla is friend, the meaning of Mawla is companion, the meaning of Mawla is this, and the meaning of Mawla is to love,' and so on. You started stating 36 meanings from the lexicon. Where the Prophet said very clearly, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am Mawla, Ali is his Mawla), and this hadith—even someone like Ibn al-Albani, who is among the strict hadith scholars of the Ahl-e-Hadith, who wrote books like 'Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah' and 'Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sa'imah'—even Nasiruddin al-Albani declared this hadith as Sahih (authentic). That 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa Aliyun mawlahu' is a Sahih hadith. And InshaAllah, when we discuss the Hadith of Ghadir, we will explain its chain of narration in detail. Now look here, what is it? 'All are from the Quraish.' And if by that, the intent was Ali and his progeny, then this talk of 'balaghat-e-khilaf' (rhetorical opposition) and such things—the answer to that, one answer I have already presented to you, is that even where the Prophet spoke, you did not accept it. The second answer is that apart from that, the Prophet used different words in different places so that no one would have any argument or any excuse left. Is it clear to you? Look, for example, the Prophet sometimes referred to Ali as Quraish, sometimes Banu Hashim, sometimes Ahl-e-Bayt, sometimes Qurba; the word 'Qurba' has also been used in the Quran. And for instance, many verses and traditions have come. Right? Now, let's look at the verses, the sequence of verses. In the verse, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) has been called 'Wali'. It is verse number 55 of Surah al-Ma'idah: 'Innama waliyyukumullahu wa rasuluhu walladhina amanu alladhina yuqimuna-s-salata wa yu'tuna-z-zakata wa hum raki'un' (Your Wali is only Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe, who establish prayer and give Zakat while they are bowing). Now, the word 'Wali' has come here. Amir al-Mu'minin understood this word 'Wali'. So now, they interpret this 'Wali' as well, whereas what does the 'Sha'n-e-Nuzul' (occasion of revelation) tell us? For example, look at the Tafsir of Tha'labi in 'Al-Kashf wal-Bayan'; in the context of this verse, Tha'labi has narrated the entire story. He has narrated the occasion of revelation. How and when was this verse revealed? That the Prophet was in the mosque, and Amir al-Mu'minin was praying, and a beggar came, and Amir al-Mu'minin was wearing a ring on the little finger of his right hand. The Master of the Universe gave it to him, and the beggar took it. The story is in the entire Tafsir. Now, if you are not ready to accept it, then what is the remedy for that? Besides that, for example, in the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), the Prophet called them Ahl-e-Bayt. The Quran called them Ahl-e-Bayt, not the Prophet—the Quran said: 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumu-r-rijsa Ahl-al-Bayti wa yutahhirakum tathira' (Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O Ahl-e-Bayt, and to purify you with a thorough purification). Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. It is verse number 33 of Surah al-Ahzab. Did you notice? Here Allah is saying 'Ahl-e-Bayt', and now they will interpret it: 'Ahl-e-Bayt means this, Ahl-e-Bayt means that, Ahl-e-Bayt means the wives, Ahl-e-Bayt means so-and-so.' This kind of interpretation—they just want to interpret it somehow. The third is the Verse of Mawaddah (Affection), in which 'Qurba' was used. It is verse number 23 of Surah ash-Shura: 'Qul la as'alukum 'alayhi ajran illal-mawaddata fil-qurba' (Say, 'I do not ask of you for this message any payment except affection for my relatives'). What is 'Qurba'? It is the feminine of 'Aqrab'. 'Aqrab' means closest, and 'Qurba' is its feminine gender. 'Qurba' means you should love my closest relatives. Everyone said, who is 'Qurba'? It is the Ahl-e-Bayt of the Prophet. After that, in the Verse of Mubahila, the Prophet called Amir al-Mu'minin his own 'nafs' (self). Now, what greater proof can there be than this? 'My nafs'—meaning 'call your own nafs, and I will call my own.' And the entire occasion of revelation shows that after saying 'anfusana', whom did the Prophet take with him? Only Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was taken along. Did anyone else go with him? No one else went. Then after that, in the Verse of Inzar (Warning), Amir al-Mu'minin was called 'Hadi' (Guide). 'Innama anta mundhirun wa likulli qawmin had' (You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide). It is verse number 7 of Surah ar-Ra'd, the Verse of Inzar. Then came, 'Wa qifuhum innahum mas'ulun' (And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned). Or, for example, in Surah al-Waqi'ah, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the Ahl-e-Bayt are called 'Sabiqun' (the forerunners). 'Was-sabiquna-s-sabiqun'—this is one verse, verse number 10, and in the next verse, verse number 11, they are called 'Muqarrabun' (those brought near). 'Ula'ikal-muqarrabun'. Was there anyone in Islam who took the lead like Ali (a.s.)? Was there anyone in the religion? 'Awwalu man amana bi' (The first to believe in me)—for whom is this? For Amir al-Mu'minin. After the Verse of Purification, what did the Prophet say? Allahumma inna ha'ula'i Ahlu Bayti wa khassati wa hamati, lahmum lahmi wa damuhum dami, yu'limuni ma yu'limuhum wa yahzuni ma yahzunuhum. (O Allah, these are my Ahl-e-Bayt, my special ones, and my supporters. Their flesh is my flesh, and their blood is my blood. What pains them, pains me; what saddens them, saddens me.) This is the entire Hadith al-Kisa. The Prophet said it this way. Oh brother, all these virtues—what I have presented just now is not even a pinch. This is an entire ocean of virtues. 'Qul law kanal-bahru midadal-likalimati Rabbi lanafadal-bahru qabla an tanfada kalimatu Rabbi wa law ji'na bimithlihi madada.' Say, O Prophet, to them—meaning the virtues of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) can never be written. This is the interpretation of this verse. If all the oceans—'Qul law kanal-bahru midadal-likalimati Rabbi'—if all the oceans were to become ink, 'lanafadal-bahru'—the oceans would dry up 'qabla an tanfada kalimatu Rabbi'—before the words of my Lord, meaning the virtues of the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.), would ever end. Similarly, in the Hadith of Ghadir, he said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyun mawlahu.' Then I presented that they interpreted 'Mawla'. In the Hadith of Manzilat, what did they do? In the Hadith of Manzilat, the Prophet said, 'Anta minni bi-manzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di' (You are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me). They are interpreting that too, saying, 'Aaron died first, then this, then that'—these kinds of interpretations. Then there was the Hadith of Wilayah: 'Inna Aliyyan minni wa ana minhu wa huwa waliyyu kulli mu'minin ba'di' (Indeed, Ali is from me and I am from Ali, and he is the Wali of every believer after me). In this, the Prophet clearly says it for everyone. There are many references from the Ahl-e-Sunnah. InshaAllah, there will be a detailed discussion on each one. In the Hadith of Tashbih, he said, 'Man arada an yanzura ila Adama fi 'ilmihi wa ila Nuhin fi taqwahu...' (Whoever wants to look at Adam in his knowledge, Noah in his piety, Abraham in his forbearance, Moses in his awe, and Jesus in his worship, then he should look at Ali ibn Abi Talib). Now, what more proof do you need than this, brother? Anyway, then there is the Hadith of Tayr (the bird), a famous hadith. There is the Hadith of Munasiba, that whoever showed enmity towards Ali—'Man nasaba Aliyyan lil-khilafati ba'di' (Whoever contested Ali for the Caliphate after me)—is outside the fold of religion. He has waged war against Allah and His Messenger. 'Wa man shaqqa fi Aliyyin' (And whoever doubted Ali) is outside the fold of religion. This is a tradition, and this is not a Shia tradition. I mean, it is in Shia books, but it is also written in the Mustadrak of the Ahl-e-Sunnah in abundance. 'Ana madinatul-'ilmi wa Aliyyun babuha' (I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate). Now, they called Ali the gate of the city of knowledge. They are calling him the gate of the city of knowledge. Now they are objecting to that too, and then they made someone a window, someone else I don't know what, and these kinds of things. Then there is the Hadith of Nur (Light): 'Ana wa Aliyyun min nurin wahid' (I and Ali are from one light), and it is a famous hadith. Ali is light. Ali's light was created with the Prophet's light. There is the Hadith of Rayat (the banner), in which Ali was called a 'man'. There was one man there, because the Prophet offered the banner to everyone, saying, 'Who will go?' So look, see the proof, InshaAllah, if Allah grants the opportunity, there will be a discussion on this. They say that so-and-so went to fight. Oh brother, he went, but why don't you tell the whole story? Did he fight? That he went is certain. But as soon as the opponent came and stomped his foot, he ran back quickly. Because, brother, life is everything. And this sequence continued. Until the Prophet said, 'Ghadan la'utiyanna-r-rayata rajulan' (Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man) 'yuhibbullaha wa rasulahu wa yuhibbullahu wa rasulahu' (who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him). 'Karraran ghayra farrarin' (He will be a Karrar—one who attacks repeatedly—not a runaway). He will fight firmly. He will not run away like you people. He will not be a 'farrar' (runaway), he will not flee the battlefield. 'La yarji'u hatta yaftahallahu 'ala yadayhi' (He will not return until Allah grants Islam victory and success at his hands). Now, object to the word 'rajul' (man) here—why did he call him a man, why not Caliph? 'Tomorrow I will give the banner to my Caliph.' You have seen there are so many titles. There is the Hadith of Qital (Battle), the Hadith of Haqq (Truth). Ali was called the Truth. 'Aliyyun ma'al-haqqi wal-haqqu ma'a Ali. Allahumma adiri-l-haqqa haythu ma dara Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali. O Allah, turn the truth wherever Ali turns). Similarly, 'Aliyyun ma'al-Qur'ani wal-Qur'anu ma'a Ali.' Ali is with the Quran and the Quran is with Ali. And then the Hadith of Thaqalayn. Now, what more proof do you need than this? So many words were used, and you will sit there saying, 'Why didn't he say Ali and the progeny of Ali here?' He said it in so many places. So, what will you do with all of this? Therefore, it shows that there is nothing but prejudice and bigotry. That's all. This is the only thing. That is why it is the duty of every Muslim to pray to Allah: 'Ihdina-s-sirata-l-mustaqim' (Guide us to the straight path). Pray this from the heart. 'Ihdina-s-sirata-l-mustaqim.' O Lord, show us the straight path. Every Muslim should pray this, and when praying, it means the veils of prejudice must be removed. Prejudices should be cast aside. Now, no one can deny these objections except a person who is completely drowned in prejudice and hates the Ahl-e-Bayt. Hates the Ahl-e-Bayt of the Prophet. No matter what they claim, that 'we love the Ahl-e-Bayt,' no, they do not love the Ahl-e-Bayt until they accept these hadiths. Wa akhiru da'wana alhamdulillahi Rabbil 'alamin. In which a few questions related to the previous four episodes will be asked. The link for the quiz is available in the video description and the comment section. This link will remain live for one week, meaning you have a full week's time to submit your answers. If you do not know the answer to any question, you can watch the video again to answer. From among all those who give correct answers, 14 lucky winners will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system, who will receive a gift of 1000 Indian Rupees. The winners will be announced in our next episode, InshaAllah. Therefore, you are requested to watch these videos carefully and try to give correct answers to the questions asked in the quiz, and at the same time, share these videos as much as possible. Participate in the quiz in large numbers and join us in helping to convey this message of Wilayah of Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.) to others so that you too can be included among those who propagate Wilayah.

title: Sach Ki Haqeeqat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound nature of truth, or 'sidq', and its significance in Islamic ethics. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi emphasizes that truthfulness is a divine trust, while falsehood acts as a destructive calamity that necessitates further lies. The talk highlights the moral responsibility of using the gift of speech in accordance with Allah's will.
content:
Those who speak the truth... the agony of death, its point is like that, in Arabic it is called 'sidq' (truthfulness). That is, when someone feels it, truth is something that pricks [music]. This is often the truth that you know. It is written: those who speak the truth... the point of agony, in Arabic it is called 'sidq'. That is, when someone feels it, truth is something that [music] temperature [music] but how... and falsehood... to hide one lie, one has to tell more lies [music]. It was very big, you see, peace, truth is a trust, and falsehood is a calamity. Peace, truth is a trust, and falsehood is a calamity. That is, Allah has given us a power to speak, a power to speak. If we speak the truth, then this, and if we lie, then we have committed betrayal against the right of Allah [music].
Truth is described as 'sidq', a concept that can be difficult or painful to uphold.
Falsehood is inherently unstable, requiring a chain of lies to maintain.
Truth is a sacred trust bestowed upon human beings by Allah.
Lying is considered a betrayal of the rights and gifts granted by the Creator.
The power of speech is a divine blessing that carries significant moral responsibility.
Falsehood is characterized as a calamity that corrupts the soul.
