title: Ep#04 | Muntaqim e Khoon e Husain (a.s.) Kaun?
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological and traditional basis for the belief that Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is the divinely appointed avenger of Imam Hussain (a.s.). It highlights specific narrations, including the Imam's first sermon at the Kaaba, which detail his mission to seek justice for the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse also clarifies the Islamic perspective on why descendants of the killers may be held accountable, emphasizing that those who are pleased with past atrocities are considered partners in the crime.
content:
A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim. Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya Rasulullah. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaykum wa Rahmatullah. We extend our heartfelt congratulations to all of you on the auspicious occasion of the 3rd of Sha'ban. Today is that day, today is the day when the hearts of all of us, of all believers, are filled with emotion. The 3rd of Sha'ban is when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was born; so on one hand, there is the joy of the birth of Imam Hussain (a.s.), and on the other hand, the tragic scene of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) comes before our eyes. We take the name of Hussain. Yes, respected viewers, Imam Hussain (a.s.) is that personality for whom we weep the most, and every Hussaini knows very well that the vengeance for the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.) has not yet been taken. And today's episode's question is in this regard: on what basis do we say that Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) will avenge the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.), that he is the avenger of Imam Hussain (a.s.)? So let us see... ...Imam Hussain (a.s.). So let us look at those narrations which prove that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the one who will avenge the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The greatest Hadith where we find this is that when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) reappears, he will deliver his very first sermon in the Holy Kaaba, between the Rukn and the Maqam, in which he will make five proclamations. Among those proclamations, three are regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.), where the Imam (a.s.) remembers the tragedy and martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). In the first proclamation, the Imam of our Time (a.s.) introduces himself: 'I am that Mahdi (a.s.) whom everyone is eagerly awaiting.' And in the second proclamation, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Anash-Shamsan al-Muntaqim'—'I am the avenger, I am the designated avenger whom Allah has chosen.' And after that, he says: 'Ala ya ahla al-alam, inna jaddi al-Hussain qataluhu 'atshana'—'O people of the world, indeed they killed my grandfather Hussain while he was thirsty.' The Imam says this, and then he says: 'Ala ya ahla al-alam, inna jaddi al-Hussain tarahuhu...'—'O people of the world, indeed they...' ...Hussain, and O people of the world, know that they left the body of my grandfather Hussain without shroud and burial. And then the Imam says at the end: 'Ala ya ahla al-alam, inna jaddi al-Hussain sahaquhu'—'O people of the world, know that they ruthlessly trampled upon my grandfather Hussain.' That is, Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred, his body was left without shroud and burial, and that shroudless body was trampled upon. This scene is always before the eyes of the Imam of our Time (a.s.), and that is why, upon his reappearance, in his very first sermon, he mentions Imam Hussain (a.s.). This also proves that the Imam of our Time (a.s.) himself declares himself to be the avenger, that Allah has sent him as the avenger, and he will take revenge on the killers of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and avenge his martyrdom. Now let us look at another Hadith where Allah, the Almighty, Himself tells us that the Imam of our Time (a.s.) is the avenger of the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.). This Hadith is from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.): when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred, the angels complained to Allah, saying, 'O Lord, such oppression is being committed against Hussain, who is the son of Your Prophet!' While... ...such oppression is being committed against Hussain, while he is Your chosen servant and the son of Your Prophet! At that moment, Allah, the Almighty, showed His angels a glimpse of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and said, 'Through him, I will avenge the oppressors of Imam Hussain (a.s.).' Through the Imam of our Time (a.s.), I will take revenge on the oppressors of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Therefore, this also proves that Allah Himself declares the Imam of our Time (a.s.) to be the avenger of the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Furthermore, this is proven in various traditions, such as the Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) who told Ali (a.s.): 'Know that this son of mine will take revenge on your killers, and he will also take revenge on those who oppressed the Shiites in this world.' Yes, respected viewers, we find in traditions that not only will this son take revenge on the killers, but also on those who oppress the Shiites of the Household of Muhammad (a.s.) in this world, and Allah, the Almighty, will punish these oppressors and killers in the Hereafter. As soon as Salman (r.a.) heard this, he immediately asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, who is that son?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'He will be the ninth son of Imam Hussain...' ...'He will be the ninth son from the lineage of Imam Hussain (a.s.).' Yes, meaning the ninth descendant from the lineage of Imam Hussain (a.s.) will reappear after a long occultation. After a long occultation, the Imam (a.s.) will reappear, he will establish the religion of Allah, take revenge on the enemies, and fill the earth with justice and equity just as it would be filled with injustice and oppression. So in this Hadith as well, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) clearly stated that the ninth descendant of Imam Hussain (a.s.), the Imam of our Time (a.s.), will take revenge on all oppressors upon his arrival. And finally, in this Hadith, a narrator asked Imam Reza (a.s.): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the Hadith narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that when Al-Mahdi (a.s.) reappears, he will kill the descendants of those who killed Imam Hussain (a.s.)?' Imam Reza (a.s.) replied, 'Yes, it is so.' The narrator asked in surprise, 'How can that be, when the Quran says: "Wa la taziru waziratu wizra ukhra" (And no bearer of burdens shall bear another's burden)?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'That is because they are pleased with the deeds of their ancestors...' Because they were pleased with this action of their ancestors and felt proud that their ancestors killed Imam Hussain (a.s.). [The Imam] says: If someone is pleased with an action, it is as if he performed that action himself. And finally, he says that if someone is killed in the East, and a person living in the West is pleased with this killing, then in the eyes of Allah, the Almighty, this person is an equal partner in the murder. So, from all these traditions, it becomes absolutely clear and proven that the vengeance for the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.), or the revenge for Imam Hussain (a.s.), is still pending, and Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will accomplish this task after his reappearance and will take revenge. Surely, the more love one has for Imam Hussain (a.s.) in his heart, and the more enmity he has towards his killers, and the more intensely he desires that the Imam (a.s.) should reappear as soon as possible and take revenge on the killers of Imam Hussain (a.s.), the more intensely he prays for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). So, let us also pray by reciting these sentences from the Ziyarah of Imam (a.s.) for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). ...by reciting [this], we will pray that the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) happens as soon as possible, that there be haste in the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.), and that we too are included among those who take revenge. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. 'O Allah, Lord of Hussain, heal the heart of Hussain. O Allah, Lord of Hussain, avenge the blood of Hussain. O Allah, Lord of Hussain, take revenge on those who were pleased with his killing. O Allah, Lord of Hussain, take revenge on those who opposed Hussain. O Allah, Lord of Hussain, take revenge on those who rejoiced at the killing of Hussain.' O Lord of Hussain, heal the heart of Hussain. O Lord of Hussain, avenge the blood of Hussain. Take revenge on those who were pleased with his killing. Take revenge on those who opposed Hussain. Take revenge on those who rejoiced at the killing of Hussain. And O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and grant us the grace to be counted among his helpers. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdu lillahi Rabbil 'alamin. ...to submit the correct answer to the question, click on the link in the comment section or the description of this video. Two winners who give the correct answer will be chosen in the next episode and will receive 1000 Indian Rupees. Also, subscribe to this channel.

title: EP01 | Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ka Khalifa Kaisa Ho? | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 💐
excerpt: This lecture serves as the first episode of the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz, exploring the theological and logical requirements for the successor of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It emphasizes that a true Caliph must possess the same divine attributes as the Prophet, including infallibility, comprehensive knowledge, and the authority to interpret the Quran. By analyzing verses from Surah Jumu'ah and historical debates, the session argues that an infallible Imam is essential for the guidance and unity of the Muslim Ummah.
content:
TSR presents. Ghadir is that... [Poetry in praise of Ghadir]. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Respected and honorable listeners and dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Ya Ali Madad. All praise is for that pure and holy Essence of Oneness, who granted honor to the weak-founded human being over all His creations, adorned him with the jewelry of knowledge and wisdom, and informed him through the tongues of His messengers about His Sharia laws, adhering to which He made a means of His pleasure and a source of salvation for him. And no matter how much gratitude is offered to that Almighty God, no matter how many prostrations of gratitude are offered in His court, it is less, for He sent His beloved for our guidance, who is himself the cause of the creation of the universe and a mercy to the worlds. Blessings and peace be upon the pride of the prophets and messengers, the cause of the creation of the world and Adam, the means of guidance and salvation for the children of Adam, the intercessor of the Day of Judgment, Ahmad-e-Mustafa, Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Who, in his 23-year missionary life, accomplished such a feat of preaching Islam that the Almighty God Himself was seen saying in the Holy Quran: 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum wa atmamtu alaykum ni'mati wa raditu lakumul-islama dina' (This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion). But this perfection of religion, the completion of favors, and the approval of Islam as a religion did not happen until the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the plain of Ghadir, openly, by showing, telling, identifying, and making 125,000 pilgrims hear, and by raising him on his hands, declared: 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyun mawla' (Whosoever's master I am, this Ali is his master). In connection with this day of Ghadir, that is, the Eid-e-Akbar, the team of 'The Strong Rope' (TSR) is once again present before you with the 'Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz'. So viewers, first of all, let us offer congratulations for this blessed Eid in the court of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) through a loud Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. And we also offer congratulations to all of you for this Eid and welcome you all from the bottom of our hearts to the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz. Come, viewers, let us begin today's episode with these four lines: 'Day and night my prayer is Ya Ali Madad. The only cure for my sorrows is Ya Ali Madad. Just as there are blessings in Hadith-e-Kisa, in the same way, the guarantor remains Ya Ali Madad.' In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Respected viewers, come, first of all, let us tell you a few things about the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz. There will be seven episodes of this, and in every episode, a discussion regarding Ghadir and the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), will be presented to you, and the questions of this quiz will be related to that discussion. In every episode, there will be seven lucky winners who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system, in which the first prize is 5,000, the second two prizes are 3,000 each, and the third four prizes are 1,000 each. And finally, the mega prize of our Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz is the one that every lover of Ali (a.s.) keeps in his heart—he wants to go to the threshold of his Master and bow his head in submission, that is, a pilgrimage to Iraq. Yes, viewers, the mega prize is a pilgrimage to Iraq, which will be announced in a special episode after this series ends. To be eligible for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq, one must watch all seven episodes and participate in the quiz for each one. You must provide correct answers to all questions in at least five out of the seven episode quizzes. From among all such individuals, the winner of our mega prize—the Ziyarat of Iraq—will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. We hope you will stay with us throughout this series and continue to participate in every quiz. The quiz link will be activated at the start of each episode and is available in the live chat and description of this video. The quiz link will remain active until the end of the episode. At the end of each episode, there will be Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, after which the link will be closed. We request you to listen to our episodes carefully and answer all questions correctly. Respected viewers, let us move towards our first episode today, the topic of which is: 'What should the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) be like?' In the history of Islam, the greatest and most fundamental subject of disagreement among Muslims has been that of Caliphate and Imamate. After the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the biggest issue that arose among Muslims was who would take the reins of the Muslim Ummah. That is, who would be the Caliph and successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? This became the reason that spread division among Muslims. In the Islamic world, Muslims should, before searching for who the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is, search for what he should be like—that is, what the character of the Caliph and successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should be. If this is understood, the disagreements among Muslims will be resolved very easily. So, let us move towards our topic today, to discuss which our brothers, Mr. Ahsan Jafri and Mr. Kazim Syed, are present in our gathering. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. Before we begin today's discussion, we offer you congratulations on this Eid-e-Akbar, Eid-e-Ghadir. Many congratulations to you as well, and we offer our heartfelt congratulations to all our viewers on this Eid-e-Saeed, Eid-e-Akbar, Eid-e-Ghadir. So, Kazim Bhai, regarding today's topic—what the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should be like—we would like you to shed some light on it first. A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim minash shaitanir rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Gulzar Bhai, if this can be answered in the simplest way, it is that the successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should be exactly like the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself. Indeed, indeed, indeed. Subhan Allah. Now, let us learn through a few proofs what kind of person the successor of the Messenger of Allah should be. Yes. Let us shed more light on this through Quranic verses and Hadith to clarify this for our viewers. Yes. Why? As you said, if it becomes clear what the successor of the Messenger of Allah should be like, the chances of resolving all the disagreements prevalent among the Muslim Ummah will increase significantly. So, Gulzar Bhai, if I present the answer in simple language: the duty of the successor of the Messenger of Allah, or the Caliph, will be to perform the same tasks that the Messenger of Allah performed. Indeed, indeed, indeed. Right? So, we must first understand what the duties of the Messenger of Allah are. What are his tasks? Which tasks has Allah imposed upon him? If this is understood, we will understand what the duties of his Caliph or successor are. Indeed. Right? So, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala has described the duties of the Messenger of Allah in countless places in the Quran. However, we would like to resolve this through one verse, and this is a very famous and well-known verse that the Muslim Ummah has been hearing repeatedly every Friday. Such great virtue has been given to Friday prayer among the Muslim Ummah; it has been called the 'Sayyidul Ayyam' (Master of Days). From the morning, if you look at WhatsApp and various social media platforms, there is a constant stream of messages saying 'Jumma Mubarak'. So, regarding this Friday prayer and this day, and regarding this Surah Jumu'ah, we want to present the duties of the Messenger of Allah to the viewers: what are the duties of the Messenger of Allah? Through this, it will become known what the duties of the Aimma-e-Masumeen (a.s.) or their Caliph or successor will be. And as you said, Kazim Bhai, Muslims are so sensitive about Friday—and have always been so sensitive—that if someone taught it on Wednesday, they would be ready to read it then too. Yes, yes, yes. You said it perfectly, Ahsan Bhai. So, anyway, that was on the side, but here, let us present the duties of the Messenger of Allah to the viewers, as stated in the second verse of Surah Jumu'ah: 'Huwal ladhi ba'atha fil ummiyyina rasulam minhum yatlu 'alayhim ayatihi wa yuzakkihim wa yu'allimuhumul kitaba wal hikmah wa in kanu min qablu lafi dalalim mubin.' In this verse, Khuda-e-Muta'al is presenting the responsibilities of the Messenger of Allah to the people. What is the responsibility of the Messenger of Allah? And three important responsibilities are being announced in this noble verse. What are those three important responsibilities of the Messenger of Allah? The first responsibility is to recite the verses: 'Yatlu 'alayhim ayatihi'. The second responsibility: 'Wa yuzakkihim', that is, to perform Tazkiyah-e-Nafs (purification of the soul). This is the second responsibility of the Messenger of Allah. What is the third responsibility? 'Wa yu'allimuhumul kitaba wal hikmah', that is, to teach the Book and Wisdom to the people. Right? Now, if one reflects on the last part, where the command of the Lord of Honor is: 'Wa in kanu min qablu lafi dalalim mubin', that before this—meaning until the Messenger of Allah had not performed these tasks—before this, people were in misguidance. That is, until the Messenger of Allah recited, performed Tazkiyah-e-Nafs, and taught the Book and Wisdom, if one looks at it according to this verse of the Quran, humanity was in misguidance; the people of that time were in misguidance. Yes, indeed, Kazim Bhai. That is, according to this verse of Surah Jumu'ah that you recited, there are three responsibilities of the Messenger: one is to recite the verses, second is to purify the souls of the people, and third is to teach the Book and Wisdom. Absolutely correct. So, let us clarify these three things: what is it regarding the recitation of verses, what is Tazkiyah-e-Nafs, and what is the teaching of the Book and Wisdom? So, the first point: recitation of the verses. Now, there are two very important things here that we want to present to the viewers regarding 'Yatlu 'alayhim ayatihi': the Messenger of Allah receiving the revelation, accepting the revelation, and propagating the revelation—these are two aspects. Right? 'Yatlu 'alayhim ayatihi' has two aspects: that the Messenger of Allah accepted the revelation and then propagated that revelation. In both these aspects, the Messenger of Allah being Masoom (infallible) is a condition. Yes, indeed. Why? Because if the Messenger of Allah, God forbid—may Allah protect us—if there were any mistake in receiving or any mistake in the propagation, then the entire Islam, the entire Quran, the entire religion would become questionable. That is, in any way—as you stated, Kazim Bhai—to even imagine that in these two aspects the Prophet made a mistake, God forbid, or that he forgot something, or that when Jibra'il (a.s.) brought the revelation to him, he forgot a word or a piece of it, this is absolutely impossible. This is against reason. Because he has to receive that thing from the court of Allah and propagate it among the people. Therefore, in both these aspects, the infallibility (Ismat) of the Prophet is a condition, a necessary condition. Indeed. Yes, Kazim Bhai. Yes, yes. So, in both aspects, as Ahsan Bhai explained in more detail, the Messenger being Masoom is a condition. So, in 'Yatlu 'alayhim ayatihi', the Messenger being Masoom is a condition. Now, the result of this is that the Caliph of the Messenger, the successor of the Messenger, who comes in the place of the Messenger after him, should also be Masoom just as the Messenger is Masoom. Although we do not consider the Messenger Masoom only in these two aspects; we see the entire life of the Messenger within the circle of Ismat. From the birth of the Messenger to the martyrdom of the Messenger, the entire life of the Messenger is within the fortress of 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur rijsa ahlal bayti wa yutahhirakum tathira'. So, in the same way, the successor of the Messenger must also be Masoom. This is the first aspect. So, regarding the recitation of the verses of the Messenger, we present this to the viewers here. Yes, so viewers, here Kazim Bhai presented a very important point: that the Messenger of Allah being Masoom in receiving the revelation and in its propagation is very necessary. That is, if we look at the Islamic world, people so easily point fingers at the infallibility of the Messenger of Allah, saying he could make mistakes. That is, if the Messenger is not considered Masoom, then the truthfulness of the Quran will be questioned. And here, one is truly surprised at the intellects of those people who insist that the infallibility of the Prophet should be proven through narrators. Yes, indeed. That is, those narrators who, even if they are reliable, are still non-Masoom. Indeed. So, these people insist on proving the infallibility of the Masoom through non-Masoom individuals. One is surprised at the intellects of these people. And certainly, the disagreement found among people, whether it is the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah or the Quran, right? It is found precisely because those people made a mistake in selecting the successor of the Messenger of Allah. Indeed. They made a mistake in selecting and also in accepting. Both things are there. The one whom the Prophet declared clearly before the people, they did not accept him, and when they selected, they selected someone for whom there is no testimony of infallibility anywhere. Indeed. That is, here it is that the Caliph of the Messenger must be Masoom. Indeed, indeed. If he is not Masoom, then there will be errors in understanding the Quran as well. And how beautifully the poet said: 'What greater proof of enmity could there be? What greater proof of enmity could there be? It is written one thing in the Quran, but the world read something else.' Wah, wah, wah, wah, wah, wah. Subhan Allah. So, what do you say, Gulzar Bhai? This was the first part of this verse. Right? We now want to draw the attention of the viewers to the second responsibility, which is Tazkiyah-e-Nafs. What is meant by Tazkiyah-e-Nafs? Tazkiyah-e-Nafs means purifying the soul from sins. Now, before purifying the soul from sins, I would like to point to a point: that a person must have knowledge of sins. Indeed. Until he has knowledge of sins, how will he purify himself from that sin? Yes. And not only should there be knowledge, but he should also know its effects—that, for example, if we committed some insolence in your honor, its effect will be different; this sin we committed, or if there was any deficiency in the respect of a Momin, its sin will be different, its effects will be different. And those people who put someone else in the place of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), whose right... It was not. The world has been suffering the consequences of their sins to this day. Hmm. Look at the Ummah today, look at the Muslim Ummah, it is stumbling from door to door. Yes. This is the result of that one decision, that today everywhere—in whichever city, whichever region, whichever village, whichever town, whichever country you look—the Muslim is humiliated. And troubled, disgraced. Everywhere, they are being humiliated. Just because of that one decision the Muslim Ummah made at that time, the Ummah is still suffering the consequences of that same decision today. Now, Gulzar Bhai, the second aspect—we just described one aspect, which is the knowledge of sins and their effects. The second aspect is that Iblis misleads people through sins. So, one must be saved from the attacks or the evil of Iblis. And it is the duty of the Prophet to save his Ummah from his evil or his attacks. Right? So, for the Prophet to be more powerful than this cursed one, this Iblis, is logically evident. In the same way that the Prophet is more powerful than Iblis, more capable than Iblis, in the same way, the Prophet's successor and the Prophet's Caliph must also be more powerful than Iblis. Indeed. And here is a very interesting point. We would like to present this to the viewers, as Kazim Bhai just said, that the Prophet and the Prophet's successor—whoever claims to be the successor of the Prophet—must possess more knowledge than Iblis. Indeed. Only then will he be able to save people from the attacks of Iblis. Now, in this regard, an interesting incident is found. This incident is very interesting. This is the incident of Abul Hasan Ali ibn Meesam al-Tammar, the son of Janabe Meesam al-Tammar. Oh. It is a discussion between him and a person named Abul Huzail. Abul Huzail was a Mu'tazili. Right? He did not belong to the Shia Imami creed. There is a discussion between the two, a conversation in which Ali ibn Meesam, the son of Janabe Meesam al-Tammar, asked Abul Huzail some questions, and how Abul Huzail answered those questions. And it is exactly on this point: that whoever is the successor of the Caliph, it is necessary for him to be more powerful and more knowledgeable than Iblis. Listen carefully. Viewers, we would like you to listen carefully to this incident. We have heard the name of Janabe Meesam al-Tammar, and we have heard stories about the odes he recited in praise of Hazrat Ali (a.s.); this is an incident regarding his son. Pay attention to the incident. And this incident has been narrated by Sheikh Mufid (alaih-ir-rahma) in his book 'Al-Fusul al-Mukhtara'. As we all know about Sheikh Mufid, he is the personality for whom, when he departed from this world—when he said goodbye to the world—Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) recited a dirge (marsiya) for him. And this dirge is still written on Sheikh Mufid's grave today, buried just outside the Zarih of Imam Kazim (a.s.) in Kadhimiya. There, on his grave, this dirge of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is still written today. So, Sheikh Mufid (alaih-ir-rahma) narrates this incident in his book 'Al-Fusul al-Mukhtara' that Abul Hasan Ali ibn Meesam al-Tammar once asked Abul Huzail al-Mu'tazili: 'Do you not know that Iblis forbids all good and commands all evil?' Abul Huzail said, 'Yes. Yes, that is true.' Then Ali ibn Meesam asks a second question: 'Is it appropriate? Is it permissible? Is it possible that he commands all evil but does not know it? Wow. Yes. And he forbids all good but does not know it? He has no knowledge of what good is?' So he said, 'No, it is not possible that Iblis does not know.' Now, look, step by step, he is reaching his goal. Then Ali ibn Meesam says, as soon as he said that it is not possible for Iblis not to have knowledge of that thing, then Abul Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said, 'Then it is proven that Iblis knows all evil and all good.' Wow. He knows both things. So Abul Huzail said, 'Certainly.' Meaning, yes, indeed he knows. He is absolutely knowledgeable; he knows both good and evil. If he doesn't know, how will he stop people from goodness and good deeds? How will he stop them? So, as soon as he said, 'Yes, certainly'—meaning Iblis must have that knowledge—then Janabe Ali ibn Meesam says, 'Then tell me about your Imam, whom you followed after the Prophet, whom you considered an Imam. Did he have the knowledge of all good and all evil or not?' Wow. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. So then he says no. He clearly admitted that the one we considered an Imam after the Prophet did not have the knowledge of all good and evil. So, as soon as he said this, Abul Huzail had no answer. And as Kazim Bhai was explaining, whoever claims to be the Caliph of the Prophet must have more knowledge than Iblis. He must have the knowledge of all good and all evil. If he does not have that knowledge, then his claim is false. And what to say about the knowledge of my Mawla, that in the history books, those words are still present in golden letters that from the pulpit of the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) declared: 'Ask me, ask me before you lose me.' And not only that, not only did Ali (a.s.) claim this, but we see that history is a witness to the fact that among all our Imams (a.s.), whoever was the Imam of the time, whenever it came to knowledge, everyone sat at the feet of our Imams (a.s.). And whoever was the ruler of the time, whatever trouble or difficulty befell them, the solution was provided only by the sons of the 'Mushkil Kusha' (the Solver of Difficulties) and no one else. Gulzar Bhai, the third point in this verse of Surah Jumu'ah, or the third important point to which the Almighty is pointing, is teaching the Book and Wisdom to the people. Now, if we turn to the traditions, the 'Book' refers to the Quran, and 'Wisdom' refers to the Sunnah of the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), which is present with us and also found among the opponents, that Wisdom means Sunnah. And in our books, especially in our books, Wisdom means the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). (Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum). So, an important task of the Prophet of Allah is to invite people to the Quran, to teach it, and to call people towards Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Meaning both things, meaning the Quran, meaning the Thaqalayn, right? 'I am leaving among you the two weighty things.' Right? To invite towards the Thaqalayn, to teach that this is the Quran, and after me, accept this Quran, act upon this Quran. And who will explain the Quran? The Heir of the Quran. Let us look at a Hadith which is present in 'Basa'ir al-Darajat', one of our ancient books. In it, a Hadith is narrated in which the Imam (a.s.) is saying: 'There is no one among the people who says that he has gathered the entire Quran as Allah revealed it, except that he is a liar. And no one gathered it or preserved it as Allah revealed it except Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the Imams after him.' Right. Now, the second part of this Hadith says that no one gathered or preserved the Quran as Allah revealed it except Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) or the Infallible Imams (a.s.) after him. Yes, the point Kazim Bhai made here is important because, as we are discussing the third responsibility—teaching the Quran and Sunnah—the one who teaches the Quran and Sunnah should be the one who has complete knowledge of the Quran and Sunnah. So here, Imam Baqir (a.s.) is saying that no one gathered the Holy Quran as it was, except Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the Imams after him. And if anyone claims that he has gathered the Quran as Allah revealed it, he is a liar. So, along with the verse, there will be its interpretation (ta'wil), its commentary (tafsir), its revelation (tanzil), all these things. So where is that Quran today? Yes. No one should think that we believe in distortion (tahrif); we do not believe in distortion at all, because if someone believes in the distortion of the Quran, then the whole religion is finished. Indeed. Then there is nothing left. So here, it is not about distortion. Here, it is only about the order. In the order in which Allah revealed it, Is that Quran with us today? No. Who gathered that Quran? No one gathered that Quran except Ali (a.s.). Because the Mawla of the Universe himself pointed towards this. It is the Hadith of the Mawla of the Universe himself that immediately after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the first thing the Mawla of the Universe did was the compilation of the Quran. Gathering the Quran. And the Mawla of the Universe swore that I will not put a cloak on my shoulders—people were calling the Mawla of the Universe outside, saying 'come out and pledge allegiance'—but the Mawla refused to pledge allegiance. Yes. And why did he refuse? The Mawla clearly announced that I will not put a cloak on my shoulders, except for prayer, until I have fully compiled the Holy Quran. And then when the Mawla compiled it, the Mawla brought that Quran and presented it to the people, saying, 'This is that Quran. This is the Quran that the Messenger of Allah brought. There is no verse in it that was revealed in the city or during a journey, except that the Prophet gave me its knowledge.' I mean, I am aware of every single thing about it. I have the knowledge of its revelation, the knowledge of its interpretation, the knowledge of its commentary, I have all these things. That is why I have gathered this Quran between these two covers, and this is the same Quran that the Prophet left among us. But what did those people do? Did those people accept that Quran of the Mawla of the Universe? No. Instead, what did they do? Did they tell the Mawla of the Universe, 'No, we don't need this. We have another book, another Mushaf. We don't need this'? And Hassan Bhai, if you look at the last sermon of the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in Ghadir, the Prophet also pointed out in it that the knowledge of the interpretation of the Quran is with Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Indeed. And it is clear, it is written there: 'And my Caliph over my Ummah and over the interpretation of the Book of Allah (Azza wa Jall).' Wow. That he will be my Caliph in my Ummah and he will be my Caliph regarding the interpretation of the Quran. Wow. While the Prophet clearly announced the word 'Caliph'. The Prophet brought the word 'Caliph' in the Hadith. Exactly. Here, Hassan Bhai, a question for you: you were just saying that Hazrat Ali (a.s.) gathered the Quran and brought it among the Muslims, and the Muslim Ummah rejected it. Indeed. Now, a question arises: where is that Quran now? That Quran... very good, very good that you asked this question, Gulzar Bhai. Because it is possible that someone might think, 'Is it possible that the Shias have a different Quran, that the Shias have started believing in a different Quran?' Yes. So no, that is not the case. And in this regard, a tradition is found in our books. As Kazim Bhai also referred to 'Basa'ir al-Darajat', a Hadith is found in 'Basa'ir al-Darajat' in which a person came to the presence of the sixth Imam. He comes to the service of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and says, 'I have heard a person reciting in a way that is slightly different from how the rest of the people recite.' Yes. I mean, he was reading the letters in a different way. Yes. The Imam forbade him. The Imam forbade his follower. The Imam said, 'No, recite just as the people recite.' Wow. Meaning, the Quran that the people have is correct. Yes. There is no distortion in it. You read it and read it just as the people read it. But then, after this, what the Imam explained, the Imam said, 'Read this until when? Recite just as the people recite, but until when? Until our Mahdi appears.' Wow. Meaning, when Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) appears at the end, Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) will bring that Quran, the Quran that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had gathered; it is with Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) today. Because Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that when he rises, 'He will recite the Book of Allah with all its boundaries (hudud).' “Yatlu alayhim ayatihi” (He recites His verses to them). Wonderful. And then the Imam says, “Wa akhraja al-mus-hafa alladhi katabahu Aliyun alayhis-salam” (And he will bring out the Mushaf, the book, the Quran that Ali alayhis-salam had transcribed, the one he had written, the one the Master of the Universe had compiled). And then after that, the Imam alayhis-salam says, “Akhrajahu” (He brought it out), meaning the Imam pointed towards the same fact that this is the very Quran that the Master of the Universe had presented to the people, but the people rejected that Quran. Now, Gulzar Bhai, Kazim Bhai, the troubles that the Muslim Ummah is going through today are because people claimed that the Quran is sufficient for us. Yes. But they abandoned the Quran that was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the way it was revealed. Indeed. And this complaint of the Prophet himself is present in the Holy Quran, that on the Day of Judgment—this is a verse of the Quran—the Prophet will complain in the court of Allah: “Ya Rabbi, inna qawmi ittakhadhu hadhal-qur’ana mahjura” (O my Lord, my people, my Ummah, have abandoned this Quran). Meaning, in other words, if it is said, the Prophet had asked for paper and pen to save people from misguidance so that he could write his will. At that time, in the final moments of the Prophet, people rejected the Prophet’s will, and after the Prophet’s passing, they rejected the Prophet’s successor. Meaning, Hasan Bhai, regarding this matter of the Quran, it appears to us, the viewers, that what Allah has reserved for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is that the interpretation of the Quran can only be done by the true Caliph of the Messenger. It is in this way that Allah has bestowed this virtue upon them. Meaning, if anyone abandons their door, they have abandoned the Quran as well. Indeed. But here, Hasan Bhai, the question is: did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) not fulfill his responsibilities completely, such that a Caliph is now needed to carry it forward and complete it? If that is the case, then it implies the Prophet did not complete his work. So, if someone raises such a question, what answer can be given? It is a good question, Gulzar Bhai, and if we clarify the question for the viewers once more: the Prophet stated everything during his lifetime. He stated the entire religion, to the point that the religion was perfected, it was completed on the day of Ghadir, everything was done. Despite that, when the Prophet had stated everything, explained the Book, explained the Sunnah, then what is the need for a Caliph—a Caliph who is like the Prophet? If people just get together and make someone a Caliph, and if that Caliph follows the Prophet’s Sunnah, isn't that enough? That is the question, right? A person came with this very question from Sham, from Syria, to the sixth Imam, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.). He did not believe in the Imamate of the Imam (a.s.). He came to debate. Yes. And he made a big claim upon arriving. What was the claim? “Ana sahib-e-kalami” (I am the master of Ilm-e-Kalam/theology). Oh. He made a big claim. A very big claim. And he said, “I know jurisprudence, I am a jurist. And I have the knowledge of all the obligations. And I have come here,” he says to the Imam, “to debate with your companions.” Yes. This entire narration is reported from Yunus ibn Yaqub; it is a famous narration. Just stating the essence quickly to answer this question. Keep this question in mind: the question was, when the Prophet had stated all these things, then what is the need for a successor? And that too, a successor who should be like the Prophet? So he said, “I have come to debate with your companions.” The Imam first asked him some questions. The first question the Imam asked was: “This kalam of yours, you said you are a master of kalam, so this kalam of yours, your method of debate, whatever it is, whatever evidence you have, is this from the kalam of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) or from yourself?” Wonderful. “Is this kalam of yours from the Prophet or from yourself?” Yes. Wonderful. So he said, “Some from the Prophet, some from myself.” Meaning, right there, the Imam defeated him. Now, this is just the beginning; see how the Imam cornered him further. He said, “Some from myself, some from the Messenger of Allah, some from myself.” Now the Imam turned and asked him three more questions. He said, “Alright, tell me one thing, if you are saying this, if this is your claim that some is from yourself and some from the Messenger, then first of all, tell me, are you a partner in the teachings and knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)?” Wonderful. Since you are claiming that some is from the Messenger? So he said, “No.” In every question, the Imam is cornering him. Cornering him in every question, absolutely. So he said, “No, I am not a partner in the Messenger’s knowledge.” Then the Imam asked the second question: “Does revelation descend upon you?” Wonderful. So he said, “No.” And here, especially, those people should pay attention—the greatest insult that those who recite the Kalima committed against the Prophet was that they considered the Prophet to be like themselves. Indeed. And for this, they bring the Quranic verse: “Ana basharun mithlukum” (I am a human being like you). But the question to those who recite the Kalima, those blind in intellect, is: why are you quoting this verse today? The verse... It has come, let it be proven. That if the Prophet said, “Ana basharun mithlukum,” what does the verse say after that? “Yūhā ilayya” (Revelation is revealed to me). Is revelation being revealed to you? Indeed. So, revelation is not revealed to you, yet you consider yourself like the Prophet? The Imam asked the same question: “Does revelation descend upon you?” He said, “No, revelation does not descend.” Then the Imam asked the third question: “Is your obedience as obligatory as the obedience of the Prophet is obligatory?” Wonderful! Wonderful! He had no answer to that. Right? He is neither a partner in the Messenger’s knowledge, nor does revelation descend upon him like the Prophet, nor is his obedience obligatory like the obedience of the Messenger. Yet, he came to argue with the progeny of the Messenger. Wonderful! Right? This happens when someone thinks of themselves as a very great scholar. But he did not see where he had come. Yes, he thought... And this is what happens to those who consider themselves more knowledgeable than the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) or even equal to them; their fate is what is about to happen to him. So, when he had no answer to these three questions, he started looking here and there. He did not understand what to answer. The Imam (a.s.) turned towards Yunus—Yunus ibn Yaqub, who is the narrator of this entire Hadith—the Imam looked at Yunus and said, “Ya Yunus, hadha khasama nafsahu qabla an yatakalama.” (O Yunus, this person has contradicted himself before even starting his argument). Wonderful! He has gone against himself. And then, a long Hadith, the Hadith goes on much further. But the main part, the most important answer to the question—many people debated there, the Imam called them, but finally, the one who actually debated was the Imam’s prominent companion, the young companion, Janab Hisham ibn al-Hakam. The debate took place between Janab Hisham ibn al-Hakam and this person, this Syrian. Now, as soon as Janab Hisham came for the debate, this Syrian looked at Janab Hisham and said, “Ya ghulam, O boy,” because he was young. Okay, some narrations mention that Hisham’s beard had just started to grow. Hisham was that young at the time. So he says, “Ya ghulam, sallini fi imamati hadha.” (Ask me questions about the Imamate of this person). Meaning, he is addressing the Imam (a.s.) with such insulting, derogatory words. Hisham could not tolerate it. Hisham’s religious zeal could not tolerate that someone should come and say something about my Imam and leave. This is a lesson for us. Absolutely. We should have enough religious zeal that if someone speaks against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), we should have the courage to answer them. Indeed. Indeed. And we must not back down from this at all. Indeed. Indeed. The phrase in the narration is, “Faghadhiba Hisham” (Hisham became enraged). Hisham became furious. “Hatta irtada” (To the point that he started trembling) out of rage, out of anger. And then Janab Hisham immediately asked him, “Akhbirni” (Tell me), tell me one thing: does the Creator, does Allah take more care of His creation, or does the creation take care of itself? So he said, “No, indeed, Allah will take more care compared to the creation.” Then Janab Hisham asked the second question, “Then alright, tell me, what arrangement has Allah made to take care of those people?” So that they do not stray, do not go astray. So how has Allah taken care of them? So then that Syrian says that Allah has made them accountable. “Kallafahum wa aqama lahum hujjatan wa dalila.” (He has burdened them and established a proof and evidence for them). So Janab Hisham asked, “What is that evidence? Ma hadhal dalil? What is the evidence, what is this proof that Allah has appointed for them?” So the Syrian immediately said, “That evidence is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).” So Janab Hisham said, “The Messenger, alright, it is the Messenger of Allah, I accept your point.” That Allah appointed the Messenger of Allah to take care of the people, to guide the people. “After the Messenger, who? Who is after the Messenger?” So he said the same thing, “The Book and the Sunnah.” He immediately replied, “The Book is sufficient, the Sunnah is sufficient.” There is the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, that is sufficient. If the servants act upon it, they will find guidance by themselves. So then what question did Janab Hisham ask? “Alright, if this is your point, if this is your claim, then do the Book and the Sunnah benefit the people? Do these two things benefit the people? Do they prove beneficial for the people?” So he said, “Yes.” He immediately said, “Yes, the Book and the Sunnah are sufficient.” So to this, Janab Hisham said, “If this is your claim that the Book and the Sunnah are sufficient, then why have you traveled from so far away from Sham to come here to Medina to argue with us?” Indeed. This difference among the Muslims itself shows that there must be someone to resolve the differences. Indeed. So there must be someone to resolve the differences, and in such a way, and in such a manner, that his evidence is present within the Quran. Indeed. Absolutely, he must have knowledge of the entire Quran. The one who will resolve the differences is none other than the successor of the Prophet. This right to resolve differences among people is the greatest need after the Prophet—a successor of the Prophet. Indeed. The question was that the Prophet had stated all things, he also gave the same argument: the Book and the Sunnah. Yes. But the Book and the Sunnah were not sufficient. If the Book and the Sunnah are sufficient, then why are there differences among the Muslims today? Indeed. Today, these differences are proof that there must be someone to resolve the differences, and that is none other than the successor of the Prophet. That is why it is said that intellect says, it must be someone like the Prophet. Intellect says, it must be someone like the Prophet. Just as the Master is Mustafa, such a Master is needed. Indeed. Indeed. Indeed. If the Muslim Ummah had understood this, there would be no differences among the Muslims today. Indeed. So viewers, as we have seen in our discussion, what should the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) be like? The simple answer is that he should be like the Messenger. But the arguments we presented before you, such as through the verse of Surah Jumu'ah, that he should fulfill the responsibility that was the Prophet’s—under that, his being infallible (Masoom) is very necessary. And finally, the important point that emerged is that through the Prophet’s Caliph, the differences of the Ummah will be resolved. He will be the one to resolve the differences among the Ummah. So, let us conclude our discussion today here. With this stanza of Musaddas that describes the characteristics of the Imam: that if there is an Imam, a Caliph, what should he be like? That he is the foundation of truth, without whom he is the Imam. He whose title is Truth, the solver of knots, he is the Imam. Wow! The one who is the essence of these prayers is the Imam. Wow! Wow! Wow! The one whose very nature is Prophetic is the Imam. How wonderful! The heart of even an enemy admits the truth for him; when he sleeps in sweet slumber, the world calls him the Prophet. Wow! Wow! Subhan Allah! Subhan Allah! Come, ladies and gentlemen, let us turn our attention towards Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, and with the conclusion of Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, our quiz link will close. If you have not submitted your answers yet, submit them immediately because, right after Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, our seven lucky winners will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Insha'Allah, we will be back in your service tomorrow. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad. O, Alayka ya Wali al-Asr, adriknā wa lā tuhliknā. Come, ladies and gentlemen. Come, ladies and gentlemen, let us now see who our seven lucky winners for today's episode are, who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. Among whom, first are our four third-prize winners, whose names are on your screen. Many, many congratulations to you all. Come, now our second-prize winners, who are two people, will also be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. Their names are on your screen. Many, many congratulations. Come, now for our final, the first-prize winner of today's episode, their name is on your screen. Many, many congratulations to you all. So, let us bid you farewell now. Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Speech vs. Silence: What is better? | کلام یا خاموشی: بہتر کیا ہے؟ | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the philosophical and spiritual comparison between speech and silence as taught by Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). The Imam explains that while both have potential pitfalls, speech is ultimately superior because it is the medium through which divine guidance, the Wilayah of Allah, and salvation are communicated. The talk concludes by highlighting that speech is necessary to articulate the value of silence, whereas silence cannot define the virtue of speech.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr. When Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) was asked about speech (kalam) and silence (sukoot)—which of them is better?—the Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Both of them have certain afflictions. If both remain safe from their respective afflictions, then speech is better than silence.' The narrator asked, 'How is that, O son of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Allah, the Almighty, did not send any of His prophets with silence, but rather sent them with speech. Because by remaining silent, no one can deserve Paradise, nor can the Wilayah of Allah be attained through silence, nor can one be saved from the fire of Hell. All these things can only be achieved through speech. I cannot compare the moon and the sun.' In the end, the Imam (a.s.) stated something that every rational person can intuitively realize. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'You can describe the virtue of silence through speech, but you cannot describe the virtue of speech by remaining silent.' We pray to Allah, the Lord of the Universe... ...cannot be described. We pray to Allah, the Lord of the Universe, to hasten the reappearance of our and your last Imam, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and to grant us the grace to benefit from the traditions of the Imams (a.s.).

Salvation, Paradise, and the Wilayah of Allah are attained through speech.

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Ziyaarat Ko Tark Karne Ka Anjaam [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual and worldly significance of performing the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). It highlights traditions from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) warning that abandoning this pilgrimage leads to a shortened lifespan and reduced sustenance. Furthermore, the speaker explains that failing to visit the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) can jeopardize one's status as a true Shia and impact one's standing in the afterlife.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. The Ziyarat of Hazrat Aba Abdullah al-Hussain (a.s.) is such a great duty from the Lord of the Worlds that in the traditions, not only has abandoning it been severely condemned, but the losses caused by abandoning it in this world and the hereafter have also been described. Mansur ibn Hazim states that we heard Imam Sadiq (a.s.) saying: 'If a year passes for a person and he does not go for the Ziyarat of the grave of Hussain, the Lord of the Worlds reduces one year from his life. And if I were to say that due to abandoning the Ziyarat of Hussain, some of you will die 30 years before your destined time, my statement would be true.' Therefore, never abandon his Ziyarat. Allah will prolong your life and increase your sustenance. But if you abandon his Ziyarat, Allah will shorten your life and decrease your sustenance. So, encourage one another to perform his Ziyarat and do not abandon it, because Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself will testify to your Ziyarat before Allah, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Hazrat Fatima (s.a.), and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). These are the worldly losses that a person will have to bear due to intentionally abandoning the Ziyarat. As for the loss in the hereafter, in this regard, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) states: 'Whoever does not go for the Ziyarat of the holy grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and assumes that he is our Shia, and passes away from this world in this state, he is not our Shia. And even if he is among the people of Paradise—meaning if he is interceded for and enters Paradise—he will only be a guest of the people of Paradise, meaning he will have neither his own status nor any house in Paradise.' We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that He grants every Shia of Imam Hussain (a.s.) the honor of performing the Ziyarat of his holy grave. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: EP#11: Ghadeer Mein Bay'at-E-Ali (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound historical and theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm, where the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) formally declared the successorship of Imam Ali (a.s.). It details the specific process of the Bay'ah (allegiance) and emphasizes the gravity of the covenant made by the companions. The discussion highlights the spiritual consequences of breaking this pledge and underscores the enduring importance of this event in Islamic history as a definitive moment that left no room for ambiguity.
content:
...and you can subscribe. You can go to all our social media handles and see their names, and the link to the top scorer's scoreboard is also given in our description, you can go and see their names there. Let us move towards our episode. In the field of Ghadir Khumm, the allegiance (bay'ah) taken by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) for all the people present there, and this... ...for all the people present there, and not only in this world, but even before this world, in the realm of souls (Alam-e-Arwah), although we do not remember it, but it is present in a documented and historical manner. And before this, in our episodes, it has been mentioned. Our topic today is the allegiance of Ali (a.s.) in Ghadir. In the open field of Ghadir Khumm, in the daylight, among 125,000 soldiers, this allegiance was taken for Islam. To discuss this, 'Bay'ah of Ali in Ghadir', we would like you to shed more light on this topic for our viewers. Bismillah... First of all, it is very important for us to know that the allegiance (bay'ah) of Amir al-Mu'minin taken by the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in the field of Ghadir Khumm—neither was any such allegiance taken before this, nor was any such allegiance taken after this. In the sermon of Ghadir, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) clearly summarized the entire religion. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) neither delivered such a sermon before this, nor did he deliver such a sermon after this. During the 23 years of the propagation of Islam, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) continuously announced the successorship of Mawla Ali (a.s.). If we reflect on this, we will realize that from the very beginning of the propagation of Islam, such as the very first invitation of Islam, the Invitation of the Close Relatives (Da'wat dhi al-'Ashirah), to every subsequent occasion, the Messenger of Allah announced the successorship of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). But the kind of announcement he made in the field of Ghadir... But the kind of announcement he made in the field of Ghadir regarding the Wilayah of Mawla Ali, such a grand gathering, the Messenger of Allah had never done before. Let us see how the allegiance (bay'ah) of Ali (a.s.) was taken in Ghadir and what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated in the sermon. First of all, 'I have pledged allegiance to Allah, and Ali has pledged allegiance to me, and I am taking this allegiance from you on behalf of Allah.' This makes it clear that Mawla Ali pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah took allegiance from the people on behalf of Allah. After this, he says, 'So whoever breaks [this covenant]...' This means that whoever breaks this allegiance, whoever breaks the allegiance of Mawla Ali, has indeed acted against himself and committed a crime against himself. 'Therefore, I have been commanded to take allegiance from you...' '...I have been commanded to take allegiance from you and to take your solemn pledge regarding what I have brought from Allah, the Almighty, concerning Ali (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.) after him.' He says, 'O people, fear Allah and pledge allegiance to Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin, and to Hasan, Hussain, and the Imams (a.s.) who are from their pure and everlasting progeny. Allah will destroy whoever rejects or betrays this allegiance, and Allah will have mercy on whoever remains faithful to this allegiance. And whoever breaks the allegiance, indeed breaks it to his own detriment. O people, those who hasten to pledge allegiance to Ali (a.s.), accept his Wilayah, and greet him as Amir al-Mu'minin, they are the ones who will succeed in the gardens of bliss...' I am writing in the box... regarding the allegiance to Ali (a.s.) in this era, the matters being presented to us, such as the Sermon of Ghadir delivered by the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in which he presented the summary of the entire religion. Indeed, they pledged allegiance to Ali (a.s.) there, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) on his pulpit announced all his virtues, and whatever message he delivered, the people accepted it and became convinced of it. Now, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explained this. Here, in that manner, they went to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) so that they could first pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and then to Amir al-Mu'minin, and also offer congratulations to them. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'All praise is due to Allah Who has granted us superiority over all the worlds.' It is found in history that the people present there... It is found in history that the people present there said in a loud voice, 'We heard your words and we support the command of His Messenger with our heart, soul, and tongue.' After this, they gathered around the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) and began trying to precede one another in pledging allegiance. They pledged allegiance to both, and there was a huge crowd trying to excel in pledging allegiance to them. Since the number of people was very large, the Messenger of Allah arranged the process of allegiance by setting up two tents. He organized it in such a way that people would first enter the tent of the Messenger of Allah, pledge allegiance to him, and congratulate him. After that, there was no way to go back; from that same tent, Maula Ali's tent was connected. Moving forward from there, they would enter Maula Ali's tent, pledge allegiance to him, congratulate him, and address Maula Ali as 'Amir al-Mu'minin' (Commander of the Faithful). It is worthy of attention, Brother Gulzar, that... ...it is worthy of attention, Brother Gulzar, that before this allegiance, the Messenger of Allah had never said, 'Congratulate me.' From the beginning of Islam until Ghadir Khumm, whatever commandments the Messenger of Allah brought from Allah through revelation, he never said regarding his prophethood, 'Congratulate me.' But the Wilayah of Maula Ali was such a matter for which the Prophet said, 'Congratulate me.' In this manner, the men pledged allegiance to Maula Ali, and this process of allegiance continued for three days. For three days, people pledged allegiance to Maula Ali. After this, all the common and elite, the Ansar and Muhajirun, pledged allegiance in this manner. And regarding those who came... after pledging allegiance... well, you mentioned that they pledged allegiance, but among those present there, women were also present. So, what was their method of pledging allegiance? For the women, the Messenger of Allah had arranged that water was kept in a large vessel, and in the middle of it... ...water was kept in the vessel, and a curtain was hung in the middle of it. From one side, the women would put their hand in that water, and from the other side, Maula Ali would put his hand in the same water and take their allegiance. Similarly, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) also took the allegiance of Maula Ali in this manner. Now, if any practice goes against Amir al-Mu'minin, it means they broke this allegiance. And in Ghadir Khumm, Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was herself present. This was the method; in this manner, in the plain of Ghadir, the women and all the people pledged allegiance. The greatest arrangement was that the Messenger of Allah tied his personal turban, named 'Sahab', on the head of Maula Ali, and placed one end of it on Maula Ali's shoulder. And Maula (a.s.) states, 'This is how the angels...' ...states, 'This is how the angels [descended] who helped Maula Ali.' Similarly, the turban... as we are seeing in this discussion, how the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed [his successor] in Ghadir. How people excelled and pledged allegiance to this announcement. But the tragedy was that people broke this allegiance. Brother Gulzar, the greatest tragedy of Islam is that after the demise of the Messenger of Allah, people not only broke the allegiance but also forgot the event of Ghadir. This is the greatest tragedy of Islam. And Janabe Zahra (s.a.), after the demise of her father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), used to remind people, 'You pledged allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.)...' ...'that you pledged allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.).' It is worthy of consideration that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) delivered her historical sermon in the court, after which people came to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and said, 'If you had told us earlier, we would not have pledged allegiance to anyone other than Maula Ali.' To this, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) replied, 'Did my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), leave any excuse or room for anyone after Ghadir Khumm?' Similarly, it is mentioned in the book 'Dala'il al-Imamah' that when Janabe Zahra (s.a.), after delivering her historical sermon in the court, was returning to her home, Rafe' bin Rifa'ah said to her, 'O Leader of the Women of Paradise! If Ali (a.s.) had discussed the matter of allegiance with us earlier, we would not have pledged allegiance to anyone else.' Janabe Zahra (s.a.) replied... Janabe Zahra (s.a.) said, 'Leave me alone! My father left no excuse for anyone after Ghadir Khumm.' Zulqarnain Sahab, regarding the discussion on allegiance here, since people broke the allegiance, if a person has already pledged allegiance to someone first, and later pledges allegiance to another, can he do so? Therefore, if we look according to their own beliefs, if someone has already pledged allegiance to one person and later pledges allegiance to another, it means he has broken the first allegiance. In this regard, there is a clear fatwa of the Sunni school of thought that the second caliphate will be considered void and he should be executed. When the allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) was taken in Ghadir, then according to the beliefs of the Sunni school... ...the second allegiance that was made is void, and his execution is obligatory. As Rizwan Sahab explained, according to their own beliefs, leaving one to pledge allegiance to another is void. And in the end, whoever accepted the allegiance of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) and remained steadfast on it, surely Allah will forgive his sins, look upon him with mercy, admit him into His Paradise, and elevate his status. And whoever broke this allegiance, no matter how many good deeds he performs, they are not acceptable in the court of Allah, simply because their deeds will not be accepted. On the Day of Judgment, the curse of Allah will be upon them, and Hell will be their abode. We pray to Allah that, through the intercession of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), Allah keeps us steadfast and firm on this great blessing. Yes, thank you very much... ...keep us steadfast and firm. Yes, thank you very much for discussing the topic of Ghadir and the allegiance to Ali (a.s.) in such a beautiful manner. As you mentioned, despite pledging allegiance in such large numbers, how people broke this allegiance, and what the consequence is for those who break it and pledge allegiance to another. Regarding those who pledged allegiance to Maula Ali and then broke it, we would only say to them: 'Remember what you did; you left the path of Ali, what did you do? You sold your conscience for worldly gains, and you hurt the heart of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.).' In this manner, the importance of this allegiance has been explained at every moment... ...explained the importance of this allegiance, and our small effort is also to carry this message forward. As this message continues to spread, whoever has love in their heart will be heard saying: 'There is a distance of centuries between him and me, there is a distance of centuries between him and me, but I know that I was present in Ghadir.' Now, respected viewers, with this, we conclude our episode here. Before saying goodbye to all of you, let us remind you that the link to our special episode for the Day of Ghadir, which is our 8th episode, is still active, and you can submit your answers until our final episode. If you haven't watched that episode, please watch it and answer the questions. The link for our quiz is also active. We request all of you to go there as soon as possible and give the correct answers to the questions. With this... Answer the questions quickly. With this, let me bid you farewell, Khuda Hafiz...

chapters.title: The Imam as the Spring of Humanity
chapters.summary: Believing in Imam al-Mahdi represents a divine promise of hope and renewal, akin to the arrival of spring after a long winter.

chapters.title: Moving Beyond Theoretical Belief
chapters.summary: Many believers treat the Imam as a distant, abstract concept like a planet, which fails to impact their daily lives or decision-making.

chapters.title: Integrating the Imam into Daily Life
chapters.summary: A true Shia must actively involve the Imam in their life, seeking his pleasure and guidance in every personal and moral decision.

chapters.title: The Shia's Daily Pledge of Allegiance
chapters.summary: True followers of the Imam express their devotion through constant yearning, daily renewal of their pledge, and a deep, painful longing for his presence.

chapters.title: The Significance of 15th of Shaban
chapters.summary: The 15th of Shaban is highlighted as a spiritually decisive night, comparable to Lailatul Qadr, offering a unique opportunity to deepen one's connection with the Imam.

chapters.title: The Imam's Reciprocal Gratitude
chapters.summary: The Imam is described as a grateful master who reciprocates acts of devotion, charity, and prayer performed in his name with personal care and spiritual support.

chapters.title: Establishing a Personal Connection
chapters.summary: Practical advice is given on how to build a tangible relationship with the Imam by stepping out of comfort zones and approaching him as a compassionate father figure.

chapters.title: The Imam as a Loving Father
chapters.summary: The Imam is characterized not as a distant figure, but as a loving, intimate brother and father who cares deeply for his followers and will treat them with affection upon his return.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Prayer for Reappearance
chapters.summary: The Imam explains that his return is dependent on Allah's permission and urges believers to pray for his reappearance rather than complaining about the delay.

chapters.title: Building a Personal Connection with the Imam
chapters.summary: Believers are encouraged to speak directly and persistently to the Imam for guidance, emphasizing that sincere effort and purification will lead to a response.

chapters.title: Seeking Knowledge from the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against seeking spiritual guidance from deviant paths, stressing that true knowledge and direction come solely from the Imam.

chapters.title: Seeking Approval from the Imam
chapters.summary: The story of Yunus ibn Abdul Rahman illustrates that one should prioritize the Imam's approval over the slander and negative opinions of others.

chapters.title: Commitment and Anticipation of the Savior
chapters.summary: Historical examples of the Jews of Medina and the followers of Prophet Nuh demonstrate the extreme commitment and patience required while awaiting a promised savior.

chapters.title: The Meeting with the Imam
chapters.summary: Ali ibn Mahziyar's long-awaited meeting with the Imam reveals that personal actions and spiritual readiness are the true keys to finding the Imam.

chapters.title: Barriers to Meeting the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that attachment to worldly wealth and mistreatment of others act as spiritual veils that prevent us from recognizing and connecting with the Imam.

chapters.title: The Importance of Repentance
chapters.summary: Using the example of a historical figure who humbly accepted the Imam's correction, the speaker emphasizes that sincere repentance is the key to spiritual proximity.

chapters.title: Stories of Encountering the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker shares a moving anecdote about a man who met the Imam in Karbala, illustrating the profound emotional impact and longing associated with such encounters.

chapters.title: Praying for the Imam's Reappearance
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with a heartfelt supplication, invoking the suffering of the Ahlulbayt to pray for the hastening of the Imam's reappearance.

title: 120 Martaba Meraaj Par Bula Kar Kis Cheez Ki Takeed Ki Gayi
excerpt: This lecture discusses a tradition from Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the Mi'raj of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It highlights that the Prophet was taken to Mi'raj 120 times, and on every occasion, Allah emphasized the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.). The speaker notes that this emphasis on Wilayah surpassed even the importance placed on the obligatory religious duties (Fara'id).
content:
Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) states: "Urija bin-nabiyyi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi mi'atan wa 'ishrina marrah," meaning the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) went to Mi'raj 120 times. "Ma min marratin illa wa qad awsal-lahu 'azza wa jalla fihal-nabiyya sallallahu alayhi wa alihi," and there was no occasion that passed in which Allah (Azza wa Jall) did not emphasize to His Prophet (s.a.w.a.) regarding what? "Bi-wilayati 'Aliyyin wal-a'immati 'alayhimus-salatu was-salam," that Allah (Tabaarak wa Ta'ala) gave special emphasis to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) regarding the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and all the Imams (a.s.). "Akthara mimma awsalahu bil-fara'id," meaning that the emphasis given regarding the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.) was much greater than the emphasis given regarding the obligatory duties (Fara'id). The Messenger of Allah was called to Mi'raj 120 times. Indeed. And the thing that was emphasized the most 120 times was Wilayah.
The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ascended to Mi'raj 120 times.
On every single occasion of Mi'raj, Allah emphasized the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.).
The importance given to Wilayah was greater than the emphasis placed on obligatory duties (Fara'id).
Wilayah is established as the most critical message delivered during the Mi'raj.
The tradition is attributed to Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.).
