title: Winner Announcement | Ali (a.s.) Nahin to Kuch Nahin | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological significance of the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib within the context of the Ghadeer-e-Khum event. It emphasizes that devotion to Ali is a fundamental criterion for faith, salvation, and the acceptance of religious deeds. The discourse highlights the Prophet's teachings regarding Ali's status as the lighthouse of faith and warns against the spiritual consequences of harboring hatred toward him.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Hassan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his supporters, his Shia, his servants, and his followers, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. Thereafter, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Mentioning Ali is worship.' The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), in this famous and well-known hadith which has been narrated by both sects, states that 'Mentioning Ali is worship.' Alhamdulillah, you have been listening to the mention of Ali continuously for three days and participating in this quiz. Jazakumullah Khairul Jaza, Insha'Allah. And may Allah give you the best reward. It is necessary that we understand the importance of this mention, the importance of the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.); it is very important. Since time is short, I will present two or three narrations for your service so that the matter becomes clearer, regarding how important the mention of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is and how important love for him is. Look at this narration; the first narration I am presenting for your service is from Basa'ir al-Darajat, and this narration has been narrated by Abu Hamza al-Thumali, that is, Thabit ibn Dinar. He says: 'I heard Aba Ja'far (a.s.) saying: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called for water for Wudu.' One day, the Messenger of Allah asked for water so he could perform Wudu. 'When he finished, he took the hand of Ali (a.s.).' He held the hand of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) firmly, 'and joined his hand with the hand of Ali (a.s.). Then he said: Indeed, you are a warner.' The Prophet recited this verse of the Quran, which addresses the Prophet: 'O Prophet, you are only a warner.' 'And then he brought his hand to his chest,' he took the blessed hand of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and pressed it against his own chest, 'and after pressing it to his chest, he said: And for every people, there is a guide.' Meaning, the Prophet is the warner and Ali is the guide. And then he said, 'O Ali, this is an important sentence, look, pay attention to this: O Ali, you are the foundation of the religion.' Meaning, if there is no Ali, there is no religion; if there is no Ali, there is nothing. 'You are the foundation of the religion and the lighthouse of faith.' The lighthouse of faith, meaning if anyone wants to look towards faith, they should look at Ali ibn Abi Talib. If the standard of faith is Ali ibn Abi Talib, if you want to recognize a believer, look at Ali ibn Abi Talib. The further one moved away from Ali, the further they moved away from faith. And Insha'Allah, in the next hadith, we will also mention the hatred of Ali. And then the Prophet says, 'And you are the ultimate goal of guidance, O Ali.' You are the target of guidance, you are the culmination of the guidance that comes from Allah. Ali is the goal of guidance, meaning whoever reaches Ali has found guidance, and whoever deviates from Ali has gone astray. Whoever moves away from Ali has gone astray. The further away, the more astray. 'And you are the leader and guide of the Ghurr al-Muhajjalin.' Now, these are two Arabic terms; there is no time to explain them in detail, just understand briefly that 'Ghurr' refers to a horse that has, for example, a black body, but only its forehead is white. This is a sign that the horse belongs to a pure breed, pure, Tayyib and Tahir, of pure birth. It is called 'Ghurr', meaning its birth is pure and clean. And 'Muhajjalin' in Arabic refers to a horse whose four legs are of a different color than its body. This is a sign that its... parents are both pure and clean. In other words, as is commonly used, 'Najib-ut-Tarafain' (noble from both sides). Both parents are noble and chosen. So, you are the leader and guide of the 'Ghurr al-Muhajjalin', those whose birth is pure and clean; you are the guide only for them. This means that if someone does not accept the leadership and guidance of Ali, and stands in opposition to Ali, it means there is a problem with their birth. There is a problem with their purity, a problem with their birth. And then the Prophet says, 'I bear witness to this.' Now, if the Prophet bears witness to something, then there is no room for any discussion after that, nothing remains, because the Prophet, about whom we bear witness to his Prophethood daily in our prayers when we recite the Tashahhud—'I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger'—if that Prophet bears witness to someone, you can understand their status. Here the Prophet is testifying to the Wilayah of Ali. "Ash-hadu bi-dhalik"—this testimony, this is what is called testimony. To bear witness, this is what is called bearing witness. This is one Hadith that I just presented from 'Basair al-Darajat'. 'Basair al-Darajat' is a book written by the late Saffar, and this late Saffar was Muhammad bin Hasan bin Farrukh al-Saffar. He passed away in 290 Hijri and witnessed the era of the Aimmah, the Aimmah Masumeen (a.s.). He was a teacher to great scholars like Sheikh Kulayni and others. So, you can estimate his status and rank from this. Now listen to the second Hadith, from 'Amali al-Sheikh al-Tusi'. Sheikh al-Tusi, Sheikh al-Ta'ifa, the Sheikh of the Shias, the guide of the Shias, who laid the foundation of the Hawza of Najaf al-Ashraf. He started the Hawza of Najaf al-Ashraf. He narrates a Hadith that Zazan said, "Sami'tu Salman Rahmatullah alayh"—Zazan says I heard from Salman, and Salman was saying, "La azalu uhibbu Aliyyan"—I will continuously love Ali, I always love him, meaning I do, and I will continue to do so. I love Ali immensely. Why? Salman presents the proof. Listen to the proof: "Fa-inni ra'aitu Rasulallahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi yazribu fakhzahu"—one day I saw the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) striking his thigh. When does a person strike their thigh? When they emphasize something. When they stress a point, they strike their thigh and speak. Just like you might have seen a Khatib. When a Khatib emphasizes a point, he strikes his thigh so that even if someone is not paying attention, they become attentive. So that the one not listening, listens. What am I saying? The Prophet "yazribu fakhzahu"—and Salman, O Salman, to whom the Prophet gave the title "Nafas-ur-Rahman" (The Breath of the Merciful), Salman is Nafas-ur-Rahman, the breath of Allah. "Wa yaqulu"—the Prophet says, "Ya Ali! Muhibbuka li muhibbun"—O Ali! Whoever loves you, loves me. "Wa muhibbi lillahi muhibb"—and whoever loves me, loves Allah. And then after that, he says, "Wa mubghiduka li mubghid"—and whoever bears hatred toward you, bears hatred toward me. "Wa mubghidi lillahi ta'ala mubghid"—he bears hatred toward Allah the Almighty. Allahu Akbar! He is bearing hatred toward Allah. The one who bears hatred toward Ali. Now come and see, let us look at another Hadith which is present in 'Amali al-Sheikh al-Tusi' itself, and this narration is reported from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas, as you know, was a student of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). And he says, "Qultu lin-nabiyyi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi awsini"—I submitted, "O Messenger of Allah! Give me a bequest, give me advice. Please advise me." "Qala sallallahu alayhi wa alihi"—now look at the advice. Such a great scholar whom people call 'Hibr-ul-Ummah' (The Ink of the Ummah), the ink of the Ummah, Hibr-ul-Ummah Ibn Abbas. He says, "Advise me." The Prophet says, the Prophet said, "Look, you do this, you do that, you do that." He said nothing of the sort. The Prophet said, "Alayka bi-mawaddati Aliyyi-bni Abi Talib alayhimus-salatu wassalam"—do you want to hear my bequest? Do you want to hear my advice? Love Ali. Love Ali. "Walladhi ba'athani bil-haqqi nabiyya"—I swear by that Being who sent me as a Prophet with the truth. Meaning the Prophet is swearing by Allah. That Prophet who is Sadiq (Truthful). He is swearing by Allah so that there is no doubt in anyone's heart, so that no one thinks the Prophet is saying something from his own accord. "Walladhi ba'athani bil-haqqi nabiyya, la yaqbalullahu min 'abdin hasanatan hatta yas'alahu 'an hubbi Aliyyi-bni Abi Talib"—until He asks him about the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib. He will ask, was there love for Ali ibn Abi Talib or not? Was there enmity toward his enemies or not? This is where the questioning will end. If it was there, then the matter will proceed. If it was not there, then the matter ends right there. Then there is no place for you in Paradise. "Wa huwata'ala a'lam"—while Allah is A'lam (All-Knowing), He knows who is who. The Prophet says, Allah knows, but to complete the proof (Hujjat), so that the 'Ru'us-ul-Ashad' (the leaders of the enemies), meaning those in the public who bear hatred toward Ali, are disgraced and those who love Ali, their dignity is increased. They should be decorated publicly, that is why Allah is saying this. "Fa-in ja'ahu bi-wilayatihi qabila 'amalahu 'ala ma kana minhu"—Allah will accept all his deeds, no matter what they were. No matter what they were. Look, this is a Hadith, a Hadith of the Prophet, and Sheikh al-Tusi, Sheikh al-Ta'ifa, has narrated it. "'Ala ma kana min"—"Wa in lam ya'ti bi-wilayatihi"—and if he does not come with the Wilayah of Ali, if there is no Wilayah of Ali, then "lam yas'al 'an shay'in"—there will be no further questions, go straight to Hell. Brother, you have nothing here, nothing at all. Go, go to Hell. There is no further questioning. "Summa amara bihi ilan-nar"—and then Allah will say, go, go to Hell. "Ya Ibna Abbas! O Ibn Abbas! Walladhi ba'athani bil-haqqi nabiyya, inna-nara la-ashaddu ghadaban 'ala mubghidi Aliyyin minha 'ala man za'ama annalillahi walada"—O Ibn Abbas! The fire of Hell will be more wrathful toward the one who bears hatred toward Ali than toward the one who believes that Allah has a son. Meaning the Mubghid-e-Ali (hater of Ali), the one who bears hatred toward Ali, his punishment is greater than the one who believes in a son of Allah. Meaning the one who believes Allah has a son is a Mushrik (polytheist) and will go to Hell. But his punishment will not be as great as that of the Mubghid-e-Ali, the one who bears hatred toward Ali. And then after that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, "Ya Ibna Abbas! O Ibn Abbas! Law annal-mala'ikatal-muqarrabina wal-ambiya-al-mursalin"—if all, if the favored angels, those angels who are favored in the court of Allah, are near, the 'proximity angels', and all the sent Prophets "ijtama'u 'ala bughdihi"—if all of them were to gather on the hatred of him, "wa-la-yaf'alu"—although this will not happen. Although this will not happen, because neither the angels will bear hatred toward Ali, nor will the sent Prophets. The Prophet is just conveying a point. If this were to happen, "la-'adhdhabahumullahu bin-nar"—then Allah would cast all those angels and Prophets into Hell. Although this will not happen, but here the Prophet is trying to say what He is saying that no matter how great a person considers themselves in this world, if there is hatred of Ali in the heart, you will be thrown into Hell face-first. No matter how much people respect you, no matter how highly esteemed you are in the eyes of the masses, if there is hatred of Ali, then remember this. The Prophet is trying to explain this to the people who were sitting around him. He is trying to explain to them. But still, nevertheless, some people understood, and some people, the majority, did not understand. Qultu ya Rasulallah. Now Ibn Abbas asked: O Messenger of Allah, hal yubghiduhu ahadun? Will there be anyone who will bear hatred toward Ali? Is it possible that someone bears hatred toward Ali? Qala Ibn Abbas. The Prophet said, yes Ibn Abbas. Na'am yubghiduhu. Yes, there are such people who will exist. Qawmun yadhkuruna annahum min ummati. These are the people who will claim that they are from my Ummah. They will claim that they are from my Ummah. But lam yaj'alillahu lahum fil-islami nasiba. Allah has not kept any share for them in Islam, that they will not even be Muslims. What is their claim? That they are from my Ummah. But what is the reality? That they are not Muslims. Ibn Abbas. O Ibn Abbas, inna min 'alamat bughdihim. And what is the sign of their hatred? Look at what the hatred is. Look, the Prophet has already told everything beforehand. What is the sign of hatred? Bughduhum lahum tafdi lahum. Tafdi lahum man huwa dunahu 'alayh. That they will consider those people superior. They will prefer those who are inferior to Ali over Ali. In fact, even saying 'inferior' is not correct, it is not appropriate because there is no comparison at all. There is no comparison. In Arabic, there is a proverb that is used, 'Qiyasu ma 'al fariq'. It is an idiom in Arabic. 'Qiyasu ma 'al fariq' is when two things cannot be compared. Where is the eye of the Pleiades (Thurayya) and where is the eye of the earth (Sara)? Where are the heights of the Pleiades? And where are these depths of the earth? Is there any comparison? There is no comparison. But the Prophet is just speaking to explain the point that some people will be such that they will bring others and prefer them over Ali. This preferring over Ali is a sign of their hatred. It reached the point that Ibn Abil Hadid, who was a Mu'tazili scholar who wrote the commentary on Nahj al-Balagha. He says in the introduction of his commentary that all praise is for Allah, who gave preference to the 'mafzul' (lesser) over the 'afzal' (superior). Meaning, he gave preference to those who were lesser in virtue than Ali—who were nothing in comparison to Ali—over Ali. It is as if someone who failed in class was given a gold medal, saying, 'You did very well by failing.' Walladhi ba'athani bil haqq (By the One who sent me with the truth), the Being by whose oath He sent me with the truth, Allah has not sent any Prophet more honorable than me, wala awsiya akram alayhi min wasi Ali (and He has not appointed any successor more honorable than my successor, Ali). And He has not appointed any successor more honorable and noble than Ali. Qala Ibn Abbas (Ibn Abbas says), when I heard all these sentences from the Messenger of Allah, falam azallahu kama amarani Rasul Allah (I did not deviate from what the Messenger of Allah commanded me). And he advised me to love him. Wa innahu la akbaru amali indi (And for me, the Wilayah of Ali and the love of Ali is the greatest deed). There is no deed greater than this. What word did Ibn Abbas use? 'Amali', deed. Deed, Wilayah of Ali is a deed. So now, when people say, 'Recite something that is about deeds,' the deed is this: the Wilayah of Ali is a deed. If there is no Wilayah of Ali, then all other deeds are useless. Wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibina at-tahirin al-masumin al-mazlumin, wa la'natullahi da'im ala a'daihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri faza'ilihim wa manaqibihim wa mukhalifi aqwalihim wa ahkamihim wa ma'rifihim. Allah, the Lord of Majesty, has stated in the Holy Quran: {Wa ma khalaqtul jinna wal insa illa liya'budun} (And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me). Now the question arises, what is the meaning of worship? Is worship only praying, fasting, performing Hajj, or giving Zakat? No, the scope of worship is very vast. Worship means doing everything for the pleasure of Allah that Allah likes. If you serve your parents, this is also worship. If you help a poor person, this is also worship. If you acquire knowledge, this is also worship. If you speak the truth, this is also worship. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) has said: 'Worship is not just the name of prayer and fasting, but treating Allah's creation well and adhering to Allah's commands is true worship.' Therefore, we should mold our entire life into worship. We should do every task for the pleasure of Allah. When we do this, our entire life will become worship.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 27 | Tafseer of Surah an-Nasr (110) - Part 1
excerpt: This lecture provides an introductory commentary on Surah an-Nasr, exploring its significance as a divine announcement of Islam's victory and the Prophet's impending departure. The speaker discusses the spiritual merits and rewards associated with reciting this Surah, including safety from Hellfire. Additionally, the lecture details the historical context leading to the Conquest of Mecca, specifically focusing on the breach of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah by the Quraysh and their allies.
content:
Masha'Allah, wa la quwwata illa billahil Aliyyil Azim. A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdu lillahi Rabbil 'Alamin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Ashrafil Anbiya'i wal-Mursalin, wa 'ala Alihit-Tayyibinat-Tahirin... Once again, we are present in your service. Previously, the commentary of Surah al-Kauthar was going on, and today it is regarding the commentary of Surah an-Nasr. I am starting this from Tafsir al-Thaqalayn, page number 486. I am starting from page number 486. In this Surah, Allah has announced the victory of Islam, that now Islam has gained dominance over disbelief (kufr) and polytheism (shirk). Now people will enter Islam in crowds. Upon this victory and help, praise and glorify your Lord. Regarding its recitation, in the book 'Faza'il al-A'mal', Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Whoever recites this Surah in his obligatory or supererogatory prayers, Allah will grant him victory over his enemies. On the Day of Judgment, he will rise from his grave in such a state that he will have a letter of safety from Hell and its heat, and he will enter Paradise.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Whoever recites this Surah will receive the reward as if he was with the Prophet during the Conquest of Mecca.' In the book 'Sawab al-A'mal', it is narrated that whoever recites this Surah in his prayers, God will grant him victory over all his enemies, and on the Day of Judgment, he will be raised in such a state that he will have a letter of safety in his hand, which God sent with him from his grave, granting him safety from the fire of Hell. In Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan, it is stated that whoever recites this Surah, it is as if he was with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) on the day of the Conquest of Mecca. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)... ...It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) used to frequently recite istighfar, saying, 'Indeed, He is the Acceptor of repentance, the Merciful.' Another narration states that when the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited this Surah to his companions, they all became happy, but his uncle Abbas (a.s.) began to weep. The Prophet asked, 'O uncle, why are you weeping?' He replied, 'My assessment is that you are about to depart from this world.' He (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Yes, you are speaking the truth.' But the Prophet remained alive in this world for two years after this event. This Surah is also called Surah at-Tawdi' (the Surah of Farewell). In Al-Kafi, Imam (a.s.) said: 'The first thing that was revealed was Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, Iza ja'a nasrullahi wal-fath... This help and victory is the grand victory of Islam.' Other commentators have presented this explanation regarding the victory: their view is that at the place of Hudaybiyyah, the treaty that was made between the Muslims and the polytheists of Mecca... ...the polytheists of Mecca did not give any importance to that treaty. They committed excesses against the allies of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). When his allies complained to him, the Messenger of Allah decided to help his allies. Among the causes of the Conquest of Mecca is that when the Messenger of Allah directed his military campaign towards Mecca, during this time, while the Prophet was in Medina, Banu Bakr attacked Banu Khuza'ah. In those days, the basis of the dispute between the tribes was that a man named Malik bin Abbad, who was on a trade journey, was killed by the people of Banu Khuza'ah. In the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, among the conditions between the Messenger of Allah and the Quraysh of Mecca, one condition was that whoever wished could enter into an alliance with the Quraysh, and whoever wished could enter into an alliance with the Messenger of Allah. Consequently, Banu Bakr allied with the Quraysh, and Banu Khuza'ah allied with the Messenger of Allah. During this period of truce, Banu Bakr, along with Banu Dil, thought it a good opportunity to take revenge on their rivals, Banu Khuza'ah. For this purpose... ...thought it a good opportunity. For this purpose, Nawfal bin Muawiyah al-Dili, along with some other individuals whose leader he was—although not all Quraysh agreed to this, some individuals considered him their leader and followed him—set out and launched a night attack on Banu Khuza'ah who were camped near a spring named Al-Wateer, killed one of their men, and after that, war broke out between them. On this occasion, the Quraysh helped Banu Bakr, and finally Banu Khuza'ah had to take refuge in the Haram. Historians have written that Safwan bin Umayyah, Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl, and Suhail bin Amr also helped Banu Bakr in disguise during this night attack. When Banu Khuza'ah took refuge in the Haram, Banu Bakr attacked them there as well. A member of Banu Khuza'ah, Amr bin Salim, appealed against this incident in the court of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). This man came to Medina, and when he entered Masjid-an-Nabawi, the Messenger of Allah was present in the mosque with all his companions. He presented his entire situation before him in verses. He presented his entire state before you in verses, and this very incident became the cause of the Conquest of Makkah. He said, 'O Muhammad, I remind Muhammad of the ancient alliance between our fathers, and I invoke it. Indeed, the Quraysh have breached the treaty with you and have broken your firm covenant, and they have killed us while we were in the state of ruku' and sujud.' After this, he said, 'We have accepted Islam, yet they have killed us.' Upon hearing this, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Amr ibn Salim, rest assured, we are ready to help you.' And Budayl ibn Warqa himself came to Madinah with a few people and narrated the entire incident to the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah said to his companions, 'Abu Sufyan will come to us to renew this treaty.' When Budayl ibn Warqa was returning from Madinah towards his destination, Makkah, he met Abu Sufyan on the way. Abu Sufyan was heading towards Madinah for the confirmation of the treaty. The Messenger of Allah already had knowledge that Abu Sufyan would come for the renewal of the treaty, and he met him on the way. The same thing happened; when Abu Sufyan saw Budayl, he guessed that he must have surely come after meeting the Messenger of Allah. He guessed that he must have surely come after meeting the Messenger of Allah. When Abu Sufyan asked him, he said that he had gone to the seashore to meet the members of his tribe. Abu Sufyan asked, 'Did you not go to Muhammad?' He replied, 'No.' When Budayl departed towards Makkah, Abu Sufyan said to his companions, 'If he had gone to Madinah, his camel must have eaten the date-stones of Madinah.' He went to the resting place of his camel, picked up its dung, broke it, and saw date-stones inside it. Abu Sufyan said, 'I swear by Allah that Budayl is returning after meeting Muhammad.' In this way, these people used to guess who went to whom and who did not, because Abu Sufyan and his followers were very advanced in plotting and deception. Respected audience, I conclude my talk here today. Inshallah, tomorrow our discussion will continue from here. When Abu Sufyan went to Madinah and reached the Messenger of Allah, what conversation took place, what was discussed, and what actions were taken? Inshallah, tomorrow there will be a discussion on this topic. Until then, I take your leave. Khuda Hafiz. Wa Akhiru Da'wana Anil Hamdulillahi Rabbil 'Alamin.

title: EP#16: Kya Bibi Zahra (s.a.) Ko Fadak Na Dena Sahih Tha?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical controversy surrounding the refusal to grant Fadak to Bibi Fatimah (s.a.) after the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker references Sahih al-Bukhari to highlight the disagreement between Fatimah (s.a.) and Abu Bakr regarding the inheritance of the Prophet's property. The lecture emphasizes the spiritual significance of Bibi Fatimah's anger and the missed opportunity to honor the leader of the women of Paradise.
content:
Was it right not to give Fadak to Bibi Zahra (s.a.)? Not giving Fadak to Bibi Zahra (s.a.) was a very big mistake. This famous Hadith is found in Sahih al-Bukhari: After the passing of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Fatimah (s.a.), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), asked Abu Bakr to give her her share of the inheritance left by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) from the Fai' which Allah had bestowed upon him. Abu Bakr said, 'The Messenger of Allah had said, "We do not leave inheritance; whatever we Prophets leave behind is charity."' Upon this, Fatimah (s.a.), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), became angry and stopped talking to Abu Bakr, and she maintained this stance until her last moments, meaning she did not even speak to Abu Bakr. The land of Fadak was part of that very Fai' which Bibi Fatimah (s.a.) had demanded. Fai' refers to the property acquired without fighting a war. If the Lady (s.a.) had demanded her share from that Fai', then before refusing her, they should have at least thought that she is the daughter of the Prophet and the leader of the women of Paradise. If they had pleased her, they would have secured a guarantee of Paradise, but alas!

title: EP#5: Agar 2 Khalifa Ki Bay’at Ki Jaaye | Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture examines the theological and historical implications of the Islamic ruling regarding the pledge of allegiance to multiple caliphs. The speaker references a narration from Sahih Muslim to argue that the first legitimate pledge of allegiance takes precedence over any subsequent ones. By applying this principle to the event of Ghadir Khumm, the lecture asserts that the leadership of Imam Ali (a.s.) was established first, rendering any later claims to the caliphate invalid according to this specific jurisprudential logic.
content:
Can a caliph be liable to be killed? The Ahl-as-Sunnah are of the view that if allegiance is pledged to two caliphs, the one to whom allegiance was pledged first will be accepted, and the person to whom allegiance was pledged later should be killed. As proof, there is a narration in one of their major books, Sahih Muslim, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'If allegiance is pledged to two caliphs, kill the one to whom allegiance was pledged later.' If we study the history of Islam, the allegiance to Maula Ali (a.s.) as the successor of the Prophet had already been pledged at Ghadir Khumm, where Maula Ali (a.s.) was also congratulated on being the master of all Muslims. Now, according to this law of allegiance, if allegiance is pledged to anyone after the allegiance of Ghadir, then not only is that allegiance unacceptable, but that second caliph would be considered liable to be killed.
Sunni jurisprudence dictates that the first pledge of allegiance is the only valid one.

excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual significance of Dua-e-Nudbah, which is recommended for recitation every Friday. content:
And the command of 'Sadd-al abwab illa babahu'—that all doors should be closed except his door—we read this sentence in both forms. And this is very famous in Dua-e-Nudbah, which we are commanded to recite on Fridays. Every Friday, as a lover of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), we are reminded of this every Friday; we are reminded of that very door in this Dua-e-Nudbah. It is our responsibility that every person should not only recite it themselves but also encourage others to do so.

excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the importance of deeply immersing oneself in the grief of Imam Hussain (a.s.) during the days of mourning. content:
We should try to immerse ourselves in the grief of Hussain (a.s.) as much as possible, so that the effect is visible on our faces. And by the time the Day of Ashura arrives, our grief should become so intense that if someone merely takes the name of Hussain, it should be enough to make us weep. title: Har Nabi (a.s.) Ne Tabarra Kiya | #Wilayat & #Tabarra
excerpt: This lecture explores the fundamental connection between the prophethood of all messengers and the concepts of Wilayah and Tabarra. Citing Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), the speaker explains that every Prophet was sent with the dual mandate to call people to worship Allah and to disassociate from Taghut. The discourse highlights that the rejection of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) is the root cause of spiritual deviation and historical destruction.
content:
Every Prophet practiced Tabarra (disassociation). Hazrat Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) states that Allah never sent a Prophet except with the belief in our Wilayah and Bara'at (disassociation) from our enemies. This is Allah's call in His Book. Then the Imam recited the verse from Surah An-Nahl: 'Wa laqad ba'athna fi kulli ummatin rasulan' (And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger), who was saying to his nation, 'Anbudullah' (Worship Allah) 'wajtanibut-taghut' (and avoid Taghut). [Music] 'Faminhum man hadallah' (And among them were those whom Allah guided) 'wa minhum man haqqat alayhil-dalalah' (and among them were those upon whom error was deservedly decreed). And why did they deserve it? The Imam says, 'Takdhiban li-Ali Muhammad (a.s.)' (because they denied and belied the family of Muhammad (a.s.)). And then the Imam recited the final part of the verse: 'Fasiru fil-ard' (So travel through the land) 'fanzuru kaifa kana aqibatul-mukadhdhibin' (and observe how was the end of the deniers). It is as if the Imam (a.s.) is saying: Go and see what was the end of the beliefs, the laws, and the religion of those who belied the family of Muhammad (a.s.).

title: Ep#12 | Kya Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Nabiyon Se Afzal Hain?
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological status of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) within Shia Islam, specifically addressing his superiority over previous Prophets. The speaker details the five resemblances Imam Mahdi shares with Prophets Yunus, Yusuf, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Furthermore, the lecture emphasizes that the position of Imamat is the highest rank granted by Allah, as evidenced by the life of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) and the future descent of Prophet Isa (a.s.) to pray behind the Imam.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum Wa Rahmatullahi Wa Barakatuh. When discussions on Imamat and Khilafat take place among different sects of Muslims, one topic is always on superiority—whether a certain companion is better and more superior than another companion or not. Alhamdulillah, among the Shia, this debate never occurs as to whether a companion is better than our Imams, because it is our complete belief that our 12 Imams, except for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), are superior and better in every aspect than all the Prophets. In today's episode, we will see how Imam Mahdi (a.s.) not only possesses the resemblances of other Prophets, but is also superior to the Prophets. Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will complete the mission of the Prophets. If Imam Mahdi (a.s.) were not there, the missions of all the Prophets and Messengers would have remained in darkness. That is why Allah... Our fifth Imam, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) states, 'Indeed, in this Qa'im...' ...states, 'Indeed, in this Qa'im (a.s.), there is resemblance to five Prophets: Hazrat Yunus, Hazrat Yusuf, Hazrat Musa, Hazrat Isa, and Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (peace be upon our Prophet and his family and upon them).' Let us see how this resemblance is. His resemblance to Hazrat Yunus (a.s.) is that when he returned to his people, even though his age was advanced, he still appeared young. His resemblance to Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) is that when he was in occultation, his distance from his father, Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.)—his respected father—was not very far, yet they could not recognize him. His resemblance to Hazrat Musa (a.s.) is his hidden and concealed birth, the fear of his enemies, his reappearance by Allah's command, and prevailing over his enemies with the help of the people. His resemblance to Hazrat Isa (a.s.) is the different differences of opinion regarding him. One group says that he was born... One group says that he was not born at all, one group says that he passed away, and some people say that he was either killed or crucified. And his resemblance to his grandfather Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is that he will rise with the sword and will slay the enemies of Allah and the oppressors. This is his resemblance to the Prophets. Let us look at how he is superior to other Prophets. First of all, let us see how the position of Imamat is superior to the position of Prophethood. The verse of Surah al-Baqarah in which Allah, addressing Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.), says: 'Inni ja'iluka lin-nasi imama' (Indeed, I will make you an Imam for the people). In the exegesis of this verse, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states that Allah first made Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) His servant, after that He made him His Prophet, after that He made him His Messenger, after that He made him His friend, and finally He made him Imam. And when all these attributes were gathered, then Allah... ...when all these attributes were gathered, then Allah appointed him. From this, it becomes clear that the last and most grand position that Allah gave to Ibrahim (a.s.) was the position of Imamat. And in this position, Allah kept only and only the successors of His last Prophet, because in the eyes of Allah, this is the greatest position. That is why our Imam, in another explanation of this verse, states: 'Lau `alima-llahu anna isman afdalu minhu la-sammāna'—'If Allah knew of any name more superior than this, He would have named us by it.' If there were any name or position better than this in the eyes of Allah, He would have called us by that name. From these traditions, it is absolutely clear that the status of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is so high that even Hazrat Isa (a.s.) testified to his closeness to Allah. In Sahih al-Bukhari, a Hadith is found narrated by Abu Hurairah in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'What will be your state when Hazrat Isa (a.s.) descends to the earth and your Imam is from among you?' And your Imam will be among you. This hadith proves that at that time—please subscribe to the channel—the companions will be present. On the other hand, it is found in Sahih Muslim that Jabir narrates: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say that a group from my Ummah will never stop upholding the truth and will remain victorious until the Day of Judgment.' Then, Hazrat Isa ibn Maryam (a.s.) will descend, and their leader will invite him to come and lead the prayer, but he will refuse and say, 'No, some of you are leaders over others, and this is an honor from Allah for this Ummah.' Here, who is Hazrat Isa (a.s.) pointing towards? Who is the one behind whom he will pray? It is none other than the Imam of the time, the Mahdi (a.s.), who will arrive. Just as Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is superior to Hazrat Maryam (s.a.), in the same way, Hazrat... [audio unclear]. This is the noble hadith of Hazrat Isa and... Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin... [audio unclear/noise]. To give the correct answer, write it in the comment section of this video. Those who answer the question correctly... for the reward of 1000 rupees, please subscribe to this channel.

title: 11 #Muharram | J. Zainab (s.a.) Aur Imam Sajjad (a.s.) Ki Guftugu [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture recounts the events of the 11th of Muharram, focusing on the profound grief of Imam Sajjad (a.s.) as he witnessed the unburied bodies of his family in Karbala. It highlights the comforting words of Sayyida Zainab (s.a.), who reminds the Imam of a divine covenant regarding the future reverence and preservation of the shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The talk concludes by reflecting on how, despite centuries of oppression, the legacy and shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.) continue to flourish as a testament to his ultimate victory.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Assalamu ala al-Husayn, wa ala Ali ibn al-Husayn, wa ala awlad al-Husayn, wa ala ashab al-Husayn. On the 11th of Muharram, 61 AH, after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.), the order was given to take the captives to Ibn Ziyad. Sayyid al-Sajjad, Hazrat Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), and the family of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) were mounted on camels and preparations were made to take them towards Kufa. May Allah never show any father the sight of his children in such a state. Imam Sajjad (a.s.) says: 'I saw the bodies of the Prophet's family lying without shrouds. My heart was sinking, and what I was witnessing at that time was very heavy for me, and due to the intensity of the grief, it was as if my soul was about to depart from my body. At that time, my aunt Zaynab bint Ali (a.s.) saw my condition and...' Seeing my condition, [the Imam] (a.s.) comforted me and said to me, 'O sign of my grandfather, my father, and my brother, I feel that you are about to lose your life.' I replied, 'O my master, why should I not be restless and distressed when I see the blood-stained bodies of my father, my brothers, my uncles, my cousins, and my family members lying there? There is no one to give them ghusl (ritual bath) and no one to bury them, and no one is even going near them.' Upon this, my aunt comforted me and said, 'O son, do not be distressed by what you see. By Allah, this is a covenant that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made with your grandfather Ali (a.s.) and your uncle Imam Hasan (a.s.), that Allah has taken a pledge from some people of this Ummah—whom the tyrants of this Ummah do not recognize, but who are known in the heavens—that they will gather these scattered pieces and bury these blood-stained bodies.' And they will bury these blood-stained bodies, and they will erect a sign on the grave of your noble father, Imam Hussain (a.s.), on this land of Karbala, the effect of which will never fade. Its mark will never be erased despite the passing of days and nights. The oppressors and the followers of misguidance will strive hard to erase and destroy it, but it will only become more manifest and its status will only continue to rise. Today, the gathering of the lovers of Imam Hussain (a.s.) at the shrine of the Imam of Truth is the result of that very prophecy of Princess Zainab (s.a.). As time passed, centuries went by, and tyrannical kings broke mountains of oppression; restrictions were placed on Hussain (a.s.), pilgrims were killed, and their hands and feet were cut off, but Karbala is still vibrant today. The shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and that magnificent structure are themselves proclaiming the victory of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the defeat of Yazid. I pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He hastens the reappearance of the successor of Hussain, Imam Mahdi (a.s.), and grants every lover of Imam Hussain (a.s.) the Ziyarat of Karbala soon. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. I pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He hastens the reappearance of the successor of Hussain, Imam Mahdi (a.s.), and grants every lover of Imam Hussain (a.s.) the Ziyarat of Karbala soon. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. ...

title: Asli Sharaab Khor Kaun? | Maulvi Abdul Hafeez Ko Jawaab
excerpt: This lecture provides a critical rebuttal to Maulvi Abdul Hafeez regarding his accusations against Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker analyzes the historical and theological inaccuracies in the Maulvi's claims, specifically focusing on the misattribution of Quranic verses and the reliance on weak hadith chains. By citing Sunni historical sources, the lecture challenges the integrity of the accusations while highlighting the bias present in the Maulvi's methodology.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali-ul-Asr. Help us. Do not let us perish. Who is the real drunkard? There is something that is being concealed. May 20, 2021. Thursday. In the daily newspaper 'Sahafat', an article by a person named Maulvi Abdul Hafeez Islami, who is an insulter of the Sahaba, an insulter of the Rashidun Caliph, and an insulter of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), was published. In that article, that Maulvi displayed his shallow study and his prejudice against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to the world. Maulvi Abdul Hafeez dared to write that in the Holy Quran, in verse 43 of Surah An-Nisa, the prohibition of approaching prayer while intoxicated refers to the Master of the Universe, the Conqueror of all, the Commander of the Faithful, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). God forbid. God forbid a hundred times. May my mouth be filled with dust. To express his point and to apply that command to Imam Ali (a.s.), the Maulvi presented a hadith as evidence that was taken from the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir. Then that Maulvi wrote a sentence there that this narration is also in Abu Dawood and Nasa'i. That person who calls himself a 'Maulana' does not even know that Abu Dawood and Nasa'i are not books. Rather, they were two authors of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni school). The name of the book by Abu Dawood al-Sijistani was 'Sunan', which is included in the Sihah al-Sittah (the six authentic books). And there are two books by the name of Sunan by Nasa'i: 'Sunan al-Kubra', which is not included in the Sihah al-Sittah, and 'Sunan al-Sughra', which is called 'Sunan an-Nasa'i', which is included in the Sihah al-Sittah. The point worth noting is that this Maulvi did not even write whether this hadith was taken from Nasa'i's 'Sunan al-Kubra' or 'Sunan al-Sughra'. Perhaps that Maulvi's study has not reached that far yet. Anyway, calling a lack of knowledge 'study' cannot hide anyone's ignorance. In 'Sunan Abi Dawood', in 'Kitab al-Ashriba', in the chapter 'Babun fi Tahrim al-Khamr', this hadith is number 3671. And in Nasa'i's 'Sunan al-Kubra', volume 10, page 65, this hadith is number 11041. As far as 'Sunan an-Nasa'i' is concerned, it is necessary to know first that Nasa'i himself, in 'Sunan al-Kubra', collected the hadiths he considered authentic into 'Sunan al-Sughra'. And this 'Sunan al-Sughra' is included in the Sihah al-Sittah. The hadith under discussion is in 'Sunan al-Kubra', not in 'Sunan al-Sughra'. That is, Nasa'i himself did not consider this hadith worthy of mention in his authentic book. However, if we refer to both these references and get to the bottom of this, these results emerge. First, both hadiths were declared authentic by the famous Salafi scholar, Sheikh Nasiruddin al-Albani, even though Nasa'i himself did not record it as an authentic hadith in his 'Sunan al-Sughra'. And Albani's hatred and prejudice against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is well-known. Second, in both references, Ata ibn al-Sa'ib and Abu Abdurrahman al-Sulami are the common narrators. All the books in which this hadith has been quoted have been quoted with reference to Ata ibn al-Sa'ib and Abu Abdurrahman al-Sulami. That is, this hadith has not been narrated through any other chain. And in this respect, it is a 'Khabar-e-Wahid' (solitary report). It is one of the fundamental principles of the science of hadith that no belief can be established on the basis of a 'Khabar-e-Wahid'. Dhahabi, in his book 'Siyar A'lam al-Nubala', volume 6, pages 111-112, recorded about Ata ibn al-Sa'ib that it is the statement of Shu'bah that when Ata came to Basra, he said that he had written 30 hadiths from Ubaidah. But the truth is that he had never heard any hadith from Ubaidah. And this is a severe 'Ikhtilat', meaning adulteration. That is, Ata gave a mixed statement. Not only that, it is the statement of Shu'bah that Ata used to narrate hadiths, but he suffered from severe forgetfulness. It is the statement of Yahya that Abu Awana had heard hadiths from Ata, but 'wala yahtajju bi hadithihi'—he never used his narrated hadith as a proof. The Ahl-e-Tasannun scholar Imam Shawkani, in his book 'Nayl al-Awtar', volume 8, page 196, wrote about Ata ibn al-Sa'ib that 'la yu'rafu illa min hadithihi', meaning this hadith has not been narrated by any narrator other than Ata ibn al-Sa'ib. On the same page, it is further written that it is the statement of Abu Bakr al-Bazzar that except for these two narrators, we did not find this hadith through any other continuous chain that has been narrated from Imam Ali (a.s.). After this, it is written that it is the statement of Mundhiri that there is a disagreement in both the chain and the text of this hadith. The disagreement in the chain relates to the fact that Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated it from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib as a 'Mursal' (disconnected) hadith. The disagreement in the text is that Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi write that Imam Ali (a.s.) was leading the prayer, and Nasa'i and Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas wrote that at that time, Abdurrahman ibn Awf led the prayer. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar even wrote that some third person was leading the prayer. Besides this, Ali ibn Ahmad al-Wahidi, in his book 'Asbab al-Nuzul', page 157, hadith 316, has narrated this hadith from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, but there is no mention of Imam Ali (a.s.) in it. And this same hadith has been narrated by Fakhruddin al-Razi in his Tafsir 'Mafatih al-Ghayb' in the interpretation of this verse, and there is no mention of Imam Ali (a.s.) in this either. That is, from the disagreement in the text, it is clear that this is a slander against Imam Ali (a.s.). As far as the second narrator of this hadith, Abu Abdurrahman al-Sulami, is concerned, it is found about him that he held hatred and enmity towards Imam Ali (a.s.). Abu Ja'far Tabari, in his book 'Al-Muntakhab min Dhayl al-Mudhayyal', volume 1, page 147, narrated that a person asked Abu Abdurrahman al-Sulami, 'I ask you by swearing by Allah, since when have you held hatred for Ali? Is it not since the time he distributed the spoils of war in Kufa and did not give any share to you and your family?' He replied, 'Since you have sworn me by Allah, my answer is yes.' Even an ordinary person would accept that someone who considers Imam Ali (a.s.) his enemy, what else can be expected from him? Besides this, the Khawarij always spread many lies against Imam Ali (a.s.) based on their hatred and enmity. This is also one of them. The famous Ahl-e-Tasannun scholar Hakim al-Nishapuri, while analyzing this hadith, wrote that 'annal khawarija tansibu hadhas sukr wa hadhihil qira'at ila amirul mominin Ali ibn Abi Talib, duna ghayrihi, wa qad barra-hullahu minha, fa innahu rawi hadhal hadith'. That is, the Khawarij attributed this state of intoxication and incorrect recitation to the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and no one else, while the Lord of the Worlds kept him pure from such acts, even if he were the narrator of this hadith. That is, according to Hakim al-Nishapuri, even if Imam Ali (a.s.) is the narrator of this hadith, this accusation cannot be attributed to him because he is free and pure from these sins. These were just a few brief arguments through which we hope that for truth-seekers and fair-minded individuals, it has become clear how this Maulvi, without deep research and based on his shallow study, leveled such a serious accusation against his own fourth Caliph and our first Imam, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). But now we want to present another betrayal and trickery of that Maulvi before you, so that it becomes clear to everyone, and especially to that Maulvi, that the spit thrown at the sky falls back on one's own face. Now let us see what Maulvi Abdul Hafeez's betrayal is and who the real drunkard is. If we refer to the same chapter from which the hadith of 'Sunan Abi Dawood' was taken, a shocking fact comes to light, which that Maulvi hid. The hadith presented against Imam Ali (a.s.) was hadith 3671. If we look at just one hadith before this, which is hadith 3670, i.e., hadith 2 of 'Kitab al-Ashriba, Babun fi Tahrim al-Khamr', a different revelation occurs. The hadith is something like this: Abbas ibn Musa al-Khuttali narrated from Ismail ibn Ja'far, from Abi Ishaq, from Amr, and he from Umar ibn Khattab that Umar ibn Khattab said, 'When the command for the prohibition of wine was revealed, I said, O God, explain to us clearly about wine.' Then this verse was revealed: 'They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, in them is great sin.' (2:219). Then Umar was called and this verse was recited. Umar again said, 'O God, explain to us clearly about wine.' After that, this verse was revealed: 'O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying.' (4:43). After this, whenever the caller of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would call for prayer, he would definitely announce that beware, whoever is in a state of intoxication should not come for prayer. Then once again Umar was called and this verse was recited. Umar again said the same thing, 'O God, explain to us clearly about wine.' Finally, this verse was revealed: 'So will you not then desist?' (5:91). Then Umar said, 'Yes, now we will stop.' According to this hadith of 'Sunan Abi Dawood', even after the command of the prohibition of wine came three times, Umar ibn Khattab had not stopped drinking wine. The point worth noting is that the verse which Maulvi Abdul Hafeez made the basis for his insulting article, even after the revelation of that same verse 43 of Surah An-Nisa, Umar ibn Khattab continued to drink wine, and these are Umar ibn Khattab's own words that finally, after the revelation of verse 91 of Surah Al-Ma'idah, we stopped drinking wine. Let us also clarify for you that this was just one hadith. Otherwise, Ahl-e-Tasannun scholars have recorded many other such hadiths in their books in which stories of Umar ibn Khattab's drinking exist before and after the revelation of the verse of the prohibition of wine, even until his final moments. Another interesting thing is that that Maulvi did not even read 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' properly, because if he had, he would have known that like 'Sunan Abi Dawood', in 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' too, the hadith of Umar ibn Khattab regarding the occasion of the revelation of this verse is recorded first. But perhaps that Maulvi did not see this hadith, or the hatred of Imam Ali (a.s.) forced him to hide the truth from the world and, like the Khawarij, use lies and slander against the Commander of the Faithful, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). However, in the end, we want to bring one thing to the attention of Maulvi Abdul Hafeez: that in the future, before writing such an article, broaden your study, otherwise it should not happen that the truths hidden in history books become public in newspapers like this, and Maulvi gentlemen keep being guilty of disrespecting the Sahaba. We want to submit to all of you that this was just a brief answer. If we were to state the occasion of the revelation of verse 43 of Surah An-Nisa only from the books of Ahl-e-Tasannun scholars, many pages would be required. In conclusion, we have the honor of presenting a famous and well-known hadith of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to end our speech, in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Imam Ali (a.s.): 'La yuhibbuka illa mu'min wa la yubghiduka illa munafiq.' O Ali, no one will love you except a believer, and no one will hold hatred and enmity towards you except a hypocrite. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that He hastens the luminous reappearance of His final proof and our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.), so that he may take revenge from all the insulters of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the enemies of the religion and establish complete justice and fairness in this world. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Kya khud ko Shia kehne se koi Shia ho jaata hai?
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes that the title of 'Shia' is a noble and exalted status that requires more than just a verbal claim. The speaker highlights the teachings of Imam Zain-ul-Abideen (a.s.), explaining that true followership is defined by obedience to divine commands and abstaining from prohibitions. Claiming to be a Shia without fulfilling these spiritual and moral requirements is described as a sin that increases one's burden before Allah. Instead of making grand claims, believers are encouraged to express their love and allegiance while striving to embody the qualities of a true follower.
content:
Imam Zain-ul-Abideen (a.s.) pointed out and said, 'I am your follower, I am your follower.' This matter is not just about our claim. O servant of Allah, if you include yourself among our followers, then act upon what we have commanded and abstain from everything we have forbidden. Only then can you be truthful in your claim. But what is the condition? To act upon what has been commanded and to distance yourself from everything that has been forbidden. If you do not abstain from what we have forbidden and instead fall into it, then you are not our follower. If you act upon what we have commanded, then you are truthful. If it is contrary to this, then you cannot be our follower. Do not increase your sins in the sight of Allah. Do not increase your sins by making such a grand claim that 'I am a Shia,' because the Imams (a.s.) state that this is a noble status. This is a noble and exalted status. If you make this claim and you are not worthy of it, if you do not fulfill its requirements, and if you do not qualify for it, then you are only increasing your sins, because making such a claim is a sin. The Imams (a.s.) say: do not increase your sins. This is a noble status; it is not for everyone. Do not say, 'I am your Shia.' Instead, say, 'I am your follower, I love you, I am an enemy to your enemies.' Just say this much. Do not say 'I am a Shia,' because if you say that you are a follower... If you say that you are a follower, then you are in a state of trying to become one, and your end, Insha'Allah, will be good.
Being a Shia is a noble status, not merely a label.
True followership is proven through action, not just verbal claims.
Obedience to divine commands is the primary requirement for a Shia.
Abstaining from forbidden acts is essential for authentic followership.
Making a false claim of being a Shia can increase one's sins.
It is better to express love and allegiance than to claim a title one has not earned.
The path of a follower is a continuous process of striving for improvement.

title: Maah-e-Shabaan ke Aakhri Jume' ko Yeh Dua Na Bhoolein |  Imam Reza (a.s.) Ki Takeed (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture highlights the specific advice given by Imam Ali al-Reza (a.s.) regarding the final Friday of the month of Shabaan. The Imam emphasizes the importance of spiritual preparation, repentance, and settling personal grievances before the arrival of Ramadan. He provides a specific supplication to seek Allah's forgiveness for any shortcomings during the month, noting that Shabaan is a time when many are freed from Hell-fire.
content:
Abu Salt Harawi narrates that I went to Imam Ali Reza (peace be on him) on the last Friday of Shabaan and he (peace be on him) advised: O Aba Salt! Surely most of the Shabaan has passed away and this is its last Friday So whatever of your shortcomings have remained in this month you fulfill it and it is incumbent upon you to perform that action which benefits you Recite excessive supplications repentance and recitation of the Holy Quran Turn towards Allah for your sins so that the month of Allah accepts you in a way that you are sincere for Allah, Mighty and Majestic be He There should not be anything belonging to anyone on your neck except that you should return it There should not be any malice in your heart for a believer except that you get rid of it nor should there be any sin which you have committed except that you uproot it Fear Allah and rely upon Him in all your secret and open affairs Whoever relies upon Allah then He suffices him Certainly, Allah fulfills His affairs Indeed, Allah has placed a measure for everything And, in the remaining part of this month, say as much as possible "O Allah! If you have not forgiven us in whatever has passed from Shabaan then forgive us in whatever remains of it." For surely Allah, Blessed and High be He releases many people in this month from the Hell-fire as a mark of respect for month of Ramadan Uyoon Akhbaar al-Reza (peace be on him), vol. 2, p. 51
