title: EP01 | Khalifa Banaane Ka Ikhtiyaar Kisey Hai? | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 2023💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological and historical arguments surrounding the leadership of the Islamic Ummah, focusing on the event of Ghadir Khumm. It emphasizes that the appointment of an Imam is a divine prerogative, contrasting this with the historical events at Saqifah and the subsequent Shura process. The speaker argues that human-selected leadership lacks the legitimacy of the Prophet's divinely ordained successor, Ali ibn Abi Talib.
content:
PSR presents. [Poetic introduction in praise of the Prophet and Imam Ali]. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 18th Dhu al-Hijjah, 10 Hijri, is that great day in Islamic history when the sacred religion of Islam, which the Lord of the Worlds sent for this world through the Seal of the Prophets, the Master of the Messengers, the Mercy to the Worlds, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), was completed. This is what the third verse of Surah al-Ma'idah in the Holy Quran declares. This was the day when, in the open field of Ghadir Khumm, by the clear command of the Lord of the Worlds, the immediate Caliphate and succession of the Commander of the Faithful, Mawla Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), was announced after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). With this announcement, the Great and Exalted God completed His blessings upon His servants and declared Islam the only religion without believing in which that True Lord will not accept any deed of any human on the Day of Judgment. But those who had opposed divine decisions from the beginning, Iblis and all the enemies of the religion with him, were disappointed to see the responsibility of the rise and protection of Islam in the hands of Imam Ali (a.s.). Since Iblis is the enemy of God, he decided that from that day until the Day of Judgment, he would put all his effort into diverting all people from this true religion that was completed in Ghadir—that is, the Ghadiri religion. Therefore, while on one hand, by the command of God, the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah, Imamate, and Caliphate of Mawla Ali (a.s.), on the other hand, Iblis also started whispering into the hearts of some people. As soon as the eyes of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) closed, some people, under their pre-planned conspiracy, deviated from the path of guidance and established a self-made system of Caliphate against the system of Wilayah created by God. The Islam that was shining in the world like a bright sun as the true religion, these people mixed truth and falsehood and led the Ummah to the path of misguidance instead of the true religion. To prove their self-made system of government and Caliphate correct, they sometimes took the support of 'Ijma' (consensus), sometimes 'Istikhlaf' (nomination), and sometimes 'Shura' (consultation), and in the end, tired and defeated, they even announced: 'Nahnu ma'a man ghalaba' (We are with whoever wins by the power of the sword). Through this video, our two brothers, Mr. Sajjad Mehar Ali and Mr. Gulzar Naqvi, will try to prove, Insha-Allah, why all those methods that the Ummah adopted to choose their Caliph are all false. [Poetic verses]. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Wa sallallahu alaika ya Wali al-Asr, adriknā wa la tuhliknā. Respected and honorable listeners, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. First of all, we offer congratulations on Eid-e-Ghadir and Eid-e-Mubahila to all of you and begin today's episode. We will divide our discussion today into five parts: that appointing an Imam and Caliph is Allah's responsibility. Second, that Prophethood and Imamate are not the responsibility of the people. Third, what happened after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? Fourth, when, why, and how was the foundation of Shura laid? And fifth, who is the true successor of the Prophet? So let us begin our discussion with the first part: that appointing an Imam and Caliph is Allah's responsibility. And as is the case when any argument is presented before this Muslim Ummah, their demand is for the Holy Quran, that you present arguments from the Holy Quran. So we also present a few verses of the Quran for our topic, which will make it clear that appointing an Imam and Caliph is Allah's responsibility. If we study the Holy Quran, we find some verses on this topic, such as Surah as-Sajdah, verse number 24, in which the Lord of Majesty says: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, {Wa ja'alna minhum a'immatan yahduna bi amrina} (And We made from among them leaders who guide by Our command). The second verse, in which Allah Subhanah wa Ta'ala announces the Imamate of Ibrahim (a.s.), the Lord of Majesty says: {Wa idh ibtala Ibrahima rabbuhu bi kalimatin fa atammahunna, qala inni ja'iluka lin-nasi imama, qala wa min dhurriyyati, qala la yanalu 'ahdi-z-zalimin} (And remember when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words and he fulfilled them, He said: 'I am going to make you an Imam for the people.' He said: 'And of my offspring?' He said: 'My covenant does not include the wrongdoers'). Another verse of the Holy Quran, which is verse number 30 of Surah al-Baqarah, in which the Lord of Majesty says: {Wa idh qala rabbuka lil-mala'ikati inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifa} (And remember when your Lord said to the angels: 'I am going to place a successor on the earth'). And we present the last verse related to our topic: {Ya Dawudu inna ja'alnaka khalifatan fil-ardi fahkum baynan-nasi bil-haqq} (O Dawud, indeed We have made you a successor on the earth, so judge between the people with truth). If we ponder over these verses, the word 'Ja'ala' has been used in all four verses we recited, which means to make, to appoint, or to select. So this proves, it becomes completely clear, that appointing a Caliph or Imam on earth is only and only in the authority of Allah, not the people. As Gulzar Bhai pointed out, the authority to appoint a Caliph or Imam belongs only to Allah, not to the people. Continuing this topic, we will discuss today whether appointing a Prophet or Imam is the responsibility of the people or not? On this topic, the Holy Quran says: {Wa rabbuka yakhluqu ma yasha'u wa yakhtar, ma kana lahumul khiyarah, subhanallahi wa ta'ala 'amma yushrikun} (And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him). They do not have the authority for this, and Allah is pure and All-Powerful, far above their shirk (polytheism). If we reflect on the concluding part of this verse, it becomes clear that people have no role in selecting Allah's Hujjah (proof/representative). In fact, doing so is shirk. Furthermore, if we look at Surah Al-An'am, verse 124, Allah declares: 'Allahu a'lamu haythu yaj'alu risalatahu' (Allah knows best where to place His message). Thus, after all these arguments, it is evident that selecting a Hujjah on this earth is Allah's prerogative. People have no say in this, and doing so is counted as shirk. Moreover, if we consider that from Prophet Adam (a.s.) to Prophet Isa (a.s.), if anyone could prove—even through a false or fabricated hadith—that the Ummah appointed a successor to any Prophet (we are not even talking about authentic hadith, but fabricated ones), it still cannot be proven. So, if it is established that the Ummah has no authority in this, then how did this concept arise after the martyrdom of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.)? As Sajjad Sahab explained, the selection of the Messenger and the Imamate—that is, both Prophethood and Imamate—is solely in the hands of Allah. And not only is it in Allah's hands, but if anyone takes this task upon themselves and starts doing it, they become guilty of shirk. Just as selecting a Hujjah on this earth is Allah's work, people have no role in it, and doing so would be counted as shirk, as the verse presented to you states. Yet, despite all these Quranic verses, what action did this Ummah take after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? They acted completely against the Quran. As Sajjad Sahab was saying, if there is any instance where a Prophet's successor was chosen by the people, it should be shown, but it is not found. However, the Muslim Ummah, after the martyrdom of the Messenger, performed such a feat that, if viewed through the spirit of the Quranic verses, they became guilty of shirk. For instance, after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), when Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was occupied with his ghusl and kafan, and because of this tragedy, all the Banu Hashim had distanced themselves from the people, some Muhajireen and Ansar took advantage of this situation to gather at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah to try and appoint their own caliph. That is, they abandoned the funeral of the Prophet of Allah to gather at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah to select a caliph among themselves. And Gulzar Bhai, those who gathered at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah, if they were on the truth, they should have gathered at the Prophet's Mosque. Indeed, if they were on the truth, they would have announced this and made their decision at the Prophet's Mosque. But this itself—all the arguments, the Quranic verses, the hadiths, and historical events aside—is a very strong proof that if they were on the truth, they would have been at the Prophet's Mosque. They gathered to appoint a caliph for a religion after which no other religion is to come, a Messenger after whom no other Messenger is to come, and a Book after which no other Book is to come, and this religion is to remain until the Day of Judgment. Indeed. So, they abandoned the funeral of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to gather at a place like Saqifah to choose a ruler for themselves, and upon gathering, the Ansar wanted to choose Sa'd ibn Ubadah as their caliph. At that time, one of the Ansar gave a speech there. It is narrated in Sahih Bukhari that Umar ibn al-Khattab said that as soon as he wanted to give the speech he had prepared beforehand after that speech... notice that he himself admits he wanted to give a speech he had already prepared, meaning the planning for this was already underway. Meaning the entire planning of Saqifah was already in place—the speech was ready, and he wanted to deliver it there. So he said that as soon as he wanted to deliver the speech he had prepared, Abu Bakr stopped him and gave the speech himself. At the end of which, Abu Bakr took my hand and the hand of Abu Ubaidah al-Jarrah and said to the people, 'If you want to make a caliph, if you want to make a successor to the Messenger of Allah, then choose one of these two.' Then one of the Ansar said, 'One caliph will be ours, and one will be yours.' As soon as he said this, an uproar broke out. People started arguing with each other, and noise and commotion began there. So, as soon as the voices were raised, Umar ibn al-Khattab says that I told Abu Bakr, 'Extend your hand.' He extended his hand, and I pledged allegiance (bay'ah) to him, and then the Muhajireen and Ansar present there also pledged their allegiance. So, the point to consider is that there was no Shura (consultation) in Saqifah—meaning no committee was formed to consult and choose a caliph, nor is there any sign of consultation in this narration present in Sahih Bukhari. Thus, after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), contrary to the Divine Sunnah, by claiming their own action to be Allah's action, some individuals selected a caliph for themselves at Saqifah and led the Ummah astray. And Gulzar Bhai, as far as consultation is concerned, where were the people who should have been consulted? Indeed. Where was Mawla-e-Kainat Ali (a.s.)? Where was Salman-e-Mohammadi? Where was Ammar-e-Yasir? Where was Miqdad ibn Aswad? Where were they all? Indeed, Sajjad Sahab, apart from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), who is worthy of being consulted in this religion of Islam? Truly, no one else, and yet they talk about consultation. Now, hear an even more interesting incident: the first caliph was chosen this way. Now let us see how the second caliph was selected. In the Sunni book 'Al-Kharaj', this incident is found: when the final moments of Abu Bakr arrived, he chose Umar for the caliphate, and when he chose Umar, people objected, saying: 'Atukhallifu 'alayna fazzan ghaliza' (Will you appoint as our caliph a man who is extremely rude and harsh?). And then they further said: 'Law qad malakana kana afazza wa aghlaz' (If he becomes our ruler, he will become even more rude and harsh). In this situation, the people asked Abu Bakr, 'In this state, when you meet your Lord, what answer will you give? You have made this decision, what will be your answer?' Responding to this objection, Abu Bakr said, 'Are you trying to frighten me with my Lord? I will tell Him: O Lord, I have appointed the best of Your creation as their guide.' So, look, people are objecting, but if he thinks he is the best, then he has chosen him, so there is no need for anyone's consultation, nor is there any need for a Saqifah. So the second caliph was selected in this manner. And if we reflect further on this incident, an important point emerges: the foundation of the second caliph's caliphate is neither any word of the Messenger of Allah, nor any Shura, nor any selection by the Ummah—that the Ummah collectively chose him. Nothing of the sort is found here. Rather, the first caliph made his own preference the justification for the caliphate. If we shed more light on the selection of the second caliph, another famous Sunni author, Zamakhshari, describes this incident in his book 'Al-Fa'iq fi Gharib al-Hadith' as follows: on the day Abu Bakr was ill and eventually passed away due to that illness, he said to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, 'I am suffering from severe pain due to this illness, but the trouble the Muhajireen have caused me is far greater than this.' 'I have entrusted your affairs to a man who, in my opinion, is the best. Yet you all seem unhappy with this.' If you reflect on this sentence of the first caliph in history, it becomes clear that the people are not happy. He is just pushing his own preference and making it the justification for selecting a caliph. So Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf replied, 'O successor of the Messenger, whatever you have decided will be.' Although this decision was made by you on your own. So, respected audience, from this incident it becomes clear that this action of the first caliph was against the Divine system, yet Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf agreed with it. Furthermore, it is found in other Sunni books that when Abu Bakr's final moments were near, he had a private conversation with Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Uthman, and had his will written by Uthman. While dictating the will, he fainted. During this time, Uthman wrote in Abu Bakr's will that 'I (Abu Bakr) have appointed Umar ibn al-Khattab as your successor.' So, respected audience, after all these arguments, it is evident that Abu Bakr did not consult anyone in this matter except Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Uthman, and no one other than these two individuals was satisfied with this decision. It is clear that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Uthman played a key role in the selection of the successor after Abu Bakr. Look, Gulzar Bhai, yesterday when the Messenger of Allah, in a gathering of 125,000, openly and emphatically selected and appointed his successor, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and the people pledged allegiance to him for three consecutive days, after the martyrdom of the Messenger, people were not ready to accept that caliph. And today, when the first caliph selects his successor in a state of unconsciousness—someone who is harsh—people had to accept it. And in what condition! Look at that. He fainted while writing his will. He fainted! These are the same people who, God forbid, accuse the Messenger of Allah, whereas the Messenger of Allah was asking for pen and paper in his full senses, saying, 'I will write something for you so that you do not go astray after me.' They accused the Messenger of Allah there, and here, a will is being written in a state of unconsciousness, and it is being accepted as a caliph. Now we will see when, why, and how the foundation of Shura was laid. To clarify this, we will take the help of Sahih Bukhari, Hadith number 6830. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that when he was with Umar during his last Hajj, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to him, 'I wish you had seen a man who came to Umar today and said, 'What is your opinion about a man who says that if Umar dies, I will pledge allegiance to so-and-so?' By Allah, Umar said, 'The pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr was sudden (faltah).' Upon this, Umar said angrily, 'I will address the people this evening and warn them against those who want to deprive others of their rights.' At this, Abdur Rahman ibn Awf said to Umar, 'Do not do that. During the Hajj season, people of low intellect and naive nature gather. I fear that you will say something and they will misinterpret your words. Therefore, wait until you reach Medina, for it is the place of Hijrah and Sunnah, where you can connect with the people of knowledge and express your thoughts to them.' Umar said, 'By Allah, as soon as I reach Medina, the first thing I will do is deliver a sermon on this topic.' Ibn Abbas said, 'We reached Medina at the end of Dhul-Hijjah, and it was a Friday. As soon as the sun set, we arrived at the mosque. When the Muezzin finished the Adhan and fell silent, Umar began the sermon. After praising Allah and stating the rules of Hajj, he said, "Today I have come to know that one of you has said, 'By Allah, if Umar dies, we will pledge allegiance to so-and-so.' Do not let any of you be deceived into thinking that the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr was sudden—meaning it was a mistake—and then everything became fine. Rather, it was exactly that—it was a mistake—but Allah protected you from its evil. Therefore, whoever pledges allegiance to someone without consulting the Muslims, and whoever does so, the result will be that both the one who pledges and the one who accepts the pledge will lose their lives." So, Sajjad Sahab, the point to note here is that two things are found here. Firstly, he himself confessed that in the selection of the first Caliphate, there was neither any consultation nor any Shura. That is correct. And secondly, he is seen condemning his own action, saying that it was a mistake and that what he himself did should not happen. That is, the very first pledge of allegiance to the first Caliph was done by him, and he himself said that Allah protected from its evil. Allah protected from that evil—meaning he committed that evil, and he confessed it himself. If we reflect on this incident, the question is, who is that 'so-and-so' person to whom people wanted to pledge allegiance? Ibn Hajar, in his commentary on Bukhari, has tried to identify this person, and the word 'so-and-so' has been used. He says, 'I found this narration with a strong chain in Baladhuri's book, *Ansab*, that here 'so-and-so' refers to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).' Now let us see how the Shura was established and how it was organized. At the very beginning of his Caliphate, Umar considered Uthman his successor and wanted the Caliphate to remain in Uthman's hands after him. To bring this desire to fruition, he established the Shura. There was only one way to achieve this goal: to form a committee in which he himself appointed six individuals, and it was mandatory for all of them to choose a Caliph within three days, otherwise, they would all be killed. So, Sajjad Sahab, it is truly surprising that it is as if a game is being played with the religion. That is, he selected the committee himself and appointed the people chosen to become Caliph himself. After that, he ordered them to be killed if a Caliph was not chosen within three days. Just think, whom will he kill? The one who is going to be the Caliph, the one who is going to be the successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), will be killed. These are the companions of the Prophet. That is, he is talking about killing the companions here. Now, whether to be surprised at this or what to do, it is incomprehensible. That is, if a Caliph was not chosen within three days, those who were 'obligatory to be obeyed' became 'obligatory to be killed'. Indeed. And Gulzar Bhai, there is one thing here: if one of these six separates and five become one, then that one will be killed. If two and four are divided, then the two will be killed. And if it is three and three—what we call a tie—if it is like that, the casting vote will go to the party where Abdur Rahman ibn Awf's vote lies. Now, Gulzar Sahab, there is a question: why was Abdur Rahman ibn Awf given the right to decide? A question comes to mind. There were six people: Talha, Zubayr, Abdur Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Uthman, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Six people. Why was Abdur Rahman ibn Awf given the right to decide? One reason is that Abdur Rahman ibn Awf was Uthman's brother-in-law. Abdur Rahman ibn Awf knew what the Master of the Universe, Ali (a.s.), thought about Abu Bakr and Umar. Regardless, Abdur Rahman ibn Awf placed a condition on Ali (a.s.): 'Will you act according to the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of the Prophet, and the Sunnah of the two Sheikhs?' If you give me this promise, I will cast my vote in your favor. The Master of the Universe accepted two conditions but refused the third. What happened? The same thing was presented by Abdur Rahman ibn Awf to Uthman, who immediately accepted it. So, Sajjad Sahab, the point to note here is that the way we saw how the Caliphs were chosen—the first, the second, or all three—if you look at their methods, all three are different, and no method matches the other. Even the way the first Caliph was chosen, the second Caliph is opposing it, objecting to it, and condemning it, saying that in the future, no Caliph should be appointed or designated in this manner. So, if we look at this, it is completely against the Quran to choose a Caliph in this way; secondly, it is against the Sunnah of the Prophet; and thirdly, this itself... that they themselves are not in agreement with each other regarding the method used. There is disagreement among them as well. Now, the point to see here is: what should the true Caliph, the true Imam, be like? How should he be chosen? And our topic was also this: that the Caliph of the Prophet, or the Imam, will be chosen only and only by Allah, and if any Ummah chooses him otherwise, it is invalid. And we have presented Quranic verses for this, and for these methods adopted to choose a Caliph, no Quranic verse or Sunnah of the Prophet is found. Now, let us come to the most important point of our discussion: then who is the true successor of the Prophet? Just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was appointed to the position of Prophethood in that realm, in the same realm, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was made the successor of the Prophet. What is that realm? The Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself said regarding this. He says: 'Kuntu ana wa Aliyyun nuran bayna yadayillahi ta'ala qabla an yakhluqa Adama bi-arba'ata 'ashara alfa 'am, falamma khalaqallahu Adama qassama dhalikan-nura juz'ayn, fajuz'un ana wa juz'un Aliyyun.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that I and Ali were in the form of light in the presence of Allah 14,000 years before the creation of Adam. When Allah created Adam, He divided that light into two parts. One part for me and one part for Ali. Dear brothers, this Hadith has been narrated in numerous books of the Ahl al-Sunnah. Such as *Manaqib-e-Ali (a.s.)*, *Riyad al-Nadirah*, *Tadhkirat al-Khawas*, *Kifayat al-Talib*, *Nazm al-Durar al-Simtayn*, *Fara'id al-Simtayn*, *Manaqib-e-Khwarizmi*, *Sharh-e-Nahj al-Balagha*, and *Tarikh-e-Madinat-e-Dimashq*. There is another version of this Hadith in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Faja'ala fihin-nubuwwata wa fi Aliyyinil-khilafata.' He gave me Prophethood and gave Ali the Caliphate. From these narrations, it is known that the Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was established in the Realm of Dharr (the world of souls) before this world. Despite presenting these clear proofs, if someone now denies the Imamate and Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and supports the theory of Shura, then surely there is a veil over their intellect, and they oppose the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet. And these are the people for whom the Almighty God says in the Holy Quran: 'Man kana fi hadhihi a'ma fahuwa fil-akhirati a'ma.' That is, whoever is blind in this world will also be blind in the Hereafter. So, O God! For the sake of the right of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Imam al-Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), and count us among his sincere helpers and supporters. Amin, O Lord of the worlds. With this, this episode of the Hareer Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz concludes here. We hope that you all have provided the answers to all the questions by now. If not, there is still time. A countdown timer has started for you. The quiz link will remain live as long as this timer runs. As soon as the countdown timer ends, the quiz link will also be closed. Therefore, make sure to submit your answers before the quiz link closes. Let us all turn our attention towards the Ziyarat-e-Aminullah. Immediately after this, we will announce the winners of today's episode through our computerized lucky draw system. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. Come, ladies and gentlemen, let us now see who our eight lucky winners of today's episode are, who are being selected through our computerized lucky draw system. Among whom, first are our five third-prize winners who will receive 1000 Indian Rupees; their names are here on your screen: Zainab Sayyeda from Alipur, Hasan Mehdi from Bhavnagari, Nerul Navi from Mumbai, and Siddiqa Mohsin Ghabrani from Bombay. Elia Fatima Zamani from Bhuj, and Sayyid Arbaz Fatima from Bengaluru. Many congratulations to you all. Come, now we will select our second-prize winners, who are two individuals and will receive a prize of 2500 Indian Rupees, through our computerized lucky draw system. Their names are here on your screen: Shagufta Devji from Mumbai, and Sayyid Shams Hasan Taqvi from Lucknow. Many congratulations to you all. Come, now let us announce the first-prize winner of today's episode. Who is that lucky person who will receive 5000 Indian Rupees? Their name is here on your screen: Kulsum Zahra from Bangalore. Many congratulations to you. So, viewers, we now bid you farewell. Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Imam Reza (a.s.) Ne Apne Zaaireen Se Kya Vaada Kiya? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of performing Ziyarat (visitation) to the shrine of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) in Mashhad. It highlights the specific promise made by the Imam to assist his visitors at three critical moments on the Day of Judgment: the distribution of deeds, the crossing of the Sirat bridge, and the weighing of deeds. The speaker emphasizes that this intercession is contingent upon the visitor's sincere recognition (ma'rifat) of the Imam's status.
content:
A believer is always striving to attain proximity to Allah through the intercession (tawassul) of each of the Ma'sumeen (a.s.), and under their shadow, to find the means for the acceptance of their prayers and needs. Because the easiest way to attain the pleasure of Allah and His proximity is the visitation (ziyarat) of the holy shrines of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Among such visitations is the magnificent shrine of the eighth Imam, the ornament of the pious, the third Ali among the twelve Imams, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.). These are his blessed footsteps and his holy shrine, due to which the land of Mashhad al-Muqaddas... ...is called holy. The visitation (ziyarat) of Imam Rida (a.s.) is not just any visitation, but it is a promise made by Imam Rida (a.s.) himself to every visitor (za'ir) of his. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Whoever comes to visit me on this land which is far from my family's home, I myself will come to him at three places on the Day of Judgment, until I rescue him from the terrors of those places. First, when the book of deeds is being given in their right or left hands; second, at the Bridge of Sirat (Pul-e-Sirat); and third, when the deeds are being weighed on the Scale (Mizan).' These are the three places... ...where this visitation will benefit a person when they need it the most. But this will only be granted to the person who believes in the Imamate of Imam Rida (a.s.) and visits him recognizing him as the rightful Imam. The explanation of this has been narrated by Imam Rida (a.s.) himself in this Hadith. He says: 'Whoever among my followers visits me with the recognition of my true status (ma'rifat), I will intercede for him on the Day of Judgment.' The TSR team present in Mashhad al-Muqaddas presents salutations (salam) to Mawla Imam Rida (a.s.) on behalf of all of you, and congratulates you all on the auspicious birth anniversary of Imam Rida (a.s.). We pray to Allah Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of the heir of the Imams (a.s.) and the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), so that in his company, just like the shrine of Imam Rida (a.s.), we may also beautifully reconstruct Jannat al-Baqi. And may He grant the visitors of Imam Rida (a.s.) the opportunity to perform his visitation with the true recognition of his rights. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen. [Music] [Applause]

content:
The arms that were severed, holding the water-skin in the teeth... In the visitation (ziyarat) of Bab al-Hawa'ij Hazrat Abul Fazl al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), we find: 'May Allah's curse be upon the one who killed you, and may Allah's curse be upon the one who was ignorant of your right, and may Allah's curse be upon the one who violated your sanctity, and may Allah's curse be upon the one who stood between you and the River Euphrates (Furat).'

title: Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course  (With LIVE Demo) - Session # 4
excerpt: This session of the Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course focuses on the critical importance of Tajweed and precise articulation for the validity of daily prayers. The instructor provides a detailed breakdown of heavy letters, specific phonetic challenges like the distinction between 'Ayn' and 'Alif', and the correct placement of the tongue for sounds like 'Zaal'. Emphasizing that age is no barrier to learning, the lecture combines technical instruction with practical feedback to help students refine their recitation skills.
content:
Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Respected viewers, we welcome you with Salawat to this fourth episode of our program. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Ali Muhammad. Friends, in the previous two or three episodes, we saw how the beginning and middle verses of Surah al-Hamd should be recited. This great task has been carried out in the last three episodes by the world-renowned scholar, Hujjatul Islam wal Muslimeen Maulana Shandar Abbas Khan Sahib. We are grateful to him for helping our viewers correct their recitation. May Allah protect him from all evils so that he may continue to perform such works in an even better way. Friends, the Quran is the word of the Lord of the worlds, the constitution of Islam, the treasure of gnosis, and a guide for those who wander, leading them from darkness to light and towards God. The Quran itself declares: 'A Book which We have revealed to you, so that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into the light...' ...into the light. So, let us once again turn to Maulana Shandar Abbas Khan Sahib to learn the correct recitation of this most important Surah of the Quran, so that he may shed more light on it and increase our knowledge. Let us go to his presence. Maulana Sahib, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Is there anyone who would turn to it, adopt it, take advice from it, and become familiar with it? It is the grace and mercy of Allah Almighty that He gave us the opportunity, and Alhamdulillah, the effort we started to learn and teach the blessed Surah al-Hamd has now entered its fourth stage. So far, Alhamdulillah, we have learned and understood the correct pronunciation, Arabic style of recitation, and the articulation points (makharij) of the first five verses of Surah al-Hamd. We also learned that if we pronounce the words of these verses with proper mastery, what the meanings will be, and if we make a mistake (Allah forbid) and recite them incorrectly, how the meaning changes. We learned that 'Alhamdu lillah' means 'All praise belongs to Allah', and if we recite it incorrectly as 'Al-hamdu lillah' (with a different 'h'), it could mean something else entirely (like destruction or death). And 'Rabbil 'Alamin' means the Lord of the entire universe... ...meaning the Lord of the entire universe, and 'Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim' means the Beneficent, the Merciful. 'Iyyaka na'budu' means 'You alone we worship', and 'Iyyaka nasta'in' means 'from You alone we seek help'. And in verse five, we learned that we must recite it as 'Ihdinas-Siratal-Mustaqim', pronouncing the letter 'Sad' thickly. Now, I will quickly recite these verses so we can move to the next one, as our time is limited... Should I leave it... when we recite 'Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'een' and 'Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqeem'... after that, how we recite in prayers, we will discuss that later. Let's go directly to verse number 6. Verse number 6: when 'Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqeem' is used, we have already discussed its details. So in verse number 6 as well, in the word 'Sirat', I had read out the names of the letters and mentioned to you that out of the 28 letters in the Arabic language, 8 to 10 letters are pronounced heavily (mufakhkham), especially when there is a fatha (zabar) or damma (pesh). And among these letters, these four: Saad, Daad, Ta, Za (ص, ض, ط, ظ)... yes, they are called 'itbaq' letters. Saad, Daad, Ta, Za... Saad, Daad, Ta, Za... and these four must be pronounced heavily. Especially when there is a fatha (zabar), it is pronounced very heavily; when there is a damma (pesh), slightly less; and when there is a kasra (zeer), even less. These are the three levels of heavy pronunciation. Now, in 'Siratalladhina' and 'ghayril maghdoobi'... as we pointed out to you on the first or second day as well, a person who does not recite [the Quran] is like wood or stone. And if we have to pray, we must recite Surah al-Hamd under all circumstances. No one can say, 'I have been reciting it for so many days, today I will recite Surah al-Hamd in the first rak'ah and some other Surah in the second rak'ah.' We do not have the right to do this. So, the first Surah at the beginning of the prayer is the blessed Surah al-Hamd. After that, you will recite another Surah. This is compulsory for us in the first two rak'ahs, whether the prayer is of four rak'ahs, three rak'ahs, or two rak'ahs; we must recite it in any case. ...we must recite it in any case. So why not? If we have corrected Surah al-Hamd, then consider that we have crossed a major milestone in reciting it correctly and performing the prayer correctly. And I have submitted this to you: we can recite it correctly only when we observe the rules of Tajweed. Regarding the observance of the rules of Tajweed, one way is that we learn the rules of Tajweed by first taking the rules, understanding their definitions, seeing which letters they apply to, and practicing them on those letters. That is one way. The second way is that we directly learn to pronounce the word correctly. We pronounce the word correctly, but we might not know which rule applies there or what its details are. So, if we do not want to go into the details... And what are its details? If we do not want to know the details, or if we do not have the time or the opportunity, then let it be; at least let us directly learn to pronounce the word correctly, and our responsibility will still be fulfilled. I would just like to point to a very brief incident to show what the importance of the rules of Tajweed is, what kind of language Arabic is, and why people learn the rules of Tajweed. Why did our scholars emphasize it? So that we recite with the rules of Tajweed. Why were we asked to learn it? If we don't value it or say we don't have time, so we aren't doing it, at least we should read with Tajweed. But in this world, there are people who are not even Muslims... Yes, so I was submitting that right around us in this world, in our neighborhood, in our city, there are some people who are not Muslims, but they give importance to Tajweed in order to present their work well, to perform their work in an excellent manner. Now, this is a very small matter, but I am quickly sharing this example for my brothers so that they give some importance to this work. You saw that some elders around 60-65 years old presented recitation here yesterday and the day before, and they presented those verses with correct Arabic pronunciation, Masha'Allah. Seeing that, some people developed an interest. And just yesterday, a gentleman from Saudi Arabia, who is about 55 years old, said, 'Give me half an hour, I will come after finishing my work here in India.' He said, 'I developed an interest seeing them, and I will definitely learn.' I welcomed him and said, 'Insha'Allah, I will teach you.' This is from around 2006 or 2007, when there was a studio in Andheri, Mumbai. Actually, we were recording some things for children there... let me repeat, it is a small matter. We arrived there at the scheduled time, and after that, we spoke to the studio people. You can search for 'Mumbai Brothers' in Andheri on the internet, it is still there. Back then, the recording rate was 500 rupees per hour, I don't know what it is now. ...back then, the recording rate was 500 rupees per hour, I don't know what it is now. So we arrived, and he said, 'Give us some time, we are going to record.' I had two or three other people with me to record the 30th Juz. The team working inside had delayed a bit. They came out of the studio, and they had a lot of equipment and things with them; they were people from Bollywood. One of them came forward and asked, 'Who are you, sir, and what will you record?' The person with us said, 'He will recite something in Arabic.' They asked the studio owner, 'Are these people next? Will they record after us?' He replied that we would record something. So the person thought that perhaps I was going to sing a song in Arabic. He kept talking to us and asked, 'Will you please sing an Arabic song for me? I like Arabic songs very much.' I said, 'Brother, I do not sing. I will recite something else in Arabic.' He asked, 'What?' I said, 'I will recite the Holy Quran.' The person said, 'Oh, that's very good. So, will you recite it with Tajweed?' Looking at his appearance and demeanor, I felt he was not a Muslim. So I said... Since it was time for our recording, I asked him, 'Do you know what Tajweed is?' He said, 'Yes, I know.' I said, 'Excuse me, what is your name?' He told me his name and that he was from Chennai. I asked, 'How do you know about Tajweed?' What he said is what I want to share with you, to show its importance. If we value our work, we must find time and work hard. That person said many things, mentioning that he was invited by certain people, and named several films he worked on—I am mentioning this just to make things clear. He told me about himself. Then he said, 'It would be great if you could recite a little.' So I recited, and he was very pleased. I asked him, 'How did you develop this interest in Tajweed and correct pronunciation?' He told me that a very famous singer had come from Oman, and he was selected from Bollywood to collaborate with him. title: Shahadat e Janab e Mohsin Ibn Ali (a.s) | Majlis-e-Aza | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the tragic martyrdom of Janab-e-Mohsin (a.s.) as a pivotal moment in Islamic history and a focal point for grief and reflection. The discourse emphasizes the importance of Wilayah, urging believers to align their actions with the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Dr. Rizvi addresses the historical oppression faced by the Prophet's household, highlighting the necessity of spiritual accountability and the divine status of the Prophet's family. Ultimately, the session serves as a reminder to uphold the truth and remain steadfast in faith despite historical trials.

title: Hadees-e-Saqalain & #ImamMahdi (a.t.f.s.) | Nabi (s.a.w.a.) Ki Wasiyyat
excerpt: This lecture explores the significance of Hadith al-Saqalain, where the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) commanded Muslims to hold fast to the Quran and his Ahlulbayt to avoid misguidance. The speaker emphasizes that this divine testament remains binding until the Day of Judgment. The lecture concludes by identifying adherence to the twelfth Imam, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), as the essential requirement for fulfilling the Prophet's final will.
content:
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my Ahlulbayt. As long as you hold fast to both, you will never go astray after me. And these two things, the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, will never separate from each other until they reach me at the Pond of Kawthar.' This means the things the Prophet was leaving behind as a testament were the Quran and his Ahlulbayt. If a person holds onto the hem of both, they will be saved from misguidance until the Day of Judgment—the very thing the Prophet wanted to save them from. But those who intended to prevent the Messenger from writing were not allowed to stop it. However, it was Allah's will that the Prophet's testament be recorded, and so it was. Therefore, Alhamdulillah, there is only one group today—from the martyrdom of the Prophet until today, and Insha'Allah until the Day of Judgment—that truly acts upon this testament by holding onto both the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So, if anyone today wants to act upon the true testament of the Messenger, they must follow the last Imam among the twelve Imams whom the Messenger named. Among them, the last Imam whose name he mentioned in his testament, who is Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), one must hold onto his hem. As long as a person does not hold onto his hem, they cannot be saved from misguidance. As long as they do not hold onto his hem, they will not attain the Prophet's testament, nor will they be attached to the Prophet's testament. Being attached to the Prophet's testament means being attached to Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). And that is why, by invoking the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), we pray to the Lord of the Worlds: 'O Lord, hasten the reappearance of our Imam (a.s.).'

title: Ep#10 | Ghaayab Imam Deen Kaise Chalaa Sakta Hai?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common skepticism regarding how the Twelfth Imam can lead and protect the religion while in occultation. The speaker argues that the Imam's physical presence is not required for his authority, as his existence alone sustains the world and provides spiritual guidance. By drawing parallels to the hidden influence of Satan and the metaphor of the sun behind clouds, the lecture emphasizes that the Imam remains the essential Hujjah (proof) of Allah for all creation.
content:
The voice of... tell me, oh Satan, I am in this... Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim. Sallallahu Alaika Ya... peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Before we begin our current topic, we offer congratulations to all our viewers on all the joys that have descended upon the Prophet and his family (Ahlulbayt) during this blessed month, along with a Salawat. May Allah bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Dear viewers, our topic today is a very important one, and many people are wandering in doubt, asking how someone can lead the religion while being in occultation. Certainly, the opponents of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) appear to be drowning in a sea of astonishment, wondering how someone can protect the religion while being hidden, or how they can manage the affairs of Islam while in occultation. Here, we want to draw the attention of the entire Muslim Ummah to the fact that the Shia Imami perspective on this matter is... The Shia Imami perspective on this matter is that for us, the appearance of the Imam is not obligatory, but the existence of the Imam is necessary. For the stability of the world and the religion, it is not the appearance that is the condition, but the presence. And in this regard, our traditions also echo this, stating: 'Innal-ardha la takhlu min hujjatim-ma dhahirin aw mustatir' (Indeed, the earth is never devoid of a Hujjah, whether manifest or hidden). No human should have any doubt in this regard as to how someone can lead the religion while being hidden. Viewers, this is a mystery, a deep secret that a human cannot understand with their limited intellects. These are personalities who, while in human form, are among the secrets of Allah. What is the capacity of a human to understand their essence and their actions through their limited faculties? Unless He wills it, His secrets cannot be revealed. How beautifully the poet said: How beautifully the poet said: 'How can we help you, O Mawla, when we cannot even create another like you?' Dear viewers, let us clarify this through arguments, as it is a very important topic: how can the hidden Imam understand the religion, or how can the hidden Imam help people or guide them? We want to present the first argument before you. The reality of people and the nature of people is such that even the enemies of Tawheed (monotheism) acknowledge this. The enemy of Tawheed, Iblis, acknowledges that he can misguide people while being hidden. But on the other hand, the lovers of Tawheed, who are the followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), deny that the Imam can guide people while being hidden. This is a reality, a cycle that is not only for humans but for every creature. From the throne to the earth, from Jinn to human, from the atom to the heavens, from man to animal, from the ant to the elephant, from the hidden to the manifest—whoever Allah is the Creator of, the Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the Hujjah for them. So, viewers, it becomes clear from this argument that if Satan can misguide people while being hidden, then why can the Imam of the Time (a.s.) not guide people while being hidden? If Satan can misguide people while being hidden, then why can the Imam of the Time (a.s.) not guide people while being hidden? Let us present the second argument before you, which occurred in a debate in the mosque of... (inaudible). We want to present a summary of it to you. The senses are young, they are old, they are manifest, but when they fall into doubt, they turn towards something hidden. What is that hidden thing? When the senses are in doubt, they turn towards the hidden. If the hidden can guide the senses, then why can the Imam not guide people while being hidden? Dear viewers, let us try to shed some more light on this topic through a few traditions. The first tradition that I have to present before you is from 'Umdah', whose author is Muhammad Hasanain Ashraf (rah). He narrates in his book from the companions of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) that Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, never leaves the earth without a Hujjah... Never leaves the earth without a Hujjah. Do not think that the things people add to the religion, the Imam reduces them, and the things they reduce, the Imam restores. If this were not the case, the entire religion would have become difficult for the people. Dear viewers, from this tradition, it becomes clear that the Imam is the protector of the religion. Similarly, if we draw your attention to other traditions, it will become clear what the benefit of the Imam's existence is. It is mentioned in a hadith: 'Lawla al-Imamu la-sakhat al-ardhu bi-ahliha' (If the Imam were not on earth, the earth would have collapsed with its inhabitants, just as the waves of the sea collide). From this, it is clear that if this were not the case, the earth would be destroyed with its inhabitants. Similarly, if you look at the sentences of Ziyarat, they are very important sentences found in Ziyarat, which say: 'Bikum yumsiku al-sama'a an taqa'a 'ala al-ardhi' (By your existence, the sky is held from falling upon the earth). Your existence is the reason the world remains, and it is by your blessing that the earth and sky are established. By your blessing, the earth and sky are established. If you were not there, if your essence were not there, why would this sun rise? Why would this moon shine? Why would these canopies of the sky exist? Why would these birds chirp? Why would these rivers flow? Why would these oceans have tides? Why would this entire world not be destroyed? And this is what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says in a hadith: 'If the Hujjah were removed from this earth, the earth would sink with its inhabitants.' Let us try to understand our topic with one final point. A person asked Imam Sadiq (a.s.): 'O Mawla, how will people benefit from the hidden Imam?' The Imam replied: 'Just as people benefit from the sun behind the clouds.' In the same way, the Imam (a.s.) guides people while being hidden. Dear viewers, this points to the fact that the world remains due to the existence of the Imam, and you are constantly helping us... The world remains due to your existence, and you are constantly helping us. Every moment you are helping us. And you (a.s.) say: 'If we were not attentive towards you, the enemies would have destroyed you.' In the end, on behalf of all those who love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), there are two lines: 'When the beginning of the Hujjah starts, let it be written on my forehead: This is the grace of Ali. Ali is the Imam of the time, I am the slave of Ali.' O Allah, hasten his reappearance. title: Khidmat e Ahle Bait (a.s.) ki Ehmiyyat  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual significance of serving the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the Imam of the Time. Drawing upon historical accounts, such as the correspondence between Imam Jawad (a.s.) and Ali ibn Mahziyar, the speaker emphasizes that true devotion requires consistent effort that transcends worldly hardships. The lecture highlights that service to the Imam is a divine privilege, promising eternal recognition and a shared status with the Ahlulbayt in the Hereafter.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of Hassan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his supporters, his Shias, and his servants, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. Amma ba'd, our master Imam Sadiq (a.s.) has said: 'Law adraktuhu la-khadamtuhu ayyama hayati' (If I had reached him, I would have served him all the days of my life). Truthful is our master Imam Sadiq (a.s.). In this Hadith, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that if I had reached the time of the Imam of the Time, I would have served him for the rest of my life. Now, look, the Infallible Imams (a.s.) never use exaggeration; they do not use exaggeration, rather they state what is the truth, what is the reality. From this Hadith, it is known how much importance there is in serving the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). Now, reflect on this, and when someone spends days and nights in the service of the Imam and keeps serving the Imam, then in the eyes of the Imam, his rank and his status are very high. This tradition that we are about to present to you is from the book 'Al-Ghaybah' by Sheikh Tusi (may Allah have mercy on him), page number 226. In this Hadith, Imam Jawad (a.s.)—meaning the ninth Imam, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali (a.s.)—wrote this letter to one of his followers whose name was Ali ibn Mahziyar. Let us tell you that in history, two or three people named Ali ibn Mahziyar have passed among the companions of the Imams, from whom traditions are narrated. This Ali ibn Mahziyar is a companion of the ninth Imam, Imam Jawad (a.s.). The Imam wrote that letter. Well, writing a letter means that this Hadith has become even more authentic because it has come in written form. That is, it is not by word of mouth, but in written form, in a written format. Now, look, the Imam says: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.' The Imam is writing in the letter: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Ali,' who is he addressing? Ali ibn Mahziyar. 'O Ali, Ahsanallahu jazaka' (May Allah give you the best reward) 'wa askanaka jannatahu' (and may He lodge you in His Paradise). Look at how many prayers the Imam is giving in the first sentence; count how many prayers the Imam has made in the first sentence. There are four prayers. May Allah give you the best reward, second is that He lodges you in His Paradise, and third is 'wa mana'aka minal-khizyi fid-dunya wal-akhirah' (and may He protect you from disgrace and humiliation in this world and the hereafter). Allah will not let you be humiliated in the world nor disgraced in the hereafter. That is, whoever remains engaged in the service of the Imam will never be humiliated or disgraced. 'Wa hasharakallahu ma'ana' (And may Allah gather you with us), and then the greatest prayer, the Imam says: 'May Allah gather you with us.' There can be no greater prayer than this, and the Imam himself is making it. Look, there are two things: one is that we ourselves pray—we mostly pray in Ashura or other Ziyarats and prayers—that Allah gathers us with the family of Muhammad (a.s.). That is one prayer. But when the Imam himself prays, and the Imam is 'Mustajab al-Da'wah' (one whose prayer is answered), the Imam is the one whose prayer is accepted. The Imam is saying: 'May Allah gather you with us.' Now the Imam says: 'O Ali, qad balawtuka' (O Ali, we have tested you). That is, before becoming a Shia, the Ahlulbayt always test their Shias. And then after the test, what is it? 'Wa khayartuka' (Then we chose you). First, we tested you, then we chose you. Chose you for what? 'Fin-nasihati' (That you are a well-wisher of ours), 'wa ta'ati' (that you obey us), 'wa khidmati' (and serve us), 'wat-tawqiri' (and honor and revere us), 'wal-qiyami bima yajibu 'alayka' (and perform everything that has been made obligatory upon you). That is, the Imam says that we tested you, and after testing, we chose you for all these things. For well-wishing, for obedience, for service, for honor and reverence, and for performing everything that has been made obligatory upon you. Five things. This is a strange sentence of the Hadith. After that, he says: 'Fa law qultu lam ara mithlaka la-rajawtu an akuna sadiqan' (And if I were to say that I have not seen anyone like you, I hope that I would be truthful). If I were to say that I have not seen any Shia like you, any follower like you—meaning as much as you love us, no one loves us like you—then I hope my statement will be true. That is, the Imam says that you are definitely our best Shia. 'Fa jazakallahu jannatil-firdawsi nuzulan' (May Allah lodge you in the gardens of Firdaws). The gardens of Firdaws—meaning the gardens of Firdaws are the highest gardens of Paradise, which is the station of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), may He lodge you there. Look, there were the first four prayers in the first sentence, after that the Imam is making the fifth prayer in the middle sentence. May Allah lodge you in the gardens of Firdaws. And then after that, the Imam says: 'Fa ma khafiya 'alayya maqamuka wa la khidmatuka' (O Ali, your station, your status, your value, your worth, and your service are not hidden from us). We know, O Ali, we know. That is, whether the people of the world value you or not, it has no value what the people of the world think. However, in our view, you have value and worth because your services are not hidden from us. And regarding these services, the Imam says, 'Fi al-harr wa al-bard, fi al-harr wa al-bard,' meaning even in the heat and in the winter, meaning even in the cold. This means you did not care about the heat; even while drenched in sweat, you remained engaged in our service. You endured the discomforts of the heat, you endured the difficulties, and despite shivering in the cold, you remained engaged in our service. This means that for our service, you did not offer excuses of heat, nor did you offer excuses of cold. Just as people generally offer excuses for serving the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), we usually say, 'Actually, it is too hot right now,' or 'It is too cold.' The Master of the Universe (Imam) says that when I ask you in the heat, you say it is too hot; when I ask you in the cold, you say it is too cold. Here, the Imam says, 'You neither care about the heat nor worry about the cold; you remain engaged in our service.' And after that, the Imam says, 'Fi al-layl wa al-nahar,' and day and night you remain engaged in our service. Meaning you do not look at the day, you do not look at the night. Allahu Akbar. This is what a servant is called. That is why the qualities of the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) are described as: 'Rahban bil-layl wa asad bil-nahar' (Monks by night and lions by day). These are the ones who will worship all night and roam like lions during the day. Then Imam Jawad (a.s.) writes, 'Fa-as'alu Allah'... Yes, yes, I pray to Allah. 'Idha jama'a al-khala'iqi lil-qiyamah' (When Allah gathers all creatures for the Resurrection). When He gathers everyone from the beginning to the end. 'An yahbuka bi-rahmatin' (That He may bestow upon you a mercy). I pray to Allah that on the Day of Judgment, when Allah gathers all creatures, He bestows upon you such a mercy. 'Taghtabitu biha' (That people will envy you for it). Meaning the people of the Resurrection will envy you. People will look and say, 'Who is this person? He is the servant of the Imam. He is the one who served the Imam.' 'Innahu sami'u al-du'a' (Indeed, He is the Hearer of prayers). And if the one praying is an Imam, then surely the prayer will be answered. Now, what could be greater than this? There is nothing greater than this. So, let us all strive to serve our Imam of the Time, and serve him day and night, and in every season, and in every climate, and let us not make any excuse, let us not declare anything as an excuse—not this reason, not that reason. Keep the service of the Imam-e-Zamana as your top priority in everything, so that tomorrow when the Imam (a.s.) reappears, the Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) may utter the same words that Imam Jawad (a.s.) wrote for Ali ibn Mahziyar. So, let us look at another incident that occurred during the time of Imam Jawad (a.s.). Imam Jawad (a.s.) narrated this incident, but the event itself is from the time of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The narrator's name is Muhammad ibn Walid al-Kirmani. He says that this hadith is present in the book 'Al-Kharaij wal-Jaraij', which is the book of the late Qutbuddin Rawandi, and Allama Majlisi has recorded it in volume 50 of 'Bihar al-Anwar'. So the narrator, Muhammad ibn Walid al-Kirmani, says that I used to visit Imam Jawad (a.s.) frequently. But as many times as I went to Imam Jawad (a.s.)—that is, the ninth Imam, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali (a.s.)—I did not get the opportunity to meet him or have a proper conversation with him. One day, Alhamdulillah, I got the opportunity to see the Imam and meet him properly. Now, because I had been going repeatedly, the Imam surely knew that this Shia was coming regularly. So the Imam said to Muhammad ibn Walid al-Kirmani, 'O Muhammad ibn Walid al-Kirmani, stay at our house today and eat with us.' Seizing this opportunity—this was an opportunity—I asked the Imam a question. I asked the Imam a question, and look at how beautiful the question was. I asked, 'Ma li-muwalikum fi muwalatikum?' (What is the reward for those who accept your Wilayah, or for those individuals who accept it? What is their reward?). In response to this question, the Imam narrated an incident, and that incident is from the time of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam says that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) had a slave, and that slave's responsibility was to look after the Imam's mount. Meaning feeding it, washing it, bathing it, whatever it was—looking after it. Once, a delegation came from Khorasan, that is, from Iran—a group came in which there were many merchants, and some merchants were very wealthy. So one merchant kept his eyes on this slave. That merchant, that businessman, asked this slave, 'Hal laka ya ghulam an tas'alahu an yaj'alani makanaka wa akuna lahu mamlukan wa aj'ala laka mali kullahu fa-inni kathiru al-mali min jami'i al-sufuf' (O slave, is it possible for you to request the Imam to put me in your place, and I become his slave, and you take my place, and you become the owner of all my wealth? For I have much wealth from all trades). Look at the question! All his wealth, and he said, 'I have so much in worldly wealth. You become the owner of it all, and I just get the chance to serve the Imam.' Amazing thing. Look at how we usually abandon the service of the Imam for our petty matters. We make excuses for it, saying, 'I had that work, I had this work, I had this job, I had that job.' We talk like this and neglect the Imam's work. We abandon the Imam's work. We don't pay attention to it, we are negligent about it. Anyway, this was such a tremendous offer; who would reject it? This slave went to Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and said, 'Master, you know that I have served you a lot and served you for a long time. So if Allah sends some goodness and blessing for me, would you have any objection to it?' The Imam replied, 'U'tika min 'indi wa amla'uka min ghayri' (I will give you from my side, and I will not make you dependent on anyone else so that you have to spread your hands before anyone). Look, there is a lesson in this sentence: if we trust our Imam, the Imam will provide everything; you don't need to worry. We should just keep serving the Imam; we serve the Imam, and the Imam will take care of us. If you consider your Imam as your Master, then our Master will take care of us. We should also serve like a servant. Anyway, the slave told the Imam that a certain merchant who came with the Khorasan delegation has made me this offer. The Imam said to him, 'It is fine. In zahidta fi khidmatina wa raghiba al-rajulu fina' (If you are not interested in our service and that man is inclined towards our service, he is interested in serving us, then it is acceptable; we will accept him. Wa arsalnaka, and we will release you, we will let you go, there is no problem. Go, we will exchange). The slave was very happy to hear this and started going towards that merchant happily, thinking the Imam had given his consent. Once, the Imam called him and said, 'Because you have served me for so many days, I will give you some advice. Although the choice is in your hands, I will not force you.' 'Wa laka al-khiyar' (And the choice is yours). The choice is in your hands. 'Fa-idha kana yawmu al-qiyamati kana rasulu Allahi salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi muta'alliqan bi-nuri Allahi' (On the Day of Judgment, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will be holding onto the Light of Allah. 'Wa kana amiru al-mu'minina 'alayhi al-salam muta'alliqan bi-rasuli Allahi salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi' (And the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) will be attached to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)). 'Wa kana al-a'immatu muta'alliqina bi-amiri al-mu'minina 'alayhi al-salam' (And the Imams (a.s.) will be attached to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)). 'Wa kana shi'atuna muta'alliqina bina' (And our Shia, who were our Shia in this world and were attached to us, were attributed to us, were attached to us. So whoever is our Shia...) 'Yadkhuluna madkhalana wa yariduna mawridana' (They will enter where we enter, and they will arrive where we arrive). They will reach where we reach. Where our existence is, there is their existence. They will be attached to us. Its example is exactly like you see a train engine that is tied in the front; wherever that engine goes, the rest of the train's compartments follow, right? Exactly in the same way, those who are attached to the Imam will keep going with the Imam. They will be with the Imam. Now, obviously, what will be the status of the Imam in Paradise? The same status as the Imams (a.s.), the status of the Commander of the Faithful, the status of the Commander of the Faithful is the status of the Messenger of Allah, the status of the Messenger of Allah is the Light of Allah. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. What a status! The slave just heard this and immediately came back. He came back and said, 'No, bal uqimu fi khidmatik' (No, I will remain in your service). 'Wa uthiru al-akhirata 'ala al-dunya' (And I will prefer the Hereafter over the world). I don't care about the world at all. Saying this, the slave went back to that merchant, the Khorasani, and said, 'I have no interest in your offer, your proposal, your gift. I cannot leave the service of the Imam.' And whatever the Imam had said to that slave, he told the merchant exactly every single word. After that, he brought that slave, that merchant, to the Imam. He brought him into the service of the Imam. The Imam accepted the Wilayah of that merchant, and in return, the merchant gave the slave 1000 gold coins and requested the Imam, 'Mawla, please pray for me.' This is the reward for those who serve the Imam. In this world and the hereafter, they will always be with the Imam. So, do not forget your Imam. Everyone has worldly difficulties. Every person has their own struggles and troubles. The nature of these changes, but there is no one in the world who does not have difficulties. Only the type changes. But these difficulties, these problems, should never be made an excuse for not serving the Imam. And day and night, day and night, remain engaged in the service of the Imam. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin, wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi tayyibina tahireen ma'sumeen, wa la'natud da'imu ala a'daihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri fada'ilhim wa manaqibihim.

title: Khaak-e-Shefaa ka Ehteraam [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the profound importance of showing respect toward the Khak-e-Shifa (the sacred soil of Imam Hussain's grave). Through a narrated incident involving the family of Muhaddith-e-Noori, the speaker illustrates that Imam Hussain is aware of how his followers treat this holy soil. The talk emphasizes that such negligence can be displeasing to the Imam and encourages believers to maintain proper etiquette when handling the soil.
content:
A'udhu billahi sami'il alimi minash shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir rahmanir raheem. Wa sallallahu alaika ya waliyyal asr adrikna wala tuhlikna. Assalamu alal Husaini wa ala Aliyibnil Husaini wa ala awladil Husaini wa ala as-habil Husain. Sheikh Abbas-e-Qummi (r.a.), in his famous and popular book Mafatih al-Jinan, narrates an incident in the chapter regarding the benefits of the soil of the holy grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.). He writes that my honorable teacher, Thiqatul Islam Muhaddith-e-Noori, wrote in his book Darussalam that one day, my mother saw one of my brothers keeping the soil of Imam Hussain's (a.s.) grave in the pocket of his coat that was on the side. She scolded him and said, 'This is disrespect to the Khak-e-Shifa (healing soil), because keeping it there might cause the Sajdagah (prayer tablet) to get crushed and break.' My brother admitted that this had happened twice, and then he promised that from today onwards, he would not keep the Sajdagah in such a pocket. Many days passed since this. One night, my late father, the Allamah, who had no knowledge of this incident, saw in a dream that our master and Mawla, Imam Hussain (a.s.), had come to visit him and was sitting in the library, expressing extreme affection. After that, Imam Hussain (a.s.) said to my father, 'Call your children so that I may give them something.' Consequently, my father called all five of us brothers there, and we all stood before the Hazrat. Imam Hussain (a.s.) had garments and some items with him. Imam (a.s.) called each of us one by one and bestowed gifts upon us. When it was the turn of that brother of mine, the Hazrat looked at him with anger and said to my father, 'This son of yours has broken two Sajdagahs made from the soil of my grave.' Saying this, instead of calling him like the other brothers, the Hazrat threw something towards him from a distance, which, in my opinion, was likely a comb case. After this, my late father woke up from his sleep and narrated his dream to my mother, and my mother narrated her story to my father. They were extremely astonished at the truthfulness of that dream. Mourners of the Oppressed of Karbala, respect for the Khak-e-Shifa is mandatory because not only is it the soil of the most superior land, but as we found in this incident, Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself is so sensitive about the soil of his grave that he does not tolerate even the slightest negligence in this regard. Ibn Qulawayh, in his famous book Kamil al-Ziyarat, has mentioned 34 traditions in five chapters related to Khak-e-Shifa, which include the presence of healing and safety in the soil of Imam Hussain (a.s.), the etiquette of tasting the soil, and the prayers to be recited before using it. We pray to the Almighty God that He grants us the ability to respect the Khak-e-Shifa while keeping its importance in mind, and grants us the ability to train our children to respect it. Ameen ya Rabbal Alameen.
