title: Ek Guftugu (Part: 2) | Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.) Par Jaanleva Hamla Kisne Kiya? | Najaf-e-Ashraf
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological accounts surrounding the martyrdom of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the various assassination attempts made against him. It highlights the distinction between external threats from polytheists and internal threats from hypocrites within the early Muslim community. The discussion emphasizes the Prophet's strategic patience in dealing with these individuals and the significance of the event of Ghadir-e-Khumm in the context of subsequent disobedience. Finally, it touches upon the role of Hudhayfah (r.a.) as a keeper of secrets regarding the identities of those who conspired against the Prophet.
content:
Ali Bhai, peace be upon you. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Hasan Bhai, are you in Najaf al-Ashraf at this time? What a coincidence! Yes, Ali Bhai, Alhamdulillah, I received the grace from the Lord, and I was blessed with the Ziyarat of this shrine. Let's go to the shrine of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Regarding the 28th of Safar, seeing these banners reminds me of the conversation you and Ahmad Bhai had last year, where you proved in the light of both the Quran and Hadith that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was martyred. Believe me, after listening to that conversation, I went home and wrote 'Martyrdom' next to the 28th of Safar in my calendar. If you hadn't given a lecture on this topic, I would still be a believer in the death of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) like others. You did exactly the right thing, Hasan Bhai. It is a matter of belief that when all Muslims start writing 'Day of Martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)' on the 28th of Safar in the Hijri calendar, in reality, there will be no room for doubt or suspicion. And for us, it is absolutely clear that the Prophet's martyrdom took place. And how can anyone doubt this when he had been subjected to life-threatening attacks so many times? Life-threatening attacks, and that too on the Prophet? How can you say this? Who attacked him and when? Hasan Bhai, undoubtedly, immediately after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s mission, he had to face many difficulties. You know why the wars were fought. The goal of the enemies of the Prophet was only to kill the Prophet. So, all the enemies who came—the more than 80 wars that were fought for Islam—what was the purpose of all of them? Only to kill the Prophet. And you will be surprised to hear that not just once, but at least 10 times during the Prophet's life, there was a direct attempt on his life. And these 10 attacks on the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) are in addition to the wars. That is, apart from those 80+ wars, these 10 attacks, of which 8 were carried out by the polytheists and 2 by the hypocrites who used to sit in the Prophet's gathering, recited his Kalima, but remained engaged in planning against the Prophet. And as far as the polytheists' attacks are concerned, like Abu Lahab trying to attack the Prophet, all the wars are one thing. Why did the migration have to happen? The migration from Makkah to Madinah, the attack by a person named Malik on the night of migration... The history of attacks on the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is a witness to this fact; history is a witness that due to the fear of these attacks, the people of the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to weep. You asked about the attacks by the hypocrites (munafiqeen)—when and how they tried to attack the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Hassan Bhai, this is a good question. You must have heard about the Battle of Tabuk. It actually took place, and this was the battle in which Maula Ali (a.s.) did not participate alongside the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) because he had to stay in Medina to safeguard the Islamic government, as the hypocrites were plotting against the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) there as well. This is the same battle in which the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) was ordered by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to stay in Medina, and this stay proved to be one of the countless virtues of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) likened him to Harun (a.s.) by saying, 'O Ali, you are to me as Harun was to Musa.' And this is also the strongest evidence for the undisputed Caliphate of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). You have said it absolutely correctly, Hassan Bhai, and in fact, if I may say so, you have presented the entire summary of the event of the Battle of Tabuk. But do you know what happened when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was returning from the Battle of Tabuk? You tell us. This is known as the 'Event of the Aqaba'. In this event, an attempt was made to assassinate the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) while returning from that battle. Is it possible that those who had proclaimed 'La ilaha illallah' and 'Muhammadur Rasulullah' became enemies of the life of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? How is this possible? It is possible, and it is recorded in history. Although Muslims tried for many centuries to hide this, they were not successful. This attack, the entire event of Aqaba, and the attack associated with it, are alluded to in the Holy Quran itself. In the Holy Quran, Surah At-Tawbah, verse number 74, Allah (s.w.t.) says—and in fact, what did He say? What they said was a word of disbelief; they exceeded the limits and became disbelievers after having accepted Islam. They were on Islam until then, but by swearing false oaths and performing a specific act, they exited Islam. 'Wa hammu bima lam yanulu'—they intended to do something which they could not complete. They tried, but they could not complete it; they did not succeed in their objective. Regarding this Surah At-Tawbah, in the famous commentary 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir'—who is considered an Imam of Tafsir among them—he has written in his Tafsir, Volume 4, page 181 and 182, that when returning from this battle, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave an order to a herald, and he made an announcement. What was the announcement? That the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has chosen the path of Aqaba. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) returns from Tabuk, he will go through the path of Aqaba, and he ordered that no one should come there. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is returning from Tabuk via the path of Aqaba, while the Muslims are taking another path, and he ordered that no one should accompany him. Who was with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) at that time? Only... what happened? Some people riding camels with their faces covered... What happened? A group came riding on camels with their faces covered. Several people came together; they surrounded Hazrat Ammar and threw a cloth over his face. After throwing the cloth over Hazrat Ammar's face, these people started following the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). The people who had come started hitting the faces of the camels of those who were riding. And then what happened? Those people did not succeed in their objective. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Hazrat Hudhayfah, 'Slow down,' because he had sensed that something was happening behind him. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) got off his mount, and meanwhile, Hazrat Ammar returned because he was trying to drive away those who were hitting the camels. So, as soon as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) got off his mount, Hazrat Ammar replied that he had recognized those riders because they had come with cloths over their faces. Even though the riders had covered their faces, Hazrat Ammar said he recognized them by their mounts. Upon this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'Do you know what their intention was?' He said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Their intention was to take the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) along with his mount and throw him off the mountain.' These were the hypocrites. Also, do you know that the hypocrites who came to attack the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... Do you know that the hypocrites who came to attack the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—Tafsir Ibn Kathir has written this, and not only did I write that some hypocrites came, but their exact number was written, and their names were also stated by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It is written in my books that there will be 12 such people among my companions who are hypocrites, who will never enter Paradise and will not even be able to smell its fragrance. Now look further at what is written here: these people used to call themselves companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and would gather, but what kind of hypocrisy and hypocrisy was in their hearts! So that no one thinks that all those sitting around the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) were all moths to the flame—no, rather, sitting in the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) gathering is not a guarantee of entering Paradise. Although among those sitting in the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) gathering, there were some who disobeyed the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and were seen fleeing from battles to save their own lives without caring for the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) life. Everyone knows about the Battle of Tabuk. One must know that the hypocrites were among those surrounding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and this... Among those around [the Prophet], these hypocrites were seen mocking the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Holy Quran, in Surah Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), verse 16, also states that when the hypocrites listen to your words, O Prophet, they do not truly listen. They listen to your words, but as soon as they leave your presence, they go to the people of knowledge and ask, 'What did the Prophet say just a moment ago?' They would forget everything as soon as they stepped outside; they would not even remember what the Prophet had said. And regarding these companions, whom people today—and indeed always—insist we should not criticize, saying, 'Do not say anything against the companions,' these are not our words; these are from their own books. Look at Sahih Bukhari, which they consider authentic. What is the narration? It is that on the Day of Judgment, at the Pond of Kawthar, the companions of the Prophet will be driven away from him. Upon this, the Prophet will ask, 'O Lord, these are my companions!' Then it will be said to the Prophet, 'You do not know what innovations these people introduced after you left.' And these people, whom people consider companions—look, it is written in the narration... It is written in the narration that these people are all apostates. Those who are considered companions are, in reality, enemies of the religion. But the question arises: who were these hypocrites? If they attacked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and tried to martyr him, why did the Prophet not kill them or take revenge during his lifetime? People often raise this question: when the Prophet knew—and he had even disclosed this to Hudhayfah and Ammar—why did he not take revenge? The answer to this was provided by the Prophet of Islam himself. He said in response, 'I do not want the Arabs to say about me that once he gained victory with the help of his companions, he started killing his own companions.' I do not want people to say such things about me. Therefore, what did the Prophet do? The path he chose was the best one. The Prophet invoked a curse; he invoked a curse against those people, saying, 'O Lord, strike them with Dhaliba.' Meaning, they will not depart from this world until the effect of Dhaliba is upon them. Now, a question is raised on this... When asked what 'Dhubaila' is, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'A ball of fire that will enter their hearts and consume them.' This means it will be an incurable disease for them that will consume them. This is a narration from Al-Bidaya wan-Nihaya, and it is quite easy to find out which people died of 'Dhubaila'. Indeed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left the revenge to Allah and made such a supplication against them that would consume them. Apart from this, after the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) granted peace to his mortal enemies, so how could he take revenge on such people? It would be against the dignity of the Mercy to the Worlds (s.a.w.a.) to do so. Ali Bhai, after this incident, did people come to know about their actions, and did people find out who those people were? Yes, Hassan Bhai, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself had told Hudhayfah (r.a.) and Ammar (r.a.) their names, as I mentioned earlier. Hudhayfah (r.a.) knew the names, and Ammar (r.a.) also knew the names, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded both of them, Hudhayfah and Ammar, that they should... He also commanded them to remain silent about their names. Now, either the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) knew the names, or the attackers themselves knew. Apart from them, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not tell anyone else, and commanded that these names should not be mentioned or revealed to anyone. By ordering them not to reveal the names, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) launched such a psychological attack on those hypocrites that it became a lifelong torment for them. This is why Hudhayfah (r.a.) is counted among the confidants of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), because the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) shared this secret with him, and he knew who was counted among the hypocrites. We find that people were curious about who the hypocrites were. So, what would people do? They would observe who Hudhayfah (r.a.) would attend the funeral prayers of. If Hudhayfah (r.a.) avoided a funeral and did not participate, people would conclude that no Muslim should attend that funeral. Therefore, history itself is a witness that when those hypocrites would get tired of asking, 'Hudhayfah, tell us the names, Hudhayfah, tell us the names,' he would not reveal the names until the end. Finally, one of the hypocrites—and this is a point with a reference— Look, this is a point with a reference. The hypocrite, tired and defeated, even asked if his name was on that list or not. First, he asked whose names were on it, and finally, he came to ask, 'Brother, is my name on it or not?' He would repeatedly ask Hudhayfah (r.a.) this question. And what happened in the end? There is a narration where the very person who used to come and ask Hudhayfah (r.a.) daily had to say himself, 'By God, Hudhayfah, I am one of those hypocrites.' During the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) lifetime, they conspired and disobeyed him so much that there is no doubt the Ummah was bound to be misled after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Now, Hassan Bhai is saying that these people left no stone unturned in disobeying the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). This is just after the event of Ghadir-e-Khumm; the abundance of opposition to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is recorded in history. The hypocrites had made a pact among themselves, which is called 'Sahifa', a pact among themselves against the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Then, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ordered them to join the army of Usama, they showed reluctance, meaning they did not obey that either and did not go. Well, look, we found such time in our conversation that we didn't even realize it. Presenting ourselves in the court of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), to discuss the martyrdom of the Messenger, and the martyrdom of the son of the Master of the Universe, the leader of the youth of Paradise, Hazrat Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). Going to the court of the Master, through his intercession, we asked the Master...

content:
Making Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) a means (waseela) to pray is among the teachings of the Imams, and through this, our prayers are answered quickly. It is narrated that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) is present, and a person complains about someone to whom he had lent some money, and he did not return it. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Go to Makkah, and after going to Makkah, perform Tawaf, and pray two rak'ahs of prayer at the place of Hazrat Abdul Muttalib (a.s.), then at the place of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), and then pray; Insha'Allah, you will get your money back.' He goes to Makkah, performs Tawaf, and says, 'As soon as I was at the door of the Safa, I saw that the person who had not returned my money came in front of me and said...'

title: Imam Ali (a.s.) Ki Wilaayat Ke Baghair A'maal Radd | Short Clip from GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI 2021
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes that the acceptance of good deeds in Islam is fundamentally dependent on the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). Citing a narration from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), the speaker warns that even extreme acts of worship, such as excessive fasting, are rendered void if accompanied by enmity toward Ali. The discourse challenges the notion that deeds alone are sufficient for salvation, asserting that Wilayah is the essential prerequisite for divine acceptance.
content:
Hazrat Zayd ibn Arqam narrates from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that he said: 'Ali, if my Ummah fasts so much that they become like a bow, meaning they bend like a bow, and even then, if they hold enmity towards you, Ali, then Allah will throw them into Hell face-first.' That is, those who say 'deeds, deeds, deeds,' we must keep in mind that the requirement for deeds is Wilayah. Whoever thinks that with deeds alone he will go to the court of Allah, he will be mistaken and will go to Hell face-first.

title: Incident of Pen & Paper - Analysis & Responses | Wafaat Ya Shahaadat (Ek Guftugu - Part: 3)
excerpt: This lecture provides a critical analysis of the 'Incident of the Pen and Paper' (Hadith al-Qirtas), exploring the events surrounding the Prophet Muhammad's final days. The speaker examines historical accounts from major Sunni sources, arguing that the obstruction of the Prophet's final will was a deliberate act of defiance and part of a broader conspiracy. The discussion emphasizes the necessity of divine guidance through the Ahlulbayt and challenges traditional interpretations of the events that occurred on the 'Thursday of Calamity'.
content:
Who was that person who forbade the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) from giving paper and pen? No Muslim can deny this hadith or reject it because it is present in every one of their books. Despite it being present, today these people never mention this hadith on their pulpits. When the calling of the Messenger is not like our calling, then can the Messenger be like us? Oh, my innocent Muslims. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Sallallahu ala ya waliyyana wa la tuqina. Wafat or Shahadat, a video series in which we have been continuously discussing the topic that when the Seal of the Prophets, the Master of the Messengers, the Beloved of the Worlds, Hazrat Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) departed from this world, it was not a natural death, but he was martyred; meaning it was not a Wafat (passing), but a Shahadat (martyrdom). In the first episode of this series, we clarified through verses of the Holy Quran and historical facts that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not pass away, but was martyred. Then in the second episode, we looked at the event of the Battle of Tabuk and the event of Aqaba, how the Messenger of Allah... Looking at the event of Aqaba, how a lethal attack was made on the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and that too by those whom the Holy Quran called hypocrites. So, Muslims should not be surprised at the martyrdom of the Prophet because from the very beginning of Islam, the polytheists and hypocrites had been plotting and attempting to kill him. And now, in the third episode of this series, we will discuss in detail the event which is a blot on the history of Islam, which is also called the Event of the Parchment (Waqi'at al-Qirtas), or the Pen and Paper, or the Tragedy of Thursday. This is the event in which the audacity of the opponents of Wilayah increased so much that they not only put obstacles in the way of the Beloved of Allah writing his will but also insulted the dignity of the Prophet through inappropriate words. In this episode, we will see what this Tragedy of Thursday was and what happened that day. Who insulted the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and how? Was not letting the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) write his will an expression of sympathy, or something else? Finally, what did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) want to write that some people present in his house did not let him write? Let us try to know these things through this discussion, and a special thing about this is that in this entire discussion... A special thing is that not a single reference from a Shia book has been given in this entire discussion; rather, the talk will be based solely on the most authentic books of the Sunni school of thought. 'Yawm al-Khamis, wa ma yawm al-Khamis'—in Arabic, Thursday is called Khamis. Thursday, and what was this Thursday? These are the words of Ibn Abbas. The famous Sunni book Sahih Muslim narrates from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that Ibn Abbas repeated these words in a state of intense weeping. What was that scene? After all, what did Ibn Abbas remember that this state occurred while weeping, that the pebbles lying in front were soaked with his tears? This was the same incident that happened on Thursday before the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Abbas bhai, this is a point to note: when Ibn Abbas wept so much, no Muslim objected to his weeping. But if any Shia weeps over the calamities of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) or the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), then fatwas of innovation (bid'ah) are issued against them. Why is that? You are absolutely right, Akhil bhai. Regarding weeping, Muslims should clarify their position, clear their stand. Either stop issuing fatwas of bid'ah on the weeping and mourning of Shias, or condemn Ibn Abbas, who was a companion of the Messenger. Whatever it is, the standard should be one. Correct. Sa'id asked Ibn Abbas the reason for his weeping, what happened on that Thursday that you are weeping? So Ibn Abbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was suffering from intense pain, he said, 'Bring me a parchment so that I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray.' Here we must understand one thing: we are talking about that Prophet for whom the Quran says that he does not speak without divine revelation. That is, if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) intended to write something, it must have been a message from Allah. This is also the last Thursday night, meaning a few days before the departure of the Messenger of Allah. That is, surely this is the will of the Prophet that he wanted to write. And the tradition says that people stopped the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) from stating the message of Allah. Muslims are silent on such a great insult. Muslims are silent on such a great insult. It is surprising. And more surprising is that this event is present in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. But in the tradition of Sahih Muslim, it is not written that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was stopped. This is an old habit that you will find one part in one hadith in one book, and the continuation of that same hadith will be in another book. That is, it is as if things have been divided in such a way that if a person goes after one book and tries to find the truth in one book, he will not reach the truth. This is a deliberate conspiracy in their books, and very often, stating only half the matter is their old habit. Anyway, and that is why we look at the hadith of Sahih Bukhari. In it, the same thing is stated by Ibn Abbas that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was on his deathbed, some people were present, among whom was Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Bring me a parchment so that I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray.' It is clearly written that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave this order... When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave this order, what was said to him? 'Umar said the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is...'—this is how it is written in the hadith, although it is not complete without 'wa alihi'—'is overcome by intense pain, and you have the Quran, and the Book of Allah is sufficient for us.' If looked at carefully, this sentence 'the Book is sufficient for us' is itself against the Quran. Because Allah Almighty says in the Holy Quran in Surah an-Nahl, verse 43: 'Ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know.' That is, the Quran itself is ordering you to go and ask the people of the Reminder, and they are saying the Quran is sufficient for us. Now, if we think that the Quran is sufficient, then we should also see that there are 'Huruf al-Muqatta'at' (abbreviated letters) in the Holy Quran. That is, these are letters whose apparent meaning people do not know. So, is the Quran still sufficient? And if we look at the method of prayer, has the method of prayer been described in the Quran, how many rak'ahs are there in prayer? Even then, we say the Quran is sufficient. Even then, we say the Quran is sufficient. Well, if we look at the Muslims, there are so many sects among Muslims, and all of them use the Quran as evidence and try to prove that we are correct, and for that, they only provide evidence from the Quran. But still, there is so much disagreement. So, is it still correct to say that the Quran is sufficient? And this is a matter that even an ordinary person can consider: have we ever seen any school, any university, or any college where children are just given a book and told that this book is sufficient for you? You don't need someone to teach you this. You don't need someone to explain it. Even those who do a PhD, who are educated people, they also need a guide. So, if a teacher, a guide is needed for worldly education, then is only the Quran sufficient to understand the religion of Allah? Indeed. And this stopping of the Prophet is clearly an insult to the Prophethood. If this is not called an insult, then what will it be called? Whereas the Quran itself in Surah an-Nur, verse 63, Allah is commanding: 'Do not call the Messenger...' Even then, if we say that the Quran is sufficient—well, if we look at the many sects among Muslims, all of them use the Quran as evidence and try to prove that they are correct, and for that, they rely solely on the Quran. Yet, there is so much disagreement. So, is it still correct to say that the Quran is sufficient? Even an ordinary person can reflect on this: have we ever seen a school, university, or college where students are just given a book and told, 'This book is enough for you; you do not need anyone to teach it to you, you do not need anyone to explain it to you'? Even those who pursue a PhD, who are educated individuals, need a guide. So, if a teacher or a guide is needed for worldly education, is the Quran alone sufficient to understand the religion of Allah? Certainly not. And this act of stopping the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is undoubtedly an open insult to his Prophethood. If this is not called blasphemy, then what should it be called? Whereas the Quran itself, in Surah An-Nur, verse 63, commands: 'La taj'alu du'a ar-rasul'. In this, Allah is commanding, 'La tarfa'u aswatakum fawqa sawti an-nabi' (Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet). Meaning, when you are calling the Prophet, when you are calling the Messenger of Allah, do not call him in the way you call one another. That is, when it is a matter of calling the Messenger of Allah, the Quran or Allah is giving this guidance: do not call the Prophet the way you call each other. And here, the Messenger of Allah is being openly opposed. He is being stopped from stating and writing his will. Look here, Abbas Bhai, when calling the Messenger is not like calling us, then can the Messenger be like us? Oh, my naive Muslims. Therefore, we can understand that this act of the people is an open rebellion against God. Aqeel Bhai, looking further into this tradition, we see that those present there were divided into two groups: 'Fatahal-Ahl al-Bayt, fa-khasamu' (The Ahl al-Bayt were displeased and they objected to this). And contrary to this, it is narrated, 'Qulu li-nabiyyi sallallahu alayhi wa-alihi wa-sallam kitaban li-tada' (Say to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to write a book/document). Again, it says 'sallallahu alayhi wa-sallam', whereas this way of sending salutations is not correct. And one person among them says, 'Come to the Messenger and let him write that will...' Come to the Messenger and let him write that will, that document after which the Muslims will never go astray. At the same time, there was one person, 'wa-ma'a Umar', and the other group was the one that was satisfied with Umar's statement that the Prophet should not be allowed to write the will. And in the midst of this, when voices began to rise there, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to the people, 'Qumu' (Get up, leave from here). After that, the hadith continues, 'Qala Ubaydullah, fa-kana Ibn Abbas yaqulu: Inna ar-razi'ata kulla ar-razi'ati ma hala bayna rasulillahi sallallahu alayhi wa-alihi wa-sallam wa-bayna an-yaktuba lahum dhalika al-kitab ikhtilafuhum wa-laghatuhum'. Ubaydullah said that Ibn Abbas used to say after this that the greatest calamity of that day was the disagreement and the noise of the people that came between the Messenger and the document he wanted to write. And Ibn Abbas is also admitting that this is a calamity, and the greatest calamity. And this is not mentioned in Bukhari or Muslim. It is regrettable that all this... It is regrettable that despite knowing all this, despite there being so many hadiths, people defend this incident. That is, people come and say, or try to explain it in such a way that those who were present there found that the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) was in severe pain, and they were told that 'the Book of Allah is sufficient for us.' So they said this because they did not want to cause the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) the pain of writing. Look at their cunning, how they are trying to justify their act where they did not let the Messenger of Allah write; they are justifying it in any way possible. But they are not looking at the Messenger of Allah here, at what pain was caused to him. Then, Aqeel Bhai, I would like to ask, this 'not causing trouble to the Messenger', this 'respecting the Messenger'—can it be said that they were respecting the Messenger by fighting and making noise there? Is respecting the Prophet to raise one's voice in front of him? If they really wanted to respect the Messenger, they should have said... They should have said that you should not trouble yourself. We are your companions. We are the scribes of the revelation. You tell us what to write. We will write it for you. But instead of doing all this, they only created a commotion and noise. Whereas in the Quran, Allah says, 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu la tarfa'u aswatakum fawqa sawti an-nabi' (O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet), 'wa la tajharu lahu bil-qawli ka-jahri ba'dikum li-ba'din' (and do not speak aloud to him as you speak aloud to one another). If you do this, 'an tahbata a'malukum wa antum la tash'urun' (your deeds will become void while you do not perceive it). This is a clear command of the Quran: do not raise your voice in front of the Prophet and do not speak to him as you speak loudly to one another. And this is being included in the scope of respect. This is how Muslims were respecting the Messenger of Allah in his final moments. And Abbas Bhai, perhaps that is why it happened that as soon as they said that the Quran is sufficient for us, at that very moment they started opposing the Quran. Also, another thing they did there is something that no self-respecting Muslim can accept. And that is... No self-respecting Muslim can accept. And that is, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I will write a document for you after which you will never go astray,' they first created a commotion there, raised their voices, and then said about the Prophet, 'Faqalu ma lahu ahajara? Istafhimuhu' (They said, what has happened to him? Is he delirious? Ask him). And this sentence is in Sahih Bukhari and also in Musnad Ahmad. The Prophet replied to them at that very moment and said, 'Da'uni, falladhi ana fihi khayrun mimma tad'unani ilayhi' (Leave me, for the state I am in is better than what you are calling me to). Was stopping the Prophet from writing the will an expression of sympathy, or something else? Here, they did not stop at just making noise and saying 'the Quran is sufficient.' They went one step further and accused the Prophet of, God forbid, losing his mental balance. And this is an accusation that... An accusation that a person thinks twice before making even against their own elders. But they did not think before making this accusation against the Messenger of Allah; they just made it. It is surprising. They call this respect. They were very concerned about the Prophet, which is why they did all this. Tanveer Bhai, you are talking about making accusations here, but if we look at the society, these people have gone even further. These people are objecting to the Shias now and are saying that on one hand, the Shias object to our elders that they committed insolence against the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) by not giving him the pen. But the Shias also have an objection against them that they did not say anything about Imam Ali (a.s.). Now, this is the incident of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. These people bring up this incident of Hudaybiyyah where they have said that when the peace treaty was signed between the polytheists of Mecca and the Messenger of God, at that time, when the peace document was fully written on paper, all the conditions were written, and finally, when the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) was to sign, where... Where he was to sign, Imam Ali (a.s.) had written the name of the Messenger of God in such a way: 'Muhammadun Rasulullah'. The polytheists of Mecca were troubled by this name, by this title. And the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) said to Imam Ali (a.s.), 'Write my name as Muhammad ibn Abdullah.' But Imam Ali (a.s.) did not do this work. And this is the same accusation they make against Imam Ali (a.s.), saying that Imam Ali (a.s.) also, God forbid, disobeyed the Messenger of God, and despite the Messenger of God saying to change the name, Imam Ali (a.s.) did not change it. Now, what can we say to this? To justify one mistake, they are bringing another incident here and misusing it. But it is a serious objection. The answer to this is very simple, Aqeel Bhai. The answer is present in the incident of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah itself. When Mawla Ali (a.s.) refused, saying 'I cannot erase Muhammadun Rasulullah,' the Messenger of God was not angry. He did not say, 'Go away from here.' This fact itself tells us that the comparison these people are making is 'Qiyas ma' al-fariq' (an invalid analogy)... This comparison is 'Qiyas ma' al-fariq'. It is not a similar comparison. In this, Mawla Ali's faith is visible. He is not willing to erase his belief with his own hands. 'Muhammadun Rasulullah'—when he accepted it, became a believer, he could not erase this belief with his own hands. Therefore, he left it for the Prophet, saying, 'In your presence, I cannot do this work.' Abbas Bhai, but you have brought a very different angle to this topic. It is a very different angle. We had never thought about this. Our books have this incident in this way. It is another matter that because those people wanted to bring something against the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin) through some incident and wanted to misuse it, they narrated this incident in such a way as if the Commander of the Faithful was opposing him. Whereas this is a virtue of the Commander of the Faithful in this incident, that he did not erase the thing he believed in with his own hands, and the Prophet was not even angry, asking 'Why did you do this? You should not have done this.' This is wrong—this is not mentioned anywhere, even in their books. Rather, there were some people present at that very occasion, some of their great elders, among whom were some people... Among whom were some people who clearly said that at the time of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, they had as much doubt about the Prophethood of the Messenger of God as they had never had before. Now, you are remembering Hudaybiyyah through this matter or through this talk, so why are you forgetting that the great people themselves announced with their own tongues that we had so much doubt about the Prophethood of the Prophet as we had never had before? Leaving such a big thing, you are after this matter which is ambiguous and was not clear in their books, and you are twisting it and presenting it as if the Commander of the Faithful was disobeying, God forbid, the Messenger of God. So, if we look at it, the Commander of the Faithful proved the status that Allah gave to the Messenger of God once again before the people. But these people, in this incident of 'Razi'at al-Khamis', are lowering the status of the Messenger of God. So there is no comparison between the two. Correct, correct. So here, as you said, you said it correctly, the Commander of the Faithful is expressing his belief, that this is his belief and faith. And there, people are saying that 'we are having doubts,' or in 'Razi'at al-Khamis', the status of the Prophet is being lowered. His disobedience—the matter reached such a stage that the Prophet had to drive the people away from there. Abbas Bhai... Had to drive the people away from there. Abbas Bhai, there is another thing that is worth noting here, and that is that if you study their books—that is, the books that are their authentic books like Bukhari, Muslim, or Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal—if you study these books, you will find that some parts of this incident have been narrated in different hadiths. But in all these books, you will not find this entire hadith, this entire incident that happened, together in one hadith. And perhaps the reason for this, the one reason that could be, is that these people did not want to bring this before the people: who was that person who forbade giving paper and pen to the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.)? Perhaps this is the only reason for those people. Who was that barrier because of whom the Prophet could not write his will? Which was the most important thing. And when it is a matter of a will, one question here is also this: the Prophet who taught us that we should write our will before our death—and this hadith is also found in their books that if a Muslim possesses enough wealth to write a will, for him this... It is held that whoever possesses wealth should write a will; it is not appropriate for them to spend two nights without having their will written and secured. So, the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) who taught us to write our wills, God forbid, did he not write his own will? And in their books, from the event of 'Raziyatul Khamees' until the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), which is Monday—in these four days, is there any incident or hadith found where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) wrote his will? At the very least, they bring forward the 'Hadith al-Qirtas', in one version of which it is written at the end that when those who created the commotion were removed from the house, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave three instructions to Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas narrates that the first instruction was to expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula, and when any delegation arrived, to give them gifts just as he used to give. And it is surprising that even Ibn Abbas forgot what the third instruction was. At the very least, they can bring this hadith, in which it is becoming clear that these are not the things the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) wanted to state, through which the Ummah would never be led astray. Here we are talking about the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)... Here we are talking about the will of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the two points you just mentioned—if we think about them, even an ordinary person could make such a will, like 'if someone comes to my house, welcome them' or 'if someone does not agree with my words, do not let them enter my city or my house.' We do not find anything in this that addresses the purpose of the will, which was 'so that you do not go astray after me.' We do not find any point regarding guidance or avoiding misguidance in this. In fact, even the will itself does not contain such points. Even an ordinary person, if they were to sit down to write a will, would not write it like this—just two points about hosting guests. This is far from mentioning how to avoid misguidance. In fact, it is certain that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) wanted to write something through that pen and paper, a will that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were satisfied with. But there were some people present there who did not want the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to state those things or his... ...state those things or his will. Those people had a motive for not wanting this to happen. You said something very important, Aqeel Bhai, that if we reflect on the sentences of this hadith, what did Ibn Abbas state? He said the hadith contains 'Lan tadillu ba'dahu abada' (you will never go astray after him). These are actually the sentences of 'Hadith al-Thaqalayn', which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) repeatedly taught people: 'I am leaving behind two weighty things among you: the Book of Allah and my Ahlulbayt. If you hold fast to both, you will never go astray until they meet me at the Hawd al-Kawthar.' No Muslim can deny this hadith or reject it because it is present in every one of their books. Despite it being present, today these people—if you look at their pulpits, this hadith is never stated in this way. Even if it is stated, they change the 'Ahlulbayt' to 'Sunnah'. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wanted it to be written down in a documentary form... ...so that when every Muslim goes to read the will of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), it becomes clear what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wanted to state, whom he wanted to keep at the forefront of the religion of Islam, and into whose hands he wanted to give Imamate and Caliphate. It becomes very clear to all Muslims. And these people recognized this very well through the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) words—what he wanted to state—and there was an uproar, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was stopped from writing. That is, keep in mind the background of this event. This event occurred when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had ordered the people of Medina to join the army of Usama bin Zayd. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was repeatedly stating to join Usama's army, and he explicitly cursed those who were not joining it. This is mentioned in the famous book 'Al-Milal wan-Nihal' by the famous Sunni author Shahrastani. In the section where he mentions the disputes that arose among Muslims before the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) passing and martyrdom, the first dispute he mentions is this... ...and the first dispute he mentions is this 'Hadith al-Qirtas', and immediately after that, he brings this event—the order to join the army of Usama bin Zayd. But these people did not go there; they clearly disobeyed the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) by not joining Usama's army and became deserving of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) curse—'La'ana Jaysh Usama'. This tradition is explicitly present. This is the entire background; a complete preparation was being made, a complete conspiracy was being hatched on how to disobey the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) at every step. They did not go to Usama's army, and then they did not let the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) write his will, creating obstacles. So you are saying it was pre-planned, with full planning? Yes, with full planning. And this is the summary of this entire event. It cannot be a coincidence that at the time the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) ordered people to join the army of Usama, they did not go with him and stayed in Medina, and when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked for paper and pen, they created a commotion and stopped the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) from writing his will. Coincidence or conspiracy? Passing or martyrdom? I hope this discussion has provided you with answers to some questions regarding the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). ...provided you with answers to some questions, and some questions may have arisen in the minds of some people: how did those who are considered devotees of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not only oppose him but also stop him from writing his will, which is the right of every Muslim? So, did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) have no will? We will discuss this in the next episode of this series, Insha'Allah. Until then, let us understand our responsibility and tell the world that the best of Allah's creation, Rahmatul-lil-Alameen, was martyred. It was a martyrdom, not a natural passing. O Allah, for the sake of the martyrdom of Your Beloved, hasten the reappearance of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) final successor and the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), so that revenge can be taken from all those who insulted the Prophethood. Ameen, Ya Rabb al-Alameen.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Thursday
chapters.summary: The lecture introduces the 'Event of the Parchment' (Waqi'at al-Qirtas), where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was prevented from writing his final will.

chapters.title: Ibn Abbas and the Incident
chapters.summary: The speaker analyzes the account of Ibn Abbas regarding the Prophet's request for a writing implement and the subsequent obstruction by those present.

chapters.title: Critique of 'The Book is Sufficient'
chapters.summary: The speaker challenges the claim that the Quran alone is sufficient without the Prophet's guidance, arguing that this rationale was used to insult the Prophet's authority.

chapters.title: Disrespect and Rebellion against Prophethood
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the Quranic prohibition against raising one's voice above the Prophet's and characterizes the obstruction of his will as an act of rebellion.

chapters.title: The Calamity of the Pen and Paper
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the incident where the Prophet's request for writing materials was denied, highlighting Ibn Abbas's description of this event as the greatest calamity.

chapters.title: Critique of Justifications and Accusations
chapters.summary: The discussion analyzes the excuses used to defend those who prevented the Prophet from writing, including the false claim of protecting him from pain and the disrespectful accusation of delirium.

chapters.title: Refuting False Analogies with Hudaybiyyah
chapters.summary: The speakers refute the attempt to equate Imam Ali's refusal to erase the Prophet's name at Hudaybiyyah with the disobedience shown during the incident of the pen and paper.

chapters.title: Fragmentation of Historical Narratives
chapters.summary: The speakers note how authentic sources fragment the narrative of the pen and paper incident to obscure the identity of those who opposed the Prophet's final will.

chapters.title: Analyzing the Hadith al-Qirtas
chapters.summary: The speaker questions the authenticity of the instructions attributed to the Prophet during the Hadith al-Qirtas, arguing they do not align with the Prophet's goal of preventing the Ummah from going astray.

chapters.title: The Connection to Hadith al-Thaqalayn
chapters.summary: The discussion highlights how the Prophet intended to document the leadership of the Ahlulbayt to ensure the Ummah's guidance, a move that was intentionally blocked.

chapters.title: Conspiracy and Disobedience
chapters.summary: The lecture links the obstruction of the Prophet's will to the earlier refusal of certain companions to join the army of Usama bin Zayd, suggesting a pre-planned conspiracy.

chapters.title: Conclusion on the Martyrdom of the Prophet
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes that the Prophet's passing was a martyrdom caused by those who opposed his commands and prevented his final will.

title: Majlis 1 |  Mehnat (Hard Work) | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 2023 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the concept of 'Mehnat' or hard work as a fundamental requirement for both worldly success and spiritual growth. The discourse emphasizes that human life is transient and that true purpose is found in striving toward the Creator through the foundation of Wilayah. By examining personal accountability, the dangers of procrastination, and the influence of companionship, the speaker encourages listeners to dedicate their youth and efforts to the path of Allah. The session concludes by reflecting on the ultimate sacrifice of Qasim ibn Hasan at Karbala as the pinnacle of devotion and spiritual exertion.
content:
When he said goodbye, a commotion erupted in the tents. When he said goodbye, the one who was awaited, the time is near, the day is setting. [Music] The calamity is near, there is something to fear, the Day of Judgment is near. [Music] Zainab (s.a.) is poor, the brother's departure is near. Saying this, the shirt was torn, a commotion erupted, a commotion erupted, a commotion erupted. It is a little distance to the tent, said the King of the World. [Music] If the gathering is not there, then raise your arms, O companions. [Music] Where will it be bound, O Messenger, raise your arms, I was crying, we are the special ones. We are the special ones. [Music] A commotion erupted, a commotion erupted. [Music] Mother's words came to my mind today, I will stay there, where the theft will go. [Music] Raise your arms, kiss the throat of the heart. [Music] A commotion erupted. A commotion erupted. Sing. Singing [Music] [Praise] Oh [Music] My heart is always [Music] weeping [Music] Maula Allah chose this topic for this discussion, for this chose this topic for this discussion, for this gathering. In this hadith, it is stated that 'O Adam, i.e., O human, your reality is nothing but days. Your reality, what is your reality? It is just like days. As the day passes, a part of you is passing away.' From the day a human steps into this world, their back is towards the world and their face is towards the hereafter. But humans get so lost in this world—you were not created for the world, you were created for the hereafter—yet we get so lost in this world. All the worldly relationships and attachments become so strong, so much so that we actually forget where we came from, where we are now, and where we came from, where we are now, and where we have to go. These are three stages; remember, there are three stages. There are three stages of Ma'rifat (gnosis). Where did we come from? Before this world, where were we? People think this world is the beginning, but those who are knowledgeable, those who are blessed with the teachings of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), know that this world is not the beginning. There is a world before this world. Apart from that, when we came into this world, then after this world, there will be the Day of Judgment, and after the Day of Judgment, there will be Paradise and Hell. So these are the stages, these are the phases that we need to understand. And it is necessary, although it is not possible for us to understand everything. The topic of this discussion is how a youth can develop their personality. This is especially for youngsters. See how the Imam (a.s.) described the reality of a human in just a few sentences, and see how the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) describes it in other words. See what beautiful words he uses to describe it. See what beautiful words they are. He says, 'Nafsun wa rajul...' (The soul and the man). Every single breath that a human takes... The word 'Al-Insan' (The Human) appears 58 times in the Quran. 'O human, what has deceived you concerning your generous Lord?' What is that thing that deceived you? The wealth of the world, the family, the family, the car, the mansion. Allah created you well, He fashioned you well. Basically, this is for youngsters who have time now and can develop their personality. Because it is narrated that once the Imam (a.s.) sent his companion to a place for preaching. He went there, stayed for a few days, and came back. Many people talk like this—when they send someone for preaching, they send someone who is mature in age and experienced. If a person is old in age, it is understandable, but at least in their heart, they should not be old. At the very least, they should be young at heart. So he went and what he did was... So he went and what he did was, he met a few people and came back. The Imam (a.s.) asked him, the sixth Imam (a.s.) asked him, 'Did you go? Did you achieve any success?' He said, 'They are very useless people, no one is there to listen. There is no benefit in talking to them.' Like many of us talk like this, often in gatherings you will hear people say, 'Oh, there is no benefit, look, there is no point in talking to them, I am telling you, they are not going to improve.' So the Imam (a.s.) asked a question. See how the Infallibles (a.s.) are aware of the soul. He asked, 'Did you go to the youth?' He said, 'I went to the elders.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'I spoke to the elders.' The youth—we call them 'naujawan' in Urdu—are called youth because a youth runs the fastest, like a horse. So the topic is that in personality, two things are very important. These are fundamental things, so we won't discuss them in detail, but just by pointing towards them, we will move on. The first thing is Faith (Iman), meaning there should be the correct belief. There should be the correct belief in Tawheed (Oneness of God), in Prophethood, in Imamate, and in the Day of Judgment. There should be correct belief. Until this belief is correct, everything else is useless. Nothing is correct. The belief must be correct, and the belief should be that which is in the light of the Quran and Hadith. Apart from that, no belief is correct or sound. The only belief is that which Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) have stated. That is the chapter. The name of the chapter is 'The Chapter of Submission and the Excellence of those who Submit' (Bab al-Taslim wa Fadl al-Musallimin). In its sixth hadith, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'If any person wants his faith to be complete, in which there is no defect, his faith should be completely correct, then he should say: My belief in all things is the same as what the family of Muhammad (a.s.) has stated. Whatever they have stated, I believe in it.' Whatever they have stated, I believe in it. Whatever they have hidden or kept secret, whatever has reached me, I believe in it. Whatever has not reached me, I believe in it. For the Infallibles (a.s.), and not for anyone else. You have 12 Imams, and you are going elsewhere? So this is a very important thing. A person who has the wealth of the world but stands on the street begging, there can be no one more unfortunate than him in the world. If the belief is not correct, then everything else is useless because belief is the soul of a human. Belief is the most important thing, and among all beliefs, the most important is Wilayah (Guardianship). If that is correct, then everything else is correct. If that is not correct, then everything else is useless. Therefore, Wilayah is the most important thing. 120 times, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I went 120 times, and 120 times, there was a common topic, and that common topic was Wilayah.' Because the Imam (a.s.) said that if you have Wilayah, there are chances of sins being forgiven, no matter how sinful a person may be. But if the Wilayah is not correct, then no matter how many good deeds one does, they will be thrown back at them. Nothing will be accepted. No matter how much effort one puts in, how much they worship, pray, fast—all of that is useless if there is no Wilayah. It will not be like that. 'Those who believe and do good deeds...' (Quran 2:25). Those who believe and do good deeds—in good deeds, the first thing is the recognition of Wilayah, and after that, there are prayers, fasting, and other acts of worship. So faith and good deeds go hand in hand. And Insha'Allah, during the discussion, we will keep presenting examples before you from the Infallibles (a.s.). We won't take much time, but those people whose hadith we are reading today, whose hadith we are narrating, whose hadith has reached us through them—what kind of people were they? Were they like the people we see today? People often say, 'It is impossible for a follower of Ali (a.s.) not to pray, or for a follower of Ali (a.s.) not to fast.' It is possible, it is impossible, because Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.) present this before you. Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 25: Allah says, 'And give glad tidings to those who believe and do good deeds...' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is told to give them glad tidings. Give them the good news that for them is Paradise, gardens beneath which rivers flow. This is a promise in Surah Baqarah and Surah Ma'idah, and Allah never breaks His promise. For those who have done good deeds, Allah has promised them that He will forgive their sins and grant them a great reward. If Allah calls something 'great' (Azeem), you can imagine its magnitude. If Allah grants the opportunity, there is a discussion on this word 'Azeem' that spans at least three pages in the traditions. Just this one word—when Allah says 'Azeem', what does it mean? How does it begin and where does it end? When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, and then the sequence begins, what is the meaning of 'Azeem'? It requires time to explain, but for now, the two most important things are that for a believer, their faith (Iman) must be correct. For a believer, their faith must be correct, and for that, one must study the Hadith and the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Alhamdulillah, all these books are now available in Urdu and English translations. The transformation begins with how you develop your personality. Along with this, Allah says in the Quran: 'O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion and will meet Him.' Here, the word 'Insan' (mankind) is used. Strive, O man, for the sake of your Lord; strive for His recognition (Ma'rifat). Strive for Ma'rifat because you are soon going to meet your Lord. You will face your Creator. Everyone is going to the grave; there is no one who can say, 'I do not have to die,' or 'I want to live in this world forever.' And nowadays, you see that no one can say anything; there is no guarantee of anyone's life. So the Quran says, 'Strive.' This is the very foundation. The Quran uses the word 'Kadhan' (exertion)—meaning to work so hard that one falls from exhaustion. Generally, the reason we are not successful in this world or the hereafter is that we are empty-handed. It is not that you should only work for religion and not for the world at all. Rather, what does the Imam say? If you know the Hadith, you will be surprised that a person says, 'I am working for religion and not for the world.' Because if you do not work for the things that are right in front of you, what will you work for in the hereafter? As it is in Surah Al-Qasas, 'Seek the home of the Hereafter by means of what Allah has given you, but do not forget your portion of the world.' Do not forget the world. Whatever Allah has given you in this world, use it to attain the Hereafter. Use it to achieve the Hereafter. It is like when a child is told to study, and they keep a book in front of them, but their mind is elsewhere—just to show their parents they are studying, while they are actually reading something else. Whatever it is, they are doing that. See, by doing this, a person is only deceiving themselves, not anyone else. If you do not move toward your goal yourself, no one else will take you there. No one else will take you. See, it is written in the Quran, in Surah Al-Qiyamah—I advise the youngsters to read Surah Al-Qiyamah with translation. It is the 75th chapter. In one verse, Allah says: 'Rather, man, against himself, is a witness, even if he presents his excuses.' Man knows himself; he knows how much effort he is putting in, no matter how many excuses he makes. We make excuses to soothe our hearts, but actually, if we wanted to, we could do it. If you were working until 2:00 AM and had a flight at 5:00 AM to go somewhere else, and you had to present something, you would do it because the company demands it. But if you are told to pray, you say, 'I am very tired, I have done this homework and assignment, I am very tired.' Who are you calling tired? You are calling yourself tired. One does not get tired. The Mawla (a.s.) said—you will hear a strange Hadith—the Imam (a.s.) says that the body will never become weak if a person intends to do a task. From Najaf to Karbala, it is 87 kilometers, and even further. A 95-year-old man, completely hunched over, with a cane in his hand, was walking. Someone asked him, 'In this journey, where did you drink water?' He replied, 'They killed Hussain (a.s.) thirsty, how can I drink water?' Everything... there must be a purpose. 'Balil-insanu 'ala nafsihi basirah, wa law alqa ma'adhirahu' (Rather, man, against himself, is a witness, even if he presents his excuses). Man knows his own soul well, no matter how many excuses he makes. Now, let me present two or three Hadith very quickly. Here, the Mawla of the believers (a.s.) says, and Imam Sajjad (a.s.) says—read this one year later. In the explanation of this verse, he says that one of them is: 'No one else will perform my deeds.' The eldest son has certain duties, but it is not on anyone else. But the eldest son has the duty to perform the Qada prayers and Hajj of the father. Allah has placed it on the eldest son. Whether others do it, Allah accepts it, that is a different matter. But in today's age, no one accepts anything, and no one does anything. So the Imam says, 'I know no one will perform my deeds, so I must perform my deeds myself.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Prepare, prepare. This life is serious. This life is not a game or a pastime. This worldly life...' I go from the sun into the shade. Tell me, how was this 2,500-year journey? It felt just like coming from the sun into the shade. That is how it felt. And those who are elderly, those who are old, they know. You ask them, it feels like it was yesterday. Life passes by so fast. But Satan does 'Tajzeen' (makes it seem easy); he makes you feel relaxed. If you keep your burden light, you will reach your destination quickly. If your burden is light, you will reach your destination quickly. The more burden you have, the more attachments you have to the world, the harder it is to carry it on your back. The more burden you have, the harder it is to carry it on your back. This is common sense logic; there is nothing else to it. If you give a man a small mouse to carry, he will feel the burden. If you give him 25 kilos and tell him to walk a kilometer or two, he will walk. But if you give him 100 kilos, how long will he walk? But for his wife and children, who are not going to support him, he thinks he must fulfill their needs, but not more than that, and he should not ruin his hereafter. So why does the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say, 'Keep the burden light'? Because ahead of you is a steep slope to climb. These are the words of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It is a slope, an ascent, and it is very steep. No one can cross this journey except those whose burden is light. Only they can do it, and no one else who is full of the world's burden and sins for the hereafter. It is not just the burden of the world, but the burden of sins. The burden of sins will be very heavy for them. Verification, verification, and hard work. Look, we repeat this so that the youth remember. The word 'Ijtihad' is used in Arabic for the time when a person gets exhausted from working. That is why our scholars who study a lot and are experts are called 'Mujtahid', because they study day and night, work hard, and research, and only then do they issue fatwas and issue orders in the light of traditions. The world, what does it command? And the destination of 'Tasawwuf' (spirituality), you can collect it. This is the place; once your eyes close, then there is no problem. Once your eyes close, there will be no problem. It doesn't take time for the eyes to close. Many people have gone before us, we also have to go, and many people will come after us. That is why it is said, what does it command? That Allah has not created anything that is absolutely certain, yet people doubt it the most. Allah has not created anything that is certain, yet people behave as if it is doubtful, as if it is not going to happen, and they do not believe in it. Like death; no one trusts death. We always think that everyone else will die, but we are here. Look, you all have to grow old. Everyone who came before you was ruined by the affairs of this world and left. Mawla says, Allah's permission cannot be attained until a person works hard. They used to work very hard, and that is why their numbers were so few. Others were just talkers, but not workers. In the path of Wilayah, when there are no people to strive (Jihad), and that is why Allah gives 'Tawfiq' (divine guidance/opportunity) only to those who work hard. In a tradition narrated by Ayyub—Ayyub is also a very great companion—look, you often hear names that people don't know because they are called, in the science of Hadith, 'Majhul al-Qadr'. These people were the representatives of two Imams; the tenth and eleventh Imams. Whoever understands them is a scholar; otherwise, we add 'Allama' to our names, that is a different matter, isn't it? There are many who are fond of... That is a different matter, isn't it? Many have a passion for it, like 'What is my name? Allama'. That is a different thing, but if a very great scholar says someone is a scholar, then by Allah, when they narrated a Hadith, you could trust them 100%. Zameer and the others were companions of the three Imams before them. They were companions, and both are reliable. So, narrate traditions from them. Imam Reza (a.s.) says that if seven things are not accompanied by seven other things, then a person is making a mockery of himself. If he does not work hard, he is making a mockery of himself. He is making a mockery of himself. He says, who is Masoom (infallible)? And from this, it is known that Tawfiq is in the hands of Allah, not in our hands. Yes, there is no Tawfiq because of us. Are we the ones to distribute Tawfiq? It is possible that someone else has better Tawfiq than them, so a person can seek Tawfiq, but Allah gives Tawfiq. So, what is the meaning of Tawfiq? Tawfiq means 'Wafaq' (to align/accord). When it happens, it means the youth is granted 'Tawfiq'. In Arabic, it is derived from the word 'Wafaq'. When Allah aligns all the links together, that is called Tawfiq. When all the links are connected, a person cannot even speak, their tongue stops working, they become bedridden, and it is all over. Therefore, a person should always pray for Tawfiq because the one who grants Tawfiq is Allah. No one else grants Tawfiq except Allah. But along with Tawfiq, one must also work hard. We cannot just sit at home doing nothing and say, 'O Lord, give me sustenance, O Lord, give me sustenance.' Allah will provide sustenance, but that person is making a mockery of themselves; they are a fool. Go, work hard, strive, and reach your destination quickly. This is a book for the youth. For success in any field, you must look at what your goals are and what obstacles will come. The Hadith has explained this to us as well. Who are the enemies of hard work? The first thing is sleep. Whoever has a love for sleep in their heart will never be successful. In English, it is said, 'Burning the midnight lamp.' Until you burn the midnight lamp, you will not achieve success. Unless you work hard in that manner, look at what the Hadith says. There is an entire chapter in the Hadith books, 'The Chapter of Sleeping,' and there are many Hadiths. 'Inna Allah yubghidu kathratan-nawm' (Verily, Allah dislikes excessive sleep). Now look at what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Avoid excessive sleep, avoid excessive sleep. Why? Because excessive sleep will make the sleeper a pauper on the Day of Judgment. On the Day of Judgment, they will be a pauper and needy.' The paupers are those who sleep too much. Young men ask, 'What is the meaning of sleeping too much?' In the Hadith, it is written that to set a jungle on fire, how big a spark is needed? Then they used to read, and when the spear was being pulled out of his chest, it had pierced deep inside. The spear had pierced deep into his chest, so people asked his son how it happened. He said he used to sleep while keeping a book on his chest; he would fall asleep while reading. Read his life history, read the biographies of the scholars; this sleep is a very bad thing. The second thing is laziness. The Imam (a.s.) says that laziness is a calamity for success. There is a lot of potential, but nothing is achieved in life with just potential. We have seen many people who had a lot of potential but could not achieve anything because of laziness, and we have seen many people who had no potential but succeeded through hard work. Therefore, it is necessary. And then the third thing, look at these two things, we are on the topic quickly, stay away from bad friends. Look, keep the company of friends who help you achieve your goals, and if you even slightly sense that someone is pushing you away from your goals—'Oh, it's useless, don't do it, what will you get by working? Come on, let's go watch a movie, let's lighten up'—stay away from such people. The Imam (a.s.) says, look what a strange time it is, the Imam (a.s.) says... Always keep friends, but keep good ones. You should have hand-picked friends. These things shape a person's personality. Just like in English, if you want to see what a person is like, look at the people they are with. If they are all loafers, understand that this person is also a loafer. If educated people are with them, or hardworking people, understand that they are also like that because friends will not let them be anything other than what they are. This is very important; it shapes a person's personality. It is a separate topic. And lastly, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) says that never postpone any action that you need to achieve. Do not delay it. 'I will do it tomorrow.' The time for prayer has come, go immediately. Whatever time it is, do it now. If you have to study, study now. Who has seen the 'later'? The Imam (a.s.). If a person does not fulfill their rights—neither the rights of Allah, nor the rights of their wife and children, nor the rights of their friends, nor the rights of this world, nor the rights of the hereafter—then the person who has the habit of saying 'I will do it later,' such were the individuals who gathered around him. Even the effect of iron would not work on such people. Even the effect of iron, arrows, spears, or swords would not work on them. Why? Because they were so deeply immersed in the love and Wilayah (guardianship) of the Imam that they were unaffected by anything. There was one martyr who had not been struck by any arrow until the Imam completed his prayer. As soon as the Imam finished his prayer, saying 'Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh,' it is written in the Maqtal that he was martyred on one side. On the other side, the Imam placed the martyr on his lap. The martyr first asked, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, did I fulfill my duty? Did I fulfill the right or not?' Look at what the level was! Such were these individuals. Today, I have to recite the martyrdom of such a young man, a child, who, when he heard that Hussain (a.s.) was not there, sat in a corner and started crying, saying, 'Why is my name not there?' Look at the longing for martyrdom! Strange people they were. Look at the longing. He was crying, and suddenly he remembered that when his father was leaving this world, he had tied an amulet to his arm. When he was leaving the world, he tied an amulet to his arm and said, 'Open this amulet when you are in trouble and read it; the solution to your problem will be in it.' Qasim thought, 'What could be a bigger trouble than this?' As soon as Qasim opened the amulet, it was written in it, 'O my son Qasim, when you see your uncle Hussain in trouble, go and help him.' Qasim came, took the amulet, and came smiling, saying, 'Uncle, this is my father's writing.' When Hussain (a.s.) saw the writing, he said, 'Qasim, you have not come with your father's writing, but you have brought the message of your own death.' He said, 'Uncle, it is my father's writing.' Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Qasim, your name was also in the list of martyrs; I just didn't mention it. Otherwise, Qasim, you are not the only one; Ali Asghar will also be martyred.' So, while Qasim was happy that he would attain martyrdom, hearing the name of Ali Asghar made his heart tremble. He asked, 'Uncle, will Ali Asghar come to the battlefield?' Hussain (a.s.) was worried that if he said no, he would be lying, and if he said yes, he would be bringing Ali Asghar. He said, 'Qasim, you got worried about this? This thought, this love, this is not something that will come to the battlefield.' This thought, this love, this is not something that will come to the battlefield. Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) was watching how the day of Ashura was unfolding. The morning of Ashura came, the noon of Ashura came. Now, when the sequence of the martyrs of Bani Hashim began, it is written in the Maqtal—listen carefully—that after that, Qasim, the son of Hassan (a.s.), came. He was a young boy, his beard had not yet grown. When Hussain (a.s.) saw that Qasim was ready to fight, he embraced Qasim. Both uncle and nephew began to cry until they both fainted. When someone faints, water is sprinkled on them, but today it is the tragedy of Zainab (s.a.). The tears were sprinkled. When he regained consciousness, Qasim said, 'Uncle, give me permission.' Hussain (a.s.) did not give permission. Qasim would sometimes kiss the hands of Hussain (a.s.) and sometimes fall at his feet, kissing them, saying, 'Uncle, give me permission.' Then Hussain (a.s.) gave permission. Now, when Qasim departed, in what state did he leave? He mounted his horse. He was not wearing armor. Qasim was crying and lamenting, saying, 'If you do not recognize me, then know that I am the son of Hassan (a.s.). I am the son of the Prophet Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). This is Hussain (a.s.) whom you have besieged and made a prisoner, depriving him and his children of water. May Allah do to you such that you never get the water of Paradise.' Qasim says that he was like a piece of the moon. And think, if Qasim was like this for the enemy, how must he have been for his mother? Qasim, even at this age, sent at least 35 people to Hell. It is written in the Maqtal that one soldier saw that the lace of Qasim's shoe had come undone. The lace of his shoe came undone. As Qasim bent down to tie his shoe, an enemy struck Qasim on the head with a weapon. Qasim cried out, 'O Uncle, come to my aid!' When the sound reached Imam Hussain (a.s.), he rushed like a lion and fell upon the enemy. But by the time he arrived, Qasim's body had been trampled. Qasim said his final farewell. May Allah grant healing to those who are ill, may He settle the debts of those who are in debt, may He grant us the opportunity to perform Hajj, and may He protect the holy places. Protect the holy places, protect those who are in need, protect our families, the Lakhani family, and all our families.

title: Qayaamat Mein Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.) Ka Apni Ummat Se Sawaal (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture highlights a profound tradition from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir regarding the Day of Judgment. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explains that he will be the first to appear before Allah, followed by the Holy Quran and his Ahlulbayt. He will then question his Ummah on how they treated these two weighty trusts. The talk concludes with a prayer for guidance to remain steadfast in following the Quran and the Ahlulbayt to ensure salvation.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) has stated that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'On the Day of Judgment, I will be the first to appear before the Almighty Lord, followed by His Book (the Holy Quran) and my Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and then my Ummah will come. I will ask them: What did you do with the Book of Allah and my Ahlulbayt?' O Allah, grant us the guidance and ability to hold fast to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in this world, so that we are not ashamed before Your Prophet on the Day of Judgment. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds.
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) will be the first to stand before Allah on Judgment Day.
The Holy Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will accompany the Prophet.
The Prophet will hold his Ummah accountable for their actions regarding the Quran and his family.
Holding fast to the Quran and Ahlulbayt is essential for success in the afterlife.
The speaker emphasizes the importance of avoiding shame before the Prophet on the Day of Resurrection.

title: Paighambar (s.a.w.a.) Ka Janasheen Kaun? Ek Yemeni Wafd (Delegation) Ka Waqeah
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual impact of the Prophet's companions and the profound emotional reactions of those who encountered them. The speaker reflects on the transformative nature of these interactions, suggesting that witnessing such figures offers a glimpse into the reality of the hereafter. The discourse emphasizes the importance of spiritual recognition and the clarity of heart required to perceive divine truth amidst worldly confusion.
content:
They look at the screen and ask, 'Who is your companion?' They say, 'Stand up from here.' When people like Jafar come, when they enter this room or this mosque, you will see and understand that this is the world of the hereafter. This is the second [realm]. I have your mother... [The speaker describes a sequence of events regarding delegations and reactions, noting that upon seeing them, their hearts began to beat faster and tears began to flow from their eyes, signifying a deep spiritual recognition]. Is it in the heart, watching your mind? So friends, today your mind is confused.
The presence of the Prophet's companions serves as a bridge to understanding the hereafter.
Spiritual recognition often manifests through physical signs like tears and a racing heart.
The world of the hereafter is reflected in the character and presence of righteous individuals.
Human confusion often stems from a lack of spiritual focus and clarity.
True understanding requires looking beyond the surface to the state of one's heart.
