title: Saamarrah aur Shahadat e Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the spiritual significance of the city of Samarra as the home and resting place of Imam Ali al-Naqi and Imam Hasan al-Askari. It recounts the final days and martyrdom of the 11th Imam, highlighting his connection to the birth of Imam Mahdi. The speaker emphasizes that despite historical attempts by enemies to destroy these holy sites, the light of the Ahlulbayt remains eternal. The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi to establish justice and avenge the injustices faced by the Prophet's family.
content:
The problem... [unclear]... in the Samarra, the waiting... 1968, the main task of the Muslims, the main... only change... Ram Mohan Kwatra list... Prime Minister Modi... hello, hello... [unclear]... and suddenly you want that your Muhammad Bukhari, the team there, Sanjay... [unclear]... the village ceremony... this tradition is also called 'Surur-e-Man-Raa'. 'Surur-e-Man-Raa' means whoever saw it became happy. That is why a believer's heart feels an indescribable joy when he goes to Samarra. But while on one hand, Samarra is a source of joy for the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), on the other hand, this place has always been a target for the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). When the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) got tired of taking revenge on the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), they took revenge on their followers or their holy shrines. But despite all the oppression and tyranny of the hateful, narrow-minded people, today this magnificent, glorious shrine of Samarra... This magnificent, glorious shrine of Samarra is pointing towards some verses of the Holy Quran: 'Yureeduna an yutfi'u noorallahi bi-afwahihim wa ya'ballahu illa an yutimma noorahu wa law karihal kafiroon' (They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it). One thing worth noting is that in the shrines of all the Imams (a.s.), and especially in the shrine of Samarra, there is one thing: Samarra is not only the shrine of the Imams, but it is also the house of the Imam. This is the same house where Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) lived. It is the same house where the Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), was born. When the time of the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) was approaching, he gave some instructions to his servant, Abu al-Adyan. Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) told Abu al-Adyan that your journey would take 15 days, and when you return, the voices of mourning will welcome you from this house of mine. When Abu al-Adyan returned to Samarra after 15 days, the martyrdom of Imam al-Askari (a.s.) had already taken place there. His statement is that I saw the body of the 11th Imam (a.s.) in that... I saw the body of the 11th Imam (a.s.) kept in the room where he used to pray. After some time, the family of the Imam (a.s.) performed the Namaz-e-Janaza and buried him beside his father, Imam Naqi (a.s.). May the curse of God be upon the killers of Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Regarding the martyrdom of the 11th Imam, it is found that he was poisoned on the 1st of Rabi al-Awwal, and the Imam spent eight days in agony. The narrator states that in his final moments, when the 11th Imam was picking up the cup for water, his hand was trembling. Today, 8th Rabi al-Awwal, on the occasion of the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), we offer our condolences to Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Is it not that in Samarra, the Imam of the time is also waiting for his followers and pilgrims to come and offer condolences for the martyrdom of his father? Today is the day when the followers of the Imams have raised their steps towards their master, and it has been 12 years since they have been performing these rituals, but the mourning of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) continues to this day. He is still waiting for the command of the Lord of the Worlds. Not only him, but the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), Fatima Zahra (s.a.), and all the Imams (a.s.) are waiting... Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), Fatima Zahra (s.a.), and all the Imams (a.s.) are waiting for their last descendant, Mahdi, to come and take revenge for every injustice done to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and fill this world, which is full of oppression and tyranny, with justice. My Lord, on this day of the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and every injustice done to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), may Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) appear and grant us the opportunity and guidance to join him in taking revenge from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

title: #6 - Anbiyaa (a.s.) Ka Waaris Aur Wasi Kaun? | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of Imam Hussain (a.s.) as the rightful heir to the Prophets, as referenced in Ziyarat-e-Waritha and Ziyarat-e-Arba'een. The speaker explains that the Imams inherited the divine knowledge and scrolls of previous Prophets, serving as the ultimate proof of God on earth. The session emphasizes that Imam Hussain (a.s.) acts as a ship of salvation, requiring both love for him and disavowal of his enemies for true guidance.
content:
A'udhu billahi sami'il alimi minash shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir rahmanir raheem. Wa sallallahu alaika ya waliyyal asr adrikna wala tuhlikna. Assalamu alal Husaini wa ala Aliyibnil Husaini wa ala awladil Husaini wa ala as-habil Husain. In Ziyarat-e-Waritha, Imam Hussain (a.s.) is declared the heir of the Prophets (a.s.). The phrases of Ziyarat-e-Arba'een also point towards this: 'Wa ash-hadu annaka qad tahammalta mawarithal anbiya'i wa ja'altahu hujjatan ala khalqika minal awsiya'i' (And I bear witness that you have carried the inheritance of the Prophets and made him a proof over your creation from among the successors). O Lord! You granted him the inheritance of the Prophets (a.s.) and made him a proof over Your creation among the other successors. Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) says that surely the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) was granted the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa. Then the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) entrusted them to Ali (a.s.). He handed them over to Imam Hassan (a.s.), and he handed them over to Imam Hussain (a.s.), until these books reached us. It is clear from this Hadith that all our Imams (a.s.) are the heirs of the Prophets (a.s.). Since this earth can never be devoid of the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda), that is why God sent Prophets and Imams (a.s.) for the guidance of humanity. One example of the inheritance of the Prophets (a.s.) in Imam Hussain (a.s.) is that just as God Almighty made the Ark of Nuh (a.s.) a ship of salvation, similarly, Imam Hussain (a.s.) is that Proof of God whom God has made a lamp of guidance and a ship of salvation. Just as boarding the Ark of Nuh (a.s.) was the cause of salvation, similarly, without boarding the ship of Imam Hussain (a.s.), without loving him and seeking guidance from him, no one can find salvation. Along with this, it is also necessary to express disavowal (Bara'at) from those who did not board this ship and opposed it, i.e., all the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). It is absolutely clear that whoever is pleased with the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the government of Yazid will never be able to board the ship of salvation because they are not walking on the path shown by the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.). We pray in the court of the Almighty God that He grants us the ability to remain attached to Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his mission until our last breath, and to always remain on the ship of salvation through his mourning (Azadari) and his Ziyarat, and never make us a supporter or partisan of the opponents of this ship of salvation. Ameen ya Rabbal Alameen. Jin ya balak ya habibi wa ahbab fidak Hussain.

title: Majlis 6 | Marefat-e-Nooraaniyyah (Part-5) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual status and divine knowledge of Imam Ali (a.s.) within the context of the Marefat-e-Nooraaniyyah. It delves into the theological concepts of Ilm-e-Ghayb, the Knowledge of the Book, and the essential role of Wilayah in the acceptance of faith. The discourse also connects these lofty spiritual truths to the tragic events of Karbala, highlighting the sacrifice of Qasim ibn Hasan as a model for youth and the importance of instilling religious devotion in future generations.
content:
Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. When the King of Karbala set out for the battlefield, there was a cry of doomsday in the tents. When the King took his daughter in his arms, she cried and asked him again: 'Father, will you tell me, will you be able to forget Sakina? Will you be able to forget Sakina? Your throat is so dry, there is no strength left to sigh. How will you sing lullabies? Will you be able to forget Sakina? You controlled your emotions, you held back your tears. How will you hide the wounds of your heart? Will you be able to forget Sakina? And there is no one left, Father. You yourself have brought the corpse. Oh, whom will you call for your sake? Will you be able to forget Sakina? And let me see your face one last time. Why am I certain, Father, that you will not return after leaving.' Will you be able to forget Sakina? And send Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Rahimallahu man qara al-Fatiha. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best disposer of affairs. The best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. And the end is for the righteous and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of the prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. May Allah send blessings upon him and his infallible family, whom Allah has kept away from impurity and purified with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Peace be upon the Baqiyatullah (Remnant of Allah) on the earth, the Imam of the Time, the Master of our Affair, our Master, our Mawla, our Beloved, our Physician, our Companion, our Guide, the Fortress of Protection, the Succor of the Distressed, the Straight Path; may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our Master and our Chief, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) said: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn has wounded our eyelids and caused our tears to flow, so...' So, for the likes of Husayn, let the weepers weep. Our Master and Chief, Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) has spoken the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. The hadith that I have chosen for this series of gatherings, in it Imam Rida (a.s.) says: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn has wounded our eyelids'—meaning Ashura, the grief of Husayn has wounded our eyelids—'and caused our tears to flow'—and has made us weep, has made us weep profusely—'so for the likes of Husayn, let the weepers weep.' The discussion was regarding the Hadith of Marifat-e-Nuraniyah (Recognition of the Light). I began by stating that the Imam said if people were aware of the reality of creation, if the Shia were aware of the reality of creation, there would be no disagreement among them. The cause of their disagreement is that they are not aware of the reality of creation. And then the discussion reached the point, as I submitted to you yesterday, that when Surah al-Bara'ah was revealed, which is also called Surah al-Tawbah, the Prophet first sent someone else, and then sent the Master of the Universe (Ali) to go and take it from him and announce it himself. When that person came to the Prophet and began to question, he felt very bad. Surely, as I submitted to you yesterday, it was a matter to feel bad about. So he felt bad and came and asked, 'Has any verse been revealed regarding me?' The Prophet said, 'No, rather the command was given that no one shall deliver this except you yourself, or one who is from you.' Meaning, 'Except me or Ali, or Salman or Jundab.' He said, 'Labbayk, O Messenger of Allah.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'O Salman, O Jundab, the one who is not fit to carry a scroll to deliver it on behalf of the Messenger of Allah, how can he be fit for Imamate? How can he be fit for this position, which is such a great position?' It is absolutely clear that when you are not fit for a small task, when you are not worthy of being given a small task, how can you be given a great task? It is a perfectly clear example. After that, the Mawla says, 'O Salman and O Jundab, I and the Messenger of Allah were one light. The Messenger of Allah, Muhammad al-Mustafa, became the Messenger, and I became his successor, al-Murtada.' In this way, the light was divided into two parts. 'O Salman, Muhammad became the Munzir (Warner), and I became the Hadi (Guide).' And this is the word of Allah, Azza wa Jall; Allah Azza wa Jall says: 'You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.' Meaning, generation after generation, there will be an Imam who will continue to guide the people. Allah has kept this entire system, this order. 'And for every people there is a guide.' So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is the Warner, and I am the Guide. After that, he says: 'And I am the Master of the Preserved Tablet (Lawh-e-Mahfuz).' Allah, Azza wa Jall, has inspired me with the knowledge of what is within it. Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! With a loud voice, Nara-e-Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Now, it is possible that children and young people may not understand what is meant by the 'Master of the Preserved Tablet.' So look, the knowledge of Allah, the 'active knowledge' (Ilm-e-Fi'li) which is the created knowledge of Allah, which Allah has created, Allah divided that knowledge into two parts. 'Indeed, Allah has two types of knowledge.' One is called Umm al-Kitab (Mother of the Book), and one is called Ilm al-Kitab (Knowledge of the Book). Umm al-Kitab and Ilm al-Kitab. Meaning, there is one knowledge that Allah has not given to anyone; Allah has kept it only to Himself. And Ilm al-Kitab is the knowledge that, as it is in the hadith, 'He taught it to His Prophets,' to His Messengers and Successors, He taught it to them, and we know it. So this is the Ilm al-Kitab. In other words, Umm al-Kitab is called the Preserved Tablet (Lawh-e-Mahfuz), and Ilm al-Kitab is called the Tablet of Effacement and Affirmation (Lawh-e-Mahw-o-Isbat). Meaning, the Tablet of Effacement—'Mahw' means to erase, and 'Isbat' means to rewrite. Meaning, in these two books, in one—the Mahw-o-Isbat, which is the Ilm al-Kitab—destinies are written, and destinies are erased. Allah writes destiny, and Allah erases destiny. It happens many times that it depends on the behavior of the servant, on a person's character, or a person's worship, or a person's prayers, etc. Meaning, this is the knowledge in which Allah keeps changing destinies. Changes keep happening in it. Allah keeps making changes, He changes destiny. For example, a person's death is written; suppose his death is written for tonight. It is written that this person is going to die tonight. But what does that person do? He gives charity (Sadaqah). When he gives charity, Allah likes charity so much—this act is so pleasing to Allah—that Allah postpones his death. For example, He postpones it for three years. How much He erases is in Allah's authority. Or it may be that Allah has written his death, and he goes and performs Silat al-Rahm (maintaining family ties). He goes and meets his relatives. And the relatives with whom the ties were broken, with whom there was no conversation, he ends that, goes and says, 'Brother, let it go, forgive me, if I have made a mistake, forgive me.' Just like that, but 'Brother, do not do this, that you break ties, this is not right.' Allah likes this act so much that Allah increases his lifespan. This is Mahw-o-Isbat—Mahw means to erase, Isbat means to write. So Allah has kept this law in which changes keep happening. And He has kept another law in which everything is written. Meaning everything—meaning what? Everything means that first, it is written in it that Allah will keep his death for tonight. Then he will go and give charity, then Allah will postpone his death. Everything is written in it. His death was written, but he goes and meets his relatives, he will perform Silat al-Rahm with them, so Allah will postpone his death for three years. So everything is written in the Preserved Tablet. There is no change in it. In which, usually, it is written in the hadith that usually Allah has given this knowledge... ...to no Prophet or Angel, nor to any Successor. Usually, this is the principle, but in the Hadith of Nuraniyah, Amir al-Mu'minin says—Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali!—Allah has given me this knowledge too. Allah has made me the master of it. Now I know what will happen, from where the destiny will change, how whose destiny will change, what will happen from which action. Subhan Allah! That is why whenever anyone came before the Mawla, the Mawla would look and understand. A man came, many narrations exist regarding this, hadiths exist. A man came and said, 'Ya Ali, inni uhibbuka wallah' (O Ali, I swear by Allah, I love you). He said, 'Kazabta' (You are lying). You are lying. He said, 'O Ali, I am swearing by Allah, I love you,' and you are saying, 'You are lying.' Now look, why, why is he saying that? He is saying, 'Ali, I love you,' but in reality, he does not even recognize Ali. There is no Marifat (recognition) of Ali at all. So he says, 'Ya Ali, I am telling you, I love you,' and you are saying, 'You are lying.' He said, 'Wallahi inni uhibbuka' (By God, I love you). The Maula (a.s.) again said, 'You are lying.' Now he became a bit annoyed, saying, 'Ya Ali, I am saying repeatedly that I love you, and you are repeatedly saying I am lying.' The Maula (a.s.) said, because it is found in the traditions that the Aimma-e-Masumeen (a.s.) possess such knowledge that as soon as they look at a person's forehead, their entire life appears before the Imam. And whether this person is a Momin or not, the Imam knows everything. Everything. So, the Maula (a.s.) knows what this is. The Maula (a.s.) said, 'You say you love me, but when souls were meeting one another in the Alam-e-Zarr (the world of particles), the souls of the Momineen gathered in one place, and you were not there at that time. Where were you then? If you were there when the souls were meeting, shaking hands, and talking, you were not among the Momineen.' Meaning, your soul was wandering among the hypocrites. And today, you come here and claim to have faith. You are telling Ali (a.s.). So, it is written in the traditions that he got up and left silently. And there are many such incidents, many. And such extraordinary incidents, if you just read about the Ilm-e-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen) of the Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.). A woman and her husband had a fight. They had a fight. She came to Amirul Momineen (a.s.) to seek justice. She said, 'My husband did this, my husband did that.' The Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) heard her entire story. After hearing the whole story, the Maula (a.s.) told her, 'The fault is yours. You should not have behaved this way with your husband. You were ill-mannered, meaning you treated your husband with bad manners.' He did not give the verdict in her favor. So, she became angry. She said, 'Ya Ali, I came to seek justice. You do not give justice. Your verdict is completely wrong.' And in the end, she said, 'Even Allah is not pleased with your verdict.' As soon as she said that—now the sentence of the Hadith is amazing, I won't be able to read the whole Hadith, there is a reason for that—the Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) stared at her forehead. And he used a few titles for her. One of those titles was, 'O foul-mouthed one. O foul-mouthed one. O you who hurl abuses.' And the Maula (a.s.) used three or four such words for her. And then, in the end, the Maula (a.s.) made such a comment about her, about her personal life, that she fled from there. She fled and left. A hypocrite ran after her. Amr ibn Huraith. He was a hypocrite, his name was Amr ibn Huraith. He ran after her, after that woman. And he said, 'Hey, you did such a great thing. You came and spoke like that to Ali. My heart was so happy when you spoke to Ali like that. But Ali said a little something to you, and you left and fled. Why did you do that?' Meaning, in other words, he was egging her on. That she did very well. She said, 'Ali told me something about myself that neither my parents know, nor does my husband know.' That, Ali told me. That is why I chose to flee from there. This is what they call Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Meaning, he is fully aware. Now, pay attention. He says, 'Allah alhamani' (Allah inspired me). Forgive me, now see, the same point comes up again, which we bring proofs for repeatedly because people object. They say, 'This Hadith is not authentic, you are reading from it.' It is clear, isn't it? What is the objection? That the Hadith is not authentic. Firstly, we have already answered that, brother, who are you to decide it is not authentic? Allah Alhamani has narrated it in Bihar al-Anwar. Allah Alhamani says my noble father narrated it, he narrated it from a very ancient book in which he found the Hadith, he narrated it from there. This is one proof. Secondly, the contents of the Hadith are being stated, which an ordinary human being cannot state. If an ordinary human being could state such contents, it would have appeared in the books of others by now. It would have appeared, but its absence is proof of this. It is proof that this Hadith is authentic. Anyway, this is one proof, or rather, two proofs. Now, let us present another proof; if you do not accept this Hadith, then fine, we will bring another one for you. You will accept that, won't you? Now look, there is Surah Ar-Ra'd, Surah number 13 of the Quran. Its last verse is verse number 43. The Quran says, 'Wa yaqululladhina kafaru lasta mursala' (And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger'). It is addressing the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Who is Allah addressing? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.). 'Yaqululladhina kafaru lasta mursala. Qul' (Say, O Prophet, tell them), 'Kafa billahi shahidan baini wa bainakum wa man indahu ilmul kitab' (Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book). Between me and you, two witnesses are sufficient. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is saying to whom? To those who did not believe. Listen. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is addressing the disbelievers, addressing the polytheists, that you do not believe in my Prophethood? Do not believe. There are two witnesses between me and you. There are two witnesses. Who are the two witnesses? Now, he is Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.), the Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin (Seal of the Prophets), the Ashraful Anbiya wal Mursalin (Most noble of prophets and messengers). Obviously, he will not bring just any random person to be a witness. And don't you see? Now, the position is so great, so the witness must also be equally great. You are not understanding the point. You are listening very silently, very calmly. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and Ale Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. It is raining outside, it is getting cold inside. Strange, recite one more Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. It is a tremendous verse. They say you are not a messenger. O Prophet, tell them. 'Qul kafa billahi shahidan baini wa bainakum wa man indahu ilmul kitab.' Allah is sufficient as a witness. Hey, if Allah Now, if you don't believe, this is the second one, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). If you want to take testimony, take it from him, ask whatever you want, he will tell you right now. About whom do you want to ask? Do you want to ask about ancestors? Or do you want to ask about future generations? Ya Ali. Ya Ali. 'Wa man indahu ilmul kitab' (And whoever has knowledge of the Book), he possesses the entire knowledge of the Book. From the beginning to the end, whatever you want to ask, this is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) could have said, 'Ask me.' Is it clear to you or not? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) could have said, 'Ask me.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not say, 'Ask me,' he said, 'One is Allah and the second is Ali.' If you don't believe him, then here stands Ali, ask him. That child went into a corner and started crying because his name was not in the list of martyrdom. His name was not there. He started crying, 'Why is my name not in the list of martyrdom? Why did my uncle not take my name?' And what was he doing? He was crying. While crying, suddenly a thought came to his mind that when his father was departing from this world, his father had tied an amulet (ta'wiz) on his arm and said, 'Son Qasim, when a very great calamity comes, open this amulet and read it. Look at this amulet. The solution to your calamity will be present in it.' Qasim thought, what could be a greater calamity than this? Qasim opened the amulet. Now, when he saw, it was written in it: 'Bunayya Qasim, izraka ammakal Hussain.' (My son Qasim, assist your uncle Hussain. Be of help to your uncle. Help your uncle.) He was a 13-year-old child. As soon as he read it, a smile appeared on his face. He took that very letter and went and handed it over to the Imam. As soon as Hussain (a.s.) read his brother's letter, tears flowed from his eyes. 'Son Qasim, you have not brought your brother's letter; you have brought the message of your own death.' 'Ma Qasim, oh son Qasim, your name was in the list of martyrdom. I just didn't mention it. Otherwise, your name is also in the list of martyrdom. Qasim, tomorrow you too will be martyred, and Qasim, what can I tell you? Not only you will be martyred, but your younger brother Ali Asghar will also be martyred.' And when Qasim heard this news of his martyrdom, he was very happy. But hearing the name of Ali Asghar there, the honorable child of Bani Hashim was once stirred. He asked in agony, 'Ya Ammah, will these wicked ones enter the tents? Will they enter the tents?' That they will kill my brother Ali Asghar? Hussain (a.s.) said, 'No Qasim, they will not kill Ali Asghar in the tent, rather I will take Ali Asghar in my arms, and they will martyr him there.' As soon as Qasim heard this, Qasim was reassured that the wicked ones would not enter the tents. I would say, 'O honorable child of Bani Hashim, today you are so concerned that the wicked ones should not enter the tents. Oh, come and see the evening of Ashura. Ask the heart of Sayyid-e-Sajjad (a.s.), he is seeing the scene with his own eyes that the wicked ones are entering the tents. They are snatching the veils of the ladies. They are looting everything else, setting fire to the tents.' Anyway, the evening of Ashura came, after the Zuhr prayer, when the sequence of sacrifices of Bani Hashim came, Qasim came once, stood before Hussain (a.s.), 'Uncle, give me permission, Uncle, give me permission.' How could Hussain (a.s.) give permission? Qasim is the sign of my brother, how can I give permission? How can I give permission? There is a sentence in the Maqtal, there is a sentence, I don't know if we will be able to express it or not, but a strange sentence is found that as soon as Qasim saw that Hussain (a.s.) was not giving permission, he took both of Imam Hussain's hands. After taking his hands, he placed both his eyes on Hussain's hands and started rubbing them. 'Uncle, give me permission, Uncle, give me permission.' He insisted so much that Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Go Qasim, I have given you permission.' Now Hussain (a.s.) himself prepared Qasim. After Qasim was fully prepared to go to the battlefield, Hussain (a.s.) once hugged Qasim, and it is written in the Maqtal that both uncle and nephew cried so much, cried so much, cried so much that both fainted. Mourners, now you tell me with justice, today if someone faints, what do you do to bring them to consciousness? You sprinkle water on them. Alas, Zainab! What should Zainab do? See the helplessness of Zainab, she sprinkled tears. When he regained consciousness, Zainab said, 'Brother, now let Qasim go, do not stop Qasim now.' Hussain (a.s.) gave permission to Qasim, gave permission to Qasim, now he mounted him on the horse. Before leaving, Hussain (a.s.) said once, 'Wait a minute,' he stopped Qasim for a moment and tore Qasim's collar. He said, 'Uncle, what is this?' He said, 'Son, this is a sign of orphans. Perhaps the wicked ones might have some mercy on you.' Qasim went to fight, while fighting, a strange phrase is found in the Maqtal that Qasim sent many wicked ones to Hell. Many wicked ones, just once while fighting, the strap of Qasim, the strap that was there, the horse's rein, the stirrup that was in it, got stuck. Now when someone attacked, Qasim fell from the horse in such a way that half his body was on the horse. When half his body was on the horse and half below, the horse took Qasim among the wicked ones. Now as soon as he took him among the wicked ones, someone struck with a sword, someone threw a stone, someone struck with a spear, they did it to such an extent that Qasim came down. When he came down, people started trampling Qasim's corpse. Qasim called out, 'Ya Ammah, adrikni' (O Uncle, reach me), 'Uncle, come, my ribs are being broken.' Hussain (a.s.) ran, just as a hawk attacks, Hussain (a.s.) ran, attacked the wicked ones, reached near Qasim, but by the time Hussain (a.s.) reached, Qasim's corpse had been torn to pieces. Hussain (a.s.) gathered the corpse in his cloak. Wa Qasima, Wa. 'Wa saya'lamul-ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun.' 'Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz-zalimin.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, count us among his helpers and supporters. Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain (a.s.). Count us all among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Those who are sick, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the high scholars and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Whoever protects them, You protect them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Grief of Imam Husayn
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the profound sorrow of the Ahlulbayt regarding the tragedy of Karbala, citing Imam Rida on the necessity of weeping for Imam Husayn.

chapters.title: The Criteria for Imamate
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the capacity to carry out divine commands is a prerequisite for Imamate, using the example of the delivery of Surah al-Bara'ah.

chapters.title: The Light and Knowledge of Ali
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the station of Imam Ali as the Guide and his unique access to the Preserved Tablet, distinguishing between Umm al-Kitab and Ilm al-Kitab.

chapters.title: Divine Knowledge and Recognition
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how the Imams possess deep insight into human souls and destinies, illustrating this with the Imam's ability to discern true faith.

chapters.title: The Ilm-e-Ghayb of Imam Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts an incident where Imam Ali (a.s.) demonstrated his knowledge of the unseen by revealing personal truths to a woman, highlighting his divine insight.

chapters.title: Imam Ali (a.s.) as the Witness of the Quran
chapters.summary: The lecture analyzes Surah Ar-Ra'd, verse 43, identifying Imam Ali (a.s.) as the one possessing 'knowledge of the Book' who serves as a witness alongside Allah.

chapters.title: The Knowledge of the Book and Asif ibn Barkhiya
chapters.summary: The speaker contrasts the miracle of Asif ibn Barkhiya, who possessed partial knowledge of the Book, with the absolute knowledge possessed by Imam Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: The Vast Knowledge of Ali ibn Abi Talib
chapters.summary: The speaker contrasts the limited knowledge of Asif ibn Barkhiya with the infinite ocean of knowledge possessed by Imam Ali.

chapters.title: The Encounter Between Musa and Khidr
chapters.summary: The lecture recounts the story of Prophet Musa and Prophet Khidr to illustrate the hierarchy of divine knowledge and the humility required before Allah.

chapters.title: The Parable of the Bird and Divine Knowledge
chapters.summary: A parable involving a bird and four drops of water demonstrates that all prophetic knowledge is negligible compared to the knowledge of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

chapters.title: The Manifest Book and the Angels
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the nature of the Kitab-e-Mubeen and how it contains all deeds, even those hidden from the recording angels.

chapters.title: Ali ibn Abi Talib as the Great News
chapters.summary: The lecturer explains that Imam Ali is the 'Great News' (An-Naba' al-'Azim) mentioned in the Quran, emphasizing that acceptance of his Wilayah is the defining factor of faith.

chapters.title: The Pillar of Religion and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The lecturer asserts that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Straight Path and the Pillar of Religion, stating that no act of worship is accepted without his Wilayah.

chapters.title: The Status of Ali as Heir and Divider
chapters.summary: The lecturer discusses titles of Imam Ali from Ziyarat, such as the Heir of the Prophets and the Divider of Paradise and Hell, highlighting his authority in salvation.

chapters.title: Taqwa, Guidance, and the Meaning of Wilayah
chapters.summary: The lecturer connects the concept of Taqwa and the 'Firmest Handhold' to the Wilayah of Ali, using Ayat al-Kursi to explain how the Wali of Allah leads believers from darkness into light.

chapters.title: The Importance of Teaching Progeny
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the necessity of educating children about the Ahlulbayt and the events of Karbala to ensure they remain connected to the light of Islam.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Qasim ibn Hasan
chapters.summary: The narrative recounts the emotional story of Qasim ibn Hasan, his discovery of his father's letter, and his eventual martyrdom at Karbala.

chapters.title: The Final Farewell and Sacrifice
chapters.summary: The lecture describes the heart-wrenching farewell between Imam Hussain and Qasim, followed by the tragic details of Qasim's death on the battlefield.

title: MOHSIN E ISLAM (a.s.) GRAND QUIZ 2022 | Presentation and Live Quiz on Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture presents a comprehensive defense of the faith of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), arguing that he was a true believer and a devoted guardian of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Through historical analysis, theological arguments, and the examination of Prophetic conduct, the session refutes claims of his disbelief while emphasizing his role in the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt. The program also incorporates the spiritual significance of the Hadith of the Cloak and provides guidance on the true meaning of worship and preparation for the hereafter.
content:
Hey la, hey la, hey la... Hey la, hey la, hey la... In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance and our relief through them, and send blessings upon them all. From Fatimah al-Zahra (a.s.), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), she said: I heard Fatimah say, 'My father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), entered upon me one day and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Fatimah.' I said, 'And upon you be peace.' He said, 'I feel a weakness in my body.' I said to him, 'I seek refuge in Allah for you, O my father, from weakness.' He said, 'O Fatimah, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it.' So I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it, and I began to look at him, and his face was shining as if it were the full moon in its perfection and completeness. It was only an hour later when my son Hasan (a.s.) approached and said, 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I said, 'And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said, 'O mother, I smell a pleasant scent with you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Yes, your grandfather is under the cloak.' Then Hasan approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah. Do you permit me to enter under the cloak with you?' He replied, 'And upon you be peace, O my son and master of my pond (Hawd), I have permitted you.' So he entered under the cloak with him. Only a moment had passed when my son Husayn (a.s.) approached and said, 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied, 'And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said to me, 'O mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said, 'Yes, your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak.' Husayn approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather. Peace be upon you, O one whom Allah has chosen. Do you permit me to be with you both under the cloak?' He replied, 'And upon you be peace, O my son and intercessor of my nation, I have permitted you.' So he entered under the cloak with them. Then Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abi Talib approached and said, 'Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah.' I replied, 'And upon you be peace, O Abu al-Hasan and O Commander of the Faithful.' He said, 'O Fatimah, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah.' I said, 'Yes, he is here with your two sons under the cloak.' So Ali (a.s.) approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' 'Do you permit me to be with you under the cloak?' He replied, 'And upon you be peace, O my brother, my successor, my caliph, and the bearer of my standard, I have permitted you.' So Ali entered under the cloak. Then I approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O father, O Messenger of Allah. Do you permit me to be with you under the cloak?' He replied, 'And upon you be peace, O my daughter and my part (Bidh'ah), I have permitted you.' So I entered under the cloak. When we were all gathered under the cloak, my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), took the two ends of the cloak and gestured with his right hand toward the sky and said, 'O Allah, these are the people of my house (Ahl al-Bayt), my elite, and my close ones. Their flesh is my flesh, and their blood is my blood. What pains them pains me, and what saddens them saddens me. I am at war with those who war against them.' And peace to those who are at peace with them, and an enemy to those who are hostile to them, and a lover of those who love them. They are from me and I am from them. So grant Your blessings, Your favors, Your mercy, Your forgiveness, and Your pleasure upon me and upon them, and remove impurity from them and purify them with a thorough purification. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, 'O My angels and O residents of My heavens, I have not created a built heaven, nor a spread-out earth, nor a shining moon, nor a luminous sun, nor a rotating sphere, nor a flowing sea, nor a sailing ship, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak.' The trusted Jibra'il asked, 'O Lord, and who is under the cloak?' The Mighty and Majestic replied, 'They are the people of the house of Prophethood and the mine of the Message: they are Fatimah and her father, her husband, and her sons.' Jibra'il asked, 'O Lord, do You permit me to descend to the earth so that I may be the sixth with them?' Allah said, 'Yes, I have permitted you.' So the trusted Jibra'il descended and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. The Most High, the Exalted, sends you greetings, honors you with salutations and respect, and says to you, 'By My Might and Majesty, I have not created a built heaven, nor a spread-out earth, nor a shining moon, nor a luminous sun, nor a rotating sphere, nor a flowing sea, nor a sailing ship, except for your sake and your love. And He has permitted me to enter with you. So do you permit me, O Messenger of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah said, 'Peace be upon you, O trusted one of Allah's revelation. Yes, I have permitted you.' So Jibra'il entered with us under the cloak. He said to my father, 'Indeed, Allah has revealed to you, saying: 'Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.' Ali said to my father, 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me, what is the merit of our sitting here under the cloak in the sight of Allah?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'By the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me with the Message as a confidant, this news of ours is not mentioned in any gathering of the people of the earth, in which there is a group of our Shia and lovers, but that mercy descends upon them, the angels surround them, and they seek forgiveness for them until they disperse.' Ali (a.s.) said, 'Then by Allah, we have succeeded, and our Shia have succeeded, by the Lord of the Kaaba.' My father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), said, 'O Ali, by the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me with the Message as a confidant, this news of ours is not mentioned in any gathering of the people of the earth, in which there is a group of our Shia and lovers, and among them is one who is distressed, but that Allah removes his distress, nor one who is sorrowful, but that Allah dispels his sorrow, nor one who is seeking a need, but that Allah fulfills his need.' Ali (a.s.) said, 'Then by Allah, we have succeeded and attained bliss, and likewise our Shia have succeeded and attained bliss in this world and the hereafter, by the Lord of the Kaaba.' I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Guardian of the Era (Wali al-Asr), help us and do not let us perish. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, for Your representative, the Proof (al-Hujjah), son of al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, be a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside in Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. We hope that you are all well, and we pray that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the sake of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), protects our lives, wealth, honor, and dignity, and grants us all the courage and success to sacrifice our lives and wealth in the defense of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.). We welcome all of you to the third round of TSR's famous and well-known program, 'Mohsine Islam Grand Quiz.' Let us all together offer our congratulations to the court of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) on the birth of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) with a loud Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Before we begin the discussion, let us inform you that at the end of this program, there will be a quiz containing some questions related to this program, the answers to which you will find in this presentation. There is no special prize or reward for answering quickly this time, so listen to this presentation with great patience and answer all the questions correctly at the end. Those who answer correctly will have some winners chosen through our computerized lucky draw system, and those winners will receive these prizes. Before moving the program forward, we request all of you that if you have not yet subscribed to this channel, i.e., TSR The Strong Walk's YouTube channel, please do so now, and do not forget to press the bell icon for notifications. Although we have made the quiz link live, you can see all those questions, and for their answers, listen to our presentation very carefully. Through the 'Mohsine Islam Grand Quiz,' we try to provide answers to questions raised about the personality and faith of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) through the Holy Quran and the traditions of the family of Muhammad (a.s.). In today's presentation, we will try to answer some such objections, Insha'Allah, and our brother, Janab Danish Rizvi Sahab, will assist us in this. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. And Janab Abbas Patel Sahab, Assalamu Alaikum Abbas. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. We offer you both congratulations on the birth of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.). Congratulations to you as well, and congratulations to the viewers on this blessed birth. So viewers, let us begin this discussion with that tradition from the book 'Al-Kafi' which is from Dawud al-Raqqi. Dawud al-Raqqi comes to Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) and... complains about someone to whom he had lent some money, and he was not returning it. Imam (a.s.) listens to his complaint and says, 'Go to Makkah, and after going to Makkah, perform Tawaf and offer two rak'ats of prayer on behalf of Janab Abd al-Muttalib (a.s.). After that, perform Tawaf again on behalf of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) and offer two rak'ats of prayer, and do the same on behalf of Janab Abdullah (a.s.), Janab Amina (s.a.w.a.), and Janab Fatimah bint Asad (s.a.w.a.). And after that, pray; Insha'Allah, you will find that your debt or your money will be returned to you.' Dawud al-Raqqi does exactly that; he immediately goes to Makkah, performs Tawaf, and says, 'As soon as I was at the door of Safa, I saw the same person who had borrowed my money and was not returning it; he comes before me and says, 'O Dawud al-Raqqi, you have cornered me, here is your money.'' So viewers, we see three things from this tradition. The first thing is that seeking the solution to one's problems directly from the Imam of one's time, the Proof of Allah (Hujjat Allah), is not Shirk; rather, it has been the way of the companions of the Imams. Yes. The second thing is that making the friends of Allah (Awliya Allah) a means (Wasilah) to pray is also not Shirk; rather, it is among the teachings of the Imams, and through this, our prayers can be answered quickly. And Abu al-Hasan brother, among these five personalities you mentioned in this tradition, one thing that is found is that they were either the parents of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) or his guardians. Yes. And the most important among them, whom we have gathered here to mention today, is the Benefactor of Islam, Janab Abu Talib (a.s.). Various objections are raised against him regarding his faith. Yes. But if the opponents look at their own book, in fact, their greatest book, Sahih al-Bukhari, they bring a Hadith from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that 'I and the guardian of the orphan will be in Paradise,' and the Messenger then gestures with his fingers like this. This is to show that I and the guardian of the orphan will be in Paradise like this. Meaning, completely together. Completely together. Yes. And in Surah Ad-Duha, verse number six, the Lord of Majesty says: 'Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?' Here, the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) is being reminded that he was an orphan and was given shelter. So Zahid Bhai, this orphan—meaning not just any ordinary orphan as you described—Ali ibn Ibrahim (R.A.) narrates in his book that 'al-yatimu alladhi la mithla lahu' (the orphan who has no equal), these were such an orphan who had no parallel. Meaning, we are talking about the Messenger of Allah here; there was simply no one like him. 'Wa lidhalika summiyat' (and because of this it was named) 'Durrat al-Yatimah' (the unique pearl), meaning he was called a unique orphan. That is why he was called this; 'Durra' (pearl) is used as an example. Exactly. So Abbas Bhai, our point was that a Hadith from Bukhari was mentioned earlier, that if any ordinary person takes care of an ordinary orphan, they will be in Paradise with the Messenger. Yes. And if someone takes care of the Messenger himself, how could they be in Hell? What a reward the opponents have given to Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.) for taking care of the Messenger of Allah. They sent the one who protected him to Hell, and those who attacked his door were made the Caliphs of the Messenger. So viewers, it is possible that due to prejudice against Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.), and due to hatred and enmity, someone might object that he did not recite the Kalima. But no one can deny that Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.) was the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (S.A.W.A.), and the testimony of this is present in the Holy Quran itself. Certainly, Abul Hasan Bhai, not only Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.), but Janabe Fatima bint Asad (S.A.) was also involved in this guardianship. Indeed, indeed. And just as those five personalities mentioned in the first narration you brought from Al-Kafi are present, the fact that Janabe Fatima bint Asad remained in the marriage of Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.) until the very end is itself a very strong proof of Janabe Abu Talib's (A.S.) faith. Could you clarify this a bit for the viewers? This is because in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 221, it is stated: 'Wa la tankihu al-mushrikati hatta yu'min' (Do not marry polytheist women until they believe). Do not marry polytheists until they become believers. Meaning, it is a clear command of Islam that a believer cannot remain in marriage with a polytheist. Although this is a Meccan verse, revealed in Mecca, and after this verse was revealed, even the scholars of the Ahl-e-Tasannun—for example, Haythami in his book 'Majma'—narrated that when this verse was revealed, because according to their belief, the Messenger of Allah had many daughters, among whom was Zaynab, and Zaynab's marriage had taken place with Abul-Aas ibn Rabi. Haythami writes in his book that 'Wa kana al-islamu qad farraqa bayna Zaynab binti Rasulillahi (S.A.W.A.) wa bayna Abil-Aas ibn Rabi' (And Islam had separated Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, and Abul-Aas ibn Rabi). Meaning, when Islam came—specifically when this verse was revealed—the Messenger of Allah separated Zaynab bint Rasul and Abul-Aas ibn Rabi due to Islam, and their marriage became void. Yes. Yes. And Haythami further writes that when the Messenger of Allah (S.A.W.A.) migrated to Medina, Zaynab was with him, and Abul-Aas ibn Rabi remained in Mecca. But no such matter regarding Janabe Fatima bint Asad (S.A.) and Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.) is narrated anywhere in history. Yes. Yes. And it is not found in any book that the Messenger of Allah caused a separation between Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.) and Janabe Fatima bint Asad after this verse was revealed. So, either the opponents should admit that the Messenger of Allah (S.A.W.A.) did not act upon the verses of the Quran, or the opponents should accept that Janabe Abu Talib (A.S.) was a believer. Yes. Absolutely. And their marriage remained intact with Janabe Fatima bint Asad (S.A.) until the very end. No historian in any book of history has mentioned that the Messenger of Allah spoke of any separation between these two. Yes. Yes. Although in their own books, it is narrated in very clear words that the Messenger of Allah established a separation between Zaynab and Abul-Aas ibn Rabi after this verse or this command was revealed. title: Khaana-e-Kaaba Mein Ibaadat Bhi Radd! Kyun? | خانہ کعبہ میں عبادت بھی رد! کیوں؟
excerpt: This lecture highlights the supreme importance of Wilayah (allegiance to the Ahlulbayt) as the essential condition for the acceptance of worship. Citing a narration from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.), the speaker explains that even centuries of intense worship performed in the most sacred location, the Holy Kaaba, will be rejected if the individual lacks the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt. The talk emphasizes that spiritual deeds are only fruitful when accompanied by the correct spiritual leadership and devotion to the Imams.
content:
[Music] A'udhu billahi sami'il 'aleem min ash-shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Raheem. Wasallallahu 'ala waliyyika. Janab Abu Hamza al-Thumali (r.a.) narrates that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) asked us which place is the most virtuous. We said Allah, His Messenger, and the son of the Messenger know best. Then he (a.s.) said that the most virtuous land is between the Rukn and the Maqam, meaning in the Holy Kaaba, the place between Rukn-e-Yamani and Maqam-e-Ibrahim. Then he (a.s.) said, if a person gets a long life, as much as Hazrat Nuh (a.s.) spent among his people, i.e., 950 years, and in that life, if that person fasts during the day and spends the whole night in worship at that place, i.e., between the Rukn and the Maqam, but then meets Allah (Azza wa Jall) without our Wilayah, then this worship will not benefit him at all. Here, we want to present an important point to you that there are various places in the world that have their own respect and importance, such as Makkah Mukarramah. Such as Makkah Mukarramah, where offering two rak'ats of prayer is more virtuous than offering two rak'ats of prayer in any ordinary place. In such a respected place, if a person worships for the duration of Hazrat Nuh (a.s.)'s preaching life, but if he does not have the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then worshiping on such a great and blessed land will not benefit him. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds to hasten the reappearance of the heir of the Kaaba, Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the opportunity to perform Hajj and Ziyarat while remaining steadfast on the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.
The area between Rukn-e-Yamani and Maqam-e-Ibrahim is the most sacred spot in the Kaaba.
Worship performed for 950 years is insufficient if the person lacks Wilayah.
Wilayah is the fundamental prerequisite for the acceptance of all religious deeds.
Makkah holds special status, but location alone does not guarantee the acceptance of worship.

title: EP04 | ‘Maula’ Yaane Dost? | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 💐
excerpt: This lecture provides a deep linguistic and theological analysis of the term 'Mawla' as used by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) during the event of Ghadir Khumm. It challenges the common interpretation of 'Mawla' as 'friend,' arguing instead that it denotes divine authority and leadership, supported by Quranic evidence and historical context. The session also incorporates an interactive quiz format to engage participants in understanding the significance of Imam Ali's (a.s.) succession.
content:
Haider, Haider... [repeated]... TSR presents. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Ya Ali Madad. We are present once again to serve you with another episode of 'Ghadir, the Divine Scale,' and we welcome you all to this episode. Come, honorable viewers, let us begin today's episode with these lines: The hand of the Prophet and the Lion of God, Ya Ali Madad. The solver of the problems of humanity, Ya Ali Madad. When we said it, we became accused of blame. In Khaybar, the Prophet himself said, Ya Ali Madad. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjat son of Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. Honorable viewers, first of all, let us tell you a few things about the 'Ghadir, the Divine Scale' Mega Quiz. There will be seven episodes, and in each episode, a discussion regarding Ghadir and the Wilayat of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) will be presented to you, which will be the basis for the quiz questions. In each episode, there will be seven lucky winners who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. The first prize is 5,000, the second two prizes are 3,000 each, and the third four prizes are 1,000 each. And finally, our mega prize for the 'Ghadir, the Divine Scale' Mega Quiz is the one that every lover of Ali (a.s.) desires in their heart—to go to the threshold of their Mawla and bow their head in submission, that is, a pilgrimage to Iraq. Yes, viewers, the mega prize is a pilgrimage to Iraq, which will be announced in a special episode after this series concludes. To be eligible for the mega prize of the Iraq pilgrimage, one must watch all seven episodes and participate in the quiz of each episode, and you must provide correct answers to all questions in at least five out of the seven episodes. From among all such individuals, the winner of our mega prize, the Iraq pilgrimage, will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. We hope that you will stay with us throughout this series and keep participating in every quiz. The quiz link will be activated as soon as each episode begins, and the link is present in the live chat and description of this video. At the end of each episode, there will be Ziyarat-e-Aminullah. Immediately after the Ziyarat, the seven lucky winners of the episode will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. We request you to listen to our episodes carefully and answer all questions correctly. Honorable viewers, in the previous episode, all the verses of the Holy Quran presented to describe the characteristics of the Caliph prove one thing: that all those verses apply to the sacred person of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.). And the event of Ghadir-e-Khumm is that event in Islamic history which is 'azharum minash shams' (brighter than the sun), where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) declared Ali (a.s.) as the Mawla and Imam of the people in the plain of Ghadir-e-Khumm in broad daylight, in the presence of 125,000 pilgrims. In his hadith, he stated, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyunil mawla' (Of whomsoever I am Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla). And this is such a continuous and authentic hadith that no Muslim can escape from it. But those whose hearts Allah has sealed, who are the manifestation of 'khatamallahu ala qulubihim'—what can they do? To escape from this Wilayat, they twist and turn this hadith. They say that here, 'Mawla' means friend, that the Messenger of Allah declared Ali (a.s.) as the friend of the Muslims. Our scholars have answered this objection in various ways on multiple occasions. Today, we too will have the honor of presenting a few points on this very topic of the word 'Mawla,' for which our brothers are present in this gathering: Mr. Abul Hasan Syed Sahib and Mr. Abbas Nahid Sahib. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. Abul Hasan Bhai, we would like you to start the discussion on the word 'Mawla.' We would like you to present some points for our viewers through a few aspects regarding this word 'Mawla.' Insha'Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As you said, this objection, this point that the word 'Mawla' is used in the sense of 'friend,' is not new. This is not a new objection, but our scholars and our zakireen have answered it many times. And it will be our humble student-like effort to convey the true and real meaning of the word 'Mawla' to you in the light of traditions and the Quran. So, we will divide this topic into five parts. First, we will look at the linguistic meaning of the word 'Mawla,' because as per the custom, when a word is analyzed, when a word is discussed, it becomes necessary to refer to the dictionary and see what meanings have been given to it. So, first, we will look at its linguistic meaning. After that, we will see if the word 'Mawla' has been used in the Holy Quran, and then we will turn to the traditions to see if this word has appeared in hadiths, and if it has, in what sense it has been used in the Quran and hadith. And since this is about the Hadith of Ghadir—'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyunil mawla'—we will see if the word 'Mawla' is used in the sense of 'friend' in this hadith or in some other sense. And finally, we will see if any Caliph has used it, if any Caliph has called himself a Wali or a Mawla. So, come, viewers, let us see what the linguistic meaning of 'Mawla,' its dictionary meaning, its literal meaning, is. The word 'Mawla' is derived from the word 'Walayah,' from which other words are also formed, such as Wali, Wilayat, Walayat, etc. So, there is a famous and well-known book by Ibn Manzur called 'Lisan al-Arab,' which is a very famous dictionary. In it, these meanings of the word 'Mawla' have been given: that a Wali and a Mawla is called one who is a guardian and who has authority over people, and who possesses the right of disposal. Along with this, similar meanings are stated in Ibn Athir's book 'An-Nihaya', where it is written that whoever has complete authority over people, or 'Wilayat-e-Mutlaqa' (absolute guardianship), is called 'Mawla'. This makes it very clear that in dictionaries, we do not find the meaning of 'friend' clearly anywhere, but rather 'Wali' and... in the sense of authority, meaning one who has complete authority and the right of disposal (Haq-e-Tasarruf) is called 'Mawla'. Yes, Gulzar Bhai, so this covers the linguistic meaning of 'Mawla', which is authority and the right of disposal. Abbas Bhai, we would like you to clarify for the viewers how the word 'Mawla' has been used in the Holy Quran. Yes, Gulzar Bhai, just as you presented the linguistic meanings, the Quran also contains verses in that same sense and according to those same meanings. If we look at several occasions, Allah has used this word 'Mawla'. However, here we would like to benefit from only two verses. The first verse is the 51st verse of Surah At-Tawbah, in which the command of the Lord of Honor is: 'A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Qul lan yusibana illa ma kataballahu lana'—meaning, O Messenger (s.a.w.a.), say that no calamity will ever befall us except what Allah has written for us. What is stated further in the verse? 'Huwa Mawlana'—meaning, He is our Mawla. 'Wa 'alallahi falyatawakkalil-mu'minun'—and the believers should rely only on Allah. So, if we look, the word 'Mawla' appears in this verse with the same meaning, i.e., one who has the right of disposal over us. If we look for confirmation of this, it is also mentioned in a famous and well-known commentary of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, 'Tafsir al-Baghawi', while discussing the word 'Mawla', that it refers to the one who has more right over our life and death than our own selves. Meaning, the right of disposal (Haq-e-Tasarruf). The right of disposal. Along with this, if we look at the second verse, which is verse number 15 of Surah Al-Hadid: 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim, Fal-yawma la yu'khadhu minkum fidyatun wa la minalladhina kafaru'—meaning, on the Day of Judgment, neither will any ransom be accepted from you nor from those who chose disbelief. 'Ma'wakumun-naru hiya Mawlakum wa bi'sal-masir'—and your abode is the fire of Hell. 'Hiya Mawlakum'—meaning, Hell is your Mawla, and what a wretched destination it is. So, viewers, if we take the meaning of 'Mawla' in this verse as 'friend', it would mean that the fire of Hell would become a friend to the deniers of the faith, which is absolutely wrong. Its purpose is to burn the deniers, not to embrace them as a friend. Along with this, if we look at the meaning of the word 'Mawla' in Sahih Bukhari and its commentary written by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, 'Fath al-Bari', we find that it refers to 'Awla' (more entitled). Meaning, Hell is not a friend, but Hell has authority. Here, it is about the right of disposal, not friendship. So, viewers, after the linguistic meaning, we have also seen that in the two verses of the Holy Quran presented to you, 'Mawla' is used to mean authority or the right of disposal. Let us see how the word 'Mawla' appears in Hadith and what meaning is attributed to it. We would like Abbas Bhai to present further discussion on this. Yes, Gulzar Bhai. Just as 'Mawla' appears in the Holy Quran in the context of authority and the right of disposal, we find similar concepts in the traditions as well. Yes. For example, once again we will take the help of the famous books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, one of which is known as 'Sunan Abi Dawud', which is considered quite authentic among them. In its 'Kitab-un-Nikah' (Book of Marriage), when the mention of a 'Wali' comes—the chapter regarding the Wali—that if a woman marries without the permission of her Wali, her marriage is void. And in this tradition, it is found that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) emphasized three times that this marriage is void. Now, the point to consider here is, if we look at the word 'Wali' used here, in what sense is it used? Is it used in the sense of a friend? Yes. Think about it—if we were to interpret it as 'if a woman marries without the permission of a friend, her marriage is void', then which people would a woman have to go to for permission? Here, it is absolutely proven that the word 'Wali' used here is in the sense of a guardian, not in the sense of a friend. Yes, indeed, Abbas Bhai. If this Hadith is considered, no explanation is provided here, but the occasion and context in which the word 'Mawla' appears in this Hadith is more important to look at, and from that manner, one can determine what 'Mawla' means here. Indeed. You said it absolutely right, Gulzar Bhai. And let us look at another Hadith which is from Sahih Bukhari, where it is stated by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that there is no believer over whom I do not have 'Awlawiyat' (more entitlement) in this world and in the hereafter. Here too, the word 'Awla' is used, and here 'Awla' means authority, the right of disposal. And after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'If you wish, read the Quran,' and then he recited verse number 6 of Surah Al-Ahzab, which is as follows: 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim, An-Nabiyyu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim'—and the Prophet has more authority and right of disposal over the believers than their own selves. Yes, indeed, Gulzar Bhai. Abbas Bhai, as we saw the linguistic meaning of 'Mawla' is authority and the right of disposal, and as the opponents claim that 'Mawla' means friend, this meaning might also exist. So, what is the proof that the 'Mawla' we are discussing here means authority and the right of disposal? This is a very good question, Gulzar Bhai. We find in the book 'Al-Ghadir' that the late Allama Amini (may Allah have mercy on him) brought 27 different meanings of the word 'Mawla', and he proved that the declaration of Wilayat at Ghadir could only mean the right of disposal and Wilayat, and no other meaning could fit that occasion. Subhan Allah. And if we look to prove this further, we will try to provide some arguments here, God willing. The first argument we would like to present here is the words of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the question he asked the people at that time, which the Ahl-e-Sunnah books themselves—namely Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Majah—have recorded. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked the people present there: 'Alastu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim?'—'Do I not have more authority over the believers than their own selves?'—the same meaning we saw in the sixth verse of Surah Al-Ahzab. The question of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was similar to that. Meaning, those over whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had more authority than their own selves, after the declaration of Ghadir, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) has more authority over them than their own selves. Indeed. And Abbas Bhai, then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed: 'Allahumma wali man walahu', which many people translate as 'O Allah, keep him as Your friend who keeps Ali as his friend.' But the most correct meaning of this would be: 'O Allah, be his Mawla, be his Wali, who considers Ali as his Mawla, who considers Ali as his Wali.' What a statement. Subhan Allah. Subhan Allah. So, viewers, this is a matter of great consideration that usually this prayer is translated as 'O Allah, be a friend to him who keeps Ali as a friend,' but when the Hadith preceding this prayer uses the word 'Mawla' in the sense of authority, the right of disposal, and Wali, then in this prayer too, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would use the same meaning. This is truly a matter of deep thought. Indeed. Indeed. And I really do not understand why people take the meaning of 'friend'. Think for yourself, does an ordinary person ever announce their friendship in this way? Does anyone ever cause trouble and then announce their friendship? Here we see that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stops 125,000 pilgrims—in fact, pilgrims who were tired and exhausted after performing Hajj—and then makes a pulpit of saddles, and then gives a long sermon, and then says this, just this much: 'Whoever's friend I am, this Ali is also his friend.' No, it is not like that; rather, this is a declaration of Wilayat, a declaration of his successorship. And along with this, another thing that can come to a person's mind is: was Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) an enemy to all these people before this? That the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is now saying, 'No, from today Ali has become everyone's friend.' And it is also worth noting that today many people discuss the word 'Mawla' in the sense of 'friend' and I don't know what else. So my question to them is, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was calling Ali (a.s.) 'Mawla' in a gathering of 125,000, there must have been some people among them—two, four, ten— who would ask, 'Do we not mean friend here by Mawla?' None of them objected, meaning it was absolutely clear to all of them that 'Mawla' here means 'Wali', the person who has complete 'Wilayat-e-Mutlaqa' (absolute guardianship), the complete right of disposal. Meaning, just as the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has more authority over our souls than we do, in exactly the same way, Ali (a.s.) also has more authority and the right of disposal over our souls. Gulzar Bhai, if we look, this declaration of Wilayat has troubled those who lived in hatred of Ali in every century so much that a veil has fallen over their intellects, and they have committed strange follies just to remove this matter from people's minds—that this is about Wilayat, this is about 'Tasarruf' (disposal). For example, there is an incident from the eighth year of Hijri, the incident of Buraydah in Yemen, where some people went and complained about Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and people link it to the event of Ghadir, saying the event of Ghadir was a result of that. Whereas there is no connection between the two, no relation at all. But because of frustration and hatred, those people keep trying to confuse others. Meaning, to take the meaning of 'Mawla' as 'friend' in this Hadith, they bring an incident from before—the incident of the eighth year of Hijri—and link it to the tenth year of Hijri. And dear viewers, let us tell you that the detailed explanation of this incident of Buraydah has already been covered in our previous episode on 'Objections to Ghadir'. You can listen to this incident in its entirety by clicking the link in the description. Yes, along with this, let me also tell you that as soon as this declaration of Ghadir was made, when this sermon ended, it was declared: 'Man kuntu Mawlahu fahadha Aliyun Mawlahu', immediately after that, a long series of congratulations began. One after another, they started coming to congratulate Ali (a.s.) on becoming their Mawla, and Umar ibn al-Khattab also congratulated him with these words: 'Bakhin-bakhin laka ya Ibne Abi Talib'—'Congratulations, congratulations to you, O son of Abu Talib! Today you have become our Mawla and the Mawla of all Muslims.' So now, this is a matter of reflection: if this issue were only about friendship, why would everyone come and offer congratulations? Meaning, everyone understood the word 'Mawla' that today Ali (a.s.) has become our Mawla, our Wali. Now he has complete authority over us, over our souls, and he has attained the complete right of disposal. Indeed, Gulzar Bhai, and after the congratulations, what happened? The series of giving allegiance (Bay'ah) began. Yes, it is found in the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni scholars) themselves that it lasted for three days. As we see that Al-Tabari has described this matter in his 'Kitab al-Wilayah' in this way: 'Wa kana awwalo man safaha al-Nabi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi wa sallam wa Aliyan Abu Bakrin wa Umaro wa Uthmano wa Talhato wa Zubayro wa baqil muhajirina wal ansara.' Meaning, the first ones to shake hands and pledge allegiance (Bay'ah) to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Talha, Zubayr, and the other Muhajireen and Ansar. Yes, Tabari further wrote that then all the people gave their pledges. So much so that the Dhuhr and Asr prayers were offered together there. And the process of Bay'ah started again. Meaning, after the Dhuhr prayers, the process of Bay'ah resumed, which continued until the Isha prayers, meaning until the Maghrib and Isha prayers. And the Maghrib and Isha prayers, i.e., the Isha'ayn prayers, were also offered together at that time, and this process continued for three days. So, let us pay attention here as well. Congratulations are being offered, pledges are being given, so would all these things happen just because someone became a friend? Gujjar Bhai, you have stated a very interesting point here that while the process of Bay'ah was going on for three days in the field of Ghadir-e-Khumm, the pilgrims had no other preoccupations. This is a strange stage; there is no possibility of rain here, no heavy crowds, no fear, no preoccupation, yet the prayers were offered together, and that too for three days. So, this proves that offering prayers together is a sign of the people of Ghadir, and those who are Ghadiri remind people of Ghadir by offering prayers together. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. And those who offer prayers separately have either forgotten Ghadir or are trying to hide Ghadir. Subhan Allah, absolutely correct. Gujjar Bhai, let me tell you another interesting point: if the meaning of 'Mawla' is only 'friend', then why did Harith bin Nu'man come to the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) and ask whether this command was from Allah or from you? Because as soon as this announcement was made, 'Man kuntu Mawlahu fahadha Aliyun Mawlahu', this news spread like wildfire in all the cities. And when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came to Medina, Harith bin Nu'man asked him, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have heard that you have made Ali (a.s.) the Mawla at Ghadir-e-Khumm.' You said that we testified to the Oneness of Allah. You said, 'Call me the Messenger, accept my Prophethood,' and we did. We obeyed all your commands regarding Hajj, Zakat, Khums, and Jihad. So, this matter of you making Ali (a.s.) the Mawla is not making sense. Tell me, is this command from Allah or from you? So, the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) said that this command is undoubtedly from Allah. But this cursed man still did not believe. He repeated the same question and asked again, 'Tell me, is this command from Allah or from you?' The Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) said again that this is Allah's command. At that moment, that cursed man prayed in the Divine Court, 'O Lord, if he is speaking the truth'—meaning even then he did not believe the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.)—'then send down a stone upon me from the sky right now, send a punishment upon me.' So, it is a matter of reflection here that if the word 'Mawla' only meant 'friend', then the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) would have stepped forward and said, 'Brother, this is just a matter of friendship, it is just a small matter that you have to consider Ali (a.s.) as a friend. Why are you asking for punishment? Why are you asking for destruction?' But nothing like that happened, and the punishment came immediately from Allah, and this cursed man was sent to Hell. Gujjar Bhai, another point arises here: if the word 'Mawla' had only come in the meaning of 'friend', then why would the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) be seen presenting this event of Ghadir as proof of his Caliphate on various occasions? Correct. Whether it was the Shura, or Rahba, or various other places where the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) presented this event of Ghadir and the announcement of Ghadir as proof of his Caliphate to the people. Meaning, the word 'Mawla' does not mean 'friend' here at all, otherwise Ali (a.s.) would never have done such a thing. Indeed. It is not such a small matter to present as evidence just to announce friendship. Indeed. And along with this, we also see that not only the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) but other rulers also used the word 'Wali' to prove themselves the successor of the Prophet. So, dear viewers, in the 2020 Ghadir Objections series, we had a detailed discussion on this topic regarding the places where Hazrat Ali (a.s.) presented protests through Ghadir. You can also watch this video by clicking the link in the description. In the book of Muslim, we find that when the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib went to demand Fadak, what did he say? 'Ana Wali-u-Rasulillah.' 'Ana Wali-u-Rasulillah wa Wali-u-Abi Bakrin.' Meaning, I am the friend/successor of the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) and Abu Bakr. Meaning, they are using it in that way. Dear viewers, think for yourselves. It is so strange that when we see a Hadith where the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) is using the word 'Mawla' for Ali (a.s.), people very calmly and easily say that the word 'Mawla' here means friend, and when their own Caliphs use this word for themselves, it is used in terms of succession, authority, and Wilayah. So, really, look at this hypocrisy. Rather, I would say this is nothing but hatred for Ali (a.s.), that in their hatred, as soon as they see the word 'Mawla', it becomes 'friend', and this is their love for the Caliphs, that when it is used for them, they see succession and Wilayah in it. A historian cannot present even the falsest of narrations where the word 'Mawla' has been used for any other companion.
