title: Kya Baraa’at Aur Tabarra Ek Nahin Hain? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explains the theological concepts of Bara'at and Tabarra within Shia Islam, clarifying their relationship and necessity. The speaker defines Bara'at as the internal distancing from the enemies of the Ahlul-Bayt, while Tabarra is the outward expression of that hatred. It emphasizes that these concepts are foundational to the belief in Imamate and are supported by Quranic principles regarding the rejection of Taghut.
content:
Al-roz-e-azal ta roz-e-qiyamat, ay bar dushman-e-ahle-bait. Bara'at means to distance oneself from someone with one's heart, and the expression of this hatred and distance is called Tabarra. For example, the belief in Tawheed is that we distance ourselves from any god other than Allah with our hearts. The Kalima 'La ilaha illallah' is the expression of this belief. Similarly, Bara'at is a part of our belief in Imamate, which has two foundations. One is to accept the Wilayah and Caliphate of the twelve successors after the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.), and to distance oneself from all the opponents and enemies of those twelve Imams and to send curses upon them, as found in the Ayat al-Kursi of the Holy Quran: only the one who rejects Taghut and believes in Allah can hold onto the firm rope of Allah. Taghut refers to those who usurped the rights of the Ale-Muhammad, and the firm rope of Allah is the Wilayah of the twelve Imams.
Bara'at is the internal distancing from the enemies of the Ahlul-Bayt.
Tabarra is the outward expression of hatred toward those who opposed the Imams.
The belief in Tawheed requires distancing oneself from false gods, similar to how Imamate requires distancing from its enemies.
The Kalima serves as an expression of the belief in Tawheed.
Imamate is built on two pillars: accepting the Wilayah of the twelve Imams and rejecting their opponents.
Ayat al-Kursi highlights the necessity of rejecting Taghut to truly believe in Allah.
Taghut is interpreted as those who usurped the rights of the Ahlul-Bayt.

Why is the light of Fatima being discussed? So that when people reach the Sirat (the bridge), they carry that light with them. And then, [music]... and then, they quote the mosque, saying that some people are taking notes, but if they take them, they will say, 'Did you really come to the contact?' It is understood that this is about the hypocrites. They are on the Sirat, but they will be deprived of the light. So, they will say, 'Can we get the light to cross the Sirat?' And it will be said to them, 'Go back, go back!' And they are not just saying 'go back,' they are saying, 'Go back and ask them...' Go back and ask them for the light. [Applause] You can read the 80,000-year-old narrations yourself. Listen to the time, and then go and ask them for the light. Do not come here; this is the Sirat. After that, there will be the reckoning—the accounting. And whatever complaints there are, they will be settled without account. Now look, when they read such narrations, what do they say? They say, 'Allah is the witness.' Some people objected, saying, 'Do you read these Hadith? People will become misguided.' The answer is, 'We should have thought before the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke.' Oh, I see. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke incorrectly, and Allah... Allah spoke incorrectly? You should have thought before writing the Hadith, 'What am I writing?' You should have thought before writing what you are writing, which will cause people to go astray. [Music] You people become so good, so pious, that you forget your own status. You start thinking that you will enter Paradise based on your own deeds. By Allah, if anyone thinks that without Wilayah, without the Wilayah of Fatima, they can even smell the fragrance of Paradise, they are living in a delusion. Is there anyone equal to Fatima who will enter Paradise? So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Salman, and listen to this Hadith: 'O Salman, whoever is pleased with my daughter Fatima, I am pleased with him. And whoever I am pleased with, Allah is pleased with him.' And whoever I am pleased with, Allah is pleased with him. Now, how is this pleasure achieved? I will not speak about that. The one who understands, understands; if they don't, they don't. Now, look at this. If they say that, then what is displeasure? I have mentioned the Hadith; remember, I have already told you what the displeasure is. The third one was lying there, and the lady had passed away. Would anyone dare to touch her? If anyone touched her, they would be punished. Alright, and that is why when the lady said, 'Saluni' (ask me)... She said that it is correct that until... when the body was lying there, and until the body... they were being buried in the graveyard. But they were not being buried in the graveyard. [Music] So, it was said, 'Take them away, take them to the graveyard in Medina.' And the graveyard... they are taking them. So, the Uthman who is in Jannat al-Baqi, that Uthman is so oppressed. And Uthman is oppressed—the one who is the companion of the Maulana—the one who plants trees in Jannat al-Baqi. So, that lady's Hadith is correct. As soon as the second question was asked, he understood, and he became angry and started saying, 'In such a short time, you have...' So, when he passed away, you understand that there was a gathering of millions. It is like that, he used to do it for free. He used to do it for free. Then he saw that you are a stranger, so he said, 'You have come here without permission from your city.' If you have come without permission, then... and if you have gone, then... another question can arise. The one who came... [unclear]... and made it blind. And the rest of the Hadith... this is what they call the Shia. When he enters the gathering, restlessness begins. People start shifting in their seats. 'Ya Salman, whoever loves Ali, loves me. And whoever loves me, loves Allah.' [Music] 'O Salman, Hell is the valley for the one who bears malice towards Fatima, and bears malice towards the progeny of Fatima, and bears malice towards the children of Fatima.' Whoever bears malice towards the children of Fatima, for him is that... now look at the status. That is why it is said, 'And it is a very, very authentic narration.' Whoever... the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is the one whose prayers are answered. Every Masoom's prayer is answered. If a Masoom prays for someone, there is no doubt that the prayer will be accepted. If they pray for someone, then that prayer is accepted; there is no doubt in that either. Absolutely, remember this Hadith. This is a very beautiful Hadith: 'O Fatima, whoever hurts you, I give you the glad tidings that for you is the Maqam-e-Mahmood (the Praised Station).' And it is said that if all the people—all of them—if 100,000, 200,000, 900,000, 999,000 people stand up... And all the angels, all the creatures of the universe stand up and try to take those people out of Hell who are your enemies, upon whom you have sent curses, Allah will not take them out of Hell. Now, here is the answer. Why do you ask this? If there is any other Hadith, they will give it to me. This objection that you feel... why are you asking in English? It is a waste of time. They ask for the sake of asking. It is a waste of time. These things come up in the film, some people say this, some say that. And what is in it? What is gained from this? I am telling you the Hadith now, so I am finishing it while taking time. I am finishing it while taking time. The narration, when the Masoom says, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that if we... for one moment, if anyone shows enmity towards Fatima... for one moment... for one moment, if anyone shows enmity... better than a year of worship... after that, the Wilayah is not accepted until there is Tabarra. Until there is Tabarra, the Wilayah is not accepted. Tabarra is in the Hadith; in Urdu, it has become Tabarra. The whole thing is on that—Tabarra. Yes, in Arabic, Tabarra is well understood. So, until there is Tabarra, the Wilayah is not accepted. Until there is Tabarra, the Wilayah is not accepted. Because anyone can help. And sometimes we feel pity for this nation. We are talking to you; it is very pitiful. They have made a mockery of the Panjtan, and they have given their number to them. Now it turns out that they are reading... 'Hey brother, what are you doing? Is there any courtesy?' Everyone will call anyone a 'brother.' There is no issue with that. And the reason for that is that the gentleman has made a mockery of the Hadith. What is the religion? It will remain like that until the Day of Judgment. The gathering is a different thing. And the work you did for Hussain, you keep saying it is for the sake of the Zahra. And I will tell you, make it so that they come to our gatherings. That is a very good thing, very good. Okay, no problem. We are not telling anyone to mix, do not come. But the condition is that you must do Tabarra along with the love. They are going to make fools of you. Look, it is completely smooth, now there is a plan in it. Hmm, okay. If someone feels bad, that is fine. Two rotis and greens are enough, that is the reality. Look, what happens is that they come and praise a little, people say 'very good, very amazing'. Tell those who spread this flag to cut it a little for me. Brother, at the time when the right of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) was usurped, curses upon that, and we sit and say 'leave it, it is over'. Just say it twice, that is enough. Now we will give you a good... yes, but you think that you should speak to them like this. Look, there are settings for that, which we are also telling you. Set it. There is a narration, a Hadith, that a believer is not a fool; he is wise and recognizes his time. The strategy is: first come, first praise them, they will be happy, they will be pleased. Okay, when they are happy, then what will you do? Start praising your own people. And you are sitting silently watching, 'this has happened, that has happened'. Now what to do? We are sitting quietly, we are doing our own thing, we are sitting in this gathering and praising, we are all sitting and not even saying anything. We are all sitting and not even saying anything. I should also speak. Until now, they were saying that it should start this much. That is why Tabarra (disassociation) is important, and that is why our scholars and elders loved you more than themselves. Those who perform Tabarra, you should understand that this is the history of this group. This is the history, I will just tell you this much. Who does not know this? This is for the sake of clarity, and they have searched for the history in large numbers. But they are describing the notification. This person was martyred, it is known who martyred him. Therefore, they used to stand outside Masjid-e-Nabawi. You all are sleeping. They used to stand outside Masjid-e-Nabawi, and for those who came there to pray, they used to recite Surah At-Tahrim. Do not be like those who forgot Allah. Where do you think we are? Masjid-e-Nabawi. There is still a lot of time between us, and the enmity between us has become completely manifest and clear. To the extent that 'until you believe in Allah alone'—until you acknowledge the oneness of Allah, no one can say, 'What are you doing? This is a prayer-offering person.' But those who were speaking understood this, and those listening also understood that until there is the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and the Wilayah of Zahra (s.a.), and until there is disassociation (Bara'ah) from their enemies, until that time, no one can claim to have faith. It is also possible that you might say, 'Brother, you love these people so much, is there some kinship?' That is why you are mentioning them. It is possible you might think, 'Why are you promoting them?' But one should not do this; they used to do it, and then you took it as an open challenge and decided not to change, but as soon as their martyrdom... But as soon as their martyrdom occurred, people confirmed it with blood. When they were in power, people went and complained, 'We are being oppressed, he stands there, and you are reading this, so why are you complaining to us?' But when they were called, we heard how they behaved. Why were we considered to be in such a state? And this liquid, this person who is keeping the secret, do you know the consequence? The one who is carrying out this task, there is no one more foolish than him. But one must be fearless, otherwise, one will be afraid of everything. He will be afraid of everything; what will he do? Now, the name is 'fearless'—without it, the Quran is incomplete. The whole story is of the magicians of Pharaoh. So what will happen next? What have you thought? Keep your attention on this. Now, what is the consequence of this? Now, what is the consequence of this? Why did he threaten them, saying, 'I will cut off your hands and feet'? He threatened them for a long time. They only replied with one sentence: 'No problem, inna ila Rabbina munqalibun' (Indeed, we are to return to our Lord). We have to go to our Lord anyway. Even if one goes to the hospital and spends a lot of money, or if one is killed by magic or something else—is there any difference? This is what our faith is. I asked, 'Why are you so afraid? You write books, you were twisting things.' So what is the matter? If one goes to the hospital and spends lakhs of rupees, it is better to be martyred. Martyrdom is a great blessing. They were trying to scare them, saying, 'We will do this to you,' but they did not respond; they just said, 'It is no issue.' After that, when the martyr goes—when they were martyred, when the news reached... May the rain of Allah's mercy be upon you. We have to discuss matters later, but first, let us address the questions. Keep your books with you. You asked about the 'Hawari' (disciples/closest companions) of the Imams. The one who is closest to a person is called a Hawari. When the question was asked about the Hawari of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he mentioned them. Then, when the question came to the Hawari of Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.), the first name mentioned was Abu Khalid al-Kabuli. He was among the companions of the fourth Imam. It is not that everyone was martyred; the fourth Imam's mother... when this training happens, this kind of love for the Ahlulbayt... When this training is done in such a way that the news reaching them is completely wrong, then the first thing to do is to bring our children to these gatherings, to these Majalis. Train them, show them, so that, Insha'Allah, our children may also remain in the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Especially when Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is the hope of the world, we should prepare ourselves just as you desire. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen, Was-salatu was-salamu ala Rasoolillah, wa ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in. Wa ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in. Amma ba'd, fa-audhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Raheem. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen, was-salatu was-salamu ala Sayyidina Muhammadin wa alihi at-tahireen.

title: Sab Se Afzal Ibaadat Tasbeeh-e-Fatima (s.a.) Hai
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense significance of Tasbih-e-Fatima (s.a.) as the most superior form of worship. Citing Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), the speaker explains that no praise of Allah surpasses this specific invocation. The fact that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gifted this to his daughter, Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), serves as definitive proof of its supreme status in the eyes of Allah.
content:
The fifth Imam, Hazrat Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), states that if a servant praises Allah, no servant can praise Allah in a way that is better than the Tasbih of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). There is no better way to worship Allah than this Tasbih. The Imam further says that if there were anything better than this Tasbih, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would have given that to his daughter. The Prophet giving this Tasbih to his daughter is itself proof that this Tasbih of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) is the most beloved thing to the Prophet and to Allah.

title: Jaanwar Bhi Yazid Par La'nat Karte Hain | Marg-e-Yazid | #Yazid Par #Lanat
excerpt: This lecture recounts a narration involving Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) visiting the land of Karbala, where he was injured after falling from his horse. Jibra'il (a.s.) explains that the injury occurred in anticipation of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.), leading the Prophet to curse Yazid. The speaker emphasizes that even animals recognize the wickedness of Yazid, suggesting that those who refuse to condemn him are lower than beasts.
content:
It is narrated that when Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) passed through the land of Karbala, he was riding a horse. Suddenly, the horse's foot slipped. Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) fell from the horse to the ground. His head was wounded and blood began to flow. Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) immediately sought forgiveness and prayed, 'O Lord, what sin have I committed?' At that moment, Jibra'il (a.s.) descended and said, 'O Ibrahim, you have not committed any sin. But this is the place where the grandson of the Last Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Imam Hussain (a.s.), will be martyred. Therefore, your blood has flowed in grief for his blood.' Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) asked, 'Jibra'il, who will kill him?' Jibra'il (a.s.) replied, 'The inhabitants of the heavens and the earth send curses upon him.' The Pen also wrote a curse upon him on the Preserved Tablet (Lawh). Then Allah (t.w.t.) revealed to the Pen, 'Through this curse, you have become worthy of praise.' Then Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) raised his hands and cursed Yazid profusely, and his horse said 'Ameen' in its own tongue. I felt ashamed, and the reason for this was Yazid. May the curse of Allah be upon him. This means that not only Prophets but even animals curse Yazid. Therefore, whoever does not curse Yazid is worse than animals.
Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) was injured at Karbala as a sign of the future tragedy of Imam Hussain (a.s.).
Jibra'il (a.s.) informed Ibrahim that the blood shed was in sympathy with the blood of the Prophet's grandson.

title: Zuhoor Ki Hatmi Alaamaton Mein Badaa | ⛅IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological concept of 'Bada' (divine change in decree) in relation to the signs preceding the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). It highlights a narration from Imam Jawad (a.s.) clarifying that while the reappearance of the Imam is an unchangeable divine promise, the specific signs leading up to it, such as the arrival of the Sufyani, are subject to Bada. This distinction emphasizes the certainty of the Imam's return while acknowledging the flexibility of the preparatory events.
content:
Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari says that we were with Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, meaning Imam Rida (a.s.). We were with Imam Jawad (a.s.) when the mention of Sufyani began, and the traditions that exist in books regarding Sufyani, which consider his arrival as 'Mahtum' (inevitable/certain). Abu Hashim says I asked Imam Jawad (a.s.), 'Can Allah perform Bada (change in divine decree) even in Mahtum matters?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Yes.' Abu Hashim then said to the Imam, 'We fear that Allah might perform Bada regarding the Sahib al-Amr (Imam Mahdi).' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Al-Mahdi is from the promise (of Allah).' Meaning, the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is Allah's promise, and Allah does not break His promise. Therefore, it is certain that the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will occur. It is certain that the Imam (a.s.) will reappear, but regarding all the signs mentioned as 'Mahtum', including the arrival of Sufyani, it is possible that Allah may perform Bada in them—meaning changes may occur, and Allah may not manifest these signs, and the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) may occur before these signs are manifested.
The concept of Bada allows for changes in divine decrees regarding certain events.
The arrival of the Sufyani is traditionally considered a 'Mahtum' (inevitable) sign.

Signs of the reappearance may be altered or omitted, but the return of the Imam is certain.
The reappearance could potentially occur without the manifestation of all traditional signs.

title: Baqee Mein Kaun Dafn Hain
excerpt: This lecture provides an overview of the historical and spiritual significance of Jannat al-Baqi, the sacred cemetery in Medina. It highlights the prominent figures buried there, including four Shia Imams, the daughter of the Prophet, and several other revered companions and family members of the Prophet Muhammad. The talk emphasizes the sanctity of this site and the legacy of those resting within its grounds.
content:
Jannat al-Baqi is not an ordinary graveyard. Who is buried there? Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), who, besides being the grandson of the Prophet, is also the leader of the youth of Paradise. Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zainul Abideen (a.s.), who is the nephew of Imam Hasan (a.s.) and the son of Imam Husayn (a.s.). Then, the son of Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.), Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), and his son, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), at whose feet the Imams of the four schools of thought of the Ahlus-Sunnah sat to learn. According to some narrations, the grave of the daughter of the Prophet, the Princess of the Worlds, Hazrat Siddiqa Tahira Fatima Zahra (s.a.), is also in Baqi. Besides them, the mother of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Hazrat Fatima bint Asad (s.a.), the brother of the Master of the Universe, Aqeel ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), Bibi Umm al-Banin (s.a.), Bibi Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib, Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, Abdullah ibn Jafar ibn Abi Talib, the famous companion of the Prophet, Uthman ibn Maz'un, whom the Prophet himself buried there. The Prophet's son, Janab-e-Ibrahim, who is buried near Uthman ibn Maz'un, and Asad ibn Zurara, who was the first among the people of Medina to embrace Islam. Yusuf Zahra [Music]
Jannat al-Baqi is a highly significant historical and spiritual site in Medina.
Four Shia Imams are buried in Baqi: Imam Hasan, Imam Zainul Abideen, Imam Muhammad Baqir, and Imam Jafar Sadiq.
The grave of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is believed by many to be located within the cemetery.
Other notable figures include Hazrat Fatima bint Asad, Bibi Umm al-Banin, and Aqeel ibn Abi Talib.
The Prophet's son, Ibrahim, and early companions like Uthman ibn Maz'un are also interred there.
The cemetery holds the remains of early converts to Islam, such as Asad ibn Zurara.
Imam Jafar Sadiq's scholarly influence is noted through the attendance of various Sunni school leaders at his lectures.

key_points: Jannat al-Baqi is a highly significant historical and spiritual site in Medina.
Four Shia Imams are buried in Baqi: Imam Hasan, Imam Zainul Abideen, Imam Muhammad Baqir, and Imam Jafar Sadiq.
The grave of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is believed by many to be located within the cemetery.
Other notable figures include Hazrat Fatima bint Asad, Bibi Umm al-Banin, and Aqeel ibn Abi Talib.
The Prophet's son, Ibrahim, and early companions like Uthman ibn Maz'un are also interred there.
The cemetery holds the remains of early converts to Islam, such as Asad ibn Zurara.
Imam Jafar Sadiq's scholarly influence is noted through the attendance of various Sunni school leaders at his lectures.

chapters.title: The Sacred Figures of Jannat al-Baqi
chapters.summary: An enumeration of the holy Imams, family members of the Prophet, and companions buried in the Baqi cemetery.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Remembrance
chapters.summary: A brief concluding segment reflecting on the spiritual connection to the figures buried in Baqi.

title: Majlis 5 | Ma'refat-e-Namaaz | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 1444
excerpt: This lecture, the fifth in the Khamsa-e-Majaalis series, explores the profound connection between the recognition of the Ahlulbayt and the spiritual necessity of prayer. It emphasizes that true worship, including Namaz, is inseparable from the acceptance of Wilayah and the practice of Tabarra. Through historical accounts of Karbala and theological insights, the speaker highlights prayer as a vital companion in the afterlife and a manifestation of one's devotion to Allah.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The son of the desert (Abbas) rose like the moon with a sword in his hand, his gaze fixed on the moon-like face of his brother. First, he stood before the master of the sword (Husayn), then he came to his brother, the bearer of the water-skin. His standard was high, a sign of nobility, in every attribute, the mark of the seal of Prophethood. With the presence of the master, the heart became ready, the pen became correct, and the speech flowed. All the eloquence of the master of the universe, when it comes, is beyond the reach of words. In the face of the moon, the senses were lost, O son of Zainab, your pen has arrived. He would go to look at his mother, sometimes without a banner, sometimes shouting, taking the signal from the King of Umam (Husayn). Both brothers would sometimes wrestle together, today everything was there, from that same majesty. What dust is this on the signs of Ali al-Wali? Mother, who knows the banner of the one who is not known? If the King of the highest status does not do anything, he himself remains in the seal, explaining. With the cup of etiquette, he requested, 'Call us too,' he has a desire that the Nawab (Husayn) should call him. He is the slave of the Master and a sacrifice, he seeks honor, he is not the heir of those. O like of the Messenger, in the army, everywhere, but our root, the Prophet, gave the sign. In Khaybar, look, the army of the noble is going, the banner of Ali has become, do not hold your unity. There is no lack in the leadership, they are thirsty, even if we are, we are also the grandsons. Zainab then said, 'What do you have to do with this? Do you think I know what you are doing?' Look, if there is any disrespectful speech, I will write it, if it is from the tongue, the banner will be made. Go, stand ten, with the banner in your hand, those who have come, we are on the banner, so leave it. O master of dignity, move your head, move forward, do not stand near the banner, lest you see the sign of the pen of the creator. You and those who came to me, the voice, enough, in a dream, it is not accepted, this coincidence. You will start saying that you were called, what else will you call this except childhood? Hussain, Hussain, or the killer of the righteous, Hussain, or the killer of the righteous. Removing the stone from the corpse, Zainab also cries out. Are you my Hussain? How are the pieces of the body lying, separated? Are you my Hussain? Removing the stone from the corpse, Zainab also cries out. Are you my Hussain? Alas, alas, what have they done to my poor one? They trampled the body with horses. Oh, how should I recognize you? The head is separated from the body. Are you my Hussain? Removing the stone from the corpse, Zainab also cries out. Are you my Hussain? Oh, I will recognize you, give me a voice. When I saw the young man who had breathed his last, there was no light left in the eyes of the restless one. Are you my Hussain? Removing the stone from the corpse, Zainab also cries out. Are you my Hussain? Oh, recognizing you has become difficult. This is the first time I have seen Zainab without a veil. I am ashamed, tell me, tell me a little. Are you my Hussain? Removing the stone from the corpse, Zainab also cries out. Are you my Hussain? I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the High, the Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the pious and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. May Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our Master of command, our Owner, our Mawla, our Beloved, our Physician, our Companion, and our Confidant, the awaited one. May my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: From our Mawla and our Master, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (a.s.), 'He lies who claims that he knows us while he is holding onto the rope of others.' Our Mawla and Master Ja'far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) spoke the truth. May Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. This hadith has been selected. Peace be upon all the truthful ones in the noble hadith. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. He says that he lies, the one who imagines, the one who thinks that he has our Ma'rifat (recognition), but is holding onto the rope of others. He is holding onto the rope of outsiders, leaving us and going to others. He ties his hopes at the door of another, he begs at the door of another. He lies, the one who says he is ours; he is not ours at all. Yesterday, in the service of the hadith series, I mentioned a few things. And as I mentioned yesterday, this topic is very vast, very special. So, I will present only a few things, as much as is needed, as much as is possible, and in as little time as possible. The Prophet said that whoever memorizes 40 hadiths from my Ummah, and his intention is only what? The intention is for the sake of Allah and for the sake of the Hereafter, Dar al-Akhirah. Allah will resurrect him with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are they as companions. As I mentioned, it is in Surah An-Nisa, verse 69. So, the one whom the Prophet used in this hadith, that Allah will resurrect him—if someone memorizes 40 hadiths, Allah will resurrect him with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And what an excellent company this is; there cannot be a better company than this. After that, when the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what are these 40 hadiths?', he explained that these 40 hadiths are not actually just 40 hadiths, but rather 40 topics. One of which I presented to you was Tawheed (Monotheism), about which I spoke in detail. It wasn't a full exegesis, but rather a single gathering was dedicated to it; otherwise, the topic of Tawheed itself is very vast and very special. That is why he only pointed towards it. And then, the second topic I presented to you was the importance of Wudu (ablution) in Islam and how much emphasis is placed upon it in Shi'ism—how much indeed—that one should always remain in a state of Wudu. And this conversation is like protection and insurance. Today, I will try to emphasize another aspect of that same hadith, that same sentence, where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Pray, and pray at its appointed time.' And if someone does not pray on time, without any excuse, without any reason, without any cause, just unnecessarily delaying the prayer—they are delaying it unnecessarily. They are just sitting there, having no work. 'Unnecessarily' means, for example, playing a game or watching a game—let's talk about the youngsters—that they are watching a game and saying, 'We will pray later.' Or talking with friends, saying, 'We will do it later.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that in this, there is the wrath of Allah. Allah becomes wrathful. Wrath means that just as Allah's Essence, Allah's Being, is infinite—'la-mutanahi' means infinite—in fact, He is infinite in His being infinite. That is, He is infinite in His infinitude. He has no limits or boundaries. Similarly, His actions also have no limits or boundaries. His deeds, His actions, also have no end. So if Allah has said there is His wrath, then it is very dangerous for the one who is among 'wal-maghdubi alayhim' (those upon whom is Your wrath). 'Wa ghayril maghdubi alayhim wa lad-dallin' (not of those who have earned Your wrath, nor of those who go astray). That is, we should not be among those upon whom is Your wrath. And I had submitted to you that the Quran has sent a curse upon the worshippers. Upon the worshippers! 'Fa-waylun lil-musallin' (So woe to those who pray). Who are these 'musallin'? 'Alladhina hum an salatihim sahun' (Those who are neglectful of their prayers). Those who take their prayers lightly. They do not give importance to the prayer and will pray only when they get leisure, when they get time. The Quran says there is 'Wayl' for them. 'Wayl' is the name of a valley in Hell, a valley in Hell that is for such worshippers. That is why there is so much emphasis on prayer. I am addressing the youngsters more; look, in the Holy Quran, there is a verse in Surah Al-Muddaththir... 'Fi jannatin yatasalun, anil mujrimin' (In gardens, they will ask one another about the guilty). When the people of Paradise go to Paradise and the people of Hell go to Hell, the people of Paradise will ask those of the people of Hell whom they recognize. When they converse, they will ask, because they will recognize each other—they might be friends, relatives, neighbors, or business partners, who knows what—so they will ask, 'Ma salakakum fi saqar?' (What has brought you into Saqar/Hell?). They will reply, 'Lam naku minal musallin' (We were not of those who prayed). We used to abandon prayer, we used to leave prayer, we used to give importance to prayer [by neglecting it]. 'Lam naku minal musallin.' Of course, this is the apparent meaning. Shall I tell you the inner meaning? The inner meaning is that when the Imam (a.s.) was asked what the meaning of this verse is, the Imam replied that they will say, 'We were not among those who recited Salawat.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. One should recite Salawat, and recite it loudly. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. A gentleman came after reciting [elsewhere] and started reciting in a gathering. He had been reciting for many years, you understand. And he started saying in the gathering, 'I feel'—he was speaking English—'I feel this Salawat is a waste of time.' You understand? He is saying it in the gathering. 'I feel this is a waste of time.' So, anyway, we asked him, we said, 'Brother, how did you silence them?' He said, 'No, one should send Salawat in the heart. Why loudly? So much of the gathering's time is wasted.' We said, 'This Salawat is one of the reasons for the gathering.' Indeed, indeed. And this 'in the heart' that you are talking about, it is against the teachings of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It is against the teachings of the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah has commanded: 'Irfa'u aswatakum inda as-salawati ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin fa-innaha tadhhabu bin-nifaq' (Raise your voices when sending Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, for it removes hypocrisy from the heart). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. And do not doubt. 'How should we send Salawat? What will people think? And what have we... How should we send Salawat? People will think...' People will not think anything. You do not worry about that at all. Right? And you are not that great either. And there is one more thing, right? I was going to say this at the end, but sometimes what happens is that there is no time left at the end. So that point remains. That when once the Imam (a.s.) was asked what is the 'illat' (reason/cause) of prayer? The Imam explained the reason. Then he asked, 'Asbab' (causes), he started asking about its beginning, its middle, what is this, what is that? After asking all the questions, the narrator asked, 'How is the prayer completed?' He said, 'Our prayer is completed through our Wilayah (guardianship) and by performing Tabarra (disassociation) against our enemies.' Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Raise your voices with Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. This is present, the sentence is present. That the prayer is completed, 'Bima tamamaha'—how is the prayer completed? How is it made perfect? So the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Through our Wilayah, and by disassociating from our enemies.' And until you perform Tabarra against our enemies, the prayer will not be complete. The prayer will be deficient, half. The prayer will not be complete. So if one sends half a prayer, then look, the chances of acceptance of half a thing by Allah are low. Although He is Allah, we don't know. We cannot say. But when He has set a condition... For example, I prayed the whole prayer but did not recite the Salam, I am giving an example. I did not recite the Salam, today I am not in the mood to recite the Salam. Just finished the prayer after Tashahhud. Will the prayer be accepted? Similarly, the Imam says, until there is Bara'ah (disassociation), the prayer will not be accepted. Therefore, it is necessary that in the prayer—look, just as you recite Salawat, at least recite this much, at least. 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in.' 'Wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in.' At least this much. And yesterday also I submitted to you that this La'n (curse) and this Bara'ah, this is Rizq (sustenance) from Allah. Indeed, indeed. Allah does not give it to everyone. Therefore, read Ziyarat Ashura. Mostly it is written in Ashura that Allah has given Rizq: 'Wa razaqani bil-bara'ati min a'da'ikum' (And He has granted me the sustenance of disassociating from your enemies). And Allah has given Rizq. This Rizq, this Rizq is spiritual. It is spiritual Rizq. And the spiritual Rizq is much higher than the material Rizq. Indeed. And look, the custom of the whole world is the same. I don't know why when it comes to the matter of religion, people start compromising on it. The custom of the whole world is the same. But anyway, recite one Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. So what is this prayer? Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) had prayed. It is a verse of Surah Ibrahim: 'Rabbi-j'alni muqimas-salati wa min dhurriyyati, Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a' (My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication).' O Lord, Prophet Ibrahim is Khalilullah (the Friend of Allah). Khalilullah, he is the friend of Allah. But he is praying, 'My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.' O Lord, count me among the worshippers. Make me among those who establish prayer. 'Rabbi-j'alni muqimas-salati'—those who establish prayer. And do not make only me, 'wa min dhurriyyati'—also make those in my progeny worshippers. 'Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a'—and O Lord, accept this supplication. Subhan Allah. That is, he is asking for the supplication and also emphasizing that this supplication should be accepted. Allah, obviously, accepts the supplication. Because in reality, what is the problem with the youngsters is that they do not have the 'Ma'rifat' (gnosis/deep knowledge) of prayer. That is the problem. Look, if you reflect on the narrations. Well, all these narrations that I am presenting to you, they are all from whom? From the Ma'sumin (a.s.). We are not saying a single thing from ourselves. These are all in the hadiths. And Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and other Imams (a.s.) used to pray in such a way that we cannot even imagine. That when Abu Darda came at night to meet Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was in the palm grove. 'Nakhlistan' is called a garden, the garden that is of dates is called Nakhlistan. A date garden. Abu Darda came to the Nakhlistan. What did he see? That the Master (a.s.) is in prostration. And in prostration, he is weeping, he is weeping. And then suddenly what happened was that his voice stopped. Abu Darda comes closer. After coming closer, after coming closer, Abu Darda sees that the Master has completely laid down. And when he touches him, 'Assalam.' When Abu Darda touches him, there is absolutely no movement. So Abu Darda lays him straight. And then he sees that there is absolutely no movement found. Abu Darda got worried. He got worried and came and knocked at the door of Janabe Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) and said, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' The Princess asked, 'What happened, Abu Darda?' 'Ali ibn Abi Talib has passed away.' She said, 'How are you saying this?' He said, 'I saw this condition that he was in prostration and while weeping, he suddenly became completely unconscious and then finished. No movement is being found now.' She said, 'Abu Darda, this is the state of Ali ibn Abi Talib's swoon in the fear of God.' This is the state. That is, you are a follower of such an Imam whose worship is like this. So how is it possible that the followers of such an Imam do not pray? Is it possible that they do not pray or worship? Now look, see what 'Ma'rifat' (gnosis) is. There is a Hadith of the Imam. Sheikh Saduq has recorded this Hadith in his book. The Imam says, "Law ya'lamul musalli ma yaghshahu min jalalillahi"—if the person praying knew how the majesty of Allah encompasses him during prayer. How Allah's majesty, Allah's greatness, Allah's grandeur, and Allah's mercy encompass him during prayer, how it surrounds him. If he only knew this, the Imam says, if he only knew how it surrounds him, then "Ma sarrahu an yarfa'a ra'sahu min sujudih"—he would never like to lift his head from his prostration. He would remain in this state of prostration. This is a station. And young people, you are often in a hurry. You think that, for example, this three-rak'ah prayer should be finished in a minute and a half. If it were up to you, you would use a stopwatch to pray. You are in a hurry. Do not be in a hurry. Because this is a 'Tawfiq' (divine opportunity). Understand this, that it is the opportunity to go to His court, which is not granted to everyone. And let me present one more thing to you. If you are ready to listen. If you are ready to listen, then send Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. It is not granted to everyone. And why? Let me tell you a small story first. So that you know your own importance, for the Mawla says, "Rahimallahu man ya'rifu qadrah"—may Allah's mercy be upon the servant who recognizes his own worth. Who recognizes his own value. Know your value. Who are you? Abu Basir came to the Imam, he presented himself to the sixth Imam. In Medina, in Mecca. In Mecca, and he was standing at Jamrat al-Rahma. Abu Basir said, "Ya Ibn Rasulullah! Ma aktharal hajij"—there are so many pilgrims. The Imam said, "Pilgrims are very few. These are all animals." Pilgrims are few. And what is it? Pilgrims are few. You are saying you are not using another word. The one who comes for Hajj is a pilgrim. These are all the same. And what is it? These are all those saying 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk'. And you are saying they are not pilgrims. The Imam wiped his hands over their eyes. And removed the veils of the world for him. The veils were removed. His eyes became 'Barzakhi' (spiritual). Then Abu Basir saw. So all these people saying 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' were not pilgrims. Rather, they were all animals. And there were very few pilgrims among them. Those who were saying 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk'. The Imam said, 'Do you understand, Abu Basir? These who are truly saying 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk', those whom you are seeing, these are the ones who are saying it with our Wilayah.' Nara-e-Takbir: Allah-hu-Akbar. Nara-e-Risalat: Ya Rasul Allah. Nara-e-Haidari: Ya Ali. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. 'Bi shartiha wa shurutiha'. Imam Reza (a.s.) said, 'Kalimatu La ilaha illallah hisni, faman dakhala hisni amina min 'adhabi'—the Kalima 'La ilaha illallah' is My fortress. And whoever says this Kalima will enter My fortress. But there is a condition for that. 'Bi shartiha wa shurutiha'. And I am one of its conditions. Meaning, Imamate is a condition. Until that condition is fulfilled, there is nothing. So, in the same way, when you go to pray, you say Takbir. So surely, there is a small prayer before the Takbir. And in that prayer, you recite exactly this. That is, you invoke the intercession of Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. And in it, you say—it is a prayer, you can check, it is present in the books—that 'Allahumma inni ataqarrabu ilaika'—O Lord, the closeness we are seeking from You, this closeness can only be with Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Without them, it cannot be. After that, without this Wilayah, whatever is done cannot be worship. It will not be worship. You may give it any name you want, but without Wilayah, nothing is accepted. Remember this point. So now, the Prophet was asked, 'What is prayer?' The Prophet replied that prayer is the Sharia of the religion. Prayer is the will of Allah. Allah is pleased when a servant prays. And Allah has made this prayer the path of the Prophets. This prayer is the path of the Prophets. Young people, understand this. If you want to walk on the path of the Prophets, then remain steadfast in prayer. Remain steadfast. In this prayer, there is 'Hubbul Mala'ika' (love of the angels). There is the love of the angels in it. Let's move forward a little. Nara-e-Takbir: Allah-hu-Akbar. Nara-e-Risalat: Ya Rasul Allah. Nara-e-Haidari: Ya Ali. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. There is the love of the angels. 'Hubbul Mala'ika'. The angels like it. Meaning, when a worshiper says 'Allah-hu-Akbar' with Wilayah, the angels like it. And prayer is most unpleasant to Satan. Because, in reality, when a believer goes into prostration, he is actually prostrating to Allah, but along with that, he is rubbing the nose of Iblis. He is rubbing the nose of Iblis. And Iblis says, 'Sajada wa abaytu'—he is prostrating, while I refused. This was the very task he was asked to do, but I refused. 'Sajada wa abaytu'—he is prostrating, I refused. 'Karahu lish-shaytan' (it is hateful to Satan). And... This prayer, this prayer is a weapon against the enemies of the religion. It is a weapon. Now think, how is prayer against the enemies of the religion? You know, this is a method Allah has created, to put awe into the hearts of the enemies of the religion. Allah says in the Quran, 'Wa udkhilu fi qulubihimur-ru'b'—Allah has put awe into their hearts. Awe, meaning fear. And as soon as... look, all the conspiracies that happen against prayer, against the Adhan, why do they happen? You understand, don't you? The reason for that. Yes. The reason for that is that it causes them some confusion. Why does this confusion happen? It happens because of this awe. It happens because of this awe. And as soon as a believer says 'Allah-hu-Akbar', meaning he is declaring the greatness of Allah. 'Allah-hu-Akbar min ayyu yusuf'—that Allah whose description cannot be made, that Allah whom no one can define, that Allah whom no one can understand, that Allah who is beyond human intellect. People are afraid of this Takbir. They were afraid of this Takbir. Allah-hu-Akbar. In reality, what happens is... That when someone gets blessings very easily, they don't value them. For example, we received Wilayah very easily. So therefore, often—I won't say often, many people among us—I won't say often, 'often' slipped out by mistake—many people among us are such that they raise different kinds of objections to Wilayah. Why is this? Why is that? Why is it like this? Why is it like that? To the extent that I heard a gentleman saying that, for example, Sayyid Hashim Bahrani's book 'Madinat al-Ma'ajiz' is 'Ghulu' (exaggeration). Ghulu. Actually, he has become afflicted with 'Ghulu'. You understand 'Ghulu', right? The diseases of them. Meaning, a person should always remember one thing. Always remember this thing. The Hadith you just read: 'Rahimallahu man ya'rifu qadrah'—may Allah have mercy on the servant who recognizes his own worth. And what is the next part of it? 'Wa lam yata'adda haddah'—and does not exceed his limit. Recognize your limit. What is your limit? Do not talk beyond that. Before passing a comment on Sayyid Hashim Bahrani, stand in front of a mirror once and look at your own face. Look and see, brother, what are we? How many books have we read? Who is Sayyid Hashim Bahrani? And what is his contribution to Shi'ism? That even today, those who are sitting here from Bahrain, who are familiar with Bahrain, where Sayyid Hashim Bahrani's grave is in Bahrain, that is where his house is. You know, this hall, as big as it is, his entire house was about one-third of this, or even less. His house was that big. But in that small house, the King used to come to meet him. Sayyid Hashim Bahrani lived in that small house. There was a mosque nearby. He would keep writing and reading. As soon as it was time for prayer, he would put down his pen, go, and lead the prayer. He would come back and start writing and reading again. And whatever little he got as 'Riza' (sustenance), he would eat that. He would be content with that. And then start writing and reading again. He would write and read for 17-18 hours. And he has written many books. There is no time here for us to list his books for you. Just understand this much, that he is the author of 'Tafsir al-Burhan'. 'Tafsir al-Burhan' is in 10 volumes, in which he has written the commentary of the Quran. Commentary of the Quran, and solely and exclusively from the Hadiths of the Masumin (infallibles), that's it. He did not state even a single word from himself. Not a single word. In 10 volumes. That was Sayyid Hashim Bahrani. These people who say 'Madinat al-Ma'ajiz' is 'Ghulu', 'Ghulu'—do they even know anything? 'Madinat al-Ma'ajiz' contains the miracles of the Imams (a.s.). Miracles written in 14 volumes. And then this... why? They said the common people cannot digest these miracles. Not the common people, they themselves are unable to digest them. Now look, Allah has created man in such a way that things are digested. And if they are not, then there are medicines for it. Recite one Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Not everything is digested. So you take medicine. Or leave the Hadiths. Go to the door of those things that you can digest. Come to the answer. Like I said to a gentleman, just presented it in service. He was objecting in English. How he was objecting in English, 'How is it possible that Hazrat Ali struck Marhab with such a sword and Marhab was cut into two pieces and exactly like that his horse was also cut into two pieces? How is it possible? Is it possible? Logically does it seem possible?' He started speaking English logic. So, well, he thought this 'Maulvi' is someone, so what will he understand of this English? So, well, we said that you were not told the whole Hadith. He said, 'Meaning?' We said, not only Marhab and his horse were cut, the earth beneath them was also being cut. Hazrat Ali had placed his foot on it. Clap, just that. Nara-e-Haidari: Ya Ali. And what else? So he said, 'This is too much. This is too much.' So we said, 'Okay, wait now. I have to speak.' I had to give a speech. It was an opportunity. It's a matter from outside India, not from here. Not a matter of India. We said that we are giving a speech now, we will answer your question in it. And it is possible that you have spoken with bravery. There could be many such things, they have happened. Youngsters must have had that question in their hearts. Now, whatever deficiency remains, 'in kana fihi khalalun aw naqsun min ruku'iha aw sujudihah' (if there is any flaw or deficiency in its Ruku or Sujud), then You overlook it, and in the end, say to Allah, accept this for the sake of Your Proof, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Subhan Allah. That's it. When you go into the last prostration, stay in the prostration with a little peace. Do not be in a hurry to get up. Calmly, calmly. This is prayer. And this is the prayer that is completed through Wilayah. And this is—the whole matter presented before you—the purpose of Imam Hussain (a.s.)'s uprising, the purpose of Hussain, 'Aliyun Waliullah', 'Aliyun Waliullah'. Otherwise, there were many who prayed there too. The army of Umar ibn Sa'd was full of people who prayed. One after another, Huffaz (memorizers of Quran)—that is, this is written in the Maqtal, we are not saying it. They were Huffaz-e-Quran, there were many memorizers of Quran. They were narrators of hadith. They were companions. They were children of companions. Now what to tell, how they were. And on this side, only a few individuals, 72. But all were so immersed in Wilayah that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that these people—this is the Prophet's hadith—that they will be so immersed in the love of Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) that the sword will have no effect on them. And that is why we have already submitted in your service that when the time for prayer came, Abu Thumamah al-Sa'idi said that Mawla, the time for prayer has arrived. 'Fadhakkara as-salata, jazaka Allahu min al-musallin' (He remembered the prayer, may Allah count you among those who pray). Now Abu Thumamah remembered the prayer. May Allah count you among those who pray. And then Hussain (a.s.) prayed the prayer of fear, prayed together, and what is the state that Sa'id and Zuhair both moved forward. And now let me submit one more sentence to you about Hammad, just that Sa'id and Zuhair, there was no part of them that did not have an arrow in it. It was raining arrows. But Sa'id and Zuhair were taking them all on their bodies. And no effect, you know, right, that when one arrow hits, a man falls. But here, from head to toe, they were full of arrows, but they were standing as if nothing was wrong, it is written in the Maqtal. And after that, as soon as Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatu-llahi', then on one side Sa'id fell, on the other side Zuhair fell. Imam Hussain (a.s.) placed Sa'id's head on his knee. What sentence did Sa'id say, 'Hal awfaytu ya ibna Rasulillah?' (Have I fulfilled the right of loyalty, O son of the Messenger of Allah?). That's it. When every companion and every relative was martyred. They were all martyred, thirsty. Now no one was left, Hussain (a.s.) came to the tent, called out, 'Ya Zainab, o ya Umm Kulthum, ya Fizza, ya Sakina, 'alaykun minni salam.' O the ladies of my tent, O Fizza, O Sakina, my final peace be upon you all. As soon as Zainab (s.a.) heard, she came out in agony, 'Ya akhi, ahista sabr ka le lo.' O brother, have you prepared for death? So Hussain (a.s.) replied, 'This is how it is, yastaslimu lil-mawt, man la mu'ina lahu wa la nasir.' (He who has no helper and no supporter submits to death). How could he not be prepared for death, who has no companion, who has no helper? She said, 'Brother, do not say such things, Zainab is still alive.' He said, 'Brother, so when Zainab is alive,' so he said, 'Zainab, Zainab, take me to Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.).' Zainab (s.a.) held Hussain (a.s.)'s arm and brought him to Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.). He said, 'Sayyid al-Sajjad, look, Father has come, now the time for departure has arrived.' I might not be able to translate, I won't be able to recite, just telling you quickly. Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.) opened his eyes, said, 'Aunt, Aunt, where is Father?' Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.) could not recognize him. There are markets of Kufa and Sham, have patience, patience, have patience.' Saying this, she consoled him and in the end, conveyed the peace to you. When Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.) was going to Medina, he called the Shias of Medina, greeted them and said, for the Shias, 'Ma'e musharraf ho, ma'e minnat-e-qurbani.' O my followers, whenever you drink cold water, remember my thirst, and whenever you see a helpless and oppressed person, remember my helplessness. Saying this, Hussain (a.s.) departed, the right of departure, alas, alas, so he looked towards the battlefield once and called out, looking at the bodies, 'Ya ahl-e-safa.' 'Ayyukum yuqaddimu jawadi.' Who among you will answer me? No one answered. Zainab (s.a.) came, 'Brother, I will answer. I am an elderly lady, you will ask questions. Husayn (a.s.) emerged and launched three attacks to complete the proof (hujjat). The first attack was towards Qadisiyah; he attacked the army, and the forces collided with the walls of Qadisiyah. As soon as Husayn (a.s.) launched the third attack, he paused for a moment. Then, to support him for a moment, a call of truth came: 'O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, and enter among My servants and enter My Paradise.' O soul at peace, return to your Lord. Your Lord is pleased with you, and you are pleased with your Lord. Husayn (a.s.) placed his sword in its scabbard, he placed Zulfiqar in its scabbard. Now, listen to the words of the martyrdom (maqtal) from Janab-e-Sajjad (a.s.), in which I am not mentioned. Sajjad (a.s.) said, as narrated by him, that as soon as my father placed his sword and shield in the scabbard, someone threw a stone, someone rained arrows, and someone struck with a spear. Husayn's (a.s.) entire body was drenched in arrows. Once, Husayn (a.s.) came down from the back of his horse onto the earth of Karbala, or rather, he fell upon the arrows. Just then, preferring the tragedy, he did not mount the horse, but rather climbed onto Husayn's (a.s.) chest and, taking a dagger himself, began to cut Husayn's (a.s.) throat. Alas, Husayn! When Husayn (a.s.) could not see Husayn, he came to the ground, and when he saw Husayn and the Shimr, he was on Husayn's chest. So he became the oppressed one, and the dagger of the serpent said, 'O dagger of the serpent, hold yourself, what have you done?' My oppressed master is being slaughtered. As soon as Husayn (a.s.) heard Zaynab's (s.a.) voice, he signaled to Zaynab (s.a.) to return to the tent. 'I am still alive.' You cannot describe the scene; the earth of Karbala turned black. For the sake of God, O son of Sajjad (a.s.), what is happening? He said, 'O mother, what can I say?' Then Sajjad (a.s.) saw the scene that no son was ever shown: the head of his father raised on the tip of a spear. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Father, you were martyred and I remained alive. excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual parallels between Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) and Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), focusing on the concept of occultation (Ghaybah). content:
Yo, Sah-e-Zaman, Sah-e-Zaman, Yo. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-Hujjatibnil-Hasani, salawatuka alayhi wa ala abihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan, hatta tuskinahu... The quiz link is now live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. Answer all the questions. There is no prize for answering first; there is only one condition for the quiz prize, which is that answering all questions is necessary because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have answered all questions correctly in all episodes. That is, even if someone did not become a daily winner but has answered correctly in all episodes, then the mega in all episodes, then the mega prize, the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will include all those people. Audhu billahi samil alim minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. On behalf of the TSR team, we offer congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf) and welcome you all. We begin this program, the Panah-e-Kainat Imam Mahdi (ajtf) Mega Quiz, with the praise and glorification of Allah. May there be infinite praise and glorification for that pure and holy essence, that All-Knowing, Wise God, the Creator of the universe, who, for the welfare and salvation of humanity, to keep them away from ignorance and the ignorant, has continuously sent His Hujjat (Proof) in every era without any interruption, whether it be Hazrat Adam (a.s.), Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.), Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), or our final Prophet Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). But the question arises, who is the Hujjat of Allah in this world after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Because 'Law la al-hujja lasakhat al-ard bi-ahliha' (If there were no Hujjat, this earth would collapse with its inhabitants). collapse with its inhabitants. Yes, viewers, he is the heir of the Ashab al-Kisa. He is the personality who will establish justice and fairness in this world just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. He will elevate the religion of Allah above all other religions. The poet has said it well: 'There is a heart in the chest, and the Beloved resides in the hearts. You are the one by whose breath the world remains; you are the certainty. You are before our eyes, but you are not visible. The one whom our eyes search for, you are that beauty.' O Yusuf of Batul, lift the veil; show your face to the longing eyes. Come, gentlemen, to join us in this discussion, we have Mr. Sahir Abbas Sahab and Mr. Tanveer Abbas Sahab. Let us welcome them to this program. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. First of all, we offer our heartfelt congratulations to you all on the 15th of Shaban, the auspicious birth of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (ajtf). Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the one about whom, from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.), everyone has spoken. As Abbas brother mentioned, Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the personality who shares similarities with many Prophets. And our topic today is where we will look at the aspects where Imam Mahdi (a.s.) shares similarities with Hazrat Yusuf ibn Yaqub (a.s.). If we study the Hadith, we will find more than 20 such similarities between Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and Hazrat Yusuf. But in today's episode, we will look at six things. The first thing attributed to Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is his Ghaybah (Occultation). And if we look at his similarity with Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was also in occultation. Let us see how there is a similarity between the two. For this topic, we will take the help of a Hadith of Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.). Here, Imam Baqir (a.s.) says to his companion Muhammad ibn Muslim: 'Ya Muhammad ibn Muslim, inna fil-Mahdi min Ali Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) shabahan min khamsatin min ar-rusul: Yunus ibn Matta, Yusuf ibn Yusuf ibn Yaqub, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad (a.s.).' The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Muhammad ibn Muslim, Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has similarities with five Prophets: Hazrat Yunus ibn Matta, Hazrat Yusuf ibn Yaqub, Hazrat Musa (a.s.), Hazrat Isa (a.s.), and the final Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).' Zahir brother, since our topic today is limited only to Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), let us see how his similarity with Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) is. Moving forward from the beginning of the Hadith to our topic, where the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Wa ammash-shabahu min Yusuf ibn Yaqub (a.s.) fal-ghaybatu min khifatihi wa amratihi' (And as for the similarity with Yusuf ibn Yaqub (a.s.), it is his occultation due to fear and his affair). Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was in occultation from every special and common person. That is, the Imam (a.s.) was in occultation from every special and common person like Hazrat Yusuf. And Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.) was very worried about the affair of Yusuf (a.s.). Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.) knew that Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was alive, but still Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.) knew that Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was alive, but still he worried about him, where he was and in what state. Exactly in the same way, our belief is that the Imam (a.s.) is alive, but we do not know where the Imam is and in what state. Therefore, it should be necessary for us to worry about the Imam and pray for his safety along with his reappearance. This was one aspect regarding Ghaybah. This Ghaybah is such an important topic that there are many other similarities between Hazrat Yusuf and Imam Mahdi (a.s.). For example, when the word Ghaybah is mentioned, often opponents say that the Imam is sitting somewhere far away on an island or in a cave, or they think the Imam is limited to one place. But for us, it is a settled belief that the Imam is not limited to one place; rather, the Imam lives among us. And this can also be compared to the Ghaybah of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), that when Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was in Egypt, when his brothers met him, traded with him, bought and sold, but still they could not recognize him. In the Holy Quran, Allah Almighty describes this in this way: Allah Almighty describes this in this way: that when the brothers of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) met him, Hazrat Yusuf recognized them, but they could not recognize Hazrat Yusuf. Exactly in the same way, there is the Ghaybah of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) that we see him, but we cannot recognize him. Taking the help of a Hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) on this topic, where you (a.s.) say that indeed, the similarity of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is with Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.). So the narrator asked, 'Mawla, how? How is this similarity?' So the Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Why does this Ummah not understand that just as the affair of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was, in the same way, the affair of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is. The brothers of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) were from the progeny of Prophets. They had seen Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) in childhood and they were in front of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), but still, they could not recognize Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) until Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) introduced himself. When Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) said, "Ana Yusuf" (I am Yusuf), then his brothers recognized that yes, this is Yusuf.' The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Exactly' the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Exactly in the same way, people see Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), but until Allah gives the command, the Imam does not make himself known, and people see him but cannot recognize him.' After that, the Imam (a.s.) says that it is not that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is limited to some far-off place, but the Imam (a.s.) says that he walks in your markets and steps on your carpets, but you cannot recognize him. That is, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) lives among us, and it is possible that we have seen him, but this is the command of Allah. And the Imam (a.s.) ends his Hadith on this point that this is the command of Allah, this is the order of Allah that people should not recognize him. So, the second point we get here is that just as the brothers of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) or other people of Egypt used to see Hazrat Yusuf, but they did not know that he is the same Hujjat of Allah whom Allah has sent for their salvation. And the brothers of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) also saw him but could not recognize him. And after that, similarly in another Hadith... And after that, in another hadith, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Wa amma sunnatu min Yusufa fal-sitru, ja'alallahu baynahu wa baynal-khalqi hijaban yarawna wa la ya'rifun.' Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that there is a resemblance between Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and Prophet Yusuf (a.s.), and that is the 'Ghaybah' (occultation). Allah has placed a veil between the people and the Imam, a veil such that people see the Imam (a.s.) but do not recognize him. So, the resemblance here is not just regarding the occultation, but also that he does not reveal his identity to people until Allah gives him the command. Certainly, Tanveer Bhai, when we talk about the resemblance between Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) and Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), an interesting resemblance I would like to mention here is that when Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) was taken away from Prophet Yaqub (a.s.), despite knowing that Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) was alive, he mourned for him so much, and he was so overcome with grief that his eyes turned white, and the Holy Quran has also mentioned this. He mourned for him to such an extent, and was so overcome with grief, that his eyes turned white. The Holy Quran mentions this when Allah (t.w.t.) describes the story: 'Falamma an ja'al-bashiru alqahu 'ala wajhihi fartadda basira'—meaning when the bearer of good news brought the shirt of Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) and touched it to the eyes of Prophet Yaqub (a.s.), his vision was restored. This shirt belonged to Prophet Yusuf (a.s.), and if we look at the history of this shirt, Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) was wearing it when he was thrown into the fire, and because of this shirt, the fire could not even touch him. Through the medium of this shirt, Allah protected him, and this shirt passed down to Prophet Ishaq (a.s.), Prophet Yaqub (a.s.), and Prophet Yusuf (a.s.). Prophet Yaqub (a.s.) had tied this shirt to the arm of Prophet Yusuf (a.s.). In our traditions, the traditions of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.), it is found that this shirt passed through the Prophets (a.s.) and is now with the Ale Muhammad (a.s.), and today this shirt is with Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). By the blessing of this shirt, Prophet Yaqub (a.s.)'s vision was restored. When the reappearance (Zuhur) occurs, the companions surrounding the Imam will surround his mount, and they will touch the saddle of the Imam's mount to seek blessings. It is narrated in these words: 'Yatamassahuna bi-sarji-l-Imam (a.s.) yatamassahuna bi-tilka-l-baraka'—meaning they will touch the saddle of the Imam's mount and seek blessings from it. When it comes to healing through Imam (a.t.f.s.), I would like to narrate an incident where a Hashimi person says that he brought a guest home with him and asked his maid, 'Why don't you tell them about that newborn and the kohl applicator (surme ki salai)?' The maid began to narrate that there was a sick child in our house, and I was ordered to go and bring something from the house of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) that would heal this child. I went and said to Bibi Hakima (s.a.), 'Please give me something so that the child in our house may be healed.' Bibi Hakima (s.a.) called her maid and said, 'Go and bring that kohl applicator with which I applied kohl to the newborn child's eyes yesterday,' and she gave me that applicator. When I brought that applicator and touched it to the child, then... When I touched that applicator to the child, the child was healed. Through that applicator, whoever was sick in our house would seek healing, until that applicator was lost. Masha'Allah, Zaheer Bhai, that was a very interesting incident, and this incident reminded me of another incident where a newborn healed someone. And this newborn is none other than the ancestor of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), that is, Sayyid al-Shuhada Imam Hussain (a.s.). When Imam Hussain (a.s.) was born, and the angel (Futra) whose wings Allah had taken away, Prophet Jibraeel (a.s.) took that angel to Imam Hussain (a.s.), and the angel touched his wings to the cradle of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and was healed. So, if the cradle of Imam Hussain (a.s.) can heal an angel, why can't the kohl applicator used for Imam Mahdi (a.s.)'s eyes heal a child? Indeed, indeed. And you spoke about the shirt that Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) gave to Prophet Yaqub (a.s.) so that his eyesight would return; we find in our hadith that when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) appears, he will bring some things with him, and one of the things he will bring is this shirt... One of the things he will bring is this shirt, through which Prophet Yaqub (a.s.) received healing. Let us continue the topic: the kindness that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) or Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) showed to people was not limited to their own family, their brothers, or their father, but that grace was universal. We find this in the story of Prophet Yusuf (a.s.): Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) was in Egypt, and in his early days, the people of Egypt kept him as a slave. But by the command of Allah, by the permission of Allah, he became the Aziz of Egypt. However, when he attained that position, he did not oppress the people; rather, he became their protector and showed them the way to get rid of the famine. Exactly in the same way, when Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) was young, his brothers oppressed him and threw him into a well, but when the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) came to him seeking help, Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) did not refuse them or turn them away from his court; rather, like an affectionate brother, he helped his brothers. Exactly in the same way, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.)... Exactly in the same way, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is also the protector of his Shias, and it is his grace that we are safe today. If the gaze of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) were not upon us, we would be wiped out. It is found in a hadith where there was a person named Zareef who met the Imam (a.s.), and the Imam (a.s.) asked me a question and asked, 'Do you recognize me?' That person said, 'Indeed, you are my Mawla and the son of my Mawla.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'No, I am not asking you that.' He replied, 'Then Mawla, you know better, you give the answer.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'I am the one who brings relief (al-mutamallis), and through me, Allah removes all the troubles of my Shias and my family.' Meaning, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is the means through which Allah removes all the troubles and difficulties of the Shias. Here, I would like to narrate an incident to you; the incident is very long, and this incident is so famous that... It is so famous that our scholars, our speakers, and our Zakirs have narrated it from the pulpit many times. This is the incident of Bahrain, where there was a Nasibi king, and some Shias also lived there. Once, the minister of this Nasibi king brought a pomegranate to the king, and on it were written things that were against the Shia religion. In short, the king said to the Shias, 'Bring the answer to this.' The Shia scholars, the Shia scholars, asked the king for three days' time and said, 'Give us three days so that we can bring the answer.' The Shia gentlemen chose three people from among themselves who went far from the city and sought help from the Imam (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) came on the third day and told the person named Muhammad ibn Isa the secret of that pomegranate, and they told that secret to the king, and in this way, the Shias were saved from the king's oppression and violence. So, we have many such incidents where Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) helped his Shias, his followers... Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) helped his Shias, his followers, and saved them from tyrannical rulers. Stopping here, I would like to state one thing for the viewers: Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) himself emphasizes to us that when you have any trouble, when you have any need, remember us, and we will come to your aid. The Imam (a.s.) says that when you have any trouble, when you have a need for something, just move your lips—meaning call us—and you will see that a response will definitely come to you from us. So, this is a lesson for us, this is our responsibility, that whenever we have a problem, whenever we have a need for something, the only person to whose door we should go is our Sahib al-Amr, our Wali al-Asr, our Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Certainly, Tanveer Bhai, just as you spoke about the Imams (a.s.) protecting people, in the same way, the Imams (a.s.) also protect people's beliefs. Connecting this incident to the story of Prophet Yusuf (a.s.), when Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) was in prison, his companions who were in prison, two of them, saw a dream, and to interpret that dream, they came to Prophet... They came to Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) and said, 'Will you tell us the interpretation of this dream?' So, along with telling the interpretation of the dream, Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) also took steps to improve their beliefs and their hereafter, which Allah (t.w.t.) mentions in the Holy Quran in these words: 'Ma ta'buduna min dunihi illa asma'an sammaytumuha antum wa aba'ukum ma anzala Allahu biha min sultan'—meaning, the gods you worship are just names; they have no real existence. And while stating all these things, Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) awakened their nature and guided them towards the true Creator. In the same way, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) even today, in this era of occultation, corrects people's beliefs. We find proof of this in the lives of the Imams (a.s.) and their hadith, when Burayd al-Ijli asked Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) a question. The hadith is as follows: 'Qultu li-Abi Ja'far (a.s.) innama anta mundhirun wa likulli qawmin hadin'—meaning Burayd al-Ijli says that I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) a question... I asked Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) regarding this saying of Allah (t.w.t.): 'You are only a warner, and for every nation, there is a guide.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Fa-qala (a.s.) al-mundhiru Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.).' Meaning, correcting people's beliefs, reforming their beliefs, protecting their beliefs is an important duty that the Imam (a.s.) performs, and in this way, the Imam (a.s.) has a great favor upon our necks. Zaheer Bhai, this is a very important point you have stated, that just as Prophet Yusuf (a.s.) used to guide people even while in prison, so the prison did not limit him... He used to guide, and imprisonment did not limit him from being able to guide people. Similarly, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), although not visibly before us, does not mean that Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) does not guide people. Allah (s.w.t.) has sent us into this world for the hereafter, and there are many verses in the Quran where Allah (s.w.t.) declares that Allah has made this world a means for the hereafter so that people may succeed in the test of this world. So, Allah sent guides and leaders (Hadi) from His side who continuously guided people. If people's journey toward the hereafter does not stop, then would Allah disconnect His guide from the people so that he cannot guide them? If that were to happen, the very purpose for which Allah sent people into this world would be nullified. Just as Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) was in prison yet was a guide and guided people, in the same way, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), although in occultation (ghaybah), guides the people. And this hadith you narrated is clear evidence of that. So, a guide who is from Allah may be silent, but a guide... may be silent, but a guide does not stop performing his duty, whether he is present or absent. When that Arab told him about his destination, Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) said, 'When you pass through a certain valley, stop there and call out: O Yaqub, O Yaqub!' Hearing this voice, a person of great status will appear, who will be well-built and very handsome. Taking this message of Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), the Arab left, and just as Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.) had said, when he began to pass through that valley, he stopped and raised his voice, 'O Yaqub, O Yaqub!' Hearing this message, Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.) fainted and fell. When he recovered from his faint, he asked the Arab, 'O Arab, do you have any need?' Through the prayer of Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.), Allah (tabarak wa ta'ala) granted that person children.
