title: E'teraazaate Ghadeer Ep#06: Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.) Ne Ghadeer Ke Ailaan Mein Takheer Ki?
excerpt: This lecture addresses common historical objections regarding the timing and delivery of the Ghadir Khumm announcement by Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It explores the significance of the Verse of Tabligh and the divine mandate to declare Ali ibn Abi Talib's (a.s.) leadership, emphasizing that the Prophet never delayed divine instructions. The discussion further examines the internal opposition faced by the Prophet, including the incident of pen and paper, and highlights how political interests and disobedience led some companions to reject the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt.

So one should think that if you do not deliver this message in the way it was meant to be, then the religion we have brought will not reach us. Indeed, very important points have been pointed out by you, that the revelation was made to the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) that... The revelation was made to the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) that this is for us, if this message is not delivered, then the whole of Islam is not complete. And the second thing, in this same verse, the Lord of the Worlds says, 'wa Allahu ya'simuka minan-nas' (And Allah will protect you from the people). This means it is telling us that in this, this message is such that both of these will not be liked by the people. There is a possibility of rebellion by the people, they might rebel against this message, they might refuse to accept this message. If you are in this whole situation, this is found. And as we saw in the previous episode, you showed many narrations from your books that when the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) was in the world, how much he was troubled, they used to complain about him repeatedly, and here his Wilayah, his faith is being tested. Indeed, and all those things will be completely destroyed... those who were the companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... indeed, and now see, in this, the verse that follows, 'innallaha la yahdil-qawmal-kafirin' (Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people). The Lord of the Worlds also knows that the people's faith is in the Messenger (s.a.w.a.)... The Lord of the Worlds knows that the people's faith is in the Messenger (s.a.w.a.). At that time, whatever companions were present, how they were recognizing the life of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), this is a question, so Allah knows very well that there will be such people among them, all these things... it is not that all of them are the companions of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.)... they will accept it very easily, but when this command came from Allah to the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) that 'O Messenger, deliver this, worship Allah', when this happened, after that, when he was about to go, after that, he called Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and said to them, 'Deliver this in the way...' This proves that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) did not refuse this matter at all, rather, to deliver any word of Allah, the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) never said anything. Indeed, he never refused to deliver any word, any message. And this which you said, but here it is also necessary for our viewers to understand what kind of people these were. Who were these people? Among them, there were many such people who... that is why Mecca was conquered... There were many such people who... that is why Mecca was conquered. This means there were many such people who, after accepting Islam, did things... it happened that there were always some individuals who had a negative mindset, who from the beginning used to oppose the Messenger (s.a.w.a.). They said, 'No, we will not listen,' they used to forbid. Even they were there, and the world and history are present, which says about these people how these people disobeyed the Messenger (s.a.w.a.). They disobeyed, this is all... you see, this Muslim always... about Friday, very... absolutely, and the Friday prayer, which we understood, what happened, you want to say, here, little by little, for the Friday prayer, preparations start. For 10 minutes, from the prayer... For 10 minutes, from the prayer, preparations start, and the last verse of Surah Jumu'ah, what do we do? That... when these people, when they used to hear the call, when they used to write, 'Come, O Messenger of Allah', all these things used to return to their homes, then what used to happen? They used to leave the prayer immediately and run towards those things. That is the verse, and you will have to read it, leaving the prayer, and they were thinking that they could not be right. In the eyes of the people, they were companions, but these people were very much... and who were those people who left the prayer and went to their business and their trade? Here we get this thing, that what kind of companions of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) were they? If we look at what the definition of a companion is, it is found that whoever saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in a state of faith, even once, then he is called a companion, he is counted. But these are those who are not only Muslims, but they pray behind the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.), but as soon as there is some noise outside, they leave the Prophet and go outside. You can imagine what type of companions they were, of what level they were. From this, it is also proven that every person who... It is established that every person who has seen the philosophy of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—it is not necessary that they were completely righteous—they were troubled and distressed. Let us point towards their worship; it is not that we are [perfect], but we mention the names of all people. Those who consider themselves companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—those who do this—they cannot do it in this way because, after that, this is also a big thing. Furthermore, other things were also extracted from the Seerah, which they used to perform. Certainly, they used to drink alcohol, but just to justify it, to legitimize it, what did they do? They used to do this; they did not take care of their hair. It was not alcohol; it was named 'Navees'. These things, but in reality... These 'Navees' things, but in reality, we can say that they changed the names of their actions just to justify them. In this way, they used to commit these sins. There are many accounts of this. And it should be kept in mind that wherever people opposed the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in 1857 or other times, they burned in the fire of rebellion. You will see this in our upcoming episodes, and we will tell you how they behaved. I am giving clear instructions to those people: whatever happens, they should remain firm in their place. What was the result? When they saw that the Muslims were winning, they ran to take the spoils of war, which caused the enemy to attack, and the Muslims suffered losses. Why? Because of the disobedience of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Whoever does not follow the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will face nothing but loss. This is absolutely true, and this is not just for them; look at other places, for example, the 39 days of the Battle of Khaybar... For 39 days in the Battle of Khaybar, the enemy challenged [the Muslims], asking who would come and fight. But the Muslims were given the message: 'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), rely on yourself, rely on this mission.' They fought for 40 days. After that, there were other small battles. And everyone knows that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Bring me paper and pen so I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray,' the people said, 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is hallucinating.' He said, 'I am writing for you something after which you will never go astray.' And this is in number 4, December, page 409... In number 4, December, page 409, it is written, but only there. The people who were there, some of them could not go there. The names were not mentioned there, but the people here found out that if these people do not refrain from their actions, then this will happen. There are four books, but if, as in others, the names of those people were mentioned, then in this century, they are doing this. In number 6, 64454, it is not said when this happened, but the information regarding the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s companions is present. The information is present, but despite this, in that situation, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s companions—one should use such language for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s companions? Does anyone know this? We spend our whole lives because of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Muslims recite the Kalima because of him, and against him, such language is used. Here, the word 'Hajr' (delirium) was used. But if one goes to Sahih Bukhari, Hadith number 696, Hadith number 90, if one goes to that Hadith, the name is written there: who said this sentence? 'We have the Book of Allah, so the Book is enough for us.' Here you can see how, in the final moments, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was telling the people, 'Bring me paper and pen so I may write something for you after which you will never go astray.' How can these companions disobey the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s command? Along with that, they are also saying that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is not in his right mind. Such language they were using for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). They were using such language for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Why? I feel that because from the beginning until now, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had always conveyed only Ali (a.s.) to the people. So this was the fear, or rather, it was certain that if he were given paper and pen, he would write nothing but Ali (a.s.). And it would become completely clear that after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), if we have to follow anyone, it is him. Without a doubt, they would oppose him. They would oppose the one whom Allah had appointed as the successor after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Vizier, the one who would be the leader after him—Ali (a.s.). And for these people, this fact was unbearable. This fact was unbearable to them: how can they accept Ali (a.s.) as their leader? Because, as mentioned earlier, a large number of people who became Muslim after the conquest of Mecca—before becoming Muslim, they had come to fight against the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). They opposed him in all those places, and their behavior and character were such. Ali (a.s.) is the one who... Ali (a.s.) is the one who brought them to the level of humanity. When these people, and some of their descendants who accepted Islam after the conquest of Mecca, were present in the Ummah, the fear was that if this announcement were made, they might revert to their old ways. This was the concern of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) at that time. He was concerned about those people who might revert to their old ways when they saw that we have to follow the same Ali (a.s.) whom we had fought against. While he had done nothing on his own; whatever he did, he did as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told him. So, they would revert to their old ways. Therefore, this is called the 'Sahifa' (document), and in previous history, such things are found. We also observe that all these things are based on politics. And after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), those people who accepted the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.)—that whole matter was political. Politics is such a thing that, as is famous in English... As is famous in English, 'There are no permanent friends and no permanent enemies, only permanent interests.' So this whole politics was such that because of it, people went in a different direction instead of following the truth, and they refused to accept the Wilayah and leadership of Ali (a.s.). But when Allah (s.w.t.) commanded, 'Do not fear, Allah will protect you,' then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made the announcement at Ghadir. And here, it is important for all of us to know that this announcement—'Allah will help you'—is not just for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.); it is a message for us as well. Allah will protect us as long as we follow the path of Ali (a.s.). This message is not just for that occasion; this message is for whenever and wherever the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), is followed, and his Wilayah and leadership are accepted, death will never come [in the sense of spiritual loss]. Allah... Allah will protect us. It is our responsibility to spread this message to the world as much as possible, to bring more people towards this path. This is a part of the mission. As we have seen, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not deny any message from Allah, but he conveyed the best message in the best place and in the best way. Yes, with this, our 'Nabuwwat' series ends here. We hope you all liked the episodes, and we thank you from the bottom of our hearts for watching our series. We also hope that you will convey the message of this series to others. We believe...

title: Imam-e-Hasan-e-Askari (a.s.) Ki Shahaadat | 8th #RabiulAwwal
excerpt: This lecture recounts the martyrdom of the eleventh Shia Imam, Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), who passed away on the 8th of Rabi' al-Awwal in 260 AH after being poisoned. It highlights the historical context of his life in Samarra, the concealment of his son, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), due to intense political persecution, and the significance of his burial alongside his father. The talk concludes with a prayer for the hastening of the reappearance of the awaited Imam.
content:
The martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.): On the 1st of Rabi' al-Awwal, 260 AH, Abu Muhammad, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), was poisoned, which caused him to fall severely ill. After eight days, on the 8th of Rabi' al-Awwal, a Friday in 260 AH, his martyrdom occurred. At that time, his blessed age was 28 years. He was buried in the same room where his noble father, Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.), was buried, which was their house in Samarra. He left behind his son, who is the awaited one for the establishment of truth. He had kept the birth of his son hidden and his affairs concealed due to the severity of the times and the intense search by the king of that era. That king was trying very hard to find him because the belief of the Shia Imamiyyah regarding him had become well-known, and it was also known that they were waiting for him. Therefore, he did not reveal his son during his lifetime, nor could the common people recognize him after his martyrdom. We pray to Allah (s.w.t.) to send His severe punishment upon the killers of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and to hasten the reappearance of his heir and the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

He was poisoned and suffered for eight days before his passing at the age of 28.
He is buried in his house in Samarra alongside his father, Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.).
The birth of his son, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), was kept hidden due to severe political threats.
The Abbasid rulers were actively searching for the Imam's successor to prevent the rise of the awaited savior.
The concealment of the Imam's son was a strategic necessity for his protection.

title: Majlis 1 | Dushmani Aur Dosti Ka Me'yaar: Wilaayat-e-Ahle Bait (a.s) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the fundamental theological concept of Wilayah (allegiance) to the Ahlulbayt and its inseparable counterpart, Bara'at (disassociation from their enemies). The discourse emphasizes that true faith requires a clear stance against oppression and an unwavering commitment to the path of the Imams. By examining historical precedents and spiritual gnosis, the lecture highlights how love for the Ahlulbayt is tested through trials and serves as the essential foundation for attaining proximity to Allah.
content:
Shahr-e-Khidama, Shahr-e-Ya Hussain. Shahr-e-Khidama, Shahr-e-Ya Hussain. Shahr-e-Khidama, O the wounded body of Zahra's son, my Hussain, Hussain. O the wounded body of Zahra's son, my Hussain, Hussain. You did not even find a shroud, my Hussain, Hussain. My oppressed one, my hungry one, my thirsty one. My oppressed one, my hungry one, my thirsty one. My martyr of desires, my Hussain, Hussain. O the wounded body of Zahra's son, my Hussain, Hussain. Oh, I have come from heaven to mourn you, my son. I have come from heaven to mourn you, my son. Give me consolation by rising, my Hussain, Hussain. And the settlement of Shaam is inhabited, Medina is desolate. The settlement of Shaam is inhabited, Medina is desolate. My shrine is empty, my Hussain, Hussain. O the wounded body of Zahra's son, my Hussain, Hussain. Was it for this that Fatima raised you? Was it for this that Fatima raised you? Oh, the body of my Hussain, Hussain, is lying in the sun. O the wounded body of Zahra's son, my Hussain, Hussain. You did not even find a shroud, my Hussain, Hussain. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim. Bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'ali al-'azim. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man nasir. Alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin, wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqin. Wa as-salatu wa as-salamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya'i wal mursalin, habibi ilahil 'alamin, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi al-ma'sumin, alladhina adhhaba Allahu 'anhum ar-rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sima, sima Baqiyatullah fil-ardhin, Imam-e-Zamanina, huwa wali amrina wa sahibuna wa mawlana wa habibuna wa tabibuna wa anisuna wa munisuna, al-kahf al-hasin wa ghiyath al-mudtar al-mustakin, ruhi wa arwah al-'alamin lahu al-fida'. Amma ba'd, faqad qala Allahu tabaraka wa ta'ala wa jalla jalaluhu fi kitabihi al-karim, wa qawluhu al-haqq wa huwa asdaq al-qa'ilin: 'Ma ja'ala Allahu lirajulin min qalbayni fi jawfihi'. Sadaqa Allahu al-'ali al-'azim. Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. The hadith and the verse of the Quran that I have chosen for this discussion is verse number four of Surah Al-Ahzab, which I have made the heading of my speech: 'Ma ja'ala Allahu lirajulin min qalbayni fi jawfihi' (Allah has not made for any man two hearts in his interior). Allah has not placed two hearts in the interior of any human being; He has placed only one heart, that is all. The topic, Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the ability and if the series continues, bi-awnillah (by the help of Allah), Insha'Allah, wa quwwatihi wa hawlihi (and His power and might), then Wilayah and Bara'at. Insha'Allah, and in the light of these two narrations of the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.), it is obvious that you all know about their importance. Therefore, the effort will be to present some points from these that will, Insha'Allah, become a cause for the strengthening of Wilayah and Bara'at. Recite one Salawat for Muhammad and Aal-e-Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. The fundamental principle of Wilayah and Bara'at is not just to love Muhammad and Aal-e-Muhammad and to dissociate from their enemies. That is the fundamental principle, and look at the secret behind it, look at the mystery. Rather, we should love those who love them, and we should be enemies to those who are enemies to them. We should love those who love the Aal-e-Muhammad and accept their Wilayah, and we should accept their Wilayah, no matter how many flaws they may have. This is the test. This is the test. And we should hate and be enemies to their enemies, those who have malice towards them, we should have malice towards them, no matter how good they may appear outwardly. And in today's context, you know better yourself how important this has become. You must have seen a clip recently. You must have seen it. Where someone said that the kings of Banu Umayya and Banu Abbas should be praised. Just think. I mean, they were patrons of knowledge. Strange. Patrons of knowledge. I mean, those who killed our Imams (a.s.), who martyred them—you are sitting on the pulpit of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and promoting their Wilayah. In this context, it becomes even more important that we know these things well and understand them thoroughly so that the true Wilayah remains in our hearts. And these are not superficial things that exist in the hearts of common people, which are like the example where when the wind blows, 'yameeluna ma kulle reeh' (they incline with every wind), they lean that way. 'Atba'u kulle na'iq'—they follow every 'na'iq'. In Arabic, 'na'iq' refers to someone who makes the sound of a crow. One who makes the sound of a crow is called a 'na'iq'. This is an Arabic word; we are not saying anything from ourselves. It is an Arabic word. 'Na'iq', meaning one who makes the sound of a crow—Nun, Alif, Ayn, Qaf. It is an Arabic word, yes. So, there is no need for anyone to take offense. So, 'atba'u kulle na'iq'—they follow every speaker. Whatever anyone says. 'La yastadhi'una bi nur-il-ilm'—they do not benefit from the light of knowledge at all, they do not take guidance from it. I mean, because they do not have knowledge, and if they do not have knowledge, they do not have intellect. Therefore, they cannot distinguish between good and evil, they cannot understand. So, such Wilayah and such Bara'ah should not exist where one starts following whoever speaks next and starts believing them. Anyway, I will try to present as many Hadith as possible in your service, for as many days as this series of gatherings continues, if Allah grants the opportunity. So, the first Hadith is from Imam Ja'far—I mean Imam Baqir, Imam Abu Ja'far, Imam Baqir (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Regarding this verse of the Quran, which has been made the heading of the discourse: 'Ma ja'allahu lirajulin min qalbayni fi jawfihi' (Allah has not placed two hearts in the chest of any man). Keeping this verse in mind, the Imam says: 'Fayuhibbu bihadha wa yubghidu bihadha' (He loves with this and hates with this). With this same heart, he loves, and with this same heart, he hates; so both things cannot exist at the same time. Either there will be love for someone, or there will be hatred for someone. Yes. This is the principle, so you cannot say that we love the Ahlulbayt with the same heart, and with the same heart, we also love the kings of Banu Umayyah, the kings of Banu Abbas, love their killers, and also love the one who was killed. For everyone—this is the way of those who say about everyone: the killer is also 'Radiyallahu' (may Allah be pleased with him) and the victim is also 'Radiyallahu'. The envious one is 'Radiyallahu', and the one envied is 'Radiyallahu'. The usurper is 'Radiyallahu', and the one whose right was usurped is 'Radiyallahu'. This is their way. The way of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is not this. This is not the way of Allah. This is not the way of the Prophets (a.s.). Allah has taken a stand throughout the Holy Quran; look at it. Nowhere did Allah say that Satan was a very good man but had a few minor flaws. Wow. He was very good, a pious servant. He just didn't prostrate. Otherwise, look at him, praise him, yes. Satan was a patron of worship. Satan was a patron of worship. That he used to worship so much, what a prostration he used to perform. Yes? Can you say that? Has Allah said this in the Quran? Then how are you saying it? That Banu Umayyah, the kings of Banu Abbas—and the Imam says: 'Fayuhibbu bihadha wa yubghidu bihadha'. 'Fa'amma muhibbuna fayukhlisu al-hubba lana kama yukhlisu az-zahabu bin-nar' (As for our lovers, they purify their love for us just as gold is purified in fire). The one who is our 'Muhib' (lover), the one who loves us—Allah tests him. As there is a saying in English, 'Baptism by fire' or 'Test by fire'. They use these idioms in English. Meaning, Allah tests him, and this test is severe. And what does the Imam give as an example, what kind of simile? Gold. When gold is raw, that gold is put into fire. Through fire, the gold is purified, cleansed, so that all its impurities, the filth in it, is removed. Similarly, the one who is a lover of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), Allah tests him severely so that it becomes clear and evident who is a true lover and who has only come outwardly. It will be known immediately. And look, in the context of Karbala, Sayyidush-Shuhada (a.s.) was repeatedly testing his lovers for this very reason. And look how pure they were. That Sayyidush-Shuhada, until the night of Ashura—and this is not just a statement of the night of Ashura, yes. I mean, this test is not just for the night of Ashura. If you read the history of Karbala, Sayyidush-Shuhada has been saying from the beginning, from Medina, that I am going for martyrdom. Whoever wants to come, come with me. He is announcing it beforehand. He is announcing beforehand that look, I am going for martyrdom. Now, whoever wants to come, let them come. Meaning, the coward, the timid one, should stay behind; they are not needed. I only need those individuals who walk with their lives on their palms. Who are not afraid of death, who say about death: 'La nubali bil-mawt, la nubali bil-mawt' (We do not care about death). We do not care about death. Whether death comes upon us or we go upon death, it makes no difference. 'Alasna alal-haqq?' (Are we not on the truth?). 'Idhan la nubali bil-mawt' (Then we do not care about death). That is the end of the matter. So, whoever is brave, courageous, will never be afraid. 'Afaman assasa bunyanahu ala taqwan min Allahi wa ridwanin khair' (Is he who founded his building on piety from Allah and [His] pleasure better?). He recites the verse again. 'Afaman assasa bunyanahu' (Is he who founded his building...). The Quran is asking, it is asking the intellect, the human intellect. Which of the two is better? The one whose foundation is on 'Taqwan min Allahi wa ridwan' (Piety from Allah and pleasure). Fear of Allah, regard for Allah, he fears Allah and he is pleased with Allah, 'Ridwan'. Is he better? 'Aman assasa bunyanahu ala shafa jurufin harin' (Or is he who founded his building on the edge of a crumbling bank?). Or is he who places his building, his structure, on the edge of a river that has become hollow and is breaking? Subhan Allah. That is, the building of hypocrisy, the foundation of hypocrisy is like this. You understand the point; this is the Quran's simile. In Surah at-Tawbah, verse 109, Allah is giving a simile. It is a foundation, 'Nuh (a.s.) ala shafa jurufin harin'. That is, here you see, if someone builds a house on the edge of the sea, if someone builds a house on the beach, that beach is hollow, and here the Quran says it is not only hollow but also cracking, it is splitting. The house of hypocrisy is like this, the building of hypocrisy is like this, the building of hypocrisy is like this, the building of hypocrisy is like this, and the building of piety is very strong. That is, this building of hypocrisy is so weak that the Quran has said it is like, that is, weaker than the house of a spider. That is, the foundation of hypocrisy is weaker than the foundation of disbelief. In the Quran, regarding his house, it is said, 'Inna awhanal buyuti labaytul ankabut' (Indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider), it is a verse of Surah al-Ankabut. Whose house is the weakest? The spider's web. But even the spider's web stays for a few days. It also stays for a few days. Until someone sweeps it away. When he sweeps it, that web will vanish. But the foundation of hypocrisy, the building, is such that as soon as it is built, it cracks. But 'Wa hum la yash'urun' (And they do not perceive it). They do not understand the matter. They think that we are on a building, we are living in a building. They are not living in a building; they have already sunk. They are unable to understand the matter. The Mawla of the universe takes the support of this verse and says, 'Fa-ka'anna dhalika shafa jurufin harin bihi fi nari jahannam' (And this thing is, it is a Quranic verse, 'Fa-anhara bihi fi nari jahannam'—and it collapses with him into the fire of Hell), 'Wallahu la yahdil qawmaz-zalimin' (And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people). The Quran's Mawla of the universe, taking the support of this verse, says that these go straight to Hell. These hypocrites will go straight to Hell. 'Wa kana babur-rahmati qad futihat li-ahliha' (And the doors of mercy have been opened for those who are the people of mercy). 'Wa... li-ahlir-rahmati rahmatuhu wat-ta'asu li-ahlin-nar' (And for the people of mercy is His mercy, and for the people of the Fire is destruction, nothing else). 'Wan-naru lahum jahannam' (And the Fire, for them, is Hell). And then after that, the Imam repeats that tradition: 'O Hubaysh, if anyone wants to know if he is our lover or the lover of our enemy, then he should examine his own heart.' In kana yuhibbu waliyyan lana—if he loves one of our lovers—it does not say if he loves us, but if he loves our lovers, then he cannot be our enemy. And if he loves our enemies, he cannot be our lover. Both Imams have clarified this. Wala yasa bi-ahmad, innallaha ta'ala akhadha mithaqal muhibbina—Allah had taken this covenant in the realm of 'Dhar' (pre-existence). He had taken the covenant of our love and affection beforehand, and then wa kataba fi-dhikri—in the Wise Remembrance (Quran), Allah had already written down the names of the 'Mubghizeen' (those who hate us). The names of all those who harbor enmity towards us were written by Allah in the Wise Remembrance beforehand. Everyone's name is already written, everyone's name is already present. So, do not worry too much. If someone goes astray and says it is the patronage of Banu Umayya and Banu Abbas, understand that their name was already written there. It is just a coincidence that they were born here. Coincidences and incidents keep happening in the world. Incidents keep happening in the world, so do not worry too much. Do not worry at all about such people, because these are the people for whom Hell is written. And then He says, 'Nahnu Nujaba'—we are the chosen, noble ones of Allah, we are the 'Najeeb'. The Imam says, 'Wa afratuna afratul Anbiya'—and our progeny is the progeny of the Prophets. Do not consider our progeny ordinary. So, the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) stated this. A lot of time has passed, so just a few sentences of 'Masaib' (tragedies) for you, as these are the days of mourning and lamentation. Imam Ridha (a.s.) says: 'Man tadhakkara musabana wa baka lima urtukiba minna kana ma'ana fi darajatina yawmal qiyamah'—whoever remembers our tragedy and weeps for what was committed against us, will be with us at our rank on the Day of Judgment. 'Wa man dhukkira bi-musabana fabaka wa abka lam tabka aynuhu yawma tabkil uyun'—and whoever is reminded of our tragedy and weeps and makes others weep, his eyes will not weep on the day when all eyes will weep. 'Wa man jalasa majlisan yuhya fihi amruna lam yamut qalbuhu yawma tamutul qulub'—and whoever sits in a gathering where our cause is revived, where our Wilayat is revived, his heart will not die on the day when all hearts will die. On that day, his heart will be alive; his heart will not die. Yes, mourners, today I am going to mention a martyr whose Ziyarat you recite: 'Assalamu alayka ayyuhal abdus saleh wal muti'u lillahi wa li rasulihi wa li amiril mu'minina wal hasani wal husayn.' We are mentioning Janab-e-Muslim, Janab-e-Muslim ibn Aqeel, whose martyrdom you know how it occurred. Janab-e-Muslim reached Kufa, was a guest at the house of Janab-e-Mukhtar, and people came; at least 18,000 Kufans pledged allegiance at his hands. I do not have to recite the entire tragedy, just listen to a few sentences of the Masaib. Janab-e-Muslim was such a personality that when he came to Kufa to lead the prayer, the mosque was overflowing, but as soon as he said 'Assalamu alaykum wa Rahmatullah', he saw the mosque was empty. You know the rest of the tragedy, that Muslim became a stranger in that same Kufa, and there was no one to give refuge to that same Muslim. Until Muslim was arrested, brought to the gallows, and Muslim was beheaded. Before being beheaded, Muslim was wounded. Muslim asked for a little water so he could drink, but look at the effect of the water—look at the effect of the water on Muslim—that when the water was brought, as soon as he tried to drink it, blood from his mouth fell into the water, the water became impure, Muslim did not drink the water, he threw it away. He turned once and said, 'Assalamu alayka ya Aba Abdillah, Assalamu alayka ya Ibna Rasulillah', he saluted Husayn, and Husayn replied. You know you recite the Ziyarat of Janab-e-Muslim, this sentence: 'Wa salamun ala ibadihilladhina istafa Muhammadin wa alihi, wa jazakallahu afdalal jaza wa aufaral jaza jaza'an mimman wafa li-bay'atihi'—peace be upon His servants whom He chose, Muhammad and his family, and may Allah reward you with the best reward, the most abundant reward, the reward of one who fulfilled his allegiance, 'wa tajaza walahu da'watahu'—whose prayer is answered, who obeyed his Imam. Regarding Hazrat-e-Muslim, Imam Husayn's (a.s.) sentence: 'Wa ashhadu annaka qad balaghta fin-nasiha wa atayta ghayatal majhud'—I bear witness that you reached the limit in sincerity and exerted the utmost effort possible. Here Muslim was beheaded and Muslim fell from the balcony. Here Muslim was martyred. They came, Imam Husayn (a.s.) started stroking the head of the orphan of Muslim. He asked, 'Uncle, you are treating me as one treats orphans.' I would say, O orphan of Muslim, alas, it was Husayn who was stroking the head, alas, Sakina came, what did she say, 'Father, the Ziyarat remained there.' Sakina, Sakina, they will take Husayn's Tazia, they will take Husayn's Tazia, this tribe, the tribe that healed, wa Muslima, wa Sakina, wa Muhammada, mourning for Husayn. Sayyeda, peace be upon Zahra, peace be upon Zahra.

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Ziyaarat Ka Maqsad [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual purpose behind performing the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.). While many pilgrims visit with personal requests or needs, the speaker emphasizes that the highest intention is to offer sincere condolences to the Ahlulbayt for the tragedy of Karbala. By doing so, pilgrims align themselves with the love of the Prophet and his family, ultimately earning a place under the banner of the Messenger of Allah on the Day of Judgment.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Whoever goes for the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) has their own specific intention. Some go for the sake of Allah, some to seek the fulfillment of their needs, and some to ask Imam Husayn (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to fulfill their desires. Although all these intentions are valid in their place, and Allah (s.w.t.) will reward every person according to their intention, the most beautiful purpose of this Ziyarat was told to us by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'When the Day of Judgment comes, where is Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.)? Where are the pilgrims of Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.)?' Then, from among all the people, such a group will rise that no one except Allah (s.w.t.) can count them. They will be asked, 'What was your intention...' On the Day of Resurrection, when you are asked with what intention you went for the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.), you will answer: 'O Lord, we went solely out of love for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Imam Ali (a.s.), and Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.m.a.), and to offer condolences to Imam Hussain (a.s.) for his tragedy.' You will be told: 'These are Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, Hassan, and Hussain (a.s.); join them, for you shall be with them at their rank.' You will then go towards the banner of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and you will quickly gather under the banner of the Messenger and in his shade. That banner will be in the hands of Imam Ali (a.s.), and all those people will enter Paradise while being gathered around that banner from all sides. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) has drawn our attention to a profound truth through this hadith, the depth of which perhaps most of us do not realize. We do not realize that it is humanity to offer condolences to someone and their family upon their tragedy. It is a demand of humanity, and when this condolence is offered upon the martyrdom of the son of the Messenger to his grandfather and his parents, it becomes something greater than humanity—it becomes a divine act. That is why even today, people are seen in the holy shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.) on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O Hussain!' May Allah grant us the opportunity to go to Karbala and offer these condolences to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and especially to the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Majlis #7 Khauf-e-Khuda (Fear of God) | Ahle Bait (a.s.): Daawate Husnaa | Muharram 1443
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound concept of Khauf-e-Khuda (Fear of God) through the lens of the sacrifices made by Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt during the tragedy of Karbala. It emphasizes that true fear of God is not mere dread, but a state of reverence and constant awareness rooted in love, knowledge, and the pursuit of Taqwa. The discourse highlights how this spiritual consciousness empowers believers to resist worldly tyrants, uphold the rights of others, and remain steadfast in their commitment to divine mission.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance. O Allah, make us among those who mourn the oppressed one, the martyr of Karbala, and grant us the intercession of Hussain (a.s.) on the day of great fear. O Allah, make our hearts filled with the love of Hussain (a.s.). Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Ali. Peace be upon you, O Fatima. Peace be upon you, O Hassan. Peace be upon you, O Hussain. Peace be upon the Imams of the progeny of Hussain. Peace be upon the martyrs of Karbala. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Ali. Peace be upon you, O Fatima. Peace be upon you, O Hassan. Peace be upon you, O Hussain. Peace be upon the martyrs of Karbala. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Ali. Peace be upon you, O Fatima. Peace be upon you, O Hassan. Peace be upon you, O Hussain. Peace be upon the martyrs of Karbala. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, accept our small efforts and forgive our sins for the sake of Hussain (a.s.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, grant us the Ziyarat of Hussain (a.s.) in this world and his intercession in the hereafter. Hussain is the beloved of the Prophet. Hussain is the son of Abu Turab (Ali). Hussain is the rose blooming in the worship of God. In every mouth, there is the mention of Hussain. He is the one who defines the meaning of sacrifice. He is the one who defines the meaning of martyrdom. Hussain is the one who defines the meaning of martyrdom. Where else can one find a Hussain? He is like a rose blooming on a branch. If the blood is pure, the lineage is pure. Go and offer your salutations with respect. The court is open, come quickly. The banner is raised, come quickly. The door is still open, come quickly. The world of Haider (a.s.) is the 14th, it is very profound. Oh, the chador is one of personality. My Hussain (a.s.) is the essence... Oh, the chador, the way it is meant to be gathered, and the way it is meant to be gathered on the face; the charity of my Hussain (a.s.) is about to be distributed. So, Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) was Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). He reached the principles, he was the one to write the essence. He reached the principles of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) worship. If the prayer of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is considered invalid, then say that the prayer of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is invalid. She was mourning her brother, she had no fear of the oppressors, she had no fear of the oppressors, nor of the cruelty. There is no fear of the oppressors, nor of the cruelty and oppression. The courage of those who are oppressed is immense. The palace of destiny, the palace of the judge, in which there is the truth. This man, this afternoon, the courage of his own... from the side that is in the influence, here is the step, when the patient arrives, it becomes forbidden in the city of the enemy. The perfection is that the heart is different, the perfection is that the heart is different, the same majesty, the same attitude, the same majesty, the same attitude. When Hussain (a.s.) used to step into the battlefield, the army of Sham used to tremble. How many were sacrificed for him? It is not understood how many Hussain (a.s.) there are. It is not understood how many Hussain (a.s.) there are. Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the one from whom the fear of the enemy has been removed. The enmity of Yazid should be called Karbala. We are being erased, yet we are still found; we need the taste of the love of Ali (a.s.). Throughout my life, my entire life was spent in this, and my heart was Karbala and Hussain (a.s.). Many people entered the hearts of many, but no one could settle in the heart except Hussain (a.s.). There was no solution for them except for Hussain (a.s.). Thus, the people of loyalty went towards Hussain (a.s.). They did not go towards those who were without principles. The question remains for everyone until now: will you go in the direction the wind blows? Why don't you understand, brother? What is good and what is evil? The killer of Fatima (s.a.) will never find salvation. What happened? One must meet the truth. And yes, upon the rules and regulations, we are two glasses... [Music] Peace and blessings be upon the master of the messengers... [Music] May Allah's blessings be upon him and his family. Oh mind, take the path of righteousness... [Music] And do not follow the path of the misguided... [Music] May Allah guide us. And as for the command, bring it forth... [Music] In the Holy Quran, Allah (s.w.t.) is commanding: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction.' This is the way to invite people to the religion—with wisdom and beautiful preaching. We have forgotten this; we are busy with other things instead of inviting people to the path of Allah. In the religion, there is no room for harshness. It is not about being superior; it is about the essence of the message. The best invitation is one that teaches the religion with kindness so that people understand what the religion is. Those who leave the path of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) and follow other paths based on doubt—I am saying this clearly—it is not because of the religion, nor because of arrogance, nor because of oppression. It is about spreading the truth of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). It has become clear in the age of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) that Islam means... if you want to prepare people in that same way, it means Islam means that Wilayah and Imamate upon which the religion is founded. Renew the Wilayah so that people understand what is meant by religion. And this is why, after that, so that He may bring His servants out of darkness, and from blindness, and from... From blindness, and from misguidance, and from doubt, and from ignorance—to bring them out of all these things. To bring people out of all these things—misguidance and everything else—and lead them towards the path of guidance, so that people understand what guidance is, and what the true and correct path is. And then, after that, the preparation... that which is from Allah, to read it, this was the subject... If I were to bring forth that which allows a human to attain salvation—the delicacy of a human, the essence—the thing that provides employment to the unemployed, it should be the fear of Allah (Khuda). It should be present in a human both in solitude and in public. It is not that one only shows off in front of others; they fear people greatly, yet commit sins in solitude. It should not be like that. So, let us see what this fear is and what its components are. First, those who can attain salvation through this, their worship, their prayer, and their success are achieved through it. And the word used is 'Ma'rifat' (gnosis/recognition). And that is why you see this prayer: 'O Allah, who is it that fears You but does not dread You? Who recognizes You but is not afraid of You?' Who is it that recognizes You but is not afraid of You? And he knows who You are, and he is in awe of You; there is a sense of reverence in his heart. It is strange, is it not? It is not that a human recognizes Allah and is afraid of Him, but rather, he has a sense of reverence in his heart. Those who love Allah, they are the ones who are truly pious. So, when you come to the people, when you come to the Book, you say, 'This is it.' And to fully understand it, you need these gifts. And this entire book is about fearing Allah properly, not just pretending. Do not make false promises, for if you do, the consequences will be severe. If you harbor false hopes, these false hopes will lead you to the very thing you are trying to avoid. To be ignorant means to not recognize the reality of things. He does not recognize the truth, and he follows the path of his own desires. The one who walks on the right path is the one who is guided. But the one who goes astray, he will fall. So, look at the whisperings of the devil (Iblis). Iblis whispers into the heart of a human, making him feel that he should fear Allah, but then he incites him to do things that are against the will of Allah, and he gives him false hope in the mercy of Allah while making him commit acts that are against that very mercy. He incites him to do things that are against the will of Allah and gives him hope in the mercy of Allah, while making him commit acts that are against that mercy. Many people fall into this trap. This is the greatest deception. If you harbor false hopes, you will be led away from the purpose of Allah. You will think you are safe, but both of these things are wrong. To feel safe from the plan of Allah is one of the major sins. It is narrated that feeling secure from the plan of Allah is a major sin. Therefore, the believers, their nature, their temperament, is that they fear Allah. And what does it mean to fear Allah? Our Imam (a.s.) says—and these are beautiful words—that... These are beautiful words: 'He who has fear, he has...' On the Day of Judgment, a person will see and realize that all these people were innocent. And that is why, as much as possible, one should be among those who fear Allah the most. And who will love Allah the most? The one whose command he follows. If he loves Allah, he will perform the deeds that Allah loves. And obviously, if you want to see what Allah loves and what He hates, then read the Holy Quran. Read it a thousand times. If you are afraid, then go and read the verses of the Holy Quran. Read the verses of the Holy Quran. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is announcing, he is announcing the command. If you do not read it today, then Allah will... The one whom Allah loves, and those who love Allah, they are the ones who are truly guided. 'Those who believe are stronger in love for Allah.' So, it is known that there are two types of fear. One is fear, and the other is also fear. But the foundation of fear is love. And you see, the foundation of fear is also in love. How? The Quran says that when a person loves someone immensely, he tries not to do anything... He tries not to do anything that would displease his beloved. If he truly believes that Allah is watching, he will not do anything that Allah has forbidden. That is not to be done. After that, the most honorable in the sight of Allah is the one who does the work that brings him closer to Allah. 'The most honorable of you in the sight of Allah is the one who is most pious (Taqwa).' What is Taqwa? Taqwa means to act upon what is commanded and abstain from what is forbidden. This is called Taqwa. Our Mawla (a.s.) has clearly stated: 'Look, if you want to be close to Allah, perform the deeds that please Allah, and this will be the sign of your love.' So, 'Fear Allah, fear Allah.' What does it mean? Is Allah something to be feared? Allah is the One who created us and blessed us with these bounties. He has blessed us with so many bounties. As the Quran says, 'If you try to count the bounties of Allah, you will never be able to count them.' The Surah Ar-Rahman keeps asking, 'Which of the bounties of your Lord will you deny?' People talk about bounties, but some scholars have said that there are spiritual bounties. If you were asked to give up your eyes, you would be ready to give up everything, but you would not be ready to give up your eyes. For children, they give an example... For children, they give an example to explain this. For example, if we say to you, 'We will give you a lot of wealth, we will give you a huge mansion with servants and cars, and all the material things of the world that people desire, we will give you all of that, but you have to do one small thing: we will make you insane.' If you are ready to become insane for all these things, then this hut of mine is better. You keep all these things; I do not want anything. Because the greatest desire is one's own self. What else could be greater than that? Or if someone says, 'Become paralyzed, lose your ability to move, but you will have all the wealth.' You would say, 'No, brother, I do not want it.' You can eat with your hands, you can drink with your hands, you can see, you can walk, but if you lose these, you cannot do anything. You walk with your feet, but you are paralyzed. But the doctor says, 'Brother, I do not want it.' 'Okay, no problem, we will give you all these things, but we will take away your freedom, we will make you a slave.' What is the use of this? These are the spiritual bounties about which Allah is repeatedly asking in the Quran: 'Which of the bounties of your Lord will you deny?' It is on the basis of these spiritual bounties that a human benefits from material things. If these are taken away, that material wealth is of no use. That is why Allah is using this term. And the other term Allah has used is: 'We have given you spiritual powers.' If you do not recognize them, you will never be able to improve in life; you will keep falling. If you want to fear, then fear your sins, and fear the consequences of your sins, and fear nothing else but Allah. Fear Allah, for that is the thing that a person must hold onto. Therefore, they [the Imams] wanted you to attain two levels: to meet Allah, the All-Forgiving, the One who accepts repentance, and to connect with your Lord. Do not deal with us [the Imams] as if we are separate from Him; if you deal with us in that way, we will become a problem. And if the Wilayah is true, then many sins will automatically be forgiven, Insha'Allah. If the Wilayah is sincere, remember that it was said to the Bani Israel, 'Before you enter the gate, say Hitta (forgiveness/repentance).' It was said to the Bani Israel that when you enter the gate, say 'Hitta'—meaning, 'forgive our sins.' And it is written that when they were told to prostrate before the gate, they did not understand it. They were told to say 'Hitta,' and it is written in the books of Muhammad and Ali (a.s.)—this is not something I am inventing, it is present in the authentic books—that the image of Muhammad and Ali was written there. This is the example of the Wilayah of Muhammad and Ali. This is the example of the Wilayah of Muhammad and Ali. In all the 12th-century books, the image of Muhammad and Ali was the example. They were told to prostrate before the gate while saying 'Hitta.' But because of their arrogance, they did not prostrate. What do you think? We are not like those people who refuse to prostrate. If you do not prostrate, you are disobeying Allah. Allah has promised that if you do this, He will forgive all your sins and elevate your status, for He is the Most Forgiving. He is the Most Forgiving. You must believe that if people knew to what extent the Wilayah is mentioned in the Hadith, we would provide the references for those who want them. We have the references. In a chapter of a book, why was it selected? Because Allah selected names for Himself so that people could call upon Him through those names. So, when we come to the names, consider the first one. The first name Allah selected for Himself is Ali, and Allah... The first is different, but the first must be Ali, and call upon Allah through these names. In these names, there is a change. It is because of this that Muslims fight among themselves. If they used these names, they would call upon Allah. And fear Allah—fear Him regarding the rights of others. When a person dies, he is questioned about whether he violated the rights of others. Did he cause pain to any servant of Allah? Did he violate the rights of any person? Allah may forgive His own rights, but He will not forgive the rights of His servants, and He is the One who loves the most. He is the One who loves the most, the One who knows everything. And this is not just me saying this; the Hadith says that Allah's mercy is vast. Whoever insults a believer has declared war against Me. So, I do not do anything to anyone. It is Allah's mercy and kindness to forgive. I want to meet the believers, but they do not like it; they are afraid of death. This is not because they are angry with Me, but because they are afraid of death. I like them, so I postpone death for them. I postpone those moments, but when He speaks, He speaks the truth. Therefore, even small things must be accounted for. You will have to answer for small actions. After that, He says, 'Obey Allah and His Messenger,' and follow the two things He has commanded. Fear Allah, and do not disobey Him. Once you have done these things—first, repent for your sins; second, fulfill the rights of the people; third, do what He has commanded; and fourth, abstain from what He has forbidden—if you do these four things, then Allah says, 'Fear Allah.' Never do anything that would cause your heart to become hardened. Keep praying that your heart remains pure. Do not do anything that would cause Allah's displeasure. Always be mindful of this. Even in a small gathering, a minor action can become a cause for Allah's displeasure. He says that when you seek Allah, He gives you gifts. Keep doing good deeds. And if you are committing sins, never think that Allah cannot do anything. If Allah is leaving a sinner alone, it is because He has given him respite. He has given him respite. Therefore, always try to keep this in mind. Allah says to always keep in mind that whatever you do, Allah is watching you. And if you do not feel that Allah is watching you, then at least realize that He is watching you. And if someone goes outside this boundary—if he does not believe that Allah is watching him—then he is outside the fold of Islam. Therefore, we must always remember Allah. It is written about the Imams that they were always mindful of Allah. Always keep in mind that Allah is watching. What happens is that when there is no one around us, Satan attacks us the most. Satan is always busy trying to ensure that we commit sins. He is watching us, and he is happy when we sin. People who commit sins are foolish. Allah says, 'I am watching.' The more a person is aware of this, the more he can distance himself from sins. The more you distance yourself from sins, the more you will be protected. Satan's biggest goal is to keep you away from the Wilayah. Why? Because if you have Wilayah, you are dangerous to Satan. If you don't have it, you will be swayed by the winds of the world; whatever anyone says, you will follow. But if you have Wilayah, you will only follow Allah and what Allah has commanded. For the sake of... it is a great matter, only and only Allah, and no one else fears Allah except those who have knowledge. The more a person has knowledge, the more they will fear Him. The responsibility of the society is to keep this in mind: who is Allah? I know your secrets, do you not fear Him? That servant who believes, 'Who is there that knows what you are?' And... he cannot do anything. I cannot do anything if Allah does not will it. Therefore, one should fear Allah, one should fear the majesty of Allah. As it is said in the Quran: 'Allah gives sovereignty to whom He wills, and He takes sovereignty away from whom He wills. He honors whom He wills and He humbles whom He wills.' He snatches from whom He wills. That intoxication—the intoxication for the sake of the Almighty—is such that one should keep in mind that in Iran, there is a very beautiful parable. Listen, it is a very beautiful parable. Listen, what is this 'intoxication' called? You know, the dervishes, the ones who are ascetics and servants, they wear the clothes of the poor and go out onto the road. They have a staff in their hands, and at the bottom of the staff, there is iron or steel attached to it. They keep it with them and walk. You know that when someone walks on the road like this, children tease them—you know children tease them—and if they go a bit towards the jungle, animals start barking. You don't pay attention to this parable; animals keep roaming around. So, the children tease them, and the dervish does not react, so the children run away out of fear. And if he hits the animals with that staff, the animals run away. Even though this staff is in his hand, he doesn't use it until they come close. When they come close and don't listen, then he uses it. If they don't listen, then he uses it. In the same way, understand this—or perhaps this is the 'intoxication' of Allah—that He leaves it like that, saying, 'Let them be, otherwise they will do this.' So the child understands, 'It's okay, what are they saying?' And if he becomes like an animal, if he is understanding like an animal, then what kind of man is he? This is the state of those who are with Allah. As I mentioned, the inner state of reliance on Allah—the Imams (a.s.) have explained this. Some are like those who explain the food, and for them, there is a staff to break their pride. If they use the staff a little, they should be careful. Some are such that the fear of Allah has broken them, and they have broken themselves. The fear of Allah in their hearts is such that, oh Lord, may the Almighty break the hearts of both. May the Almighty break the hearts of both. Allah says in the Quran, in Surah Al-Hashr, 'Law anzalna hadhal-Qur'ana 'ala jabalin la-ra'aytahu khashi'an mutasaddi'an min khashyatillah' (If We had sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and splitting asunder from the fear of Allah). It would crumble into pieces from the fear of Allah. Allah says this for all people so that they may reflect. And they will reflect—the more this fear exists, the more it will come. Now, if we talk about it, we don't even recognize it. And if you want to see it, look at the history of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). The Almighty came, and he was crying, falling into prostration. Look at how Ali (a.s.) was—how he was lying down, like a snake sleeping, that is how the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) fell into prostration. Like this, 'O Lord, this lowly servant has come before You.' O Lord, this lowly servant has come before You. O Praised One, this servant has come before You. Ali (a.s.) was crying, and while doing so, suddenly, I say, 'I thought he had fallen asleep.' So when I came close and touched Ali (a.s.), he was like a dry piece of wood. I tried to move Ali (a.s.), but Ali (a.s.) was not moving. I thought, 'What has happened?' Then I recited the verse of the Quran, 'Wa ja'a rabbuka wal-malaku saffan saffa' (And your Lord has come, and the angels, rank upon rank). What happened? Then I saw that Ali (a.s.) was lying there, lost in Allah. This is the station of Ali's (a.s.) gnosis (ma'rifat). This is the state of that fear, the state of that gnosis, that while talking to Allah in that state... and the rest of the people, you see them fighting in front of you, that they have become strange. Anyway, you see that they fear Allah. They have so much fear of Allah in their hearts that... They have so much fear of Allah in their hearts that they become silent. This usually cleanses the filth. This is pure; it cleanses the tongue of filth. This is... yes, this is the station of the noble ones. These are all noble deeds. This is the state of those who are in awe of God. And after that, they try to compete with each other in good deeds, to be the first to do this work. These are the people who have the fear of God in their hearts. And as it is said, when they do a lot of work, they still consider it very little. They do a lot, but they consider it little, and they are never satisfied with a little. But whatever Allah has given them, they are satisfied with that; they never complain to Allah. And people think, 'What kind of people are these?' People think, but they don't care about people. And these are the people who are the most intelligent in the eyes of the Almighty. The most intelligent person is the one who is wise. This deep influence remains firm. This bill, in many ways, is like this—instead of the mind, it is the soul. If a man hopes for something, he pursues it and runs after it, and if he fears something, he hates it. If you desire Paradise, you will walk towards it, and if you want to avoid something, you will stay away from those deeds. This trap, which is called 'Senior Vice President' [metaphorically], destroys the soul. Think about this carefully; these are not just ordinary words, but words of wisdom that keep one away from the world's illusions and prevent one from doing certain things. And it keeps one away from doing things, making one think ten times. That is why it is said that he who fears Allah does not fear anything else. He who fears Allah is never afraid of anything else, and that is why, if you look at history, take the example of a person who has recognized Allah—he is never afraid of the threats of any tyrant. He has found the opportunity to be with Him. The traditions state that whoever fears Allah, Allah makes everything fear him, and whoever does not fear Allah, Allah makes him fear everything. He will fear everything—'What if my sustenance decreases?', 'What if I don't have abundance?', 'What if this happens?'. But the believer does not fear anyone; Allah makes everything fear him. It is strange, look at how he stands before anyone. Even the Mughal Emperor Jahangir, who was so powerful that he had the whole world under his control—how much he must have tried to threaten and intimidate people. They intimidated and threatened the narrator, and I, being under their influence, told them that he is writing a book about our changes. And he said, 'I am going to write a book on this, and its pages will be like lightning, burning the individuals who give such responses to men and women.' He wrote the answer, and he said, 'I am going to write this book, and its pages will remain.' He feels great sorrow for those people, and when he gives an answer, he uses [strong words]. He uses [strong words] to help. They were treated very cruelly, from this district, saying, 'Go away from here.' But the introduction about the Imam (a.s.) is present in the English language. It is a complaint, he is crazy, and this is a very important thing. The one who has this in their heart never fears anyone. And this was the reason why the entire tragedy of Karbala happened. What happens is that in any army, if there is a very brave person, then the others have great comfort and peace. And if the commander is like Abbas (a.s.), then you can imagine that the others were, of course, with us. Abbas (a.s.) said, 'This is my job, the river is not my name.' People say, 'We will give a thousand, how did he introduce himself in the battlefield?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) sent them, 'Go and fight,' and when they returned, they were covered in weapons. He returns, and in the film, he returns again, a rain of diamonds, and then he returns a third time. When he was sent, the Mawla had a sword on his back, and Muhammad Rafi was there. This is the result of your mother's milk, the milk that is within you. And in the battle of the river, they were sending more to fight. Here, someone asked, and Muhammad Hassan Hussain said that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had said... and there, the bride... this was their issue. On the other side, you know that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was destroying idols, and Ali (a.s.) was there, then he sent Abbas (a.s.). Mawla Abbas (a.s.) was sent with a veil over his face. And Mawla Abbas (a.s.) would strike, and when he returned, it was known that he fell like lightning. No, he returned, and what did he do in the roots? He was 13-14 years old. The sun rose, and for the family, it was a structure of how he would return. Everyone was saying, 'Abbas, Abbas, Abbas,' and that is why... Abbas, Abbas, and that is why they repeatedly say, 'Mawla, give permission, let Abbas be the Alamdar (standard-bearer).' But when Ashura happened, Sakina (s.a.) was thirsty. Sakina (s.a.) ran to the standard-bearer and remembered how she had been promised, 'You have given me peace, go and bring water.' Life is in the words. Hearing this, Sakina (s.a.) ran and brought the water skin, trembling. As soon as she brought the water skin, the children saw that it was Abbas (a.s.). 'Lady, where are you taking it?' 'My uncle is going to bring water for the children.' And the one who was promised, he would definitely fulfill it. 'Children, you will get water.' Sakina (s.a.) gave the water skin, and he took it towards the river. You know it is written in the Maqtal that when Abbas (a.s.) reached the river, the soldiers started running away on their own. Abbas (a.s.) reached the river, and he took the horse and made it drink. He got down, and he had taken water in his cupped hands. He said, 'O children, I am Abbas, you have...' You are children, I am Abbas. You are coming to me. If I want, I can drink water, but my children are thirsty. He filled his cupped hands with water and, mounting the horse, started moving forward. Now, to face the enemy, he made another attack. The second attack was successful. Allah, with his speed, he held the water skin with his teeth. And he was heading towards the camp. This was the situation, and then he was heading towards the thirsty ones. When he was hit on his arm, he fell from a height. The first thing one does when falling is to put their hands forward, and my... his arms were broken. He reached the edge of the river, towards the camp, putting his head on his brother's lap. For a while, he was on the lap, and then he passed away. In this way, water reached Hussain (a.s.). Abbas (a.s.) reached... Abbas (a.s.)... Papa... [Music] ...May those who are troubled have their troubles removed. May those who are in difficulty have their difficulties removed. May those who are ill be granted health. Wherever in the world, those who have sacrificed their lives... [names of deceased individuals]... And the late Riyaz, and the late... and the Mithwani family, and may Allah have mercy on the late... and the late... [Music] Ya Hussain, Ya Hussain. Muhammad, my Muhammad, Muhammad, my Muhammad. Muhammad, my Muhammad, like the moon and stars, like the moon and stars, like the moon and stars. You are my... my lion, my moon, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad. Be ready, in the chest, you are Akbar, in the chest, you are Abbas, in the chest, you are Abbas. You are Abbas, in the chest, you are Abbas. In the battlefield, in the desire for death, in the time of the battle, like this, like this, you turn, you read, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad. Your Talib, your... your river, this is the one who is wandering, this is the one who is wandering. I am the daughter of the one who gives milk, I will see, I will see. Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, my Muhammad, my Muhammad, my Muhammad. The battle began, saying, 'Brother Muhammad, listen, Brother Muhammad, Brother Muhammad, on one side you advance, on one side you advance, on one side you, on one side you, they will commit oppression, we are Muhammad, we are Abbas,' saying, 'Muhammad, my Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad.' Muhammad, Muhammad, both of them, the face, the face, not like Ali, death, death, together, in the... O guest, and a miracle happened, your Ali, such a movement, and Muhammad, my Muhammad, my Muhammad, my Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad. Where until the thirst, struck by thirst, both started writhing, writhing, brother, saying, 'Again, the children of... your, my red one, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad.' Now they were... they were far away, and this... And this... to someone, he gave, he turned, he said, 'Shukr, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad, my Muhammad, Muhammad, Hussain (a.s.).'

title: Majlis 4 | Maut, Qabr aur Wilaayat-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the critical role of Wilaayat (devotion to the Ahlulbayt) in navigating the afterlife, from the moment of death through the trials of the grave and the Day of Resurrection. The speaker emphasizes that true faith requires an exclusive love for God and His chosen representatives, which serves as a protective shield during the soul's journey. By highlighting the spiritual significance of the Ahlulbayt, the lecture provides guidance on how believers can prepare for accountability and find peace through trust in Allah.
content:
[Music] ...I have seen the one you gave, I have seen it. [Music] The one you gave, I have seen it. The body and the soul, from the films, then Hussain (a.s.) said... Then he said, 'This body and soul, I have seen the mirror of the sick, I have seen it in the reflection of the city, I have seen it given by your city, and look, this is the world of relief, this is what he said, yes, look at this, this is the world of relief, this is what the questioner said, he said, 'I have seen it, I have seen it given by your fuel, I have seen it, these are connected now.' These are connected now, he will cast a glance, he keeps laughing at his own, he has cast a glance on the part, oh today I have seen the handshake, I have seen it given by your table, I have seen it, I have become stubborn, oh body, I am all gems, because the beginning has become, I am the life of all gems, I have seen it, [music] I have seen it given by your city. And the religion of Islam, Shabbir, your family, the religion of Islam, Shabbir, your family, I have seen it pressed by the knees, I have seen it given by your city, I have seen it, and from the pulpit of the city, Tabarra, read the Tabarra from the pulpit of the city, I have seen it, I have seen it given by your fuel. That he is saying in front, 'Sit, my last mourning of the city,' he says in front, 'Sit, my mourning, whatever my end is,' I have seen it, I have seen it given by your city, [music]... Guest, [music] Alhamdulillah, Rabbil Alamin, ... [music] ... The decline has started, then a little bit ... [music] ... Come back, [music] MashaAllah, ... Allah has not placed two hearts in the chest of any human being; there is only one heart. If there is love for Allah, then there cannot be love for Satan. If there is love for Shabbir (a.s.), then there cannot be love for his enemies. If there is love for Ibrahim (a.s.), then there cannot be love for Nimrod. If there is love for Musa (a.s.), then there cannot be love for Pharaoh. If there is love for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), then there cannot be love for Abu Lahab. And if there is love for Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), then there cannot be love for his enemies. Send a Salawat. This love should be pure love. For Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and his infallible progeny, it should be pure love. There should be no adulteration in it, nothing that would cause a crack in this love. It should not seem like this person is not sincere, that he carries everyone along. The one who carries everyone along is not a true believer. A believer keeps his stance and says, 'This is my stance, and whatever I do, I will do it for the pleasure of Allah.' Whether it pleases or displeases anyone, it doesn't matter. chapters.title: The Exclusivity of Divine Love
