title: EP08 | Imam (a.s.) Ki Marefat | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological necessity of recognizing the Imam (Ma'rifat) as the essential gateway to understanding Allah and the Quran. It emphasizes that the Imam serves as the divine light and source of wisdom required for spiritual life, contrasting this with the spiritual death that results from ignorance of the Imam. The discussion highlights that authentic interpretation of the Quran and true worship are exclusively tied to the guidance of the Ahlul-Bayt, warning against the theological deviations that arise when this connection is severed.
content:
TSR presents. Ash-hadu an Aliyan Waliullah. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and curse their enemies all together. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat (Proof), son of Hassan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—at this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and cause him to enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and curse their enemies all together. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. To proceed: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says in His Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good.' As Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, states in the Holy Quran, whoever is given wisdom has been given 'Khair-e-Kaseer' (much good). Before starting the discussion, I once again request that if you have any questions regarding the Imamate or these lectures, or even questions outside of these lectures concerning the Imamate, please send your questions to the number shown on your screen. Whether you send them in written format, or via audio or video—in any form—please do send your questions. InshaAllah, if we are able to answer, we will do so, if Allah grants the ability. In any case, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says in this verse that whoever is given wisdom has been given much good. A great deal of good. Our topic is: what is the importance of the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam? You see, until now we have been discussing how necessary it is for the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda) to exist. What are the benefits of the Proof of Allah? And now we are coming to the topic of recognizing the Imam—who is the Imam? Who is that sacred personality whom Allah has made His Proof? And who are the Imams we have today, and the eleven Imams who preceded him? That is, who are the successors of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? So, first, let us shed some light on the Ma'rifat of the Imam for you. Look at how the family of Muhammad (a.s.) has shed light on this topic in the traditions, showing how great its importance is. The first thing is that the Ma'rifat of the Imam is wisdom itself. Regarding the verse I recited, 'And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good,' Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Obedience to Allah and the recognition of the Imam.' What is wisdom? Wisdom means 'Hikmah.' In Arabic, 'Hikmah' is on the pattern of 'Fi'ala,' which in Arabic grammar is called 'Masdar-e-Nau'i'—the method of doing something. So, if the word is 'Hik,' then this 'Hikmah' is derived from 'Hukm' (command/decision). So, Hikmah means 'Hukm.' And what is 'Hukm'? It is a decision. And what is 'Hikmah'? It is the method of deciding, that is, making the correct decision. So Allah says that whoever is given wisdom has been given much good. In its interpretation, the Imam says: what is this 'much good,' what is this wisdom? It is obedience to Allah and the recognition of the Imam. A person must recognize their Imam—who is our Imam? Who is the one teaching us the religion in the way it deserves to be taught? The one who is introducing Allah to us, describing Allah, explaining Allah, and explaining the truth about Tawheed (monotheism) as it deserves to be explained. Now, if someone wants to know what the truth of understanding Tawheed is, they should read the sermons of Nahjul Balagha, where the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali a.s.) has praised and glorified Allah. They should read Hadith-e-Mufaddal to see how Imam Sadiq (a.s.) has praised and glorified Allah. Read these traditions, read these Hadiths. Ma'rifat-ul-Imam (recognition of the Imam) is this very wisdom. That is why this recognition of the Imam is also called 'Noor' (light). What is the recognition of the Imam? It is light. Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli is a very prominent companion of the Imam. He is famous as Burayd al-Ijli. He is a great companion, about whom it is said that if it were not for four individuals—including Abu Basir, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Zurara, and Burayd al-Ijli— If these four individuals had not existed, the Imam says the traces of Prophethood would have been erased. These people revived the traces of Prophethood and the teachings of the Infallible Imams (a.s.). That is, they learned from the Imams and then taught others, instructed them, and gave lessons. It is obligatory upon all of us to learn the teachings of the Imams (a.s.) and convey them to the people. It is present in the Hadiths. This is our responsibility. The Imam says if people were familiar with the beauty of our speech and our teachings, they would certainly follow us. They would certainly follow us and adhere to our path. So, the shortcoming and the mistake lie with us, the followers of the Ahlulbayt. We have not conveyed their teachings as they deserve to be conveyed. Become familiar with the traditions of the family of Muhammad. Become familiar with the books of Hadith. So, this is Burayd al-Ijli. He says I heard from Imam Baqir (a.s.) regarding this verse: 'And is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people?' Did you reflect on the verse? 'And is one who was dead'—one who was dead, a corpse—'and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people.' Now tell me, O Muslims! Explain the interpretation of this—what is its interpretation? We also want to know. How many such dead people are there whom Allah brought to life and they are walking among the people? Do you see any? How many dead people are walking around, brother? The Quran is saying this is verse 122 of Surah Al-An'am. We brought the dead to life and gave him light, and he is walking by means of that light. You didn't understand the verse, did you? If someone from another religion asks, 'Brother, tell us, how many—we haven't seen any Muslim who died and then stood up, came to life, and started walking among the people.' People would start running away upon seeing that. But now, come to the door of the family of Muhammad and see what interpretation the family of Muhammad has provided. The Imam said—it was Burayd al-Ijli's question about this verse. Now the Imam is answering; Imam Sadiq (a.s.) is answering, Imam Baqir (a.s.) is answering: 'A corpse is one who does not recognize anything.' He does not possess recognition, does not possess the recognition of faith, does not possess the recognition of the self, does not possess the recognition of the origin, does not possess the recognition of the return—he does not possess the recognition of anything. He knows nothing; he is dead. He is a walking corpse. One who has no recognition, no Ma'rifat. If someone wants to be called 'alive,' they must attain Ma'rifat—the Ma'rifat of Allah, the Ma'rifat of the Messenger, the Ma'rifat of the Imam, the Ma'rifat of the origin, the Ma'rifat of the return, the Ma'rifat of the self. Only then will he be called alive. 'He knows nothing.' 'And made for him light by which to walk among the people.' So what is this light? The Imam says, 'The Imam.' This light is the Imam, 'whom he follows.' This Imam is the light. And then the verse continues: 'Is he like one who is in darkness?' 'Who never emerges from it.' So who is this one living in darkness? The one who never emerges from the darkness. So the Imam says, 'Peace be upon him, the one who does not recognize the Imam.' The one who does not possess the Ma'rifat of the Imam. He is in darkness, wandering in the dark. He has no light at all. Rather, he is a corpse. He is dead, dead. He is without guidance. That Imam who is 'appointed by Allah'—he should follow him. Is it clear to you? Now, obviously, this can only be for that Imam who is the 'most knowledgeable of people' (A'lam al-Nas), which, InshaAllah, will be explained later, regarding what qualities an Imam must possess. So, he must be the 'most knowledgeable of people,' the Imam who possesses knowledge. And that Imam who—that is, the one claiming Imamate, who does not have knowledge and every little while says, 'Call him quickly, call Ali, call Ali.' And then when Ali (a.s.) solves his difficulty and answers his questions, he says that if it were not for Ali, I would have been destroyed. 108 times it was recorded in history, 108 times he said it. He said it 108 times. It is present in historical documents, 108 times. Ali Labbaf has explicitly recorded it in his book. That 108 times, 108 times. It is a strange incident. And yet people believe. And yet people believe, just as if you remember, a few episodes ago I served you with the information that some people say that even if an Imam is ignorant, he can still become an Imam, no problem. As long as he comes to power, he is the Imam, and he doesn't need to be a scholar because he can take help from any scholar. InshaAllah, when that discussion comes, it will be even clearer. So the Imam says, this is the one who has no Imam, who does not have the Ma'rifat of the Imam. And why is there so much emphasis on Ma'rifat? On the Ma'rifat of the Imam? What is the reason? Because without recognizing the true Imam, a person cannot even attain the Ma'rifat of Allah. If he is not under the guidance of the true Imam, remember, this is a very important point. How? How? First, let me present a Hadith for your service. It is a very famous Hadith. Sayyidush-Shuhada (a.s.) says, when Sayyidush-Shuhada came to his companions, 'Kharajal-Husain bin Ali alaihima-salam ala ashabihi' (Husain bin Ali, peace be upon them both, came out to his companions), he came among his companions, 'Faqala ayyuhan-nas' (He said, O people), 'Innallaha jalla dhikruhu' (Indeed, Allah, whose mention is glorious), 'Ma khalaqal-ibada' (He did not create the servants), 'Illa liya'rifuhu' (Except that they should know Him, attain the recognition of Allah). What is written in the Quran? 'Wa ma khalaqtu', it is a verse from Surah Adh-Dhariyat, right? 'Wa ma khalaqtul-jinna wal-insa illa liya'budun' (And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me). The Imam is explaining that same verse in this way. How is the Imam explaining it? That Allah, whose mention is glorious, did not create the servants except that they should attain His recognition. 'Fa-idha arafuhu' (So when they attain His recognition), 'Abaduhu' (Then they will worship Him). Meaning, if there is true recognition, there will be true worship. 'Fa-idha abaduhu' (And when they worship Him in the correct manner), 'Istaghna bi-ibadatihi an ibadati man siwahu aw ma siwahu' (Then they will be independent of the worship of anyone or anything other than Him). Meaning, they will not bow their heads before anyone except Allah. That will be true worship. 'Ibada min siwahu'. 'Faqala lahu rajul' (Then a man asked him), 'Ya ibna Rasulillah' (O son of the Messenger of Allah), 'Bi-abi anta wa ummi' (May my father and mother be sacrificed for you), 'Fama ma'rifatullah' (Then what is the recognition of Allah?). 'Qala alayhis-salam' (He, peace be upon him, said), 'Ma'rifatu ahli kulli zamanin imamahum' (Meaning, what is the recognition of Allah? That every person should recognize the Imam of their time). Which Imam? 'Alladhi yajibu alayhim ta'atuhu' (The one whose obedience is obligatory upon them). Now why this? Meaning, what is the connection between the recognition of Allah and the recognition of the Imam? Look, when we follow and emulate the true Imam, look, let's start from the very beginning, we all believe in the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). It is our collective belief that the Messenger of Allah is the Messenger of Allah. Is there any Muslim who would not believe this? They would. We all believe that the Quran is the Book of Allah. The Quran is the Book of Allah and whatever is in the Quran is the truth. This is our belief. This is the belief. Now, obviously, for the Quran, there needs to be an explainer, someone to clarify it. The Quran itself has announced this. The Quran has announced that there are two types of verses in the Quran: Muhkam (clear) and Mutashabih (ambiguous). And this Mutashabih, meaning Muhkam is clear and Mutashabih is what is ambiguous, not clear, this is verse number 7 of Surah Ali 'Imran of the Quran. The Quran is announcing this. So here, the claim of those people who say, 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us) is already refuted. That claim became wrong. The Quran is saying no, you are in need of the 'Rasikhuna fil-'ilm' (those firmly rooted in knowledge). You are in need of the 'Rasikhuna fil-'ilm', those who are acquainted with the Quran. This is a verse of the Quran, you can recite the whole verse, 'Huwalladhi anzala alaikal-kitaba minhu ayatun muhkamatun hunna ummul-kitabi wa ukharu mutashabihat' (It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses [that are] precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific). In this, some verses are Muhkam, some are Mutashabihat. This is the Quran. 'Hunna ummul-kitab' (They are the foundation of the Book). Meaning, one must return to them, and the rest are Mutashabihat. And then the Quran says, 'Fa-ammalladhina fi qulubihim zaighun' (As for those in whose hearts is deviation), deviation meaning crookedness, those who always think in reverse, whose thinking is twisted, 'Fayattabi'una ma tashabaha minhu' (They follow that which is unspecific of it). Why? 'Ibtigha'al-fitnati wa ibtigha'at-ta'wili' (Seeking discord and seeking an interpretation). Because their goal is only to create discord, not to seek the truth. And they interpret the Quran according to their own whims. They interpret it themselves because they themselves do not know, they do not possess divine knowledge. They themselves say that they do not have divine knowledge. Not at all. And that is why you will see that they have so many differences in every single thing. There are many differences. And then the Quran is announcing that no one knows its interpretation except Allah and the 'Rasikhuna fil-'ilm'. 'Wa ma ya'lamu ta'wilahu illallahu war-rasikhuna fil-'ilm'. This is the announcement of the Quran. And there are many other such verses that I have presented to you before as well. So who will explain this? Who will explain true Tawhid (monotheism)? So now, the Imam who is the true successor of the Messenger of Allah, he alone will explain the correct interpretation, he alone will explain the correct exegesis, he alone will explain the correct Tawhid, he alone will explain the correct justice, he alone will explain the correct Prophethood, and the rest of the Usul-e-Deen (principles of religion), Furu-e-Deen (branches of religion), ethics, manners, and all correct teachings, only he can tell them who is the true successor of the Messenger of Allah. And the one who does not know, who is not the true successor, he knows nothing. He knows nothing at all. So therefore, Ma'rifatullah (recognition of Allah) is the correct recognition. Now, the proof for this, the proof is very clear. Look, those who abandoned Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Gate of the City of Knowledge, who did not attend the threshold of Ali and the progeny of Ali, look at their Tawhid. Either they became believers in Tashbih (anthropomorphism) or they became believers in Tajsim (corporealism). Meaning, God has a body, and on the Day of Judgment, God will come with His full body. Because they could not understand the Mutashabih verses of the Quran and took them in their literal sense. That Allah will actually be very tall and wide, 66 feet, 70 feet, whatever it is. And some people say, no, Allah will exist, but in what form, in what nature, we do not know, but He will definitely come, but He has a body, but we do not know about the body, but it is a body. These are called Mushabbiha. So those who abandoned the threshold of the Ahlul-Bayt, either they became Mujassima (corporealists) who used to say that Allah's body is just like our body, or they became Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) who say that there is a body but we cannot describe what kind of body it is, but it exists and we will see Him on the Day of Judgment. But the Quran is saying, 'Lan tarani' (You will never see Me). When the Quran says, 'La tudrikuhul-absaru wa huwa yudrikul-absar' (Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision), and such numerous verses and narrations from Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them). This Allah is not visible. Allah cannot be seen. Therefore, the correct recognition is that in which, if the recognition of the true Imam is attained, then through that very Imam, the recognition of Allah will be attained. Insha'Allah, we will continue this in the future. Wa akhiru da'wana anil-hamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin. Respected viewers, as announced, there will be a quiz after every fourth episode of this video series 'Itam-e-Hujjat'. In which a few questions related to the previous four episodes will be asked. The link for the quiz is present in the video description and the comment section. This link will remain live for one week. Meaning, you have a full week's time to submit your answers. If you do not know the answer to any question, you can watch the video again to answer. Out of all those who provide correct answers, 14 lucky winners will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system, who will receive a gift of 1000 Indian Rupees. The winners will be announced in our next episode, Insha'Allah. Therefore, you are requested to watch these videos carefully and try to provide correct answers to the questions asked in the quiz, and along with this, share these videos as much as possible. Participate in the quiz in large numbers and join us in helping to convey this message of Wilayat-e-Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) to others so that you too can be included among those who propagate Wilayat.

title: Maraj-ul-Barayn - A Marriage between two equals | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture explores the divine nature of the marriage between Imam Ali (a.s.) and Lady Fatima (s.a.), emphasizing that their union was ordained by Allah rather than human choice. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the spiritual equality of the couple, the historical context of their marriage, and the significance of Lady Fatima's status as a part of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The talk also touches upon the political implications of the Fadak incident and the spiritual superiority of the Ahlulbayt over worldly wealth and status.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. [Arabic Quranic recitation]. [Arabic Quranic recitation]. So first of all, let us all together [recite]. If Ali (a.s.) were not there, Fatima (s.a.) would not have had a match. If they were not equal, no one could have been their equal. They were equal, and that is why the union of the two... And what happens from that? The background is that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) called Ali (a.s.) and said, 'O Ali, [Arabic phrase].' The wealthy people of the tribe were upset that he had married her to Ali (a.s.). They wanted to say—and you will see this in the sermon—that they were like us, and you married her to an ordinary man like Ali (a.s.). What is the wealth we have, the status we have, the position we have? And look here, in every single thing... And look here, in every single thing, there is a lesson for our society. Whenever you give your daughter's hand to someone, you have raised your daughters with great care. You don't just hand them over to anyone. Islam has set the criteria: the boy should have faith, the boy should have good character. Even if the boy is not very wealthy, it is not an issue. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) took the guarantee. If they are in the same level, then you should marry them off. Otherwise, some people have this mentality: 'Let's see if he is at our level.' Even if the boy is educated and religious, they think, 'He doesn't have as much wealth as we do.' But look at what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said... What was the answer the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave? The same answer when people were asking, 'Why Ali (a.s.)?' I am waiting to burn [the doubts]. I am saying exactly what Allah has commanded. I swear by God, He has guaranteed the truthfulness of Ali (a.s.), that he does nothing except what is simple and based on the teachings of Allah. I did not marry her off, but Allah did. I did not marry Fatima (s.a.) off, rather it was Allah (s.w.t.) who did. Allah placed the hand of Ali (a.s.) in the hand of Fatima (s.a.). You were there, O Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and Allah (s.w.t.) said: 'If I had not created Ali (a.s.), there would have been no match for your daughter Fatima (s.a.) on the face of the earth.' If Ali (a.s.) did not exist, from the beginning of creation until the Day of Judgment, there would be no one equal to her. From the beginning of creation until the Day of Judgment, no one can equal her. Her status was such that she would live in a way that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would be pleased. A woman came to her and asked questions. She said, 'My mother sends me to you to ask questions, as she is very ill and cannot come herself.' She asked one question, the Princess (s.a.) answered. She asked a second, she answered. She asked a third, she answered. Then she became silent. The woman asked, 'Why have you stopped?' She replied, 'I remember that you might get tired of my questions.' The Princess (s.a.) said, 'Ask, ask whatever you wish, for I am...' A small question for me, like in 1947, how many things were discussed? Just as Ali (a.s.) is the deepest among men, in the same way, I am among women. Therefore, we should keep a motherly change. And the second thing is, I have told you that whenever someone comes to you to ask religious questions, never get tired or annoyed; instead, answer as much as you can. This is a blessing from Allah. Now, this dispute happened when a learned person asked about it. In the beginning, it is said that when water is released, it is asked to be released so that both these seas go and meet each other. Bring them to the seas; these two are for each other. That they should talk about something that is unpleasant to others. They say that Allah has taken the guarantee of the union. They say that Allah has taken the guarantee of the union, that they will treat each other with such love that it will be an example for the whole world. If this has happened, then listen, this is a very important thing. The question is, why was Janabe Zahra (s.a.) so quick to get angry? Was it just fabricated? Do you know why? In their families, it was fabricated that Janabe Zahra's temperament was very strange, why she got angry so quickly, to the extent that she was angry with them and left the house. And who did the Muslims blame? To justify it, they reached the point that when they came, the Princess of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I will not speak to both of you until I die, and on the Day of Judgment, I will complain to my father.' She did not even return their greeting, whereas returning a greeting is obligatory. But if someone is not a Muslim, then... But if someone is not a Muslim, then one should not return their greeting. So, the Princess not returning the greeting is raising many issues, it is closing many things. And it is written in their books, in their own books, that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Fatima (s.a.) is a part of me.' When the narrator asked, 'Is Ali (a.s.) and Fatima (s.a.) the same?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'These two are like two vast oceans, two oceans of knowledge, both are vast and deep.' And he says that one cannot be preferred over the other. Tell me, Allahu Akbar, can one be preferred over the other? They hold this belief, and this fatwa... They hold this belief, and this fatwa that Ali (a.s.) and Fatima (s.a.) are less, they can say this. This is their own separate matter. Now tell me, for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), after the comparisons, there is no comparison. The very imagination of a comparison should not exist. Then why is it that today, they are giving preference to someone else? There is no comparison. You see, on one side, what teachings you will get, and on the other side, what is coming from America. It is written in history that for this, there is a formal request, just don't ask. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is such, this era is such, and the period is such, then... Then who is the one doing the comparison? The one who gives the girl is called the one who gives the girl, but this is not just a girl, but Allah's... Allah's... It became Allah's. The people of the city also join in, that the believer hears, this is Ali (a.s.). Rather, the soul becomes filled with faith. Who is the one who is purified? Look, 'Innalaha yutahhirukum' (Verily, Allah intends to purify you). Listen, Allah has... Allah has purified Fatima (s.a.). In your hands, in your hands... the whole universe, Fatima (s.a.) is with me, the whole earth, the whole earth. And understand something, today if we take away Fadak from Fatima (s.a.), we become lions. See, we took it away because those who are from the usurpers always consider themselves lions. You will see that those who are from the usurpers will present themselves as lions, as if they have done a very big job. They could not understand that it was just a piece of land. Fadak was the whole earth, the earth where everything is, the mountains, the forests, and the earth on which you walk. Look, the whole of India is in my hand, Harris, your boss is walking in it. Harris, your boss is walking in it, walking on Fatima's (s.a.) land. And they will meet... Yes, here, listen. Demanding one's right, asking for one's right, this was an excuse to prove the government as false. To prove that their Islam... Islam... Islam... They say, and Fatima (s.a.) was involved in everything. And Fatima's (s.a.) refusal, her refusal... Now Fatima's (s.a.) refusal, her refusal, Fatima (s.a.) the Princess of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), was trying to prove, and she proved it in a brief manner, without any argument, in a simple way, that whatever government is in power, this government has no connection with Islam. They will feel absolutely hesitant in doing this, so whatever is going on, so now the matter has come, then they should... This is the first one, Abdur Rahman and Uthman came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Now, Fatima (s.a.) is in hand, take the marriage done. If you have... then... Then I will give... I will give 100 private jets, 100 private jets, and private... I will give 100 private jets, airplanes, so that the children understand, and in each one, there will be this much... and 10,000 dinars, 10,000 dinars. Multiply 50,000 by 10,000, it is increasing. And after this, the argument is written in the book, in the books, Dala'il al-Imamah, in which the narration is present, Imaduddin Ahmad Muhammad Rafi... It is present, Imaduddin Ahmad Muhammad Rafi has written that in the presence of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Abdur Rahman and the whole of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) companions, these two had no connection with them, neither this nor that. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Whatever you are ready to give, I am also ready to give.' And in other narrations, it is also present, and this is that before this, Islam... Islam... The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was angry with the words of both of them, and after that, what was done? A handful of pebbles was filled, and he took it towards Abdur Rahman. Allah is the Master. I have... we have... you... Allah is the Master. You are everything to us, and in reality, this is not a competition. The reality of the dowry was that it was transformed into jewels. These were such jewels that they were worth more than the entire world. It was just a matter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) saying, 'O Ahmad, O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.),' and peace be upon him. The guardian of Paradise is in charge. He said, 'Decorate the four corners of Paradise. Decorate the four lights of Paradise.' And the command was fulfilled. The inhabitants of the world were adorned in new garments, and the marriage was celebrated. The command was given to go down, and the one named Rahil was called. And his name was Rahil. He was the one with the most weight and the most beauty. He stood there, and this was the means through which Ali's (a.s.) marriage to Fatima (s.a.) would take place. And after this, the entire world would be for Fatima (s.a.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I want to marry my daughter Fatima (s.a.) to you, by the command of Allah (s.w.t.).' Ali (a.s.) was shy, but the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) insisted. Ali (a.s.) said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing to give as a dowry except my sword and my armor.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I want you to...' After that, I want you to do something. Take this as a gift from me. Listen, whenever Jibraeel (a.s.) came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in human form, he would appear in this shape. This is a powerful form. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) returned it, and then the preparations were made, and this event took place both on earth and in the heavens.

title: Kya Hum Allah (a.w.j.) Se Kiya Hua Waada Nibha Rahe Hain? (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the importance of the Holy Quran as a sacred covenant between Allah and His creation. The speaker highlights a tradition from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that encourages Muslims to recite at least fifty verses of the Quran daily to honor this commitment. The talk concludes with a prayer for the strength to fulfill this promise and for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Guardian of the Age, help us and do not let us perish. Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'The Quran is Allah's covenant to His creation.' Therefore, it is necessary for every Muslim individual to look into His covenant and to recite fifty verses from it every day. According to this hadith, the Holy Quran has been declared as the covenant of Allah Almighty. That is, it is a promise that Allah the Almighty has taken from every Muslim regarding the Holy Quran. Therefore, if someone considers himself a Muslim but is not reciting at least 50 verses a day, then it is as if he is not fulfilling the promise made to Allah the Almighty. So let us pray in the presence of Allah the Almighty, using this covenant—the Holy Quran—as a means, that He grants us the ability to fulfill this covenant and hastens the reappearance of the true interpreter of the Quran, Hazrat Sahib al-Zaman (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance). Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Log Imam Kyun Nahin Banaa Sakte? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of divine appointment for an Imam, referencing a historical encounter between Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi and Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The speaker explains that humans lack the 'Ilm al-Ghayb' (knowledge of the unseen) required to distinguish between a true reformer and a potential corrupter. Consequently, the selection of an Imam must be reserved for Allah, as human intellect is insufficient to discern the hidden intentions of leaders.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Wali of Allah. There was a tribe of Ash'ari in Qom that belonged to the Banu Umayya. Some people of this tribe became Shia and settled in Qom. Among them was Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, who was a staunch follower and had the honor of meeting the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and specifically Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). At that time, the Imam's son and our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), was also present. Sa'd had some questions, and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) asked his son, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), to answer them. One of the questions Sa'd asked was, 'My Master, tell me, why is it that people cannot choose an Imam for themselves?' Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) asked Sa'd, 'A reformer (musleh) or a corrupter (mufsid)?' Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) asked, 'What kind of Imam? A reformer who corrects people, benefits them, and is better for them, or a corrupter who causes chaos and is harmful to people?' Sa'd replied, 'A reformer, an Imam who is better for the people.' Then the Imam (a.t.f.s.) asked Sa'd, 'Is it possible for people to choose a corrupter, since no one knows the inner thoughts of others?' Sa'd replied, 'Yes, it is absolutely possible.' Upon this, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) said, 'This is the reason I have presented as proof for you, so that your intellect can rely on it.' This means it is clear from the Imam's answer that only one who possesses the knowledge of the unseen (Ilm al-Ghayb) can choose an Imam, and since people do not possess this knowledge, they can never choose a correct and good Imam for themselves. This is the benefit of asking the 'People of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Dhikr), the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), that their answer is a firm proof that aligns with intellect and upon which we can rely. We thank Allah (s.w.t.) for giving us such Imams, and we pray that He hastens the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and keeps us steadfast on his Imamate and Wilayah. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 21 | Tafseer of Surah al-Qadr (97) - Part 4
excerpt: This lecture provides an in-depth exploration of the virtues and signs of Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) within the context of Surah al-Qadr. The speaker details the spiritual significance of the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan, citing traditions from the Imams regarding how to identify and observe these nights. Practical advice is given on worship, including prayer requirements and the importance of intercessory prayer for the global community.
content:
Masha'Allah, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil-aliyyil-azim. A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Alhamdulillahi rabbil-alamin. Wassalatu wassalamu ala ashrafil-anbiya wal-mursalin. Wa khatimin-nabiyyin. Sayyidinal-muwajjad. Bashiran al-musaddad. Naziran al-mu'ayyad. Al-Mustafa al-amjad al-Mahmud Ahmad. Abil-Qasim Muhammad. Wa ala ahli baitihit-tayyibinat-tahirin al-ma'sumin. Wa la'natullahi ala a'daihim ajma'in. Minal-ani ila qiyami yawmid-din. Amma ba'd. Faqad qalallahu ta'ala subhanahu fi kitabil-karim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Inna anzalnahu fi laylatil-qadr. Wa ma adraka ma laylatul-qadr. Laylatul-qadri khairum min alfi shahr. Tanazzalul-mala'ikatu war-ruhu fiha bi-idhni rabbihim min kulli amr. Salamun hiya hatta matla'il-fajr. Sadaqallahu al-aliyyul-azim. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum. I have once again appeared before you to present the exegesis of Surah Al-Qadr. And my continuous discussion here is under the title of Surah Al-Qadr. And the discussion that took place yesterday, it must be preserved in your noble minds, regarding the virtues I described, that if one sleeps during the Night of Qadr, what will they be deprived of? On the Night of Qadr, the names of those going for Hajj are written, and sustenance is written, and deaths are written. The system for the whole year is written. All these things are written in this night. Then after that, I submitted, if you want to be free from debt, then the sixth Imam, the fifth Imam said, that we should keep our tongues moist with the recitation of Surah Al-Qadr and seek forgiveness as much as possible. Come, respected viewers, today let us discuss which night is the Night of Qadr. When someone asked Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq (a.s.). Which night of the blessed month of Ramadan is the Night of Qadr? He (a.s.) said: 'Seek it in the 21st and 23rd nights of the month of Ramadan.' Then, regarding the signs of Shab-e-Qadr: The narrator says, 'I asked Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), what is the sign of Shab-e-Qadr?' He replied, 'The fragrance of this night is pure and clean. If it is winter, this night is warm. If it is summer, this night is cooler than other nights.' Meaning, there is a difference. If it is summer, the weather is slightly cool; if it is winter, it is slightly warm. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that Shab-e-Qadr is a moderate night; it is neither too cold nor too hot. When the sun rises on its morning, it has no rays. This is the Hadith of the Prophet and the Hadith of the Sixth Imam that I have narrated before you. How can one attain Shab-e-Qadr? A man asked Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.). He came to your holy presence and said, 'O Son of the Prophet, if I say something, will you not be angry?' This is the way of asking. He replied, 'No, say what you wish to say.' He said, 'You have looked at this verse of the Holy Quran: ﴿لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾. O Son of the Prophet, how do we know that Shab-e-Qadr comes every year?' He replied, 'When the month of Ramadan begins, recite Surah Dukhan 100 times every night. When the 23rd night of the blessed month arrives, you will find the answer to your question and you will confirm that I have attained Shab-e-Qadr.' The night of the 21st of Ramadan: The virtues of the 21st night are such that it is narrated from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) that when the martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) occurred, Imam Hasan (a.s.) delivered a sermon in the Mosque of Kufa. He praised and glorified Allah, sent salutations upon the Holy Prophet, and said, 'O people, today a personality has departed from this world who surpassed all those who came before, and those who come after will not be able to reach even his dust. They will not be able to reach the dust of the one who has passed.' Meaning, no one will be able to equal Ali ibn Abi Talib. By God, on this very night, the successor of Moses (a.s.) departed from this world. On this very night, Jesus (a.s.) was raised towards the heavens. This is the night in which the Holy Quran was revealed. Respected viewers, regarding the revelation of the Quran, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) further said that the Holy Quran was revealed all at once from Bayt al-Ma'mur during the month of Ramadan. Then, over a period of 20 years, it was revealed gradually—meaning slowly, in parts. Then he said, the Messenger of Allah said that the Holy Quran was revealed on the 23rd night of Ramadan. And respected viewers, you already know the acts of Shab-e-Qadr, as the Sixth Imam, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), said to seek Shab-e-Qadr in the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan. Recite one hundred rak'ats of prayer on both these nights. Perform Ghusl at the beginning of both these nights. A questioner had asked, 'If I cannot do this much, then what should I do?' People say, 'Maulana, we will not be able to do this much; we cannot pray 100 rak'ats.' The scholars said, 'If you have missed prayers (Qada), then pray for 6 days, so that 6 days of missed prayers will be reduced from your life. Otherwise, if there are no missed prayers, then pray 100 rak'ats.' He said, when that person said, 'I will not be able to do this,' meaning, 'I will not be able to pray these prayers while standing.' He said, 'Pray while sitting.' He says, 'I asked, if I cannot pray while sitting?' He said, 'Then pray while lying on your bed.' He said, 'There is no harm if you sleep in the first part of the night and stay awake later to worship all night, because the doors of the heavens open in the month of Ramadan, and the devils are chained in this month. In this month, the deeds of the believers are accepted. How blessed is the month of Ramadan! In the time of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), people used to call this month 'Marzuq' (the month of sustenance), because sustenance increased in this month, which was a cause of blessing throughout the year. And I have narrated this tradition before, that the sustenance for the whole year is written on Shab-e-Qadr. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said that destiny is formed on the 19th of Ramadan, the decision is made on the 21st night, and it is signed on the 23rd night. Interpretation of the verses: ﴿إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ * وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ * لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾. We have sent down this Quran on the Night of Qadr, and what do you know what the Night of Qadr is? The Night of Qadr is better than a thousand months. Respected viewers, many commentators have narrated regarding this Shab-e-Qadr and this Surah Qadr that it refers to the Princess of the Worlds, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). But since we are discussing the Quran, we are talking about the Quran here. Otherwise, Allah's saying ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ﴾, 'What do you know what the Night of Qadr is?' Imam Zain al-Abidin (a.s.) recited these verses and said that Allah Almighty expressed this reality that He revealed the Holy Quran on the Night of Qadr, and when He said to His Messenger ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ﴾, 'What is the Night of Qadr?', the Prophet said, 'I do not know what the Night of Qadr is.' Allah said, ﴿لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾, 'The Night of Qadr is better than a thousand months.' Respected viewers, when the Lord of the Worlds Himself is saying about this Shab-e-Qadr that it is better than a thousand nights, then we should think that when the virtue of this night is such that it is better than a thousand nights, then surely... We will receive more good deeds, and our sins will also be forgiven accordingly. Therefore, do not let Shab-e-Qadr slip through your hands. The opportunity is coming; Shab-e-Qadr is coming. Let us stay awake at night, worship, seek forgiveness, and pray for the world that the Lord of the Worlds grants the world salvation from the coronavirus and that everyone's conditions improve, that Hajj may take place, and that people may go to visit Karbala. May the doors of the holy shrines open, and may people start going for Ziyarat again. It is everyone's responsibility to pray. And when we pray for each other, our prayers will be answered even faster because the Lord of the Worlds says to the angels, 'Look, how much he cares for Our servants. He did not ask for himself first; he is asking for Our servants first. Therefore, bear witness that I have answered his prayer, and since he has prayed for the servants, We have answered their prayers too.' Respected viewers, consider the virtue and importance of this night. Therefore, I hope that you all will stay awake on this night, Shab-e-Qadr, worship, pray, and include everyone in your prayers, Insha'Allah. Please include me, the humble one, in your prayers as well. I seek your leave. Insha'Allah, the discussion will continue tomorrow. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. And our final prayer is, all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

title: Eesaal e Sawaab Majlis-e-Azaa | Baraaye Marhoom Muhammad Husain ibn Gulam Abbas
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound connection between the Holy Quran and the Ahlulbayt, emphasizing that the Quran is both a silent text and a living, speaking reality embodied by the Prophet and his progeny. It highlights the divine protection of the Quran and the religious obligation to defend the sanctity of Islamic scriptures and the Prophet against insults. The session concludes with a traditional Majlis-e-Azaa, recounting the tragedy of Karbala and the martyrdom of Abbas, while offering prayers for the soul of the late Muhammad Hussain.
content:
[Music] A spear pierced through, it went into the chest. A spear pierced through, it went into the chest. Oh, the mother will sit and weep, it pierced through the chest. Ya Ali, I say to you, Ya Ali, I say to you, the spear pierced through the chest. Tonight, peace has come, meaning whatever news comes, the spear will have pierced through. When the wounds are inflicted, when the sins are forgiven, when the sins are forgiven, Akbar, alas, has also passed away. The spear will have pierced through. The spear will have pierced through. When the wounds are inflicted, the wounds will be there. When the sins are forgiven, the wounds will be there. The spear will have pierced through. When the wounds are inflicted, the spear will have pierced through. The spear will have pierced through. [Recitation of Arabic supplication: Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin...] [Recitation of Arabic supplication continues...]. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. I request you to recite Surah Al-Hamd once and Surah Al-Ikhlas three times for the late... For the late Muhammad Hussain, son of Ghulam Abbas Sahib, may Allah grant him a high place in Paradise. [Recitation of prayers]. I request all the respected attendees, who have gathered here for the sake of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and for the mourning of Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala, to also pray for yourselves. I request all the respected attendees to pray for yourselves, for all the believers, for all the deceased whose Isal-e-Sawab (transfer of reward) is being organized, and for every believing man and woman. May Allah accept our prayers. The verse of the Holy Quran that I have chosen for today's discussion is famous throughout the Islamic world. Through this verse, the Almighty Lord, in His glorious book, the Quran Majeed, is guiding the world and conveying a message. The verse states: 'Thumma awrathnal kitabal ladheena astafayna min ibadina' (Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants). The revelation of this verse of the Quran and its message reaching until the end of time is an indication that while there were other books in the world that became 'heirless' (lost or corrupted), the greatness of the Quran lies in the fact that Allah says, 'We have appointed an heir for this Book.' We have appointed an heir for this Book. And who is this heir? This heir is not from among the people, nor is this heir from among the angels, but as I mentioned, the heir of the Quran is from among His servants. Now, imagine that for the Quran, Allah has not left the Book without an heir. The question arises: if the Torah was the Book of Allah, then why was it abrogated? If the Gospel was the Book of Allah, then why was it abrogated? The Torah had its heir, the Gospel had its heir, and similarly, the Quran has its heir. The question is, why are the Torah and Gospel not valid today? The belief of the Islamic world is that if there is any book today that is for the common people... At this time, if there is any book that is widely discussed, that is luminous, radiant, enlightened, bright, and urgent, which is being practiced, and by which the Sharia is being followed, then it is the Book of Allah. Along with it, the Book of Allah came with the prophets. Just as the Torah came with a successor, the Gospel came with a successor, and the Psalms came with a successor, the era of those books ended when their successors passed away. The era of the Torah ended, the era of the Gospel ended, and the era of the book that came with its successor also ended. So, why is the era of the Quran still ongoing? Its continued existence is proof that there was a successor to the Quran yesterday, and there is a successor to the Quran today. Allah has made Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny the guardians of the Quran. I want to explain this to you in a very simple and normal way, so that it reaches your hearts. Consider this example: if you go out into any neighborhood, suppose we go out and see a house that is magnificent, colorful, decorated with diamonds, chandeliers, and wonderful paintings. It has chandeliers, wonderful paintings, and all kinds of arrangements inside. I asked, 'Whose house is this?' Someone said, 'It belongs to so-and-so.' But it had completely changed; it was falling apart. I asked, 'How did this happen?' I saw the whole house had chandeliers, lighting, and paintings, but there is no one to look after this house; the walls are collapsing. Friends, this is a house whose owner has left, and it has been handed over to someone else. Now, do you understand? The era of the previous books ended because their successors passed away. But, O Muslims, tell me, the fact that the Quran has remained for 1400 years—shouldn't its continuity point towards something? Its continuity points towards this fact; it indicates that the Quranic successor was present yesterday and is present today. The proof is that when the successors of the previous books passed away, the era of those books ended. But the fact that the era of the Quran remains is proof that there was a successor to the Quran yesterday, and there is a successor to the Quran today. Another point, O respected audience, is that Allah has presented the Quranic verses as magnificent and glorious. Allah says, 'We have revealed this Book.' Now, if someone considers themselves a scholar in the eyes of the world, but they are doing this, I want to say that one must maintain a certain perspective. I want to say that one must maintain a certain perspective, and a verse regarding the protection of the Quran is present in the Quran itself. Allah says that for this Quran, a successor is present. And for this Quran, Allah has appointed the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny. Allah says, 'We will protect it.' This points to the fact that wherever this Book of Allah exists, it is a book that no one can alter. Allah says, 'We will protect it.' So, how is it possible for anyone to make changes to something that Allah has promised to protect? Yet, we see that some people show disrespect to the Messenger. We see someone showing disrespect to the Messenger, or someone not understanding something and saying, 'This should be removed.' This Quran, which speaks of humanity, which strings together pearls of love and affection—how can anyone raise their voice against this Book? They say, 'These verses, we don't understand them, they should be removed from the Quran.' Whether it is a common person or someone reaching the Supreme Court, they say, 'These verses should be removed.' If someone is confused, they should be forced to think, 'Should I follow this or not?' But the reality is that those who call themselves Muslims are the ones who do such things, saying, 'We don't understand these verses, they should be removed.' However, if a person were to read the Quran, perhaps they would realize that there is no greater book of humanity and ethics than this, which teaches everyone the lesson of humanity, teaches everyone how to be a human, and conducts classes on unity and morality. O respected audience, to be against such a book, and to say, 'We don't understand these verses...' They came against it, and I do not understand this balance. I even joked that there were some who knocked on the doors of the Supreme Court to remove verses of the Quran, but they were unaware that by removing these verses, they were removing themselves from Islam. To take this to a question, I asked to bring milk, and in another verse, Allah said that We have revealed this Book and We will protect it. The world is witnessing that Allah is the Protector of Allah's word. Regarding those who said that these verses should be removed, they... Those people said that they should be removed. The state of Muslims was such that, tell me, Taslima Nasreen had said before that Islam says this and that. Tell me, did any Muslim come out against Salman Rushdie to protest, saying that my Prophet has been insulted? No one came out. But may Allah keep that nation safe, those loyal people who were the first to protest against Salman Rushdie, issued a fatwa against him, and showed that yesterday we were loyal to the Prophet and today we are still loyal to the Prophet. Where everyone on social media is raising slogans against him, saying he is a disbeliever, cursed, and a blasphemer. It is a matter of great joy to say before the entire Islamic world that if anyone insults the Quran, which Allah has protected, then Alhamdulillah, you protest against it. But my question is, if someone insults the Prophet, you should protest against that too. In fact, wherever they are, there should be a protest against them. Now listen, and subscribe, that it is a matter for Muslims that we stand with you to give a befitting reply to those who insult the Quran. But our only point is that if someone insults the Quran, they are cursed, and if someone insults the Prophet, they are also... And for that, I chose Allah, and then for this, the picture of the verse... subscribe, because if anyone still doubts, this Book is the truth, and Allah has taken the responsibility for it. If Allah has taken the responsibility, it means there is no room for doubt for anyone. So, according to this, if any person in the world has any doubt about the verses of the Holy Quran... If anyone is seen having even the slightest doubt about the verses of the Holy Quran, understand that they are mocking the verses of the Quran. It is against the Quran, Islam, and the Muslims. If someone does this, it is... Muslims, may Allah keep all Muslims steadfast. You have proven that if someone does this, they become a disbeliever. So, for Salman and others, Allah has said, 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, We have not sent Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) for anything else...' If this logic... and the Quran... Allah has not sent His Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) for anything else. It is the Quran, the Radiant Quran, the Clear Quran (Quran-e-Mubeen). The Quran is Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the Quran. This means the Quran is Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), his progeny, and their Quran. It is understood that the Quran has stated that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the Clear Quran. The one who is the Quran is also the Clear Quran. The one upon whose heart it is revealed is also the Quran. The one who is receiving it is also the Quran. It is understood that Allah has called this the Quran, but the one who receives it is called the 'Clear Quran' (Quran-e-Mubeen). Now, for that, Allah says there is no room for doubt in it. For the Quran, Allah says in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 2, 'Dhalikal kitabu la rayba feeh' (This is the Book about which there is no doubt). This means the silent Quran and the speaking Quran are one. I have explained the greatness of the Quran and the greatness of the Quran-e-Mubeen. I wanted to summarize the points quickly. I have placed before you the verse of the Holy Quran: the silent Quran is the Quran, and the speaking Quran is also the Quran. Regarding the silent Quran, I have presented the verses, and regarding the speaking Quran, Allah has described it as the Quran-e-Mubeen. For the Quran, Allah said in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 2, that there is no room for doubt in it. For it, Allah has said that it must stand shoulder to shoulder with the entirety of Islam. The decision should be that he and his heir are the truth, and anyone who opposes them is wrong. Prove your being a Muslim by showing that whoever speaks against the silent Quran is a dweller of Hell, and the same applies to the speaking Quran. I am trying to conclude quickly. The Messenger (s.a.w.a.) said that Allah has chosen an heir for this Book. We have kept it for this heir, and respected elders, you will find him in every era, in every age. You will find in every era, and you will find it very quickly—if you speak about it in this society of yours, in the field, among the people, it won't be in the oldest of markets, but rather everyone... but with this increasing [question of] who is related to what, and our youth, these children of the Muslims... who is the one who truly understands the Quran? Who is the real one? Who is the one who can explain it? I have the strength to present this before you, a matter that is absolutely clear. Look, there is a legacy, and the heir to this legacy has been chosen by Allah. But when Allah has chosen, the command of people from every stratum will come to us. You will find people from all over the world here. If I only show you this much, that which is needed, but now cover it... You have what is needed, but now cover it, subscribe to the solution. Now you will say, 'Sir, the legacy is not visible, what does this mean?' So I say, look at the example of the sun, it is absolutely clear. I present a matter before you: look, every Muslim believes, or rather everyone believes, that the Holy Quran is a book within which every single thing is mentioned, every verse exists, every... [inaudible]... and then by reading the verses, the Quran says—Allah says—that there is no small thing or big thing in the Holy Quran [that is not mentioned]. In this book, in this book, the entire universe is contained, and every small and big thing is present. So, if you understand it this way, then at least understand it as that which establishes every single thing, where every small and big thing is established. Do not understand it as something where, if a problem arises, one knocks on the door of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and if one comes to seek a solution, one goes to his daughter's door. It should not be... It should not be that if someone is asked about a word from the Holy Quran, they are seen struggling. By God, we have seen very big names in the Islamic world, but we did not find a face that could be looked at and said, 'This is the heir to the Quran.' But one personality was found who came to the pulpit of the Mosque of Kufa and challenged, saying, 'Saluni, saluni' (Ask me, ask me) before I depart from among you. Do you know who that personality is? The one who brings the Quran to life is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And why not? Because the Master of the Universe knew that if the Quran is presented with me, then I am the one who decides the judgment of the one who is near, the one who is far, the one who is in the heart, and the one who is in the soul. And he said, 'I am the speaking Quran, I am the Commander of the Faithful.' So where is the Quran's solution to be found? If there is any light or fire anywhere, then the entire universe is in the manifest Imam, and the noble Messenger, and the Quran. Now, can he do anything in this world? You will find about this, but if our youth... You will find about this, but if our youth, if all of us want to know what the Quran is and who its heir is, then I will just say this: my brothers, look for the power of the Quran within the Quran. Wherever this power is seen, understand that this is the heir to the Quran. Now you will say, 'What is the power?' So come, I will only say three things, although these three things are present in the verses of the Quran. The first thing is that the Holy Quran has written its own power in the Quran, which is: 'Surah... [inaudible]... power, power.' This is the power of the one who recites the Quran. Your religious texts... so tell me, what is the need for you to be driven or moved by others? Like the verses of the Quran, read them, remove the stones, read the verses, remove the obstacles. We are Ajami (non-Arab) people; in our language, what is said, and where our... [inaudible]... where our recitation is, where our understanding is, where that language is, where all those words are... the Quran is that which is the source, that which is the light, where the miracle is, where the... [inaudible]... Where the miracle is, where the... [inaudible]... is. You tell me, these are things from seven or eight years ago, that then it became a disaster, and I don't know how many thousands of people were martyred there. You tell me, what is the need to apply this? The Quran is stating its own challenge and its own power, that our verses can move mountains. So, is there anyone in the Islamic world who, by reading the verses of the Quran, can move the Quran? But dear ones, as far as my own mind goes, until today, no one has been found who could be looked at and said, 'This is the heir to the Book.' He will read the verses, but he will move the mountains. But yes, when we looked with the eye of analysis, it was revealed that the Panjtan Pak (the five holy ones) were the ones who came out into the field of Mubahala, seeing whom the Christians of Najran wrote that we will not do Mubahala. They said, 'Why not?' Because their faces were such that if they were to point, every mountain would move. And so it was revealed that the Panjtan Pak, if you have the light, seeing whom the Najranis pointed out... the face is power, power. And then, so you tell me, this... Power, power, and once again, tell me, how many of our Muslims are currently deprived of Umrah, how many are unable to go, ambitions are being blocked, and it feels like the lights have gone out. Tell me, in such a situation, what is happening? If there is no attention towards Muslims, then there is a need for something to happen so that it is understood. And clearly, this is why it is visible from here as well, standing in a large field. People are coming home and saying, 'Look, if you want to see the power of the Quran, look at the Ummah, look at it properly.' You say, 'Look at the Ummah, look at it properly,' and if that is not the case, then tell me, how many people in the world have had their relationships and lives pass by on this path? If someone truly possessed the power of the Quran, they could bring the Ummah back to life, they could revive it, even if it were in total darkness. But has anyone ever been found who has actually done this? And there are many things in the world that suggest that the earth shrinks under our feet. We worry, but thank God, our books contain all of this. It has been said that they do things to save themselves, but the reality of those who are true is that even if their lineage is thin, it will not end. But the enemies thought that by killing Hussain, his lineage would end. However, the severed head of Hussain showed that Hussain can go, he can do things, he cannot be stopped, and his legacy cannot be erased. To know all of this, what should I do? Tell me, how can I describe the recitation of Hussain? As a poet once said, 'The era has passed, Hussain will take it.' There is water, and from the very beginning, different voices are heard, hoping for different doors. A voice comes, 'Accept my salaam, O Hussain,' and they keep the lamps burning. It was coming from the side of the desert... subscribe, subscribe. As soon as she said this, Hussain fulfilled the sisters' request. He stood in the middle of the sisters. title: Wilaadat, Ghaibat, Intezaar - Ahle Tasannun Kitab Mein Maujod
excerpt: This lecture examines historical evidence from the Sunni scholar Salahuddin Safadi's book, 'Al-Wafi bi-l-Wafayat', regarding the existence and lineage of Imam Mahdi. The speaker highlights how the text confirms the Imam's birth, his ancestral connection to the Prophet's household, and the Shia belief in his occultation. By citing a non-Shia source, the lecture reinforces the historical consensus on the identity of the twelfth Imam.
content:
Al-Wafi bi-l-Wafayat, authored by Salahuddin Safadi, was written in the eighth century. Here he writes about 'Al-Hujjat al-Muntazar' and then he mentions the name of the Imam: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Askari, son of Ali al-Hadi, son of Muhammad al-Jawad, son of Ali al-Rida, son of Musa al-Kazim, and in this way, he traces it back to Imam Ali (a.s.). Then he says, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with them all).' Then he says that this person, meaning Hujjat al-Muntazar, is the one who is the twelfth Imam of the Shia, and the Shia know him as the Muntazar (the Awaited One), the Mahdi, and his birth took place in the cellar (sardab) of Samarra in the year 255 AH. After this, he further says that this is the one whom the Shia are waiting for. That is, from this book, we not only learn that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has taken place, but his father's name is also mentioned, and his ancestors—the Imams of the Pure (a.s.)—are also mentioned, explaining from whose lineage Imam Mahdi (a.s.) descends. The last thing he mentioned was that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) would go into occultation and the Shia would wait for his reappearance.

title: Ilm Ek Khazaana Hai | Knowledge is a Treasure | Kalaam e Noor # 02
excerpt: This short lecture highlights the profound wisdom of Imam Ali (a.s.) regarding the nature of knowledge. It emphasizes that unlike material wealth, true knowledge is an inexhaustible treasure that provides eternal value. The teaching encourages believers to pursue learning as a spiritual and intellectual investment.
content:
Imam Ali (a.s.) said: 'Knowledge is a great treasure that will never be exhausted.'
Knowledge is defined as a great treasure.
Unlike worldly possessions, knowledge does not diminish when shared.
Imam Ali (a.s.) serves as the primary source of this wisdom.
The pursuit of knowledge is a lifelong endeavor.

title: Aashur Ke Din Duniyaawi Kaamon Mein Mashgool Rehne Ka Azaab [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the spiritual significance of the Day of Ashura and the importance of mourning for Imam Hussain (a.s.). It highlights a tradition from Imam Rida (a.s.) warning against engaging in worldly activities or treating Ashura as a day of celebration. The speaker encourages believers to immerse themselves in grief and prayer, aligning their hearts with the sorrow of the Ahlul-Bayt.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon you, O Guardian of the Age, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Hazrat Imam Rida (a.s.) said: 'Whoever refrains from seeking their worldly needs on the day of Ashura, Allah the Almighty will fulfill their needs of this world and the hereafter. For the one for whom the day of Ashura is a day of tragedy, grief, and weeping, Allah the Almighty will make the Day of Judgment a day of joy and happiness for him. His eyes will find coolness in Paradise because of us. But whoever considers the day of Ashura a day of blessing and brings new things into his house, then whatever new thing he has brought will have no blessing in it, and on the Day of Judgment, such a person will be resurrected with Yazid, Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, and Umar ibn Sa'ad (may Allah curse them), and he will be in the lowest level of Hell.' Keeping the hadith of Imam Rida (a.s.) in mind, remember that the day of Ashura is a day of great tragedy for the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). No one can estimate the state of the heart of that son of Imam Hussain (a.s.) who sits in the veil of occultation, who declares in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah: 'O my grandfather Hussain! I weep for you morning and evening, and I weep blood instead of tears.' Therefore, for a mourner, let alone being busy with worldly affairs on this day, even thinking about them does not befit them. Try as much as possible that our mind, our soul, our self, and indeed our entire being be immersed in the grief of Hazrat Aba Abdillahil-Hussain. Try, as a true mourner, that this day, this Day of Ashura, passes in such a state that tears of grief for Hussain flow from our eyes and on our lips there is only one prayer: 'Ya Rabbal-Hussain, bihaqqil-Hussain, ishfe sadral-Hussain, bizuhuril-hujjah.' O Lord of Hussain! For the sake of Imam Hussain, grant solace to the heart of Hussain through the reappearance of Your final Proof. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Par Girye Ki Ehmiyat [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the profound spiritual significance of weeping for Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the rewards associated with this act of devotion. It highlights the sorrow of the heavens and the angels over the tragedy of Karbala, noting that these celestial beings await the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) to seek justice. The speaker encourages believers to perform Ziyarat and express their grief to attain forgiveness and proximity to the Prophet in Paradise.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his progeny. Peace be upon you, O Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. Imam Reza (a.s.) said: 'If you wish to weep over anything, then weep over Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), for he was treated in a way that no other person was treated, and eighteen of his companions were martyred with him, the likes of whom are not found on this earth. Indeed, the seven heavens and the earths have wept over his martyrdom. Forty thousand angels descended from the heavens to assist him, but when they arrived, they found Imam Hussain (a.s.) already martyred. They remain there, covered in dust, waiting for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.).' And they will be his helpers, and their slogan will be 'Ya Latharat al-Hussain' (O avengers of Hussain). If you weep over Hussain until your tears reach your cheeks, Allah will forgive all your sins, whether they are small or large, few or many. If you wish to meet Allah (s.w.t.) without any sins, then perform the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). And if you wish to reside in the highest station of Paradise with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), then curse the killers of Hussain. O Allah, curse the killers of Hussain. Just as the sky is weeping, my eyes are weeping; someone is bringing a handkerchief for me. I have been told that in weeping for Imam Hussain (a.s.)... I have been told that in weeping for Imam Hussain (a.s.), there is a connection to the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). May Allah hasten his reappearance and grant us the opportunity to be among his companions to take revenge for Imam Hussain (a.s.). Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: EP#13: Kya Imam Ali (a.s.) Ne Haakim Ki Bay’at Ki?
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical validity of the claim that Imam Ali (a.s.) gave voluntary allegiance to the first Caliph. The speaker argues that the event described in historical texts was not a genuine Bay'ah but rather a forced submission under the threat of death. By referencing Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinawari's 'Al-Imama wa al-Siyasa', the lecture challenges the legitimacy of a Caliphate established through coercion.
content:
Forcing the hand of Imam Ali (a.s.) to be placed on the hand of a ruler is not called 'Bay'ah' (allegiance). It is famous among Muslims that Mawla Ali (a.s.) gave allegiance to the ruler of his time, but can it be considered a true allegiance? Let us see what actually happened. The famous historian Ibn Qutaybah al-Dinawari wrote in his book 'Al-Imama wa al-Siyasa' that those people (the people of Saqifah) forcibly brought Ali (a.s.) out of his house, and after presenting him before Abu Bakr, they demanded his allegiance. In response, Ali (a.s.) asked, 'If I do not do this, what will you do?' They replied, 'We swear by Allah, besides whom there is no other god, we will behead you.' Now, every Muslim should reflect on this: can demanding allegiance by threatening someone with death be considered a true allegiance? And that too, from Mawla Ali (a.s.)! If such an allegiance were the basis for choosing a Caliph, what value would such a Caliphate hold? This might be politics, but it is not Caliphate.
True allegiance requires voluntary consent, not coercion.

title: #8: Sabr Aur Jehaad | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen | شرح زیارت اربعین  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound nature of patience (Sabr) as demonstrated by Imam Hussain (a.s.) throughout his life, culminating in the tragedy of Karbala. It highlights his unwavering obedience to God despite witnessing the martyrdom of his father, brother, and companions. The speaker connects this historical sacrifice to the anticipation of the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), emphasizing the need for believers to maintain their faith during worldly trials.
content:
Peace be upon you. But Imam Hussain (a.s.) is the one who, for the sake of the awaited one, fought against those enemies. From 11 AH to 36 AH, you (Hussain) remained patient with your father, the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and in 40 AH, you remained patient through his martyrdom. Then, in 50 AH, you saw the pieces of the liver of your elder brother, Imam Hassan (a.s.), and remained patient through his martyrdom. In Karbala, you saw your brothers, sons, nephews, relatives, loved ones, and companions being martyred before your eyes. Yet, despite all these calamities and trials, you declared on the battlefield of Karbala, 'We will remain patient through all His trials.' It is easy to talk, but when one is surrounded by calamity, the reality is different. When a person's life is at stake, that is the true test of obedience to God. Imam Hussain (a.s.) sacrificed not only his own life but also his companions and family. This is the pinnacle of obedience to God. O God, for the sake of Imam Hussain's (a.s.) sacrifice, hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) to take revenge for his martyrdom. May He hasten his reappearance, and grant us the ability to remain patient through the calamities and trials of this world, and not sacrifice our religion, and remain completely with our Imam.
