title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 8 | Tafseer of Surah al-Faatiha (Surah # 1) - Part 8
excerpt: This lecture explores the interpretation of the 'Straight Path' in Surah al-Faatiha through the lens of Shia traditions. The speaker emphasizes that the straight path is synonymous with the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, particularly Imam Ali (a.s.). The session concludes by discussing the identity of those 'bestowed with favor' and the spiritual significance of Taqiyyah as a divine blessing.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and peace and blessings be upon the master of the prophets and messengers, Abul Qasim Muhammad, and upon his pure, clean, and infallible family, and may the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies from now until the Day of Judgment. To proceed: Allah the Almighty says in His Noble Book, 'Guide us to the straight path.' Dear viewers, peace be upon you. Once again, I am present to serve you with the Tafsir of Surah Al-Hamd, by the grace of God. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), while interpreting 'Guide us to the straight path,' said that its meaning is: 'O God, guide us to the straight path and show us the path that can lead us to Your love and Your religion, and act as a barrier for us against following desires, so that we do not fall into destruction by acting upon our own opinions.' With the same chain of narration, Thabit Asmani narrated from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) that he said: 'We are the gates of God, and we are the straight path.' In the previous clip, you heard me mention, based on the traditions of the Infallibles, that the straight path refers to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and indeed all the Imams. The fourth Imam is also saying that we are the 'Babullah' (gates of God) and we are the straight path. This means that if a human wants to reach God, they need to be connected to these personalities, to the Infallibles, to the Imams; only then can they reach God. Otherwise, it is just a delusion that we have reached God. To reach God, it is necessary to be connected to the Imam, and the straight path is also the same: when we are connected to the Imams (a.s.), the first thing is to acknowledge their Wilayah, to accept their Wilayah. Wilayah means the right they have over us; we must fulfill this right and give them the status that is theirs, and understand and place them at that status. Anyway, I will explain the Tafsir of Wilayah on some other occasion, God willing. Meanwhile, it is narrated from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) that he narrated from his pure ancestors and from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that the Prophet said: 'Ali, when the Day of Judgment comes, you, I, and Gabriel will sit on the Sirat (bridge), and only the one who has the permit of your Wilayah will pass through the Sirat.' Allahu Akbar. This means that even if a person keeps praying prayer after prayer, fasting, performing Hajj, giving Zakat, doing everything, but if there is no Wilayah of Ali, they cannot pass through the Sirat. This is what the Prophet said: 'O Ali, whoever does not have the permit of your Wilayah will not be able to pass through the Sirat.' In Usul al-Kafi, it is narrated from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) that Allah revealed to His Prophet: 'What has been revealed to you, hold fast to it; indeed, you are on the straight path.' The purpose is that you are on the Wilayah of Ali, and Ali is the straight path. It is Ali who is the straight path. Another tradition from Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.): when asked about this verse, he said: 'Is one who walks fallen on his face better guided, or one who walks straight on the straight path?' In response to this verse, Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.) said that this verse describes the example of a person who deviates from the Wilayah of Ali, and the one who deviates from the Wilayah of Ali is like a person who has fallen on his face, while the one who follows Ali is walking straight on the straight path, and the straight path is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Allahu Akbar, reflect on this noble tradition where the Imam said that the person who deviates from the Wilayah of Ali will be fallen on his face. Now, it is not just that he has fallen; all his acts of worship, if he is deviated from the Wilayah of Ali, will be thrown on his face; there will be no benefit from those acts of worship. But if he is connected to the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib, then he will stand straight, be guided, and be on the path that is the path of the Ahlulbayt, which is the path of the Imams and the straight path. In the book Ma'ani al-Akhbar, it is narrated from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that he said regarding the verse 'The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor,' that the 'people of favor' refers to Muhammad and his progeny. That is, those who are referred to in 'the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor' are the progeny of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Ibn Sayyar asked Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) about the interpretation of 'the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor,' and he said that its meaning is... that you say: 'Guide us to the path of those whom You have favored by granting them the success of Your religion and Your obedience.' And regarding the 'people of favor,' Allah said: 'And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, they are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor—the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous—and excellent are those as companions' (Surah An-Nisa, verse 69). The same interpretation is narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). The 'people of favor' does not refer to those who have the favor of wealth and health, although this is also an apparent favor from God. Do you not see that the favor of wealth and health is also available to disbelievers and evildoers, and you have not been commanded to pray for their path? You have been commanded to pray for the path of those upon whom the favor of faith in Allah, confirmation of the Messenger, Wilayah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, righteous companions, and the best Taqiyyah has been bestowed. Allahu Akbar, through which they remain protected from the evil of the enemies of God, and because of the best Taqiyyah, they become a cause for the increase in the sins and disbelief of the enemies of God. Beware, maintaining Taqiyyah, treating opponents with courtesy, not creating difficulties for yourself and other believers by abandoning Taqiyyah, and remaining aware of the rights of your believing brothers. Allahu Akbar. Now reflect on the discussion here regarding Taqiyyah, how important it is. Practicing Taqiyyah is a divine favor that we have received as a blessing. It is a divine favor, a bounty that Allah has given, and it is a cause for the increase in the sins of the enemies of God and a cause for the protection of the believers so that the believers remain safe from it. Therefore, we should not abandon it under any circumstances. It has been emphasized, and you have realized from this the importance of the straight path, and after 'Guide us to the straight path,' the 'path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor' that you pray for in Surah Al-Hamd—that you seek the path of those upon whom You have sent down favors. God willing, we will discuss this tomorrow. Until then, goodbye. And our final prayer is that all praise is due to... Allah, Lord of the worlds.

excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual status of the Ahlulbayt, emphasizing that their station transcends human intellect and is divinely appointed. The discussion covers the necessity of absolute submission to Wilayah, the dangers of rejecting Hadith based on personal reasoning, and the historical context of the Imamate. content:
That we will be called the free ones of the Master (Sarwar). We will be called the free ones of the Master. We have love for Islam, we will be called that. We will be called the free ones of the Master. Listen: 'Kalma ko ajre risalat to ada pehle karo'—first pay the reward of the Prophethood for the Kalma. Then you will be called a devotee of Muhammad. We will be called the free ones of the Master. Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. So, we cannot be friends with the enemy of Haider. We cannot be friends with the enemy of Haider. When the time comes, we will be called those who stood at the gallows. We will be called the free ones of the Master. So, that Muslim who does not remember that calamity, that Muslim who does not remember that calamity, is certainly called mentally ill. We will be called the free ones of the Master. So, especially: come, mourn and become the free ones of the Master. Come, mourn and become the free ones of the Master. Otherwise, you will be called a supporter of the killer. We will be called the free ones of the Master. So, the one in whose prostration the love of Ali is not included, the one in whose prostration the love of Ali is not included, every prostration of his will be called useless. Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. The one in whose prostration the love of Ali is not included, every prostration of his will be called useless. We will be called the free ones of the Master. So, those who snatched and sat on the garden of Zahra, Fida. Those who snatched and sat on the garden of Zahra, how can they be called landlords? Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. We will be called the free ones of the Master. So, especially: look at the miracle of these tears in the field of Hashr, Ehsan brother, look at the miracle of these tears in the field of Hashr. We will be called the buyers of Paradise. We will be called the liberated ones of the Master (Sarwar). So, one who is not infallible (Masoom) but is infallible in their deeds—one who is not infallible but is infallible in their deeds—will be called the standard-bearer (Alamdar) of the Master. We will be called the liberated ones of the Master. This is the final couplet: that whoever’s eyes do not weep in the grief of the Master, O Danish, whoever’s eyes do not weep in the grief of the Master, O Danish, Such eyes will be called the sinful ones. We will be called the liberated ones of the Master. Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. May Allah have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. What an excellent Master and what an excellent Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. And the final outcome is for the righteous and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of the prophets and messengers, The Beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And only the one who is 'Khashi' (humble) will accept Wilayah. Wow, wow, wow. In whom humility will be found. So the Imam says, 'Wa lam yaqul' (And Allah did not say) 'wa innahuma la-kabiratun' (and these two are hard). Allah did not say 'wa innahuma la-kabiratun illal-khashi'in'. 'Fasabru Rasulullah, was-salatu iqamatu wilayati, faminhuma qalallahu ta'ala wa innaha la-kabiratun, wa lam yaqul wa innahuma la-kabiratun, li-annal-wilayata kabiratun' (So patience is the Messenger of Allah, and prayer is the establishment of my Wilayah, so regarding them Allah the Almighty said 'and it is indeed hard', and He did not say 'and they are indeed hard', because Wilayah is hard). What is hard? 'Hamluha illal-khashi'in' (To bear it, except for the humble). To bear this Wilayah, to be a believer in the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, this is only for the 'Khashi'in'. And who are these 'Khashi'in'? The Imam says, 'Wal-khashi'una hum shi'atuhum, hum shi'atul-mustabsirun.' Wow, wow, wow, wow, wow, wow. These 'Khashi'in' are only our Shia who are the possessors of insight. In whom insight is found, in whom that insight is found. Wow. Only they are 'Khashi'. 'Khashi' means that a person is humble. Meaning, there is humility before the Ahlulbayt. Look, this is a very important thing. What is the meaning of humility? That is, what is called 'Khashi Khushu'? It means for a human to submit, for a human to surrender. This is called Khushu. And these are only the Shia, and those who possess 'Baseerat' (insight). I mentioned to you in the Majlis the day before yesterday that those whom Allah grants light, those who see with the light of Allah, Allah grants them belief, Allah grants them faith. They are established on that level of faith which is bestowed by Allah. They do not wander through books and merely the words of books, but rather it is the light that Allah implants in their hearts. That which Allah places in their hearts. And the Imam says, what is the reason for this? 'Li-anna ahl al-aqawil min al-Murji'ah wa al-Qadariyyah wa al-Khawarij wa ghayrihim min al-Nasibiyyah yuqirruna li-Muhammadin salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi.' Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Forgive this, because Murji'ah was a name of a sect, and those who are the majority today, they had a name in that era: Murji'ah. They were called Murji'ah. So these Murji'ah, these Qadariyyah, in opposition to them—meaning the Mu'tazilah, those who were two different sects of Muslims in that era—and the third, the Khawarij, the Khawarij who were enemies of everyone. The Mawla is saying here that all these sects, all of them, they all believe in the Messenger of Allah. There is no one among them who does not believe in the Messenger of Allah. They all testify that 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah.' But he says there is no disagreement among them in this, there is no difference. But when it comes to Wilayah, 'wa hum mukhtalifuna fi wilayati.' But when it comes to my Wilayah, then disagreement arises among them. They do not accept my Wilayah. 'Munkiruna lillik jahiduna biha illal qalil.' They deny my Wilayah. They deny it even while knowing. Even while knowing the truth, they deny it. Look, it is not as if the Messenger of Allah did not introduce the Mawla of the Universe. From the 'Dawat-e-Zul-Asheera' until his last breath. In the Dawat-e-Zul-Asheera, when the command of Allah came: 'Fasda' bima tu'mar' (Proclaim what you are commanded). Announce it. 'Wa andhir ashirataka al-aqrabin' (And warn your closest relatives). 'Asheera' refers to the family. 'Aqrabin' are those who are closest, the very closest. Meaning a maximum of two generations, no more than that. Not more than two generations. Like we say cousins, invite at most your first cousins, no more than that. Invite your first cousins, that's it. Meaning your first cousins, their children, whatever relatives they have—brothers, sisters, etc.—meaning the Banu Abdul Muttalib, invite them all, tell them all. Everyone was included in that, Abu Jahl, Abu Lahab, all of them. But only up to that point. The turn of the 'Abu's had not come yet. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Only up to here. And when the Prophet announced it, when he announced the religion of Prophethood, along with Prophethood, he announced Wilayah and Imamate. 'Haza akhi wa wasiyi wa khalifati.' This is my brother, this is my Wasi (successor), this is my Janasheen (successor), this is my Khalifa. 'Fikum' (among you), 'min ba'di' (after me). 'Fasma'u lahu wa ati'u' (Listen to him and obey him). The command was given at that time. In the first announcement, when Prophethood was announced, no one knew. No one knew who the Prophet was, that this Messenger of Allah is the Prophet, no one knew. When Allah commanded, then the Messenger of Allah announced it. When he announced Prophethood, he announced Wilayah along with it. Usually, what is the misunderstanding among us? They say that Ghadir-e-Khum was the final announcement. No, no, Ghadir-e-Khum was not the final announcement. Even after Ghadir-e-Khum, when the Prophet reached Medina, he still announced the Wilayah of Ali, he recited the Hadith-e-Saqalain. On his deathbed, he said, 'Inni tarikun fikum al-saqalayn, Kitaballahi wa itrati Ahli Bayti.' The Prophet was saying on his deathbed that look, I am leaving behind two precious things among you. One is the Book of Allah and the other is my Ahlulbayt. 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tazillu ba'di abada.' As long as you hold onto these two, if you hold them firmly, the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, then you will never go astray after me. 'Fa-innuhuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayya al-hawz.' Because they will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Hawz (the Pond). Now, since the mention of the Hawz has come up, another Hadith comes to mind, a very powerful Hadith in Bukhari. A very powerful Hadith. It is found in Bukhari. Well, if it were in a Shia book, you would say this is a Rafidi, they insult the Sahaba like this. Now we don't know whose insult is in this. But it is definitely in Bukhari, just go and Google it, you see, nowadays it is very easy, nothing is hidden. So there is no need to do Taqiyya either. So you just type, go and type 'Rabbi, ashabi ashabi', that's it. Not much, just do that. And listen to what the Hadith is, the discussion ends here today. That the Hawz, you know the Hawz-e-Kawthar. Who is the owner of this Hawz-e-Kawthar? The Messenger of Allah. Salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Now look, we are not saying this. This is actually present in the narrations, and both sides have narrated it, both sects. The Shias have narrated it and the non-Shias have also narrated it, everyone has. Who is the owner? The Prophet. Who is the Saqi (the one who serves)? You didn't understand the point. We kept the food here, meaning we sponsored it, saying 'Brother, we will sponsor this food,' yes, okay. But we said, 'Brother, so-and-so will serve the food.' Now it is in the authority of the one serving to decide who gets a piece of meat and who doesn't. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Now if you come to us for small things, 'give him a piece of meat,' brother, we just... for small things, go to him, why are you bothering us? We have made him responsible. Now it is written in the narration of Bukhari that Ali was made the Saqi. Ali will be serving everyone from the Hawz-e-Kawthar. There will be some companions who, because the Kawthar, the Hawz-e-Kawthar, is outside of Paradise, not inside Paradise. Because when people come thirsty, tired, and defeated on the Day of Judgment, the Mawla of the Universe will quench their thirst from the Kawthar there. Of course, he will quench the thirst of the people of Paradise, it is for the people of Paradise, but it is outside of Paradise. Outside, there the Mawla will quench their thirst, it is in the Mawla's authority. So the Mawla is standing there. Now, some people will come who are tired, defeated, thirsty, whatever their condition may be. Now they will go, we cannot physically describe what the state will be. I just remembered a verse of the Quran, but I will not recite it. They will just go. They will go towards the Hawz-e-Kawthar. As soon as they go, angels will be standing there for guard duty. That is very... because the Mawla of the Universe himself does not do small tasks, right? Not small tasks, he has kept angels. It is written that they have large... how do I explain? Meaning, there is a staff, right, a staff with iron attached to it. That is called 'Zirba' in Arabic. The angels are standing there holding that Zirba. As soon as they come—I am not saying anything, I am not saying anything, look, I am just telling you the Hadith. As soon as they come, these people come—which people will come, I don't know. I don't even know who these people are. Just that they will come, they will come, as soon as they get close, the angels will start hitting them with the staff. Saying, 'Go away, you will get nothing from here.' So the Prophet, seeing this, will say, 'Ya Rabbi, ashabi, ashabi!' (O my Lord, my companions, my companions!). Lord, these are my companions. So the answer will come from Allah, 'You do not know ma ahdasu ba'daka' (what they did after you). You do not know what they did after you. This is the narration. And we are not reading a Shia narration so that you can accuse us of insulting, no, no. Read this Hadith. Yes, then whatever you want to justify, justify it, explain it, whatever we don't understand, explain it to us. These are the Sahaba. So they say, 'You insult the Sahaba,' no, never. Absolutely not, we respect the Sahaba very much. We really do, we have a command to do so. There is a command for respect. But those Sahaba who respected the Messenger of Allah and the Mawla of the Universe. Those who respected the Messenger of Allah and the Ahlulbayt. They are worthy of a hundred respects. On our heads. On our heads. This is our belief. We are not using Taqiyya here. The truth is exactly this. That there is a command. But those Sahaba, remember this. Remember this point. Those who respected the Messenger of Allah. Those who respected the Ahlulbayt. Only those Sahaba. And among those Sahaba, the Prophet saw one in his childhood. Whose name was Habib ibn Muzahir. Habib ibn Muzahir al-Asadi. Of the Banu Asad. Habib. And what did he see? What scene did the Prophet see? You know? Habib was older than Imam Hussain (a.s.) in age. He was older. But he was very close to Imam Hussain (a.s.) in childhood. What scene did the Prophet see? That Imam Hussain is walking. And Habib is picking up the dust from where his feet are falling, and putting it on his head, and kissing it. Habib, to this extent. Meaning, in that childhood, Habib had this level of 'Marifat' (recognition) of the Imam. And then Habib became very close to the Imam. Very, very close. When the Sayyid-ush-Shuhada reached Karbala, he remembered Habib. When a person is in great difficulty, he remembers his special friends. The Imam wrote a letter. The messenger of Hussain, the courier of Hussain, came to Habib's door. Habib is sitting to eat food. He is sitting at the 'Dastarkhwan' (dining spread). He wants to eat food. When the courier knocked. Habib asked, 'Who?' He said, 'Ana baridul Hussain' (I am the messenger of Hussain). The messenger of Hussain? Habib got up. He went and saw. He said, 'I have brought this letter from Hussain.' Habib took the letter. He kissed it. He touched it to his eyes. He placed it on his head. Then he kissed it again. After that, he opened it. After opening it, he saw it was written: 'Minal Hussain ibn-e-Fatima, ila al-rajul al-faqir Habib ibn Muzahir al-Asadi.' This is for that poor man whose name is Habib ibn Muzahir. O Habib! You know what our kinship is with the Messenger of Allah? What our relationship is? If you are not aware of our situation, then know that we are surrounded by the wicked. We are surrounded by oppressors. The oppressors have encircled us. Habib! If it is possible, come to our aid. It is written in the Maqatil that the weight of the letter was so great that Habib sat down right there. The weight of the letter was that much. Habib sat down right there. His wife asked, 'Habib, whose letter is it?' He said, 'It is the letter of the grandson of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.).' She asked, 'What is written? What is written?' He said, 'If it is possible, come to our aid.' So she asked, 'Habib, what do you think?' He said, 'You know that the situation in Kufa is so dire that it is impossible to leave from here now. It is impossible to go now. How can I go? How can I go to help my master? To help Hussain ibn Ali?' That was all she needed to hear. His wife said, 'Habib, if you cannot go, then you stay at home. I will go to help the son of Fatima.' I will go. Habib said, Habib said, 'The son of Fatima calls for me and I do not go? I only wanted to test your faith.' Habib took his horse. He called his slave and said, 'Take this horse and stand at such and such a place. I will come there. Look, I will come there. The son of Fatima has called for help. Just stand there.' Habib said this so that he could keep the secrets secret. The slave took the horse and went and stood at a place outside Kufa. He went and stood at a place. Habib, changing streets, changing alleys, reached there. Now, when he reached there, what scene did he see? He saw that the horse was crying. Tears were flowing from its eyes. And the slave was explaining, 'O unfaithful one, O unfaithful one, there is nothing to worry about. If my master Habib could not come, then I will take you. I will take you. To help Hussain. To help my master.' For his support. Habib just saw this scene. He became restless. He started saying, 'Master, today, today the time has come upon you that animals are shedding tears and the slave is ready to help.' Habib came just once. He said to the slave, 'Go, I have freed you in the path of Allah. Go, I have freed you.' And he sat on the horse, and then when he started to leave, the slave said, 'Habib, you have not fulfilled the right. You took service until you didn't need it. Now, when the time for the service of the son of Fatima has come, you are going alone? I will also go.' Habib took the slave with him. Now, when they arrived. As soon as they got close. Imam Hussain (a.s.) saw that dust was rising. He understood that Habib had arrived. He said, he said, 'My companions, go, my childhood friend Habib has come. Welcome him. Go, welcome him.' The companions moved forward to welcome him. Now, when the news reached the tent, Lady Zainab (s.a.) said, 'Fizza, ever since we left home, only bad news has been coming, that our enemies are increasing. The enemies are increasing. Who has come that such a wave of joy has spread?' Fizza went to the door of the tent. She brought the news. She is saying, 'Lady, the master's childhood friend, Habib ibn Mazahir, has come.' As soon as Zainab (s.a.) heard this, she said, 'Fizza, go and convey our greetings to Habib. Tell him, Habib, you have done a great deed. You have come to our aid at such a time. You have done a great deed.' Now, as soon as Fizza delivered this message, Habib sat on the soil of Karbala. He put dust on his head, that today such a time has come upon the princesses of Fatima and Ali that they are greeting us slaves. I will say, Habib, this is just the beginning of the tragedies. Oh, on the evening of Ashura, Hussain was saying to Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.), 'O Sayyid al-Sajjad, when you are released from captivity and go, convey my greetings to my Shias. And tell them, O Shias...' "Ma in sharibtum ma'an azmin fadhkuruni." O my followers, when you drink cold water, remember my thirst. And when you see someone helpless, remember the helplessness of Hussain. "Wa sayalamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin." O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the troubles of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant righteous and virtuous children to those who are childless. Grant complete and swift health to those who are ill. Decree the release of those who are in prisons this very night. Return those who are far from their homeland safe and sound. Protect the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. Protect the high scholars and the Maraje-e-Izam. Protect the holy shrines. Protect them. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Virtue of Mourning for Husayn
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that true devotion to the Prophet and his family is demonstrated through mourning for Imam Husayn and accepting the authority of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Reality of the Ahlulbayt's Grief
chapters.summary: The lecturer discusses the profound grief of the Imams over the tragedy of Karbala and explains that many historical calamities stemmed from a lack of understanding regarding the Imams' divine light.

chapters.title: Defining the True Believer
chapters.summary: Using a tradition from Imam Ali to Salman al-Farsi, the speaker defines a true believer as one who submits completely to the commands of the Ahlulbayt without doubt or hesitation.

chapters.title: Intellectualism vs. Submission
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against using limited human intellect to reject authentic traditions of the Ahlulbayt, criticizing those who dismiss established narrations based on personal opinion.

chapters.title: Defining Ghulu and the Status of the Imam
chapters.summary: The Imam clarifies that he is a servant of Allah and His Caliph, warning against the error of attributing divinity to the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Divine Nature of Caliphate and Language
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the title of Caliph is a divine appointment and emphasizes the importance of preserving the sacred language of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Virtues of the Ahlulbayt Beyond Human Comprehension
chapters.summary: The Imam sets the boundary of ghulu while encouraging the recognition of the vast, indescribable virtues and knowledge of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Limitations of Human Intellect
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights that the reality of the Ahlulbayt transcends human intellect, citing both the Imam's own words and the observations of scholars like Imam Shafi'i.

chapters.title: The Exalted Status of Imamate
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the profound, inaccessible nature of Imamate as described in narrations from Imam Rida (a.s.), emphasizing that human intellect cannot fully comprehend the station of an Imam.

chapters.title: The Impossibility of Human Selection for Imamate
chapters.summary: The lecture argues that since the reality of Imamate is beyond human reach, it is impossible for people to appoint an Imam through their own choice or opinion.

chapters.title: Glorification and the Names of Allah
chapters.summary: Explaining the Quranic command to glorify the name of the Lord, the speaker clarifies that the Imams are the 'names of Allah' and that acknowledging their status is not exaggeration (Ghuluw).

chapters.title: Wilayah as the Essence of Prayer
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the connection between prayer and Wilayah, citing narrations where the Imam explains that true prayer is inseparable from the acceptance of his Wilayah.

chapters.title: The Hardship of Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that Wilayah is the difficult burden mentioned in the Quran, which only the humble (Khashi'in) possessors of insight can accept.

chapters.title: The Rejection of Wilayah
chapters.summary: Despite universal belief in the Prophet, various sects historically rejected the Wilayah of Imam Ali, which was established from the very beginning of the Prophet's mission.

chapters.title: The Continuity of the Prophet's Message
chapters.summary: The Prophet consistently proclaimed the Wilayah of Ali alongside his Prophethood, culminating in the Hadith-e-Saqalain, which emphasizes the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Hawz-e-Kawthar and the Companions
chapters.summary: The speaker references a narration found in Sahih Bukhari regarding the Hawz-e-Kawthar, where the Prophet is told that some of his companions will be turned away for their actions after his passing.

chapters.title: Habib ibn Muzahir's Early Devotion
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the deep spiritual recognition and devotion Habib ibn Muzahir held for Imam Hussain from his childhood.

chapters.title: The Call to Karbala
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain sends a letter to Habib ibn Muzahir requesting his aid, leading to a poignant display of loyalty from Habib and his wife.

chapters.title: Arrival and Welcome at Karbala
chapters.summary: Habib arrives in Karbala to support the Imam, receiving a warm welcome from the companions and a message of gratitude from Lady Zainab.

chapters.title: Final Message and Supplication
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with Imam Hussain's message to his followers to remember his thirst and a collective prayer for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana.

title: Zuhoor Ka Waqt Muayyan Karne Waale Jhoothe Hain | ⛅IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the prohibition of predicting the specific time of Imam Mahdi's (a.t.f.s.) reappearance. Citing a narration from Imam Baqir (a.s.), the speaker highlights that those who claim to know the exact timing are considered liars. The talk uses the historical example of Prophet Musa's delayed return to explain the concept of Bada, or change in divine decree, regarding the timing of the reappearance.
content:
Fudayl ibn Yasar narrates from Imam Baqir (a.s.): 'Qala qultu lihazal amri waqtun'—meaning Fudayl asks Imam Baqir (a.s.) if there is a time for the reappearance. 'Faqala alayhissalam kazabal waqtun, kazabal waqtun, kazabal waqtun'—meaning the Imam's repetition that those who fix a time are liars, those who fix a time are liars, those who fix a time are liars, indicates the importance that whoever fixes a time for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time is a liar. Then the Imam (a.s.) gives an example in this hadith: when Hazrat Musa went with his delegation to his Lord, 'Wa'aduhu thalathina yawman'—Allah promised 30 days. Then when Allah added 10 days to these 30 days, and his people did what they did—meaning they turned back on their heels from the religion of Hazrat Musa and betrayed his successor, Janabe Harun. This example is given by the Imam (a.s.) here because the matter of reappearance is similar. The possibility of Bada (change in divine decree) exists in the reappearance, and if Allah wills, He will take this matter to its end, and if Allah wills, Allah can bring about a change in this matter, i.e., the reappearance.
Imam Baqir (a.s.) explicitly stated that those who fix a time for the reappearance are liars.
The repetition of the phrase 'kazabal waqtun' emphasizes the severity of this falsehood.
The reappearance is subject to the divine will and the concept of Bada.
The story of Prophet Musa and the extension of his 30-day promise serves as a theological parallel.
Human impatience and betrayal of leadership occurred when the expected time for Musa's return was extended.
Divine decrees regarding the reappearance can change based on Allah's wisdom and will.

The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) identified his light as the first creation.

title: Majlis 4 | Ghussa (Anger) | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 2023 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual and practical implications of anger, emphasizing its destructive nature and the necessity of self-control in light of Quranic and Prophetic teachings. The speaker highlights how anger acts as a tool for Satan to disrupt families and personal growth, urging believers to practice patience and forgiveness. The discourse concludes with a poignant reflection on the tragedy of Ali Asghar (a.s.) at Karbala, illustrating the ultimate sacrifice for the sake of Allah and the preservation of Islam.
content:
My Hussain, you were raised by Fatima... what has happened to your appearance... my oppressed one, my thirsty one, my poor one. My poor one, my destitute one, my thirsty one, my martyr of desires... My Hussain, have you come? I have come from Paradise to the battlefield, my son... My Hussain, the city of Hussain, Medina, is desolate... the city of Sham, Medina, is desolate... my dear one, my Hussain. Hussain, Hussain, my Hussain, Hussain. Alhamdulillah, peace and blessings. Allahu Akbar. Allahu Akbar. As the days pass, a part of your existence diminishes. With every passing day, a part is lost, and this is how a human being is destined to leave this world at the time Allah has decreed. It may be sooner or later; it is up to Allah. Sometimes He advances the destiny, sometimes He delays it, but there is no escaping death for anyone. There is no escape from death. In Persian, there is a saying about things that are destructive. It is something that destroys. Everyone has to go; there is no one who stays. Therefore, value every day, every minute, and every moment, and use it to the maximum. And what should a person do in it? As you may have seen, the more light reflects from an angle, the more its value increases. Exactly like that is a person's personality; one should keep developing their personality. Use the idiom: if a person keeps developing themselves, a Muslim should keep sharpening their skills. Keep sharpening your skills. Great people are those whose education is continuous; they keep upgrading themselves. What I did 30 years ago... What I did 30 years ago, they won't just talk about that; rather, those people, as you know, are the same today. If we want not to become obsolete regarding the Hereafter, then it is necessary for us to keep developing ourselves, one of the most important characteristics of which is that a person should control themselves—self-control. Now, this self-control... If it is in the path of Allah, then it is a positive thing, and if it is not in the path of Allah, it is a dangerous and evil thing for one's own self, which destroys a person's personality. Similarly, there are desires that exist to satisfy one's own self. Remember, our discussion from the very first day has been that the Prophet... The discussion from the first day has been that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated that he left behind two things: the Book of Allah and the Hadith. Beyond these, nothing else matters. In every matter, no matter how great a person may be, if their personality is not in accordance with the Quran and Hadith, then it is nothing. And that is why we see that great idols are toppled, and great personalities who were big names in their society—like the one who used to sit on a throne—you know, how should I give an example? You must have seen those who run shops, or people of other religions, they have a big throne, sitting on it with blankets and sheets spread out, and two or four people fanning them from one side and two or four from the other. Now... Two or four people fanning them from the other side. Now, look, whatever the matter is, it must be in the light of the Quran and Hadith, and insha'Allah, we will understand that. Now, understand one more thing; it is very important. We look at it from two aspects. One aspect is what we usually call metaphysical, which a person cannot understand unless the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) explain it. Well, all things are like that, but there is something that is beyond human access, which people cannot understand unless it is revealed from the unseen. And the other thing they explain is what a person understands when the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) explain it, and they realize, 'Yes, this is true,' and everyone understands that this is correct. For that, revelation is needed, and this... For that, revelation is needed, and there are things that everyone can understand. Self-control, controlling one's anger—this is a very important thing, which the Quran and Hadith have mentioned quite a bit. The first thing is that this is the work of Satan. Satan, this is the spark of Satan. This anger that Satan ignites in a person's heart, it is the work of Satan. He has set everything up in humans. We say, 'I will never tell a lie, I will never tell a lie,' but if two people are to be made to fight, then as soon as... They were saying this about you. And as soon as we heard it, Satan did his work. Satan has access to the human existence; it is not that he doesn't. Satan is... that is what he said, right? When Allah said, 'Get out of My presence,' Satan asked for many things. He asked for respite until the Day of Judgment. Allah did not give him until the Day of Judgment, but until the appointed time. Why? Because at the appointed time, his work will be finished, just as the Imam (a.t.f.s.) will have the work of Satan finished. Allah asked, 'What else do you want?' He said, 'If a human is born, there should be two Satans in his senses.' Satan asked this of Allah. Every human who is born should have two in his senses, and Satan has a guarantee for the human's death. There are many verses about Satan... He has done it, and now our friend in Iran has written a book on Satan, only based on Quran and Hadith, which is 2,500 pages long. That is how much importance is given to Satan in the Quran and Hadith. And Allah has said in the Quran, 'Recognize him, he is your open enemy,' and Allah says to seek refuge from Satan. This is the reason, but often the negligence is such that when you are so pious and God-fearing, Satan's trap is upon you, and it is Satan who is speaking. So Satan gave it, everything happened, and he is negligent, and the human... And the human falls into his trap, and his eyes turn red, and when he gets very angry, he starts biting, and Satan enters him completely and dominates him. That is why when you are in this state, immediately do whatever you can—if you are sitting, lie down, drink water, whatever you can do, do it immediately so that you stay away from the anger of Satan. Allah has repeatedly pointed towards this in the Quran, that a person should stay away from this, and therefore, in every situation... In every situation, whoever has a stronger faith spends more in the path of Allah. When you hear it from our tongue, you are not affected by the emotions as much because the tongue is a sinner. So now listen from the tongue of the Master of the Universe (a.s.). What does he say? He says that one who has certainty of the return (in the afterlife) invests more. If there is certainty of the return, then one will invest more. Think about it, for 5,000 rupees of this world, they are deprived of the hereafter. Come a little forward, come a little forward, and recite Salawat on Muhammad and his family. For 5,000 rupees of this world... what is the worth of 5,000 rupees? Allah has promised, He has promised. If there is one rupee, if there is certainty, then it is fine. Therefore, if someone has certainty, the Master (a.s.) says he will be generous in giving, in investing. And the Hadith is also continuing, keep that in mind too. Whoever did bad to us, we forgave them. Whoever did bad to us, we forgave them. Consider that we have forgiven them; we have no problem. I am not saying this from my own side. If someone has done bad to you, do not take revenge. The traditions say you should do good to them. The more good you do to them, the more severe Allah's retribution will be against the one who did evil to you. O Allah, I have left my affairs to Allah; let Allah handle it, let Him understand. And anyway, what revenge can a human take? If someone slaps us, what can we do? We can slap them back twice or four times. What more can we do? But when Allah takes retribution from someone, He takes it in such a way that the person cannot even hide their face and cry, 'Where should I go? What should I do?' And then you will do everything; these are all matters of experience. Allah loves, and Allah says in the Quran, in Surah Al-Qasas, 'Just as Allah has been good to you, so you be good to others.' Do good to others just as Allah has done good to you. Now, how can I explain the blessings of Allah? We are currently breathing comfortably, talking to each other, and sitting at ease. Go and ask someone who is unable to breathe; ask them, and they will tell you what a great blessing and mercy it is. If you try to count the blessings of Allah, you will not be able to count them, let alone be grateful for them. Counting is out of the question; you won't even be able to enumerate them. This is a very important matter because anger is something that ruins domestic relationships. Nowadays, look at how easily people get divorced over trivial matters—this one got divorced, that one got divorced—there is no tolerance left at all. There is no tolerance left; no one even mentions patience for the sake of Allah. Something happens, and immediately they call their parents, saying, 'Look, they said this to me.' Just leave it, come back home. An entire family gets destroyed. Asiya (a.s.) was one of the four women of Paradise, and yet she spent her entire life with Pharaoh. Is there any comparison? There is no comparison. But Allah considers the breaking of a family to be among the worst things. I don't know what has happened to parents; the parents of girls are often more to blame because they should counsel them. I am ending this point here—it is just anger. Even if something happens, the situation at home might be bad, but one should still exercise patience. And that day will be very severe; do not take it lightly. Just as this world is fleeting, the Day of Judgment is coming; just understand this much. The Master of the Universe (a.s.) says—a strange hadith, may our lives be sacrificed for the dust of the hooves of the horses of the Commander of the Faithful's (a.s.) servants—the Master says that the moment a child steps into this world, their back is towards the world and their face is towards the Hereafter. They are moving forward; now it depends on their intellect whether they understand this or not. How foolish is the one who uses abusive language, resulting in no one wanting to stay near them. Whereas, in other places, people are treated with love and affection, and people do not want to leave them. Who would want to listen to their abuse? Who would want to listen to their abuse? And here, it is said that in all your relationships, wherever you have friendships or work, if a person controls this—it is not easy, it is very difficult—because the closer a person gets to Allah, the more intense the attack of Satan becomes. Remember this. And Insha'Allah, in that hadith, the lowest level is that of the scholar. After the scholar, there is the one who acts upon the knowledge. Then, after acting, the Imam (a.s.) says that everyone will be destroyed except those who are sincere, about whom I spoke to you the day before yesterday regarding sincerity. The day before yesterday, we spoke about sincerity; only those who are sincere will be saved, and everyone else will be destroyed. And then the Imam (a.s.) says that those who are sincere are in great danger. What is the danger? Satan will not leave them alone. And he will come in the guise of a friend; remember this. An angel constantly gives a believer messages from Allah—pray, fast, do this, do that, do good deeds—and on the other side, Satan constantly keeps whispering to them. And on the other side, the Shaitan continuously keeps prompting him, saying, 'You must do this.' And then the human says, 'Yes, friend, this is also correct; if we don't do it, someone else will, so it is better that we do it ourselves.' He does not think about what the outcome will be or what the result is. This is why Allah (SWT) commands that one should not abandon a human being. That is why, if you know, in our language, we say that the one with whom a human can converse, with whom a human can talk, is called 'hawaar'—it comes from 'hawaar', meaning to communicate. The most difficult thing is to control it. As soon as it is said, a veil falls over our eyes. Without thinking or understanding, we immediately pick up the phone and give them a piece of our mind. So, never do this; never speak while in a state of anger. As soon as you feel it, immediately become silent, sit down, and calmly have some water. It starts with madness and ends with regret. And if he is not regretting, then his madness is proven. The 'Badu'—those people who live in the desert—for example, if I just tell you, if someone lives in a jungle, someone who has no manners, no ethics, no etiquette, nothing—they are called 'Badu' in Arabic, meaning desert dwellers. One of them came to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I live in the desert.' I live in the desert, and it is not possible for me to come to you repeatedly. Such people used to speak very rudely; they had no manners. Do you know, children, that the Quran mentions them repeatedly? Look at the language of the Quran. He said, 'I live very far away, and it is not possible for me to come to you repeatedly.' Now he is saying, 'Teach me one thing, one thing that will make my life in this world and the hereafter. Just tell me one thing.' It is written in the Hadith that he asked three times, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave the same answer all three times: 'Do not get angry, do not get angry, do not get angry.' The Bedouin picked up his belongings and left, saying, 'If the Messenger of Allah has said one thing, it means that my salvation lies in this.' And he left, and after that, he did not come again. But look, the beginning, sometimes it is not under a human's control when... Sometimes it is not under a human's control when anger comes, but once it has arrived, it is then under the human's control whether to control it or to react. A person who is very cold-natured is also a hypocrite; understand this too. This is a very dangerous thing. A person who is very cold-natured—I have seen many such people in life. Bill Gates writes that he used to get very angry. So, whenever there was an issue where we were discussing something controversial or something we did not agree on, I would never discuss it over the phone. I would call them; if they were in the office, I would either go to them or call them to me, and we would sit face-to-face and talk to solve the matter. But we would not do it over the phone. It is a dangerous thing because we do not know in what state the person on the other side is speaking, what their condition is, and what they are trying to say; this is also a factor. Sometimes, what a person intends to say and what actually comes out of their mouth are different; this is a matter that needs to be controlled. As mentioned, if one is standing, they should sit; if sitting, they should lie down. Drinking water is something that extinguishes anger. If we get angry very quickly, we should always remain in a state of wudu (ablution), as being in wudu keeps one protected. However, if this anger is for the sake of Allah, then it is a very good thing; it should be for the sake of Allah. Every piece of information constricts the heart, as if the heart is being pulled upward. But in the path of Islam, one should expand their heart. What does it mean to expand the heart in the name of Islam? It means that if parents scold you, you shouldn't get angry; if there is a disagreement with siblings, you should be patient; if a friend says something, you shouldn't get angry; if a brother says something, you shouldn't get angry, but rather forgive and leave it to Allah. However, the Quran says that one should never expand their heart in a way that ignores the enmity against Allah. That is, if you see that Allah is being disobeyed, sitting silently is not right. It is not correct to remain silent, saying, 'It's okay, our child is committing a sin, he is still young, it's fine,' especially in these times. And furthermore, if the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are being insulted, one should not remain silent even for a moment. People say, 'How much can we watch? This is not our job.' Then whose job is it? If it is not your job, then whose is it? You are choosing your words very carefully, addressing the Imam as if he were an ordinary man. But there is a sentence in the Hadith—and many of my brothers are present here, and it is present in 'Abaqat al-Anwar'—that a person began to tremble with rage just hearing that someone was speaking to his Imam in such a manner. [Praise] What personality! A person should have dignity, and there should be anger in them; softness does not work everywhere. There is an entire chapter on this—'Wajib al-Wujud'—that one should show anger for the sake of Allah just as one would for oneself. In that era, 53 responses were written to that chapter. What did he write in the preface of that book? The time is up, but in the preface, he wrote: 'I am writing this book because today there is no house left in India where people are not becoming Shia.' This was 200 years ago, 150 years ago. It was 200 years ago, 150 years ago, that there was no house left, so I am writing this book. In the seventh chapter, he wrote that this was revealed in honor of Ali (a.s.). It wasn't just a response to the seventh chapter, but to the entire 'Tohfa' (Tuhfa Ithna Ashariyyah). In those old days, such large books were printed—150 years ago—and they were translated into Arabic. In fact, it wasn't even an exact translation, just a summary. He had only started writing; he had planned 16 volumes, but he passed away. 200 years ago, if a book was in someone's library and it contained a reference, he went there under the pretext of Hajj. After arriving, he went to that man's house and took a job, saying, 'I have come from India and my money has run out; if you keep me as a servant, I will do the work.' The man said, 'You look alright.' He replied, 'Yes, I am a traveler.' After that, he searched for the book. After finding it, he asked the man, 'Brother, I need this book.' The man said, 'No, this book is not for anyone.' It is the story of a wealthy man, not a scholar. Somehow, he copied the entire book. When it was done, he thanked him profusely and left. The purpose was fulfilled, and he left. Now, let's talk about the journey; the time is running short, so let's move on. In the old days, there were ships... ...there were ships that traveled from Jeddah to Mumbai, and then from Mumbai to Lucknow. It was a very long journey. While he was on the ship, he was arranging the pages of the book because, as written in his biography, he had to arrange the pages as everything was written very quickly and he had to escape with it. Just as he was arranging them, a storm came. The storm caused some pages to fly away into the water. He placed something heavy on the book and jumped into the water to retrieve those two pages. Somehow, he retrieved them, rearranged the book, and later referenced it in 'Abaqat al-Anwar'. These are the scholars. No one in India responded except for one. When this passion arises, then the religion... ...then the religion is saved. Don't complain then. And that is why, to save the religion, he sacrificed his entire household and left nothing behind. People here even sacrificed their six-month-old child. How much love there is! Just as Hussain (a.s.) called out, 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna Ahlulbayt?' (Is there anyone to help the Ahlulbayt?) [Music] [Music] [Praise] [Music] [Praise] I don't know what the father said and what the son understood, but it is written in history that he came into Hussain's lap. When Hussain took Ali Asghar (a.s.) and started walking, Rubab (s.a.) was standing at the door. 'Why are you standing here? There is work to do.' 'I am watching. Everyone who has gone since morning has returned correctly, so I thought I would see my little child one last time.' Hussain consoled her, 'Rubab, everyone who went until now was killed because they went to fight. Six-month-old babies don't fight. I am taking him so that someone might have mercy and give him water.' Hussain came and stood on a high place and began to say, [Praise] 'Is there no Muslim among you? Islam says to give water to the thirsty. My child has been hungry and thirsty for three days.' No one answered. When no one answered, Hussain said the second sentence, 'People, is there no one among you...' No one answered. Then Hussain said the third, 'O people, do you not see how he is gasping?' 'Do you not see how he is gasping, opening and closing his mouth due to thirst? How his life is slipping away?' It was the state of a fish when taken out of water; when a fish starts dying, it opens and closes its mouth. That was Asghar's state, sometimes opening his mouth, sometimes closing it. Once, he turned his face... the effect of the arrow was such that... [Praise] The arrow used for hunting large animals was used. He took that arrow and aimed it at Asghar's throat. The arrow struck. The child was in Hussain's lap. Hussain raised the blood in his palms and threw it toward the sky. The sky refused to accept it, so it fell to the earth. Hussain took the child and thought about where to take him, and... He took the child and thought of taking him to Zainab, and he had barely walked a short distance when he thought, 'Will Rubab be able to bear this?' So he came back. And as many times as he went and came back, he said, 'There is no way, there is no way.' And in the midst of this, he surrendered to the will of Allah. Seven times Imam Hussain (a.s.) performed this act. When he finally walked towards the tents, Imam Hussain (a.s.) understood that the child had passed away, so why keep the mother deprived of a final glimpse? He came and called out, 'O Rubab! O Rubab!' It is written in history that Rubab came from one side and Sakina from the other, but the girl ran and arrived first. She reached her father, 'Father, are you feeding my brother water? Is my brother thirsty?' Imam Hussain (a.s.) remained silent. And when Rubab arrived, as she turned the veil, what did she see? The six-month-old child, [music] in the state of being slaughtered [praise]. [praise] These children are also martyred [music]. Leave the recitation of one Surah Fatiha and three times [Salawat]. I am Ghulam Ali Ibn Abdul Aziz Lakhani. I have recited this for the departed souls of the Lakhani family, Rupani family, Himani family, and Dada family.

title: Glimpses | EP03 | Haqq Sirf Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ke Saath Hai | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 2026
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the ultimate standard of truth, reflecting Allah's pleasure in all matters. The speaker explains that truth is not determined by popular opinion or historical narratives, but resides exclusively with the Imams. In the current era of occultation, this truth is centered entirely upon Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
content:
When we are blessed with the Ziyarat of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and get the opportunity to go to Samarra, we should recite this Ziyarat in the Sardab. It is such an authentic Ziyarat that our scholars have mentioned it in their famous books of supplications. It is stated in this Ziyarat that 'the truth is that with which you are pleased,' meaning whatever the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are pleased with is the truth. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the mirror of Allah's pleasure. This means the scale of truth cannot be our own thinking, majority opinion, or historical propaganda; rather, the scale of truth is that 'the truth is with you, from you, and towards you it returns.' You are the people of truth, you are the mine of truth. 'Mine' refers to the source. In this era of occultation, at every moment, every day, every week, every month, every year, every century, and every age, the truth is only and only with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and in this current era of occultation, it is with Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). It is only with him. Just remember [music] look [music]. Look [music] the existence of the Imam.

title: Ziyaarat Ka Ehraam Kya Hai? | زیارت کا احرام کیا ہے؟  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture outlines the spiritual and behavioral etiquette required for a pilgrim, based on the teachings of Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) to Muhammad bin Muslim. It emphasizes the importance of kindness, constant remembrance of Allah, purity, and ethical conduct during the journey of Ziyarat, Hajj, and Umrah. The speaker highlights that true spiritual success is achieved by embodying these virtues and following the guidance of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
Tomorrow morning at this time... Assalamu Alaikum. Muhammad bin Muslim (R.A.) asked Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) a question. Muhammad bin Muslim asked, 'What are the things that I should do?' [Music] The Imam replied, 'The things you should do in this matter are: speak to your companions with kindness and only speak good words. Remember Allah (dhikr) frequently. Take care of the purity of your clothes. When you enter the Haram, perform ghusl before entering. Behave with ease and pray more than the obligatory prayers.' Behave with ease, pray more than the obligatory prayers, and send abundant blessings (salawat) upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Maintain your dignity. Do not reach out for things that are not yours. Keep your gaze lowered. Consider fulfilling the needs of your brothers as your duty. When you see someone broken-hearted, treat them well. Use taqiyya (precaution/prudence), as it is among the foundations of your religion. Abstain from things that have been forbidden, and protect yourself from arguing and swearing false oaths, especially those disputes that lead a person to swear false oaths. When you take care of these matters, your Hajj and Umrah will be complete. By staying away from your sins and because of the suspicion you have, which makes you inclined towards this virtue, you will attain the mercy and pleasure of Allah (SWT). By spending on this journey, you have attached yourself to Allah. It is the favor of Allah (SWT) that He has guided us to such matters of goodness, which not only guide us towards success in the hereafter but also show us the path to reach the heights of 'hasanah' (goodness) in this world and the next. They show us the path to reach the heights, but unfortunately, in this world, we did not value such divine guides; rather, we oppressed them and martyred them. Now, it is our responsibility to try to take our character to the destination in the light of the teachings of the Imams (a.s.) so that it becomes completely clear to the people of the world. [Music] O Lord, grant us all the ability to act upon the guidance of the Imams. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

It examines the historical corruption that led to the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his family, while providing practical guidance on human conduct and the qualities of the servants of the Most Gracious. title: Ali (a.s.) Nafs e Rasool (s.a.w.a.) | Verse of Mubaahala | آیت مباہلہ
excerpt: This lecture explores the significance of the Verse of Mubahala (Surah Al-Imran, 3:61) as a theological proof for the Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker explains the historical context of the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) debate with the Christians of Najran and highlights how the term 'Anfusana' (our selves) identifies Imam Ali as the soul and equal of the Prophet. By citing both Shia and Sunni sources, including Sahih Muslim, the lecture emphasizes that Imam Ali's unique status as the Prophet's 'Nafs' confirms his rightful leadership after the Prophet.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat (proof), son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and cause him to enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. On behalf of the 'The Stung Group' team, we present to all you believers, regarding the Holy Quran and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), specifically those verses which Allah (s.w.t.) has revealed in the Quran in honor of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Today, the verse we are to discuss is the Verse of Mubahala (Imprecation), in which the Lord of Majesty says: 'Faman hajjaka...' This is the 61st verse of Surah Al-Imran, in which the Lord of Majesty says: 'Then if anyone disputes with you in this matter after the knowledge has come to you, say: Come! Let us call our sons and your sons...' '...and our women and your women, and our selves and your selves, then let us pray earnestly (Mubahala) and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars.' This is the verse that the Lord of the Worlds revealed. Now, in its background, I have to present a few points. This verse mentions the Mubahala with the Christians of Najran. The scholars of Najran came to Medina and debated with the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) regarding the reality of Prophet Isa (a.s.). These people considered Prophet Isa (a.s.) to be 'Ibnullah' (the son of God), whereas the Messenger of God, Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), presented arguments before them based on the Quran and stated clearly that Prophet Isa (a.s.) is not the son of God, but rather a servant of Allah and a Prophet of Allah. When the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) presented all these proofs to the Christians and they were still not satisfied, Allah (s.w.t.) commanded His Messenger to tell them that now there would be a Mubahala, and the curse of Allah would be upon the liar. Now, the word 'hajjaka' here means that these people... ...the word 'hajjaka' here means that these people only argued, and in exchange for that argument, Allah (s.w.t.) invites them to a Mubahala and sends a message through His Messenger that if you are truthful in your claim, then come to the field of Mubahala, and it will be seen who is truthful and who is a liar. Now, respected viewers, on one hand, we find that these people only argued and became deserving of the curse. If they had performed the Mubahala, the curse of Allah would certainly have been upon them. We are amazed at the intellects of those who consider the individuals who came to the battlefield to fight against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to be very good people. Whereas, if you look at the sentences of Ziyarat Jame'ah Kabirah, Imam Naqi (a.s.) says: 'Man jahadakum kafirun' (Whoever denies you is a disbeliever), 'Wa man harabakum mushrikun' (And whoever fights you, O Mawla, is a polytheist). Respected viewers, now let us move to the second aspect, in which we want to present an argument for the Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) through this verse. This verse points clearly to the virtues of Imam Ali (a.s.), his status, and his central leadership in Islam. If you look at the word 'Anfusana', what is it? It is the 'Nafs' (self) of the Messenger. If anyone is to take the place of the Messenger after him, he must be the 'Nafs' of the Messenger. ...he must be the 'Nafs' of the Messenger. This is a rational argument. I mean, it is very clear; if even a child were asked who should take the place of the Messenger after him, he would say it must be the 'Nafs' of the Messenger, someone like the Messenger. So, this is a very strong argument we have that after the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.), the one who will take his place is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). And look at the word here, the plural form 'Anfusana' is used. If other gentlemen were present in Medina who were truly the 'Nafs' of the Messenger or possessed virtues at the level of the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.), then surely the Messenger would have brought them. But the fact that the Messenger of God brought only the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) there clearly indicates that if there was any 'Nafs' of the Messenger in that era, it was only and only the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Now, respected viewers, the third point I have to present here is that if we study Shia beliefs or Shia hadith regarding this verse, or if I present Shia hadith to you, what do we find? Who is called the 'Nafs' of the Messenger? In 'Amali' by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), there is a hadith on page 95, where the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) himself says... ...the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) says: 'O Ali, whoever kills you has killed me, and whoever shows enmity towards you, O Ali, has shown enmity towards me, and whoever insults you, O Ali, has used those words against me.' Because—and here is the important sentence—'Li-annaka minni ka-nafsi' (Because you are from me, like my own soul, my own self). This is the same thing being declared in 'Anfusana wa Anfusakum'; the hadith is stating the same thing: 'O Ali, you are my soul, you are my life.' The Messenger of God does not stop there. The Messenger of God further states in this hadith: 'Your spirit is my spirit, and your clay is my clay.' And then the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) says: 'O Ali, indeed Allah (s.w.t.) created me and you, chose me and you, selected me for Prophethood, and selected you for Imamate. So whoever denies your Imamate, O Ali, has denied my Prophethood.' ...whoever denies your Imamate has denied my Prophethood. Respected viewers, look at how the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) is conveying the virtues of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) to the Muslim Ummah, and how he is stating that Ali is my soul, Ali is my life, Ali is my spirit, Ali's spirit is my spirit, Ali's clay is my clay. So this was our belief, and there is not just one, but numerous narrations found in our hadith books where you will find 'Anfusana wa Anfusakum' referring to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Now, let me present a hadith from the books of the Ahlus-Sunnah regarding this same Verse of Mubahala, which they also include, and this is a very authentic book, 'Sahih Muslim'. It is a very reliable book and a highly trusted book among the Ahlus-Sunnah. In it, there is a narration that Amir, the son of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, narrates that when the Governor of Sham appointed Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas as governor, the Governor of Sham said to Sa'd, 'Why do you refrain from abusing Abu Turab (the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.))?' To which Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas replies, 'I do not abuse Imam Ali (a.s.) because I always remember those three things of the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) which he stated in honor of Imam Ali (a.s.)...' ...which he stated in honor of Imam Ali (a.s.). And the third thing he mentions is this verse: 'Qul ta'alaw nad'u abna'ana wa abna'akum wa nisa'ana wa nisa'akum wa anfusana wa anfusakum thumma nabtahil fanaj'al la'natallahi 'alal kadhibin.' He states that the individuals the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) took to the field of Mubahala were: in place of women, he took Hazrat Zahra (s.a.); in place of children or sons, the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) took Imam Hassan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.); and in place of 'Nafs' (self), he took only and only the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And then he said, 'O Allah, these are my Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' Respected viewers, you saw that the Verse of Mubahala we mentioned to you, and on which the entire Muslim Ummah agrees, that the 'Nafs' of the Messenger mentioned in this verse refers only and only to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). O Lord of the Worlds, O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
