title: Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer Ka Pasmanzar | Me'raaj-e-Ma'refat
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and spiritual background of Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir, a significant supplication often recited during the month of Ramadan and the Nights of Qadr. The speaker details a tradition narrated by Imam Ali (a.s.) to Imam Hussain (a.s.), explaining how the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) received this prayer from Angel Jibra'il during the Battle of Uhud. The supplication was revealed as a divine gift to the Prophet and his Ummah, serving as a spiritual shield more effective than physical armor.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat, son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and cause him to enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Respected viewers, the blessed month of Ramadan is such a magnificent month, a month dedicated to the recitation of the Holy Quran, worship, and supplications. The specialty of this month can be gauged from its importance, that in this blessed month, there is a specific supplication for every day. Supplication is the name of a unique relationship with the Lord, in which when a servant appears in the court of his Lord, and especially the supplications that have been narrated in this month... ...and especially the supplications that have been narrated in this month, with the help of those supplications, when he appears in the court of the Lord of the Worlds, Allah also turns towards him. Among the great supplications that have been narrated in this blessed month and are recited, one is Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir. In our Shia society, we see that often, especially on the Nights of Qadr, this supplication is definitely recited in our mosques and Imambargahs, and it should be; it is necessary. But let us try to understand, what is the background of this great supplication, Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir? When was it revealed? In what state was it revealed? Upon whom was it revealed? Let us try to understand what the background of this Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir is, and along with that, we will also see, Insha'Allah, what the great reward for reading and reciting it is, because it is an extraordinary supplication. Our high-ranking scholars have copied and recorded it in their books, such as Sayyid ibn Tawus in 'Muhaj al-Da'awat' and Muhaddith Nuri in 'Mustadrak al-Wasa'il'. In the 'Da'awat', Muhaddith Nuri in 'Mustadrak al-Wasa'il', Allama Majlisi (r.a.) in 'Bihar al-Anwar', and Sheikh Abbas Qummi in 'Mafatih al-Jinan', regarding its background, the tradition narrated by Sayyid ibn Tawus in 'Muhaj al-Da'awat' is a very long tradition. Insha'Allah, we will try to present that tradition to you gradually so that we become well-acquainted with its background. He writes, dropping the chain of narration, and after that, he writes from Mawlana Musa Jafari (a.s.), meaning from Hazrat Imam Kazim (a.s.), and then he says, he writes that from Ja'far Sadiq (a.s.), or he narrated from his father Imam Sadiq (a.s.), he narrated from his father Imam Baqir (a.s.), he narrated from his grandfather, or first from his father Imam Zain al-Abidin (a.s.), then he narrated from Imam Hussain (a.s.), and then he says that Imam Hussain (a.s.) says that my father, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), said to me one day regarding this supplication: 'O my son, shall I tell you one of the secrets of Allah, which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) taught me?' Shall I tell you the secret of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? The secret about which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) told me, he told me this secret, it is such a secret of his that he did not tell anyone else, only the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) knows, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) knows, and now Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is entrusting this secret to his son, Imam Hussain (a.s.). Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'May my father be sacrificed for you, tell me what it is.' Now the Mawla (a.s.) says, 'O my son, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was in the Battle of Uhud, and that day was a day that was passing very slowly, very slowly, it was very hot, very intense heat that day, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was wearing a 'jawshan'—by 'jawshan' is meant a coat of mail, an iron coat of mail, that is called 'jawshan'.' The 'jawshan' itself, the coat of mail that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was wearing, was so heavy in itself, it was iron, and it was so heavy that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself was feeling pain from it, feeling the pain. Because of the intensity of that day, the intensity of that heat, and the intensity of that iron coat of mail, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was feeling some pain. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I looked towards the sky, I prayed to Allah,' and then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Then what did I see? I saw that the doors of the sky opened.' The Prophet prayed to Allah, the doors of the sky opened, and the Prophet says that after that, Jibra'il (a.s.) came to me with a light, in some places it is written a light, a collar of light, in some places it is written like a thread of light, Jibra'il (a.s.) descended and arrived in the service of the Prophet and says... Arrived in the service of the Prophet and says, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' I replied to the greeting, 'O my brother Jibra'il,' and then Jibra'il (a.s.) says, 'Ali al-A'la (a.s.), the Allah who is the greatest Ali, has sent you greetings and offered congratulations in your service, and Allah (t.b.t.) says, it is the command of Allah that this 'jawshan', this coat of mail you are wearing, this heavy iron coat of mail, you take it off, you remove it, and this supplication, you recite it.' Which supplication? This 'Jawshan al-Kabir', you recite it. 'If you recite this, if you fully act upon this supplication, then what will happen? It will act as that coat of mail for you, you will not need that coat of mail which is on your body at this time.' Meaning, if you are wearing that coat of mail for your protection, you will not need it, you can protect yourself through this 'Jawshan al-Kabir'. You will not need it, you can protect yourself through this 'Jawshan al-Kabir.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'My brother Jibra'il, is this supplication specific only for me, or is it for me and my Ummah?' Look at how much the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) cares for his Ummah. When teaching a supplication, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is so concerned for his Ummah that if there is any such supplication through which my Ummah can face difficulties, then would the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) leave the world without leaving his Ummah with an Imam and a Caliph? At that time, would the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not be concerned for his Ummah? This is also a point to ponder. You decide for yourself. Then after that, Jibra'il (a.s.) says, 'O Messenger of Allah, this is a gift from Allah (t.b.t.) for you and for your Ummah.' This supplication is not just for you, but for your Ummah. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'O my brother Jibra'il, what is the reward for reciting this supplication?' In the next video, Insha'Allah, we will see the greatness of reciting this supplication. Whoever recites it, Allah will turn towards him, and whatever a person prays for in the court of Allah, Allah will answer his prayer. Allah will turn towards him, and whatever a person prays for in the court of Allah, Allah will answer his prayer. Whatever reward the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gives to the one who recites this supplication, what will He do? Allah says, 'I will give him a kingdom, a government, and for that servant, Allah creates 70,000 angels.' These angels do the tasbih of Allah, they do His sanctification, and all that reward goes to this servant.
Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir is a highly significant supplication often recited during the Nights of Qadr.
The supplication was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) by Angel Jibra'il during the Battle of Uhud.
It was revealed as a spiritual alternative to the heavy physical armor the Prophet was wearing.
The Prophet specifically ensured that this supplication was a gift for his entire Ummah, not just himself.
The supplication is recorded in authoritative Shia texts like 'Muhaj al-Da'awat' and 'Mafatih al-Jinan'.
Reciting the Dua brings divine attention and the support of 70,000 angels who perform tasbih for the reciter.

title: Masaaeb-e-Zahra (s.a) Maula Ali (a.s) Ki Zubaani | Shahaadat-e-Fatima Zahra (sa) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound grief and suffering of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.) following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It highlights the immense emotional and physical trials she endured, including the usurpation of her rights and the injustices committed against her. The discourse focuses on the perspective of Imam Ali (a.s.), detailing his secret burial of his wife and his eternal sorrow, which serves as a testament to the tragedy that befell the Ahl al-Bayt.
content:
Ajjal Allahu farajak ya Baqiyatullah, Ajjal Allahu farajak ya Baqiyatullah. Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'Whoever is not familiar with our sorrows'—meaning, even knowing, he does not believe in those sorrows, does not acknowledge them, does not weep and lament over them, those oppressions that were broken upon us, and the rights that were snatched from us, the oppressions that were committed against us, he is not familiar with them, does not know them, does not testify to them, does not weep and lament over them—'he is a partner in the oppression.' Meaning, it is the responsibility of every lover of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) to be familiar with these sorrows that were broken upon the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and to weep and lament over them, and not only that he should weep and lament over them... Not only that he should weep and lament over them, but he should tell people that these oppressions were committed against the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). As you know, after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Prophet's shroud had not even become dirty yet when the Ummah broke those mountains of oppression upon the Prophet's only daughter, the Princess of the Two Worlds, which are beyond description. If I were to mention just a few sentences of these sorrows in your service, the heart would truly burst. And if it were not for the appointed time (ajal) that Allah has fixed for everyone's death, if that were not there, then after reading these sentences, after reading these phrases, it would not be possible for a human to remain alive. I will read a few traditions in your service that have been narrated in the books of hadith. Allama has narrated these sentences in 'Anwar'. You can see, these sentences are present. The famous and well-known sentences, you already know, like the Princess reading the sorrows, 'The sorrows that were broken upon me, if these sorrows, if these calamities, if these torments were to fall upon the days, they would turn into nights.' Now look at the sentence of the tradition here: in the tradition, it is found from the Prophet... Meaning, after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Princess (s.a.) would constantly keep her head wrapped. Just as people often wrap their heads when they have a headache, the Princess (s.a.) was in such a state; her body had become extremely weak and frail. She had become completely weak, her strength was gone, and she had no strength left to stand. And the Princess (s.a.) would constantly weep. She would weep incessantly. You know, all the words used here—'baqiya'—meaning her eyes would constantly weep. It was not said that she wept at a specific time; if it had been said so, it would have been bound by time. But since the verb used here implies continuity, it means this was the Princess's (s.a.) constant state—that she would keep weeping. Her heart was burning, and her chest was burning from the tragedies; her chest was scorched, her heart was scorched by the tragedies. It was not just the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), but after the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) martyrdom, how the oppressors set fire to the Princess's (s.a.) house, set fire to the door, put a rope around the neck of the Master of the Universe (a.s.), and dragged him to the mosque, and then the way the Princess (s.a.) was insulted in the mosque. The way the Princess (s.a.) was insulted in the mosque, and the words that were used are not fit to be stated. If those who wish to read them want to, they can study the books themselves. They are not fit to be stated. Such words were used for the Princess (s.a.) in the Prophet's Mosque, in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). She would faint every little while, she would become unconscious. And she would say to her two sons, Imam Hassan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.), 'Where is your father? Where is your father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), who used to honor you so much, who used to take you both into his lap one after another, one after another, continuously? Where is your father, who had the most compassion for you, who loved you both the most? He loved you both so much that he could not bear to see you walking on the ground; he would pick you up in his lap.' You could not bear to see them, you would take them into your lap; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would not let you walk on the ground. Look, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) loved them so much, and this Ummah treated them both in such a way. There was a rain of arrows on the funeral of Imam Hassan (a.s.), and he was not allowed to be buried near the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And what happened to Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala, the world knows what they did. So, what did this Ummah do? 'Wa la ara bada'—now I will never see the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) knocking at this door, 'wa la ala ati'—and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) will never again lift you onto his shoulders, 'kamal yama'—the way the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) always used to lift you. Now let us move to the second hadith. 'An Abi Abdullah al-Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) qala: lamma qubidat Fatima (a.s.)'—when the soul of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) departed from this world, the Princess departed, 'dafanaha Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) sirran'—Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) buried her secretly without telling anyone, 'wa la mawwaja qabraha'—and he leveled her grave so that no trace of the grave could be found. This... So that no trace of the grave could be found. Why was this happening? Why did Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) herself make a will that 'do not let anyone participate in my funeral'? Ali (a.s.) then Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'thumma qama fa-wajjaha qabra Rasulillah (s.a.w.a.)'—then Ali (a.s.) stood up, turned towards the grave of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'Assalamu alaika ya Rasul Allah'—peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, 'anni'—from me, 'wa salamun ala ibnatika'—and peace be upon your daughter, 'wa tilka allati'—and she who has just come to visit you, 'wa ta-sara bi-ka'—and she who is now going to lie with you in your grave, 'wa mukhtar Allahu surataha'—and that daughter whom Allah has chosen to meet you, the honor of the earliest meeting was given to this daughter of yours. Your daughter is going to meet you. 'Qul ya Rasul Allah an safiyati'—what is my patience... My patience, O Messenger of Allah, I cannot bear the grief of your daughter. I have no patience left in me. That Ali, who crossed great battlefields and was never shaken by the calamities of the world, was never troubled, but the calamity of Fatima (s.a.w.a.) was so great that Ali would pull his knees to his chest and cry out. He would call out, 'Ya Fatima, ya bint Rasulillah,' and weep. Ali could not bear it. Sometimes the thought of the broken rib would come, sometimes the thought of the burning door. 'Wa fa-an sadus al-alamin tajalladi'—Janabe Zahra's grief is unbearable, I am unable to bear it. 'Ila sunnatika'—just as you bore great calamities, I am also trying to follow your path, to emulate you in bearing these calamities. After that, Maula says, 'Nusri sadri'—and your soul, your spirit has departed from between my neck and my chest, O Messenger of Allah. Has departed from between my chest, O Messenger of Allah. 'Bala wa fi kitabillah an qabul'—and in the Book of Allah, there is the mention of the best condolence, and what is that? 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. The trust that you had given, that trust is now being returned. I am returning that trust. 'Wa al-rahina'—and that pledge, that which was entrusted to me by you, I am now returning it. 'Wa ulisat Zahra'—Zahra has been snatched from me. O Messenger of Allah, Zahra has been snatched from me. The words Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) used—look, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is the master of Nahj al-Balagha. Look at the choice of words, pay attention to these words. He says 'ukhlisat Zahra'—Zahra was snatched from me. This Ummah did not let Zahra live. 'Fama aqba khara wa abra ya Rasul Allah'—now after the martyrdom of Zahra, the earth and the sky... Now after the martyrdom of Zahra, how gloomy have both the earth and the sky become. They have no attachment, no love for them anymore. Now here, the Master of the Universe (Maula-e-Kainat) says some sentences. This is an answer to those who say, 'Why do you mourn the martyrdom for 20 days? You mourn Hussain (a.s.) for two months and eight days, then you mourn this for 20 days, and you keep mourning continuously like this. When will you celebrate?' Maula-e-Kainat gives the answer to this objection in these words. Listen and pay attention to this. Maula says, 'Amma huzni fa-sarmad'—as for my grief, it is eternal, not for one year or two years. It is eternal. 'Wa amma layli fa-musahhad'—and as for my nights, they will be spent awake; I cannot sleep at night. 'Hamla qalbi'—and this grief can never be erased from my heart. That is why, about 29 years after the martyrdom of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.), when Ibn Abbas said, 'Maula, now you should dye your beard, now you should dye your hair.' You never dyed your hair or beard after the martyrdom of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.). Maula-e-Kainat said, 'Ibn... Ibn Abbas, what are you saying? The grief of Fatima (s.a.w.a.) is still fresh in my heart. The grief of Fatima (s.a.w.a.)... the meaning of the narration is this. I am presenting this meaning to you; you can check the original words. Maula is saying, 'This is only a matter of 25-30 years,' but here Maula is saying 'always, eternal.' And the Imams (a.s.) are not those who exaggerate. Remember, there is never exaggeration in the sayings of the Imams (a.s.). 'Abraha qalbi'—until Allah calls me to your house, O Messenger of Allah, where you are currently residing. 'Kam muk'—this wound is always fresh. This wound of Zahra (s.a.w.a.) is such that it is fresh. 'Kamad muk wa al-muhjun'—and this is such a grief that will never end, it will always remain. 'Sarra'—how quickly you left me. Maula-e-Kainat then says, 'Wa la ashku'—I will complain only to Allah, 'wa satukafuka ya Rasul Allah'—very soon your daughter will tell you... Very soon your daughter will tell you how your Ummah gathered against her and how mountains of oppression were broken upon her. 'Fasal ya Rasul Allah'—O Messenger of Allah, you ask your daughter yourself. Just check on her yourself, inquire from her yourself. Then he says, 'Gali sad lam tajid bihi sala'—there was so much grief in Zahra's heart, so much pain. 'Fakam gali'—meaning 'gali' is used when there is restlessness, anxiety, and trouble in the heart due to pain. 'Mutbas sadaha'—in her heart, 'lam tajid bihi sala'—there was no way for Zahra to express it. To whom should Zahra express it? Her ribs were broken. But if you study the narrations, you will see that whenever Maula-e-Kainat entered the house, even after the breaking of these ribs, when Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) came before him... Even after that, when Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) came before him, she would smile so that Ali (a.s.) would not realize the pain. So that Ali (a.s.) would not realize the pain. 'Wa sat waqula khaimi'—now the things that have been stated, Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) will tell you, O Messenger of Allah, and Allah will judge, and He is the best of judges. Ali (a.s.) buried Zahra (s.a.w.a.). After that, a few sentences that Ali (a.s.) said after the burial: 'Wa la gatu musta'—if it were not for this, because Maula-e-Kainat did not tell them about the martyrdom of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and did not invite anyone to Zahra's funeral, did not inform anyone of the burial, so Maula says that if it were not for this, 'lu muqa wa zamafa'—I would not leave this grave, I would stay sitting right here. I was sitting at the grave, I would not leave the grave, and not just sit, but 'wa la ala jalil raziya'—and I would weep like a woman who weeps for the grief of her young son. Weeps... there is one word 'musibat' (calamity) and another is 'raziya' (great tragedy). 'Raziya' means a very great calamity. And when they say 'jalil raziya', it means a very great calamity, the extent of which cannot be imagined. The calamity that Ali (a.s.) calls a calamity, how great could that calamity be? 'Fala taftara'—and before the eyes of Allah, your daughter is being buried secretly. 'Wa tuha'—and her right was usurped. 'Wa saha'—they kept her deprived of her inheritance. 'Wa lam yat ahad ya Rasul Allah'—not much time has passed since your era, and the Ummah did this. 'Wa lam yadhkur'—your mention has not even become old or erased, and this Ummah treated Zahra (s.a.w.a.) this way. They set fire to the house, martyred Mohsin (a.s.), broke her ribs. Now what else could this Ummah do? Oppression, kept her deprived of her inheritance, kept her deprived of her rights, the result of which is that when Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) made the will, 'Ali, bury me in solitude, at night'... Made the will, 'Ali, bury me in solitude, in the solitude of the night, in the darkness of the night, so that no one knows that the daughter of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) has left this world.' Then after that, Maula says, 'Wa Allah ya Rasul Allah mustaki'—O Messenger of Allah, I will complain to Allah. 'Wa fi ka ya Rasul Allah aza'—O Messenger of Allah, I offer you condolences, which is the best way to offer condolences that I can, I am offering condolences. Sallallahu alayhi wa ala salam, Ridwan Allahu ala Fatima Zahra, Allah Fatima Zahra, Allah Fatima Zahra.

title: EP04 | Madine Mein Hua Quran-e-Majeed Ka Inkaar | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical account of Imam Ali (a.s.) compiling the Holy Quran immediately following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It highlights the rejection of this compilation by the leaders at the time, who claimed they had no need for it. The speaker emphasizes that only Imam Ali and the Imams possessed the complete and authentic revelation as intended by Allah. The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of the Imam of our time to guide humanity through the true teachings of the Quran.
content:
They were saying that they neither need Ali (a.s.) nor his Quran, although this was a complete lie. Because it is not found anywhere in history that immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), those people had assigned anyone the responsibility of compiling the Quran. Those people had gone to Saqifah to choose their leader, so where would they have compiled the Quran from? It has already passed that after the incident of Saqifah, when Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) was forced to come out of his house to pay allegiance in Medina, he refused clearly, saying that he was busy compiling the Holy Quran. It is narrated from Janab-e-Abu Rafe that when after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), after the martyrdom, Ali (a.s.) compiled the Holy Quran, then according to the will of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he (a.s.) presented the Holy Quran before the Muhajirun and Ansar. But as soon as the leader opened that book, the gathering of the people present at that time—the Muhajirun and Ansar—the leader's face jumped with surprise, and he said to the Mawla, 'O Ali, I was busy with their affairs and arrangements, and after that, I was busy with the compilation of the Holy Quran, and now I have fully compiled it in this cloth. Allah did not reveal any verse of the Holy Quran to His Prophet except that I have fully compiled it in this cloth, and there is no such verse in it except that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had it written by me and explained its interpretation to me.' But the people, by saying this, refused to accept that Quran, but the people refused to accept that Quran by saying, 'La hajata lana bihi, indana mithluhu' (We have no need for it, as we have a Quran like it). How quickly those people forgot the status of Ali (a.s.). They were saying that they neither need Ali (a.s.) nor his Quran, although this was a complete lie, because it is not found anywhere in history that immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), those people had assigned anyone the responsibility of compiling the Holy Quran. They had gone to Saqifah to choose their leader, so where would they have compiled the Quran from? That is why Imam Baqir (a.s.) stated, 'No one among the people can claim that he has compiled the Holy Quran just as Allah revealed it, except that he is a liar. No one compiled the Holy Quran as Allah revealed it and protected it, except Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the Imams after him.' O Allah, by the sanctity of the Holy Quran, the true heir of the Quran, the Imam of our time, may he grant us that we may hear the Quran from the speaking Quran and illuminate our hearts and faith through divine teachings. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. states that we may hear the Holy Quran from the speaking Quran and illuminate our hearts and faith through divine teachings. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Ep#07 | Wiladat -E- Imam Mahdi: Shia Kitabon Mein
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical and theological proofs for the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) on the 15th of Sha'ban, 255 Hijri. The speaker cites key Shia scholars, including Sheikh Kulayni, Sheikh Saduq, and Sheikh Tusi, who documented the birth in their seminal works like 'Al-Kafi', 'Kamaluddin', and 'Al-Ghaybah'. By examining these authentic hadiths and historical accounts, the lecture affirms the reality of the Imam's birth and his status as the proof of Allah.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. As-salatu was-salamu 'alayka ya Waliyyal-Ahad. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. The 'The Strong Rope' team welcomes you to another episode of 'Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)' and presents the blessed days of the month of Sha'ban for your service. 15th of Sha'ban, the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), is such a great day that every child in the Shia community knows and waits for it, because this day is no less than any other. Because in the Shia school of thought, there is no doubt that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) took place on the 15th of Sha'ban in Samarra, and Alhamdulillah, we have such authentic hadiths and events that testify to this. In our hadiths, it has been stated explicitly that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has taken place, sometimes the circumstances of his birth are described, sometimes his... his birth is proven by the presence of Allah's worship. In today's episode, we will look at some such proofs. When the names of Shia books are mentioned, the name of 'Al-Kafi' comes first, meaning among the four authentic books, the first name is Al-Kafi, whose author is Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni (r.a.). He has brought a whole chapter in his book Al-Kafi, which is named 'Bab Mawlid al-Mahdi'. In this chapter, he brings 31 hadiths that are about the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and his being the proof of Allah. And in the very first hadith of this chapter, he states that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) took place on the 15th of Sha'ban in the year 255 Hijri. Respected viewers, it is known from the biography of Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) that he was born in the year 250 Hijri and his... birth was in the year 250 Hijri and he passed away in 329 Hijri. That is, he lived through the era from the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) until the Minor Occultation. Apart from this, a famous and well-known Shia scholar named Sheikh Saduq, in the second volume of his book 'Kamaluddin', brings a chapter named 'Bab Mawlid al-Qa'im al-Mahdi', and in the 34th hadith of this chapter, he narrates from Sheikh Kulayni that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) took place in the year 255 Hijri. Apart from this, another famous scholar named Sheikh Tusi, in his book 'Al-Ghaybah', narrates this hadith. These famous and well-known scholars have stated the date of the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) in their books with dates. These were the hadiths of the scholars. Let us look at some hadiths in which the circumstances of the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) are described, such as in the book 'Kamaluddin', a... hadith is found that when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) was born, he went and raised his two fingers towards the sky and then he... and he said, 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil-Alamin, and blessings upon Muhammad and his family.' And then he said that they testify to the proof of Allah, and if we (a.s.) are allowed to greet, then all the doubts will be removed. That is, when did he state this? When his birth had already taken place. That is, from a different aspect, we get to know here that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has taken place and what work he performed after that. Apart from this, another hadith is found in the book of Tusi, this hadith is narrated that the maid of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) whose name was Naseem, she proves that I went to meet Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) 10 days after his birth, and when I met him, I was given... and he said, 'May Allah have mercy, I have...' said, 'May Allah have mercy, I have...' I became very happy. Then he said, 'I give you glad tidings that because of this, Allah has delayed your death for three days.' Similarly, our scholars have not just brought authentic hadiths but have brought chapters, have brought books, in which the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and the circumstances of his birth have been described. These proofs make it clear to us that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has taken place. We pray in the court of the Almighty that Allah hastens the reappearance of His last proof and fulfills the promise He made to him. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. content:
The hadith is from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). It states that when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred, the angels complained to Allah, saying, 'O Lord, how much oppression is being inflicted upon Hussain, while he is Your chosen servant and the son of Your Prophet?' At that moment, Allah (s.w.t.) showed the angels a glimpse of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and said, 'Through him, I will take revenge on the oppressors of Imam Hussain (a.s.).' This also proves that Allah (s.w.t.) is telling the angels about the Imam of the time (a.s.) even before his arrival.

excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance and historical context of 'Intezaar' (waiting) for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). It emphasizes that true waiting is an active state of preparation and alignment with the Imam's mission rather than passive anticipation. The session also provides essential guidelines for a mega quiz competition, highlighting the virtues of those who remain steadfast in their faith during the occultation.
content:
[Music] Auzubillahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. The link for the quiz is now live and available in the live chat and comment section of this video. Meaning, even if someone did not become a daily winner, but in seven out of 12 episodes, they have given correct answers, then all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. Allahu kullu waliyyin Hasan, salwa kullu sa khata tasahu ha fa ha [Music] Auzubillahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem. Auzubillahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Eyes are fixed, hearts are restless, yearning on the right and left. I am not the only one waiting, O Muntazar (the awaited one), the Day of Judgment is held back in your wait. 1190 years have passed. 12 centuries have gone by. But the wait for Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is as vibrant today as it was at the beginning of the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra). And in these 12 centuries, countless lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), scholars, orators, poets, and our ancestors have departed from this world holding this belief of waiting. We all acknowledge one thing, and we feel it in our lives, that as time passes, the intensity of the wait increases. For some, the wait grows with the passage of time, while others, out of despair, live their lives and depart from this world just holding onto this belief. Death is certain, but does this mean that if the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) does not happen in our lifetime, we should lose hope? Let us divide this topic of waiting into two parts. First: The importance of waiting and the virtue of the one who waits (Muntazir). Second: Waiting in the mirror of history. The importance of waiting: We are waiting for that personality who is the heir of the People of the Cloak (Ashab-e-Kisa), through whom the religion of God will prevail over all other religions, who is the hope of the oppressed against the oppressors, who is the final proof (Hujjat) of Allah on earth, and by the blessing of whose footsteps the system of the earth and the heavens is maintained. Regarding him, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has said, 'Afzalul ibadati intizarul faraj'—the most virtuous worship is to wait for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). So, the question arises: are we the only ones performing this most virtuous worship? No. Rather, Imam Reza (a.s.) says, 'How excellent it is to be patient while waiting for the reappearance. Have you not heard the saying of Allah (Azza wa Jall): 'Fartaqibu inni ma'akum muna-tazirun' (Quran, Surah Hud, 11:93), 'So wait, indeed I am also waiting with you.' Therefore, it is incumbent upon you all to be patient, for surely the reappearance will occur after despair, and those who passed before you were more patient than you.' In another tradition, Abu Khalid Kabuli narrates from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). The Imam says, 'O Abu Khalid, indeed the people of the time of occultation who believe in his Imamate and wait for his reappearance are the most virtuous of all people of every age.' One day, some companions were present with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). He (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Allahumma li ikhwani marratayn'—O God, let me meet my brothers. O God, let me meet my brothers. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) uttered these words, the companions sitting near him said, 'Are we not your brothers, O Messenger of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah said, 'No, you are my companions, and my brothers are those who will be in the end times.' Then the Messenger of Allah describes their virtue: 'They will be people who have not seen me. I have been told their names and the names of their ancestors by Allah while they were in the loins of their fathers and in the wombs of their mothers,' meaning they have not yet come into this world. Meaning they have not yet come into this world. Each one of them will remain steadfast on their religion with such intensity that it will be more difficult than walking on thorns in a dark night or holding hot coals in one's hands. They are the lamps of light, and Allah will protect them from all the tribulations that come like dark storms in history. And we have seen, in the light of Quranic verses and the hadiths of the Masumeen (a.s.), what is the status and position of a person who waits (a Muntazir) in the eyes of Allah and in the eyes of the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda). Now, let us move to the second topic: Waiting in the mirror of history. Before studying history through events, let us see if we are the only ones waiting or if it has happened before. Today, when we have known how much importance waiting for the Imam holds according to Allah (Azza wa Jall) and the sayings of the Masumeen, and what the virtue of a Muntazir is, let us try to see in the mirror of history whether any nation in history has waited in this way and what lessons and warnings are there for us. Continuing this topic, we will present two examples. The first example is of the Jews who migrated from their homeland and came to Medina. Migrated from their homeland and came to Medina, only because it was written in their books that a solver of difficulties would be present. So, we go into the detailed discussion of this. When Abu Basir asked Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) about this saying of Allah (Rabbul Izzat) in verse 89 of Surah Baqarah: 'Wa kanu min qablu yastaftihuna 'alalladhina kafaru'—'And before that, they used to seek victory over the disbelievers.' On this, the Imam (a.s.) said, 'The Jews found information about the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in their books, so they migrated and set out in search of the place that is between Ayr and Uhud.' Their state of waiting was such that leaving all their homes and belongings to migrate to an unknown place is not easy, and that too in Arabia, searching for two mountains was even more difficult. In that era, there was no map system like today to reach there, and they were only told the names of two mountains. Now, the Jews somehow reached Medina. They settled there and had also accumulated a lot of wealth. When this news reached a Yemeni king named Tubba, then When this news reached a Yemeni king named Tubba, he attacked those Jews. Those Jews saved themselves from his attack. After which, they felt pity for the weak members of Tubba's tribe, and therefore, they used to throw barley and dates at them at night. When this matter reached Tubba, he felt sympathy for those Jews. He said to those Jews, 'I want to live with you.' So those Jews said to him, 'It is not for you to live in the place where a Prophet will migrate.' He (Tubba) said to those Jews, 'I am leaving my family and children among you. So when that happens, he will help them.' Therefore, he left his two tribes, Aws and Khazraj, there. So when the population of those tribes increased, they started snatching the wealth of the Jews. Those Jews often used to say to them, 'When Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is sent, he will drive you all out of our homes and along with our wealth.' When Allah sent Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) among them, the Ansar believed in him, but now those Jews... They believed in them, but now those Jews have rejected you. And this is the declaration of the Lord of Majesty: 'Wa ja'ahum ma 'arafu kafaru bihi, fa la'natullahi 'alal kafirin' (And when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers). When the Book came to them from Allah, confirming what was already with them, and when they had previously been seeking victory over the enemies of the faith, then when that which they recognized came to them, they rejected it. So, the curse of Allah is upon the rejecters. Why did the Jews reject the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Despite waiting with such intensity, the Jews rejected the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Let us see in the traditions of the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) what the reasons were, what reasons were stated for why the Jews rejected him. Hazrat Imam Hasan (a.s.) says that when the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) came to the Jews, whom they recognized... ...whom they recognized through his signs and attributes, they rejected the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) and also rejected his Prophethood, out of envy and rebellion. 'Falamma ja'a Muhammadun (s.a.w.a.) hasadu, li annahu minal 'Arab, fakazzabu hu' (When Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) came, because he was an Arab, the Jews envied him and rejected him). Janab Jabir ibn Yazid Ju'fi narrates that I asked Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) about this verse. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Its inner interpretation is that when he came to them, they rejected what they knew about Ali (a.s.), so Allah said about them: The curse of God is upon the rejecters, meaning the Banu Umayya, who reject the inner meaning of the Holy Quran.' This was the waiting of those Jews, in which, despite such intense waiting, out of envy, they rejected the very one they were waiting for. God... ...the very one they were waiting for. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds to protect us from such waiting, where a waiter becomes a rejecter of the awaited one himself. That is, the one who is waiting denies the one being waited for. Now let us look at another example of waiting. Anas ibn Harith Kahili, who was a companion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and was present with him in the battles of Badr and Hunayn. When he heard from the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) that 'My son, meaning Mawla Hussain (a.s.), will be killed in the land of Iraq. So whoever among you finds his time, let him support him, let him help him.' History tells us that when Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his caravan reached Karbala, Anas ibn Harith Kahili was waiting for them there, solely based on that command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that whoever finds his time should help and support him. If we look at the summary of this entire discussion, the two things that are a lesson and warning for us... ...the two things that are a lesson and warning for us are what? Number one: On one hand, the waiting of the Jews, where they left their homes for their awaited one, and their purpose was completely different from the purpose of their awaited one. Therefore, they became rejecters of the awaited one. That is, they became those who deny the one they were waiting for. Number two: On the other hand, there were individuals like Anas ibn Harith Kahili who truly fulfilled the right of waiting and gave us the lesson that if one is waiting for the awaited one, then the goal and purpose of the waiter should be solely and exclusively the support of the Imam. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa salla Allahu 'ala... They will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees, and their names are on your screen: Mohammad Rizvi from Prayagraj, Binte Zahra from Azamgarh, Shabi Zahra Zaidi from Meerut, Syed Sadiq from Mumbai, Sham-e-Zahra from Bengaluru, Zahra Hashmi from Alipur. Many congratulations to all the winners. If anyone's name did not appear in today's winners, there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series. And those who have given all correct answers in the quizzes of seven episodes out of twelve will all be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize, i.e., the Iraq pilgrimage. We thank all of you once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time with another new video. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

title: EP#15: Kya Nabi (a.s.) Ki Wiraasat Nahin Hoti?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the theological controversy surrounding the inheritance of Prophets in Islam. The speaker challenges the validity of a specific tradition used to deny Lady Fatima (s.a.) her inheritance by contrasting it with explicit verses from the Holy Quran. By citing the examples of Prophet Sulayman (a.s.) inheriting from Prophet Dawud (a.s.) and the prayer of Prophet Zakariya (a.s.), the lecture argues that inheritance is a proven prophetic tradition.
content:
It is proven from the Holy Quran that Prophets (a.s.) are heirs and also make heirs. The Prophetic tradition that was used to deprive Shahzadi Zahra (s.a.) of her right stated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'We, the group of Prophets, neither inherit nor leave inheritance; what we leave behind is charity.' But is this hadith in accordance with the Holy Quran? In the Holy Quran, not one but two verses are found which prove that Prophets (a.s.) are heirs and also make heirs. Surah Naml: 'Wa waritha Sulaymanu Dawuda' (And Solomon inherited David), and he said, 'O people, I have been taught the language of birds and have been given a portion of everything. Indeed, this is a clear grace and favor from God.' In Surah Maryam, the prayer that Hazrat Zakariya (a.s.) made to Allah contains: 'So grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, pleasing.' Both these verses prove that a Prophet is an heir and also makes an heir.

title: Arbaeen Ka Pehla Zaair | Jabir Ibn Abdullah Ansaari (a.r.) Ka Poora Waaqeya [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture recounts the historic first pilgrimage (Ziyarat) of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari to the grave of Imam Hussain in Karbala on Arbaeen. It details the rituals Jabir performed, his emotional salutations to the Imam, and his profound explanation of how those who love the Ahlulbayt share in the rewards of their struggle. The talk concludes by reflecting on the massive scale of modern Arbaeen pilgrimages and the importance of maintaining love for the followers of the Prophet's family.
content:
Assalamu alaikum... [Arabic recitation]... Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari (r.a.)'s servant, who was the slave of Abdullah Ansari (r.a.), narrates that I and Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari went out for the Ziyarat of the grave of Imam Hussain ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). When we reached Karbala, Jabir went to the bank of the Euphrates river. He performed Ghusl, tied one sheet as an Ihram, and wrapped another sheet over his body. He opened the bag that contained perfume, sprinkled it on his body, and then took one step after another, reciting the remembrance of God, until he reached the grave of the Imam. He said to me, 'Bind me to the grave.' I... ...I bound him to the grave. After that, when he threw himself onto the grave of Hussain (a.s.) and fainted, I sprinkled some water on him, and when he regained consciousness, we cried out three times, 'Ya Hussain, Ya Hussain, Ya Hussain.' Then Jabir said, 'Do you not answer a friend? How will you answer me when your jugular vein is severed from your body, and your head has been separated from your body? I bear witness that you are the descendant of the Prophets and the descendant of the Master of the Believers, and the descendant of the one who was in the cloak. You are the son of the guide and the son of the pious, and you are the son of the leader of the leaders, and the son of Hazrat Fatima, the leader of the women of the worlds. And why should you not be so, when you have been fed by the hands of the Master of the Prophets?' ...fed by the hands of the Master of the Prophets, and you have been raised in the lap of the pious, and you have been nurtured with faith and Islam. Your life was pure and clean, and you were granted a pure death. But the hearts of the believers are restless due to your separation. Yes, but they have no doubt in what has been chosen for you. May the peace of Allah be upon you, and may His pleasure be with you. I bear witness that you spent your life just as your brother Yahya ibn Zakariya spent his life.' Then Jabir turned his eyes towards the grave of Hussain and said, 'Peace be upon you, O souls that have descended upon the courtyard of Hussain. I bear witness that you established prayer, gave Zakat, and enjoined good and forbade evil.' ...enjoined good and forbade evil. You fought against the misguided and the ignorant, and you worshipped Allah until death came to you. Then Jabir said, 'By the One who sent Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) with the truth as a Prophet, we are surely equal partners with you in this work of yours.' At this, his servant asked, 'O Jabir, how is this possible when we have not descended into any valley, nor climbed any mountain, nor struck anyone with a sword, while the heads of these people were separated from their bodies, their children became orphans, and their women became widows?' Jabir replied, 'I heard my beloved Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) saying that whoever loves a group of people will be resurrected with them.' It will be felt with them, for whoever loves the actions of a group is considered a partner in that action. I swear by the Lord of that Being who sent Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) with the truth as a Prophet, that my intention and the intention of my companions is the same path upon which Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions departed. Jabir said, 'When we left and had traveled some distance, I said to him, "Jabir, shall I make a will for you? I do not think we will meet after this journey." [He said], "Love the followers of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) as long as you love them, and keep enmity with the enemies of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) as long as you keep enmity with them, even if he fasts all year and is a devout practitioner of religion. And be gentle with the lovers of Ale Muhammad (a.s.), because even if one of his steps is [heavy with] many sins, his other step will remain firm due to the love of Ale Muhammad (a.s.)." But due to the love of Ale Muhammad (a.s.), the other step will remain firm, and surely his lover will return towards Paradise, and the one who holds enmity towards them will return towards Hell. This is what is required. And before this, the honor of visiting Imam Hussain (a.s.) was only attained by Jabir bin Abdullah al-Ansari. May millions of salutations be upon Jabir. And the heart desires to say to him, 'O Jabir, you were alone in your pilgrimage, but today, look at the splendor of Karbala.' The lovers of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) from every corner of the world are expressing their devotion, overcoming all kinds of obstacles, enduring all hardships, and reaching Karbala so that the tradition you established may continue until the Day of Judgment. In the end, to act upon the will of Jabir bin Abdullah al-Ansari, we pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that today, in our final moments, He grants us the sustenance of loving the lovers of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) and keeping enmity with their enemies, and for the establishment of the government of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) in this world, in our time... For the establishment of the government in our time, may the reappearance of our Imam, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), be hastened. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. [Music] Hussain [Music]

title: Fadak Se Kitni Aamdani Hoti Thi? | Watch EP 1 of #The_Fadak_Podcast
excerpt: This lecture explores the economic and political significance of Fadak, arguing that its income was essential to the functioning of the early Islamic state. The speaker analyzes historical valuations of the land, estimating its worth in modern terms, and contrasts the legal concepts of 'Maal-e-Ghanimat' and 'Fay'. Furthermore, the discussion touches upon the theological implications of the dispute over Fadak regarding the status of Lady Fatima (s.a.) and the historical figures involved.
content:
The entire government's budget was run by this. Only and only these properties. Yes, meaning, of course, in any state, the biggest budget is defense. After that, social activities. Both these things were being done from the income of Fadak. Meaning, the Islamic Empire of that era was run by Fadak. Meaning, the entire government was established from Fadak, from the income of Fadak. Anyway, it is present in the books. Ibn Abi al-Hadid mentioned its valuation in Sharh Nahj al-Balagha as 500,000 dirhams for half the land. Just half. So for the whole land, it becomes 1 million dirhams. If we estimate one dirham as 10 grams of silver, then according to today's value, it becomes almost 1 billion. Yes, it becomes 1 billion, and the inflation on top of that is separate. We will discuss all these things. But the very first question that arises is, when we use the word 'Maal-e-Ghanimat' (spoils of war) and there is a word 'Fay', what is the difference between Maal-e-Ghanimat and Fay? The Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni) criteria—often, whenever a narrator states something against the established beliefs of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, they are immediately stamped as a 'weak narrator', even if it is the truth. Despite that, meaning if someone says something against their core fundamentals, especially regarding Wilayah and Imamate, if we consider the Princess (s.a.) as Siddiqa in the true sense... If we consider her (a.s.) as Siddiqa in the true sense, then it is not permissible for us to consider the one who usurped her rights as a Siddiq. If we are calling him a Siddiq, then the direct result of this is that we are insulting the Princess (s.a.). If he is a Siddiq, then...

title: Raj’at Mein Imam Husain (a.s.) Waapas Aayenge
excerpt: This lecture discusses the theological concept of Raj'at, the return of the Imams to this world before the Day of Judgment. Citing a narration from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker highlights that Imam Hussain (a.s.) will be the first among the Imams to return and rule. The talk connects this belief to the mission of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) in seeking justice for the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
Janab Maula ibn Quraish narrates from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that the Imam (a.s.) said: 'Awwalu man yarji'u ilad-dunya'—the first to return to the world—'Al-Hussain ibn Ali alayhimas-salam'—Imam Hussain (a.s.) will come to the world. The first, meaning among the Imams (a.s.), Imam Hussain (a.s.) will be the first. This is how it is in this hadith. In some hadiths, it is mentioned that the Commander of the Faithful will also come, and all the Imams will come. An interesting point in this hadith is that the Imam further says that after that, Imam Hussain (a.s.) will rule over this world. And look, this belief—the return of Imam Hussain (a.s.)—is completely connected to our belief that after the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), the Imam (a.s.) will take revenge from the killers of Imam Hussain (a.s.). This revenge will also be after the reappearance. That is why we recite Dua-e-Nudba, 'Ayna at-talibu bi damil maqtuli bi Karbala'—we are calling out to the Imam of the Time (a.s.) in this way, asking where is the one who will take revenge for the blood of the martyr of Karbala.

title: How Ameerul Momineen Imam Ali (a.s.) transformed a Singer into a Quran Recitor?
excerpt: This lecture recounts the miraculous transformation of a man named Zadan, who was a singer, after a brief encounter with Imam Ali (a.s.). Upon the Imam's guidance, Zadan was miraculously granted the ability to recite the entire Quran instantly. The speaker uses this story to emphasize the transformative power of the Imam's attention and encourages listeners to seek spiritual guidance from the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda).
content:
Friend, what a story it is! In the time of Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.), there was a man named Zadan. This Zadan had a habit of singing songs and doing such things. And his voice was very beautiful. So, Maula-e-Kainat was passing by once and saw Zadan singing, so Maula said to him, 'Zadan, Allah has given you such a beautiful voice, why don't you use it in the right way?' He said, 'What should I do, O Commander of the Faithful?' He said, 'Recite the Quran.' He said, 'I don't know how to read the Quran.' So, Maula took a small pebble lying there, a small stone, placed it on his blessed forehead, and then told Zadan to put it in his mouth. As soon as Zadan put it in, he became a Hafiz of the entire Quran. And then he started reciting. And then Zadan became a companion of Maula. A tremendous companion. Look, a person who has been committing sins his whole life, but when the attention of the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda) was upon him, he changed. So, our main task should be to seek help from the Proof of God: 'O Sahib-e-Zaman, we don't know the Quran, please teach us.' And then try yourself, and God willing, you will see how help comes.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#10 - Kya Imam Ali (as) Ne Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) Ki Difaa Ki?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common objection regarding why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not intervene during the attack on the house of Lady Fatima (s.a.). The speakers clarify that Imam Ali (a.s.) did indeed defend her but was bound by a specific covenant of patience given to him by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The discussion highlights the hypocrisy of critics who praise the patience of others in similar historical contexts while questioning the actions of Imam Ali (a.s.).
content:
Do it. [Music] I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May peace be upon you, O Wali of Allah. Peace be upon you, O successor of the Prophet. Peace be upon you, O Ahlulbayt of Prophethood. Peace be upon you, O Lady of the Worlds, Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Welcome to another episode of 'Better than a Thousand Months'. Today, we are present in your service again. In the previous episode, we saw what the reason was for Imam Ali (a.s.) not taking action. But does this mean that when the House of Purification was being attacked, Imam Ali (a.s.) did nothing at that time? Regarding this, those who want to deny this entire event or hide the oppressors raise an objection. Their objection is: if the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was really attacked and Imam Ali (a.s.) was present in that house, then why did Imam Ali (a.s.) not defend Janabe Zahra (s.a.)? Their objection is: could anyone attack Lady Zahra (s.a.) while living in the house of the Lion of God? And if it was done... And if it was done, why did Imam Ali (a.s.) not defend her? To answer this objection, our brother Abbas Patel is present with us today. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Abbas Bhai, as you heard, the objection today is that there is a conspiracy through this objection to deny the entire event. So, what should be the answer to this? If the attack on the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was so... if... Brother, it would be completely wrong to say that Imam Ali (a.s.) did not defend her. If we turn to Shia sources, for example, 'Kitab Sulaym ibn Qays' or 'Bihar al-Anwar', we will find out that this objection is completely baseless. Before you is a narration from 'Bihar al-Anwar'. When we read that the oppressor said to Hazrat Ali (a.s.) and Fatima Zahra (s.a.), 'If you do not pay allegiance, we will burn your entire house.' Here, note that these people came with the intention of burning the entire house. After that, they brought fire and wood, burned the door, pushed it, and entered the house. At that time, Janabe Fatima (s.a.)... At that time, Janabe Fatima (s.a.) cried out, 'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)!' After that, the oppressor drew his sword and struck the side of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). This makes one thing clear: even though those people were prepared to kill, something definitely happened at that time due to which only Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was martyred, and the rest of the family members were saved. Meaning, what was that thing due to which their plan failed and they could not succeed? Brother, when the oppressor entered, Ali (a.s.) grabbed him, threw him to the ground, broke his nose, and grabbed his neck. He was about to kill him, but he stopped himself. When Ali (a.s.) had grabbed that oppressor and was about to kill him, what happened that he stopped himself? The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had willed to Ali (a.s.) that... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had willed to Ali (a.s.) that after him, he would face difficulties, so he should exercise patience and forbearance. This is present in 'Kitab Sulaym ibn Qays'. Not only that, but in the book of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the name of the book is... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'After me, if you can exercise patience, it would be better.' And the oppressor knew this because in a letter to Muawiyah, he wrote, 'I am not unaware, and I am certain, and I know one thing very well about which there is no doubt: if I and all the people of the earth tried, it would not be possible [to overcome Ali].' But there was a secret that was in the heart of Ali (a.s.), and I know it, but I will not reveal it. So surely, Abbas Bhai, Ali (a.s.) is... So surely, Abbas Bhai, Ali (a.s.) is about to reveal it, and indeed no human had the courage to attack him. And Ali (a.s.) himself pointed towards this when he did not kill that oppressor and stopped his hand. At that time, he said, 'By the One who sent Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) with the truth as a Prophet, if it were not for the covenant that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had taken from me, you would have known that you could never have entered my house.' Meaning, Ali (a.s.) would never, under any circumstances, disobey the command of Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.), because it is stated in the Holy Quran regarding them: 'They do not speak until He speaks, and they do not act except by His command.' Indeed, those who [question] the patience of Ali (a.s.)... Certainly, now speak to those who try to portray the patience of Ali (a.s.) as his weakness. We have one piece of advice for them: at the very least, they should study the subject matter of their own books. The name of the book is 'Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah'. This is a book whose main sections were written by the famous historian Ibn Kathir. He mentions the siege of Uthman bin Affan's house and observes the events with his own eyes. However, we do not find anywhere in history that Uthman bin Affan gave any response to this attack and this siege, even though the reins of the government were in his hands at that time. It even reached the point where Ibn Taymiyyah, in 'Minhaj as-Sunnah', described this incident as a virtue of Uthman, saying: 'Anna Uthmana asbara an-nas' (Uthman was the most patient among the people) despite the disrespect shown to his honor. Abbas Bhai, from this incident, the hypocrisy of our opponents becomes clearly visible. Because on one side, there is Uthman, whose honor was insulted and whose fingers were cut off, but Uthman doing nothing about his own insult became a virtue and a merit for him. And on the other side, there is Imam Ali (a.s.), who, when Lady Zahra (s.a.) was attacked, grabbed the oppressor... ...grabbed the oppressor and threw him to the ground. Even when he went to kill that oppressor, people still say that Imam Ali (a.s.) did not defend Lady Zahra (s.a.). This incident is very strange. Thank you very much, Abbas Bhai. Nasir, despite all these arguments, if any of you have any questions on this topic, you can contact us on our WhatsApp number or our social media handles. We will try our best to present the answers to these questions with evidence for your service. Insha'Allah, we will be present again tomorrow with another episode of this series, namely, answering the objections regarding the attack on Zahra (s.a.). With this, viewers, give us permission. Pray for us. Ya Ali Madad, Khuda Hafiz. [Music]

title: Tasbeeh -e- Fatima (s.a.) Ka Poora Waaqeah | SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2022
excerpt: This lecture recounts the historical origin of Tasbeeh-e-Fatima, a sacred prayer taught by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) to his daughter Lady Fatima (s.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.). It details the physical hardships Lady Fatima faced in her daily household chores, which prompted Imam Ali to suggest she ask the Prophet for a servant. Instead of a servant, the Prophet provided them with this spiritual gift, which brought immense blessings and ease into their lives.
content:
Certainly, the teaching of this Tasbih that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) gave to Lady Zahra (s.a.) and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), because of which so many blessings entered the life of Lady Zahra (s.a.) that they cannot be counted. The incident is narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) that when Lady Zahra (s.a.) used to be busy with household chores, she had to endure so much hardship. For example, when she used to fill the water skin, that water skin was so heavy that her hands would get injured from carrying it. Or when Lady Zahra (s.a.) used to operate the hand mill, the effort of operating that mill would cause her hands to bleed. Often, when Lady Zahra (s.a.) was busy cleaning the house, the dust and dirt would affect her clothes, or when she would light the stove—meaning, in that era, we didn't have a gas system like today—in that era, one had to blow into it to light the fire, and the smoke that came from it would affect her clothes. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and Lady Zahra (s.a.)—Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) gave a suggestion to Lady Zahra (s.a.): 'Why don't you go to your father's service'... ...'Why don't you go to your father's service and request a servant?' Lady Zahra (s.a.), upon the request of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), left the house and went towards the mosque. There she saw that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was talking with some companions. The sentences of the Hadith are like this: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) went towards the mosque and saw that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—he saw the Princess had come to the mosque and left without speaking. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked Lady Zahra (s.a.)—before the Princess could explain, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) narrated the whole story, how Lady Zahra (s.a.) was struggling with household chores, the suggestion that was made, for which Lady Zahra (s.a.) went to the Messenger of Allah... Now, after hearing this whole story, the Messenger of Allah [Music] said to them, the sentences of the Hadith: 'Qala salla Allahu alayhi wa alihi, shall I not teach you both something that will be better for you than this servant? Ila akaltuma ma'akuma' (When you go to sleep, before sleeping, this Tasbih, which we call Tasbih [Music] will be better). Because of this, so many blessings entered the life of Lady Zahra (s.a.) that they cannot be counted.

title: Kitne Waqt Mein Ziyaarat Par Dobaara Jaana Chaahiye [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the recommended frequency for performing the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) based on a Hadith from Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.). It highlights that while those living nearby should visit monthly, those living far away should aim for at least once every three years to maintain their spiritual bond with the Ahlulbayt. The speaker emphasizes the immense spiritual rewards of Ziyarat, including the forgiveness of sins and the protection of angels, and encourages believers to prioritize these pilgrimages.
content:
A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytanir rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala ya wali al-asr, Allahumma ajjal farajahu wa sahl makhrajahu. Wa as-salamu ala al-Husayn wa ala Ali ibn al-Husayn wa ala awladi al-Husayn wa ala ashabi al-Husayn. It is written in a reliable Hadith that a person asked Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.): 'When a person returns from the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.), how many days should pass until he goes again, and for how many days should he not abandon that Ziyarat?' In response to this matter, he said: 'For those living nearby, once a month, and for those living far away, once every three years. If more than three years pass, it is as if he has broken his bond with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and has cut himself off from him.' Except for a valid excuse, one should do this. If a lover of Husayn (a.s.) knows that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.)... ...Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.) and the martyrs of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are watching, and they pray for him in his favor, and because of this, Allah grants him goodness in this world and the hereafter. So he will want that as long as he lives, his house should be near the shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.). Indeed, when a pilgrim of Imam Husayn (a.s.) gets off his mount, no foot touches the ground but that it prays for him, and when the sunlight falls on him, it washes away his sins just as fire burns wood, and the sun does not leave any of his sins remaining. Then he returns in such a state that no sin remains on him, and his status is raised to such an extent that even a person bathed in his own blood in the way of Allah cannot reach that level. And an angel is appointed for him who is his protector and continues to pray for him until he returns for Ziyarat, or three years pass, or he passes away. That he, among the poets, peace be upon him, his... ...that he, among the poets, peace be upon him, should be proud of his destiny. From this, and from the importance of Ziyarat, one should never be deprived. Where is the one who is martyred in the way of Allah, and where is the one who is a pilgrim of Imam Husayn (a.s.)? And then Imam (a.s.) says that the status of a pilgrim is so high that it should not be that without any valid excuse, we become among those who abandon Ziyarat. We pray in the Divine Court that every Shia's heart should realize the importance of Ziyarat. May we fulfill all the etiquettes of going for Ziyarat, and may He grant us the Ziyarat of the Leader of the Martyrs, Imam Husayn (a.s.) every year, which is the cause of the pleasure of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), especially the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and may it be our intercession in this world and the hereafter. Amin, Ya Rabbal Alamin. This was known among the people, media, Muslim, women [Music].

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 3 | Tafseer of the verse الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of the phrase 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin' as discussed in the Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain. The speaker highlights various traditions from the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the spiritual benefits, gratitude, and healing properties associated with reciting this phrase. Additionally, the session touches upon the vastness of Allah's creation, referencing traditions that describe the existence of multiple worlds and Adams.
content:
And billahi min ash-shaytanir rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum. In the series of 'Tafsir-e-Surah', I have appeared in your court once again. Keep this in mind, the teachings of Islam, in this, some of the blessings of Sharia have been stated. It is narrated from you, 'Alhamdulillah', the performance of this gratitude, which Allah has made necessary for His servants, for the believers. And with these words, the servant expresses gratitude for receiving blessings from the Lord of the Worlds, that there is no one worthy of worship except Allah, and he is firm on this belief, and that there is no other Creator or Master besides Him. It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the context of the blessing, he said: 'Allah has favored me by revealing the book to me.' And its specialty is 'Alhamdulillah'. And its specialty, 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin', is the first blessing of Paradise, that God will bestow upon the one who recites it. So, 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin' is beyond this, and this tradition is authentic. In it, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'Whoever says 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin' four times in the morning has fulfilled the gratitude for his day, and whoever says this in the evening has fulfilled the gratitude for his night.' It is narrated from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) through his father that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) used to recite 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin' 360 times in the morning, and he used to recite this same phrase the same number of times every evening. In the Tafsir of Ibrahim, it is narrated from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) in which he has stated with reference to... That a person came before Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) and after something, he said 'Alhamdulillah'. But here, Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) did not consider this a good opportunity and said, 'You have fallen short in our right.' The person asked, 'How?' So he said, 'Whenever something is given to any of you, he should say 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin Muhammad'. Hearing this, that person repeated the words taught by him, and in response, he prayed for his well-being. In this same context, there is a tradition of Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). When Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) needed something, he said 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin', and then he placed his finger on his nose and said, 'My nose is always engaged in this, and it remains busy in it.' There is another tradition where Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says that whoever... Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says that whoever, after something, says 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin 'ala kulli hal', will be protected from pain in the nose and teeth. We look for the cure for our ailments here and there, but the Masumeen (a.s.) have given us the cure for our ailments through these words. There is another tradition from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). Some people came to him, and then talking about his nose, he placed his hand on it and said, 'Yes, this is it.' He said 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin'. The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) says that from his left nostril, a creature will emerge that will be smaller than a fly, and it will cut under the Throne, and it will keep seeking forgiveness until the Day of Judgment. Seeking forgiveness until the Day of Judgment—what a great thing! So, respected listeners, there is a need to pay attention. This forgiveness is only for saying 'Alhamdulillah-i...' This forgiveness is only for saying 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin'. Imam Reza (a.s.) said in the book 'Uyun', 'God is the One who nourishes when there was no one present to be nourished.' Indeed, it is established, and in the book 'Shams', it is also narrated from Hazrat Ali (a.s.) that God is the One who nourishes at that time, and there is no one else to nourish. Is there anyone to say this? Now, I will mention another very famous tradition. Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) has stated 41 words of a Hadith. He says, 'Perhaps you think that God created only one world, and you think that He did not create anyone else besides you? Yes, yes, He created one hundred thousand worlds, and He created one hundred thousand Adams.' In fact, some traditions say one hundred thousand... In fact, some traditions say one hundred thousand Adams. Now, the time is up. I have mentioned the rest, and God willing, I will state the rest of it in the next session. Until then, goodbye. Peace be upon you. Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alamin.

excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive theological and historical defense of the doctrine of Imamate, specifically focusing on the Twelve Imams. It analyzes both Sunni and Shia sources, including Sahih Bukhari, Kitab al-Kafi, and Kifayat al-Athar, to establish the divine designation and names of the Imams. The session also addresses common doubts regarding the concept of nass and emphasizes the infallibility of the Ahlulbayt as a core tenet of faith.
