Allahumma kulli waliyyika... [Music] ...wa habibi... [Music] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala... Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala ya Wali al-Asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Regarding the belief of Imamate, the Ahl-e-Tasannun, i.e., the opponents, raise an objection regarding our belief in Imamate, which is that the 'nass' (explicit designation) of the 12 Imams is not present in our ancient books. Neither are their noble names present in our books. And all the Hadiths that are found have been fabricated by later narrators and later scholars. And we do not find any authentic Hadith to prove the Imamate of the 12 Imams. In response to this, let us first see whether any 'nass' or any Hadith regarding the 12 Imams exists in their own, i.e., the Ahl-e-Tasannun's, authentic books or not. Muhammad ibn Ismail Bukhari narrates a Hadith in his book which is as follows: 'Yakunu ithna 'ashara amiran, faqala kalimatan lam asma'aha' (There will be 12 Amirs, and then he said a word I did not hear). This Hadith is narrated from Jabir ibn Samura. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Yakunu ithna 'ashara amiran, faqala kalimatan lam asma'aha.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said there will be 12 Amirs, and then... The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said there would be 12 Amirs, and then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said something that Jabir ibn Samurah could not hear. Then he said, 'All of them will be from Quraish.' His father told him that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said all of them would be from Quraish. This is the first hadith present in Sahih Bukhari, and based on the references of Bukhari, their belief is clear that, according to them, all hadith in Bukhari are authentic. Meaning, in their books, the hadith of the 12 Imams exists; the number exists. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said something that the narrator could not hear. Besides this, the second hadith which is narrated in Sahih Muslim by Muhammad ibn Muslim Nishapuri—this is also a book that is considered entirely authentic by them, and they consider all its hadith to be authentic. The hadith in Muslim is as follows. This is also from Jabir ibn Samurah. He says, 'I entered with my father to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and heard him say, "This matter will not end until 12 Caliphs pass through it." Meaning, this matter—the Imamate—will not end until 12 Caliphs come among them. Then he said something in a voice that was quiet to me.' Then he said something in a voice that was quiet to me. Then I asked my father what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said. His father said, 'He said all of them will be from Quraish.' This is the second hadith present in Sahih Muslim. Besides this, there are two more hadith present in Sunan Abu Dawood. The hadith presented from the references of Sunan Abu Dawood are considered authentic by them, and Al-Albani has verified these hadith. The book of Sunan where this hadith is found is called 'Kitab al-Mahdi'—meaning, the book within the Sunan that specifically concerns Imam Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.). This is also from Jabir ibn Samurah. He says, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say, "This religion will remain mighty as long as 12 Caliphs exist in it." Then the people raised their voices in Takbir and began to cry out. Then he said something in a quiet voice.' Kalmatan khafiyatan (a quiet word), then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said something softly. I asked my father, 'Ya Abati, ma qala?' (O my father, what did he say?). He replied, 'Kullu min Quraysh' (All of them are from Quraysh). One point worth noting here is that all these hadiths are in their authentic books, and all these hadiths are pointing towards the 12 Imams and the 12 Caliphs. They are explaining the 12 Caliphs and the 12 Imams. Furthermore, the names of the 12 Imams are not present in all these hadiths. That is, we should ask these people, we should raise the question: what happened that you did not hear the names of these 12 Imams or the 12 Caliphs from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? It is possible that in response to this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told things that were not compatible with their beliefs, or the names of their Caliphs might not have been in them, due to which they did not mention this in their books. It cannot be that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated the number of 12 Imams but did not state their names; that would mean the hadith itself makes no sense if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is stating the number but not specifying their names. Anyway, if we want to know the clarification of this, we will have to refer to our own books, where very clearly and openly, the names of the 12 Imams and... ...and clearly and openly, the names of the 12 Imams and their nass (designation) and their appointment are present in our books. Not just hadiths, but entire chapters of hadiths exist. Entire books exist that point towards the nass of the 12 Imams, which clarify the nass of the 12 Imams for us. And who these 12 Imams are is stated in our books. And these books are not from the later scholars (muta'akhireen) but from the earlier ones (mutaqaddimeen), meaning these are ancient books; we are talking about books from a thousand years ago, and even older books exist. Anyway, we go to those books against which the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunnis) cannot raise any objection. The first book is Kitab al-Kafi al-Sharif, which is the book of Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.), and Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) lived from 255 AH to 329 AH. That is, the third century AH, meaning this book is approximately 1100 years old. And this book is a world-renowned book, and everyone is familiar with it. Even the Ahl-e-Tasannun themselves do not raise any objection regarding this book. That is, they do not raise any objection regarding the existence of this book. In this book, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) brings a book in its first volume... ...brings a book in its first volume which is titled 'Kitab al-Hujjah'. And in this Kitab al-Hujjah, Chapter number 126, 'Bab ma ja'a fi al-ithna 'ashar wa al-nass 'alayhim al-salam' (Chapter on what has come regarding the Twelve and the nass upon them, peace be upon them). This means that the chapter in which the nass regarding the Ithna 'Ashar (the Twelve Imams) is present. Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) brings 20 hadiths in this chapter alone, which are present regarding the nass of the 12 Imams. In this same book, i.e., Kitab al-Hujjah, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) records hadiths from Chapter 65 to Chapter 76—that is, 12 chapters—regarding each Imam being 'mansus min Allah' (designated by Allah). The name of the chapter is 'Bab man nassallahu 'azza wa jalla wa rasuluhu 'ala a'immatina 'alayhim al-salam wahidan fawahidan' (The chapter on those whom Allah the Almighty and His Messenger have designated as our Imams, peace be upon them, one by one). The chapter in which the nass from Allah the Almighty and His Messenger regarding the Imams (a.s.) is present, one after another—that is, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) has a chapter for every single Imam in this, and various hadiths are present within these chapters. That is, know that these are just the names of the chapters we are stating; inside them... ...are various hadiths, including authentic (sahih) and sound (sanad) hadiths. In addition, Sheikh Kulayni brings chapters 113 to 124—that is, another 12 chapters—in which there is a discussion regarding their birth. 'Bab mawlid al-a'imma 'alayhim al-salam' (Chapter on the birth of the Imams, peace be upon them), meaning the mention of the birth of every Imam and the nass of their Imamate is present in it. That is, if we do a rough calculation, there are 25 chapters in Al-Kafi alone regarding the nass or the birth of the Imams (a.s.) or regarding their names. This is the discussion of Al-Kafi. That is, the book that was compiled 1100 years ago, which is still present among us today, has 25 chapters just regarding the nass of the Imams (a.s.) in which various hadiths are present. Another book that was compiled by one of his students, whose name is Ibn Khazzaz al-Qummi. He compiled a book. The name of this book is 'Kifayat al-Athar fi al-Nusus 'ala al-A'imma al-Ithna 'Ashar' (Sufficiency of Traditions regarding the designation of the Twelve Imams). That is, if you just look at the name of the book, you will understand what the title of this book is, what the topic is, what the subject is. Kifayat al-Athar, meaning those hadiths that are sufficient regarding the nass of the Imams... ...the Twelve Imams, meaning those hadiths that are sufficient regarding the Twelve Imams being designated by Allah. This entire book is only regarding the 12 Imams being 'mansus min Allah', regarding their nass—that is, nass means the documented evidence that this Imam made a will regarding the Imam coming after him, along with the name. He brought a chapter for every Imam. There are a total of 39 chapters in this book that only discuss this topic. A total of 39 chapters only discuss this topic, which, again, this book was written and compiled in the fourth century, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Khazzaz al-Razi al-Qummi is the author. He was alive in the fourth century, from 360 AH to 381 AH. And this book was compiled during this period, during this era. That is, this book is also an approximately 1100-year-old book that is still present among us today. The mention of Sheikh al-Khazzaz is also present in our books of Rijal (biography). For example, Rijal al-Najashi, which is known as 'Fihrist Asma' Musannifi al-Shi'a' (Index of the Names of Shia Authors), whose author is Abu al-Abbas, and he lived from 372 AH to 450 AH. Maruf Najashi says about Ibn Khazzaz... ...says about Ibn Khazzaz in his book: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, thiqat ashabina' (Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, a trustworthy one of our companions), meaning he was 'thiqa' (trustworthy), he was reliable, he was among our teachers. And know that he was among the students of Sheikh al-Saduq and Sheikh Kulayni. His kunya is Abu al-Qasim, 'wa kana faqihan wajihan' (and he was a jurist and a leader), meaning he was a jurist of his time and a leader of his time—that is, he was counted among the great personalities of that era. 'Lahu kitab' (he has a book), and he mentioned his books. Besides this, Sheikh Tusi mentioned Sheikh Khazzaz in his Rijal like this: 'Al-Khazzaz, nazeel Rayy' (Al-Khazzaz, a resident of Rayy), 'yukna Abu al-Hasan' (his kunya is Abu al-Hasan), 'mutakallim jalil' (a great theologian), and a high-ranking theologian. If we read the introduction of this book, he states the reason for the compilation of the book like this. Ibn Khazzaz says that he found some weak Shias being influenced by the doubts of the opponents... ...being influenced by the doubts of the opponents. And who were these opponents? 'Wa al-Mu'tazila' (and the Mu'tazila). So also know that some people raise this objection that the Mu'tazila were Shias—no. This is a book from a thousand years ago; in its introduction, Sheikh Khazzaz is stating that the Mu'tazila was the group that was casting doubts into the hearts of the Shias and was creating doubts and suspicions. They were saying that 'la tujad nusus wa riwayat 'ala a'immat ahl al-bayt' (there are no nass and narrations present regarding the Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt, peace be upon them). 'Wa ma rawa al-shi'a fi al-bab' (And the Shias have nothing regarding the nass of Imamate). And the Shias have nothing regarding the proofs of Imamate. And a similar doubt is raised by the opponents even today. That is, this doubt that we hear on their channels today is not a new doubt. It is not a new suspicion. That is, 1000-1100 years ago, Sheikh Khazzaz was recording this doubt in his book. Not just recording, but after this, he is giving an answer in the form of a very powerful, authentic book... ...in the form of a very powerful, authentic book. And in this book, 39 chapters are proving the nass of the Imamate of the Imams (a.s.) of the Ahl al-Bayt. In 39 chapters, and all the hadiths are only from the companions (Sahaba), and there is no hadith from the Imams themselves. So Sheikh Khazzaz divided this book into two parts. The first part recorded hadiths from those companions who were narrating hadiths from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) regarding the Imamate of the 12 Imams. Among them, at the top of the list is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, Imam Hasan (a.s.), Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Zayd ibn Arqam, Imam Husayn (a.s.), Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, Ammar ibn Yasir, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Salman al-Farsi, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman—these are the companions. This is the list of companions who narrated the nass of Imamate from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), whom Sheikh Khazzaz has recorded in his book. The second part of this book consists of those narrations that are transmitted from the Imams (a.s.) themselves. That is, the Imams (a.s.) themselves are directly narrating hadiths regarding the Imamate, regarding the Imam coming after them, regarding their successor. So that is what the second part of this book consists of. Furthermore, the last two chapters of this are very interesting, which are its last two... ...very interesting, which are its last two chapters. These are narrations from Zayd himself, which point to the Imamate of the Imams (a.s.) and prove that Zayd did not claim Imamate. So for those who today accuse the Shias that the Shias did not know who the Imam was after Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), there are two chapters for them—detailed chapters—he compiled hadiths only on this topic. Let us look at one hadith from this book for blessings. The first hadith present in this book is from Ibn Abbas. He narrates from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.): 'He says, indeed Allah chose him (the Prophet) for Prophethood, and chose Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) for Imamate, and chose from the progeny of Husayn (a.s.) the Imams (a.s.), and Allah sent them as proofs over His servants, and the ninth of them will be the Imam...', ...and the ninth of them will be the Imam Mahdi from the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and he will be the Mahdi of this Ummah, and he will appear after a long occultation, and he will fill this world with justice and equity just as it will have been filled with oppression and tyranny. So these two ancient books, which were compiled in the third and fourth centuries, from which we saw chapters and one hadith that is pointing to the nass of Imamate. In addition, the third book, 'Kamal al-Din', which is the book of Sheikh Saduq (r.a.). Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) passed away in 381 AH. That is, this is also a book of the fourth century. In this book, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) compiled the nass regarding Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and the nass regarding his Imamate, and compiled proofs of his occultation in this book, in which there are also Hadith Qudsi. Hadiths are also present from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and hadiths are also present from the Princess of the Two Worlds (s.a.). Furthermore, Sheikh Saduq has compiled hadiths from every Imam in this book. And there are a total of 16 chapters in this book alone regarding Imamate. Chapters in this book regarding Imamate—specifically the Imamate of the 12 Imams—are found from Chapter 23 to Chapter 38. The fourth book is 'Al-I'tiqadat al-Imamiyyah' by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.). Again, this is a book approximately 1,000 years old, or more than a thousand years old. On page 122, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) narrates in a hadith: 'The Imamate will be completed through the 12th Imam, who is Imam Mahdi of the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). He will fill this world and this earth with justice and fairness just as it had been filled with oppression and tyranny before him.' So these are some ancient books in which the names of the 12 Imams and the texts (nusoos) regarding them exist, and proofs of their Imamate exist. Besides this, we have the names of the 12 Imams in our supplications. Besides this, we have the names of the 12 Imams in our supplications, and not just one, but many supplications contain the names of the 12 Imams. We will briefly mention three supplications in this video. The first book is 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih' by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), again a book more than a thousand years old. In the section on 'Ta'qibat', Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) mentions the Sajdah of Shukr (prostration of gratitude). And in this dhikr, which a believer should perform in the Sajdah of Shukr, there is a long dhikr, a part of which is: 'Allah is my Lord, Islam is my religion, Muhammad is my Prophet, and Ali, Hasan, Hussain, Ali ibn al-Hussain, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and our Hujjah, Hasan ibn Ali, are my Imams.' It contains the names of all 12 Imams, which we were taught to recite in the Sajdah of Shukr. Again, this is a 'Ma'thoor' supplication, meaning it is a dhikr narrated in hadith through the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) for the Sajdah of Shukr, containing all 12 names. And the sentence after it is: 'I love them and I express disavowal (bara'ah) of their enemies.' This was the first supplication. I express disavowal of their enemies. This was the first supplication that Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) mentions under the title of Sajdah of Shukr in the Ta'qibat of prayer. The second supplication is in 'Misbah al-Mutahajjid' by Sheikh Tusi (r.a.), who passed away in 460 AH. This is also a book nearly a thousand years old. In the section regarding the 'Ghusl of the deceased' and its rulings, there is a hadith where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that for every Shia, when they are shrouded and given Ghusl, a testimony (shahadat-namah) should be placed with them. A part of this testimony that I want to present, which relates to our topic, is: 'And I testify that Ali is the Wali of Allah, the Commander of the Faithful, and the Imam appointed by Allah. And from his progeny, the Imams (a.s.) are the Imams appointed by Allah. And the first from the progeny of the Commander of the Faithful is Imam Hasan, then Hussain, Ali ibn al-Hussain, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and...' Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and the Master of the Special Name, the Hujjah (a.s.).' These are the names of all 12 Imams and the special title of Imam Zaman (a.s.) which is present in this hadith, which should be placed with every Shia when they are given Ghusl and shrouded. The third supplication is the one famous as 'Dua-e-Asharat', which is emphasized to be recited on Fridays. In this supplication, when a person gives testimony, they repeat these types of sentences: 'I testify that there is no god but You, there is no god but Allah, You are One, You are Ahad, and You have no partner. And I testify that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is Your servant and Your Messenger, and that You have power over all things. You give life, You cause death, You cause death, You give life. And I testify that Paradise is true, Hell is true, the Resurrection is true, and the graves are true.' These are all the beliefs being stated—the beliefs of this Shia religion are being stated. And I testify... And I testify that Ali ibn Abi Talib, Hasan, Hussain, Ali ibn al-Hussain, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and the Successor, the Hujjah, the Master of the Special Name, the Awaited one—may Your blessings, O Lord, be upon them all.' The names of all 12 Imams (a.s.) and the special title of Imam Zaman (a.s.) are present in this testimony as well. Finally, I will conclude the discussion by pointing to two famous hadith. The first is the hadith famous as 'Hadith al-Lawh'. This hadith has been narrated by Sheikh Nomani in 'Al-Ghaybah', Sheikh Tabarsi in 'Al-Ihtijaj', the late Daylami in 'Irshad al-Qulub', Mulla Salih Mazandarani in 'Sharh Usul al-Kafi', Mulla Fayd Kashani in 'Al-Wafi', and Sheikh Hurr al-Amili in 'Isbat al-Huda'. There is no time to go into detail, but it is a famous hadith that reached us through the Princess (s.a.). Besides this, the second hadith is also a hadith of Mi'raj, which is very famous and has been narrated by Ibn Ayyash in 'Kifayat al-Athar'... Narrated by Ibn Ayyash in 'Kifayat al-Athar', by Sheikh Hurr al-Amili in 'Isbat al-Huda', by Sayyid Hashim Bahrani in 'Madinat al-Ma'ajiz', and by Allamah Majlisi in 'Bihar al-Anwar'. Let us read this hadith and conclude the discussion here, Insha'Allah. The hadith is from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Umm Salama is the narrator. She says the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'When I was taken to the heavens (Mi'raj), I looked and saw written on the Arsh: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and I supported him with Ali." And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was shown all the lights of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) during Mi'raj. The hadith continues: "I saw the light of Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Hussain, and the lights of Ali ibn al-Hussain, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and I saw the light of the Hujjah like a shining star..."' Like a shining star. I asked, 'O Lord, who is this? Whose lights are these? And who are these people?' I was called out, 'O Muhammad, this is the light of Ali and Fatima. This is the light of your two grandsons, Hasan and Hussain. And these are the lights of the Imams who will come after you.' So, from the progeny of Imam Hussain (a.s.), in this very hadith, two beliefs are proven: they are 'Mutahhirun' (purified) and 'Ma'sumun' (infallible). 'And this is the Hujjah through whom the world will be filled with justice and fairness.' So these are the hadith. This was just a brief overview of those hadith in which the blessed names of the Infallible Imams (a.s.) are present, and texts regarding them exist. In our ancient books, this proves that the objection raised is a completely baseless objection, and it is only... It is a completely baseless objection, and it is brought only to create doubt in the hearts of weak Shias. Finally, we pray to Allah that just as Allah showed His Beloved the light of that Imam—Imam Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.)—may He also let us witness the light of Imam Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.) in this world and after this world. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his progeny. title: Ek Guftugu (Part: 1) | Hazrat-e-Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.) Ki Wafaat Hui Ya Shahaadat?
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological and historical discourse surrounding the passing of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), specifically addressing the debate between natural death and martyrdom. The speaker examines Quranic verses and historical traditions from both Sunni and Shia sources to argue that the Prophet attained the status of a martyr. By analyzing linguistic nuances and citing authoritative texts, the discussion highlights the importance of recognizing this aspect of the Prophet's life as part of the broader narrative of the Ahlulbayt's sacrifices.
content:
Assalamu Alaikum, Ali Bhai. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah, Ahmed Bhai. Are you going to the Imambargah? Yes, brother, today is the Majlis for the Wafat (passing), right? I am going there too. Please, sit down. Jazak Allah Khair. It is good that I met you, otherwise, I would have been late waiting for a bus or auto for the Majlis. You are right, brother; attending the Majlis is as important as reaching there on time. By the way, Ahmed Bhai, if I may, can I ask a question? Certainly, please ask. Why did you use the word 'Wafat'? Today is the martyrdom of two Masoomeen (infallibles). 'Wafat' is used for a natural death. But the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Hasan (a.s.) were martyred. I believe in the martyrdom of Imam Hasan (a.s.) because his wife, Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath, poisoned him. But how can you say that about the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? I have often heard 'Wafat', and the calendar in my house also says 'Wafat'. Ahmed Bhai, it is a simple matter. Just think, the status, virtue, and rank that Allah (s.w.t.) bestowed upon His most superior creation and His beloved Prophet (s.a.w.a.) were not given to anyone before him, nor will they be given to anyone after him. most superior creation and His beloved Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Allah (s.w.t.) chose him for the propagation of His most important religion, revealed His greatest book upon him, made him the Seal of the Prophets and the Master of the Messengers. In the Holy Quran, He called him 'Rahmatul-lil-Alameen' (Mercy to the Worlds), the one who speaks with God, the possessor of great character, and the best example for humanity, i.e., 'Uswat-ul-Hasana'. In short, when the personality and life of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) are the most superior, how is it possible that he would not attain superiority in the final stage of his worldly life, i.e., death, and be deprived of the great honor of martyrdom? On one hand, there are other prophets who have no comparison with the Prophet in terms of rank, yet they were blessed with martyrdom. Even the companions who participated in battles alongside the Prophet and sacrificed their lives for him were blessed with martyrdom. So, is it acceptable that the most superior creation would be deprived of martyrdom? And the sad part is, brother, that people in our society hesitate to even use the word 'martyrdom' for the Prophet. hesitate to even use the word 'martyrdom' for the Prophet. I do not know what reality people are trying to cover up, whereas scholars of high status from both sects have acknowledged that the Prophet was martyred. There is definitely a difference of opinion between Shias and Sunnis regarding how he was martyred and who martyred him, but the martyrdom of the Prophet is a proven fact. But Ali Bhai, in the Holy Quran, Allah says in Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 67: '...and Allah will protect you from the people.' When Allah took the responsibility of his protection, how could anyone kill him? This would be against the Quran. Ahmed Bhai, granted that this is the apparent text of the Quran, but its actual apparent meaning is not what you are saying. How can you say that? I am not saying this; it is stated this way in the Tafsir of the famous Sunni scholar, Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen. Look, my phone is right here. Unlock it. Go to the gallery. The first screenshot you see is the one I have. Look what is written here: When someone asked al-Uthaymeen... When someone asked al-Uthaymeen, how can the statement of al-Zuhri be considered correct, which says: 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was martyred,' and that the Jews were the cause of his killing and the cause of his martyrdom, whereas Allah (s.w.t.) said in the Quran: '...and Allah will protect you from the people,' the same verse you just quoted? In response, al-Uthaymeen wrote: 'The meaning of 'protect you from the people' here refers to the state of propagation.' That is, while in the state of propagation, Allah will protect the Prophet from the evil of the people. And that is why Allah further commanded the Prophet: 'O Messenger, convey...' (Tabligh). And as long as you are in the state of propagation, you will be protected. 'And no one could overcome him during his propagation.' Therefore, whenever you propagated, no one could overpower you or kill you. This is the Sunni perspective. This is the Sunni perspective. As far as the Shias are concerned, Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 67, relates to the event of Ghadir. This verse was revealed regarding the propagation of the Wilayat of the Master of the Universe, Imam Ali (a.s.). And this declaration of Wilayat was not limited to the Prophet alone; rather, the propagation of the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) was the responsibility of every human being. Because the style of conversation in the Holy Quran is that the address is to the Prophet, the address is to one, but the message is for all who are listening. Therefore, the guarantee of protection in this verse is not just for the Prophet, but for all those who propagated the message of this Wilayat and will continue to do so until the Day of Judgment. So, does this mean that those who defend and propagate the Wilayat of Ali until the Day of Judgment will never be killed? No, not at all. And it does not mean that the Prophet was given eternal life in this world. Therefore, when the occasion of revelation and the interpretation of this verse have nothing to do with the Prophet being killed or his martyrdom, using it to deny his martyrdom is wrong. But Ali Bhai, there is another Quranic verse, and that is in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 91: 'Say, why did you kill the prophets of Allah before...' Allah says in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 91: 'Say, why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?' This verse mentions the killing of prophets, but we all know that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had a higher status than a prophet. He was not just a prophet but also a Messenger (Rasool). So, this verse proves that only prophets can be martyred, not Messengers. And that is why you see that Prophet Yahya ibn Zakariya (a.s.), who was only a prophet, was killed. But Prophet Isa (a.s.), who was a Messenger, was saved by Allah and raised alive from the earth with protection. What is the answer to this? What kind of question is this, Ahmed Bhai? Twisting the verses of the Holy Quran and using them for your own purposes is not right. This question itself shows that behind it lies a conspiracy to deny the killing of the Prophet. Although the answer to this is present in the Holy Quran itself. You presented the verse from Surah Al-Baqarah, but how did you forget the verse from Surah Ali 'Imran? Which verse? Surah Ali 'Imran, verse 144, does not talk about the killing of Messengers, but specifically mentions the martyrdom and killing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). What does the verse say? Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim: 'And Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]?' And Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful. Ahmed Bhai, this verse was revealed specifically about the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), so how can anyone assume that only prophets are martyred and Messengers are not? No, Ali Bhai, but in this verse, it is written 'afamata aw qutila'. 'Aw' means 'or'. That is, either he dies or he is killed. Both possibilities are present here. It could be a natural death or he could be martyred. So how can you say that he was definitely martyred? Ahmed Bhai, you will at least admit that the word 'aw' points towards possibility. Of course. So, are you trying to say that Allah did not know what was going to happen to the Prophet? was about what is going to happen to the Prophet? Will it be a natural death or will he be martyred? And that is why the word 'aw' (or) has been used here. No, no, we cannot say that. Allah is the Knower of all things. He knows everything. But still, the word 'aw' has been used here. It is clearly evident from this that 'aw' here does not mean 'or'. Then what is it? Here 'aw' means 'bal' (rather), i.e., 'afain mata bal qutila' (if he dies, rather if he is martyred). But Ali brother, you are drawing this conclusion on your own that 'aw' here means 'bal' (rather). What is the proof for this? This is the eloquence (balaghat) of the Quran, which is not understood by everyone. That is why one has to turn to the heirs of the Quran, i.e., the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), to understand these things. In this regard, there is a narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) in Tafsir Ayyashi, in which the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Do you people speculate that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) passed away or was he martyred?' Then the Imam quoted this very verse, that Allah says, 'If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?' After this, the Imam (a.s.) explains it by saying, 'Fasumma qutila bil-sam' (so he was given poison before death). He says, 'Fasumma qutila bil-sam' (so he was given poison before death). Meaning, the Prophet was martyred. 'Innama saqatahu' (and those two women gave him poison to drink). 'Saqata' is the feminine form used here. It is the dual form; it refers to two. Two women gave him poison to drink. From this narration, it becomes absolutely clear that according to our Imams (a.s.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was martyred through poison. Meaning, 'aw' does not mean 'or' but 'rather'. Meaning, if he dies, rather, if he is martyred. And do not think that I am presenting this hadith just to prove a point on my own. Rather, this is also proven by another verse of the Holy Quran that 'aw' here should be taken as 'bal' (rather). Which verse is that? It is Surah As-Saffat. You know that in Surah As-Saffat, the mention of Prophet Yunus (a.s.) is present. When Allah Almighty brought Prophet Yunus (a.s.) out of the belly of the fish and sent him to his people, what does the verse of the Holy Quran say? 'Wa arsalnahu ila mi'ati alfin aw yazidun' (And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more). Here too, did Allah not know whether there were 100,000 people or more? Here too, did Allah not know whether there were 100,000 people or more? No, no, He absolutely knew. So here too, Ahmad brother, the meaning of the verse will be the same, that He sent him to 100,000, rather more people. And similarly, for the Prophet, the same meaning will be taken, that if he dies, rather, if he is martyred. And it is not that this belief of the Prophet's martyrdom is only found among us Shias. As I said earlier, even the scholars of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni) are in agreement that he was martyred. The disagreement is over who gave the poison. Only someone who is completely distant from the Quran and Hadith, or has some other agenda or motive, can deny the martyrdom. Just now you saw the screenshot of Al-Saimeen's book on my phone. Yes, yes, exactly. Scroll to the right there. Yes, and there you will see another screenshot. Found it? Yes, found it. This is Tafsir Baghawi. Yes, Tafsir Baghawi, look here, what is written here? In this Tafsir Baghawi, this sentence is clearly written: 'Wa al-muslimuna 'an Rasullillah (s.a.w.a.) ma shahida' (And the Muslims have the view that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was martyred). 'Kama akramallahu al-nabiyya' (Just as Allah honored him with Prophethood). Meaning, He honored him with Prophethood. Meaning, just as Prophethood is an honor for him, martyrdom is also his honor. Now look at the next screenshot. Oh, this is Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Yes, Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, which is considered a very authentic book among the Ahl-e-Tasannun. Now look at what is written there: The narrator states, 'I am ready to swear by Allah not once, but nine times. Yes, nine times I am ready to swear. What is the oath? That the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was killed (martyred). He was martyred. And this is because, 'Wa kadhalika akramallahu al-nabiyya wa huwa shahida' (And this is because just as Allah Almighty made him a Prophet, He also blessed him with martyrdom). After so many proofs, one is surprised at those people who cover up this reality. May Allah guide those who do not know, and those who are hiding it intentionally, I do not know what their state will be when they are presented before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) on the Day of Judgment. Anyway, Ahmad brother, we have reached our destination. It was very nice talking to you. Oh no, no, Ali brother, I should thank you. No, no, Ali brother, I should thank you. If only this issue had been explained in our society as easily and openly without any 'taqiyya' (dissimulation), then today, at least everywhere, we could have put up banners of the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). But one problem still remains, Ali brother. Which one, brother? Who exactly gave poison to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Oh, Ahmad brother, this is a complicated issue and it will take a lot of time to discuss. But if you want to know our belief, then Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), whose martyrdom also took place on the 28th of Safar, has a hadith in which the Imam (a.s.) said, 'I too will be martyred by poison just as my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), was martyred.' That is all I can say at this moment. You go to the Imam-bargah, I will come after parking the car. [Sound of groaning] Ali brother, this sentence of Imam Hasan (a.s.) is enough for me. Thank you very much, my brother. Today, for the first time, I will perform the Azadari (mourning) of the Prophet as a martyrdom. And yes, after going home, the first thing I will do is remove 'Wafat' (death) from the calendar and write 'Shahadat' (martyrdom). Ahmad brother, do not forget to pray for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) by remembering the oppression of the Imam (a.s.), performing his Azadari, and weeping over his tragedy, because he is the... He is the true heir of this grief.

title: Allah Ki Marefat | Recognition of Allah | Kalaam e Noor # 03
excerpt: This lecture explores the foundational concept of Ma'rifat, or the recognition of Allah, as the essential starting point for all worship. Drawing upon the teachings of Imam Rida (a.s.), the discourse emphasizes that true devotion cannot exist without a deep, intellectual, and spiritual understanding of the Creator. It highlights that the journey of faith begins by knowing the One who is being worshipped.
content:
Imam Rida (a.s.) said: 'The beginning of the worship of Allah is His recognition (Ma'rifat).'
Ma'rifat (recognition) is the starting point of all religious worship.
Worship without knowledge of the Creator is incomplete.
Imam Rida (a.s.) serves as the primary source for this theological principle.
The intellect plays a crucial role in the process of recognizing Allah.
True devotion is rooted in the depth of one's understanding of God's attributes.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 10 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture addresses various practical questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting during the holy month of Ramadan. The speaker discusses the rules for paying Khums in advance, the obligations of travelers regarding fasting, and how individuals who are physically weak or ill should manage their fasts. Additionally, the session clarifies common misconceptions about activities like watching television and getting married during the month of fasting.
content:
I remembered yesterday that I have to go here... [unclear audio]... I am very disturbed. Ramzan has arrived, and ten days of this blessed month have already passed. And if in this month we... ...have passed, and if in this month we do not seek forgiveness for our sins, we will be very unfortunate. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has said that we should turn towards the court of the Lord of the Worlds. And in His court, you should be repentant. May Allah include us all in His mercy and forgive our sins. May this blessed month of Ramadan not pass us by while we remain in our sins. We should seek forgiveness. Today, in this session, we will begin the Q&A session. Respected Maulana, please begin. Respected Maulana, there are a few questions from the friends. The first question is: due to the coronavirus, can we pay our Khums before the end of the month of Ramadan? And similarly, can we pay our annual Khums in advance? See, Khums cannot be paid before it is due, nor can Khums be paid in advance unless you know the amount. One way is that if you want to give it, you can give it as a loan to the Marja' (or their representative), and later, when the calculation is done, you can adjust it against that loan. The next question is regarding travel. If someone is traveling and has not kept the fast, what should they do? Regarding travel, if you travel before a certain time, the fast is not obligatory. But if you travel after that time, the fast remains. If you are traveling and you are worried about your health, you must fulfill your obligations. If you reach your destination... But if you cannot do that, you will have to make up for that day later. And it is not possible that if you are 5 or 6 years old, you can just skip it. If you are able, you should fast. Besides, in travel, if the travel is for a sinful purpose, the fast is not exempted. The traveler must fast. It is not that you can just choose to fast or not. The questioner asked about our young girls who are weak and find it difficult to fast. What is the ruling in this situation? Regarding this, in Ruling Number 19, it is mentioned that for some people, fasting becomes difficult. Some girls are not physically strong enough to fast. If they fast, there is a risk of them becoming ill or fainting. In such cases, the ruling for the sick applies. If the heat is extreme and it is very difficult for them to bear, then in such a situation, they say... In such a situation, they say that one should start the fast with the intention of fasting, and when they feel extreme thirst or hunger, they can drink water or eat food. But this is only to the extent of necessity, to gain enough strength to continue. They will have to make up for these fasts later when they regain their strength. Another interesting method mentioned is that if one is a laborer, they should try to rest as much as possible during the day to conserve energy. The fourth question is: what is the ruling on watching movies or TV during the state of fasting? Does watching them invalidate the fast? Watching movies or serials does not invalidate the fast, but as we mentioned earlier, the essence of fasting is to refrain from hunger and thirst and to focus on spirituality. Watching such things might lead to sins or distract you from the purpose of the fast. Even if it doesn't invalidate the fast, one should avoid it. One should avoid such things and focus on worship. Yes, Maulana, if someone does this for marriage purposes, and they get married... They say that getting married is forbidden, that one must avoid it on this day. In Sharia, it is not that marriage is forbidden in Ramadan; generally, it is that if you do it, then... Islam is a great religion, and Allah (SWT) can make things easy for a Muslim. Islam is... look at this. This is the way it is. So, this thing that the whole world has kept as a gift, one should definitely do it. If someone else and... we are grateful to the viewers who are constantly asking questions on our WhatsApp number, and we are answering them here.
Khums cannot be paid in advance unless given as a loan to the Marja'.
Travelers must fast if the journey is for a sinful purpose or if they depart after a specific time.

excerpt: This lecture explains the fundamental Shia theological concept that the earth can never exist without a Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda). Drawing from the authoritative text Al-Kafi, the speaker highlights a narration by Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) which asserts that the presence of an Imam is essential for the stability of the world. The session emphasizes that the absence of such a Proof would lead to the destruction of humanity, similar to a turbulent sea.
content:
The earth cannot remain without a Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda). We are presenting this hadith of Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) before you, which is from the book Al-Kafi, in which the Imam (a.s.) states that if the Imam were to be removed from the earth even for a single moment (أن الإمام رفع من الأرض ساعة), if he were removed even for a moment (لما جد بأهلها), then the earth would destroy its inhabitants (كما يموج البحر بأهلها) just as the waves of the sea collide and destroy those who live within them. Let us assure you that this is not the only hadith we have presented to you from Imam Baqir (a.s.); rather, in the greatest and most authentic book of the Shia school of thought, known as Al-Kafi, Sheikh Kulayni (may Allah have mercy on him) has brought approximately 13 hadiths and has established a chapter titled 'The earth is never devoid of the Proof of Allah.' In this chapter, Sheikh Kulayni (may Allah have mercy on him) has presented 13 hadiths, in which it becomes crystal clear that this earth cannot remain empty without a Proof of God. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad.

excerpt: This lecture shares a moral story about a man who discovers a precious diamond and chooses to donate it for a noble cause rather than keeping it for personal gain. The speaker emphasizes that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) do not leave any act of kindness unrewarded, illustrating how generosity leads to unexpected blessings. The narrative highlights the importance of detachment from worldly possessions and trusting in divine providence.
content:
I gave an example of someone relying on others, saying 'I will come, this will happen,' and your personal matter... every person is determined, as is famous among people. I am not going back, and people there... they call it 'remind cement'. So, in whatever state a person is... there was a person whose financial condition was not very good, not very good at all. They only had two rooms in their house. So, he said to his wife, 'Let's do one thing, let's keep some animals in one of the two rooms—chickens, goats, whatever—so that we have some income.' So, this is how the life will go on. She said, 'Okay, fine, no problem.' So, the husband and wife lived in one room. After that, he started keeping animals in the other room. He started cleaning it, and while cleaning, a big diamond came out. It was a diamond... so this lady, who is telling you, it was about... according to the machine, it was a big diamond. When the diamond came out, this person was clear that it was a diamond ring. This person was clear that it was a diamond ring. He went to the jeweler with this, and the jeweler said, 'This is very precious. We can buy our needs from here, and the whole nation will benefit from this.' So, he needed to go to Baghdad. In Baghdad, the jewelers would give him the right price. He said, 'Okay, I will go.' Before going to Baghdad, he got an opportunity to perform Hajj. He thought, 'I will perform Hajj first, then I will go to Baghdad.' He went for Hajj, and after Hajj, he went to Baghdad. When he reached Baghdad, he realized that he had arrived. When he arrived, he stopped to rest. There, the caretaker was announcing, 'O people, O wealthy people, don't you see that this wood is rotting? The king of the world deserves better than this. If you donate some money, we can fix this place.' This man was very generous, so he told the caretaker, 'I don't have anything else...' I told the caretaker, 'I don't have anything else, just this diamond. You keep it, sell it, and whatever money comes from it, use it for this.' He gave it away. [Music] What should I do? That is why I gave the example of relying on others, saying 'I will come, this will happen,' and your personal matter... and nowadays, people are famous for this. I am not going back, and people there were very worried. Someone knocked on the door. The whole police force was there, the one I told you about. 'Are you the one? Yes, we have been tracking you. Where did you come from? Hindustan? How did you get this diamond?' He said, 'What happened?' 'He has no children, no heirs, so all his land is being given to the poor.' So, this is the reward... this is the reward. This is the reward, this is the reward. The pension department people were standing there, and it is attractive. When you saw your old memories, we don't keep anyone's trust. So we... [Music]

content:
Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'My father (a.s.) made a will to me, saying: Preserve this supplication, pay special attention to its reverence—meaning it should be taught, and there should be an emphasis on reciting it. We should be aware of the importance of this supplication.' This is the will of the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat) for his son Imam Hussain (a.s.), and not just for him, but through him, for all of us. An important part of the reverence for this supplication is that we should participate when it is being recited. In the end, the Mawla willed, 'My father willed that I should write this supplication عَلَى كَفَنِهِ (on his shroud) وَأَنْ أُعَلِّمَهُ أَهْلِي (and that I should teach this supplication to my family), and that I should emphasize it to them.' title: Insaaniyyat ki Aakhri Ummeed: Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s)
excerpt: This lecture explores the universal belief across various religions in a future savior who will establish global justice. It highlights references to this figure in Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, Judaism, and Christianity, demonstrating a shared anticipation of an end-times redeemer. The speaker concludes by confirming that this savior is Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), whose mission is to fulfill the Divine promise of inheriting the earth for the righteous.
content:
Whether it is Divine Religion or human religion, in every religion, this belief is found: that in the end times, a savior will appear who will rescue the world. The savior of the world, the one who will fill this entire universe with justice, is mentioned in every religion. In Hinduism, there is a mention of the one who will come in the end times, called 'Kalki Avatar', who will ride a white horse and hold a sword in his hands, and after he comes, he will fill the world with justice just as it was filled with injustice. This is found in Hinduism. In Zoroastrianism, the Parsis, there is a place mentioned between 'Ahriman' and 'Yazdan' that in the end times, there will be a war between Ahriman and Yazdan, in which Ahriman will be defeated—in a way, Satan will be defeated. Satan will be defeated. Among the Parsis, the savior of the world, the one who will bring justice, is mentioned; his name is 'Soshyant'. According to them, Soshyant is the one who will benefit people and will bring about a revolution in the end times. If we come to Divine Religion, to Divine guidance, then in the Torah, they have left no stone unturned—the Jews, the Muslims, especially the followers of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)... The followers of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) have tried to erase the signs of the Prophet, but despite all their efforts, they could not erase the fact that someone will come in the end times who will fill the world with justice. The one who will be the savior of this entire universe, who will bring salvation. In the Torah, in the book of Isaiah, in the 11th chapter, it is mentioned that a person will establish a just government. He will awaken humanity. His way of life, his conduct, and his loyalty will be a way of loyalty. A strange thing is found there, in this part of the book, it is written that the wolf will live with the sheep, but it will not harm them. Although their shepherd will be a small child, when he is there, he will not harm the small child, nor will he harm the sheep. Such an environment will exist in the world; there will not be even an atom's worth of crime because the world will be filled with justice, just as it is written in that book, just as the sea is filled with water, just as the river is filled with water, the world will be filled with justice. Then, in the books of Prophet David (a.s.), which are called the Psalms, in the 37th Psalm, sentence 22, it is written that in the world... It is written that in the world, all the wicked and corrupt people will be eliminated. Then, in the same, sentence number 29, it is written that the righteous people will be the heirs of the world. And similarly, the Holy Quran has pointed to this: 'My righteous servants will inherit the earth.' This is the record of the scriptures. If we come to the Gospels, in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 24, it is written that the coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning flashing from the east to the west. That is how he will come. The first thing the one who comes will do is send his angels, call out from the heavens, and through them, he will gather his companions. This is written in the Gospel of Matthew. And similarly, in the Bible, in the Gospel of Luke, it is written that the coming of that person will be sudden, and his arrival will be sudden. This is to prepare oneself, to keep oneself ready, to make oneself such that when you present yourself before that coming one, when you offer yourself, that coming one will grant you salvation. This is written in all these books. If we reflect on all these things, what is the result? The result is that whether it is Divine religion or human religion, this... Whether it is Divine religion or human religion, the hope of this entire universe, rather the whole world, is attached to such a coming one who will fill the world with justice. This is the purpose, this is the great Divine mission for which Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) will appear, and the hopes of this world will be fulfilled. That is why the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'If there were only one day left in the end of the world, Allah would prolong that day until He sends a person from my progeny, whose name will be my name, whose character will be my character, and he will fill the earth with justice just as it was filled with injustice.'

title: EP2 | Do Prophets Leave An Inheritance? - Argument of H. Fatima (s.a.) | 🎙️ The #Fadak #Podcast
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical and legal controversy surrounding the seizure of Fadak from Lady Fatima (s.a.) following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It analyzes the conflicting interpretations of inheritance laws, contrasting the Quranic evidence of prophetic inheritance with the solitary hadith used to justify the confiscation of property. The discussion highlights the theological and jurisprudential arguments presented by Lady Fatima (s.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.), emphasizing the necessity of prioritizing Quranic principles over contradictory reports.
content:
We, the group of Prophets, are not inherited; whatever we leave behind is charity. So, what would be the answer to this? They refused to accept it. She (a.s.) said, 'Kitabullah' (It is the Book of Allah). It is the Book of Allah that is speaking, meaning I am speaking from the Book of Allah, and you are saying it is not as it is? To reject the Book of Allah is equivalent to rejecting the Book of Allah itself. What happened next? 'Fasaktu' (They fell silent). Those people became silent; they had no answer. There was no answer! Where could they find an answer when the proof of the Quran was presented before them? After that, how could they have an answer? Then the Princess (a.s.) said, 'Fallahtun' (It is before the eyes of Allah). Whatever you have done is before the eyes of Allah. Very soon, the oppressors will know to which side they will be turned. What will they get in their hands by turning back? Disgrace, distress, shame, and the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. Ehsan Bhai, opponents often raise this objection while quoting our Shia book, 'Kitab al-Kafi', which is the first of the 'Kutub al-Arba' (The Four Books) and is considered one of the most authentic books. They say that the sixth Imam, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), stated that indeed, the scholars are the heirs of the Prophets, because the Prophets do not leave behind dirhams or dinars, but they leave behind their sayings, the Hadith, as inheritance. So, whoever takes any one of them has certainly acquired a great share. So, has certainly acquired a great share. So, here it is clearly written that Prophets do not leave behind dirhams or dinars. Their inheritance is not dirhams or dinars. So, what is the answer to this? See, in this... A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytanir rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, wa sallallahu ala... Yes, viewers, in this 'Fadak Podcast' series, we are trying to have a detailed discussion on the issue of Fadak. In the previous episode, we learned about the importance and background of Fadak, where, by the command of Allah (SWT), the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had given this land to his daughter, Siddiqa Tahira Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.), as a gift (fay), and after which this land remained in the ownership of the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.), and during the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the right of possession was in the hands of the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.). And today is the second episode. Let us welcome our dear brother, Mr. Ehsan Jafri. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. As we learned in the previous episode, Fadak was the property of the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.). The right of possession was in the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) possession was in the hands of the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.) during the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Now the question arises, what happened to this land after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytanir rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu ala Fatima Zahra (s.a.)... As you asked, Ehsan Bhai, what happened to the land after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? Before moving to that, the most important thing here is what happened immediately after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Yes, the event of Saqifah happened immediately. That is, on one hand, the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has occurred, his funeral rites have not even been performed yet, and the Muslims gathered at Saqifah. The debate of the Caliphate broke out there. Those people thought—you see, this was their faith—on one side, the Prophet's funeral is kept, and here, in the Prophet's house, the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali a.s.) is present, the Ahlulbayt are present, and some close companions... are present. Some close companions, countable on the fingers, like Janab-e-Salman, Janab-e-Abu Dharr, etc. These are just a few individuals present. For them, what was most important at that time? The funeral rites of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Yes, they gave priority to that. On the other hand, those who gathered at Saqifah—this shows what their faith in the Prophet was like. Why did they gather at Saqifah? To choose a Caliph. Yes. This shows that the Prophet, who made Muslims aware of even the smallest things of Sharia—even how to cut nails, whether to apply kohl in the eyes or not, and even taught the etiquette of the restroom—but those who gathered at Saqifah, their belief is that if there was something the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not state before leaving this world, if he did not state who would be the Caliph after him, this is logically impossible. That is, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left the Ummah wandering? That is their belief. Rather, on the other side, what is it? On the other side, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and his companions, those who follow him, are completely satisfied with this matter. It never even crossed their minds that the issue of Caliphate would arise because there was no doubt in their minds. The Prophet had announced it repeatedly in his life. repeatedly announced it in his life. Even at the plain of Ghadir-e-Khumm, he announced who would be the Caliph after him. He raised the hand of the Commander of the Faithful and said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am the master, Ali is his master). So, these people are satisfied that Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is the successor, the Wasi, the Caliph, and the representative of the Prophet after him. Yes, that is why these people were busy with the most important responsibility at that time: the Prophet's funeral rites. While they were busy with that, on the other side, the Muslims went and gathered at Saqifah and did what they did. Now, when they gathered there through an election, or call it a selection—to this day, Muslims have not been able to decide what it was: an election, a selection, a consensus (ijma), what was it? All Muslims were not even gathered there. Despite that, it was given the name of 'consensus'. Anyway, I don't want to go into that debate right now. But what did those people do? They chose their Caliph there. When the Caliph was chosen there, they all came to Masjid al-Nabawi. There, their chosen Caliph is on the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) pulpit, and as a Caliph, he is on the throne of power. The first thing they did was that they removed the agents of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) who were sitting there in the land of Fadak, who... who were sitting there, the caretakers, yes, they had them removed and placed their own caretakers, and usurped the land of Fadak. They took it into their possession. That is, the thing that was until now in the possession of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), in her ownership, her ownership was snatched from her. Permission was not even taken from Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) that we are doing this. Without telling her, without her permission, their caretakers were removed from there, and their land was occupied. When Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) received this news, at that time, Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) did not consider it appropriate to remain silent. Exactly. And she immediately came, arrived at the court, and it is written in history how she came, taking some women of her family and some maids with her, and demanded Fadak in the court. She did not sit silent. She did not consider it appropriate to remain silent because now the issue was of the Princess's right. Therefore, where the issue of the Princess's right comes, silence cannot be maintained. Indeed, this is a lesson not only for the Princess but also for us. That is why, even today, if there is an issue regarding the Princess, raise your voice. Absolutely, one should not remain silent in that. You should speak with arguments. one should not remain silent in that. You should speak with arguments. There is no need to say anything from your own side. The arguments that are present in history, you present references through those arguments. You speak. Whoever wants to accept it will accept it. Whoever does not want to, will not. But at least we have fulfilled our responsibility. This should be our effort. On the Day of Judgment, we will be free of responsibility. We raised our voice for the Princess. We raised our voice for the Princess. Now the demand for Fadak began. The Princess (s.a.) delivered a long sermon. It is a detailed sermon. It is present in our books. That is, I don't want to go into the whole sermon right now; that is not the topic. If Allah gives the opportunity, a complete discussion can be held regarding that sermon as well. Its commentary is properly present in the books. Insha'Allah. When the Princess (s.a.) first demanded her right, that this land should be returned to me, the first thing those people put before the Princess (s.a.) was, 'Do you have any witnesses for this? Do you have any proof for this?' That is, on one side, first the right of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) was usurped—the Caliphate, which was his right, was snatched away through Saqifah—then after that, Fadak was snatched away, the right of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) was snatched. Who are these two personalities in that era? After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), there is no one more excellent than Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the Princess Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). Indeed, even discussing their virtues is a debate in itself—that is, bringing others in front of them, comparing them, is in itself, if seen, underestimating their virtues. Exactly. Yes, a good question, but not a new question. This same question was also placed before the sixth Imam, Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). It was asked of him too. Abu Basir came to the service of the Imam and presented this question. Abu Basir himself narrates, and this is present in Kitab al-Ihtijaj, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) has brought it in chapter number 124: 'Ba'da ma amira al-Mu'minin (a.s.) Fadaka lamma waliya al-nas' (After Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) became the apparent caliph of the people, what was the reason he did not take back Fadak and left it? Why didn't he take Fadak into his possession at that time?). Yes. So Abu Basir came to Imam Sadiq (a.s.) with this question, asking the same thing: 'Li ayyi shay'in' (For what reason)? What was the reason that Amir al-Mu'minin abandoned it? So in response to this, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'Lamma yajtama'u al-zalimu wa al-mazlumu' (When the oppressor and the oppressed will have to come before Allah on the Day of Judgment). Yes, both will come. 'Wa yas'alu Allahu al-mazluma wa yu'aqibu al-zalima' (And Allah will ask the oppressed and punish the oppressor). What will Allah do with both of them at that time? He will reward the oppressed one because he was oppressed and he remained patient in the face of oppression; therefore, Allah will give the reward to that oppressed person. And what will He do with the oppressor? He will subject him to punishment. He will punish him. Then the Imam says, 'The Mawla (Ali a.s.) felt aversion to this, to taking back that thing, because of the fact that if it were taken back, the punishment of the oppressor who committed the oppression would be reduced even slightly.' That is, it should not happen that if it were taken back, the punishment would be averted from the oppressor, and the one whose right was usurped would not get the reward. So, because of this, the oppressor will remain an oppressor until the Day of Judgment. Indeed, as long as that thing is in the possession of the oppressor, he will remain an oppressor. Until he realizes this, until he feels remorse for his oppression and does not return the right to the oppressed, he will remain an oppressor. And if he leaves this world in that state, he will rise from the world as an oppressor; he will be raised as an oppressor on the Day of Judgment, and the oppressed will be raised as the oppressed. Therefore, Allah will reward the oppressed and punish the oppressor—that is, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). That is, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) knew that whether he received his right in this world or not, on the Day of Judgment—the day of justice—he would definitely receive his right. He would definitely receive his right. And all these arguments and objections that are presented, we can answer them all. But ultimately, if a person's intellect does not open even then, what can be done? This is why Muslims are still ashamed today regarding the usurpation of the right of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.), and they will remain ashamed until the Day of Judgment. Indeed, as long as they continue to support those oppressors, they will remain ashamed. And not only ashamed, but they will continue to be disgraced throughout the world. Do you know why the condition of Muslims is like this today? Because in that very Sermon of Fadak, the long sermon that Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) delivered, she invoked a curse against those oppressors. And in what words did she curse? The Princess says, 'What is left for you people? In what state will you remain? For you, there is only disgrace, only shame. May the wrath of Allah be upon you.' The wrath of Allah has been written on your foreheads; this mark has been placed on your foreheads, this seal has been stamped that Allah is angry with you. And forever... Allah is angry with you. And there is eternal regret. You will continue to be humiliated and disgraced. Why are the conditions of Muslims like this today? Because they usurped the right of the Princess (s.a.w.a.) and are still supporting those usurpers today. This is the Princess's curse. This is its effect. Yes. Then the Princess says, quoting a verse of Surah, quoting the Quran: 'Al-lati tattali'u'—that is, the fire that will reach them. Which fire? The fire that is from Allah, the fire that Allah has prepared, 'Narullahil-muqada, allati tattali'u 'alal-af'idah'—the fire that completely surrounds the hearts, that is, it will burn the hearts. That fire will completely burn the person's personality. Then the Princess says, 'And Allah is watching what you do.' Everything you have done is before the eyes of Allah. 'And soon the wrongdoers will know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.' That is, what will they get in their hands when they are turned back? Disgrace, regret, shame, and the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. That is, I want to conclude my point by saying one last thing: many people today, and in every era, talk about supporting the oppressed. Indeed, it is a good thing for a person to support the oppressed. But if a person has supported every oppressed person in the world... If a person has supported every oppressed person in the world but has not defended the right of the Princess (s.a.w.a.), on the Day of Judgment, he will find himself standing in the list of those very oppressors. Indeed, the litmus test for supporting the oppressed is the defense of the Princess's right. If he is not defending this, then even if he defends every oppressed person in the world, he will get nothing on the Day of Judgment. On the Day of Judgment, he will be counted among the oppressors. So, she is the greatest oppressed one; defending her right is the litmus test. Yes, absolutely. Viewers, in today's episode, we saw the hadith that was misused to deprive the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.w.a.) of her right. It is not only fabricated but also contrary to the Holy Quran itself. Those who claimed that 'the Book of Allah is sufficient' (Hasbuna Kitabullah) were the same people bringing a hadith against the teachings of that very Book. On one side was the Book of God, and on the other, they were bringing a hadith that was against the realities of the Quran. This clearly shows that a hadith that is against the teachings of the Quran is not acceptable. So, when that hadith itself is not acceptable, how can the seizure of the land of Fadak using it be justified? With this, we conclude this discussion here and will meet you again in this series of The Fadak Podcast. We will meet in the final episode of this series of The Fadak Podcast. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

chapters.title: Saqifah and the Usurpation of Fadak

chapters.title: Fatima's (s.a.) Demand for Justice
chapters.summary: Lady Fatima (s.a.) challenged the usurpation of her property, emphasizing the importance of speaking out against injustice and presenting historical arguments for her rights.

chapters.title: The Rejection of Witnesses and the Inheritance Hadith
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how the testimonies of Lady Fatima (s.a.) and her witnesses were rejected, and introduces the controversial Hadith used to deny her inheritance.

chapters.title: Sheikh Mufid's Grammatical Refutation
chapters.summary: Sheikh Mufid (r.a.) uses Arabic grammar to challenge the interpretation of the inheritance Hadith, arguing that the word 'Sadaqah' should be read with a Fatha to change the meaning.

chapters.title: Lady Fatima's (s.a.) Protest and Anger
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights that Lady Fatima (s.a.) rejected the Hadith presented against her, citing historical accounts from Sunni sources that confirm her anger as a reaction to this injustice.

chapters.title: Conflicting Interpretations of the Hadith
chapters.summary: The lecture examines the disagreement between Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and Abu Bakr regarding the interpretation of the Prophet's statement on inheritance, noting that they held fundamentally opposing views.

chapters.title: Quranic Evidence vs. Khabar-e-Wahid
chapters.summary: Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and Janabe Zahra (s.a.) presented Quranic verses to challenge the claim that Prophets do not leave inheritance, contrasting these verses with the isolated narration provided by the Caliph.

chapters.title: The Silence of the Opponents
chapters.summary: When confronted with clear Quranic evidence regarding the inheritance of Prophets like Dawud (a.s.) and Zakariya (a.s.), the opponents were unable to provide a satisfactory response and chose to remain silent.

chapters.title: Refuting Objections on Quranic Inheritance
chapters.summary: The speaker addresses the objection that inheritance refers only to knowledge, using Quranic verses to demonstrate that Prophets inherited physical authority and kingdom as well.

chapters.title: Refuting the Misuse of Hadith Regarding Inheritance

chapters.summary: The speaker explains the spiritual consequences of usurping the rights of Lady Fatima (s.a.) and references Quranic warnings regarding divine punishment.

chapters.title: Defending Fatima (s.a.) as a Litmus Test
