title: EP18 | Hadees-e-Saqalain Aur Ahle Tasannun Ki Kitaabein Part 2 | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines the Hadith al-Thaqalayn through the lens of prominent Sunni scholarly sources, specifically Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The discussion focuses on the linguistic and theological definition of Ahlulbayt, clarifying that it excludes the Prophet's wives and refers to the specific families for whom charity is forbidden. By analyzing the reliability of narrators and the context of the Prophet's warnings, the lecture establishes the inseparability of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt as a foundational directive for the Ummah.
content:
Presenting the teaser. [Music] [Applause] [Music] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family. The discussion was about Fadak, and in your service, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said many times, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things, two caliphs, two successors: the Book of Allah and my Itrat, my Ahl-e-Bayt. As long as you hold onto them firmly, as long as you do not let go of their hem, you will never go astray after me.' You will never go astray after me because these two will not separate from each other until they meet me at the Pond (Kawthar). Now, I will present two or three references from authentic books in your service, and then the results. Regarding Hadith al-Thaqalayn, as I mentioned the names of the books in the previous episode, those were brief books, not all books, and not all narrators' names, just brief book names. There are many more books than this. But still, today, the book from which we are selecting the hadith and discussing it is Sahih Muslim. The author's name is Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi. He is a very great scholar of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, and as I mentioned in the previous episode, his book is considered authentic and is considered the most authentic book after Bukhari. Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are called 'Sahihayn', and if something is in the Sahihayn, it is considered authentic. There are other authentic things too, but in that, look at Hadith number 2408. In 2408, see, the hadith is like this: Yazid ibn Hayyan says that 'I, Husayn, and Saburah—we three individuals went to Zayd ibn Arqam, who is a companion of the Messenger.' When we sat with him, Husayn and Saburah said, 'O Zayd, you have received much good, much good.' Look, we are reading from Sahih Muslim; this is not a Shia book, remember. 'Zayd, you have received much good, much good.' They say, 'You have received much good, you are very lucky, your luck is very good.' Now after this, they say, 'Tell us, O Zayd, tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' Now look, they did not demand any specific hadith, that 'tell this hadith' or 'tell that hadith'. No, whatever hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah, tell it. So now Zayd ibn Arqam, because the situation was not good in that era, the situation was very bad, but Zayd ibn Arqam was a companion of the Messenger, he had some respect, some honor. So he said, 'O my nephew'—this is a way of speaking—'O nephew, by God, I have become old, very old, and my time has passed, or my death is near, you can say it like this, and I have forgotten some of the things I heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). I have forgotten most of the things. I have forgotten many things. So now what I...' I have forgotten many things. So now what I... I have forgotten the Famas, but now, whatever Hadith I narrate to you, accept it, and that which I do not narrate, do not force me or insist upon me. If I do not speak, or if you ask me to narrate the virtues of others—Zayd knew that if he said this, they would say that, and if he said that, they would ask for more—Zayd understood this beforehand. So, Zayd then said, 'I am narrating this Hadith.' Zayd is narrating the Hadith: 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stood among us one day to deliver a sermon (khutbah) near a pond named Khumm, which is located between Makkah and Madinah.' He is describing the event of Hajjat al-Wada (the Farewell Pilgrimage), which is the event of Ghadir. Zayd ibn Arqam is narrating this, and after that, he says, 'The Prophet praised Allah...' After that, he says, 'The Prophet praised Allah and glorified Him, and then the Prophet exhorted the people and gave them many pieces of advice.' Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Amma ba'd (to proceed), O people, know—'Ala' is a particle used to draw attention—'know that I am a human being like you. It is near that a messenger from my Lord will come to me, and I will respond to his call.' He is referring to the Angel of Death, and he says, 'I will say Labbayk (I am present) to the invitation of that angel,' meaning soon I will depart from this world... Meaning soon I will depart from this world. I am leaving, I am departing from among you. The Prophet is saying goodbye. This is the Prophet's last Hajj, which is called Hajjat al-Wada in Urdu and Arabic. I am reading to you the exact Hadith from Sahih Muslim: 'And I am leaving among you two weighty things (thaqalayn).' Why are they called 'weighty'? The scholars of Arabic literature, the masters of the language, say that they call something 'weighty' when it is very precious. And here, they are called precious because taking them, acting upon them, and holding fast to them is very difficult; that is why they are called precious. And holding fast to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt is difficult and very precious. 'Among you are two weighty things: the first is the Book of Allah, in which there is guidance and light.' In it, there is guidance and light. 'So take the Book of Allah and hold fast to it.' Then the Prophet encouraged the people to hold onto the Book of Allah, urging them to read it and understand it, and he drew people toward it, saying, 'Come close to the Book of Allah.' Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'And my Ahlulbayt. I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt. Be mindful of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt; fear Allah in how you treat my Ahlulbayt.' Muslim recorded this sentence from Zayd ibn Arqam, saying that the Prophet... Zayd said that the Prophet repeated this sentence three times. In Arabic, to emphasize something, twice is sufficient. For example, if you say 'Allah, Allah,' it is enough, or you are emphasizing Allah. But if you say it three times, it means this matter is of extreme importance. 'I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt; see that you take care of my Ahlulbayt.' Insha'Allah, there will be further discussion on this. Then Husayn asked, Husayn ibn Sabra asked, 'And who are his Ahlulbayt, O Zayd? Who are his Ahlulbayt?' Are his wives not from his Ahlulbayt? So Zayd said, 'The wives are generally counted among the Ahlulbayt, but here, in this Hadith, Ahlulbayt refers to...' But here, in this Hadith, Ahlulbayt refers to those upon whom charity (Sadaqah) is forbidden. Then Husayn asked, 'And who are they?' So Zayd ibn Arqam said, 'They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Ja'far, and the family of Abbas,' meaning the descendants of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Aqeel ibn Abi Talib, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib. Charity is forbidden for all their descendants; they are all Ahlulbayt. Then Husayn asked, 'Is charity forbidden for all of them?' Zayd said, 'Yes, charity is forbidden for all of them.' This is a clear Hadith for you from Sahih Muslim. Immediately after this, Hadith number 2408, Muslim records another Hadith, the same Hadith, and in it, it says that Husayn asked Zayd, 'Are his wives from his Ahlulbayt?' And Zayd replied, 'No, his wives are not.' No, his wives are not. Wives are not from the Ahlulbayt. That was Zayd's answer. Why? Zayd also presents the evidence for it: A woman stays with her husband as long as she is in his marriage. When he divorces her, she returns to her father's house, she returns to her tribe. So, when we analyze and reconcile these two Hadiths, it becomes clear that the wives are not included. Both of these are narrations from Sahih Muslim, one immediately after the other. Now, it is possible that, as you know, some people immediately say the Hadith is 'da'if' (weak). However, it is a narration of Sahih Muslim; how can they call it weak? Who called it weak? Ibn al-Jawzi said the Hadith is weak, that this Hadith is not authentic. Why? Yahya ibn Ma'in said, a man said this Hadith is weak. We will present the evidence for that, Insha'Allah, but for now, I am just mentioning who the narrators are. Who is the narrator of this Hadith? Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri. We don't need to go into the details, just know about Sa'id ibn Masruq that the experts of the Ahlul-Sunnah in Rijal (biography of narrators), the greatest of them is Dhahabi... Dhahabi has written many books on Rijal, for example, Mizan al-I'tidal is his, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib is his, Al-Ibar is his, Al-Kashif is his. These are all his books on Rijal, and Siyar A'lam al-Nubala is his. Dhahabi has written so many books on Rijal. So Dhahabi is an expert, a tremendous one; he is counted among the top-most, there is no greater expert in Rijal than him. So he writes in his book 'Al-Kashif', which is about the scholars of Rijal, in Volume 1, page 272, that Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri narrated from Abu Wa'il and Sha'bi, and Sa'id ibn Masruq had two sons who narrated from Sa'id, and Abu Awana narrated from Sa'id. And then Dhahabi writes that he was 'Thiqah' (reliable), he was authentic, and he passed away in the year 126 Hijri. And after that, another great scholar of Rijal of the Ahlul-Sunnah, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, a very great personality, he also wrote a book on Rijal, 'Tahdhib al-Tahdhib', in which in Volume 4, page 82, he writes—Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani is different from Ibn Hajar al-Makki. Ibn Hajar al-Makki was from the 10th century; Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani was from the 9th century. So Ibn Hajar writes that Ibn Ma'in (Yahya ibn Ma'in), Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, Abu Hatim, Ijli, and Nasa'i, all of them considered Sa'id to be 'Thiqah'. According to all of them, Sa'id is Thiqah, reliable, meaning his Hadith is authentic. And a very great scholar of the Ahlul-Sunnah named Ibn Hibban—Ibn Hibban wrote a book 'Al-Thiqat', meaning a list of all the reliable narrators—Ibn Hibban, remember the name, Ibn Hibban, the book's name 'Al-Thiqat'—he says that Ibn Hibban mentioned Sa'id in 'Al-Thiqat', that Sa'id is authentic. When he described the biography of Sa'id, Ibn Hibban wrote that Sa'id passed away in the year 128 Hijri (meaning according to Sha'bi it was 126 Hijri, according to Ibn Hibban it was 128). Regardless, and Ibn Khalaf stated his reliability... And Ibn Khalaf stated his reliability. So this is one narration. Now let's read the second Hadith so that the matter becomes clear. The Hadith of Thaqalayn, from whom is this narration? From Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Ahmad ibn Hanbal is the Imam of the Hanbalis, a very great scholar. In his Musnad, he records the narration that Atiyyah al-Awfi narrated. He says that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated this. Look, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, Sulayman Mehran al-A'mash narrated it; he also passed away in 148 Hijri, he is also among the reliable ones. Okay, Atiyyah al-Awfi, both are reliable, and the book is Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad is clear, right? So he says Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said that the Prophet said, 'I am about to be called, and I will respond to the invitation,' meaning the Lord will tell me to come back and I will go, meaning my death. And then after that, he said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' I am leaving behind two things: the Book of Allah (Azza wa Jalla) and my Itrah, my Ahlulbayt. Here, he did not say 'Ahlulbayt' initially, it came later. 'Kitabullah hablum mamdud minas-sama'i ilal-ard' (The Book of Allah is a rope extended from the heavens to the earth). After that, he says, 'wa itrati' (and my Itrah). And who is my Itrah? Who are my Ahlulbayt? In this very hadith, he has clarified: 'my Ahlulbayt'. 'Wa latifal-khabiru akhbarani' (And the Subtle, the All-Aware has informed me). Allah has informed me and told me that these two will never separate from each other until they reach me at the Hawd al-Kawthar. Until they come to me. Now, after that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Fanzuru bima takhlufuni' (So look at how you treat them after me). 'Fanzuru'—look at me, take care of me, watch how you treat them after I am gone. Why did the Prophet say this? What was the reason? The Prophet knew that after him... What was the reason? The Prophet knew what was going to happen after him, which is why the Prophet emphasized this. And this is not just one narration, but many narrations like this. Insha'Allah, this is the concept of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, which I have presented to you. I mentioned the names of the books in the previous episode. Today, I presented the hadith from two important books. After this, Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the ability and life, then in the next episode, we will continue with the Hadith al-Thaqalayn...
Hadith al-Thaqalayn is verified within Sahih Muslim, confirming its high status in Sunni tradition.

excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual connection between the faithful and the Ahlulbayt, focusing on the significance of mourning for Imam Hussain. It delves into the occultation of the Imam of the Time, emphasizing that true waiting requires personal piety, spiritual preparation, and a deep understanding of the Imam's presence. The discourse also examines the exclusive divine titles of Imam Ali, the nature of the Ahlulbayt as the signs of Allah, and the eternal impact of the tragedy of Karbala.

It took a long time to build the grave of Sarwar, it took a long time to hide a moon. The grave of Sarwar... The Shah (Hussain) picked up every corpse quickly, but it took a long time to pick up every corpse of Akbar. The grave of Sarwar... Picking up the pieces of Qasim, the Master said, 'Alas, it took a long time to come.' The grave of Sarwar... The throat of Sarwar was so dry from thirst, the throat of Sarwar was so dry from thirst, oh, it took a long time for Shimr to swing the sword. The grave of Sarwar... The body of Asghar, the body of Asghar was hidden quickly by the Shah, but it took a long time to hide the face of Asghar. It is a few steps away from the bazaar to the court, yet it took a long time for the princess to come. It took a long time to build the grave of Sarwar. And Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. May Allah have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best disposer of affairs, the best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the people of piety and certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance. Blessings be upon his infallible family from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our guardian, our master, our leader, our beloved, our physician, our companion, and our confidant. The helper of the distressed and the succor of the seeker of the straight path, may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our master and leader Ali ibn Musa ar-Rida (a.s.) said, "Indeed, the day of Hussain has wounded our eyelids and caused our tears to flow, so let the weepers weep for the likes of Hussain." Our master and leader Ali ibn Musa ar-Rida (a.s.) spoke the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance. The Hadith that has been chosen for this series of gatherings, in that noble Hadith, Imam Rida (a.s.) says, "Indeed, the day of Hussain has wounded our eyelids." Certainly, the day of Hussain, meaning the grief of Hussain, has wounded our eyelids. 'Akraha jufunana', meaning when a wound becomes so severe that blood flows from it, it is called 'karh' in Arabic. 'Akraha', it has wounded it so much; by weeping continuously, the Imam's eyes have become wounded. 'Wa asbala dumunana', and tears are flowing from them continuously. "So let the weepers weep for the likes of Hussain." If anyone wants to weep, they should weep for Hussain. There are many narrations in this regard. If anyone wants to refer to this, the name of the book is 'Kamil al-Ziyarat', which is by the late Ibn Qulawayh. The late Ibn Qulawayh was among the friends of Sheikh al-Kulayni, and also among his students, and he was one of the teachers of Sheikh al-Saduq. His grave is in Kadhimiya, right next to the grave of Sheikh al-Mufid, they are both together. The name of the book is 'Kamil al-Ziyarat', and because the book has been translated into English and Urdu, the original book was in Arabic, and it is also in Persian. So, I request the youth to definitely read that book; it is also available online. Download it, read it, and see how important it is, how much emphasis has been placed on weeping for the Master of Martyrs. It is mentioned in supplications, it is in Hadiths, and it is mentioned in the exegesis of verses. Especially the first verse of Surah Maryam, the disjointed letters (Huruf-e-Muqatta'at), that 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim, Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ain-Sad'. This is also related to Karbala; 'Kaf' stands for Karbala. So, please refer to the whole thing, Insha'Allah, it is of great importance. Anyway, our discussion was about the Hadith-e-Ma'rifat-e-Nuraniya, and the matter reached the point where Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says, "Ya Salman wa-ya Jundab, qala labbayk ya Amirul-Mu'minin, qala inna mayyitana lam yamut." Those of us who die, do not actually die. This is what was explained to you yesterday. After that, he says, "Wa-ghaibana lam yaghib." And those of us who go into occultation (ghaybah), do not actually go into occultation. They do not actually go into occultation. See, I will present two proofs for this before we move forward, Insha'Allah. One proof is in Dua-e-Nudba: "Bi-nafsi anta min mughayyabin lam yakhlu minna." This is a sentence from Dua-e-Nudba. "Bi-nafsi anta," may my life be sacrificed for you. Who is being addressed? It is an address to Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa-ali Muhammad wa-ajjil farajahum. "Bi-nafsi anta min mughayyabin lam yakhlu minna." May my life be sacrificed for you, the one who is 'mughayyab', meaning the one who has been hidden, but "lam yakhlu minna," in reality, he is present among us. This is a sentence from Dua-e-Nudba, and this sentence is from Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.) himself, "wa-nahnu ma'ahu." The Imam himself is saying, "Bi-nafsi anta min mughayyabin lam yakhlu minna." Meaning, the Imam wants to say in Dua-e-Nudba that I am present among you. And there are many such traditions that contain the definition of ghaybah, and in those definitions, it is present that the Mahdi will participate in your gatherings, will come to your carpets (majalis), will come to your mourning carpets—well, the word 'aza' is not there, but he will come to your carpets, will be in your markets, will be among you; it is present in the traditions. Now, the only problem is from our side, and that problem is that our habits, our eyes are so accustomed to sinning that they are deprived of the Ziyarat of the Imam. They are deprived of the recognition of the Imam. They are deprived of the Ma'rifat of the Imam. That is why, look at the famous hadith of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), which he said to Abu Khalid al-Kabuli: "Ya Aba Khalid, inna ahla zaman-e-ghaybatihi al-qa'ilina bi-imamathi, al-muntazirina li-zuhuri, afdalu ahli kulli zaman." O Abu Khalid, those people who will be in the time of his ghaybah, who believe in his Imamate, and along with that, wait for his reappearance—the Imam mentioned two conditions. Two conditions. What is the first condition? To believe in the Imamate. The second condition? To wait for the reappearance. If these two conditions are found in someone, the Imam says, "Afdalu ahli kulli zaman." They are better than the people of every era. And why? The Imam presents the proof for it. See, often in our traditions, the Imams (a.s.) have presented proofs so that the matter should be completely clear for the people. The Imam says, "Li-annallaha ta'ala," because Allah (s.w.t.), "atahum," Allah has granted them. What has He given? "Minal-uqul," firstly, the intellect, He has blessed them with the light of intellect. Meaning, Allah protects their light of intellect, there is grace, there is divine confirmation and divine bestowal of the light of intellect. Allah gives the light of intellect, "Li-annallaha ta'ala atahum minal-uqul," one. Secondly, "wa-al-afham," and not just intellect, He also gave understanding (fahm). Understanding is the second stage, the stage after intellect. Meaning, Allah gives the intellect, but when a person contemplates in the light of the intellect, thinks about something, and then analyzes it, that is called 'fahm'. Meaning, to understand something. 'Fahm' means to understand something. Allah has given them understanding. Meaning, they understand every single thing. If you have been listening to the majalis from the beginning, then see, it was submitted to you that a Momin is one who is a person of insight (basirat). Allah grants him insight. What is the Momin? "Yanzuru bi-nur-illah," he sees with the light of Allah. Now, the Imam is repeating the same thing here in different words. Allah gives him intellect, gives him understanding, "minal-afham," and ma'rifat. And the third thing that Allah gives is Ma'rifat. So there are three things. Meaning, those who are in the time of the Imam's ghaybah, who believe in the Imamate of Imam-e-Zamana, and are truly, seriously waiting for the Imam's reappearance. Not just verbally, but truly waiting for the Imam's reappearance. This itself is a discussion: how is the reappearance of the Imam awaited? Not just by waiting verbally. Rather, a person should try to pave the way for the reappearance. First, prepare oneself, then one's family, and then one's relatives and society. As much as possible, a person is not responsible for anyone other than himself. He is responsible only for himself, that's all. Even not for his brother or his wife, not even his parents. He is responsible only for himself, that's all. But he tries as much as possible to prepare the ground. To bring people closer to the Imam. To defend the belief of Imamate. To tell people, look, this is the actual Imamate. To introduce Imam-e-Zamana, to make him known. This is how the ground is paved. Pray. Pray as much as possible. So, if these two qualities are found in someone—one, that he believes in the Imamate, and two, that he waits for the reappearance—then Allah gives him three things: one, intellect; second, understanding; and third, ma'rifat. When these conditions are fulfilled, when Allah gives him these three things, then the Imam says—these are the words of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.)—that the Imam says, "Ma sarat bihi al-ghaybatu 'indahum bi-manzilati al-mushahadah." Now, for these people in whom these three things are found, there is no difference between ghaybah and witnessing (mushahadah), meaning seeing the Imam. No difference. For them, the Imam is not hidden at all. The Imam is hidden for others, not for them. Meaning, they are so close to their Imam. And such personalities have passed in history. Although they did not do propaganda, did not announce that yes, we met, we met here yesterday, we met there yesterday; they did not do all this. But those personalities exist. Among them, the best personality, the famous personality, is Sayyid ibn Tawus. We introduced Sayyid ibn Tawus a few days ago, that Sayyid ibn Tawus was his title, Ali was his name. He was a very great personality, also the grandson of Shaykh Tusi. And he was a very big name, Sayyid ibn Tawus. The family of Ale-Tawus has served the religion and Shi'ism greatly. We cannot even imagine. He was a very great Marja, a religious authority in his time. He passed away in 664 Hijri. 664 Hijri, meaning he was a scholar of the seventh century. He was so close to Imam-e-Zamana, so close to Imam-e-Zamana, and he used to tell everyone to be close to the Imam, to go near the Imam, to come close to the Imam. So much so that it is written about him that he even had the honor of meeting him, Sayyid ibn Tawus was blessed with a meeting. Anyway, people say about him that he was so close to the Imam that he was familiar with the fragrance of the Imam. That in whichever gathering or majlis the Imam came, Sayyid ibn Tawus knew that the Imam was present in this gathering. He is a very great personality, we cannot even imagine. He also did a lot of work, wrote many books, did a lot of work. And the other thing is that in the background of history, in the time when the Mongols attacked Iraq, the way Khwaja Nasir al-Tusi and Sayyid ibn Tawus together saved the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias is a very big thing. We cannot imagine. Anyway, that is a separate historical incident, I don't have to narrate that now. So these two things, the Imam says, "Ma sarat bihi al-ghaybatu 'indahum bi-manzilati al-mushahadah." The Imam says for them, the Imam's ghaybah is not ghaybah. It is like witnessing, as if they are meeting the Imam. Because they have these three things. Then the Imam says, "Ula'ika al-mu'minuna haqqan." These are the true Momins. These people are true Momins. Just by calling someone a Momin, one does not become a Momin. The Imam says, these are true Momins. "Wa-shi'atuna sidqan." And these are our true Shias. These are truly Shias, true Shias. "Wa-al-du'atu ila dinillahi sirran wa-jahran." And these are the individuals who continuously invite people to the religion. They invite to the religion, call to the religion, that come to the religion, become pious, become people of religion. Do not lose the religion from your hands. Do not get colored in the colors of the environment. Do not get colored in the colors of society. A lot happens in society; nowadays, many youths have started drinking alcohol. Many youths are committing immorality, vice is very common. Alcohol is also common. And this is not about outsiders. Meaning, taking drugs, alcohol, drinking alcohol, and all these things, all this is haram. It is in the tradition, "Kullu muskirin haram," every intoxicant, everything that causes intoxication is haram. And whoever consumes intoxicants, whether he drinks alcohol or takes drugs, anyone, whatever it is, however the intoxication is, then that person cannot be close to his Imam, it is impossible. It is impossible. If, God forbid, someone has such an addiction, then he should continuously pray to his Imam that Mawla, you yourself remove this addiction. He should pray to his Imam. He sees the event of Karbala with his own eyes. He sees it; he sees every scene himself. The Imam himself sees every stage of the tragedies. He sees it with his own eyes, repeatedly. He keeps weeping. O oppressed grandfather. You must read Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah. Reflect on the phrases of Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, where Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) mentions the honor of the Ahlulbayt. That the tragedy of Husayn was so severe that the honor of Imam Husayn—meaning the women of his household—came out without their veils. These phrases are present in the Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah. Imam Husayn (a.s.) is watching each one being martyred, watching each one before his own eyes. Until the scene comes where, standing in the desert of Karbala, the son of Fatima calls out: 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna? Hal min mugithin yugithuna?' (Is there any helper to help us? Is there any rescuer to rescue us?) Is there anyone to give us refuge? And if you hear the third sentence, your heart will break: 'Hal min zabbin yazubbu 'an harami Rasulillah?' (Is there anyone who will defend the harem of the Messenger of Allah? Is there anyone who will take care of the honor of the Messenger of Allah?) Is there anyone? No one answered, but a commotion broke out in the tents. Husayn came to the door of the tent. 'Sister Zaynab, what is this commotion?' She said, 'Brother, you raised the call for help, and Asghar threw himself out of the cradle.' Husayn said, 'Zaynab, bring Asghar to me.' She said, 'Brother, he does not go into anyone's lap; you come yourself.' Husayn came into the tent. Now, I don't know what Husayn said, what the father said, and what the son understood. But in the Maqtal, it is only written that as soon as Husayn whispered something into Asghar's ear, Asghar eagerly came into his father's lap. Husayn took Asghar. Now, as he started to walk, the mother was standing at the door of the tent. Rubab was standing there. Rubab, why are you standing here? She said, 'I am watching; whoever has gone since morning has not returned alive. So, my heart desires to see my beloved one last time. To see the light of my eyes one last time.' Husayn comforted her, saying, 'Rubab, whoever has gone to the battlefield so far, the wicked ones thought he came to fight. That is why they killed him, martyred him. But six-month-old babies don't do Jihad, they don't fight. I am taking him; perhaps the tyrants will have mercy and give my six-month-old baby some water.' A mother's heart is a mother's heart. It is written in the Maqtal that Husayn brought Ali Asghar and, after reaching an elevated place, called out: 'Ama fikum muslim?' (Is there no Muslim among you?) Islam commands that the thirsty be given water. No one answered. Husayn raised his voice a second time: 'If you are not Muslims, then is there no one among you who is a parent?' 'My child has been thirsty for three days.' 'Ama tarauna kayfa yatalazza?' (Do you not see how he is writhing?) He opens and closes his mouth like a fish, opens and closes his mouth. This state of thirst is called 'tatalazza'. 'Ama tarauna kayfa yatalazza?' No one answered. It was just that the army of the enemy was on the verge of a revolution. It was just that Ibn Sa'd called out: 'Ayna, ayna Hurmala?' Hurmala the accursed came forward. He said, 'Iqta' kalamal Husayn' (Cut off Husayn's speech, stop it). Hurmala took an arrow, took a bow. It was a three-headed arrow. It was a three-headed arrow, used for hunting large animals. Hurmala took aim. He aimed at Ali Asghar's throat. The arrow came and pierced Ali Asghar's throat. The child turned. It is written in the Maqtal that the arrow went through Ali Asghar's throat from one side and came out the other, and pierced Husayn's arm as well. Now, when Husayn looked down, the child was smiling. 'Father, do not be worried.' Husayn started walking with Ali Asghar. Offer your condolences. The last nights of the first ten days of Muharram, the gathering is approaching, Ashura is near. Offer condolences to Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Offer condolences to Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Offer condolences to the Infallible Imams (a.s.). Offer condolences to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Condolences for the tears, condolences for the lamentation and wailing. Husayn is carrying Ali Asghar in his arms. Now Husayn goes towards the tents. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' He walks a few steps and stops, thinking, 'How can I show this to the mother now? How will the mother bear it? How will the mother be able to bear it?' Thinking this, Husayn takes a step back. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' Husayn does this seven times. Finally, he stops and thinks, 'The child has left this world now, so why should the mother be deprived of a final glimpse?' Thinking this, Husayn comes and stands at the door of the tent. He stands at the door of the tent for a while. He calls out once: 'Rubab!' Now, it is written in the Maqtal that as soon as Husayn gave this call, Rubab came from one side, and Sakina came from the other. But Sakina came first and started saying, 'Father, did my brother drink water? Now my brother is not thirsty, right?' Sakina was asking, and then Rubab arrived. As soon as Rubab arrived, Husayn did not have the strength to say anything with his tongue. He just pulled back the edge of his cloak. Now, when Rubab saw the scene—the six-month-old baby with the arrow pierced in his throat—Rubab slapped her face. She recited a dirge: 'Ya bunayya! Abaka mislaka la yanhaya.' Allah! O my son! Are children like you also slaughtered? Wa sayalamu-lladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Ala la'natullahi 'alal-qawmiz-zalimin. O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain (a.s.). Count us all among his helpers and supporters. O Lord! Relieve the troubles of those who are distressed. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant those who have no children, righteous and virtuous offspring. Grant those who are ill, complete and swift recovery. Return those who are far from their homeland, safe and sound. Decree the release of those who are in prison. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the scholars of the world and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) in the hereafter. Accept this small act of Azadari of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Hadees Samajh Mein Na Aaye To Kya Karein?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the proper approach when encountering a Hadith from the Progeny of the Prophet (a.s.) that is difficult to understand or accept. The speaker emphasizes that one should not immediately reject or label such narrations as false simply due to a lack of personal comprehension. Instead, believers are encouraged to withhold judgment and refer the matter back to Allah, the Prophet, and the Imams, as premature denial can lead to spiritual destruction.
content:
When a hadith of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) comes before you, or any saying, فَلَانَتْ لَهُ قُلُوبُهُمْ (and your hearts soften towards it), وَعَرَفْتُمُوهُ (and you understand it), فَاقْبَلُوهُ (then accept it). But if there is a hadith that makes you nervous or that you cannot understand, then it is permissible to withhold judgment. Just because we do not understand it, we should not say, 'This hadith is not authentic, this hadith is wrong.' فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ (Refer this hadith, leave it to whom?) To Allah, to His Messenger, وَإِلَى الْعَالِمِ مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ (and leave it to the Scholar from the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.)). وَإِنَّمَا الْهَالِكُ أَنْ يُحَدِّثَ أَحَدُكُمْ بِالشَّيْءِ مِنْهُ لَا يَحْتَمِلُهُ (And indeed, the destruction lies in one of you being told something from it that he cannot bear). Look, any one of you—this point is important, understand this key—if a hadith is narrated to you and you do not understand it, you cannot digest it, you cannot bear it, فَيَقُولُ: وَاللَّهِ مَا كَانَ هَذَا (then you say: 'By God, this is not so,' this hadith is not correct). وَالْإِنْكَارُ هُوَ الْكُفْرُ (And denial is disbelief). This is a very important point: we do not have the right, if something is not within our understanding—we haven't heard it until today, we haven't read it until today—to decide so easily in matters of religion, to deny something so easily, to reject something so easily. So, if something is not understood at a certain level, do not deny it; instead, the things present in the traditions suggest that we should refer to the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), read their other traditions, or refer to those who are experts in this field, those who have spent their lives in this arena.

title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 3 | Characteristics of Imam Mahdi (peace be upon him) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture provides an in-depth exploration of the characteristics, lineage, and divine mission of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). It details the historical context of his birth, the necessity of the occultation as a spiritual test, and the reality of his presence among humanity. The session emphasizes the importance of spiritual preparation, steadfastness in faith, and the avoidance of sin to align oneself with the Imam's expectations before his sudden reappearance.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik aduwwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. Astaghfirullahalladhi la ilaha illa huwal hayyul qayyum ar-rahmanur-rahim dhul jalali wal ikram wa atubu ilayh. Audhu billahis sami'il 'alimi minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Allahumma kun li waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan. Salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'i. Fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah. Waliyan wa hafiza wa qa'idan wa nasira wa dalilan wa 'ayna. Hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil li waliyyikal faraj. Waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddami. Wa la taj'alna min a'da'i. Wa waffiqna lima tuhibbu wa tarda. Wa la takilna ila anfusina tarfata 'aynin abada. Wa la tastabdil bina ghayrana. Bihaqqi Muhammadin wa alihi-t-tahirin. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. By the grace of Allah, through the prayers and support of all of you, this Mahdaviyat webinar is being highly appreciated and liked. Our first two sessions have been uploaded to 'The Strong Rope' YouTube channel. You can watch them and also share these videos with those who are unable to watch this webinar live due to their busy schedules. Such Momineen can benefit from the discussions held in this webinar and especially the Q&A sessions through these videos. I hope you have subscribed to 'The Strong Rope' YouTube channel. If not, you can subscribe to this channel and must press the bell icon so that whenever a new video or update is posted, you will automatically receive the information. Additionally, for those who are on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram, you are all requested to follow 'The Strong Rope' Twitter handle, Facebook page, and Instagram account as well. For those who could not join us yesterday, and as a reminder for those who were present, here is a summary of yesterday's discussion. The topic of yesterday's second session was 'The Characteristics of Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.)'. It is important to know about these characteristics because many individuals have passed in this era of Ghaybah who falsely claimed to be Imam Mahdi, and many people were misled by their deception. One thing is clear from these false claims: the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is so important and universal that all Muslims are in agreement and united that a Mahdi will come in the end times who will save humanity. In yesterday's discussion, a total of three characteristics were mentioned. The first is that Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) will be a Sayyid and will be from the lineage of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). In this point, it was mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had said to his beloved daughter, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), at the time of his passing, that Mahdi will be from your lineage, from your children. The second point is that the name of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) is the same as the name of the Messenger of Allah. In this regard, a Hadith was mentioned that if only one day remained in the end of this world, Allah would prolong that day until He sends a man from the lineage of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) whose name and Kuniyat will be the same as the name and Kuniyat of the Messenger of Allah. The third point was that the third characteristic mentioned about Imam-e-Zamana is that he will be from the Quraish and also from the lineage of Imam Hussain (a.s.). In this regard, the Hadith of the 12 Caliphs was mentioned, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated that after me, 12 successors will come, and all of them will be from the Quraish. Among whom the first is Ali and the 12th is Mahdi. And in another Hadith, the Messenger of Allah, pointing towards Imam Hussain (a.s.), stated and clarified that the 12th, meaning the Mahdi, will be from the lineage of this Hussain. And regarding this Imam-e-Hussain (a.s.) and Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), please listen to a few verses: 'When he appeared, the manifestation of life, when he appeared, the manifestation of life, the darkness of the heart turned into light with life. He is the son of the one who, in the plains of Karbala, buried death and laid the foundation of life. And that is why he received the Zulfiqar of Haider, to cut through the paths of death and save life. And why is the world amazed at his long life? Why is the world amazed at his long life? He has received the prayer of life from Muhammad.' Dear friends, since this topic is so vast and only three characteristics could be discussed yesterday. Therefore, we will continue this topic, i.e., the characteristics of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.), today. To carry forward yesterday's discussion, we have with us again today the honorable Dr. Shabib Rizvi. Assalamu Alaikum, Sir. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. All viewers, you are once again requested to send any questions you have regarding the topic and discussion via 'The Strong Rope' WhatsApp number or through the Q&A or chat in Zoom. Bar Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Audhu billahis sami'il 'alimi minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Allahumma kun li waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan Salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'i fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah. Waliyan wa hafiza wa qa'idan wa nasira wa dalilan wa 'ayna hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma j'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi wa atba'i. Wa la taj'alna min a'da'i bihaqqi Muhammad wa alihi-t-tahirin. Assalamu 'alal Mahdi. Alladhi wa'adallahu bihil umam. Ayyajma'a bihil kalim wa yalumma bihis sha'as. Yamla'ullahu bihil arda qistan wa 'adla. Ba'dama muli'at zulman wa jawra. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.). Continuing the series of characteristics, today we discuss the fourth characteristic, and then as much as Allah permits, we will cover as many characteristics as possible; the rest, Insha'Allah, some other time. The fourth characteristic is that Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) is from the lineage of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). In fact, he is his child. And such narrations are abundant that we find. Not only that, if you look at the chain of narrations, Ayatollah Lutfollah Safi Golpaygani has formally recorded it in his valuable book 'Muntakhab al-Athar', numbering the narrations according to the lineage. Now observe. He states that there are 148, 148 Hadiths about Hazrat-e-Mahdi (a.s.) being the 9th descendant of Imam-e-Hussain (a.s.). There are 148 Hadiths. 103 Hadiths state that Hazrat-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is the 7th descendant of Imam-e-Baqir (a.s.). 99 Hadiths state that Hazrat-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is the 6th descendant of Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.). 98 Hadiths state that he is the 5th descendant of Imam-e-Kazim (a.s.). 95 Hadiths state that Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is the 4th descendant of Imam-e-Riza (a.s.). 90 Hadiths state that Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is the 3rd descendant of Imam-e-Jawad (a.s.). 146 Hadiths state that Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.) is the grandson of Imam-e-Hadi (a.s.). And there are 146 Hadiths, narrations present, that Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.) is the son of Imam-e-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Such narrations are numerous, abundant, and for anyone who wants to hold this belief, these narrations are sufficient. Now, if someone insists on denying it, then there is no cure for that. Just presenting one or two narrations here for your service so that the matter becomes completely clear. The first narration is that Imam-e-Kazim (a.s.), through his ancestors, narrates a Hadith from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that 'I and Ali are the two fathers of this Ummah'. I and Ali. (أَنَا وَعَلِيٌّ أَبَوَا هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ) I and Ali are the two fathers of this Ummah. And there are two grandsons of this Ummah, meaning the grandsons of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and two Sayyids who are the leaders of the youth of Paradise, namely Hasan and Husayn. And both these, Hasan and Husayn, are the sons of Ali. And from the lineage of Husayn, 9 Imams will come. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) explicitly clarified that 9 Imams will come from the lineage of Husayn. And obedience to these 9 Imams will be obedience to me. Their obedience is my obedience, and their disobedience, meaning their defiance, will be my defiance. And the one who is the 9th successor from the lineage of Husayn, the 9th one, will be the Mahdi. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) specifically mentioned the name of the Imam. So, you see, you will find many such traditions where you will see that the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) has been discussed in detail, that he is the son of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), and each Imam is mentioned, for example, that he is the grandson of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). So, if you study the traditions, by looking at these traditions and these Hadiths, you will very easily find out who is truly Imam-e-Mahdi and who is a false claimant. Because all the false claimants who have passed, none of their lineages, none of their lines, match the way it has been described in these traditions. And then, the next characteristic—because time is short, I am trying to cover as many characteristics as possible—is the 5th characteristic: whose son will Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) be? A slave-maid (kaneez) of high status. Although this is a separate topic, and God willing, we will try to cover it; the scholars who will speak in this series in the future will cover this topic. The second question is via WhatsApp: 'What is the hadith in which it is said that we have to stand up and place our right hand on our head for the special title? Also, if someone does not do so, will it be considered haram?' No, no, it is not haram; it is just mustahab (recommended). This tradition comes from Imam Reza (a.s.), that it was his characteristic that whenever the special title of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) was mentioned—for which one has to stand up, as it mentions his rising—Imam Reza (a.s.) would stand up, face the Qibla, place his right hand on his head, and then, after mentioning that name, say 'Ajjallallahu Ta'ala Farajahush Sharif'. May Allah hasten his reappearance. So, this was the Sunnah of Imam Reza (a.s.). It is not haram; it is mustahab. If someone does not do it, there is no sin in it. But it is mustahab, and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) like this. If you do it, it is a good thing; if not, there is no issue. Yes, this tradition exists among us. If there are more questions related to this topic and there is time, we can take another question or two if possible. Sir, another question related to the topic is regarding the discussion about Prophet Isa (a.s.) asking Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) to step forward. The question was: 'Is Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) superior to the prophets?' Yes, definitely, it goes without saying, yes. Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), except for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Panjtan (a.s.), is superior to all the Masoomeen (a.s.). So, all the prophets—the 14 Masoomeen (a.s.) as we commonly call them—are superior to all the prophets. In terms of their creation, even in terms of their luminous creation, they are superior; they are the most superior. Therefore, they are superior, and there are no two opinions about this, and that is why... The Masoomeen (a.s.) do not have formal etiquette (takalluf) like we say, 'After you, after you.' The Masoomeen (a.s.) do not have such formalities. So, if Prophet Isa (a.s.) says 'taqaddam' (step forward) after the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) to lead the prayer, it is not out of formality. Keep this in mind. It is not a formality because the Masoomeen do not have such formalities; rather, it is based on rank and position. So, this 'taqaddam'—that you step forward and lead the prayer—and Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will lead the prayer and Prophet Isa (a.s.) will pray behind him. That is why I submitted earlier that in our traditions, it is clearly written that Prophet Isa (a.s.) will say 'taqaddam' and Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will step forward and lead the prayer. However, in the traditions of others (Ahl-e-Tasannun), they have it that he will say 'after you, after you, after you.' We do not have such traditions of 'after you.' Because the tradition of leading the prayer exists among them too, that when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) reappears—it is explicitly present in their books like Kitab al-Fitan in the Sihah al-Sittah—that Prophet Isa (a.s.) will pray behind him. It is present in the Sihah al-Sittah, in Kitab al-Fitan, that when Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) or Imam Mahdi (a.s.) reappears, Prophet Isa (a.s.) will pray behind him. Before that, Prophet Isa (a.s.) will ask him to step forward, and Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will ask him to step forward. We do not have such traditions. This is found among them. These formalities do not exist among the Masoomeen. Here, the line is clearly demarcated; the line of superiority is drawn. And this superiority is established and proven that Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is superior to Prophet Isa (a.s.) and he will lead the prayer. Yes. Yes, thank you, sir. Although there isn't much time left, sir, since one of our viewers has a question—it is not entirely related to the topic, but it was slightly touched upon during the three days of discussion—their question is: 'How to know if the Imam is happy or sad at any point in time?' This is a bit tricky, how to know... of course. It is very simple, not exactly tricky, but look, the Imam is in occultation, and no one can claim that they meet him or anything of that sort. There is just one thing. There is a hadith, a Tawqi (signed letter) from the Imam, which I will present to you so it becomes clear whether the Imam is happy or displeased. The Imam says—this is the Imam's own hadith—a Tawqi of the 12th Imam: 'Falyamal kullu imrin bima yaqrubu bihi min mahabbatina walyatajannab ma yudnihi min karahiyatina wa sakhatina' (Everyone among you should do what brings you closer to our love and avoid what brings you closer to our dislike and displeasure). Do not do any such work. Now, what are those works? If one acts upon the Wajibats (obligatory) and Mustahabats (recommended) of the Sharia, the Imam is happy. If, God forbid, a person being a Shia commits Haram (forbidden) acts or Makruh (disliked) things, then the Imam is displeased with them. The Imam does not like that. And in that same hadith, in that same Tawqi, the Imam has also warned us by saying: 'Fa inna amrana baghtatan faj'atan' (For our reappearance will be sudden and unexpected). 'Hina la tanfa'u tawbatun' (At a time when repentance will not be of any use). It will be sudden and unexpected. It will happen when you don't expect it. At that time, repentance will not be of any use. Then the Zulfiqar will have been drawn. It is now placed on the neck; what is the point of repenting now? 'Hina la tanfa'u tawbatun wa la yunjiihi min iqabina nadamun 'ala hawbatin' (And at that time, if you regret or repent, this repentance will be of no use). Because death is standing right in front. The punishment is in front; what is there now? Therefore, what has been made very clear is that you should do every act that brings you closer to our love. 'Falyamal kullu imrin bima yaqrubu bihi min mahabbatina' (Everyone should do what brings them closer to our love), meaning all Wajibats and Mustahabats. Because Islam is the religion that is Allah's religion. Yes. Thank you, sir. We have exceeded the time. Thank you very much, sir. Thank you all very much, and if there has been any shortcoming, we apologize to the viewers. If there has been any shortcoming, just pray that the reappearance of Imam-e-Asr (a.s.) happens as soon as possible. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. With this, our third session today comes to an end. Insha'Allah, tomorrow with a new topic, as the sir mentioned during the speech, tomorrow's topic will be related to the mother of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), Hazrat Narjis Khatun (s.a.), and the birth of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). A scholar will join us tomorrow. I request everyone to recite a loud Salawat, and let us all pray together at the end that the Lord of the Worlds hastens the reappearance of the Imam of our time and counts us among his sincere servants. title: Who Are Ahle Zikr? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the Quranic command to consult the 'Ahl al-Dhikr' when one lacks knowledge. By referencing a tradition from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), the speaker clarifies that the 'Dhikr' refers to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the 'Ahl al-Dhikr' are the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt. The talk emphasizes the necessity of turning to the Progeny of the Prophet for divine guidance and religious understanding.
content:
[Music] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Was-salatu 'ala ya Rasulallah, wa 'ala alihi al-tayyibina al-tahirin. Allah (Tabarak wa Ta'ala) commands us in the Holy Quran: 'Ask the people of the Dhikr if you do not know.' In this verse, two groups are mentioned: one is the Ahl al-Dhikr, who possess knowledge, and the second group is those who do not possess knowledge. Those who do not possess knowledge are commanded to ask the Ahl al-Dhikr. Therefore, it becomes necessary for us to seek out who these Ahl al-Dhikr are, whom Allah has commanded us to ask. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) says regarding this verse: 'The Dhikr is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and we are the Ahl al-Dhikr.' And I, meaning Imam Baqir (a.s.) and the other Imams, are the Ahl al-Dhikr. From this hadith, it becomes absolutely clear that the Ahl al-Dhikr are none other than the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), whom Allah has commanded us to ask. Wa sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad.

excerpt: This lecture discusses the profound connection between the awaited Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and the historical oppression faced by the Ahlulbayt. It highlights a tradition from Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) stating that the Imam will use the very logs gathered to attack the house of Fatima (s.a.) as a means of divine retribution. The speaker reflects on the emotional weight this carries for the Imam, who remains deeply affected by the memory of the burning door and the martyrdom of his ancestor.
content:

[Music] Meaning, the logs gathered to attack the house of the Prophet's daughter—today, even the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.)—I don't know what must pass through his heart when he sees those logs. It is no wonder that in those burnt logs, he sometimes sees that image, that burning door, and sometimes he remembers the martyrdom of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.).

title: Namaz Ko Halka Samajhna | Belittling Prayers | Kalaam e Noor # 18
excerpt: This lecture explores the severe spiritual consequences of belittling or neglecting the daily prayers (Namaz) in Islam. It highlights a profound tradition from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) stating that those who treat their prayers lightly are not considered part of his followers. The discourse emphasizes the importance of sincerity, punctuality, and reverence in the performance of Salah as a fundamental pillar of faith.
content:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: "ليس مني من استخف بصلاته". The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'He is not from me who takes his prayer lightly.'
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) explicitly distanced himself from those who belittle their prayers.

title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#15 - Darwaaze Par Imam Ali (a.s.) Kyun Nahin Aaye? - Part 2/2
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical objection regarding why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not personally come to the door during the events following the Prophet's passing. The speaker clarifies that Lady Fatimah (s.a.) went to the door to uphold the sanctity of their home, enforce the Quranic command regarding permission, and complete the argument against those attempting to force entry. The discussion emphasizes that the Imam's absence from the door was not a sign of weakness, but a strategic and moral stance against those who disregarded Islamic etiquette and the Prophet's will.
content:
Do it, do it. After [music] July, all winners and... this is the Rahman alias team loot. This entire program, Shaheen, we are grateful that you are interested in our channel and through suggestions, one of the suggestions that came from you regarding our video, which we are discussing in today's episode, was why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not come to the door. In this regard, the questions we received, we will present the detailed answer and more evidence to you. Acting on this suggestion, we have appeared in your court today to answer this question. So come, I will invite our... Appeared in your court, so come, I will invite our dear guest to present the detailed answer to this question in your court. Brother, as per the suggestion from the viewers, we had the objection of why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not come to the door, I would like you to present the detailed answer and more evidence. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and peace be upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Before I turn to the answers, I want to present the summary of the previous episode to the viewers so that we can move forward. The first conclusion we saw in that episode was that saying Imam Ali (a.s.) did not come to the door is completely wrong, because they came to the house of the Lady (a.s.) three times, out of which the first two times the attack on the door happened, and the third time when their house... The third time when their house was attacked. Along with this, we also saw that it was clear that those who came to the door of the Lady (a.s.) had no involvement of the government of the Ansar and Muhajireen. Despite the Lady (a.s.) forbidding them, those people forced the door of the Lady's house. The third thing we saw in this episode was that despite being at home, the Imam (a.s.) not going to the door does not affect his status or his bravery, because we saw that during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), it happened that he was present at home, but none of his wives went to open the door. Finally, we saw in the case of Abdur Rahman bin Awf that when he was given the right to take custody, he went to his sister's house, hoping that people would enter without permission, and he was sure that it was a problem for them, and they would enter without permission, and his life would be saved. So this is what we saw in the previous episode regarding the answer to this objection. In this episode, we move forward with three answers to this objection and keep the support of the Lady (a.s.) in mind. The first answer we want to give is that the Lady (a.s.) closing the door... we have seen three times at the house of the Lady (a.s.), and the door being dropped on the Lady (a.s.) was not done by any... [reference to historical source]... whose narrators were followers of that person, but he was the grandson of the person who... In the narration that was mentioned about the attack on the house, he was involved. After hearing this narration, we all decide that the Lady (a.s.) went to close the door. Secondly, in some ways, people attacked the house, and this is... the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stopped him, and after a while, he returned. When he returned, he asked Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), 'What is the matter?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has not made anyone else my successor except me.' And he refused to accept anyone else as his successor. This is one thing, and there were others present when he went there... There were others present when he went there, and he sent him back with a message that you should come because the people have gathered, including the Muhajireen and Ansar, and they have pledged allegiance, and you are also a Muslim, you should also pledge allegiance. This message was sent again. Today, the same thing happened; when the door was knocked, he returned and brought a new message from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.). What was that message? It was that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had made a will to me that I should not leave the house until I have finished writing the Quran. Go and tell those people the answer. He was among those people, and this time he says that he told others that we should all go together to the house of Ali (a.s.). We said that the first two times you... We said that the first two times you came to Imam Ali (a.s.), he turned you away both times. Apart from this, we find another narration that once Lady Fizza (a.s.) also turned them away. That is, when they asked to send Imam Ali (a.s.) out, Lady Fizza (a.s.) turned them away by saying, 'Innahu mashghul' (He is busy), so you go away. That is, these people had been turned away three times. In the narration that was mentioned, they were present, and the name of a great scholar is mentioned. It is worth noting that when they go to attack the house of the other... now if you look further in this same narration, it is found that when these people reached near the door of Imam Ali (a.s.), they said, 'Assalamu Alaikum', and it is said that they closed the door in front of those people... They closed the door in front of those people and said... the important point here is that they came to... and if we analyze this event, these questions come before us. That is, first, the objection was raised that the Lady (a.s.) was definitely at the door, but to close the door, not to open it. The second time they closed the door and the meaning of breaking it is that in those days... without permission... these two times when the door of the house was closed, then you said absolutely correctly. So this is the reason for the door being closed by the Lady (a.s.). They closed the main door of those people, and the important point here is that they were appointed for it. If we examine this sentence, several questions arise before us. Firstly, regarding the election of the caliphate, the Princess (a.s.) was definitely at the door, but the door was closed. To open it, they closed the door a second time, and breaking it means that without being appointed in those days—if the door of the house is closed twice—then you have said it absolutely correctly. So, this is the situation at the door, and the reason for closing the door in this manner is why she went there. The second method is that she went there because she was certain that they were not in the house, and we find this in the phrase 'La ilaha illa Allah'. This means there is no doubt that people entered their house. If we look at the Holy Quran, Allah has given a very precise instruction, which is a fundamental Islamic teaching: that you cannot enter a house until the owner gives you permission. As we saw in the previous episode, according to Surah An-Nur, verse 27: 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants. That is best for you; perhaps you will be reminded.' In the very next verse, it is stated: 'And if you do not find anyone therein, do not enter them until permission has been given you.' And if it is said to you, 'Go back,' then go back; it is purer for you. Despite knowing this, people were trying to enter the house. This shows that in the eyes of those people, there was no sanctity, and no permission was needed. The famous scholar of the Ahlulbayt, in his book 'Al-Imamah wal-Siyasah', writes that when Lady Fatimah (s.a.) raised her voice and asked the people to return, many did return, but a group still remained there. In this book, on page 33, it is mentioned that whoever knew the importance of the door, whoever had it in their sight, could not ignore it when she was telling them to leave, yet some people still remained. This is our second answer to the objection: she went to close the door, and she went with the intention that since she had not given them permission to enter, they should not enter. Now, let us move toward the third answer to this objection. The third answer is regarding the presence of Lady Fatimah (s.a.) at the door. In the historical accounts, it is found that when people gathered at the door, they asked, 'Why is Ali (a.s.) not at the door?' The answer to this question also serves as a response to this objection. In the historical records, it is mentioned that I was forced to come here, and I said, 'O Allah, I complain to You about the loss of Your Prophet and the betrayal of his Ummah.' She came to the door to complete the argument. This is the third answer; she was completing the argument against those who had such madness that they threatened to burn the house down if they did not come out for the pledge of allegiance, even though the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had not yet been buried. Think for yourself: if Imam Ali (a.s.) had been at the door in this situation, those people—who had not even performed the funeral rites—would have burned the whole house and the people inside. It was already announced in Medina that either they pledge allegiance or they would be martyred in the dust. Was it because of Ali (a.s.) that they were martyred? Not at all. It is possible that later those people would have said that it was because of Ali (a.s.) that they were at the house, and it is possible that the oppressors would have killed Lady Fatimah (s.a.) and then said that Lady Fatimah (s.a.) was not innocent, meaning she was not free from these things. She gave this point clearly. And if we look at it, Lady Fatimah (s.a.) is a personality whose help the people did not deserve. She was the infallible one. The fact that she came to the door forced them to realize she was present in the house. The writers who say this might claim that the people did not know she was in the house, but with this, for future generations, Lady Fatimah (s.a.) made it clear that she was neither with those who pledged allegiance to Ali (a.s.) nor with those who were against him. This is a way to oppose them. There is no doubt that if she were not present in the house, they would say that she was not there. By being there, she showed the people that those who were at the door were completely misguided. As you have seen through this discussion, the answer to why she came to the door is very clear. If you have any other questions or objections in your mind, you can send them to our social media handles or our WhatsApp number. We will try to answer them in the next episode. Let us conclude this episode, which was about answering objections regarding the attack on the house.
Imam Ali (a.s.) did not come to the door because he was occupied with the Prophet's final will and the compilation of the Quran.
Lady Fatimah (s.a.) went to the door to explicitly deny permission to those attempting to enter without consent.
The Quranic verse in Surah An-Nur (27-28) mandates that one must seek permission before entering a home; the aggressors violated this sanctity.
The presence of Lady Fatimah (s.a.) at the door served to document the injustice for future generations.
The aggressors threatened to burn the house down, and the Imam's restraint prevented further immediate bloodshed.
The Lady's actions demonstrated that she did not support the forced allegiance sought by the group at the door.
