chapters.title: Ghadir Mega Quiz Overview
chapters.summary: The host introduces the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi quiz series, explaining the format, prizes, and the requirement to participate in all seven episodes to win the mega prize of Ziyarat of Iraq.

chapters.title: Divine Protection and the Defense of Ghadir
chapters.summary: The discussion explores the significance of the Ayah-e-Tabligh and how Allah promised to protect the Prophet during the announcement of Wilayah, despite the presence of hypocrites and potential opposition.

chapters.title: The Importance and Denial of Imamate
chapters.summary: Reflecting on a Hadith from Imam Kazim (a.s.), the speakers discuss how the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt was the most emphasized command from Allah, yet it faced the most significant denial from the Ummah.

chapters.title: The Obligation to Proclaim Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the Prophet's announcement at Ghadir was a divine command for all Muslims to uphold and propagate the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib throughout their lives.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Saqifah and Defense of Wilayah
chapters.summary: This section discusses the immediate post-Prophetic era, focusing on the resistance of the Ahlulbayt against the usurpation of Caliphate and the martyrdom of Janabe Mohsin.

chapters.title: Janabe Zahra's Defense of Ghadir
chapters.summary: Janabe Zahra (s.a.) confronted those who usurped the Caliphate by reminding them that Ghadir left no room for excuses, as the Prophet had clearly appointed Ali as the Mawla.

chapters.title: The Duty to Convey Ghadir
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the Prophet's command for every present person to convey the message of Ghadir to the absent, a duty carried forward by the Imams.

chapters.title: The Continuous Defense of Ghadir
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) consistently defended the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) throughout history, emphasizing that the Imams are the true heirs and protectors of the Ghadir message.

chapters.title: The Two Weighty Things
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left behind the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) as an inseparable pair, yet the Muslim Ummah's failure to follow the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) has led to widespread disagreement.

chapters.title: Scholarly Defense and Allama Amini
chapters.summary: Prominent scholars like Allama Amini and Mir Hamid Hussain have authored monumental works defending Ghadir, using logical arguments that remain unanswered by opponents.

chapters.title: Patience vs. Silence
chapters.summary: The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) practiced patience in the face of adversity, but they were never silent, consistently defending the truth of Wilayah in every era.

chapters.title: Ahlulbayt's Defense of Ghadir
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the patience and prudence of the Ahlulbayt in defending the message of Ghadir while preventing civil unrest.

chapters.title: Mega Quiz Results and Announcements
chapters.summary: The episode concludes with the announcement of quiz winners and details regarding eligibility for the mega prize of Iraq Ziyarat.

title: Muharram 1442 English Majlis #07: The Biggest Deviation | Sayed Mahdi Modarresi
excerpt: In this lecture, Sayed Mahdi Modarresi examines the historical and spiritual deviations that occurred after the Prophet Muhammad, tracing the root of these issues to the rejection of Ghadir. He emphasizes the necessity of absolute submission to Allah's will, contrasting the moral clarity of Imam Hussain and his loyal companions like Abbas with the corruption of the Umayyad regime. The discourse highlights how societal pressures and psychological manipulation can distort faith, urging believers to maintain moral integrity through halal sustenance and unwavering trust in divine guidance.

chapters.title: Innovations After the Prophet
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how innovations and pagan traditions were introduced into Islam following the Prophet's demise, leading to the corruption of the faith.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Call to Action
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain sent letters to noblemen in various cities, including Basra, to invite them to join his mission and revive the true tradition of the Prophet.

chapters.title: The Treachery of Al-Mundhar
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the betrayal of Al-Mundhar, who turned in the Imam's messenger to the authorities, contrasting the binary choice between supporting the Imam or choosing damnation.

chapters.title: Moral Clarity and Modern Manipulation
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain offers a path of righteousness, which the speaker contrasts with modern behavioral economics and marketing tactics designed to manipulate human behavior.

chapters.title: The Gradual Distortion of Faith
chapters.summary: The speaker uses the boiling frog metaphor to explain how cultural manipulation slowly erodes religious values, leading people to abandon the truth.

chapters.title: The Essence of Islamic Submission
chapters.summary: True Islam requires submission to divine commands even when they defy human logic, as demonstrated by the Imams' responses to questions about religious rituals.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Ghadir and Karbala
chapters.summary: The denial of the Prophet's declaration at Ghadir led to the widespread corruption that culminated in the martyrdom of Imam Hussain by those claiming to follow the Prophet.

chapters.title: The Importance of Halal Sustenance
chapters.summary: Maintaining a righteous path requires strict adherence to consuming only halal, as haram sustenance is a primary cause of spiritual and moral downfall.

chapters.title: Trusting Allah in Marriage
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that marrying based on worldly desires like wealth or beauty leads to regret, whereas prioritizing religion and trusting Allah brings true fulfillment.

chapters.title: The Siege of Karbala and Abbas
chapters.summary: The narrative shifts to the seventh of Muharram, describing the thirst in Imam Hussain's camp and the role of Abbas as the protector of the women and children.

chapters.title: The Loyalty of Abbas
chapters.summary: Lady Zainab visits Abbas to confirm his loyalty after the enemy offers him immunity, leading to a poignant exchange about his commitment to Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Abbas
chapters.summary: The lecture recounts the final moments of Abbas on the battlefield, his sacrifice for the camp, and the profound grief of Imam Hussain upon finding him.

title: Majlis 2 | Ma'refat Ki Ahmiyyat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual significance of Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Imam and its necessity for authentic worship. Through the lens of the events of Karbala, the speaker highlights the virtues of humility, asceticism, and the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt. The session concludes with a moving account of the sacrifices made by companions like Anas ibn al-Harith and Hazrat Abbas, emphasizing their unwavering devotion to Imam Hussain (a.s.).
content:
When the Shah (Imam Hussain a.s.) came to the tent and said farewell, a cry of grief arose, a cry of grief arose. The one whose wait was long is now near, the day of calamity is setting in. It is a matter of a few moments, the Day of Judgment is near, Zainab, the departure of your poor brother is near. Saying this, when he asked for his mother's shirt, it was fulfilled, a cry of grief arose, a cry of grief arose. Moving a little away from the tent, the Shah-e-Zaman said, 'Do not be troubled, extend your arm, O sister, let me kiss the place where the ropes will be tied.' Extending her arm, the sister wept, and when the brother began to kiss the arm of his sister, a cry of grief arose, a cry of grief arose. Hearing this, the daughter of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was restless and said, 'Extend your throat, enough now, today I remembered my mother's words. Let me kiss the place where the dagger will run.' When Zainab stepped forward and kissed her brother's throat, a cry of grief arose, a cry of grief arose. Then he began to say to his daughter, 'Fatima's son, stay, who will take care of you, Aunt? It is a time of exile, do not ask any questions of your Aunt, otherwise, your body will feel great sorrow.' Then, placing his hand on her head, when he began to give blessings, a cry of grief arose, a cry of grief arose. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the end is for those who are God-fearing and certain. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the infallible ones, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The Master, the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our Wali of command, our Master, our Mawla, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our confidant, the cave of the oppressed, the helper of the distressed and the desperate, may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Now then, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in His Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'Keep to forgiveness, and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant.' (Quran 7:199). Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. In this noble verse, which is verse number 199 of Surah Al-A'raf, Allah the Almighty commands: 'Khudh al-afwa' (Keep to forgiveness), meaning you should make forgiveness, good manners, and good character your profession—that is, forgive people and treat them with kindness. And 'wa'mur bil-urfi' (and enjoin kindness). Yesterday, I submitted in your service what is meant by 'Ma'ruf'. Ma'ruf means that which the intellect accepts, which the intellect approves, and which brings pleasure to a human being—meaning, in English, something that brings pleasure to a person. And 'wa a'rid 'anil jahilin' (and turn away from the ignorant). So, here, regarding 'Khudh al-afwa', I spoke about it yesterday; today, a little discussion on 'wa'mur bil-urfi'. See, there is an instance of 'wa'mur bil-urfi'. Its primary instance, 'Urfi'—meaning enjoin the 'Ma'ruf'—is the Wilayat of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And 'wa a'rid 'anil jahilin'—turn away from the ignorant—means those individuals who are not ready to accept the Wilayat of Ali and are adamant that they will not accept the Wilayat of Ali and the 11 Imams after him. So, turn away from them. However, if we take this in its literal meaning—that you should forgive people, enjoin Ma'ruf, enjoin good things, and turn away from the ignorant—turning away means that you should not react in front of them. When an ignorant person speaks to you, do not react to them as ignorant people usually do to each other, and as an ignorant person reacts. As in another verse of Surah Al-Furqan: 'Ibadur-Rahman alladhina yamshuna 'alal-ardi hawna wa idha khatabahumul-jahiluna qalu salama' (The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them, they say words of peace). The servants of the Most Merciful are those who, when they walk on the earth, walk with humility. This 'hawn' (humility) is also very profound; this is a verse of the Quran. Look, how strange it is. So, walking with humility means that when they walk on the earth, they do not walk with great pomp and show, like having 10 men walking in front and 10 behind, and so on—they walk with humility, with moderation. Moderation means they do not walk with arrogance, nor do they bow down so much that people trample over them. That is another verse of the Quran, which I will also mention in your service. So, 'Ibadur-Rahman alladhina yamshuna 'alal-ardi hawna' is a verse of Surah Al-Furqan. 'Wa idha khatabahumul-jahiluna qalu salama'—and when the ignorant address them, they say 'Assalamu Alaikum' (peace), meaning I have no interest in talking to you. There is no benefit in talking to you. When the ignorant address them, they do not engage with them. So, one does not engage with the ignorant. And in the verse of Surah Bani Israil, which I just mentioned, it is commanded: 'Wa la tamshi fil-ardi maraha' (And do not walk on the earth exultantly). Look, when you walk on the earth, do not walk with arrogance. Innak lan takhriqal arda wa lan tabluqal jibala toolan. Because if you walk with arrogance, your arrogant walking will neither split the earth, nor will you reach the height of the mountains. Meaning, you will not become as tall as a mountain if you walk with arrogance. Therefore, walk moderately. Wa la tamshi fil ardi maraha. Maraha means to walk with arrogance. The Quran is giving a command, forbidding you from walking with arrogance. Wa la tamshi fil ardi maraha. Why? Innak lan takhriqal arda. Kharq means to split. By your walking, the earth is not going to split. No matter how great a man is today, no matter how arrogantly he walks, the earth will not split. And if it were to split, it would be more harmful to him. And he is not going to reach the height of a mountain; he will not reach the height of a mountain. Meaning, the Quran is saying here, do not act with arrogance, do not act with pride. Rather, one should act with zuhd (asceticism). What does zuhd mean? Zuhd means asceticism or, as the word used in English, abstinence. Abstinence means that if Allah gives something, if Allah gives a blessing—meaning, a zahid (ascetic) and a wise person means that if Allah gives a blessing, he shouldn't say, 'No, no, no, astaghfirullah, I don't want anything,' no. If Allah gives a blessing—this is a verse of the Quran, a verse of Surah Hadid. If Allah is giving a blessing, one should express gratitude for it, and if Allah keeps one deprived of something or takes back a blessing, one should still be patient and express gratitude for it. Alhamdulillah. In every state, there is gratitude to Allah. This is a verse of Surah Hadid: Likayla ta'saw 'ala ma fatakum wa la tafrahu bima atakum. What is the sign of zuhd? What is its symbol? No, the peace treaty Imam Hasan (a.s.) made with Muawiyah does not mean Imam Hasan didn't do anything, he just didn't wage war. He didn't wage war. And Imam Hussain (a.s.) also, even after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, Imam Hasan and Imam Hussain all kept speaking. Now, if I try to present one or two examples quickly, if not, at least one, and the rest tomorrow, Insha'Allah. Look, Imam Hasan and Imam Hussain (a.s.), what is the Imam's age now? Barely 15 years old, 15-16 years old. 15-16 years old. And the one who usurped Ali's right, usurped Ali's right, is saying to people from the pulpit—now look at the sentence he said, what sentence did he say while sitting on the pulpit? He said, he said this, "أنا أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم" (I am more entitled to the believers than their own selves). What sentence did he say? "أنا أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم" (I am more entitled to the believers than their own selves). Meaning, I am the Mawla of the people and I have more power, more authority over the people than they have themselves. As soon as he said this, "فقال له الحسين عليه السلام من ناحية المسجد" (Hussain (a.s.) said to him from a corner of the mosque), Imam Hussain (a.s.) was in a corner of the Mosque of the Prophet. From there he said, "انزل" (Get down). "أيها الكذاب" (O liar). "عن منبر أبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله" (From the pulpit of my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)). I intentionally said father, yes. I intentionally used the word father. Get down from the pulpit of my father, the Messenger of Allah, "لا منبر أبيك" (Not the pulpit of your father). Is it clear? Now, we think this hadith cannot be true, the character was not like that. The character was exactly this. Why? Because he was seeing oppression. What is the meaning of oppression? Something that is not in its place. When the Imam sees any kind of oppression there, he immediately raises his voice. "لا منبر أبيك" (Not the pulpit of your father). He immediately said, "فمنبر أبيك لأمري يا حسين" (By my life, O Hussain, it is indeed the pulpit of your father). It is your father's pulpit. "لا منبر أبي" (Not the pulpit of my father). What is it? It is not my father's pulpit. Look, this is what happens immediately. This is what happens to the oppressor, that when the oppressor is challenged, he immediately goes on the back foot. But the condition is that he must be challenged continuously, spoken to continuously. If people remain silent, saying 'what does it have to do with us?' And the Ummah did exactly that, the Ummah remained silent. The Ummah did this, now Insha'Allah we will explain that. So then he asked, "من علمك هذا" (Who taught you to say this?). Your father Ali ibn Abi Talib? Your father Ali ibn Abi Talib taught you to say this? "فقال الحسين عليه السلام" (Imam Hussain (a.s.) said), "إن أطع أبي فيما أمرني" (If I obey my father in what he commanded me), then by my life, by my life, Ali is the guide and I am his follower. Ali is the guide, I am his follower. "ولو في رقاب الناس البيعة" And people gave allegiance (bay'ah) at his hands, the allegiance is on the necks of the people. In the time of the Messenger of Allah, when Gabriel descended with this verse that 'O Messenger, convey...', so no one can deny this allegiance, the allegiance of Ali, except the one who denies the Quran. So the Master of Martyrs (Sayyid-al-Shuhada) said that "قد عرف الناس بقلوبهم" (People recognized Ali with their hearts), but "وأنكروها بألسنتهم" (but denied it with their tongues). Denied it with their tongues, denied Ali. They knew he was on the truth, they knew, everyone knows what is right and what is wrong, but they were following the wrong. They left the truth and followed falsehood, even though they knew it was falsehood, they knew it was wrong. But still, they were silent. They had a pigeon sitting on their heads (an idiom for being oblivious/passive). No one came to help Ali, Ali was alone. And there were only a few people who could be counted on fingers. Very famous companions whose names you have heard, Insha'Allah, their mention will come another time. There was one companion who was among the first martyrs of Karbala. And what was his name? Anas ibn al-Harith. Anas ibn al-Harith al-Kahili al-Asadi, he was from Banu Asad. Anas ibn al-Harith. Look, see the level of submission. He is a companion of the Messenger of Allah, a servant of the Messenger of Allah. When he was young, he was a servant of the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah departed from this world, was martyred. Anas served the Commander of the Faithful (Amir-ul-Mu'minin). The Commander of the Faithful was martyred, Anas served Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). Until 50 AH, Anas kept serving. Anas ibn al-Harith al-Kahili al-Asadi. Great scholars, scholars of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, Bukhari wrote in his book, wrote in Sahih Bukhari. He wrote, the name is written, "Anas ibn al-Harith al-Kahili al-Asadi, من الصحابة (from the companions), companion of the Messenger, killed with Hussain." Think about it, martyred with Hussain. He doesn't write further, who martyred him? He doesn't write who martyred him. And the one who martyred him, was he a Muslim or not? Those who killed Hussain, those who fought Hussain, were they Muslims or not? Anas ibn Kahili Asadi, if the one who martyred him—this is what Bukhari is writing. This is what Ibn Abi Hatim is writing. Ibn Abi Hatim is writing in his book, he is a scholar of the 3rd/4th century. Bukhari is from the third century. This is written, you see he is writing openly. Now, if those who killed Hussain were Muslims, anyway, in 50 AH he had become very old. And he was so old that he was not fit for any work. So he said, 'Okay, I don't know when my death will come. So I am going to Karbala.' In 50 AH, Karbala was completely desolate, there was nothing in Karbala. There was no one, it was a desert. It was a complete desert. And he went searching for Karbala and pitched a tent there. In the middle of the desert, he pitched a tent and sat alone. We don't know where his food was coming from. We don't know, but it is written in history, it is written in history that from 50 AH to 61 AH, for 11 years, Anas ibn Harith al-Kahili al-Asadi was alone in the desert of Karbala, until the caravan of Hussain arrived on the 2nd of Muharram. Before that, people came, that is also written in history. People came and asked, when they saw the tent in the desert, they came and asked, 'O old man, what are you doing here? Alone in the desert, you will die of hunger and thirst.' There is no one here, for miles around, neither human nor jinn, no one. He said that I have heard from the Messenger of Allah that my grandson will be killed in Karbala. I should either die before that, or if I am alive, I should die helping Hussain. Because the Prophet said, 'Whoever helps Hussain, he has helped me.' He has helped me. Allah kept Anas ibn Kahil alive in that desert for 11 years. For 11 years. When Hussain arrived, he met Anas, they both embraced. You stayed with Anas, when? Until the morning of Ashura. Until the morning of Ashura. The very first dialogue, the very first discussion that happened with Umar ibn Sa'ad, may Allah's curse be upon him, was with Anas ibn Harith. Imam Hussain... although, listen to what is written in history about that too. That Anas had become so old that his eyebrows, these, these, they had turned completely white and had come down over his eyes. He was that old, he had become that frail. He was the oldest among all the companions of Imam Hussain. Of all the companions, he was the oldest. The Imam sent him so that the proof would be completed against Umar ibn Sa'd, that a companion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has come. Umar ibn Sa'd recognized him. And he said—meaning Anas said—'Do you know who you are coming to fight?' He said, 'Yes, I know. I know that I am going to fight someone whose end, or rather, the end of fighting whom, is nothing but Hell.' So he said, 'When you know this, then why?' He replied, 'That Ibn Ziyad is forcing me so much, that is why I have to do it.' In reality, that was not the cause. It was the love of the world, the love of worldly rule. Anyway, Anas ibn Harith came and took permission from the Master of Martyrs (a.s.). He took permission from the Master of Martyrs and came and recited Rajaz. He was old, but he recited Rajaz; he recited verses with bravery. And the last two lines of the Arabic Rajaz verses he recited, the meaning of which is: "Ali and the family of Ali are from the Shias of the Merciful," or "Ali and his companions are from the Shias of the Merciful, and Harb and his companions are from the Shias of Satan." That is, Ali and his children and his companions are among the followers of Allah, among those who believe in Allah, and Abu Sufyan and his children are among the followers of Satan. And saying this, he sent many people to Hell and then drank the cup of martyrdom himself. We gave you this as an example. Now look, his name is mentioned among the martyrs of Karbala in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah by the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). His name is in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, you can read it: "Peace be upon you, O Anas ibn Harith al-Kahili al-Asadi." The Imam has mentioned his name in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah. So, a companion of the Messenger and a companion of the Imam, having such a spirit of martyrdom—just think, what kind of spirit of martyrdom would one have who is under the influence of Ali's prayers? Just think what that spirit would be, and to kill this spirit was the real bravery and the real courage. This is what Abbas ibn Ali is called. He who killed this spirit is called Abbas ibn Ali. That Abbas who kept asking for permission continuously, but Husayn kept refusing. Until the time of Ashura came, when Hazrat Abbas came again. Mir Anees says: "He did not ask for permission, for he was a man of great honor." Hazrat Abbas came and stood just in front. Husayn understood why Abbas had come. So he said, "Abbas, go and bring water for the children." The children are thirsty. The Master came and called out at the tent door, "Sakina!" As soon as the girl heard the voice, she came running and said, "Uncle, how did you remember me?" "Child, bring your water skin." She said, "Uncle, what will we do with the water skin?" He said, "The Master has ordered me to bring water. I am to bring water; the Master has ordered to bring water." Sakina went and was walking with the water skin when it is written in the Maqtal that as soon as Sakina walked with the water skin, small children were walking with Sakina, "Lady, where is this water skin going?" She said, "My uncle is going to fetch water. Children, now be assured. Father has told Uncle to bring water, now my uncle will definitely bring water. Now you be assured." Sakina gave great comfort to the children, and the children also became very assured. Sakina brought the water skin, and Abbas left. Now listen to the sentences of the Maqtal. Abbas came, he came to the bank of the Euphrates, He came to the bank, pushed the armies aside, and the armies moved away on their own. Once Abbas, Abbas put his horse into the river, he put the horse into the river, got down from the horse, took water in his cupped hands, and said, "O wretched ones, O oppressors, do not think that I am helpless, I can drink water, I can take water, but what can I do, the children are thirsty in the tents, Sakina is thirsty in the tents." Saying this, he threw the water away. After throwing the water away, Abbas wetted the water skin, filled it with water, and then mounted the horse again. Now as he started moving towards the tents, Abbas had only one goal and one purpose, only one aim, that somehow the water must reach the tents. Now as Abbas started moving, as he started moving upwards, as soon as he started moving up from the lowlands, a wretch attacked from behind in such a way that his right arm was severed. Abbas recited Rajaz that even if you sever my right arm, I will still continue to help my Master. Then another wretch attacked in such a way that his left shoulder was cut. As soon as his left shoulder was cut, Abbas recited the second line and said, "O soul, never be disappointed, continue to help your Master." Abbas was just reciting Rajaz, holding the water skin with his teeth. Look, it is a very, very harsh scene. A person is thirsty, holding the water skin with his teeth. Just imagine this oppression. Abbas is holding it with his teeth, but he is remembering the thirst of the children, he is not remembering his own thirst. Now as Abbas moved, as soon as he moved, an arrow of tyranny struck, it hit the water skin. Water started flowing from the water skin. As soon as the water started flowing, Abbas bowed his head. He turned the horse's direction. Now what will I do by going to the tents? Now what will I do by going to the tents? It is written in the Maqtal that as soon as Abbas bowed his head, a wretch came from behind and struck a mace of iron, a mace of iron, with full force on Abbas's head. Abbas fell from the back of the horse onto the earth of Karbala. O mourners, look, there is a natural thing, a physical thing, when a person falls from a height, his hands come forward first. But alas, Abbas-e-Alamdar, he had no hands, he fell face down. He fell on the earth of Karbala, and called out, "Master, come to help!" As soon as the voice reached Husayn's ears, Husayn held his back, and recited a dirge, "Now my back has broken. Now my back has broken. And my stratagem has failed. Abbas, now nothing can be seen, now nothing can be understood. And my enemy is taunting me." Abbas, the enemy is taunting! What happened to your standard-bearer? Your standard-bearer has been killed. The one you were proud of, he has been killed. Abbas reached a side, reached the lowlands, reached the bank of the Euphrates, and placed Abbas's head on his lap. There was some conversation between the brothers. Abbas made a will. Among the wills, one was that his body should not be taken to the tents. Now, while talking, Abbas's eyes closed. As soon as Abbas's eyes closed, Husayn recited a dirge again, "Today the eyes have slept." Abbas, with your death, those eyes that used to sleep will now wake up. Those ladies, those children who used to sleep peacefully because of you, will now wake up, now the wretches will sleep. Husayn took leave of Abbas while reciting the dirge. Woe to Husayn, woe to Abbas. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are troubled. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant righteous and virtuous children to those who are childless. Grant complete and immediate healing to those who are ill. Protect the life, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. Protect the high-ranking scholars and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Especially protect the shrine of Lady Zainab. O Lord, bless us with the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. By reciting one Surah Fatiha and three times Surah Tawhid, bestow the reward upon the deceased of Ghulam Ali ibn Abdul Aziz Lakhani, Lakhani family, Rupani family, Himani family, Lada family, and Narsidani family.

title: Dajjaal Se Zyaada Khatarnaak Kaun? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses a profound warning from Imam Reza (a.s.) regarding individuals who claim to love the Ahlulbayt but act in ways that harm the Shia community. The speaker explains that these people are more dangerous than the Dajjal because they befriend the enemies of the Ahlulbayt and alienate their true friends. This behavior creates confusion, making it difficult to distinguish between truth and falsehood or between a true believer and a hypocrite.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Guardian of the Age (Wali al-Asr), help us and do not let us perish. Hassan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz narrates that I heard Imam Reza (a.s.) saying: إِنَّا مِمَّنْ يَنْتَحِلُ مَوَدَّتَنَا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ فِتْنَةً عَلَى شِيعَتِنَا مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ (Indeed, among those who claim to love us, the Ahlulbayt, there will be those who are a greater trial for our Shias than the Dajjal). I asked, why is that? The Imam (a.s.) replied: بِمُوَالَاةِ أَعْدَائِنَا وَمُعَادَاةِ أَوْلِيَائِنَا (Due to befriending our enemies and showing enmity towards our friends). When this happens, اخْتَلَطَ الْحَقُّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَاشْتَبَهَ الْأَمْرُ (the truth will be mixed with falsehood and the matter will become ambiguous). فَلَمْ يُعْرَفْ مُؤْمِنٌ مِنْ مُنَافِقٍ (And it will become difficult to distinguish a believer from a hypocrite). Through this hadith, Imam Reza (a.s.) has warned us that those who show tolerance towards the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and act against basic Shia principles are actually weakening the school of Tashayyu. The biggest difficulty is that the Imam (a.s.) says these people will be among those who claim to love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Therefore, the trial of such people is more dangerous than the Dajjal, because these people mix truth and falsehood in such a way that it becomes difficult to distinguish between right and wrong, and a believer cannot be identified from a hypocrite. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds to hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). May He protect us from the trials and the instigators of this end time. May He grant us the ability to distinguish truth from falsehood and to recognize the believer from the hypocrite. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: EP#2 | Me’raaj Mein Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ka Noor | IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) Mi'raj and the divine presentation of the Ahlulbayt's Wilayah. The speaker highlights how Allah established the authority of the Imams, including Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), as a prerequisite for the acceptance of worship. The talk concludes with a prayer for the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of our time.
content:
That the war of the mind, login, there, longing, and meeting, at this time, red chili powder, juice, if it is not applied, then in the first phase, we have number 230, 371, that now the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) and all of you have the statement that I have gone on the path that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) went, then Allah's number 285, that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) has been revealed from one side on all things, on this the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ravan', and on this Allah said, 'You have spoken the truth, Muhammad, have you accepted this in your age, that the Prophet is the best among those of today?' Allah asked, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib', the Prophet replied, on this Allah, while bestowing upon them, Salman said, said that and subscribe and for you, you will never doubt one of your names, but this should also be done with me because I am, and you, after that, I again said at this time, and chose from them, and also worked for them, that I am Allah and He is the Wali, Muhammad, I have called you, and Ali, Fatima, Hasan, Hussain, and all from their lineage, I have chosen, and I presented your Wilayah before the first heavens and the earth, so whoever accepted it is a Momin in my sight, and whoever denies it is a Kafir in my sight. Muhammad, if any of my servants worships me so much that he becomes as thin as a thread, and then comes to me in such a state that he is a denier of your Wilayah, I will not accept his worship until he acknowledges the Wilayah of all of you. Muhammad, where would they like to see? The Prophet says that I said, 'Yes, O Lord', and believe that I said, 'Yes, O Lord', and then Allah said to me, 'And look to your right.' As soon as I turned, I saw that Ali was there with me, and Fatima, Hasan, Hussain, Ali, or Hussain, Muhammad ibn Ali, Jafar Iqbal, Muhammad Saeed, Jafar, Ali Musa, Muhammad Ali, Muhammad Hasan Ali, and all of them were reading in a state of connection, and I had shining stars in their midst. He said to me, 'Muhammad, these are my proofs, and this is the one who will take revenge for your blood. I swear by my honor and majesty, these are the proofs for my lovers, and they are the ones who will take revenge on my enemies.' We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He, by His honor and majesty, whose light He showed to His beloved on the night of Mi'raj, i.e., Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), may He hasten his reappearance and count us among his lovers and those who remain steadfast on his Wilayah. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

title: KULL-E-IMAAN (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2024 🎁🎉 | 28-JAN-2024 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive exploration of the status and virtues of Imam Ali (a.s.) through the lens of Quranic exegesis and historical battles. It addresses the theological necessity of recognizing the Ahl al-Bayt's unparalleled station while cautioning against both doubt and extremism. The session also features the 'Kull-e-Iman Grand Quiz,' which uses historical accounts like the Battle of Dhat al-Salasil to illustrate the leadership and spiritual authority of Imam Ali (a.s.).
content:
TSR presents 'Kull-e-Iman Al-Salaam Grand'. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Al-hu Kull-e-Wali Hasan [Music] Saf Kull-e-Sa Wali Waja Wan Daleel Khat Tasahu Wahu Faha [Music]. A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Sallallahu Ala Sayyid-e-Kull-e-Iman Al-Salaam Grand. The quiz rules and quiz link are now live, which The quiz link is now live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who have given the correct answers to all the questions, 14 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, who will be given these prizes. A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Dear ones, let us begin our discussion with the praise of that One who has no partner, whose throne of power was always there and will always remain. Blessings and peace be upon those chosen, Mustafa, Murtaza blessings and peace be upon those chosen, Mustafa, Murtaza servants of Allah, from whom the blessings received such honor that the One without a partner Himself sent blessings upon them and made them a means to reach Himself. The Lord of the Worlds has stated in His firm Book, the Holy Quran, 'Wa lillahil asmaul husna fad'uhu biha' (And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them). This matter was mentioned by Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in one of his long sermons: 'I am the beautiful name that Allah has commanded to be invoked through.' I am the Dhul-Qarnayn mentioned in the previous books. I am the owner of Solomon's ring. I am the companion of Nuh, and it was I who saved him. I am the companion of Ayyub, who was afflicted with trials, and it was I who gave him healing. I am the companion of Ibrahim. I am the one who made Musa cross the river, and I am the one who drowned Pharaoh and his army. In this way, from Hazrat Adam to Hazrat Isa, the Ali who helped all the prophets invisibly, on 13th Rajab, 30th year of Aam-ul-Feel, that helper of the prophets arrived in the apparent world in the House of arrived in the apparent world in the House of Kaaba. This matter was expressed in a very beautiful way by the late poet Ehsan Rizvi Danapuri in these verses: 'Sometimes becoming the voice of Truth, sometimes becoming the Wali of Truth. Sometimes becoming the voice of Truth, sometimes becoming the Wali of Truth, the hidden secret started appearing as a clear letter. A lightning bolt had started from the valley of Sinai, which, after swaying, finally settled in the Kaaba, becoming Ali.' Respected viewers, on the occasion of this blessed 13th Rajab, on behalf of the TSR team, we are once again present in your service with this 'Kull-e-Iman Grand Quiz', in which we discuss the life of the Master of the Universe, the Conqueror of all, Hazrat Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And based on this discussion, you have to give the correct answers to the questions asked. Among all those who give the correct answers, 14 lucky winners will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system, Insha'Allah. This is the third round of this 'Kull-e-Iman Grand Quiz'. Alhamdulillah, in the first round, we discussed the arrival of Amirul Momineen Ali (a.s.) in the House of Kaaba. We described its background, described its background. In that context, we narrated Hadiths. In the second round, i.e., last year, we mentioned the names and some titles of the Master of the Universe. If anyone wants Hadiths related to the arrival of Maula Ali (a.s.) in the House of Kaaba or wants to know about the names and titles of Maula, they can watch these videos on our YouTube channel. In today's third round, the important topic we have brought for you is 'Ali in the Quran', i.e., the mention of Imam Ali (a.s.) in the Holy Quran. And in this discussion, our two brothers, Ehsan Bhai and Kazim Bhai, will accompany us. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Ehsan Bhai and Kazim Bhai, we welcome you both to our gathering. Thank you, brother, and we begin the discussion with you. Ehsan Bhai, first of all, we ask you which verses have been mentioned in the Holy Quran regarding Maula Ali? Please present them before our viewers. Certainly, Insha'Allah. A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa Sallallahu Ala Sayyid-e-Awsia, Ghalib-e-Kull-e-Ghalib, Matlub-e-Kull-e-Talib, Sayyid-e-Awsia, Ghalib-e-Kull-e-Ghalib, Matlub-e-Kull-e-Talib, Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Shahzad Bhai, although this topic, i.e., 'Ali in the Quran', meaning the virtues of the Master of the Universe described in the Holy Quran, the verses that were revealed regarding him, and the discussion related to the virtues of the other Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), to have a complete debate on this or to mention those virtues completely is impossible. Indeed, indeed, indeed. But even if a person wants to have a detailed discussion, for that—and I am saying this without exaggeration—even one life is not enough for a detailed discussion. Indeed, and I am not just talking about my life, your life, but if the lives of all the creatures in the universe were combined, even then, a detailed discussion on the virtues of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) would not be possible. Subhan Allah. Indeed, well said. As far as the verses are concerned, we will try to discuss only a few verses and a few books. Insha'Allah. So, some books that specifically mention the virtues of the Master of the Universe, especially the verses revealed in the Holy Quran regarding the Master of the Universe. If anyone wants to refer to those verses or wants to study them, then a few books... If one wants to study, then by citing a few books, let us move our discussion forward. First of all, the treasure of Shi'ism, the treasure of the Shia religion, which we know by the name of the book 'Bihar al-Anwar'. Allamah Majlisi (may Allah have mercy on him) has discussed the general Imamate in volumes 23 to 27 of Bihar al-Anwar—these are five volumes, 23 to 27. In volume 23, from chapter 8 to 22, in approximately 525 pages, and then he continued this in volume 24. In volume 24, from chapter 23 to 68, there are approximately 400 pages. So, if you take only these volumes 23 and 24 of Bihar, there are a total of 61 chapters, 61 sections, in which, in more than 600 pages, only those verses of the Holy Quran have been discussed that were revealed regarding the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Subhan Allah. And then this was the discussion of general Imamate. Now, if we come towards the specific Imamate, that is, the actual life history of the Infallible Imams (a.s.), which begins from volume 35 regarding the life of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). In volume 35, from the fourth chapter to chapter number 24, there are approximately 250 pages. Besides that, this discussion continues in volume 36, continuing up to volume 36, only discussing the verses. In this, from chapter 25 to 39, there are approximately 190 pages. So here, 39, from 25 to 39, there are approximately 190 pages. So here, combining volumes 35 and 36, there are a total of 36 chapters, approximately 450 pages. That is, 600 pages there, 400 pages here, 450 pages here—in more than 1000 pages, only in one Bihar al-Anwar, only those verses have been discussed. There are a total of 97 chapters. Allamah Majlisi has collected more than a thousand pages only regarding the verses. Then, besides this, there is a book that the late Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him) compiled, named 'Mashariq Anwar al-Yaqin fi Fada'il Amir al-Mu'minin' (the virtues of the Commander of the Faithful, our master, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)). He collected 500 verses in this book. This book consists of more than 300 pages. 500 verses have been collected in it. Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani (may Allah have mercy on him) collected 1000 verses in the honor of the Master of the Universe, and that too in more than 900 pages. That is, so much discussion is present in the Holy Quran only regarding the Infallible Imams (a.s.) and especially regarding the Master of the Universe. But, Ahsan Bhai, I had a question for you. Yes, about this Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi, this book, and the author—there are different opinions and people's doubts and suspicions about him. People have also accused him of 'Ghulu' (exaggeration) and being a 'Ghali'. Yes. People have also accused him of being a 'Ghali'. Yes, yes, yes. Will you shed some light on this? Certainly, Insha'Allah. Now, as you said, many individuals have accused Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him) of 'Ghulu', that he was a victim of 'Ghulu', a 'Ghali'. Now, we will not state our own words. Among the most important books written in defense of Wilayah, which every Shia child knows—it is discussed in every house—among all those books, one important book is 'Al-Ghadir', authored by Allamah Amini (may Allah have mercy on him). Allamah Amini himself has given this clarification regarding Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi. So, these are not my words. In this book, which has been compiled—this book of Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him)—the compiler, the translator, has brought the entire quotation from Allamah Amini's 'Al-Ghadir' into this book. In its introduction itself, the one who wrote the biography of Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi, in that very introduction, he has brought this clarification of Allamah Amini regarding Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi. And Allamah Amini says this himself, and he has taken it from 'Al-Ghadir'. So, in 'Al-Ghadir', Allamah Amini has written about Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him): About Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him), Allamah Amini says—what does he write? That 'Al-Sheikh Radi al-Din Rajab Muhammad Rajab al-Bursi, known as Al-Hafiz'—this is his full name—he belonged to Hilla. He was a resident of Hilla. He was famous as 'Al-Hafiz', among the 'Urafa' (mystics) and scholars of the Imamiyyah. That is, he was among the famous 'Urafa', the well-known scholars of the Imamiyyah sect. Okay? So, the accusation of 'Ghulu' that is leveled, one should not be deceived by those accusations. He was our Shia scholar. That is, he was among the 'Urafa', meaning he was truly a man of gnosis, and among the Imamiyyah scholars. And a 'Faqih' (jurist) in his time, he had a good command over Hadith. He was a master of various sciences, an expert in Hadith, and an expert in Arabic literature and poetry. He possessed expertise in various sciences, Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him). And then, after that, what does the Allamah himself write about him regarding the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)? That as far as the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) is concerned, in that regard, he writes for Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him): He writes for Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him) that 'he had opinions and theories that were not understood by the people'. He writes that his opinions, his views—obviously based on Hadith—were such that most people did not agree with them. Why? Because their reach did not extend that far; those people could not understand those Hadiths that Hafiz al-Bursi had reached. And therefore, they accused Hafiz al-Bursi of 'Ghulu'. 'Irfa' (exaggeration), that is, exceeding the limit. They leveled that accusation. While further he writes, 'This is not true, this is not the truth, this is not reality.' And the one who wrote his biography here, in the introduction, he has also collected all those Hadiths from Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi's book where Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi himself has written against 'Ghulu'. Oh, he himself has recorded these Hadiths in his books. For example, and these Hadiths that Hafiz al-Bursi (may Allah have mercy on him) has brought, in them he writes that 'do not commit Ghulu'. In this, there is no mention of 'Ghulu' anywhere, not even from afar. It does not point towards 'Ghulu' from anywhere. And it is not that he did the act of exceeding the limit regarding the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Regarding the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), the act of exceeding the limit—what they call 'Irfa'—it is not that he described the Ahl al-Bayt as having the status of Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). There is nothing like that about them. Whereas, what kind of Hadiths has he brought in his books? He himself narrates a Hadith from the Master of the Universe and what does he narrate? That the Master of the Faithful (a.s.) said: 'Beware! Never commit Ghulu regarding us. And if you want to say something about us, then say that we are the servants of Allah and the created ones of that Lord.' Wah, Subhan Allah. 'And after that, say whatever you want about our virtues.' Subhan Allah. And then he also narrates a Hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in this same regard, in which Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Consider us as created beings. Do not consider us as the Creator. Consider us as created beings. After that, say whatever you want about us, for you will never reach our reality.' He has collected this in this book. That is, the limit of the true virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), the level that exists, no one can reach it. And it often happens that people level the accusation of 'Ghulu' when virtues are described. Why do they do this? Because it is not within everyone's capacity to... It is not within everyone's capacity to bear the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). It is true. According to the Hadiths, to bear these virtues, one must either be a sent Prophet, or a close angel, or such a believer whose faith has been tested by Allah. And that is why there are degrees of faith and gnosis. You see, for example, Janab-e-Salman was at the 10th degree, Janab-e-Abu Dharr was at the 9th degree. Abu Dharr does not know what is at the level of Salman. And that is why what narrations do we find? That if Abu Dharr knew what was in Salman's heart, he would have killed him. Right? Even Abu Dharr could not bear it. Janab-e-Abu Dharr, yes, on whom the earth has not seen anyone more truthful than him. Even Janab-e-Abu Dharr could not bear what the level of Janab-e-Salman's faith was. And yet, despite this, Janab-e-Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) never objected to Janab-e-Salman. He did not object. He never leveled the accusation of 'Ghulu'. Because Janab-e-Abu Dharr knew what his level was, what Janab-e-Salman's level was. And as far as the level is concerned, the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) themselves—these are the Master's own words from his sermon. No one can reach the status and the destination of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). These people who actually level the accusation of 'Ghulu' do so because they try to measure this status with their own intellects. Subhan Allah. While the Master's saying... Subhan Allah. While the Master's saying is: The Master says, 'Who is there who can reach our gnosis? Or recognize our degree? Or, having seen our miracles, have the strength to bear it? Or be able to measure our destination?' That is, there is no one. 'The intellects are bewildered, the intellects are bewildered, and the understandings are helpless in understanding what I describe.' The Master says, 'What I am describing, people do not understand.' Then, 'The scholars, the scholars, the scholars, the scholars'—the scholars, despite the level of their knowledge, the great scholars cannot reach there. Indeed, that is, the scholars, the right—that is, the right to describe the virtues, no one can fulfill it. Poets run out of words. The Master is saying, the Master is describing. Poets do not have the words. Often in our society, it happens that poets are accused of describing too much, of using 'Ghulu' in their poetry, of exceeding the limits based on their own thoughts. Although, if seen according to this saying of the Master, then all the Khatibs, all the poets, all the scholars who describe the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), if seen in the light of this Hadith, then the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), the virtues of the Commander of the Faithful... The virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), the virtues of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), are such a vast ocean, such a roaring ocean, whose waves are flowing constantly. And all the scholars, the jurists, the wise, the poets—all of them are standing on the shore of that ocean, standing with their bowls of words, hoping that some moisture from that ocean of virtues might fall into this bowl, so that some words might flow from their tongues. The reality is just this. The reality is that no one can reach the limit of their virtues. After this, the Master says in this same sermon, the Master says: 'Who can recognize him? Who can measure him? Who can know anything about him, who is a ray of the splendor of Allah's Majesty and the nobility of the heavens?' Wah, wah, wah, wah. One cannot compare this to the sun. One cannot even look at the sun. And where have they set out to measure the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)? One cannot bear the light of the sun. How can anyone bear the splendor of Majesty? No one can reach there. The Master says, 'The status of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) is far higher than that...' Far higher than that, that their status should be described, that it should be described. People do not have the words, no one has the words to describe their status. And to compare or equate anyone in the worlds with the family of Muhammad (a.s.), this is impossible. No one can do it. Those who actually object to the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), they should look at themselves, what they are. When the Master says that no one can reach us, then when no one can reach them, where does the question of equating them arise? To this day, Muslims are bewildered, troubled. So it is not possible for anyone to measure their virtues, for anyone to reach their virtues. This reference of Allamah Amini (may Allah have mercy on him) that you gave about Hafiz Rajab, may Allah have mercy on him, was a very, very important discussion because the doubts and suspicions that people have put in their hearts, Allamah Amini (may Allah have mercy on him) has set aside all those doubts and suspicions. Indeed, indeed. And viewers, it is requested of you that people who object to the virtues, often those who measure the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) do so based on their own intellect. Whatever things, whatever virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) fit into their intellect, they accept them. That they accept what comes to their intellect and deny and reject what does not. Doubting the virtues (Faza'il) of Mawla is actually a very grave sin. Regarding this, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked to explain something about doubt. He narrated a hadith before the people regarding this virtue and this doubt: 'No one doubts them except that they will exit the fold of religion.' Wow, wow, wow. 'And no one will doubt them except that they are a hypocrite.' Indeed, the consequence is so dangerous regarding the virtues of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the authority that Allah has granted them. If anyone doubts it, it is as if they have exited the fold of religion. Indeed, indeed. So, how dangerous a thing it is to doubt the virtues of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Indeed, indeed. Kazim Bhai, taking this point forward, let us advance our discussion. Regarding our topic, 'Ali in the Quran,' please explain what other verses exist in the Holy Quran that were revealed in the honor of Mawla Ali (a.s.). Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi. Wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi. First of all, I offer congratulations to the viewers on the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). And as Shahzad Bhai asked where the mention of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) exists in the Quran, we would like to say: where is the mention of Ali not present in the Quran? Subhan Allah, wow, Subhan Allah. Ali is hidden in every verse of the Quran. Indeed, Ali is hidden in every letter of the Quran. Ali is hidden in every chapter of the Quran. Ali is hidden in every dot of the Quran. And as Ahsan Bhai presented many proofs in the beginning regarding how many books contain the mention of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and how many pages it covers. Proving the Wilayah or Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin through Quranic verses—you have just witnessed all those proofs here, whether it is Bihar al-Anwar, the book of Sayyid Hashim Bahrani, or the book of Hafiz Rajab Bursi. All these books were mentioned, and Ahsan Bhai presented things with proper, reasoned arguments. So, our every belief, Shahzad Bhai, contains certainty. It contains proofs, it contains arguments, it is full of evidence. So come, a few... It is full of evidence. So, let us present a few verses to the viewers from Surah Al-Furqan, in which Allah (SWT) is presenting the mention of Amir al-Mu'minin. If you ponder over verse number 27 of Surah Al-Furqan or observe it, you will see the mention of Amir al-Mu'minin, in which the Lord of Majesty says: 'Yawma ya'addu al-zalimu 'ala yadayhi yaqulu ya laytani ittakhadhtu ma'a al-rasuli sabila' (The day the wrongdoer will bite his hands, saying: 'Oh, I wish I had taken a path with the Messenger'). Now, two people are being mentioned here. The Quran says that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoer will bite his hands, and not just bite his hands, but will say, 'Oh, I wish I had taken the Sabil (path) with the Messenger.' Wow, wow. That he should have followed the Messenger, and along with the Messenger, he should have taken the Sabil. Now, let us see from the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) who is meant by 'Sabil.' Because here, the person who is expressing regret over his life on the Day of Judgment is mentioning the acceptance of the Sabil, saying, 'I wish I had accepted the Sabil, then my life would not be in this state today.' Imam (a.s.) states... Meaning 'Ma'a al-rasuli sabila'—what is meant by this verse? It means Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) (Sallallahu 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad). Here, 'Sabil' in this verse refers to Amir al-Mu'minin. Right? The person is saying, 'I wish I had accepted the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin along with the Messenger.' And because I did not accept the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin, today I am biting my hands. In a way, Kazim Bhai, many people accuse us, saying, 'You have made up your own Kalima.' In light of this verse, it is clear that on the Day of Judgment, if someone does not accept 'Aliyun Waliullah' along with 'Muhammadur Rasulullah,' they will have to bite their hands. Indeed, indeed, they will have to bite them. And the point to ponder is how people can ignore such clear verses. What a speaking verse of the Quran! Who is the Sabil? We say, 'I wish I had accepted the Sabil.' So, viewers, Kazim Bhai, this means that enmity towards the Sabil is very dangerous. Indeed, very dangerous. A person will bite their own hand. Indeed, indeed, indeed. So, those who hold enmity towards the Sabil should be very, very careful about what their end will be in the hereafter. What to say, Subhan Allah. Shahzad, as you just said, what will their end be in the hereafter? So, let us present one more... What will their end be in the hereafter? So, let us present one more hadith for you and the viewers, in which Imam Sadiq (a.s.) is stating—listen carefully: 'Amir al-Mu'minin is the door of Allah, except through whom no one can enter the presence of Allah.' What to say! And he is the Sabil, and he is the path, and whoever tried to walk on any path other than his will be destroyed. What to say, Subhan Allah. Meaning, if someone wants to walk on the right path, it is the path of Amir al-Mu'minin. Indeed, that is why he is the Sirat al-Mustaqim (the Straight Path). That is why he is the Sirat al-Mustaqim. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. And Ahsan Bhai, I would like to clarify through another verse that whoever abandons or leaves the Sabil, what will be their state? I would like to present this through a verse of the Quran, in which the first verse of Surah Muhammad mentions: 'Alladhina kafaru wa saddu 'an sabilillah' (Those who disbelieved and averted others from the path of Allah). They not only stayed away themselves but also tried to keep others away. So what will happen? 'Al-a'mal'... So what will happen? 'Al-a'mal'—Allah will destroy their deeds. Meaning, if someone is trying to keep people away from Amir al-Mu'minin, or as Ahsan Bhai just said, from 'Aliyun Waliullah,' then Allah will not just destroy him, but will destroy his deeds and him as well. Meaning, without Wilayah, no one's deed will be accepted at all. It will not be accepted at all. And then, if you look at the exegesis of this verse by Imam Baqir (a.s.), he states: 'Fi qawlihi alladhina kafaru'—meaning the Banu Umayya. And then Mawla says: 'Wa saddu 'an sabilillah'—those who keep people away from the Sabil, that Sabil is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Wow, wow. The Sabil from which people are kept away is the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), it is the person of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). The interesting point here is that in this verse of Surah Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), Ali (a.s.) is called the Sabil of Allah. Exactly, the Sabil of Allah—the path that leads a person to Allah. Exactly. We mentioned verse 27 of Surah Al-Furqan here. If you look at the verses after it, verse 28 and 29, they are also such speaking verses... So, we will travel at night and go to them, and go so close to them that tomorrow when the battle starts in the morning, they will not even expect how close we have come to them. And it will be easy for us to face them. We will attack in a way they did not even expect.' Now, the battle started in the morning. In what state did the battle start in the morning? The battle did not start directly. First of all, the sentence of the narration is that when the morning first appeared, when the dawn appeared, first of all, Maula (a.s.) gave the Adhan for prayer. The sound of Ali (a.s.)'s Adhan reached their ears. Now, just imagine what the quality of that Adhan would be whose Muezzin is Ali (a.s.). The Adhan that Ali (a.s.) gave, what would be the quality of that Adhan? Hearing the Adhan, those enemies were terrified, their senses were blown away, that how did Ali (a.s.) come so close to us? How did he come so close? So, one of them said, meaning some said to others, 'Let's do...' They said, meaning some said to others, 'Let us do one thing, let us go for a confrontation.' So, a young man came forward, he appeared there. These people had arrived there with their entire army, all their horses, and everything. Ahsan Bhai, this is where this verse of the Quran is being revealed, perhaps, in which the first verse is 'Wal-Adiyati Dabha'—swearing by those running horses with which Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) attacked. Now, viewers should note that here Allah is swearing by the horse. Right? So, what must be the status of the rider on that horse? Subhan Allah. Right. And if you go towards the second verse, the Lord of Majesty is declaring, 'Fal-Muriyati Qadha'—those that strike sparks with their hooves. Meaning, here it is not about the horse, but about that spark; when those hooves strike the stones and the sparks that emerge, Allah is swearing by that spark. Then after that, 'Fal-Mughirati Subha'—then those who attack at the time of dawn. Then it is talking about that dawn which Ahsan Bhai was just mentioning, that Amir al-Mu'minin gave the Adhan; that is being referred to here. Then after that, it mentions 'Fa-Atharna bihi Naq'a'—then those who stir up clouds of dust in battle. And now, Ahsan Bhai, from here the sequence of the battle begins. Now, how did the sequence of the battle begin? That a young man came from there. Right? Which is in the traditions, that he who was in his... Right? Which is in the traditions, that he was very intense in his Kufr, meaning his enmity towards the Muslims was very severe. Such a young man came forward and he just gave this call. Now look, he insulted the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and showed audacity. What did he say? He said, 'Ya Ashab Sahil Kazzab'—Allah is the Greatest. Meaning, calling the Prophet—God forbid, God forbid—a sorcerer and a liar; he used such words for the Prophet. He used insulting words. And he challenged the Muslims, 'Where are his followers? O Muhammad, who among you is Muhammad? Whoever it is, come forward and face me.' That is how he challenged. So, when Maula heard his insulting words, he had challenged—what had he called out? He had asked, 'Who is Muhammad among you? Come forward.' Ali (a.s.) went immediately. Ali (a.s.) went forward. The sentence in the tradition is: 'Fakhraja Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).' Maula went immediately and first of all, he answered his audacity. It is not that he didn't fight directly. He had shown audacity. He answered his audacity. Maula said, 'Thikalat-ka Ummuk' (May your mother mourn you), 'Wa anta Sahir, Antal Kazzab' (And you are the sorcerer, you are the liar). 'Haqq-u Muhammad, Haqq-u Muhammad'—Muhammad is the one who has come from the Truth, has brought the Truth. Wah, wah, wah, wah! When this happened, now after that... Wah, wah, wah! When this happened, now after that, when he saw that such answers were coming from the front—answers like which had not come until now—because until now, those who were there were fleeing. But when he saw that such an answer was coming from the front, and such a fluent and eloquent answer, and the same words that the opponent was choosing were being used to answer him back, he immediately turned and asked, 'Who are you?' So Maula said, 'I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his son-in-law.' Wah, Subhan Allah! So as soon as he heard this, he immediately turned and asked, 'Have these virtues, this status, this rank been given to you by Muhammad? Meaning, has Muhammad bestowed all these virtues upon you?' Maula said, 'Yes, this is his honor for me; he has bestowed this honor upon me that I am his son-in-law.' And then after that, as soon as he heard that 'Yes, this is from him,' he is an enemy, yes, he is an enemy, but he immediately admits, 'If that is the case, that all these ranks you have received are from him, then you and Muhammad are one and the same.' Wah, wah! 'To us, you both are one.' Wah, wah! Meaning, even the hypocrite and the non-believer has the discernment that, 'Brother, the status that Amir al-Mu'minin is describing, and if this...' Amir al-Mu'minin is describing, and if this status is from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), then both are one. And here you see the condition of the Muslims; the Muslims do not understand. To this day, the Muslims have not been able to understand this; the polytheists understood, but the Muslims did not. Yes. Right after that, he says, 'Ma kuntu ubali' (I do not care), 'whether I kill you or kill Muhammad; to me, you both are equal.' Equal. Now he said this, and as you said, the beginning of the battle. Now here the battle began. First of all, between these two—the young man who came to fight and Maula—first, there were two strikes, which both parried. After that, the third strike, Maula-e-Kainat struck such a blow that he collapsed. That one strike killed him. And in the tradition, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, as soon as Maula struck that blow, 'Wa bi ruhihi ila-n-nar' (And Allah sent his soul to Hell very quickly). Wah, wah, wah, wah! Beshumar! And after that, as soon as his soul reached Hell, Maula struck here, and after that, he hit him with one hand, struck him, and immediately gave a call, 'Hal min mubariz?' (Is there anyone who will face me?). Wah! And the tradition says then his brother came, that wretched one's brother came forward. Now this one who came, this was not even for one strike... He came forward. Now this one who came, he was not even worth one strike. When Maula struck one blow, he collapsed in that very strike. Right? Then after that, Ali (a.s.) finished him off too. He also sent him to Hell. He struck such a blow upon him that he could not withstand it. He could not bear it. Right? He also went to Hell. Allah sent his soul to Hell as well. Then a third person came. He had brought 500 people with him. He brought 500 people. He met the same fate. He did not last even one strike. After that, a fourth person came; Maula sent him to Hell in one strike as well, and then his cousin came; he also sent him to Hell in one strike. In this way, Maula was cutting down each one in a single strike and was breaking the courage of their enemies. Now, here the verse of the Quran is being revealed in which it is declared, 'Fasata-ta bihi naq'a'—Ali killed their brave soldiers, the brave soldiers of the enemy. Indeed, here what you are describing, that they were coming one after another and Ali was sending everyone to Hell, this verse of the Quran is pointing towards that. And after this, yes, so meaning in the Holy Quran, the way this sequence of battle happened, the verses have come in the exact same way, which happened during the entire sequence of the battle. Indeed, indeed, because you... Happened inside. Indeed, indeed, because you asked, right, that the entire Surah is describing that battle, and the entire Surah was revealed in the virtue of Maula, in his merits. Subhan Allah. Now what happened is that as soon as Maula sent them all to their deserved end, one by one, now the remaining army—now the tradition says that no one came forward to attack. Now, whoever was there, Maula took them all as prisoners, and as you said, 'Dhat al-Salasil' (The possessor of chains), because Maula shackled them all in chains and took all the wealth as war booty. Now the battle was won; the battle was won here. Now after this, Maula is returning with his army. Here Maula is returning with the army; there, Archangel Gabriel informed the Prophet that victory had been achieved. As soon as that news was received, the Prophet left from there. The Prophet left from Medina. Maula left from here. The tradition says that the Prophet came three miles ahead with his companions, and there he met Maula. And there, the Prophet welcomed Maula, and he welcomed him in such a way that as soon as Maula-e-Kainat saw the Prophet coming from the front, Maula got down from his horse. In honor of the Prophet, he got down from his horse, and here the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) also, in his love for Maula, he also got down from his horse and... In his love, he also got down from his horse, and both of them came face to face. The Prophet kissed Maula's forehead, and then in the same way, all the Muslims—since both of them had gotten off their horses—all the Muslims, in honor of both of them, all of them got off their horses. Everyone who was brought as a prisoner from there was taken as a prisoner, and the war booty, all those things were taken into their possession. After that, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that the amount of war booty the Muslims received in this battle, which came into the hands of the Muslims, did not happen in any other battle. After this, if there was any—meaning, if the Muslims received such war booty, it was the Battle of Khaybar. Wah, wah! Meaning, after the Battle of Khaybar, if the Muslims received the most war booty, it was in this battle. And that is why the Imam says, 'Tabarak wa Ta'ala fi dhalika al-yawm' (On this day, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala revealed this Surah, Surah Al-Adiyat). Wah, wah! This was it. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah! Very good, Mashallah, Mashallah. Ahsan Bhai, Kazim Bhai, the background that you mentioned, the last point that you made, that the Messenger of Islam came from Medina and Maula Ali from the battle, this background seemed just like the background of Ghadir, where Maula Ali and the Messenger of Islam are meeting together. And the way the Messenger of Islam welcomed Maula Ali here reminds one of Ghadir. Meaning, if we look at the reminder that... Reminds us. Meaning, if we look, it seems like an open field. The Messenger of Islam is welcoming him. It is exactly the same as we found in Ghadir, how the Messenger of Islam made Maula Ali the Master (Maula). So, the virtues of Maula Ali will never end. And they cannot, because if you look, a tradition is found from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Islam has said, 'If all the trees become pens, all the oceans become ink, the Jinn keep calculating, and humans start writing, even then the virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) cannot be counted.' title: Waajib Hajj Ke Badle Ziyaarat? - E'teraaz Ka Jawaab [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common misconception that Shias view the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) as a substitute for the obligatory Hajj. The speaker clarifies that Ziyarat does not exempt a believer from the duty of Hajj, but rather serves as a spiritual opportunity for those currently unable to afford the pilgrimage. By citing narrations from Imam Reza (a.s.), the lecture emphasizes that the reward of Hajj is granted by Allah to Ziyarat pilgrims as a divine favor, not as a replacement for the Sharia-mandated Hajj.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa Sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa Aalihi. Assalamu ala al-Husain, wa ala Ali ibn al-Husain, wa ala awlad al-Husain, wa ala ashab al-Husain. Those who object to Imam Hussain (a.s.) often say that people have placed this (Ziyarat) in competition with the obligatory Hajj, and by doing so, they are distancing people from the obligatory Hajj. To those people, we want to say that this is not our Hajj, but our Ziyarat. It is narrated from Abdur Rahman that Imam Reza (a.s.) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is like one who has performed Hajj and Umrah.' They asked, 'Mawla, is this a substitute for Hajj?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'No, rather this Ziyarat holds the reward of Hajj for those who are not financially capable, until they become capable and perform Hajj at Baitullah al-Haram.' Do you not know that every day 70,000 angels... Do you not know that every day 70,000 angels perform Tawaf of the House of Allah (Azzawajal)? When night falls, they return to the sky, and in their place, another group of 70,000 angels comes for Tawaf of the Kaaba, who remain there until morning. However, the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is more honorable in the sight of Allah (Azzawajal) than the Kaaba. Therefore, at the time of every prayer, 70,000 angels with disheveled hair and covered in dust go for his Ziyarat, and they do not get the opportunity for this Ziyarat again until the Day of Judgment. From this Hadith of Imam Reza (a.s.), it is proven that the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is not a substitute for Hajj. Therefore, no one should fall into the misunderstanding that if they have performed Ziyarat, they are exempted from the obligation of Hajj; that is not the case at all. But on the other hand, due to one's own negligence or lack of resources, one should not think that if they cannot go for Hajj, they should not go for Ziyarat either. Because according to this Hadith, this Ziyarat will give the reward of Hajj to those who are not financially capable. Granting the reward is in the hands of Allah (Azzawajal). Granting the reward is in the hands of Allah (Azzawajal), and it is the decision of that Almighty God to give the reward equal to Hajj for the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Therefore, objecting that Shias consider Ziyarat a substitute for Hajj is merely an accusation against Shias and has no basis in reality. Rather, through such objections, they are trying to distance Shias from Ziyarat. May Allah (SWT) grant everyone the opportunity to perform Hajj of Baitullah repeatedly and Ziyarat of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Aali Muhammad (a.s.). Ameen Ya Rabbal Alameen.

The importance of invoking and remembering the Imam of our time, Sahib al-Zaman.
