chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the arrival of Imam Mahdi at the Kaaba and the establishment of divine justice worldwide.

title: Majlis 8 | Marefat-e-Nooraaniyyah (Part-7) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound metaphysical status of the Ahlulbayt, focusing on their luminous (Nurani) existence and their role as the source of creation under Allah's authority. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the significance of mourning for Imam Husayn and the unique spiritual station of Imam Ali, emphasizing his presence in the lives of past prophets and his role in divine deliverance. The session concludes by connecting these theological concepts to the tragic martyrdom of Ali Akbar at Karbala, highlighting the eternal life of the martyrs.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Keep looking back at me, Ali Akbar. Keep looking back at me, Ali Akbar. Live for a while, live for a while, your father, Ali Akbar. Keep looking back at me, Ali Akbar. If you fall from your life, the world will change. Who will take us towards the battlefield? The killers will tell, won't they, the killers will tell the way, Ali Akbar. Keep looking back at me, Ali Akbar. News of the sick one of Medina must be coming. You are taking my eyesight with you too. How will I read the letter, how will I read the letter, Sugra, Ali Akbar. Keep looking back at me, Ali Akbar. And it will become difficult for me, it will become difficult for me to come, my son. Do not go far away in the battlefield, my son. Now I cannot even walk, Ali Akbar. Keep looking back at me, Ali Akbar. And if my grandfather asks why you were late. Tell him that permission was obtained with great difficulty. Come and embrace me, come and embrace me again, Ali Akbar. Oh, grandfather went when old age had come upon mother. You are leaving, the state of the daughter of Ali (a.s.) is strange. Zainab (s.a.) is becoming frail, Zainab (s.a.) is becoming frail, Ali Akbar (a.s.). And oh my son, I entrust you to your father. Those with spears are standing and laughing on the battlefield. Let me look at you one more time, let me look at you one more time, oh chest of Ali Akbar (a.s.). Oh, keep looking back at me as you go, Ali Akbar (a.s.). Beating his head, the Maula (a.s.) gave this call, oh Takallum. The veil of Zainab (s.a.) is the witness to my loneliness. I cannot give you a shroud, I cannot give you a shroud, Ali Akbar (a.s.). Keep looking back at me as you go, Ali Akbar (a.s.). Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. May Allah have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the pious and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Blessings of Allah be upon him and his infallible family, those from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, our Imam of the time, the master of our affair, our owner, our master, our beloved, our healer, our companion, and our intimate friend. The secure cave and the helper of those who seek help, the upright, may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Our master and our leader, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.), said: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn (a.s.) has wounded our eyelids and caused our tears to flow; so let the weepers weep for the likes of Husayn (a.s.).' The truth was spoken by our master Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.), Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The Hadith Sharif whose recitation I have had the honor of performing, in that Hadith, Imam Rida (a.s.) says: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn (a.s.) has wounded our eyelids.' Surely, the grief for Husayn (a.s.) on the day of Husayn (a.s.) has wounded our eyelids. Meaning, we weep so much, we cry so much for Husayn (a.s.) that our eyes have become wounded. 'And our tears have flowed,' and the stream of tears from our eyes is continuous, we are weeping incessantly. 'So let the weepers weep for the likes of Husayn (a.s.).' So, if anyone is to weep, they should weep for someone like Husayn (a.s.). Meaning, if anyone is truly worthy of weeping, the most worthy is Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.). The discussion was ongoing regarding the Hadith of Ma'rifat al-Nuraniyya. As I submitted, this Hadith, in terms of its contents and concepts—concepts which are a bit difficult—is such that after reading them, a person becomes aware to a great extent of the reality of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and their luminous reality. Which people generally do not describe, and if someone does, a fatwa of exaggeration (Ghuluw) is issued against them, and such things happen; that is ignorance. But it is not like that, because in our traditions, as I submitted, in the traditions of both schools, in the books of Hadith, there are many such traditions. Meaning, if you study the Shia books yourself, even the great scholars of the past—and the later scholars like Allama Majlisi and others—they wrote books, and even before them, scholars wrote books under the names of 'Anwar' or 'Nur al-Anwar', or for example, they dedicated entire chapters to this. For instance, in Bihar al-Anwar, volume 15, the first chapter is entirely about the luminous creation of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the creation of the light of the Messenger of Allah, and it is a very detailed discussion. Similarly, in Bihar al-Anwar, volume 25, the first chapter is very detailed about the light creation of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), there are many Hadiths in it, and it is also in many other authentic books. It is in Usul al-Kafi and other books, in many places. It is found in traditions, in Ziyarat, everywhere. So there is no exaggeration in this. Just as I submitted to you, what is the standard for exaggeration? Exaggeration is to make any human, any creature, a creator. Not to make the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) God, for example. That they have reached the level of God, or that God has incarnated in them, or they have united with God, or they have become one with God, or they are avatars of God—all of this is exaggeration. Just bring them below the level of God, and even then, as mentioned before—in this very tradition, there is a part that we are continuing—the Maula of the universe (a.s.) says, recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The Maula says: 'O Salman, O Jundab (Abu Dharr), Allah has granted me things that He has not granted to anyone before me, neither among the first nor the last.' Neither has anyone ever had them before, nor will anyone ever have them in the future. Allah has granted that to me. Just understand this much, that Allah has granted this to me. Meaning, this cannot be grasped by our intellects. But the Maula is giving hints here that Allah has granted me such things. Just keep one thing in mind: except for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Maula of the universe (a.s.) is superior to everyone else. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is the noblest of prophets and messengers, the noblest of all creation. So, apart from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), no one can compete with the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). No one can match him. So he says, 'among the first and the last.' Not for any sent prophet, nor for any close angel. Allah has not granted these things to any prophet, nor to any angel—and which angels? There are many angels. The number of angels is many times greater than humans, meaning there is no comparison. Allah has created so many angels. So leave the angels aside, that is a different topic. Meaning, we are talking about the 'Mala'ik al-Muqarrab' (the close angels). And who are they? They are only four. They are only four: Jibra'il, Mika'il, Izra'il, Israfil, that's it. There is no one else besides them. You know Jibra'il is the angel of revelation. You know Mika'il is the angel of sustenance. You know Izra'il very well; there is no one who doesn't recognize him, and if you don't recognize him, you will recognize him soon. They call him the Angel of Death. Right? And make friends with him from now on. So that when he comes to take your soul, he takes it gently. So whenever you take his name, the Angel of Death, take it with great respect. Hazrat Malakul Maut (a.s.). So that he says, 'This person used to respect me,' and when he comes, he also takes the soul with respect. Right? Because there are many ways to take a soul. You know it is present in the traditions that Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) said, 'O Angel of Death, how do you take a soul?' How do you take a soul? He said, 'You will not be able to bear it.' Anyway, Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) was a prophet, Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) was a prophet of firm resolve, upon our Prophet and his family be peace, such a great prophet, but the Angel of Death says to him, 'You will not be able to bear it.' He said, 'No, no, I will bear it, tell me, tell me, tell me.' He insisted a lot, so he said, 'Alright, turn your face away.' He said, 'Alright.' So when he asked, 'In what state do you come when you go to take a soul?' Whose? A non-believer's, other than a believer, not a believer. Other than a believer. So the Angel of Death said, 'You cannot bear it.' He said, 'No, I will bear it, tell me.' So he said, 'Alright, turn your face away.' We are reading this Hadith, we are not telling a story. This is a Hadith of the family of Muhammad (a.s.). So he said, 'Turn your face away.' He turned his face away. He said, 'Alright, now when...'—the form in which he takes the soul of a non-believer—so he said, 'Yes Ibrahim, now look at me.' So it is written in the Hadith that as soon as Ibrahim (a.s.) looked, he fainted. He fainted upon seeing him. The Angel of Death hadn't even performed any procedure yet. Is it clear? He fainted upon seeing him. He said, 'You are a prophet.' When he regained consciousness after a while, the Angel of Death came in his normal self, as he used to meet prophets, in that condition. So Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) said to him, 'O Angel of Death, if you only show your face to a non-believer, that is enough for his punishment.' That is enough for his punishment, and nothing else. I mean, it is so terrifying when he... However, it is not like that for a Momin (believer). A Momin, who is Ali-un-Waliullah—meaning one who practices Wilayah and Bara'ah, who performs both Wilayah and Bara'ah—the Angel of Death comes to him like a very affectionate brother. And he takes his soul with great kindness, very gently, and with much love. With great mercy, very nicely. In fact, a word is written in the Hadith, a simile is given, that it will be just like a slight pinch; that is all, nothing more than that. But for others, those who are not Ali-un-Waliullah, who do not practice Wilayah and Bara'ah, it is very severe. Anyway, this is Hazrat Izra'il (a.s.), so I just submitted in your service that you should be very friendly with Hazrat Izra'il. Right? Recognize him too. Allama Majlisi Rizwanullah... Allah (s.w.t.) has a whole chapter in Bihar al-Anwar about these people, do you know? I mean, this whole chapter on the Malaika al-Muqarrabin (the near angels), these four angels. Anyway, after that, the last one is Israfil. You know Israfil; he will blow the Sur (Trumpet) when the world is to be annihilated. Annihilated means their existence will be taken away from them. Not death—annihilation is not death. There is a difference between death and annihilation. Death is a creation of Allah, remember. It is written in the Quran, in which Surah? Surah Mulk, you recite Surah Mulk, right? 'Tabarakalladhi biyadihil mulk', Surah number 67. Surah number 67, 'Tabarakalladhi biyadihil mulk wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir'. Blessed is the Being of Allah, 'Tabarakalladhi', in whose hand is the entire ownership. Ownership means the kingdom, and which kingdom? The kingdom of existence, from which all things come into being and exist. All things that exist, exist because of this, otherwise everything would be 'ma'dum' (non-existent). So, 'Tabarakalladhi', blessed is that Being, the Being of Allah, 'biyadihil mulk', everything is under His control, 'wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir', and He has power over all things. 'Alladhi'—this is the second verse—'khalaqal mawta wal hayata', He created death and life. Look, in the Quran too, death is mentioned first, then life is mentioned; life comes later. Now, there is a secret in this too, but that is not the topic here. It is a bit of a tough discussion. 'Alladhi khalaqal mawta', He created death, He created life. Both these things are Allah's creation; they are creatures of Allah, they are created by Allah. So death is not the name of annihilation. What is annihilation? Annihilation is when Allah takes away existence from them, the 'Nur-e-Wujud' (Light of Existence) is completely taken away from them. And that is why, now, to whom will the 'Nur-e-Wujud' go? To those who are its original owners, whom Allah has made the original owners. Who has He made the original owners? Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.). Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. This is their light, right? And listen to the proof of this from the Quran too. This is the proof from the Quran. The Quran says, 'Kullu man 'alayha fan', everything that is on it will perish. 'Fan' means annihilation; 'fan' is the subjective noun of annihilation. Everything is going to perish. 'Wa yabqa wajhu rabbika dhul jalali wal ikram', and nothing will remain except the Face of your Lord, the Face of your Lord who is 'Dhul Jalali wal Ikram', the Possessor of Majesty and Honor. It is not talking about Allah—Allah is 'Dhul Jalali wal Ikram' anyway—but 'Wajhullah' is 'Dhul Jalali wal Ikram'. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Now, who is Wajhullah? Who is Wajhullah? Mawla (a.s.) says, 'Wa ana Wajhullah' (And I am the Face of Allah). Recite a Salawat: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. In this same Hadith, it will come later, Insha'Allah, you will see if Allah grants the opportunity to reach there, 'Ana Wajhullah', I am the Face of Allah. Meaning, all such attributes that are in the Quran, all belong to the Ahlulbayt. Wajhullah, Aynullah, Lisanullah, Jambullah, Yadullah—all are the Ahlulbayt. Who is Yadullah? Amirul Momineen (a.s.). Who is Lisanullah? Amirul Momineen (a.s.). Who is Aynullah? Amirul Momineen (a.s.). Who is Jambullah? Amirul Momineen (a.s.). All these things are for Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.). Is it clear to you? I mean, it is a great status, a great position. The Quran says, 'Wa yabqa wajhu rabbika', only that which remains, everything else will perish. Allah will take away the 'Nur-e-Wujud' (Light of Existence) from everyone. Meaning, they will not die—look, I am emphasizing this a lot—they will not die. Dying is a creation of Allah. Meaning, they will become 'ma'dum' (non-existent). 'Ma'dum' means non-existent. Now, what does 'ma'dum' mean? What does non-existent mean? Meaning, they will not even be worthy of mention. If someone tries to mention them, tries to point towards them, they won't even be able to point. Let me give an example. If someone is not here, for instance, and we ask, 'Where is so-and-so?', if he is not here, you cannot point and say, 'He is sitting there,' because you cannot see him. Oh brother, he is not there; he simply does not exist. When a person dies, his identity by name is taken away; that much is there. Look, as long as his last breath continues, people ask, 'How is your father's health? How is your brother's health?' They ask by name, 'How are they?' But as soon as his soul is taken, death comes, his identity by that name ends. The identity of the body ends. Now what do people say? 'Has the body arrived or not? How long until the funeral procession starts?' People talk like this. Today, in this world, if you try talking to someone like this, 'Has your body arrived?', see what he does to you. You can speak, but after death, this is the fate of everyone, no matter how great a person he was in the world, he had a great government, but once he died here, it is over. Now, after that, when they bury him, just a plaque is placed on the grave. Now you recite Surah Fatiha; we don't even know who that person is, what kind of person he was. Anyway, this is death. This is what is called death. Now, there is a reference through his name that 'this is him', but when annihilation happens, there will be nothing, and only Ale Muhammad (a.s.) will remain. 'Wa yabqa wajhu rabbika dhul jalali wal ikram'. Because from their light, from their light, every existence received existence, every existent received existence. Therefore, every thing that has come into existence is because of them. That is why it is found in the traditions: 'Khalaqallahu al-mashiyyata binafsiha, thumma khalaqal ashya'a bil-mashiyya'. Allah created the 'Mashiyya' (Will)—the existence of the Prophet, the existence of Ale Muhammad—by Himself, directly, and then all the remaining things received existence because of Ale Muhammad. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! They are in existence because of them; they came into existence because of them. If they were not there, nothing would be there. If their existence was not there, nothing would be there. What is there to be surprised about in this? Everything, everything... look, this introductory discussion is because the two or three sentences we are about to read might be a bit tough, so I am telling you this as a preface. Look, when you understand that everyone received existence, everyone came into existence from their light—everyone, there is no exception in this—whether it is a Prophet, a Messenger, an angel, a Jinn, the Arsh (Throne), the Kursi (Chair), the earth, or the sky. And small creatures are not even worth mentioning; they came into existence after who knows how many mediums. They are not even worth mentioning. We are talking about the great things. Is it clear to you? Now, when Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says in Nahjul Balagha, 'Nahnu sana'u Rabbuna' (We are the creation of our Lord), meaning Allah created us, 'wal khalqu ba'du sana'u lana' (and the creation after us is our creation). This is a Hadith from Nahjul Balagha, check it in the Hikam (sayings). And all the creatures after us, all the existing things, we created them all. Allah created us directly, and we created the remaining creatures. When this Hadith is stated, then this is 'Hulu' (a belief in incarnation). Well, these people, those who are completely unaware of the Hadiths, they do all this. And there are many such individuals among them whose clips people sometimes send us, saying, 'Look, he said this.' So, there are some such individuals—I won't take anyone's name. They are just 'Kasrat-e-Talawwun' (chameleonic) people. 'Kasrat-e-Talawwun' is a word in Arabic; do you know what it means? One who keeps changing sides. Sometimes he jumps here, sometimes he jumps there. There is no trust in his faith, what he is. There is no trust in his faith at all. Sometimes he says, 'No, we should say Ya Ali Madad,' sometimes he says, 'No, don't say Ya Ali Madad.' Say 'Ya Ali Madad', you ask Allah to help me. He has so much time. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and Ale Muhammad. Ya Ali. Yes, they talk like this. 'Oh Ali'—those who speak English, I am even more afraid of them. You know, I am very afraid of those who speak English. Those who start speaking in English are very dangerous. So what do they do? They say, 'We say, Oh Ali, you ask Allah that He should help me.' Brother, read a little, read books, read Hadiths, read traditions. When you read, you will understand things. Listening to hearsay here and there, getting impressed by someone's talk, getting influenced by it, and sitting and talking nonsense, and they have many different influences on them. Anyway, we are not influenced. Look, one should not be influenced by anyone. We should only be influenced by one thing, and what is that influence? Traditions, Quran, and Hadith. Nothing else. People say, 'You cannot ask them directly.' Oh brother, go and read, read books. What did Allah say to Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.)? A fierce, terrible battle is going on. Rasulullah is looking up, seeking help. 'Parwardigara!' A voice comes: 'Nadi 'Aliyan madhharal 'aja'ib'. Allah says, 'Call Ali.' He is saying it to Rasulullah. Actually, this was a lesson for us. Not for Rasulullah; Rasulullah already knew. But sometimes one has to do all this to teach others. So, 'Nadi 'Aliyan madhharal 'aja'ib'. Call Ali, who is the manifestation of wonders. Ali will come and manifest the wonders, and your difficulties will be removed automatically. 'Nadi 'Aliyan madhharal 'aja'ib, tajidhu 'awnan laka fin-nawa'ib'. O Prophet! If you... look, if those who understand Arabic, if I tell them, then tell them, it's fine. 'Tajid' is what is called 'Jaza-e-Shart' or 'Jawab-e-Shart'. 'Nadi' is 'Fi'l-e-Shart' (the verb of the condition), meaning it is an order, and 'Tajid' is the result of the order. The result of the order. If you call, the result will be 'Tajidhu', you will find Ali. Ali will be present there. 'Tajidhu', you will find him there. Ali will be present there. So just call Ali, wherever you are. I quoted a Hadith in the service of the speech. Mawla (a.s.) is saying, 'Mashariqal ardi wa magharibiha'. East, West, West, and Mawla is saying there is no difference. Wherever you are, call Ali, Ali will come. Allah is saying here 'Tajid', this is a Hadith-e-Qudsi. This is a Hadith-e-Qudsi. That is why many people tried to label it as 'da'if' (weak). 'It is da'if, it is da'if.' No, you are da'if, brother. Go and take some good medicine. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and Ale Muhammad. Ya Ali. Then Mawla (a.s.) said, 'Ya Salman, Ya Jundab.' O Salman, O Abu Dharr. He said, 'Labbayk Ya Amirul Momineen.' 'Qala ana alladhi hamaltu Nuhan fis-safinati bi-amri Rabbi.' I was the one who carried Nuh (Noah) in the ark by the command of my Lord. So, every time the lots were drawn, every time they voted, the same name would come up in the vote. What do they call it? What do they call it? Voting? A slip? What do they call it? What is 'Qur'an-dazi' (drawing lots) called? A lottery. Well, it's not exactly a lottery, because a lottery is positive; you win something in it. Here, one had to jump into the sea. A man had to jump into the sea. So, every time the slip was drawn, Hazrat Yunus's (a.s.) name came up. So, brother, go. As soon as he jumped into the sea, a large fish—a whale, as they call it—came and swallowed Hazrat Yunus (a.s.), and he went straight into its belly. Regardless, he was a Prophet, and Allah had destined everything for him. This entire story is present in the Quran. There is a whole Surah named after him. The entire Surah, Surah Yunus. It is Surah number 10 of the Quran, chapter number 10. So, you should read it very calmly. It is very good; if children read it, if the youth read it, they will understand many things. So, he said that when he went inside, when the fish swallowed him, he understood that there wasn't much time left to live. Now, this is the situation. So the Quran says: ﴿فَنَادَى فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ (Then he called out in the darkness). He called out in the darkness of the fish's belly: ﴿لَّا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ (There is no god but You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers). O Lord! There is no god except You. Your essence is pure. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers. By 'wrongdoer' here, it does not mean a sinner. Here, it refers to the one who, out of anger, moved away from his people. Right? This is it. So the Quran says, "فَنَادَىٰ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَن لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ" (Then he called out in the darkness, 'There is no god but You'). Then Allah says, "فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ" (So We saved him). "فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ" (So We saved him). So, the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) says that the one who took Yunus out of the fish's belly was me, by Allah's permission. Allah gave me the command, 'O Ali! Take Yunus out of the fish's belly.' Wow! Wow! Wow! There is no surprise in this. "وَأَنَا الَّذِي" (And I am the one who) "أَخْرَجْتُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مِنَ النَّارِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّي" (brought Ibrahim out of the fire by the permission of my Lord). When Ibrahim (a.s.) was thrown into the fire and Allah commanded, "يَا نَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَىٰ إِبْرَাহِيمَ" (O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim), then I brought Ibrahim out of the fire. The Master says. Regardless, and after that, he says, "The punishment that descended upon the people of Shu'ayb, Hazrat Shu'ayb 'ala nabiyyina wa alihi as-salam." So, a punishment descended upon his people. What do they call that punishment? "يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ" (The Day of the Shadow/Cloud). This is also present in the Quran. If you study the Holy Quran, it is verse number 189 of Surah Ash-Shu'ara. What did the people of Shu'ayb do? "فَكَذَّبُوهُ" (They denied him). They denied Shu'ayb, they denied Hazrat Shu'ayb (a.s.). "فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ" (So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Shadow seized them). So this "يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ"—'Zulla' means, for instance, actually, it has two meanings. One is 'Zill', which means shadow, and when they say 'Zulla', it means intense heat. Intense heat, extremely fierce heat. So the Quran says that "عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ" (the punishment of the Day of the Shadow), meaning a day of intense heat, descended upon them in the form of punishment. That is, Allah destroyed the people of Shu'ayb, the people of Madyan, and sent such a punishment upon them that intense heat descended, intense. Meaning, today, as you see, if it reaches 50-55 degrees, a person cannot bear it. What happens? Fires break out in the forests everywhere, you know that. And if this temperature were to become 100-150 degrees, what would happen? Yes? So you can understand what would happen. And if it were a blacksmith's furnace—do you know what a blacksmith's furnace is? The furnace, which the Master of the Universe (a.s.) mentioned, 'The one who came to fight in the Battle of the Camel, she has as much hatred for me in her heart as a blacksmith's furnace.' Is it clear to you? Now you understand the point, don't you? The Master says, meaning this is what the Quran says, "فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ" (So the punishment of the Day of the Shadow seized them). "يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ" means the punishment of intense heat descended upon them. He says, "أَنَا عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ" (I am the punishment of the Day of the Shadow). That "يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ", that punishment, was me, and it is written in the Hadith that it was not just "يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ", there was also "سَمَائِمُ". Meaning, along with the heat, there were also hot winds blowing. That is, when the Master of the Universe (a.s.) was attacking the people of Shu'ayb, it wasn't just heat, it wasn't just heat, but there were also hot winds. So you understand that the people of Shu'ayb were destroyed and perished because of that. Now, when this same Ali (a.s.) attacks in battle here, the same thing must be happening. Punishment must be descending upon them, there must be heat, and hot winds must be blowing. Meaning, hot winds also slap you; you know that hot winds slap. It's not just heat; just heat is like the heat of Bombay. It only has humidity; there are no hot winds blowing there. But if you go to a place where hot winds blow, like in UP, etc., then the hot wind slaps you completely. That's why people tie things around their faces, so that the hot wind doesn't hit them, so they don't get affected by the hot wind. It hits very badly. But regardless, here the Master of the Universe (a.s.) was the punishment, and then the Master cites another verse of the Quran, "وَأَنَا الْمُنَادِي مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ" (And I am the caller from a near place). And the other type of punishment mentioned in the Quran, this is a verse from Surah Fussilat, verse number 44. Meaning, this is for those people who did not believe. The Quran says, "وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ" (And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness). They have become deaf, they have become deaf. "وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى" (And it is blindness upon them). And they have also become blind. They are deaf, and they are blind. "فَيُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ" (They are being called from a distant place). Meaning, one way of punishment for them will be this. The Master says, "أَنَا الْمُنَادِي" (I am the caller), "أَنَا الْمُنَادِي مِن مَّكَانٍ" (I am the caller from a place), meaning for them, this is "مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ" (from a near place). For the good people, the Master is near, and for those who are far, they are from a near place. Regardless, this call that I will give, the Master says, "قَدْ سَمِعَهُ الثَّقَلَانِ الْجِنُّ وَالْإِنسُ" (Both the Jinn and Mankind have heard it). When I give the call, listen very carefully to this sentence, when I give the call, all the Jinn and Mankind will hear it. Both the Jinn and the humans. Look, among the Jinn, there are both believers and non-believers. Just as among humans there are believers and non-believers, there are also among the Jinn. Both exist in both. So the Jinn—the Master of the Universe (a.s.) also fought with the Jinn. The Master of the Universe (a.s.) actually fought with the Jinn. So the Jinn, both believers and non-believers. Humans, both non-believers and believers. The Master says, both Jinn and humans will hear. And those in this world who were not used to listening, who was not used to listening? Those who were oppressors, tyrants, and hypocrites; these two were generally not used to listening to the Master's voice. Meaning, they were not used to listening to the truth. So the Master says, I will explain to them in their own language as well. Right? "لَأُسْمِعَنَّ كُلَّ قَوْمٍ الْجَبَّارِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقِينَ بِلُغَاتِهِمْ" (I will certainly make all the tyrannical and hypocritical people hear in their own languages). I will make them hear, I will explain to them in their language. Meaning, they are not going to understand the straightforward language, the language of the world. Because when he explained in the world, they did not understand. What did they think? That 'brother, we have taken control, we have gained power, now what can Ali do? Now what can Ali do?' Look, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) could have done a lot, but there was a command from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), as I just presented in your service, that there was a command from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that 'Ali, exercise patience.' That is why the Master of the Universe (a.s.) exercised patience. Otherwise, it is not that the Master could not do anything. And the Master did. When these people came to set fire to the house, the one who was their leader, who gave the order to everyone to go and set fire, he entered the house and he even used a whip on Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). And he also did other things that are disrespectful and not worth mentioning; at least our tongues cannot bring themselves to say it. He was disrespectful, he was very vulgar, he was vulgar anyway. You know him, don't you? Right? So when he thought that 'now I have become a great lion,' by entering their house and doing this. He did not understand that the Master was exercising patience. It was a stage of patience. But when the Master saw that he had entered the house and had been so insolent, had dared so much, then the Master of the Universe (a.s.) gave him one blow, a tremendous one, and he fell straight to the ground. With just one hand. He probably didn't even hit him with full force. Otherwise, he would have died. So he fell to the ground. Then the Master climbed onto his head, onto his chest. And the Master says it himself, it is in the Master's own words, that 'it was near that I would have crushed his throat. But I remembered the saying of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), 'Ali, be patient.' That is why I got off his chest.' And another incident also, before this, in your service, not in these gatherings, but before this. When the Master of the Universe (a.s.) refused to give allegiance, that 'I will not give allegiance.' So he used to go and sit in the mosque, he used to pray in the mosque. But he had not given allegiance. So, regardless, it was bothering those people that 'brother, he has not given allegiance, now what should we do?' So the person who had become the 'Sahib-e-Mimbar' (the one on the pulpit), he called Khalid ibn Walid. He said to Khalid ibn Walid, 'Khalid, when I am leading the prayer and if Ali comes to pray, then you do this: as soon as I say 'Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah', you get up and strike Ali on the head with your sword, finish him off. The matter of allegiance will be finished.' Khalid said, 'Okay, I will do it, no problem.' He had been incited, even though he had already been beaten a lot by the Master before. But people get incited, right? So he was incited, 'Brother, do it.' Okay. He said, 'Okay, I will do it, no problem.' So now this brother who was the 'Sahib-e-Mimbar', he was leading the prayer, right? Now he had become the Imam, he was everything. Until yesterday, he was nothing. Is it clear to you? Khalid ibn Walid, yes, okay. As soon as he, 'Assalamu Alaikum', lift the sword and strike straight on Ali's head and finish Ali's matter. He said, 'Okay.' But now, brother, as soon as he went into the prayer, he was thinking throughout the prayer, 'If Khalid tries and Ali survives, and he asks Khalid who told you to do this? Then I am finished.' He was thinking this throughout the prayer. Is it clear how much focus was on the worship of Allah? Now he is thinking throughout the prayer. 'If this happens, what will happen? If that happens, what will happen? This will happen, that will happen.' Regardless, he was very brave. So, in the end, his condition became so bad that by the time he reached the 'Salam', after reaching the 'Salam', 'Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah, O Khalid ibn Walid, la taf'al ma amartuka bihi.' He said, 'Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah, O Khalid ibn Walid, do not do the thing I told you to do.' 'La taf'al', do not do it. So he did not do it. Regardless, the Master asked him, 'What did he say to you?' He asked him, 'What did he say to you?' This is the entire Hadith; we are narrating this to you from Bihar al-Anwar, the entire Hadith. In Bihar al-Anwar, Allama Majlisi has narrated the whole event. He said that he [Khalid] said, 'I will kill you.' He had said it; he was, after all, a mercenary. Brother, he said, 'I will kill you.' So Maula [Ali (a.s.)] said, 'You will kill me? Yes. You will kill me? Do you know your worth? Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes.' So he said, 'Yes, I will kill you, I can kill you.' He said, 'Is that so?' The phrase in the Hadith is that Maula grabbed his hand just once. His right hand. And when he squeezed his hand, all his fingers broke. All his fingers broke. After that, he could never lift a sword again. Khalid ibn Walid could never lift a sword in his life. This is the state he was reduced to after that incident. I mean, he was a fierce enemy. A fierce enemy. But later, when he embraced Islam, they gave him the title 'Saifullah' (Sword of Allah). They gave him that title. Regardless, he had a very strong grudge and enmity towards Maula's declaration. But look, if Allah wants to guide someone, if Allah wants to guide someone, look at how He guides them. Guidance is in the hands of Allah. Khalid ibn Walid had two sons. He had two sons. He had named both of them Abdurrahman. But to differentiate between the two, he named one Abdurrahman ibn Khalid ibn Walid, and the other he named Abdurrahman al-Muhajir ibn Khalid al-Walid. Both had the same name, but the only difference was 'al-Muhajir'. Now, this first Abdurrahman, the one who was just Abdurrahman, was like his father. But this al-Muhajir became such a devotee of the Master of the Universe (Maula-e-Kainat) that he always remained by the side of the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin). So much so that when the Battle of Siffin took place, one brother was on that side, and one brother was on this side. Now, this one who was with the Master of the Universe was repeatedly saying, 'Ya Ali, Ya Amir al-Mu'minin, give me a chance for martyrdom.' Look at the passion, whose son he was, look at how he was. 'Ya Ali, give me a chance, I want to be martyred, give me a chance.' And then when Maula gave him the chance, he went and was martyred. Abdurrahman al-Muhajir ibn Khalid ibn Walid. He was blessed with martyrdom. Fighting alongside the Master of the Universe, who gets such an opportunity? Very few individuals. He got that opportunity. And look, his brother, who was on the other side, did not die [a martyr's death]. He did not die. His end was very bad. Very bad. I mean, Muawiya killed him through deception. He killed him through a terrible deception. There is a long history to that which is for another time, Insha'Allah. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Then Maula says, 'Ana al-Khidr 'alim Musa' (I am the Khidr who taught Musa). I narrated the whole story to you. 'Ana al-Khidr 'alim Musa.' When Khidr went to teach Musa, I was the one teaching Musa. Meaning, I was teaching Khidr, and he was teaching Musa. Is it clear to you or not? At that time, whatever Khidr was receiving, he was speaking that. That is why I narrated the whole story to you that day, so that your minds would be prepared for it. How could Khidr, who was an ordinary prophet, teach that Prophet [Musa]? So he was teaching because the 'Gate to the City of Knowledge' (Bab-e-Madinat al-Ilm) was teaching him. Haidari Ya Ali. Ya Ali. Haidari Ya Ali. Nara-e-Haidari Ya Ali. 'Wa ana mu'allim Sulaiman ibn Dawud' (And I was the teacher of Sulaiman ibn Dawud). I was the teacher of Sulaiman. 'Wa ana Dhu al-Qarnayn' (And I was Dhu al-Qarnayn). I was Dhu al-Qarnayn too. 'Wa ana qudrat Allah' (And I was the power of Allah). I was the power of Allah. The power through which these people were performing all these tasks, that 'Noor-e-Qudrat' (Light of Power) was me, Ali ibn Abi Talib. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib. This is the family of Muhammad (Aali Muhammad) (a.s.). You recognize them. This is called 'Marifat' (Gnosis). After that, he says, 'Ya Salman, Ya Jundab.' Now this is very powerful. Listen. These are just the final sentences. 'Ya Salman, Ya Jundab.' O Salman, O Jundab. Jundab was the name of Janab-e-Abu Dharr. Jundab, Jundab ibn Junada. 'Ana Muhammad wa Muhammad ana' (I am Muhammad and Muhammad is I). Both are from the same light, right? Allah created one light, He created one light. And then He divided them into two parts. One became Muhammad, one became Ali. Is there anything surprising in this? No. When we read this Hadith, many people say this is all 'Ghulu' (exaggeration), why do you read all this? Okay, fine, we won't read it. Next time, don't read from the pulpit either: 'Husayn minni wa ana min al-Husayn' (Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn). This is exactly what it means, nothing else. Husayn is from me, I am from Husayn, it is the same thing. No difference. 'Muhammad ana, ana Muhammad.' 'Ana min Muhammad wa Muhammad minni.' I am from Muhammad and Muhammad is from me. Sallallahu alayhi wa aalihi, recite a Salawat. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. We are the same ocean. We are the same ocean. 'Maraj al-bahrayni yaltaqiyan, baynahuma barzakhun la yabghiyan.' We are the same ocean. We are not separate. 'Ya Salman, Ya Jundab,' he said, 'Labbayk ya Amir al-Mu'minin.' Then he addressed them, 'O Salman, O Jundab.' They said, 'Labbayk ya Amir al-Mu'minin.' He said, 'Inna mayyitana lam yamut' (When one of us dies, he does not die). When one of us dies, he does not die. 'Inna mayyitana lam yamut.' Now, people object to this too. What does this mean? How can this be? Oh brother, read the Quran. What is the problem, you don't read. And you hear things from here and there and come and object. Heard from here, heard from there, heard from there, heard this one, heard that one. Oh brother, study, do research. Don't just talk about hearsay. The Imam says, 'Inna mayyitana lam yamut.' What does the Quran say? The Quran says, 'Wala tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabilillahi amwatan' (And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead). Those who have been killed in the way of Allah, do not call them dead. They are not dead. The Quran is even forbidding calling them dead. Rather, what is the custom among us? That those who are dead, we put 'Shaheed' (martyr) before their names. Call them Shaheed. Shaheed means, he is still a witness. He is alive and is testifying. He is alive, that is why we call him Shaheed. What does Shaheed mean? The one who is a 'Shahid' (witness). Shaheed is its intensive form. The one who testifies a lot. Meaning, when he was alive, he could not testify as much as he is testifying now after dying. Because he hasn't died, he is actually... now he is just in the Barzakh. So, Allah is saying, 'Wala tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabilillahi amwatan, bal ahya'un' (And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive), 'inda rabbihim yurzaqun' (with their Lord, they are being provided for). They are receiving sustenance from their Lord, they are getting sustenance. They are alive. And in another verse, it is said that you do not understand how they are alive. The Quran says, you will not understand how they are alive. Allah has forbidden calling them dead in two verses, not just one, in two Quranic verses. Now, if Allah has forbidden it for a common martyr, then is it any surprise for the Ahl al-Bayt who are the most superior? And they are also martyrs. The Ahl al-Bayt, Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, all are martyrs. Even the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is a martyr. Someone was poisoned, someone was martyred with a sword, this is also a narration. What is the Hadith? 'Ma minna illa maqtulun aw masmum' (There is none among us except that he is either killed or poisoned). So all the Masumin (a.s.), all of them from the Messenger of Allah down to the rest of the Imams, were either killed by the sword or poisoned. Meaning, all of them up to the 11th Imam. And then, Insha'Allah, when Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Ya Ali! And the family of Muhammad, the family of Muhammad, voices raised, Haidari! Ya Ali! Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Then there will be 'Raj'at' (the return), Insha'Allah. And in Raj'at, the Imam will take revenge even after the reappearance, and after Raj'at, there will be revenge again. Insha'Allah, then people will see what the glory of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) is. At that time, they will see their glory. They will see the glory of each Imam. Then they will understand what the reality is. So the Imam says, the one who dies among us, he is not dead. The one who is hidden among us, he is not hidden. Now let's stop here, because this needs a little explanation. So Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the opportunity, then in tomorrow's Majlis, if Allah gives life and opportunity—both things are necessary, life and opportunity—then I will explain it to you, Insha'Allah, and 'bi-awnillahi wa bi-tawfiqihi' (with the help and guidance of Allah), the family of Muhammad (a.s.) all gave sacrifices. Without exception, every single one. And not just them, but their youths, their children, everyone. In the way of Allah, they kept getting martyred with Imam Husayn (a.s.), they kept getting martyred. Until that moment came in Karbala, when Husayn said to the likeness of the Prophet, Hazrat Ali Akbar, 'Taqaddam ya bunayya' (Go forward, O my son). O son, now you go to fight, now you go to perform Jihad. Ali Akbar was already prepared, he had been waiting for a long time for his father to give permission so he could go and sacrifice himself. As soon as the Imam said it, Janab-e-Ali Akbar was immediately ready. As soon as he was ready, the Imam said, 'First go to the tent and take permission.' Now when Ali Akbar came to the tent, he first took permission from his mother, Janab-e-Umm-e-Laila. So Umm-e-Laila said, 'Go and take permission from your aunt, who raised you for 18 years with such love and care.' When Ali Akbar came before Janab-e-Zainab to take permission, Janab-e-Zainab said, 'Son, is this why I raised you? Are you taking permission from your mother?' Ali Akbar said, 'Aunt, if you give permission, then... if you don't give permission, then don't, but tomorrow on the Day of Judgment, if Grandmother asks whether Ali Akbar was dearer or Husayn?' Zainab gave permission. Now here, Hamid ibn Muslim, who is the historian of Karbala, I present his words to you. Hamid ibn Muslim says that when Ali Akbar wanted to leave the tent, the ladies had surrounded Ali Akbar, and it looked as if a funeral was leaving a house full of people. Such women were standing at the door of the tent, as if a funeral was leaving a house full of people. But every time Ali Akbar came out, it felt like someone was holding his garment and pulling him back inside. It is not written in any Hadith who was holding Ali Akbar's garment and pulling, but if it were an elder, they would have held Ali Akbar's arm. But this holding of the garment shows that there was a 6-year-old girl who was repeatedly stopping him, 'Brother, don't leave us alone.' Ali Akbar said, 'My father is alone, my father has no friend or helper.' Ali Akbar left, he came out. Now when Ali Akbar mounted the horse, Imam Husayn (a.s.) looked towards the sky and said, 'Allahumma ishhad ala haula-il-qawm' (O Allah, be a witness against this nation). O Lord, be a witness against this nation. 'Qad baraza alayhim ghulamun' (A youth has gone out against them), 'ashbahu al-nasi khalqan wa khuluqan wa mantiqan bi-nabiyyika' (who in appearance, character, and speech, resembled Your Prophet more than anyone else). Whenever we longed to see the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), we would look at Ali Akbar. Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Go, my son Ali Akbar.' Now Ali Akbar left, and the Imam said goodbye. He had not gone far when a sound was heard. When he heard the sound, he looked back and saw his elderly father with his hands on his waist, calling out, 'Ya Ali! Ya Ali! Ya Ali!' Now, it is unknown whether he was remembering this Ali Akbar or calling out to Ali (a.s.) in Najaf. But Ali Akbar said, 'Father, you have already bid me farewell, why are you coming now?' He replied, 'My son, if you had children, you would know what the grief of a young son is.' The Imam bid him farewell, Ali Akbar went, fought in Jihad, and sent many enemies to hell. Now, when he returned, he returned, but why did he return? What was the reason? It was a mother's heart, a young son. He said, 'Fizza, Fizza, it is a young son, go and stand at the door of the tent and see if my son is in any trouble. Look at the color of his father's face. If my son is in trouble, it is a matter of a young son, the father's complexion will change, the color of his face will alter.' So, as soon as Fizza saw that the color of Hussain's face had changed, she came and said, 'Bibi, the master's face has changed color.' She said, 'Please trouble the master a little.' Hussain came to the door of the tent and asked, 'Why has your face changed color?' He replied, 'A great, famous warrior has come to fight my son.' He is a lion, and my son is hungry and thirsty for three days. So, it was a mother's heart, she began to say, 'What should I do?' He said, 'Hussain said, pray. A mother's prayer is accepted for her son.' But Umm Layla said, 'Ladies, form a circle.' A circle was formed, Umm Layla stood in the middle and called out, 'O Allah! By the loneliness of Hussain, O Sustainer, by the intercession of Hussain's helplessness, O You who reunited Yusuf with Yaqub, my Ali Akbar.' Just as the mother's prayer was not even finished, Ali Akbar came from the battlefield, but in what state did he come? He came in a state where he was covered in wounds, blood was flowing, and he came before Hussain and said, 'Ya Abata! Father, is there any way to get some water?' Hussain said, 'My son, you know there is no water, there is no water to be killed for.' But come, put your tongue in my mouth. As soon as Ali Akbar put his tongue in the blessed mouth, he immediately pulled it back. He said, 'Father, oh, in your mouth, on your tongue, there are thorns. Your tongue is drier than mine.' Hussain gave him his ring, he gave his ring, 'My son, keep this now, InshaAllah your grandfather will quench your thirst.' Ali Akbar went, fighting, and now as he was fighting, someone said, 'Attack him from behind, then this will happen.' Someone attacked from behind, and just as Ali Akbar was looking towards the back, a cursed one struck him with a spear from the front. As the spear pierced Ali Akbar's chest, Ali Akbar fell from the back of his horse onto the earth of Karbala, calling out, 'Ya Abata, Alaykum as-salam, Father, my final farewell.' Now when Hussain reached him, he saw Ali Akbar writhing, the spear stuck in his chest. Hussain pulled out the spear, Ya Ali, and as the spear came out, a fountain of blood erupted. Ali Akbar passed away. Hussain recited a dirge, 'Ya bunayya, ala ad-dunya ba'daka al-afa' (O my son, may the world be ruined after you). O my son, you have departed from this world. It was like this, 'Man hum ad-dunya, wa ghammuha, wa baka abuka, wahidan faridan bayn al-a'da' (From the grief of the world and its sorrow, your father wept, alone and solitary among the enemies). Wa Aliya, Wa Husayna. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of Hussain's blood. O Lord, remove the troubles of those who are distressed. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant those who are childless, righteous and virtuous children. Grant those who are ill, a complete and swift recovery. Some people have asked for prayers, especially for them, grant them a complete and swift recovery. O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the eminent Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: Lamentation for Ali Akbar
chapters.summary: The speaker recites a heart-wrenching lamentation (latmiya) regarding the departure of Ali Akbar to the battlefield and the grief of Imam Husayn.

chapters.title: The Significance of Mourning for Husayn
chapters.summary: The speaker references a Hadith from Imam Rida regarding the depth of grief for Imam Husayn and introduces the concept of Ma'rifat al-Nuraniyya.

chapters.title: Understanding the Luminous Reality of Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that discussing the luminous creation of the Ahlulbayt is supported by authentic traditions and is not an act of exaggeration (Ghuluw).

chapters.title: The Unique Status of the Commander of the Faithful
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the unique gifts granted by Allah to Imam Ali and touches upon the nature of the close angels, specifically the Angel of Death.

title: Maah-e-Ramazan Ke Aakhri Jume Ko Ye Dua Mat Bhooliyega [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses a specific supplication recommended by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) to be recited on the final Friday of Ramadan. It highlights the spiritual significance of this day, emphasizing the hope for forgiveness and the opportunity to witness future Ramadans. The speaker also connects the sanctity of Friday to the Imam of the Time (a.s.), encouraging believers to pray for his reappearance and for the acceptance of their worship.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Waliy al-Asr (Guardian of the Era), assist us and do not let us perish. It is narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari that I was in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) on the last Friday of the holy month of Ramadan. When his (s.a.w.a.) gaze fell upon me, he said: 'O Jabir, this is the last Friday of the month of Ramadan. So bid it farewell and recite: O Allah, do not make it the last of our fasts in this month; but if You have made it so, then make me among those who are shown mercy and do not make me among those who are deprived.' For whoever recites this prayer on this day will succeed in attaining one of two virtues: either they will live to see the next month of Ramadan, or they will receive Allah's forgiveness and infinite mercy. Therefore, on the last Friday of the holy month of Ramadan, we should recite this prayer, but before reciting it, one should keep in mind that the day of Friday is dedicated to the Imam of the Time (a.s.). On the day of Friday, which is the Ziyarat (visitation) of the Imam of the Time (a.s.), we say to our Imam of the Time: 'This is the day of Friday, and it is your day, in which your reappearance is expected, and the relief for the believers is expected at your hands.' We pray in the court of Allah (t.w.t.), through the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), that O Allah, hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the Time (a.s.) and count us among his helpers and supporters. And whatever good deeds we have performed in this holy month of Ramadan, grant them the honor of acceptance. Grant us the ability to perform more good deeds and to keep away from sins after this month and in other months as well. Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Qayaamat Mein Har Shakhs Ki Teen Kitaabein (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the process of reckoning on the Day of Judgment based on a narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). It explains that a believer's deeds are weighed against their blessings, and the Holy Quran acts as an intercessor for those who recited it with devotion. The talk highlights that the number of Quranic verses memorized or recited in this life directly determines one's elevated status and ranks in Paradise.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. It is narrated from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that on the Day of Judgment, there will be three books: a book of blessings, a book of good deeds, and a book of sins. Then the book of blessings and the book of good deeds will be placed in front of each other. The book of blessings will dominate the book of good deeds, and then only the book of sins will remain. Then the believer will be called for reckoning. Then the Quran will appear in front of that believer in a beautiful form and will say: 'O Lord, I am the Quran, and this is your believing servant. He took pains to recite me and spent long hours reciting me, and his eyes would fill with tears at the time of recitation. So, be pleased with him just as... So, be pleased with him just as he kept me happy.' Imam (a.s.) says that then the Almighty God will say, 'My servant, open your right hand.' Then Allah will fill his right hand with His pleasure and his left hand with His mercy. And then it will be announced: 'This is Paradise, which has been made permissible for you.' So recite the Quran and rise in ranks. Then that servant will keep rising in the ranks of Paradise as much as he recites the verses of the Holy Quran. That is, from this, one thing is certain, and that is that there will be as many ranks in Paradise as there are verses in the Holy Quran. Therefore, whoever has recited as many verses in the world, his ranks will be elevated in Paradise to that extent. May the Almighty grant us the ability to memorize as many verses of the Holy Quran as possible, and may the Holy Quran and Imam (a.s.) come to our aid in the grave and place their hands on our heads. Come there and keep our group united so that we may not become scattered again; we have called these friends.

title: Ghaibat Ke Fitnon Se Bachne Ka Waahid Raasta
excerpt: This lecture discusses the importance of maintaining belief in the Imamate of the twelve Imams during the period of occultation. Drawing from a narration involving Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Rahma and Imam Hasan al-Askari, the speaker highlights the spiritual parallels between the Imam of the Time and figures like Khidr and Dhul-Qarnayn. The central message is that salvation from the tribulations of the occultation is found through firm belief and the consistent act of praying for the hastening of the Imam's reappearance.
content:
Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Rahma is among those companions who had the honor of visiting Imam Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.). In the era of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), in this hadith, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'O Ahmad ibn Ishaq, the likeness of this Ummah is like the likeness of Khidr (a.s.) and the likeness of Dhul-Qarnayn.' The Imam (a.s.) is swearing by Allah that the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.) has a likeness to Khidr (a.s.) or Dhul-Qarnayn in this Ummah, and he will have an occultation (ghaybah). And in this occultation, no one will be saved from destruction except the one who holds the belief in his Imamate and whom Allah grants the ability to pray for the hastening of his reappearance. That is, the person who prays for the hastening of the reappearance of Imam Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.) and believes in his Imamate—meaning he believes in the Imamate of all twelve Imams—such a person will remain safe from the tribulations of the occultation. The Imam (a.s.) telling this to Ahmad ibn Ishaq points to the fact that there is room for hastening the reappearance, and it is possible that Allah may cause the reappearance of Imam Zaman (a.s.) to occur without manifesting any signs. title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 1 | Necessity of Divine Proof / Hujjat e Khuda ki Zaroorat
excerpt: This webinar session explores the theological necessity of a Divine Proof (Hujjah) in every era, arguing that the existence of the universe is contingent upon the presence of an Imam. Drawing from Quranic verses and Prophetic traditions, the lecture establishes that the Ahlulbayt serve as the essential guides for humanity and the conduits of divine mercy. The session emphasizes that true faith and valid worship are only possible through adherence to the guidance of the infallible Imams, whose authority remains continuous from the time of Adam until the Day of Judgment.
content:
O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjah (Proof), son of al-Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him dwell on Your earth in obedience and cause him to enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, hasten the relief of Your representative, and make us among his helpers, supporters, followers, and servants. Grant us success in what You love and are pleased with, and do not leave us to ourselves even for the blinking of an eye, ever, and do not replace us with others, by the right of Muhammad and his pure progeny. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Congratulations to you all on these joyous dates of the month of Shaban. Another world, another world came to the fore. Wa idha afala najmun tala najmun. And when one star disappears, another star rises. Falamma qabazahu Allahu Azzawajall alayhi zanantum annallaha qad hasama baynahu wa bayna khalqih. Meaning, when Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) passed away, you thought that Allah had ended the chain of Imamate. This thought entered your minds. Kalla ma kana dhalik. No, no, it is not so. Wa la yakunu hatta taqumus sa'ah. And this is not possible until the Day of Judgment arrives. There will be a Hujjat (Proof) of Allah, and there will always be one. Wa yazharu amrullahi wa hum karihun. And the command of Allah will manifest, even if people dislike it. And then the final sentence of the Imam in this regard was: 'Ya Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, la yadkhulukash shakku fi ma qad imtu lahu.' O Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, look, never let doubt enter your heart regarding this matter. See how much the Imam cares for his Shias. How much he cares. Meaning, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim was not denying it. There was just a doubt, a slight doubt. But the Imam wants that no, his Shias should have complete certainty in Imamate, certainty. Not even a doubt. Fa innallaha la yukhalli al-arda min hujjah. Because Allah has never left the earth without a Hujjat of Allah. There has always been a Hujjat of Allah. And then after that, the Imam mentioned the details that were in the previous hadith, regarding the money your father entrusted to you; the Imam mentioned all those details, and then at the end, there were some pieces of advice from the Imam. And these pieces of advice are for all of us. The Imam said: 'Fattaqillaha fi nafsika awwalan thumma fi fiyya fakhallisni.' Is it clear? Meaning, fear Allah, fear Allah. And then, in any case, this is our responsibility. We will cover the chapter of responsibilities, InshaAllah. But there is an important thing here. And that is that surely, in every era, the presence of the Hujjat of Allah is necessary and mandatory. There is no doubt; so many verses and traditions exist regarding this. Allah has kept this chain from Prophet Adam until the Day of Judgment. But especially in today's era, meaning from after Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) until now, and from now until the Day of Judgment. Belief in the Hujjat of Allah is very mandatory and very necessary. Because our Imam, who is the twelfth Imam, is Imam Mahdi (ajtf). And this is the Imam upon whom not only the hopes of the Shias but of the Muslims, and not only the Muslims but of all religions, all religious individuals, are pinned. That there is definitely such a person in the world, and he will come to fill the world with justice and fairness, just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. So, let us begin this webinar, this was the first speech in this series, and there will be more speeches, InshaAllah. Together, let us all pray: 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyika al-hujjati bnil-hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihi al-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila.' Rabb salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Bi-jahi Muhammad wa alihi al-tahirin. Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. We are very grateful to the honorable Dr. Shabih Rizvi Sahab that through his statement, he clarified the topic of the need for the Hujjat of Allah in the light of the verses of the Holy Quran and the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). May Allah grant us all the ability to remain attached to the Hujjat of Allah, the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (ajtf), and to hold onto his hem until the last moment. Sir, we have received some questions. We do not have much room in the span of time. Therefore, we can take two questions, sir. The first question is from Mr. Jafar Hussain Sahab. He has asked this question through both WhatsApp and Zoom, Alhamdulillah. He wants to know more traditions on this topic; he wants to know more about what will be the fate of the person who performs worship without recognizing the Hujjat of Allah or without attaining their Ma'rifat (recognition)? As was submitted during the speech, 'Bina ubidallahu wa bina urifallahu, lawlana ma ubidallahu ma urifallahu.' Meaning, if there is worship, it will be in the way that the Hujjat of Allah has taught. The same way, because that is the way Allah has taught. Allah has taught only one way of worship. Look, Iblis also gave a suggestion. So, the first thing is, if we take this historically from the beginning, meaning if we understand the chronology, take it in chronological order, that first Iblis said, 'Command me to do anything else, I am ready to do it, but I will not prostrate to Adam.' So Allah gave the same answer that was submitted during the speech: 'Uridu al-ubudata min haythu uridu wa la min haythu turidu.' I want my worship to be as I want, not as you want. So the way of worship is the same as Allah's. The second thing is the hadith that was just presented, that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Sallu kama ra'aytumuni usalli.' So pray in the way you see me praying. Now, look, did you notice? The way you see me praying. So, meaning the prayer will be as the Prophet used to pray. Now, because people left the hem of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), did not hold onto the Ahlulbayt, did not act upon the hadith of the Messenger of Allah, 'Inni tarikun fikum al-thaqalayn.' So what was the result? The result was that today there are so many disagreements among Muslims. So many differences. On every single thing. Differences on every single thing. Meaning, there are differences among Muslims on small things. There are differences in how to perform Wudu. There are differences in how to pray. In almost everything, you see, in almost everything. What is the reason? The reason is only this, because they left the hem of Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.). The Prophet's hadith: 'Inni tarikun fikum al-thaqalayn, Kitaballahi wa 'itrati.' Now, some people here might say that they don't read the merits (Faza'il). Look, just reading merits is not enough; rather, 'Tamassuk' (holding fast) means taking everything from them that they have commanded. As we find in our traditions, in 'Bab al-Taslim' in Usul al-Kafi, there is a tradition that 'Man sarrahu yastakmil al-imana kullahu fal-yaqul...' Whoever wants his faith to be completely perfected should say: 'My statement in all matters is the statement of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) in what they have kept secret and what they have declared, and in what has reached me from them and what has not reached me.' Meaning, if someone wants his faith to be completely perfected, he should say that my belief in all things is the same belief that Ale Muhammad (a.s.) has. What has reached me, what has not reached me, what they have announced, what they have not announced, in everything. That is called 'Tamassuk'. Therefore, our tradition is that 'Al-Hujjatu qabla al-khalqi wa ma'a al-khalqi wa ba'da al-khalqi.' Whether you go East or West, you will not find the correct knowledge anywhere except that which has emanated from us, the Ahlulbayt, which has come from us. That is the only correct knowledge. So, in the same way, the method of worship is also the same. If someone leaves the correct Imam and goes here and there, then he will not find the correct method of worship either. Yes. Thank you, sir. The second and final question, we probably won't have much more time today. This question has come through Mr. S.M. Faiz Haider Sahab. And his question, sir, you mentioned a hadith during the speech: 'Al-Hujjatu qabla al-khalqi wa ma'a al-khalqi wa ba'da al-khalqi.' Now, related to this, his question is: Is the Hujjat of Allah different from other creations? Meaning, whenever the word 'khalq' (creation) is used in the Quran and Hadith, should we include the Hujjat of Allah in it, or is the Hujjat of Allah exempt from this word 'khalq'? No, look, this tradition, 'Al-Hujjatu qabla al-khalqi wa ma'a al-khalqi wa ba'da al-khalqi,' obviously this is a special hadith in which, here, Hujjat refers to Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.). And they are the Hujjat of Allah over all, all creations. Without any exception. There is no exception in it. Even no one. Master, is there a reason for 'Wajhullah'? Who is 'Wajhullah'? Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.). And on that day, Allah will ask, when no one is in the universe, everyone will perish. This will be the state of annihilation, then it will be asked, 'Liman al-mulku al-yawm?' To whom does the kingdom belong today? Then the voice of Truth will come, 'Lillahi al-wahidi al-qahhar.' So who will answer this? This answer will be the lights (Anwar) of Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.). Because at that time no one will be there, even the angels will not be there. Because when Israfil blows the Trumpet and everyone perishes, Allah himself will say to Israfil, 'Israfil, now you also perish.' So Israfil will also perish. So now who will remain? Who will bear witness? So only the lights of Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (a.s.) will bear witness. Yes. 'Wa akhiru da'wana an al-hamdu lillahi rabbil 'alamin.' Thank you, sir, thank you very much. And we are grateful to all the viewers for staying with us. InshaAllah, our topic for tomorrow, 'The Belief in Mahdism in the light of the Holy Quran and the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.),' under this same topic, bringing another subject, InshaAllah, InshaAllah, we will be present tomorrow at this same time, 10:30 PM India time. Until then, request for prayers, Khuda Hafiz. Upon Muhammad and Ale Muhammad, Salawat. 'Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in.'

title: Ep#09 | Kya Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Jaan Ke Khauf Se Ghaibat Mein Hain?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common misconception that Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) remains in occultation due to a fear of death. The speaker clarifies that the term 'fear' used in religious texts refers to the concern for the guidance of the people, not personal safety. By citing historical examples of prophets and the nature of the Ahlulbayt, the lecture explains that the Imam's occultation is strictly by Divine command, not human cowardice.
content:
Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan. A'udhu billahi al-sami' al-'alim min al-shaytan al-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alayka ya Wali al-'Asr adrikna. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. We welcome you to another episode of the 'Ma'rifat-e-Mahdi (ajtf) Questions and Answers' series. Let us move forward with this program and see what today's objection and question is. The objection is something like this: that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is in the occultation (Ghaybah) due to the fear of death or fear for his life. Yes, meaning the Imam (a.s.) fears death, fears for his life, and that is why he is not coming out of occultation; he is in occultation. So, let us see what answer we have for this question. First of all, let us see where this objection and question originated. The first thing is a sentence from the Ziyarat of the Imam recited on Fridays, where we find: 'Assalamu alayka ayyuhal muhazzabul khayif.' Here, the word 'khayif' (fearful) is used. We greet the Imam and say, 'Peace be upon the one who is purified and fearful.' Meaning, this sentence is used for the Imam (a.s.) that the Imam is fearful. Secondly, the sentence from Dua-e-Iftitah: 'Abdilhum min ba'di khawfihim amna' (Change their fear into security). Meaning, we are praying here that Allah (s.w.t.) may change the Imam's (a.s.) fear into security, implying the Imam (a.s.) is fearful. So, because the word 'fear' is used for the Imam (a.s.), the opponents conclude that the Imam (a.s.) fears death or for his life, and that is why he is in occultation and not reappearing. So, first of all, we should see that it is quite clear from these sentences that the Imam (a.s.) is indeed in danger of his life, and not just the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), but every proof (Hujjah) of Allah has been, is, and will be in danger of their life. Because as long as the enemy of Allah remains on this earth, the Hujjah of Allah will be in danger, because these are those luminous personalities by seeing whom people would embrace faith, by hearing whose voices people would embrace faith, which was absolutely intolerable to the enemy. They could not bear that anyone should turn towards Allah (s.w.t.) and believe in Him. Therefore, their entire effort was, and still is, to eliminate the representatives of Allah so that people do not incline towards them. Along with this, if we look, Pharaoh wanted to kill Prophet Musa (a.s.), people wanted to crucify Prophet Isa (a.s.), and there were several attempts to kill the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Meaning, people tried to kill all the prophets; their lives were all in danger. Similarly, the life of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is also in danger, but one cannot conclude from this that the Imam (a.s.) is in occultation because his life is in danger. If we look at Surah An-Naml, verse 10, Allah (s.w.t.) says: 'Ya Musa la takhaf inni la yakhaful ladayyal mursalun' (O Musa, do not fear; indeed, in My presence, the messengers do not fear). Meaning, Allah Himself protects them. Furthermore, if we look at the exegesis (Tafsir) of this verse, it is quite clear that Prophet Musa (a.s.) did not fear death; he did not fear that Pharaoh would kill him, but rather he feared that seeing the magic of these magicians, the believers might turn back. So, the Hujjah of Allah never fears that they will be killed or their lives will be taken; they always fear that people might turn away or become distant from Allah. Along with this, if we look, Prophet Musa (a.s.) himself crossed the Nile with his companions; this was not due to the fear of death, but by the command of the Lord. Allah called Prophet Isa (a.s.) to the fourth heaven and sent his likeness to be crucified; this was not due to Prophet Isa's (a.s.) fear, but it was Allah's command or Allah's will. And finally, if we look at the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), his migration from Makkah to Madinah—was it due to the fear of death, or was it the command of the Lord? This was truly a command from Allah for all these prophets, and they complied with this command. So, just as Prophet Musa, Prophet Isa, and the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) complied with Allah's command, in the same way, even today, Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is in the veil of occultation due to the command of Allah, not due to the fear of death. And finally, dear ones, if we look at those hadiths—even if we assume for a moment, for the sake of argument, that yes, Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is in the veil of occultation due to the fear of death—what about those hadiths that state that when the time of reappearance (Zuhur) comes, it will be a very turbulent environment? The Imam-e-Zamana will have many enemies; wherever the Imam looks, there will be enemies—meaning even his own people will have become strangers. When the Imam comes, people will say, 'We do not need you; go back.' So, there will be such an environment, meaning enemies everywhere. So, I would say that the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) should come today! If he is in occultation due to the fear of death, then at the time of Zuhur, there will be many more enemies, far more enemies, so it is better that he comes today. But it would not be surprising if a voice comes from the veil of occultation, if Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) calls out and says, 'Perhaps you do not know that we are those at whose door even the Angel of Death does not come without permission. We belong to that household whose youth, if he draws a line on the ground with a broken spear, the army of 900,000 does not have the courage to take even one step forward. We are those whose six-month-old child goes into the battlefield, challenges the enemy, and after receiving a three-pronged arrow in his throat, smiles and strangles death itself.' So, do you imagine that we, the Imam of the time, will fear death? Rather, death is sweeter than honey to us. And the Imam whose protection has been taken upon Himself by Allah, how can that Imam have a fear of death? He does not fear death, but he certainly has a longing to put the enemies of Allah to death. So, in the end, we pray that O Lord, by the intercession of Janabe Fatimatuz Zahra (s.a.), by her broken ribs, may You hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) for the sake of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), hasten his reappearance, and grant us the honor of being counted among his helpers and supporters. Along with this, may the service of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) be our destiny in this world and the hereafter. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. To give the correct answer to this question, go to the comment section of this video or check the video description and click on the link provided there to give the correct answer. From those who give the correct answer, two winners will be chosen through a lucky draw in each episode, and they will be given an Indian ₹1000 voucher as a gift. Insha'Allah, the quiz link will be active until the 20th of Shaban.
