title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Par Jhoota Ilzaam Lagaane Waale Ka Anjaam
excerpt: This lecture recounts a historical incident where a man falsely claimed 1000 dinars from Imam Hasan (a.s.). When brought before the judge Shurayh, the Imam allowed the man to take an oath to receive the money, but specifically dictated the wording of the oath. Upon swearing falsely and taking the money, the man immediately died, illustrating the severe consequences of lying against the Ahlulbayt and the profound spiritual insight of the Imam.
content:
A man was making a false claim against Imam Hasan (a.s.). The narration is as follows: 'Idda'a rajulun 'alal Hasani bni 'Aliyyin 'alayhimas salam alf dinarin kadhiban' (A man falsely claimed 1000 dinars from Imam Hasan (a.s.)), while it was not like that at all. Imam Hasan (a.s.) did not have to give him anything. The man went to Qadi Shurayh. Now, Shurayh said to Imam Hasan (a.s.), 'Are you ready to take an oath?' The Imam (a.s.) said that if my opponent takes an oath, I will give him 1000 dinars. Now, Shurayh is stating the formula of the oath for this man. He says, 'Qul billahilladhi la ilaha illa huwal 'alimul ghaybi wash shahadah' (Say by Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Knower of the unseen and the seen). Imam (a.s.) said that I do not want this kind of oath. The Imam says, 'Just say: By Allah, you have to give this to me, and take these 1000 dinars.' The man took the oath just as Imam Hasan (a.s.) stated, 'Billah' (by Allah), and he took the 1000 dinars. As soon as he stood up from his place, he breathed his last right there. The Imam says that I was afraid that if he had taken the oath using the first formula, he would have been forgiven. On what basis? 'Bi barakatit tawhid' (By the blessing of Tawhid). Meaning, who can tell what the blessing of Tawhid is? When will its effect occur? Even someone like Shurayh, who sat on the chair of judgment, did not have the knowledge of this. Where will you bring an Imam like this? Binur Maulana Hasan Salli, Binur Maulana Hasan Salli. Ya Rasul Allah, Sallallahu alayhi wa ali Muhammad, wa ali Muhammad.

title: Ep#05 | Quran e Majeed Mein Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s)
excerpt: This lecture explores the validity of the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) within Islam, arguing that it is a foundational concept supported by both the Quran and the Sunnah. The speaker cites evidence from both Shia and Sunni scholars, such as Sayyid Hashim Bahrani and Sheikh Sulayman Qunduzi, to demonstrate that the Quranic verses regarding the ultimate victory of Islam refer to the reappearance of the Imam. The session concludes by emphasizing that belief in the 'unseen' (al-ghayb) is a defining characteristic of a true believer.
content:
He la he la he la he la he la he la he la he la he la he la he la he la Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan. A'udhu billahi sami'ul 'alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya waliyal asr, ajjallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif, adriknah. Respected viewers, Assalamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. The topic of our discussion today is: Is the belief in Mahdism an Islamic belief, or is it specific only to the Shias? Dear ones, the most fundamental condition for any belief to be correct and valid is that its mention should be present in the Holy Quran. If the mention of any belief or principle is present in the Holy Quran, then this is an irrefutable proof that this belief is correct and valid. The belief in Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) or the belief in Mahdism is a valid Islamic belief, the mention of which is found in both the Holy Quran and the hadiths of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Scholars of both Shia and Sunni sects have mentioned in their books the verses that relate to Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.). For example, a famous and well-known Shia scholar, Sayyid Hashim Bahrani (r.a.), in his valuable book 'Al-Mahajjah', has mentioned 120 verses that relate to Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Similarly, a great Sunni scholar, Sheikh Sulayman Qunduzi Hanafi, in his famous book 'Yanabi al-Muwaddah', has included a complete chapter in which he has mentioned the verses related to Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.). And interestingly, he has named this chapter: 'The mention of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) in the Holy Quran.' Let us present a part of this book for you. In his book, he mentions verse number 9 of Surah Tawbah: 'Huwalladhi arsala rasulahu bil huda wa dinil haqqi liyuzhirahu 'alad dini kullihi wa law karihal mushrikun' (It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it). Meaning, Allah is the one who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth so that he may make Islam victorious over all religions... ...even if the polytheists find it unpleasant. In the exegesis of this verse, he writes: 'Wallahi ma yajee'u ta'wiluha hatta yakhrujal Imamul Mahdiyyu 'alayhis salam' (By God, the interpretation of this will not come until Imam Mahdi (a.s.) reappears). He further writes that when Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) reappears, he will bring a revolution such that no polytheist or enemy of the religion will remain except that he will be killed. And if an enemy of the religion hides even in a stone, that stone will call out, 'O believer, an enemy of the religion is hidden in me; break me and kill him.' Similarly, there is another famous Shia scholar whose name is Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Babawayh al-Qummi (r.a.), who is famous by the title of Sheikh Saduq. He writes in his valuable book 'Kamal al-Din wa Tamam al-Ni'mah', and this book is specifically related to Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) and was written at the command of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). At the beginning of this book, in the exegesis of the opening verse of Surah Baqarah, 'Alladhina yu'minuna bil ghayb' (Those who believe in the unseen), he writes that here 'the unseen' refers to Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), and it is this belief in occultation that distinguishes a believer and a Shia from the members of other sects. So, respected viewers, the belief in Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is a belief that is proven by both the Quran and the Sunnah. We pray to Allah that He hastens the reappearance of Hazrat Wali al-Asr (a.j.t.f.s.) and counts us all among his helpers and supporters. Amin ya Rabbal Alamin. Wa sallallahu ala Muhammad wa alihi tahirin. title: Ali (a.s.) is the Best of Men | Verse of Khair al-Bariyyah | آيت خیر البرية
excerpt: This lecture explores the interpretation of the Quranic verse 'Khayrul-Bariyyah' (the best of creatures) from Surah al-Bayyinah. The speaker provides evidence from both Shia and Sunni scholarly sources to demonstrate that this title refers specifically to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib and his followers. By citing narrations from the Prophet Muhammad, the lecture emphasizes the consensus regarding the high status of the Imam and his Shia in the eyes of Allah.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless our master and our guide. Regarding the Holy Quran and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), the discussion we will have today is about verse number 7 of Surah Bayyinah, where the Lord of the Worlds states: 'Inna ladhina amanu wa amilus-salihati ulaika hum khayrul-bariyyah' (Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they are the best of creatures). Regarding this verse, it has been narrated in a large number of books of both the Shia and Sunni schools, and they are unanimous and in agreement that the Master of the Universe and the Shia are the best of Allah's creatures, i.e., Khayrul-Bariyyah. Let us begin with the books of the Shia, where Sheikh Tusi narrates in his book 'Al-Amali' from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), where Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) narrates from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), that he says: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) reciting this verse, then when he looked at me and said, O Ali, by Allah, O Ali, by Allah, you and your followers, you and your...' By Allah, you and your followers, you and your Shia are Khayrul-Bariyyah, meaning the best of Allah's creatures. And in the same way, we see in other books, such as 'Tafsir Furat al-Kufi', where Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) narrates from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated: 'O Ali, indeed those who have believed and done righteous deeds, they are Khayrul-Bariyyah, the best of Allah's creatures. And O Ali, this Khayrul-Bariyyah is you and your followers, you and your Shia. And you and your Shia will come to me on the Day of Judgment, and at that time Allah will be pleased with you and your Shia, and you and your Shia will be pleased with Allah.' So here we saw that it has been clearly stated that the Master of the Universe and his Shia are Khayrul-Bariyyah in the books of the Shia. Likewise, let us now see how the narration is recorded in the books of the Sunni school. So, the famous and well-known scholar of the Sunni school, Jalaluddin al-Suyuti, narrates in his book 'Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur' from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari that he was present in the service of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and at that time the Messenger... He was present in the service of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and at that time the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated: 'By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, Khayrul-Bariyyah is Ali and the Shia of Ali.' And at that very moment, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), arrived, and upon his arrival, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated: 'O Ali, you and your Shia are Khayrul-Bariyyah, the best of Allah's creatures.' And immediately after that, this verse was revealed. So after that, whenever the companions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) saw the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), they would say, 'Look, Khayrul-Bariyyah, the best of Allah's creatures, is coming.' And in the same way, Atiyyah narrates from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri; Abu Sa'id al-Khudri states that Ali (a.s.) is Khayrul-Bariyyah, the best of Allah's creatures. And in this way, from this summary, it becomes clear to us that the books of the Shia and the Sunni are unanimous and in agreement that Khayrul-Bariyyah refers to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and his Shia. Only and only his Shia. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.)  |  Ep#03 - Bait e Tatheer Par Hamla - Ahle Tasannun Ki Kitaabon Mein
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical controversy surrounding the attack on the house of Sayyida Fatima Zahra (s.a.) by examining narrations found within Sunni historical texts. The speakers argue that the threat to burn the house is documented in reliable sources like 'Tarikh al-Tabari' and 'Ansab al-Ashraf'. By analyzing these accounts and the reported deathbed regrets of Abu Bakr, the presenters conclude that the attack is a historically substantiated event rather than a mere allegation.
content:
Has received the award. In all the rivers, including... Yes, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Respected brothers, in the month of Rajab, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. In the series of answers to the attacks on Sayyida Zahra (s.a.), after answering the first one, today we present the second one and its answer. It is that the biggest objection raised by the opposition is that the attack on the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is not proven in any reliable book or through any reliable hadith. So, to clarify this, we request our brother... to present the answer to this objection to our viewers. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi. As you have heard, this is the objection raised by the opposition, and it is a major objection that this door-burning incident is not proven through any reliable hadith. So, is the reality of this painful incident present in any Sunni book? Can this incident be presented through any reliable hadith? We request you to present a clear answer to this for our viewers. Certainly, Insha'Allah. In the name of Allah, I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Peace be upon Fatima Zahra, and her father, and her husband, and her children... Before answering this, I want to clarify one thing at the beginning of my speech: as the question has been raised that it is not proven through any reliable hadith in the Sunni school, we are trying to remove this academic doubt—an academic doubt in which we will present only and only those narrations that are proven through authentic and reliable hadiths, which are present in the reliable books, because... The important subject present here is because our only purpose is to convey the truth to people as much as possible, for the benefit of the city. After that, whether to accept or reject the results derived from the hadiths is up to each individual's own conscience. However, we will not say anything that is baseless. Our approach will remain to present our points through authentic hadiths. Now, regarding the response to this objection, we will present three hadiths from the Sunni books. One is from 'Tarikh al-Tabari', and the author of this 'Tarikh al-Tabari' is Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari. He is considered a very great scholar and a very great historian. Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani writes about Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his book, saying that Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari is an Imam of the highest order. It is with these words that al-Tabari is remembered. And which item is this? If we talk about 'Tarikh al-Tabari', in volume 3, page 208, it is written that he [Umar] came to the house of Ali, in which... He came to the house of Ali, in which he [Ali] and those who were with him were present. At that time, he said, 'By God, I will burn you all, unless you come out for allegiance.' This is one thing. And the second hadith is also present in 'Tarikh al-Tabari'. It is exactly this; 'Tarikh al-Tabari' is in front of you: 'I will burn the house, or you come out for allegiance.' And the other hadith is from 'Ansab al-Ashraf' by al-Baladhuri. Its author is Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Jabir al-Baladhuri. Before reading this hadith, it is necessary to know who this Ibn Abi Shaybah is, according to our Sunni brothers. Let us tell our viewers that this Ibn Abi Shaybah is one of the narrators of Sahih Bukhari. Many hadiths in Sahih Bukhari have been narrated through this Ibn Abi Shaybah. In 'Ansab al-Ashraf', volume 1, page 432, this hadith is found, and in this hadith... In 'Ansab al-Ashraf', volume 1, page 432, this hadith is found, and in this hadith, all the narrators are authentic. If we start arguing about its chain of narration, we can verify every narrator through the books of the Sunni brothers. But since there is no room in this program, we will not go into the chain of narration. What is written in this hadith? When people talked about allegiance after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), they came to Ali (a.s.) and Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and consulted them, but they did not give allegiance. When this news reached Umar, he said, 'I will burn the house.' When this news reached the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), what happened? When he came to the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.w.a.), Umar said, 'O daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), by God... By God, we love you the most, and if we love anyone after your father, it is your husband. And by God, we do not love anyone after your father more than him. But then, what is this statement of his? 'By God, because you have gathered these people in your house, I will burn this house.' This is an expression of love, and after that, he immediately said, 'Because you have gathered these people, I will burn the house.' Giving the order to burn the house is a historical fact, and it is present in both 'Tarikh al-Tabari' and 'Ansab al-Ashraf'. It is absolutely clear and evident from both books that they threatened to burn the house of Maula Ali (a.s.). They threatened to burn the house of Ali (a.s.). Now, if we look at it, it is proven from both sides that a threat was made to burn the door of the house. But one might ask, was the door actually burned? If someone asks us this, we will present the answer. You have asked a very good question. Before giving the answer, let us say that for all of us, it is a matter of concern that if there is a threat to burn the house, then the question arises: is burning a house or threatening to burn it something the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ever did in his life? Did he ever order such a thing? And whose house was being threatened? This is the house where the Ahl al-Risalah lived. This is the house where Hazrat Fatima (s.a.w.a.) lived. This is the house where Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (a.s.) lived. They are talking about burning that house. This is the Ahl al-Risalah, and on one side is this love, and on the other side is the talk of burning the house. What kind of love is this? Secondly, as you asked, those who try to save their reputation by saying that this was only a threat and the house was not actually burned, this argument does not hold up. This argument is against the Quran and the hadiths. Both hadiths swear by God—the oath of God—that 'I will burn it.' And if someone says that in the hadith, there is a condition that if they do not give allegiance, then I will burn it, then if someone says that Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance, then the hadith of Sahih Bukhari is proven false. Which hadith? The one in Sahih Bukhari which says that until Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.w.a.) was alive in this world, Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance to anyone. If this is the case, then this door was not burned? If this door was not burned, then according to the other hadith, one has to admit that Umar swore a false oath by God and ordered the burning of the house, and he was only bluffing. Either this is possible, or the other possibility is that if there was no allegiance, then one has to admit that the hadiths included by the Sunni brothers are false. What Aisha said is what everyone says. One has to admit this. And if neither of these is possible, then only one possibility remains: the order to burn the door and the threat to break it were given, and this door was indeed burned, and the house was attacked. And not only this, we will cover this in the third and final hadith to complete our point. How did the news reach that the door was burned? It is that Abu Bakr, in his final days, said three things and regretted them, saying, 'I regret these three things.' This is also in the history books. This is also in the history books, and he regretted it. He said, 'I regret that I did these three things.' Among these, the first thing he was asked about was, 'I wish I had not opened the house of Fatima, even if they had locked it for war.' This means there was a door, and it was locked from the inside. By saying this, he is pointing towards the fact that it should not have happened, but it did happen, and there was an attack. If there was an attack, then the regret makes sense. This regret points to the fact that they attacked the house of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.w.a.). Some have presented the answer in this way, that those who raise objections on this issue are raising objections because they do not study their own books. You have seen that this hadith about burning the door is not from any Shia source; it is present in the books of the Sunni brothers. I hope that even after this, if someone is not satisfied with this answer, they can contact us through our WhatsApp number and our social media handles. You can send your objections and questions to us, and God willing, we will try to provide you with the answers. With this, we conclude this episode, and in the next episode, I will be with you... And in the next episode, I will be with you. Subscribe. [Music]

chapters.title: The Wisdom of Dawah and Death
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the Quranic principle of inviting people to Allah's path through wisdom and good instruction, emphasizing that true Dawah should offer hope rather than fear.

chapters.title: Reflections on Mortality
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the human tendency to fear death despite witnessing its inevitability, contrasting this with the peace and composure displayed by Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions on the day of Ashura.

chapters.title: Understanding the Reality of Death
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that death is a necessary transition and that understanding its nature is vital for human spiritual growth.

chapters.title: The Soul and the Day of Judgment
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the soul's journey after death, the concept of the 'ajb al-dhanab', and the sharpening of human insight on the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: Sleep as a Minor Death
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the prophetic tradition of viewing sleep as a minor death, emphasizing the importance of remembering Allah in both life and death.

chapters.title: The Dangers of Sin and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker warns that sinning can distance a believer from the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and advises avoiding environments where sinful activities occur.

chapters.title: Death as a Bridge to the Afterlife
chapters.summary: Death is described as a bridge that transitions the believer from the 'prison' of this world to the 'palace' of Paradise, while disbelievers face eternal consequences.

chapters.title: The Inevitability of Death
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that death is inescapable regardless of one's status or location, urging listeners to prepare for their inevitable meeting with Allah.

chapters.title: Human Ambition and Aging
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how human desires and ambitions often persist even into old age, despite the certainty of death and the need for spiritual readiness.

chapters.title: The Role of Izra'il and Divine Sovereignty
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that Allah holds ultimate authority over death, and while Izra'il is the Angel of Death, there are specific exceptions for the Prophet and the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Exceptions to the Angel of Death's Authority
chapters.summary: Drawing from historical texts, the speaker explains that the Prophet and Imam Ali (a.s.) are exempt from the standard process of having their souls taken by the Angel of Death.

chapters.title: The Intercession of Ahlulbayt at Death
chapters.summary: The love and Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt serve as a source of salvation and comfort for believers during the critical moments of death and the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Promise to the Believers
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the story of Hashim Ansari to illustrate that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) will personally visit and comfort the believers at the time of their passing.

chapters.title: The Departure from Madinah
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical context of Imam Hussain's departure from Madinah despite warnings from others.

chapters.title: The Caravan of Bani Hashim
chapters.summary: A description of the members of the Ahlulbayt, including Ali Akbar and others, preparing to depart with Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: Lamentation for Bibi Sugra
chapters.summary: A poetic and emotional reflection on the suffering of Bibi Sugra, who was left behind in Madinah while her family faced tragedy in Karbala.

title: The Reality of Rumi  |  Sayed Mahdi Modarresi
excerpt: Sayed Mahdi Modarresi critiques the widespread admiration for the poet Rumi among some Shia Muslims who are unaware of his controversial theological views. He highlights specific passages in Rumi's Masnavi that insult Abu Talib, the father of Imam Ali, by questioning his faith and labeling him a wicked man. The lecture serves as a warning to be discerning and to use the teachings of the Ahlulbayt as a litmus test before promoting figures whose beliefs contradict core Shia tenets.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 13 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture discusses the laws and etiquette of fasting, focusing on the distinction between obligatory and recommended (mustahab) fasts. The speaker emphasizes the importance of acting upon the Quran and explains the rules regarding breaking a voluntary fast to honor a social invitation. Additionally, the session covers specific dates for recommended fasting and the validity of making a vow (nadhr) to fast for spiritual needs.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. [Music] As we are in the beginning of our program, 10th of Ramadan and the Quran, today also, in front of you, the martyrdom of the Imam, immediately after that, which is eagerly awaited, that many... Which is eagerly awaited, that many who recite the Quran do so... therefore, we realize that those who read the Quran and do not act upon it... we should act upon it so that we can make it a habit of the Quran and can do it. And 15 days, it should not be that in acting upon the Quran, we take the lead. Imam (a.s.) says while sharing with all the people, 'For God's sake, for God's sake, act upon the Quran. See, no one should take the lead over you in acting upon the Quran. You should try your best that before anyone else, you... keep in mind.' Regarding the matter of fasting, I can keep it in mind, and if not, I can eat. I should abstain from eating and drinking. Look, it was mentioned in 1997, according to the golden rules... before the time of Imam al-Abidin (a.s.), if there is something that breaks the fast, the fast becomes invalid. However, if a person intends to fast during the day, even if it is after Dhuhr (noon), it is not obligatory for them to fast that day. And since it is not obligatory, if they want to eat or drink, there is no restriction. It is not obligatory for a person to fast in such a situation; rather, they have the choice. They have the choice, and they can eat. Regarding the question of whether it is true that if I am keeping a mustahab (recommended) fast and someone invites me to eat, is it permissible for me to break it to accept their invitation? There is no doubt that accepting an invitation is a virtuous act. Our scholars have also stated very clearly that if a person is keeping a mustahab fast, they should accept the invitation. In fact, they have gone as far as to say that even if it is after Dhuhr, you should eat, because the respect for a believer is very great, and refusing might hurt their feelings. And if you refuse, it will cause some distress. Pleasing a believer is a very great reward. So, both points are true: if you are keeping a mustahab fast and someone invites you after Dhuhr, you should eat. You don't even need to tell them that you are fasting. If someone brings food before me, I should eat it so as not to hurt their feelings. If you think you will get the reward of fasting, perhaps you will get the reward for this as well. You should consider that mercy is greater than everything. Why would you choose otherwise? If you are worried about breaking the fast, remember that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Seeing. Insha'Allah, we will not think ill of anyone. We will say that their intention was good, and if they broke it, they broke it. Remember, you will get the reward. Yes, when you are breaking it, it is not that you are angry; you will get the reward for fasting and the reward for accepting a believer's invitation. And if you are getting something to eat, then this is fine. There is no doubt or difficulty in this according to our scholars, so you can definitely break it. But remember, don't get angry. Regarding mustahab fasts, I will give you some dates. It is highly recommended to fast on the first of every month, the last Thursday of the month, and... The first Thursday of the month, and after the 10th of the month, the first Wednesday that comes. These are mustahab fasts. There are many such fasts. Also, fasting on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of every month is mustahab. Even if you want to keep them, look, keeping mustahab fasts is recommended. There are specific dates like the 4th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the 1st of Dhu al-Hijjah, and the 1st, 3rd, and 7th of Muharram, and the 15th of Muharram. [Music] That is fine. After that, whenever you want to keep a mustahab fast, there is a lot of room for it. There is a lot of room for it. Whenever you want, you can keep it. There is no restriction. If you can keep it, it is good. It is not necessary, but it is recommended. You can read as much as you want and keep as many fasts as you want. It is fine. Except for the day of Ashura, you can keep fasts on other days; there is no restriction. Look, a person's strength matters. If you are keeping a fast and you feel weak, then... What is the benefit? It is for the recitation of the Quran and for the fulfillment of needs. In both cases, it is very beneficial. If you pray to Allah, it is the best way to ensure the health of these children. Nothing else is needed. There are so many narrations about this; it is not just one or two places. For many prayers and needs, if you have a need, you can make a vow (nadhr) to fast. This is allowed in Sharia. It is a legal act, and our scholars have confirmed this. It is present in our Sharia, and all our scholars and maraji have confirmed it. All our maraji have confirmed this in this regard, that when one makes a vow (nadhr) to fast, they must fulfill it. There is no doubt about it. Now, the second point: regarding mustahab fasts, if a person stays hungry all day without the intention of fasting, and then makes the intention before Dhuhr, does it count as a mustahab fast? It does not count. The difference is that if you are not performing the act of fasting and you are just staying hungry, and you decide before Dhuhr... And before Dhuhr, we have scholars who say that even after Dhuhr, you can break it. It is mustahab, so it cannot be obligatory. You can keep it as you wish. Regarding the traveler, we have discussed this before. For today, you can keep it for three days. You can keep it on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. This act is based on the intention. If someone changes their mind, it is fine. You have asked us, and we have answered. For those who are watching, you can send your questions to this WhatsApp number [number removed]. If there is any confusion in this month, then...

title: Kiska Hajj Qubool Hoga? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the criteria for the acceptance of Hajj, emphasizing that performing the rituals is not enough on its own. Drawing from a narration of Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker highlights that the spiritual validity of one's worship is deeply tied to the concept of Wilayah. Ultimately, the talk concludes that only those who hold love for the Ahlulbayt and disassociate from their enemies will have their deeds accepted by Allah.
content:
Every Muslim hopes and tries to perform this great worship at least once in their life. The command of Islam is also that if a person has the financial means, they should go for Hajj once in their life. And it is also seen that every year, millions of people from different countries reach the House of Allah (Kaaba) to perform Hajj and carry out the rituals of Hajj, sacrifice, etc., only with the hope that Allah will accept their worship. But is everyone's Hajj accepted? Is Hajj just the name of completing a few rituals? Dawud bin Kathir narrates that one year I was on Hajj with Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). When we were passing through a path, the Imam... When we were passing through a path, Imam (a.s.) climbed a mountain and looked towards the crowd of people and said, 'Ma... [Music] Indeed, Allah will never forgive those who associate partners with Him. He is the one who worships someone other than God.' Dawud bin Kathir says that I asked, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, do you know who among these is your friend and who is your enemy?' Imam (a.s.) replied, 'O Dawud, there is no servant who, when he is born, it is not written on his forehead whether he is a friend or an enemy of the religion. And indeed, when a person comes to us with our Wilayah and disassociation (Bara'at) from our enemies... With our Wilayah and disassociation from our enemies, when he arrives, we read the writing on his forehead whether he is a friend or an enemy. He recites, 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim' [Music]. Based on this sign, we recognize who is our enemy and who is our friend. [Music] From this Hadith of Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), it is absolutely clear that only the Hajj, prayers, and deeds of that person will be accepted who has the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and his pure family in his heart, and includes disassociation from their enemies. We pray to the court of Allah Ta'ala that He grants them a great place in Makkah and grants us the Hajj of Baitullah and the Ziyarat of the Masumeen (a.s.) in a way that is accepted. Ameen.
Hajj is a mandatory obligation for those who possess the financial means.
Performing the physical rituals of Hajj does not automatically guarantee acceptance by Allah.
Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) possessed the divine knowledge to distinguish between the friends and enemies of the Ahlulbayt.
A person's spiritual status is inscribed upon them from birth.
Wilayah (allegiance to the Imams) is the essential foundation for the acceptance of all religious deeds.
Disassociation (Bara'at) from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt is a necessary component of faith.
True worship requires both love for the pure family of the Prophet and rejection of their oppressors.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 4 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture, the fourth in a series on the laws and etiquette of fasting, features Maulana Zulfiqar Mehdi answering questions from believers regarding Ramadan. The discussion covers the permissibility of feeding non-fasting individuals, strategies for maintaining focus during prayer, and the impact of touching a corpse on one's fast. The session emphasizes the importance of spiritual preparation, mindfulness, and verifying information before sharing it on social media.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad... Peace be upon you all, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. In this fourth episode of the series on the rituals of fasting, we welcome and greet all our viewers. In the second episode, Maulana... in a very relevant manner, presented answers to the questions. Friends, this month... Presented answers to the questions. Friends, this month is a month full of the blessings, mercy, and forgiveness of Allah. This is a month that is better than all other months, its nights are better than all other nights, its days are better than all other days. It is a month in which Allah is inviting us for a purpose. It is a month in which even breathing is worship, sleeping is worship, and all our deeds are going to be accepted in this blessed month. We should pray to Allah more and more that He grants us the maximum ability to perform good deeds. Once again, to answer the questions, we have with us the respected Maulana Zulfiqar Mehdi Sahab. I request all viewers to welcome Maulana with a Salawat. The first question that has come from a believer is: If a person feeds someone in Ramadan who is not fasting, or has broken their fast, is it permissible to feed that person or not? ... The question is, if you feed someone, will you be a sinner? If you feed someone who is sick, or a traveler, or someone who is not obligated to fast, then feeding them is permissible. But it becomes forbidden if, by your feeding them, they are encouraged to abandon fasting, or if you are helping them in a sin. At that time, it will be a sin for you. At that time, it will be a sin for you if you are helping them in a way that encourages them to break their fast. You should not help in sin and transgression. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahab, for clarifying this. The next question that has come to our WhatsApp number from a believer is: 'Whenever I perform any worship, evil thoughts often come to my mind, due to which I have to perform prayers, etc., again. And I always think of performing the worship perfectly. If these are satanic whispers, please shed some light on how to avoid them.' See, this issue... Allah has many ways... First of all, know and understand well that if you keep trying continuously to keep your focus, your mind will be engaged... but our Masumeen (a.s.) have given a great solution for this. The reason these things arise is that you are [overthinking]... If you are constantly preoccupied with worldly matters and chasing after things, you will only attain those things. If you work in this world, you have to live with your children and share things with them; that is a worldly matter. On the other hand, consider this: the more you weaken your attachment to the world, the more you strengthen the other side. Secondly, regarding our prayers, it has been stated that if you want to focus, try to prepare 8 to 10 minutes before the prayer to alleviate any distress. Another thing is, why does the mind wander? It is because of the state of one's body. The reason it is on your body is because of the work you are doing and how you are moving. When you are praying, you should be standing as if you are in front of someone, standing still. You must be aware of where you are. After the intention (niyyah) and saying 'Allahu Akbar', you should be focused. If you are reciting Surahs, you should do so with tranquility and contemplation. You should recite with tranquility and contemplation. This means you should understand what you are saying. Before you begin, seek help from Allah, and a sense of peace will be born. Secondly, let the greatness of Allah settle deep into your heart so that you realize you are standing in prayer. If a person prays like a bird pecking at grain, quickly and without focus, then they cannot truly speak to Allah. If you have any confusion or distress, ask about it. Many people keep things to themselves. What you are saying is very good, but I am going to say something else. If you want to walk on the path of spirituality, there is a method. If you want to leave behind worldly distractions for those two hours of prayer... For this, I have seen many young people like you who have increased their social interactions. If you are in a place where there is a lot of noise, move to a quiet place. Why shouldn't you? This is a great blessing. We are very grateful to you. As you observed, when we are performing Wudu, we should be very attentive. Before prayer, we should recite some Quran and perform our prayers with peace and the recognition of God. If we keep training our body and soul in this way, it will certainly become easier, and we will be able to perform our acts of worship in the best possible manner. Thank you, thank you for answering the questions. Thank you for answering the questions. The next question for you is regarding touching a corpse and fasting. Please shed some light on this. Touching a corpse does not invalidate the fast. It is not something that breaks the fast. The question of touching a corpse and fasting has nothing to do with each other. If you touch a corpse, you must perform Ghusl to pray, but it has no effect on your fast. Your fast will remain valid unless you do something that actually breaks the fast. Touching a corpse or being near it does not matter; it is just like any other situation. To pray, you must perform Ghusl. This is a very good question, especially since WhatsApp and social media have become common. If you know something is a lie, you cannot spread it. But if you do not know and you are sharing it, you are not necessarily lying, but you should be careful. You can only attribute something if you have seen it in a book or have verified it. The truth is that if you are not sure, you should say that you have heard it, or that it has been reported. You can say that you have heard it or that it has been reported. You should not attribute it to someone if you are not certain, just to add weight to your words. If you do that, you are lying. Similarly, if you do not know something and you repeat what people are saying, you should be careful. Thank you very much for your help. We are grateful to our viewers who are watching our program. Viewers, if anyone has any questions regarding Ramadan, please send them to our WhatsApp number. On this WhatsApp number, we are very grateful to the Maulana for taking his precious time to answer all our questions, which increases the knowledge of the believers. With this, we bid farewell to our viewers and Maulana Masood. Until the next episode, Fi Amanillah, Khuda Hafiz.

title: #2 - Ziyaarat-e-Arbaeen Mein Imam Husain (as) Ki Mazloomiyat | Sharh-e-Ziyaarat-e-Arbaeen [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of Imam Husayn's (as) oppression and martyrdom as highlighted in the Ziyarat-e-Arbaeen. The speaker emphasizes the title 'al-mazlum al-shahid,' reflecting on the Imam's suffering and his status as the one martyred while in a state of grief. The talk encourages believers to prioritize the tragedy of Karbala in their daily lives and personal moments of sorrow.
content:
[Music] A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alayka ya Waliyyallah. As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. As-salamu 'alal Husayn, wa 'ala 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, wa 'ala awlad al-Husayn, wa 'ala ashab al-Husayn. [Music] An important aspect of Imam Husayn (a.s.) is his oppression and his oppressed martyrdom. In this phrase of the Ziyarat of Arba'een, a believer remembers the oppression of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and greets him: 'As-salamu 'ala al-maẓlum al-shahid'—peace be upon Husayn, who is both oppressed and a martyr. Peace be upon the one who was surrounded by calamities and the one who was killed while being made to weep. Imam Hussain (a.s.) is the martyr upon whom oppression was inflicted first and then he was martyred. This can be gauged from the statement of Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself, which he said while remembering his Shias in his final moments: 'O my Shias, whenever you drink cold water, remember me, and whenever you hear about a stranger or a martyr, weep for me.' The requirement of being a follower and a Shia of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is that we prioritize the grief and tragedy of Imam Hussain (a.s.) over all our own troubles and sorrows. That is why we Shias also commemorate the memory of our deceased by mentioning the tragedies of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and shedding tears for him. Imam Hussain (a.s.) was surrounded by enemies from all sides; he was mourning over the bodies of his companions and loved ones, and the oppressors martyred him in that very state of grief and weeping. So much so that Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself stated: 'Ana qateelul abarāt' (I am the one who was martyred while being made to weep). I am the one who was martyred while being made to weep. Whenever any believer mentions me, he will weep. O Allah, for the sake of the oppression of Imam Hussain (a.s.), when we go to Karbala for his Ziyarat, grant us the ability to remember his oppression and weep for him. Amen.

title: Pehli Ummul Momineen – Hazrat e Khadijatul Kubra (s.a.) Ki Wafaat [ENG SUBS] | 10th of Maahe Ramazan
excerpt: This lecture honors the life and sacrifices of Hazrat Khadijatul Kubra (s.a.) on the anniversary of her passing. It highlights her status as the first woman to embrace Islam, her unwavering support for the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) through her wealth, and her role as the mother of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). The talk concludes with a reflection on her heavenly status and a prayer for devotion to her legacy.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, may Allah the Almighty hasten his noble reappearance, help us. Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) is that great and sacred personality, like whom no woman came into the world before her, and except for her daughter, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), no one is superior to her. You (s.a.) were the first wife of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and among all the wives of the Prophet, Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) holds this status that as long as she was in this world, the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had no other wife. Among all the wives of the Prophet, the lady who spent the most time in the marriage of the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.). Your services and efforts for Islam are so immense that no matter how much they are mentioned, the right of mention cannot be fulfilled. What greater virtue could there be for any woman than the fact that Allah the Almighty chose you to be the noble mother of Hazrat Siddiqa-e-Tahira Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) is the foundation and basis of the progeny of the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.). You are the first woman in Islamic history who believed in the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and you were also the first woman to pray behind the Messenger in Mecca. Believing after Islam spread and gained supremacy in Medina is one thing, and expressing one's faith among the polytheists in Mecca is another. You helped your husband, Hazrat Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.), by spending your wealth and defended the true religion when the Prophet was surrounded by opponents from all sides. The Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself confirmed this in his hadith when he said: 'Ma nafa'ani malun qattu ma nafa'ani malu Khadija' (No wealth ever benefited me as much as the wealth of Khadija (s.a.) benefited me). The religion of Islam will always be indebted to Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) because her wealth helped the religion of Islam stand on its feet. Ten years after the Bi'that (Prophethood), on the 10th of Ramadan, you bid farewell to this transient world. Your separation was so heavy for your beloved daughter Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that when Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) passed away, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) clung to her father Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.) and asked, 'O Father! Where is my noble mother?' Then Jibra'il (a.s.) descended and said to the Prophet that your Lord has commanded you to tell Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) that your noble mother is in a house whose minarets are made of red ruby and studded with gold, and this house is between the houses of Lady Asiya and Maryam bint-e-Imran (s.a.). Upon this, Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) said that indeed Allah is Salam (Peace), peace is from Him and for Him. On behalf of all the believers, we offer our condolences on the occasion of the death anniversary of Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and especially to the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), and all the Infallible Imams (a.s.), especially Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), and we pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us and our progeny the special grace of devotion to Umm al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija (s.a.). Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This lecture introduces a new program titled 'Shamime Ma'rifat', which focuses on the spiritual recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt. The speaker emphasizes the necessity of loving the Prophet's household as a prerequisite for intercession and the acceptance of deeds on the Day of Judgment. The series aims to explore various aspects of this divine recognition through weekly sessions.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Hold fast to the love (mawaddat) of us, the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), for whoever meets Allah on the Day of Judgment with our love will enter Paradise through our intercession. And I swear by the One in whose hand is my soul, no deed will benefit a servant except with the recognition (ma'rifat) of our right.' Keeping this hadith in view, 'The Strong Rope' is presenting its new program for you from June 6, 2020, to August 15, 2020, every Saturday at 10:00 PM India time, titled 'Shamime Ma'rifat', meaning the Fragrance of Recognition. In this program, we will discuss various topics related to the recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), Insha'Allah.

title: Jo Ahle Bait (a.s.) par zulm karne waalon ke Kafir hone par shak karey
excerpt: This lecture discusses the theological stance regarding those who oppressed the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Citing Sheikh Saduq and Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker emphasizes that doubting the disbelief of the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt constitutes disbelief itself. The talk further explores the spiritual consequences of waging war against Imam Ali (a.s.), equating it to waging war against the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Allah.
content:
Sheikh Saduq narrates from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that, 'Man shakka fi kufri a'da'ina wa-z-zalimina lana fahuwa kafir'. Now listen to the translation. Whoever doubted—we are talking about doubt, not certainty—whoever doubted the disbelief (kufr) of our enemies. That whether our enemies are disbelievers or not, if there is hesitation in that. Who are our enemies? 'Wa-z-zalimina lana' (and those who oppressed us), if he has doubts about them. He is in doubt whether they are disbelievers or not. So if someone has doubt, 'fahuwa kafir' (then the one who doubts is himself a disbeliever). 'Wa'tiqaduna'—now listen here, see what Sheikh Saduq says, it is powerful. 'Wa'tiqaduna fi man qatala 'Aliyan 'alayhis-salam kaqawli-n-nabi sallallahu 'alayhi wa-alihi'—our belief regarding the one who fought Ali (a.s.), the one who came to fight Ali, whoever comes against Ali. Scholars state in the principles of jurisprudence, the rule of 'tahqiq al-manat', meaning whoever fits that, as it is translated in English, 'Whoever fits that'. Now whoever comes against Ali, our belief, Sheikh Saduq says, our belief regarding him is the same as the saying of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). What is the Prophet's statement? That the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Man qatala 'Aliyan faqad qatalani' (Whoever came to fight Ali has fought me). He fought me. 'Wa qawluhu man haraba 'Aliyan faqad harabani' (And his saying: whoever waged war against Ali has waged war against me), and whoever waged war against me has waged war against Allah the Almighty. Whoever fights Ali has fought the Prophet, and whoever fought the Prophet has fought Allah.
Doubting the disbelief of the enemies of Ahl al-Bayt is considered an act of disbelief.

title: Rizq Mein Izaafa Kaise Karein? | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common human concern regarding the expansion and blessing of sustenance (Rizq). The speaker emphasizes that while many seek prayers for financial increase, the primary obstacle to abundance is one's own sinful behavior. By citing Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), the talk highlights the direct correlation between abstaining from sins and the expansion of one's provisions.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali of Allah. In our society, the issue that worries people the most, the subject for which the most prayers are made, and the matter for which people request and ask others to pray for them, is the issue of sustenance (Rizq). Everyone wants their sustenance to be blessed, increased, and expanded. But most of us do not realize that the biggest obstacle to the expansion of sustenance is we ourselves. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) states: 'Innal abda layuznibu al-dhanb fayuzwa 'anhu al-rizq' (When a servant commits a sin, his sustenance is restricted for him). 'Yuzwa' comes from 'zawiya', which means to contract, to tighten, or to reduce. Its opposite is to increase or expand. Therefore, if we want an increase and blessings in our sustenance, and we ask others to pray for us that Allah increases our sustenance, then we must abstain from sins. The more a servant abstains from sins... The more a servant abstains from sins, the more Allah will increase his sustenance. Salutations upon Muhammad and his progeny.

title: Logon Ko Kaunsi 3 Baaton Ka Hukm Diya Gaya Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #YouTubeShorts  #muharram
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses three fundamental obligations regarding the Ahlulbayt as narrated by Imam Sadiq (a.s.) through Sulaym ibn Qays. The lecture emphasizes that true faith requires not just rituals, but the recognition, submission, and reliance on the Imam of the time. Failing to adhere to these conditions, even while performing prayers and fasting, is described as a state of misguidance.
content:
Sulaym ibn Qays says that I heard from Imam Sadiq (a.s.): 'People have been commanded to recognize us.' People have been commanded; recognition is mandatory. If one does not recognize the Imam of their time, they will die the death of disbelief, hypocrisy, and misguidance. He has commanded, and this recognition is sufficient—no, it is mandatory to refer to us in every matter and to submit completely before us. These are the three conditions: the first is recognition, the second is referring to them (i.e., taking all knowledge from them), and the third is submitting before them. If someone does not do these three things, the Imam says: 'Even if he fasts, prays, and testifies to the oneness of Allah, but in his mind, he thinks that he does not need to refer to us, he will not be a Muslim; he will be a polytheist.'

One must refer to the Ahlulbayt for knowledge and guidance in all matters.

Rituals like prayer and fasting are insufficient without acknowledging the Imam's authority.
Rejecting the need for the Imam's guidance is equated to polytheism.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#05 - Kya Kitaab e Sulaim Ibn Qais Ghair Mo'tabar Hai? Part 1/2
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common objection that the book 'Kitab-e-Sulaym ibn Qays' is fabricated and unreliable. The speakers argue for the book's authenticity by highlighting its historical validation by the Imams (a.s.) and its recognition by prominent Shia scholars like Allama Hilli. The discussion emphasizes that the book serves as a vital record of the oppression faced by the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and remains a foundational source for Shia historical tradition.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali of Allah. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We are here with another episode of our series responding to objections against the tragedy of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). So far in this series, we have seen how it is proven even from the books of the opposition that the door of Janabe Zahra's (s.a.) house was set on fire. As far as the Shias are concerned, people believe that the biggest evidence for this event is the book 'Kitab-e-Sulaym' by Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali. However, the opponents label this book as fabricated. The objection being presented in today's episode is that 'Kitab-e-Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali is a false book and cannot be relied upon.' To answer this objection, our brother Abbas Bhai is with us today. Assalamu Alaikum, Abbas Bhai. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. As we saw, today's objection is regarding the book of Sulaym. So, would it be correct to say that this is the book in which the oppression inflicted upon the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) has been recorded? Yes, certainly, Akhil Bhai. The facts stated in this book prove to be a bone in the throat for the enemies, so perhaps that is why the opponents thought it better to label the entire book as fabricated rather than facing the facts. So, can you tell us something about Sulaym ibn Qays? He holds a high status because when he met the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (a.s.), he had his entire book with him. He presented it before him, and the Imam (a.s.) confirmed it. The Imam said, 'O Sulaym, this is your book,' and prayed for him. This is also pointed out by Allama Hilli and other scholars. Regarding him, the truth is what Allama Hilli and other scholars have said: that he is a reliable narrator. He is counted among the companions of the Imams. Anyone for whom the Imams have prayed is not considered weak. As far as the book is concerned, in today's discussion, we will examine the book itself. Before you mentioned that the book was present during the time of the Imams, how do we know that? To know the answer, we are discussing the book known as 'Asl', which is the record of what he heard from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Because of the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), there was a danger to our records. They know under what circumstances this book was written. During the Umayyad era, there was a ban on narrating the oppression. If someone was writing a book, it was a great risk. When the governor found out that someone possessed a book containing the details of what happened after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he intended to kill him. But he escaped and met an Imam. The details are present, but that is a separate discussion. We will try to cover that in the next episode. After listening to the book for three nights in the presence of the Imam, he confirmed it. After listening to the subscribers until late at night, the accused is becoming Rahmatullah. So, what you have mentioned here, the translation would be that it was said regarding this that Imam (a.s.) said that he spoke the truth, may Allah's mercy be upon him. And not only this, we also said that all these hadiths in this book, we recognize all these hadiths. So, this means that if anyone doubted this book, they doubted Imam Sajjad (a.s.), because firstly, this is authentic, and secondly, this narration is not just present in this book, but actually in other books as well. So, as far as it reached, this was about this book. Now let us move to the second point. For example, in the books of... in the books of Tafsir, Sheikh Saduq, Al-Ayyashi, and others, and in the books of Allamah Majlisi, these narrations are present. As far as these narrations are concerned, the Shia scholars have included these narrations in their books. And it is said that as far as the authenticity is concerned, this book is famous in the books of Tafsir and in our books. And in Delhi and Faizabad, this book was mentioned. As a summary, the view of the scholars of the school of thought is before you, and you can decide for yourself about this book. This book is a collection of all the issues of the religion and is from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and from the Imams (a.s.). It is from those who are the true followers of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). In this book, they have mentioned the things that the Shias deserve. Those who study this should definitely ponder over these points, and especially on those... And especially on those who have put their seal of approval on the authenticity of this book. Regarding the objection that this book is [not authentic], and there are so many proofs of its authenticity as you have just presented, despite all these arguments, if anyone still has questions in their mind, they can contact us via our WhatsApp number or through our social media, and they can send their questions to us. We will try to answer these questions, Insha'Allah. We will present the second aspect of the answer to this objection in the next episode, Insha'Allah. With this, viewers, allow us to take leave. Dua, Khuda Hafiz, Ya Ali Madad. [Music]
