title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 9 | Duties of Shias during Ghaibat (Occultation) - Part 1
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological significance of Imamate and the essential duties of Shias during the period of the Major Occultation. It emphasizes that the Imam is a divine authority whose status transcends human comprehension, serving as the essential intermediary for spiritual guidance and sustenance. The session highlights the necessity of recognizing the Imam's loneliness, practicing gratitude, and maintaining steadfastness in faith as a means to prepare for the promised reappearance of Imam Mahdi.
content:
There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Lord of Majesty and Honor, and I repent to Him. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside in Your earth in obedience, and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, hasten the reappearance of Your Wali, and make us among his helpers, supporters, followers, and servants. And grant us success in what You love and are pleased with. And do not leave us to ourselves for even a blink of an eye, ever. And do not replace us with others. By the right of Muhammad and his pure family. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance and curse all their enemies. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. It is the immense favor of the Lord of the Worlds, and the grace of His Proof, that through this unique program, the Mahdavi Webinar, very authentic and beneficial discussions have taken place so far on the belief of Mahdaviyat in the light of the Holy Quran and Hadith. It is hoped that you all liked this webinar, its title, and the discussions that have taken place here so far. Our past videos are available on 'The Strong Rope' YouTube channel, which you can watch and share with your friends, loved ones, and relatives. So that wherever Urdu-Hindi language is spoken and understood in the world, all those people can benefit from it. If I present a summary of the discussion on the Major Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Kubra) and Taqlid that took place yesterday, it is something like this: that in the occultation, our duty is to refer to those scholars who know the lawful and unlawful of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and have a keen insight into their hadiths. The concept of Taqlid and its foundation was laid in the time of other Imams (a.s.). Then we saw that every human being among us is 'mukallaf', meaning responsible for their deeds. But no one has any direct contact or means to the Proof of Allah, Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). And that is why there are three ways to act upon the Sharia. The first is that a person should acquire religious knowledge himself, and that too deep knowledge, which is used in the Holy Quran as 'tafaqquh fid-din' and the same word is used in the narrations, 'tafaqquh fid-din', acquire deep knowledge and become a Mujtahid himself, so that he does not have to follow anyone else. The second is that one should research the fatwas of all the scholars and Maraje who have passed from Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) until today and act according to the strictest and most difficult issue. The third is that whoever cannot act upon these first two methods, then reason demands that just as a person refers to experts in his worldly matters, similarly in religious affairs, one should refer to scholars and Maraje who explain the solutions to problems in the light of the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and follow them. Taqlid itself is not obligatory, and if a person does not do Taqlid, he will be accountable on the Day of Judgment for all his deeds as to what was the basis of the way he acted upon the Sharia in his life. Lastly, the Maulana who joined us yesterday clarified that if someone does not follow Taqlid, it does not mean they have gone outside the fold of religion, Sharia, or Shi'ism. Their respect is as obligatory as that of any other Momin. Now, let us move toward today's topic. After a brief overview of Ghaybat-e-Sughra, Ghaybat-e-Kubra, and Taqlid, our topic for today and tomorrow, InshaAllah, will be the responsibilities of the Shia during the Ghaybat. For further discussion on this, we have with us again today the respected Dr. Shabib Rizvi. Assalamu Alaikum, Sir. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I hope you are doing well, Sir. Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah. Viewers, once again, I request that any questions you have regarding the discussion and the topic can be sent to our TSR (The Strong Rope) WhatsApp number. However, as I mentioned yesterday, please keep in mind that questions should be related to the topic and the discussion. Secondly, it is important that these questions do not concern any specific personality, because if such questions reach us, we apologize that we will not be able to include them in this webinar. Bar Muhammad wa Aali-e-Muhammad Salawat. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum wal'an Aada-ahum Ajma'in. A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alimi min ash-shaytani ar-rajim. Bismillahi ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim. Allahumma la awwala zalimin zalama haqqa Muhammadiw wa Aali Muhammadin 'alayhimus-salam wa akhira tabi'in lahu 'ala dhalika Allahumma al'anhum jami'an. Bismillahi ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim. Allahumma aslih 'abdaka wa khalifataka bima aslahta bihi anbiya'aka wa rusulaka wahuffahu bimala'ikatika wa ayyidhu biruhi al-qudusi min 'indika waslukhu min bayni yadayhi wa min khalfihi rasadan yahfazunahu min kulli su'in wa abdilhu min ba'di khawfihi amnan ya'buduka la yushriku bika shay'an wa la taj'al li-ahadin min khalqika 'ala waliyyika sultanan wa'dhan lahu fi jihadi 'aduwwika wa 'aduwwihi waj'alni min ansarihi innaka 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. Amma ba'du, faqad qila li-Amiril Mu'minina 'alayhis-salam wa man ibnu khiratil ima'? Faqala 'alayhis-salam: Dhakal faqidu at-taridu ash-sharidu M-H-M-D ibnu al-Hasani ibni 'Aliyyi ibni Muhammadi ibni 'Aliyyi ibni Musa ibni Ja'fari ibni Muhammadi ibni 'Aliyyi ibni al-Husayni hadha, wa wada'a yadahu 'ala ra'si al-Husayni 'alayhis-salam. The Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), was asked, 'Who is the son of the best of the bondmaids (Ibn-e-Khairatil Ima) that you are mentioning?' How did the Mawla introduce the Imam of the Time? He said (a.s.), 'That is the Faqid (the one who is missing/absent), the Tarid (the one who will come to people's doors, but they will shut the door in his face and not give him refuge), the Sharid (the one who has no one in the world and wanders here and there, a stranger, poor), Muhammad, the son of Hasan, the son of Hasan al-Askari.' And then the Mawla gave the entire lineage, up to 'Ibnul Husayn hadha' (this son of Husayn). And he placed his hand on the head of Imam Husayn (a.s.), indicating he would be from his progeny. See, before moving forward, understand that this itself is a miracle—that the Master of the Universe is tracing the lineage through so many generations. This is a miracle in itself. Otherwise, you know that a person cannot even tell about the next generation... One cannot predict if a child will be born, if it will be a boy or a girl. Here, not just the next generation, but nine generations later, the Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), is naming each one and saying he will be his son. And then the three attributes he mentioned: Faqid, Tarid, and Sharid—the Mawla will be missing. So, before we discuss the responsibilities of the Imam, let us first recognize the personality of the Imam in this regard, so that we may try to reduce the Imam's loneliness (Ghurba) as much as we can. Let us first understand what 'Gharib' (stranger/lonely) means for the Imam. The first concept of 'Ghurba' is that the Imam is 'Majhul al-Qadr' (unrecognized in his worth), just like the other Imams. Every Imam in his time was Majhul al-Qadr, whose worth people did not recognize. And in reality, this is not just about the Imam, but about failing to recognize the worth of Allah Himself. In the Holy Quran, Surah Al-An'am, it is stated: 'Wama qadarullaha haqqa qadrih.' They did not value Allah as He should have been valued, when they said, 'Ma anzalallahu 'ala basharim min shay' (Allah has not revealed anything to any human being). No prophet came, no revelation came. When they did not value the Prophet, the Hujjat of Allah, they essentially did not value Allah. Because this Prophet, or the Prophet's successor, is actually Allah's representative. So, if one does not value that representative, the Hujjat of Allah, then in reality, they have not valued Allah. This is Surah Al-An'am, verse 91. See how Allah begins the verse by saying they did not value Allah. Then He says, 'They said Allah has not revealed anything to any human.' So, the other Imams were also Majhul al-Qadr; people did not value them. The Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) himself was Majhul al-Qadr. Years before the Battle of Nahrawan, when the Mawla gave a prophecy... About a man who was outwardly a Momin, praying Namaz-e-Shab, reciting the Quran, and the Mawla and Janab-e-Kumayl were returning from the mosque. The Mawla said, 'He is among the people of Hell.' Kumayl objected, 'Mawla, he is one of ours, he is a Shia, a follower of yours.' He said, 'No, no, he is among the people of Hell.' And the Mawla fell silent. When, in the Battle of Nahrawan, the Mawla was surveying those who had been killed and sent to Hell, he saw a head. The Mawla looked at that head with his sword and called, 'Kumayl, come here. Do you recognize this? This is the same one who was reciting the Quran at night, the one you were talking about. Today he has come to fight against us. He is finished, sent to Hell.' At that moment, Kumayl fell at the feet of the Master of the Universe. And the phrase from the Hadith is, 'Wa salla 'ala Majhul al-Qadr.' And he saluted the Mawla and sent Salawat upon him with the title 'Majhul al-Qadr' (the one whose worth is not recognized). 'Assalamu 'alayka ya Majhul al-Qadr.' And after that, you are familiar with history, how people did not value each Imam, one after another. They did not value the Imam. Until the chain of Imamate reached the final link, Hujjat ibn al-Hasan al-Askari, our Imam, Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf), and he too had to go into Ghaybat. Two Ghaybats occurred, as you have heard in previous speeches: Ghaybat-e-Sughra and Ghaybat-e-Kubra. So, this era of Ghaybat is a time of loneliness for the Imam. 'Ghurba' means one who has no one; he is called 'Gharib', 'Gharibul Watan' (a stranger in his own land). Even while living among his own, if his own do not recognize him. Therefore, today I will try to clarify this topic more so that this concept becomes clear: that the Imam is Majhul al-Qadr in three aspects. First, in terms of Imamate; second, in terms of Wilayat (Mastership); and third, in terms of Ismah (Infallibility) and other perfections. Imamate, Wilayat, and Ismah—the infallibility and other perfections like 'Taj al-Arz' (the crown of the earth) and other virtues. If we try to understand just the Imamate—why? I have already mentioned the reason. Today, the general concept of Imamate is that anyone can become an Imam. Some people have even written in their books that if someone reaches a certain intellectual level, they can become an Imam. No, no. Imamate is not a worldly position that one can achieve through effort. Therefore, let us study this narration from Al-Kafi, Usul al-Kafi. If you want to know the importance of Usul al-Kafi, read the book by Ayatollah al-Uzma Khoei, Sayyid Abul Qasim al-Khoei. 'Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith' is his book; it is an encyclopedia on Rijal-e-Hadith. It is in about 28 volumes. In the introduction, he writes that his teacher, Mirza-e-Naini—who is Mirza-e-Naini? Mirza-e-Naini is not the name of an ordinary scholar. In the time of Ayatollah Khoei, all the Maraje had bowed their heads in respect before Mirza-e-Naini; they had learned from him. A very great personality, who also had the honor of meeting Imam-e-Zamana. So, Ayatollah Khoei writes that his teacher, Mirza-e-Naini, used to say that whoever debates the authenticity of Usul al-Kafi is helpless. This is his statement. Regardless, it is not a saying of the Masoom to be accepted blindly, but it is the statement of such a great scholar. Mirza-e-Naini is no ordinary personality. So, this is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, Kitab al-Hujjah. In Kitab al-Hujjah, page 198, there is a chapter: 'Bab al-Nazirun Jami'un fi Fazl al-Imam wa Sifatihi.' This is a rare and comprehensive chapter about the excellence of the Imam and his attributes. The first hadith is in it. The narrator says, the narrator's name is Abdul Aziz ibn Muslim. He says that we were with Imam Ridha (a.s.) in Marv, that is, in Khorasan. We were gathered with our companions, 'wa ijtama'na fil jami' yawm-e-jumu'ah'. It was a Friday, we were all in the Jame Mosque, and when—meaning we had just arrived—Imam Ridha (a.s.) had come to Khorasan. And a conversation broke out regarding Imamate. And people talked among themselves that there are many differences regarding Imamate. There are many views among the people. Look, there are many views among the people, because every person thinks about Imamate according to their own understanding. Why are they bringing up this topic? Because if people just understand this hadith—meaning if they understand this hadith well—then it would be clear to them who the Imam-e-Zamana is. Who is the Imam-e-Zamana? Now, here, when the narrator says that there was a lot of discussion among the people. In it, and then people said there are many differences, there are many differences regarding what the concept of Imamate is, what it is not. 'Fadkhalatu 'ala sayyidi 'alayhis-salam'. I went into the presence of my Sayyid and Master, meaning Imam Ridha (a.s.), and I told him how people were debating this and presenting their own opinions. 'Fatabassama 'alayhis-salam'. The Imam began to smile. Now, what kind of smile is this? It should be clear to you that it is exactly like, for example, when a small child who knows nothing stands before a great scholar and starts presenting his opinion on a subject to that scholar—a very great scholar, for instance, a Marja—if a small child who is completely ignorant and knows nothing starts telling the Marja, 'My opinion on this matter is this,' then if that Marja is smiling, you can understand the reason for his smile, you can understand why he is smiling. It is exactly in this way that the Imam is smiling. 'Fatabassama 'alayhis-salam'. 'Summa qala', after that the Imam said, 'Ya 'Abdal 'Aziz', O Abdul Aziz, this nation, meaning this millat—actually, not millat, the word millat would be wrong, millat means religion. And this nation, these people, these individuals, this Ummah, is ignorant regarding Imamate, and they have been deceived based on their own opinions. They started giving their own opinions. Allah Azza wa Jall did not take the soul of His Prophet until He brought the religion to the stage of perfection and did not reveal such a Quran in which there is an explanation of everything. Pay attention to the Imam's sentence. He did not reveal such a Quran in which there is an explanation, meaning an exposition of everything. I would ask the Imam with folded hands and respect, 'Mawla, you are saying He did not reveal such a Quran in which there is an explanation of everything? We read this Quran, and we see that the mention of Fajr prayer is not in it—that it is two rak'ats—the mention of Dhuhr prayer is not in it—that it is four rak'ats—other details are not in it, it is not about fundamental things, and you are saying there is an explanation and exposition of everything?' The answer will come immediately: 'You are ignorant, that is why you are asking such questions.' I said, He did not reveal such a Quran, meaning you are only looking at the Quran-e-Samit (the silent Quran). If you only look at the Quran-e-Samit, you will be deceived. Whenever you look at the Quran-e-Samit, look at the Quran-e-Natiq (the speaking Quran) alongside it. When you look at the Quran-e-Natiq, then the matter will be understood by you, what the reality is, and the Quran-e-Natiq will tell you what the explanation of this verse is, what the explanation of that verse is. That is why both—did you not read the Prophet's hadith? 'Inni tarikun fikumuth-thaqalayn: Kitaballahi wa 'itrati Ahli Bayti' (I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahlulbayt). 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abadan fa-innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayyal-hawd' (As long as you hold onto both, you will never go astray after me, for they will never separate until they return to me at the Pond [of Kawthar]). So the Quran in which there is an explanation of everything is not just the Quran-e-Samit, but it is alongside the Quran-e-Natiq. 'Bayyana fihil-halala wal-harama wal-hududa wal-ahkam' (He explained in it the lawful, the unlawful, the limits, and the rulings). The Messenger of Allah explained everything in it—lawful, unlawful, limits, rulings, everything, every single thing was explained. 'Wa jami'a ma yahtaju ilayhin-nasu kamalan' (And everything that people were in need of, he explained completely). Not incompletely, not defectively, not deficiently; he explained everything completely. 'Faqala Azza wa Jall', and Allah also announced, 'Ma farratna fil-kitabi min shay'in' (We have not neglected anything in the Book). Everything is present in it. And then after that, the Imam says, and in the Farewell Pilgrimage, which were the last days of the Prophet's life, the Farewell Pilgrimage, in it Allah revealed this verse upon the Messenger of Allah: 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum wa atmamtu 'alaykum ni'mati wa raditu lakumul-islama dina' (This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion). Today, I have perfected your religion for you, and I have completed My blessings upon you, and I am pleased for you that Islam is your religion; I am pleased with it. And the matter of Imamate—now the Imam says, the matter of Imamate, Imamate is that which completes the religion, and the Messenger of Allah did not leave this world—this is all the Imam's statement. The Imam is saying, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not leave this world until the Messenger of Allah had explained for his Ummah, 'Ma'alima dinihim' (the landmarks of their religion), and 'wa awdaha lahum sabilahum' (and clarified for them their path), and pointed out their path to them, and told them the path of truth, that look, if you want to walk on the path of truth, if you want to walk on the path of Haqq, then this is the path; you have to walk from here. There is no other path; do not look here and there, do not look to the right, do not look to the left. 'Aliyun ma'al-haqqi wal-haqqu ma'a 'Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali). 'Wa aqama lahum 'Aliyan 'alayhis-salam 'alaman wa imaman' (And he established Ali (a.s.) for them as a landmark and an Imam). And Ali was made a landmark—meaning 'alam, nowadays in processions, what is it? They call it a flag, but the actual meaning of 'alam in Arabic is a mountain. So that is why they used to call a mountain an 'alam, because in that era, when people wanted to meet each other during a journey, they would say, 'Look, when you reach that mountain, then wait for us there; we will reach there, then we will meet you.' That is why they used to designate a mountain as a sign, and then slowly this 'alam came into this meaning, the meaning of a flag. So he appointed Ali as 'alaman wa imaman, he made Ali an Imam. The Messenger of Allah made it very clear at Ghadir-e-Khumm: 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha 'Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am the Master, this Ali is his Master). Now, is there any doubt for anyone after this? Or the Ummah, whatever issues are going on, the reason for it is only this and no other reason. 'Wa ma taraka lahum shay'an yahtaju ilayhil-ummatu illa bayyanahu' (And he did not leave anything for them that the Ummah was in need of except that he explained it). Now, if anyone imagines—the Imam says—if anyone imagines that Allah did not complete His religion, then he has rejected the Book of Allah. He has rejected the Book of Allah, and whoever has rejected the Book of Allah has gone outside the circle of religion; he has gone outside of Islam. This is the introduction the Imam gave. Now the Imam will talk about the essence of Imamate, what actual Imamate is. 'Hal ya'rifuna qadral-imamti wa mahallaha minal-ummah?' (Do they know the value of Imamate and its position in the Ummah?) Do these people, these Ummah people, even understand the value of Imamate? Do they know the Qadr of Imamate, and does the Ummah know what the status of Imamate is, what its place is, in comparison to the Ummah? What is the position? There is no comparison; it is a false analogy. Now the Imam clarifies. 'Fayajuzu fiha ikhtiyaruhum?' (Is it permissible for them to choose their Imam?) Do they even know Imamate such that it would be permissible for them—meaning allowed for them—to select an Imam for themselves? 'Innal-imamta ajallu qadran wa a'zamu sha'nan wa a'la makana wa amna'u janiban wa ab'adu ghawran' (Imamate is more majestic in value, greater in status, higher in position, more inaccessible in its aspects, and deeper in its depth). What is Imamate? The value of Imamate is more glorious than this, its value is more majestic than this, its status is greater than this, it is bigger than this, its position is higher than this, and its aspects are more lofty, more fortified, and its depth is more profound than this, that people should understand it with their intellects. Imamate is not something that comes into people's intellects. Imamate is a divine position. And this is the very thing the Master of the Universe says in the Sermon of Shaqshaqiya, in Nahjul Balagha, Sermon Number Three, you look at it, in it he says: 'Yanhadiru 'annis-saylu wa la yarqa ilayyat-tayru' (The flood of knowledge was descending from me, and the bird of intellect did not have the reach to reach my reality). The bird of intellect did not have the reach to reach my reality. It could not understand what Imamate is. The Imam says, Imamate is something that people cannot comprehend with their intellects; they cannot comprehend it. 'Aw yanaluha bi-ara'ihim' (Or they can understand it through their opinions). Their opinions. 'My opinion is this, my thought is this.' Sir, keep your opinion and your thought to yourself. Imamate is something that even the great ones could not understand, those who, when individuals like Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad came before the Imam, who were at the tenth, ninth, and eighth levels of faith, they used to sit like this—actually, I said too little—when Gabriel used to come before the Commander of the Faithful, he would sit—the hadith sentence is—'yaq'udu qi'datal-'abd' (he would sit in the sitting posture of a slave), Gabriel would sit before Ali just as a slave sits before his master. Gabriel! And other angels considered Ali their master, their teacher, their instructor. All this is present in the traditions, in the hadiths in detail, but there is no time now, so I will try very quickly to finish my subject. So their intellects cannot reach it, not their opinions. Or that they should select the Imam by their own choice? They can never do that. 'Famin ayna yakhtaru ha'ula'il-juhhal?' (So from where would these ignorant ones choose?) These are the Imam's words, not ours. These 'juhhal', 'juhhal' means the plural of 'jahil'. It is the plural of 'jahil'. These ignorant people, will they select the Imam? 'Innal-imamta hiya manzilatul-anbiya' (Imamate is the position of the Prophets). 'Wa yarithuha al-awsiya' (And the successors inherit it), actually, Imamate, which is the Imamate of the Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), is even superior to the Prophets. And the proof for that has been presented in your service in the previous lecture, that Hazrat Isa (a.s.)—upon our Prophet and his family and upon him be peace—will himself pray behind the Imam-e-Zamana. So this makes it clear: 'Innal-Imamata Khilafatullah' (Indeed, Imamate is the Caliphate of Allah). And before that, 'Manzilat-ul-Ambiya wa yarithuha awsiya' (The status of the Prophets, inherited by the successors). These Imams (a.s.) are the heirs of the successors. They are the heirs of everyone, the inheritors, the successors. What is Imamate? Khilafatullah, the Caliphate of Allah. 'Wa Khilafatur-Rasul sallallahu alayhi wa alihi' (And the Caliphate of the Messenger, peace be upon him and his family). 'Wa maqamu Amir-ul-Mu'minin alayhis-salam' (And the station of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him). Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. Imamate is the Caliphate of the Messenger of Allah and the station of Amir-ul-Mu'minin (a.s.). O Muslim Ummah, what have you done? Did you gather yourselves and select an Imam? Did you even understand what an Imam is? Did you understand the reality of what an Imam is? 'Mirathul-Hasani wal-Husayn alayhimas-salam' (This is the inheritance of Hasan and Husayn, peace be upon them). After that, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) continues that Imamate is 'Zamam-ud-Din' (the reins of the religion). That is, the Imam is the one who controls the religion. The Imam is the one who sets the system for the Muslims, the 'Nizam-ul-Muslimeen'. 'Wa salah-ud-dunya' (And the goodness of the world). The Imam is the cause of the world's excellence, its improvement, and its betterment. I have mentioned this in your service before, that the 15th of Sha'ban is approaching, the night of the 15th of Sha'ban, and a plague has spread across the world, and people are distressed. So, my request to you is, as our Maraji' have also commanded, remember the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Call him 'Ya Sahib-az-Zaman'. 'Ya Waliyyal-Asri adriki' (O Guardian of the Age, reach me). 'Ya Sahib-az-Zamani adriki' (O Master of the Time, reach me). And if everyone does this together, believe me, the effect will be tremendous. Of course, this does not mean that you should not follow the directions given by the government or what the doctors are saying; no, no, follow all of that, but pray alongside it. Make the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.) a means (Waseela) for your prayers. And you will see the effect. Then the Imam says, Imamate is the foundation of Islam. It is the foundation of Islam, the principles of Islam, the root, the growth. 'Wa far'uhus-sami' (And its lofty branches). And the branches of the religion, of Islam, that is Imamate. 'Sami' means lofty. That is, if Islam and its principles and branches—the principles of religion and the fundamentals of religion—need to be elevated, there is no other way except to present oneself at the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And especially today, beg and plead before the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.), pray to him, request him, and refer to his teachings—the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—and see what their teachings are. What are their teachings regarding Tawheed (Monotheism), Adl (Justice), Nubuwwah (Prophethood), Imamate, Ma'ad (Resurrection), and what are their teachings regarding Halal and Haram? Just look. There are supplications (Duas) and Munajat (whispered prayers). These are all the teachings of the family of Muhammad (a.s.). And there is no conflict in them at all. Look, it is a very simple thing. Two men are fighting; one says, 'I am taller, my height is greater,' and the other says, 'No, I am taller, my height is greater.' What is the solution? The solution is very simple: stand them both side-by-side, measure the one who is taller, and it is done, the matter is finished. You have a standard. That is, to measure, you immediately said, 'Look, we have seen, this one is taller,' and the matter is finished. The dispute ends. Provided both are wise and intelligent. Similarly, if you want to see who is with the truth, there is no need for a dispute; just compare the teachings. Compare the teachings of Tawheed, Adl, Nubuwwah, Imamate, Ma'ad, Halal and Haram, Duas, and Munajat; just compare them, and the whole dispute will end right there. You will immediately know. Who is who? Who said what? What was said about whom? Regarding whom did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) make the announcement: 'Ana madinatul-ilmi wa Aliyyun babuha' (I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate)? The Messenger of Allah made the announcement. And what did those who came after the Messenger of Allah say? 'Call Ali, call Ali,' whenever a difficulty arose, 'Call Ali.' Anyway, this is a separate topic; I do not want to go into that. Let me quickly come to my point. So, what is an Imam? The Imam is the one who makes Allah's Halal, Halal; makes Allah's Haram, Haram; fixes Allah's Hudud (penalties/punishments); and protects Allah's religion. And invites people to the path of Allah with what? 'Bil-hikmati wal-maw'izatil-hasanah' (With wisdom and beautiful preaching). Invite people with wisdom and good words, with good advice and admonitions. Not by cutting off heads, and that too while shouting 'Allahu Akbar' while cutting off heads. No, no, not like that; that is not the religion, that is not Islam. That is someone else's Islam, not the Islam of the Ahlulbayt. 'Wal-hujjatil-balighah' (And with the conclusive argument), invite people to the religion. 'Al-Imamu kash-shamsi tali'atun...' (The Imam is the rising sun that illuminates the entire universe with its light). That is what an Imam is, sir. With his knowledge, with his existence. 'Wa hiya fil-ufuqi' (And it is on the horizon). The Imam is that shining sun on the horizon that neither hands can reach nor intellects can grasp. These are the words of Imam al-Rida (a.s.). Neither can people's hands reach him, nor can people's intellects reach him. The Imam is the full moon. The Imam is the shining lamp. The Imam is the radiant light. The Imam is the star that guides people. In the dark, in pitch darkness, when there is darkness all around. If you cannot see any solution, if you cannot see anything, then just call out from your heart, 'Ya Aba Saleh, Ya Mahdi, adriki.' And let me tell you one thing here: whatever your religion may be, whatever your faith may be, whatever your sect or school of thought may be, it does not matter. Whether someone is Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian, or anyone else, if they call out from the heart, 'Ya Sahib-az-Zaman, adriki,' because this is the door that whoever went to, did not return empty-handed. Today, the representative of that door is the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.). Our responsibility during the Occultation is to introduce people, to tell them, 'This is your Imam, this is the Sahib-az-Zaman. This is the Imam of the Time, go to him.' And we ourselves should also call out; it is not that we tell others and do not call out ourselves. No, we should remember the Imam all day long. At the very least, as a minimum, in every prayer, in the Qunut of every prayer, 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-Hujjatibnil-Hasan...' Ayatollah Khoei (r.a.) used to say that for 40 years, as far as I remember, he said, 'As far as I remember, it has been 40 years, I have not abandoned this Dua in any prayer, I have not left this Dua.' 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-Hujjatibnil-Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi...' (the entire Dua). Just this, at the very least. So, remember the Imam in every situation, and it is found in a Hadith, what is the phrase in the Hadith? 'Faharrik shafatayka fa'innal-jawaba ya'tika' (Just move your lips, surely the answer will come to you, surely the answer will come to you). Just move your lips. And tell others too, 'Look, your Imam,' because the Imam of the Time is not just our Imam. Imam Husayn (a.s.) is not just our Imam, the Master of the Universe is not just our Imam. The Master of the Universe, Imam Husayn, Imam Hasan al-Mustafa (a.s.), and all the Imams (a.s.), all of them are the Imams of the entire universe. They are the Imams of everyone. And as I submitted, this is the door from which no one ever goes empty-handed, remember. However, 'bi-shartiha wa shurutiha' (with its conditions and requirements). Those conditions are necessary. And then the Imam says, the Imam is the guide. If someone is lost in the cities, he is the guide. In the desert, in the wilderness, the Imam is the guide. In the oceans, the Imam is the guide. The Imam is the name of that sweet water that quenches the thirst of the thirsty. That is called an Imam. That is, if someone is thirsty for knowledge, go to the door of the Imam. The Imam will give him knowledge. If someone wants guidance, go to the Imam, the Imam will guide him. If someone is being destroyed, ruined, the Imam will guide him, the Imam will save him. He will save him from destruction. For example, nowadays you see, you read in the newspapers, what is happening in India? So many farmers have committed suicide, so many businessmen have committed suicide, people are committing suicide, everyone is committing suicide. Regardless of which religion they belong to—Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Christian, anyone. Why are you committing suicide? This life is not yours. Call upon the Imam of the Time, say—remember this name, it is very simple—'Ya Mahdi,' it is very simple. 'Ya Mahdi, help me. Help me,' just say this much. Ask for his help, he will help you. Trust in the Being of Allah. The Imam continues, because who is the Imam? The Imam is 'Anis-ur-Rafiq' (the companion and friend). He is the friend with whom you can share your confidential matters. 'Wal-walidush-shafeeq' (And the compassionate father). The Imam is that compassionate, kind father to whom you can go in any situation, in any difficulty, in any trouble. A father is compassionate, right? Benevolent, kind, kind father. You go to him and he will do all he can for all your difficulties. 'Wal-akhush-shaqiq' (And the brother by blood). The Imam is like an equal brother. He is like an equal brother with whom you can talk about many things. 'Wal-ummul-barratu bil-waladis-saghir' (And the mother who is kind to her small child). And the Imam is like that mother who loves her infant, loves him immensely, is ready to give her life for her child. Who is the Imam? The Imam is the refuge of the servants. Look, it did not say for Muslims, it did not say for Shias, but it is a refuge for the servants. The Imam is 'Amin-ullah fi khalqih' (Allah's trustee over His creation), over everyone. The Imam is Allah's proof over all servants. He is Allah's Caliph over His cities. The Imam is the one who invites towards Allah and the one who protects the sanctuaries of Allah. The Imam is the protector. Wherever there is talk of a sanctuary, the Imam will protect it. The Imam is infallible, pure and clean from sins. There is no passage for sin in him, nor any passage for any defect. The Imam is the one who is the fountain of knowledge, 'makhsus bil-ilm' (specialized in knowledge). And the Imam is 'al-mausumu bil-hilm' (marked by forbearance). Look, actually, every single word, every single phrase, requires a lot of discussion. But because it is not our topic, I am only telling you this so that you know the reality of Imamate, and a lot of time has passed. The Imam is 'Nizam-ud-Din' (the system of religion). That is, if someone does not follow Imamate, the religion will be in disarray. And that is what we have seen; this is what has happened in history. This is what has happened in history. 'Wa izzul-muslimeen' (And the honor of the Muslims). The Imam is the cause of the honor of the Muslims. 'Wa gaizul-munafiqin' (And the rage of the hypocrites). And the hypocrites, upon seeing the Imam, because of the Imam, because of the Imam, the hypocrites, who are the 'Munafiqin', become angry. Or another meaning could be that the Imam's wrath will be upon the hypocrites. The Imam will be wrathful towards the hypocrites (munafiqeen). The Imam's wrath, the anger that the Imam will display, will be directed at the hypocrites. 'Wa bawaru al-kafirin' (and the destruction of the disbelievers) — the Imam is the one who destroys the disbelievers. This is the Imam. This is who the Imam is. Have we understood the Imam in this way? Have we attained the recognition (marifat) of the Imam in this manner? Have we recognized the Imam as described in this tradition? This tradition is very long; I have presented only a brief summary to you, otherwise, this hadith is much longer. I have also given you the reference: Al-Kafi, Volume 1, Page 190. List number one. You can refer to it. The second meaning of the Imam's 'ghurbat' (strangeness/isolation) is that the Imam is the 'Wali-un-Nima' (the Guardian of Blessings). That is, the 'Ayn-as-sabab-ul-muttasil-bayn-al-ard-wa-s-sama' (the connection between the earth and the heavens) that you recite in the Dua-e-Nudba. Where is it? That being who is the connection between the heavens and the earth. Meaning, the blessings that descend, descend through the Imam. He is the 'Mumkin-e-Ashraf' (the noblest of possibilities). Among all the noble beings, he is the noblest of all creatures (Ashraf-ul-Makhluqat). The noblest creature of Allah. Through him, blessings reach us. Everything we possess, even the blessing of existence, is because of the Imam. How many times a day do we thank the Imam? How many times do we say, 'Ya Sahib-az-Zaman, O Imam-e-Zaman, thank you for protecting us'? Thank you, because of you we are safe and sound. Thank you, thank you that, Masha'Allah, our children are healthy. Thank you, everything we have is because of you. We are safe from diseases and ailments, Alhamdulillah. You have kept many troubles away from us, Ya Sahib-az-Zaman. Do we teach this to our children? Do we tell our children? This is our duty. To thank the Wali-un-Nima. That being, that entity through whom everything has reached us. Do we ever teach our children? Say thank you to your Imam. Today we sat and ate food, Alhamdulillah. Now, some people here say that one should thank Allah. Obviously, one must thank Allah. But that same Allah has taught us that we should thank the one through whom we receive things. Otherwise, when Allah sent Jibra'il with the revelation, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should have said, 'Brother Jibra'il, go back. If I receive revelation, I will take it directly from Allah and thank Him alone.' No, brother, you go back. But no, Allah's way is to send things through means and intermediaries, and to receive things through means. That is why He has appointed angels who write down our deeds, right? Otherwise, what is the need? Does Allah have a need? Allah does not need anything. Even Allah did not need the Prophets. Allah could have sent revelation directly to every human's heart; it would have been done, and the matter would have ended. But Allah selected this means so that it becomes clear to everyone that it is through this means. That is why it is found in a tradition; the narrator says that I heard from the eighth Imam, Shams-ul-Aimma Hazrat Imam Reza (a.s.), that he said: 'Man lam yashkur al-mun'im min al-makhluqin, lam yashkur Allah azza wa jall' (Whoever does not thank the benefactor among the creatures, has not thanked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic). But in reality, this is a matter of religion, and in matters of religion, we often show some defect or keep saying something, 'This is not right, that is not right.' Otherwise, for our worldly purposes, if we go to even a minor peon or clerk to get our work done, and they do it, we thank them too. But here, the being through whom we received everything, we are not thanking him. That being whom Allah has appointed—this is the position of Imamate. 'Bi yumnihi ruziqal wara' (By his blessing, the creatures are provided with sustenance). Through his blessings. 'Wa bi wujudihi' (And by his existence), and because of his sacred existence, his holy existence, 'sabatal ardu wa-s-sama' (the earth and the heavens remain established). If he were not there, the whole world would be annihilated. 'Law la al-hujjat la-sakhat al-ardu bi ahliha' (If the Proof of God were not there, the world would be annihilated, it would be). No one would survive. Let us stop the discussion here today. Insha'Allah, we will continue this discussion tomorrow, if Allah grants the ability. 'Wa ma tawfiqi illa billah' (And my success is only by Allah). Insha'Allah-o-Ta'ala, if Allah grants the ability, we will continue it. 'Haza wa salla-llahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi-t-tayyibina-t-tahirin al-ma'sumin al-mazlumin, wa la'natu-llahi da'iman ala a'da'ihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri fada'ilihim wa manaqibihim wa mukhalifi aqwalihim wa ahkamihim wa ma'arifihim.' Now, if there are any questions, I am present. Thank you very much, sir. There are questions. Let us take the first question. Actually, we have some questions that the Momineen asked in previous sessions, but since they were not related to the topic at that time, we did not reject those questions; we kept them saved. So, among them, a few questions for you, sir. The first question is: 'What are the greater signs of zuhoor of Imam Mahdi (a.s.)?' There are many signs, such as the uprising of the Sufyani, the cry from the heavens, and the sinking of the earth (khasf al-bayda); all these traditions exist. But what our Infallible Imams (a.s.) have commanded us is not to wait for the signs. They have told us to wait for the Imam. 'Tawaqqa amra sahibika laylaka wa naharaka' (Wait for the affair of your Master day and night). 'Intaziru al-faraj wa la tay'asu min rahmati-llah' (Wait for the relief/reappearance and do not despair of Allah's mercy). Whatever the signs are, whether they are definite (hatmi) or non-definite (ghayr-hatmi), remember this: 'Bada' (a change in Allah's decree) can occur in all of them. 'Bada' can occur in every one of them. Because our belief is that Allah's hands are not tied. It is not 'Yadullahi maghlula' (Allah's hand is tied). Allah's hands are not tied. Allah can change any sign at any time. Remember, no sign is a promise from Allah. Remember this point, this sentence. The promise of Allah is Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). The reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman is the promise. 'As-salamu ala al-Mahdi alladhi wa'ada-llahu bihi al-umam' (Peace be upon the Mahdi whom Allah promised to the nations). That promise of the Mahdi. And after that, the promise is that 'Yamla'u-llahu bihi al-arda qistan wa 'adlan ba'da ma muli'at zulman wa jawra' (Allah will fill the earth with justice and equity through him, just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny). Allah will uproot and throw away oppression and tyranny. That is, through Imam-e-Zaman, yes, but 'Alladhi wa'ada-llahu bihi al-umam'. And the promise is that 'Ay yajma'a bihi al-kalim' (That He will unite the word through him). And that all creatures will be gathered through him. Everyone will gather under his banner. Everyone will be one Ummah. 'Wa yalummu bihi ash-sha'ath wa yamla'u al-arda bi haqq' (And He will gather the scattered ones through him and fill the earth with truth). Yes. Thank you, sir. The second question is that the Imam will reappear when there are 313 sincere Shias. The Sunni brothers say that there are not 313 true Shias among the Shias yet, so what should be the answer to this? Look, what the Sunni brothers say, well, let them take care of their own thoughts and solve their own problems first. And then the answer to this is that this talk of 313 refers to very special companions. Their specific names have also been given. Very special. And we know this, as this discussion will come up in tomorrow's talk, that remaining steadfast on the religion in the era of occultation is very difficult. It is very hard. Very difficult. And that is why we have many traditions. For example, there is a tradition in Tuhaf al-Uqul that remaining steadfast on the true religion is very difficult. In this, when most people reach a certain height, the Imam says, 'Imma yasful wa imma yarfau yarfau' (Either they fall down or they rise higher). And then after reaching that height, either they fall or they go to a higher level, and then the Imam says a sentence: 'Wa aksaruhum yasful' (And most of them fall down). They fall down because it is very hard. It is a severe test. The tradition says, 'Tugharbaluna, summa tugharbaluna, summa tugharbaluna' (You will be sifted, then you will be sifted, then you will be sifted). You will be tested, you will be tested, you will be tested. So these 313 are very special; they have never existed in history. Not just now, this is not just about this Imam. The Sunnis who talk about 313 not being there, this is not just about today. Our belief is that after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the entire Ummah became apostate, except for three, except for four; some traditions reach up to 17. There were 500,000 Muslims at that time. 500,000 Muslims, only 17 were those who remained on faith. Only that many. And similarly, Sheikh Mufid (r.a.) wrote a book. The name of the book is 'Al-Ikhtisas'. 'Ikhtisas' is Sheikh Mufid's book. In it, he brings a whole discussion about the 'Hawari' (apostles). 'Hawari' means very close companions of the Imam. Like, for example, these 313, just like that. So, for every Imam, when the discussion of companions, very close confidants, very special companions comes up, then for any Imam, some had four, some had three, some had two; the Imams only had that many companions who remained on the true religion. The majority are those who follow the world, and the Quran has said this, and the Quranic verse exists: 'Wa qalilun min 'ibadi ash-shakur' (And few of My servants are grateful). And my grateful servants are very few, and the Quran has condemned the majority. 'Wa aksaruhum la ya'qilun' (And most of them do not use their intellect). The majority does not use their intellect, the majority does not understand, the majority does not know. The Quran has condemned the majority. The Quran has praised the minority. So, do not go by that. So, they were not with any Imam. Meaning, in that hadith which Sheikh Mufid has narrated from the sixth Imam, that there will be very few individuals in every era—after the Messenger of Allah, they were few. And because this test is severe. Only about Sayyid-ush-Shuhada Imam Hussain (a.s.) is it found that when the call will be made on the Day of Judgment, 'Ayna hawari al-Hussain ibn Ali alayhimussalam?' (Where are the apostles of Hussain ibn Ali?). So the sentence of the hadith is that these 72 who were martyred with him, they will all be raised. The largest number is these 72, that's it. Other than that, there are not more than three or four anywhere. Look at the whole hadith. The number of apostles of the two Imams, Imam Baqir and Imam Sadiq (a.s.), is about six or seven, approximately. Combined, let's say the average is four, not more than that. Therefore, staying on this path is very strict, very difficult. Insha'Allah, we will try to cover this in tomorrow's discussion, if Allah grants the ability. Masha'Allah, sir, and the last question for today because our time is also running out. What is the difference between the position of Imamate given to Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) and that of the Imams (a.s.) in the vicegerency of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? I mean, what is the difference? Look, the difference is that naturally, they were also Imams and divinely appointed. Just like these 12 Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). They were also divinely appointed, and they were also divinely appointed. Allah appointed both. In fact, our argument is that Prophethood, Imamate, Nabuwwat, and Wilayat are all positions that Allah appoints. People have no authority in this. There is a verse in Surah Al-Ahzab: "Wa ma kana li-mu'minin wa la mu'minatin idha qadallahu wa rasuluhu amran ay-yakuna lahumul-khiyaratum min amrihim." When Allah and His Messenger decide on a matter, no believer, whether man or woman, has the right to use their own authority or choice in it. So, this is our argument regarding that. Similarly, the position of Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) was divinely appointed. There is no doubt about it. But if you want to compare, it is our belief that no one is superior to the 12 Imams. The 12 Imams are superior to all the Prophets. Now, if someone feels bad, let them feel bad; if they feel good, let them feel good; that is not the issue. This is a matter of belief; this is our belief. And among the Ulul-Azm (Arch-Prophets) as well, the 12 Imams are superior to the Ulul-Azm Prophets, and the proof is this. Look, what is the proof? It is very simple. The proof is that when Hazrat Isa (a.s.) will arrive—and all Muslims have narrated this tradition, both sects have narrated it in their respective books, even it is present in the Sihah al-Sittah—that when Hazrat Isa comes, when he descends, he will pray under the leadership and Imamate of Imam-e-Zamana, i.e., Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). Well, there is a slight difference in the tradition between us and them. In our tradition, it is that Hazrat Isa himself will say, 'You step forward and lead the prayer.' In theirs, it is that he will say, 'You step forward,' and the other will say, 'No, you step forward.' We do not have such traditions because there are no formalities in religion. There are no formalities in greetings. Therefore, we have a tradition that Hazrat Isa will pray behind, and Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) will be in front, and this is proof of his superiority. Because, is the Imam superior or the follower (Ma'mum) superior? Obviously, reason says—ponder over this—reason says that the Imam is superior, and the follower who is behind is the subordinate. It never happens that an inferior is placed in front and a superior is placed behind. Only foolish people do this. So, our belief is not 'Alhamdulillah-illadhi' (Praise be to Allah) that He has 'Faddalal-mabdhula alal-afdal' (preferred the inferior over the superior). This is not our belief. Our belief is that the Imam who is superior will be in front, and the Prophet who is inferior will be behind, even if he is an Ulul-Azm Prophet. And the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) themselves—this is a very detailed discussion, how their superiority is, what it is. So, in terms of creation, there is a whole discussion which there is neither time for here nor is it appropriate. Yes, thank you, sir. Finally, if the responsibilities—whatever responsibilities you have mentioned, sir—one thing becomes very clear: to fulfill responsibilities, just the realization is enough. If there is a realization that this is our responsibility, and as it came up in the discussion, gratitude to the Benefactor (Mun'im) through whom blessings are received, if there is a realization of who it is through whom we are receiving all blessings, then automatically, Insha'Allah, a person will also realize their responsibilities. We are very grateful, sir, that through your statement, you made us realize how lonely, poor, and oppressed the Imam of our time is. How much we should remember our Imam, but how little we remember him. May God grant us the ability to mention our Imam more and more, Insha'Allah, and grant us the ability to pray abundantly for the reappearance of our Imam. Wa akhiru da'wana anil-hamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin. A'udhu billahis-sami'il-'alimi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-hujjatibnil-hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'i fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyaw-wa hafizaw-wa qa'idaw-wa nasiraw-wa dalilaw-wa 'ayna hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'aw-wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Rabbi salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in.

title: Allah Aur Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.) Ko Sab Se Zyaada Kya Pasand Hai?
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual significance of the Tasbih of Fatima (s.a.) according to the teachings of Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.). It explains that this specific form of worship is the most beloved to Allah and the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker emphasizes that the Prophet's gift of this Tasbih to his daughter, Janabe Zahra (s.a.), serves as definitive proof of its superiority over all other forms of worship.
content:
The fifth Imam, Hazrat Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), says: 'Ma umila Allahu bi shay'in min al-tasbih' (Allah has not been worshipped with anything like the Tasbih). The Tasbih of Fatima (s.a.) is the best way to worship Allah. And the Imam further says: 'Law kana shay'un afdala minhu la-nahalahu Rasulullahi (s.a.w.a.) li-Fatimata (s.a.)' (If there was anything better than this Tasbih, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would have given it to his daughter). The Prophet giving the Tasbih to his daughter is itself proof that the most beloved and precious thing near the Prophet and near Allah is the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.).
Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) states that nothing is better than Tasbih for worshipping Allah.
The Tasbih of Fatima (s.a.) is considered the most precious form of worship.
If a better form of worship existed, the Prophet would have taught it to his daughter.
The Prophet's gift of the Tasbih to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) validates its supreme importance.
The act of Tasbih is deeply connected to the love of Allah and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 2 | Excellence & Importance of The Holy Quran - Part 2
excerpt: This webinar session explores the profound spiritual significance and practical importance of the Holy Quran in the life of a believer. It emphasizes that the Quran serves as a divine guide, a source of healing, and a spiritual companion that must be understood through the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The lecture highlights the necessity of attentive recitation, the power of reflecting on its meanings, and the lifelong obligation to study and teach the Quran for salvation in this life and the hereafter.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. [Recitation of prayers/salutations]. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. I congratulate all of you on this evening. The webinar of the Holy Quran, whose title is 'Teachings of the Quran in the Light of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)', the discussion that started yesterday, the second session of this webinar, you are all welcome. Alhamdulillah, in our first session yesterday, there was a discussion on the virtue and importance of the Holy Quran, in which we saw that the Holy Quran distinguishes between truth and falsehood and states that beyond its language and expression, its subjects and addressees are such that it will remain until the Day of Judgment. The importance of the Holy Quran can only be told by those who are the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Therefore, the Quran can only be understood in the light of the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), not otherwise. And besides this, memorizing, understanding, and reading the Quran... and there is more. As usual, we will start our second session with the recitation of the Holy Quran. For this, our respected Maulana Asad Abbas Khan Sahab is present with us. Salam. Maulana Asad Abbas Khan Sahab is present with us. Assalamu Alaikum, sir. [Greetings]. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I congratulate you very much on this evening. [Greetings]. Thank you very much. And all the viewers... [Greetings]... and may we be saved from all kinds of calamities. We thank the respected organizers who, because of their efforts, have made this webinar possible. There is no doubt that they are a source of guidance for us, and may their character, friends, and work be blessed. [Recitation of Quranic verses in Arabic]. That Salman, Sayyiduna Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) - there is no power... Indeed, Allah the Almighty and Exalted has spoken the truth. As I mentioned in the previous night's program, in this program, after the recitation of the Quran and before the speech, Insha'Allah, a brief Hadith related to the recitation of 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' will be presented for the viewers. The Hadith selected for today regarding the recitation of Bismillah is found in 'Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn', Volume 1, page 216, Hadith number 330. It is narrated that Muhammad ibn Sinan reports that Hazrat Imam Riza (a.s.) said: 'Indeed, Bismillah is closer to the Greatest Name of Allah (Ism-e-A'zam) than the pupil of the eye is to its white.' Indeed, my Mawla Ali ibn Musa al-Riza (a.s.) Indeed, my Mawla Ali ibn Musa al-Riza (a.s.) has spoken the truth. We do not realize the power of this Name. title: EP07 | Bait-e-Tatheer Par Hamle Ki Doosri Dhamki | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical controversy surrounding the threat to burn the house of Lady Fatimah (s.a.) if allegiance was not pledged to the caliphate. The speaker argues that the historical record presents a logical dilemma: either the oath to burn the house was false, or the act was actually carried out. By analyzing the implications of these threats, the lecture asserts the historical reality of the attack on the Prophet's daughter's home.
content:
This leads to only one of two conclusions: either those who issued the threat swore a false oath by God that if allegiance was not pledged, they would burn the house down, or if that oath was not false, then indeed the house of the Prophet's daughter, meaning the house of Fatimah (s.a.), was set on fire. At that time, Ali (a.s.) and Zubair... I swear by God, no one is dearer to me than your noble father, and after him, no one is dearer to me than you. But you will not stop me from setting your house on fire. Many Muslims try to downplay the authenticity of this narration by saying that in reality, the house was not set on fire. But alas, they forget that there is no need to set fire to the house of the Prophet's daughter, the Princess of the Women of Paradise, Lady Fatimah (s.a.). We would just like to say to those people that in this incident, an oath was taken by God that if allegiance was not pledged, the house would be set on fire. And history does not record that those who threatened swore a false oath by God that if allegiance was not pledged, they would burn the house down. And if that oath was not false, then indeed the house of the Prophet's daughter, meaning the house of Fatimah (s.a.)... Indeed, the house of the Prophet's daughter, meaning the house of Fatimah (s.a.), was set on fire.

title: Mazloomiyyat e Ali (a.s.) | Majlis#01 | Maulana Meesam Zaidi Sahab | Majaalis e Azaa e Ali (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture by Maulana Meesam Zaidi explores the profound martyrdom of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the enduring legacy of his suffering. It highlights the Imam's supreme character, exemplified by his mercy toward his assassin, and connects his sacrifice to the broader history of oppression faced by the Ahlulbayt. The discourse emphasizes the spiritual significance of mourning for the Imam and the resilience of the Shia community in upholding the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) despite centuries of hardship.
content:
The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan (divine pleasure). The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. The congregation of the Quran was established there. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. Even then, the heart was restless, waiting for the arrival of the Imam. Waiting for the arrival of the Imam of the believers... Waiting for the arrival of the Imam of the believers. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. The voice was heard, the house was left behind, and the remembrance of the sacrifice was left behind. The house was left behind, the remembrance of the sacrifice was left behind. The entire earnings were lost, the mihrab was stained with the blood of the Quran. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. When he went to prostrate... When he went to prostrate, when he went to prostrate in life, when he went to prostrate in life, he did not return. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. In the eyes of the father, the tears of the daughter were reflecting... The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. It was the last day of the month of fasting, the atmosphere was filled with sorrow. It was the last day of the month of fasting, the atmosphere was filled with sorrow. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. The mosque of Kufa is a witness to the centuries of Rizwan. It was the last day of the month of fasting, the atmosphere was filled with sorrow. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdulillah... [Arabic recitation]... We are gathered here to remember the Mawla, the owner of the ship, Abdul Hassan, Imam Hussain (a.s.). We seek the intercession of the Masumeen (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). May Allah (s.w.t.) bless Muhammad and his progeny. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Ali (a.s.) is the essential truth. This world was created, but if I were to choose a topic for these Majalis... If I were to choose a topic for these Majalis, I would select a verse of the Holy Quran or a Hadith of the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) that addresses the oppression of the oppressed and the downtrodden. Since these Majalis are dedicated to the cause of the oppressed, I deemed it appropriate to present this famous and well-known Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), which highlights the success of the Prophet and his progeny. Despite the hardships, they are successful in this world and the hereafter, while those who oppressed Mawla Ali (a.s.) are failures in this world and the hereafter. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated this when he recited... He recited this verse: [Music] 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds, they are the best of creatures.' People asked the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) who this referred to. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) pointed towards Ali (a.s.) and said, 'This is Ali.' When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had established this status for Mawla Ali (a.s.) in front of everyone, he called Ali (a.s.) close to him, looked towards him so that the people would focus entirely on the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and then towards Ali (a.s.), and said, 'This Ali has achieved success in this world and the hereafter.' He has achieved success in this world and the hereafter. Alhamdulillah, being a follower of Mawla Ali (a.s.) and being a Shia is a matter of pride, not shame. If one reflects, the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) did not belong to any other sect, nor did he follow any other path. The bond between the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.) is so profound that one cannot be a true follower unless the love of Mawla Ali (a.s.) and the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) resides in their heart. To prove this status of Mawla Ali (a.s.), one must look at the history and the teachings... Therefore, on the Day of Judgment, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is present, those who followed Ali (a.s.) will be the successful ones. So, who is the Mawla? It is not difficult to understand. Our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.) are the path. It is not just me; they were and will remain the path. Just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was oppressed, the followers of Ali (a.s.) have also faced oppression and tyranny under various pretexts. They are being oppressed and harassed. It was said that when a tyrant had a boil, a physician suggested that the blood of a Shia should be applied to it to cure it. This is why the Shia community has been targeted. Look at how many were killed in Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and India. Everywhere, oppression and tyranny have been unleashed against them. Oppression and tyranny have been unleashed. If you look at the world, you will see that the Shias do not hold power anywhere. This means we do not have political power; we do not have the majority. We are holding Majalis, we have our faith, and we have our children. Why do they oppress us? Why are they troubled? Despite suffering so much, the Shias are not just in one place but all over the world. If you look from a worldly perspective, they do not seem successful. If Shias ruled the world, it would be said they are successful in this world, but since they are oppressed everywhere, it means... It means that for 1400 years, we have been oppressed, but to this day, those who oppressed us have not been able to break us. They could not turn any of our scholars, our leaders, or even our children away from the path of Ali (a.s.). Even if you ask a child, they will say they are a follower of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.). This shows that despite all the oppression, they have not been able to change our faith. Even those who were troubled had to turn to the Mawla of the Universe (a.s.). They go to the door of Ali (a.s.) when they are in distress. Whether they admit it or not, if someone is a Shia, they are on the path of Ali (a.s.). If you ask them on what basis they say this, I say it because if you study all the books, you will see that people have spent all their energy trying to prove that Mawla Ali (a.s.) was pleased with their leaders. Tell me, if someone is pleased with you, does that make them your follower? They are troubled and try to prove that Ali (a.s.) was pleased with them. But being pleased does not change the reality. One must provide evidence and proof that Mawla Ali (a.s.) came to solve problems and judge cases. But Mawla Ali (a.s.) is not a 'Mushkil Kusha' (problem solver) just to please people. If you ask someone, they will say that if Allah (s.w.t.) is pleased with someone, He gives them power. But did Allah (s.w.t.) give power to Nimrod? Tell me, does giving power to Pharaoh or Nimrod mean that Allah (s.w.t.) is pleased with them? The answer is no. The argument for Him not being the Lord of the Worlds was that if He were, He would not be providing for His enemies and those who do not subscribe to Him. Similarly, in the school of thought, they also solve the difficulties of non-believers. Just ponder, it was only Ali (a.s.) who solved the difficulties of those who tried to seal the door of Ali (a.s.). He would fulfill the needs of his followers, but here, providing water—how to provide water—this is what you can see. How to provide water, this is what you can see. It is visible to you that he provided it. We are saying that he is the one who gives water to his own killer; he is seen doing that. That is, he is seen giving water to his own culprit. So, is the Master of the Universe giving water to his own culprit a proof of his divinity? It is not a proof of divinity, but along with this, I will also emphasize one thing: there are some people who have a soft corner for the Commander of the Faithful, but if they are asked, they say that since Ali (a.s.) gave water to the culprit, if we want to follow him, what should we do? It is a matter of understanding. If he is giving water to his own enemies, then we should also do the same. How should our attitude be towards our enemies? For this, we should not look at the beautiful words online, but for this, you should look at the attitude of Salman (r.a.), the attitude of Abu Dharr (r.a.), the attitude of Miqdad (r.a.), and the attitude of Malik al-Ashtar (r.a.). They were given the status of companions. I believe the greatest injustice done to the Master of the Universe was this, and today, if this issue is explained to people, we... [audio unclear]. Even if you talk about it, do not try to do it properly, but it is done. Many times, it is done in silence, and the sermon is delivered while sitting alone. It is delivered, and the sermon is delivered while sitting alone. There are no listeners present for the Friday prayer, so you should realize this. For that, you must subscribe and explain the injustice done to him. So, in this regard, subscribe and like, and this work is also important. I am just finishing the talk. Now, in the line, one more thing, and the one who strengthens the father, this is the night of the 19th. The one who strengthens the father, this is the night of the 19th. For the betterment of the 19th, he brought a bowl of milk and a little salt before the Iftar. He looked towards his daughter, and said, 'Daughter, a father does not let his killer go hungry.' Therefore, the 14th was removed. Because of being the Master of the Universe, and after Iftar, he is busy in prayers. But this time, he looks towards the sky, looks again, and says, 'Then he comes out, then he goes back in.' I had never seen this before. I had never seen my father in this state, the state of restlessness in which my father was that night. Again and again, my father would take me... Again and again, my father would take me. Why was my father so restless? He is known for his patience. Why was he restless? The Master of the Universe spent the whole night in worship. This was the state of restlessness. He spent the whole night, and after that, when the dawn approached, the Master wanted to leave the house. But when he wanted to leave the house, the duck was also there. She caught the hem of his garment. This animal, in its own language, was saying, 'Do not go out,' and he himself would use the water. I will... He would use the water. I will tell you, the animals are also restless. Whether they remain hungry or not, but in the field of Karbala, the small children of the house of Hussain (a.s.) were thirsty. Just think of that scene of Karbala that we hear about, and we cry; tears flow from our eyes. Just think, the small children must have come to Hussain (a.s.) and said... [audio unclear]. The shrine of Ali (a.s.) is before you, I will explain it in detail. Imam Hassan and Imam Hussain took their father to the alley, but when he was martyred, the voice came, 'O son, return my family, return my friends, for I am being taken away from here today.' The voice came, 'O son, return my family, return my friends, for I am being taken away from here today.' The wives and daughters of the house of the one who watched the spectacle, the family of Ali (a.s.), what hardships they endured! What a state of helplessness it was! A year ago, it happened, and water used to come. It seems as if Ali (a.s.) is lamenting. It seems as if Ali (a.s.) is lamenting. Just listen, the call of the Master, 'Take me, take me far away.' When he was being taken towards the house, we were asking, 'Where are you going?' The companions asked, and the voice was coming from the Master, 'O Jabir, the companion of my grandfather, go far away from my grave, for my sister Zainab is coming with 4,000 women.' I have heard that the creation is crying over the Master, both of them are saying... The creation is crying over the Master, both of them are saying, 'The mother, the son, the earth, and the sky are all mourning.' There is an oath on the 19th, the blood of the Master, the history of the Master, which has not been seen since the Day of Judgment. Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the witness. You do what you have to do on your head, then this wealth... [audio unclear]. Whatever comes out of me, it is the truth. The tongue of the Master is saying, 'Do not cry, have patience, this is the decree of God.' Do not be impatient, have patience. As the moon of Muharram appears, the sorrow of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) begins. Just as the moon is sighted, the mourning begins in the mosques. The sorrow of Ali (a.s.) is seen everywhere. The grief is immense, and the hearts are heavy with the pain of the martyrs. The atmosphere becomes filled with mourning, and the hearts of the believers are restless in the remembrance of the tragedy. The deep color of grief reaches its peak. When the sword was drawn, the head was separated from the body. The tragedy of Karbala is such that even the heavens wept. When Hasan (a.s.) and Hussain (a.s.) went to the mosque, the house was left in silence. The mother (Fatima s.a.) was waiting, and the house was filled with the scent of sorrow. Even the prayer mat was left waiting for them to return. They did not return. The daughter (Zainab s.a.) was waiting with tears in her eyes. The house was filled with the shadow of grief. When the news of the martyrdom reached them, the hearts of the believers were shattered. The tragedy is etched in the history of the believers, and the pain remains in the society.
