title: EP13 | Imam Banane Ka Ikhtiyaar Kisey Hai? | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological and historical debate surrounding the appointment of an Imam, contrasting Sunni and Shia perspectives. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines the necessity of leadership for religious duties while arguing that human selection is inherently flawed due to the inability to discern true character. The discussion highlights historical events like Saqifah and the suppression of virtues of the Ahlul-Bayt to emphasize the Shia doctrine of divine appointment.
content:
Haider Haider... [repeated]... I bear witness that Ali is the Wali of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Before we begin today's episode, let us see who the winners of the third quiz of our 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' series, i.e., from episode number 9 to episode number 12, are. Their names are on your screen. Iffat Lalani from Mahua, Ali Raza Noorani from Bhavnagar, Hasan Raza from New Delhi, Syed Ali Abbas from Thane Mumbra, Qonain Fatima from Srinagar, Musani Mohammad Raza from Bhavnagar, Maryam Zahra Bhandari from Sadat, Syed Anush Hussain from Alipur, Jamshed Ali Jafri from Mumbai, Safa Haider from Alipur, Syed Muskan Zahra from Bengaluru, Liaqat Jafri from Badgaon, Yunaz Hasan from New Delhi, Ibtisam Fatima from Bengaluru. Congratulations to all of you. Now let us move towards our new episode today. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his assistants, and his Shias, and do not make us among his enemies. By the right of Muhammad and his pure family. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. The discussion was about Imamate or Caliphate, meaning who has the authority to select or choose the successor of the Messenger of Allah? Now, there are two different opinions among Muslims here. First, let us see what the view of the Ahl-e-Tasannun is. You see, Mawardi is a very great theologian whose book is 'Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya'. In it, he writes—he is a theologian of the Ahl-e-Tasannun—he writes: 'But the Sharia came with the delegation of affairs to its Wali in religion.' The Sharia came. Meaning, after the Prophet, to whom should the religion be entrusted? To the Wali. And what proof do they bring? They say there is a verse of the Quran: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنكُمْ﴾ 'O you who believe, obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you.' This is verse number 59 of Surah Nisa. Surah Nisa, Surah number 4, verse number 59. 'And it was made obligatory upon us to obey the Ulil Amr among us.' And they are the Imams, the ones who have been appointed as Amirs over us. Now let us see what Qushi says. This is the great Qushi, Imam al-Mutakallimin. What is his title? Imam al-Mutakallimin. Even today, everyone accepts his opinion. Now he says that the Sharia commanded the establishment of Hudud. Qushi says, okay? The Lawgiver (Allah) commanded that the Hudud—Allah's Hudud—be established. Hudud means laws, meaning the specific punishments and laws, they should be established, applied, and implemented. And the borders should be protected. 'Sugur' means the frontier, the border. And armies should be mobilized, armies should be prepared, ready for Jihad. And many, many of the affairs related to the preservation of the system, and many such affairs that are for the system, for the protection of the system. For that, the presence of an Imam is necessary. And the protection of the 'Bayzat al-Islam' (the community of Islam), and the Imam—meaning for the protection of Islam, for advocacy, for its protection—'Mimma la yatimmu illa bil-Imam' (that which cannot be completed except through the Imam). And all these things—meaning the establishment of Hudud, protecting the borders, mobilizing armies, and other things through which Islam is protected—cannot happen unless there is an Imam. Until there is an Imam. Right? 'Wa ma la yatimmul wajib al-mutlaqu illa bihi wa kana maqdooran fahuwa wajib.' Therefore, any action without which a mandatory duty cannot be completed, provided it is within one's capability, is itself mandatory. So, for these things, it is necessary—meaning, what can they not be done without? They cannot be done without an Imam. Therefore, appointing an Imam, making an Imam, is mandatory upon us. It is our duty; it is mandatory upon us to appoint an Imam. Right? So, 'Yajibu an yu'raf anna wilayata amrin-nasi min a'zami wajibati-deen.' Therefore, appointing an Imam, choosing an Imam from among ourselves, is among the greatest obligations of the religion. Rather, 'bal la qiyama illa biha,' rather, the religion cannot be established unless this is done. This is what Hafiz Qushi is saying, who is the Imam of the Mutakallimin (theologians). 'Li-annallaha awjabal amra bil-ma'ruf wa nahya anil-munkar,' because Allah has made 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' (enjoining good) and 'Nahya anil-Munkar' (forbidding evil) mandatory, 'wa la yatimmu zalika illa bi quwwatin wa imaratin,' and this Amr bil-Ma'ruf and Nahya anil-Munkar cannot be fulfilled unless one has power and authority. Having power is necessary. Right? 'Wa kazalika sayiru ma awjabahu minal jihadi wal adli wa iqamatil hajji wal jum'ati wal ayati wa nasril mazlumi wa iqamatil hudud,' and similarly, all other things that He has made mandatory, such as Jihad, establishing justice, performing Hajj, organizing Hajj, organizing Friday prayers, organizing Eid prayers, helping the oppressed, and establishing the Hudud (penal laws)—all these things cannot be established unless a person has strength, authority, and power. Therefore, what is the most important duty of the Muslims? To appoint an Imam for themselves. Right? 'Ilman na sahabata,' that is why the Sahaba did—'Rizwanullahi' (he says, not us), 'alayhim' (that Allah is pleased with them)—'ajma'u ala anna nasbal imame ba'dal fara'izi zamanin-nubuwwati wajibun.' Therefore, after the Prophethood, the Sahaba decided that appointing an Imam is mandatory. 'Bal ja'alu-hu ahammal wajibati,' rather, they considered the appointment of the Imam to be the most important of all obligations. Pay attention to the sentence. He says, 'Haythu ishtaghalu bihi an dafni nabi sallallahu alayhi wa ali.' To the extent that they gave so much importance to appointing the Imam that they abandoned the burial and funeral preparations of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). They left the body of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and went to decide among themselves who would be the Imam, who would become the Caliph, and at whose hands the allegiance (Bay'ah) would be taken. Did you notice? It is absolutely clear. This is in page 19 of 'Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya' by Abu Ya'la, and similarly, 'Al-Imamat al-Uzma'—what is this 'Al-Imamat al-Uzma'? It was a PhD thesis by someone at Umm al-Qura University in Makkah, and it is from page 54 to 58. This matter is explicitly recorded there, and everyone acknowledges it. No one denies it. They left the Prophet's body and went away. Right? Now, after that, the debate began about how... Meaning, what are the conditions? What should be the qualifications of the Imam? So, they start by saying there are seven conditions. 'Adalah' (justice) is one condition; second is knowledge that reaches the level of Ijtihad; third is that his senses—hearing, sight, and speech—all five senses must be perfectly sound; and there are seven such conditions, similar to what we have for an Imam of Jama'ah (congregational prayer). An Imam who leads a prayer must have these, and he must have courage (Shaja'ah). Now, if we look at all these things and analyze them—Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the opportunity, we will analyze their statements too—but it is currently outside our topic to analyze these things. However, Insha'Allah, when we do, you will see that if all these conditions were applied, many people would be disqualified. They neither had the knowledge—they were not even aware of basic Quranic matters, they were unaware of basic rulings—nor did they have courage. Stories of them fleeing from the battlefield were famous. And there are many such things which, Insha'Allah, are currently outside our subject. Let's leave this for now. So, you noticed what their religion is, what their faith is: that they should appoint one themselves. Now, this is a very simple discussion. We will not go into all the details. I will present just one Hadith from a Shia book for your service. This narration is from 'Kamal al-Din,' and the narrator is Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, who himself asked the 12th Imam, Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), this question. He asked, 'Do people have the authority to choose an Imam for themselves?' The Imam asked Sa'd in return, 'Which Imam? One who works for the betterment of the people or one who creates corruption? Meaning, an Imam who builds Islam or one who ruins it?' Sa'd said, 'Certainly, one who brings reform.' Then the Imam asked, 'Fahal yajuzu an takhtaruhum alal mufsid?' (Is it not possible that they selected a man thinking he was right, but later it turned out he was wrong, because no one is familiar with another's thoughts, no one knows?) No one is familiar with another's thoughts. In history, one finds many such people. Like that king of the Banu Umayya who did nothing but fast and read the Quran. As soon as he received the news that 'you have now been made king,' he closed the Quran and said, 'Hadha firaqu bayni wa baynik' (This is the parting between me and you). Now, this is the separation between you and me; we will meet on the Day of Judgment. Meaning, the appearance he was presenting was that of a very pious, religious man. So the Imam said that no one is familiar with or knows another. Sa'd said, 'Yes, that is true.' The Imam said, 'This is the reason.' Then the Imam said, 'Now I will bring you a proof'—the 12th Imam says to Sa'd—'to prove my point. Even though the first thing the Imam said was also intuitive and rational, but now the Imam is bringing a proof.' He says, 'Akhbirni anir-rusul.' Tell me about the Messengers whom Allah chose. Upon whom He revealed books, and helped them with revelation (Wahi) and infallibility (Ismah), and they were the most learned individuals of their Ummah. And Allah had obviously granted them many things. Right? Who were these Prophets? They were the Ulul-Azm (Arch-Prophets) Prophets: Prophet Musa, Prophet Isa (a.s.)—peace be upon our Prophet and his family and them. Their intellect was immense, perfection of intellect, perfection of knowledge. Despite that, when they chose people, selected people, they selected them thinking they were believers, but they turned out to be hypocrites. Thinking they were believers. Then the Imam narrates the story that when the time came to go to Mount Tur, Prophet Musa (a.s.) shortlisted 7,000 from the 70,000 special Israelites he had. From those 7,000, he shortlisted 700. Now think, how difficult it is to shortlist. And while it is Prophet Musa—remember, he is an Ulul-Azm Prophet, a possessor of a Book, a possessor of a Shari'ah, infallible, everything in its place. From 700, he then shortlisted 70. And when he took these 70 with him to Mount Tur, the Quran says they all went there and became apostates. They said, 'Musa, we will not believe in you until you show us God. You have seen God, show Him to us just like that.' This is explicitly mentioned in the Quran. All this is in the light of Quranic verses. The Quran says, 'Wakhtara Musa qawmahu sab'ina rajulan limiqatina.' 'Ikhtara Musa'—Musa selected from his people—'sab'ina rajulan limiqatina.' So we saw that when the Imam says that Musa's selection was such that this problem occurred—that the 70 individuals who were the best in his view, when they reached there, they actually became apostates. And the Quran says that Allah struck them with lightning and they were all destroyed. Then they were brought back to life. Is it clear to you? So when this is the case for the Ulul-Azm, then what can be said for others? And if some people say, 'No, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed so-and-so, appointed so-and-so,' if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had appointed so-and-so, then when there was a dispute at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah, and the language being used was such that, 'If you listen to me, I will cut your neck,' another said, 'You listen to me, I will cut your neck,' another said, 'You listen to me, I will cut your nose,' another said, 'I will do this, I will do that.' There was such a dialogue, so the easiest way in that was, 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed me. I am the next one,' and there is proof for that. But no one presented such proof. And the person for whom the 'Nass' (explicit designation) existed—that person, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)—was busy with the Prophet's Ghusl and Kafan. He was giving Ghusl to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and shrouding the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was performing the funeral preparations of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Tell me, when this Qushi writes that it was so important for the Sahaba that it was among the 'Ahamm al-Wajibati' (most important obligations)—that the Sahaba left the Prophet's burial to go and select a Caliph, to select an Imam—then tell me, was Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) not aware of this reality? Did Amir al-Mu'minin not know that selecting a Caliph is more important, that the Prophet's burial can be done later, that anyone can do it? I mean, who is Amir al-Mu'minin, about whom the Prophet said, 'Ana madinatul ilmi wa Aliyyun babuha. Faman aradal madinata wal hikmata falyatiha min babiha.' I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate. If anyone wants to enter the city, they should enter through the gate. Is Ali (a.s.) unaware? Ali (a.s.) is busy with the burial, the washing, the funeral preparations of the Prophet. Suddenly, a voice was raised, 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.' This was the tragedy of Islam. So the Master of the Universe asked, Those who were with them during the Ghusl were only four individuals, whom I can count on my fingers. They said, 'Do you know what this Takbir is for? Do you know what this Takbir is for?' They had chosen their Caliph. Now, here the Imam explicitly states that the Ulul-Azm Prophets, the possessors of the Book, the possessors of the Sharia, the chosen servants of Allah—whom Allah helped with knowledge, infallibility, and revelation—could not select [their successors], yet these individuals, who possessed no such characteristics, stood up. So, what happened? What was the result? The result was that the entire religion, the entire faith, was based on Qiyas (analogy) and Ra'y (personal opinion). A ban was placed on Hadith. This ban lasted for 100 years, 110 years, until the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. They tried to hide the virtues (Faza'il) of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). So much so that Nasa'i, whom people call Imam Nasa'i, actually wrote a book. 'Khasa'is-e-Aali Abi Talib'. He had to write this book. People asked him, 'Why did you write this book?' He said, 'Because I saw that people are not aware of the virtues of the Mawla of the Universe. They are not aware of the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). That is why I had to write the book.' And this incident is present; it is in the books, it is not just me saying it. I am not talking about a Shia book. This is present in the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni), as to what the reason for writing 'Khasa'is' was. And then when the people of Sham asked, 'When you wrote a book in praise of Ali, why didn't you write a book in praise of our Amir?' Imam Nasa'i replied, 'What should I write in his praise? When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) only said about him, "May his stomach never be filled."' What should I write for him? So, this is written in history. The people of Sham beat Imam Nasa'i so much, they beat him so much that it resulted in his death. And this tradition of the Muslims has continued to this day. To this day, the same thing continues: they will not engage in scholarly debate; they will talk about fighting, quarreling, and violence. You should fight, you should engage in scholarly debate, and whatever the matter is, resolve it through dialogue, through knowledge. Then, God willing, the truth will be clear. Therefore, that thing has continued to this day. The rest, God willing, we will present to you in the future. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin, wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin al-ma'sumin, wa la'natullahi da'imun ala a'daihim ajma'in, wa qatalatihim, wa ghasibi huquqihim, wa munkiri faza'ilihim wa manaqibihim.

title: Niyaabat mein Ziyaarat - Imam (a.s.) Ki Sunnat Hai [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the practice of performing Ziyarat by proxy (Niyaabat) for the Imams. Using the historical account of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) sending a deputy to Karbala during his illness, the speaker highlights that certain holy sites are specifically favored by Allah for the acceptance of prayers. The talk concludes by encouraging believers to perform Ziyarat on behalf of others and to prioritize praying for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) when visiting these sacred locations.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. The Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) is that great act of worship, the reward for which is evidenced by hundreds of traditions, proving how much the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) emphasized this Ziyarat. The importance of this Ziyarat can be gauged from the fact that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) not only encouraged their followers through their words but also proved its importance by practically going to Karbala themselves. And in some instances, it appeared in traditions that when the Imam himself could not go to Karbala due to illness, he sent someone else as his deputy and ordered them to pray for his recovery at the shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The high-ranking companion, Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari (r.a.), narrates that I went to the service of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). At that time, the Imam (a.s.) had a very high fever. The Imam (a.s.) said to me, 'O Abu Hashim! Send one of our followers to the holy shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.) so that he may go there and pray to Allah for me.' Abu Hashim says that I immediately came out of the Imam's house and met Ali ibn Bilal. I told him everything the Imam (a.s.) had said and requested him to send someone to the holy shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.) who would pray for Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). Now, the same question came to Ali ibn Bilal's mind that comes to the minds of most of us when someone reads or hears this Hadith for the first time. Ali ibn Bilal said, 'The Imam's command is on my head, but my belief is that the status of the Imam (a.s.) is superior to the shrine, and his rank is equal to the owner of the shrine, i.e., Imam Husayn (a.s.), and the prayer made by the Imam himself for himself will be superior to the prayer I will make for him at the shrine.' Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari says that I informed the Imam (a.s.) about this. Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) said, 'Tell him that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was also superior to the House of Kaaba and the Hajar al-Aswad, yet he performed Tawaf of the House of Allah and touched the Hajar al-Aswad.' After this, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Inna lillahi ta'ala biqa'an yuhibbu ay-yud'a fiha fayastajiba liman da'ahu' (Indeed, Allah has certain lands where He loves to be supplicated so that He may answer the one who supplicates to Him). 'Wal-ha'iru minha' (And the shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.) is one of those lands). Three important points become clear from this Hadith. First, sending someone else as a deputy for Ziyarat is the Sunnah of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). Therefore, if we cannot go for Ziyarat ourselves, we should try to send a relative, a loved one, or any other deserving person for Ziyarat as our deputy. Second, Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) himself ordered someone to be sent to Karbala as his deputy. Therefore, going for Ziyarat as a deputy of the Infallible Imams (a.s.) is also a Sunnah established by the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And the third point is that since Allah has made the shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.) a place for the acceptance of prayers, and Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) ordered prayers to be made for himself, whenever we go to Karbala, before praying for our personal needs, we should pray for the early reappearance of the son of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). Because this is a prayer that will not only be a cause of salvation for every believer but is also the most important prayer in the sight of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). O God! By the sake of the blessed land of Karbala, which You made a place for the answering of prayers, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) and grant us the Ziyarat of Karbala in his company. Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: EP#4: Kya Saqifah Mein Ijmaa Hua Tha? | Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture challenges the historical claim that a consensus (Ijma) was achieved at Saqifah regarding the Caliphate after the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker utilizes references from Sahih Bukhari to demonstrate that prominent figures, including Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Ansar, actively opposed the proceedings. The lecture argues that the absence of Imam Ali (a.s.) renders the legitimacy of the Saqifah event invalid in the eyes of Allah and His Messenger.
content:
It is a lie that all Muslims pledged allegiance at Saqifah. Muslims believe that there is a consensus (Ijma) among all Muslims regarding the allegiance that took place at Saqifah. That is, they believe that the majority of the Muslim Ummah, and specifically the prominent people, had accepted the decision of the Caliphate made at Saqifah and were satisfied and agreed upon it. But they cannot prove this claim even from their own books. In Sahih Bukhari, it is found: 'We received news that after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Ansar opposed us and gathered at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah. Ali (a.s.), Zubayr, and whoever was with them also opposed us, while the other Muhajireen gathered with Abu Bakr.' This tradition of Bukhari proves that far from consensus, the majority of Muslims opposed the allegiance that took place at Saqifah, and a decision in which Imam Ali (a.s.)—who was with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) at every moment and every occasion—did not participate, that allegiance can have no importance in the sight of Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.).

title: Bejaan Cheezein Imam Husain (a.s.) Par Kaise Girya Kar Sakti Hain? | E'teraaz Ka Jawaab | #muharram
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common objection regarding the Shia belief that inanimate objects wept over the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The speaker utilizes Quranic verses to establish that all creation possesses the capacity for glorification and praise, even if it remains beyond human comprehension. By citing historical traditions from Sunni sources and referencing Surah Ad-Dukhan, the speaker argues that the heavens and earth mourn for the friends of Allah, while they do not weep for the wicked.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Wali of Allah. Peace be upon Hussain, upon Ali ibn Hussain, upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. Respected viewers, as soon as the moon of Muharram appears, the Shia community prepares for their mourning (Azadari) and becomes grief-stricken over the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). At the same time, a barrage of objections comes from the opponents, who bring forward various strange objections to attack Azadari. For example, one objection is that Shias exaggerate in their mourning, claiming that not only humans but even inanimate objects wept over the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). In response to this, we ask these objectors: do they believe in the Holy Quran or not? Because Allah (S.W.T.) Himself states in the Holy Quran: 'Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah.' And similarly, in the Holy Quran... And similarly, there is another verse of the Holy Quran in which the Lord of Honor states: 'The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.' Allah states that everything in the seven heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and there is nothing that does not glorify Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Respected viewers, if one reflects on these two verses, where Allah is stating in the Holy Quran that the heavens, the earth, and all the creatures within them glorify Him and praise Him—if you observe, these are actions that humans perform. But here, Allah (S.W.T.) is stating in this verse that all creation, whether animate or inanimate, glorifies and praises Allah. And furthermore, He states that they glorify and praise Him, but you people cannot understand it. So here, the thing that... If we cannot understand it, then regarding things that are beyond our comprehension, our belief is based on what Allah says in the Quran: that they perform Tasbih (glorification) and Hamd (praise), even though we do not understand it. And the Quran itself says that we will not be able to understand it. So, the weeping that occurs over the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.), who is the Hujjat (Proof) of Allah, is manifest. As it is recorded in the book 'Tarikh Madinat al-Dimashq', Volume 14, from Awad bin Qais, that after the killing of Imam Hussain (a.s.), the horizon of the sky remained red for six months. This redness appeared on the horizon of the sky as if it were blood. Al-Dhahabi, who is a famous, well-known, and reliable scholar of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, has narrated this tradition in his book 'Siyar A'lam al-Nubala', Volume 3, page 312, and has also included that for six months, it remained like blood. The narrator of this tradition, Awad, was extremely truthful and pious. Isa ibn Harith al-Kindi saw something like a yellow sheet, and the stars were colliding with each other. And on the same page, it is also mentioned that when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was killed, it rained blood from the sky, and in the morning, whatever we had... ...rained, and in the morning, whatever we had was filled with blood. Respected audience, the Quranic verse and the traditions from the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah that I have presented before you make it clear and evident that the heavens and the earth wept over Imam Hussain (a.s.). Now, if someone argues based on the Quranic verse that it refers to Tasbih and Hamd and not weeping, then if one reads or recites verse number 29 of Surah Ad-Dukhan in the Holy Quran, Allah Almighty states: 'Fama bakat alayhimus-sama'u wal-ard' (Neither the heavens nor the earth wept over them). This verse refers to Pharaoh and his army, who were pursuing Prophet Musa (a.s.) and his people with the intention of killing them, and were drowned and destroyed in the Nile River. So, when Pharaoh and his army were destroyed, Allah stated in this verse of the Holy Quran that neither the heavens shed tears for them nor the earth. By revealing this verse, Allah has indicated that for the enemies of Allah, neither the heavens shed tears nor the earth. This means that if someone is a Wali (friend) of Allah and is martyred in the path of Allah, then the heavens and the earth also weep for him. Sallallahu ala Muhammad wa Aalihi al-Tayyibin al-Tahirine, wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil...

title: Majlis-e-Aza (Urdu) for Esaal e Sawaab of Marhoom Chaudhary Syed Mohd Naqi Ibne Chaudhary Mohd Yusuf
excerpt: This lecture, delivered as a Majlis-e-Aza for the Esaal-e-Sawaab of Marhoom Chaudhary Syed Mohd Naqi, explores the profound connection between true worship, self-knowledge, and divine submission. The speaker emphasizes that worship must transcend mere ritual, requiring spiritual insight and a deep understanding of one's self to avoid the pitfalls of religious deviation. By reflecting on the life and sacrifices of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the tragedy of Ali Asghar, the discourse illustrates the ultimate model of patience and total surrender to the will of Allah.
content:
Oh Ali Asghar, for you, the sky has become dark. Come into my lap, my beloved, my dear one. Where have you gone, my darling? I have come back for you, Ali Asghar, so that I may quench your thirst. My heart is restless, and my eyes are searching for you. How can I hide my grief? Oh Ali Asghar, in your thirst, I am losing myself. Peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his purified progeny (a.s.). We seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may peace and blessings be upon our Master and Prophet, Muhammad, and his pure and infallible household (a.s.). The discussion was about the remembrance of Allah, the worship of Allah, and the path of the righteous. If a person is occupied in the worship of Allah, it is as if you are seeing Him. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Imams (a.s.) have emphasized this. In this tradition, it is sufficient for a person to be a believer. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'The best of people is the one who loves worship intensely, embraces it, and clings to it with his heart.' This is the state of a person who is truly devoted to the worship of their Lord. Worship your Lord until certainty comes to you. This means he loves worship intensely and embraces it with his heart, soul, and body. He expresses this love through his prayers, fasting, Hajj, and every action, proving he is a true servant of Allah. He considers prayer the coolness of his eyes, and he pays great attention to it. If a believer truly wants to follow the path of the Imams (a.s.), they must be punctual in their prayers. They should set aside special time for Allah, ensuring no other task interferes with the time of prayer. As the tradition says, one should sit and wait for the prayer before the Adhan, showing their intense love for worship. This love is from the heart and is expressed through one's actions. When a person does this, they are not concerned with the state of the world or what it brings them. Their connection with their Lord is so strong that they remain indifferent to worldly affairs, focusing entirely on their worship. The goal of a believer should always be worship. Imam Ali (a.s.) says that one cannot attain closeness to Allah except through worship. This is logical; if we claim to be His servants, we must worship Him as He has commanded. To understand who the true followers of Imam Ali (a.s.) are, reflect on the words of Dua-e-Kumayl. Imam Ali (a.s.) describes how he heard someone crying in the darkness of the night. When he approached, he found a person in the state of prostration, worshiping with such intensity that it seemed as if he had become one with his worship. This was the state of the true servants of Allah. When such a state is achieved, one should focus on the Lord, knowing that one will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that Allah says, 'My servant draws near to Me through nothing more beloved to Me than the obligatory acts of worship.' Allah says, 'I become the hearing with which he hears, the sight with which he sees, the tongue with which he speaks, and the hand with which he acts.' This means the servant will only perform actions that are in accordance with the will of Allah, constantly reflecting on whether his deeds please Him. Therefore, in the book Al-Kafi, there is a chapter where it is mentioned that the most difficult duty for a servant is the remembrance of Allah. Imam (a.s.) explains that this does not just mean reciting 'Subhanallah' or 'Alhamdulillah,' but rather, in every situation, one must remember Allah and ensure that every action is in accordance with His will. They perform [actions], and if it is according to Allah's will, then they abstain from it. This withdrawal... [The speaker] says that today he is saying this, but I become his hand, I become his tongue, I become his eyes, I become his feet, I become indifferent to him. I love him so much that when he prays to me, I accept his prayers. That human... when he asks of me, I grant it to him. Therefore, I begin to... and I do this with such... but one thing, one thing, this matter when he... and with Ma'rifat (gnosis). When there is no Ma'rifat, then this Ma'rifat can be dangerous, this habit can be dangerous. I will [mention] a Hadith and a small part of it so that the matter of youth... [unclear]... those who did not create this... To provide justice, those who did not create this... for my worship, only for worship I have taken... that in this... Allah did not create them except that they worship Him. Allah did not create them except that He be... and when they worship Allah, they should worship Him in the correct way. He will be the one who will be guided. Such worship... and they will worship in the correct way, in such a way that they will never worship Allah in front of others. I will not [worship] in front of anyone in any era, not in front of anyone, not in front of any stone, not in front of any star, not in front of the sun, because he knows that... In front of the sun, because he knows that all of this... He created, therefore all of this... [Music] If someone asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the Ma'rifat of Allah?' You replied, 'The Ma'rifat of Allah is the Ma'rifat of all your affairs.' And the Ma'rifat of Allah is the Ma'rifat of your own self. Why is this so? Because if he does not recognize his own self, then he will not be able to worship correctly. If the worship is not correct, then his Ma'rifat will not be correct. If the Iman (faith) is not correct, then his deeds will be wrong. Therefore, this... all of this will be... if the Ma'rifat of the self is correct, then he will reach the destination. But if the Ma'rifat of the self is not correct, then he will go on the wrong path, and the faster he walks, the further he will go from his destination. And that is why you see that history or the Kharijites... See that history or the Kharijites, they are called Kharijites. Who are these Kharijites? They were those who used to worship, their foreheads had deep marks of prostration, as it is written in history, like the knees of a camel, that is how their foreheads were due to prostration. But they did not have Ma'rifat. That is why when they were attacking the Imam (a.s.), and they were... [unclear]... Now these Kharijites became against the truth. And look, they went against their own Imam, and they martyred the Imam. This is the result, and even today, these Kharijites exist in the world. And they have divided into many sects, but the condition was that their worship or they... even today they exist. So it is very important that a person attains Ma'rifat. That is why in history, a person whose name was... he did this... he was 94 years old, and he used to worship idols or something else. But at the age of 94, he realized that I am on the wrong path. 94... see, apart from this, whoever... he gives guidance to anyone. There is a proverb, 'It is never too late to wake up.' When a person realizes, he should return to the right path. The long story of Salman... he came to the Prophet and said, 'Give me your disciples.' The Prophet said, 'Go to the one who... go to him, you will find the life of the world.' Now, you have to talk to the one who is steadfast. He is so... he saw the Prophet on his back, he is not ready to accept our prayers. So he went to the mosque... Now I and the Messenger of Allah... and it is far away. After performing... then I came to you. Now we will do... he said, 'Okay, come.' He did... and now he is telling us things that are for us, for our life, they are lessons for our life. What are they? See, Ma'rifat and gain benefit... if you follow these steps, then first of all, find the reality of servitude in your own self. Be humble, become a true servant of God. And Imam Mahdi (a.s.) said, 'Worship is something else, and servitude is something else.' And gain knowledge to use it, not for show, not to be better than someone, not to do this, but to use it... and when you don't understand something, then ask Allah to make you understand. When you don't understand, then ask Allah to make you understand. Allah will make you understand. It is... if He makes you understand, then surely his knowledge will be... and will be illuminated. Now, when he heard all these things, he asked for three things. The first thing: find servitude in your own self. Second: gain knowledge to use it, not for show. Third: ask Allah to make you understand. So he... [unclear]... what is the reality of servitude? What is it? It is... [unclear]... one should understand that whatever Allah... whatever blessing, whatever property, whatever He has given, one should not consider it as one's own property. This is mine, no... everything is Allah's. When He wants, He will give, and when He wants, He will take it back. When He wants, He will take it back. He said, 'I am in your hands.' So, to consider something as one's own, 'This is mine,' we all... in the world, when a little bit of the world comes, he considers it his own. Remember, if he has to give to the poor, 'This is my Khums, this is my Zakat,' if someone says, 'Why should I give this?' He thinks it is his own wealth, but it is not his. All things are given by Him. Understand everything as Allah's. Allah is the owner of everything. Slaves used to be there, they had no property of their own, nothing. They had no property of their own. They had nothing. They were Allah's property. Allah's wealth, they consider it Allah's wealth. They do nothing. Allah... therefore, when it is Allah's wealth, they will keep this wealth and spend it where Allah has commanded. If he spends it according to his own will, then it will not be spent here. If a servant of Allah becomes... then this money... not even a single penny, if he is bringing an offering, that 'this should be spent in this work,' it will not be spent otherwise. A servant should understand that Allah has given it, and the second thing... what to do? He should... and the servant should... in any planning or work, he should be... Like we read in the supplications, we read in our religion, in the supplications, or in the destiny, the destiny for which all planning and all destiny, the planning is also made by Him, the destiny is also made by Him. A person should plan, do this, do that, but after doing it, he should say, 'Insha'Allah, if Allah wills.' If Allah wills, then the planning will be what Allah wills. One, when you plan, say that it is with Allah's help. And if Allah's will is there, then this work will be accomplished. If Allah's will is not there, it will not happen. If Allah's will is not there, a leaf cannot move from its place. A leaf cannot move. If the will of the Lord is there, then this place... [unclear]... there is a saying, and we... if Allah wills... the one who is the disposer of affairs, he lives in that state. A person makes plans, but Allah makes the plans, but Allah... He creates, but He creates with purpose. Now, it is true that every human being's planning and way of life is different, but in the matter of religion, or in our life, our destiny and our actions—for that, this is the final way. His planning will be the ultimate one, so entrust everything to Allah. 'Inna Allaha basirun bil-'ibad' (Indeed, Allah is All-Seeing of His servants). And the second thing is, 'Wa-li-kulli amrin ja'alna...'. Whatever he does, he should see whether Allah has permitted it or not, whether Allah has allowed this action or not. It will be a military operation of the universe. It is said that when a businessman starts, he should first understand the factory, he should read about the business, he should read the law. So, in the Sharia side, in the last chapter, it is written there; read it well, then go ahead. Read it well, then go ahead. Understand the Sharia, and after that, start your business. After that, whatever decision you take, in every action, you should see if Allah is pleased with it or not. And that is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Do not perform any action without the knowledge of Allah's Sharia.' It does not mean that you should not perform actions, but along with that, you should keep an eye on the Sharia of Allah. This is the matter, and this was the point, this was the instruction, and this was the reason why, when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was tasked... When Imam Hussain (a.s.) was tasked, a person like him—no one can describe him. He spent his entire life, his whole life, in the worship of Allah. And at this station, today, the proposal was placed before him. He gave everything for the sake of Allah. He sacrificed everything. Then a voice called out, a call of distress, 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna' (Is there any helper to help us?), 'Hal min dhabbin yadhubbu 'an harami rasulillah' (Is there any defender to defend the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah?). Will anyone help me? Is there anyone who will make what you have created? Is there anyone who will pass us to the Messenger? Is there anyone who will pass us to the Messenger? Hussain (a.s.) raised his voice in such a way that the heavens and the earth were shaken. The call was such that when he raised his voice, the ladies threw themselves from their camels. Hussain (a.s.) did not call anyone; he went himself. What Hussain (a.s.) said and what he understood, no one knows, but it is such that you will take the path of the martyrs. He is walking, reaching the battlefield. Why are you standing there? When he was in the tent, he thought of his six-month-old child. He thought of his six-month-old child. 'O Muslim, you are not a Muslim! People say, give the child water. My child has been thirsty for three days.' Someone replied, and Hussain (a.s.) asked another question, 'If you are Muslims, do you have no humanity?' He asked, and the people started to panic. He took out [the child], and you know, for hunting, when there is a hunt for a large animal, it stops. It does not die from a small arrow. He took out a three-pronged arrow and... He took out a three-pronged arrow and hunted. The arrow hit the throat of the six-month-old child. The throat was severed. Hussain (a.s.) saw that the six-month-old child was bleeding. He was worried, very worried. Hussain (a.s.) took the child and started walking towards the tents. He walked a little distance, then thought, 'How will I show this to his mother?' This is Hussain, the child's work is done. He was carrying the body... He was carrying the body, on one side was the brother, on the other side was Sakina. But Sakina reached first. Sakina reached first. [Music] The six-month-old child has been martyred. And the preparations... the companions, the children are also crying. The tragedy was visible, and he said, 'O companions, those who are...' And he said, 'O companions, those who are worried, they are sick.' May Allah protect the humanity of the whole world. Wherever they are in the world, may He protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. O Lord of the worlds, and those who are protecting them, may He protect them. And recite Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.

title: Taqleed: Ahmiyyat Aur Taqaazey | EP#02 - Taqleed Ke Hudood
excerpt: This lecture explains the fundamental distinction between Usul-e-Deen (principles of religion) and Furu-e-Deen (branches of religion) regarding the practice of Taqlid. It emphasizes that while blind imitation is forbidden in the core beliefs of Islam, where personal intellectual conviction is mandatory, Taqlid is necessary and obligatory for the practical laws of religion for those who have not reached the level of Ijtihad. The speaker supports these points by citing Quranic verses, traditions from the Ma'sumin, and the rulings of contemporary Maraji'.
content:
So, the first point you have stated is something like this: for every Muslim, it is necessary to know the Usul-e-Deen (Principles of Religion) with insight, because in the Usul-e-Deen, there can be no imitation (taqlid) in any way. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. In this series on the importance of Taqlid, you are once again welcome. We are discussing Taqlid, and today we will reflect on another aspect: in what things should Taqlid be done, and what is the scope of Taqlid? In religion, it is divided into two categories: one is called Usul-e-Deen (Roots of Religion) and the other is called Furu-e-Deen (Branches of Religion). Now let us see what Usul-e-Deen is. Now let us see what Usul-e-Deen is. Usul-e-Deen, meaning the roots, the roots of religion. In our view, there are five: Tawhid (Monotheism), Adl (Justice), Nubuwwah (Prophethood), Imamah (Imamate), and Ma'ad (Resurrection). Now, in these Usul-e-Deen, it is the responsibility of every sane and adult person; it is obligatory upon them that they should understand these Usul-e-Deen themselves. It is obligatory for every sane and adult person to understand these matters themselves. Using their intellect, in the light of the verses of the Holy Quran and the narrations of the Ma'sumin (a.s.), they should use their intellect to gain deep knowledge in religion or perform research, and based on proofs and evidence, they should believe in them. That is, for every person, it is necessary that they use their own intellect in the light of the Quran and the narrations of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), use evidence, gain insight, and through them, establish their beliefs or have faith in them. Establish your beliefs or have faith in them. It is important to mention here that there are certain principles of religion (Usul al-Din). Not everything can be done based on blind imitation. Therefore, it is necessary that the intellect (Aql) be used in the light of the Quran and traditions. Let us see what the Quranic indication is in this regard—that is, what the Quran has said about using intellect in Usul al-Din. First, let us turn to Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 111, in which Allah (SWT) says: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Qul hatu burhanakum in kuntum sadiqin.' (Say: Bring your proof if you are truthful). In this noble verse, humans are invited to present their proofs. Humans should research and understand matters in the light of clear proofs (Burhan) and then accept them. In contrast, those who adopt someone else's opinion in Usul al-Din without thinking—which is called 'blind following' in English—have been criticized, because in Islam, blind imitation in the principles of religion is not supported, and those who do so have been rebuked. And those who do so have been rebuked. For example, in Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 104, Allah (SWT) says: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa idha qila lahum ta'aw ila ma anzala Allahu wa ila ar-rasul qalu hasbuna ma wajadna 'alayhi aba'ana.' (And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' they say, 'Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers.') These people are being invited to use their intellect, but they are saying that they will only do what they found their ancestors doing. In this same verse, Allah (SWT) rebukes such people and says: 'Awa law kana aba'uhum la ya'lamuna shay'an wala yahtaduna' (Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided). Despite the fact that their ancestors possessed no knowledge and were not guided, in the first part of this verse, people are invited to use their intellect in matters of Usul al-Din, to understand what has been revealed in the Quran and Hadith in the light of intellect, and then establish their faith. In the second part of the verse, those who refuse to do so are explicitly rebuked. In the second part, those who refuse to do so are explicitly rebuked. Let us try to understand the importance of using intellect in Usul al-Din through a tradition. A person came to the presence of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and said that the foundations of religion are Tawhid (monotheism). They claim that there are traditions in the religion that have been introduced; among them is a Hadith that says: 'Inna usul ad-din tawhid...' (The foundations of religion are Tawhid...). When this person presented this to Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the Imam did not reject his statement. He was saying that it is necessary for a human to acquire the knowledge of these sciences—that is, the knowledge of the soul, the knowledge of the intellect, and the knowledge of the Hereafter. When he presented this to Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the Imam did not reject his statement. If his statement that it is necessary for every intellectual to acquire this knowledge were wrong, the Imam would have corrected him. If his statement were wrong, the Imam would have corrected him and verified it, telling him that it is not necessary to use intellect in Usul al-Din. But instead of correcting him or not verifying it, the Imam praised him and said that in the next part of the Hadith, the Imam explained the use of intellect. This tradition proves that the use of intellect is necessary in Usul al-Din, and the Imam even praised this. Furthermore, all the Maraji' al-Taqlid (religious authorities) have forbidden Taqlid (imitation) in Usul al-Din in their rulings. For example, if we look at the Tawdih al-Masa'il of Ayatollah al-Uzma Sayyid Ali al-Husayni al-Sistani (may Allah protect him), the very first ruling he has stated is something like this: 'It is necessary for every Muslim to know the principles of religion with insight, because Taqlid is not allowed in Usul al-Din in any way.' That is, it cannot be that a person believes in something in Usul al-Din just because someone else knows it. The great scholars and Maraji' al-Taqlid have also stated in their rulings that Taqlid is not permissible in Usul al-Din. That Taqlid is not permissible in Usul al-Din. This is regarding the principles of religion, which are outside the scope of Taqlid. In this, a human must research, investigate, and in the light of the Quran and traditions, use their intellect to establish their faith based on proofs and evidence. Now, let us move to the other aspect, which is the matter of Furu' al-Din (branches of religion). Furu' al-Din—that is, the practical laws of religion—are generally known to us. The acts of worship and the etiquette can also be included in these Furu' al-Din. Although there are many such acts, generally speaking, the Furu' al-Din are considered to be: Prayer (Salah), Fasting (Sawm), Khums, Zakat, Jihad, Amr bil-Ma'ruf (enjoining good), Nahi 'anil-Munkar (forbidding evil), and others. These are considered our Furu' al-Din. Now, when it comes to acting upon these laws, a person who is aware of all the lawful (Halal) and unlawful (Haram), who knows everything... Aware of Halal and Haram, who knows everything, who possesses mastery over the sciences of the Quran and Hadith, and through this, can derive the Sharia rulings and use the fatwas to act upon them—if they reach the level of Ijtihad, then there is no need for them to do Taqlid of anyone. But generally, it is not possible for everyone to acquire all these sciences, learn Arabic, and understand the various aspects of the Quran—which verse is a command, which is clear (Muhkam), which is ambiguous (Mutashabih), which is abrogating (Nasikh), and which is abrogated (Mansukh)—and understand the chain of narrators to know which Hadith is authentic and which is not. If they do not possess the knowledge of all these matters, then it is obligatory for them to do Taqlid of someone, follow someone, and follow the path of someone in Furu' al-Din. And the fatwa and the ruling that the Mujtahid has included in his Tawdih al-Masa'il, they must act upon it and follow it. This act of following is called Taqlid. The person who does Taqlid is called a Muqallid, and the one whose Taqlid is done... Is called a Muqallid, and the one whose Taqlid is done—that is, the one whose Taqlid is performed—is called a Mujtahid. So, the conclusion is that Taqlid is absolutely permissible in Furu' al-Din; in fact, it is obligatory. And as we stated in the previous video, Taqlid is a rational act that makes it easy for a human to act upon the Sharia. If a person cannot perform Ijtihad and precaution (Ihtiyat) themselves, then it is obligatory for them to do Taqlid of a Mujtahid. Understanding this point—that Taqlid is permissible in which things and what is the scope of Taqlid—the simple answer is that Taqlid is not permissible in Usul al-Din, and Taqlid is obligatory in Furu' al-Din. Alhamdullilahi Rabbil Alamin, wa Sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin wa Alihi at-tahirin. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad.

title: #7: Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Naseehatein | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of Imam Hussein's (a.s.) mission, focusing on his role as the Ark of Salvation who sought to guide the Ummah away from ignorance. The speaker highlights how Imam Hussein consistently offered sincere advice and fulfilled his duty by exhausting all excuses for the people from Medina to Karbala. By sacrificing everything, including his family and his own life, the Imam aimed to restore the true path of the Quran and Ahlulbayt. The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and a deeper understanding of the Imam's ultimate purpose.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr (Master of the Age), reach us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon al-Hussein, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussein, and upon the children of al-Hussein, and upon the companions of al-Hussein. Imam Hussein (a.s.) is the Ark of Salvation who, until his final moments, kept trying to bring his grandfather's strayed Ummah onto the straight path. These phrases of Ziyarat-e-Arbaeen point towards this reality: 'He fulfilled his duty in calling (people to the truth) by offering sincere advice, and he sacrificed his life for Your sake, in order to save Your servants from ignorance and the bewilderment of misguidance.' By inviting people towards the religion, he closed all paths of excuse for them, offered them advice, and sacrificed his life for Your sake so that he might lead Your servants out of the confusion of ignorance and misguidance. Imam Hussein (a.s.) kept closing the paths of excuse for people through his advice at every step from Medina-e-Munawwara to Karbala-e-Mualla. First, you refused to pledge allegiance to Yazid, then while bidding farewell to Medina-e-Munawwara, you stated the purpose of your journey. In response to the letters from the people of Kufa, you sent Hazrat Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.) to Kufa to complete the proof. When you received news that Yazid's army had reached Mecca-e-Mukarrama and a conspiracy had been hatched to assassinate you inside the Holy Kaaba, then for the sake of the sanctity of the Kaaba and to unmask your killer, the son of the Maulud-e-Kaaba (the one born in the Kaaba) changed his Hajj to Umrah and departed from Mecca-e-Mukarrama towards Karbala-e-Mualla. Throughout this entire journey, even after reaching Karbala-e-Mualla and on the day of Ashura, until his final moments, even after mounting his horse, he continued to warn people through his sermons. It even reached a point where, after his martyrdom, by reciting the Holy Quran from the tip of a spear, he made it clear to everyone what is truth and what is falsehood. The Muslims had forgotten the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) by pledging allegiance to Yazid. The result was that they fell into ignorance and misguidance. Imam Hussein (a.s.) rose up to awaken those people. Family, children, friends, and companions are very dear to any human being, but Imam Hussein (a.s.) sacrificed everything in the path of God, even his own life. O God! By the sake of the blood of Hussein, hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajuhush sharif), so that this era may once again hear divine advice from his blessed tongue, and grant us the Ziyarat of Imam Hussein (a.s.) by understanding his true purpose and acting upon his advice. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. Karbala, Karbala, Karbala, Karbala.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 5 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This session of the Ahkaam series focuses on the spiritual rewards of providing Iftar during Ramadan and addresses specific jurisprudential questions regarding fasting. The speaker emphasizes the importance of generosity, even with minimal means, and clarifies rulings for breastfeeding women and the elderly. Additionally, the lecture advises against reading non-Muslim authored literature about the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) if the content is known to be inaccurate or fabricated.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. In this fifth session of our program, we welcome all our viewers with Salawat. In the fourth session of this program, we discussed the questions raised by the Quran and Sunnah. There is a great difference in the rewards. And it is mentioned regarding this month that if a believer in this blessed month of Ramadan... If a believer provides Iftar to another believer in this blessed month of Ramadan, it is said that Allah will give that believer who provides the Iftar the reward of freeing ten slaves in His path, and all his previous sins will be forgiven. At that time, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not all have the means to perform this act.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Save yourselves from Hell, even if it is with half a date.' In the same way, save yourselves from the fire of Hell, even if it is with a sip of water. The environment of Iftar is ongoing; wherever you live, you must definitely perform Iftar. Feed the believers, arrange for Iftar. Let us now move to our questions and once again present them to the presence of the scholars and benefit from their explanation. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi. I understood, Alhamdulillah. Allah knows best. The question is similar to the previous one. People want to know if we can read books about the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that are written by non-Muslims, because in their books, they have written things that are not accurate. If you could shed some light on this, A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. If you know that the information is incorrect or fabricated regarding the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), then you cannot read it, as it is not true. It is not appropriate to read such things. When you know it is false, you should not engage with it. Those who have written such things for their own worldly motives or purposes—if you know this, you cannot read it, and it is upon you. You cannot do it, and it is upon you. But when you and I know, as the scholars say, that if some people are saying things, and we adopt what they are saying, then in such a situation, what will be the ruling? This is not right. We do not know; we are not aware of the reality. You have seen that we... You have seen that we should not go towards darkness; we should go towards the light. Regarding the books of non-Muslims, because we do not know and are not aware, we should avoid them. We should not read their books. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahab, for helping us with this. Now, the second question we have is from a viewer: If a woman is breastfeeding, is it permissible for her to keep a fast? And if the Sharia does not deem it permissible to fast, then from which month should she start fasting? Please shed some light on this, Maulana Sahab. If it is difficult for her, and she fears that fasting will harm her or her child, then that woman should not fast. The first opinion is not that four months have passed; rather, for a woman who is breastfeeding, if she fasts and her child does not get milk or she herself suffers harm, then in both cases, she cannot fast. But for a breastfeeding woman, if she is breastfeeding, then the 24 months do not matter. The scholars have stated the same. The scholars have stated that it depends on the woman herself, based on how she feels, whether she should fast or not. The third question we have, Maulana Sahab, is regarding the elderly who are unable to fast and cannot bear hunger and thirst. In this situation, what is the ruling of the Sharia? See, in this regard, for those who are elderly and for whom fasting is a hardship, for them, it is not obligatory. When a person becomes old and cannot bear the fast, and cannot live without food or water, then fasting is not obligatory for them. However, it is not that one should just decide on their own; one must assess if they have the strength. If it is a temporary old age or illness from which they might recover strength, then they should not fast. It depends on whether the strength returns. If a person is very weak and cannot stay without food for long, then they can be excused. I have even seen small children who have started following Islam; it is not possible for them to fast. Therefore, they themselves say that it is okay. In such a situation, Allah is merciful, and one can do what is necessary. We thank everyone who is watching this program and sending in their questions. We hope to meet you again soon. Until then, pray to Allah.

title: Kya Ghar Jalaana Paighambar (s.a.w.a) Ki Sunnat Thi? | Girya e Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical and theological contradiction of threatening to burn the house of Lady Fatima (s.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker questions whether such actions could ever be considered part of the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) Sunnah. By highlighting the sanctity of the Ahlulbayt's residence, the speaker challenges the sincerity of those who claim love for the Prophet while simultaneously threatening his family.
content:
Is it the Sunnah of the Messenger to burn down a house or threaten to burn it down just because someone refuses to pledge allegiance? Did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) ever do such a thing in his life? Did he ever give an order that if someone does not pledge allegiance, then burn them with fire? We have never seen this in the life of the Messenger. And whose house is being threatened to be burned? This is the house where the family of Prophethood resides. This is the house where Janab Ali and Fatima (s.a.), Ali (a.s.), and Janabe Zahra (s.a.) live. This is the house where the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) live. Imam Hassan and Imam Hussein (a.s.) live there. This is the house that is being threatened to be burned—the house where the family of Prophethood resides. I mean, on one hand, claims of love, and on the other, talk of burning the house? What kind of love is this?

title: Jo Nek Kaam Mein Deyr Karey | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #YouTubeShorts  #muharram
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the importance of acting immediately on good deeds based on a teaching from Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha. He warns against the habit of procrastination, explaining that delaying righteous actions leads to the neglect of various responsibilities. The lecture emphasizes that one should prioritize fulfilling duties to Allah, family, and society without waiting for a 'tomorrow' that is never guaranteed.
content:
The Master of the Universe (Imam Ali) says in Nahj al-Balagha, never postpone any action that you need to achieve; do not delay it, saying 'I will do it tomorrow.' The time for prayer has come, 'I will pray later.' No, right now, it is time for prayer, pray now. Pray immediately. Whatever the time is, do it right now. If you have to pray, pray now. Has anyone seen 'later'? No one has seen 'later.' Look at what the Master said: 'He who obeys procrastination wastes rights.' The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) is saying—these are the words of the Master—that whoever obeys postponement, who delays everything, who postpones everything saying 'I will do it tomorrow, I will do it later,' he will always waste rights. He will squander rights; he will never fulfill the right of Allah, nor the right of the Imams, nor the right of his wife and children, nor the right of his friends and companions, nor the right of the world, nor the right of the hereafter. He will not fulfill any right. A person who has the habit of saying 'I will do it later'—do today what you would do tomorrow, do now what you would do today. But this applies to good deeds, not for sins.
