So that through it you can reach Allah. Okay. Now you... on this sentence... Allah's names are beautiful for Allah, so call upon that same name. Now look, what does 'call upon' mean? I want to give an example. Look, Allah is... I tell you a story. The provision is that we... Allah has given the human being in this world, in the same way, and the one who brings the human being between the angels... so this hand... it is on the fourth heaven. Now, this means that the angels will see, and the angels'... becomes... The angels will see, and the angels'... becomes... so... the interpretation of... with this work of his, so much and something, do this thing. And whenever any good deed is mentioned in the Quran, Allah... between the angels... and if this human being... intends to do any bad deed, Allah says to his angels, 'Put a... on this human.' He intended to commit a sin, he did not commit it yet, just intended. What is the first thing? For the attribute, you need... that if you... what will happen? That if you... what will happen? You can say, then this... Allah has sent every person in this world with a target, that reaching that target is the perfection. So this is the second one, or this is simple, that I show the attribute, I show the wisdom. I am inviting the reader to this. And if any person could do this, you know, you know, you believe, you are fulfilling the purpose of... and your... is happening. Your... is the effort. After that, there is a very big problem that every Quran reader has, and this is not known. What is that? As I read in the verses, it tells the Quran readers... What does it mean when we say there are veils over the hearts regarding the Quran? It means that in understanding the Quran, in reaching the depths of its meaning, certain things become obstacles. Certain things become hurdles in our path, preventing us from reaching the reality of the Quran, the path of the Quran, and the guidance of the Quran. It is necessary to remove these from your heart. What are these things? I have taken twelve points, and look, some of our respected scholars have passed away in this century, and so much has been written about their interpretations and their principles that people have forgotten that as long as they are alive, the Quran does not guide them. Yet, the Quran is such that it guides those who remain firmly attached to it. Look, one thing is very important regarding the Quran. What is that thing? One thing is very important in understanding the Quran, in being attached to it, in its recitation, and in its contemplation. People have tried to remove these obstacles, but let it not be that I am saying we should not be attached to it. Rather, I am saying we must be attached to it. Let me give you another example. Some of our ideologies talk about our interpretations, and do not consider it a small thing; it is a very good work. We must be attached to the Quran in every way, as Allah (S.W.T.) has commanded us. Allah (S.W.T.) has commanded us, and we are connected to all these things—the Quran, the closeness to it, and the house of the Prophet. If we are to be Muslims, then this is another point I want to address. Is it a big sin? What is this big sin? It is that I lied, or I committed a sin, and then I should seek repentance from Allah. It is not just that. Is it true that other small sins like backbiting, slandering, or lying are not sins? Committing sins and persisting in them is an obstacle to reaching the reality of the Quran. So, this is a new thing that is an obstacle. That is why in the Quran, some people read it, but as they read, their faith increases. Their faith increases because they have removed the obstacles that were preventing them from understanding the Quran. They reached that place where the Quran is. But when the Quran came before them, when any verse of the Quran was recited, it was as if it was being revealed to them. Therefore, my dear ones, you cannot understand it if your heart is veiled. My heart must be in front of the Quran to reach its reality. So, this is the address of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). If you are a believer, if you are a Momin, when Allah... If you are a Momin, when Allah calls you, what does He say? He is talking to me. Where is He? He has solved the problems of the believers and made arrangements for those whose footsteps we are not even worthy of. That God is giving us a chance to talk to Him. He is addressing me, He is giving me a message. What is this called? Sometimes He addresses the Children of Israel, sometimes the believers. It is not just that. When He addresses you like this, you must listen to the Quran. It is a great honor that we focus our attention on the voice of that God. How great it is that from Allah's side, 'O you who believe'... O you who believe. So, one of the things is that we should recite the Quran with focus, and He is speaking to us. So, what should we do? That is why it is a great honor for us that the Quran is a message from Him. I am saying that whenever you sit to recite, you should listen to the message He is giving after 'O you who believe'. One meaning is that when He says something, I should act upon it. I want to give an example of what this means. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came to the house of his wife, and she said that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was very sad because a verse had been revealed, and he was weeping so much that no one had the courage to go and talk to the Prophet. No one had the courage to talk to him. How can we get the Prophet out of this state of grief? We cannot understand. If you go to the Prophet, because you love him so much, if you go before him and ask something, the Prophet will come out of his state of grief. And then it is said that when she went, what happened? The Prophet recited the verse. The wife had the strength to make him stop, and it is said that do not just recite it, but let it be felt in your heart. My heart should feel the joy of it. Everyone's heart should be affected by it. And at the same time, if God is saying that I will put you in Hell, then tears should flow from our eyes. Then tears should flow from our eyes, and the grief and pain of it should be felt in our hearts, and we should ask for forgiveness. 'O Allah, my body is weak, O Allah, I do not have the strength to endure even a small part of Your punishment.' So, when you are connecting with the Quran, when you are reading the Quran, it is not just with your tongue; your heart should also respond. If there are verses of joy, your heart should be happy, and if there are verses of warning, you should seek refuge and ask Allah to include you among those who receive His mercy. There is another thing: if Allah has created man... Allah has created man and made his status very high. There is no time now to talk about it in detail, but the summary today is that just as you recite the Quran, and when you read it in this manner, your status will be elevated. You will not know, but the point is that when you are reading the verses of the Quran, your status will be elevated, and you will know what you have read. Why is this spiritual connection important? Because the first thing is that when it is the Book of Allah, I will tell you a Hadith. Look at how amazing this Hadith is. Imam Ali (a.s.) was praying one day, and in his prostration... Until I kept repeating it, I heard that verse from the tongue of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and its power settled in my heart. Its majesty was such that my eyes could not bear it, and I fainted. See, to what heights he reached! And I also want that. And what is that? That no matter how much you do good deeds, no matter how many books you gather, if you go before the Quran to read it, you must go as a beggar before Allah, and you are asking for something. Therefore, do not consider yourself anything until you consider yourself nothing before God. As long as you consider yourself a servant of God, when you stand before Allah, you should say, 'O Allah, I am Your weak servant. Do not let me be arrogant for even a moment.' You might have seen a dead dog somewhere; perhaps I am like that. When you stand before Allah, say, 'O Allah, I am coming to You, and You are the one who gave me the life for which I am now standing before You.' I am standing before You, and if you think, 'I am better than such and such an animal,' then you are mistaken. If you want to take spiritual benefit, sit before the Quran like a sinner so that the Quran can extract your inner impurities. And the last thing I want to say to conclude my talk is about reading the Quran with presence of heart. I will read a Hadith, and please pay close attention to it. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said that the one who recites the Quran needs three things. The first is a heart that is present. We do not read it just for the sake of reading; we read it to connect with Allah. One of these things is a heart, and the second is a pure body. If you want to do this work... The second is a pure body. If you want to do this work, your mind and your body must be pure from everything. When you recite the Quran in that state, the pleasure of recitation will be different. And the third thing he mentioned is a quiet place where there is no coming and going of people, and there is distance. That is why verse 16 of Surah Al-Hadid says: 'Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humble at the remembrance of Allah?' This is the state of the heart that the Imam wanted—that my heart should be connected to the Quran from beginning to end. So that it can be connected from beginning to end. I have taken much of your time, so I will conclude here. With this prayer, may Allah connect me and you to the Quran, and may He grant us the ability to recite it, understand it, and act upon it. Now, I am ready for the questions. The last question is: 'While reciting the Quran, various thoughts come to our minds, and we are not as focused as we should be, just as it happens during prayer. What should we do in such a situation?' I will answer this. When you realize the importance of something and understand its significance, your heart will naturally incline towards it. Our Imams say that if you... Our Imams say that if you are aware of the importance of the Quran and its greatness, when you sit before the Quran, your heart will not wander, and your eyes will not be distracted. Another thing I want to say is that a major problem is that our hearts do not feel engaged. The answer is that you have become worldly. As long as your connection with the world is strong, it will not be easy for you to focus. So, my brother, as you asked, think about it. Analyze which things are stopping you from reaching the meanings within the Quran and remove them. Be sympathetic to others. The second question is: 'If the mind is stressed due to other reasons during the recitation of the Quran, should one continue or stop and resume later?' You have asked a very relevant question. Imam Ali (a.s.) used to say, 'Engage your heart with the words you are reciting.' But if your heart is not in it due to anger or other reasons... But if your heart is not in it due to anger, then recite as much as your heart is engaged. If you are not reciting with your heart and your attention is wandering elsewhere, it is better to close the Quran and pray to Allah. As I mentioned, a person needs three things to recite the Quran: a present heart, a pure body, and a mind that is not occupied with other things. The third question is: 'How can we be sure that we are receiving guidance from the recitation of the Quran?' Look, I have already explained this. Some people say, 'Has the time not come?' Now, if you used to steal, and the Quran says the punishment for stealing is cutting the hand, and you still steal, then you haven't understood it. I want to say... I want to say that when I went to the Ashram to study, I saw something beautiful that impressed me greatly. It is that after every prayer, one page of the Quran is recited. It takes only two or three minutes, and every worshiper there participates. It is not that only one person recites. It was very attractive, and this is what the Quran does. After that, you become a different person. This is how the Quran blesses you with spirituality. The more a person finds themselves distant from their sins, the more they will naturally feel inclined toward the Quran. If you are not distancing yourself from sins, but your heart is still wandering, then you should take your time. And the last question, which is very practical—though all were practical—is a problem seen very often nowadays: messages about 'Khatm-e-Quran' (completing the Quran) are sent on WhatsApp groups. If we intended to recite a portion but couldn't, are we sinners? My brother, Allah's mercy is very vast. Especially, it is a strange thing that Allah has bestowed mercy upon the Ummah of our Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). If you intend to do a good deed, you get the reward. But if you haven't done it, there is no sin in it. And this issue also arises when people distribute parts of the Quran for a 'Khatm' and force others to recite. If you cannot recite, it is not a religious obligation. It is not a religious obligation. You are forced, and it doesn't benefit the deceased if you do it under pressure. If you have given your word, it is a matter of trust. If one person recites, it is enough. Before someone finishes it with difficulty, it is better to do it willingly. If someone is forcing you, it is a burden. So, if you can recite, it is very good; if you cannot, you will not be held responsible for it. May Allah keep us and you safe and help us stay on the path of Islam. May our connection with the Quran remain forever, and may He grant us the ability to illuminate our hearts with its light. Besides these ten, there are others who gave correct answers; their names will be updated on the social media pages of the group by tomorrow, Insha'Allah. Let us begin this session with the supplication that has been emphasized to be recited after every prayer in the month of Ramadan, in which prayers have been made for all the needy and those in need of every kind. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.

title: Ayat-e-Tatheer in Shia & Ahle Tasannun Books
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological significance of the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tathir) from Surah Al-Ahzab, emphasizing its role in establishing the infallibility and status of the Ahl al-Bayt. The speaker references both Shia and Sunni traditions, specifically Hadith al-Kisa, to demonstrate that the Prophet Muhammad and the Panjtan-e-Pak were the intended recipients of this divine purification. The lecture concludes by arguing that this purity serves as a rational proof for the Imamate and Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the subsequent Imams.
content:
Greetings to you, viewers. We, the 'The Strong Group' team, present to you the verses of the Holy Quran and the traditions regarding the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) that God Almighty has revealed in His Quran concerning him. The entire Muslim Ummah is unanimously convinced that all these verses were revealed regarding the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). The verse we are presenting today is the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), which is mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse number 33. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. 'Innama yureedullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa ahlal-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathheera.' The translation is: 'Indeed, Allah wishes to remove all impurity from you, O People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt), and to purify you with a thorough purification.' Now, viewers, this Verse of Purification is the greatest proof regarding the infallibility (Ismah) and virtue of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and if God Almighty has emphasized any verse the most, it is... It is this verse that has been emphasized, and this emphasis is known as the Hadith al-Kisa, whose narrator is Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who narrates it from Lady Zahra (s.a.). Dear friends, the reference for Hadith al-Kisa, which is found in our Shia books, was recorded by the Shia scholar Abdullah Bahrani in his book 'Awalim al-Ulum', where he narrates the Hadith al-Kisa. Hadith al-Kisa is such a magnificent tradition that describes the virtue and infallibility of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and clarifies their status. This event, which Abdullah Bahrani is recording in his book, takes place in the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.) and describes the gathering of the Panjtan-e-Pak (the five pure ones) under her cloak. Although every sentence in this Hadith al-Kisa is a miracle, there are two major proofs within it. The first proof is that Allah (swt) created all of creation based on the love for the family of Muhammad (a.s.), saying, 'O Ahl al-Bayt, it is for the love of you that I am creating this entire world.' Look at the sentences in Hadith al-Kisa: 'Wa izzati wa jalali, inni ma khalaqtu sama'an...' Allah is swearing by His Honor and His Majesty, and then He says, 'I would not have created the high heavens, nor...' Nor would I have spread out the earths, nor would I have created the luminous moon, nor the shining sun, nor the rotating spheres, nor the flowing seas, nor the ships sailing upon the seas, were it not for the love of you, O Ahl al-Bayt. So, the first most important point being presented here is that Allah created the entire world out of love for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). And the second point to be presented here is regarding this Verse of Purification, that when Allah presents this fact before His angels in the heavens—that I have created all the worlds, all the heavens, and all the earths out of love for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)—then through Gabriel (a.s.), Allah sends this message when the People of the Cloak (Ahl al-Kisa) were present under the cloak. Who were those individuals present under the cloak? First, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was present under that cloak. After him, Imam Hassan (a.s.) went in, then Imam Hussain (a.s.) was present there, then the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) was also present, and Lady Zahra (s.a.) herself was... Present under that cloak. When these Panjtan-e-Pak were present there, Allah sent Gabriel (a.s.) with this verse. Gabriel comes to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), offers his greetings, and says: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Innama yureedullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa ahlal-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathheera.' Indeed, Allah intends to purify you, O Ahl al-Bayt—your children, your daughter, your son-in-law, and all the descendants who will come from Lady Zahra (s.a.)—with the purification that is their right. Dear friends, this is the reference we have presented to you from our books. Now, here is a book from the Sunni tradition, which is present in the Sihah al-Sittah (the six authentic books), and within it, this hadith regarding the Verse of Purification is present, in which it is stated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) comes to the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.), and then Imam Hassan (a.s.) comes under the cloak, then Imam Hussain (a.s.), the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and Lady Zahra (s.a.). When these five individuals come under that cloak, then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) recites this verse: Innama yureedullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa ahlal-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathheera. So, not only in our books, but even in the major Sunni book, Sahih Muslim, this hadith points towards the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), that 'O Ahl al-Bayt, Allah intends to purify you.' Now, viewers, we want to present a very important point regarding the argument for the Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.): how can the Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) be argued from this verse? First of all, the word 'rijs' (impurity) that appears in it—the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have been kept away from all 'rijs'. All 'rijs', meaning both physical impurity and spiritual impurity. Physical impurity means the filth of the body. If Allah had not kept the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) away from physical impurity, why would the door of Ali (a.s.) have been opened towards the mosque? Why, if the birth of Ali (a.s.) took place in the Kaaba, would this not indicate that Allah has kept them protected from all physical impurities? After that, the spiritual 'rijs', meaning the inner impurity—the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have been kept pure and cleansed from all such impurities. That is, disbelief, hypocrisy, polytheism, ignorance, cowardice, malice, and bad character—Allah has kept the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) pure and cleansed from all these impurities. Now, let us move to the argument... Regarding the fact that because they are far from all 'rijs', they are 'protected from error' (Ma'sum). Now, they will not commit any error. They cannot do anything wrong. If they are protected from error, then no other individual can be better than them. Meaning, if any other individual were protected from error, they would have been present under the cloak. So, after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), whoever takes the place of the Messenger can only be the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), because just as the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is protected from error, so too is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Now, here I must present a rational point: Can a believer and a transgressor (Fasiq) be equal? The Quran itself says, 'Is the one who is a believer like the one who is a transgressor? They are not equal.' And who is the believer? The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), who is protected from error. Can the learned and the ignorant be equal? 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?' So, dear friends, from this, it can be clearly argued from this verse that the rest of the Ummah was ignorant, and since Ali (a.s.) is protected from error and has been kept away from all impurities, if there is any greatest scholar in this Ummah after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), it is my master, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Now, I am presenting the final point. It is possible that this question might arise in your mind: that here only the Panjtan (the five) are being discussed. In the Verse of Purification, only the Panjtan were gathered under that cloak. The word 'banu' (sons) has been used for Lady Zahra (s.a.), and 'banu' is used for three or more children, and there were only two children present there—Imam Hassan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.). So, the word 'banu' is being used there. Therefore, besides the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), Imam Hassan (a.s.), and Imam Hussain (a.s.), the remaining nine Imams were also present in the Hadith al-Kisa. They are also protected from error. So, this Verse of Purification is the greatest proof regarding the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). This Verse of Purification is the greatest proof regarding the Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.).

title: Are we really attached to our Imam? (may Allah hasten his reappearance) (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of the final verse of Surah Al-Imran, focusing on the command to 'remain stationed' (rabitu). The speaker explains that this term implies a deep, continuous, and firm attachment to the Imam of our time, Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.). By maintaining this heartfelt bond and constant remembrance, believers can attract the Imam's attention and navigate the challenges of the occultation.
content:
God says in the Quran, in the last verse of Surah Al-Imran: 'O you who have believed, persevere (1) and endure (2) and remain stationed (3) and fear Allah (4) that you may succeed.' If you want the path of happiness and salvation, its path is in these four words. 'Isbiru' (persevere), be patient. 'Sabiru' (endure), I mean do not flee from the enemy, stand firm, resist. The third command addresses the answer to this question: 'Wa rabitu' (remain stationed/connected). 'Rabit' is not just connection. We do not use 'connection' in the Arabic sense in our Persian or Urdu language. Right now, my hand is on this chair; well, in Persian, we say it has a connection. Is that right? My hand is attached to this black fabric on the chair right now, it is connected. The connection that the Quran speaks of is not this. What does connection mean? It means a firm attachment. A human being should have a continuous, firm connection with that Presence (the Imam). So, the way to attract the attention of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) and to benefit more from the lights of that Presence during the time of occultation is to have a bond with Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). A person should not forget that they have an Imam. Blessed is the one who remembers Imam-e-Zaman fifty times a day. This heart-felt bond, this connection, and heart-felt remembrance are important. When there is heart-felt remembrance, other duties follow.
The Quranic command 'rabitu' signifies a firm, continuous spiritual attachment to the Imam.
Success and salvation are linked to perseverance, endurance, and remaining connected to the Imam.
The connection to the Imam is not merely physical but a deep, heartfelt bond.
Believers should strive to remember Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) frequently throughout the day.
Heartfelt remembrance of the Imam serves as the foundation for fulfilling other religious duties.
Maintaining a bond with the Imam helps believers benefit from his spiritual light during the occultation.

title: Duas | Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali دعاء ابي حمزة الثمالي (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali is a profound and deeply spiritual supplication traditionally attributed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin, recited during the nights of Ramadan. The prayer serves as a comprehensive dialogue between the servant and the Creator, emphasizing themes of divine mercy, human frailty, and the necessity of absolute reliance on God. Through its poetic and humble language, the supplicant acknowledges their shortcomings while seeking refuge in the infinite forbearance and grace of Allah.
content:
And whenever I desired my need and sought help for it from other than You, without an intercessor, my need was fulfilled. Praise be to Allah, whom I do not call upon except Him, and if I were to call upon other than Him, He would not answer my prayer. And praise be to Allah, whom I do not hope for except Him, and if I were to hope for other than Him, He would not fulfill my hope. And praise be to Allah, who entrusted me to Himself, so He honored me, and did not entrust me to people, so they would humiliate me. And praise be to Allah, who showed love to me while He is independent of me. And praise be to Allah, who is forbearing with me as if I have no sin. So my Lord is the most worthy of praise to me and the most deserving of my praise. O Allah, I find the paths of requests to You open, the springs of hope to You overflowing, and seeking help through Your grace for those who hope in You is permissible, and the doors of prayer to You are open for the righteous. And I know that You are for those who hope in You in the position of response, and for the distressed in the place of relief, and that in the generosity of Your grace and satisfaction with Your decree is a substitute for the stinginess of the stingy, and a replacement for what is in the hands of the possessors. And that the traveler to You is close in distance, and that You are not veiled from Your creation except that their deeds veil them from You. And I have aimed for You with my requests, and turned to You with my need, and made my plea through You, and my prayer to You... My Master, not because I deserve to be heard by You, nor because I deserve Your forgiveness, but because of my trust in Your generosity, my reliance on the truth of Your promise, my resort to faith in Your Oneness, and my certainty in Your knowledge, that there is no Lord for me other than You, and there is no god but You, alone, You have no partner. O Allah, You are the One who said, and Your word is truth and Your promise is certain, 'And ask Allah of His bounty, indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you.' And it is not among Your attributes, O my Master, to turn away a request and refuse a gift, and You are the Bestower of gifts to the people of Your kingdom, and the One who returns to them with the tenderness of Your compassion. My God, You raised me in Your blessings and kindness when I was small, and You made my name famous when I was grown. So O You who raised me in the world with Your kindness, favor, and blessings, and pointed me in the hereafter to Your forgiveness and generosity, my knowledge, O my Master, is my guide to You, and my love for You is my intercessor to You. And I am confident in my guide through Your guidance, and tranquil in my intercessor through Your intercession. I call upon You, I call upon You, O my Master, with a tongue that has been silenced by its sins, my Lord, I whisper to You with a heart that has been ruined by its crimes. I call upon You, O my Lord, trembling, hoping, fearing. When I see my sins, O Master, I am terrified, and when I see Your generosity, I am greedy. So if You forgive, You are the best of the merciful, and if You punish, You are not unjust. My argument, O Allah, for my boldness in asking You while I commit what You dislike, is Your generosity and kindness. And my provision in my hardship, despite my lack of shame, is Your compassion and mercy. And I have hoped that You will not disappoint my desire between these two, so fulfill my hope, and hear my prayer, O best of those whom a caller calls, and the most excellent of those whom a hopeful person hopes for. My hope, O my Master, has become great, and my deeds have become evil, so give me from Your forgiveness in the measure of my hope, and do not hold me accountable for my worst deeds, for Your generosity is too exalted to punish the sinners, and Your forbearance is too great to retaliate against the negligent. And I, O my Master, am seeking refuge in Your grace, fleeing from You to You, expecting what You have promised of pardon for those who think well of You. And who am I, O Lord, and what is my worth? Grant me by Your grace, and bestow upon me Your forgiveness. O Lord, cover me with Your veil, and pardon my being rebuked by the generosity of Your Face. For if anyone other than You had seen my sin today, I would not have done it, and if I had feared the hastening of punishment, I would have avoided it. Not because You are the least of observers and the lightest of witnesses, but because You, O Lord, are the best of those who cover, and the wisest... of judges, and the most generous of the generous, the Coverer of faults, the Forgiver of sins, the Knower of the unseen. You cover the sin with Your generosity, and delay the punishment with Your forbearance. So to You is the praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge, and for Your forgiveness after Your power. And what carries me and emboldens me to disobey You is Your forbearance towards me, and what invites me to lack of shame is Your covering of me, and what hastens me to jump upon Your prohibitions is my knowledge of the vastness of Your mercy and the greatness of Your forgiveness. O Forbearing, O Generous, O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Forgiver of sin, O Acceptor of repentance, O Great in bounty, O Ancient in kindness, where is Your beautiful covering? Where is Your great forgiveness? Where is Your near relief? Where is Your swift succor? Where is Your vast mercy? Where are Your excellent gifts? Where are Your pleasant bounties? Where are Your sublime deeds? Where is Your great grace? Where is Your immense generosity? Where is Your ancient benevolence? O Generous One, by Your generosity, rescue me; and by Your mercy, deliver me. O Beneficent, O Beautifier, O Bestower, O Giver of favors. O Beneficent, O Beautifier, O Bestower, O Giver of favors. O Beneficent, O Beautifier, O Bestower, O Giver of favors. I do not rely for salvation from Your punishment upon our deeds, but rather upon Your grace towards us, for You are the Lord of piety and the Lord of forgiveness. You initiate blessings with benevolence and pardon sins out of generosity. We do not know what to thank: the beauty You spread, or the ugliness You conceal, or the greatness of what You have tested and bestowed, or the abundance of what You have saved and healed us from. O Beloved of those who show love to You, and O coolness of the eyes of those who seek refuge in You and turn to You. You are the Beneficent and we are the evildoers, so overlook, O my Lord, the ugliness that is with us by the beauty that is with You. What ignorance, O my Lord, is not encompassed by Your generosity? Or what time is longer than Your forbearance? What is the worth of our deeds compared to Your blessings? And how can we consider our deeds great to match Your generosity? Rather, how can the mercy that encompasses them befit the sinners? O Vast in forgiveness, O You who stretch out Your hands with mercy, by Your might, O my Master, if You were to drive me away, I would not depart from Your door, nor would I cease my flattery, because of the knowledge I have attained of Your generosity and kindness. You are the Doer of what You will; You punish whom You will, with what You will, how You will, and You have mercy on whom You will, with what You will, how You will. You are not questioned about Your actions, nor are You disputed in Your kingdom, nor are You shared in Your command, nor are You opposed in Your judgment, nor does anyone object to You in Your management. To You belongs the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds. O my Lord, this is the station of one who has sought refuge in You, sought shelter in Your generosity, and become accustomed to Your benevolence and blessings. For You are the Generous One whose pardon does not narrow, whose grace does not diminish, and whose mercy does not decrease. We have expanded ourselves with Your ancient pardon, Your great grace, and Your vast mercy. Do You, O my Lord, break our expectations or disappoint our hopes? Never, O Generous One, for this is not our opinion of You, nor is this our desire in You. O my Lord, we have a long and great hope in You; we have a great expectation in You. We have disobeyed You while hoping that You would conceal us, and we have called upon You while hoping that You would answer us. So fulfill our hope, our Master, for we have known what we deserve by our deeds, but Your knowledge of us and our knowledge that You will not turn us away from You—even if we are not deserving of Your mercy—means You are worthy to be generous to us and to the sinners by the grace of Your vastness. So bestow upon us what You are worthy of, and be generous to us, for we are in need of Your attainment. O Oft-Forgiving, by Your light we have been guided, by Your grace we have become self-sufficient, and by Your blessing we have entered the morning and the evening. Our sins are before You; we seek Your forgiveness, O Allah, for them and we repent to You. We show love to You with blessings, while we confront You with sins. Your good descends to us, while our evil ascends to You. And there has never ceased to be, and there will never cease to be, a noble, generous angel who brings You our ugly deeds, yet that does not prevent You from surrounding us with Your blessings and favoring us with Your bounties. So glory be to You; how Forbearing, how Great, and how Generous You are, as the Originator and the Restorer. Holy are Your names, majestic is Your praise, and generous are Your deeds and actions. You are my God, of more vast grace and greater forbearance than to measure me by my deeds and my sins. So pardon, pardon, pardon, my Master, my Master, my Master. So pardon, pardon, pardon, my Master, my Master, my Master. So pardon, pardon, pardon, my Master, my Master, my Master. O Allah, occupy us with Your remembrance, protect us from Your wrath, save us from Your punishment, provide us from Your gifts, bestow upon us from Your grace, and grant us the pilgrimage to Your House and the visitation of the grave of Your Prophet—may Your blessings, mercy, forgiveness, and pleasure be upon him and his family. Indeed, You are Near, Responsive. Grant us the ability to act in Your obedience, and take our souls while we are upon Your creed and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family. O Allah, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small. Reward them with goodness for their benevolence, and with forgiveness for their sins. O Allah, forgive the believing men and women, the living among them and the dead, and join us and them in good deeds. O Allah, forgive our living and our dead, those present and those absent, our men and our women, our young and our old, our free and our slaves. Those who equate others with Allah have lied, gone far astray, and suffered a manifest loss. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and seal my life with goodness. Suffice me against what concerns me of my worldly and hereafter affairs. Do not give power over me to one who does not have mercy on me. Place upon me a lasting protection from You. Do not deprive me of the good things with which You have blessed me. Provide me from Your grace with a vast, lawful, and pure provision. O Allah, guard me with Your guardianship, protect me with Your protection, and shelter me with Your shelter. Grant me the pilgrimage to Your Sacred House in this year of ours and in every year, and the visitation of the grave of Your Prophet and the Imams (peace be upon them). Do not deprive me, O my Lord, of those noble shrines and honorable stations. O Allah, turn to me in repentance so that I do not disobey You, inspire me with goodness and the action thereof, and the fear of You by night and by day as long as You keep me alive, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, whenever I say that I have prepared and equipped myself, and stood for prayer before You, and whispered to You, You cast upon me drowsiness when I pray, and You deprive me of my intimate conversation when I whisper to You. Why is it that whenever I say my inner self has become righteous and my seat has drawn near to the seats of the repentant, a calamity befalls me that causes my feet to slip and comes between me and Your service, my Master? Perhaps You have driven me away from Your door and removed me from Your service. Or perhaps You saw me taking Your rights lightly and cast me aside. Or perhaps You saw me turning away from You and despised me. Or perhaps You found me in the station of the liars and rejected me. Or perhaps You saw me ungrateful for Your blessings and deprived me. Or perhaps You missed me from the gatherings of the scholars and abandoned me. Or perhaps You saw me among the heedless and caused me to despair of Your mercy. Or perhaps You saw me frequenting the gatherings of the idle and left me among them. Or perhaps You did not like to hear my supplication and distanced me. Or perhaps You have punished me for my crime and my sin. Or perhaps You have recompensed me for my lack of shame before You. If You pardon, O my Lord, then You have long pardoned the sinners before me, for Your generosity, O my Lord, is too great to recompense the negligent. I am returning by Your grace, fleeing from You to You, seeking the fulfillment of what You have promised of pardon for those who think well of You. My God, You are of more vast grace and greater forbearance than to measure me by my deeds or to humiliate me for my sin. And what am I, my Master, and what is my worth? Grant me by Your grace, my Master, bestow upon me Your pardon, cover me with Your veil, and overlook my rebuke by the generosity of Your countenance, my Master, my Master. I am the small one whom You raised, the ignorant one whom You taught, the lost one whom You guided, the lowly one whom You raised, the fearful one whom You made secure, the hungry one whom You fed, the thirsty one whom You quenched, the naked one whom You clothed, the poor one whom You enriched, the weak one whom You strengthened, the humiliated one whom You honored, the sick one whom You healed, the seeker whom You gave, the sinner whom You covered, the wrongdoer whom You forgave, the few whom You made many, the oppressed whom You helped, and the outcast whom You sheltered. I am, O my Lord, the one who did not feel shy before You in private, and did not watch over You in public. I am the owner of the great calamities. I am the one who dared against his Master. I am the one who disobeyed the Compeller of the heavens. I am the one who gave bribes for the sins of the Majestic. I am the one who, when I was given the good news of them, went out seeking them. I am the one whom You gave respite, yet I did not take heed; You covered me, yet I did not feel shy; I committed sins and transgressed; and You cast me out of Your sight, yet I did not care. So by Your forbearance, You gave me respite, and by Your covering, You concealed me, until it was as if You had overlooked me, and from the punishments of sins You kept me, until it was as if You were shy of me. My God, I did not disobey You when I disobeyed You while denying Your Lordship, nor taking Your command lightly, nor exposing myself to Your punishment, nor being heedless of Your threat. But a sin occurred, and my soul seduced me, and my desire overcame me, and my wretchedness helped me against it, and Your veil stretched over me deceived me. So I have disobeyed You and opposed You with my effort. So now, who will rescue me from Your punishment, and who will deliver me from the hands of the adversaries tomorrow? And by what rope shall I hold if You cut Your rope from me? So what a disgrace is upon what my book records of deeds, which, were it not for what I hope of Your generosity, the vastness of Your mercy, and Your forbidding me from despair, I would have despaired when I remembered it. O Best of those who are called upon, and Most Excellent of those who are hoped for. O Allah, by the covenant of Islam I seek a means to You, and by the sanctity of the Quran I rely upon You, and by the love of the unlettered, Qurayshi, Hashimi, Arab, Tihami, Meccan, Medinan Prophet, I hope for closeness to You. So do not make my faith a cause for my destruction, and do not make my reward the reward of one who worshipped other than You. For there is a people who believed with their tongues so that they might protect their blood, and they attained what they hoped for. And we have believed in You with our tongues and our hearts so that You may pardon us, so let us attain what we have hoped for, and establish Your hope in our hearts, and do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed, You are the Bestower. So by Your might, if You were to drive me away, I would not depart from Your door, nor would I cease my flattery, because of the knowledge my heart has of Your generosity and the vastness of Your mercy. To whom does the servant flee except to his Master? And to whom does the creature take refuge except to his Creator? My God, if You were to bind me in shackles, and prevent me from Your bounty among the witnesses, and point out my scandals to the eyes of the servants, and command me to the Fire, and stand between me and the righteous, I would not cut off my hope in You, nor would I turn away my expectation of Your pardon, nor would Your love depart from my heart. I do not forget Your favors upon me and Your covering of me in the abode of the world. My Master, remove the love of the world from my heart, and join me with the Chosen One and his family, the best of Your creation and the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family. And transfer me to the degree of repentance to You, and help me by weeping for myself, for I have wasted my life with excuses and hopes, and I have descended to the station of those who despair of goodness. So who is in a worse state than me if I am transferred in my current state to my grave, which I have not prepared for my rest, and have not furnished with righteous deeds for my comfort? And why should I not weep, and I do not know what my destination will be, and I see my soul deceiving me, and my days fighting me, and the wings of death have fluttered over my head? So why should I not weep? I weep for the departure of my soul, I weep for the darkness of my grave, I weep for the narrowness of my niche, I weep for the questioning of Munkar and Nakir of me, I weep for my exit from my grave, naked, humiliated, carrying my burden on my back, looking once to my right and another to my left, while the creatures are in a state other than my state. Each person among them that day will have a concern that occupies him. Faces that day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing, and faces that day will have dust upon them, covered by darkness and humiliation. My Master, upon You is my reliance, my trust, my hope, and my confidence, and upon Your mercy is my attachment. You strike with Your mercy whom You will, and You guide with Your generosity whom You love. And to You is the praise for what You have purified my heart from polytheism. And to You is the praise for the loosening of my tongue. So with this tongue of mine, shall I thank You, or with the utmost of my effort in my deeds, shall I strive? And what is the worth of my tongue, O my Lord, compared to Your gratitude? And what is the worth of my deed compared to Your blessings and Your benevolence? My God, Your generosity has expanded my hope, and Your gratitude has accepted my deed. My Master, to You is my neck, to You is my fear, to You is my expectation, and my deed has driven me to You. And upon You, O my One, my ambition has stopped, and in what is with You, my desire has expanded. And to You is my sincere hope and fear, and in You my love has found comfort, and to You I have cast my hand, and by the rope of Your obedience I have extended my fear. O my Master, by Your remembrance my heart has lived, and by Your intimate conversation the heat of fear has cooled from me. So, O my Master, O my Hope, and O the ultimate of my request, separate between me and my sin that prevents me from reaching Your obedience. For I only ask You because of my ancient hope in You and the greatness of my expectation of You, which You have made incumbent upon Yourself of compassion and mercy. So the command is Yours alone, there is no partner for You, and the creation is all Your dependents, in Your grasp, and everything is submissive to You. Blessed are You, O Lord of the worlds. My God, have mercy on me when my argument is cut off, and my tongue fails to answer You, and my mind is confused when You question me, O my Lord. So, O my Great Hope, do not disappoint me when my need intensifies, and do not reject me for my ignorance, and do not punish me for my lack of patience. Give me for my poverty, and have mercy on me for my weakness. My Master, upon You is my trust, my reliance, my hope, and my confidence, and upon Your mercy is my attachment. At Your courtyard I have cast my luggage, and by Your generosity I seek my goal, and by Your kindness, O my Lord, I open my supplication, and with You I hope for my need, and by Your wealth I mend my poverty, and under the shadow of Your pardon is my standing, and to Your generosity and kindness I raise my sight, and to Your benevolence I direct my gaze. So do not burn me with the Fire, for You are the object of my hope, and do not lodge me in the abyss, for You are the coolness of my eyes. O my Master, do not belie my opinion of Your benevolence and kindness, for You are my trust. And do not deprive me of Your reward, for You are the Knower of my poverty. My God, if my sin has drawn near and my deed has not brought me near to You, then I have made the confession to You of my sin my means to You. My God, if You pardon, then who is more worthy than You of pardon? And if You punish, then who is more just than You in judgment? Have mercy in this world on my loneliness, and at the time of death on my closeness, and in the grave on my solitude, and in the niche on my desolation, and when I am resurrected for the reckoning, on the humiliation of my standing. So forgive me what was hidden from the human beings of my deed, and make lasting for me what You have covered me with. And have mercy on me quickly on the bed as the hands of my loved ones turn me, and favor me with kindness as my righteous neighbors turn me on the washing place, and be compassionate to me as the relatives take me and the sides of my funeral, and be generous... To whom have I turned, having descended to You alone in my grave? And You have had mercy on my loneliness in that new house, so that I may not find comfort in anyone but You. My Master, if You entrust me to myself, I will perish. My Master, to whom shall I cry for help if You do not forgive my stumbling? To whom shall I attribute my affairs if I lose Your care in my resting place? To whom shall I take refuge if You do not relieve my distress? My Master, who is there for me, and who will have mercy on me if You do not have mercy on me? Whose bounty shall I hope for if I am deprived of Your bounty on the day of my need? To whom shall I turn for my sins when my term ends? My Master, do not punish me while I am hoping in You. My God, fulfill my hope and secure my fear, for You will remove me [from this world], and I hope for nothing in it except Your pardon. My Master, I ask You for what I do not deserve, and You are the Lord of piety and the Lord of forgiveness, so forgive me and clothe me with a garment from Your sight that covers my transgressions, and forgive them for me, and do not hold me accountable for them. Indeed, You are the Possessor of ancient grace, great pardon, and generous forgiveness. My God, You are the One who pours out Your bounty upon those who do not ask You, and even upon those who deny Your Lordship; so how, my Master, will You treat one who has asked You and is certain that creation belongs to You and the command is Yours? Blessed and Exalted are You, O Lord of the worlds. My Master, Your servant is at Your door, brought before You by his need, reading the door of Your benevolence with his supplication. So do not turn Your generous face away from me, and accept from me what I say, for I have called upon You with this supplication, hoping that You will not turn me away, out of my knowledge of Your kindness and mercy. My God, You are the One whom no petitioner exhausts, and no giver diminishes. You are as You say, and above what we say. O Allah, I ask You for beautiful patience, near relief, truthful speech, and a great reward. I ask You, O my Lord, for all goodness, what I know of it and what I do not know. I ask You, O Allah, for the best of what Your righteous servants have asked You for. O Best of those who are asked and Most Generous of those who give, grant me my request regarding myself, my family, my parents, my children, my loved ones, and my brothers in You. Make my life pleasant, manifest my honor, rectify all my conditions, and make me among those whose life You have lengthened, whose deeds You have improved, upon whom You have perfected Your blessing, with whom You are pleased, and whom You have given a good life in the most lasting joy, the most abundant honor, and the most perfect living. Indeed, You do what You will, and no one else does what they will. O Allah, single me out with the specialness of Your remembrance, and do not make anything of what I use to draw near to You in the hours of the night and the ends of the day a matter of showing off, or seeking reputation, or pride, or arrogance, and make me among the humble before You. O Allah, grant me abundance in provision, security in my homeland, coolness of eyes in my family, wealth, and children, stability in the blessings You have bestowed upon me, health in my body, strength in my physique, and safety in my religion. Employ me in Your obedience and the obedience of Your Messenger, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), as long as You employ me, and make me among the most fortunate of Your servants in every good You have sent down and will send down in the month of Ramadan, on the Night of Decree, and what You send down every year of mercy that You spread, well-being that You clothe, calamity that You repel, good deeds that You accept, and evil deeds that You overlook. Grant me the Hajj to Your Sacred House in this year of ours and in every year, and grant me wide provision from Your vast bounty. Turn away from me, O my Master, all evils, and settle my debts and grievances so that I am not burdened by any of them. Take charge for me against the ears and eyes of my enemies, my enviers, and those who transgress against me, and grant me victory over them. Cool my eyes, gladden my heart, and grant me relief and a way out from my worries and distress. Place those who wish me evil from among all Your creation under my feet. Suffice me against the evil of Satan, the evil of the ruler, and the evils of my own deeds. Purify me from all sins and save me from the Fire. by Your pardon, and enter me into Paradise by Your mercy. Marry me to the Houris by Your grace, and join me with Your righteous friends, Muhammad and his family, the pious, the pure, the clean, the chosen—Your blessings be upon them, their bodies, and their souls, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. My God and my Master, by Your might and Your majesty, if You hold me accountable for my sins, I will hold You accountable for Your pardon. If You hold me accountable for my baseness, I will hold You accountable for Your generosity. And if You enter me into the Fire, I will inform the people of the Fire of my love for You. My God and my Master, if You do not forgive anyone except Your friends and the people of Your obedience, then to whom shall the sinners return? And if You do not honor anyone except those who are faithful to You, then from whom shall the evildoers seek help? My God, if You enter me into the Fire, that would be the joy of Your enemy, and if You enter me into Paradise, that would be the joy of Your Prophet. And I, by Allah, know that the joy of Your Prophet is more beloved to You than the joy of Your enemy. O Allah, I ask You to fill my heart with love for You, fear of You, belief in Your Book, faith in You, awe of You, and longing for You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Make meeting You beloved to me, and love meeting me, and grant me in meeting You rest, relief, and honor. O Allah, join me with the righteous who have passed, make me among the righteous who remain, take me on the path of the righteous, and help me against my own soul with that which You help the righteous against their souls. Seal my deeds with the best of them, and make my reward for them Paradise by Your mercy. Help me with the good things You have given me, keep me steadfast, O Lord, and do not return me to an evil from which You have saved me, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for faith that has no end before meeting You. Keep me alive as long as You keep me alive upon it, take my soul when You take it upon it, and resurrect me when You resurrect me upon it. Clear my heart of showing off, doubt, and seeking reputation in Your religion so that my deeds may be sincere to You. O Allah, grant me insight into Your religion, understanding of Your judgment, jurisprudence in Your knowledge, a double portion of Your mercy, and piety that restrains me from Your disobedience. Whiten my face with Your light, make my desire for what is with You, and take my soul in Your path and upon the creed of Your Messenger (s.a.w.a.). O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness, failure, anxiety, cowardice, stinginess, heedlessness, hardness of heart, destitution, poverty, need, every calamity, and indecencies, both apparent and hidden. I seek refuge in You from a soul that is not satisfied, a stomach that is not filled, a heart that does not humble itself, a supplication that is not heard, and a deed that does not benefit. I seek refuge in You, O Lord, for my soul, my religion, my wealth, and for everything You have provided me, from the accursed Satan. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. O Allah, no one can protect me from You, and I find no refuge other than You. So do not place my soul in any of Your punishment, do not return me to destruction, and do not return me to a painful torment. O Allah, accept from me, exalt my mention, raise my degree, remove my burden, do not remember me for my sin, and make my reward the reward of the assembly, the reward of the speech, the reward of the prayer of Razzaq, and Paradise. And grant me, O Lord, everything I have asked for, and increase me from Your bounty, for I am longing for You, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, You have revealed in Your Book that You pardon those who have wronged us, and we have wronged our own souls, so pardon us, for You are more worthy of that than we are. You have commanded us not to turn away a petitioner from our doors, and I have come to You as a petitioner, so do not turn me away except by fulfilling my need. You have commanded us to be kind to those whom our right hands possess, and we are Your servants, so free our necks from the Fire. O my refuge at the time of my distress, and O my helper at the time of my hardship, to You I have cried out, and in You I have sought help. I do not take refuge in anyone else, and I do not seek relief from anyone but You. So help me and relieve me, O You who unbind the prisoner, O You who pardon the many, accept from me the little, and pardon from me the much. Indeed, You are the Merciful, the Forgiving. O Allah, I ask You for faith that touches my heart, and certainty until I know that nothing will afflict me except what You have written for me, and make me content with the life You have divided for me. O Most Merciful of the merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief.

title: Azaadaari Par Kharch Karne Ka Sawaab [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual rewards of spending wealth for the sake of Azadari (mourning) for Imam Hussein (a.s.). It references divine promises made to Prophet Musa regarding the blessings of feeding others in the name of the Imam and the merit of shedding tears for his tragedy. The speaker emphasizes that the true purpose of a Shia is to support the Ahlulbayt through financial sacrifice and emotional connection in their grief and happiness.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon al-Hussein, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussein, and upon the children of al-Hussein, and upon the companions of al-Hussein. Allah the Almighty revealed to Hazrat Musa (a.s.) saying: 'O Musa, if any of My servants, out of love for the grandson of My Prophet, i.e., Imam Hussein (a.s.), feeds others from his wealth or performs any such act, if he spends even one dirham, I will make it so blessed that I will turn that one dirham into seventy dirhams, and that servant will enter Paradise with safety and protection. I will forgive all his sins. By My honor and majesty, if any man or woman sheds a tear in grief for Imam Hussein (a.s.) on the day of Ashura or any other day, even if it is just a single drop, the reward of one hundred martyrs is written for them.' Furthermore, our Master and Mawla, Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), stated: 'Indeed, Allah the Almighty looked towards the earth and chose us, and for us, He chose our Shias who will help us, will be happy in our happiness, will be grieved in our grief, and will spend their wealth and sacrifice their lives for us.' They are from us and will return to us. In this Hadith, it is as if the Master is giving us a message that Allah created the Shias only so that they would spend everything they have on the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So, when everything we have is for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then if we spent some of it on the Azadari (mourning) of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, it means we have fulfilled the purpose of our creation to some extent. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He expands our hearts, removes all kinds of stinginess from our hearts, grants us the ability to sacrifice everything we have for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), and does not include us among those who object to Azadari. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.
