title: EP05 | Imam Kaun Hai? |  ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological significance of Imamate, emphasizing that it is a divine appointment rather than a human selection. It highlights the central role of the Ahlul-Bayt as the source of spiritual guidance and the essential foundation for the unity and order of the Ummah. The discourse further warns against the consequences of enmity toward the Ahlul-Bayt, stressing that true devotion requires both intellectual recognition and moral alignment with their teachings.
content:
TSR presents. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Let us see who the winners are from the first quiz, i.e., from episode number one to episode number four of 'Itam-e-Hujjat'. Their names are on your screen. Tooba Rizvi from Faizabad, Sayyeda Kirdar Fatima from Alipur, Razmi Fatima from Bengaluru, Jasmine Zahra from Bengaluru, Daleer Haider from Bangalore Alipur, Insha Naqvi from Allahabad, Sayyeda Afshana Bano from Bengaluru, Qissa Syed from Rustampura, Hussain Agha from Delhi, Mir Yadgar Ali from Alipur, Farhat Fatima Bujani from Bhavnagar, Sayyeda Shaista Bano from Bangalore, Syed Ruhullah from Chikka Ballapur, Asma Rizvi from Mumbai. Congratulations to all of you. Now let us move on to today's episode. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum wal an a'dahum ajma'in. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan, wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahummaj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi, wa khuddamihi wa atba'ihi, wa la taj'alna min a'da'ihi, bihaqqi Muhammadin wa alihi at-tahirin. Amma ba'd, faqad qala Mawlana al-Imam ar-Rida (a.s.), 'Innal imamata ussul islaminnami wa far'uhussami.' Sadaqa Mawlana al-Imam ar-Rida (a.s.). Before the translation and explanation of the Hadith, I would like to state again that if you have any questions regarding these lectures—that is, the topic of Imamate that is being discussed, has been discussed, or will be discussed—or any questions regarding Imamate in your mind, you can send that question to The Strong Rope's WhatsApp number. God willing, we will try to answer it. And regardless of the sect—whether Shia, Sunni, Deobandi, whoever—anyone who wants to ask a question can ask, and God willing, we will try to answer it. Wa ma tawfiqi illa billah. Anyway, this narration that I presented to you is from Imam Rida (a.s.): 'Innal imamata ussul islaminnami wa far'uhussami.' What is Imamate? Imamate is the foundation of Islam. 'Ussul Islam', 'Uss' is derived from 'Asas'. Asas means foundation. Imamate is the foundation of Islam. 'Annami' means that which causes the growth of Islam, from which Islam grows. 'Numu' means growth. 'Wa far'uhussami' and its branch is... what is Imamate? 'Far'', 'Far'' means branch. It is the branch of Islam, which is a very lofty branch. So Imamate is that which is both the root and the branch. Imamate is both things. Is it clear? Meaning its importance is so significant, so great, that we cannot estimate it. That is why in the school of Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), not everyone can become an Imam. Or people do not have the authority to appoint an Imam on their own. People do not have the authority to do so. Whether it is by any method—election, selection, Shura, whatever name you give it, Ahl al-Hall wal-Aqd, anything—people are not allowed to appoint their own Imam. This selection, this appointment is only and only from Allah. Just as the selection of a Prophet and Messenger is from Allah, the selection and appointment of an Imam is also from Allah. Because Imamate is a divine position. As I mentioned in the previous lectures, this is a divine position. It is not like we can just select any person, so we select him. No, it is not like that. This is religion, this is faith, this is not a game. So look at what the Imam says. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'Nahnu aslu kulli khayr.' We, the Ahlul-Bayt, meaning we, the Infallible Imams (a.s.), are the root of every goodness. Every goodness, meaning whatever goodness there is, it will originate from us. We will be its cause. Whatever goodness is in the world, the root of goodness. 'Wa min furu'ina kullu birr.' And from our branches is every virtue. All the goodness, all the goodness that is seen in the world, is a branch, an offshoot of Imamate. 'Famina al-birr' and from this virtue is... 'At-Tawhid'. Tawhid, meaning true Tawhid. Not the Tawhid where Allah has a body or resembles a body, or that Allah will show Himself to you on the Day of Judgment—how He will show Himself, we don't know, but it will be that Allah is a body—no. If you look here, in the light of the Quran and narrations, it is impossible for anyone to see Allah. With these eyes, meaning with physical eyes, it is impossible to see Him, neither in this world nor in the hereafter. Never. Yes, a human finds Allah with the eyes of the heart, that is a different matter. So, 'At-Tawhid' means true Tawhid. 'Was-Salat' means prayer, meaning correct prayer. 'Was-Siyam' means fasting, meaning correct fasting. 'Wa kasb al-ghayz' and suppressing anger. 'Wal-'afwu 'anil-musi'i'—these are all virtues that the Imam is counting. And forgiving the sinner, pardoning him. The sinner who has made a mistake, committed a fault, to forgive him. This is a sign of a follower of the Ahlul-Bayt. A person who remains stubborn on his point and does not forgive anyone, does not pardon anyone, cannot be a follower of the Ahlul-Bayt. He can be anything, but he cannot be a follower of the Ahlul-Bayt. 'Wa rahmatu al-faqir' meaning to have mercy on the poor, to have mercy on the needy. These are among the virtues. Look, how much the Imam has included in one comprehensive Hadith. Meaning, those who are followers of the Ahlul-Bayt, those who are the Shia of the Ahlul-Bayt, must have these qualities. 'Wa ta'ahhud al-jar' and take care of the neighbors. Take care of the neighbor. 'Wal-iqrar bil-fadli li-ahlihi' and acknowledge the virtue of those who are worthy of virtue. Meaning, consider the superior as superior and the inferior as inferior. It should not be the other way around, that we know this one is superior, so we make him inferior, and make the inferior superior. So that is the issue. 'These are also good, those are also good, what a temperament they have found. They have decorated flowers with thorns in the vases.' Meaning, everyone is good. It is said, 'Who is this?' It is said, 'This is the killer, who is this? The victim.' They say 'Radiyallahu' for their names, and 'Radiyallahu' for their names too. Oh, how did this happen, brother? They say, 'No brother, you have to respect everyone, we have to respect everyone.' Okay, right? So it is not like that. Or, for example, Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili, in the introduction to his commentary on Nahj al-Balagha, in the sermon he writes, 'All praise is for Allah who preferred the inferior over the superior.' Meaning, he preferred the inferior over the superior. Allah did it. Meaning, an ordinary sensible person, who is just ordinary, would not do this, but Allah did it. Meaning, you understand the example of this, that if in a class, say there are 30 children in the class, and one child came first, and one child who came 30th in the class of 30 children, so you are giving the prize to the 30th child in the prize distribution, 'Well done, son, first prize for the 30th.' Oh, at least he came from the back. Is it clear? Meaning, this is an insult to intellect. This is an insult to intellect. This cannot be religion, this is not religion, this kind of religion cannot be. 'Wa aduwwuna' and now after that the Imam says, 'And our enemy...' The root of all evil. Our enemies are the root of every evil. And among their branches is every abomination, every evil thing, and every indecency (fahisha); indecency, evil, all of this is their branch. And what are they? Lying, bukhl (meaning stinginess, miserliness). And nameema (meaning backbiting, complaining). Right? And qati' (meaning severing ties of kinship). Meaning, those who love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will not have any of these things. Those who love the Ahlulbayt will never have these things. And consuming usury (riba). And consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly. This meaning of consuming the orphan's wealth, as it is in the traditions, is as follows: 'Whoever consumes anything from our wealth, he is only consuming fire into his belly and will burn in a blazing fire.' This tradition is from the Imam of the Time (a.s.) himself. That whoever consumes even an atom's weight of our wealth, he is taking fire into his belly and will remain in it forever. This is the interpretation of that verse of the Quran where the Quran says about those who consume the wealth of orphans, 'Alladhina yakuluna amwalal yatama zulma.' They consume it unjustly. 'Innama yakuluna fi butunihim nara wa sayaslawna sa'ira.' They are consuming fire into their bellies and will burn in a blazing fire. And will burn in a blazing fire. Soon they will be cast into the fire. So, what does the Imam say in the interpretation of this verse? 'Whoever consumes anything from our wealth.' That is, whoever consumes from the Sahm-e-Imam (Imam's share) unjustly, when he is not in need, he is not entitled to it. But he is consuming it unjustly, he is consuming it. 'Then he is only consuming fire into his belly and will be cast into the fire, the fire of Hell.' And after that, he says, 'And transgressing the limits that Allah has commanded.' Meaning rights, meaning transgressing the boundaries, meaning crossing the limits that Allah has set, meaning committing sins. Any sin that Allah has set. 'And committing indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden.' And committing indecencies, evils, sins, whether they are manifest or hidden, whether they are open or concealed. A person should abstain from all kinds of indecent things. And zina (adultery, fornication), and sariqa (theft). Whether it is a small theft or a big theft. A person cannot touch another's property without permission. Those who love the Ahlulbayt will never have these things in them. And everything that is considered evil. And whatever evil of this kind there is, those who love the Ahlulbayt stay away from it, and whoever does it will be included in the list of enemies. Whoever does all these things will be included in the list of enemies. After that, the Imam says a sentence, 'So he lies, the one who claims that he is with us.' So that person lies who claims or assumes that he is with us, meaning he is our lover, our Shia, our follower. 'While he is attached to the branches of others.' While his actions are those that are the actions of our enemies. The actions of the outsiders, the deeds of others, he is performing all of them. He cannot be our Shia. Meaning our Shia is one in whom all these qualities, all these characteristics are found. Anyway, so what is the Imam? The Imam is the Nizam-ul-Ummah (the system of the Ummah). The Imam is the system of the Ummah. The Imam is holding the Ummah together. Meaning organized, meaning what is 'nazm' (order)? Nazm is like poetry. Like you say, in a verse there is a radif and a qafiya. Meaning things are connected equally. They are connected to each other. Because of the Imam, the Ummah is organized. If there is no Imam, the Ummah will scatter. If the Imam is not followed, if the Imam is not followed as he should be followed, then the Ummah will scatter. Therefore, following the Imam is very important. And this Muslim Ummah today has split into so many sects, and whatever is happening to it, whatever problems, whatever trouble, the only reason for this is that the Muslim Ummah, those who call themselves Muslims, who call themselves the Ummah of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they have left the hem of the successor of the Messenger of Allah, meaning Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). They have left the Ahlulbayt of the Messenger. Meaning there are many who claim that we also love them, we also, but actually they do not follow those traditions. How many hadiths do you follow, how much do you believe in them? That is a separate debate, Insha'Allah if Allah ever gives the opportunity. Then Imam Reza (a.s.) says, 'Indeed, the Imamate is the zimam (rein) of the religion.' Imamate is the rein of the religion, zimam means rein. Rein means that which controls the religion. Meaning if, if the Imam is left behind, then a person's religion will be completely without any control. He will follow the religion as he wishes, he will do anything, whatever comes to his mind, whatever his heart desires, he will follow the religion like that. Without the Imam, the religion will be like this. That one believes in something else, the second believes in something else, the third believes in something else, the fourth believes in something else. There is no account at all. And everyone is also declaring each other as kafir (takfir), calling each other kafir, calling each other mushrik. This one is a mushrik, that one is a mushrik, that one is a mushrik, all are mushriks. The result is that all, all Muslims are mushriks. 'Wa nizamul muslimeen.' And what is the Imam? The system of the Muslims, meaning the Imam is holding the Muslims together, binding them, keeping them one. Meaning the Imam, 'Wa hablillahil matin.' He is the strong rope of Allah, about whom it has been commanded, 'Hold fast to the rope of Allah all together and do not be divided.' Look, hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not be scattered. Do not leave it. Whoever left the Imam, he has left the strong rope of Allah. In the context of this verse, there is a tradition, both sides (Sunni and Shia) have narrated it. That in the context of this verse, the Prophet said, who is the strong rope of Allah? Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And as it is in Hadith-e-Saqalayn, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things, the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahlulbayt, as long as you hold fast to them.' As long as you hold fast to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, 'You will never go astray after me, never go astray.' 'For they will never separate from each other until they return to me at the Pond (Hawd).' Meaning returning means both will come and the Prophet will accept them, and those who have held fast to both will be accepted. And those who left them, then about them there is a tradition in Bukhari. It is present in Bukhari. That some people will come on the Day of Judgment and will try to enter the Pond, then the angels will beat them with sticks and drive them away. So the Prophet, this is a tradition of Bukhari, the Prophet will say, 'O my Lord, my companions, my companions.' But he will say these are my companions. Why are they being driven away? So from the Prophet, this is a tradition of Bukhari, then it will be said that you do not know what they did after you. Allahu Akbar. So on one hand, it is said that 'My companions are like stars, if you follow any one of them, you will be guided.' This hadith was fabricated, fabricated and put into books. So if this is the outcome, then may God have mercy, brother. May God have mercy. Otherwise, they will not be allowed to come to the Pond of Kawthar, they will be driven away. Look, this tradition of Bukhari, we are not saying it. We are not saying it. 'Wa salahud dunya' (and the welfare of the world), and through Imamate, there is also the betterment of a person's world. Meaning the betterment, welfare, and success of people in the world can only be through the Imam. That the right way, what is called success in the world? Meaning a person should use the world in the right way. So that he, he gets the hereafter. Like the verse of the Quran in Surah Qasas, 'And seek in that which Allah has given you the home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of the world.' This world was made by Allah for His worship. This world was made by Allah so that people may prostrate to Him. This world was made by Allah so that it may be a farm, a field for the hereafter. That is why Allah made it. The world is the farm of the hereafter. And what is Imamate? The honor of the believers. Imamate is a cause of honor for the believers. Whoever held the hem of the Imam, whoever it is, he will be a cause of honor. He will be honored. Honor in the world, honor in the hereafter. And whoever left the hem of the Imam, by Imam, it means those twelve Imams. The first of them is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and the last of them is the Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). These are the twelve Imams. And especially in today's time, it is the Imam of the Time. The twelfth Imam (a.t.f.s.) and we are with him. It is the Imam of the Time. 'Whoever dies and does not know the Imam of his time, he dies the death of ignorance.' Whoever died and did not recognize his Imam of the time, meaning did not submit to him, then he died the death of ignorance. He died the death of kufr, hypocrisy, and misguidance. It is the death of hypocrisy. He did not recognize the Imam of the time, he is not submitting to the Imam of the time. What is the benefit of his life? That is why Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'And our love, the Ahlulbayt, is the system of religion.' It is the system of religion. There is a verse of the Quran, Surah Furqan, verse number 57. Qul ma as'alukum 'alayhi min ajrin illa man sha'a an yattakhidha ila rabbihi sabila. Say, O Prophet, tell them, I do not ask you for any reward for my prophethood, for my message. Except for the one who wants to take a path to his Lord. To go towards Allah. 'Illa man sha'a an yattakhidha ila rabbihi sabila.' Meaning take, 'ila rabbihi sabila.' Meaning follow the path that Allah has determined. This is the reward, this is the reward. Apart from this, I do not want any other reward. Just follow the path that Allah has made. And I do not want any reward. Who is this, who is this path? This is what we read in Dua-e-Nudba. In Dua-e-Nudba, which should be recited every Friday and every, meaning every Eid. Recite this dua every Friday and every Eid. Dua-e-Nudba, which is narrated from the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) himself. 'Wa kanu humus sabila ilayk.' The Ahlulbayt are the path to You. Which is the path that leads to You, meaning O Allah, the path that leads to You, the Ahlulbayt are that path. Wal maslaka ila ridwanik. And it is the path, it is the way that leads to Your pleasure. That with which Allah becomes pleased. So the reward will be for the one who held the hem of the Ahlulbayt. And the pleasure from Allah is greater, and this is the greatest thing. He has the right. And that is why it is found in the tradition that 'Allah will not accept the deed of a servant while he doubts us.' Whoever doubts us. Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) says, 'Hold fast to our love, the Ahlulbayt.' Look, become bound to our love and affection, the Ahlulbayt. Hold it firmly. 'By Him in whose hand is my soul,' meaning Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) narrates this from whom? He narrates from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). That the Messenger of Allah said, 'Love my Ahlulbayt. Hold fast to the love of my Ahlulbayt. Because by Allah, no servant's deed will benefit him unless he has the recognition of our right.' Unless he knows the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And this is the truth. There is no other truth besides this. 'Aliyun ma'al haqqi wal haqqu ma'a Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali). 'Allahumma adilil haqqa haithuma dara' (O Allah, turn the truth wherever Ali turns). All these traditions are present in Sheikh al-Mufid's 'Al-Amali'. If anyone wishes, they can refer to it. Just the final hadith, that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Wa law anna rajulan salla wa saffa qadamayhi baynar rukni wal maqam' (And if a man were to pray and stand with his feet together between the Rukn and the Maqam). If a man prays so much, as much as he can, between the Rukn and the Maqam—Maqam meaning Maqam-e-Ibrahim and Rukn meaning the corner of the Kaaba—and he prays a lot with his feet joined, and performs a lot of worship. He is a great worshipper, a Haji, obviously, if he is going there, he is going for Hajj. He is a Haji, he is worshipping, he is doing everything. But 'wa laqiyallaha bibughdikum' (and he meets Allah while having hatred for you), if he dies in a state where there is hatred for the Ahl al-Bayt in his heart—hatred—he will enter the Fire. 'Laqiyallaha bibughdikum ahlal bayti dakhalan nar' (He meets Allah while having hatred for the Ahl al-Bayt, he will enter the Fire). That is it. Now, how to know if there is hatred? It is absolutely clear, you can see for yourself. A person follows the one they love. And the one they hate, they celebrate on the day of their murder. They celebrate with joy. Now you see who mourns on the day of Ashura and who celebrates. From this, you will know. The truth will be separated from the falsehood. Making a claim is one thing. But if we are celebrating on the day of Ashura and holding weddings on the day of Ashura, then it means that we are happy. We are celebrating the martyrdom and the murder of the Ahl al-Bayt. And we have to answer to the Messenger of Allah. So, you will have to answer to the Messenger of Allah, Insha'Allah Ta'ala. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Nahj-ul-Balaagha Mein Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) ka Tazkera | Khutbaa 100
excerpt: This lecture explores Khutbah 100 of Nahj al-Balagha, where Imam Ali (a.s.) describes his own status as the 'banner of truth' and the necessity of adhering to his Wilayah. The speaker explains how the Imam warns of the turmoil that follows the neglect of divine leadership. Ultimately, the lecture highlights Imam Ali's prophecy regarding the eventual reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the one who will establish global unity and justice.
content:
The status of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his family. The Mawla says: 'All praise is for Allah, who is the one to bestow His grace upon the creation and the one who extends His hand through friendship among them. We praise Him in all His affairs and seek His help in fulfilling His rights. We bear witness that there is no god but Him, and that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent to manifest His command and to be the announcer of His remembrance. He (the Prophet) conveyed His messages with utmost honesty and departed from this world as a guide, leaving behind among us a banner of truth such that...' Leaving behind among us a banner of truth such that whoever goes ahead of it is cast out, whoever lags behind it is ruined, and whoever remains attached to it is with him. In this phrase, the 'banner of truth' refers to the noble personality of the Master of the Universe, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), because it was regarding him that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with Ali.' The truth turns wherever Ali turns. From this, the conclusion is drawn that whoever goes ahead of Ali is cast out, whoever lags behind in accepting Ali's leadership is ruined, and whoever remains attached to Ali's Wilayah is with the truth, because the truth is with Ali. And then the Mawla says, what is the proof that this banner of truth speaks? It stands with certainty, but when it acts, it does so with great speed. And then the Mawla, this banner of truth, describes himself to the people: 'But as long as you point your fingers at him in every matter, death will come to him and take him away, and then...' It will go and take it away, and then as long as Allah wills, you will remain in this state. These people will continue to wander in misguidance, turmoil, and trouble because they did not listen to the Prophet and did not accept the Wilayah, the leadership, and the Caliphate of the rightful successor, Ali (a.s.). This will continue until Allah brings forth the person who will gather you in one place and remove your waiting—that is, the Master of the Universe. In this phrase, the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) is pointing towards his reappearance, explaining that when Allah brings Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) to the public, it is only after this period of turmoil that unity will be established among the people, and that unity will be upon the Imamate of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). That is, Imam Mahdi (a.s.) himself will establish unity among the people and remove their waiting. That is why the Master (Ali a.s.) says: do not pin your hopes on anyone other than the one who is to come, and do not despair of the one who is leaving. This means a person should not place their hopes in anyone other than Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), because it is possible that the one who is leaving might be a temporary figure, but the next one will be steadfast. It is possible that one Imam may pass, but immediately upon his departure, another will come. Then, circumstances will arise where both will pass, and after that, the manifest government of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) will be established. Regarding the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), the Master (Ali a.s.) says: 'Know that the example of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) is like the stars; when one star sets, another rises.' Thus, Allah has perfected His blessings upon you and has taught you everything you were hoping for. Allah has stated all the signs of the reappearance; now, human hope should be attached only and solely to the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). O Master, Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), indeed my Master, Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), has spoken the truth. O God, I beseech You by the Master of the Universe and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Kin Logon Se Baraa'at Waajib Hai? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of Tabarra (disavowal) in Shia Islam, framing it as an essential branch of religion alongside prayer and fasting. The speaker references a tradition from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) found in 'Al-Khisal' to delineate who must be disassociated from, including historical oppressors of the Ahlulbayt and those who violated their rights. The talk emphasizes that practicing Bara'ah is a mandatory act of worship that will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us and do not let us perish. There have been different opinions among Shias regarding the subject of expressing disavowal (Tabarra) from the enemies of Allah the Almighty, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). However, the mention of the belief in Tabarra is present in numerous verses of the Holy Quran and Hadiths. Shia theologians and scholars have unanimously accepted that Tabarra is included in the branches of religion (Furu-e-Deen) just like prayer, fasting, Hajj, Khums, etc. That is, just as these acts are obligatory and are a cause for the pleasure of the Creator, Tabarra is exactly the same. Let us turn our attention to one such Hadith in which expressing disavowal from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) has been declared obligatory. Sheikh Saduq (may Allah have mercy on him) has narrated in his book 'Al-Khisal' from Al-A'mash that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Allahumma inna awliya'aka humul-fa'izun' (O Allah, indeed Your friends are the successful ones). The love of the Awliya (friends) of Allah is obligatory, and accepting their Wilayah is obligatory. Bara'ah (disassociation) from their enemies is also obligatory. It is obligatory to disassociate from those who oppressed the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), violated their sanctity, snatched Fadak from Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.), kept her away from her inheritance, usurped her and her husband's rights, gathered to burn down her house, laid the foundation of oppression, changed the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and from the Nakithin (those who broke their oath and came to Jamal), the Qasitin (the sinners who came to Siffin), and the Mariqin (the disbelievers of Nahrawan). It is also obligatory to disassociate from the Nasibis, the leaders of misguidance who shot arrows of oppression, and the guides of tyranny, from the first of them to the last. It is obligatory to disassociate from the first and the last of the wretched, including the one who killed the she-camel of Salih (a.s.), the killer of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and all the killers of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). In summary, whoever ignores Bara'ah from the enemies of Allah (s.w.t.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) has in fact opposed the Quran and Hadith and turned away from an obligatory act, about which they will certainly be questioned on the Day of Resurrection. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability to act upon this important duty until our last breath, and that this worship of Bara'ah remains established and lasting in our generations. Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 2 | Tafseer of the verse الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
excerpt: This lecture provides an exegesis of the phrase 'Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen' from Surah Al-Fatiha, drawing upon narrations from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). The speaker distinguishes between human mercy, which often arises from emotional distress, and the divine mercy of Allah. The session emphasizes the profound significance of expressing gratitude through the phrase 'Alhamdulillah' and encourages listeners to adopt it as a daily habit.
content:
Peace be upon you. I am present today with the exegesis of Surah Al-Hamd from the Holy Quran. May Allah make this month of Ramadan blessed; it will be my constant endeavor to provide the exegesis of the short Surahs we recite. In this series, I had explained the exegesis of 'Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim', and today I am continuing that discussion. The Lord of the Worlds is Rahman (Most Gracious), and His mercy encompasses the entire universe. But sometimes it happens that a person prays for relief from some trouble. There is a difference between human mercy and God's mercy. When the word 'mercy' is attributed to a human, and the word 'mercy' is used continuously... And the word 'mercy' is used continuously, it is given the name of generosity and benevolence. It refers to that which one bestows upon their loved ones. In humans, mercy arises when one sees someone in pain, in trouble, in suffering, or sees a sick or needy person; then the sentiment of sympathy arises within them. The sentiment of mercy and the sentiment of generosity arise, and their heart feels for their condition. And when the heart feels, the person bestows upon the human, and the observer says that so-and-so has removed the trouble, so-and-so has treated the sick, so-and-so has removed the distress of the troubled person, so-and-so has done this. This refers to the mercy that arises from a feeling of distress. It begins with a feeling of distress. As a result of this distress, it is attributed to Allah, but it does not include Him, because that mercy is with us, but it is not the creation of God. This is the difference between human mercy and God's mercy and generosity. And after that... now I am moving forward because the exegesis of Bismillah is complete. Regarding Surah Al-Hamd, there is a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that it contains four things; it is the light of Allah. If someone reaches it, they say 'Alhamdulillah'. He said that 'Alhamdulillah' is from the root of 'Al-Hamd'. He said that when one says 'Alhamdulillah', they have thanked God for His blessing and said that their habit... And said that it should be their habit. Whoever one meets, they should thank the Lord, even if it is just 'Alhamdulillah'. People say it, but it is very profound. You have said that Allah has thanked for a small blessing... and after the blessing, if one says 'Alhamdulillah', they have thanked for the blessing. The Imam (a.s.) is saying, whether it is small or large, but by saying 'Alhamdulillah', you have thanked for the blessing. What will you remember? If you say... if... Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) went out and his animal went missing from there... You said, 'O God, if God returns my riding animal, I will fulfill the complete right of thanking Him.' After a while, the animal was found, so you said 'Alhamdulillah'. I asked you, 'Did you not say that you would fulfill the right of thanking Allah?' Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) replied, 'Did you not hear me say Alhamdulillah? That is the complete thanks for the blessing.' There is another narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) regarding 'Alhamdulillah'. Its excellence is that it is thanks for Allah. 'Alhamdulillah' means the Creator of all creation... in the language of the heart... Imam (a.s.) says 'Alhamdulillah', Allah has... Allah has chosen it for His own right. Allah wanted that if our servant thanks us, then through this word, through 'Alhamdulillah', he should thank. It is related to the Lord of the Worlds, and then upon receiving news, one thanks. In the words 'Rabbul Alameen', there is nothing but the grace and generosity of Allah. There is another narration from the Prophet of Islam, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), let me convey it to you. He says that Allah did me a favor by revealing the Fatiha (the Opening) to me, and its verse 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alameen' is the greatest speech of Paradise. We recite it five times in our five daily prayers. We have to recite 'Alhamdulillah' first. You can understand the speech of the Lord... You have to recite it. That when God blessed us with the Fatiha, we say 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alameen'. 'Alhamdulillah' is... and there is a narration in the book of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that whoever says 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alameen' four times in the morning has thanked for his day, and whoever says this in the evening has thanked for his night. Let us make it a habit to recite this beyond our prayers so that we may be among the thankful. 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alameen'.

title: Allah Kaisa Hai? Imam Hasan (a.s.) Ka Jawaab
excerpt: In this lecture, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) provides a profound theological description of the nature of Allah in response to a seeker's request. The Imam emphasizes that Allah is beyond the limitations of time, space, division, and human intellect. He explains that Allah is the infinite Creator who exists outside the constraints of 'before' or 'after' and whose essence remains beyond the reach of human comprehension.
content:
A man came to Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) and said, 'Describe your Lord to me, and describe Him in such a way that it is as if I am looking at Him.' The narration says that the Imam bowed his head for a while, then raised it and said: 'All praise is due to Allah, for whom no beginning is known as to when He existed, nor is there any limit to His end; He is infinite. There is no thing by which it can be stated what He preceded, for "before" is not applicable to Him. Nor can it be said that He is after anything, for if He were said to be after something, He would be limited. There is no specific time for Him such that a person could say "until this time"; this cannot be said of Allah either. He is not a personality that can be divided into parts, nor can there be a discussion about His separate components. There is no contradiction in His attributes that would imply an end where the attribute ceases; there is no such thing. All His attributes are infinite. Intellect, with all its imagination, cannot perceive Him, nor can thought reach Him. One cannot discuss His attributes; so if one cannot discuss His attributes, how can one discuss the Essence of Allah? It cannot be said that He manifested upon something, nor can it be said that He is inside something. Allah created the creation; He initiated that which never existed before. And having initiated them, there is nothing like Him. Whatever He intends, He executes, and if He decides to increase something, He merely intends it, and the increase occurs; there is no gap. "Dhalikumullahu Rabbul-Alamin" (That is Allah, your Lord, the Lord of the Worlds).'
Allah is infinite, having no beginning and no end.
Concepts of 'before' and 'after' do not apply to the Creator.
Allah is not a composite being and cannot be divided into parts.
Human intellect and imagination are incapable of perceiving the Essence of Allah.
Allah is not contained within or manifested upon created things.
The creation of the universe occurred through Allah's immediate intention.
There is nothing comparable to Allah in existence.

title: Lecture 2: The Chosen Companions Of Imam Ali (a.s.) | Respected H. I. SAYED MAHDI MODARRESI
excerpt: This lecture by Sayed Mahdi Modarresi explores the lives, spiritual depth, and unwavering loyalty of the companions of Imam Ali (a.s.). It examines the Imam's profound wisdom, his struggles against political injustice, and the deep emotional connection between the Ahlulbayt and their followers. The discourse also highlights the significance of the Imam's foresight regarding future tragedies and the essential role of faith and humility in seeking salvation.

title: Aaj Musalmaan Pareshaan Kyun Hain? | Janaab-e-Salman-e-Muhammadi (a.r.) Ki Peshangoi
excerpt: This lecture explores the prophecy of Janab Salman al-Muhammadi regarding the state of the Muslim community. The speaker explains that the current humiliation and calamities faced by Muslims are a direct consequence of the historical rejection of the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). By choosing their own leadership over the divine appointment, the community forfeited the protection and unity that would have otherwise been guaranteed.
content:
So now, 'Abshiru bi-dhull' (I give you the glad tidings of humiliation). 'Basharat' usually refers to good news, but here Janab Salman is warning you: calamities will break upon you. Be alert! Do not keep any hope that you will find comfort. Humiliation and disgrace are now the destiny of the Muslims. Why? Because the Wilayah was rejected. History tells us that three days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the people abandoned Ali (a.s.) and chose their own Caliph. There is no doubt about the personality of Salman. If you were to signal to the birds flying in the sky, or if you were to call out to the fish in the sea, they would obey you. Those who accepted the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) would never be poor. There would never have been any disagreement between two people regarding any decision of Allah if the people had accepted the Wilayah. Salman further says: 'But what did you do? You rebelled, and what did you do with this Wilayah? By Allah, you have gone astray. You gave this authority into the hands of someone other than Ali (a.s.). So now, what will be the result? Now, 'Abshiru bi-dhull' (I give you the glad tidings of humiliation)...' What will be the result? 'Abshiru bi-dhull' (I give you the glad tidings of humiliation). 'Basharat' usually refers to good news, but here Janab Salman is warning you: calamities will break upon you. Be alert! Do not keep any hope that you will find comfort. We will keep fighting; that is, we will not sit silently. We will keep reminding you of the cause of your humiliation and disgrace—it is that very rejection. And finally, Salman says: '...and because of accepting this Wilayah, we used to protect one another. We are now withdrawing that protection from you. We will not come to save you anymore, because until yesterday, we were under the same Wilayah. We were both followers of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), so protecting each other's lives and property was our responsibility. But now, if troubles come to you, we will certainly not save you, because you are responsible for it yourself.'
Janab Salman al-Muhammadi warned of humiliation as a consequence of rejecting Wilayah.
The abandonment of Imam Ali (a.s.) shortly after the Prophet's death is the root cause of Muslim suffering.
True acceptance of Wilayah would have resulted in prosperity and unity.

Those who remain faithful to the Wilayah will no longer provide protection to those who rejected it.

title: EP23 | Ayat e Tatheer: Panjatan Ya Aur Bhi? | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi provides a detailed theological and linguistic analysis of the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tathir) in the Quran. The discussion focuses on the exclusivity of this verse to the Panjtan Pak (the Prophet Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn) and explores the nature of their divinely granted infallibility. Dr. Rizvi addresses common counter-arguments, specifically regarding the inclusion of the Prophet's wives, by distinguishing between the context of Quranic compilation and the original revelation.
content:
We present this. 'Ash-hadu anna Aliyan waliyullah'. It is inscribed on the Throne of God. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Hassan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers and assistants, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The discussion was about the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir). And first, in terms of authenticity, I presented to you traditions from the Sihah al-Sittah and the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, after which there remains no doubt regarding the chain of narration. I also provided a list of scholars who have narrated this Verse of Purification and the tradition revealed in its honor—the Hadith al-Kisa, as we call it. Although, with us, the Hadith al-Kisa is very detailed, while with them, it is very brief, and that is no surprise. Right? When they even cut the Salawat, then it is no surprise if they cut the hadith. They removed the 'Aal' (family) from the Salawat. So, likewise. The argument regarding the Verse of Purification was being discussed, specifically the word 'innama'. 'Innama' indicates that this honor is exclusively for the Ahl al-Bayt. And I submitted to you that this is a declaration of purity. It does not mean that, God forbid, they were not pure until now and have only now become pure. No, they were pure from the beginning. They were pure and clean from the beginning. Their purity is merely being declared so that the world may know that these Ahl al-Bayt are pure and clean from every kind of impurity, filth, dirt, sin, and all the evils and vices in the world. So, when 'innama'—this 'innama' is only for this incident. Because, look, people try to show that all the wives are included. I will prove to you that no, the wives are not included. There is not a single hadith anywhere that mentions the wives. So, look, there is a poem in Arabic. Many things have to be proven through literature. So, there is a verse in Arabic. It says that 'al-husnu yazharu fi shay'in raunaquhu'. Beauty manifests its splendor in two things. Meaning, something is beautiful, something is lovely, through two things. Meaning, 'al-husnu yazharu' (beauty manifests). 'Fi shay'in' (in two things). 'Raunaquhu' (its splendor). 'Baytun minash shi'ri wa baytun minash sha'ri'. Meaning, a 'bayt' (verse) of poetry. If you want to make speech beautiful, you add rhythm and poetry to it, and the speech becomes beautiful. Prose does not have the effect that poetry has. That is why rhythm is kept in speech to attract people. For beauty. And the second is 'baytun minash sha'ri' (a 'bayt' of hair). What is a 'bayt' of hair? A blanket. The blanket that is made of hair. The woolly blanket or cloak that is made of hair is considered very beautiful. It has great value. So, that is its splendor. It is clear, right? So, a blanket is also called a 'bayt' in Arabic. Therefore, Ahl al-Bayt means only those of the Kisa (cloak), that is all. Now, in history—in any tradition of both sects—show me one tradition where anyone other than these Panjtan (the five) has come. And for whom the Prophet said, 'Allahumma inna ha'ula'i ahli bayti wa khassatii' (O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt and my special ones). Is there anyone else besides them? No. Now, some people say, 'Well, even if we accept your point, this only proves the infallibility of the Panjtan. What about the rest of the Imams, from Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) to Imam al-Zaman (a.j.t.f.)?' So, Insha'Allah, we will discuss the details of this under the 'Ayat al-Wilayah' (Verse of Authority), Insha'Allah. So that the discussion there will be deep—a better discussion—because 'innama' also appears in the Ayat al-Wilayah. 'Innama' appears in both verses. Only and only. Meaning, Allah is repeatedly saying, 'Look, these are the only people.' Meaning, do not push anyone else here and there. So, they want to exclude the other Imams, but we will prove that they are not excluded. Anyway, Insha'Allah, the details will come later under the Ayat al-Wilayah, Surah Ma'idah, verse 55. Now, what is the next argument? It is the word 'irada' (will). 'Innama yuridullahu'. 'Yuridu' (He wills). 'Yuridu' means Allah is willing this. This is Allah's will. 'Innama yuridu'. This is a 'fi'l-e-muzare' (present tense verb) in Arabic. 'Innama yuridullahu'. Who is the one willing? Allah. Now, every Muslim who reads the Quran, who is familiar with the Quran, knows that there is absolutely no similarity between Allah's will and the will of His servants; they are completely distinct. When a servant wills, he thinks about how to do it, what to do, and whether he will succeed or not. But a Muslim who reads the Quran and is familiar with it knows what Allah's will is, which the Quran has mentioned. Allah says, 'Innama amruhu idha arada shay'an ay yaqula lahu kun fayakun' (His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is). Allah has just willed it. So, if Allah has willed it, it is the stage of 'Kun fayakun' (Be, and it is). Be, and that thing happens. Allah does not wait for anyone. 'Innama amruhu idha arada shay'an ay yaqula lahu kun fayakun'. He says to any thing 'Be' and it happens. So, when this word 'irada' came, they tried to interpret it. They tried to justify it. What do they justify? They say, 'No, this will is Tashri'i (legislative).' Tashri'i. What does Tashri'i mean? For those who do not know, let us explain. Look, there are two types of things. One is called Takwini (existential/creative) and the other is called Tashri'i (legislative). And will is also of two types. Allah has discussed two types of will in the Quran. What is the Takwini will? The verse I just presented to you, that it is Allah's will—'Be' and it happens. What is the Tashri'i will? The Tashri'i will is when Allah, for example, commands something, and it is in the servant's power to do it or not. This is called Tashri'i will. Or some people call it Taklifi will. Taklifi means responsibility. The responsibility is the servant's. So, what did they do? Look, they say that this will is Taklifi and Tashri'i. It is not Takwini. So, it is in the hands of the Ahl al-Bayt whether they keep themselves pure or not, whether they stay away from sins or not. Did you notice? Now, listen to the answer. If this will were Tashri'i and Taklifi, meaning it is in the hands of the Ahl al-Bayt whether to remain pure or not, Then why did Allah declare their purity by saying 'Innama yuridullahu'? And why did the Prophet say, 'O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt'? And this will, Allah has for all servants, so what is special about the Ahl al-Bayt? Have you ever seen Allah saying to some servants, 'O My servants, you remain impure. O My servants, you commit sins. O My servants, you commit forbidden acts. O My servants, you remain in filth'? Has Allah ever said that? Allah has never said that. So, this should have been a general declaration. If it were Taklifi and Tashri'i, then it would be general. So, why was it specifically said for the Ahl al-Bayt? This means it is not for the entire Ummah. It is only for the Ahl al-Bayt. This means this is a Takwini will. And Allah has kept them pure, as is the right of keeping pure. And Allah has kept all filth, sins, and dirt away from them. And all evils, everything, has been kept away from them. And in some traditions, it is mentioned that the Prophet prayed before the verse was revealed and also after the verse was revealed. So, this prayer of the Prophet, why is it only for the Ahl al-Bayt? If this will were Tashri'i, then why only for the Ahl al-Bayt? This means that the Prophet is praying to Allah that this will be a Takwini will—meaning Allah keeps them pure, as is the right of keeping pure. This responsibility is not a Tashri'i responsibility like, 'All of you Ahl al-Bayt, you must remain pure.' That is for the entire Ummah. What virtue would there be in that? But the existence of this virtue, the mention of it by the scholars of hadith in their books, its appearance in the Quran, and the subsequent explanation by the exegetes in their commentaries and the scholars of hadith—all of this is proof that this will is a Takwini will, not a Tashri'i one. Once it is proven that the will is Takwini and not Tashri'i, it means that the Ahl al-Bayt are infallible (Ma'sum). And infallibility means superiority. This means superiority (afzaliyat). And when superiority is proven for someone, it is obvious that there must be an inferior (mafzul). Afzal is superior and mafzul is inferior. So, giving preference to the inferior over the superior is against reason. Now see what Ibn Abul Hadid writes. Ibn Abul Hadid says that he is the commentator of Nahj al-Balagha. He was a follower of the Mu'tazila school of thought. So he says that, according to Abu Muhammad Ibn Matwayh—may Allah have mercy on him, according to his view—in his book 'Kitab al-Kifaya', Ibn Abul Hadid says that Abu Muhammad Ibn Matwayh writes that Ali (a.s.) is infallible (ma'sum), even if infallibility was not mandatory or a condition for him. This is according to his view. Yes, why? He says, 'Because infallibility is not a condition for Imamate.' According to him, this is being discussed, yes brother. This is not about the Shia school of thought. But he is acknowledging the infallibility of Ali (a.s.). 'However, the proofs of the texts (nusus) have indicated his infallibility.' And it is certain regarding his inner self and his unseen (batin and ghayb). And this clearly shows that Ali (a.s.) was infallible in his inner self as well, certainly, because infallibility is something that cannot be proven [by observation]. Infallibility can only be announced. Because no one knows what a person does in solitude. So, only that person can be infallible whose infallibility is announced by Allah. And that is why the infallibility of the Ahl al-Bayt al-Athar is being announced through the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir). Because if Allah had not announced it, the Ummah would have said, 'How do we know that he is infallible?' Now do you understand why the Verse of Purification was revealed? So that the entire Ummah would know, so that no one could say, 'We did not know.' This is the reason. Ibn Abul Hadid is acknowledging it. 'And it is certain regarding his inner self and his unseen' means in the unseen, meaning even in secret, meaning in his inner self, Ali's infallibility is proven and certain. 'And this is a matter that is specific to him, not others.' Ibn Abul Hadid says that this infallibility is specific only to Ali ibn Abi Talib. And it is not for others. Ibn Abul Hadid is saying it is not for others. Which others? 'And not others among the companions.' Meaning he declares—Ibn Abul Hadid declares—that none of the companions were infallible. And it is true. Brother, the entire history is present, isn't it? The history is all there. Who can deny it? Can anyone deny it? Now, what do they do? They say, 'Try somehow to bring the wives into this, into the Ahl al-Bayt.' In the last-to-last episode, meaning the episode before the previous one, I proved to you that the wives are not included in this, and if the Verse of Purification appears between the verses about the wives—which we will read out for you now—then that is a matter of the compilation of the Quran, not its revelation (tanzil). It is not a matter of the revelation of the Quran, but a matter of the compilation of the Quran. And everyone who is even slightly familiar with history knows how many problems arose in the compilation of the Quran; everyone knows. And if they don't know, they should contact us via WhatsApp or signatures, etc. Insha'Allah, we will provide them with those details as well. Anyway, so now they say that the wives are included, so we bring more proofs, the ones we brought last time, meaning in the episode before the last one. Now we present further proofs for you. Look, how did this discussion about the wives come about? There were some extreme scholars among the Ahl al-Sunnah who had some issues with the 'Aal' (family). Among them, meaning they had issues with the Aal-e-Muhammad, the Ahl al-Bayt, they had enmity. Among them is Fazl ibn Ruzbahan. This Fazl ibn Ruzbahan wrote a book, 'Ibtal al-Batil' (Refutation of Falsehood). This book, 'Ibtal al-Batil', was a response to Allama Hilli's 'Nahj al-Haqq' (The Path of Truth). Allama Hilli had written 'Nahj al-Haqq', meaning the path of truth. Meaning the path of the Shias is the path of truth. So he wrote 'Ibtal al-Batil' as a response. Qazi Nurullah Shustari—Ridwanullah Ta'ala Alayh—in India we call him Shustari, in Iran they call him Shushtari; Shushtar is the actual name of the place, in India it became Shustari—so he wrote 'Ihqaq al-Haqq' (Establishing the Truth) as a response. Meaning establishing the truth again. He said 'Ibtal al-Batil', he said 'Ihqaq al-Haqq'. Anyway, so this gentleman Fazl ibn Ruzbahan writes, 'Bal akthar al-mufassirin' (Rather, most of the commentators)—look, now it's just talk in the air—'most of the commentators' is not a proof, it's nothing. 'Most of the commentators'—meaning the majority of commentators—'are of the opinion that the verse was revealed regarding the wives.' Regarding the wives. 'And this is appropriate for the order of the Quran.' And this is also appropriate according to the order of the Quran. Therefore, the wives should be included in this. Insha'Allah, in the next episode, we will give a complete answer to what Fazl ibn Ruzbahan has brought, and how Qazi Nurullah Shustari, Shaheed-e-Salis, and other scholars have answered him. Insha'Allah, we will explain in detail in the next episode that this claim itself was based solely on obstinacy. Enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt, and hatred and malice towards the Shias, so that somehow the Ahl al-Bayt must be belittled and others must be elevated. But at the same time, also claiming that 'we love the Ahl al-Bayt very much, very much.' Insha'Allah, we will clarify this for you in the next episode. Insha'Allah. And our final prayer is, all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure, clean, and infallible family, and may His eternal curse be upon their enemies, their killers, those who usurped their rights, and those who deny their virtues and merits.

title: Taqleed: Ahmiyyat Aur Taqaazey | EP#03 - Maraaje Fatwa Kaise Dete Hain?
excerpt: This lecture explores the methodology used by Shia Mujtahids to derive religious rulings (fatwas). It details the four primary sources of Islamic jurisprudence in the Jafari school: the Holy Quran, the Sunnah of the Masumeen, intellect (Aql), and consensus (Ijma). The speaker emphasizes that these sources are used in conjunction rather than independently to ensure rulings remain grounded in divine revelation.
content:
Now, they cannot take any decision independently without the light of the Quran and traditions. They cannot solve problems. This is the meaning of Taqlid in our Jafari school of thought. But before this, let us clarify that this is a separate lecture. If this remains, what they understand is actually conjecture. While in our school of thought, there is no place for conjecture. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Welcome back to our series. In the previous video, we discussed Taqlid and proved in the light of Hadith what Taqlid is and in which matters it is required. Let us shed light on this episode: how do the scholars issue fatwas? What are the things through which a Mujtahid derives his fatwa? A Mujtahid derives his fatwa. The sources through which one can reach the truth are called 'Ma'akhidh' (sources) of jurisprudence in Islam, or the proofs of Ahkam. And these proofs are four in our school of thought. The first proof or the first source of Taqlid is the Holy Quran. After that, the Sunnah of the Masumeen (a.s.), then consensus (Ijma), and the fourth source is intellect (Aql). Let us shed some light on these four sources one by one. First, let us go towards the Holy Quran. The Holy Quran is the first and most important source of Islamic laws and jurisprudence. The Holy Quran is a collection of heavenly revelations. That is why, from the time it was revealed to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) until today, the Holy Quran is the first source of Islamic law. It has been the source of Islamic laws and the fountainhead of its sciences. It is famous that there are about 500 verses in the Holy Quran related to Ahkam (laws), which are called 'Ayat al-Ahkam'. However, to derive laws from the Holy Quran, one needs knowledge of Arabic language, grammar, rhetoric, and the context of the verses, such as which verse is Nasikh (abrogating) and which is Mansukh (abrogated), which is general and which is specific. It is very important to have knowledge of these. Besides this, expertise in the science of Hadith is necessary. The scholars understand the interpretation of the verses in the light of these and derive fatwas and laws. In this regard, our scholars have written many books. Like the book by Muhammad al-Ardabili, who is famous as the 'Muqaddas Ardabili'. He passed away in 993 Hijri. His book 'Zubdat al-Bayan' and other books have been written on this topic. There are many laws about which no explicit mention is found in the Holy Quran. This does not mean that the Quran does not contain everything. The Quran contains everything, but it means that reading the Quran alone will not solve the problem. At this point, the second source of Islamic law comes into play, which is the Sunnah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. To understand the Quran, the Sunnah of Muhammad and his family is the source of Islam. The Sunnah of the Masumeen (a.s.) refers to their words, actions, and approvals. Let us understand these three things one by one. 'Qawl' (words) means the words spoken by the Masumeen (a.s.) and their statements; these are called the traditions of the Masumeen (a.s.). 'Fi'l' (action) means any action performed by the Masumeen (a.s.); this is also Sunnah. The third, 'Taqrir' (approval), means that a person... The third meaning of 'Taqrir' (tacit approval) is that a person performs an action or says something in the presence of an Infallible (Ma'sum) (a.s.), and the Infallible does not reject or stop them. The Infallible is responsible for stopping any wrong action or speech in their presence. Therefore, if the Imam does not stop it and does not confirm it, it is considered 'Taqrir' (tacit approval), meaning the Imam agrees with it, and this also falls within the scope of Sunnah. It is necessary to mention here that previously, some believed that Sunnah only refers to the actions of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). However, according to our Shia belief, because the twelve Imams (a.s.) are appointed by Allah and the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself has confirmed their authority, their words, actions, and tacit approvals are also Sunnah. This is a better way to understand the religion. The Sunnah explains the verses and interpretations of the Quran. We have four major books of Hadith, which are known as 'Al-Kutub al-Arba'ah'. These are known as 'Al-Kutub al-Arba'ah'. Let us see what these four books are. The first book is by Sheikh Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, who passed away in 329 AH, and the book is 'Al-Kafi'. It was completed in 329 AH, the same year the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.) went into major occultation. The second book included in these four is by Sheikh Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, known as Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), who passed away in 381 AH. This is the same year that, through the prayers of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.), he was brought into this world. His book included in the four is 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih'. The third book in this series is by Sheikh Muhammad ibn Hasan, known as Sheikh Tusi (r.a.), who passed away in 460 AH. His book is 'Tahdhib al-Ahkam'. The fourth book is also by Sheikh Tusi (r.a.), known as 'Al-Istibsar'. In his time, there was no jurist (mujtahid) of his caliber. Besides these, there are other books in which narrations related to religious issues have been collected, such as 'Wasa'il al-Shia' by Sheikh Hurr al-Amili, who passed away in 1104 AH. After that, 'Jawahir al-Kalam' by Sheikh Muhammad Hasan Najafi, who passed away in 1266 AH, and 'Mustadrak al-Wasa'il', whose author is Mirza Husayn Nuri (r.a.), who passed away in 1334 AH. These are the books in which some matters related to religious issues have been stated. The third source that mujtahids and jurists use to reach a verdict is 'Aql' (intellect). But it should be noted that 'Aql' does not have the right to create laws independently. You have to search for issues in the light of the Quran and Hadith and then reach a conclusion. This is the principle of our Jafari school of thought. This is the principle of our Jafari school of thought, but we do not consider 'Aql' as an independent source of law. What they (others) consider as 'Aql' is actually 'Qiyas' (analogy), whereas there is no place for 'Qiyas' in our school. This was about the Quran, Sunnah, and Aql. Now let us move to the fourth source of jurisprudence, which is 'Ijma' (consensus). By 'Ijma', it is meant that all jurists agree on a certain issue. But keep in mind that it is not the case that if all jurists agree on an issue, it will be accepted as a final verdict. 'Ijma' alone is not the criterion. For this 'Ijma' to be valid, the support of the Holy Quran and the Hadith of the Infallibles (a.s.) is necessary. So, in summary, a mujtahid or jurist uses four things to derive a ruling: first, the Holy Quran; second, the Sunnah of the Infallibles (a.s.)—who are the Infallibles? The 11 Infallibles... The 11 Infallibles. Third, 'Aql' (intellect), but it should be clear that 'Aql' cannot issue rulings independently; it requires the light of the Quran and Hadith. And 'Ijma' is the fourth source, but it is only considered valid when it has the support of the Quran and the Sunnah of the Infallibles. Wassalam, and praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.
A Mujtahid cannot issue rulings based on conjecture or personal opinion.
The four sources of Shia jurisprudence are the Quran, Sunnah, Aql, and Ijma.
Sunnah includes the words, actions, and tacit approvals (Taqrir) of the Prophet and the twelve Imams.
Al-Kutub al-Arba'ah (The Four Books) are the primary repositories of Shia Hadith.
Intellect (Aql) is not an independent source of law but a tool to understand Quran and Hadith.
Consensus (Ijma) is only valid if it reflects the underlying support of the Quran and Sunnah.
Analogy (Qiyas) is rejected in the Jafari school of thought.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.)  |  Ep#01 - Darwaaza Ya Pardah? - Part 1/2
excerpt: This lecture addresses a common polemical argument used to deny the historical attack on the house of Hazrat Fatimah (s.a.). The speakers analyze a specific Hadith often cited by opponents, which describes the homes of the Ahlulbayt as having no doors, and explain that this is a metaphorical description of trials and hospitality rather than a literal architectural statement. By examining the context of the Hadith within 'Bihar al-Anwar' and other classical texts, the lecture demonstrates that the objection is a deliberate misinterpretation intended to obscure historical events.
content:
Peace be upon you. [Music] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Today, we are starting a series in which we will try to answer the questions raised regarding the attack on the house of Hazrat Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Khisal', Sheikh Mufid (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Irshad', and Allama Majlisi (r.a.) in his book 'Bihar al-Anwar' have narrated a Hadith from Hazrat Ali (a.s.). In this, the Mawla says that we used to live in houses without roofs and doors. Taking this short phrase from the Hadith, the opponents point towards it and, by misusing it, bring an argument that when Hazrat Ali (a.s.) is saying that it was a house without a door... When he is saying that it was a house without a door, then the talk of an attack on Hazrat Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) and the burning of her house door is completely baseless and a fabrication of the Shias themselves. So, what really happened? What is the truth? Let us invite our guest, our dear brother Janab Ehsan Jafari, to answer this. Ehsan Bhai, peace be upon you. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. As you heard, this objection is raised, and these books are cited to claim that when there was no door, where did the attack come from? We would like you to clarify the answer to this objection for our viewers. Yes, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon Fatimah Zahra, and upon her father, and upon her husband, and upon her sons... This objection is raised so that if it can be proven that the house of Ali and Fatimah (a.s.) had no door, then if there was no door, there was no attack. If there was no attack, then the oppression on Fatimah Zahra (s.a.), the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) in her house—all these crimes can be easily denied, and the oppressors can be exonerated, and the innocent can be labeled as killers. Therefore, it is very important to get to the root of this objection. This objection is as baseless as if someone says, 'My stomach is growling with hunger,' does it mean mice have entered the person's stomach and started running? If someone says, 'My heart has come to my mouth due to thirst,' does the heart actually come up? These are metaphors. These are used to express the intensity of hunger and thirst. The Hadith of Imam Kazim (a.s.) that the opponents use to raise this objection—they have taken a small part of the Hadith and intentionally left out the rest because... Intentionally left out the rest because if they took the whole Hadith, it would create doubts about their own beliefs. They intentionally do this to create division among the Shias. The way of the liars has always been that they do not present the whole statement; they take a small part and present it to prove their point. But if we look at the Hadith that is the basis of the opponent's objection, first let us see what is in the book 'Bihar al-Anwar'. On page 373 of volume 27, the sentence of this Hadith is written where Imam Kazim (a.s.) says: 'We did not have roofs on our houses, nor doors, nor curtains, nothing except some palm leaves.' Now, tell me, from these accounts, where there is no door, no roof, and only palm leaves instead of walls, can that be called a house? This means the meaning of this Hadith... This means the meaning of this Hadith is something else. So let us see what Imam Ali (a.s.) has stated through these sentences. What is the Mawla saying? And for this, we do not need to look anywhere else. The people who have brought this objection based on this Hadith—if we look at the same Hadith in their books, just look at the chapter under which this Hadith is written, the answer will become clear by itself. The chapter in which the author of 'Bihar al-Anwar' narrates this Hadith is titled 'The Trial of the Prophets and their Successors'. This chapter is about the trials Allah (s.w.t.) took of the Prophets and their successors in seven places during their lives and seven places after they passed away from this world. This is the meaning of this chapter. In this Hadith, Imam Ali (a.s.) is describing those trials, how much hardship they faced, what kind of difficulties they endured. This is a metaphor used by the Infallibles. This idiom has been used for 10 grams, because before this connection, if you look at the acquisition of this Hadith, it is stated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had so much affection, mercy, and love for those who had newly become Muslims—that if someone was hungry, he would feed them; if someone was thirsty, he would provide them water; if someone had no clothes on their body, he would provide them clothes. Before all these trials, for the Musharraf (those honored), the exams... I am describing the face of the exams, and that is why this idiom has been used. The door, the glimpse, after that, this idiom is used. Yes, this idiom has been used correctly. It is used in a way that in your houses, it was not like this. Not having a door means that changes in the weather, they had no worries about them; they used to do all the work and dance. It is not a door; this is also an idiom. It means that those who used to come to ask, those who came to ask for help, those who were of high quality or any king, the doors of the Muslims' houses were always open for them. This means that whenever someone came to ask, the Messenger of Allah would never turn them away. This means that... [the speaker] is saying that we, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), are... are saying that we, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), prioritize the needs of other Muslims over our own comfort, without caring for ourselves. This is the real meaning of this idiom and the sentence used. Similarly, Allamah Majlisi, in the book 'Bihar al-Anwar', in the chapter he has brought these narrations under, the name of that chapter is 'Bab al-Imtihan' (Chapter of Trials). Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)—this is again about those trials, the trials that came. Besides that, there are calamities and their tests, how Allah tested Ali (a.s.)'s palace and organization. And then the last one, Allamah Majlisi, in this volume, in the 238th narration, this chapter is 62, the 62nd chapter, in it Allamah Majlisi... that chapter is the one under which he brings these narrations. The name of that chapter is 'Bab al-Imtihan' (Chapter of Trials), and that is the chapter where Allah has tested Ali (a.s.) in various ways, both during the life of the Messenger and after the Messenger. The description of the books that is being given there, these difficulties and trials are mentioned there. If the door of the house, then for this, absolutely... if the door of the house, then for this, it is absolutely correct. This is how it is used there. These are all things that, through this, he is explaining that in his own... [the speaker] is explaining. To promote Islam, now here, those people who make this Hadith a basis and try to find that there was no door in the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), we have two questions for them. The first question is, as we saw, the chapter in which Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) has mentioned this Hadith, what was the name of that chapter? Did Allah (azwj) test the successor of the Prophet? So those people who are raising objections by using this Hadith of this chapter, do they accept this fact? That Ali (a.s.) is the successor of the Prophet? They are taking a part of the narration of that chapter, but they are completely ignoring where the chapter starts. Why don't they read that? And the successor of the Prophet is always... the Prophet's passing away... it doesn't happen after seven times, it always happens correctly and clearly. So why don't they read that the successor of the Prophet... and the second and last point, and for today, this is enough in our channel, that those people who do not have... and they keep trying to return others in place of Ali (a.s.) and keep making failed attempts, they have [ignored] the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)... the difficulties of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the mercy that is in the house of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), in which the Prophet says: 'We are the Ahlulbayt', and Allah says... Those people have added sentences from their own side to this Hadith. Instead of describing the physical state of some people, in that attempt, they added more. This is the thing: 'I am the door of Ali', but further, they have shown sentences in such a way that 'so and so...'. When you are not even accepting the door, then where are you from? And the one on which you are raising an objection, in it, the description of the previous era... if a person should be, then the connection of the door... all these things, if they remove them, and just try to create a doubt in the minds of the people, in the minds of some people. For our today, this is enough. There are other answers to such questions, which we will try to take in the next episode because in it, we will try to prove through historical and authentic narrations that in that era, there used to be doors in houses. Ehsan Bhai, you have given excellent points regarding this objection, that just as that Hadith has come in the chapter, it is about the trial, and secondly, if you are taking that Hadith, then also look at the context that it is about the successor... also look at the context that it is about the successor. This is a matter that is brought only and only to hide the only daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and what was done to her. title: Quran Mein Zaahir Aur Baatin Gunaah Kya Hai? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the interpretation of Surah Al-A'raf, verse 33, which distinguishes between apparent and concealed immoralities. The speaker references a narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) to explain that concealed sins are rooted in the leaders of misguidance, while concealed virtues are rooted in the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ultimately, the talk emphasizes that every action, whether sinful or virtuous, reflects one's allegiance to either the enemies or the followers of the Prophet's family.
content:
[Music] A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Sallallahu alayka ya Mawlay ya Aba Abdillah. In Surah Al-A'raf, verse 33, the Lord of Glory says: 'Say, my Lord has only forbidden immoralities (fawahish) - what is apparent of them and what is concealed.' Regarding the apparent immoralities mentioned in this verse, we know that the Quranic verses mention apparent sins. But if we want to understand the 'concealed' (batin) immoralities mentioned here, it is necessary for us to ask the 'People of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Dhikr). Let us ask the Ahl al-Dhikr: what are the sins referred to by the 'concealed immoralities' in Surah Al-A'raf, verse 33? Muhammad ibn Mansur asks our seventh Imam, Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.). The title used for the Imam here is 'Abd al-Salih' (The Righteous Servant), because the era of Imam Kazim (a.s.) was a period of intense Taqiyya (dissimulation). In that era, the narrators, because they wanted to save themselves from the oppression of the enemies... because they wanted to save themselves from the oppression of the enemies, therefore, instead of the name of Imam Kazim (a.s.), 'Abd al-Salih' was used here. And similarly, in the era of Imam Kazim (a.s.), because it was a period of intense Taqiyya, several titles were used for the Imam, such as 'Abu al-Hasan al-Madi' or 'Abd al-Salih', which appears in this narration, or 'Alim'. In some narrations, the word 'Alim' is also used for Imam Kazim (a.s.). Muhammad ibn Mansur asked the Imam: 'What is meant by apparent and concealed immoralities in this verse of Surah Al-A'raf, verse 33?' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'The Quran has an apparent and a concealed meaning. Everything that Allah has forbidden in the Quran is apparent, or apparent immorality, apparent sin. And the concealed immorality is the leaders of misguidance, or the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The root of every sin, the origin of every sin, the root of every evil is the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' Then the Imam continues: 'And everything that Allah has made lawful in the Book is apparent...' Then the Imam continues: 'And everything that Allah has made lawful in the Quran is apparent, apparent things. And in the concealed meaning of that, the Imam says: 'And the concealed meaning of that is the leaders of guidance and the truth, or the origin of every virtue, the root of every virtue, the source of every virtue is the Masumin (a.s.).' The point we understand from this Hadith is that whenever someone commits a sin, whenever someone commits an immorality, in reality, they are following the enemies of the Ahlulbayt. And when a believer does a good deed, they are a follower of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi al-Masumin al-tahirin ajma'in.

content:
Imam Hussain (a.s.)'s letter to Janab Habib ibn Muzahir: 'From Hussain ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) to the learned man, Habib ibn Muzahir. Amma ba'd (To proceed), O Habib, you know our kinship with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) well, and you have more knowledge of us than others. You are a person of character and honor.
