title: Khud Ko Halaakat Mein Na Daalo | E'teraaz Ka Jawaab | #muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common objection regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.) going to Karbala despite knowing his impending martyrdom, specifically in relation to the Quranic verse forbidding self-destruction. The speaker clarifies that the verse refers to the failure to spend in the way of Allah rather than avoiding physical danger. By citing the example of the magicians of Pharaoh, the lecture demonstrates that choosing a path of truth despite certain death is an act of faith, not destruction. Ultimately, Imam Hussain's journey is explained as a fulfillment of his duty to complete the argument (hujjat) upon the people.
content:
A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya Mawlay. As-salamu 'ala al-Hussain, wa 'ala 'Ali ibn al-Hussain, wa 'ala awlad al-Hussain, wa 'ala ashab al-Hussain. Among the objections raised against the mourning (Azadari) of Imam Hussain (a.s.), one objection is: when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was certain that his martyrdom was going to happen in Karbala and the people of Kufa were going to betray him, why did he still go towards Kufa, whereas in the Holy Quran, there is a clear verse: 'And do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction'? Let us see the answer to this. First of all, what does this entire verse command us? Allah Almighty says in this verse: 'And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction. And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.' Here, Allah is commanding to spend in My way, spend in the way of Allah. If a person does not spend in the way of Allah, then for them, this is a warning that they are throwing themselves into destruction with their own hands. Here, the destruction... It is leading [one] into destruction. Here, destruction does not mean that a person will fall ill or lead themselves towards death, but if they are not spending in the way of Allah, then it is a warning for them that by not doing so, they are leading themselves into destruction. From this verse, we learn that Allah invites us to spend in His way, and if a person does not act upon it, they cast themselves into ruin. As for a person being certain that they are heading towards ruin or that their death is imminent, and even after that, they perform an action—we find such incidents where people knew [the consequences] and yet they carried out that act. We are all well-acquainted with the story of Prophet Musa (a.s.) and Pharaoh, when Prophet Musa (a.s.) went to Pharaoh's court and faced the magicians. When the magicians were defeated, they believed in the God of Prophet Musa (a.s.) and Prophet Harun (a.s.). At that time, Pharaoh threatened them, saying that if you do this, I will cut off your hands and feet. Despite that, those people believed in Prophet Musa (a.s.) and said, 'Indeed, Inna ila Rabbina' And they said, 'Indeed, Inna ila Rabbina munqalibun'—that indeed, we are to return to Allah. So they knew they would be killed, their hands and feet would be cut off, but still, they believed in Allah. And as for Imam Hussain (a.s.), he knew that the people of Kufa would betray him and would not come to his aid. But this was from Imam Hussain (a.s.)—he had completed the argument (hujjat) upon the people, that the people called me and I came, so tomorrow people cannot say that we invited Imam Hussain (a.s.) but Imam Hussain (a.s.) did not come. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin, and

title: EP#2: Hijaab-e-Khuda Ki Behurmati |  Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.) | #ayyamefatmiya
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance of the house and door of Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.) in relation to the sanctity of Allah. Citing a narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), the speaker highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) declaration that violating the sanctity of Fatima's house is equivalent to violating the Hijab of God. The discourse concludes with a poignant reflection on the grief of the Imam as he recounts these tragic events in Medina.
content:
In Medina, the sanctity of the Hijab of God was violated. The narrator's name is Isa ibn Mustafa. He says that it is the statement of Imam Kazim (a.s.) that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Know that indeed, the door of Fatima (s.a.) is my door, and her house is my house. Whoever violates the sanctity of that door, has violated the sanctity of the Hijab of Allah.' Isa ibn Mustafa says that after this, Imam Kazim (a.s.) wept for a long time, until he could not even complete his sentence. He just cried out three times, 'Hutika wallahi hijabullah'—by God, the Hijab of Allah was violated. And then, heaving a sorrowful sigh, he only said, 'Ya Ummah, salawatullah alayha.'
The house of Fatima (s.a.) is considered the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).
Violating the sanctity of Fatima's door is equivalent to violating the Hijab of Allah.
Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) narrated this tradition with deep sorrow.
The phrase 'Hutika wallahi hijabullah' emphasizes the gravity of the injustice.

title: Quran Mein J. Mohsin Ibn Ali (a.s.) | Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Mohsiniyyah (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the identity of the 'newborn child' mentioned in the Quranic verse regarding those killed for no crime. Citing a narration from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) to Mufazzal ibn Umar, the speaker identifies this child as Janabe Mohsin (a.s.). The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the ultimate avenger of this tragedy.
content:
In the Quran, the child who was killed is Janabe Mohsin (a.s.). Mufazzal ibn Umar (r.a.) asked Imam Sadiq (a.s.) regarding this call of Allah: 'And when the newborn child will be asked for what crime he was killed?' Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'O Mufazzal, by God, that newborn child is Janabe Mohsin (a.s.), because he is from us, not from anyone else. So, if anyone says anything other than this, reject it. We pray in the court of Allah that He hastens the reappearance of the avenger of Janabe Mohsin (a.s.), that is, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Bow your heads.'
The Quranic verse regarding the killed child refers to Janabe Mohsin (a.s.).

title: Dua Qubool Kyun Nahin Hoti? | دعا قبول کیوں نہیں ہوتی؟ | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual reasons behind the non-acceptance of prayers based on a Hadith from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.). It emphasizes that while Allah intends to fulfill the needs of His servants, committing sins creates obstacles and invites divine wrath. The speaker encourages believers to seek forgiveness for the specific sins that hinder the acceptance of their supplications.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) says: 'Innal-abda yas'alullahal-hajah' (Indeed, when a servant asks Allah for a need), 'fayakunu min sha'nihi qada'uha' (it is of His status to fulfill it), 'ila ajalin qaribin aw ila waqtin bati'in' (whether He does it soon or after a delay). 'Fayudhnibul-abdu dhanban' (Then the servant commits a sin). 'Fayaqulullahu tabaraka wa ta'ala lil-malak' (Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to the angel): 'La taqdi hajatahu' (Do not fulfill his need), 'wahrimhu iyyaha' (and deprive him of it), 'fa'innahu ta'arrada lisakhati' (for he has exposed himself to My wrath), 'wastawjabal-hirmana minni' (and has made deprivation from Me obligatory upon himself). Dear brothers, there are several points in this Hadith that we should reflect upon. One is that when a servant asks Allah for a need, it is of Allah's status to accept it. And when a servant commits sins, those sins become the cause of the rejection of that prayer. Third, sins become the cause of Allah's wrath. So, dear brothers, we must avoid committing sins because these sins also create obstacles in the final stages of the fulfillment of prayers. But no one can estimate when they enter the stages of acceptance. So let us pray with this sentence from Dua Kumayl in the court of the Almighty: 'Allahummaghfir liyadh-dhunuballati tahbisud-du'a' (O Allah, forgive those sins of mine that hinder the acceptance of prayer). And hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), and count us among his helpers and supporters. Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.
Allah is naturally inclined to fulfill the needs of His servants.
The fulfillment of a prayer may be immediate or delayed according to divine wisdom.
Committing sins is a primary cause for the rejection of supplications.
Sins expose the servant to the wrath of Allah and lead to spiritual deprivation.
It is difficult for humans to know when their prayers are in the process of being accepted.
One should specifically repent for sins that act as barriers to prayer, as mentioned in Dua Kumayl.

title: Majlis 2 | Saheeh Deen Kahaan Milega? | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 1444
excerpt: This lecture explores the necessity of deriving religious knowledge exclusively from the Ahlulbayt, warning against the dangers of human opinion, innovation, and unreliable sources. It highlights the historical suppression of the Ahlulbayt's virtues and the importance of documenting authentic knowledge as instructed by the Imams. The discourse concludes with a poignant reflection on the sacrifice of Hazrat Abbas and the profound grief of Imam Hussain at Karbala.
content:
She is weeping while thinking, she is weeping while thinking, Ummul Banin even today. She is weeping while thinking, Ummul Banin even today. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. I used to envy the dust, that is at the door of the Lion of God (Ali). Oh, the feet used to give respect to him, while sitting on the horse. Alas, for my lion, alas, for my lion, what a condition has become of him. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. And even after dying, he fulfilled the promise he made to me. On the loyalty of my son, oh, I am very proud. Now I have no shame before the mother of Ali Asghar. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. In exchange for the father, the Muslims took it from the son. Oh, the head is severed, the body is severed, the arms of the lion are severed. Your picture is in pieces, it is lost, O Ali. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. And the Syrians trampled the corpse, saying this. The Syrians trampled the corpse, saying this. Oh, was the daughter of Ali proud of this very Abbas? The second Zahra (Zaynab) kept watching, and kept weeping. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. And who could fight him, who had such courage? Oh, I hear that a hundred thousand surrounded him and killed him. Oh, even his corpse remained intact, in the hands of the enemy. Like the grave of Ali Asghar, is the grave of Abbas. And when did you fit, when did you fit, in my veil, O my son? Oh, the oppressors have done this, to the state of your corpse. My head's veil is also, my head's veil is also, greater than your closeness. The grave of Abbas is like that of Asghar-e-Besheer (the infant Asghar). And saying 'Ya Abbas', the tents perform wudu with tears. Oh, I fear that blood might flow from his eyes again. I never say such things in front of Abid (Imam Sajjad). Oh, the grave of Abbas is like that of Asghar-e-Besheer. Takallum (the poet) pays salutations to them while weeping in Karbala. Takallum pays salutations to them while weeping in Karbala. The son showed such loyalty to his mother, Fatima Zahra. Oh, the closeness of Abbas's mother is also broken. The grave of Abbas is like that of Asghar-e-Besheer. The grave of Abbas is like that of Asghar-e-Besheer. May Allah have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome is for the people of piety and certainty. And peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the God of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. May Allah bless him and his purified progeny, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, the Imam of the Time, our Master of Command, our Master, our Mawla, our Beloved, our Physician, our Companion, our Confidant, the fortified cave, and the helper of the distressed and the seekers of help. May my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our Master and Leader, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), said: 'He is a liar who claims to know us while holding onto the rope of others.' Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their relief, and curse their enemies all together. I have designated this Hadith as the subject of these five gatherings and the guiding principle of these five sessions. In this Hadith, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that he is a liar, he is a liar who imagines, who imagines that he possesses our Ma'rifat (recognition). Meaning, he imagines that he has our recognition, but in reality, he does not possess it. Why? 'Wa huwa mutamassikun bi urwati ghairina'—while he is holding onto, clinging to the rope of others. Leaving our rope, he is clinging to the rope of others. Here, in Arabic, this 'Waw' is called 'Waw-e-Haliya'. In Arabic, the 'Waw' has several types. When the word 'Waw' comes in Arabic, I don't need to explain the grammar because it might get a bit difficult, but just briefly. In English, it is translated as 'While'. 'Waw-e-Haliya' means it is describing the state, 'While'. It translates it. Meaning, he is lying when he thinks he possesses our Ma'rifat, while he is fastening to the rope of others. He is holding onto someone else's hem and claiming that he loves us, claiming that he possesses our Ma'rifat, but he goes to others, places his head on others' thresholds, bows his forehead on others' thresholds. Therefore, it is necessary and essential that if we possess the Ma'rifat of the Ahlulbayt, we should only cling to the Ahlulbayt, only ask from them, only petition them, and not go to anyone else. Yesterday, I presented a few narrations in your service regarding this. Now, continuing the sequence of those same narrations, as discussed yesterday, the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) said: 'Never, ever take narrations from our enemies. Do not take the Hadith of our enemies.' Yes, of course, I presented a rider in your service regarding that, that an exception is if this Hadith—even if he is an enemy—if he says, 'I heard it from Imam Baqir, I heard it from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), I heard it from Ali (a.s.),' if he says this, then it must be accepted. Then it should not be rejected. Otherwise, if we are calling him a liar, then obviously we are calling Ali (a.s.) a liar, calling the fifth Imam a liar, calling the sixth Imam a liar. Therefore, do not call it a lie. If we are certain, yes, certain that he is 100 percent lying, then that is a different matter; otherwise, do not call it a lie. If he is taking their name, and if he is not taking their name and is just speaking about someone or quoting someone, as I explained in detail in your service yesterday, that is, nowadays you have seen it is the age of WhatsApp, anyone is quoting anyone, videos of enemies are being circulated, and then what justification do they give? 'But he said a good thing, right?' No, the standard for understanding good and bad is not in our control. Subhan Allah. Only the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) know what is good and what is bad. So this is a very important thing. Now look at what Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.) says. Now, what is the reference for this Hadith? Tafsir-e-Imam-e-Hasan-e-Askari (a.s.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief, and curse their enemies all together. Now, as soon as one mentions the name of this Tafsir, many say, 'Oh, that Tafsir is not authentic.' Look, before saying anything, think about what we are saying. Before saying anything, think about what we are saying. 'Tafsir-e-Imam-e-Hasan-e-Askari is not authentic.' No, a few people said that, 'In our opinion, this is not authentic,' a few people. But the number of those who accepted it is so large, and they are such great people, that there is no justification for their denial, no possibility of it. Meaning, there is no possibility of denying the Hadith, no possibility of denying the Tafsir. Tafsir-e-Imam-e-Hasan-e-Askari (a.s.). The background of this Tafsir is that there is a place called Astarabad in Iran, Astarabad. The people there are called Astarabadi. At that time, there was Zaydi rule there. The people of this government, meaning this government, the king, his minister used to incite the king a lot against the Shias. So the king used to oppress the Shias a lot. The result was that he used to persecute the Shias. So a family of Shias fled from there and came to Samarra, and after coming to Samarra, they took refuge with Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) and said, 'Mawla, the king we have oppresses us a lot, so we have fled from there and come here.' Mawla Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) said to them, told them, 'You go back to Astarabad, your problem has been solved.' They said, 'Mawla, we have just come running.' He said, 'I am telling you, go, your problem has been solved. When you arrive, you will get the news that your problem has ended, in fact, you will get the news before that.' So the poor people were hesitating; there was a hesitation in their hearts. Now, they could not disobey Mawla, and they were also afraid to go back, as the whole family had fled from there. Well, in that era, Astarabad wasn't very small, but news used to reach everywhere that the family had fled. Anyway, the summary is that to reassure them, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) said, 'You do one thing, you keep your two, there were two families, so keep two young men here, and I will teach them Tafsir. I will teach them Tafsir, you go, and when you get the news that your problem has been solved, then send me the news, and then I will teach these children Tafsir until they get tired.' Wah wah. 'I will teach them until then.' They were happy, 'Okay.' They went back. They hadn't even reached halfway when they met a messenger from Astarabad who said that the king, the minister who used to incite the king, was found dead one morning; his head was separated from his body. Someone had killed him, and that problem was solved; the king became completely normal. Now there was no one left to incite, no one left to provoke. So their problem was solved. The Imam taught these people Tafsir for 7 years. 7 years, and it's not like that, he used to teach daily, daily. And he said, 'I will keep teaching as long as you have the ability, keep writing.' Walaikum Assalam. 'As long as you have the ability, you have the capacity, you keep writing, I will keep teaching.' That is why Ibn Shahr-e-Ashub says that this Tafsir was in 110 volumes or 120 volumes, it was in 120 volumes, this Tafsir. But when the Baghdad riots happened, this entire Tafsir was burned; only one volume of it survived. One volume. And in that too, we ourselves raised objections, and anyway, whatever it is, that Tafsir is not available now, and only one volume of it is available. From that Tafsir, this reference is being quoted. In it, Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.) says—now pay attention to the words of the Hadith—'Ya ma'shar-ash-shi'atina wal muntahalina mawaddatana.' O our Shias, the society, the group, the community—O community of our Shias, O Shias, and those who claim to have mawaddah (affection) and love for us, you claim, you claim that you love us—beware of those who follow the religion based on their own opinions. They follow the religion based on opinion, and they follow their own opinions in matters of religion, because they neither understand the Quran nor the Hadith. Their Mawla explains it. Yes, yesterday I explained the Quran in your service, and today's Hadith is about the Hadith itself. They follow the religion based on their own opinions. And there is another phrase in another Hadith, where someone came to Imam Ridha (a.s.) and asked, 'What is said about these Ashab al-Hawa? Ashab al-Hawa, meaning those who follow their desires. What opinion should we hold about them? What should we think about them?' The Imam replied, 'They have no Islam, except for facing the Kaaba.' That is the extent of their Islam—that they face the Kaaba. The Imam explained everything in one sentence: their Tawheed (monotheism) is not correct, they do not even believe in Adl (Divine Justice), their Nubuwwah (Prophethood) is not correct, they do not believe in Imamah, and as for the Day of Judgment, only Allah is their protector. This is their belief. And as for the Furu al-Deen (branches of religion), you know better—fasting, working all day, staying hungry and thirsty, and then breaking it ten minutes early, ruining everything. So, this religion, these Ashab al-Hawa and Ashab al-Ra'y (people of opinion)—they are called Ashab al-Ra'y because the Mawla says they follow their religion based on opinion. And that is why a beautiful Hadith just came to my mind, suddenly, that once a man came to the Imam and asked, 'Mawla, what is your opinion on this matter?' What is your opinion? The Imam said, 'Our religion does not run on opinion; our religion runs on Wahi (revelation).' Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Salawat, Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. It is not on opinion; it is on Wahi. We only speak based on Wahi. So, the Mawla's point here was that in the Hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), as I mentioned in the service of your intellect, do not read them like a newspaper. Rather, ponder over every single word, just as we have been commanded regarding the Quran. The Quran itself says, 'Afala yatadabbarunal Quran' (Do they not ponder over the Quran?). 'Walaw kana min indin ghayrillahi la wajadu feehi ikhtilafan katheera' (If it had been from other than Allah, they would have found much discrepancy in it). If this Quran were from anyone other than Allah, you would find many disagreements, many contradictions, many differences in it. But because this Quran is from Allah, it is not based on anyone's perspective; rather, the entire Quran is based on 'Wijdan' (innate conscience/certainty). And 'Wijdan' is something that no one can deny. For example, you are sitting here right now, and if someone asks you who is speaking, you will say, 'So-and-so is speaking.' If someone tells you, 'No, I have a hundred proofs that he is not speaking, you just think so,' you will say, 'Bring not a hundred, but a thousand proofs; I will not accept a single one, because I am seeing with my own eyes and hearing with my own ears.' This is called 'Wijdan.' So, the entire Quran is based on 'Wijdan,' because its denial—(a.s.), (a.s.)—because its denial... come a little forward, make some space. It is a verse of Surah al-Mujadila: 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu idha qeela lakum tafassahu fil majalisi fafassahu yafsahillahu lakum' (O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Space yourselves' in assemblies, then make space; Allah will make space for you). Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Now listen to the Mawla's sentence—these are not our sentences. The Mawla says, and we have even given you the reference, and that is why we read the Arabic along with it, so that whoever listens to the Majlis can check it if they want. We are not reading the concept, we are not reading the translation; we read the direct Arabic so that if anyone wants to check, they can. We are not speaking from ourselves: 'Fa-innahum ada'us-sunan' (For they are the enemies of the Sunnah). Now, let me add a point in brackets, from myself: generally, look, Abbas bhai is sitting here, Abbas bhai is present, you know it always happens, right, that the thief blames the guard? So, the thief, you know what his habit is? That the very thing he is accused of, he starts claiming that others are doing it. Now, because they were enemies of the Sunnah—Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Lanat on the enemies of Ahlulbayt, be-shumar—'Tafallatat minhumul ahadith ay yahfazoha' (The Hadiths slipped away from them, that they might preserve them). They let the Hadiths go, they lost them. How did they lose the Hadiths? How did they lose them? Immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—I am saying this for the youth, for the children, so that you should know history—immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, from 11 Hijri, there was a ban on Hadith. That no one will narrate a Hadith, no one will teach a Hadith, there will be no discussion of Hadith. Why? Because wherever a Hadith was narrated, the virtues of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) would be mentioned. So, if the virtues of the Ahlulbayt were to flow freely, then people would say, 'Brother, if they are superior, then why are you in front?' Therefore, they banned it. They said, 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us). And while the Book was not even compiled yet, they were busy compiling that too—that is also history. 'Bring the book, bring the book.' One wife even said, 'Our book was eaten by a goat.' Now, solve this problem! And they would cut the goat's stomach—where to bring it from, what to do? And in that era, there was no surgery to extract it from the stomach and retrieve it, so it was gone. But all this, all this is history, and we are not reading this from a Shia book. Look, Alhamdulillah, in today's age, so many things have been translated into English, and everything is available on the net. There is a book by Ali Shahristani, 'A History'—the name of the book, I am saying in English, although the original book is in Arabic—'History on the Banning of, on the Prohibition of Narration of Traditions.' This is the name of the book. I am saying this so you can look it up; the name might vary slightly. We don't read books in English, but I have seen it, we have it. It is available on the net; just remember the author's name: Ali Shahristani, 'A History of the Prohibition of Narration of Traditions,' or 'Prohibition of Narration,' something like that. You check it. In it, the entire history—it is a voluminous book of 400-500 pages—in it, the entire history of the ban imposed immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, and this ban lasted for more than 100 years. 100 years! Look, for today's generation, for the youngsters who are sitting here, for example, what they call 'millennials' nowadays, those who reached adulthood in the millennials, right? I am not saying anything wrong, those who reached adulthood in the millennials, because I am not very familiar with this terminology, so I keep asking the youngsters. So, the millennials, those who reached adulthood in 2000, if you ask them, 'What do you remember about the Emergency?' The Emergency was imposed in 1975, '75-'76. Ask anyone if they can tell you anything about the situation in '75-'76. The youngsters will know nothing. How many years has it been? Barely 40-50 years. Today they know nothing. In this age of technology, in that era, there was nothing like this. In the whole of Arabia, only seven people knew how to read and write. Today, understand what the situation is. There were many poets, yes, because poetry and literature were famous among the Arabs, but only a few were literate. So, this means that to be a poet, it is not necessary to be literate. Recite a Salawat, Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. So, this is a fact. The fact is just that a man needs imagination, thoughts, words, and he becomes a good poet, and people do become that. Yes, it is true that if one is literate, their imagination is better, and things are better; this also happens. But anyway, that is not the topic. So, what happened in that era was that a total ban was imposed on Hadiths, a total ban, and this ban remained for more than 100 years. Now, when this ban was lifted after 100 years, Then when people came, they didn't even know what had actually happened and what the Hadiths were. And this method, Insha Allah, we will take this discussion forward tomorrow, Insha Allah, that what is our responsibility. In this era of Ghaybah, what did the Aimma-e-Masumin (a.s.) teach? And how should we read these hadiths, so that we understand these things. And if anyone really wants to learn the spirit of obedience, then they should come to the battlefield of Karbala. And in the battlefield of Karbala, they should see how the spirit of obedience is there in front of the Aimma-e-Masumin, meaning the Imam of the time. And if one has to mention loyalty, then mention only one loyal person. That loyal person who endured so much patience that from Medina to Karbala, he kept saying only this to Imam Hussain (a.s.), 'Abbas, be patient, Abbas, be patient.' He kept saying only this, 'Abbas, be patient, Abbas, be patient.' The Imam did not give permission for battle. He did not give permission for battle. Until one time, on the day of Ashura, a voice came at the door of the tent, 'Sakina, daughter Sakina, bring the water skin.' It is found in the Maqtal that a small girl ran to the door of the tent and said, 'Uncle, how did you remember?' He said, 'Daughter, bring the water skin.' She said, 'Uncle, what will you do with the water skin?' He said, 'Baba has given the order, the Master has given the order to go and fetch water.' So I will go and bring water so that the children may be quenched, so that the ladies may be quenched. Sakina went to take her water skin. Now, it is found in the Maqtal (chronicle of martyrdom) that as soon as Sakina was bringing the water skin, small children gathered around her. 'Lady, where are you going? Lady, where is this water skin going?' She said, 'My uncle, my uncle is going to the bank of the Euphrates, my uncle is going to fetch water, my uncle will now bring water. Children, be assured now. My uncle fulfills the promise he makes. My uncle will bring water.' Sakina brought and gave the water skin. Abbas lifted the water skin. He moved towards the Euphrates. He pushed the soldiers aside, put the horse into the Euphrates, wetted the water skin, and took water in his cupped hands. He took it in his cupped hands so he could say to the wretched ones, 'O wretched ones! Do not consider me helpless and destitute. If I wanted, I could drink water, but the children, the children in the tents are thirsty, the princesses are thirsty, therefore I will not drink water.' He wetted the water skin, filled it, and after filling it, he mounted the horse. In one hand was the standard, he was the standard-bearer, right! So he took the standard in one hand and the water skin in the other. Now Abbas moved on, and it is in the Maqtal—you take it, you also express this, O mourners, weep, offer condolences to the Princess. Offer condolences for Abbas-e-Wafadar (the loyal Abbas). Now as he moved, a wretched one struck such a blow that his right hand was severed. When his right hand was severed, Abbas recited a Rajaz (heroic poem) that even if you sever my right hand, I will still continue to help my Imam. Then another wretched one struck such a blow that his left shoulder was severed. As soon as his left shoulder was severed, Abbas held the water skin in his teeth. He held it in his teeth, but he held it like an orphan, not letting his lips get wet. He did not let his lips get wet. Now as Abbas moved forward, Hurmula shot such an arrow that it hit Sakina's water skin. Water flowed from the water skin. Abbas now bowed his head. 'Now what will I do when I go to the tent?' He turned the horse's direction. As soon as he stood with his head bowed, a wretched one who was hiding behind came and struck such a mace that Abbas fell from the back of the tent onto the land of Karbala. He called out, 'Master! Farewell!' As soon as Hussain heard the voice, he recited a dirge: 'Al-aan inkasara zahri' (Now my back is broken). 'Abbas, now my back is broken. Wa qallat heelati' (And my stratagem has diminished). 'Abbas, I cannot see anything. I cannot see anything. Al-aan shatama biya aduwwi' (Now my enemy is mocking me). 'Abbas, the enemy is mocking me. Your support has gone, your support has gone.' Stumbling, Hussain reached the bank of the Euphrates. He placed the head of the loyal one on his lap. A conversation took place between the brothers. Abbas, while making his will, departed from this world. Just as he departed, Hussain recited a dirge again. 'Al-aan, Abbas, now those eyes will sleep that used to stay awake until yesterday. Now they will wake up. Wa saya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin.' O mourners, pray for the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. O mourners, pray for the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. For the sake of Hussain, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. Count the sins among the helpers. O Allah, Amen. O Lord, those who are in distress, remove their distress. O Allah, Amen. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. O Allah, Amen. O Lord, grant us righteous and pious children. O Allah, Amen. O Lord, O Lord, those who are away from their homeland, return them to their homeland safe and sound. O Allah, Amen. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Allah, Amen. Protect the scholars of the world and the great Maraje. O Allah, Amen. Protect the holy shrines. O Allah, Amen. Protect them, You protect them. O Allah, Amen. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. O Allah, Amen. For all the deceased of the organizer and the gathering, Surah Al-Fatiha and Surah Al-Ikhlas.

chapters.title: Lamentation for Abbas and the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a poetic lamentation for Abbas ibn Ali, comparing his sacrifice and the state of his grave to that of Ali Asghar.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Exclusive Allegiance
chapters.summary: The speaker explores a Hadith from Imam Sadiq regarding the importance of exclusive reliance on the Ahlulbayt and the danger of seeking guidance from their enemies.

chapters.title: Authenticity of Tafsir-e-Imam-e-Hasan-e-Askari
chapters.summary: The lecturer defends the authenticity of the Tafsir attributed to Imam Hasan al-Askari and recounts the historical context of its compilation in Samarra.

chapters.title: The Dangers of Following Personal Opinion
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against following religious interpretations based on personal opinion rather than the Quran and Hadith, emphasizing that true guidance comes from the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Importance of Recording Knowledge
chapters.summary: Imam Ali (a.s.) emphasized the necessity of writing down knowledge, contrasting the preservation of the Ahlulbayt's teachings with the loss of traditions by others.

chapters.title: The Deviation from Sunnah and Innovation
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how early leaders introduced innovations into the faith, rejecting the Sunnah and creating a precedent for 'good innovation' that contradicted the teachings of Imam Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: The Oppression and Characteristics of False Leaders
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights how the Ummah was misled by leaders who acted like tyrants and lacked true knowledge, contrasting them with the divine wisdom of Imam Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: Imam Ali's Superiority in Tawhid and Knowledge
chapters.summary: The speaker contrasts the ignorance of false leaders with Imam Ali's profound explanation of Tawhid to a Jew, emphasizing his role as the gate of knowledge.

chapters.title: The Oppression of the First Oppressed One
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the historical oppression of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the importance of reading and understanding the true history of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Oppression and Isolation of Imam Ali
chapters.summary: The Imam discusses the immense hardships and lack of support Imam Ali faced, explaining that his silence regarding his rights was due to a divine promise made to the Prophet.

chapters.title: Arrogance and the Distortion of Religion
chapters.summary: The speaker analyzes how people's pride led them to reject the truth and substitute divine revelation with their own opinions, contrasting Quranic exegesis from Ahl al-Bayt with external interpretations.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Following the Ahl al-Bayt
chapters.summary: The lecture critiques the use of analogy (qiyas) in religion and addresses the necessity of following the Ahl al-Bayt, while clarifying the legitimacy of taqlid.

chapters.title: The Source of Correct Knowledge
chapters.summary: The Imam emphasizes that true religious knowledge originates solely from the Ahlulbayt, and during the Occultation, believers must refer to the narrators of their hadiths.

chapters.title: Criteria for Religious Guidance
chapters.summary: Imam Ali Naqi explains that in the absence of direct access, Shias should rely on scholars who have dedicated their lives to the love and service of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Authority of Non-Masoom Scholars
chapters.summary: The Imam clarifies that referring to trusted scholars like Zakariya ibn Adam is valid because the Imam guarantees the authenticity of their teachings as being in line with the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Spirit of Obedience in Karbala
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by highlighting the absolute obedience of Hazrat Abbas to Imam Hussain, exemplified by his actions on the day of Ashura.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Abbas ibn Ali
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the tragic final moments of Abbas ibn Ali at Karbala, highlighting his loyalty and sacrifice while carrying water for the children.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Grief and Final Supplications
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain expresses profound sorrow upon the loss of his brother Abbas and leads the congregation in collective prayers for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time.

title: SIBT E AKBAR (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2024 🎁🎉 | 🗓️ Sunday, 24-Mar-2024 | 9:30 PM IST | 16:00 GMT
excerpt: This lecture, presented as the Sibt-e-Akbar Grand Quiz 2024, explores the profound spiritual status and historical challenges faced by Imam Hassan Mujtaba (A.S.). It delves into theological concepts of Tawheed as explained by the Imam, while providing historical evidence regarding the systemic abuse of Imam Ali (A.S.) by historical figures. The session emphasizes the importance of defending the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt and concludes with the announcement of quiz winners and a recitation of Dua-e-Iftitah.
content:
Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider Haider In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him inhabit Your earth willingly and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us. The quiz link is live, which is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered before, click on the quiz link to register. Then on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in any hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first; there is only one condition for the quiz prize, which is that all the answers to the questions must be correct. Among all those who have given the correct answers to all the questions, 14 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, who will be given these prizes. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Infinite praise to that Great and Exalted God who kept us all attached to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and those from his progeny who are the Imams (peace be upon them). Blessings and peace be upon the pride of the prophets and messengers, the cause of the creation of the world and humanity, the means of guidance and salvation of the children of Adam, the intercessor of the Day of Judgment, Ahmad-e-Mujtaba, Muhammad Mustafa (peace be upon him and his family). And upon his rightful successor, the immediate Caliph, the Commander of the Faithful, the slayer of infidels and polytheists, the soul of the Master of Messengers, the Imam of the Pious, the leader of the radiant ones, the Lion of Allah, the Victorious, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). And upon his pure and immaculate progeny, who are the guides and leaders of God's creation after him. That is, their word is the word of the Prophet, their action is the action of the Prophet; the one who follows their sayings and actions is a believer and destined for Paradise, and the one who opposes their sayings and actions is a disbeliever and destined for Hell. The fourth link in this chain of infallibility and purity, that is, the one whose generosity is described by Surah Ad-Dahr, whose infallibility and purity is the ode of the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), the one who is the rider of the Prophet's shoulder, the one who is the leader of the youth of Paradise, the one whose grandfather is the Prophet, father is the Commander of Hunayn, mother is like Fatima, and strength of arm is like Hussain. Yes, respected viewers, Imam Hassan Mujtaba (peace be upon him), whose date of birth is 15th of Ramadan, 3 AH, and on the occasion of this blessed birth, we are once again present in your service with this Sibte Akbar (Grandson of the Prophet) Grand Quiz. Alhamdulillah, this is the fifth round of our Sibte Akbar Grand Quiz. So before starting today's discussion, let us take a bird's-eye view of the topics we have discussed in our Sibte Akbar Grand Quiz over the past four years. The first year, the topic we discussed was the luminous creation of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him). We discussed his generosity, the Hajj he performed on foot, and all the conditions of the peace treaty of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him). In the second round in 2021, we presented the discussion of Prophet Khidr (peace be upon him) before you, and the first sermon of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) which he delivered after the martyrdom of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). And in our third round in 2022, we saw why Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) was named Hassan, and the teaching of the Iftar prayer was stated by Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) himself, and besides this world, where else does the authority of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) lie? The conversation of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) with the ruler of Syria, in which he tried to portray himself as better than the Imam (peace be upon him) and how the Imam (peace be upon him) answered him, besides this, an incident of Tawassul (intercession) from Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) and how the Battle of Jamal was won because of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him), we presented this before you. In the episode of the previous year, 2023, we explained to you how the knowledge of Imamate was handed over to him. An incident of an old woman regarding the generosity of the Imam (peace be upon him), what answer the Imam (peace be upon him) gave to the ruler of Syria when he tried to intimidate the Imam (peace be upon him) with wealth. The fear of God of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) and the detailed explanation of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) as to why he made peace. Respected gentlemen, if we look, the month of Ramadan is superior to all months. It is called Ghurrat al-Shuhur, meaning the most beautiful month. Another name for it is that it is also called Sayyid al-Shuhur, meaning the leader of all months. Allah chose this month for the arrival of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) into the world. This itself is a virtue for this month. That is, the arrival of the leader of the youth of Paradise in the leader of the months, and this adds to the honor of the month of Ramadan because the creation of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) is before the creation of the month. So come, respected gentlemen, let us take this discussion of ours further, and present in our gathering to discuss with us are our dear brother Mr. Ahsan Jafri and our dear brother Mr. Abbas Patel. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. And peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Ahsan brother, the way the birth of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) took place in this blessed month, we would like you to shed more light on how this is not the honor of Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) but the honor of this month that his arrival was in this month. Certainly. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. First of all, we offer many congratulations to all you viewers regarding the date of the blessed birth of Imam Hassan Mujtaba (peace be upon him) which is coming up. And Gulzar brother, as you said absolutely correctly, the arrival of Imam Hassan Mujtaba (peace be upon him) in this world in this month, the arrival of the Imam in this month is itself an honor for this month, and we can present the proof for this with reference to the Quran. In the Holy Quran, in Surah At-Tawbah, Allah the Almighty states where the number of months is mentioned. What does the verse say: 'Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah.' That is, according to Allah, the number of months is 12 months in His book. And since when have these 12 months existed? 'Yawma khalaqas-samawati wal-ard' (The day He created the heavens and the earth). Since the creation of the heavens and the earth, the number of these months has been 12. Now, those who... claim to follow the 'Kitabullah' (Book of Allah) find this verse standing before them like a question mark. Has Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala mentioned that there are 12 months, but the names of these 12 months are not mentioned in the Quran-e-Majeed? Therefore, if one wants to know the names of those 12 months, one must at least turn to someone other than the Quran. That is why we are not just followers of the Quran alone; we are followers of the Hadith-e-Saqalain, that as long as the Quran and the Ahlulbayt are not together, neither will the Quran be understood, nor will the religion be understood. Here, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala has declared, since when have the 12 months existed? Since the creation of the heavens and the earth, since Allah created the heavens and the earth. Now, for the creation of the heavens and the earth, the system that governs the heavens and the earth requires the existence of the sun and the moon. Days are formed based on the movement of the sun and the moon. From days, weeks are formed; from weeks, months; and from months, years. This is how the system of the universe operates. So, for this system—the system of these 12 months—to function, the sun and the moon are necessary. And now, what do we find regarding the sun and the moon, how were they created? It is found in the traditions that when Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala created the light (Noor) of Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.), then the tradition says, 'Thumma fataqa nooral Hasani alayhis-salam' (Then He split the light of Hasan (a.s.)), Allah split that light, the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.), 'Fakhalaqa minhush-shamsa wal-qamar' (And from it, He created the sun and the moon). Subhan Allah, Masha Allah. Meaning, the creation of the sun and the moon is indebted to the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.). And then what does the tradition say? 'Fanurus-shamsi wal-qamari min nooril Hasani alayhis-salam' (The light of the sun and the moon is from the light of Hasan (a.s.)). 'Wa noorul Hasani min noorillah' (And the light of Hasan is from the light of Allah), it is the light of Allah itself because Allah created this light. 'Wal-Hasanu afdalu minash-shamsi wal-qamar' (And Hasan (a.s.) is superior to the sun and the moon). So, when you said that the arrival of Imam Hasan (a.s.) in this month is an honor for this month, why? Because this month comes into existence through the rotation of the sun and the moon, and the sun and the moon would not exist if the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.) did not exist. Because if you are talking about the month, that is far off; Imam Hasan (a.s.) is superior to the moon and the sun. He is superior to the moon and the sun. Meaning, if we look at this, since Imam Hasan (a.s.) is superior to the creation of the moon and the sun, then if the grandfather of Imam Hasan (a.s.) split the moon, people should not be surprised. If his father turned back the sun—the incident of 'Radd-ush-Shams'—people should not be surprised at that either, for when the son has such authority, what must be the authority of his grandfather and his father? This is Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.). Now, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala bestowed this honor upon the month of Ramadan due to the existence of Imam Hasan (a.s.) and described these virtues of Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.). Now, if we look at the traditions regarding what Imam Hasan (a.s.) stated about Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala—that is, when Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.) teaches Tawheed (monotheism), what does the Imam say? Look, it is a very interesting Hadith. As you said in the beginning, in the 'Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz' that we held previously, we saw that the very Dua we recite for Iftar—when a fasting person breaks their fast, the Dua they recite, 'Allahumma inni laka sumtu'—is taught by Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.) himself. Now, if we talk about Tawheed, what did Imam Hasan (a.s.) say about it? Look, it is a very interesting incident where a person came to Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.), presented himself in his service, and requested, 'Ya Ibna Rasoolillah sallallahu alayhi wa alihi' (O son of the Messenger of Allah), 'Sif li Rabbak' (Describe your Lord for me). Describe Allah for me, describe your Lord, define Him. 'Hatta ka-anni anzuru ilayh' (So that it is as if I am looking at Him). The question is very interesting, that I want a description like this, I want the description of the Lord of the Worlds like this. Now, what happened? Look, this question is similar to the one when the Children of Israel came to Prophet Musa (a.s.) and said, 'Show us your Lord.' Correct. Now, that was Musa, and this is 'Fakhr-e-Musa' (the pride of Musa). That was Prophet Musa (a.s.), and after explaining for a while, the answer finally came from Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala: 'Musa, tell these people that Lan tarani (You cannot see Me).' But listen to the answer of the 'Fakhr-e-Musa'. The tradition says that the Imam bowed his head for a while, 'Fa-atraqa maliyyan, fa-atraqa al-Hasanu ibnu Aliyyin alayhimas-salamu maliyyan' (He bowed his head for a while), then after that, 'Farafa'a thumma rafa'a ra'sahu' (Then he raised his head), and then the Imam (a.s.) said—now the Imam is explaining Tawheed, what is Tawheed? The tradition says, 'Faqala alayhis-salam: Alhamdu lillahilladhi lam yakun lahu awwalun ma'lum' (Praise be to Allah for whom there is no known beginning). That since when He has existed, no one can state that. For Him, when the beginning is, no one can describe that. 'Wa la akhirun muntaha' (And no end or limit). Neither is anything known about when He began, nor is there any end to His existence. Meaning, He has no conclusion, no limit, He is infinite. Then the Imam states, 'Wa la qablun mudrak' (And there is no 'before' that can be grasped), nor is there anything through which it can be known or stated that He is before something. 'Before' is not applicable to Him. This cannot even be stated for Allah. 'Wa la ba'dun mahdud' (And there is no 'after' that is limited), nor can it be said that He is after something, because if it were said that He is after something, He would become limited. Therefore, there is no 'before' for Him, no 'after' for Him, no 'prior' for Him, and no 'subsequent' for Him. 'Wa la amadun bi-hatta' (And there is no time fixed for Him), that any human could say 'until this time'—this also cannot be said for Allah. 'Wa la shakhsun' (And He is not a person/entity) that can be divided into parts, about whose separate parts one could speak. He is not even a person. 'Wa la ikhtilafu sifatin' (And there is no difference in His attributes), 'Fayatannaha' (that would have an end). There is no difference in His attributes at all. Meaning, there is no such thing as His attributes reaching a point where they end. All His attributes are limitless, infinite. 'Wa la tudrikul uqulu' (And intellects cannot grasp Him), nor can intellects grasp Him with their imaginations. 'Wa la al-fikru wa khataratuha' (And thought and its wanderings cannot reach Him), and as far as thought can run, as far as thought can go, no matter how much thought runs, it cannot reach Allah. 'Wa la al-albabu wa adhhanuha' (And neither can minds and their perceptions), and where minds can think, where the mind can reach, if there is a limit to the mind's reach, Allah is many times beyond that reach. Meaning, the mind cannot reach where Allah is; the mind cannot discuss Him. 'Sifatuhu'—it cannot discuss His attributes. So, when it cannot discuss His attributes, then who can discuss the Essence of Allah? The Imam is explaining about His attributes. Meaning, there is no end to His attributes. Look, we just passed the month of Rajab two months ago. There is no end to His attributes—how? If we understand this through an example, in the month of Rajab, in the blessed month of Rajab, we recite a Dua after every prayer, 'Ya man yu'ti man sa'alahu' (O He who gives to those who ask Him). There is a sentence in that Dua. Look, there is no end to Allah's attributes. How? What do we pray in it? He points towards the event of Mubahila—that Allah, meaning in the field of Mubahila, when this verse of Mubahila was revealed: 'Faqul ta'alaw nad'u abna'ana wa abna'akum wa nisa'ana wa nisa'akum wa anfusana wa anfusakum thumma nabtahil fanaj'al la'natallahi 'alal kadhibin'—this is the entire verse of Mubahila. In it, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says that I saw that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) took the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, with him in place of his own self. And then after that, meaning 'da'a rasulullahi sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi'—I am saying here, they only wrote 'sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam', 'Aliyan wa Fatimatan wa Hasanan wa Husaynan'—he took all four with him, called all four, and then the Prophet prayed in the court of Allah, 'Allahumma ha'ula'i ahli' (O Allah, these are my family). Meaning, those who are the Ahlulbayt of the Messenger, the one who made that Sa'd a governor is ordering them to insult them, God forbid, God forbid, to curse them, to use abusive language. Is this religion? Is this Islam? So viewers, we are seeing how our brothers have explained the entire map drawn in the history books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, showing the kind of era Imam Hasan (a.s.) was living in, where cursing the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) was very common, and people invited each other to come and curse in the name of Imam Ali (a.s.). So now let's see how Imam Hasan (a.s.) defended his father, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), in this era. We would like Abbas brother to shed some light on this. So Gulzar brother, when the ruler of Sham came to Kufa, Imam Hasan (a.s.) was quite famous among the people of Kufa. He was quite famous. So someone advised him that if you order Imam Hasan (a.s.) to go to the pulpit and give him a chance to speak, you will find that his words are not that firm; he is a young man who—God forbid, if one were to translate it literally—stammers, there will be a stutter in his tongue. And when people see that he is speaking on the pulpit in this manner, his status will fall in the eyes of the people, and they will turn away from him. So, the only delay is for you to order Imam Hasan (a.s.) to come to your place on the pulpit and deliver a sermon. So, the people incited him, and he fell for their words. And he gave Imam Hasan (a.s.) the opportunity to come to the pulpit and deliver a sermon. So, 'Fahamidallaha wa athna 'alayhi thumma qala'—the Imam (a.s.) praised and glorified Allah and then said, 'Amma ba'du fa'innakum law talabtum ma bayna kadha wa kadha latajidurajulan jadduhu nabiyyun'—meaning if you want to know what the difference is between me and him, you will find on one side the person whose grandfather is a Prophet. Allahu Akbar. Meaning, the one who is the progeny of the Prophet. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. 'Lam tajiduhu ghayri wa ghayra akhi'—and you will not find anyone else in the progeny of the Messenger except me and my brother. Indeed, indeed, Subhan Allah. And we have made this peace treaty with this rebel—the Imam points towards the ruler—because we considered saving the blood of the people, the blood of the Muslims, to be superior. Compared to shedding the blood of Muslims. Meaning, one reason is also that because of that peace treaty of Imam Hasan (a.s.), the killing of Muslims stopped. Correct. The blood of Muslims was saved. Whereas in my view, this blood—shedding the blood of Muslims is just a sedition and nothing else. So the ruler, the ruler of Sham, said to the Imam (a.s.), 'Ma aradta biqawlika'—meaning what do you mean by your statement? 'Faqala 'alayhis salam aradtu bihi ma aradallahu 'azza wajall'—by this statement, by this speech, I want what Allah Azza wa Jall wants. Subhan Allah. So he stood up and started to deliver a sermon, and the point is that when he started to deliver the sermon, there was a stutter in his tongue. Allahu Akbar, wow, Subhan Allah. Meaning, they had intended to insult Imam Hasan (a.s.)—God forbid, God forbid—that this would happen to the Imam. But as they intended, Allah's intention was that a stutter should come into their tongues. Correct. And he, as usual, started to curse the Commander of the Faithful and started using abusive language. 'Faqamal Hasanu bnu 'Aliyyin 'alayhimas salam'—Imam Hasan (a.s.) stood up. 'Faqala wahuwa 'alal minbar'—while he was on the pulpit. 'Ya ibna akilatil akbad, atasubbu amiral mu'minin?'—Are you cursing the Commander of the Faithful? 'Waqad qala rasulullahi sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi'—whereas the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had said regarding the Commander of the Faithful, 'Man sabba 'Aliyan faqad sabbani'—whoever curses Ali is cursing me. 'Waman sabbani faqad sabballah'—and whoever curses me is cursing Allah; he is, in reality, using abusive language regarding Allah. Allahu Akbar. 'Waman sabballaha adkhalahullahu naran'—and whoever curses Allah, Allah will admit him into the fire. Indeed, indeed, 'khalidan fiha'—he will remain in it forever. 'Mukhalladan'—forever. 'Walahu 'adhabun muqim'—and for him, a severe punishment has been prepared. 'Thumma thummanhadaral Hasanu 'alayhis salam 'anil minbari fadakhala darahu'—so the Commander, Imam Hasan (a.s.), descended from that pulpit and turned and left from there, left that mosque, and the Imam never returned to that mosque and never offered prayers in that mosque. Meaning, Abbas brother, if we look at the traditions, Imam Hasan (a.s.) proved that in a place where insulting things or any act of insult is being performed against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), he does not like to stay there even for a moment. He does not even want to offer prayers. Meaning, yes, any other place is a different matter, but Imam Hasan (a.s.) never returned to the mosque. This means that we should think that if any inappropriate thing or inappropriate words are being used for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) anywhere, we should never go there. Indeed, indeed. You should keep away from such places. Indeed, indeed. And this work, where the conversation started, that the greatest work, the achievement, the act that Imam Hasan (a.s.) performed in that era during his era of Imamate, is this defense of Wilayah. Indeed. And regarding this defense of Wilayah, there is a very interesting hadith from Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) himself, that how important the defense of Wilayah is and what its reward is. It is found in the tradition that a person came, presented himself to Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), and had brought some gift for the Imam. He had brought a gift, and then the Imam (a.s.), now obviously... You say, the generosity of Hasan is famous? Indeed. Indeed. So now Imam Hasan (a.s.) wanted to give more in return for that gift. But the Imam did not give him anything directly in return for that gift. He gave him an option, gave him a choice. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Ayyuhuma ahabbu ilayka?'—which of the two things do you like? 'An arudda 'alayka badalaha 'ishrina za'ifan'—that I return to you twenty times more than what you have brought as a gift for me? Do you want this? 'Ishrina alfan dirhamin'—meaning I give you 20,000 dirhams? This shows that he had brought 1,000 dirhams as a gift for the Imam (a.s.). The Imam said, should I give you 20 times more? I can give you 20,000 dirhams. You decide what you want? Do you want these 20,000 dirhams? Or 'Aw aftahu laka biha baban minal 'ilmi'—I can open a door of knowledge for you, if you wish. Wow! Wow! Wow! I can open a door for you, and what will happen because of that? If I, who is the heir to the knowledge of the Commander of the Faithful, indeed, indeed, is saying to that person that as a gift, I can open a door of knowledge for you. Masha'Allah. Right? The heir to the 'City of Knowledge' is saying I can open a door of knowledge for you. He says, and then what will happen through this? It will happen that 'taqharu fulanan nasibi fi qaryatik'—that certain Nasibi in your homeland, in your village, where you have come from, from the region you have come from, you will overcome him. Wow! The knowledge that I will grant you, you will overcome him. And not only that you will overcome him, 'tunaqizu bihi zu'afa'a ahl-e-qaryatik'—your fellow countrymen who are weak, our followers who are weak, poor things—meaning those who cannot defend, who cannot defend the creed, through this knowledge, you will be able to protect them too. Wow! The choice is in your hands. 'In ahsantalkhtiyar'—if you made a good choice, if your choice was good, you chose a good thing, then what will happen? 'Jama'tu lakal amrayn'—I will give you both this world and the hereafter. 'Wa in asatalkhtiyar'—but if you made a bad choice, didn't make a good choice, even then there is no problem. 'Khayyartuka litakhudha ayuhuma shita'—I will still give you the choice, take whatever you want, no problem. But now the decision is in your hands, what decision do you have to make? Meaning, the Imam's kindness is that he is even telling him. Yes. Which thing to select, and he gave a hint, absolutely gave a hint, and despite that, the Imam said that okay, because he had brought a gift for the Imam, so now the Imam (a.s.) would not keep anyone's favor. Indeed. Then the Imam said that I will give you the choice, take whatever you want. Now that person says, 'Ya Ibna Rasulillah sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi'—the reward that will be there, on the basis of which I will overcome that Nasibi and the weak followers of yours, your weak followers, weak in the sense that they will not be able to defend the creed, whom I will save from his clutches, will set free, so is its value 'ishrina alfan dirham'? Meaning, is its value 20,000 dirhams? Because the Imam had said in the beginning that I can give 20,000 dirhams. So is its value also 20,000 dirhams? The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Bal aksaru minad dunya'—more than the world, how much more? 'Ishrina alfan alfa marratin'—20 million, meaning 20 million times more than the reward of the world. Wow! This is—no human can calculate this. That knowledge with which the defense of Wilayah is done. That knowledge with which victory is achieved over the Nasibis. Indeed. That knowledge with which the weak Shias, who are weak in creed, are defended, is far superior to all the wealth of the world. The Imam says 20 million times, 20 million times. 20 million times, this is one door of knowledge, one door, one door. Indeed, one door. And then that person immediately says, 'Ya Ibna Rasulillah fakayfa akhtarul adwan?'—then Mawla, why should I take the first thing? Correct. I will take the superior thing, right? Indeed, indeed. 'Bal akhtarul afdal'—my choice, my choice will be the better thing. 'Al kalimattallati aqharu biha aduwwallah'—my choice is that word through which I can overcome the enemy of Allah. Give me that. And through which I can defend the Auliya-e-Allah, can take them out of the clutches of that Nasibi. Grant me that. So the Imam (a.s.), now since he chose this thing, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) says, 'Qad ahsantalkhtiyar'—you have made an excellent choice. Excellent. Your choice is truly very good. Then the Imam (a.s.) taught him that knowledge and 'a'tahu'—not only that, the Imam had given a choice in the beginning, either take 20,000 dirhams and go or this knowledge. But when he chose, what had the Imam said? If you made a good choice, I will give you both this world and the hereafter. So regarding the hereafter, the Imam gave him that knowledge, and regarding the world, the Imam also gave him 20,000 dirhams. Subhan Allah. The Imam also granted him 20,000 dirhams, and then after that, he went from there, the Nasibi went, rather the tradition says 'fa afhamar rajul'—that person defeated that Nasibi in such a way that the Nasibi was not left with any face to show. Subhan Allah. Right? 'Afhama', 'Afhama'—this is a term, in Arabic terminology, it is said to blacken the face of the enemy. He defeated him in such a way, he crushed him in such a way that he was totally humiliated. He was embarrassed. 'Fattasal khabaru bihi alayhis-salam' (The news reached him, peace be upon him). Now, what happened was that the news of how he had defeated that Nasibi reached the Imam. The news reached Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). 'Faqala lahu iza hazarahu' (When he came to him). Now, when he had defeated him, he came to the Imam (a.s.) to give him the good news. When he arrived in the presence of the Imam (a.s.), Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) said to him, 'Ya Abdullah' (O servant of Allah), 'Ma rabiha ahadun misla rabihek' (No one has gained as much as you have gained). 'Wa la katasaba ahadun minal awwida'e maktasabta' (And among our lovers, no one has earned what you have earned). And what did he earn? The Imam said you have earned five such loves, five such mawaddats (affections). The first mawaddat, the first love, the Imam says is 'Mawaddatullah' (the love of Allah), you have earned the love of Allah. Second, 'Wa mawaddat Muhammadin sallallahu alayhi wa alihi wa alihi alayhis-salam' (And the love of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.)), you have earned the love of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.). This is the second. 'Wa mawaddat tayyibeen min alihima salisan' (And the love of their pure progeny, thirdly), you have earned the love of their pure and holy progeny, this is the third thing. 'Wa mawaddat malaikatillahil muqarrabeen rabi'an' (And the love of the angels of Allah who are near, fourthly), and the love of the Malaika-e-Muqarrabeen (the closest angels of Allah), you have earned their love, this is the fourth mawaddat. 'Wa mawaddat ikhwanikal momineen khamisan' (And the love of your believing brothers, fifthly), and the fifth is that you have earned the love of all your believing brothers. 'Wa katasabta bi adad kulli mominin wa kafir' (And you have earned [reward] equal to the number of every believer and disbeliever). All the individuals in the world, whatever their number is, your reward is equal to that. Meaning, whatever good deeds all the people have done, you have that much reward. Subhan Allah. 'Ma huwa afzalu minad dunya' (This is better than the world), and this is superior to all the things of the world. 'Wa ma feeha' (And whatever is in it), 'Alfa alfa marratin' (one hundred thousand times), one hundred thousand times superior to this. The things that are in the world. And then after that, the Imam says, 'Fa haniyan laka haniyan' (Congratulations to you, congratulations). Meaning, this is the defense of the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), its importance, and its reward. There is nothing superior to this. Therefore, wherever we are, in whatever state we are, whenever we come to know, if we have the knowledge that if someone, God forbid, has tried to show disrespect to the status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then the first voice should be raised from our side. We will not tolerate any disrespect to the status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) at all. So, meaning, a befitting reply will be given to him, and the reply he deserves, the reply he is entitled to, should be given to him in his own language. This is the importance of defending the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), because the Imams (a.s.) have taken it so seriously. The Imam (a.s.) considers this as knowledge. He knows it as knowledge and teaches it as knowledge. Therefore, the world is nothing before its importance. The Imam had placed the world before him, gave him an option, but he did not choose the world. He chose the religion, he chose the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt. Today, for us, it is the Wilayat of Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.). Today, if there is any talk against Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.)—'wa nahnu ma'ahu wa la ma'a aduwwihi' (and we are with him and not with his enemy)—if there is any talk against his status, then first of all, we should raise our voice in his defense. Jazakallah, Mashallah, Subhan Allah. We are extremely grateful to both brothers that you have presented a very comprehensive and well-argued discussion regarding the life and the virtues and merits of Imam Hasan (a.s.), and how Imam Hasan (a.s.) defended the Wilayat of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) in an era where it was difficult to even mention the name of Imam Ali (a.s.), let alone discuss his virtues. So, we also pray in the court of the Almighty that, O Lord, for the sake of Imam Hasan (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). And grant us the ability to acquire the knowledge required to defend the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt, and through it, attain the love of Allah, His Messenger, His Ahlulbayt, and His closest angels. With this, viewers, we, the TSR team, conclude this year's Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz, and we hope that this discussion will be useful for you. The quiz link is still active, and as soon as this timer you see on the screen ends, the quiz link will also be closed. Therefore, you are all requested that there is still time, read the questions carefully, give the correct answers, and submit them. So, let us now move towards Dua-e-Iftitah, and immediately after the prayer, the 14 lucky winners of today's quiz will be selected through our computerized lucky winner system. So, let us turn our attention to Dua-e-Iftitah. And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. [Arabic text of Dua-e-Iftitah follows]. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your messenger, Your trustee, Your chosen one, Your beloved, and the best of Your creation, the guardian of Your secret and the conveyor of Your messages, with the best, most beautiful, most complete, purest, most growing, most pleasant, cleanest, most exalted, and most numerous blessings, benedictions, mercy, affection, and peace that You have ever bestowed upon any of Your servants, prophets, messengers, chosen ones, and those honored by You among Your creation. O Allah, send blessings upon Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, the successor of the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, Your servant, Your guardian, the brother of Your Messenger, Your proof over Your creation, Your greatest sign, and the Great News. And send blessings upon the truthful and pure Fatima, the leader of the women of the worlds. And send blessings upon the two grandsons of mercy and the Imams of guidance, Hasan and Husain, the leaders of the youth of Paradise. O Allah, send blessings upon the guardian of Your command, the Awaited One, the Just, the Expected, and surround him with Your closest angels and support him with the Holy Spirit, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, make him the caller to Your Book and the upholder of Your religion. Appoint him as Your successor on earth as You appointed those before him. Establish for him his religion which You have approved for him. Replace his fear with security, so that he may worship You and not associate anything with You. O Allah, honor him and through him honor others, help him and through him gain victory, and grant him a mighty victory. Open for him an easy path and grant him from Yourself a supporting authority. O Allah, we desire from You a noble state in which You honor Islam and its people and humiliate hypocrisy and its people, and make us among those who call to Your obedience and lead to Your path, and grant us through it the honor of this world and the hereafter. O Allah, whatever truth You have made known to us, help us to bear it, and whatever we have fallen short of, help us to reach it. chapters.title: Introduction and Quiz Guidelines
chapters.summary: The program introduces the Sibte Akbar Grand Quiz, explaining the registration process, rules for participation, and the selection of winners.

chapters.title: Virtues of Imam Hassan Mujtaba (A.S.)
chapters.summary: The speaker honors the lineage of the Prophet and introduces the significance of Imam Hassan Mujtaba, whose birth is celebrated during Ramadan.

chapters.title: Review of Previous Quiz Topics
chapters.summary: A summary of the themes covered in the past four years of the Sibte Akbar Grand Quiz, including the Imam's generosity and life events.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Significance of Imam Hassan's Light
chapters.summary: The discussion explores the Quranic concept of the twelve months and explains the tradition that the sun and moon were created from the light of Imam Hassan.

chapters.title: The Superiority of Imam Hasan (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the spiritual status of Imam Hasan (a.s.), asserting his superiority over the sun and moon and highlighting his connection to divine light.

chapters.title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Explains Tawheed
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan (a.s.) provides a profound theological description of Allah in response to a request to define the Creator, emphasizing His transcendence beyond human intellect.

chapters.title: The Miracle of Divine Speech
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that the eloquent teachings and definitions of Tawheed provided by the Imams are greater miracles than physical wonders like the splitting of the moon.

chapters.title: The Miracle of Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Tawheed
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan (a.s.) demonstrates the profound power of Tawheed by preventing a false claimant from using the Kalima to escape divine punishment.

chapters.title: Defending Wilayah and the Peace Treaty
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan (a.s.) utilized the peace treaty to historically document and condemn the state-sponsored vilification of Imam Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: Historical Evidence of Abuse Against Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker cites Sunni historical sources to demonstrate that Imam Ali (a.s.) and his family were historically subjected to public cursing and abuse.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Warning Against Abusing Ali
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights authentic narrations from Umm Salama where the Prophet explicitly equates abusing Imam Ali (a.s.) to abusing himself.

chapters.title: Contradictions in Historical Narratives
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques Ibn Taymiyyah's claims in Minhaj al-Sunnah, noting the contradiction between the Prophet's definition of a hypocrite and the historical reality of hatred toward Imam Ali.

chapters.title: The Historical Practice of Cursing Imam Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the historical tragedy where Mu'awiyah ordered the cursing of Imam Ali (a.s.), highlighting Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's refusal to comply based on the Prophet's virtues of Ali.

chapters.title: Prophetic Virtues of Imam Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas cites three major virtues—the status of Harun to Musa, the love of Allah and His Messenger at Khaybar, and the event of Mubahila—as reasons he could not curse Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Defends the Wilayah
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan (a.s.) confronts the ruler of Sham in Kufa, defending his father's honor and declaring that cursing Ali (a.s.) is equivalent to cursing the Prophet and Allah.

chapters.title: The Lesson of Disassociating from Insult

chapters.title: The Superiority of Defending Wilayah

chapters.title: Rewards for Defending the Ahlulbayt
