title: SIBT E AKBAR (a.s.) GRAND QUIZ | Presentation and Live Quiz on Hazrat Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive overview of the life, status, and divine authority of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) within the framework of a grand quiz competition. It explores theological concepts such as Wilayat-e-Takwini, the significance of the Ahlul-Bayt, and the spiritual benefits of fasting and reciting the Hadith al-Kisa. The session emphasizes the divine appointment of Imams and the importance of aligning one's life with the teachings and virtues of the Prophet's progeny.
content:
Allah. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. From Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, from Fatimatuz Zahra (a.s.), daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). She said: I heard Fatimah (a.s.) say: My father, the Messenger of Allah, came to visit me one day. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O Fatimah.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace.' He said: 'I feel a weakness in my body.' I said: 'I seek refuge in Allah, O my father, from that weakness.' He said: 'O Fatimah, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it.' I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it. I began to look at him, and his face was shining like the full moon in its perfection and beauty. It was not long before my son Hasan arrived. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said: 'O mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah.' I said: 'Yes, your grandfather is under the cloak.' Hasan approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah. Do you grant me permission to enter under the cloak with you?' He said: 'And upon you be peace, O my son and master of my pond (Hawd), I have granted you permission.' So he entered under the cloak with him. It was not long before my son Husayn arrived. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O my son, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said to me: 'O mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak.' Husayn approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, peace be upon you, O one whom Allah has chosen. Do you grant me permission to enter under the cloak with you both?' He said: 'And upon you be peace, O my son and intercessor of my Ummah, I have granted you permission.' So he entered under the cloak with them. After that, Abul Hasan, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) arrived and said: 'Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah.' I replied: 'And upon you be peace, O Abul Hasan and O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'O Fatimah, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah.' I said: 'Yes, he is here with your two sons under the cloak.' Ali (a.s.) approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Do you grant me permission to be with you under the cloak?' He said to him: 'And upon you be peace, O my brother, my successor, my caliph, and the bearer of my standard, I have granted you permission.' So Ali (a.s.) entered under the cloak. Then I approached the cloak and said: 'Peace be upon you, O my father, O Messenger of Allah. Do you grant me permission to be with you under the cloak?' He said: 'And upon you be peace, O my daughter and part of me, I have granted you permission.' So I entered under the cloak. When we were all gathered under the cloak, my father, the Messenger of Allah, took the two ends of the cloak and raised his right hand toward the sky and said: 'O Allah, these are my Ahlul-Bayt, my elite, and my close ones. Their flesh is my flesh, and their blood is my blood. What hurts them hurts me, and what saddens them saddens me. I am at war with those who war against them, and at peace with those who are at peace with them. I am an enemy to those who show enmity toward them, and a lover of those who love them. They are from me and I am from them. So bestow Your blessings, benedictions, mercy, forgiveness, and pleasure upon me and upon them, and remove impurity from them and purify them with a thorough purification.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Then Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, said: 'O My angels and dwellers of My heavens, I have not created the established sky, the spread-out earth, the luminous moon, the bright sun, the rotating planets, the flowing seas, or the sailing ships, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak.' The trusted Gabriel said: 'O my Lord, and who is under the cloak?' The Almighty and Majestic said: 'They are the people of the house of Prophethood and the mine of the Message: they are Fatimah and her father, her husband, and her sons.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Gabriel said: 'O my Lord, do You grant me permission to descend to the earth so that I may be the sixth among them?' Allah said: 'Yes, I have granted you permission.' So the trusted Gabriel descended and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. The Most High, the Exalted, sends you greetings and honors you with salutations and respect, and says to you: By My Might and Majesty, I have not created the established sky, the spread-out earth, the luminous moon, the bright sun, the rotating planets, the flowing seas, or the sailing ships, except for your sake and your love. And I have been granted permission to enter with you, so do you grant me permission, O Messenger of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'And upon you be peace, O trusted one of Allah's revelation, yes, I have granted you permission.' So Gabriel entered with us under the cloak. Then my father said to me: 'Allah has revealed to you, saying: *Verily, Allah intends to keep away from you, O Ahlul-Bayt, all impurity and to purify you with a thorough purification.*' Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Ali (a.s.) said to my father: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me what is the merit of this gathering of ours under the cloak before Allah?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'By the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me for the Message, this story of ours is not mentioned in any gathering of the people of the earth, in which there is a group of our Shia and lovers, but that mercy descends upon them, the angels surround them, and they seek forgiveness for them until they disperse.' Ali (a.s.) said: 'Then, by Allah, we have succeeded, and our Shia have succeeded, by the Lord of the Kaaba.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said again: 'O Ali, by the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me for the Message, this story of ours is not mentioned in any gathering of the people of the earth, in which there is a group of our Shia and lovers, but that mercy descends upon them, the angels surround them, and they seek forgiveness for them until they disperse.' There is no distressed Shia, and among them is a worried one, but Allah removes his worry. There is no one with a sorrow, but Allah removes his sorrow, and no one seeking a need, but Allah fulfills his need. Ali (a.s.) said: 'Then, by Allah, we have succeeded and attained happiness, and likewise our Shia have succeeded and attained happiness in this world and the hereafter, by the Lord of the Kaaba.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him dwell in Your earth in obedience and enjoy him in it for a long time. O Lord, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. First of all, we offer congratulations to all of you on the 15th of the blessed month of Ramadan, the birth of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). 15th of Ramadan, 3 AH, is the day when, in the most beautiful house of Medina, after the Dhuhr prayer, the second Quran of Imamate descended in the lap of purity of the matchless Batul as Hasan. Which Hasan? The one who is the son of the Master of both worlds, the complete nobility of the universe, the second name for beauty, the likeness of the Prophet, the first interpretation of Surah al-Kawthar, the one who saved Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) from the taunts of not having offspring, the first of the family of Muhammad, the mountain of forbearance, the messenger of patience, and the Imam of an Imam like the Master of Martyrs, Imam Husayn (a.s.). Yes, dear ones, on this luminous night, we, the Strong Rooh team, are present once again with that program, with that quiz for which you all were waiting very impatiently. Yes, we have brought 'Sit-e-Akbar: The Grand Quiz Competition' before you at this time. Before the discussion begins, before this presentation starts, let us tell you a few things about the quiz. The link for the quiz is present in the live chat right now and that link has become active. Yes, so we request you all that those who have already registered, please click on that link and check your name, your mobile number, and your email ID so that if your name appears among the lucky winners, there is no difficulty in reaching you. Check if all those things are correct or not. The second thing is that if any person has not registered yet, you can still register by clicking on this link. As soon as you click on this link, five questions will appear before you, and the answers to these questions will be in an option form, but every option is not correct; indeed, only one option for each question is correct, and to know that correct answer, you will have to listen to this presentation very carefully. Insha'Allah, during this presentation, during this discussion, the answers to all those questions will be provided to you. So let us begin our presentation, and to present this presentation before you, we have two brothers present here, Brother Tauqeer Sahab and Brother Ahsan Jafri Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. Insha'Allah, we will discuss Imam Hasan (a.s.), and because Imam Hasan (a.s.) arrived in this world in the blessed month of Ramadan, so Insha'Allah, there will be some discussion related to the month of Ramadan. On one side is the son of Ali, and on the other side is the month which is the 'Ali' (the highest) of the months. So Insha'Allah, our brothers here will shed some light on both these things. Brother Tauqeer, we would like you to tell us something more about this, Insha'Allah, and take the discussion forward. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. We offer congratulations to all the attendees on the blessed birth of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), and let us learn some things about this blessed month of Ramadan from his own words. Imam Hasan (a.s.) says that once a Jew came to the service of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and asked: 'Tell me, why are only 30 days of fasting obligatory upon Muslims, whereas more days of fasting were obligatory upon past nations, so what is the reason for this?' In response to this, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated that when Prophet Adam (a.s.) ate that fruit from the tree in Paradise, it remained in his stomach for 30 days. Therefore, 30 days of fasting were made obligatory upon this Ummah. However, Allah (s.w.t.) bestowed this favor upon the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) that this fast was only for the days, not for the nights. Meaning, the believers and the followers of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) can eat and drink during the night. So, Tauqeer brother, this means that for the previous nations, fasting during both day and night was obligatory; they had to fast during the day and also during the night. And this is a special favor and grace of Allah upon the Ummah of the Messenger of God, that we only have to fast during the day, not at night. Indeed, and as this hadith continues, after stating this, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) recites that verse of the Quran which is very famous and well-known regarding the blessed month of Ramadan, that is, Surah Al-Baqarah, verses 183 and 184, in which it is stated: 'Kutiba 'alaikumus-siyamu kama kutiba 'alalladhina min qablikum la'allakum tattaqun' and further 'Ayyaman ma'dudat', meaning that fasting for the blessed month of Ramadan has been made obligatory upon you, just as it was made obligatory upon the nations before you for a few days. So, this is the complete summary that 30 days of fasting are obligatory for the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and day and night fasting is not obligatory. The second thing I want to know, Tauqeer brother, is that since you just said that 30 days of fasting are obligatory for the Ummah of Muhammad, it often happens that we only fast for 29 days in the month of Ramadan. So, have our fasts become invalid, or did we make a mistake there? This is a very good and very pertinent question of yours, Abul brother. And look, this is the miracle of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) that they read our minds in their narrations beforehand. So, they have certainly clarified this in this very hadith, where they state: 'Ma min mu'minin yasumu shahra ramadanal ihtisaban'. Here, the word 'ihtisaban' means according to the days. Meaning, if it is a 30-day fast, then according to 30 days, and if it is 29 days, then according to 29 days. So, this point becomes clear here. Meaning, if the month is of 29 days, we only have to keep 29 fasts in the month of Ramadan. Yes, meaning there is no restriction of 30 or 29 days; whatever the month is, the believer has to fast accordingly. After understanding this, that Jew asked further, 'Tell me, if a person fasts in this blessed month of Ramadan, what is his reward?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) replied that if a person fasts in this month, Allah will bless him with seven qualities. The first quality is that if, God forbid, there is any forbidden food in his stomach, He will melt it away. Second, this fast will become a cause for closeness to Allah's mercy. Third, this fast will be an atonement for the act of our father Adam (a.s.). Fourth, the agony of death will be made easy for him. Fifth, he will be protected from the intensity of hunger and thirst on the Day of Judgment. Sixth, Allah will grant him salvation from the fire of Hell. And seventh, Allah (s.w.t.) will bless him with the pure and clean foods of Paradise. We find this narration in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 93, Page 369. Jazakallah Tauqeer brother, meaning through this hadith, We also learned the reason for fasting, and at the same time, the various rewards for keeping a fast also became clear to us. And now, along with this, I will request Ahsan brother to tell us and our viewers a few things regarding Imam Hasan (a.s.). Certainly. First of all, I offer my congratulations to you and all the viewers on this joyous occasion, and we pray to Allah (s.w.t.) that for the sake of this Eid, He may hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). As far as the biography of Imam Hasan (a.s.) is concerned, there is an interesting hadith in which not only is the status and rank of Imam Hasan (a.s.) described, but his Imamate is also proven. It is a hadith known as Hadith-e-Lawh. When Imam Hussain (a.s.) was born on the 3rd of Shaban, at that time, Allah (s.w.t.) revealed this Lawh (tablet) to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), as a gift, which was presented to her, in which the name of every Imam from the first to the twelfth is mentioned, and their life circumstances are briefly described. And quite clearly, when Imam Hasan (a.s.) is mentioned in this hadith, Hadith-e-Lawh, it is stated for Imam Hasan (a.s.), and this is a Hadith-e-Qudsi, meaning the words are of Allah Himself. It is the word of Allah. In the hadith, it is found for Imam Hasan (a.s.) that 'Faja'altu Hasanan ma'dina 'ilmi', meaning I have made Hasan the mine of My knowledge, the treasurer, the mine of knowledge. Allah is saying this, attributing it to Himself, that I have made Hasan the mine of My knowledge. 'Ba'da inqida'i muddat-e-abihi', meaning after the completion of his father's term, meaning look, this is an immediate indication of the continuous Imamate of Imam Hasan (a.s.), the Imamate and Caliphate without any gap, that after the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (a.s.), the era of the Imamate of Imam Hasan (a.s.) will begin. And such hadiths, in which the name of the Imam is clearly stated, there is not just one hadith, but there are many other such hadiths in which the 12 Imams are mentioned by name. Such hadiths are called 'Nass'. Nass means clear text. It is clearly stated who the Imam will be. Meaning, there should be no doubt or suspicion left. Exactly, there is no room for doubt or suspicion. And it cannot be translated otherwise, no other meaning can be derived from it; only one meaning will be derived, and this 'Nass' which comes from Allah (s.w.t.), this hadith which is called 'Nass', which is clear text, is the proof of being an Imam. And our belief as Shia Imamis is that whether it is a Prophet or an Imam, for them to be an Imam or a Prophet, 'Nass' is required. Correct. This concept and this belief do not exist among us, this attitude is not found among us. This method does not exist among us that someone should be made an Imam through Shura (consultation) or through Ijma (consensus). There is no selection, nor is there an election. These are all 'Mansus min Allah' (appointed by Allah), that is why the Imam is called 'Mansus min Allah' among us because there is 'Nass' for him. Correct. And on one hand, there is this 'Nass' for the Imamate of Imam Hasan (a.s.), and on the other hand, Allah (s.w.t.) blesses every one of His Hujjah (proofs) with two things. Two special things that distinguish him from false claimants, the distinction between the two is through these two special things that Allah grants. One is what we call Divinely Gifted Knowledge, 'Ilm-e-Ghayb', which Allah grants. The second is Divinely Gifted Power, the power that Allah gives. Meaning, one is Ilm-e-Ghayb, the second is power. Allah gives these two things to His Hujjahs. So here, Ahsan brother, I would like to pause and draw the attention of our viewers to a very important point. If you look closely at this hadith, Allah has used the word 'Faja'altu'. Indeed. 'Ja'ala' means to make. And this word has appeared many times in the Quran. Especially if we look, Allah has used this word whenever He has talked about making an Imam or a Caliph. For example, Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 30, in which Allah (s.w.t.) says to Prophet Adam (a.s.), 'Inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah'. Look, the word is 'Ja'il', which is made from 'Ja'ala'. Meaning, I am going to make a Caliph on this earth, and no one else can make one. If we look at the other verse, Allah (s.w.t.) says in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 124, to Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), and says, 'Inni ja'iluka linnasi imama', I have made you an Imam for the people. Meaning, twice in the Quran, this word has been used, and Allah has taken the responsibility of making an Imam upon Himself and has not left this matter to the people. Subhan Allah. Ahsan brother, as you mentioned that Allah gives His Hujjah two specific things, one is Ilm-e-Ghayb and one is power. So, can we bring some such examples from the life of Imam Hasan (a.s.), from his biography, through which it becomes absolutely clear that Imam Hasan (a.s.) also had Ilm-e-Ghayb and power? Indeed, a very good question. And as far as Ilm-e-Ghayb is concerned, a very interesting incident is found in the narrations that once Prophet Khidr (a.s.), who is a Prophet, a Prophet of God, comes to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and asks a few questions. At that time, Janabe Salman was also with the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and Imam Hasan (a.s.) was also present. Ali (a.s.) said to Imam Hasan (a.s.), 'Son, you answer his questions.' Now, Janabe Khidr (a.s.) asked many questions, but I would like to draw the attention of our viewers to one question, which is a very interesting question. Janabe Khidr (a.s.) asked, 'Akhbirni 'anir-rajul', tell me about a man, 'Kayfa yadhkuru wa yansa', how does he remember something and how does a person forget something? Now, this matter relates to the Unseen (Ghayb) because, apparently, no one knows the reality of this. These are all matters of the Unseen, and only the one who has a connection with the Unseen, who has Ilm-e-Ghayb, and whom Allah has granted this special Ilm-e-Ghayb, can make us aware of these matters of the Unseen. Indeed. So, it is an interesting question: how does a person remember something, and how does he forget? In response to this, Imam Hasan (a.s.) says that the heart of a human, the Mawla says, is inside an empty, hollow space, a socket. Which is covered by a lid, meaning it is kept covered. When a person sends Salawat, sends Durood upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), at that time that covering, that lid, meaning the thing with which it was covered, is removed from above the heart, that lid is removed, the heart illuminates, the heart shines, and then the thing that the person had forgotten, he remembers it. This happens only because of Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. But the opposite also happens. Because he had asked two things. One, how a person remembers something, and how he forgets. Imam Hasan (a.s.) says that if he did not do so, meaning if that person did not recite Salawat or recited half-hearted Salawat, did not recite complete Salawat, complete Salawat meaning if he did not include the 'Aal' (progeny), if he did not recite Salawat upon the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), then what will happen? That same heart which is inside the socket, which has a covering on it, which is kept covered, it will remain covered just like that, that heart will become dark, will become black, and then the thing that the person remembered, he will forget that too. This is the Ilm-e-Ghayb of Imam Hasan (a.s.) which Imam Hasan (a.s.) possessed, through which the Imam answered this question. Subhan Allah Ahsan brother, I think very few people would have heard this virtue of Salawat, and thank you very much for telling us a new thing, a good thing. And after hearing this hadith, this interesting thing also comes to mind that whenever our poets or our Zakirs, while reciting a Majlis or in a gathering, if God forbid, something slips from their mind, they immediately ask the audience to recite a Salawat, and perhaps this is the reason that all those people are aware of this hadith, so they want the audience to recite Salawat so that they can remember the forgotten thing. It is not far-fetched, it is not far-fetched, there is no room for doubt in this that if a person recites Salawat, he remembers that thing. And one more thing in this regard that I would especially like to say to my children and also to the youth, meaning those who are preparing for their exams or doing some professional course, if at the time of any exam or while memorizing something, if the thing does not come to mind, does not sit in the memory, So there is nothing to worry about. We have an excellent weapon like Salawat. We should use it. Whenever you are studying or memorizing, if there is a possibility of forgetting, send Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and proceed. Insha'Allah, through the blessings of this Salawat, we will remember that thing. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. Indeed, Tauqeer Bhai, you said it absolutely correctly, and I would also like to tell the viewers that you will remember the forgotten thing. That is, you must first study that thing. If you think that you will pass the exam just by reciting Salawat, that will not happen. First, you have to study, you have to memorize, and God forbid, if you forget, then you can use Salawat as a support to recall it. Anyway, Ahsan Bhai, as you told us this incident from the life of Imam Hasan (a.s.), through which it becomes quite clear that Imam Hasan (a.s.) possessed Ilm-e-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen), and we are sure that there must be many other such incidents. Since there is no time, we cannot narrate all those incidents here. So, can you tell one more such incident that would also reveal Imam Hasan (a.s.)'s power, that Allah had given him a special power, a capability? Certainly, by all means. There is an interesting incident in this regard as well, but before that, it is necessary to clarify one thing for the viewers: this power that Allah gives to His Hujjahs (proofs), this power that the Hujjat-e-Ilahiya possesses, is a special kind of power. That is, through this, the entire Alam-e-Takween—Alam-e-Takween means creation—and although humans have no interference in this creation. This is solely and exclusively for Allah. That is, just as Allah has created us, we have no role in it. No human has any role in how our eyes are or how our face is. Allah has created this entire universe, and no human has any interference in it. But this power that Allah gives over this entire creation is called Wilayat-e-Takwini. That is, through which Allah's Hujjah has complete command, complete power, and complete strength over this entire Alam-e-Takween. And examples of this are present in the Holy Quran itself. Not only the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), but even before the Ahlulbayt, Allah had granted this Wilayat-e-Takwini to the Prophets (a.s.). It is granted by Allah. He gave it to the Prophets and also to the Imams (a.s.). Let me present a verse before you that mentions Wilayat-e-Takwini, which mentions Hazrat Isa (a.s.). There is a verse in the Holy Quran where Hazrat Isa (a.s.) says: 'Inni qad ji'tukum bi-ayatin mir-rabbikum' (Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord). What is the sign? Hazrat Isa (a.s.) says: 'Anni akhluqu lakum' (I create for you). This power to create—the Creator is Allah, but Allah granted this power to Hazrat Isa (a.s.). This is that Wilayat-e-Takwini. Allah has made the Prophets and Imams (a.s.) masters over this entire creation. Hazrat Isa (a.s.) was saying that I create for you. What? 'Minat-teen' (from clay). 'Kahay'atit-tair' (in the shape of a bird), I create a bird. And then what do I do? I blow into it. 'Fa-anfukhu fihi fayakunu tairan bi-iznillah' (And then I blow into it, and it becomes a bird by the permission of Allah). And then, as soon as I blow into it, by Allah's permission—see, this will come up again—by Allah's permission, by Allah's leave, that is, this is Allah-granted strength, power, and capability. By Allah's permission, it becomes a bird. Now, when Hazrat Isa (a.s.) made the bird from that clay, he only made its shape from the clay. He did not create its organs inside—like the heart inside the body, he did not create the veins of the bird. He only made a shape from the clay. He just blew into it, and by Allah's permission, it became a flying bird. This is one sign mentioned therein. Then, in the same verse, Hazrat Isa (a.s.) says: 'Wa ubri-ul akmaha' (And I heal the blind from birth), I restore their sight. 'Wal-abras' (and the leper), those who suffer from leprosy, I can cure them. 'Wa uhyil mawta bi-iznillah' (And I bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah), and I give life to the dead by Allah's permission. I grant them life. And if you want, 'Wa unabbi-ukum bima ta'kulun' (And I can inform you of what you eat), I can also tell you what you should eat or what you are eating. 'Wama taddakhiruna fi buyutikum' (And what you store in your houses), and I can also tell you about the things you have to store in your house. That is, both things are there. Both the power of creation and the knowledge of the unseen are found in this verse regarding Hazrat Isa (a.s.). That is, Hazrat Isa (a.s.) stated so many things. This is verse number 49 of Surah Al-e-Imran. Indeed, Ahsan Bhai, you said it very correctly, and we find numerous examples of this in the lives of the Prophets. Such as Hazrat Musa (a.s.) turning his staff into a snake. The successor of Hazrat Sulaiman, Asif bin Barkhiya, bringing the throne of Bilqis into his presence in the blink of an eye. The she-camel of Hazrat Saleh emerging from behind the mountain. Imam Kazim (a.s.) and Imam Reza (a.s.) turning the picture of a lion on a carpet into a real lion. And among the companions, Janabe Salman-e-Farsi ordering the dogs in Mada'in to bite all the thieves. All these are the effects of the Wilayat-e-Takwini granted by Allah. Indeed, and you said a very good thing. Especially the mention of Janabe Salman at the end. Now, these things, this Wilayat, Allah gives not only to the Prophets and Imams (a.s.) but also to ordinary humans. Why? And this is also pointed to in the Holy Quran. Wilayat-e-Takwini is found in the Quran itself. That is, if someone understands the reality of the Quran, perceives it, and attains the power of the Quran, then that person can possess Wilayat-e-Takwini. As it is mentioned in the Holy Quran, Surah Ar-Ra'd, which is the 13th Surah, verse number 31. What is commanded therein? The command of the Lord of Majesty is: 'Wa law anna qur'anan' (And if there were a Quran)—that is, if a human perceives the reality of this, its power, and attains it, then what will happen? 'Suyyirata bihil jibal' (by which the mountains could be moved from one place to another). And 'Wa qutti'at bihil ard' (and the earth could be folded), that is, 'qatta' means to cut, meaning the earth will be folded; a human can attain the power of Tayy-ul-Arz (traversing the earth instantly). 'Qutti'at bihil ardu aw kullima bihil mawta' (the earth could be folded or the dead could be spoken to). A human can talk to the dead. This is if someone understands the reality of the Quran. That is, even an ordinary human, if they understand the reality of the Quran, if they attain its reality and its power, then even an ordinary human can possess all this power. Indeed, indeed. Allah has given these powers to the Quran. The Holy Quran possesses this power, and the person who understands it, perceives its power, can possess all these things; they can possess Wilayat. Just as Tauqeer Bhai gave the example of Janabe Salman. And the interesting thing to note here is that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left behind two precious things for us. One is the Quran and the other is the Ahlulbayt. And what word did he use for both? Thaqalayn (the two weighty things). Both are equally precious things. And it has been said to walk with both of them together. So it is impossible that one thing has that power and the other does not. So the power that the Quran has, the same power the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have. Because both are equal to each other. And similarly, when you were talking about the Wilayat-e-Takwini of Imam Hasan (a.s.), the incident that comes to mind is that once Amr ibn al-Aas, the ruler of Sham, Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan—now this is an incident of the court of Sham, an incident of Sham. What happened in this was that Amr ibn al-Aas gave a suggestion, a piece of advice to the ruler of Sham, that Imam Hasan (a.s.) was present in the court at that time. So he said, let us do one thing: ask Imam Hasan (a.s.) to go to the pulpit and deliver a sermon. Imam Hasan (a.s.) will go, and if he hesitates, even a little bit, then his hesitation will become completely clear before the people, and through this, Imam Hasan (a.s.) will feel humiliated, will feel embarrassed. So they hatched a conspiracy. The ruler of Sham immediately addressed Imam Hasan (a.s.) and said, 'Ya Aba Muhammad, law sa'adta al-minbara wa wa'aztana' (O father of Muhammad, if you could ascend the pulpit and preach to us). He tried to request the Imam in this way. Anyway, the Imam knew better. The Imam went to the pulpit without any hesitation. He began with the praise and glorification of Allah. After beginning the praise and glorification of Allah, now the Imam, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), introduces himself. And how is the Imam introducing himself? Those people, Amr ibn al-Aas, did not realize this. He thought he would conspire against the Imam and succeed. But on one side is Iblis's plan, and on the other side is Allah's plan. When Imam Hasan (a.s.) came to the pulpit, what did Imam Hasan say? 'O people, man 'arafani faqad 'arafani' (Whoever knows me, knows me). But whoever does not know, let him know that 'Ana al-Hasanu ibnu Aliyyin ibni sayyidatin-nisa' (I am Hasan ibn Ali, the son of the Chief of the Women of the Worlds), 'Fatimata binta Rasulillah' (Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah, s.a.w.a.). And after this, Imam Hasan (a.s.) made a... By doing this, he stated his praise. 'Ana ibnu Rasulillah' (I am the son of the Messenger of Allah). 'Ana ibnu bashir-in nadhir' (I am the son of the bearer of glad tidings and the warner). He is again pointing towards the Prophet. That I am the son of that Prophet who gave glad tidings, that Prophet who warned. 'Ana ibnu man bu'itha rahmatan lil-alamin' (I am the son of the one who was sent as a mercy to the worlds). I am the son of the one who was sent as a mercy for the worlds. 'Ana ibnu man bu'itha ilal-jinn wal-ins' (I am the son of the one who was sent to all jinns and humans). I am the son of the one who was sent for all of them. The one who is the most excellent among all of Allah's creation, I am his son. And after that, here, he introduced himself with reference to the Messenger of Allah. After this, Imam Hasan (a.s.) introduces himself with reference to his father, the Commander of the Faithful. What does he say? 'Ana ibnu sahibil fada'il' (I am the son of the master of virtues), the one who is the owner of all virtues, I am his son. 'Wa ana sahibul mu'jizatid-dala'il' (And I am the son of the master of miracles and proofs). And the clear proofs, those things through which people are rendered helpless, those things which people cannot understand, I am the son of those proofs. That is, pointing towards the Master of the Universe himself. 'Ana ibnu Amirul Mu'minin' (I am the son of the Commander of the Faithful). And in this way, Imam Hasan (a.s.) kept praising himself. And this—there is a long list, that is, through many things, Imam Hasan (a.s.) praised himself. But now, as Imam Hasan (a.s.) kept praising himself, kept introducing himself, those people—both Amr ibn al-Aas and the ruler of Sham—they kept getting worried that what we thought and what is happening here? So, they got scared. And the ruler of Sham started feeling that through Imam Hasan (a.s.)'s speech, all the people present in the court, or all the Syrians present, would be mesmerized. He would charm them all, amaze them. So he immediately said—first he tried to stop him. He said, 'No, first you...'—you know how it is sometimes—'No, you must be tired, here are some wet dates' (offered to the Imam), 'take these, stop.' Okay, but the Imam kept introducing himself. Finally, he said in exhaustion, 'Ya Aba Muhammad, injil' (O father of Muhammad, come down). He requested Imam Hasan (a.s.) that no, now you come down. 'Faqad kafa ma jara' (What has happened is enough). That is, now they did not have the strength and power to bear any more. That is, whatever happened is enough, just come down. Then, as soon as the Imam came down from the pulpit, the ruler of Sham said, 'I feel that you are in a great hurry to become the Caliph, but that will not happen.' That is, he taunted the Imam. Then the Imam replied in return. Now the Imam explained who a Caliph is. Because he had used the word Caliph. Now Imam Hasan (a.s.) explains who a Caliph is. The Imam says that a Caliph is not one who acts against the Sunnah of Allah and His Messenger, who rules through oppression. What did the Imam say? The Imam said that a Caliph is one who follows the path of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger, who walks upon it. A Caliph is not one who walks on the path of oppression. One who changes the Sunnah, who invents innovations, is not a Caliph. One for whom everything is just this world, is not a Caliph. And he has become so busy in the greed of the world that he even forgets that he is the ruler of something that is not going to last forever, something that is going to end. He is going after such a thing. And the more he goes after this world, he is not free from its consequences, from the results that will follow. Whatever he goes after in the world, he will have to face the consequences. So a Caliph is not one who goes after the world. A Caliph is one who follows the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger. Now, as soon as the Imam stated this, a person from the Umayyads, a young man, could not bear it. What did he do? He came there and started using bad words against Imam Hasan (a.s.), started cursing everyone. So much so that not only against Imam Hasan (a.s.) but also against his noble father, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), he started cursing everyone. He started remembering them with bad words. And the sentence of the narration is that he crossed all limits. He crossed all limits. He exceeded every boundary. Now, as soon as this happened, when he committed blasphemy against the Imamate, he insulted Imam Hasan (a.s.) and spoke ill of the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin), Imam Hasan (a.s.) utilized his Wilayat-e-Takwini (creative authority). And what did the Imam do? The Imam prayed to Allah. How did the Imam pray to Allah? 'Allahumma ghayyir ma bihi min an-ni'mah' (O Allah, change the blessing that You have given him). 'Waj'alhu untha' (Make him a woman). Turn this man into a woman. 'Li-yu'tabara bihi' (So that it may be a lesson for those who are watching). Now, as soon as the Imam (a.s.) made this prayer, the Imam had only just prayed. That person from Banu Umayya saw himself transforming into a woman. In fact, the narration states that even his beard fell off. In this way, Allah transformed him from a man into a woman. Now, as soon as he turned into a woman, Imam Hasan (a.s.) immediately addressed him and said, 'O Jubi! Go away from here. Malaka wa mahfil ar-rijal? (What business do you have in a gathering of men?) Go away from here.' This was Imam (a.s.)'s Wilayat-e-Takwini. This entire Wilayat—the power we are talking about, the power that Allah grants to His Hujjah (Proof)—this was just one example of it. Now, as soon as that happened, he turned into a woman. The Imam also shook off his mantle and began to leave. As he was leaving, he saw where the matter had started, what Amr ibn al-Aas had thought, and where it had reached. On one side was the Imam (a.s.)'s sermon, the Imam (a.s.) introducing himself through such words. After that, the Imam (a.s.) defined what a Caliph should be—that a Caliph should be someone who acts according to the Quran and the Sunnah of the Messenger. After that, the way the Imam (a.s.) dealt with that Umayyad, transforming him from a man into a woman—seeing all this, even Amr ibn al-Aas was stunned for a moment. He felt that it was necessary to change the atmosphere a little, otherwise, if Imam Hasan (a.s.) took a few more steps, who knows what might happen. So, he requested the Imam (a.s.), 'Master, please sit down. Sit, sit, you sit. I have something to ask you.' He tried to change the atmosphere here. Imam Hasan (a.s.) understood, and the Imam sat down. As soon as he said, 'Master, I have something to ask you,' the Imam said, 'Sal amma badalaka' (Ask whatever you wish). Ask whatever you wish to ask. Now, look, only the son of the master of the pulpit who said 'Saluni' (Ask me) can make such a claim—that 'ask whatever you wish.' Because this is a claim of knowledge, and only one who has a connection to Ilm-e-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen) can make such a claim. Indeed. Because the person in front hasn't even asked the question yet, and making such a claim—'ask whatever you wish'—is proof in itself that the Imam has the answer to whatever he asks. Therefore, he asked three questions from the perspective of ethics. First, he asked, 'Master, tell me, what is Karam (nobility)?' What is called nobility in English. 'What is Karam, Master?' Second, 'Tell me, what is Najdah?' Najdah means help, support, assistance. And third, 'Master, tell me, what is Muruwwah?' What we call Muruwwah in Urdu/Hindi, which is called chivalry in English. He asked about these three things: what is Karam, what is Najdah (help/assistance), and what is Muruwwah. The Imam (a.s.) quickly explained all three things. The Imam said, first of all, Karam. Karam is when a person gives in an excellent manner, without the other person asking. That is, when a person gives without being asked, it is called Karam. That is why he is called Karim. Why are the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) called Karim ibn Karim? For all our Imams (a.s.), including Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), why are they called Karim ibn Karim? Because even if a person has not asked, they still give. They give by seeing our needs. That is why they are called Karim. Then, as far as the question of Najdah (assistance/help) is concerned, the Imam says that the most important thing in this help is that a person should stay away from the haram. And when a makruh (disliked) act comes before him, he should abstain from it, and he should exercise patience in performing that act. That is, he should be patient and not even go near what is makruh. Through that, he helps; he helps himself. And third, what is Muruwwah? The Imam said Muruwwah means the most important and necessary thing: that a person protects his religion. Protects his religion, keeps himself away from filth and impurities, stands up to fulfill the truth, always stands for the truth, raises his voice for the truth, and spreads peace and security. These things are included in Muruwwah. And when the Imam answered these three questions and explained these three things, the Imam (a.s.) left. Now, when the Imam left, the ruler of Sham (Syria) came back to Amr ibn al-Aas, because he was the one who gave the original advice. So, the ruler of Sham said to Amr ibn al-Aas, 'You have corrupted all the people of Sham.' That is, in a way, these people used to follow me until now, but now they won't. Now everyone will go towards Imam Hasan (a.s.). Yes, the people realized the status of Imam Hasan (a.s.). Yes, absolutely. And the Imam proved through Wilayat what the status of the Imam (a.s.) is. After that, as soon as the ruler of Sham said this, do you know what Amr ibn al-Aas replied? This is a strange sentence of his as well. He turned to the ruler of Sham and said, 'Do you think that all these people of Sham around here, all these Syrians present here, love you for the sake of religion and faith? It is not like that at all. They only love you for your wealth. They are with you only because their worldly needs are being fulfilled through you. And they fear your sword because they fear for their lives, and they are greedy for your wealth; that is why they are with you. Whereas Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.) has proven through his words that he does not need you.' Now, the matter ended here. But what about that man who had turned into a woman? Now, the news spread throughout Sham that such an incident had occurred and that Imam Hasan (a.s.) had turned a man into a woman. His wife came to the Imam (a.s.) and came weeping, requesting, 'Master, please, just as my husband was before, please return him to his original state.' So when she came, weeping, and asked with humility, the Imam (a.s.) accepted her request. Now look, this is the Karim (Generous one). That the Imam had punished him, but after that, he forgave him. Why? Because that woman had come with a recommendation. The Imam (a.s.) understood her helplessness, and the Imam (a.s.) prayed to Allah again, and that man who had turned into a woman was transformed back into his original state. This is an excellent incident you have narrated, through which it becomes clear that Imam Hasan (a.s.) possessed Wilayat-e-Takwini, the power given by Allah, through which he turned a man into a woman and then back from a woman into a man. But along with this, the opponents use this to cast doubts in the minds of our youth, saying things like, 'If your Imam has Wilayat-e-Takwini, so much power, and you also say that the rights of your Imams were often usurped, then when the rights of the Imams (a.s.) were being usurped, why didn't they use this Wilayat-e-Takwini?' Why didn't they use it? It is a very good question, and it is not as if this question was asked to the Imams (a.s.) for the first time. That is, it is not as if this question has been raised for the first time. The opponents who ask this question—Alhamdulillah, we are followers of those 12 and 14 Masumeen (a.s.) who never left us thirsty or wanting for an answer to any question. They have provided us with the answer to every question. Exactly this question—why don't they use Wilayat-e-Takwini when your right was usurped? This exact question was asked to the father of Imam Hasan (a.s.), the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And this is also a very interesting incident. It is not the goal to narrate the whole incident, otherwise, it would take a lot of time. The name of the book is 'Khasa'is al-A'immah'. Sharif Razi, Sayyid Razi (may Allah be pleased with him), who compiled Nahj al-Balagha, this book is also compiled by him, 'Khasa'is al-A'immah'. In it, when he discusses the Khasa'is (characteristics) of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), on page 46, he has recorded an incident. It is a very long incident. Briefly, what is found in this incident for us as an answer to this question is that people came to Ali (a.s.) and asked this very question. What happened was that the Commander of the Faithful had given a verdict between two people. Let's narrate it quickly. The Commander of the Faithful gave a verdict between two people. One of them was a Kharijite. But the verdict went against the Kharijite. So, the Kharijite accused Ali (a.s.) of injustice, saying that Ali (a.s.) had committed injustice, and he expressed his dissatisfaction with the verdict. Ali (a.s.) immediately transformed him into a black dog. So, everyone present there was worried, everyone was stunned—what exactly happened? So the Imam (a.s.) asked them, 'Why are you stunned?' They said, 'Master, what have you done? How did you do this?' The Imam (a.s.) turned and asked them, 'Tell me, is your Prophet superior or is Solomon (Sulayman) superior?' Just now, Tauqeer Bhai also mentioned Solomon's successor, Asif ibn Barkhiya. Yes. So Ali (a.s.) asked this question, 'Tell me, is your Prophet superior or is Solomon superior?' They said, 'Undoubtedly, our Prophet is superior.' Then the Master asked again, 'Is the successor of your Prophet superior or is the successor of Solomon's Prophet superior?' Because Solomon's successor, Asif ibn Barkhiya, had brought the throne of Bilqis in the blink of an eye, in less than a moment. So, if I transformed him like this, then what is there for you to be surprised about? What is there to be surprised about? There should be no surprise in this. On this, those people asked the Master, 'Master, O Commander of the Faithful, Master, when you have this power, when you have this ability, then Master, what is the need for Ansar and Awan (helpers and supporters)?' Can't you fight the enemies just like that? Indeed. On this, the Imam (a.s.) replied, and in his reply, the Imam (a.s.) recited a verse of the Quran and explained it to them. The Imam says, it is verse number 26 and 27 of Surah Al-Anbiya. 'Faqala bal...' No, it is not like that. 'Ibadun mukramun' (They are honored servants). We are those who are the honored servants of Allah. 'La yasbiqunahu bil-qawl' (They do not precede Him in speech). They never speak before Allah; they speak according to Allah's command. 'Wa hum bi-amrihi ya'malun' (And they act by His command). So, this Wilayat-e-Takwini that we are using, we are using it according to Allah's command. It is not as if we are doing it on our own or according to our own will. No, this is Allah's command; when it is Allah's command, then this Wilayat-e-Takwini will be used. It will not be used in every matter. And as far as the question is concerned—since the rights of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) were usurped, it is not that their rights will always remain usurped. Their rights will return. And that, Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah, will happen after the reappearance (Zuhur) of Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.). Indeed. And Imam Hasan (a.s.) himself pointed towards this. Once, Imam Hasan (a.s.) was passing through the Prophet's Mosque. He went into the Prophet's Mosque. There, many people from Banu Umayya were sitting. And the sentence of the narration is that those people, seeing the Imam (a.s.), started signaling to each other with their eyes. That is, there is a way people signal to each other with their eyes, 'Oh, look at him, oh, look.' So, in this way, they signaled to each other upon seeing Imam Hasan. Imam Hasan (a.s.) also saw them, how they were signaling to each other with their eyes. The Imam went into the mosque, prayed two rak'ats of prayer. When the Imam was coming out from there, the Imam said to those people, 'I have seen the signals you made to each other about me.' Then the Imam said, 'By God, you will not rule for a day, but our rule will be for two days. You will not rule for a month, but our rule will be double that, two months. And you will not rule for a year, but our rule will be two years.' That is, whatever you want—that is, in the end, what Allah will grant us will be double what He grants you. And then, another interesting thing Imam Hasan (a.s.) mentioned in this Hadith: 'As far as your rule is concerned, you have usurped our right, but you are helpless in one thing, you are forced in one thing. What?' The Imam says, 'Inna lana'kulu fi sultanikum' (We can eat in your rule, we can drink in your rule). That is, we can wear clothes as we wish, we can marry, we can live comfortably with whatever transport we want. 'But when our rule comes, you will not be able to live comfortably like this. When our rule comes.' And now, when those people heard this, they turned and asked the Mawla, 'O son of Muhammad, how can this be? While you are the most generous (Sakhi).' Now look, they immediately remembered the Imam's generosity. When they were in need, they immediately remembered the Imam's generosity. 'You are generous, meaning you are very compassionate and merciful. So how can it be that you will not show mercy to others? Meaning, you lived in peace and security under the rule of others, but others will not live in peace and security under your rule.' The Imam said, 'No, it is not like that.' The Imam explained. What did the Imam say? 'Innahum aduna' (They are our enemies). These people, the people of Banu Umayya, they are hostile towards us according to the devil's plot. Although the devil's plot is weak, it is feeble. But when our government is established, we will rule according to Allah's command, and that is more intense, strong, and powerful. Meaning, in our government, there will be no mercy for any hypocrite. Indeed. And in the same way, this very matter is what the month of Ramadan, the blessed month of Ramadan, Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) has taught us, that in every night, Dua-e-Iftitah... This same point is also alluded to in Dua-e-Iftitah. 'Allahumma inna narghabu ilaika fi dawlatin karima' (O Allah, we desire from You a noble state). Mawla, O Lord, we have a longing. For what? For that state, that government, that noble government, we have a longing in our hearts. What kind of government? 'Tu'izzu bihal-Islama wa ahlahu' (By which You honor Islam and its people). 'Wa tudhillu bihan-nifaq wa ahlahu' (And by which You humiliate hypocrisy and its people). Isn't it? Why isn't it? This is the treasure of the noble court of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Such supplications are for us. Besides, who else has such supplications? If you go to any non-Shia, you will not find this treasure of supplications in this way. Imam Hasan (a.s.) has also pointed towards that noble state, the government of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), in which the hypocrite will not sit in peace. Yes. Certainly, Ehsan Bhai, we are all waiting for that government and noble state. And our prayer to the Lord of the Worlds is that He keeps us always attached to the mantle of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Not only in this world but also in the hereafter. And as it is found in the hadith, the love and Wilayah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is very effective. Once, Janab-e-Abu Dharr (r.a.) asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) about the love of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and he said, 'O Abu Dharr, whoever loves Hasan and Husayn and their progeny sincerely, the fire of Hell will not be able to harm his face.' Even if his sins are equal to the sand of the desert. But the condition is that he must be a believer. And in another hadith, we find that Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that whoever bears malice against Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Husayn (a.s.), then on the Day of Judgment, he will be raised in such a way that there will be no flesh on his face. And he will not be worthy of our intercession. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He keeps us attached to the love of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and especially Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (a.s.). We are grateful to our brothers that they told us many things related to Imam Hasan (a.s.) in an excellent manner. Such as, Allah gave the chosen Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.) knowledge of the unseen (Ilm-e-Ghayb), power, and Wilayah-e-Takwini, and in this connection, a few questions related to this were also asked of you all. We hope that you have given the correct answers. And with this, this presentation ends here, and at the same time, that link is also closed. Immediately after this, Insha'Allah, there will be Dua-e-Iftitah, and as soon as Dua-e-Iftitah ends, the names of the lucky winners will be announced to you, and the first prize winner will get an Apple iPad, and two second prize winners will get Lenovo tablets, and Insha'Allah, three third prize winners will get smartwatches. So, if your name comes among the lucky winners, meaning to know this, you will have to stay with us. Insha'Allah, immediately after Dua-e-Iftitah, the names of the winners will be on your screen, Insha'Allah. Let us all get ready for Dua-e-Iftitah. [Recitation of Dua-e-Iftitah follows in Arabic] [Continuation of Dua-e-Iftitah in Arabic] [Continuation of Dua-e-Iftitah in Arabic] [Continuation of Dua-e-Iftitah in Arabic] [Continuation of Dua-e-Iftitah in Arabic] [Conclusion of Dua-e-Iftitah in Arabic] O Allah, we complain to You about the loss of our Prophet, may Your blessings be upon him and his family, the absence of our guardian (Imam), the multitude of our enemies, the scarcity of our numbers, the severity of the trials upon us, and the hostility of time against us. So, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and assist us against this with a victory from You that You hasten, a distress that You remove, a triumph that You honor, a sovereign of truth that You manifest, a mercy from You that You cover us with, and a well-being from You that You clothe us with, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. So, through the blessings of guidance, may all our troubles be removed. And the greatest trouble today for the Arsh—that is, for Hazrat-e-Karrar—is the occultation of the Imam of the Time. O Lord, for the sake of Imam Hasan al-Mustafa (a.s.) and for the sake of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the Time. Viewers, the time has come to know the names of the lucky draw winners. So let us first see who the three third-prize winners are. Their names are on your screen. Congratulations to you all. Let us move forward and see who the second-prize winners are. Yes, these are two people. Let us see who those two lucky people are who will receive two Lenovo tablets. Many congratulations to you as well. Now, the name of the first-prize winner of the Sibt-e-Akbar Grand Quiz Competition is about to appear. Yes, it is right here on your screen. Congratulations to all of you on these prizes, and we also offer congratulations to all the viewers for listening to the remembrance of Imam Hasan (a.s.); the reward that comes from that will be much greater than these prizes. These prizes are nothing in comparison to that. With this, let us conclude our program. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
