It examines the distinction between the Shia perspective of Imamate as a divinely ordained office and the political interpretations that led to historical opposition. The session also addresses the challenges faced by the Ahlulbayt, the nature of human defiance against divine authority, and concludes with the announcement of the winner of the Ghadeer Paymaan-e-Ilaahi Mega Quiz 2026.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their relief, and curse all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat, son of Al-Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their relief, and curse all their enemies. Furthermore, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says in the Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: "This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion." Allah Almighty says in the Holy Quran: Today I have perfected your religion for you, "and completed My favor upon you," and I am pleased that Islam is your religion; I am pleased with Islam as a religion for you. On this occasion of Ghadir, we all reach the holy presence of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.) to offer him congratulations and greetings, and we discuss a few points regarding Ghadir. If we examine the biography and life history of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), we see that throughout his life, along with his Prophethood, he continuously announced his successor. From the very first day, when Allah commanded him, "And warn your closest kindred," the Prophet invited his relatives and announced his Prophethood. In that same gathering, the Prophet announced the immediate Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). In this way, on many occasions, the Prophet continuously introduced the Wilayah and Caliphate of Ali (a.s.). The purpose and goal of this was that when the Messenger of Allah departed from this world, this chain would continue until the Day of Judgment. Because Islam did not come for a fixed time, but rather until the Day of Judgment, and therefore the chain of the Prophet's successors must continue until the Day of Judgment. And the Prophet clearly stated this: "This religion will remain honorable and established as long as there are twelve successors in it, all of whom will be from the Quraish." If we look at this chain of twelve successors, the twelve Caliphs, it is found only in the school of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and these are the twelve Infallible Imams (a.s.) who are the progeny of the Messenger. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made continuous arrangements for this. When we look at the belief in Imamate, we find that all Muslims—there is no exception—believe in Imamate. Everyone believes in Caliphate, that there should be a Caliph and a successor after the Prophet. If we look at this belief, there are two important aspects: the first is the importance of the belief, and the second is what is called "who occupied this position," or who took this office. In terms of importance, all Muslims agree—there is no exception—that this is a very important belief. It is so important that when the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) occurred, the Muslims left the Prophet's funeral and went to Saqifah to fight and argue over the Caliphate, grabbing each other by the collars. Read the entire story of Saqifah to determine who the Caliph is after the Messenger of Allah. And it is surprising that the theologians and scholars justified this action by saying that Imamate is such an important matter that the Muslims left the Prophet's funeral so that they could select or elect a successor or Caliph after the Prophet. So, a question arises: if it was such an important matter, did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) not realize it himself? Did he not think that he should appoint his successor after him? This was such an important matter that if you look at how much the Prophet emphasized the importance of a will in his life—a will is a very important thing—if you study the books of Hadith, you will see it is explicitly written that the importance of a will is such that if someone dies without a will, it is as if they did not die upon the religion. And who do they attribute this Hadith to? They attribute it to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself. And even though the Prophet knew the importance of a will, he did not appoint his own successor? How surprising this is. This is against reason. Anyway, no one denies its importance. Now the question arises: "who occupied this position," who snatched it, took it—whatever word you may use—who took this position? The main dispute is over this: the Shia belief is that Imamate is a divine position and office, an extension of Prophethood. This is the Shia belief, whereas the belief of other Muslims was that it is like a tribal position, like a government. Therefore, we can appoint someone as our leader through elections or some other method of selection, election, or Shura (council). Their position had no connection or relation to this divine office. But in the school of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it is not like that. This position is purely a divine position, like Prophethood. Just as Allah appointed the Prophet, Allah appoints the Imam, and this Imam will remain until the Day of Judgment. As we believe, and history and traditions are witnesses, all Muslims have described in detail that the Prophet repeatedly appointed Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) on many occasions, in different words and different styles. For example, he introduced him by saying, "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate." Somewhere he said that Ali is to me as Aaron was to Moses, which is called the Hadith of Manzilat: "O Ali, you are to me in the position of Aaron to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me." The only difference is that there is no prophet after me. Or he compared the Ahlulbayt to the Ark of Noah: "The likeness of my Ahlulbayt is like the Ark of Noah." What is the example of my Ahlulbayt? It is like the Ark of Nuh (Noah), like the ship of Nuh. "Man rakibaha naja" - whoever boards it will be saved, "wa man takhallafa anha gharaqa wa hawa" - and whoever stays behind, whoever does not board it, will perish, will be destroyed, will drown. Meaning, their afterlife will be ruined. And there are many such hadiths, many such narrations where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) consistently introduced Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and... his 11 successors as his successors, in the capacity of his caliphs. Among which, the main culmination, where this series of announcements ended, where did it happen? At Ghadir-e-Khumm. At Ghadir-e-Khumm, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) reached there during the Hajjat al-Wida (Farewell Pilgrimage), after leaving Makkah and reaching towards Madinah, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made a formal announcement. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave a long sermon, and this sermon itself is worthy of investigation and research. It is a very powerful sermon in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) discussed various principles of religion, of which Imamate was one topic. Otherwise, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) discussed various topics. So, among them, one sentence the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) uttered—first, he took a confirmation from the people after the sermon. He asked the people, "Alastu awla bikum min anfusikum?" (Am I not more authoritative over you than you are over yourselves?) Meaning, this was a verse of the Quran. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was presenting a verse of the Quran to the people in his own words. What was the Quranic verse? "An-Nabiyyu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim" (The Prophet is more authoritative for the believers than their own selves). The Quran stated this in very clear terms. But the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was reminding them again here at Ghadir, because it is possible that people might have forgotten, as the memory of Muslims is generally quite weak. That is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) took confirmation again. "Alastu awla bikum min anfusikum?" (Am I not more authoritative over you than you are over yourselves?) They said, "Bala" (Yes), everyone said in one voice, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, you are, certainly, Bala, O Messenger of Allah." So when he said, "I am the authority," then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced, "Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyun mawlah" (Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla). Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla. Even after that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed: "Allahumma wali man walahu" (O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him), "wa adi man adahu" (and be an enemy to whoever is an enemy to him), "wansur man nasarahu" (and help whoever helps him), "wakhdhul man khadhalahu" (and forsake whoever forsakes him). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) formally made this announcement, and after that, the people pledged allegiance at the hands of Ali (a.s.). The caravan stayed at Juhfa for three days. People pledged allegiance, people came and congratulated him. They said, "Bakhin bakhin ya Ibn-e-Abi Talib" (Congratulations, congratulations, O son of Abi Talib). "Asbahta mawlaya wa mawla kulli mu'minin wa mu'mina ya muslimin wa muslima" (You have become my Mawla and the Mawla of every believing man and woman, and every Muslim man and woman). People formally congratulated him, and there was a gathering of 120,000 pilgrims, and everyone witnessed this. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) formally lifted Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and raised him on his hands and introduced him. Now, the various objections to this—that the meaning of 'Mawla' was not that, or the meaning of 'Mawla' was not this, and all such things—we have often given answers to these, that no, the meaning of 'Mawla' is absolutely clear. 'Awla' to 'Mawla' is completely clear, and different words have also been used. "Man kuntu waliyyahu fa Aliyyun waliyyuh" (Of whomsoever I am the Wali, Ali is his Wali). The matter is finished. So we do not call the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) a friend; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is 'Awla', our 'Mawla'. Anyway, this is a topic—answers to this have often been given. One objection is that if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced it in front of 120,000 people, how did so many people forget? Whereas there were great, prominent companions among them, great people, so how did they forget? How is it possible that people did not remember? And why did the people not listen to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? It is impossible that those individuals who were ready to give their lives for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would not listen to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). So look, the answer to this question is quite simple: if anyone studies the life of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), his biography, they will see that even in the 13 years of life in Madinah, people refused to accept many things the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said and did not listen to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and many such incidents are found. If we were to discuss all those incidents here, it would require a very long speech, or let's say at least five speeches, or five to ten speeches, to discuss how many times the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was disobeyed. How many times? Let me present a few examples for you. One that is most important, and everyone knows it, and it is present in all books of hadith, is what is called 'Raziyat al-Khamis'. No one can deny this. 'Raziyat' refers to a very great tragedy. 'Raziyat' means a great calamity. And 'Khamis' means Thursday. This is the incident of Thursday. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was ill, very ill, during which his martyrdom occurred. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to the people, "Bring me a pen and inkpot so that I may write something for you after which you will never go astray." This is exactly like the Hadith al-Thaqalayn where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "I am leaving among you two weighty things: one is the Book of Allah and the other is my Ahl al-Bayt, and these two will not separate from each other until they meet me at the Hawd al-Kawthar." And in exactly the same way, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, "Bring it, let me write something, meaning in written form, so that after that you will never go astray." So, some individuals there understood what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would write, which would cause their schemes and plans to fail. Therefore, those people started making a commotion, and all this is documented, authenticated. Yes, it is not that we are citing it from Shia books, no, no. They started making a commotion, making noise. They created so much disturbance that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had to say, "Qumu anni" (Get away from me). Go, all of you, leave from here. And only his Ahl al-Bayt remained. Everyone else left, and they refused to give the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) a pen and inkpot. This was a very painful incident. In fact, it did not stop there. Some individuals there even said, "Inna hadha ar-rajula yahjur" (This man is delirious, God forbid). And look at the words—those who are familiar with Arabic will understand this. "Inna hadha ar-rajula"—these are words of extreme disrespect. "This man, this man has lost his mental balance." Astaghfirullah Rabbi wa atubu ilayh, may my mouth be filled with dust. You observe, look. Is this tragedy not enough for the Muslims? Now they try to justify it in different ways, but anyway, look, a person can justify anything, but that is not the subject of our discussion right now. Let me give another example: once the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told the people to take off their Ihram and wear normal clothes. The Muslims objected to this, asking why he was giving this order. What is the reason? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) felt this so badly that he became extremely angry. He was very upset. So people came and asked, "O Messenger of Allah, you seem very angry, why are you angry?" The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, "Amuru wa la uta" (I command, but I am not being obeyed). Let me give another example: in the Battle of Uhud, this is the incident of the Battle of Uhud, there was a passage. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told some people to guard this passage. Do not leave this passage under any circumstances. Do not leave this passage under any circumstances. But what happened was that as soon as those who were guarding the passage thought that they had won the battle, they left the passage for the sake of war booty and got busy looting the booty. So much so that the enemies entered through that very passage and attacked the Muslims from both sides, due to which the Muslims were defeated in the Battle of Uhud. And so much so that the Prophet's uncle, Janab-e-Hamza, was also martyred, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) circled around the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and saved his life. He fought a fierce battle and saved the Prophet's life. And besides that, another incident is found where a companion had a great love for the books of the Jews. Despite having Islam, despite having the Quran, he used to go to the Jews to gain knowledge. You can check this yourself. Everything is available on the internet today; if you just search for one word, you will find it. "Ahmarat wajnatahu"... let me explain the meaning of the keywords of the whole incident. He had a great love for them and came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, can I go to the Jews and write notes from their lectures?" The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) forbade him. He said, "No. It is enough here; what I am giving you of the teachings of Islam is enough." Still, he went a second time. Then when he came, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was angry again. So he is saying, "I forbade you, yet you are doing the same thing, coming and asking the same question again." But even after being forbidden twice, he went a third time. And after going, when he brought the notes the third time and said, "O Messenger of Allah, look, I have brought all these notes," the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was so angry that the phrase in the hadith is that "ahmarat wajnatahu" (his cheeks turned red with anger). Think about it, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) who is "Rahmatan lil-Alamin" (Mercy to the worlds), was so extremely angry that his cheeks turned red. He ordered to call the people to the mosque. "As-salah, as-salah, al-jama'ah" (Prayer, prayer, congregation). The Ansar understood that this is not the time for prayer, so why is this order being given? And they came with their unsheathed swords and said, "Who has angered the Messenger of Allah?" This whole incident is present. You see, there are numerous such incidents in the life of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). If you look, then when they were not listening to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in his lifetime, then what would they listen to after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? And specifically, whom did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appoint at Ghadir? Whose announcement did he make? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had been appointing throughout his life, but the final appointment, the call, was "Amir al-Mu'minin", and who was "Amir al-Mu'minin" Ali ibn Abi Talib? The one against whom all those so-called people, individuals, Muslims, all held a grudge in their hearts. As the phrase is found in the hadith, in the supplication, "Wa yuqatilu ala ta'wil" (And he fights for the interpretation of the Quran), "wa la ta'khudhuhu fi Allahi lawmatu la'im" (and he does not fear the blame of any blamer in the way of Allah), "qad watara fihi sanadid al-Arab" (he had killed the great warriors of the Arabs in it), he killed their great brave men, their great chiefs, "wa qatala abtalahum wa nawasha dhu'banahum" (and he killed their heroes and he dealt with their wolves), and their great heroes he killed, "wa nawasha dhu'banahum" and their wolves, the soldiers, the warriors, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) tore them apart in the battles. What was the result? "Fa awda'a qulubahum ahqadan" (So he deposited hatred and malice in their hearts). Their hearts were filled with hatred for Ali (a.s.). He had killed someone's father, someone's brother, someone's uncle, someone's nephew, someone's relative, Ali (a.s.) had killed them. In various battles, in various battles of Islam, "Badriyyah wa Khaybariyyah wa Hunayniyyah wa ghayruhun" (Badr, Khaybar, Hunayn, and others), in different battles, "fa adhabbat ala adawatihi wa akabbat ala manabadhatihi" (therefore they insisted on enmity towards him and decided that they would oppose Ali (a.s.) in any case, they would not let him become the Caliph). Therefore, after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Ali (a.s.), the 'Amir al-Mu'minin', was left all alone. Those people—the enemies and the opposition—brought forward various excuses to deprive Ali (a.s.) of this position. And what was one of those excuses? For instance, that Ali is still very young and he jokes too much, and other such things that were all matters of Jahiliyyah (ignorance). These were things of Jahiliyyah, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself said many times—you can see this in the hadiths—'I fear for you that you will turn back to Jahiliyyah after me.' This was the Prophet's fear during his own lifetime. So, what was the reason? Well, the reason was that those people thought Imamat was a worldly position, a tribal position, a worldly position. They never understood it as a divine position, as the Shia understand that Imamat is a divine position, that Imamat is an extension of Prophethood. They thought it was a tribal position. The Quran has clarified this. In the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) lifetime, in Surah Al-i-Imran, verse 154, it is stated: 'wa ta'ifatun qad ahammathum anfusuhum' (and a group whose own selves had become important to them), and there is a group that only thinks about themselves, that gives importance to themselves. For them, their own personal interests and goals were important. 'yazunnuna billahi ghayral-haqqi zannal-jahiliyyah' (they think of Allah other than the truth, the thought of ignorance). They harbor the same unjust thoughts about Allah that they used to harbor during the time of Jahiliyyah. Meaning, that same belief of Jahiliyyah still remains with them. This is being said about the time of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). 'yaquluna' (they say), they come to the Prophet and say, 'hal lana minal-amri min shay' (is there anything for us in this matter/authority?). Meaning, will we get any government or not? We are fighting so much alongside you, so won't we get anything? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'qul innal-amra kullahu lillah' (Say, indeed the matter belongs entirely to Allah). Government, this decision, Imamat, and Caliphate—the decision for this rests solely with Allah. No one else has the right to it. 'innal-amra kullahu lillah' (the matter belongs entirely to Allah). Then the Quran says, 'yukhfuna fi anfusihim ma la yubduna laka' (they hide within themselves what they do not reveal to you). But this thought still remains in their hearts, which they are not revealing to you. They are not revealing this matter to you, and what is that thought? 'yaquluna law kana lana minal-amri shay'un ma qutilna hahuna' (they say, 'If we had any authority in the matter, we would not have been killed right here'). If we don't get authority, then what is the benefit of us fighting? Why have we come here to fight? So Allah answered this thought of theirs as well. Look, they did not express this with their tongues; they thought it, but Allah answered that too. 'qul' (Say), O Prophet, tell them, 'law kuntum fi buyutikum labarazalladhina kutiba 'alayhimul-qatlu ila madaji'ihim' (If you had remained in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their places of death). Even if you sit in your homes and do not help Allah, and do not come to fight, it does not matter. Allah will bring a people who will come out and defend Islam. This is clearly known from Surah Al-i-Imran, verse 154. And similarly, you know that at the occasion of Ghadir, it is not just these three verses that are usually recited, but 22 verses were revealed. 22 verses, as present in the narrations. One of those verses was verse 28 of Surah Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), where the Quran says, 'dhalika bi-annahum ittaba'u ma askhatallah' (That is because they followed what angered Allah) and the reason for that is, what did they follow? What did they follow that Allah is displeased with? 'wa karihu ridwanahu' (and they disliked His pleasure), and they do not like Allah's pleasure, 'fa-ahbata a'malahum' (so Allah rendered their deeds worthless). In the commentary of this verse, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) says, 'ittaba'u ma askhatallah' (they followed what angered Allah), meaning they followed what Allah did not like, and 'wa karihu ridwanahu' (and they disliked His pleasure), and the Imam says, 'karihu 'Aliyan' (they disliked Ali), 'wa kana 'Aliyun ridhallahi wa rida rasulihi' (and Ali is the pleasure of Allah and the pleasure of His Messenger), 'amara Allahu bi-wilayatihi' (Allah has commanded his Wilayah) on various occasions. But when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made the announcement, it is found in the narrations that some people were there who became angry. What did they say? 'wa qalu yuridu Muhammadun (s.a.w.a.) an yaj'alal-imamata fi ahli baytihi' (And they said, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) wants to place the Imamat in his Ahlulbayt). The Messenger of Allah wants this Imamat to remain in his Ahlulbayt. 'fa-kharaja minhum arba'atu nafarin ila Makkah' (So four people from among them went back to Mecca) and 'wa dakhalul-Ka'bah' (they entered the Kaaba) and 'wa ta'ahadu wa ta'aqadu' (and they made a covenant and an agreement among themselves), meaning they made an agreement among themselves, 'wa katabu' (and they wrote), and they formally put this agreement into writing, 'wa katabu fima baynahum kitaban' (and they wrote a document among themselves). And what was written in it? That 'in amata Allahu Muhammadan (s.a.w.a.) aw qatalahu' (If Allah causes Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) to die or kills him), 'la yuraddu hadhal-amru fi ahli baytihi abadan' (the matter of authority will never return to his Ahlulbayt). Then another verse was revealed, and this was verse 79 and 80 of Surah Az-Zukhruf, where Allah says, 'am abramu amran fa-inna mubrimun' (Or have they devised a plan? We too are devising a plan). Have they decided something? They have decided? It does not matter, Allah says we have also decided. 'am yahsabuna anna la nasma'u sirrahum wa najwahum' (Do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations?). 'bala wa rusuluna ladayhim yaktubun' (Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording). Not only do We hear, but Our angels, the Kiraman Katibin, are formally writing down their words and their whisperings. And then, you know the whole incident of what happened—that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made the announcement, and regardless, people kept Ali (a.s.) deprived of this Imamat and Caliphate, the consequences of which we are seeing to this day. Whereas the reality is that Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari formally wrote a book on the occasion of the announcement of Wilayah at Ghadir-e-Khum, titled 'Al-Wilayah fi al-Radd 'ala al-Harqussiyah', a complete book by the name of 'Al-Wilayah', in which he narrated the Hadith of Ghadir through 75 chains of narrators. And this hadith is so Mutawatir (widely transmitted) that no one can deny it. No one can deny it. So, let us on this occasion of Ghadir convey this message to all people and explain that this message was from Allah, conveyed to the people through the Messenger, and it is the responsibility of all of us to take this message to every corner of the world so that no one has any excuse left. Wa akhiru da'wana anil-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim, Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim, wa salla Allahu 'alayka ya Wali al-'Asr, adrikna wa la tuhlikna. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. First of all, we extend our heartfelt congratulations to you all on Eid-e-Ghadir and Eid-e-Mubahala. We pray that Allah (s.w.t.) grants us the ability to remain steadfast on the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and grants us the honor of spreading this message to the whole world. To go or not to go is a matter of destiny, but unfortunate is the one who did not even intend. We pray that everyone is granted the honor of Ziyarat, and whoever the winner is, we humbly request them to definitely perform Ziyarat on behalf of all of us. And now the time has come that you all were waiting for, that is, the announcement of the mega winner of the Ghadir Payam-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz 2026, who is being selected through our computerized lucky draw system. The one who is going to receive that prize, which every lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) desires, which is the Ziyarat of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimayn, and Samarra, meaning the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. So let's see who that lucky person is, and their name is here on your screen. Seerat Zahra Syed from Pune, many congratulations to you that you are the lucky one who has received the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. The TSR team is once again grateful to all you viewers. Please remember us in your prayers that the Lord of the Worlds grants us the ability to organize such quizzes. And if you have any feedback or suggestions regarding this series, please contact us on our WhatsApp number [number removed]. And if you also want to join us in conveying the message of the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then you just need to subscribe to our channel. Like our videos and share them as much as possible with your contacts so that the message of the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) reaches as many people as possible. And besides this, if anyone wants to join in this good deed through donation, they can send a donation to our provided bank account details or by scanning the QR code. Allah and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will give its complete reward, Insha'Allah. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that He hastens the reappearance of the Heir of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), our Imam of the time, and grants us the ability to hold firmly to the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) until the very end, and counts those who convey our videos to others among those who propagate the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). title: Ek Saanp Ne Diya Maula Ali (a.s.) Ko Jinn Ka Paigham | ایک سانپ نے دیا مولا علی (ع) کو جن کا پیغام
excerpt: This lecture recounts a miraculous event at Masjid al-Kufa involving Imam Ali (a.s.) and a dragon (thuban). The speaker explains that the dragon was a messenger from the Jinn who came to convey their deep devotion and obedience to the Imam. The narrative emphasizes that the love and Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) are the keys to salvation, suggesting that if all humanity followed the example of the Jinn, Hell would not need to exist.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon the Prophet and his progeny. It is Allah's favor that He granted us the opportunity to perform acts of worship here in Masjid al-Kufa today. This is the mosque where two rak'ahs of prayer are equal to 100 rak'ahs elsewhere. When we enter Masjid al-Kufa, the door we usually enter through is called 'Bab al-Thuban'. 'Bab al-Thuban' means the Gate of the Dragon. There is an incident and a hadith associated with this. Once, when the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), was delivering a sermon from the pulpit of Kufa, a dragon (thuban) appeared from the very back of the mosque. When the people saw the dragon approaching, they moved toward it to kill it. The Master of the Universe (a.s.) said to them, 'Wait, stop! May Allah have mercy on you. Stop, wait a moment, because this dragon has been sent with a specific command.' So the people stopped. The people stopped and restrained themselves. The traditions state that the dragon came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and brought its mouth close to the ear of the Master of the Universe. The narration says that whatever Allah willed, the dragon whispered into the ear of the Master of the Universe. Then, the dragon descended, and Ali (a.s.) followed it, bidding it farewell. When the people saw this whole scene, the narration says they asked, 'O Commander of the Faithful, will you not tell us what the dragon said to you?' Ali (a.s.) replied, 'Yes, I will tell you. It did not come as an ordinary dragon. It was a messenger from the Jinn. It said to me, "I am the Wasi (successor) of the Jinn." It said to me, 'I am the Wasi of the Jinn, and I have brought a message for you from them.' The leader of the Jinn said, 'I have brought this message to you.' What is the message? He says, 'If all humans loved you, O Ali, just as our tribe of Jinn loves you, and if they obeyed you just as we obey you, then Allah would not have sent anyone from among the humans to Hell.' Allahu Akbar! The virtue of the Master of the Universe is such that the reward for loving him is that the fire of Hell will not touch that person. Alas for those who regret this; if all people loved Ali (a.s.) the way the Jinn love him, Allah would never send anyone to Hell. And that is why it is found in another tradition that if all humans and Jinn together accepted the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), Allah says, 'I would not have created Hell at all.' This means Hell was created specifically so that the enemies of Ali (a.s.) could go there. Allah will burn only the enemies of Ali (a.s.) in Hell, not the lovers and followers of Ali (a.s.). Not the lovers and followers of Ali (a.s.).
