title: Majlis 4 |  Allah Ki Reza | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | #Muharram 2026 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual concept of 'Rida' (contentment with Allah's decree) as the pinnacle of faith and submission. The speaker connects the necessity of total obedience to Allah and the Ahlulbayt with historical lessons from the era of the Prophet and the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse culminates in the heart-wrenching account of the martyrdom of Ali Asghar, illustrating the ultimate sacrifice and the profound patience of Imam Hussain (a.s.).
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome is for the righteous and the certain. Blessings and peace be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Blessings of Allah be upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the Time, the guardian of our affairs, our master, our leader, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate friend, the secure refuge and the helper of the distressed and the seekers of help. May my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Our master and leader, Al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon them), said: 'And know that a good deed (Ma'ruf) earns praise and brings a reward.' If you were to see a good deed as a person, you would see it as beautiful and handsome, pleasing to the beholders and surpassing all the worlds. Our master and leader, Al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon them) spoke the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. The Hadith-e-Sharif I have chosen for this discussion, in that Hadith, the Master of Martyrs, Imam Hussein (peace be upon him), says: 'And know that a good deed earns praise.' Know that a good deed (Ma'ruf) is something that, if you perform it, people will praise you, and in the Hereafter, you will also receive a reward for it. If you were to see a good deed as a person, you would see it as beautiful and handsome; it is extremely beautiful. Truly handsome. If Allah brings this good deed on the Day of Judgment, it will be pleasing to the beholders and will encompass the entire universe. This Ma'ruf—and I have submitted to you that this is the teachings of the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them). And this is the very thing that Lady Zaynab (peace be upon her) established after the tragedy of Karbala. This is a very important matter, and you should never take it lightly. There should be no other criteria for it; there should be no criteria of quantity, such as whether few people are coming, or any other criteria. The only aim and purpose is that this Ma'ruf should continue to spread. Just keep spreading it, and what is the main thing in this? The main thing is that the teachings of the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) should be discussed. This is very important. There are many traditions and hadiths regarding this, but because time is very short and we must not deviate from the topic, we will try our best. So, regarding the Hadith we were discussing, that the Prophet—meaning Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought a Hadith, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah is giving you a gift that He has not given to anyone before you, and will not give to anyone after you.' The Prophet asked, 'What is it?' Among all the things, he said the first thing Allah is giving is 'patience' (Sabr). Then he asked, 'What is better than that?' He said, 'Contentment' (Rida). 'What is after that?' He said, 'Asceticism' (Zuhd). 'After asceticism?' He said, 'Sincerity' (Ikhlas). 'Sincerity, and after that?' Then he said, 'And the culmination, the summit, and the peak of all these things is Trust' (Tawakkul). Meaning, relying on the essence of Allah, which we discussed in the first session. Then we discussed patience, and yesterday I submitted to you how the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who was the embodiment of patience, practiced it. So, continuing that sequence today, and since today and tomorrow are the final sessions, I will try to cover things quickly. Yesterday, time was spent on narrating history, but it was necessary so that the youth should know the history. Unfortunately, actual history is not studied here. It is very regrettable. But it should be studied. As someone beautifully said, because nowadays people have stopped reading about Khaybar and Khandaq from the pulpits, mothers have stopped giving birth to brave children. Subhan Allah. Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali. Therefore, it is also very important to know what the contribution of Ali (peace be upon him) was. Because such intense propaganda took place that people forgot. Among those who came to Ali (peace be upon him), there were many who did not know him or recognize him. So, let it not be that we end up in the same state. And it is happening, it is happening, which is why I am saying that our current condition is that we are very far from the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. So, we try to present as many hadiths as possible for you. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Then the Prophet asked, 'Is there anything better than this?' Gabriel said, 'Yes.' The Prophet asked, 'What is it?' He said, 'Contentment' (Rida). Rida. So the Prophet asked, 'O Gabriel, what is meant by Rida?' Rida means satisfaction. Satisfaction. Now, the answer Gabriel gave is very important. Gabriel replied, 'The Razi (the one who possesses this Rida), he does not become angry with his Lord, whether he receives from the world or not.' Meaning, the Razi is one who is never angry with Allah. The Razi is one who is never angry with Allah, whether he gets the world or not. Whether something of the world comes to him or goes away, whether Allah grants something or takes it away. This is a very important thing. He never gets angry, he never asks in the court of Allah, 'O Lord, why did You do this?' And this is the criterion of faith. It is the criterion of faith. 'Fala wa Rabbika' (But no, by your Lord) is a verse from Surah An-Nisa. 'Fala wa Rabbika'—by your Lord, 'La yu'minun' (they will not believe) until that time they will not be believers. Look, this is the Holy Quran. 'Fala'—the 'La' came once. 'Wa Rabbika'—by your Lord. 'La yu'minun'—they will not believe. The 'La' came twice. Did you notice? And along with the two 'La's, there is also an oath. And who is swearing the oath? Allah is swearing. Does Allah need to swear? Allah does not need to swear. Allah wants to show that this is such an important thing. 'Fala wa Rabbika la yu'minuna hatta yuhakkimuka fima shajara baynahum thumma la yajidu fi anfusihim harajan mimma qadayta wa yusallimu taslima'—O Prophet! They will not believe until they make you the judge in all their issues and problems. What a thing. In all their problems, and when you have made a decision, they should have no objection to it. This is a verse of the Quran. And after that, Allah emphasized it in another verse. That was the verse of Surah An-Nisa; listen to the verse of Surah Al-Ahzab: 'Ma kana li-mu'minin wa la mu'minatin'—for any believing man or woman, Allah even included believing women, consider this. Any believer, meaning any man or woman, has no choice 'idha qada Allahu wa rasuluhu'... When Allah and His Messenger have made a decision. 'An yakuna lahumul khiyaru min amrihim.' Did you notice? So in the first verse, it was: 'By your Lord, they will not believe until they make you the ruler, and when you have made a decision, they should not feel even an atom's worth of doubt in their hearts and should submit completely to you.' This is called being Razi, this is called being Razi. And what is in the second verse? No believing man or woman has the right that when Allah and His Messenger have made a decision, 'An yakuna lahumul khiyaru min amrihim'—to say, 'My opinion is this.' No one has the right. Allah and His Messenger have made a decision. Now after that, nobody has any right to say anything. So if Allah gave the command, 'O Messenger, proclaim what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, you have not conveyed His message,' then the Prophet said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyyun mawlah.' Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali. Now no one has the right to present their own opinion on it. 'My perspective is this, mine...' No, absolutely not. So then, what did these Muslims do? Look at this aspect of history. Here is the Prophet's funeral, and there at Saqifah, leaving the Prophet's funeral, do you know who was at the Prophet's funeral? Meaning, look at the Messenger of Allah's funeral, let me give you a small example. If news of a great man's death comes, that so-and-so has passed away, all the city dwellers rush there. Here, the Messenger of Allah's funeral is lying there, and there is no one among the Muslims. Except for a few individuals: the Commander of the Faithful, Ibn Abbas, Salman—whom you could count on your fingers, that's all. Where were the rest of the main people? They were at Saqifah. And what were they doing? Arguing. 'I am the Caliph,' 'You are the Caliph,' 'I am the Caliph.' And I am not saying this; read their own books. I am speaking very quickly, I will not spend much time on this. Just look, when Allah said that Ali is the one, then who has the right? But they are saying, 'No, we are the Caliph.' The Ansar say, 'We gave you shelter.' The Muhajir say, 'No, but we are from the Prophet's tribe.' These are saying, 'We are from the tribe.' Those are saying, 'We spent money.' 'We gave you shelter. If we hadn't given you shelter, you would have been killed in Mecca.' How many Muslims were there in total in Mecca? How many total Muslims were there in Mecca, brothers? The young ones are the ones to answer. How many in Mecca? Look, I am saying we are very far from history. The number of Muslims in Mecca in 13 years was not above 80. And among them, there were people who had accepted Islam three or four times. You understand, right? Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad. Please, move a little forward. Move forward, move forward. Move forward. Is it clear to you? Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Did you notice? Some people were arguing there, and what were the words and the tone? Look, I won't say anything; you just go to Google. And see in Google what happened at Saqifah? Just type it there, and you will find out. 'I am the Caliph,' 'You are the Caliph,' 'I am this,' 'I am that'—they were arguing, and look at this aspect, and there was the funeral of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was performing the Ghusl and Kafan. Anyway, when one party gained the upper hand, they said, 'Pledge allegiance to one, come, let me pledge allegiance, let me pledge, let me pledge.' They forced the allegiance. Right? Now everyone pledge, everyone pledge. Now pledge quickly and finish this off. They pledged, it was done. Now he became the Caliph of the Muslims. Allahu Akbar. You understand, right? The end of Islam started from here, as Allama Iqbal says. That is why the beginning of 'Allahu Akbar' from Saqifah led to the situation today where a Muslim cuts a throat while saying 'Allahu Akbar.' So, he is not cutting someone else's throat; in reality, he is cutting the throat of humanity, the throat of Islam. As soon as the call of 'Allahu Akbar' reached the ears of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), what did Ali (a.s.) say? 'Salman, they have chosen their Caliph.' He did not say—Ibn Abbas asked, or perhaps he asked Abbas—'What is this Takbir?' Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) said, 'They have chosen their Caliph. They have selected him.' This was it. Islam was finished. That is why it is found in traditions. The Imam says that the foundation of Ashura was laid at Saqifah. And for us, for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), if any day can equal the day of Ashura in grief and calamity, it is the day of Saqifah. This is a tradition, a Hadith from the Imam. This is what happened to Islam. The problem with us is that we do not read. That is why we tell everyone, 'Brother, read, read.' Go and study, research, then you will know everything, everything will come to light. Anyway, so this 'Rida' (contentment)—meaning if Allah has decided, then one is 'la yaskhtu ala sayyidihi'—never angry with his Lord. 'Assaba minad dunya am lam yusib'—whether he receives the world or not, because the whole argument was about what? The world, authority, power. That is why, and in this, many people get angry too; if something slips out of their hands, they get upset. Did Allah only find our house? Did He not find any other house? Our young son died. Did you notice? That is why the Prophets and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) gave such great sacrifices so that you might think about your small sacrifices. And this world is brief. This world is very brief. It is here today, gone tomorrow. It has no comparison with the Hereafter. That is why the Prophet said, and Imam Hussain (a.s.) said on the day of Ashura—Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) said that the Prophet said, 'Ad-dunya sijnul mu'min wa jannatul kafir' (The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever). And for the people of the world, what is this? It is paradise. Enjoy, do whatever you want. Look, a believer thinks before doing anything: 'Is this Halal or Haram? Is this permissible or not?' Insha'Allah, if we have time, we will read the Hadith; we will try. And then, look, did you notice the Hadith? The first thing is that he is not angry with Allah, no matter what happens. One. Second, Jibrail says, 'wa la yarda linafsihi bil-yasiri minal amal' (and he is never satisfied with his own deeds). Meaning, no matter how much he does, he will always think he has done nothing. Now, let me quickly tell a historical event here. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had a very staunch follower, Amr ibn Amr al-Khuza'i. What sentence did Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) say about him? When the Prophet was there, the Prophet had made a prayer for him. Do you know what prayer the Prophet made? The Prophet said, 'I am thirsty, will someone bring water?' So, before anyone else could rise, Amr—he was a young man, very young—nowadays kids say, 'You drink it yourself.' But what did Amr do? He jumped up. As they say in English, 'He leapt.' 'Wa saba'—in Arabic, they say he jumped and went and quickly brought water for the Prophet. The Prophet liked his gesture so much, Amr's gesture, that the Prophet said, 'Amr, you have gladdened my heart. May Allah keep you young like this until the end.' And Amr became old, 70-80 years old, and not a single hair of his turned white. Such was the Prophet's prayer. The Prophet prayed. This Amr comes to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and says, 'Ya Amir al-Mu'minin, by God, I love you so much. Not for any worldly gain, that you give me some worldly wealth, this or that. Nothing, by God, I do not love you for that. I only love you because you are the brother of the Messenger of Allah, the husband of Fatima Zahra, and the father of Hassan and Hussain. That is why I love you. If you tell me to break mountains and move them from one place to another, and if you tell me to empty the ocean bowl by bowl, and I keep doing this work my whole life, even then I would think I have not fulfilled the right.' And even if I defeat your enemies with my sword and strengthen the hearts of your friends, even then I would think I have done nothing. And Amr had done work, but it is not worth mentioning here. Right? But now, as soon as the martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) occurred, and after that, the Faqir of Sham (Muawiyah) gained the upper hand over everyone. So, he immediately issued an arrest warrant for Amr. He issued an arrest warrant, and after issuing it, Amr was immediately arrested. Meaning, Amr was in hiding for many days. When he saw that Amr was not being caught—Amr ibn Amr al-Khuza'i, write down the name, you can search for it—Amr ibn Amr al-Khuza'i. When he was not caught, what did he do? He abducted his wife. And when he abducted his wife, he said, 'Now, this news has spread, brother, your wife has been arrested. Now, if you don't come, then you know what will happen.' Meaning, you understand. So, Amr got himself arrested in Mosul, Iraq. Meaning, he had fled from Kufa to Mosul. So, from there, he got himself arrested. After getting arrested, as soon as he was caught, he wrote a letter to Muawiyah saying, 'Brother, Amr has been arrested. What should be done?' He said, 'Immediately cut his throat and parade him in the market with his head on a spear.' It is written in history books that this was the first head in Islam to be placed on a spear. After that, this same practice was repeated with Imam Hussain (a.s.). It happened with the martyrs of Karbala. This was the first time in the history of Islam. How many wars did the Prophet fight? Do you know? 77 battles. The Prophet fought 77 battles within 10 years. But in no battle did the Prophet do this. But here, this happened. This thing happened. Amr's head was cut off. 'Awwal, awwal ra's'—it was the first head. So, a person should never be happy with this. Anyway, this head was brought and thrown in front of his wife. His wife took the head in her lap. As soon as she saw it, she fainted. When she saw the head, she fainted. When the wife regained consciousness, what did she say? If it were our women, they would say, 'What have you done? What was the need?' But Amr's wife says, 'Amr, today I am proud that I am your wife.' I am proud. I am proud that I am your wife. She says this after seeing the head. Did you notice? This spirit should be there. This is religion. No matter how much you do, you have done nothing. After doing a little work, it feels like—for example, the example we often use, you might have heard it too: 'Innal-ahmaqa idha salla rak'atayn yantazirul wahy' (The fool prays two rak'ats and starts waiting for revelation). That is called a fool. Did a little work and thinks we have done a lot. Anyway, so this 'Rida' (contentment), this satisfaction, is of two types. This Hadith shows it. One is what Allah does with you. One. In that, we have no interference. For example, if we get sick, get an ailment, can we do anything? We cannot do anything. God forbid, if someone's child dies, can he do anything? He cannot. God forbid, if someone's wealth is gone, can he do anything? He cannot do anything. God forbid, if someone goes to jail, can he do anything? He cannot do anything. Meaning, not because of his own actions, yes. If it is because of his own actions, then he is responsible. But for example, whatever it is, if he went to jail because of Wilayah, okay. It is not his fault. It is not his fault. So this is called—meaning this thing, it is called 'Qada'. The Qada that comes from Allah, this is from Allah. In terminology, it is called 'Takwini'. Takwini means the servant has no role in this. 'Innama amruhu idha arada shay'an an yaqula lahu kun fayakun' (His command is only when He intends a thing, that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is). Allah's command is that when He wants something, He says 'Be,' and that thing happens. The servant has no role in it, the servant has no interference. This is a verse of the Quran, right? The servant has no role. What is the servant's job in this? Only to submit, that's all. Whatever Allah has decided, to submit before it. Not to say, 'Why did You do this? Why did Allah do this? Why that?' We used to pray regularly. It is clear, right? No one does a favor to Allah. So, anyway, Allah did this. So, whatever this is, it is called 'Takwiniyat', meaning the servant has no role in it. The second thing the Imam mentions here, 'Amal' (deeds). Allah is not involved in this. It is 100% the servant. 100% the servant. Allah has no role. Absolutely none. Zero. Zero. Allah only did what? He gave him strength, He gave him power, He gave him ability. Now, do whatever you want. 'Imma shakiran wa imma kafura' (Either grateful or ungrateful). 'Faman sha'a falyu'min wa man sha'a falyakfur' (So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve). Whoever wants to be grateful, whoever wants to be ungrateful. Allah is not involved in that even by an atom's weight. Allah has no role. Absolutely none. Allah—this is a Hadith Qudsi. 'Ya ibn Adam'—the Imam said to one of his companions, 'Uktub' (Write). The Imam said to his companion, 'Write, uktub'—meaning Allah says, 'Qala Allahu azza wa jalla bi qudrati qawitu ala ma'siyati' (By My power, you gained the strength to disobey Me). Meaning, the sins you are committing, the forbidden acts you are doing, the fact that you are disobeying Allah, that strength to disobey was also given by Allah. And then after that—meaning these are the sentences of the Hadith—'And by My Taufiq (divine enablement), you can perform My obligations.' I gave you the Taufiq. That is why you can pray. That is why you can fast. That is why you can go for Hajj. That is why you can do all other things. Whatever service you are doing for religion, it is because of Taufiq. Allah supported you. 'Wa ma taufiqi illa billah' (And my success is not but through Allah). 'Alayhi tawakkaltu wa ilayhi unib' (Upon Him I rely, and to Him I return). The matter is finished. So both things, Allah gave the power. Now it is in the servant's choice, the servant has it, how he can use that power. What example did the Imam give? The Imam gave the example that it is the same as if you tell your servant, 'Take this money and go to the market and buy goods.' This is the Imam's example. Not ours, yes. 'Take the money and buy goods from the market.' That person takes the money from you and with that same money, what does he do? He goes and gambles. He comes back. The master asked, 'Did you bring the goods from the market?' He said, 'No.' 'Why?' He said, 'I gambled it away and lost, and if I win, I will give it. If Allah makes me win, I will give it.' Did you notice? So, is there any problem with the master in this? Is it the master's fault? The master gave him money for the market. The servant misused it. Whose fault is it? The servant's. Allah created us. Allah gave us power. Allah gave us knowledge. Allah gave us intellect. Allah gave us choice. Allah gave us power. Allah gave us consciousness. Allah gave us understanding. Allah gave us understanding. After giving all the perfections, Allah said, now 'Inna khalaqnal insana min nutfatin amshajin nabtalih, faja'alnahu sami'an basira, imma shakiran wa imma kafura' (Indeed, We created man from a drop of mingled fluid that We may test him; and We made him hearing and seeing. Either grateful or ungrateful). Read the initial verses of Surah Al-Insan. 'Inna khalaqnal insana min nutfatin amshajin nabtalih, faja'alnahu sami'an basira, inna hadaynahus sabil' (Indeed, We created man from a drop of mingled fluid that We may test him; and We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way). We also showed him the path. We have already explained that if you want salvation and wish to enter Paradise, this is the path. Look, for a Momin (believer), entering Paradise is very easy. What does a Momin need to do? Just act upon the Wajibats (obligatory acts). It is very simple. Act upon the Wajibats and abstain from the Haram. That is all. It is very simple. After that, the Imam says that your entry into Paradise is guaranteed. It is already there for the Momin. Whoever holds the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.), the Imam has taken a guarantee for them. 'Ana dhaminun laka' (I am a guarantor for you). But what is next? Why should you 'fatanafisu' (compete)? Compete in what? 'Fi al-darajat' (in the ranks of Paradise). So there are two things. The Imam says—or rather, Jibraeel says to the Prophet—never be satisfied with a small deed. Obviously, this is not for the Prophet, but for us. No matter how much you do, never think you have done enough. No matter how much you spend, do not think, 'Oh, I have spent so much.' You did not do it for anyone else; you did it for yourself. The Quran says, in a verse of Surah Bani Israil, 'In ahsantum ahsantum li-anfusikum' (If you do good, you do good for yourselves), 'wa-in asa'tum falaha' (and if you do evil, it is for yourselves). You are not doing a favor to anyone; you are doing it for yourself. So, what does this 'Rida' (contentment) mean? To be content with Allah's Qada (decree). Allah's decree is of two types. One is what happens in our daily lives, where we have no role, and the other is what Allah has commanded us—pray, fast, do this, do that, all these things. One should be content with both. One should be content with both. Because do you know what happens sometimes? This is not just about us; it is mentioned in the Quran. When Hazrat Musa (a.s.) saved the Bani Israil from the clutches of Pharaoh, and you know how the Bani Israil are—you see the Israelis today, right? Understand that they have been like this from the beginning. They never improved. They were very absurd. Have you noticed? Hazrat Musa (a.s.) took them out. He made them cross the Nile, they were saved from Pharaoh, and Pharaoh drowned. He drowned. Now, as soon as they went out, they saw—this is a Quranic verse, yes. I am reading a Quranic verse, understand that. As soon as they came out, what did they see? That some people were worshipping idols. They had set up many idols. You understand idols, right? They said, 'Ya Musa, ij'al lana aalihan kama lahum aaliha' (O Musa, make for us gods just as they have gods). This is the meaning of the verse. O Musa, you also prepare many gods for us, just like these people have such good gods. What a strange, foolish nation they were. Hazrat Musa (a.s.) was introducing them to one God, and they were saying, 'Make many gods for us.' 'Kama lahum aaliha' (just as they have gods). Make them for us just like theirs. Hazrat Musa (a.s.) understood. 'Innakum qawmun tajhalun' (You are an ignorant people). I am telling you about one God, and you are saying... this is a Quranic verse. Meaning, immediately after leaving, they started showing their true colors. After that, you know, they used to kill thousands of prophets in a single night. Then, when the Prophet forbade them, saying, 'Do not fish on Saturday,' they still did it. Allah sent His punishment upon them. Allah said, 'Kunu qiradatan khasi'in' (Be you apes, despised). Qird means monkey. This is a Quranic verse; I am not reading it, brother, do not think I am saying something from my own side. 'Be monkeys,' whom people hate. Okay? They used to kill without any reason. Allah says that we then turned them into swine and monkeys. 'Wa ja'ala minhum al-qiradata wa-al-khanazir' (And He made from among them apes and swine). Allah gave them punishment. In Islam, this is called 'Mask'. Anyway, this is Mask, meaning Allah changed their forms. He turned them into swine and monkeys. Allah's punishment descends. The blessing of Allah upon the Muslims is that Allah said to the Prophet, 'O Prophet, as long as you are among them, Allah's punishment will not descend upon them.' That is why when Harith ibn Nu'man al-Fihri—la'natu-Allahi 'alayhi—denied the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.), the Prophet said, 'Go away from here. Get out of my sight.' When he moved away from the Prophet's sight, the divine punishment descended upon him. 'Sa'ala sa'ilun bi-'adhabin waqi'in' (A questioner asked about a punishment bound to happen). The verse of Surah al-Ma'arij was revealed. He said, 'If this declaration of Ali's Wilayat is true, then let a stone fall from the sky and split my head.' The Prophet said, 'Fine, get away.' He left. When he left, he had not even reached his mount, he had barely gone out of the Prophet's sight, when a stone immediately fell and split his body into two halves. He was finished. So, this is... anyway, this word 'Rida' has appeared 73 times in the Quran. It has been used 73 times. Even this, look, it is a very important thing. Now, I will quickly present a Hadith. Hazrat Musa (a.s.)—ala nabiyyina wa alihi wa 'alayhi as-salam—you know, was Kalimullah. He used to converse with Allah, right, Hazrat Musa? He used to go to Mount Tur. He used to talk to Allah. He said, 'Ya Rabbi, O Lord, tell me a deed by which You will be pleased with me. Tell me one deed by which You will be pleased.' Allah said, 'Musa, son of Imran, My pleasure is such that you will not be able to bear it. It is very difficult for you. You do not have the strength.' Allah said—this is a Hadith Qudsi—do not be afraid, yes. Do not be afraid of these sentences. Because in the Quran, the same thing is mentioned about Hazrat Musa. When Allah sent Hazrat Musa (a.s.) to Hazrat Khidr (a.s.), Khidr said, 'You will not be able to bear my actions.' And how will you bear that about which you have no knowledge? This is a Quranic verse. Okay? So, there is nothing to be afraid of. So, as soon as Allah said, 'Musa, you will not be able to bear it. It is beyond your capacity,' 'Fakhara Musa 'alayhi as-salamu sajidan' (Musa fell down in prostration). He started crying. 'Ya Rabbi, khasastani bi-al-kalami' (O Lord, You specified me with Your speech). I am Kalimullah, and 'wa-lam tukallim basharan qabli' (and You have not spoken to any human before me). I am the first person, and You are not telling me any deed by which You will be pleased. Allah said, 'Fa-awha Allahu ilayhi' (Then Allah revealed to him), 'Inna ridayya fi ridaka bi-qada'i' (O Musa, if you want Me to be pleased with you, then be content with My decree). Whatever I do to you, be content with it. Whatever I command you, be content with it. Did you notice? This was the conversation, and we have also told you with the help of the Quran that there is nothing to be afraid of. Isn't it? Now, after hearing this Hadith, you will understand what religion you are on. Who is your Mawla? Hazrat Musa (a.s.) is requesting Allah, 'O Lord, by which deed will You be pleased?' Allah is saying, 'It is beyond your capacity.' And there, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), on the night of Hijrah, is asking the Prophet. The Prophet said, 'Ali, sleep on my bed.' He said, 'Prophet, will your life be saved by this, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'Yes, just fine. You go, be assured.' Ali (a.s.) covered himself with the sheet and slept in such a way that he had never slept like that in his life. And he slept in such a way that first, Allah asked Jibraeel and Mika'il, 'Are you two ready to sacrifice your lives for each other?' Both said, 'No. If there is life, there is the world.' Then Allah said, 'Fine, Jibraeel, now you take the verse: "Wa-min an-nasi man yashri nafsahu ibtigha'a mardati-Allahi, wa-Allahu ra'ufun bi-al-'ibad" (And of the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah; and Allah is Kind to [His] servants).' Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Subhan Allah. Ali and the Prophet woke up comfortably. Ali did not scream, nor did he cry, that the Prophet had to be silenced. What a sign! Subhan Allah. Nothing at all. They are sleeping, and in fact, when those 40 people came and lifted the bed—meaning removed the sheet—Ali (a.s.) was sleeping very comfortably. He opened his eyes. 'What happened, brother? What happened? Is there a problem?' They said, 'Where is Muhammad?' He said, 'He left him with me. If he left him with me, then ask me.' Well, Ali (a.s.) had that aura anyway. So, no one had the courage. Because he had been defeating everyone since childhood. He carried a reputation. In Mecca itself, the Mawla of the universe had a reputation. It was not like that. The Prophet used to walk alone, right? So Ali (a.s.) was very young. Meaning, young means 12-13 years of age is not an age, right? So when the Prophet used to walk, Ali (a.s.) was 13 years old. So the Quraish used to tell their children, 'Throw stones at them, throw stones.' So the children used to throw stones from all sides. They used to throw stones at the Messenger of Allah. This is all in history, yes, brother. And we are not saying it from our own side. Tarikh al-Tabari has recorded it. Tabari has recorded it. So what did Ali do? He used to pick up those same stones and throw them at them. Their aim used to miss, but Ali's aim never missed. Subhan Allah. So someone's hand would break, someone's leg would break, someone's head would break. When they went home, 'Who hit you?' They said, 'Ali hit me.' So one man would ask another, 'Look, our boys... oh, he hit our boys too?' He hit our boys too? Oh, how can he hit so many boys? So Ali carried a reputation. Did you notice? So this is the difference. So, know the value of this Wilayat. Know the value of whom you follow. So this is it, and if Allah has written this Wilayat in your destiny, then do not expect anything else besides this. Never even think that Allah should do something else. Look, I will read a Hadith in your service. That Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) says: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. 'Man ittakala 'ala husni al-ikhtiyari min-Allah' (Whoever trusts that Allah has selected the best thing for him). If someone has trust, then 'lam yatamanna annahu fi ghayri al-hali allati ikhtara-Allahu lahu' (then he will never wish to be in any other state than the one Allah has chosen for him). If Allah gave money, Alhamdulillah. If He did not, Alhamdulillah. If He gave children, Alhamdulillah. If He did not, Alhamdulillah. Alhamdulillah, gave children, Alhamdulillah, took them away, Alhamdulillah. In every state, Alhamdulillah. That is why it is Mustahab for us, you know it is Mustahab to recite Ayat al-Kursi after prayer, it has great reward. After Ayat al-Kursi, which verse should be recited? 'Quli-Allahumma malika al-mulki tu'ti al-mulka man tasha'u wa-tanzi'u al-mulka mimman tasha'u wa-tu'izzu man tasha'u wa-tudhillu man tasha'u.' Our teacher used to say, may Allah have mercy on him, he used to say, 'Be afraid of this "tasha'u" (He wills) of Allah. Fear this "tasha'u". The "tasha'u" that you recite, O Lord, You are the Owner of the Kingdom, let us translate the verse. Then I will explain it. O Lord, You are the Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will. You take away the kingdom from whom You will. You take away from whom You will. You give honor to whom You will. You humiliate whom You will. All good is in Your hand, the choice is in Your hand, You have power over everything, Allah can do anything. Our teacher used to say that is why the Sufis in Khorasan, those Sufis who are fakirs, the poor, they did not beg from people, so they used to walk with a staff. In that staff, at the bottom, they used to tie something like aluminum, steel, or some tough material. They used to tie it up, wrapping it in such a way that it remained in that state. It served two purposes for them. Listen very carefully, they used to give a very good example. They say those dervishes used to walk at night, and in those days, for instance, if you were walking on the road and night fell, people would trouble you, and during the day, children would trouble you. Children would keep running behind them during the day, bothering them. And at night, dogs and animals would trouble them. So our teacher used to say that those dervishes would just show the stick to the children to scare them so they would get frightened and not come near. And for the animals, they used to use the iron part to hit them. And they named that stick 'Muntasha'. They say that Allah's Muntasha is like that. It is only to scare and threaten the believer, and to strike the enemies of the faith. Therefore, a believer should always remain content, knowing that whatever Allah does, He does it for their good. Never be anxious. So, look, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Lam yakun Rasullullahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi yaqulu shay'an qattu mada law kana ghayrahu'—meaning the Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.)—Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad—says that the Prophet never said in his life, 'If only such and such had happened, it would have been better,' he never said that. And we should not say that either. And this is also in management books—this humble servant knows a little bit about management. Right? In books, we teach in management that if someone discusses the past, he is a loser. Meaning, if you ask him, 'Was it like this?' Look, it is not that one should not take a lesson from the past; taking a lesson is a different thing. But sitting and crying over the past is a different thing. Meaning, that crying implies regret—'If this had happened, I would be a millionaire today,' 'If this had happened, I would be a billionaire,' 'If that hadn't happened, I would be a minister today.' 'We were cheated, otherwise we would be in that position.' None of that. Whatever Allah has done, Alhamdulillah, thank Allah for whatever He did. If He gave, it's fine; if He didn't, it doesn't matter. This is the saying of the Prophet, meaning Imam Sadiq (a.s.). And today, the same thing is being taught in management, and all these books I am telling you about, these books are mostly written by Jews. And we are telling you this from experience, that many of the books we teach are written by Jews, and we have seen that many things in them are already present in our traditions. They are present in the hadiths. But because the Shias did not use them, others took them. It is unfortunate, it is a great loss for us. Anyway, so what is ultimate obedience? Obedience to Allah lies in what? Being content with His Qada (decree), whatever He has decided, be content with it. I am reading quickly now in your service. Now, how can a person develop this if they are not satisfied with Allah? The first thing is that a person should acquire Ma'rifah (gnosis). What is the way to Ma'rifah? Read those same hadiths. We keep reading those hadiths repeatedly so that you remember them. 'I'rif manazilash-shi'ati ala qadri riwayatihim ma'rifatihim'—if you want to recognize the status of the Shias, look at how many hadiths they know. 'Fa innal ma'rifata hiyad-dirayatu lir-riwayati'—because Ma'rifah is understanding the hadiths. 'Wa bid-dirayati lir-riwayati ya'lul mu'minu ila aqsa darajatil iman'—because through understanding the hadiths, a believer reaches the highest degrees of faith. This is the teaching of the Ale-Muhammad, read it, read it well, teach it to your children, teach them as much as possible. Do not think, 'Oh, we are old now,' no, a believer never gets old. A believer never gets old; the Companions of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf) lived for 309 years, 309 years, and the Quran called them 'youths'. What did the Quran say? 'Innahum fityatun'—they are youths, 'amanu bi rabbihim'—who believed in their Lord. That is why the Prophet said, 'Who among you wants to test their faith?' So, anyway, all the companions stepped back, thinking that if the Prophet tests their faith, it would be difficult, right? But some people who had already planned that after Ali we will do this, they said, 'Ya Rasulullah, we want to test our faith. We are believers.' The Prophet said, 'Fine, today it will be known who is a believer and who is not.' What did the Prophet do? He chose four men. You understood who the four are, right? The fourth was Amir al-Mu'minin. You understood, right? Yes. Now the Prophet said that there should be a witness over them. Who will be the witness? Salman. 'Salman, you go too.' 'Where to go, Ya Rasulullah?' Immediately, the Prophet ordered a carpet; the carpet arrived. Gabriel brought a carpet. He made everyone sit down and said, 'Go to the Companions of the Cave.' Where is the Prophet? In Medina. Where are the Companions of the Cave? You go there, right? Yes. Ahsan, Syria, Jazakallah. Go to the Companions of the Cave, the Companions of the Cave are sleeping there. You go, the Prophet said that the sign of faith will be that you all, all four, will greet them; whoever's greeting the Companions of the Cave answer, he is the believer. Now they all went and said, 'Assalamu alaykum ya Ashab-e-Kahf,' they didn't even know how to greet them. No answer came. After that, as soon as Amir al-Mu'minin said—it's done, brother. Are you telling the meaning of the tradition, brother? It's done? Yes, it's done. Now move aside. Now Amir al-Mu'minin said, 'Assalamu alaykum ya Ahl al-Kahf.' And then he addressed them, he spoke to them. They said, 'Wa alaykumus salam ya Amir al-Mu'minin.' Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! 'Wa alaykumus salam ya Amir al-Mu'minin'—meaning the Prophet was talking about faith, the Companions of the Cave said 'Amir al-Mu'minin.' Not just a believer, but the leader of the believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. This is very necessary, very important, that a person should acquire Ma'rifah. See, there is no other way; we are repeating this repeatedly so that the matter is hopefully preserved in your noble minds. There is no other way because the Prophet announced, 'Ana madinatul ilmi wa Aliyyun babuha'—that's it, there is no other talk. 'I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate.' Now, whoever wants knowledge, there is no other way for him except to come to the door of Ali. Come to the door of the children of Ali. If he goes anywhere else, he will get nothing but failure. He will get nothing but ignorance. In this regard, there are at least 40-50 hadiths, so we are not saying them, we are just presenting them to you. The Imams used to repeatedly test their enemies through this means. 'Brother, I heard you are a dervish from Basra,' so he used to speak nonsense too, yes. He didn't say, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, where am I standing before you?' He didn't say that, whereas there should have been humility; who is he sitting in front of? In front of the Sadiq of the Ale-Muhammad. It is clear to you, right? 'I heard you are a dervish from Basra? People say so.' 'Oh? So fine, come, I will ask you a question.' He asked a question, he couldn't answer even one. 'Son of the Messenger, you answer it yourself.' Never say that I am a dervish. And what else? So this is the only door, that's it. Second point, how to increase? Trust in the essence of Allah. 'Siqah billah, siqah billah' is in the traditions. There is no other way besides this. Trust in the essence of Allah. Whatever it is, ask from Allah. Or make the Hujjat of Allah a means (Wasilah). Make the Hujjat of Allah a means, ask from the Hujjat of Allah. Those whom Allah has given authority. Those whom Allah has given full powers, you ask them. You ask them. Here some ignorant people say, 'Only ask from Allah, only ask from Allah.' Did you? You can't ask from the Hujjat of Allah? Who said that? When you have to borrow from someone, you don't say that then? 'Only ask from Allah.' At that time you will say, 'Brother, will something happen?' Then you will say, 'Ask from Allah.' Oh brother. So they say, 'No, the matter of the living is different, the matter of the dead is different. Ali is dead. The Messenger of Allah is dead.' This is their terminology. Ibn Taymiyyah used this word, 'dead.' Strange foolish man. Yes? 'Ali is dead.' The Quran says: 'Wa la tahsabannalladhina qutilu fi sabilillahi amwatan bal ahya'un inda rabbihim yurzaqun'—do not think of those who are killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive, receiving sustenance from their Lord. They are alive and receiving sustenance from their Lord. Meaning, the Messenger of Allah is not alive and these are alive? Strange people. Anyway, trust in the essence of Allah. Third thing, certainty (Yaqin). There should be certainty. Whoever has true faith, whoever has true certainty, then you can be sure that he will be content with every decree of Allah, whatever it is. And what is the reward for this? What is the reward? Whoever is content with Allah. The first thing, I am speaking very quickly, is that it is a sentence from a hadith that if Allah puts any trouble or difficulty on someone, if he is patient, then he is 'Mujtaba' in the sight of Allah. Mujtaba means the one whom Allah selects, good. And if he is content, then he is 'Mustafa'. This is a sentence from a hadith. Second thing, what is the second benefit? Look, I am telling you everything for your benefit. Be content with Allah's pleasure, with Allah's decree. It is written in the hadith that whoever is content with Allah's decree, Allah will make his prayers answered (Mustajab). Allah will immediately accept his prayer. If he asks, Allah will answer his prayer. Meaning, this is a very important thing. Although in all this, Wilayah is a condition. Yes, without Wilayah, there is nothing. Wilayah is a condition in everything, and what is the second condition for prayers to be answered? That Halal should go into the stomach. Because it is in the traditions that if someone eats Haram or Najis, his prayer is not answered for 40 days. So if someone keeps eating Haram and then prays and thinks, 'No, we are content with Allah's decree,' Allah does not answer his prayer. Yes, brother. Therefore, be very, very careful about what you are eating. Right? Third thing, what is the third benefit? That he becomes independent of people. He will never spread his hand in front of anyone. What a strange sentence of the Master of the Universe. The incident regarding Imam Ali (a.s.)—you know, not Imam Hussain (a.s.), but may our lives be sacrificed on the dust under the hooves of the horses of his slave Qambar. What a strange sentence. He says: 'Istaghni anin-nasi kun nazirahu'—become completely independent of people, you will be equal to them. No matter how big a person in the world is, no matter how great. Never go in front of him. And you know one thing, I am telling you this in brackets. Many big people have this complaint that everyone comes to us, but so-and-so doesn't come. So many people benefit from us, but so-and-so doesn't come. They complain. Their ego gets hurt. That, 'Look, he has nothing, but he doesn't come to us to ask.' It's strange. The Master says, there is someone. And then after that, there is a strange sentence. The Master says, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says that his life will become very easy. I am translating the hadith very quickly, that the Master of the Universe says: 'Ma a'jaba hadhal insan'—it is surprising about this human that 'Masrurun bima lam yakun liyafutahu'—he is happy about that thing which was already written in his destiny. It is already in his destiny. Look, whatever is in the destiny, it will be received. It will not go away. He is happy after receiving that thing, 'I got it.' Oh, that was bound to be received anyway. Allah had written it in the destiny. And he is disappointed, saddened for that thing which was not in his destiny at all. These are the words of the Mawla (Imam), not ours. If one applies a little thought—as the Mawla says, 'Wa law fakkara la-absara' (If he had reflected, he would have seen)—then he will see, and he will understand the point. He will be convinced that he is a creation, that there is a Planner, and that someone is guiding him. He has a Creator who is turning his life upside down. Is the point not clear? Turning it upside down. Yes? There was a time when we were young, we had strength. Have we not become old today? If you ask someone if they like this white beard, what will they say? Yes? Do you like this illness? What will they say? Yes? Or not? The Sixth Imam (a.s.) gave all these examples, didn't he? He gave 22 examples in one hadith. In one hadith, the Sixth Imam (a.s.) gave 22 examples to an atheist. An atheist came to debate the Imam. 22 examples. And 'Wa annar-rizqa muqaddarun alayhi muqaddarun'—sustenance is destined. Whatever is to be received will be received. Therefore, do not take too much stress. The Mawla says: Work, put in the effort. If you get it, fine. If you don't, there is no grief. Those who take stress, who go crazy—you must have seen them—they become insane. They go crazy over small, trivial things. They fight and quarrel. They even kill each other. How ignorant these people are, how foolish. Just this last sentence for today's Majlis, as it is a Hadith-e-Qudsi. We have summarized this very quickly, otherwise, this is a vast topic. A very vast subject. What does Allah say? O Prophet, tell them: 'Man lam yarda bi-qada'i fal-yaltamis ilahan ghayri' (Whoever is not pleased with My decree, My Qada, My destiny, then let him go and seek a god other than Me). 'Fal-yaltamis ilahan ghayri'—let him go and find another god. This is 'Rida-e-Qada' (contentment with the divine decree). Gratitude in every state. Gratitude for acts of worship, O Lord. You made Namaz-e-Shab (night prayer) recommended, gratitude. You made Namaz-e-Subh (morning prayer) obligatory, gratitude. You made Tasbih obligatory and recommended, gratitude. You made fasting obligatory, gratitude. Be grateful. Do not consider fasting a burden. It is a great blessing. Today, the world is realizing its importance. Today, the world is realizing how important it is. And if anyone has created a complete embodiment of all these beliefs, it was Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala, who demonstrated each thing. That this is what contentment is. The people with Hussain (a.s.) were strange. Imam Hussain (a.s.) had brought strange people along with him. Look, you will understand and accept this well. Especially mothers will understand more. Those who have children, especially those with small children, even fathers will understand. It is not that fathers won't, but a mother will understand more. See, those who are older can endure difficulties. They can bear troubles. But they can bear their own troubles, but they cannot bear the trouble of their child. It is very hard for them. Ever since the water was cut off, Rubab would come again and again to look at Ali Asghar (a.s.). Ali Asghar is thirsty. But what can a mother do? There is no water. Just understand the suffering of Rubab. Rubab lost Ali Asghar in Karbala and lost Sakina in Shaam. Rubab is very oppressed. After the event of Karbala, Janabe Rubab never sat in the shade. She never sat in the shade. She always sat in the sun. She would remember the thirst of Ali Asghar. She would remember the suffering of Sakina. It was a great sacrifice. Meaning, it was the ultimate test for Imam Hussain (a.s.). Of the Imam (a.s.). The sacrifice of Janabe Ali Asghar (a.s.) is there. And that is why when Imam Hussain (a.s.) raised the call of distress, 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna' (Is there any helper to help us?), 'Hal min mugheethin yugheethuna' (Is there any rescuer to rescue us?), 'Hal min dhabbin yadhubbu an harami Rasulillah' (Is there any defender to defend the harem of the Messenger of Allah?). Understand the importance of all three sentences. One is Nusrat (help), second is refuge, third is defending the harem of the Messenger of Allah. Ali Asghar (a.s.) said 'Labbayk' to all three things. As soon as Hussain's call of distress was raised, there was an uproar in the tents. Hussain came to your tent, asked Janabe Zainab (s.a.), 'Sister Zainab, what is this uproar?' She said, 'You raised the call of distress, Asghar threw himself out of the cradle.' He said, 'Zainab, bring Asghar, give him to me.' She said, 'Brother, he does not go into anyone's lap.' Hussain came and stood by the cradle. Now what the father said and what the son understood, no one knows, but it is written in books that Asghar eagerly came into his father's lap. Now, as Hussain walked away carrying Asghar, Rubab was standing at the door of the tent. She said, 'Rubab, why are you standing here?' She said, 'I am watching that whoever has gone since morning to the battlefield has not returned alive. I want to see my son one last time.' Hussain explained that Rubab, those who went until now went to fight; six-month-old babies do not do Jihad. The mother's heart calmed down. Hussain brought him, brought Ali Asghar, stood at a height, and called out, 'Ya qawm, if you do not have a Muslim among you, my child has been thirsty for three days. Islam has commanded to give water to the thirsty.' No one answered. Hussain said a second thing, 'If you are not Muslims, then is there no parent among you? Do you not see how my child is suffering? Kayfa yatlazza (how he is gasping), how he sometimes closes his mouth and sometimes opens it.' Then the Imam said, 'Ali Asghar, they are not understanding my words, son, you explain it to them.' Ali Asghar began to move his dry tongue over his dry lips. There was an uproar among the wretched enemies; they turned their faces away and began to weep. The effects of a revolution were about to appear when Ibn Sa'ad said, 'Ayna, ayna Hurmula?' (Where, where is Hurmula?). The accursed Hurmula came forward. He said, 'Iqta' kalam al-Hussain' (Cut off the speech of Hussain). Just as he said that, it is written in the Maqtal that the accursed Hurmula took out a three-pronged arrow. O mourners, this was not just an ordinary arrow; it was a poisoned arrow. It was an arrow dipped in poison, and with that arrow, he aimed at Asghar's throat. The child turned over in his father's hands. Now, when Hussain bent down to look, what did he see? That Asghar was smiling, 'Father, do not be worried.' Now, Hussain wanted to take Asghar away. He came near the tent, and it is written in the Maqtal what words Hussain uttered: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, radan bi-qada'ihi wa tasliman li-amrihi' (We are from Allah and to Him we shall return, content with His decree and submissive to His command). Saying this, Hussain came near the tent. Once, the thought came: how will the mother bear this? Then Hussain took small steps and came back, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, radan bi-qada'ihi wa tasliman li-amrihi.' Seven times Hussain performed this action. Finally, he stopped at the door of the tent, stopped at the entrance of the tent. After that, he thought—Hussain thought that now the son, now Asghar has left this world, why deprive the mother of a final glimpse? Now he came and called out, 'Rubab.' From the sentences in the Maqtal, it seems that Rubab came from one side, Sakina came from the other, but the girl reached first. 'Brother, father, is my brother not thirsty anymore? Father, I have to give water to my brother.' Hussain was not giving any answer. When Rubab reached and he turned the hem of his cloak, Rubab saw that scene which Allah should not show any mother. A six-month-old child completely bathed in blood, a three-pronged arrow pierced in his throat. Rubab recited a dirge, 'Ya bunayya, amithlukal yudhbah?' (O my son, are children like you slaughtered?). Hussain buried Asghar behind the tent. Rubab's suffering did not end here, mourners. Do you want to hear the suffering? Usually, I do not recite this tragedy because I cannot recite it. But today, even today, I present it in your service. Rubab's suffering did not end here. On the 11th of Muharram, when the wretched enemies were severing the heads of each martyr from their bodies and raising them on spears, the counting of the heads began. A wretched one said, 'Ibn Sa'ad, one head is missing here.' He said, 'Whose head is that?' He said, 'That of the child whom Hussain was holding.' Now the search for that head began. You know how they were searching? They were piercing the ground with spears because one person had said, 'I saw that Hussain took that child behind the tent and was burying him there.' So, the wretched ones started piercing the ground behind the tent with spears. One wretch struck a spear in such a way that the child's body came out, and he severed the head from the body. When Rubab saw this scene, she struck her face, 'Wa raziya, wa bunayya!'
Rida is defined as complete submission to Allah's will without anger or personal desire.
True faith requires accepting divine decree (Qada) while taking personal responsibility for one's choices.
The events at Saqifah are identified as the historical origin of the deviation from Islamic principles.
Ma'rifah and spiritual growth are achieved through the study of Ahlulbayt traditions and the observance of Wajibats.
The martyrdom of Ali Asghar serves as the ultimate example of sacrifice and the cruelty faced by the Ahlulbayt.
Consuming Halal sustenance is a prerequisite for the acceptance of prayers and spiritual development.
Imam Ali (a.s.) is presented as the gate of knowledge and the primary model for selfless devotion to the Prophet.

chapters.title: The Peak of Spiritual Qualities
chapters.summary: An explanation of the spiritual hierarchy of virtues, culminating in Tawakkul (Trust) and Rida (Contentment).

chapters.title: The Essence of Rida and Submission
chapters.summary: Defining Rida as total acceptance of Allah's decree, supported by Quranic verses regarding absolute submission to the Prophet's authority.

chapters.title: Historical Context of Leadership
chapters.summary: A critique of the events at Saqifah following the Prophet's passing, contrasting the companions' actions with the divine appointment of Imam Ali.

chapters.title: The Foundation of Saqifah and Its Consequences
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical events of Saqifah, arguing that the deviation from the leadership of Imam Ali (a.s.) marked the beginning of the decline of true Islamic values.

chapters.title: Understanding Rida and the Nature of Sacrifice
chapters.summary: The lecture explains the concept of 'Rida' (contentment with Allah) and highlights that the foundation of Ashura was laid at Saqifah, emphasizing the importance of studying history.

chapters.title: The Story of Amr ibn Amr al-Khuza'i
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates the life and martyrdom of Amr ibn Amr al-Khuza'i, a loyal companion of Imam Ali (a.s.) who became the first martyr in Islamic history to have his head displayed on a spear.

chapters.title: Two Types of Divine Decree: Takwini and Amal
chapters.summary: The lecture distinguishes between 'Takwini' (divine decrees beyond human control) and 'Amal' (human deeds where individuals have free will and responsibility).

chapters.title: Human Choice and Divine Enablement
chapters.summary: Allah provides humans with the power and intellect to act, but the choice to obey or disobey remains with the individual.

chapters.title: Striving for Higher Ranks in Paradise
chapters.summary: Believers are encouraged to compete in good deeds and not settle for the minimum, as all good actions ultimately benefit the soul.

chapters.title: The Meaning of Rida and Divine Decree
chapters.summary: True contentment (Rida) involves accepting Allah's decrees, illustrated by the historical failures of Bani Israil and the lesson given to Prophet Musa.

chapters.title: The Secret to Allah's Pleasure
chapters.summary: Allah reveals to Prophet Musa that the key to attaining His pleasure is to be content with whatever He decrees.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Imam Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts Imam Ali's (a.s.) willingness to sleep in the Prophet's bed during the Hijrah, highlighting his unwavering faith and divine recognition.

chapters.title: Contentment with Divine Decree
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes the importance of trusting Allah's choices and maintaining contentment in all life circumstances, as taught by the Imams.

chapters.title: Avoiding Regret and Seeking Ma'rifah
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against dwelling on the past with regret and encourages believers to seek Ma'rifah (gnosis) through the study of Hadith.

chapters.title: Testing Faith through the Companions of the Cave
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) tests the faith of his companions by sending them to the Cave of the Sleepers to see whose greeting would be acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Gate of Knowledge and Divine Trust
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the gateway to divine knowledge and stresses the importance of placing absolute trust in Allah.

chapters.title: Contentment with Divine Decree
chapters.summary: The lecture explains the spiritual benefits of being content with Allah's decree, including answered prayers and independence from worldly people.

chapters.title: Destiny and the Example of Imam Hussain
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how understanding destiny reduces worldly stress and highlights Imam Hussain's ultimate demonstration of contentment in Karbala.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Ali Asghar
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain (a.s.) brings his infant son, Ali Asghar, to the battlefield to plead for water, highlighting the cruelty of the enemy.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Ali Asghar
chapters.summary: Hurmula strikes the infant with a three-pronged arrow, leading to a heart-wrenching moment of submission to Allah's will by Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Grief of Rubab
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain reveals the martyred child to his mother, Rubab, and the subsequent desecration of the grave by the enemy forces.

The speaker discusses the concept of Itmaam-e-Hujjat (the completion of proof) and the necessity of following a Ma'sum (infallible) leader. The discourse highlights that just as prayer and ablution are obligatory acts, recognizing and following the Imam is a fundamental duty for a believer.

title: EP06 | As'haab -e- Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉 #ImamMahdiعج
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual status and essential characteristics of the 313 companions of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). It emphasizes the importance of supporting the Imam during the period of Occultation through prayer, intellectual defense of Wilayat, and unwavering faith. The session also highlights the necessity of Marifat and total submission as the foundation for those who aspire to serve the global government of the Imam.
content:
We present PSR. O our Sahar, O Sahar, O you who are the hidden desire in the longing of my eyes, O, O comfort of my heart. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali-ul-Asr, help us.
