In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of Hassan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 'Wa layansurannallahu man yansuruh' (And Allah will surely help those who help Him). Respected brothers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Our topic today is Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and his companions. And before discussing the verse whose recitation we have had the honor of, I want to say one thing to the viewers: this topic of the companions of Mahdi is a very important topic, and in today's age, because we are living our lives in this era, and in all of us Shias of Haider-e-Karrar (a.s.), the love for the Imam (a.s.) and the spirit of helping him is found. Let us see, this is the spirit of love and support in the hearts of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar. Let me present to you a hadith regarding the spirit of support for Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) in the heart of Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.), in which Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Law adraktuhu la-khadamtu-hu ayyama hayati' (If I were to reach his time, I would serve him all the days of my life). Dear respected ones, these words are being spoken by one Imam about another Imam, and the intensity of these words shows how Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.) is expressing his longing in this hadith regarding the support of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), that if he were present in that era, he too would wish to support Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). So, this is the status and position of being included among the companions of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.), that Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.) is seen longing that if he had reached the time of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.), he would have dedicated his life to his service. So let us return to the verse of the Holy Quran with which I began my discourse, in which the Lord of Honor states: 'Wa layansurannallahu man yansuruh' (And Allah will surely support those who support Him). Now, regarding this verse, Ayatollah Mohammad Taqi Musawi Isfahani has stated in his book 'Mikyal al-Makarim' that the exegetes of the Quran say that the meaning of 'Allah's support' here is the support of the Messenger of Allah and the Infallible Imams (a.s.). Thus, it becomes clear that if anyone wishes to support Allah, they must carry out this task, meaning they must support the Messenger and the Infallible Imams (a.s.). Especially in the era we are living in, it is our duty to provide support to the Imam of our time. Now, since the topic is about the companions of Mahdi (a.s.), let us turn to the characteristics of his companions and the nature of their support. Since we are talking about support, the nature of support in the era of Ghaybah (Occultation) will be different from the nature of support for Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.) after his reappearance. Now, if you come to the first part, regarding how to support Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) during the era of Ghaybah, there are various ways through which you can perform the support of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.). The easiest way is through Dua (supplication). Pray for Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Pray as much as possible for his reappearance. Indeed, in a hadith, the Mawla himself says—it is a hadith of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) himself—in which he says: 'Akthiru ad-du'a bi-ta'jil al-faraj' (Pray abundantly for the hastening of the relief/reappearance, for in it lies your relief and your welfare). So, one of our most important tasks in the era of Ghaybah, as part of our support, is to pray abundantly for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). The second task is to narrate his virtues and merits, and these characteristics will be found in the companions of the Imam. So, to convey all the virtues and merits of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to the people, to study their knowledge, and to acquaint people with their teachings. In a hadith, Imam-e-Riza (a.s.) says: 'Rahimallahu 'abdan ahya amrana' (May Allah have mercy on the servant who revives our affair). And when the Imam was asked, 'Mawla, how is your affair revived?', the Mawla replied: 'Yata'allamu 'ulumana wa yu'allimuhumu an-nas' (He learns our knowledge and teaches it to the people). So, this sequence of virtues and merits is such that it is incumbent upon us, it is necessary for us, to acquire as much knowledge as possible about the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and acquaint our children, our friends, and our relatives with these virtues and merits of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This is also a most important responsibility in this era of Ghaybah. Then, if we look at other various things that can be done in the era of Ghaybah, one is to help those who are lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If someone is distressed, if they are in a difficult situation, we should help them so that through that, we can attain the pleasure of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Apart from this, one of the most important tasks in this era of Ghaybah is to address the objections raised by enemies and opponents regarding the Infallible Imams (a.s.). Their objections should be answered thoroughly. This is the best method of defense through which we can defend Imamate and Wilayat. This list could be quite long if one were to count them one by one, but since time is short, these are a few things I wanted to present to the viewers. This is a very big and important task for us in the era of Ghaybah. And those who will be the companions of the Imam, those who will earn the status of being a companion of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), will possess this specific characteristic: that in this era of Ghaybah, they will perform many deeds for Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.). Besides this, their responsibility after the reappearance will be different; they will support him on the battlefield and carry out all the commands given by Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), implementing them and taking them to the final stage—this will be the responsibility of the people of that time and among the special responsibilities of the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Now the question arises: this is support, but what are the benefits of support? Although in matters of Wilayat, we do not think much about the benefits—that if we help and support Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) or any of the Infallible Imams (a.s.), what will be the benefit? I am reminded here of the words of the late Irfan Haider Abidi (may Allah have mercy on him), in which he quoted that hadith of Imam Ali (a.s.). The concept of the narration was that the Mawla says regarding the worship of Allah: 'I did not worship Allah out of greed for Paradise, nor did I worship Allah out of fear of Hell, but rather my God is worthy of worship, which is why I worship Him.' On this, the late Irfan Haider Abidi said that we do not love Ali out of greed for Paradise, nor do we love Ali out of fear of Hell, but rather my Mawla is worthy of love. So here, the question of what the benefits of support are—benefits have their place, but if we do anything regarding the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it is only and only because my Mawla is worthy of love. We perform these deeds for the Infallible Imams (a.s.) from the depths of our hearts. But since it has been mentioned in the narrations what the benefits are for those who support the Imam (a.s.), you will find many narrations. I want to present one narration here in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'I will intercede on the Day of Judgment,' and then there is a very powerful sentence after this, where he says: 'Wa law atawni bi-zunubi ahlil-ard' (Even if a person comes on the Day of Judgment carrying all the sins of the people of the earth). Even after that, I will intercede for him. And what reason does the Messenger of Allah give? Viewers, listen carefully to what reason he gives—that even if someone comes to the field of Mahshar with all the sins, the Messenger of Allah says: 'Ana shafi'ul-hum yawmal-qiyama' (I will be their intercessor on the Day of Judgment). Then he says, on what basis will the Messenger of Allah intercede? The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) clarifies it further: 'Mu'inun li-ahlil-bayti' (One who supports my Ahlulbayt, who helps them), and then he further says, 'wa man qada hajatihim' (and one who fulfills their needs), and then he further says, 'wal-muhibbu lahum bi-qalbihi' (and one who loves them from the depths of his heart). And this has no condition; this love cannot be described. A poet has beautifully said: 'Love cannot be brought into words, it is a delicate reality that cannot be explained.' So, this state cannot be explained—how a lover will love the Imam (a.s.), its state cannot be described. But there is a condition here: if anyone wants the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they must perform these tasks. They must help them, support them, fulfill the needs of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and love them with their heart ('bi-qalbihi') and express that love with their tongue ('wa lisanihi'). It is not just love from the heart; here, expression is a condition—you must express it. And then he says, 'wa dafi'un 'anhum bi-yadihi' (and defends them with his hands/limbs). So, all these characteristics that will be found in him—meaning he helps them, fulfills their needs, loves them from the heart, expresses that love with his tongue, and defends the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) with his body—the result will be that the Messenger of Allah will be seen interceding for him in the field of Mahshar. Now, we want to point to another aspect: what will be the number of these companions in the very beginning, when Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.) reappears? Although this number will gradually increase, what will be the number when he arrives? If we look at various narrations, it is found that the number of companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is stated to be 313 in various narrations, and they will have a great task because they have to form a universal government: 'Yamla'ul-arda qistan wa 'adla kama muli'at zulman wa jawra'. To establish justice and fairness in a world filled with oppression and tyranny will be the task of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and his companions. And it is not that this work is to be done in one region, one city, or one country, but rather to spread the government of Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.) across the whole world. The companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will carry out this work, and under the guidance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), they will bring it to completion, Insha'Allah. Here, the narration I want to present to you, which mentions the 313 and who the different people will be in the initial phase with Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), can be found in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 52, Page 348, which is taken from Tafsir al-Ayyashi, in which it is stated: 'Idha qama Mahdiyyu ali Muhammadin istakhraja min zahri al-Ka'bati sab'atan wa 'ishrina rajulan' (When our Mahdi from the family of Muhammad rises, when he comes out from the Kaaba, he will bring 27 people with him at the start). And then in the narration, it is written: 'Khamsata 'ashara min qawmi Musa' (15 individuals from the nation/followers of Prophet Musa (a.s.) will be found with Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) in the initial phase). Then the narration further says: 'Alladhina yaqdhuna bil-haqqi wa bihi ya'dilun' (Those who will judge with truth and will establish justice through it). Right? After that, the tradition states that seven individuals from the Companions of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf) will be present among the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). And who else will be there? Yusha, the successor of Musa (a.s.), and the successor of Janabe Musa (a.s.), Janabe Yusha bin Nun, will also be resurrected with Hazrat-e-Hujjat. Furthermore, the believer from the family of Pharaoh (Aal-e-Firaun) will also come with Hazrat-e-Hujjat. In addition to them, the companions of Hazrat-e-Mohammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) will also be counted in the list of the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), and their names are explicitly recorded here: Salman al-Farsi, Abu Dujana al-Ansari, and Malik al-Ashtar. Janabe Salman-e-Mohammadi will be with you, as will Abu Dujana al-Ansari and Malik al-Ashtar. All these individuals will emerge in the initial phase with Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and will come to support you. Now, viewers, I want to present a few characteristics that will be found in the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). The first characteristic is that they will be very strong regarding their faith (aqeedah), and everything depends on faith. If the faith is not correct, then all actions and deeds that a person performs in this life will appear worthless. There is no 'qaza' (making up for) for faith; you will find qaza for everything else. If some religious duties—like prayer, fasting, Hajj, and Zakat—that were supposed to be performed in life were missed, their qaza can be performed, and even after a person's death, their qaza can be fulfilled. However, there is no qaza for faith. Once a person leaves this world, there will be no qaza for it. Therefore, everything depends on the foundation of faith. Right? So, their faith will be... The companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will have an incredibly strong faith. Let us look in the light of traditions at what Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.) says about the faith of the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). He states: "كَالرِّجَالِ كَأَنَّ قُلُوبَهُمْ زُبَرُ الْحَدِيدِ" (Like men whose hearts are like pieces of iron). The companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will have hearts like iron. And then he says, "لَا يَشُوبُهَا شَكٌّ فِي ذَاتِ اللَّهِ" (No doubt regarding the Essence of Allah will taint them). They will not show any doubt regarding the Essence of Allah or Tawheed (monotheism). They will be very strong in their belief in Tawheed. Then the Imam says, "أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْحَجَرِ" (Harder than stone). Their faith will be as firm as stone. It is not as if they will be like a tree that sways when the wind blows; their faith will not be like that. And there is a reason for this, because these people will not have taken their religion from the mouths of others; rather, their religion will depend on the Book of Allah and the purified Sunnah. There is a tradition from the Imam that whoever takes their religion from the Book of Allah and the purified Sunnah, even if mountains move from their place, the faith of those who have taken their religion from the Book of Allah and the sayings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will not move from its place. So, they will be extremely strong regarding their faith. Within this, the phrase "فِي ذَاتِ اللَّهِ" means their belief regarding Allah will also be very strong. Their belief regarding Tawheed will be very powerful. All things depend on the belief in Tawheed because most errors are found regarding the belief in Tawheed. There is a tradition from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in which he says, "مَعْرِفَةُ اللَّهِ أَعْلَى الْمَعَارِفِ" (The recognition of Allah is the highest of all recognitions). In this matter, the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will be very firm and strong, having a powerful belief in Tawheed. Regarding this, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says: "وَيْحًا لِلطَّالِقَانِ فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ بِهَا كُنُوزًا" (Woe to the people of Taleqan, for Allah has treasures there), "لَيْسَتْ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلَا فِضَّةٍ" (which are not of gold or silver). Then the Imam says, "وَلَكِنْ بِهَا رِجَالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ" (Rather, there are believing men there). What is that treasure? That it contains believers. And then the Imam continues, "عَرَفُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ مَعْرِفَتِهِ" (Who have recognized Allah with the recognition He truly deserves). And then the Imam says, "وَهُمْ أَيْضًا أَنْصَارُ الْمَهْدِيِّ فِي آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ" (And they will also be the helpers of the Mahdi in the end times). Now, the most important thing here is that these people, the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), will be at the highest level regarding the recognition of Allah. "عَرَفُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ مَعْرِفَتِهِ". This will be one of the characteristics of the Ansar-e-Mahdi, that they will be at the highest peak regarding recognition (marifat). This recognition is very important. A person asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), "مَا رَأْسُ الْعِلْمِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ" (O Messenger of Allah, what is the head of knowledge?). To which he replied, "مَعْرِفَةُ اللَّهِ حَقَّ مَعْرِفَتِهِ" (The recognition of Allah as He truly deserves to be recognized). This is the head of knowledge, and in this field, the companions of Mahdi (a.s.) will be at the forefront. In the same way, I want to present another tradition where the Imam explains the position of 'marifat' (recognition) compared to other deeds. He says: "بَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ صَلَاةً مِنْ بَعْضٍ" (Some of you pray more than others), "وَبَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ حَجًّا مِنْ بَعْضٍ" (Some of you perform more Hajj than others), "وَبَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ صَدَقَةً مِنْ بَعْضٍ" (Some of you give more charity than others), "وَبَعْضُكُمْ أَكْثَرُ صِيَامًا مِنْ بَعْضٍ" (Some of you fast more than others). Then the Imam says, "وَأَفْضَلُكُمْ أَفْضَلُكُمْ مَعْرِفَةً" (But the best among you is the one who is best in recognition). If there is recognition, their prayers will be excellent; if there is recognition, their Hajj will be excellent; if there is recognition, they will give charity correctly; if there is recognition, their fasts will be accepted because they will perform them with recognition. So, everything depends on recognition. So, the companions of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) will be seen at the forefront in this field. The third characteristic I want to present is regarding 'tasleem' (submission). The companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will have a spirit of submission at its peak. The Imam has stated in a tradition: "أُمِرَ النَّاسُ بِمَعْرِفَتِنَا وَرَدَّ إِلَيْنَا وَالتَّسْلِيمِ لَنَا" (People have been commanded to attain our recognition, to refer to us, and to submit to us). They must submit to our commands, our traditions, our sayings, and our decisions. Now, how will the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) submit to the Imam? Through this tradition, we see how they will serve Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and the spirit of submission they will possess. It is stated in a tradition: "يَتَمَسَّحُونَ بِسَرْجِ الْإِمَامِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَتْلُبُونَ بِذَلِكَ بِذَلِكَ الْبَرَكَةِ" (They will wipe themselves on the saddle of the Imam (a.s.) seeking blessings). Amazing! They will circle around the Imam and protect him from every calamity and trouble, and they will strive with their hearts and souls to fulfill every wish and desire that the Imam (a.s.) expresses. This spirit of submission will be found in them. And "وَهُمْ أَطْوَعُ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَمَةِ لِسَيِّدِهَا" (They will be more obedient to him than a maidservant is to her master). And then the Imam says, "كَالْمَصَابِيحِ كَأَنَّ قُلُوبَهُمُ قُلُوبُهُمُ الْقَنَادِيلُ" (Like burning lamps, their hearts will be like lanterns). And it is further stated, "وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ مُشْفِقُونَ" (And they are fearful out of the awe of Allah). So, this will be the spirit of submission—just as a slave is obedient to his master and tries to fulfill every word with all his energy and strength, these companions will do even more to achieve the pleasure of the Imam (a.s.). "كَيَدْعُونَ بِالشَّهَادَةِ وَيَتَمَنَّوْنَ أَنْ يُقْتَلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" (They will call for martyrdom and wish to be killed in the way of Allah). This is amazing! There will be very few people in the world who possess this quality of desiring martyrdom. And what will be their slogan? "شِعَارُهُمْ يَا لِثَارَاتِ الْحُسَيْنِ" (Their slogan will be 'O avengers of Hussain'). Now, viewers, the final characteristic—though there are many—that I want to present is regarding the defense of Wilayah. The last quality is their active work for the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and their defense of it. They will be very active, and they will truly fulfill the message of Ghadir, where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: "فَلْيُبَلِّغِ الشَّاهِدُ الشَّاهِدُ الْغَائِبَ" (Let those who are present convey it to those who are absent). So, never think regarding Wilayah that we have conveyed enough; always remain continuously engaged so that Wilayah can be conveyed to as many people as possible. Whatever work is done in this regard is less. These individuals, the companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), will be seen at the forefront in this field. Now, I want to draw your attention to Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 148, where the Lord of Majesty says: "فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا". Regarding this verse, Abu Khalid narrates from Imam Baqir (a.s.) that 'Al-Khairat' here refers to 'Al-Khairat al-Wilayah' (the goodness of Wilayah). So, 'hasten towards goodness, wherever you are, Allah will gather you all.' Here, 'goodness' refers to Wilayah; they will invite people towards this goodness as much as possible, and Allah will gather all these people. If you look in Al-Kafi, you will find the commentary regarding this verse: "أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا" (Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together), meaning the companions of Al-Mahdi. The words mean that all these people will be gathered with Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.), and their number will be 300 and some individuals, as present in this tradition. And then it is stated: "وَهُمْ وَاللَّهِ وَاللَّهِ الْأُمَّةُ الْمَعْدُودَةُ" (And by Allah, they are the numbered community). And then it is stated: "يَجْتَمِعُونَ وَاللَّهِ فِي سَاعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ" (By Allah, they will be gathered together in a single hour). This means all these people will be seen working for Wilayah. All those who love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and are companions of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will be seen working for Wilayah, and when the reappearance of the Hazrat occurs, Allah will gather them. Let me conclude by giving an example of what the defense of Wilayah is. A very famous and well-known scholar of India, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi, did such a monumental work that in the history of Islam, perhaps no one has performed this work on the subject of Imamate and Wilayah as excellently as he did. He wrote various books, and the best book he wrote on the subject of Imamate was 'Abaqat al-Anwar'. Before writing 'Abaqat al-Anwar', he wrote a book titled 'Istiqsa al-Ifham wa Istifha al-Intiqam fi Radd-e-Muntahal al-Kalam'. This book was written against Haider Ali Faizabadi's book 'Muntahal al-Kalam'. Muntahal al-Kalam's challenge was that Haider Ali Faizabadi claimed that even if all the scholars from the time of the occultation of the Imam until today were to rise from their graves, they could not answer it. Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi answered that challenge through this book. He even named it 'Istiqsa al-Ifham' (to blacken the face) and 'Istifha al-Intiqam' (to take full revenge). He published this book in three volumes, consisting of about 600 pages each. He did not just defend; he attacked and blackened the faces of the enemies, bringing their own arguments into the public domain. Another book, 'Faza'il al-Lusus' (The Virtues of Thieves), was written to refute the virtues of thieves. You can see the names Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi chose. After that, he wrote 'Abaqat al-Anwar', about which every scholar who expressed an opinion said that such a book could not have been written without divine support and the special grace of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). These are all the things that will be found in the companions of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.): their spirit of Wilayah will be at its peak, their spirit of submission, their recognition, and their strong faith. We pray to the Almighty Allah to adorn us with all these qualities and grant us the opportunity to defend and support the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and especially Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr (Master of the Age), reach us and do not let us perish. Greetings, viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Now is the time to announce our daily lucky draw winners who will be awarded a prize of ₹1000. Their names are on your screen: Ali from New Delhi, Qissa from Rustampura, Syed Tamaniyat from Bengaluru, SB Bhojani from Sangli, Mohammad Abbas Damani from Mumbai, and Fauzia Bano from Alipur. Congratulations to all of you. If your name did not appear in today's winner list, there is no need to be disappointed because the link for this quiz will remain live until the end of the series. For the mega prize, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq, it is only necessary to provide correct answers to all questions in at least seven out of these 12 episodes. That is, all those who have provided correct answers to all questions in at least seven episodes will have one winner announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Now it is time to bid you farewell. InshaAllah, we will meet again tomorrow at this same time with a new episode. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad. Allah, the Lord of Majesty, has stated in the Holy Quran: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 'O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow (i.e., the Day of Judgment). And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.' My dear believing brothers and sisters, in this blessed verse, Allah has commanded us to prepare for our afterlife. The world is a traveler's inn, and we have to depart from here one day. Whatever we do here will be of use to us there. Therefore, we should examine our deeds and see if we are living our lives according to the pleasure of Allah. May Allah grant us the ability to perform righteous deeds. Amen.

title: Imam Baqir (a.s.) aur Ism e Aazam ki Taaqat
excerpt: This lecture recounts a historical narration involving Umar ibn Hanzala and Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) regarding the Ism-e-Azam (the Greatest Name of Allah). The Imam tests Umar's spiritual capacity by demonstrating the overwhelming power associated with this sacred knowledge. Upon witnessing a manifestation of this power, Umar realizes his own limitations and declines the request to be taught the name. The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.).
content:
Umar ibn Hanzala narrates that I said to Abu Ja'far, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), 'I suspect that I hold a special honor and status in your eyes.' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Certainly.' Umar ibn Hanzala says, 'I then said, I have a need.' The Imam (a.s.) asked, 'What is it?' I said, 'Teach me the Greatest Name of Allah (Ism-e-Azam).' The Imam asked, 'Do you have the strength to bear it?' I said, 'Yes.' Then the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Enter this room.' Umar ibn Hanzala says that I and the Imam (a.s.) both entered the room. Then Hazrat Abu Ja'far (a.s.) placed his hands on the ground, and the whole room was plunged into darkness. Seeing this scene, Umar ibn Hanzala's body began to tremble. Imam Ali (a.s.) asked, 'What do you say now? Should I teach you the Ism-e-Azam?' Umar ibn Hanzala, out of fear, said, 'No.' Then the Imam (a.s.) raised his hands, and the room became illuminated just as it was before. We pray to Allah, the Lord of Majesty, for the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.s.), may Allah hasten his noble reappearance. And grant us the opportunity to witness his miracles and the strength to bear them. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Misle Kaaba Kaun? | 13 Rajab | Birth of Imam Ali (a.s.) in the Holy Kaaba
excerpt: This lecture commemorates the birth of Imam Ali (a.s.) inside the Holy Kaaba, highlighting his unique status in Islamic history. The speaker emphasizes that Imam Ali is the only person to have been born in the House of Allah, establishing a profound spiritual connection between him and the Kaaba. The talk concludes by urging the Muslim Ummah to align their lives with the Wilayah and Imamate of Imam Ali as a necessary act of faith.
content:
I heard what we said, that who is not familiar with the status of Ali (a.s.)? Every Muslim is aware of this. Before leaving this world, one should at least visit the House of Allah once, which the chosen Prophets (a.s.) built with their own blessed and pure hands. It is certain that every Muslim has an indescribable love and devotion for the Kaaba. But when the Almighty manifested His love and devotion, this great miracle was born in this very Kaaba, whom his parents, Haider and Allah, named Ali. This is the blessed date of the birth of the Master of the Straight Path, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), which took place in the House of Allah, the Kaaba. Hazrat Fatima bint Asad (s.a.) entered it, and the period of Imamate began in the Kaaba. Three days later... The period of Imamate began in the Kaaba. Three days later, when you came out of the Kaaba, you opened your eyes to the efforts of Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Upon entering the house, the Mercy to the Worlds, in one moment, Imam Ali (a.s.) completed a journey of the Prophet's efforts. From here, the world of the Master of the Faithful was born, because the beginning of these virtues was in the Haram. Let us take another look at the unique relationship of Imam Ali (a.s.) that the entire Islamic world agrees that no one except Imam Ali (a.s.) was born in the Kaaba. The famous Egyptian scholar from the university, in the following pages, the scholar of the Ummah, in his book 'Mustafa', page 156... In his book 'Mustafa', page 156, the mention of Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) is there. In this same page, it is taught that no one before you was born in the Kaaba. The scholars of the Islamic world agree that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is not only famous for his birth in the Kaaba, but Ibn Asakir, in his book 'Tarikh Dimashq', volume 42, pages 355 and 356, has recorded that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Looking at the face of Ali is worship.' Just as going to the Kaaba for worship and Hajj is necessary, so too is looking at Ali. In 'Tarikh Dimashq', volume 42, page 356, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has stated... Volume 42, page 356, records the research of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), which states that looking at Ali (a.s.) is worship. That is, on one hand, looking at the Kaaba is worship, and on the other hand, mentioning Imam Ali (a.s.) and remembering his virtues is also worship. Allah the Almighty granted Imam Ali (a.s.) the honor and status that no one else was granted, and that is that no one except him was born in the Kaaba. The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) holds the same status and position as the Kaaba. And in this virtue, he has no equal. Just as the Kaaba is a focal point for Muslims, so too is Imam Ali (a.s.) a focal point. Giving preference to anyone else over Imam Ali (a.s.) is like giving preference to a building that has no connection to Allah over the Kaaba. The Kaaba does not depend on the arrival and departure of people, but in the light of a famous hadith, it is the responsibility of the people. Just as people are responsible for aligning themselves towards the Kaaba for prayer, it is the duty of the Muslim Ummah to help Mawla Ali (a.s.) and follow his Wilayah and Imamate. To claim that Imam Ali (a.s.) is among the people just as we are, and that we can just sit in our homes and claim to be his followers, is a mistake. Just as people subscribe to things today, Imam Ali (a.s.) warned that failing to follow his path would lead to loss. This path was initiated by Imam Ali (a.s.) for those in whose hearts the love of Wilayah resides. Today, every Muslim, regardless of their differences, performs their most important act of worship—Salah—facing the Kaaba. This is a point of reflection for all Muslims. This is a point of reflection for all Muslims: to follow the Wilayah and Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), in complete obedience to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Allah (s.w.t.). We extend our heartfelt congratulations to all believers of Islam on this occasion. We pray that on this blessed date, Allah (s.w.t.) hastens the reappearance of the Master of the Age, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), so that the entire Muslim Ummah may unite and establish the values of Islam, just as the love for the Kaaba unites us. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This lecture addresses the importance of mourning for Imam Husayn (a.s.) through loud wailing and weeping. The speaker refutes those who discourage public displays of grief, arguing that such mourning is a form of loyalty to the Prophet and a means of receiving Divine mercy. By citing the prayers of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), the lecture emphasizes that raising one's voice in sorrow for the Ahl al-Bayt is a blessed act that invites God's compassion.
content:
Haydar, Haydar... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. The sacrifice and martyrdom of the Master of Martyrs, Imam Husayn (a.s.), is so great that wherever humanity is found, people shed tears over the grief of Husayn. But on the other hand, there are also people who cannot tolerate the Azadari (mourning) of Imam Husayn (a.s.). They are always trying to somehow reduce the Azadari so that people move away from humanity and adopt savagery and extremism. One such failed attempt is being told not to cry loudly. As if they want to say, cry softly so that the remembrance of Husayn does not become common in the world. We have no concern for what our opponents say. For the opponents, it is enough to say that in the light of the Quranic verse, the grief of Husayn is the reward of the Prophethood, and through this, we offer condolences to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) for the martyrdom of his grandson and present proof of our loyalty to him. But for us Shias, it is clear that wailing and crying loudly over Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (a.s.) is a cause for the descent of the mercy of the Lord. Just as Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) prayed to the Almighty in the state of prostration for those whose voices are raised for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). The narrator says that I saw Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) in the state of prostration praying: 'Warham tilkal-a'yunallati jarat dumu'uha rahmatan lana' (O Lord, have mercy on those eyes whose tears flow out of mercy for us). 'Warham tilkal-quluballati jazi'at wahtarqat lana' (Have mercy on those hearts that yearn and burn for us). 'Warhamis-sarkhatallati kanat lana' (And send mercy upon those loud voices that are raised for our sake). After knowing this prayer made by an infallible Imam in prostration, if anyone forbids crying loudly, it means they are pushing people away from Divine mercy. O God, grant us the ability to cry loudly for the Master of Martyrs, Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (a.s.), this year and every year. Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: EP11 | Alaamaat -e- Zuhoor Aur Badaa | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉 #ImamMahdiعج
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological concepts of Mahdism, the signs of the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), and the critical role of 'Bada' in divine decree. It emphasizes that while signs serve as tests of faith, the timing of the reappearance remains hidden and subject to divine change, prohibiting any attempts to fix a specific date. The session also highlights the importance of constant expectation and collective supplication in hastening the arrival of the Imam.
content:
He la he la he la... TSR presents. Ya Abna al-Zahra, Ya Abna al-Zahra... O you who are the desire hidden in the longing of my gaze, O the architect of my heart. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us. The quiz link is now live and is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who gave the correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear in today's winners, or if an episode was missed, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all questions in seven out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone was not a daily winner but gave correct answers in seven out of 12 episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Among Islamic beliefs, there is a belief in a reformer and promised personality known as Imam Mahdi, and this thought and belief is called Mahdism. Among the Shia, believing in the Promised Mahdi holds double importance because the Shia consider the Promised Mahdi to be alive. Mahdism encompasses various issues, including the blessed birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), his occultation, the deputyship of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), his longevity (prolonged life), his reappearance, and its signs. Consequently, the description of the signs of reappearance determines specific details in the discussion of Mahdism. As far as the signs of reappearance are concerned, in the treatises and books written on this topic, the signs of reappearance are often divided into two categories: those that are definitive signs. Or those that have been declared as definitive signs, and the second are those that are called non-definitive. Among these signs, those stated as definitive events include: the emergence of Yamani and the emergence of Sufyani, Khasf al-Bayda (the sinking of the earth in the region of Bayda), a large part of the earth sinking, the heavenly cry (a voice from the sky), and the killing of Nafs al-Zakiyyah. These signs are described in books as definitive signs. Respected viewers, an important point regarding the signs is that many hadiths regarding the signs, which are found through multiple chains of transmission and in books, mention the possibility of 'Bada' in these signs. As far as Bada is concerned, let us first try to understand what Bada is. In lexicographical books, Bada is derived from 'badwa'. Regarding Bada, it has also been expressed that if the verb 'bada yabdu' is used with the infinitive 'badwa', it carries the meaning of appearing. And when this infinitive 'bada' (with Ba, Dal, Alif, Hamza) is used, it means change in opinion or view. In summary, the terminological meaning of the word Bada is 'naskh' (abrogation). Just as there are abrogated verses in the Quran, Bada is used in the same sense terminologically. With this difference, when the word 'naskh' is used, it is in the realm of 'tashri'i' (legislative/Sharia matters), and when the word 'Bada' is used, it is specifically related to the realm of 'takwini' (existential/creation). Ayatollah Khoei (may his soul be sanctified) writes in the definition of naskh: Naskh means the removal of a command from religious laws due to the passing of its time or duration. That is, the command of something changes, or its time passes. In other words, Bada means replacing one matter with another. But in the realm of creation, not in the realm of Sharia, but in the realm of 'takwin' (creation), in which the first matter is erased and the second is established. And this is derived from the verse of the Quran: 'Allah eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.' And Allama Majlisi (may Allah have mercy on him) in Bihar al-Anwar has mentioned the discussion of both, i.e., naskh and Bada, in the same chapter. So, viewers, in summary, the belief in Bada is a purely Shia belief. And regarding the signs of reappearance, the hadiths present in our books contain the possibility of Bada. The word 'possibility' is used here because it cannot be said with certainty that there will be Bada in the signs of reappearance; rather, the possibility of each one occurring exists. But declaring each or some signs as definitive in the sense that there is no possibility of Bada in them... Is against some narrations. To prove this, we will divide those narrations into five groups, based on which we understand that in all these signs, whether definitive or non-definitive, the possibility of Bada exists. And these five groups are as follows: those hadiths that command us to wait morning and evening. For example, it is narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, where Mufaddal ibn Umar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.): 'The Imam (a.s.) said: The closest a servant is to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the most pleased He is with them, is when the Proof of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is missing from among the people.' The servants of God are closest to the Lord of the Worlds, and He is most pleased with them, in this state—that is, when the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda) is hidden from the people. 'Walam yajhar lahum walam ya'lamu makana'—and this Proof is not manifest to them, nor is it manifest to the servants of Allah. 'Walam ya'lamu makanahu'—nor do these people know the place of the Proof of God. That is, they do not know where the Proof of Allah is. 'Wahum fi dhalika ya'lamuna annahu lam tabtul Hujjatullah jalla dhikru'—but despite this, they are certain that the Proof of Allah never becomes void. That is, the Proof of Allah exists. 'Walam yadhhabu mithaqu'—and Allah does not break His promise. 'Fa'indaha fatawaqqa'ul faraja sabahan wa masa'an'—in this state, these people wait for his reappearance (zuhur) morning and evening. That is, this phrase here is the keyword: 'fatawaqqa'ul faraja sabahan wa masa'an'—meaning to wait for the reappearance morning and evening. Therefore, what is proven by this sentence is that whether the signs have occurred or not, the believers must wait for the reappearance morning and evening. That is, morning and evening, meaning day and night, one must wait for the reappearance, whether the signs have occurred or not. Then the hadith continues: 'Fa'innashaddama yakunu ghadabullahi 'ala a'da'ihi'—and Allah is most wrathful upon His enemies when His Proof is hidden from among them. 'Walam yajhar lahum'—and he is not manifest to them. 'Waqad 'alima anna awliya'ahu la yartabuna'—and Allah certainly knows that His saints (awliya) will never fall into doubt and suspicion. 'Walaw 'alima annahum yartabuna'—if there were even a tiny possibility of them falling into doubt, 'ma ghayyaba hujjatahu'—Allah would never have hidden His Proof from them, not even for the blinking of an eye. 'Wala yakunu dhalika illa 'ala ra'si shararin-nas'—that is, the occultation (ghaybah) is for those who are the worst of people. That is, the believers, while living in the time of occultation, believe that their Imam and the Proof of Allah remains, whether he is before their eyes or not. That is, viewers, the first group of the hadith, 'fatawaqqa'ul faraja sabahan wa masa'an'—wait for the reappearance morning and evening, expect the reappearance day and night—clearly states that we must wait for the reappearance day and night, whether the signs have occurred or not. Let us move to the second group of hadiths, from which we learn that the possibility of 'Bada' (divine change in destiny) exists in both definite and non-definite signs. The second group of hadiths points toward the reappearance happening suddenly (baghtatan). The words worth noting in these hadiths are 'baghtatan' (suddenly) or 'laylatan' (at night). These are two key terms found in this group of hadiths, and there are multiple hadiths pointing toward this. For example, a hadith is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.): It was asked of him, 'O Messenger of Allah, when will the Sahib al-Ism al-Khas (the one with the special name) emerge?' The question was asked of the Prophet. Here, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) compared the time of the reappearance of the Imam of the Time to the time of the Day of Judgment. He said, 'Masaluhu masalus-sa'ah'—the example of his reappearance is like the time of the Day of Judgment. That is, just as no one can fix a time for the Day of Judgment, similarly, no one can fix a time for the reappearance. 'La yujalliha liwaqtiha illa hu'—only Allah knows its time. It will be heavy on the heavens and the earth. 'La ta'tikum illa baghtatan'—it will not come to you except suddenly. That is, just as 'baghtatan' is used for the Day of Judgment—meaning the Day of Judgment will come suddenly—similarly is the reappearance of the Imam of the Time. It will happen suddenly; it will come suddenly and the reappearance will happen suddenly. Therefore, we have been commanded in the traditions to wait for the reappearance day and night. In one night, the Lord of the Worlds will gather his affairs in such a way that He will bring about his reappearance. And viewers, such hadiths show that only Allah can reveal the time of the reappearance. Therefore, considering the signs of the reappearance as a prerequisite for his reappearance is not correct. Let us now move to the third group. The third group is of those hadiths which consider the time of the reappearance to be subject to 'Bada'. That is, the possibility of 'Bada' exists even in the time of the reappearance. As far as the reappearance itself is concerned, it is a divine promise and it is definite. There is no possibility of 'Bada' in it. But as far as the time of the reappearance is concerned, there is certainly a possibility of 'Bada' in it, and this has been stated for us according to explicit traditions. In the book Al-Kafi, in the chapter on the dislike of fixing a time (tawqit), it is mentioned that it is disliked to fix a time for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time. In it, the late Kulayni (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates a hadith. The hadith is as follows: Fudayl ibn Yasar narrates from Imam Baqir (a.s.). He says: 'I asked, is there a time for this matter?' Fudayl asks Imam Baqir (a.s.), 'Master, is there a time for the reappearance?' He (a.s.) said, 'Kadhaba al-waqqatun, kadhaba al-waqqatun, kadhaba al-waqqatun'—that is, the Imam repeating this means those who fix a time are liars, those who fix a time are liars, those who fix a time are liars. This emphasizes that whoever fixes a time for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time is a liar. Then the Imam (a.s.) gives an example in this hadith: 'Inna Musa 'ala nabiyyina wa alihi wa 'alayhis-salam lamma kharaja wafidan ila rabbihi'—when Prophet Musa went with his delegation to his Lord, 'wa'adahu thalathina yawman'—Allah had promised him thirty days. 'Fallamma zadahullahu 'ala thalathina 'ashran'—then when Allah added ten days to those thirty days, 'qala qawmuhu qad akhlafana Musa fasana'u ma sana'u'—and his people did what they had to do. That is, they said Prophet Musa broke his promise and they did what they had to do. That is, they turned back on Prophet Musa's caliphate. They turned back from the religion of Prophet Musa and betrayed his successor, Harun (a.s.). Then the Imam (a.s.) says—the Imam (a.s.) mentions this example here because the matter of the reappearance is also like this. There is a possibility of 'Bada' in the reappearance, and if Allah wills, He will take this matter to its end, and if Allah wills, Allah can bring about a change in this matter—that is, the reappearance. So this is the group of traditions that point to the possibility of 'Bada' in the time of the reappearance. The third group of hadiths found in our books is of those hadiths in which the signs of the reappearance are described as subject to 'Bada'. That is, not just the time of the reappearance, but the signs of the reappearance are also subject to 'Bada'—meaning there is a possibility of change even in the signs of the reappearance. As has passed, the signs of the reappearance are described as definite (hatmi) and non-definite (ghayr-e-hatmi). That is, they are categorized. It should be clear that according to the traditions, there is a possibility of 'Bada' even in the definite signs, and this becomes clear from the tradition narrated by Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari from our and your ninth Imam, Imam Jawad (a.s.). This tradition is present in the book Al-Ghaybah. Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari says: 'Kunna 'inda Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali'—that is, we were with Imam Jawad (a.s.). 'Fajara dhikru' Sufyani. So the mention of Sufyani began. 'Ma ja fi riwayat'—that is, the traditions present in the books regarding Sufyani, 'min anna amrahu min al-mahtum'—that consider the coming of Sufyani as definite. The mention of those traditions came up. I said to Abu Ja'far (a.s.), Abu Hashim says that I said to Imam Jawad (a.s.), 'Hal yabdu lillahi fil-mahtum?'—can Allah perform 'Bada' even in the definite (mahtum) things? He (a.s.) said, 'Na'am'—the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Yes.' We said to him, then Abu Hashim said to the Imam, 'Fanakhafu an yabdu lillahi fi sahibil-ismil-khas'—then we fear that perhaps Allah might perform 'Bada' in the coming of Imam Mahdi. He (a.s.) said, 'Al-Mahdi min al-mi'ad'—the Imam (a.s.) said, 'This is Allah's promise.' That is, the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is Allah's promise. So Allah does not break His promise. Therefore, it is necessary that the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) will happen. It is definite that the Imam (a.s.) will reappear. But all the definite signs that have been mentioned, even the coming of Sufyani, it is possible that Allah may perform 'Bada' in them. That is, changes may occur and Allah may not manifest this sign. Before this sign manifests, the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) may occur. The last group of hadiths is those in which the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have taught us the supplications that have been taught regarding the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). The Infallibles (a.s.) have prescribed many deeds to avoid going astray during the time of occultation. That is, severe trials will appear in the time of occultation, and to save ourselves from these trials, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have taught many deeds. Among them are the supplications for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.), by virtue of which Allah will keep the believer safe from the trials of the end times. For example, the hadith that Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) taught to Ahmad ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) when he was shown the direct visitation of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). That is, Ahmad ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) is among those companions who directly visited the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) during the time of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.). In this hadith, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'O Ahmad ibn Ishaq, mithluhu fi hadhihil-ummah mithlul-Khidr (a.s.) wa mithluhu kamathali Dhil-Qarnayn'—the example of the Imam of the Time in this nation is like Khidr (a.s.) or like Dhul-Qarnayn. 'Wallahi layaghibanna ghaybatan'—just as they had an occultation, the Imam is swearing by Allah that he too will have an occultation. 'La yanju fiha minat-tahlukati illa man yuthabbituhullahu 'alal-qawli bi-imamathi'—and no one will be saved from destruction in this occultation except the one whom Allah keeps firm on the belief in his Imamate, 'wawaffaqahu lid-du'a'i bita'jilil-faraj'—and whom Allah grants the success to pray for the hastening of his reappearance. That is, the person who prays for the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of the Time and believes in the Imamate of the Imam of the Time—that is, believes in the Imamate of all twelve Imams—such a person will remain safe from the trials of the occultation. The Imam (a.s.) telling this to Ahmad ibn Ishaq points to the fact that there is room for hastening the reappearance, and it is possible that Allah may bring about the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) without manifesting any signs. Or the famous Tawqi' of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) in which the Imam of the Time himself is commanding: 'Wa akthirud-du'a'a bita'jilil-faraj'—that is, pray abundantly for our reappearance. Pray abundantly for the hastening of the reappearance. In other words, the term 'ta'jeel' (hastening) being used itself points to the fact that the possibility of 'bada' (divine change in decree) exists regarding the appearance. Or consider the statement of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), in which he explained that the cause for the salvation of the Children of Israel was their collective weeping, lamenting, and praying to Allah for 40 consecutive days. That is, when the Children of Israel wept and lamented together in the court of Allah for 40 days, Allah reduced the occultation of Prophet Musa (a.s.) by 170 years. Originally, the punishment Allah had decreed for them was 400 years; Allah reduced it by 170 years and granted Prophet Musa (a.s.) permission to appear after 230 years. Here, Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'Ha kadha antum' (Your example is the same). If you collectively weep and lament in the court of Allah and pray for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time, then Allah can bring about 'bada' in this matter and hasten his reappearance. And if you do not do so, then the matter of the reappearance will reach its destined end. The important point here is that this instruction and command to pray points to the fact that there is room for 'bada' in the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.). Besides this, there are many such supplications taught by the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) that are found regarding the hastening of the reappearance. So, viewers, a significant question arises at the end: if the possibility of 'bada' exists in all signs, whether definite or indefinite, then what is the wisdom behind stating these signs? In summary, many wisdoms have been stated in two traditions. We will present two of them to you. The first wisdom is that when any of these signs occur, the hearts of the believers become assured regarding the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.). The second wisdom is a test. When any of these signs do not occur, the non-occurrence of the sign becomes a cause for testing the hearts of the believers. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Amma innahu lam yuwaffaq lana fihi waqt' (Know that do not fix any time for the reappearance for us). 'Walakin idha haddathnakum bishay' (But when we tell you something), 'Fakana kama naqul' (and it happens just as we say), 'Faqulu sadaqallahu wa rasuluhu' (then say, Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth). And if it is contrary to that, then say, 'Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.' That is, it becomes a cause for testing; when a sign does not occur, do we still believe in the Imam's word or not? If we do, then 'tujaru marratayn' (you will be given double the reward). You will receive double the recompense. Thus, the second wisdom behind stating the signs is the testing of the hearts of the believers. However, we must be very careful that no one misuses these signs and leads us astray. If someone claims to be the Yamani, we should know that according to the hadiths present in our books regarding the Yamani, it is clearly stated that the Yamani will come from Yemen. He will not come from anywhere else. As found in a tradition in Al-Kafi, 'Wa zahara al-Sufyani wa aqbala al-Yamani' (The Sufyani will appear, and at that very moment, the Yamani will come from Yemen). He will not come from Iraq or any other place. Or in another hadith, it is found, 'Al-Yamani wal-Sufyani ka-farisay rihanin' (The Yamani and the Sufyani are like two competing racehorses). Meaning they will appear at the same time. So, if someone claims to be the Yamani today, we should know that he is a liar. Why? Because our belief must be based on these hadiths. Finally, we pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He shows us the matter of the reappearance—which has been described in traditions as 'abyanu minash-shams' (clearer than the sun or the light of day)—as soon as possible with our own eyes. That is, when the reappearance occurs, no person will have any doubt whether it has happened or not. It is called 'abyanu minash-shams'. So, we pray to Allah that He shows us that day of reappearance as soon as possible and counts us among the helpers and supporters of Hazrat Hujjat (a.j.t.f.s.). Wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibina at-tahirin al-ma'sumin, wa la'natullahi 'ala a'daihim ajma'in. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alayka ya waliyyal 'asr, adriknā wa lā tuhliknā. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Before we announce today's winners, we would like to inform you that tomorrow, i.e., the 12th episode, will be the final episode of this series. And those individuals who have not yet participated in this quiz, there is no need to be disappointed. The quiz link will remain live until Sunday, March 3rd, at 9:00 PM. And those who have given all correct answers in 7 out of the 12 episodes' quizzes will be included in the mega prize lucky draw, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq. The announcement for which will be made that same night at exactly 9:30 PM, Insha'Allah. Now let's see who our daily lucky draw winners are today, who will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees. And their names are on your screen. Sahil Abidi, Syed from Mumbai. Syed Ahmad Ali, from Alipur. Tasneem Jafri, from Mumbai. Karrar Hussain, from Prayagraj. Mubeen Zahra, from Bengaluru. Syed Wahida, from Mumbai. Many congratulations to all the winners. We thank all of you once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time with another new video. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Iltemase Dua. Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Janabe Hurr (a.s.) Ki Tauba | Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture recounts the profound moment of repentance of Janabe Hur (a.s.) before Imam Husayn (a.s.) on the plains of Karbala. It highlights the Imam's immense mercy and compassion in accepting Hur's apology despite his role in blocking the Imam's path. The narrative emphasizes the spiritual transformation of Hur from a soldier of the enemy to a martyr who attained true freedom in both worlds.
content:
When Janabe Hur, remorseful for his mistake, reached the presence of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and submitted, 'I have come to your presence, repenting before my Lord for the error I committed, so that I may sacrifice my life for you until my last breath. Is my repentance acceptable to you?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Yes, Allah has accepted your repentance and forgiven you. What is your name?' Hur said, 'I am Hur, son of Yazid.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'You are truly free, just as your mother named you. God willing, you are free in this world and the Hereafter.' What a compassionate voice! 'Hur, lift your head, do not be so distressed. You have reached the destination of Truth. Be grateful that I have forgiven you, and my Allah has forgiven you. When the world rejects you, the martyrs will call you the symbol of freedom. Embrace that freedom.'

title: EP#1: Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.) Par Girya-e-Rasool (s.a.w.a.) |  Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound grief of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) regarding the future suffering of his daughter, Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.). It details the specific injustices she would face after his passing, including the violation of her home and the loss of her child. The talk highlights her emotional isolation and the divine comfort she received from angels during her period of mourning.
content:
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) described the pain of his daughter in these words: 'Whenever I see my daughter, I am reminded of the troubles that will be inflicted upon her after me. It is as if I see wicked people forcibly entering her house, showing no respect, usurping her rights, and depriving her of her inheritance. Her side will be broken, and her child will be martyred. She will be crying out, "Ya Muhammada!" but no one will answer her. She will raise a cry for help, but no one will come to her aid. After me, she will always remain sorrowful, distressed, and weeping. Sometimes she will remember the cessation of revelation in her house, and sometimes my departure. When night falls, she will feel lonely because she will no longer hear the recitation of the Quran that I used to perform during Tahajjud. She will see that people are not treating her as they did in my presence. At that time, Allah will comfort her through angels, just as they comforted Maryam bint Imran (a.s.): "O Fatima, indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and exalted you above the women of all worlds. O Fatima, worship your Lord, prostrate, and bow with those who bow."

title: Ikhteyaar-e-Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) | Maddaah-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.) Farhan Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Farhan Rizvi explores the spiritual authority and miraculous powers of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Through poetic recitation, the speaker highlights her status as a source of divine grace, capable of transforming human existence and performing extraordinary feats. The talk emphasizes her unique position in the household of the Prophet and her profound connection to the concept of Tawheed.
content:
May it be a wonderful pleasure at the gathering of the Resurrection to have Ali by one's side, and call upon Allah by saying 'Ali', and call upon Allah by saying 'Ali'. May Zahra (s.a.) turn the dust of a human being back into dust, may Zahra (s.a.) turn the dust of a human being back into dust. I recite the second verse: if she turns her hand-mill, if she turns her hand-mill in reverse. If she turns her hand-mill, if she turns her hand-mill in reverse, O Zahra (s.a.). Dust of a human being... what is this matter of belief? The first line is according to your mood, Mujahid brother, do I have permission? Dust of a human being, may Zahra (s.a.) make someone a Musa, make someone a Salman. This is the authority, brother; may Zahra (s.a.) make someone a Musa, make someone a Salman. The secret of Tawheed, whatever she tells someone, the secret of Tawheed, whatever she tells someone, O Zahra (s.a.). May Zahra (s.a.) turn the dust of a human being back into dust. I recite a line; in this line, I describe two scenes at once. I seek your attention. Dust of a human being... the daughter-in-law of Abu Talib and the wife of Ali (a.s.), the daughter-in-law of Abu Talib and the wife of Ali (a.s.), if the truth is on the Kaaba, if she puts a lock on the Kaaba, Haider, Haider! The daughter-in-law of Abu Talib and the wife of Ali (a.s.), if the truth is on the Kaaba, if she puts a lock on the Kaaba, O Zahra (s.a.). May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Listen to this authority too: if she wishes, she can make a Houri luminous with her handkerchief, if she wishes, she can make a Houri luminous with her handkerchief, and if she wishes, she can create air from dust. If she wishes, she can make a Houri luminous with her handkerchief, if she wishes, she can make a Houri luminous with her handkerchief, and if she wishes, she can create air from dust, O Zahra (s.a.). If she wishes, she can create air from dust, O Zahra (s.a.). Since we are talking about one lady, it is my duty to talk about another lady. Creating air from dust is also a miracle. Creating air from dust is also a miracle. Oh, if she wishes, she can teach this skill to Fizza. Ya Ali! May Zahra (s.a.) turn the dust of a human being back into dust, may Zahra (s.a.) turn the dust of a human being back into dust. I am reciting the last two couplets, as the martyrdom of Lady Umm Hani (s.a.) had passed, I added an extra couplet to it. The mother of Abbas (a.s.) had prayed for this, saying: 'Make my son an Alamdar (standard-bearer).' The last couplet is 'Khak mein khak bashar', and one must listen to the truth in the same way: 'Sar-e-Mahshar ho ajab lutf, Ali saath mein ho.' Sar-e-Mahshar ho ajab lutf, Ali saath mein ho. Sar-e-Mahshar ho ajab lutf, Ali saath mein ho, and call upon Allah by saying 'Ali'.

title: Ep#11 | Itni Toolaani Umr Kaise?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the skepticism surrounding the long life of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) by highlighting the omnipotence of Allah. The speaker provides multiple examples from the Quran and history, such as Prophet Nuh, the People of the Cave, and Prophet Isa, to demonstrate that extended lifespans are well-documented divine phenomena. The talk concludes by arguing that if Allah grants respite to Iblis, it is logically consistent that He would preserve the life of the Imam who guides humanity.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Master of the Age. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Today, the answer we must provide is: how long can a human's life be? The purpose behind this question is solely to address the objections regarding the long life of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). The Muslim Ummah should not object to this. Those who object are those who have not studied the Quran or lack faith in it. My brothers, when the Quran says, 'Indeed, Allah has power over all things,' and this is according to the Quran, then those who object to the long life of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) are essentially denying the power of Allah. If someone has doubts about Allah's power, they are free to ask, but those who believe in Allah's power know that there is no limit to it. A long life is a very minor matter for Him. Allah gives a long life to whomever He wills. When someone dies young, people say it is Allah's will. Here, when it comes to a long life, the same people start doubting Allah's power. My dear friends, this matter is clear. My dear friends, this matter is clear, whether it is the waiting for the end or the waiting for the Quran, the Quran itself mentions the long lives of the Prophets (a.s.) in many places. Let us look at four such verses of the Holy Quran that mention the long lives of the Prophets (a.s.). First, Prophet Nuh (a.s.), whose age in the traditions is 950 years, including the time before the Ark and after the flood, as mentioned in Surah al-Ankabut, verse 14: 'And We sent Nuh to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years, less fifty years.' The second incident in the Holy Quran is about Prophet Musa (a.s.). Regarding him, Allah says in Surah as-Saffat, verses 143-144: 'And had he not been of those who exalt Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection.' If Prophet Yunus (a.s.) had not glorified Allah, He would have kept him in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection. Here, the point to note is that Allah kept not only Prophet Yunus (a.s.) alive but also the fish. The third incident is of Prophet Isa (a.s.), whom Allah raised to the heavens, as mentioned in Surah Al-i-Imran, verse 55. As mentioned in Surah Al-i-Imran, verse 55, Allah says: 'O Isa, I will take you and raise you to Myself.' Besides the Prophets, there are others to whom Allah has granted long lives, as mentioned in the Holy Quran, such as the People of the Cave. Their long life is mentioned in Surah al-Kahf, verse 25: 'And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and they added nine.' We saw that the People of the Cave remained alive in the cave for 300 years without any hesitation. The point to note here is that if Allah can keep someone alive for 300 years without any hesitation, is it not possible for Him to give such a long life to His Proof (Imam)? This was the Quranic evidence. Now, if we talk about history, there are many individuals who are alive, which the entire Muslim Ummah acknowledges, such as Prophet Isa (a.s.), Prophet Khidr (a.s.), and Prophet Ilyas (a.s.). Allama Majlisi, in Bihar al-Anwar, has mentioned many historical figures, such as Salman al-Farsi, who lived for 300 years, and others. In the advice of 1920, and finally, the mention of that which has no oath hidden. Truth is recognized by its head; just as their identity cannot be known without the jail, similarly, the identity of the truthful cannot be known without the criminal. The one who says 'I am', meaning the one who misleads—yes, I am talking about the one who is the cursed Iblis. In the Holy Quran, Allah knew at that time that he is the one who is cursed. In the Holy Quran, it is mentioned, 'Qala anzirni ila yawmi yub'athun' (He said: Respite me till the day they are raised). 'Qala innaka minal munzarin' (He said: Surely you are of the respited ones). The 'respited ones' is the time that is associated with the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Would it not be a question on Allah's decision that He keeps the one who misleads His servants alive, and does not keep the one who guides His servants, the Imam, alive? Will Allah keep the one alive who is the giver of life to His religion? He does everything through His signs. How beautifully the poet has said: 'Khuda ne aap logon ko izzat banakar bhijwaya, Khuda ne batool ko project banakar batlaya, khilafat agle hai aur mat ho aur yeh mamla ho, 84 percent haq-e-Hussain is percent, grant send with full bhuja aur loop.' [Music] To give the correct answer to the question, go to the comment section of this video or the video description, click there, and provide the correct answer. The person who gives the correct answer will be selected in the episode, and they will be awarded 1000 Indian Rupees. [Music]
