title: EP#12: Imam Ali (a.s.) Ke Ehtejaajaat
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical significance of Imam Ali's (a.s.) Ehtejaajaat, focusing on his repeated use of the Ghadir declaration to defend his divinely appointed Imamate. It examines how Imam Ali (a.s.) utilized the Hadith of Ghadir as a legal and spiritual argument against his contemporaries, particularly during the Shura. The discussion further connects the rejection of this Wilayah to the underlying motivations behind the tragedy of Karbala. The session concludes by emphasizing the importance of recognizing Ali's (a.s.) status as the completion of the Prophet's mission.
content:
A message, this is in our useful... [Arabic recitation]... Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. As you all, respected audience, know very well that today is the night of the martyrdom of Hazrat Muslim ibn Aqeel (a.s.). We offer our condolences for this martyrdom to all of you and to the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). In this episode, let us first inform you that the names of the winners of all the episodes so far are present on our social media channels, along with the list of top scorers who gave the correct answers to all questions as quickly as possible. Their names are also present in that list. You must have seen them; those who haven't can check their names there. Let us begin the final episode of 'Hadith-e-Ghadir', the 12th episode, where we discuss whether Imam Ali (a.s.) presented Ghadir as proof for his Imamate. Did he present Ghadir as proof for his Imamate? Although the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed Ali (a.s.) as his successor and executor many times, and announced this from the invitation of Dawat-e-Zul-Asheera until now, it has been announced many times. But Ghadir is the place, the station, where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not just hold Ali (a.s.)'s hand among thousands of people, but announced in front of everyone, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am master, this Ali is his master). So, did Imam Ali (a.s.) present this event of Ghadir as proof or not? And if he did, what were those occasions? To discuss this further, we have our brother Tanveer Deji Shah with us. Brother, Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam. As you heard the topic, we want you to tell us when and where Imam Ali (a.s.) presented this event as proof. Since this is our final episode, and we have looked at many hadiths related to Ghadir in this series, it is very important to tell the audience that the Hadith of Ghadir is a certainty. And if someone says there is no Ghadir, then there is no word of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) because no other hadith has reached us with such frequency and through so many different chains of transmission. It cannot be denied. And if someone says that Imam Ali (a.s.) did not present his right to the people through this hadith, then they should study and look at the books. Because if we study and look at the books, we find more than 22 such incidents where Imam Ali (a.s.) kept the Hadith of Ghadir in front of people to state his right, and spoke about his Wilayah and Imamate. It will not be possible for us to state all of them in today's episode, but we will present some for the audience. But we will present some for the audience. The first incident we find is the first place after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). People abandoned the Wilayah and appointed a Caliph for themselves. When Imam Ali (a.s.) was called for allegiance, he refused. A person named Bashir Ansari says that if you had heard the words before the allegiance of the Caliph, you would never have pledged allegiance to him. Not even two people would have differed in your allegiance. If the audience has seen any episode, this same point was presented before Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). If we had known that we had to talk about Imam Ali (a.s.) or had pledged allegiance to him earlier, we would not have pledged allegiance to him. So this is the excuse that this person is bringing. Imam Ali (a.s.) replied to this. Imam Ali (a.s.) says, 'Would I have left the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) funeral on the ground for Ghusl and Kafan and gotten involved in the matter of Caliphate?' The matter of Caliphate was so clear that I could not even imagine that people would become greedy for it and oppose the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) command. The matter of Caliphate was so clear that I could not even imagine that people would become greedy for it and oppose the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) command. Imam Ali (a.s.) says, and this is our topic today, that Imam Ali (a.s.) is presenting the proof: Did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not complete this proof upon the Muslims on the day of Ghadir? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) completed it that day, and now no one has any excuse. And beyond that, Imam Ali (a.s.) swears the people and says, 'I swear to Allah, whoever heard this statement of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) on the day of Ghadir, and if he has heard it, he should stand up and testify: Did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not say this?' And after that, Imam Ali (a.s.) And after that, Imam Ali (a.s.) narrates the sermon of Ghadir, which every child of ours knows: Did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not say, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am master, this Ali is his master)? After that, Imam Ali (a.s.) recites the prayer that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself said in Ghadir: 'Allahumma wali man walahu wa adi man adahu' (O Allah, befriend those who befriend him and be the enemy of those who are his enemy). Imam Ali (a.s.) completes this proof before the people by pointing towards the companions, showing how they had turned away. And after that, there is a person named... he says that such people were present there, and they say that we were present there and we saw that it really happened like this. But still, I was present in the field of Ghadir and heard this from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), but still, I denied these words of Ali (a.s.), and because of that, my eyes'... And because of that, my eyes lost their light. This is one occasion where Imam Ali (a.s.) reminded the people in Rahba that you were present and you heard these proofs of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and even after that, you are denying it. After this, we find another, and this is famous by the name of 'Khutbah-e-Ghadir'. Imam Ali (a.s.) gave this sermon on the seventh day after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). In this sermon, you explained the verses of Ikmal and the sermon of Ghadir in detail and placed your right before the opponents. Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) has also recorded this sermon in his book 'Rawdat al-Kafi'. This is a long sermon, but we will present a part of it to the audience. These are the words of Imam Ali (a.s.): It was the last age of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the last part of his life, when a person stood up and was claiming that... When a person stood up and was claiming that they knew the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s intention, that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would leave this world in a few days, so after that, we were claiming the Caliphate. After that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) went on the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat-ul-Wida), went from Medina to Mecca, completed all the rites of Hajj there. After that, when he reached Ghadir, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ordered that a pulpit be prepared. And Imam Ali (a.s.) says that when this pulpit was prepared, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) called me to him and raised me on his hands, and raised me so high that the whiteness of his armpits became visible, so that everyone present could see that this is Ali (a.s.). After that, Imam Ali (a.s.) repeated the words of that sermon: 'Man kuntu mawlahu'. Did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not say, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyun mawlahu'? And after that, Imam Ali (a.s.) recited that prayer: 'Allahumma wali man walahu wa adi man adahu'. Here, it is necessary to say that Imam Ali (a.s.) did not just draw the people's attention to that sermon, but also to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s prayer, where friendship and enmity were defined. Regarding the appointment of friendship and enmity, you should also repeat this point. Many say that enmity towards the enemies of Allah is essential. Today, in our series of episodes, we have shed light on how, if we want to recognize true monotheism (Tawhid), then the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) is necessary. Here, Imam Ali (a.s.) is saying in clear words that my Wilayah is the Wilayah of Allah, and enmity towards me is enmity towards God. After that, Imam Ali (a.s.) recites the Quranic verse: 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum' (This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion). And then Imam Ali (a.s.) says that my Wilayah is the means for the perfection of religion and the pleasure of Allah. Meaning, if religion is perfected, favors are completed, and Allah is pleased, it is only and only through the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.). So, this is the second instance where Imam Ali (a.s.) presented Ghadir before the people. Imam Ali (a.s.) presented Ghadir before the people to declare his right. The third point, and the last one to be presented in today's episode, is a very famous event that every Muslim knows and recognizes, and has read about. When the period of the second Caliphate was ending, we all know that a committee was formed, which we know as the 'Shura'. There were six people in this committee, one of whom was Imam Ali (a.s.). When these six people were in this Shura, Imam Ali (a.s.) presented several arguments where he explained that I am the most superior and this Caliphate is my right, not yours. This Hadith is also famous as 'Hadith al-Inshidat' or 'Hadith al-Munashada'. Here, Imam Ali (a.s.) gives an oath of God to the other members of the Shura and says: 'I give you an oath of God, tell me, in this assembly, who among you, other than me, is the one about whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyyun mawlahu (Of whomsoever I am the Master, this Ali is his Master)?' Of whomsoever I am the Master, this Ali is his Master. The Messenger (s.a.w.a.) said this about him. And then Imam Ali (a.s.) repeats that claim again. He says: 'May God befriend his friends and be the enemy of his enemies.' And after that, Imam Ali (a.s.) says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) even said that it is the responsibility of those present to convey this message to those who are absent, to those who are not present there. Make it public that at Ghadir, Imam Ali (a.s.) was declared the Master of the people. All the people present there, the five individuals present with Imam Ali (a.s.), all said: 'Yes, this is true, there is no doubt in it.' So, these were some occasions where Imam Ali (a.s.) presented his appointment and Wilayah before the people. As mentioned at the beginning of the episode, Imam Ali (a.s.) presented his right and his claim to the Caliphate before the people through the Hadith of Ghadir. But if we could explain in detail that people would accept... If we could explain in detail that people would accept and acknowledge Imam Ali (a.s.) as their Imam, if they had done so, then not only would there be no corruption, but the events that followed would also not have occurred. These were people whose calling them 'human' is an insult to humanity. Just a few days ago, we commemorated the martyrdom of Muslim bin Aqil (a.s.), and today we are mourning his children. And this was the peak of cruelty in Karbala, where the last piece of the Prophet's heart, Imam Hussain (a.s.), was martyred by these very people in the anger of Imam Ali (a.s.), hungry and thirsty for three days in Karbala. And this martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is nothing but the result of hatred towards Imam Ali (a.s.). Because when on the day of Ashura, Imam Hussain (a.s.) asked these people: 'Why are you killing me? What wrong have I done to you?', those people gave only one answer: 'We are killing you because of the hatred we have for your father.' Meaning, hatred for Ali (a.s.) is the crime for which people even kill the son of the Prophet. For which people even kill the son of the Prophet. We always pray to God Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and keeps us and our children steadfast on the Wilayah and Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Thank you very much for proving through these events and through these arguments that Imam Ali (a.s.) presented Ghadir as a proof. All these arguments prove that it is not that Ali (a.s.) just sat back and did not demand his right, but to think so is a misunderstanding. The reality is that whenever, wherever, and however it was appropriate, Ali (a.s.) presented the event of Ghadir as the greatest proof to establish his Imamate and kept reminding people repeatedly that the right he was claiming was nothing but a divine command. With this, this episode and this series come to an end. We hope you liked our series. If you liked any episode of this series or even a small part of any episode, and the name of Ali (a.s.) was mentioned in your presence... And the name of Ali (a.s.) was mentioned in your presence, then it is a matter of happiness for us. The goal of our entire series was that in this month, we all together keep remembering Ali (a.s.) and learn from this series. If you have any questions—yes, so far we have been asking you questions, but if you also want to ask us any questions, you can send them to our WhatsApp number. Insha'Allah, we will definitely get the answer to that question to you. As we conclude, as always, let us remind you once again that the link for this episode will become active as soon as the episode ends. We request all of you to click on that link and participate in it. Answer all the questions correctly, and the winner of this episode will be announced, as always, the next day, i.e., tomorrow, on our social media channels. And now, the most important question that will be in your minds: who will get the Ziyarat of Karbala, and who will be the lucky ones to receive all these prizes, and when will this be announced? Let us tell you that soon, Insha'Allah, we will hold a celebration in which the names of all the winners will be announced. In that celebration, Insha'Allah, we will announce the winners from Iraq, India, and other countries. In that celebration, Insha'Allah, all these names will be declared. We request you all to stay tuned to our social media channels. Insha'Allah, information about the celebration will reach you through those channels. So, with this, the time has come to say goodbye. Until next year, Allah Hafiz.

title: Paighambar (s.a.w.a.) Ka Janaaza Zaroori Tha Ya Khalifa Chunna?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical controversy surrounding the events immediately following the passing of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It contrasts the actions of the companions who prioritized the selection of a Caliph at Saqifah over attending the Prophet's funeral. The speaker emphasizes the Shia perspective that Imamate is a fundamental pillar of faith and critiques the decision to abandon the Prophet's funeral rites for political succession.
content:
According to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Imamate and Caliphate are among the fundamentals of religion, and the one who denies the Imam of his time is also considered a disbeliever. The companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) considered it more important to select an Imam and Caliph after his martyrdom than to participate in the funeral of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). That is why, leaving his funeral, they went towards Saqifah. Or in other words, in the eyes of those people, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had no importance, or perhaps for the companions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it is so important that the Prophet whose Kalima they recited to become Muslims, it was more important for them to select an Imam and Caliph than to participate in his funeral. May Allah's blessings be upon Muhammad and his family. So this is also a reality of the Infallibles (a.s.).

title: Kis Ki Ziyaarat Qubool Hogi? | Arbaeen 2025
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual significance of performing Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) with pure intentions. It highlights the teachings of Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the cleansing of sins and the immense rewards associated with each step taken during the pilgrimage. The speaker concludes with a prayer for the sincerity required to attain these spiritual benefits.
content:
Only the one who performs Ziyarat with a sincere heart will be purified from sins. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Whoever performs the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) for the sake of reward, not for show, not for pride, not for hypocrisy, and not for fame, then all his sins are washed away just as clothes are washed clean with water, and no impurity remains on them. And for every step he takes, the reward of a Hajj is written for him, and for every step he lifts, the reward of an Umrah is written for him.' We pray to God Almighty to grant us the ability to perform Ziyarat every year with a sincere heart, which is free from show, pride, hypocrisy, and fame-seeking. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.
Sincerity is the primary condition for the acceptance of Ziyarat.
Performing Ziyarat for show, pride, or fame invalidates its spiritual benefits.
Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) equates the cleansing of sins through Ziyarat to washing clothes with water.
Every step taken toward the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) carries the reward of a Hajj.
Every step lifted during the pilgrimage is credited with the reward of an Umrah.
The ultimate goal of Ziyarat is the total removal of spiritual impurity.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 5 | Tafseer of Surah al-Faatiha (Surah # 1) - Part 5
excerpt: This lecture continues the tafseer of Surah al-Fatiha, focusing on the spiritual significance of the Ummah of Muhammad and the divine promises bestowed upon them. The speaker narrates a tradition regarding the pre-existence of the Ummah answering Allah's call, establishing the origin of the Talbiyah. The session emphasizes the virtue of reciting 'Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen' and the profound power inherent in Surah al-Fatiha. Ultimately, the speaker urges believers to maintain a strong connection with the Quran and the Ahlulbayt to fulfill their duties as members of the Prophet's community.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the master of the prophets and messengers, and the seal of the prophets, Abul Qasim Muhammad, and upon his pure, clean, and infallible household, and may the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies from now until the Day of Judgment. To proceed, Allah the Almighty has said in His Noble Book: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum. Once again, I am present before you to present the interpretation of the signs of Surah Al-Hamd, and the tradition I mentioned yesterday was not completed because this tradition was long and we have to finish our talk within ten minutes, and I try that our clips are not so long that you face difficulty in watching and listening. I am continuing this same tradition, starting where Janab Musa (a.s.) had a conversation with the Lord of the worlds, and Janab Musa (a.s.) had said that I want to hear. At that time, the Lord of the worlds called out to the Ummah of Muhammad, and when Allah called the Ummah of Muhammad, everyone answered from the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers and said, 'Labbayk'. Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk, La Sharika Laka Labbayk, Innal Hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, La Sharika Lak. Allah the Almighty made this answer the Talbiyah of Hajj. Then our Lord called out and said, 'O Ummah of Muhammad, this is My decision for you: that My mercy has surpassed My wrath, and My forgiveness has exceeded My punishment. I have accepted your supplications even before your prayers; before your asking, I have bestowed My gift upon you. Whoever among you comes before Me sincerely confessing 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lahu wa anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh' and is a follower of the truth in his actions, and also acknowledges that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the brother of Muhammad and after him his successor and guardian, and also obeys him just as it is necessary to obey Muhammad, and after Muhammad and Ali, the pure and purified chosen guardians of God, who are the manifestors of the signs of God, are his successors—then I will admit those who hold this belief into My Paradise, even if... Even if his sins are equal to the foam of the sea. Allahu Akbar. Respected viewers, ponder a little, viewers, what is the greatness of the Ummah of Muhammad! I wish we would try to get rid of sins, our sins would decrease, try to gradually reduce sins, if they end, it is a very good thing, so that on the Day of Judgment, when we are called as the Ummah of Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), we should neither have to be ashamed nor should the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) have to be ashamed of our actions. Have you pondered in this tradition what is the virtue of the Ummah of Muhammad? Hazrat Ali (a.s.) says that when Allah sent our Prophet Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), He said to him, 'Wa ma kunta bijanibit-turi iz nadayna' (And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called), meaning, Muhammad, you were not present at the side of the Mount when We called your Ummah and bestowed this honor upon them. Then Allah the Almighty said to Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), 'Say Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen, for God has distinguished me with this virtue,' and Allah also said to the Ummah of Muhammad, 'You... Also say Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen, for He has distinguished you with these virtues.' Allahu Akbar. Respected viewers, ponder what is the virtue of saying this 'Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen'. I had submitted before you in the beginning that the meaning of saying 'Alhamdulillah' is that you have expressed gratitude, and every believer who is truly a believer and who has faith in the Quran, Muhammad, and the family of Muhammad, should, while believing in this, try daily to thank the Lord of the worlds for His blessings, acknowledge the blessings, and express gratitude so that the Lord of the worlds may increase His blessings upon them. There is another tradition in 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih' where Imam Ali Ridha (a.s.) was asked about some matters regarding causes, in addition to Sharia rulings. In it, regarding Surah Al-Fatiha, after explaining 'Rabbil Alameen', Imam Ali Ridha (a.s.) explained 'Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim', saying that with these words, Allah the Almighty has reminded His subjects of His favors and bounties again. Allahu Akbar. Anyway, Surah Al-Hamd has two parts, two components. In the first... Part, there is a conversation; in the second part, there is also a conversation. In the first part, Allah is talking to the servant; in the second, the servant is talking to Allah. There are two parts. How important is this Surah Al-Hamd! And anyway, it has great virtue. If it is recited seventy times over a sick person, his illness will vanish. In fact, the Infallibles (a.s.) even say that if you recite Surah Al-Hamd seventy times over a dead person and he comes to life, I would not be surprised. Why? Because they are certain, they know what the virtue of Surah Al-Hamd is. And Alhamdulillah, we recite Surah Al-Hamd in every prayer. So, respected viewers, this is the grace, favor, and kindness of the Lord of the worlds that He has placed us in the Ummah of Muhammad. We should also try to fulfill the right of being the Ummah of Muhammad, and that right will only be fulfilled when we are connected to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, because our existence is based on being connected to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt. If we are not connected to them, we have no existence. And our duty is only clear communication. Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen.
The Ummah of Muhammad responded to Allah's call in the spiritual realm, which became the basis for the Hajj Talbiyah.
Allah's mercy and forgiveness are promised to those who believe in the oneness of God, the prophethood of Muhammad, and the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The Ummah of Muhammad holds a unique status of honor and virtue in the eyes of Allah.

title: Mega Winner Announcement | Imam Mahdi (a.s.) Aur Hamaara Khuloos | ⛅  PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of Ikhlas (sincerity) as the foundational element of faith and devotion to Imam Mahdi (a.s.). It emphasizes that true sincerity involves purifying one's intentions, performing acts of service without seeking worldly recognition, and aligning one's life with the Imam's will. The session also highlights the importance of Marifat (recognition) of the Imam, the necessity of constant self-improvement, and the role of compassionate service to humanity as a reflection of one's spiritual commitment.
content:
TSR presents. Oh, oh, the hidden desire in the longing of my gaze, oh, oh, the comfort of my heart, oh, the comfort of my heart. My Mawla, my Mawla, half of this moon, half of this moon, the wings of my flight, have opened with the longing for your face. Oh, son of Al-Hassan. Your midnight has become the wings of my flight, the excuse for my life, the certificate of my servitude, the certificate of my servitude. Your midnight has become the wings of my flight, the excuse for my life, the certificate of my servitude, the certificate of my servitude. I wish you would smile, capture my heart, leave a mark, oh moon that delights the heart, at the foot of my gaze. I wish you would smile, capture my heart, leave a mark, oh moon that delights the heart, at the foot of my gaze. Half-severed, oh son of Zahra, my head is at your path, I give my life, oh worthy one. Since childhood, you have struck sparks in my existence, the breeze of your memory has struck flames in my tearful eyes. My heart has reached the alley of the garden of your imagination, the lovers have flown towards you again. The night of the dawn, the night of your moon-like face, my tearful eyes are always on your path, I have laid my head at the foot of your threshold. You are the one who has become my autumn, lip to lip, from your spring, you are the one who has been the life of my soul, sacrificed for you. The longing for your era, gave me a new life, at every moment. Come, for I sacrifice my life at your arrival, I fulfill my promise on the mornings of Friday. Come, come, come, for I sacrifice my life at your arrival, I fulfill my promise on the mornings of Friday. Come, come, to your side, I make the poor one, and I cure the old wounds. My dear, the hope of Haidari, the fragrance of Kausari, the unique one of heart-stealing, oh you who buy me, and me in your service. Eyes on your path, with the gaze of you, oh you who give life, I am your army. Forgive, your patient stone, I did not become, even if my heart, is tight for your reappearance, I did not become. Forgive, life, sacrificed for you, it did not happen, my heart, the moisture of your loyalty, it did not happen. You are the one who, every evening and morning, is my memory, you are the one who prays for this unhappy heart of mine, you are the one who buys this miserable heart of mine. You are my beloved, the hand and the helper, and I am the one who is bad, but I have a friend. In your love, in your love, I have refuge, oh descendant of Ali, I have a friend. Oh descendant of Ali, I have a friend. You always have a friend, who has removed the thought from my head. I called out, you looked at me, for your love, you manifested in my heart. For your love, you manifested in my heart. Come Master, you are the world, come Master, you are the world. My moon, my light, my arrest, my end, from the hand of Haider. Again, the lock of dignity, the bearer, again, the lock of dignity, the bearer. For I am happy, you are my fortune, written that, you are, my Master. I am a sinner, but without you, O Master, you are always, my religion and my world. You are always, my religion and my world. You are always, my religion and my world. In longing for you, my eyes have turned to blood, O, waiting for the water. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon our master Muhammad and his pure and immaculate family. And may there be eternal curse upon all their enemies. So the topic is, it is, regarding the Imam of the Time (a.s.), and regarding his personality of high attributes, regarding the Master, how to adopt sincerity, and how to bring sincerity into our lives, and in simple words, if we say, we are sincere with the Imam. How can this be? So first of all, let us have a little discussion on this word 'sincerity' (ikhlas), what is the meaning of sincerity? If we can understand the meaning of sincerity through worldly examples, then it will become very easy for us to understand what sincerity with the Imam of the Time means. When we say that this milk is pure (khalis), 'ikhlas' is derived from 'khuloos', 'khalis', 'khuloos', all these words belong to the same family. So when we say 'khalis' or 'khuloos' in Urdu, let us first look at the word 'khalis'. This milk is pure, what does it mean that it is pure? There is no water mixed in it, there is no other chemical mixed in it. This honey is pure, meaning it is exactly honey, there is no other thing, syrup, or any kind of extract mixed in it. We say for example, take any food or drink, it is absolutely pure. We say about gold, the gold is pure, there is nothing else mixed in it. So this has come into our minds, 'pure'. If we say that there is brass inside this gold, then calling it pure is also wrong. You extracted milk from a cow or buffalo and then after that, in one seer of milk, you added half a glass of water, then it is not pure, or you added some chemical to it, it is not pure. So one thing is understood, the meaning of pure is that whatever thing is being referred to, it is that very thing, nothing else. Sometimes, the presence of water in milk creates a flaw that the milk is not pure, and sometimes the presence of milk in water creates a flaw that the water is not pure. If you want pure water, and someone mixes a little milk in it, you would say I want pure water, I cannot drink this. If there is milk and someone mixes a little water in it, then if I ask you, are you troubled by the water or the milk, I don't understand, I am mixing water in milk, you are objecting, I am mixing milk in water, you are objecting. So you will say, Maulana, whatever thing I want at that time, it should be pure. Date syrup, honey was mixed in it, you ate it, you said I told you I wanted date syrup, pure. Why did you mix honey? Okay, I say fine. So now you, reverse this example, that you want syrup, you want honey, and I mixed a little date syrup in it, both food and drink items are pure. No, not that. From this, it is understood that whatever thing we use for a specific purpose, we only want that thing at that time, we do not want any other thing. The thing itself, and nothing else besides it, in simple words. This one thing became clear to us. Now when we talk about 'khuloos' regarding the Imam of the Time, it means that here we have to see how to apply the example of gold, syrup, honey, or milk here, meaning in such a way that through this example, 'khuloos' regarding the Imam of the Time is understood. Now I will talk to you again through an example here. We say that because until now the talk was about food and drink items, worldly things. Now the example I am giving, this is about a human being. We say this person is very sincere with his job. He is very sincere with his business. What does it mean? He does not put his job and business at stake at any cost, he does not put them in danger. Be it wind, rain, or storm, he is standing at his office door at 9:00 AM. And until he finishes the whole work, he does not leave. If any friend comes, relative comes, he does not give them extra favor. He is sincere with his job. Then we come, it will take you a little while to understand the examples, but understand this a little. Then we come, we say he is very sincere with his parents. He is very sincere with his brother, sister, sincere with his wife and children. When we come to the members of the parliament who win the seat, the members of the assembly, we say this person from our area, sir, who won the seat, he is very sincere with his area. What does it mean? He does not tolerate any political maneuvering, he says brother I don't want anything, I want to get a road built in my area, I want a school for the children, I want this hospital for the girls. He keeps working in his area. Now you must have understood that I will say one sentence, what does it mean to be sincere with the Imam of the Time? Now the meaning of being sincere with the Imam of the Time, now this matter has come that this is a completely different thing, the personality of the Imam of the Time. First of all, when I say I am sincere with my area, the area from which I won the election, I am getting roads and schools built there, so it is understood. I am sincere with my parents, I am serving them, whatever they need, I am providing it. But when we say we are sincere with the Imam of the Time, then what does the Imam of the Time lack that I should give? One question is this. And does the Imam need a road in my area, I built it, does he need a school, I built it. My father needs medicine, my mother needs clothes, I provided them. My wife and children need these things, I provided them, I made them available. What thing should I provide to the Imam that the Imam does not have? The Imam has everything. The Imam does not need anything. So then what is the meaning of this discussion? How to be sincere with the Imam? In the easiest words, it means, whatever the Imam is saying, you perform it in a sincere way, in a pure way, with sincerity. So it means that being sincere with the Imam, meaning whatever is the Imam's will, whatever is the Imam's preference, whatever the Imam wants, that a believer, a Shia should live like that, you perform those things with the Imam in that way. Now when the matter came here, then what is the status of the Imam? The status of the Imams in our religion is the Religion of God. Meaning if you write on a paper, blackboard, whiteboard, 'Religion of God' or in other words 'Allah's Religion', then write 'is equal to what?'. People of the world might be confused, you will not be confused. You will say Religion of God, Allah's religion means the Imam of the Time. Meaning if you say Religion of God, if you say Imam of the Time, both in our view, according to our belief, even according to the Quran, the matter is one and the same. Because in narrations, the Infallible Imam has been called the Religion of God in many places. What does it mean? Meaning whatever the Imam has said, that is the Religion of God. So Imam, what did the Imam mean? Religion of God. Now when it became the Religion of God, then I will read two verses before you, not more. First of all, if we look at it, when we talk in common words that some person is of God and we call him a very sincere servant of Allah. The examples have passed now. Sincere with parents, sincere with job, and sincere with his electoral area. Now here the matter is coming to the servitude of God. When we say this gentleman is a very sincere servant of God, then what does it mean? It means this has been written by the scholars that when we call someone a sincere servant of God or 'mukhlis', the Quran has used both words, 'mukhlis' and 'mukhlis'. So 'Sadaqal-abdu fi tawajjulihi ilallahi i'tiqadan wa 'amalan'. Meaning this servant of God who is performing the work, according to God's command, in terms of knowledge and action, his full attention should be towards God, pure. I stood up and prayed, now people should say to me whether you prayed or not? People object to me. My full attention is towards God. If I have prayed my prayer in the right way, then now whatever the world keeps saying, I should not care about it. This matter is clear. I am slowly bringing you closer to the topic so that after that we can go, in the time we have, half the discussion we have done on sincerity, then the sincerity of the Imams and then we will talk about our sincerity, how our sincerity should be regarding the Imam. You, I give you an example. Go and see in Nahj al-Balagha. Go and see the Saif-e-Sajjad, Imam-e-Sajjad. Look at all the works of the Imams. Imam-e-Hasan-e-Mujtaba, helping the poor, he is blind. Who are you? I am a servant of God. We cannot even think about the Imam that 'riya' (showing off) will come into the Imam's heart. But sincerity is such a big gift, such a big gift that the Imam is saying that I have in my heart that I should not want anything from any servant. Amir-ul-Momineen is helping, he does not even know who this is. And later people told him that this is the Caliph of the Muslims in Kufa. So then he used to be very surprised. Similarly, we see the incidents of Imam-e-Sajjad. Similarly, we see the incidents of Imam-e-Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), so we find these incidents. But if you look in the Quran, the definition of sincerity has been given by God Almighty in very simple words that 'La nuridu minkum jaza'an wa la shukura'. When they, the Ahlul-Bayt, the incident is before you, for three days the beggar, orphan, needy came, the Ahlul-Bayt gave them bread. If we count, the five loaves of bread were of the Ahlul-Bayt, the sixth loaf was of Janab-e-Fizza. And Amir-ul-Momineen had not told anyone to give bread. Everyone saw the Master giving, so everyone gave their bread. There is a simple matter here, but it is a very difficult matter and a very important matter. While giving the bread, the Ahlul-Bayt did not say, 'Take it, brother, my beggar, you are my Muslim brother or brother in terms of humanity.' Take this bread, we do not want any thanks from you, we do not want any reward, we do not want any reward against this. They did not say this. It is not in any history. God is saying that these people say that we do not want any reward from you, nor thanks. So if they did not say it, then why is God saying that they are saying it? Scholars have written that God has brought the state of the Ahlul-Bayt's hearts into the verse. Meaning the state of their heart was such, it was so pure, so pure that God said that these people are saying this. This is a very big thing. That I say one sentence here that the Imam was asked which charity is superior? He said, 'Ala zir-e-rahm-e-kashih', your blood relative who, in simple words, who does not thank you, whose good deeds do not reach you, give charity to that blood relative, help him. Second narration, this was about the relative, second narration, all this is revolving around our discussion of 'khuloos'. Second narration that 'Su'lan ajwadun-nas'. Who is the most generous, the most giving, the most charitable? He said that he is the one who gives to him from whom there is no hope of getting anything in return. This 'khuloos', meaning even up to thanks, this hadith is saying do not even hope for thanks. What is Amir-ul-Momineen saying in Nahj al-Balagha, to Kumayl? It is a long hadith, so I will summarize it that Kumayl, look, tell your family members, your tribe to acquire good morals and try to fulfill the need of the person who is sleeping. O Master of the Universe, Commander of the Faithful, leave everything else and fulfill the need of a sleeping person. The Master said, 'Look, I swear by that Being from whose ears no sound escapes—I am speaking in my own words now, these are my words—you will go to the sleeping person, and that sleeping person will not hear the sound of your footsteps, but God will hear it.' It is a strange sentence. The third, fourth, or rather fifth example of sincerity (ikhlas) is that it should not make you indifferent. What do we say in our Urdu? 'Dil uchaat ho jana' (to become disheartened). Do not let your heart become disheartened. You are doing good to people, and no one is responding to your kindness. Beware, do not let your heart become disheartened. The one to whom you did a favor, this one, that one, this one—they didn't even return a greeting, didn't offer you tea. Meaning, they didn't even look at you with a smile. Let them all go to hell, let society go, I am... Let the prayers be given, let the Imam-e-Bada go anywhere, I am not worthy of this. The Imam says, 'You do good to them, and you are not getting a response. The One who will reward your kindness is the One who never took advantage of you, and through that stranger, God will give you so much that you cannot even expect.' Subhan Allah. Here, the Commander of the Faithful—and let's leave aside to what extent this is about sincerity or not. But this also tells us a strange thing, that the Commander of the Faithful is pushing us, urging us, 'Look, do good with sincerity.' So, the whole concept of kindness is there. Now, if I say something here, that the Imam of the Time—meaning the religion of God—and truly, sometimes I will quote a sentence here, very great personalities, very great figures, and perhaps if I say it is no exaggeration, it is a gift from the Panjtan, the Fourteen Masumeen (a.s.) to the Shias. Hazrat Ayatollah Uzma Vahid Khorasani. I am quoting his sentence. He says that in the day, some time, some moment, some duration—two minutes, three minutes—sit alone, even if you are with everyone, let your mind go towards the Imam, think about the Imam. 'Sir, what should I think?' Just think. Think about the Imam. And then he said, 'It is impossible that a person who thinks about someone excessively, the effects of that person do not manifest in their own being.' Subhan Allah. This is a very important thing. Why did the Ayatollah say this? That such a personality is such that if you think about him, he will bestow some grace. Now, you have that supplication before you: 'O God, grant me the recognition (marifat) of Your Being.' Now, it is even embarrassing to recite this prayer and explain the translation, because the Momineen, Masha Allah, and the Momineen who will watch this lecture, they all know 'Allahumma arrifni nafsak'. O God, make me recognize Your Being. Because if I don't, I won't be able to recognize Your Messenger. Make me recognize the Messenger. Because if You don't make me recognize Your Messenger, I won't be able to recognize the Imam of the Age, Your Proof (Hujjat). Make me recognize my Imam, grant me his marifat. Because if I haven't recognized my Imam, then look, 'wa zalaltu an deeni' (and I have strayed from my religion). If the marifat of the Imam does not come, you will go astray from your religion. Brother, I don't believe in the twelfth Master, he is 1400 years old, 1200 years old, he is 40 years old right now, he has children, he doesn't, which prayer to recite, at what stage of infallibility (ismat) is the Imam, how much is his oppression, the grief of his ancestor—these are not the important things. You are praying, fasting, that's fine. This hadith is saying, this prayer is saying, no matter how much worship you do, if there is no marifat of the Imam, you are in danger of straying from your religion. Meaning, the worships—our prayers, fasting, Hajj, Zakat, all these things—what should be their foundation? The marifat of the Imam of the Time. If this is there, then I am saved from going astray. So, first of all, this is one thing. From here, another aspect of sincerity is that the personality whose marifat guarantees me protection from going astray, this is the marifat of that personality. Pay attention yourself. In prayer, people ask the Marja, 'Sir, I kept my thumb like this, I forgot.' So, the wudu was like this, the Marja will say, 'Okay, fine, you tried to learn, right? Okay, this happened? Fine, don't do it from now on, the rest of the prayers are correct, go.' You did this while fasting, you thought it wasn't obligatory, so now do the qada (make-up), go. No problem, do the qada, there is no kaffara (expiation). Okay, this happened, this happened? You ate by mistake, no qada. This is how it is in Fiqh. It cannot be like this with the Imam. The moment you bring the Imam down from that position in your heart, your downfall, your decline begins. Because God is saying, I am... the Imam is saying, 'zalaltu an deeni'. From here, we understand how to maintain sincerity with the Imam. And let me say one sentence: the first sign of sincerity with the Imam is that a person says to himself with regret, 'I could not be sincere with the Imam.' This topic is very strange, and I will finish in the allotted time, God willing, but by the blessing of this topic, I was given this topic myself to bring it up in the lecture later, Insha Allah Ta'ala. That the Imam feels bad when we say, 'I am your staunch Shia.' The Imam said—there is an incident of Imam Sajjad (a.s.)—he said, 'You call yourself a Shia?' 'Yes.' He said, 'Are you Salman? Are you Abu Dharr? Are you Miqdad? Are you Ammar? Who are you?' He said, 'Master, I am not.' He said, 'When you are not these, why are you calling yourself a Shia?' These were Shias. So, when this thing is before us, no matter what high stage we reach, we cannot be Salman. Therefore, the meaning of sincerity is that a person should always see the flaws, shortcomings, and deficiencies within himself. Never think that we have done a great job. Because, let me tell you one thing, if I do a great job in Fiqh, I cannot leave behind a 'Jawahiri'. If I work within Wilayat, I cannot leave behind a book like the one by Mir Hamid Hussain Musavi (may Allah elevate his status) or Allama Amini. If I give lectures, give sermons, I cannot give sermons like Imam Sajjad (a.s.). So, where are we, at what stage are we? We are at no stage; we should realize our humility and poverty. Okay, now let me read two verses before you. The first verse is from Surah Bayyinah: 'Wa ma umiru illa liya'budullaha mukhlisina lahud-din' (And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion). This is one thing. Worship God in this way. The second thing, well look, this is about the worship of God, worship God, but 'mukhlisina lahud-din', keep purifying your religion continuously. This means that if you and I were given a life of a thousand years, then the sincerity I had at the age of nine hundred should increase at the age of nine hundred and one. The second thing: 'Illa alladhina tabu wa aslahu wa'tasamu billahi wa akhlasu dinahum lillahi' (Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their religion for Allah). All people will be ruined except those who repented and corrected themselves, 'wa'tasamu billahi' (held fast to Allah), 'wa akhlasu dinahum lillahi' (and purified their religion for Allah). What is the Infallible Imam? What did I submit to you in your service? The Infallible Imam means the religion of God. If it is said about these verses that the religion of God means you keep purifying your marifat with the Imam, then this verse also includes this meaning. Now, I have about half the time left, which is about sincerity regarding the Imam. The first thing, why should we go left and right to the people of the world? The eleventh Imam. When the narrator came to meet the eleventh Imam, he came to ask who would be after him. Before the narrator could ask the question, the Imam said, 'Have you come to ask this?' He said, 'Yes, O Son of the Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Wait.' He went quickly, came back, and said, on his shoulder 'ala atihi' (on his shoulder) was a child, very radiant, very charming, heart-stealing, attractive to the eyes, and very radiant, very innocent. He said, 'This is your Imam after me.' And then he said, 'Lawla karamatukum 'alallahi wa 'ala hujajihi lama 'aradtu 'alaika ibni hadha' (If it were not for your honor in our presence, in the presence of my ancestors, and in the presence of God, I would not have shown you this son of mine). This means that the first condition for connecting with the Imam is honor in the presence of God and the Fourteen Masumeen. Am I honorable or not? Do the Imams honor me or not? How do the Imams honor? There is no room for any ambiguity here. Everyone knows this. From the moment you wake up in the morning, the work I am about to do, will the Imam honor me after this or not? Life will become completely clear. Then after that, the Imam said that he will have an occultation (ghaybah) and after that 'la yanju minal-halakati' (no one will be saved from destruction) 'illa man waffaqahullahu lil-qawli' (except for the one whom God grants the success to say) 'illa man waffaqahullahu lid-du'a bi-ta'jilil-faraj' (except for the one whom God grants the success to pray for the hastening of his reappearance). So, one thing we understood is that to be saved from destruction—and what I told you about 'zalaltu an deeni', that is also destruction—God is saying to call upon your religion with sincerity. This means that praying for the Imam himself is a ladder of marifat, a level, a stage of the marifat of the Imam. Second, that God Almighty 'thabbatahullahu 'alal-qawli bi-imamatihi' (God keeps him steadfast on the belief in his Imamate), only these two will be saved from destruction. This became a fundamental thing. Now I have to see to what extent I pray and to what extent my attention is towards the Imam. Now a point has come here: prayer. I will talk about these two points and finish the talk. First, look, I am repeating again and again that there are countless things in the hadiths. Our Shias should do this, our Shias should do that. The strange thing is, and truly regarding the Imam, that the good work you are doing with the Shias—this is a Momin, this is a Momin, this is an Azadari—the work you are doing, the Imam is saying, 'Do it with me.' This is a very strange thing. Okay, Master, then should we completely finish off the people of other religions? Leave it, no. Whatever work you do in society that increases the honor of the Imam, the Imam is happy with it. So, when we say that this work should be done with the followers of the Imam, it does not mean that you should leave those who do not believe in the Imam, who do not love him. We are living in the subcontinent. The Imam's command is regarding the neighbor. Your neighbor is Hindu, Sikh, It is correct, his respect, and it has come in the traditions. He is sleeping hungry there and you are sleeping with a full stomach, your faith is gone. Women are going, respect their homes, treat the children of their homes with love and mercy. Treat the elders of their homes with mercy. They are non-Muslims, but this is being told to you. This means that if there is one follower of the Imam and he is among non-Muslims, then he is not a threat to them, he is a blessing for them. This is what our religion teaches. But if someone thinks that a follower of Imam Hussain, an Azadari, is living in society, and society considers him a threat to itself, or there is some flaw in his love for Imam Hussain and the Imam of the Time, or he is an ignorant person, he has not read what the Imam wants and how the Imam wants to treat humanity—we have a word in Urdu, I think it is Hindi, 'bhale manas' (be a good person), live like a good person. One is 'bhala manas', one is 'band manas'. 'Band manas' means a jungle human, lives in the jungle. 'Bhale manas', learn to interact with humans. So why did I say this? Because when we talk about Momineen, about the 'arbab-e-aza' (people of mourning), those who come to the 'farsh-e-aza' (mourning carpet), it does not mean that the rest, the non-Muslims, have no honor or status. Coincidentally, they have great honor, great importance, status; this is what our Imams have told us. Anyway. First thing: prayer. When you pray, what should be the standard of prayer? The quality of the prayer will tell how much sincerity there is. Praying for the Imam, for the hastening of the Imam's reappearance. Look, there is a detailed discussion on this, conversation, but I will make that conversation useful in a brief way. I give an example. For children and for the elderly. A ninth-class student has to go to take an exam, it's a board exam. Matric. There is a young boy, our girl, she has to go for a job. Time is running out, he is looking at the watch, no auto, no bicycle, no rickshaw, no bus, he is not getting anything. Now what will he do? He will pray, pleading. God forbid this time comes for anyone, but it has come for many. The father is severely ill, the father is in the struggle between life and death, the mother is in the struggle between life and death. How will this person pray? Pray in the presence of the Imam in that way. Okay, now if one is to pray for the Imam, then what should be prayed? O Lord, may the Imam not sleep hungry, may the Imam have AC in the summer, a heater in the winter, a blanket, may the Imam not have any trouble, may the Imam not be sick. What should be prayed, in what way? This is a question. But you can pray at that time if I find out that a friend of mine, a brother, a close relative, his cold hasn't been cured for 20 days. 'Maulana, please pray, may his cold be cured.' I will say, 'Insha Allah, whenever I remember, I will do it.' Once it will be said that a Maulana has been on a ventilator for 20 days—God forbid, I swear by the intercession of the Panjtan (a.s.) that may God not bring this time upon any of the organizers of Azadari—the Maulana has been on a ventilator for 20 days. Now the prayer will change. Now the prayer will change completely. So, how will you pray now? Pray for the Imam in this manner. Now, how can one reach the stage of praying for the Imam? Until we understand the oppression (mazlumiyat) of the Imam, we cannot reach this stage of prayer. That is, imagine a person who possesses every power in the universe, and the enemies of his noble mother, the enemies of his grandfather, the enemies of his grandfather's Azadari, those who claim to follow his grandfather, the enemies of Nahj al-Balagha—all of them are doing their work, and those who love the Mawla are being subjected to oppression and tyranny. If the Imam wishes, one gesture could set everything right. But due to God's command and servitude, the Imam keeps a stone on his heart, and after placing that stone, from morning until evening—I cannot say since the Imam opens his eyes until he sleeps at night, we do not know what the Imam's life is like—but from morning to evening, in what state of agony is the Imam? Tell me one thing: you see a very tragic accident on the road. You come home immediately, your wife has prepared food, you say I will eat after a while, you cannot eat. Your children are coming, you are not talking. Even any activity in the house, you are not doing. Why? Your day, your thoughts are stuck there, on the accident I saw, the poor innocent child. So look at the Imam; until we absorb this aspect of the Imam, we cannot pray this prayer. Therefore, our elders used to weep over the Imam's oppression, wondering what the Imam's oppression is like. This is one thing. The second thing is, what am I doing in society to help people recognize the Imam's essence? 15th of Shaban is coming, we were just discussing this. How many books have been written about Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) that I like, some you like, some I don't like, but that Momin likes. The book you like, it's a good book, buy five of those books; for poor children in the family who have a passion for reading or rich children who are unable to buy them, you can buy five or three books. Buy the books and give them away, keep them in the mosque for a week and make an intention that if someone takes it, it is Halal for them, and if they keep reading it, I will come and take it back after 20 days. Do this one thing, spread the recognition (Ma'rifat). Why is there such emphasis on Majlis? Because the Mawla's Ma'rifat is being spread. Therefore, this is one thing. Within the family, various things can be done; I will not go into that, my time is running out. So, books about the Imam. After that, when Nime Shaban arrives, regarding the Imam's Ma'rifat, we owe a great debt to the poets of Ahlulbayt who write poems and Qasidas about the Imams. But if there is a poet, my heart says that Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.) will pray for him, who writes a Qasida about Dua-e-Ahad. Someone who brings the prayer of Imam-e-Zamana, 'Allahumma Kun Li-Waliyyika', into a Qasida. What does this mean? The Ma'rifat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) that our children have received, it is not directly through Ziyarat, it has come through Nohas, so the one who writes the Noha deserves credit, the one who recites the Noha deserves credit. When the voice 'Ya Hussain' comes, children come to the Imambargah while performing Matam. How did this happen? You brought the grief of Imam Hussain to a human level, so it spread among the people. Therefore, the Ma'rifat of the Imam should be brought to this level, that books should be taught, there should be a 'Khamsa' (five-part study) in which the Imam's personality is discussed, what will happen after the reappearance, what will happen before the reappearance. As far as I remember, the late Janab Nomani wrote 'Ghaybat-e-Nomani', in which I think the topics generally brought, if I speak chapter-wise, I remember about 22 very important topics, and for every topic, he has brought about 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 narrations. There are 22 major topics about the Imam. And suppose we teach children the method of prayer. Then another important thing is to give Sadaqat and charity in the name of the Imam. That is, with the Momineen, we have a narration that whatever work we do with the Momineen, we are doing all those works with the Imam. This is one thing. Now I return to the topic of sincerity (Ikhlas). When God says 'Mukhlisina lahu ad-din', sincerity. What is the meaning of sincerity? That is, if I have done this work for the Imam, then look at two things: one is 'Sum'a' (seeking fame/hearing), one is 'Riya' (showing off). What is the meaning of Riya? I am giving a speech here and for show, Momineen are sitting, seeing that the Maulana is giving a speech. This is Riya, for show. One is Sum'a, where does Sum'a come from? From 'Sama'at' (hearing). I gave a speech, no one was there, I said no, I am doing this for the Mawla. Now after that, 10-20 people heard it, now I want to be praised, I am sitting hoping someone praises me, a feeling is arising in my heart. Both these things are against sincerity. Well, this is for me. Suppose the Momin person I came with, who brought me, what is their intention? I am serving for the Imam. What is my intention? I should thank them. So this is from my side, that I should not have expectations. But regarding the Momineen, they have a separate responsibility, that they should thank and respect whoever is doing religious work for them. Not because—although I am sitting—whoever it is, even the one who recites Noha, the one who is sweeping the Imambargah, doing service, respect them. This went somewhere else. So what is the meaning of Sum'a? The good work I did, I want it to be heard, people should hear, someone should tell someone else, someone should tell me, my talk should be mentioned to someone else, there is a discussion on the internet, my mention should come; I did the work at that time. Therefore, the Imam has sought refuge from both these things, Sum'a and Riya. So when there is sincerity, it will be in such a way that whatever work I am doing in connection with the Imam, I should neither expect praise from anyone nor do it to show anyone, this is sincerity. Well, one thing. Actually, sincerity is a gift from God according to the Quran. God is saying in the Holy Quran that God Almighty is far above what these people describe of God. Except for 'Ibadallah', those servants of God whom God Himself has purified. Therefore, in the Quran, sometimes 'Mukhlis' is used, sometimes 'Mukhlis' is used. When 'Mukhlis'—well, I tell you, the month of Shaban is a great month to bring sincerity, because there is a command to recite 1000 times 'La ilaha illallah wa la na'budu illa iyyahu, mukhlisina lahu ad-dina wa law karihal-mushrikun'. So this, it means that the fast of Shaban, the worship of Shaban brings sincerity. Anyway, so this matter, that Sum'a and Riya, the Imam has sought refuge from this. God is saying that no matter how much you describe God, God is like this, God is like that, God is above this, but there is a group of humans that glorifies God, God says their glorification is good. Which servants? The sincere servants. What is the meaning of 'Mukhlis'? They did not purify themselves. God has bestowed His grace upon them. I am telling you from a grammatical perspective, not from a theological one. The grammatical meaning is 'Mukhlis', God has purified them. God is doing this work with me, it means I need success (Tawfiq) from God, so I should pray. Now, do I recite Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin or not? Do I recite Abul Hasan-e-Zarra-e-Isfahani on Friday at the time of Asr or not? Maulana, there is no time, Arabic is weak, I am a driver, a salesman at a shop, where should I open Mafatih? You keep reciting Salawat for the Imam, you keep reciting Qulhuallah for the Imam, you keep reciting Inna-Anzalna for the Imam. Do small things. You say you are going to Karbala, keep this 500 rupees from me, and go there and recite a small Ziyarat, in Samarra, in Karbala, 'Assalamu Alaikum' on behalf of the Imam. All these works, the Majlis that is happening, we should gift it to the Imam. If the law is that sincerity will come from there, as a gift, then until something goes from here, nothing can come from there. Therefore, send the human from here, and then surely something will come from there. Maulana, how do we know if there is sincerity or not? If you have this thing in you that you are doing the work that the Imam will do after coming, after the Ghaybat, with the Momineen, with humans. The most fundamental thing: widows, orphans, the destitute. As much as you can uplift them, if there is a widow or orphan in someone's house, consider them like your own children, and after that, you have the spirit that you say, 'No, don't thank me, it was my responsibility.' No son, don't thank me, it's an orphan child, it's my responsibility. I am a postman, a courier, and truly in my heart. It means fall into prostration, you have sincerity within you. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal hujjat ibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba-ihi fi hadhihis sa'ah wa fi kulli sa'ah waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim, bismillahir rahmanir rahim, wa salla Allahu alayka ya Wali al-Asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. First of all, we once again extend our congratulations to all of you on the occasion of the blessed birth of the refuge of the universe, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). And we pray to God Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of our Imam of the time. May He grant us all the success to remain steadfast on his Wilayah and grant us the success to convey the message of the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to the whole world. This 12-episode video series was our small effort for this propagation of the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.). We hope you liked these videos, and the topics discussed in these videos proved helpful in taking a step towards the recognition of our Imam of the time and serving him. And in today's special episode, we are also grateful to Hujjat al-Islam wal-Muslimeen Aali Janab Maulana Abu Talib Tabatabai for bringing us closer to our Imam of the time through his speech. By participating in the quiz related to our videos, you all have encouraged us a lot, and that is why we are deeply grateful to all of you. It is certain that among all the individuals who participated in this quiz, only one will be the lucky one whose name will be selected through the computerized lucky draw system for the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. But there is no denying that this lucky draw winner would not have been selected if you all had not participated in this quiz. Therefore, we pray in the court of God Almighty through the intercession of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) that whoever participated in this quiz with the intention of Ziyarat, may He grant them the reward and merit of Ziyarat according to their intention. And whoever is the winner, we humbly request them that whenever they go for Ziyarat, they should go for Ziyarat on behalf of all the members of the TSR team and all the people who participated in this quiz. So come, viewers, now the time has arrived for which you all were waiting impatiently. That is, the announcement of the mega winner of the Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Refuge of the Universe Mega Quiz 2024, whose selection is being done through our computerized lucky draw system, who is going to receive the prize that every lover of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) desires, which is the Ziyarat of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimiya, and Samarra, that is, the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. So come, viewers, let us see who is that lucky person, and their name is here on your screen: Wajiha Jafri from Mumbai. Many, many congratulations to you for being the lucky one who has received the prize of a Ziyarat to Iraq. The TSR team is once again grateful to all you viewers. Please do remember us in your prayers that the Lord of the Worlds grants us the ability to organize such quizzes. If you have any feedback or suggestions regarding this series, please send them to our WhatsApp number [number removed]. If you also want to join us in spreading the message of the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then subscribe to our channel, like the videos, press the bell icon, and keep the notification bell on so that every video of ours reaches you first. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that the Heir of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), hastens his reappearance, and grants us the ability to hold firmly to the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) until the very end, and may those who share our videos with others also be counted in the reward of propagating the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ameen, Ya Rabb-ul-Alameen. Insha'Allah, we will meet again in our upcoming Sibti-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz, which will be held in the coming month of Ramadan on the occasion of the blessed birth of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). Until then, goodbye, request for prayers, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen, was-salatu was-salamu ala Sayyidil Anbiya-i wal Mursaleen wa ala Aalihi-t-Tahireen. Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala says in the Holy Quran: 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanut-taqullaha waltanzur nafsun ma qaddamat lighad, wattaqullah, innallaha khabirun bima ta'malun' (O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow - and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do). My respected Momineen, in today's Majlis, we will examine our lives in the light of this blessed verse. Man often gets so lost in his worldly preoccupations that he does not worry about his afterlife. But the Quran reminds us repeatedly that we have to return to Allah. Amirul Momineen Hazrat Ali (a.s.) has said: 'Ad-dunya daru mamarrin la daru maqarrin' (The world is a place of passing, not a place of staying). We should rectify our deeds and try to attain the pleasure of Allah. May the Lord of the Worlds grant us the ability to perform good deeds. Ameen.
Ikhlas is defined as the purity of intention, where actions are performed solely for the sake of God and the Imam without desire for fame.
The Imam of the Time is considered the embodiment of the divine path, making devotion to him synonymous with following the religion of God.
True Shia identity is rooted in humility, constant self-reflection, and the recognition that one's devotion is always a work in progress.
Serving the needy, orphans, and society at large with mercy is a practical way to demonstrate sincerity and serve the Imam's cause.
Regular prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is essential for spiritual steadfastness and maintaining a connection to the divine.
The Ahlul-Bayt serve as the ultimate models of selfless generosity, teaching followers to give without expecting worldly return.
Spreading the recognition of the Imam through education and social media is a vital responsibility for the faithful.

chapters.summary: The lecture introduces the concept of sincerity (ikhlas) by comparing it to physical purity in substances like milk and gold.

chapters.title: Applying Sincerity to the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explores how to apply the concept of sincerity to the Imam of the Time, emphasizing that it means aligning one's life with the Imam's will.

chapters.title: The Imam as the Religion of God
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the Imam of the Time represents the Religion of God, meaning his commands and preferences are the standard for a believer.

chapters.title: Defining Sincerity (Ikhlas) in Servitude
chapters.summary: The speaker defines sincerity as complete, pure devotion to God in both belief and action, regardless of external opinions.

chapters.title: Ahlul-Bayt and the Essence of Generosity
chapters.summary: Using examples from the Imams, the lecture highlights that true sincerity involves giving without expecting reward, thanks, or recognition.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Marifat of the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that religious practice is incomplete without the recognition (marifat) of the Imam, which serves as the foundation for avoiding spiritual deviation.

chapters.title: Humility and Sincerity in Shia Identity
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that true sincerity requires acknowledging one's own shortcomings and humility, rather than claiming a status that one has not earned through the level of devotion shown by figures like Salman al-Farsi.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Praying for the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the importance of purifying one's religion and maintaining a connection with the Imam, highlighting that praying for the hastening of the Imam's reappearance is essential for spiritual salvation.

chapters.title: Ethical Conduct and Universal Compassion
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that a follower of the Imam should be a blessing to all of society, including non-Muslim neighbors, by embodying kindness and moral integrity.

chapters.title: The Depth of Prayer for the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker urges believers to pray for the Imam with the same intensity and urgency one would feel for a loved one in a life-threatening situation, rooted in an understanding of the Imam's suffering.

chapters.title: Spreading the Recognition of Imam Mahdi
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the importance of spreading the Ma'rifat (recognition) of Imam Mahdi through books, poetry, and community service.

chapters.title: The Essence of Sincerity in Service
chapters.summary: True sincerity requires avoiding Riya (showing off) and Sum'a (seeking praise), focusing instead on serving the Imam through humble acts.

chapters.title: Practical Ways to Serve the Imam
chapters.summary: Small, consistent acts of charity and service to the needy, performed with the intention of pleasing the Imam, cultivate spiritual sincerity.

chapters.title: Mega Quiz Winner Announcement
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with gratitude for the participants of the Imam Mahdi Mega Quiz and the announcement of the Ziyarat prize winner.

chapters.title: Upcoming Programs and Spiritual Reflection
chapters.summary: The host announces the next quiz for Ramadan and begins a lecture on the importance of preparing for the afterlife.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 10 | Our Duties Concerning The Holy Quran
excerpt: This webinar session explores the essential duties of believers regarding the Holy Quran, emphasizing the necessity of seeking its true interpretation through the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The lecture warns against the dangers of interpreting the Quran based on personal opinion or unqualified intellect, which is described as a grave spiritual error. It also highlights the historical context of Hadith preservation and the importance of fostering a Quran-centered environment in the home to maintain spiritual guidance and salvation.

But the intention must be there. Our problem is that when we read newspapers, we read everything in them. When we watch TV, we watch everything. In the news, there is nothing but gossip. We spend time searching the internet or shopping. We waste our time. We are all victims of this. Another big problem is WhatsApp. We are all victims of this; we keep checking it. content:
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: Everything has a Zakat, and the Zakat of the body is fasting.
Fasting serves as the spiritual Zakat for the human body.
The concept of Zakat extends beyond wealth to include physical purification.
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) established the link between fasting and bodily refinement.
Fasting acts as a mechanism to cleanse the physical self.
Every aspect of a believer's life, including the body, requires a form of Zakat.

title: Hajj Kaise Mukammal Hota Hai
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes that the perfection of Hajj is intrinsically linked to the belief in Wilayah. The speaker argues that just as ritualistic precision is required for the physical acts of Hajj, a deep understanding of the spiritual pillar of Wilayah is essential for the pilgrimage to be accepted. Without the recognition of the Master of the Universe, the speaker contends that the Hajj remains incomplete and spiritually void.
content:
The Prophet says, "Ma'ashiran-nasi hujjul-bayta bikamalid-din" (O people, perform the pilgrimage to the House with a complete religion). Do you understand what a complete religion means? It is that complete religion which was perfected at Ghadir, perfected with the announcement of the Wilayah of the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat). "Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum" (Today I have perfected your religion for you). Therefore, it is a condition until the Day of Judgment that one must go with the belief in Wilayah for that Hajj to be a perfect Hajj. Otherwise, it is incomplete; it is an imperfect Hajj. In reality, he has not performed Hajj at all. And "at-tafaqquh" (deep understanding of religion)—people are so careful about the rituals of Hajj, ensuring they know every detail. People save their life's earnings to go for Hajj. If even one ritual is misplaced, their Hajj remains incomplete, and all their money is wasted. All that effort and hardship would be in vain. That is why it was said to perform it with Tafaqquh (deep understanding). So, when people pay such attention to the rituals of Hajj, how much knowledge should they have regarding the most important, the most vital pillar, which is the soul of the worship of Hajj—the Wilayah of the Master of the Universe? Indeed.
