title: E'teraazaate Ghadeer Ep#04: Kya Ghadeer Ka Ailaan Waaqeah-e-Yemen Se Mutalliq Tha?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common objection that the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) announcement at Ghadir Khumm was merely a call to love Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) rather than a declaration of his Wilayah and successorship. The speaker refutes this by examining the historical context of the Yemen expedition, where companions complained about Ali (a.s.) to the Prophet. By citing Sunni historical sources, the lecture demonstrates that the Prophet's defense of Ali (a.s.) was a firm assertion of his authority and status, intended to silence those who were jealous of his position.
content:
In this fourth episode of 'Aish-o-Dehri', as you know, in every episode we present an objection raised by the opponents and provide its answer. So, let us move towards the new objection of this episode, which concerns the event of Ghadir. The objection is regarding the claim made about Ali (a.s.) and certain companions. The objection is that whatever the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced at Ghadir Khumm was only to encourage people to love Ali (a.s.) and keep affection for him in their hearts. Does this event have any connection to the Wilayah (guardianship) and successorship of Ali (a.s.)? Let us first understand this objection, and then we will see what the answer is. For the answer, we have our brother with us. As you heard the objection, they claim that the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) words were merely to encourage love. You have studied this subject well; please explain to the viewers what this event was and whether it has any connection to the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). You have presented this very well. If you look at this objection, it becomes clear that the opponents are trying to deny the Wilayah, and they constantly try to find excuses to undermine the status of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.). This is a deliberate attempt to divert people's attention, and this has been done in a very calculated way. If we look at this objection, it is not new; scholars have answered it, and the answers are available on the internet. We can look at this from three perspectives: first, the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) own words; second, the context in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke; and third, the historical evidence. We will examine whether their claim holds any weight. Is their claim really a valid answer, or is it just a fabrication? Let us look at the facts. First, if we look at the historical records, we find that the companions did not deny the status of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). The first incident occurred during the expedition to Yemen. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) sent Ali (a.s.) to Yemen, and later, when some companions who were with him had a disagreement, they decided to complain to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about Ali (a.s.). They decided to complain to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about Ali (a.s.). The statement that comes up in this context is found in the book 'Al-Musnad' by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The author is a famous scholar, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and in their view, he is a reliable narrator whose narrations they accept. In volume 1, page 147, it is mentioned that people started complaining to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about Ali (a.s.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) became so angry that he came out of his house, and the narrator mentions that the anger was visible on his face. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Do not speak ill of Ali. Refrain from speaking ill of Ali (a.s.).' It is mentioned in their books that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was displeased with those who complained about Ali (a.s.). When they complained, he stopped them. He stopped them from complaining. In fact, if anyone speaks ill of Ali (a.s.), it is equivalent to speaking ill of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself. This is a significant point. Furthermore, they have written this in their books, and other scholars have also recorded it. So, this is a well-documented fact. Now, let us look at the second important aspect. Regarding the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) statement, they claim it was just about love. But if we look at history, Ali (a.s.) was sent to Yemen to manage affairs and collect the Zakat. When he returned, there was a dispute regarding the distribution of the spoils. The people who were with him wanted to use the spoils according to their own wishes, but Ali (a.s.) did not allow it. That is why they wanted to complain to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). I am going to present the evidence from their own books. In the book 'Sirat al-Nabi', volume 4, pages 47-48, it is recorded that when people came to complain about Ali (a.s.) to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he was very angry and said, 'What do you want from Ali? Ali is from me, and I am from Ali.' He rebuked them for their complaints. That if the mother remained on my side, she would not complain about Ali (a.s.), and the sunnah (actions) which are completely from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—he expressed his displeasure and his weight was heavy. And some write about this incident in their books that they have taken this incident from the book of Ustad Ahmad. On that day, first of all, when he wrote this book, it became very clear that there were some people who did not like this preference. There were many such people present who were jealous of his status and his position. They did not like at all that he (the Prophet) should praise Ali (a.s.) in this way. Therefore, they used to try repeatedly to go and complain to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). We have also seen that this historian himself writes in his book that at that time, if any companion was most feared by Allah (s.w.t.) or was most popular in the hearts, it was none other than Ali (a.s.). It was from the sight, and the death occurred. Speaking ill of Ali (a.s.)—this is the time to prove what kind of people these are. Some will know, and this is the interpretation of Islam. Despite having so much authority, their eating, drinking, sitting, and the way they behave in this matter—the second opportunity that is received, towards this, you have to run the United coverage, which he writes after banning this issue. That after this, after this incident happened, the voice of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) becomes even more distinct and absolutely clear. That is, if this was before, and if it was before, then surely this is... and this attempt is made to invent an objection and explain to people that the objection that was raised against Ali (a.s.) was the answer, then it is absolutely... now the third and final one is to bring such a thing. To confront the Mahdi, it will be done. We do not find such a thing anywhere in the tradition. We do not find anywhere in the tradition that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said in this way, 'You people should not complain to me against him,' or in this way, we have seen that today, it was quite clear from the incident of the 14th that when people complained about Ali (a.s.) to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) warned them, he told them to refrain from this act. But we do not find any such tradition in this. Only in the middle, we praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and due to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and him being the successor, this matter becomes absolutely clear that the objection is only on this basis so that people can get their rightful due. If you look at the history of the incident, and the tradition itself, it is only and only the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Indeed, as we have seen, this objection is not correct, and there is no reality in the incident of this time, but rather, it was a failed attempt by those who wanted to continue it, through which they wanted to reduce the status of Ali (a.s.), and all such... They wanted to reduce it, and all such things are put into the hearts of the people so that they may turn away from the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). Insha'Allah, in the next episode, we will appear before you with another objection and another hadith. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Do not pray for anything... that the Lord of the worlds...

title: Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course  - Session # 1
excerpt: This session serves as the introductory lecture for a comprehensive Quranic recitation course, focusing specifically on the foundational importance of Surah Al-Hamd. The lecture emphasizes the spiritual necessity of learning Arabic and Tajweed to ensure accurate pronunciation and meaningful prayer. Participants are guided through the articulation points of specific letters, such as 'Ra' and 'Ha', while being encouraged to integrate the recitation of Bismillah into their daily lives. The program aims to foster a lifelong commitment to Quranic study across all age groups through consistent practice and expert guidance.
content:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I hope you all are in the best state of health and faith, Insha'Allah. Allah, as the Lord of the worlds, has brought a unique program before you. The global Quranic... The global Quranic... who is known worldwide for the recitation of the Holy Quran. You are invited as a judge in various competitions and recitations worldwide. I am referring to Qari Islam Ali Jada, who has been with us for 5 years. In this episode, Insha'Allah, in the first episode of the Quranic support, we welcome and greet you with Salawat. According to the narration, number 2, number 66, it says that the house in which the Quran is recited and Allah is remembered, its blessings increase. The angels come there, the devil stays away from that place, and that house shines to the inhabitants of the first heaven just as the stars appear to the inhabitants of the earth. And the house in which the Quran is not recited and Allah is not remembered, blessings decrease in it, the angels stay away from it, and the devils are definitely present. Dear viewers, the program will consist of 15 episodes, Insha'Allah. It will consist of 15 episodes, Insha'Allah, the series of which is starting today. In this, we will try to learn the correct recitation of the Holy Quran from Maulana Masood, Insha'Allah. And then immediately after that, all the viewers who are connected to this program through your links can recite the Holy Quran before Maulana Masood, and if there is any room for correction in that recitation, Maulana Masood will be here, Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah, to pray. Dear viewers, the recitation of the Holy Quran is obligatory in every month. Therefore, we should recite the Quran correctly so that our prayers are correct. So let's go to Maulana Masood. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I hope you are well. Yes, by the grace of Allah. It is a prayer before you. Alhamdulillah, we are starting the first episode of this program. Yes, Allah is better. Islam... Alhamdulillah, we are starting the recitation of the Holy Quran. We welcome all the gentlemen. And as far as I understand, this is a great gift from the Lord of the worlds. And this is the month, the blessed month of Ramadan, in which the Lord of the worlds revealed this pure book. And the night that has been mentioned, it is said about it that it is better than the nights of a thousand months. And this month is blessed because the entire Quran, which is the constitution of humanity, which is the law of human nature, which is the guidance for human transformation, and the final word of the Lord of the worlds, for which I would like to say that it is the guide for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), as the verse says, 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylatil qadr'—it was revealed in this month, and we are sitting to learn from it. It was revealed in this month, and we are sitting to learn from it. I remember a few things. In Iran, in the class of the late Ayatollah, the teacher said—may Allah keep him safe—that the angels have some boxes and vessels for our 24 hours. Before this, I have pointed towards this in the past. Yes, sir, when I present, for example, at this time, from 10 to 11, what work did we perform? The judgment and the result, the angels put it in that and move it forward. And for every hour of our passing life, there are boxes. Although these boxes are not material, they are like... as we see, many things are not of that type, but I would like to give a small example, like in a memory card, we have the material of thousands of books, millions of books, but when we look, we don't see them. In that same way, on the Day of Judgment, all those things will come before us. May Allah, for the sake of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, forgive our sins and our mistakes, and grant us the ability to do good deeds. So, at that time, the people who will come, the teacher said that the best box and the best vessel that one will find... And the best vessel that one will find will be the moments that we have spent learning the pure book of the Lord of the worlds. And the second place I saw, where we learn the recitation of the Quran, in that place, whatever things are there—like I am sitting in my room at home, I am looking, the table is there, the chair is there, the books are there, the files are there, and the sofa-cum-bed is there, the TV, laptop, computer—these things will all testify that 'this servant of Yours has learned Your book at this time.' What greater blessing can there be for us? By the grace of Allah, what will happen? And if it comes to anyone's mind, 'How will this speak? How will it testify?' Then, if our faith is on the Quran, then the Quran says in Surah Jumu'ah, 'Yusabbihu lillahi ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard'—everything on the earth and in the heavens glorifies Allah. That which comes into your sight, as you see, those who know grammar, who know the Arabic language, know that 'man' is for living beings and 'ma' is for non-living beings. For every living being, Allah says that 'yusabbihu lillahi ma fis-samawati'—the glorification of Allah is by every... Praise be to Allah, the image of Allah, every person, every human being who is on earth, not in the image of a mother, I present all of this to the Book of Allah and to you, where you are sitting today, in front of us, that your voice has been silenced, so is there anyone who uses this, are you aware of this, and I want to welcome you to this program. You see, as my brother hinted a little, and you know that Alhamdulillah, I am famous, in these directions, I have been working in India since '99, teaching thousands of people, and we have been missing opportunities to go and do things. In India, one thing that I want to say openly and clearly is that in the subcontinent, we have been a little distant from the mosque, and Allah has always been there, Alhamdulillah, the campaign has started. title: EP#3 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Par Musalmaanon Ka Ijmaa | IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT
excerpt: This lecture discusses the universal consensus among all Muslim sects regarding the inevitable arrival of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) in the end times. The speaker cites historical Sunni sources and scholars to demonstrate that the belief in the Mahdi is a well-established fact within Islamic tradition. The talk concludes by questioning why, despite this shared belief, the concept of his Imamate and Wilayah is not universally accepted, and offers a prayer for his swift reappearance.
content:
That [the] war... [Arabic: A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, Sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi wa sallam]. In his book 'Muqaddamah', on page 514, it is stated that it is a well-known fact among all Muslims in every era that there will certainly be a person in the end times who will be from the progeny of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). He will be a helper of the religion, justice will prevail, Muslims will follow him, and he will have authority over all Islamic lands. His name will be Mahdi. On this same page, it is recorded that the hadiths regarding Imam Mahdi (a.s.) are authentic, and the elders of the Ahl al-Sunnah, such as Abu Dawud, Bazzar, Ibn Majah, Hakim, Tabarani, and Abu Ya'la al-Musili, have narrated these hadiths on the authority of the companions. Abu Ya'la al-Musili has narrated these hadiths on the authority of the companions, such as Ali (a.s.), Ibn Abbas, Abdullah bin Umar, Talha, Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Abu Hurairah, Anas bin Malik, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Umm Habiba, and Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with them). From these sources, it is absolutely clear that all Muslims, regardless of which sect they belong to, believe in the appearance of Imam Mahdi (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance) in the end times. So the question arises: when all Muslims, regardless of their sect, believe in the arrival of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), his government, and the establishment of justice at his hands throughout the world, then why do all Muslims today not accept the Imamate and Wilayah of Imam Mahdi (a.s.)? We pray to Allah (s.w.t.) to hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance) and grant us the ability to live our lives under his Imamate and Wilayah while remaining steadfast. Grant us the ability to live our lives under his government. Give us permission, O Lord of the Worlds.

"Wa'rifur rasula bir-risalah" know the Messenger through the Risalah (message), through his message. How do you know the Messenger? You know him through the message. This is the Messenger. So you say yes, this is a true Messenger because his message, the things he is saying, are taking us towards Allah. His words are not making us worldly. His words remind us of Allah. The words of this Messenger remind us of the Day of Judgment. The words of this Messenger make us pious, take us towards worship. So "I'rifur rasula bir-risalah" and how to know the Uli-Amr (leaders)? "Bil 'adli wal ihsan" when the Imam speaks, he will talk about justice and kindness. Know the Imam in this way. That is why there is so much emphasis in the traditions to narrate our hadiths, so that people know us. But what happened in history is that people were kept away from hadiths, that we cannot understand hadiths, it is not our job to understand, how will we understand? No, why won't we understand? The Imams have told us for this reason, they have told us for our understanding. So look, I present the third hadith to you, that the narrator says we heard Imam Sadiq (a.s.) saying, "Ma min shay'in ahabba ilallahi" there is nothing more beloved to Allah, that is, the thing that is most beloved to Allah, what is it? "Ikhrajud darahim" that is, spending dirhams for the Imam. This is for Azadari, for Tabarrukat (blessings). And after that, he says, "Wa innallaha layaj'alu lahud dirhama fil jannati mithla jabali Uhud." One dirham will be equal to the mountain of Uhud in Paradise. One dirham, just think, see the reward. "Thumma qala" then the Imam says that Allah says in His Book: "Man dhal-ladhi yuqridullaha qardan hasanan fayuda'ifahu lahu ad'afan kathirah" whoever gives a goodly loan to Allah, whoever gives a goodly loan to Allah, pay attention to the words. What does a goodly loan mean? A goodly loan is that loan which is given with this intention, and the one who takes it also takes it with the intention that he will return it. Good, because interest is not allowed in Islam. Interest is usually not allowed. Therefore, the person who is taking a loan, what should he do? That when he is taking a goodly loan, that is, interest-free, taking an interest-free loan from someone, then when he returns it, he should give a little more. This is the law. This is the basic simple law. Meaning, not so much that there is pressure of interest on him. Just a little bit more, for instance, as a token of appreciation. That, brother, you helped me in my bad times, this is it. Here, Allah says in the Quran that if someone gives to Allah, meaning to the Imam, then its example is that of one who has given a 'Qarz-e-Hasana' (a beautiful loan) to Allah. With what intention is Allah taking it? That of a Qarz-e-Hasana. Allah will return it, but how much will He return? Allah is clarifying that too, "أضعافا كثيرة" (Ad'afan Kathira), He will give him many times more. Many times, now what does many times mean? Millions of times. When Allah says many times, see, whenever something is talked about, it is discussed based on who is speaking. Remember this, see, I am giving a very simple example. It is discussed based on the speaker. A small man who has nothing, if he says, 'Brother, if you help me with this, I will also do something for you,' then it comes to your mind that this poor fellow is himself like this, what will he do for me? But okay, let's accept it, he is saying it. But if a great man says it, then the thought comes to mind that, 'Look, this great man is speaking at this time, for example, he is on a journey, traveling.' He says, suppose he went for Hajj, I am giving an example. He has gone for Hajj, he faces some problem there, so he says to someone there, 'You help me, I am a very big man in India. I will help you many times more than the help you are giving me.' So, the one helping there thinks that if I give him, for example, 1000 Dinars, what will he give me? 2000 Dinars, 3000, 5000. Why? Because he is measuring it according to him. Now, when the Being of Allah is the one speaking, then this is a Being who is infinite in His infinitude. Who is infinite in being infinite, limitless in being limitless. So when He makes a promise, then when He gives, He will give so much, so much that there is no account for it. Just, what should be the condition? The condition should be sincerity. The condition is just, I mean, sincerity from a person, see, there is nothing else besides this. And in this, another important thing I would like to submit for your service is that it should never cross a person's mind that the Imam needs my money or that I am doing a favor to the religion. I am doing a favor to Imam Hussain (a.s.) by performing Azadari. I am doing a favor by organizing a Majlis. No one is doing a favor, rather, if Imam Hussain (a.s.) accepts it, if the Princess (Bibi Fatima s.a.) accepts it, then they are doing a favor upon us. If Imam Hussain (a.s.) accepts it, this is a favor upon us. Whenever we distribute Tabarruk, we should never think that we are doing a great favor by distributing Tabarruk, that we have done a great job. And that is why if someone comes and says, look, we are telling you all these things from experience, if someone says, 'Brother, give me two,' you give two. If he is asking for two, of course, the one asking should also think first, 'Let others get it, then I will take two or three,' but that is a different matter. But never think that if we gave him two, we did him a favor. Why? I will submit this in your service as well, it is possible that the thought came to his heart that he is asking for double because he is being tested whether we are giving or not. Therefore, never even think about Tabarruk that we are doing a favor. We, instead of eating this, we distribute this, it is better, let's distribute two Jalebis, two, for example, whatever people distribute, let's distribute this. No, see, every person should do according to their capacity. As much as Allah has made him capable. See, it is not that if someone distributed something bigger, Allah will accept it, the Imam will accept it, and the one who had no money, he distributed something small, so it is accepted—it is not like that. Whoever does whatever, should do it with sincerity. The deal that happens there, in the presence of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), is a deal of sincerity. It is not a deal of wealth. It is just that a person should never think that we are doing a favor to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The Quran has also spoken about this: لَا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُم (Do not count your Islam as a favor upon me). You have accepted Islam, rather Allah has done a favor upon you, that He gave you the opportunity to become a Muslim. So today, if we have received this opportunity for Azadari, then this is an opportunity from Allah. It is not destined for everyone. Allah distributes this Wilayat after careful consideration. He does not give it to everyone. Do not think that it is just being distributed like this. No, no, He distributes it after careful consideration, and for this, I will also present a Hadith in your service that not only this, but Allah first makes his purity, then his birth pure, makes his birth pure, then gives him Azadari. These things are strange, see. Meaning, if someone assumes—this is also a narration from Al-Kafi—the sixth Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ الْإِمَامَ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مَا فِي أَيْدِي النَّاسِ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ (Whoever assumes that the Imam is in need of what is in the hands of the people). The Imam is in need of what the people have. The Imam is needy of that. The Imam is a needy person. He has gone outside the circle of religion. Meaning, when does this effect of neediness or this feeling occur? When we think that we have done a favor to Imam Hussain (a.s.) by organizing this Majlis. We have done a favor to Imam Hussain (a.s.) by keeping this Azadari. We have done a favor to Imam Hussain (a.s.) by keeping this Tabarruk. No one is doing a favor. No one is doing a favor. Listen further. إِنَّمَا النَّاسُ يَحْتَاجُونَ (People are needy). People are needy. For what? أَنْ يَقْبَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْإِمَامُ (That the Imam accepts from them). People are needy. People are needy. That the Imam accepts. قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ (And Allah Azza wa Jall says in the Quran), the Imam is confirming his point with the Quran. Supporting it with a verse of the Quran. He says, خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً (Take from their wealth a Sadaqah), Sadaqah, for example, charity, meaning whatever they give, they give with sincerity. That is not Sadaqah in the sense of the Sadaqah that is usually taken out, not that. Here, Sadaqah means to spend. خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً. After that, what is the sentence? تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ (You purify them and cleanse them). If you have taken it, accepted it, through this you have purified them and their deeds have been accepted. This is a sign of the purity of lineage. The Imam is telling through the Quran. Therefore, no one should ever have this pride and this thought. Whatever little amount we spend, what is it? What is its worth? What is its value? Oh, the lovers of Ali (a.s.) have passed by who gave their lives and gave them smilingly. I presented the example of Janabe Rushayd in your service before this. The permission that Allah gave to the devil, in that permission, what did Allah say? 'You share in the wealth and children of these people.' So, the one in whose children the devil is a partner, he is not 'Halalzada' (born of lawful wedlock). He cannot be 'Halalzada' because the devil is a partner. Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi was the one in whose birth the devil was a partner. This is found in the narrations. So this devil, this Hajjaj, one day what did he say, do you know? He says, أُحِبُّ أَنْ أُصِيبَ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي تُرَابٍ فَأَتَقَرَّبَ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِدَمِهِ (I wish, today I am in the mood. Hajjaj asked, the cursed one, he said, "Anta Qambar?" (Are you Qambar?) He said, "Na'am." (Yes, I am Qambar.) He said, "Abu Hamdan?" (Is your Kuniyat Abu Hamdan?) Meaning, he is confirming. He said, "Yes." "Na'am." He said, now look at his question. "Mawla Ali ibn Abi Talib?" (Are you the slave of Ali ibn Abi Talib?) Now listen to Qambar's answer. See, this is what happens to the one who stays at the door of Ali (a.s.), then he is the same in eloquence and rhetoric as Ali (a.s.) trained him. And no one can stop this tongue. The one whom Ali (a.s.) has taught to speak, then no power in the world has the strength to silence him. Now this Hajjaj is very cruel, in front of him, great people have become silent. Meaning, if I present examples in your service, you will be surprised. قَالَ اللَّهُ مَوْلَايَ (Allah is my Mawla). Allah is my Mawla. So Hajjaj gave the order, ابْرَأْ مِنْ دِينِهِ (Disavow his religion). Yes, express your disavowal (bara'ah). 'Ibra min dini' (I am free from my religion). Well, Qambar said, 'I will do it. He said, 'No.' 'Do you know what the consequence is? Choose the method of your own death. Choose the method of your own death.' Qambar replied that I leave this in your hands. So he said, 'Now I will kill you in exactly this way.' Fadhbaha (and he slaughtered him). And he killed Qambar. He slaughtered him. Just as an animal is slaughtered, he slaughtered Qambar. 'Yara' means he will see, meaning he will have to give an account. He will have to give an account, listen to this Zilzal. These come, that whoever does a good deed will have to give an account for that one good deed, and whoever does an evil deed will have to give an account for it, his reckoning will be very severe. These are the people who left the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt and went away. And those who are connected to the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, who held fast (tamassuk), Allah will save them from the severe reckoning through this light. Those who are submissive to the Ahlulbayt, for them there will be no such reckoning. The Imam is saying, 'Yes brother, if anyone has an objection to our words, then go and read the Hadith. If there is an objection to the Hadith, then we have no quarrel with him. If he has an objection to the Hadith, then we have no quarrel with such a person. Then there is no issue at all.' And then after that, the Imam says, 'Wa amanahu min faza'i yawmil qiyamati al-akbar'—Allah will keep him safe from the 'Faza-e-Akbar' (the greatest terror) on the Day of Judgment. What is Faza-e-Akbar? Faza, Faza means fear, terror, and Akbar means the greatest. Meaning the fear that will be on the Day of Judgment will be the greatest fear. There will be no fear greater than that, no terror greater than that. Meaning this is a stage of the Day of Judgment, Faza-e-Akbar. How many stages are there of the Day of Judgment? 50 stages. How many years will each stage be? 1000 years. How many days will the Day of Judgment last? Up to 50,000 years. The Quran says that one day near your Lord is equal to 50,000 years. What is this 50,000 years? This is the Day of Judgment. Which will be equal to 50,000 years. In that, one stage of the Day of Judgment is Faza-e-Akbar. What is Faza-e-Akbar? Faza-e-Akbar means the day of the greatest fear. How will that day be? Read the Hadiths. It is in the Hadith that on that day there will be darkness all around, and people will be so afraid, they will sweat so much, they will sweat so much in Faza-e-Akbar that the sweat will flow, flow, flow, passing through their knees and reaching up to here. Now don't think, 'Oh, then there will be weight loss, this will happen, that will happen.' No, no, the condition will be very bad at that time. It will not be a good condition at that time. It will be a very bad condition. There will be too much fear. And it is found in the Hadiths, and this is also taken from a verse of the Quran, Insha'Allah, we will explain it to you tomorrow. That in that too, only he will be saved, only he will be saved who has held fast to the hem of the Ahlulbayt. Whoever held the hem of the Ahlulbayt firmly, only he will be saved. Therefore, look, this holding fast to the Ahlulbayt, this is a very important thing. We are emphasizing this again and again because no matter how much we emphasize, it is because the Prophet spent his whole life saying it. So what is our worth, what is our status, and we are just presenting these things to you for four or six days. The Prophet spent his whole life saying, 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abada'—if you hold fast to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, you will never go astray after me. But what did the Ummah do? The Ummah abandoned the Ahlulbayt. 'Wal-ummatu musirratun 'ala maqti mujtami'atun 'ala qati'ati rahimihi wa iqsa'i wuldihi.' The Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) says in Dua-e-Nudba that 'Wal-ummatu mujtami'atun 'ala qati'ati rahimihi'—the Ummah united to sever ties of kinship with the Ahlulbayt. 'Wa iqsa'i wuldihi'—and drove his children from door to door. 'Illa al-qalil'—very few were those who truly fulfilled the covenant. The rest all abandoned the Ahlulbayt. And that is why Karbala happened. Otherwise, Karbala would not have happened. If the Ummah had held fast to the Ahlulbayt, Karbala would not have happened. Today is the night of the seventh, and this is the night when a youth, a 13-year-old youth is mentioned, 13 years. This 13-year-old youth. This 13-year-old youth is a child who is waiting for death with great longing. That Sayyid-e-Shuhada (Imam Hussain) asked, 'Son Qasim, how is death in your view?' Qasim replied, 'Ahla min al-asal'—it is sweeter than honey. Now when on the night of Ashura, the night of Ashura, Hussain is reciting the list of martyrdom. He took the name of every martyr, he took the name of every martyr, but he did not take Qasim's name. The child, in his senses, went to a corner and started crying. While crying, suddenly he remembered that when his father was leaving this world, he had tied an amulet on his arm and said, 'Son Qasim, when a very big calamity comes, open this amulet.' Now when Qasim opened the amulet, what was written in it? 'Bunayya Qasimu adrik 'ammaka al-Hussain'—O my son Qasim, help your uncle Hussain. When your uncle is surrounded by enemies, then help your uncle. As soon as Qasim read this amulet, he started smiling and came and handed his father's letter to his uncle. As soon as Hussain saw the letter, read his brother's letter, tears flowed from his eyes, he looked at Qasim from head to toe and said, 'Qasim, oh, your name was also in the list of martyrdom. I just didn't mention it. Tomorrow everyone has to be martyred, and Qasim, it is not just your name, but in the list of martyrdom is also the name of your brother Ali Asghar.' Now, where Qasim was happy on one side that my name is in the list of martyrdom, hearing the name of Ali Asghar, the honorable child of Bani Hashim was distressed. He started saying, 'Ya 'ammi hal yasiluna ila al-khiyam?'—O uncle, will the wretched ones reach the tents? Hussain consoled him, 'No Qasim, I will take Ali Asghar on my hands. I will take Ali Asghar on my hands.' Qasim's heart was consoled that the wretched ones will not go into the tents. I will say with folded hands, O honorable one of Bani Hashim, just the thought that the wretched ones will reach the tents and you were distressed. Oh, come and ask Sayyid-e-Sajjad. Asr-e-Ashura, the wretched ones are entering the tents. Sayyid-e-Sajjad is watching the whole scene with his own eyes. Asr-e-Ashura passed. Now the day of Ashura came, the companions were martyred. After Dhuhr, the series of sacrifices of Bani Hashim began. Once when the turn of the children of Hasan came, Qasim came and stood in front of Hussain, and in that letter it was also written that 'Son Qasim, if your uncle does not give permission, then keep insisting until your uncle gives permission.' Then Qasim came and stood there, saying, 'Uncle, please give me permission, Uncle, please give me permission.' Now, I present a sentence from the Maqtal (chronicle of martyrdom) to you; I can barely bear it myself. It is written in the Maqtal that when Hussain (a.s.) was just looking at Qasim and could not bring himself to give permission, Qasim took both of Hussain's (a.s.) hands and began to rub his eyes against them, saying, 'Uncle, give me permission, Uncle, give me permission.' Hussain (a.s.) embraced Qasim and said, 'My son, I give you permission. Come, today is the day everyone must die; today is the day of martyrdom, everyone must die.' Qasim was given permission. Then he came, and Qasim was prepared. After being prepared, both uncle and nephew embraced. They wept so much, they wept to such an extent, they wept so bitterly that both fainted. O mourners, tell me with justice, if someone faints today, what is done to bring them back to consciousness? Water is sprinkled. Alas, Zainab-e-Kubra (s.a.)! Look at Zainab's (s.a.) helplessness; where would she bring water from? She sprinkled her tears. Both uncle and nephew regained consciousness. He said, 'Uncle, now give Qasim permission.' Hussain (a.s.) seated Qasim on the horse. But before he left, Qasim tore his collar once. He asked, 'Uncle, what is this?' He replied, 'It is the sign of orphans. This is the mark of orphans. Go, my son.' Now Qasim went, and he kept fighting, kept battling. It is written in the Maqtal that someone fired an arrow such that when Qasim fell from the horse, he fell in such a way that one of his feet got stuck in the horse's stirrup. It got stuck in such a way that as Qasim hung from the horse, the horse carried him into the midst of the enemies. The enemies began to cut Qasim with their swords. After that, the enemies trampled the body in such a way that they galloped horses from one side to the other. They began to gallop horses over the 13-year-old tender body, over the 13-year-old tender body. In his faint, suppressed voice, Qasim called out, 'O Mother! Uncle, accept my final salaam.' Hussain (a.s.) came to Qasim's body. He came to Qasim's body. But how Hussain (a.s.) brought Qasim's body into the tent, my heart cannot bear to describe. Just listen to one sentence from the Maqtal, just listen to one sentence. Hussain (a.s.) gathered the pieces of Qasim's body in his cloak, 'Wa sa-ya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun', 'Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin'. O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord! Remove the troubles of those who are distressed. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant children to those who are childless, righteous and pious offspring. Grant complete and swift healing to those who are ill. Return those who are far from their homelands safely and soundly. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar (a.s.) are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the scholars of the world and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Whoever protects them, You protect them. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.). Whoever protects that shrine, You protect them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: #9: Kaamyaab Zindagi Aur Kaamyaab Maut | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of a successful life and death through the lens of Ziyarat-e-Arba'een. It highlights Imam Husayn (a.s.) as the ultimate example of success, being the trustee of Allah and a martyr whose greatness is acknowledged by both friends and foes. The speaker emphasizes that true success is defined by Divine validation rather than worldly perception, concluding with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Waliyul-Asr (Master of the Age). Help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. A successful life is the desire of every human being, and every person makes many efforts for this success. It is possible that people of the world, due to their limited vision, might see someone's apparent success and consider them successful. But true success is that which receives validation from the Divine Court. The success of Imam Husayn (a.s.) was that great success whose validation is present in the Ziyarat-e-Arba'een. In this Ziyarat, a believer testifies: 'Ashhadu annaka aminullahi wabnu aminihi, ishta sa'idan wa madayta hamidan wa muttafaqidan mazluman shahidan' (I bear witness that you are the trustee of Allah and the son of His trustee; you lived a life of happiness, you departed in a praiseworthy manner, and you are a deprived and oppressed martyr). 'Amin' means a trustee or one who protects trusts. Imam Reza (a.s.) says, indeed, Muhammad al-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) was Allah's trustee among His creation. After the passing of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), we, the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), became his heirs. Thus, we are His trustees on His earth. Meaning, 'Amin' is the title of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). In Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, the title of Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (a.s.) is also 'Amin'. Similarly, Imam Husayn (a.s.) is also 'Amin', and your sacred essence is so great that both your lovers and your enemies have acknowledged your greatness. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to Imam Husayn (a.s.), 'Welcome, O Abu Abdillah! You are the adornment of the heavens and the earth.' Imam Husayn's (a.s.) killer, the accursed Shimr, himself confesses about him, 'Indeed, he was an unparalleled noble.' And when the announcement of someone's success is present in the Holy Quran, there can be no one more successful in the universe than him. In the 28th verse of Surah Al-Fajr, the Lord of the Worlds announced that He is pleased with Imam Husayn (a.s.), and according to Hadith-e-Kisa, Allah created the heavens and the earth only for the sake of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). But Imam Husayn (a.s.) was deprived of every right in Karbala. Even a basic necessity like water was denied to him. Before his martyrdom, when Imam Husayn (a.s.) asked his enemies, 'Knowing my status and my family, why do you want to kill me?' the reply given to him was, 'We know everything, but we will not leave you until we martyr you while you are thirsty.' O Allah! By the sake of the great martyrdom of Aba Abdillah (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of that son of Imam Husayn (a.s.) who is the trustee of Allah in this universe today—our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)—and grant us the ability to become the trustees of his Wilayah. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. 'Wa a'lamul-huda, wal-'urwatul-wuthqa, wal-hujjatu 'ala ahlid-dunya, fa-ashhadu anni bikum mu'min, wa bi-iyabikum muqin' (And the banner of guidance, and the firmest handle, and the proof over the people of the world, so I bear witness that I am a believer in you, and certain of your return).

title: Aashur ke Din Khushi? | Watch 👆 Full Video | Majlis 05 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the historical and theological significance of Ashura, specifically addressing the misconception that it is a day of celebration. He cites Hadith Qudsi and historical sources to explain that the Umayyad dynasty, including the families of Ziyad and Marwan, celebrated the martyrdom of Imam Husayn. The lecture emphasizes that the tragedy of Karbala is not a matter to be forgotten, as it remains a central point of divine justice and remembrance in Shia tradition.
content:
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has sent curses upon them. Allah, Abu Sufyan, and Ziyad—keep reading. Look, 'al-la'natu 'ala al-ladhina'—meaning, may the curse of Allah be upon them forever and ever. 'Wa yawmun'—and then the Imam [mentions] the Hadith Qudsi, meaning the words of Allah. These are the words of Allah, the Hadith Qudsi: 'Ashura wa yawmun'—this is the day that the family of Ziyad and the family of Marwan celebrate. The family of Marwan, meaning Marwan bin al-Hakam, Abdul Malik, and Marwan—these are the individuals. So why did they celebrate? 'Fahad'—meaning to celebrate the killing of Husayn. They celebrated the killing of Husayn. 'Sal Allah al-la'na ka wa 'adhab'—O Lord, send upon them manifold curses and punishment. And obviously, in other hadiths and supplications, we have this in many places in our Shia culture. This is Shia culture. You will see anywhere, some say, 'No, no, it is very good, it is very good, whatever happened, forget the old matters.' No, no, how can we forget the old matters? When Allah has not forgotten the old matters, why should we forget? Allah repeats the story of Iblis again and again in the Quran.

title: Ep#1: Imamat Ke Baghair Tauheed Naaqis Hai
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of Imamate as an essential component for the perfection of Tawheed (the oneness of God). The speaker emphasizes that faith is only accepted by Allah when it includes the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and the guidance of the Ahlulbayt. By analyzing the 'Golden Chain of Narration' and the metaphorical interpretation of divine attributes, the discourse warns against anthropomorphic misconceptions of the Creator. Ultimately, the lecture establishes the Imam as the 'Wajhullah' or the face of Allah, through whom true monotheism is realized.
content:
Peace be upon you all, and the mercy of Allah. We welcome you all to the first episode of the 'Wali-e-Paimana-e-Ilahi' series. Along with this, we extend our heartfelt congratulations to you all on this auspicious occasion [Eid al-Adha]. Let us offer our congratulations on this Eid al-Adha to the Masumeen (a.s.) and our Imam of the time, Imam-uz-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), with a beautiful Salawat: Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. We hope that you have watched the video regarding the rules and regulations of our 'Wali-e-Paimana-e-Ilahi' series, where you will learn what to expect. Firstly, you must watch all 12 episodes, which are being released daily until July 22nd, along with the quizzes. Secondly, you must participate in the quiz held after every episode and provide the correct answers to all the questions. You must participate and try to provide the correct answers to all the questions as quickly as possible. It is very simple, and if you do this, you will receive a lot of rewards, and along with that, you can win one of these prizes. So, let us begin the first episode of 'Wali-e-Paimana-e-Ilahi', which is on the topic: 'Is Tawheed complete without Imamate?' Many people bring up this hadith, which is from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), that 'La ilaha illallah' is the price of Paradise. This hadith clearly shows that if someone believes in Tawheed, they have paid the price for Paradise. So, how can we say that if someone does not believe in Imamate, their Tawheed will not be accepted? To shed more light on this, we have with us our guest, [Name]. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. First of all, we offer you many congratulations on Eid al-Adha. We also extend our heartfelt congratulations to you on this auspicious occasion. As you saw, today's topic is 'Is Tawheed complete without Imamate?' We want you to explain why we say this, and what proofs or narrations we have to justify this position. Certainly, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. [Arabic recitation]. As you mentioned the hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), many people fall into the misunderstanding that 'La ilaha illallah' is sufficient for entering Paradise. Many people fall into this misunderstanding, and not just others, but sometimes our own people also fall into this trap. Although the hadith presented from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) is not incorrect—it is absolutely correct, and the hadith presented from the book 'Tawheed' by Sheikh Saduq is indeed authentic—that 'La ilaha illallah' is the price of Paradise. On the other hand, in the same book, there are other hadiths that clarify this matter. In this hadith, it says 'La ilaha illallah' is the price of Paradise. Here, the Tawheed being spoken of is the one that is complete in itself, not the incomplete one. And what is complete Tawheed? It is clarified by the hadiths in the same book, such as the famous 'Hadith al-Silsilat al-Dhahab' (The Golden Chain) narrated by Imam Ridha (a.s.). When the Imam was passing through Nishapur, the people requested him to narrate a hadith. He narrated this hadith before them, proving that 'La ilaha illallah' is the fortress of Allah. The Hadith Qudsi states that Allah says: 'La ilaha illallah is My fortress; whoever enters My fortress is safe from My punishment.' He became my beloved, but right there, the responsible person, before moving forward, before moving his ride forward, stopped the matter right there, took the Mahishwar out, and after that, he said, 'Oh, it started, but this is the daily, this La ilaha illallah, there are some conditions in the lizard, and I am one of them.' Imam Reza (a.s.) was stating this, he was explaining that until you are not a follower of my Imamate, until then your Tawheed will not be accepted. This is the condition of La ilaha illallah. Imamate is a bit of a message, it is entrusted to us, it will surely take us to Paradise, but those who are with the next of Imamate, along with it, one thing is found, that those who stopped us, this Islam, they were from the August, but they knew that the senior school is, and if you want the Hakim, then you will get it at this house. This is the reason why they stopped the Khan and said that no clean family, we absolutely state things, absolutely correct. Because when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) narrated this Hadith, we have the entire Hadith-e-Qudsi, but this entire chain was narrated with such a chain. Why did this chain become so special? Because the chain that the Imam narrated, all the people in the entire chain are all Masoom (infallible). It remains in us, the chain first said that my father told me, from his father, from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), from his father, from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), from his father, from Imam Hussain (a.s.), from his father, from Imam Hussain (a.s.), from his father, from Imam Ali (a.s.), from his father, from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Prophet narrated this to Jibraeel, and then Jibraeel brought it from Allah (s.w.t.). This entire chain starts from Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) and ends at Allah (s.w.t.). Because every person in this chain is Masoom, this Hadith is called the 'Hadith-e-Silsilat-uz-Dhahab' (The Golden Chain). And the interesting thing here is that the Hanbali sect, their Imam, Ahmad bin Hanbal, has this sentence in his Musnad, and what is it? He stated it on the occasion of... On the occasion of... this book is, who is it? Asmanon Hanbal, that line, then you are from the narrators, Delhi High Court, that is from the Imam (a.s.). Ahmad bin Hanbal, although he was not from the followers of the Imam (a.s.), despite that, whenever Ahmad bin Hanbal narrated this Hadith from the Prophet, from the Imam (a.s.), he narrated it in such a way. Ahmad bin Hanbal states, 'That my father narrated to me from my ancestors...' So, after this entire chain is narrated, Ahmad bin Hanbal states, and what does he state? He states that if this chain were to be recited over a madman, a crazy person, he would be cured. This is how much he trusts this chain. If he is not, then he is still aware of the greatness of these Imams. When Ahmad bin Hanbal says this, think about how great the status of these Imams must be. Absolutely, if you yourself, Ahmad bin Hanbal, says this about the Silsilat-uz-Dhahab, then it shows what the greatness of these Imams is. After knowing this, we should be more... After knowing this, we should be more loyal, and if someone does not become loyal even after knowing this, then he is foolish. Indeed, and one more thing, this Silsilat-uz-Dhahab is not only in our books, but similar Hadith on this very topic is found in the books of the Sunnis. Al-Haskani is very famous, he has mentioned this in his book 'Shawahid-ut-Tanzil'. And who is the narrator of the Hadith? The narrator of the Hadith is Abdullah bin Umar. I have narrated this entire Hadith in my book in this way. After mentioning the entire chain, he says, 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, Jibraeel said to me, and Allah (s.w.t.) said, what did He say? Oh, my servant, the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib is My fortress. So whoever enters My fortress, he is safe from My punishment.' This Wilayah is the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), which is the strong fortress of Allah. Whoever enters it, whoever holds onto the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), he will find safety, he will go to Paradise. This means that if you want to keep yourself safe from the punishment of Allah, then it is necessary for you to have the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). It is necessary for you to have the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), you must accept the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). And the entire chain after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), one condition of which is that the Imam (a.s.) said that they are Masoom. This is the condition, that whoever has faith, his faith will be accepted only when he has this. Until then, man will not be able to save himself from the fire of Hell. He will not be able to enter the strong fortress of Allah. The Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is the strong rope, this is the strong rope that we have to hold onto. This is the rope that can save you from falling into Hell and take you to Paradise. Indeed, and the book that was referred to, this Ahmad bin Hanbal, people make such accusations against us that we invent things in our books. So come, let's see page 71 of the same book, and an interesting Hadith, what do we get in the explanation of this Silsilat-uz-Dhahab? In that book, the name of the chapter is 'The conditions of La ilaha illallah'. The name of the chapter is to tell that the Tawheed of everyone is not accepted, so whose will be accepted? Let's see, and what are its conditions, let's see, and interestingly in this... Let's see the conditions, and interestingly, we find this here. There is a narration, this incident is mentioned in the book, that one day the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was sitting on the pulpit, and the companions were sitting there. Suddenly a person stood up and said, 'Whoever believes in La ilaha illallah will enter Paradise.' That person said this, and after that, the narration says that two people from the Prophet's companions said, 'We also believe in La ilaha illallah.' They were happy to hear that whoever believes in this will go to Paradise, so they thought we also believe in it, so we will go. But immediately after this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Be silent, do not be proud, and do not rely on the fact that you recite the Kalima of La ilaha illallah.' Why? Because the testimony of La ilaha illallah, this testimony only... This testimony of La ilaha illallah will be accepted only from the one from whom it will be accepted, pointing towards Maula (a.s.), 'It will be accepted from Ali and the Shias of Ali.' It is only Ali and the Shias of Ali from whom the Tawheed will be accepted. And the verse of the Quran, 'Those from whom our Lord has taken a covenant,' this entire series is about the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Now, when those two heard this, they immediately said, 'We believe in La ilaha illallah, but oh Prophet, you also say this, what does this mean? Does our La ilaha illallah not count?' Their meaning was that this is useless. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'But I will explain to you.' First, what did I do? I will answer. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) placed his blessed hand on the head of Ali (a.s.). And after that, he said, 'Listen, this La ilaha illallah, this is the sign of the acceptance of your Tawheed. If you say that you believe in Tawheed, that you have faith in La ilaha illallah, then its sign should be that you should never, ever break the covenant of Ali (a.s.). The knot that is tied, the knot of the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) that you have promised, never break this knot.' Look, the Wilayah that you have promised, do not betray it. The first sign of this is the Hadith of the Golden Chain, never break it. And never dare to sit in the place of Ali (a.s.), on the position of Ali (a.s.). If you sit in the place of Ali (a.s.), then your La ilaha illallah will not be accepted. This is the second thing, the second condition, the second sign. And the third sign, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'Do not ever deny the words of Ali (a.s.), do not forget the words of Ali (a.s.).' This means that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated the first sign, whoever broke the covenant made with Ali (a.s.), the second, whoever dared to sit in the place of Ali (a.s.)... The second, whoever dared to sit in the place of Ali (a.s.), on the position of Ali (a.s.), which is not for them, which is the position of Ali (a.s.). If any person comes and sits in the place of Ali (a.s.), then his La ilaha illallah will not be accepted. And the third and final sign is that do not do what Ali (a.s.) has forbidden, do not do the work that Maula (a.s.) has forbidden. That decision should be accepted only because it is his. If these signs are in someone, then his La ilaha illallah will be accepted, otherwise not. And in this discussion, we also saw that if any person, even if they are the companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), sitting in the company of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), if they believe in Tawheed but do not have Wilayah, then their faith is worth nothing. So, when the companions sitting in the company of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) are like this, then in our time, those who recite La ilaha illallah but do not have Wilayah, what does this mean? This sign that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated means that after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), no one can be the successor except the Imam (a.s.). Except the Imam (a.s.). Whoever has done this, those who have stayed with Ali (a.s.), their Tawheed is complete. And whoever has taken someone else as their leader besides Ali (a.s.), their faith should also be rejected. Because not only did he put someone else in the place of Ali (a.s.), but he also denied the words of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and called his words a lie. And denying the Imamate of Ali (a.s.) proved to be so expensive, that even the Muslims... on one side, such a Tawheed on which they boast so much, and they insist so much on the discussions of Tawheed, if you pick up their books, what is the status of Tawheed in their books? I asked, 'Tell me, what is Tawheed?' The result of denying the Imamate was that the Tawheed they are holding onto, it has become empty of its essence. How far is it from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? It has no trace left. They do not believe in the Imams, they do not believe in the Imams from Ali (a.s.) to Mahdi (a.s.). Now their condition is even worse, that their Tawheed is what? That if the Quran says that Allah has a body, then... If it is said in the Puran that Allah has a body, it means that the body is a gap, it is a veil. If that meeting is absolutely historic, then it means that Allah is the creator of faces. This is not just a matter of two, but it was considered mandatory that He is the creator of the body. Speak up, and I will present this argument before you. I present to you the evidence from Bukhari, who is considered the most authentic among them. The Hadith is present in Bukhari. What is the Hadith? The Hadith states: 'Khalaqallahu Adama 'ala suratihi' (Allah created Hazrat Adam (a.s.) in His own image). Now look at what is written: that Allah created Hazrat Adam (a.s.) in His own image. And they even specified the height, how much it was—30 meters. Is God's height 30 meters? What is the logic behind this? Then it says that the Lord said to Hazrat Adam (a.s.), 'Go and greet the angels.' Greet the angels, who were given the command to prostrate. Now the same person is being told to go and greet the angels. Hazrat Adam (a.s.) is the power of Allah. Yesterday, the angels were prostrating before him; today, Adam (a.s.) is being told to go and greet the angels, and see how the angels respond. According to a Hadith, Adam (a.s.) went and greeted them, and then the angels replied to the greeting, saying, 'Wa alaykumus-salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.' Allah liked this, and that is why the response to the greeting was taught. This is how Adam (a.s.) learned from the angels how to respond to a greeting. Look, this is their Tawheed (monotheism); are they calling this Tawheed? This is Allah's Tawheed. And finally, what is described in this Hadith? It is 'Khalaqallahu Adama 'ala suratihi' (Allah created Adam in His own image). So, all the people who will enter Paradise will be in the image of Adam (a.s.). And from that era until today, the height of 30 meters has been decreasing. From that time until today, the height has been decreasing. Strange. Strange things have been written. The lineage of Adam (a.s.) started with 30 meters, and after that, people's height kept decreasing. They say that until the Day of Judgment, human height will keep decreasing. These are the kinds of things they say. And this is the Tawheed that they have. The result of abandoning the door of Imamate is that their Tawheed has become completely distorted—not just a little, but entirely anthropomorphic. They became believers in a physical body for Allah. And it is not that this Hadith is only found in their books; 'Khalaqallahu Adama 'ala suratihi' is also found in ours. But what is the difference? The interpretation is different. And that is why we are saying, and this is why we are inviting the entire Muslim Ummah to this point. If the religion is to be correct, if the faith is to be correct, then we must refer to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). When this Hadith is mentioned in our books, see how it is found. A person named... it is present in the book of Sheikh Saduq, 'Kitab al-Tawheed'. The Tawheed that we are discussing... Sheikh Saduq, in his book, in Hadith number 18... Hadith number 18, first of all, look at the title. 'Bab al-Nafi 'anillahi al-jismi wal-surah' (Chapter on negating body and image from Allah). It is about the Tawheed of Allah, that Allah has no body and no image. This is the title of the chapter. This is the Tawheed. Now, in this, Hadith number 18 is narrated by the famous scholar, Muhammad ibn Muslim, who narrates from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.). I asked, 'I asked about the narration that Allah created Adam in His own image.' He replied to this. Now look, this makes it absolutely clear that until a person reaches the door of the Imam, he will not attain the correct Tawheed. Here, they believe that Allah created Adam (a.s.) in His own image. And what is the meaning? The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Suratun hiya suratun makhluqah' (It is a created image). We say that this image does not mean that Allah has a face like ours—God forbid, shame on them. It is not like that. This image is one that Allah created; it is one of the many images that Allah created. It is one of the many images that Allah created. Among them, Allah chose one image to create the image of Hazrat Adam (a.s.). This image of Adam (a.s.) that was created is a created image of the Lord. Allah created many images, and from them, He chose one for Adam (a.s.). The image of Adam (a.s.) is an image chosen by Allah. And then, Allah attributed this image to Himself, just as Allah says 'Bayti' (My House) in the Quran. Does this mean Allah lives inside the Kaaba? No, Allah attributed that house to Himself. Similarly, when it is said in the Quran that Allah breathed His 'Ruh' (spirit) into Adam, what is this? This is Allah attributing His creation to Himself. This is Allah's spirit. This is Allah's spirit. What does it mean? Now look, the Imam (a.s.) says that the meaning of creating Adam (a.s.) in His image is that it is a created image, a chosen image of Allah. We have attributed it to ourselves, just as we attribute things to ourselves to honor them. This is not Shirk (polytheism). So, when we say things related to Allah's attributes, like 'Yadullah' (Hand of Allah), 'Wajhullah' (Face of Allah), or 'Aynullah' (Eye of Allah), these are metaphorical. This is an attribution to the Lord. It does not mean that these are actual parts of Allah's body. When we say 'Ali is Wajhullah', it does not mean what is written in their books. Rather, we say 'Ali is Wajhullah' because a face is used when one is facing someone. When I am talking to you, I am looking at your face. Your face becomes the means for me to pay attention to you. Your face helps in directing attention towards you. So, when we say 'Ali is Wajhullah', it means that Ali's name, Ali's remembrance, and Ali's face remind us of Allah. It directs us towards Him. There is no doubt that Allah does not have a face like ours. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'An-nazaru ila wajhi Aliyyin ibadatun' (Looking at the face of Ali is worship), it means that whenever a person looks at Ali's face, he remembers God and remembers Allah. Similarly, in every era, the Imam of the time is the 'Wajhullah'. So, whenever a person turns towards the Imam of his time, it means he is turning towards the Lord. That is the true Tawheed. And this is the Tawheed that we believe in, which has reached us through the Imams (a.s.). If a person does not keep the Imamate, his Tawheed will not be correct, and his worship will be void. Thank you very much for bringing this up. Abandoning the door of the 12 Imams will lead one to a god that has a body, a god that sits, and a god that has a height. If one wants to reach the God that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have introduced, then we must take our Tawheed from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If we go to anyone else, we will never find the true God. And I must also say that if someone wants the correct Tawheed today, they must accept the Imamate of the 12 Imams. If they do not do that, they will have to spend their whole lives searching for their 30-meter god, and they will never find anything. But I tell you, you will never find God that way. In the end, we pray that as long as we live, the love of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) remain in our hearts, and in the hereafter, the intercession of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is granted to us. With this, this episode ends, but before leaving, I want to remind you what you have to do. In the description and comments of the episode, you will see a link that will appear once the episode ends. You have to click on it and participate. So, you do that, and we will prepare for the next episode. God willing, we will meet again tomorrow at the same time, 9:30, Insha'Allah. Watch the next episode until then. Khuda Hafiz.

title: Haqeeqi Mehr-e-Fatimi (s.a.) Kya Tha? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the profound spiritual status of Imam al-Hasan and Imam al-Husayn, emphasizing their equality as vast oceans of knowledge. He transitions to the significance of the dowry (Mehr) of Sayyida Fatimah (s.a.), noting that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared the entire earth as her dowry. The lecture reflects on the spiritual weight of this reality and the disconnect between this divine status and the current state of the world.
content:
Regarding the question about Imam al-Hasan and Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'They are both oceans.' They are both oceans of knowledge. They are both so profound and deep that one cannot be preferred over the other. You cannot say that one has more knowledge than the other. Yes, they both have knowledge, but you cannot say that one is greater than the other. They are both equal. So, when the situation is such, then the one who calls them 'Tashbih' (anthropomorphism) is wrong. Those who give them human attributes are called 'Mushabbiha'. But... They call this an office, but the father of the girl, according to the weather and all these things... Allah has made it strange. Allah is everything. Now, what should the city be like? Who are we? The hatred, the things that are worldly, from the family... now what is the importance? Listen to this: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'O Ali, verily Allah...' Listen carefully, 'Verily Allah has placed the dowry of Fatimah (s.a.) in your hands.' He has made the entire earth the dowry of Fatimah (s.a.). It is in my hands. To say that... but in what state? But in what state? My life, your life... is it going well? On the earth of Fatimah (s.a.), oh, how Fatimah (s.a.) is being treated, and they are enjoying it. The fifth city, the torch, this is the question.
Imam al-Hasan and Imam al-Husayn are both infinite oceans of knowledge.
It is incorrect to prefer one Imam over the other as they are equal.
The term 'Mushabbiha' refers to those who incorrectly attribute human limitations to divine figures.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared the entire earth as the dowry of Sayyida Fatimah (s.a.).
The dowry of Sayyida Fatimah (s.a.) was placed in the hands of Imam Ali (a.s.).
There is a spiritual disconnect between the divine status of the Ahlulbayt and the worldly behavior of people.

title: Muharram Mein Siyaah Libaas, Maatam Aur Tabarruk Kyun? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explains the historical and religious basis for the Shia practices of wearing black clothing and providing food (Tabarruk) during the mourning period of Muharram. The speaker cites classical Islamic texts to demonstrate that these traditions originated from the family of the Prophet (Ahlulbayt) following the martyrdom of Imam Husayn. The talk encourages believers to maintain these practices as a way to honor the legacy of the Master of Martyrs.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Waliyul-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Mahasin', Sheikh al-Ramli (r.a.) in 'Wasa'il al-Shia', and Allama Majlisi (r.a.) in 'Bihar al-Anwar' have recorded that after the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.), the ladies of Bani Hashim wore black and woolen clothes. They never complained of heat or cold. When they mourned, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) would arrange food for them. From this, it becomes clear to us that wearing black clothes and mourning in the grief of Imam Husayn (a.s.) is the tradition of the Bani Hashim family, and arranging Tabarruk and Niaz for mourners in the Azadari of the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) is the Sunnah of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.). Therefore, try to remain in black clothes as much as possible during the days of mourning and participate in the Azadari of Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (a.s.) as much as you can. Allah is the Seer and Knower of intentions.
