title: EP03 | Ghaibat: Ek Imtehaan | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2025 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological significance of the Ghaybah (Occultation) of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as a divine trial rather than a mere absence. It emphasizes that the withdrawal of the Imam is a consequence of the community's negligence and spiritual shortcomings, reflecting the Quranic principle of self-transformation. The session provides guidance on maintaining steadfast faith in the digital age by adhering strictly to the Thaqalayn—the Quran and the Ahlulbayt—while cautioning against the dangers of unverified information.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan, wa qa'idan wa nasiran, wa dalilan wa 'aynan, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an, wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, then subscribe now and do not forget to click the bell icon. The quiz link is live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, then click on the quiz link to register, then on that same quiz link you will... Register, and then on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all questions will be selected for today's episode winners through our computerized lucky draw system at the end of the segment. However, those whose names did not appear among today's winners or if you missed an episode, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner—that is, the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq—will be selected from those who have answered all the questions correctly in all episodes. Meaning, even if someone was not among the daily winners but answered correctly in all episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa sahhil makhrajahum. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Salla Allahu alaika ya Waliyyal Asr, adrikna wala... Rahmanir Rahim. Salla Allahu alaika ya Waliyyal Asr, adrikna wala... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. On behalf of TSR, we welcome you to the third episode of 'Panah-e-Kainat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)' and extend our heartfelt congratulations to you all on this blessed month of Shaban al-Muazzam. Let us first collectively offer our congratulations on the birth anniversary of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Lady of the Worlds (s.a.), and all the Prophets (a.s.) and Imams (a.s.) through a loud Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. And we pray to Allah (s.w.t.) that in this blessed month, He grants us our greatest joy, which is the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Let us begin our episode, the topic of which is 'Ghaybah: A Trial'. Allah (s.w.t.) says in the second and third verses of Surah Al-Ankabut: 'Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? Wa laqad fatanna min qablihim... We have certainly tested those before them, so that Allah may know who is truthful and who is among the liars.' Wa laqad fatanna min qablihim... We have certainly tested those before them, so that Allah may know who is truthful and who is among the liars. In light of these verses, one thing is clear: it is not enough for a person to just say they believe. A person must undergo a test of their faith, and this era of Ghaybah is a period of trial. To discuss the various aspects of this trial and how to remain steadfast, we have with us today Mr. Sajjad Mehar Ali and Mr. Abbas Nahid. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Salla Allahu ala Waliyyil Asr, adrikna wala... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Our topic today, the subject of our discussion, is that the Ghaybah of Imam-e-Asr (a.s.) is a trial. Ghaybah is the wrath of Allah, and God Almighty has chosen the Imams from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) for the guidance of humanity so that people may turn to them and find salvation from misguidance. And this salvation from misguidance... And this salvation from misguidance is the honor of their obedience. Indeed, Allah sent 11 Imams to the Islamic Ummah from whom people could benefit, and could be enlightened by their knowledge and recognition. But it is with great regret that we must say that apart from a few individuals, people did not take advantage of this blessing. However, Allah did not withdraw this blessing from the people until the Ghaybah of the last Imam, Imam Mahdi (a.s.). It is important to understand that if Allah grants something to a person without them being entitled to it or deserving of it, it is His grace (Fadl). And if, after that, Allah withdraws that blessing, it is not an injustice from Allah; it is justice (Adl), because that person was not truly deserving of it. Indeed, it is not obligatory upon Allah to always treat everyone only with grace. It is not obligatory upon Allah to always treat everyone only with grace. Therefore, we find in the supplications of Imam Reza (a.s.): 'Allahumma amilna bi fadlika wa la tuamilna bi adlika.' The translation of this supplication is: 'O Allah, treat us with Your grace, not with Your justice,' because if You treat us with grace, we might succeed, but if You treat us with Divine justice, the situation could be very difficult. Sometimes Allah acts with grace, sometimes with justice, and in both actions, there is wisdom hidden that human intellect cannot grasp. To understand the wisdom of Allah's actions, one must seek the help of the Thaqalayn (the two weighty things), which are the Book of Allah and the Progeny of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). A person cannot understand Allah's wisdom on their own. Indeed, you have drawn people's attention to a very important point, meaning that Ghaybah is a sign of Allah's wrath. And one thing we find is that it is also a universal Sunnah of Allah—that whenever a person is ungrateful for a blessing, if they do not show gratitude... If they do not show gratitude for a blessing, Allah withdraws that blessing. To elaborate on this, we will take the help of two verses along with a narration. As we find in Surah Ar-Ra'd, verse 11: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Innallaha la yughayyiru ma bi qawmin hatta yughayyiru ma bi anfusihim' (Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves). So that is one verse. After this, the withdrawal of blessings is also mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-Anfal, verse 53, where the Lord of Majesty says: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Dhalika bi annallaha lam yaku mughayyiran ni'matan an'amaha ala qawmin hatta yughayyiru ma bi anfusihim' (That is because Allah would not change a favor which He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves). So, if we keep both these verses in mind, the point that emerges is that when Allah's blessing is withdrawn, the reason is the actions of the humans themselves. They have done something. And pointing towards this, I would like to present a Hadith of Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) in which the Imam says: 'Innallaha qada qada'an...' The Imam says: 'Innallaha qada qada'an...' (Indeed, Allah has made a decree). This is a universal decree: 'La yusallimu ala 'abdin ni'matan fa yakhudhuh...' (Allah never withdraws a blessing He has given to a servant unless the servant commits a sin that makes them deserving of that withdrawal). And the Imam (a.s.) further says, quoting the same verse 11 of Surah Ar-Ra'd, explaining it: 'Innallaha la yughayyiru ma bi qawmin hatta yughayyiru ma bi anfusihim.' So, this is a Divine Sunnah. And while Allah's essence is the essence of mercy—as we find in the phrases of supplications: 'Ya man sabaqat rahmatuhu ghadabahu' (O He whose mercy precedes His wrath)—Allah's essence is such that... and the point I wanted to make is that this is why... This is why we find that when a person only intends to do good deeds, those good deeds are recorded. But when a person commits a sin, when a person is involved in a sin, Allah (s.w.t.) delays the recording of those sins so that perhaps the servant might repent and seek forgiveness. This is the essence of Allah. Therefore, Allah (s.w.t.) does not withdraw a blessing from a people until they become ready to be ungrateful for the blessing, do not appreciate it, and disobey Allah. That becomes the cause for Allah to withdraw the blessing from a people. Keeping this in mind, we can say that although the exact reason for the Ghaybah of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is not fully known to us—and according to Hadith, the reason for his Ghaybah will be revealed—one reason that has been stated relates to people's own actions. It is said that the Imam's Ghaybah is a sign of Allah's wrath that has been imposed upon the ungrateful people of the Islamic Ummah. Indeed, let me state one thing: the Imam (a.s.)... Indeed, let me state one thing: the Imam (a.s.) was asked about the reason for this Ghaybah, and he replied, 'Do not ask about things that, if you knew, would make you ashamed.' Allahu Akbar. The presence of the Imam (a.s.) is a great grace and mercy from Allah for the Islamic Ummah, but because of their sins, people were deprived of this blessing, and due to Allah's wrath, Imam Mahdi (a.s.) went into Ghaybah. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Idha ghadiballahu tabaraka wa ta'ala ala khalqihi nahana 'an mujawaratihim' (When Allah is angry with His creation, He removes us, the Ahlulbayt, from among them). This is a Hadith from Usul al-Kafi. Very important. You have drawn our attention to a Hadith that means if we look at it, from Imam Ali (a.s.) to Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.), the presence of all these Imams among the people so that they could directly turn to them and benefit from them was Allah's grace. But the Ghaybah of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is Allah's justice... Justice and people's sins—meaning the actions this Ummah committed after the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) became the reason for Allah (s.w.t.) to convert this grace into justice. And it would certainly be correct to say that in this era of Ghaybah, turning directly to the Imam (a.s.) as the Shia used to do in the time of other Imams (a.s.) is a very difficult stage for us. It is a trial, it is difficult, but it is a deficiency that nothing can fulfill. However, because of this deficiency, we are not permitted to be angry with Allah; rather, this anger is with ourselves, our own negligence, our sins, and those people because of whom Allah (s.w.t.) converted His grace into justice. We also know that Allah (s.w.t.) is testing people through the Ghaybah, and in this test, many individuals who claim to have the recognition of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) will not be successful. As you said, many people will fail in this. In this context, we present to you a Hadith of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) taken from Usul al-Kafi. Imam Musa... It is taken from Usul al-Kafi. Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) says: 'Indeed, the master of this matter of Wilayah and Imamate must necessarily go into an occultation, to the extent that those who claimed to believe in his Imamate will abandon their faith. This is merely a test that Allah (s.w.t.) has ordained for His creation. This test is only for those who believe in the Imamate, while others who have already failed the first test will not be subjected to this trial.' The occultation of the final Divine Guide is intended to separate the steadfast from the weak and those who only claim to have faith outwardly. There is a Hadith from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) that says: 'Listen, by Allah—and this is a Shari'i oath—your Imam will remain in occultation for many years, and you will be tested very severely, Allahu Akbar, to the point that people will say he has passed away, he has been killed, he is no more, he has gone to some valley...' ...he has gone to some valley. Indeed, the eyes of the believers will shed tears for him, and you will be overturned just as a ship is overturned in the waves of the sea.' This Hadith is narrated from Usul al-Kafi. So, now, believers must ensure their faith does not waver. For this reason, we should be grateful to our Imams (a.s.) that they warned us in advance about the occultation and its dangers so that we may succeed in this test. It is not just that the Imams (a.s.) warned us; in the narrations, we find an incident where, due to the hardships the believers would face during the occultation, the Truthful one of the Progeny of Muhammad, Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.), was found weeping. This stage is very difficult. In Kamal al-Din wa Tamam al-Ni'mah, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) narrates this tradition from Sadeer al-Sayrafi, who says that he, Mufaddal ibn Umar, Abu Basir, and Ibn Tayyab... ...Mufaddal ibn Umar, Abu Basir, and Ibn Tayyab went to the presence of our Mawla, Imam Sadiq (a.s.). When the people arrived, Sadeer says that we saw him sitting on the ground, wearing a khaibar cloak over his shoulders, and he was weeping—listen carefully—weeping like a mother weeping over her dead child. Allahu Akbar. The Imam was weeping, and what was his state? Besides that, Sadeer says that the signs of grief and intensity were evident on his face; his complexion had changed, and the area around his blessed eyes was soaked with tears. In this state, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) was addressing Imam Mahdi (a.s.). Sadeer says, and what was he saying? These were the words that Sadeer narrated exactly as they were, for Sadeer says we asked, 'O son of the best of people, O son of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah never make your eyes tearful, what has made you weep? What calamity has made you so sorrowful?' The Imam (a.s.) heaved a deep sigh, a deep sigh the Imam (a.s.) heaved... ...heaved a deep sigh, and the Imam (a.s.) said: 'This morning I reviewed the Book of Jafr.' And the Imams explain what the Book of Jafr is. The Imam says it is the book that contains the knowledge of deaths, calamities, trials, and all past and future events. This Book of Jafr, which Allah has reserved only for Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)—meaning only the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)—and the Imams (a.s.) after him. In this book—the Imam himself is explaining this—I have... here Imam Sadiq (a.s.) uses the special title and epithet of the Imam, saying: 'In this book, I contemplated the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), his occultation, the delay in his reappearance, his long life, and the calamities that will befall the believers of that time. I saw that due to the long duration of his occultation, doubt will arise in the hearts of the believers, and many of them will turn away from their religion. I saw that they will take the rope of Islam off their necks and throw it away—the same rope regarding which Allah says...' Here, the Imam (a.s.) recited verse 13 of Surah Bani Israil: 'Wa kulla insānin alzamnāhu ṭā'irahu fī 'unuqih...' ...recited verse 13: 'Wa kulla insānin alzamnāhu ṭā'irahu fī 'unuqih' (And We have fastened every man's omen to his neck). The Imam explains in the commentary that this means 'Al-Wilayah'—the record of deeds that Allah has fastened to everyone's neck is the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), meaning turning towards the Divine Guides. So, people will distance this Wilayah from themselves. The Imam (a.s.) further says: 'When I saw all this, my heart was filled with sorrow, and grief surrounded me.' We see that the era we are passing through and the difficulties we are facing are not unknown to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), nor were they unconcerned about it. The fact that the Truthful one of the Progeny of Muhammad, Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.), wept over this stage is proof of our love for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This weeping and grief are for those who, during the occultation, will become distant from their Imam, will have lost their Imam, and will fall into doubts and suspicions—doubts that could eventually lead them to apostasy from the religion... ...lead them to apostasy from the religion, exclude them from the religion, and ruin their eternal life. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) weeping over the fitna and severe tests that would come during the occultation—as you mentioned, continuing from that, we see that today, in this era of occultation, how can we save ourselves? It is a very important topic. If there is danger, Allah must have provided some means of protection because He is Just, and justice demands that if there is misguidance, there must also be a means of guidance. As stated before, the greatest danger in the era of the occultation of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the corruption of one's correct belief. Staying steadfast is the most important thing, and for this reason, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have emphasized and stressed the protection of religion and faith. As Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) said: 'Idhā fuqid al-khāmis min wuld al-sābi' fa-Allāh Allāh fī adyānikum lā yuzīlukum 'an dīnikum...' ...the translation of the Hadith of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) is: 'When the fifth descendant of the seventh Imam, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), goes into occultation, then for the sake of Allah, for the sake of Allah, pay great attention to protecting your religion. Be careful that no one leads you away from your religion.' Protecting the religion in the era of occultation is not easy. Just having an intention in the heart does not achieve this goal. Everything has a specific method, and if one does not follow the correct method, one should not expect success. Protecting the religion is also only possible through a specific method. The first point is protecting the nourishment of the soul. One way to protect the religion is for a person to look at the source of the knowledge they acquire—where they obtain it from, which books they study, which influencers they follow on social media, and what things influence them. Until a person is certain that what they are reading, hearing, or watching... ...is correct in terms of belief and thought and will not weaken their faith, they should not go in that direction. One who cannot distinguish between right and wrong should not read every post or article. Indeed, it is not necessary to listen to everyone's words, and it is not necessary to open the door of one's heart to everyone. Just as a person checks if something is pure, impure, or safe before eating it, one should not take their thoughts and beliefs from just anyone. As the Almighty says in the Holy Quran: 'Falyanzuri al-insānu ilā ṭa'āmihi' (Then let mankind look at his food). Surah Abasa, verse 24. This is not limited to physical food; it also includes the nourishment of the soul and the self. When Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) was asked about this verse, specifically the word 'ta'amihi' (his food), the Imam (a.s.) said: 'Ilmuhu alladhī ya'khudhuhu, amman ya'khudhuhu' (His knowledge which he acquires; he should see from whom he is taking it). ...'Ilmuhu alladhī ya'khudhuhu, amman ya'khudhuhu' (His knowledge which he acquires; he should see from whom he is taking it). There is another Hadith: if a person listens to a speaker, and if the speaker is stating the Word of Allah, then the listener is worshipping the Lord. And if the speaker is talking about disbelief and misguidance, then he is worshipping Satan. And our final Prophet, Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), has given us a key for success. There is a Hadith in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Innī tārikun fīkum al-thaqalayn, kitāb Allāh wa 'itratī ahl baytī...' The Messenger of Allah says: 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: one is the Book of Allah, and the other is my Itrah, meaning my Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If you hold fast to them and remain connected to them, you will never, ever go astray, and these two will not separate from each other until they meet me at the Pond of Kawthar.' O Allah... ...until they meet me at the Pond of Kawthar. The Messenger of Allah gave us a key. We must remain cautious regarding our spiritual nourishment, especially regarding our beliefs. The point you made about 'man al-nās' (from whom one takes) is very important for the youth. The elders know these things better. In today's age of social media, ChatGPT, and research, people often find it good to study and research everything. It is good, there is no problem with that, but at the same time, we must keep in mind that in the quest to acquire knowledge and facts, we often start referring to sources that, for example, are adult-oriented or not properly vetted. The youth think they are researching and familiarizing themselves with different ideas, but they do not understand that everything they see and expose themselves to has an effect on them. As you touched upon earlier, if a person has the ability to distinguish between right and wrong, that is a different matter, but if one's own knowledge is not sufficient, then indeed, this is very... If there isn't enough information, it will become very difficult to research, study, and understand things. The result will be that we will gradually put our own faith in danger. In today's age of social media, who can analyze and verify what a person is saying and from what source? This is a very important matter for the youth, and we see that their faith and strong beliefs have turned into doubt. They were in a state of certainty, but began to doubt, and they filled their minds and hearts with so much nonsense that they stopped accepting the truth. Whether or not to accept falsehood is one thing, but they even stand in opposition to the truth. Many times, we see that because they read something on social media, they make it their belief. Therefore, the youth must be very cautious, especially where we can easily access data, but we must also understand whether we can analyze it and distinguish between what is right. As you mentioned, in the light of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, what is the standard, the yardstick, the criteria? It is only and solely... What is the criteria? It is only and solely Thaqalayn, meaning the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—the Quran and the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). There is no one else. No matter what anyone says, this was a very important point that you, Alhamdulillah, brought to the attention of the youth. It is truly surprising how easily one can lose their faith in this era of Ghaybah (Occultation). As indicated in the narrations, a person might be a believer in the morning and leave the faith by evening. We have received these warnings, especially when we are faced with an enemy who never gets tired, never rests, and has sworn to sit on the Straight Path (Sirat al-Mustaqim). As we find in Surah al-A'raf, verse 16, Satan says: 'La-aq'udanna lahum sirataka al-mustaqim' (I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path). Satan will not leave us alone; therefore, we must act upon the Hadith al-Thaqalayn and remain attached to the Thaqalayn so that we can remain steadfast in our religion. I would also like to add that the scholars emphasize that the youth should exercise caution and avoid reading books or articles when they are not sure about the source, the author, their ideology, or the direction in which they are leading you. This is an important matter. This was an important matter that we should be very cautious about. As we are in the end times, the era of Ghaybah, remaining a believer is very difficult and arduous, but not impossible. It is difficult, and the comparison given is that it is like holding a thorny tree with one's hand until the hand is covered in blood; that would be easier than remaining steadfast in faith and belief in the end times. The second example given is that it would be easier to hold a ball of fire in one's hand than to remain a believer and steadfast in religion in the end times. Therefore, there is a Hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that one who holds firmly to his religion during the Ghaybah is like one who holds a thorny tree in his hands. It would be easier to hold a ball of fire than to remain steadfast in religion. In the end, we pray that the True Master, Rabbul Alamin... We pray that the True Master, Rabbul Alamin, grants us the ability to remain steadfast in this era of Ghaybah until our last breath, remaining attached to their hem. May He grant us the ability to remain steadfast on what has been explained. Akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. We are extremely grateful to our brother who spoke beautifully on this topic, and we pray in the court of Allah (s.w.t.) that He keeps us steadfast on Imamate and Wilayah in this era of Ghaybah. Let us conclude this episode with these lines: 'It is the night of Ashura, O friends, do not leave the tent of the Imam.' We take your leave now. Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad. Viewers, the quiz link will be closed as soon as the timer on your screen ends. Now it is time for Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin. You are requested to be attentive for the Ziyarat. The announcement of the winners will be made through our computerized lucky draw system, Insha'Allah. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma... Allah, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad. Salamun ala Yasin. Assalamu alayka ya Da'iyallah wa Rabbaniya Ayatihi. Assalamu alayka ya Baballah wa Dayyana Dinihi. Assalamu alayka ya Khalifatallah wa Nasira Haqqihi. Assalamu alayka ya Hujjatal-lahi wa Dalila Iradatihi. Assalamu alayka ya Taliya Kitabillahi wa Turjumana Zamanihi. Assalamu alayka fi ana'il layli wa atrafin-nahar. Assalamu alayka ya Baqiyyatallahi fi ardihi. Assalamu alayka ya Mithaqallahi alladhi akhadhahu wa wakkadahu. Assalamu alayka ya Wa'dallahi alladhi dhaminahu. Assalamu alayka ayyuhal-Alamul-Mansub wal-Ilmul-Masbub. Assalamu alayka ya Baqiyyatallahi fi ardihi. Assalamu alayka ya Imamal-Ma'mum. title: Maah e Ramazan Ki Aakhri Raat Mein Allah Kis Ki Maghferat Karta Hai? | [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of the final night of Ramadan, drawing on narrations from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq. It highlights how Allah grants forgiveness and salvation from Hellfire to those who fasted throughout the month. The speaker emphasizes the importance of using this spiritual renewal as a fresh start for one's deeds and concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Waliyul-Asr, help us. Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi says that I heard Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) saying: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, Allah the Almighty has certain angels appointed for those who fast, who seek forgiveness for those fasting every day during the blessed month of Ramadan. Until the end of this month, and every night at the time of Iftar, they call out to the fasting ones: O servants of Allah! Glad tidings to you, for surely you remained hungry for a very short time and soon you will be fully satisfied. Congratulations to you, and there are blessings for you. Until the last night of the blessed month of Ramadan arrives, that angel calls out: Glad tidings to you, O servants of Allah!' Allah (s.w.t.) has forgiven your sins and accepted your repentance. Therefore, be mindful of how you will make a new beginning for your deeds now. Meaning, Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) is saying that by the end of the blessed month of Ramadan, Allah (s.w.t.) forgives all the sins of the fasting ones, and we should make a new beginning for our deeds. As for the last night of this blessed month, Imam Ja'far Sadiq (a.s.) says that every night of the blessed month of Ramadan, Allah (s.w.t.) frees many people from the fire of Hell and grants them salvation, except for the person who provides Iftar to a drunkard. When the last night of this month arrives, He frees as many people from the fire of Hell as He had freed throughout the entire month until then. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds: O Lord! By the sake of this blessed month of Ramadan and its blessings, accept our worship and count us among those freed from the fire of Hell. O Allah! By the sake of this last night of the blessed month of Ramadan, after which You have given us the opportunity and command to make a new beginning for our deeds—a new beginning in the reality of our deeds and our entire lives is only possible when You grant the reappearance of Your Wali, Your final Proof, our Imam of the time. Therefore, to grant salvation to this world filled with oppression and tyranny, hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Grant us the ability to live a life of faith under his rule. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

This entire family was involved in the killing of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). To what extent? It is a matter of great sorrow, but it is necessary to mention that whenever the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) would speak, he would interrupt and behave insolently. He would show audacity to the extent that he used inappropriate language in the presence of the entire gathering. Regardless, one time he came to meet the Mawla (a.s.). The Mawla (a.s.) had attained apparent caliphate. We say that he was the rightful caliph, 'Khilafat-e-Bila Fasl'. If anyone is offended by this, let them eat two more rotis; that is their problem, not ours. So, he was a hypocrite. This is our belief: 'Khilafat-e-Bila Fasl'. But when the caliphate came, in this apparent caliphate, he came because, since the passing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he had received special privileges in every government because he was an enemy of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). He received money, so much money. Now, his habits had been spoiled. His habits had been spoiled, so he came with arrogance in his mind, and now... He came with arrogance in his mind and asked the Mawla (a.s.), 'Brother, give me what everyone else gets.' The Mawla (a.s.) said, 'What everyone else gets, you will get.' So he kept coming and bothering him. Then, Ammar (ibn Yasir) came. You know Ammar was a bit hot-tempered; he was young, and his blood was hot. So, he said, 'O Ash'ath, keep your anger to yourself. Do not do this; this anger of yours is not right.' The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) had clearly told him, 'This is not right for you.' But regardless, Ash'ath wanted to meet the Mawla (a.s.), and the Mawla (a.s.) said, 'I will not meet you, go back.' As he turned, he thought, 'This ordinary man is talking to me like this?' He raised his hand and punched Ammar hard. Blood started flowing from Ammar's nose. If Ammar had hit him back, he would have been finished that very day, but Ammar showed patience. But regardless, when the voices were raised, the Mawla (a.s.)... Besides, when he raised his voice, the matter was: what happened? I saw that he said, 'I will not meet with you.' Some of the Maghrib prayer had passed. I told him, 'You have a complaint against these innocents.' Let me explain this to you, Khalid, in a way that you will understand. The Maulana said, 'Today, we treat you so well, that is why you are behaving this way. Because we do not treat you badly, that is why you are acting like this. Remember, after 20 years, or a few years from now, a man will rule over this Kufa who will treat you the same way you treated me today. That man will be from the Bani Umayya, the Bani Thaqif. He will rule over this Kufa. If you had done to his brother or his gatekeeper what you did to me today, he would have treated you the same way.' Then the Maulana used some words that I do not find appropriate to mention here, describing what your condition would become. So, he got scared, thinking that this man is from the Bani Umayya. And he will rule over this. The Maulana said, 'In 75 Hijri, this rule...' He even gave the exact year. And someone who would stop the people... 'He will rule for 20 years.' He saw the exact year later. We are keeping this in a box, but at the same time, he knows what the Maulana is saying is the truth. And he is also being questioned. If he didn't believe it, he would say, 'Brother, say whatever you want, I don't believe any of it.' But he accepted that the Maulana had predicted that this person would rule over the people of Thaqif. Now, let me tell you about this Hajjaj. This Hajjaj was the one who used to sit on the roof of the Kaaba and drink wine. And what did he do to the Kaaba? This was all the doing of the Bani Umayya, not the Bani Hashim. This Hajjaj, the Maulana brought him up, yet Muslims still say, 'May Allah be pleased with him,' because he was one of the commanders. Just as it is written about this Hajjaj, he used to play with monkeys, bears, and wolves; he would keep them and play with them. And all this is written in history books, in the books of Ibn al-Athir, in Al-Kamil. And Ibn al-Athir and Tabari... he was a very great man, and he was not a poet, he would not do that. He had taken a new poet, a very great one of the Umayyads, and in that same book, it is written today... And in that same book, it is written today that he gave orders to kill. He was a disciple of the Umayyads. So, he said, 'Whoever confesses their love for Ali and the progeny of Ali, bring them before me.' He would not even spare women; he would call women and have them killed. So, people saw that there was a man who was a great lover of the son of Hussein. When this... Hajjaj... he had already passed away in 99 Hijri. When Saeed bin Jubayr was brought, when the martyrs were brought, it became known everywhere that wherever there were followers of Ali, they were spies of the Umayyads. So, when it was declared, they were caught and brought. When he saw Saeed, he recognized him and said, 'Come, O Shaqi (wretched one), son of a Shaqi.' He reversed the name, calling the martyr a Shaqi, son of a Shaqi, and a dweller of Hell. And the one who was speaking, the one who was not breaking his silence, he reversed the whole name and said, 'O Shaqi, son of a Shaqi...' The martyr said to him, 'My mother named me Saeed, and she knows better who my father is.' Look at this bravery! People were afraid of the name of Hajjaj. The Maulana had predicted that people would fear his name, and here the martyr stood, answering very calmly. He said, 'I don't have time for useless talk. Seriously, tell me, to the point. What is your opinion about the first and second Caliphs?' The martyr said, 'What is it to me? Let them go to their own business.' He said, 'Tell me, are they in Paradise or Hell?' He replied, 'I have not seen Paradise, nor have I seen Hell. If I go to Paradise, I will see who is there, and if I go to Hell, I will see who is there.' He said, 'And if you go there?' He said, 'If possible, I will look.' Then he said, 'Tell me, among the Caliphs, whom do you like the most?' See how he is trying to extract an answer to justify his actions. He wants a justification so he can give a verdict. He said, 'Whom do you like the most?' He said, 'I like the one whom Allah likes.' The martyr said, 'Now Allah knows, and the one who is inside knows. It is for Allah to decide where the martyr will go.' He said, 'Fine, you are going to be killed, but understand one thing. I will kill you, it is my will.' He said, 'Whether you kill me or not, it is your will, do whatever you want. But remember one thing: the way you kill me, Allah will deal with you in the same way.' And it is written in history that Hajjaj was killed in a very bad, very bad way. The martyr was killed, he became a martyr, but while dying, the martyr said, 'Remember, Hajjaj, whatever you do to me, will be done to you.' Such bravery! He was not affected by the threats. And you should know that Saddam or Hajjaj did not live long after the martyrdom of the martyr. He caught a deadly disease, he prayed for death but could not die, and night after night... He prayed for death but could not die, and night after night he would writhe and scream, 'Woe to me, woe to me, Saeed! Woe to me, Saeed!' Why did I do that? These are the people, these are the personalities, but all these qualities were found in them, which you are discussing repeatedly. These are the personalities. Tomorrow, if Allah gives life and the opportunity, we will mention a woman who, when she found out that someone loved Ali, she would... well, anyway. These personalities were such that they were lovers of Ali, they were immersed in the love of the progeny of Ali. One of their qualities was that they were never busy with the faults of others. They did not look at what others were doing, nor did they spread it. This is from the Quranic verse. And which verse is it? The verse of Surah An-Nur: 'Inna alladhina yuhibbuna an tashia al-fahishatu fi alladhina amanu...' (Indeed, those who like that immorality should be spread among those who have believed...) Those who like that the faults of the believers should be spread, or they like it, they don't spread it, they just like that the matter should spread. For them, there is a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter. The Quran says this. And this is very relevant today because today this has become our habit, so much so... this WhatsApp and all this Facebook, and because of this, good people get involved in it. They don't see what we are spreading, whether it is true or false. They just see it and share it. And the Quran, in Surah Al-Hujurat, forbade it: 'Wala tajassasu' (And do not spy). Do not spy on who is doing what. They are more concerned about others. Now look at the tradition, the Hadith, for you. There is more. The Infallible (a.s.) says, listen to what the Maulana said. The Maulana said, 'You will be leaders...' It is narrated from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that 'Spread the greeting...' (Salam). He says, 'Look at the night and the morning, always speak good things so that you are known for that. Except for goodness, nothing should come from you.' Except for goodness, nothing should come from you. Either it should be a good word, or it should be silence. There should be no lies, no other things. 'Speak only good.' So that you are known for that, that this man never does any evil, this man never says anything wrong. Always speak good things. And after that, he says, 'And always ignore...' (the faults of others). 'Be among the people of goodness.' Some people are like this, this man is good, and he only stays with good people. You will never see him with a bad person. In English, they say, 'You are known by the company you keep.' This English proverb came later. These people became human later; this was 1400 years ago. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Al-mar'u 'ala dini khalilihi' (A person is on the religion of his friend). Then he said, 'Wala takunu...' (And do not be...). What a strange Hadith! When we read it, it feels like we don't do any such thing. Who is the Infallible? 'Wala takunu...' Who is the Infallible? 'Wala takunu...' And 'al-mudh'i' (the broadcaster). title: How to meet Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)?  |  Ayatullah Mohammad Reza Shirazi (r.a.)  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture recounts the story of a man who was blessed with the honor of meeting Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) multiple times. The speaker explains that the man achieved this spiritual station after seeing the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in a dream and asking how to meet the Imam. The Prophet instructed him to lament for Imam Husayn (a.s.) every morning and evening, emphasizing that this sincere practice serves as a key to spiritual connection with the Imam of our time.
content:
He said that there was a man who was among those who were blessed with the honor of seeing Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and it is narrated that he was honored with this many times, not just once. This man was asked: 'How did you reach this station? What was the beginning?' He said: 'One night, I saw the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in a dream, and I asked the Prophet—note the focus in the dream—that I be blessed with seeing Imam Mahdi.' This need was so urgent in his mind that even in the dream, he was asking for this. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'If you want that, then weep for my son Husayn every morning and evening.' It is not something where one just plays a recorded tape of a speaker and weeps morning and evening. In Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, we recite: 'Fa-la-andubannaka sabahan wa masa'an' (So I will surely lament for you morning and evening). He said: 'I performed this act for a period, and then this became the key to the success of seeing Imam Mahdi.'

title: Jo Ziyaarat Ke Sawaab Par E'teraaz Karey [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the skepticism some people express regarding the immense spiritual rewards promised for visiting the holy shrine of Imam Husain (a.s.). The speaker narrates a tradition from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) where the Imam advises his follower to ignore those who deny these rewards. The discourse emphasizes that Allah Himself takes pride in the pilgrims of Imam Husain and has decreed Paradise for those who visit him out of sincere love.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr (Guardian of the Era). Help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husain, and upon Ali ibn al-Husain, and upon the children of Husain, and upon the companions of Husain. Zari al-Muharibi narrates that I complained to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that when I tell my relatives and children about the reward of visiting the holy grave of Imam Husain (a.s.), they call me a liar and say that I am attributing lies to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (a.s.). As if they are saying that there is no such Hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) replied, "O Zari! Leave those people, meaning ignore them. Let them go wherever they wish. By Allah, Allah takes pride and boasts about the pilgrims of Imam Husain, and the angels brought near and the carriers of the Throne welcome them. The Lord of the Worlds says to them, 'Have you not seen the pilgrims of the grave of Husain who have come to his grave out of devotion to him and to Hazrat Fatima bint Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)? Know that by My Honor, Majesty, and Greatness, I have made My grace obligatory upon them and will surely admit them into My Paradise, which I have created for My Awliya (friends), Prophets, and Messengers.'" "O My angels! These are the pilgrims of Husain, who is the beloved of My Messenger Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), and Muhammad is My beloved. So, whoever loves Me must love My beloved, and whoever loves My beloved must love the one whom My beloved loves. And whoever bears enmity towards My beloved has borne enmity towards Me, and whoever bears enmity towards Me, I have the right to subject him to punishment—My severe punishment—and burn him in the fire of My Hell. I shall make Hell his abode and dwelling place. I will punish him with a punishment that I have not inflicted upon anyone in the worlds." We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that He counts us among the pilgrims of Imam Husain (a.s.), and not among those who doubt his pilgrimage or prevent others from it. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. City of Shabak, O Husain; City of Khitama, City of Shabak, O Husain.

title: Imam Ali (a.s.) Kiske Janaaze Mein Shareek Nahin Huey? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical stance of Imam Ali (a.s.) regarding the funerals of certain prominent figures in Medina. The speaker highlights that despite their proximity, Imam Ali (a.s.) deliberately chose not to participate in the funeral processions of those who had previously distanced themselves from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). This act is presented as a reflection of the Imam's unwavering principles and his reaction to the historical events following the Prophet's passing.
content:
I present to you a very famous historical fact: those people with whom Ali (a.s.) is said to have had good relations, as is often proclaimed in history, all died in Medina during Ali's (a.s.) lifetime, living right next to his house. Yet, they did not participate in the funeral of any of them. title: Ghaibat Mein Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Se Tamassuk | ⛅ IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture discusses the prophecy regarding the occultation of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as narrated by Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.). It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and Wilayah during the period of Ghaibat. The speaker highlights the high status and divine rewards promised to those who hold firmly to the Imam's guidance despite the prolonged wait.
content:
Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman says that I asked Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), "Are you the one who will rise with the truth?" The Imam replied, "Indeed, I will rise with the truth, but the one you are speaking of will be my fifth descendant from my lineage, who will fill the world with justice and equity just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. He will have a prolonged occultation, during which many nations will go astray, wondering how anyone can live for such a long time. But there will be some who will remain steadfast. Blessed are those people," the Imam says, "glad tidings, the promise of Paradise is for our Shias who remain steadfast in the occultation of our Mahdi, holding onto our rope, our Wilayah, and disavowing our enemies. They are from us and we are from them. They are pleased that we are their Imams, and we are pleased that they are our Shias. So, Tuba (a tree in Paradise), Tuba is for those people; by Allah, they will be with us at our rank on the Day of Judgment."
Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is the fifth descendant of Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.).

Steadfastness in faith and Wilayah during the occultation is highly rewarded.

Those who remain steadfast during the Ghaibat will attain the rank of the Imams in Paradise.

title: Ep#2: Imamat Ke Baghair Nubuwwat Naaqis, A'maal Radd
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of Imamate and Wilayah as the essential foundation for the acceptance of all religious deeds in Islam. It distinguishes between the outward submission of Islam and the inward conviction of Iman, emphasizing that faith in the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is incomplete without the acceptance of his divinely appointed successors. The discourse highlights that acts of worship, such as prayer and fasting, are only validated through the recognition of the authority of Ali (a.s.) and the Twelve Imams.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. Welcome to the second episode of the 'Seerat' series. I am very pleased to mention that many of you participated in the first episode and provided correct answers. The winner's name has been announced on our social media channels. Let us move on to today's episode, titled: 'Without Belief in Imamate, Deeds are Void.' Yes, if someone does not believe in the Imams, if someone does not accept the Twelve Imams, then their deeds become void. Even if they perform prayers and fasting, all their actions will be rendered useless. To discuss this further, we have with us our brother Abbas Naqvi Sahab. Peace be upon you. We heard the topic that without belief in Imamate, deeds are void. We want you to explain on what basis we say that if someone does not believe in Imamate, even if they are praying and fasting, their prayers and deeds will be void. On the other hand, if someone says 'La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah', isn't that enough to enter Paradise? I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As you have mentioned, the recitation of the Kalima is the foundation of Islam, and the Muslims have accepted the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Muslims have subscribed to the peace and blessings, but if we look at the first letter of a journey, which his mother... the harvest of potatoes, the second Muslim becomes necessary, the insistence on marrying them is the same way, see that subscribe to it, but what should I do? Martyrdom is a guarantee of a new paradise, but no, it is not found anywhere like this. And let us turn to the Holy Quran, that Allah Almighty, in this regard, in the Holy Quran, Surah Baqarah, verse number 66, subscribe to me, remind me tomorrow, O Habib (s.a.w.a.), they come and say that we... Allah Almighty says that people have started to believe that they are 'kullu aslam', but how much can you say? You have brought Islam, you have submitted, so you are Muslims, and with the help of this... have done, so you are Muslims, and with the help of this, Manju Sahu Sharma, why is it like this? Allah Manisha Sharma says, and the whole of the Muslims, therefore, this is because 'iman' has not yet entered your hearts. 'Ya-ya-hani', from this, one thing becomes absolutely clear, that I feel a Muslim is different, 'iman' is different, Islam is different. Salvation is kept for that person who is a 'momin'. The person entitled to salvation will be the one who has complete 'iman'. Here, the Quran has created a difference, so what is the difference between Muslim, Islam, and 'iman'? What is the difference? In Islam and 'iman', undoubtedly, those who subscribe to the channel and those who are only reciting the Kalima Shahadat without understanding, will be called Muslims, but their 'iman' will not be complete without... without listening, it cannot be complete. And this, the glimpse of which we find in the famous saying of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), that no person will love you unless he is a 'momin', and whoever hates you is that... this statement of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) makes this thing absolutely clear that 'iman' is something else and Islam is something else. But here is a question: are these things signs of 'iman'? If a person intentionally abandons his prayers, does not pray, then he is not entitled to be called a 'momin'. Even if a person, without any reason, without any excuse, does not fast, and in the month of Ramadan, eats and drinks without any valid reason, then we cannot call him a 'momin' either. Along with this, if a person, while having wealth, if Hajj is obligatory upon him, still does not perform it, does not pay Zakat, then we do not count such people among the 'momineen'. Like... Like, let us try to gain more knowledge about these things in the light of the guidance of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). This decision... for the names of the people of the village, from the side of the village... if we... they follow their Imam, their ministry, they follow their Imam Mahdi (a.s.). From the traditions of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), the foundation of Islam is what he has stated, its history, forever and ever. The foundation of Islam is five things: the first is prayer, the second is... and subscribe to it. Beyond this, Imam (a.s.) says, meaning when Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) asked, 'Which of these is the most excellent?' Among these five things mentioned, which one is the best? In response, he (a.s.) says, 'Wilayah' is the most excellent, and its explanation is also given by the Imam (a.s.) in this way... The Imam (a.s.) explains it in this way, that 'Wilayah' is the foundation because this is the 'Wilayah' that leads to the others. Meaning, the Imam (a.s.) separates all these things, and in every era, how to perform these, for example, in the issues of travel, we... the issues of travel, this is absolutely true that if a person is traveling, then for him, it is not... but here everyone says that they are following the Sunnah, but their... for example, one thing that is very famous here, the time, the mention of which is found in the Holy Quran, this is... but when a politician, one of the... of the When a politician, one of the... of the, was asked this question, that during travel, if a person does not have water, and this person, the traveler, has to pray the next prayer, then what should he do? Then, without any... he said, 'Brother, do not pray,' whereas in the Sharia and the Sunnah, who is it that will guide in the performance of all these matters? In the era, and no, rather the Imam of the era, whose obedience has been made obligatory upon all people, this is the Imam (a.s.) who, in the first Hadith, mentions it... here a question arises, if we look at these traditions, here along with prayer, fasting, and Zakat, 'Wilayah' is also being mentioned. But these issues of prayer, fasting, and Zakat, are they and 'Wilayah' separate? Is it not that 'Wilayah' is a part of 'Iman' itself? And the principles of this triangle, you asked a very good question, and if we look, this is the main topic of our discussion today, because if we see that what is our duty? Our duty is whatever the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has brought for us, to do all these things. To do all these things from the side of our guide, that if we see that whoever says, 'I am a follower of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.),' then for him, it is necessary to have 'iman' in all those things that the Messenger has brought. In this, it will be mentioned that prayer is obligatory, in the same way, when the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) has... subscribed... subscribed... towards it, it is necessary that this is our... so do we consider this 'Wilayah' of the Imam (a.s.) as a part of it, or should we not pay attention to it? It is necessary for every Muslim that he... the 'Wilayah' of the Imam, and the matter is that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) for his... his 'Iman' until it is completely... Keep your 'Iman' until it is completely... the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), then our... is on it, and in this regard, there are many... here they are found, and here to take support from it, this is his... and subscribe... in this way, in this way, people, and he was always trying in this way that somehow or other, it is found that one day it is found, and some people... what is the name, they will become the owners of their wealth? This is one, this is the second, whose name is... the third is Ibn-e-Abbas, and the fourth was... these four people subscribed, and in this... These four people subscribed, and in this, what should happen next? Subscribe here, please, it is present, so the thing was present upon you, in which two, and the second thing, when it reached the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he said, 'If these four do not give testimony for you, then I will not... your this second thing, it does not happen on the spot, that you... your own... if they give testimony, then the truth is... the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) had already... from the Quran, they had already done it, and not only their own, but their... are... Up to that time and... meaning that mat and that... and the donkey, the 'Niru', one by one, first of all, in the court of Allah Almighty, he testified to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and along with this, the... to testify, first of all, he is the... of the 'Wilayah', he is the... and he is the best among the people after you, he says, 'Whoever makes friends with you, he is with you, and whoever is hostile to you, he is with you, and whoever has enmity with you, he is... and Allah's 'Wilayah' and Allah's pleasure are achieved, and along with this, whoever opposes you, he has opposed Allah, and if your future is more than that, that... If you are concerned about your future, look at the prayer to Allah. In the context of the verses, when the people were tested, despite the denial of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they began to say such things. Then Allah revealed that this youth is the successor of the Messenger of Allah, appointed by Ali (a.s.), and he is his successor, his vizier, created from his light, the fulfiller of his promises, the helper of his friends, and the one who uproots his enemies. That is, the mat (on which the Prophet sat) was testifying, which Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala had gathered—meaning the testimony of Ali (a.s.)—that it was a witness. After that, the mat says, 'I testify to Ali (a.s.) as well, and I am a believer in him, the one whom Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has declared his successor.' And that mat said, 'It is not befitting for anyone...' It is not befitting for anyone to possess the Wilayah—that is, the invitation of the Messenger of Allah and the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.)—to ride upon it. And when the mat threw all the people sitting on it off, it said, 'How can you sit on it when you are not the one who upholds the mountain of Wilayah?' So, when this mat said this, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'If you sit on it, you will be able to bear all these things.' This became the second thing. Regarding the donkey, it threw him off and began to say, 'I will continue to do this until you acknowledge the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his purified family.' So, to save himself from its wrath, he outwardly accepted Islam, but inwardly he was... Outwardly he accepted Islam, but inwardly he was trying to do the same thing. But again and again, it threw him to the ground until Allah gave that donkey the ability to speak and the grace to testify. It testified, 'I testify that there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is His Messenger.' After that, what testimony did it give? It gave the testimony of Wilayah. It says, 'I testify that Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is the one who, if Allah grants someone the status of a martyr, only he can ride upon it who acts upon all the commands of Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.) and acts upon their succession, and who is their friend...' All these things, in any case, are about those who are the leaders of their religion... About those who are the leaders of their religion, those who fulfill their promises. Then it gave the testimony again. If we look here, the discussion was about the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his Prophethood. They were acknowledging the Prophethood, but along with the Messenger of Allah and the Messenger of Allah's (s.a.w.a.) commands, when Allah commands these things, it becomes essential to acknowledge the Imamate of Ali (a.s.). Without this, both are incomplete. Similar examples are found in the Holy Quran regarding the magicians of Pharaoh. When they were in the court, they were magicians, and their eyes were opened. Who were they? They were considering Pharaoh as God, but when Musa (a.s.) and Harun (a.s.) went to the court, what did these people say? They were swearing by the honor of Pharaoh, but when Musa (a.s.) showed them the miracles... And Musa (a.s.) showed them miracles, what did they say? 'We believe in the Lord of Musa and Harun.' This is not just about them; it is about the fact that from the 47th verse of Surah Taha, if we look at how they were in the court, they were swearing by the honor of Pharaoh, but it changed into belief in the Lord of Musa and Harun (a.s.). Here, a question can be asked: 'Are the Lord of Musa and Harun different from the Lord of the worlds?' No, this points towards the fact that their saying 'We believe in the Lord of Musa and Harun'... Their saying 'We believe in the Lord of Musa and Harun' means that faith in any Prophet is not complete until the belief in his successor is also present. In the same way, this verse points out that those who are in the circle of this Wilayah, no matter how many good deeds they perform, will not benefit them. And I am not talking about my own books; our Imams (a.s.) have said that the one who does not accept the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is a dweller of Hell. That is, those who are our enemies, we must keep in mind whether our... We must keep in mind whether our acceptance is a requirement. Whether it is the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) or the belief in the Oneness of God, both become incomplete if a person does not believe in the Imamate of Ali (a.s.). And we have also seen how a mat and a donkey, when the donkey was asked, it spoke, but these things proved the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). It is absolutely proven that it is not complete until one accepts the one who is to sit upon it. And how can we imagine that such a person will enter Paradise who does not believe in the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.)? Finally, it is also proven that a person, no matter... Finally, it is also proven that a person, no matter how many good deeds they do, how many prayers they offer, or how many fasts they keep, if they do it without the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), then all these deeds will be rejected. None will be accepted. With this, this episode ends, but your work is just beginning. That is, you have to click on that link right now and give the correct answers to all the questions of today's quiz. Insha'Allah, we will be present again tomorrow with the next episode. Until then, goodbye, Fi Amanillah.

title: EP05 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ke Mukhtalif Naam Aur Alqaab | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture explores the significance of the various names and titles of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as a means to attain deeper spiritual recognition (Ma'rifat). The speaker discusses several specific titles, such as Ahmad, Al-Ghaib, and Baqiyatullah, citing Quranic verses and Hadith to explain their theological importance. The session emphasizes that understanding these attributes is essential for believers to connect with the Imam and fulfill their religious obligations.
content:
TSR presents. Oh, the desire of the soul in the longing of my gaze, oh, the comfort of my heart. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us. The quiz link is now live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in any hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear among today's winners or if an episode was missed, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from among those who have given correct answers to all questions in 7 out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone did not become a daily winner but has given correct answers in 7 out of 12 episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-hujjatibnil-hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ah, wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafiza, wa qa'idan wa nasira, wa dalilan wa ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'a, wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us and do not destroy us. Respected viewers and lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. First of all, we offer our congratulations to you all on this blessed month and all the births that take place in this month. This is the same month in which happiness upon happiness descended upon the house of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). In this month, such blessed personalities descended who have no equal in the Islamic world. A poet has beautifully said: 'In this, many sultans of the world of possibility descended, many glorious ones descended in the courtyard of Abu Talib. What should I write as an introduction to Shaban al-Muazzam, it is one month but many Qurans descended.' Viewers, today we are here with an important discussion, in which if you look, the effect of a name on people is sometimes more, sometimes less. That is, when a birth happens in someone's house, we try to keep a good name for them. Our intention in keeping a good name is that if we keep a good name, then somewhere or other, the effect of that name might be found in them. We also see that sometimes the effect of that name on them is more, sometimes less. But in the case of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), if they have any title or epithet, it is definitely included in the attributes of the Imam or the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). That is, the name and the attributes/titles by which we have called the Imam are definitely for the Imam. The environment in that era was turbulent. The enemies of the Imams (a.s.) were everywhere. They wanted to cause harm to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in any way possible. So, different titles were used for the names of the Imams (a.s.) at different places. The reason behind these titles they used was so that the enemy would not know why these titles were being used. On this basis, our important topic today is regarding the names and titles of Imam-e-Asr (a.t.f.s.). You all know very well that attaining the Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is obligatory upon every human being. The best way to attain the Ma'rifat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is to have the Ma'rifat of their names and titles. Since these titles and epithets of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are bestowed by Allah, this is the best way through which we can attain the Ma'rifat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Many names and titles of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) have appeared in the Holy Quran, and the Hadith of the Masumeen (a.s.) have also explained this. The book 'An-Najmus Saqib fi Ahwal-e-Imamil Ghaib', authored by Janab Muhaddith-e-Noori (r.a.). In this book, 182 names and titles of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) have been mentioned. The first is Ahmad. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says: 'A person will come from my progeny in the final era who will have two names.' One hidden and the other famous. His hidden name will be Ahmad. Further on, we see in the Hadith that the Imam has mentioned another name, M-H-M-D. In the context of this name, we find a Hadith that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Mahdi is from my progeny. His name is the same as my name. His kunniyat (patronymic) is also the same as my kunniyat.' That is, his name is the same as the name of the Messenger of Allah. Al-Khalaf. This is the third title of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). A famous and well-known Hadith in which Janab Jabir saw near Janab Zahra (s.a.) that after the name of Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), Allah said: 'After that, I will complete this chain of Imamate with his son. The successor (Khalaf) who is a mercy for the world, will have the perfection of Musa, the radiance of Isa, and the patience of Ayyub.' The fourth title we find is Al-Ghaib. In the initial verses of Surah Baqarah and in the context of the 20th verse of Surah Yunus, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'In Surah Baqarah, Ghaib refers to Imam-e-Zamana. He is Hujjat ibn al-Hasan, who is one of the conditions of the Imam, and the Muttaqun (the pious) refers to the Shia of Hazrat Ali (a.s.).' The foundation of any human's faith is the Ma'rifat and obedience of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). In this same context, we see further that another title of the Imam is Ni'mat-e-Zahir (apparent blessing) and Ni'mat-e-Batin (hidden blessing). In the 20th verse of Surah Luqman, Imam Kazim (a.s.) says in the interpretation of this verse: 'Ni'mat-e-Zahir refers to the apparent Imam, and Ni'mat-e-Batin refers to the hidden Imam.' Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the source of all blessings received by Allah's creatures in this era. All blessings emanate from your blessed existence. You are the essence of all blessings, whether these blessings are material or spiritual, such as knowledge and Ma'rifat, intellect, worship, and the ability to obey. In this same context, we turn to the famous title of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), which is Baqiyatullah. In verse 86 of Surah Hud, Allah states: 'Baqiyyatullahi khayrun lakum in kuntum mu'minin'. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) says in the exegesis of this verse that when Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) reappears, he will stand with his back against the House of Kaaba. 313 companions will gather around him. The Imam will begin his address by reciting this very verse, then he will say: 'Ana Baqiyyatullah' (I am the Remnant of Allah). Those who accept his Wilayah will greet him by saying, 'Assalamu alayka ya Baqiyyatullah'. A person asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) if one could greet Imam Mahdi (a.s.) by calling him the 'Commander of the Faithful' (Amir al-Mu'minin). The Imam replied that Allah has reserved this title exclusively for Imam Ali (a.s.). If anyone before or after him is addressed by this title, they are outside the fold of the religion of Islam. The person asked, 'Then how should we greet him?' The Imam replied, 'Say: Assalamu alayka ya Baqiyyatullah.' Then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) recited this verse: 'Baqiyyatullahi khayrun lakum in kuntum mu'minin'. Allah has attributed the Imams (a.s.) to Himself so that people may know that Allah's pleasure and displeasure, obedience and disobedience, are hidden within the essence of the Imams (a.s.). In the books of Rijal, the title 'Al-Asl' (The Origin) is used for Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Apparently, all the Imams (a.s.) are the 'Asl' because the Imams (a.s.) are the original source of all knowledge, all goodness, blessings, and all truths. Whatever blessings or trials reach us, everything comes to us through the Imam of the Time. We turn to the Imams (a.s.) in all matters of this world and the hereafter and seek refuge in them; in fact, even the realm of Malakut and the animals turn to them. In the exegesis of verse 69 of Surah Zumar, the Imam says regarding Allah's statement, 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord', that 'Rabbul-Arz' means the Imam of the earth. Soon, people will become independent of the light of the sun and the moon due to the light of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.). Come, gentlemen, let us move to the last title of this discussion, which is mentioned in the books as 'Amir al-Umara' (Commander of the Commanders). This title, 'Amir al-Umara', is also a title of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) says, while mentioning the era of all the tribulations, wars, restlessness, wandering, and distress, that then the Dajjal will emerge, then the 'Amir al-Umara' will appear, who will be the one to fight the transgressors and the Sultan of those who have hope. In his occultation, intellects will be bewildered and confused, and he will be from the progeny of Husayn (a.s.). So, gentlemen, believers, we have just seen these few titles regarding Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). There are many such titles; as I referred to the book 'Najm al-Thaqib', approximately 182 names and titles have been mentioned. These names and titles are an excellent means to attain the recognition (Ma'rifat) of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), because they are the 'Babul-Allah' (Gateway of Allah). Through them, we can reach Allah. Attaining their recognition is obligatory upon us all. And our final prayer is praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Allah, the Lord of Majesty, has stated in the Holy Quran: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa ma khalaqtul jinna wal insa illa liya'budun.' I have not created the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. Worship does not just mean prayer and fasting. Worship means performing every action for the sake of Allah's pleasure. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) has said: 'The best way to worship Allah is for a person to refine their character and do good to people.' We should lead our lives on the path shown by the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). This is the path to success. Wassalam.
Attaining the Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Imam is an obligatory duty for every believer.
The book 'An-Najmus Saqib' by Muhaddith-e-Noori documents 182 titles of Imam Mahdi.
Titles like 'Ahmad' and 'Al-Ghaib' are rooted in Quranic verses and the traditions of the Masumeen.
The title 'Baqiyatullah' signifies the Imam as the Remnant of Allah on earth.

title: Haqeeqi Kalema-e-Tayyeba Kya Hai? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the Quranic concept of 'Kalima-e-Tayyeba' (the good word) mentioned in Surah Fatir, verse 10. By referencing traditions from Imam Ali al-Rida and Imam Jafar al-Sadiq, the speaker explains that the true 'good word' includes the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). The lecture emphasizes that the acceptance of a believer's righteous deeds by Allah is fundamentally dependent upon their confession and adherence to this Wilayah.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon the Wali of Allah. Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala, in this part of verse 10 of Surah Fatir, mentions: 'To Him ascends the good word.' After reading this verse, a question comes to our mind: what does Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala mean by the 'good word' (Kalima Tayyiba)? So let us turn to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who are the 'People of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Dhikr), whom Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala Himself has commanded us to ask. Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) states: 'The good word is: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, Ali is the Wali of Allah, and the successor of the Messenger of Allah, and the true successor of the successors of Allah.' That is, the good word ascends to Him, and this good word is the statement that there is no god but Allah, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the Messenger of Allah, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is the Wali of Allah and the successor of the Messenger of Allah, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is... Haqq and Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) are the true Caliphs of Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), and they are the Khulafa-e-Khulafa-e-Allah, meaning they are the successors of Allah. Imam Ali ibn Musa ar-Riza (a.s.) states: 'The righteous deed (Amal-e-Saleh) that ascends towards Allah is the knowledge of this Kalima which is in one's heart, for this is the true Kalima that I have confessed with my tongue.' In another tradition, Hazrat Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) states: 'Al-Layna Ahlulbayt, the righteous deed that ascends towards Allah refers to the Wilayah of us, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' And while saying this, the Imam (a.s.) placed his hand on his chest. After that, he further stated: 'Falam tawalana lam yarfa' lahu amalan,' meaning the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Whoever does not possess the Wilayah of us, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Allah will not elevate his deeds,' meaning Allah will not accept any deed from such a person. So, viewers, you have observed that the Kalima Tayyibah refers to 'La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah, Aliun Waliullah'... ...Muhammadur Rasulullah, Aliun Waliullah, after the confession of which Allah accepts all the deeds of a servant. And the servant who does not confess this Kalima Tayyibah, no deed of such a person is elevated in the court of Allah, meaning Allah (Tabaarak wa Ta'ala) does not accept any deed of such a person. So, viewers, you have observed that the Kalima Tayyibah is the condition for the acceptance of deeds, or the reliance for the rejection of deeds, is upon this very Kalima Tayyibah, meaning the Kalima that starts with 'La ilaha illallah' and ends with 'Aliun Waliullah'. We pray to Allah (Tabaarak wa Ta'ala) that He hastens the reappearance of the final link of this Kalima Tayyibah, the final successor and Caliph, Imam Mahdi (atfs), and as long as our existence remains, may He grant us the ability to remain steadfast on this Kalima Tayyibah. Ameen ya Rabbal Alameen.
The 'good word' (Kalima-e-Tayyeba) in Surah Fatir refers to the confession of Tawhid, Prophethood, and Wilayah.
Ahlulbayt are the 'People of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Dhikr) whom believers must consult for understanding.
Imam Ali al-Rida explicitly includes the Wilayah of Imam Ali in the definition of the Kalima.

Without the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, Allah does not elevate or accept a person's deeds.
The acceptance of deeds is contingent upon the confession of 'Aliun Waliullah'.
Steadfastness in this Kalima is essential for a believer's spiritual success.
