title: EP21 | Ayat-e-Tatheer | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi provides a detailed theological and linguistic analysis of Ayat al-Tat'hir (Surah al-Ahzab, 33:33) to define the identity of the Ahlulbayt. By utilizing exclusively Sunni sources such as Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the speaker demonstrates that the Prophet Muhammad specifically identified Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn as the purified members of his household. The lecture further employs grammatical analysis of Quranic shifts in gender and address to argue that the verse serves as a distinct, divinely ordained designation of the Ahlulbayt, separate from the wives of the Prophet.
content:
Presenting the teaser [Music] Laala. Before we begin today's episode, let us see who the winners are from the fifth quiz of this series, i.e., from episode number 17 to episode number 20, and they are being selected through our computerized lucky draw system. And their names are on your screen: Abul Hasan from Azamgarh, Akri Hussain from Alipur, Gadar Haider from Zaidpur, Virani Sakina from Prayagraj, Syeda Manjoom Fatima from Bhavnagar, Syeda Mubeen from Alipur, Arshiya Bano from Mumbai, Wajahat Hussain from Bengaluru, Syeda Fatima Anjum from Bengaluru, Murtaza Chashmawala from Bengaluru, Salman Ali from Mumbai, Syed Hasan from Alipur, Bashira Abbas Ali Bajani from Palitana. Congratulations to all of you. Now let us move towards our today's... ...congratulations. Now let us move towards our today's new episode. [Music] Rahman Rahim. In the series of 'Hujjat' that we have discussed so far in the last 20 episodes, it was: firstly, what is the position of Imamate in Shia beliefs? And after that, the second important question was whether the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appointed anyone as his successor or not. So, in response to this question, the first discussion we brought forward was the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) explicitly announced his successor, about which we have spoken in detail—although we cannot call it detailed, but it is sufficient according to the episode. Now, in that, the attempt... ...according to the episode, it is sufficient. Now, in that, people's attempt is to say that 'No, they say that here Ahlulbayt refers to the wives,' and the wives are also counted among the Thaqalayn. So, today, Insha'Allah, we will first discuss the Ayat al-Tat'hir, and in the light of Ayat al-Tat'hir, Insha'Allah, this matter will also be proven that Ahlulbayt here does not refer to the wives. So, let us see the second status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), meaning through these verses and these traditions, we will prove that the Holy Quran has praised the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Allah has praised them, and has kept them pure and purified in such a way that their [Imamate] is proven by it; otherwise, Allah has not kept anyone else pure and purified. Allah has not announced the Imamate and purity of anyone else; He has only announced the Imamate and purity of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And look, from the beginning until now, all the references given in the 'Hujjat' series are all, without exception, from the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, except for the beginning regarding the Shia belief of Imamate. After that, the arguments regarding whom the Messenger of Allah appointed as his successor, all the proofs were from the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, and not a single reference was from a Shia book. Continuing that sequence, today we will discuss the Ayat al-Tat'hir... ...today we will discuss the Ayat al-Tat'hir, which is a status of the Ahlulbayt and a very great status, a very great greatness. It is the Ayat al-Tat'hir, which the Quran has announced. So, the first reference is Sahih Bukhari, as you know that among the Ahl-e-Sunnah, the most important books among the books of traditions are the six books which are called 'Sihah al-Sittah', and among the Sihah al-Sittah, the most important are the two books, Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. And many scholars of the Ahl-e-Sunnah say that if a tradition is not in Bukhari and Muslim, we will not accept it. This is their belief, this is their method, this is their approach to these things. Therefore, today we are discussing, we are giving the first reference from Bukhari, that in Bukhari, Hadith number 205, in 'Al-Tarikh al-Kabir' and 'Bab al-Kuna', look, the tradition is very clear, it is from Abu Hamra, and Abu Dawood says from Abu Hamra that 'I stayed with the Prophet for nine months. I stayed with the Messenger of Allah for nine months, I remained in his company. Fa kana...' Every morning, every morning, or without any exception, every day morning without exception, 'ya'ti baba'... ...exception, he used to come to the door of Fatima, the Messenger of Allah, Janab-e-Amir, and Hazrat Zahra (s.a.). He would come to the house every morning and say: 'Assalamu Alaikum ya Ahlulbayt,' peace be upon you, O Ahlulbayt. He was addressing whom? Janab-e-Zahra and Hazrat Amir (a.s.), the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.) and Hazrat Amir (a.s.). And after that, he used to recite: 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa Ahlal-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathira.' This is a part of verse number 33 of Surah al-Ahzab. He is emphasizing this part. This is a part of verse number 33 of Surah al-Ahzab. So, when the Prophet used to come, he would only and only call out at the house of Ali and Fatima, and he never went to anyone else's house to do this, nor did he address anyone else as Ahlulbayt, nor did he recite this verse. This is a tradition from Sahih Bukhari, which I have presented for your service. So, this is the first point, keep this in mind. The second tradition is from Sahih Muslim, and this is in 'Kitab Fada'il al-Sahaba', 'Bab Fada'il Ahlulbayt', and it is in the seventh volume, and the page number is 130, Hadith number 2424. Okay, now in this, the tradition that has been narrated, this tradition is 'Qala Aisha'. Aisha has narrated this tradition that 'Kharaja al-Nabiyyu ghadatan', the Prophet went out in the morning, okay, and he went out in the morning, 'wa 'alayhi mir'atun murakkabun min sha'rin aswad', and he was wearing a black cloak. Listen very carefully to this Hadith, it is a tradition of Sahih Muslim, not a tradition of a Shia book. The name of the narrator is Aisha, okay, and she says that 'Kharaja al-Nabiyyu ghadatan wa 'alayhi mir'atun murakkabun min sha'rin aswad', the Prophet had a black blanket or a black cloak, and then after that, 'Faja'a al-Hasan', Imam Hasan arrived, 'Fadakhala ma'ahu', the Prophet included Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) in that blanket. 'Summa ja'a al-Husayn', then Imam... ...included, 'Summa ja'a al-Husayn', then Imam Husayn (a.s.) came and he also entered into this Rida, into this blanket. 'Summa ja'at Fatima', then Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.)—there is no 'salamullah alayha' there because it is Janab-e-Zahra, so 'salamullah alayha' is not there—'Faja'a... Summa ja'at Fatima', so the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) also included Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) in this, in this Kisa, he included her. 'Summa ja'a Ali', then he also included him. Then after that, the Prophet said: 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa Ahlal-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathira', and then he recited this verse, which makes it clear that the Prophet's Ahlulbayt are only these. The Prophet did not take anyone else in this Kisa, in this blanket, he did not take anyone else, even the one who narrated the Hadith, she was not taken either, no one was taken, only these, and... ...no one was taken, only these, and for them, the Prophet recited this verse, which proves that the Ahlulbayt are only these. Now, if you want to prove the matter further, then look, I am giving the reference of the third book of the Sihah al-Sittah. I will not take much of your time, just briefly presenting the Hadith for your service. This is 'Sunan al-Kubra' of Nasa'i, this book is very important after Bukhari and Muslim. 'Al-Sunan al-Kubra', it contains 'Kitab al-Khasa'is', 'Dhikr Manzil Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)', Volume 7, page number 410, Hadith number 8342. Okay, now pay close attention to this Hadith. Who is the narrator of this Hadith? Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Amir, the son of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Okay, let me also mention this for your service so that you know that according to the Ahl-e-Sunnah, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas—remember, this is the belief of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, not the Shia belief—yes, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is among those individuals who are called 'Ashara Mubashara' by them, meaning those 10 individuals whom the Prophet [promised] Paradise. He did not take anyone else, only these few, and for them, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited this verse, which proves that the Ahlulbayt are only these. Now, if you want to further prove this point, look at the reference from the third book of the Sihah al-Sittah. I will not take much of your time; I will briefly present this hadith to you. This hadith is from Sunan al-Kubra, which is a book by al-Nasa'i, and after Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, it is a very important book. In Sunan al-Kubra, there is Kitab al-Khasa'is, mentioning the status of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), Volume 7, page 410, hadith number 8342. Now, pay close attention to this hadith. Who is the narrator of this hadith? Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, the son of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Furthermore, let me mention this to you so that you know that according to the Ahl al-Sunnah—remember, this is the belief of the Ahl al-Sunnah, not the Shia belief—Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is among those individuals who are referred to as 'Ashara Mubashara' (the ten promised paradise), meaning those ten individuals whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) promised Paradise. The 10 individuals whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave the glad tidings of Paradise—those whom the Prophet called the 'Ashara' or the ten, the ten who were given the glad tidings—these are the 10 individuals, correct? Now listen, I am giving you the reference for the book. Look, Sunan al-Nasa'i. Now look, the tradition has been worded very carefully so that the honor of the people remains protected. Muawiya ordered Sa'd, or Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Who is the narrator? The son of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, or Amir, Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. He ordered—who ordered? Muawiya ordered whom? Sa'd. It is not written what he ordered, but what is known from the tradition is that Sa'd refused to obey the order. So, Muawiya questioned him, 'Ma mana'aka an tasubba Aba Turab?' (What prevents you from cursing Ali ibn Abi Talib?) He asked, 'Sa'd, what thing stops you from speaking ill of and cursing Ali?' So, it reached the point where Muawiya gave an order to a high-ranking companion to... to curse Ali, to speak ill of Ali, to use abusive language. Look, this is a tradition from al-Nasa'i, not from a Shia book, okay? And those who justify it by saying, 'No, they were just having a disagreement,' look, truth is truth and falsehood is falsehood. Never try to justify falsehood. Call what is right, right, and what is false, false. If we start explaining away everything, if we justify everything, then there will be no criminal left in the world; all courts will have to be closed. Not just the world's courts, but the accounting of the Hereafter will also have to be shut down. We would have to abolish the Day of Judgment, because whoever comes will justify their actions. If someone killed their brother, and if Allah asks, 'Why did you kill?', they would say, 'We were brothers, we killed each other, what is the problem?' They would present the same argument to Allah. Therefore, making such arguments is against reason, against the Sharia, and against religion. Call what is right, right, and what is wrong, wrong, no matter who does it, no matter who it is. So Muawiya asked, 'Ma mana'aka an tasubba Aba Turab?' (What was the thing that was stopping you from cursing Abu Turab?) He said, 'Amma ma dhakartu thalathan...' (As for what you mentioned, three things...) As for what you mentioned, three things that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), because of those three things, I will never curse Ali. That is, I will not obey your order. Why? Sa'd says, 'If I possessed even one of these three things, it would be better for me than having the most expensive camels.' These were the 'Humr al-Na'am' (red camels). Now he explains what he heard from the Messenger of Allah and why he is not speaking ill of Ali. He says, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)...'—in some versions it says, 'when the Messenger of Allah left him in some of his battles...' when the Messenger of Allah left him in some of his battles, he left the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) in Medina. Now look here, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says 'some battles,' but it is an incident from one battle, and that is the Battle of Tabuk. This is an incident from one battle, but he says 'some battles.' So Ali (a.s.) asked the Prophet, 'O Messenger of Allah, are you leaving me behind with the women and children?' This is the Hadith al-Manzila, which will be discussed in the topic of Hadith al-Manzila, God willing. You left me behind for the women and children because the hypocrites were spreading propaganda in Medina that the Messenger of Allah left Ali behind for the women and children and did not take him to battle, or that the Messenger of Allah did not trust Ali. This was the propaganda of the hypocrites. Whereas, why did the Prophet leave him? Because the Prophet said, 'Ali, in Medina, either I should stay or you should stay. One of the two must remain.' So when this happened, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) asked this question, and the Prophet replied, 'Ama tarda an takuna minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di?' (Are you not pleased that you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me?) This is the Hadith al-Manzila. except that there is no prophet after me. You are my successor after me. The Prophet clearly stated this virtue. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas considered it a virtue that was better than red camels. God willing, when the details of the battle come, we will discuss that incident. What was the second virtue? 'Wa sami'tu yawma Khaybar...' Sa'd says, on the day of Khaybar, I heard the Prophet say, 'Tomorrow I will give this banner, this flag, to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him.' Sa'd says, 'We all stretched our necks, looking up like this, hoping that perhaps we might receive the banner, that perhaps the Prophet meant us.' But the Prophet did not look at anyone, rather he said, 'Call Ali, bring Ali to me.' So Ali (a.s.) came, and his eyes were inflamed; he had red eyes. His eyes were inflamed. So the Prophet took some saliva and applied it to the eyes of Ali (a.s.). By applying this blessed saliva, he was immediately cured. Look, this is a tradition of al-Nasa'i, this is a tradition of al-Nasa'i. And he gave the banner to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and after that, this became the second virtue. Now, what is the third virtue? Sa'd says the third virtue is: 'When this verse was revealed...' Which verse? Surah al-Ahzab, verse number 33: 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa ahlal-bayti wa yutahhirukum tathira.' (Allah only intends to keep away from you, O Ahl al-Bayt, all impurity and to purify you with a thorough purification.) That is, from every kind of evil, whether it is Takwini (existential) or Tashri'i (legislative), the Ahl al-Bayt are pure and purified. So Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says this was a virtue... So Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says this was a virtue for the Ahl al-Bayt, this was the status and virtue of Ali (a.s.). Now here, Sa'd says when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) invited—look, this is a tradition of al-Nasa'i—the Prophet called Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn. There is no one else's name. There is no one else's name. The Prophet only called these four individuals, that's it. He invited them and said, 'Allahumma ha'ula'i ahli...' (O Allah, these are my family, these are my Ahl al-Bayt.) It is completely clear; what could be clearer than this? Can there be anything clearer? So he presented three instances in the service of the Prophet, from which the meaning is only the Ahl al-Bayt—only and only the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), Lady Zahra, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba, and Imam Husayn (a.s.). Because Fatima is 'Abaha wa Banuha' (her father and her sons), God willing, that is a separate discussion. So this is according to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and similarly... According to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and similarly, there is another tradition in 'Al-Sunan al-Kubra', whose number is in the same chapter, or it is volume 7, page 417. Remember, there are two Sunans of al-Nasa'i: 'Sunan al-Sughra' and 'Sunan al-Kubra', okay? And in that too, the same thing, a similar hadith has come, and in it, what he narrated is that the Prophet said, 'Ha'ula'i Ahlu Bayti wa 'Itrati.' (These are my Ahl al-Bayt and my progeny.) That's it. So now, all these things that come up—what is meant by Ahl al-Bayt and what is the proof for it—they bring up this same verse 33 of Surah al-Ahzab. What is verse 33 of Surah al-Ahzab? Now pay attention to that. Look, those who know even a little bit of Arabic grammar—and if they don't know Arabic grammar, I will explain it by translating it—they use this and say that Ahl al-Bayt and the wives are the same. No, look, the verse starts from the beginning, and there are other verses that are about the wives. After that, the discussion of the wives continues in verse 33. Allah is commanding the wives of the Prophet: 'Wa qarna fi buyutikunna wa la tabarrajna tabarrujal-jahiliyyati al-ula...' (And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance...) and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance. This is a verse of the Quran, not a hadith where we would debate its chain of narration. And who is being addressed? The wives of the Prophet. 'Wa aqimnas-salata wa atinaz-zakata wa ati'nallaha wa rasulahu...' (And establish prayer and give zakat and obey Allah and His Messenger.) Do not disobey Allah and His Messenger. Now here, those who know Arabic grammar understand well that every pronoun used here is feminine. It is feminine. There is not a single masculine one. 'Qarna' is feminine, 'Buyutikunna'—'kunna' is feminine. 'Stay in your houses,' okay? 'Tabarrajna' is feminine, 'Aqimna' is feminine. Everything is feminine, nothing is masculine. The address is only for women. 'Atina'—this is also an address to women. This is not an address for men... This is also an address to women; in Arabic, it is not an address for men, only for women. 'Atina'—this is also for women, this is also feminine. Up until here, all the addresses in the previous verses are only feminine, for women, that's it. Now, after that, the address changes. Allah says, 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumur-rijsa...' Now 'kum' is for men, or if there are men and women where men are in the majority, then 'kum' is used for them. 'Your'—this is masculine, this is for men, or for both men and women if men are in the majority. Look, I am emphasizing this: 'Wa yutahhirukum tathira.' (And purify you with a thorough purification.) Here, there is not a single feminine pronoun. So, if someone asks, then why was this verse, this piece, placed among the verses of the women or the wives? So this is another question that will be addressed when the compilation of the Quran is discussed, and only this verse... There will be a debate on the gathering, and this is not the only verse; there are many such verses that, if you ponder upon them, you will wonder why they were placed here. Regardless, this has now become an argument. Look at the second argument: what do they say when the angels came? The second argument is Surah Hud, verse 73. They say that when the angels came to Hazrat Sarah (a.s.) and Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.), they said that you would have a son. Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) was 96 years old at that time, and Janabe Sarah (a.s.) was 92. Now, at this age, the glad tidings are being given. Janabe Sarah (a.s.) heard this and began to laugh—as the Quran says—and said, 'A'ajuzun (an old woman)? I have become an old woman.' 'A'ajuz' refers to a woman who has lost hope of childbirth. 'How can there be childbirth at this age? And my husband is an old man.' So the angels said, 'Ata'jabina min amrillah?' Now, ponder again. They bring this argument to prove that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are not mentioned here. But what is written here? 'Ata'jabina min amrillah?' The address is only to Janabe Sarah (a.s.). The address is to Janabe Sarah (a.s.). 'Do you wonder at Allah's mercy, at Allah's command?' Do you have doubts about Allah? The address is only to Janabe Sarah (a.s.). But after that, the Quran's address changes. Look, 'Ata'jabina' is a verse of reproach; it is a rebuke. If someone does not trust your word, you ask them, 'Do you not trust my word?' This is the tone of the address. Now, the next sentence is, 'Rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu alaikum ahlal-bayti.' 'The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O Ahlulbayt.' Now, 'alaikum' (plural) has come. There, it was 'ta'jabina', which was the feminine singular form. Here, 'alaikum' has come, which is the masculine plural form. This means there are other people as well. In Arabic, if there were only two, it should have been 'alaikuma ahlal-bayti'. There were no other individuals; there were no children, only those two. 'Alaikuma ahlal-bayti'—there was no one besides Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) and Janabe Sarah (a.s.). But 'alaikum' indicates that there is someone else, or the address here is to someone else, and its connection... The address here is to someone else, and it has no connection to this part. That is why Imam Sadiq (a.s.) brings it into our Shia hadith so that the matter becomes clear. The Imam (a.s.) says that the Quran—every verse of the Quran—the first part is about one thing, the middle part is about something else, and the last part is about something else. And it is 'kalam muttasil' (connected speech). This is a separate debate, Insha'Allah, regarding the compilation of the Quran. So, this is Surah Hud; this verse was regarding the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir). Although the debate on the Verse of Purification is very detailed, just to prove the status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and to prove their excellence—if someone does not accept it even after this, then it is their problem. So look here, there is a verse in Surah Yusuf, verse 29. The address is to Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.). Allah says, 'Yusufu a'rid 'an hadha'—'O Yusuf, turn away from this,' from these women. 'Wastaghfiri li-dhanbiki'—turn away from Yusuf (a.s.). Now, this is one verse, verse 29, and in it... And 'wastaghfiri'—'istaghfiri' is the feminine form. The address is to a woman, to one woman. 'You ask for forgiveness for your sin.' So you might say the address is to Hazrat Yusuf (a.s.), and immediately after that, to a woman in the same verse? This means the address is to two different people. So, if there are two different addresses in one verse, is there anything surprising about that? There is nothing surprising. But someone might say, 'No, when Allah says it is an address to Yusuf, then the woman mentioned must also be Yusuf.' Can anyone say that? This would be an insult to the Prophet; it is an insult to the status of the Prophet. And it says, 'Wastaghfiri'—'O woman, ask for forgiveness for your sin, for you are among the sinners.' 'Innaki kunti min al-khati'in.' 'Innaki'—'kunti'—this is for the woman. So, this is for Yusuf (a.s.). There are two addresses in one verse. Why? How did you decide that this part is for Yusuf and that part is for Zuleikha? How did you decide that this part is for Yusuf and that part is for Zuleikha? You said it is the pronoun. Look, the address here is to Yusuf, and there it is Zuleikha because it is the feminine form. So, the matter is understood here, but the matter regarding the Verse of Purification is not understood? It is quite clear that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are only those individuals whom Allah has chosen. And that is why in Hadith al-Thaqalayn, 'Iti Ahlulbayti' refers only to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and his infallible descendants. Besides them, there is no one else. Wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi al-tahirin.

title: Shakeel Ahmed Salafi Ki Mazammat | Maulana Zeeshan Haider Zaidi
excerpt: Maulana Zeeshan Haider Zaidi strongly condemns the derogatory language and anti-Islamic rhetoric used by individuals like Waseem Rizvi (Waseem Tyagi) and Shakeel Ahmed Salafi. The speaker emphasizes that such individuals have been declared outside the fold of Islam by Shia scholars due to their criminal behavior and insults against the Ahlulbayt and the Quran. He urges the Shia community to remain vigilant, avoid being influenced by these figures, and maintain the dignity of their faith through proper knowledge and character.
content:
There are many things that are a matter of shame. On one hand, there is a person named Waseem Rizvi who calls himself a scholar. You might feel angry, but he is not just ignorant; he is worse than that. He has a way of speaking that is completely unacceptable. He has said something that is absolutely shameful. We should be very concerned that Waseem, who has said such things, has long been declared outside the fold of Islam by all our Shia scholars, and he has been declared a criminal. He should have known this, and he has said many things... There is a lot of hatred in his heart. It is surprising that there are people who love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and can be influenced by such people. The Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.), whose hadith and family and the waiting for the savior of the entire world [music]—people are waiting for him. They will do this with a new knowledge and awareness. And his arrival in the world is a reality. We see the life that we are waiting for, for which we say, 'Ask us where he is.' Just understand where he is not. Understand where he is not; your own eyes are the veil. He is not hidden. We believe that he is watching us and is present. But why did this arise? The responsibility of this preparation... he used very low language, language that even a common person would not use. In this regard, the level he is stooping to, and the things he is starting, which are not even appropriate for a common person—let alone someone who claims to be a scholar of Islam—can he use such language? We strongly condemn this. And one should understand that this is not just about one person. Sometimes, out of enmity for someone, you abandon good things. You are a follower of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and you are comparing Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) to him? This is wrong. This is a wrong thing. You should listen first, then become very firm, and then if you have said it, it is fine. And then, on that, there are books showing that in such and such place, when he said this wrong thing, after that, he is a criminal. You are not going to him; he is a criminal, and a criminal cannot be a Muslim. The Quran says that a criminal cannot be a Muslim. Therefore, he is not a Muslim, and he who uses such language for his own Imam is... For him, may God... On one hand, to call that person a Muslim... if he acts like a criminal, he is truly not a Muslim, and we strongly condemn him. And there are two days of talk with him. And where is Waseem Rizvi, who has now become Waseem Tyagi? If you target them, you are targeting them, but we have already declared them criminals. We do not like to talk about them. We will also condemn those who do this. Whoever does this will not become a Muslim; he cannot even be a human, let alone a Muslim. And their supporters—what will their supporters do? They will also insult the Quran. They are the supporters of Hussain (a.s.). The one who is a follower of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who changes before the recitation of the Quran... we are disgusted with the one who has said this nonsense before, and we are disgusted with Waseem Tyagi. And those who target him while targeting the Shia—we are disgusted with them too. And we love his (the Imam's) discourse and his actions, and we want to fight for him again. If you are a Muslim, then first study those books in which the faith is mentioned... And we use it. You also see in your character that you have done it many times. Using inappropriate language for them is equivalent to being outside the fold of Islam.

title: Darwaaza Jalaaya Ya Sirf Dhamki Di - Sach Kya Hai? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture examines historical accounts from Sunni sources regarding the events at the house of Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) following the passing of the Prophet. The speaker analyzes narrations from Tarikh al-Tabari and Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah to discuss the threats made by Umar ibn al-Khattab to set the house on fire. The lecture argues that the historical evidence supports the occurrence of these events, challenging those who deny the burning of the door.
content:
So, in Tarikh al-Tabari, volume 3, page 202, it is written that Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the house of Ali (a.s.), and at that time, Talha, Zubayr, and some individuals from the Muhajireen were present in that house. He said, 'By God, I will set you all on fire unless you come out of the house for the Bay'ah (allegiance).' This is one point. Before moving to the second hadith, it is necessary to know the status of this author, Ibn Abi Shaybah, in the eyes of the scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah. Let us inform our viewers that this Ibn Abi Shaybah was a teacher of Bukhari. His book is 'Al-Musannaf', and on page 432 of volume 7 of that book, this hadith is found. And in this hadith—let me clarify this for them as well—in this hadith on page 432 of volume 7 of Al-Musannaf, all the narrators mentioned can be proven reliable through the books of Ahl al-Sunnah themselves. But since there is no room in this short time, we will not go into that debate right now. We will come straight to the hadith. What is written in the hadith? What is written in the hadith? After the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), when people gave Bay'ah to Abu Bakr, Ali (a.s.) and Zubayr came to Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) and consulted with her, and they did not give Bay'ah. They did not give Bay'ah. When the news reached Umar ibn al-Khattab, what happened? He came to the house of Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) and after that, this sentence of Umar ibn al-Khattab: 'By God, if there is anyone we love the most, it is your father. We do not love anyone as much as we love your father.' This is very good, but then what is the sentence of Umar ibn al-Khattab after this? 'By God...' By God, because you have gathered these people in your house, you have forbidden them from coming out, and people are gathered in your house, I order—by God, the sentence is—I order that all of them be set on fire in this house. First, there is an expression of love, and immediately after that, this sentence, because you have given shelter in your house to those who refused to give Bay'ah, I am setting the house on fire. I am ordering the house to be set on fire. They are ordering it to be set on fire. In Tarikh al-Tabari and Al-Musannaf, both books I have cited so far, it is absolutely clear and evident from both books that Umar ibn al-Khattab threatened to set the house of Ali (a.s.) on fire and also gave the order. Whose house is being threatened to be set on fire? This is the house where the family of the Risalat (Prophethood) lives. This is the house where Ali and Fatimah (s.a.) live. This is the house where Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (a.s.) live. It is being talked about setting fire to the place where the family of the Risalat lives. On one hand, love, and on the other hand, talk of setting the house on fire. What kind of love is this? You know, in Sahih Bukhari, Aisha bint Abu Bakr... What kind of love is this? You know, in Sahih Bukhari, it is narrated from Aisha bint Abu Bakr that after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), as long as Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) remained in this world, Ali (a.s.) did not give Bay'ah to anyone. In this situation, if someone says that the door was not set on fire, then two conclusions can be drawn from Sahih Bukhari: either one has to accept that Umar ibn al-Khattab swore a false oath by God and ordered the house to be burned and then went back on his word, or one has to accept that the hadith narrated from Aisha bint Abu Bakr in Bukhari is false, that Aisha lied, or that Bukhari wrote a false hadith. Either one has to accept this, and if both these situations are not possible, then only one situation remains, and that is that not only was the order given to burn the door and the threat made to burn the door, but that door was actually burned and the Bay'ah was taken by force.

The occultation of Hazrat Imam-e-Asr (a.t.f.s.). Regarding this occultation, although many things have been stated in the traditions. The conditions of the occultation have been described. The trials of the occultation have been described. It has been described how people will go astray during the occultation. How people will be afflicted with bewilderment, distress, and wandering. All these things have been pointed out. But if someone tries to find out what the wisdom behind the occultation is? What is the reason for the occultation? What is its real reason, its true reason? Then the traditions are silent about it. Although some hints have been given, the real reason for the occultation has not been stated. In this regard, there is a tradition. Abdullah ibn Fazl al-Hashimi, it is narrated from him that I heard the sixth Imam, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), saying this, that the Imam says, 'Inna li-sahibi hadhal amr.' That is, for the Imam-e-Asr, the Master of the Affair, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), there will be an occultation, 'Ghaybatun, la-budda minha yartabu fiha kullu mubtilin.' In which everyone, that is, every person who is on falsehood, who is on invalidity, that is, who is on a false belief, will definitely be afflicted with doubt. This will be such an occultation. 'Faqultu', I asked. Abdullah ibn Fazl al-Hashimi asks, 'I said, Walima ju'iltu fidak? Mawla, why will this happen?' Imam (a.s.) says, 'Li-amrin lam yu'dhan lana fi kashfihi lakum.' It is such an affair that we have not been given permission to reveal its real reason to you. That is, the Imam (a.s.) clarified in these words that we do not have permission from Allah yet to explain the real reason for the occultation to you. Abdullah ibn Fazl al-Hashimi then asks, 'Fama wajhul hikmati fi ghaybatihi?' Then what is the wisdom behind his occultation, Mawla? Imam says, 'Wajhul hikmati', that is, when will it be known, when will its reality be known? When will it be clear to us why there is an occultation? Imam (a.s.) says, 'Wajhul hikmati fi ghaybatihi, wajhul hikmati fi ghaybati man taqaddamahu min hujajillahi ta'ala dhikru.' That is, the wisdom of this occultation is exactly the same as the occultation of the Prophets (a.s.) who preceded him. The Hujjatullah, the proofs of Allah, their occultation, the wisdom behind it was exactly the same. And what was that? 'La yankashifu illa ba'da zuhurihi.' And the wisdom of this occultation will not be revealed until the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.). Just like, now this is an interesting point, just like until the separation between Janab-e-Khizr (a.s.) and Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) did not happen, the actions that Janab-e-Khizr (a.s.) performed, that is, he made a hole in the boat, killed the child, or repaired the wall, he did not reveal the wisdom behind them to Janab-e-Musa (a.s.). Until when was it not revealed? 'Ila waqti iftiraqihima.' Until the separation between the two did not happen. When the separation happened, at that time Janab-e-Khizr (a.s.) clarified to Janab-e-Musa (a.s.) why he had actually performed those actions. Similarly, the Imam says, the real reason for the occultation will also be revealed to us only when the Imam (a.s.) reappears. Then after that, the Imam (a.s.) says, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'O Ibn al-Fazl, O Abdullah ibn Fazl al-Hashimi, Inna hadhal amr', surely this affair, this occultation, 'Amrun min amrillahi ta'ala.' It is one of the affairs of Allah. 'Wa sirrun min sirrillah.' It is one of the secrets of Allah. 'Wa ghaybun min ghaybillah.' It is one of the unseen things from the unseen knowledge of Allah. 'Wa mata 'alimna annahu 'azza wa jalla hakimun', and when we have established this belief that Allah is Wise, Allah (Azza wa Jalla) is Wise, we have become convinced of His wisdom. When we have become convinced that Allah does not perform any action in vain, 'saddaqa', then we have also confirmed this. What? That 'bi-anna af'alahu kullaha hikmatun', that all His actions are not devoid of wisdom. There is some wisdom behind every action of Allah. 'Wa in kana wajhuha ghayru munkashif.' Even if its reality, its real reason, is not clear to us. Despite that, our belief is that there is definitely some wisdom behind every action of Allah. Similarly, there is wisdom behind the occultation as well. But its real reason will be revealed when the Imam (a.s.) reappears. So the real reason for the occultation has not been stated, but what kind of trials will there be in the occultation, how many occultations will there be, what will happen in it, this has definitely been stated. Now this is a tradition from Ishaq ibn Ammar. Ishaq ibn Ammar is a famous narrator, a very prominent companion of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and Imam Kazim (a.s.). He has narrated a tradition on the authority of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in which the Imam (a.s.) says that for the 'Sahib al-Ism al-Khas', that is, for the Imam, the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), using that specific title, the Imam (a.s.) states that there will be two occultations for him. There are two occultations. One of them will be a short occultation (Ghaybah), and the other will be a long occultation. Regarding the first occultation, no one will know his location—meaning, in that short occultation, where the Imam (a.s.) is residing or which place he is in—no one will know his location except for his special Shia. And the other, the long occultation, no one will know his location in it except for his special loyalists. No one will know his location except for a few of his special followers. This means that in the short occultation, there are some special Shia, and in the long occultation—the Major Occultation—there are some special followers who will know where the Imam (a.s.) is. Now, if we look at this hadith, it mentions two occultations. One is the short occultation, where it is said that no one will know the Imam's location except for his special Shia. This means there are some special Shia who know where the Imam is during the Minor Occultation. The use of the word 'Khas' (special) here points towards the four special deputies (Nawwab) of the Imam (a.s.). They are called 'Khas' because they were chosen by the Imam (a.s.) himself. The Imams (a.s.) themselves selected these four deputies, who are known as the special deputies, the four Nawwab, or the four ambassadors (Sufara). They are called 'Khas' because the Imam (a.s.) personally selected them. What does this mean? It means that even in occultation, it is not as if the Imam is hidden from everyone's sight. No, there are definitely some select individuals who have access to the Imam. Similarly, if you reflect on the hadith regarding the Major Occultation, it is said that in the long occultation, only his 'special loyalists' will know his location. This means whether it is the Minor or Major Occultation, there are definitely some people in both who will know, and who will have permission from the Imam (a.s.) to reach him. However, the difference in the terminology used for those who have access to the Imam in the Minor Occultation—'his special Shia'—refers to these four special deputies. Why was their presence necessary in that era? Why did the Imams (a.s.), and specifically the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.), choose these deputies? It is because, as I mentioned in the beginning, although the wisdom behind the occultation is not clear to us and its true reason has not been fully disclosed, the trials of the occultation, the difficulties that will arise, the people who will go astray, and the doubts and suspicions—all these matters regarding the occultation have certainly been explained. This is also narrated from the sixth Imam, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). Here, the narrator is Abdullah ibn Sinan. He says, 'My father and I went to the presence of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.).' We appeared before the sixth Imam, and the Imam addressed us, saying, 'What will your condition be when you live in an era where there will be no guiding Imam visible among you, and no visible banner (Alam)?' A visible banner—why is 'Alam' used? The Alam is a sign of guidance. When a banner is raised, all those under its shadow are proof that they are guided by it. But here the Imam says, 'And no visible banner,' meaning there is no clear banner that you can see to follow toward the Imam. Here, 'no visible banner' refers to the four special deputies, and its explanation will follow. Its explanation will follow. In his explanation, Ibn Abi Zaynab—meaning Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nu'mani (r.a.)—when he narrates this hadith in his book 'Kitab al-Ghaybah', being one of the students of Sheikh al-Kulayni, writes after narrating this hadith that 'no visible banner' points to the events and the reality of the affairs of the ambassadors (Sufara), those four ambassadors who were between the Imam and the Shia. And he further writes that because the ambassador who is between the Imam and his Shia during his occultation is the 'banner' (Alam), this is the banner the hadith is pointing to. It means the hadith is referring to the Major Occultation: what will your state be in the Major Occultation when you will neither see the Imam before you, nor will you see any of the four special deputies? Now, when none of these four will be present in the Major Occultation, what should you do? Nothing will save you from this bewilderment except the one who seeks help through the 'Dua al-Hariq' (The Prayer of the Burning). 'Hariq' means burning—the prayer that saves a person from being consumed or destroyed. We also call it the 'Dua of the drowning' or the 'Dua of the burning'. If a person wants to be saved from destruction, they must seek the help of that prayer during this Major Occultation. So, Abdullah ibn Sinan says that my father immediately asked Imam Sadiq (a.s.), as soon as the Imam said that no one will be saved except the one who recites this prayer, 'By Allah, O Mawla, this is a calamity (Bala).' This is a tragedy. Meaning, the occultation is a tragedy for us. Alas, what happens to us is that we do not realize this is a tragedy. For us, life goes on comfortably; mornings come, evenings pass, and we continue living a normal life. This hadith points to the fact that we should consider the occultation as a tragedy. It is a tragedy, truly a tragedy. What greater tragedy could there be than the fact that it is not possible for a person to have direct access to the Imam of their time? You cannot reach him. Where is the Imam? No one knows. No one can even claim a direct meeting. What greater calamity could there be for us than the fact that the representative of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the Imam of the time, is present in the world, yet we cannot reach him? This is what Abdullah ibn Sinan's father is pointing to: 'O Mawla, this is a calamity, this is a tragedy. So what should we do, may I be sacrificed for you?' When this happens, what should we do? What is our responsibility? The Imam (a.s.) says, 'When this happens, when such circumstances arise and you cannot reach your Imam, then hold fast to what you have in your hands—the religion, the creed you are upon. Hold fast to it.' This is the Imam's reference to the Hadith al-Thaqalayn—the Quran and the Ahlulbayt; hold onto them. Hold onto them firmly. Never let them go. Do not let this creed slip from your hands. That which you hold in your hands, do not let it go. This is our responsibility in the Major Occultation. 'Hold fast to what you have in your hands until the matter becomes clear for you,' meaning until the reappearance (Zuhur) happens, so that the Imam is present and a person can reach him directly and find guidance. Until that happens, hold firmly to your creed. So, the important point that became clear to us from this hadith is that the occultation is a period of calamity and tragedy. However, in the Minor Occultation, the mention of the deputies refers to their specific responsibility, and that was... The Imams (a.s.) knew that people would have to pass through all these trials during the occultation. The condition of our Shia would become very difficult. It would not be easy for people to reach the Imam, nor would it be easy for them to protect their faith. Therefore, in the Minor Occultation, these four ambassadors, these four special deputies, were chosen to be a medium, a bridge between the Imam and the people. Now, in this regard, these four special deputies had certain responsibilities. Why were they appointed? The first reason that comes to mind is that the era was so tumultuous and dangerous, especially for the Shia, and not just the Shia, because we all know the Abbasid Caliphs were waiting for the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Their soothsayers and diviners had told them that a child would come who would overthrow their government. Besides that, there were other hadiths regarding the Imam of the Time (a.s.). So, these people were constantly searching for the Imam. The biggest task of these deputies, and the greatest achievement they accomplished, was keeping the actual location of the Imam (a.s.) a secret. This was the first service they performed for the Imam. The second responsibility they had was guiding the Shia. How did they guide them? When the Shia would come and meet them, giving them their letters for the Imam (a.s.), they would take those letters to the Imam, deliver them, and bring back the answers. When they brought back the answers, the people would be reassured that, 'Yes, our Imam truly exists.' This guidance was very necessary; this message, this communication reaching the people was essential so they would know we are not orphans. We have someone; our Imam is present, our Imam is alive. This guidance was crucial for the people. Furthermore, since people knew that the last one to come, the 12th, would have such a great government, many people—even today, and in that era as well—claimed to be the Mahdi. We have seen this in history. There were many claimants. Through these special deputies, the claims of these imposters were proven false, because these special deputies would take the messages to the true Imam of the Time and bring back the answers. Thus, they also accomplished the refutation of these claimants. Besides this, it is not that only they were in contact with the Imam and everyone else was cut off; no, that was not the case. They appointed their own deputies in different cities and selected them personally. They were stationed there. For example, Ahmad ibn Ishaq was in Qom, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar was in Ahvaz, Qasim ibn Ala was in Azerbaijan, and Muhammad ibn Salih was in Hamadan. These people remained in constant contact with the deputies. That is, people would come to these individuals, these individuals would come to the deputies, and the deputies would then take matters to the Imam. They established this entire system so that the people's religion could be protected. And in these meetings, the exchange of letters that took place—the letters people wrote and the 'Tawqi'at' (signed letters) that came from the Imam (a.s.)—contained the solutions to many religious issues. People would come and present their problems to the Imam (a.s.). These special deputies would bring back answers from the Imam (a.s.). This was an entire training period. This was a period of upbringing, the era of the Lesser Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra), and the important role these deputies played was—what was the most important thing?—preparing the people for the Greater Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Kubra). When these deputies fulfilled their responsibilities with such protection and trustworthiness for 69 years, they reassured the people—the special Shias who remained steadfast on Shi'ism—that our religion is the true religion. We do not need to fall into any doubt because our Imam is truly present. These two people [the deputies] gave this assurance to the people during those 69 years of the Lesser Occultation. This was the entire preparation so that when the Greater Occultation began, no one would fall into doubt. This was the most important responsibility, and besides this, collecting Khums—the religious dues—from the people and delivering them to the Imam was also their duty. And this is proven by traditions. It is proven by traditions, and in the hadith of the deputies that I will narrate, God willing, the status and rank of the Imam's (a.s.) deputies are also pointed towards. There is a tradition that some people came to Samarra to meet Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). A whole group had arrived. They saw that many people, the Imam's followers, were gathered there. This is an incident from the time of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Allama Majlisi has recorded this incident in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 51, pages 345-346. He narrates that the people who came said, 'We entered upon Abu Muhammad al-Hasan (a.s.) in Surra Man Ra'a (Samarra),' and many of his followers and Shias were present there, 'until his servant Badr entered upon him,' meaning many people were present there. Then a time came when one of the Imam's servants named Badr came there, and after arriving, he said to the Imam (a.s.), 'O my Master, there is a group at the door,' a delegation had arrived, 'disheveled and dusty,' meaning in the same state that angels go to visit Imam Hussain (a.s.), in that very state these people had come, a delegation had come to meet you, Master. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'These are a group of our Shias from Yemen.' Regarding these people, it is stated that a group of Shias, an entire delegation, had come from Yemen. When they came to the Imam (a.s.), what did the Imam (a.s.) say? The Imam (a.s.) said to his servant Badr, 'Go and bring Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri to us.' Do one thing, bring them in, give them permission, and Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, who was the first special deputy of the Imam of the time—that gentleman Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, may Allah be pleased with him—Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) says that you should take that Yemeni delegation to Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri. Now, what happened? As the Imam ordered, Uthman was called, 'Uthman entered, and our master Abu Muhammad (a.s.) said to him, 'Go, O Uthman, for you are the agent,'' O Uthman, come, come because why? Because you are an agent, meaning you are our agent, 'and you are trustworthy,' meaning you are reliable. We trust you. 'And you are the trustee over the wealth of Allah.' You are the custodian of Allah's wealth. Meaning we trust you, you are honest, and you will not commit betrayal regarding Allah's wealth. Therefore, O Uthman ibn Sa'id, come and do this, 'and take from these Yemeni people the wealth they have brought,' meaning the wealth these people have brought, you take it from them, and look at what these people have brought; you assess it. Now, what happened after that? This entire Yemeni delegation met with Uthman ibn Sa'id, and they handed over the wealth to Uthman ibn Sa'id. Some important things must have been discussed there because as the sentence of the hadith continues, after their meeting with Uthman ibn Sa'id concluded, they came to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Now, when it was time to say goodbye, when it was time to depart, they said—they are saying to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)—what do they say? They all say together to the Imam, they submit to the Imam, 'O our Master, by Allah, Uthman ibn Sa'id is one of your best Shias.' 'And you have increased our knowledge,' and because of the guidance you gave us towards him, 'you have increased our knowledge.' 'You have increased our knowledge'—the fact that you sent us to serve him, this increased our knowledge. Meaning, they also realized the extent of Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri's knowledge in that one meeting. And they testified to that fact. 'And he is your agent,' we are now fully convinced that Uthman ibn Sa'id is your agent, 'and your trusted one over the wealth of Allah,' and you trust him regarding Allah's wealth. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Yes,' indeed, you are saying the truth. At the same time, look, you also bear witness, 'and bear witness before me,' you remain witnesses to this. What? That Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri is my agent, and that his son, Muhammad—meaning Muhammad ibn Uthman Sa'id al-Amri—is the agent of my son, the Mahdi. The one who will be your Mahdi, the son of Uthman ibn Sa'id will be the agent of my son. Meaning, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) formally announced the agency of both the father, Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, and the son, Muhammad ibn Uthman Sa'id al-Amri. These were not ordinary personalities. They were chosen by the One whom Allah chose. These were such personalities. And since the responsibility was so great, the selection was such. If one were to discuss them in detail, it is not possible through a single video or a single lecture. And why is it not possible? Because it would not be fulfilling their right. These four deputies have a right upon our necks. From the beginning of the Lesser Occultation, it would not be wrong to say—and this is no exaggeration— From the beginning of the Lesser Occultation until the reappearance of the Imam, there will be no person who can equal these four deputies. Their status and rank—all our Maraje (religious authorities) are on our heads and are worthy of respect, truly worthy of respect. But if you go and ask the Maraje, they too would envy their status. That they attained that status. Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri was the deputy of three Imams. Not just the Imam of the time. He was the deputy of the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth Imams. Around 267 AH—it is not exactly known when he passed away, but it is mentioned in history and hadith around 267 AH—if the Lesser Occultation began in 260 AH, then even if we go up to 267 AH, his period of deputyship is about 7 years. After him, his son, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, was appointed as deputy after his father. His period of deputyship was the longest among the four deputies. He passed away around 305 AH, meaning his total period of deputyship was 38 years. Then after him, Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti—who had the second longest period of deputyship—was Husayn ibn Ruh. He passed away in 326 AH. Meaning he performed the duties of the Imam's deputyship for about 21 years. And finally, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Samari or al-Samuri, as he is called. He passed away in 329 AH. And his period of deputyship was about 3 years. So, as I submitted to you, a complete discussion regarding these four deputies is not possible in one sitting. God willing, if Allah grants the opportunity, we will discuss these four in detail in the future. Just one important point in conclusion that I want to draw your attention to: the graves of all four deputies are in Baghdad. Today, in the main market of Baghdad city, the graves of all four deputies are located. Whenever we get the opportunity, we should try—whoever is blessed with the honor of Ziyarat (pilgrimage) by Allah— We should try, because they are in Baghdad, meaning when we go to Kadhimiya, their graves are not far from Kadhimiya. You can take a taxi and go. Look, do not stay in this effort—do not give this reason, we should not give this reason—that 'no tour guide is taking us.' It is not like that. If it is convenient for them, then that is 'light upon light' (excellent), but even if it is not, we can go individually. It is not far, and they have a right upon our necks. They have fulfilled such a great responsibility. Therefore, as a Shia, as a lover of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), the Ziyarat of these four is a right upon our necks. Why? Because the Imam (a.s.) personally selected them. They were the special Shias of the Imam. Therefore, it is their right that we go for their Ziyarat. They are the 'Babul-Hujja' (the Gate to the Proof of Allah). They are the door to reaching the Proof of Allah. Even today, Shias benefit from their Ziyarat. And you will find their Ziyarat in the Mafatih (Mafatih al-Jinan). If you pick up the Mafatih or the books of Ziyarat, you will find the Ziyarat of these deputies in the same chapter where the Ziyarat of Kadhimiya is mentioned. And the sentences of that Ziyarat are so extraordinary; from the sentences of these Ziyarat, one can gauge what their status is, what their rank is. Standing by their grave, one must recite the Ziyarat in this way. For whichever deputy we go to visit—although all four graves are nearby, not far from each other—so whenever you go for their Ziyarat, what are the phrases of the Ziyarat? Mention the name of the deputy whose grave you are visiting, let that deputy be in your intention, and then the phrases of the Ziyarat are: 'I bear witness that you are the gate to the Wali of Allah. You fulfilled the trust on his behalf.' And 'wa addaita ilayh' (and you conveyed it to Him), and then the Ziyarat proceeds. What are the following phrases? 'Jituka arifan bil-haqq' (I have come to your presence, recognizing the truth). 'Arifan bil-haqq' (with the recognition of the Truth). 'Alladhi anta alayh' (with that true belief, with that faith, with that belief in Imamate upon which you spent your life). I confess to that. 'Wa annaka ma khunta fi ta'diyati wa sifara' (and I also bear witness that you fulfilled the responsibility of the Imam's deputyship that was given to you, you fulfilled it perfectly). You never betrayed it. Finally, what are the phrases at the end of the Ziyarat? See, we will not read the entire Ziyarat, but only the important sentences at the end: 'Jituka mukhlisan bi-tawhidillah' (I have come to you, sincerely believing in the Oneness of Allah). 'Wa muwalati awliya'ihi' (and I have come bearing the Wilayah of those whom Allah has declared as His Awliya). 'Wal-bara'ati min a'daihim' (and I have come to you with the belief of disassociation from their enemies). 'Wa minalladhina khalafu-ka' (and I also express disassociation from those who opposed you). Meaning, I also express disassociation from those who refuse to accept you as the special deputy. 'Ya hujjatal-mawla' (O you who were the proof upon us from our Master). Meaning, we are sending salutations upon them. 'Bika Allahumma tawajjuhi wa bihim ilayka tawassuli' (O Allah, through you is my orientation, and through them is my means of approach). Then, it is written at the end: 'Summa tad'u' (then make your supplications), 'wa tas'alullaha ma tuhib' (and then ask Allah for whatever you desire). 'Tujab insha-Allah ta'ala' (Allah will surely, Insha-Allah, answer your prayer). Therefore, it is the responsibility of all of us, since the right of the deputies is upon our necks, to try, whenever we go for Ziyarat, to spare some time for the Ziyarat of these special deputies. 'Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin wa sallallahu ala Muhammad wa alihi tayyibin tahirin al-ma'sumin'. We thank all of you once again. Insha-Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time with another new video. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

The Minor Occultation functioned as a critical training period for the community to prepare for the challenges of the Major Occultation.
The four special deputies (Nawwab) acted as essential bridges between the Imam and the Shia community to ensure religious guidance.
Steadfastness, prayer, and adherence to religious duties are vital for believers navigating the spiritual trials of the current era.

Ziyarat of the deputies is a profound act of acknowledging their role as the 'Gate to the Proof of Allah' and renewing one's pledge of allegiance.
