chapters.title: The Wisdom Behind the Occultation
chapters.summary: The lecture explains that while the specific wisdom behind the Imam's occultation remains a divine secret, it is compared to the actions of Prophet Khizr, which were only understood after the fact.

chapters.title: The Two Occultations of the Imam
chapters.summary: This section discusses the tradition of the two occultations—Minor and Major—and the role of the special deputies (Nawwab) who maintained a connection with the Imam.

chapters.title: Trials During the Era of Occultation
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the challenges believers face in an era where the guiding Imam and his visible signs are hidden from public view.

chapters.title: The Nature of Major Occultation
chapters.summary: The Major Occultation is described as a period of profound trial and tragedy where believers lose direct access to the Imam and his special deputies.

chapters.title: Responsibility During Occultation
chapters.summary: In the absence of the Imam, believers are instructed to hold firmly to their creed and the teachings of the Quran and Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Role of the Special Deputies
chapters.summary: The four special deputies served as a vital bridge, protecting the Imam's location, refuting imposters, and preparing the community for the Major Occultation.

chapters.title: Status of the Deputies
chapters.summary: Historical accounts, such as the delegation from Yemen, illustrate the high status and trust placed in the special deputies by the Imams.

chapters.title: Appointment of the Special Deputies
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) formally appoints Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri and his son Muhammad as his agents, establishing the foundation for the Lesser Occultation.

chapters.title: The Four Deputies and Their Legacy
chapters.summary: An overview of the four special deputies of the Imam, their respective tenures, and their unparalleled status in Shia history.

chapters.title: The Importance of Ziyarat
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the significance of visiting the graves of the four deputies in Baghdad as a duty for Shias and explains the meaning of their Ziyarat.

chapters.title: Quiz Winners and Conclusion
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with the announcement of the Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz winners and closing remarks.

title: Shabaan - Noor (a.t.f.s.) Ki Aamad | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual concept of 'Noor' (Divine Light) in relation to the Ahlulbayt and the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). It emphasizes the necessity of Sharh-e-Sadr (expansion of the heart) for true faith and the importance of recognizing the Imams as the manifestation of Allah's light. The discourse highlights the significance of Wilayah, the rejection of worldly deception, and the necessity of preparing for the hereafter through spiritual purification and steadfastness in the teachings of the Infallibles.
content:
The Imam says, who is the 'Noor' here? Noor means the Imam. Meaning, when Allah intends to guide someone, He places the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib and his infallible progeny (a.s.) in their heart. [Arabic recitation]. In Surah Al-An'am, Allah Almighty is stating that whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands their heart for Islam, and when Allah intends to lead someone astray—meaning, intends to leave them to their own devices—He makes their heart narrow and completely closed, as if they were climbing into the sky. And thus, Allah places impurity upon those who do not believe. Sadaqallahul Aliyul Azeem wa sadaqa Rasulul Kareem, Amin ya Rabbal Alamin. In the context of the meaning and significance of this blessed verse, the topic we are going to discuss today will be divided into two parts. The first will be about the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam, and the second will be regarding waiting (Intizar). The first topic regarding the recognition of the Imam is based on the fact that Allah Almighty has made guidance obligatory upon Himself. In the Holy Quran, Allah Almighty states: 'Inna alaynal huda' (Indeed, guidance is upon Us). 'Inna alaynal huda' (Indeed, guidance is upon Us). Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to guide people. This is something Allah has made obligatory upon Himself. However, no one else has the right to make anything obligatory upon Allah. If Allah Himself makes something obligatory for Himself, then that thing becomes obligatory for Allah. And continuing this chain of guidance, Allah Almighty states in the Holy Quran: 'Faman yuridillahu an yahdiyahu' (When Allah intends to guide someone), 'yashrah sadrahu lil-Islam' (He expands their heart for Islam). For Islam, because expanding for Islam is one thing, and expanding for disbelief (Kufr) is another. Because the heart can also be expanded for disbelief. That is, if a person sees non-Islamic things, or sees falsehood, sees disbelief, hypocrisy, and other things, and remains satisfied, and it does not affect their health to see that these things are happening in society, and they are satisfied, there is no problem. Meaning, if a haram act is happening somewhere, they are satisfied; if something wrong is happening, they are satisfied; if there is Shirk, they are satisfied; if betrayal is happening, they are satisfied; if theft is happening, they are satisfied; they are satisfied with everything. So, the satisfaction here, the 'sharh-e-sadr' here, is for disbelief, and Allah Almighty has mentioned this in the Holy Quran as well. For example, in Surah An-Nahl, verse 106, Allah Almighty states: 'Wa lakin man sharaha bil-kufri sadran' (But those who have expanded their hearts for disbelief). Meaning, expanded for disobedience to Allah, expanded for sins, and for all the examples I gave, their heart is expanded for all of that. Meaning, they are satisfied. They do not feel that constriction in their heart, they do not feel bad when they see disbelief and its pillars spreading all around. 'Fa alayhim ghadabun minallah' (Upon them is the wrath of Allah), 'wa lahum adhabun azim' (and for them is a great punishment). This is verse 106 of Surah An-Nahl. Therefore, if the heart is to be expanded, it should be expanded for Islam, expanded in the path of Islam. For example, regarding the Master of the Universe (a.s.), we read in Dua-e-Nudba: 'La ta'khudhuhu fillahi lawmatu la'im wa yuqatilu alal-ta'wil' (He used to fight for the interpretation and the Quran). 'Wa la ta'khudhuhu fillahi lawmatu la'im' (And in the path of Allah, he did not care about the blame of any blamer). Blame, meaning if anyone spoke ill, if anyone said anything, if he did any work in the path of Allah, he did not care who was pleased or displeased by it. His goal, his aim, his target, and his purpose was only and only to please Allah. Nothing else. Only to please Allah, that's it. And then if someone is displeased, let them be displeased; the Master did not care about that. And this concept, this meaning of 'La ta'khudhuhu fillahi lawmatu la'im', is also taken from the Holy Quran. For example, it is stated in the Holy Quran, Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 54. 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu man yartadda minkum an dinihi' (O you who believe, if any of you turns back from your religion), 'fasawfa ya'tillahu bi-qawmin' (then soon Allah will bring a people), 'yuhibbuhum wa yuhibbunahu' (He loves them and they love Him). Meaning, it is not just one-way; it is both sides. Allah also loves them, and they also love Allah. 'Adhillatin alal-mu'minin a'izzatin alal-kafirin' (They are very humble towards the believers, and very dignified towards the disbelievers). When the word 'adhilla' or 'zaleel' is used in Arabic, 'adhilla' is the plural of 'zaleel'. Meaning, they humble themselves completely, they break themselves down with great humility before the believers. But when they go before the enemies, 'a'izzatin alal-kafirin', they go with great honor and dignity. They never bow their religion or their faith, they never let it fall. They go with great dignity. 'A'izzatin alal-kafirin, yujahiduna fi sabilillah' (They strive in the path of Allah), they work very hard. 'Wa la yakhafuna lawmata la'im' (And they do not fear the blame of any blamer). No matter how much someone blames them or speaks ill of them, they do not worry about it, they do not care about it. They work only and only for the sake of Allah. And then Allah says: 'Dhalika fadlullahi yu'tihi man yasha'u, wallahu wasi'un 'alim' (This is the grace of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing). So, did you notice? This verse was revealed in honor of the Master of the Universe (a.s.), it is verse 54 of Surah Al-Ma'idah. So, the Master of the Universe did not fear anyone, and here the Imam of the Time (a.s.) says in Dua-e-Nudba: 'Wa la ta'khudhuhu fillahi lawmatu la'im' (He did not care about the blame of any blamer in the path of Allah). So, just like that, if you are working in the path of Islam, you should not care about anyone, about what they are saying, whether they are saying good or bad. Do not be too happy with praise, and do not be too troubled by criticism. Just Allah should be pleased, the Imam of the Time should be pleased. As for the people of the world, let them praise or criticize. However, it is necessary not to do any work against the Sharia, against the religion, such that Allah and the Imam of the Time become displeased. So here the Imam says: 'Yaj'al sadrahu dayyiqan harajan' (Meaning, when Allah intends to guide someone, He expands their heart for Islam, and when Allah intends to lead someone astray). What is the meaning of leading astray? This is a Quranic verse, not a Hadith. Or does he object, saying 'What does this mean?' No. That is, what is the meaning of this? What is the concept? What is the interpretation of its explanation? Allah simply leaves him to his own state. When Allah leads someone astray, it means He leaves him to his own state, which we commonly call 'khidhlan' (abandonment). Khidhlan means Allah leaves him to his own state. So, what is his condition? Allah makes his heart extremely constricted in the path of Islam. Here, the Quran uses two words: 'dayyiqan' and 'harajan'. Now, the Imam explained this, as the word appears in the books of hadith commentary, regarding how the Imam clarified it. Regarding 'dayyiq', the Imam said that when his heart is constricted in this way, a little space, a little possibility, a little chance still remains that he might incline towards Islam, that he might come a little closer. And 'harajan' means his heart is now completely closed. Now he is not ready to tolerate even a particle of anything in the path of Islam, and he does not like Islam, and he has completely turned away from Islam. Now the Quran says, 'ka-annama yassa'adu fis-sama'i' (as if he were climbing into the sky). Look, this phrase of the Quran itself is a miracle, just this much. Because in that era, there was no concept of going into the sky; it was something no one could understand—that he is going into the sky. But in today's era, you can certainly understand this better: if you are sitting in a flight and suddenly the flight takes off, suddenly it goes to a height, then how the human heart starts feeling, that is a state of his. That is exactly 'ka-annama yassa'adu fis-sama'i'. And then after that, Allah says, this is how Allah imposes filth upon those who do not believe; Allah makes this their condition, this is their state. This was verse number 125 of Surah Al-An'am. Now let us move towards the second verse. This is verse number 22 of Surah Az-Zumar. In Surah Az-Zumar, it is declared, 'Afaman sharahallahu sadrahu lil-islami fahuwa 'ala nurim mir-rabbihi' (So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to [accept] Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]?). When Allah expands someone's heart for Islam, he remains upon the light that is from his Lord. That is, the Lord's light is continuously upon him. 'Fahuwa 'ala nurim mir-rabbihi'. 'Fawaylul-lil-qasiyati qulubuhum min dhikrillahi' (Then woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah). Now they are not ready to accept the remembrance of Allah, they are not attentive towards it. Why? Because their hearts have become hardened. What is the remembrance of Allah? The remembrance of Allah is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). One of its manifestations is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). One interpretation is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). They are not ready to accept even a little bit of the truth because their hearts have become hardened. 'Ula'ika fi dalalim-mubin' (Those are in manifest error). These are the people who are in manifest error. 'Fawaylul-lil-qasiyati qulubuhum min dhikrillahi'. 'Wayl' is also the name of a valley in Hell. So these are also the people of Hell whose hearts have become hardened. Now they are not ready to accept anything in the path of Islam. So this verse is of great importance, that 'Afaman sharahallahu sadrahu lil-islami'. The 'a' that comes at the beginning of the Quran here, this is called 'istifham' (interrogative), meaning a question is being asked. Allah is asking a question, asking the intellects of people, that is the one whose heart has been expanded for Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord—'Fawaylul-lil-qasiyati'—is he like those who have gone astray? Is there any comparison between the two? No. Now, in the commentary of this verse, the Imam says, 'Wa ruwiya 'anin-nabiyyi sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi' (And it is narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family), and he recited this verse, 'Afaman sharahallahu sadrahu lil-islami fahuwa 'ala nurim mir-rabbihi'. 'Faqala sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi' (Then he said, peace be upon him and his family), 'Innan-nura idha waqa'a fil-qalbi infasaha lahu wansharaha' (When the light falls into the heart, it makes space for it and the heart expands). When the light falls. Now, obviously, light is not something material, not a physical thing, such that, for example, if we drank water, we would know that water went into the body, if we ate food, nourishment went into the body, if food went in, it shows that water went, food went. But light is not something that you can feel when it falls into the heart. So, obviously, the people sitting there also did not understand the matter. So they asked, 'Faqalu ya rasulallahi fahal lidhalika 'alamatun yu'rafu biha' (So they said, O Messenger of Allah, is there a sign for that by which it can be known?). 'Qala sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi' (He said, peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet replied in response that yes, there are three signs for it. One, 'At-tajafi 'an daril-ghurur' (Turning away from the house of deception). Deception, what does deception mean? That is, the house of deception means the world. He leaves its bed. 'Ad-daril-ghurur' is also taken from a verse of the Holy Quran. In verse number 16 of Surah As-Sajdah, it is declared, 'Tatajafa junubuhum 'anil-madaji'i' (Their sides forsake their beds). These are the people, these are the individuals who leave their beds in the darkness of the night, they empty their beds. 'Tatajafa junubuhum 'anil-madaji'i', 'yad'una rabbahum khawfan wa tama'an' (They call upon their Lord in fear and hope), and they keep praying to their Lord, and in this prayer, in this state, there is also fear—that is, the fear of Hell—'wa tama'an' (and hope) for Paradise. 'Wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun' (And from what We have provided them, they spend). And these are the people who spend in the way of Allah from what We have provided them. 'Wa mimma razaqnahum yunfiqun', they give charity, they spend it. So what is the first thing? 'At-tajafi 'an daril-ghurur'. What is the second attribute? 'Wal-inabatu ila daril-khulud'. 'Inaba' means to turn back, to turn towards. Towards what? Towards the 'Darul-Khulud' (the eternal house). That is, now they become attentive towards the primary destination, the primary abode of man that is eternal, that is Paradise, they turn towards the Hereafter. Their focus is on the Hereafter. Now their focus has shifted away from the world. Their focus is only on where? On the Hereafter. 'Wal-isti'dadu lil-mawti qabla nuzulil-mawt'. What is the third attribute found in them? How do you know that the light has entered the heart? That they are prepared for death before death arrives. Now they are fully prepared, ready for death. Now they do not fear death, they are not worried by death because what is death? It is 'liqa'ullah' (meeting Allah). Death is the name of meeting Allah. Death is the name of meeting the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Especially, it is the name of meeting the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). So, not only does he not fear death, but he is eager for death. That is why Allama Majlisi (r.a.), in his precious book 'Bihar al-Anwar', has brought a specific chapter, and the name of the chapter is 'Babu hubbi liqa'illah' (Chapter on the love of meeting Allah). That is, what is this chapter about? 'Liqa'illah', meaning about the love of death. Love of death. So these are those individuals, for whom? For those in whose hearts Allah has placed the light. So these three things are found in them. Which three things? One, they leave the house of the world and turn towards the Hereafter and turn their entire focus towards the Hereafter, and the third thing is they are prepared for death before death arrives. Now, when this fundamental matter became clear, now let us move towards the actual destination, which is the 'Ma'rifat' (recognition) of the Imam, and that is, what is this light? What is this light? About which the Holy Quran is mentioning. About which there is a proper discussion in the Holy Quran. So let us go towards the book 'Al-Kafi'. 'Al-Kafi', which was written by Sheikh Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kulayni (r.a.), and Sheikh Kulayni, who saw the era of the Minor Occultation and passed away in 329 AH, the same year in which the Minor Occultation ended and the Major Occultation began. So Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) has brought a proper chapter in 'Al-Kafi', and the name of the chapter is 'Babu annal-a'immata 'alayhimus-salamu anwarullahi' (Chapter that the Imams (a.s.) are the lights of Allah). They are the lights of Allah (Azza wa Jall). Who is the light of the Lord? The Ahlulbayt (a.s.). In this chapter, he brings a hadith. This hadith is from Hasan ibn Mahbub, and he narrates from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl that Imam Kazim (a.s.) said—that is, the narrator says, who is the narrator? Fudayl Muhammad ibn Khuda. He says that I asked Imam Kazim (a.s.) about this noble verse. Which noble verse? 'Yuriduna liyutfi'u nurallahi bi-afwahihim' (They intend to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths). They intend to extinguish the light of Allah by blowing with their mouths. Here, 'bi-afwahihim' means by their efforts, and they want to extinguish this light. Their intention is, their motive is, 'yuriduna' 'liyutfi'u' (they intend to extinguish), 'nurallahi' (the light of Allah). Look, this human who has no standing, who has no worth—look at his thoughts, what they are! He wants to extinguish the light of Allah. The Allah who created him. And he has no access to that light, his eyes are... but he intends to extinguish that light. So Imam Kazim (a.s.), in clarification of this sentence of this verse, says, 'Yuriduna liyutfi'u' (They intend to extinguish), they want to extinguish, what? To end, what to end? 'Wilayata amiril-mu'minina bi-afwahihim' (The Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful by their mouths). Now, let me give you an example of extinguishing by blowing with the mouth, which is very clear today, this is 1443 AH. Look, a bomb exploded in a neighboring country. They martyred approximately 60 lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). 60 individuals were martyred in it, the rest were injured. What was their fault? Their only fault was 'Aliyun Waliullah' and nothing else. That they say 'Aliyun Waliullah'. Immediately after 'Muhammadur Rasulullah' (s.a.w.a.), 'Aliyun Waliullah wa Wasi'u Rasulillahi wa Khalifatuhu bila fasl' (Ali is the Wali of Allah, the successor of the Messenger of Allah, and his immediate Caliph). 'Ashhadu anna 'Aliyan Amiral-Mu'minina Waliullah'. That is their only fault. They believe in the Caliphate without separation. This is their fault and nothing else. So 'Wilayata Amiril-Mu'minina bi-afwahihim' with their mouths. I asked a question. That is, Muhammad bin Fudayl says I asked. Then what is the meaning of this phrase? 'Qawluhu ta'ala wallahu mutimmu nurihi' (Allah will perfect His light). Allah will take His light to the stage of perfection, He will complete it. The Imam replied in response, clarifying that the interpretation is, 'Wallahu mutimmul-imamti' (And Allah will take the Imamate to the stage of perfection), He will take it to the stage of perfection. That is, He will take it to the 12th Imam. Even if these people dislike it. That is, all the Imams will come. They wanted to extinguish the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). After Ali (a.s.), 11 more Imams came, and they did everything to all of them—some they killed, some they poisoned, they made them wander from door to door, everything they could do, they did, and not only to them, but also to their lovers, to their honor. But Allah protected this Wilayah and kept it remaining. The Imam says, 'Wal-imamatu hiyannuru' (And the Imamate is the light). The Imamate itself is the light. 'Wa dhalika qawluhu azzawajalla' (And this is the saying of Allah Azza wa Jall). 'Fa'aminu billahi wa rasulihi' (So believe in Allah and His Messenger). 'Wan-nurilladhi anzalna' (And the light which We have sent down). So there is talk of belief in three things: believe in Allah, believe in His Messenger, and believe in the light which We have sent down. Then the Imam says, 'Qala 'alayhis-salamu an-nuru huwal-imamu' (The Imam said, peace be upon him, the light is the Imam). Now look, 'Afaman sharahallahu sadrahu lil-islami'. Look, what was the first verse that was read? When Allah wants to guide someone, 'Famayyuridillahu ayyahdiyahu yashrah sadral-islami' (When Allah wants to guide someone, He expands his heart for Islam). This was the first verse. What was the second verse? 'Afaman sharahallahu sadrahu lil-islami fahuwa 'ala nurim-mir-rabbihi'. Now, the one whose heart Allah expands for Islam, he is upon the light of his Lord. The Lord causes His light to penetrate into his heart. Now here the Imam says, who is the 'Light' (Noor) here? That is, the Light is the Imam. Meaning, when Allah intends to guide someone, He places the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib and his infallible progeny (a.s.) into their heart. Allah guides them in such a way that the Wilayah of Ali is born in their heart, and when there is the Wilayah of Ali, it is obvious that it will not just be the Wilayah of Ali; along with it, there will also be Bara'ah (disassociation). There will be enmity towards the enemies of Ali. Allah cannot befriend the enemies of Ali, because Allah Almighty has made a formal promise in the Holy Quran. Look, He has made a formal announcement. It is verse number 4 of Surah Al-Ahzab. Surah Al-Ahzab, which is Surah number 33, verse 4. Allah says, 'Ma ja-alallahu lirajulim-min qalbayni fi jawfihi' (Allah has not made for any man two hearts in his chest). And in the commentary of this verse, the Imam says, Allah does not place two loves in anyone's heart. If there is the love of Allah, then the love of Satan will not enter. If there is the love of Habil (Abel), then the love of Qabil (Cain) will not enter. If there is the love of Musa (Moses), then the love of Fir'aun (Pharaoh) will not enter. If there is the love of Ibrahim (Abraham), then the love of Namrud (Nimrod) will not enter. If there is the love of Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.), then the love of Abu Jahl will not enter. Now, in the same way, if there is the love of Ali, then the love of Ali's enemies will not enter. The entire foundation of Wilayah rests on this. Now, let us move to the second Hadith, which is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 194, Hadith number 1. The narrator is Abu Khalid al-Kabuli. Abu Khalid, a resident of Afghanistan; Abu Khalid is his Kunniyah, his name is Kankar, and because he was from Kabul, he is called Kabuli. He is a companion of the fourth Imam and the fifth Imam. He witnessed the era of two Imams—the fourth and the fifth. So, he comes to the service of the fifth Imam and says—meaning he narrates the tradition—'Sa'altu Aba Ja'farin alayhis-salam' (I asked the fifth Imam) about this saying of Allah: 'Fa-aminu billahi wa rasulihi wan-nurillazi anzalna' (So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down). 'Faqala alayhis-salam' (Then he, peace be upon him, said). Now the fifth Imam, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), says, 'Ya Aba Khalid!' 'O Abu Khalid! An-nuru wallahi al-aimmatu min ali Muhammadin alayhimussalam' (By Allah, in this noble verse, 'Light' refers to the Imams from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.)) 'Ila yawmil qiyamah' (until the Day of Resurrection). This is the Master's saying. Until the Day of Resurrection. 'Hum wallahi' (By Allah, they are) the Imams of Light. 'Nurullahi' (They are the Light of Allah) 'allazi anzala' (which Allah has sent down). 'Wahum wallahi' (And by Allah, they are...) Look, the Imam is swearing, swearing repeatedly. This shows the importance, because an oath by an Imam is a Shari'ah oath, and if the Imam simply states something, that is sufficient for us, it is a proof (Hujjah). But if the Imam is swearing, you can understand how important this matter is. Reflect on how important it is, and he is not swearing just once. The Imam is swearing repeatedly in this Hadith. Look, first the Imam swore, 'Ya Aba Khalid! An-nuru wallahi' (once). Then after that, he says, 'Hum wallahi nurullahi' (the second time). Then the Imam is swearing for the third time, 'Wahum wallahi nurullahi fis-samawati wal ard' (By Allah, they are the Light of Allah in the heavens and the earth). The Light of Allah in the heavens and the earth are the Imams from the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). Then the Imam swears for the fourth time, 'Wallahi ya Aba Khalid! O Abu Khalid! By Allah, la-nurul imami fi qulubil mu'minin' (Indeed, the light of the Imam in the hearts of the believers, in the hearts of the believers). Meaning, it is not in everyone's heart. Only those who believe, who believe in Allah, believe in the Messenger, and believe in the Infallible Imams (a.s.), in their hearts this faith is so radiant that the Imam says, 'Anwaru minash-shams al-mudi-yati bin-nahar' (brighter than the sun that shines in the day), which shines at noon, brighter than that. Then the Imam swears, 'Wahum wallahi' (By Allah, they are) the Infallible Imams (a.s.), 'Yunawwiruna qulubal-mu'minin'. The believers, who illuminate the hearts of the believers. And Allah guides to His Light whom He wills, and darkens their hearts. And the result is that their hearts become dark, gloomy, and black. Because they are deprived of the Light of the Imam. Their hearts become black. 'Wallahi' (By Allah), the sixth time he swears, 'Ya Aba Khalid! O Abu Khalid! By Allah, la yuhibbuna 'abdun wa yatawallana' (No servant will love us and accept our Wilayah) 'hatta' (until) 'yutahhirallahu qalbahu' (Allah purifies his heart, makes it pure). 'Yutahhirallahu qalbahu wa la yutahhirallahu qalba 'abdin' (Allah will not purify the heart of any servant) 'hatta yusallima lana' (until he submits to us completely, bows his head in complete submission, bows his head in complete submission). 'Hatta yusallima lana wa yakuna silman lana' (Until he submits to us and is in a state of peace and reconciliation with us), meaning he does not wage war against us. When he is in this state, meaning he submits and is in a state of peace, then Allah will purify his heart. 'Fa-idha kana silman lana' (When he is in a state of peace with us), meaning at peace, 'he will be at peace with us', 'sallamahullahu min shadidil hisab' (Allah will save him from the severe reckoning) that will take place on the Day of Resurrection, He will not take his account. 'Sallamahullahu min shadidil hisab wa amanahu min faz'i yawmil qiyamatil akbar' (And Allah will keep him safe from the Great Terror of the Day of Resurrection). And on the Day of Resurrection, which will be the Great Terror, the great fear, Allah will keep him safe from this Great Terror, he will keep him sound. He will not be troubled in the Great Terror when everyone else is troubled. You know what the Great Terror is, right? It is necessary for the youth to know what this Great Terror is. In the Resurrection, there are 50 stages of Resurrection, and each stage is 1,000 years. 1,000 years, so the total Resurrection will be 50,000 years. The total Resurrection is 50,000 years, and out of those 50,000 years, one stage of 1,000 years will be the Great Terror. There is quite a lot of detail about this Great Terror in the traditions. Allah, in Majlis-e-Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh, in Bihar al-Anwar, they have discussed this in detail in a chapter. Al-Faz'ul Akbar. And what is it? It is that stage, that position of the Resurrection when there will be darkness all around. All around, 'La yasma'una illa hamsa' (They will hear nothing but a faint sound). People will hear nothing except the faint whispers that will occur. No one will have the voice, no one will have the courage to speak in a loud voice. This will be the condition. 'La yasma'una illa hamsa'. This Great Terror is also mentioned in the Holy Quran. It is mentioned in the Holy Quran as well. So, 'La yasma'una illa hamsa'. And there will be so much sweat, so much sweat that the condition of the people will be completely changed. There will be so much fear. Now let us move to the second noble verse. And this noble verse itself is famous as the Verse of Light (Ayat al-Nur). 'Allahu nurus-samawati wal ard'. 'Mathalu nurihi kamishkatin fiha misbah. Al-misbahu fi zujajah. Az-zujajatu ka'annaha kawkabun durriyyun yuqadu min shajaratin mubarakatin zaytunatin la sharqiyyatin wa la gharbiyyatin yakadu zaytuha yudi'u wa law lam tamsashu nar. Nurun 'ala nur.' In the context of this verse, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) says, 'Nurun 'ala nur' (Light upon light) means 'Imamun ba'da imamin' (one Imam after another). 'Yahdillahu linurihi man yasha' (Allah guides to His Light whom He wills). Meaning, He does not guide everyone. He guides whom He wills. 'Wa yadribullahu linnas' (And Allah presents parables for the people), He is presenting an example. 'Wallahu bikulli shay'in 'alim' (And Allah is Knowing of all things). Then the Imam continues, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) says, 'Fannuru 'Aliyyun' (The Light is Ali). The Light is Ali. 'Yahdillahu liwilayatina man ahabba' (Allah guides to our Wilayah whom He loves). Allah, whom He loves, He guides them towards our Wilayah. 'Wa haqqun 'alallahi' (And it is incumbent upon Allah), and Allah has made this incumbent upon Himself. 'Ay yab'atha waliyyana' (That He should raise our friend/follower) on the Day of Resurrection in what state? 'Mushriqan wajhuhu' (His face will be shining), he will have a radiant face. 'Nayyarul burhanuhu' (His proof will be bright), and his argument, his evidence will be completely clear. 'Zahiran indallahi hujjathuhu' (His proof will be manifest before Allah). He will bring the proof, his proof, his argument, and it will be completely clear. 'Haqqun 'alallahi ay yaj'ala waliyyana' (And it is incumbent upon Allah to place our follower) with whom, in whose company? 'Ma'an-nabiyyina wa siddiqina wa shuhada'i wa salihin wa hasuna ula'ika rafiqa' (With the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions). That Allah will place our followers with the prophets, with the truthful, with the martyrs, with the righteous, and what an excellent company this is, what excellent friends these are. Will anyone find better friends than them? 'Hasuna ula'ika rafiqa'. The Quran is saying they are excellent friends. 'Hasuna ula'ika rafiqa'. So, the one who holds Wilayah, this is his reward from Allah. And look, that his face should be radiant, this is what we recite in Dua-e-Nudba, right? I request the youth to recite Dua-e-Nudba. Wherever you are, in any corner of the world, in your home, mosque, center, Imambargah, organize Dua-e-Nudba anywhere, recite Dua-e-Nudba. It is not that if there is a Dua-e-Nudba, you should have it stopped. Have an ongoing Dua-e-Nudba stopped. Some people are experts in this too. That they don't like that a Dua is happening here. And on some pretext or another, they remove it. No, rather you organize it yourself. If it is not happening, and if it is happening, then participate in it. So, in Dua-e-Nudba, the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) says that 'Wa lawla anta ya Ali'. Look, the Prophet said, in Dua-e-Nudba the Imam of the Time says that the Prophet said, 'O Ali, if you were not there, lam yu'rafil mu'minuna ba'di' (the believers would not have been recognized after me). There would be no standard for recognition. You, Ali, you are the standard for recognizing who is a believer and who is a hypocrite. And in that same Dua-e-Nudba, it says, 'Wa shi'atuka 'ala manabira min nur' (And your Shia will be on pulpits of light). 'Manabira', 'manabir' is the plural of 'minbar'. Manabiran min noor. Mubayyazatan wujuhuhum. Their faces will be white. Mubayyaza, white. Wujuhuhum. Hauli fil jannah. And they will be around me in Paradise. Wa hum jeerani, and they will be my neighbors. They will be my neighbors, and after that, he (the Prophet) says: O Ali, if it were not for you, there would be no standard for the believers, no way to recognize a believer. In any case, the conclusion of these verses and traditions is that those who are deprived of the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam of the Time, those who do not have the Ma'rifat of the Imam of the Time, their hearts are dark. And this darkness is the cause of this deprivation. Deprivation of what? Deprivation of what? That is, the blessings of Allah. These people are deprived of Allah's blessings. That is, they are deprived of guidance, deprived of divine success (Tawfiqat), and deprived of religion. They are truly deprived of the real religion, deprived of true monotheism (Tawheed), and deprived of the real meaning and concept of Prophethood. Look, just superficially like this, that talking about corporate religion is not religion. Religion is that which is in the light of the teachings of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Exactly in the light of their teachings. And then, to conclude the discussion, a tradition of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), and this letter was written by Imam Sadiq (a.s.) to his Shias. And this is a complete constitution for the Shias. It is in Rawdat al-Kafi, the eighth volume of Kafi. Its first Hadith. The Imam wrote a letter. It is a very long letter. Its final sentences are these, the very last ones. I will not read the whole Hadith because it is a 14-15 page Hadith. Just two or three sentences from it for your service. Wa'lamu, and know, the Imam is saying to the Shias, know. Annallaha iza arada bi'abdin khayran, when Allah desires good for a servant, sharaha sadrahu lil-Islam, He expands his heart for Islam. Therefore, saluhu ayyashraha sudoorakum lil-Islam. You pray to Allah, ask Allah to expand your hearts and your chests for Islam. Wa ayyaj'ala alsinatakum yantiqu bil-haqq. And pray to Allah that as long as you are alive, your tongue speaks nothing but the truth. Just speak only the truth. Hatta yatawaffakum, until death comes to you. Wa antum 'ala zalik, and you are upon that. So, speak the truth, speak of Wilayah, speak of Bara'ah. Do not be afraid of anyone, do not step back. Wa ayyaj'ala munkalabakum munkalabas-saliheen qablakum, and may Allah make your end the same as the end of the righteous people who were before you. Wa la quwwata illa billah, and there is no power except with Allah. Walhamdullilahi Rabbil Alameen, wa sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibeen at-tahireen al-ma'sumeen al-mazlumeen, wa la'natullahi da'im 'ala a'daihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri faza'ilhim. This was the first topic, which was about the Ma'rifat of the Imam. Now, Insha'Allah, we will move to the second topic, and that is waiting (Intizar) and its several aspects. Insha'Allah, if Allah grants success, recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.).

title: Hazrat Fatima (s.a) Ka Naam Mansoorah Hai | From SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance behind the names of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.), specifically focusing on why she is titled 'Fatima' on Earth and 'Mansura' in the heavens. It explains that her earthly name signifies the protection of her followers from Hellfire, while her heavenly name relates to the divine promise of victory and assistance for her devotees. The discourse references Quranic verses to illustrate the spiritual connection between the help of Allah and the intercession of the daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).
content:
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked, "O Gabriel, why is her name Mansura in the heavens and Fatima on the earth?" The reply came, "She is called Fatima on earth because her Shias are kept away from the fire of Hell, and her enemies are kept away from her devotion. And she is called Mansura in the heavens because Allah Subhanhu wa Ta'ala says in Surah Ar-Rum, verses 4 and 5, 'On that day, the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah, and He helps whom He wills.' What is meant by 'Nasrullah' here?" The Imam (a.s.) further explains, "It means the help of Fatima for her lovers, meaning she will be happy because of the help given to her devotees."
Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) is named Fatima on Earth because her Shias are protected from Hellfire.
The name Mansura in the heavens signifies divine victory and assistance.
The term 'Nasrullah' in Surah Ar-Rum is linked to the help provided to the devotees of Fatima (s.a.).
Her enemies are intentionally distanced from her devotion and intercession.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) sought clarification from Gabriel regarding the dual nature of her titles.
The status of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) is elevated both in the physical and spiritual realms.

title: EP03 | Hadees-e-Saqalain Mein Tabdeeli Ki Nakaam Koshish | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ💐
excerpt: This lecture provides a rigorous analytical defense of the authenticity of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, emphasizing the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt. It critiques historical attempts to alter the wording of the Hadith—specifically the substitution of 'Sunnah' for 'Itrah'—by highlighting the unreliability of the narrators associated with the latter version. The session concludes that the Ahlulbayt are the divinely appointed interpreters of the Quran, whose guidance is essential for the Ummah until the Day of Judgment.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The failed attempt to alter the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. What did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) not give us during his 23 years of preaching? The correct belief that becomes the cause of success on the Day of Judgment; the deeds through which a human can attain closeness to Allah Ta'ala; and the height of noble character by practicing which humanity can reach the stages of perfection. The Messenger, whose entire life the Creator of the universe declared as 'Uswah-e-Hasana' (the best example to follow), his great status and his message deserved that Muslims accept his words, deeds, and even his silence as Sunnah. Today, wherever the name of the religion of Islam is found in the world, and wherever it will be found until the Day of Judgment, it is solely the result of that 23-year preaching of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). In every era, Muslims also take great care of the respect and greatness of the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and cannot tolerate even the slightest disrespect towards him. A thought comes to mind here: if the later Muslims are so sensitive about the respect of their beloved Prophet (s.a.w.a.), then how much must the Muslims and companions at the beginning of Islam have observed the words and deeds of the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? But is it really so? History tells us something else. History is a witness that those who claimed to love the Prophet and sat with him were the ones who, in his final moments, sometimes opposed his command, and sometimes, God forbid, accused him of not being in his right mind. They broke the promises made to him, and it reached the extent that not only did they forge false Hadiths in his name, but they also tampered with and altered the Hadiths he had stated. The purpose behind all these conspiracies was only one: to establish a religion of their own choosing for the sake of power, and to oppose the one whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had appointed as his successor and Caliph for the protection of the religion, namely Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). You might be surprised to know that to fulfill this purpose, after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), they even tried to alter his famous and well-known Hadith al-Thaqalayn, which no Muslim can deny. Through this video, we will expose this failed attempt, Insha'Allah Ta'ala, so that it becomes clear that after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), if one wants to remain steadfast on the path of guidance and avoid going astray until the Day of Judgment, what must one do? So let us move towards this topic with our brothers Muhammad Abbas Patel and Ahsan Ali Jafri. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him inhabit Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Abbas brother, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. And peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. As the topic is the alteration made in Hadith al-Thaqalayn, the failed attempts at these alterations. The topic is a bit complex, so let us try to cover this topic together, and viewers, we will try to discuss the various aspects of this topic in your service. And what we have done is that we will try to divide this topic into five separate parts, Insha'Allah, we will try to cover it in five separate parts. In which, first of all, we will look at the background of Hadith al-Thaqalayn and its connection to Ghadir. Then after that, we will take a cursory look at the various versions of this Hadith found in both Shia books and Sunni books, Insha'Allah. Then we will come to the topic of when Hadith al-Thaqalayn was altered, and a proper analysis of it will be done, Insha'Allah. After that, the fourth part, in the fourth part, we will try to see that on one side is Hadith al-Thaqalayn, which no Muslim can deny. Finally, who in history, when, and in what circumstances opposed this Hadith al-Thaqalayn? And finally, the most important, the eight important results of this Hadith al-Thaqalayn, the eight important conclusion points, what are the eight important points that emerge from this Hadith al-Thaqalayn? So, InshaAllah, we will try to discuss these five topics. Let us first move to the first point, which is the background of this Hadith al-Thaqalayn and its connection to Ghadir. The famous version of Hadith al-Thaqalayn that is narrated, which is the most common version among people, is as you all know, that the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated: 'Inni tarikun feekum al-thaqalayn, kitaballahi wa itrati ahli bayti, ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abadan, wa innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida alayya al-hawd.' That is, I am leaving among you two precious... things. Two precious things. This should be kept in mind. What are the two precious things I am leaving behind? Kitab Allah, the Book of Allah, and Itrati Ahli Bayti, my progeny, my Ahlulbayt. 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima'—as long as you hold fast to these two, you will never go astray after me. And these two things, the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, will never separate from each other until they meet me at the Hawd al-Kawthar on the Day of Judgment. 'Hatta yarida alayya al-hawd'—until they both arrive at the Hawd al-Kawthar to me. This is the famous version of Hadith al-Thaqalayn that is generally narrated. The book in which this version is present is titled 'Al-Murshid fi Imamat-e-Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)'. Its author is Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari. This is a Shia author. Although there is also a Sunni author named Tabari, and coincidentally his name is also Muhammad ibn Jarir, so do not be confused. The Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari in 'Al-Murshid' is a Shia author. And on page 559, this is Hadith number 237. This is where this hadith is found. This is the famous version of Hadith al-Thaqalayn that is narrated. Now, when we talk about its background, we will try to look into both Sunni books and our own Shia books to see on which occasions the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) narrated this Hadith al-Thaqalayn. First, we look at a very famous and well-known Sunni book, 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa'. On page 432 of 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa'—this screenshot is in front of you—on page 432, he has a lengthy discussion, meaning there is an entire page dedicated to this hadith and where the Prophet narrated it, it is all mentioned there. Ibn Hajar al-Makki is the author. Remember, this is not our book; it is a Sunni book, and specifically 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa'. The full name of this book is 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa fi Radd 'ala Ahl al-Bid'ah wal-Zandaqa'. This means 'The Burning Thunderbolts against the People of Innovation and Heresy'. He wrote this book against the Shias. And in it, he discusses the Caliphs—the ones they consider the Rightly Guided Caliphs—the first three caliphates, and then the caliphate of Ali (a.s.), his Imamate, and the Imamate of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). So, he wrote this book against the Shias, and the Shias were explicitly labeled as people of innovation. The purpose of writing this book was against the Shias. But when it comes to Hadith al-Thaqalayn in this book, regarding it, he writes on page 432: 'Wa fi riwayatin sahih'—in a sahih (authentic) narration. First of all, he admitted that the narration is absolutely authentic. According to them as well, it is authentic. 'Inni tarikun feekum amrayn'—I am leaving among you two matters, meaning two important things. 'Fi amrayn'—meaning two. 'Feekum amrayn'—meaning two important things. 'Lan tadillu in tabi'tumuhuma'—if you follow these two, you will never go astray. 'Kitabullahi wa ahli bayti itrati'—the Book of Allah and my Ahlulbayt, my progeny. And then he writes that Tabarani has added to this. What did Tabarani add to this version? 'Inni sa'altu dhalika lahuma'—that when I, the Prophet—meaning the narrator asked the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about these two—then what did the Prophet say? 'Fala taqaddumuhuma'—look, never try to go ahead of them. Otherwise, what will happen? 'Fatahliku'—otherwise you will all perish. 'Wa la tuqassiru 'anhuma fatahliku'—in one version, it is also found that look, neither try to go ahead of them nor be negligent regarding them. Meaning, do not stay behind them, and do not try to lower their status or diminish it, otherwise you will perish. 'Wa la tu'allimuhuma'—and look, do not try to teach them. Neither try to go ahead of the Quran, nor try to teach anything to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Otherwise, what will happen? Why? Why should you not try? 'Fa-innahum a'lamu minkum'—because they know more than you. Therefore, this version, this entire statement he narrated, and then after that, he also said that 'Kitab Allah wa Sunnati' is also narrated according to another version. But after that, he writes something interesting. 'Wal-hasil'—meaning what is the conclusion? Because in one place 'Book and Sunnah' is mentioned, and in another 'Book and Ahlulbayt' is mentioned. Although he has not brought any evidence regarding the Sunnah. What did he say about the 'Ahli Bayti' hadith? 'Wa fi riwayatin sahih'—in an authentic narration. But regarding the 'Sunnati' hadith, there is no such evidence; he says 'wa fi riwayatin'—and in one narration, but he did not bring evidence. Anyway, since they have compulsions to keep the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) behind and try to bring the Sunnah forward. Now look here at how he tried to combine these two things, but even then, he could not sideline the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). What does he write? 'Wal-hasil'—meaning what is the conclusion? 'Anna al-haththa waqa'a 'ala al-tamassuki bil-kitabi wa bil-sunnati wa bil-'ulama'i bihima min ahli al-bayt'—the conclusion is that the command to hold fast is given to... the Book of God, the Sunnah, and the scholars among the Ahlulbayt who know them. Meaning, it is said to hold fast to all three. Even here, he could not push the Ahlulbayt behind. How could he? When the authentic hadith exists. Therefore, he cannot keep the Ahlulbayt behind. He brings this addition of 'Sunnah' from his own side, and then further states that until the Day of Judgment, it is necessary to hold fast to all three. And then he writes, 'Summa i'lam'—after that, know that regarding the command to hold fast in this hadith, 'bi-dhalika turuqan kathiran'—there are many chains of narration, meaning it has been narrated from many different narrators. Its chain of narrators is very extensive, and more than 20 companions have narrated this hadith. 'Wa marra lahu turuqan madbutatan fi hadi 'ashara al-shubaha'—and it has been mentioned from many narrators, and there are 11 different chains for it, and 11 different branches; these hadiths are coming in different ways. 'Wa fi ba'di tilka al-turuq'—and look, the important thing here is this. We are talking about the background of this hadith, where this hadith was narrated. Some of its chains of narration contain that when did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) narrate this hadith for the first time? 'Bi-hajjat al-wada' bi-'arafah'—at the Farewell Pilgrimage, in his last Hajj. Although, apparently, that last Hajj is famous by the name of Hajjat al-Wada', but apparently, with such a large gathering, it was the first and last Hajj of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Apparently. So, at Hajjat al-Wada', where? In the plain of Arafat. 'Wa fi ukhra annahu qalahu bil-madinati fi maradihi'—the second, meaning another chain of it is found like this, that when did the Prophet state it? In Medina, at his final time. Okay? When he was, meaning at his final time, in his last days, at that time. And that too in what state? When his room was full of companions. There were many companions in the room; among all those companions, he narrated Hadith al-Thaqalayn. 'Wa annahu qala dhalika bi-ghadiri khumm'—third, meaning when was the third occasion it was narrated? At Ghadir-e-Khumm. This hadith was narrated at Ghadir. chapters.title: The Importance of Hadith al-Thaqalayn

chapters.title: Structure of the Analysis
chapters.summary: The speakers outline a five-part plan to analyze the background, versions, and historical opposition regarding the Hadith al-Thaqalayn.

chapters.title: Authenticity and Interpretations
chapters.summary: The discussion covers the standard version of the Hadith and examines how even Sunni sources like 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa' acknowledge its authenticity while attempting to reconcile it with other narratives.

chapters.title: Authenticity and Multiplicity of Hadith al-Thaqalayn
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the extensive chains of narration for Hadith al-Thaqalayn and how the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) emphasized the importance of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Occasions of Proclamation
chapters.summary: The Prophet repeated Hadith al-Thaqalayn on numerous occasions, including Hajjat al-Wada' and Ghadir-e-Khumm, to solidify the status of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Variations and Interpretations of the Hadith
chapters.summary: Various versions of the hadith from both Shia and Sunni sources are analyzed, highlighting the explicit mention of the Ahlulbayt and Ali ibn Abi Talib as the successors.

chapters.title: The Inseparable Bond: Quran and Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) designated Ali (a.s.) as the sole interpreter of the Quran, establishing a divine link between the two.

chapters.title: The Alteration of Hadith-e-Saqalain
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the historical attempt to replace 'Itrati' (my progeny) with 'Sunnati' (my Sunnah) in the Hadith of Saqalain, noting its absence in Shia sources.

chapters.title: Critique of the 'Sunnati' Version
chapters.summary: The speaker analyzes the sources of the 'Sunnati' version, demonstrating that they lack authentic chains of transmission (Sanad) and contain unreliable narrators.

chapters.title: Analyzing the Concept of Sunnah
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that even if the 'Sunnati' version were accepted for argument's sake, the definition of the Prophet's Sunnah inherently requires the guidance of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Sunnah and the Methodology of Prayer
chapters.summary: The speaker contrasts the diverse prayer methods of various schools of thought with the consistent practice of the Shia Ithna Ashari, while defining Sunnah as the words, actions, and silent approvals of the Prophet.

chapters.title: Ghadir and the Hadith al-Thaqalayn
chapters.summary: The lecture examines the events at Ghadir Khumm, arguing that the Prophet's actions and words established the authority of Ali (a.s.) and the Ahl-e-Bayt alongside the Quran.

chapters.title: Attempts to Alter Hadith al-Thaqalayn
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses historical attempts to replace 'Ahl-e-Bayt' with 'Sunnah' in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn and highlights the contradiction of those who claimed 'the Book of Allah is sufficient' while opposing the Prophet's will.

chapters.title: Eight Conclusions of Hadith al-Thaqalayn
chapters.summary: The lecture outlines the necessity of the Ahl-e-Bayt's leadership, their infallibility, and their role as the sole interpreters of the Quran to prevent the Ummah from going astray.

chapters.title: Ali (a.s.) as the Establisher of the Quran

chapters.title: The Authority and Permanence of the Ahlulbayt
