title: EP1 | Fadak in Islamic History | 🎙️ The Fadak Podcast: Fadak, Fatima (s.a.) aur Hum
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical, economic, and theological significance of Fadak in early Islamic history, focusing on its status as the personal property of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his subsequent gift to Bibi Fatima (s.a.). The discussion clarifies the distinction between 'Fay' and 'Ghanimah' to establish the legal basis for Fatima's claim, while addressing historical biases in narrations. It further analyzes the political motivations behind the usurpation of Fadak and its impact on the economic standing of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
And if you want to know how much its value was, then the successor of the ruler, when he expelled the Jews from this land and sent them towards Sham—the present-day Palestine—he paid 500 dirhams at that time for half the land, which was the price of half the land where the Jews were, and the rest was what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had agreed upon in a truce, that half is for you and when we want we can take it. But the first question that arises is, when we use the word 'Maal-e-Ghanimat' and the word 'Fay', what is the difference between Maal-e-Ghanimat and Fay? The criteria for 'Dhaif' (weak) in the Sunni school of thought is often that whenever a narrator says something against their established beliefs, they are immediately stamped as a 'Dhaif' narrator, even if it is the truth. Despite that, if someone says something against their core fundamentals, especially regarding Wilayah and Imamate, and here these disagreements... we can say that out of the six, about three authors of the Sihah Sittah considered it authentic because the land of Fadak was so important and this topic was so significant. Therefore, Allah mentioned its expenditure in the very next verse in Surah... In the very next verse in Surah Hashr, verse number 7, it is mentioned. Fakhr Razi says in the commentary of this verse that this verse was revealed regarding Fadak, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) conquered without any battle. The Prophet used to spend the expenses of his household from this for the whole year. And what was left over, he used to spend on other works. This proves that Fadak was the Prophet's personal property, which the Prophet gifted and bestowed upon the Princess (s.a.) after receiving the command. The word used in the Hadith is 'gifted'. Before the conquest of Khaybar, the Muslims did not get enough food to eat. Ibn Umar himself testifies to this in Sahih Bukhari: 'We did not eat to our fill except when we conquered Khaybar.' That is, the condition was so dire before Khaybar. And there is the opposite too, that after Khaybar, there was such abundance of wealth for the Muslims that the entire state, the entire government, ran on its budget, solely from these properties. And if you look, on one side is Siddiqa, and if we truly consider the Princess (s.a.) as Siddiqa, then it is not permissible for us to consider the one who usurped her right as a Siddiq. If we are calling him Siddiq... If we are calling him Siddiq, then the direct result of this is that we are denying the Princess (s.a.). If she is Siddiqa, then A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala Ya Wali al-Asr. Dear viewers, today's podcast is to discuss an extremely important topic. This topic is about a personality whose greatness, whose status, whose loftiness perhaps you and I cannot even comprehend. Yes, I am talking about the Princess of the two worlds, Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.). In today's episode, we are going to see the importance of Fadak and its background—how this land came into the ownership of the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) and what steps the Prophet took regarding this land in his own lifetime. Remember that this issue is not just about a piece of land, but it is so important because... It is so important because this matter is directly related to usurping the property of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), whose right of disposal was in the hands of the Princess of the two worlds (s.a.) during the Prophet's lifetime. So, to shed light on all these aspects, we have with us today our dear brother, Mr. Mohammad Abbas Patel. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. First of all, we would like to know that the Holy Quran, the book in which everything is mentioned, what has been stated in the Holy Quran regarding this Fadak? So that through this, we can understand its background. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala... In Surah Bani Israil, verse 26, Allah (s.w.t.) commands His beloved: 'And give the relative his right.' So the question arises here, 'And give the relative his right'—who are these relatives in this verse who are so strongly emphasized to be given their right, and what is this right? That is, in the books of both our school and the Sunni school, this is a Mutawatir (consecutive) Hadith and it has been stated very clearly, and the Sunnis themselves... And in the Sunni books, if we study, then in this verse, 'relatives' refers to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and they have also considered themselves entitled to it. For example, in Tafsir Tabari, a narration is reported from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). Abu Dailam says that Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) said to a Syrian, 'Do you read the Holy Quran?' He said, 'Yes.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Have you read Surah Bani Israil?' He said, 'Yes.' Then the Imam drew his attention to this verse which was just recited, 'And give the relative his right.' 'Who is meant by this?' The Imam asked him, and he replied, 'Is it you?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Yes, it is us.' And we should also know that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) without any delay, under this command of Allah, gave the land of Fadak to Janabe Zahra (s.a.). And this is present in many Sunni books, such as in 'Shawahid al-Tanzil', under the verse 'And give the relative his right', Hakim Haskani says that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave Fadak to Fatima (s.a.). Besides this, Suyuti in 'Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur' has said under this same verse that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) called Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and gave her Fadak. This is also found in 'Musnad Abu Ya'la'. Yes, that is, we can say that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave Fadak to his only daughter, Janabe Zahra (s.a.), without any delay, in his own lifetime. And we can say that here, the reference you quoted, 'Musnad Abu Ya'la', an objection is raised that how can you accept this narration when there is a narrator in its chain named Atiyyah al-Awfi, who is a 'Dhaif' (weak) narrator? What is your answer to this? Actually, one thing should be clear to us and the viewers: the criteria for 'Dhaif' in the Sunni school is often that whenever a narrator says something against their established beliefs, they are immediately stamped as a 'Dhaif' narrator, even if it is the truth. Despite that, if someone says something against their core fundamentals, especially regarding Wilayah and Imamate, and here these disagreements... in the early history, it is recorded, and this is a very sensitive topic for them. Therefore, wherever... Therefore, wherever, for example, they say the same thing about Janabe Aban. Whereas in their own books, the authentication of Janabe Aban is also present. And the same thing is regarding Atiyyah al-Awfi. Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani says in his book 'Taqrib al-Tahdhib' that they consider Atiyyah al-Awfi 'Saduq' (truthful). Ibn Hajar states in 'Nata'ij al-Afkar', and he states the point I referred to in very clear words: 'The only reason for declaring Atiyyah weak is his Tashayyu (Shiism).' That is, his inclination towards Shiism. That is why the whole narrator becomes weak. The narrator immediately becomes weak. Wherever he brought things that are helpful for Shiism or strengthen Shiism or prove the arguments of Shiism, then immediately the label of 'Dhaif' is put on him. And Ibn Hajar further states, 'Wa nafsahu Saduq' (while he himself is truthful). Despite that, he is being called weak. 'Wa akhraja Bukhari fi Adab al-Mufrad' (Bukhari has recorded his Hadith in Adab al-Mufrad), and Abu Dawood records many Hadiths from him in his books. Those Hadiths which end with him. It is. Yes, Hasanuhu Tirmidhi, and other hadith. Tirmidhi has declared his hadiths as 'Hasan', meaning acceptable. So, we can say that out of the six (Sihah al-Sittah), there are about three authors who have declared him authentic. Absolutely, and they have declared his hadiths, the hadiths narrated from him, as Hasan. Apart from this, the other references that will be shown on the screen can also be used to understand whether Atiyyah was actually weak (da'if) or if he was only declared weak based on a belief, based on a creed. Yes, meaning based on some hadiths that he narrated, especially on this topic, the topic of Fadak. Al-Muhaqqiq al-Nahhasi has considered him 'Saduq' (truthful) in 'Imta al-Asma'. He says he is Saduq, meaning truthful, and in my opinion, his hadith is no less than the grade of Hasan, and Tirmidhi has declared many of his narrations as Hasan. Ibn Khuzaymah has also called him truthful, i.e., Saduq, in his book 'Al-Tawhid'. Ibn Sa'd goes one step further. Ibn Sa'd has said in his book 'Tabaqat al-Kubra', 'Wa kana thiqatan insha'Allah wa hadithuhu salih'—he is reliable (thiqah) insha'Allah, and his hadith is sound. This is one level above Saduq or Hasan. He declared him 'thiqah', meaning reliable, and called his hadith sound (sahih). Besides this, Al-Ijli has entered his name in his book 'Ma'rifat al-Thiqat' at entry number 125. What does he say about Atiyyah? 125. What does he say about Atiyyah? 'Tabi'i thiqah' (a reliable Tabi'i). So, on one hand, weakness is being attributed to him, and on the other hand, authors of such books are using terms like 'thiqah', 'saduq', and 'Hasan' for him. So, there are so many opinions present regarding him. Thus, it is quite clear why he is being declared weak—because he narrated some narrations on this topic, yes, which were sensitive topics, and he stated the truth there. Now, we would like to know that when the matter of the Garden of Fadak comes up, overall everyone knows that this was a land where the Jews lived, and they used to spend their daily lives in such a way that where there were date palm orchards, they used to generate their income through their cultivation. So, the question arises, how did the Muslims acquire this land of Fadak? It is a very interesting question, Atta Bhai, and a very important question. In various books of the Ahl al-Sunnah, we find how this land was acquired. Abu Dawud al-Sijistani brings a book in his Sunan, 'Kitab al-Kharaj wal-Imarah wal-Fay'. This is the name of the book. The book is Abu Dawud al-Sijistani's Sunan, it is Sunan Abu Dawud. And there is a book inside it whose name is this, 'Al-Kharaj wal-Imarah wal-Fay'. Inside it, the name is 'Al-Kharaj wal-Imarah wal-Fay', the book in which discussions regarding Kharaj, governorship, or Fay are present. In it, there is a chapter, 'Bab ma ja'a fi hukm ard Khaybar'. In it, he narrates the details. The narration is narrated by Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri from Abdullah bin Abu Bakr and some narrators from Muhammad bin Maslamah, meaning from their chain. These people say that when Khaybar was conquered, some people of Khaybar remained in that fort. In the fort of Khaybar, yes. Meaning it was not that Khaybar was just one fort. Khaybar consisted of various forts from before. There were various forts there. After reading history, it is understood that there were about five forts, out of which three were acquired through war, they were captured, and the two forts that remained, neither horses were galloped for them, nor camels, nor was any effort made. And the two that are brought under the ruling of 'Fay'—insha'Allah we will see its discussion—but these two forts were acquired in this way. So, some people remained in these forts, some people were left in these forts, and when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) besieged them, the Prophet's army besieged these people, then these people requested that we be exiled from here. We... meaning whatever wealth is here in this fort... We... meaning whatever wealth is here in this fort, we will leave it and go. Spare our lives. Yes, meaning we want to exit peacefully. They wanted to exit peacefully. So, these people exited from the remaining forts of Khaybar. When this news reached the people of Fadak, the people there also made a similar peace treaty with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). They tried to make this peace treaty as well, and we too want to save our lives and leave from here, from the land of Fadak. So, when they requested this peace treaty to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Prophet accepted their peace treaty, meaning he accepted their terms that 'go, save your lives and exit peacefully'. But the Prophet gave them permission to stay on half the land, on half the land of Fadak, with the condition that whenever the Muslims want, they can expel you from here. And the half who remained, the half who left from there, from the land of Fadak. Apart from this, Tabari has narrated this incident in great detail in his history. And regarding this land of Fadak and the land of Khaybar, how this land was acquired, regarding this he says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) gave the people of Khaybar their two forts, meaning these two forts that remained, Al-Watih and Al-Sullam, these are the names of the two forts which these two... Al-Sullam, these are the names of the two forts which these two forts, in which, meaning those acquired without war, these two forts, finally when they became convinced that they would be destroyed, they asked him to exile them, meaning the Prophet should exile them and spare their lives, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) accepted. And all these properties, meaning besides these, the other three forts which were Al-Shiqq, Natat, and Al-Katibah, yes, these total five forts were acquired, and the Prophet captured all these forts. These were the total, meaning three were captured through war, these two which remained—we mentioned in the beginning—these two remained, to whom peaceful exit was given, and these forts came into the Prophet's possession. So, the important factor here, the important point is that these two forts were acquired without war. Besides this, when the people of Fadak heard this news, when the people of Fadak heard this news, they also sent a message to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that you spare their lives. In exchange for this, the Prophet should take this land peacefully into his possession. Thus, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made a peace treaty with them for half of the land, on the condition that if we want to... For. On the condition that if we want to expel you from here, then you will have to leave. Then the people of Fadak made a peace treaty with him based on these conditions. So, the important thing here is, as Tabari has narrated, Khaybar became 'Mal-e-Ghanimah' (spoils of war) for the Muslims. What Tabari narrated, Khaybar became Mal-e-Ghanimah for the Muslims. And Fadak was purely the property of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) along with those two forts. Meaning why are we using the word 'purely'? Because there was no war here, there was no war to acquire this land of Khaybar, it came into the Prophet's possession peacefully. Yes, meaning from these two narrations you mentioned, we can draw some conclusions, which is that Fadak was purely for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). This is not part of Mal-e-Ghanimah. The reason for this is that camels and horses were not galloped for it. It was the sole property of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And in this, we can say we will discuss all these things. But the first question that arises is, when we use the word 'Mal-e-Ghanimah' and there is a word 'Fay', what is the difference between Mal-e-Ghanimah and Fay? When we want to know the difference between Fay and Mal-e-Ghanimah, let us turn to the Holy Quran, and in a very clear manner, the Holy Quran... And in a very clear manner, the Holy Quran has explained the difference between these two terms. For example, in Surah Al-Hashr, verse number 6: 'Wa ma afa Allahu 'ala rasulihi minhum...'. And the wealth that God has caused His Prophet to receive from them, you have no right in it, meaning He caused him to receive it without fighting, you have no right in it. And what is the reason for it? Because for this, you did not gallop horses, nor camels. Meaning the point here is, you did not make any effort. Yes, meaning the Muslims did not make any effort. Therefore, this is not Ghanimah. This is Fay. This is purely the property of the Messenger of Allah. Meaning that for which camels and horses were not galloped. For which the Muslims did not make any effort to acquire. So that will be classified into Fay, it is Fay, and the Muslims have no right in it. Yes, it is purely the property of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and Allah imposed it. Meaning in this verse, Allah is saying, 'Wa lakinna Allaha yusallitu rusulahu 'ala man yasha'—Allah imposed the Prophet's awe upon them, due to which they gave this property to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) without any war, without any effort, without galloping horses and camels. 'Wa Allahu 'ala kulli shay'in qadir'. So we saw that this verse is defining Fay in a very clear manner and is differentiating Fay from Mal-e-Ghanimah... And is differentiating Fay from Mal-e-Ghanimah and considering it separate. And the exegetes of the Ahl al-Sunnah themselves have said this in the context of this verse. For example, Razi brings in his Tafsir: Mal-e-Ghanimah is that for which horses and camels were galloped. And in contrast, Fay is called that for which no effort had to be made. And the land of Fadak is counted in Fay. Because we saw its history, how it was acquired. Therefore, it will be brought into the category of Fay. It will be categorized as Fay, not Mal-e-Ghanimah. And its direct result is that this was the Prophet's own personal property. It was purely the Prophet's property, and the Muslims had no interference in it. No authority, no ownership in it. Yes. And immediately after, as soon as this became the Prophet's property, as soon as the land of Fadak came into the Prophet's authority, the Prophet immediately gave it to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), which we saw the 'Shaan-e-Nuzul' (reason for revelation). So, therefore, this was the Prophet's personal property, which, according to Allah's command, the Prophet handed over to his daughter, his only daughter, Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and gifted it to her. And because the land of Fadak was so important, and this topic was so important, therefore Allah has also stated its expenditure in the immediate next verse in Surah... Expenditure in the immediate next verse in Surah Al-Hashr, verse number 7: 'Ma afa Allahu 'ala rasulihi min ahlil qura...'—meaning what Allah gave to the Prophet through the people of the city, meaning the land of Fadak, for whom? 'Fa lillahi wa lir-rasuli wa liz-zil qurba...'—for Allah, and for His Messenger, and for the relatives, and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer, 'kay la yakuna dulatan baynal aghniya'—so that this wealth does not remain only among the rich. Yes, among you. Therefore, Allah has also stated its expenditure here, that where to use this land, meaning whose right is it? Fakhr al-Razi says in the commentary of this verse: This verse was revealed regarding Fadak, which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had conquered without any fighting. Yes. So, the reality is that if we talk about the land of Fadak, the Quran itself is saying that it is the property of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), which we mentioned the verses of. And does this also mean that during the Prophet's own life, in his lifetime, Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the daughter of Fatima, was using it for her needs? Absolutely, meaning in the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... In the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the children of Fatima (s.a.) held possession of this land, and the children of Fatima (s.a.) used its income. Yes, meaning the Messenger used to spend on his family, especially Janabe Zahra (s.a.), he used to spend on them. The expenses for the whole year used to come out of this, and there was also some left over, which he used for others, meaning those mentioned in the verse above, verse number... so in which book is this found? In Sahih Bukhari, there is a statement of Hakim Sani: 'Wa kana al-Nabiyyu (s.a.w.a.)...'—meaning this 'Dada Batra' as it is called, this is not a sound chain, but because it is present like this, therefore we are reading it—'Wa kana al-Nabiyyu (s.a.w.a.) yusrifu 'ala ahlihi nafaqata sanatin...'—meaning the Prophet used to spend the expenses of the whole year for his family from this wealth, 'min hadhal mal, thumma yaj'alu ma baqiya...' and after that, what remained, he used for other works. Yes, this proves that Fadak was the Prophet's own personal property, which the Prophet, after the command of 'Wa ati dhal qurba haqqahu' came, gifted and gave to the Princess (s.a.). The word used in the hadith is 'Haba', meaning gifted. And in history, it is also found that the children of Fatima (s.a.) had possession of this in the Prophet's lifetime. Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili in his... was obtained. Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili mentions this in his book 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha'. He was a Mu'tazili, meaning he was from the Sunni sect. There were 11 date palm trees in that land, meaning the land of Fadak, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself had planted with his own hands. Yes, and the children of Fatima (a.s.) used to take their fruits. This shows their authority during the Prophet's lifetime. Not only that, he further states that when pilgrims (hujjaj) came to Medina, they (the children of Fatima) would give them these dates as a gift, and they would pray for them. This amounted to a very large sum; it was not a matter of a small piece of land. The income was very large. They themselves accept that the income from Fadak was very high. It was very high. This is in their own books. Apart from this, if you look at Sunni books, this matter has been stated very clearly. Yes. So, it is clear from all these traditions that this land was purely the property of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). It was his property. And as we saw in the initial discussion, it is proven from the Holy Quran that as soon as the verse 'Wa ati dhal-qurba haqqahu' (Give the relative his due) was revealed, he immediately, without any delay, gifted it to his daughter, his only daughter, Janabe Zahra (s.a.), by the command of Allah. by the command of Allah. So, this was not his inheritance; it was his property during the Prophet's lifetime, and how she used to spend its revenue on the pilgrims. So, the question arises, as it is written that its income was very high, we would like to know if you can provide some more references regarding its income. As far as the income and revenue are concerned, before the conquest of Khaybar, the Muslims did not even have enough to eat to their fill. Ibn Umar himself testifies to this in Sahih Bukhari: 'We did not eat to our fill until we conquered Khaybar.' The situation was so dire before Khaybar. Yes. And the opposite is also true, that after Khaybar, there was such an abundance of wealth for the Muslims that the entire state, the entire government's budget, was run by this. Only and only by these properties. Yes. Of course, in any state, the biggest budget is for defense, followed by social activities. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was doing both of these things from the income of Fadak. Meaning, the Islamic Empire of that era was run by Fadak. The entire government was established through the income of Fadak. And this is not our claim; Hakim al-Awwal himself has admitted this. Abu Bakr al-Jawhari has recorded this in his book 'Saqifah wa Fadak'. O Prophet... recorded this in his book 'Saqifah wa Fadak'. O Prophet, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to run the budget of his army from this. He used to prepare people with this wealth. 'Wa anfaqu fi sabilillah' (and spend in the way of Allah). So, not only the army budget but social schemes were also being run from this. Meaning, whatever the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was spending in the way of Allah, both these things were happening in the government. Fadak was the mainstay of the government of that era. All its income... the entire empire that was flourishing was due to the wealth of Fadak, the revenue of Fadak. And if you want to know its value, when the successor of the ruler (Hakim) expelled the Jews from this land and sent them towards Sham, the present-day Palestine, he paid 500 dirhams for half of the land—the part where the Jews were—when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had made a treaty with them that half the land was for them and we could remove them whenever we wanted. 500 dirhams in that era for half the land. If you look at the whole land, the valuation that was made... it might not even be accurate, we don't know how judicially and equitably this valuation was done. It is present in the books; Ibn Abi al-Hadid brought this in 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha'. Ibn Abi al-Hadid brought this in 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha', 500 dirhams for the valuation of half the land. So, for the whole land, it becomes 100,000 dirhams. If we consider one dirham to be 10 grams of silver, then according to today's value, it would be 100 crores. Yes, it becomes 100 crores. And the inflation on top of that is separate. If you apply that from that era, you can estimate that the value of just this land was huge. The income was separate. For so many years, the income was used to feed the Muslims, and the government's army was being maintained. The government's expenses were being paid from this. And then, Muawiya divided this land into three parts. He divided it into three parts and gave them to his governors. Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili also mentions this in 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha'. When Muawiya bin Abu Sufyan took over the caliphate, he gave one-third to Marwan bin al-Hakam, one-third to Amr bin Uthman (i.e., Amr bin Uthman bin Affan), and one-third to Yazid bin Muawiya. So, the land was split into three parts again and given to his own people, depriving those who had the right to it, and distributing it to those who had no right to it. distributed it to those who had no right to it. So, we can say that Fadak was a land that generated immense revenue in that era, and we can say that the entire empire was resting on this land. We can say that if its wealth were estimated in today's era with inflation, it would be impossible to estimate. Now, here too, we saw that as Ibn Abi al-Hadid said in his book 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha', Muawiya bin Abu Sufyan divided this land into three parts. We can see this because the ruler's son Yazid, and also Amr bin Uthman bin Affan and Marwan bin al-Hakam, were both governors. So, for example, if a wealthy person is already a governor, they should receive an amount that is beneficial to them. So, we can estimate its income even more—how much Fadak was... Exactly, the governors were given this land, it was providing benefits. Yes, so it certainly couldn't have been a small amount. It was not a small amount, nor was it a small property. And this was the reason why, immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), before the Prophet's funeral was even buried, the Saqifah occurred, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was usurped of his right. usurped of his right, as we all know. So, first of all, they targeted this financial backbone. As we see in some traditions, how the representatives (wukala) of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) were removed from that land. So, we would like to know how her representatives were removed from this land. As far as the removal of the Princess's (s.a.) representatives from this land is concerned, this matter is mentioned in very clear words in our books, and there is an indication of this in Sunni books as well. Yes, it was under her control. We have seen this in very clear words in the previous discussion that this land and property were under the control of the Princess (s.a.). Yes, and the income from it was also used by the children of Fatima (a.s.). There was also a claim by Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) that this is our land—Fadak is being referred to here—and this Fadak is our right. And how were they removed? As far as our books are concerned, for example, Allama Majlisi in 'Bihar al-Anwar' records a tradition from 'Kafi Sharif': 'Falam yazal wukalauha fiha hayata Rasulillah (s.a.w.a.)'—the representatives of the Princess (s.a.) were always present on this land during the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). present on this land during the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). 'Falamma waliya akhadha minha'—and when the ruler came to power and took the reins of the caliphate into his hands, he usurped it. 'Akhadha minha wa azala'—he removed the representatives of the Princess (s.a.) from the land of Fadak. Furthermore, in 'Ehtijaj', from Ammar bin Uthman, from Imam Abu Abdullah (a.s.) (Imam Sadiq (a.s.)), it is recorded: 'Lamma waliya wa istaqama amruhu 'ala jami' al-muhajirin wal-ansar'—as soon as he took over the reins of the caliphate and the Muhajirin and Ansar pledged allegiance to him, 'ba'atha ila Fadak'—he immediately sent his people to Fadak. To whom? To those who removed the representative of Fatima (a.s.). Meaning, the first thing he did upon coming to the seat of the caliphate was to break the financial backbone of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Yes, through which the government was running. Now, if you observe, this means that this land was not just a piece of land, nor was it a financial matter for which a small piece of land was being protested over, and for which... protested over, and for which an attempt was being made to usurp it, but rather the entire government depended on this land. Meaning, whoever is the rightful owner of this land will be the rightful owner of the government. Yes, the 'Wali al-Amr', if he has to sit on the government, if he has to prove himself as the 'Wali al-Amr', then this land was necessary for him so that he could cover his expenses. A state that does not have the power to cover its expenses, how will it run? That state—meaning the 'Wali al-Amr' in the ruler's sense, let's say—yes, in this sense, it was necessary for him to take this land under his control. Otherwise, the government's expenditures... he wouldn't be able to run the government. Meaning, the matter of this land is not just a dispute over a piece of land. It goes far beyond that. And the important point here is that if this land is not under his authority, if this is proven, then many truths will be unveiled. Just from this land. Yes, if this land was not his property and he usurped it, this is proven. That is why we see that this discussion never comes into the mainstream. The discussion of Fadak is never held. And whoever has done it, they are immediately labeled as 'Rawafid' or Shia, or... labeled as 'Rawafid' or Shia, or they try to suppress it, because this is a veil that, if lifted, all veils will be lifted at once. Yes, and as soon as the Princess (s.a.) had the land usurped—as soon as they usurped Fadak—the Princess (s.a.) expressed her displeasure, and until she left this world, she was angry with them. This is in Sahih Muslim, yes, in Sunni books, in their 'Sihah al-Sittah' (the six most authentic books), as the tradition is present there. Yes, tell our viewers, the tradition is narrated from Aisha. After the death of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), his daughter Bibi Fatima (s.a.) demanded from Abu Bakr her inheritance from Fadak, which Allah had bestowed upon him and which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had left for his family. But the matter is clear to everyone, and it is in the traditions that the Princess (s.a.) did not get her right, due to which the Princess (s.a.) was angry with them until she left this world. And this is a tradition of Bukhari, a tradition of Bukhari, such an authentic book. Yes, this makes it clear that when this tradition came in the book of Bukhari, there is no doubt that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was kept deprived of her right, and she was 'Siddiqa'... kept deprived of her right, and she was 'Siddiqa'. Yes, and if you look at it, on one side is the 'Siddiqa', and if we know the Princess (s.a.) as 'Siddiqa' in the true sense, then it is not permissible for us to consider the one who usurped her right as 'Siddiq'. If we are calling him 'Siddiq', then the direct result is that we are denying the Princess (s.a.). If she is 'Siddiqah', then viewers, this was our discussion today, where we learned about the importance and background of Fadak, how this land came into the possession of the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.), and what steps the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) took regarding this land in his lifetime, and that Bibi (s.a.) had the right of possession over this land during the Prophet's lifetime. And certainly, usurping Fadak was actually a failed attempt to extinguish the light of Wilayah, as Allah Almighty says in the Holy Quran: 'Yuriduna an yutfi'u nurallahi bi-afwahihim wallahu mutimmu nurihi wa law karihal-kafirun' (They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it). So, this was our episode today. Insha'Allah, we will meet again in this series. InshaAllah, we will meet again in the second episode of this series. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

chapters.title: The Historical Significance of Fadak
chapters.summary: This section introduces the historical context of Fadak, distinguishing between Maal-e-Ghanimat and Fay, and discusses its status as the Prophet's personal property gifted to Bibi Fatima (s.a.).

chapters.title: Quranic Basis and the Gift of Fadak
chapters.summary: The discussion explores the Quranic command in Surah Bani Israil to give relatives their rights, identifying this as the divine instruction for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to gift Fadak to Bibi Fatima (s.a.).

chapters.title: Addressing Narrator Reliability and Bias
chapters.summary: The speakers analyze the scholarly bias in Sunni hadith criticism, specifically regarding the narrator Atiyyah al-Awfi, who is often labeled weak solely due to his Shi'a leanings despite being considered truthful by many authorities.

chapters.title: Historical Acquisition of Khaybar and Fadak
chapters.summary: The lecture details how Khaybar and Fadak were acquired peacefully without military conflict, distinguishing them from spoils of war.

chapters.title: Distinguishing Fay from Mal-e-Ghanimah
chapters.summary: Using Quranic verses from Surah Al-Hashr, the speaker explains the legal distinction between Fay (property acquired without war) and Ghanimah.

chapters.title: Fadak as the Property of Janabe Zahra
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that Fadak was the Prophet's personal property, which he gifted to his daughter, Fatima (s.a.), as commanded by Allah.

chapters.title: Evidence of Fatima's Possession
chapters.summary: Historical accounts and hadith confirm that the Prophet used the income from Fadak for his family's needs and that Fatima (s.a.) held possession during his lifetime.

chapters.title: The Economic Significance of Fadak
chapters.summary: Fadak was a highly productive land gifted to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), serving as a major source of revenue for the early Islamic state.

chapters.title: Valuation and Political Misuse of Fadak
chapters.summary: The immense wealth of Fadak supported the Islamic government's military and social expenses, but it was later divided among governors by Muawiya.

chapters.title: Usurpation of Fadak and Its Implications
chapters.summary: The removal of Janabe Zahra's representatives from Fadak was a strategic move to undermine the financial independence of the Ahlulbayt and consolidate political power.

chapters.title: Historical Evidence of Fadak
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the historical documentation of the usurpation of Fadak in Sunni sources, specifically Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

chapters.title: The Status of Siddiqa and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The discussion explores the theological implications of Bibi Fatima's (s.a.) status as Siddiqa and how the denial of her right relates to the broader concept of Wilayah.

title: Majlis 9 | Ahle Bait (a.s) Par Durood-o-Salawaat Ka Sawaab | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual significance of reciting Salawat upon the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and its role as a bridge for prayer acceptance. The discourse connects these devotional practices to the core pillars of Wilayah and Bara'ah, emphasizing their necessity for a believer's spiritual journey. Through the heart-wrenching narrative of the tragedy of Karbala, including the final farewells and the martyrdom of Ali Asghar, the speaker highlights the ultimate sacrifices made by the family of the Prophet (PBUH) for the sake of truth.
content:
[Music] Upon the corpse of... [Music] O Lord, may the support of no poor person be broken. O Lord, may the support of no poor person be broken, from the veils of sisters. May fate not be hostile [Music], O Lord, may the protector of every veil be safe. Sleeping in the lap of [Music]... I have endured the grief of the martyrs of the religion [Music]. I will never forget the grief of two brothers in my lifetime. One brother was lost in the clutches of the army of Sham [Music], and the other fell asleep on the banks of the Euphrates. My inner [Music]... may there be no calamity, O Lord, may no brother be separated from a sister. Zainab (s.a.) wept and said over the corpse of Shabbir (a.s.), 'Caravan of captivity, wait a moment. A lion of mine is sleeping on the riverbank. I will go from the corpse of Hussain (a.s.) to the river, I will show Abbas (a.s.) his bound arms.' When the sister of Hussain (a.s.) went towards Alqama, it is written she was bareheaded, the daughter of Haider-e-Ali. 'O people, destroy my existence from the earth, pick me up and bury me in the grave of the strangers. O helplessness, take me into your lap, O honor, hide me somewhere in your lap. O sky, take me into your lap, move aside, O earth, take me into your lap. How will I see the unveiled one on the Euphrates? The lady is coming with her head uncovered to the Euphrates [Music].' When Zainab (s.a.) saw Alqama from afar, the daughter of Ali (a.s.) When the sorrowful one heard the Alqama, the lion of Ali (a.s.), she looked here and there with great longing. The eyelids were fluttering, and on the riverbank, two severed arms were twitching. The moment the daughter of Ali (a.s.) reached the riverbank [Music], she called out to Abbas (a.s.) and fell upon the corpse. A stream of tears flowed from her eyes. Seeing this, the brave one felt great pain. Tears were in his eyes, but his lips were sealed. Zainab's (s.a.) hands were tied behind her neck. When she stood up, reciting Nad-e-Ali, the grief-stricken sister said, 'Tell me, with the rope pressed into your blood, Abbas, my brother, my lion of the battlefield,' Rope, Abbas, my brother, my lion of the battlefield. After being looted and becoming a captive in the name of the Panjtan, the veil was lost in the army of Sham. The sister of 18 brothers is imprisoned. Tell me something of yourself, what is your condition?' As if with great respect, the corpse of the loyal one said [Music], 'Accept my salutation, daughter of Fatima (s.a.). What should I do? I am in great pain. What should I do? I am in great pain. A lady is weeping over my corpse with her head uncovered. She is sorrowful, she is mourning, she is helpless, and she is weeping and calling out to the water-bearer.' [Music] Zainab (s.a.) writhed and said, 'She is very grief-stricken.' Zainab (s.a.) writhed and said, 'She is very grief-stricken. Abbas, know that she is my mother Fatima (s.a.).' [Music] 'Abbas, know that she is my mother Fatima (s.a.). Even in the grave, Fatima (s.a.) will not sleep in peace.' At Zainab's (s.a.) words, the command of the oppressors came, the army of Yazid moved away from the river. The silence was filled with pain. Arif, saying this, Zainab (s.a.) clung to her brother. 'Let me mourn over the corpse of my devoted one, let me weep to my heart's content over the corpse of my brother. O Lord, may no brother be separated from a sister.' In the tent, When the King (a.s.) said goodbye, a cry of lamentation arose. The one who was awaited is near, the day is fading, the day of calamity is near. It is a matter of a few moments, the Day of Judgment is near. The departure of Zainab's (s.a.) poor brother is near. A cry of lamentation arose. A cry of lamentation arose. When the King (a.s.) came to the tent and said goodbye, a cry of lamentation arose. A cry of lamentation arose. Moving a little away, the King (a.s.) said in the tent, 'Raising her bound arms, the sister of the broken-bodied one was weeping.' When the brother began to kiss the sister's arms. A cry went up, a cry went up [Music] When the Shah (Imam Hussain) came to the tent and said farewell, a cry went up, a cry went up [Music] Hearing this, the daughter of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was distressed, 'Today I remembered the words of my mother' [Music] Zainab (s.a.) stepped forward and kissed the throat of her brother when The throat was kissed, a cry went up [Music] A cry went up. When the Shah came to the tent and said farewell, a cry went up, a cry went up [Music] He began to say to his daughter again, 'O beloved of Fatima, stay with your aunt, she will take care of your questions, otherwise your father will be very troubled,' then placing his hand on her head, he began to give blessings. A cry went up [Music] When the Shah came to the tent and said farewell, a cry went up [Music] A cry went up. When he had entrusted his daughter to his sister, the Imam wept and said to his sister, 'O heavenly abode [Music] Go to your homeland after being released from captivity, thirsty [Music] The mention of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) came to his lips, a cry went up A cry went up. When he came to the tent and said, a cry went up, a cry went up [Music] He began to say to Abid (Imam Sajjad) again, 'O Shah of Karbala, you are now the support of the widows and orphans. Whatever my trial was, I have fulfilled it all.' It happened, a cry went up, a cry went up. She came weeping near Hussain (a.s.) and then holding the stirrup, she said, 'O Shah of the religion [Music] Let me mount, Abbas is not at home [Music].' The beloved of Zahra (s.a.) mounted, a cry went up, a cry went up. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, La hawla wa la quwwata... Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azim, Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man nasir, al-hamdulillahi rabbil alamin, wa salatu wa salamu ala ashrafil mursalin, habibi ilahil alamin, Abul Qasim [Music] Muhammad sallallahu alayhi wa alihi [Music]... [Music] Mawlana wa habibi [Music] ... [Music] ... [Music] ... [Music] ... [Music] ... [Music] ... Amin, Rabbil Alamin. This is the last Majlis of the Majlis series, the Majlis of the night of Ashura. The topic was Wilayah and Bara'ah, and the effort was to present a few traditions of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in your service so that it becomes clear to the youth and the young ones what our responsibilities are regarding these two important pillars of religion, Usul al-Din and Furu al-Din, which are called Wilayah and Bara'ah. Today, a few things in your service, very quickly, and it is the night of Ashura, then we will move towards the stage of Masaib, Insha'Allah [Music]. The first thing is that we should make Salawat very common in our society. The reason is that we see that the things our elders taught us—that in everything, at all times, try to keep sending Salawat—this is decreasing among us now. Therefore, make this as common as possible. Just two traditions in this regard, I present in your service. Although there is a whole discussion on Salawat, a very detailed discussion, but I will present only two Hadith in your service. Please recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad [Music]. The Hadith is from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) that he says the Prophet of God (s.a.w.a.) said, 'There is no prayer except that there is a veil between that prayer and the sky, until the Prophet Muhammad and the family of Muhammad are blessed [Music]. When the person praying sends Salawat, this veil is torn, and the prayer enters the sky.' Entering the sky is used as a metaphor, meaning it implies that the prayer is accepted. 'And when he prays without Salawat, the prayer is turned back,' meaning the prayer is not accepted. So, for the acceptance of prayer, the most important thing is Salawat upon... For the acceptance of prayer, the most important thing is Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Now, the second Hadith I am going to recite in your service, the entire concept is contained in it because usually people say, 'We don't recite that many Tasbih of Salawat; we recite, for example, Tasbih al-Arba'a, we do this, we do that.' Yes, people don't recite the Tasbih of Salawat. People say, 'This is better, that is better.' Now you see the tradition narrated by Allama Majlisi in Bihar al-Anwar and from Mar'at al-Anwar al-Yaqin, which is the book of Hafiz al-Barsi, about whom I told you that he was a great devotee (Muwali) and about whom Allama Majlisi himself says that he used to exaggerate a lot regarding Wilayah, and Allama Amini defended him and said that he did not exaggerate; whatever he stated is one hundred percent correct, there is nothing wrong in his statements. Allama Amini, defending him, narrates that the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) said, the Prophet says... It is narrated that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: When Allah created the Arsh (Throne), He created 70,000 angels along with it. Allah commanded them, 'Perform Tawaf of the Light of the Arsh, which is the light of the Arsh, and glorify Me (Tasbih), and carry My Arsh.' Observe this carefully at every stage—Allah commanded them to perform Tawaf, glorify Him, and carry the Arsh. They performed the Tawaf and the Tasbih, and they intended to lift the Arsh, but they were unable to do so. You noticed that 70,000 angels, despite the power and strength Allah granted them, could not lift the Arsh. Then Allah commanded them again, 'Perform the Tawaf of the Arsh.' Perform the Tawaf of the Arsh, and send blessings (Salawat) upon the Light of My Majesty, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). When you perform the Tawaf, do not just perform the Tawaf; along with the Tawaf, keep sending blessings upon My beloved, the light of My majesty, Muhammad. And then, carry My Arsh. They complied with Allah's command because angels are infallible and they follow Allah's command. They sent blessings, and after sending blessings, they lifted the Arsh, and they were able to carry it. They said, 'O our Lord, You commanded us to glorify You and sanctify You, and despite our glorification and sanctification, we could not lift the Arsh, but when this matter of Salawat came...' They could not lift the Arsh, but when the matter of Salawat came and You commanded us to recite Salawat, we were able to lift the Arsh. So Allah replied to them, 'O My angels, when you send blessings upon My beloved Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), it is not just a blessing; rather, in this blessing, there is My glorification, My sanctification, and My exaltation. Everything is present in it.' That is, the collection of all worship is the Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. But we send ordinary Salawat, like you are sending now, 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad,' and then stop. And if one wants to increase it, one should say more, one should pray for the reappearance of the Imam, but along with that, there should be more. The Master of the Faithful (a.s.) was performing Tawaf, and the Master of the Faithful objected to a person. When that person was performing the first Tawaf, he was sending Salawat, so the Master of the Faithful greeted him. The Master of the Faithful greeted him and prayed for him briefly. But when he passed by the Master of the Faithful a second time, the Master of the Faithful did not greet him nor pray for him. He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, when I was performing the first circuit, you greeted me and prayed for me; now you neither greeted me nor prayed for me.' He said, 'You did not fulfill our right.' He asked, 'I am sending Salawat.' He replied, 'You are sending Salawat, but you are not sending curses (Lanat) upon our enemies.' This is the right of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, exactly as I presented the Hadith in your service that day, that Allah said He will not accept Wilayah unless Bara'ah (disassociation) is with it. Similarly, the Salawat will not be complete unless there is Lanat in it. Then you recite Salawat upon Muhammad. See, many people are afraid to express these things; there is nothing to be afraid of. This is our worship, this is our principle of religion, this is the foundation of religion. If it bothers someone, let it bother them; the Quran says in every matter... The Jews and the Christians will not be pleased with you until you follow their religion. You will follow their religion; they will be pleased with you only when you follow their religion. Therefore, this is why people are afraid here—'Oh no, how can we do this? How can we say this?' And nowadays there is a new thing, let it be. Send one more loud Salawat. Now it is the eve of Ashura. We have discussed Wilayah and Bara'ah so far. Now, what is the essence of this Wilayah and Bara'ah? How should the summary be stated? How can our responsibility towards our Imam be stated? Just as people abandoned Imam Hussain (a.s.), if our Imam calls us today, 'Hal min nasir,' will we also abandon him? The question is, if the Imam calls today, if the Imam raises his voice, then see, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) stated in two or three sentences how a believer is... Stated how a believer is connected to his Imam. See, there is a powerful narration present in Al-Kafi, which I presented in your service, that Muhammad ibn Tahr, who was the teacher of Sheikh Kulayni, narrated from some people who narrated from Harun ibn Sadaqah, and Harun ibn Sadaqah narrated directly from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam says that the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) said: 'Do not commit betrayal regarding the right of your Imam. Fulfill the promise you made to your Imam; never betray it.' Or breach of trust, breach of oath—the promise made, the trust we have, and this trust is Wilayah. Never betray this Wilayah, or hold this Wilayah with great strength... Hold this Wilayah with great strength. Iblis has various tactics to weaken this Wilayah; there are different ways. This is not the time or place to present the various methods of Iblis in your service, but regardless, Allama Majlisi, in Bihar al-Anwar, has mentioned the tactics and tricks of Iblis on approximately 200 pages. In the 60 volumes of Bihar al-Anwar, in volume 6, from page 131 to page 326, approximately 200 pages—five pages less—Allama Majlisi mentions only the tricks of Iblis. What is his strategy? What are his methods? How does he mislead? Because the thing that is most hateful to Iblis—see, he will mislead the one who is on the Straight Path (Sirat al-Mustaqim). He said to Allah, 'I will sit on the Straight Path.' He will mislead the one who is walking on the Straight Path; what will he mislead the one who is not walking on it? Why kill the dead? Iblis knows, and who is walking on the Straight Path? The one who is connected to his Imam, who is committed to his Imam. 'Do not betray this,' meaning remember your Imam morning and evening, especially... Meaning remember your Imam morning and evening, especially since it is the eve of Ashura. On the day of Ashura, until the evening of Sham-e-Ghariban, keep offering condolences to Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Keep saying 'Ajjarakallahu,' may Allah reward you for this great tragedy. I don't know where the Imam of the Time is, where he is weeping. Do not forget your Imam even for a moment. Allama Amini (r.a.) used to say that on the eve of Ashura and the day of Ashura, give charity on behalf of Imam-e-Zamana, because he is watching the entire scene of Ashura with his own eyes. We hear it and tears flow from our eyes, even though we are just listening, and we are not infallible, and we do not have the faith we should have, but still, we are weeping because we love the Ahlulbayt. And think, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is watching with his own eyes, so it would be no surprise if his heart were to burst. Allama Amini says that Imam-e-Zamana... Allama Amini says, take great care of the Imam of the Time. Pray for the health of the Imam of the Time. It is truly a Day of Judgment. So the Master of the Faithful says, 'Do not deceive your guides, your Imams.' As if the Master of the Faithful is seeing the scene, he sees how the Ummah will deceive its guides. Never deceive the Imam of the Time. And if you read it as 'la tajhalu,' it means never be ignorant about your Imam. Have recognition (Ma'rifah) of your Imam. If you do not recognize your Imam, if there is no Ma'rifah, then you will be misled. You will die the death of an ignorant person; it will be a death of disbelief, hypocrisy, and misguidance. And if you read it as 'la tajalu,' it means never say to your Imam, 'O Master, you do not understand my situation, you do not understand my problem,' just as many people stated their excuses to Imam Hussain (a.s.). Stated their excuses to Imam Hussain (a.s.). One aspect of the oppression of the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) is that it is not that the Master of Martyrs did not address the people; it is not that he did not explain it to them. From Medina to Mecca, and from Mecca to Karbala, along the way, at many stops and stages, the Master of Martyrs was repeatedly addressing the people, but no one was ready to listen to him, and every person was busy trying to fix their own worldly affairs. Here he says, 'Do not do this with your Imams.' And finally, he says, 'Do not loosen this strong rope of Allah, do not abandon it.' This strong rope of Allah, 'Habl-ul-Matin,' this strong rope of Allah, do not abandon it, do not loosen it. It should not be that you leave its company. This is the Imam, the Imam of the time. From the Master of the Faithful (a.s.) to the last Imam, every Imam was the strong rope of Allah. Do not abandon it. The Master of the Faithful is saying, what will be the consequence? He says the consequence will be, if you abandon it, you will deviate from the Straight Path. If you deviate from the straight path, you will slip, you will wander, and you will become weak. If you deviate from the straight path, you will be destroyed, and your dignity will be lost; your honor will be gone. Hazrat Amir (a.s.) has taken this from verse 46 of Surah Al-Anfal, in which Allah (s.w.t.) says: 'Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute with one another, lest you lose courage and your strength (dignity) departs.' The word used is 'rih', meaning your wind or your dignity—it will vanish, it will end. 'Wa-s-biru' (and be patient)—look, one must be patient on this path. This path of 'tamassuk' (holding fast) requires a lot of patience. If Allah is not testing someone on this path, then understand that it means they are not truly on this path; their 'tamassuk' is not correct if they are not being tested. If there is no test, and if they are truly on the path, then they will certainly be tested. Just as Ammar's test was, just as Maytham al-Tammar's test was, just as Hujr's test was, just as Muhammad bin Abi Bakr's test was. Read the biography of each one of them; what kind of tests they endured. When Muawiyah found out that Ammar bin Humran was a fugitive, he gave orders to find him anywhere. He was a staunch lover of the Master of the Universe (a.s.). When they could not find Janab-e-Ammar, Muawiyah did something: he arrested his wife and threw her into prison, spreading the news that his wife was in their custody and that if he did not surrender, they would kill her. Ammar (r.a.) could not bear this, and his sense of honor did not allow it, so he immediately surrendered himself to the government. He was likely arrested in Mosul, Iraq. He was arrested in Mosul, Iraq. When he was arrested, Muawiyah's agents wrote to Muawiyah saying that Ammar bin Humran had been arrested and asking what should be done with him. Muawiyah said, 'Cut off his head. Behead him, raise his head on a spear, parade it through all the markets, and announce that this will be the fate of anyone who opposes Muawiyah.' This was the first head in Islam to be paraded; it was the first head to be raised on a spear. This became a Sunnah—the Sunnah of Banu Umayyah—which the followers of the 'shajar-e-khabeeth' (the cursed tree) of Banu Umayyah are still following to this day. They still do the same. So, the head was paraded in the market and then brought to Sham. When it was brought to Sham, Muawiyah said, 'Go and throw it into the lap of Ammar bin Humran's wife.' Look at these executioners; they were not Muslims, they were not even human, let alone Muslims. They brought Ammar bin Humran's head and threw it into the lap of his wife, who was in prison at the time. As soon as she saw the head, she fainted. When she regained consciousness, she kissed the head of her husband and said, 'Ammar, I am proud that I am your wife. I am proud that I am your spouse. I am the wife of such a brave and courageous man, the wife of such a man of honor.' These were the sacrifices for which they gave their lives, like Janab-e-Hujr, and the list is very long. If we are not being tested on this path, it means we need to hold on even more firmly, to strengthen our love even more, so that the matter becomes clear. Then the Master of the Universe (a.s.) says, 'Look, your entire life should be based on this Wilayah and Bara'ah.' 'Ta'sis' means foundation; all your affairs should be based on this Wilayah and this Bara'ah. Whatever work one does in the world, one should see if it relates to Wilayah and Bara'ah or not. Is it not a hindrance on the path? The Master says if anyone has an objection... The Master says if anyone has an objection, go and ask. 'Wa haza tariqa'—look, remain committed to this path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), do not leave this path, no matter what happens. 'Wa haza tariqa fa-qum'—because if you could see what those who have died before you have seen, you would rush towards this matter. If you could see the results of Wilayah, what its consequences are, you would rush towards it. You would certainly hear, you would understand. The importance of this Azadari you are performing, if the veil of this world were lifted, you would know it then. But those whom we call dead... But those whom we call dead, those who have left this world, they are seeing what has been hidden from you. And soon, this veil will be lifted from you too. Soon, you too will face death, and then you will understand the importance and the virtue of this Azadari, this mourning, and this weeping. What is the true reward of this? The Master of the Universe (a.s.) is saying, do not leave this easily. I am completing my topic very quickly because today is the last Majlis. Whoever remains with their Imam of the time will be successful, and whoever leaves the mantle of their Imam of the time will never find success. They might appear successful in worldly terms, but in reality, they will never be successful. That is why this Majlis and mourning have so much importance. The reason is that you are wearing black clothes, saying 'Ya Hussain, Ya Hussain'... So do not leave this Azadari, and hold firmly to the mantle of your Imam of the time. Do not leave your Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) even for a moment. And all year round—and that is why our scholars emphasize this Azadari, and we have witnessed it ourselves, which we are telling you—in the month of Ramadan, in some centers, there are scholarly debates at night. Every night, starting from the night of the moon, there are scholarly or jurisprudential debates. We have seen and witnessed this ourselves; we are not talking about hearsay. That scholarly debate goes on for about 40-45 minutes, discussing different issues daily. But at the end, when the debate finishes, for five to seven minutes, a person recites the Masaib of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.). This is how much the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) value it, and how much our scholars value it—not just in Muharram, but every day in the month of Ramadan, the Masaib of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.). Think about it; this is called 'tassuk' (holding fast), and we should learn this from our scholars. And we should learn this from our scholars; this is their Seerah, their way. And this is what happens here in India too, that after every Majlis, there are Masaib, even if it is a Majlis for the reward of someone else, the mention of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) is there, the mention of his Masaib, the mention of Karbala. Do not even think of separating this from your life for a single moment. And in the Seerah of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.), in the words that Tawus narrated, a sentence is recorded that when Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) was leaving for Karbala, he gave a sermon. In that sermon, he said, 'Whoever is ready to shed their blood with us on our path, let them prepare their soul for death.' 'Maut' (death)—they say 'tadeen' (to accustom). Accustom yourself to death. We are not worried about death. The same dream that Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) was seeing on the path, he opened his eyes and said, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. Janab-e-Ali Akbar asked, 'Father, what is the reason for reciting this?' Janab-e-Ali Akbar asked, 'Father, what is the reason for reciting this?' He said, 'I just dozed off and saw in a dream that someone was saying that these people are walking, and death is walking ahead of them.' Now look at the education—what is the education of the youth and children of Banu Hashim? Look at what they received in their homes. It is amazing. 'Ya abati, alasta 'ala al-haqq?' (Father, are we not on the truth?) 'Bala' (Yes). 'Idhan la nubali' (Then we do not care about death). Whether we go towards death or death comes upon us. 'Fal-yamsi ma'ana' (Then let them walk with us)—only those who are ready to shed their blood and those who are ready for death should walk with us. Meaning, walking with us, walking with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), is not the work of the faint-hearted; it is not the work of the small-hearted. Walking with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—and that is why on the night of Ashura, Imam Hussain (a.s.) asked Janab-e-Qasim, 'Kaifa al-mawt?' How is death for you? A 13-year-old child—what would he know about death? You ask any 13-year-old child today. But this was no ordinary child; he was the beloved of Hassan (a.s.), he was the son of Hassan (a.s.), a child of Banu Hashim. What a sentence, what an answer, what a powerful answer! 'Kaifa al-mawt?'—'Beta (son), how is death near you?' When he was weeping, Janab-e-Qasim's name was not on the list. He replied, 'Ahla min al-asal' (Sweeter than honey). Have you noticed? Look at the two answers from the youth of Banu Hashim: one answer from the son of Imam Hussain (a.s.), one answer from the son of Imam Hassan (a.s.). This is the upbringing of Banu Hashim, this is the style. And the third answer—if you hear the third answer, it was such a قیامت (apocalyptic) answer that the world is still amazed by it today. When the three-pronged arrow hits even a great warrior, he would fall clutching his chest, but this six-month-old child, this Banu... But this six-month-old child, this child of Banu Hashim, smiled in his father's lap. It is the night of Ashura. Before reciting the Masaib (tragedy) of Janab Ali Asghar (a.s.), I offer you the opportunity to weep; this is a night of mourning. On the night of Ashura, Imam Hussain (a.s.) went towards the battlefield. Suddenly, he felt footsteps. He turned and saw Hilal. He asked, 'Yes, Mawla?' He said, 'Why are you following me?' He replied, 'I fear that some coward might attack you.' Now the Imam is moving forward with Hilal. 'Mawla, why are you coming to this place tonight?' He said, 'I am looking at the place of slaughter. Who will be martyred where? Hilal, here Habib will be killed. Hilal, here Muslim will be killed.' The Imam was pointing out each spot of martyrdom: 'Here this one will be martyred, there that one will be martyred.' Then, as he continued, 'Hilal, here my Ali Akbar will be killed, here my Abbas will be killed.' As the Imam was pointing out the places of martyrdom, he suddenly began to descend into a valley. Just as he was descending, the Imam stopped Hilal. 'Hilal, just stop here. This is your limit.' He asked, 'Why, Mawla?' He said, 'My mother Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is cleaning that valley where my head will be separated from my body.' May Allah grant you reward, O servants of Allah. The Imam returned towards the tents. Once he went into the tent of Janab Zainab (s.a.). Janab Zainab (s.a.) was restless. What was the reason for this restlessness? The reason was that she had already asked the question: 'Brother, these companions of yours, have you tested their loyalty? Will they stand by you?' Before the Imam could answer, Habib was standing outside, and the voice reached his ears. Habib was standing outside, and the voice reached his ears. Habib was deeply moved. 'O Ansar-e-Hussaini, come out of your tents! Come out of your tents! The daughter of Ali and Fatima (s.a.) does not believe in our loyalty.' Habib took off his turban and cried out, 'O Princess, if you command us now, we will cut our own throats with our swords!' How loyal were the Ansar-e-Hussaini! These were the events of the night of Ashura. The morning of Ashura dawned, and one by one they were martyred. The sequence began until the afternoon of Ashura arrived, and everyone was martyred. All the young men of Banu Hashim were martyred; no one was left. When no one was left, the Imam raised his voice: 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna?' Is there anyone among you who will defend the harem of the Messenger of Allah? Is there anyone among you who will defend the harem of the Messenger of Allah? When no answer came from the battlefield, there was an uproar in the Imam's camp. Hussain (a.s.) went to the tent. 'Sister, what is this uproar?' 'Brother, you raised your voice so loudly that Asghar threw himself out of the cradle.' 'Sister, bring Asghar to me.' 'Brother, he is not coming into anyone's lap; you come and see for yourself.' Hussain (a.s.) came into the tent and stood by the cradle. I do not know what the father said and what the son understood, but it is written that Asghar came into Hussain's lap. Hussain took Asghar and started walking. When he reached the tent door, Rubab was standing there. 'Rubab, why are you standing here?' 'I am watching; whoever has gone since morning has not returned, so I thought I would see my little son one last time. It might be the last glimpse.' Hussain consoled her, 'No, Rubab, whoever has gone to the battlefield so far has gone on his own feet.' Whoever has gone to the battlefield has gone on his own feet. Six-month-old children are not taken to the battlefield. Hussain's consolation did not work. Hussain brought him and stood on high ground and said, 'O people, is there any Muslim among you?' No one answered. Then Hussain asked a second question, 'Is there anyone among you who has children? My child has been thirsty for three days.' Hearing Hussain's voice, a revolution was about to break out in the ranks of the enemy. They were hiding their faces and crying, when suddenly Ibn Sa'd said, 'Where is Harmala? Harmala, come forward!' Harmala came forward. Sa'd said, 'O Harmala, cut short Hussain's speech.' Harmala took a three-headed arrow and aimed at Asghar's throat. He aimed at Asghar's throat. It was a three-headed arrow; it struck Asghar's throat. The child was slaughtered. When Hussain saw the child, there was a smile on his face. Hussain began to weep bitterly. He took Ali Asghar's blood and threw it towards the first heaven. The heaven refused to accept it; the earth refused to accept it. Hussain smeared Ali Asghar's blood on his own face. 'I will meet my grandfather on the Day of Judgment in this state and say, O Grandfather, these two killed me.' He started walking towards the tent with the body of Ali Asghar. Just a few sentences—you have wept enough, and keep weeping. It is the night of Ashura. Now he is walking towards the tent. Hussain is thinking, 'I had promised to give him water; how will I show him to his mother now?' He takes seven steps forward... How will I show him to his mother now? He takes seven steps forward, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' Hussain repeated this action seven times. He went forward and came back, went forward and came back. Hussain decided that since the child had departed from this world, why deprive the mother of a last glimpse? Hussain came to the tent door and called, 'Rubab!' Rubab came from one side, but Sakina came from the other. Sakina came running, 'Baba, are you giving Ali Asghar water? Are you giving my brother water?' Hussain did not answer, but when Rubab arrived, Hussain turned the hem of his cloak. As soon as he turned the hem, Rubab saw the scene that may Allah never show any mother: a six-month-old child with a three-headed arrow stuck in his throat. Rubab beat her chest... A six-month-old child with a three-headed arrow stuck in his throat. Rubab beat her chest and slapped her face. She recited a dirge, 'O my son, are children like you slaughtered?'

title: Jannat Aur Badkalaami
excerpt: This lecture highlights a profound Hadith from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) regarding the spiritual dangers of foul language. It emphasizes that the use of abusive speech and a lack of shame are barriers to entering Paradise. The speaker concludes with a prayer for protection against such destructive behavior.
content:
The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Verily, Allah has made Paradise forbidden for the person who uses foul language, who has no shame, and who does not care what he is saying or what is being said about him.' We pray to Allah to keep us safe from this worst of deeds. Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Zameen-e-Karbala Ki Afzaliyat [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the unique spiritual status and sanctity of the land of Karbala in Shia theology. The speaker highlights traditions suggesting that Karbala is considered superior to the Holy Kaaba, having been chosen by Allah before the creation of the world. The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi and the hope that believers may be among his companions in seeking justice for Imam Hussain.
content:
We are getting an opportunity in Shimla Dhalli, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, Assalamu Alaikum. Assalamu Ya Hussain. Hazrat Imam Hussain (a.s.) said that Karbala is a land that Allah has chosen as a sacred and blessed land. It is more sacred than the Holy Kaaba, because before Allah (s.w.t.) created the world, He chose this land of Karbala. When the Day of Judgment arrives, this land of Karbala will be raised in such a state that it will be pure and holy, and it will be placed in one of the most excellent gardens of Paradise. It will be considered the best place, and no one will reside there except the Prophets and the chosen ones. This land of Karbala will shine among the gardens of Paradise just as the sun shines among the stars in the sky. It will shine just as the sun appears as the brightest star among all the stars in the sky. Its light will dazzle the eyes of all the inhabitants of Paradise. See, this land of Karbala is the sacred and blessed land of Allah that held Sayyid al-Shuhada and Sayyid al-Shabab (Imam Hussain) in its embrace. From this Hadith of Hazrat Imam Sajjad (a.s.), it is absolutely clear that the land of Karbala cannot be compared to any other land, even the blessed land of the Holy Kaaba, which Allah designated as His house and commanded all Muslims to face during prayer. But Karbala is superior. We pray that Allah grants us all the opportunity to visit it. When our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), reappears, he will emerge from the wall of the Holy Kaaba and will call out for the revenge of his grandfather, Imam Hussain (a.s.). May we be among his companions. Ameen Ya Rabbul Alameen. [Music] Royal Bullet, [Music]

excerpt: This lecture introduces a new 15-episode educational video series titled 'Panaah-e-Kainaat,' focused on the life and reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The speaker highlights the current state of global oppression and the promise of ultimate justice through the Imam's return, citing traditional Islamic sources. Viewers are invited to participate in a quiz series organized by 'Bana-e-Karbala' to deepen their knowledge of the 12th Imam.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu Alaikum. There is no city, town, or region in the world today where there is no one in distress. Poverty and hardship are spread everywhere. Moreover, oppressive governments, through their arbitrary actions, are under the illusion that there is no one to stop them and no one to curb their oppression. But this will not last. The era of oppression will end; justice will prevail in the world. Every petitioner will find a responder, and the oppressed will receive their rights. This will only happen when the 12th and final successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), reappears. The famous scholar, Sulaiman Qunduzi, in his book 'Yanabi al-Mawadda', Chapter 94, page 547, narrates a Hadith from Abu Saeed Khudri on the authority of Muhammad al-Hamswini. Narrating a Hadith from Abu Saeed Khudri, in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'I give you the glad tidings of Mahdi, who will appear in my Ummah when people are filled with discord and strife. He will fill the earth with justice and equity just as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. All the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will be pleased with him, and he will distribute wealth among the people in a just manner.' Keeping this Hadith in mind, the 'Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Quiz' series is being presented by the team of 'Bana-e-Karbala'. This video series will consist of 15 episodes related to Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The most important thing is that all the discussions in these videos will be based on the books of reliable scholars with evidence. So, let us make this month memorable and increase our knowledge by participating in this 'Bana-e-Karbala' quiz. If you have any questions regarding this quiz... If you have any questions regarding this quiz, message us on our WhatsApp number [number removed]. May Allah hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the opportunity to be among his helpers. Ameen Ya Rabbul Alameen.
