title: Majlis 2 | Haqq ki Talaash | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the intellectual and spiritual requirements for seeking the truth, emphasizing the role of Aql (intellect) and Marifat (divine insight) in worship. The discourse connects the necessity of following the Ahlulbayt with the historical struggle of Imam Hussain (a.s.) against the tyranny of Yazid. It highlights the dangers of ignorance, prejudice, and haram consumption, while underscoring the importance of sincerity in Azadari and the divine authority of the Imams.
content:
O moon, O moon, O moon, O moon, O moon, O moon, O moon, O moon. Affirmation of Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. O moon, O moon of Karbala, you must have seen, they descended upon this earth, the stars of the highest heavens, O moon. O moon, you are radiant, is it the moon of desire or, take the charity of light from here, O moon. O moon, upon this earth, you always kept coolness, those who sleep here, they are the beloved of Zahra, O moon. They are the masters of Tasneem and Salsabil and Kawthar, those who were killed thirsty, on the banks of this canal, O moon. Like Hur and Habib, the brave and the beloved, were killed right here, the companions of the King of Religion, O moon. And the body of Qasim was being trampled in the battlefield, Abbas and Sarwar, were picking up his pieces, O moon. And arms were severed right here, of Abbas the loyal, he did not get permission to fight, he could not even bring water, O moon. And Sarwar brought a moon-faced one to give water, to bring comfort and peace, after being struck by the arrow of oppression, O moon. The neck of the son was pierced, the arm of the son was pierced, both writhing in pain, passed away from the world thirsty, O moon. And in that forest, a little girl was looking for her father, scattered were lying, when the severed heads and bodies, O moon. Then you also saw that grief-stricken girl, sleeping on the chest, clinging to the headless father, and arms were tied right here, for the first time the harem, passed through this land, Sajjad with his head bowed, O moon. And the Prince of Paradise, is the master of Karbala, the Prince of Paradise, is the master of Karbala, who has the courage to come, until he calls, and those who have reached Karbala, who are the descendants of Jafar, I wish that destiny, shows this to their hearts, O moon, of Karbala. Upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, Salawat. A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim. Bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'ali al-'azim. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man nasir. Alhamdullilahi Rabbil Alameen, wal 'aqibatu li ahlit-taqwa wal yaqeen. Was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashraf al-anbiya'i wal mursaleen, habibi ilahi al-'alameen, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sallallahu 'alaihi wa alihi al-ma'sumeen, alladhina adhhaballahu 'anhum ar-rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Sima sima Baqiyatullah fil aradeen, Imam-e-Zamanina, wa wali amrina, wa sahibina. O Mawlana, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate friend, the cave of protection, the helper, the straight path, may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for you. Furthermore, our Mawlana and Sayyiduna, Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), said: 'Whoever worships Allah as is His due right of worship, Allah will grant him more than his desires and his needs.' May the truth be spoken by our Mawlana Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), Salawat. I have chosen this Hadith Sharif for the discussion of this Ashra. In this Hadith, Sayyid al-Shuhada Imam Husayn (a.s.) says: 'Man abadallaha haqqa ibadati'—whoever worships Allah as is the right of worship, meaning in the way it should be done, the right way of worship—'atahullahu fawqa amanihi wa kifayatihi'—Allah will give him more than his wishes and more than his needs, things he cannot even imagine or conceive in his mind. Allah will grant him this in this world and in the hereafter. Remember, it is not that Allah leaves His sincere servants alone in this world; no, Allah is always with them because they worship Allah as is the right of worship. And what is the right of worship? The fundamental thing is first to have Ma'rifah (gnosis), which we discussed yesterday. The basic discussion yesterday was summarized as giving preference to Allah in everything—not to your desires, not to your emotions, but to prefer Allah, to prefer Allah's commands, to prefer Allah's orders and prohibitions. That is called the right of worship. Yesterday, I also discussed the intellect (Aql) with you, stating that intellect is such an important thing that Allah has distributed among His servants, and it is through this intellect that Paradise is attained and Allah is worshipped. When a narrator asked the Imam about the intellect, the Imam said: 'Al-aqlu ma ubida bihir-Rahman wa ktusiba bihil-jinan'—Intellect is that through which the Most Gracious (Allah) is worshipped and through which Paradise is earned. A human will enter Paradise through intellect. This means that the 'right of worship' we are discussing can only be fulfilled by those who utilize the light of their intellect, who use their intellect, and who utilize this great boundary that Allah has given them. When they use the light of their intellect, they use their reasoning. Therefore, the foundation of all our discussions should be on the light of intellect. But remember, we are not like the Mu'tazilah or some theologians who say, 'Whatever does not fit into our intellect, we do not accept.' This attitude is wrong because Allah has set a limit for the intellect as well. For example, what is the limit of intellect in Tawheed (Monotheism)? The limit of intellect in Tawheed is only that it can prove the existence of Allah—that Allah is the Creator who created us. But can the intellect explain the details of that Creator? The intellect can never explain the details of that Creator. A human can only understand as much about the Creator as the Creator introduces about Himself; a human cannot understand more than that. Let me give an example quickly to move forward because the topic is very vast. For instance, if you see a building, you only understand two things: one, that this building has a maker—a builder, an engineer, whoever it is. Your intellect says this building did not come into existence by itself. If someone tells you the building built itself, you would say they are out of their mind. If a building—or even a small thing like this tissue paper, which is so precise in its dimensions—cannot come into existence by itself, how can this entire universe come into existence? So, the intellect says there must be someone who created it. The second thing you can say upon seeing the building is that the designer, the engineer, or the architect is very brilliant. You can say the architect is very good, the engineer is very good, the building is very strong. You cannot know anything more about that engineer or architect. Can you know anything else about the builder? Can you know if he is very kind, if his character is good, or if he is very knowledgeable in religious studies? Whatever comes to your mind, it will certainly be wrong. This is about Tawheed. Similarly, regarding Adl (Divine Justice), the intellect says that a human is free in all their actions; therefore, there should be reward and punishment, accountability. If someone says that a human is not free in their actions and is compelled, you would say this is foolish. If a human is compelled like a robot and has no choice or freedom, then Paradise and Hell are wrong for them, and commands and prohibitions are wrong. You cannot tell them to pray or fast, and you cannot punish them if they don't. It is not like that. Anyway, that is a discussion on Adl. Similarly, regarding Nubuwwah (Prophethood), as I mentioned yesterday, the intellect can only work to the extent of identifying who is a true Prophet and who is a false one. You go to the Prophet and ask, 'Are you a Prophet?' 'Yes.' 'Show me a miracle. Do you have any sign from Allah? Is there any proof, any authority, any evidence?' He will provide proof, and that proof must be something no one else can do. If he says, 'My proof is that I remain silent,' your intellect will say he is fooling you. That is why you see many fake 'babas' today whose miracles are exposed everywhere, because a sign or evidence from Allah—a miracle—has a characteristic: first, the Prophet does not learn it from anyone, he does not study in any school; and second, the Prophet can do something that you cannot say he practiced. That is why Prophet Salih (a.s.) was a Prophet, and his people asked him, 'If you are a Prophet, bring such a she-camel from the mountain.' Look at their demand—they were that kind of people. They have been like this since the time of Qabil, and they are like this even today and will remain so until the reappearance (of Imam Mahdi). So, do not be surprised at all. That is why the Quran condemned the majority. The Quran condemned the majority. You can read as many verses of the Quran as you want; the Quran has condemned the majority. In fact, Allah even addressed the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) saying: 'Wa in tuti' akthara man fil-ardi yudilluka 'an sabilillah'—O Prophet! If you follow this majority, they will lead you astray from the path of Allah. But the world's system runs on the majority; it says we believe in democracy. You see, the world's system, the entire order is upside down, completely upside down. So, nothing can be done about that now; Insha'Allah, everything will be fine after the reappearance. Recite a Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. So, the Prophet was the same. The people of Prophet Salih (a.s.) said, 'Bring us such a she-camel, and where from? From the mountain.' And then they set a condition. And this she-camel should be one that is not from a male and female camel, but directly from the mountain. And this she-camel, this she-camel must also be pregnant. They set this condition too. Now tell me, even if a camel is born from a male and female camel, how can a she-camel directly from the mountain be pregnant? But what did Prophet Salih (a.s.) do? He was a Prophet. He sat down, prayed two rak'ats of prayer. As soon as he prayed two rak'ats, he prayed to Allah. And the prayer was answered, the supplication was accepted, Allah fulfilled the prayer. That boulder, which was a very large mountain, split loudly and a very large she-camel came out. So, Prophet Salih (a.s.) introduced it, saying, 'Look, this is a miracle of Allah.' It is mentioned in the verses of the Quran. 'Bayyina' (clear proof), it has come in the terminology of the Quran. It is said, right, a miracle? The word 'mu'jiza' never appeared in the Quran. I mean, in this meaning. It never appeared in the meaning of a 'sign'. This word 'mu'jiza' came much later. It came about 125 or 150 years after Islam. I mean, it was not among the Muslims before. It came later. And it was brought by others, but anyway, it became so common later that slowly it also entered our traditions and Hadiths. This is called 'naql bil-ma'na' (narrating by meaning) in the terminology of Hadith. Anyway, so it came, and they said this is a sign from Allah. So, Prophet Salih (a.s.) said, 'Do not kill it, do not harm it.' But would that nation listen? Just like we don't listen to our Prophet today, they didn't listen to their Prophet. They killed that she-camel. For which—I mean, what are these people called? The one who killed it, his name, the main culprit, was Qidar ibn Salif. Qidar ibn Salif was his name, the one who killed Prophet Salih's she-camel. So, he is called the 'Ashqal al-Awwalin' (the most wretched of the first). I mean, among the ancient people, the most wretched human was this Qidar ibn Salif because he killed a sign of Allah. And who is the 'Ashqal al-Akhirin' (the most wretched of the last)? Ibn Muljam (la'natullah alayh), who killed the greatest sign of Allah in the last times, i.e., Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Salam to Ibn Muljam (la'natullah alayh). Ibn Muljam al-Muradi. He martyred Amir al-Mu'minin. That is why he is called the 'Ashqal al-Akhirin'. I mean, among the last ones, among the last Ummah, the most wretched and the most cursed is this Ibn Muljam. Ali ibn Abi Talib, who is Ali ibn Abi Talib? Who is the Ayatullah al-Uzma (the Greatest Sign of Allah). Ayatullah al-Kubra is Ali ibn Abi Talib. In the Ziyarat, this title is for Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ayatullah al-Uzma. It is the title of Amir al-Mu'minin. The greatest sign of Allah. Look, everything is a sign, from every atom to the Durr-e-Baiza (the white pearl). I mean, up to the Pleiades, the pinnacle of the universe. All these are signs of Allah, the Ayat of Allah. But Ayatullah al-Uzma is Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). 'Uzma' means the greatest. Because 'Ayat' is feminine in Arabic, so 'Uzma' is feminine. The gender used in Arabic is like this. So, Ayatullah al-Uzma, the Greatest Sign of Allah, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Just like that, look, where is the role of intellect? Now the talk of Imamate has come. I mentioned yesterday that the Imam should also be like the Prophet. Because it is a very basic principle. A very basic principle is that if a Managing Director in a company retires or resigns, or whatever, who will come in his place? Will a Managing Director come with the same qualifications, or will a peon come? So, after the Messenger, whoever is the successor of the Messenger will be like the Messenger. Or will any random person on the street say, 'I look like one, put me in charge'? Will that happen? No. Rather, he must be like the Messenger. Now, what characteristics did the Messenger have? The Messenger had power, had signs and clear proofs. The Imams also had such signs, and the Imams actually showed—for ease, we call them miracles—these miracles. Our scholars have written books on this topic. I mean, both specific books and general books. I mean, specific means there is a chapter inside a big book, for example, a whole chapter is on miracles. Moreover, in the fifth century, there was a very great scholar named Husayn ibn Shaykh al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Wahhab. He wrote this book, 'Uyun al-Mu'jizat'. And in it, he narrated miracles and with more details and specifics, who compiled the book? Sayyid Hashim Bahrani. He wrote in five volumes, 'Madinat al-Ma'ajiz'. I mean, the city of miracles. I mean, the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) are the city of miracles. This is the city, that is why when you say 'Nade Ali', teach it to your children. This is a new fashion that has emerged today, 'Don't teach Nade Ali.' Our child knows Surah al-Hamd, Ayat al-Kursi, that is a very good thing, that should also be taught. Certainly, it should be taught. But does your child know Nade Ali? They say, 'No, Nade Ali is not authentic.' Sir, before uttering such sentences, think a little about what we are saying. Are there no other secrets being revealed that Nade Ali is not authentic? No, no, Nade Ali is 100% authentic. When the Prophet prayed to Allah for help, Allah commanded the Prophet, 'Nade Aliyan mazhar al-aja'ib' (Call upon Ali, the manifestor of wonders). O Prophet, the Prophet is praying to whom? To Allah. What is Allah saying? 'O Prophet, O My beloved, call upon Ali.' The Prophet called upon Ali. What is this Ali? He is 'Mazhar al-Aja'ib'. Ali (a.s.) is what? Miracles personified. I mean, the one upon whose hands miracles keep appearing. Anyway, Insha'Allah, if there is time, we will mention one miracle for you. So, the intellect says that the Imam must also be like the Prophet. It cannot be that the Prophet is of a high status and the Imam does not know anything, that in every small matter he says, 'Call so-and-so, call so-and-so, I don't understand.' They didn't understand anything. And they would immediately give a fatwa too. They said, 'If, for example, there is no water, what should we do? Should we pray?' He said, 'Don't pray.' Oh brother, what are you? Immediately, Janab-e-Ammar rebuked him. He rebuked him right there. He said, 'What are you saying? Have you forgotten? We were both in the desert, and we were both in a state where Ghusl (ritual bath) became obligatory upon us, but there was no water. So I remembered that the Prophet said to do Tayammum. So I rolled in the dust,' Janab-e-Ammar said, 'and I rolled and prayed.' And when I asked you, 'Did you pray?' you said, 'No, I didn't pray because there is no water.' Look, whatever I am telling you, I am speaking with proper references, yes, nothing is without reference. Okay, and that is not a Shia book. It is not a Shia book; if anyone is under the misconception that I am taking references from a Shia book, no, no. It is not a Shia book, rather it is from the books of the opponents, from the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah. So he says, 'Have you forgotten that matter?' Then when we came back to the Prophet, you didn't even pray. When we came to the Prophet, I said, 'Ya Rasulullah, my Ammar said, Ya Rasulullah, we were in a state where Ghusl was obligatory, but there was no water, so I did Tayammum like this.' The Prophet said, 'No, that is not the correct way of Tayammum; the correct way is this.' The Prophet explained the method, but you didn't even pray. And even now you are giving the same fatwa that 'don't pray.' Now, the gentleman's reputation was ruined in front of everyone. In the full court. Now what to do? So he said, 'Beat Ammar.' Ammar, the companion of the Prophet. A companion of the Prophet, and there are many such incidents present. I mean, not one. Janab-e-Mir Hamid Husayn Hindi (rizwanullah ta'ala alayh), in his book 'Abaqat al-Anwar', brings hundreds, more than 100 such incidents where he was sitting and saying, 'No, no, don't do it, it doesn't matter. Don't pray, don't do this work, don't do that work, it will be fine.' Oh, it is the worship of Allah, how will it be fine? If you ask any Shia jurist among us, even if he is not a Marja', not a scholar, just a Mujtahid. Even a minor one who reads 'Tawdih al-Masa'il', who is a little familiar with the rulings, if you ask him, 'Can prayer be abandoned in any situation?' He will say, 'Never.' If there is no water, do it with Tayammum, but you cannot abandon prayer. Anyway, the one who is the successor of the Messenger must be like the Messenger. Now, let us quickly take this discussion a bit further. See, it is mandatory for every human being, regardless of their religion, faith, or sect, without exception, to seek the truth and reality in everything. We are not talking about just one sect; this issue applies to everyone, including us. Often, we ourselves do not remain in search of the truth. We just do what we see others doing or what we understand to be right. What is 'Haq' (Truth)? Haq is that which the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have explained. Nothing else is the truth. So, if someone wants to seek the truth, there are certain conditions for it, which I will quickly explain in the light of the Quran and Hadith. Please listen. The first thing is that if a person seeks the truth, they should pray to the court of Allah, 'O Lord, show me the truth.' Truth is a very difficult task. I repeat, speaking is easy, listening is easy, but seeking the truth and finding the truth is very difficult. Very difficult, it is a very hard task. That is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) provided a standard for truth. Look, this is the truth: 'Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with Ali.' 'O Allah, turn the truth wherever Ali turns.' Wow! So, one person has defined what the truth is. Now, if anyone wants to see the truth, they should look at Ali. Is this clear to everyone? Now, look at the first condition: there must be sincerity. A person must have sincerity, meaning a sincere heart. Their intention must be pure. And for the intention to be pure, there are two important things. If someone wants to keep their intention pure, first, no 'haram' (forbidden) thing should enter their mind. When 'haram' enters the mind—meaning things that Allah has forbidden, things He has prohibited—and we are doing, watching, listening, and reading those things, then obviously, when a person's mind is filled with forbidden acts and corruption, how will they seek the truth? And the second thing is that no impure or 'haram' thing should enter a person's stomach. No impure or 'haram' thing should enter. If they are eating something impure that Allah has forbidden, something that the Sharia has forbidden, then obviously it will have an effect. If they are eating 'haram', it will definitely have an effect. That is why the first command in our Sharia, the Hadith, is that before starting any work—whether it is a job, a profession, or a business—the first condition is that you must be aware of the jurisprudential laws. Meaning, you must know the laws of Islam. It is very important to know them. That is why it is found in the Hadith: 'Fiqh (knowledge of law) first, then trade.' Gain knowledge first, then start your business. Whatever business you are going to do, first see if it is 'haram' or 'halal' or what it is. Right? Otherwise, a person might be very sincere but ignorant. And this sincere ignorant person is very dangerous. The Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) says, 'Two people have broken my back.' My back is broken. The Master of the Universe says this, and the words he uses, 'inkasara zahri,' mean it is broken in such a way that it cannot be mended. My back has been broken by two types of people. And who are those two people? Look, these are the words of the Master of the Universe, pay attention. 'Alimun mutahattik'—an 'Alim' (scholar) who is knowledgeable but commits forbidden acts very freely. He is 'mutahattik' (shameless/reckless). Or he does not protect his knowledge and gives his knowledge to those who are 'na-ahl' (ineligible). That is called 'mutahattik'. 'Hattak' means to tear the veil. Tearing the veil has many meanings that I do not need to explain right now. I will just stop here. One is that scholar, and the second is who? 'Jahilun mutanasik'—the ignorant person who worships a lot. He has broken my back. The ignorant person who worships excessively without knowledge. Without knowledge. He is very harmful to the religion. You know that those people—this Ibn Muljim (may Allah's curse be upon him)—he was a Kharijite. Do you know who these Kharijites were? They were all among the Master's soldiers in Kufa. Those who killed the Master were the Master's soldiers. After the Battle of Siffin, they separated. They used to worship so much that history books write their foreheads had become like the knees of a camel. From worshipping so much. Worshipping so much. Such worship, but they were ignorant; they did not possess 'marifat' (divine insight). And their ignorance was revealed at the Battle of Siffin. When the army of Muawiyah raised the Quran on spears, these people started saying, 'O Ali, look, these people have also raised the Quran, they also believe in the Quran, they also pray, why are you fighting them?' The Master of the Universe explained, 'They have not raised the Quran; they are playing a trick, this is their conspiracy. The Quran has not descended below their throats. They do not understand the Quran; they do not know the Quran.' The Master was trying to explain that I am the Quran and the Quran is me. But those ignorant people did not understand anything. They surrounded Ali (a.s.) and put their swords to his head, all together, saying, 'Stop this war now, stop this war now, or we will kill you.' So the Master of the Universe... Then he had to call back Malik-e-Ashtar. Malik-e-Ashtar had gone so far that he had reached Muawiyah's tent. So when the message reached him, Malik-e-Ashtar said, 'Just give me a few more moments, give me a little more time, I will go and finish his work, the problem will be solved.' But the people said, 'No, Ali ibn Abi Talib has said that if you want to see Ali alive, come back now.' So Malik-e-Ashtar came back. And what was the result? The result was that he used these same Kharijites, whom Malik had gone to kill, to martyr Ali ibn Abi Talib and to martyr Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. The intention must be absolutely pure. Absolutely pure. And when will the intention be pure? When good things enter a person's mind and 'halal' things enter their stomach, not 'haram'. If 'haram' enters, their intention will be like that. That is why it is absolutely clear that Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (Imam Hussain (a.s.)) said this on the day of Ashura. You know that Sayyid-ush-Shuhada gave several sermons on the day of Ashura. After giving several sermons to the enemies, their words were not being understood by them. They were not understanding anything. So Sayyid-ush-Shuhada finally said, 'The reason you are not understanding this is because your stomachs are filled with 'haram'. Your stomachs are filled with 'haram'. That is why you will not understand anything.' So, therefore, if someone does not understand something, the reason is that their stomach is filled with 'haram'. So anyway, this is one thing: their intention must be pure. Let me quickly recite a short Hadith, then we will move to the second point. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says—Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad—'La tahullul futya la yastafti min Allah azza-wa-jal.' Meaning, if any person wants a 'fatwa' (judgment/verdict) from Allah Azza-wa-Jal, if anyone wants—and 'fatwa' here does not just mean the verdicts given by Mujtahids, but it means if you want to ask something from Allah seriously—Imam says, 'La yastafti min Allah azza-wa-jal,' the condition for that is: 'bi-sifa-e-sirrihi,' that their inner self must be pure. Their inner self must be pure. The second thing is: 'wa ikhlas-e-amlihi,' and their action must also be pure. There should be no 'riyakaari' (hypocrisy/show-off) in that action, no showing off. Even if there is an atom's weight of showing off, hypocrisy, then the action is useless. And this is called 'shirk-e-khafi' (hidden polytheism) among us. Meaning, where a person does things to show others. And the third thing is 'wa ala niyyatihi,' that whatever they do openly, they should do it with a pure intention. For example, this 'Azadari' (mourning) we are doing, whoever does this 'Azadari' should do it with a pure intention. There should not be an atom's weight of showing off or hypocrisy in this. There should not be even an atom's weight of, 'Oh, if so-and-so comes, then I will mourn; if so-and-so doesn't come, then I won't.' If this many people come, if that many don't... no, these things should not happen. 'Azadari' means there must be a pure intention. So he said 'ala niyyatihi,' and after that, 'burhan-e-min rabbihi fi kulle halin.' Imam says, after that, in every situation, one should expect light from their Lord, the 'noor' (divine light) that will come from their Lord. Provided that they are completely pure and clean. What is the second point? Imam says that in it—meaning the condition to receive the truth—is that there should be no 'ta'assub' (prejudice) in a person. There should be no prejudice. What is 'ta'assub' called? In Arabic, it is called 'asabiyat', in Urdu, it is called 'ta'assub', and in English, it is called 'prejudice'. What does prejudice mean? Prejudice means that we know something is right, but because it is not in our favor, we say it is wrong. This is called prejudice. This thing is going against one of our relatives, so we take our relative's side and say, 'No, this is wrong.' Why? Because it is going against our relative, against our tribe, against our friend, against our nation, so we say it is wrong. No, wrong is wrong and right is right. And this was the reason why, whenever people mentioned the Ahlulbayt, the result was that the 'Ummah' (community) would fall victim to 'asabiyat'. Victim to prejudice. 'We will not let the Ahlulbayt come, no matter what happens. We will not accept the Ahlulbayt.' That is why I will quickly recite two Quranic verses for you. One is Surah Az-Zumar, verse number 32, in which Allah says: 'Faman azlamu mimman kazaba 'alallahi wa kazzaba bis-sidqi iz ja'ahu.' Who is a greater 'zalim' (unjust) than the one who invents a lie against Allah—meaning, attributes false things to Allah—and two, when 'sidq' (truth/reality) comes to him, he rejects it? Based on his 'asabiyat', based on his prejudice. He says, 'No, I will not accept this.' Why? 'It is going against me.' So, if a Shia presents a point, they say, 'No, we do not accept the words of the Shias.' Why don't you accept them? 'Because Shias have magic in their speech. There is magic in their statements.' Oh brother, you prove the magic, and if you are so truthful, then debunk that magic. Wow! Wow! Wow! You keep proving magic, we will not accept it, and we have the counter to that. But what do they do? They take the support of lies and in that way, they corrupt people; they corrupt people's minds and their beliefs. In another verse, Allah says, 'Wa man azlamu...' the verse is the same, only one word at the end has changed. This is verse number 68 of Surah Al-Ankabut. Allah says, 'Wa man azlamu mimmaniftara 'alallahi kadhiba'—there is also one where the first verse said 'kadhaba 'alallah', two words have changed. In the verse above, it was 'kadhaba 'alallah', in this verse, it is 'iftara 'alallah', meaning one who fabricates a lie against Allah. 'Iftara' means to attribute something that does not exist. To say something exists when it does not. He attributes a lie to Allah. He attributes a lie to Allah. Has a lie been attributed to Allah or not? It has been attributed a lot. If we start telling you the list, if we start narrating the list, then at least another 'Ashra' (ten days) would be needed for that. Not a Majlis, but an Ashra. Not one Majlis, but at least 10 Majlises just to list how many lies were attributed to Allah after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). So many false things. Anyway, that is a separate topic, so here the Quran says, 'Wa man azlamu mimmaniftara 'alallahi kadhiba'—and who is a greater wrongdoer than the one who attributes a lie to Allah? 'Aw kadhdhaba bil-haqqi lamma ja'ahu'—or the one who denies the truth when it comes to him. Now, we have already told you who the Truth is. The Truth is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). The Quran is saying that there is no greater wrongdoer than the one to whom Ali ibn Abi Talib came to claim his right, and he denied Ali ibn Abi Talib. For three days after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Ali ibn Abi Talib, Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), and—Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad—for three consecutive days, they kept going to the house of every Muhajir and Ansar, knocking on their doors. Ali ibn Abi Talib was there, Janab-e-Zahra was with him, Imam Hassan and Imam Hussain (a.s.) were with him. That is, all the individuals of the Verse of Mubahila were together, whose honesty, whose truthfulness, whose truth, Allah Himself testified to. Allah said these... are the truthful, and upon whoever opposes them, there is the curse of Allah. For three days, these 'Ahl-e-Mubahila'—that is, these people of Mubahila who had come to the field of Mubahila, whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had brought with him—kept knocking on the door of every Muhajir and Ansar. But everyone made excuses. If you read the books of history, you will see what is written in them. Someone said, 'O Ali! You came very late.' Someone said, 'Ali! We will come tomorrow.' Someone didn't even open the door. They didn't even talk. What do we know about all this? These are matters of 'great people'. These are matters of those two great people. You hear these phrases, don't you? This is exactly what has been going on in Islam. And this same thing continued when the war between Yazid and Imam Hussain (a.s.) took place; it was said that this is a war between two great people. That is why the late Dabeer Sitapuri said: 'If this Karbala is a war of princes, then if there is strength in the pen, write that Hussain lost.' This is it. This has been going on in Islam. The Quran has said that these are the greatest wrongdoers. The greatest wrongdoers; there is no wrongdoer greater than them. Why? Because they denied the Truth, the Truth whose verification Allah did, the Truth whose announcement the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made. We have already told you about the Hadith of Truth. The event of Mubahila is its proof. Besides that, there is the Sermon of Ghadir. And as many Hadiths as you want to mention, they exist. But in every matter, prejudice plays a big role. Prejudice does what in everything? What does prejudice do? 'No, no, this didn't mean this, they meant that, meaning this, meaning that'—in this way, they dismiss the matter. Now look, let's take the matter further; this was the second thing. What is the third condition? These are the three conditions for seeking the Truth. First, I mentioned to you: sincerity, purity—not just purity, but purity. Second, there should be no prejudice. And what is the third thing? The third thing is that a person must work hard for it. Must strive. Only then is the Truth found. Allah has promised in the Quran: 'Walladhina jahadu fina lanahdiyannahum subulana'—those who strive in Our way, work hard, endure hardships, bear everything, surely, definitely, We will guide them to the straight path and Our ways. We will guide them to Our path, 'Lanahdiyannahum subulana'—We will guide them to Our ways, We will tell them that this path is Our path. This is Our path. If someone truly works hard in the way of Allah, puts in the effort, then Allah will show him the path. These are the three conditions. Until a person fulfills these three conditions, he will not come to the straight path. And that is why the first sign of faith that has been mentioned—we will just give a hint, we will narrate a story quickly for you, which Sheikh Hussain ibn Abdul Wahab has narrated in 'Uyun al-Mu'jizat', and because he was a very great Muhaddith, in the books, it is written before his name: 'Al-Muhaddith al-Kabir', 'Al-Muhaddith al-Kabir', 'Al-Muhaddith al-Jalil', a very great scholar of the fifth century, the fifth century, Al-Muhaddith of the fifth century, he was a very great scholar. He narrated the incident, but before that, let me tell you what a very important condition is for reaching faith, and that is to love the Truth. Subhan Allah. A person should love the Truth. He should make himself in such a way that he loves the Truth. Until he does this, he will not find the Truth. If there is hesitation in his mind—hesitation, that if the Truth comes before him, should he accept it or not—it means there is some doubt, there is no purity, there is some problem. But if it is known that no, this is the Truth, for example, if this Hadith is known: 'Aliyun ma'al-haqqi wal-haqqu ma'a Ali'—Ali is with the Truth and the Truth is with Ali—then loving Ali becomes a condition of faith. The condition of faith, the condition for belief, what is it? Love of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Love for Ali is a condition of faith. That is why the narrator asked further, asked the Imam, 'Is love a part of faith?' The Imam replied, 'Halid-dinu illal-hubbu wal-bughd?'—Is religion anything other than love and hatred? That is, friendship and love for the Truth, and enmity towards falsehood is what religion is. Subhan Allah. This is necessary; it is not that we like this one and we like that one too. We love both. This is not correct. That is why the Imam said—meaning a man came to the Master of the Universe (a.s.) and said, 'I love you, and I also love those who usurped your right.' The Imam replied to him in one way, what did he say? This is the reply of the Master of the Universe. Look, it is not ours, that if someone has a problem with us, they don't accept our word, brother. Isn't it? But one should not reject the word of the Master of the Universe, right? So the Master of the Universe said, 'Right now, you are one-eyed. You are one-eyed. Either become two-eyed or become completely blind.' This will not work. That is, either keep both love and hatred—that is, love us and have enmity towards our enemies—or become completely of our enemies. Go completely over there, no problem. At least it will be known that this one is from the other side. This 'walking on both sides' and fooling people, that should not happen. And remember that this love of Ali is very useful. It is very useful, it comes in very handy. Let me quickly narrate the story for you. He also narrated this story in 'Uyun al-Mu'jizat', this very story, let me present it to you. A person came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) at the time when he had the government, the apparent government. In the apparent government, the government of the Imam was in Kufa, and the Master was sitting on the judge's chair in the Dar al-Qada, and he said, 'O Ali! 'Ana min shi'atika, inni muhibbuka'—Master! I love you, I am your follower.' Now the Master is a judge at this time, yes, remember that. He is a judge. He said that I love you very much, but I have committed a very big sin. I have been committing this sin for a long time. Now that sin was such that we do not consider it appropriate to mention it here in the Majlis. But it is in the Hadith; if anyone wants it, take it from us. He committed such a sin, the Master asked, 'What is your sin?' The Master, he said, 'Master! This is my sin.' Ugh! A very big sin, truly. Severe. Tremendous. The Master said, 'Your punishment is very severe. Now I can give you three punishments. Options, three options. You select one of the three options. One, I will behead you with my Zulfiqar. Two, I will crush you against a wall—like in today's language, they say 'bulldoze', meaning, for example, I will drop a wall on you and kill you.' He committed such a big sin. 'And three, I will burn you in fire.' He said, 'Master! I am most afraid of fire.' Listen to his sentence, his reply. 'I am most afraid of fire. That is why you burn me with fire so that I die by burning, so that when I go to the Hereafter, I go without sin.' The Master ordered Ammar and Qambar to gather wood. Tomorrow morning after the Fajr prayer, he will be burned. After the Fajr prayer, he is to be burned. Now the news spread in Kufa that, brother, this was a follower of Ali, he committed this sin, Ali said that brother, burn him, burn him with fire. Tomorrow morning he will be burned. Now you know that in Kufa, most were Ali's... enemies too, you know that, right? The majority of Kufa were enemies of Ali, they did not love Ali. That is, there were many Shias in Kufa, there was a large number of Shias in Kufa, but there were also many enemies of Ali. Now they all started talking among themselves that we used to hear Hadiths from them that fire will not burn a follower of Ali. Now here, Ali himself is burning him. Ali himself is burning him. Okay? 1000 logs of wood were ordered, 1000 wooden logs, and a pile of them was made, and after that, he was placed on top of everything. Okay? When he was placed there, now the Master of the Universe is going to set fire to the wood. But before setting it, he says, 'What did you say when you came? You love me?' Now these logs will tell whether you love me or not. Now it is written in the Hadith that the Master of the Universe set the fire, the wood caught fire. Just think, 1000 logs of wood, you know, right, how much 1000 wooden logs are. Then the wood kept burning, and burning, until each piece turned to ash. He sat there with great composure. Nothing happened to him. I mean, the wood and the fire were such that they would have burned a human's bones, but nothing happened to him at all. Not even the slightest bit. He was truly a lover of Ali (a.s.). He had committed mistakes, but then the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat) reminded him that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had said about me, 'Ya Ali', and many times the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ya Ali anta qasim al-jannati wan-nar' (O Ali, you are the one who distributes Paradise and Hell). This person, this young man, did not even have a single scratch on him. But let me add a rider here: this does not mean that we should commit sins. It does not mean that. Why? Because sin has an effect; sin can even distance a person from the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt. He was fortunate that despite such a major sin, there was something that held him back. Anyway, God willing, we will present the rest of the discussion tomorrow. This is love, and if anyone in the world has shown the manifestation of this love, it is the companions of Imam Hussain (a.s.). When the young men of Banu Hashim received the news at night—the news was that Imam Hussain (a.s.) had said, 'Sister Zainab, I have been summoned to the court.' Janab-e-Zainab was worried, wondering why he was summoned to the court at such an hour. The court does not convene at night. The Imam said that their governor has passed away, and I know why I have been called, and my answer is quite clear. Janab-e-Zainab said, 'Brother, if this is the matter, I will not let you go to the court alone.' Turning around, she said, 'Brother Abbas, son Ali Akbar, look, the Master is going to the court, you all go with him.' It is written in the Maqtal that there were 30 young men of Banu Hashim who surrounded Imam Hussain (a.s.) and took him to the Dar al-Imara. Upon reaching the Dar al-Imara, as they got close, Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'You all wait outside; I will go inside alone. It is not appropriate for you to come.' But he added, 'If my voice is raised, then you come inside.' Now, when he entered, the Imam was seated, and the news of the governor's death was announced. According to Islamic law and principles, the Imam recited Istirja, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. Walid said, 'The new governor who has arrived, Yazid ibn Muawiya, has ordered that you pledge allegiance at his hands.' The Imam explained that this is a matter of allegiance, and it is not decided in the darkness of the night. Call the Muslims tomorrow during the day; the matter will be decided in front of everyone as to who will pledge allegiance and whose allegiance will be taken. Walid said no, but the governor insists that you pledge allegiance now, at this very moment, and there is no permission to grant a delay. The Imam said, 'If you want to hear my decision now, then listen: "Mithli la yubayi'u mithlahu" (One like me will never pledge allegiance to one like him).' 'Mithli la yubayi'u mithlahu.' Saying this, Imam Hussain (a.s.) rose and began to leave. Just as he was leaving, Marwan called out, 'Walid, Hussain is leaving, stop him! Otherwise, if he slips through your hands today, then until rivers of blood flow in Medina, you will not be able to take Hussain's allegiance.' As soon as Marwan uttered these words, the son of Fatima (s.a.) became enraged. He said, 'Atuhaddiduni bi-qatli ibn al-zarqa?' (O son of the blue-eyed woman, do you threaten me with death? Who will kill me? Will Walid do it, or will you?) As soon as Hussain's voice was raised, the young men of Banu Hashim entered the Dar al-Imara. Swords were about to be drawn from their sheaths. Abbas said, 'Master, who dared to challenge you? Because of whom was your voice raised?' It is written in the Maqtal that Hussain placed his hand on the hilt of his sword. 'Brother Abbas, this is not the time for war, this is not the time for war, be patient.' Abbas was patient. I would say, Mawla, oh Abbas, until when should you be patient? Hussain returned. Now, having come back, he said to his sister, 'Sister Zainab, Medina is no longer a place to live; we have to leave Medina.' Hussain said just this sentence and went to the grave of his grandfather. Now this news echoed in Medina that the Prophet's grandson is leaving Medina. When Hussain returned from his grandfather's grave, Umm al-Mu'minin Janab-e-Umm Salama came and asked, 'Son, what am I hearing, that you are leaving Medina? Where are you going?' He said, 'I am going to Iraq.' As soon as she heard the name of Iraq, Umm Salama's heart trembled. 'Oh son, your grandfather had said something about Medina.' He said, 'Yes, Grandmother, he said it correctly, and the same will happen as my grandfather said.' Umm Salama could not bear it. Imam Hussain (a.s.) comforted her and did something: he miraculously picked up the soil of Karbala and said, 'Grandmother, I will be killed here.' He took the soil of Karbala and said, 'Keep this; as long as this soil remains as soil, I am alive. When this soil turns into blood, then understand that your Hussain is no longer alive.' Umm Salama took that soil and placed it near the soil that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had given her. And now, when Hussain had departed from Medina, Umm Salama would come again and again to look at that soil. She would look at it, and if it was still soil, her heart would find peace. Time passed until the afternoon of Ashura arrived. Umm Salama was sleeping. What did she see in her dream? The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has come, his collar is torn, his sleeves are rolled up, and he is throwing dust on his head. 'O Umm Salama! You are sleeping peacefully, my Hussain!' Umm Salama woke up, and when she came and looked, she saw that the soil had turned into blood; it was flowing blood. Umm Salama slapped her face, mourned, and cried, 'Wa Husayna!' Hearing Umm Salama's voice, the ladies came. 'Oh Lady! Do not say that, our Master is on a journey, our Hussain is on a journey.' She said, 'No, Hussain is not on a journey anymore; Hussain is no longer in this world.' 'Wa Husayna! Wa Mazluma!' [Quranic verses recited]. O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, help them pay their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. O Lord! Grant us the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: ⚡ Anbiya (a.s) Ki Wiraasat Nahin Hoti - Sach Kaise Pataa Karein? | Watch Ep 2 of #The_Fadak_Podcast
excerpt: This lecture examines the controversial Hadith claiming that Prophets do not leave behind inheritance, which was used to deny Janabe Zahra (s.a.) her rights. The speaker argues that this Hadith contradicts the Quran and that the perspective of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) aligns with divine scripture. By utilizing non-Shia sources, the lecture highlights the inconsistency of those who claim the Quran is sufficient while simultaneously prioritizing a contradictory Hadith.
content:
'We, the group of Prophets, do not leave behind inheritance; whatever we leave is charity.' So, what is the answer to this? This very Hadith is the root of the entire issue. The most interesting thing about this Hadith is that we will present evidence for it, Insha'Allah, and we will present it from non-Shia books. We will provide clarification on this because all the references are present, and we will present them not from Shia books, but from non-Shia books. Those people were adamant about their stance; they did not agree and insisted that they would not return it. The Princess (Janabe Zahra) became angry with them and severed her ties with them. So, the meaning that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) took from this Hadith is different, and the meaning that Hakim took is different. Indeed. So, is an attempt being made to suggest that both are correct in their own place? That is, the one whose right was snatched is also correct, and the one who usurped the right is also correct? This is the spirit of the Quran. Therefore, when there is a conflict between two things, if two contradictory views are seen, then to know which one is correct, the Quran must be checked to see which view is in accordance with the Quran. And here, only the view of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is in accordance with the Quran—that Prophets do inherit and Prophets do make others heirs. That is, the thing that Allah is pleased with, which is the prayer of the Prophet, the Muslims... They denied that thing. They are denying the pleasure of Allah. They are bringing this Hadith in opposition to the pleasure of Allah. And claiming it to be a book of truth. On one hand, there is the claim of 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us), and on the other hand, they are bringing a Hadith against the Book of Allah. Where is the justice in this? Is this knowledge? Are their claims truly sincere?

title: EP15 | Haqeeqi 12 Imam Kaun? | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines the theological significance of the Prophetic Hadith regarding the twelve successors. The speaker critiques various Sunni interpretations that attempt to reconcile historical caliphs with this prophecy, arguing that these efforts are inconsistent and avoid the clear implications of the Prophet's words. The discourse reinforces the Shia belief in the twelve Imams, starting from Ali ibn Abi Talib and concluding with the occultation of the 12th Imam, while emphasizing the necessity of spiritual vigilance and adherence to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
PSR presents: 'Ashhadu anna Aliyan Waliullah'. [Arabic recitation]. The topic was that there are numerous narrations—meaning they are found in abundance—from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). If not Mutawatir, they are at least Mustafiz. They are found in the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah that there will be twelve successors after me, and all of them will be from the Quraysh. This is very famous, and Muslim has recorded this narration and narrated it from Jabir ibn Samura. Jabir ibn Samura says that my father was also present there, and I was a little behind. The Prophet said that there will be twelve successors after me. After that, those who were close to the Prophet started making noise; as soon as the Prophet spoke, they started making noise. So I could not hear what the Prophet said. I asked my father later what the Prophet said, and he said that the Prophet said, 'Kulluhum min Quraysh' (All of them are from Quraysh). Now the question arises here, why were these people who were making noise doing so? Were these the same people who, when the Prophet asked for a pen and ink to write a will for you so that you would never go astray after him, had a problem with the Prophet's will? These were the individuals who, at any cost, did not want the Prophet to write a will and appoint a successor; nothing should be in writing so that it does not become an argument. And to make noise in front of the Prophet himself is against the explicit command of the Quran. That is, if someone makes noise in front of the Prophet, their deeds are rendered void, and they go outside the fold of Islam. The meaning of deeds being rendered void is exactly this. The Quran says in Surah Hujurat, verse number 2: 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu la tarfa'u aswatakum fawqa sawtin-nabi' (O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet). 'Wa la tajharu lahu bil-qawli kajahri ba'dikum liba'din' (And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another). If you do this, 'An tahbata a'malukum wa antum la tash'urun' (Your deeds will be rendered void while you do not perceive it). In other words, you won't even realize when you have stepped outside of the religion, when you have stepped outside of Islam. And this is not a difficult matter. The Quran itself, in Ayat al-Kursi, states: 'Allahu waliyyul ladhina amanu' (Allah is the Guardian of those who believe). 'Yukhrijuhum minaz zulumati ilan nur' (He brings them out of darkness into light). 'Walladhina kafaru' (And those who have chosen disbelief, who are not actually following the Prophet), 'Walladhina kafaru awliya'uhumut taghut' (And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the Taghut/tyrants). 'Yukhrijunahum minan nuri ilaz zulumat' (They take them from light into darkness). From what light? The light of Islam that existed during the time of the Prophet, and after the Prophet, they led them from the light of Islam into the darkness of disbelief. This is a verse of the Quran; if not, then how do you explain this? Tell me the interpretation of this. Tell me the interpretation. Meaning, in what light were the disbelievers? 'Walladhina kafaru'—who is being spoken of here? Meaning those who never even brought Islam. 'Walladhina kafaru awliya'uhumut taghut, yukhrijunahum minan nuri ilaz zulumat'—if they were never in Islam, as the Quran defines, then in what light were they? Were they in the light of disbelief? In what light were they? And then from there, 'Yukhrijunahum minan nuri ilaz zulumat'—now what darkness did they go into? That darkness of disbelief was enough for them. If they were outside the circle of Islam, that is enough. Now, where else did they go from there? And it is called 'light'—so reflect on this. This is a matter worthy of reflection. Regardless, another narration has been recorded by Muslim ibn Hajjaj al-Shapuri in his Sahih, in volume seven, from Wasila ibn al-Aqsa. Wasila ibn al-Aqsa says that I heard the Prophet saying that Allah chose Kinana from the sons of Ismail—meaning the tribe of Kinana—and from Kinana, Allah chose the Quraish, and from the Quraish, Allah chose the Banu Hashim, and from the Banu Hashim, Allah chose me. It is absolutely clear; the Prophet is stating very clearly that 'all of them are from Quraish,' meaning 'all of them are from Banu Hashim.' The Prophet is clarifying it; this is a narration in Sahih Muslim. If anyone has any doubt. Regardless, even if we don't accept this, let's say, okay, you say this was for the Prophet, it was not for his successor, not for his Caliphs—it doesn't matter. It doesn't matter, you say we don't accept it, fine. We accept your point, and now come and see—the Hadith is absolutely clear, and it is in many books, even in Sahih Muslim, in Tirmidhi, this narration is in many places. Now, see how you justify it. See the explanation, see the justification. Listen to the response of the Ahl al-Sunnah. The first response is that they say it is not correct to limit their number to twelve. The Prophet said there would be twelve successors after me. He didn't say there would be 'only' twelve successors. Is this an explanation? It could be more than twelve, it could be less than twelve. Meaning, placing one's own words before the words of the Prophet. Who is saying this? The commentator of Sahih Muslim, who wrote the commentary on Sahih Muslim. His name is Nawawi. Nawawi, and in volume twelve, page number 201, 202, in the context of this very Hadith, he explained it in such a way that it is not necessary that it be twelve; there could be more, there could be less. Meaning, you are rejecting the Prophet's words just to make your own point prevail. Reflect a little. Think a little. See, this thought is a moment of reflection, and this same point has been recorded by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in Fath al-Bari. Fath al-Bari fi Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari. This is a commentary on Bukhari. In it, volume number 16, page number 339, it is in Fath al-Bari that the number can be less or more. Now you tell me, how can the number be less or more when the Prophet is stating it? Anyway, now look at the second explanation. Jalaluddin al-Suyuti, a very great scholar of the Ahl al-Sunnah. How great a scholar he is—if I just present one thing for your service: he passed away in 911 Hijri, and in the autobiography he wrote himself, he mentioned that at least until he was alive when he wrote it, he had written more than 300 books, and the list prepared after his death contained 550 books. Jalaluddin al-Suyuti. He wrote two and a half Tafsirs. One is Tafsir al-Itqan, the second is Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur, both are his, and the third Tafsir is half a Tafsir, meaning written in partnership with Jalaluddin al-Mahalli. These were Jalaluddin al-Suyuti and Jalaluddin al-Mahalli, so both were Jalaluddin, both were Jalal, so that is why it was named Tafsir al-Jalalayn, meaning the Tafsir of two Jalals. So they wrote it in partnership, and that makes it two and a half Tafsirs. Meaning, I just want to tell you how great a scholar of religion he is, and if you want to see more, everything about him is present in books; you can refer to them. Anyway, let's not go into those details; he just wrote a book, Tarikh al-Khulafa. In Tarikh al-Khulafa, see what he writes. Meaning, he brings the Hadith of the twelve Imams, that there will be twelve Imams. Now he brings the Hadith about twelve, and now he says that these Imams will continuously remain on the truth, even if they are not one after another. The Prophet said 'after me.' 'After me.' He says it is not necessary for them to be consecutive. Then he says it is possible that there might be a gap, a large gap. And then he starts counting the twelve. Counting the twelve. Now listen to this count. He says four are the Rashidun Caliphs. These are four Caliphs. The fifth is Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), the sixth is Muawiya. He declared Muawiya as the successor of the Messenger of Allah. Actually, there should be no discussion after this. But still, let's say, just for the sake of argument, we accept it. Then after that, he says Ibn Zubayr, and then he says directly after Ibn Zubayr, who? Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. In between, he left out all the other Caliphs of the Banu Marwan, who were kings, not Caliphs. So he says these are a total of eight. Which eight? Rashidun Caliphs four, Imam Hasan five, Muawiya six, Abdullah ibn Zubayr seven, and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz eight. He kept skipping in between. Okay, right? He dodged a bit from here, dribbled from here, went from here, came out from here, and reached eight at the goalpost. Okay, right? Now four are left. Now in the four, he says, he says, perhaps you can include Mahdi al-Abbasi in this. Mahdi al-Abbasi, nine. Okay, right? Why? Because that Mahdi al-Abbasi was a just ruler like Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and had a government. And Tahir, include Tahir al-Abbasi as well. So that makes ten. So Mahdi al-Abbasi and Tahir al-Abbasi, two kings of the Banu Abbas, he left out everyone else. What is the standard? Why? Any proof for it? Just that they were just, just kings. Firstly, whoever usurps the right of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and is pleased with that usurpation, he cannot be just. But still, you say ten, so okay, no problem, these are ten. Now two are left, so he says, now about the two, we don't know. One is the Mahdi, eleven. Okay, right? Because he is from the Ahl al-Bayt. But the other one is also unknown. Is this your belief? Meaning, that thing which the Prophet said, that there will be 12 successors after me, 12 Caliphs, all of them will be from the Quraish, and Islam will remain dear, Islam will remain strong and powerful until these 12 are there. All these narrations exist, meaning you are saying it like this? Ibn Hajar al-Haythami brings this same argument, Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa, Ibn Hajar al-Makki. Ibn Hajar al-Makki, whose death occurred in 974 Hijri. In 974 Hijri, remember. Meaning, he was a scholar of the 10th century, Ibn Hajar al-Makki, Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa. And on page number 19 of that, he brings this same argument. Now you decide for yourself, look, we have requested from the beginning that you have to make the decision. Meaning, the listeners, the viewers have to decide whether this argument is correct or incorrect. Now here, this is it, and now we are presenting the final argument for your service, just listen to this, and then if you are not surprised, then I am surprised at you. Look, this is what Ibn al-Jawzi writes. Now Ibn al-Jawzi is such a great scholar that what can we say about him? He is a student of Ibn Taymiyyah. That much is enough to say. And he considered himself such a great scholar of his time that he once even made the claim of 'Saluni' (ask me before you lose me). Anyway, what happened after that is a different story. Then Allah showed him that no brother, 'Saluni' is not for you; only one was entitled to 'Saluni,' whose name was Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the progeny of Ali has the right to make this claim. No one else has the right to say 'Saluni qabla an tafqiduni.' Whoever tried, their end was very bad. Anyway, these were the people. Now he has actually explained this, this Hadith, now look what it is. He says that the first Caliph from the Banu Umayya is Yazid ibn Muawiya. Listen to this. Yazid ibn Muawiya. Now listen to his description, what it is. Meaning, this is present in Tarikh al-Tabari and all history books about him. That he used to drink wine, he used to play with monkeys, he used to make a mockery of religion. He had no belief in religion at all. He used to say: 'La'ibal Hashimu bil mulki fala khabarun ja'a wa la wahyun nazal' (The Hashim played with the kingdom, for no news came and no revelation descended). Islam is not something of any name; the Banu Hashim just played with the people, otherwise, no news came, no revelation descended. 'La'ibal Hashimu bil mulki fala khabarun ja'a wa la wahyun nazal.' This was Yazid's poem. This is his poem, the poem of such a man. You understand. He has no religion, and you are calling him the successor of the Messenger of Allah. And if you are not satisfied even with this characteristic, then listen, Yazid is the one who martyred Imam Hussain (a.s.) in the year 61 Hijri. They say no, he didn't do it, the Shias did it. Okay, fine, let's say. In the year 62 Hijri, Yazid is the one who plundered Medina. He plundered Medina, and its details are present in history books; it is called the Incident of Harra. You can check it. Nowadays there is Google, it will be very easy to find, youngsters go and check, The Incident of Harra. Yazid conducted the whole thing, whereas the Prophet's Hadith was: 'Man akhafa ahlal Madinati akhafahullahu yawmal qiyamah' (Whoever frightens the people of Medina, Allah will frighten him on the Day of Judgment), and Yazid did this. He didn't stop at that either; in the year 63 Hijri, Yazid rained fireballs on the Kaaba and tried to demolish the Kaaba. This same Yazid, Yazid, the same. And you are saying he is a Caliph—it is surprising about Ibn al-Jawzi. And then after that, he says that the first of the Banu Umayya is Yazid ibn Muawiya and the last is Marwan, whom people in history have named what? Marwan al-Himar. Meaning, 'Himar' means donkey. And then he says that in this regard, the number becomes a total of 13. It becomes 13. And he says I have not included Uthman, Muawiya, and Abdullah ibn Zubayr in this because they were companions of the Messenger of Allah and not among the Caliphs. Have you seen? This is the explanation. Is it clear? Now, just to help you make a decision, we will recite a Shia Hadith for the sake of blessings so that it becomes clear to you what the belief of the Shias is. He is a very great companion of the Imam, Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.). His name is Abdullah Azeem al-Hasani. He presents himself in the service of Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.). As soon as the Imam's eyes fell upon him, the Imam said, 'Marhaban bika ya Abul Qasim.' Meaning, welcome, O Abul Qasim. 'Anta waliyyuna haqqan' (You are truly our follower). 'Faqultu lahu ya ibna Rasoolillahi inni ureedu an arida alayka deeni' (I submitted, O son of the Messenger of Allah, I wish to present my religion to you). Look, Shias should always—it should be a habit of Shias—regularly re-evaluate their religion, meaning, has any weakness crept into their beliefs? So here, I want to present my religion before you. And then, he presented Tawheed (the Oneness of God). A very sound Tawheed, and then he stated the belief in Risalat (Prophethood), and in it, he said very clearly, 'Anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasooluhu khatamun nabiyyina fala nabiyya ba'dahu ila yawmil qiyamah' (That Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets; there is no prophet after him until the Day of Judgment). This is the Shia belief. Until the Day of Judgment, there will be no prophet after Allah's Messenger. And then he says, 'Innal imama wal khalifata wa waliyal amri ba'dahu' (Meaning, who is the Imam, the Caliph, and the Wali al-Amr after the Messenger of Allah?). Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Look, you keep counting. 'Thummal Hasanu thummal Husaynu' (Then Hasan, then Husayn)—that makes three. 'Thumma Aliyyu bnil Husayn' (Then Ali ibn al-Husayn)—four. 'Thumma Muhammadubnu Aliyyin' (Then Muhammad ibn Ali)—five. 'Thumma Ja'farubnu Muhammadin' (Then Ja'far ibn Muhammad)—six. 'Thumma Musabnu Ja'farin' (Then Musa ibn Ja'far)—seven. 'Thumma Aliyyu bnu Musa' (Then Ali ibn Musa)—eight. 'Thumma Muhammadubnu Aliyyin' (Then Muhammad ibn Ali)—nine. 'Thumma anta ya mawlaya' (And then you, O my Master), meaning Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.), Ali ibn Muhammad an-Naqi (a.s.). He stopped there. Why? He did not know what came next, or even if he did, he remained silent before the Imam. So the Imam said, 'Faqala alayhis salam wa min ba'di al-Hasanu ibni' (And after me, my son Hasan), meaning Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). And then the Imam, the 10th Imam, says, 'Fakayfa linnasi bil khalafi min ba'di' (Then how will the people fare regarding his successor after me?). So Abdul Azeem asked, he inquired, 'Faqultu fakayfa dhaka ya mawlaya?' What will happen, Master? He said, 'Liannahu la yura shakhsuhu wa la yahillu dhikruhu bismihi' (Because his physical appearance will not be seen by people, meaning he will remain hidden from their sight, and it will not be permissible to mention him by his name). However, one can refer to him by his titles. 'Hatta yakhruja' (Until he reappears). 'Fayamla'ul arda qistan wa adlan' (He will fill the earth with justice and equity just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny). And then the Imam said to Abul Qasim, meaning Abdul Azeem Hasani, 'Hadha wallahi' (This, by Allah, O Abul Qasim), 'Hadha wallahi deenullahi' (This, by Allah, is the religion of Allah) which you have just stated regarding Tawheed, Prophethood, and Imamate; this is the religion 'alladhi irtadahu li'ibadihi' (which Allah has chosen for His servants). 'Fathbut alayhi' (So remain steadfast upon it, remain steadfast upon it). 'Thabbatakallahu bil qawlith thabiti fil hayatid dunya wa fil akhirah' (May Allah keep you steadfast on this firm word in this life and in the Hereafter). And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure, clean, infallible, and oppressed progeny, and may there be eternal curse upon their enemies, their killers, those who usurped their rights, and those who denied their virtues and merits.

title: Verse of Mawaddah | Holy Quran & Ameer al-Momineen (a.s.) | آیت مودت
excerpt: This lecture explores the significance of the Verse of Mawaddah (Surah Ash-Shura, 42:23) and its interpretation in Islamic tradition. The speaker highlights that the command to love the Prophet's near relatives refers specifically to Ali ibn Abi Talib, Fatima al-Zahra, and their children. By citing both Shia and Sunni sources, the lecture emphasizes the consensus among Muslims regarding the identity of the Ahl al-Bayt as the recipients of this divine obligation.
content:
Ya Billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala... Regarding the verse of the Holy Quran and the words of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), today we will discuss verse 23 of Surah Ash-Shura, in which Allah (s.w.t.) says: 'Say, I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my near relatives.' Furat ibn Ibrahim, in his Tafsir, and Sayyid Hashim Bahrani, in Tafsir al-Burhan, narrate from Ibn Abbas that when the verse 'Say, I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my near relatives' was revealed, people asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.): 'O Messenger of Allah, who are your near relatives whose love and affection Allah has made obligatory upon us?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied: 'Ali (a.s.), Fatima (s.a.), and their children (a.s.).' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) repeated this sentence three times. In the interpretation of this verse, the Ahl-e-Sunnah... In the interpretation of this verse, it is narrated in the famous book of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, Sahih Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas that when I was asked about 'love for my near relatives,' Saeed ibn Jubayr, who was present there at that time, said: 'The intent here is the Progeny of Muhammad (Ahl-e-Bayt).' You have observed that all Muslims are unanimous and agreed that the command to love and show affection to the near relatives in this verse refers to the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.)—that is, Ali (a.s.), Fatima (s.a.), and their children (a.s.). Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alameen.
The Verse of Mawaddah is found in Surah Ash-Shura, verse 23.
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) defined 'near relatives' as Ali, Fatima, and their children.
The Prophet emphasized this definition by repeating it three times.
Sunni scholars like Saeed ibn Jubayr also identified the 'near relatives' as the Ahl al-Bayt.
There is a broad consensus among Muslims that this verse commands love for the Prophet's family.

title: Wo Kaisi Talwaar Thi Jis Se Imam Ali (a.s.) Ko Shaheed Kiya Gaya?
excerpt: This lecture recounts the tragic martyrdom of Imam Ali (a.s.) at the hands of Ibn Muljam, instigated by a conspiracy with Qatam. It details how the sword used in the attack was deliberately poisoned to ensure the Imam's death. The speaker reflects on the profound loss this caused for the Ahlulbayt and how it paved the way for the subsequent oppression and martyrdom of the remaining Imams by the Bani Umayya.
content:
The 16th is approaching, and it is happening. Listen, Urmila, Hissa, Mir Ali Mir, my technology... what is to be written? Regarding the sorrowful events of the blessed month, for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), this was a month of doomsday. Because on the 19th of this month, the wretched Ibn Muljam (may Allah curse him) struck the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), with such a blow that on the 21st of Ramadan, the 'Mushkil Kusha' (Solver of Difficulties) bid farewell to this world. On the night of the 19th of Ramadan, there was a conspiracy between Ibn Muljam and Qatam, in which both of them together plotted the martyrdom of Imam Ali (a.s.). They plotted the martyrdom of Imam Ali (a.s.). This woman, whose name is mentioned as Qatam, was the one who promised to marry Ibn Muljam on the condition that he would kill Ali (a.s.). Ibn Muljam agreed to kill Ali (a.s.) in that same state. When Ibn Muljam was at Qatam's house, he said to her, 'O Qatam, tonight I will kill Ali ibn Abi Talib for you.' Saying this, he began to sharpen his sword. After sharpening it, he placed the sword in front of Qatam. She said, 'I want to poison it.' Ibn Muljam asked, 'What kind of poison are you mixing? If it were placed on a mountain, it would shatter it into pieces.' She insisted, 'Leave it to me. I am mixing it with poison because when you strike the Commander of the Faithful, your senses will be lost, your hands will tremble, and when you strike, it might not have an effect. But if the sword is poisoned, even if the strike does not work, the poison will do its job.' Finally, that time also came. Finally, that time also came when Ibn Muljam did the deed, which caused a tremor in the universe under the sadness of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), and by God, the pillars of guidance were shaken. The stars of the sky and the banners of piety were broken. By God, the 'Futuwwah' (chivalry) was broken. The brother of Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) and his successor were killed. Ali Murtaza was killed. By God, the true successor was killed, and the most wretched person in the world killed him. The martyrdom of Ali (a.s.) was a painful and great tragedy for the family of Prophethood. It was the presence of Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) and Ali (a.s.) that was the protection for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). While Ali was there, no one dared to harm the family of the Prophet. But the martyrdom of the Mawla opened the doors of oppression for the Bani Umayya. They poisoned Imam Hasan (a.s.), shot arrows at his funeral, and did not allow him to be buried next to his grandfather. In Karbala, Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his children and... Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his children, and after that, the family of the Prophet was paraded in the markets of Kufa and Sham. After that, from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) to Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.), everyone was martyred. Every Imam was martyred either by poison or by the sword. But why was the enmity towards Ali so deep in the hearts of the Bani Umayya? The tyrant martyred Ali (a.s.) with both the sword and poison. Like Ali's life, Ali's martyrdom is unparalleled; it has no equal. Once again, we remember the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). At the beginning of this month, we offer our condolences for the martyrdom of the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (a.s.), and pray in the court of Allah Almighty: 'O Lord, accept this small service, and may it reach the Imam of the time. O Lord, give solace to the heart of Ali, and may your final proof (Imam Mahdi) come soon. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.'
