title: E'teraazaate Ghadeer Ep#05: Ailaan-e-Wilaayat Ghadeer-e-Khum Mein Kyun? Arafah Mein Kyun Nahin?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the theological and historical questions surrounding why the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) at Ghadir-e-Khumm rather than during the Hajj at Arafah. It clarifies that the announcement was a divine mandate, strategically timed to ensure maximum impact and clarity for the entire Muslim community. The discussion emphasizes that the Prophet acted solely upon revelation, and that true faith requires complete submission to this divine appointment despite historical resistance.
content:
Welcome to all of you in this program. Today, we will present a new question before you, and we will also provide the answer. So let's see our fifth question, which is as follows: 'Why did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announce the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) at Ghadir-e-Khumm instead of at the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjatul Wida)? Why was this announcement made at Ghadir, when it could have been made at Arafat?' To answer this, we have with us our brother, Syed Rahat Hussain. Peace be upon you, brother. How are you? How are you? As you heard, we want you to tell us the answer to this. What is the answer? Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. First of all, I offer my congratulations to all of you on these blessed days. May it be blessed for you too. As far as the question is concerned, what was the reason that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made this announcement of the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) at Ghadir, when it could have been made at Arafat? Why was it done at Ghadir? Many people raise this objection, and it is very important to understand the motive behind the objection. Unless one understands the subject, one cannot give a complete answer. The motive behind this objection is: 'Why was it done at Ghadir? It could have been done during the Hajj, or at Arafat.' There are several answers to this. First of all, the announcement of Wilayah that happened at Ghadir... The announcement of Wilayah that happened at Ghadir was not the first time the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was announcing the Wilayah and Imamate of Ali (a.s.). Ghadir was not the first occasion, nor was it the only one. Besides Ghadir, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) on several occasions. There are many such instances before Ghadir found in books. I can point to some of these. First of all, the 'Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira' (Invitation to the near relatives), which is also called 'Yawm al-Indhar'. When the Prophet called his near relatives and first presented this invitation, he asked, 'Who among you will help me in this work, in spreading this religion, and through that, he will be my brother, my successor, and my caliph?' No one stood up except the Master of the Universe, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Volume 2, page 321, this is present. In the book of Tabari, Volume 2, page 321, this Hadith is found, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, asking his near relatives, 'Who among you will help me in this matter, in spreading this religion, and through that, he will be my brother, my successor, and my caliph?' No one stood up. Only the Master of the Universe, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), stood up and said, 'O Prophet of Allah, I will help you.' And when he showed his determination to remove the obstacles in this work, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'This is my brother, my successor, and my caliph among you.' So, from the very first day of the invitation to Islam, not only... Not only was the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) telling people about Ali (a.s.), but the chain of succession after him was also mentioned in the very first invitation. This is a Hadith found in books. From that time, we see that Ali (a.s.) was considered the successor and the heir. There is another Hadith found in the books, which says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced about Ali (a.s.): 'He is from me, and I am from him.' And after that, the famous Hadith that is on the tongue of every child of ours, 'You are to me as Harun was to Musa.' After this, it becomes clear that this objection is baseless. It becomes clear that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has called Ali (a.s.) his successor and caliph with all these titles, and everyone was well aware that after him, there is no other caliph or Imam. Yes, yes, the objection that is raised—that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made this announcement at Ghadir, and because the Hadith mentions Ghadir—this objection is, in itself, correct. This objection could have been valid at that time if it were the first announcement of its kind, but since this was the first time such an announcement was made, questioning it in this way is not a logical or realistic approach. However, since the objection exists, the first response is this: and the second response is this—in this regard, when we try to present all the answers from this perspective, the second response is: why was it not done after the Hajj, and is it possible that there were people who had already left? The answer to all these questions could be this: it is not necessary that at that entire Hajj, at every place and every location where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was present, all the companions were present at the same time with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It is possible that someone might claim, 'I was praying' or 'I was busy with something else,' so they might not have been present at that location. This is a point that can be raised. Therefore, this objection does not make sense as to why it was not announced in Mina or Arafat, because people were busy with other Hajj rituals, and while one announcement was being made... and while another announcement was being made, someone might not have been present there and later said, 'We did not hear this because we were performing Tawaf or were busy with other rituals.' This is the second response. Now, regarding the arrangement of this location—look, this place, Ghadir-e-Khumm, is a place that is not at all suitable for staying because one has to endure the desert, the desert sun, and there is no shelter around. There was only one pond of water. So, making arrangements for this announcement in such a place itself proves that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was doing something out of the ordinary routine. For example, if I have to give you an important message, and I call you and say, 'Brother Roshan, this is an important matter, please pay attention,' you might be busy with other work and forget or not pay full attention. In contrast, if I wake you up in the middle of the night... if I wake you up in the middle of the night and call you, it will not be easy to forget. To give an example, if I wake you up in the middle of the night and call you, you will not forget it. If you come out of your house and have to search for someone, that thing will always remain in that person's memory because it is something out of the ordinary. Yes, so here too, it was completely out of the ordinary, and let me give another example so that this matter becomes completely clear. Whatever happened in 2020, none of us could forget it. Just as in 2019, 2020—everyone remembers it. No one even needed to remind anyone in early 2020. Why? Because it was such a year that if we all recall it, the amount of hardship and the way it affected all Muslims—we remember it more than anything else. So, because this was out of the ordinary, no person in their right mind could ever forget it. It has been 5 to 6 months, and before this, it used to be that people would forget things after 1 or 2 months. But if someone gives you a text message while you are at home, this is out of the ordinary, so it can never be forgotten that such an arrangement was made for that announcement. that such an arrangement was made for that announcement, and people—in fact, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stayed there for three days, and water was available in your vicinity. This water means that whenever someone felt the heat, they would need water, and when they got that water, they would remember that heat—the heat of the desert of Khumm. So, whenever they would drink that water, they would remember. It is like this: we drink water many times in the desert, and every time they drank that water, they would remember the pond, they would remember the event. This is the fourth response. Now, as far as it is said that it was like a caravan before... that it was like a caravan before, and they started moving—so if the purpose is that you would have been in the desert, more than the others, for example—then this is not a valid objection. Why? Because in Islam, the importance of a place is not greater than the importance of the command. Before this, many announcements were made, many sermons were given, many mosques were built in Medina. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was conveying the message to the people, so were there no people there? To say today that there were no people there is wrong. Some had already left, but the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) waited for the people there. Those who had gone ahead, he waited for those who were left behind. After everyone gathered, he started the announcement. So, this crowd and this gathering is not an objection in itself. Furthermore, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) also said that those who are present should convey this message to those who are absent. So, through this, it is also clear that this message was to be conveyed to every house. It is the responsibility of the present to convey it to the absent. This is another point, and later, an interesting point arises that if... an interesting point arises that if those people—if this was to be conveyed to everyone—then why was it not sufficient there? Our question to the people is: how many people were there? There were very few, with great difficulty, they were gathered there. They were not gathered there because it was a place for everyone, but rather because it was not a place where all people could be. In fact, he said that in their hearts, with them, yes, this is all from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). They cannot deny the pictures and the events. Here, we see a very important point: how much they loved the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). At the time when the announcement was being made, people were busy with their own affairs, leaving him there—this should be the focus. this should be the focus. And then the fifth point is that for those who object, it is always necessary to see what the objection of the companions was. Because among all the people who were present, did any of them object, 'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), why did you not make this announcement in Mina? Why did you not make the announcement in Arafat?' Is there any such thing in the entire history? Is there any such thing found anywhere that any of them raised such an objection? In fact, there were more than a hundred thousand people, and it was difficult and troublesome, but none of them complained, 'You left our friends behind, the message did not reach them.' No one raised an objection. But among those who came later, those who want to delay this, those who want to adopt a path of withdrawal and use other excuses, those are the people who present this. And in the end, it is not like this; many times such things have happened. For example, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) brought the Quran, those people said, 'We are looking at what he has brought.' They... they said, 'We are looking at what he has brought.' They said, 'We do not want this, bring another one.' It is the same way, and in this regard, there is an indication in Surah Yunus: 'When Our clear signs are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring us a Quran other than this or change it."' So, they say, 'Bring something else or change it.' Now, here, just briefly pointing out, while pointing out the matter of the Quran—the matter of the Quran was before this—so this is an objection that shows they said, 'Bring another Quran.' So, the Quran was completed, and they said, 'Change it, change it from here.' they said, 'Change it from here,' meaning they are not obeying. This is not about the message you are conveying regarding the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). We are not ready to accept Ali (a.s.), so either change the Quran or change Ali (a.s.). This was the mentality of those people. And they always wanted to either move away from the Quran or change it. This is visible everywhere in the Holy Quran. In fact, in the Holy Quran, it is mentioned in many places. So, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'It is not for me to change it on my own. I follow only what is revealed to me.' I cannot change it. I will follow only what has been revealed. I cannot do anything else from myself. Why? Because I fear the punishment of a Great Day. So, the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is not a matter of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) own choice. the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not bring Islam from himself. Therefore, those who believe in the statement of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should believe in the Wilayah. As it is said in the Quran, 'By your Lord, they will not believe until they make you the judge in all disputes between them.' They will not believe until they accept your judgment. And then, after you have made a decision, they should not find any hesitation in their hearts. If anyone shows hesitation, they are not believers. So, they should completely submit. Just as there is a right to submit, there is a right to be submissive. Why should one be skeptical of the rights of the West? This currency and the decisions of the ninth... it was a soft and pink movie. These answers will be based on their links. Absolutely, as we have seen that in such months, very tough answers were presented, and a lot of batting was done during the time, tea was also drunk. This clearly shows that this objection, first of all, is not even worthy of being called an objection. And the reason for this is that whoever keeps the love of Ali (a.s.) in their heart, their intellect becomes clouded. They can only expect these types of objections from them; they cannot do anything else. Because the religion is being understood, they do not understand truth and falsehood, right and wrong. So, we should remain attached to Ali (a.s.), and we have millions... the Lord has seen that He has attached us to the door of the family of Muhammad (a.s.)... as long as we live, as long as our breaths continue, in our hearts...

title: Majlis-e-Azaa | Hadees-e-Kisa | Maulana Meesam Zaidi Sahab | Mahdiyyah Imambargah
excerpt: This lecture by Maulana Meesam Zaidi explores the profound spiritual significance of Hadith al-Kisa and the sanctity of the Ahlulbayt. The discourse highlights the divine status of the Prophet and his family, emphasizing the healing power of Bibi Zahra's cloak and the theological importance of weeping for Imam Hussain. The session concludes with a poignant reflection on the tragedy of Karbala, specifically focusing on the disrespect shown to Bibi Zainab and the subsequent pursuit of justice by Mukhtar al-Thaqafi.
content:
Haider Haider... [Recitation of Salawat and Arabic supplications]. Gentlemen, this is the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), in which the Divine command is being issued that Allah has intended to keep every impurity away from the Ahlulbayt and to keep them so pure and clean, as is the right of being kept pure. In the more than 6,000 verses of the Holy Quran, there has not been as much care and preparation for the revelation of any verse as there was for the revelation of the Verse of Purification. If you reflect, when Allah granted Prophet Musa (a.s.) a book like the Torah, Prophet Musa (a.s.) had to go to the Sacred Valley to receive the Torah, to obtain the tablets of the Torah. He went for 30 days, later 10 days were added, but Musa (a.s.) had to go. However, Allah did not call the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) anywhere to grant him the Quran. Some verses and chapters of the Quran are called Makki, and some chapters and verses are called Madani. Why is this Quran Makki and Madani? It is said that the Quran revealed to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) during his stay in Mecca is called Makki, and the Quran revealed to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) after the migration is called Madani. So the conclusion is that if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is in Mecca, the Quran is being revealed in Mecca. If the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is in Medina, the Quran is being revealed in Medina. It goes to the extent that if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is in the Cave of Hira, the Quran is being revealed in the Cave of Hira. If the Prophet is in the Cave of Thawr, the Quran is being revealed in the Cave of Thawr. If the Prophet is on the battlefield, the Quran is being revealed on the battlefield. If the Prophet is making peace somewhere, the Quran is being revealed right there. If the Prophet is riding a camel, the Quran is being revealed right there. If the Prophet is sitting on a horse, the Quran is being revealed right there. You will find all these instances. If the Prophet is among his companions, the Quran was revealed right there. If he is among the Ahl al-Bayt, the Quran was revealed right there. Meaning, Allah did not trouble the Prophet to go anywhere for the revelation of any verse. I believe that in the entire Quran, there is only one verse, the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), for the revelation of which the Prophet was called to the house of Sayyeda. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. But along with this, let me also submit that not us, but scholars of other sects—our issue is different—but when they describe the state of the revelation of Wahi (revelation), they write that when the Quran was revealed to the Prophet, the Prophet would start trembling, shivering, sweat would appear on the Prophet's face, and if the Prophet saw Jibra'il, he would not recognize him; they narrate all these traditions. The extreme is that they even state that the Prophet was riding a horse when the revelation began, and the weight of the revelation was so much that the horse's belly touched the ground. They state that when the revelation began to descend upon the Prophet, the Prophet—God forbid, God forbid—would become distressed, and sweat would appear on the Prophet's face. I am presenting a very valuable point to you. Now you tell me, when people write all this, then traditions of this kind will not be seen anywhere, where a verse of the Holy Quran was revealed and the Prophet was lying down, so he sat up. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Finally, wake up, or the Prophet was sitting and stood up, or the Prophet was riding a horse and got down from it. It is said that there is no question of this; no such verse, no such incident, or any tradition is seen. So, brother, it is strange that if a Surah of the Quran is revealed, the Prophet does not sit up if he is lying down, and does not stand up if he is sitting, but when Zahra (s.a.) arrives, the Prophet stands up. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. That when the Lady (Bibi) arrives, the Prophet is seen standing in respect. Now, the revelation of the Verse of Purification and the arrangements made for it, I believe that is what is called Hadith al-Kisa. If someone asks what Hadith al-Kisa is, there is no easier answer than saying that the arrangements and preparations for the revelation of the Verse of Purification are called Hadith al-Kisa. This is what is called Hadith al-Kisa. It is said the Prophet came to his daughter's house. Look, it is obvious that half the night has passed and there is still the night vigil to be held, so we do not have to give a very long speech. It is intended to present a few things to you briefly: the Prophet came to his daughter's house. What did he say after coming? After coming, he said, 'I am feeling weakness in my body.' Where am I feeling weakness? 'I am feeling weakness in my body.' So the Lady brought a cloak and covered her father with it. The Prophet lay down after covering himself with the cloak. Now, when the Prophet lay down after covering himself with the cloak, what does the Lady say? She says, 'I looked towards my father and saw that my father's face was shining like the moon of the fourteenth night.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. This is the meaning, isn't it, that the face was shining like the moon of the fourteenth night? A very intelligent gathering is sitting here. Let me present one point to you: the Almighty has stated in the Quran, 'Wash-shamsi wa duhaha, wal-qamari iza talaha.' I swear by that sun which is shining, which is bright, which gives light, and I swear by that moon which follows the sun. When someone asked the Prophet in the mosque who is meant by 'Shams' (sun) and who is meant by 'Qamar' (moon) here, the Prophet said, 'Here, by Shams, I am meant. Here, by Shams, I am meant, and who is meant by Qamar?' He said, 'By Qamar, Ali is meant.' So one thing was understood, right? Who is the Prophet? He said, 'The Prophet is the Sun, the Prophet is the light.' Did you ponder or not? The Prophet is the light, but the one whom Allah is calling the light, whom Allah is calling the Sun, when he covers himself with Zahra's cloak... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. So what is the Lady saying? That the face is shining like the moon of the fourteenth night. Among educated people, So, I will present one sentence that one thing was also understood: when Sayyeda comes in between, the Majesty (Jalal) turns into Beauty (Jamal). Recite Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The Majesty turns into Beauty. So it was said, 'Like this, like the moon of the fourteenth night.' Now, the critics need an opportunity. We said that the Messenger of Allah is the sun, Mawla Ali is the moon. So they said, 'Look, the sun is big, the moon is small; the sun has its own light, the moon does not have its own light. When the sun's light falls on it, it shines.' Oh, you didn't understand at all! This moon that shines, it doesn't just shine; rather, by shining, the moon gives proof of the sun's life. Recite Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. It tells us, 'Look, the sun has not died; it has gone behind a veil.' So, anyway, this is a separate issue. So the Prophet was called the sun, Mawla Ali was called the moon. But the one whom Allah called the sun, when he covered himself with the cloak—did you notice?—when he covered himself with the cloak, Bibi Zahra is saying, 'The face is shining like the moon of the fourteenth night.' So now I understood that the Prophet is the sun, but if he covers himself with a cloak, he looks like the moon. Whether you reached it or not, I think you must have reached it, that the Prophet is the sun, but if he covers himself with a cloak, he looks like the moon. So once the Prophet covered himself with a cloak, this sun started looking like the moon, and once on the night of migration (Shab-e-Hijrat), Ali covered himself with the cloak. Recite Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. So when Ali covered himself with the cloak, the polytheists thought the Prophet was sleeping. Now, if I have permission, let me say one sentence: brother, the issue is that the Prophet is such a sun that if he covers himself with a cloak, he looks like the moon, and Ali is such a moon that if he covers himself with a cloak, he looks like the sun. So the Prophet lay down after covering himself with the cloak. Look, if someone is sick and you go to visit them, all the human suffering is visible on their face. Now, you went one day, you saw someone is sick, they are being treated, and after a few days you went again and saw that they have some relief. So that relief is known from the face itself. Often people say, 'Brother, Mashallah, now the face is restored, it seems there is some relief in the illness.' Now the Prophet came to Bibi Zahra's house as a patient. He is feeling weakness in his body, but when the Lady covered him with the cloak, he received such healing that his face started shining like the moon. This is one aspect. But here, the only thing I want to present to you regarding Azadari is that Bibi Zahra only covered her father with a cloak. She did not bring a glass of water to give him, so that he could drink it and the weakness of the body would go away. She did not feed him milk mixed with honey. If someone's blood pressure starts to drop, this is what happens, right? Feeling weak. So the Lady did not do this. She did not bring any fruit, did not bring dates. She did not bring any medicine; she only covered him with the cloak. But by Bibi Zahra covering him with the cloak, the Prophet's bodily weakness went away. The Prophet's bodily weakness went away. Now I will definitely say one thing: no one should be surprised that how did the Prophet's bodily weakness go away by Bibi Zahra covering him with the cloak? Read the Quran and see. When putting Yusuf's shirt on Yaqub's eyes can restore lost eyesight, then if a daughter's cloak can remove a father's bodily weakness, is it a surprise? This was a very old matter; I have presented it to you. But listen with great attention: it is true that it can be presented as evidence. But where is Yusuf's shirt and where is Bibi Zahra's cloak? What can I say, wonderful! No, listen to the argument for the point as well. Where is Yusuf's shirt and where is Bibi Zahra's cloak? Let me present a second sentence, because where is the eyesight of Yaqub's eyes and where is the weakness of the body of the 'Sahib-e-Lolak' (the reason for creation)? I said 'Sahib-e-Lolak' intentionally. I said the weakness of the body of the 'Sahib-e-Lolak'. Because the eyesight of Yaqub's eyes was only the eyesight of a single individual. It was the eyesight of Yaqub's eyes. It was the eyesight of a Prophet's eyes. It was not the eyesight of the eyes of the entire universe. Because he was a Prophet but not the 'Sahib-e-Lolak'. Our Prophet is the one about whom Allah says, 'Lawlaka lama khalaqtu al-aflak' (If it were not for you, I would not have created the heavens). This means the universe would not have been created if the Prophet did not exist. All creation is because of him. So now we have to admit that if there is height in the heavens, it is because of him. If there is light in the sun, it is because of him. If there is moonlight in the moon, it is because of him. If there is shine in the stars, it is because of him. If there is fragrance in the flowers, it is because of him. If there is beauty in the Hoors, it is because of him. If the angels are doing Tasbih, it is because of him. Ponder, because of him. If the Prophets have Prophethood, it is because of him. The messengerships of the messengers are because of him. Adam's knowledge is because of him. Nuh's piety is because of him. Ibrahim's friendship (with Allah) is because of him. Musa's awe is because of him. The piety of the God-fearing is because of him. The worship of the worshippers is because of him. The prostrations of the prostrators are because of him. So whatever exists is because of him. Whatever exists is because of him. Now, if the Prophet felt weakness in his body... Look, I think the people of this city might not have faced this problem, but often people here belong to UP. Although now this happens very little in UP too, but a few years ago this used to happen a lot. One thing was that the power would just go out. So the power going out is a different matter, and sometimes it would happen that the voltage would drop completely. Do you have experience with this? Recite one Salawat on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. For that, a stabilizer is being used, this is happening, that is happening. So when the voltage dropped, look, there can be no better example than this. So when the voltage dropped, what would happen? It was said, 'Brother, the voltage has dropped.' Now when the voltage dropped, the fan is there but it is moving very slowly. It is moving very, very slowly. It is running, but it is running slowly. What can I say, wonderful. Look, 'weakness' (zof) cannot be defined better than this: the fan is running slowly. The tubelight is not even turning on; it flickers repeatedly and then goes out. It is not working. The AC is not working. Nothing is working. Everything is there, all the appliances are fine, there is no fault in any of them, but the voltage has just dropped. This means that the source of energy has developed some weakness. Now that this weakness has developed, nothing is working. So, no one will call an engineer or a mechanic to fix our AC or our fridge. Why? Because they know that this is the reason why nothing is working. Suddenly, the voltage becomes normal. Now that it is fixed, everything started working. The Qibla, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), who is the master of 'lawla' (the reason for creation), felt weakness in his body. So, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) felt weakness in his body, the entire universe felt weakness, because everything exists because of him. Now, when the Lady (Bibi Fatima (s.a.)) covered her father with a cloak and the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) bodily weakness vanished, it was not just the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) bodily weakness that vanished. The weakness of the heights of the sky vanished. The weakness of the vastness of the earth vanished. The weakness of the flow of the rivers vanished. The weakness of the turbulence of the oceans vanished. The weakness of the prophethoods of the prophets vanished. The weakness of the messengerships of the messengers vanished. The weakness of the worship of the angels vanished. The weakness of the beauty of the houris vanished. The weakness of the entire creation vanished. I am submitting a point: oh brother, the Lady whose cloak removes the weakness of the entire creation in one moment, if the handkerchief of that same Lady removes our weakness of deeds on the Day of Judgment, then it is not a matter of surprise. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. If that same Lady's handkerchief removes our weakness of deeds, is there any problem? Nowadays, people do not understand the issue of tears. They say, 'Sir, these people say that one tear will take us to Paradise. We will weep for Imam Hussain (a.s.) and go to Paradise.' Oh brother, people say strange things. Paradise in exchange for tears? Paradise in exchange for tears? This is not the claim of the mourners. In any gathering where there has been much weeping, where people have cried, stand at the door where Tabarruk (blessed food) is being distributed, grab the shoulder of every person and shake them, and ask them, 'Why did you cry?' We will stop reciting Majlis if anyone tells you, 'I cried because I want to go to Paradise.' Tell me, of all the people who have come here, has anyone brought the thought of Paradise in their mind, saying, 'Let's go, a Majlis is happening in Mehdiya, and if we go to the Majlis, we will get Paradise'? Very excellent. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Here, the temperament is different. You were just listening to poetry; there is a couplet, and since people of insight are sitting here, and the great orators used to recite this couplet—I heard it from them, and they also used to say that I do not know the name of the poet, so obviously I do not know either. If anyone knows, please search and tell me, but the couplet is truly amazing. Some poet said, 'What a wonder Karbala is, by God, that Karbala...' and look, this is the state of every mourner and every pilgrim. They say, 'If Karbala reached up to Paradise, then what is my fault?' Listen to the second line, look, no one can remain silent. They say, 'If Karbala reached up to Paradise, then what is my fault? The earth itself rose, I did not rise from the door of Shabbir (Imam Hussain (a.s.)).' The earth rose. 'If Karbala reached up to Paradise, then what is my fault? The earth itself rose, I did not rise from the door of Shabbir.' So brother, no one cries in a Majlis thinking that if we cry, we will go to Paradise. Nor has any mourner ever claimed, 'Master Hussain, we cried for you, send us to Paradise.' Paradise in exchange for tears is not the claim of the mourners. Paradise in exchange for tears is the promise of the Infallibles (a.s.). Recite another Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Look, the letters are almost the same, but it is not a claim, rather it is their promise, promise, promise. Yes? Now, some people say, 'Sir, you talk about Paradise in exchange for tears, look at your own character too.' Oh brother, if Paradise in exchange for tears—listen to the sentence—if Paradise in exchange for tears is our claim, then argue about our character. If Paradise in exchange for tears is our claim, then argue about our character, and if Paradise in exchange for tears is their promise, then if you have a tongue in your mouth, argue about their authority. Argue about their authority, whether they have the authority or they do not have the authority. Whether they have the authority or they do not have the authority. May the Master keep you safe, the way you are listening. Although my heart wants to submit to your service—I think we have recited this before in Zainabia—but seeing your taste for listening, I want to submit it. Look, Qibla, in an era, especially in the time of Mir Anees and others, and even today, this question arises, this point was raised that, 'Sir, among those who weep, what about those whose tears are for show, those who cry for pretense?' Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. What will happen to their tears? So Mir Anees (a.s.), the master of his place—obviously, the God of Speech, Mir Anees—he recited a Ruba'i (quatrain). Here, Mashallah, poets are also sitting. We understand that it is not easy to compose a Ruba'i. So, anyway, Mir Sahib recited a Ruba'i, and he recited a truly amazing Ruba'i. He said, 'The scars of the grief of the King (Imam Hussain (a.s.)) are the flower buds of the chest.' Allahu Akbar. If you feel it, you will enjoy it. He says, 'The scars of the grief of the King are the flower buds of the chest. What pleasures of the mourning of the Master have been enjoyed.' Listen, listen, listen. 'The scars of the grief of the King are the flower buds of the chest. What pleasures of the mourning of the Master have been enjoyed.' And in the Majlis, due to Riya (pretense)—you understand Riya, anyway, you gentlemen understand—due to Riya in the Majlis, meaning for the sake of showing off, 'those who cry, Anees, their tears are also pearls, but they are fake.' Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. 'Their pearls are also...' Now you know that fake pearls are even more beautiful. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Now, Qibla, you have given appreciation, but now listen to the real debate. Now, when Mir Sahib said this, Mirza Dabeer (a.s.), the master of his place—and I believe that there was no quarrel or conflict between Mir Anees and Mirza Dabeer, rather the issue there, I think there is no better sentence than this, was exactly the same issue as trying to outdo each other in service. It was exactly this issue. So, after hearing this Ruba'i, Mirza Dabeer recited a Ruba'i. You will give even more appreciation than you gave just now. Now listen to Mirza Sahib's Ruba'i. And listen to the Sayyid Sahib's. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. It is an amazing Ruba'i. Mirza Dabeer says—recite another Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad—in the same meter, in the same rhyme and refrain, Mirza Sahib said. What did he say? He said, 'What, what...' look, how the lines are decorated, listen by God. He says, 'What, what pearls of the tears of mourning have been looted.' The second line itself is amazing, by God, the whole explanation became clear. He says, 'What, what...' look, we are talking about tears, right? So he is saying, 'What, what pearls of the tears of mourning have been looted, and it is proven that the glass of the heart has broken.' Look, Qibla, that issue of Riya just went away, right? You are not understanding, 'and it is proven that the glass of the heart has broken.' 'What, what pearls of the tears of mourning have been looted, and it is proven that the glass of the heart has broken.' Then he says, 'Here, here, meaning in the Majlis, here even the tears of Riya have the price of Paradise.' Listen, listen, listen. He says, 'Here, meaning in the Majlis, here even the tears of Riya have the price of Paradise; the pearls are real, the jeweler is fake.' The pearls are real, the jeweler is fake. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The pearls are real, the jeweler is fake. What can I say, wonderful. The jeweler is fake. The jeweler is fake. That is it, dear ones, the real issue is just this. Look, people do not understand the point at all. I said, 'Sir, all this is recited, so if all this is recited, then people will stop acting and people will stop worshipping.' Who will stop, brother? Why will they stop? For what reason will they stop? Stating the authorities of the family of Muhammad does not mean that at all. That is just your understanding. It is never stated, nor is it in any Hadith, that on the Day of Judgment, whoever says 'Ali is ours' will go to Paradise. Very excellent. This is never stated, right? 'Whoever says Imam Hussain is ours will go to Paradise.' Every person will say this. What can I say, what can I say. Even today, every person says that Ali is ours, Hussain is ours. Rather, on the Day of Judgment, the one for whom Ali will say, 'This is mine,' will go to Paradise. For whom Ali will say, 'Haza Li' (this is mine), 'Haza Laka' (this is yours). So, I think this is the account: Haza Li, Haza Laka. People say, 'Sir, do some preaching too.' Once I said that brother, this sentence is heavier than a thousand or two thousand preaching speeches: 'Live your life in such a way that on the Day of Judgment...' Ali says that this is mine. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Bismillah, I do not know why we try not to recite many couplets in the Majlis, but today I do not know why I kept reciting poetry to you. So listen to one more couplet and let the Majlis conclude. Look, Qibla, regarding intercession, whatever is stated, whatever the scholars, orators, and Zakireen state, that is all in its place. But I think you know that it often happens that in an hour-long speech, whatever a scholar, a Zakir, an orator, or a preacher states, a poet states it in one couplet. He states it in one couplet. Here in Lucknow, a poet passed away, and I think he passed away long before my birth. I have not seen him; his sons are there. His name was Qarrar Lakhnavi. He was a very amazing poet, Qarrar Lakhnavi. And many of his Nohas (elegies) exist, and much of his poetry exists. One of his poems is very popular. It is a Salam (salutation), and I just want to recite one couplet of it to you. But for you to become familiar with that couplet, just one more couplet, and only so that its rhyme and refrain are preserved in your minds, only then will you enjoy that couplet. That he composed couplets in this meter, 'kahan rakh di aur jahan rakh di, wahan rakh di'. Do you understand? So, in this meter, he composed couplets, 'zaban rakh di', 'dukan rakh di'. So, listen to one couplet first so that you become a bit accustomed. He says, 'Kasauti par yaqine haq ki jab parkha gaya imaan. Kasauti par yaqine haq ki jab parkha gaya imaan. Chamakti dhaar par khanjar ki Meesam ne zaban rakh di. Chamakti dhaar par khanjar ki Meesam ne zaban rakh di.' Now listen to that couplet, Qibla, which describes intercession. It is a magnificent couplet, by God. Now, you hear that on the Day of Judgment, a person's limbs will be testifying against them. If one has done even an atom's weight of good, it will be accounted for, and if one has done an atom's weight of evil, it will also be accounted for, and it certainly will be. And there, no one will have any opportunity for excuses. Because one's own hands will be testifying against oneself, one's own feet will be testifying against oneself, eyes will be testifying against us, ears will be testifying against us. But he was a poet, so he took the matter much further. That brother, not just hands, feet, nose, ears, but he said, 'Bayan jab kar chuka har mue tan'. Whenever we read this anywhere, it requires a lot of explanation. But anyway, I think no explanation will be needed here. He says, 'Bayan jab kar chuka har mue tan afsane isiyan'—meaning every hair on a person's body, 'Bayan jab kar chuka har mue tan afsane isiyan'—meaning when every hair on the body has narrated the story of our sins. Listen to the second couplet, will you listen to the second line? InshaAllah, whoever feels it will not remain silent. He says, 'Bayan jab kar chuka har mue tan afsane isiyan, Wilaye Aale Ahmad ne ulat kar dastan rakh di. Bayan jab kar chuka har mue tan afsane isiyan, Wilaye Aale Ahmad ne, Wilaye Aale Ahmad ne ulat kar dastan rakh di.' That's it, Qibla, may Mawla keep you safe. So, where the matter started, that if Bibi Zahra's (s.a.) chador can remove the weakness of the entire universe, then why can't her handkerchief remove our weakness of deeds? Dear ones, the chador, and Bibi Zahra's (s.a.) chador. It is found in traditions that several times the chador of the Prophet's daughter came to be sold in the market. Sometimes there is hunger at home, and sometimes a beggar comes. A beggar came. After coming, he asked at the door of Zahra (s.a.). There was nothing in the house of worldly wealth to give him. The Bibi stopped him and sent her chador through Janabe Fizza to Salman, who was sitting at the door. That you take this chador to the market and sell it, and whatever amount is obtained, bring it and give it to this beggar. Qibla Salman took that chador and left. People were looking at the chador. Salman kept moving forward. When he reached the crowded market, a Jew's eyes fell on that chador kept on Salman's shoulder. He said, 'Salman, have you brought this chador to sell?' He said, 'Yes, this is the chador of the Prophet of Allah's daughter. Such and such is the matter, we have brought it to sell.' That Jew said to Salman, 'Come with us to our house.' Salman went to his house. He stood outside, and he went inside the house. He brought out an old book from his library. He would read that book, look at the chador. Then he would read the book, then look at the chador. Then he would read the book, then look at the chador. Slowly, tears began to flow from his eyes. Salman said, 'What are you looking at the chador for after reading the book?' He said, 'This is our religious book. It is written in it that the chador of the last Prophet's daughter will come to be sold in the market, and this will be the proof of the truthfulness of that Prophet's prophethood, that they will have nothing in terms of worldly wealth, only then will their daughter's chador come to be sold.' So he says that I saw all those signs in this chador. He asked Salman, 'What is its price?' Salman told him the price that could fulfill the beggar's need. He went to his house, brought that much money, and handed it over to Salman. Salman said, 'I want to hand over this chador to you.' He said, 'No, not this chador. You take me to the mosque. This deal will be finalized there.' Salman brought him to the mosque. The mosque was full of companions. The Prophet of Islam was seated on the pulpit. He looked towards the Prophet and said, 'I read something in my book, I saw your daughter's chador, and I understood the truthfulness of your prophethood. I want to recite the Kalima, make me recite the Kalima.' The Prophet made him recite the Kalima. He believed, he became a Muslim. The companions of the Prophet raised the slogan of 'Nara-e-Takbir'. Janabe Salman lifted the chador on both hands and extended it towards him and said to him, 'You take this chador.' He said a strange sentence, he said, 'Salman, I have just become a Muslim. A while ago I was a Jew, but you are a witness that when I was a Jew, even then I did not touch Zahra's (s.a.) chador.' May Allah reward you with the best reward. The gathering is ending. He said, 'I did not touch Zahra's (s.a.) chador.' When I was a Jew, even then I did not touch the chador, so now how would I touch the chador? I would say, the Jew had so much respect that he would not touch Zahra's (s.a.) chador. That's it, Qibla, the gathering is over. It is the court of Janabe Mukhtar. People are being brought in after being arrested. Janabe Mukhtar asks everyone, 'What crime did you commit in Karbala?' Someone said, 'I hit Qasim with a mace,' he was punished accordingly. Someone said, 'I struck Aun,' he was punished accordingly. Someone said, 'I killed Muhammad,' someone said, 'I [struck] Ali Akbar's chest,' Janabe Mukhtar kept asking, kept punishing everyone. Someone said, 'I cut Abbas's right arm,' someone said, 'I struck Abbas's left arm,' someone said, 'I shot an arrow at the 6-month-old child,' someone said, 'I hit Hussain's forehead with a stone,' someone said, 'I ran a dagger on Hussain's throat.' A soldier of Mukhtar brought a man arrested. When he brought him, Janabe... Then Mukhtar asked him, 'Tell me, what crime did you commit in Karbala?' The gathering is over. He remained silent. Then Janabe Mukhtar asked, then he remained silent. Janabe Mukhtar himself asked, 'Tell me, did you strike anyone with a sword?' He said, 'No, I did not strike anyone with a sword.' He said, 'Did you strike anyone with a spear in Karbala?' He said, 'No, I did not strike with a spear.' He said, 'Did you shoot an arrow at anyone?' He said, 'I did not shoot an arrow at anyone either.' He said, 'Did you use a mace on any martyr?' He said, 'I did not use a mace either.' He said, 'You must have hit Hussain with a stone?' He said, 'No, I did not hit with a stone either.' Now Janabe Mukhtar turned towards the person who had brought him arrested. He said, 'When he did nothing in Karbala, why have you brought him arrested? He is saying I did not use a sword, I did not use a spear, I did not use a dagger, I did not use a mace, I did not use a stone. Why have you brought him arrested?' So that soldier said, 'Mukhtar, what he has done, he is not saying that.' That's it, dear ones, Janabe Mukhtar drew his sword. He stood over his head, said, 'Tell me what crime you committed in Karbala?' Dear ones, he began to say, 'Mukhtar, I snatched the chador from Zainab's (s.a.) head.' That's it, dear ones, as soon as this was heard, Mukhtar fainted while crying. Oh, in Karbala, snatched the chador from the head of this daughter of Zahra (s.a.).
Ayat al-Tat'hir and Hadith al-Kisa establish the unique spiritual purity and divine status of the Ahlulbayt.
The Prophet Muhammad is described as the foundational cause of existence, with the cloak of Bibi Zahra serving as a source of spiritual healing.
Weeping for Imam Hussain is a profound act of devotion and a means of seeking intercession, rather than a transactional demand for Paradise.
The chador of Bibi Zahra and Bibi Zainab symbolizes purity, truth, and the ultimate dignity of the women of the Prophet's household.
Poetry, such as that of Mir Anees, serves as a powerful medium for conveying complex theological truths regarding faith and salvation.
The narrative of Mukhtar al-Thaqafi underscores the gravity of the crimes committed at Karbala and the necessity of seeking justice for the Ahlulbayt.
The confession regarding the snatching of Bibi Zainab's chador highlights the depth of the tragedy and the emotional impact on those who love the Prophet's family.
