chapters.title: The Significance of Ayat al-Tat'hir
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces the Verse of Purification, highlighting its unique importance and the divine preparation surrounding its revelation compared to other Quranic verses.

chapters.title: Hadith al-Kisa and the Prophet's Respect
chapters.summary: The lecture explains that Hadith al-Kisa represents the specific preparations for the revelation of the Verse of Purification, emphasizing the Prophet's deep respect for Bibi Zahra.

chapters.title: Symbolism of Sun and Moon
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the metaphorical relationship between the Prophet as the 'Sun' and Imam Ali as the 'Moon', and how the cloak of Bibi Zahra reflects their divine light.

chapters.title: The Healing Power of the Cloak
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how the Prophet's weakness was healed by Bibi Zahra's cloak, drawing a parallel to the miraculous healing power of Prophet Yusuf's shirt.

chapters.title: The Prophet as the Source of Creation
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the 'Sahib-e-Lolak', the reason for the universe's existence, and that all creation derives its qualities from him.

chapters.title: The Significance of Bibi Zahra's Cloak
chapters.summary: The speaker uses the analogy of voltage to explain that when the Prophet felt bodily weakness, the entire universe felt it, and Bibi Zahra's cloak restored strength to all of creation.

chapters.title: The True Meaning of Weeping for Imam Hussain
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that mourners do not weep for Imam Hussain (a.s.) to earn Paradise, but rather that Paradise in exchange for tears is a promise made by the Infallibles.

chapters.title: Mir Anees on Tears of Pretense
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses a quatrain by Mir Anees regarding tears shed for show, noting that even fake pearls have their own beauty.

chapters.title: The Value of Tears and Intercession
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the spiritual value of mourning for Imam Hussain and clarifies the concept of intercession, emphasizing that true salvation comes from the recognition and acceptance of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Poetry and the Testimony of Faith
chapters.summary: Using poetry by Qarrar Lakhnavi, the speaker illustrates how the love and guardianship (Wilayah) of the Ahlulbayt can transform one's spiritual standing even when one's own limbs testify against their sins.

chapters.title: The Story of Bibi Zahra's Chador
chapters.summary: A historical account is shared regarding a Jew who recognized the truth of the Prophet's mission upon seeing the chador of Bibi Zahra, highlighting the immense respect even non-believers held for her.

chapters.title: The Justice of Mukhtar
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with a brief depiction of Mukhtar al-Thaqafi's court, where those who committed atrocities at Karbala were brought to face justice for their crimes.

chapters.title: Mukhtar's Interrogation of a Karbala Criminal
chapters.summary: Mukhtar al-Thaqafi interrogates a captive regarding his specific crimes committed against the Ahlulbayt during the tragedy of Karbala.

title: Majlis 4 | Imam Ali (a.s.) Ki Manzelat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound status of Imam Ali (a.s.) within the context of the Prophet's mission and the tragic events of Karbala. The discourse connects the historical declaration of Imam Ali's Wilayah with the challenges faced by the Ahlulbayt, emphasizing the necessity of patience, spiritual mentorship, and disassociation from hypocrisy. Through a blend of Quranic analysis and historical accounts, the speaker highlights the virtues of the Imams and the importance of aligning one's life with the guidance of Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.).
content:
This narrator is describing Karbala. He wrote the scene of the night of Ashura. The daughter of the King of Guidance (Bibi Zainab) on the chest of the King (Imam Hussain), and Shabbir (Imam Hussain) used to say this repeatedly, 'We have to go tomorrow to fulfill the promise of loyalty, the stage of patience will come upon you.' Sakina heard everything from the King and in response, she kept saying just this, 'Okay Baba, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Shabbir said, 'O my light of eyes, you have to travel until evening now, the wicked will make you a prisoner now,' the Princess said, 'I have no fear, you say you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Okay Baba, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' The King began to say, 'O my beloved, the hour of the evening of grief will come upon you, there will be fire in your hem,' she said, 'I have no such worry, you will come to extinguish my hem, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' With an anxious heart, the King of Religion began to say, 'O daughter, there is no peace in your destiny now, now the wretched Shimr will slap you,' hearing this, she began to say in sorrow, 'You will come to save me from Shimr, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Then the King spoke to his daughter like this, 'All the ladies of the harem will be prisoners of suffering now, ropes will be tied on your hands too,' hearing this, the thirsty-lipped one said, 'You will come to embrace me, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Shabbir (a.s.) wept and kissed her, saying, 'Your cheeks will also be wounded, the days of your weeping, O Princess, have arrived.' She said, 'How will you watch me weep? Yes, you will come to comfort me, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Shabbir's (a.s.) restlessness kept increasing, she agreed to endure every hardship. She could not understand that her father would not be alive. Hearing all the difficulties, she just kept saying, 'You will come to console me when I am upset at home, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Salman, my heart is breaking as I write this. When the King of the World (a.s.) wept and said, 'Now, neither will you be alive, nor will your grave exist,' the daughter of Sabir (a.s.) was a patient one; she said, 'You will come to lift my corpse, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Good father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Hussain, Hussain, Ya Qatil-al-Abarad Hussain, Ya Qatil-al-Abarad. Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out, 'Are you my Hussain? Oh, how are the pieces of your body lying scattered? Are you my Hussain?' Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out, 'Are you my Hussain? Alas, what have they done to my poor one? By horses... They have trampled him in the desert. Oh, how do I recognize you when your head is separated from your body? Are you my Hussain? Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out. Are you my Hussain? Oh, I will recognize you, give me a voice. I saw the strapping youth breathing his last. There is no light left in the sister's eyes now. Are you my Hussain? Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out. Are you my Hussain? Oh, it has become difficult even for you to be recognized. It is the first time I have seen Zainab (s.a.) unveiled. Oh, I am ashamed, tell me, just tell me. Are you my Hussain? Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out. Are you my Hussain? Where and how many times have they tried to slaughter you? There are marks on the dagger and on the severed neck. How has the tyrant cut your throat? Are you my Hussain? Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out. Are you my Hussain? Oh, what have these wretched ones taken after looting everything? Only this stitched shirt of my mother remains on your body. You were not in this state when you left the tents. Are you my Hussain? Removing the stones from the corpse, Zainab (s.a.) cried out. Are you my Hussain? La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil adheem. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil. Ni'mal mawla wa ni'man naseer. Alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alameen. Wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqeen. Wassalatu wassalamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya'i wal mursaleen, habibi ilahil 'alameen, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Salla Allahu 'alaihi wa Aalihi al-ma'sumeen. Alladhina adhhaballahu 'anhumur rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Siyyima baqiyyatillahi fil aradeen, imami zamanina wa wali amrina wa sahibina wa mawlana wa habibina wa tabibina wa anisina wa mu'nisinal kahfil hasin wa ghiyathil mudtarril mustakin, ruhi wa arwahul 'alamina lahu al-fida'. Amma ba'd, faqad qalallahu 'azza wa jalla fi kitabil karim wa qawluhul haqq wa huwa asdaqu al-qa'ileen: Khudh-il-'afwa wa'mur bil-'urfi wa a'rid 'anil jahileen. Sadaqallahu al-'aliyyul adheem. Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. The verse of the Quran that was being discussed, in that verse, God Almighty is commanding to adopt forgiveness, make forgiveness your motto, make it your profession, keep forgiving people. Meaning, do not keep any matter in your heart, do not keep any grudge or malice in your heart. Keep forgiving people, treat them with gentleness, treat them with gentleness, adopt forgiveness. And command people to do good. Do favors, do good. And command people to do good, 'urf means ma'ruf (good). As much as possible, keep doing good to people. The definition of good is that when we do good to someone, it means we do not expect anything in return. If we are doing a good deed for someone, the intention should be that if we do this for them, we will get this in return. Then it becomes a transaction, it will not be a good deed. A good deed, a favor, is one in which a person does not expect anything. That is a different matter regarding the person to whom they are doing the favor, He Himself is so magnificent, so great, that He can give whatever He wishes in return for it. 'Wa amur bil urf wa ariz anil jahileen' (And enjoin what is right and turn away from the ignorant). In the first gathering, I had submitted that when the word 'jahil' (ignorant) is used, it has two opposites. One opposite of 'jahil' is one who does not have knowledge, and there is no harm in that. There are many people who do not have knowledge of things. The second is one who acts against the intellect. That is the 'jahil' who has been condemned. And when a person does things that are against the intellect, one should not talk much to such people; one should turn away from them. This is the command of the Quran, and I had submitted a few verses regarding this in the last three gatherings. Now, what we observe, and what I have been submitting to you, is that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) dealt with his life with great patience and forbearance. That is, with great patience and great endurance. Although those people caused the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) a lot of harm. Do not think that everyone listened to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), was very obedient, and did everything the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said. No, they caused a lot of harm, and those who caused the harm were those who were their own, those who were very close to them. They caused a lot of harm. That is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ma udhiya nabiyun mithla ma udhitu' (No prophet was harmed as much as I was harmed). 'Adhiyat' means harm or suffering. The amount of suffering I have been caused, no one else has been caused. I have been caused the most suffering. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says—this is a hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—'Ma udhiya nabiyun mithla ma udhitu'. Now, let me narrate a small incident for you, which I promised yesterday, and then try to take the matter further. Ever since these people saw that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had decided—because you know this, I am telling this for the children—that the very first invitation the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave, in which he invited everyone, which is called Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira, in that he announced the Wilayah and Imamate of the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.). In that, when he first asked for help, people did not help, no one offered help. So, on all three occasions, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave the invitation. On all three occasions, the Commander of the Faithful (Ali a.s.) was only 13 years old, but all three times, the Commander of the Faithful (Ali a.s.) stood up and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I will help you.' Tabari writes that Ali (a.s.) was so lean that his legs... he was just like a sturdy youth, what we call in the teens, where the teenage years begin, at 13, that was Ali (a.s.)'s age. Very young. But all three times he said, 'I will help you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced, 'Hadha Aliyyun akhi wa wasiyyi wa warithi min ba'di' (This Ali is my brother, my successor, and my heir after me). 'Fasma'u lahu wa ati'u' (So listen to him and obey him). The Quraish mocked Abu Talib. Anyway, that is not the topic right now. In any case, continuously after that, wherever the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) found an opportunity, he introduced Ali (a.s.), and we have hundreds and hundreds of such hadiths. There are hundreds of traditions where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) introduced the Commander of the Faithful (Ali a.s.). Although the opponents, the staunch opponents—you understand what an opponent is. One who was a great enemy of the Shias, whose name was Muhaddith Dehlavi, he spewed as much poison as he could in his book, 'Tohfa-e-Ithna-Ashariya'. As much poison as a man can spew against the Shias, he spewed in that entire book. It is a book of about 500-600 pages, 'Tohfa-e-Ithna-Ashariya'. It is also available in Urdu. Those people translated it into many languages. It is our tragedy that we did not do any work on it. Although in response to it, Mir Hamid Hussain gave a tremendous reply in the form of 'Abaqat al-Anwar', but we did not do the work that should have been done on it. Anyway, so he said that there are only 12 hadiths regarding the virtues of Ali (a.s.). Which the Shias produce for the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Even if there are 12, that is a lot. If we take only 12, then 12 is also a lot because they themselves say that they have none. They themselves say about their own people that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint anyone. And when he did not appoint anyone, at least here there are 12. But then they justify that even those 12 do not prove the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Anyway, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) at every opportunity—and there are many hadiths. For example, 'Ya Aliyyu anta minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di' (O Ali, you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me). That is it. Otherwise, you are the same. After me, you are the successor just as Aaron was. And besides that, many hadiths, the Hadith of Sadd al-Bab (closing of the doors). The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) closed everyone's doors to the mosque. 'Wa saddal abwaba illa babahu' (And he closed the doors except for his door). He closed all the doors to the mosque. And there are many such hadiths. But anyway, now what did these people see? Some people also came. People from other tribes came. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to them, 'If you are bringing Islam, will you fight for Islam? Will you wage war for Islam?' A tribe came, it is mentioned in the Quran. It is explicitly mentioned in the Quran. You should study the verse of the Quran. They said, 'We will fight, but on one condition. Hal lana minal amri min shay?' (Will we have any share in the authority?). If we fight, will we get the government after you? The condition is, 'Hal lana minal amri min shay?'. So the answer came from Allah, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Qul innal amra kullahu lillah' (Say, all authority belongs to Allah). This authority is in the hands of Allah. They said, 'Meaning we will get nothing?' He said, 'If Allah wills, you will get it, otherwise not. You will not get it.' So then they said, 'Then we have no interest in fighting.' The entire Quran has described this in a very beautiful way. 'We have no interest in fighting.' So a verse was revealed from Allah, 'Prophet, tell them, you go, you do not fight. Even if you lie on your beds, Allah will bring such a people who will come and fight.' Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. So the entire mentality of the Arabs was that they wanted power, power. I mean, of course, not just the Arabs, today in the whole world, everyone's mentality is the same. Whoever thinks a little, they just want power. If something is against power, then they have no interest in it. If they are not getting power, then nothing. So they were like that too. Now, these people who gathered, these were a total of 15 men who, as our hadiths say, were the 'Ashab-us-Sahifa'. They are called 'Ashab-us-Sahifa'. Not Saqifah, yes. Although they were the same people who [wrote] the Sahifa. Sahifa means what? Document. These people did what? These 15 people among themselves prepared a document, and this document was prepared during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and it was that if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has appointed Ali (a.s.) as his caliph and successor, we will not let Ali (a.s.) become the caliph and successor after the death of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). There were many discussions among them that, 'But how long will we wait?' And there were some among them who were so old that their feet were dangling in their graves. Is it clear? Now they said, 'Brother, how long will we wait? There must be some solution to this.' So they said, 'Okay, there can be one solution. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is now going for Tabuk.' Tabuk was an event after Ghadir, yes, remember. When did Ghadir happen? On the 18th of Dhu al-Hijjah. After that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—I am telling the children to find out the dates and years. 18th Dhu al-Hijjah, 10 Hijri. Okay? And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) passed away in 11 Hijri, meaning his martyrdom occurred. So now, after Ghadir in 10 Hijri, a small battle took place, a small battle which is called the Ghazwa-e-Tabuk. So when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was going for that Ghazwa-e-Tabuk, the hypocrites had spread so much in Medina that a verse of the Quran was also revealed that hypocrites are spread throughout Medina. 'Maradu alan nifaq' (They are persistent in hypocrisy). There was no one in Medina all around except hypocrites. This is what the Quran is saying. Yes, you understood, right? So this is a verse of the Quran. It is a verse of Surah Tawbah, read it. 'Maradu alan nifaq, la ta'lamuhum nahnu na'lamuhum' (They are persistent in hypocrisy; you do not know them, We know them). Did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not know? He knew. But then, as I said in the first gathering, the Quran was not revealed except with this slogan: 'Iyyaka a'ni wasma'i ya jarah' (I mean you, but listen, O neighbor). So this is Allah saying to the other Muslims, the simple-minded Muslims, 'You do not know that these are all hypocrites. We know them, they are hypocrites.' The Quran says, go and read Surah Tawbah, and then we emphasize. To the children, to the youth, you must read the Quran. Read the Quran, it is the emphasis of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), it is his confirmation. The Commander of the Faithful (Ali a.s.) has emphasized it a lot, he has emphasized it greatly. Read the Quran, read the Quran. A lot, the Imams have emphasized it a lot. Our traditionists in their books... They have brought books in the hadith collections under the name 'Kitab al-Quran'. For example, in Usul al-Kafi there is Kitab al-Quran, in Bihar al-Anwar there is Kitab al-Quran, in all these books there is Kitab al-Quran. Unfortunately, nowadays our children are not inclined towards that, they are not inclined, they have no interest, and whose fault is this? It is not the children's fault, it is the parents' fault. As Akbar Allahabadi says—your father is not here right now, otherwise there is a couplet by Akbar Allahabadi—he says, 'What is the surprise that the children have forgotten the house, while the elders have forgotten the path of the religion of God.' So he says, 'What is the surprise that the children have forgotten the house, while the elders have forgotten the path of the religion of God.' Now what happened? That many verses of the Quran were revealed, verses of Surah Munafiqun were revealed, the entire Surah Munafiqun is a full chapter. There are many verses of Surah Tawbah, which showed that hypocrites were spread all around among the Muslims. Now these hypocrites started a propaganda. What did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) do when he saw that the hypocrites were spread, and he didn't know what these people could do? So the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) adopted a strategy, yes? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself went to Tabuk as Commander-in-Chief and said to Ali (a.s.), 'Ali, you stay in Medina. The hypocrites will fear you. If you stay, they will do nothing. You stay here, I am going to the Battle of Tabuk.' So the Master (Ali a.s.) said, 'Okay.' Now, as soon as they found out that, 'Oh, Ali has been left behind.' Now the plan started to fail. So they started a whispering campaign that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has started doubting Ali's fighting abilities. Do you understand? Look, propaganda is always like this. Do not think that propaganda only comes out in today's age, all that. No, no, it has been going on since that time. There was a doubt about Ali's fighting abilities. That is why he left Ali behind to take care of the women and children. Because now Ali no longer has the ability to fight, he doesn't have that strength. Now, obviously, one man comes and says, two men come, everyone comes, 'O Ali, the Messenger of Allah left you behind.' So Ali (a.s.) felt bad, 'What is all this going on?' So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had not gone very far. Ali (a.s.) went on his horse. He reached the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), 'O Messenger of Allah, these people are saying things like this? That you... meaning I no longer have the ability to fight, that is why you left me behind?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said a sentence. And what a sentence! He did not say, 'No, Ali, you can still fight,' because the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) knew that. But listen to how the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) silenced the hypocrites. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ama tarda an takuna minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di' (Are you not pleased that you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no other prophet after me?). Not after me, prophethood ends with me. The Seal of the Prophets is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), after him there is no prophet, no messenger. But the chain of guidance is continuing. The chain of guidance is continuing, and it is through the Imams. That is why I just submitted that the definition of Imamate they have in their books... what is 'Al-Imamah'? It is a leadership. 'Riyasatun 'ammah' (A general leadership). Leadership is the name of government. 'Fi umurid dini wad dunya khilafatan anin nabiyyi' (In the affairs of religion and the world, as a successor to the Prophet). That is it. This leadership, this is the definition of Imamate. Whoever becomes the ruler is the Imam. But it was not like this among the Shias. Among the Shias, the position of the Imam is very different, that is a separate debate. Now what happened was that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) went to the Battle of Tabuk, to the Ghazwa-e-Tabuk, and the people who were there, the opposing army, they had already accepted defeat, they had conceded. Now the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) started coming back. Now the hypocrites saw that Ali (a.s.) is not with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Now they said, 'This is the best opportunity to kill him. The best opportunity.' Now I submit that hadith to you. Keep reading a little, you just listen, listen carefully. The hadith, now what happens? That they decided that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will go through this path. They knew the path, and on that path from Medina to Tabuk, there was a vibe, a mountain pass. Which went up, meaning an elevation, on which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) went like this, and then after that, the mountain went down like this. These people climbed up and brought a very large boulder along with smaller ones, and they decided that as soon as the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) she-camel passed by, they would immediately push these boulders down. They would roll them, and as soon as the she-camel saw the large stone, she would be startled and throw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) off her back. Once he was thrown off, they would kill the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and the matter would be finished. Now, look at what happened. Allah, naturally, warned the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). So the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—and remember, who narrates this tradition? Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. Remember the narrator's name, as I will tell you something else about him later. Hudhayfah says, 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called me and called Ammar ibn Yasir, and he ordered him to lead the camel while I drove it.' Look at the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) strategy. 'Ammar, you walk behind, and Hudhayfah, you walk in front.' We reached that mountain pass, and suddenly these people appeared from the front and placed a large boulder in the path. Hudhayfah is narrating this. I am reading it very quickly. As soon as it came near the she-camel, she was startled. And she thought of running away with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). So the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) called out to the camel, 'Be still, stay in your place, no harm will come to you.' So the camel stood still. Allah commanded the camel, and by Allah's command, the camel began to speak. In eloquent Arabic, the camel replied, 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, by your command, I did not move a single step forward or backward.' The camel said this in Arabic. After that, what happened? When these people saw that they had failed, they moved forward. They tried to push the camel off the mountain so that it would fall and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would go down with it. As soon as that happened, Hudhayfah says, 'I and Ammar began to fight.' It was pitch dark, but both were very brave. They were together, so we attacked them directly in their faces. Hudhayfah says this. And what happened in that darkness? When we launched a fierce attack, you know, they were brave, all fifteen of them. There were only three of us, and they were fifteen. And after that, they began to flee. Hudhayfah's sentence is, 'And they became disappointed in what they had thought, estimated, and planned.' Everything failed; by Allah's help, everything failed. Now, when they fled and stood on top of the mountain, Hudhayfah asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, who are these people? What is their plan?' It was a very evil plan. Even Hudhayfah was not fully aware of how low these people could stoop. Only the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) knew what was in their hearts. No one else knew. So he asked, 'Who are these people? Are they from the Muhajirun or the Ansar?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'These are the hypocrites (Munafiqin), and they are hypocrites in this world, and in the hereafter, they will be counted among the hypocrites.' After that, Hudhayfah said, 'O Messenger of Allah, why don't you send someone to have their necks struck?' Finish them off. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) then said the sentence which is the entire subject of our discussion. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Hudhayfah, if I do this, people will say: Look, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) kept taking their help to fight, and they helped him win all his battles. Now that he has won, he has turned against them and started killing them.' Therefore, 'Leave them, Hudhayfah.' Why? Allah will take care of them; Allah will bring them to their destination and subject them to severe punishment. Hudhayfah asked, 'Who are these people? From the Muhajirun or the Ansar?' Hudhayfah says the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) named them one by one. He named them one by one; nine were from the Muhajirun and five from the Ansar. Hudhayfah says as soon as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did that, I bowed my head. I said, 'Whose names are you taking? Such great elders.' Hudhayfah did not like it. You must read this hadith. I have given you the reference; it is in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 28, pages 199-200. Allah has narrated the whole hadith. It says Hudhayfah bowed his head, wondering whose names he was taking. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) saw that Hudhayfah had a slight doubt about his words—not a denial, but a slight doubt. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Hudhayfah, does it bother you? You don't like it? Lift your eyes once and look there.' As soon as Hudhayfah looked up, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed to Allah, and in an instant, lightning flashed loudly and lasted for a long time. Their faces were exposed, and the lightning was as bright as the sun, as if it were daytime. Hudhayfah saw all their faces. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recounted all the names he had mentioned. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Look, Hudhayfah, do not tell these names to anyone except those you fully trust, and they must not be hypocrites.' So Hudhayfah would not tell these names to anyone. One of those fifteen men was very worried, 'Is my name on the list?' He kept asking, 'Hudhayfah, is my name among those fifteen?' Hudhayfah said, 'Why are you worried if you were not one of them?' 'No, no, I'm just asking.' He kept asking. When Hudhayfah wouldn't tell him, he once came in a rage and said, 'O Hudhayfah, by Allah, am I among the hypocrites?' He said it himself. He couldn't help it. He thought, 'Now what? They know all the secrets.' Regardless, the hadith contains all the names of who these people were and how they plotted to kill the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). But the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), look, Hudhayfah said, 'Have them killed, finish it.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'No,' and continued to treat them with good character. See, if we found out that people were plotting to kill us, we wouldn't let a single one survive. But he was the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Mercy to the Worlds, a mercy for the entire creation. What strange patience and endurance. And this continued. The same happened during the life of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). What does the Master of the Universe say? 'I exercised patience, while there was a thorn in my eye and a bone in my throat; I saw my inheritance being looted.' What was the inheritance? Knowledge, Imamate, Prophethood. The religion was being looted, the religion was being ruined. Anyone would ask something, and they would give wrong fatwas. Anything was happening. 'Oh, I didn't find water? It's okay, don't pray, what difference does it make?' Is that how it works? Don't pray? Everything was being toyed with, not just the branches of religion, but the fundamentals of religion too. 'Where is Allah? Allah is sitting above.' Does that mean the earth is empty? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was being insulted. The religion was being insulted. The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) was sitting in a corner of the mosque. Ali (a.s.) is oppressed; the oppressed one of humanity is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), remember that. And that is why whatever you do for Ashura and Wilayah, it is never enough. Every person, with whatever strength they have—if someone has the strength of youth, they should use it fully to convey the message of Ashura and the message of Imamate. This is the greatest good (Ma'ruf). The greatest good is this. Whoever has wealth, use wealth; whoever has power, use power. Whatever anyone has, they should use it to convey the message of Ashura and Wilayah. Do not show even a ذره (particle) of negligence in this. See, nothing is easy. I mentioned this to you yesterday; if anyone thinks it is easy, it is not. And this is the way to be closest to Allah. Read Ziyarat Ashura and see what the sentences are. That we attain closeness to Allah through your Wilayah and by expressing Bara'ah (disassociation) from your enemies. Wilayah and Bara'ah—this is the identity of Shi'ism, the recognition of Shi'ism. Otherwise, there are many people who claim to love the Ahlul-Bayt. There are many claimants, but the true Shia is the one who bears enmity toward their enemies. Try to be as close as possible to your Imam of the time, your Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Because the true heir of Karbala is Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). The heir of Wilayah is Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). And the closer a person is to him, the better they will understand this message. The more Ma'rifat (gnosis) they will have. That is why, when I started, I asked you: it was asked of the Master of Martyrs (a.s.), what is the Ma'rifat of Allah? Imam Hussain (a.s.) replied, 'The Ma'rifat of the Imam of the time is the Ma'rifat of Allah.' That is why it is said, the more... now look at the hadith. Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) himself wrote in a Tawqi. Tawqi—now our children are not familiar with Tawqi'at. Not just children, I have seen great people who are not familiar with Tawqi'at. They don't even know how many Tawqi'at are in Kamal al-Din, how many are in Bihar al-Anwar. Which volume of Bihar al-Anwar are they in? They are not familiar with Tawqi'at. Well-educated people, whom I know personally, I am telling you about them. What are Tawqi'at? They are the letters of Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) that the Imam sent. Read those Tawqi'at, those letters. Nowadays, Kamal al-Din is in English, and you can see from Bihar al-Anwar that it is also in English. Go and read the letters. Go and read what Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) wrote. Listen to a sentence from one of those Tawqi'at; it is from Ehtijaj-e-Tabarsi. 'Falyamal kullu imrin bima yaqrubu bihi min mahabbatina.' Each one of you should do what brings you closer to our love. And this is the same in Ziyarat Ashura. The same sentence is in Ziyarat Ashura, and the same sentence is being said by Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) in the Tawqi. Each one of you should do what brings you closer to our love. 'Wa yatajannab ma yudnihi min karahatina wa sakhatina.' And one should distance oneself from every act that causes us displeasure. That which makes Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) angry. If Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) is angry, then a person's world and hereafter are both ruined. Remember that. 'Falyatajannab ma yudnihi min karahatina wa sakhatina. Fa-inna amrana bakhtatun faj'a.' Because when our reappearance happens, it will be sudden. I am reading the Tawqi myself, yes? I am not saying anything from my own side. This Tawqi is in Bihar al-Anwar, it is from Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Our reappearance will be sudden. 'Fa-inna amrana bakhtatun faj'a. Hina la tanfa'uhu tawba wala yunjiihi min iqabina nadabul ala huba.' At that time, no repentance will be of any use, and nothing will save you from our punishment. If you regret it at that time, it will not save you. There is no benefit. The time to do the work is now, at this moment. And as I mentioned to you yesterday, keep asking Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Keep asking continuously. You will see that he himself will open doors for you in every way. The world will think, 'We will close this door,' but Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) will open another door. The world will close the second door, and Imam will open a third door. Believe me, it is just a matter of being close to the Imam. That is why this is very important. Now, generally, this is specifically for 'Ma'ruf' (good), meaning Wilayah and Bara'ah. But generally, what is the identity of a Shia? Let's look at that too. What did the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) teach? Truly, the Ahlulbayt teach strange and wonderful things. I mean, no one in the world can speak like this. The Ahlulbayt say: 'Make it your nature to do good to people.' That is, develop the culture of doing good to others. Once, Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, Imam Hussain (a.s.), was sitting when one of his companions asked, 'If, for example, we do a good deed and later find out that the person did not deserve it, will that good deed be spoiled, wasted, or ruined?' What did the Imam reply? He said, 'The example of a good deed, the example of Ma'ruf, what is the example of Ma'ruf? It is like rain.' That is, torrential rain. That is, the heavy, powerful rain that falls—that is what is called torrential rain. So, what is the example of a good deed? It is like torrential rain that falls on everyone. It falls on the greenery, and it falls on the rocks. And when there is a lot of rain—you see in areas where there is a lot of rain, for example, nowadays—if you go to hilly areas like Lonavala or Mahabaleshwar, what do you see? That even the rocks have some greenery on them. Did the point reach you? Yes? Even the rocks have some greenery. The greenery in the fields is there anyway. So, when you keep doing good to everyone, even those with stony hearts will soften. They will also incline towards you. You will see chances of faith in them too. Of course, doing good does not mean we blindly do good to everyone; that is not it. Doing good means that when you do a good deed, see that the work you are doing—for example, if you are giving money to someone, it should not be so that they go and drink alcohol. No, no, we have to do good to everyone. I mean, if they are committing sins, no, no, not for that. God forbid, if they are wasting it on useless things—you say, 'We sponsor everything'— No, no, that is not allowed, to sponsor everything. If it is a necessity, that is different. But it is not allowed to think, 'No, no, we must do good to everyone,' no, no, no. If you know that this is going towards a forbidden act, or for useless play and entertainment, then one should abstain. If someone is spending money on such things, they will have to account for it. That is a sin, a sin. Otherwise, do good. In doing good, let me give an example so that the matter is clear for the children. And this example is not ours; it is in the Hadith. Would you like to hear the example from the Hadith? It is a powerful example. The sixth Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.), says: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. If a person sees a blind man on a straight, smooth road—a blind man of any religion, it doesn't matter—see, religion or faith is not important here, yes? Regardless of their religion, if they are crossing the road and you take their hand and help them cross, the Imam says—this is not our statement—the reward for this is so great that if the entire earth were filled with gold, even that gold would be insufficient as a reward. Helping a blind man cross the road—just look at how small a task that is. This is an example from the Hadith. And the Imam even clarifies which road it is. He says if the road is smooth, then that is the reward. And if the road is such that there are many dangers, many dangers, and in such a situation you guided that blind person and reached them to their destination—this is an example, it could be anything else—you reached them to their destination, the Imam says that if you multiply this entire world by one million times, even then, it would not equal the tip of the reward. One million times! I mean, what example is the Imam giving? If someone is in great distress—let's give an example—there is a child who is very poor, and his parents are poor. You find the child selling fritters on the street. You ask him, 'Son, why don't you study?' He says, 'There is no money.' 'Do you have the passion?' 'Yes, I do.' What do you do? You go and get the child enrolled in school. You enrolled him, and the child started studying. You paid his fees until he reached the tenth grade. After that, when he went to college, you paid his college fees. Finally, you take him to the stage where he becomes a qualified professional himself. This is what is called 'taking them to their destination.' Of course, what is important here is that a person must first ensure that the needs of their own are met, then do for others. It shouldn't be that there is darkness under the lamp. So, no, first your own. That is why in the Hadith, it is said: 'Start with whom?' First of all, with your relatives. Look among your relatives. And this is a very important thing; I am presenting this in your service. Look among your relatives to see if there is anyone in need, in any way. That is why a great Marja-e-Taqlid, Sayyid Bahrul Uloom, once called his student at night and scolded him severely. At night, the student was asleep. The whole of Iraq, the whole of Najaf was sleeping. He called him, sent a servant, 'Go and bring him here,' and scolded him severely. He asked, 'What happened?' He said, 'Your neighbor slept hungry and you are sleeping in peace?' He said, 'I didn't know.' He replied, 'That is why I am scolding you. Why don't you know?' If you had known he was sleeping hungry and still slept in peace, you would have been outside the fold of religion. If you knew he was sleeping hungry and you slept in peace, then you would be outside the fold of religion. My point is, why don't you know? In Arabic Hadith, a word is used for this: 'Ta'ahhud'. Ta'ahhud. Ta'ahhud means to take care of. Take care of everyone. Try, as much as your circle is, as much as your reach is, to see if there is anyone in need. Is there anyone destitute? And who is this for? This is for material needs. And what are greater needs than this? Spiritual needs. Regarding spiritual needs, there are many Hadiths. Allama Majlisi (r.a.) has brought a chapter in Bihar al-Anwar. It is in Volume 2, Chapter 8—the first chapter of Volume 2. In it, he says in Bihar al-Anwar, the name of the chapter is 'The reward for guiding people.' He brings 92 Hadiths of the Imams about guiding people. One of the Hadiths is that the 11th Imam compares two types of orphans. One orphan is the one whose father has died, and he has nothing to eat or drink. So a 'Kafeel' (sponsor) comes, and that Kafeel takes care of that orphan, sponsors him, and takes care of him in an orphanage. And the second one is the one who takes care of a Shia who does not have knowledge, and guides him. We said in the first Majlis too, remember, you should have a passion for this. He guides him, teaches him, makes him aware of the Sharia, tells him the Usul-e-Deen (roots of religion), the Furu-e-Deen (branches of religion), tells him the Ahkam (laws), the Akhlaq (morals)—he teaches him everything. The Imam says, the virtue of this spiritual guide over this material sponsor is like the virtue of the sun over the stars. Over the stars. That is his reward, that is his recompense. There are many Hadiths about this. In fact, let me just say one sentence from a Hadith, just understand this much. The Imam says, if someone guides spiritually, meaning he just gives him religious education. Two hours, three hours a week, not more than that. If they are children, one hour, not more than one hour. Two hours, three hours. Now teach him the Usul-e-Deen, teach him the Furu-e-Deen, teach him Akhlaq, teach him to read the Quran. The Mawla says—listen to the Hadith: 'Ala, faman hadahu'—whoever guided him, 'wa arshadahu'—'Arshad' comes from 'Rushd', which means to make him grow— Meaning, while guiding him, making him grow. Making him grow while guiding him, that is called 'Arshadahu'. 'Wa 'allamahu shari'atana'—and teaches him our Sharia. Teaches him our religion. Sharia does not just mean laws. Sharia means the path. Meaning, teach him our religion, teach him the roots, teach him the branches. If someone does this work, then what will happen? 'Kana ma'ana fir rafiqil a'la.' He will be with us in the highest companionship. 'Rafiq-e-A'la' means in Paradise, the highest station, which is the place of the Ahlulbayt. The Imam says, he will be with us in Paradise at that station. There is no higher station in Paradise than this. A person cannot even imagine it. Therefore, a person should have this passion. Keep thinking, how many people can I guide? How many people can I bring to the straight path? Bring them to the 'Sirat-e-Mustaqeem' (straight path), keep guiding them. As much as possible, and this should be his nature, this should be his character. And the Ahlulbayt have given another guarantee in this, that if someone keeps doing this work, he will never die a bad death. He will never die a bad death. What does a bad death mean? Meaning Now, it could have many meanings, but one meaning is that, for example, he will not die misguided, and another is that you see many people whose death is very bad; it will not be like that, but he will die a very peaceful death. The death about which it is mentioned in the Hadith in Usul al-Kafi that Allah says—this is a Hadith Qudsi; Hadith Qudsi means those sayings of Allah that are not in the Quran—Allah says, 'I do not hesitate in anything as much as I hesitate in taking the soul of a believer.' This is a Hadith from Usul al-Kafi: 'Ma taraddadtu fi shay'in ana fa'iluhu katarrududi fi qabzi ruhi 'abdiyal mu'min.' 'I do not hesitate in anything as much as I hesitate in taking the soul of a believing servant.' Why? Allah says, 'He dislikes death.' Now, why does he dislike it? There could be many reasons. Because a believer has a sign that he should like death, but sometimes it happens that, for example, you are writing a book, so you pray to Allah, 'Let this book be finished,' then it is not the time to die. Or, for example, you are training some children, so you pray to Allah, 'O Lord, let these children be trained, after that, You give me death.' So Allah says, 'He dislikes death, and I love meeting him.' 'Yakrahul mawta wa ana uhibbu liqa'ahu.' 'I love meeting him.' Now, two or three options have come in the Hadiths—there are different Hadiths—that in some cases, Allah postpones death. He says to the Angel of Death, 'Let him go, he does not have to die.' And in some Hadiths, it is written that Allah says, what He does is that He first makes it clear to him that death is good for him, and He sends two breezes, two fragrances—one is called 'Muskiya' and one is called 'Munsiyah'—and then what happens is that the love of death enters his heart, and then he becomes ready to die. His death is very good. Such are the lovers of the Ahlulbayt. I presented the incident of Meesam-e-Tammar in your service that the Mawla had told Meesam-e-Tammar that Ibn Ziyad would hang him on the gallows. Meesam-e-Tammar said, 'It doesn't matter, no problem.' He said, 'He will kill you very brutally.' He said, 'It doesn't matter, I will be patient.' The Mawla said, 'Then if you are patient in this, will you be with me in Paradise or not?' How many things are hidden in this one sentence! How many things are concealed! In such a small sentence—if we bear a little difficulty in the path of the Ahlulbayt, what reward do the Ahlulbayt give for it? How much reward, how much recompense do they give? And the Ahlulbayt always led by example. Today, I gave you a small example of the Mawla of the Universe. Inshallah, if there is grace and life tomorrow, we will give some more examples of the Mawla of the Universe, and then some things about the companions of the Imam-e-Zamana. Tomorrow is the last Majlis, so we will try to sum it up for discussion. So, this passion was in the Ahlulbayt. In your service, Janabe Qasim is only 13 years old, but Imam Hussain asked, 'Kaifa wajadtal mawt?' (How do you find death?) He is still alive, but he has already tasted the sweetness of death. Isn't it strange? Someone is alive, how can he taste the sweetness of death? But Janabe Qasim says, 'Ahla minal 'asal' (Sweeter than honey). Death is sweeter than honey for me. It is surprising, but it is even more surprising when Imam Hussain (a.s.) raises his voice of distress. He says, 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna? Hal min yughisuna mughisuna? Hal min dhabbin yadhubbu 'an harami Rasulillah?' (Is there any helper to help us? Is there any savior to save us? Is there any defender to defend the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah?) Is there anyone to defend the Ahl-e-Haram? Here, Hussain raised the voice of distress, and there was an uproar in the Ahl-e-Haram. Imam Hussain came to the door of the tent. 'Sister Zainab, what is this uproar?' She said, 'Brother, you raised the voice of distress.' Asghar threw himself from the cradle. He said, 'Sister, bring Asghar, give him to me.' She said, 'He doesn't go into anyone's lap, you come yourself, you see.' Imam Hussain came, and after coming, Asghar was in the cradle, in the swing. Now, I don't know what the father said and what the son understood. What the Imam said and what Asghar understood, but in the Maqtal, it is written that Hussain... He just bowed his head and said something, and Asghar came into his father's lap. Perhaps he was saying, 'Father, I do not have feet to walk, otherwise I would have come myself to be sacrificed.' Hussain went carrying Asghar. When he walked, Rabab was standing at the door of the tent; the mother was standing there. Hussain asked, 'Rabab, why are you standing here?' She said, 'I am watching that whoever has gone to the battlefield since morning has not returned alive, so I thought I would see my beloved one last time.' Hussain consoled the mother, 'Rabab, whoever has gone to the battlefield so far, the oppressors do not understand that he has come to fight. Oh, 6-month-old babies do not wage Jihad; 6-month-old babies do not fight.' Hussain consoled her, the mother's heart settled. Hussain came and stood on an elevated place and addressed the wretched ones, addressed the enemies. He began to say, 'Amma fikum muslim? Is there any Muslim among you? My child has been thirsty for 3 days.' No one answered. Hussain asked a second question, 'If there is no Muslim among you, then is there not even a parent among you? Do you not see how my child is struggling?' You know what 'talazzi' is called. In Arabic, 'talazzi' is used when you take a fish out of water, it keeps gasping, keeps struggling; when its strength runs out, it opens and closes its mouth, opens and closes its mouth. That is called 'talazzi'. Asghar's condition was like that. When no one gave an answer, Hussain said, 'Son Asghar, perhaps they do not understand my words, you tell them yourself how thirsty you are.' Once, the child started moving his tongue over his dry lips. The enemies started turning their faces away and weeping. The signs of a revolution were about to appear when the son of Sa'ad shouted, 'Ayna, Ayna Hurmula? Where is Hurmula?' Hurmula came forward. He said, 'Iqta kalamal Hussain, stop Hussain's speech.' That wretch took out a three-headed arrow and aimed at Asghar's throat. The three-headed arrow pierced Asghar's throat. The child flipped over in his father's lap. Now when Hussain looked, there was a smile on Asghar's face. 'Father, do not worry.' Now Hussain is holding the child, now how should he go? He moved towards the tent, carrying the child in his lap, Hussain moved forward. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, radan bi qada'ihi wa tasliman li amrihi.' He went a little distance, then he thought, 'How will I show the child to the mother? The mother will not be able to see, the mother's heart will burst.' Thinking this, he came back. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, radan bi qada'ihi wa tasliman li amrihi.' Hussain performed this action 7 times. Then finally, Hussain thought, 'Now the child has left this world, why deprive the mother of the final farewell?' He came to the door of the tent and called out, 'Rabab!' Now it is written in the Maqtal that from one side Rabab came from the tent, from the other side Sakina came. The little girl had come running, she reached first. She said, 'Father, have you brought water for my brother? Is my brother not thirsty anymore?' She was still asking when Rabab arrived. Now when she arrived, Hussain pulled back the hem of his cloak. Rabab saw the scene that may Allah not show any mother. A 6-month-old child, a three-headed arrow pierced in the throat. Rabab recited a dirge, 'Ya bunayya, amithluka yudhbah?' Oh my son, are children like you slaughtered? 'Sayalamu-lladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, ala la'natullahi 'ala qawmi-z-zalimin.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Amen. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Amen. Protect the great scholars and the Maraje-e-Izam. Amen. Protect the holy shrines. Grant us the privilege of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Amen. Recite one Surah Fatiha and three times Surah Tawhid and dedicate the reward to the souls of the late Ghulam Ali ibn-e-Abdul Aziz Lakhani, Lakhani family, Rupani family, Himani family, Ladha family, and Narsidani family. Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim.

chapters.title: The Tragic Farewell of Imam Hussain and Sakina
chapters.summary: The narrator recounts the heart-wrenching final conversations between Imam Hussain and his daughter Sakina on the night of Ashura, focusing on her desperate pleas for his return.

chapters.title: Zainab's Lament at the Battlefield
chapters.summary: Bibi Zainab searches for and identifies the mangled remains of Imam Hussain on the battlefield, expressing her profound grief and shock at the brutality inflicted upon him.

chapters.title: Quranic Teachings on Forgiveness and Patience
chapters.summary: The lecturer discusses the Quranic command to adopt forgiveness and avoid the ignorant, highlighting the Prophet Muhammad's immense patience despite the suffering caused by those close to him.

chapters.title: The Early Declaration of Ali's Wilayah
chapters.summary: The lecture details the event of Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira, where a young Imam Ali stood to support the Prophet, leading to the Prophet's public declaration of Ali as his successor.

chapters.title: The Divine Authority of Imam Ali
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the Prophet's explicit declarations of Ali's status, comparing his role to that of Aaron to Moses, and addresses the historical rejection of this authority by those seeking worldly power.

chapters.title: The Conspiracy of the Ashab-us-Sahifa
chapters.summary: A group of hypocrites formed a secret document to prevent Ali from assuming leadership after the Prophet, despite the clear divine appointment at Ghadir.

chapters.title: Hypocrisy and the Strategy of Tabuk
chapters.summary: The lecture explains the prevalence of hypocrisy in Medina and the Prophet's strategic decision to leave Ali behind during the Battle of Tabuk to maintain order.

chapters.title: The Hadith of Manzila and Hypocritical Propaganda
chapters.summary: The Prophet silenced hypocritical rumors regarding Ali's fighting abilities by reaffirming his status as his successor, while hypocrites plotted to harm the Prophet upon his return.

chapters.title: The Failed Assassination Plot Against the Prophet
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) survives an assassination attempt by hypocrites at a mountain pass, with Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman witnessing the event.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Mercy and the Hypocrites
chapters.summary: Despite knowing the identities of the fifteen conspirators, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) chooses patience and mercy over immediate retribution.

chapters.title: The Oppression of Imam Ali and Wilayah

title: Bismillah-ir-Rahmaan-ir-Raheem Ka Kya Matlab Hai?
excerpt: This lecture provides a profound esoteric interpretation of the phrase 'Bismillah-ir-Rahmaan-ir-Raheem' as narrated by Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam breaks down the individual letters of the phrase to reveal deeper theological meanings, linking them to Allah's attributes and the significance of Wilayah. The discourse emphasizes the distinction between Allah's general mercy to all creation and His specific mercy reserved for the believers.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Sallallahu 'alaika ya Waliyyal Asr Adrikna. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) was asked about 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'. The Imam (a.s.) stated: The letter 'Ba' refers to Baha-Allah, meaning the beauty of Allah. 'Seen' means Sana-Allah, meaning the greatness of the Lord of the Worlds. And 'Meem' refers to the Kingdom of Allah. Then the narrator asked, what is the meaning of the word 'Allah'? The Imam (a.s.) replied: 'Alif' refers to Ala-Allah, meaning the blessings of Allah that He has bestowed upon the creation due to our Wilayah. 'Lam' refers to Allah making our Wilayah obligatory upon the creation. And 'Ha' refers to 'Hawan', meaning the humiliation and disgrace that He has kept for those who oppose Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). The narrator then asked, what is meant by 'Rahman'? The Imam (a.s.) said that He is Rahman, meaning Merciful, to the entire world. Finally, the narrator requested to know the meaning of 'Rahim'. The Imam (a.s.) stated that it is specific only to the believers, meaning Allah will have mercy only and only upon the believers. Sadaqa Mawlana Jafar ibn Muhammadis-Sadiq (a.s.). Indeed, my master Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) has spoken the truth. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum.
The letter 'Ba' in Bismillah represents the beauty of Allah (Baha-Allah).
The letter 'Seen' signifies the greatness of the Lord of the Worlds (Sana-Allah).
The letter 'Meem' refers to the Kingdom of Allah.
The name 'Allah' is linked to the blessings of Wilayah and the consequences for those who oppose the Prophet and his progeny.
The term 'Rahman' denotes Allah's mercy extended to the entire world.
The term 'Rahim' signifies a specific mercy reserved exclusively for the believers.

title: Ahle Bait (a.s) Ki Hadeeson Ka Inkaar Na Karien
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the importance of accepting the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) even when they are difficult to comprehend. The speaker warns against the arrogance of denying traditions simply because they fall outside one's personal understanding. By referencing Kitab al-Kafi, the lecture explains that these teachings are profound and require a heart tested by Allah for true faith.
content:
Regarding the teachings, traditions, and hadiths of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), a very important aspect is that if we do not understand their hadiths, it is not permissible for us to deny them. Rather, it is not permissible—meaning if someone denies them just because they do not understand them, then this is disbelief. There is a saying in Arabic: "'Adam al-wijdan la yadullu 'ala 'adam al-wujud," meaning if you cannot perceive something, it does not mean that the thing does not exist. Just because we do not understand, it does not mean that the thing is not there. The first hadith is present in Kitab al-Kafi, Volume 1, Page 401, Hadith 1. And that hadith is as follows: "Qala Abu Jafar (a.s.)," meaning Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, narrating from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), "Inna haditha Ali Muhammad sa'bun musta'bun," meaning the hadiths of the Progeny of Muhammad are very difficult and hard to grasp. However, it is clear that just as the Quran has levels of understanding, so do the traditions. So one level is "sa'bun musta'bun." Now, "sa'b" and "musta'b"—both meanings, the root is the same. "Sa'b" means difficult, "musta'b" also means difficult. But "sa'b" is slightly less difficult and "musta'b" is more difficult. How did the Imam explain it? In the words of the Imam, listen, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: "Ammas-sa'bu fahuwal-ladhi lam yurkab ba'd," meaning "sa'b" is that hadith which, when a person sees it, they do not ride it again, meaning they do not read that hadith, they get scared because they cannot digest it, so it is a bit difficult for them. "Wa ammal-musta'bu fahuwal-ladhi yahrumu min izarihi," and "musta'b" which is hard, meaning one flees upon seeing it because it is difficult. Regardless, there is no room for denial, which is why it is said that the hadith of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) is very difficult. "La yu'minu bihi," now look here, the important thing is that no one will believe in these hadiths except who? "Illa malakun muqarrab," except the angel who is close to Allah. "Malakun muqarrab," meaning those angels, there are four angels: Jibra'il, Mika'il, Izra'il, Israfil; these are all angels close to Allah. So except for them, "aw nabiyyun mursal," or the Prophet whom Allah has sent, "aw 'abdun imtahana Allahu qalbahu lil-iman," or that servant whose heart Allah has tested for faith. Meaning Allah has tested him severely and this servant has been successful in his test. Meaning, "He has been successful." Allah tested him, faith, meaning the test of faith was taken.
Denying a hadith simply because it is not understood is a form of disbelief.
The principle 'Adam al-wijdan la yadullu 'ala 'adam al-wujud' means lack of perception is not proof of non-existence.
Hadiths of the Ahlulbayt are described as 'sa'bun musta'bun' (difficult and very difficult).
Some people flee from difficult hadiths because they cannot digest the profound meanings.
Only angels, prophets, and servants tested by Allah for faith can fully grasp these traditions.
Faith requires submission to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt even when they challenge human intellect.
