title: Majlis 4 | Bandagi | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound concept of 'Bandagi' (worship) through the lens of the events of Karbala and the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The discourse emphasizes that true worship is incomplete without the recognition and Wilayah of the Imam, drawing parallels between historical precedents like the story of Samiri and the challenges faced by the modern Ummah. Dr. Rizvi also clarifies the jurisprudence of Taqiyya, the status of the Ahlulbayt, and the necessity of aligning one's life with the divine commands exemplified by figures like Hur ibn Yazid al-Riyahi and Habib ibn Mazahir.
content:
Listen to a few verses of the elegy regarding Hur (a.s.). That it was in Hur's destiny to be a believer. To be a believer was in Hur's destiny, to be a servant of the court of the noble Master. To be a believer was in Hur's destiny, to be a servant of the court of the noble Master. To be sacrificed by the sword he brought himself, to be sacrificed by the sword he brought himself, it is true it is not easy to be a Muslim like this. It is true it is not easy to be a Muslim like this, the one who wakes up, wakes up from the world regardless. The one who wakes up, wakes up from the world regardless, the restlessness of the heart all night wakes up at the morning Adhan. The restlessness of the heart all night wakes up at the morning Adhan. And when impurity separates from the human heart. When impurity separates from the human heart, there is a brilliance of purity on the tablet of the mind. If the pen is pure, the atmosphere becomes pure, and like a flower, the eye of desire opens in longing. Like a flower, the eye of desire opens in longing, the distance that shrinks while watching. The distance that shrinks while watching, even if the world comes in front, it moves away. Even if the world comes in front, it moves away, and whoever is fortunate enough to have the companionship of the King for a few moments. Whoever is fortunate enough to have the companionship of the King for a few moments, whenever he rises from lowliness, may he be fortunate enough to have loftiness. May he place his head on the holy feet so that Paradise is attained. May he place his head on the holy feet so that Paradise is attained, may the wealth of both worlds be attained from the dust of the feet. May the wealth of both worlds be attained from the dust of the feet, and may this dust become like a rosary in the hand. May this dust become like a rosary in the hand, if it goes with you, may it become the key to the door of Paradise. If it goes with you, may it become the key to the door of Paradise, and Hur fulfilled this longing by risking his life. Hur fulfilled this longing by risking his life, life fulfilled the hope of the night of separation. Today the worship of destiny has been completed. Today the worship of destiny has been completed, and the list of martyrdom began to appear. Look, look at the attraction of the day of Paradise. Oh, look, look at the attraction of the day of Paradise, as if someone has pulled the collar. Look, look at the attraction of the day of Paradise, as if someone has pulled the collar. When he saw that the riders are coming from there to here. When he saw that the riders are coming from there to here, the companions of the King became ready in their places. The sword in the hand of the brave was waiting for the command. The sword in the hand of the brave was waiting for the command, everyone was stopped, everyone was stopped by the dignity of the noble Master. The King explained that we are afraid of guests, they are poor, where do they go if they come here? They are poor, where do they go if they come here? And in what state did Hur come? On foot, he came towards the noble Master. The owner of faith came towards the center of truth. The pain of sins was in his heart, he came for a remedy, he came with tied hands and tearful eyes. Hur requested, 'Do a favor, O envy of the Messiah.' Hur requested, 'Do a favor, O envy of the Messiah, we are dying without death, make us alive.' We are dying without death, make us alive, and we were ruined by making a mistake, help me, Master. We were ruined by making a mistake, help me, Master, what a path I blocked, that the destination itself testified, Master. What a path I blocked, that the destination itself testified, Master, nothing of the world's ways worked, Master. A hope of favor brought me here, Master. A hope of favor brought me here, Master, and we are on the dust carrying the burden of sins. We are on the dust carrying the burden of sins, the heads of the sinners are undoubtedly on the holy feet. The heads of the sinners are undoubtedly on the holy feet, and remorse does not let me lift my head, Master. Remorse does not let me lift my head, Master, the honor of the slaves is in your hands, Master. If you wish, change my destiny, Master. Paradise is in these very feet for the sinners, Master. Holding the hem of the King, he started washing his face with tears. Holding the hem of the King, he started washing his face with tears, oh, such a brave man as Hur started weeping with sobs. Such a brave man as Hur started weeping with sobs. And a voice full of affection came, 'Hur, look.' A voice full of affection came, 'Hur, look, lift your head, do not be so worried.' You have come towards the destination of truth, be thankful. I have forgiven, my Allah has forgiven you. I have forgiven, my Allah has forgiven you, and whenever nations reject the oppressed, whenever nations reject the oppressed, they will call that freedom 'Hurriyat'. They will call that freedom 'Hurriyat', the King looked at Hur with a look of grace. Repentance was proud that it was looked at with a look of mercy. He granted life with a look of miracle, he saw his guest with a look of farewell. He saw his guest with a look of farewell, he entrusted the spiritual connection to the word of destiny. The Master said to Hur, 'Go, I have entrusted you to God.' The Master said to Hur, 'Go, I have entrusted you to God,' and Hur, having taken the permission to die from the King of Religion, left. Hur, having taken the permission to die from the King of Religion, left, his companions left with an increasing aura of loyalty. They left with elegance, they left with the color of eternity, they left carrying Zainab's prayer in the bowl of their hearts. They left carrying Zainab's prayer in the bowl of their hearts, and those who die shake off the hand of death. Those who die shake off the hand of death, this is how those who do it pay the atonement. This is how those who do it pay the atonement, the atonement was paid, all the sorrows were erased. He gave this voice to the King, 'Take the slave's greeting.' May your shadow remain safe, the slave is leaving. His breath began to break, his breath began to break, his speech was choked, and after taking the name of the King of both worlds, he became silent. After taking the name of the King of both worlds, he became silent, he became unconscious as soon as he said, 'Ya Hussain ibn-e-Ali.' He became unconscious as soon as he said, 'Ya Hussain ibn-e-Ali.' When the King placed his hand on the wound, his eyes opened. It was the final moment and the Master was in front. A smile came to his lips, the bud of desire blossomed, and the breeze of Paradise started blowing from the hem of mercy. The breeze of Paradise started blowing from the hem of mercy, Hur requested that my eyes are closing. Hur requested that my eyes are closing, my destiny is waking up, I am feeling sleepy. My destiny is waking up, I am feeling sleepy, and I have received the wealth of both worlds from the sight of the King's face. I have received the wealth of both worlds from the sight of the King's face, the heart found peace, the soul started finding comfort. If the meeting was a duty, then the sight was also essential. If the meeting was a duty, then the sight was also essential, wherever Hur turned his face, Hussain was the Qibla of the world. So where do you turn? Hur broke his breath after visiting the King (Imam Hussain a.s.). Oh, Hur broke his breath after visiting the King. He departed after reciting the 'Mus-haf-e-Natiq' (the Speaking Quran). He departed after reciting the Speaking Quran. And what did the Chief of Martyrs (a.s.) do after that? He attended to him with great care, like the envy of the Messiah. He attended to him with great care, like the envy of the Messiah. He provided a very special remedy in a special situation. He provided a very special remedy in a special situation. He bound the wound on Hur's head with his mother's handkerchief. He bound the wound on Hur's head with his mother's handkerchief. And see for yourself, O oppressor, who died and who lived. See for yourself, O oppressor, who died and who lived. Hur received the gift of life, and this connection to the lineage of purity. Hur received the gift of life, and this connection to the lineage of purity. He received the point of exegesis for 'La-Taqulu' (do not say). He received the point of exegesis for 'La-Taqulu'. And the Master is upon the eye of mercy, sacrificing his head and body. And the Master is upon the eye of mercy, sacrificing his head and body. We will weep for you our whole lives, O King of the Age. We will keep soaking our garments in your grief. We will keep soaking our garments in your grief. By God, it is through your grace that we are better. Our eyes will yearn to weep for themselves. Our eyes will yearn to weep for themselves. When your name is mentioned, they will pour forth. When your name is mentioned, they will pour forth. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and the end is for the people of piety and certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the Worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad, the infallible, from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, the Imam of our time, the guardian of our affairs, our master, our patron, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate friend, the fortified cave, and the succor for the distressed and the helpless; may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our master and leader, Hussain ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), has said: 'Whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped, Allah grants him more than his wishes and his needs.' Truthful is our master, Hussain ibn Ali (peace be upon them both). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. The Hadith I have chosen for our discussion, for this gathering, in this Hadith, the Chief of Martyrs says: 'Man abadallaha haqqa ibadati'—whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped—'atahullahu fawqa ma nihi wa kifayati'—Allah will give him more than his desires and more than his needs. The discussion was about Imamate, and the point was that the 'right of worship' means worship that is accompanied by 'Ma'rifat' (divine recognition). As long as a person does not possess Ma'rifat, their worship has no meaning or concept. There is no benefit in worship if one does not recognize the One they are worshipping. And for Ma'rifat, it is necessary to recognize the door that Allah has created to reach Him—that is, to recognize the Imam of the time. That is, to recognize the 12 Imams whose obedience has been made obligatory upon us. Therefore, as I mentioned to you yesterday, how the situation changed after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And when we present the argument that, for example, there are so many verses and traditions regarding the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), there are many verses. There are more than 500 or 600 verses in the Quran. More than 600 verses discuss only Wilayah. And similarly, there are many traditions. There are many Hadiths, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was repeatedly introducing Ali (a.s.) during his lifetime as his successor and Caliph after him. And finally, upon reaching Ghadir-e-Khumm, he declared that the Wilayah of Ali is the religion, and the religion is the Wilayah of Ali. By saying, 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum wa atmamtu alaykum ni'mati wa radhitu lakumul-islama dina' (This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion), the Prophet made it clear that a religion without the Wilayah of Ali is not a religion. Therefore, this Wilayah holds great importance, but the question arises: if the Prophet introduced him so many times, why did the people not listen to the Prophet? Look, the answer to this question is present in both the Quran and the traditions. There are many verses in the Quran; I will present only two or three for you, which will make the matter completely clear. It is said in the Holy Quran: 'Ma yuqalu laka illa ma qad qilar-rusuli min qablik' (Nothing is said to you, [O Muhammad], except what was already said to the messengers before you). O Prophet, these people who are talking to you—that is, the nonsense they are saying, those who are around you—they are not just saying this to you; all the messengers who passed before you, they said these things to them. That is, their people all said such things. So 'Ma yuqalu laka'—that is, what is being said to you—'illa ma qad qilar-rusuli min qablik'—in Arabic, when 'ma' and 'illa' come together, it is used for restriction. That is, exactly what the previous nations did, this Ummah will do exactly the same. There is no difference in it. In another verse, it is stated: 'Wa in yukadhdhibuka faqad kuddibir-rusulu min qablik' (And if they deny you, then already were denied messengers before you). If they are belying you, denying you, then all the messengers who came before you, they denied them all. This has always been the problem with the majority of this Ummah. This is not the first time. Their job is to belie, their job is to deny. So the Quran is saying this in very clear words. But when such verses are mentioned, they say, 'No, this refers to the polytheists in Mecca, those who did not believe in the Messenger of Allah, and the people of Mecca; it is not talking about Medina.' In Medina, there were Muslims, Sahaba, and so on. So if you look at those verses, if you study them, it will become completely clear to you. For example, in Surah Al-e-Imran, verse 144, it is stated: 'Wa ma Muhammadun illa rasul' (Muhammad is not but a messenger). Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad-o-Aal-e-Muhammad. Muhammad is nothing but a messenger. 'Wa ma Muhammadun illa rasul, qad khalat min qablihir-rusul' (Messengers have passed on before him). Messengers have passed on before him. 'Qad khalat' means they have passed away. 'Min qablihir-rusul' 'Af-in mata aw qutila' (So if he was to die or be killed). If this Messenger passes away—'mata', or 'qutila'—actually, 'aw' here means 'bal' (rather), rather if he is killed, if the Messenger of Allah is martyred—'bal qutila, in-qalabtum ala a'qabikum' (would you turn back on your heels?), will you turn back on your heels and flee? Will you choose to escape? Will you leave the Messenger? Will you leave the religion and go? 'In-qalabtum ala a'qabikum, wa may yanqalib ala aqibayhi, falay yadurrallaha shay'a' (And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all), and whoever turns away, whoever turns his back, will not harm Allah. Never, never will he harm Allah. 'Falay yadurrallaha shay'a, wa sa yajzillahu-sh-shakirin' (And Allah will reward the grateful). That is, those who stand with the Prophet, Allah will reward them, and those who turn away, those who show their backs to the Prophet, they will receive their punishment, and they will be counted among the enemies of the Prophet. Among the enemies of Islam, but they do not harm the Prophet, they do not harm the religion. And there are many such verses that interpret this. If you study the verses, you will find it exactly. And the Quran has said repeatedly, the Quran has said repeatedly, that regarding the Prophet—this is also in Surah Tawbah—that all those around you, they are hypocrites. They are around you, 'Maraduna alan-nifaq' (persisting in hypocrisy). Look at the verses of Surah Tawbah, the verses of Surah Munafiqun; read them all. Look at the environment in which the Prophet was living. So the situation on all sides was such that no one was with the Prophet except for a few individuals who could be counted on one's fingers. There were many in name, but very few with true faith. For example, look at this—the Prophet's famous Hadith, Sallallahu Alayhi Wa Aalihi. 'Wa qala Nabiyyu Sallallahu Alayhi Wa Aalihi, yakunu fi hazal ummati'—the Prophet prophesied, the Prophet prophesied, he predicted beforehand that in this Ummah, everything will happen exactly as it happened in the Children of Israel. And this Hadith is not only in Shia books; it has been narrated by both sects; it is a very famous and well-known Hadith. Everything that the Children of Israel did, exactly the same thing will happen here in this Muslim Ummah. 'Hadhwan-na'li bin-na'li, wa hadhwal-quddati bil-quddah.' (Like a shoe to a shoe, and a feather to a feather). That is, wherever the Children of Israel stepped, this Ummah will step there. And wherever their arrow flew, this Ummah's arrow will follow behind that same arrow. This is called 'Hadhwan-na'li bin-na'li, wal-quddati bil-quddah.' That is, exactly what happened—now you read the entire history of the Children of Israel. The entire history of the Children of Israel is before you. Prophet Musa (a.s.) went away for just a few days, for only 40 days, and what did they do? They prepared a calf and worshipped it. A calf—that is, a calf, a small baby cow—and they said, and who was the one who prepared it? It was Samiri. And he prepared it and said, 'Hadha ilahukum' (This is your god), this is your god, our god, Musa's god, everyone's god is this, this calf. And this—that is, the calf—and Samiri had this power, what he did, just to deceive those people, he did something with the calf so that it would make a sound. He made it make a sound, so that it would make the sound of a cow, and the calf that he himself had prepared was making that sound. That was not a natural child; this, he had prepared it. Now, how did this sound come about? How was this man-made animal producing this sound? So, when Prophet Musa (a.s.) asked Samiri how he did this, he replied, 'I saw...' because Samiri was very close to Prophet Musa (a.s.) at one time. What did he see? He saw that Archangel Jibraeel (a.s.) was accompanying Prophet Musa (a.s.) on his horse. Jibraeel (a.s.)—so he understood that this is an angel of Allah, and since it is an angel of Allah, the horse he is riding is also a celestial horse. So his children asked, 'You have so much knowledge, you have served so much, you have written so many books, and you passed so easily?' He said, 'None of that worked.' Wow. They asked, 'Then what happened?' He said, 'Next to me was a Bedouin, a villager from near Karbala, who was buried there. When the angels came, they went to him first. In Karbala. They went to him, and when they started asking him questions, for every question, he gave the same answer. He was a resident of Karbala: 'La arifu illa sahib hazal qubba' (I know no one except the owner of this dome, I only know Hussain). Subhan Allah. 'I don't know anyone else.' Whatever question they asked, he would say, 'I don't recognize anyone, I only know him. I know Hussain ibn Ali, I don't know anyone else.' He kept giving this same answer. La arifu illa sahib hazal qubba. So the angels, Nakir and Munkar, started looking at each other, saying, 'He is giving the same answer to everything.' They were still thinking when a voice came from behind: 'Let him go. He is ours. He is ours.' That is why you should teach children to perform Matam. That is why you should tell them to mourn for Hussain, to perform Zanjeer Zani, Kama Zani, whatever you do, mourn for Hussain. Encourage them, take them along so they know what our culture is, what our civilization is. And then that scholar says that when the angels were done with him, they came to me. So I said, 'This is a very good formula.' So when they asked, 'Man Rabbuka?' (Who is your Lord?), I said, 'La arifu illa sahib hazal qubba' (I know no one except Hussain). Now, whatever question they asked, I would say, 'Brother, this is the same.' They said, 'Let him go.' So that is why the night in the grave passed very easily. Very easily. This is a very famous incident of a very great religious scholar, yes. And the one who narrated this incident is also a very great religious scholar, very great. Alhamdulillah, we even have his recording. Meaning a video recording, not just audio. You might say, 'No,' and this is from before AI, yes. So you can watch it; it is very old. It is not as if it was fabricated. So, recite a Salawat for Muhammad and Aal-e-Muhammad. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Subhan Allah. So he says, 'La,' this is our Wilayah. 'Wa lam yurakhkhas li-ahadin minal muslimina fi tarki wilayatina, la wallahi ma fiha rukhsa' (And no exemption has been granted to any Muslim in abandoning our Wilayah; no, by Allah, there is no exemption in it). The Imam says, the Imam Alaihissalam says. And you see this same thing in Karbala, when Imam Hussain Alaihissalam reached Karbala, he wrote a letter to his childhood friend, Habib. Now, Habib was sitting at the dining spread, about to eat. Suddenly, someone knocked on the door. He asked, 'Who is it?' He said, 'Ana barid al-Hussain' (I am the messenger of Hussain). My Mawla's messenger. Habib stood up, went, took the letter, opened it, touched it to his eyes, and placed it on his head. The letter started with 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. Min al-Hussain ibn Ali ila ar-rajul al-faqih Habib ibn Mazahir al-Asadi. This letter is from Hussain ibn Ali. To whom? To a 'Rajul-e-Faqih'. That jurist, that scholar, that man of understanding, Habib—the letter is for him. 'O Habib! If you are not aware of our situation, then know that we are surrounded by enemies. You know what our relationship is with the Messenger of Allah. Habib, you are our childhood friend. You are aware of our status and position. We are surrounded by enemies, Habib. If possible, come to our aid.' Habib just read the letter and sat down. He sat down. His wife asked, 'What happened? Whose letter is it?' He said, 'It is a letter from my master, Hussain ibn Ali.' She asked, 'What is written?' He said, 'He has called for help. Hussain ibn Ali is surrounded by enemies.' She said, 'Then what are you thinking?' He said, 'You know how the situation in Kufa is. In such circumstances, how can I go to help my master?' His wife said, 'Then you stay at home, I will go to help the son of Fatima.' When Habib tested his wife, he said, 'O believing woman, the son of Fatima calls me for help and I do not go? I was only testing your heart.' Saying this, Habib stood up and called his servant and said, 'This is my mount, this is my horse. Take it and stand at such and such a place, and from there we have to go to help the grandson of the Messenger of Allah.' The servant took the horse and left. He went and stood there. Habib got ready and left. He was going through the alleys. He was a little late in arriving, and what did he see? That tears were flowing from the horse's eyes. The servant was explaining, 'O loyal one, do not be afraid. Even if my master Habib does not come, I will take you to help the son of Fatima.' Habib saw the scene and slapped his own face. He began to say, 'Today, such a time has come upon the grandson of the Messenger that animals are weeping.' The servant is ready to go. Habib mounted the horse. After mounting, he said to the servant, 'Go, I have set you free in the way of Allah.' freed for the sake of Allah. Now the slave said, 'Habib, this is not justice. As long as you needed service, you took it. Now that the time for the service of Fatima's son (a.s.) has come, you are leaving me behind? I will also go with you.' Habib took the slave and left. When they reached near Karbala, and the dust rose, Hussain (a.s.) understood. Hussain (a.s.) understood that this is Habib ibn Mazahir. He said, 'Rise, rise, my friends, rise. Go and welcome Habib. My childhood friend Habib is coming. Welcome him. My devoted Habib is coming.' When this news reached the tent, Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.) asked Janab-e-Fizza, 'Fizza, ever since we left home, only bad news has been coming. What has happened now that waves of joy are spreading?' Fizza went and inquired at the door of the tent. She came back and told the Bibi that the master's childhood friend, Habib, has arrived. As soon as Zainab (s.a.) heard the name of Habib, she said, 'Fizza, go and convey our salaam to Habib. Tell him, Habib, you have done a great deed by coming to our aid.' As soon as Fizza conveyed the salaam, Habib threw his turban onto the soil of Karbala. He sat down right there. He poured dust on his head. 'Today, the state of the Prophet's daughters is such that they are sending salaams to slaves like us.' I would say, 'Habib, this is just the beginning of the calamities. When it is the evening of Ashura, Hussain (a.s.) will say to Zainab (s.a.), 'Daughter, when you go to Medina, convey my salaam to our Shias and tell them: O my followers, whenever you drink cold water, remember my thirst, and whenever you see someone helpless, remember my helplessness.' Fasaya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqin, 'ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and companions. Remove the difficulties of those who are in distress. Those who are in debt, help them pay it off; those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children; those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar (a.s.) are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the high-ranking Ulema and Maraje-e-Izam, protect the holy shrines, and protect those who protect them. Grant us the privilege of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Repentance and Martyrdom of Hur
chapters.summary: The lecture recounts the spiritual journey of Hur, who leaves his past to seek forgiveness from Imam Hussain (a.s.) and ultimately achieves martyrdom.

chapters.title: Forgiveness and Final Moments
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain (a.s.) graciously forgives Hur, who then departs for the battlefield and breathes his last in the presence of the Imam.

chapters.title: Worshiping Allah Truly
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces a Hadith from Imam Hussain (a.s.) regarding the rewards of worshiping Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Wilayah for True Worship
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that worship is only valid when accompanied by Ma'rifat, which requires recognizing the Imam of the time and the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: Historical Parallels and the Ummah's Denial
chapters.summary: The Quranic verses indicate that the current Ummah would repeat the same patterns of denial and hypocrisy seen in previous nations, specifically the Children of Israel.

chapters.title: The Calf of Samiri and Modern Parallels
chapters.summary: Drawing a comparison between the Children of Israel's worship of the calf and the events following the Prophet's death, the speaker highlights how power-seeking individuals manipulate religious symbols.

chapters.title: Historical Justifications and Taqiyya
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques historical justifications for the events following the Prophet's death and introduces the concept of Taqiyya as a means to preserve religious identity.

chapters.title: The Necessity and Limits of Taqiyya
chapters.summary: Using the analogy of a honeybee, the speaker explains that Taqiyya is essential for survival, while noting that it is not a blanket permission to hide one's faith.

chapters.title: Jurisprudence of Taqiyya and Religious Duty
chapters.summary: Referencing Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, the speaker clarifies that Taqiyya is forbidden when it leads to the abandonment or destruction of core religious teachings like Wilayah.

chapters.title: The Primacy of Obedience to Divine Command
chapters.summary: The speaker illustrates that worship without adherence to specific divine commands—such as the command to prostrate to Adam—is ultimately rejected by Allah.

chapters.title: Prostration to Others in the Quran
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that prostration to others besides Allah is not inherently Shirk, citing the examples of angels prostrating to Adam, the family of Yusuf prostrating to him, and the Children of Israel entering the gate of Hitta.

chapters.title: Taqiyya and the Nature of Satanic Plots
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that Hazrat Yaqub used Taqiyya to protect Yusuf from his brothers' jealousy, noting that Satan often works through human relationships to incite conflict.

chapters.title: The Status of Ahlul-Bayt and Divinity
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that while the Ahlul-Bayt are not God, they hold a status far above ordinary creation, citing Nahj al-Balagha and the teachings of the Imams.

chapters.title: Angels Learning Worship from the Ahlul-Bayt
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates traditions suggesting that angels learned the concepts of Tasbih and Tahlil by observing the Noor of the Ahlul-Bayt and following their lead in glorifying Allah.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that while other religious obligations have exemptions, the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt is mandatory and non-negotiable for the acceptance of deeds.

chapters.title: The Intercession of Imam Hussain
chapters.summary: A narrative illustrates how devotion to Imam Hussain serves as a source of salvation and ease during the questioning in the grave.

chapters.title: Habib ibn Mazahir's Response to Hussain
chapters.summary: The lecture recounts the story of Habib ibn Mazahir receiving a letter from Imam Hussain and his immediate, devoted response to join him in Karbala.

chapters.title: The Message of Imam Hussain to the Shias
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the emotional reaction of Habib ibn Muzahir to the message of the Ahlulbayt and highlights Imam Hussain's final message to his followers regarding his thirst and helplessness.

chapters.title: Closing Supplications and Prayers
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with collective prayers for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time, the well-being of the Shia community, and the protection of the faithful.

title: Imaan Ki Azeem Daleel |  #muharram
excerpt: This lecture highlights a profound teaching from Imam Baqir (a.s.) regarding the significance of love between believers. It explains that mutual affection among the faithful is considered one of the greatest branches of faith. Those who practice this sincere love are elevated to the status of the chosen servants of Allah.
content:
Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, the love of one believer for another believer is among the greatest branches of faith. A'zam shu'abul-iman. Wuddul-mu'mini lil-mu'min, and whoever does this work, min asfiya'illah, he will be among the chosen servants of Allah. Meaning the chosen servants of Allah.

title: Majlis 3 | Hubb aur Bughz | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: In this Muharram 2025 lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual significance of 'Hubb' (love) and 'Bughz' (hatred) for the sake of Allah, emphasizing their role in defining the identity of a true believer. The discourse highlights the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, cautioning against the dangers of personal opinion and the rejection of the Imam's guidance. The session concludes with a poignant reflection on the dignified departure of Imam Hussein (a.s.) and his family from Medina, contrasting their honor with the subsequent tragedies of Karbala.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... [repeated]... O those who are going, when you go to the door of Abbas (a.s.), recite this petition to my master. O those who are going, when you go to the door of Abbas (a.s.), recite this petition to my master. First of all, tell him to listen to my plea, then say that the slave is suffering in his homeland, then say that the slave is suffering in his homeland. Do not bring anything, just bring this message. Recite this petition to my master. O those who are going, when you go to the door of Abbas (a.s.), recite this petition to my master. I know that one does not go to Karbala with money; if you call, the provision for the journey is found by itself. If you call, the provision for the journey is found by itself. If it is written to come, it does not cost a single penny. Recite this petition to my master. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab, do not cry yet, sister Zainab. The shadow of your brother is still over your head. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. The oppressors are not yet near the tents, they have come to burn the prayer mat of your Abid (Imam Sajjad a.s.). My sick brother is still absorbed in worship. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. You are shedding tears while resting your head on my chest; after us, O Bibi, when Baba comes from Najaf, then embrace Baba and cry, my sister. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. Akbar's chest has not yet been pierced by a spear, Bibi; the chest has not yet been brought out of the heart, Bibi. Zainab, look at Akbar's chest to your heart's content. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. Thinking of the veil (Rida), my heart also aches; even after death, I have to bear this grief. The blood on the tip of the spear will also make me cry. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. Sister, look, the arms of Abbas (a.s.) are still safe; do not recite 'Ya Ali' and shed tears over them. If Abbas (a.s.) does not return from the river, then cry. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. I place Sakina's hands in your hands; this is the only request I make to you. If she sees you crying, the innocent one will cry. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. Do not cry yet, sister Zainab. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. A'udhu billahi-sami'il 'alim minash-shaytanir rajim. Bismillahi-rahmanir rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'aliyyil 'azim. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man nasir. Alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin wal 'aqibatu li ahlit taqwa wal yaqin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya'i wal mursalin, habibi ilahil 'alamin Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi ma'sumin alladhina adhhaballahu 'anhumur rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Siyyama baqiyyatillahi fil ard, imami zamanina wa waliyyi amrina wa sa'i. He is my master, my leader, my Habib, my physician, my companion, my confidant, the awaited one, the helper, the straight path, my soul and the souls of the worlds are sacrificed for him. Amma ba'd, our master and leader Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) said: 'Whoever worships Allah as He deserves to be worshipped, Allah will give him more than his desires and more than his needs.' Sadaqa mawlana al-Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. The Master of Martyrs says in this noble hadith that whoever worships Allah as He deserves to be worshipped—the right of worship—if he worships Allah as He should be worshipped, Allah will give him more than his desires and more than his needs. More than he can think or imagine, Allah will give him. The discussion was about Imamate, and for a Shia—or rather, for every human being—it is necessary to seek the truth through their intellect, to understand the truth, and to use the intellect for that, this great blessing that Allah has given him. See, as a person's ranks increase, as a person's virtue increases, their status near Allah increases, and Allah blesses them with special things that Allah does not bless others with. I present a narration to you that reveals the status and position of a lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) near Allah. See, this is a very famous and well-known narration in which Sadir al-Sayrafi, a companion of the sixth Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.)—Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum—is a very prominent companion, a great lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Sadir al-Sayrafi, and many narrations are narrated from him; he is thiqah (reliable), he is called thiqah in Rijal books, he is authentic. This narration is narrated from him; he says, 'I and some other companions were present in the service of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Once the Imam turned towards me and addressed me, 'O Sadir, O Sadir, indeed our followers worship Allah while standing, sitting, sleeping, living, and dying.' O Sadir, our follower is one who worships Allah. Look at what the 'right of worship' is. Look at what Sayyidush Shuhada (a.s.) said regarding the right of worship. Now Imam Sadiq (a.s.) is explaining that right of worship—who can fulfill it, and what it entails. See what the Imam says: our follower worships Allah while standing, sitting, sleeping, alive, and even when dead—in every state, he worships Allah. Standing, sitting, sleeping, alive, and dead (a.s.). So, when Sadir heard this—and he was a very prominent companion—this statement of the Imam was a bit heavy for him; he could not digest it. He said, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah. Worship while standing, sitting, and alive—that is understandable. But while sleeping and when dead—how can one worship in those states?' It is clear, isn't it? Usually, it is said that the 'Talqin' of beliefs is recited because, after death, beliefs can be rectified, but deeds cannot be performed. However, here the Imam is saying that even when he dies, his worship continues; even when he is sleeping, his worship continues. Our follower, who loves us, is like this. Now, look, Sadir said this is not making sense to me. And let me tell you, Sadir was no ordinary man; he held a very high status. He was not like us, unable to understand traditions; he understood the words of the Masumeen (a.s.). There are traditions where the Imam shared his secrets with Sadir. Such traditions exist where the Imam confided his secrets to Sadir al-Sayrafi. So, Sadir says, 'This is not making sense to me.' The Imam replies, 'O our follower, when he lies down and sleeps, at that moment, when the time for prayer arrives and he is asleep, Allah appoints two angels. These are angels whom Allah created on Earth; they have never gone to the heavens, and the inhabitants of the heavens have never seen these two angels. These two angels were created on Earth by Allah. So, these two angels begin to pray on his behalf, as his deputy, until he wakes up. They pray for him, and the reward goes to his account. Why? Because he loves the Ahlulbayt; he is a follower of the Ahlulbayt. Just as I mentioned in the previous lecture, the wood burned, but the follower of the Ahlulbayt did not burn. In the same way, this man is sleeping, the angels are praying on his behalf, as his deputy, and the reward is being written in his name. 'Fayaktubullahu sawaba salatihima lahu'—this is the phrase from the tradition—Allah writes the reward of their prayer for this believer. And what kind of prayer? Listen to this: 'Wa rak'atun min salatihima ta'dilu alfa salatin min salatil adamiyyin'—one rak'ah of these angels' prayer is equal to one thousand rak'ahs of human prayer. One thousand rak'ahs! So, this is about sleeping; as long as he sleeps, two angels keep praying on his behalf. The condition is that the heart must be overflowing with the love of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The heart must be filled with 'Ya Ali'. If this passion exists, then he will be at this station. Up to here, it was about sleeping. After that, the Imam says, 'And when our follower dies, these two angels go to the heavens. They go up and appear before Allah and say, 'O Lord, this servant of Yours, who was a Shia, has now died. His death has come, and You know better than us that he has passed away. So, grant us permission to stay in the heavens and worship You only.' Allah commands them, 'I have no need of your worship.' Go to the grave of that believer. Look, I am giving you the essence of the tradition quickly. Go to the grave of that believer, and continuously, until the Day of Judgment—listen to this phrase of the hadith—keep praying at his grave, the reward of which will keep reaching him. And this prayer will be such that one rak'ah is equal to 1,000. Now, the angels are startled and ask, 'Who is this? When he slept, there was a command, and now that he has died, we thought we would go up and worship Allah, but Allah says no, stay at his grave and worship Me, and keep praying on his behalf.' So they ask, 'O our Lord, who is this fortunate one? Who is this lucky person who has attained Your love to such an extent? Your love—meaning You love him so much? Who is this fortunate one?' Look at the question of the angels. Allah replies. Allah reveals to them, 'That is the one who took the covenant with My servant Muhammad.' And with his successor, meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and after him, with the 11 Imams from his progeny, that he would accept their Wilayah. 'Go to the grave of such-and-such follower, son of such-and-such, and pray until I resurrect him on the Day of Judgment.' So, these two angels go and continuously pray for him until the Day of Judgment, and this prayer is the same—1,000 rak'ahs, 1,000 rak'ahs, one rak'ah equal to 1,000 rak'ahs. After hearing this tradition, Sadir said, 'Master, may I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah. Does this mean that when your follower sleeps and when he dies, his worship is better than his state of being alive and awake? He is worshipping more when he sleeps and dies.' The Imam said, 'O Sadir, this is nothing.' Do you know what his status is? Do you know his rank? Look at the status and position of a Shia, a follower of the Ahlulbayt. Do you know? On the Day of Judgment, whoever he asks Allah to grant safety to, Allah will grant him safety. This is the status. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and his family. So, how is this station and status achieved, and how will a person know if there is truly love for the Ahlulbayt in his heart or not? As I mentioned in the service, which I started yesterday and promised to discuss today, what is the most important criterion? What is the most important standard? 'Al-hubbu fillah wal-bughdu fillah'—meaning if you love someone, this love should be for the sake of Allah, for the sake of the Messenger, for the sake of the Ahlulbayt. And if you harbor hatred, this hatred should also be for the sake of Allah, for the sake of the Messenger, for the sake of the Ahlulbayt. Look, let me present a book to you called 'Wasa'il al-Shia'. Wasa'il al-Shia was written by a very great scholar of the 11th century who passed away in the 12th century, in 1104 AH. His name was Sheikh al-Amili (r.a.). He was a very great scholar of religion, and his book 'Wasa'il al-Shia' is read by all jurists, and they benefit from it. They use it; all the great Maraji'—anyone who wants to become a Mujtahid—must read this book. Everyone is familiar with it. This book is very important, and in it, he has detailed all the chapters of jurisprudence. In it, he includes a chapter: 'The chapter on the obligation of love for the sake of Allah, hatred for the sake of Allah, giving for the sake of Allah, and withholding for the sake of Allah.' He says it is obligatory. Look, it is obligatory that if you love, it is for the sake of Allah; if you hate, it is for the sake of Allah; if you give to someone, it is for the sake of Allah; and if you deprive someone, it is for the sake of Allah. This is a very important thing. What is the red line for us? The red line, the standard, is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Meaning, where there is—obviously, love for Allah is necessary, love for the Messenger is necessary, and after that, the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt is a necessary prerequisite, and dissociation (Bara'ah) from their enemies is necessary. Look, dissociation, meaning Tabarra—we keep saying this repeatedly because this is the identity of the Shias. Everyone praises Ali (a.s.). The whole world praises him. When all the ladies had mounted, Hussein (a.s.) stepped forward and said to his brother Abbas (a.s.), whom he was going to make his standard-bearer in Karbala, 'Abbas, my dear brother, bring my mount.' Abbas (a.s.) immediately brought the mount, the horse. Hussein (a.s.) mounted. I would say, 'O on the afternoon of Ashura, Hussein (a.s.) must have been asking, "Who among you will help me mount, who will bring my mount?" When no one answered, Hussein (a.s.) looked towards the battlefield where the bodies were lying. Hussein (a.s.) called out each one by name, "O my knights, O my brave ones!" Fasaya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. 'Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are away from their homeland, return them safe and sound. O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar (a.s.) are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the high-ranking Ulema and the Maraje-e-Izam. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who protect them. Grant us the honor of the Ziyarat of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in the hereafter. Wa'at-e-Hussein.

content:

There is a way to take a part of it. Click on the link provided or on account.com. If the link is not opening, then open the Google Chrome browser on your phone or computer and copy and paste this link there. The link will open. When the program starts, you have to click on this registration link again. For your convenience, when the program starts, this registration link will also be present in the description and live chat of the program's YouTube video. After the quiz link goes live, when you click on this registration link, you will see the quiz link there. Click on that quiz link, and all the questions of the quiz will appear in front of you. Do not be in a hurry to answer, because there is no prize for answering first. For the lucky draw prize, it is necessary to give correct answers to all the questions. You will get the correct answers to all the questions during the program's presentation and the discussions that take place. After the quiz ends, the selection of lucky draw winners will be done through a computerized system in front of you, meaning... Through the system, it will be done in front of you, meaning it will be live. Therefore, it is necessary to check your details at the time of registration and update them. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that may He hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and through this quiz and the discussions held in it, our recognition may increase so that we can remain attached to the strong rope of Allah, i.e., Amirul Momineen Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Wilayat of his progeny. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.
