title: Majlis 1 | Ma'refat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the fundamental concept of Ma'rifah (divine recognition) as the core purpose of human existence. Using the transformative journey of Hur ibn Yazid al-Riyahi as a focal point, the speaker emphasizes that true worship and salvation are inextricably linked to recognizing the Imam of the time and adhering to the Ahlulbayt. The session highlights the role of intellect, the primordial covenant (Fitrat), and the significance of mourning for Imam Hussain (a.s.) as essential components of a complete religious life.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... When Hur-e-Didar (Hur) came from the side of the King (Hussein), with what joy he rode his mount. The supporter of the oppressed Master (Hussein) appeared; the dear friend of the progeny of Haider-e-Karrar (a.s.) appeared. A light is visible on his head, the manifestation of Allah's power is visible. Where he walks, the earth is illuminated; his body is so radiant that even the soul desires it. His armor is like the arm of David (a.s.). The fairies are stunned by his horse. In the garden of the world, when the spring breeze came, the rider of Solomon (a.s.) appeared in the ranks. Hur called out, 'You speak the truth, undoubtedly, the hem of Hazrat-e-Shabbir (a.s.) has covered my faults. My hem is not empty of the wealth of faith, nor my pocket.' Bravo, the unseen caller (Hatif-e-Ghaib) calls out, 'Having received grace, I have come to fight.' Having heard this, the one on the battlefield called out, 'Yes, come towards the supporter of the King of Faith with spears and arrows.' The massive army advanced with weapons. After reciting the Fatiha, the brave man drew his sword. Hur's face turned red, the army of tyranny turned pale; the flash of the sword became like lightning in the dust. The night passed, the roars of the lion (Ali) shook the bones beneath the earth, like Rustam. The ranks of the army were turned upside down, repeatedly. Fearing the lightning of the sword, even the brave trembled. The time for battle had not yet come, but hearts were broken, banners fell, and signs slipped from hands. There was a commotion that the sword of the King of Faith had struck; lightning moved towards the battlefield to rain fire. With what miracle did that lion move, sometimes stopping, sometimes advancing, sometimes pausing, sometimes moving. The chests of the enemies were bursting like the poor; what was your movement that thousands of necks were being severed? It was not stopped by stone, nor by iron; it took away hands from wrists and heads from necks. His strike was not lifted by any armor; it moved like a contrary wind, wherever it came with a whistle. Showing the intensity of the storm, he went with such grace; in the river of blood, every boat of the body sank. Advancing, Abbas (a.s.) would say, 'Bravo to your courage and soul,' the beloved of the King (Hussein) would call out 'Bravo.' The son of Hassan (a.s.) would say, 'Wow, O brave one, wow,' the King (Hussein) would say 'Mashallah' at every strike. The brave one, receiving the reward for his bravery, would bow down in submission with a smile. Alas, in bowing, the enemy found an opportunity; leaving the front, the whole army came from behind. Bloodshed there, and here... [He was] alone, the horse turned, he was struck by a spear. He fell into the clutches of death, it didn't take long. A mace struck, two sword blows struck. The chest was pierced, arrows of the enemies flew. The lion placed his head on the dust. Ali Akbar (a.s.) flew and said to the Hazrat (Hussein), 'If permitted, I will go and take care of my mother.' From the house of life, the traveler of Adam (a.s.) falls. He falls to the dust from the horse, the brave Hur falls. Hazrat-e-Abbas (a.s.) requested, 'The slave is going.' In a state of emotion, the King (Hussein) said, 'No, my dear.' In my love, the righteous Hur was martyred. What kind of friends are they who do not help in difficult times? When a difficult time comes for them, we will come. Will we go to the grave as a guest of the corpse? Saying this, Hazrat-e-Shabbir (a.s.) went to the battlefield. Seeing Hur fall to the dust from the horse with dignity, the heartless ones fled. The Imam of the two worlds reached the corpse at the final moment. He saw the garden of the guest's life being destroyed, he saw the wounded one rubbing his heels on the dust. Falling beside the corpse, the Master (Hussein) called out, 'Alas, alas, my helper, my supporter! Did a mace strike you, has my back broken? You fell from the horse and did not inform me. In the separation of a friend, which friend finds peace? Open your eyes, Hussein has come to his brother.' With half-open eyes, he saw the face of the Master (Hussein). Under his head, he saw the pillow of the knee of Shabbir (a.s.). Smiling, he looked towards the standard-bearer. The King (Hussein) asked, 'O Hur, O brave Hur, what did you see?' He requested, 'The face of Hur is visible to me. From the throne to the earth, light is visible. O Qibla, turn my corpse towards the Qibla, O Qibla of Faith. Recite Yasin, for this is the final breath. The journey is ahead, O King sitting on the throne. Take my sad soul out of my body. Now, I cannot even speak with my tongue. O Master, blow something, I am feeling sleepy.' Saying this, he took a breath in the lap of Shabbir (a.s.). Sweat appeared on his forehead, yellowness covered his face. The King (Hussein) said, 'Why are you leaving us, brother?' The brave Hur passed away, then no sound came. The bird of the soul took flight towards the Beloved. The pupils remained turned towards the King. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and the final outcome is for the righteous and the certain. Blessings and peace be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the Worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and his pure progeny, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. Especially the Baqiyatullah on earth, the Imam of the Time, our Master, the Master of our Affairs, our Owner, our Mawla, our Beloved, our Healer, our Companion, our Confidant, the secure cave, the succor of the distressed, the straight path—may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Our Master and Leader, Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), the Master of Martyrs, said in this noble hadith: 'Whoever worships Allah as is His due, Allah will grant him more than his wishes and needs.' May the blessings of Allah be upon our Master, Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.). In this noble hadith, he says that whoever worships Allah as is His due—that is, the right of worship—if he... performs worship in that manner, Allah will grant him more than his wishes and needs. Allah will give him so much that he could not even imagine; He will give him more than what he desires and more than what he is asking for. The Master of Martyrs is pointing towards a very important matter in this hadith. This hadith is narrated in 'Majmu'at Warram' by the late Warram. In it, the Master of Martyrs says that whoever worships Allah in such a way—what does it mean to worship Allah in such a way? It means that he becomes Allah's. He becomes Allah's. That is why it is found in the tradition: 'Whoever is for Allah, Allah is for him.' Now, for the one... whose Allah becomes his, he has no need for anyone else in the world. And the Master of Martyrs mentions this same thing in another hadith, which Sheikh Saduq has narrated in 'Ilal al-Sharai'. As you know, there is a verse in the Quran, in Surah Adh-Dhariyat: 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.' Meaning, I have created them for worship. Allah says He created them for His worship. In this context, the Master of Martyrs says: 'O people, Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, did not create the servants except to know Him.' Meaning, Allah did not create the people, the servants... just to worship Him; He created them so that they may attain His Ma'rifah (recognition/gnosis). What is written in the Quran? That He created them for worship. How is the Master of Martyrs explaining it? That He created them for Ma'rifah, so that they may recognize Him. 'When they recognize Him, they will worship Him.' Which worship? This is the 'due of worship.' This due can only be fulfilled when a person recognizes Allah as He deserves to be recognized. When he recognizes Allah, then he will worship Allah as is the due of worship. 'When they recognize Him, they worship Him; and when they worship Him, they become independent of the worship of anyone else.' When he worships Allah with Ma'rifah, then he will not be in need of worshipping anything else—anything other than Allah. He will not bow his head before anyone. People of the world bow before everyone else, but the one who possesses the Ma'rifah of Allah, who recognizes Allah, will never bow his head before anyone except Allah. He will never ask from anyone else; he will not spread his hands before anyone except Allah. This means that when he says he will not spread his hands before anyone other than Allah, it does not mean the ideology that 'you should only ask Allah.' No, it means he will ask through those whom Allah has made His means (Wasilah). It means that which Allah Himself has mentioned in the Quran: 'And seek the means (Wasilah) to Him.' You go and seek the means for the sake of Allah. Seeking the means is the work of the servants, and making the means is the work of Allah. So the Imam says: 'When they recognize Him, they worship Him; and when they worship Him, they become independent of the worship of anyone else.' Then a person stood up and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, what is the Ma'rifah of Allah?' His question was this. So the Master of Martyrs replied: 'The Ma'rifah of the Imam of every age, the Imam whom Allah has made obligatory upon everyone to obey.' Meaning, the Imam whose obedience is obligatory. Now look, where did the conversation start? From the Ma'rifah of Allah, from the worship of Allah, and where did it reach? What did the Imam clarify? That the Ma'rifah of the Imam of the time, the Imam of the age. The reason for this is that the Imam is the one who teaches the method of Ma'rifah. The Imam is the one who teaches the method of worship. The Imam is the one who introduces and explains the correct Tawheed (monotheism), telling what true Tawheed is. If someone does not go to the door of the Imam, does not go to the door of the Ahlulbayt, he will neither find the correct Tawheed, nor will he attain the correct Ma'rifah, nor will his worship be correct. And this is the saying of the Prophet himself. It is not something new; it is a very famous hadith that even children are familiar with, which is called the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. The Prophet stated this hadith many times in different words. This hadith, which is called the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, the Prophet said: 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my Ahlulbayt. As long as you hold fast to them, you will never go astray after me, and they will never separate until they return to me at the Pond (al-Hawd).' I am leaving behind two precious, very valuable things. One is the Book of Allah and the other is my Ahlulbayt. As long as you hold fast to them, you will never go astray after me. And they will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Pond of Kawthar. So this is the command of the Prophet. The Prophet's order is that you hold fast to the Ahlulbayt. Until a person holds fast to the Ahlulbayt, he cannot attain salvation. That is why the example of the Ahlulbayt has been given as the Ark of Nuh. That is why the example of the Ahlulbayt has been given as the Gate of Repentance (Bab al-Hitta). What is the Ark of Nuh? It is said about it: 'Whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind is drowned and destroyed.' What is the example of my Ahlulbayt? 'The likeness of my Ahlulbayt is like the Ark of Nuh.' The likeness of my Ahlulbayt is like the Ark of Nuh. Whoever boards this ark will find salvation, and whoever is left behind will be destroyed and ruined. Therefore, it is very important to hold fast to the mantle of the Ahlulbayt. So, what does this mean? What is the concept of holding fast to the mantle of the Ahlulbayt? It means to learn the teachings of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt and to act upon them. The Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) himself says: 'O people, know that the perfection of religion is seeking knowledge and acting upon it.' The perfection of religion is this. Perfection—that is, the thing that is absolutely perfect, its pinnacle, its glory. Its pinnacle, the very top, the peak of religion is this: that you seek knowledge and act upon it. 'The perfection of religion is seeking knowledge.' Seek knowledge and act upon it. Therefore, when we study this hadith that you just saw, Ma'rifah is a very important thing. Allah has sent man to attain Ma'rifah. See, the first hadith that was read before you, if Allah grants the opportunity, the entire Majlis will revolve around the importance of Imamate. But we will try to approach it in the way that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have explained. We will try to explain it slowly, just as the Master of Martyrs himself has said that if a person worships Allah as is the due of worship, Allah will grant him beyond his wishes. SubhanAllah. See, to understand this hadith, understand the meaning of the word 'Tamanna' in Arabic. Actually, in Arabic it is called 'Tamanni', in Urdu it is called 'Tamanna'. So this 'Tamanna'—do you know what it means in Arabic? In Arabic, when they say 'Tamanna', it means to desire something, to want something that is impossible for him. Wow, wow, wow. That which he cannot attain, which is very difficult for him, but his heart desires that he gets that thing. That is called 'Tamanna'. In Arabic, it is called 'Tamanni' or 'Amani'. He wants to get that thing. The Imam says, if he worships Allah, then Allah will give him beyond his wishes. That is, the thing he considers impossible, just thinking that if I could get this, how good it would be—Allah will give him that. So now, the importance of Ma'rifah will be clear to you, that this Ma'rifah is a very important thing. See, this 'Marifat' (gnosis/recognition) that we have been repeatedly commanded about in this world, our scholars have referred to it in their books by various names, such as 'Marifat-e-Tarkibi', 'Marifat-e-Sani', and so on. This is the Marifat that a person attains after coming into this world—the Marifat that Allah has granted them. Before coming into this world, man was in another world, which in the language of Hadith is called 'Alam-e-Dharr'. He was in that Alam-e-Dharr, and in that realm, Allah introduced Himself to him. And not only did He introduce Himself, but Allah created him upon that Marifat, upon that recognition. And this is verse number 30 of Surah Ar-Rum, in which Allah says, "Fa-aqim wajhaka lid-dini hanifa"—turn your face towards the religion as a Hanif. Hanif means to turn your focus straight towards Allah. "Fitrat-Allah allati fataran-nasa 'alayha"—the Fitrat (nature) upon which Allah created mankind. Fitrat means creation, Fitrat means to create. The Fitrat upon which Allah created man, that nature—what is it? It is the Marifat of Allah. It is Tawheed. This is the nature upon which Allah created man, and having created him, He sent him into this world. Meaning, we were in another world before this. That is a separate topic, which is very vast and is not our subject right now. But when Allah sent us into this world, He placed certain responsibilities upon us. And what is that responsibility? That in this world, we should reawaken that Fitrat, that Marifat. We should attain it again through our deeds. Through our deeds. And for this, look, this is a very important point and a very important discussion. If the children understand this—I am trying to explain it in very simple words so that the children can understand. See, Allah has made this Marifat—Marifat means knowledge, Marifat means recognition, Marifat means to recognize—Allah has made it obligatory to recognize Allah, to recognize His Messenger, and to recognize your Imam. These three entities—recognizing Allah, recognizing the Messenger, and recognizing the Imam—all of this is obligatory. It is Wajib. There is no exception to this. There is no exception to this. It is everyone's duty. It is an obligation upon everyone. And Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) clarifies this in the first sermon of Nahj al-Balagha. See, we will read the sentences of this sermon slowly and explain them to the children so that they know how Allah has made the arrangements. See, it is possible that many people might feel that this topic is very dry. But if you read it, if you read Nahj al-Balagha yourself, it will become clear to you that this is the very aim of our creation. This is the very purpose of our creation, and if someone does not achieve this purpose, then his life is like that of animals; in fact, it is written in the Quran that it is worse than animals. Meaning, if he does not achieve this purpose, this aim, then what example has been given for him? The example of animals has been given. And what has the Quran stated as their destination? It has stated Hell. The Quran has said that they have intellect but do not use it. "Wa lahum a'yunul la yubsiruna biha"—they have eyes but do not see with them. "Wa lahum adhanul la yasma'una biha"—they have ears but do not hear with them. "Ula'ika kal-an'am"—they are like cattle. They are like animals, in fact, what are they? "Bal hum adall"—they are worse than animals. But what happened? What was the tragedy? The tragedy was that the Shias were kept away from the Hadith. Those of our own kept us away, not others. By saying, 'Oh, we don't understand the Hadiths, understanding Hadiths is not our job, Hadith is beyond our capacity.' If the Imams (a.s.) did not state the Hadith for the Shias, then for whom did they state it? If Nahj al-Balagha is not for the Shias, then for whom is it? Therefore, look, we are—although there are many narrations in this regard, very many—but we are bringing only one Hadith for your service and trying to explain it slowly so that the youth and children can understand. Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says that a time came when all of humanity was completely astray. Completely misguided. Which the Quran... In Surah Al-Baqarah, verse number 213, it said. All of humanity was completely astray. Then Allah—then Mawla (a.s.) says that 'Fa-ba'atha fihim rusula'. Allah sent Messengers for humanity. Rusul means Messengers. Allah sent Messengers. 'Wa watara ilayhim ambiya'. These are the words of Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.), yes, not ours. And Allah sent Prophets one after another. 'Wa watara' means consecutively, constantly, without any gap. Allah kept sending them. In a continuous manner. Consecutively, one after another. 'Wa watara ilayhim ambiya'. Why did He send them? Mawla (a.s.) says, 'Liyastaduhum misaqal fitrati'. So that He could make them pay, make them fulfill the 'Misaq-e-Fitrat'. Misaq means the covenant. The promise that we all made in the Fitrat, meaning in that Alam-e-Dharr, before coming into this world. The promise of our Fitrat, which is still present in our Fitrat. Everyone's, whether he is a Hindu, a Muslim, a Christian, or a Sikh, anyone. Whether he lives in India, or in Africa, or in America. Any human in the world, Allah created everyone upon this nature, which is called the 'God-knowing nature'. So Mawla (a.s.) says, upon that nature. The Prophets came so that they could remind them: 'Look, why were you created? Think about this. Reflect on why you have come into this world.' Just to eat, to drink, to earn money, to build a house—even animals do that. The smallest animal, the largest animal, understands all these things. Even a bird understands that it has to eat and drink; everyone understands that. There is no such thing that does not understand this. Every living being understands it. So, the thing that distinguishes man from animals, birds, and other things is that he recognizes Allah and knows the way to worship Him. He recognizes Allah and understands the way to worship Him, and through this, he attains closeness to Allah. He becomes close to Allah. So Mawla (a.s.) says, that covenant, that promise, that covenant, that promise that Allah had taken—the Prophets came to fulfill that promise. The Prophets came so that you people fulfill that promise. Allah says in Surah Yasin, 'I have taken a promise from you that you will worship only Me and will not worship anyone else.' You will not worship anyone other than Allah. So here, Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) says, 'Misaqal fitrati wa yuzakkiruhum mansiyal ni'mati wa yahtajju 'alayhim bit-tablighi wa yusirul lahum dafa'inal 'uqul'. And the treasures of intellect that are present in their existence, the treasures of intellect. See, the thing that distinguishes man from other creatures is intellect. So now, look, Mawla (a.s.) is mentioning three important things in this Hadith. Remember. Three important things. One: Fitrat. Two: Intellect. And three: Prophets and Messengers. These three things are very important. Meaning, these are the three things through which a person can attain 'Marifat-e-Tarkibi', i.e., the Marifat that Allah has given. He can recognize Allah, recognize the Messenger, recognize his Imam, and achieve the purpose of his life. See, this discussion we are having today is very fundamental, very basic. If this matter is understood, Insha'Allah, then the next discussions will be very easy. Now, this might seem a bit hard to you, a bit dry, because this topic is discussed very rarely; there are very few talks about it in the Hadiths. That is why we are presenting it to you and explaining it a little. So, Allah—meaning Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.)—says these are three important things. Allah sent the Messengers, one. So, for Marifat, for recognizing Allah, the Messenger, and the Imam, the most important thing is the coming of the Messengers. The second thing is Fitrat, meaning that thing upon which Allah created all creatures. Especially, He created humans. And the third thing is intellect. Now remember this. Intellect is the third thing. And this is very important. Meaning, if a person does not have intellect, then the coming of the Messenger will not benefit him, and his Fitrat will also not benefit him. Nothing will benefit him if he does not have intellect. So now remember, in the school of Ahlulbayt, in the teachings of Ahlulbayt, as much importance as has been given to intellect, that much importance has not been given to anything else. And the rest of the religions or sects that are prevalent in the world today, whenever you talk to them, when the talk of intellect comes up, they will deviate from the talk of intellect in religion, meaning they will turn their faces away. They will say, 'Brother, don't talk about intellect in this.' This is not a matter of intellect, there is no intellect in this. But the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have emphasized that look, nothing will happen without intellect. Meaning, the Prophets came only to explain through intellect. The Prophets came only to talk to the intelligent. The Prophets did not come to talk to the fools. SubhanAllah. The Prophets did not come to talk to the ignorant. The Prophets did not come to talk to those who have set their intellect aside. SubhanAllah. But we see that there are so many verses about intellect in the Holy Quran, so many verses that you will hardly turn a page of the Quran in which there is no address to the intellect, it has addressed the intellect itself. The whole Quran is filled with it. Now look, we present two or three verses for your service. We will just present them quickly, very quickly. The Quran says: 'Inna fi khalqis-samawati wal-ardi wakhtilafil-laili wan-nahari la-ayatul li-ulil-albab.' Meaning, in the creation of these heavens and the earth, and in the coming and going of the nights, there are signs. For whom? For the people of intellect, those who possess intellect. They understand that someone has created them. If someone had not created them, they would not have come into existence by themselves. There is someone who created them. 'Ulil-albab' itself means that. 'Lub' means intellect. This is a sign for the people of intellect. After that, in the second verse, it is stated that Allah says: 'Kadhalika yubayyinullakumul-ayati la'allakum ta'qilun.' And Allah explains the signs to you in this way, describes them, explains these sciences in this way—all these worldly sciences—so that you may use your intellect, use your intellect. Here the Quran says: 'Afala yanzuruna ilal-ibili kaifa khuliqat.' Do they not look at the camel, how it was created? 'Wa ilas-sama'i kaifa rufi'at.' Or how the sky was raised? 'Wa ilal-ardi kaifa sutihat.' Or how the earth was spread? 'Wa ilal-jibali kaifa nusibat.' Or how the mountains were made? How they were set up? 'Fadhakkir.' O Prophet, you remind them. You just remind them. Your job is only to remind. So the Prophet was only reminding, giving 'Tadhakkur', giving reminders so that people would pay attention to the fact that someone has created us. Someone has created us, and the One who created us, created us for a purpose. The Quran says, the Quran questions the intellect of man: 'Afahasibtum annama khalaqnakum abathan wa annakum ilayna la turja'un.' Do you think that We created you in vain? That you come into the world, eat, drink, play, jump, and that's it, and then you will not be returned to Us? Will there be no accounting? No questioning? No interrogation? All these things will happen. Every single thing, every individual will be asked: 'What did you do in the world?' And you will be questioned for every single minute. You will be questioned about every single thing. This is what the Quran is asking, this is what the Quran is questioning. 'Wa annakum ilayna la turja'un.' Do you think that you will not be returned to Us? 'La turja'un'—this is passive voice in Arabic—meaning you will not be brought back, you will be brought back forcibly. No, even if you do not feel like going, even then... Even then, you will be taken forcibly. If the Angel of Death comes and says 'Let's go,' and you say 'I don't want to go,' you cannot stop yourself in this world just by saying so. That is why there is a Hadith of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) where he says, you know the vulture, in Arabic it is called 'Nasr' (Nun, Seen, Re). The vulture makes a strange sound, it screams, you know? And especially when it sees a corpse, you see how the vulture swoops down on the corpse and makes a strange sound. Sayyid-ush-Shuhada says, 'Do you know what this sound is saying? What is this vulture saying?' Sayyid-ush-Shuhada says, Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'It says: O you who are spending your life in this world, O you who are living in this world, this is your ultimate end.' Wow! Wow! Subhan Allah. You have to go here, you have to reach here. Everyone has to die, everyone has to answer. There is no one who will live in this world forever. Anyway, there are many such verses and many such traditions in this regard, many Hadiths that Allah told man to contemplate and reflect upon himself. You are a servant of Allah, you have been created, you are a creation of Allah. There are many Hadiths about this, and if a person reflects on this, he will understand how important it is to use his intellect. But anyway, Insha'Allah, we will continue this sequence tomorrow if Allah grants the ability and life, that now that Allah has given intellect, how should we use this intellect to recognize Allah, recognize His Messenger, and then recognize our Imam. And how the Imamate of the 12 Imams is proven through intellect. The Imamate of the 12 Imams is proven through intellect. And if a person does not use his intellect, his example is that of animals. So, let us wrap up this discussion here today. It is the first night of Muharram, the night of the new moon, and this is the moon upon seeing which every believer cries and laments. This is the night when the Imams used to wear black clothes and weep, and they used to weep in such a way that they would neither sleep comfortably nor sit comfortably, but rather there was nothing but weeping and lamenting. It is found in traditions, in Hadith, that when Rayyan ibn Shabib came to the service of Imam Reza (a.s.) during the days of mourning, the Imam said, 'Yabna Shabib, in kunta bakiyan lishay'in fabki lil-Hussain ibn Ali.' O son of Shabib, if you ever have to cry over anything, then cry over my grandfather Hussain ibn Ali. 'Fa-innahu dhubiha kama yudhbahul kabsh.' Because Hussain was slaughtered just as sheep and goats are slaughtered. 'Wa qutila ma'ahu ahlu baytihi thamaniyata ashara rajulan.' And along with him, 18 men of Bani Hashim were slaughtered, killed. O Rayyan ibn Shabib, there is no other example like them in the universe. These are the ones for whom the heavens and the earth used to weep, and still weep. O son of Shabib, therefore, weep for them. Debil says, 'I went to the service of Imam Reza (a.s.) during the days of mourning. The Imam said, "Ya Debil, irsil lil-Hussain." Recite a dirge for Hussain.' Debil began to recite the dirge when suddenly the sound of women screaming came from behind the curtain, and the women wept so much that they were fainting. Hearing the tragedies, I would say, O ladies of the Haram, you only heard the tragedies and you started screaming? Oh, come to Karbala, come to the afternoon of Ashura, see how Zainab is enduring the tragedies. Zainab's heart is breaking and she is saying, 'O son of Sa'ad, are you watching? My master is being slaughtered.' 'Fasaya'lamul ladhina thalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, ala la'natullahi alal thalimeen.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are away from their homeland, return them safely to their homeland. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the high scholars and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Those who are protecting them, You protect them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Maah e Ramazan Mein Ahle Bait (a.s.) Ke Liye Kya Karein?
excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual practice of gifting the reward of Quranic recitations to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) during the month of Ramadan. It recounts a tradition involving Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) and his companion, Ali ibn Mughira, regarding the spiritual benefits of this act. The speaker encourages believers to adopt this habit to foster a deeper connection with the Imams and ultimately be gathered with them on the Day of Judgment.
content:
That I have to meet... Imam Kazim (a.s.) presented... My master, I used to complete 40 recitations of the Quran in the blessed month of Ramadan, and after him, I have continued this series of Quran recitations. But sometimes it happens that due to lack of time and busyness, I recite more, and sometimes it also happens that due to being busy with my work or due to laziness, there is a decrease in this recitation. But master, when the day of Eid-ul-Fitr comes, I present one recitation of the Quran to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), I present one recitation of the Quran to Imam Ali (a.s.), I present one to Fatima Zahra (s.a.), and after them, I present them to all the Imams. And I also present one recitation of the Quran to you as a gift. And master, I have been presenting one recitation of the Quran to you as a gift since I have been in your service. So, what reward will I get for this? Imam... What reward will I get in return? Imam Kazim (a.s.) replied, 'The reward for this will be that you will be with the one for whom you have recited the Quran.' Hearing this, Ali ibn Mughira said, 'Allahu Akbar, will I really get this?' Imam (a.s.) said three times, 'Yes.' Let us resolve in this blessed month of Ramadan that whatever recitation of the Holy Quran we do in this month, we will present it as a gift to the Imams (a.s.). Insha'Allah, may He hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and grant us all the ability to be more and more aware of the Imam of our time in this blessed month of Ramadan. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 23 | Tafseer of Surah al-Qadr (97) - Part 6
excerpt: This lecture explores the significance of Surah al-Qadr and the role of the Imams in receiving divine knowledge on Laylat al-Qadr. The speaker emphasizes the necessity of unity among Shias and the importance of studying the teachings of the Ahlulbayt to avoid ignorance. The session concludes by explaining how angels descend upon the Imam of the time to deliver divine commands, ensuring the continuity of guidance after the Prophet.
content:
Masha'Allah... I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the Prophets and Messengers, the master of the prophets, the chosen one, Muhammad, and his pure progeny... Peace be upon you all. Once again, I am present with the Tafsir of the Quran, and yesterday's discussion... Yesterday's discussion... which will be felt in the days of the Imams, that I had said, the Almighty God has appointed His Caliph for His religion and His worship after the Prophet. Just as after the passing of the Prophets, Allah's proofs have been there, and the later ones were performing the same duties as the previous Prophet. After Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), since no such Prophet is to come, after the Prophet, until the Day of Judgment, the proofs have been chosen from his progeny, and that is the Imam. We ask the Imam, but the time has not yet come when the religion will be manifest and there will be a clear understanding among the people because there is a long wait for it. When the time comes, there will be a common opinion, there will be a command, and it has been decided that the first Imam (a.s.) will be finished. That is why they were called martyrs, that we are witnesses over our Shias, and the Messenger of Allah is a witness over us, and our Shias are witnesses over other people. And Allah does not like that there should be disagreement among them... Here, the point is worth noting. The point is worth noting that the Imam (a.s.) says that there should be no disagreement among our Shias. He says there should be no disagreement among our Shias, or Allah does not like that there should be disagreement among them, or there should be disagreement in their knowledge. Now consider, the disagreements that are visible among the Shias, what is it? What is the result? The reason for this is that the Shias have distanced themselves from the knowledge of the family of Muhammad (a.s.). They have distanced themselves from the Quran. How many people are there who find the biography of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)? How many people are there who bow their heads to the interpretation of the Holy Quran and its meanings? Books have been published a lot, and Alhamdulillah, books are available in every language, but how many people are book lovers who say that we make friends with books? How many people will spend time on mobile, laptop, tablet, Facebook, WhatsApp, and other things, but cannot spend time on books? In today's era, libraries are also available on mobile, in which books are present; they can be studied. People have done a great job; they have scanned the books and put them on the net. We cannot make any excuse that the Lord did not provide the means. Every person has time to use a mobile; every person has time to use Facebook and WhatsApp, so we... So we should give a little time to the life of the pure Imams. Surely, when we start doing this, our society will become much better. A little work is needed in the society, and every human being in the society needs to understand their responsibility. Because neither the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) like it, nor does God like it that there should be disagreement among your followers. Therefore, it is our duty to give more and more time to the Quran. You said, 'The person who keeps faith in the Surah and its interpretation, their superiority over those who do not keep faith is like the superiority of humans over animals.' That is, reading the Tafsir, that is, knowing the short information, knowing the interpretation of the short Surah, and keeping faith in it, its virtue is such that it is like the superiority of humans over animals. Similarly, this person has superiority over those who do not have faith. Now think, if in reality, since these are the Surahs that are recited daily, if one is well-aware of their translations and interpretations in a proper way, then what will be the status? You can estimate this; God can know, the Imams can know that the status of that person will be even more... It is that the status of that person will become even more erroneous who gains more knowledge of its excellence, its translation, and its commentary, for this is our responsibility. If God gives [knowledge], then by virtue of those who believe in it, He averts the punishment even from those who believe. Allahu Akbar. And listen to this again: God Almighty, by virtue of those who believe in it, averts the punishment even from those who believe in it. That is, those who keep faith, who believe in Surah al-Qadr, then Allah, by virtue of them, averts the punishment from other people as well. Think for a moment, if we perform devotion, what rewards will be attained? Just as the calamities of the world are averted through the Mujahideen, and in this era, there is no Jihad other than Hajj and Umrah. Therefore, there is a need to reflect. This person asked you a beautiful question: Yes, we know that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) departed from this world, he made Hazrat Ali (a.s.) the heir to all his knowledge. According to your decree, every year on Laylat al-Qadr, the angels bring new knowledge. So, does this mean that Hazrat Ali's (a.s.) knowledge became greater than the Messenger of Allah's (s.a.w.a.)? Hearing this, Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said: Who are you? Who sent you to me? He... Who are you? Who sent you to me? He submitted: O Master, try to understand what I am. When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) ascended to the heavens, Allah Almighty said: 'O Muhammad, these are the teachings of the religion, the knowledge regarding the religion, and my good fortune is that you have brought me here for the religion.' You said: 'Try to understand what I am saying.' He is saying: 'I am what I am because of the religion.' He said: 'Try to understand that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) went on the Mi'raj, Allah Almighty gave him the knowledge of the principles, but they were in the form of formulas and rules, and they were general, the details of which are brought by the angels on Laylat al-Qadr every year.' During the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) life, their details kept coming, and after him, this process continued with his successors. Thus, Hazrat Ali (a.s.) knew all the knowledge as a whole, as the status of the successor, but the details were brought by the angels from Allah Almighty on Laylat al-Qadr. And this is how it has been with the rest of the Imams, that the angels kept bringing details from Allah, for instance, 'do this' or 'do that', 'do it this way', and regarding such matters whose principles they already knew. They already had the knowledge of the principles. The questioner asked: 'What knowledge comes to them other than the principles they already knew?' You said: 'That is a matter which no one has been given the responsibility to disclose, and its details are in Allah's knowledge.' Then he asked: 'Is it possible that the Imam's knowledge is greater than the Prophet's knowledge?' You said: 'It is not like that, rather the successor only knows as much as his Prophet had conveyed to him through the testament.' The questioner asked: 'Can we say that one Imam possesses knowledge that another Imam did not possess?' You said: 'This is also not the case. When a Prophet leaves the world, all his knowledge is with the successor, and after that, the angels bring the details of the tasks to be performed among the servants. The questioner asked: 'Did you not have the knowledge of these tasks before?' You said: 'They have the knowledge, but they cannot execute it until the command is given to them as to what to do and what not to do until the next year.' Look, reflect on how profound the things are that this questioner asked the Imam (a.s.), and I must definitely talk a little bit today, take a little more time. You said: 'Whoever denies it will not be one of us.' The questioner had said: 'Can he not deny it?' He will not be one of us. The questioner said: 'Can he not deny it?' He said: 'Whoever denies it is not from us.' The questioner asked: 'Were they told things in the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that they did not know?' You said: 'Asking this question is not permissible for you. Just know that when a Prophet departs, his knowledge is with his successor. In this way, when a successor departs, his knowledge is with the successor after him.' The questioner submitted: 'How do we know that it comes every year on Laylat al-Qadr?' You said: 'When the month of Ramadan arrives, recite Surah al-Qadr 100 times every night. When the night of the 23rd arrives, this secret will not remain hidden from you.' Continuing the sequence of his speech, he said: 'Every night and day, the devils come to the Imams, and in the same amount, the angels come to the Imams, and on Laylat al-Qadr, a very large number of angels come to the Imams. So, when someone narrates to the Imams that I saw this or that, the Imam can immediately say: 'Oh, you have seen the devils, and whatever you have received is the information given by the devils.' So, the news of the truth comes to the Imams from the angels. So, this is for us, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had said to Ali (a.s.) in the month of Ramadan: 'After me, he is your guardian and ruler. If you obey him, you will remain on guidance, and Allah...' If you obey him, you will remain on guidance, and Allah's majesty is greater than sending His command through angels to some disbeliever. If people say that those angels do not descend upon anyone, then this is a lie, because when the Spirit and the angels bring the command, it is necessary that there must be a person on earth upon whom they bring the command. In another narration, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'If the earth remains empty, then the proof will also be gone.' You said: 'On the 19th of Ramadan, the affairs are gathered, on the 21st, the decision is made, and on the 23rd, the name is signed.' Our discussion on Surah al-Qadr is being completed here. Insha'Allah, tomorrow we will be present with a new topic and a new Surah. Until then, I take your leave. Khuda Hafiz, wa al-hamdullillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Is Dua e Nudba not authentic and too Imam-centric? | Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi

He argues that critics often apply inappropriate legalistic standards to devotional texts and utilize rhetorical fallacies to undermine Shia theological foundations. The lecture emphasizes that honoring the Ahlulbayt is a core component of true God-centricity and that the supplication serves as a vital expression of hope for divine justice. Ultimately, the speaker defends the spiritual significance of the Dua against what he describes as pseudo-intellectual agendas.

title: Ep#20 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) - Ummeed e Jahaan
excerpt: This lecture explores the universal human aspiration for a divine savior who will establish ultimate justice and peace on Earth. It highlights the role of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the promised figure who will resolve global crises like poverty and conflict by implementing a governance model based on the equity of Imam Ali. The session concludes with a spiritual call to action, encouraging believers to pray for his reappearance and actively prepare to be his helpers.
content:
It was issued from... Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Our series of answers to the questions of the Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), the series of episodes that started at the beginning of this month of Sha'ban, today is the last link of that series, our 20th and final episode. And in this final episode, we will try to answer a question upon which the entire universe depends. That is, not only does all of humanity rely on the answer to this question, but until the answer to this question appears in its true form, until it comes before the world, the purpose of Allah creating this entire universe will not be fulfilled. The purpose of sending the Prophets (a.s.) into the world for the guidance of these people will not be fulfilled. And what is the purpose? In the Holy Quran, Surah al-Hadid, verse number 25, it is stated: Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. 'Laqad arsalna rusulana bil-bayyinat...' that... '...We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, so that people may establish justice.' The commentary of this verse is not our purpose at this time, otherwise, the direction Allah pointed to in this verse—that He sent the messengers with two things: one, the Book, and second, the Balance. Has anyone ever seen a Prophet walking with a scale? No, but people have definitely seen such a person walking with the Prophet, pointing to whom the Prophet said: 'Looking at his face is worship, looking towards his face is worship. Whoever loves him has loved Allah. Whoever opposes him is an enemy of Allah. His love is love for Allah.' And he is none other than the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). As I said, the commentary of this verse is not our purpose. The purpose is: 'li-yaquman-nasu bil-qist'—so that people may establish justice. Justice is a different thing. Justice does not mean that everyone is given the same thing equally. No, that is not it. The meaning of justice is: 'to give everyone their due right.' Allah is saying that He sent the Prophets so that... Allah is saying that He sent the Prophets so that people may establish justice in this entire world. And Allah has placed the love of justice in human nature. Every human being is a lover of justice. Every human being hates oppression and the oppressor. Even if he is a criminal, if he is given a punishment greater than his crime, he will find it unpleasant. He will not like it because Allah has placed the love of justice, 'Adl and Insaaf', in human nature. To make man a lover of justice. And not only Muslims, but Christians, Parsis, Hindus—everyone, you will find this belief in everyone that someone will come who will fill the earth with justice just as it is filled with oppression and tyranny. Whether it is a divine religion or a man-made religion, this belief is found in everyone. In the end times, the mention of such a savior, the mention of the 'Munj-e-Alam' (Savior of the World), the mention of a leader who will save this entire universe, is found. Hindus, in this era, mention a savior who will come. They call him Kalki Avatar, who will be the tenth avatar of Vishnu, who will come riding on a white horse, who will have a sword in his hands, and after coming, he will fill the world with justice just as it is filled with oppression. Just as it is filled with oppression. This is what is found in Hinduism. The Zoroastrians, the Parsis, have a place between Ahura Mazda and Ahriman, where it is said that in the end times, there will be a battle between light and darkness, in which Ahriman will be defeated. In a way, Satan will be defeated. Satan will be defeated. Among the Parsis, the savior, the one who will save the world, is mentioned. His name is mentioned as Saoshyant. According to them, Saoshyant is the one who will benefit people and will bring about a revolution in the end times. If we come to the divine religions, the Abrahamic religions, then in the Torah, the Jews have left no stone unturned to erase the signs and traces of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), but despite all their efforts, they could not erase these things: that in the end times, someone will come who will fill the world with justice. The one who will be the savior of this entire universe, the one who will bring salvation. In the Torah, in the book of Isaiah, the Prophet, in chapter 11, it is found that he will establish a government in the land, he will awaken humans. His way will be... his way will be a way of loyalty. A strange thing is found there, that in this part of the book, it is written... In this part of the book, it is written that the wolf will live with the sheep, but it will not cause harm. Although its nature will be that, it will be a small child, and when the wolf comes, it will not harm the small child, nor will it harm the sheep. Such an environment will be in the world; there will not be even an atom's worth of oppression because the world will be filled with justice just as it is written in that book: just as the sea is filled with water, just as the river is filled with water, in this way, the world will be filled with justice. Then, in the books of Hazrat Dawood (a.s.), which are called the Psalms, in the 37th Psalm, sentence number 22, it is written that all the wicked people in the world will be eliminated. Then in the same, sentence number 29, it is written that the righteous people will be the heirs of the world. And in the same way, the Holy Quran has pointed to this: 'Indeed, My righteous servants will inherit the earth.' This was the discussion of the Torah. Now, if we come to the Gospels, in the Gospels, which is the Bible of Matthew, in the Gospels, it comes in part 24, it is written that the voice of the Son of Man will be, and it will be like lightning flashing from the east and reaching the west. In this way, he will come. The one who is coming, first of all, what... What will the one who is coming do first when this tension arrives? He will send his superiors, he will provide guidance from the heavens, and through that, he will gather his companions. This is written in a 'Big Boss' format, and similarly, in the 'Nahj al-Balagha' and the 'Engineer's' writings, it is mentioned that the arrival of the one who is to come will be sudden, and his voice will be sudden. Prepare yourself for his arrival, make yourself ready for his appearance. Make yourself such that when you present yourself before that coming one, you present yourself in a way that he grants you salvation. If we reflect upon all these things, what is the conclusion? The conclusion is that whether it is a religious day or a worldly day, the hope of this entire universe, rather the entire world, is attached to such a coming one who will fill the world with justice. This is the purpose, this is the great divine mission for which Hazrat Hujjat-ibn-al-Hasan Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) will manifest, and the hopes of this world will be fulfilled. That is why the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'If only one day remains in the life of this world, Allah will prolong it until He sends a person from my progeny, from my offspring, whose name will be my name...' From my offspring, whose name will be my name, whose foundation will be my foundation, and he will fill the earth with justice and equity just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. But today, if we look at the state of the world, it appears to be the exact opposite. Justice and equity are far off; today, the situation in this entire world is such that there is no country, no government, no group that can claim that in their rule, no one is oppressed. The gap between the rich and the poor is increasing day by day. On one side, there are people who do not even have the realization or the concern of how much immeasurable wealth they possess, and on the other side, there are people who are consumed by the worry of whether their rights will be snatched away, or their children are being oppressed. Oppression is rampant. Inflation and the prices of essential commodities are touching the sky, due to which the broken backs of the poor are being crushed further. This is the state of the world. On top of that, diseases—even the greatest scientists and researchers have not yet found a complete or confirmed solution for them. Oppression is increasing to such an extent that families are being destroyed due to mutual animosity; families are being ruined. National and sectarian... National and sectarian economic reasons have led to the spread of terrorism across the world. Terrorism has established its roots in such a way that innocent people are being killed. The end of all these problems will only happen when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) arrives, when his reappearance takes place. Because it is narrated that when he reappears, justice and equity will spread in people's homes just as the sunlight enters people's homes. There will be an atmosphere of such justice that it is narrated that a lion and a goat will drink water from the same trough, and the goat will not even look at the lion with fear, nor will it cause any harm. A woman will travel for miles wearing all her jewelry, but no one will dare to even look at her with ill intent. Such will be the atmosphere of justice. Inflation will end because the earth will bring out its treasures. There will be such an abundance of wealth that people giving money will be roaming the streets, but there will be no one to take or beg for it. If someone is told today that the government of Mahdi (a.s.) will be like this, perhaps they might express doubt because the world has never seen such a government, but it has seen a small glimpse of it. It has seen a small glimpse of it, and that too for only four years, from the year 36 to 40 Hijri, when the caliphate and government of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) was manifest. The government about which we only hear, and it fills our hearts with an indescribable feeling of joy. The government of Ali (a.s.) was such that no person would sleep hungry. When Imam Mahdi (a.s.) comes, he will establish the same government of Ali (a.s.), in which not even an atom's worth of oppression will be tolerated. Ali's government was such that those who followed him were called 'Alawi'. People raised objections against Ali, and the one who is coming is Ali's son, Mahdi. How will he be? What can we imagine? And the world will witness it. The month of Ramadan is near; this is the holy month of Ramadan. When people martyred such a just and wise ruler, the days of Ali's martyrdom are near. When Ibn Muljam (la'natullah) was asked why he martyred Ali, he replied that it was because of Ali's strictness in religion. May Allah grant us... title: Why Firaun Did Not Kill Prophet Moosa (a.s.)? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological question of why Pharaoh, despite his extreme tyranny and intent to kill Prophet Musa (a.s.), never succeeded in murdering him. Citing a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker explains that Pharaoh was restrained by the fact that he was not a 'Walad al-Haram' (born of illicit union). The lecture emphasizes that only those born of illicit unions are capable of killing Prophets or their progeny, applying this principle to historical figures who harmed the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his family.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Whenever there is a mention of tyrannical rulers, one name that every Muslim—and not just Muslims, but followers of all other religions—knows as a tyrant and oppressor is the accursed Pharaoh. In English, he is called 'Pharaoh'. He was a person whose story, especially regarding Hazrat Musa (a.s.), is very common and has appeared in the Holy Quran and other heavenly books. When we mention the atrocities of Pharaoh, the first one that comes to mind is that he killed thousands of newborn babies and ripped open the wombs of many pregnant women, just so that Hazrat Musa (a.s.) would not be born. While there is a long list of Pharaoh's atrocities, including the torture of the Children of Israel and the various torments he inflicted upon Hazrat Musa (a.s.) himself, there is one sin he did not commit, and that was the murder of Hazrat Musa (a.s.). Yes, the murder of the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Ilahi). But why? Let us find the answer to this from the people of knowledge. Why is this so? Let us ask for the answer from the 'Ahl al-Dhikr' (People of the Reminder), meaning let us ask the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). A person asked this very question to our sixth Imam, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), and said: 'When Pharaoh said, "Leave me, leave me, I will kill Musa," what was the thing that stopped him?' The Imam (a.s.) replied in his response: 'Qatala man'a-hu' (His legitimate birth stopped him). The Imam (a.s.) said that his legitimate birth prevented him, because no one kills a Prophet or the children of the Prophets except a 'Walad al-Haram' (one born of illicit union). This proves that if a person has a hand in the martyrdom of a Prophet or the children of the Prophets, he is a 'Walad al-Haram'. Pharaoh was a powerful king of his time; it would not have been a difficult task for him to kill Prophet Musa (a.s.). If someone says he did not kill Prophet Musa (a.s.) out of fear, this is a baseless claim. The only reason he did not kill Prophet Musa (a.s.) was that he was 'Halal-zada' (legitimately born) and his birth did not occur through an illicit method, and this is what stopped him from killing Prophet Musa (a.s.). This fact reveals the reality of those who [harmed] the Messenger of Allah reveals the reality of those who gave poison to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), who dropped a burning door upon his beloved daughter Janabe Zahra (s.a.), which led to her martyrdom, and they martyred the children of the Prophets. People should reflect and ponder upon this Hadith and maintain vigilance against such people. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil...

excerpt: This lecture examines the historical evidence regarding Imam Ali's (a.s.) claim to leadership following the event of Ghadir Khumm. The speaker analyzes accounts involving figures like Anas bin Malik to highlight how historical narratives were manipulated or suppressed by opponents. The session emphasizes the religious obligation of believers to propagate the truth of Wilayah and the status of Imam Ali (a.s.) despite historical attempts to obscure these facts.
content:
... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... The third victory, which is the third book, if you start it, you will understand who the person is. In the oil brush, Anas bin Malik... Shah Nawaz, these are the white spots on the face of Anas bin Malik. Who is he? If you go into every hadith under this, you will find the details. Kabir... Tusi... Nasib... We... He said that I have become old and have forgotten, so he cursed the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). And that whole incident is like this. And here is the giver... wait, whose name has also been mentioned, while hitting someone else, and the curse he made was present in the hadith before this one. So, may Allah be pleased with them... those chapters... if you are lying, then in such a situation, we will detail it here with our body as much as possible. As much as possible, and it is not hidden from people. And tell them to destroy their crops until morning, so that this message becomes firm. Thank you very much, Pasina. As we have seen, it has become completely clear that this incident has been presented as an argument in the books, and many scholars have also debated it. They have placed this argument before the people that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself declared Ali (a.s.) as the Mawla, made him the master, and people had formally pledged allegiance to him. It is not difficult to understand that the opponents, as they have done before, have tried very hard to hide the right of Ali (a.s.). And when these people can deny the verses of the Quran regarding Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.), who is the mistress of the women of the worlds, then hiding a hadith or changing it is not a big deal for them. So, our responsibility increases even more to convey the right of Ali (a.s.), his Wilayah, his status, and this incident of Ghadir to as many people as possible. And this is the command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that we should convey the Wilayah of the Imam (a.s.) to others. It is obligatory upon those present to convey this message. Until this message reaches everyone, our episode ends here. Insha'Allah, in the next episode, we will present a new translation and its answers. Until then, goodbye. Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen.

title: EP07 | Inkaar-e-Ghadeer Ka Anjaam | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological and historical consequences of denying the event of Ghadir and the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). It argues that the rejection of this divine appointment led to the corruption of religious practices, the infiltration of anthropomorphic beliefs, and the eventual tragedy of Karbala. The session also serves as an educational component of a Mega Quiz series, emphasizing that true Islamic unity and correct worship are inextricably linked to the leadership of the Ahl al-Bayt.
content:
TSR presents... [Poetry/Chanting in Urdu/Persian]... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless you, O Wali-ul-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Ya Ali Madad. We are once again present to serve you with the final episode of this year's Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz, and we welcome you all to this episode. So come, viewers, let us begin today's episode with these lines: 'By sleeping, he bought all the pleasures of God. Gabriel woke him up and said Ya Ali Madad. And Mohsin, that scene in my grave was strange when I myself said to Ali, Ya Ali Madad.' In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjati ibnil Hasan. Salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi. Fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kullis sa'ati waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Respected viewers, first of all, let us tell you a few things regarding the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz. There will be seven episodes, and in each episode, a discussion regarding Ghadir and the Wilayat of Amir-ul-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) will be presented to you, and the questions of this quiz will be related to that discussion. In each episode, there will be seven lucky winners who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. In which the first prize is 5000, the second two prizes are 3000 each, and the third four prizes are 1000 each. And finally, our Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz's mega prize is the one that every lover of Ali (a.s.) keeps in his heart, that he wants to go to the threshold of his Mawla and bow his head in submission. Meaning, the Ziyarat of Iraq. Yes, viewers, the mega prize is for the Ziyarat of Iraq. Which will be announced in a special episode after this series ends. To be eligible for the mega prize of Ziyarat of Iraq, one must watch all these episodes, i.e., all seven episodes, and participate in the quiz of each episode, and you must give correct answers to all the questions in at least five out of the seven episodes. And from all such individuals, the winner of our mega prize, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. We hope that you will stay with us throughout this series and keep participating in every quiz. As soon as each episode starts, the quiz link will be activated, and the quiz link is present in the live chat and description of this video. At the end of each episode, there will be Ziyarat-e-Aminullah. As soon as the Ziyarat ends, the seven lucky winners of the episode will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. We request you to listen to our episodes carefully and give correct answers to all the questions. Respected viewers, the Wilayat of Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) is that essence in which every person can dive as much as he wants according to his recognition and devotion. To the extent that he reaches the station of 'Minna Ahlul-Bayt' (from us, the Ahlul-Bayt), and without this, he cannot even attain the honor of acceptance of his worship in the Divine Court. Meaning, without this, neither his worship is accepted, nor obedience, nor recitation, nor reading, nor intercession, nor nobility. And Allah Almighty has also decided this, that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is seen saying to Hazrat Ali (a.s.): 'Ya Ali, law ijtama'atil khala'iqu ala wilayatik lama khalaqallahu nara.' That if all people, all creatures had gathered upon your Wilayat, Allah would not have created Hell. Meaning, Hell was created precisely because those who will deny Wilayat. And Ghadir-e-Khumm is that reality of Islamic history which no Muslim can deny. If, despite the event of Ghadir, someone is seen denying the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), then they are making their abode in Hell. Our episode today is also about this very subject: the consequences of denying Ghadir. That is, when the Almighty Allah, through the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), established the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) at Ghadir, it is not as if someone can deny it without facing any consequences. They will have to suffer the results, and we will examine what happened to those in Islamic history who denied Ghadir—that is, those who denied the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). So, to discuss this topic today, we have with us in our gathering Mr. Mohammad Abbas Patel and Mr. Ahsan Jafri. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Ahsan Bhai, we would like you to begin today's discussion on what consequences the Muslims had to face due to the denial of Ghadir. We would like you to shed some light on this topic. Certainly, Insha'Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Billaah Bhai, as the topic of today's discussion is the consequences of denying Ghadir, the first thing I want to place before the viewers is that there is no doubt that Islam is the religion of truth. It is a divine religion, and it is the religion that Allah has chosen for His creation until the Day of Judgment. But on one hand, there is this religion, its truthfulness, its messages, and its teachings, which are divine. On the other hand, if we look at the state of Muslims and observe them, they do not align with those teachings. Today, the name of Muslims is disgraced all over the world. Why is this? What was the reason? What were the causes that led the followers of this divine religion, those who raise the slogan of the Kalima of Tawhid, those who recite the Kalima of Tawhid, and those who believe in that Eternal God, to face these calamities today? This was pointed towards, and its reasons are found in history. The biggest reason found for this is our topic today, which is the denial of Ghadir. Yes. The denial of the Wilayah of the Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). It is found in history that three days after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Janab-e-Salman al-Muhammadi (r.a.) delivered a sermon in Masjid al-Nabawi. This happened on the third day after the Prophet's martyrdom. By then, the allegiance had already taken place; people had abandoned the Master of the Universe and chosen their own Caliph. The event of Saqifah had been completed. Janab-e-Salman saw these things with his own eyes. Janab-e-Salman rejected that allegiance because he remained steadfast on the allegiance he had given at Ghadir at the hands of the Master of the Universe. Now, Janab-e-Salman goes to the pulpit and addresses the people. Although it is a long sermon, I want to present the relevant sentences that connect to our topic today to the viewers. Janab-e-Salman says—and these are the words of Janab-e-Salman, and no one has any doubt about the personality of Janab-e-Salman, who was honored with the status of 'Minna Ahl al-Bayt'—Janab-e-Salman says: 'Ama walladhi nafsu Salman-i bi-yadihi' (I swear by the One in whose power is the soul of Salman). He is taking a solemn oath, swearing by Allah. And he is saying to the people: 'Law wallaytumuha Aliyan alayhi-s-salam' (If you had entrusted this Wilayah to Ali (a.s.)). If you had remained steadfast on his Wilayah, what would have happened to you? What would have been the results? 'La-akaltum min fawqikum wa min tahti arjulikum' (You would have been provided sustenance from above you and from beneath your feet). That is, the heavens and the earth would have provided you with sustenance. And then, 'Wa law da'awtumu-t-tayra fi jawwi-s-sama'i la-ajabatkum' (And if you had beckoned a bird flying in the sky, it would have responded to you). That bird would have come to you. 'Wa law da'awtum hitanan mina-l-bahri la-atatkum' (And if you had called the fish from the sea, they would have come to you). This means people would have had this power. This authority over the creation, over other creatures, this power would have belonged to humans. To those who accepted the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). 'Wa lamma 'ala waliyyu-llahi' (And a Wali of Allah would never be poor). 'Wa la tasha lakum sahmin min fara'idi-llahi' (And not a single portion of Allah's obligations would have been lost or scattered). This means if the obligations are being sacrificed, the reason is the denial of Ghadir. The reason is the denial of Wilayah. 'Wa la-khtalafa ithnani fi hukmi-llahi' (And no two people would have differed on a command of Allah), if people had accepted the Wilayah. But Janab-e-Salman says further: 'Wa lakin abaytum' (But you refused). And what did you do with this Wilayah? 'Wa wallaytumuha ghayrahu' (And you gave this Wilayah into the hands of someone else). So now, what will be your result? 'Fa-abshiru bi-l-bala'i' (Now I give you the glad tidings of calamities). This word 'bashara' is used for good news, but here Janab-e-Salman is warning them that now calamities will break upon you; be warned. 'Wa-qnutu mina-r-rakha'i' (And do not hope for comfort and ease). No, this humiliation and disgrace is now the fate of the Muslims. Why? Because they denied the Wilayah. You chose this yourselves. They chose this thing themselves. 'Wa qad nabadhtumu-hu 'ala sawa'in' (And we will continue to fight you on this issue, we will continue to fight equally). That is, we will not sit silently, says Janab-e-Salman. Those who have affirmed it will never sit silently. We will keep reminding you again and again: what is the reason for your humiliation and disgrace today? It is the same denial of the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). We will keep reminding you of this. We, too, who are bringing this episode of 'Paimana-e-Ilahi, Ghadir', are doing the same—reminding people of what happened at Ghadir. Indeed. This is the Sunnah of Janab-e-Salman. It is the Sunnah of Janab-e-Salman, who is at the status of 'Minna Ahl al-Bayt'. And then, in the end, Janab-e-Salman says: 'Fanqata'ati-l-'ismatu fima bayni wa baynakum mina-l-wala'i' (And because of accepting this Wilayah, the protection that we used to provide each other, I am now withdrawing that hand of protection from you). We will not come to save you anymore. Because until yesterday, we were under the same Wilayah, both you and we were under the shadow of the Wilayah of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), so protecting each other's lives and property was our responsibility. But now, if you face troubles—and you certainly will—we will not come to save you. You are responsible for it yourself, because you are the ones responsible for it. This is what Janab-e-Salman is saying. And Ahsan Bhai, here, the sermon of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), the sermon of Fadak, also uses similar words that the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.) used, which shows us what the effect was on those who denied the Wilayah. The Princess of the Worlds (s.a.) says: 'Baqiyatan ka-l-'ari mawsumatan bi-ghadabi-l-jabbar' (Everlasting disgrace is branded on your foreheads due to the wrath of the Almighty). 'Wa shanari-l-abadi mawsulatan bi-n-nar' (And eternal shame connected to the Fire). This means the result of denying Wilayah will be—and its consequence will be—that whoever denied the Wilayah in this world, their abode in the hereafter will be Hell. This is what the Princess is saying. And who is the Princess? She is Siddiqa-e-Tahira. If Siddiqa is passing a verdict on someone that they will be a dweller of Hell, then there is no room for any doubt or suspicion in this. And here in this world, too, for them, there is always humiliation and disgrace. Indeed, as we all see. The Wilayah, the state of Muslims that is visible in the world, there is disgrace and infamy everywhere. That is, this was prophesied just three days after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) departed from this world. And that too by great personalities; who can compete with the personality of the Princess? The personality of Janab-e-Salman, who is 'Minna Ahl al-Bayt'. So, Gulzar Bhai, it didn't start after the Prophet, but during the lifetime of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) itself, this attempt had begun. That is, when the Prophet requested a pen and paper and ordered, 'Bring me a pen and paper,' which is known as 'Raziyat al-Khamis'—it is present in books, in books of Hadith, in the books of the opponents, and in our books, both.
