By killing the grandson of the Messenger. From the Messenger. And that Abu Jahl upon whom the Quran has cursed. Yes. Whoever defends such a cursed one is himself cursed. Indeed. And yet, one is surprised at those who do not curse Yazid. And then in the end he says, 'Lastu min Khindafin illam antaqim min Bani Ahmada ma kana fa'al' (I am not from Khindaf if I do not take revenge from the children of Ahmad for what they did). That if I had not taken revenge, I would not be from the people of Badr and the people of Khindaf, from their lineage. I have taken revenge today, I have hidden the revenge of the children of Ahmad. Meaning, such enmity, such malice Yazid and, meaning, the family of Yazid had towards the family of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Muslims had to bear the result of denying Ghadir that they had to accept such a person as Caliph. Such a person as Caliph, and today this is the reason. This denial of Ghadir, denial of Wilayah, is why Muslims are scattered today. Indeed. Today there is disagreement among them. Today the many sects that are seen, the many different groups that are seen. Indeed. That is the result of that denial of Ghadir. Whereas what did the Quran say to the Muslims? The Quran said for the Muslims, 'Wa'tasimu bi-hablillahi jami'an' (And hold fast to the rope of Allah, all of you together). Indeed. 'Wala tafarraqu' (And do not be divided). Look, do not be divided. Surah Ale-Imran, verse number 103. Do not be divided. Just by stating this last thing, we will take leave from the viewers. Meaning, in the interpretation of this verse, in the interpretation of this verse, Hazrat Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) himself says that when explaining this verse, the Imam (a.s.) says, what is meant by 'Wala tafarraqu'? There is division among Muslims today, right? Every human wants to remove division. Every human, indeed. Unity is a very good thing. It is truly a good thing. Indeed. But what is its condition? The condition is what the Quran has set, and that is to hold fast to the rope of Allah. This is the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) that if people hold onto it, then they will not be divided. Indeed. And Imam Baqir (a.s.) is also pointing towards this. What is meant by 'Wala tafarraqu'? Imam (a.s.) says that Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala knew. What? That they would surely divide after their Prophet. Immediately after the Prophet left, they would all become divided. Indeed. They would split into factions. There would be division among them. Allah knew this. And they would differ; there would be disagreement among them. That is why Allah forbade them from this division. He forbade them from division, just as He forbade those who came before them. Allah forbade them. Then Allah commanded them to gather, to become united, to establish unity upon the Wilayah of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.). The Wilayah of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.). And if, truly, if a human being wants to return to the message of Ghadir, if Muslims want to return to the true religion, The center of unity for Muslims, meaning the center of unity, is Ghadir and it is the Wilayah of the Ahl-e-Bait-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). If this is abandoned, then those people will remain divided into factions and will never be able to stand on one platform, and unity will never be established. And if they try to establish unity through any path other than Ghadir, it is not even possible. It is simply not possible. When Allah is showing the path, what else could anyone bring? Indeed. Indeed. And Ahsan Bhai, this division is not just about minor things, meaning a few small differences. Rather, this division is such that their entire Islam has become different. Now, because of abandoning Ghadir, between those who have held onto Ghadir and those who have abandoned it, it is not a 5% or 10% difference, as people say. Actually, nothing is the same except facing the Kaaba. Meaning, they also face the Kaaba in their worship, and we also face the Kaaba in our worship. The prayer being performed while facing the Kaaba, that is the only thing—and these are the words of the Imam—the narrator says to Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) that I mentioned these 'Ashab-e-Ahwa' (followers of whims) before Abu Abdullah (a.s.). Look, here terms like 'opponents' or 'Ahwa' have been used. Those who follow their own desires. They followed their whims and denied Allah's command. Following their whims, they appointed their own Caliph. The companions of the Imam (a.s.) used to refer to the opponents by these names. I mentioned them before Imam Sadiq (a.s.). He said, 'No, by Allah, they are not following anything that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) brought,' except for facing the Kaaba. Meaning, it is not that there is a 5% or 6% difference between us and them. Rather, there is no similarity except for facing the Kaaba in worship, which they do and we also do. Because their Tawheed has changed, their Adl (justice) has changed, and regarding Prophethood, various slanders were cast upon the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and accusations were leveled against him. We could not even reach this topic, the topic of how much they slandered the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). This topic is so vast that it actually requires multiple lectures. Yes. And it is not just about abandoning, Gulzar Bhai. It was not just that they abandoned Ghadir, but there was actual malice towards Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) in their hearts, which brought them to this point, and this became their state, the result of which they are facing today. Their double-faced attitude is clearly visible. When it comes to their third Caliph, that people killed him and surrounded him, they call those people rioters. Yes. And they call them criminals and say they were rebels, without caring that among them were people who were among the 'Ashara-e-Mubashara' (the ten promised paradise). They did not care about that either and called them rebels, criminals, and leveled every kind of accusation against them. They gave them all sorts of titles. But when it came to the killers of Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.), they are sometimes seen praising the Kharijites. Now, the interesting thing is, as Ghadir Sahab mentioned, this one about Imam Sadiq (a.s.) too, right? It is truly surprising, and sometimes a person is left in awe that the one thing they have in common, which is facing the Kaaba, is also the very place where Ali (a.s.) was born. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. Meaning, no matter what happens, no matter what these people do, indeed, they cannot turn their faces away from Ali (a.s.). Wherever they go, they will have to face Ali (a.s.). Allah has made such an arrangement. Allah has made such an arrangement. Indeed, indeed, indeed. And Insha'Allah, when Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) reappears, the entire Ummah will be united under the shadow of his banner. Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah. We are very grateful to you for shedding light on this topic with such excellent arguments. So viewers, in this episode, we saw how those who denied Ghadir, meaning the Wilayah of Amir-ul-Momineen Ali ibn-e-Abi Talib (a.s.), denied the Wilayah, how they became distant from their religion, distant from the Quran, distant from the teachings of their Prophet, and how they are not even able to practice their Sharia correctly. The reason for this is that they denied Ghadir. And a very beautiful point that came at the end is that if Muslims want to stay away from division and have unity among themselves, the best path for that, which Allah Himself stated in the Holy Quran, is to hold firmly to the rope of Allah. And our 'The Strong Rooh' team's effort is also that this Wilayah should be presented to people in such a way that they understand it, acknowledge it, and there is unity among Muslims. There is not even a hint of hurting anyone's feelings here, because these four lines are: 'Just look, to get the certificate of slavery, the Caliphate itself comes to our doorstep.' Yes. 'We did not say anything bad by taking anyone's name, yes, but the matter comes back to where it belongs.' Indeed. Wah wah. 'Yes, but the matter comes back to where it belongs.' So, viewers, with this, we bid you farewell. But before we go, let us tell you that our episode today will conclude with Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, and immediately after Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, our seven lucky draw winners for today's episode will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. If you have not yet answered the quiz, go to the quiz link immediately and provide the correct answers to all questions. Viewers, before we go, one important announcement for you: tomorrow will be our special episode in which the winner of the mega prize of our 'Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi' mega quiz will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system, and the winner of this mega prize will be one of those who have given correct answers to all questions in at least five of our seven episodes. So viewers, do not forget to watch our special episode tomorrow, in which the mega winner of the mega quiz will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Until then, we bid you farewell. Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Before announcing the winners of this final episode today, we want to thank all of you for staying with us throughout this entire series and not only watching the videos and participating in the quiz, but we are also grateful to you for encouraging us with your prayers. Please listen to this important announcement in this final episode: as mentioned, if someone has given correct answers to all questions in five out of seven episodes, they will be eligible for the mega prize, i.e., the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq. title: Rizq Ke Khazaane Ki Chaabi | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the spiritual and practical keys to increasing one's sustenance (Rizq) based on the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. He emphasizes that maintaining a loving home environment, cultivating excellent character, and feeding others are direct catalysts for divine provision. By prioritizing these virtues, a believer can attract Allah's blessings and ensure both worldly and spiritual prosperity.
content:
Usually, people are worried about their sustenance (Rizq). If we study the teachings of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), we will see that some things have been stated very clearly. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Man hassan birrahu ahli baytihi zeeda fi rizqihi' (Whoever treats his family well, his sustenance is increased). Whoever lives very well with their family, with great gentleness, and treats them with love and affection, their sustenance increases; Allah increases their provision. So, this is a very important first thing: a person should keep the home environment very good. When the home environment is good, the house is like paradise, and all the residents look forward to going home. When the house is like paradise, Allah sends down sustenance upon such homes and increases their provision. This is one thing. The second thing, Imam says, Hazrat Amir (a.s.) says: 'Fi sa'atil akhlaqi kunuzul arzaq' (In the breadth of character lie the treasures of sustenance). That is, in good character, in good ethics, in treating everyone with the best conduct, the treasures of sustenance are present. If someone wants the treasure of sustenance, they should treat people very well, behave well, and not treat them with harshness or sharp-tongued behavior. It is very important to help whoever you can; all this comes under good character and good ethics. A person should be someone whom people want to meet, talk to, and sit with. It should not be that people want to flee from them or run away. Allah increases their sustenance because they are treating Allah's servants well. So, whoever treats Allah's servants well, Allah increases their sustenance; Allah rewards them in this way. And the third important thing is feeding people. It'am: 'Ar-rizqu asra'u ila man yut'imut ta'ama minas sikkini fis sanami' (Sustenance reaches the one who feeds food faster than a knife reaches the hump of a camel). That is, the person who feeds others, whether they feed the poor or friends, anyone at all, receives sustenance very quickly. Allah will reward them very fast. Because when they are feeding people, Allah has promised them sustenance. Now, when they feed people, Allah is pleased with them that this is a very virtuous servant who is feeding others, especially those poor people who are deserving. Therefore, we should do at least these three things: make the home a paradise, not a hell; secondly, treat people very well, in which the treasures of sustenance are present; and thirdly, feed people. It should not be that we eat to our fill while someone in our area, our neighborhood, or among our friends and relatives is sleeping hungry.
Treating family members with love and affection increases one's Rizq.
A peaceful home environment acts as a magnet for divine blessings.
Good character and ethical conduct are described as the treasures of sustenance.

Feeding others, especially the poor, is a rapid way to receive sustenance from Allah.

This version of the hadith that we are going to mention is present in Sunan Abi Dawud. title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#2 | Our most important religious duty? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this second episode of Shameem-e-Ma'refat, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound religious duty of reviving the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The lecture emphasizes that the Ahlulbayt are the divinely appointed guardians and heirs of the Quran, possessing the esoteric knowledge required to interpret its hidden layers. Dr. Rizvi highlights the necessity of submission to the Imams and the importance of recognizing the Wilayah of Imam Ali as a fundamental pillar of faith. The session concludes by providing guidance on how followers can engage with these teachings and participate in future discussions.
content:
That now they... [Arabic recitation]... [Music] ...Peace be upon you, O viewers. Peace be upon you, O viewers, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. In this second episode of our program regarding the recognition of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), 'The Fragrance of Recognition', I welcome all of you. In the first episode, there was a discussion regarding the importance of the recognition of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), in which the hadith of Imam Reza (a.s.) was mentioned, in which the Imam said to his famous companion, Abi Salt al-Harawi: 'May Allah have mercy on the servant who revives our affair.' He asked: 'How is your affair revived?' The Imam said: 'By learning our knowledge and teaching it to the people.' Then he further said: 'If people knew the beauty of our speech, they would follow us themselves.' And along with this, in this session, we also saw that in the light of the hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), this truth can only be obtained from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And it is our responsibility that we read the history of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) more and more, read their hadiths, and study them. Read their hadiths and study them, or understand these hadiths. And with this, our today's topic is the most important duty towards the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), which we will find out. We request the respected Dr. Salim Rizvi Sahab to welcome him with a loud Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. [Arabic recitation]... Today, we are talking about... Today, we are talking about the command of the world... [Arabic recitation]... 'Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.' Before this, the discussion was about what is obligatory upon us regarding Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.): to acquire knowledge, to attain recognition. And in that connection, it was discussed that it is obligatory upon us to read the hadiths of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Continuing this series, there is a very important point, I will point towards it so that we can try to share those points while moving forward. It is a very important thing that if we do not understand a hadith, it is not permissible for us to deny it. Rather, is it permissible or not? If someone denies it just because they do not understand it, then there is a proverb in Arabic: 'A person is an enemy of what they do not know.' If you are not able to understand it, you are feeling it, then it does not mean that you do not understand it, so it does not mean that it is not a thing. And as the series continues, in the light of all this, and from the hadiths of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), those who want to accept it, let them accept it; those who do not want to accept it, let them not. Anyway, we are going to read the 34th hadith. The first hadith is present in Al-Kafi, and in it, it is said that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'The hadith of Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.).' The hadith of Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). The level of understanding of the words of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) varies. Some things are easy, some are slightly difficult, and some are very difficult. How did the Imams explain this? In the words of the Imam (a.s.), he clearly states: 'There is a matter that is difficult for a person to bear, and he cannot handle it, so he gets worried and scared. Therefore, it is difficult.' There was no room for doubt; it is very strict. Now look here, there is no one—except for the angels who are close to Allah, or a Prophet who is sent by Allah, or a servant whose heart Allah has tested for faith—who can bear it. And this servant has succeeded in this test. After that, look, this is a matter of testing. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'When a Hadith comes before you, if it is the command of your religion, then accept it. But if there is a Hadith that makes you scared and you cannot understand it, then do not reject it by saying, "This is beyond my understanding." Instead, submit it to the Imam.' O followers of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), leave this in the hands of the Imam. Look, if any of you cannot bear a point and cannot understand it, do not reject it. Instead, refer it to the Imam. The Imam himself said that if you do not understand, do not reject it. This is a very important point. If something is beyond our understanding, we should not be hasty in making decisions or rejecting it. If you do not understand something, refer it to those who are experts in this field, those whose lives have been spent in this arena. Refer it to those whose lives have been spent in this field, those whose beards have turned white, and who have a deep love for the family of Muhammad (a.s.). Those who love us and whom we love, and whose lives have been spent in the field of traditions—this is very important to understand. Ask them. And if you still do not understand, it is not your place to reject the Hadith. Because today, it has become very easy for some to say, 'We do not believe in this Hadith.' We only believe in the Quran, they say. This is not about the enemies; this is about our own people. Some have emerged today who say, 'We do not believe in the Quran, nor do we trust these Hadiths.' They are ready to accept the words of others, but when it comes to the words of the family of Muhammad (a.s.), they apply such intense scrutiny that they reject it. If you do not understand it, it is not your place to reject it. And it is necessary to mention that all knowledge is with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Look, this Al-Kafi, which I am reading to you, is present. It is necessary to state that this was present before us and before others. The Imam (a.s.) says, and this is the command of the family of Muhammad (a.s.): 'Regarding the spoils of war...' Regarding the spoils of war, it was the right of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). This is something you must know. Allah has given this right to the Messenger. The spoils of war are for us. The people of that time could not understand these things. The Imam (a.s.) used to complain to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that Ali (a.s.) had taken his right. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'Ali is the most entitled to these things among you all. Ali is the one.' If Ali (a.s.) wishes, he has the right. The verse says, '...and those who are firmly rooted in knowledge...' It has come in the Quran that there are some verses that are clear, and some are ambiguous. 'As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that which is unspecific.' They do not have the knowledge; they do not have the Imam. They follow the ambiguous verses. And what is the purpose of this following? The purpose is to create discord and fitna. They seek their own interpretation, while no one knows its interpretation except Allah. But the scholars say, 'And those who are firmly rooted in knowledge.' Now, look, the enemies did a great job by placing a small mark—a 'jeem'—saying that no one knows its interpretation except Allah. They separated 'those who are firmly rooted in knowledge' from Allah. They did not connect 'those who are firmly rooted in knowledge' to Allah. They said no one knows the interpretation except Allah. And then, 'And those who are firmly rooted in knowledge say, "We believe in it; all is from our Lord."' This 'waqf' (pause) was added later. Remember, this is not about changing the Quran; it is about the way of reading. I am not talking about distortion; I am talking about the way of reading. The enemies changed the way of reading. That is why I repeat that the matter should be clear: 'No one knows its interpretation except Allah and those who are firmly rooted in knowledge.' In the way of reading, we see that there are at least 10 to 15 Hadiths where the Imam (a.s.) read it as: 'And those who are firmly rooted in knowledge.' And he says, 'By God, we are those who are firmly rooted in knowledge. We are the ones who are deep in knowledge. We know its interpretation.' There are more than 10 Hadiths on this. I have found at least 19 Hadiths in different books. Now, some people bring up one Hadith where the Mawla says that those who are firmly rooted in knowledge are those who admit they do not know. If the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) do not know the interpretation of the Quran, then the question is: who knows? Who knows that Book? And if no one knows its interpretation, then what is the purpose of those verses? Then what is the purpose of those verses? What is the point? Why are those verses in the Quran? What is their benefit if no one knows them? Is it just for recitation, or after a decision, does a person just leave it? Is the Quran only for that? No, it is part of a plan, and they have been placed there so that people feel the need to seek guidance. And while seeking guidance, they should go to the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and ask them and learn from them. 'Ask the people of the Reminder (Ahl al-Dhikr) if you do not know.' If you know, then believe. If you are not aware, then come to us. We will explain. This is a very famous and powerful tradition. I once asked Imam (a.s.) about the interpretation of a verse. Listen to the hadith: I asked about the interpretation of a verse. I asked about the interpretation of a verse, and the Imam gave an answer. I asked again about the same verse, and the Imam gave me a second answer. The first answer was completely different—totally different—from the second. The answer was the exact opposite. I said, 'O Master, I asked you about this before, and you gave me one answer. Now I am asking again, and you are giving a different answer.' Now listen to the Imam's answer. The Imam said, 'This is the Quran. The Quran has a hidden meaning (batin) and an apparent meaning (zahir). And for every hidden meaning, there is another hidden meaning, and for every apparent meaning, there is another apparent meaning. There are layers and levels to the hidden and apparent meanings.' People say we should think about the Quran. Thinking, pondering, and contemplating is necessary. But if you think in the light of the teachings of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), you will understand much more. In this matter, there is no one more distant from the understanding of the people than the interpretation of the Quran. 'Indeed, there is no verse that does not have a back and a front.' There is no verse that is not about one thing and then also about something else. It is one verse, but it has multiple layers. So, what is this? These are the three or four levels. No one denies that the apparent Quran—what we see without ta'wil (esoteric interpretation) or tafsir—is also the Quran, but it is not enough. It is not enough. If you want to understand the entire Quran completely, then... If you want to understand the entire Quran completely, then going to Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is necessary. They are the ones who know the Quran. And the traditions do not say this without reason. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things.' He did not say that without a reason; there is wisdom behind it. There is a hidden secret as to why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is saying, 'Go to Ali.' 'I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate.' There is no other reason for this. And that is why, in the traditions, it is very clearly stated in the light of the Quran that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have explained it. Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) narrates from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari. Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari is a very famous companion; he has seen three Imams. Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari is a very great personality. He asked Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) a question. Pay attention to this verse: 'Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants.' We made them the heirs of the Book, the Quran. 'Those We have chosen of Our servants.' We have made them the heirs. Meaning, the Quran has an heir; it is not without an heir. Even today, the heir of the Quran is alive, and he is the proof of Allah. Allah has not left the Quran without an heir. So, when Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari asked this question, the Imam (a.s.) replied, 'O Abu Hashim, all of this refers to the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).' Who are these heirs? The Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Is there anyone else besides them? If you say that the Shias believe this, then please tell me—tell me—if this is the case, then there will be a discussion. We want you to discuss so that the truth becomes clear, so that the milk is separated from the water. Because if we say it from our side, you object that we are being biased. You take it from your own sources so that you can tell us who it is. Because if we say it from our side, you object that we are being biased. You take it from your own sources so that you can tell us who it is. Who is the heir of the Quran? We are the Shias. So, Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, being a Shia and loving them, says, 'Tears were flowing from my eyes that Allah has bestowed such a status upon the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).' And my heart began to think, 'Has Allah bestowed such a favor upon the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) that He has made them the heirs of the Quran?' Thinking this, tears flowed from my eyes. Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) looked at me and said, 'O Abu Hashim, what is this thought coming into your heart? Our status is much higher than what you are thinking.' Our status is much higher than what you are thinking. You don't even know what our status is. The thought coming into your heart—our rank is many times higher than that. Our status is much greater; your mind cannot even comprehend it. What a favor Allah has done upon us! Alhamdulillah, thank Allah. Thank Allah. Allah has made you our followers. You have been made to hold fast to the rope of Allah. So, thank Allah. This is our belief. We should all thank Allah that Allah brought us to the door of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Otherwise, what was our worth that we would even be on this earth? Allah helped us. Thank Allah, it is Allah's favor. Alhamdulillah. Thank Allah, it is Allah's favor. Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, for the Wilayah of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), that He has connected us to the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). To hold onto this Wilayah is the greatest favor of Allah. If He had not done this favor, we don't know where we would be wandering. We should be grateful. We find in the traditions that when you feel our love in your heart, then pray for your mother. Pray for your mother. Your mother and sister will be with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Others will be called by their names, but you will be called by your names along with theirs. This is the glad tiding, O Hashim. This is the glad tiding, O Hashim. O Hashim, take this glad tiding. And you are on the truth. And when you get a chance, read the entire Quran. In the Quran, whatever you see, you can see that it refers to the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Abu Hashim also refers to this, saying that we do not have any doubt. This is just one example. I am telling you to what extent it is. There are 19 hadiths that say the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the path. Besides that, there are also verses in the Quran that say that knowledge is only for Allah. It says knowledge is only for Allah. So, what does that mean? Does it mean He didn't give it to you? He didn't teach you? He says He has taught you. So, what is the meaning of that verse? 'The keys of the unseen are with Him; none knows them except Him.' So, did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) not know? Did the other Imams (a.s.) not know? So, what is the meaning of this verse? It means that wherever such things are mentioned, it refers to the fact that Allah is the owner of all perfections by His essence (dhat). Allah has bestowed these perfections upon His chosen ones and the Masumeen (a.s.), and they are owners of these perfections by the grace of Allah. That is why the Imams (a.s.), whenever they described their perfections, they used to say this. When people used to confirm their faith, they would say that they considered a portion of it due to Allah, and they would thank Allah. Now, if you take only half of the matter and work on it, and you claim to be a follower of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then you must accept the consequences. Otherwise, leave it and say, 'We do not believe in this.' There is a group that says, 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us). Fine, go ahead, that is not an issue. But clarify your stance; do you want to stay on both sides? No, if you are on this side, then we must say with certainty that we are followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and this is the honor that remained with them. Now, I will mention another excellence; it is that when this honor is mentioned in the Holy Quran, in one verse, Allah (s.w.t.) says that 'Innal izzata lillahi jamee'a' (Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah). All people are lowly; that is why when it is not there, there is no honor for others. And in another verse, it was said that it is for Allah, for His Messenger, and for the... For Allah, for His Messenger, and for the believers. What does this mean? On the other hand, it is for Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. This means that wherever all excellences are, they are under His authority. By His authority, He gave permission to His Messenger and gave permission to all the believers. So, whomever He gives honor, that person is honored. Whomever Allah degrades, that person is lowly. That is why you see, I had mentioned a verse of the Holy Quran to you, after the verse of 'Qul Allahumma malikal mulk' (Say, O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty), you give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent. So, the authority is in the hands of Allah. All authority belongs to the Prophets and the Imams. And then, if Allah wills, He gives it to whom He wills. So, it is for Allah, for His Messenger, and for the believers. So, this authority is not with others. If it is not with the believers, then who are these others who can take it? When they present their strange arguments, this is a very important issue that we need to address. Finally, the last point is that in this, Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq (a.s.) says, and this hadith is also present in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 398, Hadith number 5. The Imam says, this hadith is from our companions, that I heard from Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq (a.s.) that he said: 'Call the people to our recognition.' Call the people to our recognition, and it was commanded to follow us. Our recognition means to recognize us, to confirm us, to submit to us, and to follow us. And whoever says, 'I am a Shia,' must have recognition, confirmation, and submission before him. So, this hadith has three things in its first part: 'Call the people to our recognition.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... In Arabic, 'Ma'rifa' means to recognize, to know. If they do not know, then turn towards them. How well it is being understood, so they should turn towards us... How well it is being understood, so they should turn towards us, confirm us, and submit to us. Submit, submit, submit. And whoever says, 'We will understand it ourselves,' and they listen... especially those who say, 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah), even if they keep that and pray and fast, saying 'La ilaha illallah,' but in their hearts, they do not accept this. The point is that if they do not turn towards us, they will go astray because they left Allah and His Messenger and followed their own desires, their own opinions, and their own logic. We, all these... We, all these things that we bring out from the traditions, and you yourself see that we are reading this, and these people who are ready to accept anything, they are the ones who are ready to accept anything. And this is not at all different from others. And this is the oppressed aspect of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Just look at this, Imam Ali (a.s.) says in the sermon of 'Shaqshaqiyyah', what he calls the 'Khutbah al-Shaqshaqiyyah'. What does he say? He says, 'I remained patient while there was a thorn in my eye and a bone in my throat.' I remained patient while there was a thorn in my eye and a bone in my throat. I saw my inheritance being looted. Ali (a.s.) was sitting in his place, and he was seeing how the people were talking, how they were playing with the religion. One thing is that he is the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, but he sees that the religion is going away. I was seeing that my inheritance was being looted. And this sequence continued, one Imam after another, until the time of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.). This matter also came to light that people used to sit and make their own new religions, saying, 'We are this, we are that,' and they played with the religion. They played with the religion. They were seeing that I was seeing my inheritance being looted. So, they claim that when the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) appears, he will bring the knowledge of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) to the world and will fill the world with justice just as it will be filled with oppression. We are very grateful to the respected Dr. Syedna Sahab, and we are grateful to you that you have shown interest in this program with your prayers and your questions and joined us. But I want to make a request, and that is that your question should be related to the topic. Your question should be within the scope of the discussion, meaning if something was presented or a hadith was narrated during the discussion, you can definitely ask a question related to that. And the third important point is that your question should not be about any personality, especially any political personality. Keeping these three things in mind, use the WhatsApp number of the program, [number removed]. You can send your... [number removed]. You can send your questions through voice messages and you can also send your questions through text messages. With this, we would like to take your leave. Next Saturday, at 10:00 PM India time, we will be present again, Insha'Allah, with the third episode of 'Samajat'. Walhamdulillah Rabbil Alamin. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. O Muhammad, O Ali... title: Muharram 1442 English Majlis #02: What has he found who lost you? | Sayed Mahdi Modarresi
excerpt: In this lecture, Sayed Mahdi Modarresi explores the spiritual significance of Ziyarat Ashura and the profound humility found in prostration before Allah. He contrasts the fragility of human power and secular distractions with the eternal value of divine connection and mourning for the Ahlulbayt. Through the historical lens of Muslim ibn Aqil’s sacrifice and the moral lessons of figures like Hurr and Barsisa, the talk emphasizes the necessity of divine guidance in overcoming human weakness. Ultimately, the session serves as a reminder that true loss is found in turning away from the Creator, while redemption remains accessible through sincere repentance and loyalty to the path of Imam Hussain.

Ziyarat Ashura serves as a sacred, authentic link to the divine, emphasizing its importance in a believer's spiritual practice.
Prostration is the ultimate act of humility, representing the closest point of connection between a human and their Creator.
True loss is defined as substituting the Creator with worldly status, wealth, or secular distractions.
Human achievements are inherently fragile, and divine guidance is essential to prevent moral collapse and spiritual blindness.
Mourning for Imam Hussain is a unique, transformative act of worship that elevates the believer's breath to the level of Tasbih.
The story of Muslim ibn Aqil illustrates the highest standards of loyalty, selflessness, and concern for the Imam’s safety.
Sincere repentance, as seen in the life of Hurr, can bridge the distance to Allah regardless of one's past sins.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ziyarat Ashura
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces the profound nature of Ziyarat Ashura, emphasizing its divine origin and the importance of the final prostration.

chapters.title: The Power of Prostration and Human Frailty
chapters.summary: Prostration is presented as the ultimate act of submission and proximity to Allah, highlighting human vulnerability through examples of illness and worldly loss.

chapters.title: Finding God vs. Losing Everything
chapters.summary: The lecture reflects on the famous supplication of Arafat, questioning what one truly possesses if they lose their connection to the Creator.

chapters.title: Secular Spirituality vs. Divine Connection
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques modern attempts to replace religious spirituality with secular alternatives like hallucinogenic drugs, contrasting them with the true spiritual connection found in God.

chapters.title: The Power of Prostration and Humility
chapters.summary: Prostration is presented as an act of acknowledging one's own nothingness and vulnerability, which paradoxically leads to finding everything through total reliance on Allah.

chapters.title: The Value of Mourning for Imam Hussain
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses how even flawed acts of mourning for Imam Hussain are accepted by Allah as a form of worship, offering hope and salvation to the believer.

chapters.title: The Need for Divine Steadfastness
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that human beings are inherently weak against temptations and desires, necessitating divine intervention to remain steadfast on the path of Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Fragility of Faith and Moral Failure
chapters.summary: Using the story of Barsisa, the speaker illustrates how one sin can lead to a catastrophic downfall, highlighting that even those with high spiritual status can lose their way.

chapters.title: Redemption and the Path to Allah
chapters.summary: The speaker contrasts those who fell from grace with those like Hurr who repented, emphasizing that sincere intention allows for a quick return to Allah regardless of one's past.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Muslim ibn Aqil
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by honoring the sacrifice of Muslim ibn Aqil, highlighting his loyalty and his death in a state of thirst, mirroring the tragedy of Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Final Will of Muslim ibn Aqil
chapters.summary: Muslim ibn Aqil requests to settle his debts and asks that his body be treated with dignity before his martyrdom in Kufa.

chapters.title: News of Betrayal and Martyrdom
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain receives news of the betrayal in Kufa and the martyrdom of Muslim ibn Aqil, prompting him to warn his companions of the impending danger.

chapters.title: Consoling the Orphan Hamidah
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain comforts Muslim ibn Aqil's daughter, Hamidah, foreshadowing the tragic events that would later befall his own daughter, Sukayna.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.)  |  Ep#02 - Darwaaza Ya Pardah? - Part 2/2
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical controversy regarding whether the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) had a physical door or merely a curtain. Scholar Ehsan Jafri refutes the claim that the Ahlulbayt lived in houses without doors by citing Quranic verses and authentic Hadith. He concludes that references to doors, keys, and the Prophet's visits confirm the existence of a solid, wooden entrance to her home.
content:
Welcome to the second episode. In the first episode, we saw how our opponents try to present objections using references from our books, claiming that the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) did not have a door, and that she used to meet Hazrat Ali (a.s.) behind a curtain. They claim that in the houses of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), there were neither doors nor roofs, just curtains. We have already presented the answers to these baseless objections in our first episode. If any of you have not seen that video, If any of you have not seen that video, we request you to watch it. In today's second episode, we will try to present the second part of the answer to the same objection, specifically using references from the Quran and Hadith to explain why there were indeed doors in that era. To present this answer, our respected scholar, Ehsan Jafri Sahab, is with us today. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. Thank you very much for the excellent way you presented the answer to this objection in the previous episode. Since you mentioned that you would provide further answers from the Quran and Hadith in this episode, we would like you to present them to our viewers. Yes, certainly. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu Alaikum. Before giving the answer, it is very important to clarify one thing, and that is... It is very important to clarify one thing, and that is that some people might wonder why we are presenting these narrations if we already gave a complete answer in the previous episode. The answer is that this objection is not only raised by opponents but also by some from within our own ranks—those who harbor enmity or lack sympathy for Janabe Zahra (s.a.). Therefore, it is necessary to answer this in the light of narrations. Secondly, as you mentioned, it is proven through the Holy Quran and authentic narrations that there were indeed doors in those houses. Without taking much of your time, I will proceed. First, regarding the Holy Quran, in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 189, Allah (s.w.t.) says: 'It is not righteousness that you enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses from their doors.' The Quran says, 'Enter houses from their doors.' This means the door must open first for a person to knock on it. If there were no door, this command would be baseless, and Allah does not know or command anything baseless. Furthermore, in Surah An-Nur, verse 61, there is a mention of houses that require a key to be opened. As for the Hadiths, I will present four to you. First, the famous scholar Allamah Majlisi, in his book 'Mir'at al-Uqul', Volume 20, page 37 and page 40, mentions a narration regarding the verse of Tatheer. He writes that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to go to the door of Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) for six months. The word 'Bab' (door) is used here, which refers to the locking system of the door, and he would stand at the door. He would stand at the door and say... Now, the word 'Salah' (in the context of the Prophet standing at the door) can have two meanings. The first meaning is prayer, as in waking someone up for prayer, like the Adhan. But according to the status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), this is not the case, because they do not need to be woken up for prayer. They are the ones who are the essence of prayer. And regarding Janabe Zahra (s.a.), it is said that when she stood in the Mihrab, her face would shine so brightly that it would illuminate the entire city of Medina. This is the spirituality of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So, the first meaning of 'Salah' as prayer is not applicable here. The second meaning of 'Salah' is 'Salam' (greeting), which is more applicable and appropriate here. This is supported by the following sentence: 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would come to the door of his daughter for six months and say, 'Assalamu Alaikum ya Ahlulbayt an-Nubuwwah' (Peace be upon you, O Household of Prophethood).' He would recite the Verse of Tatheer at the door of Janabe Fatimah (s.a.). The people who attacked the house did not care about this; they did not respect the door where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to offer Salam. This is the second point. The third point is from Surah Al-Insan, where it is mentioned that for three days... For three days, they fasted, and at the time of Iftar, a needy person, an orphan, and a captive would come and ask for something. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) would give away the food they had prepared for themselves. It is written in the narrations that they spent three days with only water, sacrificing their own food. In those narrations, it is also written that the needy person would come and stand at the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) to ask. Furthermore, Sheikh Saduq, in his book 'Tafsir al-Ayyashi', Volume 1, page 50, and other sources, mentions that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ordered that all doors opening into the Prophet's Mosque be closed, except for the door of Ali (a.s.). Except for the door of Ali (a.s.). Only he was given permission to have his door open into the mosque. One companion asked for permission to make a small hole in the door to look into the mosque, but the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) strictly refused and said, 'Not even the size of a needle's eye.' If he was not allowed to make a hole to look through, it means the door was made of wood. This proves the existence of a door. There are many such references in books like 'Al-Kafi', Volume 8, and others, which confirm this. It is mentioned that all doors were closed except for the door of Ali (a.s.). This is a narration we read in our sermons. It is a reminder for every Shia, every lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), to remember that door. If there were no door, this command would be meaningless. Finally, a Hadith from the book of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), 'Al-Kafi', Volume 4, Book 42, Hadith 666, mentions that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to give food to the needy, and it is written that he went to the upper floor, opened the door with a key, and gave the food. This confirms that the door was opened with a key. Doors are not opened with keys if they are just curtains; they must be made of wood. If someone argues that this refers to an inner room, then if an inner room has a door that can be opened with a key, why couldn't the main door have one? These objections are merely attempts to cast doubt. Thank you, Jafri Sahab, for presenting such a comprehensive answer. We hope our viewers are satisfied. If anyone is still not satisfied, they can send their questions to our WhatsApp number or social media handles. Insha Allah, we will try to answer them. That is all for today. As much as we have reached for today, we do not publish our program, and tomorrow in our next episode, I will be here with objections. On this same topic, regarding the attack on the house of Sayyida Zahra (s.a.), the answers to the questions are this morning's office...
The Quran explicitly commands entering houses through their doors, implying doors are a standard feature of homes.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to stand at the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) to offer Salam for six months.
Historical narrations mention the use of keys to open doors, which is impossible with curtains.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ordered all doors leading to the mosque to be closed except for the door of Imam Ali (a.s.).
The refusal to allow even a needle-sized hole in the door of Imam Ali (a.s.) confirms the doors were made of solid material like wood.
These objections are often raised to cast doubt on the historical events surrounding the attack on the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.).

title: Qasam Ba Rizq Farishta Nawaaz Hain Zahra (s.a.) | Janab Ali Jawad Sahab | JASHN -E- FATEMI 2023
excerpt: This lecture by Janab Ali Jawad Sahab celebrates the exalted status of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) during a Jashn-e-Fatemi event. The speaker emphasizes her role as the source of Wilayah, the provider of sustenance, and the ultimate model of motherhood and truth. He passionately defends her honor, highlighting her divine authority and the significance of her legacy in the lives of believers.
content:
Listen to this, take this proof: the one on whose head is the crown of Wilayah, on his heart too is the rule of Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Sometimes we are wounded hearts, you show them the door directly. He gave... [Music] This will be useful in the rain and on the Day of Judgment. It will be useful in the rain and on the Day of Judgment, it will save me from the earth to the sky. I keep reciting, the difference of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) image is a secret that only God knows. Zahra, there are many who are kind to servants in the world, but by God, she is the one who is kind to the angels. She is the one who is kind to the angels. Without Zahra, there is no prayer; tell me, can you perform any prayer without the conditions of prayer? Tell me, can you perform any prayer without the conditions of prayer? Zahra, I had to write a title on the book of existence, so I wrote it. The destiny of the world is Zahra. If you want to be there, then go and become united, free from the house. Zahra, the heart says, let me praise Batool (s.a.). The heart says, let me praise Batool (s.a.). Let me elevate the words to the peak of excellence. Let me decorate the verses and praise her. We are so happy that we don't know what to do. [Music] We are so happy that we don't know what to do. With the breath of Kausar, watch, I will perform a miracle today. I will not do 'middhat' (praise), I will do 'tilawat' (recitation). She is the daughter of the Messenger, Fatima Zahra (s.a.), that is her name. She is 'Sayyidat-un-Nisa' (Leader of all women), her status is great. All the lovers go to her door. Her management is the system of the Almighty. If she wishes, she can turn night into day and day into night. She distributes Paradise in matters. Her status is great, all lovers go to her door. Her management is the system of the Almighty. If she wishes, she can turn night into day and day into night. She distributes Paradise in matters. The princes of Paradise are her two sons. Her door is the one where people like Salman (r.a.) are servants. Before her, all are humble. The crown is on his head, and on his heart is the rule of Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Her door is the one where people like Salman (r.a.) are servants. Listen to this, take this proof: the one on whose head is the crown of Wilayah, on his heart too is the rule of Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Whatever one thinks, it is even more than that. The one who has it has the authority of protection. I am going to say one thing, be alert. The daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is this... Be alert. The status of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is such that just as the soul remains safe in the body, all the Wilayah of the Almighty is in her action. She remains safe in the body, all the Wilayah of the Almighty is in her action. Observe this, see her as a face, especially see that her gift is the source of light in the world. Her influence will be such that the path of motherhood for children was taught by her. Her path was taught, the path of motherhood for children. It was she who rebuked falsehood for the sake of children. It was she who rebuked falsehood. May the heat of oppression never come upon the oppressed. Everyone will know how Zahra's upbringing is. Everyone will know how Zahra's upbringing is. The one who is the lion of Zahra's power, it is only a matter of Zainab (s.a.) reaching Sham. I will do the 'tazkira' (remembrance) of the daughter of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). If anyone has a problem, then let them have it, what is it to me? For the sake of God, think a little. The Quran is praising this very personality. Why did I not do 'madh' (praise)? Do not talk nonsense. If you have the strength, then go and refute Surah Al-Kawthar. [Music] Why did I not do 'madh' (praise)? Do not talk nonsense. If you have the strength, then go and refute Surah Al-Kawthar. O killer of Mohsin and killer of Batool (s.a.), I am Javed, I do not talk nonsense. You have given rise to enmity with oppression and tyranny. If you fall into my hands, I will grind you into dust. The door by which you pushed, I will break that hand. I am the son of two fathers if I do not break your ribs. We are looking for the footsteps of the master. [Applause] We like the truth. We are just looking for the footsteps. They say we are also loyal, loyal, we are in their procession with the Alam. Loyal, loyal, we are in their procession with the Alam. [Applause] [Music] It is safe, write and tell me, do you believe? In the days of Ghadir, those who are looking for grief... Brother, and whatever is lying on the table of Zahra... And imagine everything that lies on a judge's table; whatever they look for in enmity, and we stay far away from them with a hammer in hand.

Her kindness extends even to the angels, and she is the distributor of Paradise.
The path of motherhood and upbringing is perfectly exemplified by her life.

title: Majlis 6 | Haqeeqat-e-Imaamat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound theological concept of Imamate, emphasizing its necessity as the divine guide and 'rein' of the Islamic faith. The discourse covers the requirement of Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Imam, the role of Wilayah in spiritual life, and the historical and spiritual significance of the Ahlulbayt. It further connects these concepts to the tragedy of Karbala and the essence of Azadari as a means of maintaining the legacy and message of the Prophet's family.
content:
Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Shabbir (a.s.) said, 'O light of my eyes, you do not have to travel until the evening now. They will make you a prisoner in the land of Sham.' The Princess replied, 'I have no fear of anyone.' Tell me, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? You will come to protect my modesty, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? The King said with a heavy heart, 'Daughter, peace is no longer in your destiny. Now the wretched Shimr will slap you.' Hearing this, the beautiful one began to say, 'You will come to save me from Shimr, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Then the King said to his daughter, 'Your hands will also be bound with ropes.' Hearing this, the thirsty one said, 'You will come to embrace me, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Shabbir (a.s.) stopped her and said, 'Your cheeks will also be wounded.' The Princess wept for a long time, and the day arrived. He said, 'How will I see you crying?' 'You will come to console me, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you?' Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? You will come to make bread at home, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? You will come to lift my army, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? Alright Father, you will come to put me to sleep, won't you? You will come to show your face every day, won't you? The scholar said, and Zinda said, 'O sister, you were imprisoned, O Nayabazi.' When the veil was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, 'O Nayabazi.' The evening of grief has arrived, the banners have been looted, walking on the sand. The banner has gone cold, to offer condolences, to meet me. Father Ali (a.s.) has arrived, O Nayabazi. When the veil was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, 'O Nayabazi.' You are in the sun, the house is inhabited because of you. O my head, don't you have any news? O Alamdar-e-Wafa (Standard-bearer of loyalty), by God, this sister could not fear you. You are matchless. When the veil (rida) was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, you are matchless. What can I say, my lion, taking the grief-stricken ones. These Muslims all went from city to city. The people of Kufa, sometimes the people of Sham, and the self. They arrived, you are matchless. When the veil was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, you are matchless. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. And the good end is for the pious and those who possess certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, our beloved of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. May the blessings of Allah be upon him and his infallible family. O, 'Those whom Allah has kept away from all impurity and purified with a thorough purification.' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our Master of affairs, our Owner, our Master, our Beloved, our Physician, our Companion, our Consoler, the fortress of the fortified, and the relief of the distressed and the upright—may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Our Master and our Lord, Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them), said: 'Whoever worships Allah as is His right of worship, Allah will grant him more than his desires and his needs.' Our Master Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them) has spoken the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The Hadith-e-Sharif that has been chosen for these ten nights of Majalis, in that Hadith, the Imam says that 'whoever worships Allah as is His right of worship,' meaning whoever worships Allah in the way that is the right of worship, Allah will give him more than his wishes, his hopes, and his needs. That is, Allah will give him so much that he cannot even imagine. I just submitted in service that the right of worship will only be fulfilled when a person possesses Ma'rifat (gnosis/recognition). And in the light of the Hadith of Imam Husayn (peace be upon him), Ma'rifat-ullah (recognition of Allah) is Ma'rifat-e-Imam (recognition of the Imam). And yesterday, I submitted in service why Ma'rifat-ullah is Ma'rifat-e-Imam? Because the Imam is the one who shows the path. The Imam is the one who introduces the correct beliefs, who provides the recognition of correct beliefs. The Imam is the one who teaches the correct method of worship. If one does not attend the threshold of that Imam who is 'Mansus min Allah' (appointed by Allah), if one does not acquire teachings from that Imam, then neither will the beliefs be correct, nor will the faith be correct, nor will the deeds be correct. Neither the prayer will be correct, nor the fasting, nothing will be correct. Therefore, it is necessary to recognize the goal and status of Imamate. Recognize the reality of Imamate, recognize the station of Imamate. If a person thinks by his own intellect that I will reach Imamate, that I will understand the reality of the Imam, then it is impossible for him to ever recognize the Imam. The Imam and Imamate are beyond human intellect; they are beyond human interaction. The reality of the Imam is beyond human intellect; a person can never grasp the reality of Imamate. That is why the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) says in Khutbah al-Shiqshiqiyyah: 'The torrent of knowledge flows from my being.' The ocean of knowledge is flowing from my being. 'And the bird of intellect, no matter how high it flies, can never reach me.' And this is the same thing Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) says. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. 'Indeed, Imamate is greater in value and more exalted in status, its glory is more magnificent, its depth is greater than that people could reach Imamate through their intellects or grasp its reality.' To comprehend it, to understand it. So then, what is the way? When it is beyond human intellect to understand the Imam and the reality of Imamate, then how will a person recognize the Imam? The answer is that just as a person cannot understand the reality of Allah unless Allah introduces Himself, in the same way, a person cannot recognize the reality of the Imam unless the Imam introduces himself. Unless the Imam speaks about Imamate, it is impossible for people to understand what an Imam is and what is called Imamate. What will these people understand with their intellects? What will they know? When they cannot understand the reality of the Imam and Imamate with their own intellect, then how can they choose the Imam? Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Is it clear to you? That is, because no one can recognize Allah unless Allah Himself introduces Himself. A narrator asked the Imam, 'Is there the ability in people to reach Ma'rifat, to discover Ma'rifat, to pursue Ma'rifat? Do they have this ability, this capacity?' The Imam replied, 'No.' This is from Allah; whoever Allah grants Ma'rifat, he will receive Ma'rifat. Ma'rifat is only the grace of the Lord; it is a creation of Allah. The servants have no role in it. So if someone asks the question, then what is the meaning of these Hadiths that say 'acquire Ma'rifat'? So this means, there are two important meanings. One meaning is that at the time when Allah introduces Himself, at that time the servant should accept it. And the second thing is that providing the premises of that Ma'rifat is the work of the servant. And who will teach this? The Prophet will teach this. And how will we recognize the Prophet? We will recognize him through intellect. Through intellect, we will recognize the Prophet; the Prophet is the one who leads towards Allah. Therefore, when a person does what the Prophet has commanded through the Prophet, he will reach Allah. That is why in the Quran, repeatedly, see the verses of the Quran: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah.' That is, obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah. Or in another verse, it was declared: 'O you who have believed, when Allah and His Messenger invite you, respond to Allah and the Messenger when they call you to that which gives you life.' When they invite you, say 'Labbayk' (I am here) to their invitation, towards that which grants you life. That is, the Messenger will grant you life if you say 'Labbayk' to the Messenger's invitation. Without saying 'Labbayk' to the Messenger's invitation, a person will have the outward appearance, a person... A person will not be a person. He will be dead. He is only living life in an outward sense. This is what the Quran is saying: 'When He calls you to that which gives you life.' When this Prophet—see, there is a bit of Arabic grammar here, understand that point, it is very important. This is a verse of the Quran, that O believers, when you say 'Labbayk' to the call of Allah and His Messenger. But when these two, two people are mentioned, Allah and His Messenger. But when it says 'when He calls you,' this is singular. It is singular, 'When He calls you,' because who is the one calling you? Allah will call you. Allah will not call you. Who will call you? The Messenger will call you. 'When He calls you to that which gives you life.' When he invites you towards that thing which makes you alive. So, the thing by which you become alive—when the narrator asked the Imam, 'What is that thing to which Allah and His Messenger invite, and through which life is obtained?' The Imam replied, 'Our Wilayah (guardianship), the Ahl al-Bayt.' Life is obtained through our Wilayah. Through our Wilayah. This is the station of Imamate. It is beyond the intellect of people. In the same way, when the Imam introduces himself, when the Imam gives a small introduction of himself, only then can people understand what Imamate is. This is when people follow that Imam who is 'Mansus min Allah' (appointed by Allah), whom Allah appoints. Mansus means the one who has an appointment from Allah. And if people—this question was asked by Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi to the 12th Imam, Imam-e-Zamana (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Qummi was a very special companion of the 11th Imam. Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Qummi was a very special companion. He was going to meet the Imam, and Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi remembered some work; he had some questions. So he thought, 'I will give them to Ahmad ibn Ishaq so you can ask the 11th Imam.' When he came to his house, it was found that he had already left. He asked, 'Ask where he went?' They said, 'He went to Samarra.' Samarra, where would he have reached? They said, 'He must have just reached here, no problem, this way.' So Ahmad ibn... so Sa'd ibn Abdullah went after him. He reached. Sa'd ibn Abdullah asked Ahmad ibn Ishaq, 'Are you going to Samarra? Take these questions of mine and go.' Ahmad ibn Ishaq said, 'Now that you have come this far, Sa'd, you also come. You also come to Samarra.' He said, "Should I also come?" He replied, "You come too." So he took Sa'd ibn Abdullah along. The hadith is very long, but I will present only a brief summary, just two sentences for your consideration. When they arrived there, what did they see? That Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) was in the lap of Imam-e-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) was in his lap. A small Imam-e-Zamana. Now, how old is the child in the lap? Hardly a year or two, not like that. So when Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi said, "Master, I have brought some questions, and these are questions that the opponents have asked, for which I had no answer." There is a whole preface to this, you can read it yourself; it is in 'Kamaluddin'. You can look in Volume 2, it is in 'Kamaluddin'. It is approximately Hadith number 192 of 'Kamaluddin', you can check it. There is a full introduction of Sa'd ibn Abdullah where he himself speaks about what he used to do. Now is not the time for those details; we are just speaking quickly so that we can reach our destination. So the Imam said, "Tell me," meaning Imam-e-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) said, "Ask these questions to him, my son, your Imam." So Sa'd began to ask questions. From whom? From that Imam who was still a child in the lap. That is why, listen to one definition of Imamate. One definition of Imamate is that the Imam is the one who is "أَعْلَمُهُمْ صِغَارًا وَأَعْلَمُهُمْ كِبَارًا" (the most knowledgeable among them when young, and the most knowledgeable among them when old). This is the definition of an Imam. An Imam is one who is the most wise in childhood and when he grows up, he is the most learned. Meaning, even in childhood, the Imam possesses knowledge and wisdom in abundance. It is a fountainhead from childhood, meaning from the moment of birth. An Imam does not learn from anyone in the world from the moment of birth. That he should acquire education from someone. So the Imam began to answer. One of the questions from Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi was this: Why was the right to select the Imam not given to the people? So that they could select their own Imam. Because the opponents say exactly this, don't they? That the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left this world and said, "Brother, you people select your own Imam, yes?" Meaning, "I am handing over the entire religion to you, and you people select whoever you wish." Alas! Is this religion? So the Imam said, "Well, tell me, who is to be selected? The reformer (musleh) or the corruptor (mufsid)?" These are Arabic terms. The reformer or the corruptor? Musleh means a good person or a bad person? Who is to be selected? Who is to be selected for the Imamate? So he said, "Obviously, the reformer, the good person is to be selected." Then the Imam asked several such questions; the hadith is very long. The point is that no one is aware of what is in another's heart. We do not know about anyone, who is what. A person's outward appearance may be whatever it is, but who knows what is inside. For example, it is found about Abdul Malik ibn Marwan that people say he spent his whole life either praying, fasting, or reciting the Quran. Who? Abdul Malik ibn Marwan (may Allah's curse be upon him). And just as he was sitting in the House of Kaaba reciting the Quran. He was reciting the Quran. Where? In the House of Kaaba. And how was he defined? Either he prayed, fasted, or recited the Quran. He remained in this state. As soon as he received the news that you have now been made the Caliph. Now you have become the Caliph. He closed the Quran and said, "هَذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكُمْ" (This is the separation between me and you). Now we will meet on the Day of Judgment. Whatever I had to get, I have received. So no one knows about anyone's true state. Now, what is Imamate? Just think. See, it is a coincidence that today we were reading a psychiatrist's statement, it just happened today. There is a very famous psychiatrist. He was saying that a certain person, for example, went into depression. He said, "Yes, it happens. When someone's loved one dies, they go into depression." He said, when one or two people die, someone goes into depression. But alas, Hussain ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). From the morning of Ashura until after Dhuhr, he kept picking up corpses until the time came when he said, "Taqaddam ya bunayya" (Come forward, my son). "Go, sacrifice yourself. Ali Akbar, go, sacrifice yourself." Ali Akbar was just waiting for this moment, waiting for this very instant. Ali Akbar immediately got ready to go, but Hussain (a.s.) stopped him, Hussain (a.s.) restrained him, saying, "Son Ali Akbar, first go to the tent and take permission from your noble mother, take permission from your aunt, then go." Ali Akbar came to the tent, stood before his mother, and said, "Mother, I am going to die, give me permission. I am going to be sacrificed for my father, give me permission." The mother said, "Son, why are you taking permission from me? Go, take permission from your aunt, Lady Zaynab, who raised you with tenderness and luxury for 18 years." Now, as soon as he came before Lady Zaynab and said, "Aunt, give me permission, I am going to be sacrificed for my father," Zaynab looked at Ali Akbar from head to toe and said, "Son, was it for this day that I raised you with such tenderness that you ask for permission to die?" Ali Akbar joined his hands and said, "Aunt, if you do not give permission, it is fine, but what if my grandmother asks me on the Day of Judgment?" Zaynab gave permission. Humayr ibn Muslim says that as Ali Akbar wanted to leave the tent, as soon as he stepped out, someone would grab his hem and pull him back. Then, as he wanted to leave, someone would grab his hem and pull him. It felt as if the funeral of a youth was leaving a house full of people. I did not understand who it was, but it is not written in the Maqtal who it was, but one thing is understood: if it were an elder, they would have held Ali Akbar's arm, but holding the hem means it was the little sister, Sakina. "Brother, have mercy on our loneliness." Ali Akbar said, "Oh, my father is also lonely." Ali Akbar came, Hussain (a.s.) prepared Ali Akbar, seated him on the horse, looked towards the sky once, and said, "Allahumma ishad ala ha'ula'il qawm" (O Allah, be a witness against this nation). "Qad baraza ilayhim ghulam" (A youth has gone out to fight them). "Ashbahun-nasi khalqan wa khuluqan wa mantiqan ila nabiyyika" (The one who most resembles Your Prophet in character, conduct, and speech). "When we longed for the sight of Your Prophet, we would look at Ali Akbar." Hussain (a.s.) bade farewell to Ali Akbar. Ali Akbar went, and he hadn't gone far when he felt a sound, he felt a sound, and when he turned back, what did he see? The old father, the old father with his hand on his back, "Ya Ali, Ya Ali, Ya Ali." "Oh father, you had already bade me farewell." Hussain (a.s.) said, "Oh son, bidding farewell to a young son is very difficult." Hussain (a.s.) bade farewell, Ali Akbar went, fought a fierce battle, and sent many wretched ones to Hell. It is found in the Maqatil that Ali Akbar sent at least 120 wretched ones to Hell. Until now, whoever went to the battlefield did not return alive, except for Wahab al-Kalbi; and the others who came were Ali Akbar. Why did Ali Akbar come? Because it was a mother's heart, it was a matter of a young son. For a moment, the mother's heart could not be controlled. She said, 'Fizza, stand by the door of the tent; see if the color of the Master's face changes, then understand that my son, my son is in trouble, some calamity has befallen my son.' Fizza came and stood at the door of the tent. Once, she saw the color of Hussain's face change. She came and said, 'Bibi, the color of the Master's face has changed.' She said, 'Go and trouble the Master a little.' Hussain came. Hussain asked, 'Master, what is the matter? The color of your face has changed.' He said, 'A famous warrior has come to fight my son, he is well-fed and quenched, and my son has been hungry and thirsty for three days.' As soon as she heard this, it was a mother's heart; 'Master, what should I do?' He said, 'Pray; a mother's prayer is accepted for her son.' Umm Layla said, 'Ladies, form a circle.' The ladies formed a circle. Umm Layla prayed, 'O Allah, by the loneliness of Hussain, O Sustainer, I beseech You by the helplessness of Hussain, O You who reunited Yaqub with Yusuf.' The mother's prayer had not even been completed when Ali Akbar returned, but in what state? He was drenched in blood, covered in wounds. He came and said a strange sentence, he began to say, 'Ya Abata, O Father, Hal ilaika min sharbatin min ma'in sabeel? Is there any way to get a drink of water? Al-atash qad qatalani, thirst is killing me. Wa saqlul hadeedi qad ajhadani, and the heaviness of the sword has become very burdensome for me now.' What did Hussain say? What else could Hussain do? Hussain had no choice. 'Son, you know there is not a drop of water in the tent. Move your hand, give me your tongue.' As soon as Ali Akbar placed his tongue in Hussain's blessed mouth, he pulled it back immediately. 'Oh Father, there are thorns on your tongue.' Hussain gave him his ring and said, 'Son, keep this; now you will be quenched by the Grand Master at the Hawd-e-Kawthar.' Ali Akbar went, and while fighting, a wretched man took aim at Ali Akbar's chest and thrust a spear into him. The spear pierced Ali Akbar's chest. Ali Akbar began to fall from his horse; when he fell down stumbling—now this is a sentence from the Maqtal—'Faqata'uhu, faqata'uhu bi-suyufihim irban irba', they began to cut Ali Akbar into pieces. Ali Akbar called out, 'Father!' Hussain reached the corpse of Ali Akbar, holding his back. There is a strange sentence in the Maqtal, a strange sentence. The Maqtal writes that when Hussain came, as soon as he reached near, just as a furious lion attacks its prey, Hussain attacked the wretched ones. He pushed the wretched ones away, the wretched ones moved back, Hussain came and reached near Ali Akbar, placed his head on his lap, pulled out the spear, and a fountain of blood erupted. Ali Akbar... Hussain ran and recited the elegy, 'Ya bunayya, alad-dunya ba'daka al-afa, O my son, after you, may there be dust upon the life of this world. Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we have found relief from the grief of both worlds. Wa baqiya abuka wahinan baynal a'da, and your father is left all alone among the enemies. Wa sa'ya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, and those who do wrong will soon know what turn their affairs will take. Al-ajjal, al-ajjal, ya Mawla, ya Sahib az-Zaman. May the Almighty hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Allah, Amen. May the Almighty hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. May the Almighty hasten the reappearance of Hazrat Baqiyatullah fil-Arzeen. O Allah, Amen. Count us all among his helpers and supporters. O Allah, Amen. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. O Allah, Amen. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. O Allah, Amen. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. O Allah, Amen. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Allah, Amen. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. O Allah, Amen. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. O Allah, Amen. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. O Allah, Amen. Protect the high Ulema and the great Maraje. O Allah, Amen. Protect the Atabat-e-Muqaddasa (Holy Shrines). Whoever protects them, You protect them. Especially protect the shrine of Janabe Zainab. Whoever protects it, You protect them. Accept this small act of Azadari of ours. Grant us the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. By the right of Hussain.
