title: Aqeeq Ki Angoothi Kyun Pehanni Chaahiye? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of wearing an Aqiq (agate) ring according to Shia Islamic traditions. It explains that the creation of various worlds, such as the World of Spirits and Atoms, involved a divine test based on the testimony of Tawhid, Prophethood, and Wilayah. The speaker highlights that the mountain of Aqiq was the first to testify to these truths, making it a symbolic and recommended practice for believers.
content:
A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim, bismillahir rahmanir rahim, wassala ya wali. In the Holy Quran, there are 40 verses and more than 200 traditions that prove that besides this world, there are many other worlds and nations, and these worlds and nations have different names, such as 'Alam al-Anwar' (World of Lights), 'Alam al-Ashbah' (World of Shadows), 'Alam al-Arwah' (World of Spirits), and 'Alam al-Dharr' (World of Atoms). God Almighty created His creation in all these worlds and tested them. So, on what basis did God Almighty test all this creation? God Almighty took an oath of His Oneness (Tawhid), the Prophethood of the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.), and the Wilayah of the Master of the Universe, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Since one of the creations among all these creations is the mountain, in this regard, our eighth Imam, Imam Reza (a.s.), narrates from his forefathers that he heard the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), saying from the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) that: He heard him saying from the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) that 'Wear Aqiq (agate), for it is the first mountain that testified to the Oneness of God Almighty, my Prophethood, and your Wilayah.' So, when it became clear to us that whoever testifies to 'La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah, and Ali Waliullah' and believes in it, it is incumbent upon them to wear an Aqiq ring on their hand.
There are multiple spiritual worlds including Alam al-Anwar and Alam al-Arwah.
God tested all creations based on their acceptance of Tawhid, Prophethood, and Wilayah.
Aqiq is identified as the first mountain to testify to the truth of the Prophet and Imam Ali.
Wearing an Aqiq ring serves as a physical manifestation of one's spiritual testimony.
The practice is supported by traditions narrated by Imam Reza from the Prophet Muhammad.
Belief in the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib is central to the spiritual significance of the stone.

title: Majlis 1 | Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Shakhsiyat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual and historical significance of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and the tragedy of Karbala. It delves into the theological concept of 'teenat' regarding the creation of a believer, the importance of mourning as a spiritual bond, and the strategic necessity of the peace treaty between Imam Hasan and Muawiya. The discourse emphasizes the Imam's role as the protector of the Quran and his unwavering refusal to pledge allegiance to Yazid, highlighting the authority of the Ahlulbayt as the true guides for the Ummah.
content:
O Moon, O Moon of Karbala, you must have seen, where the stars of the highest heaven descended upon that land. O Moon, O Moon, the moon of Hashim is shining there, take the charity of light from there. O Moon, O Moon, keep that land always cool, those who sleep there are the beloveds of Zahra. O Moon, they are the masters of Salsabil and Kawthar, those who were killed thirsty on the banks of that river, O Moon. Warriors and loved ones like Hur and Habib, were killed right here, the companions of the King of Martyrs, O Moon. And the corpses were being trampled, trampled in the battlefield, Abbas and Sarwar were picking up their pieces, O Moon. And the arms of Abbas-e-Wafa were severed right here, he did not get permission to fight, he could not even bring water, O Moon. And Sarwar brought a thirsty one to give water, what a strange scene, struck by the arrow of oppression. O Moon, and the neck of the son was pierced, the neck of the son was pierced, the arm of the father was pierced, both passed away from the world thirsty, O Moon. Oh, in that camp, a little girl was looking for her father, when the heads were scattered, O Moon. Then you also saw that grief-stricken girl sleeping on the chest, clinging to the headless father, O Moon. And the arms were tied right here in the first watch, the harem passed through that land, Sajjad with his head bowed, O Moon. And the Prince of Paradise is the master of Karbala, who has the courage to come, oh, until he calls, O Moon. And those who have reached Karbala, O Sibte Jafar, if only destiny would show them this day again, O Moon of Karbala. Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Rahamallahu man qara'al Fatiha. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. A'udhu billahi as-sami'il 'aleem minash shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'aliyyil 'azeem. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakeel, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man naseer. Alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alameen. Wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqeen. Was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya'i wal mursaleen, habibi ilahil 'alameen, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sallallahu alayhi wa alihi masumeen, alladhina adhhaballahu 'anhumur rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sima Baqiyatillahi fil-ard, Imam-e-Zaman wa wali amrina wa sahibina wa mawlana wa habibina wa tabibina wa anisna wa munisina, al-kahfil haseeni wa ghiyasil muztaril mustaqeem, ruhi wa arwahul 'alameen lahul fida. Amma ba'd, faqad qala mawlana wa sayyiduna Ali ibn-e-Musa ar-Rida alayhimus salam, 'Inna yawmal Husayni aqraha jufunana wa asbala dumuna, fa'ala mithlil Husayni fal yabkil bakun.' Sadaqa mawlana Ali ibn-e-Musa ar-Rida alayhimus salam. Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. The hadith I have chosen for this series of gatherings, in that hadith, the Master of Martyrs says, and this hadith is present in 'Wasa'il ash-Shia', Sheikh Saduq (may Allah be pleased with him) has narrated it in his Amali. Imam Ridha (a.s.) says, "Inna yawmal Husayni aqraha jufunana." That is, the day of Husayn, the grief of Husayn, wounds our eyes and tears flow from them. So, if anyone wants to weep, they should weep for Husayn. "Fa'ala mislil Husayni fal yabkil bakoon." The Imam narrated this tradition when a narrator, Ibrahim ibn Mahmud, came to the Imam's service on this very night, the first night of Muharram. The Imam said, "Innal Muharrama shahrun kana ahlul jahiliyati yuharrimuna fihil qital." Muharram was a month in which the people of Jahiliyyah, the disbelievers in the age of ignorance, also acknowledged its sanctity. They would not fight in it either. They respected this month so much that they would not fight in it. But, "Fastullat fihi dimauna." These Muslims made our blood lawful in this month. They killed us, they shed our blood. "Wa hutikat fihi hurumatuna." And in this month, our sanctity was violated. Our respect was destroyed. In which month? "Wa hutikat fihi hurumatuna wa subiya fihi zararina wa nisauna." And in this month, our children and our women were taken prisoner. Imam Ridha (a.s.) is saying about Muharram, "Wa uzribatinniranu fi mazaribina." And fire was set to our tents. In our camps, in our tents, fire was set in this month. "Wa untuhiba ma fiha min siqlina." And our tents were looted in this month of Muharram. "Wa lam tura lirasulillahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi hurmatun fi amrina." The sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was not observed regarding our affairs in this month, the month of Muharram. And then the Imam says, "Inna yawmal Husayn." This day of Husayn, this day of grief for Husayn, "Aqraha jufunana." It wounds our eyelids. It wounds our eyes, meaning by weeping and weeping, our eyes become wounded. Imam Ridha (a.s.) is saying this. By weeping, our eyes become wounded. "Wa asbala dumunana." And our tears do not stop. "Wa asbala dumunana." "Wa adalla azizana bi-ardi karbin wa bala'in." And they tried to humiliate and disgrace us in Karbala. They did to us as much as they could. "Wa awrasatnal karba wal bala-a ila yawmil inqiza." And this chain of difficulties will continue forever, until the Day of Reckoning. The commentators have explained different meanings for 'Yawmil Inqiza'. One meaning is that this chain will continue until the reappearance (Zuhur). The Ahlulbayt will remain oppressed until the reappearance. Until Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) reappears. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. And until the Imam takes revenge. Until the Imam takes revenge. That is why you recite in Dua-e-Nudba, "Aynat talibu bidamil maqtuli bi-Karbala." This is the reason. The suffering of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will end when Imam-e-Asr (a.s.) takes revenge. Then the Imam says, "Fa'ala mislil Husayni fal yabkil bakoon." If anyone wants to weep, they should weep for a personality like Husayn. This is what I was saying, what the Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) says in Dua-e-Nudba. We pray this in Dua-e-Nudba, don't we? That if anyone wants to weep, if anyone wants to wail, whatever—meaning weeping, lamenting, wailing, crying out—if for anyone, then only for Sayyidush Shuhada. Only for Sayyidush Shuhada. And certainly for the other Ahlulbayt. Because the Imam used the word 'misl' (like). 'Mislil Husayn'. Meaning only the Ahlulbayt are worthy of this. Otherwise, what is the world's suffering, what is the world's grief? The world has no importance before them. Then the Imam says, "Fa'innal buka-a alayhi yahuttuz zunubil izam." Weeping for Husayn causes major sins to be forgiven. Major sins, the Imam is saying. This is important because many people say what is the benefit of weeping, one should not weep. The purpose of Imam Husayn was not weeping, and such absurd things, some people in society raise these days, absurd things. These are the people who are very far from the traditions. They don't even know that the Ahlulbayt What is the tradition of Al-Mustaram? They don't even know what tears mean. They don't know the value of tears. Tears are something that bring about a revolution. Tears are something that topple governments. Such is the value of these tears. They cannot understand what this means. These are the same individuals who, regarding the supplications that the Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) makes—Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum—say that just praying doesn't do anything, just praying doesn't do anything. Because they are not familiar with the traditions. They are not familiar with the supplications, they are not familiar with the verses and traditions. Allah Ta'ala is saying in the Quran, "Ma ya'ba'u bikum rabbi lawla du'a'ukum" (Say, 'My Lord would not value you were it not for your supplication'). If it weren't for your supplications, your Lord would not even care about you. This is Allah's grace upon the servants because of supplications. These are signs, it is mercy. They cannot understand the meaning of supplications. They don't know the meaning of tears. And there is only one reason for it, and no other reason. That they have become distant from the traditions, distant from the Hadith. They don't even know what the sayings of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) are. And the Imam says, "Kana abi"—meaning Imam-e-Kazim (a.s.)—Imam-e-Ridha (a.s.) says that when "Idha dakhala shahru Muharram" (when the month of Muharram entered), my noble father "La yura dahikan" (would not be seen laughing). Imam-e-Kazim (a.s.) would only weep. "La yura dahikan" and "Wa kanatil ka'batu taghlibu alayhi" (and a grief and sorrow would completely overwhelm the Imam). And in this state, the Imam would spend 10 days. He would not smile, he would not laugh. Rather, an atmosphere of grief would remain, he would keep weeping, keep lamenting. Until the 10th day, "Fa'idha kana yawmul 'ashir" (and when it was the 10th day), "Kana dhalikal yawmu yawma musibatihi wa huznihi wa buka'ihi" (my noble father would remain grief-stricken on the day of Ashura, it was a day of tragedy, a day of sorrow, a day of weeping for him). He would keep weeping, only keep weeping. This is Muharram. "Wa yaqulu" (and he used to say), "Huwal yawmul ladhi qutila fihil Husayn" (this is the day when Husayn was killed). So, Insha'Allah Ta'ala, in this series of Majalis, we will try, in the light of traditions, as much as possible, the biography of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and Muharram, because, as I will submit to your service, it often happens that we limit Imam Husayn (a.s.) to the last 6 months of his life. Sayyid-ush-Shuhada said to Janab-e-Zainab, 'I have been called to the court.' Janab-e-Zainab was frightened upon hearing this. 'Brother, what kind of court at night? What kind of court is arranged at night?' A court is not decorated at night. Sayyid-ush-Shuhada said, 'I know why I have been called. Their ruler has passed away. And I also know what they want from me.' Janab-e-Zainab understood. She understood the gestures of Imam Hussain (a.s.). She said, 'Brother, I will not let you go alone.' Zainab will not let you go alone. I will say, Bibi, today you are not letting him go alone. What will you do on Ashura? When Hussain will be all alone? Zainab said, 'Brother Abbas, son Ali Akbar,' and it is written in the history books, in Rawzat al-Wa'izin, that he told 30 young men of Banu Hashim, 'Surround the Imam and go, go to the Dar al-Imara.' It is written in the history books, in Rawzat al-Wa'izin, that 30 young men of Banu Hashim surrounded Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, surrounded the Imam, and reached the Dar al-Imara. But the Imam stopped them there and said, 'It is not in the best interest for you to come inside. I will go inside alone, I will talk inside alone. But yes, if my voice is raised, then come without any delay.' The Imam went into the Dar al-Imara. After entering, the Imam sat there. This Walid gave the news. He said, 'The ruler has passed away.' According to Islamic custom, the Imam recited 'Istirja' (Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un) softly. Then Walid mentioned Yazid's letter. Walid said that Yazid has said to pledge allegiance. The Imam said, 'These are matters of allegiance. They are not decided like this in the darkness of the night. Let the morning come. We will come in the morning, you come in the morning. And gather the Muslims. All the Muslims will gather, and after that, we will decide who will pledge allegiance to whom.' Who will pledge allegiance to whom and whose allegiance will be taken. This matter will be solved like this. Walid said, 'But Yazid has insisted.' The Imam said, 'If Yazid has insisted, then hear my answer,' and that is—there are three or four sentences, but I am saying it briefly—that the Imam said, 'Mithli la yubayi'u mithlahu' (A person like me does not pledge allegiance to a person like him). We are the Ahlul-Bayt. We do not pledge allegiance to people like Yazid. And saying this, the Imam got up and started to leave. As soon as the Imam intended to leave, Marwan said, 'Walid, stop Hussain and take his allegiance right now, and if he does not pledge allegiance, then kill him. Behead him.' That was all it took for the son of Zahra (s.a.) to get angry. And he said, 'Atuhaddiduni bil-qatli ya ibnaz-zarqa'?' (Are you threatening me with death, O son of the blue-eyed woman?) Are you threatening me? Are you scaring me? Just the author of Rawzat al-Wa'izin says, just as the voice of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada was raised, the Imam's voice was raised, the door of the Dar al-Imara opened and the young men of Banu Hashim came in. At the very front was Hazrat Abul-Fadl Abbas. He immediately drew his sword on his hands, 'Maula, who dared? Tell me, Maula.' Hussain placed his hand on Abbas's sword. 'Abbas, this is not the time for war.' I will say, Maula, today only your voice was raised and all the young men of Banu Hashim came. On Ashura, Hussain is calling out, 'Ya Aba al-Fadl al-Abbas wa ya fursan al-Hind' (O my lions, O my brave ones, where are you?). 'Fala tastajibuna li' (You do not respond to me). What has happened to you? I am calling you, you do not answer me. 'Wa saya'lamu alladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun wa la'natullahi 'alal-qawmiz-zalimin.' O Lord, O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the troubles of those who are troubled. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant righteous and pious children to those who are childless. Grant complete and swift recovery to those who are ill. Return those who are away from their homeland to their homeland safe and sound. If they are in prisons, then ordain their release this very night. O Lord, protect the life, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraji. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Karbala
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the heart-wrenching events of Karbala, focusing on the suffering of Imam Husayn and his companions.

chapters.title: The Significance of Weeping for Husayn
chapters.summary: The speaker cites a tradition from Imam Ridha regarding the sanctity of Muharram and the spiritual importance of mourning for Imam Husayn.

chapters.title: The Tradition of Mourning in Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker describes how the Imams, including Imam Kazim, observed the month of Muharram with deep grief and constant lamentation.

chapters.title: The Eternal Heat of Husayn's Martyrdom
chapters.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) prophesied that the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) would ignite an inextinguishable fervor and grief in the hearts of believers.

chapters.title: The Nature and Origin of the Believer
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the concept of 'teenat' (clay/nature) and the spiritual origins of the believer, emphasizing the unique connection between the Shia and the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Divine Creation of a Believer
chapters.summary: Using narrations from Al-Kafi, the lecturer explains that the birth of a believer is linked to a divine drop from a tree in Paradise, highlighting the high value of a believer in the sight of Allah.

chapters.title: The Importance of Scholarly Traditions
chapters.summary: The lecturer emphasizes the necessity of studying the works of great scholars like Sheikh Kulayni and Sheikh Saduq to understand the virtues and responsibilities of a true believer.

chapters.title: Context of the Peace Treaty
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines the historical timeline between the martyrdom of Imam Hasan (a.s.) and the events of Karbala, explaining the necessity of the peace treaty with Muawiya.

chapters.title: The Nature of Muawiya's Hostility
chapters.summary: The lecture refutes claims of friendship between Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Muawiya, citing the mistreatment of the Imam's funeral as evidence of deep-seated enmity.

chapters.title: Imam Husain's Sermon and Status
chapters.summary: Muawiya attempts to discredit Imam Husain (a.s.) through propaganda, but the Imam responds with a powerful sermon asserting his divine status and authority.

chapters.title: The Ahl-e-Bayt as the Weighty Things
chapters.summary: Imam Husain (a.s.) defines his identity as one of the Thaqalayn, emphasizing the Ahl-e-Bayt's inseparable connection to the Quran and the obligation of obedience.

chapters.title: The Authority and Interpretation of Ahl-e-Bayt
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that only the Ahl-e-Bayt possess the divine authority and capability to derive the true meaning and interpretation of the Quran.

chapters.title: Warning Against Following Satan
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain (a.s.) warns against listening to the voices of Satan, illustrating through Quranic verses how Satan abandons his followers in times of crisis.

chapters.title: The Succession of Yazid and the Demand for Allegiance
chapters.summary: Following Muawiya's death, Yazid demands allegiance from Imam Hussain (a.s.), leading to a tense confrontation in the governor's court in Medina.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Refusal of Allegiance
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain (a.s.) firmly rejects pledging allegiance to Yazid, asserting that a person of his stature cannot submit to such a corrupt ruler.

chapters.title: Concluding Supplications and Prayers
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes the lecture with heartfelt prayers for the well-being of the community, the release of prisoners, and the protection of scholars and holy shrines.

title: SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024 | 7-Jan-2024 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture presents the 'Shahzaadi-e-Kaunain Grand Quiz 2024,' an educational event focused on the spiritual status and divine origin of Fatima Zahra (s.a.). The session explores deep theological concepts, including the creation of the Ahlul-Bayt, the significance of the Tablet of Fatimah, and the attributes of the Imams. Alongside the quiz proceedings and prize announcements, the discourse emphasizes the importance of Taqwa and spiritual reflection in preparation for the hereafter.
content:
TSR presents Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us. Rules of the Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz. The quiz link is live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link and register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Out of all those who have answered all questions correctly, 14 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, and they will be given these prizes. A'udhu billahi sami'ul 'alim minash shaitanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim wa sallallahu ala ya waliyal asr adrikna wala tuhlikna. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. The TSR team is once again present to serve you with the Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.w.a.) Grand Quiz. Before we begin today's discussion, let us offer congratulations on this birth, especially to Hazrat Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik aduwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. And offer them in the holy presence of Ummul Momineen Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) and the holy personalities of the Household of Infallibility and Purity (Ismat wa Taharat), especially Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), with a loud Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik aduwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. In this era, every person living on the face of the earth is a victim of oppression and disorder in every aspect of their life. Despite all this, there is a faint ray of hope in their heart that tells them that eventually, everything will be fine. Enduring the hardships of life, they are living their lives. This reminds us of an incident mentioned in the traditions. The angels complained in the Divine Court, 'O Lord, ever since You created us, we have not seen such a scene. O God, for the sake of these lights (Anwar), remove this cloud of oppression from us.' At that time, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala removed that cloud of oppression through the light of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). That light was so bright and radiant that the angels fell into prostration and asked, 'O Lord, what is this light?' The Voice of Power came, 'I have created this from My Greatness. I will manifest this light from the loin of My Last Prophet.' When Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) would be absorbed in worship in the prayer niche (Mehrab-e-Ibadat) at the time of Fajr, the light emanating from her holy existence would fill Medina. The people of Medina, astonished by this, would reach the presence of Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.) and express their wonder, upon which the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would guide them toward the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). When they reached the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), they would see that the Sayyeda of the two worlds was busy in worship, and that light was manifesting from her holy existence. Similarly, when the golden light would fill Medina in the daylight, these people would again reach the presence of Rasool-e-Akram (s.a.w.a.) and ask, 'What is this light?' Once again, Hazrat Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.) would send them toward the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). When they looked, this light would be emanating from the holy existence of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Similarly, in the last part of the day, a red light would emanate from the holy face of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). This continued until the birth of Imam Hussain (a.s.) took place, and this light transferred to Imam Hussain (a.s.). After Imam Hussain (a.s.), this light continued to transfer through these links of light, until today, this light is emanating from the radiant face of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), illuminating the universe with the light of Zahra (s.a.). Viewers, the objection raised regarding the greatness and status of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) is because people view their greatness and status based on prejudice. Just as the people of Medina in that era could not understand the light emanating from the house of Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.), and when Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.) guided them toward the house of Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.), their astonishment vanished. Similarly, if we want to understand their greatness and status today, and attain the recognition (Marifat) of their greatness and status, we must turn to their traditions. And to discuss this topic, our two brothers are present with us today, Janab Abbas Nahid Sahab and Janab Abbas Patel Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Yes, indeed Zahir Bhai, what you said is very important for these things to be clear to our youth. So, let us first try to understand the radiant form (Paikar-e-Noorani) of the Shahzadi (s.a.). Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.)—Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum—states, 'Ama wallahi lau alimu kaifa kana aslul khalq mukhtalifa isnan.' Meaning, I swear by God, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) is saying, I swear by God, if people knew the reality of creation, no two people would ever have a disagreement among themselves. Meaning, there would never be a disagreement between two people. This means people are not aware of the creation of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.). Because if they understood the reality of their creation, they would never deny their perfections. And Abbas Bhai, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) brings a chapter in Al-Kafi, which is titled, 'Babu Khalq-e-Abdan-e-Aimma-e wa Arwahihim wa Qulubihim (a.s.).' Meaning, the chapter that discusses the creation of the bodies, souls, and hearts of the Imams (a.s.). Okay. In this chapter, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) narrates a Hadith through his chains of narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam says, 'Innallaha khalaqna min Illiyyin.' That surely Allah created us from Illiyyin. Illiyyin is the substance of Paradise, from which He created us. 'Wa khalaqa arwahana min fauqe zalik.' And He created our souls from a substance higher than that. 'Wa khalaqa arwaha shi'atina min Illiyyin.' And He created the souls of our Shia from the substance of Illiyyin. Meaning, the bodies of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) were created from the same substance from which the souls of their Shia were created. 'Wa khalaqa ajsadahum min dune zalik.' And their bodies, meaning the bodies of the Shia, He created from a different substance. 'Famin ajle zalikal qarabato bainana wa bainahum.' And because of this, a connection exists between us and our Shia. 'Wa qulubuhum tahannu ilaina.' And this is the reason why the hearts of the Shia incline toward the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. And since we are talking about the radiant form of the Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.), let us state another Hadith from the presence of Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), which he narrates from his grandfather Hazrat Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.). The Imam says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'Khuliqa nooro Fatima (s.a.) qabla an yakhluqal arza was-sama.' Meaning, the light of the Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.) was created before the creation of the earth and the heavens. Wow. When Allah Azza wa Jall created Hazrat Adam (a.s.) and brought me out from his loin, and Allah Azza wa Jall wanted to bring her, meaning the Shahzadi-e-Konain (s.a.), out from my loin, the words of the Hadith are, 'Ja'alaha tuffahatan fil jannah.' So Allah placed her in Paradise in the form of an apple. And Abbas Bhai, this apple does not mean that it is talking about a worldly apple. Indeed. It is talking about the apple of Paradise, and as far as the things of Paradise are concerned, it is found that, 'Kullu shayin minal akhira ayanuhu azamu min samaihi.' Seeing every thing of the Hereafter is greater than hearing about it. Meaning, today when we hear 'apple of Paradise,' an image of an apple comes to our mind, but when we go to Paradise and see an apple, we will find that it is completely different. Indeed. Meaning, it is something we have never even imagined. Indeed, indeed. Then Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.) further states that then Jibraeel, Janab-e-Jibraeel (a.s.), brought this apple to me and greeted me. I replied to the greeting, and then Janab-e-Jibraeel said to me, 'Your Lord has sent you greetings.' Meaning, Janab-e-Jibraeel is conveying the greetings of the Almighty God to Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.). Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.) replied that the beginning of the greeting is also from Him and the end is also upon Him. Wow. Then Janab-e-Jibraeel said to Janab-e-Rasool-e-Khuda (s.a.w.a.), 'O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), surely Allah has sent this apple to you as a gift from Paradise.' Then Janab-e-Jibraeel said that Allah is saying that you should consume it. You should consume it. So then I split that apple, meaning Rasool-e-Akram (s.a.w.a.) says that I then split this apple, 'Fa-ra'aitu nooran sati'an wa faza'tu minhu.' Meaning, Rasool-e-Akram (s.a.w.a.) says that when I split it, I saw that a light emanated from it, seeing which I was astonished. Then Jibra'il (a.s.) said to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), 'O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), consume this and do not worry.' Why? 'Fa-inn dhalikal nura lil-mansurati fis-sama wa hiya fil-ard-e Fatimah.' Because this is the light of the one who is called Mansura in the heavens and Fatimah (s.a.) on this earth. So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'O Jibra'il, why is her name Mansura in the heavens and Fatimah on the earth?' The reply was, 'Summiyat fil-ard-e Fatimah (s.a.) li-annaha fudimat shi'atuha minan-nar wa fudima ada'uha an hubbiha.' If we pay attention to the word 'fudima', it means to keep away. That is, she is called Fatimah on earth because her Shia have been kept away from the fire of Hell, and her enemies have been kept away from her love. Wow. And she is called Mansura in the heavens because Allah (s.w.t.) says in Surah Ar-Rum, verses 4 and 5: 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, wa yawma'idhin yafrahu-l-mu'minuna bi-nasrillah, yansuru may-yasha.' And on that day—which day? The Day of Judgment. On the Day of Judgment, the believers will rejoice with the help of Allah, and Allah grants victory to whom He wills. Meaning, what is meant by 'Nasrullah' here? The Imam (a.s.) further clarifies it: 'Ya'ni nasra Fatimata li-muhibbiha.' That is, the help of Fatimah (s.a.) for her devotees. Meaning, they will be happy because of her help. And viewers, another point understood from this hadith is that Allah (s.w.t.) granted the Princess (s.a.) such excellence and superiority that He transferred her light directly to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), whereas the lights of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself and the Infallible Imams (a.s.) were transferred from Adam (a.s.) through Abdullah and Abu Talib (a.s.) generation by generation. Allah (s.w.t.) mentions this in the Holy Quran: 'Wa taqallubaka fis-sajidin.' And Allah transferred your light into the loins of those who prostrate; this excellence is also present in the Quran. That is, Abbas bhai, the Quran is clearly testifying here that the ancestors of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) were monotheists, worshippers, and people of Tawhid, whereas the opponents, due to their own ancestral compulsion to hide the idol-worship of their forefathers, level accusations against the ancestors of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, but when Allah (s.w.t.) intended for the light of Fatimah (s.a.) to be sent into this world in human form, He transferred this light into the loins of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in various stages. Whether it was during the Mi'raj, when He called His beloved directly and entrusted this light to him, or through the Ruh-ul-Amin, transferring this light from the highest of the high (A'la-Illiyyin)... as we just observed in this incident. Subhan Allah, Abbas bhai, what can be said about the luminous journey of this light, which sometimes resided in the A'la-Illiyyin, sometimes in the loins of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and sometimes in the lap of the Mother of the Believers, Khadija (s.a.). Indeed, Zahir bhai, and viewers, we can gauge the greatness and majesty of this light from the fact that when the Ruh-ul-Amin, Jibra'il (a.s.), was carrying this light to present it to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), due to the greatness and majesty of this light, sweat began to pour from his body. And Zahir bhai, this is a point worth noting: Jibra'il (a.s.) is the being who, when Allah (s.w.t.) intended to send punishment upon a nation, was the same Jibra'il whose single movement of his wings caused that nation to be lifted so high that they could hear the sounds of the heavens. When this angel, Jibra'il (a.s.), carried this light to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he began to sweat due to the greatness and majesty of this light. So viewers, we learned that our limited intellect is incapable of understanding the greatness and loftiness of her luminous form. Indeed, indeed, indeed. So how is it possible for us to grasp her spiritual greatness and loftiness? And if someone rejects her greatness and loftiness simply because it does not fit into their intellect, this does not cast any doubt on the greatness of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), but rather is proof of their own lack of intellect. Indeed, indeed. So viewers, as we saw, the light of the Princess of the Two Worlds (s.a.) was a gift from Allah to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, a mention of a similar gift is found in the traditions of the Family of Muhammad (a.s.), which Allah sent through the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) for his daughter, the Lady (s.a.), which we remember as the 'Tablet of Fatimah (s.a.).' Indeed, Zahir bhai, and if we want to know the value and status of this gift, who is sending it? The Lord of the Worlds is sending it. Through whom is He sending it? Through the Mercy to the Worlds. Wow, Subhan Allah. For whom is He sending it? He is sending it for the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds. Subhan Allah. And on what occasion is He sending it? On the occasion of the birth of the Master of Martyrs of the first and the last. Wow, Subhan Allah. This tells us about the greatness and status of this gift. Subhan Allah, Abbas bhai, the Tablet of Fatimah (s.a.) is that luminous board—what we call a tablet—which, after the Holy Quran, is the most important and firm proof for the Shia belief in Imamate. Indeed, when the high-ranking companion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari (r.a.), went to offer congratulations to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the Princess (s.a.) on the occasion of the birth of Imam Hussain (a.s.), his eyes fell upon this tablet—a green tablet—and he says that this tablet was so green that even the light of emeralds was nothing in comparison. He says that he asked the Princess (s.a.) about this tablet, and she told him that Allah (s.w.t.) gave this tablet to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) as a gift on the occasion of the birth of my son, Imam Hussain (a.s.), and he entrusted that gift to me—meaning my father gifted it to me—and in this tablet are inscribed the names of my father, my husband, and my father's successors who are from my descendants. So Jabir says, 'I asked, if you permit, may I write it down?' And the Princess (s.a.) gave him permission, and he transcribed it in the best manner. That is, Abbas bhai, Jabir (r.a.) wrote down the names and attributes of all twelve Imams (a.s.), exactly as they were present on that tablet, on that luminous board. So, Abbas bhai, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) narrates that one day his noble father, Imam Baqir (a.s.), said to Jabir ibn Abdullah, 'Give us a time when we may come to your house.' There is an important point here: why did Imam Baqir (a.s.) want to go to Jabir's house? It was so that Imam Baqir (a.s.) himself could go to Jabir's house to verify the text of the Imamate that Jabir had transcribed from that luminous tablet of Fatimah (s.a.). This highlights the importance of the purpose for which the Imam (a.s.) was visiting Jabir's house. Jabir replied, 'Maula, all our times are for you; our entire lives are a sacrifice for you.' 'Come whenever you wish. I am a follower of your command. Whether you come now or tomorrow, come.' Imam Baqir (a.s.) went to the house of Jabir (r.a.). The Imam recited that hadith and asked Jabir to look at the transcript to see if the hadith was the same or not. Jabir (r.a.) confirmed, 'Maula, all the words are exactly as you have stated.' So viewers, the collection of hadith we have, the heritage of hadith, is different from the hadith of the opponents. Indeed, their hadith are based only on 'Mu'an-an'—one narrator hearing from another—whereas our books, in which hadith are recorded, have a written chain of authority that was transferred generation by generation, and one narrator is reporting to another in written form. And in this very hadith, the mention of all twelve Imams (a.s.) is present, which is a proof for us regarding Imamate, besides the Holy Quran and other hadith. At the end of this very hadith, there is a mention of our and your final Imam, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.): 'Summa akmilu dhalika bi-ibnihi Rahmatul-lil-Alamin.' Then I will complete this Imamate with his son—the son of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.)—who is the Mercy to the Worlds. That is, the title used here for Imam-e-Zamana is the same title used for the Messenger of Allah: 'Rahmatul-lil-Alamin.' 'Alayhi kamal Musa'—and the Imam-e-Zamana possesses the perfections of Musa (a.s.). Just as Musa (a.s.) drowned Pharaoh and the Pharaohs in the Nile, Imam-e-Zamana will also drown his enemies and annihilate them. 'Wa baha'u Isa'—and the majesty of Isa (a.s.) is found in the Imam-e-Zamana. 'Wa sabru Ayyub'—and the patience of Ayyub (a.s.) is found in him. That is, he is seeing with his own eyes how the shrines of his ancestors are being desecrated, or how oppression is being inflicted upon his Shia. His followers are being killed, and in this long occultation, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is patient through all these troubles and calamities. That is, the gift that came from the Lord of the Worlds, reached the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds through the Mercy to the Worlds, that gift is still preserved today through Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), who is the Mercy to the Worlds. Subhan Allah, what can be said, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, Abbas bhai. So viewers, you observed that the matter returned to the same hadith from where we started: that light, the light of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.), which used to fill Medina with its radiance, when Imam Hussain (a.s.) was born, that light transferred to Imam Hussain (a.s.). It entered the sacred body. And from there, that light, traveling through these links of light, is illuminating this entire universe today with the light of Zahra (s.a.w.a.) through the radiant face of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. Come, viewers, let us conclude this discussion with the prayer that the Almighty removes this darkness of occultation from us through the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Ameen, Ya Rabbul Alameen. Viewers, it is hoped that you have submitted the answers to all your questions. The quiz link will be closed as soon as the timer on your screen ends. Wa sallallahu-umma ala Muhammadin wa alihi-t-tahirin. A'udhu billahis sami'il alimi minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim wa sallallahu alayka ya waliyal asr adriknah wala tuhlikna. title: Majlis 8 | Hujjat-e-Khuda Ki Zaroorat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of a Divine Proof (Hujjat-e-Khuda) as the essential guide for humanity and the preservation of religious truth. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi contrasts the intellectual and spiritual authority of the Ahlulbayt with historical attempts to distort the Quranic message and the virtues of Imam Ali. The discourse culminates in a poignant reflection on the tragedy of Karbala, focusing on the ultimate sacrifice of Abbas ibn Ali and the profound grief of Imam Hussein.
content:
Hai na... [repeated filler]... Hai Abbas, Hai Abbas, Abbas, Hai Abbas, Hai Abbas. Ali Imran said and Zinda said, 'O brother, you were not there, O Ghazi, when the veil was snatched from my head.' I kept calling out, 'You were not there, O Ghazi.' The world has been looted in Shaam, the harem has been left on the burning sand. To offer condolences, to meet you, Baba Ali has come. You were not there, O Ghazi, when the veil was snatched from my head. I kept calling out, 'You were not there, O Ghazi.' I am in the sun, I wish there was shade; if you were there, my head would be covered. Don't you have any news? O standard-bearer of loyalty, that sister, by God, had hopes in you. You were not there, O Ghazi, when the veil was snatched from my head. I kept calling out, 'You were not there, O Ghazi.' What should I say, my lion? These Muslims took our veils and paraded us through every city. Sometimes the people of Kufa, sometimes the people of Shaam laughed at us repeatedly. You were not there, O Ghazi, when the veil was snatched from my head. I kept calling out, 'You were not there, O Ghazi. Oh, how helpless the sister of the King of Loyalty was. When the tyrant said, 'The one you are proud of, call him now,' and I kept crying, 'You were not there, O Ghazi.' If we didn't get water, your fragrance should have remained. Your arms should not have been severed, even if the water skin was pierced, but this could not happen. Your arms are severed, and I am thirsty. You were not there, O Ghazi, when the veil was snatched from my head. I kept calling out, 'You were not there, O Ghazi.' What should I tell Sakina, who is the peace of my heart? 'Alas, I went for water, all your blood was shed.' Now there is no hope, you are not by my side. Ropes were tied in Shaam. You were not there, O Ghazi, when the veil was snatched from my head. I kept calling out, 'You were not there, O Ghazi.' When the knife ran over the throat, my lion, the sister was dying. I went a few steps away, alas, my brother, I kept calling out to you, 'Where are you, O Ghazi?' When the veil was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, 'Where are you, O Ghazi?' When Sakina (s.a.) met her end in the prison, seeing her shirt as a shroud, she was buried. That oppressed one did not show her face to Ali (a.s.), she just kept repeating, 'Where are you, O Ghazi? Where are you, O Ghazi?' When the veil was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, 'Where are you, O Ghazi?' Rehan cries, the pen is writing the tragedy, the standard of my Ghazi was drowned in blood. Zainab's (s.a.) heart is wounded, 'Where are you, O Ghazi?' When the veil was snatched from my head, I kept calling out, 'Where are you, O Ghazi?' The broken-hearted messenger of God, writing the victory and defeat, called his scribes and Umar gave this order: 'Write the victory letter quickly. What is the reality of the defeat of my enemies? The defeat of the son of Khaybar is inevitable. From Medina to Yemen, China, Egypt, Rome, Aleppo, and every country, write the victory letter. In every name, let this be inscribed: Hussein is killed, Zainab is unveiled, the throne and crown of the Imam are brought down. If you ask who is the owner of the throne, it is Yazid today. Write on my behalf, write on my behalf, a petition for Yazid, that Hussein has been killed by your hand. I will give the head of the martyred Imam as a gift of victory. There are a few more women in severe captivity. We did not even spare Ali Asghar, but the women of the Prophet's household are in your hands.' But in the letter to Medina, he would exaggerate the figures. Before the war, the thought was always that the Imam would fight for at least two months. The brave men of Arabia... are partners of the King of Nations. There is the power of God in the son of the King of Men. They will hold a front in the battlefield for months, but when the battle started with the followers of Hussein, it was the tenth of Muharram, a Friday. Not even two months passed, nor even a day, and the army of Shabbir was killed by the afternoon. From dawn, the strength of the King's army was cut down, and at the time of Asr, the place where Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) used to kiss was severed. They prayed the Asr prayer after cutting off the head of Shabbir, and after looting the tents, they recited the Takbir at sunset. In our army, all the ladies of the Prophet's household are captives. The grandson of the Lion of God is in chains. The Prophet does not come to the aid of the household, they call out to Ali (a.s.), but Ali (a.s.) does not come. The news of the messenger's arrival spread in the homeland. Once, the messenger went to the mosque of Medina, helpless. People, young and old, left their homes and went to the mosque. And he was saying with his tongue, 'Alas, alas, Hussein!' The messenger was in distress. The dome of the Prophet's grave was shaking, the pillars of the Mosque of the Best of Mankind were shaking. He was still reading the letter on the pulpit, he had only read one sentence that caused a commotion, when suddenly a clamor arose from the door of the mosque, 'Make way, make way, the second Zahra (s.a.) is coming.' When the Hashimite women made arrangements, the messenger also paid respect and saluted. Leaning on a staff, she stood there, sighing, and said, 'Brother, read this letter later, as you wish. First, tell me with your tongue if the King is safe.' He began to cry and said, 'La ilaha illallah, you are a great lover of Hussein and a mother of martyrs, but now in the world, you are in place of Zahra (s.a.).' She called out, 'Where am I, and where is Batool (s.a.)? I am a servant, she is the mistress of the earth and the heavens.' He said, 'Your noble son...' then she said, 'Yes, I am the widow of Ali (a.s.), the mother of Abbas the renowned, but I am not a mother yet, nor is he my son, if he is not of use to Hussein, he is not my heart.' 'It is shameful for me to even speak to strangers, this is not the way of Ali's (a.s.) handmaidens, but the love of Hussein has made me helpless. I have come out like this, wearing a veil in the marketplace. Tell me the news of Hussein, I am his slave-girl in desire, if I am his mother, then I am his.' 'I am eating my heart out, brother, you are torn-garmented, in the form of mourners, you have put dust on your head.' He said, 'Whatever grief I express is less, O sorrowful one, such cruelty was done to Hussein by the bloodthirsty army. If one's heart were of stone, or one's tongue of steel, how could one describe that thirst? A bloodthirsty dagger, and a Hussein; the world is a buyer of his head, and a Hussein; thousands of cruel arrows, and a Hussein; a crowd of hundreds of tortures, and a Hussein. The enemies did not give him even a drop of water, whom Zahra (s.a.) had fed thirty streams.' The mother of Abbas (a.s.) called out, the mother of Abbas called out, 'As for his life, that is fine.' He said, 'I am telling you, O lady, be patient.' That three-day thirst, and that condition, helpless from thirst, that loneliness, that poverty, that visit to the slaughterhouse. Shabbir used to look at the river with despair, Shabbir used to lick his own lips from thirst. 'Which tragedy should I tell you, O sorrowful one? There was no one to hold the stirrup of the pure Master.' The sister of Hussein came out of the tent with a torn garment, she was putting dust on her hair with both hands. In the enemy's army, everyone cried at that moment when Zainab (s.a.) held her brother's stirrup. This was her saying, Ummul Banin was shaken, she called out in anger, 'What happened to Abbas? Oh, he considered holding the stirrup as a shame and disgrace, here he used to pick up the shoes of the Master of Martyrs. Pride was not in my son, nor was it a habit to hold the stirrup, it was not pride, it was devotion.' Turning towards Najaf, he cried out, 'O Ali, hear my plea!' Your Abbas filled hearts with joy through his blood. This is what you used to preach as the path of loyalty, yet the rights of the one who raised him were destroyed. Do you hear, O noble one, what this servant says? A slave remains in service to his master just like this. That noble one called out, 'Listen, if you will, by God, the mark of loyalty is upon Abbas.' I mentioned the morning ride; when the master prepared to mount in the morning, there were standards, drums, and attendants in the procession. Your son was present, holding the stirrup. Akbar, of blessed character, held the reins, and Qasim was on his uncle's shoulders, waving a handkerchief. The glory of the Husseini army was behind him. Such was the splendor in the morning, but at the time of sunset, there was no army, no soldiers, no multitude of people, no Qasim, no Ali Akbar, and no Abbas. Bidding farewell to the daughters of the Prophet, that master stood at the tent door, helpless and alone. There was no one to hold his stirrup, no one to cry out. Husain (a.s.) looked towards the battlefield and the river, calling for Ali Akbar and weeping, calling for his brother and weeping. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. The best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. And the end is for the people of piety and certainty. And peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Blessings be upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, the Imam of our time, our guardian, our master, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our confidant, the fortified cave, and the succor of the distressed and the downtrodden. May my soul and the souls of all the worlds be his ransom. After this, our master and leader, Al-Husain ibn Ali (peace be upon them), said: 'Whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped, Allah will grant him more than his wishes and his needs.' May our master Al-Husain ibn Ali (peace be upon them) speak the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. In the noble hadith chosen for these ten nights, the Master of Martyrs says: 'Whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped, Allah will grant him more than his wishes and his needs.' The discussion was about worship and gnosis (marifah), and it reached the point that both intellect and tradition—meaning the verdict of the intellect as well as the Quran and Hadith—demand that there must be a guide, a leader, who guides humanity. That guide, that leader, must be someone who possesses knowledge from Allah and is himself a light, so that whoever seeks intercession through him and holds fast to him becomes guided. So, I present a few more points for your consideration: the Imam is the proof (hujjah) of Allah. He is the proof from Allah, and the earth can never be devoid of a proof. When we use the word 'hujjah' in the dictionary, it means that when a person presents an argument, and that argument is completed, it leaves the other party with no response. That is the meaning of 'hujjah'—a statement or evidence so clear that the other person falls silent. If they are stubborn, that is a different matter, but if they are rational, they will accept this evidence and fall silent. This word has been used many times in the Holy Quran, but I will present the most famous verse regarding this. The most famous one is: 'Rusulan' (Messengers), from Surah An-Nisa: 'Rusulan mubashshirina wa mundhirin'. We sent messengers as bearers of glad tidings and as warners. Glad tidings of what? Of happiness and good fortune in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter. And warners against what? Against the punishment of Allah in this world and the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, which is Hell. The Prophet's duty is both: he gives glad tidings and he warns. Allah says in the verse of Surah An-Nisa: 'We sent messengers'—meaning, what is implied or hidden here is 'Inna arsalna rusulan' (Indeed, We sent messengers)—'mubashshirina wa mundhirin' (bearers of glad tidings and warners). Why were they sent? Allah says: 'Li-alla yakuna lin-nasi 'ala Allahi hujjatun ba'da ar-rusul' (So that after the messengers, people would have no argument against Allah). Now they cannot say they did not know, because Allah gave man intellect and also sent messengers, and placed gnosis in his very nature. So, Allah has covered all three aspects. He gave him intellect, the light of reason, through which he can distinguish truth from falsehood, and He also sent messengers so that after the messengers provide a reminder, after the messengers' warning, people will have no other argument left. Allah has completed the evidence to such an extent. And Allah also mentioned in the Quran what people would say if He had not done these three things. And what is that? They say: 'Lawla arsalta ilayna rasulan mundhiran fanattabi'a ayatika min qabli an nadhilla wa nakhza' (If only You had sent us a messenger who would warn us, so that we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced). Allah has clearly stated this in the Quran. Now, after this, no argument remains for people to say, 'If only we had known.' That is why when Allah casts people into Hell, the angels will ask them: 'Alam ya'tikum nadhir?' (Did no warner come to you?). 'Nadhir' means a warner. Did no warner come to you? They will say—and Allah is telling us their answer—'Qalu bala qad ja'ana nadhir' (They will say: Yes, a warner certainly came to us—meaning prophets, Imams, and successors all came). 'Fakadhhabna' (But we denied them). We did not believe them. 'Wa qulna ma nazzala Allahu min shay' (And we said: Allah has not revealed anything). Allah has not revealed any Quran, He has not sent any messengers, He has not sent any light—the light we mentioned yesterday. They will deny it. 'We did not know. We were unaware. Allah sent nothing.' That is why when they say this, Allah says they are insulting Him. Whose insult is this? It is an insult to Allah. How? Allah says in the Quran: 'Ma qadaru Allaha haqqa qadrihi' (They have not appraised Allah with the true appraisal that is due to Him). When someone is not appraised as they should be, it is an insult, a humiliation. This is a verse of the Quran: 'Ma qadaru Allaha haqqa qadrihi'. Why? Because when they say that Allah sent no one, it is an insult. This is a verse of the Quran regarding the 'hujjah' (proof), that Allah completes the proof in this way. By sending messengers, prophets, successors, and Imams, no argument is left for anyone. And as I submitted to you, Allah also gave intellect and placed gnosis in human nature. Now, nothing is left. In Masjid al-Nabawi, he is telling the worshippers, 'We do not consider you Muslims until you believe in Ali.' He took it from a verse of the Quran. It is a verse of Surah al-Mumtahanah, 'Kafarna bikum' (We disbelieve in you). 'We do not consider you Muslims until you believe in Allah alone.' Yahya ibn Umm al-Tawil used to use this verse and stand in Masjid al-Nabawi and say this. Look, we do not even know who Yahya ibn Umm al-Tawil is. Now, when he started doing this not once, but regularly, what happened? People complained. They went to the ruler and said, 'This man is ruining our faith, he keeps saying things like this to us.' So he called him and asked, 'Do you say this?' He said, 'Yes, I say this.' He did not say, 'No, no, sorry, sorry.' He said, 'Yes, I say this and I believe in it too. I don't just say it, I believe in it.' He asked, 'Do you know the consequences?' He said, 'Do whatever you want.' And it is a very detailed story; we are not narrating it, we are speaking very briefly, that's all. He had Yahya ibn Umm al-Tawil killed; he was martyred. When the news of his martyrdom reached Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), the Imam said, 'Rahimahu Allah' (May Allah's mercy be upon him). The Mawla did not say, 'Oh, he did wrong, he shouldn't have done this, he should have used Taqiyya (dissimulation), he should have done this...' No, no, he said, 'Rahimahu Allah,' may Allah's mercy be upon him. For the survival of the religion, a person should do everything. And what is the religion? It is the message of the Ahl al-Bayt. Nothing else. And this was the very thing, this was the thing in which the son of Amir al-Mu'minin, Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas, was completely immersed, completely drowned. He was so immersed that he never considered himself equal to Husayn. He was the commander of the army, Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas, he was the standard-bearer, the Alamdar. But Husayn did not give him permission to fight. Until the day of Ashura arrived. Once, a voice came at the door of the tent, 'Sakina, daughter Sakina.' Sakina came running hearing her uncle's voice, the niece came running, 'Uncle, why did you call?' Sakina had great love for Abbas. She had great love and great hopes. She had many hopes. So Sakina said, 'Uncle, why did you call?' He said, 'Daughter, bring the water skin.' She said, 'Uncle, what will you do with the water skin?' He said, 'I went to the Master and asked for permission to fight, and the Master said no, you bring water for the children. So bring it, let me bring water for the children.' Sakina heard just this, she ran and brought the water skin. Now, when the little children saw the water skin in Sakina's hand, they started saying, 'Bibi, where are you taking this water skin?' She said, 'My, my uncle is going to bring water now. Father has ordered. Father has ordered Uncle to bring water. Children, now be assured. Now, now, now water will definitely come. My uncle will bring water.' Sakina gave the water skin to Abbas. Abbas set off with this water skin. Now, the way Abbas walked, there was such awe and majesty, he pushed the armies aside. Abbas's mere gaze was enough. Abbas's mere awe and majesty were enough. The soldiers started running here and there. Abbas took his horse into the Euphrates. The horse entered, Abbas... He got off the horse, put the water skin aside, took water in his palms, and said, 'O wicked ones! Do not think that I am helpless, I am powerless. I can drink water, but I will not drink, because the children in the tent are thirsty, my niece is thirsty.' Abbas put the water skin aside. After putting it aside, he filled the water skin. After filling the water skin, Abbas mounted the horse again. Abbas mounted and as he started walking towards the tent, Hurmula fired such an arrow of oppression that the arrow hit the water skin. Before that, what did the wicked ones do? They severed Abbas's right arm. Abbas recited a Rajaz (epic poem) that 'Even if you sever my right arm, I will still continue to serve my Master.' Then they severed his left arm. Abbas held the water skin with his teeth. Now, even though he held it with his teeth, he was still heading towards the tent. Both arms were gone, when suddenly another arrow of oppression was fired. Hurmula fired such an arrow that it hit the water skin. Water started flowing. As soon as the water flowed, Abbas, Abbas thought, 'Now what will I do by going towards the tent?' He stood with his head bowed. As soon as he stood with his head bowed, a wicked one, a cursed one, struck such a mace of iron on his head that Ali's lion, Ali's lion, fell from the back of the sky onto the land of Karbala. He fell onto the land of Karbala. Mourners! Mourners! Remember, whenever someone falls from a height, falls down, then naturally, in a natural way, what do they do? They first extend their hands forward. Alas, my oppressed one! Abbas fell face down. The wicked ones attacked. Abbas called out, 'Master! Accept my final salutation. Accept my final salutation.' As soon as Husayn heard this final salutation, he held his back. He recited a strange elegy: 'Al-ana inkasara dhahri' (Now my back is broken). Abbas, now my back is broken. Mourners! Remember, there are many words for breaking in Arabic. One word is 'Kasra'. 'Kasra' is used when something breaks in such a way that it can never be mended again. Husayn said, "Abbas! My back is broken now, and it will never be mended." "Al-āna inkasara ẓahrī" (Now my back is broken). "Wa qallat ḥīlatī" (And my stratagem has diminished). Abbas, I can see no way out now. I cannot understand anything anymore. And now, listen to the final lines of the elegy. He says, "Wa shamuta bī ʿadūwī" (And my enemy has gloated over me). Abbas, the enemy is taunting me. The enemy is taunting me. The one you were proud of, your standard-bearer, has been killed. Saying this, Husayn reached Abbas. He reached the banks of the Euphrates. He took Abbas's head and placed it on his lap. There was a conversation between the two brothers for a while. Abbas made a will, "Master! Do not take my body towards the tents. Let my body remain here." And as he said this, Abbas's eyes closed. Husayn then recited an elegy and said, "Abbas! Now those eyes that used to stay awake out of fear of you will sleep in peace. Now the ladies will stay awake, now the children will stay awake. Abbas, goodbye." "Wa sayaʿlamu alladhīna ẓalamū ayya munqalabin yanqalibūn" (And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned). "Alā laʿnatu Allāhi ʿalā al-ẓālimīn" (Verily, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers). O Lord! O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord! Remove the difficulties of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant those who are childless, righteous and virtuous children. Grant those who are ill, complete and swift recovery. Return those who are far from their homelands, safe and sound. Wherever the Shia of Ali-e-Qarrar are in the world, O Lord! Protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the sacred shrines. Protect those who are protecting them, especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zaynab (s.a.). Protect those who are guarding this shrine. O Lord! Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Husayn.

chapters.summary: The speaker explains that both intellect and tradition necessitate a divinely appointed guide who possesses knowledge and light to lead humanity.
