title: EP04 | Hujjat-e-Khuda Ki Haqeeqat |  ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of divine guidance and the role of the Imam as the Hujjatullah (Proof of Allah). It utilizes logical arguments, such as those presented by Hisham ibn al-Hakam, to demonstrate that just as the human intellect resolves sensory confusion, an Imam is required to resolve human disagreement and maintain order in the universe. The discourse further clarifies the concept of the hidden Imam, comparing his presence to the sun behind clouds, and emphasizes the importance of Waseela as a divine system for human guidance.
content:
PSR presents. 'Ashhadu anna Aliyyan Waliullah'. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjah son of Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance and curse all their enemies. To proceed: Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in the Holy Quran, 'Qala faman rabbukuma ya Musa? Qala rabbunalladhi a'ta kulla shay'in khalqahu thumma hada' (He said, 'Who then is the Lord of you two, O Musa?' He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it'). In this verse of the Holy Quran, in these two verses, Allah is narrating a story, a conversation between Pharaoh and Prophet Musa (a.s.). Pharaoh asked, 'Who is the Lord of you two, O Musa?' meaning you and Harun. So Prophet Musa replied, 'Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it.' Our Lord is the one who creates everything and then guides it. Meaning, whatever Allah has created, 'a'ta kulla shay'in khalqahu thumma hada', Allah has guided it, and Allah has not left any creature without guidance. Before starting the discussion, I have to submit one thing to you: whatever this discussion will be, God willing, it will be on the topic of Imamate as long as Allah grants the ability. And whatever objections there are regarding Imamate, or if anyone has any questions in their mind—either from this speech or on the topic of Imamate—from any religion or school of thought, whether they are Shia, Sunni, Deobandi, Wahhabi, anyone who has a question, they should send their question to the provided phone number, send it to The Strong Rope, and if they want to send audio, send audio; if they want to send video, send video. Whatever it is, whatever the question, if it is written, send it in writing; God willing, we will try our best to answer it. Just a request to you: let the conversation remain within the bounds of etiquette. So our discussion was that in every era, there must be a Proof of God (Hujjah) who is the cause of creation, who is the cause of the universe, who is the connection between the creatures and Allah. 'Aynas sababul muttasilu baynal ardi was sama' (Where is the cause that is connected between the earth and the sky?). Where is that cause, that connection between the sky and the earth, meaning between God and the creatures? Look, every wise person will accept that Allah would never create anything without a purpose, pointlessly, or without an objective. No rational, wise human would do this. Even an ordinary person would not do this. So when an ordinary wise person would not do this, how can we expect from Allah that He created the entire universe—such a huge universe, such huge galaxies, rather galaxies—and left them without any goal, without any purpose? No, it is not like that. Rather, in the light of the teachings of the Holy Quran, Allah has created everything for a goal and a purpose, whether they are inanimate objects, plants, animals, or humans. Inanimate objects, meaning things like stones, etc., are called inanimate objects. What we generally call in English 'inanimate objects', although in the light of the Quran and the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), nothing is inanimate. Everything glorifies Allah, 'wa lakin la tafqahuna tasbihahum' (but you do not understand their glorification). Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah. So Allah has created such a vast universe containing inanimate objects, plants, animals, then humans, then angels, then jinns, and all the things in the world. So it is obvious that Allah would not leave the universe without a guide, without a leader. That is why when Pharaoh asked—this question of Pharaoh—'Qala faman rabbukuma ya Musa', Prophet Musa replied, 'Rabbunalladhi a'ta kulla shay'in khalqahu thumma hada'. And exactly this point was used by Hisham ibn al-Hakam in his debate with Amr ibn Ubayd. This is present in Al-Kafi, the famous book of traditions, which Sheikh Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, who passed away in 329 AH, compiled. In it, in the 'Kitab al-Hujjah', he narrated this tradition. And the tradition is such that Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who is an author of an 'Asl' (original manuscript) and one of the very special companions of the Imam, narrated this hadith. We were some companions of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) with the Imam, among whom were Humran ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Nu'man—who is famous as Mu'min al-Taq—Hisham ibn Salim al-Jawaliqi, Hamza ibn Muhammad—who is famous as al-Tayyar—Hamza ibn Muhammad, and Hisham ibn al-Hakam. All these people were sitting, and Yunus ibn Ya'qub says Hisham was the youngest, the youngest of all. So in that gathering, the Imam asked Hisham, 'Faqala Abu Abdillah ya Hisham ala tukhbiruni kayfa sana'ta bi Amr ibn Ubayd' (Imam Abu Abdillah said, 'O Hisham, will you not tell me how you debated with Amr ibn Ubayd? And how you questioned him?'). Hisham said, 'Ya Ibna Rasoolillah inni ujilluka' (O son of the Messenger of Allah, I respect you, and I feel shy, and my tongue does not open before you'). Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'Idha amartukum bishay'in faf'alu' (When we command you to do something, then comply with it). When we say something. So Hisham says—I will narrate the entire debate to you very quickly. Hisham says that I found out that Amr ibn Ubayd, whose school of thought, whose religion was the Mu'tazili religion. In that era, the Mu'tazili religion was prevalent everywhere, which was the opposition to the Shias. The Mu'tazili religion, which has almost disappeared today—the Mu'tazili religion does not exist now. In that era, it was the main religion. So I heard that he was following the Mu'tazili religion in the Mosque of Basra, and he had a good gathering there. So I could not digest this; it was hard for me that this man was speaking against Imamate and I am sitting here in Kufa, doing nothing. Therefore, I went to Basra on a Friday and entered the Mosque of Basra. There I saw that people were sitting in circles, and Amr ibn Ubayd was wearing a very scholarly attire, meaning he had a wool cloak draped over him, and another cloak over that, and he was sitting like a very great scholar, answering people's questions. I pushed through the people, went inside, and sat in the last circle. I sat on my knees so that he could see me. Then, when I got the chance to ask a question, I said, 'Ayyuhal alim' (O scholar)—I addressed him with great respect so that he would pay attention to me—'Inni rajulun gharib, ta'dhan li fi mas'alah?' (I am a traveler; will you permit me to ask you a question?). He said to me, 'Na'am' (Yes). I said to him, 'Alaka ayn?' (Do you have an eye?). He said, 'Ya bunayya ayyu shay'in hadha minas su'al?' (O my son, what kind of question is this? A thing you see, how can you ask about it?). I said, 'Hakadha mas'alati' (My question is like this). He said, 'Ya bunayya is'al' (Okay, son, ask, even if your question is foolish, it is a stupid question, still I will answer it, no problem). I said, 'Ajibni fiha' (Answer me). He said to me, 'Sal' (Ask). I said, 'Alaka ayn?' (Do you have an eye?). He said, 'Na'am' (Yes). I said, 'Fama tasna'u biha?' (What do you do with it?). He said, 'Ara bihal alwan wal ashkhass' (I see colors and people with it). Then I asked the second question, 'Falaka anfun?' (Do you have a nose?). He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What do you do with it?' He said, 'Ashummu bira'iha' (I smell fragrances with it). I said, 'Do you have a mouth?' He said, 'Yes.' 'What do you do with it?' He said, 'I taste food, various foods, I taste their flavor.' 'Qultu falaka udhun?' (I said, do you have ears?). He said, 'What do you do with it?' He said, 'Asma'u bissawt' (I hear sounds with it). Then after asking all the questions, Hisham asked, 'Alaka qalbun?' (Do you have a heart/intellect?). Here, 'Qalb' refers to intellect (Aql). Because the heart is that essence in the soul that perceives the light of intellect. Therefore, in traditions, it is also called Qalb. So, 'Alaka qalbun?' (Do you have an intellect?). He said, 'Na'am' (Yes). 'Qultu fama tastaw bihi?' (I said, what do you do with it?). 'Qala umayyizu bihi kullama warada ala hazil jawarih wal hawas' (He said, I distinguish with it everything that comes to these limbs and senses). Whatever I see, do, or hear with these limbs and senses, whatever I perceive, I present all those perceptions before my intellect. Then Hisham asked, 'Awalaysa fi hazil jawarih ghaniyan anil qalb?' (Are these limbs and senses of yours not independent of this intellect?). "What is the need for intellect? When these (senses) are there, then you do not need intellect." So he (the opponent) said, "No, I am not independent of it; I need it." I asked, "How is that? And these are the sound senses, or rather, they are sound." While all these limbs and body parts, these five senses, are all working perfectly, then what is the need for intellect? He replied, "O my son, when the limbs doubt something—whether they smell it, see it, taste it, or hear it—whenever they doubt, they refer it to the intellect. And when the intellect convinces it of something and removes the doubt, I reach that stage of certainty." Then Hisham asked, "So Allah has established the heart (intellect) to resolve the doubts of the limbs?" He said, "Yes, that is so." Then Hisham asked, "So the heart (intellect) is necessary?" "Otherwise, you would never reach the state of certainty." He said, "Yes, that is so." "So I said to him," then Hisham changed his tone and said, "O Abu Marwan, Allah (T.B.T.A.) did not leave your limbs alone until He provided them with an Imam (intellect) to correct what is right for them and remove their doubts, turning doubt into certainty. And do you imagine that Allah would leave the entire universe, such a vast galaxy, such a vast creation, without an Imam so that they remain wandering in doubt, and there is disagreement among them, and they have no Imam to whom they can refer? And for your limbs, Allah has appointed an Imam to remove your doubt and bewilderment?" Hisham says, "He fell silent and did not say a thing." He was completely silent, and all his students were listening. Then the hadith is a bit longer, so we will summarize it: "Then he embraced me and seated me in his place, in the seat where he was sitting." For any great teacher, the seat he sits on is a great honor. If he seats someone in his place, it is a great honor for that person. And this Ibn Ubayd al-Mu'tazili was such a great teacher, and he seated a young man in his place. "And he moved away from his seat and did not speak." And until I remained seated, he did not come near that seat, and he did not utter a word until I stood up myself. Hisham says, "I stood up myself." The debate was completed. "Then Imam Sadiq (a.s.) laughed." Imam Sadiq (a.s.) laughed after hearing this whole story. "And he said, 'O Hisham, who taught you this?'" "I said, 'It is something I took from you.' And I compiled it." He said, "By Allah, this is written in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa." This is written in the heavenly books, this thing you have discussed. So, the existence of an Imam, the existence of a Hujjah (proof), is something written in the scrolls, which no one can deny. Now, let us move to another hadith, and the narrator of this hadith is Sulayman ibn Mehran al-A'mash. He was not a Shia; he was among the opponents, but he narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), and he was considered reliable and truthful; people believed he was truthful and did not lie. So he narrates this tradition, which is present in Kamal al-Din, Volume 1, Page 207, Chapter 21, that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that he heard from his father, and he from his father, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), that the Imam says, "We are the Imams of the Muslims." The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the Imams of the Imams. "And we are the Proof of Allah (Hujjatullah) over the worlds," over the entire universe that Allah created, all the creatures He created. "And we are the masters of the believers." "And we are the leaders of the radiant and noble ones." "And we are the masters of the believers." "And we are the security for the inhabitants of the earth." "We are the cause of safety for the earth, just as the stars are a cause of safety for the inhabitants of the heavens." "We are those through whom Allah holds the sky from falling on the earth, except by His permission." By Allah's permission. "And through us, Allah holds the earth from shaking with its inhabitants." "And through us, Allah sends down the rain." "And through us, Allah spreads His mercy." "And the earth brings forth its blessings." Look at what the concept of Hujjatullah is. This is the concept of Hujjatullah we have. An Imam is not just someone who becomes a king, and then even if he is a drunkard or a sinner, it does not matter, as long as he is praying, that is enough. Just that is sufficient. And then it is forbidden for people to rebel against him; one should not rebel. Yes, that is fine. And then what is the principle? "We are with whoever wins." The goal is just kingship. No, here it is not a king; here it is truly the Divine Proof. He is Allah's representative. He is the link between Allah and the creation. Or in other words, as it has come in the traditions, he is the Wali al-Ni'mah (Guardian of Blessings). The Imam, the Hujjatullah, is the one who is the guardian of blessings; Allah reaches His blessings to the creation through him. Then the Imam says, "And if there were no one from us on the earth, it would collapse with its inhabitants." Then he (a.s.) said, "And the earth has not been without a Hujjah of Allah since Allah created Adam, and it will not be until the Day of Judgment." Not even for a moment. It is not possible. Whether that Hujjah is manifest and famous, Or hidden and veiled. He is hidden. People may not see him, that is fine, but the Hujjatullah is there. These are all his benefits. It is not just about government. People ask, "If he is not ruling, what is the benefit?" These are ignorant people. They do not understand the purpose of Hujjatullah; they do not know the meaning. Because their knowledge has not reached that far. Why? Why has it not reached? Because they did not attend the door of the City of Knowledge. Then the Imam says, "And it will not be until the Hour (Day of Judgment) arrives that there will be a Hujjah of Allah on it." Until the Day of Judgment, there will always be a Hujjatullah on earth. "And if it were not for that, Allah would not be worshipped." Meaning, if Allah is being worshipped in the universe, if there is a perfect human who is performing the worship of Allah as it is rightfully due, then he is the Hujjatullah. Today, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is the Hujjatullah, the Perfect Human, the Wali al-Ni'mah. Then, when the Imam explained all these things, Sulayman, the narrator, asked, "I said to Sadiq (a.s.), 'How do people benefit from the hidden and veiled Hujjah?'" title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#04 - Kya Shaikh Mufeed (a.r.) ne Bait e Tatheer par hamle ka inkaar kiya?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common misconception that the prominent Shia scholar Sheikh al-Mufid denied the historical attack on the house of Sayyida Fatima al-Zahra (s.a.). The speaker clarifies that Sheikh al-Mufid's comments in 'Kitab al-Irshad' were directed at the unreliability of a specific distorted manuscript he possessed, rather than a denial of the historical event itself. The lecture emphasizes the importance of scholarly context and warns against the manipulation of historical texts to serve modern agendas.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. We are here to serve you with a new objection and its answer. The objection is that some people are seen saying that Sheikh al-Mufid has denied the attack on the house of Sayyida Zahra (s.a.) in his book. So, did Sheikh al-Mufid really deny this incident? Come, to get this objection and its answer, we request that you try to... Try to understand that some people claim that Sheikh al-Mufid denied the attack on the house of Sayyida Zahra (s.a.). So, what is this number, what is the difficulty, and what is its answer? We would like you to present a scholarly answer to this in the service of the viewers. Some people, through their failed attempts, try to say that great scholars like Sheikh al-Mufid have denied that this happened here, and they want to make people deny this incident in one way or another. If we look at the view of Sheikh al-Mufid in his book 'Kitab al-Irshad', which they quote... They quote from this book, saying that this is not a reliable book, and this book is what is written in it. They also deny the incident along with the book. Now, let us try to understand the manuscript of the book that Sheikh al-Mufid had. If we look at the book 'Kitab al-Irshad' by Sheikh al-Mufid, on page 149, he discusses this incident and writes that whatever is narrated from the traditions... if we look at the testimony of Sheikh al-Mufid, who was the teacher of Sheikh al-Mufid, he says that regarding the traditions of the Sunnis, he says that the traditions written about... in the book... In which he has narrated the traditions of his ancestors... now, what is this? He says it is correct. It is absolutely correct; he has no objection to it. In that regard, he says, 'This book is...' But this manuscript is unreliable. It is clear that he is not denying the incident itself; he is questioning the manuscript he had. He is not questioning the incident itself, but the authenticity of the manuscript he possessed. Therefore, we can say that he did not fully rely on it. That he did not fully rely on it. We will present this before you. And one thing we want to point out here is that when he reached this, he said that those who raise this slogan that Sheikh al-Mufid denied the attack on the house of Sayyida Zahra (s.a.) are committing a great scholarly dishonesty. If we look here, what is he seen writing? 'This is correct,' meaning its meaning and its content are correct. This sentence comes before what he says. People just want to twist and present this thing to support their point. If we look at 'Kitab al-Irshad' and the pages of 'Kitab al-Irshad', the remaining part can also be kept in view. See how people have manipulated this to suit their own agenda. If we look at the manuscript that Sheikh al-Mufid had regarding 'Kitab al-Irshad', he says that it is not permissible to act upon most of the things in this manuscript because it is distorted. The traditions were distorted, and things were added to them by others. Therefore, he is speaking about the manuscript. He says that it is necessary to refrain from acting upon everything in this manuscript and not to completely reject it, nor to follow its narrators. If we look, none of our books are considered 100% correct. We do not accept any book as 100% correct. So, he is saying that we should be cautious and distinguish between what is correct and what is incorrect. He says that it is necessary to investigate the traditions in this manuscript and clarify which things are correct and which are false. Therefore, this is Sheikh al-Mufid's view regarding that manuscript which he had at that time. In summary, if we look at what Sheikh al-Mufid said, it is quite clear. If the intention is to clarify, then this is absolutely clear. The Vice-President and the Deputy have once again repeated the attack on the Princess (s.a.). The researchers are raising questions about the sources of this incident, and they are seen saying that the claim is correct. When they say that my leader covers her face, that is considered correct. On the other hand, if you look at Syed Masoom's statements, you will see that they are trying to give a completely new color to things. They are trying to deny it. Indeed, brother, the perspective regarding the incident that you are presenting, and the difficulties regarding the sources you are mentioning, can be presented. You are famous for this, and the main point is this: look at the entire family, if Rizwan Sahab, the Shia scholar, says in this regard that the books we have received, the sources that have reached us, there is no such city or any such thing that is fundamentally against the 5th class, this is wrong. And they are pointing towards this. And they are pointing towards this, that there is no such thing with the looters. It is absolutely clear that you were in a rally and there were different sources, and regarding the one you mentioned, about which there is a difference of opinion, the researcher has expressed his opinion. And another thing we have to keep in mind is this: the city, the reconstruction, and the people who live in Baghdad and its surrounding areas, for them, it is very important. If we look, for example, at the Tarek-e-Khilafat, it is found there that 20,000, 196, those who sit, those two people, usually in those circumstances, such a thing that describes things very clearly, it is possible that here too, this is a very natural approach, and all this is happening because this incident is being described in this way. And the big thing is that this incident, which happened to the Princess (s.a.), if it is not described, then what do we find? That among them, how many arguments are there? Here, in my book... How many arguments are there? Here, in my book, I have described it. For example, in the very famous book 'Dala'il al-Imamah' and others, in 18506, where they describe it, and they describe it... it is a very famous book in which they have [music]... and they state that after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was the honor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). That is, the one whose name the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) mentioned, in the way that the famous Imam Hussain (a.s.) here... In the way that the famous Imam Hussain (a.s.) here, here the example is exactly when they are describing the incident of the attack. This whole thing is a conspiracy, due to which people are saying this. They say that they did not even attack the Princess's (s.a.) house, that there was some disturbance, or in some way, people want to deny this incident and create doubt in people's hearts regarding this incident. title: Sakhaawat e Ahle Bait (عليهم السلام)  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi recounts a historical encounter between a beggar and the third caliph, contrasting his limited charity with the profound generosity and wisdom of the Ahlulbayt. The lecture highlights the specific conditions under which Islam permits seeking financial assistance, emphasizing dignity and self-sufficiency. Through the actions of Imam Hasan, Imam Hussain, and Abdullah ibn Ja'far, the speaker illustrates the superior moral and material support provided by the Prophet's household.
content:
It was the era of the third ruler after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). You know that people give him grand titles, don't they? They say he was very generous and open-handed. Okay. He was sitting outside the mosque. The third ruler was sitting outside. He was sitting on a chair, and I said, he wouldn't be alone. Naturally, a ruler doesn't sit alone, as you know. A beggar came. A seeker, and he said, 'I need some money. Please help me.' He said, 'Give him five dirhams.' Five dirhams. Even if you calculate by today's standards, a dirham is about 20 rupees. In today's time. Right? He was so generous, 'Give him 100 rupees.' Understand? 100 rupees. Give this beggar 100 rupees. Clear? He said, 'This won't solve my problem.' He said, 'Arshit, arshit,' meaning, 'Tell me another door, brother.' Meaning, this won't suffice. Anyway, he was also wise in this regard. He said, 'Look, in the mosque, do you see those three men sitting there? Go to them. You will find it there.' Who were the three sitting there? It is in the hadith: Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.), Imam Hussain (a.s.), and Janabe Abdullah ibn Ja'far, the husband of Janabe Zainab. These three were sitting in Masjid-e-Nabawi. This beggar came and said, 'I need help.' Now look at Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.). Look at his generosity. He says, 'It is not permissible to spread one's hand before others.' Meaning, there is training happening, and there is generosity happening. 'It is not permissible to spread one's hand before others unless there are three things.' If there are no three reasons, three causes, then never spread your hand before others. One, either you have to pay blood money (diyat), to save someone's life. To save someone's life. To pay the blood money. You know what blood money is, right? When someone kills another, the murderer or the murderer's family has to pay the victim's family. That is called blood money, it is called diyat. Either for that reason. Two, or you are heavily indebted, drowning in debt, and are very troubled because of the debt. And third, such poverty and such neediness that breaks a person. Break, meaning the Imam not only stated the reason, one is blood money, and second, if there is debt, then the debt that keeps a person awake at night, that debt. And third, such poverty, such trouble that breaks a person. Unless these three reasons exist, do not spread your hand before anyone. Look at what a beautiful Islam this is. On one hand, it emphasizes being generous, and on the other, it says begging is forbidden. Begging is not permissible, 'la yahil', unless these three things are present. A Shia will never forcefully spread his hand before anyone. So now, which of these three things is the reason you are asking? Now his answer, he was also a clever man. He said, 'It is one of these three, but I cannot tell you.' One of these three. There is some reason, anyway. The Imam said, 'Okay, no problem.' He did not insist. Now what did the Imam do? Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.) gave him 50 dinars. Dinars. Meaning, if you take the dinar at today's rate, it is likely 200 rupees. So 50 * 200, that is 1000 rupees right there. Then after that, Imam Hussain (a.s.) gave him 49 dinars. Then Janabe Abdullah ibn Ja'far gave him 48 dinars. Thus, 147 dinars, although the rate we are mentioning is just based on today's currency, otherwise you know what a dinar is, right? It was the gold coin, right? That is what it is called. A gold coin. Now you calculate its value yourself. So the Imam gave, meaning they gave so much, 50, 49, 48. All three gave him money from their own pockets. He left with it. Now as he was leaving, he came back to the door of the mosque. The old man was sitting there. He was watching the scene from afar. He couldn't help himself. He asked, 'What happened?' He said, 'I came to you, and you only gave me five dirhams. But when I went to them, they not only gave me money, but they also asked about my problems, guided me, and told me when one should ask for money and when one should not. And after that, those three gave me such and such an amount.' When he heard this, he said—who? The ruler said. He said, 'These are the individuals for whom Allah has written all goodness in their share.'

title: Fadak Ki Zameen Kitni Badi Thi? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses a historical dialogue between Harun al-Abbasi and Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) regarding the land of Fadak. Imam Kazim (a.s.) explains that the true boundaries of Fadak are not limited to a small piece of land but encompass the entire world. This narrative highlights the spiritual and symbolic significance of Fadak beyond its material value. The lecture emphasizes the Imam's perspective on the rightful inheritance of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
There is a Muslim, Harun al-Abbasi, and Imam Kazim (a.s.). In this, Harun al-Abbasi asks Imam Kazim (a.s.) why you do not demand Fadak. Imam Kazim (a.s.) says that we will not take it back until we get it with all its boundaries. Harun was surprised, and that is why he asked this question. Then Harun asked, 'Alright, tell me, what is the boundary of Fadak?' The Imam said, 'Its first boundary is Aden, its second boundary is Samarkand, which is a city in that region, its third boundary is Africa, and its fourth boundary is the world.' That is, you can imagine how big the land of Fadak is.
Harun al-Abbasi questioned Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.) about reclaiming Fadak.

Fadak is not merely a piece of agricultural land but a symbol of the Ahlulbayt's rights.

title: Majlis 7 | Deen Ka Dushman Kaun? - Part 1 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the fundamental Shia concepts of Wilayah and Bara'ah, emphasizing that true faith requires both love for the Ahlulbayt and disassociation from their enemies. The discussion highlights the spiritual dangers of harboring malice toward Imam Ali and the Ahlulbayt, citing historical narrations and the foundational works of Shia scholars like Sheikh al-Tusi. The session concludes with a poignant reflection on the martyrdom of Hazrat Abbas at Karbala, illustrating his unparalleled loyalty and the profound grief experienced by Imam Hussain.
content:
If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. Your princess would not have been dragged from door to door. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. Zaynab used to call out to Abbas: If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. And sometimes she would look towards the grave, and sometimes towards Najaf. Sometimes she would look towards the grave, and sometimes towards Najaf. Sometimes she would look at your severed shoulders. She pulled the spear out of the chest of Shah-e-Akbar. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. And the second Zahra (Zaynab) also became weak. The second Zahra also became weak. I am breathing, but I am not alive. I swear by your severed pieces, your sister is broken. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. And my hands were also tied with ropes. My hands were also tied with ropes. I could not even take the support of my hands, brother. Just as you fell from the horse, I fell from the camel. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. Even the prison laments my poverty. Even the prison laments my poverty. Where does it happen that the laborers lift the corpses? Ali's daughter fulfilled the duty of the sons. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. And how can I describe the scene of that court, brother? How can I describe the scene of that court, brother? The tyrant was playing with the head of the Master, brother. He was hitting my lips, he was hitting the lips of my brother with a cane. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. And the feet used to stumble a lot, so they would fall. The feet used to stumble a lot, so they would fall. They would ask, "Where are my young ones?" The body of my brother Ali Akbar could not be found. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. They did not let the innocent one sleep in peace in the grave. That atrocity was committed upon you... The body of Ali Asghar was searched for with spears. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. And Mir Sajjad, you will also feel this. Mir Sajjad, you will also feel this. The voice of the Master also comes upon the grave of Ghazi. Even today, my child is imprisoned in the dungeon. If you were here, this would not have happened, Ghazi. Raḥima Allāhu man qaraʾa al-Fātiḥah. Aʿūdhu billāhi as-samīʿi al-ʿalīmi min ash-shayṭāni ar-rajīm. Bismillāhi ar-raḥmāni ar-raḥīm. Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīm. Ḥasbunā Allāhu. Wa niʿma al-wakīl, niʿma al-mawlā wa niʿma an-naṣīr. Alḥamdulillāhi rabbil ʿālamīn, wal ʿāqibatu lil-muttaqīn, wal yaqīn, waṣ-ṣalātu was-salāmu ʿalā ashrafil anbiyāʾi wal mursalīn, Ḥabībi ilāhil ʿālamīn, Abil Qāsim Muḥammad. Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa āli Muḥammad. Ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa ālihi al-maʿṣūmīn, alladhīna adh-haba Allāhu ʿanhumur-rijsa wa ṭahharahum taṭhīrā. Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa āli Muḥammad, siyyamā baqiyyatillāhi fil arḍ, Imām-e-Zamāna wa waliyyi amrinā wa ṣāḥibinā wa mawlānā wa ḥabībinā wa ṭabībinā wa anīsinā wa munisinā, al-kāfiri ḥasīn wa ghiyāthul muḍṭaril mustaqīm, rūḥī wa arwāḥul ʿālamīna lahul fidā. Ammā baʿd, faqad qāla Allāhu jalla jalāluhu: "Mā jaʿala Allāhu lirajulin min qalbaini fī jawfihi". Sadaqallāhu al-ʿaliyyul ʿaẓīm, wa sadaqa rasūluhul karīm, amīn rabbil ʿālamīn. Ṣalawāt, Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa āli Muḥammad. Khuda-e-Muta'al is stating in the fourth verse of Surah Al-Ahzab, the verse which I have made the opening of my speech. Allah has not placed two hearts within any man; there is only one heart. Now, whether a person fills that heart with Allah or Satan, with Habil (Abel) or Qabil (Cain), this chain of truth and falsehood has been continuing. Allah has given man the choice: 'Faman sha'a falyu'min wa faman sha'a falyakfur' (Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve). There is no issue; in this world, Allah has kept everyone free. He has given everyone total freedom; everyone has freedom, choice, and liberty. The discussion was about Wilayah and Bara'ah, and because this is a very sensitive topic among us in one sense, and in another sense, its importance and its position... Its importance and significance are so great in Islam that it is very necessary to understand its various aspects, especially for the youth, because our faith is based on this, and our religion is based on this. Therefore, it is very necessary to understand it. Until now, by the grace of Allah and His help, we have been discussing one sub-topic of this subject daily. Today's sub-topic is the classification made by Allama Majlisi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alaih) regarding 'Dhammu Mubghidihim' (Condemning those who hate them), meaning the condemnation of those who hold hatred against the Ahlulbayt. Whoever holds malice or enmity against them—the title of the chapter itself explains which types of narrations Allama Majlisi has included in this... He has brought into this chapter, and there is a good number of narrations discussed in this chapter. Obviously, our discussions are very brief, so it is difficult to discuss the whole thing. Therefore, we will be very brief, and we will explain less today; we will read more Hadith because, Masha'Allah, this is a gathering of intelligent people, and there are many Hadiths. Therefore, there is no need for explanation in both respects, rather these are explanatory Hadiths, so there is no need to explain much. The first Hadith is—and some brothers also gave an order, and obeying an order is mandatory—that you should also mention the narrators of the Hadith so that a kind of credibility is established. This Hadith that we are presenting to you... We are narrating this from Sheikh Saduq's 'Amali', and the reference Sheikh Saduq has given for this Hadith is Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar. We have read about Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar ourselves in the books of Rijal; we are not saying something we heard from others. What we read, we speak. It is written in the books of Rijal that he is 'Majhul al-Qadr' (of unknown value), meaning the value that we should have placed on him—that is, the Shias—we did not place. For example, if we ask in this gathering how many people have heard his name, if only those who have heard the name raise their hands, I think it would be a minority within a minority. So, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar was also a teacher of Sheikh Kulayni. And Sheikh Saduq narrated from him; you can understand what level of person he must be. And it is written about him in the books of Rijal that he was a fountain of Hadith, a source of Hadith. He was a fountain, but people don't even know about him. And from whom such people have narrated—Sheikh Saduq, who has been given such titles, and Sheikh Kulayni, 'Thiqatul Islam' (the Trustworthy of Islam), they narrated Hadiths from him. Anyway, and he narrates from Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Qummi al-Ash'ari (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alaih), a very great personality. If we were to write about him, one volume would be the minimum required to write about him. At the very least, one volume. Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari al-Qummi is such a great personality, meaning Muhammad ibn Yahya narrates from him... And he narrates from Abdus Samad ibn Muhammad, and he narrates from Hannan ibn Sadir. Look at how strong the chain of narration (Sanad) is! Who is Hannan ibn Sadir? He is the son of Sadir al-Sayrafi. 'Sayrafi' in Arabic refers to those who deal in foreign exchange. So, Hannan is the son of Sadir al-Sayrafi. He is also a companion of the Imam, and his father was also a very special companion. These are great personalities, isn't it clear? These people narrated the Hadith, and he narrated from Sudayf al-Makki, and he narrates from Imam Baqir (a.s.). Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. You noticed how strong the chain was? So the Imam says, 'Wa ma ra'aitu...' Muhammadian qattu ya 'adlahu. Qala haddathana Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari qala... Meaning Imam Baqir (a.s.) says that I have never seen a 'Mohammadi' (a follower of the Messenger of Allah) to this day. Who is saying this? Imam Baqir (a.s.). Meaning the number of those who truly follow the Messenger of Allah is so small. You might say there are so many, look Masha'Allah, a golden age, and here the Imam is saying there is no one. 'Ma ra'aitu Mohammadan qattu ya 'adlahu'. Qala, and then he says, 'Haddathana Jabir ibn...' The Imam says Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari told me. Because Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari was a companion of the Messenger of Allah who was alive until the time of Imam Baqir (a.s.). Until that time, and the Messenger of Allah had prophesied to him, 'Jabir, you will live until that time, and when you meet my son Baqir, give him my salaam.' So here, Imam Baqir (a.s.) cites Jabir and says, 'Khatabana Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.)... Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad.' The Messenger of Allah addressed us, meaning he gave a sermon. And obviously, a sermon is given in a gathering. A sermon is not given by locking oneself in a room, so that no one hears, completely silent, right? This is completely secret, huh? What does a sermon mean? A sermon, meaning that which is being delivered in the mosque. So he said, 'Ayyuhan-nas, Ayyuhan-nas' (O people, O people), telling them that it is for everyone, huh? It is for the gathering. 'Man abghadana Ahlulbayt, ba'athahullahu yawmal qiyamati Yahudiyya' (Whoever holds hatred against us, the Ahlulbayt, Allah will resurrect him as a Jew on the Day of Judgment). He will not remain a Muslim. Whoever holds hatred against us, the Ahlulbayt. Now, what does hatred mean? There are many signs. One sign is fasting on the day of Ashura. So, whoever fasts on the day of Ashura or praises the virtue of that fast and celebrates on that day, then in this world, he might be called a Muslim, but in the hereafter, he will definitely be raised as a Jew. Subhanallah. Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! So Jabir asked, 'Ya Rasulullah, wa in sama wa salla wa za'ama annahu Muslim?' (Even if he fasts and prays and thinks he is a Muslim?) If he fasts and prays and thinks he is a Muslim, will he still be a Jew? He said (s.a.w.a.), 'Wa in sama wa salla wa za'ama annahu Muslim.' If he prays, fasts, and assumes he is a Muslim, he will still be raised as a Jew. And then the Prophet did not stop there, he did not stop here. The Prophet says, and this will be the state of his faith—O those who fast on the day of Ashura, understand this—this will be his state. The Prophet says, 'In adrakad-Dajjala amana bihi' (If he encounters the Dajjal, he will believe in him), he will not believe in Imam Mahdi. This will be his state. Did you notice? So it is very necessary for faith to be strong, it is very necessary to have love for the Ahlulbayt, and do not let even an atom's weight of hatred enter inside. And the way hatred enters is through sin. And when hatred for the Ahlulbayt enters a person's heart through sin, then many actions follow, and especially if this sin, God forbid, is committed by the mother, then when a sin is committed by the mother, hatred definitely enters the child's heart. There are many narrations in this regard. You understand that you have studied the narrations on this topic in this chapter, but it was not clear which Hadith to read and which not to. So I said, let it be, let's read two or three Hadiths and be content with that, otherwise, where will you sit and listen to 50-60 Hadiths? Recite a Salawat on Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Meaning a woman insulted Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) in the middle of the market. In the middle of the market, she insulted Amir al-Mu'minin. Amir al-Mu'minin called her by such a title, called out to her, 'Be silent!' and used that title. He used an Arabic title; I will not explain it. Whoever wants to understand later can understand, ask later and I will tell. He said, 'Uskuti ayyatussalaqliyya' (Be silent, O Salaqliyya). That woman understood what it meant. Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated a Hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.): 'Law anna ghayra waliyyi Aliyyin ata al-furata' (If someone other than a friend of Ali comes to the Euphrates—pay attention to the Hadith—if someone other than a lover of Ali comes to the bank of the Euphrates), 'wa qad ashrafa ma'ahu ala janbayhi' (and he is looking at the water of the Euphrates from both sides, meaning the Euphrates is overflowing, full), 'wa huwa yazukhu zakhiran' (and the Euphrates is surging—not just full, but surging on both sides). So much water, but in his heart, there is no Wilayat-e-Ali. Remember this. There is no Wilayat-e-Ali in his heart. So, is it permissible for him to drink the water of the Euphrates? The Imam says, 'Fatanawala bikaffihi' (he takes the water in his palms), 'wa qala' (and says), 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah), meaning he is drinking water saying Bismillah. And when 'falamma faragha' (when he finishes drinking), he says, 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to Allah), meaning he is a very great Muslim. The Imam is saying, he is a very great Muslim. He is drinking water and saying Bismillah, and finishing and saying Alhamdulillah. The Imam says, when he is drinking this, he is drinking nothing but impure blood and 'lahmi khinzir' (swine flesh). He is eating pig meat. That is, it is not permissible for him to drink the water of the Euphrates. Here, the water of the Euphrates is just given as an example. That is, he cannot use any blessing of the world. It is haram for him. Why? Because this entire universe that was created was created for the sake of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It is their charity that the universe is eating. If it does not have faith in them, then it is haram for them. This is blood, 'daman masfuhan... wa lahma khinzirin' (shed blood... or swine flesh). This is actually a verse of the Quran. It is verse number 145 of Surah Al-An'am. It is verse number 145 of Surah Al-An'am that whenever they took the water, they were not taking that water or eating that thing, except that the water was blood—flowing blood, boiling blood. Like when an animal is slaughtered, it is this boiling blood or swine flesh. It is not permissible. It is haram for him if there is no Wilayat-e-Ali. The matter is harsh, but it is the truth. Now let's move to the third Hadith, and this Hadith is very long, so we will try to read it as quickly as possible. This Hadith is from Amali al-Sheikh al-Tusi. We introduced Sheikh al-Tusi at the very beginning. Who is Sheikh al-Tusi? His title is 'Sheikh al-Ta'ifa'. And let me tell you in just one sentence who Sheikh al-Tusi is: in the history of Shi'ism, no scholar greater than Sheikh al-Tusi has been born. In the history of Shi'ism. That is, in 413 AH, when Sheikh al-Mufid passed away—who was the teacher of Sheikh al-Tusi—and Sayyid al-Murtada (r.a.), Sayyid al-Murtada was a landowner, and from Baghdad to Karbala, Sayyid al-Murtada owned 70 villages for which he was the landlord. It wasn't just land, not just two or four acres of land, not just two or four buildings; he was the owner of 70 large villages that fell on the way from Baghdad to Karbala. And along with that—meaning the religious mentor Sayyid al-Murtada—his title was 'Alam al-Huda'. He was the brother of Sayyid al-Radi, who wrote Nahj al-Balagha; he was his brother, and his elder brother, three years older than him. Sayyid al-Murtada was born in 356 AH. 356 AH, and he passed away in 436 AH, and Sayyid al-Radi was born in 359 AH, meaning three years later, and Sayyid al-Radi passed away in 406 AH, meaning he passed away at a very young age. That is, he passed away at the age of 47, and Sayyid al-Murtada lived up to 80 years. So in 413 AH, when Sheikh al-Mufid passed away, Sayyid al-Murtada became the teacher of Sheikh al-Tusi. Sayyid al-Murtada became the teacher of Sheikh al-Tusi, and for how many years was he his teacher? For 23 years, 23 years. It is clear, right? In fact, it happened that he used to teach him daily, Sayyid al-Murtada, every day. And because in that era there was no such system that, you know, stipends were not given—you know what a stipend is, the monthly allowance—that was not there. So Sayyid al-Murtada told Sheikh al-Tusi, 'I will give you 20 gold coins every month, every month.' 20 gold coins. Now you calculate yourself what the price is these days. If you take the price of 50,000, and if you take 20, then even if it was one tola, you understand how much it became per month? 50,000, so 1 million rupees per month, and don't do anything, just study. And Sheikh al-Tusi was not the type to say, 'Now I am getting money, what do I need to do?' No, no, he used to study a lot, he studied day and night, and that is why in whatever field of Islamic studies you go, you will see Sheikh al-Tusi there. And that is why we are showing the Kutub al-Arba (The Four Books) to the youngsters so that you understand how much hardship our scholars endured. Although time is spent on it, it is necessary to tell this too. Sheikh al-Tusi, the Kutub al-Arba, which are our four important books, two of them are by Sheikh al-Tusi, meaning 50% are his. One is by Sheikh al-Saduq and one is by Sheikh al-Kulayni. Sheikh al-Kulayni has Al-Kafi, Sheikh al-Saduq has the Faqih, 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', and Sheikh al-Tusi has 'Al-Istibsar' and 'Tahdhib al-Ahkam'. So this 'Tahdhib al-Ahkam' is actually a marginal commentary he wrote on his teacher Sheikh al-Mufid's book 'Al-Muqni'ah'. And Sheikh al-Mufid's book was in one volume, and the commentary he wrote on it—you know what 'marginal comments' are—the comments he wrote are in 10 volumes. In 10 volumes, that book exists, everyone reads it, scholars read it. And he didn't just stop there—meaning the fatwa that Sheikh al-Mufid gave, because Sheikh al-Mufid's 'Al-Muqni'ah' is a book of fatwas—so in comparison to that, Sheikh al-Tusi brought Hadith, either in support of the fatwa or, for example, contrary to the fatwa. Then he reconciled both of them; this is called 'Ta'adul wa Tarajih' in the terminology of scholars. He performed Ta'adul wa Tarajih to see which Hadith is in accordance, and if it is not in accordance, then why is it not in accordance? And in this way, he explained everything, Sheikh al-Tusi, and in any field you go, if you go to Tafsir, then Sheikh al-Tusi; if you go to Fiqh, then Sheikh al-Tusi; if you go to Hadith, then Sheikh al-Tusi; if you go to the field of Duas, for example, Sheikh al-Tusi; in everything. That is why his title was 'Sheikh al-Ta'ifa', meaning the Sheikh of the Shias, the teacher of the Shias. Sheikh al-Tusi. So this is from Sheikh al-Tusi's book, and what does Sheikh al-Tusi say? 'Al-Mufid'. From Mufid, from Sheikh al-Mufid, he narrated, and from whom did Sheikh al-Mufid narrate? From Ahmad ibn Walid. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Walid. From whom did he narrate? From his father, Muhammad ibn Walid. From whom did he narrate? From Sa'id ibn Abdullah, from Sa'id ibn Abdullah ibn Musa. From whom did he do it? Muhammad ibn Abdurrahman. It is a very long chain of narration, but anyway, we come directly to the part of the Hadith that is relevant to our discussion. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. That is, this Hadith is what Ibn Abbas asked the Messenger of Allah. In response to him, the Messenger of Allah is saying this, that 'Qala li' (Allah said to me), the Messenger of Allah is saying to Ibn Abbas, that Allah said to me, 'Ya Muhammad, inni ja'altu Aliyyan wasiyyaka wa waziraka wa khalifataka min ba'dika' (O Muhammad, I have made Ali your successor—your Wasi, Wasi means successor, the one who fulfills your will is called Wasi—and your minister, and your Caliph after you). Here, the Prophet used the word 'mawaddah'. The scholars have explained the difference between 'mawaddah' and 'muhabbat'. 'Muhabbat' is a qalb (heart-based) action, an action of the heart, while 'mawaddah' means to manifest it practically, to express it in action. 'Walladhi ba'athani bil-haqqi nabiyya' (By the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet). 'Wa huwa ta'ala a'lam' (And Allah is the All-Knowing). Although Allah already knows the state of his heart. Allah knows. chapters.title: Lamentation for the Tragedy of Karbala
chapters.summary: The speaker delivers a poignant lamentation from the perspective of Lady Zaynab, mourning the loss of Abbas and the suffering of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Concept of Wilayah and Bara'ah
chapters.summary: The lecture introduces the theological concept of having one heart, focusing on the necessity of loving the Ahlulbayt and dissociating from their enemies.

chapters.title: Condemnation of Hatred Against Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker analyzes narrations regarding those who harbor malice toward the Ahlulbayt, emphasizing the severe spiritual consequences of such enmity.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Warning on Hatred
chapters.summary: The lecture cites a Hadith from Imam Baqir via Jabir ibn Abdullah, warning that those who hate the Ahlulbayt will be resurrected as Jews, regardless of their outward religious practices.

chapters.title: The Role of Mothers in Faith
chapters.summary: The speaker explains how a mother's spiritual state and sins can influence the heart of her child, potentially leading to hatred for the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Value of Tears and Mourning
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the immense spiritual value of tears shed for Imam Hussain and the importance of praying for mothers who instill this love.

chapters.title: Authenticity of Hadith and Wilayat
chapters.summary: The speaker defends the reliability of scholars like Al-Kulayni and discusses the necessity of Wilayat-e-Ali for one's sustenance to be considered pure.

chapters.title: The Legacy of Sheikh al-Tusi
chapters.summary: An introduction to the scholarly stature of Sheikh al-Tusi and his educational background under Sayyid al-Murtada.

chapters.title: Sheikh al-Tusi and the Four Books
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the immense scholarly contributions of Sheikh al-Tusi, noting his authorship of two of the four primary Shia Hadith books.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Testament to Ibn Abbas
chapters.summary: The Prophet Muhammad informs Ibn Abbas of Ali ibn Abi Talib's status as his successor and emphasizes the necessity of mawaddah (practical love) for Ali.

chapters.title: The Severity of Hatred Toward Ali
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the dire consequences of harboring hatred for Ali, stating that good deeds are contingent upon his Wilayah.

chapters.title: Identifying Hatred for Ali
chapters.summary: The Prophet warns Ibn Abbas that some will claim to be part of the Ummah while harboring hatred for Ali, evidenced by preferring others over him.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Command Regarding Ali
chapters.summary: Ibn Abbas recounts the Prophet's final instructions to oppose those who oppose Ali and to follow his path as the only way to please Allah.

chapters.title: The Oppression of Imam Ali
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical oppression of Imam Ali and warns against the modern trend of showing respect to his enemies.

chapters.title: The Lineage and Bravery of Hazrat Abbas
chapters.summary: The lecture explains the importance of noble lineage and maternal influence, highlighting the extraordinary bravery and status of Hazrat Abbas.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Hazrat Abbas at Karbala
chapters.summary: The narrative details Hazrat Abbas's heroic attempt to fetch water for the thirsty children of Imam Hussain and his ultimate sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Abbas ibn Ali
chapters.summary: The speaker describes the tragic final moments of Abbas at Karbala, focusing on his sacrifice and his fall from his horse.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Grief and Final Prayers
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain mourns the loss of his brother Abbas and recites prayers for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time.

chapters.title: Concluding Supplications for the Community
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with collective prayers for the well-being, protection, and prosperity of the Shia community worldwide.

The discourse highlights the importance of parental responsibility, ethical conduct, and the necessity of aligning one's actions with the teachings of the Ahlulbayt to navigate the spiritual struggles of life.
