As soon as he heard this, he became angry. As soon as he heard this, he became angry, and he said, 'You know the reason for this? The reason is that you do not follow us, the Shias. You do not follow our teachings. You do as you please, and then you keep calling yourself Shia. That is why you do this. So, you are defaming us; you are being defamed. You are facing trouble because of us, and we are facing trouble because of you.' Then he explained what is good and what is evil. This is a point of question: what is good and what is evil? This question arises. Now, I will bore you a little for two minutes because this discussion is written in English, and there are four types of it. To remove this doubt and to answer it, because some people have written that 'good' means that which is according to one's nature, according to one's temperament, that is 'good', and that which is against one's nature is 'evil'. That is, the thing that is according to nature—in other words, the thing that we like—is 'good', and what we don't like is 'evil'. Some have written this in their books, and actually, some of our own people have written this in English. Some of our own people have translated it into English, and all these things are available. Therefore, youngsters should understand that just because something is written in a book, it is not necessarily correct. Do not accept it with your eyes closed. What does the Imam (a.s.) say? The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Be a critic of every statement.' Critically evaluate every statement. Do not accept anything with your eyes closed, no matter who says it. We only follow when it comes from the Imam (a.s.). If it is against the three principles of Shiaism, if the Hadith is fabricated, if it is a lie, and if it is against the principles of our Imams, then do not accept it. But if it is not against them, and we don't understand it, do not reject it. It is not permissible to reject a Hadith. So, the matter is that the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Be a critic, be a scholar.' When the Imam (a.s.) says something, it is better to accept it; it is not just better, it becomes obligatory. One should not apply one's own logic there. Why? Because in front of the Imam (a.s.), one's own logic is invalid. Imam (a.s.) said, 'Take the book of Hadith.' There is a debate about this, and Allama Shustari has also translated it into English. He has translated it into Urdu as well, under the name 'Isbat-ul-Haq'. He translated it under the name 'Isbat-ul-Haq'. Allama Tustari (r.a.)'s book is available. In 'Isbat-ul-Haq', he discusses the whole incident and the people who used to present their own logic against the Hadith and how they brought innovations into Islam. This is a very famous and excellent book. It has been translated into English; if you search on the net, you will find it. Anyway, this is the view of some people, and this view—this philosophical view—is all wrong because it is strictly against the Quran and Hadith. Now, look, it was said in the Quran, 'Fighting is ordained for you, while you dislike it.' Who is it talking to? It is talking to the Muslims. And when it addresses the Muslims, they will submit before the command of Allah. But this was addressed to the people, to the Shias, because they were saying, 'We are peace-loving people.' This was about the defense of Islam, about the survival of Islam, and how others were misleading them, saying, 'It is so hot, it is not right to fight in this heat. We will be defeated. In winter, it is too cold.' They were trying to make excuses and decided not to fight. They decided not to fight. We are peace-loving; we should not fight. And today, they have a command from Allah: 'Fighting is ordained for you, while you dislike it.' Actually, Jihad is a very difficult task; it is not easy. That is why it is called 'Jihad' in Arabic. Jihad means that a lot of patience is required, and a lot of difficulties are faced. It is a great struggle. What does 'Jihad' mean? Those who go to war, like our soldiers, you know they go to great heights, in winter, in summer. They are away from their families, they are away from their homes, they don't get their favorite food, and they face great difficulties. That is why soldiers are respected all over the world. Whether it is the Army, Navy, or Air Force, they are respected because they make such a great sacrifice. And a nation that does not respect its soldiers can never progress; it can never move forward. The Quran is saying, 'Fighting is ordained for you, while you dislike it.' But then, what is the matter? You have to fight; you have to go. The Quran says, 'Perhaps you dislike a thing, but it is good for you.' The Quran says, 'Perhaps you dislike a thing, but it is good for you.' And it is possible that you like a thing, but it is bad for you. This is Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 216. So, when the Quran has said this, that it is possible that you like something but it is bad for you, then the question arises: 'If this is the case, then which things are good and which things are evil? How will we know?' The answer was given by the Imam (a.s.). The Quran says, 'And Allah knows, and you do not know.' There is a very beautiful Hadith in 'Usul al-Kafi', volume 2, page 122. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'The criterion for good and evil is Paradise.' That is, if a person does something that leads to Paradise, that work can never be evil. It can never be evil. And the work that leads to Hell can never be good. So, the Imam (a.s.) has defined what is good and what is evil. The criterion is: that which leads to Paradise is good, and that which leads to Hell is evil. And that which does not lead to Paradise, look at it with contempt. It is a blessing, but if it does not lead the human to Paradise, its result is not Paradise. It is a blessing. Now, let me give you an example. Sometimes it happens that a person has children. A person loves his children very much. When he doesn't have children, he wishes for them. When children are born, he thinks, 'This is my child, I will give him the best education, the best clothes, I will do whatever I can for him.' And a person does that, doesn't he? He does it, but... A person does that, doesn't he? He does it, but what happens sometimes? May Allah protect everyone and give everyone righteous children who follow the right path. Sometimes, the children turn out to be bad. They turn back and answer their parents, and sometimes they are even responsible for their parents' blood. They give the children things they shouldn't, and the children become spoiled. When children are spoiled, they don't behave correctly, and then they start disobeying their parents, and then they start disobeying Allah. Their nature becomes such that they start defaulting. Disobedience becomes their temperament. Now, they say, 'We will not change, we will not listen to our parents.' What is the result? The result is Hell. Is this child a blessing for the parents or a curse? And this is not just about our or your matter; this was the case with Prophet Nuh (a.s.). The example of his son is before you. 'O Nuh, he is not of your family.' Allah says, 'He is not of your family.' Why? Because he was not righteous. The relationship that should exist between a father and a son, the relationship of righteousness, was not there. It was a relationship of indulgence—supporting him in forbidden acts. 'I am going to watch a movie with my friends tonight.' 'It's okay, son, go watch it.' And in many places, fathers and sons go together to watch movies. We are talking about practical things. So, what will happen? The relationship is broken. The Quran is saying, 'He is not of your family.' This is the son of Prophet Nuh (a.s.), the first of the prophets. So, therefore, what should be good and evil? The Imam (a.s.) explained it simply: 'Good' is that which pleases Allah, and 'Evil' is that which displeases Allah. He is pleased with that which is good, and He is displeased with that which is evil. It is better if we divide this a little. There are things that are permissible, and there are commands of Allah; all this is being discussed after the basics. Keep the basics in mind first; if these are not addressed, then everything else is useless. If you do not revive [your faith], everything is useless. Remember this, and if your Wilayah is weak, then everything is useless. So, after having Wilayah, the exam is clear. This Wilayah must be strong. We have traditions regarding this, and what is the strength of this in the Hadith? Today, 'Addibu Awladakum' (train your children). In Arabic, the word 'Ta'dib' is used. In Arabic, when this is done, it is 'Allahumma...'. You can do other things, but the Hadith says 'Addibu'. What does 'Addibu' mean? It means if you have to be strict, then be strict. If he is doing something that is Haram, then punish him. In the exam, it is not too much, but enough to leave a mark. If he is playing games at home and we say, 'Let's go, let's have fun,' he says, 'No, I am...' He is not even listening, and you are not being strict. And dear ones, training children on the path of Allah is everything. If you say, 'Let it be, let him go,' then the child's courage increases. He says, 'Okay, I have support now.' This thing is ruining the child. It is not right; you have to be strict. There are two reasons: one is that if you don't, then Allah leaves him to his own state. And you and I know how Allah deals with him, how He leaves him to his state, and after that, you and I will only regret it. We won't be able to do anything else. If we don't waste time then, today that child has turned out like this—what can we do? And then, these were your duties, that we refer to three things. The first thing is Allah; Allah means training in the rights of Allah. Brother, thank Allah. What is this Allah? What is obligatory and difficult in it? You have to perform it. It is obligatory and difficult, and you have to perform it. And the things that are Haram or Makruh, you must try to abstain from them. I am saying this for the children: look, whenever there is a Mustahab (recommended) act, try to do it. If you have the mood, do it; don't waste time. If you have the intention to do a good deed, do it immediately. Otherwise, what will happen? You will say, 'I will do it later,' and then you will get tired. Why go through so much trouble? Let it be. The Hadith says, 'If you have the intention, do it immediately.' Now, we have to pray. Okay, I have two Rak'ahs, I will pray at that time. But there is a lot of pain in my feet and knees. Okay, no problem, pray sitting down. So, pray sitting down. This is the command of the Sharia; there is no other way. There is no other way. If I say I will skip prayer, skip fasting, skip Hajj—if there is a Sharia reason, that is different. Pay the Kaffarah (expiation) for it. And if you cannot pay the Kaffarah, then at least look at the other things that are present. See what it says; it also does that, but understand it deeply. It is necessary to perform it. Abstaining from Haram is necessary. Allah has forbidden it, so I will not do this work; I must not do it. The second thing is this. Do not do it. The second thing is this: what are the rights of the people? These are the rights of the people. What is Haram, people have taken it, and it is wrong. For this, you should read the 'Risalat al-Huquq' (Treatise on Rights) of Imam Sajjad (a.s.). What is the right of a father over a son? What is the right of a son over a father? What is the right of a husband over a wife, and a wife over a husband? What is the son doing to the father? You should understand the rights. And when you understand the rights, then act according to them. Whatever problems we have, the reason is that we use our rights wrongly. We design rights that are not ours, and because of that, problems arise. Anyway, this is the second thing. And the third thing is... the third thing is the rights of the soul. And this is a kind of government, but a person should do it, should do it. So, keep all these things in mind. Our own character—if our character is bad, then this is the worst situation. We are talking about these things, but if your character is not good, then you very quickly go outside the circle of faith. Outside the circle of faith. In the absence of other governments, Insha'Allah, if we get the opportunity, we will cover it. If we don't get the opportunity, we don't know if we will meet again. Do you know what the Hadith is? The Imam says that if Allah had given a physical form to good character, it would have looked like the face of Hazrat Fatimah Zahra (s.a.)... [unclear]... people are happy. This is good character, gentleness. It is present in it, but the heart is not inclined. Insha'Allah, sometime later, but anyway, how should the character be? So, all these things—obligatory acts, recommended acts, abstaining from Haram, abstaining from Makruh, keeping the rights of the soul, keeping the rights of everyone, keeping the rights of the neighbor. What is the Hadith about the neighbor? What is the Hadith? That your neighbor has a right over you. This is what Islam says. Being a good neighbor does not mean... Being a good neighbor does not mean that you do not harm your neighbor. That is a strange thing—'do not harm your neighbor.' Why? You are not understanding. This is the minimum—'do not harm your neighbor.' Being a good neighbor means that when he harms you, you show patience. That he is your neighbor and he tortures you, creates problems, then show patience. And when he comes in front of you, meet him well, treat him nicely. And he knows that you did this to him, then meet him well and forgive him. Now see, his character will change, his nature will change. Islam is all this. If Allama Iqbal... there are some verses, but I am not quoting them. Allama Iqbal says that Islam has suffered as much harm from Muslims as it has not suffered from others. It has not suffered as much from outsiders. The damage that Muslims have caused to Islam, the most damage was done by Muslims. So... The most damage was done by Muslims. So, the scholars clearly say, as it is with the companions of Abdullah... this is the Hadith. Everything that is good is in front of you, and everything that is evil is in front of you. Everything—good and evil—is in front of you. Now it depends on you, whom you choose. It is up to you. 'Inna hadaynahu al-sabil' (We have shown him the way). The result will be given in the Hereafter. It will not come in this world. If you expect it in this world, then forget it. The Imam says the result will come in the Hereafter. Whatever you do, do it for the Hereafter. And this world is not anyone's anyway. There is no loyalty in the temperament of this world, nor is there any comfort. The Imam says there is no loyalty in the temperament of this world, nor is there any comfort. Never be confident in this world, never be loyal to it. If you are loyal to it, it will be loyal to you. Keep your trust for Allah; in the end, it will betray you. Keep it; in the end, it will betray you. Yes, if it is for Allah, then the result... everything is for Allah. 'Al-Jannatu dar al-khayr, wa al-Jahannamu dar al-sharr' (Paradise is the abode of good, and Hell is the abode of evil). And these two things, Paradise and Hell, will remain forever. Both of these will remain forever. Now, I have finished this, so I will move on quickly like a traveler. Now understand this. The Imam explained how you will know what is good and what is evil. How will you know? The Imam explained: 'Al-Ilm' (Knowledge) and 'Al-Jahl' (Ignorance). Knowledge is the fountainhead of all good, and ignorance is the fountainhead of all evil. It means that if you want to know what evil is, you have to acquire knowledge. You have to follow the knowledge. As long as you don't follow knowledge, you won't achieve anything. And if anyone remains in ignorance, ignorance means either he is... Ignorance means he is stupid. It means he knows this is good, but he does not follow it. So, both are wrong. So, the source of all evil is ignorance, and the source of all good is knowledge. This matter is clear. Therefore, acquiring knowledge is obligatory. There is no school for knowledge; acquiring it is obligatory. And especially if someone is a Shia, he cannot be ignorant. He cannot be ignorant. If he is ignorant, then understand that this means there is a lack of Wilayah somewhere. There is a lack of Wilayah. Whether it is in the soul or the mind, there is a lack somewhere. Why? Because the Imam says, 'Al-nasu thalathah' (People are of three types): 'Alimun rabbani' (A divine scholar whose knowledge is from Allah), 'Mutallimun fi sabil al-najat' (A student on the path of salvation). A person should always be in these two states. And the third state is... And the third state is 'Huma'an wa-ghutha'an' (scum and rubbish). If he is not in these two, then he is scum and rubbish. Therefore, always acquire knowledge. This is the command of the Mawla. Now, if you have to follow the Mawla, then follow him completely. If you have to follow the Mawla, follow him completely. The followers of the Mawla in the past, the followers of Ali, were such that they were great warriors, and they were so educated that people would ask them. Ask the follower of Ali, ask him. And that is why when Sufyan asked, 'Tell me, how did eloquence and rhetoric come into you?' Your mother replied, 'Come to the house of Ali, you will find hundreds like me.' Amr ibn al-Aas said, 'If you give me half, I will give you half of my government.' So, you said to him, 'You become half a man, I will stand him on the pulpit.' The followers of Ali should be like this. And being ignorant, illiterate, and having no interest in reading or religion, and just making claims—no, not claims. Many people make claims. And this is in the Hadith, and this is line one, there are hundreds of such Hadiths. There are hundreds of such traditions, and in them, it is written... [unclear/fragmented speech]... Anyway, let's come to the point of proving your argument. Whenever you prove your argument, if it is present in Al-Kafi, you know Sheikh Muhammad Yaqub—no, his name was not Muhammad Yaqub at all. Many people used to call him Yaqub, saying it was his father's name, and his father had written a book, and the son had written a book. The common man... our four books are thirty, and all three had the name Muhammad. All three were named Muhammad. The one who wrote Al-Kafi, the common man... Ali Muhammad Arif Hussain asked... [unclear]... wrote Al-Kafi, and the one who wrote the two books... so all three were named Muhammad, which is why they are called 'Muhammadan'. So, those three Muhammads wrote our four books. Regarding Al-Kafi, Sheikh Al-Kulayni (r.a.)—may Allah be pleased with him—in his book, in the introduction of his book 'Usul al-Kafi', wrote that my teacher... In the introduction, it is written that my teacher... [unclear]... such a great personality, we can submit to it. Understand this much and generate... we say what they used to do, which is from Al-Kafi... and if you do not do it from Al-Kafi, then it is... that is why I am saying that Al-Kafi is enough. Listen, Insha'Allah, very soon... [unclear]... a prayer was recited, just a prayer... and now... [unclear]... he says that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'Nawaqis al-Dihan' [unclear]... and from here, we also know... [unclear]... and that is why you will see that... [unclear]... I have set it aside for now, there is no time... and there will be progress, that they became enemies. How could you say that? How did people accept the 'Kafi' that you mention? We say 'Usul al-Kafi', and our branches—there are branches of others—are good, good, excellent. And among these, what is it? What is the main point? Tawhid—the correct belief in Tawhid. Second, Salah—prayer. For prayer, a person who claims to be a lover of Ali (a.s.) must pray. It is not possible that he is a lover of Ali (a.s.) and tells others about prayer, but does not pray himself. Ali and prayer—in all this, how will it be? Only this... and prayer. The third is Sawm—fasting. Fasting is... [unclear]... Sheikh Hassan Ali Isfahani, they call him 'Tehrani'. And they also call him 'Nakhudaki' because there is a village far from Mashhad called 'Nakhudak', where his grave is. And the grave of Nakhudaki, where was it? Where was the grave of Nakhudaki? In the Haram, in the door through which one enters, on the side, there was the grave of Sheikh Hassan Ali. But one night, he saw in a dream that he was telling the pilgrims, 'Remove my grave from here, take out all my body, take out my body, remove me from here.' Why? He was saying that people leave Imam Reza (a.s.) and sit by my grave, and they make vows to me. I do not like this filth. One pilgrim saw it, he thought it was his own dream. He went and told another pilgrim, 'I also saw it.' The third one said, 'I also saw it.' The fourth one said, 'I also saw it.' This is a very great personality, a very great personality, by Allah. Now, Sheikh Nakhudaki was a great scholar... it is not possible to tell you about his life in just one sitting. But about his life, it is written in his books that from the age of 17 to 1706... [unclear]... 17 years of age, and until 80 years of age, not a single one of his prayers was missed, and not a single... [unclear]... his fasting. What is 'Ayyam-e-Beed' fasting? 13th, 14th, 15th of every month... 13th, 14th, 15th of every month, and three months of fasting—Rajab, Sha'ban, and Ramadan. In Ramadan, he would fast the whole month, and he would fast on all the days of the 'Ayyam-e-Beed'. I am telling you about him... it was a cold winter night, and he came home and saw a man sitting there. He said, 'Come quickly, my brother has been bitten by a snake or a scorpion, please do something.' He had just been bitten. At that time, he was tired and exhausted at home, so he said, 'Put your hand in my pocket, take a date, and go, tell your brother to eat it.' He said, 'You eat it.' He said, 'I haven't been bitten, my brother has.' He said, 'Eat it, whatever I say, do it.' So he ate it. He said, 'Now go,' and his brother was perfectly fine. And I am telling you just one thing... [unclear]... their students were great scholars, not small ones. And it's not like they were running a shop... [unclear]... his daily routine was: fasting in Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, and the three months, and the 13th, 14th, 15th of every month. And his prayers... someone asked his mother, 'Why does your son never miss a prayer?' She said, 'When he was in my womb, I was very punctual with my prayers, and...' When he was in my womb, I was very punctual with my prayers, and after he was born, he would pray... when he was a small child, I would wake him up for prayer, I wouldn't let him sleep. I would make him pray. Then, as time passed, he became... even as a small child, he would pray. But after that, he became so accustomed to it that from the time he was conceived until the end, it was impossible for him to miss a prayer. And so many books have been written about him. And those who met him, they told some reasons. And they also say that when his students came to see him, and he had gone to some invitation, and they were sitting there for half an hour, waiting for him... so you can ask them without hesitation, 'What were the memories of Hassan Ali Tehrani?' What were the memories of Tehrani? So, some things are direct, he has written them in his books. But what answer should I give? Perhaps you know that I am a direct witness of Sheikh Ali, but Sheikh Ali says that the work you are doing is the best work. Being a 'Mulla', being someone who shows the path to people, is better than what he himself is doing. But who is this Hassan Ali Tehrani? You know, in Nakhudaki, he was a great scholar. He was very young, his age was 16-17, 18 years old at that time. And this was during the time of... [unclear]... of Imam Reza (a.s.). So, the pilgrims said to him—and his students are still present, there is a video of the students, it is still there on mobile, if anyone wants it, they can give it—they saw that Imam Reza (a.s.) was absolutely... in Muharram and Safar, he would give a lecture every morning after the morning prayer. And he said to a person in Nakhudaki, 'You recite the Masa'ib [tragedies] today.' So, Sheikh Nakhudaki was very young, but he went and recited the Masa'ib. You know, there is a custom among the Arabs that they read the Masa'ib by looking at a book, they read the Maqtal. So, this was the date of the tragedy, today's... or yesterday's... [unclear]... he said, 'Stop, stop.' And he threw away his book and started reciting from his heart. 'I am taking the tragedy of the one who came to that gathering in which he had given a message... a message to the brother... now...' In that gathering, in which... [unclear]... who is the one who is 786... [unclear]... peace be upon him. Who is the one who is 786? Peace be upon him. He says, 'I reached Medina on the day Imam Hussain (a.s.) left Medina, 28th Rajab. The whole of Medina was completely deserted. Everyone's face was pale, everyone was worried. I asked, 'What is the matter? Why are you all like this?' The traveler said, 'Don't you know that the grandson of the Prophet is leaving Medina?' He is leaving Medina. So I thought, I should also see how the people of Medina bid farewell to the grandson of the Prophet. And I went to the door of the house, and I stood outside the house. There was a crowd there. Why? Meanwhile, two young men came out of the house and said, 'Move away, move away! The daughters of the Prophet are coming out, the daughters of the Prophet are coming out! Move away!' So, I stepped back. Our eyes started... one by one, they started mounting. One mounted, I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the widow of Hassan (a.s.).' She mounted. And Qasim was mounting. She mounted. The second one came, I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is Umm Layla, and Ali Akbar, who is the son of Hussain (a.s.), the grandson of the Prophet.' He mounted. Then the third one... Then the third one came, and a young girl came out, she was like a shining moon. She mounted with great difficulty. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'She is the youngest daughter of Hussain (a.s.).' She mounted with great difficulty. Then, Hussain (a.s.) mounted. Just as he was mounting, what did I see? This is the personality... as soon as he came out, Imam Hussain (a.s.) stood up in his place. The young men of Banu Hashim surrounded him. Someone held the stirrup, someone held the reins, someone removed the curtain of the Howdah. Everyone helped him mount. I saw... [unclear]... hands were tied with ropes, and... [unclear]... which were not... [unclear]... in their hands, shackles... and in this state, they were being taken... [unclear]... O Allah, remove the difficulties of the troubled ones. O Lord of the Worlds, fulfill the needs of those who are distressed. O Lord, according to the status of our leader, remove the troubles of those who are suffering. May the people of this entire world be awakened, and in the hereafter, may we attain the intercession of Husayn (a.s.). Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas three times for the deceased... O Husayn, O Husayn, O Husayn. May the peace and blessings of Allah be upon you. O Husayn, O Husayn. O Husayn, O Husayn, O Husayn.

chapters.title: Salutations and Opening Prayers
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with traditional salutations to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his purified household, followed by prayers for spiritual guidance.

chapters.title: The Concept of Khair and Sharr
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the metaphysical struggle between good (Khair) and evil (Sharr), tracing this conflict back to the world of spirits.

chapters.title: The Army of Knowledge and Ignorance
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the symbolic armies of knowledge and ignorance, emphasizing the importance of correct belief and the role of divine leadership.

chapters.title: Divine Grace and the Concept of Tuba
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that goodness flows through those blessed by Allah and introduces Tuba as a symbol of the guardianship of Ali.

chapters.title: Divine Knowledge and Human Free Will
chapters.summary: This section discusses the theological balance between Allah's foreknowledge of human actions and the reality of human free will and responsibility.

chapters.title: The Responsibility of the Shia Identity
chapters.summary: The lecturer emphasizes that Shias must embody good deeds to uphold their identity and avoid bringing defamation upon the community.

chapters.title: Critical Thinking and Religious Teachings
chapters.summary: The speaker urges youth to critically evaluate information and prioritize the teachings of the Imams over personal logic or unverified sources.

chapters.title: Defining Good and Evil
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the true criterion for distinguishing good from evil is whether an action leads to Paradise or Hell, as defined by the Imams.

chapters.title: Parental Responsibility and Training
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes the importance of raising children with strict adherence to Islamic values, warning that failing to do so can lead to spiritual ruin.

chapters.title: Fulfilling Rights and Obligations
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines the three essential pillars of Islamic conduct: fulfilling duties toward Allah, respecting the rights of others, and maintaining the rights of one's own soul.

chapters.title: The True Meaning of Neighborly Conduct
chapters.summary: Being a good neighbor transcends not harming others; it involves patience, kindness, and forgiveness when mistreated, reflecting the true essence of Islamic character.

chapters.title: Knowledge as the Foundation of Good
chapters.summary: Imam Sadiq (a.s.) identifies knowledge as the source of all good and ignorance as the root of evil, making the pursuit of religious knowledge an obligatory duty for every believer.

chapters.title: The Legacy of Ali's Followers
chapters.summary: True followers of Imam Ali (a.s.) are characterized by their profound knowledge, eloquence, and dedication to faith, contrasting with those who merely make empty claims.

chapters.title: The Exemplary Life of Sheikh Nakhudaki
chapters.summary: The life of Sheikh Hassan Ali Nakhudaki serves as a model of piety, demonstrating the importance of consistent prayer, fasting, and humility in the pursuit of spiritual excellence.

chapters.title: Sheikh Hassan Ali Nakhudaki and Imam Reza
chapters.summary: The speaker shares anecdotes about the early life and spiritual devotion of Sheikh Hassan Ali Nakhudaki in the presence of Imam Reza.

chapters.title: The Departure of Imam Hussain from Medina
chapters.summary: A poignant account describing the emotional scene as Imam Hussain and his family depart from Medina on 28th Rajab.

chapters.title: Closing Supplications and Commemoration
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with prayers for the distressed and a collective recitation of salutations upon Imam Hussain.

title: Majlis #1: Shak (Doubt) | Ahle Bait (a.s.): Daawate Husnaa | Muharram 1443
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual and intellectual dangers of doubt (Shak) and its corrosive effect on faith and social cohesion. Drawing from the teachings of the Ahlulbayt, the speaker emphasizes the importance of certainty, reflection (Fikr), and the necessity of aligning one's life with divine guidance. The session concludes by contrasting the doubt-filled leadership of the era with the unwavering resolve of Imam Hussain (a.s.) in his stand against tyranny.

When he was walking on the road, he saw some people troubling a madman, some throwing stones, and others doing something else. He asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'He is a madman.' He said, 'Is this a madman? He is a patient, he is ill. A madman is one who is arrogant and proud.' He has no status; if his parents had wished, they would have ended his existence at that very moment. He has no status, he is 'najis' (impure), 'napak' (unclean), 'raees' (lowly)... He is lowly. What is his status? Where did his material existence come from? It came from there. And then he becomes arrogant. How many people will be humiliated? How many people in this world become unemployed? Today, we are caught up in problems like 'dharam' (religion) and debt. I didn't even mention that. This is the 'tashreeh' (explanation) being brought forward. And we were listening to the 'real magic'. That is why in this hadith, and in other hadiths, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Between the two, there is a 'nutfah' (drop) that is 'najis' (impure).' And after that, he shows arrogance? He shows pride? Who is he showing pride against? Being a 'najis' (impure) drop, and after that, this... this was also discussed last year, so we will not cover it in today's... We will not cover it in today's discussion. The next sentence is, 'I am amazed at the one who doubts the existence of Allah.' While he sees the signs of Allah all around him, he sees the faces of the four directions, and yet he doubts Allah. A very big, powerful, and strong argument was given. A person used to deny and doubt. So, he came to Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and argued with him. He asked him, 'Does He exist or not?' The Imam (a.s.) gave him 22 arguments, 22 proofs from his own 'nafs' (self), from his own soul, from his own mind. These 22 conditions of his 'nafs' were such that when he turned back, his friends asked him, 'What happened? You went to argue, but you look completely...', You look completely overwhelmed, confused, and astonished. What happened? He said, 'Muhammad (Imam Sadiq) gave me so many proofs that I felt as if Allah was between him and me.' He gave so many proofs. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'I am amazed at the one who doubts.' The word 'shakk' (doubt) appears 15 times in the Holy Quran. Allah has severely condemned it 15 times. Those who doubt are called 'shakk' (doubters). Allah has condemned them 15 times. And sometimes the Quran uses other words, like 'mushrik'. So, we read, 'Inna...'. What happens is that Allah has promised to keep all 'rijs' (filth) away from you. 'Rijs' means 'najasat' (impurity), 'gandagi' (filth), 'na-layak' (unworthy) things. Keep them away, not just remove them, but keep them away. The translation is 'keep away'. Keep away. Remember, the translation is 'keep away'. It is done after something comes, but 'keep away' means not letting it come near at all. Regarding this, the commentary says, and it is in 'Kafi', that Allah has kept the doubt of the 'shaitan' (Satan) away from you. The Imams (a.s.) never even doubt. Doubt is a disease that is kept away from them. That is why the Imam (a.s.) says, which you often hear, and they explain it, that if the veil were removed from before Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), his 'yaqeen' (certainty) would not increase. This is the reality. So, Allah has kept doubt away from them. And the second word used is 'zulm' (oppression), which, God willing, when the verse comes, we will discuss. So, first, understand the word 'shakk'. You have brought the topic of 'shakk', but as in today's lecture, the word 'shakk' appears 15 times in the Quran, and Allah has condemned it 15 times. And the second thing is that in the narrations, all our great enemies, whether you take... Whether you take the 'Sihah al-Sittah', or take 'Allah-badi', or take 'Tirmidhi', or take the books of the 'Ammah' (Sunni scholars), all the great books have written a lot about doubt. Everyone has written a full chapter on doubt in their books. And the Imam (a.s.) has questioned it. Let me give you a reference. In 'Usul al-Kafi', in 'Usul al-Kafi', if you open it carefully, there is a chapter on 'shakk'. And it explains that it leads to 'kufr' (disbelief). In the book of 'Kufr and Iman', the second volume, it discusses the foundation of 'shakk'. Now, pay attention. The first thing is that there are two types of things. You discuss one, a 'drop'... the 'waswasa' (whispering) of the 'shaitan' is needed. So, when arrogance enters the 'shaitani' mind, the 'shaitan' comes. People think doubt is always a work of the mind; it is not like that. It is not necessary. Sometimes it happens that... It is not necessary. Sometimes it happens that a brother, sister, mother, son, daughter, or wife plays a big role in creating doubt. 'This happened, so-and-so must have done it,' or 'Your brother must have done it.' Immediately, a seed of doubt is sown about the brother. Now, when a person's 'zimmadari' (responsibility) begins, it is not that if someone creates doubt, if someone is spreading doubt, then the person is not responsible for the doubt created by others. He is not responsible. Now, his responsibility begins here; this is very important to understand. The responsibility begins from the point of how he treats that doubt. As soon as someone creates doubt, say, 'Brother, go and investigate, do the work.' Its product is to send them to the 'haqq' (truth). Remove the doubt. Immediately, entertain it? Should he go and ask him, 'Did you see it with your own eyes?' On the basis of 'zann' (conjecture), on the basis of 'shakk' (doubt), on the basis of 'conjecture', you are creating such a situation that brothers are fighting brothers, fathers are fighting sons, husbands and wives are fighting. This is 'haram' (forbidden). The one who does this, his state is not... the 'shaitan' will be judged by Allah, but we are the ones who entertain it. Therefore, look, why is this in the light of this discussion? Now, what does the Imam (a.s.) say? What is the beauty? This is 'Ilm' (knowledge). This is how the Imam (a.s.) speaks. What is the 'final goal'? The 'final goal' is the 'aql' (intellect) that resides in the human existence. And when the Imams (a.s.) give teachings, they bring out what is inside. This is the proof that Allah sent the Prophets (a.s.) for the 'final goal'. To bring out what is inside. When they explain the purpose of sending the Prophets (a.s.), they themselves start crying. A question arises: why did Allah send the Prophets (a.s.)? To remove the 'physical' obstacles, to keep them far away. If they say it is bad, then accept it. So that the 'hujjah' (proof) is completed. To convey the message and complete the 'hujjah'. To convey the message and complete the 'hujjah', so that no one can say, 'We did not know, we did not understand, we were good.' And then the Imam (a.s.) says, 'The final goal is to bring out what is inside the human existence.' Now, understand this point. This 'bringing out' has a connection with 'taharat' (purity). The more a person is away from 'tamas' (impurities), the more he will understand the words of the Imams (a.s.). The more he stays away from 'tamas', the more he will not understand the words of the Imams (a.s.). And this is the reason why, if you ask any 'aqil' (wise) person, 'Should the 'aql' (intellect) be given the material, or should the material be given to the 'aql'?' This is a foolish question. The 'aql' should be given the material, not the material given to the 'aql'. But those who have moved away from the 'aql', they have written in their books—all history is for Allah—that they gave preference to the 'inferior' over the 'superior'. He gave preference to the superior, or rather, he gave preference to the one who was forced. Now, when Ali (a.s.) was the superior officer, everyone else was far behind him, but it was the grace of Allah that he (the person mentioned) performed better than even a child would. I am attributing this to Allah. You see, what is being said? What is the mountain of doubt? Brother, doubt is something that has forty aspects—perhaps forty branches. There are four aspects to it. The first one is: to what extent do we argue? To be stubborn and argue when someone is debating something and not using their intellect, then understand that there is doubt in their heart. And when doubt sits in the heart, its cure is not with Luqman the Wise. They were discussing how to extract this from the Quran. Why is it important? Because this is the very thing that breaks good relationships—it breaks the relationship between husband and wife, breaks the relationship between brothers, breaks the relationship between father and son. Imam (a.s.) says: 'Tamari' (stubbornness)—this person does not adopt a balanced approach; this is not right. And the second thing is 'Hawn'... This is not right. And the second thing is 'Hawn'. 'Hawn' means being hesitant or having a suspicious nature. How does he say it? That one remains in doubt because of 'Hawn', so he doubts whether a thing is right or not. And what is the third thing? 'Taraddud' (indecision) regarding something. Many people are like this; they have doubts about their prayers or how much water to use (for wudu), and they get worried. At home, there are arguments. We know such people who keep repeating their prayers. When a person is in the second or third rak'ah, they get confused. This is what is called 'Tashweesh' (confusion). The one who is confused does not have a balanced doubt; he cannot decide. He keeps repeating the prayer. This is a sickness. Its cure is to let a child continue, let it go, it's fine. But when this thing enters relationships, when we start doubting our friends, our wives, our... Our friends, our wives, our parents, our brothers and sisters—we doubt everyone and look at everyone with suspicion. That is where relationships are ruined. And because one of the important reasons for the coming of Islam, for the coming of the religion, is to build bonds, and doubt breaks those bonds. Islam is so against this that in any situation, look at this bond—let me give you an example. This is how Islam is against it. Let's take the example of a husband and wife. How was the bond between the husband and wife? Pharaoh said, 'I am your Lord, the Most High.' And where was Pharaoh's wife? She was Asiya (a.s.). When the time came, among the women of Paradise, there is also this woman. Think about it: did Lady Asiya (a.s.) get permission to leave Pharaoh? She did not. So, this is a message being given intentionally—that sometimes it may happen that a woman becomes a 'Pharaoh'... Sometimes a woman becomes a 'Pharaoh', but the husband is not necessarily a 'Pharaoh'. So, should I leave my husband? The scholars of Islam say no. We are not followers of a religion where relationships break so easily. If you ask any scholar, they will give the same answer: 'No, stay with your husband, and stay with your wife, and present such character that they themselves will say, 'How did you become so good?'' The Imam (a.s.) says that 'Tashweesh' is a disease, and Islam emphasizes character so much. Here, this is not allowed, which is allowed by others. So, this bonding is a very important thing. Then the Imam (a.s.) mentions 'Taraddud' and the fourth thing he mentions is 'Al-Istislam' (submission). By 'Istislam', he means bowing down to everything, accepting everything that comes. The person who accepts everything will always be a victim of doubt. Then the Imam (a.s.) says about this—his words are strange: 'The person who accepts everything as it is...' The person who accepts business or these matters and keeps doing the work, if he makes that his life, his way of living, then his morning will never come. He will always remain in darkness and shadow; his morning will never come. And then he says, 'Al-Hawf' (fear). The person who is afraid of everything, who is ready to flee from everything—he will be ready to flee from everything. Let me give you an example. I mentioned a name before, but because I don't remember it well, let me just say 'Ibn Abi al-Awja'. He was a very big skeptic. We have this story—he used to be afraid of debating. He used to find something in every debate that would make him come to the Imam (a.s.)... I am speaking fast because the lecture is a bit long, but I will summarize it. Ibn Abi al-Awja was a leader of the skeptics. Why was he a skeptic? He used to ask... He used to ask specific questions, but he couldn't answer anything. The next day he would come prepared again. He would say, 'The one who is in the school, the one who passes the school, this is his condition.' Look at how Satan deceives him. And this is his 'Hawf' (fear). But anyway, the Imam (a.s.) already knew that he would give this answer. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Okay, stand there.' He asked him, 'Tell me one thing, in your school, in the insects and creatures that are there, tell me how many are male and how many are female?' He couldn't answer. He was a pathological skeptic. He didn't have any logic, but people used to support him. But anyway, this Ibn Abi al-Awja was a Muslim before. When he was asked why he became a skeptic, he said, 'My teacher taught me.' His teacher was Hasan al-Basri, who... His teacher was Hasan al-Basri, whom some Muslims respect a lot. There is a very famous incident about him in the books. He said, 'I am a skeptic because of him.' So, look, he is wandering around, sometimes he says this, sometimes he says that. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'I don't understand, if he is there, then what is he? If he is not there, then what is he?' So, if this is the condition of my teacher, then what is the point of following him? The governor had given him a name, he had made a name for himself. When he met the Imam (a.s.) in Basra, and the Imam (a.s.) was giving a sermon, he started writing. The Imam (a.s.) stopped him. No one stopped the others, but the Imam (a.s.) knew what he was doing. He knew what he was writing. He said, 'This is my logic, this is my theory, this is my idea.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Stop writing. What you are doing is the 'Samiri' of this Ummah.' This is the 'Samiri' of the Ummah, the one who... This is the 'Samiri' of the Ummah. The one who... when the time for confrontation came, he came to the Imam (a.s.) and said, 'I am with you, I am with you.' But then suddenly he started running away. He was ready to flee. Why was he running? He said, 'I heard you reciting the Kalima, so I am running away.' He ran away. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'He is the Samiri of this Ummah.' He ran away out of fear. The point here is that whoever is always in a state of 'Hawf' (fear) will always be ready to flee from everything. When there is a confrontation, one should face it. Whatever is in front of you, you should face it. And after that, we come to 'Tashweesh' and 'Taraddud'. Then, whoever always doubts something, if he remains in doubt, the Imam (a.s.) will crush him with his logic. And finally, the one who submits to everything will ruin his hereafter and his world... And will ruin his world too. So, these are the four things. The first thing is 'Tamari' (stubbornness) in arguing. The second thing is 'Hawn' (hesitation/suspicion)—not being able to decide on something, being indecisive. One should decide in the heart, 'We will do this.' This thing—should it be done or not? And the fourth thing is 'Istislam' (submission)—to bow down before everything. Whatever comes in front, one should not just submit. One should not be like that. Today, I cannot cover the whole topic as I am speaking very fast, otherwise, I would have explained it. Understand that we usually submit to everything. Someone says something, and we submit. But it shouldn't be like that. We should remain firm on our own principles. Don't try to please everyone. The one who tries to please everyone cannot be a 'Mumin' (believer). He cannot be a 'Mumin'. A 'Mumin' is like the one who, when the Amir (a.s.) sent him a message, 'Go and tell these people that if they still sit and fight, we will crush them.' He used a very harsh tone for the one he sent... So, do your work, let me do my work. This is called 'Shuja'at' (courage). Look, the Imam (a.s.) is very firm, but we usually submit to pressure. So, this was an important thing. In this, the Imam (a.s.) meant that the small hadiths are 'Ghurar al-Hikam'. Every year, we introduce this book so that people read it. This is a small book that contains small hadiths. The Imam (a.s.) calls them 'short sayings', like short sentences. Like the 10,000 hadiths that were collected, he knew that these hadiths... 10,764. Now you will ask, did the Imam (a.s.) collect them? No, Sayyid Razi collected only those things that, according to him, were close to literature. Only those things that could be considered literature were collected. And all the hadiths were collected. Small hadiths, especially this book's name is 'Ghurar al-Hikam'. 'Ghurar' means the best of things. So, in this, look, the foundation of doubt is what is called the first basic cause: 'Hawn'. If you look at the situation, how much distraction is there in it? It will go red now. How big a thing is it? Wherever the situation is, whatever the condition is, therefore, if you always want to fight against doubt, then make that society, that family, educated, make them 'Aalim' (knowledgeable), and make them 'Aalim-e-Rabbani'. Now, I am not just talking about 'Aalim' here, but 'Aalim-e-Rabbani' along with the page. If they are like this and their birth is like this, then they will understand. The first thing is that we should not argue. The thing that is not good, do not even talk about it. Always remain silent. If someone starts a discussion here, creates a space, even if we don't know about the court or the rocket, we will definitely give our opinion on it, we will definitely comment. Silence is better. The second thing is, if there is 'Jameel' (beauty/grace), there will be no noise. It will be because you will not be there. Therefore, you know that whatever happens, it brings benefit or loss. It is not in the hands of a human to cause harm. Whatever is written in destiny will be received; what is not, will not be received. So, there will be no loss, there will be no fault of anyone. Just fear Allah with 'Taqwa' (piety), just fear. Just fear Allah with 'Taqwa'. Whatever is ahead of the people, and for anyone... and the third thing is 'Taraddud' (hesitation/doubt). What will he do? He will consult in 'Bait-ul-Mal'. Why? Because he has stopped the 'Warsa' (inheritance) and 'Ilzam' (accusation). Look, the Quran is here. This Quran has gone. 'Fashawirhum fil-amr' (consult them in the matter). In every matter, consult people. 'Fa-idha azamta fatawakkal 'ala Allah' (and when you have decided, then rely upon Allah). So, rely upon Allah. Because no one knows the outcome as well as He does. This is the outcome. If he stays in jail, if he is in business, then in any matter, he can tell, 'Brother, don't do this.' No, there is no need for that. Consult and do it. In our village, we don't understand, okay. Once a decision is made, then rely on Allah. And the last thing is 'Tasleem' (submission). He will submit before someone. He will submit before Allah, before the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), before the Messenger of Allah, and he will submit before the 'Wali'. He will not submit before anyone else. He will be... if he is in this, then Allah tells the second day, there is no second way. Doubt: when a person disobeys the command of Allah, when he starts to disobey Allah, then different kinds of doubts arise in his heart. Why? What is the reason? And look, what a tremendous... who is this? And look, what a tremendous... who is this? He is 'Masoom' (infallible). What a flower he brought out at night. Tremendous. Whoever disobeys Allah, whoever disobeys Allah, he will be a victim of doubt. Why? When he is disobeying Allah, he is naturally giving himself into the hands of Satan. He should also understand this. Why? Because when he is disobeying, he will naturally go into the hands of Satan. When Satan... Satan will constantly influence him. When Satan whispers, he will become a victim of Satan. Then Satan will play with him until his world is ruined and his hereafter is ruined. But what is the matter? To be honest, on one thing, after this, he will be occupied with wrong matters. He will not be able to see anything in front of him. He is not using himself. 'Mind it'. One way to remove this doubt is to use yourself, 'Fikr' (reflection). Through 'Fikr', remove the doubt. Look, these are the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). All these things that our scholars have tolerated, collected the narrations, brought them to one place, when the narration was... they compiled it, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his family. And his family. I am doing a very great task. When you use the 'Fikr' before the 'Daud' (call), it will be the result. The doubt is that when you are active, you are planting the seeds of doubt in your own existence. Why? You have to understand something. The thing in front of you is simple. It is according to your... it is 'Mukhlis' (sincere). You don't get angry. Focus and do it. Then they do 'Fikr'. This is called 'Fikr'. When you are focused on something, it is called 'Fikr'. When you focus, like this carpet, we look at this carpet. It is understood that what is in this carpet? This is called 'Fikr'. This carpet is a good thing, a bad thing... the result is, if it is good, then it is a place to sit, a good thing. This is called 'Anzur'. But if the 'Harf' (letter) changes here, then the meaning changes. If the 'Harf' changes, its name changes. And 'Waras' is 'Dhur-hil', if it has such a mistake, then 'Dhur' goes away. Now what has this carpet become? It is a place to sit, a good thing. So, it is not bad, it is a good thing to sit. Here, the 'Aql' (intellect) is, you are the light of these eyes. We reflect more on this, we research. We reflect more on this, we research. About this carpet, there are black marks. Where is this carpet made? What is it? How is it? Whatever the world is, depending on what the industry is, fill it. So, this is called 'Fikr'. So, when you reflect on anything, it is called 'Fikr'. And 'Fikr' means to go deep. And 'Fikr' is an Arabic word. Go deep into anything. And especially, I tell the youngsters that you should go into the depth of any subject. If you go into the dictionary, it starts from 'Fikr'. If you don't go into the depth, you will not be able to understand that thing well, and you will not get success in it. That is why the PhD process continues, why does he do a PhD? To go into the depth. Anyway, now you see, people doubt about the Quran. Today, no, the narrations in the books of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) get relief. So, so many books, 'Tawheed' (monotheism), this book is 'Tawheed'. So, this whole book is on the subject of 'Tawheed'. Almost 400 pages, the Quranic pages. In it, one narration, one page, a man came to the Imam (a.s.) and said, 'O Amir, I have doubt in my heart.' And said, 'O Amir, I have doubt in my heart.' So, the book was received by the Imam (a.s.) that, 'O Amir, I have doubt about the verses.' What is the doubt? He should have said, 'This verse is not in my understanding, explain it.' And everything is very old. Now we are telling it clearly. His doubt is that its verses contradict each other. The verses of the Quran contradict each other. They are against each other. Therefore, there is a conflict. If you see a contradiction in the Quran, it is not from Allah. This is the Quran. 'Afala yatadabbarunal Qur'an' (Do they not reflect upon the Quran?). If they reflect on it, there are many benefits in it. If it were from anyone other than Allah, there would be many... if it were not from the Quran, it means there is no contradiction in it. Now, this verse was not understood. And he reached the point that the Quran is like this. Mawla (a.s.) said, 'Satarhamuha' (You will understand it). Satarhamuha. Yes, your mother is sitting in mourning for you. My 'Satarhamuha'... and he received the book, 'How did he start doubting?' Then he explained to him, 'This is your face, I will see.' Mawla (a.s.) said, 'Walakinna... you do not have the 'Aql' (intellect) to take advantage of it. You don't have it. If you had it, this matter would be understood.' So, the basic thing is that he had to go to the Masoom (a.s.) himself, that 'I am not understanding this.' And then after that, he should have doubted. And we see this thing ourselves. Anyway, it is clear from this that the condemnation of doubt in the Holy Quran, and the doubt that has come from Allah, is for doubt. Anyway, this is one type of doubt, and the other place is 'Qarar diya hai'. Like this, 'Wassas' (whispers). They say that 'Sallu...' when I asked about it, that Allah is praising... Praising, that He is praising some people. He is praising the 'Sahiban-e-Iman' (people of faith). Those who believed and did not mix their faith with 'Zulm' (injustice/wrongdoing) and spoiled it. They did not mix their faith with 'Zulm'. 'Falam yalbisoo imanahum bi-zulm' (and did not mix their faith with injustice). So, the companions asked, 'What is the 'Zulm'?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'They spoiled their faith by doubting.' Not 'Shirk' (polytheism), not any other oppression. So, remove this disease from your existence. Faith... the Imam (a.s.) said, 'I will do it.' And what is it? That 'Rabbi arini kayfa tuhyil mawta' (My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead). Ibrahim (a.s.) said, 'How do You give life?' So, Allah said, 'Do you not believe?' Ibrahim (a.s.) said, 'I believe, but...' I believe, but... Ibrahim (a.s.) replied, 'Bala, walakin liyatma'inna qalbi' (Yes, but so that my heart may be at rest). So, he only has a little bit, not complete. Like Ibrahim (a.s.) said, 'That is how it is, I want my heart to be at rest.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.) had faith, but he wanted to increase his faith, he wanted to increase the certainty of it. But your problem is that you are not at the level of faith, you are at the level of doubt.' And here, the great meaning is that whoever has doubt in his heart, this whole gathering, the summary of this is, look, whoever has doubt in his heart, then there is no 'Khair' (good) in it. [Music] It is possible that he is outwardly a believer, but with doubt, the matter has come. It is possible that he is praying, but praying with doubt. He is relying on Allah, but with doubt. He is always... outwardly, but the 'Hadaf' (goal) on which his 'Peecha' (pursuit) is, it is not with certainty. It is not with certainty. If someone says something else, then he says, 'Maybe something is right, right?' The doubt... Mawla (a.s.) says, 'Ma shakaktu mundhu ra'aytu al-haqq' (I have not doubted since I saw the truth). Mawla (a.s.) says, 'Allah showed Himself, and from that day until today, I have never doubted Allah.' What a great word! And then, just the last thing, that whoever doubts, his 'A'mal' (deeds) will be rejected. Allah will not accept any of his deeds. This is a Hadith. And we have... the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have... it is that whoever doubts, Allah will not accept any of his deeds. His 'A'mal' are... his special thing is that keep doubt away. 'A'mal' are... well, as I said, from the whispers of Satan, humans don't have control, but here, the main thing is 'A'mal'. And then, the last stage, the family in this, and this family... very tremendous, they used to worship Allah. This, when... He used to worship Allah tremendously. When you use this term in Hadith, you need to understand the language. Just as it was used in Bani Israel, it meant that he would pray all year round, fast all year round, and even manage Tahajjud prayers during the day. How can we claim to be like that? There was a whole family that was pious. Whenever any member of that family made a supplication, it would be answered. They would destroy the roots of the wicked and bring the oppressors to justice. People came to him and said, 'Brother, please pray for us.' The person who came was from that same family and he prayed, but his prayer was not answered. People complained to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about this, saying, 'O Prophet of Allah, you know him, he is a pious man, why is his prayer not being answered?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked Allah, 'O Lord, what is the matter? Why are his prayers not being answered?' Allah replied, 'O My Prophet, the person who was praying was doubting Me. If someone comes to Me and talks to Me, but in his heart, there is even a grain of doubt about My power, then I will not accept that prayer.' How can it be otherwise? How can it happen? There are so many people who, even in the presence of the Imam, doubt him, calling him a liar or a deceiver. And that is why their prayers are not answered. Remove the doubt from my heart so that he may pray again. He prayed again, and after that, it was as it was before—his prayers were answered. This was the whole story, the whole revelation regarding this question. But regarding the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), there are two types of people. One group is clear to everyone, but the Hadith says—this is a Hadith—'After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), all the people turned back (irtidad).' 'Irtidad' means to turn back or deviate. They turned away from the religion because of this doubt. And because everyone in Medina had pledged allegiance at the hands of Ali (a.s.), they used to say, 'Brother, I have pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, and Ali (a.s.) is the successor.' Why not him? Why not that one? All these questions, which exist even today, this disease developed slowly. How did it develop? When the Caliphate was taken away from Ali (a.s.), the Muslims should have stood up. Instead, the Muslims went to war. In the Battle of Siffin, more than 30,000 people were killed. And after that, the Battle of Nahrawan happened. And this continued. What was the reason? It was the same doubt, the same suspicion in their hearts. Those who had certainty were very few—three, four, five, or six. At most, the maximum number mentioned is sixteen. Only sixteen people had true certainty in Ali (a.s.). We listen to this, and it sounds very easy. We listen to this, and it sounds very easy, but the reality is the same. This doubt and hesitation kept growing to the extent that what was done to Ali (a.s.) was done, and then what happened to the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) family. After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) passed away, when Muawiyah started his rule, he began his tyranny. But when he made Yazid his successor, you know what happened. And then, a message was sent to Imam Hussain (a.s.) that he was wanted. He was called to the court at night. Imam Hussain (a.s.) told Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.), 'Sister, I am going to the court.' Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.) asked, 'Brother, why is the court being decorated at night? Has the Caliph passed away? That is why I have been called, and I know what he wants from me.' That is why I have been called, and I know what he wants from me. Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.) understood and said, 'Brother, you are not going alone.' She turned to Janab-e-Abbas (a.s.) and said, 'Brother Abbas, take the youth of Bani Hashim with you and go to the court.' It is written in the Maqtal that Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) took thirty youths of Bani Hashim. These thirty youths surrounded Imam Hussain (a.s.). When they reached the door of the palace, the Imam said, 'You stay here; it is not appropriate for you to enter. But if you hear my voice, come inside immediately.' The Imam entered and was given the news of Muawiyah's death. According to Islamic tradition, the Imam recited 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un'. The governor said, 'O Hussain, you know that Yazid has become the Caliph. I suggest you pledge allegiance to him.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) replied, 'These are very important matters; they are not decided in the darkness of the night in such isolation.' These are very important matters; they are not decided in the darkness of the night in such isolation. Call the Muslims; I will also come. Everyone will gather, and then it will be decided who will pledge allegiance and to whom. The governor said, 'Yazid insists that you pledge allegiance, and if you don't, I will be forced to take it.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) replied, 'If you want to hear my decision, then listen: We are the household of Prophethood, the source of the Message, and the place where angels descend.' The Imam then said, 'And Yazid is a corrupt, sinful, and immoral person. A person like me can never pledge allegiance to a person like him.' As the Imam started to leave, Marwan said, 'Stop Hussain, otherwise he will not let you leave alive until rivers of blood flow in Medina.' Just as Marwan said this... Just as Marwan said this, remember, the son of Fatima (s.a.) became enraged. 'Are you threatening me with death? Do you know who you are talking to? Do you think you can force me to pledge allegiance?' As soon as the Imam's voice was raised, Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) and the youths of Bani Hashim entered, hands on the hilts of their swords, and said, 'Who dared to be disrespectful? Who dared to raise their voice? If anyone moves, I will not leave anyone alive.' May Allah protect the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the believers wherever they are in this world. May He protect the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). May He grant us the intercession of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) in this world and the hereafter. May He bless us with the love of Ali (a.s.) and the followers of Hussain (a.s.).

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Par Aansu Bahaana Momin Ki Pehchaan Hai | Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual connection between a believer and Imam Hussain (a.s.), emphasizing that shedding tears for him is a core identity of the faithful. It references a narration from Imam Ali (a.s.) identifying Imam Hussain as the 'tear of every believer' and highlights the Imam's own words regarding the inevitability of weeping upon remembering his sacrifice. The discourse underscores the deep emotional and theological bond that defines the Shia mourning tradition during Muharram.
content:
Shedding tears for Imam Hussain (a.s.) is the identity of a believer. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) narrates that Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (a.s.) once looked at his son Imam Hussain (a.s.) and said, 'O tear of every believer.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) asked, 'Is it me, O father?' The Mawla replied, 'Yes, my son.' From this Hadith of the Mawla, one realizes why every believer cries so much at the mention of Sayyid al-Shuhada (a.s.) and his tragedies. Sayyid al-Shuhada (a.s.) himself said, 'I am the one who was killed in a state of weeping. No believer remembers me except that he sheds tears for me.' Eyes will long to weep for themselves; when your name is mentioned, they will pour forth. O oppressed Hussain!

title: Zuhoor Ki Alaamatein Momineen Ke Liye Imtehaan Hain
excerpt: This lecture discusses the nature of the signs preceding the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (atfs). It emphasizes that these signs are intended as a spiritual test for believers rather than a fixed timeline for the event. The speaker encourages maintaining unwavering faith in the truthfulness of Allah and His Messenger, regardless of whether specific signs manifest as expected.
content:
Do not fix a specific time for the reappearance (Zuhur). But when we describe a sign to you, if it happens exactly as we said, then say 'Sadaqallahu wa Rasooluhu' (Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth). And if that sign does not occur, still say 'Sadaqallahu wa Rasooluhu'. This serves as a test; when a sign does not occur, do we still maintain our belief in the Imam's words or not? If we do, you will be rewarded twice over. The wisdom behind describing signs is to test the hearts of the believers. Peace.
