Is there any religion visible in the world that prevails over all others? And specifically, that Mahdi's religion should be dominant. But nothing of the sort is visible. So, how can they call themselves the Mahdi? And the final point is, no matter how much they claim their religion is the religion of truth and call themselves the Mahdi, the simple fact is that, let alone all the religions of the world, they cannot even bring life to the 'death' in their own neighborhood. They cannot fill their own neighborhood with justice and fairness. Even if they claim they will fill the world, if there are four religions in their own neighborhood, their religion is not even prevailing over those. The talk of all the world's religions is far off. Viewers, the mention of the twelve Mahdis has been presented to you. Now, let us see in this narration who these twelve Mahdis are. This narration is being reported by Sama'a ibn Mehran, who himself states that he, Abu Basir, and Muhammad ibn Imran—who was a slave of Imam Baqir (a.s.)—were present in a house in Mecca. Muhammad ibn Imran states there that he himself heard Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) saying: 'Nahnu ithna ashara Mahdiyyan' (We are the twelve Mahdis). Upon this, Abu Basir, who was present in that house, said: 'Wallahi laqad sami'tu dhalika min Abi Abdillah alayhis salam' (By Allah, I have also heard this from Abu Abdillah, meaning Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.)). And then, not once, but twice, Abu Basir swore that he had heard this from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). And then Abu Basir says that he has not only heard this Hadith from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), but he has also heard it from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.). So, viewers, the conclusion is that these Hadith were stated not just by one Imam, but by two—Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) and Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.). They stated in clear words: 'We are the twelve Mahdis.' And the second conclusion is that whoever claims to be the Mahdi must be from this list of twelve. If someone is not from this list of twelve, it becomes clear that they are a false claimant and not the true Mahdi. Continuing the discussion on the twelve Mahdis (a.s.), let us look at another Hadith in which Imam Sadiq (a.s.) has made it even clearer that if there are twelve Mahdis, they are from us. Let us look at this Hadith in which Abu Basir narrates from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), who says: 'Sami'tuhu yaqulu minna ithna ashara Mahdiyyan' (Twelve Mahdis are from us). The Imam has emphasized that the twelve Mahdis will be from us. And then the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Mada sittatun wa baqiya sittatun' (Six have passed and six remain). 'Yasna'ullahu bis-sadisi ma ahabba' (Allah will do with the sixth what He wills). And among them, the sixth—meaning Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.)—Allah will do with him what He wills. Meaning, if Allah wants to grant him a long life, He will; if Allah wants to keep him in occultation, He will. Allah will do what He wills with him. The summary of this Hadith is that the Imam (a.s.) says these twelve Mahdis will be from us, the Ahlulbayt. Anyone outside this blessed lineage cannot be in this list of Mahdis. They will only be from the twelve successors of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). And if anyone in this era claims to be the Mahdi of this time, they must be the sixth from the progeny of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). They must be from the Imam's progeny. So, let us see if those who are claiming today to be the present Imam, to be from the Ahlulbayt, and to be the Mahdi of this time—are they from the progeny of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) or not? And if they claim to be, are they from his sixth generation or not? And if they cannot prove that they are from the Imam's progeny, then that person is a liar. Respected viewers, the Hadith we are going to look at now is the one whose misuse has led many false claimants to falsely claim to be the Mahdi, and they continue to do so to this day. Which Hadith is it? They bring the will (Wasiyyah) of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) for their claim, in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said there would be twelve Imams after him and then twelve Mahdis. They use this phrase for their claim—that twelve Mahdis will come after the twelve Imams. So, let us look at this Hadith and examine that very will to see what is actually stated in it. The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) will was narrated by Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Meaning, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) narrates it from his father, Imam Baqir (a.s.), who from Hazrat Imam Zainul Abidin (a.s.), who from his father Hazrat Imam Hussain (a.s.), Sayyidush Shuhada (a.s.), who from his father Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), saying that on the night the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) closed his eyes and departed from this world, the night his martyrdom occurred, what did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) do that night? The Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) says that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to me, 'Ya Aba al-Hasan, ahdir sahifatan wa dawatan' (O Abu al-Hasan, O Ali, bring me paper and a pen). Those who were asked initially did not provide it, but the Prophet received the paper and pen. From whom? From his true successor. This is one way to identify who the Imam is after the Prophet; whoever provided the paper and pen is the first Imam after the Prophet. Amir al-Mu'minin provided the paper and pen, and he says that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) dictated the will to him. I wrote that will until we reached the point where the Prophet said to me, 'Ya Aliyyu innahu sayakunu ba'di ithna 'ashara imaman' (O Ali, after me there will be twelve Imams), 'wa min ba'dihimu ithna 'ashara mahdiyyan' (and after them, after that sequence of twelve, there will be twelve Mahdis). That is, first twelve Imams will come, then twelve Mahdis will come. Taking advantage of this phrase, many people claim that these twelve Mahdis are not among the twelve Imams, but rather they have started a separate sequence of Mahdis. But the clarification follows; they present only that much, but do not state the subsequent part. What does the Prophet say next? He stated up to this point that after me there will be twelve Imams, and after them, twelve Mahdis. 'Fa-anta ya Aliyyu awwalu al-ithnay 'ashara imaman' (But you, O Ali, are the first of those twelve Imams). 'Sammaka Allahu ta'ala fi sama'ihi Aliyyan al-Murtada' (Allah the Almighty has named you Ali al-Murtada in His heavens). 'Wa Amira al-Mu'minin' (You are also Amir al-Mu'minin). 'Wa al-Siddiq al-Akbar wa al-Faruq al-A'zam' (You are the Siddiq al-Akbar in Allah's heavens, you are the Faruq al-A'zam). 'Wa al-Ma'mun' (And al-Ma'mun—here it is a title for Amir al-Mu'minin, meaning the source of peace and security who will grant peace to the people; who is he? Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)). You are Amir al-Mu'minin, you are Siddiq al-Akbar, you are Faruq al-A'zam, you are the Ma'mun who grants peace to people, 'wa al-Mahdiyyu' (and you are the Mahdi). That is, among the twelve Imams, the first is Ali (a.s.), and if a sequence of twelve Mahdis is started separately after the twelve Imams, then the first of those twelve Mahdis is also Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). So, whoever is trying to take advantage of this hadith to claim that they are the first of the twelve Mahdis, they are essentially claiming to be Ali ibn Abi Talib. You can easily catch their lie with this point: whoever claims to be the first of the twelve Mahdis is claiming to be Amir al-Mu'minin. And why is their claim false? Because the Prophet, in this very hadith, immediately says, 'Fala tasihhu hadhihi al-asma'u li-ahadin ghayrika' (These names are not valid for anyone other than you). So, if anyone other than you is calling themselves the first Mahdi, they are a liar; they are wrong. Because you are the first Imam and you are also the first Mahdi. 'Ya Aliyyu anta wasiyyi 'ala ahli bayti' (O Ali, you are my successor over my Ahl al-Bayt), 'hayyihim wa mayyitihim' (over those who are alive among them and those who have passed away, you are my successor), 'wa 'ala nisa'i' (and over my wives, you are my successor). 'Faman sabbatha laqiyatni ghadan' (Whoever among my wives accepts your Imamate will meet me tomorrow, i.e., on the Day of Judgment). And 'wa man tallaqatha' (whomever you divorce on my behalf, I give you the right, whoever you divorce), 'fa-ana bari'un minha' (I disassociate myself from her). Meaning, the Prophet has disassociated (tabarra) from that wife whom Ali divorces on the Prophet's behalf. 'Lam tarani wa lam araha fi 'arsati al-qiyamati' (Neither will she see me, nor will I see her in the arena of Resurrection). That is, that wife who rejected the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) will not even be granted the sight of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). 'Wa anta khalifati 'ala ummati min ba'di' (And you will be my Caliph over my Ummah after me). The hadith is very clear; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explicitly stated that the twelve Imams are the same as the twelve Mahdis. And the sequence of the twelve Imams begins with Ali (a.s.), so the sequence of the twelve Mahdis also begins with Ali (a.s.). Many people here say, 'No, these twelve Mahdis are those of the Raj'ah (Return), a new sequence.' So, it is necessary to pause here and address this. If anyone makes this claim, you can easily refute it. And what is that point? If someone says, 'No, this is the sequence of Raj'ah, the sequence of everyone returning,' and that this is the first Mahdi among the twelve Mahdis, meaning the Raj'ah has begun—how do you catch their lie? It is that in the belief of Raj'ah, the way the Imams (a.s.) return, there are no new Imams coming. It is the same twelve Imams who will return. Their Raj'ah, meaning their return. So those who have passed will return. There will be no new sequence of Imamate in Raj'ah. It is very important to keep this in mind. So if someone uses Raj'ah as a reference to make this claim, their lie can be easily caught. In summary, if someone claims to be the Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.), do one thing: keep a few basic questions ready. If you ask them, based on their response, you can immediately catch their lie. First, ask them, 'What is your father's name? What is your mother's name?' Ask for their parents' names. If they give names other than the parents of the Imam-e-Zamana, they are wrong. Then, the most important thing: 'Where were you born?' The birth of the Imam-e-Zamana took place in Samarra. He did not come from Basra, he did not come from Yemen, he did not come from Canada, the US, or London. If they are from anywhere in the world other than Samarra, they are not the Imam-e-Zamana. Third, the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is well-versed in the Sharia. Ask them a few basic questions about inheritance laws and see if they can answer or not. That will catch their lie. Then, an important thing: the Imam is infallible (Ma'sum). So, if someone is claiming to be the Imam, they will not openly promote forbidden acts. They will not declare sinful acts as permissible. They will not suddenly change the entire religion, declaring something that was permissible in the Sharia until yesterday as suddenly forbidden; that means they cannot be the Imam. They cannot normalize sin. If someone is normalizing sin or promoting sin, their lie will be caught. One more important point: what is our belief regarding Imamate? That the Imam is the knower of every language in the world. If someone claims to be the Mahdi, ask them a question in your own language and see if they answer or if they take the help of a translator. Then, what is in the traditions regarding the reappearance (Zuhur) of the Imam? That the reappearance will be from the Kaaba. If someone is sitting in some corner of London, or somewhere in Yemen, or Basra, or anywhere in the world, if they have not come from the Kaaba, they are not the Imam-e-Zamana. Their coming from the Kaaba is necessary. And the Imam-e-Zamana is the one—what is in the traditions? Whether Shia or Sunni, it is famous and present in everyone's books that when the Imam-e-Zamana comes, who will pray behind him? Prophet Isa (a.s.). So, Prophet Isa (a.s.) is not visible anywhere in the world right now. Through this, we can easily catch their lie. In the end, we pray to the Lord of the Worlds that, as in the traditions, when the Imam-e-Zamana (a.j.t.f.s.) comes, he will stroke the heads of his followers. And when he strokes their heads, their intellects will become perfect. So, it means he will stroke the heads of his followers, which will make their intellects perfect. That is, he himself will make people perfect. He will not be wandering around taking support from others. And as the brother mentioned earlier, he will not announce his reappearance through social media. His reappearance will be something more manifest than the sun, which no one will be able to deny. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds to grant us the true recognition (Ma'rifat) of our Imam, the Imam of our time. Protect us from the deceit and fraud of every false claimant. And to prove all these false things and false claimants wrong, and to wave the flag of truth, may He hasten the reappearance of our Imam, the true Imam, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), who is the descendant of Zahra (s.a.), who is the heir of Amir al-Mu'minin, and who is the final successor of the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Amin ya Rabbal Alamin. Viewers, the quiz link will be closed as soon as the timer on your screen ends. And now it is time for Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin. You are requested to focus for the Ziyarat. Because immediately after the Ziyarat, our daily winners for today will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Insha Allah. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Guardian of the Age, reach us and do not destroy us. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. First of all, we offer congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of the Sanctuary of the Universe, Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), and we pray to the Lord of the Worlds to hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time. title: Namaaz Kaise Mukammal Hoti Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the spiritual requirements for a complete and accepted prayer in Shia Islam. He emphasizes that the perfection of Salah is intrinsically linked to the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt and the practice of Tabarra (disavowal of their enemies). The lecture highlights that this disavowal is a form of spiritual sustenance granted by Allah, as evidenced in Ziyarat Ashura.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... [repeated]... O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. And what, how should we send Salawat? What will people think? People will not think anything, do not worry about that at all. Right? And you are not that great either. Just that, right? And one more thing, we are saying this at the end. When, because there is no time left at the end. Then that point remains. That when once the Imam was asked, what is the cause (illat) of prayer? So the Imam explained the cause, then it was asked what is its beginning? What are its timings? What is this? What is that? After asking all the questions, the narrator asked, how is the prayer completed? He said, the prayer is completed by our Wilayah and by doing Tabarra (disavowal) against our enemies. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Raise your voices with Salawat. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum. This is what is present. That the prayer is completed, wa ma tamamuhu. How is the prayer completed? How is it perfected? So the Imam said, first connect with our Wilayah, wal bara'atu min a'da. And until you do Tabarra upon our enemies, until then the prayer will not be complete. The prayer will be deficient, half. The prayer will not be complete. So if you get half a prayer, then see what will happen with half from Allah? The chances of acceptance are low. It is just Allah, I don't know. We cannot say. But the condition He has set, I am giving an example, pray the whole prayer and then do not recite the Salam, I am giving an example. Did not recite the Salam, why are we in the mood to recite the Salam today? Just finish the prayer after reciting Tashahhud. Will the prayer be accepted? Similarly, as the Imam says, until there is Bara'ah (disavowal), until then the prayer will not be accepted. Therefore, it is necessary that in the prayer, see, like the Qunut you recite, at least recite this much, at least: Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum wal an a'daahum al-wa'id. Wal an a'daahum al-wa'id. At least this much. And even today, this is its performance. This Lan (curse) and this Bara'ah, this is a sustenance (Rizq) from Allah. Allah does not give this sustenance to everyone. Read Ziyarat Ashura, it is written in Ziyarat Ashura. This is what Allah has given as sustenance. 'Wa razaqani minal bara'ati min a'daikum' (And He has granted me the sustenance of disavowal from your enemies). And Allah has given sustenance. This sustenance, this is spiritual sustenance. And the spiritual sustenance is much higher than the material sustenance. Indeed.

Tabarra (disavowal of the enemies of the Ahlulbayt) is a necessary condition for the perfection of Salah.

title: Imam Sajjaad (a.s.) Ko 'Sajjaad' Kyun Kaha Jaata Hai?
excerpt: This lecture explains the origin of the title 'Sajjad' given to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.). It highlights his deep devotion and habit of performing prostration (sujud) in response to divine blessings, protection from harm, and the completion of prayers. The narrative, attributed to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), illustrates the physical marks of worship that earned the Imam this honorable title.
content:
Why is Imam Sajjad (a.s.) called 'Sajjad'? Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi narrates that Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) said: 'Whenever my father, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.), remembered a blessing bestowed upon him by Allah (azza wa jal), he would prostrate. Whenever he recited a verse of prostration from the Holy Quran, he would prostrate. Whenever Allah (azza wa jal) averted a terrifying calamity from him or protected him from the plot of a conspirator, he would prostrate. Whenever he finished a obligatory prayer, he would prostrate. Whenever he was granted the opportunity to reconcile between two people, he would prostrate. The marks of prostration were visible on all the parts of his blessed body used for prostration. That is why he was called Sajjad.'
Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) is known as 'Sajjad' due to his frequent prostrations.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 11 | Tafseer of Surah at-Tauheed (Surah # 112) - Part 1
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual and practical benefits of reciting Surah al-Tawhid as taught by the Infallibles. The speaker emphasizes the power of the Quran for both physical healing and resolving worldly difficulties like poverty. By following the specific methods provided by the Ahlulbayt, believers can attain divine protection, prosperity, and a deeper understanding of the nature of God.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Blessings and peace be upon the master of all messengers, the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, and his pure and purified progeny. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. I once again seek refuge in Allah. Yesterday, I mentioned some benefits, and today I will continue with that. I presented before you that whoever desires to depart from this world purified of sins, as if they were just born, and wishes to have no accountability on the Day of Judgment, should recite Surah al-Tawhid 12 times after the five daily prayers and then raise their hands in supplication. I will now present the supplication to you: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your hidden, pure, and blessed name...' ...by Your hidden, pure, and blessed name, I ask You, and I supplicate through Your supreme and eternal authority, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O You who grant, O You who provide, O You who grant freedom from Hellfire, send blessings and peace upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and grant me salvation from Hellfire. When You take me from this world, take me in peace and safety, and when You admit me into Paradise, admit me with safety. Make my supplication a success, make its outcome a victory, and make its end the best. You are the Protector. Respected listeners, reflect on how the Master of the Faithful, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), is teaching us the method of supplication. If you wish for the Lord of the worlds to answer your prayers, then adopt the method I have described, which is the method of the Infallibles (a.s.). This is the method taught to us by the Infallibles (a.s.). Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) said this is one of the 'hidden treasures'. If you want to obtain this treasure, then follow it. When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) taught me this supplication, he commanded me to teach it to the believers. I told them... [narrative regarding a scorpion sting]. When he was stung, he said, 'May Allah curse the scorpion; it is neither a believer nor a disbeliever.' He took his blessed shoe and killed it with his shoe. Then he asked for water and salt, mixed them, applied it to the sting, and recited Surah al-Fatiha and the Mu'awwidhatayn. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) was once told by a companion that he had a toothache that kept him awake all night. The Imam (a.s.) said: 'Whenever you have pain in your tooth or molar, place your hand on it and recite...' ...recite verse 89 of Surah al-Naml: 'And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they shall pass away as the passing of the clouds. It is the work of Allah, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is well-acquainted with what you do.' When you do this, you will be healed. The Imam (a.s.) said that when you recite Surah al-Fatiha and then this verse of Surah al-Naml while placing your hand on the painful spot, your pain will vanish. Thus, both physical and spiritual cures are present in the Holy Quran. In this tradition, it is mentioned that a man complained to the Imam (a.s.) about his poverty and difficulties. The Imam (a.s.) said: 'When you enter your house, whether there is anyone inside or not, say Salam, and after that, recite Surah al-Tawhid once.' When the man did this, Allah made him prosperous, to the extent that his neighbors also became prosperous. Now, reflect on how we often get worried... ...we get worried about the scarcity of sustenance and look for shortcuts. We go to people, asking them to do this or that, or to perform magic, or to ask someone else. All these superstitions and nonsense are things we engage in, while everything is present in the Holy Quran. So, what should you do? When the Infallible (a.s.) has told us, we should go to the Quran. We should not go to those who have made a business out of religion. We are disgusted by them. Can they be good? No. You have forgotten the Quran, the Infallibles, and the scholars. You must know the solution to your problems. We worry a lot about sustenance, but our solution is the Holy Quran. It is a very simple method. When we enter our homes, whether someone is there or not, we should say 'Assalamu Alaikum' and then recite Surah al-Tawhid once. Note that by reciting Surah al-Tawhid and saying Salam, not only will you become prosperous, but this blessing will also reach your neighbors. ...your neighbors will also become prosperous. Your neighbors will also be blessed. It is better that through us, blessings reach our neighbors. Respected listeners, reflect on this. If we remain attached to the Quran and the Infallibles (a.s.), our difficulties will surely be removed. When people asked the Infallibles (a.s.) about Surah al-Tawhid, they said: 'Allah knew that in the end times, there would be people who would be deep thinkers, so He revealed Surah al-Tawhid and the beginning of Surah al-Hadid for them.' Whoever seeks more than this will be ruined. In a tradition, it is narrated that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to tell him about his Lord. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited this Surah to him, he said: 'O Muhammad, is your God as you have described?' Meaning, as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) described that God is the Creator but cannot be seen, and that He is not born of anything nor has He given birth to anything. He said: 'Your God is exactly as you have described.' Your God is exactly as you have described. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

title: Imam Ali (a.s.) Ki Aakhri Dua
excerpt: This lecture explores the final moments and prayers of Imam Ali (a.s.) leading up to his martyrdom on the 19th of Ramadan. It highlights his profound longing for death as a meeting with his Creator, fulfilling the Quranic challenge of truthfulness found in Surah Al-Jumu'ah. The speaker connects the Imam's ultimate success, 'Fuztu wa rabbil-ka'bah,' to the ongoing prayers of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) for the fulfillment of divine promises.
content:
Torchlight billah, ism-e-azam... (Arabic phrases). Throughout the history of Islam, many individuals have appeared who claimed to be truthful. But when the 6th verse of Surah Al-Jumu'ah declared, 'Fa-tamannawul-mawta in kuntum sadiqin' (Then wish for death if you are truthful), then living up to this verse, the Imam (a.s.) saw Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), the remover of difficulties, or after him, his progeny. When Imam Hasan (a.s.) saw his father attacking the enemy's army, he asked, 'O Father, why were you fighting with such intensity?' The Maula replied to his son, 'O son, your father does not care whether death comes to him or he reaches death.' On the 19th of Ramadan, he was praying to his Lord for the meeting of his desire at the house of his daughter, Sayyeda Umm Kulthum (s.a.). He was praying for the meeting of his desire with his Lord. Sayyeda Umm Kulthum (s.a.) says, 'My father was sometimes in a state of restlessness, sometimes in peace, sometimes in Ruku, and sometimes in Sujud. Every little while, he would come out of his room, look at the stars in the sky, and say, 'By God, I have never lied, nor have I ever been lied to. Surely, this is the secret that was promised to me.' Then he would return to his prayer mat and pray like this: 'O Lord, make death a blessing for me.' After this, he would frequently say, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' and 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azim.' Then he would perform ablution and pray a lot. I asked him, and the Maula replied, 'My daughter, I am saying this only because...' And I am saying this only because the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) promised me this. On one hand, Maula Ali (a.s.) proved who is truthful in the light of the verse of Surah Al-Jumu'ah by wishing for death in his prayers, and on the other hand, Allah Almighty accepted his prayer. Therefore, when the cursed Ibn Muljam struck his head, he announced his truthfulness by saying, 'Fuztu wa rabbil-ka'bah' (By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have succeeded). O Allah, I beseech You by the sake of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), just as You accepted his prayer, in the same way, the Imam of our time, who is sitting in the veil, holding the rope of the Ka'bah, is praying: 'Allahumma anjiz li ma wa'adtani' (O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me). O Lord, I beseech You by the tears flowing from the eyes of his progeny in the separation of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), grant us the ability to mourn the martyrdom of Maula Ali (a.s.) along with Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Grant us the ability to mourn the martyrdom of (a.s.). Amin Ya Rabbal Alamin. [Music]

title: Intezaar e Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) - Insaaniyat Ki Aakhri Ummeed
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of 'Intizar' (waiting) for Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as a source of hope amidst global oppression and suffering. The speaker references the teachings of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) to establish the necessity of the Hujjah (Proof of God) for the world's existence and blessings. The talk emphasizes that true waiting requires steadfast faith and constant prayer for the Imam's reappearance as a means of personal and spiritual welfare.
content:
With the grace of Allah, we begin. (Arabic recitation). Today, the state the world is passing through—whether it is the oppression on the Shias, attacks on the academies, opposition to Azadari, or the pandemics spread across the world and the resulting deaths—despite all these troubles and calamities, the only thing that does not let us despair of Allah's mercy is 'Intizar' (Waiting). I am waiting for the one whom Allah is waiting for, when He declared in the Holy Quran: 'Faintaziru inni ma'akum minal-muntazirin' (So wait, I am with you among those who wait). If we want to understand the importance of Intizar, let us turn to that Hadith of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) in which the Imam (a.s.) said to Ahmad bin Ishaq: 'The earth is never devoid of the Proof (Hujjah) of Allah Almighty since He created Adam (a.s.), and it will not be devoid of it until the Day of Judgment. It is the Hujjah of God through whom first... It is the Hujjah of God through whom first, calamities are removed from the earth, blessings descend from the sky, and bounties emerge from the earth. Ahmad bin Ishaq asked, 'O Son of the Prophet, who is the Imam and Caliph after you?' The Imam (a.s.) immediately went inside and brought his son out from the inner room, who was about three years old and whose face was shining like the full moon. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'O Ahmad bin Ishaq, if you were not honorable in the sight of Allah and His Proof, I would never have shown this son of mine to you. His name is the name of the Messenger of Allah, and his Kunya is his Kunya. He will fill the earth with justice and fairness just as it will be filled with oppression.' For this, there will be a long occultation (Ghaybah) in which no one can be saved from destruction except the one whom Allah Almighty keeps steadfast on the belief in his Imamate and grants the ability to pray for his reappearance. These moments are a test for all of us. Are we waiting for the Imam as we should? Are we, before every prayer, before every sorrow, before every wound, before every difficulty, in every prayer... First of all, in every Imam-e-Haram, in the kneeling postures of our prayers, we pray for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). When Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) himself advises in his letters to pray abundantly for his reappearance, because therein lies your welfare, then why should we not make this prayer, 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal hujjatibnil Hasan', our heart's desire so that every moment of ours passes in anticipation of our Master?
Intizar (waiting) is the ultimate source of hope for believers during times of global crisis.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 12 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture features Maulana Zulfiqar Ali Shah addressing various practical questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting in Islam. The discussion covers emergency situations like choking while fasting, the rules and requirements for I'tikaf, and the permissibility of fasting while traveling or when facing medical issues. The session emphasizes the importance of following Shari'i guidelines while prioritizing health and safety.
content:
I welcome all the viewers to this program. We begin with the recitation of the Holy Quran and immediately after, we will address your questions. We are joined by Maulana Zulfiqar Ali Shah. Welcome, Maulana. How are you? I hope you are well. When you recite the Quran in your homes, it attracts the angels. The Shaytan flees from the house where the Quran is recited. Why is it that in the house where it is recited, the angels descend? Because we want to make our homes a place of light. Let us move on to today's questions with Maulana Zulfiqar Ali Shah and learn how to answer them. Peace be upon you, Maulana. I hope you are well. May Allah keep you happy and blessed. Regarding the question of what to do if something gets stuck in the throat while fasting: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. If something is stuck, one should try to remove it. If it is possible to bring it out, do so. If you are choking, you must try to clear it. If you are choking, you must try to clear it. If you have used your finger to induce vomiting, it will not break the fast. Now, regarding the other matter: if you are in a state where you are choking, you must seek medical help. If you are on the verge of dying, you must go to the doctor. If inducing vomiting is necessary to save your life, it will not invalidate the fast. Now, regarding your question about I'tikaf: I'tikaf means that a person confines themselves in a mosque for the sake of worship. I will talk about this. I will dedicate my time to worship. This is called I'tikaf. I am confining myself in a mosque so that I can worship. This lasts for three days and two nights. It begins before the morning prayer and ends on the third day at Maghrib. One should keep the fast for these days. It can be 3, 5, 7, or 9 days. I'tikaf is not valid without fasting. When you are in I'tikaf, you must observe certain rules. You should not leave the mosque without a necessary reason. For example, you cannot leave for food and drink if it is not available in the mosque. You can leave for a funeral, to pray Jumu'ah, or to visit a sick person, but you must return immediately. You cannot engage in leisure activities. Similarly, certain things are forbidden during I'tikaf, such as smelling perfumes, engaging in intimacy with one's spouse, arguing, or conducting business transactions. If you are sitting in the mosque for I'tikaf, you must avoid these things. Remember, I'tikaf in the last ten days of the holy month is very virtuous. It is very virtuous. One can keep the fast of I'tikaf on any day. Regarding the question of whether one can keep a fast while traveling: In a Shari'i journey, one cannot keep a fast, except for a vowed fast (Nadr) where one has specifically stipulated that they will fast even while traveling. Other than that, one cannot fast during a journey. If you are a traveler, you cannot keep the fast, nor can you keep a Qada fast. Regarding the doctor's advice: if you are certain and the doctor has advised against fasting because it is harmful, then you should follow that. You must be certain that the fast is harmful to you. He can see many patients. Friends, regarding suggestions, Muslim doctors suggest that you can take medicines, injections, etc. It is absolutely permissible; any medicine for a cold or any other medicine can be taken. You can take injections if you need strength. So, whether you apply it on your forehead or throat, does it make a difference? If you are taking it, it is separate from eating and drinking. If you are taking it, it is separate from eating and drinking, but using medicine can be good for you. I said if you have a fever and need an injection, it is absolutely fine. Thank you very much, brother, for answering all the questions. Those viewers who have not yet asked their questions can send them to this WhatsApp number. We will try our best to answer your questions.

title: Ma'refat Ke Saath Ziyaarat Ka Kya Matlab Hai? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of performing Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) with 'Ma'rifat' or true recognition. Drawing from Kamil al-Ziyarat, the speaker explains that the promise of forgiveness for past and future sins is conditional upon recognizing the Imam's divine authority, his role as a proof of Allah, and his status as the gateway to the Divine. The talk emphasizes that true pilgrimage requires an internal belief in the Imam's intercessory power and his position as the ultimate guide.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. Ibn Qulawayh (may Allah have mercy on him), in his famous book Kamil al-Ziyarat, has narrated 11 hadiths from various chains on the authority of Imam Kazim (a.s.) and Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The summary of which is that whoever visits Imam Hussain (a.s.) while recognizing his right, his sanctity, and his Wilayah, his past and future sins will be forgiven. In these hadiths, the recognition of Imam Hussain's (a.s.) right, his sanctity, and his Wilayah has been made a condition for the Ziyarat. The question arises, what does it mean to come for Ziyarat with Ma'rifat (recognition) here? The answer is present in various hadiths and in the phrases of other Ziyarats themselves. Ziyarat with Ma'rifat means that a pilgrim must believe that the infallible whose blessed grave he intends to visit is Allah's proof over all His creation. He is the door of Allah, through which one enters the presence of the Divine. Whoever opposes him and his Ahl al-Bayt is misguided. He is the Imam of guidance and the source of guidance. He is the Wali of Allah, who occupies a lofty position. He is the intercessor in this world and the hereafter, the one who saves us from the fire of Hell, and apart from him, no one can save us from the fire of Hell. All these rights are present in various hadiths and in the phrases of the Ziyarat of the Infallibles (a.s.) themselves. This is the Ma'rifat which, if one carries in their heart while going for Ziyarat, the Lord of the Worlds will forgive their past and future sins. There is no doubt that this does not refer to sins committed intentionally and knowingly, but this does not mean that there is any exaggeration in the hadith. Forgiving sins is in the hands of Allah, and this is Allah's own decision; He will forgive the pilgrim of Imam Hussain (a.s.). We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds to forgive those sins of ours that are the cause of obstacles in our path to the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. Ya Hussain, Ana laka ya Hussain, man-e-tezo.

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#8 | Ahle Bait (a.s.) - The Source of Guidance  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture explores the central role of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) as the divinely appointed source of guidance and the embodiment of truth for humanity. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines the significance of Wilayah, highlighting historical milestones like Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira and Ghadir to establish Ali (a.s.) as the successor to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The discussion emphasizes that true knowledge and spiritual salvation are inextricably linked to adherence to the Ahlulbayt and the recognition of their infallibility.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. I will come back. Do not forget to subscribe to my channel. In this blessed month, the month of the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), to spread the message of Wilayah, to lay the carpet of guidance in every corner of the country. To lay the carpet of guidance in every corner of the country. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We offer our heartfelt congratulations on this month and welcome you to this episode. The month of Rabi is such that many events have occurred during the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), in which the reality of the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) has been highlighted and made clear to the people. Sometimes through the event of Mubahala, sometimes through the birth of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), sometimes through the public declaration of Ghadir, the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) was revealed. And sometimes, even more than the battlefield of Karbala, where the pilgrims of Imam Hussain (a.s.) are present for his martyrdom, upon whom his mercy and blessings descend. In this very month, there are events where the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) proved their superiority in the field of Mubahala. In this same month, there are also signs of Wilayah. There are also signs of Wilayah in this month. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in their own era gave evidence of this. This is proof and points towards the fact that this entire month clearly reveals the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to the people. That is, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are those personalities about whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself said, regarding the famous Hadith al-Thaqalayn, that if a human holds onto both the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, they will never go astray until the Day of Judgment. If they want guidance, they must present themselves at their door. Furthermore, many verses were revealed in the Holy Quran regarding the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Allah (s.w.t.) has recited a eulogy for them in the Holy Quran, where they are introduced as the 'Imam' (leaders). Allah (s.w.t.) says that We made them leaders so that through them, and through our command, they guide people. And the sixth Imam, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), says: Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says that we are the source of all guidance. Therefore, the topic of our eighth episode is 'Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the Source of Guidance'. I request the viewers to welcome the respected doctor with a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. In this series of Ma'rifat (recognition), the topic today is that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the ones who distinguish between truth and falsehood. Ali (a.s.) is the one who reveals who is who, who is the believer, and who is the hypocrite. Look, when people hold onto a rope firmly... When they hold onto it firmly, and it becomes very tight, and they start walking, what did people do in the olden days? They would tie a belt around their waist and hold onto it so it wouldn't slip or get lost. Metaphorically, holding onto the rope firmly means never letting go. Why is it necessary? Because Ali (a.s.) is the Siddiq-e-Akbar (the greatest truthful one). We were discussing the Farooq (the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood). These were titles. Later, people took them for themselves. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had already designated them. When talking about the five, one after another... When talking about the five, one after another, and whoever leaves Ali (a.s.) and turns to others, will be destroyed. Allah will honor the one who loves Ali (a.s.). In other words, if anyone wants to receive Allah's guidance, they must love Ali (a.s.) because there is no other way to reach the truth. Love is the key. And the one who stays behind, the one who abandons this path, Allah will destroy them. Allah will destroy them. Those who are not from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are not the progeny of the Prophet. The Prophet said, 'Hassan and Hussain (a.s.) are my sons.' He strengthened them. He said, 'They are my Ahlulbayt.' And that is why those who are descendants of the Prophet are called 'Ale-Rasool'. These are the ones who are the true progeny. And Hussain is from me, and I am from Hussain. May Allah grant this recognition to everyone. Accept their Wilayah (guardianship), accept their patronage, accept their leadership, and accept their guidance. And do not take anyone else as your guardian, director, confidant, authority, or confidant besides them. If you seek anything from anyone other than them, you will be turning away from your Lord. Do not go anywhere else leaving the progeny of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Turning away from the Lord means that His influence and His command are ignored. 'And the life of this world is nothing but a deception.' If you reflect on this command, there is a point here: whenever the word 'Siddiq' is used, it means that not only is the tongue truthful, but it is also very important that the person is truthful in their actions. It is a great virtue to always be truthful and not lie, but when someone is called a Siddiq, it is not just their tongue... When someone is called a Siddiq, it is not just their tongue that is truthful; rather, their actions testify to their tongue. Their actions are also truthful. A person might be a Muslim, but their Islam might not have sincerity or depth. But look at Ali (a.s.); he was the Siddiq. His actions always confirmed his words. That is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said he is not just a Siddiq, but 'Siddiq-e-Akbar' (the greatest truthful one). There is no one greater than him. Then he said, 'Ali is the Farooq' (the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood). They were the ones to look at. And when he said, 'Hold firmly to Ali,' it was because Ali (a.s.) is the one who shows the way. But people did not act upon the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) advice. And it is a belief that whoever loves Ali (a.s.), Allah will guide him. And as you know, there is a punishment in this world... The punishment of Allah is in this world. He takes it in this world, and then there will be 50 stations, and each station will be 1,000 years long. This period of 50,000 years—some say the Day of Judgment is 1,000 years, others say 50,000. When we combine these, it means a person will have to stand for 50,000 years. It will be very difficult, very hard. After those 50 stations are completed, then the turn for Paradise and Hell will come. Then the turn for Paradise and Hell will come. For those whose accounts are settled, they will go to Paradise or Hell. Those who are in Hell will remain there forever. So, the love of Ali (a.s.) is for every believer in this world. Understand this well; it is in this world that a person strives for it. And whoever holds enmity towards Ali (a.s.), his punishment in this world is that Allah will hold enmity towards him. And if Allah holds enmity towards someone, then there is no one to help him. There is no one to help him. Imam Hussain (a.s.) is the one to test. He said, 'Ali is the truth, then Hassan, then Hussain, and then the Imams.' The chain ended with the last one. Now, do not try to bring anyone else. Whoever brings someone else, that is a deviation. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that the life of this world is nothing but a deception. So, love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) completely, and know that the life of this world is nothing compared to the hereafter. Can the wealth of this world and all its things satisfy a person? Can they fulfill them? To the extent that Allah says about it... and if you understand the 'Ilm' (knowledge) of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it is a different thing. 'Ilm' is knowing the reality of something, and 'Fahm' is understanding how that thing works, understanding the whole system. They possess the knowledge and the understanding of the entire system of the universe. They know how everything exists. They know how everything exists. This is a point to consider. Let's look at another point. Sometimes people follow the wrong path. What does that mean? It means never follow anyone who is a follower of Satan. Satan keeps coming to me. If I stray from the path, and if I am on the right path, then I must follow them (the Imams). People should know that at this time, Satan has overcome you, which is why you are going on the wrong path. This happens when we are not with the Infallibles (Ma'sumeen). When the Infallibles are not there, every sin is a far-off thing; even the thought of sin is not there. They are pure. Whereas others claimed leadership, and when they faced difficulties, they would say, 'Leave me, leave me alone, I am not the best among you.' You should have thought before! After becoming the leader, you say this? Ali (a.s.) is the best. And when questions were asked, they would say, 'Ask Ali.' Ali (a.s.) was called 108 times to the court to answer, and he solved every problem. Hello, hi. During this time, all of us are here, and if we have a few questions, and if your answer is in accordance with the truth, then we will understand that you are the true successor of that Messenger whom we are searching for. We will understand that you are also wrong, and the Messenger you are following, his 3514 companions were present. They said, 'Ask, ask.' The questions were asked to the companions, and they were told, 'Tell us, what is the answer?' But they said nothing. And Janab Salman was standing there, watching what was happening. Now the honor of Islam was at stake. When Salman saw the situation, he put his cloak on his shoulders. As soon as he saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) on the pulpit... ...saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) on the pulpit, he saw the so-called noble ones. You saw, and you stood up and said, 'O Allah, may I never be in a difficulty when you are present.' Come, come, side by side, but he did not answer this and sat on the chair. Right, brother, as soon as he saw, because they were saying 'Ya Ali, Ya Ali,' he saw, 'Why do you get so excited?' Now, the one who was saying 'bank' is on the chair, and now he started asking questions. And he said, 'Answer the question.' What is the position? The companions were... and from this, every human being, the laborers, the unemployed, their things are... Anyway, the first ones were never... Anyway, the first ones were never those who say, 'Allah answers every question.' He wants, he loves very much, that my life, my life... and what he promised, he should fulfill. And the other innocent one, call his mother, call his mother, that my life and my... and Chanakya, my companions should be with me. Absolutely do it. Who is this? Meaning, this is the massage of guidance. Who is this? Meaning, this is the massage of guidance, and this is the lamp in the darkness. After the Messenger, this is the face. Now let us take it out. This is the light of guidance, this is guidance personified, this is the straight path (Sirat-e-Mustaqim). This is the straight path. Allahu Akbar. That is why it is very important here. See, it is said that whoever wants to live my life, live my death... it is very important. Not just... they brought a whole chapter on this topic. Many people, this whole chapter, whose name is 'Babul-Mawali' (The Gate of the Masters), to whom faith... whose name is 'Babul-Mawali', to whom faith was given, was launched. It is very important for a human being; it is very crucial that his end is firm. There are many people whose lives are very good, but at the time of death, they go astray. A few days before death, they go astray, they go astray. And there is such a personality in history, all the youth were there. It is said that in this school, at least, at least... Muslims, Shia and Sunni, the second one who spent his whole life... Adnan, the era of the Caliphate of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that began, that Caliphate... at that time, but it happened. This is the world, the religion has been divided, and they were killed in the turmoil, the youth were killed. So it is written in the stars, this is the sword of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and it was taken away. 'I will give you the sword of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).' You stay here, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... but today look what it is. This turmoil... after that, Zubair opened his eyes and started saying, 'O Hussain, you were with the Messenger of Allah.' You were with the Messenger of Allah, you were a relative of the Messenger, but Satan entered your head, Satan climbed onto your head, and led you to that end. I want the Caliphate. So the one who was... the enmity was there, and for the sake of the place, to fight, and the culprits were these people who fought in the wars, who did this work, and ultimately, at the instigation of the enemies of Sham, they martyred the Prophet's family, but the conspiracy was hatched in Syria. They martyred the family, but the conspiracy was hatched in Syria. And all around... that I am leaving two weighty things among you: the Book of Allah and... those who will explain the Book. And it is something... today Muslims are coming, and it is coming. This is enough for you, and wherever you are, no one has the right to... wherever you are, no one has the right to use their own opinion. 'My perspective is this, my opinion is this.' And that is why we see in history that those who were better in Islam, they rejected it. They formally... the Messenger... according to the Messenger, they changed it. Or rather, they made it forbidden. So these two concepts... one was the companions, and one was the Ahlul-Bayt. So in these two eras, see, these people made it forbidden. And then after that, Basra... this question was always there. Regarding the companions, it was said that now there is no need for it, whereas at that time... now there is no need for it, whereas at that time, it was... it was allowed. But they made it forbidden. If not, then now, in this way, what have they done? When they heard, then that person... for him also, it became forbidden. Allah did not... until this is a very strange thing. This is... and the church is also there. So these two... and today, they try to set a little bit of a standard. And then we will see how much time the incident of... the next session will be, because if this is coming... now, regarding Ghadir, it is necessary, but before this, a lot of... it is necessary. The argument is that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used 'Man Kunto Mawla,' why did he use it? Such things... first of all, first of all... that was not the occasion when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced the guidance and Imamate. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah, Imamate, and Caliphate. This was not the first occasion; before this, he had already begun various projects related to the mission he was entrusted with. He was commanded to 'warn your nearest kinsmen.' For three years, he had been preaching secretly, but after three years, when he began the public invitation, the first gathering was the Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira. I will explain this clearly so the youth can understand, as there are many accounts of it, the most famous being the one where everyone was invited. They were invited to a feast. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wanted to establish his mission. He invited his closest relatives, the Banu Hashim. He organized it properly, creating a chart of who was closest. 'Dhul-Ashira' means those who are your closest kin, those with whom you interact regularly. This is what is meant by 'Ashira' and 'Dawat'. This is what is meant by 'Dawat' (invitation) and 'Adawat' (kinship). He invited them all. There were about forty of them. These were the people who, apart from the polytheists and the disbelievers, were invited to the house of Abu Talib (a.s.). The responsibility for the food was given to Ali (a.s.). You must understand that for those who were invited, slaughtering a goat was not a big deal. A large goat was enough for the whole household to eat at one time, which would normally last us here in India for at least a week. But here, forty people were invited, and they ate the entire feast, leaving nothing behind. The people were amazed, saying, 'He has bewitched us; this is magic.' Once they had all eaten and were satisfied, the youth should know what happened before the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke. He asked them, 'If I tell you that there is an army behind this mountain, would you believe me?' They all replied, 'Yes, we have never heard you tell a lie.' Then he declared his mission, saying, 'I am the Messenger of Allah, and I have brought this message. Whoever helps me in this mission will be my successor, my heir, and my Caliph after me.' This was the first invitation and the first announcement. As soon as he said this, everyone remained silent, except for a 13-year-old boy—Ali (a.s.)—who stood up. He stood up and said, 'I will help you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked him to sit down. He repeated the call, and again, only Ali (a.s.) stood up. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) repeated it a third time, Ali (a.s.) stood up again. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) then declared, 'This is my brother, my successor, and my Caliph after me.' The relatives began to mock Abu Talib (a.s.), saying, 'Now you have to listen to your son.' Now you have to listen to your son. Anyway, this is the summary of the Dawat. Let us look at the proofs of Wilayah. First, there is the event of Ghadir, which is undeniable. Then there is the event of the Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira, which is also authentic. Then there is the event of Mubahila, and the fourth is the event of the ring (giving the ring while in Ruku). These are the proofs. I have already told you about Dhul-Ashira. Generally, the world tries not to mention it, or if they do, they do so in a distorted way. Alhamdulillah, I hope today's session will be beneficial. We are very grateful to everyone for their efforts in this regard. I have a very important announcement to make. On the occasion of this auspicious event, we are bringing a unique program, and this program is for all poets and all organizations. This program is called the 'International Jashn-e-Nahlane Wilayat'. This will be an online Jashn. You will be given a 'Misra' (line of poetry), and the details are available on our Facebook and Instagram pages. You must write a poem based on that Misra, consisting of 12 to 18 lines, and send it to our WhatsApp number: [number removed]. Along with the full poem, record a 2-minute video of yourself reciting it and send it to our WhatsApp number. Include your name, city, and organization name. The deadline for sending the video and the poem is August 8, 2020. The videos will be uploaded to our Facebook and Instagram pages. This online Jashn will be held on Sunday, August 16. This online Jashn will be held on Sunday, August 16. In this Jashn, the two best poems, two best Manqabats, and two best full poems will be awarded. All details are on our Facebook and Instagram pages. Women can also participate, but they should only send their written poems via WhatsApp; they should not send videos or audio. I request everyone to participate enthusiastically in this Jashn-e-Nahlane Wilayat. As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, it is the duty of every person to convey this message. By participating, let us try to spread the message of Wilayat worldwide. Since this is an international Jashn, anyone from around the world can participate. Now, in honor of the date of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), I present a few lines of poetry. The operation of the arithmetic mean is the wazifa of your name, the wazifa of your face is your name. What does the face of Shabbir need during the day? What news is there on the Arsh, or the veil, or this picture? What news is there on this, or the four days that were kept? When you prostrated to Allah, Zahra, and in the Lauh-e-Mahfooz, He has kept the truth safe. He who has kept the Lauh-e-Mahfooz safe, in your protection, Zahra, remains the Wali. In your protection remains the Wali, Zahra. The affairs of the universe are the picture of the Messenger, the affairs of the universe are the picture of the House, and the picture of Allah is Zahra, and the picture of Allah is Zahra. The one who is the helper of all in difficulties is Akbar, the one who is the helper of all in difficulties is Akbar. That Ali also called out in the mobile, Zahra. With the Salawat of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), we want to continue until next week, and in the end, we all pray that in this matter, the biggest one among the Muslims, the biggest one regarding the body, may Allah grant patience to them and their father-in-law. Regarding the patience of them and their father-in-law, come, let us all together help for the sake of... [Arabic phrase] ...

title: Ep#18 | Mahdaviyyat Ke Jhootey Daawedaar
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical phenomenon of false claimants to Mahdism, who have sought to mislead followers by falsely declaring themselves to be the awaited Imam Mahdi. The speaker highlights specific examples of such figures, including Sajah bint Harith, Mirza Ghulam Ahmad Qadiani, and the founders of the Baha'i faith, to illustrate the recurring nature of this deception. By contrasting these claimants with the authentic signs of Imam Mahdi as described in Islamic Hadith, the lecture emphasizes the importance of religious knowledge and discernment. Ultimately, the speaker concludes that the true reappearance of the Imam will be an undeniable, global event as clear as the midday sun.
content:
And listen, brother, what happened? We have appealed to the court... [Arabic phrase] ... Peace be upon you. By the grace of Allah, the topic we will try to present before you today is the false claims of Mahdism, which is nothing but a deception and its result. And for those who believe in it, this promise of guidance has been made. Some mischievous people, with the intention of taking wrong advantage of this and to mislead innocent people, made false claims of being Imam Mahdi. Such false claimants are called 'Mudda'iyan-e-Mahdaviyat'. In history, many such claimants have appeared who belonged to different regions of the world. Let us try to know about some such claimants. Although there is a long list of these false claimants, if we sit down to describe them, it would take several generations. Among them, it would take several generations. Among them, by describing only a few, we will try to see how we can keep ourselves safe from the deceit and fraud of these claimants. The most ancient and first claimant mentioned in history is named Sajah bint Harith, who also claimed to bring a new Quran. She ordered to keep the fasts of Ramadan in the month of Rajab and ordered to pray 10 prayers a day instead of five. In 1828, in Senegal, a person claimed to be Imam Mahdi. He tried to bring a revolution against the tyrant government of that country by saying that he himself is Imam Mahdi, but that government defeated him and his companions and killed them. A few years ago, Mirza Ghulam Ahmad Qadiani claimed not only Mahdism but also Prophethood, on the basis of which all Muslims who believe in the finality of Prophethood, who believe in the finality of Prophethood, declared this Qadiani sect as infidels and apostates. In the thirteenth century Hijri, a new sect emerged which is known as the Baha'i faith. The person who laid the foundation of this group was named Mirza Ali Muhammad Shirazi, and his followers remember him by the name of Sayyid-e-Bab. 1300 years after the advent of Islam, the Bab first claimed Prophethood, then through the word 'Bab', claimed that he is the door, i.e., the gateway to reach the Imam of the Time. But due to the opposition of the people, this door itself, i.e., Mirza Ali Muhammad Shirazi, closing himself, claimed the end of the claim, and finally claimed divinity. The followers of the Baha'i faith believe that the Bab, through his divinity, has abrogated the religion of Islam and Islam is no longer the religion liked and chosen by Allah. Recently, a person named Rahmat Ali Hasan from Basra made a false claim of being Mahdi. He was born in 1968 and with the help of some people, he first claimed to be the Mahdi, and also claimed that he is the first Mahdi. His followers call him the 'Universal Mahdi' and declare his invitation a global invitation, which includes Jews, Christians, and Muslims. This was brief information about some people who were among the claimants. But the Shias of the Ahlulbayt in every era, whose faith is strong, do not fall into the trap of these claimants. The reason for this is that in the Holy Quran and the Hadith of the Masumeen (a.s.), the signs of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), his attributes, the signs of his reappearance, and the mention of his government are present. The only way to keep oneself safe from these claimants or false claimants and to avoid misguidance and deviation is to increase our knowledge and recognition. Let us point towards some of the Hadiths of our leaders and the important things mentioned in them. First, the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) says that Mahdi is from my progeny, his name is my name, his kunniyat is my kunniyat. In some Hadiths, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that when he comes, he will fill this world with justice just as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. Third, it is stated in a Hadith that Imam Mahdi will be from the progeny of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.). A narration also states that on the head of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), there will be a shadow of clouds, just like the coming of Hazrat Isa (a.s.) with Imam Mahdi. Perhaps these claimants have forgotten the 313 companions about whom narrations exist, who will gather in Makkah Mukarramah in one night. At the time of reappearance, a voice will come from the sky which will be of Hazrat Jibraeel (a.s.). If we reflect, none of these signs are found in any of these claimants. Neither did Hazrat Isa (a.s.) descend, nor in the world has justice been established. The claimant is not the son of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), and Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.). Those false claimants were neither possessors of miracles, nor was their complete information possible, nor was there a shadow of clouds over them. And the heavenly voice, let alone, no one even heard any news of anyone coming near the Kaaba via a loudspeaker. In the end, we would like to complete our talk with the help of a Hadith of Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), in which the Imam (a.s.) says that when our affair, i.e., the reappearance of Imam Mahdi, truly happens, it will be brighter than the sun. When the sun is shining in the sky, there is no room for doubt in anyone's mind whether it is day or night. Even if a blind person is there, he will also be able to tell easily from the heat of the sun that it is now day. He will be able to tell easily that it is day. Similarly, the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is such a divine affair that after it happens, no one will have any doubt whether the son of Zahra has come or not. Now it has become absolutely clear that the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has not happened yet, and the waiting hours for the Yusuf-e-Zahra, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.), have not ended. And all those who claim this or consider others as Mahdi are all liars. [Music] ... gave the correct answer to the questions in the comment section of this video, in the description of the video, and by clicking there, those who give the correct answer to the question, in the episode, 2 minutes and they will be given a prize of 1000 rupees for the word...

Authentic signs include the descent of Hazrat Isa (a.s.) and a heavenly voice from Jibraeel (a.s.).

In those things, three things are regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.). He says that 'Anas-Sirat-ul-Mustaqeem', the straight path which Allah has made straight, that was him, and after that, he says, 'Ala ya ahlal-alam, inna jaddi al-Hussain qataluhu atshana', 'Know, O people of the world, my grandfather Hussain was killed thirsty.' title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#14 - Kya Imam Ali (a.s.) Ne Khalifa e Awwal Ki Bay'at Ki? Part 2/2
excerpt: This lecture concludes the two-part analysis regarding the historical controversy surrounding Imam Ali (a.s.) and the pledge of allegiance to the first caliph. The speaker examines theological and historical evidence, arguing that Imam Ali (a.s.) did not voluntarily offer allegiance, as it would contradict his divine appointment at Ghadir Khumm. By referencing Nahj al-Balagha and the status of the Ahl al-Bayt, the discourse emphasizes that the Imam's mission remained consistent with the Prophet's explicit declarations, rejecting any forced political contracts.
content:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah. Welcome to another episode of our series on the life of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). As we promised in the previous episode, we will share more gems regarding this subject. In the last report, we saw that Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance (bay'ah) to any person or any caliph; rather, the allegiance that was taken was forced. Ali (a.s.) did not voluntarily pledge allegiance to anyone. We also noted that one of the biggest reasons for the martyrdom of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was this very issue of allegiance. Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance, and Janabe Zahra (s.a.) saved his life. We have invited our brother, Zakir Sahab, to explain the reasons behind this. Brother, Assalamu Alaikum. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. As you promised in this new episode to share more gems and explain why Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance and what the reason behind it was, we would like you to inform our viewers. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Peace be upon Fatima Zahra (s.a.). After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left this world, the biggest issue among Muslims was politics. Many people believe that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint a successor during his lifetime. They claim he taught every small and big thing of Sharia—how to cut nails, how to apply kohl, the length of a beard, the length of trousers—but they claim he did not mention who his successor was. They claim he taught everything, but not who his successor was. However, the Shia belief is that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did, on many occasions, introduce Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as his brother, successor, caliph, and vicegerent. From the beginning to the end, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) kept mentioning who his successor would be. As you mentioned, the most prominent event was Ghadir Khumm, where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) held his hand and declared, 'Of whomsoever I am Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.' Not only that, but in the field of Ghadir, people were asked to pledge allegiance to Ali (a.s.). But after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) passed away, what happened? They forgot that day. They forgot that day, and as soon as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) closed his eyes, they did not accept Ali (a.s.) as the Imam and Caliph. If we talk about the allegiance (bay'ah) taken by those people, we can say that all these individuals had pledged allegiance at Ghadir. They forgot that pledge and took a different one. Today's generation asks why the caliph's allegiance is discussed. The allegiance taken by Ali (a.s.) is the subject. We are trying to show that the issue of allegiance is being distorted. In this episode, we will see that Mawla Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance to anyone, and whatever happened was forced. So, the question arises: why did Ali (a.s.) refuse this allegiance? In Arabic, if we look at the literal meaning of 'bay'ah', it means to sell or to make a contract between a seller and a buyer. In Islam, for a contract to be valid, both parties—the buyer and the seller—must be willing. If one party is not willing, the contract is not considered valid. In Islam, pledging allegiance means handing oneself over to someone else, giving one's authority to another. In the tradition of Muslims, the one giving the allegiance places their hand under the hand of the one receiving it. If you remember the previous episode, we saw that in the forced allegiance, they grabbed his hand and placed it on top of theirs, declaring it a bay'ah, and he was forced into it. It would not be wrong to say that in this rush to take forced allegiance, these people forgot that according to the rules of bay'ah, they did not take a valid allegiance from Ali (a.s.). You are absolutely right. The rule of bay'ah is that the hand of the one giving it is below, and the hand of the one receiving it is above. As it happened at Ghadir, no Muslim can deny that this happened at Ghadir. We don't have enough time to go into detail, but I will present a proof from their own books. In the book 'Tarikh al-Madina al-Dimashq', Volume 42, page 234, it is written that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) held Ali's hand... The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) held Ali's hand and said, 'Of whomsoever I am Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.' This narration continues. Abu Hurairah narrates that after that, Umar came to Ali (a.s.) and said, 'Congratulations, O son of Abu Talib, you have become the Mawla of all believing men and women.' He congratulated him, and then for three days, people pledged allegiance to him. This is proof that the congratulations were for Ali (a.s.) becoming the successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). If all Muslims had already pledged allegiance at Ghadir, why ask again? So, the question arises: why did they not pledge allegiance in Islam? This is a question for the viewers. As you said, we don't have time to cover everything, but our viewers can check our YouTube channel for previous episodes where these details are available. Moving forward, there is an interesting point regarding this bay'ah. The scholars of the other side believe that if multiple allegiances are taken, the first one is valid, and the second one should be rejected. This is mentioned in Sahih Muslim, Book 33, Hadith 1853, which states: 'If allegiance is taken for two, kill the second one.' It says, 'Kill the second one.' If we look at it according to their own standards, since Ali (a.s.) was the first to be pledged allegiance to at Ghadir, then the allegiance taken by the first caliph was invalid. This is why Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance to anyone. Ali (a.s.) knew his right. He knew that not only did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appoint him as his successor, but he was also the most excellent among all Muslims. No one can deny this, as it is a famous narration. It is famous in 'Tarikh al-Madina al-Dimashq', Volume 42, pages 373-374. You will find these narrations from great companions like Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who narrated from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that 'Ali is the best of people; whoever denies this is a disbeliever.' This is the Prophet's own verdict. If we discuss Ali's excellence, this series would not be enough. Besides this, I will give you another point. Ibn Abi al-Hadid wrote in the introduction to his book 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha'... In the case of the 'Ubla' (the boiling/burning incident), the process described is what is written. Alhamdulillah, we are praising Allah. All praise is for the One who gave preference to the superior over the inferior. The reference being given is that the inferior is being given preference over the superior, which is against our beliefs. Wait, let's pause here. Many people say that because he spoke a lie—that the wine was spilled—that is why... many people say this is 666. While saying this sentence itself, remember that it has no connection with the Shia Imamiyyah school of thought. Because if we look at the Shia Imamiyyah school of thought, if we look at the beliefs, even the general beliefs of Islam, our stance is that Ali (a.s.) is not only the most superior among all the Sahaba, but among all people, and excluding the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he is the most superior among all the Prophets. Here, I must clarify that while the discussion is about the 'Ubla' and Ali (a.s.) not arguing, I must say that even if all the people of the world, all Muslims, were to gather and do this kind of injustice, it would not diminish his status. At the same time, if all people, all Muslims, were to gather... At the same time, if all people, all Muslims, were to gather and even if they were to accept someone else as their Mawla, it would not affect Ali (a.s.)'s status. It would not decrease his status, but rather it would increase the status of the person who accepts Ali (a.s.) as their Mawla, because they would be on the right path. And as far as this issue of 'Ubla' is concerned, people give the example of the world: if there is a company where many employees work, some are very good and some are not as good. If the owners of that company, the CEOs, etc., are just people, they would never give preference to an inferior employee over a superior one. They would not be satisfied with that. And if the mood is to shut down the company, that is a different matter. They said that if it is a matter of justice, they would never make such a decision. When a common human can perform such an act, how is it possible that the Mawla of the Universe, whose life is filled with such dignity and honor, and in whose hands the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—from the beginning to the end—has declared his virtues, repeatedly called him at every opportunity, called him the most superior at every opportunity, and remembered him as his successor, his caliph, and his deputy, introducing him to the people... Introducing him to the people, saying, 'Know that this is my brother, this is my successor.' Despite all these efforts, can Ali (a.s.) expect or talk about any of his inferiors? This is absolutely impossible. Now, see what the Mawla says in this regard in his own words. As I said, the Mawla considered this atmosphere of disagreement as his right. In this regard, the Mawla's statement is in Nahj al-Balagha, sermon number two. If you turn the pages, at that time, Ali (a.s.) is clearly saying, 'There is no one in this Ummah who can be compared to the Ahl al-Bayt of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).' No one can be compared to them, nor can anyone be equal to them, because they are the foundation of the religion... Because they are the foundation of the religion. Those who have gone ahead must return to them, and those who have lagged behind must reach them. They cannot remain behind; if they remain behind, they are lost. Therefore, they must also follow Ali (a.s.). Then the Mawla says, 'They are the source of the right, they are the trustees of the Prophet, and they are the inheritors of the Prophet.' Being the successor of the Prophet, being the heir of the Prophet, is only their right. These are the Prophet's successors, and this inheritance is only for them. After this, finally, the Mawla says, 'To say that he considered this his right...' It is clear that the Mawla himself said this, and he said it on the pulpit. And those who say, 'Now that he has reached the caliphate, now he says this,' it is because he has reached his rightful place. Finally, I would just like to say, if the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) were to summarize this... I would like to summarize just this: if Ali (a.s.) were to speak about someone else while he himself is the most superior, what would be the result? If he were to praise someone, what would be the result? The first question that arises is about the command of Allah. If Imam Ali (a.s.) was made the Mawla according to the command of Allah, then if Ali (a.s.) were to speak about someone else, it would be a violation of the command of Allah and the right of Allah. And it would be a violation of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), who, in the field of Ghadir and from the city to the village, in front of all the people, had declared Ali (a.s.) as his successor and deputy. Therefore, this would be a violation of the Prophet. This is the Prophet who tells you, 'This is my successor after me, this is my caliph.' He declared it many times, and if Ali (a.s.) were to speak about someone else, it would be a violation of the Prophet. Finally, if Ali (a.s.) were to speak about someone else, it would mean joining hands with those against whom the Princess of the Worlds, Fatima Zahra (s.a.), was angry. It is impossible for Ali (a.s.) to praise anyone else. We thank you from the bottom of our hearts... It is difficult. We thank you for taking the time and for the fact that such difficult topics have been addressed with such excellent Zulfiqar (arguments) so that the opponents and all the questions that arise can be answered in the light of Islam. With this, our episode ends here. Viewers, we hope you are enjoying these episodes. If any objection comes to your mind or any point you want to understand, you can contact us on our social media handles. It will be our full effort to answer every such question through these episodes. Until then, goodbye. [Music]
