title: Ahkaam | Session # 3 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture addresses common questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting during Ramadan. The speaker clarifies the priority of breaking the fast versus performing prayers, the precise timing for Suhoor, and the importance of following reliable timetables from Maraji. Additionally, the session provides guidance on health precautions and the obligation to isolate when dealing with infectious illnesses to protect others.
content:
Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. La ilaha illallah. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Dear viewers, welcome to this episode of our program. In this second episode, we will continue our discussion regarding the fasts of a traveler, and I am sure you have benefited from the previous points. You must have benefited from these points. Dear friends, this blessed month of Ramadan teaches us many things. The hunger and thirst we feel while fasting reminds us of humanity; it makes us realize the hunger and thirst of the poor and needy. It reminds us of the hunger and thirst of the Day of Judgment. Ramadan teaches us how to protect our tongues from all kinds of evils and our eyes from looking at things that are forbidden by the Sharia. It tells us to keep our ears safe from listening to things that the Sharia has forbidden us to hear. The time has come to present your questions. In this third episode, we have a guest with us. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Please tell us about the rulings of fasting. A few questions from the viewers have come to us. The first question is: Believers are often in a dilemma about whether to break their fast first or offer their prayers first when the time for Iftar arrives. Please shed some light on this so our viewers can benefit. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Regarding the issue of whether to pray first or break the fast, I would say that if you want to perform your prayers with focus and presence of heart, you can break your fast first. If you are hungry, your mind is on food, and you are standing in prayer, it is better to break your fast first. When your stomach is empty, it is better to break your fast before praying. Also, if you have invited guests, you should not keep them waiting; you should serve them first and then pray. Remember, the devil tries to distract us. When we are hungry, our mind is often on food. It is a human nature that when we are hungry, we think about food, but we must focus on the worship of Allah. Many people ask about the timing of Suhoor and whether they should stop eating 10 or 15 minutes before the Adhan as a precaution. Also, believers want to know about the timing of the prayer. Could you please shed some light on this? See, these are a few questions. Regarding when we should stop eating for Suhoor, all scholars say that the Quran says: 'Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread of the night.' This means you should continue until the dawn is clear. Some say stop at 4:52 or 5:07, but the ruling is that as long as you are not certain that dawn has broken, you can continue eating. If you are eating and you realize dawn has broken, you must stop immediately. If you continue eating intentionally, your fast is void. If you continue eating intentionally, your fast is void. You should be careful. In many matters, we need to be cautious. For example, in Wudu, you must wash the area between the thumb and the finger. Similarly, regarding eating and drinking, you should be careful. I am not saying you should be overly cautious to the point of obsession, but one should be careful in all matters of religion. Our eating and drinking should be according to the pleasure of Allah. Regarding the prayer time, if you follow the rulings of Ayatollah Sistani or other Maraji, you should follow their provided timetables. If someone asks about the timetable, they should follow the one provided by their Marja. See, in the past, there were no clocks, so people used to observe the sky. Now, even with clocks, there might be a slight difference, but you should follow the reliable timetables provided by the offices of the Maraji. The third question is regarding the state of illness. If a person has contracted a virus and another person is living with them but shows no symptoms, what is the ruling for the second person? I would say that if a person knows they are infected, it is Wajib (obligatory) for them to isolate themselves from the person who is not infected. If the second person gets infected because the first person did not take precautions, then the first person is responsible. It was not appropriate for it to become old, its expiry date... if this person is at the door, they will kill him. If he dies after that, then our stance is very clear: if there are two people, one is affected and the other is not, then the one who is not affected should save his life at the door. Precaution is like a defense. Now, regarding the people at home, it was asked how many times I work. Doctors say if you want to stay safe from the virus, then this will not happen. When I am working outside, I feel that... if you go outside and despite taking precautionary measures you feel afraid, then you should stay at home, it will be cleared. So, you see how much of an area it is, and the doctor has said it is true, if we... So the doctor said it is true. If we do this, that Islam is for saving lives, and if there is no other way, then one should also avoid it so that no one else gets it. You are patient. If you wanted to ask, then the answer I gave to this question is exactly this. Its medicine is this very question, and thank you for saying that a person should take it. Both, if it has happened, should also act with caution and isolate themselves from people, and the one who has not been affected should also isolate themselves. And as you also mentioned here that because of this, it has not ended, it is being taught, and we will be face-to-face once again. Those who have not yet sent their questions are requested to send them to the WhatsApp number 109 without fail. Thank you. Thank you very much for your questions. Our entire team thanks you for these questions, and we pray to the Almighty in His court that may He grant us the ability to continue this work until next year. May He grant us the full right.

title: Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) Ke Liye Dua | Dr Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi emphasizes the spiritual significance of praying for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). He references a tradition from Usul al-Kafi regarding the immense benefits of dedicating one's prayers and Salawat exclusively to the Prophet and his family. By prioritizing the needs of the Ahlulbayt over one's own, a believer secures divine support for both their worldly and spiritual affairs.
content:
And pray as much as possible for the Imam. As much as possible. (Aksiru al-du'a bi-ta'jil al-faraj fa-inna dhalika farajukum). In Usul al-Kafi, there is a narration that a man came to the Prophet and said, 'I keep about one-third of my Durood and Salawat, meaning my prayers, for you sometimes.' Then after a while, he said, 'No, sometimes I keep half of my Durood and half of my prayers for you.' Meaning half for myself, half for you. He says, 'No, sometimes I pray only for you.' Meaning for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), and I don't do any other prayer. Only for you, only in your favor. Look at what a great thing this is. I don't pray for myself. As soon as he said this, the Prophet replied, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'If you do this, then be certain that Allah will take care of all your worldly and hereafter, religious and worldly troubles. Allah will make you needless of troubles. Because you have prayed in our favor, we will take care of you. You have prayed for us, we will pray for you because He is Generous, and if the Prophet prays in someone's favor, then the Prophet and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) are those whose prayers are answered. It is mandatory and necessary for their prayers to be accepted. It is wajib that their prayers be accepted. Whether our prayers are accepted or not, there is always a question mark about that. But the prayer of the Prophet and the prayer of the family of Muhammad (a.s.), if they pray in someone's favor...'

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Tumhein Naam Se Pehchaante Hain - Aye Zaair-e-Arbaeen | Arbaeen 2025
excerpt: This lecture addresses the concerns of Arbaeen pilgrims who feel discouraged when they cannot physically reach the Zari of Imam Hussain (a.s.) due to massive crowds. The speaker cites a tradition from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) to reassure believers that Imam Hussain (a.s.) personally recognizes every pilgrim by name and watches over them. The talk emphasizes that the Imam seeks forgiveness for his mourners from Allah and his own ancestors, ensuring that pilgrims return purified of their sins.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon the Prophet. It is the immense favor of the Almighty that He granted the opportunity to visit Karbala for the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the martyrs of Karbala on the occasion of Arbaeen. Millions of people come to Karbala on this occasion of Arbaeen. Every pilgrim has the desire to somehow reach the Imam's shrine, the Imam's Zari. Some are able to reach, but some, due to the crowd of millions, are unable to reach the Zari themselves. Sometimes, a thought of despair enters the mind: 'Is it possible that after calling me from so far, the Mawla did not call me to Him? Is it possible that the Mawla's gaze is not upon us? Is it possible that the Mawla did not show mercy to us? Will our Ziyarat really be accepted or not?' And other such thoughts keep coming. For those people, especially listen to this Hadith, because there is no need to be disappointed. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) narrates on behalf of Imam Hussain (a.s.): 'Imam Hussain (a.s.) is with his Lord, from where he looks towards his army and towards everyone who sacrificed their lives for him, that is, all the martyrs of Karbala.' He keeps looking towards the martyrs of Karbala, keeps his gaze upon them, and after that, the Imam says, and then after that, he looks towards his pilgrims. Yes, every pilgrim of the Imam is under the Imam's gaze. And the Imam recognizes them well. How? He recognizes them by their names, by the names of their fathers. He knows about their status and their ranks, who is at what rank, who is at what level. In the sight of Allah, Imam Hussain (a.s.) knows all these things about every one of his pilgrims. Even more than you know about your own children, Imam Hussain (a.s.) knows all this about every one of his pilgrims, says Imam Sadiq (a.s.). And then what does the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) do? When he sees who is weeping for him, who is in that state, who is mourning for him, whatever person weeps for the Imam, what does the Imam do for him? The Imam seeks forgiveness for him in the court of Allah. For every one of his mourners, for every one of his pilgrims, the Imam seeks forgiveness, and not only does the Imam do it himself—the sentence is: 'He requests his ancestors to also seek forgiveness for his pilgrims.' He requests them to seek forgiveness for his pilgrims. Who are the ancestors? The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Lady Zahra (s.a.). He requests them, 'Imam Hussain says, seek forgiveness for my pilgrim.' And then the next sentence of the tradition is: 'And the Imam says, the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) himself says, if my pilgrim realized, if he knew what reward Allah has prepared for him in exchange for the Ziyarat, his joy would overcome his grief.' We who come to Karbala and weep for Imam Hussain (a.s.), this weeping is proof that the person does not yet realize that reward. He does not have an estimate of what reward Allah has prepared for him on the Day of Judgment for this Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). And in the end, the Imam says, when the pilgrim of Imam Hussain (a.s.) returns, when he goes back home from this Ziyarat, no sin remains upon him. He has become purified of all his sins. This is the grace of Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself for his pilgrims. Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself, the Ark of Salvation, is seeking forgiveness for his pilgrims and praying to his ancestors for my pilgrim. Thanks to the Almighty that He gave the opportunity to visit Karbala, Imam... Thanks to the Almighty that He gave the opportunity to visit Karbala, the shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.). We pray to the Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of the heir of Imam Hussain (a.s.), our Imam of the time (a.t.f.s.), and grants us the opportunity to take revenge for Imam Hussain (a.s.) and all the martyrs of Karbala and the oppressed along with him, and grants all the believers the opportunity to visit Karbala this year and every year. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This lecture addresses the theological debate regarding the passing of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), specifically questioning whether it was a natural death or martyrdom. The speaker cites Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, a highly regarded source, to support the claim that the Prophet was indeed martyred. By referencing historical narrations, the lecture emphasizes that martyrdom is a divine honor bestowed upon the Prophet alongside his prophethood.
content:
How can you say this about the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? I have often heard about his natural death. Look, what is written here? Oh, this is from Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, which is considered a very authentic book. Now look there, what is written: 'The narrator states that I am ready to swear by Allah not once but nine times, what to swear, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was martyred.' He was martyred, and this was because, why? 'Lillah-il-Ajal, he was a martyr,' and this is because just as Allah the Almighty made him a Prophet, He also blessed him with martyrdom.

title: Qamees (Shirt) Chaak Karke Maatam Karna Sunnat Hai [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the legitimacy of tearing one's shirt as an act of mourning, citing the historical example of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) during the funeral of his father. The speaker recounts how an individual questioned the Imam's action, only to be rebuked and warned that such mourning is a Sunnah practiced by Prophets like Moses. The lecture concludes by emphasizing the spiritual dangers of objecting to the actions of the Infallible Imams, noting the dire consequences that befell the individual who questioned the Imam.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. Allama Majlisi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates from Rijal-e-Kashi that Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) came out of his house for the funeral of his noble father, Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.), with his shirt torn. Seeing this, a man named Abu Awn al-Abrash wrote a letter to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and asked, 'Whom have you seen, or which of the other Imams tore their shirt like you did?' In another hadith, it is also found that he had written, 'People were terrified to see you like this.' In response to his insolence, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) wrote in the letter, 'O fool! What do you think of yourself? Surely, Moses (peace be upon our Prophet and his family and him) tore his shirt upon the passing of Aaron (peace be upon our Prophet and his family and him).' The Imam (a.s.) further wrote, 'Indeed, there are some among people who are born believers, live like a believer, and depart from this world as a believer.' But there are also some people who are born believers, live like a believer, but their death is upon disbelief. Surely, you will not leave this world until you are outside the fold of religion and you become insane.' And it happened exactly as the Imam (a.s.) had predicted. That man left this world in that state. His own children had locked him in a room and kept him away from people's sight due to his insanity, delusions, incoherent speech, opposition to the Ahl al-Imamah, and the manifestation of his hypocrisy. The point to note in this hadith is that the punishment that person received for doubting and objecting to the action of an infallible Imam was that he became insane, and due to the denial of Imamate, his end was upon disbelief. Therefore, whoever objects to mourning by tearing the shirt in this manner, it should be clear to them that mourning in this way is the Sunnah of the Prophets (a.s.) as well as the Sunnah of the Imams (a.s.). Sadaqa Mawlana al-Hasan ibn-e-Ali (a.s.).

excerpt: This lecture explains how Surah Al-Qadr serves as a definitive theological proof for the necessity and existence of the Imam of the time. The speaker highlights the guidance of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), who instructs Shias to use this Surah to debate and establish the reality of Imamate. It emphasizes that since angels descend with divine decrees to the Imam, he remains the central authority and controller of affairs on earth.
content:
Hazrat Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) says, and this is specifically the Imam's message to his Shias: If you want to prove your Imam, the existence of your Imam, if you want to present evidence that we are the nation that Allah has not left orphaned, our Imam is there, our Imam is alive, remains, is on this earth, and the angels come to him. The Imam says, 'Ya ma'shar shi'ati' (O my Shias), debate with the enemies regarding this Surah Qadr, argue. Why? The Imam says, 'Tafluju' (You will be successful). You ask those people, if these angels are descending, then where, to whom are they descending? The Imam is giving us a key, a tool for argument and debate, that if you want to prove your truthfulness, prove it from the same Quran and prove it in front of those who keep saying that the Quran is enough for us. Make them realize that claiming is one thing and the Quran actually being enough is another. The Imam says, 'Fa-wallah' (By Allah), this Surah is a proof from Allah over His creatures, it is the proof of Allah the Almighty. Because after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), this Surah is also a kind of proof. This Surah is the master and leader of your religion. Keep this Surah with you always. If you keep this Surah with you, you will never feel difficulty in proving the belief of Imamate. Then the Imam says, 'Innaha la ghayatul ilmina' (It is the limit of our knowledge), this Surah. Why? Because the angels are bringing every thing, all affairs, all destinies to the Imam of the time. Meaning, the Imam of the time is the personality in whose power of control is everyone's destiny. Therefore, now in the Night of Qadr, it is our responsibility that if we ask, we should ask from the Imam, and first of all, if we ask for anything from Allah, we should ask for the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.), pray for the reappearance of our Imam. The most important prayer in this Night of Qadr should be only and only the reappearance of the Imam for us.

title: A Dua For All Needs-Dua Abu Hamza Somali | Part 2-The Brilliance Of Dua Abu Hamza Somali
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance and structure of Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali, a comprehensive supplication attributed to the companion of the Imams. It highlights the prayer's role in cultivating proper etiquette before Allah, fostering deep repentance, and balancing worldly needs with spiritual aspirations. The session emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the afterlife, the mercy of the Divine, and the necessity of maintaining a strong connection with the Imam of the time.
content:
His name was Abu Hamza al-Thumali, Thabit ibn Dinar. The fourth Imam (a.s.) had pointed out the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) to Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says he was the Salman of his time. Imam Rida (a.s.) says he was the Luqman of his time. Imam (a.s.) says, 'O Rida, when you return, go to Abu Hamza and convey my greetings to him.' Indeed, the one who receives the certification from the Sadiq of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) that 'Yes, he truly loves us, he is our Shia,' then what else is there in the world? That is why his status and rank are strange and unique, and that is why he was chosen, which is understood from these things. That is why he was chosen for the teaching of such a great supplication, which, if a person truly reads with a sincere heart—these are the words of the fourth Imam (a.s.)—in which the Imam has described such secrets of monotheism, has described such a relationship between a servant and the Worshipped, the fourth Imam (a.s.) has described how a servant's humility and Allah's self-sufficiency are. The Imam taught how a person should beg and pray before Allah. The method of supplication, although the name of this supplication is Dua-e-Sahar... The method, although the name of this supplication is Dua-e-Sahar, Dua-e-Abu Hamza al-Thumali, but it is famous by the name of this famous companion. Now, just a few phrases, let us turn our attention towards this supplication. The Hadith which was chosen at the beginning of this discussion, the Hadith which was chosen: 'There is no drop more beloved to Allah the Almighty than a drop of blood in the darkness of the night, out of fear of Allah, which no one sees.' A drop of a tear, not blood, 'in the darkness of the night, which comes out in the fear of Allah.' A drop of a tear that no one sees, and that person, the servant who is weeping out of fear of Allah, behind this weeping there is no purpose, only and only Allah. His intention, his resolve is only and only Allah, no one else except Allah. When a servant reads this Dua-e-Abu Hamza al-Thumali... No, when a servant recites this Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali with sincerity of heart and sincerity of intention, their state becomes truly unique. It is such a strange and wonderful supplication, and it even elevated the companion to such a status that this Dua was attributed to his name. Regarding this Dua, Sheikh Tusi (may Allah have mercy on him) mentions it in his Misbah al-Mutahajjid. He narrates that Ali ibn al-Husayn, Sayyid al-Abidin (peace be upon him), the Fourth Imam (peace be upon him), used to spend most of the night in the month of Ramadan in prayer and supererogatory acts. But when the time of Sahar (dawn) arrived, he would present himself before Allah through this Dua, Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. What is this Dua? If we reflect on a few of its words, how does it begin? It begins like this: 'O Allah, do not discipline me by giving me punishment.' What strange and wonderful phrases! 'And do not plot against me.' Because this has also been alluded to in the Quran, that people plot—people plan—they make plans. People make plans, but against them, Allah also has a plan, and Allah is the best of planners. Then the Imam says, 'My Lord, my Sustainer, from where can goodness come to me? And where will I find it except through You?' The goodness I possess is what You have given me; I have nothing of my own. 'How will I find salvation, O Lord? There is no means of salvation for me except through You; salvation can only be attained through You.' Then, how should a servant praise and glorify Allah? The Fourth Imam says through this Dua, 'All praise is due to Allah, for when I call upon Him, He hears my prayer and answers it.' This is also taken from the Quranic verse where the Almighty commanded, 'Call upon Me, I will answer you.' The Fourth Imam (peace be upon him) is praising and glorifying Allah, saying, 'All praise is to You, my Lord, that whenever I called upon You, You answered.' But this is my Lord. You answered, but what was my condition? 'But whenever You called me, I delayed.' I procrastinated in answering Your call. And we see in our daily lives, especially when it comes to opportunities for worship, particularly if we talk about prayer, how much do we care about the timely performance of prayer? The Fourth Imam (peace be upon him) says, 'My Lord, when You call me, I delay; I procrastinate in coming to Your presence.' 'All praise is due to Allah, for whenever I asked Him for something, He granted it, but when He demanded something from me, I was negligent.' 'All praise is due to Allah, for whenever I called upon anyone for my needs, I called upon You, my Lord.' The Dua continues, 'All praise is due to Allah...' There are phrases like this: 'All praise is due to Allah who expressed love to me while He was independent of me.' He does not need my love; He does not need anything. He does not need anything from me, yet despite that, He expresses love to me, that Lord. 'All praise is due to Allah who tolerates me, my God, as if I had never committed a sin.' He keeps tolerating me. Then the Dua continues. Further on, the Fourth Imam (peace be upon him) taught the method of asking from Allah, how one should ask in the presence of Allah. The Imam says, 'And O my Master, among Your attributes, it is not befitting—never, never does it befit You—that You command me to ask, but then deprive me and leave me empty-handed. That does not befit You, my Lord. Or if I am asking You for something, I am certain, my Lord, that You will give, You will grant, otherwise, You would not have given me the opportunity to be present in Your court. If You have given me this grace to come to Your court and ask, it means You will grant.' 'But what is my condition, my Master? I am asking You in what state? With a tongue that has been made dumb by sins.' I am not worthy, I do not deserve that... I do not deserve to come to Your court and ask You for anything because I have committed so many sins with this tongue. 'With what face should I come to You?' 'So, my Master, when I look at my sins, I tremble; I tremble and shake.' 'But when I observe Your grace, when I look towards Your grace, hope awakens in me; hope is born that yes, You are the one who will forgive me.' 'So, if You forgive me, my Lord, then You are the best of those who show mercy. And if You punish me, even then, You are not unjust, my Lord.' The Fourth Imam (peace be upon him) is teaching the way to ask, how a human should bow before Allah and ask. And then, one part of this Dua is also the confession of one's sins. The Imam taught how to confess one's sins before the Almighty. What is the phrase of the Dua? 'You keep covering my sins by virtue of Your grace.' 'And You tolerate me so much that You do not punish me; You delay the punishment.' 'So all praise is to You, my Lord.' All praise is to You, my Lord. Knowing everything, You still tolerate me. 'And You have the power, You have full authority to punish me, but You forgive me.' But this forgiveness of Yours, this covering of my sins—You keep covering my sins from the eyes of the people, You do not expose my sins before people. The Fourth Imam says, the next phrase is a strange and wonderful phrase: 'And because You tolerate me, even more audacity to commit sins is born in me.' Allahu Akbar! He is tolerating in such a way as if the human had never committed a sin. Despite all these sins, the next part of the Dua is about how immense and boundless Allah's grace is. The Imam says, 'You keep expressing love to us by giving us blessings, while we respond by committing sins.' 'The things that reach us from You are only goodness and goodness.' 'But the things that reach Your court from us...' The things that reach Your court from us are only and only evils. 'And the noble angel who writes our deeds, who is appointed by Allah for us, he always goes to You...' When he goes to You with our record of deeds, there is nothing in it but evils. 'But despite this, my Lord, nothing stops You from showering us with Your blessings.' Despite all these things, my Lord, You keep giving us blessings, You keep giving. 'You keep surrounding us completely with Your blessings.' Then, look at another part of this Dua—strange and wonderful phrases in this Dua. Praying for parents, Abu Hamza al-Thumali taught. Praying for the believers, you will find in this Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. If you want the good of this world and the hereafter, you will find it in this Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. If you want the grace of Hajj and Ziyarat, you will find it in this Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Look at the phrase regarding the forgiveness of parents: 'O Allah, forgive my parents.' Forgive them. 'The good deeds they did for me, in return for those good deeds, O Lord, do good to them. And my Lord, if any sins were committed by them, forgive them.' 'O Allah, forgive the believing men and women.' This is all a prayer for the believers. 'O Allah, forgive those of us who are remaining, who are alive. And have mercy on those who have passed away from this world, forgive them.' 'Have mercy on those who are present, and have mercy on those who are not present, and forgive them.' 'Have mercy on our men and women, our young and our old, our free and our slaves.' 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' You see, again and again, after every little while in this Dua, you will find Salawat (blessings). This in itself is sufficient for the acceptance and loftiness of this Dua, that in short intervals, Salawat is found within this Dua. It is a prayer for the good of this world and the hereafter. 'O Lord, make my end good.' Make my end good, meaning upon goodness, meaning upon Wilayah (guardianship of Ahlulbayt). 'Let my end be upon goodness.' My Lord, if I depart from this world, may I rise with the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (peace be upon them). 'And suffice me for the most important things in my world and my hereafter.' Grant me only those things. 'And do not let anyone be imposed upon me who will never have mercy on me.' This is very important for the world, very important. This thing often happens to us; many people have observed this, that people of the world keep us troubled. In the smallest of tasks, people trouble us; that work cannot be done. Why? Because the person in front has more power, more capability, more authority from a worldly perspective. So, what does he do? He suppresses the believers and oppresses them. The Fourth Imam is saying through this Dua, the Imam is teaching what to ask: 'My Lord, do not impose upon me anyone who will never have mercy on me.' And then, if you want abundance in sustenance, you will find it in this Dua. 'And grant me the Hajj of the House of Allah, its sustenance.' Or Hajj is a sustenance. 'Every year, my Lord, grant me this sustenance of Hajj.' 'And the Ziyarat of the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).' Grant me, and the Ziyarat of the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). 'My Lord, grant me the sustenance of the honor of visiting Your Prophet.' 'Do not ever keep me away from those holy courts, O Lord, from those noble places.' If you want the grace of Hajj and Ziyarat, Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Praying for parents, Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Praying for the believers, Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. If you want the good of this world and the hereafter, Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Then, after that, there is a strange and wonderful part of the Dua in which a human declares his helplessness, how helpless I was, and despite that, how my Lord had mercy on me. The Imam says, 'I was small, You nurtured me. I was ignorant, You taught me, You granted me knowledge. I was astray, You guided me. I was low, You elevated me. I am nothing, my Lord.' Despite all these things, what is my condition? 'I, O my Lord, my Sustainer, the one who did not fear You while committing sins in solitude, I kept committing sins shamelessly, and I did not feel any shame. And I did not see You in the gathering, to the extent that I went so far in sins that even to commit sins in a crowded gathering...' In the crowded gathering of the world, I did not even refrain from sinning for a moment; I was not afraid. 'Ana sahibu dhalika'—I am the one who, in front of my Sayyid, my Master, my Lord, stood boldly and continued to sin. 'Ana al-jari'—I sinned before the One who shakes and terrifies the heavens. 'Ana alladhi'—O Lord, I fell to such a level that I even gave bribes to commit sins. It is a strange sentence from the Mawla. When a person reaches such a state while remembering the stages of the grave and the Day of Judgment, and when he sees what his final moments will be like, the Fourth Imam (a.s.) brings us to this stage where, after reaching it, the human being has nothing left but to weep and cry out in the court of Allah. And the human being weeps and cries out: 'Fama li la abki'—Why should I not weep? 'Abki li khuruji nafsi'—I am weeping remembering the time when my soul will depart from my body, when my spirit will be seized. 'Abki li zulmati qabri'—I weep remembering the darkness of my grave. 'Abki li su'ali Munkar wa Nakir'—I weep remembering the time, O Lord, when my grave will press me. O Lord, when my grave will press me, I will experience the pressure of the grave. 'Abki li su'ali Munkar wa Nakir'—Munkar and Nakir will question me. I will be questioned about everything I did throughout my life. And then, I weep remembering the Day of Judgment, that when I am raised, 'urayyanan dhalilan'—naked, humiliated, drowned in my sins, facing disgrace and shame, I will be raised. My book of deeds will be given behind my back because my sins are so many. 'Anzuru marratan yamini wa shimali'—I will look to my right and to my left, hoping to find some help, someone to assist me. But when I look, everyone will be in their own state. These are strange and amazing things, and these are the means to bring a human being closer to their Lord. Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali is such a masterpiece of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), of the Fourth Imam (a.s.), that everything a human needs to get closer to their Lord is present in this supplication. Therefore, it is our responsibility to try to recite this supplication as much as possible during the blessed month of Ramadan. If you cannot recite the whole supplication at once, then... If you cannot recite the whole supplication at once, then recite it in parts—divide it into two or three parts. But it should not be that the entire month of Ramadan passes and we remain indifferent to this great supplication. It should be observed, and especially, this supplication should be recited collectively. And an effort should be made to recite some sentences with their translation, because it is a long supplication, so each time, the translation of different sentences should be presented to the people so that they become familiar with this supplication and love for it grows in our hearts. Why? Because it is the right of both Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) and Abu Hamza al-Thumali upon us. Such a great supplication has reached us that we should not forget it. And finally, always remember that if we get the opportunity to recite this supplication today, the cause and means of this opportunity is the Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Therefore, at the beginning of this supplication and after finishing it, definitely pray for the reappearance of your Imam, saying: 'O Lord, all these things that I have asked for in this Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali, if You do not consider me worthy of having even one of them accepted in my favor... If You do not consider me worthy of having even one of these things accepted in my favor, then just accept one thing: for the sake of this Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali, for the sake of these words that were issued from the blessed tongue of the Fourth Imam (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time. Grant us all the opportunity to be counted among his sincere servants, and grant us the opportunity to remain steadfast on his Wilayah until our last breath. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive overview of the life and spiritual significance of Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) as the primary protector and guardian of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Through Quranic exegesis and historical analysis, the session explores how Abu Talib's unwavering support and devotion were instrumental in the early success of the Islamic mission. The lecture also emphasizes the divine status of his guardianship and the theological importance of his faith, culminating in a competitive quiz to reinforce these historical and religious teachings.
content:
TSR presents. What should I tell you, what is Abu Talib's? Oh, I swear by the Lord of the Kaaba, the Kaaba belongs to Abu Talib. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside in Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Guardian of the Age, reach us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Infinite praise to that Great and Exalted God who kept us all attached to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Blessings and peace be upon the pride of the Prophets and Messengers, the cause of the creation of the universe and Adam, the means of guidance and salvation for the children of Adam. The intercessor of the Day of Judgment, Ahmad-e-Mustafa, Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), and upon his pure and immaculate family. Respected listeners, 29th Shawwal, which is the day of the auspicious birth of Hazrat Imran ibn Abdul Muttalib, i.e., Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.). Come, first of all, let us offer congratulations for this blessed day in the court of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) through a Salawat. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum wal'an a'daahum ajma'in. And we also offer congratulations and greetings to all of you for this blessed day. And we welcome you all to our grand quiz today, i.e., the Mohsine-e-Islam Grand Quiz by the TSR team, which is the fifth round today. Let us begin today's discussion. With these four lines: I took upon myself hardships and nurtured wounds in my heart, I took upon myself hardships and nurtured wounds in my heart, but I attained the priceless springs of Islam. And why do you seek the Kalima from Abu Talib? Why do you seek the Kalima from Abu Talib? While he is the one who did not just attain the Kalima, but attained the prayers. While he is the one who did not just attain the Kalima, but attained the prayers. Respected audience, the noble personality of Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) is that great personality that, although many people perform good deeds, from Janab-e-Adam until the Day of Judgment, people have done good deeds and will continue to do so. But the good deed of Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) is that good deed which he performed alongside the one who is the Master of the Universe, who is the Chief of the Messengers, who is the Seal of the Prophets, who is the Intercessor of the Day of Judgment, for whose sake God created this universe. So who can estimate the value of that virtue? What must be the greatness of that virtue? Namely, Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) provided support to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) during his orphanhood. He raised him, he took care of him. And not just that—that the care was only during his childhood. Even when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) proclaimed his Prophethood, there too, Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) stood by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) like a shield. So much so that until his very last breath, Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) did not leave the side of the Messenger of Allah. Respected audience, the topic of our discussion today is how Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) took care of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And we will divide this into three parts. Namely, first: how the care provided by Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) is mentioned in the Holy Quran. Second: how the care began, and how Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) fulfilled the duty of guardianship. So, respected audience, please listen to this discussion carefully and attentively so that you can answer all the questions asked about it correctly. And before moving forward in the discussion, let us take a look at the rules of our quiz, and Insha'Allah, after that, we will begin our discussion. These are the poems of Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) from which the support and guardianship of Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) are clearly understood, in what manner it was regarding the Prophet, and what his belief was in the religion of Islam and the religion brought by the Messenger of Allah, that he considered this religion to be the best in the world. Respected listeners, the way Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) comforted the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) here, as you have just heard, and the things he expressed in the form of poetry, clearly show and reflect what the belief of Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) was, what his faith was. That is, first of all, he begins by swearing by Allah. After that, he expresses the verse of the Holy Quran in the form of poetry. After that, he gives the Messenger of Allah glad tidings of success, that in this command you have received, your eyes will be cooled, meaning you will be successful, and he considered the religion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to be the best religion. So let us now move towards the final part of our topic. Here we saw how Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) supported the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the propagation of the message. Now let us see how, in his final days and in his will, Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) is fulfilling the guardianship of the truth. When Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) was in the final days of his life and was making his will to his relatives and his tribesmen, even at that time, regarding the Messenger of Allah, Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) made a will in this way: 'Wa usikum bi-Muhammadin khairan'—I mean, after many wills regarding religion, good character, and the Kaaba, as a leader to his relatives and tribesmen, he was making a will regarding the Messenger of Allah. 'Wa usikum bi-Muhammadin khairan'—I advise you well regarding Muhammad. 'Fa-innahu aminun fil Quraishi'—For he is indeed the trustworthy one among the Quraish. 'Wa siddiqun fil Arabi'—And the most truthful person among the Arabs. 'Wa huwal jami'u likulli ma ausaitukum bihi'—And all that I have advised you about before, these good qualities are found in him and are gathered in him. So, even while bidding farewell to this world, Janab-e-Abu Talib (a.s.) was expressing the immense, boundless love he had in his heart for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and was advising people towards him, that it is necessary for people to take care of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). May the blessings of Allah be upon Muhammad and his pure, immaculate, and infallible progeny, and may the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies. Respected audience, if we reflect here, the will that Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) made in his final moments, in that will, he gave instructions regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that he should be taken care of. And if we look, then when a person makes a will in their final moments, they express only that which is closest to their heart, that which holds the greatest importance for them. So, making a will regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) here is proof of how close the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was to the heart of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.), how much he respected him, and what importance he held in the life of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.). And this has been the tradition of the Banu Hashim family; if you look at Janab Abdul Muttalib (a.s.) when he was making his will, he also made a will regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and then after him, when one reflects on the will of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.), he also makes a will regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). So, respected dear ones, this was our discussion regarding Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) and how he fulfilled the guardianship of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). That is, throughout his entire life, from the moment Janab Abdul Muttalib made a will to Janab Abu Talib regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), until the final moments of his life, how he fulfilled the right of guardianship. And not only that, but throughout his life, the religion that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) preached, the religion he brought, Janab Abu Talib continued to protect that religion during his life and, if we reflect, even after his life. Even if Janab Abu Talib is not physically present, his blood remained engaged in its protection. So much so that Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.) is also from the lineage of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.), through whom the Almighty God will fill this world with justice and equity just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. So, let us pray in the Divine Court that He hastens the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.) and counts us all among his helpers and supporters, and by following the path of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.), may He grant us the ability to spend our lives in the service of the Proof of God. title: #5 - Imam Husain (a.s.) Aur Hifaazat -e- Deen | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of Imam Husayn (a.s.) as a protector and leader of the Islamic faith, as highlighted in the Ziyarat of Arba'een. The speaker emphasizes that while the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) laid the foundation of Islam, Imam Husayn's sacrifice at Karbala was essential for its survival and preservation. The discourse concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and a commitment to upholding the true teachings of the faith.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr (Guardian of the Age), assist us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. In the Ziyarat of Arba'een, Allah the Almighty has designated Imam Husayn (a.s.) as a leader and a commander. In this Ziyarat, we recite: 'And You have made him a master among masters, a leader among leaders, and a defender among defenders.' You appointed him as a master among masters, a guide among guides, and a protector among the protectors of the religion. Allah the Almighty bestowed divine leadership upon Imam Husayn (a.s.) in various ways. Your grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), is the Sayyid al-Anbiya (Master of the Prophets). Your noble father is the master of all successors and Imams (a.s.). Your mother, the Princess Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.), is the mistress of the women of the worlds. Your elder brother, Imam Hasan (a.s.), and you are the masters of the youth of Paradise. Your own title is Sayyid al-Shuhada (Master of the Martyrs), meaning you are the leader of all those who are martyred in the path of God. From your lineage, nine Imams are the guides, leaders, and Imams of their time. As for the protection of the religion, it is essential to know that two things are vital for the survival of anything: a good foundation and strong protection. The foundation of the religion of Islam was laid by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). But if Imam Husayn (a.s.) had not offered his sacrifice in Karbala, the religion of Islam would have been completely destroyed and ruined. Imam Husayn (a.s.) provided such a defense of Islam that no one before or after him could match. Yes, it is necessary to state that whatever outward form and teachings of Islam remain today, it is solely because of Imam Husayn (a.s.), for Imam Husayn (a.s.) is the soul of Islam. O God, for the sake of that true religion of Islam for which Hazrat Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (a.s.) sacrificed everything, hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the ability to follow this true Ghadiri religion until our last breath. Amen, O Lord of the worlds. O Imam, accept our devotion to the religion... O my beloved, and the beloved of those who sacrifice for you, O Husayn.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 7 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) & The Holy Quran - Part 1
excerpt: This webinar explores the profound connection between the Holy Quran and Imam Mahdi, emphasizing their role as the inseparable guides for humanity. The session highlights the spiritual necessity of recognizing the Imam of the time and the duty of believers to prepare for his reappearance through moral development and knowledge. Furthermore, it addresses contemporary societal challenges, including corruption and political instability, while grounding the discussion in the Quranic promise of ultimate justice and divine victory for the oppressed.
content:
Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We will begin this seventh session, and I welcome all of you. I welcome all of you to this seventh session. We are grateful to Allah (SWT) that He has given us the opportunity to continue this series in this blessed month, regarding the Holy Quran, and we thank those who have helped with the books and the two or three reciters. We thank you, and through your prayers, we begin today's session with the recitation of the Holy Quran. To make it blessed, we have with us the respected Maulana Asad Abbas Khan Sahab. Let us welcome him with a Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. And he will recite... [Recitation of Quranic verses in Arabic] [Recitation of Quranic verses in Arabic] [Recitation of Quranic verses in Arabic]. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Indeed, Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. Continuing our daily routine, today's Hadith regarding 'Bismillah' is from the book 'Wasa'il al-Shia', Volume 1, page 219, Hadith number 250. It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Man qara'a Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'—whoever recites Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim... 'Man qara'a Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim', Allah writes 4,000 good deeds for every letter for that person, erases 4,000 sins, and elevates them by 4,000 degrees. This is for every letter of Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. A person can estimate for themselves: if a person recites Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, for every letter, 76,000 good deeds will be added to their record, 76,000 sins will be erased, and 76,000 degrees will be elevated. This is what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has said. With this, we move forward with today's session. Regarding the subject we are discussing, there is a tradition recorded from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) which mentions the 'Masoom' (infallible). The Masoom is one who holds firmly to the Book of Allah, and Allah holds firmly to him. It has been mentioned previously that in one instance, the 'Thaqalayn' (two weighty things) refers to the Quran and the Ahlulbayt. As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, they will never separate from each other until the Day of Judgment. The Imam is the one who guides towards the Quran, and the Quran guides towards the Imam. Our topic today is Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and on this extremely important occasion, On this extremely important occasion, joining us for this discussion is the respected Maulana Syed Naseer Abbas Rizvi. May Allah keep him safe. How are you? I hope you and your family are well. Alhamdulillah, we are grateful to you for joining this program. I request everyone to send their questions related to this topic to the WhatsApp number displayed on the screen, [number removed]. Please try to send your questions as early as possible so that we do not miss them due to time constraints. Alhamdulillah, we are live now. We are grateful to Allah for this opportunity. As we continue our discussion on the topic, we are focusing on the Imam of our time. It is essential for people to recognize the Imam of their time. We have started our series on this, and we hope you will subscribe to our channel to stay updated. Regarding this verse, our second point... Regarding this verse, our second point is that it points towards the status that Allah the Almighty has bestowed upon certain people. In the Holy Quran, the answer is given to those who ask why Allah created these individuals. It is not merely for the sake of creation; there is a divine purpose and a specific status assigned to them. For more information, one can refer to the verses where the Quran mentions two things. When one opens the Quran, it speaks of Allah (s.w.t.) and the 'Nur' (Light) He has appointed. Who is that Nur? It is our love, the love of Allah and His Messenger. For 14,000 years, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has spoken about who will come after him. He has stated that after him, there is Ali (a.s.) and the Imams. Where are the people now? We must follow the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). As mentioned in the traditions, we must recognize the Imam of our time. After the Prophet, it is the leadership of Ali (a.s.) and the Imams of the Ahlulbayt. It is the leadership of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If we do not recognize them, we cannot truly follow the Quran. We must study our books and teach our children about the Ahlulbayt so that they are well-informed. We must ensure our children know about the Imam. He was born in 255 AH, his father passed away in 260 AH, and his occultation began in 329 AH. There were four deputies during the minor occultation. We must strive to gain knowledge about the Imam of our time. It is necessary to understand the Quran and the Imam, as they are inseparable. We should ask ourselves: how many of us truly know our Imam? We should be preparing ourselves for his reappearance. We should remember him in our daily lives. If we claim to be his followers, we must prove it through our actions. We talk about our families, but do we talk about our Imam? Today is the time to reflect on our relationship with the Imam of our time. Some people ask, 'Will those who do not recognize the Imam be included among his followers?' Those who do not recognize the Imam will not be included among his followers. We must prove our loyalty. We should prepare our children for the battlefield of faith, whether it is through knowledge, character, or devotion. This is our need, and we must strive to uphold the path of the Imam. We should sacrifice everything—our lives, our mothers, our families, our honor, and everything we possess. Just as there should be love for a mother in our hearts, in the same way, if the Imam (a.s.) is hidden from our sight for even a few moments, we should become restless. We should be desperate to find him. We should be lost in this love. When people are truly in love, they wait for a sign. If you are told that someone is coming, you would be restless, wouldn't you? If you are told that the Imam (a.s.) is coming, tell me, who would be more beloved than him? If you truly love him, you will understand that this world is nothing. You know, this world is nothing compared to the love of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny. After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), it is their path that is the true path. It is the path of guidance. We call ourselves the followers of the Imam (a.s.). Peace be upon the Imam of the time. He is the master of the universe. Think like a believer, think like a follower. If the master of the universe is the owner of everything, and he is even closer to us than our own souls, then it means he is more concerned for us than our own selves. He is the most compassionate, and his family is the most compassionate. This does not mean that when we read about them, we just read words. If you look towards Ali (a.s.), you see a crowd of people around him like moths around a flame. This means that it was difficult to be the first one to follow him, but those who did were his true companions. You must show your loyalty; you must show your devotion. There should be no party-based politics; the love for the Imam (a.s.) should be supreme. Until we leave this world, we will not be separated from them. Until we reach that point, we must remain steadfast. And this is not just about us; it is about our families as well. We are not here just for ourselves. If we understand that the Imam (a.s.) is more compassionate to us than we are to ourselves, then we must entrust our lives and our families to him. We must live our lives according to his guidance. Living a life based on his guidance means that we must avoid what is forbidden. It is not just about words; it is about actions. After the mention of the Imam (a.s.), the Holy Quran says that Allah has promised those who have believed and done righteous deeds that He will grant them authority on earth. This is a sign pointing towards the Imam (a.s.). It is not about being entangled in the webs of this world, but about being truly guided. It is a promise from Allah that just as He granted authority to those before us, He will grant it to the believers. Allah promises that if we perform righteous deeds, He will make us successors on earth. He will establish the religion that He has chosen for us. He will replace our fear with security. This is the promise of Allah. Our duty is to prepare for his arrival. When will this happen? It is not for us to decide; it is in the hands of Allah. The Holy Quran does not speak of the past alone; it speaks of the future. Our intention should be to strengthen the oppressed. Those who were made weak on earth will be made leaders. When they rise, they will be the ones who establish justice. Allah keeps the believers under His protection. Through the guidance of the Imam (a.s.), you are being prepared. The Quran says that Allah will surely help those who help His cause. If you do any work for His sake, He will reward you. If you walk on this path, a wall of protection will be built around you. His power is absolute. Everything is under His control. If you are with the Imam (a.s.), you are under the protection of Allah. If you are with the Imam (a.s.), you will be successful. These two groups—the followers of the Imam (a.s.) and his enemies—are in conflict. The Quran says that among these two groups, the one that is on the path of truth will be victorious. Those who are with the Imam (a.s.) are the ones who are truly guided. Those who are with the Imam (a.s.) are the ones who will be protected. We will not let their homes be destroyed. It is known from the Quran that the family of Abu Sufyan and the family of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) are two different paths. title: Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ki Wilaadat Par Iblees (l.a.) Ki Mayoosi  | رسول (ص) کی ولادت پر ابلیس کی مایوسی
excerpt: This lecture details the miraculous events surrounding the birth of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) as narrated by Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.). It describes how the birth caused the heavens to be barred to Iblis, idols to fall, and the palace of Kisra to tremble. The talk highlights the significance of this event in shifting the spiritual landscape of the world and notes Iblis's subsequent focus on leading the Prophet's Ummah astray.
content:
Iblis, upon whom is the curse of Allah, called his devils, and when they came to him, the devils asked, "What has frightened you, O our leader?" Iblis said, "Woe be upon you, since last night I have been unable to access the other heavens and the earth. Surely, an event has occurred on this earth that has not happened since Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (a.s.) was raised to the heavens. Go and find out what this event is." A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim, Bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim. Wa salla Allahu 'ala wali al-'asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. Allahumma salli 'ala... In the book 'Bihar al-Anwar', a tradition is narrated from Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.) in the Amali of Sheikh Saduq. The Imam says: "Iblis, may Allah's curse be upon him, used to traverse the seven heavens, but when Isa (a.s.) was born, he was barred from three heavens, and he could only traverse four heavens." Iblis, may Allah's curse be upon him, used to go to the seven heavens, and when Isa (a.s.) was born, three doors of the heavens were closed to him; he was veiled. Now he only had access to four out of the seven heavens. The Imam further says: "When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was born, he was barred from all seven." When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was born, all the doors of the heavens were closed to this accursed one. "And the devils were pelted with stars." That is, O viewers, the purpose for which stars are used is to strike the devils, not to ride upon them. Anyway, the hadith continues. The people of Quraish said, "The time of the Hour (Qiyamah) has arrived, about which we used to hear from the People of the Book." Amr bin Umayyah, who was a famous astrologer in the days of ignorance, said, "Look at the stars that show the way and through which you know the seasons of winter and summer. If those stars have been struck, it means that the Hour has arrived, and if those stars remain, it means that some new event must have occurred on earth." Many events took place on the day of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) birth. Imam Jafar as-Sadiq (a.s.) describes them in this tradition as follows: "There was no idol but that it fell face down." In the places of worship, there was no idol that did not fall face down. "And the palace of Kisra (Chosroes) shook that night, and fourteen of its towers fell." That night, the palace of Kisra began to tremble and fourteen of its towers collapsed. "And the lake of Sawa dried up, and the valley of Samawa overflowed." The lake of Sawa dried up and the river in the valley of Samawa flooded. These are all the events that occurred on that night when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was born. "And the fires of Fars (Persia) were extinguished, which had not been extinguished for a thousand years before that." The fire temple of Fars, which had not been extinguished for thousands of years, was extinguished that night. "And the Mobedan (chief priest) saw in his dream that night some difficult camels leading Arabian horses." The Mobedan, who was a leader of Fars, saw in his dream that night that some camels were entering their borders, the borders of Fars, and they were leading horses. That is, these camels were leading the horses, and they had crossed the Tigris River and entered their borders, the borders of Fars. "And the crown of the King of Kisra split in the middle." That night, the crown of the King of Kisra split into two from the middle. "And the Tigris River burst its banks, and water entered the city." And the dam of the Tigris River broke and water entered the city. "And a light spread from the direction of Hijaz that night, then it flew until it reached the East." A light began to spread from Hijaz, until it reached the East. "And there remained no throne for any king of the world but that it became overturned." And there was no king in the world whose throne did not overturn that night. "And there remained no throne for any king of the world but that it became overturned." There was no king in the world whose throne did not overturn that night. "And the king became mute and could not speak that day." And every king became mute that day and was unable to say anything. "And the knowledge of the soothsayers was snatched away, and the magic of the magicians was invalidated, and there remained no soothsayer among the Arabs but that he was veiled from his companion." That night, the knowledge of the soothsayers was snatched away and the magic of the magicians was rendered ineffective. The soothsayers of the Arabs were abandoned by their companions. "And the status of Quraish increased among the Arabs, and they were called the Family of Allah (Aal-Allah)." Then the Imam explains it this way, "Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said": "They were called the Family of Allah only because they resided in the Sacred House of Allah." Then Bibi Amina (s.a.) says, "Indeed, my son was born, by Allah, and he placed his hand on the earth, then raised his head towards the sky and looked, then a light shone from me and illuminated everything for him. From the light of that radiance, I heard someone saying: 'You have given birth to the master of the people, so name him Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).'" Then Hazrat Abdul Muttalib (a.s.) was brought so that he too could visit the child. When the news reached him of what the child's mother had described, he took the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) into his arms and said, "All praise is due to Allah who has granted me this pure and clean child, who is the master of all the worlds in his cradle." Then he entrusted the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to the pillars of the House of Kaaba and recited poetry in his honor. Then the Imam (a.s.) said, "Iblis, upon whom is the curse of Allah, called his devils, and when they came to him, the devils asked, 'What has frightened you, O our leader?' Iblis said, 'Woe be upon you, since last night I have been unable to access the other heavens and the earth. Surely, an event has occurred on this earth that has not happened since Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (a.s.) was raised to the heavens. Go and find out what this event is.' Then they scattered everywhere, but when they returned, they said, 'We saw nothing.' Iblis said, 'I will find out about this event myself.' Then he went to every corner of the world, until he reached the Haram, that is, the House of Kaaba. There he saw that the angels were guarding from every side. When he tried to enter, the angels stopped him. Then he went back. Then he tried to enter the Haram in the form of a creature like a bird. There, Jibra'il (a.s.) stopped him and said, 'Be gone, may the curse of Allah be upon you.' He said to him, 'I have one question for you, O Jibra'il.' Iblis said, 'O Jibra'il, just tell me one thing, what is this event that has occurred on earth since last night?' He said to him, 'Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has been born.' Jibra'il (a.s.) replied, 'Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has been born.' He said to him, 'Do I have any share in him?' This accursed one says, 'Will I be able to test any of my tricks on him?' He said, 'No.' Here, Jibra'il said, 'No.' He said, 'What about his Ummah?' He asks if he will be able to lead his Ummah astray. He said, 'Yes.' Jibra'il (a.s.) said, 'Yes.' He said, 'I am satisfied.' He left saying that he was satisfied with this. That is, O viewers, since the seven heavens were veiled for Iblis, and his access to the seven heavens was closed after the birth of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he will take revenge on this Ummah by spreading his devils on the earth and trying his best to lead the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) astray. Therefore, we should be cautious of this accursed one and always keep ourselves under the protection of the Imam of our time, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), and always keep ourselves under the protection of the Family of Muhammad (a.s.). This is it, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure, clean, and infallible family, and may the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 11 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture addresses common Fiqh questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting during the month of Ramadan. The speaker clarifies rulings on Ghusl-e-Janabat, the necessity of Tayammum when water is unavailable or harmful, and the consequences of forgetting to perform ritual purification. Additionally, the session covers the validity of fasting after breaking it due to necessity and provides clarity on the permissibility of using alcohol-based sanitizers and perfumes.
content:
Apart from... [unclear]... May Allah's blessings be upon the Prophet... Ramadan is called the month of the Quran, and we have been continuously reminding you that in this month, we should try our best to perform the recitation of the Quran. The recitation has been performed, and if we do not recite the Quran, then who will? Recitation is for everyone, and we do it. We should make daily recitation of the Quran our routine. In the previous episodes, we answered all your questions in very simple language, Alhamdulillah. Let us go once again and take some of your questions to his presence and seek answers. The first question that has come is: if it is not possible for a person to perform Ghusl-e-Janabat, or if water is not available, or if water is harmful, and the time for Fajr prayer arrives, then how should they keep the fast? [Response:] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. If water is not available, or if the time is short, or if water is harmful, then one must perform Tayammum. If one does not perform Tayammum, the prayer time will pass, and one cannot keep the fast. This is the ruling for such a person. If water is harmful, one should not use it. Using water when it is harmful would be wrong. It is better for him to perform Tayammum quickly. Regarding the question of whether I can drink water after the Fajr Adhan if I have already broken my fast, or if I have to make up for it... if you are in a state where you cannot bear the thirst, then you can drink water, but only as much as is necessary. If you drink water, your fast will break, but you must wait. It is not that you have found an opportunity and can eat and drink as much as you want. You must observe the sanctity of the day. You will have to make up for the fast later. Because it was a necessity, there is no sin, but you must make up for it. The third question is: if I made a mistake and forgot to perform Ghusl-e-Janabat, and two or three days passed, will those days be valid? If you forgot to perform Ghusl-e-Janabat, then your fasts for those two or three days are invalid. After three days, you realized that you were not in a state of purity. So, for the days you acted in that state, your fasts are not valid, and you must make up for them. You cannot perform the fast without making up for the missed ones. There are two scenarios: one, if the person did not know about the obligation of Ghusl, then the fast might be valid. But if they knew and forgot, they must make up for it. The fourth question is: if I had made a vow (nadhr) to fast on the 15th of Shaban, and I forgot, what should I do? If you made a vow, you must fulfill it. If you missed it, you must make up for it. If it was a mandatory fast, you must perform it. Regarding the use of sanitizer and whether it contains alcohol: firstly, sanitizer does not contain pure alcohol; other things are mixed with it. When things are mixed and a new substance is formed, it is no longer considered alcohol. Even if there is alcohol, since it has transformed into a new substance, the rulings of alcohol do not apply to it. The result is that you are now against this, which is why our homes are as they are. In today's age, alcohol is divided into two types: one is the type of alcohol that is consumed, and the other is the type that is not. However, in contrast to this, they speak of 'industrial alcohol'. What does industrial alcohol mean? It means alcohol used in cleaning, medicine, or for personal use. Similarly, it is found in perfumes. In the past, it was said that applying perfume was not correct, but today, our scholars, based on this, have divided it. They say you can apply this perfume; there is no issue with it, and it has no effect. It has no effect. For those viewers who have not yet asked their questions, please send your questions to the WhatsApp number [number removed], and we will try our best to answer them. Dear viewers, I will call you in the next list. For now, goodbye.

If one breaks a fast due to extreme necessity, they must observe the sanctity of the day and make up the fast later.
Vows (nadhr) are binding and must be fulfilled or made up if missed.
Alcohol-based sanitizers and perfumes are generally considered permissible as the alcohol is industrial and chemically transformed.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 8 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture, part of an Ahkaam series, addresses common questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting in Islam. Maulana Zulfiqar Mehdi clarifies the rulings on making up missed fasts before the next Ramadan and the conditions under which a laborer may break their fast due to extreme hardship. The session also touches upon the importance of parental guidance in marriage and the proper timing for breaking the fast at sunset.
content:
Let's face it. Yes, hello. Um, that which was... [Arabic: La ilaha illallah]... [Arabic: ...]. During the time of confession, [Arabic: ...]. May Allah bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. In your field, friends, your consensus... [Arabic: ...]... first of all, in the park management, the president... In the park management, the president says that may He grant us the ability to perform good deeds in this blessed month. And when we go to His presence, may He grant us the ability to come and go. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and send such blessings upon all their pure descendants that cannot be counted, blessings that cover the creation, and may the heavens and the earth be filled. Of all those who show mercy, He is the most merciful. Send such blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and upon his pure family. Respected audience, today is the eighth or tenth class. Let us go to the presence of Maulana Zulfiqar Mehdi. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon you too. Tell us, what is the command of Allah? Tell us, what is the command of Allah? Allah the Almighty. The first question today—there are four questions—is about fasting. The question is: if someone has missed fasts, can they keep recommended (mustahab) fasts? [Arabic: Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim]... Peace be upon the Prophet... You were asking about the month of Ramadan, that apart from the blessed month of Ramadan, there is no other way... Apart from the month of Ramadan, there is no other way. Check. And your question is, is it necessary to keep the missed fasts of the previous year before the coming Ramadan, or can they be kept afterwards? This is quite clear: every missed fast must be completed before the next year. This must be completed. But now, regarding the clothes... look, all these rules... so remember, if you did this, you have two... If you did this, you have two, and there are other days as well. It is necessary to complete them before the last Ramadan. And then, it will be done, and there will be no such burden on you. It will not happen. But instead of Ramadan... to talk about it.
