title: EP06 | Zameen Par Hujjat-e-Khuda Na Ho to Kya Hoga? |  ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of the Imam as the 'Hujjat-e-Khuda' (Proof of God) on earth, even during periods of occultation. It emphasizes that the Imam serves as the spiritual soul of the universe, essential for maintaining the cosmic order and protecting the integrity of religious teachings. By acting as the ultimate standard of truth, the Imam ensures that the message of the Ahlulbayt remains uncorrupted against distortion and ignorance.
content:
They did it. This is the Ummah, this is the treatment they gave to the family of the Prophet. History is full of it. You should pick up history and read it. Look, our biggest problem is that we only act on hearsay. We do not read, we do not study history. Whereas Islam is the religion that is founded on 'Iqra' (Read). 'Iqra'. It started with Surah Iqra, didn't it? But this is the Ummah that 'la taqra', which does not read. We only act on hearsay. Read, study, and reflect on it, ponder over it, contemplate it, deliberate on it, think about what is written. What is the truth, what is falsehood? So the Imam says, "Zahirun ghayru muta'ayyin" (Manifest but not identifiable), come, "muktatibun yataraqqab" (hidden and in a state of waiting), meaning always in anticipation, always alert is the Imam. "In ghaba 'an an-nasi shakhsuhum fi hali hudnatihim" (Even if their person is hidden from the people during their time of truce), although his personality, that is, outwardly, physically, he is hidden, he is not among the people. "Fi hal-i hudnatihim" (In the state of their truce). The word 'hudna' in Arabic has several meanings. Hudna means tranquility, hudna means reconciliation, and hudna means weakness or frailty. There are various meanings for hudna. So, this is their state, the state of hudna. That is why he is hidden. "Falam yaghib 'anhum qadimu mabsusi 'ilmihim" (The ancient, spread-out knowledge of them is not hidden from them). The personality is hidden, but their ancient knowledge, which is spread throughout the universe, will not be hidden from the people. This means the Imam will manifest his knowledge among the people, albeit through selected individuals. Through selected individuals, this knowledge will be manifested, and this knowledge will spread. "Wa adabuhum fi qulubil mu'minina muthbatatun" (And their manners are established in the hearts of the believers). And the manners of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are established and firm in the hearts of the believers. Their manners, their character—this means that a true believer will follow the manners and character of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And they will be well-acquainted with their teachings. "Fahum biha 'amiluna" (And they act upon them). The believers act upon their manners and character. And what words of the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat) these are, the words of Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.), the words of the Gate of the City of Knowledge. "Wa innaka la tukhli ardaka min hujjatin laka" (And You do not leave Your earth without a proof for You). O Lord, You will never leave Your earth without a proof, Your proof; You will never leave it empty. The earth can never remain empty without the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda). "'Ala khalqika zahirun laysa bi muta'ayyin" (Manifest to Your creation, yet not clearly identified). Then the Mawla repeats it, "laysa bi muta'ayyin"—meaning he is manifest, but he is not obeyed. "Wa kha'ifun maghmurun kay la tabtula hujjataka" (And fearful and obscured, so that Your proof may not be invalidated). The existence of the Imam is necessary and essential so that Your proof is not invalidated. That Your proof may remain established. "Wa la yadilla awliya'uka ba'da idh hadaytahum" (And Your friends may not go astray after You have guided them). This is another benefit. Look at how many benefits are in one hadith. Look at the words of the Mawla in one hadith. And Your friends, meaning those who love the Imam, may not go astray after You have guided them. This is an interpretation of that verse of the Quran: "Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana" (Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us). Then after that, "Ba'da idh hadaytahum bal ayna hum wa kam hum" (After You have guided them; but where are they and how many are they?). Where are these individuals and how many are they? "Ula'ikal aqalluna 'adadan al-a'zamuna 'indallahi qadran" (They are the fewest in number but the greatest in status before Allah). These are the people who are few in number, but in the sight of Allah, their status and rank are very great. They possess a very magnificent status. And the hadith is very long; you can refer to it. So, this is one thing. Then another benefit of the Imam, this Proof of God, is that the Imam of the time is the Proof of God, and that is that the earth cannot remain for even a single moment without the Proof of God. Even for a single moment. A narration is reported from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), that is, Abu Hamza al-Thumali, whose name was Thabit ibn Dinar, whose supplication is famous—the Supplication of Abu Hamza al-Thumali which you recite in the month of Ramadan. So his name was Thabit ibn Dinar, and he asked the Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.), "Atabqal ardu bighayri imamin?" (Can the earth remain without an Imam?) "Qala 'alayhis salam" (He, peace be upon him, said), "Law baqiyatil ardu bighayri imamin lasakhat" (If the earth were to remain without an Imam, it would collapse/sink). If the earth were to be without an Imam, then the entire earth, rather the entire universe, would be destroyed, would perish. Meaning it would swallow everyone along with its inhabitants; no one would remain on the face of the earth. Look at the Proof of God; what I am presenting to you is to show that this position of Imamate is such a magnificent divine position. It is not, as I mentioned last time, a position where five people sit together and say, 'Let us appoint an Imam for ourselves.' Usually, we do not even easily accept a prayer leader (Pesh-e-Namaz), let alone that Imam who is "mansusun minallah" (appointed by Allah). Similarly, in another hadith, Imam Baqir (a.s.) says that "Law annal imama rufi'a minal ardi sa'atan" (If the Imam were removed from the earth for a moment), meaning if the Imam were removed from the earth for a single moment, "lamajat bi ahliha" (it would swallow its inhabitants). How? "Kama yamujul bahru bi ahlihi" (Just as the sea tosses its inhabitants). You must have seen that when there is a high tide, if someone is standing on the shore during high tide, when the big waves come, what do they do? They take along whoever is with them, whoever is standing there, they take them along. Whoever is standing there, no one can escape from its fury. From the fury of those waves. Similarly, if the glance of favor of the Proof of God were to be removed from the universe for a single moment, the entire universe would swallow its inhabitants in the same way, would take them away, just as this high tide takes away those standing on the shore during high tide. Is it possible? Is it possible that there is no Proof of God and yet the universe exists? This is not possible. This is because the Proof of God is before creation, with creation, and after creation. "Innal hujjata qablal khalqi wa ma'al khalqi wa ba'dal khalq" (Indeed, the Proof is before creation, with creation, and after creation). The Proof of God is together with it, rather it is before it and after it. In other words, the example of the Proof is like the example of the soul and the body. In light of the narrations, souls were created 2,000 years before bodies. "Khalaqallahu al-arwaha qablal ajsadi bi alfay 'am" (Allah created the souls 2,000 years before the bodies). So the soul and... Not 2,000 years of this world. It is not specified, it is not clear whether these are 2,000 years of the world or the hereafter, meaning 2,000 years of the afterlife. So this soul was before the body. The soul is with the body, and when the body ends, the soul remains. The body will end. Rather, whatever strength comes into the body, whatever power comes, and whatever perfections the body possesses, all this is because of that light which it receives from the soul. Because of the light that is received from the soul, these perfections are found in the body, and as soon as this soul is taken away, the human becomes dead and that body is taken and buried. The work of the body is finished because the soul has separated from its body. Then after that, the final benefit of the Proof of God—although there are many other benefits, but since we are keeping the discussion brief to conclude it here—is that because of the Proof of God, people do not go astray. Now look at the hadith, pay attention to the hadith. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: "Fi kulli khalafin min ummati 'adlun min ahli bayti" (In every generation after me, there will be a just one from my Ahlulbayt). In every generation, from my Ahlulbayt, and it is clear who the Ahlulbayt are: "Hum Fatimatu wa abuha wa ba'luha wa banuha" (They are Fatima, her father, her husband, and her sons). Only these, that is all; there is no one else besides them. My Ahlulbayt, meaning those Ahlulbayt upon whom charity (Sadaqah) is forbidden, they are the Ahlulbayt, only they. So from my Ahlulbayt, Allah will surely keep one scholar or another, meaning one who is just and knowledgeable, "Yanfi 'an hadhad dini tahrifal ghalina" (Who will repel from this religion the distortions of the extremists), who will keep this religion safe from the distortions, the deviations, and the corruptions of those who commit 'Ghulu' (exaggeration). Meaning, it is a responsibility of the Proof of God. The Proof of God will convey the truths to the people so that it becomes clear to them that this is a distortion, this is not correct, this thing is not right, this is 'Ghulu' (exaggeration), the distortion of the extremists. Meaning he will clarify that this is exaggeration. "Wa intihalal mubtilina" (And the false claims of the invalidators). And he will keep people safe from the beliefs of the people of falsehood. Meaning, it is the Imam of the time through whom clear proofs come before the people, and from which it is known that so-and-so is on the truth and so-and-so is on falsehood. The Imam is the one through whom the distinction is made between what is truth and what is falsehood. The Imam is the distinguisher; the Imam is the one who distinguishes and tells people, 'Look, this is truth, this is falsehood,' so that if ever any falsehood raises its head, the Imam clarifies to the people that this is falsehood, and the Imams do this. "Wa ta'wilal juhhali" (And the misinterpretations of the ignorant). And the Imams keep the religion safe from the interpretations of the ignorant. Meaning, in response to every Muhaddith Dehlavi, the Imam brings a Mir Hamid Hussain (r.a.), who responds in such a way and removes the falsehood, removes the invalidity, that then the falsehood cannot easily raise its head again. This happens through the support of the Imam, through the help of the Imam. So this is the work of the Proof of God. The rest, God willing, in the next episode. "Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin wa sallallahu 'ala muhammadin wa alihi al-tayyibina al-tahirina al-ma'sumina al-mazlumina wal la'nud da'imu 'ala a'da'ihim" (And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure, clean, infallible, and oppressed progeny, and may the eternal curse be upon their enemies).

The existence of the Imam is a fundamental requirement for the stability and survival of the universe.

At which places will the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) be useful to us? To shed more light on this, we have our brother Tanveer Deji Shah with us. Brother, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. Is everything fine? Alhamdulillah. As you heard the topic of this episode, how will the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) be useful to us in the Hereafter? In this world, the name of Ali (a.s.) is so useful that whenever we stumble or want to get up, 'Ya Ali Madad' comes out of our tongues spontaneously, and Ali (a.s.) reaches out to help us. So we want you to tell us how the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) will be useful in the Hereafter. Walaikum Assalam. InshaAllah, A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. First of all, I present my congratulations to the viewers on the auspicious occasion, and the question that you have asked, how will it be useful in the Hereafter, this is a... This question, how it will be useful in the Hereafter, is a very beautiful one. In today's era, when people are raising questions about Wilayat, it is similar to everything. It is similar that a person comes to the service of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and asks, 'Ya Rasulullah, what about the love of Ali (a.s.)?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied and said, 'Whoever loved Ali (a.s.) loved me, and whoever loved me loved Allah, and whoever loves Allah, Allah will never punish him.' That is, the best way to be saved from the punishment of Allah is the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). If we reflect on this Hadith, it shows that these questions being raised today are not new. These questions have been raised since the time of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). What will it tell us? Will it be useful to us? And when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told them, he rebuked them and told them that this is completely wrong, and today... Told them that this is completely wrong, and today, if anyone raises a question about it, one should understand that they do not see the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). This journey from this world to the Hereafter, the very first stage is death, and it is such a time where we... Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'Our lover, who keeps enmity with our enemies, that is, our lover, and he has enmity with our enemies, he will not face any trouble at that time until the Messenger of Allah, Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Hasan, and Imam Husain (a.s.) come to him.' Then they see him, that is, they see that person, and they give him glad tidings, they give him good news. But we find that if he is not our lover, then this dying person... that he will be tortured, and... The dying person... that he will be tortured, and he says that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) himself said to one of his companions, 'I come in the form of... there is no doubt for the believers in this world, except that I love them, whether they love me or...' And from the Hadith, some things come before us. First, every dying person, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Imam Ali (a.s.), and the Hasanain (a.s.) come to him. If he is a Mumin, they give him glad tidings, and it will be a place of happiness for him. But if he is a hypocrite, then their coming there will be a torture for him. Now it is up to us whether we want to be happy or sad to see the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) at our last moment. From this, I remembered that Paradise... Paradise is death, death is a meeting. So this was the second, when... When one meets death, this is the second stage. When a person leaves this world and their relatives lay them in the grave and depart, we all know—and every child among us knows—that at that moment, the questions are asked. If the deceased is a believer, they see that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and others are present in their grave. When they arrive, they first greet the Messenger of Allah and Imam Ali (a.s.), then they turn and greet the Imams Hasan and Husayn (a.s.) and whoever else is present. They say, 'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), we know this person is your follower, that is why you are in their grave.' But Allah has commanded us to question every deceased person; it is necessary for us to question them. Then they ask the questions, and when they answer all of them, they are told, 'You have lived and died upon this belief.' You have lived and died upon this belief, and you will be raised from this state. And Insha'Allah, there will be Allah's mercy in your grave. Now, tell me with justice—and we find in the Hadith that for a person, the most intense and difficult time is the first night in the grave. It is a stage that no human has ever seen before; it is completely unknown. If we go to a place where we do not know anyone, but we find someone there who knows that place very well, we feel a sense of relief. But if we find out that the place we have gone to, and the person who not only knows that place but is the owner of that place and has complete power over it, then how much relief and comfort will we feel? This is exactly what the Wilayah does. How beautifully it has been said: 'Before I even reached the grave, my high-ranking Master arrived; before my funeral even reached the grave, my Master came to my aid.' How my funeral came to my aid first—how the difficulty of death is eased for a person. It is not easy; death is difficult, and one has to face it. At that moment, the arrival of Ali (a.s.) himself and easing our death is a major problem solved for us. We also saw this when a person goes into the grave and faces the first night, which is the most painful and terrifying—this in itself is a great help. We have seen that the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) helps us from death until the grave. Let us see what else lies ahead and where else this Wilayah will be useful. Yes, the third stage is the Day of Judgment, and the Day of Judgment needs no explanation; every Muslim knows it exists. In the traditions, we find that when the Day of Judgment arrives, it will be asked, 'Where is the Caliph of Allah?' The Caliph on earth. Then Prophet Dawud (a.s.) will step forward, but at that moment, another voice will come, and it will be said, 'Indeed, you are the Caliph of Allah, but this is not the time for our meeting with you.' Here, it is... This is not the time for our meeting with you. It is necessary to say here that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will not just stand up and come forward; in the Quran, Allah addressed Prophet Dawud (a.s.) by the title of Caliph: 'O Dawud, We have made you a Caliph on earth.' Then Dawud (a.s.) will step forward, and after that, this call will come a second time: 'Where is the Caliph of Allah?' Then Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) will stand up. And after that, another voice will come: 'O people of the gathering, this is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), who is the Caliph of Allah on earth and the Proof over His servants.' And whoever held onto his rope firmly in the world, let them hold onto his rope firmly today, and they shall go with him, following him, to the high ranks of Paradise. Then some people will stand up and hold onto the hem of Imam Ali (a.s.) and go with him to the ranks of Paradise. That is, those who came to Amir al-Mu'minin... Those who came to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) with belief and were his followers, they will reach the ranks of Paradise following him. And it does not end here; after that, the command of Allah will come, and it will be said that whoever in this world considered anyone else as their Imam—meaning, leaving Imam Ali (a.s.) aside—they will be sent with that very Imam. That is, if we want to be with Imam Ali (a.s.) in the Hereafter, we must remain steadfast on his Wilayah in this world. If we have accepted someone else as our Imam, we will be raised with that same person in the Hereafter. And we can understand better that such a person who did not believe in the true Imam cannot go to Paradise. So, if they are going to Hell, we will go to Hell with them. Another thing worth noting here is that when Allah called His Caliph, Allah was not satisfied until Ali (a.s.) himself came forward. That is, Allah wants to tell the whole world that 'My Caliph is none other than this Ali.' And why shouldn't it be? Ali (a.s.) is the one who, throughout his entire life, always stepped forward for Islam; he never... Always stepped forward for Islam; he never retreated. So what will happen to them? Their lives will pass. At every moment, they said 'Labbayk' to the call of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and always prioritized Islam. After that, the next stage is the Reckoning. We all know that on the Day of Judgment, our deeds will be accounted for, and there is no one among us who can claim that they will enter Paradise based on their own deeds. So here, we find a Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in which he says that if anyone wants to pass like a swift wind and enter Paradise without any reckoning, they should love my Wali, my successor, my companion, my Caliph—that is, Imam Ali (a.s.). And if anyone wants to not go to Paradise, they should turn away from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.). A great way to avoid the reckoning is the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). A similar thing is found in a narration where it is stated that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)... When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, Allah said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I will not punish them as long as they do not wish to go to Hell.' The Messenger of Allah asked, 'Who would be such a person who wishes to go to Hell?' The answer was, 'This is the person who has the love of Ali (a.s.) in their heart.' If someone wants to go to Hell, there is an easy way for that. If we desire Paradise, it cannot be achieved without the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Indeed, the next stage—this is also a very important stage—and we all know this is the Mizan (the Scale), where our good and bad deeds will be weighed. And every person wants their scale of good deeds to be heavy on the Day of Judgment. Here too, the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) will be useful. We find a Hadith from our fifth Imam, Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), who says that the heaviest thing placed on the scale on the Day of Judgment will be the Salawat and greetings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad... Upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). This is a weapon for the believers that will be useful to them in this world and the Hereafter. If we talk about this world, if a person wants their faith to be strong, wants an increase in their sustenance, wants to remove hypocrisy from their heart, wants to refrain from sins, then they should recite Salawat as much as possible. As much as possible, recite Salawat. Much effort has been made to talk about its virtues, but if we want our scale of good deeds to be heavy on the Day of Judgment, we should recite as much Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as possible so that our scale can be heavy on the Day of Judgment. The fifth stage, and this is also an important stage, is the bridge of the Hereafter, a difficult stage—the Sirat. Because when asked about the Sirat in the Hadiths, one said that the Sirat is a bridge that is thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword. This shows that... This shows that crossing it will not be easy; it will be very difficult. A person will not be able to cross it unless they have someone with them, and there is no one better than Ali (a.s.). Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) says that when the believers—meaning the followers of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)—are crossing the Sirat on the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out and say, 'The fire of Hell, on the Day of Judgment, will be cooled for the followers of Ali (a.s.).' So, another thing is that these people will pass quickly. Why? Because the flames of my fire have been extinguished for them. That is, this will be the status of the lovers of Ali (a.s.) that if they cross that Sirat... If they cross that Sirat, the fire of Hell will be extinguished. And this is not the miracle of the believers, but the status of the one who holds the Wilayah. If the Wilayah can provide such a benefit to a servant, if it can cool the fire of Hell, then it will definitely be useful for us at the time of our death as well. Our final discussion is this, and in it, we will include the Hadith where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'O people, you need our help, because if you meet Allah with our Wilayah, our help, and our love, then through our intercession, Allah will admit you into Paradise.' After that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'I swear by Allah, in whose hands is the soul of Muhammad, that on the Day of Judgment, no deed will be accepted except our recognition and our love.' This shows that at every stage of the Hereafter, if anything will be useful to us... If anything will be of use to us in the hereafter, it is the Wilayah. You have explained very simply how the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is the strong rope of Allah, the long rope that, if held onto in this world, will surely lead one to Paradise and save one from Hell. With this, we pray that as long as our breaths continue, our hearts may keep saying 'Ya Ali'. When death comes, may it come with the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and when we are in the hereafter, may we be granted the intercession of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). With this, our episode ends here. But before I quickly conclude, let me remind you that as soon as the episode ends, the link to today's quiz will be provided. You must click that link and answer all the questions correctly as soon as possible. Insha'Allah, the winner's name will be posted on our social media accounts tomorrow. Until then, Allah Hafiz.

title: Majlis 1 |  Tawakkul | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | #Muharram 2026 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual concept of Tawakkul (reliance on Allah) within the context of the tragedy of Karbala. It emphasizes the importance of Ma'rifah (gnosis) through the teachings of the Ahlulbayt and highlights the intellectual and spiritual legacy of Shia scholars. The session concludes with a poignant account of the martyrdom of Qasim ibn Hasan, illustrating the ultimate sacrifice made for the preservation of faith.
content:
Haider Haider... [repeated]... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and the end is for the pious and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and make their exit easy. Blessings be upon the infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and make their exit easy, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, our Imam of the time, our master of command, our owner, our master, our beloved, our physician, our intimate friend, our companion, the cave of the distressed, and the relief of the troubled, may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Our master and leader, Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.), has said: 'And know that a good deed is a means of earning praise and a cause for reward. If you were to see a good deed as a person, you would see it as beautiful and handsome, pleasing to the onlookers and surpassing the worlds.' Truthful is our master and leader, Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and make their exit easy. I have chosen this hadith, this noble hadith, for the discussion of these five gatherings. It is narrated from Sayyid al-Shuhada, Imam Hussain (a.s.): 'And know'—meaning you all should know—'that a good deed is a means of earning praise and a cause for reward.' Whatever good Allah rewards, and after that, the Chief of Martyrs (a.s.) says: 'If you were to see goodness in the form of a man.' This means a day will come when Allah will present goodness in the form of a man. All these narrations exist. If you read the narrations about the Day of Judgment, it is explicitly written in these hadiths that Allah will materialize everything on the Day of Judgment. There will be a station—as you know, there are a thousand stages in the Day of Judgment—one of those stages will be the stage of embodiment, where Allah will give every thing a physical form, a shape. To give you an example so the matter becomes clear—this is an example from a hadith, not our own—for instance, those who are arrogant and consider themselves great, it is written in the hadith that Allah will present them in the form of ants on the Day of Judgment. That is, arrogance will be in the form of an ant, and every person will trample over them. This will be the state of the arrogant on the Day of Judgment. Arrogance, pride, conceit—that is, the person who thinks, 'I am better than him.' We think we are better than him? No. There is a narration that a person cannot truly possess religion until he considers himself the lowest of all. Until then, he will not have religion. It is in the hadith; otherwise, everyone claims to follow religion. Imam Hussain (a.s.) said exactly this on the day of Ashura: 'People are slaves of the world, and religion is only on their tongues, which they rotate according to their convenience.' Whatever is convenient for us, we like a thing and do it according to our own calculations, and then we drape it in the cloak of religion. This is religion. Anyway, the Chief of Martyrs is pointing towards this. The Chief of Martyrs says in the narration: 'If you were to see goodness as a man, you would see that he is very beautiful and handsome.' 'Hasan' means handsome and 'Jamil' means beautiful. These are actually Arabic phrases. If we explain them, we will deviate from the topic, so we try to stay on topic. Hasan is that which is created perfectly, and Jamil is that which, when a person sees it, they feel good; that is, they feel happy. So, if you were to see goodness, it would be 'yusurrun-nazireen'—that is, goodness would be so beautiful that those who see it would be delighted and happy. They would find pleasure in it, just as when you see any good scenery. For example, let me give you an example quickly so the matter becomes clear. For instance, you go out here in Bombay and see a concrete jungle all around; no one likes it, and there is traffic, this and that, chaos. That is why people run away, go outside the city. Why? To see greenery, to see—well, obviously, that is why Bombayites go on weekends. But of course, a person who lives in a village does not go on a weekend because there is enough greenery in his village, you see. And 'yafuqul-alameen'—and this goodness will have superiority over all the worlds. Superiority means excellence; it will excel over everything, it will dominate. There will be nothing superior to it. These are the words of the Chief of Martyrs, and the hadith is very long; we have only selected a small part. It is for you. So, before moving forward, let's make a small point about what 'Ma'ruf' (goodness) means. Now, people think Ma'ruf is just 'good deeds.' Peace be upon you. It is not that kind of good deed. What is Ma'ruf? 'Al-Ma'rufu ma amartum bihi, wal-munkaru ma nahaytum 'anhu.' Ma'ruf is that which the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) command, and Munkar (evil) is that which they forbid. This is one definition of Ma'ruf, of goodness—that is, all the commands and prohibitions of the Ahlulbayt. And similarly, when Imam Sadiq (a.s.) asked Abu Hanifa what Ma'ruf is, he said 'good deeds.' The Imam said, 'No, I meant Ma'ruf is the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and make their exit easy. Then the Imam asked what Munkar is. He said, 'You tell me.' So the Imam said, 'Munkar means evil,' the opposite of Ma'ruf. Those are the people who usurped the right of Ali. Those who usurped the right of Ali are Munkar. So this is Ma'ruf. Now, if one wants to understand this Ma'ruf, there is only one way for it. There is no other way. As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate. So whoever desires the city and wisdom, let them come through its gate.' Whoever wants knowledge and wisdom, there is no other way except to go to the door of Ali and the children of Ali. Indeed. Subhan Allah. There is no other way. If a person thinks there is another way, they will go somewhere else, but they cannot reach Ma'ruf, they cannot reach knowledge and wisdom. They will never find it. And further clarification, a little more explanation: Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Recognize the status of our Shia according to their narrations and their knowledge.' If you want to recognize our Shia, to recognize their status, their levels, then look at which of our Shia knows how many hadiths. 'According to their narrations and their knowledge.' Whoever knows more hadiths, that is their level. 'Because knowledge is the understanding of the narration.' Because what is Ma'rifah (gnosis)? It is understanding the hadiths. This is Ma'rifah. There is no other way for Ma'rifah. No other way. Look, there are people like us who come, and we feel very ashamed, actually embarrassed. It is just that there is a reward, so this is a selfish motive, that okay, let's recite the Majlis, otherwise we are not worthy of reciting Majlis. All this is the work of great people. That is, let me narrate an incident for you, this is a real incident, and it is very important to recognize our great scholars, the ones who were our true scholars. I am telling the children, especially the youth, that you should know all these names, and if possible, memorize them, then go home and Google them. Don't ask ChatGPT yet, because ChatGPT hallucinates a lot. So don't rely on it too much. But Google it; you will get a lot of information on Google. Sheikh Jafar-e-Tustari or Shustari. Shustari, in Iran they say Shushtar and in Arab they say Tustar. For example, we had Shahid-e-Salis, he was also Tustari, Shustari. So we say Shustari. Coming to India, it became Shustari. Among Arabs, Tustari; among Iranians, Shustari, and actually that is correct because Shushtar is a place in Iran, from there. Shushtar, but coming to India, it became Shushtar. But it's okay, that is not very important. Sheikh Jafar was a very great scholar. He passed away in 1303 Hijri, in 1303 Hijri. And he was a student of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari. A very great personality, Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, the Seal of the Jurists (Khatam al-Fuqaha). Among the jurists, the greatest—that is, no one has been born to compete with him to this day, you understand. That is, even today, when Ayatollah Sistani gives Dars-e-Kharij—well, he doesn't give it now, he used to give it before, now his health is not good for the last 15-20 years, so now his son, Sayyid Muhammad Reza Sistani, gives the Dars-e-Kharij. So when Ayatollah Sistani used to give Dars-e-Kharij, I am just saying this to explain to the children. I will try not to deviate from my topic. So he wrote a book, 'Risalat al-Taqiyya.' A book on Taqiyya. You know Taqiyya, right? Taqiyya means hiding one's religion. He wrote a book on it of 48 pages. Risala does not mean a book; Risala means a treatise, a small essay, an article. An article, it was only 48 pages. And in it, he explained that Taqiyya is obligatory, and recommended, and forbidden, and disliked, and permissible, and he wrote it all briefly. When Agha Sistani was giving Dars-e-Kharij, he explained this only in 'Manasik al-Hajj.' Where did he explain this book? In 'Manasik al-Hajj.' You go for Hajj, right? So this book of Agha Sistani's Dars-e-Kharij is in many volumes. So its 18th volume, this 18th volume is 800 pages long. Similarly, all of them are like that. His teaching Dars, it is an 800-page book. That is, one volume, I am just telling you about one volume. And what is it? 'Buhuth' (Discussions) concerning Manasik al-Hajj. Look, I don't want to tell you too much academic stuff so you don't get bored. But I just want to tell you the importance, that about Hajj, that is, in the rituals of Hajj, there is only one discussion there: whether you can pray behind them, behind their Imam, or not? Agha Sistani, may Allah protect him, had a discussion on Taqiyya regarding that. Ayatollah al-Uzma Sistani, yes. He only explained this Risala, and he explained this Risala in 300 pages. 300 pages. 18th volume, I am giving you the reference, I am giving you the exact reference, whoever knows Arabic, read it, read it. Download it, then read it at your leisure. The name of the book is 'Buhuth fi Manasik al-Hajj,' page number 499, that is, the discussion starts from about 500 and goes to the end of the book, up to 800 pages. Only on Taqiyya. He only explained this treatise of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari. So think about what Sheikh Murtaza Ansari was. You can estimate from this. The grave of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari is in the shrine. In the shrine of Imam Ali (a.s.), Sheikh Murtaza Ansari, at Babul Qibla, as soon as you enter, on the left side is his holy grave. Sheikh Murtaza Ansari. Sheikh Jafar Tustari was his student. He gained a lot of knowledge, and after that, he thought, 'I will recite Majlis.' Now look, these people are such great people, we understand that they have the right to recite Majlis. People like us do not. But anyway, mentioning Hussain is a reward, okay, and whoever does it, does it, it's a good thing. So he went, that is, he said, 'I will recite Majlis,' and immediately this thought came to his mind, 'I will recite a great Majlis.' But he could not get the pulpit he wanted, that is, he could not recite. And I am telling you quickly. Now he wept a lot, he cried a lot that it didn't happen as he had thought. And he was a very great scholar, yes, Sheikh Jafar. He cried a lot, he wept a lot. And after crying, he said, 'Maula,' that is, he pleaded in the court of Imam Hussain (a.s.), 'Maula, the right that I am not able to fulfill, and I don't like it, and I am thinking of leaving the pulpit.' So look yourself, this is not some small person who is saying this, yes brother. I am telling you so you will know what kind of personality it was, I am just telling you. So Sheikh Jafar says that that same night I saw Imam Hussain (a.s.) in a dream. May Allah bless him and his family. May Allah bless him and his family. I was honored with his Ziyarat. Honored with Imam Hussain (a.s.). I saw Imam Hussain (a.s.) came, and who is with him? Janab-e-Habib ibn Mazahir. In this too, look, what is the wisdom? What is the wisdom? That Janab-e-Habib is the jurist of the Ahlulbayt. Whom Imam Hussain (a.s.) addressed as a jurist. 'From Hussain ibn Ali to the jurist man, Habib ibn Mazahir.' That is, if the Imam calls him a jurist, he is a jurist. So Janab-e-Habib is with him, and remember that Janab-e-Habib, actually, we usually say that he was a childhood friend of Imam Hussain, actually it is not like that. There was a 17-year difference between Imam Hussain and Janab-e-Habib. Imam Hussain (a.s.) was, or 17-18 years. The age of Imam Hussain (a.s.) at the time of martyrdom was 57, and Janab-e-Habib was 75 at that time. Janab-e-Habib was a companion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). He was a companion of Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.). But he loved Imam Hussain very much. There was a lot of affection, a lot of love for Imam Hussain. Boundless love. So much love that when Imam Hussain (a.s.) used to walk, he would pick up the dust from his feet and put it on his head. If a big man does this for a small child, suppose if someone is 20 years old and does this for a 3-year-old child, then it will be clear to you how much love, how much devotion there would be for Imam Hussain (a.s.). So now he saw Janab-e-Habib, right? Now what can I tell you about the status of Janab-e-Habib? You see, now those who have gone for Ziyarat, their Zarih is also separate. You saw, right? What is his status, his position? Anyway, so Sheikh Jafar says that I saw that he is with him. He asked, 'Sheikh Jafar, what is the matter?' He replied, 'Mawla, I wanted to recite a Majlis, but I was unable to, and so on.' So the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Habib, these are our guests. You know there is a shortage of water.' (The Imam is speaking in the dream). 'But since guests have arrived, show them hospitality. Whatever we have, offer it to them.' Pay attention, you understand what 'pazirai' (hospitality) is, right? Show hospitality. Treat them well. They are our guests. So, Janabe Habib said, 'Sheikh, here is some halwa for you.' He mentioned a specific name of a sweet; it is a type of sweet among the Arabs. Oh, my Sayyid-e-Sajjad, my Imam, what must have been passing through his heart? Every moment, the soul of Sayyid-e-Sajjad would not have remained. By God, how must he have endured it?' The day of Ashura came, Qasim came again, stood there after Dhuhr. He started saying, 'Uncle, give me permission.' Hussain is standing silently. Qasim is repeatedly asking for permission, 'Uncle, give me permission.' When Hussain was not saying anything, it is written in the Maqtal that Qasim held both of Hussain's hands and started rubbing his eyes. He started rubbing his eyes and while rubbing, he said, 'Uncle, give me permission, give me permission.' Hussain said, 'Qasim, today everyone has to be martyred.' And he embraced him and then prepared Qasim. He prepared Qasim with his own hands. When Qasim was ready, Hussain embraced him. It is written in the Maqtal that both uncle and nephew cried so much, so much that both fainted. Now I do not know if they fainted due to thirst or if they were so weak that they fainted due to crying. Now when both were unconscious, oh mourners, when someone is brought to consciousness from unconsciousness, water is sprinkled. But alas, Zainab-e-Kubra (s.a.) sprinkled tears. She sprinkled tears. When both regained consciousness, Zainab said, 'Brother, do not stop Qasim now, let Qasim go.' Hussain gave permission, Qasim was mounted. But as soon as Qasim was mounted, Hussain stopped him again. Stopping him, he said, 'Qasim, wait for a moment.' Hussain tore Qasim's collar, tore his shirt. He said, 'Uncle, what is this? What is this?' He said, 'This is the sign of orphans.' He remembered his brother; this is the sign of orphans. Perhaps the wicked ones might have mercy. But it is written in the Maqtal, Qasim went and fought, and fought a fierce battle. He is a 13-year-old child; while fighting, someone attacked in such a way that Qasim could not steady himself, and when he started swaying on the horse, the strap of Qasim's shoe got stuck in the horse's saddle. Now, Qasim, with his hands... ...put them around the neck, so the wicked ones started attacking Qasim. When Qasim came down completely, what did the wicked ones do? They started trampling Qasim with horses. Horses from here to there, horses from there to here. Qasim is calling out, 'Ya Ammah, adrikni' (O Uncle, help me), 'Uncle, come to help, Uncle, come to help.' By the time Hussain reached, Qasim's body had been torn to pieces. Hussain wrapped Qasim's body in a bundle. And he brought that bundle to the tent. Wa Qasima, Wa Husaina. 'Sayalamul-ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun.' Al-la'natullahi 'alal-qawmiz-zalimin. O Lord, O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. Hasten the reappearance of the avenger of Hussain's blood. Amen. Count us among his helpers and supporters. Amen. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Amen. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Amen. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Amen. Those who are sick, grant them complete and swift recovery. Amen. Those who are away from their homeland, return them to their homeland safe and sound. Amen. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Amen. Protect the great scholars and the esteemed Maraje. Amen. Protect the holy shrines. Amen. Whoever protects them, protect them. Amen. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.). Amen. O Lord, grant us the privilege of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Amen. By reciting one Surah Fatiha and three times Surah Tawheed, grant the reward to the souls of the late Ghulam Ali ibn Abdul Aziz Lakhani, all the deceased of the Lakhani family, all the deceased of the Rupani family, all the deceased of the Himani family, all the deceased of the Lahda family, and all the deceased of the Narsidani family. Bismillah.

title: Ghar Mein Daakhil Hotey Waqt Salaam Karna Chaahiye
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the importance of greeting with a loud voice when entering one's home, regardless of whether anyone is physically present. It explains that such greetings acknowledge the presence of angels and serve as a form of spiritual protection. The speaker highlights the specific invocation 'Assalamu alayna min indi Rabbina' as a beautiful practice derived from the teachings of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
Greet with a loud voice. Even if someone is at home, greet them, and if no one is at home, still greet with a loud voice. Why? Because if a believer is there, angels will be in the house. For example, when you open the door with a key, say: 'Assalamu alayna min indi Rabbina' (Peace be upon us from our Lord). Peace be upon us all—meaning upon me and upon you, O angels who are present, peace be upon you from Allah. Look at the teachings of the Ahlulbayt, this is the 'Dawat-e-Husna' (the beautiful invitation).

title: Ek Momin Ka Aqeedah Kaisa Hona Chahiye? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the foundational importance of Ma'rifat (recognition) and Tasdiq (affirmation) of Allah as the core of a believer's faith. Drawing from the first sermon of Nahj al-Balagha, he emphasizes that true faith must remain unshakable despite worldly calamities or doubts. He concludes by highlighting that a true believer's heart remains steadfast in its conviction, even under the most extreme trials.
content:
Now, this is the tragedy of the Ummah, of the followers, which I am not even talking about—that we ourselves have become distant from Nahj al-Balagha. We have become distant from Nahj al-Balagha. If you read Nahj al-Balagha, the first sermon of Nahj al-Balagha... look, I will state sentences that some people might not understand. But these are the words of the Infallible, the words of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The Imam says—look at the sentence: the first sermon of Nahj al-Balagha, 'Awwalu al-din ma'rifatuhu' (The beginning of religion is His recognition). If you want to enter the religion, enter it with the recognition of Allah. 'Awwalu al-din' means entering, going into the religion. If someone does not have Tawheed (monotheism), they have not entered the religion at all. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. 'Awwalu al-din ma'rifatuhu. Wa kamalu ma'rifatihi, al-tasdiqu bihi' (The beginning of religion is His recognition, and the perfection of His recognition is to affirm Him). The perfection of recognition is the peak of recognition, that you affirm Allah. You say, 'Yes, Allah exists.' Even if a thousand atheists come before you, if a thousand lives, a thousand atheists come and tell you there is no God, you should say, 'What are you talking about?' You are denying that which is more manifest than our own existence. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. His existence is more manifest than our own existence. Are you denying Him? 'Al-tasdiqu bihi' (Affirming Him). This is the perfection of recognition. Affirm Him. No matter how many whispers of the devils there are, there should never be even an atom's worth of doubt in your heart about Allah. Look, it is a small issue. The issue is small. What does 'Tasdiq' (affirmation) mean? Tasdiq means having faith, the correct belief. Meaning, to tie a knot so firm that no matter how many whispers there are, no matter how many whispers there are... Now, how do these whispers occur? Let me present that for your service. I am telling this for the children; the elders understand more. I am telling this for the children, for the youth. How do these whispers occur? For example, some great trouble, some great calamity occurs. For instance, someone's young son passes away. The young son died. Now, the faith is weak. 'Now Allah, what did Allah gain by taking our young son?' Look. The faith, there is wavering in the faith. A little trouble came. I have even seen people who, when they had a loss in business, said, 'What happiness did Allah get from this?' I said, 'The same happiness that He got by giving you profit.' Yes. People are like this, small things, small problems. There are small problems, and they immediately point fingers at Allah. What is this? Why did He do this? Why did He do that? So, what is the limit of recognition? What is the perfection of recognition? That is 'Tasdiq'. What does 'Tasdiq' mean? Faith. Faith should be so strong that even if the world turns upside down, regarding Tawheed, regarding the belief in Allah—that Allah exists—there should not be even the slightest wavering. That is why, that is why Sayyid al-Shuhada (a.s.) says in a hadith, it is a hadith of Sayyid al-Shuhada, that 'Inna al-mu'mina ashaddu min zuburi al-hadid' (The believer is stronger than a piece of iron). The believer is stronger, more powerful than iron. 'Inna al-hadida idha ukhila fi al-nari taghayyar' (If iron is put into fire, it melts). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Iron melts. 'Walakinna al-mu'mina idha qutila thumma nushira thumma qutila, lam yataghayyar qalbuhu' (But if the believer is killed, then resurrected, then killed, his heart does not change). His faith does not change. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali!

title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Muntaqim e Girya e Zahra (سلام الله عليها)
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound grief of Imam Ali (a.s.) following the passing of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) and the theological significance of her oppression. It emphasizes the duty of believers to defend the truth of the Ahlulbayt and highlights the role of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the ultimate seeker of justice for these historical injustices. The session also commends the efforts of youth in utilizing modern research and technology to address theological objections and uphold the legacy of the Prophet's family.
content:
Ali (a.s.) is hiding his grief, Ali (a.s.) is hiding his grief. Ali (a.s.) is hiding his tears. Why is his back bent? Why is the Mawla of the believers, whose Mayyat (funeral) he is carrying, hiding his tears? Ali (a.s.) is hiding his grief. The wounds and marks of the past are being slowly covered by Ali (a.s.), who is hiding his tears. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Peace be upon Fatimah Zahra (s.a.), her father, her husband, her sons, and the secret deposited in her. Imam Ridha (a.s.) narrated from his ancestors that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'I will not intercede for four types of people on the Day of Judgment, even if they come to me with the sins of all the people of the earth. First, the one who harmed my Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Second, the one who did not fulfill their needs when they were in dire need. Third, the one who did not love them with their heart and tongue. And fourth, the one who did not defend them with their hands, meaning their actions.' From the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), the central personality is Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). This series of answers to the objections against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) was a humble effort on our part to defend them as much as possible, so that the painful incident of the attack on the house of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the realities associated with it could be conveyed to the people. We wanted the oppression faced by the oppressed daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to be revealed to the world, so that the world knows what mountains of oppression were broken upon the Prophet's own family as soon as he closed his eyes. So that on the Day of Judgment, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asks us if we told the world about the oppression faced by his daughter, we do not feel ashamed. And so that when Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) is present before Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), we can... ...stand before our Mawla and say that we tried our best to defend the honor of your grandmother. Perhaps for this reason, when Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) takes revenge for all the oppression inflicted upon the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and specifically for the attack on the house of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), he will include us as well. Because Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) is the one about whom Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will burn those people with the same wood that was used to burn the house of Ali (a.s.), Fatimah (s.a.), Hasan (a.s.), and Husayn (a.s.), because that wood is our heritage. The wood collected for the attack on the house of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is still with Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). I wonder what must pass through his heart when he sees that wood. It is not impossible that in that burnt wood, he sees the burning door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Sometimes he might see the burning door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), sometimes the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) comes to mind, sometimes the sight of Mawla-e-Kainat Imam Ali (a.s.) being dragged with a rope around his neck to the court makes him suffer. Or perhaps he remembers his grandmother Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) going to the court to claim her inheritance, and the oppressors tearing her document to pieces. The door that had the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) blessing, perhaps its echo still rings in the ears of Zahra (s.a.). Or he remembers Imam Ali (a.s.) burying the daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in the darkness of the night and expressing his loneliness. How can the one who has been waiting for nearly 1200 years to take revenge for the oppression on his ancestors not be restless? He is waiting for true helpers and for the command of the Almighty. We pray in the court of Allah that He includes our efforts in answering these objections in the advocacy of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). ...in the advocacy of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). And may Allah include those who watch these videos and share them with others in this reward as well. Because before the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), we can only defend the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), but the true justice for Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) will only happen after the reappearance. Because I am certain, my Mawla, that after your reappearance, the world will change. After your reappearance, the prostration of gratitude will be performed. The world cannot function under any tyrant; only your decree will prevail after your reappearance. Now that Imam Sajjad (a.s.) has smiled, Zahra (s.a.) will celebrate after your reappearance. Those sleeping in the waves, yes, the ones in the grave, will have to rise after your reappearance. The secrets that are in the hearts of the loved ones, Mahdi (a.s.), even those veils will be lifted after your reappearance. Where will Zahra (s.a.) remain... ...one of her own, one of her own. They are carrying the funeral, Ali (a.s.) is hiding his tears. Ali (a.s.) is hiding his tears. May Allah accept the hard work and intentions of all the brothers and sisters. First of all, we have reached six videos. You are doing a very good job. After reaching six videos, all things are clear, and there has been an increase in knowledge. Now we want all the Shia brothers and sisters to share these videos as much as possible. These videos are very important for those whose knowledge is lacking, and for those who had doubts even within this stage, they have been cleared. The topics the brothers have clarified are very clear. It is very important for the young generation. In the Strong Group, whatever platforms have been used to spread knowledge, for all Shia people, for all the followers, as far as the knowledge can reach, every effort is being made. So we try our best to share them. The brothers say that we want more difficulties in our path, whether giving knowledge or taking it. This concept that started with the series, we are noticing it. The concept of 'Gham-e-Zahra (s.a.)' is very good. May Allah grant success to the entire Strong Group team. You are doing a very good job, and may Allah increase the knowledge of you all. ...and may Allah increase the knowledge of you all. Until then, pray for us, Allah Hafiz. The program that has been done from the beginning and the episodes set for it are very good and quite informative. People should watch them. It is said that this happens, and the things we were afraid to tell until now are present in history. We should tell them, we should tell our children, our youth. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Peace be upon our master Muhammad and his family. As the brothers are trying, I have watched the videos, and this is a very commendable step they have taken in explaining the Hadith. This is very good for our youth. Although, the oppression on Fatimah (s.a.) is the same today. Yesterday, the oppressed was the one on whom the burning door was dropped; today, even after 1400 years, people do not understand that oppression was committed against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Today, there are arguments that there was no door in the house, and then it was burned. That there was no door in the house, and then what was burned, and this itself, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), the pride of Jannat-ul-Baqi, remains a proof even today that it was a tragedy. And even today, to take revenge for the hateful face... subscribe [music] and subscribe to the channel. That unfaithful one, that Amir... in any case, Salamullah Alayha, this is a bond that is incumbent upon all believers. And through this channel, our brothers are performing this project in an excellent manner. The efforts they are making, the love they are creating in the hearts of the believers, they are being pointed towards. I believe that prayers from the heart go out for them, and the believer is not only being blessed by both worlds, but it is my belief that the work they are performing is such a great work, such a religious work, that believe me, Allah (s.w.t.) will bless both the world and the hereafter. And I present one of its aspects in a nutshell, and that is, the mission of 'Makkari' (deception), he says that I went to the Imam and asked, and you were saying this at that time, I... At that time, you were saying this to me. I greeted the Imam, the Imam replied. Where did you go? I said, 'I have come after seeing something, after which I cannot show my face.' The Imam asked, 'What did you see?' I said, 'I saw that people were taking this lady as a prisoner, and they were taking her away with great cruelty and beating her. I asked the people, 'Why is she being taken as a prisoner?' They replied, 'This lady, her foot slipped, and from her tongue, a curse escaped against the enemies of Allah.' I said, 'A curse upon those who oppressed her.' When I mentioned this to Bibi Salamullah Alayha, as we have heard, she had not heard this, and tears began to flow from her eyes. The Imam said, 'Get up, let us go to the mosque and pray for her.' And this means that whoever speaks of the tragedy of Janab-e-Sayyeda (s.a.) in this world, they will receive the prayers of the Imam for their tongue. In any case, I pray in the court of Allah (s.w.t.) that may God grant them the reward for this, and may He also accept our deeds in His court. We are... I want to say to you personally, when I see the youth, and especially those... When I see the youth, and especially those youth who, while fulfilling their worldly responsibilities, while living their lives well, also turn towards religion, and they also perform the religious duties with heart and soul, then it is truly commendable. Because retirement life is for this, and what else are the brothers doing? Worldliness has been enough; now, along with the world, they are doing something for the hereafter. This is commendable. And I would like to say that a team of such strong people is needed. These people do not just talk; they act. The work they have done, even in difficult circumstances, the way this program was received, the number of messages, the number of people who liked it, is commendable. And secondly... Liked it, is commendable. And secondly, the thing was that these people have the ability to take initiative. I have said before that I was looking for such people. Now, these are educated people. They are detached from the world, and it is a matter of great happiness that the first effort they made, which was highly appreciated, in the name of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and now, because after one success, another responsibility arises, therefore, in these programs, they have revived the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and the way they showed that program to the world is in itself a great achievement. That by using technology, we introduce the world to the teachings of Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). title: Kya Tabarra Sunnat-e-Masoomeen (a.s.) Hai? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of Tabarra, or disassociation, as a fundamental practice rooted in the Sunnah of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.). It highlights that true faith requires not only devotion to Allah but also the open rejection of and enmity towards those who oppose divine truth. The speaker emphasizes that this stance of Bara'at is an essential component of the path followed by the infallible Masoomeen (a.s.).
content:
[Music] Regarding the Sunnah of Ibrahim (a.s.), we find that in Ibrahim and his companions, there is an excellent example of action. When they said to their nation, 'We are disgusted with you and those whom you worship besides Allah.' Then they said, 'We reject you, and there has arisen between us and you enmity and hatred forever,' and this is until you believe in Allah alone. This is the Sunnah of the infallible Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), in which there is also 'Bara'at' (disassociation) and enmity and hatred towards the enemies of religion, and their displeasure.
Tabarra is established as a practice within the Sunnah of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.).
True belief involves both love for the righteous and hatred for the enemies of religion.
The Quranic verse regarding Ibrahim (a.s.) serves as a model for disassociation.
Bara'at is defined as an open rejection of those who worship other than Allah.
Enmity towards the enemies of God is a requirement until they accept monotheism.
The Masoomeen (a.s.) uphold this principle as part of their divine tradition.

title: The Era Of The Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)  |  Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi
excerpt: This lecture by Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi explores the theological necessity and transformative impact of the arrival of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The speaker critiques modern society's reliance on consumerism, systemic inequality, and social isolation, contrasting these issues with the promised era of divine justice and universal prosperity. The talk concludes by urging believers to move beyond performative rituals and cultivate a genuine, active longing for the Imam's reappearance through moral alignment and spiritual preparation.

The lecture emphasizes that the recognition of the Ahlulbayt and the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) are the essential foundations for the acceptance of all religious deeds. Then after that, turning towards the Imams (a.s.) is our most important duty, light was also shed on this. Then after that, we moved to the third episode, in which we saw that turning towards the Imams (a.s.) who are among us, or who are the Imams of the time, how necessary it is, and denying them, denying those infallible Imams (a.s.) is like, and if anyone denied even one Imam, it is as if he denied all the Imams, he denied Imam Hussain (a.s.), rather he denied all the Imams (a.s.). Then we moved forward, we also saw that the discussion of the 12 Imams, in that regard, we saw from the books of the Ahlul Sunnah, that the mention of the 12 Imams, from the books of the Ahlul Sunnah, this proof was also presented, and after that, two episodes were about some such personalities on which, in which, there was a discussion. After that, we moved forward and saw that in the light of the hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the verses of the Holy Quran, Allah has always made the truth the criterion, not personalities. Therefore, we saw that in the authentic narrations, people are recognized by the truth; the truth is not recognized by people. Thus, the truth is the criterion, not personalities. We discussed the events that took place before the incident of Ghadir, and we examined them in light of the Hadith of Manzilat. title: Imam Ali (A.S) Ka Marsiya | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the profound grief of Imam Ali (a.s.) following the burial of his wife, Janabe Zahra (s.a.). It highlights a specific passage from Nahjul Balagha where the Imam describes her as a divine trust returned to Allah. The talk emphasizes the eternal nature of the Imam's sorrow and his sleepless nights after her passing.
content:
The statement of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) which he said after burying Janabe Zahra (s.a.): 'Fatarat-u-hina amman huzni fasarmad mali.' The translation of this is: 'Indeed, that trust has been returned and taken back.' Janabe Zahra (s.a.), who was a trust in this world from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), has been taken back. And as far as my grief is concerned, Amirul Momineen (a.s.) says, 'It will remain forever, and my nights will be spent in wakefulness.' This is present in Nahjul Balagha.
