title: EP22 | Ayat-e-Tatheer aur Ahle Tasannun Ulama | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines the theological significance of Ayat-e-Tatheer (the Verse of Purification) through the lens of Sunni scholarship. By analyzing primary sources such as Sunan al-Tirmidhi and Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the speaker demonstrates that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) explicitly defined the Ahlulbayt as Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn. The presentation highlights the linguistic exclusivity of the verse and argues that it serves as a foundational proof for the infallibility and spiritual status of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
TSR presents. I bear witness that Ali is the Wali of Allah. It is related. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance and curse all their enemies. In the series of 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' (Completion of Proof), we started the discussion of the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir). And that verse is as follows, it is verse number 33 of Surah al-Ahzab: 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumu al-rijsa ahla al-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathira' (Allah only wishes to remove all abomination from you, O members of the Family, and to make you pure and spotless). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance and curse all their enemies. And in the previous episode, we presented to you the narrations in Bukhari, Muslim, and Nasa'i, which clearly show that this Verse of Purification was revealed solely and exclusively for the Ahlulbayt, meaning the Panjtan-e-Pak (the five holy ones), and for the Infallible Imams (a.s.), and for no one else. Continuing this discussion of this verse, we mention a few more points, a few more references and sources from the Sunni tradition, so that the matter becomes completely established. In the Sahih Sittah (the six authentic books), there is another famous book, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, which is very popular among the Sunnis and about which the famous saying is that Tirmidhi himself said, 'If anyone wants the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to speak to him, he should keep my Sunan in his house.' Meaning, its status is so high, and that was their own opinion about it. Anyway, in Sunan al-Tirmidhi, there are four hadiths regarding this Verse of Purification, and the meaning of all of them is the same: that this verse was revealed in honor of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). We read one hadith for you from these four, and you can refer to the rest yourselves. It is hadith number 3205: 'Nazalat hadhihi al-ayatu 'ala al-nabiyyi salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi' (This verse was revealed upon the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family). And what was the verse? 'Innama yuridullahu liyudhhiba 'ankumu al-rijsa ahla al-bayti wa yutahhirakum tathira.' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Where was it revealed? It says: 'Fi bayti Ummi Salamah' (In the house of Umm Salamah). It was revealed in the chamber of the Mother of the Believers, Lady Umm Salamah. 'Fada'a al-nabiyyu salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam' (The Prophet called...). According to them, 'salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam', but actually it should be 'wa alihi wa sallam'. The Prophet called out, whom did he call? Fāṭimata wa Ḥasanan wa Ḥusaynā. Meaning, he invited Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the Princess of the Two Worlds, and called her and the Hasanain (a.s.). Fa-jallalahum bi-kisā'. And he took them all under a cloak, under a blanket. Wa 'Aliyyun khalfa ẓahrihi. Ali (a.s.) was behind him. Fa-jallalahu bi-kisā'. So he took him also under that cloak, under the blanket. Thumma qāla. Look, this is a narration from Tirmidhi, and before proceeding, I must state that whatever discussion we have will be from the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni scholars) and their narrations; there is not a single Shia reference here. Everything will be based on the foundation of truth and the creed. And these are all traditional books; it is not as if this is a matter of history where you might debate whether it is correct or incorrect—no, these are all narrations, hadiths. And I also mentioned that Sunan al-Tirmidhi is one of the Sahih al-Sittah (the six authentic books). Thumma qāla: Allāhumma hā'ulā'i Ahlu Baytī. O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt, that is all. These are the Ahl al-Bayt. Fa-adhhiba 'anhumu al-rijsa wa ṭahhirhum taṭhīrā. O Allah, keep all evils, all impurities, all filth, and everything away from them, and keep them pure as is the right to be kept pure. Keep them pure as is the right. Qālat Umm-e-Salama. Umm-e-Salama asked, 'Wa ana ma'ahum yā Rasūlallāh?' O Messenger of Allah, am I also among them? Qāla ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa ālihi. The Prophet said, 'Anta 'alā makānik.' You are in your place; you are the Mother of the Believers, that is fine, that is all. Is that right? Wa anti ilā khayr. You are upon goodness, you are good, you are righteous, but you are not Ahl al-Bayt. The Prophet is trying to say this; you are in your place, you have your own status, you have your own rank. You are good, you are righteous, but you are not among the Ahl al-Bayt. Although this sentence is not in the hadith, its conclusion is obviously this. And similarly, if you look, the remaining three hadiths in Sunan al-Tirmidhi also indicate the same thing. Although, remember that some people have done a 'good deed' here too and claimed that the Prophet said, 'Yes, you are also among the Ahl al-Bayt.' Meaning, in some places, this 'good deed' has also been done. Anyway, so now we come to Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, which is the next book. As you know, Ahmad ibn Hanbal is a very great jurist, hadith scholar, and Imam. Yes, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, their Imam. He recorded 10 hadiths regarding the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tathir) in the Musnad alone, and eight more in other books; he recorded 18 hadiths regarding the Verse of Purification alone. And through various chains of narration, through various narrators. Now, just listen to the names of these narrators, from whose paths and chains they were recorded, so you know how authentic this narration is. For example, Abu Salama (1), Ata ibn Abi Rabah (2), Shaddad ibn Abdullah (3), Ibn Jushab (4), Sahl (5), and Umm-e-Salama (6). All these hadiths are very similar to each other. Now, we will record one hadith here for you, and you can look at the rest; whoever wants to research can do so very easily. And if someone does not understand, they can contact the WhatsApp number of 'The Strong Rope'; if Allah grants us the ability, we can send all the references and all the hadiths, there is no problem. In this narration that we are presenting to you, Rawā al-Imām Aḥmad (meaning Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who is an Imam according to them), 'an 'Aṭā' ibn Rabāḥ anna al-Nabiyya ṣallallāhu 'alayhi... (then they removed 'wa-ālihi', which shows how much love they had for the Progeny of Muhammad). Kāna fī bayti Umm-e-Salama. He was in the chamber of Umm-e-Salama; where was the Prophet? He was in the chamber of Umm-e-Salama. Fa-atat-hu Fāṭimah. Janabe Zahra, the Princess of the Two Worlds (s.a.), arrived. Fa-qāla: Idh'ī zawjaki wa-ibnayki. O Fatima, go and call your husband and your two sons. Fa-jā'a 'Aliyyun wa-al-Ḥasanu wa-al-Ḥusayn. The Princess brought them; they came, the Master of the Universe came, and the Hasanain (a.s.) came. Fa-dakhalū 'alayhi. They entered into the presence of the Prophet. Fa-jalasū 'alā disārin wa-kāna taḥtahu kisā'un lahu Khaybariyyun. There was a Khaybari cloak, which the Prophet took. Qālat Umm-e-Salama: Wa-ana uṣallī fī al-ḥujrah. Janabe Umm-e-Salama says that I was praying in the chamber, I was praying in my chamber. Fa-anzala Allāhu 'azza wa-jall. That Allah revealed this verse: Innamā yurīdu Allāhu liyudh'hiba 'ankumu al-rijsa Ahla al-Bayti wa-yuṭahhirakum taṭhīrā. Allāhumma ṣalli 'alā Muḥammadin wa-āli Muḥammad wa-'ajjil farajahum wa-al'an a'dā'ahum ajma'īn. Fa-akhadha al-Nabiyyu ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa-ālihi wa-sallam fa-ṣalla al-kisā'a fa-ghashshāhum bihi. The Prophet took the cloak and covered them all with this cloak, this blanket, this sheet. Thumma akhraja yadahu fa-alwā bihā ilā al-samā'. Then the Prophet took out his blessed hand, his blessed hand, and raising it towards the sky, he prayed. Thumma qāla Rasūlullāhi ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa-ālihi wa-sallam: Allāhumma hā'ulā'i Ahlu Baytī. O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt, that is all. Wa-khāṣṣatī. And these are my chosen ones, these are my very own. Fa-adhhiba 'anhumu al-rijsa wa-ṭahhirhum taṭhīrā. Keep all impurities, sins, filth, and every kind of existential and legislative impurity away from them, and keep them pure as is the right to be kept pure. Now look, we are reading the narration of Musnad Ahmad to you. Qālat Umm-e-Salama, Janabe Umm-e-Salama, the Mother of the Believers, asked, 'Fa-adkhalat ra'sa al-bayt.' I put my head into that room, and I said, 'Wa-ana ma'akum yā Rasūlallāh?' O Messenger of Allah, am I also with them, am I also among the Ahl al-Bayt? Qāla ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa-ālihi: Lā. He said, 'No.' Innaki ilā khayr, innaki ilā khayr. You are upon goodness, you are upon goodness. Meaning, you are a good woman, a good wife. You are a righteous woman, of good character. You truly have the right to be called the Mother of the Believers, but you are not among the Ahl al-Bayt. You are not among the Ahl al-Bayt. This is the narration of Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and if you wish, you can study this too; whoever wants to, can study it and see. So you noticed, the Prophet took them under his blanket, under the cloak, under the mantle, and after that, the Prophet prayed to Allah, and then the verse was revealed, and then the Prophet said, 'These are my Ahl al-Bayt.' And there was no one else in it. There was no one else in it, otherwise, the Prophet should have said, 'Go and call everyone else.' Why only these? Could he not have called others? He could have. 'You all come too, you all come too, everyone come.' But the Prophet says, 'No, only these, no one else besides them.' And the third reference we present to you is the book of Ibn Hajar al-Makki, as we have mentioned to you, his book is Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa, page 143. He says that it is the belief of most exegetes that this verse was revealed only and only in honor of the Ahl al-Bayt. Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa, as you know, this entire book shows how much prejudice he had, despite that. So, there is a long list of traditionists, jurists, and scholars of the Ahl-e-Tasannun who have recorded this Verse of Purification in their books, narrated the traditions, and people read them. But for some reason, the reality does not become clear. Which, God willing, when we present the arguments to you, the matter will become clearer. Those scholars who have linked this Verse of Purification with this hadith and this status of the Prophet, which we just presented to you and in the previous episode, who are they? For example, Ibn Hibban has done it, Bayhaqi has done it, Hakim al-Nishapuri—Hakim al-Nishapuri who is the author of Al-Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn. Haythami has recorded it, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani has recorded it, Dhahabi has recorded it. These two, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani and Dhahabi, are counted among the greatest scholars of Rijal (biographical evaluation). Very great, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani and Dhahabi. They are not among the minor scholars. They are considered the pillars of the science of Rijal among the Ahl-e-Tasannun. So these people, Dhahabi, Ibn Abi Asim, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Athir, Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, who is also the author of history and the author of tafsir (exegesis). Qurtubi, Jalaluddin al-Suyuti, who is a very great exegete, wrote two and a half tafsirs. Two are his own tafsirs, and half he wrote in partnership with someone. The two that are his own are Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur and the other is Tafsir al-Itqan. And the one written in partnership is called Tafsir al-Jalalayn. Meaning Jalaluddin al-Suyuti and Jalaluddin al-Mahalli wrote it together. So it is called Tafsir al-Jalalayn. Then Tabarani, as you know, Tabarani has the Ma'ajim, he has three dictionaries: Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir, Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir. So these people... this is a very long list. But we do not want the viewers to get tired of watching. Therefore, we have presented a very brief list to you; otherwise, if names were to be recorded, there are more than 150 scholars. More than 150. So, in terms of the chain of narration, it is very strong. Now, let's come to the argument of the Verse of Purification. The Verse of Purification points to the infallibility (Ismah) of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). The greatest proof of it is Ismah. Because what did the Prophet say in it? That is, the Quran says, 'Innamā yurīdu Allāhu'—it is Allah's intention. Right? Now, we will discuss each word, God willing, if Allah grants the ability, so that the matter becomes clear to you. How this noble verse argues for the Imamate and the immediate Caliphate of the Ahl al-Bayt. How does this noble verse point to it? First of all, the word 'Innamā'. The word 'Innamā', as people know, is used in Arabic for 'Inhisar' (exclusivity). Inhisar means only, limitation, to confine, that's it. 'Innamā yurīdu Allāhu liyudh'hiba'—Allah's intention is only this. Now, there is a debate on that intention regarding 'Innamā'. Some people want to dilute it, saying, 'No, this Innamā is only used for intention.' What does it have to do with the Ahl al-Bayt? Obviously, if you turn its referent towards Allah's intention, even then, if Allah intends to purify only the Ahl al-Bayt, then it is only for the Ahl al-Bayt because there was no one else in it. So, by saying 'Innamā', Allah has bestowed a very great honor upon the Ahl al-Bayt. This honor is for you alone, O Ahlulbayt, that Allah will keep you away from all filth, impurities, and sins, and will keep you as pure as is the right to be kept pure. It is absolutely clear, completely clear. Now, many people try to translate this in such a way that it means 'Allah will purify you.' What is their mischief in this? The mischief is that they want to imply that, God forbid, the Ahlulbayt used to commit sins before, and now they will not. God forbid. So, if someone translates it this way, they are forgetting that this does not only include the Ahlulbayt—meaning the Master of the Universe (Ali), Lady Zahra, and Hasan and Husayn (peace be upon them)—but the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is also included in it. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is also included. That is one argument, and the second thing is that Allah has not mentioned the purity of only the Ahlulbayt. In another verse, Allah commands Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) to purify the House of Kaaba, meaning to keep it pure for the worshippers. So, was the House of Kaaba impure, that it needed to be purified? Was it impure? No. Meaning, Allah—who built the House of Kaaba? Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) himself built it. But what is Allah commanding Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.)? 'Wa tahhir bayti' (And purify My House). 'Wa tahhir bayti lit-ta'ifeen' (And purify My House for those who perform Tawaf/worship). So, 'purify'—did Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), God forbid, keep the House of Kaaba impure? No. Rather, Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) himself is a Prophet. He made the House of Kaaba pure and kept it pure. But Allah announced its purity. This is one argument. Besides that, when we say 'Tawheed' (Monotheism), what does Tawheed mean? When you use the word 'Tawheed', it is from the 'Bab-e-Taf'eel' (form of verb), just like 'Tat-heer' (purification), so is 'Tawheed'. So when you say 'Tawheed', do you make Allah one? Was Allah two or three before this, and now we have made Him one? Hold this belief. Is it like that? Rather, no, Allah was already one. By affirming Tawheed, we have announced His Oneness. We have only announced His Oneness. When we say we are believers in Tawheed, we are 'Muwahhid' (monotheists). Therefore, those who talk like this—that 'purify' means He wasn't pure before—this is just mischief. It is nothing but mischief. The purpose is to somehow diminish the status of the Ahlulbayt. So, God willing, we will cover the remaining arguments in the next episode, Insha'Allah. And our final prayer is praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure, purified, and infallible family, and may His eternal curse be upon their enemies, their killers, those who usurped their rights, and those who denied their virtues and merits.

title: 🎁🎉 SIBT E AKBAR (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2026 🎁🎉 | 6-MAR-2026 🇮🇳 9.30 pm IST 🇬🇧 16.00 GMT
excerpt: This lecture, centered on the Sibt-e-Akbar Grand Quiz 2026, explores the profound spiritual status and virtues of Imam Hasan (a.s.) as the 'Speaking Quran.' It emphasizes the necessity of Wilayah (allegiance) to the Ahlulbayt for the acceptance of deeds and spiritual salvation. The session combines scholarly discourse on Quranic interpretation, the significance of Ziyarat, and the recitation of Dua-e-Iftitah with a community-focused quiz event celebrating the birth anniversary of Imam Hasan (a.s.).
content:
Allahumma wali-kal hujjati ibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala abaihi fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. A'udhu billahi minash shaitanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala... [unclear]... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. On behalf of the TSR team, we congratulate all of you on the auspicious birth of Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.) and welcome you all to this 'Grand Quiz: Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.)'. Let us all together offer congratulations on this joyous occasion in the court of the Fourteen Masumeen (a.s.) with a Salawat. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Respected viewers, in this blessed month, Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala revealed two Qurans, and both Qurans were revealed in the house of Janabe Fatima (s.a.). One Quran is the 'Quran-e-Samit' (Silent Quran), about which Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala says: 'Shahru Ramadanal ladhi unzila fihil Quran' (The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed). So, respected viewers, what is the book that Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala is revealing in this blessed month? Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala himself gives the answer in the Holy Quran: 'Ma shifa'un wa rahmatun lil mu'mineen wa la yaziduz zalimina illa khasara' (It is a healing and mercy for the believers, and it increases the wrongdoers only in loss). So, viewers, in this blessed month, Allah did not reveal only one part of the Thaqalain (the two weighty things), but the second part of the Thaqalain arrived in the house of Janabe Fatima (s.a.) on the 15th of this blessed month. But alas, the Muslim Ummah accepted the first part of the Thaqalain... but left the second part of the Thaqalain. In Surah Furqan, verse number 30, Allah Rabbul Izzat says: 'Wa qalar rasulu ya rabbi inna qawmit takhazul qur'ana mahjura' (And the Messenger will say, 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Quran as abandoned'). The Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will complain in the court of Allah on the Day of Judgment that after me, my Ummah abandoned the Quran. So, respected viewers, which is that Quran that the Ummah abandoned? That 'Quran-e-Natiq' (Speaking Quran) who was the cause of the creation of the creation. That Quran-e-Natiq due to whom there was worship and glorification. Due to whose existence, the confession of Allah's Oneness was taken. Due to whose existence, Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala bestowed honor upon the believers. Due to whose existence, believers will be given reward and punishment. This is that Quran-e-Natiq, Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.)... [Salawat]... who is the second link in the chain of Imamate and Wilayat. Sayyid-e-Shabab-e-Ahl-e-Jannah, Imam Hasan Mujtaba (a.s.), on the occasion of whose auspicious birth, the TSI team has come with the 'Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz'. In today's program, why is it necessary to state the virtues of Imam Hasan (a.s.)... why is it necessary to state his virtues, and there is a Ziyarat of Imam Hasan (a.s.), we will discuss this. Our brothers are present with us, Janab Kazim Sahab, Janab Abbas Tahid Sahab. Salam Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. So, respected viewers, before starting this discussion, let's take a look at some of the rules of this quiz. The quiz link is live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered before, click on the quiz link and register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prizes: all the answers to the questions must be correct. Among all the people who have given correct answers to all the questions, 18 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, who will be given these prizes. So, viewers, along with the rules of the quiz, let us tell you one thing: a surprise question... a surprise question... Let me tell you one thing: there is a surprise question where there is no question, only answers. So, if you want to answer that question, you must listen to this conversation very carefully, because at any point during this discussion, that question might be asked of you. So, listen to this conversation attentively. Kazim Bhai, I would like to start the conversation with you. Tell us, what is 'Fazeelat' (virtue/excellence)? Is this word 'Fazeelat' present in the Quran? And is this Fazeelat for specific individuals, or does Allah bestow Fazeelat upon everyone? Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. First of all, thank you for presenting this question to us. We also want to thank all the viewers, and especially, we want to offer congratulations on the blessed birth of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) along with a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. As you asked about Fazeelat, I would like to explain what it actually is. Fazeelat is not an ambiguous complimentary phrase, nor is it merely social respect, nor is it just popularity. It is not just social respect or popularity; rather, if viewed through the spirit of the Quran, it is the name of a divinely bestowed superiority. Allah (S.W.T.) says in the 33rd verse of Surah Al-i-Imran: 'Innallahas-tafa Adama wa Nuha wa Aala Ibrahima wa Aala Imrana 'alal-'alamin' (Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over the worlds). title: Ahkaam | Session # 9 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture addresses common questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting during Ramadan. The speaker clarifies rulings on breaking a fast due to extreme hardship, the requirements for Kaffarah (expiation) when a fast is broken intentionally, and the permissibility of rinsing one's mouth to alleviate thirst. The session emphasizes the importance of consulting Marja-e-Taqleed rulings for specific religious obligations.
content:
So please... [audio unclear/garbled]... 15th of Ramadan... [audio unclear/garbled]... the name of the grandson of the Prophet... The result of the upbringing of Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) was that... [audio unclear/garbled]... Islam is passing through its most difficult stages. Indeed, every Muslim will remain a seeker of Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) until the Day of Judgment. Gentlemen, today's lecture... [audio unclear/garbled]... in the presence of Mehdi Sahab Qibla... Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. And peace be upon you too. Rahmatullah Alaikum. Regarding this first question that has come from a history book, he asks: 'I am a student, and in the coming years, the fasts will fall during my exams. My concern is that while I will keep the fast during that time, I cannot study on an empty stomach. What does Sharia say about this?' The next point is regarding the ruling on fasting. The question is: 'What is the ruling on fasting?' The answer is that one of the conditions for fasting is that it should not cause 'Haraj' (extreme hardship). What does 'Haraj' mean? It means a situation that is unbearable. If you do not work, your life will be ruined. In such a situation, they say that if you have a genuine concern and... If you have a genuine concern and a very great loss is about to occur, and it is a loss that you cannot bear, then you may break the fast, but you will have to make it up later. This is a reminder. And the second point they mention is that if it is a matter of suffering a great loss, or if you are not willing to bear it—well, that is fine—but why would you suffer a loss? For example, if keeping the fast would endanger your child's life, then in that case, they say you cannot keep the fast. Take the fast, but later you must make it up. However, the decision to determine whether this is a 'great loss' or not, and how important this task is in my life, and what the consequence will be if I do not perform this task, is something you must decide. The question is about the food packets that are being distributed in the current atmosphere of the world. Can they be given? Look, our Marja-e-Taqleed has said that you must give food (grains). So, if you are looking at those food packets, if they contain different types of grains, that is fine. When you are eating grains, you eat what is commonly consumed. For us, the staple food is wheat or rice. So, if it is something that is eaten and falls under the category of grains, then you can give it. You cannot give money. So, if you make a food packet or anything else, if it contains grains, then there is no problem. The next question is: if a person intentionally breaks a fast or intentionally does not keep a fast, these are two different situations. So, the example given is: one case where it was broken intentionally, and one where it was not kept intentionally. Will the penalty for both be the same? No, see, if he does not keep it, he will have to make it up. That is a sin, and he will have to make it up. But the person who has broken the fast—what did he break it with? Was it with something forbidden (Haram) or something permissible (Halal)? If a person broke it by eating or drinking, for example, he must keep the fast, make it up, and also pay the Kaffarah (expiation). Even though Ayatollah Sistani, in ruling number 2054, has said that if a person intentionally breaks a fast in Ramadan, he is not a slave... okay, he must either feed a poor person, and if he does not have the strength for that, he must give 750 grams of grain. If he does not have the strength for that either, he should give as much as possible to the poor. If he cannot even do that, he should seek forgiveness from Allah. If he cannot even do that, he should seek forgiveness from Allah. Okay, so here it is said that if someone does it intentionally, they have to pay the Kaffarah. It is a Kaffarah. Okay, so in this situation, it cannot be that you just keep the fast; you have to make it up. One fast was missed, so the replacement is to give Kaffarah for the other. But if you take the Kaffarah, if you take it from something Haram, then it is three days... no, it is a Kaffarah for breaking the fast. And if it is a woman in a state where she is excused, in such a situation, she has to pay the Kaffarah. Why should she pay the Kaffarah? She should free a slave. Okay, and this is... if not, then the common man's... the Sharia has given a way. Thank you. Thank you. The fourth question that has come to us is: 'Can one rinse their mouth with water during a fast to reduce the intensity of thirst? If not, should we not even rinse our mouths as is done in Wudu, as it is Makruh (disliked)?' To reduce the intensity of thirst, you may rinse your mouth, or you may just wet your mouth. It is a Makruh act to do it excessively. And if water goes down the throat, the fast will be broken. On the other hand, while doing Wudu, if water accidentally goes down, it is not a problem. But you have to be careful. If you are rinsing your mouth, you must spit the water out. And if there is water... so this can be done. You can just wet your mouth to reduce the intensity of thirst. If it is done quietly, if it is like that, then... If it is like that, then for such a person, he can drink water, the fast will not be valid, but he can drink water, and later he can make it up. To reduce the intensity of thirst, and it is permissible. And we request all our viewers to send their questions to the group number, and Insha'Allah, we will answer them. Along with the issues, we also request our viewers to stay with us until the end.

title: Fadak & Our Responsibility | Watch EP3 of The #Fadak #Podcast | #DoNotMiss
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical usurpation of Fadak, a property granted to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker highlights that subsequent governments, including the Banu Umayya and Banu Abbas, acted in direct contradiction to the Prophet's explicit actions by seizing this land. The talk emphasizes the moral and spiritual responsibility of believers to recognize this injustice and choose their allegiance carefully for the Day of Judgment. Ultimately, it challenges listeners to consider whether they wish to stand with the oppressed or those who caused the Prophet's daughter to depart this world in anger.
content:
In this final episode, the topic of our discussion is Fadak and our responsibility. When the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were fully convinced and it is proven that this right belongs to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and this is the right of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and this right was usurped from them in a tyrannical manner, then did the governments that came later, the Banu Umayya and Banu Abbas, ever realize that this was the right of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) which was usurped from them, which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had granted them? It means that this was the property of the Princess (s.a.), the proof of which is the action of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) here, showing that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had given it to Hazrat Zahra (s.a.). So if you are... that property which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself had given, if you are taking that thing back, then you are directly contradicting the action of the Prophet. Now, if a Muslim has even an iota of intelligence, he will immediately reach the conclusion of who he would prefer to be resurrected with on the Day of Judgment. Does he want to be in the group of Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) or in the group of those people? He wants to be a part of those from whom Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) departed from this world in anger.

excerpt: This lecture explores Quranic verses that prophesy the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and the ultimate triumph of Islam. The speaker analyzes Surah An-Nur (55) and Surah At-Tawbah (32-33) through both Shia and Sunni interpretive traditions, emphasizing the role of Wilayah and the establishment of global justice. The session also includes a community quiz segment aimed at engaging viewers with the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt.
content:
TSR presents. Oh, oh, the hidden desire in the longing of my gaze, oh, oh, the peace of my heart. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us. The quiz link is now live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just need to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not rush to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first; the only condition for the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. Among all those who have provided correct answers to all questions, the winners of the episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear among today's winners or who missed an episode need not be disappointed, because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have provided correct answers to all questions in 7 out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone did not become a daily winner, but has provided correct answers in 7 out of 12 episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Dear viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. The title of our episode today is 'The Mention of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) in the Holy Quran.' Today, we will mention two verses of the Holy Quran that were revealed in honor of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). In Surah An-Nur, verse number 55, Allah says, 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds...' '...that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made those before them successors, and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has chosen for them.' When, in the plain of Ghadir Khumm, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin and said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyyun mawlahu' (Whomever I am his master, this Ali is also his master), at that time, Jibra'il (a.s.) descended with this verse: 'Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion.' That is, with the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Allah's religion was perfected, and Allah was pleased with that religion. In the second part of this verse, it is found: '...and will surely replace for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me.' '...and whoever disbelieves after that, then those are the defiantly disobedient.' Sayyid Sharaful-Din Husayni Astarabadi, in his book 'Ta'wil al-Ayat al-Zahira fi Fada'il al-Itrat al-Tahira,' narrates from Abdullah ibn Sinan. Abdullah ibn Sinan says that I asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) about the saying of Allah the Almighty: 'Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made those before them successors.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'This verse was revealed regarding Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.) from his progeny.' Regarding '...and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has chosen for them, and will surely replace for them, after their fear, security,' the Imam (a.s.) said: 'This refers to the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.).' Let us move towards the narrations of the Ahl al-Sunnah. The author of 'Tafsir Ibn Kathir' is Ismail ibn Kathir. In his book, he narrates from Jabir ibn Samurah: 'Jabir ibn Samurah says that I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) saying: The affairs of the people will continue as long as twelve men rule over them.' Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said a word that I could not hear. So I asked my father, 'What did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say?' He said: 'He (s.a.w.a.) said: All of them will be from Quraysh.' Further in the narration, Jabir ibn Samurah says: '...and among them will be the Mahdi (a.s.), whose name will match the name of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and his kunyah will be his (s.a.w.a.) kunyah. He will fill the earth with justice and equity just as it will have been filled with oppression and tyranny.' The second verse is from Surah At-Tawbah, verses 32 and 33. Allah says: 'They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth...' '...to manifest it over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it.' In the last part of this verse, Allah is saying that He will make the religion of Islam, i.e., the religion of truth, dominant over all religions. If we look from the time of the mission of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) until today, that time has not yet come when Allah has granted the religion of Islam dominance over all religions. So, when will this happen? Let us turn to the 'Quran-e-Natiq' (the Speaking Quran) to understand the fulfillment of the purpose of this verse of the 'Quran-e-Samit' (the Silent Quran) and look at the interpretation of this verse in the presence of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). This is a narration from Muhammad ibn Fudayl. From Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Abul-Hasan al-Madi (a.s.). He said: I asked him about the saying of Allah the Almighty: 'They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'They want to extinguish the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin with their mouths.' The narrator asked, i.e., Muhammad ibn Fudayl: 'And Allah will perfect His light?' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'Allah will perfect the Imamate.' Then Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) recited this verse of Surah At-Taghabun: 'So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'By the Light, it means the Imam.' Then the narrator asked further: 'He is the one who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'He is the one who commanded His Messenger regarding the Wilayah of his successor, and the Wilayah is the religion of truth. The Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is the religion of truth, and whoever does not accept this Wilayah is not upon the religion of truth.' Then the narrator asks about this part of the verse: 'To manifest it over all religion.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'He will manifest it over all religions at the time of the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.).' Qala Yaqulullahu, 'Wallahu mutimmu nurihi' (And Allah will perfect His light) regarding the Wilayah of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). He (a.s.) stated that Allah will perfect His light through the Wilayah of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). 'Walau karihal kafirun bi-wilayati Ali (a.s.)' (And even if the deniers dislike the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)). Let us look at the tradition of the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni scholars). Tafsir al-Baghawi, authored by Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Mas'ud, narrates from Abu Hurayrah and Dahhak: 'Wa qala Abu Hurayrah wa-Dahhak wa dhalika inda nuzuli Isa bin Maryam (a.s.)' (And Abu Hurayrah and Dahhak said this will be at the time of the descent of Isa bin Maryam (a.s.)). 'La yabqa ahlu dini illa dakhala fil-Islam' (No follower of any religion will remain except that they will enter into Islam). The second Tafsir from the Ahl-e-Tasannun regarding this verse is Tafsir al-Tabari. It also contains a narration from Abu Hurayrah: 'An Abi Hurayrah fi qawlihi liyuzhirahu alad-dini kulli qala khuruju Isa bin Maryam' (From Abu Hurayrah regarding His saying 'to manifest it over all religion', he said it is the emergence of Isa bin Maryam). That is, when Isa (a.s.) descends, Allah will make this religion dominant over all other religions. There is a very surprising point here in both narrations, whereas all Muslims agree that through Imam Mahdi (a.s.), Allah will establish justice and fairness across the entire earth. But here, in these two narrations, the name of Isa (a.s.) has been mentioned, while the name of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has not been mentioned. There is no doubt that Isa (a.s.) will also arrive, but Allah will establish His government in this world through Imam Mahdi (a.s.). Let us all pray together to Allah to hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and count us among his helpers and supporters. Amin Ya Rabbal Alamin. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr. Help us and do not destroy us. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Now the time has arrived for which you all were waiting impatiently. That is, the announcement of the daily lucky draw winners of the Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz, which is being conducted through our computerized lucky draw system. Those who will receive a prize of ₹1000 Indian Rupees, their names are on your screen. Sajiya Zainab from Bengaluru. Ru from, Zahra Syed from Mumbai, Arshiya Banu from Bengaluru, Binte Zahra from Azamgarh, Fazila Amir Ali Ghabrane from Bhavnagar, Mohammad Rizvi from Prayagraj. Many congratulations to all these winners. If someone's name did not appear in today's winners, there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz will remain live until the end of the link series. And

title: A Dua For All Needs-Dua Abu Hamza Somali | Part 1-Who Was Abu Hamza Somali? ابو حمزہ ثمالی کون تھے؟
excerpt: This lecture introduces the profound spiritual significance of Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali, a supplication taught by the fourth Imam, Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.). The speaker explores the life and status of Abu Hamza al-Thumali, a highly trusted companion who served four Imams and was compared by the Ahlulbayt to figures like Salman al-Muhammadi and Luqman al-Hakim. The talk emphasizes that his 'service' to the Imams was defined by his dedication to learning and propagating their teachings, a model for modern believers.
content:
A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim minash-shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran, wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an, wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil farajahum waj'alna min ansarihim wa atba'ihim, la taj'alna min muhammadin wa tarihin. Amma ba'd, faqad qala mawlana Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (a.s.): 'Ma min qatratin ahabba ilallahi 'azza wa jalla min qatrati dam'in fi sawadil layli makhafatan minallahi la yurad biha ghayruha.' In the journey of recognition (Ma'rifat), the supplication we are to discuss today is a masterpiece of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and such a miracle that after its recitation, its words and meanings are so overflowing with the recognition of Allah. Overflowing with the recognition of Allah, that if a person truly recites this supplication with a sincere heart, it is not impossible that he will become so enlightened that he will be able to traverse the stages of the recognition of Allah. And the name of that supplication is Dua Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Before moving towards this supplication, let us first try to know a little about the famous companion who was taught this supplication. Who was that personality? What was his status and rank near the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)? The fourth Imam, Hazrat Sayyid al-Sajjad Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), chose Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali for the teaching of this supplication. Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali, his name was Thabit ibn Dinar, and the first time he met the fourth Imam (a.s.) was after the tragedy of Karbala. At that time, he was a young man. He was among the devotees of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If one wants to see a glimpse of his status, rank, and his position near the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then... If one wants to see a glimpse of it, then it can be estimated from the fact that the fourth Imam (a.s.) pointed out the grave of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali and took him along. Pointing towards the grave of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), he said, 'Hadha qabru jaddi Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Abu Hamza, this is the grave of our grandfather Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.).' Now, if we look at the books of Rijal regarding Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali, Sheikh Tusi (r.a.) writes about him in his book 'Fihrist'. In it, he writes, 'Abu Hamza al-Thumali' was his kunya, and he writes that he was a 'thiqah' narrator. 'Thiqah' refers to the narrator who is most trusted, meaning he was a reliable narrator. And in the same book, he writes that he had three books. He had three books: one is a book of Tafsir, the Tafsir of the Quran by Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali; one book is 'Nawadir', meaning the one that contains rare hadith; and the third book is 'Zuhd'. These three books were with Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali. Apart from this, the late Najashi writes about him in his 'Rijal al-Najashi' that... In 'Rijal al-Najashi', he writes that he met Ali ibn al-Husayn, Abu Ja'far, Abu Abdillah, and Abu al-Hasan (a.s.), meaning he witnessed the era of four Imams: the fourth Imam, the fifth Imam, the sixth Imam, and the seventh Imam (a.s.). And he narrated traditions from them, from all four Masum Imams (a.s.), from the fourth Imam to the seventh Imam (a.s.). And the late Najashi further writes that 'wa kana min khiyar as-habina', he was one of our best companions, meaning one of the best Shias. 'Wa kana', and among them, he was one of the most reliable individuals, 'far-riwayati wal-hadith', and among those who could be trusted the most regarding traditions and hadith, he was one of those individuals, Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali. And from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), this hadith is found regarding Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali, that the Imam says that the example of Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali in his time, or Abu Hamza in his time, was like Salman was in his time, Janabe Salman al-Muhammadi (ridwanullahi ta'ala 'alayh). That was the status and rank of Janabe Abu Hamza al-Thumali, and this is also... Hamza was Sumali, and these are not just my words or yours; Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the truthful one of the family of Muhammad (a.s.), is speaking about the personality of Janab Abu Hamza Sumali. Furthermore, if you look at the books of Rijal, Allama Hilli (may Allah have mercy on him), citing Rijal-e-Kashi, writes that we have heard this hadith from Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.). The narrator states that Abu Hamza was, in his time, like Luqman was in his time—the same Luqman about whom a full Surah exists in the Holy Quran, Surah Luqman, the 31st chapter of the Quran. He was famous for his wisdom; he is called Luqman al-Hakim. Imam Rida (a.s.) gave the same comparison to Janab Abu Hamza Sumali, that he was the Luqman of his time. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says he was the Salman of his time, and Imam Rida (a.s.) says he was the Luqman of his time. Janab Abu Hamza Sumali was no ordinary personality. And then Imam Rida (a.s.) further says why this was so: 'Because he served four of our Imams.' He served four of them. Now, pausing here, a thought comes to mind: nowhere in any hadith book, history book, or Rijal book will you find that Janab Abu Hamza Sumali used to come to the house of the Ahlulbayt as a slave or lived in their house. Despite this, what is Imam Rida (a.s.) saying? That he served four of our Imams. So, what was this service? This service was learning the hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and teaching these hadiths to others and conveying them. This means that whoever enters this field, learns the hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), teaches these hadiths to others, and spreads and conveys them to others, is actually, in reality, performing the service of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Even today, the exact same example is found; the same thing is applicable today. That whoever in this era reads and learns the hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and goes and propagates these hadiths to others, it is as if he is performing the service of Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.) in this era. That was the service that Janab Abu Hamza Sumali performed, and he served four of us: Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, and... Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, and Ja'far ibn Muhammad—three Imams, the fourth, fifth, and sixth Imams (a.s.). And then Imam Rida (a.s.) further says that he also spent some time during the era of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s.). He passed away in the year 150 Hijri. This is what the scholars of Rijal write. Now let us see what the Infallible Imams, like Imam Rida (a.s.), said. We have seen the hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) as well. Here is another hadith regarding what Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says about him. The narrator of this hadith is Janab Abu Basir. Abu Basir says: 'I entered into the presence of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), and as soon as I arrived, the Imam (a.s.) immediately asked me, "What is Abu Hamza Sumali doing these days, or how is he?"' Janab Abu Basir says, 'I said, "O my master, I left him in a state where he was ill."' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'When you return to Abu Hamza, convey my salaam to him and inform him that he will pass away in the month of [so-and-so] on the [so-and-so] day.' On the [so-and-so] day of the month of [so-and-so], he will pass away. Then, as the Imam said this, Janab Abu Basir immediately inquired and asked, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, O my master! By Allah, Abu Hamza Sumali has great affection for you, great love, and he truly loves you. And he is indeed among your true Shias.' As Janab Abu Basir said this, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'You are telling the truth.' To be validated by Imam Sadiq, the truthful one of the family of Muhammad—'Yes, he truly loves us, he is our Shia'—what else does he need in this world? Upon this, Janab Abu Basir asked again, 'Master, will your Shias be with you?' The Imam said—and this is a message for all of us from Imam Sadiq (a.s.)—the Imam says, 'Yes, they will certainly be with us if that Shia possesses the fear of Allah, observes the traditions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and protects himself from sins. Then, when he performs these deeds, he will be with us, occupying our rank.' Then these people say that when we returned... Then these people say that when we returned and gave all those messages to Abu Hamza, they state that the sentence of the narration is: 'Only a few days, only a short time did Janab Abu Hamza spend in the world until he passed away.' But when the time of Sahar (dawn) would come, he would present himself in the court of Allah through this Dua-e-Sahar. The fourth Imam (a.s.) taught the method of asking from Allah, how to ask in the court of Allah. Praying for parents, Janab Abu Hamza Sumali taught; praying for the believers, you will find in this Dua-e-Sahar of Abu Hamza Sumali. If you want the good of this world and the hereafter, you will find it in this Dua-e-Sahar of Abu Hamza Sumali. If you want the opportunity for Hajj and Ziyarat, it is in this Dua-e-Sahar of Abu Hamza Sumali.

title: E'teraazaate Ghadeer Ep#02: 1 Lakh Se Zyaada Sahaaba Ghadeer Ke Baad Kahan Ghaayab Ho Gaye?
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological controversy surrounding the events following the Ghadir Khumm declaration. It examines why a large number of companions seemingly disregarded the Prophet's appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.) by analyzing historical precedents of disobedience during the Prophet's lifetime. The speaker utilizes Sunni sources to argue that worldly attachments and conscious choices led to the abandonment of the Ghadir pledge, as referenced in the Hadith of the Pond.
content:
He la he la he la... Noor-e-Ali Zahir, Ya'lamu azhar min shamshi, Ali Zahir, Ya'lamu azhar min shamshi... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat son of Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Once again, we welcome you all to the second episode of 'Eterazat-e-Ghadir'. As we mentioned yesterday, today we will present ourselves with another objection. So let us move towards our second objection and see what the answers to it should be. The objection is that in the field of Ghadir-e-Khumm, more than one hundred thousand companions were present, who not only saw the whole event with their own eyes but stayed there for three days, performed Bay'ah (allegiance) at the hands of Ali (a.s.), and also offered congratulations to him for becoming the Mawla. So, immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), where did these one hundred thousand companions go? And if they were all present there, why did they not turn back on their Bay'ah? Did none of these companions object? Yes, this is the objection, this is the question, and to answer it, we have Tanveer Bhai with us. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. How are you all? Alhamdulillah, how are you? Your prayers. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us. First of all, we offer congratulations to the viewers on Eid-e-Akbar, Eid-e-Ghadir. And Abul Hasan Bhai, the question raised here, we will answer it in two parts, Insha'Allah. Insha'Allah. So, the first objection raised is: why did no one object when Imam Ali (a.s.) was not made the Caliph, even though the Messenger of Allah had announced it among more than one hundred thousand companions? Yes. So, the first thing is that those people cover up the fact that there were no objections, just to show that whatever happened after the Messenger was absolutely correct. So that if people come to know that there were objections, people will study it, and then questions will arise that people will have to answer. Yes. Okay, then the matter is, why did no elder companion object to this? Yes. So, all Muslims are convinced that if Ali (a.s.) is not the most superior companion, he is counted among the most superior companions. Hmm, hmm. Okay. So, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) himself objected to this. And according to some narrations, for two months, and according to some narrations, for six months after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he did not perform Bay'ah to anyone. Yes. And we find the reference for this in the book Sahih Bukhari, Book 64, Hadith 278. Good. This is present in the book of Ahl-e-Tasannun themselves. Yes. It is found in their books that as soon as Amir al-Mu'minin became Caliph, he did not perform their Bay'ah. For six months, Ali (a.s.) did not perform Bay'ah to anyone. Yes. And I would also like to tell our viewers that all these references taken are from the books of Ahl-e-Tasannun, and all these references are available on the internet. Yes. Okay. Today's youth are quite familiar with the internet and mobile apps, so they can go and search for these things themselves, and the result will be in front of them. Yes, absolutely. So, first of all, that there were no objections; Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) himself objected. He objected himself. Okay. As for the matter that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) openly declared Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) as his successor and his Caliph, why did people not obey him and not perform Bay'ah to him? So, this is nothing new. We find numerous such incidents in the life of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) where people openly disobeyed him. Yes. You must have heard the name of the Battle of Uhud. Absolutely, the Battle of Uhud is a famous battle of Islam. Yes. Okay. It is found that the Messenger of Allah had deployed some of his companions in a place, there was a pass, there was a trench, and he had told them: 'In ra'aitumuna yaqtufun tairu fala tabrahu makanakum' (If you see birds hovering around us—meaning when do birds hover? When corpses are lying there—meaning even if we are killed, even if we are martyred, do not leave your place). Yes. And the next sentence of the Hadith is: 'And if you see that we have achieved victory over the enemy, even then do not move from your place.' Meaning they had very strict instructions that they were not to move from there at all. Very strict instructions, clear instructions, and both extremes were mentioned: if we are martyred or if we are successful, you must not move from your place until you are given this message. Yes. Okay. But if we look at history, it is found that as soon as people saw that the Muslims were achieving success, people left that place and fled. Yes. Due to which 70 Muslims were martyred in that battle. And the reference for this is Sahih Bukhari, Book 56, Hadith number 245. Meaning, it is found in their books that the companions themselves opposed and were against the word of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Absolutely. And as I said, this was absolutely clear disobedience. When you were told and given the situation that you should not move from there, still people moved from there, and the Muslims had to face the loss. Yes. A couplet by a famous poet of India, Kaifi Dangipuri Sahab, also comes to mind here: 'Sab Uhud mein bhaag khade hue, bas juz ek Zaigham-e-Kibriya, Koi gird-o-pesh-e-Nabi na tha, na to sasur hi na hi sale hi.' (Everyone fled in Uhud, except for the Lion of Allah, there was no one around the Prophet, neither father-in-law nor brother-in-law). Wah. Okay. So, the result of the battle was that 70 Muslims were martyred, many people left their places and fled, only Imam Ali (a.s.) was present there. So, this is an example where people disobeyed the Messenger of Allah. Here, viewers, you get to see that if someone does not obey the message of the Messenger of Allah, then undoubtedly, it causes loss, both to Islam and to that person. So, in the same way, perhaps if someone does not obey Ali (a.s.), then undoubtedly, because of that, his religion also comes into danger, and he also suffers loss, just as we saw that in this battle, due to not obeying the Messenger of Allah, 70 Muslims were killed. Yes. The second incident is also a famous incident that every Muslim would know, and that is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. When the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah happened, yes, and the Muslims were not allowed to enter Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ordered his companions, the other Muslims, to slaughter their sacrificial animals there. Yes. But the companions did not obey him. Yes. And the Messenger of Allah became angry at this. Okay. And then he went to one of his wives, and seeing him in this state, she said: 'Man azabaka azab hullahu' (Whoever angered you, may Allah be angry with him). Then the Messenger of Allah said: 'Faqala mali la azab wa ana amuru bishai fala yuttabe' (Why should I not be angry when I command something and they do not follow me?). Yes. Meaning, this is the second occasion where the Messenger of Allah gave clear instructions, but people did not obey him, and the result was that the Messenger of Allah became angry, and people saw that he was angry and went to his wife, but people still disobeyed him. Yes. Okay. This reference we find in Amali Ibn Bushran, Volume 1, page number 70. This is also found in the book of Ahl-e-Tasannun. Yes. Okay. So, this was the second incident. So, from this, we also get a message that if the word of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is not obeyed, then he becomes angry. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will be angry because he himself gave this order that after me, you... consider Ali (a.s.) as your Mawla, your Imam. So, the person who does not accept this, it means he is angering the Messenger of Allah. Absolutely. And slaughtering a sacrificial animal is a small thing, but not accepting the one whom the Messenger of Allah has made his successor, so imagine how great his anger would be. These were two incidents. Another incident is found that the Messenger of Allah was traveling with his companions, and it was the month of Ramadan, so the Messenger of Allah told the people to bring water for him. The Messenger of Allah showed the cup of water to the people and then drank it, so as to tell them that one should not fast during a journey in the month of Ramadan. But still, people disobeyed him and remained on their fast. After that, the Messenger of Allah said a sentence for those people: 'Ula'ika usat, ula'ika usat' (These people are disobedient, these people are disobedient). And the reference for this is also found in the book of Ahl-e-Tasannun, Sahih Muslim, Book number 5, Hadith 672. Yes. Meaning, the Messenger of Allah said not to fast in the month of Ramadan, but still, people continued the fast. Yes. Okay. So, if you look at all these, these are clear instructions. Yes. Okay. Apart from this, we find other incidents that will perhaps be covered in our future episodes, but this shows that in the life of the Messenger, they disobeyed him, so what would they not do after his passing? Yes. Okay. And the final point in this matter is that since people did not obey the Messenger of Allah and disobeyed him, that is why it is found in a Hadith that on the Day of Judgment, the companions will be brought to the Pond of Kawthar, and then they will be taken from there and thrown into Hell. When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will see this, he will say: 'These are my companions. Why are you throwing them into Hell?' Okay. So, a voice will come: 'La tadri ma ahdathu ba'daka' (You do not know what these people did after you). Meaning, the companions of the Messenger, whom people consider reliable, okay, people know them as famous, they will be thrown into Hell. And this reference is also found in the book of Ahl-e-Tasannun, Sahih Bukhari, Book 92, Hadith number 2. Yes. Okay. Meaning, people will do some things after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) because of which they will be thrown into Hell. Okay. And as I said, this is also found in the book of Ahl-e-Tasannun. If this matter were found in Shia books, I don't know how many fatwas would have been issued against us. Absolutely. Okay. So, to conclude in the end, why does all this happen? It is found in Hadiths that a person disobeys the Messenger of Allah when there is love for the world in his heart. So, it is this love for the world that made them let go of the hem of Ali (a.s.) and they held onto the hem of others. Thank you very much, Tanveer Bhai. Viewers, so we saw that more than 100,000 companions were undoubtedly present there, and they all had heard this announcement, and it was not that all those people had forgotten; rather, they knowingly did not turn back on their Bay'ah. And we have seen other such incidents where people, the companions, disobeyed the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). So, this is a second example where, even after hearing such a great announcement, people disobeyed the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Apart from this, nothing else. With this, our episode ends here. Insha'Allah, tomorrow we will be present with our third objection and its answer. Until then, goodbye. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Sab Se Zyaada Gumraah Kaun Hai? | Ahle Zikr Se Poocho
excerpt: This lecture explores the Quranic definition of the most astray individual, specifically focusing on Surah Al-Qasas, verse 50. The speaker explains that following personal desires over divine guidance leads to the deepest form of misguidance. By referencing the teachings of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), the lecture emphasizes that true guidance is found exclusively through the Ahlulbayt, who are the designated Imams of the era.
content:
[Music] A'udhu billahi as-sami' al-'alim min ash-shaytan ar-rajim. Bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim. Salli 'ala waliyyika... Allah says in the 50th verse of Surah Qasas: 'And who is more astray than one who follows his own desire without guidance from Allah?' Two things are mentioned in this verse: one is the person who is most astray because he followed his own desire; the second thing is the guidance of Allah. After all, what is this guidance that is for every servant from Allah, leaving which is the cause of the greatest misguidance? Come, for the explanation of this, let us turn to those whom the Lord of the Worlds has commanded us to ask in the Holy Quran, that is, the Ahl al-Dhikr, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Imam Ja'far Sadiq (a.s.) says in the interpretation of this verse: In the interpretation, he says: 'The one who prefers his own opinion over the guidance of the Imam of guidance is the most astray.' That is, whoever abandons those whom Allah has made Imams—those Imams besides whose door there is no other door to guidance—and follows his own will or the Imams created by himself, he is not only astray but the most astray. It is the prayer to the Lord of the Worlds that He hastens the reappearance of the guide of our time and the Imam of our era, Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.), and grants us the opportunity to spend our lives under the shadow of the guidance of him and his pure and holy ancestors. Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.
