title: EP07 | Aakhiruzzamaan aur Panaah-e-Kainaat (a.t.f.s) | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉 #ImamMahdiعج
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual challenges and moral complexities of the era of Ghaybah, emphasizing the importance of seeking refuge in Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). It highlights the signs of the end times, such as the normalization of sin and the decline of moral values, while urging believers to maintain Taqwa and steadfastness. The session also serves as part of a mega quiz initiative, encouraging participants to deepen their knowledge of the Imam to qualify for a pilgrimage to Iraq.
content:
TSR presents. O my longing, O longing, O desire hidden in the longing of my gaze. O comfort of my heart. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us. The quiz link is now live and is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. However, those whose names did not appear in today's winners or if an episode was missed, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, meaning the lucky draw winner for the pilgrimage to Iraq, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all questions in 7 out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone did not become a daily winner but has given correct answers in 7 out of 12 episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the pilgrimage to Iraq. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside in Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. In this episode of 'Panah-e-Kainat' (Refuge of the Universe), the discussion we will have today is that the era of Ghaybah (Occultation) is a very difficult era. It has been prophesied in traditions. Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) have explicitly told their followers that this era will be a very difficult era and one will have to be very patient in it, and how a person should make themselves such that, while enduring the difficulties of this era, they can then make themselves among the helpers, companions, and associates of Imam-e-Zamana (may Allah hasten his noble relief). So let us look at one or two Hadiths that discuss the difficult era of Ghaybah. And the purpose of this, as submitted, is that when a believer faces hardship or trouble in this era, they should not panic, but rather, as much as possible, they should get closer to the Imam, get closer to Imam-e-Zamana (may Allah hasten his noble relief), hold fast to him, and hold fast to the Ahlulbayt (peace be upon them), and take refuge in their protection because they are the best place of refuge, and under no circumstances, God forbid, should they fall prey to despair. So let us look at the first Hadith, which is from Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him), where the Imam says: 'A man came to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) says that a man came to Hazrat-e-Amir (peace be upon him) and complained to him about the length of the rule of oppression. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to him: 'By Allah, what you are expecting, what you are hoping for—meaning, for example, that there will be a good government, a government of truth, and a government of justice—all your expectations will not be fulfilled until the people of falsehood perish, and the ignorant vanish, and the pious (Ahl-e-Taqwa) are safe. And it will not happen until one of you is such that one of his feet is on the ground, and the value of his companion, the value of his friend, is less than a dead body in the eyes of its owner.' Meaning, human life will have no value. The situation will be so bad that human life will have no value. And at that time, the Master (Ali) wants to say that there will be massacres everywhere, looting everywhere, people will be troubled, they will kill each other, there will be wars all over the world, and human life will have no worth or value. Meaning, the situation will be so bad, so bad. This is the tradition of the Imam that I have presented to you. Now, another sermon of the Master of the Universe (Ali) from Nahj al-Balagha, Sermon number 187, the Master says: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for them.' Look, the Master of the Universe is saying, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed.' Meaning, what kind of individuals are they for whom the Master of the Universe is sacrificing his parents? 'For a group whose names are known in the heavens, but they are unknown on the earth.' On earth, they are of unknown status; people do not know them. Meaning, the people of the earth do not value them, while the people of the heavens are aware of their value. 'Know that you should expect what will happen from the turning away of your affairs.' Just expect at that time that your situation will be very bad, 'Idbar-e-Umoorikum' (the turning away of your affairs), meaning there will be a lot of trouble, trouble in everything. Meaning, in financial conditions, in livelihood, in relationships, in society, in every respect, there will be an atmosphere of chaos. The Master is saying, 'From the turning away of your affairs and in...' And you will cut off ties of kinship with one another. You will cut off ties of kinship with one another. This, and the phrase 'istimal-e-sigarakum' (the rise of the lowly) is a strange sentence. Those who are of low status will become high. They will have value and worth. Those who are of low character will have value and worth. For example, one who has neither knowledge, nor understanding, nor anything at all. What does he have? Only 'lahw-o-laib' (amusement and play), sports, and the absurd things of the world. All such people will have a name, they will have value and worth. People will actually praise them. Just as we see today. In society, all over the world, there is this kind of atmosphere. Mawla (a.s.) says, "ذَاكَ حَيْثُ تَكُونُ ضَرْبَةُ السَّيْفِ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِ أَحْوَنُ مِنَ الدِّرْهَمِ" (That is when a sword strike on a believer will be easier/cheaper than a dirham). That same sentence from the previous hadith, that at that time, striking a believer on the neck will be easier, cheaper than a dirham. Cheaper than a dirham. The killing of a believer, meaning the value of a believer's life, will be cheaper than a dirham. Meaning, there will be no value for the life of a believer. And then he says, "مِنْ حِلِّهِ ذَاكَ حَيْثُ يَكُونُ الْمُعْطَى أَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا مِنَ الْمُعْطِي" (That is when the one receiving will have a greater reward than the one giving). This will be at a time when the one being given to—meaning the one begging—will have more value than the one who is giving to others. Meaning, the era will be completely upside down. "حَيْثُ تَذْكُرُونَ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَرَابٍ" (Where you will be intoxicated without wine). Meaning, these will be the conditions when you will be intoxicated. But this intoxication will not be due to wine. This intoxication will not be due to wine. Rather, what will it be due to? "بَلْ مِنَ النِّعْمَةِ وَالنَّعِيمِ" (Rather, it will be from the blessings and bounties). Rather, this intoxication will be the intoxication of blessings. Those who will be gifted with Allah's blessings, those whom Allah will bless with His bounties, they will be so immersed in the intoxication of those blessings. There will be so much pride, so much arrogance. And they will trample upon Allah's commandments so much. Sins will increase so much that they will not even have the sense of what they are doing. They will not even know. Such sins, such destruction all around, moral destruction, destruction of religion. No one will care about religion. Just as it has come in other traditions, that in the name of religion, wrong things will be done. Just as we are observing today, what is happening in the name of religion. That which is completely against the Quran and Hadith is happening in the name of religion. Meaning, mixed gatherings are happening in the name of religion. Everywhere, and they say, 'Brother, you don't understand, this is the culture here, it has to be done here, and all this happens, it's fine here, it's acceptable here, or so-and-so scholar said we can do it, there is no issue.' It is not about this scholar or that scholar. Does the Sharia permit it or not? So Mawla (a.s.) says you will be so immersed in the intoxication of religion—meaning you will be so immersed in the intoxication. This is not because of wine. "وَتَحْلِفُونَ مِنْ غَيْرِ اضْطِرَارٍ" (And you will swear oaths without necessity). And you will swear false oaths. Meaning, there will be no need, yet you will swear oaths. Swearing an oath is not a light matter in Sharia that anyone can just swear. One should not swear an oath in Sharia unless it is a Shari'i oath. But it will happen, Mawla (a.s.) says that everyone will swear oaths and will swear on anything. "وَتَكْذِبُونَ مِنْ غَيْرِ إِحْرَاجٍ" (And you will lie without embarrassment). And you will lie without necessity. Meaning, what is meant by 'without necessity' is that even if there is no 'taqiyya' (dissimulation), you will still lie; even if there is no need to save a life, you will still lie. You will lie in every situation and will justify your lies with different names. This is also happening nowadays in the name of religion. That, 'Brother, we used *tawriya* (equivocation).' We keep lying and say we used *tawriya*. Oh brother, look at what you are doing. Is it not that, God forbid, religion is being toyed with in the name of *tawriya*? So lies are being told, and people are lying openly. They are lying in trade, people are lying in business. They are lying in kinship, lying is common everywhere. Mawla (a.s.) says, "تَكْذِبُونَ مِنْ غَيْرِ إِحْرَاجٍ إِذَا عَزَّكُمُ الْبَلَاءُ كَمَا يَعُدُّ الْقَتَبُ غَارِبَ الْبَعِيرِ" (You will lie without embarrassment when calamities surround you, just as the saddle constantly strikes the hump of the camel). At that time, calamities will keep coming upon you continuously, just like the hump on a camel, the saddle that is on the camel, it constantly strikes its back. As you have seen, the 'qazawa' (saddle) of a camel—so whenever the camel walks, that saddle strikes its hump, its back. Mawla (a.s.) says when you do all this, calamities will keep breaking upon you continuously. Likewise, one after another, calamities. In other words, if someone is truly doing all these things that are mentioned, and if calamities are coming upon him, then he should not blame anyone except himself. Meaning, if he is not doing all this and still faces trouble and distress, then he should pray to Allah. And make the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) his 'waseela' (means). So that his distress is removed, and Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), who is the Imam of the time, who is the 'Kahf-e-Haseen' (fortified refuge), who is the 'Ghiyath al-Mustaghithin' (helper of those who cry for help)—meaning the best refuge, Imam-e-Zamana—so take refuge in him. Mawla (a.s.) says, "مَا أَطْوَلَ هَذَا الْعَنَاءَ" (How long is this suffering). Because when a person faces trouble, every single moment is difficult. He counts every single moment. "مَا أَطْوَلَ هَذَا الْعَنَاءَ" (How long is this suffering), "وَأَبْعَدَ هَذَا الرَّجَاءَ" (And how far is this hope). And he will think that the reappearance (Zuhur) is very far. He will consider the Zuhur to be very far. That is why in the Quran and in the traditions, or even in Dua-e-Ahad, we read, "إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا" (They see it as far, but We see it as near). Those who are faithless will consider the Zuhur to be very far. But those who are enlightened will consider the Zuhur to be near. "وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا" (And We see it as near). One should never despair of Allah's mercy. Then Mawla (a.s.) says, "إِنَّمَا مَثَلِي بَيْنَكُمْ كَمَثَلِ السِّرَاجِ فِي الظُّلْمَةِ" (My example among you is like a lamp in the darkness). What is the example of the Imam? It is that of a lamp that gives light. Provided that people pay attention to it. In that era, it was Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Today, it is the son of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), whose example is like that lamp. "يَسْتَضِيءُ بِهِ" (That people seek light from it). Look, "يَسْتَضِيءُ" (He who seeks light), the one who seeks the 'zawq', the 'ziya' (light), the 'noor' (light). Whoever seeks the light, for him there will be light. "مَنْ وَلَجَهَا" (Whoever enters it), whoever enters this house, whoever enters this room. "فَاسْمَعُوا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ" (So listen, O people). Mawla (a.s.) says, 'O people, listen to my words.' Look, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) always used to tell their followers to listen to our words. But there were very few people who paid heed. Very few people. They say to Allah, "O people, listen," and remember this, memorize it. "وَأَحْضِرُوا آذَانَ قُلُوبِكُمْ تَفْهَمُوا" (And bring the ears of your hearts so that you may understand). And apply the ears of your intellect so that you may understand what I am saying. Go to the Ahlulbayt, take light from them, learn from them. And then there is another hadith in this series, which is in Usul al-Kafi, Volume 1, Page 370, and Hadith number 3. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) says, "O Mansur," he says to Mansur ibn Hazim, "O Mansur, this affair (Zuhur) will not come to you except after despair." O Mansur, this affair, meaning the Zuhur, will not happen until people generally become desperate. People will become desperate in every way, they will be troubled. Such oppression and injustice will increase, such oppression and injustice will increase, and they will have experimented with every kind of government. But none will work for the people. Every person who comes into power will be for his own authority, for his own benefit, and will come and be so immersed in intoxication, the intoxication of power will be so dominant over him that he will not care for anyone. "وَلا وَاللهِ" (And no, by Allah), and this Zuhur will not happen "حَتَّى تُمَيَّزُوا" (Until you are distinguished/tested) until you are tested, until it is distinguished who is truly a believer and who is not a believer. Who is the one who remains on his religion, who is the one who starts flowing with the tide of the time. "وَلا وَاللهِ حَتَّى تُمَحَّصُوا" (And no, by Allah, until you are sifted/purified) and no, by God, no, until you are sifted, you will be sifted, it will be seen, you will be tested. Who among you is right, who among you is wrong. "وَلا وَاللهِ" (And no, by Allah), then look, the Imam is swearing a Shari'i oath, by God, no, the Zuhur will not happen until "حَتَّى يَشْقَى مَنْ يَشْقَى وَيَسْعَدَ مَنْ يَسْعَدَ" (Until the wretched one is wretched and the fortunate one is fortunate). Until the 'shaqi' (wretched) manifests his wretchedness and the 'sa'id' (fortunate) becomes fortunate. 'Shaqi' means hell-bound. 'Shaqi' means hell-bound, that the one who is wretched, the one who is 'shaqi', meaning unfortunate, manifests his misfortune, his being hell-bound in the world, manifests it. And 'sa'id' means heaven-bound. So the one who is heaven-bound will prove his being heaven-bound, meaning he will remain on the truth, will remain on the religion, and this 'shaqi' will be this 'shaqi', meaning he will manifest his wretchedness, will manifest his being hell-bound. So it is absolutely clear that the Imam says that this Zuhur will not happen until humans are sifted. Until they are tested. Meaning, the era of 'Ghaybah' (Occultation) will be very difficult. The era of Ghaybah will not be easy. Now the question arises, should a human despair of Allah's mercy? Like others who are not on the path of truth. So if we study the traditions, study the hadith of the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.), then we find that no, it should never be like that. Rather, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have told us how we can save ourselves from this turbulent atmosphere, by keeping our religion intact, and with success, with victory, we can be triumphant. And what is that method? The very first thing the Imam said is, "Akthirud-du'a bi-ta'jilil-faraj, fa-innahu dhalika farajukum." Pray for the reappearance (Zuhur) as much as possible. Pray for the reappearance as much as possible because your relief and your salvation lie in it. In the prayer for the reappearance. Look, the Imam himself says, "In this lies your relief," meaning your relief is in the prayer. This is a strange sentence. This is a strange hadith. Some people say that prayer alone does nothing. They are unaware of the importance of prayer. They should go and read what the importance of prayer is. It is found in the traditions, "Ad-du'a silahul-anbiya." Prayer was the weapon of the Prophets. Prayer is the essence of worship. Great difficulties are solved through prayer. So, one thing is prayer. Insha'Allah, there will be more discussion on prayer another time. This was just a hint. But after that, the Imam himself says what should be done? He says, "Fal-ya'mal" or in one hadith, in one version, "Fal-ya'mal kullu imri'im bima yaqrubu bihi min mahabbatina." Each one of you should do what brings you closer to our love. Do the things that bring you closer to the love and devotion of the Ahlul-Bayt. "Wa l-yatajannab ma yudnihi min kirayati-na wa sakhati-na" and avoid every such act. The Imam says, avoid every act that brings you closer to our displeasure. That is, stay away from those things that we do not like. Avoid them, maintain distance from them. So there are two things, there are two commands here. One, do the things that bring you closer to our love, and second, avoid and stay away from the things that bring you closer to our displeasure or our dislike. Stay away from them. That is, if we say it in simple words, then act upon the obligatory (Wajib) and recommended (Mustahab) acts that are according to the Sharia, according to the Tawdih al-Masa'il, as it is written in the Sharia, as the jurists have stated; act upon the Wajib and Mustahab acts accordingly, and avoid the forbidden (Muharramat) and disliked (Makruhat) acts. That is, avoid things that are Haram, and also avoid things that are Makruh; avoid everything, not just the Haram. This is the saying of the Imam. The saying of the 12th Imam. "Fal-ya'mal kullu imri'im bima yaqrubu bihi min mahabbatina wa l-yatajannab ma yudnihi min kirayati-na wa sakhati-na." Why? "Fa-innahu amruna bakhtatun faj'ah." Because our reappearance will be sudden. Bakhtatun, sudden. Faj'ah, unexpected. It will happen when people do not expect it. Bakhtatun means sudden. Faj'ah means it will happen when people do not expect it. Bakhtatun faj'ah. And when the reappearance happens, the Imam says, "Hina la tanfa'uhu tawbah." At that time, repentance will not be of any benefit. If a person thinks at that time that we will repent after the reappearance, the Imam says that repentance will not be of any benefit at that time. "Wa la yunjiihi min iqabina nadamun 'ala haubah." And at that time, even if he is remorseful for his deeds and his sins, he will not be able to escape our punishment. That is, he will not be able to escape the Imam's punishment or the Imam's Zulfiqar at that time. Because he has become an enemy of Allah. He has committed so many sins. A human being should keep this in mind not to do such things that would make the Imam of the Time (a.s.) displeased. Just one last hadith to complete this topic, on how we can survive in this turbulent environment during the time of Occultation (Ghaybah). Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that "Mansuran yakunu min ashabi"—if someone wants to be among the companions of the Imam, that is, the special companions of the Imam for whom it is mentioned that a person should stand up, face the Qibla, and place a hand on their head. This is not obligatory, but regardless, if someone wants to be among the companions of the Imam, what should they do? The sixth Imam says, "Fal-yantazir." They should wait. Wait for the reappearance. How does one wait for the reappearance? Remember your Imam morning and evening, and do what I just presented to you, do the things that the Imam expects from them. "Wal-ya'mal bil-wara'" and he should act with Wara', with Wara' meaning Taqwa, meaning caution, which is an even higher status than Taqwa. What is the definition of Wara'? "Al-wuqufu 'indash-shubuhat"—that is, where there is doubt, one should abstain. "Wa mahasinil-akhlaq" and keep his character as the best character. That is, in society, when meeting people, meet them with the best character. So that people say, yes, these are the lovers of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), their character is the best character. The character should be such that people attribute it to the family of Muhammad (a.s.) that these are the lovers of the Ahlul-Bayt, their character is the best. And in all this state, "Wa huwa muntazirun," then the Imam is emphasizing that while he is waiting, he should do all these things. If he does this, then his reward will be, "Fa-in mata wa qamal-imamu ba'dahu," if the Imam's reappearance happens after his death, he dies, "Fakana lahu minal-ajri mithlu ajri man adrakahu," then he will get the same reward as the one who lived to see the time of the Imam. The one who lived to see the time of the Imam will get it. Then the Imam says a sentence, ponder over this, just the last sentence. "Fajiddu wantaziru." Look, be serious, be serious in life. "Jiddu" means strive. Be serious. Do not make life a game. Do not make life a joke. Do not think that life is just for today and will be gone tomorrow; no, rather work for the Hereafter. Build your Hereafter as much as possible. "Fajiddu wantaziru, hani'an lakum." Congratulations to you. The Imam is also giving congratulations to those who are waiting and whose deeds are praiseworthy. "Hani'an lakum ayyatuhal-'isabatul-marhumah." Congratulations, O group upon whom is the mercy of Allah. So it is known that whoever is waiting for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time in his Occultation, is patient in all the difficulties that exist in the Occultation, endures those difficulties, and despite those difficulties, holds fast to the Imam, remains on his religion, adopts Taqwa, and keeps praying for the reappearance of the Imam, remembers the Imam morning and evening, remembers his Imam, then surely, surely such a person will be among the helpers and supporters of the Imam after the reappearance of the Imam. So let us all pray together, O Lord! By the sake of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.), count us among his helpers and supporters. When the Imam reappears, may we be among the helpers of the Imam, among the servants of the Imam. If death comes to us before the reappearance of the Imam, then O Lord! "Bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad," O Lord! Bring us out from our graves alive, resurrect us in such a state that we can help the Imam. "Wa akhiru da'wana anil-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin." I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us and do not destroy us. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Before the winners of today are announced, on the occasion of tonight, the TSR team presents congratulations to the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), especially to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and to all of you on the birth of the refuge of the universe, that is, Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). Now the time has come for which you all were waiting impatiently. That is, the announcement of the daily lucky draw winners of the Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) Refuge of the Universe Mega Quiz, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. Those who will get a prize of ₹1000 Indian Rupees, and their names are on your screen. Bashir Ahmed from Budgam, Majid Want from Bemina, Binte Zahra from Azamgarh, Mehdi Hussain from Bengaluru, Samir Bakhri from Alipur, Akbar Ratnam from Mumbai. Many congratulations to all the winners. If someone's name did not appear in today's winners, then there is no need for them to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series, and those who have given all correct answers in the quizzes of 7 out of 12 episodes will all be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize, that is, the pilgrimage (Ziyarat) to Iraq. We want to thank all of you once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time with another new video. Until then, goodbye. Iltimas-e-Dua. Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Ahle Bait (a.s.) Ne Fadak Waapas Kyun Nahin Liya? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical question of why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not reclaim the land of Fadak during his caliphate. The speaker explains that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) followed the precedent set by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), who chose not to reclaim property seized from him unjustly. Furthermore, the Imams taught that they prioritize divine justice on the Day of Judgment over worldly reclamation, ensuring the oppressors receive their full accountability.
content:
Because the land belonged to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), why did Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) not demand it? From this, we get a hadith in which our sixth Imam, Imam Ja'far Sadiq (a.s.), says that on the Day of Judgment, both the oppressor and the oppressed will be made to stand in the court of Allah. Allah will grant the reward to the oppressed and punish the oppressor. Then he (Imam Ali (a.s.)) did not want to take back that thing on the basis of which Allah would determine the reward for the oppressed and the punishment for the oppressor. That is, Imam Ali (a.s.) knew that whether he gets his right in this world or not, on that day, which will be the day of justice, he will definitely get his right. And one aspect of this is also that Imam Ali (a.s.) knew that the oppressor would be punished, so he did not want the punishment of those oppressors to be reduced even slightly on the Day of Judgment. Besides this, there is a famous book named 'Ilal al-Sharai', in which some narrations are found from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and Imam Kazim (a.s.) on this topic. We will see both narrations one by one, God willing. The first narration is from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), that he was asked when it was the era of the apparent caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), why did he not take Fadak into his possession? Why did he not take Fadak into his possession? So, in response to this, he says—the Imam was asked, yes, about this. Indeed, this also shows that this is not a new question; people in that era also used to ask the Imams (a.s.) about this. And Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, we are grateful that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the Imams (a.s.), have told us the answers to this in a very good way. So Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that when the migration of the Prophet took place and he went from Makkah to Madinah, he had a house in Makkah. When he returned, that house was in the possession of someone else. When people asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) if he would not take his house back, he (s.a.w.a.) said, 'No, we, the Ahlulbayt, do not take back things that have been snatched from us unjustly.' Now, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), who is the true successor and caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and who can follow his lifestyle more than him? So, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not demand his house, which was taken from him unjustly, Amir al-Mu'minin also followed his lifestyle and did not demand Fadak, which was snatched from him unjustly. Which was snatched from him unjustly. Besides that, the second hadith I mentioned, which is from Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.), in which he says that we, the Ahlulbayt, do not take back things that have been taken from us unjustly. And when we gain authority over the believers, we demand from the oppressors those things to which the believers have a right, but we do not demand those things to which we have a right. [Music]
Imam Ali (a.s.) did not reclaim Fadak to ensure the oppressors faced full divine judgment.
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) set the precedent by not reclaiming his house in Makkah.

The Imams prioritize the rights of the believers over their own personal property rights.
Historical records like 'Ilal al-Sharai' contain narrations explaining this specific policy.
The question of Fadak was raised during the time of the Imams themselves, not just in modern times.
Reclaiming property taken unjustly is not the practice of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).

title: #4 - Shahaadat, Sa’aadat, Wilaadat | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen | شرح زیارت اربعین  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of Imam Husayn's (a.s.) life and martyrdom as described in the Ziyarat of Arba'een. It highlights the divine honor bestowed upon the Imam through his pure birth, his status as the treasurer of revelation, and his unparalleled rank among martyrs. The speaker emphasizes the importance of purity of birth and faith, drawing upon the Verse of Purification and the words of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) to inspire believers to lead lives of spiritual integrity.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr (Guardian of the Era), assist us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. The arrival of any human into this world and their departure from it are two significant occasions through which every good or bad person is remembered. The fortunate and blessed person is one whose arrival is celebrated by the world and whose departure is mourned. In the Ziyarat of Arba'een, the arrival of Imam Husayn (a.s.) into this world and his departure from this transient abode are remembered in this way: 'Akramtahu bish-shahadati wa habawtahu bis-sa'adati wajtabaytahu bitibil-wiladati' (You honored him with martyrdom, bestowed upon him felicity, and chose him through a pure birth). The purity and cleanliness of Imam Husayn (a.s.) is evidenced in the Holy Quran in the thirty-third verse of Surah al-Ahzab, known as the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), in which Allah Almighty has declared the removal of all forms of impurity, filth, and defilement from the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) has mentioned ten signs of faith, the first of which is that one's birth is pure and clean. As for the nobility and honor of Imam Husayn (a.s.), the famous Hadith al-Lawh, which is also a Hadith Qudsi, contains the declaration of the Creator of the universe Himself: 'I have made Husayn the treasurer of My revelation, honored him through martyrdom, and granted him felicity. Thus, he is the most excellent of those who are martyred, and his rank is the highest among all martyrs.' This pure birth and honorable martyrdom are impossible without divine help and support, and this is what the Ziyarat testifies to in this phrase. O God! By the sake of the pure life and great martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.), grant us the ability to spend our lives with pure and clean thoughts and beliefs, and count us among the mourners (azadars) of Imam Husayn (a.s.). Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Ek Nujoomi Ne Imam Sajjad (a.s.) Ka Kalima Padha
excerpt: This lecture recounts a miraculous encounter between Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) and an astrologer who visited him. By demonstrating his divine knowledge (Ilm-e-Ghaib) regarding the man's personal affairs and hidden possessions, the Imam guided the astrologer to accept the truth of his Imamate. The narrative emphasizes that true faith in the Proof of God is a divine gift granted only to those whose hearts have been tested and purified by Allah.
content:
Imam Sajjad (a.s.), through his knowledge of the unseen (Ilm-e-Ghaib), turned an astrologer into a Shia. Abu Khalid Kabuli narrates that a man came to the presence of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), while his companions were present. The Imam (a.s.) asked him, 'Who are you?' He replied, 'I am such-and-such an astrologer and mystic.' The Imam (a.s.) looked at him and said, 'Shall I tell you about a person who has been traveling the world since you arrived here?' He asked, 'Who is that?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'If you wish, I can tell you what you ate and what you have stored in your house.' He said, 'Tell me.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Today you ate harees (porridge), and in your house, there are 20 dinars, three of which are underweight.' Upon hearing this, he immediately said, 'Amanta billah, wal-masala, wal-kalimat-ut-taqwa' (I believe in Allah, you are the supreme proof, the highest example, and the word of piety). To this, the Imam (a.s.) said, 'And you are truthful; Allah has tested your heart.' This means no one can have faith in the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda) unless Allah has tested their heart.

title: 3 Types of Brothers | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses a narration from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) categorizing brothers into three distinct types based on their impact on our lives. The Imam compares these types to food, disease, and medicine, emphasizing the importance of choosing our company wisely. The talk concludes with a reminder that our social interactions reflect how we are treated by others and includes a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.).
content:
Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that there are three types of brothers. The first is like food, meaning we need him at all times, and he is the wise one. The second is the one we view like a disease; this is a foolish person, and just as we run away from a disease, we should stay away from this person. And the third is like medicine, meaning he is the intelligent person. Now it is up to us how we live with others, because the way we treat others, they will treat us in the same way. In the end, we pray that Allah hastens the reappearance of our Imam and counts us among his helpers and supporters. Along with this, we also pray that Allah grants us the ability to live with our brothers as our Imam desires. Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Ke As'haab Ki 5 Khususiyaat | #muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture outlines five unique characteristics that distinguish the companions of Imam Husayn (a.s.) from all others in history. The speaker highlights their unparalleled loyalty, their vision of their stations in Paradise, their unwavering certainty, their immunity to the pain of martyrdom, and their status as leaders among all martyrs. The talk concludes by emphasizing why these companions are honored during Ziyarat and how their devotion serves as a model for believers today.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. 'Fa-laytani kuntu ma'akum, fa-afuza fawzan azima' (Would that I were with you, to attain a great success). There are five such characteristics found regarding the companions of Imam Husayn (a.s.) that are not found for the companions of anyone else. And what are those five characteristics? The first characteristic is that they were the best of companions. Imam Husayn (a.s.) himself stated: 'Fa-inni la a'lamu ashaban' (I do not know of any companions who are more loyal and better than my companions). The second characteristic is that Imam Husayn (a.s.) showed his companions their place in Paradise. It is found in the narrations that when Imam Sadiq (a.s.) was asked about the companions of Imam Husayn (a.s.), the Imam said: 'Fa-innahum kushifa lahumul-ghita' (The veils were removed from before their eyes), 'Hatta ra'aw manazilahum minal-jannah' (Until they saw their stations in Paradise). This is the second characteristic. Third, they were at such a level of certainty that even if something were to happen to them, they were not prepared to leave Imam Husayn (a.s.). A companion named Sa'd ibn Abdullah al-Hanafi himself said these words on the night of Ashura to Imam Husayn (a.s.): 'By Allah, if I knew that I would be killed, then brought back to life, then burned, and then my ashes scattered in the wind, and this were done to me seventy times, even then, O Master, I would not leave you.' The fourth characteristic: in their love for Imam Husayn (a.s.), in their devotion, and in their recognition (marifat), the companions had such deep knowledge and love for Imam Husayn (a.s.) that it is mentioned—and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself had prophesied this to Imam Husayn (a.s.)—that the Prophet said: 'O my little son, soon you will have to go towards Iraq, and it is a land where every Prophet and the successor of every Prophet has gone, and one name for this land is also Amura.' Then the Prophet says, 'O my little son, you will be martyred there, and not only you, but a group of your companions will be martyred with you.' And what kind of companions will they be, who were so immersed in your love? The Prophet says: 'La yajiduna alama massil-hadid' (They will not feel the pain of the touch of iron, meaning the strike of the sword). They will be so immersed in the love of Imam Husayn (a.s.) that they will not even feel the pain of the sword's cut. And the fifth characteristic, the Prophet himself says to Imam Husayn (a.s.): 'O my little son, tansuruhu 'isabatun minal-muslimin' (A group of Muslims will help you, meaning your companions), 'Ula'ika min sadati shuhada'i ummati' (They will be the masters and leaders of all the martyrs of my nation on the Day of Judgment). These five characteristics regarding the companions of Imam Husayn (a.s.) are such that they are not found for the companions of anyone else. That is why every pilgrim, when going to Karbala, along with the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.), also separately recites the Ziyarat of the companions of Imam Husayn (a.s.), which is known as the Ziyarat of the Martyrs. Haza wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi-tayyibinat-tahirin al-ma'sumin. May the Lord of the worlds grant us the ability to be among the true helpers and supporters of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.), and hasten the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.).

content:

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#3 | Denying an Infallible Imam (a.s.) is disbelief | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this episode of Shameem-e-Ma'refat, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the critical necessity of absolute submission to the authority of the Infallible Imams (a.s.) as a cornerstone of faith. The lecture emphasizes that true worship and religious practice are only accepted when aligned with the divine commands and the recognition of the Imam. Furthermore, the discussion highlights the importance of seeking knowledge through qualified scholars and honors the pivotal role of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) in the history of Islam.
content:
We are... [Music] Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Welcome to this episode of our program 'Khushbu-e-Islam'. In the previous episode, we understood the importance of the Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and in the second episode, it was discussed that the knowledge of the Quran is only with the Imams (a.s.). It is our responsibility... It is our responsibility to turn towards the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in every situation. We have received many questions from the previous episode, among which this question is relevant and related to the previous discussion. Therefore, we present three such questions from the viewers before you. The first question was: 'How to know what Western influence is injecting into our community or society?' How do we know, how can we find out that Western culture is influencing our Shia society? This was the first question. The second question was: In the first session, the first episode, it was discussed that reading the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), understanding them, and the science of Hadith is very important. But in the previous episode, this discussion took place and this point was also presented that it is difficult to understand the traditions and narrations of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So, what is the way out? How can one resolve this? On one hand, it is said to read the Hadith, and on the other hand, it is said that they are difficult to understand. So, how can a person acquire this knowledge? How can one acquire the interpretation of Hadith? The things we understand through our own intellect, is that the interpretation of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)? And the third and final question is: What is said in the light of the Quran and the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) about a person who opposes or objects to any action or statement of any Masoom (a.s.)? So, let us take these three questions to our respected guest and request him to answer these three questions. And with this, let us begin today's third episode, whose title is 'The Denial of the Masoom (a.s.) is the Denial of Allah'. This is the topic of our special episode today. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. He was the third part of the African... [Arabic recitation] ...He says that Allah has not appointed anyone over His servants except... [Arabic recitation] ...and people have not denied anything as much as they have denied the Imamate. Just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said... Just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said... The first question was: 'How to know what Western influence is injecting into our community or society?' How do we know what is being injected? See, today the whole world is connected. You get information from everywhere. Whatever happens there, it comes here. Things from here might go to the West. In this way, everyone is influenced by each other. This is an inevitable thing that cannot be avoided. This is the first thing. The second thing is that it is our responsibility to become influencers and... It is our responsibility to become influencers and influence others through our vision. Introduce the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And you see, people will follow the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The late scholars... and the books available in Urdu... and a glimpse of that... keeping in mind what was in the world at that time, how to do it, and how to be enlightened and religious. This is the second thing. In this society, things like drinking alcohol... these things are very... and others... so for this, we should... The perfection is this, otherwise, it is not that if we... So, the answer to this question is: How to know what is Western influence? It is very simple. The standard is the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If you are in the field, you have the books of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) from the beginning until today. Everything is there. Look at the narrations, look at the discussions that are present. Sit and read, study, teach your children so that they know what is Haram and what is Halal. So that if any influence comes from anywhere, it becomes clear to them that this is Haram, we should not do this. This is allowed, this is Halal, we can do this. And in this way, whatever impact we see... Whatever impact we see, according to Islamic teachings—that is, in the field of action—it is very clear. You see the options, the examples, and the matters you are thinking about; look at their nature and act accordingly. For example, in the field of action, there is a question, and in the next part, we will answer it. So, this was the first question. Now, the second question was about the difficulty of understanding Hadith and how we can make sense of them. How can we be sure we understood the Hadith correctly? The answer to this is that when you want to acquire religious knowledge, you must do so under the training of a well-educated teacher. Do not go to someone who is not well-versed in religious knowledge; go to the scholars (Ulama) who have mastered these fields, learn from them, and acquire knowledge from them. This is a very good thing. Learning from them is a very good thing, and the teacher should also be someone who possesses the necessary qualities. When these qualities are present, it has an impact on the student. Therefore, it is necessary to seek knowledge from those who are qualified. In the books of Hadith, the qualities required for such a person are described. For instance, in the book 'Al-Kafi', there is a chapter regarding this, and in that chapter, it is mentioned how to choose such a person. This is taken from a very great scholar, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, who was a great scholar of his time. He was a great scholar, and he compiled these things. However, there was a specific context for this, which was to suppress and eliminate certain false ideas. It is a well-known tradition in our reliable books, and our scholars, like Sheikh al-Saduq and others, mention that Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) was asked about this, and his brother also asked... His brother asked, and he wrote two answers. In one answer, he said, 'I understood what you are trying to say—about whom to take knowledge from. I understood that you should look for someone among our followers who is old in his love for us, someone whose entire life has been spent in our love, and who has gained deep experience. Anyone who has spent their life in our path and has increased their knowledge in these matters, Allah will place wisdom in their heart.' So, if we do not understand something, we should ask those who have spent their lives in the field of religious knowledge. Spending one's life in the field of knowledge means studying for 12 to 15 years, and doing so continuously. It doesn't mean you leave all your work, but even if you have a weekly day off, you should dedicate three or four hours to studying. This is the best way to gain knowledge. The first command given to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was 'Read' (Iqra). Islam is based on knowledge, but unfortunately, Muslims have moved away from it. You should ask those who have spent their lives in the field of knowledge and are truly experts. Ask those who are experts in Hadith, books, and traditions. As I mentioned, in this age of technology, nothing is hidden. You can find such teachers; it is not a difficult task. Now, the third question: what is the view of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) if someone objects to a tradition? Regarding this, the first thing is that the Quran says: 'It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair.' And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error. They have certainly strayed into clear error. If Allah and His Messenger have made a decision, and after the Messenger, his successor Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) has made a decision, then even if the entire Muslim community gathers and makes a decision, it has no value. If someone disobeys after Allah and His Messenger have decided, they have gone into clear error. In another verse, Surah An-Nisa, verse 65, Allah says: 'But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves.' In the Arabic language, repeating a word is a way of emphasizing. Allah has used an oath here: 'By your Lord.' Can there be a greater oath than Allah swearing by Himself? Can there be a greater oath? Can there be a greater witness than the Prophet? Allah says: 'They will not believe until they make you the judge in all their disputes.' This means you, or the Imams, or those who are experts in the Quran and Hadith and are judging in the light of Hadith—no one else has the authority. After you have made a decision, they should not feel any resentment in their hearts. If the Prophet has made a decision, no one has the right to object to it. No one has the right to object, asking 'Why is this?' or 'Why is that?' If the Prophet or the Imams (a.s.) have made a decision, it is actually Allah's decision. To object to it takes a person out of the circle of faith. One must submit completely. Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni wrote in his book 'Al-Kafi' a chapter titled 'The Chapter of Submission to the Imams.' In this chapter, he narrates that the Imam said: 'Whoever wants their faith to be complete...' Whoever wants their faith to be complete must act upon it. They should say, 'I believe in everything that comes from the family of Muhammad (Aal-e-Muhammad), whether they have kept it hidden or revealed it, whether it has reached me or not.' This is what true submission is. So, in the commentary of this verse of Surah An-Nisa, there is a tradition in Al-Kafi where the Imam says that if people... If people worship Allah in the way that Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.) have commanded, and do not act according to their own whims—meaning they do not say that what Allah has ordained is incorrect or what the Messenger has done is incorrect—if they do not do this, and if they do not feel any hesitation or discomfort in their hearts regarding any decision made by Allah or His Messenger, even if it is something they find difficult to accept or if they think it is not right... ...if they feel hesitation in their hearts and think it is not right, then it is not just that they are saying it is not right, but it is as if they are saying Allah and His Messenger are not present. Why? Because this is a matter of faith. In the time of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), things were accepted, but later generations, especially those after the Prophet, did not like certain things. They disliked them and declared them forbidden (haram). This is wrong. When Allah and His Messenger have ordained something, who are we to object? The Hadith says that if someone feels hesitation in their heart or tongue, they are not a true believer. ...they are not a believer, but then it comes to light that they feel hesitation or discomfort in their hearts. After that, they must submit (taslim). This was the answer to the third question: if a Hadith comes before us and we do not understand it, many people today, because they have become 'capable' through modern knowledge, say, 'This Hadith is against the Quran, it is against reason, so this Hadith is false.' They have started to understand so much that they reject narrations. In 'Al-Kafi', Volume 2, Chapter 6, it is explained that if you do not understand a Hadith, you cannot simply reject it. ...you cannot understand which is abrogated (mansukh) or specific (khas). How can we mix things up? If it is good, to what extent can we mix it? If something is beyond our understanding, we cannot just reject it. We must wait until we have complete certainty. It must be proven that it is forged (jaali). Just because we do not understand something does not mean we reject it. But continuing the discussion on media reports, the next topic is that Allah has emphasized one thing more than anything else. ...and that is the status of the Imam. The book 'Qurb al-Isnad' is a book by a great scholar from the 10th or 11th century. In this book, he mentions that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) emphasized the status of the Imam more than anything else. How? Look at the Quran. Study the Quran from beginning to end. Look at the verses from the start, and you will see that before everything else, Allah emphasized this. I will explain this to all the scholars. ...I will explain this to all the scholars: 'I know what you do not know.' He taught Adam all the names. Then He asked the angels, 'Tell me the names if you are truthful.' The angels said, 'We do not know.' They realized their position before Allah. They realized that they had made a mistake. Then Iblis refused and showed arrogance. He was among the disbelievers because of this refusal. So, look at what they refused. The angels' prostration was for the one whom Allah had chosen... ...the one whom Allah had made His Caliph. Now, apply all the stories of the Quran to this. People have always refused the Prophet of their time, the representative of Allah. They kept refusing. And regarding the Children of Israel, the Quran has so many narrations because whatever is going to happen in this Ummah is exactly what happened to the Children of Israel, what happened in the time of Musa (a.s.). It is exactly the same. Allah has emphasized the Quran and the obedience to the one whom Allah has appointed. Here, the appointment of an Imam is clearly established. ...you will find narrations where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explicitly named the Imams and said, 'Look, these will be the Imams.' But after that, the Ummah did not follow. They said, 'We will not do this.' I say this calmly: before doing anything, someone asked, 'Should we do this?' Allah immediately replied, 'Do what I say. I want My worship to be as I desire, not as you desire.' Allah's worship is done as Allah wants, and Allah wants submission to the one He has chosen. This is not democracy. Allah did not appoint a single Prophet through democratic election. In fact, the principle of the Quran is: 'And most of My servants are not grateful.' And if you follow the majority, they will lead you astray. ...if you follow the majority, they will lead you astray. If you follow the majority, they will deceive you. That is why Allah forbids following the majority. So, where did this idea of following the majority come from? This is something that must be addressed. Regarding the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), it is said that he did not do anything without the command of Allah. And listen, the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.)—if the foundation of the religion is not based on his command, then... ...if the foundation of the religion is not based on his command, then the foundation of the religion is not from Allah. And who raised the Prophet? It was Abu Talib (a.s.). Even though our discussion is not about the birth of Abu Talib, it is necessary to mention him. If Abu Talib was not a believer, then there is no believer in the world. This is the truth. If you say Abu Talib was a disbeliever because of the things he did, then we will also say we are disbelievers. Abu Talib was a disbeliever in idols. He was a disbeliever in them. And that is why those who have the love of idols in their hearts... That is why those in whose hearts there was love for idols, they hated Abu Talib (a.s.) because Abu Talib (a.s.) rejected their idols. There is a complete qasida (poem) of Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) regarding this. And if the one who performed the Nikah of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—if he is considered a disbeliever, then where will the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) go? See, I do not want to prolong this, I am just explaining to you. They were trapped in their own logic. Actually, those who were followers of their forefathers, in order to justify the disbelief of their forefathers, they try to make Ali's (a.s.) father a disbeliever, so that if Ali's (a.s.) father is a disbeliever, then their forefathers' disbelief will be justified. But they do not understand what 'Deen' (religion) is. Deen is that which has come from the beginning, which goes back to Adam (a.s.). In this, you will not find any disbelief; disbelief is a far-fetched thing. And they are using the word 'volume'—just look at their status, what they are saying and about whom they are saying it. Anyway, before pointing fingers at Abu Talib (a.s.), think for yourself: what do we call Deen? Deen is the sign of the pleasure of the Divine. If someone is in the depths of the ocean, surrounded by darkness on all sides, and they see a lighthouse, they know that this is the path, this is the way. Even in the ocean, one understands which path to choose. So, who is making Ali's (a.s.) faith the lighthouse? Understand this, it is the pinnacle of guidance. The purpose of guidance is... When a horse has a white mark on its forehead, it is considered a good breed. And they say that if a horse is completely black but has a white mark on its foot, it is a sign of a high-quality breed. It is a sign of a good horse. So, they say that those who are the followers of Ali (a.s.) will have a mark on their foreheads, a sign of being servants of Allah. And there will be a sign that is a mark of good character. Whoever has the love of Ali (a.s.) in their heart, that will be the sign of their faith. This is the testimony... And I am giving testimony to this. If the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gives testimony, does any room remain for anyone else to speak? And if someone gives the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) testimony and accepts Allah's testimony, or if Allah makes them a witness, then does anyone in the world have the right to object to it? Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was the one whom Allah made a witness to the Prophethood of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in Mubahila. And here the same point arises: to hide the mistakes of their own people, they say such things. You understand what I am saying, right? And the one saying it doesn't even know what he is saying because he is completely... Because he is completely... here, the curse of Allah is upon those who deviate. Now, the matter of Fatima (s.a.)—when everything was read, what was read? That when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left someone behind, and Zahra (s.a.) gave the same answer to them, that 'Are you teaching me?' And it was told to those who have idols in their homes, that 'Are you teaching them?' And the one teaching is someone who is not even aware of the Quran's teachings. And your tongue is wagging... anyway, leave that. We will discuss this in detail some other time, God willing. But this point is clear. And the second point, today's hadith—one more thing you should understand, and that is that the worship of Allah is not possible except through... Through the recognition of the Imam. And if someone performs worship without this recognition, no matter how much they do, look at this... if someone performs worship, but without the recognition of the one whom Allah has made obligatory to follow, whose obedience Allah has made mandatory—if they do not recognize the Imam, then their worship is nothing. It is nothing. Their bowing and prostrating will not benefit them without the guidance of the Imam. Without the guidance of the Imam, it is pointless. The proof is right in front of you. The Quran says, 'Do you not ponder?' It is not about not pondering; they are not pondering. 'Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found many contradictions in it.' There are many contradictions in their beliefs. This is the reason why there are so many sects among Muslims today. You tell me, how many issues are there? Why is the whole world divided? This is the reason. They performed the task, and if someone does this, all their worship... and if I talk about the recognition of the Imam, before this, if one does not recognize the Imam, then they have followed someone else. And by following someone else, they have committed shirk (polytheism). But if a person does so much... when it comes to Ma'rifat (recognition), nothing will be accepted without it. Until there is recognition of the Imam, no matter how much a person performs... That is why in all the teachings, whatever is there, it is all related to the reality of the Imam. They speak just as the Imam (a.s.) has commanded. That is why it is not permissible for any person to not recognize the Imam of the time. As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, and as this verse says—this is the last verse of Surah Al-Kahf, verse 110: 'And let him not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.' In response to this question, the Imam (a.s.) said that 'Ma'rifat' (recognition) is the best of deeds. The best deed is not just performing rituals, but to 'not associate anyone in the worship of your Lord.' And these people, they are the ones who are completely submissive to Ali (a.s.). To not consider anyone equal to Ali (a.s.) or to not associate anyone with Ali (a.s.)—this was the right path. And all Muslims agree on this, but... It is not about anyone else, but we say that money is not the only thing; only the rich were appointed, and we have arguments for that. We will keep fulfilling our duties little by little. Here, the matters of the Caliphate were rejected by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Allah's command in a very clear way. He said, 'I will not accept it.' He rejected Allah's command, and Allah's command was rejected. Today, it is strange that people are surprised by this. If they are displeased, let them be; whatever the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has announced, the result will be the same. It will be a test. No one has been given permission to go against the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) regarding who Ali (a.s.) is. How many traditions are there about Ali (a.s.)? It is impossible that the verses of the Quran and the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) words... The late Mir Hamid Hussain, in his entire work, said that it has been translated, and it is about the Caliphate and Imamate. The decision is only about these two, but what was done with Ali (a.s.)? What was done with Ali (a.s.)? Why was he killed? He kept saying this until the last days of his life: 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) told me...' Let us try, even if we cannot do everything, to do something. It is their compulsion, so let us try to show the world and tell them that this is the truth, so that we can say we made an effort. So that we can say we made an effort. We are deeply grateful to the respected speakers and all the citizens who made this program interesting through their questions. Continue sending your questions related to the topics discussed to the WhatsApp number of the 'Sultan-ul-Qalam' group. You can send your messages via voice recording or text. Our number is [number removed]. Yes, this is our WhatsApp number; you can continue your series of questions. Before we go, a very important announcement: tomorrow, Sunday, June 21, 2020, at 9:30 PM India time, a 'Mohsin-e-Islam' quiz is being organized. It is about the life of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.). There will be a presentation on his life, and some questions related to his life will be presented to you, and you have to provide the answers. You have to provide the answers during this live program. The process is that you click on this link and register: account.sultanulqalamgroup.com. Go there and register yourself. This registration will remain open until 2 hours before the program starts. If the program is at 9:30 PM India time, the registration link will be open until 7:30 PM. The program will start at 9:30 PM live. In that program, a presentation regarding Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) will be shown, and the quiz link will be launched during that presentation. You will find the answers to the questions within the presentation itself. Therefore, watch the presentation carefully and answer the quiz questions. At the end of the program, there will be a prize for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd winners, and a total of 6 winners will be chosen through a lucky draw, just like the previous quiz. Six winners will be chosen through a lucky draw. Those who have answered all the questions correctly will be eligible for the lucky draw. Since this 'Mohsin-e-Islam' quiz is on the occasion of the birth anniversary of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), let us recite a few couplets in his honor: 'He who does not know the benefactor of Islam (Mohsin-e-Islam), he is a Muslim but not a man of faith. And he who does not have Surah Al-Imran in his heart, he may be someone else, but he is not of the Quran. And you think the enemies of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) are your friends? There is no greater loss than this. And those who are sitting for the sake of the enemies, they are so mean that they are not even remorseful yet. It is the grace of the Truth that Ali (a.s.) is recognized by his father, otherwise, some people would not even be recognized by their fathers.' Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin...
Complete submission to the Prophet and the Imams is a mandatory requirement for true faith.
Rejecting or objecting to the authority of an Infallible Imam constitutes a departure from the circle of faith.
Religious deeds are only accepted when performed with the recognition of the Imam.
Islam is a religion of knowledge, requiring study under qualified scholars rather than personal opinion.
Divine commands must be followed as revealed, regardless of whether they align with human logic or democratic consensus.
The appointment of Ali (a.s.) as successor was a clear divine mandate that cannot be ignored.
Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) is a foundational figure whose life and faith are essential to understanding Islamic history.

title: Ummul-Momineen Hazrat Khadijah (s.a.) Par Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) Ka Girya
excerpt: This lecture recounts the emotional moment when Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) mourned the passing of her mother, Hazrat Khadijah (s.a.). It highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) role in comforting his daughter through a divine message delivered by Jibra'il (a.s.). The narrative describes the heavenly abode of Hazrat Khadijah (s.a.) and concludes with Hazrat Fatima's (s.a.) expression of submission to Allah's will.
content:
Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that when Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) passed away, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) clung to her father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and asked, 'O Father! Where is my dear mother?' Then Jibra'il (a.s.) descended and said to the Prophet that your Lord has commanded you to tell Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) that your dear mother is in a house whose towers are made of red ruby and studded with gold, and this house is between the houses of Lady Asiya and Maryam bint Imran (s.a.). Upon this, Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) said, 'Indeed, Allah is Peace (Salam), peace is from Him and for Him.'

title: Quran-e-Majeed Mein Imam Mahdi (a.s) Ki Khilaafat | IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the interpretation of Surah An-Nur, verse 55, which promises the establishment of believers as successors on earth. The speaker argues that these divine promises—global rule, the dominance of the true religion, and universal security—have not yet been fulfilled in history. Consequently, the lecture concludes that these Quranic prophecies point specifically to the future reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the ultimate savior.
content:
The verses of the Holy Quran, Surah An-Nur, verse 55, are being recited: 'Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted it to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has preferred for them, and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security. They will worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.' Allah has promised those who believe and do good deeds that He will establish them on the earth as He did for those before them. This verse is a subject of thought for every ruler and scholar in the history of Islam. If the perspective of the previous commentators is accepted, then Yazid would be included in this Caliphate, whereas the majority of Muslims consider Yazid unworthy. If we analyze this verse, the word 'earth' is used, meaning the entire earth, not just Makkah, Madinah, or Islamic countries. History has never seen a time when a ruler of Allah ruled the entire earth. The second point in this verse is that Allah will establish the religion He is pleased with. In his book 'Jami al-Bayan', Tabari has mentioned on page 58 that this means the dominance of Islam over all other religions. But to this day, Islam has not achieved dominance over all other religions. Every Muslim must know which religion Allah is pleased with, because our salvation depends on it. Muslims should think in the light of reason: is it the religion that was completed with the announcement of the Imamate and Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and his 11 successors, or some other religion? The third promise is that God will change the state of the believers into security, and the fourth is that only Allah will be worshipped on earth. And the fourth is that only Allah will be worshipped on earth, and there will be no sign of polytheism. Today, the oppressors have created an atmosphere of disbelief through tyranny. Every Muslim is a witness that these promises have not yet been fulfilled. But as a Muslim, we claim that the promise of the Quran will definitely be fulfilled. There is only one way this promise will be fulfilled, and that is through the last successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). We pray to Allah to hasten the reappearance of his true successor, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), to establish the religion of Islam and peace on this earth, and grant us the strength to remain steadfast on his Wilayah. Amin, Ya Rabbil Alamin.
