title: EP17 | Hadees-e-Saqalain Aur Ahle Tasannun Ki Kitaabein | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological significance of Hadith al-Thaqalayn and its recognition within Sunni scholarship. The discussion challenges the misconception that Islamic legitimacy is tied solely to worldly political authority, emphasizing instead that true leadership is rooted in divine appointment, knowledge, and spiritual guidance. By citing authoritative Sunni texts such as 'Abaqat al-Anwar' and 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa,' the lecture demonstrates the historical consensus regarding the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahl-e-Bayt. Ultimately, it highlights the importance of spiritual steadfastness and intellectual insight during the occultation of the 12th Imam.
content:
Presenting the teaser [music] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, Salaat-o-Salam ala Nabiyina, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Before we begin today's new episode of Imam Hujjat, let us see who the winners are for the fourth quiz of this series, covering Episode 13 to Episode 16. Their selection is being done through our computerized lucky draw system, and their names are on your screen: Nazia Yusuf from Srinagar, Mir Hamza Hussain from Bangalore, Safar Ali from Azamgarh, Naz Zahra from Bangalore, Zahra Sani from Kashmir, Gaur Syed from Pune, Syed Saqib Raza from Bangalore, Azan Shafi from Kashmir, Arji Mirza Rizvi, Zainab from Mumbai, F. Fatima from Azamgarh, Akar Sada from Alipur, Rozi Garani from Bhavnagar. Akar Sada from Alipur, Rozi Garani from Bhavnagar, Abbasi Begum from Bangalore. Congratulations to all of you. So, let us move on to our new episode today. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, Allahumma Kulli Waliyyika Salawatuka alaihi wa ala abaihi fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah... In the Imam Hujjat series, let us first take the question. The question received is: 'Assalamu Alaikum. You mentioned in the lecture that Islam will have honor and greatness as long as there are 12 Caliphs. But we see that Hazrat Ali (a.s.), whose rule lasted only four years, and none of the other Imams of the Ahlulbayt had any rule, to the extent that some Imams even went into occultation. So, how can we say that Islam attained honor and greatness through them?' Yes, so this is an objection of theirs. As I submitted in the previous episode, they have raised a few objections, and their answers have been given. Just like the objections of the previous episodes, this is also a childish objection. They say that the Imams of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) were 12, but they did not have authority or rule, so where did Islam get its honor and greatness from? Whereas the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'La yazalu ad-dinu qaiman... hatta yakuna ithna ashara khalifah' (The religion will remain honorable, strong, and elevated as long as there are 12 Caliphs), and then said, 'Kulluhum min Quraish' (All of them will be from Quraish). Now, regarding the rest of the objections... In this, they say that if they were Imams and had rule, then Islam would have received honor and greatness. The essence of this objection is that they link this honor and greatness to worldly rule. So, first of all, in Islam, rule and authority are not the criteria for greatness and honor. This is the first thing, and there are many narrations in both Shia and Sunni schools of thought regarding what the criteria for greatness and honor are. It is Taqwa (piety). 'Inna akramakum indallahi atqakum' (Indeed, the most honorable of you in the sight of Allah is the most pious) is the verse of Surah Hujurat. And the criteria for honor are knowledge and virtue. All these things—religion, Taqwa, fear of God, and closeness to Allah—are the criteria. So, true Islam will be honorable as long as it has knowledge, Taqwa, and virtues, and as long as there are these 12 Caliphs and 12 successors. This Hadith is a kind of prophecy that there will be 12 Imams, 12 successors after the Prophet, and all of them will be from Quraish. The meaning of Caliphate here is not just worldly rule and authority. Allah said about Hazrat Adam (a.s.): 'Inni ja'ilun fil ardi khalifah' (Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority) in the verse of Surah Baqarah. The angels' objection was also that ordinary humans are worldly, they are sinners and transgressors. The angels' objection was: 'Ataj'alu fiha man yufsidu fiha wa yasfikud dima'a' (Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?) While we declare Your praise and sanctify You. Why are You making them? Why are You making these beings? Allah answered the angels by saying: 'Inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun' (Indeed, I know that which you do not know). Now, Hazrat Adam came to the world. How much rule did Hazrat Adam have? He had only two sons, one of whom killed the other. That was his rule. After that, Allah gave a third son, Hazrat Sheeth, and Hazrat Adam passed away during Hazrat Sheeth's lifetime. That was the extent of Hazrat Adam's rule. If you call this rule, then it means Hazrat Adam's Caliphate was not honorable according to your interpretation. If rule and authority were the criteria for honor, then Allah should have given rule to all His Prophets and all His successors—all those chosen members of Allah. But when we look at history, out of 124,000 Prophets, the rule of only two is mentioned: Hazrat Dawood and Hazrat Sulaiman. Out of 124,000 Prophets, the rule of only two is mentioned: Hazrat Dawood and Hazrat Sulaiman. Now, because the name of Hazrat Dawood came up, an interesting narration comes to mind, and this Hadith is in Shia books, the essence of which is that Allah gave Hazrat Dawood (a.s.) two options: Wisdom and Rule. Hazrat Dawood (a.s.)—see, 'Hikmat' (Wisdom) and 'Hukumat' (Rule) are written similarly in Arabic, with only a difference of one 'waw'. Hikmat means wisdom, and Hukumat means power/authority. Hazrat Dawood chose rule, and Hazrat Luqman (a.s.), when these two options were placed before him—both were in the same era—Hazrat Luqman chose Hikmat. He selected wisdom. So, Hazrat Dawood got rule, and Hazrat Luqman got wisdom. He got rule, he got wisdom. But in our narrations, it is found that whenever Hazrat Dawood faced a problem, he would go to Hazrat Luqman (a.s.) to solve it. Even though he was a Prophet of Allah, he would go to Hazrat Luqman to solve his own problems. And this quality of Hazrat Luqman was so pleasing to Allah that Allah dedicated an entire Surah of the Quran to him—Surah number 31, Surah Luqman. And that is why we see that even though people took away the apparent Caliphate from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), whenever they faced difficulties, especially intellectual difficulties, they would remember and call upon Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) to solve them. They would immediately say, 'Call Abu al-Hasan.' There are many such incidents. And the saying, 'If Ali were not there, so-and-so would have perished,' even though some people say this Hadith is weak, as is their habit to deny wherever the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin are mentioned—they say, 'No, this is not like this, that is like that, this Hadith is weak, so-and-so narrator is in it'—even though this narration has appeared in many of their books. For example, Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned it in his 'Isti'ab', and others have recorded this Hadith. People repeatedly called upon Amir al-Mu'minin, and there was nothing surprising in that. It was the prayer of Hazrat Sulaiman that Allah gave him worldly rule, and what kind of rule was that? You know... And you know what kind of rule that was. It was not just rule over humans, but over Jinn, the wind, birds, animals, and the seas. When Allah gives rule, He gives such rule, not just human rule. He gives a rule of knowledge and virtue. Hazrat Sulaiman, in his place, gave his successor, Janab Asif ibn Barkhiya, so much authority that he brought the throne of Bilqis from Yemen to Palestine before the blink of an eye. And this is all present in the Quran. So, this is rule—this is Allah's rule, not the one others had, whom we will mention later. And furthermore, if worldly rule is the only honor and greatness, then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stayed in Mecca for 13 years and had no rule. So, does that mean the religion had no honor in those 13 years? Did Islam not attain greatness? And after the Prophet came to Medina after the migration, the Prophet's rule in Medina was also very limited. It is not that the Prophet was ruling the entire world; it was a limited rule, but Islam was elevated, and it was elevated just as it was after the Prophet... And it was elevated just as it was for those who spiritually accepted the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) after the Prophet. Apart from that, if you look at the great Sufi Pirs and Murshids of the world—of course, we do not believe in Sufi Pirs and Murshids, but other Muslims do—everyone knows them. In fact, they have entire lineages: Chishtiya, Naqshbandiya, Suhrawardiya, and I don't know how many lineages of the people of Tasawwuf (Sufis) there are. None of them went after rule; rather, they would go to the mountains and build their Khanqahs far from the cities. So, does that mean Islam gets disgraced because of them? What answer will you give to that? Although most of those who object, like Ibn Taymiyyah and others, were against the Sufis too. Ibn al-Jawzi was also an enemy of the Sufis. But regardless, many Muslims believe in them. So, if this objection stands, then it means the lives of Sufis, Pirs, and Murshids are a cause of disgrace and humiliation for Islam. And then, regarding your Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) who went into occultation, as I submitted, what is the criterion for virtue? As I submitted, the criterion for virtue is knowledge, excellence, and Taqwa. And the Imam, even if he is all alone, performs the duties of his Imamate. Whether you put the Imam in prison or keep him completely isolated, the Imam performs his duties of Imamate. And being in occultation or being present is a different matter for the Imam. In Shia narrations, it is found that for those who are people of intellect, people of understanding, or those whom Allah has granted Ma'rifah (gnosis), it makes no difference whether the Imam is in occultation or present. There is a Hadith from Imam Zain al-Abidin (a.s.). The Imam says to one of his companions, Abu Khalid al-Kabuli: 'O Abu Khalid, those who will be in the time of the occultation of the 12th Imam...'—remember, the fourth Imam said this, he is prophesying—'...those who will be in his time, who will believe in his Imamate, and who will be waiting for his reappearance, they will be superior to the people of all times. Why? Because Allah the Almighty has given them...' Allah Ta'ala has given them intellect (Aql), understanding (Fahm), and insight (Ma'rifat). These are the three blessings Allah has bestowed upon those who believe in the Imam of the Time, the Imam who is in occultation, those who believe in Imam Mahdi. Allah has given them these three blessings. For them, occultation is like witnessing (Mushahada). It is exactly like the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was for Uwais al-Qarni. Janabe Uwais al-Qarni is respected by all Muslims, yet he never even saw the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). But Allah had given him such immense intellect, understanding, and insight that he loved the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) boundlessly. He loved the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) so much that once the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked his companions, 'If you were told to ask for one prayer that would be 100% granted, what would you ask for?' The companions all started thinking. Someone said they would ask for this, someone said they would ask for that. Someone said, 'I don't have a house, I would ask for a house.' Someone said, 'I don't have this, I would ask for that.' Someone said, 'I don't have a wife, I would ask for a wife.' Everyone started thinking according to their own needs. This is the gist of the narration. Everyone started thinking according to their own needs. This is the gist of the narration. Right, when all the companions expressed their desires, what did the Prophet say? The Prophet said, 'I wish Uwais were here. I wish Uwais were here.' So people asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what would Uwais say?' He said, 'If Uwais were here, he would say this prayer.' Meaning, the Prophet said this much. Later, when Uwais came, he did not meet the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), so someone asked Uwais, 'What would you have asked for?' He said, 'I would have asked that the Messenger, through whom we are receiving all these blessings, O Lord, keep the shadow of that Messenger upon us.' Did you notice? This is the difference. Uwais had the intellect, understanding, and insight that the other companions did not have. This is the reality. Just like that, 'Ma sarra min mushahada la-kum min haqq'—these are the true believers, and these are our true Shias, 'Wa la-da'una ila din-illah sirran wa jahran'—and these are the people who invite towards the religion of Allah, both secretly and openly. Depending on the opportunity and the situation, they perform their work of invitation and propagation. They perform the work of invitation and propagation. So, the problem is this: you people have considered government and power as honor and religion. You think this is religion, or that government means Islam, or that government is religion, or that government means power. This is a very wrong interpretation. And this is the reason why you have made a filthy person like Yazid so respectable. Who is that Yazid? As I have mentioned before, he is the one who martyred the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) in 61 AH. You remained silent. In 62 AH, what did he do? He plundered Medina. And in 63 AH, he rained fireballs on the Kaaba. Despite that, Muslims say he is honorable, or that Islam is honorable, and they write his name among the Caliphs. These are Muslims? The Jews would be ashamed to see them. And this is the reason why you see today that those you consider honorable, look at what they have done to the Haramain. Look at the state of the Kaaba, Mecca, and Medina today. The entire Islamic world is witnessing it, but not a single Mufti is opening their mouth to ask what they are doing. What are you doing? There is dancing happening in Mecca and Medina, open dancing. Gambling houses are opening on the land where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) walked, and the Muftis of the entire Islamic world are silent. This is the reason. This was the answer to your question. Now let us move to our second topic, and that is 'Imamat-e-Khassa' (Specific Imamat), meaning the discussion about those whom the Prophet declared would be his successors, his Caliphs, and we will try to provide answers to the objections raised against them, Insha'Allah. So, the first Hadith that people try very hard to hide, even though it is present in a very large number in their books, is the 'Hadith al-Thaqalayn'. 'Thaqalayn' means two precious things, 'Giran-baha' (precious), things that are very precious, which a person keeps very carefully. In Arabic, it is called 'Saqal'. One is 'Saqal' and two are 'Thaqalayn'. In Arabic, it is called 'Saqal'. One is 'Saqal' and two are 'Thaqalayn'. 'Thaqalayn' means two precious, very precious things. And this Hadith has been narrated in many different wordings. I will present the most famous one to you. The Prophet said, 'Inni tarikun feekum al-thaqalayn'—I am leaving among you two precious things: 'Kitab Allah wa 'itrati Ahl-e-Bayti'—the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahl-e-Bayt. The Prophet explicitly clarified that by 'Itrat' he meant Ahl-e-Bayt. 'Inni tarikun feekum al-thaqalayn, Kitab Allah wa 'itrati Ahl-e-Bayti, ma in tamassaktum bihima...' Now, look, before moving forward, there are different wordings. Somewhere it is written that the Prophet said, 'And this Quran, Kitab Allah, is a rope stretched from the sky to the earth,' and somewhere it is written that one end is in Allah's hand and the other end is in your hand. There are such narrations. But in brief, what you should note is: 'Kitab Allah wa 'itrati Ahl-e-Bayti'. Kitab Allah wa 'itrati Ahl-e-Bayti, ma in tamassaktum bihima—as long as you hold onto both of them firmly, 'lan tadillu ba'di abadan'—when 'lan' comes in Arabic, it is for 'nafi-e-abad' (eternal negation). You will never go astray as long as you hold onto the hem of these two. The Quran and the Ahl-e-Bayt, never let go of their hem. The Prophet is making a will. And this is also an interesting point to remember, which is present in many places in the narrations of the opponents, the narrations of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, that the Prophet said this Hadith on different occasions. For example, he said this Hadith at Hajjat al-Wida, then at Ghadir-e-Khumm, then during the illness that led to the martyrdom of the Prophet. Some people even said that these were the Prophet's last words. This is also written in the books. 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima'—as long as you hold onto the hem of these two firmly, As long as you hold onto the hem of these two firmly, if you hold onto them, 'lan tadillu ba'di abadan'—after me, you will never go astray. You will never go astray. 'Fa-innahu-ma lan yaftariqa'—and these two will not separate from each other, meaning the Quran and the Ahl-e-Bayt will not separate from each other, 'hatta yarida 'alayya al-hawd'—until they return to me at the Pond of Kawthar. This means that from the time of the Prophet until the Day of Judgment, the Quran and the Ahl-e-Bayt will be together. The Quran and an individual from the Ahl-e-Bayt, who will be the successor of the Prophet, who will be the Caliph of the Prophet, will be with the Quran immediately after the Prophet and until the Day of Judgment. And these two will not separate from each other. Insha'Allah, this has been narrated by 20 companions. This has been narrated by 20 companions. Whereas, if 4 to 8 companions of the Ahl-e-Sunnah narrate a Hadith, it reaches the status of 'Tawatur'. They say this Hadith is 'Mutawatir' (consecutively narrated). If something is consecutively narrated, it is 'Mutawatir', then it cannot be rejected. That is, it is 'Qat'i al-Sudur' (definitely issued), meaning it was 100% said by the Prophet, and its example is like the Quran. There is no chance of rejection; no one can reject it. So here, the Prophet clearly says that these are the 'Thaqalayn'. I am leaving them among you. If you hold them firmly, you will never go astray. And these two will be together. In other words, just as the Prophet said, 'Ali ma' al-Qur'an wa al-Qur'an ma' Ali' (Ali is with the Quran and the Quran is with Ali). Now let's see in which books this Hadith has been narrated. See, although I should mention to you that Janabe Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh), in his book 'Abaqat al-Anwar', until his time—that is, he passed away in 1306 AH—until that time, he wrote the names of approximately 188 or 189 books and authors who narrated this Hadith. And after 1300, until now, Janabe Ali Tabatabai, who wrote a supplement on it, Who wrote a supplement on it, added at least 100-150 more authors' names who—we are not talking about the Shias, we are not talking about the Shias, let no one misunderstand—and Janabe Mir Hamid Hussain did what? For each one, he properly stated their biography, which is called 'Tarjama' in Arabic, explaining how their own scholars considered them 'Thiqah' (reliable) and trustworthy. It is clear, isn't it? He explained this thing with such detail. So, anyway, let's quickly read the names of the books. Which books... Insha'Allah, more details later. First of all, 'Sahih Muslim', which is considered the most important book among the Ahl-e-Sunnah after Bukhari. And Bukhari and Muslim are considered so authentic among them that if something is not in Bukhari and Muslim, they object to it, saying, 'The Sheikh did not narrate this.' Sheikh Bukhari and Sheikh Muslim. Muslim, i.e., Hajjaj Nishapuri, who wrote 'Sahih Muslim'. After that, Ahmad ibn Hanbal's 'Musnad'. Then after that, Tirmidhi, whose book is counted among the 'Sihah al-Sittah' (the six authentic books) of the Ahl-e-Sunnah. Is counted among the 'Sihah al-Sittah' of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, the six authentic Hadith books, among which is Tirmidhi. He narrated it. Then after that, Nasa'i. Nasa'i is also counted among the 'Sihah al-Sittah'. So, out of the six, these three are there. Then after that, if you look at the current era, Nasiruddin al-Albani has counted it among the authentic Hadiths. He wrote a book, 'Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah'. He wrote a whole book, detailing everything in it, stating which Hadiths are authentic. After that, Hakim Nishapuri, whom people call 'Nisaburi' in Arabic, wrote a book, 'Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn', meaning those Hadiths that Bukhari and Muslim did not narrate, he narrated them. And what did he narrate? That the narrations I am recording were not narrated by Bukhari and Muslim, but they fulfill their conditions. That is, they fulfill the conditions. Then after that, Haythami narrated it. Nawawi, who wrote the commentary on Muslim, will also do so. Those who wrote the Sharh (commentary) of Sahih Muslim, then after that Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, then al-Bayhaqi, Ibn Abi Asim, al-Athir, and Ibn Hajar al-Makki—whose death occurred in 974 AH—wrote the book 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa' (The Burning Thunderbolts). The title means 'burning thunderbolts,' and he wrote that he was going to cast these thunderbolts upon the Shias so that they would be burnt to ashes. The sole purpose of writing 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa' was this. If you read the book—and we will provide all the references—they all wrote, poor souls, intending to burn [the Shias], but instead, they ended up narrating all the Hadith in favor of the Ahl al-Bayt. Alhamdulillah, we take many references from those very books. Then there is the book by Ibn Asakir, then Ibn Abi Shaybah, then after that, Al-Muttaqi al-Hindi, Mulla Muttaqi al-Hindi Burhanpuri, the author of 'Kanz al-Ummal' from India, which is an encyclopedia—the encyclopedia of the Ahl al-Sunnah. He was from Burhanpur, which is in today's Madhya Pradesh, so he was from there, and besides that... Yes, and besides that, look at Ibn Abi al-Hadid who was Mu'tazili, then after that Al-Aqili, Al-Hamawi, Imam Hamawi, Sahib Fara'id al-Simt, and after that Al-Juwayni al-Hanafi, the teacher of Al-Dhahabi, who was the teacher of Al-Suyuti, Salih al-Shami, Zarandi al-Hanafi, then Al-Baghawi, then Al-Qunduzi al-Hanafi from Turkey, then Ibn Manzur, the author of 'Lisan al-Arab', who is considered the greatest linguist of the Islamic world. Among the Muslims, there was no linguist greater than him; his book is a dictionary, a lexicon, 'Lisan al-Arab'. And after that, Al-Fasawi and many other sources. There is a whole list, as I just mentioned a few for your service. It is clear, isn't it? And if I were to describe the chain of narration for each one, it would take at least 500 to 100 episodes, but I don't want to tire you out that much. Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the ability, we will try to cover it in a few episodes regarding the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. In the next episode, you will see what the results are. Wa Sallallahu ala Muhammad, Tariq Mas'ud Malumi.

chapters.title: Addressing the Objection on Imamate and Rule
chapters.summary: The speaker addresses the misconception that the honor of Islam is dependent on worldly political rule, clarifying that the 12 Imams represent spiritual authority.

chapters.title: Defining True Caliphate and Honor
chapters.summary: Using the examples of Prophets Adam, Dawood, and Luqman, the speaker explains that divine Caliphate is based on knowledge and wisdom rather than mere political power.

chapters.title: Spiritual Leadership vs. Worldly Authority
chapters.summary: The lecture argues that spiritual influence and knowledge define the greatness of Islam, citing the historical role of the Imams and the irrelevance of worldly rule to their divine status.

chapters.title: Intellect and the Occultation of Imam Mahdi
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that true believers possess intellect and insight, allowing them to perceive the Imam in occultation similarly to how Uwais al-Qarni perceived the Prophet.

chapters.title: Critique of Historical and Modern Hypocrisy
chapters.summary: The speaker criticizes the glorification of Yazid and the silence of modern religious authorities regarding the current state of the holy cities.

chapters.title: The Authenticity of Hadith al-Thaqalayn

chapters.title: Scholarly Evidence for Hadith al-Thaqalayn
chapters.summary: The speaker cites numerous Sunni sources, including Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad, that document the Hadith al-Thaqalayn as a mutawatir narration.

chapters.title: Sunni Scholars and Ahl al-Bayt Narrations
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses various Sunni scholars who authored works intending to refute Shias but inadvertently documented numerous Hadith supporting the Ahl al-Bayt.

chapters.title: Scholarly Sources and Future Discussions
chapters.summary: A list of prominent Sunni scholars and linguists is provided, highlighting the vast historical evidence available regarding the Hadith al-Thaqalayn.

title: Majlis 7 | Marefat-e-Nooraaniyyah (Part-6) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual status of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Ahl al-Bayt through the lens of Ma'rifat-e-Nooraaniyyah. It connects the foundational injustices of Saqifah to the tragedy of Karbala, emphasizing the divine authority, knowledge, and patience of the Imams. The discourse concludes with a moving tribute to the bravery and loyalty of Janab-e-Abbas, highlighting his role in the events of Karbala.
content:
She is weeping while thinking, she is weeping while thinking, that it has become a desert even today. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. I used to envy the dust at the feet of Haider-e-Karrar. The wind used to sit and deliver his letters. Alas, the state my lion has been reduced to, alas, the state my lion has been reduced to. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. Even after dying, he fulfilled the promise he made to me. I take great pride in the loyalty of my son. Now, I have no shame before the mother of Asghar. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. In exchange for the father, the Muslims took nine sons. The head is severed, the body is severed, the arms of the lion are severed. Your picture is in pieces, your picture is in pieces, O Ali. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. What a stature he had, he himself knew that. How did Qasim come, huddled into a bundle? I, Farwa, know what my helplessness is. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. When did my desire fit in the door, you are my son. Where have the oppressors placed these corpses of yours? Even the veil on my head, even the veil on my head, is greater than your grave. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. She is weeping while thinking, it has become a desert even today. Like Asghar-e-Basheer, is the grave of Abbas. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome is for the people of piety and certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of the prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family, the infallible ones from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, our Imam of the time, our Master of affairs, our Owner, our Master, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate friend, the fortified cave, and the succor of the distressed and the needy. May my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our Master and Leader, Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon them both), has said: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn has wounded our eyelids and caused our tears to flow. So, let the weepers weep for the likes of Husayn.' The voice of our Master Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (a.s.), peace and blessings be upon him. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. So our Imam al-Ridha (a.s.) says that 'Inna yawmal Husayn' (Indeed, the day of Husayn) has surely wounded our eyelids and a flood of tears is flowing from our eyes; we are weeping. So if one must weep, one should weep for a person like Husayn. The discussion was regarding the 'Marifat-e-Nuraniya' (the luminous recognition) of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and the matter reached the point where the Mawla says, 'Ana Sirat al-Mustaqim' (I am the Straight Path). And in the context of the Ziyarat of the Mawla in 'Mafatih al-Jinan', specifically the fifth Ziyarat, a brief explanation—though the actual condition is known only to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) themselves—continuing with that Ziyarat, the Mawla says, 'I am the strong rope of Allah, and I am the Straight Path.' That is, the apparent meaning is that you are the strong rope of Allah and you are the Straight Path, and then the one performing the Ziyarat bears witness. I bear witness. 'Annaka Hujjatullahi 'ala khalqihi' (That you are the proof of Allah over His creation), 'Wa shahiduhu 'ala 'ibadihi' (And His witness over His servants). Look, what does 'witness' mean? When you call someone as a witness, who is called as a witness? A witness is someone who has seen the entire scene with their own eyes. Only such a person can be made a witness. Otherwise, you cannot make someone who was not there a witness. Regarding the Master of the Universe (Amir al-Mu'minin), it is found in the Ziyarat that you are a witness. Allah has made you a witness over His servants. That is, all the servants of Allah, from the beginning to the end, the Master of the Universe sees them all, is seeing them, and will continue to see them, and will bear witness for everyone on the Day of Judgment as to who was like what. 'Shahiduhu 'ala 'ibadihi wa aminuhu 'ala 'ilmihi' (His witness over His servants and His trustee over His knowledge). That is, Allah has entrusted His knowledge to Amir al-Mu'minin as a trust. He has deposited it as a trust, entrusting Amir al-Mu'minin, saying, 'This is My knowledge, you must take care of it.' Amir al-Mu'minin is the trustee of Allah's knowledge. Allah entrusted His entire knowledge to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). 'Wa khazinu sirrihi' (And you are the treasurer of His secret). That is, you are the treasurer. You possess the secrets of Allah. Allah has not told these secrets to anyone except Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and, for instance, Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.). No one else is aware of these secrets. Allah will reveal this when He deems it appropriate. 'Khazinu sirrihi wa mawdi'u hikmatihi' (The treasurer of His secret and the place of His wisdom). And you are the place of Allah's wisdom. That is, if anyone needs wisdom, they should go to Hazrat-e-Amir. Look at what is found in the Holy Quran: 'Wa man yu'tal-hikmata faqad utiya khayran kathira' (And whoever is given wisdom, he has been given much good). Wisdom means insight. Whoever Allah has given wisdom has been given much good. Allah has given much goodness in his favor. Allah knows best what this 'much good' is. So, where is the place to receive this wisdom? It is Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). If someone needs wisdom, they should go to Amir al-Mu'minin. If we look at the interpretation of wisdom that has come in the narrations, it is 'Marifatullah' (the recognition of Allah). The recognition of Allah is wisdom. That is, knowing Allah is wisdom. So, if someone wants to know Allah, if someone wants to recognize Allah, who should they go to? They should go to Amir al-Mu'minin. The recognition of the Imam is with Amir al-Mu'minin. The lawful and the unlawful are with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). The Quran is with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). The interpretation (Tafsir) of the Quran is with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). The inner meaning (Ta'wil) of the Quran is with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Now, whoever needs wisdom should come to the door of Amir al-Mu'minin. They should present themselves at the door of Amir al-Mu'minin. Until they present themselves at the door of Ali, they will neither recognize Allah, nor the Imam, nor will they understand the lawful and the unlawful, nor will they understand obedience. They will not understand anything. They will not recognize the Quran, nor its interpretation, nor its inner meaning. Nothing will be understandable to them. Look, memorizing something by rote is not the same as understanding it. That we have memorized something and said we have understood it—there is a difference between the two. That is why we have many narrations. We have narrations that say: 'A Hadith that you understand is better than a thousand Hadith that you merely narrate.' One Hadith that you understand well is better than a thousand Hadith that you just narrate. That is, the emphasis here is on understanding. On understanding the concept, on understanding the meanings. On understanding its depth, its profundity. There is an emphasis on that; we have an insistence on it. But where must one go? To the threshold of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Only then will all these things be attained, and I bear witness that you are the brother of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Akhu Rasul. Wa ashhadu. Now look here, as I mentioned regarding the Mawla in this Ziyarat—this is the fifth Ziyarat in Mafatih—especially when you go for the Ziyarat of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) in Najaf al-Ashraf, you must recite this Ziyarat. Otherwise, if you do not have time or for whatever reason, although one should recite all the Ziyarats—all the seven or eight Ziyarats in Mafatih should be recited—besides that, one should recite Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah Kabirah. Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah Kabirah should be recited in whichever shrine you visit, whether it is Najaf, Karbala, Samarra, Kadhimiya, Medina, or for instance, when in Iran; wherever you go, you must recite Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah Kabirah in every shrine. Allama Majlisi’s (r.a.) noble father, Sheikh Muhammad Taqi Majlisi, says that it was my practice that whenever I visited any shrine, I would definitely recite Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah Kabirah. Because Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah Kabirah contains the mention of the perfections (kamalat) of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and their Ma'rifat (gnosis). A very profound Ma'rifat of theirs is present within it. So, you must recite it and try to understand what is written in it. Now, the Masa'ib (tragedies) begin from here. Ashhadu anna da'wataka haqq. I bear witness, O Ali, that your call—meaning your Imamate, your Caliphate—was the truth. It was yours, only yours. We are using the word 'only' intentionally because the Quran has used it. The Quran said: 'Innama waliyyukumullahu wa rasuluhu walladhina amanu alladhina yuqimuna-s-salata wa yu'tuna-z-zakata wa hum raki'un.' Your... Wali is only Allah. Only Allah, and His Messenger, and those believers who establish prayer and give Zakat while they are in the state of Ruku. This is the announcement of Wilayah. Look, many exegetes debate about it—what this means, whether he gave the ring or not, what it was, and what it was—there is no need to debate all this. See, although our scholars have debated and presented evidence to complete the argument (hujjat) and have proven that the occasion of revelation (shane nuzul) is that Ali (a.s.) himself gave the ring and after that, the verse was revealed. This is in our tradition, and our scholars also debate it. And it is also written after this that some people gave rings 60 times so that it might be revealed in their honor, but nothing was revealed. Every time they would come and ask, 'Has anything been revealed?' And they would say, 'No, nothing yet.' 'O Messenger of Allah, no one? But I just gave a ring.' Perhaps they kept giving and taking it back. But they could not understand that the one who came to ask was not an ordinary human being. This was an angel. And Ali (a.s.) gave the ring, and after that, the verse was revealed. It turns out that Allah had sent the angel to ask for the ring. After that, He sent Jibra'il with the verse. This means that the beggar (sa'il)—the one who was asking—was also sent by Allah. The verse was also revealed by Allah. So, it means that on both sides, Allah is sending the beggar here and the verse there. So, it is clear that there is nothing else to it. Allah only had to make an announcement. It was only an announcement of Wilayah. What is there to debate about this? What are you debating, brother? That this does not mean this, that does not mean that... there is no benefit in all these debates. But anyway, it is fine; our scholars have debated it, provided answers, and given excellent responses regarding the verse of Wilayah, and you can refer to the scholarly books. The part of the verse in 'Abaqat al-Anwar' also contains a response. Besides that, it is also in 'Misbah al-Hidaya', in which they have discussed 40 verses, and this is one of them. And 'Misbah al-Hidaya' is available online; it is also available in English. You can see the entire discussion within it. But anyway, I bear witness that your call—meaning your Imamate, your Caliphate—is the truth; there is nothing besides it. Wa kullu da'in mansubin dunaka batilun madhujun. And every caller besides you—whoever is calling, whoever is claiming Imamate, whoever is claiming Caliphate besides you—and 'mansub' (the one who has been installed/appointed), is false and 'madhuj'. 'Madhuj' is derived from 'dahaza', meaning the one who has been refuted. 'Madhuj' means rejected. And 'dahaza' is just like 'rafada'. 'Rafada' means to reject, to refute. 'Rafada' and 'dahaza' both have almost the same meaning; they are synonyms. Meaning to reject, not to accept. So, we do not accept them at all. We reject every person who came in opposition to Ali (a.s.); we 'rafz' (reject) them. That is why we are Rafidi. And we are proud of this title. There are some ignorant individuals among us who say, 'We are not Rafidi.' Oh brother, if you are not a Rafidi, then you are a hypocrite. Understand the meaning. You don't know the meaning, and you say anything. The Rafidis have been praised in the traditions, and Allah has given this name. Rafidi, Rafidi—this is a good name. 'Rafid' means the one who rejects, the one who refutes, the one who turns away. Turning away from whom? Turning away from falsehood. So, is the one who turns away from falsehood good or bad? Obviously, it is good. So, this sentence is in the Ziyarat. I bear witness that whoever is besides you is false, is 'madhuj'. I do not accept him. I do not accept him even by a particle. I do not accept him for even a second. Anta awwal al-mazlum. O Ali, this is a sentence from the Ziyarat. You are the first oppressed one. Meaning, after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), among the Imams, you are the first oppressed one. Awwal al-mazlum wa awwal al-maghsub. And you are the first whose right was usurped. Your right was usurped, your right was snatched away. Maghsubin haqqa. Fasabarta wahtasabta. You observed patience, and all this was only in the path of Allah. It was 'ehtesab'. 'Ehtesab' means in the path of Allah. The Mawla of the universe observed patience only to attain reward from Allah. And in Khutbah al-Shaqshaqiyyah, the Mawla says exactly this. Look at Khutbah al-Shaqshaqiyyah, which is the third sermon of Nahj al-Balagha. In it, the Mawla says this sentence. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. When the right was snatched away... you should read the whole sermon; we are not reading the whole sermon now, just reading two lines for you. When this right was snatched away, the Mawla says, 'Fasadaltu dunaha thawban.' 'Dun'—meaning other than the Caliphate. 'I cast a veil over this Caliphate.' Meaning, I did not even want to look in that direction. 'I cast a veil over it.' 'Wa tawaytu 'anha kashhan.' And I turned away from it. Now I did not want it anymore. I turned away. 'Wa tafiqtu art'i bayna an asula bi-yadin jadhtha.' Now I was thinking, I had two options before me. The Mawla says, I had two options before me. One, that I should attack. Attack completely. 'Bi-yadin jadhtha'—with a broken hand. What does a broken hand mean? That there is no helper, no supporter. There was no companion, no one was with me then. Except for a few individuals, that's it. And their number is said to be from four to a maximum of 16. That's it. No more than this. These were the helpers, these were the supporters with me then. There were no more than this. That is why the Mawla says, should I attack with these few men, or what was the other thing? Or should I observe patience? 'Aw asbira 'ala tihatin 'amiya.' On what should I observe patience? Should I observe patience on a calamity that is blinding? This is a calamity that makes a person blind. It makes a person lose their sight, makes them blind. And then he says, 'Yahramu fiha al-kabir.' This is a calamity in which the elderly—meaning those who are, for example, 60 years old—become 80 years old. 'Yahramu.' They call it 'yahramu' in Arabic, which is for someone who is about 80 years old. And 'kabir' means someone who is 55-60 years old. 'Yahramu fiha.' It was such a calamity that a person would age in it. 60-year-olds would become 80-year-olds. 'Wa yashibu fiha al-saghir.' And the young, the youth, would become old. Meaning 20-year-olds would become 40-year-olds, 50-year-olds, their beards would turn white. Such a severe calamity. 'Wa yakdahu fiha mu'minun hatta yalqa rabbah.' And the believer had no choice in it but to keep struggling, keep struggling until death comes to him. That's it. He has 'kad' (effort) and nothing else. So, I had these two options, the Mawla says. These were the only two options. Two possibilities. Therefore, I chose the second, I selected the second. 'Fasabartu.' I observed patience. 'Wa fi al-'ayn qadha.' While there were thorns in my eyes. There were thorns in my eyes. 'Wa fi al-halqi shaja.' And there was a bone in my throat. You see, these are two calamities. If a tiny particle goes into a person's eye, what is their condition? If someone puts a large thorn in it, then what will be the condition? My Mawla says, that was my condition. There were thorns in my eyes. There was a bone stuck in my throat. And I was seeing my inheritance being looted. The religion was being ruined, the religion was being destroyed. This is Nahj al-Balagha, Khutbah al-Shaqshaqiyyah, Sermon number three. You must read it, read the whole sermon with attention, and see what the Mawla says. I was seeing my inheritance being looted. As it is found in history and traditions, the Mawla would sit on the prayer mat in the Prophet's Mosque, in a corner, in a niche. He would sit on the prayer mat in the corner and keep watching, watching the whole scene. That the ruler is sitting there, and people are coming and pledging allegiance at his hands and asking him questions, and he is giving any answer. He is giving the answer that comes to his heart, he is giving an answer. Because he had no knowledge of the lawful, no knowledge of the forbidden. He didn't even know the religion; what answer would he give? And the Mawla is watching everything. So here he says that I observed patience. Patience—and this is what we recite in the Ziyarat, this same sentence. That you 'fasabarta wahtasabta'—you observed patience only for the sake of Allah, only because of Allah. Just for the sake of Allah, accountability. Because you know that one has to be patient in the path of Allah. A promise was made to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Since the topic has come up, let me present another point for your service: there are some people among us who love others very much. They do not love their own; they love others very much and say that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was pleased with them, and he was satisfied with those people. They claim that initially, he said his right was snatched, but later, when he saw that the right could not be obtained, he became satisfied. Nowhere in any tradition or hadith is there a mention of Ali (a.s.)'s pleasure and satisfaction with others. In fact, it is the opposite in a hadith. You pick up the book; it is present in Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali. Allama Majlisi has quoted it in Bihar al-Anwar, volume 29. Allama Majlisi has quoted in Bihar al-Anwar that the Master of the Universe, even when he attained the apparent caliphate, meaning when he became the Caliph, even after that, whenever he came to the pulpit, he would say, 'Mazil, mazil, I am oppressed, I am oppressed.' Since the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left this world, I have been oppressed. Since the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left this world, I have been oppressed. And in the end, the Banu Umayya came and said, 'Brother, this is our man, so we will bury him.' Then Ali said, 'You cannot bury him here in Jannat al-Baqi. Go and bury him in Hash-e-Kawkab.' Hash-e-Kawkab was the Jewish cemetery. 'Bury him there, you cannot bury him here.' Is this Hadith true?' So he understood who she was. He said, 'You are a Shia, aren't you? If you have come here with your husband's permission, then may Allah's curse be upon your husband. And if you have come without your husband's permission, then may Allah's curse be upon you.' So she said, 'Correct. Third question.' Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Ya Ali! Third question. The lady who came to fight in the Battle of Jamal, did she come with her husband's permission or without permission?' Now, as soon as Ibn Jawzi heard this, he sat down silently. And after that, he never repeated, 'Ask me before I depart from among you.' Because for his answer, one ordinary Shia woman was enough. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and his progeny: Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib. And likewise, the progeny of Ali ibn Abi Talib was also the same. Tremendous offspring. Like Janab-e-Abbas. Such upbringing, in which the mother also had a very big role. The mother, Janab-e-Ummul Baneen, had a very big role. Whenever the Masa'ib (tragedies) of Janab-e-Abbas are recited, our scholars and our Zakireen always used to mention Janab-e-Ummul Baneen first, and this should be the case. Do come. That Janab-e-Ummul Baneen must be mentioned. That along with the upbringing of the Mawla-e-Kainat, Janab-e-Ummul Baneen provided such upbringing, such training to Janab-e-Abbas, that she herself was consistently like that—she never imagined herself as anything else, but considered herself a maid in the house of Sayyeda Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), and she raised her children the same way: 'You are the slaves of Hasan and Hussain.' This is the effect of upbringing. This is the effect of a mother's training. And the external training—how did the Mawla-e-Kainat train him? The Battle of Siffin—when did the Battle of Siffin take place? It took place in 38 Hijri. In 38 Hijri, the Battle of Siffin took place. What was Hazrat Abbas's age at that time? That is, it was very young. It was not more than 12-13 years. But regardless, his personality was very impressive. He was tall, well-built. He had a good personality. So people thought he was older, but he was not more than 13-14 years old. Even if you take his age to be higher, it was still not more than 15-20 years. If someone—we are just saying this for the sake of argument, to complete the proof. But when you look at the Battle of Siffin, two characters appear in the Battle of Siffin. I am just bringing you to one point. That is, how important the mother's role, the mother's training is. Peace be upon Janab-e-Ummul Baneen. If any of your prayers are not being answered, then ask Hazrat Abbas by invoking the name of Janab-e-Ummul Baneen. Janab-e-Ummul Baneen, you see, your prayer will surely be answered. It is upbringing; I present two incidents before you. Both of these are from the Battle of Siffin. Or one is perhaps from the Battle of Jamal, currently it is not in our mind. The Mawla-e-Kainat told Muhammad ibn Hanafiyyah, 'Go and attack.' As soon as Muhammad ibn Hanafiyyah went, there was a rain of arrows, and Ibn Hanafiyyah came back. The Mawla sent him again, 'Go.' He went again, there was a rain of arrows, and he came back. When he sent him the third time and he came back, the Mawla-e-Kainat struck his sword—the blunt side, the side with the edge—on Ibn Hanafiyyah's back and said, 'This is the effect of your mother's milk.' This is its effect. Now, what we see in the Battle of Siffin is the opposite of that. That the Mawla-e-Kainat is sending them one by one to fight. But Janab-e-Abbas in the Battle of Siffin is constantly circling, trying to get a chance. Now when he goes, when the Mawla sends him, there is a rain of arrows, so the Mawla sends Janab-e-Abbas. And he beheads all the sons of a wrestler. Janab-e-Abbas. There was an uproar that Ali himself had come to fight! Ali himself had come to fight! When there was an uproar, when Janab-e-Abbas returned, the Mawla-e-Kainat said to Janab-e-Abbas, 'Remove the veil from your face.' When Janab-e-Abbas removed the veil, people said, 'Abbas! Abbas ibn Ali!' That is, so brave and courageous, at such a young age! That's it. From this, you can estimate the bravery of Janab-e-Abbas, you can estimate his courage. That is why Imam Hussain (a.s.) made him his standard-bearer. But every time he asked for permission to fight, the Imam would refuse, saying, 'Abbas!' "You are the standard-bearer of my army." Now, when Abbas (a.s.) used to see the children crying, "Al-atash, al-atash, al-atash" (thirst, thirst, thirst), what must have passed through Abbas's heart? What must have gone through the heart of this brave Abbas? What must have been his state, his condition? Just think for a moment. The children are crying, "Al-atash, I am thirsty." Just once, after Dhuhr on the day of Ashura, a wave of hope ran through the hearts of the children when Abbas came and called out at the door of the tent, "Sakina! Daughter Sakina!" So Sakina came running, "Uncle, why did you call?" He said, "Child, bring your waterskin." She asked, "What will you do with the waterskin?" He said, "The Master (Imam Hussain) has ordered me to bring water." To bring water. Sakina heard this and became happy; she went and brought the waterskin. Now, it is written in the Maqtal that when Sakina brought the waterskin, the children started walking along with her, "Bibi, where are you taking this waterskin?" She said, "My father has ordered my uncle to bring water. Now my uncle will bring water." "Children, now be at peace. Now you will have water, you will surely get it. My uncle will definitely bring water." When he makes a promise, he fulfills it. Sakina gave the waterskin to Abbas. Abbas took the waterskin and came towards the Euphrates. He urged his horse into the Euphrates, cutting through the armies, and entered the Euphrates. After entering the Euphrates, Abbas dismounted and took some water, and after taking it, he said, "O oppressors! Do not think that I am helpless and powerless. The water is in my control, but I do not drink it because the children in the tent are thirsty, Sakina is thirsty, the ladies are thirsty." And saying this, he threw away the water that was in his cupped hands. After throwing it, Abbas wetted the waterskin, filled it, and after filling it, he mounted his horse and started to move. As he began to move, a wretch struck from behind and severed his right arm. Abbas's right arm was severed. Abbas recited a Rajaz, saying that even if you cut off my right arm, I will still continue to support my Imam, I will continue to help him. Just a little later, another wretch attacked and severed his left arm. Now that his left arm was severed, Abbas held the waterskin with his teeth so that somehow the water might reach the tent. Just that the water might reach. Abbas was galloping the horse so that the water would reach the tent. He had not gone far when Hurmula fired such an arrow of tyranny, Hurmula fired such an arrow of tyranny that it hit the waterskin. As soon as it hit the waterskin, the water fell out. The water of the waterskin flowed away. Now Abbas bowed his head. Now what will I do when I go towards the tent? Now what will I do? As soon as Abbas bowed his head, a wretch came from behind and struck a mace, a heavy mace, on Abbas's head. The Lion of Ali fell from the back of his horse onto the land of Karbala. O mourners, whenever someone falls from a height, they first put their hands forward, taking the support of their hands. But both of Abbas's hands had been severed. Abbas fell face-first onto the land of Karbala. Then the wretched ones attacked in such a way that Abbas called out, "Master! Goodbye!" As soon as Abbas's voice reached Hussain's ears, Hussain arrived, Hussain came, and held his back. "Al-aan, inkasara zahri." Abbas! Now my back is broken. Now my back is broken. "Qallat heelati." Abbas, I cannot see anything. Darkness has fallen before my eyes. Abbas! "Shamata biya aduwi." The enemy is taunting me. The enemy is taunting me. Your standard-bearer has been killed. Your standard-bearer has been killed. He reached the edge of the stream, and placed the lion's head on his lap. There was some conversation between the brothers. Abbas made his wills. One of the wills was that do not take my body to the tent. I had promised that I would bring water. What is this? Enough now. He departed from this world. As soon as his eyes closed, Hussain recited a dirge again. O Abbas, now with your departure, those eyes that were awake until now due to your awe will now sleep in peace. Now the ladies will stay awake, the noble ladies will stay awake. Hussain took the standard and the waterskin, and now went towards the tent with the empty waterskin. Now, when she saw the standard from afar, Sakina said, "Children, look, my uncle has come." Didn't I say that my uncle would definitely bring water? Now, as soon as Hussain came near, she saw that it was only Hussain. Sakina asked, "Father, didn't Uncle come?" He said, "Child, do not wait for Uncle anymore. Uncle is at the edge of the Euphrates." "Wa saya'lamu alladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. La'natullahi 'ala al-qawmi al-zalimin." O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. Count us all among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Grant the sick a complete and swift recovery. Grant the prisoners their release. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Those who are protecting them, You protect them. Grant us the privilege of the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Haq aur Ahle Haq Ki Pehchan
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the importance of identifying the truth through gentleness and discernment rather than following the crowd. The speaker warns against the tendency to sway with popular opinion or prevailing winds, which often leads people away from the path of righteousness. True recognition of the truth requires personal courage and a steadfast commitment to principles regardless of majority influence.
content:
And the Mawla was saying, it was he who stated, "Al-rifqu bil-haqq" (gentleness with the truth), always recognize the truth, "ta'rifu ahlahu" (then you will recognize its people). For this, one needs courage, and if there is no courage, then what does a person do? "Yamiluna ma'a kulli reeh" (they sway with every wind). Wherever the wind blows, these people start going there. Where the wind blew, they went there. Where the wind blew, they went there. This is Subhan Allah, that is Subhan Allah. They look at where the wind is blowing. Towards whom is the wind? Towards whom is the majority? Towards whom is the multitude?
Gentleness is a key tool in recognizing the truth.
Recognizing the truth leads to identifying its true followers.
Lack of courage causes people to sway with every wind.
Following the majority or popular opinion is a sign of weakness.
True believers remain steadfast rather than following shifting trends.
One must prioritize principle over the direction of the crowd.

title: Wabaa (Pandemic) Ko Khatm Karne Ka Aazmaaya Hua Tareeqa
excerpt: This lecture discusses the spiritual response to pandemics, specifically referencing a historical plague in Samarra. The speaker highlights how the household of Aqa Buzurg Shirazi remained protected from the outbreak through the continuous recitation of Majlis for Imam Hussain. The talk emphasizes the efficacy of reciting Ziyarat-e-Ashura as a divinely inspired remedy to ward off calamities and illnesses.
content:
Now you have seen how something like Corona brought the whole world to its knees. A trivial thing that no one can even see, no one is actually able to understand what it is. And many people even denied it; initially, people said it, but when their own people started dying, they realized, 'No, no, this is real.' Otherwise, many people had denied it, saying it was someone's conspiracy, so there were many theories. But regardless, when people started dying themselves, they understood. Meaning, when Allah wills, one thing—now it's not that a plague has come for the first time, it has happened before. Once, a plague came to Samarra, and Aqa Buzurg Shirazi was the Marja-e-Taqlid at that time. So, a Marja-e-Taqlid narrates that his grandfather told him that there was no house in Samarra where someone did not die. There was no such house. Even the one who gave ghusl to the dead, he also died. The one who recited talqin, he also died. The one who dug the graves, he also died. Such was the situation. But in our house, not a single death occurred. Not one. And the reason for that was that we continuously held Majlis of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada in our house. Meaning, not a single month went by without a Majlis of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada in our house. This Majlis. At that time, the condition of Samarra was very bad. And all this is present in books; scholars have narrated it. Ayatollah Vahid Khorasani has also narrated this. People came to the Marja-e-Taqlid of that time, who was Aqa Buzurg Shirazi, the one who had issued the fatwa on tobacco. So his fatwa—if any young person here doesn't know what the fatwa was and what its significance was—it was something due to which the British government had to leave the region. Aqa Buzurg Shirazi issued that fatwa at that time. And that fatwa was, upon the suggestion of Aqa Fazl-ul-Din, that it is Wajib (obligatory) for everyone to recite Ziyarat-e-Ashura daily. Ziyarat-e-Ashura. And when Ziyarat-e-Ashura was recited, this plague ended in Samarra. And it ended. Meaning, with difficulty, in three or a few days. I don't remember the exact number of days, but it ended very quickly. Ziyarat-e-Ashura has great effect, it has a very great impact.
Pandemics are historical realities that test human resilience and faith.
The household of Aqa Buzurg Shirazi was protected from a plague in Samarra.
Continuous Majlis of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada serves as a spiritual shield.

Reciting Ziyarat-e-Ashura daily is a recommended spiritual practice during crises.
The plague in Samarra subsided rapidly after the community adopted the recitation of Ziyarat-e-Ashura.
Spiritual devotion can have tangible effects on physical well-being and protection.

title: Majlis 2 | Ahle Bait (a.s.) Ki Mohabbat, Nusrat aur Wilaayat Ka Sawaab | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the fundamental concepts of Wilayah, Tawalla, and Tabarra, emphasizing the necessity of absolute devotion to the Ahlulbayt. He provides theological and historical evidence from the Quran and Hadith to validate the status of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the importance of disassociating from his enemies. The discourse also addresses historical distortions, the significance of scholarly defenses like Abaqat al-Anwar, and the moral imperative of standing against tyranny as exemplified by Imam Husayn (a.s.).
content:
O moon of Karbala, you must have seen, the stars of the highest heavens descended upon this earth, O moon, O moon, the moon of Hashim is shining here, take the charity of light from here, O moon, O moon, keep this land always cool, those who are sleeping here are the beloveds of Zahra, O moon, they are the masters of Tasnim, Sabil, and Kauthar, those who were killed thirsty, on the bank of this river, O moon, brave warriors like Hur and Habib and companions were killed right here, O companions of the King, O moon. Killed right here with cruelty and tyranny, both beloveds of Muslim, both sons of Zainab, O moon. And the body of Qasim was being trampled in the battlefield, Abbas and Sarwar were picking up his pieces, O moon. And the arms of Abbas-e-Wafa were severed right here, he did not get permission to fight, he could not even bring water, O moon. On this land, this tragedy also passed upon Sarwar, the likeness of Mustafa took a spear in his chest, O moon. And Sarwar brought a little darling to give water. What a strange news, after being hit by the arrow of tyranny, O moon, and the neck of the son was pierced, the arm of the father was pierced, both passed away from the world in agony and thirst, O moon, and at that moment a little girl was looking for her father, when the heads were scattered, a difficult search, O moon, then you also saw that grief-stricken girl sleeping on the chest, clinging to the headless father, O moon, and arms were tied right here in the first watch, Sajjad left this land with his head bowed, O moon, the Prince of Paradise is the master of Karbala, who has the courage to come until he calls, O moon, and those who reached Karbala, O Sibte-Jafar, I wish destiny would show them this day again, O King of Karbala. A'udhu billahi as-sami'i al-'alim min ash-shaytani ar-rajim, bismillahi ar-rahmani ar-rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahi al-'aliyyi al-'azim. Hasbunallahu wa ni'ma al-wakil, ni'ma al-mawla wa ni'ma an-nasir. Alhamdullillahi rabbil 'alamin, wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya'i wal mursalin, habibi ilahil 'alamin, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Salla allahu 'alayhi wa alihi al-ma'sumin, alladhina adhhaba allahu 'anhum ar-rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Especially the Baqiyatullah on the earths, the Imam of our time, the guardian of our affairs, our master, and our mawla. O our beloved, our physician, our companion, our master, the one who is sufficient for the believers, the helper of the righteous, the straight path, may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala says in the Holy Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'Allah has not made for any man two hearts in his interior.' Allah the Exalted, the Almighty has spoken the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. The Almighty God says in His glorious book that 'Allah has not made for any man two hearts in his interior.' Allah has not placed two hearts inside any human being; there is only one heart. Meaning, if he loves the truth, then the love of falsehood is impossible in his heart. Yesterday, I submitted to your service regarding the Wilayah and Bara'ah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), how it is obligatory, and it is such an obligation that no human can escape, and there is no excuse for it. In every situation, one must act upon it. For example, for prayer, there is Qasr (shortened) prayer; if the situation is not right, for instance, if a person is sick or traveling, then fasting is not obligatory upon them. If one is not capable (Mustati), Hajj is not obligatory. But this Wilayah is such a thing that even if a person is dying, until their last breath, they should be mindful of the Imam of their time. Until the last breath, meaning even when the soul is departing, one should be mindful; in fact, it would not be wrong to say that if the soul is departing, one should be even more mindful. Remember your Imam more, worry about your Imam more, and keep remembering your Imam every moment, every second. Jabir al-Jufi is a strange personality. 90,000 hadiths. 90,000, and he said, 'Jabir, this is only for you, do not give it to anyone.' And in Bihar al-Anwar, there are many repetitions, things have been reiterated, but here there was nothing like that. Naturally, 'Maula, you gave so many hadiths, I cannot bear it.' Recite a Salawat, Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aale Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. So these were 90,000 hadiths, 90,000 hadiths, this was only for Jabir. And what he narrated is different, yes? That is different. There is no discussion about that. 'Oh, we mention his kohl, we mention his locks, we mention his cloak, we mention his horses, we mention his camel, we mention his sword, we mention everything.' Certainly, there is a curse on him. But do not limit the curse only to Yazid. Whoever is responsible for bringing Yazid to that position, there is a curse on all of them. All of them, all those who are responsible. If you say, 'We did not know,' then when you did not know, you should not have done such a thing. This is why Allah has forbidden it, that this position of Imamate can only be from Allah. Now it happened, history bore witness to what happened. What was Yazid? He was a fasiq (sinner), a fajir (wicked), a drunkard, he played with monkeys and dogs. Sister, daughter, mother, wife, slave-girl—he had no sense of anything. Nothing at all. There was no mention of Islam anywhere near him. No trace of it. Now, today's Muslim is trying his best to find some fabricated hadith to claim that the Messenger of Allah prophesied about Yazid. So, a curse on such a Muslim who goes into such defenses. Anyway, history says that Yazid became the king of the Muslims. And as soon as he became king, the first thing he did was write a letter to all his governors, saying, 'Tell all the big people there to pledge allegiance (bay'ah) to me.' But the first letter he wrote was to Walid. And he said, 'Tell Husayn ibn Ali to pledge allegiance at my hands.' Imam Husayn (a.s.) was called to the court. Imam Husayn (a.s.) said to Janabe Zainab, 'Sister, I have been called to the court.' Janabe Zainab said, 'Brother, no court is held at night. Why have you been called at this late hour?' Imam Husayn (a.s.) said, 'I know why I have been called, and what they are demanding from me, I will never accept it. I will never accept it.' So Janabe Zainab said, 'Brother, I will not let you go to the court alone. Zainab will not let you go alone. Brother Abbas, son Akbar, you take the youths of Bani Hashim and go.' Imam Husayn (a.s.) came, and the Imam sat down. Once, according to Islamic laws, he came before them and recited Istirja. Then listen: Inna Ahl-e-Baytin ma'dinur-risalati wa mukhtaliful-mala'ikah (We are the Ahlulbayt, the mine of messengership and the place of descent of angels). Our status, bina yaftahullahu wa bina yakhtimullah (With us Allah begins and with us Allah ends). Our status, our position, and who is Yazid in comparison to us? Yazid, who is a drunkard, who is a fasiq, who is a fajir—there is no comparison, Walid.' Inna mithli la yubayi'u mithlahu (Someone like me can never pledge allegiance to someone like him). This is my final decision.' Just saying this, Imam Husayn (a.s.) started to leave, when Marwan the cursed called out, 'O Walid, stop him and take the allegiance by force, otherwise you cannot take the allegiance until rivers of blood flow in Medina.' 'Maula, why was your voice raised? Who dared?' Hazrat Abbas placed his hand on the hilt of his sword. As soon as he placed his hand, Husayn placed his hand on Abbas's hand. Brother, this is not the time for war. This is not the battlefield. I will say, 'Oh Maula, you stopped Hazrat Abbas.' These personalities will remain until the last breath. Hazrat Abbas, the oppressed. Alal la'natullahi alal qawmiz-zalimin. Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. chapters.title: The Obligation of Wilayah and Single-Hearted Devotion
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that humans possess only one heart, meaning true love for the Ahlulbayt excludes love for falsehood. Wilayah is presented as a constant, lifelong obligation that remains critical even at the moment of death.

chapters.title: Scholarly Defenses of Wilayah and Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the importance of Allama Majlisi's work and introduces key scholarly texts like 'Misbah al-Hidayah' and 'Abaqat al-Anwar' that provide theological proofs for Wilayah.

chapters.title: Refuting Attacks on the Shia Faith
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical context of 'Tuhfa-e-Ithna Ashariya' and the extensive scholarly responses it generated, specifically focusing on the monumental work 'Abaqat al-Anwar' by Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi.

chapters.title: Addressing Accusations Against the Shia Community
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the scholarly efforts to defend the Shia position against accusations of insulting companions, emphasizing that these responses are based on evidence rather than mere malice.

chapters.title: The Verse of Wilayah and Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the Quranic verse of Wilayah (5:55), identifying Imam Ali (a.s.) as the one who gave Zakat while in Ruku, and discusses the concept of Tawalla.

chapters.title: Prophet Ibrahim's Prayer and the Minority
chapters.summary: The speaker analyzes Prophet Ibrahim's prayer for hearts to incline toward the Ahlulbayt, noting that it applies to a small, grateful minority of believers.

chapters.title: The Ummah's Deviation and the Few
chapters.summary: Reflecting on Dua-e-Nudba, the speaker highlights how the majority of the Ummah abandoned the Ahlulbayt, leaving only a very small number of faithful followers.

chapters.title: The Inseparability of Tawalla and Tabarra
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that true love for the Ahlulbayt (Tawalla) is incomplete without disassociation from their enemies (Tabarra), as one cannot hold love for both simultaneously.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Declaration on Arafah
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates a Hadith from Lady Fatima (s.a.) where the Prophet declares that Allah boasts of the Ahlulbayt and that true salvation lies in loving Ali (a.s.) during his life and after his death.

chapters.title: The Fate of the Enemies of Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the Quranic verse regarding the casting of tyrants into Hell, highlighting the steadfastness of the narrator Sulayman ibn Mehran al-A'mash in his devotion to Wilayah despite pressure.

chapters.title: Historical Context of the New Year
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that the Islamic New Year originally began in Rabi-ul-Awwal during the Prophet's time, and the shift to Muharram was a later historical change that ignores the sanctity of the month of mourning.

chapters.title: Taqiyya and the Status of Jabir al-Jufi
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies the role of Taqiyya in the modern era and introduces the high status of Jabir al-Jufi, who was entrusted with 90,000 secret hadiths by Imam al-Baqir (a.s.).

chapters.title: Faith, Enmity, and the Love of Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explains that true faith requires love for the Ahlulbayt, noting that enmity towards Ali (a.s.) invalidates one's belief regardless of outward declarations.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Yazid and Imam Husayn's Refusal
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical responsibility for Yazid's rise to power and details Imam Husayn's (a.s.) firm refusal to pledge allegiance to a corrupt ruler.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at the Court of Walid
chapters.summary: Imam Husayn (a.s.) confronts the demand for allegiance with the support of his family, asserting his divine status and rejecting the legitimacy of Yazid.

chapters.title: Closing Supplications and Prayers
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes the lecture with prayers for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and petitions for the needs of the believers.
