excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive biographical and spiritual overview of Imam Ali (a.s.) in celebration of his birth on the 13th of Rajab. It explores the miraculous nature of his birth inside the Kaaba, his divine creation from the same light as Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and the exalted status of his parents, Abu Talib and Fatima bint-e-Asad. The session also features the 'Kull-e-Imaan' Grand Quiz, which highlights key historical and theological facts regarding the Ahl al-Bayt. The discourse emphasizes the unique bond between the Prophet and Imam Ali, underscoring his role as the Wasi and the embodiment of faith.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. From Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: I heard Fatimah (a.s.) say: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) entered upon me and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Fatimah.' I replied: 'Peace be upon you.' He said: 'May I come in?' I said: 'Yes, O my father.' He said: 'Is there anyone with you?' I said: 'Yes, O my father.' He said: 'Come under the cloak (al-kisa).' So I entered with him under the cloak. Then his face shone like the full moon... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then it was only a moment when Hasan (a.s.) came and said: 'Peace be upon you...' Hasan (a.s.) came and said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I said: 'Peace be upon you, O the coolness of my eyes and the fruit of my heart.' He said: 'O mother, I smell the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, he is under the cloak.' So Hasan (a.s.) approached and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah, may I enter with you under the cloak?' He said: 'Peace be upon you, O my son and owner of my intercession, you have permission.' So he entered under the cloak... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then it was only a moment when Husayn (a.s.) came and said: 'Peace be upon you, O mother.' I said: 'Peace be upon you, O my son and the coolness of my eyes and my fruit...' [Music] '...I smell the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said: 'Yes, he is under the cloak.' So Husayn (a.s.) approached and said: 'Peace be upon you, O grandfather, peace be upon you, O the one whom Allah has chosen, may I enter with you under the cloak?' He said: 'Peace be upon you, O my son and intercessor of my nation, you have permission.' So he entered under the cloak... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then came the father of Hasan, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). He said: 'Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah.' I said: 'Peace be upon you, O Abu al-Hasan and O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'O Fatimah, indeed I smell the scent of the Messenger of Allah...' ...and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Is that you, O Ali?' I said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Peace be upon you, O my brother, my successor, my caliph, and my companion, you have permission to enter under the cloak.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then I said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, may I enter with you?' He said: 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter, you have permission.' So I entered under the cloak... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then when we were all gathered... ...the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) took the edges of the cloak and said: 'O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt, my special ones, my flesh is their flesh, and my blood is their blood. Whoever hurts them, hurts me, and whoever is hostile to them, is hostile to me. I am at war with those who war against them, and I am at peace with those who are at peace with them. O Allah, bestow Your blessings, Your mercy, Your forgiveness, and Your pleasure upon me and upon them, and purify them from all impurity.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then Allah said: 'O My angels and O dwellers of My heavens, indeed I have not created the heavens, nor the earth, nor the moon that shines, nor the sun that illuminates...' ...nor the earth that is spread, nor the moon that shines, nor the sun that illuminates, nor the sea that flows, nor the ship that sails, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then Jibra'il (Gabriel) asked: 'O my Lord, who are these five under the cloak?' Allah said: 'They are the people of the house of the Prophet and the source of the Message: Fatimah, her father, her husband, and her two sons.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Jibra'il said: 'O my Lord, may I descend to the earth to be the sixth with them?' Allah said: 'Yes, you have permission.' So Jibra'il descended and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, the Most High sends you greetings, honor, and respect, and says: By My Majesty and My Glory...' ...by My Majesty and My Glory, I have not created the heavens, nor the earth, nor the moon that shines, nor the sun that illuminates, nor the sea that flows, nor the ship that sails, except for your love and your devotion. May I enter with you?' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Peace be upon you, O Amin (Jibra'il), yes, you have permission.' So Jibra'il entered under the cloak... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me what is the merit of our gathering...' ...The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'By Him who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me for the Message, this gathering of ours is not mentioned in any assembly of the people of the earth, in which there is a Shia of ours, except that mercy descends upon them, the angels surround them, and they seek forgiveness for them. Ali (a.s.) said: 'By the Lord of the Kaaba, we have succeeded, O Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'O Ali, by Him who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me for the Message, this gathering of ours is not mentioned in any assembly of the people of the earth, in which there is a Shia of ours, except that Allah removes their grief, fulfills their needs, and answers their prayers.' Hajat Ali (a.s.) ila fana wa na wa katu wa dunya wa akhir wa rab ka wa sallallahu ala sayyidina wa nabina Muhammad. Click on this link. You will see all the questions, and you have to provide their answers. You can answer these questions right now if you wish. But there is no prize for answering first. So, let us begin this discussion, ladies and gentlemen. Let us move this program forward, and to support us, we have Mr. Ahsan Jafri Sahab and Tauqeer Devji Sahab with us. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam. Assalamu Rahmatullahi. First of all, we extend our heartfelt congratulations to both of you on the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Many, many congratulations to you too, and heartfelt congratulations to all the viewers as well. Before you begin your discussion, we want to say a few things for the children as well, because along with the youth and the elderly, many children are also connected with us. So, a few basic things first: the Imam who was born on the 13th of Rajab, his name is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). His father's name is Janab-e-Abu Talib ibn Abdul Muttalib (a.s.). His mother is Janab-e-Fatima bint Asad (s.a.). And as you all know, his birth took place on Friday, the 13th of Rajab, 30 Aam al-Fil. Yes, 30 Aam al-Fil, and his martyrdom took place on the 21st of Ramadan, 40 Hijri, in the Mosque of Kufa. May Allah curse the killer of Ali (a.s.) and all those who oppressed the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and those who killed them. And here... And those who killed them. And here, let us also tell the children that cursing the enemies of the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) and invoking Allah's curse upon them is in itself a very great act of worship. The kunya (patronymic) of Ali (a.s.) is Abul Hasan and Abu Turab, and the title attributed to him is Amir al-Mu'minin. Yes, this is the title that is used only and only for Ali (a.s.). In fact, we even find in the hadith that when someone used this title for our sixth Imam, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), the Imam immediately stopped them, corrected them, and said that this title can only be used for our grandfather, Ali (a.s.). So, let us continue this sequence with this, and Tauqeer Bhai, we want you to tell us that as we just mentioned that the birth of Ali (a.s.) took place on the 13th of Rajab, 30 Aam al-Fil. So, we want you to tell us what this 'Aam al-Fil' (Year of the Elephant) is. Thank you, Abul Hasan Bhai. Now, let us clarify to the viewers what this Aam al-Fil is. As you stated, the birth of Mawla Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) took place on the 13th of Rajab, 30 Aam al-Fil. So, Aam al-Fil is the year in which a king named Abrahah came with his army of elephants to attack the House of Kaaba and demolish it. And the Almighty, through His power and His miracle, sent an army of Ababil (birds)... Sent an army of Ababil, the mention of which is also present in the Quran in Surah al-Fil, and those Ababil rained stones and pebbles upon that army of elephants, due to which the army of elephants was destroyed and the House of Kaaba was saved. So, this year is considered the year of Aam al-Fil because the event was very famous, so that year was attributed to the year of Aam al-Fil. title: Har Neki Aur Buraai Ki Jadd | ہر نیکی اور برائی کی جڑ | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the fundamental roots of virtue and vice as taught by Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) in the book Kafi Sharif. The speaker explains that the Ahlulbayt are the origin of all goodness and virtues, while their enemies represent the root of all evil and sin. By understanding these spiritual lineages, believers are encouraged to align their actions with the virtues of the Ahlulbayt and distance themselves from the vices associated with their enemies.
content:
Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu alaika ya Wali al-Asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. If we want to understand the reality of anything, it is necessary to go to its root. And when we reach its root, its cure can also be found. Similarly, there is a root for both virtue and vice. And when we reach the root of virtue and vice, we will understand how to treat it. In this regard, a Hadith is found from our and your sixth Imam, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), in the book Kafi Sharif. The narration is as follows, the Imam says: Qala alayhis-salam: Nahnu aslu kulli khayr (We are the root of all good), wa min furu'ina kullu birr (and from our branches is every virtue). Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the root of every virtue, and all virtues are branches of this root or this tree. Wa min al-birr (And from the virtues), the Imam (a.s.) lists these branches of virtue one by one. Famin al-birri at-tawhid (Among the branches of virtue is Tawhid). Was-salah (And prayer), was-siyam (and fasting), wa kazm al-ghayz (and suppressing anger), wal-afwu anil-musi (and forgiving the sinner), wa rahmatul-faqir (and showing mercy to the poor), wat-ta'ahudul-jar (and being loyal to the neighbor), wal-iqraru bil-fadli li-ahlihi (and acknowledging the merit of those who deserve it). Wa aduwwuna aslu kulli sharr (And our enemies are the root of all evil). Wa min furu'ihim kullu qabihin wa fahishah (And every evil is their branch). Meaning, all evils originate from the enemies of Ahlulbayt. Faminhum al-kizb (And these branches are like this: lying), wal-bukhl (and stinginess), wan-namimah (and backbiting), wal-khati'ah (and severing ties of kinship), wa aklur-riba (and usury), wa aklu malil-yatimi bighayri haqqihi (and consuming the orphan's wealth without right). Meaning, there is an exception here that one who is taking care of an orphan can take as much as is spent on their maintenance. Wa ta'addil-hudud allati amarallahu (And transgressing the limits commanded by Allah), wa rukubul-fawahish ma zahara minha wa ma batan (and committing indecencies, both apparent and hidden), waz-zina (and adultery), was-sariqah (and theft). Wa kullu ma wafaqa dhalika min al-qabih (And whatever evil aligns with that). Finally, the Imam (a.s.) says: Fakadhaba man za'ama annahu ma'ana (So he is a liar who claims he is with us), wa huwa muta'alliqun bi-furu'i ghayrina (while he is attached to the branches of others). If a person is a perpetrator of these sins and is committing these sins and considers these sins light, then it is as if he is related to the enemies of Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Therefore, this is the reality of sin, this is its root: the enemies of Ahlulbayt (a.s.). When we understand what the reality of sin is, we will automatically like to stay away from sins and incline towards virtues. Because these virtues, all the virtues mentioned here, Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are their root. Haza wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin al-masumin, wa la'natullahi ala a'daihim ajma'in.

It should be subscribed to, as it has been explained through 120 Snapchats. So much so that this is not just a sentence of Hadith, 'Man Kunto Mawla fa Ali-un Mawla', but a verse of the Quran was revealed before its declaration, and along with this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself explained it in other gatherings, in which he stated this, and even after that, a Quranic verse was revealed. That is, it is so clear, and despite being so well-documented in books, it is not there. So much so that 'Man Kunto Mawla fa Ali-un Mawla' is found in books, but where is the declaration that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave there found in books? And the second intention is that when 'Mawla' means friend, then why the attempt to hide this Hadith? So let us now turn to the Quran and conclude our talk, and place this matter before all fair-minded people. We place this matter before fair-minded people: if the meaning is understood, then speak openly. If the meaning is understood, then speak openly. We are with Ali, who are you with? So, with this, we conclude our episode here. First, you will subscribe, and immediately after Islam, our [next segment] will be there. You subscribe, and we will meet with our next episode. Until then, subscribe.

title: Karbala Paidal Kyun Jaana Chaahiye? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance and immense rewards of performing the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) on foot. It highlights traditions from Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the forgiveness of sins and the protection granted to pilgrims by angels. Furthermore, it explains that the physical hardships of the journey serve as a symbolic tribute to the suffering endured by the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) after the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, wa sallallahu alaika ya Waliyyal Asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Assalamu alal Husayn, wa ala Ali ibnil Husayn, wa ala awladil Husayn, wa ala as-habil Husayn. Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) said to Ali ibn Maymun as-Sa'igh, "O Ali! Go for the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and beware, do not abandon it." Ali ibn Maymun asked, "What reward will one get who goes for his Ziyarat?" The Imam (a.s.) replied, "Whoever goes for his Ziyarat on foot, Allah will grant him one virtue for every step, forgive one sin, and increase his rank by one degree. When he reaches for Ziyarat, Allah appoints two angels for him, who record every good word that comes from his tongue, and if any bad word comes from his tongue, they do not write it. Apart from this, those angels do nothing else. When that pilgrim returns, those angels also bid him farewell, saying, 'O Friend of Allah! Your forgiveness has been granted. You have joined the group of Allah, His Messenger, and the Messenger's Ahlulbayt (a.s.). By God! You will never see the fire of Hell with your own eyes, nor will that fire see you or burn you.' Besides this, in the forty-ninth chapter of the book 'Kamiluz Ziyarat', it is also recorded in other Hadiths that when a person takes the first step for this Ziyarat, all his sins are forgiven, and as he completes his journey, he becomes even purer and his virtues increase." Going on foot for Ziyarat is not easy, but it is not impossible either. On this path, pilgrims face hardships, their feet get wounded, but these pilgrims know very well that we are walking on foot, but we are neither tied in ropes, nor shackled in chains, nor riding on camels without saddles. Therefore, without caring for all their hardships, these pilgrims go to Karbala on foot only so that they can, to some extent, feel the calamities and sufferings that Hazrat Sayyid-e-Sajjad (a.s.) and the Sayyidani (ladies of the Prophet's household) endured. Therefore, this journey to Karbala on foot is a sign of paying tribute to Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and being sorrowful in their grief. O Allah! For the sake of the calamities of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), grant us the opportunity to go to Karbala-e-Mualla on foot every year, and grant us the day when the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), takes place and we go for the Ziyarat of Karbala on foot along with him. Amin ya Rabbal Alamin. Allahumma arzuqna haram, haram, haram, haram.

title: EP#10: Imam Ali (a.s.) Darwaaze Par Kyun Nahin Aaye?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical question of why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not initially come to the door when confronted by the oppressors. It explains that Imam Ali (a.s.) had already communicated his position to Qunfudh, clarifying that he was occupied with the divine task of compiling the Quran as instructed by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The talk highlights that the Imam had already provided his justification before the subsequent events at the door of Lady Fatima (s.a.).
content:
This Hadith is an answer to those who ask why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not come to the door himself. First, Qunfudh was sent to Imam Ali (a.s.)'s house, saying, 'Go and tell Ali to answer the Prophet's successor.' Qunfudh came, but returned after a while. Upon returning, he said, 'Ali says that the Prophet did not leave anyone other than me as his successor.' Qunfudh was sent again with the message, 'Go and tell Ali (a.s.) that all people have pledged allegiance, the Muhajireen and the Ansar too, and you are like the common Muslims; what is yours is theirs, and what is not yours is not theirs.' Qunfudh came again but returned and said, 'Ali is saying that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded me and bequeathed to me that when I complete his burial, I should not leave my house until I have compiled the Quran.' This Hadith clarifies that before coming to the Lady's (s.a.) door, the Mawla himself had come to the door and had already explained to the oppressors the reason for not coming out of his house.

title: Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course  (With LIVE Demo) - Session # 2
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive guide to the correct recitation of Surah Al-Hamd, emphasizing the critical importance of Tajweed for the validity of daily prayers. The instructor covers specific articulation points for Arabic letters, the rules of Madd and Tashdeed, and the necessity of maintaining composure during recitation. Through live demonstrations and interactive feedback, students learn to avoid common pronunciation errors that can alter the meaning of the Quranic text.
content:
O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness, there is no god but You, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Lord of Majesty and Honor, and I repent to You. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and allow him to enjoy it for a long time. Blessings, O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. The Strong Rope team welcomes you to this second session, the second episode of the Surah Al-Hamd recitation course, with a Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Viewers, let us inform you that this Surah Al-Hamd recitation course consists of five episodes, which started yesterday. In our program, we have with us the world-renowned Qari, Hujjat al-Islam, honorable Maulana Azadari Abbas Khan Sahab, who yesterday recited the Bismillah in different ways and styles, presented the correct recitation as it truly should be to us and our viewers, and helped us in learning and in our own recitation. And believe me, viewers, as Maulana Sahab highlighted yesterday, many of us who speak Urdu, English, or Gujarati do not recite Surah Al-Hamd correctly. We realized this well in yesterday's episode and learned how the Bismillah should be recited correctly and in what style. Friends, Surah Al-Hamd is such an essential Surah that life cannot go on without it. It is commanded to be recited in every prayer, so we must know the correct pronunciation of this Surah. That is why the Strong Rope team has organized this program, and we have the aforementioned Maulana with us, who has been performing this great task for years, and God willing, he is here to help us as well. Viewers, immediately after Maulana's statement today, whatever he teaches here, God willing, you can recite it before him without hesitation, and if there are any mistakes in it, God willing, Maulana Sahab will correct them. And as Maulana Sahab mentioned in yesterday's program, this is not just a program for children; the elderly and especially the youth should participate as much as possible, and we should not feel shy at all regarding acquiring religious knowledge. Therefore, we request the viewers not to be shy and to recite before Maulana Sahab without hesitation so that he can correct it, God willing. Come, viewers, we will now invite Maulana Sahab to begin his statement today, God willing. Maulana Sahab, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. And peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I hope you are well, Maulana Sahab. Yes, by Allah's grace, favor, and your prayers. I hope you all are also well, God willing. Alhamdulillah, Maulana Sahab. All the viewers are waiting for your statements, so you can begin today's statement, God willing. God willing. Bismillah, Maulana Sahab. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, when the punishment is called upon, and blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, His Beloved, His Prophet, and his pure family, who are the pure ones on earth, and may the eternal and lasting curse be upon their enemies, their oppressors, their killers, their envious ones, those who flee from them, those who doubt their infallibility, and those who usurp their rights, who are among the filth and the impure on earth. My Lord, expand for me my chest, ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Welcome once again to the Mission Surah Al-Hamd or Surah Al-Hamd recitation course. I welcome you and hope that you all, by the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), are in good health and safety. It is a prayer in the Divine court that He keeps you all, especially and generally all the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar living on the face of the earth, safe from every kind of earthly and heavenly calamity, especially from this contagious epidemic. As you know, our mission is to present and explain the correct method of pronunciation and recitation of Surah Al-Hamd to those whose mother tongue is Urdu or any language other than Urdu. For your information, I would like to mention that during my 15-20 year stay in Bombay, many respected senior scholars, prayer leaders, and Friday prayer leaders of our school of thought contacted me, tried, and some small work was done in this regard. For example, one of our brothers said that I want to correct this, you listen, and some work was done, so this process continued occasionally. But some friends called, we talked, I informed them that some of our brothers have started this effort, this work is happening, so they also expressed happiness. So, the point is that today, Alhamdulillah, some of our students who were in our camps 8-10, 12 years ago and are now in Qom, Najaf, or busy with preaching in different places in India are with us in this program, and some are scholars from Bombay who are prayer leaders and Friday prayer leaders. There is no need for more detail; there are wise people, elders, brothers, and sisters, all are present, Masha'Allah. And I am proud that in this blessed month, I have received this small opportunity, and I will be happy if the time we are giving, especially the time you are sitting and taking the trouble, you leave after learning and understanding something. And when you understand that you have learned the correct thing, then pass it on to others. I begin with these two verses of the Persian language, and as I said yesterday, I will not repeat the long conversation from yesterday; today we have to come directly to Surah Al-Hamd, God willing, in 2 minutes. The poet says: 'The ancient sky is the arch of our palace, the ancient sky is the arch of our palace, this pride is from our Quran.' This high and lofty sky is a part of my house, it is not bigger than the height of my house, if you consider the meaning. 'This pride is from our Quran.' Well, the poet says that the pure height of the high sky, the beauty of the sky, the blue sky, is not more than my house. Why? Why does he want to say that? Because the Quran is kept in my house. Because the Quran is in my house. 'The ancient sky is the arch of our palace, this pride is from our Quran.' 'Whoever has no knowledge of the Quran, the plant of his existence has no fruit.' Now, if the Quran is such a high and great book, then the poet said in the next two verses, in two lines, that now whoever is unaware of the Holy Quran, the reality is that his heart, the depth of his heart, the inside of his heart, His inner self, his soul, is not beneficial in any way, it has no effect. It is fruitless and like a tree that has no fruit. So, the summary is that there is nothing greater, higher, or more important than the Quran. There is no doubt that our house is blessed by the existence of the Quran, but the responsibility does not end there. The poet has also said in the next two lines that now we have to seek benefit from the sciences, teachings, light, and blessings of that Quran. If we are not doing this, then our inner self is useless, baseless, and has no benefit. This is the Husseini tradition that we are following, trying to implement. Imam Hussain (peace be upon him) also, as you know, emphasized and requested a Sheikh, a Qari of Medina, to teach my son Ali Akbar Surah Al-Hamd. And when he taught Surah Al-Hamd, he expressed immense happiness and rewarded him with gifts; you all know this. When people asked, 'Maula, you are honoring him so much for teaching just one Surah, you are giving so much,' then he replied, 'What I gave him is something that will end.' And what my son was unaware of, this was 100%, 101% only to tell our society, otherwise who understood the Quran better than the family of the Prophet? What other family has a bond between the Quran and the Ahlul-Bayt? A member of the Ahlul-Bayt themselves could have taught it better, but surely this is a lesson for others that wherever you feel that someone can teach you the Quran, go to them and learn. This is not just in one place, not just here, wherever we feel that someone is teaching the Quran correctly, we should learn correctly. This is the tradition of our Imams; it is the command and emphasis of the Holy Prophet and all the pure Imams (peace be upon them). So he said that my son was unaware of something, he taught him, made him aware of it, and he did me a favor forever. The things I gave him are things that will end, but what he gave to my son will remain forever, and it is a continuous charity (Sawab-e-Jariya). So I hope that those who are sitting in front of me, those who are ready and prepared for this work, will definitely benefit from it, God willing. Look, I would like to point out only two things to you. One is that those who are sitting here should not just listen and forget, but think that I have to learn and benefit. For that, do two things. Number one, try every day, the three-four days that are left, to come here in a state of ablution (Wudu), because the Quran is light and Wudu is also a kind of light, so light upon light. This will happen, and surely, God willing, being in a state of Wudu will be helpful and supportive in learning the Quran and Surah Al-Hamd ourselves. The second thing is that those who are sitting, those who can write, can note down something, in any language, either if their mother tongue is Urdu, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, anything, then write in that, or write in Roman, English, or any language. It is possible that there is something that might be useful for you later on, so definitely note it down, because writing itself is an act of worship, of religious matters, of religious texts, and after writing, those things become etched in the mind. 'Writing is half of knowledge,' this is also a very famous saying in the Arabic language. Anyway, yesterday I spoke to you regarding 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'. Let me repeat it quickly once again, and those who recited before me here, most of them, Masha'Allah, read it correctly, and there were very small things that we can correct by practicing again. The second thing was, I politely request you that in the meantime, no one should speak, and everyone should not recite together. At the end of the program, present your recitation one by one, as happened at the end yesterday. This method is better, otherwise, people are having trouble hearing on YouTube, etc., as many people have mentioned this and reminded us. So I will request you that at the end, God willing, you will present your recitation and recite one by one. We will try to correct the small things in it. And after seeing yesterday's program, some people sent the entire Surah Al-Hamd recorded on my personal number. Anyway, this work is good, the effort is good, we appreciate it, but I request you to see, we have a full course of Surah Al-Hamd here, and yesterday we only learned 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'. So I am requesting politely and respectfully that you walk with us step-by-step. If we have read Bismillah, then you try to focus only on Bismillah and see if our recitation has become as it was told? If there is any shortcoming in it, then practice it and do not move forward yet. As we move forward, God willing, walk along with us. Yes, I apologize. So let us begin with Bismillah. With a Salawat, wherever you are sitting, recite Salawat for Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. We recited Bismillah. I submitted that in our Urdu society, Bismillah is mostly recited as 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim', which is not correct according to the rules of Tajweed. You have recited Bismillah, but in the eyes of the scholars of recitation, Quranic teachers, and those familiar with the Arabic language, there are flaws in it. So we must recite it as 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. And yesterday, I presented several ways to recite Bismillah before you. I will not go into detail today. Today, our effort will be to recite at least the first four verses of Surah Al-Hamd, which are easy. Because the next five, six, seven, three verses are a bit difficult, involving the articulation point (makhraj) of the letter 'Dad', 'Sad', 'Ta', etc., so that will take some time. Therefore, these are easy verses at the beginning, and we will try to complete these four today. We can recite Bismillah in slow motion, in a medium way, and in a fast way. For now, we have to leave these three things. We do not need to learn Tarteel, Tahqiq, and Tahdeer. For now, our only goal is that when we recite Bismillah with Surah Al-Hamd in prayer, or when we recite Bismillah anywhere in our daily tasks, this Bismillah should not be incorrect. At the very least, its pronunciation should be simple but Arabic. For example, like this: 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. And I submitted to you that we will not say 'Bismillah' (with a short 'a'), and the full detail of this passed yesterday. Those who are new today can watch yesterday's episode, otherwise, time will be wasted here with repetition. And after Bismillah, in 'Rahman', we said that we will pronounce the 'Ra' thickly. Yesterday, I submitted to your service that whenever there is a Fatha (zabar) or Damma (pesh) on 'Ra', or if 'Ra' is Sakin and the letter before it has a Fatha or Damma, or if 'Ra' is Sakin and the letter before it is also Sakin, and the letter before that has a Fatha or Damma, we pronounce it thickly. I will give an example of the last one, it is a bit difficult. Like 'Qadr', 'Shahr', 'Nahr', 'Fajr'. So here too, we will pronounce 'Ra' thickly. And like 'Usr', 'Yusr', 'Khusr', etc. In all these places, we will pronounce 'Ra' thickly. Do not bring 'Lahn' (melodic embellishment), very good. Do not bring a pleasant, attractive, delightful melody or Lahn. This will be done by those who have time, who have interest, who teach the Quran, who lead prayers, etc. For now, we are talking about those who generally recite Bismillah. Although this statement, this class, this program is also extremely useful for those respected gentlemen who lead prayers or teach the Quran to someone, because the foundation is simple pronunciation. After that, Lahn is introduced. So we will say, 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim', and we will articulate the 'Ha' from the middle of the throat. 'Ar-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. 'Ar-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. We stood in prayer, we recited the Takbir-e-Ehram, after that we can recite it simply like this: 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim'. You know, I repeated this yesterday, I said this, and I am repeating it today that there is a condition of 'Tamaniyat' (composure) in the Surah Al-Hamd and the next Surah that we recite in prayer. That is, you should recite with complete peace and composure. Most wise scholars, those who lead prayers, you will see that they recite Surah Al-Hamd very well. Then, whether you recite the rest of the prayers with a Surah is a different matter. But since this is a part of the Quran, therefore you have to recite it with composure. Bismillah-hir- Rahman-nir-Rahim. Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim. If you go to interpret this Bismillah, to know its meaning, surely a 600-page book is available on it, an 800-page book is also available. A thesis is also available, from 8-10-12 pages to theses, entire books are available. For now, we only need to learn to recite Bismillah correctly. Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim. Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim. Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim. I think that is enough for now, let's move on. 'Sab'a Mathani', meaning the Surah with seven verses. The first verse is, 'Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin'. I explained why we recited Bismillah the way we did. Now, the same word, the same articulation is a bit here too. We will recite 'Alhamdulillahi' as 'Lillahi'. Look, those who are not familiar with the Arabic language, those who are not familiar with Ilm-e-Nahw and Sarf, those who cannot read Arabic text without diacritics (zabar, zer, pesh) correctly, it is obligatory for them to pay attention to these words of mine right now. And especially those who teach the Quran to someone, I am saying this sentence repeatedly, this is not a matter of taking offense, but a matter of understanding and thinking: am I teaching the Quran correctly? Am I fulfilling my responsibility correctly? Is the one I am teaching the Quran learning it correctly? So that later they teach someone else, or even if they don't teach anyone, at least when they recite it themselves, they recite it correctly. Therefore, we should think about this. If we read 'Alhamdu' as 'Alham-do', 'Ha'—I said the sound will come from the middle of the throat, dark, thick, and 'Ha'—the sound will come from the end of the throat. Proper articulation of letters like 'Ha' and 'Ain' from their correct makhraj is essential.
The letter 'Ra' requires a thick, full-mouth sound when accompanied by Fatha or Damma.
Mispronunciations can fundamentally change the meaning of Quranic verses, such as confusing 'worlds' with 'grief'.
Students should prioritize slow, plain recitation over melodic modulation to ensure accuracy.
Applying Tajweed rules like Madd-e-Ariz and Tashdeed is necessary for rhythmic and linguistic precision.
Consistent practice and direct instructor feedback are the most effective ways to improve Quranic recitation.

chapters.title: Introduction to the Surah Al-Hamd Course
chapters.summary: The Strong Rope team introduces the second session of their five-part Surah Al-Hamd recitation course, featuring Maulana Azadari Abbas Khan.

chapters.title: The Importance of Quranic Recitation
chapters.summary: Maulana discusses the necessity of learning correct Quranic pronunciation and shares the historical significance of Imam Hussain's emphasis on teaching Surah Al-Hamd.

chapters.title: Practical Guidelines for Learning
chapters.summary: The instructor advises students to maintain Wudu while learning and to take notes to better retain the knowledge of the Quran.

chapters.title: Methodology and Bismillah Recitation
chapters.summary: The instructor emphasizes a step-by-step learning approach and corrects common errors in the pronunciation of Bismillah.

chapters.title: Tajweed Rules for Bismillah and Al-Hamd
chapters.summary: The lecture covers specific Tajweed rules, including the thick pronunciation of 'Ra' and the importance of maintaining composure (Tamaniyat) during prayer.

chapters.title: Correcting Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin
chapters.summary: The instructor explains the critical importance of proper articulation in 'Alhamdu' to avoid changing the meaning of the verse.

chapters.title: Correct Pronunciation of Alhamdu
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the importance of using correct Arabic pronunciation for 'Alhamdu' and 'Lillahi', specifically focusing on the Damma sound and the articulation of the letter 'Ha'.

chapters.title: Tajweed Rules for 'Ra' and 'Alamin'
chapters.summary: The lecture covers the Tajweed rules for reciting the letter 'Ra' thickly and explains the critical difference in meaning between 'Alamin' (worlds) and 'Alamin' (pain/sorrow).

chapters.title: Reciting Ar-Rahmanir-Rahim
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the correct articulation of the 'Ha' in 'Ar-Rahmanir-Rahim' to ensure the divine meaning of mercy is preserved rather than a literal meaning of applying ointment.

chapters.title: Correct Pronunciation of Rahman and Rahim
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the proper articulation of the letter 'Ha' in 'Ar-Rahman' and 'Ar-Rahim' to ensure accurate recitation.

chapters.title: Rules of Qaida-e-Leen and Madd-e-Ariz
chapters.summary: The lecture covers the soft pronunciation of 'Waw' and 'Ya' (Qaida-e-Leen) and explains the rules for stretching the final letters of verses (Madd-e-Ariz).

chapters.title: Understanding Tashdeed and Recitation
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the linguistic origin and purpose of the 'tashdeed' symbol in Arabic, emphasizing its role in indicating emphatic pronunciation.

chapters.title: Live Recitation and Correction
chapters.summary: Participants recite Surah Al-Hamd while the instructor provides feedback, stressing the importance of slow, deliberate recitation to ensure correct 'makhraj' and pronunciation.

chapters.title: Live Recitation Practice and Feedback
chapters.summary: Participants of various ages practice reciting Surah Al-Hamd while receiving direct feedback from the instructor on pronunciation and pace.

chapters.title: Focusing on Plain Recitation
chapters.summary: The instructor emphasizes reading the Quran plainly without melodic modulation (lahn) to ensure correct pronunciation and delivery.

chapters.title: Encouraging Adult Participation
chapters.summary: The instructor encourages adults to participate in the recitation course rather than just having children perform.

chapters.title: Closing Prayers and Conclusion
chapters.summary: The session concludes with a collective prayer for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi and gratitude to the participants and instructor.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 7 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture addresses common Fiqh questions regarding the month of Ramadan, specifically focusing on the rules for making up missed fasts and the validity of fasting while in a state of Janabah. Maulana Mehdi clarifies the obligation to prioritize Qada fasts over recommended ones and explains the conditions under which a fast remains valid after waking up in an impure state. The session concludes with a warning against spreading unverified religious narrations, emphasizing the importance of verifying sources before sharing information.

We start with the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. We start today's program. We welcome all our viewers with a salaam. First of all, we, on behalf of the Ali Jafri team, wish all our viewers a very happy Ramadan-ul-Mubarak. Continuing with the blessings of Ramadan, let us tell you that in this blessed month of Ramadan, we will present the answers to the questions asked by you through the Ali Jafri channel, via Maulana Mehdi Sahab. Friends, this month is a very blessed month, and it is mentioned in a narration that in the blessed month of Ramadan, after Iftar, Allah (s.w.t.) frees one lakh people from the fire of Hell. So friends, we should keep doing Istighfar every moment in this blessed month of Ramadan so that our sins may be forgiven. In this episode, we will once again go to the Maulana and discuss the answers to these questions. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Please, go ahead, sir. If a person realizes after some time that for some reason, some fasts of the month of Ramadan were missed, and if he cannot remember the number of days, what should he do? Can the missed fasts be replaced by recommended (Mustahab) fasts? And if not, should he not consider all the missed fasts as Qada? Please explain. Wa Alaikum Assalam. The second situation is that I found out that I have Qada fasts on me. Once you know, you have to perform Qada. Now that you know you have Qada, you cannot keep recommended fasts. You cannot keep recommended fasts; you must first perform the Qada of whatever fasts you have missed. You have to keep as many fasts as you are certain you have missed. If you don't know the exact number, keep as many until you are certain that there are no more obligatory fasts on you. That is the third point. Thank you very much for the answer. The second question I have is: if a person keeps a recommended fast as a precaution, in case some obligatory fasts were missed, to make up for them, can he break his fast like other recommended fasts? See, regarding recommended fasts, we have the option that if he has made a Niyyah (intention) for a recommended fast, he can break it before the time of Asr. He can break it before that time. As for the second question, if a person is in doubt whether he has broken his fast or not, he should keep it until the time of Maghrib. In this case, if there is any missed fast, it will be compensated. Therefore, he says that if he knows that the fast has broken, he cannot keep it, and it is possible that... and if you get the fast, it is fine. When will it be? That is the recommended fast. Thank you very much for answering. The next question is: if a person is in a state of Janabah (impurity) after... If a person is in a state of Janabah after waking up, meaning he was awake and his eyes opened in the morning, what should he do in such a situation? If the situation is that the person who fell asleep did so with the intention that 'I will wake up and perform Ghusl,' and he tried, then in this case, his fast is not invalidated, and if morning comes, it is fine. But if he did something like... he was a person who knew he would not wake up, he is a very deep sleeper, and I did not wake up, then if he slept, it means this person who knew this... Such a person should not have slept. It is fine. He is responsible if he is not sure he will wake up. Yes, that is fine. And if he is taking a risk, perhaps he will wake up. There are two situations: one is that he intends to perform Ghusl, and the second is that he is not sure he will wake up, rather he is sure he won't. In both cases, he should perform Qada. If he slept intentionally and it was not his habit, then he should perform Qada. And Qada will be necessary. Yes, that is fine. These are the two situations. And the situation that arises is: the person who slept with the intention of fasting for the coming day, in the night of which the fast of the coming day is... Yes, that is fine. If he is in a state of Janabah after waking up, his fast is valid, and it is obligatory for him to keep that fast, and there is no Qada for it. Is there or not? No, there is not. Thank you very much for talking, sir, and for presenting different aspects before us. Regarding the questions you have, we will address them with you. In response to these questions, we will present something slightly different before you. You cannot feel suspicious about something, and if you investigate and find out whether someone was a Masoom (infallible) or not—in both these cases, we have been guided in our path. He has spoken about this: this is a Masoom's statement, and then his Masoom [status]—this is something you do not know about, you do not know. You do not know about it, you do not know where the phone went, where my knowledge went, have you seen it in a book, or is it a new book nowadays, have you seen it in WhatsApp University? So what will be your responsibility? Someone else's shoulder is below, but if you do not do the work and say something, the Masoom has said that you do not know about it because you do not know what should be done in this. It does not remain like that. If this matter changes, and if you say that I have investigated, and after investigating, if it does not work, then you will say [it is so]. But after typing, if it is found out that no, this is not our Masoom's statement, then you cannot say again that it is Masoom. And if it is found out that this is necessary, then today there are many such things named after Masoom, and they keep circulating in this WhatsApp University. And they keep circulating in this WhatsApp University, and people forward them recklessly. People also narrate them to others recklessly. So you should be careful while forwarding, and when you narrate something, is it necessary? And it is like doing [a good deed]. Thank you, Munasa. You saw that Masoom, in reality, the reason for this is that first, we should investigate. If we are narrating a Masoom's Hadith or sending it to someone on WhatsApp, we should investigate first, and then we should make it public. Just WhatsApp... all those things that we will keep calling our time. The entire team of this Strong Room gives you the answer, and we thank you from the bottom of our hearts. Those people who have not asked us their questions yet can send them to the Strong Room's WhatsApp number [number removed], and Insha'Allah, we will try to answer your questions. We will try to answer your questions. Dear viewers, thank you all. Insha'Allah, we will meet again in the next session. Until then, Allah Hafiz.
Obligatory Qada fasts must be completed before performing any recommended (Mustahab) fasts.
If the exact number of missed fasts is unknown, one should fast until they are certain no obligation remains.
A recommended fast can be broken before the time of Asr if the intention was made.

content:

They say, "Idhan wallahi la ilaha illa huwa nadribu unuqaka" (Then, by God, besides whom there is no god, we will cut off your neck). Meaning, these slogans of 'Nara-e-Takbir' and 'Allahu Akbar' used today to cut the throats of innocent people, perhaps this whole tradition started right here.

title: Taqleed: Ahmiyyat Aur Taqaazey | EP#04 - Maraaje Ke Fatwon Mein Ikhtelaaf Ka Sabab
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common skepticism regarding why Shia Maraje (grand jurists) issue different fatwas despite relying on the same Quran and traditions. The speaker explains that these differences are minor, typically involving quantity or methodology rather than fundamental contradictions of Wajib and Haram. The variations stem from factors like the reliability of narrators, the historical use of Taqiyyah by the Imams, and the practice of narrating traditions by meaning rather than verbatim. Ultimately, the lecture concludes that such differences are natural in any field of expertise and do not invalidate the necessity of Taqlid.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum. Under the title 'The Importance and Requirements of Taqlid', let us discuss another aspect of Taqlid in today's video. In the previous video, we learned how a Faqih (jurist) gives a fatwa, meaning what things they refer to in order to derive a fatwa or ruling. In today's video, we will learn why there is a difference in the fatwas of the Maraje-e-Kiram (grand jurists). Despite so many points in support of Taqlid, there are some people who do not believe in Taqlid and raise doubts against it. One such question raised about Taqlid is: why is there a difference in the fatwas of the Fuqaha (jurists) and Maraje? When Allah is one, His Messenger is one, the religion is one, the Sharia is one, and the Quran is one, then how is it possible that when a Faqih or Mujtahid, based on the same Quranic verses... When a Faqih or Mujtahid, based on the same Quranic verses and the same traditions, investigates and gives their fatwa, how is it possible that many times the fatwa of one Marja differs from the fatwa of another Marja? Let us shed light on this question today and try to understand why there are differences in the fatwas of the Ulema, and whether, based on these differences, the concept of Taqlid becomes refutable or can be rejected. That is, just because the fatwa of one Marja is different from the fatwa of another, can Taqlid be rejected? Can the concept of Taqlid be rejected? There are many answers to this question. The very first answer is that infallibility (Ismah) is limited only to the fourteen Masoomeen (a.s.), and these are the Masoomeen (a.s.) among whom no difference is found. That is why the famous and well-known tradition of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is: 'Awwaluna Muhammad, Awsatuna Muhammad, Akhiruna Muhammad, wa Kulluna Muhammad' (Our first is Muhammad, our middle is Muhammad, our last is Muhammad, and all of us are Muhammad). That is, there are no differences among the Masoomeen (a.s.). Now, let us move forward and talk about the second point. Yes, there are differences in these fatwas... Moving forward to the second point: Yes, there are differences in these fatwas, but there are not many major differences. And the differences that do exist are not about issues of Wajib (obligatory) and Haram (forbidden). That is, there is no difference regarding Wajib and Haram. For example, it is not the case that one Marja has declared an act Wajib and another Marja has declared the same act Haram. Let us try to understand this with an example. In prayer, reciting Tasbihat-e-Arba in the third and fourth Rak'at: one Faqih's fatwa is that reciting Tasbihat-e-Arba only once in the third and fourth Rak'at is sufficient, whereas according to another Marja, for example, Ayatullah al-Uzma Sayyid Ali al-Husayni al-Sistani (may Allah prolong his life), the repetition of Tasbihat-e-Arba should be three times. But the Marja who said to recite it once, or said that it should be recited once or that reciting it once is sufficient, has not forbidden reciting it three times; it has not been declared Haram. There is a difference here, but it is a minor difference, and it is not a matter of Wajib and Haram. And it is not a matter of Wajib and Haram either; it is only a matter of quantity. Now let us see what the reason for these minor differences is. Why is it that according to one Marja, something—if we take the example of Tasbihat-e-Arba—is sufficient to recite once, and according to another Marja, it should be recited three times? What is the reason for these minor differences? Why does one Marja issue one fatwa and another issues a slightly different one? As we learned in the previous video, one source of Ijtihad is the traditions of Muhammad and Aali Muhammad (a.s.). These traditions are narrated in different ways, and this Marja has not heard these traditions directly from the Imam. These traditions reached them through a chain of narrators. It is possible that all the narrators of a tradition are reliable according to one Faqih or Mujtahid, and according to another Faqih, due to some reasons, one or two of those narrators are not reliable. Therefore, the fatwa resulting from that tradition will be different for that Faqih, and according to the other Faqih... The fatwa will be different, and according to the other Faqih, the fatwa will be something else according to someone else. The second reason why there is sometimes a difference in traditions and consequently in fatwas is that our Imams (a.s.) used to practice Taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation). That is, they practiced it because the oppressive rulers and kings were always against them, and even spies were sent into their homes. What was the job of these spies? The job of these spies was to keep an eye on the Imam, to watch the activities happening in their house, and to report the news of those things to the king, based on which the king would increase the oppression on them. Those who loved the Imam were also kept under surveillance after listening to the Imam's words, and they were also oppressed. The Imam knew these spies very well and was aware of them, but those who sat in the Imam's gathering and loved him did not know about these spies. Therefore, if someone in a gathering asked a question unknowingly that the answer to... If someone asked a question in a gathering whose answer was not appropriate to give fully in the presence of spies, the Imam would use Taqiyyah. Now, the Imam stated his point, but those who did not know about the Imam's method of Taqiyyah would take that statement as it was and later narrate it in the same way. Secondly, in that era, due to distance, re-verifying or confirming something was also a difficult task. Therefore, differences in fatwas are found based on these Hadiths—that is, there was a difference in the Hadith because the meaning of what the Imam said was something else, that person understood something else, and he went and narrated the matter further in that same way. The fourth reason is that many times the narrator would not narrate a Hadith verbatim; they would only state the meaning, and there is no harm in this, and the Imams (a.s.) themselves gave permission for this. In the science of Hadith, this is called 'Naql bil-Ma'na' (narration by meaning). Let us understand this with an example. A famous and well-known companion of Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) is Muhammad ibn Muslim. You come to the service of the Imam and submit that I [want to hear] your Hadith. and submitted that I listen to your hadith but I make some omissions or additions to them, so the Imam said, 'In kunta turidul ma'ani fala ba's' (If you intend to convey the meaning, then there is no harm). This hadith is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 511, hadith number two. A second example: Dawud ibn Farqad submitted to Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that I listen to your words and wish to convey them to people just as they are, but it is not possible, so what should I do? The Imam asked him, 'Do you do this intentionally?' He said, 'No.' The Imam asked again, 'Do you intend to convey the meaning?' He said, 'Yes.' So the Imam replied, 'Then there is no harm.' This hadith is also in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 51, hadith number three. Now, if two different narrators narrate one hadith and choose words according to their own style, then this choice of words and the difference between them can later become a cause for difference in fatwas. This was about the issue of Taqlid in religion regarding the fatwas of the Mujtahids. regarding the issue of Taqlid in religion and the difference in the fatwas of the Mujtahids, but it is not that this difference is found only in religious matters or in the context of Taqlid. Differences are found in every field of the world. We see differences among experts in every field. For example, it is found among the greatest of doctors. One doctor gives one medicine, another gives another. One doctor says to take two doses, another doctor will say to take three doses. One prescribes a tablet and says to take the tablet, another talks about giving an injection. But this does not mean that because of these differences, we should stop going to the doctor. Similarly, there are some differences in fatwas in Taqlid, but this does not mean that Taqlid has become meaningless and has no benefit. Therefore, we have seen the reasons why differences in fatwas occur. These differences are minor, and reason dictates that despite these differences, for an ordinary person, an ordinary Shia, Taqlid is a better option than unity and precaution, and Taqlid cannot be rejected due to small differences, and finally... Taqlid cannot be rejected, and finally, the best solution to these differences is the glorious reappearance of our master and Mawla, Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajah al-sharif), after which the scholars, jurists, and the general public will all be in agreement on a single platform. Walhamdulillah Rabbil Alamin. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah.

Only the fourteen Masoomeen are infallible and free from any differences in their teachings.

Taqlid remains the most logical and safe path for the average believer despite minor juristic differences.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#07 - Bait E Tatheer Par Hamla - Shia Kitabon Mein
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical evidence within Shia literature regarding the attack on the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). The speaker systematically references authoritative texts such as 'Amali' by Sheikh Saduq, 'Dala'il al-Imamah', and 'Bihar al-Anwar' to validate accounts of her suffering and martyrdom. By highlighting the testimonies of the Imams, the lecture emphasizes the theological and historical significance of this event in Shia tradition. It concludes by urging listeners to acknowledge these recorded facts rather than dismissing them for the sake of social convenience.
content:
Do it, Ajay, do it. [Music] Got the opportunity, Sameer, Lalit, minute, A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'ala... [Arabic phrase]. Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. In this series of answers to the objections raised against the house of Tahir (the household of the Prophet), we have seen so far that the burning of the door of the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the attack on her house—these painful realities are proven from the books of the opponents. And along with this, the oldest book of the Shia, the book 'Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali', also contains this incident. Yet, the accusation is leveled against the Shia that apart from 'Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali', this incident is not mentioned in any other Shia book or any other Shia hadith. So, to answer this objection, we have with us our brother Asad Bhai. Assalamu alaikum. Wa alaikum assalam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. As you have heard the question, people say that... As you have heard the question, people say that in Shia books, there is only one book that mentions this incident. Apart from this, there are no other such narrations or books where this incident is mentioned. So, can you tell us if there are other such books? Yes, Insha'Allah. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'ala... [Arabic phrase]. Before answering, brother, I want to place a heartfelt concern before you and all the viewers. And that is, if such an objection is raised only by the opponents of the Ahlulbayt, it is not a matter of surprise for us. But the regret is that some of our own, for the sake of courtesy towards the opponents, raise this objection and try to prove this incident on many fronts, and make a failed and absurd attempt to deny the oppression of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). I do not understand, have these people forgotten that after death, they have to face the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? They have to face the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and answer on the Day of Judgment. How can these people deny the oppression of Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.), without whose pleasure no human can enter Paradise? Anyway, as far as the question of proving this incident from other Shia books and authentic hadiths besides 'Sulaym ibn Qays' is concerned, I want to present some hadiths from the books of some Shia scholars and authentic narrators before the viewers. The list is long, and I will only point to a few narrations. There are many, many authentic hadiths where this incident has been mentioned or alluded to, but there is not enough space in the program to present all the narrations before you. Among them, we will try to present a few hadiths before you, Insha'Allah. First of all, in the book 'Amali' by the Rais al-Muhaddithin Sheikh Saduq (r.a.). In the 'Amali' of Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), there is a mention of this incident in two places, and both hadiths are narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in which the Prophet is mentioning those oppressions... The Prophet is mentioning those oppressions that will be brought upon the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) after the Prophet. In this book, 'Amali' by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), on page 113 and 114, in hadith number 3, the Prophet says—and this hadith, in this hadith, the Prophet is informing about what calamities will befall the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) after him. When he mentions his daughter, in that context, he says: 'Wa amma binti Fatima Zahra'—as for my daughter Fatima, 'innaha sayyidatu nisa'il 'alamin'—she is the leader of all women from the beginning to the end of the world. Janabe Fatima (s.a.) is my piece, she is the light of my eyes, the coolness of my heart, and my soul is my daughter Fatima. And then the Prophet further says that when she used to come to the prayer mat, when she used to come to her mihrab of worship, a light would emanate from her face such that the inhabitants of the heavens would see this light shining just as the inhabitants of the earth see the stars shining in the sky. And the Lord of the Worlds would boast before His angels about this worship of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), saying: 'O My angels, do you see how My servant is worshipping Me without...' How My servant is worshipping Me without... In this way, the Lord of the Worlds boasts before the angels. Seeing the worship of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), Allah says to the angels: '...I will keep the followers of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) safe from the fire of Hell.' And then the Prophet says: 'I am seeing in the world, I am seeing what oppressions will be brought upon my daughter after me.' And then the Prophet says: 'Wa ka'anni biha...'—I am seeing, I am seeing that humiliation is entering her house. This is the Prophet's verdict about those people who attacked the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). In the Prophet's view, all those people are 'tughat' (tyrants). '...wa intuhikat hurmatuha'—and her sanctity is being violated. The sanctity of Fatima (s.a.) is being violated. Her right is being usurped. I am seeing with my own eyes, 'wa hiya tudrab'—she is being beaten. 'Wa yuksaru 'admuha'—her ribs are being broken. I am seeing this with my own eyes. 'Wa yusqatu janinaha'—and her child is being martyred in her womb. This... Her child is being martyred in her womb. Seeing all this with my own eyes, this is what the Prophet is saying. Similarly, on page 134, in hadith number 2, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is seen weeping. The angels asked the Prophet, 'What is the cause of your weeping?' The Prophet says: 'The cause of my weeping is that I am seeing what is going to be done to my Ahlulbayt after me.' Remembering all those incidents, keeping those incidents in view, I am weeping. This hadith is present in 'Amali' by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.). Apart from this, I present another book, the name of the book is 'Dala'il al-Imamah'. Its author is Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari. But this is not the same Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari (the Sunni historian), although his name is exactly the same. By coincidence, the names are exactly the same, Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, but this is a Shia author, that is why 'al-Tabari' is written after his name to distinguish him. So, he has mentioned this incident in three places in his book 'Dala'il al-Imamah' and alluded to it. Among them, on page 134 and 135, in hadith number 43, you have alluded to this incident. First of all, regarding the chain of narration (sanad) of this hadith, which is hadith number 43, I want to talk about the chain... I want to talk about the chain of narration. As far as the chain is concerned, in this hadith of 'Dala'il al-Imamah', all the narrators mentioned are considered reliable and trustworthy according to the standards of Ayatollah Sayyid Abul-Qasim al-Khoei (r.a.) in his 'Rijal' and his methodology. And not only him, but scholars like Sheikh Tusi (r.a.) and others have also called these narrators reliable in their books. In this book, this hadith number 43 of 'Dala'il al-Imamah', the reference I have presented before you, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) is narrating the cause that led to the martyrdom of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). He says that the cause of her martyrdom was that he (the attacker) kicked her with his foot. Because of that attack, the martyrdom of Mohsin (a.s.) occurred. Because of that attack, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) became bedridden, which became the cause of her martyrdom. And further, he says: 'Wa lam takun ahadun minhum...'—that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) did not give permission to any of those who had oppressed her to visit her. She did not tolerate meeting any of them. And further, he says: 'Wa kana...'—and two people from the companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came to her with a recommendation, asking her to forgive them and be pleased with them. When they placed their recommendation before Janabe Zahra (s.a.), she said: 'Send them inside.' When those people were brought inside, Janabe Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) said to those two: 'Ma sami'tuma min an-Nabi (s.a.w.a.)?'—'Have you not heard the hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)?' He says, 'Did you not hear him saying: Fatima is a piece of me; whoever hurts her, hurts me; and whoever hurts me, hurts Allah?' Whoever hurts me, hurts Allah. Both of them admitted, 'Yes, we have heard it.' Then Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the Siddiqa Tahira, the daughter of the Messenger, the leader of the women of the worlds, said, 'I swear by Allah, you both have hurt me.' And after that, Imam (a.s.) says, 'And after that, they left from there.' And Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) remained angry with them until her last breath, and did not even reply to their greetings. And she swore by Allah that they had hurt her. And as you remember, Roshan Bhai, when I mentioned in the previous program that this is not just from one source. I have only presented two hadiths before you. Apart from this, there are many such books, for example, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) and others, they have mentioned it in their famous books... In the meantime, they both made a covenant with Allah, saying, 'Yes, we have heard.' Then, Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), the Siddiqa Tahira, the daughter of the Messenger and the leader of the women of the worlds, swore by Allah and said, 'I swear by Allah that you both have caused me grief, and after that, I will not speak to you.' She states that after that, they both left, and Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) remained displeased with them until her final moments. Even reading this verse is enough; let alone anything else, any person with even a shred of humanity left in their heart would feel sympathy for Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). It is narrated that Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was so displeased with those two individuals that she did not even return their greetings. They themselves swore by Allah, admitting that you both—yes, you both—are responsible. And if you recall, brother Roshan, when I mentioned this previously, I stated that this is not just from one source. I have presented two narrations before you, but apart from these, there are many other books, for example, the book by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), his famous book... Al-Majlisi, in his famous book which is considered highly authoritative in our tradition, 'Bihar al-Anwar', in volume 458 to 459, hadith number 3, writes that when the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) buried Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) in the darkness of the night and erased the marks of her grave, he turned towards the grave of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and addressed him. My Mawla said—and this is a plea, rather a complaint—he said to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), 'O Messenger of Allah, your daughter will soon tell you how the Ummah conspired and united against her.' After this, he is providing references. I am presenting one reference. Ibn Shahr Ashub, in his book 'Manaqib', volume 2, page 185, according to that tradition, writes that then they attacked her—that tyrant attacked her—in such a way that my tongue hesitates to describe it. He uses the word 'attacked' in a way that her ribs were injured. If a person's ribs are injured, blood begins to drip, and after that... And after that, Sheikh Abbas Qumi has mentioned in his book 'Al-Misbah' that great supplication in which the Mawla of the Universe expressed his pain, which we know as 'Dua-e-Joshan-e-Kabir'. This is also mentioned by Sheikh Tabarsi (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Ihtijaj', volume 1, page 278, where he depicts the grief of Imam Hasan (a.s.), how Imam Hasan (a.s.) in his grief said to Mu'awiyah, 'O you who fought against Fatima bint Rasulillah (s.a.w.a.), the one who struck her until blood flowed, and the child she was carrying was martyred.' Now, after this, in the famous book 'Bihar al-Anwar', he has pointed towards this incident in two places. On page 336, hadith number 2, and on page 332, hadith number 11. This hadith number 11 on page 332 narrates the event of Mi'raj from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) went for Mi'raj, at that time Allah (s.w.t.) told the Prophet about the oppressions that would be committed against his household. He told him what calamities would befall his household. Regarding Hazrat Zahra (s.a.), God Almighty says, 'As for your daughter, she will be oppressed, she will be deprived of her rights, and that which you have given her will be snatched away from her. And after that, she will be attacked while she is pregnant, and her ribs will be broken.' It is mentioned that they will enter your daughter's house without permission and attack the house. The word 'bila idhn' (without permission) is used. Sheikh Abbas Qumi (r.a.), in his book 'Bayt al-Ahzan', mentions the Ziyarat of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) in volume 3, page 166. He records the Ziyarat of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and in that Ziyarat, Janabe Zahra is remembered with these words: 'Al-Mazlumah, al-Maghsubah haqqaha, al-Mamnua'ah irthaha' (The oppressed one, whose right was usurped, who was deprived of her inheritance), 'Al-Maksurah dil'uha' (The one whose ribs were broken). This is the Ziyarat of Janabe Zahra. Then, after that, 'Al-Bidayah' is a book in which this incident is pointed out in three places: page 179, page 404, and page 418. On page 418, there is a famous hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in which he says, 'There is no day of calamity greater for us than the day of Karbala, except the day of the passing of the Prophet, and the day when the door of the house of Ali, Fatima, Hasan, Husain, Zainab, Umm Kulthum (a.s.), and Fizza was burned, and the martyrdom of Hazrat Mohsin (a.s.) occurred, because that was the day the foundation of the oppression of Karbala was laid.' This is the famous hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). And finally, Allama Majlisi (r.a.) in 'Bihar al-Anwar' has mentioned this incident in at least five places: Volume 28, page 308; Volume 43, page 233; Volume 95, page 354; and Volume 98, page 445. In one of these, from 'Bihar al-Anwar', Volume 43, page 477, the hadith is narrated from Imam Kazim (a.s.) that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Know that Fatima is my door, her house is my house. Whoever violates the sanctity of that house has violated the sanctity of Allah.' Then he says, 'Ibn Sadiq says that when Imam Kazim (a.s.) began to mention this, he started weeping.' Imam Kazim (a.s.) wept so much that his speech was interrupted. He said, 'By Allah, by Allah, by Allah,' three times, Imam Kazim (a.s.) said, 'By Allah, the sanctity of Allah has been violated.' He was remembering his mother, remembering his grandmother, and weeping. He said this. From these sources, it is proven that oppression was committed against Fatima Zahra (s.a.) and her house was attacked. No one can deny this. Now, every person has to make a decision for themselves. Every person has to decide for themselves who they want to be resurrected with on the Day of Judgment: with the truthful Fatima Zahra (s.a.) or with those who oppressed the Princess. Thank you very much for proving through so many sources that this incident, this painful incident, occurred—which we can call a major terrorist attack that happened at the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). Looking at these references, it is understood that this is not only present in the books of our scholars, but also in other books, and other scholars like Allama Majlisi, who were born in the era of the Imams (a.s.)—these great scholars have narrated this incident and conveyed this painful event to the people. Even if we spend our whole lives weeping morning and evening remembering the oppression on Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the right will not be fulfilled. We pray that the Almighty hastens the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), who will take revenge from the killers of Fatima Zahra (s.a.). Viewers, with this, our program ends. We will be back with... With this, our program ends. We will be back with a new objection and its answer. If you have any such objection, you can send it to our social media center. Insha'Allah, the answers will be provided there as well. Alhamdullilah-i-Rabbil-Alameen.

title: Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.) Se Ailaan-e-Jung | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the profound responsibility of respecting the Ahlulbayt as commanded by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in the Hadith-e-Thaqalayn. He emphasizes that true love and obedience to the Ahlulbayt are incompatible with celebrating joyous occasions like weddings or Eids on the day of Ashura. The lecture warns that such actions constitute a declaration of war against the Prophet himself, urging believers to reflect on their conduct in relation to the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
Maulvi Muhammad Mubin, in his book 'Wasilat-un-Najat', after narrating the Hadith-e-Thaqalayn, writes in its commentary that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said three times: "Udhaakkirukumullaha fi ahli bayti" (I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt). To remember Allah, how do you treat my Ahlulbayt? So he says that your intention was to fear God and observe the rights of Ahlulbayt and wear the garment of their obedience and love. Meaning, obey them and love them. How is obedience done? How is love done? Should we celebrate Eid on the day of Ashura? Should we celebrate weddings on the day of Ashura? Is this love for Ahlulbayt? This is not just love for Ahlulbayt, but a declaration of war against Ahlulbayt, and a declaration of war against Ahlulbayt means a declaration of war against the Messenger of Allah.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) emphasized the rights of the Ahlulbayt three times in the Hadith-e-Thaqalayn.
