title: Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer Ka Azeem Sawaab | Me'raaj-e-Ma'refat
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance and immense rewards associated with the recitation of Dua-e-Jawshan-e-Kabir. It details how this sacred prayer serves as a source of divine protection, healing, and intercession for both the living and the deceased. The session highlights the legacy of the Imams in preserving this prayer and explains its role in securing mercy, forgiveness, and a direct connection with the Divine.
content:
The great supplications that have been revealed in this blessed month, which are recited, one of those great supplications is 'Dua-e-Joshan-e-Kabir'. The Prophet asks, 'O my brother Jibra'il, what is the reward for reciting this supplication?' The Prophet asked, 'O Jibra'il, what is the reward for reciting this supplication?' Now, let me mention one thing here: if we were to describe the complete reward of this supplication as it exists in the books, it would perhaps take as much time as it takes to recite the supplication itself. Such is its great reward. But we will try briefly to mention a few rewards before you. First of all, regarding the reward for reciting this supplication, Jibra'il says, 'O Prophet of Allah, the reward is known to none but Allah.' The first reward of this supplication is that no one knows its reward except Allah. Because every person who recites this supplication before leaving their house, whether they leave during the day or at night, they meet Allah in such a state that they have all good deeds... They meet Allah in such a state that they have all good deeds. They will appear in the presence of Allah with all the rewards of the Torah, the Injeel, the Zabur, the Furqan (Quran), and the scrolls of Ibrahim. All the rewards that are in these heavenly books, they will meet Allah with all those rewards. This is the first reward. Then after this, the Prophet asks, 'Will this entire reward be given to the person who recites this supplication?' Jibra'il says, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you as a Prophet and Messenger, Allah (s.w.t.) will give the reward of Ibrahim Khalil, not only the reward of reading these books, but the reward of Ibrahim (a.s.), Musa Kalim (a.s.), Isa (a.s.), and Muhammad Habib (s.a.w.a.).' Allahu Akbar! All the rewards of the Ulul-Azm Prophets, Allah will give to the one who recites this supplication. Then the Prophet asks, 'Will all this reward be for the one who recites this supplication?' Jibra'il says, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, everyone who recites...' O Messenger of Allah, every person who recites this supplication, carries it, bears it, or tries to reach the high status contained within it, the reward for them is far greater than what I have presented to you. It is far greater because where did the matter begin? It began with the fact that no one knows the true reward, the reward of Allah. Then, Gabriel says, 'I swear by the Being who sent you as a Prophet with the truth, beyond the West of this world, there is a land called 'Arz-e-Bayza' (the White Land). There are creatures of Allah there who worship Him and never disobey Him. They weep so much—the creatures weep so much—that their flesh and their faces become dry. Allah reveals a revelation to them and asks them, 'Why are you weeping when you have not committed any sin?' Despite that, you are weeping. Then, those creatures reply in the presence of Allah, saying... 'We only fear that Allah might subject us to His punishment,' and thinking of this, we weep. Allah has created such creatures outside of this world. Then, the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) says, 'O Messenger of Allah,' as if he were completing the description of the reward, 'Is Iblis not there?' Because the Prophet said they do not commit sins, and those creatures never commit sins. So, he asked, 'Is Iblis not there? Is there no one from the children of Adam, from the humans?' Then, 'I swear by the Being who sent me as a Prophet with the truth, those creatures do not even know that Allah created Adam, nor do they know that Iblis was created. They know nothing about this. Their number is known to none but Allah. A day there is equal to 40 days of this world. This is a realm where they neither eat nor drink; they are such creatures who only and solely worship Allah.' They worship Allah and never disobey Him. It is in the traditions that Allah will grant the one who recites the Jawshan Kabir a reward equal to the number of those creatures and equal to their worship. It is a strange and wonderful reward. Then the Prophet says, 'You will receive all this reward.' Gabriel says, 'I swear by the Being who sent you as a Prophet with the truth, Allah has built a house on the fourth heaven called Bayt al-Ma'mur. And that Bayt al-Ma'mur—if I were to stop here and just talk about Bayt al-Ma'mur—is actually, in traditions, directly perpendicular to the Kaaba, right above the Kaaba on the fourth heaven. It is the source or the means for the descent of all blessings. That Bayt al-Ma'mur is the means for the acceptance of prayers. Allah created that house on the fourth heaven, and 70,000 angels enter it daily and come out. These 70,000 angels get the opportunity only once in their lifetime to visit that Bayt al-Ma'mur, go there, and perform its Tawaf until the Day of Judgment. Then after that... ...perform its Tawaf until the Day of Judgment. Then after that, those 70,000 angels will never go again. This happens daily; it is a daily routine that new 70,000 angels come to that Bayt al-Ma'mur. Allah will grant the one who recites this Jawshan Kabir a reward equal to all those angels. And not only that, but equal to the number of all believing men and women, from the Jinn and humans, from the time Allah created humans and Jinn until the Trumpet is blown, until the Day of Judgment—Allah will grant the one who recites this prayer a reward equal to all of them. And then Gabriel says, 'I swear by the Being who sent you as a Prophet, if anyone writes this prayer on a clean plate, a clean vessel, using rainwater and saffron, and then washes it and drinks that water in whatever way is possible for a human to drink it...' ...if that person drinks that water, Allah will grant him relief from all the diseases in his body. He will grant him healing from all illnesses, all calamities, and all ailments. Just by writing this prayer on water and drinking it. Then the Prophet says, 'O Gabriel, my brother, is all this reward for the one who recites this prayer?' Gabriel says, 'Yes. I swear by the Being who sent you as a Prophet with the truth, every person who recites this prayer will die the death of a martyr. He will die a martyr.' The Prophet asks, 'Are these martyrs of the sea or martyrs of the land?' Gabriel says, 'He will be granted the reward of 700,000 martyrs of the land.' 700,000 martyrs! Then the Messenger asks, 'O Gabriel, my brother, will he receive all this reward?' Gabriel says, 'Yes, on the night the person recites this prayer, Allah will turn towards him, look at him with a gaze of mercy, and whatever the person prays for in the presence of Allah, Allah will grant it, whether it is a worldly need or for the Hereafter.' ...and whatever the person prays for in the presence of Allah, Allah will grant it, whether it is a worldly need or for the Hereafter. And then the Prophet says, 'O Gabriel, tell me more.' Gabriel says, 'On the night someone recites this prayer, Allah will protect that person from the evil of Satan and the traps that Satan lays for the believers. Allah will keep this servant safe from those traps. He will accept all his deeds and purify his wealth. And in the same way, He will purify the deeds of all believing men and women.' Then the Messenger of Allah says, 'Gabriel, tell me more.' Gabriel says, 'Israfil told me—Israfil, the angel—that Allah the Almighty says: 'I swear by My Honor and Majesty, whoever believes in Me and confirms you, O Messenger of Allah, and believes in this prayer...' ...and believes in this prayer, confirms this prayer, and confirms all the meanings and the rewards contained within it, then Allah says: 'I will grant him a kingdom, I will entrust a government to him.' And after that, look at Allah's generosity; when Allah gives, He gives in this manner. Allah says, 'I will grant him a kingdom, I will give him a government, and I am Allah; my treasures never diminish, and My giving never ends. I can give as long as I wish. Even if I were to give the entire Paradise to one of My servants, there would be no decrease in Paradise, no decrease in My treasures. Whether it is little or much from My treasures, there will be no decrease. No matter how much I give.' Then Allah says, 'O My beloved, I am the One who, when I intend something, I just say to it, 'Be,' and it becomes. If I have intended to grant something to this servant of Mine...' ...I will grant it to that servant according to My Greatness and according to the authority of My Power. O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), if My servant recites this prayer with a sincere intention and true faith, if he recites it 70 times, or recites it in front of those who are afflicted with calamities in the world—whether they are suffering from leprosy, paralysis, or madness—if this prayer is recited 70 times, I will grant them relief from that disease and remove the illness from their body.' Allah grants such strange and wonderful rewards. Then He says, 'Good news, Paradise, and a blessing for the person who believes in Allah and confirms His Prophet through this prayer, and he will receive the reward of this prayer. And woe, woe, woe be upon the one who denies this prayer, opposes it, and does not believe in it.' Then Gabriel says, 'O Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), if a person writes this prayer on a cup—a cup of camphor or musk—and washes it, and sprinkles it on the shroud of a deceased person, Allah will enter 100 lights into his grave and grant that dead person safety from the fear of Munkar and Nakir. Now that person will not fear Munkar and Nakir. Just by that water—because we have a custom that when a dead person is buried, this water is sprinkled around the grave—this is very important. If the water of Jawshan Kabir is sprinkled around the grave, it will become a source of comfort for the deceased in the grave, he will be safe from the fear of Munkar and Nakir, and the punishment of the grave will be removed from him. Allah will send 70,000 such angels to his grave, and with every angel, there will be a tray of light...' ...with every angel, there will be a tray of light. And the angel will come to welcome him, and what will he do? He will praise that person, congratulate him, and take him towards Paradise. And all those angels will say to him, 'Allah the Almighty has commanded us to do this—this welcome we are giving you, this reception—Allah has commanded us.' And they will say, 'We will remain your helpers until the Day of Judgment.' You do not need to worry. This is a strange and wonderful statement. The thing we fear the most is the grave, the 'Fashar-e-Qabr' (the squeezing of the grave). One of the rewards of reciting this prayer is that Allah will expand his grave as far as his eyes can see. His grave will become spacious and wide. And Allah will open the doors of Paradise for him, and he will be awaited in Paradise just as a bride is adorned and awaited. This is for the one who recites this prayer, and Allah... The one who recites this Dua, Allah will say—and this is a strange, strange phrase—Allah Almighty will say to him: 'I feel shy to punish this servant of Mine whose shroud has this Dua written upon it.' This is why we ensure that the Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir is written on our shrouds, as Allah grants him safety from punishment. Allah says, 'I feel shy to descend punishment upon this servant.' And then, another strange and wonderful thing is found regarding this Dua: Allah Almighty wrote this Dua on the pillars of the Arsh 5,000 years before creating the world. Whoever recites this Dua with pure intention and sincerity at the beginning of the month of Ramadan, he receives the reward of Laylat al-Qadr. Allah creates 70,000 angels for that person, and those angels perform the Tasbih and Taqdis (glorification) of Allah, and all that reward is given to the person who recites this Dua. And the matter does not end there; then Allah says, 'O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)...' He says, 'O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), whoever recites this Dua, there will be no veil between him and Allah Almighty.' What does 'no veil' mean? It means that whatever Dua he asks for, Allah will grant it. There will be no veil between this servant and Allah. And this is in this world; in the hereafter, when the field of Qiyamah (Resurrection) is established, when he is brought forth, all the people and all the creatures in that gathering will look at him and say, 'Who is this person surrounded by such glory?' There will be so many servants and angels in front of him and behind him, escorting him. A caller from the presence of the Most Merciful will proclaim, 'O My servant, enter Paradise without any reckoning.' Then, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'O Ali, whoever recites this Dua, the angels get tired of writing his good deeds and erasing his sins.' They get tired of erasing his sins. There is no rest for these angels; they are not permitted to stop writing his good deeds or erasing his sins. They must constantly perform this task. Then, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), 'There is no one in my Ummah who recites this Dua in the month of Ramadan—whether three times or even once—except that Allah makes Hellfire forbidden for his body.' Hell is forbidden for him, and Paradise becomes mandatory for him. Such is his greatness and status in the eyes of Allah. And another reward he receives is that Allah appoints two angels for the one who recites this Dua, who protect him from committing sins and help him so that he does not disobey Allah. They perform the praise and glorification of Allah, protect him from all calamities, and open one of the doors of Paradise for him while closing the doors of Hell for him. They close the doors of Hell for him, and this continues as long as he is alive. And then, when the time of his death arrives, he remains in the protection of Allah. These are all the things that Allah has prepared for him, which have just been described to you. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says to Ali (a.s.), after narrating this entire tradition, Imam Hussain (a.s.) says—because the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) had said this to Imam Hussain (a.s.)—Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'My father advised me to safeguard this Dua, to take special care of its recitation, and to emphasize its teaching.' We must be aware of the importance of this Dua. This is the will of the Master of the Universe (a.s.) for his son, Imam Hussain (a.s.), and not just for him, but for all of us. An important aspect of this Dua is that we should participate in its recitation, in whatever state or manner possible. And finally, the Master (a.s.) advised me, 'My father advised me to write this Dua on his shroud and to teach this Dua to my family and emphasize it to them.' And after that, the mention of Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir—why shouldn't it be mentioned? When Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir has come from the presence of the Almighty, that is why it is Jawshan Kabir. We pray in the presence of the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability to recite this Dua in this blessed month and every year as long as Allah grants us life. And through the blessing and greatness of this Dua, may He hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) and count us among his sincere servants.
The spiritual rewards of reciting Dua-e-Jawshan-e-Kabir are vast and known only to Allah.
Recitation grants the reciter spiritual status comparable to the Ulul-Azm Prophets.
The prayer acts as a powerful shield against Satanic traps and ensures the fulfillment of worldly and spiritual needs.
Using water infused with the text of the prayer serves as a remedy for physical ailments.
Placing the text on a shroud provides the deceased with protection from the fear of Munkar and Nakir.
Reciting the Dua during Ramadan is associated with the blessings of Laylat al-Qadr and protection from Hellfire.
The prayer removes spiritual veils, facilitating a direct and answered connection with Allah.
Imam Ali emphasized the importance of teaching and prioritizing this prayer to Imam Hussain.

title: Mega Winner Announcement | Special Episode | 💐 GHADEER: PEI MEGA QUIZ 2025
excerpt: This special lecture commemorates the significance of Ghadir-e-Khumm and the divine appointment of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib as the successor to the Prophet Muhammad. It explores the theological necessity of Wilayah, the qualifications of an Imam, and the inseparable link between faith and the recognition of the Hujjah. The session concludes by emphasizing the importance of Mawaddat and Tabarra, while announcing the grand prize winner of the 2025 Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz.
content:
The Hadith of Thaqalayn, the greatness of the Lord, the Hadith of the Light of God, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the status of Ali (a.s.)—Ali is the truth, Ali is the sign, Ali is the essence of life. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used every possible word to introduce the Thaqalayn, saying, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things.' He recited the entire Hadith of Thaqalayn, equating it to the Quran, equating it to the truth. 'Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali.' O Lord, turn the truth wherever Ali turns. Ali is with the Quran and the Quran is with Ali. He declared Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) to be the standard of the Quran, such that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) will complain on the Day of Judgment, saying, 'O Lord, this Ummah, this nation, chose to abandon the Quran.' Here, the Quran refers to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Amma ba'd. 'Ya ayyuhar-rasulu balligh ma unzila ilayka mir-rabbik'—this is a very famous and well-known verse in which Allah Almighty addresses the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.), saying: 'O Messenger, convey that which has been revealed to you from your Lord.' Convey it, deliver it. 'Wa illam taf'al fama ballaghta risalatah'—and if you do not do this, then you have not conveyed His message at all. It is as if your entire 23-year mission of Prophethood, all your hard work, efforts, and struggles have not been accomplished at all. 'Wallahu ya'simuka minan-nas'—and Allah will surely protect you from the people. This means that there were some individuals there, some wicked people, some evil people, who, after hearing this message of Wilayah, would have tried to harm or cause damage to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And Allah took the guarantee that you should not worry about them; Allah will protect you. And there is a similar verse revealed regarding the Prophet's mission, 'Fa la'allaka tarikun ba'da ma yuha ilayk'—perhaps you are inclined to leave out some of what has been revealed to you, and your heart is distressed by it. In any case, this was such an important matter that Allah Almighty says that if you did not convey this message, it is as if you did not perform any part of your mission. Often, the question arises in the minds of the youth: why is Wilayah so important? Look, this is a very important question, and its answer must be clearly understood. The Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) passed away, departing from this world in 11 AH. Now, Islam had to remain until the Day of Judgment. And because Islam is not a worldly religion, it is not a worldly creed; it is the Divine Religion. Islam must remain until the Day of Judgment. This message must remain. Therefore, for the protection of this message and this Sharia, there must be a successor to the Messenger of Allah who is like the Messenger of Allah, except for Prophethood. That is why the Prophet said, 'O Ali,' except for Prophethood. That is why the Prophet said, 'O Ali, anta minni bi-manzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di'—O Ali, you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me. That is the only difference. So, this is a very important matter. This must remain until the Day of Judgment. Now, whatever qualities the Prophet possessed, those same qualities must be in the Imam. The first of these is that the Prophet was appointed by Allah. The people did not appoint the Prophet; the Prophet came from Allah. Therefore, the Imam must also be 'Mansus min Allah' (appointed by Allah), meaning his appointment must come from Allah. The appointment by people can always be right or wrong. You know what the state of appointments by people is. Today, the whole world is observing, witnessing, and seeing the state of those appointed by people across the globe. So, discussing that is futile. Therefore, one thing is that the appointment must be from Allah; he must be appointed by Allah. Secondly, he must possess knowledge of the unseen (Ilm al-Ghayb), just as the Prophet did. He must be the possessor of Divine knowledge. Allah must grant it to him, Allah must bestow it upon him, Allah must gift it to him. That is, he must be the possessor of Divine, inspired knowledge. That is what is called an Imam. Meaning, he is the possessor of the knowledge of the unseen from Allah, not by his own essence. The master of the unseen (Ghayb) is not so by his own self, but by Allah. He must possess divine knowledge (Qudrat-e-Wahbi Ilahi). He must be infallible (Ma'sum). It is essential for an Imam to be infallible. If an Imam is a sinner, or God forbid, a transgressor (Fasiq) or wicked (Fajir)—as many Muslims believe that it is not an issue if an Imam is a Fasiq or Fajir, or a drunkard, or a gambler, or a wrongdoer—then that is not an issue. However, in the school of Tashayyu (Shia Islam), in the true religion of Islam, it is absolutely not the case that just anyone can become an Imam. So, let us see why there is such great emphasis on this. Now, look at the first tradition I present to you: without the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Hujjah (Proof of God), and without submitting to the Hujjah of God, no worship will be accepted, no matter how much a person worships. When Allah told Iblis to prostrate to Adam, Iblis refused. Iblis said, 'Forgive me from prostrating to Adam. Do not ask for this. Whatever other task You command me to do, I am ready to perform. I will worship You in a way that no angel brought near (Mala'ik-e-Muqarrab) has ever seen—meaning, no angel has ever done it—and no sent messenger has ever done it. I will worship You like that.' So Allah gave a reply: 'Uridu has...' So Allah gave a reply: 'Uridu wa uhibbu an ud'a min haythu uridu la min haythu turidu' (I want to be worshipped in the way I desire, not in the way you desire). Nothing happens by your desire. Now, look at what Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'By Allah, if Iblis had prostrated to Allah after that disobedience and arrogance—how much would he have prostrated? For the entire age of the world, if he had prostrated continuously, if he had remained in prostration to Allah—'Sajdatan li-ma fi al-ard'—this prostration would have been of no use to him. Think about it; we prostrate a little, our prostration lasts a few seconds. Here, the Imam says that even if he had prostrated for the entire age of the world, it would not have been of any use to him. 'Wala qabila Allah'—and Allah would not have accepted this prostration. Why? 'Ma lam yasjud li-Adam'—because he did not prostrate to Adam. Allah had commanded him to prostrate to Adam. Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam as Allah had commanded him. After that, the Imam says, 'Wa kadhalika hadhihi al-ummatu 'asiya'—and in the same way, this Ummah was also disobedient... And in the same way, this Ummah was also disobedient, which did not obey Allah and did not obey the Messenger. This Ummah, which was tested after the passing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and after abandoning their Imam—which Imam? The one whom their Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had appointed for them by the command of Allah. The Prophet said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa-Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am the Master, Ali is his Master). And it is not that the Prophet was saying this for the first time; it was not just at Ghadir-e-Khumm. If you look at history, you will see that the Prophet repeatedly announced the immediate Caliphate (Khilafat-e-bila-fasl) and immediate Vicegerency (Wisayat-e-bila-fasl) of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). He used every possible term: 'My Wasi, my successor, my Caliph, my brother.' The Prophet used all the words he could. 'Thaqal al-Akbar'—I am leaving among you two weighty things. The entire Hadith al-Thaqalayn was recited, equating them to the Quran, equating them to the Truth. 'Ali ma'al-haqq wa al-haqq ma'a Ali, Allahumma adir al-haqq haythu dara Ali' (Ali is with the Truth and the Truth is with Ali; O Allah, turn the Truth wherever Ali turns). Ali is the Quran... Turn the Truth wherever Ali turns. Ali is the Quran and the Quran is with Ali. The Quran is with Ali. He identified Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as the criterion for the 'abandoned Quran' (Quran-e-Mahjur), regarding which the Prophet will complain on the Day of Judgment: 'O Lord, this Ummah, this nation, fled from the Quran.' So, here, the Quran refers to the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin) (a.s.). From the invitation of Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira until the very last moment of his life—the last moments of the Prophet—'Bring me a pen and ink so that I may write a will for you after which you will never go astray.' The Ummah did not do that either. The Ummah abandoned the Messenger of Allah and the Imam whom Allah and His Messenger had appointed; they did not accept him. What is the problem? The problem is that we do not read. If we read, study the books, and study without bias—without any prejudice—then we will see what is written in the traditions, in the books, in history, and in the Hadith. What is written in the Quran? If we study without bias, without prejudice, we will see that what the Prophet said is exactly the same. The true religion of Tashayyu, which is explaining this, is the same. Anyway, the Imam continues: 'Falan yaqbal Allahu minhum 'amalan'—Allah will not accept any of their deeds. 'Wa la yarfa'u lahum hasanatan'—Allah will not accept any of their good deeds, 'hatta ya'tiyallaha'... Allah will not accept any of their good deeds until they come to Allah through the path that Allah has commanded, and until they accept the Wilayah of the Imam whose Wilayah Allah has commanded to be accepted, and enter through the gate that Allah and His Messenger have commanded. Allah and His Messenger have commanded it. So, it is now obligatory upon the people to follow and obey Allah and His Messenger. But the Ummah did not do so. This is what the Imam is saying. Now, no matter how many deeds the Ummah performs, no matter how much Quran they recite, no matter how much they pray, no matter how much they fast, nothing is acceptable until they go through the Hujjah (Proof) whom Allah has appointed. That Hujjah who is the master of divine sciences, who possesses the knowledge of the unseen (Ilm-e-Ghayb), who says to the people, 'Saluni qabla an tafqiduni' (Ask me before you lose me). The one about whom the Prophet said, 'Ana madinatu al-'ilmi wa Aliyun babuha' (I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate). That is Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Infallibles (Ma'sumin) (a.s.) who came after him. It is obligatory for the Ummah to hold fast to the Masumeen (a.s.) when they come. This is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said—look, the Khutbah of Ghadir is not just a few sentences, but a detailed sermon the Prophet delivered for a long time. Let me present a few sentences from it for you: The Prophet said, 'O people, the Light of Allah (Nur-e-Allah) is firmly rooted in my being, it is flowing. Then, after me, it is in the being of Ali. The Light that Allah created—the Light of existence, the Light of Wilayah—is in the being of Ali. And then, after him, it is in the progeny of Ali, up to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). It is a complete chain, one Imam after another, until it reaches Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), who will take the right of Allah from the people and will ensure that Allah's right is fulfilled.' He will ensure the fulfillment of those promises, covenants, rights, and duties that people owed to Allah, and the rights that belong to us—the Ahlulbayt. The Prophet is saying in the sermon, 'Because Allah has appointed us as the Hujjah (Proof) over the transgressors.' The meaning of Hujjah is that after this, no argument will be accepted. After this, no excuse... will be accepted. No excuse will be accepted. No plea is admissible. 'Hujjatan alal-muqassireen'—against the transgressors, meaning no plea of the transgressors will be accepted. Allah has made it a proof. Who is a 'Muqassir'? One who knows the rights of the Ahlulbayt but does not acknowledge them as they deserve to be acknowledged. He believes, but with 'Taqseer' (shortcoming); he diminishes their rights, diminishes their stature, diminishes their position. That is called a Muqassir. He raises doubts about everything, raises objections, and asks, 'How is this possible? How is that possible?' That is called a Muqassir. And the 'Mu'ideen'—those who hold enmity and hostility towards the Ahlulbayt. And the 'Mukhalifeen'—those who opposed the Ahlulbayt. And the 'Kha'ineen'—those who committed breach of trust, breached the covenant, broke their oaths, broke their promises. And it is a proof over the sinners. And the 'Zalimeen'—those who are oppressors. What does oppression mean? To place anything in an inappropriate place. In other words, those who were not entitled to Imamate, who were not entitled to Caliphate, we placed them on the seat of Caliphate. So, this is called a Zalim. And the 'Ghasibeen'—those who usurp rights. People usurp rights; those who usurp rights, the 'Ghasibeen' of all the worlds—in the entire universe, in the whole world, whoever... the Prophet is saying in the sermon. The Prophet knows that the Ummah will do this. The Prophet knows, that is why the Prophet says, 'O people, look, do not show favor to Allah through your Islam. La tamunnu islamakum. Otherwise, what will happen? Fas-alukum—Allah will be angry with you. If you show favor, do not show favor; do not show obligation, or else punishment will descend upon you from Allah. Inna Rabbaka labil-mirsaad—verily, Allah is keeping a strict watch over you.' 'Mirsaad' is taken from the Quranic verse. Inna Rabbaka labil-mirsaad. Then the Prophet says, 'O people, listen carefully.' It is a sermon; the Prophet gave a sermon at Ghadir. 'O people, after me, there will be some Imams who will invite people towards Hell, and on the Day of Judgment, they will not be helped.' Meaning, these are those individuals, those Imams, who usurped the rights of the Ahlulbayt and instead of the Imams of the Ahlulbayt, they gave themselves the title that we... instead of themselves, they gave themselves the title that we are the successors of the Messenger of Allah. 'Ma'asharan-nas, innallaha wa ana bari'an'—O people, verily Allah and I, both of us dissociate (Tabarra) from them. Because 'Tabarra' is very necessary. When you recite the Kalima of Tawheed, 'La ilaha illallah', the meaning of 'La ilaha illallah' itself is that the Creator of the entire universe is only One, the One who creates is only One, whom we call Allah, and all people are bewildered and wandering in this Essence, in the Essence of Allah. So, therefore, 'La ilaha illallah'. 'Ma'asharan-nas, innallaha wa ana bari'an min ahlil-nar'—O people, those who helped these false Imams, who followed them, who obeyed them, all of them will be in the lowest level of Hell. Whoever followed them, remember, the Prophet said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyyun mawlah.' He whose Mawla I am, this Ali is his Mawla. 'Allahumma wali man walahu, wa adi man adahu, wansur man nasarahu, wakhdhul man khadhalahu.' O Allah, whoever accepts the Wilayah of Ali... O Allah, whoever accepts the Wilayah of Ali, make him your slave, and whoever bears enmity towards Ali, make him your enemy. Whoever helps Ali, supports Ali, help him, and whoever abandons Ali, abandon him. So, whoever abandoned Ali—now you study history. Read history. Read it, definitely. Look, don't listen to us. Don't listen to anyone. You study history yourself. What happened after the martyrdom of the Prophet? Remove the veils of prejudice. The veils of prejudice. Remove the prejudice. Without prejudice, you just study history. The Prophet says, 'Wa sa'a mathwal-mutakabbireen'—verily, the abode of the arrogant is very evil. Here, 'Mutakabbir' means those arrogant individuals who removed Ali and took Ali's place. 'Inna ashabas-sahifah'—know that these are the 'Ashab as-Sahifah' (Companions of the Scroll). Therefore, everyone should look towards their own deeds, towards their own pages. What is the meaning of 'Ashab as-Sahifah'? They are called 'Ashab as-Sahifah'. Those individuals who, during the Prophet's life, sat outside the Kaaba—there were a few individuals, 141 individuals, who were apparently very close to the Prophet. There were 141 individuals who were apparently very close to the Prophet. They gathered and made a pact that after the Prophet, we will not let Ali ibn Abi Talib become the Caliph. And they all gathered and wrote this document, and after writing the document, they signed it and made one man responsible for this document. It was kept with him, and they even gave him the title 'Aminul-Ummah'. This man is the 'Aminul-Ummah'; this document will remain with him. So, these individuals who gathered and did this work are called 'Ashab as-Sahifah'. Therefore, this Wilayah holds great importance, very much so. Because without it, Allah will not accept any deed. He will not accept any worship. Now the question arises, why will He not accept it? Why will He not? Because Allah says the same thing that Allah replied to Iblis: 'Ureed'—I want my worship to be as I want, not as you want. So, if any human thinks that I will worship according to my own way, then Allah will not accept it. For example, if the morning prayer is two Rak'ats, if someone says, 'No, my heart wants to pray four,' will that prayer be accepted? In any school of thought, will it be accepted? If we say the Prophet used to pray like this, but I feel like praying like this, will the prayer be accepted? Any Muslim, of any school, of any sect, will they say it will be accepted? It will not be. Because the Prophet himself... It will not be. Because the Prophet himself said, 'Look, pray as I pray.' It is obligatory upon you to pray exactly as I pray. Therefore, the Sharia will be exactly what the Prophet brought. The religion will be exactly what the Prophet brought. The beliefs will be exactly what the Prophet brought. No one has the right to create any belief on their own. Tawheed on their own, Prophethood on their own, Justice on their own, Imamate on their own. No one has the right. And that is why it is found in the traditions that the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Bina ubidallah wa bina urifallah'—through us, Allah is worshipped, and through us, the recognition of Allah is attained. Through us, the declaration of Allah's Tawheed is made. 'Bina wahhadallah'—if we were not there, Allah would not have been recognized, Allah would not have been worshipped, Allah's Tawheed would not have been correct. Because Allah made them the medium. Allah made them the medium. Allah told them that this is the way; if you want to learn, learn from them. And this is what the Prophet said, 'Madi'—this is the Hadith. The meaning of Hadith itself is that you follow them. And in the Quran, it is written everywhere that you follow the Prophet, obey the Prophet. 'Man yuti'ir-rasula faqad ata'allah'—the Quran says, whoever obeys the Messenger, he has obeyed Allah. Obeying the Prophet is obligatory, following the Prophet is obligatory. Obeying the Prophet is obligatory, following the Prophet is obligatory, listening to the Prophet's words is obligatory, following the Prophet's commands is obligatory. Everything is obligatory. Similarly, following the successor of the Prophet is obligatory, obeying him is obligatory. If a human chooses any other path, moving away from them, then it is nothing but misguidance. Why? Because the Quran says, 'Famaadha ba'dal-haqqi illad-dhalal'—after the truth, there is nothing except misguidance. And what is the truth? Ali ibn Abi Talib. 'Ali ma'al-haqqi wal-haqqi ma'a Ali'—Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali. 'Ali ma'al-Qur'ani wal-Qur'anu ma'a Ali'—Ali is with the Quran and the Quran is with Ali. All Muslims have recorded these Hadiths in their books. You go and study the Hadiths. Therefore, never consider this Wilayah, this love for the Ahlulbayt, as light. Give it great importance. Teach this to your children. Look, it is found in the traditions that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'La tastahinu bi-mawaddatina'—look, do not consider our love as small, do not consider it insignificant. 'Fa innaha minal-baqiyat-us-salihat'—because this love and affection for us is among the 'Baqiyat-us-Salihat' (the enduring good deeds). What are these 'Baqiyat-us-Salihat'? 'Al-Baqiyat-us-Salihat' means that virtue which is always going to remain. This is that virtue which will never end. It remains until the Day of Judgment. This is that virtue, the love of the Ahlulbayt, which will take a human to Paradise. And the Prophet had demanded this very love as his 'Ajr-e-Risalat' (reward for the message). His... demanded as his 'Ajr-e-Risalat', demanded as his wages, and the Quran interpreted it in Surah Ash-Shura, verse number 23: 'Qul la as'alukum 'alayhi ajran illal-mawaddata fil-qurba'—O Prophet, say to them that I do not want anything from you, I do not demand anything as a reward for the message, I only want that you love my Ahlulbayt. That's it. But the meaning of love for the Ahlulbayt is that a human truly loves the Ahlulbayt, follows the Ahlulbayt, and consequently dissociates from their enemies. Just as the Prophet said in the Khutbah of Ghadir, that those who have usurped the rights of the Ahlulbayt, then dissociation (Tabarra) is obligatory. And 'Tabarra' is the identity of the Shias. 'Tabarra' is the identity of the Shias. Otherwise, there are many people who love Ali. There are many people who love the Ahlulbayt. If you look at Western culture, books have been written about Ali Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Many books. Great Western authors have written. This itself is a topic; Insha'Allah, we will discuss it some other time. And all over the world, people—Muslims, non-Shias, non-Muslims, others—have written a lot. But is that the 'Ajr-e-Risalat'? No, it is not. Why? Because the meaning of 'Mawaddat' (love) is that along with their love, there must also be dissociation (Tabarra). There must be 'Tabarra'. The identity of being a Shia... there must be 'Tabarra'. That is the identity of being a Shia. That is why in another Hadith, the Imam says, 'La tazunnu anna ka mufi amrina'—never assume that you are doing too much in our love, in our affair, meaning in Shi'ism. You are taking it to excess; no, this is something for which there is no extremism. There is no extremism. There is no excess in it at all. However little you do, it is less. When the martyrs of Karbala gave their lives, at the very last moment, they asked the Sayyid al-Shuhada (a.s.) this very question: 'Hal wafaytu ya ibn Rasulillah?'—O son of the Messenger, have I fulfilled the right of loyalty? This is a very important thing. And that is why it has been emphasized so much that a human should understand its value and price. It is a very great blessing from Allah. 'Fashkurullah'—do not consider this blessing light. This is a spiritual blessing, a divine blessing, and the greatest blessing. Because existence is given to everyone, but the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt is not given to everyone. True Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, with 'Tabarra', is not given to everyone. Allah gives it only to His chosen, selected servants whom Allah Himself chooses. So, let us all, on this occasion of Ghadir, take this pledge that we will love and have affection for the Ahlulbayt in this way. We will love and seek help from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in the way that is the true right of affection and love. And we will serve them in the way that is the true right of service. And we will take this message of Ghadir to every corner, to those who have not heard it, just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself said: 'baligh ash-shahidu al-ghaib' (let those who are present convey it to those who are absent). It is obligatory upon every father to convey this message to his son, to teach his son this message, because this Wilayah and this affection is a treasure that lies beneath the Divine Throne. That is why the Imam (a.s.) says that the love for us, the Ahlulbayt, is sent down by Allah from the heavens; it is from the treasures beneath the Throne. And Allah sends it down in a measured quantity, and He does not grant this love for the Ahlulbayt to anyone except the best of His creation. So come, let us all make this pledge together. Insha'Allah, that we will serve the Imam of our time, Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), who is the true heir of Ghadir today; we will remember him, and through his intercession and his help, we will attain the message of Ghadir and convey it to the people. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. Assalamu alaika ya amina Allahi fi ardihi wa hujjatahu ala ibadihi. Assalamu alaika ya Amiral Mu'minin, ashhadu annaka jahadta jihadaka wa taba'ta sunnatan-nabiyyi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi hatta da'aka Allah. Until Allah, the Healer and the Sustainer, makes the proof of wealth a proof over all of Allah's creation. So, my soul is empowered by Him, and I pray for a love that is a quality of the Awliya (friends of Allah), a love that is cherished in the heart and society, a witness, a guide, a longing for His joy, and a state of piety. A reward, a listener of the Awliya, a purifier of character, the provision of the world, and for Him, the hearts are obedient, seeking His refuge, finding contentment in Him, returning to Him, and opening the doors to His invitation, seeking His reward, repenting from sins, and weeping in His presence. And whoever seeks [music] and whoever seeks His miracle, and whoever seeks His station, and my protection is in His eternity, seeking forgiveness, and the creation is in His presence, and the glory is His, and we ask Him to accept our prayers, and our faith, and our guardianship, by the right of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Bi-haqqi Muhammadin wa Fatimata wa Hasani wa Husaynin, innaka waliyyuna wa muntaha muna wa taj'alu fi munqalabi wa ma'adi, wa anta ila, wa sayyidi, wa kuffa 'ada'a wa 'ada'a, inna kulla shay'in qadir, wa sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin sayyidil mursalin, wa 'ala wa 'ala A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Sallallahu 'alayka ya Aba Abdillah. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. First of all, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to you all on Eid-e-Ghadir and Eid-e-Mubahila. We pray that Allah (SWT) grants us the ability to remain steadfast on the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and grants us the honor of spreading this message to the entire world. These three episodes of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz 2025 video series were our small effort to propagate the message of Wilayah. We hope you liked it and that it proved helpful in understanding the reality of Ghadir. Your sincere participation in the quiz has greatly encouraged us. Certainly, the prize goes to only one, but everyone who made the intention is entitled to the reward. We pray that everyone is granted the honor of Ziyarat. We request the winner to, on behalf of all of us, We request them to perform Ziyarat on behalf of all of us. And now the time has arrived that everyone was waiting for—the announcement of the mega winner of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz 2025, who is receiving the prize of a Ziyarat trip to Iraq, the blessed lands of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimiya, and Samarra. Here is the name on your screen: Mustahreen Balwa from Mumbai, India. Many, many congratulations! The TSR team is grateful to you all. If you have any feedback or suggestions, please WhatsApp us at our number [number removed]. If you also want to join us in the message of Wilayah, subscribe to our channel, like the videos, and do press the bell icon. We pray that Allah (SWT) grants us the ability to hold firmly onto the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) until our last breath and grants a great reward to those who spread this message. Ameen Ya Rabbul Alameen. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Maatami Juloos Kyun? Ek Naasebi Ko Shia Aalim Ka Jawaab | #muharram
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common objection raised by critics regarding the necessity of public Azadari (mourning processions) for Imam Husayn. The speaker recounts an encounter where a Shia scholar explains that public mourning serves as a historical safeguard against the denial or distortion of the tragedy of Karbala. By maintaining visible rituals, Shias ensure the truth of Imam Husayn's martyrdom remains undeniable, drawing a parallel to the historical attempts to obscure the event of Ghadir Khumm. The lecture concludes by calling for a similar level of widespread propagation for the message of Ghadir and the Wilayah of Imam Ali.
content:
Haydar, Haydar, Haydar... A'udhu billahis-sami'il-'alim minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Sallallahu alaika ya Waliyyal Asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Assalamu alal Husayn, wa ala Ali ibnil Husayn, wa ala awladil Husayn, wa ala as-habil Husayn. In the book 'Shubuhat-e-Azadari', a very interesting incident is found where a scholar-looking Wahhabi asked a Shia scholar and raised this objection regarding Azadari. What is the objection? Nothing new, the same old worn-out objection. He says that Sayyiduna Husayn (r.a.) achieved a great victory by being martyred. Allah also granted you a place in Firdaws-e-Bari. But you Shias, centuries have passed since this event, you still, for centuries, perform mourning, chain-mourning, take out processions, and come out onto the streets beating your heads and chests. What do you gain by doing such absurd things? Your purpose is only to attract others' attention towards yourselves. What will be gained from all this? How long will you continue to come out onto the streets and beat your heads and chests over that old event? If you have to do it, do it in your gatherings, in your mosques, in your Imambargahs, in your homes. What will you get by coming out onto the streets and doing all these things openly? On this, the Shia scholar replies, and it is written in that book that perhaps this Shia scholar was none other than Allama Amini (r.a.). And it is not far-fetched, because Allama Amini can answer such questions very well. So, that religious scholar answers that this method of Azadari (mourning) of ours is actually based on the bitter and unpleasant experiences we have had with you people for centuries. He says that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced the mastership (Mawla) of Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (a.s.) in the open field of Ghadir-e-Khumm in front of 125,000 pilgrims, you forgot that event very easily. So much so that your people tried to deny that event altogether, asking what Ghadir was, what Caliphate, what Imamate, and what kind of announcement that was? When our scholars tried to answer, when our scholars wrote books in response, and when you people could not find a way to escape, you tried to twist and present that event in such a way that it was not actually an announcement of Wilayah, but that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was only telling people about the friendship and love for Ali (a.s.). So, it actually has nothing to do with Imamate and Caliphate, and in fact, you people still say to this day that the Messenger of Allah never appointed a successor in his entire life. Meaning, to hide one lie, you tell countless other lies. Then that Shia scholar continues his answer, and after that, he says that surely, if we had been negligent regarding the martyrdom of Hazrat Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (a.s.) in Karbala and the atrocities committed against him by Yazid and the Yazidis, and if we did not perform Azadari with the same zeal, fervor, and passion—going out into the streets and lanes beating our chests and heads—then you would have denied this historical event as well. Therefore, regarding this, you would have also said: what oppression, what martyrdom? Meaning, Imam Husayn (a.s.) was not martyred at all. That is not far-fetched for you people; you would have denied this fact. You would have said that Imam Husayn (a.s.) had left with his family for travel. He fell ill on the way, was afflicted with that illness, and died of that illness—meaning he departed from the world. And it is not far-fetched for you people to use the term 'Radi Allahu' (May Allah be pleased with him) for Yazid—although some people do use it, they do it fearfully, but they do it. You would have said 'Radi Allahu' for that cursed and rejected one, and you would have also said that he offered condolences to the family of Imam Husayn (a.s.), held a memorial service, did everything, and sent the family of Imam Husayn (a.s.) back to Medina with great honor and respect. You would have denied all these things; you would have completely distorted this event. But we did not let this happen. This Azadari that we perform, the lesson we learned from the bitter experience regarding Ghadir, we ensured—we took care—that we would not let this experience affect the event of Karbala and Imam Husayn (a.s.), and that is why we established Azadari with full passion. For centuries, we have been performing these mourning rituals so that not only do we receive the spiritual reward through this Azadari, but a message goes out to the whole world, and the whole world knows what tragedy actually occurred in Karbala in 61 AH. This was the answer of that Shia religious scholar. Now, a very important responsibility falls upon us here, and what is that responsibility? Just this last point: that when we had a bad experience with them regarding Ghadir, we did not let it affect Muharram and Karbala, and we spread the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) through our Azadari. Today, our experience regarding Karbala has been good, in that because of this Azadari, the message of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) reached the whole world, and because of this Azadari, we see that people of different religions—people of every nation, every faith, and every community—participate in this Azadari of Sayyid al-Shuhada. Now, having had this good experience because of this Azadari, it is our responsibility to make Ghadir so widespread that any person among the opponents, whoever they may be, should think ten times before saying anything regarding Ghadir—from denying Ghadir to questioning the immediate Caliphate and Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.). They should know that if they try to speak out, an answer will come from the Shias, and we do not need to be afraid. When Allah has taken the responsibility and the shadow of Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is present over our heads, then with the help of Allah and the help of the Hujjah, we move forward. May the Almighty hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Asr (a.s.) and grant us all the ability to propagate the message of the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) as much as possible. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: #3 - Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Manzelat | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen | شرح زیارت اربعین  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual status of Imam Husayn (a.s.) as articulated in the Ziyarat-e-Arba'een. The speaker emphasizes that true recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam begins with love and the acknowledgment of his divine appointment as a Wali of Allah. By examining the light of the Ahl al-Bayt, the lecture highlights that accepting their Wilayah is a fundamental condition of faith. Ultimately, the talk frames Imam Husayn's martyrdom not as a defeat, but as a divine success and a victory of truth over falsehood.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. The prerequisite for any recognition (Ma'rifat) is love and affection, and the demand of love is that it should be expressed. In these phrases of Ziyarat-e-Arba'een, a pilgrim of Husayn, while expressing his love for Imam Husayn (a.s.) in the presence of Allah Almighty, testifies: 'O Lord! I testify that he is indeed Your Wali and the son of Your Wali, and Your chosen one and the son of Your chosen one, who has succeeded through Your generosity.' Being the chosen one of Allah means that we are acknowledging and expressing that status of Imam Husayn (a.s.) about which the Almighty Allah said to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) on the night of Mi'raj: 'O Muhammad! I created you, and Ali, Fatima, Hasan, Husayn, and the Imams from their progeny from the same light as My light. I presented the Wilayah of you all to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. So, whoever accepted it is among the believers in My sight, and whoever denied it is among the enemies of the religion in My sight.' Meaning, Imam Husayn (a.s.) and all the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) are the most superior of Allah's creation. Accepting their Wilayah is a condition of faith, and this status and position is granted by Allah. That is why we testify that, due to Allah's grace, the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) is actually his success. Just as all other perfections, virtues, and merits of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) are granted by Allah, in the same way, martyrdom is also a blessing from the Almighty Allah. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability and the recognition so that when we recite Ziyarat-e-Arba'een, we recite it with the belief that Imam Husayn (a.s.) is that sacred personality who, by rejecting the allegiance to Yazid and accepting martyrdom, announced his victory. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Ilm aur Maal: 7 Farq | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the superiority of knowledge over wealth, drawing upon the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). The speaker highlights seven distinct differences between the two, as articulated by Imam Ali (a.s.), emphasizing that knowledge is a divine inheritance that benefits the soul in both this life and the hereafter. By contrasting the fleeting nature of material riches with the eternal value of wisdom, the talk encourages believers to prioritize spiritual and intellectual growth.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Knowledge and wealth are two such things that people have sought in every era. But the seekers of these have been different in every era, in every age, and they are different and will remain different. There are no two opinions about this; rather, every wise person will accept that knowledge is superior to wealth and riches in every way. There is no comparison between these two things. We, the Twelver Shias, take pride in the fact that we are followers of such Imams whose knowledge has been the talk of the town in every era and every age, and in this field, no one has been seen to be equal to them, let alone come near them. And why shouldn't it be so? They are the successors and caliphs of that Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) who is the City of Knowledge. Shia books are filled with numerous narrations in which the Imams (a.s.) have shed light on various aspects of knowledge. Come, let us look at a rare gem from that treasure, which is the speech of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Amir al-Mu'minin Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) describes seven aspects in which knowledge is superior to wealth. The Imam (a.s.) says: 'Knowledge is superior to wealth in seven ways.' First: 'It is the inheritance of the Prophets, while wealth is the inheritance of the Pharaohs'—meaning the cruel and tyrannical kings. Second: 'Knowledge does not decrease by spending, while wealth decreases by it.' Third: 'Wealth needs a guardian, while knowledge protects its owner.' Fourth: 'Knowledge enters the shroud with the owner, while wealth remains behind.' Meaning, knowledge not only benefits him in this world but will also be a helper to its owner in all the stages of the hereafter, while wealth and riches remain in this world. Fifth: 'Wealth can be obtained by both the believer and the disbeliever, while knowledge is obtained only by the believer.' Meaning, knowledge is exclusive to the believer. Sixth: 'All people are in need of the possessor of knowledge in matters of their religion, and they are not in need of the possessor of wealth.' Seventh: 'Knowledge strengthens a man to pass over the Sirat (the bridge), while wealth hinders him.' Seventh: 'Knowledge will strengthen the possessor of knowledge, making the stage of crossing the Sirat easy, while wealth and riches will create difficulties for him in this stage and will become an obstacle in his crossing the Sirat.' You have observed that referring to the hadiths of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) will not only increase our knowledge but will also strengthen our faith. And peace be upon Muhammad and his pure and purified family.

title: EP25 | Hadees-e-Ghadeer | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the historical and theological significance of the Event of Ghadir Khumm, focusing on the declaration of Ali ibn Abi Talib's Wilayah. The speaker examines the revelation of the verse of perfection of religion and addresses historical attempts to suppress or truncate the narration of this event in Sunni canonical texts. By comparing sources like Sahih Bukhari and Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the lecture highlights the importance of accurate historical transmission and the divine appointment of leadership.
content:
PSR presents. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya Waliyyul Asr adriknah wala tuhliknah. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Before we begin today's episode, let's find out who the winners of the sixth quiz of this series, i.e., from episode number 21 to episode number 24, are, and their names are on your screen. Briefly, when the Prophet was returning from Hajjat-ul-Wida, Gabriel came to a place called Ghadir-e-Khumm. Ghadir means a pond in Arabic, and the name of that place was Khumm. That is why it was named Ghadir-e-Khumm. So, Gabriel came here and revealed the verse, brought it from Allah: 'Ya ayyuhar-rasulu balligh ma unzila ilayka mir-rabbik' (O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord). If you do not do this, you have not conveyed His message. In other words, your 23-year mission—13 years in Mecca and 10 years in Medina—and in Medina, you fought about 77 Ghazwat and Sariyyat, and besides that, all the hardships you endured in Mecca, all the difficulties, all the troubles, all the difficulties, you bore everything and conveyed this message for 13 years in Mecca, then after that, all the difficulties you endured in Medina, and whatever troubles, calamities, and sorrows there were, after bearing everything, today this announcement is being made that if you have not conveyed this message, then it is as if you have not performed any task of the mission at all. Fama ballaghta risalatahu wallahu ya'simuka minan-nas (Allah will protect you from the people). That is, Allah is taking the guarantee of Ismah (infallibility). So, do not worry at all. Innallaha la yahdil-qawmal-kafirin (And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people). And those who are not willing to believe, Allah will not guide them either. Those who are not worthy of being guided, those who have stubbornness in their hearts, those who have malice, hatred, and enmity in their hearts, there is no cure for them. Allah will not guide them either; they are not even worthy of being guided. This was the verse of Surah Ma'idah that was revealed. After that, it is said that the Prophet stopped everyone at this Ghadir-e-Khumm and ordered the companions to clear the thorns under the trees, whatever was there, and then a pulpit was prepared there, and the Prophet ascended it and gave a very long sermon. However, let this remain in your noble minds that this long sermon, this lengthy sermon of Ghadir, is present in Shia books. But the Ahl-e-Tasannun avoided stating many things even about the basic matter, the reason for which we also present to you, what is it? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) delivered a very long sermon and then announced, 'O people, أَلَسْتُ أَوْلَى بِكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ (Am I not more entitled to you than your own selves?)' Everyone said, 'Yes, surely you are.' Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said—there are different wordings which, God willing, I will present to you—the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلَاهُ فَهَذَا عَلِيٌّ مَوْلَاهُ (Of whomsoever I am Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla). اللَّهُمَّ وَالِ مَنْ وَالَاهُ وَعَادِ مَنْ عَادَاهُ (O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him and be the enemy of whoever is his enemy).' Mawla means master, and Mawla also means a slave. So, whoever considers Ali as their master, treat them as Your slave. 'وَعَادِ مَنْ عَادَاهُ (And be the enemy of whoever is his enemy).' 'وَانْصُرْ مَنْ نَصَرَهُ (And help whoever helps him).' 'وَاخْذُلْ مَنْ خَذَلَهُ (And forsake whoever forsakes him).' To forsake means to abandon, to leave, to not help. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made this supplication and the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was announced, tents were pitched right there in the desert. This is how people offered congratulations, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'سَلِّمُوا عَلِيًّا بِإِمْرَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (Greet Ali with the title of Amir al-Mu'minin).' Meaning, the title 'Amir al-Mu'minin' belongs only and exclusively to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), that is all. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made this announcement, after this long sermon, then the verse was revealed: 'الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا (This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion).' And completed My favors upon you, meaning that with Wilayah, the favors were completed. Now, there is no room for anything else after this. The rest, God willing, the other narrations and the arguments, if Allah grants us the ability, we will do it next time. title: Quran e Majeed Ki Tilaawat Ka Kitna Sawaab Milega?
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual rewards associated with reciting the Holy Quran at night. Drawing from a narration by Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, the speaker details how the number of verses recited categorizes a believer into different spiritual ranks, ranging from the rememberers of Allah to the successful. The talk concludes by emphasizing the vast, immeasurable nature of the reward for reciting one thousand verses.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us and do not let us perish. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) narrates from his noble grandfather, Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), that whoever recites ten verses in a night will not be counted among the heedless; whoever recites fifty verses will be counted among the rememberers (of Allah); whoever recites one hundred verses will be counted among the worshippers; whoever recites two hundred verses will be counted among those who possess humility and submissiveness; whoever recites three hundred verses will be written among the successful; whoever recites five hundred verses will be counted among those who strive in the way of Allah; and whoever recites one thousand verses will have a Qintar of gold written for him. One Qintar is equal to fifteen thousand Mithqals of gold, where one Mithqal is twenty-four carats. The smallest of these gold ingots is equal to Mount Uhud, and the largest is equal to the distance between the earth and the heavens—meaning the reward for it cannot be measured. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has spoken the truth.
Reciting ten verses nightly prevents one from being counted among the heedless.
Fifty verses classify a person as one of the rememberers of Allah.
One hundred verses elevate a believer to the rank of worshippers.
Two hundred verses signify humility and submissiveness.
Three hundred verses lead to being recorded among the successful.
Five hundred verses count a person among those who strive in the way of Allah.
One thousand verses earn a reward equivalent to a Qintar of gold, which is immeasurable.
