title: Muharram 1442 Urdu Majlis #01: Sahi Aqeede ki Ahmiyat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound significance of correct belief (Aqeeda) through the lens of Imam Husayn’s companions and the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse emphasizes that true companionship is rooted in sincerity, spiritual insight, and an unwavering commitment to the path of the Ahlulbayt. By analyzing the nature of divine recognition and the necessity of Wilayah, the speaker encourages listeners to use these historical examples as a standard for self-reflection and moral steadfastness against injustice.
content:
I am hungry and thirsty, they are saying... [Incoherent/Garbled audio segments] [Incoherent/Garbled audio segments] [Incoherent/Garbled audio segments] [Incoherent/Garbled audio segments] The doctor is here, what is he saying? He is saying something beautiful. He is saying something beautiful about the martyrs. He is saying something beautiful about the stories of the martyrs. He is saying something beautiful, and I am enjoying it. He has crafted it well, listen to it. He has... [Arabic/Transliterated text: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad...]. Peace be upon the Hashimi family, peace be upon the martyrs of the path of Allah, peace be upon the companions of the Master of Martyrs, peace be upon the followers of the truth, peace be upon those who stood by the side of the oppressed. The Imam of the time, may Allah hasten his reappearance, is the one who guides us. [Arabic/Transliterated text: ...]. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said this. And the companions of the Imam, may Allah be pleased with them, are the masters of the righteous. And the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (a.s.), says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had told them that 'Husayn (a.s.) will be killed in this place, meaning Karbala, and your companions will be killed with you.' And their level of faith will be such that when the iron—meaning the sword or any weapon—strikes them, they will not feel the pain. They will be so immersed in the love of Imam Husayn (a.s.) that... They will be so immersed in the love of Imam Husayn (a.s.) that they will not care about anything in the world. Their bodies will be destroyed, but they will not feel the pain. This is a sign of their faith. And the companions who have waited for this moment, this is the moment. These are the beautiful companions of the Imam. There are many traditions, not just one or two, but many, where people came before the Imam and claimed, 'I am your companion, I am your helper.' But the Imam could see the reality on their faces. He would say, 'You are lying. Why? Because I saw you in the previous world, and you were not there. If you were there, you would have been with me.' Where were you? The Imam said, 'Whoever was a friend there is a friend here, and whoever was an enemy there is an enemy here.' So, this is the second point. And the next point is that when you look at them, you see these qualities. This does not mean to belittle anyone or to criticize anyone. My purpose is only to present the traditions before you and to explain the narrations that have been stated by the Imams (a.s.) so that we may know what that level is, what level the Imam expects from his followers, and what kind of people they are. If we analyze these traditions, even a little bit, we will see that even if we discuss this for ten hours, we cannot fully understand these traditions, but as much as we can take, it is better than leaving it all. What is the reason that our youth, the 313 companions, are being discussed? Why is the criteria being set? First of all, it is not to criticize anyone. It is not to point fingers at anyone. It is only so that we can be aware of the traditions. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... we have discussed this before, but it is good to refresh it. On the Day of Judgment, every Imam will be raised and asked about his followers. The Imam will be asked about his companions. Not everyone is the same. After 80, there were some, then there were others, then there were others. What is their level? When we read the traditions, we see that about the companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and about the companions of the Imams (a.s.), it is said that they were very simple people. But when the mention of Imam Husayn (a.s.) comes, it is said that when you raise the 72 who were martyred with him, they were at a level of love that we cannot even imagine today. We cannot even think of that level. They had no fear of pain or suffering. At that level, what is the most important thing? It is faith. If you discuss the traditions, you need certain conditions. Just as for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), certain things were necessary, similarly for the companions of the Imam (a.s.), it is not just about the appearance. The most important thing is the intention. If the intention is not correct, then everything is useless. Even if the action is great, if the intention is not correct, it is all useless. And then, action is also important. There is a tradition that breaks the back—not literally, but it breaks the pride of the ego. What does this tradition say? These two people, who are the sons of... they were special companions of the Imam. Among them, there are those who were brothers. When the Imam called them, they were ready. They were from a family where the mother played a great role. If a mother is on the right path, she guides the whole family. And in the same way, the father's role is also there. And in this way, until Akbar, they were cooked—the features, the principles, and the methods. Anyway, there were two sons; one was named Muhammad and one was named Hamza. These two brothers were the sons of Rashid. Now, these two—these two, they are included in such attacks. At that time, there was no major entrepreneur or big operating system that the big giants needed. It was a matter of agreement, so Marat Chetram and all these people were with the Imam, present at the time, and they were from that era. And they were our people, the brown organization—our people were feeling very good. Now, they started a discussion about the account, and the rain that followed, and our people were evidence. Everyone else was talking, and there was no child among them who was small; they were all big people. In this way, the number was very high. Salaam, according to the scriptures, said that the Imam was asking, 'Tomorrow, we will have this problem, don't worry.' So, why would you stay? Or should I? Me, Arvind Singh, I have taken an oath here, and by Allah's will, I will not open my mouth in front of you. Look at the manners, look at this. I will not open my mouth. Look at the manners. When it comes to intellect, the best application is that a man should think about how much he knows. That is the warning of the Imam. Very good. They are claiming to be the Aristotle of their time, but our people will know what the level is. The level will be known. Anyway, I have taken an oath that I will not open my mouth in front of you. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'I give you permission to speak, start.' Now, he will force it, so remember this. Now, 582, Allah, Allah, Allah—what does it mean? I will tell you this. You do it comfortably, but you cannot use it comfortably. The meaning of 'Shahadat' is 'I bear witness.' And witness is given for something that one sees with one's own eyes, that which... That which one sees with one's own eyes, that which is visible. If we are testifying with our eyes that there is no god but Allah, then we are part of this testimony. 'I bear witness'—it is like that. And the scholars of the past, the avengers, said that 'Ullah'—what does 'Allah' mean? Muslim, your humility—what does 'Ansar' mean? 'Ansar' means it is made from two roots: 'Al' and 'Ilaha'. 'La ilaha illallah'—the scholars of the past have already explained this. Therefore, 'Al' means that Being who is closest to us, and 'Ilah' means that which our nature recognizes and identifies well. And no one recognizes the Creator like the Creator Himself. And 'Ilah' means that you cannot identify Him with your eyes, you cannot perceive Him, you cannot grasp Him with your eyes, you cannot understand Him with your hands. That is why no one can be a greater witness than Him. The Messenger (s.a.w.a.) was asked, 'How did you recognize the Creator?' He said, 'I recognized Him through Himself, the energy that revealed itself...' The energy that revealed itself, the way He manifested Himself. And He said, 'I did not do anything from my side.' And the Masoom (a.s.) was amazed. And the second meaning was: when a person loses hope in everything, the Being he turns to is called Allah. And the second meaning explained that the third meaning is this: that He is the One who cannot come into human thought, who is beyond every thought and every imagination. Therefore, Allah says, 'I am beyond what you imagine.' Whatever comes into your mind, whatever you think, Allah is beyond that. You can never reach Him. So, we recognized Him through signs. We recognized Him through signs. Muhammad Rafi, where is he? The one who recognizes you, he has found you. And the one who knows what you are, he has known Allah. There is another mantra: 'And you will be able to see.' This is why we recite the Quran, but we don't understand it. We don't understand 'La ilaha illallah'. That is why in the traditions, among the things that were not understood, one is 'Allah'. The names given to Allah are called 'Surah'. Look, Allah is not just a name. That is why the Imam (a.s.) was asked, 'Have you seen Allah?' He said, 'I do not worship a God whom I do not see.' So, how did you see Him? This is the proof: 'I am talking about seeing with the heart, not with these eyes. I am talking about the eyes of the heart. I see Him, and I testify.' I see Him, and I testify. This is with the Quran, this is with the Quran. Yes, it is true that someone dug up things, it is with the Quran. The Quran says, 'Did I not make you testify?' It is necessary for the heart to testify. He showed them Himself and took a testimony from them. He showed them first. This is the proof of the Quran. In verse 172, Allah says, 'Am I not your Lord?' I am not saying this myself; it is from the Quran. So, all these people sitting here—if someone opens up, they will see it, because if they don't reflect, then there is no one. There is no one. But how did they answer? Did they answer with their eyes? 'Am I not your Lord?' Everyone said, 'Bala' (Yes, indeed). Everyone said, 'Bala' (Yes, indeed). Now, our brothers have done this: they started sitting and doing Tafsir (interpretation). When such things happen, they say Allah came in front of them with a full body, and they started talking about things that are against Allah. If they think they saw Allah with their physical eyes, then they are trapped in the limitations of Allah. This is a long debate. It is part of the tradition. There is no doubt that the Imam (a.s.) is the truth, there is no doubt. That is why the life of the Masoom (a.s.) changed everything. But never put a limit on the house of Allah. In the same way, in the discussion, they say, 'Oh, he is the one who gives, he is the one who takes.' So, our people should understand that we cannot reach Him, we can never reach Him. But it doesn't mean that we shouldn't try. Everything is there. It became a trend to say, 'Ali is Allah,' 'Adam is Allah.' This is not the way; this is to defame the religion. But anyway, the law of the Lord is the most supreme. The law of the Lord is the most supreme. He is not a father, He has no children. Allah has no children. Do not make images of Him. From here, I tell you, Allah is beyond two hands. The Hadith is very important. It says, 'Do not limit Him.' Whatever you imagine, discard it. Do not inquire into His essence. Do not inquire. And do not deny Allah. Do not say you don't believe in Allah, or you don't recognize Him. And do not compare Him to any of His creations. This is the way. If a person's tongue does not work, then the whole body is useless. Whatever image you bring, it is your own. If you bring your own memory, then this is polytheism. Here, you are talking about yourself. You are talking about yourself, or whatever image you bring, it is your own. It is your own soul. You are not dependent on the olive tree. You are not the body. This is your soul talking; you are not dependent on it. And when you remove the veil from it, it will return to its original state. It will return. I gave an example: those who think they can see Allah with their physical eyes—it is like an ant. The ant thinks the whole world is a grain of sugar, and on its two antennae, it thinks the whole world is there. And it moves forward. This is the debate of the heart. Today, if you want to go, you will learn. Some people say that whatever we do, we don't do it; Allah does it. They call it 'Jabriya'. And some people say that Allah created us and gave us power, and now Allah cannot stop us. This is called 'Tafweed'. This is called 'Tafweed'. Both of these are between the two, and both are against the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). It is important to understand that Allah created us and gave us power and gave us the ability to act. This is the truth. And along with this, Allah is the Master over us, and whenever He wants, He can take back what He gave us. He can take it back from us. And a human should always be humble. You must have seen that great people in the world reach a stage where they don't even remain human. And here, you saw that the most beautiful thing in the world was given, but no one can see it, no one can understand it. And many people, when they started thinking about what it is, they started talking, but when they started thinking about themselves, they understood. It is the same. And when they started thinking about themselves, they realized that Allah is the one who, whenever He wants, can take back anything. Before this, in the previous traditions, a story came—at that time, it was like that. So, if we reflect on the state of a servant... If we adopt a certain mindset, for instance, a grandfather once told his grandson that in Samarra, there was a situation where people were being forced to do something, and even the scholars were being pressured. It reached a point where the pressure was so immense that people were dying. It became a matter of life and death. In our house, there is only one person, and because of that, I am constantly worried about my family. It wasn't just a month; it felt like every month there was some issue in our house. Although this gathering is a good one, the conditions related to these issues were very bad. There were books, and I thought, 'Should I go to the bank?' Allah knows, the information was sent to the bank. People went to the scholars, and the Shirazi scholar issued a fatwa regarding tobacco. They were known for not being afraid of anyone, and the British were aware of this. This was something that the British... This was something that the British had to abandon. The fatwa was issued at that time, and it was: 'You must not give them any support.' It was clear that it was obligatory for everyone to stand against them. Whether it was 3,000 people or more, they stood firm. It was a difficult time, and the situation in Pakistan is also quite tense right now. We should all pray for everyone, wherever they are in the world. During this time, there is a lot of cursing and fighting, but we shouldn't get involved in that; it only leads to conflict. Let me tell you, this is history. The history of the tobacco movement—do you know how many people were killed? 30,000 people were killed. And 30,000 is such a huge number for that era. For that era, it was a huge number. And how long did that movement last? One day, two days, a month, two months? And how many people were killed? It is all recorded. And how many innocent people were there? Forget that, let's not talk about the past. 1,000 years ago, it was the same. One percent, just one percent—some people took it seriously. Just like you are here, one percent are worried. But the majority... this area, they used to say, 'What is Muharram? What are you doing?' They used to put pressure on our families, saying, 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah,' and that we couldn't do these things. But they kept accusing us. So what happened? They said, 'You take these things, the ones you have, and remove them.' So, whatever answer they give there, that is your intention. They said, 'We have to remove it.' There was a huge uproar, and it went to the authorities. It has been going on since 15422. The result was that they said, 'Forget it, let's just remove it.' They removed it. And you understand, I am not doing this. How to save it? They kept putting pressure on us. Now, whatever is left, we should keep it. This is happening everywhere, it's too much. This will happen, and then there will be more conflict. You are giving it for the second time, and there is conflict again. So, when they had to remove it, they said, 'Send it to the authorities.' Is there any verse in the Quran that says, 'Go and do this'? 'Walan tarda ankal yahudu walan nasara'—the Jews and the Christians will not be pleased with you... And the Christians will not be pleased with you until you follow their religion. Ultimately, they will not be satisfied. So, these things will continue, and this is a discussion that will keep happening. You should pray for the needy students. May Allah keep their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity safe wherever they are in the world. But the most important point is to keep their faith safe. News comes in, and it will go to the extent where there is no limit. After that, in the words of the Quran, 'Muhammadur Rasulullah'—he is the Messenger of Allah, and also a servant of Allah. He was sent to guide people so that Allah's religion may prevail over all other religions. Through the Quran, they will bring back the true path. This religion will be the one that prevails over all others. And the promise of Paradise—that is the truth. Everyone is going to leave this world. But the result is what matters. A person should think before doing anything, 'I have to give an account for this.' I have to give an account for every action. I have to give an account for every single thing. There are two volumes regarding this. If you have questions about this, bring them. There are a thousand hadiths in those two volumes. You know, those volumes are only about questions. And the Quran says in 57:8, 'Your ears, your eyes, and your hearts will all be questioned.' Don't think it's just about the traffic inspector; you will be questioned about everything. And the Quran says about the Children of Israel, 'Inna sam'a wal-basara wal-fu'ada kullu ula'ika kana anhu mas'ula.' This is the Quranic truth, and we all... This is the Quranic truth, and we all have to go. Everyone has to go tomorrow. No one is exempt. No one is special; anyone can go at any time. I am talking to you now, and maybe a little later, I might not be here. We might not be here. Many people were sitting here joking, and they are not in our thoughts now. Everyone has to go; that is a fact. Everyone has to go and face the same reality. Of course, if you are on the right path, you will go to a good place, Insha'Allah. We should all hope for that, but everyone has to go down. And here, I will give you a practical example. I was speaking very quickly. One day, at 10:30 at night, I went to the graveyard. I went to the graveyard, and I saw that they were digging a grave for someone. I thought, 'Who has passed away?' It was someone who had died during the day. This is the reality of life; no one can do anything. We are all helpless. This can happen to any of us. We have no special status; there is no exception. We have to move towards Allah. I recited the prayer, and I testified that Ali is the Wali of Allah. And when they are gone, no one's excuses will be accepted. The Quran says this, but when the time comes, they say, 'This is the only thing for which no excuse will be accepted.' None at all. No excuse will be accepted. And after that, we take the name of the Imam. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' After that, you have to follow the path of Muhammad and his family. After that, you have to follow the Imam. The Imam explained this very clearly. The Quran explained it, and the Tawhid was explained. Everything is there. The Imam said, 'Al-mizan, al-mizan.' This is the thing that breaks the back. The statement of the Imam is the standard. Who is the standard? The one who is on the straight path. You know, when builders build a wall, they use a plumb line to see if the wall is straight or not. They use it to check. And look here, when you keep this in front of every action, the Imam said... Keep this in front of every action. Every action must be in accordance with your faith. Is it according to your belief or not? Whether you are a believer or not. When you sit on the bench, the Imam said, 'What is the standard?' This is knowledge. If someone's action is not like yours, then who is he? If it is not like yours, then he is not on the path. Whatever we have heard about the Wilayah, if someone says that one can go without the Wilayah of Allah, that is not true. No one has an excuse. The Imam says that the one who does not know is the one who will be questioned on the Day of Judgment. The one who did not ask, catch him. The Quran says, 'Inna kulla shay'in ahsaynahu fi imamin mubin.' That in the qualifications for the Wilayah, in the past, there were some people, some such individuals, who were all those who had left the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). They left the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), they left the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And these were great personalities, they were called by very big names, they were considered great, and even if they were great personalities and Sayyids, even then, this is the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny, the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is that if one is a Sayyid, if one is from both sides—from both mother and father—then they are called a Sayyid from both sides. But our criteria is not just this; it is outside of that. So it became known that the means of our salvation is only through these three. If a person does anything else, no matter how good they claim it to be, it is of no benefit. That is why the reward of this Wilayah, meaning... The reward of this Wilayah, meaning the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), is that my spiritual mission, my connection with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), is what I love the most. I am from the progeny of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and I love them very much. Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is my leader. Time is very short, please read one question. Muhammad Saleh, Muhammad Meraj, they are not here. If you can do it at 12 o'clock, then do it. The Imam (a.s.) brought a chapter here: 'Ad-Deen, the Wilayah, the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' This was the status of the Imams (a.s.). As for the one who is explaining, he has already explained it. What did he say? 'This is the religion, this is the religion that...' This is the religion that Allah has selected for His servants. This is the religion that is seen in the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Then he said, 'Those who are steadfast, they are the ones.' title: Is the Hadith of "Death of Ignorance" not authentic? - Part 2 | Resp. Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi
excerpt: In this lecture, Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi examines the historical and theological controversy surrounding the status of Zurara ibn A'yan, specifically addressing claims that he died in a state of ignorance regarding the Imam of his time. The speaker clarifies the context of Imam al-Sadiq's succession, the necessity of taqiyya (dissimulation) during periods of intense state persecution, and the spiritual status of those actively seeking the truth. By analyzing Rijal literature and historical narratives, the lecture refutes misconceptions about Zurara's faith and underscores the Imam's divine knowledge and guidance.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief, and curse their enemies. May Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, assist me. So I want to respond to maybe two or three more points that were raised by this imposter, by this individual, just to demonstrate his hypocrisy, his duplicity, but perhaps more importantly, his deceptive nature and complete ignorance of the subject matter. The first is a hadith that he cites quite often, it seems, in multiple videos, where the context is you have two companions of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), one of whom is al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and the other is ibn Abi Ya'fur. And it appears that these two individuals get into an argument between them, and the argument is left unsettled until they refer to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) as the ultimate arbiter, and they seek his advice, and the Imam provides his advice. And so this guy, when he cites this hadith, he presents it as evidence for his case, but we'll see how that is most definitely not true. So I'll read through the hadith and then make some observations. So the hadith is narrated by Abi al-Abbas al-Baqbaq, he said: 'Ibn Abi Ya'fur and Mu'alla ibn Khunays discussed.' They had an argument, they had a discussion. 'Ibn Abi Ya'fur said: The successors are scholars, righteous, and pious.' Ibn Abi Ya'fur identified and described the successors, al-awsiya. Listen to these words very carefully. The successors as people who were scholars, they were learned, righteous, and they were pious. So he's restricting the status of successors to being scholars who are learned, to being righteous, and to being pious. Ibn Khunays on the other hand, Mu'alla, said to Ibn Abi Ya'fur, 'That's not the case. The successors are prophets.' So one says that successors are prophets, the other says they're merely learned individuals who are also righteous and pious. So they decide to take the matter up to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to seek his counsel and his advice. He said: 'So they entered upon Abu Abdullah (a.s.), and when they were seated.' They entered upon the Imam. As soon as they sat down, the Imam said to them, he started speaking to them. He addressed them and said, 'O Abdullah, I disassociate from whoever says that we are prophets.' Oh slave of God, right? Abdullah, perhaps was the name of Ibn Abi Ya'fur. He said, 'O Abdullah, I disassociate from whoever says that we are prophets.' Now, a few critical observations to make from this hadith. Number one, the position of Mu'alla ibn Khunays is not necessarily wrong in and of itself. Allow me to explain. We do know according to the verses of the Holy Quran as well as other ahadith that in previous times, previous prophets would appoint successors by God's order and that those successors would also be prophets. In other words, the original claim by al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays was what? 'The successors are prophets.' That successors in general are prophets. Now, we also know, I'm sure you've all heard this hadith, this famous prophetic narration about the Commander of the Faithful in which he says, 'O Ali, you are to me like Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me.' Now, what this suggests quite clearly is that Harun was not just a wasi of Musa, not just a successor and an appointed heir of Musa, but also a prophet. So, by default, the principle that Mu'alla ibn Khunays is referring to here is that generally speaking, successors of prophets like Sheeth to Adam (a.s.) was that he was not just a successor but also a prophet. Ibn Abi Ya'fur's response was that no, they are merely learned individuals who are pious and righteous and very good people, right? Now, what does the Imam say? Listen carefully. The Imam simply does, he does two things actually. The first is quite interesting. By initiating the conversation and addressing exactly the point that they were debating, the Imam proves what here? He proves ilm al-ghayb (knowledge of the unseen). So, my first counter-argument to this imposter, when you use this hadith, you deny ilm al-ghayb for the Imams. You believe the Imams do not have any ilm al-ghayb. The hadith that you're citing yourself proves that you're wrong. It proves that the Imam has ilm al-ghayb, otherwise how would the Imam know what they were talking about? As soon as they sit down, he initiated the conversation by addressing the problem at hand. That's point number one. So, next time just be careful which hadith you try to use to your advantage. Number two, the Imam isn't taking any particular side in this argument. Listen carefully to what the Imam says. You have one companion who is lowering the station of the Imams (a.s.) to that of righteous scholars, good people who are also very learned. You have the other one who may be suggesting, we don't know exactly, but maybe suggesting that the Imams of the Ahlulbayt, the successors of the prophet, are also prophets just like previous successors who might have held both titles. They were both successors as well as prophets. We don't know if Mu'alla ibn Khunays actually believed this because he wasn't talking about the Imams of the Ahlulbayt. He was speaking broadly, he was speaking generally. But let's say that this is what he believed. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'I disassociate.' I disassociate from those who say that we are prophets. The Imam is not saying that the position of Ibn Abi Ya'fur is accurate. 'Proving one thing does not negate another,' as they say. The Imam is not taking any particular position. He's simply declaring that if anybody thinks that we are prophets, we disassociate from him. So that hopefully makes this clear. Next time when he uses this hadith, don't be fooled by that. The second point I want to address is the one that has to do with Zurara. And the reason I want to address this is number one, to show how ignorant this person is. And number two, it is to address a problem that he raised, right? First of all, I'll start with Zurara. He said that Zurara died a death of ignorance because he died a few months, perhaps two or three months after the death of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). We know that according to several reports. So when Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) passed away, when he was martyred and killed by Mansur al-Dawaniqi, Zurara was already sick. He was bedridden, right? So he's saying that when Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) passed away, Zurara did not know who the successor of Imam al-Sadiq was. And he sent somebody to find out who it was, but he never knew, never learned the result of the investigation. So he died not knowing the Imam of his time. And so his argument is that if you accept the hadith of 'Whoever dies without knowing the Imam of his time dies a death of ignorance,' you have to say that Zurara died a death of ignorance as well. So how do you respond to this? The first response is that according to biographers and according to the scholars of Rijal, Zurara is identified as not just the companion of Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq, but also Imam al-Kadhim (a.s.). So to say that he didn't recognize the Imam of his time goes against these reports. For example, according to Sheikh al-Tusi—this is in Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith by the way, by Sayyid al-Khoei—he counted him in his Rijal among the companions of al-Baqir (a.s.), saying: 'Zurara ibn A'yan al-Shaybani, their mawla.' He's considered among the companions of Imam al-Baqir. And among the companions of al-Sadiq (a.s.) likewise, with the addition of saying: 'Kufan, surnamed Abu al-Hasan, died in the year 150 after Abu Abdullah (a.s.).' And he's also classified as a companion of Imam al-Sadiq, right? He was from Kufa, he was called Abu al-Hasan, he died in the year 150 after Imam al-Sadiq, so shortly after the death of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). And among the companions of al-Kadhim (a.s.), he said: 'And he's also considered among the companions of Imam al-Kadhim, the seventh Imam,' and he said: 'Zurara ibn A'yan al-Shaybani, trustworthy. He narrated from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (a.s.).' So, if he's considered as a companion of Imam al-Kadhim, how do you say he didn't recognize the Imam of his time, who was Imam al-Kadhim? Obviously he does. Al-Barqi also counted him among the companions of al-Baqir, al-Sadiq, and al-Kadhim (a.s.). So al-Barqi, who was one of the original and foremost rijalis, he also says that Zurara was among the companions of Imam al-Kadhim (a.s.). That's point number one. Point number two, there is a hadith, I'll quote the one in Tafsir al-Ayyashi, right? Which says this hadith addresses two points. Again, I'll explain later. The previous one is in Ikmal al-Din, again, Ikmal al-Din, news flash, as per Bihar al-Anwar. He said: 'I asked Abu Abdullah (a.s.), is it possible that people would be in a state where they don't know the Imam?' He said, I asked the Imam, al-Harith ibn Mughira, I said to him, is it possible that people would be in a state where they don't know the Imam of their time? He said: 'That may happen.' I said: 'So what do they do?' The Imam said: 'They hold on to the first thing until the last becomes clear to them.' They hold on to the first thing, meaning they hold on to the Imam that they knew last, the Imam that they recognized last, until matters clarify, until things become clear and they can recognize the Imam of their time. Which means that it's okay. If for whatever reason you happen to be in a situation where you don't have access to the Imam of your time, you hold on to the last one until the dust settles and things begin to become clear. The next hadith is the one I want to draw your attention to. From Abi al-Sabah, he said: 'I said to Abu Abdullah (a.s.)' and the chain is found. 'I said to Abu Abdullah (a.s.), what do you say about a man who was called to this matter and he recognized it, and he was in a remote land, then the death of the Imam came, and while he was waiting, death came to him?' He said: 'He is, by Allah, in the position of one who migrated to Allah and His Messenger, and then died, so his reward is upon Allah.' Now, I'll read the next hadith because it expands on this one, so I won't translate this one per se. From Ibn Abi Umayr, he said: 'Zurara sent his son Ubayd to Medina to inquire.' When Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) passed away, and there's a lot of details here, but I don't want to get into them. Imam al-Sadiq was under extreme pressure. And the taqiyya (dissimulation) that was practiced by the Imam in terms of the appointment of the successor and making a public declaration about it was absolutely mind-blowing, right? It was a very, very difficult moment. You had al-Mansur al-Dawaniqi (la'natullah alayh) who had sent spies and was trying to find out the successor of the Imam in order to incarcerate or kill him. So the Imam (alayhis-salam) had to leave in his will and testament, the one that was made publicly available, he appointed five individuals as his successors. Each of which had a major problem so that anyone with a modicum of understanding and who had employed the faculty of the intellect and referred to the original scriptures was able to find out the true successor of the Imam. Ibn Abi Umayr says that when Imam al-Sadiq (alayhis-salam) passed away, Zurara was left for a few months as we said earlier. In the meantime, Zurara was trying to explore and find out who the real legitimate Imam is. And in his mind, according to Ibn Abi Umayr, Zurara had only two options. He knew that the others would be ruled out for one reason or another, and he would be left with only two possible scenarios. Either it is Abdullah al-Aftah or it would be Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (alayhis-salam). 'An Ibn Abi Umayr qala wajjaha Zurara ibnahu Ubaydan ila al-Madina yastakhbir lahu khabar Abi al-Hasan wa Abdullah.' In other words, he sent him to find out whether it's Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (alayhis-salam) or Abdullah al-Aftah. It says 'fa-mata qabla an yarji'a ilayhi ibnahu.' Zurara died before his son came back to report the results of his investigation. Zurara lived in Kufa, he sent his son to Medina, by the time his son came back to tell him who the actual Imam is, to investigate, to find out the details, Zurara had already passed away. Qala Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr haddathani Muhammad ibn Hakim qala qultu li-Abi al-Hasan al-Awwal. So here is a companion who goes to Imam al-Kadhim (alayhis-salam) and asks him about Zurara. Fadhakartu lahu Zurara wa tawjiha ibnihi Ubaydan ila al-Madina. So I told him that Zurara sent his son to Medina to investigate. What's going to happen to Zurara if Zurara didn't actually know that you were the Imam? Fa-qala Abu al-Hasan (alayhis-salam) inni la-arju an yakuna Zurara mimman qala Allah: 'Wa man yakhruj min baytihi muhajiran ila Allahi wa rasulihi thumma yudrikuhu al-mawtu faqad waqa'a ajruhu 'ala Allah.' The Imam said, I wish and I pray that Zurara will be among those that Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) includes in this verse: 'He who leaves his home seeking migration to Allah and to His Prophet and death comes to them, his rewards will be awarded to them by Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala).' That's one thing which shows you a very, very important point. And that is that if someone for whatever reason happens to be in a situation where they cannot recognize the Imam of their time, but they actively try to find him and recognize him and acknowledge him, then that is accepted and we have multiple ahadith by that. As a matter of fact, there's another hadith in which somebody asks the Imam. He says to him, what happens to Zurara in this case? The Imam brings this example. He says that there was the fatra between Prophet Isa (alayhis-salam) and Rasulullah. This period of hundreds of years between Jesus and Muhammad (sallallahu alayhi wa alihi wa sallam), what happens to the people then? The Imam (alayhis-salam) explains, Imam al-Sadiq, he says that those people who lived in that era, in the fatra as it's called, if they were actively seeking to recognize the Imam of their time, then that is accepted by Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala). In other words, they hold on to their belief in Isa and they're waiting for the next Prophet or they're looking for the next Prophet, anticipating the next Prophet, Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) will accept that from them. The worst-case scenario is that they will be categorized as mustad'af. They had no way of knowing. They were trying to, but they had no way of knowing. So, to try and use this example of Zurara and then say, 'Oh, so then he died a death of ignorance.' The Imams themselves have explained that Zurara most certainly did not die a death of ignorance. As a matter of fact, there is another opinion, which is that Zurara definitely knew who the Imam of his time was. Notice that in these ahadith, it is other people who tell the Imam that Zurara was trying to find out. The Imam is not saying that Zurara didn't know. We have other ahadith that state that Zurara knew, but that he himself practiced taqiyya. The authorities knew exactly who Zurara was. They understood his proximity to Imam al-Sadiq (alayhis-salam), and so they were trying to find out from him what they failed to find out from Imam al-Sadiq and his will. So they kept eyes and spies on Zurara, so Zurara didn't speak of the next successor of Imam al-Sadiq (alayhis-salam), and toward the end of his life, he said, 'Oh Allah, I believe in whomever is your hujja and your proof,' without actually naming Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (alayhis-salam). And that definitely makes perfect sense, and it is in accordance with the previous reports that I mentioned, which say that Zurara was not only someone who recognized Imam al-Kadhim, but was also counted among the companions of Imam al-Kadhim (alayhis-salam). I will leave this discussion at this point here because I think we've provided enough evidence of the duplicity and hypocrisy of these individuals that try to lower the status of the Imams (alayhimus-salam), try to make people doubt the appointment, the divine appointment of these Imams. We've shown that they are either being deceptive, they're either lying, or they are incredibly ignorant and really don't know the ABCs of rijal. They don't know the ABCs of the sciences of hadith and how the Imams (alayhimus-salam) speak. They don't know anything about history, they don't know about anything really. Not even Arabic grammar, unfortunately. That PhD has to be thrown away, it would seem. It's not worth the ink on the paper that it's printed on. But the fact of the matter is that I think we've provided enough evidence to demonstrate this to the dear brothers and sisters and community members so that they are aware of these things, so that they ensure that such individuals are not given a platform, that they don't fool the young, unsuspecting members of the community, and so that proper safeguards are put in place to ensure that the community is protected from these doubts and misconceptions, insha'Allah.

title: Taqleed: Ahmiyyat Aur Taqaazey | EP#01 - Taqleed Kya Hai Aur Kyun Hai?
excerpt: This lecture provides an introduction to the concept of Taqlid (emulation) in Shia jurisprudence, defining it as the practice of referring to a qualified jurist for religious rulings. The speaker supports the legitimacy of Taqlid by citing Quranic verses, traditions from the Ahlulbayt, and the logical necessity of seeking expert advice in specialized fields. The presentation concludes that Taqlid is a rational and divinely ordained method for believers to navigate religious obligations.
content:
May the peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. In this program, we will discuss a very important topic. In this series, we will shed light on the concept of Taqlid (emulation/following a jurist) and its importance, and present some points regarding it. Before we delve into the topic of Taqlid, let us first look at what Taqlid means. To understand this, let us refer to the 11th-century famous scholar of the Shia school of thought. Let us take the help of the book 'Majma al-Bahrain' by the famous 11th-century scholar. It is enough to say that in the list of his students, names like Allamah Majlisi and others appear. In the third volume of this book, he defines Taqlid and says that Taqlid is a technical term. It means accepting the words of another person without asking for evidence. That is, if a person asks a question and someone answers it, the listener accepts it without asking for proof. Now, let us see what the meaning of Taqlid is in Islamic terminology. In Islamic terminology, Taqlid means referring to your jurist (Mujtahid) for religious issues and acting upon the fatwas or rulings issued by them. Acting upon the fatwas or rulings is the meaning of Taqlid. Now that we have understood the concept of Taqlid, let us see if Taqlid exists in the Holy Quran. Has Allah (S.W.T.) mentioned Taqlid in the Holy Quran? Because if any matter is found in the Holy Quran, it is considered a firm Islamic principle. Let us see if the evidence for Taqlid is found in the Quran. For this, when we turn to the Quran, we see that there are verses that describe Taqlid and support it. The first verse I would like to read before you is Surah An-Nahl, verse 43, and this same verse is also found in Surah Al-Anbiya, verse 7. You must have heard it, in which Allah (S.W.T.) says: 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, fas'alu ahla al-dhikri in kuntum la ta'lamun' (Ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know). This is a great verse in which Allah (S.W.T.) gives a command to ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know. If we look at the interpretation of this verse, it refers to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), but if you look at its literal meaning, we find two types of people: one is 'Ahl al-Dhikr', those who possess knowledge, and the second are those who do not know. And clearly, in this verse, Allah (S.W.T.) has commanded those who do not know to refer to those who do know. The word 'fas'alu' (ask) is used, which is a command, an order. And this is the basis of Taqlid. Now let us turn to the second verse. This is Surah At-Tawbah, verse 122. In this verse, Allah (S.W.T.) says: '...falawla nafara min kulli firqatin minhum ta'ifatun liyatafaqqahu fi al-dini wa liyundhiru qawmahum idha raja'u ilayhim la'allahum yahdharun' (Why should not a group from every division of them go forth to gain deep understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they might be cautious?). In this verse, Allah (S.W.T.) is saying that why do some people not go to gain knowledge and acquire deep understanding of the religion, and when they return to their people, they warn them so that they may become cautious? In this verse, the concept of Taqlid is clearly explained: that from every nation, some should come forward to become 'Faqih' (jurist), to gain deep knowledge, and when they return to their people, they should acquaint them with the religious sciences and warn them. Acquaint them with religious sciences, warn them, and teach them what is Halal and Haram so that they may become cautious and God-fearing. From both these verses, it is known that Taqlid is a purely Islamic and Quranic reality, in which the believers have been encouraged to gain deep knowledge of the religion, and the masses have been told to refer to the Mujtahids for their religious issues. Now let us see if the Masumeen (a.s.) have mentioned Taqlid. For this, I would like to draw your attention to the Hadith I read at the beginning of this series. This Hadith is from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), who says: '...fa-amma man kana min al-fuqaha...' (As for those among the jurists...). First, let us see what 'Fuqaha' is. It is the plural of 'Faqih'. It comes from 'Fiqh', meaning to gain deep knowledge of something. In Islamic terminology, a Faqih is a person who has gained deep knowledge of the religion through hard work and study. Such a person is called a Faqih. The Imam says: 'As for those among the jurists who protect their own souls (from sins),' Protect their souls, refrain from sins, guard their religion, remain steadfast on it, oppose their desires, and obey their Lord. If there is such a Faqih, then the Imam further says: '...fal-awammi an yuqalliduhu' (then it is incumbent upon the masses to follow him). In this narration, if you look closely, two types of people are mentioned: on one side are the 'Fuqaha' and on the other side, the word the Imam used is 'Awam' (the masses). The qualities of the Faqih are described, and the masses are commanded to perform Taqlid. Another very famous and well-known Hadith regarding Taqlid is this: in this Hadith, the Imam (a.s.) says: '...wa amma al-hawadith al-waqi'ah farji'u fiha ila ruwati hadithina fa-innahum hujjati 'alaykum wa ana hujjatullahi 'alaykum' (And as for the new issues that arise, refer them to those who narrate our Hadith, for they are my proof upon you, and I am the proof of Allah upon you). In this narration, the Imam has clearly commanded the people that whenever they do not understand a problem or new issues arise, they should refer to those who narrate our Hadith. If we look at the word 'ruju' (refer), from this comes 'ruju' and from this comes 'Marja' (the one to whom one refers). Refer to those who narrate our Hadith, for they are my proof upon you, and I am the proof of Allah upon you. In this narration, the Imam has clearly commanded the people that whenever they do not understand a problem or new issues arise, they should refer to those who narrate our Hadith. If we look at the word 'ruju' (refer), from this comes 'ruju' and from this comes 'Marja' (the one to whom one refers). One last Hadith I will present before you before we move forward. This is from the time of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.), where a person named Ahmad ibn Hatim ibn Mahawayh wrote a letter to the 10th Imam in which he asked, 'From where should I acquire my religion?' And his brother also wrote a letter to the Imam with the same question. The Imam replied to him in a letter, and in that letter, he stated: 'Trust in that Faqih who has spent his life in our love.' Trust in that Faqih who has spent his life in our love, and if he narrates our traditions, then he will be sufficient for you. Here too, the Imam emphasized to that person to take his religious issues to someone other than himself, to seek help from someone else, and to ask someone else. This Hadith can be found in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 2, page 82, Hadith number 3, and it is also found in Wasa'il al-Shia, page 4. From these narrations, it becomes clear that Taqlid is a reality, and its meaning has been explained by the Masumeen (a.s.) in their narrations, and they have commanded the people to act upon it. Now, in the final part of this discussion, let us try to understand whether Taqlid aligns with human intellect or not. To understand this, let us take a daily example from our own lives. Whenever a person falls ill, they have three ways to treat themselves or to get a cure for that illness. Gain knowledge, acquire information, and then treat themselves. The second option they have is that if they have two medicines, they should choose which medicine to take. If they have the option of whether to take an injection or medicine, they should choose whether to take an injection or medicine. For this, it is necessary for them to have knowledge and expertise in that field. The third path that remains for them is that whenever they have an illness or a problem, they should go to a doctor because the doctor is an expert in that field, who has gained deep knowledge and a degree in that field. Therefore, he knows better how to treat this illness, and he is more capable and qualified to answer your questions and treat this disease. In these three situations, what would human intellect think? Whether to gain knowledge when falling ill, to guess, or to go to a doctor? Surely, you and I would agree that every person, when they fall ill, selects the third option and goes to a doctor. Second example: if a person has to fight a case, they should either become a lawyer themselves and fight their own case, or go to a lawyer. Fight their own case or go to a lawyer. If they have a financial problem, they should either become a Chartered Accountant themselves or go to a Chartered Accountant. In all these things, in our daily lives, we perform Taqlid of some expert or specialist. Similarly, in religion, when problems arise, it is our responsibility that if we cannot gain deep knowledge in religious sciences ourselves, we should refer to a Faqih, and this is the meaning of Taqlid. So, in conclusion, when we perform Taqlid in our worldly matters knowingly or unknowingly, then there should be no problem in performing Taqlid in religious matters, because Taqlid is a reality included in the light of the Quran, Hadith, and intellect, and it cannot be denied. And praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual concept of 'Nur' (Light) in relation to the Ahlulbayt, emphasizing their role as the divine guidance for humanity. The discourse connects the theological status of the Imams as the manifestation of Allah's light with the historical tragedy of Karbala, specifically focusing on the unmatched loyalty and martyrdom of Mawla Abbas. Dr. Rizvi further addresses the importance of family values, the necessity of purity of heart, and the transformative power of Wilayah in securing salvation on the Day of Judgment.
content:
Mir Ali, this elegy, when the banner of Ali was raised high in the battlefield. I am presenting some verses from it in the glory of Mawla Abbas. That lion came out of the tent holding the banner, the army of the enemy came to witness the victory. Courage stepped forward and kissed the sword and the edge, victory kissed his hands, and success kissed his feet. The glory of the sun fell from his eyes, the eagle of fortune circled around his head. When he reached the desert of Kufa, galloping his horse, he raised his hand and shouted to the horse, 'Enough.' He saw the rows of the enemy standing in front and behind, and he shouted that there is a desire to go to the river. Whoever stops me will fall into the clutches of death, move aside, all of you, for the lion is going to the marshland. The wrestlers of the enemy army stepped forward and said, 'We have never seen such a great army retreat.' Here are all the warriors of Rum and Sham. Yes, they have come, drawing their sparks-scattering swords. They are not mere guards of the riverbank. They will throw heads into the canal, severed by their daggers. And impure does not mean the impurities you read about in the Tawzih al-Masa'il. Impure means those who keep the love of the enemies of the Ahlulbayt in their hearts. That is the real impurity. 'Nahnu aslu kulle khair.' We are the source of all good, and our enemies are the source of all evil. All the evils that exist, their source is the enemies of the Ahlulbayt. All the evils. Therefore, whatever impurities there are, they are their source. If someone has even an atom's weight of love for the enemies of the Ahlulbayt in their heart, they can never receive this light. They can read books, it is possible they read books. They may read books, they may read many books. But reading books is not the criterion, remember. There is a Hadith of the sixth Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Ya Ali. Ya Ali. Is it clear to you? The Imam says that 'Al-ilmu nurun.' Knowledge is light, knowledge. 'Laisal ilmu bitta'allum.' Knowledge does not come from reading. Knowledge does not come from reading. Reading is a preface, a premise, an introduction to it. But ultimately, putting knowledge into the heart is Allah's work. He does not give it to everyone. 'Al-ilmu nuru yaqzifuhullahu fi qalbe mayyasha.' Allah puts it into the heart of whom He wills. So, when a person feels the heat and warmth of the love of the Ahlulbayt in their heart, then understand that knowledge has entered their heart. Then they become Salman. Then they become Abu Dharr. Salman and Abu Dharr went, right? Both went. Meaning, first Abu Dharr came to Salman and started saying, 'Ya Salman, what is the luminous recognition of Ali?' What is the recognition of Ali's light? Which is called 'Marifat-e-Nuraniyah'. Salman says, 'I don't know either.' Salman is at the tenth level. He says, 'I don't know either.' 'Let's do one thing, let's both go and ask Ali himself.' So, the Hadith is very beautiful, I will just say one sentence of it. Both came and started asking, 'Ya Amir al-Mu'minin, you tell us, what is your Marifat-e-Nuraniyah?' So, the Master of the Universe said, 'Ya Salmanu ya Jundab.' Jundab was the name of Abu Dharr. Abu Dharr was his title. Abu Dharr, meaning the father of gold. The father of wealth, Abu Dharr. 'Ya Salmanu ya Jundab. Marifati bin nuraniyate marifatullah. Wa marifatullahe marifati bin nuraniya.' My recognition through the light is the recognition of Allah. And the recognition of Allah is the recognition of my light. Now, the Hadith we read, so is this exaggeration? Is this not exaggeration? Why is it exaggeration? We said the recognition of Allah and the recognition of Ali are one and the same recognition. So, we replied, 'Brother, when you read Hadiths by exaggerating them, why don't you think at that time?' 'Man arafa nafsahu arafa rabbahu.' You read it. 'He who has recognized his own self has recognized his Lord.' You are ready to speak of the recognition of the Lord for your own self. But for the light of Ali, you say this is exaggeration, this is not exaggeration? Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. So, no servant will love us. No servant will accept our Wilayah until, until Allah purifies his heart. Now, what is the condition for purifying the heart? Allah will not purify the heart of any servant until he is completely submissive to us. Completely submit. What does submission mean? Submission means this: if it is accepted that they are the Ahlulbayt. If it is accepted that this is the Ahlulbayt. If it is accepted that their word is the truth. If it is accepted that the Prophet said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things. Inni tariqun fikumul saqalain. Kitabullahi wa itrati Ahlulbayti. The Book of Allah and my Ahlulbayt. Ma in tamassaktum bihima, if you hold on to these two, if you hold them firmly, lan tazillu ba'di abada. You will never go astray after me. Fa innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida alayyal hauz. Because they will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Pond of Kawthar.' They will not be separated from each other until they come to me at the Pond of Kawthar. This is a saying of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and a very famous hadith. Let us mention it again. Mir Amir Hussain Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh. Now, in 'Aqat al-Anwar', he has discussed only this one hadith in four volumes, spanning 1500 pages. It is also available in English. The translation has been done in English, you can check it. 1500 pages. You can check it. A discussion on just one hadith. This is called Hadith al-Thaqalayn. If we assume the Prophet said to hold onto them only, that is it. This is the 'Hablullah al-Matin', the strong rope of Allah. 'Wa'tasimu bihablillahi jami'an wala tafarraqu'. The Quran has commanded to hold onto them. Hold them firmly, hold the Ahlulbayt firmly. If it is a command, then we must submit to them. If there is something we do not understand in front of them, and it is fine, and there is a narrator who—meaning a narrator came and asked the Imam, 'If someone narrates your hadith and we cannot digest it.' Many people cannot digest hadith, right? They cannot process it. So what should be done? The Imam asked, 'Does he narrate hadith from us regularly? Is he consistent in narrating hadith from us?' He said, 'Yes, he narrates regularly.' The Imam asked, 'Does he call day night and night day? Meaning, does he say something completely against reason?' He said, 'No, he does not say anything against reason.' He said, 'Then, if you do not understand the hadith, if you cannot digest it, then in such a case, do not reject the hadith, but leave it and ask the other Imams, they will explain it to you.' 'Istafimillah yufhimka' (Ask Allah, He will make you understand), as it is in another hadith. So pray to Allah to make you understand, Allah will make you understand. It is very simple. So, to submit. That is why the narrator said—this is in Usul al-Kafi, in the first volume—that the chapter is named 'Bab al-Taslim wa Fadl al-Musallimin' (The Chapter of Submission and the Virtue of those who Submit). In it, the narrator said to the Imam, 'Your companion, your follower, whose name is Kulayb, submits so much to your hadiths, he accepts your words so much that when we just say to him, 'Baqir said, Sadiq said,' he says, 'Sallamna' (We have submitted).' I have submitted, I have accepted. He accepts so much that we have named him 'Kulayb al-Taslim'. We named him that. Kulayb al-Taslim, meaning the Kulayb who submits. When the Imam heard this, the Imam prayed for him. The Imam said, 'Rahimahullah' (May Allah's mercy descend upon him). This is called submission. This itself is a vast subject. Insha'Allah, we will discuss it some other time. Then he says there, 'Wa yakunu silman lana' (And he should be at peace with us). Submit and do not wage war against us. There should be no malice in his heart against us, no grudge, no enmity against us. Then Allah will purify his heart. 'Fa-idha kana silman lana', if he is truly at peace with us—meaning he makes peace with us, does not wage war, submits—Allah will protect him from the severe reckoning of the Day of Judgment. The Day of Judgment... Then there will be no reckoning for him. There will be no reckoning, and Allah will protect him from the 'Faza' al-Akbar' (Greatest Fear) on the Day of Judgment, and will grant him peace. Faza' al-Akbar is a stage of the Day of Judgment. It is called Faza' al-Akbar in the Quran, 'Al-Faza' al-Akbar'. Faza' means fear and Akbar means greatest. The greatest fear. You know there are 50 stages of the Day of Judgment. There are 50 stages on the Day of Judgment. Each stage is of 1,000 years. So what will be the total duration of the Day of Judgment? 50,000 years. The Day of Judgment will be 50,000 years long. Okay? This—meaning the total duration of the Day of Judgment, its span, will be 50,000 years. Is it clear to you or not? 50,000 years. Out of that, 1,000 years will just be the Faza' al-Akbar. The greatest fear. Meaning at that time, the condition will be such that there will be darkness all around, and people will be sweating so much out of fear that the sweat—in different hadiths it is written somewhere up to the knees, somewhere up to here. It will be up to here. People will be so terrified. And it is written in the hadith that at that time, only that person will be safe who used to give the Adhan before prayer. Who used to give the Adhan before his prayer, 'Al-Mu'adhdhinun'. Anyway, the Imam says that whoever keeps our Wilayah will be safe, will be protected from the Faza' al-Akbar. He will be protected from the severe reckoning of the Day of Judgment. It is very strange. So this is the status of the Family of Muhammad. We have read only one hadith before you, or two hadiths, just two hadiths. Because there is no time for more hadiths, that is why we read very few hadiths before you. Just understand that this is the status of the Ahlulbayt. This is the status, this is their light. Therefore, never compare anyone with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Nobody can be compared with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And Imam Hussain (a.s.) is the one who is the pride of the Ahlulbayt. We have repeatedly submitted to your service in these gatherings that the Prophet said, 'Hussainu minni wa ana min Hussain' (Hussain is from me and I am from Hussain). And 'Hasanu wal Hussain sayyida shabab-e-ahl-e-jannah' (Hasan and Hussain are the leaders of the youth of Paradise). How many hadiths, how many hadiths. Then we turn to the hadith that is our main current subject, we read the hadith quickly, that the Prophet says, 'Salasatun la turaddu da'watuhum' (There are three people whose prayers Allah never rejects). Three people. Who are those three people? One is the patient. The patient is the person who is ill. So if God forbid someone becomes ill, 'Adhallakumullah', if someone becomes ill, becomes a patient, then at that time you should look for an excuse to pray for this illness. And in prayers, always pray first for the soul of the Imam-e-Zamana. 'Allahumma ajjal wali-al-faraj'. Always pray. After that, pray for yourself. When someone prays for the Imam and then for himself, then surely his prayer is answered. And then the second one he mentions, 'wa ta'ib', and the one who is a repentant. When a person realizes his sins and repents, then Allah answers his prayer, Allah accepts his prayer. These two things happened. Allah never rejects the prayer of such a person. The person who realizes his sin and comes to the court of Allah, weeps. Read the phrases of Dua-e-Kumayl. Reflect on the phrases of Dua-e-Kumayl. Dua-e-Kumayl is no less than a miracle. Meaning, if we only discuss the explanation of Dua-e-Kumayl—of course, it is not possible in gatherings, but separately, if we only discuss the explanation of Dua-e-Kumayl, 'Ilahi wa sayyidi man li ghayruk' (My God and my Master, who do I have besides You?). Who is there, O Lord, besides You? 'As'aluhu kashfa zurri wa nazra fi amri' (I ask Him to remove my distress and look upon my affairs). Who should I go to, in whose court should I go, who will remove my troubles and look with mercy upon my affairs, look with mercy upon my matters? Who should I go to, O Lord? Go to the court of Allah weeping, crying. Go crying. Allah accepts repentance. And the third one who is generous, which we have been saying repeatedly in your service. Then the Imam, the Prophet says, 'Wa salasatun la tamassuhumun nar' (And there are three individuals whom the fire of Hell cannot touch). The Prophet is giving a guarantee, brother. Look, we are not saying this, we are quoting the hadith. It is a hadith from 'Irshad al-Qulub', we have also given the reference. The late Daylami is the author's name, Daylami. Hasan ibn Hasan ibn Abil Hasan Daylami is the author. Meaning, among the sources of Allama Majlisi, you can understand what a great personality he must be. Yes? He has written this in his book 'Irshad al-Qulub'. This hadith has been narrated. There are three people whom the fire of Hell cannot touch. The Prophet says, guarantee, the Prophet is giving a guarantee. Who are those people? First of all, first of all, 'Al-mar'atu al-muti'atu li-zawjiha' (The woman who obeys her husband). Who obeys a husband. Now you see what the situation is nowadays, right? Divorce over small things, divorce. You see all around. Divorce here, divorce there, divorce there, divorce here. Now I am even afraid to speak. In the gathering, earlier I used to speak openly about many things. Now I am afraid of that too. Because many people come and say, 'You were speaking about us.' Oh, La ilaha illallah. I was not speaking about anyone, brother, I was reading what is written in the hadith. But the problem that exists, the problem in society, it is not that it is one case or two cases, no. It is rampant. We are copying this from the West. The Shias who live in the West, they copy the white people there, and the Shias here, they copy by looking at the Shias there. 'Look, divorce happens so easily there, let us also do divorce here.' We don't want to listen, we don't want to listen. Why listen to the husband? Are we servants? This is that. These are all nonsense. What is the Prophet saying? The Prophet is saying that if a woman obeys her husband, the fire of Hell is forbidden for her. The fire of Hell cannot touch her. And just for a few days, anyway, if you understand, look, let me submit one thing to your service, the most important thing in Islam, sometimes even—listen to this very carefully—sometimes it is even more important than apparent religion, that is family bonding. Family bonding, and its example is given in the Quran. The example of Janab-e-Asiya is before you. Janab-e-Asiya bint-e-Muzahim is the wife of Pharaoh. She is the wife of Pharaoh, the spouse of Pharaoh. And she should not have stayed with Pharaoh. Pharaoh used to forbid her from worshiping. But Janab-e-Asiya was with Pharaoh. And there are many details, I don't want to go into that. It is just that, let me just tell you one sentence of the hadith, that Pharaoh—obviously, Pharaoh found out that she worships Allah, so Pharaoh would have killed her. Because Pharaoh had many wives. He would have killed her, what is one? So Janab-e-Asiya—the sentence of the hadith is—used to worship Allah in such a place where it is makruh (disliked) to worship. Meaning where? In the restroom. She used to go to the restroom and there in solitude, so that no one would know, she used to worship Allah. And the second thing, 'Wal-waladu al-baru li-walidayh' (The boy who treats his parents with kindness). And the third is the generous one who has good character. This itself is a whole debate, which we don't have to do right now. Insha'Allah, we will do it some other time. Let us stop the hadith here because the time is up, so let us submit the Masaib to your service, that you see when there is a family, a culture, a bonding, then the children are also like that. If children see that there is always a fight between parents, then children also understand that this is the way to live. This is what life is called. But if a woman comes into the house and comes and says to the children, 'Children, I am your servant.' 'Children, I am your servant.' No one can compete with the Princess. She did not say that I am the wife of the Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali). Rather, she considered herself a servant. Janab-e-Ummul-Banin. And what was the result? Such children were born who all sacrificed themselves for Imam Hussain (a.s.). Janab-e-Abbas has such virtue, such importance that no one can estimate. Whatever is said about him, whatever is read, it is less. Meaning he was a model of action for the whole history. The Imams (a.s.), the Imams (a.s.) took pride in him. The Imam says, 'Ammi al-Abbas. Rahimallahu ammi al-Abbas.' (My uncle Abbas. May Allah have mercy on my uncle Abbas.) How much patience Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) exercised, how much patience, no one can estimate. No one can estimate. To the point that the moment arrived before Ashura when Imam Hussain (a.s.) gave permission, 'Abbas, you go and bring water for the children.' Now Hazrat Abbas came to the door of the tent and called out, 'Daughter Sakina, please bring the water skin.' As soon as Sakina heard her uncle's voice, she came running, 'Uncle, what will you do with the water skin?' He said, 'The Master has ordered me to bring water, so bring the water skin, I will bring water.' I will bring water. Sakina went and brought the water skin. It is written in the Maqtal that when Sakina was walking with the water skin, small children started walking with her. 'Bibi, where are you taking this water skin? Where are you taking this water skin?' She said, 'Uncle has promised that he will bring water.' Children, now be assured. Now be assured, my uncle will go now, he will bring water now. Children, now be assured.' Sakina said and brought and gave the water skin. Abbas departed and left. He cleared the armies, came, came near the Euphrates, and put his horse into the Euphrates. After that, he got off the horse, dismounted, left the water skin, filled the water skin with water, and then taking water in his cupped hands, he said, 'O wretched ones, do not think I am helpless. I can drink water, but I am not drinking it because the children are thirsty in the tents, the princesses are thirsty, that is why I am not drinking water.' Saying this, Abbas threw the water away. Then he came, mounted the horse, in one hand was the standard, in the other hand was the water skin. As Abbas started moving from the bank of the Euphrates, as he started moving towards the tents, a wretch struck such a blow that Abbas's right arm was severed. Abbas recited a Rajaz, 'Even if you sever my right arm, I will still continue to obey my Master.' And with one hand, he managed the water skin and the standard. Then a wretch struck again, the left arm was severed. Abbas now held the water skin firmly with his lips, with his teeth, so that somehow the water skin would reach the tent. Just then, an arrow of tyranny was shot. Such an arrow of tyranny that it hit the water skin. As soon as the arrow of tyranny hit, the water started flowing. As soon as the water of the water skin flowed away, Abbas bowed his head. 'What will I do now by going to the tent? How will I show my face to the children now?' Thinking this, Abbas bowed his head. There is a strange sentence in the Maqtal, 'I do not have the courage, how should I pay?' It is just written that when Abbas bowed his head, a wretch struck a mace from behind. On Abbas's head. The Lion of Ali fell from the back of the horse onto the land of Karbala. Mourners, whenever a person falls from a height, naturally their hands come forward first. But the Lion of Ali fell face down. He called out, 'Master!' As soon as the voice reached Hussain's ears, Hussain held his back. He recited a dirge, 'Al-aan inkasara zahri' (Now my back is broken), 'Abbas, now my back is broken.' Hussain's back is now broken. Hussain's back is broken. 'Al-aan inkasara zahri' That Hussain who had the courage to lift bodies until now, that Hussain is now broken. 'Al-aan inkasara zahri' Not only was his back broken, listen to the second hemistich, 'Wa qallat heelati' (And my stratagem has diminished), the eyesight has gone. Abbas, I cannot see anything. 'Wa qallat heelati', 'Wa shamata bi aduwwi' (And my enemy is gloating over me), Abbas, the enemy is taunting me. Where is your standard-bearer? What happened to your standard-bearer? Hussain, Imam Hussain (a.s.) arrived. Now he placed Abbas's head on his lap. There was some conversation between the brothers. Abbas made a will, 'Master, do not take my body to the tent. I am very ashamed, I could not bring water for the children.' Saying this, Abbas closed his eyes. Hussain recited a dirge, 'Al-yawma namat a'yun' (Today those eyes will sleep that were awake until now due to your awe). Abbas, now the ladies will wake up, the princesses will wake up, they will start mourning for the children. 'Fasaya'lamu alladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun' (And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned), 'Wal-aqibatu lil-muttaqin' (And the end is for the righteous). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Amen. Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. Amen. Count us among his helpers and supporters. Amen. O Lord, those who are in distress, remove their distresses. Amen. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Amen. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Amen. Those who are sick, grant them complete and immediate healing. Amen. O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Amen. Protect the high scholars and the great Maraje. Amen. And protect the holy shrines. Amen. Those who are protecting them, You protect them. Amen. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab. Amen. O Lord, grant us the privilege of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Amen. Accept our Ziyarat-dari. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Aashur Ke Din Kaun Roza Rakhta Hai? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the controversial practice of fasting on the day of Ashura, the anniversary of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). By referencing narrations from the Imams, the speaker explains that fasting on this day is historically rooted in the celebratory practices of the Bani Umayya. The lecture concludes that for those who mourn the tragedy of Karbala, fasting on Ashura is inappropriate, as it signifies joy over the event.
content:
Sallallahu Alaika Ya Rasool Allah. It is the day of Ashura, the day of the martyrdom of Hazrat Imam Hussain (a.s.). Instead of understanding the day of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his family, some people celebrate it as a day of happiness and fast on the day of Ashura. So, let us look at the light of the Hadith of Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) to see what it is like to fast on the day of Ashura and who fasts on this day. When a narrator asked this question to Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the Imam replied, 'Ashura is the day on which Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred. So, if you feel happy about his martyrdom, then keep a fast on the day of Ashura.' According to this Hadith of Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.), only those people fast on the day of Ashura who feel happy about the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). In this same Hadith, Imam Sajjad (a.s.) also explained the reason for this. The Imam said that the Bani Umayya had conspired that if Imam Hussain (a.s.) were martyred, they would declare that day a day of Eid and fast as a sign of gratitude, and they would make their children happy on that day. Thus, this became the Sunnah of Abu Sufyan, which continues to this day. That is why those people fast on this day and please their ancestors. The Imam (a.s.) said that one does not fast when a tragedy occurs, but rather one fasts as a sign of gratitude for safety. And the day of Ashura was a great tragedy for Imam Hussain (a.s.). If you are among those for whom Ashura is a day of tragedy, then do not fast on that day, and if you are among those who are happy with the safety of the Bani Umayya, then fast as a sign of gratitude. O Lord, by the sake of the great tragedies of Imam Hussain (a.s.), do not count us among the group for whom the day of Ashura is a day of Eid and happiness, and who fast on this day. Ameen Ya Rabbal Alameen.

excerpt: This lecture announces a poetry competition titled 'Alami Jashn-e-Elaan-e-Wilayat' organized by Dast-e-Gurooh (a.s.) to celebrate the Wilayat of Imam Ali (a.s.). content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Hazrat Imam Reza (a.s.) has said that no believer recites poetry about us in which he helps us, except that Allah creates a city for him in Paradise which will be seven times wider than this world, and in which every angel, martyr, and prophet will visit that believer. Keeping this Hadith in mind and on the occasion of the upcoming Wilayat Day, the team of 'Dast-e-Gurooh (a.s.)' is presenting a new and unique program in your service called 'Alami Jashn-e-Faelan-e-Wilayat'. In this, you will be given two couplets (misras). You have to recite your poetry on both these couplets or on any one of these two couplets, and by Saturday, August 8, 2020, you have to send a short 2-minute video of yourself reciting that poetry to our WhatsApp number. Your video will be uploaded to our Facebook and Instagram channels. Insha'Allah, the first couplet is: 'Sajid le Momin'. Insha'Allah, the first couplet is 'Sajid le Momin par man kunto ka naam hai'. The judges for this are the respected poets Janab Dr. Shoor Azmi Sahab. And the second couplet is 'Ye dil Ali ko yojana mein agar thikana chahiye hai'. The judges for this are the respected poets Janab Mashoor Thanapuri Sahab. Through the judgment of these two judges, i.e., Dr. Shoor Azmi Sahab and Mashoor Thanapuri Sahab, two best couplets will be given an award of 7,500 Indian Rupees, two best verses will be given 7,000 Indian Rupees, and two best complete poems will be given 10,000 Indian Rupees. Insha'Allah, apart from this, the videos that will receive the most likes on our Facebook and Instagram channels by Friday, August 14, 2020, will be chosen by the believers, and two such videos will be given an award of 5,000 Indian Rupees. Insha'Allah, and all those who participate in this celebration through their poetry, 12 of them will be given an award of 1,000 Indian Rupees through a lucky draw. Insha'Allah, anyone can participate in this program, whether they are a poet, a reciter, or anyone else. Just keep in mind that your poetry must be on the given couplets. The announcement of the winners and the lucky draw will be made on Sunday, August 16, 2020, in a celebration to be held on the Dast-e-Gurooh YouTube channel. Insha'Allah, remember that the last date to send the video and poetry is Saturday, August 8, 2020. Do not forget to send your name, city name, and your written poetry along with your 2-minute video to our WhatsApp number. This is our number: [number removed]. And if you want to write the name of your Anjuman, you can send it to us. Remember that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had ordered that it is the responsibility of every present person to convey this message of Wilayat to the absent ones. So, come and join our humble effort for the sake of the Wilayat of Amir-ul-Momineen Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), so that we all can fulfill the command of our Prophet. Insha'Allah. Alhamdulillahil-ladhi ja'alana min al-mutamassikeen bi-wilayati Amir-ul-Momineen wal-aimmat-e-ahle-bait (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali... Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad, wa ajjal farajahum wa ahlika aduwahum ajma'in.
