title: Iftaar Ke Waqt Is Dua Ko Na Bhooliyega [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual significance of the moment of Iftar during Ramadan, highlighting that it is a time when prayers are answered. The speaker encourages believers to acknowledge the source of their sustenance by attributing it to Allah, the Prophet, and the Ahl al-Bayt. Specifically, the lecture advocates for incorporating prayers for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) into one's daily Iftar routine as a way to show gratitude for divine bounties.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Sallallahu alayhi wa alihi. Regarding the time of Iftar in the month of Ramadan, Hazrat Imam Hassan (a.s.) says: 'Inna lillahi inda kulli iftarin da'watan mustajabah' (Indeed, Allah has a prayer that is answered at the time of every Iftar). Following this teaching, among the prayers we recite at the time of Iftar, two are famous. One is that a believer, after fasting all day and enduring all kinds of hardships, says: 'Ya Wasi'al-Maghfirati, ighfirli' (O One whose forgiveness is vast, forgive me). May all my sins be forgiven. And the other is that a fasting person should recite this prayer at Iftar: 'Allahumma laka sumtu wa ala rizqika aftartu, wa alayka tawakkaltu'... ...and upon Your provision I have broken my fast, and in You I trust. But have we ever thought that this provision which is reaching us, due to which we are able to break our fast and eat various kinds of food, from where is it reaching us? In the Holy Quran, in the 59th verse of Surah At-Tawbah, the Lord of Honor says: 'Wa law annahum radu ma atahumullahu wa rasuluhu wa qalu hasbunallahu sayu'tinallahu min fadlihi wa rasuluhu' (And if they were satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger'). That is why whenever Imam Sadiq (a.s.) used to eat something, he would raise his hands and say: 'Alhamdulillahir-Rabbil-Alamin. Allahumma hadha min indika wa min ind-e-Rasulika' (Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, this is from You and from Your Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family). And this is our belief that Allah and... And our belief is that after Allah and His Messenger, in every era, the Imam of the Time and the successor of the Messenger is the medium through which the bounties of the Lord are descended. Our Master, Mawla, Imam, Guardian, and Benefactor has rights over our necks, and it is our duty that when we receive the first bounty for Iftar, we should first thank Him, pray for the hastening of His reappearance, and then pray for ourselves. When we sit at the Dastarkhwan (dining spread) to eat, we should say: 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alameen, Allahumma hadha min Rasulika, hadha min Ahl-e-Baytika'—meaning, 'O Allah, this is from You, from the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), and from Your Ahl-e-Bayt.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time. O Allah, in this month of Ramadan, make the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) glorious and luminous, and grant us the ability to pray for his reappearance at the time of Iftar. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen. Grant us the ability to pray. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

content:
Regarding the 12 Imams, we find many Hadith that contain their names. Specifically, the names of Imam Ali (a.s.) and Imam Mahdi (a.s.) are found in almost every Hadith. The Hadith is from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself. He says: 'Al-aimmatu ba'di ithna ashara, awwaluhum Ali ibn Abi Talib wa akhiruhum al-Mahdi.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'After me, there will be 12 successors, the first of whom will be Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the last will be Imam Mahdi (a.s.).' These 12 Imams will be my Caliphs, my successors, my trustees, my guardians, and they will be Allah's proof (Hujjah) over my Ummah after me. And after that, he says that whoever acknowledges them is a believer, and whoever denies them is outside the fold of the religion.

excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm, framing it as the ultimate defeat of Iblis's efforts to misguide humanity. content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, then subscribe now and do not forget to press the bell icon. The quiz link has gone live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, then click on the quiz link and register. Then on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the series. Therefore, do not be in any hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. For the quiz prize, it is only necessary that the answers to all the questions should be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear in today's winners or if an episode was missed, then they do not need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner of the Iraq Ziyarat, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all the questions in all four episodes, and that mega winner will be selected in our special episode, InshaAllah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Praise be to Allah who has made us among those who hold fast to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams from his progeny. Infinite praise to that pure and holy Being of Oneness, to that God, the Exalted and Wise, the Merciful and Generous, who granted honor to the weak-founded human over all His creations. He adorned him with the jewelry of knowledge and wisdom and informed him through the tongues of His messengers about His Sharia laws, adhering to which He made a means of His pleasure and a means of salvation for him. And no matter how much gratitude is offered to that Almighty God, no matter how many prostrations of gratitude are offered in His court, it is less, that He sent for our guidance that Beloved of His who is himself the cause of the creation of the universe and a mercy to the worlds. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) conveyed all the commandments to his Ummah in his 23-year missionary life, performed all the tasks of the mission. To the point that the Almighty God Himself was seen saying in the Holy Quran: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have chosen Islam as your religion.' But He did not perfect this religion until then, did not complete these favors until then, nor was He pleased with the religion of Islam until the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), in the field of Ghadir, where he said: 'Of whomsoever I am the Master, this Ali is his Master.' Respected audience, this announcement of Ghadir, this announcement of Imamate, this message of Wilayah, was no ordinary matter. If we observe, it weighed very heavily upon the people. So much so that even in the verse Allah sent down, He gave a guarantee to the Messenger of Allah, saying: 'wa-allahu ya'simuka minan-nas' (and Allah will protect you from the people), that you convey this message, and I will protect you from the mischief of the people. This message was destined to become a cause of mischief for the people because if anyone was most distressed by this message, it was Iblis, who, due to his arrogance in refusing to prostrate before the Hujjat-e-Khuda (Proof of God) by the command of Allah, had been expelled from the court of Allah—the one who had claimed before Allah that he would sit on the Straight Path (Sirat-e-Mustaqeem) and would lead all the believers astray from the right path and misguide them. This announcement of Ghadir was the announcement that defeated this Iblis. So come, respected audience, today is the third episode of our 'Ghadir: The Divine Scale' series, and today's topic is 'Ghadir: The Announcement of the Defeat of Iblis.' To discuss this, we have with us our dear brother, Janab Kazim Syed Sahab. We will request him to present further discussion on this topic before us all. Kazim Bhai, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. Kazim Bhai, this is our third episode regarding Ghadir, and the topic is that Ghadir is the announcement of the defeat of Iblis. Now, regarding Iblis, the Holy Quran itself states that he is the greatest enemy of man, and among those who oppose Allah, he is the very first. So, what distress did this cause him due to the announcement of Ghadir, and how is this a defeat for Iblis through this announcement? We would like you to shed some light on this. Yes, Guzar Bhai, first of all, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. I greet the viewers and present to them congratulations on the Eid of Allah, the Eid-e-Akbar, the Wilayah of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) regarding Ghadir. Now, as you stated here that Iblis is the greatest enemy of Allah and his goal, his purpose, is to interfere in the Divine messages. Indeed. Now it is necessary to know that the greatest message from Allah is the message of the Wilayah of Amirul Momineen (a.s.). Yes. But before coming to this topic, the topic of Ghadir, it is very important to state his goal from the very first day, to present to the viewers what Iblis said when he was separated from Allah and from Paradise, and what he claimed he would do. So, if we turn our attention to the Holy Quran, okay? In it, this clear command of the Lord of Honor is being stated, where Iblis is seen saying in the Quran: 'Qala rabbi bima aghwaytani la-uzayyinnanna lahum fil-ardi wa-la-ughwiyannahum ajma'in, illa 'ibadaka minhumul-mukhlisin.' That is, he is seen saying, 'O my Lord! Since You have misled me, I will surely beautify for them [the sins] on earth, and I will mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them.' So, if you reflect on this verse, his purpose, his goal, his mission is that he will [target] all of God's servants, okay? Or the children of Adam (a.s.), his goal is to mislead all of them. Except for the sincere servants of Allah. So, if you reflect on these verses, this goal emerges. If you look in the same way at other verses, like the ones we just mentioned, you will find them in Surah Al-Hijr. Similarly, if you reflect on Surah Al-A'raf, he is seen saying similar sentences there too. Yes. That 'Qala fabima aghwaytani la-aq'udanna lahum siratakal-mustaqim.' That, 'O Lord of Honor! Since You have misled me, I will sit on Your Straight Path (Sirat-e-Mustaqeem) and what will I do by sitting there? I will lead Your servants astray.' Yes. Now it is necessary to know what this Sirat-e-Mustaqeem is. Where will he sit? So, if we turn to the exegeses (Tafasir) of the Imams (a.s.) and see whom the Imams (a.s.) have described as the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem or to whom they have pointed, then we will know what his target is. What is his purpose, towards which he is going to attack the most? Because one should never consider one's enemy weak. If we consider the enemy weak, we have lost the war. For this, it is very important to understand every tactic of the enemy, every attack he is making on us, every scheme. So now, since he himself said that I will sit on the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem and lead Your servants astray, it is necessary to know what the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem is. Indeed. If we go by the literal meaning, it is the straight path. The straight path. Which straight path? So it is very important to know this, and the best way for this is to go to the door of the Imams (a.s.) and ask them, 'Mawla, tell us what is the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem upon which this cursed one, this Iblis, is going to sit to lead us or all of humanity astray?' So, if you reflect, there is a tradition in Bihar [al-Anwar], the book written by Allama Muhammad Baqir Majlisi (r.a.) in 110 volumes, in which you bring this tradition regarding the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem, and especially this verse of Surah Al-A'raf. You bring this Hadith in this book that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said regarding 'As-siratalladhi qala Iblis'—the path that Iblis was mentioning or mentioning, yes. The one he claimed to God, the path he was pointing towards, then the Imam recites that verse: 'La-aq'udanna lahum siratakal-mustaqim.' Okay? That I will sit on the path and lead Your servants astray, okay? What is meant by this? The Imam says, 'Huwa Aliyyun (a.s.).' Subhan Allah. That Amirul Momineen (a.s.) is the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem. Sirat-e-Mustaqeem (a.s.) means now those who believe in his Wilayah, those who love him, those who have affection for him, those who have love for him, I will lead them astray. This is Satan's goal. This is Satan's goal, and he has challenged that, 'O Lord of Honor, I will lead the lovers of Amirul Momineen astray.' Jazakallah. This is a Shia book. If you look in the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah as well, because we want to complete our argument in every way, so if you look in the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, okay? Which we want to present before you, we want to present here, 'Shawahid at-Tanzil,' okay? That in this, the Mawla is saying, Imam Baqir (a.s.), "Buniyal-Islamu 'ala khamsin" (Islam is built upon five things). Okay? Which ones? "As-Salah, Az-Zakah, As-Sawm, Al-Hajj, and Al-Wilayah". Okay? You mention these five things: that there is Salah, Zakah, prayer—sorry, Hajj, Sawm, and Hajj, and Wilayah. You mention these five things and then what do you say? "Walam yunada bishay'in kama nudiya bil-wilayah" (And nothing was proclaimed as the Wilayah was proclaimed). That the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not proclaim anything as much as he proclaimed the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Not as much as he proclaimed for Ghadir, okay? And for the Master of Ghadir, for his successor, the proclamation made for Wilayah was not made for any other thing by the Messenger of Allah. And then Imam Baqir (a.s.) says a strange and unique sentence: "Fa-akhadha an-nasu bi-arba'in" (So the people took four things). Out of these five things, they took four, okay? "Wa taraku hadhihi ya'ni al-wilayah" (And they abandoned this, meaning the Wilayah). And they abandoned the Wilayah. So, it means those who had made a promise to Iblis, they put all their strength into trying to end the Wilayah and Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). But Allah is the greatest King, okay? He will not let the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) be destroyed. He will not allow it. Okay? So this was Iblis's goal, okay? And Iblis is disappointed. And defeat did happen, he was defeated, he was defeated, he faced defeat. Okay, but he is not going to sit quietly; he is also doing his work. And we must also keep doing our work, as the Messenger of Allah said that it is obligatory upon every present person to convey this news to the absent. title: Ghaibat Mein Shion Ke Liye Khushkhabri
excerpt: This lecture discusses a narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the spiritual status of believers during the occultation (Ghaibat) of the Imam of the Time. It highlights that the period of concealment is a time when believers are closest to Allah due to their unwavering certainty and constant anticipation of the Imam's reappearance. The discourse emphasizes that Allah maintains the occultation because He knows the hearts of the faithful are free from doubt, making this state a source of divine pleasure.
content:
Janab-e-Mufaddal (r.a.) narrates from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.): 'Qala alayhis-salam: Aqrabu ma yakunu al-ibadu ila Allah-i jalla dhikruhu wa arda ma yakunu idha iftaqadu hujjata Allah-i jalla jalaluhu.' When the Proof of Allah is hidden from the people, at that time the servants of Allah are closest to the Lord of the Worlds, and He is most pleased with them. The Proof is not manifest to them, nor do they know his location, but despite this, they have certainty that the Proof of Allah exists and Allah does not break His promise. 'Fahum fi intizarihi sabahan wa masa'an'—in this state, they wait for his reappearance morning and evening. Therefore, whether the signs are fulfilled or not, the believers must wait for the reappearance morning and evening. Then the Hadith continues, and Allah is most wrathful upon His enemies when His Proof is hidden from them and is not manifest to them. And Allah surely knows that the friends (Awliya) of Allah will never fall into doubt or suspicion. If there were even an atom's worth of possibility [of them doubting], Allah would never have kept His Proof hidden. Not even for the blink of an eye. [Music]

title: Abu Sufiyan Ke Imaan Ki Haqeeqat - Ahle Tasannun Kitaabon Mein
excerpt: This lecture examines the sincerity of Abu Sufyan's conversion to Islam by referencing historical accounts from Sunni scholarly texts. The speaker highlights that Abu Sufyan only accepted Islam under the threat of death during the Conquest of Mecca, rather than through genuine faith. Furthermore, the lecture cites traditions indicating that Abu Sufyan harbored deep-seated malice and doubt regarding the Prophet's mission even after his outward conversion.
content:
In the first verse of Surah Al-Munafiqun, the Lord of Majesty says: 'Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim. Idha ja'akal munafiquna qalu nash-hadu innaka la-Rasulullah.' When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah.' 'Wallahu ya'lamu innaka la-Rasuluhu.' And Allah knows that you are His Messenger. 'Wallahu yash-hadu innal munafiqina lakadhibun.' And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars. Let us see, when it is testified that Abu Sufyan was a believer, a Muslim, and a companion, what was the reality of his Islam? In the famous Sunni book 'Al-Isti'ab fi Ma'rifat al-Ashab', it is found—I am narrating the gist of the tradition—that Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib presented Abu Sufyan to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) after the Conquest of Mecca, granting him safety for his life. At that time, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) told him to recite the Shahadatain, but he started making various excuses there as well. It was absolutely clear that he was neither willing to acknowledge Tawheed (Oneness of Allah) nor willing to testify to the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). He was not willing to testify to the Prophethood. At that time, Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib said to him, 'Woe to you! Either accept faith or your head will be severed right now.' And under those circumstances, Abu Sufyan accepted Islam outwardly after the Conquest of Mecca. This Hadith makes it absolutely clear that Abu Sufyan had not brought faith until the Conquest of Mecca. In fact, despite the insistence of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he was not ready to recite the Kalima. And if he did recite the Kalima, it was only to save his life, not because he had accepted the Oneness of Allah or the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) from his heart. Not only this, Abu al-Hasan, in other Sunni books, we find traditions that make it clear that Abu Sufyan did not accept Islam from his heart. For example, in the Sunni book 'Al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba', there is a tradition that once Abu Sufyan was with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). When he saw people gathered around the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he felt envy in his heart towards the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and said to himself, 'I wish I could gather people against this man again.' Look at how much malice he had in his heart for the Banu Hashim and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Malice gathered in his heart. As soon as he thought this in his heart, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) immediately struck his chest and said, 'May Allah humiliate you! May Allah humiliate you!' Abu Sufyan said, 'I did not believe in your being a Messenger, except for Abu Talib.' Meaning, at that very moment, he was confessing with his own tongue that he had doubts about the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Abu Talib, Abu Talib, Abu Talib...

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 4 | Tafseer of Surah al-Faatiha (Surah # 1) - Part 4
excerpt: This lecture explores the interpretation of 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alameen' through the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The speaker emphasizes Allah's absolute control over sustenance and His constant care for all creations, from inanimate objects to human beings. The session concludes with a profound narration regarding the superiority of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), his family, and his Ummah as revealed to Prophet Musa (a.s.).
content:
Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alameen, Wassalatu Wassalamu ala Sayyidil Mursaleen, Abil Qasim Muhammad, wa ala alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin. Alhamdulillah, I am once again present in your service. A person came to Imam Ali ar-Rida (a.s.) and asked him to tell him about the interpretation of 'Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alameen'. He said, 'My father narrated from my grandfather, and he from Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), and he from Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), and he from his father Imam Husayn (a.s.), that a person came to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and said, 'O Ali, explain the interpretation of Alhamdulillah-i Rabbil Alameen.' Then Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) said, 'All praise is for Allah...' All praise is for Allah, and it is specifically for Him that He introduced His community to His servants in this humble way, because people have gathered according to the attainment of the new moon. The reason for this is that God's blessings are so numerous that they cannot be counted. God Himself has pointed towards the blessings, as God has said before that His blessings are so many that they cannot be counted. Allah commanded people to say, and we say on behalf of all the people of the world, that Allah has control over all the creations of His servants. Whether it relates to inanimate objects, guests, or animals, He keeps them according to His power, keeps them in motion, provides them with their sustenance to eat, keeps them in His own protection, and fulfills their needs according to His wisdom. And God's blessing upon inanimate objects is that He prevents them from falling by His power, and prevents the falling inanimate objects from colliding, and prevents the sky from falling onto the earth, and without His permission, upon the earth... ...and without His permission, upon the earth, and the earth from shaking, and it cannot move without His command. And He is kind and merciful to His servants. Now, how great a matter this is, it is completely according to the Quran. And we worry about sustenance, but the Lord of the Worlds, before we were born, had already arranged for our sustenance, which He provides to us even in our mother's womb. Will He not provide for us in this world? We just need to trust Him. Then He said, 'Allah is the owner and creator of all these things.' And how does Allah provide sustenance? Sometimes they know about the arrival of sustenance, and sometimes they do not even know where the sustenance came from. Every human being can observe this and say that sometimes it happens that we do not know where the sustenance is coming from, but sometimes the Lord of the Worlds gives such a command that it increases, it suddenly increases. We do not even know where our sustenance increased from, where it came from. Who does this? The Lord of the Worlds does this. The sustenance that has been destined will definitely reach us in this world. ...will definitely reach us. No matter what kind of deeds a person does, the arrival of sustenance is a part of a person's life. Being a part of it is not a wrong thing, but it has no connection with the path of deeds. God cannot increase the sustenance of a pious person, and no one can remove the sustenance of a needy person. There is a curtain between the seeker and the one who achieves development, which is known as death. If any person among you wants to run away from his sustenance, he will search for it, and just as death searches for him, it will find him. Now, how important this is! Respected viewers, ponder over how the Lord of the Worlds determines our sustenance. Allah Ta'ala says, 'Say that all praise is for Allah, because He has made arrangements for us, and before our arrival, He had already made arrangements for our sustenance.' Therefore, blessings should be upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and it is the duty of their followers to thank God for His favors. Because as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, when Allah made Musa bin Imran a prophet... ...when Allah made Musa bin Imran a prophet, it is a very important narration. Respected viewers, this is a very important narration, one should listen to it and act upon it, and thank God abundantly. He has given us many favors. What is it? When Allah made Musa bin Imran a prophet and asked him, and He granted him miracles, that He made a path for him in the sea and saved the Children of Israel, and He granted him the Torah and Allah's favors, then Hazrat Musa (a.s.) felt that he had a very high status in the eyes of God. So he prayed in the court of God, 'O Lord, You have granted me such status that perhaps You have not granted anyone before me.' And Allah Ta'ala said, 'O Musa, do you not know that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the best of all My creations?' Then Musa (a.s.) asked, 'O Lord, if Muhammad is the most honorable among all creations, then is there any prophet among his family who is better than me?' Then He said to him, 'Yes, the family of Muhammad will be...' ...the family of Muhammad will be. Allah said, 'O Musa, just as Muhammad is superior to all the messengers, in the same way, his family will be superior to the families of all the messengers.' Now, once again, Hazrat Imam Hussain (a.s.) remembered that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to his Ummah, 'Is my Ummah superior to the Ummah of any other prophet?' 'He shaded my Ummah with clouds, and You sent down Manna and Salwa upon them, and You split the sea for them.' Allah said, 'O Musa, do you not know that the Ummah of Muhammad is as superior to the Ummah of other prophets as Muhammad himself is superior to all creations?' Now, he asked, 'O Lord, can I see them?' Allah revealed to him and said, 'O Musa, you will never be able to see them, and if you do not see them, it is not possible. However, you will see them in Paradise, you will see them in the Gardens of Eden and the palaces, Muhammad and those people will be there, and they will be in the palaces of Paradise, you will want to hear their speech...' ...you will want to hear their speech.' 'O Lord, I would love to hear it.' Respected viewers, the Lord of the Worlds has granted this to the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). title: Shaikh Mufeed (a.r.) Ko Mufeed Naam Kaise Mila? | Ek Tareekhi Munaazera | Ghadeer Aur Jamal
excerpt: This lecture recounts the historical incident behind how the renowned Shia scholar Sheikh al-Mufid earned his title. It details a debate between Sheikh al-Mufid and the Mu'tazili scholar Qadi Abd al-Jabbar regarding the Hadith of Ghadir and the Battle of Jamal. Through his sharp logic and mastery of theological reasoning, Sheikh al-Mufid silenced his opponent, leading the Qadi to declare him 'al-Mufid' (the Benefactor).
content:
From the beginning of Islam until today, whoever has followed the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) possessed the quality of being brave and never fearing anything. Today, I want to present to you an example of such a scholar, a prominent and powerful personality, a very famous figure in history who had no concept of fear in his heart. And that was Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nu'man al-Ukbari, known as Sheikh al-Mufid (ridwanullah-e-ta'ala alaih). He was a scholar of the fourth century, passing away in 413 AH. He was a great scholar, highly educated, and to describe his excellence, it is enough to say that he was the teacher of high-ranking scholars like Sayyid al-Murtada and Sheikh al-Ta'ifa (Sheikh al-Tusi), and a student of the great Muhaddith, Sheikh al-Saduq. A great personality, Sheikh al-Mufid. Today, I present to you the story of why he was called 'al-Mufid' (the Benefactor). There are two different narrations for this. I will present one of them to you, which is famous, and who narrated this? The late Qadi Nurullah Shustari—you know, the Shahid-e-Salis, a famous personality. He wrote the book 'Majalis al-Mu'minin'. He narrated this event, and it is worth noting. It is a very interesting story. Sheikh al-Mufid was from Talla Ukbar. Talla Ukbar was in the suburbs of Baghdad. In all of Baghdad, the total Shia population was 1%, and the opposition was dominant. I mean, if the population is 1%, what would the situation be? They would live in fear, they would live suppressed. But this is not the case with Sheikh al-Mufid. Sheikh al-Mufid lived with great bravery and regularly held debates. So much so that even the great scholars of the opposition were afraid to debate Sheikh al-Mufid. One of the great scholars among the opposition, a famous name, Qadi Abd al-Jabbar al-Mu'tazili, wrote a book titled 'al-Mughni' in 20 volumes, and the 20th volume was entirely against the Shias and against Imamate. When that book was published, Sheikh al-Mufid went to his lecture. After arriving, where people were sitting in circles, and his students—great scholars—were also present, Sheikh al-Mufid went and sat at the back. When he finished teaching, Sheikh al-Mufid said, 'Teacher, if you allow me, may I ask a question?' He did not recognize Sheikh al-Mufid by his appearance, but he had heard about him—that there is a young man among the Shias who debates very powerfully and possesses great knowledge and virtue. Sheikh al-Mufid said, 'If you allow me, may I ask a question?' He said, 'Ask.' He said, 'This Hadith: "Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyyun mawlahu" (Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla), which the Messenger of Allah said at Ghadir-e-Khumm, is it authentic?' He said, 'Yes, yes, certainly it is correct, the Hadith is authentic, and all scholars have accepted it.' The second question: 'So what does "Mawla" mean here?' He said, 'Mawla means Awla, meaning the one who holds the most priority, the top priority, the number one.' Sheikh al-Mufid said, 'Meaning, whoever is after this, then he will be after him?' He said, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'So this was said about Ali?' He said, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'So how did it happen in history that Ali was delayed and others were prioritized?' He immediately realized that this was a Shia youth. He said, 'Son, look, it is not like that. The Hadith you are narrating is a Riwayah (narration), and what happened in history is Dirayah (historical reality/reasoning). So when there is a conflict between Riwayah and Dirayah, Dirayah is preferred over Riwayah. Dirayah is accepted, and Riwayah is set aside. Therefore, what happened was correct. The Hadith is correct in its place, but accept what happened in history.' He said, 'Okay, teacher, if you are saying it, then it must be correct.' Then Sheikh al-Mufid said, 'Teacher, one more question.' He said, 'Is this Hadith correct, that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.): "Ahribuka harbi wa silmuka silmi" (O Ali, your war is my war and your peace is my peace)?' 'Is this correct, authentic?' He said, 'Yes, absolutely correct, it is authentic.' The second question: 'Whoever fights the Prophet, does he remain within the fold of Islam or does he exit the fold of Islam?' He said, 'Certainly, he exits the fold of Islam.' He said, 'So those who came to fight Ali (a.s.) in the Battle of Jamal, did these Muslims die, or did they die outside the fold of Islam?' He said, 'No, son, it is not like that. It is found in narrations that those people repented and died in a state of repentance, so they died as Muslims.' He said, 'Just now you said that what happened in history is Dirayah, and if a Riwayah comes in conflict with it, the Riwayah is set aside. So here, the Riwayah you are speaking of, set the Riwayah aside and accept the Dirayah of what happened. This means whoever came against Ali died outside the fold of Islam.' Now he had no answer, he became silent. He started looking at Sheikh al-Mufid and said, 'Ma ismuka? What is your name?' Sheikh al-Mufid said, 'Ana Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nu'man. I am Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nu'man al-Ukbari.' He said, 'Come here.' He called him to himself, sat him on his own seat, on his own chair, and said, "Anta al-Mufid haqqan, anta al-Mufid haqqan, anta al-Mufid haqqan" (You are truly the Benefactor, you are truly the Benefactor, you are truly the Benefactor). Truly, you are Mufid, truly you are a scholar.' So as soon as he said that, the people who were his supporters present there, the students who were present, all started to become agitated, saying, 'What are you doing, teacher? You are sitting a Rafidi in your place and saying like this, "Anta al-Mufid haqqan"—you are truly Mufid, you are truly Mufid, you are truly Mufid—what are you doing?' So Qadi Abd al-Jabbar said, 'Silence! If anyone has an objection to my words or my action, then this Sheikh is present; if any of you have the strength, then ask him a question.' It is written that there was a silence, everyone in the gathering became quiet, and after a while, the gathering was dismissed. And what can I say? These were individuals in whom the spirit of Wilayah was so intense that no one could estimate it. Meaning, these people were drowned in the love of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), and apart from this, they didn't look at anything else. For them, the only goal and purpose of life was the support of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). Nothing else.

title: Imam Reza (a.s.) Ka Maqaam | Anwaar-e-Reza (a.s.) | Online Quiz 2025
excerpt: This lecture celebrates the auspicious birth and divine status of Imam Ali ibn Musa ar-Riza (a.s.). It details his lineage, the significance of his title 'Rida', and the miraculous characteristics that distinguish an Imam appointed by Allah from human-appointed leaders. The session concludes with anecdotes demonstrating the Imam's profound knowledge and his compassionate response to the needs of his followers.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And blessings be upon the Master of the Age. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. On behalf of the TSR team, we present congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of Imam Murtaza, Sayyidul Murtaza, the light of the eyes of the Prophet, the Imam of the believers, Abul Hassan Ali ibn Musa ar-Riza (a.s.). And let us all together present our congratulations on this joyous occasion in the court of the Masumeen (a.s.) through a Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wa ahlik a'da'ahum ajma'in. Respected viewers, the auspicious birth of our master and leader, Imam Riza (a.s.), took place on the 11th of Dhu al-Qi'dah, 148 AH, in Medina Munawwara. Your father's name is Imam Kazim (a.s.), who is our seventh Imam, and your mother's name is Janabe Najma Khatoon (s.a.). You spent 55 years in this apparent world, and your period of Imamate was 20 years, and your martyrdom took place in the last days of the month of Safar in a village in Khorasan called Sanabad, which is also known as Tus. Imam... It is narrated from Sadiq (a.s.) that when Allah (s.w.t.) sent the punishment of the flood during the time of Prophet Nuh (a.s.), the entire world was drowned in water except for four places, and one of those four places was Tus. Imam Rida (a.s.) has many titles: Rida, Sadiq, Sabir, Fazil, Qurrat Ayn al-Mu'minin, and others. But among all of these, the most famous is 'Rida'. There is an interesting incident regarding this in the narrations. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti asked Imam Muhammad Taqi (a.s.): 'Some of your opponents say that this title of your father was given by Ma'mun because he was pleased with him as his successor.' The Imam (a.s.) replied: 'Kadhaba (They lie), by Allah, they lie. They are wicked. Rather, Allah (Azza wa Jall) gave him this title because he was the most beloved to Allah in the heavens, and the most beloved to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the Imams (a.s.) after him on earth.' Then the narrator asked: 'Were your ancestors not pleased with Allah and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)?' And the Imam (a.s.) replied: 'Certainly, they were pleased.' The narrator then asked: 'Why was this title given only to your father?' Imam Jawad (a.s.) replied: 'Because those among his enemies who were his opponents were pleased with him just as his supporters and those who loved him were pleased with him, and this was not the case for his ancestors. That is why, among all of them, he alone became known by the title of Rida.' Now, let us discuss some of the virtues and merits of Imam Rida (a.s.). But before that, it is necessary to know what characteristics and signs Imam Rida (a.s.) himself mentioned regarding the Imam chosen by Allah. It is necessary to know this so that it becomes clear what the difference is between an Imam appointed by Allah and a ruler appointed by people. Imam Rida (a.s.) says: 'An Imam has certain signs: he is the most knowledgeable among the people, the most wise among the people, and the most pious and God-fearing among the people.' He is the most patient and forbearing among the people, the bravest among the people, the most generous among the people, and the most devoted in the worship of Allah among the people. The birth of the Imam (a.s.) is pure and holy. He does not need these physical eyes to see; he is aware of everything. Just as he sees in front of him, he sees behind him as well. He has no shadow. As soon as the Imam steps into this world, he recites the Shahadatain in a loud voice. He remains pure and holy at every moment. Even if his eyes are closed, he remains awake. He is a 'Muhaddath', meaning angels speak to him. The armor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) fits his body. His fragrance is better than musk. He is more entitled to the people than their own selves, and he is more compassionate and kind than their parents. He is the most obedient to Allah among the people, meaning he is the one who acts most upon what Allah has commanded, and he is the strongest in abstaining from the things Allah has forbidden. His prayer is answered; even if he were to curse a stone, it would break into two pieces. He possesses the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and his sword is Zulfiqar. He has a scroll (Sahifa) in which the names of all his Shias who will come until the Day of Judgment are present. He has a scroll in which the names of all his enemies who will come until the Day of Judgment are also present. He has 'Al-Jami'ah', which is a scroll 70 cubits long, containing the knowledge of all the needs of the children of Adam. He has 'Al-Jafr al-Akbar' and 'Al-Asghar', which are written on goat skin and sheep skin. In this scroll, all sciences are present. Even the compensation for a slight scratch, a small injury, half an injury, or a third—every kind of ruling is present in it. He possesses the Mus'haf of Janabe Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). Respected viewers, a person from the progeny of Janabe Ja'far Tayyar (a.s.) narrates: 'I was with Imam Rida (a.s.) in his garden, and at that time, I saw a bird come before Imam Rida (a.s.). It began to chirp loudly in a state of agitation and restlessness and flew here and there.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'Do you know what this bird is saying?' I replied: 'Allah, His Messenger, and the son of the Messenger know best.' The Imam (a.s.) said: 'This bird is saying that there is a snake that wants to eat my small chicks. My small chicks are in the nest.' So the Imam ordered me to take this stick and go and kill that snake. So, upon the Imam's command, when I entered that house, I found it exactly as Imam Rida (a.s.) had said. And then I saw that snake crawling, and I killed it. So, respected viewers, this is the difference between an Imam made by humans and an Imam chosen by Allah—that he not only knows the language of humans but also the language of all birds and animals, and not only does he know the language, but he also solves difficulties. Rayyan ibn Salt says: 'When I intended to go to Iraq, I thought I would take leave of Imam Rida (a.s.). I thought in my heart that when I take leave of him, I would ask him for his shirt so I could make it my shroud, and some dirhams so I could make rings for my daughters.' Then he says: 'When I took leave of him, in my grief and weeping, I forgot my needs. Then, as I was walking out of his house, he called out to me: "O Rayyan, come back." I returned. The Imam (a.s.) said: "Do you not want me to give you a shirt so you can make it your shroud, and some dirhams so you can make rings for your daughters?" O my Mawla, these things were in my heart; in the grief of parting from you, I forgot these things.' Then the Imam (a.s.) lifted his pillow, from under which he took out a shirt and gave it to me. And then the Imam (a.s.) lifted the corner of the prayer mat, from under which he took out some dirhams and gave them to me, and when I counted them, they were 30 dirhams. Respected viewers, we learn from this incident that it is incumbent upon us to ask for all our small and big needs from our Imam (a.s.). Imam Naqi (a.s.) says: 'If you have any need, just move your lips; surely the answer will come.' O Allah, I beseech You by the sake of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.), and especially Imam Rida (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) so that until now we have been speaking to him in his absence, after his reappearance we may meet him directly and ask for our needs. Amin, Ya Rabb al-Alamin.

excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual mechanism behind human memory and forgetfulness as explained by Imam Hasan (a.s.). The Imam describes the human heart as a vessel covered by a lid that obscures knowledge. By reciting complete Salawat upon Prophet Muhammad and his Ahlulbayt, this cover is removed, allowing the heart to shine and memory to be restored. Conversely, neglecting or incomplete Salawat causes the heart to remain covered and darken, leading to the loss of knowledge.
content:
When sitting, someone asked a question, that you, according to yourself, tell me about a person, how he remembers something, and how that person forgets something. Then, God has two things, this is called Divine Gift Knowledge, it shines in the heart, the second is the Divine Gift Power, which God keeps. Once, Prophet Musa (a.s.) came to Ali (a.s.) and asked a few questions. Ali (a.s.) told Hasan (a.s.), 'Son, you answer their questions.' And many questions were asked by the Prophet to Ali (a.s.), but I would like to draw your attention to one question. This is a very interesting question. Someone asked, 'Tell me about a person, how he remembers something, and how that person forgets something?' So, in response, the Imam said that the human heart is an empty vessel, a container, inside which there is a cover, a lid, it is kept covered. When a human sends Salawat upon Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)... When a human sends Salawat upon Muhammad and Ale Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), then that covering, that lid, the thing that was on the heart, is removed. It is removed, the heart shines, and then the thing the human had forgotten, he remembers. This happens because of Salawat. But if he does not do this, because he asked two questions, how does he remember and how does he forget? Here, the Imam (a.s.) says that if he did not do this, if that person did not recite Salawat, or recited it incompletely, did not include the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) in the complete Salawat, if he did not send Salawat upon Ale Muhammad (a.s.), then what will happen? The heart is inside, on which there is a cover, which has been kept covered, it will remain covered, it will keep getting darker, and then the thing the human remembered, he will also forget. To know more interesting things about the life of Imam Musa (a.s.), watch our upcoming videos, subscribe to our channel, and click the subscribe button given in the description of this video.

title: Agar Ye Chaahte Ho To Quran Padho (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound spiritual significance of the Quran as emphasized by the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali. It presents the Quran as a source of divine guidance, protection against Satan, and a means to achieve a fortunate life and honorable death. The speaker encourages believers to reflect upon, recite, and seek healing through the verses of the Holy Quran.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'And if you want the life of the fortunate, the death of the martyrs, and want to be under the shade on the Day of Judgment, and want guidance on that day when the sun will be close, then learn the Quran, for it is the speech of the Merciful God, and a protection against Satan, and a cause for the weight of your deeds on the Day of Judgment.' And Mawla Ali (a.s.) advises his companions, 'Learn the Quran, for it is the best speech, and reflect upon it as much as possible, for it is the spring of hearts, seek healing from it, for it is the healing for the hearts, and recite it in the best manner, for it is the most beneficial recitation.' Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the Imams (a.s.) have spoken the truth.

title: Imam Ali (a.s.) Ki Wasiyyat | Will of Imam Ali (a.s.) [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the profound final testament (Wasiyyat) of Imam Ali (a.s.) addressed to his sons, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn, and all his followers. The speaker highlights key moral directives, including the importance of piety, social responsibility, and maintaining family ties. The lecture concludes by emphasizing the Imam's extraordinary sense of justice, even regarding his own assassin, Ibn Muljam.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us and do not let us perish. Although Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (a.s.) gave this will to both his sons, Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Husayn (a.s.), it was not just for his sons. Rather, acting upon the will of Mawla Ali (a.s.) is the responsibility of every one of his followers. Mawla says, 'I advise you both to maintain piety (Taqwa) of Allah and never run after the world, even if the world runs after you. Never grieve over the loss of anything in this world. Always speak the truth and act for the Hereafter. Always oppose the oppressor and be a helper to the oppressed.' After this, Mawla says, 'I advise you both, all my children, my family, and whoever this message of mine reaches, all of you to adopt the piety of Allah.' Meaning, fear Allah and organize your affairs. Improve the relationships among yourselves. Because I have heard your noble grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), saying that maintaining mutual relationships is generally better than prayer and fasting. Fear Allah regarding orphans. Never let them reach the point of starvation, and may it not happen that they are ruined before your eyes. For the sake of Allah, take special care of your neighbors because your Prophet advised you regarding them, and he used to advise so much regarding neighbors that we began to think he might even include them in the inheritance. Fear Allah regarding the Holy Quran. May others not get ahead of you in acting upon it. For the sake of Allah, be steadfast in prayer because it is the pillar of religion. Fear Allah regarding His House, that as long as you live, do not let it remain empty. Because if it is abandoned, you will not be forgiven. Fear Allah regarding striving in His way with your wealth, your lives, and your tongues. It is incumbent upon you to maintain relationships with each other and keep helping one another, and beware of turning your faces away from each other and severing ties. Never abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil, otherwise, evil-minded people will be imposed upon you, and then even if you pray, your prayer will not be answered. Then Mawla gave a special will regarding his killer, Ibn Muljam (la'natullah alaih), which is the height of justice that no ruler in this world can reach. Mawla says, 'O sons of Abd al-Muttalib! I should never see you raising the slogan and shedding the blood of Muslims saying that Amir al-Mu'minin has been killed. Beware! Do not kill anyone in exchange for my blood except my killer.' Look, if I die from this strike of his, then answer his one strike with only one strike, and do not mutilate his body. Because I have heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) saying, 'Beware! Do not even cut the hands and feet of a biting dog.' Sadaqa Mawlana Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Indeed, my Mawla Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) has spoken the truth. O Allah! By the sake of that just government of the Master of the Universe, hasten the luminous reappearance of Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), so that he may establish complete justice in this entire universe, and grant us the ability to act upon this will of our Mawla. Amin, O Lord of the Worlds.

content:
Our topic today is Mawla Ali (a.s.) and the heights of worship. Traditions state that he used to fast during the day and pray all night, performing a thousand rak'ahs of prayer every single night. A person once said, 'I came to Ali (a.s.) with the intention of observing his worship, just to see how he worships.' Therefore, let us ask the Holy Quran, the book in which Allah (s.w.t.) has hidden the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). In fact, the Quran appears to be reciting a eulogy for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). I found that you are worthy of being worshipped, therefore I worship you. What can one say, Subhan Allah! This is worship in the eyes of the Master of the Universe and how it should be performed. title: Ep#14 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Se Mulaaqaat - Sach Ya Afsaana?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the apparent contradiction between the Tawqi of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) forbidding claims of meeting him during the Major Occultation and the numerous accounts of such meetings recorded by reliable scholars. The speaker clarifies that the Imam's decree warns against false claimants who spread deviant beliefs rather than denying the possibility of genuine encounters. The talk emphasizes that while meetings are rare and dependent on divine will, they serve as a source of spiritual guidance and correction for the believers.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider, Haider. Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan. Ya Ibn al-Hasan, Ya Ibn al-Hasan. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And blessings be upon you, O Guardian of the Age, assist us. Greetings, viewers. We, from 'The Strong Rope', have brought answers to the objections specifically related to Imam Mahdi (a.s.). As Imam Mahdi (a.s.) stated in a letter to his final deputy, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, that after six days you will pass away, and after you, there will be no special deputy of mine. And whoever claims to have met me before the emergence of the Sufyani and the heavenly call, that person is a liar. Viewers, on one side is the Imam's (a.s.) Tawqi (signed decree), and on the other side are the reports from reliable scholars who have presented accounts of meeting the Imam (a.s.), such as in 'Jannat al-Ma'wa', where Muhaddith Nuri has brought one hundred accounts of meetings with the Imam. Another is 'Tafsir al-Wali' by Sayyid Hashim Bahrani, in which accounts of meetings are present. Now, how should these two contradictory things be analyzed? On one side is the Imam's Tawqi, where the Imam is stating that whoever makes this claim is a liar, and on the other side are reliable scholars whose accounts we cannot deny. If we deny the Imam's statement, it means disbelief, and if we deny the words of reliable scholars, it is against our intellect and conscience. If we look at the Imam's Tawqi, it does not deny the possibility of meetings; rather, it warns against false claimants of meetings during the Major Occultation. In this situation, we need to see how to understand a false claim, and to understand this, we need a little reflection. If someone claims to meet Imam (a.s.) and brings with them beliefs that are against the Quran and Hadith, then we should understand that their claim is false. Otherwise, people have propagated many false beliefs in the name of glad tidings. If we look at the reality of the Occultation, we will find that 'yaraunahu wa la ya'rifunahu' (they see him but do not recognize him); people see the Imam but do not recognize him. People are familiar with his essence, but they do not know where their Imam is today. Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), during his own blessed life, kept the Imam hidden from people, except for his chosen companions. When the martyrdom of the Imam (a.s.) occurred, these veils increased, and it remained limited only to the Imam's four special deputies. There are only a few such chosen individuals who had the honor of meeting the Imam. Only the Imam's name and his personality are hidden from people, and we have many proofs and accounts to prove this. There are three possibilities for meeting the Imam. First, meeting the Imam without knowing that we have met the Imam. Second, realizing after meeting Imam Mahdi (a.s.) that we have met the Imam of the time. And third, meeting the Imam and realizing during the conversation that this is the Imam of the time. Such accounts are very few, and the reason for this is that during the Occultation, these accounts have been kept hidden. Through such accounts, we realize how much we need the Imam (a.s.). The Imam is greatly needed to run the religion and take hold of its reins. Through such accounts, we realize how much we need the existence of the Imam and how much we benefit from him. The presence of the Imam is essential to hold the reins of religion, and the purpose of these meetings is to save the believers from oppression and grief and to keep people on the Straight Path. Just as the account of Ali ibn Mahziyar's meeting with the Imam (a.s.) is very famous. When Ali ibn Mahziyar met the Imam (a.s.) after a long period, he said that there was no one to bring me to you. In response to which the Imam (a.s.) said, 'The reality is not what you are saying; rather, you were busy accumulating wealth, treating poor believers with arrogance, and severing ties with your close relatives.' In this way, the Imam (a.s.) guided him and, through him, guided us. This account and all such accounts where people met the Imam (a.s.) have the central figure, i.e., the focus, as the sacred essence of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and the guidance and advice reaching us from him, not the individuals who met the Imam. Those individuals are the means for these instructions to reach us, and in the period of Occultation, this meeting is only possible when the permission of the Lord and the will of the Imam are included. If we conclude our brief discussion, it is proven that meeting the Imam (a.s.) in this period of Occultation is not impossible. As far as the Imam's Tawqi is concerned, it is to warn people so that no one can spread false beliefs in the religion. And blessings be upon you, O Guardian of the Age, assist us. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance. O Ibn al-Hasan. The Shia have no one but you. We have fallen, Master, help us. We have only you. title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Ke Noor Se Kya Khalq Hua? | From Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz 2023
excerpt: This lecture explores the metaphysical status of Imam Hasan (a.s.) by referencing traditions regarding his divine light. It explains that the sun and moon were created from portions of his light, which itself originates from the light of Allah. The speaker emphasizes the superiority of Imam Hasan (a.s.) over celestial bodies and warns against arrogance in his presence.
content:
The tradition states that Allah divided the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.) into parts, and from those parts, He created the sun and the moon. Allah is creating the moon and the sun from his light. The tradition continues, saying that the light of the moon and the sun is from the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.), and the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.) is from the light of Allah. Look at the wording of the tradition: 'Hasan is the moon and the sun.' That is why Imam Hasan (a.s.) is superior to the moon and the sun. If anyone tries to show off their wealth or pride before him, they should remember that the moon and the sun were created in his service, and he is superior to them.
Allah divided the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.) to create the sun and moon.
The light of the sun and moon is derived from the light of Imam Hasan (a.s.).
The light of Imam Hasan (a.s.) originates directly from the light of Allah.
