title: Majlis 5 | Marefat-e-Nooraaniyyah (Part-4) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual significance of Azadari and the essential nature of Wilayah within the context of the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse emphasizes the primordial covenant made in Alam-e-Dharr and how human forgetfulness necessitates the guidance of the Ahlul-Bayt as the gate to divine knowledge. By examining the sacrifices of the family of Abu Talib and the patience of Janab-e-Zainab, the lecture underscores the importance of aligning one's worship and obedience with the divine will of Allah.
content:
Emerging from the lips, the Adhan is being called, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. Emerging from the lips, the Adhan is being called, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. Akbar has not even gone to the battlefield yet, Akbar's heart is still inside his chest. Akbar has not even gone to the battlefield yet, Akbar's heart is still inside his chest. But still, the tip of the spear is weeping, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. O you who were raised with affection, just wait a while, so that Zainab can decorate the wedding garland on your head. O you who were raised with affection, just wait a while, so that Zainab can decorate the wedding garland on your head. Because the mother of Aun and Muhammad is weeping, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. The Prophet watches this scene from the heavens, all the worshippers in the rows are restless. Sobbing is weeping while holding the Imamate, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. Emerging from the lips, the Adhan is being called, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. There in Medina, Sugra is weeping, here Sakina has a thirst on her lips. One sister is weeping here, another there, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. Emerging from the lips, the Adhan is being called, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. Laila is praying in Karbala, may death not come to my Akbar, my God. She is weeping while sobbing, Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. Akbar has departed from Medina, and his footprints are left upon the earth. His sister is watching and becoming restless; Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. The Adhan is echoing from his lips, and Akbar's mother is weeping on the prayer mat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad. May Allah have mercy on the one who recites Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome is for the righteous and those of certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. May Allah bless him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, our Imam of the time, our guardian of affairs, our master, our lord, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our intimate friend, the fortified cave, and the succor of the distressed and the helpless, my soul and... Lord of the worlds, to Him be the sacrifice. Thereafter, our master and our leader, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.), said: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn has wounded our eyelids and caused our tears to flow; so let the weepers weep for the likes of Husayn.' Truthful is our master and leader, Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.). Peace and blessings. The hadith which I have made the title of this series of gatherings, in that hadith, Imam Rida (a.s.) says: 'Indeed, the day of Husayn has wounded our eyelids and caused our tears to flow.' Certainly, the day of Husayn, meaning the grief of Husayn—the grief of Husayn has wounded our eyelids, meaning by weeping continuously, the Imam's eyelids became wounded, his eyes became wounded. And he says, 'caused our tears to flow,' and tears flow continuously from our eyes; there is a constant stream of tears. 'So let the weepers weep for the likes of Husayn.' If anyone is to weep, they should weep for Husayn, weep for the sake of Husayn. And truly, this Azadari (mourning), this weeping and lamenting, is a very great blessing. That is, of all the sustenance that Allah has bestowed upon His servants, the most important sustenance is this Azadari, because this Azadari contains virtues (faza'il), merits (manaqib), guardianship (wilayah), and disavowal (bara'at). Look, if you reflect, everything is present in it. There is no aspect of worship that is not present in it. In Ziyarat Ashura, you recite this, don't you? You say in the Ziyarat that Allah has given us the sustenance of Bara'at (disavowal of enemies). That is, Allah has favored us by giving us the sustenance of Tabarra. Tabarra is a sustenance. And you know that the distribution of all worldly sustenance is such that Allah does not give equally to everyone. Everyone, whatever the sustenance may be—whether material or spiritual—look, if we talk about material sustenance, that is, material wealth, Allah does not make everyone wealthy. Worldly sustenance is such that Allah gives a lot of wealth even to His enemies; He gives them a great deal. And He tells the believers, 'Do not cast your eyes toward them.' Sometimes, as an exception, He gives some to the believers, and He has mentioned this in the Quran as well. And He gives it because Allah says in the Quran that if We do not give anything to the believers, the believers will say, 'What is the benefit of having faith?' This is a verse of the Quran. And that is why He gives to some believers as an exception. Similarly, take any sustenance; Allah does not give equally to everyone. For example, the sustenance of health, the sustenance of the body—these are all material sustenance. Similarly, there is spiritual sustenance, and among spiritual sustenance, the most important is the sustenance of Wilayah and Bara'at. If someone receives the sustenance of Wilayah and Bara'at, then no greater wealth has been given to them. And that is why it is found in the hadith that if someone receives these things and imagines that someone else has received something better, then he has declared the small to be great and the great to be small. Therefore, it is very important to know its value. So, Wilayah and Bara'at are both very important; they are the most important spiritual sustenance. And this gathering, this Azadari, is the Azadari of the Master of Martyrs (Sayyid al-Shuhada), which Lady Zaynab (s.a.) established. Its style became this—the style—and it happened from the beginning. It is not that we determined the curriculum of this gathering. The curriculum of the gathering was determined by Lady Zaynab from the very first day. When Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) gave the sermon, he first recited the virtues (faza'il) and then the tragedies (masa'ib). The curriculum—who determined the syllabus of the gathering? Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.). 'I am the son of Makkah and Mina, I am the son of Medina and Marwa.' He stated his own virtues: 'I am the son of Zamzam and Safa,' and in this way, he recited all the virtues. And after reciting all the virtues, the turn for the tragedies came. So, this curriculum was determined by the Family of Muhammad (a.s.). You look at any of the sermons of the Family of Muhammad; you see that after stating the virtues, they stated the tragedies. And this should be the standard. This gathering is for these virtues and tragedies. Right now, many people here say that some Islamic rulings (ahkam) should also be stated, and this should also be done. It is correct; we do not say it should not be done. That is fine, but most people here come for 10 days, attend the gathering for 10 days. These are just 10 days. Now, if you want or think that we should teach the entire Tawdih al-Masa'il (book of rulings) or teach them all the books of rulings, then this is not very appropriate. We do not say it is wrong, but you should teach them rulings throughout the year. It is a very good thing; it should be taught. It is obligatory, necessary, and you should state other things as well. But these 10 days of Muharram, especially—the rest of the gatherings can be like that, but these 10 days, especially, should be for the virtues of the Family of Muhammad (a.s.) and the tragedies of the Family of Muhammad. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Now, this is necessary so that we take these virtues to the level where people truly become acquainted, where people truly know who the Family of Muhammad are. And that is why this is the series of 'Ma'rifat bin Nuraniyah' (Recognition through Light). Yesterday, I also submitted in your service that the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) said that it is mentioned in the Quran: '(Indeed, it is difficult except for the humble).' That is, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, this is very difficult. Indeed, this is very difficult, '(except for the humble).' And 'Ha'—meaning only the prayer—the Master of the Universe says, 'Patience' means the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and 'Prayer' means our Wilayah, the Wilayah of the Family of Muhammad. And this is very difficult. 'Kabira' means very difficult, very hard. This Wilayah is '(except for the humble),' except for those who are humble before the Family of Muhammad (a.s.). Now, the Master says this, and the Master gives the proof that you will see that all Muslims are in agreement on the Messengership and Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah, but when it comes to my Wilayah and the Wilayah of my family, they all turn their faces away. The reason is because Allah has not given that capacity (zarf) to everyone. Or this is a matter of capacity. Wilayah is not the religion of those with small capacity. It is for those with capacity. 'Ahle Zarf' (people of capacity)—they say, and because some children are looking, wondering what this is, what is 'Zarf'? 'Zarf' means capacity. That is, Allah does not give this capacity of Wilayah and Bara'at to everyone, and like, for example, the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Now, the Master continues this sermon, extends this sentence, meaning he continues the hadith, and says: 'And Allah the Almighty said in another place in His Noble Book regarding the Prophethood of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and regarding my Wilayah.' And Allah has mentioned it in another place in the Quran as well—that is, in the same verse, He has mentioned the Messengership of the Messenger of Allah and also my Wilayah. And which verse is that? The Master says this is verse number 45 of Surah Al-Hajj, in which Allah the Almighty says: 'And a ruined well and a lofty palace.' This is verse number 45 of Surah Al-Hajj. 'And a ruined well and a lofty palace.' 'Bir'—what is 'Bir'? 'Bir' means a well. The well that has dried up. 'Mu'attala'—'Mu'attala' means, for example, that which is not being used. That is, here 'Bir' refers to whom? The Imam. The Imam is not being turned to. People did not go to the Imam. People abandoned the Imam. People made the Imam 'Mu'attal' (suspended/neglected). People turned their faces away from the Imam. 'Bir Mu'attala.' The Imam says, the Master says, 'I am that well which has been abandoned, which people have left.' People left the mantle of Ali. The Prophet had said, 'And abandon the one who abandons him.' The one who abandons Ali, you abandon him. Do you remember the hadith, the Hadith of Ghadir? 'O Allah, befriend the one who befriends him, and be an enemy to the one who is an enemy to him, and help the one who helps him, and abandon the one who abandons him.' Because the Muslims abandoned the mantle of Ali, therefore Allah abandoned them. And that is why, to this day, they are wandering from door to door, and every day there is a new seminar, a program, about what should be done so that our situation improves. This committee is sitting, and that committee is sitting; nothing will come of that. Nothing will come of that. Well, in this, let me submit one more thing in your service. Now the situation has become so bad these days, look, this is a tragedy; there is no pretense in this. What is the truth is the truth. That the outsiders had abandoned Ali, but today even our own have abandoned him. The attachment that was supposed to be with the Ahlulbayt, that attachment is not happening. The way we were supposed to hold onto the traditions of the Family of Muhammad, to hold onto the hadiths, today we are not doing it. This attachment is very necessary, and this complaint is not ours that we are complaining today. This complaint was written by Sayyid ibn Tawus in his will. Sayyid ibn Tawus was a scholar of the 7th century. Now the 15th century is going on, meaning 800 years ago, Sayyid Radi al-Din ibn Tawus wrote this in his will. In which he said, 'O my son, do not trust the words of those people at all who say, "I am waiting for the Imam of the Time."' He has explicitly written it; you see, read it. Alhamdulillah, it has been translated into Persian, and God willing, if you pray, it will be in other languages too; it is a very good commentary, meaning it is a will. He says, 'Do not trust people who say they are waiting for the Imam of the Time.' How does one wait for the Imam of the Time? He gives an example of that. If a person has a small thing that he loves, if it gets lost—for example, he gives the example of a camel, a camel, meaning in today's age, like a car—if a person's car is stolen, will he sit at home peacefully that the car has been stolen? He will search here and there, 'Brother, where did the car go? Where did it go?' And if it is not found anywhere, he will go and file a complaint with the police, 'My car has been stolen. My car is gone,' and he will keep asking people. Sayyid ibn Tawus says, 'At least people should love the Imam of the Time enough to search for the Imam in this way.' And attachment is very necessary. Anyway, so here the Master gives the example of this verse of Surah Al-Hajj, verse number 45, 'And a ruined well.' They abandoned the 'Bir,' meaning the well. We are that 'Bir,' the Master says. We are that well that has been abandoned. 'And a lofty palace,' and they kept strengthening the 'Qasr.' 'Qasr' means, they say 'Qasr' means the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and they kept reciting his Kalima. 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' So he says that they suspended my Wilayah, 'And they rejected it,' they rejected it even while knowing. And whoever does not acknowledge my Wilayah, whoever does not accept my Wilayah, the acknowledgment of the Prophethood of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) will not benefit him. Just like if someone says, 'I believe in Allah but I do not believe in the Messenger of Allah,' will this belief benefit him? If someone says, 'I believe in all the prophets but I do not believe in the Messenger of Allah,' will this belief benefit him? Similarly, if someone says, 'I believe in the Messenger of Allah but I do not believe in Ali ibn Abi Talib,' then it will not benefit him at all. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Haidari Ya Ali, with a loud voice, recite Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Because they are both linked, because Prophethood and Wilayah are joined together like this. They cannot be separated from each other. Prophethood and Wilayah. The two weighty things (Thaqalayn). The interpretation of Prophethood is the Thaqalayn. The interpretation of Wilayah is the Ahlulbayt. They will never separate from each other until they reach me at the Pond (Hawd). The Master says these two are joined, 'Maqrunan'. This is because the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is a sent Prophet, and he is the Imam of all creation. And Ali (a.s.) is the Imam of all creation after him. Who is the Imam of all creation after the Messenger of Allah? It is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Acknowledge this, accept this. He is the true successor of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). I submitted in the service of the audience that it does not matter if people select anyone they want or accept anyone they choose. It is exactly like if we were to write a book tomorrow and say that we think you should read this instead of the Quran. It is clear, isn't it? So, if any Muslim says, 'Brother, I have brought this book,' would you accept his word? Why would you not? After all, the Quran is a book, and this is also a book; should it not be accepted? You would say, 'No, Astaghfirullah, what are you saying? If you talk like this, you have gone outside the religion of Islam.' Why? Because it is said that this is the Quran, this is the Word of Allah, and therefore, there can be nothing else besides the Quran; there can be no other book. So, just understand in the same way that the Imam who is appointed by Allah is the Hujjatullah (Proof of Allah), the appointed Caliph of Allah; no one else can come and sit in his place. No matter how much they claim, no matter how much they assert, it has no status, no purpose, meaning it has no significance. So, Mawla (a.s.) says, 'Kama qala al-Nabiyyu sallallahu alayhi wa alihi' (As the Prophet himself said), 'Anta minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di' (You are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me). And 'Awwaluna Muhammad, wa awsatuna Muhammad, wa akhiruna Muhammad' (The first of us is Muhammad, the middle of us is Muhammad, and the last of us is Muhammad), and we are all Muhammad. Meaning, we were all born from one light. Meaning, in terms of rank, we are all equal. In terms of rank. Meaning, in terms of excellence, it is obvious that the Messenger of Allah is the most excellent. After him is Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). After him is Janabe Zahra (s.a.), then the Hasanayn (a.s.), and then the other Masumin (a.s.). But collectively, if you say, then all of them are... 'Faman istaqbala ma'rifati' (So whoever receives my true recognition), 'Fahuwa 'ala al-din al-qayyim' (then he is upon the upright religion). Meaning, his religion—this is a verse of the Quran, verse number 30 of Surah Rum. 'Dhalika al-din al-qayyim' (That is the upright religion). This is verse number 30 of Surah Rum. 'Fa-aqim wajhaka lil-dini hanifan fitrata Allahi allati fatara al-nasa 'alayha la tabdila li-khalqi Allahi dhalika al-din al-qayyim.' This is the strong religion. This is the religion that is established upon Tawhid and Wilayah. Look, before moving forward, a gentleman sent a message today asking a question: 'You read in the Majlis that through us, the recognition of Allah is attained, through us, the worship of Allah is performed, and through us, the declaration of Allah's Tawhid comes; so this point was not understood, please clarify it a little.' So, I said, 'InshaAllah, we will clarify it in the Majlis,' so that perhaps he asked the question, and others have not asked it. So, I will clarify it, and we will do it very quickly so that the point is completed and then we can continue with the Hadith. See, giving recognition (Ma'rifah) is only the work of Allah. Sheikh al-Amili (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh) wrote a book on beliefs called 'Isbat al-Hudat'. This book is in six volumes on beliefs—Tawhid, Justice, Prophethood, Imamate, and Resurrection. He wrote this book in six volumes. It is very voluminous and contains only Hadiths, only Hadiths. So, he explained this discussion very well in the light of Hadith and Quran, that when Allah, in the Alam-e-Dharr (World of Atoms), before coming to this world—you know there were many worlds, which are called the world before this one. It has many names and there were many worlds. It was not just one world. Meaning, Alam-e-Ajilla, Alam-e-Ashbah, they have different names. There was a world of light, then there was a world of matter, a world of pure essence. He has described everything, which is not our topic here. There were different worlds that existed before coming to this world. All those worlds are mentioned in the Quran. At least 40 verses of the Quran point towards that world. Not just one or two. Let me present just one verse for your service, one verse so that the point is completed. In that world, Allah made everyone recognize Him. This is verse number 172 of Surah A'raf: 'Wa idh akhadha Rabbuka min bani Adama min zuhurihim dhurriyyatahum' (And remember, O Prophet, when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants). When your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants—when He brought out their entire lineage from Adam's back. Meaning, from the back. He brought everyone out and then took a covenant from them. 'Alastu bi-Rabbikum?' (Am I not your Lord?). 'Qalu bala' (They said, 'Yes'). No one said 'No'. No one said 'No'. Everyone said, 'Yes, You are our God.' Without exception, there was no exception in this. And in the Hadiths, in the light of this verse—meaning this verse continues—'Qalu bala shahidna' (They said, 'Yes, we bear witness' that You are our Lord). 'An taqulu yawma al-qiyamati inna kunna 'an hadha ghafilin' (Lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were unaware of this'). On the Day of Resurrection, when Allah—here in this world, no one asked us. But Allah is mentioning that realm. 'Idh akhadha Rabbuka min bani Adama min zuhurihim dhurriyyatahum' (When your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants), and took the entire proof from them, and then said, 'Alastu bi-Rabbikum? Qalu bala shahidna an taqulu yawma al-qiyamati inna kunna 'an hadha ghafilin.' Then after that, Allah took the declaration of Prophethood, the declaration of Wilayah, and especially of the Imams, Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf). Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. So, when Allah took this declaration from everyone, He gave this recognition to everyone without exception. He gave this recognition to everyone. There was no exception in this. So, whoever came into the world, came with this recognition. Every single person. But it is found in the traditions, in the Hadiths, that 'Nasa-hum al-mawquf' (They forgot the position) or 'Ansa-hum al-mawquf' (The position made them forget). Allah made them forget that position, that scene of introduction. But the recognition remains within them. Recognition is in everyone. But what is the problem? What is the nature of the world itself? The nature of the world is to make one forget. The nature of the world is to make one forget. So, people forgot Allah, the Messenger, and everything. And then they became victims of other things. Meaning, victims of desires, lusts, anger, and sins. In this way, different veils kept falling on their nature due to different victims. Man kept moving away from Allah. That is why Allah sent Prophets one after another, so that they could call them towards Allah. Now, a discussion arises here. This is a very detailed discussion, and it is not even possible to describe it fully here. It requires at least ten days, at least. But just briefly for your service. Now, when the Prophets came, Allah sent the Prophets and the Hujjats of the Prophets—meaning the successors of the Prophets—and then other preachers, the preachers who were supposed to preach, it was everyone's job to invite people towards Allah. To call them towards Allah. Now, Allah set a condition, pay attention to this. He set a condition that whoever obeys the Prophet, whoever obeys the Messenger, whoever obeys the Ulil Amr (those in authority), Allah will give him that recognition again in this world. Wow, wow, wow. The point is this. Recognition was given before, but it was forgotten in the world. Now, the purpose of giving it is only for those who obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and obey the Ulil Amr. 'Ati'u Allaha wa ati'u al-Rasula wa uli al-amri minkum.' Subhan Allah. Subhan Allah. And that is why it is stated in verse number 16 of Surah Jinn: 'Wa allaw istaqamu 'ala al-tariqati la-asqaynahum ma'an ghadaqan' (If they had remained steadfast on the path, We would have surely given them abundant water to drink). Now, look, what is the meaning of this verse? What is the apparent meaning of 'path' and 'water'? 'Ma'an ghadaqan.' Now, what have the commentators—who have it from the Ahl al-Bayt, because it is only with the Ahl al-Bayt—what did they write when they picked up the pen regarding 'path' and 'water'? But when people went to the Ahl al-Bayt and asked what it meant, 'O son of the Messenger, explain the meaning of this verse: "Wa allaw istaqamu 'ala al-tariqati la-asqaynahum ma'an ghadaqan" (If they had remained firm, steadfast, and constant on the path), we would have surely given them abundant water to drink.' The Imam says, 'If they had remained steadfast on the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib, we would have made them so familiar with our Hadiths and our teachings, so familiar, that they would have reached that station.' Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. They would have reached that station of recognition. They would have reached that station where, when the Hadith of Nuraniyah (the Hadith of Light) is read before them, they would not be afraid. No doubt would arise in their hearts. 'What is all this being read? This Hadith is not authentic.' This has been narrated by Allama Majlisi. It is clear, isn't it? Meaning, if one were to go to answer this, there are many answers, but this is not the time. We only have this much. So, there are two types of recognition. Now, these are two types of recognition. One is that which Allah gave in the Alam-e-Dharr. This is also called Alam-e-Dharr, Alam-e-Ajilla, Alam-e-Ashbah, Alam-e-Anwar, Alam-e-Ma-e-Basit. It has different names, it has many names. There are different stages, different meanings. Different worlds. So, all this—this world that existed—in it, Allah introduced Himself. Sheikh al-Amili calls that introduction, which was there which we forgot, 'Ma'rifat-e-Awwaliyah' (First Recognition). Sheikh al-Amili says, 'Ma'rifat-e-Awwaliyah', the first recognition or 'Ma'rifat-e-Ula'. The first recognition, Ma'rifat-e-Ula. Meaning, the first introduction. And in this world, when recognition is given after obeying the Messenger and the Imam, Sheikh al-Amili says, this is 'Ma'rifat-e-Thaniyah' (Second Recognition). Meaning, the second recognition. This is 'Ma'rifat-e-Tarkibi' (Composite Recognition). Now, the point is understood up to here, I tried very hard to summarize and state the point. The second recognition. This is the second recognition, okay? What is the condition for this recognition? Obedience to the Messenger, obedience to the Ulil Amr, then Allah will give it. Okay? Now, what is the meaning of 'Bina Obed Allah, Bina Oref Allah, Bina Wahid Allah'? The meaning of 'Bina Obed Allah, Bina Oref Allah, Bina Wahid Allah' is that if you want to obtain the correct method of recognition, the correct method of worship, the correct method of Tawhid, and hold the correct belief of Tawhid, then go only to those whom Allah has appointed. Only from them will you get the correct method, and you will not get it anywhere else. As I just submitted in the service, you see, to this day, Muslims have not been able to decide where to tie their hands in prayer. These quarrels are happening. And quarrels over various things, over trivial things. Why? What was the reason for that? They have become distant from the door of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). If they had stayed at the door of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), these problems would not have existed at all. So, you see, one performs the entire fast with effort, but breaks the fast before the sun sets. Similarly, there is Hajj. Similarly, there is Khums and Zakat. They do not even have Khums, they have Zakat. Similarly, everything is like that, everything. Because the right (Haq) is not with them. Therefore, it is necessary for a person to go to the door of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). To take from the door of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). Well, this is not just about you and me. Did you and I decide that we have to go to the door of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), did you and I decide? No. The decision is Allah's. And Allah told the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to announce it in very clear words, there should be no doubt in this. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "Ana madinatul-ilmi wa Aliyyun babuha." I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate. "Faman aradal-madinata wal-hikmata fal-yatiha min babiha." Whoever wants the city, whoever wants wisdom, should come through the gate. The Quran had already announced it; it is in a verse of the Quran that look, when you enter houses, enter through the doors. It is not appropriate. It is not appropriate to enter houses from the back. The Quran had already forbidden it, saying that those who jump in from the back are thieves. Whoever comes and enters through the door, only he will receive his right. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced, "Ana madinatul-ilmi wa Aliyyun babuha." Now, if you want to come, then come. Now, obviously, where would the obedience to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and his many virtues be digested? So they started fabricating Hadith, they set up an entire factory. According to the Khatib-e-Akbar, they set up a plant. Entire Hadiths are being fabricated. People are sitting there, one after another. It is not appropriate to take names, but in our Hadith, the names of everyone are present. The names are present, who all were sitting to fabricate Hadith? Who were kept? Who fabricated the most Hadith? That is also written. That is also written in our books. The Imams (a.s.) told us that so-and-so, so-and-so, so-and-so, they fabricated the most. After that, meaning the other people, it is clearly written about them. They were all fabricators of Hadith. Entire Hadiths were fabricated. Entirely, meaning so many, so many that there was no limit or end to them. And if anyone narrated the Hadith of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), they would put him in jail, lash him, and if he did not recant, they would kill him. So people were killed on this pretext if it was discovered that they were spreading the Hadiths of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). This continued for 100 years. From the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) for 100 years, from the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) onwards, meaning from 11 Hijri to 110 Hijri, this continued. So this was a big problem, a very big problem that occurred. Recite another Salawat for Muhammad and Aale-Muhammad. Now, meaning the Ma'rifat (recognition) will only be, remember this point. True Ma'rifat will only be attained by the one who goes to the door of the Hujjat of Allah. The one who goes to the door of the Hujjat of Allah, that Hujjat whom Allah has appointed. That Imam whom Allah has appointed. That Imam whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has appointed. Our will does not work in this, as to what we think. This, what we think, was the thought of Iblis. Iblis said, Allah said to prostrate to Adam. Iblis said, do not tell me to prostrate to Adam, otherwise I will worship You in such a way that neither any Prophet (a.s.) has done, nor any angel has done such worship. No one has done such worship. I will worship You like that. And he had already done it, tremendously. Meaning, one whose every prostration is for thousands of years, when he says that, what concept of worship could he have? But Allah did not accept the worship of even such a servant, and the voice of Truth came immediately. Allah said, "Uridu an u'bada min haithu uridu wa la min haithu turidu." I want to be worshipped as I wish, not as you wish. So it became known that true worship, the real worship, will only be the one that is according to the way shown by the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) and the Imam (a.s.). Nothing else is going to be of any use. So, exactly in this way, worship through us means this, Ma'rifat through us means this, true Tawheed through us means this. If you want true Tawheed, then to whom should you go? Go to the Hujjat of Allah, go to the Aale-Muhammad (a.s.). And if you do not go to them, then you will become the same kind of 'God'—66 feet tall, curly hair, clean-shaven, wearing shoes like this, wearing a gown like this, and that is God. Meaning, you will become a believer in Tajsim and Tashbih (anthropomorphism). Meaning, it is Shirk. Tajsim and Tashbih are Shirk. "La yushbihuhu shay'un." Nothing resembles Allah. Anyway, this was a very important question, that is why it took so much time to answer it. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and Aale-Muhammad. Now, Mawla (a.s.) says that this is the Deen-e-Qayyima. "Sa ubayyinu dhalika bi-awnillahi wa tawfiqi ya Salmanu wa ya Jundab." Now I will explain this to you further, I will clarify this for you. If, meaning with the help of Allah, bi-awnillah, meaning with the help of Allah and the Tawfiq of Allah. Meaning, with the help of Allah included and the Tawfiq of Allah, Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) is saying. O Salman and O Jundab. "Qala labbayka ya Amirul-Mu'minin salawatullahi alayh." They said, "Labbayka ya Amirul-Mu'minin." Now after that, Mawla (a.s.) says, "Kuntu ana wa Muhammadun sallallahu alayhi wa alihi." Recite a Salawat. "Nuran wahida." I and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) were one light when Allah created us. "Nuran wahida." "Min nurillahi azza-wa-jalla." And Allah created our light from His own light. Creating from His own light does not mean that Allah gave something from His own light. No, no. Creating from His own light means that Allah created their light, their light, directly, without any medium. This is the light through which the entire universe came into existence. The whole world came into existence. Today, even if we are sitting here and all the other things, they are all because of this light. How did it come into existence? We are also present because of this light, and all the things in the world are because of this light. This is the light, you understand. And there are many such narrations of ours. And when we say, it is not just among us Shias, but among both sects (Fariqain). Narrations of the opponents are also present. And not one, but many. Many, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi (r.a.) has brought 100 references on this in the volume of Hadith-e-Nur in Abaqatul Anwar, 100 references. Of 100 books. Now see what services our scholars have performed. Value them, value them. Not one or two, but 100, and all authentic. See, Alhamdulillah, we do not have the issue of 'Mawdu'at'. Mawdu'at means the chain of fabricated Hadiths. Because we never had any factory of fabricated Hadiths. It is clear, right? This is, anyway, an entire topic. Insha'Allah, if Allah gives Tawfiq, I will tell you how the chain of fabricating these Hadiths started among them and where it went. That is the whole discussion. Sayyid Ali Shahristani is still alive in Mashhad-e-Muqaddas, he is old and frail now. He is an old man, a very great scholar of religion. He has worked a lot on this topic, Sayyid Ali Shahristani, about the Hadiths, that what happened after the ban was imposed on Hadiths. Anyway, so Mawla (a.s.) says that this light, Allah created the light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and my light from His own light. After that, he says, "Fa-amara Allahu tabaraka wa ta'ala" Allah Tabaraka wa Ta'ala ordered that "An dhalikan-nur" this light be ordered "An yushaqqa" the light was ordered to be divided into two parts. Before, it was only one light. It was only one light. This light was Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and this light was Ali (a.s.). Now Allah said, now be divided into two parts. One became Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and one became Ali (a.s.). So "Ana wa Muhammadun nurun wahidun min nurillahi azza-wa-jalla" then after that "Faqala linnisfi" he said to the half, "Kun Muhammadan" and to the other half he said, "Kun Aliyyan" "Faminha qala rasulullahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi" "Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aale-Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum" Enough, you are tired now. With a Salawat, is it understood? I will not read much more. "Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aale-Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum" Mawla (a.s.) says and the proof for this is. Now see, he also states the proof. It is one light. The proof is that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "Aliyyun minni wa ana min Aliyyin" I am from Ali and Ali is from me. "Wa la yu'addi anni illa Aliyyun" And no one will deliver my message except Ali. Who will deliver it except Ali? And Mawla (a.s.) also states the proof for that. "Wa qad wajjaha Aba Bakrin bi-bara'atin ila Makkah" This is the Shan-e-Nuzul (reason for revelation) of Surah Tawbah. The Shan-e-Nuzul of Surah Tawbah is that when Surah Tawbah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) told him to take it to the Meccans, to the people of Makkah, and announce that this verse has been revealed. And the details of that, which I do not have to state right now, just that go and say it. He had only gone a little distance when Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.), go Ali. Well, I am giving you the reference again. This, its Shan-e-Nuzul, is present in Bukhari, Muslim, Bukhari is present, Muslim is present, but everyone did editing, used scissors. They did it very tremendously. Cut here, cut there, cut there. Readers, read what is written? What do they want to say? But yes, the details are also present. In Tarikh-e-Tabari or Tafsir-e-Tabari, the full detail is present under this verse. So if anyone wants the detail, the full detail is in Tafsir-e-Tabari. Otherwise, the scissors of editing have been used in many places. Of course, there is even more detail in our Hadiths. But there, anyway, I am reading very quickly that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said and after that said, Ali, go and take it. Why? "Nazala Jibra'ilu" because Jibra'il (a.s.) descended and said, "Ya Muhammad" "Qala labbayka" "Qala innallaha ya'muruka" O Muhammad, Allah is ordering you "An tu'addiyaha anta" either you deliver this Surah Bara'at "Aw rajulun minka" or the man who is from you. "Aw rajulun" "Fawajjahani fi istidadi Abi Bakrin faradadtuhu" I went and immediately stopped you on the way, I said brother, bring it, give it, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has told me to go. So Mawla (a.s.) says that "Fawajada fi nafsihi" "Fawajada fi nafsihi" meaning he felt very bad. Anyway, he came back. He said, "Ya Rasulallah, has a Quranic verse been revealed about me? Is that why you called me back?" The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "No, no verse has been revealed. But the command was that no one should deliver this except me or Ali. Only I or Ali." Let us stop here as time has passed. This much regarding the virtues is enough. Although the hadith is much longer, the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) provides proof of his luminous nature at every stage. This is a very important point: that I and the Messenger of Allah were from one light. And observe how this light, when it went into different lineages—first it was together, then it went into the loins of Prophet Adam (a.s.). And after Adam (a.s.), in the loins of every Prophet, this light remained together. It remained together. But when it reached Janab-e-Abdul Muttalib, after him, this light divided into two parts again. One went into the loins of Janab-e-Abdullah and the other into the loins of Janab-e-Abu Talib. Now, the part that went into the loins of Janab-e-Abu Talib, from there it went to Janab-e-Amir, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). In any case, what can we say about the virtues of Janab-e-Abu Talib? There is no time for that now. I will just say that he had four sons: Talib, Aqeel, Jafar, and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). "Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum." There were four sons. Talib, after whom he was called Abu Talib. Ten years younger than him was Aqeel. Ten years younger than him was Jafar—Jafar-e-Tayyar, as he is called. And ten years younger than him was the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). There was a ten-year gap between each. That was the difference between the four brothers. But they were the sons of Abu Talib. And when the time of trial came for Islam, who came to help? The family of Aqeel came to help. Muslim ibn Aqeel, then Muslim's children, and other descendants of Aqeel—all were martyred in Karbala. The family of Aqeel helped. The family of Jafar helped. The grandsons of Jafar-e-Tayyar, the sons of Janab-e-Zainab, the grandsons of Ali (a.s.). Tonight is dedicated to them. It is written in the Maqtal that when the family of Aqeel had been sacrificed, it was the turn of the family of Jafar. When it was the turn of the family of Jafar, Janab-e-Zainab said to her children, "Go, my sons, and be sacrificed for your uncle." Some Maqatil state that Janab-e-Zainab spent the whole night advising the children that tomorrow they must be martyred for their uncle. She kept giving them testaments and advice. Since they were young children—11 and 13 years old is no age at all—the mother was advising them intensely, fearing that perhaps they might falter, as parents do, saying, "Tomorrow you must be martyred for your uncle, you must be sacrificed for your uncle." She was constantly advising them. Now, when the time for martyrdom came, Janab-e-Zainab said, "Go, children, go and be sacrificed for your uncle." She emphasized it greatly. Now, when they came, both... The children said, "Mother, you come and ask our uncle, you come and ask our uncle." Janab-e-Zainab brings both children and stands before Hussain (a.s.). Now it is written in the Maqtal that Hussain (a.s.) looked at Zainab, and Zainab had her head bowed. "Zainab, what do you want to say?" She said, "Brother, you know what I want to say. And I am certain that you will not turn down my request. I am certain that you have never turned down my request. Brother, let these two go now." Hussain (a.s.) gave permission. Both children came, the mother dressed them with her own hands, dressing them so they would go for martyrdom, so they would go to be sacrificed. But as they were leaving, the mother said, "Children, you are going, but keep two things in mind. One is that you must fight in such a way that the enemy realizes whose grandsons you are and whose nephews you are. Why should you say you are the sons of the Wali of Allah? Let the army cry out that they are the grandsons of Ali (a.s.). This is one thing. The second thing, my sons, I know you are thirsty, I know you are very thirsty. But children, do not head towards the river. Do not let the thought of water enter your minds, because the children in the tents are thirsty. Do not drink water, even if you get the chance, do not drink. It is found in the Maqtal that both children went and fought, and they fought in such a way that Ibn Sa'ad became worried and said, "We need more army to face these two children." So he was told, "Are you calling for such a large army for two children?" He said, "What do you think? Are these the grocers and merchants of Kufa? These are the children of Bani Hashim." In any case, more troops were called, and these two children were surrounded, and then they were attacked, and both children fell from their horses. They called out, and Hussain (a.s.) rushed to their side. By the time he reached the children's heads, both had departed from this world. Hussain (a.s.) picked up the body of one, and Abbas (a.s.) picked up the body of the other, and they brought them and placed them in the tent. Fizza came and said, "Bibi, look, the children have come." She said, "Why have they come? I did not tell them to come; I told them to go and fight." She said, "Bibi, come and see the state in which they have arrived." Now when Zainab (s.a.) saw, on one side was the body of Awn, and on the other, the body of Muhammad. May Allah never show this sight to any mother. Zainab (s.a.) saw, but she performed a prostration of gratitude. "O Lord, You have preserved my honor; accept my sacrifice. I was not shamed before my brother." I have not seen in any Maqtal that Zainab (s.a.) mourned for Awn and Muhammad. Whenever she wept, she kept mourning, "Wa Hussaina, Wa Hussaina, Wa Abbasa," but she did not mourn for Awn and Muhammad. She said, "Wa Aliya, Wa Qasima," but she did not say, "Wa Awna, Wa Muhammada." Zainab (s.a.) did not say it anywhere. Only once, when the stage came that Zainab (s.a.) was released from captivity and reached Medina. In Medina, when Abdullah ibn Jafar could not recognize her, she said to Abdullah, "Abdullah, you did not recognize me? I am Zainab." "Abdullah, Abdullah, Bibi, what is this? Come, let us go inside the house, why are you sitting outside?" Abdullah held Janab-e-Zainab's arm and brought her inside the house. Now, as soon as he brought her in, the Zainab who had been enduring everything until now, once her eyes fell on the two beds, the mother's heart shattered. "Wa Awna, Wa Muhammada." [Quranic verse: And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned. May the curse be upon the oppressive people.] O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of our Imam. Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift healing. O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. O Lord, bless us with the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Mourning for Hussain.

chapters.title: The Grief of Karbala and Azadari
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a poetic lamentation of the tragedy of Karbala, focusing on the sorrow of the family of Imam Husayn (a.s.).

chapters.title: The Significance of Azadari
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that mourning for Imam Husayn (a.s.) is a divine sustenance that encompasses virtues, guardianship (Wilayah), and disavowal (Bara'at).

chapters.title: The Curriculum of Mourning Gatherings
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the structure of Majalis should follow the tradition of the Ahlulbayt by prioritizing their virtues and tragedies over other topics during Muharram.

chapters.title: Understanding Wilayah and Spiritual Capacity
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the concept of Wilayah as a difficult spiritual path that requires humility and divine capacity (Zarf) to fully accept and understand.

chapters.title: The Abandonment of the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the metaphor of the 'abandoned well' from the Quran, representing how people have neglected the Wilayah of the Imam despite the Prophet's clear instructions.

chapters.title: True Waiting for the Imam
chapters.summary: Citing Sayyid ibn Tawus, the speaker argues that true waiting for the Imam requires active searching and deep attachment, rather than passive claims of anticipation.

chapters.title: The Inseparability of Prophethood and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that belief in the Prophet Muhammad is incomplete without the acknowledgment of Ali ibn Abi Talib, as they are intrinsically linked.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Alam-e-Dharr
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the pre-existence of souls in the world of atoms (Alam-e-Dharr) where humanity testified to the Lordship of Allah.

chapters.title: The Primordial Covenant and Human Forgetfulness
chapters.summary: Allah established a primordial recognition of His Lordship and the Wilayah of the Imams in the realm of Dharr, but the nature of the world causes humanity to forget this initial knowledge.

chapters.title: Obedience as the Path to Re-recognition
chapters.summary: True recognition (Ma'rifat) is regained in this world only through steadfast obedience to the Prophet and the Ulil Amr, as symbolized by the 'abundant water' mentioned in the Quran.

chapters.title: The Necessity of the Ahlul-Bayt Gate
chapters.summary: True worship and recognition are only accessible through the gate of the Ahlul-Bayt, as they are the authorized source of divine knowledge and the only path to correct practice.

chapters.title: Worship According to Divine Will

chapters.title: The Concept of Nur (Light) and Tawheed
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that true Tawheed is found through the Hujjat of Allah, warning against anthropomorphic beliefs. He explains that the Prophet and Imam Ali were created as a single light from Allah's light.

chapters.title: The Division of the Divine Light
chapters.summary: The lecture details how the primordial light was divided into two parts, Muhammad and Ali, and provides historical proofs regarding their inseparable nature, including the delivery of Surah Bara'at.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of the Family of Abu Talib

chapters.title: Janab-e-Zainab's Sacrifice at Karbala
chapters.summary: The narrative focuses on Janab-e-Zainab preparing her young sons to be sacrificed for the sake of Imam Hussain, emphasizing their noble lineage and devotion.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Awn and Muhammad
chapters.summary: The narrative details the heroic sacrifice of Awn and Muhammad, the sons of Lady Zainab, on the battlefield of Karbala.

chapters.title: Lady Zainab's Patience and Grief
chapters.summary: Lady Zainab performs a prostration of gratitude for her sons' sacrifice, withholding her personal grief until her return to Medina.

chapters.title: Concluding Supplications
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes with prayers for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time and blessings for the believers.

title: Salman e Muhammadi (a.r.) Ka Khutba - Baraahe Raast Rauza e Salman (a.r.) Se
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound status of Salman al-Farsi (r.a.) and his historical sermon delivered after the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker highlights Salman's unwavering commitment to the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and his warnings regarding the consequences of abandoning this divine leadership. The discourse emphasizes that true faith and spiritual prosperity are intrinsically linked to the acceptance of the Imamate of Ali (a.s.).
content:
Where is my device? Salman (r.a.) is a personality whose status has been mentioned by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It is said that Salman is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt. Salman is a personality whose Wilayah is such that Allah (s.w.t.) has mentioned it in the Holy Quran in a way that He first approved it for Himself, then for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and then for the Ulul-Amr (those in authority). Obeying Allah and His Messenger means obeying the Ulul-Amr. Allah kept the selection of the Ulul-Amr to Himself and did not entrust it to anyone else, just as Allah said to Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) in the Holy Quran, 'I have made you an Imam for the people.' I have made you an Imam for the people. The selection of a Caliph and an Imam can only be done by Allah. In this regard, the Prophet's responsibility is only to announce the one whom Allah has appointed as Imam and Caliph. If anyone opposes the one appointed by Allah and announced by the Prophet, they are a criminal against both Allah and His Messenger. Among the companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) who attained the status of 'Salman-e-Mohammadi', Salman (r.a.) stood before the people of Medina three days after the Prophet's martyrdom and made it clear to everyone how necessary it is to accept the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Salman said, 'O people, listen to my words carefully and understand them. Know that I have been given a lot of knowledge, and if I were to tell you the virtues of the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) that I know, one group among you would say that Salman has gone mad, and another group would say, 'Kill Salman.' Know that you have blessings, but calamities are chasing them. But also know that Ali ibn Abi Talib has... Also know that Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) has the keys to both blessings and calamities. Regarding Ali (a.s.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'You are from my Ahl al-Bayt, my successor, my Caliph in my Ummah, and your status to me is like that of Harun (a.s.) to Musa (a.s.).' But you people adopted the tradition of the Children of Israel; you abandoned the truth. Even knowing everything, you are not acting upon it. In these sentences, he was pointing out that if those who claim to follow the Prophet's tradition do not hold onto the mantle of Imam Ali (a.s.), they will start following the tradition of the Children of Israel and will go outside the fold of Islam. Salman further says, 'I swear by the One in whose hand is the life of Salman, if you had accepted the Wilayah of Ali, you would have received more than what is in the heavens and the earth. If you called a bird flying in the sky, it would come to you; if you called the fish in the seas, they would come to you. No servant of Allah would ever be poor, and there would never be a disagreement between two people regarding the command of God.' That is, if a human accepts the Wilayah of Ali, their faith will be complete, and all creatures of the earth and sky will be subservient to that human. Then Salman says, 'But you people rebelled...' But you people rebelled and handed over this Wilayah to someone else, so now be prepared for calamities, and do not have any hope. We will keep arguing with you on this topic. Salman's words have turned into reality, as Muslims began to be caught not only in worldly but also in religious and spiritual calamities, and they are still suffering today. This is the consequence of rejecting the succession of Imam Ali (a.s.). Muslims will continue to face calamities until they return to this Wilayah. Finally, Salman says, 'I swear by God, you will become apostates and turn back from the religion like disbelievers. Some of you will kill others with swords. Know that I have placed my words before you. I have submitted to the tradition of my Prophet and have served my Master and the Master of all believers, Ali (a.s.), who is the leader of the successors, the best of people, the truthful, and the righteous.' From these statements of Salman (r.a.), we get an idea of his high status, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself said about him, 'Indeed, Salman is the door of Allah on earth.' Indeed, Salman is the door of Allah on earth. Whoever recognized Salman is a believer, and whoever rejected Salman is a disbeliever. And Salman is one of us, the Ahl al-Bayt. Thank God that this year, the 'Strong Reply' team has had the opportunity to present greetings to the court of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) on behalf of all of you, filled with the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). We pray to the Almighty that He grants a speedy reappearance to Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) and grants us the ability to defend the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) just like Salman (r.a.). Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#12 - Imam Ali (as) Ne Fadak Waapas Kyun Nahin Liya
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological complexities surrounding the land of Fadak, specifically addressing why Imam Ali (as) did not reclaim it after the passing of the Prophet (saw). It clarifies that the Ahlulbayt's (as) decision not to pursue the land through worldly means was not an admission of invalid ownership, but a strategic and spiritual choice to preserve the accountability of the usurpers for the Day of Judgment. The discussion highlights the vast, symbolic, and material scope of Fadak and emphasizes that the Prophet's (as) own precedent of non-confrontation regarding seized property guided the actions of the Imams.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Waliyul Asr, help us. Respected viewers and listeners, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We are present before you once again with another episode of 'Giriya-e-Zahra (s.a.)', 'The Attack on the House of Purification', and 'Answers to Objections'. After the martyrdom of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the mountains of oppression, grief, and calamities that were broken upon his only daughter, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), one of those oppressions is that she was deprived of her right. That is, the land famously known as Fadak, which the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had gifted to his daughter, was snatched away and usurped by people after the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). And the Ummah that claims love for its Prophet (s.a.w.a.) should grieve over this oppression, but instead, they try to prove that this land did not even belong to Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). And for this, they present various types of objections. One of those objections is that they say if the land of Fadak belonged to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then why did Hazrat Ali (a.s.) not demand it during his caliphate? So come, to get the answer to this objection, I request our dear brother, Mr. Tanveer Dev Ji, to present the answer to this objection to our viewers. Tanveer Bhai, Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi, Gulzar Bhai. As you have seen, this objection is raised by the opponents that if the land of Fadak belonged to Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.), then when the caliphate of Hazrat Ali (a.s.) came, why did Hazrat Ali not take that land back, why did he not demand it? So we would like you to shed light on this issue for our viewers and present it clearly before them. Insha'Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Waliyul Asr, help us. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Gulzar Bhai, the two important questions you have raised: firstly, did the land of Fadak really belong to Janabe Zahra (s.a.)? And secondly, if yes, then when it was the caliphate of Imam Ali (a.s.), why did he not demand it? So there is no disagreement that the land of Fadak belonged to Janabe Zahra (s.a.). And we find a very direct incident that after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), when the usurpers snatched this land from Janabe Zahra (s.a.), Janabe Zahra (s.a.) went to their court and demanded this land. Now, whether those usurpers handed over that land to Janabe Zahra or not, and what reasons they brought forward for giving or not giving it, that is a separate topic. But all Shias and Sunnis agree that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) went to the court and demanded this right. And Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is the personality who is the daughter of the Truthful (Sadiq) and the Trustworthy (Amin), whose praises the Quran itself has described in its Surahs and verses. Insha'Allah. So, if this land did not truly belong to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), then Janabe Zahra (s.a.), who has the title of 'Siddiqah', would not have gone to the court to demand her right. Yes. The second aspect of this topic is that Nahj al-Balagha, which is a collection of Imam Ali (a.s.)'s sermons, hadiths, and letters, contains a letter from Imam Ali (a.s.) which he wrote to Uthman ibn Hunayf al-Ansari. In which you write that Fadak is our property, in every sense that the sun shines upon. Then some people desired it and some people handed it over to others. But Allah is the best of judges, whether it is the issue of Fadak or not the issue of Fadak. Meaning, Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) writes this very clearly that Fadak was our property. So, Tanveer Bhai, firstly, the point you mentioned that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) went to demand it. Yes. This is a big thing that she was rejected, her demand was rejected. This itself is a very big thing and it is a place for weeping that the only daughter of the Prophet demands something and people deny it. And secondly, Hazrat Ali himself is clearly saying that everything upon which the sun shines, meaning this is clearly our land. Meaning Hazrat Ali is saying here that brother, it is our land. It is clear that from this hadith, which you are citing from Nahj al-Balagha, that this is the hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Hazrat Ali himself is saying this. Yes. Yes. Now, the second question is that since the land belonged to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), why did Amirul Momineen (a.s.) not demand it? So, from this, we get a Hadith in which our sixth Imam, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), says that on the Day of Judgment, both the oppressor and the oppressed will be brought before Allah. Allah will grant the oppressed their reward and punish the oppressor. Then he, meaning Imam Ali (a.s.), did not want to take back that which would be the basis for Allah to determine the reward for the oppressed and the punishment for the oppressor. In other words, Imam Ali (a.s.) knew that whether he received his right in this world or not, on that day, which will be the day of justice, he would certainly receive his right. Indeed. And another aspect of this is that Imam Ali (a.s.) knew that the oppressor would be punished, so he did not want the punishment of those oppressors to be reduced even slightly on the Day of Judgment. Yes. Besides this, there is a famous book called 'Ilal-ush-Sharai', in which some narrations are found from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and Imam Kazim (a.s.) on this subject. We will look at both narrations one by one, Insha'Allah. The first narration is from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), where he was asked why, during the period of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)'s apparent caliphate, he did not take Fadak into his possession? So, in response to this, he says. First, the question was asked to the Imam. Yes. About this. Indeed, this shows that this is not a new question. People used to ask the Imams (a.s.) this question in that era as well, and Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, we are grateful that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), the Imams (a.s.), have explained the answers to us in a very good way. Well, this 'Ilal-ush-Sharai' is the same book by Sheikh Saduq in which he has explained the 'illat' (reason/cause) behind everything. Meaning, he also explained the reason why he did not take it. Yes, so the reason for everything is mentioned in it. Yes. So, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that when the Hijrat of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) took place and he moved from Makkah to Madinah, he had a house in Makkah. When he returned, that house was in someone else's possession. When people asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) if he would not take his house back, he (s.a.w.a.) said, "No, we Ahl al-Bayt do not take back those things that have been snatched from us unjustly." Now, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is the true successor and Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and who could follow his Seerah (conduct) more than him? So, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not demand his house which was taken from him unjustly, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) also followed his Seerah and did not demand Fadak, which was snatched from him unjustly. Yes. Besides that, the second Hadith that I mentioned, which is from Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.), in which he says that we Ahl al-Bayt do not take those things that have been taken from us unjustly, and when we gain authority over the believers, we demand from the oppressors those things which are the right of the believers, but we do not demand those things which are our own right. Yes, so Tanveer Bhai, this narration makes it very clear that if a thing is not demanded, it does not mean, it does not become proof, that the thing is not ours. Just as the Messenger of Allah did not take back his house which was his house, it does not mean it was not the Messenger of Allah's house. Meaning, if Hazrat Ali (a.s.) did not demand it, it does not become proof that it is not his. Yes. Yes. And the last thing I want to present to you is a very interesting incident. This we find in the book 'Manaqib-e-Aal-e-Abi Talib (a.s.)', which contains a dialogue between Harun al-Abbasi and Imam Kazim (a.s.). In this, Harun al-Abbasi asks Imam Kazim (a.s.) why you do not demand Fadak? Imam Kazim (a.s.) says that we will not take Fadak back until we get it with all its boundaries. Now Harun, I mean, Harun knew that it was their right. Indeed. And that is why he asked this question. Hmm. Now Harun asked, "Alright, tell me then, what is the boundary of Fadak?" Yes. The Imam said that its first boundary is Yemen. Its second boundary is Samarkand, which is a city in Uzbekistan, up to there. Its third boundary is in Africa, and its fourth boundary is in Armenia. Oh. I mean, imagine how big the land of Fadak was. I mean, in today's era, many countries would come within it. Many countries would come. If seen, this land goes into two continents. Indeed, indeed. So when Harun heard that this land is so big, he got worried and said to the Imam, "Then if this land is given to you, what will be left for us?" The Imam (a.s.) says that is why we do not demand it, because we know that you will not return it to us. And it is after this incident that we find that Harun also made a plan to kill Imam Kazim (a.s.). Yes. I mean, these oppressive kings knew that the land belonged to the Ahl al-Bayt, and the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) knew that they would not return it to us. That is why they never demanded it. Yes, Tanveer Bhai, I mean, all the arguments you have presented make it clear that the land of Fadak belonged to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and when Janabe Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) demanded it, it was her land, so she demanded it. Indeed. And if Hazrat Ali (a.s.) did not take it, it does not mean it was not his land. And another point is that even if they had demanded it, the oppressors, the usurpers, would not have returned it to them. So he did not demand it and left it to Allah, that Allah will decide this in the Hereafter. Indeed. Insha'Allah. We are very grateful to you, Tanveer Bhai, that you have presented the answer to this objection in a very well-reasoned manner for our viewers. Respected viewers, as you have seen, the objection of why Hazrat Ali (a.s.) did not demand Fadak during his caliphate has been answered for you in a well-reasoned manner, and if you have any other questions or objections regarding this, we will welcome them. You can send your questions to us through our social media handles or our WhatsApp number. We will try, Insha'Allah, to present a satisfactory answer to you. With this, we conclude this episode of our series 'Giriya-e-Zahra (s.a.), Attack on the House of Purification, Answers to Objections'. Insha'Allah, we will be present in the next episode with a new objection and its answer. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua. Fi Aman Allah.

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#5 | Shaikh Saduq (r.a.) & Belief in Wilaayah | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological significance of Wilayah and the scholarly contributions of Sheikh Saduq. It emphasizes that the appointment of Imams is a divine prerogative and that the rejection of any Imam is synonymous with rejecting the entire chain of Prophethood. The discussion further highlights the necessity of Tabarra, or disassociation from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt, as an essential component of true faith and love.
content:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. In our program 'Shamim-e-Ma'rifat', the eighth episode of this series is dedicated to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.). We pray to the Almighty that all those suffering from physical and spiritual illnesses may be granted the opportunity to visit the shrine of Imam Reza (a.s.) in Mashhad, and that we may all be blessed by the King of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Respected viewers, I welcome you all to the fifth episode of our 'Shamim-e-Ma'rifat' program. Today's episode is about a very great personality. He is such a unique personality of the Shia school of thought who has performed such service to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) that it is the duty of every follower to acknowledge it. Whether one is a common person, a student, a religious scholar, or a Mujtahid, no one can be satisfied without reading his book. And this is a personality upon whom the Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), had a special gaze, due to which he wrote a religious book on the occultation of the Imam, titled 'Kamal al-Din'. Yes, dear viewers, you must have understood that I am referring to the great scholar, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.). In this episode, which is the fifth episode of the series regarding Sheikh Saduq (may Allah have mercy on him) and his views on Wilayah, I request the respected viewers to pay attention. Let us begin by invoking blessings upon the Prophet and his progeny: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. May Allah grant us the ability to follow the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states: 'My follower is one who follows our teachings and our path. If someone does not follow our path and our teachings, then they are not among us.' If we reflect on this hadith, it is essential for those who claim to be followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to act upon these teachings. One must act according to the pleasure of Allah, for that is how Allah is truly worshipped. Among the scholars who have extensively documented these teachings is Sheikh Saduq. Those who followed his path have become great scholars and figures of knowledge. He worked extensively on the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If you study his books, you will find that 95 to 99 percent of what he states is based on authentic narrations and evidence. As mentioned previously, for every point he makes, there is evidence in the traditions. This is why his books are so highly regarded. When his grave was discovered in Tehran after a great flood, people were amazed to find his body completely intact, as if he had just been buried, which is a sign of his devotion to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny. Keep in mind that whatever he stated was in accordance with the Quran and the traditions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). If anyone has an objection to his views, they are essentially objecting to the narrations themselves. Let us begin by discussing his views on Wilayah, which is the core of our faith. When we speak of 'Wilayah', it means accepting the leadership of those appointed by Allah and His Messenger. Those who stood in the way of Allah's path and deprived the successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) of his rightful position caused people to drift away from the true teachings of Islam, as they could no longer receive the correct guidance. There is no doubt that the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the only path to salvation. In this verse, Allah mentions those who lead people toward the fire of Hell. On the Day of Judgment, they will have no helpers. These are the leaders who lead people toward misguidance. Because of them, people were led astray, and on the Day of Judgment, they will be left alone, and no one will come to their aid. This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, where they will not be helped. In this world, we have placed a curse upon them that follows them. The verse mentions those who follow the wrong path and the punishment that will befall them—not just for their own actions, but also for those who remained silent spectators to the injustice against the rightful successor. It is our duty to inform the world about the rights of Ali (a.s.) and his progeny. Do not listen to those who say, 'This happened 1400 years ago, why bring it up?' If we were to follow that logic, we would have to abandon the words of Allah and His Messenger entirely. Forget about other matters, why was there a need to discuss everything else? But Allah is narrating a story in the Quran, He is narrating the story of the people of the cave, He is narrating the story of Pharaoh and Nimrod. Allah is narrating all these stories in the Holy Quran so that people may understand what is truth and what is falsehood, so that they may always support the truth, raise their voices for the truth, and take a lesson from history. Taking a lesson from history—the word 'Ibrat' (lesson) comes from 'Uboor', and 'Uboor' means to cross. It means you learn such a lesson from something that you reach the conclusion that what happened in the past will happen again today. What happened in the past is happening today; in English, they say 'history repeats itself'. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) believed that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Woe to the one who, after me, who is in my place, who deprived Ali of this position and this status...' where he deprived Ali of this position and status, immediately after my passing, immediately after my passing, those people who were... not just for me, but even before that, it is said that 1551, the oppressors, whoever accepts the Wilayah of the oppressor, whoever accepts it, then he is the one who accepts the oppressor. And Allah Azza wa Jall says in the Holy Quran, 'Do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over belief.' Do not take them as allies, and this... Do not take them as allies, and when they give you orders, do not accept them. If you take them as allies, they are the oppressors. And whoever accepts their Wilayah, he will be among the oppressors. In fact, he is an oppressor himself. Allah Azza wa Jall says, 'O you who believe, do not take those as your allies and protectors who take your religion in mockery and amusement.' Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day should never take them as their protectors. They do not love them because in their hearts... They do not love them because if there is even a little bit of love or affection in the heart, it turns into enmity. They are enemies of Allah and His Messenger. They will not show them affection, even if they are their fathers or their sons. But they will never accept their guardianship or their words. And leaving them, Allah says, 'Do not incline towards the oppressors.' Meaning, do not have even a slight inclination, a little bit of love, or a little bit of attachment towards them. If this happens, then... and after supporting all this... And after supporting all this, now they say, 'Zulm' (oppression) is to place something in a place that is not its own. To place it where it does not belong is 'Zulm'. Allah says, 'Verily, Shirk is a great injustice,' because the biggest oppressor is the one who brings someone else to the level of Allah or the Messenger of Allah, placing them in a position that is not theirs. Similarly, in the matter of Caliphate and Wilayah, the one who is the Wali, the one who is the divinely appointed Caliph—the Caliph is divinely appointed, he is the one appointed by Allah— He is the one appointed by Allah. Whenever Allah spoke about the appointment of a Caliph in the Quran, He attributed it to Himself. 'I am going to place a Caliph on the earth.' If you people were to appoint a Caliph, you would be infallible? No. So, if Allah did not give the angels the right to choose, even though they were infallible, then how would Allah give this right to humans, who are bundles of sins, to appoint their own Caliph? Whatever divine appointment of a Prophet or a Caliph occurred, Allah attributed it to Himself. Similarly, the Caliphate of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is also a divine position, and the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) continuously announced this Caliphate from the beginning, from the day of Dawat-e-Zul-Asheera until his last breath. If someone removes Ali from his position and places someone else there, then this is the greatest oppression, and there can be no greater oppressor than this. They say that whoever claims that he is the Imam... They say that whoever claims he is the Imam and does not know him, he is a disbeliever, and the curse of Allah is upon him. And then, whoever rejects this Imamate, the one who was appointed... and it is important to note that Sheikh Saduq says, 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Whoever denies Ali's Imamate after me, he has denied my Prophethood.' And whoever denies my Prophethood, he has denied Allah. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ali is the oppressed one after me. Ali is the oppressed one after me.' Ali is the oppressed one after me. That is why we say in Ziyarat, 'Peace be upon you, O Ameer-ul-Momineen.' You are oppressed. 'Whoever denies you, he has denied me, and he has dealt unjustly with me.' Whoever denied you, he denied me. Whoever accepted your Wilayah, he accepted my Wilayah. Whoever befriended you, he befriended me. Whoever showed enmity towards you, he showed enmity towards me. Whoever obeyed you, he obeyed me. Whoever disobeyed you, he disobeyed me. Disobedience... he has defied the Prophet. Whoever defies Ali has defied the Prophet. So, Sheikh Saduq, by quoting the verses of the Quran and Hadith, explains what our belief is. And then he says, 'We believe that whoever denies the Imamate of Ameer-ul-Momineen after him...' Whoever denies his Imamate, it is as if he has denied the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah and all the Prophets. And our belief is, Sheikh Saduq says, that whoever acknowledges the Wilayah of Ameer-ul-Momineen but denies the Imamate of any one of the eleven Imams after him, he is like one who has denied the Prophethood of all the Prophets. He has denied the Prophethood of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Because the appointment of the Imams is from Allah. If someone denies even one Imam, he has denied the entire chain. Because the one who appointed the first one also appointed the others. And this is the belief that is from Allah... It is before us, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has conveyed. Now, if a person stands up and says, 'I believe in the whole Quran, but I do not believe in Surah Al-Humazah,' now you tell me, will that person be a Muslim? No, he will not be a Muslim. Even if he believes in 113 Surahs, he is not a Muslim. You cannot deny even a single verse, let alone a Surah. We cannot deny even a single verse. Sheikh Saduq clearly says, 'Whoever denies our last Imam, he has denied our Prophet (s.a.w.a.).' And I want to take their Ummah and... Regarding those who have doubts about our enemies—whether they are truly our enemies or not—if someone has doubts about who our enemies are, then the one who doubts is himself a disbeliever. The one who doubts is himself a disbeliever.
