title: Ye Dua Ummat-e-Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) Ke Liye Allah Ka Tohfa Hai
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound love and concern Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) held for his Ummah, specifically regarding the gift of Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir. The speaker emphasizes that the Prophet ensured his followers were equipped with spiritual tools to navigate life's difficulties. Furthermore, the discourse draws a parallel between the Prophet's provision of this prayer and his responsibility to appoint a successor to guide the community after his passing.
content:
The Prophet says, 'My brother Gabriel, is this prayer specifically for me, or is it for me and my Ummah?' See how much the Prophet cares for the Ummah. That is, when teaching a prayer, if the Prophet is so concerned about his Ummah that if there is such a prayer through which my Ummah can face difficulties, then will the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) leave the world without leaving his Ummah with an Imam and a Caliph? At that time, would the Prophet not be concerned about his Ummah? This is also something to think about. Then after that, Gabriel says that this is a gift from Allah Almighty for you, 'wa ila ummati' (and also for your Ummah). That is, this Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir is not only for you but also for your Ummah.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 26 | Tafseer of Surah al-Kawthar (108) - Part 3
excerpt: This lecture provides a detailed Tafseer of Surah al-Kawthar, exploring the spiritual significance of Al-Kawthar and the command to perform sacrifice. The speaker highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) emphasis on following Imam Ali (a.s.) as the path to Allah's pleasure. Additionally, the session explains the ritual of raising hands during Takbir in prayer and discusses the miraculous, inimitable nature of the Quranic text.
content:
Masha Allah, La Hawla wa La Quwwata illa Billahil Aliyyil Azeem. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen, was-salatu was-salamu ala Sayyidil Mursaleen, Abil Qasim Muhammad, wa ala alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin, wal la'natu ala a'daihim ajma'in. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum. Once again, I am present before you with the Tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar. In our previous discussion, we mentioned the virtues of the Master of the Universe, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), as stated by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). After this, it was Ibn Abbas who asked the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) at many places, and wherever he wanted, he narrated it. When the time of departure reached the presence of Prophethood, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Ibn Abbas, live as a follower of Ali and do not oppose him.' When he asked, 'Do you not give this command to others?', the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wept and after remaining silent for a long time, said: 'If you want the pleasure of Allah, then do not leave the path of Ali, because the pleasure of Allah is in the path of Ali. Go where Ali goes, consider him as your leader, consider his enemy as your enemy, and his friend as your friend.' When the Tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar was asked, he said it is the Holy Quran. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Allah has given me five things and has given Ali five things.' I have narrated this before as well. He said: 'I have been given Al-Kawthar, and Ali has been given Al-Kawthar.' The companions asked the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about this. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'They were riding on a ship, and it stopped at a place. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'They got this, but I got something better than that.' They asked: 'How?' He said: 'Allah has...' He said: 'Allah has given me a river in heaven that flows from under the Arsh (Throne). It is that. On its banks are domes of pearls and rubies.' The Tafsir of Ali ibn Ibrahim says that Al-Kawthar is a river in heaven that Allah has given to His Prophet. So, pray to your Lord and offer sacrifice. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Ali is beloved in the heavens and beloved on the earth. His creation was through pure soil, and Al-Kawthar is also preserved in the heavens and on the earth. His creation was from pure soil, and his clay was made from sweet water.' Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Al-Nahr (sacrifice) means to raise both hands up to the ears during Takbir in prayer.' In another Hadith, it is said that when Surah al-Kawthar was revealed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked Gabriel: 'What is this Al-Nahr? Has Allah stopped me?' Gabriel said: 'This is not Al-Nahr, but Allah has commanded you that when you enter prayer, while saying Takbir, raise your hands and perform Ruku, or raise your head from Ruku, or perform Sajdah, because our prayer and the prayer of the angels of the seven heavens is like this.' Everything has an ornament, and the ornament of prayer is raising the hands during every Takbir. Raising the hands during every Takbir, meaning saying 'Allahu Akbar' while raising the hands. When the Tafsir of Al-Nahr was asked from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), he said: 'It means that during prayer, raise your hands such that their palms face the Qibla.' Meaning, your enemy is the one who is cut off from goodness. The commentators said that this verse refers to the one who was hostile to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). In the Tafsir of the verse, it is said that Allah has given the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) offspring that will remain until the Day of Judgment, and your enemy will be cut off. The one who remained deprived of offspring, the one who was attributed to him, in reality, belonged to someone else. Regarding the Surah, it is written that when a Muslim wrote this Surah and pasted it at a prominent place in the market of the infidels, the eloquent poets of that era had to write below it: 'Ma hadha kalam al-bashar' (This is not the speech of a human). And this Surah is a short Surah, no one could bring a response to it, and it... And it is a Surah, no one could bring a response to it, and those people used to say that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wrote it himself. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is a human, and he wrote this book himself. But this Surah, Surah al-Kawthar, when it was pasted, they could not write anything, they could not bring a response to it. They had to write below it: 'Ma hadha kalam al-bashar' (This is not the speech of a human). If it were human speech, they could have brought a response because very eloquent poets were present, but bringing a response and writing that it is not human speech is their admission that this is not human, but the speech of God. No human can match it. So, viewers, our Tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar ends here. Insha Allah, I will be present in your service with the next Surah. Until then, I take your leave. Khuda Hafiz. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen.

title: Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer Ki Azmat
excerpt: This lecture discusses the profound significance and divine origin of Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir. It recounts a narration from Imam Ali (a.s.) to Imam Hussain (a.s.) regarding how the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) received this prayer from Angel Gabriel during the Battle of Uhud. The prayer was revealed as a spiritual armor to protect the Prophet amidst the physical hardships of battle and extreme heat.
content:
Among the great prayers that are to be recited in this blessed month, one of them is Dua-e-Jawshan Kabir. Imam Hussain (a.s.) says that my father, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), said to me one day regarding this prayer, 'O my son, shall I tell you about one of the secrets of Allah? The secret about which the Messenger of Allah told me.' This is such a secret of his that he did not tell anyone else. Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'Certainly, Father, may my life be sacrificed for you, tell me what that secret is.' The Mawla says, 'The Spirit of the Faithful, Gabriel (a.s.), came to the service of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). It was the Battle of Uhud, the day was passing very slowly, it was very hot that day, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was wearing armor. The armor that the Prophet was wearing was so heavy in itself that the Prophet himself was feeling pain from it, the intensity of the heat, and secondly, the iron, the iron armor, its intensity.' The Prophet says that I looked towards the sky, prayed to Allah, and I saw that the gates of the sky opened. After that, Gabriel came to me with a tray of light, and then Gabriel says, 'O Messenger of Allah, the Ali-e-Aala (the Most High), who is Allah, who is the greatest Ali, has sent you greetings. Allah Almighty says, this is Allah's command, the armor you are wearing, take it off and recite this prayer.' So this prayer will act as that armor for you.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 15 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This session addresses common questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting in Shia jurisprudence. The speaker clarifies the necessity of specific intentions (niyyah) for non-Ramadan fasts and explains the rules regarding missed fasts and the payment of Kaffarah. The lecture emphasizes the importance of following the rulings of Marja' al-Taqlid, specifically Ayatollah Sistani, while concluding the series on Islamic jurisprudence.
content:
I am coming, we are present there, we eat, where we are, we are... Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. The Strong Room team is coming, think about it, thank you. Think about it, we have been continuously sharing points regarding 'Thank You' in our episodes. I want to share a few points regarding Islam with you. The Quran is not just an old book; the purpose of giving it is to provide guidance, light, and blessings. But more than just reading it, we must understand it. If you are reading the Quran, you should be careful that it is not read in a way that lacks depth. The Quran is a source of guidance, a shining lamp, and a strong rope. For all these reasons, it is necessary for us to study the Quran and focus on its meanings rather than just the number of verses. How should we do this? By looking at the narrations of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the Hadiths. Regarding the narrations and Hadiths, for one night you have today... the beginning of this month and the end of this month... Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Wa Alaikum Assalam, how are you? May Allah keep you safe. There are about five questions today. One question is about the intention (niyyah) for fasting. Is there any condition for fasting? If someone keeps a fast without making a specific intention, can it be counted as a fast later? Why not? Let's see... See, for fasts other than the blessed month of Ramadan, if you want to keep a fast, it is necessary to make a niyyah (intention). You cannot keep a fast without making an intention. So, the question is whether you can keep a fast without specifying which one it is. No, that won't happen. If you don't make a specific intention, it won't be valid. You must specify: 'I am keeping this Qada fast,' or 'I am keeping this Kaffarah fast,' or 'I am keeping this Nazar fast.' You cannot just say, 'I am keeping a fast' without specifying. It doesn't work like that. That is why it is necessary to make a specific intention. This is a wrong notion. If it were the blessed month of Ramadan, you wouldn't need to specify, but why? Because in the blessed month, the fast is only for Ramadan, so it is necessary. I will tell you from the rulings of Ayatollah Sistani, in ruling number 1533, regarding the Qada fasts, it mentions the intention. Can you help with this ruling? If someone didn't make a specific intention, can it be counted as a Qada fast? If it is not specified, is it necessary to do so? Look, if a person wakes up, for example, before noon during the month of Ramadan, and hasn't eaten anything, and makes an intention before noon, it is valid. But if they remember after noon, they must abstain from things that break the fast, and they will have to perform Qada for that day later. This is the ruling. Now, the question arises: if someone didn't make an intention, do they have to perform Qada? Even if you didn't make an intention, you should still abstain from things that break the fast for the rest of the day. So, if you slept without making an intention and woke up after noon, if you had woken up before noon, you could have made an intention. But since you woke up after noon, according to Ayatollah Sistani, the fast for that day will not be valid. Now, regarding the Qada, if you know that today is the day for which you owe a Qada, then you should perform the Qada. This ruling is clear. It means if a person intentionally didn't make an intention and knew about it, and the morning time arrived, they should still abstain from things that break the fast for the rest of the day. Is it necessary to give grain? Can we give money instead of grain for Kaffarah or Fitra? Some mention giving grain for the fast's Kaffarah. So, can we give money directly to the poor, or must it be grain? And another question is, can we give half grain and half money so they can fulfill their needs? Here, the ruling is that you must give grain. Whether you give the whole amount or part of it, it is your choice, but you must give it to a poor person. However, when you are performing this, you cannot give money instead of grain. You must give grain. Since you have to give grain, giving money will not suffice. The only way is to give the grain to a poor person. If you want to give it beforehand, you can. You can give the money to the poor person and tell them to buy the grain, and when the day of Eid comes, you can intend for it to be Zakat al-Fitra. You can convert the money you gave into Fitra. Apart from that, if you just give money, it won't be accepted; you must give grain. The question is about the 'Qada of the day'. Can a Qada fast be kept on that day? Or is it about the Qada of the year? Do we have the choice not to keep the fast? But you are saying that if one is in a state of Janabah until the morning, then you are saying something else. It is written that we should not eat or drink anything that day with the intention of Qada. We should abstain from things that break the fast. Now, when you say 'Qada', it means if I am 15 years old and the conditions for fasting are met, then it is Wajib (obligatory) for me to keep the fast. If I forgot, but I didn't know, and I abstained from eating and drinking that day... Now, this Qada fast is Wajib upon me. It relates to others, and I am keeping it with the intention of Qada and will abstain from eating and drinking. Now, it is not like that. When you are saying this, you are asking if I can keep it. Yes, it can be done. It is Wajib, and you can keep it with the intention of Qada. And the last question for today is: immediately after reaching puberty, I don't remember how many fasts I missed. How can I count the number of fasts? 15... Regarding the number of people from 15-20 years ago, if I want to pay the Kaffarah (expiation) for that, how should I do it? And do I have to give all this in thousands? Could I give it to the poor in the form of food? See, for this, we have a method. If you have missed fasts and you are unable to calculate exactly how many there are, then our Sharia has a way: you should keep as many fasts as you have doubt about. If you have a doubt, for example, if you think it might be one year or two years, then you should lean towards the higher number so that you can be sure that the obligation upon you has been fulfilled. This is what I would suggest regarding the responsibility you have. As for the question of whether money can be given instead of food, giving food is the primary and effective way to fulfill the Kaffarah for those who are needy. It is not that there is a specific amount of money; you know how much is due, so you should provide that much. If you have done this, then... Thank you very much for addressing these five questions. Through these episodes, we have been discussing these matters, and our entire team is deeply grateful to you for your continuous support. At the end of this program, the entire team is thankful to you. The entire team is thankful to you and prays from the bottom of their hearts in the court of Allah that He fulfills all your religious and worldly needs, keeps you safe from all difficulties, and grants you the ability to follow the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). May your shadow remain over us forever. We bid you a complete farewell here. The question-and-answer series concludes with this final episode. We are very grateful to you for watching these programs and sending in your questions. May Allah keep you all safe from the disease and grant us the opportunity to serve in His path.

title: Kiski Ziyaarat Qubool Hogi? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance and conditions for the acceptance of the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Based on a Hadith narrated by Hisham ibn Salim, the speaker emphasizes that the reward of Paradise is contingent upon a sincere belief in the Imamate of Imam Hussain. The talk concludes by highlighting that true Ziyarat requires the rejection of oppressive regimes and a steadfast commitment to the twelve Imams.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And blessings be upon you, O Guardian of the Age, assist us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. In a long Hadith, the high-ranking companion Hisham ibn Salim (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that a person came to the service of Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) and asked, 'O son of the Messenger! Should one go for the Ziyarat of your noble father, Imam Hussain (a.s.)?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Yes, pray there, but not in front of his holy grave, but pray behind it.' Then Hisham ibn Salim asked, 'What reward will a person get who performs his Ziyarat?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Paradise, provided he believes in his Imamate and follows and obeys him.' Hisham then asked, 'And the one who deliberately abandons his Ziyarat?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'On the Day of Judgment, he will only have regret.' Hisham asked again, 'What about the person who spends some days near his blessed grave?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'For every day, he will get the reward of a thousand months of worship.' This Hadith is very long, but in this initial part, the Imam (a.s.) clarified that the reward of the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) will only be received by the one who believes in his true Imamate and worships with this belief in Imamate. To consider Imam Hussain (a.s.) as the true Imam means the rejection of Yazid and the rejection of the entire chain of caliphate he represented. Therefore, whoever goes to Karbala without the belief in the Imamate of Imam Hussain (a.s.), it is possible that his worldly desires may be fulfilled, because Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) is the son of the Commander of the Universe, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), but in the Hereafter, that person will remain deprived of the great reward of this Ziyarat. O God! By the sake of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.), keep us steadfast until the last moment on the Imamate of those twelve Imams whom You have chosen, and especially on the Imamate of the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance). Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

title: Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Mohsiniyyah (a.s.) Kya Hain? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explains the significance of Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Mohsiniyyah, a period of mourning observed by followers of the Ahlulbayt. It details the martyrdom of Hazrat Mohsin ibn Ali (a.s.) and its foundational role in the subsequent tragedies faced by the Prophet's household. The speaker emphasizes the importance of maintaining grief and remembrance during these final days of the mourning season.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Guardian of the Era (Wali al-Asr), help us and do not let us perish. O Allah, curse the first oppressor who oppressed the rights of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and the last one who followed him in that. O Allah, curse them all. Mufazzal ibn Umar narrates that Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) said in a very long hadith regarding the arrival of Hazrat Mohsin ibn Ali (a.s.) on the Day of Judgment, that when Hazrat Mohsin ibn Ali (a.s.) is brought to the field of Mahshar, he will be carried in the arms of Hazrat Khadija (s.a.) and Janab-e-Fatima bint-e-Asad (s.a.), and both of them will be weeping loudly. Then, Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) will look at her child and proclaim, 'This is the day you were promised.' This is the day when every soul will find its good deeds present, and regarding its evil deeds, it will wish that there were a long distance between itself and those evil deeds. Saying this, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) began to weep, until his noble beard was soaked with tears. Then the Imam (a.s.) said, 'May the eye that does not weep upon hearing this mention—that is, hearing about Janab-e-Mohsin (a.s.)—never find solace.' Then Mufazzal also wept for a long time and asked the Imam (a.s.), 'O my Master! What is the reward for these tears?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'There is no count for their reward, provided that one is upon the truth.' Dear ones, the days of mourning (Ayyam-e-Aza) are passing very quickly. It feels like it was only yesterday when the moon of Muharram appeared, and we hosted Imam Hussain (a.s.) in our homes, our mourning halls, and our eyes. That moon of Muharram brought the news of the martyrdom of Fatima's son. The month of Muharram passed, and as soon as history stepped into the month of Safar, the daughters of Fatima had to step into the bazaars of Kufa and Sham. That month of Safar brought such grief in its wake that Hazrat Sayyid-e-Sajjad (a.s.) continued to weep for the rest of his life remembering it. In the final days of Safar, such mountains of calamity broke upon the household of the Princess of the Worlds (Sayyida-e-Kawnain) that the shadow of a father like the Mercy to the Worlds (s.a.w.a.) was lifted from their heads, and in the year 50 Hijri, she saw the liver of her son, Imam Hassan (a.s.), being torn to pieces in his broken grave. But dear ones, on the 28th of Safar, 11 Hijri, the martyrdom of the Prophet occurred, and in Rabi-ul-Awwal, such an attack was made on the House of Purity (Bait-e-Tatheer) that the oppressors martyred the image of Ali and Fatima in the mother's womb before it could even enter the world. It was the martyrdom of Hazrat Mohsin ibn Ali (a.s.) that laid the foundation for Karbala. That is why from the 28th of Safar to the 8th of Rabi-ul-Awwal—the martyrdom of Imam Hassan al-Askari (a.s.)—the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) observe these 10 days as the 'Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Mohsinia,' so that the world may know how the Muslim Ummah treated the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) by opposing the command of the Holy Quran, despite the Quran having commanded love and affection for them. Therefore, it is our responsibility that even though these are the last 10 days of mourning, our grief, our weeping, and our mourning should not diminish, because even if these are the last days of mourning for us, for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), this was the beginning of their sorrows. We pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability to observe the Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Mohsinia. Who knows if this is the last mourning of our lives? May He hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (ajtf), to take revenge for the killing of Janab-e-Mohsin (a.s.) and all the atrocities committed against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and may He count us among his slaves and servants. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

By referencing Quranic verses and traditions, the lecture highlights that the testimony of the Prophet's leadership and Ali's successorship was a central theme throughout the celestial journey.
content:

Welcome to another episode. We welcome you all once again to this episode. Tonight, first of all, we offer our condolences for this martyrdom. With this, we begin our episode, the topic of which is 'Meraj and the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.)'. As we mentioned in our previous episode, how Allah Almighty not only told about the importance of Wilayah in this world but also in the heavens. Our episode today is also on this topic: when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was called to Meraj by Allah Almighty, how was the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) displayed there? For more information on this topic, I request our guest, Syed Nasir Sahib, to enlighten us with more information on this topic. Welcome, sir. Our topic today is Meraj and the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). We would like you to shed some light on this topic for our viewers. Ali, I am the servant of the King, this is my pride. Well, first of all, before starting the discussion on Meraj and the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.), it would be better if we understand the journey of Meraj. It is the journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa, and after that, he was taken to the heavens, and there the Almighty showed His signs to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). And when the Messenger of Allah returned from there... well, you know that everything has a wisdom, and certainly Meraj also has a wisdom. A person asked Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq (a.s.) about the purpose of Meraj. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'God is not confined to a place, nor can time be applied to Him. But He wanted to show the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) the wonders of the heavens and the earth, and to honor him, and to show him the greatness of His signs, so that when he returned, people would understand...' Moving forward, we... Moving forward, we see that the Meraj of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was not just once, but according to the hadith of the Infallibles, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) went to the heavens 120 times. As it is narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that Allah Almighty called the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to the heavens 120 times, and every time, the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) was emphasized. I will mention more about this. It is an interesting fact that the Meraj of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) happened 120 times. And if we reflect on these matters, if we reflect on this hadith, that the Wilayah and Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.) was emphasized even during Meraj. Even during Meraj, the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) was emphasized. In fact, this was not the first time the Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.) was mentioned. As it is said, from the invitation of 'Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira' to the end, from the beginning to the end of his life, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) kept mentioning the Wilayah and Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.). So how is it possible that all his life the Prophet kept mentioning the Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.), but when the Prophet was called to the heavens, there was no conversation between the Almighty and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.)? Let's look at verse 45 of Surah Az-Zukhruf as an example: 'And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?' Here, the Almighty... Despite the good, here the manager says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is told to ask those messengers whom We sent before you. If we reflect on this, it implies that the Messenger, Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), is being asked to inquire from those who were never asked before, whether We had appointed any gods other than the Most Gracious (Rahman) to be worshipped. So, the question arises: how and why was it possible for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to ask the messengers in the heavens? The answer provided through this verse is that the Messenger is being told to ask, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) will ask them in a way that confirms the verses of the Quran. I can explain this further, as this question is also related to the status of the Imam. It is narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that a person came to the Imam while he was sitting in the mosque and said, 'O Mawla, a verse of the Quran has confused my religion because I have begun to doubt it.' I asked, 'What is it?' and that person... I asked, 'What is it?' and that person recited the 45th verse of Surah Az-Zukhruf and said, 'Were other prophets present during the time of the Messenger of Allah?' The Imam then explained and said, 'When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) went on the Mi'raj, he met the prophets in various places, and even reached the Sidrat al-Muntaha. When he returned, he reached the spring where Prophet Yahya (a.s.) greeted the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). You should understand this, and then he led the prayer there. After that, Jibril (a.s.) gave the call to prayer, and Jibril (a.s.) requested the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to lead the prayer because at that time, all the prophets were present, whose number only Allah knows, and no one else can count them. Before that, Prophet Adam (a.s.), Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), Prophet Nuh (a.s.), Prophet Lut (a.s.), and Prophet Musa (a.s.) were present. After that, he led the prayer there. If one reflects on this, in this way, Allah is describing the greatness and status of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). I am talking about the Messenger of Allah... I am talking about the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) waiting for the angels, and the rows of angels were also present behind the Prophet of Allah. So, O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), ask those messengers whom We sent before you. We took a covenant from them, and you addressed them all, and you took a covenant from everyone that you all testify that 'La ilaha illallah, wahdahu la sharika lah' (There is no god but Allah, He is One, He has no partner), and that you are the Messenger of Allah. And after that, how did they make you the leader? They called you the 'Amin' (the Trustworthy) and the 'Sayyid al-Anbiya' (the Master of Prophets). After that, they said that you are the Messenger of Allah... After that, they said that you are the Messenger of Allah and the Master of Prophets, and Ali (a.s.) is the Master of the Successors. After that, they asked, 'Were we given the testimony of the two?' The person who asked the Imam about this verse became happy and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, you have revived my religion, and it has become easy for me.' Then, it was explained in this way that these are the favors of Allah upon His Prophet. Allah's favors are upon His Prophet, and He made the messengers testify to the Prophet. This is what you will find in the Quran. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'When I was taken on the Mi'raj, I saw written on the gates of the heavens: La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah.' I saw this until... I saw this until I moved further, and when I reached the Sidrat al-Muntaha, I saw written on its pillars: La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah, Ali ibn Abi Talib. Regarding all these things and the reality of Islam, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Whoever obeys them, obeys me; whoever praises them, praises me; whoever makes their task easy, makes my task easy; whoever disobeys them, disobeys me.' And he said, 'Write this down, O Ali, so that people may follow you after me.' If we look at all these narrations and reflect, this fact becomes clear: firstly, that Imam Ali (a.s.) is the proof of Allah, meaning that upon meeting... is the proof of Allah, meaning that upon meeting, Prophet Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) is the bearer of glad tidings, and it is not that he became this on his own or that he earned this status through his own efforts. Rather, Allah has made him the successor of the Messenger of Allah. Secondly, obedience to the Imam is obedience to Allah, and disobedience to the Imam is disobedience to Allah. If anyone disobeys Allah, we all know what their destination is. Thirdly, Imam Ali (a.s.) is the successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and if anyone shows enmity towards you, they will be nothing but misguided. And fourthly, all these things are from Allah, but the most important message for the benefit of the people and the best message of the Creator is to honor Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). You have seen on this occasion of Mi'raj, regarding Ali (a.s.), what was present... regarding Ali (a.s.), what was present on this occasion, the best narrations, and whatever you have reflected upon, it should be that the purpose of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was that through it, he showed the angels. This was not just a Mi'raj, but a testimony. And look at how the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the prophets... there, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was the leader. The thing that was most emphasized in the testimony of the prophets was the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Looking at all these things, one thing becomes clear: the one who is guided is the one who has love for the Ahlulbayt. We end our episode today. As we go, let us tell you that in this episode, what was taken... in this episode, what was taken, we will meet again. Until then, goodbye.

title: 🎁🎉 MOHSIN-E-ISLAM (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2023🎁🎉 | 🗓️ Saturday, 20-May-2023 | 9:00 PM IST | 15:30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture presents the 'Mohsin-e-Islam Grand Quiz 2023,' a program dedicated to exploring the life, virtues, and faith of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.). The session addresses historical propaganda and fabricated narratives used to undermine his status, contrasting his lifelong devotion to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) with the political agendas of the Umayyads. Through historical analysis, poetic evidence, and accounts of his miracles, the lecture reaffirms his pivotal role as a protector and believer in early Islam.
content:
We offer our congratulations to all of you on the birth anniversary of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.). As you know, like every year, this year too, on this auspicious and joyful occasion, we have brought this quiz for you. In this program, we honor Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) and discuss his virtues, status, and services. InshaAllah, this year too, we will try to present such topics, and the program will proceed as always. The details are in front of you. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. On this quiz link, you just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first; the only condition for the prize is that all answers must be correct. All answers must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all questions, 14 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, and they will be given these prizes. So, let us begin this discussion. To assist us, we have [Name] Sahab with us. Assalamu Alaikum. And Abbas Naqi Sahab, congratulations to both of you on the birth anniversary of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.). We see that there is not as much debate and disagreement about anyone's faith as there is about Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.). We want to know the reason for this. Where do all these things start? Where did these objections or accusations that Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) was not a believer originate? Tell our viewers. That is a very good question, Sir. Look, if a problem is to be solved, it is very important to know its source and where it originated. Therefore, in this matter too, it is very important to find out where all these doubts, or as you said, all these accusations and talks came from and why they were given so much importance. Where did all these things come from and why were they given so much importance? As far as this matter is concerned, Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) became a victim of propaganda under which the Umayyads in their time, the Banu Umayya, launched a campaign in which they started a factory of fake narrations. If you want to compare this with the current era, we see how people spread propaganda on social media, and people take money to post comments on Twitter or Facebook or react to them, which has no reality. But for a little money, they just want to run propaganda; they have nothing to do with right or wrong; they only care about making money. So, just as we see people spreading propaganda against something today, in that era too, people took dinars and dirhams to insult Banu Hashim and praise Banu Umayya, and they fabricated hadiths in their favor. And this propaganda was so intense that they even used their own Caliph... Your hair will stand on end. For example, Aisha's nephew, the family of Zubayr, had very good relations with the Banu Umayya. And it is no secret that the family of Zubayr and the Banu Umayya were enemies of Banu Hashim. So, this narrator says—and this narration is a fabrication, and the name of the chapter is very interesting—'When he entered, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to him...' MashaAllah. And from this narrator, look, the narrator is also common in all these things. There is another hadith from this same narrator; he narrates again that Aisha said to me, 'Once I was with the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah said to her, "O Aisha, if you want to see two people from Hell, look at those two people who are coming now."' So, the objection to the faith of Abu Talib (a.s.) is truly... The objection to the faith of Abu Talib (a.s.) is truly baseless, and it was nothing but a disgusting conspiracy and propaganda by the Banu Umayya, through which they wanted to diminish the status of Banu Hashim in any way possible. One reason for this is that because they could not elevate the status of their own elders, they wanted to bring the status of Ali (a.s.)'s father down so much that they would be on the same level. But that could not happen. Where is Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) and where is Janab Abu Talib (a.s.), and where are the others? There is no comparison with these people. And look, whether he had faith or not, he protected Islam, he took care of the Messenger of Allah, he protected him, and in the early days, Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) had a huge role in the spread of Islam. In fact, this is proof itself that he was with Islam and on Islam. If a person is not on Islam, if he is an enemy of Allah and the Messenger, then why would he help Islam? But we see that the enemies objected to this too; that is, they tried to hide this thing too. They tried to hide this thing too. Here also, look, if you hear the names of these narrators—as we mentioned before—these are people who have always had enmity towards Banu Hashim and Imam Ali (a.s.). The next narration I am presenting to you mentions the one who advised to raise the Holy Quran on spears during the battle. He says that he heard from the Messenger of Allah... on page number 85. But the interesting thing is that if you try to search for it anywhere on the internet or any app today, it has been altered. They have removed the name of Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) and put 'so-and-so' there. We see such things against [the Prophet] and Imam Ali (a.s.). We see such things against [the Prophet] and Imam Ali (a.s.). People have tried to spread propaganda and lies to this extent. And the surprising thing is that these people accuse Hazrat [Abu Talib], and on the other hand, they believe in the faith of Abu Sufyan, whereas Janab Abu Talib (a.s.) is seen defending the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Islam from his childhood until his last breath. On the contrary, from the beginning of the Prophethood until the Conquest of Mecca, [Abu Sufyan] is seen opposing Islam and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and causing them harm. But Abu Sufyan just uttered the Kalima with his tongue, said 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah', and on this basis, people called him a Muslim, a believer, and a companion. It is very sad. Is reciting the Kalima enough? Because if it were so, the first verse of Surah Al-Munafiqun would not have condemned them and their hypocrisy. Absolutely, if you look... They come and testify that you are the Messenger of Allah. But let us see what the reality of the faith of the Abu Sufyan, who is testified to be a believer, Muslim, and companion, was. It is found in their famous book. I am stating here that Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib presented Abu Sufyan to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) after the Conquest of Mecca, granting him safety. At that time, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked him to testify to the Prophethood, but he started making excuses there too. He was neither ready to accept it nor ready to testify to the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). At that time, Abbas said to him, 'Woe to you! Either you accept faith or your head will be severed.' And under those circumstances, after the Conquest of Mecca, Abu Sufyan outwardly accepted Islam. Even after the conquest of Mecca, he did not bring faith. Despite the effect, he was not ready to recite the Kalima, and if he did recite it, it was only to save his life, not from his heart. He neither accepted the Oneness of Allah nor the Messenger of Allah. Firstly, in their books, there is a narration that once Abu Sufyan was with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). When he saw people gathered around the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he felt jealousy in his heart towards the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and said to himself, 'I wish I could gather people against this man again.' Look at the way he felt enmity and had so much hatred in his heart for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). As soon as he thought this in his heart, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) immediately struck his chest and said, 'May Allah humiliate you, may Allah humiliate you. I did not believe in your Prophethood, but just now...' But just now—meaning at that very moment, by his own admission, he was confessing that he had doubts about the Prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). So, viewers, we have seen that some narrations are found through which attempts are made to prove that Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) was not a believer. So, are there also narrations through which the faith of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) is proven clearly? Let's see. So, brother, we want you to shed more light on this. See, undoubtedly, such narrations are found in many places where people have talked about the faith of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.). But what did the people whom they consider respectable, who are not Shia, say about the faith of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.)? In another narration, a person came to Abdullah ibn Abbas and asked, 'O cousin of the Messenger of Allah, will you tell me something about Abu Talib (a.s.)? Was he a Muslim?' He replied, 'How could he not be a Muslim? His example is like that of the believer of the family of Pharaoh, who kept his faith hidden and did not reveal it, so Allah gave him a double reward.' These were two narrations from those people, from those companions whom they consider respectable. Besides this, if we look at the school of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), we will find narrations that prove that Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) was 100% a believer. And we will also find narrations where he appears not only as a believer but as a Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda). Indeed, brother Abul Hasan, and we should also keep in mind that the measure of any person's faith is through their writings and their sayings. The Diwan of Abu Talib (a.s.) is not hidden; the verses that Abu Talib (a.s.) recited are among the best measures of his faith. We would like to present one verse for your service, Insha'Allah, which shows how much Abu Talib (a.s.) loved the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and how much... ...he respected him. In this verse, he says—meaning the translation is: 'A bright face, through whom rain is sought from the clouds.' Now, brother Abul Hasan, through this verse, Abu Talib (a.s.) is teaching us that if you want to ask for something from Allah, then make the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda) a means (Waseela), make them a medium so that your... ...make them a medium so that your prayer is accepted as soon as possible. And because today the Proof of Allah is Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), therefore, whatever you want to ask today, you should ask Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) or give Allah the oath of this final Proof. Insha'Allah, Allah will definitely grant you. Abdullah and Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) are people of miracles. Here, we would like to present an incident that is very interesting and reveals one of these miracles. I would like to summarize this incident for you. The background is that when Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) sends Janabe Salman to investigate a person, here Salman-e-Muhammadi (r.a.) goes. When Salman goes and tells that person some things, he becomes very surprised at how Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) got the news of that thing. He accuses Ali (a.s.) of magic—Ma'shallah, listen, Ma'shallah—he accuses him of performing magic... ...he accuses him of performing magic, and he does not stop at his audacity; rather, he says to Janabe Salman, 'I have seen even greater magic than this.' The miracles of Ali (a.s.) were considered magic by them. Just as these people also accused the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) of magic, it is found that he said, 'I have seen even greater magic than this.' And not only this, he says that his father told him that he had seen similar magical things from his father, meaning Janabe Abdullah, and his uncle, Abu Talib (a.s.). Meaning, he saw magic that he had never seen before. These are his sentences. Meaning, the wonders that were their miracles were considered magic by them. And he says that my grandfather Naufal had told my father that he had seen similar magic from his grandfather, meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and from Abdul Muttalib (a.s.). Meaning, he saw a miracle that he had never seen before. So, here Janabe Salman-e-Muhammadi (r.a.) says to him, 'What did your father tell you?' ...what did your father tell you? He says that my father told me, 'One year I went towards Sham with Abu Talib (a.s.) on a trade journey.' And the Quraish used to go on trade journeys every year and take a lot of goods with them because this used to be an annual journey. He says that when we left, a time came when some Bedouin robbers in the desert surrounded us and started moving towards us with great terror. And our caravan, our caravan was in a state of chaos, and we wanted to flee—meaning we wanted to run away—but because they had surrounded us from all sides, there was no way to escape. Now, in this state of chaos, their eyes fell on Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.). He addressed them all and said, 'Come, let us all move towards this island, and we will stay here. Take all your belongings, let us enter the island.' So people looked at him in surprise, 'This is a desert, where is the island?' He pointed, and then they saw an island. ...he pointed, and then they saw an island. Now, when these people were happy and looked towards the island, it was like a whole sea. On its edge—meaning a whole sea—how could it be? He pointed, 'Look, a path has been made there.' Now people could walk on it. Allah did a favor to us through Abu Talib (a.s.). Now, these robbers who had come, they also looked closer and were surprised. 'We have been here for so many years, here there was no sign of any island.' When they saw this and started talking among themselves, one of the elders among them—meaning the old robber—said to them, 'Look, I give you advice. Go and ask them if anyone from the family of Abdul Muttalib is present among you.' Meaning, he knew that if anyone from the family of Abdul Muttalib (a.s.) is present among us, do not cause them any harm. And saying this, he separated himself. These people decided, 'No, it's okay, we will go.' And look at the path, they said, 'Let's go.' So first they went towards that path, gave water to their animals, etc. As soon as they thought they would cross it, they drowned and perished. So those who were left were terrified, they came... ...so those who were left were terrified, they came to this whole group of robbers again. Yes, what happened? He said, 'Look, I had already advised you, but you did not listen to me.' He said, 'Years ago, Abdul Muttalib...' and in this way, we were left astonished, and we did not suffer any harm. What was slightly different at that time, but the summary of it is that they could not harm that caravan even if they wanted to, they could not cause any damage. What do we see? There is no island, no sea, no water in this desert. And they say that we came to a path that we had never traveled on before. After that, we were happy for Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Meaning, this was his miracle. So the children became terrified; they came to this plunderer again. Yes, he is saying, what is it? He said, 'Look, I had already advised you, but you people did not listen to me.' He said, 'A year ago, Abdul Muttalib... and in this way, we were left astonished, and no harm came to them. It was a bit different at that time, but the gist of it was that even if they wanted to, they could not harm that caravan in any way. They could not cause any damage. We don't see any island, nor any sea, nor any water, just the desert. And they say that we arrived on such a path that we had never traveled on before. After that, we became happy for Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), meaning this was his miracle.' Despite this, what name is he giving it? He calls it magic. He says that after that we reached Sham, and he says that after that I traveled on that path 20 times, but I never found a trace of that island there. Now, he used this, but the one who narrated this incident is Salman-e-Muhammadi. How did Salman rebuke him? Salman says, 'Whatever you have stated, I swear by God,' Salman says, 'I told him, I swear by God, I do not know.' Brother, from this incident, we learn how Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) was a man of miracles, a friend of Allah, and a proof (Hujjat), and from his lineage, even today, Hazrat Imam... From his lineage, even today, Hazrat Imam (a.s.) is the proof of God, a man of miracles. From this incident, it is fully proven that Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) was a man of miracles. So, this discussion, this debate about whether Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) was a believer or not, this incident makes it very clear, and believing in God is proof of faith itself. With this, our program, our presentation, and our discussion come to an end, and we hope that you have provided the answers to all the questions by now. And if not, there is still time, as you can see a countdown timer running on our screen. As long as this timer runs, our links will remain live, and as soon as this countdown timer stops, our links will close. So, you are requested to submit the correct answers to all the questions as soon as possible. So come, viewers, towards the results, immediately after which the 14 lucky winners of the 'Grand Prize' will be announced by our computerized lucky draw system. [Music] Maula, Maula. Viewers, first of all, once again, we offer our congratulations to you. Now the time has come that you all have been waiting for eagerly. That is, before announcing the names of the winners, we are grateful to all of you who participated in this quiz and encouraged us. We move towards the announcement of today's grand prize, which is being done through our computerized system. First of all, the names of our [Music] 84 prize winners are appearing on your screen, who will receive 1500 Indian Rupees, and those names are: Lucknow's Rashida Bano, Ghabrani Mumbai's Millat Fatima, Bengaluru. The names appearing are those who will receive 3000 Indian Rupees, and their names on your screen are: Mehndi Raza Ghabrani from Mumbai, Uns Fatima from Mumbai, Asghar Hashim Patel from Alipur. Many congratulations to you, Fatima Syed from Alipur. Many congratulations to you and all the winners from our side. We thank you again. God willing, we will meet again in our upcoming events. Until then, goodbye. May God be with you, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Muharram 1442 Urdu Majlis #04: Sach aur Jhoot | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the moral and spiritual significance of truthfulness versus falsehood within the context of Islamic teachings and the tragedy of Karbala. He emphasizes that true faith requires harmony between the heart, speech, and actions, warning that lying is a grave betrayal of trust that leads to spiritual darkness and social disgrace. By reflecting on the devotion of companions like Habib ibn Muzahir and Muslim ibn Awsaja, the speaker highlights how integrity and allegiance to the Ahlulbayt are essential for salvation. The lecture serves as a reminder to cultivate honesty in daily life, business, and parenting to avoid the hypocrisy that distances a believer from divine guidance.
content:
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Fatima Zahra (peace be upon her) said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'Peace be upon you, O Fatima.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have come to you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Peace be upon you, O my daughter.' [Music] Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. May the mercy of Allah be upon him. Peace be upon her. Do not speak wrongly. Peace be upon her... Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah... [Unintelligible/Noisy audio]... Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. [Unintelligible]... May Allah grant us the opportunity to remember Him for ten days. May Allah grant us the opportunity to remember Him for ten days... Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. [Music] Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah... [Unintelligible]... Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. [Music] Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family. May Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, send blessings upon him and grant him peace. With love, they call out 'Husain'. They call out 'Husain' with love. When the news of the martyrdom of the leader of the martyrs reached, they asked about the martyrdom of the leader of the martyrs... [Unintelligible]... They threw Husain into the desert and killed him. They killed Husain... [Unintelligible]... Someone's home was ruined, someone's veil was burnt, someone's lap was emptied, someone's demand was... Someone's lap was emptied... [Unintelligible]... I am the mother and sister calling out 'Husain'. [Music] I am the mother and sister calling out 'Husain'. I am the mother and sister calling out 'Husain'. Someone did not get water, the children were thirsty, the children were left thirsty... They call out 'Husain'. Yes, I am calling out 'Husain'. O Husain, O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). My Husain, my Husain. They could not even find a shroud for my Husain. My thirsty one, my martyr, my Husain. I have come to mourn you, my son. I have come to console you, my Husain. I have come to console you, my Husain. My Husain, my Husain. The settlements of Sham are inhabited, but Medina is desolate. My home is desolate, my Husain. My Husain, my Husain. They could not even find a shroud for my Husain. Peace and blessings be upon the Prophet and his family... [Music]... May Allah's blessings be upon him and his infallible family. [Music]... Peace be upon our master, our leader... O Master, O Master, the mention of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) is ongoing. [Music] Yes, this matter was filled with emotions. [Music] O Allah, grant us the intercession of the Master of the Martyrs, Imam Hussain (a.s.), the guardian of the believers. The Master and our Leader, Hussain (a.s.), the guardian of the believers, is the beloved of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that you will be martyred in Karbala, and those who will be with you will be such that they will be martyred, and they will be so immersed in the love of Imam Hussain (a.s.) that they will not even feel the pain of the iron (weapons). And from this topic, the discussion was ongoing about who is a Shia, because claiming to be a Shia is very easy. To make this claim is very easy, but to make oneself a Shia in the way the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) want us to be, and for them to claim us as their own—this was discussed in the previous gathering. Today, we move forward to a very important topic, which is very simple in daily conversation, but its reality has no limits. The Quran and the traditions have emphasized it so much that if one were to explain it, it would require a lot of time. That topic is truth and falsehood. Regarding truth and falsehood, Allah says: 'O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful ones.' Be with the truthful ones, make yourself such that if you are truthful, be with them. And for that, He says, 'Those who always speak the truth.' This is Surah At-Tawbah, verse 119. And in the same Surah, Allah says, 'And avoid falsehood.' Avoid lying, because today, if you have not avoided lying, then try to ensure that if you are in such a company, you stay away from it. Stay away from lying, do not lie, and distance yourself from falsehood. And if we elaborate on this further, avoid the company of liars. If a person lies a lot, do not stay in their company, because if you stay in their company, you will also start lying. Your habit will become like theirs. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'A person is on the religion of their friend.' A person is influenced by the one they are close to. If your friend lies, and you stay with them, you will also start lying because you will be influenced by them. If the liar is more dominant, they will influence you, and you will end up becoming a liar yourself. The result of this is that you will become a liar yourself. Therefore, when you look at the 'dark zone'—this current [Quranic] eloquence and rhetoric—it is not just about the pressure of its eloquence. Some people say 'fasahat' (eloquence) and 'balaghat' (rhetoric) is just a speed, but its existence is a flow. You must reflect on this, and reflect on the concepts of the Quran. If the Quran were only for the sake of eloquence and rhetoric, then only the Arabs of that time would have understood it. And the answer to this is that if I am speaking Urdu, then who will understand the eloquence and rhetoric of Urdu? First, and secondly, during that time, if the language is 'Lughat' (vocabulary), then it is 'Lugha'. If some people call it 'Fasiha', it is derived from 'Fasaha'. If I translate it into Arabic, it becomes 'Lugha'. So, who will understand this? This is our language; we understand its eloquence, its rhetoric, its sweetness, and its nuances that others cannot understand. These two languages are the ones that will understand. So, if the Quran were only about eloquence and rhetoric, then only the Arabs would understand it. How much would it change? And your concepts, your own concepts, especially the concepts in religion—if you speak regarding them, it is against the rules. It is against the rules to adapt these things, and all these things are present in the Quran. So, this word 'Zoor' (falsehood) has come into the Quran. Whoever reads it will definitely see that it says 'do not speak falsehood'. Wherever it says 'do not speak falsehood', keep yourself away from it. And in 'Zoor', you see, there is that thing, and do you know what 'Zoor' means? In Arabic, they call it 'Tazweer'. What do they call it when you decorate yourself? It is 'Zeenat' (adornment). So, a person who does makeup—is makeup truth or falsehood? Makeup seems like a lie; it gives a false impression. Many people are stars; they are those who have natural beauty. In those who have a lot of natural beauty, there is no need for it. Just as Allah has made you, you are fine. But if the word 'makeup' is used in Arabic, it is used in English too, meaning it is not correct, it is not authentic, it is not real. So here, in Arabic, it is called 'Tazweer'. 'Tazweer' means makeup, meaning to decorate yourself; it is not real. The word 'Zoor' is used. Look at the word 'Zoor'—it means that which you are making up. It means it is not the truth that you are speaking. So, distance yourself from such things that are not the truth, and distance yourself from anyone who speaks such things. That is why in the Holy Quran... Distance yourself from such things. That is why in the Holy Quran, even regarding the hypocrites, it is mentioned that they do not speak the truth. Look at the Quran; the hypocrites come to you and say that you are the Messenger of Allah. This is Surah Al-Munafiqun, verse 1. You should read it. They come to you when the prayer is being offered, they come to you and say that you are the Messenger of Allah. And Allah knows that you are the Messenger of Allah, and Allah also knows that these hypocrites are lying. It is a strange thing. The Quran says their lie is exactly this: saying 'You are the Messenger of Allah'. So, it is a lie. Why? Because it is said that they speak what is not in their hearts. They are just saying it from the outside that you are the Messenger, but in their hearts, this is not the case. That is why, in Islam, when we talk about faith, there are three conditions: it must originate from the heart, it must be confessed by the tongue, and it must be manifested through actions. These three things are important. If there is even a slight discrepancy anywhere, then God forbid, as will be discussed in today's debate, how this is a lie. As will be discussed in today's debate, how this is a lie—that is the sign of a hypocrite. We will discuss it in detail. That is why Imam (a.s.) says, look at the language, 'Min al-Ilahi' (from the Divine). The meaning of a lie is that you engage in conversation, and the purpose for which Allah has created the faculty of speech—the purpose of that is truth. Truth means you only speak the truth; do not speak anything other than that. Do not speak any other word. The Imam (a.s.) says that this is the definition of 'Zoor'. It is 'Mawda'i'—placing something in its inappropriate place. So, when speech is placed in an inappropriate or wrong place, that is a lie. They are saying something that is not true, that is not correct. For example, there is a child, and he breaks something. The parents ask, 'Son, did you break this?' And his first impulsive reaction is, 'No, I didn't.' Why do they lie? What is the reason? Because parents scare them so much that if... Because parents scare them so much that if you do this, we will punish you. So, the child is afraid of that punishment. And even beyond that, in the upbringing of children, one should teach them that if you have done something, tell the truth. Even if it is the worst thing in the world, we will not punish you for it. We will explain it to you; don't be afraid, but speak the truth. There is a very big philosophy behind this. You understand, even if they have done something wrong, do not punish them. Instead, train them. Train them to speak the truth. If they get trained in this, then you can understand that if someone becomes fearless in speaking the truth, then in life, they will always try to do what is right in every matter, at every step. They will never take a step towards doing something wrong. That is why, in Arabic, look—because everything we say, this Arabic is a language that Allah has bestowed. This is the language of the Arabs, and in Arabic, there are two types of Arabic. One is called 'Arabiya' and the other is 'Arabiya'. This is a bit complicated, so I won't go into it much. But the Arabic that is the Quranic Arabic is the one that was bestowed by Allah upon Prophet Ismail (a.s.). Ismail, in the future, like Ekalavya—you can understand it this way—from now on, 13, they call it speaking the truth. You know in Arabic, this is written as 'Sadiq' (truthful). What is called 'Sadiq' is when something happens exactly as it is. The point is, in Arabic, it is called 'Sidq'. Meaning, when someone is asked something, the only thing that should come out is the truth. It is true that it might be temporarily quiet, but the result is what matters. Speaking the truth might cause a little temporary loss or a small wound, but it is permanent. When someone tells a lie, they have to tell more lies to hide it, and the consequence is very old. Look at the narrations: 'As-sidqu amanah' (Truth is a trust) and 'Al-kizbu khianah' (Lying is a betrayal). Allah has given us a power to speak. If we speak the truth, it is trustworthiness, and if we lie, it is a betrayal in the hands of Allah. We have our own habits. 'Siyasat' (politics/management) means what Allah has given us; what is a habit called? What is a habit called? For example, your friend said to you, 'I am going on a journey, please take these 1000 or 500 rupees, keep them with you, and when I return, give them back.' So, what did he give you? A trust (amanah). Now, when he returned, he asked you, 'Return my trust, the 2000 rupees I gave you.' So, what kind of lie would you tell? 'What are you talking about? I don't remember, who are you talking about?' This is called total 'siyasat' (deception). This is a total change. 'I needed it, so I used it.' So, the more a person lies, the greater the sin in the presence of Allah. We must speak the truth, for the sake of integrity. And the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were such that they did not care about their own lives; they did not care about anyone else, they were ready to give their lives, but they never told a lie. But they never told a lie. They would speak the truth even until they were hanged on the gallows. And there, if the tyrant said, 'I will cut off your hands and hang you,' they would say, 'No problem. Inna ilallahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un (Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we shall return). Everyone has to die, but there should be no betrayal of trust.' If we start going, then what is the point? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says—salawat, please—that a believer is never a liar. He will never lie, no matter how much he wants to, because... now look here, why does a person lie? One is that a lie is told for a 'maslahah' (benefit). He thinks, 'If I tell the truth, I will suffer a loss.' Especially in trade, this is common. They lie so much that... They lie so much that, 'If I tell the truth, I won't make a profit.' So, 'I bought this for 15 rupees,' he says, lying. The buyer thinks he is telling the truth. 'Razaq Allah' (Allah is the Provider). He earned 15 rupees, but the way he earned it—there are so many ways. There is a Persian proverb: 'A man went out of the city to save money, but he spent all his money.' He went to save 20 percent, and he was looted of everything. And it is the same with a liar; he thinks he is saving money or earning money... He thinks he is saving money or earning money. He is not earning; he is creating ways to lose money. He doesn't realize it. Many people are compulsive liars; they lie even when there is no need. There is no loss, yet they lie. In the narrations, it is said, 'Even if your soul desires it, do not lie. Do not look at the loss, speak the truth.' Allah is the Provider. But in business, a businessman might do a little bit. They ask, 'How much did it cost you?' We say, 'What does it matter to you? If you want it, take it; if not, don't. How much it cost me is not your concern. If you like it and think it is good, then what does it matter to you?' But people talk like that. 'I have to talk, but what does my loss have to do with you?' If you sell it, you will compensate for it. So people say, 'One has to lie in this, what to do?' You are saying one has to lie? No, you don't have to lie. If you are forced, that is a different matter. If you are forced, that is a different matter. If you are not forced, lying is not permissible. Imam (a.s.) says, 'Allah is with the truthful.' Always speak the truth because Allah is with the truthful. He will always be with those who speak the truth. Stay away from lies, because lying will take you away from faith; it will take you out of the circle of faith. The truthful one is the one who is always saved. Remember, 'Najat' (salvation) is in truthfulness. Allah will always save him, and Allah will keep his honor among people. Allah will be pleased with him, and he will be honored among people. And the liar will always be humiliated and disgraced. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says he will always be humiliated, he will be in loss, and he will be destroyed. Whoever lies, for him is destruction. This is present in the book 'Wasail al-Shia', Volume 1, Hadith number 2. In the book 'Wasail al-Shia', Volume 1, Hadith number 2, and in Volume 1, Hadith number 205, the narration is present. We often lie for our own convenience and think we are saved. No, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'No, salvation is in truthfulness.' And in this is truth, and in lying is humiliation, disgrace, and destruction. And you should try, you should try in life. Look, for example, there are two children. One child, when he always speaks the truth—'Who did this?' 'I did it'—everyone trusts him because he never lies. And the other one makes up a story for everything. There is no need to make up a story, but he has become a compulsive storyteller. And that is why in the narrations, the one who lies is called a 'qass' (storyteller). So the Imam (a.s.) says... So the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Muhammad bin Muslim is a very great, truthful, and great Muslim.' They all do this. Allah has put all sins in a room and locked it. And the key to this lock is wine. He made wine the key. When they drink wine, they will do anything; all sins are in that room. He has the key, he drinks wine, and then he does anything. Like gambling, in professional life, it is a bit different. This is a sin, and whoever defends this sin, the curse of Allah is upon him. What is written about this is that when he used to drink wine, in his intoxication, he did not have the sense... When he used to drink wine, in his intoxication, he did not have the sense of who is his mother, sister, wife, or daughter. This can happen in any house. After that, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Rather, wine is worse than gambling and drinking.' The liar is the same. Remember this, lying is worse than wine. The thing is, you said, 'Did you do this?' 'No, I didn't.' You lied. If the tyrant gives a punishment, what can the people of this world do? The same thing Pharaoh did. Pharaoh gave a threat, 'I will cut off your hands, I will cut off your feet, and I will hang you.' Can he do more than this? No. 'Inna ilallahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' (Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we shall return). Everyone has to go to Him. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'Rather, lying is worse than wine and gambling.' So you are lying, it's okay, 'I didn't do it, it's fine.' So you are lying, it's okay, 'I didn't do it, it's fine.' You are saying, 'The brother did it.' And you say to the brother, 'You did very wrong.' 'Yes, I know, but don't say it was me, say it was you.' This is our mistake. Now look at how we raise children. title: The Verse of the Foremost Ones (Saabiqoon) | Holy Quran & Ameer al-Momineen (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the interpretation of the Quranic verse regarding the 'foremost ones' (al-Saabiqoon) and their proximity to Allah. The speaker highlights the status of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the foremost in faith and excellence, citing both Shia and Sunni sources. The discourse emphasizes that Ali (a.s.) holds the highest rank among those who preceded others in belief and closeness to the Divine.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Guardian of the Era, help us and do not let us perish. The Lord of the Worlds says in the Holy Quran, 'And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near.' Regarding this verse, your and our second Imam, Imam Hassan Mujtaba (a.s.), narrates from his father Ali (a.s.) that the Imam (a.s.) said, 'I was the first to believe in Allah and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and I am the confidant of Allah and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' Similarly, in the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, it is recorded that the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat) is the one who possesses the most precedence (sabqat). The book of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, 'Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur,' written by Jalaluddin Suyuti, narrates from Ibn Abbas that in the context of this verse, there are three individuals who achieved precedence. First, Hizqil, who was a believer in the time of Pharaoh. Second, Habib al-Najjar, who is mentioned in Surah Yasin. And third, Ali (a.s.). And among these three, Ali (a.s.) is the most excellent. The summary is that among those who take precedence and in being near to Allah, Ali (a.s.) is the most excellent. And may peace be upon Muhammad and his pure and purified family.
