title: EP11 | Do Tarah ke Imam | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological concept of Imamate as presented in the Quran, distinguishing between divinely appointed leaders and those who lead toward falsehood. The discussion clarifies the status of Lady Fatima (s.a.) within the framework of Islamic belief, emphasizing her role as a model of obedience rather than a claimant to Imamate. The session concludes by highlighting the grave consequences of both falsely claiming Imamate and rejecting those divinely appointed by Allah.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... [repeated]... Ashhadu anna Ali-yun-Waliullah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjat, son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him inhabit Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and curse their enemies altogether. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. First of all, let us take a question that some brother, some gentleman, has sent. So, the question, please play my question so we can see what the question is. We will answer it. Assalamu Alaikum. Sir, my question is that when they came to burn the door, what status did Janabe Sayyeda (s.a.) hold? Because, according to my limited knowledge, she could not be at the status of Prophethood, but in 'Bid'atun Minni' (she is a part of me), it is that she was a lady bearing Prophethood. So, was she giving orders on behalf of the Commander of the Faithful, on behalf of the Messenger of Allah? Is this correct? And the Commander of the Faithful was aware of these things that Janabe Sayyeda was aware of, because he is the Imam of the time. Okay. So, the question was a bit ambiguous, but still, we will try to answer it in two or three parts. See, first of all, one thing is certain. Remember, the first thing is that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has ordered the entire Ummah that I am leaving among you two weighty things: 'Inni tarikun feekum al-thaqalayn, Kitab Allah wa Itrati Ahl-e-Bayti, ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abadan, fa-innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida alayya al-hawd.' I am leaving among you two weighty things. One is the Book of Allah and the other is my Ahl al-Bayt. My progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt. If you hold fast to both of them, you will never go astray after me, and these two will never separate from each other until they come to me at the Hawd-e-Kawthar. Just be careful how you treat them after me, how you behave with them. This is a famous Hadith of the Prophet which has been narrated extensively by both sects. Very much, it is a reliable, Mutawatir (consecutive) narration. So, whatever belief we have to adopt, it must be in the Quran or in the Hadith. Let me narrate another Hadith in this regard, then we will proceed. See, whatever we take, whatever our belief is, its foundation should be either in the Quran or in the Hadith. Nothing else. And because the Quran has ambiguous verses, it is better that even if we take a verse of the Quran, its explanation should be in the narrations, in the narrations of the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.). That is why we find a narration in Usul al-Kafi, volume one. In 'Bab al-Taslim wa Fadl al-Muslimeen', this narration is found. The Imam says: 'Man sarrahu an yastakmila al-imana kullahu' - Whoever wants his faith to be completely perfect, 'falyaqul' - then he should say, 'Al-qawlu minni fi jami' al-ashya' qawlu Aal-e-Muhammadin alayhimus-salam' - My belief in all things is the same as the belief of the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.), 'fima asarru wa ma a'lanu wa fima balaghani 'anhum wa fima lam yablughni' - what they kept hidden, I believe in that; what they announced, I believe in that; what reached me from them, I believe in that; and what did not reach me, I believe in that. So, if we have to adopt a belief, it should be only from the Quran and Hadith. This is one point that is absolutely certain. If something is in the Quran and the narrations, then accept it, and if it is not, then do not adopt anything from your own side, meaning based on analogy (Qiyas) and opinion. As the Hadith that passed a couple of episodes ago, Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.) said, from Nahj al-Balagha, what did these people of analogy and opinion do then? They established their religion on the basis of analogy and opinion and said that analogy and opinion are necessary. Now your whole religion should be based on that. Because they did not have Ilm-e-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen). Their Imam did not have Ilm-e-Ghayb, so they established the whole religion on what? On analogy and opinion. So, God forbid, that thing should not come to us. Anything based on analogy and opinion, conjecture, presenting one's own opinion in religion, that should not happen. Deducing from one's own side, no. Quran and narrations. Now, the question you asked, that she was a lady bearing Prophethood, no, she was definitely 'Bid'atun Minni' (a part of me). 'Fatimatu bid'atun minni' - Fatimah is a piece of my heart. But it is nowhere found that she was a bearer of Prophethood. That she was a bearer of Prophethood, no. She was 'Bid'atun Rasul' (a part of the Messenger). She was a piece of the heart of the Messenger of Allah. As for the claim that she (Lady Fatima (s.a.)) possessed Prophethood, that is neither in the Quran nor in the Hadith. Rather, if we say that the Commander of the Faithful (Ali (a.s.)) was the 'Nafs-e-Rasool' (the soul of the Prophet), he indeed was, and the Quran has testified to him being the 'Nafs-e-Rasool'. In Surah Bara'at and in the Verse of Mubahila—in two places, not just one. In the Verse of Mubahila, the Quran testified to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) being the 'Nafs-e-Rasool'. And secondly, when Surah Bara'at was revealed and it had to be conveyed to the people of Mecca, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) sent the Commander of the Faithful later for this very reason. He had sent others first, saying, 'Go and convey this.' After that, Jibra'il came and said, 'No, this task of conveying the revelation (Tabligh-e-Wahi) must be done either by you yourself or by one who is from you.' Meaning, one who is like you. So, the Commander of the Faithful is the 'Nafs-e-Rasool'. But what does the Hadith-e-Manzilat say about him? 'Anta minni bi manzilat-e-Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di' (You are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me). O Ali, you are to me just as Aaron was to Moses. The only difference is that there is no prophet after me. And the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) himself says in Nahjul Balagha: 'Faqafa bir-rusuli wa khatama bihil wahi' (He followed the messengers and sealed the revelation with him). This is a narration from Nahjul Balagha, a sentence from Nahjul Balagha, that after the Messenger of Allah, the Prophethood ended. The chain of revelation ended. The specific revelation that is called the Quran, that chain ended. So, to say that she was a prophet or, for instance, a lady who possessed Prophethood—if it is in a narration, then it is upon my head (I accept it). But if it is not in the Hadith, then making deductions on one's own is not correct. And following that, there was another thing in that question: that Lady Zahra (s.a.) was giving orders to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) was complying. No, look, in the entire history and in the narrations, it is not found that Lady Zahra (s.a.) was giving orders to Ali (a.s.). She was not giving orders anywhere. She was the wife of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and she was obeying him in the way that was the right of obedience. Rather, she was a role model for all the women of the world in how a husband should be obeyed. Lady Zahra (s.a.) was a role model. The Princess of the Two Worlds was a role model in how to obey one's husband. So, this is also not found anywhere in history that she was giving orders. If you have any reference where she was giving orders, then provide the reference from a reliable book or a reliable narration. If there is a reference, I will accept it; there is no problem. But as far as this humble servant's study goes, a sentence like 'Lady Zahra was giving orders to Ali (a.s.)' is not found anywhere. Anyway, now let us come to our topic, and that is Imamate. That is, the completion of the argument (Itmam-e-Hujjat). So, the discussion we have been having so far is on general Imamate. Remember, this is about general Imamate. It is not for specific Imamate—that is, whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) chose as his successor. We have not started that discussion yet. That is why I am repeating it again and again so that this remains preserved in your noble minds. So, the Quran has mentioned two types of Imams. Two types of Imams. One is the Imam who is an Imam of guidance, who is from Allah. Allah says in Surah Al-Anbiya, verse number 73: 'Wa ja'alnahum a'immata yahduna bi amrina' (And We made them Imams who guide by Our command). 'Wa awhayna ilayhim fi'lal khayrati wa iqamas salati wa ita'az zakati wa kanu lana 'abidin' (And We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of Zakat, and they were Our worshippers). That is, these were the Imams who were receiving inspiration from Allah... ...whose connection was with the Unseen Knowledge (Ilm-e-Ghayb), and they used to establish prayer and give Zakat, and they were the servants of Allah. Rather, if we go one step further, these were the individuals who never associated anyone as a partner with Allah. This is verse number 73 of Surah Al-Anbiya. 'Wa ja'alna minhum a'immata yahduna bi amrina lamma sabaru wa kanu bi ayatina yuqinun' (And We made from among them Imams who guide by Our command, when they were patient and were certain of Our signs). And We made them Imams who guide by Our command—meaning they guide by Allah's command. That is, Allah appointed them. The appointment is from Allah. Remember this, pay close attention to these words. These are the words of the Quran. Their appointment is from Allah. 'Yahduna' (they guide)—if they guide, they do so by Allah's command. 'Yahduna bi amrina lamma sabaru' (they guide by Our command because they were patient), 'wa kanu bi ayatina yuqinun' (and they were certain of Our signs). These were those servants. So, look, I have presented two verses for you in which Allah is saying very clearly that We made them Imams, and they guided people by Our guidance, and by Our guidance and Our command, they established prayer, fasted, and were Our servants. They were patient and had certainty in Our signs. All these qualities must be in an Imam. Now, study history and compare it to see if these qualities were found in those who later claimed Imamate or not. You can study it yourself. Now, let us look at the second type of Imam that the Quran has mentioned. The Quran says in Surah Al-Qasas, verse number 41: 'Wa ja'alnahum a'immata yahduna ilan nari wa yawmal qiyamati la yunsarun' (And We made them Imams who invite to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped). There are some individuals whom We have made Imams who invite people to Hell. 'Yahduna ilan nar' (they invite to the Fire). They are making people dwellers of Hell. They are inviting people to Hell, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped at all. That is, even if they call for help, they will not be helped. Now, some people raise an objection regarding this verse, saying, 'Look, it is written here too that Allah says We made them.' No, look, pay attention to this. In the first two verses, Allah was consistently attributing things to Himself—that We made them, and they are doing all these things by Our command and Our revelation. Here, 'Wa ja'alnahum a'immata' and after that 'yahduna ilan nar'. It does not say that they are making everyone dwellers of Hell by Our command. What Allah is saying here by 'We made them' means that We gave them permission. We gave them permission to do these things. That is, We gave them permission to claim the status of Imamate. That is, We did not become an obstacle in their path because the world is a house of trial (Darul Imtihan). The world is a house of testing, so if someone wants to do whatever they please, Allah does not become an obstacle in between. So, it means that Allah does not create obstacles. Allah lets it happen. Otherwise, if Allah wanted, He could stop them, but Allah does not force anyone to do anything because Allah gave man free will in this world since it is a house of testing. So, here Allah says that We gave them permission to become what they wanted, to claim Imamate. Look, the Hadith will come later, God willing, and the matter will become clearer. 'You want to claim Imamate? Okay, We said no problem, you claim it.' But what did they do? 'Yahduna ilan nar'—they invite people to Hell, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped or supported. Now, look, I submit to you that one Imam is the one whom Allah has appointed, whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has announced as the Imam. So, look at the history of Islam. We have not reached the main discussion yet; we are just pointing things out so that if anyone has anything in their mind, it may be removed. From the beginning of Prophethood, from the Invitation of the Near Kin (Da'wat-e-Zul-Ashira) until the departure of the Messenger of Allah from this world, if you look continuously—the Invitation of the Near Kin, then Hadith-e-Manzilat, Hadith-e-Dar, Saddul Abwab, Hadith-e-Tayr, and all the narrations that we will study, God willing, Hadith-e-Thaqalayn—look at all these things. Everywhere, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that Ali is my brother, Ali is my successor, Ali is my Caliph after me. The Invitation of the Near Kin, which will be mentioned, God willing, you will find it interesting how people tried to distort even that. God willing, we will mention that later. So, when people claimed Imamate—these claimants to be the successor of the Messenger of Allah, to be the Caliph, to be the Imam—we will first look at the narrations of what the school of Ahlulbayt says, and then we will see what the other so-called Muslims who claim Islam say. Not many Hadiths, just four or five Hadiths from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and a few from their side. So, you can see for yourself, and listen very carefully. Look, keep this one thing in mind: all these discussions we are having are intuitive. They are according to natural reason. If a person uses their intellect, they will immediately distinguish what is truth and what is falsehood. Now, listen to the narrations. Imam Baqir (a.s.) says regarding the Quranic verse: 'Wa yawmal qiyamati taralladhina kadhabu 'alallahi wujuhuhum muswadda' (And on the Day of Resurrection, you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces will be blackened). They will be humiliated and disgraced on the Day of Resurrection. If one is to take it in the literal sense, 'wujuhuhum muswadda'—that is, in its linguistic meaning—it will actually happen that their faces will be black. If one is to take it metaphorically, it means they will be humiliated and disgraced, because it is used metaphorically as well, like 'Look how his face has turned black.' Face turning black means how humiliated and disgraced they are. Both meanings of 'wujuhuhum muswadda'—whether you take it this way or that way. Right? That is, those who on the Day of Resurrection—look, those who lied about Allah. Now, this is a verse from Surah Az-Zumar, Surah number 39, verse number 60. In the commentary of this, Imam Baqir (a.s.), Hazrat Baqir-ul-Uloom (a.s.), says that whoever says—that is, what is meant by lying about Allah? The Imam says: 'He will say, I am an Imam, while he is not an Imam.' That is, neither is there any proof for him in the Quran from Allah, nor is there any proof from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). It is clear, right? So, seeing all these things, people have tried very hard to prepare some things, but God willing, we will discuss the details that there is no substance in the arguments they have prepared. Anyway, now let us come to the next Hadith. Now, pay attention, a great Hadith. This is from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the Sadiq of the Family of Muhammad (a.s.), who says: 'Salathun la yukallimuhumullahu yawmal qiyamati' (There are three types of people whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection). There are three individuals whom Allah will not speak to, 'wa la yuzakkihim' (and He will not purify them), and He will not accept any of their deeds. 'Wa lahu 'adhabun alim' (And for them is a painful punishment). A painful punishment. Who are these individuals? The Imam says, listen. There is a mention of three people in this, yes? A mention of three people. Three, or rather, pay very close attention. Who are these three individuals? 'Man idda'a imamatan minallahi laysat lahu' (One who claims an Imamate from Allah when he is not entitled to it). Neither did Allah make him an Imam, nor did the Prophet. But he is claiming Imamate. The second is 'wa man jahada imaman minallahi' (and one who rejects an Imam appointed by Allah). He does not accept him. He denies him, saying, 'You are not an Imam, and people have chosen us. We went and the public said, 'No, you are the Imam, you are great,' and they made us (Imams).' So now, therefore, you pledge allegiance at our hands. Meaning, the Imam whom Allah made the Imam, they sidelined him. They pushed him aside. And they are saying that the public has made him the Imam. Insha'Allah, there will be a detailed discussion on this as well, Insha'Allah. They denied it; they denied his Imamate. So that is the second one. And the third, 'man za'ama annahuma fil-islami nasiban' (the one who claims that both of them have a share in Islam), the person who thinks that these two individuals—meaning the first one who is claiming Imamate, and the second one who is rejecting the true Imam—that he considers them Muslims. If this... meaning, for all three, the Imam says, Allah will neither speak to them on the Day of Judgment, nor will Allah accept any of their deeds; rather, for them is a painful punishment. For them is a painful punishment. Is it clear? So, Insha'Allah, the remaining hadiths on this, we will cover in the next episode, if Allah grants the ability. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Arbaeen Par Ye Dua Na Bhoolna | Watch 👆 Full Video | Arbaeen Ka Pehla Zaair
excerpt: This lecture honors Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari as the first pilgrim to visit the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) on Arbaeen. It reflects on the massive growth of the Arbaeen pilgrimage, where millions now follow in Jabir's footsteps despite hardships. The talk concludes with a prayer for steadfast love for the Ahlulbayt and the hastening of the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
content:
This was the first Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.), and the honor of being the first pilgrim was attained by Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari. Our millions of salutations be upon Jabir, and the heart wishes to say to Jabir: O Jabir, yesterday you went for Ziyarat alone, but today, look at the splendor of Karbala. The lovers of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) from every corner of the world, defeating every kind of fear and enduring all hardships, reach Karbala in the millions so that the tradition you established may continue until the Day of Judgment. In the end, to act upon the legacy of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, we pray in the court of Allah (s.w.t.) that until our last breath, He grants us the sustenance to maintain love for the lovers of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) and enmity towards their enemies. May He hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), to establish the rule of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) in this world. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds.

chapters.title: The Crown Jewel of Ziyarat
chapters.summary: The speaker identifies the prostration at the end of Ziyarat as a profound expression of gratitude to Allah for the blessing of being invested in the tragedy of Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Living Reality of Ashura
chapters.summary: Muharram is described not as a historical commemoration, but as a living, present journey where the faithful feel deeply connected to the ongoing call of Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: Addressing Misconceptions and Hate
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques modern extremist rhetoric that attempts to justify the killing of Imam Hussain, contrasting this hatred with the blessing of being guided to the love of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Steadfastness and the Companions of the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the concept of being 'steadfast' like a mountain, citing the unwavering loyalty and strength of the companions of the Imams as a model for believers.

chapters.title: The Balance of Hope and Fear
chapters.summary: A believer must maintain an equal measure of hope and fear to avoid complacency and ensure spiritual growth.

chapters.title: Two Types of Fear for the Believer
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that believers should fear both their past sins, particularly those against others, and the possibility of losing their faith in the future.

chapters.title: The Danger of Going Astray
chapters.summary: Historical examples like Zubayr and the deviant jurist Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shalmaghani illustrate that even high-ranking individuals can fall into disbelief.

chapters.title: Total Reliance on Allah
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that all personal attributes and achievements are gifts from Allah, and recognizing this is essential for spiritual protection.

chapters.title: The Danger of Being Left to Oneself
chapters.summary: The Prophet Muhammad's supplication highlights the constant need for divine guidance to avoid spiritual deviation, illustrated by the story of Prophet Yunus.

chapters.title: The Erosion of Conscience
chapters.summary: The speaker explains how repeated sinning desensitizes the human conscience, eventually leading to a state where one is abandoned to their own whims.

chapters.title: The Fearless Valor of Karbala
chapters.summary: The companions of Imam Hussain displayed extraordinary courage and strength at Karbala because they were completely detached from worldly life and focused solely on their devotion.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Qasim ibn Hasan
chapters.summary: The story of young Qasim defeating experienced warriors demonstrates that spiritual training and a willingness to sacrifice for the Imam transcend physical age and strength.

chapters.title: Seeking Refuge in Allah from Shaytan
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that humans cannot overcome the traps of Shaytan alone and must seek Allah's protection, citing the examples of Prophets Yusuf and Ayub.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Lady Ruqayya
chapters.summary: The lecture transitions to the story of Lady Ruqayya, the three-year-old daughter of Imam Hussain, and the tradition of pilgrims bringing dolls to her shrine.

chapters.title: The Final Meeting in the Ruins of Sham
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the emotional journey of Lady Ruqayya, who waited to reunite with her father, only to be presented with his severed head in the ruins of Sham.

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#9 | Muqaddamaat-e-Ghadeer  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the foundational historical and theological proofs of the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the successor to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The discussion covers key traditions such as Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira and Hadith al-Manzila, while addressing the historical suppression and censorship of these events in classical texts. The session emphasizes the importance of overcoming prejudice to accept the truth and highlights the immense sacrifices made by the followers of the Ahlulbayt throughout history.

chapters.title: The Wilayah of Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt was manifested through numerous historical events, with the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) repeatedly declaring Ali (a.s.) as his successor.

chapters.title: The Hadith of Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira
chapters.summary: This section introduces the Hadith of Dhul-Ashira, where the Prophet explicitly appointed Ali (a.s.) as his Wazir and successor during the early days of his mission.

chapters.title: Historical Distortion and Suppression
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses how historical records, such as Tarikh al-Tabari, were altered or censored by later scholars to hide the explicit appointment of Ali (a.s.) by the Prophet.

chapters.title: Prejudice and the Rejection of Truth
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques the intellectual dishonesty of scholars who acknowledge the authenticity of narrators but reject the content of the Hadith due to sectarian prejudice.

chapters.title: Historical Debates and Scholarly Responses
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses various historical books and scholarly responses regarding the legitimacy of the Prophet's succession, emphasizing the importance of authentic traditions.

chapters.title: The Appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The lecture cites traditions, including a dialogue with Salman al-Muhammadi, to establish that the Prophet explicitly appointed Imam Ali (a.s.) as his successor.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice for Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the necessity of divine guidance and the severe persecution faced by those who openly declare their love and loyalty to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).

chapters.title: Sacrifice and Devotion to Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the extreme sacrifices made by followers of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the importance of remaining steadfast in one's love for the Ahlulbayt despite persecution.

chapters.title: Hadith al-Manzila and Imamate
chapters.summary: The lecture examines the significance of Hadith al-Manzila, comparing the status of Imam Ali (a.s.) to Harun (a.s.) in relation to Musa (a.s.), and refutes claims that the Prophet did not appoint a successor.

chapters.title: Context of the Battle of Tabuk
chapters.summary: The speaker details the historical context of the Battle of Tabuk, explaining why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left Imam Ali (a.s.) in charge of Medina to protect against hypocrites.

chapters.title: Celebrating the Month of Ghadeer
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by highlighting the significance of the month of Ghadeer and encouraging believers to celebrate these joyous occasions with enthusiasm.

chapters.title: The Purpose of Studying Wilayat
chapters.summary: The lecture series aims to educate people on the status and Wilayat of the Imams to remove doubts and provide spiritual guidance.

chapters.title: Ailaan-e-Wilayat Program Announcement
chapters.summary: The speaker announces a poetry competition called 'Ailaan-e-Wilayat' and provides instructions for participation via social media and WhatsApp.

chapters.title: Spiritual Reflections on Hajj and Karbala
chapters.summary: The session concludes with reflections on the mercy associated with Hajj and poetic tributes to the sacrifices of Ali Akbar and the resilience of Zainab.

title: Eesaal e Sawaab Majlis-e-Azaa | Baraaye Marhoom Meesam Sayed Ibn Mahmood Hasan (Sarosh)
excerpt: This lecture serves as an Eesaal-e-Sawaab Majlis dedicated to the memory of Meesam Sayed Ibn Mahmood Hasan, focusing on the spiritual and historical significance of the Ahlulbayt. The speaker explores the theological importance of the event of Ghadir Khum and the bravery of Imam Ali (a.s.) at the Battle of Khaybar as foundational pillars of faith. The discourse transitions into a poignant reflection on the tragedy of Karbala, emphasizing the necessity of preserving the remembrance of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the profound emotional connection between the mourner and the martyrs.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 9 | Tafseer of Surah al-Faatiha (Surah # 1) - Part 9
excerpt: This lecture continues the exegesis of Surah al-Fatiha, focusing on the interpretation of the final verses regarding those who earn Allah's wrath and those who go astray. The speaker utilizes various narrations from the Ahlulbayt to explain the concept of the 'Straight Path' as being synonymous with the recognition of the Imams. Additionally, the session addresses specific jurisprudential points regarding the recitation of the Surah during prayer, including the prohibition of saying 'Ameen'.
content:
And rarely, feeding intoxicating medicine... In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the Master of Prophets and the Seal of Messengers, and upon his pure and immaculate progeny. I am present here with the interpretation of the Surah... It is narrated from Imam Ibrahim (a.s.) from his chain of narrators from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Ali (a.s.) is the one upon whom Allah has bestowed the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). They are neither destroyed by Allah, nor are they astray. Allah does not cast His wrath upon them, nor are they lost; they are on the right path.' They are not lost; they are on the right path. In Kamaluddin, there is another narration that Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said: 'We are the path and the straight path (Sirat-e-Mustaqeem) leading to Allah, and we are the blessing of Allah upon the creation. If it were not for us, the signs of the world would not remain, and the world would not be established.' The foundation of the world is through them. In a narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), it is said: 'Our anger and the state of Allah are different, because when we get angry at someone, our language changes, and sometimes our limbs start trembling, and our color changes. After that, when we punish someone, this state is called anger. And there is a sound in people's speech; this is the same anger. Anger has two stages: the first stage starts from the heart, and the second stage appears in the form of punishment. When the first stage is in the heart, a person expresses anger or stops speaking, etc. And the second stage appears in the form of punishment, so he punishes.' It appears in the form of punishment, so he punishes. It is his own, and when it is for the sake of Allah, it is a different matter. Because of this, the body and soul are one. Similarly, when words like anger and mercy are attributed to Allah, there is a change in the state of the heart. Because the body is connected to the body. And you, these 999... from his beloved and from those... and in the explanation of the hadith, you say that... and it is said that... the recognition of the Imam is not achieved, then he is among the lost ones, surely they are astray. From Hazrat Imam Hussain (a.s.), some of these matters... Allah's own... according to the Islamic path... he said that in this, the power of speech is found, and upon those people... And the power is found upon those people upon whom blessings have descended. And for the mercy of such blessings, these words are said. 'Ghayril maghdubi alayhim' (not of those who have earned Your wrath) - through this, the servant requests that Allah should keep him among those who remember Him, and not among those who have earned His wrath. That is, O Lord, those who consider the followers of the truth as poor and deny it, do not give them mercy. Do not give us the path of the enemies. 'Walad-dalleen' (nor of those who go astray) - the servant requests that He should not make him among those who are astray, who do not have the recognition of the truth, and they think they are doing right. That is, those who are astray, who do not have recognition, but they think they are on the right path. O Lord, guide us to such a path. Regarding the explanation, a narration is that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Maghdubi alayhim' refers to the Jews, and 'Dalleen' refers to the Christians. In the book 'Tafsir-e-Ayyashi', it is narrated from Imam Ali (a.s.) that he said: '...and the Jews and Christians, and 'Maghdubi alayhim' and 'Dalleen' are included.' And in another narration, in his statement... he answered this question... it was decided for the 20th... he said, 'Who used to do this?' He said, '...the second Surah, from the second...' And in Al-Kafi, it is narrated from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that when you are praying behind an Imam and the Imam finishes the recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha, you should not say 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alamin'... there are narrations where he said that 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alamin' should be said, but after finishing the Surah, one should not say 'Ameen'. After finishing, one should not say 'Ameen'. The end of the prayer is 'Alhamdulillah-i-Rabbil-Alamin'.

title: EP01 | Saqifa Mein Kya Hua? | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn | Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Fatimiyyah (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical events surrounding the gathering at Saqifah immediately following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It highlights how certain companions prioritized political succession over the Prophet's funeral rites, leading to the appointment of a Caliph. The speaker emphasizes that this deviation from the Prophet's instructions laid the foundational grievances that eventually culminated in the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that the same day laid the foundation of Karbala. The martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.) and Hazrat (s.a.w.a.) became famous. When, due to this great tragedy, the Bani Hashim chose to distance themselves from the people, taking advantage of this, some Muhajirun and Ansar, abandoning the funeral of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), gathered to decide on their own leader. The Ansar wanted to make Sa'd ibn Ubadah the Caliph. At that time, one of the Ansar also gave a sermon. In the book Bukhari, there is a narration that Umar ibn... In the book Bukhari, there is a narration that Umar ibn Khattab said: 'As soon as I wanted to give a sermon after that sermon, for which I had prepared beforehand, Abu Bakr stopped me and then gave a sermon himself. At the end of that sermon, Abu Bakr held my hand and the hand of Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah and said to the people, 'If you want to choose a Caliph, then choose one of these two.' Then one of the Ansar said, 'One Caliph will be ours, and one Caliph will be yours.' After this, there was a commotion there, voices began to rise, so I said to Abu Bakr, 'Extend your hand.' He extended his hand, and I pledged allegiance to him. We had a lot of arguments there regarding Ubaydah. The Ansar said that you Muhajirun have killed Sa'd ibn Ubadah. I replied, 'Allah killed him.' In this way, after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Muslims did not care about the funeral of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Without caring for the funeral of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), contrary to the Sunnah of Allah, they presented this act of theirs as an act of Allah and made themselves Caliphs in Saqifah. Imam (a.s.) states that on that very day, the foundation of Karbala was laid. May Allah hasten the reappearance of our Imam, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), to take revenge for the atrocities committed against the oppressed. Ameen, Ya Rabb al-Alamin.

title: Ghadeer Ke Baad Koi Uzr Nahi | Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Mohsiniyyah (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical efforts of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) to uphold the declaration of Ghadir Khumm. It highlights how she confronted the people by reminding them of the Prophet's appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.) as his successor. The speaker emphasizes that the excuses offered by the people for ignoring this appointment were invalid, as the event of Ghadir left no room for doubt or ignorance.
content:
If you look at the books of the predecessors, it is found in both schools of thought that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) took Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and reminded all the people that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had appointed Amir al-Mu'minin as your Mawla at Ghadir. Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was the very first person to raise her voice regarding the event of Ghadir. When people said, 'If Ali had spoken to us about this matter, meaning the Caliphate, if Amir al-Mu'minin had come to us and spoken, then we would have...', they are saying, 'We would have remembered what Ali said regarding the Caliphate.' What does this mean? They are trying to say that if the Commander (Ali) had come first or you had come first and drawn our attention to this matter, then we would have declared Amir al-Mu'minin. We would not have gone there and declared someone else. This is a lie; it is presenting a false narrative. Now, look at how Janabe Zahra (s.a.) used the argument of Ghadir. She says, 'Allah will not accept any argument after Ghadir.' Meaning, after the announcement made at Ghadir, there is no excuse left, no argument left for you to say, 'If the Commander had come to us, we would have declared Amir al-Mu'minin.' Although they were lying, if you look at the history books—our books and the books of the predecessors—it is found in both schools of thought that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) took Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to the doors of all the people and reminded them that the Messenger of Allah had appointed him as their Mawla. But regarding Ghadir, Janabe Zahra said that Allah will not accept your excuse. She said that Allah will not accept your excuse. How many days had passed since Ghadir? There was no need to remind them; it was a lie.
Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was the first to actively defend the event of Ghadir.
People claimed they would have followed Imam Ali (a.s.) if he had personally reminded them, which was a false excuse.

title: SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ | 15-Jan-2023 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive exploration of the exalted status of Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.) through the lens of Quranic verses and authentic traditions. It emphasizes that her pleasure and displeasure are directly tied to those of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Allah, serving as a critical benchmark for faith. The session also details the spiritual benefits of loving the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), including the promise of intercession and protection from Hellfire on the Day of Judgment.
content:
Hazrat, Subhan Allah. If your share were to be in the place of the paper, then the pen of your destiny would also be in my hand. If it were in my hand, then the pen of your destiny would also be mine. Today's topic is the greatness of the Lady. We hear that the Imam is the ornament of my courtyard. Sarwar (the Prophet) received Prophethood through her connection, and the Prophet is the father of Hasanain (a.s.). So, where does your status stand? It is the limit that you are the daughter, yet you are the mother of your father. It is the limit that you are the daughter, yet you are the mother of your father. Respected viewers, peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. We welcome all our viewers to the Princess Fatima (s.a.) Grand Quiz. First of all, in gratitude to Allah, or in the hope of receiving more blessings, or out of fear of Him, or recognizing Him as worthy, one dedicates every breath and every action of their life to His pleasure and satisfaction. One dedicates every breath and every action to His pleasure and satisfaction. Indeed, a believer prays at least 10 times a day for Allah's pleasure and satisfaction, so that the Lord of the Worlds may show him the path of His pleasure. And then it is stated in the Quran that those who are the cause of His wrath will face a great and severe punishment. Their abode will be the curse of Allah, destruction, and Hell. These people will not be counted among the Muslims. They broke their promise to their Prophet, and Allah deprived them of His blessings. Allah is warning us against anyone who keeps friendship with them. We must strive to ensure that we are not among the wrathful, nor should we keep any relations or friendship with anyone upon whom Allah is angry. Therefore, it is essential to correctly identify those who are under His wrath. That is why we need to turn to the Imam of the Time and understand when Allah is pleased and when He is angry. When He is pleased and when He is angry. The Messenger of Allah will be angry with those with whom Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is angry, and He will be pleased with those with whom Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is pleased. From this Hadith, it becomes clear that to identify the wrathful, one must examine their heart: whether there is devotion to the beloved of the Messenger of Allah, Hazrat Fatima (s.a.), in the heart or not. Does the heart accept the Wilayat of the Lady (s.a.) or not? Whoever Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) is pleased with—which will be the proof of Allah's pleasure—Allah will keep that person's heart safe from His wrath. Allah's mercy will be pouring upon them with all its intensity. Paradise will be longing for such a person. The inhabitants of the heavens will be eager to see them. The angels and the Prophets and Successors (a.s.) will all come to greet them. The light of such a person on the Day of Judgment will be so brilliant that eyes... We begin the Princess Fatima (s.a.) Grand Quiz. Before we start, we would like to present the rules to you. So, we request all viewers to listen to the rules carefully. They are available in the live chat and comment section of the video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion; you just need to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer. There is no prize for answering first. The only condition for the prize is that all answers must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all questions, 14 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, and they will be given these prizes. They will be given prizes, so we are fully hopeful that you will be with us. To discuss this topic regarding Princess Fatima (s.a.), we have two of our brothers present in our session. I would like to introduce them to you: Janab Mohammad Abbas Sahab and Janab Eshan Bhai. Assalamu Alaikum. We offer our congratulations and extend the congratulations of the arrival of the Princess, who is the pride of the universe, to all our viewers. We begin our discussion, and as Abbas Bhai, first of all, we would like to know from you: we have seen here regarding the Quran how the Lord of the Worlds becomes angry if someone is disobedient to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So, we would like to know and also tell our viewers which verse in the Quran has come regarding the love of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and her family, and where Allah is pointing towards this. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, Rahim, Wassalam. Moving on to your question regarding which verses of the Quran refer to this: there are many verses, but keeping time in mind, the verses we have brought for the viewers today are from Surah Ar-Rahman, verses 19 to 23. It is narrated that while Ibn Shahr was consoling Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.), a verse of the Quran was revealed, specifically verse 19 of Surah Ar-Rahman: 'Marajal-bahrayni yaltaqiyan'. The translation is: 'He released the two seas, meeting [side by side].' The hadith continues: 'Anallahu arsala al-bahrayn'—meaning Allah is saying, 'I am Allah, and I have released two seas.' I have released two seas, of which the first sea is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), who is the ocean of knowledge. These two seas met—they are connected to one another. Then the hadith continues: 'Anallahu awma... thumma... baynahuma barzakh'—'I have joined their hearts, and between them is a barrier, which is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' Here, the literal meaning of 'barrier' is a partition. What is this barrier stopping? It is stopping Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) from the world; it is preventing the world from harming him. And this barrier, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), is also protecting Janabe Zahra (s.a.). The mention of these three personalities is in this hadith. The mention of these three personalities is in this hadith, and we would like to know more. Abbas Bhai, what happens when two rivers meet? For instance, when one river flows into another, the stronger one exerts pressure. Here, when the barrier comes between the two rivers or seas, one sea cannot exert pressure on the other. This barrier prevents one from encroaching upon the other. Then the address follows: 'Which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?' So, which favors are being referred to here, addressing both Jinn and mankind? The hadith continues that the first blessing is the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Allah is addressing all Jinn and mankind here: 'Which of the favors will you deny?' And the two great blessings mentioned in this hadith—how can you deny the first blessing, the first sea? Allah is declaring before the people that one blessing is the love of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). One blessing is the love of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and the second blessing is the love and devotion to Janabe Zahra (s.a.). These are the two seas. If one were to translate this in light of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it would mean: 'How long will you deny these two great blessings?' It is worth noting for the viewers that when you recite Surah Ar-Rahman, Allah repeatedly draws the attention of humans, asking how long they will deny these two great blessings. Abbas Bhai, please explain what follows. The 22nd verse of Surah Ar-Rahman states: 'From both of them emerge pearl and coral.' It is mentioned in this hadith that these are Hasan and Husayn (a.s.). And the reason given here for why they are called 'Lu'lu' (pearl) and 'Marjan' (coral)—'Lu'lu' is the larger one—is that Allah has mentioned the Panjtan in these few verses. The larger pearl is Imam Hasan (a.s.), and the smaller one is Imam Husayn (a.s.). Qasim Bhai, regarding the part of the 20th verse we saw, the hadith states: 'Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.) said: Fatima is a part of me...' What should be done about those who, in their authentic books, have this hadith that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was angry and displeased? In their books, it is found that some of their prominent figures were the ones with whom Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was displeased. Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was displeased with them. Now, what should be done? To hide this reality, they included a narration in their books claiming that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was angry with Ali (a.s.), which is actually against the clear text of the Quran. What can be done? To protect their elders, they fabricated a story and attributed it to Ali (a.s.). They didn't even realize that by claiming Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was angry with Ali (a.s.), they were denying the Quran and opposing it. Abbas Bhai, as the opponents say, 'These are the most authentic books after the Quran, like Sahih Bukhari,' but it seems these are not the most authentic books; they are the most questionable books. The hadith continues on this topic, which relates to our question. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is stating that if you want to be a believer, love them. Their love is a condition of faith; without it, one goes outside the fold of Islam. That is, faith and their love are linked; those who lack it go outside the fold of Islam. And those who love them... become believers through the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). We know some definitions, but the reality of the definition, in light of the traditions, is that those who harbor malice against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) fall into this category. Those who harbor malice fall into this category: 'If you do this, you will be cast into Hell.' If a person loves the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), they enter the fold of faith, and if someone hates them, they are destined for Hell. So, viewers, we saw that as we asked Abbas Bhai about which verses in the Quran relate to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and Janabe Zahra (s.a.), he presented the mention of the entire Panjtan through these verses. He showed how Allah expresses love for the Panjtan in His Quran and how He presents the status of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to the world. Abbas Bhai also highlighted a very important point regarding the accusations made by opponents against Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and clarified it. He revealed that love for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is faith, and malice and enmity toward them is disbelief. Let us now go to Hasan Bhai regarding this malice and disbelief and ask him: what will be the consequence of devotion to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) versus malice toward her? Become a believer through love, and avoid malice, otherwise, a person goes outside the fold of Islam. Regarding causing them harm, there is a verse in the Holy Quran, the very next verse, verse 57: 'Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger...' It does not say 'those who have annoyed'—it uses the present tense, meaning it applies until the Day of Judgment. Whoever continues to annoy Allah and His Messenger, what will be their end? Allah sends His curse upon them in this world and the Hereafter, and He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment. A humiliating punishment—meaning when they are subjected to that punishment, all other people will understand through their punishment... People will understand through their punishment why they were subjected to it. Their humiliation will be before all the worlds. And what is the reason for that humiliation? That they annoyed Allah and His Messenger. It will be clear to all the worlds what deeds these people had committed. Indeed, this is the judgment of the Quran for everyone. Now, an interesting question arises: there are two ways to annoy someone. One is physical, and one is emotional. But Allah has neither a body nor emotions, according to our creed, because we do not believe in the divisibility of Allah's body. If anyone believes in a physical body for Allah, they go outside the fold of Tawhid. We do not believe in a body for Allah, nor do we believe that Allah has emotions like humans. So, the question remains: what does it mean to annoy Allah, since He has no body and no emotions? And 'annoying' is specifically mentioned. It is not just about the sentiment; 'conveying' is mentioned separately. The Messenger (s.a.w.a.) conveying the message is one thing, but this means there must be at least one person in the world whose causing of distress is equivalent to causing distress to Allah. What do we find in the Tafsir of the verse? In the Tafsir of Surah Al-Ahzab, regarding the verse 'Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger...', they explain what it means to annoy Allah. For whom was this verse revealed? Whom does Allah curse in this world and the Hereafter? It was revealed for those who usurped the rights of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and caused distress to the Lady (s.a.). This means causing distress to the Princess (s.a.) is... and furthermore, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated in a Hadith: 'Whoever causes my daughter distress during my lifetime...' Now, let a person search history to see who caused distress to the Princess during the Prophet's lifetime. Who caused distress to the Princess? It could only be someone from within the household. What can you do? This is a historical reality. Who gave distress to Janabe Khadija (s.a.) by taunting her? Who gave distress to Princess Fatima (s.a.)? It is recorded. 'Whoever gives my daughter distress during my lifetime, it is as if he has given distress to my daughter after my death.' This is during the Prophet's lifetime. And after the Prophet's lifetime, 'Whoever gives my daughter distress after I leave this world, it is as if he has given distress to my daughter during my lifetime.' It is not just that; Allah is sending curses upon them in this world and will send curses in the Hereafter. And then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) further says, 'And whoever causes me distress, whether in my lifetime or after my martyrdom, it is equivalent to causing distress to Allah.' Whoever does this is deserving of Allah's curse. He is deserving of Allah's curse. And in this regard, there is a Hadith where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke to different people. The Hadith I am trying to present to you now is one where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke to his most beloved companion, who attained the status of being 'from us, the Ahlulbayt'. [Music] 'Whoever holds devotion to my daughter Fatima will be with me in Paradise.' He is saying 'with me'. The purpose of a human's life is to remain close to Allah's footsteps. When he is close to Allah's footsteps, he will attain the perfections of Paradise. Every human tries to ensure this. 'Whoever holds devotion to my daughter will be with me in Paradise; whoever does not, will burn in the fire of Hell.' Then the Prophet... Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'O Salman, what are the lightest moments? What are the easiest stages?' These are the easiest stages, the easiest places where devotion to the Princess will help a person. Whoever held devotion to her and her progeny in this world, did not anger them, and pleased them—the Prophet says these are the stages where a person has no control. True, nothing can help him. Whatever he has done in this world, he has done. Now, he is there with his deeds. But what will provide him comfort there? Devotion to the Princess and her progeny. Death, the grave, the bridge (Sirat), the gathering (Mahshar), and the reckoning—these are all... these are the lightest stages. What would the 'heavier' stages be? I don't know. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) described such difficult stages as 'light'. What is the reason? Only devotion to his daughter Fatima. 'I am pleased with whom she is pleased, and I am displeased with whom she is displeased.' Therefore, if anyone dares to write 'Radi Allahu Anhu' (May Allah be pleased with him) after their name or someone else's name, they should first check if the Princess is pleased with them or not. Because if the Princess is not pleased, Allah will not be pleased either, no matter how many times you call them 'Radi Allahu Anhu'; it will make no difference. The criteria is clear. When the Princess departed from this world, she was angry with some people. So, putting 'Radi Allahu Anhu' after their names and expecting that Allah will forgive them is not their right. This is not just for the early followers; the entire Muslim Ummah should ponder this. This matter concerns the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Everyone claims to have devotion to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). If you have devotion, it is incumbent and obligatory upon you to love his daughter, as stated in these Hadiths. It is not just about the pleasure of the Messenger of Allah; there is also the aspect of anger. Allah is not leaving any aspect empty, nor is the Prophet. The Prophet said, 'Fatima, I am angry with whom you are angry.' Then, the opposite of 'Radi Allahu Anhu' becomes 'Ghadib Allahu Alaihim' (Allah is angry with them). So, actually, this title should be used. Perhaps this is the point; 'Radi Allahu Anhu' is a mistake. Then the Prophet says, 'O Salman, there is a curse on those people, in one of the pits of Hell, meaning one of the valleys of Hell.' One of the valleys of Hell is named 'Wail', the lowest valley. It is also mentioned in the Quran. These will be the lowest levels of Hell. Who are these people? Those who oppressed my daughter, those who dared to oppress her progeny, her sons, her daughters, and those who oppressed her Shias. This means whoever oppresses the Shias in relation to the Princess—because they are the ones who follow the Princess, who advocate for the Wilayah, who raise their voices for it, who stand up for their rights—and because of this, some people find it unpleasant and oppose them, all of them will fall under the category of 'Ghadib Allahu Alaihim'. So, viewers, we have just seen how beautifully our brother Ahsan presented this matter to you quite easily: if someone holds malice against Janabe Zahra (s.a.), what will be their end? He presented very poignant information and very good points in the light of Hadith. Now, since he ended the talk regarding oppression, let us continue with that topic and ask: if someone oppresses the Princess... If someone oppresses the Princess, what will be their end? In this context, there are many such Hadiths. For example, in 'Bihar al-Anwar', Allama Majlisi narrates from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.): 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: Cursed is the person, cursed is the person who oppresses my daughter Fatima after me.' The meaning is clear. Muslims should go and read Islamic history to see what happened, meaning who were those individuals who usurped the rights of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). After that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) further says... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'O Fatima, I give you glad tidings of the Maqam-e-Mahmood.' Meaning, the Prophet is giving glad tidings to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) that Allah has given him the Maqam-e-Mahmood. What is the Maqam-e-Mahmood? It is the station of intercession (Shafa'at) that Allah has given to Janabe Zahra (s.a.). 'And Allah will accept your intercession.' SubhanAllah. Even if all the Prophets whom Allah has honored, and all the angels, and which angels? The 'Malaika-e-Muqarrabin' (the close angels), if they all try to intercede for any one of those who held malice against you, who usurped your rights, Allah will never grant them salvation from Hell. Even if all the Prophets or all the close angels try to intercede—although if they pray, Allah accepts their prayer—but here, Allah is showing the seriousness: if they all join together to pray for someone who has usurped the rights of the Princess and angered her, Allah will not accept it. I don't know why, despite this, some of our people advocate for those who oppressed her. If the opponents do this, it is expected because they are their followers. But if people from among us start advocating for them, it is a matter of great surprise, especially when so many Hadiths and Quranic verses exist. [Music] They say, 'There must be some positive points in them.' And the positive thing they see in the enemies of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is... Allah is saying that even if the Prophet intercedes for them, He will not accept it. Allah has given Janabe Zahra (s.a.) the status that she will intercede; that is the Maqam-e-Mahmood. She will perform intercession (shafa'at); the Maqam-e-Mahmood that Allah has granted her on the Day of Judgment, and the very prayer of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) itself—in the phrases of the prayer in 'Mehar-ul-Anwar', Allah says 'Allah-hu-Akbar', and only He can do that. So, there is no surprise in this that there is divine revelation (wahi) upon Janabe Zahra (s.a.), as we saw in the very first hadith regarding the interpretation of Surah Rahman, which is the ocean of Prophethood: 'Express your desire, and I will fulfill it.' Janabe Zahra (s.a.) said, 'O Allah, I do not desire anything else; You are higher than the one who is desired. I ask You that You... I ask You that You do not let my devotees and the lovers of my progeny be subjected to the fire of Hell.' Here, she is speaking about herself and her state, praying that the fire of Hell be kept away from these people. It becomes very clear here that if one wishes to be included in the prayer of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), it is essential to be her lover (muhib). It is certainly essential. And this hadith continues: 'Fa-awhallahu ilayha ya Fatimatu, wa izzati wa jalali wa irtifa'i makani'—Allah revealed to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), 'O Fatimah, by My honor, My majesty, and the loftiness of My station, 2,000 years before the creation of the heavens and the earth, I have made it obligatory upon Myself—Allah wajaba muhibbi—that I will not subject your devotees to punishment.' 2,000 years before the creation of the earth, Allah had already made this decision. Allah revealed, 'Ask,' and Janabe Zahra (s.a.) asked for that thing, and Allah accepted it in this manner. So, Tajam Bhai, from this hadith we have seen, it becomes very clear that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is praying for her lovers and those who love her progeny, and she will intercede for them. If someone thinks that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is praying for the opponents (mukhalifeen) or that the opponents are included in her prayer, then one must understand that the hadith mentioned above implies that, in reality, the opponents are deserving of Allah's curse. It is not possible that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) would pray for someone who is deserving of the curse. And in this tradition, the sentences that are coming are for the Momineen and Mominat. If you look at the initial sentences of this tradition, even if someone tries to apply this hadith to the opponents or their enemies, it is a very illogical argument. If someone is seen saying that the Princess (s.a.) was seen praying for her enemies or her opponents, it will not be acceptable because the traditions are filled with instances where the authorities of the time are seen saying that whoever oppressed Janabe Zahra (s.a.) or whoever caused her any kind of pain can never be included in her prayer. So, viewers, our discussion has reached a very important and interesting stage. Before we move forward, we will take a short break of 30 to 45 seconds, and then we will start our discussion with the next question and present it to Asan Bhai. Respected viewers, we welcome you once again to the program of the Princess (s.a.). Now, we move to the next question for Asan Bhai. Asan Bhai, we would like to know what will happen to the lovers of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) on the Day of Judgment? If you could shed some light on this, please. I had submitted to your service that devotion to the Princess (s.a.) and love for her progeny will be useful in many stages, the easiest of which is death, the grave, the bridge (sirat), etc. It will be useful for salvation. So, what will be the status of the Princess's (s.a.) greatness, her position, on the Day of Judgment? Regarding this, there is a famous hadith that our scholars often narrate: how Allah will give her permission on the Day of Judgment when she will be at the gates of Paradise but will not enter. When it comes to recognizing people, Allah will say, 'If you want your status to be revealed to the people, if you want people to recognize your position and your rank, then go ahead, and by your will, you may intercede for any of your devotees, any lover of your progeny, and take them towards Paradise.' Scholars of Islam state that the Princess (s.a.) will choose her devotees and her lovers from that gathering of the Day of Judgment just as a bird picks good grains from bad ones. This is the famous hadith we have heard, but when these lovers get permission to go to Paradise, they will refuse to go and will stand and wait. Now Allah will ask them, 'Why are you not going? Your intercession has already been done.' Then these people will say—all the Shias will say at that time—'O Lord, we want our status to be revealed to everyone just as the Princess's (s.a.) status has been revealed. We want people to recognize our rank as well.' Then Allah will say, 'Go back, return to the gathering, and look for those who loved you for the sake of the Princess (s.a.), who loved you because of the Princess (s.a.).' Who loved you for the sake of the Princess (s.a.), who fed you in the name of the Princess (s.a.), who gave you clothes in the name of the Princess (s.a.), who quenched your thirst in the name of the Princess (s.a.), who averted any calamity or trouble from you in the name of the Princess (s.a.)—go into the gathering and bring them with you to Paradise. They will intercede for people. This means that on the Day of Judgment, Shias will get the right of intercession. Why? Because those who arrange for Tabarruk in gatherings, meaning they feed the Momineen for the happiness of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), they will also get intercession because they fed people in the name of the Princess (s.a.), called people in the name of the Princess (s.a.), and respected them with great honor in the gatherings. So, whoever has done all these things will be entitled to intercede for all those people on the Day of Judgment. And as far as intercession is concerned, this is a very interesting point that Allah has given this authority to the Princess (s.a.). Allah has given the Princess (s.a.) the authority that her intercession and her status are such that even if someone reaches the gates of Hell, the Princess (s.a.) has the authority to bring them back from there. And in the tradition, the Imam further states that when the Day of Judgment occurs, it will be written on the forehead of the person whether they are a believer or a disbeliever, meaning the decision of Paradise or Hell will be written on their forehead. But if someone is a great sinner, even if they are a devotee of the Princess (s.a.), the order will be issued: 'Take him to Hell.' But because of the authority of Fatimah (s.a.) even at the gates of Hell, when the angels take him towards Hell, the Princess (s.a.) will look at him, and in the tradition, the Imam says... In the tradition, the Imam says, 'And Fatimah (s.a.) will see that it is written on his forehead that he is a lover and devotee of the Ahlulbayt.' Then, because the Princess (s.a.) has so much authority, she will plead in the Divine Court for that lover, for that devotee. The Princess (s.a.) will plead, and what will she say? The Imam says that the Princess (s.a.) will say, 'O Allah, You gave the fire of Hell to those who loved my progeny and those who loved me, but I had promised to keep them away from the fire of Hell. Whoever accepted your Wilayah...' Whoever accepted your Wilayah, I had promised them all that I would not subject them to the fire of Hell, I would not subject them to the punishment of Hell. And 'Wa adil-li wa'd-i haqq'—My promise is true, and 'Wa ana la ukhlifu'—I never break my promise. Therefore, 'Amartuha ila'—this person who is going towards Hell, whose forehead bears your name, now I am deciding that My angels will take this servant of Mine towards Paradise. O My angels, O My Prophets, O My Messengers, and all of you, Allah announces before everyone and says to the Princess (s.a.), 'Do you know why I did this? I had previously issued the order of Hell for him, and then you interceded for him, and I accepted your intercession. Do you know why I did this?' I wanted to make your status and rank manifest and obligatory before all the people of the gathering. Therefore, I have done one thing: before them, a person for whom the decree of Hell had already been issued was being led towards Hell, but I wanted your authority to be revealed before everyone. Thus, I accepted your intercession for him. Now, therefore, any believer whose distress you have witnessed, you may intercede for anyone, and I will free them from Hell. Provided that they are a believer—this is the condition—if such a person is your follower and your devotee, I will issue the decree of Paradise for them. This is what the Imam (a.s.) has stated regarding the status and rank of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and how her intercession will manifest before the people of the gathering, and how Allah will reveal her rank and perfection to the people. Thank you very much, Abbas Bhai. Now, we also want to know, because we have heard since childhood that the Bridge of Sirat will be thinner than a hair, sharper than a sword, and hotter than fire. So, how will the intercession or help of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) reach her followers, her lovers, or her devotees? Abbas Bhai, please tell us, no matter how many sins we have, the status of the Princess (s.a.) and her intercession cannot be higher than that. The status of the Princess (s.a.) and her intercession cannot be higher than that. Indeed, indeed. That is why, no matter how many sins a person commits, Allah will forgive them. This is the most amazing occasion. As far as the Bridge of Sirat is concerned, there is a tradition found in the Tafsir of the Imam (a.s.) regarding the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in which the love for the Princess (s.a.) is mentioned. It is stated: 'When Allah gathers all creatures, a caller from the Lord, the Almighty, will call out, saying: "Lower your gaze..."' Lower your gaze, for the people will lower their eyes. And when the Princess (s.a.) enters Paradise, a thread of her cloak (rida) will remain on the Bridge of Sirat. That thread will be made of light. One end of that thread will be in the hand of the Princess (s.a.)—she will be in Paradise—and the other end will be in the field of the gathering. It is a matter of one thread. A single thread will be over the Bridge of Sirat, which is thinner than a hair and sharper than the edge of a sword. And then a caller from the Lord, the Almighty, will call out: 'O lovers of Fatima (s.a.), O those who loved the Princess and were her devotees, O people of the Sayyid (a.s.), you all should hold onto one...' O people of the Sayyid (a.s.), you all should hold onto one thread of this cloak.' Then, no lover of the Princess (s.a.) will remain except that they will hold onto a thread of the hem of the Princess's cloak, which is there in the field of the gathering. It is a strong rope of devotion to her. How many will hold onto this one thread of her cloak? The definition of 'Sham' (a group) in this hadith has come in this way: 'They asked, "How many is a Sham? What is the number of a Sham?" He said, "One thousand million (a billion) people will be saved from the fire of Hell by this one thread."' One thousand million plus one thousand million, and then even more than that. Some are seen saying that the Princess (s.a.) or the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will have to pass through the test of the Bridge of Sirat. They have not realized the importance of a single thread of the Princess's cloak. They do not have the recognition (marifat) of even one thread of the Princess's cloak. She herself says, 'Why are these things...' She herself says, 'Why are these things?' The Princess (s.a.) says that your status is linked to the obedience of Allah and His Messenger. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger is the one who is a lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who is their obedient follower. And whoever does not obey Allah and the Messenger, who does not act according to their command, who does not submit to the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and who does not distance themselves from the things they have forbidden, then how can they be within the circle of their followers? Here, also keep in mind that we are talking about which people—what type of sinners? Those who persist in their sins, who are not even slightly remorseful. They commit sins openly and publicly. They feel no regret at all. None of us is infallible, but this does not mean that a sinful person, if they are repentant for their actions, if they are ashamed and seek forgiveness, will be worthy of the intercession of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). But if they are persisting, then the command and hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is very clear and manifest. They say: 'Whoever is obedient and submissive to Allah, he is our guardian, he is our lover, he is our follower. And whoever disobeys Allah, he is our enemy.' Those who are knowingly committing disobedience to Allah are our enemies. Keep yourself away from these things. Through these things, the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be attained, and they will be worthy of all those virtues and the intercession, only because they performed good deeds and acted with piety and obedience. This is the condition. That is all. Besides this, we saw here, and the question we asked, how the intercession or help of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) will be present on the Bridge of Sirat. Through a very excellent hadith, Abbas Bhai clarified that matter. The status of the Princess (s.a.) is very high; through one thread of her cloak, millions and billions of people will be interceded for. Millions and billions of people will be interceded for. After that, Abbas Bhai also presented very excellent points in the light of hadith about how a person should live their life and abstain from sins, and not persist in sins. And whoever lives their life in this way in this world, surely, her intercession, God willing, in the field of the gathering, the Princess (s.a.) will perform it. God willing, we have reached the end of our program, and we have discussed many topics before you and presented them through the Quran and Hadith. Viewers, as we know, the link for questions had gone live, and we hope that all your questions have been answered. The timer running on your screen—as long as that timer is live, the link will remain live. So, viewers, after the permission of the Princess (s.a.) for all the gentlemen, we will open our computerized lucky draw system. We request you to stay with us until the end. Walhamdulillahir Rabbil Alameen. Walhamdulillahir Rabbil Alameen. Peace be upon you, peace be upon you, Sayyida, peace be upon you, peace be upon you. Peace be upon you, peace be upon you. [Music] Aalam-e-Muhammad

title: MOHSIN E ISLAM (a.s.) GRAND QUIZ | Presentation and Live Quiz on Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive defense of the faith and status of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), the protector of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Through historical analysis and theological discourse, the session refutes common misconceptions and fabricated narrations that question his belief. The program also features a 'Mohsine-e-Islam' grand quiz, encouraging viewers to engage deeply with the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt and the historical legacy of Abu Talib (a.s.).
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance and our relief through them, and send blessings upon them all. From Fatimatuz Zahra (a.s.), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). She said, "I heard Fatima (a.s.) say: My father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), came to me one day and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Fatima.' I said, 'And upon you be peace.' He said, 'I feel a weakness in my body.' I said to him, 'I seek refuge in Allah for you, O my father, from weakness.' He said, 'O Fatima, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it.' So I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it, and I began to look at him, and his face was shining like the full moon on the night of its perfection and completion." It was not long before my son, Hasan (a.s.), arrived and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Mother.' I said, 'And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said, 'O Mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said, 'Yes, your grandfather is under the cloak.' So Hasan approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Grandfather, O Messenger of Allah, do you give me permission to enter with you under the cloak?' He said, 'And upon you be peace, O my son and master of my pond, I have given you permission.' So he entered with him under the cloak. It was not long before my son, Hussain (a.s.), arrived and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Mother.' I said, 'And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said to me, 'O Mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said, 'Yes, your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak.' So Hussain approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Grandfather, peace be upon you, O one whom Allah has chosen, do you give me permission to be with you both under the cloak?' title: Intezaar e Imam (a.t.f.s.) Ki Misaal - Anas Ibne Haaris Kaahili
excerpt: This lecture highlights the exemplary devotion of Anas ibn Harith Kahili, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) who awaited the arrival of Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala. By acting upon the Prophet's prophecy regarding the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, Anas demonstrated the true essence of waiting for an Imam. The talk emphasizes that the core purpose of a 'Muntazir' (one who waits) is to provide active assistance and support to the Imam of their time.
content:
Anas ibn Harith Kahili, who was a companion of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and was present with him in the battles of Badr and Hunayn. When he heard from the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) that 'My son, meaning Mawla Hussain (a.s.), will be killed in the land of Iraq. So, whoever among you finds his time, should assist him. Should help him.' History tells us that when Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his caravan reached Karbala, Anas ibn Harith Kahili was waiting for them there. Solely based on that command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that whoever finds his time should help and assist him. There were individuals like Anas ibn Harith Kahili who truly fulfilled the right of waiting, and they gave us this lesson that if one is waiting for the awaited one (Muntazar), then the goal and purpose of a waiter (Muntazir) should be only and solely the assistance of the Imam. title: EP#8: Madine Mein Hui Quran-e-Majeed Ki Mukhaalefat
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical incident involving the house of the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) following his passing. The speaker highlights a contradiction between the claims of those who profess to follow the Quran and their actions regarding the etiquette of entering homes as prescribed in Surah An-Nur. By analyzing verses 27 and 28, the lecture argues that the forced entry into the Prophet's daughter's house constitutes a direct opposition to the clear commandments of the Quran.
content:
After the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), who opposed the Quran? Allah (Azza wa Jal) stated in Surah An-Nur, verses 27 and 28: 'O you who believe! Do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their inhabitants. That is better for you, that you may be mindful.' Then, if you do not find anyone in the house, do not enter until permission is given to you. And if you are told to go back, then go back. It is surprising for those who claim to love the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) and claim that the Quran is sufficient for them, yet they went against these verses and entered forcibly without permission, and that too into the house of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). If this is not opposition to the Quran, then what is?
