title: Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Raaziq Hain - Imam Sadiq (a.s.) Ki Daleel Par Abu Hanifah Ka Tajjub
excerpt: This lecture explores a historical dialogue between Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) and Abu Hanifa regarding the role of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in the distribution of sustenance (rizq). By citing Quranic verses from Surah At-Tawbah, the Imam demonstrates that the Prophet acts as a medium for Allah's bounty. The speaker uses this incident to justify the Shia practice of Tawassul and seeking aid from the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.). Ultimately, the lecture argues that recognizing the Ahl-e-Bayt as providers is consistent with Tawheed, as they are the successors and proofs of Allah on Earth.
content:
A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Salla 'alayka ya Wali-Allah. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) proved to the Imam of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, Abu Hanifa, through two verses of the Holy Quran, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is the medium through which all sustenance (rizq) is distributed in this world. This is also the answer to all those who object to us Shias as to why we ask directly from the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.) and why we perform Tawassul, etc. The incident is that once Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and Abu Hanifa were eating together. After eating, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) raised his hands towards the sky and said, 'Alhamdulillah Rabbil 'Alamin, Allahumma hadha minka wa min Rasulik' (Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, O Allah, this is from You and from Your Messenger). As soon as he heard this, Abu Hanifa immediately objected, saying, 'O Aba Abdillah, you have associated someone with Allah, meaning you have associated the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) with Allah.' To this, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) replied, 'What are you saying? Have you not read in the Book of Allah, the Quran, this verse?' [music] Their anger is only because Allah and His Messenger have enriched the believers out of His bounty. This is Surah At-Tawbah, verse 74. Then the Imam (a.s.) further says, and Allah says in another place, meaning in another verse, '...that they would have been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us out of His bounty, and so will His Messenger.' (Surah At-Tawbah, verse 59). Hearing this, Abu Hanifa said, 'It seems as if I have neither heard nor read these two verses before today.' There are some important conclusions from this incident... ...wherever and in whatever state one receives sustenance, the Messenger is the medium. Sustenance is received through the grace and bounty of the Messenger, and since the Messenger is a provider (raziq), there is no harm in asking for our prayers directly from them. Then, the next conclusion is that what did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) leave for us when leaving the world? The Quran and the Ahl-e-Bayt, his Itrat. He entrusted the Quran and Ahl-e-Bayt to us. Just as the Messenger was the proof (hujjah) of Allah in his time, after the Messenger, his successors (awsiya), his progeny, his Itrat, and his Ahl-e-Bayt are the proofs of Allah. Therefore, just as the Messenger was the provider in his time, after him, his successors are also providers in their time. Hence, saying 'Ya Ali Madad' or 'Ya Sahib-e-Zaman Adrikni' is not Shirk, but the essence of Tawheed. And conversely, whoever denies these things is actually a denier of the Quran and the religion. Salla 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad.

title: Wilaayat-e-Ali (a.s.) Azaab-e-Ilaahi Se Bachaayegi | Ahle Tasannun Kitab Se Daleel
excerpt: This lecture discusses a significant hadith regarding the status of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as the fortress of Allah. The speaker cites the scholar Hakim al-Nishapuri and the narrator Abdullah ibn Umar to establish the authenticity of the tradition within Sunni sources. The core message emphasizes that accepting the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) serves as a divine protection against God's punishment and a path to salvation.
content:
First, listen that a very famous scholar passed away, Hakim al-Nishapuri. He mentioned this hadith in his book 'Shawahid al-Tanzil.' And who is the narrator of the hadith? The narrator of the hadith is Abdullah ibn Umar. Hakim al-Nishapuri has narrated this hadith in his book in this way. After stating the entire chain of narration, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Jibril said to me,' and Jibril said from Allah the Almighty, what did he say? 'The Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib is My fortress. Whoever enters My fortress is safe from My punishment.' This means that the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is the fortress of Allah. Whoever enters it—that is, whoever held the belief in the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and confessed to it—will find salvation and will enter Paradise.

title: EP12 | Imam -e- Adil Ya Imam -e- Zaalim? Faisla Aap Ka | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological and historical criteria for legitimate leadership in Islam, contrasting the Shia concept of an infallible Imam with the historical reality of oppressive rulers. The discussion emphasizes the divine requirements for Imamate, such as Nass and Ismah, while critiquing the historical suppression of authentic hadith regarding the Ahlulbayt. Ultimately, the session underscores that true obedience is reserved for Allah and the infallible Ulil Amr, rejecting the notion of blind submission to unjust authorities.
content:
Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. The discussion was about two types of Imams: one who claims Imamate while he is not an Imam. And under verse 174 of Surah Al-Baqarah, the tradition states, 'Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, will not purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.' So, let us look at another tradition in this regard, which Sheikh al-Ta'ifa, Sheikh Tusi (r.a.), has narrated in his book 'Majalis al-Anwar', that Imam Rida (a.s.) narrates from his forefathers that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... ...that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said that this verse, verse 174 of Surah Al-Baqarah, which was mentioned, about three types of people whom Allah will not speak to, will not accept any of their deeds, and for whom there will be a painful punishment. In this regard, the Prophet says, who are these people? This tradition is from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself. The Prophet says, 'Allah has forbidden Paradise to the person who oppresses my Ahl-e-Bayt, who kills my Ahl-e-Bayt, who imprisons my Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.). Allah has forbidden Paradise to him. And the one who helps against the Ahl-e-Bayt in any way, in any form, does any work against the Ahl-e-Bayt.' After that, the Prophet recited this verse, 'These are the people for whom there is no share in the hereafter, they will get nothing,' meaning there is no portion of Paradise for them, and Allah will not even speak to them. There is no speech for them, and Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will Allah look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He accept any of their deeds, and for them is a painful punishment. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was so concerned about the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) that He declared Paradise forbidden to anyone who oppressed the Ahlulbayt even by an atom's weight. Now, you look at history and see what the Ummah did to the Ahlulbayt. You see what they did; the entire history is before you. The moment the Prophet's eyes closed, the moment the Prophet departed from this world—the Prophet was martyred—and the sequence of events that began there is beyond description. They broke the sanctity to such an extent that the Princess (Fatima Zahra (s.a.)) had to recite a dirge: 'O Suya, such mountains of calamities were broken upon me that if they had fallen upon the days, they would have turned into nights.' If these calamities had fallen upon the days, they would have turned into nights. What kind of calamity was there that was not inflicted upon the Progeny of Muhammad (Aale Muhammad), and even today this... inflicted upon the Progeny of Muhammad (Aale Muhammad), and even today this sequence continues. InshaAllah, the details will keep coming; we will keep presenting them to you in each episode bit by bit. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explicitly stated that whoever kills them, whoever imprisons them—the Prophet knew all this was going to happen—and whoever does anything against them... There is another tradition similar to this one, with a slight difference, where the Prophet says that Paradise is forbidden to the one who oppresses my Ahlulbayt, fights them, and wages war against them. Now, you decide for yourself; you determine for yourself. Read history, look at what happened from 28th Safar, 11 Hijri onwards, and study it. See what was done, what the Ummah did. Which things will you deny? You say the door was not burned? You say no one came? While everything is present; historical evidence is present, documents are present. Everything is documented, yet still, there is denial, saying 'this did not happen, that did not happen.' Was a rope not put around the neck of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)? Was he not dragged? And they present arguments, 'If he was so brave, why did he do this? Why did he do that?' All such answers, InshaAllah... this did not happen, that did not happen. Was a rope not put around the neck of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)? Was he not dragged? And they present arguments, 'If he was so brave, why did he do this? Why did he do that?' All such answers, InshaAllah, will be given in their proper place. Right now, we are just pointing towards them. Well, suppose you say all these things—suppose for the sake of argument—then at least you will admit that the Battle of Jamal took place, or will you deny that too? You will admit that the Battle of Siffin took place, or will you deny that too? You will admit that the Tragedy of Karbala took place, or will you deny that too? How many things will you deny? History is present, history is a witness. And after that, what will you do with the things present in the books? What will you do with the things present in the Musnad (collections of hadith) with chains of narration? What will you do with what is present in the Sahih (authentic collections)? InshaAllah, we will present a document. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Whoever fights them, whoever opposes them'—in one manuscript it is written 'whoever objects to them'—Paradise is forbidden for them as well, and... whoever objects to them, Paradise is forbidden for them as well. And in one manuscript it says 'whoever opposes them.' Both have different meanings: 'whoever objects to them' and 'whoever opposes them.' Paradise is forbidden for both; Paradise is not lawful for them. And whoever curses the Ahlulbayt, Paradise is forbidden for them. Curses them! Now you tell me what was done to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), as we mentioned in the previous episodes—two or four episodes ago—that for 83 years, 70,000 pulpits were used to curse, and from every pulpit, it was mandatory for the one on the pulpit to curse Ali (a.s.). Curses were hurled. We mentioned that all these things are facts; no one can deny them. In the Hereafter, they have no share, nothing. Hell is straight for them. Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He accept any of their deeds. nor will He accept any of their deeds, and for them will be a painful punishment, a painful punishment. After that, the Imam (a.s.) says in the tradition, 'Paradise is forbidden for the one who claims Imamate while he is not worthy of it.' He is not worthy of Imamate. What does 'not worthy' mean? It means the conditions of Imamate are not found in him. There is no 'Nass' (divine designation) present for him, neither from the Quran nor from the Hadith. He has no knowledge of the Unseen, he has no Infallibility (Ismah), he has no bravery, he has no generosity. In battles, they were the first to flee; historical documents are present. We will mention everything, InshaAllah, when the battles are discussed. So, the Imam (a.s.) says that whoever is not worthy and is claiming Imamate, he is outside the fold of religion. Allahu Akbar! So, all the Hadith we have seen in the last three or four episodes—have you noticed that we discussed what the conditions are for being an Imam? Infallibility, knowledge of the Unseen, bravery, generosity, and the existence of proof and Nass from the Quran and the Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)... from the Quran and the Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—He must have explicitly announced his Imamate; only then is he an Imam, otherwise not. And if someone is claiming it, the claimant is a liar. The one who denies the true Imam is a liar, and the one who accepts both is also a liar. They are all destined for Hell. This is our stance, this is the stance of the School of Ahlulbayt. We have clarified everything in the light of the Quran and Hadith. Now let us see what happened in Islam. Look, this tragedy... we want Muslims to be educated. You read history, or the first thing that came was the revelation of 'Iqra' (Read) to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Read! But what did this Ummah become? An Ummah of 'Iqra la taqra' (Read, but do not read). They establish everything based on prejudice and fanaticism. Now you see what happened after Islam, that is, after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), after 28th Safar... after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), after 28th Safar, what happened? The very first decision made was that no one would narrate, copy, or write down the Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Nothing. A ban was imposed on everything; a total prohibition. If anyone narrated a Hadith, there was a severe punishment. And there were various excuses: 'Oh, that is a fabricated Hadith,' and this and that. No, because all the traditions contained the virtues of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (Aale Muhammad), that is why a ban was placed on them. On one side, that happened; on the other side, what happened was that Hadith were being manufactured. A factory of Hadith was created where Hadith began to be forged. Hadith were being forged in whose favor? In whose favor? Those who were enemies of the Ahlulbayt, those who had waged war against the Ahlulbayt. It was in their favor, and it was said, 'Whoever becomes the Imam, accept him. Whoever says I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah, accept him without any question.' accept him without any question. Absolutely. Now look at the traditions of other sects, besides the Shias. I won't say much, just a little. If you want to go into detail or want references, you can find plenty; it's not a big deal. But look at a few Hadith. This tradition that we are narrating for you is from Sahih Muslim. Now look at this Hadith: 'Qala Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.).' Look, pay attention to this. People claim, 'We also love the Ahlulbayt, we also love the Ahlulbayt,' but they remove their name from the Salawat (blessings) entirely. What do they say? 'Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam'—they removed 'Aalihi' (and his progeny). Oh brother, why do you have so much enmity towards the Ahlulbayt that you remove their name from the Salawat? Whereas their name was explicitly present in the Salawat during the Prophet's lifetime. And when someone recited only half the Salawat in front of the Prophet, only upon the Prophet, the Prophet said, 'This Salawat is 'Abtar' (cut off), it is an incomplete Salawat. Recite the full Salawat, recite it with 'Aalihi'.' Anyway, that is a separate debate. However, this is the tradition: The Prophet said, 'Whoever obeys an Amir...' The Prophet said, 'Whoever obeys an Amir, any Amir who becomes an Amir.' What principle did they establish? What foundation did they lay? 'Nahnu ma'a man ghalaba' (We are with whoever becomes victorious). Who becomes victorious? The one whom everyone comes and pledges allegiance to. All the Muslims pledged allegiance, so it's done. So, this became the rule. So, the Prophet says, 'Whoever obeys the Amir has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the Amir has disobeyed me.' They made this Hadith. The reference for this Hadith is Sahih Muslim, Hadith number 1835. Okay, this became a Hadith. Now you think, what is wrong with this? There is no harm in it. Now look at what is written next, so that, InshaAllah, the matter becomes completely clear to you. Now, the second Hadith is from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Prophet said, 'Do not declare your fellow believers, those who are of your religion, who say 'I am a Muslim,' as disbelievers (Takfir). Do not do Takfir, even if they commit a major sin. And pray behind every Imam, whoever stands up...' Allahu Akbar! Say 'Allahu Akbar.' In the School of Ahlulbayt, many conditions have been stated for an Imam of congregational prayer. The Imam of the prayer... The Imam of the prayer has many conditions. Here it is written, 'Pray behind every Imam, whoever stands up.' Say 'Allahu Akbar.' In the School of Ahlulbayt, we have traditions that you should not pray behind just anyone, unless... the meaning of the tradition is: do not pray behind just anyone, do not pray behind an unknown person until you are sure about him. It is talking about congregational prayer. Until you are sure of his justice (Adalah). At that time... now here, it is like this. And after that, this is present in the tradition. And after that, look at the next Hadith: The Prophet says—this tradition is explicitly present, and this tradition is from Sahih Muslim, Hadith number 1847—the Prophet says, 'There will be Imams after me. There will be Imams after me.' In the Hadith, 'La yahtaduna bi-hudaya' (They will not be guided by my guidance). Hudaaya, they will not be guided by my guidance, meaning they will not follow my guidance, they will not follow my instructions. 'Wala yattabi'una sunnati'—this is a narration from Sahih Muslim, we are not telling you this from Usul al-Kafi, this is not the limit—'la yattabi'una sunnati', they will not act upon my Sunnah. Well, when will they act upon the Prophet's Sunnah? Only when they are aware of it, right? So they will act... 'La yattabi'una sunnati, wa yaqumu fi-r-rijal, qulubuhum qulubu shayatin', and among them will stand men whose hearts are the hearts of devils. Allahu Akbar! Their hearts will be the hearts of devils, 'fi ajsami ins', in the bodies of humans. They will appear as humans, but their actual hearts will be those of devils. When people heard this Hadith, they were a bit worried, so they asked—the narrator says, 'Qultu: Kaifa ya Rasool Allah?'—'What if such a leader becomes our guide, or your successor comes, if such a Caliph of ours comes who claims this, then what should we do? In adrakta dhalika?' If we encounter such a Caliph, what should we do? Now look, the Hadith says: What should we do if we encounter them? Now look, the Hadith says: 'Isma' wa ati' al-amir', listen to the Amir and obey him, 'wa in daraba zahraka', even if he strikes your back, 'wa akhadha malaka', and even if he takes your wealth. Even if he strikes your back and even if your wealth is confiscated or snatched away, 'fisma' wa ati'', still listen and obey. Is it clear? It is absolutely clear, right? Meaning, this entire Hadith was fabricated so that you do not ask questions. If he doesn't know anything, it doesn't matter, still obey. If he is committing oppression, still obey. If he is committing major sins, still obey. So, if he is not following my Sunnah, still obey. If he is not acting upon my guidance, still obey. Whatever he does, just obey. Is this religion, or is this about preserving the government? Now, have you noticed that it is absolutely clear that you must accept their Imamate and their Caliphate in any way possible. But when you look at the Shia narrations, as you have seen so far, see what kind of narrations have come. The Amir (a.s.) says—this is present in Al-Kafi—'Ihdharu thalathatan min dinikum', beware of three types of people in your religion. Who are they? One... well, let's leave the other two, just the last one: 'Rajulun atahu Allahu sultanan', a man to whom Allah has given sovereignty, or made him an Imam—meaning Allah did not create an obstacle, He gave him authority. Okay, somehow he became a king, a Sultan. It is not said that he was made a successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and that he guided. No, only sovereignty, government, power came into his hands. 'Fama an atahu', so when he got the power, what did he start assuming? 'Anna ta'atuhu ta'atullahi', that his obedience is the obedience of Allah, 'wa ma'siyatuhu ma'siyatullahi', and his disobedience is the disobedience of Allah. He assumes this, 'wa kadhaba', and he is lying. This is his assumption, and he is lying. This assumption of his is wrong, it is a lie. 'Lianna la ta'ata li-makhluqin fi ma'siyati-l-khaliq', because if the Creator is being disobeyed, then in such disobedience, no creature should be obeyed. If any creature gives an order that is against the Quran and Sharia, which is against the teachings of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), then that obedience is not valid. 'Innama-t-ta'atu lillahi wa li-rasulihi wa li-uli-l-amr', obedience is for Allah, for His Messenger, and for the Ulil Amr. And this obedience is absolute, and it is alongside the obedience of Allah and His Messenger. Meaning, just as Allah and the Messenger cannot make a mistake, in that way, the Ulil Amr cannot make a mistake. 'Lianna-llaha azza wa jalla amara bi-ta'ati-r-rasuli ma'suman', and Allah commanded the obedience of the Messenger because the Messenger was infallible, and that is why the obedience of the Ulil Amr is also absolute, because they were infallible. All 12 Imams were infallible, that is why their obedience is obligatory without any 'ifs' or 'buts'. Obedience is obligatory without any 'ifs' or 'buts' because they were infallible. They followed Allah and His Messenger completely, and no sin was committed by them. They did not make any decision against the Quran and Hadith. So these were a few points that I presented for your service. Now, Insha'Allah, we will move to the next topic, which will be: who has been given the right to select the Imam? Who has the right to select the Imam? Insha'Allah, we will discuss this in the next episode. Wa al-hamdu lillahi rabbil 'alamin. Respected viewers, as announced, after every fourth episode of this 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' video series, there will be a quiz in which a few questions related to the previous four episodes will be asked. The link to the quiz is available in the video description and comment section. This link will remain live for one week, meaning you have a full week to submit your answers. If you are unable to answer any question, you can watch the video again to find the answer. All correct answers... try to give, and along with this, share these videos as much as possible. Participate in the quiz in large numbers and cooperate with us in conveying this message of Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to others so that you too may be included among those who propagate Wilayat.

title: Imam-e-Zamaana (a.t.f.s.) Ke Zariye Musibatein Door Hoti Hain - Ek Waqeya
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual status of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) as the final successor (Khatamul Awsiya) and his role in protecting the Shia community from calamities. Through an analysis of a historical encounter between the Imam and a narrator named Tarif, the speaker emphasizes the necessity of true recognition (marifat) of the Imam. The talk highlights that the Imam's existence serves as a shield against both physical and spiritual trials, particularly the preservation of faith in the modern era.
content:
And then what does the Imam say? 'And through me, Allah the Almighty keeps calamities away from my family and my Shia.' And through me—if you want my recognition (marifat)—then know that through me, Allah the Almighty keeps calamities away from my family, my household, and my Shia as well. That is, in this era, Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf) is the being, the sacred essence, due to whose existence calamities and troubles are averted and kept away from all Shia. Now let us move towards a hadith in which Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (ajtf) has been introduced as the final successor, his recognition has been provided, and this hadith is from Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf) himself. The incident is such that the name of the narrator is Tarif. Tarif says that I once went to the service of the Imam-e-Zamana myself. This means Tarif was among those who were allowed to be in the Imam's service, meaning he had permission from the Imam to come to him and meet him, and to meet him while recognizing him. Now, from this, you can gauge the hadith; the nature of this hadith is different. So, as soon as I entered, the Imam ordered me to bring a 'Sandal-e-Ahmar'—a red-colored sandalwood that was kept in a place. The Imam said, 'Bring that.' So Tarif brought it. I brought it. As soon as I brought it, the Imam asked me a question. What was the question the Imam asked? Now this question is very interesting. The Imam asked, 'Do you recognize me?' Tarif, do you recognize me? This incident is likely from the life of Imam Hassan al-Askari (a.s.). That is, the martyrdom of Imam Hassan al-Askari (a.s.) had not yet occurred. Since this is a household incident, the meeting with Imam-e-Zamana is taking place inside the house. This means Tarif could go to the house of Imam al-Askari (a.s.). So, the Imam-e-Zamana asked Tarif, 'Do you recognize me?' Tarif said, 'Yes.' Then the Imam asked, 'Who am I?' So he said, 'You are my master and the son of my master.' That is, Tarif thought—if you understand Tarif's answer—that you are a prince. That is, you are an Imam, you are the son of my Imam, so therefore you are also an Imam, you are also my master. So Tarif answered as if to a prince. 'Are you a prince?' The Imam said, 'I did not ask you about this.' Now look, it is a strange question. Tarif saying that you are my master, my Imam, the son of my Imam—but the Imam did not deny that. However, the Imam turning back and asking, 'Did you even understand what I am asking? What is my question?' What was the Imam's question? 'Do you recognize me?' The question is about recognition (marifat). So this means the answer to this will be a very important aspect regarding the recognition of Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf). Meaning, if someone wants to attain the recognition (ma'rifat) of their Imam of the time, they must listen to this answer carefully and preserve it, noting what the Imam is stating. The Imam asked, 'I did not ask this.' Then the narrator says, 'Mawla, may my life be sacrificed for you, fa-bayyin li (then explain it to me yourself).' Now, this is also a form of etiquette in conversing with the Imam, that you would explain it better. In other words, the narrator is saying to the Imam, 'Mawla, you yourself grant me your recognition.' So, pay close attention to the answer that comes from the Imam (a.s.). Now, what does the Imam (a.s.) say? 'Ana khatamul awsiya' (I am the last of the successors). Meaning, I am the final Wasi. This means the Imam (a.s.) has clarified the aspect of his recognition. An important aspect of the recognition of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.) is to know him as the final successor. Meaning, no new Imam will come after him. He is the final Imam, the final Wasi. And then what does the Imam say? 'Wa bi yadfa'ullahu azza-wa-jalla al-bala an ahli wa shi'ati' (And through me, if you seek my recognition, know that through me, Allah azza-wa-jalla keeps calamities away from my family, my household, and my Shias). Meaning, in this era, the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.) is the being, the sacred essence, due to whose existence calamities and troubles are averted and kept away from all Shias. The Imam is 'Khatamul Awsiya', the final successor. This means whoever seeks the recognition of the Imam must especially remember and preserve this aspect of his recognition. Meaning that he is the final successor. Just as the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is the final Prophet—meaning the belief in his finality (khatamiyat) is essential, because if someone believes in another prophet after him, they fall outside the fold of religion—in the same way, the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.) is the final successor. Therefore, it is necessary to hold the belief in his finality. Whoever does not consider him the final Imam also falls outside the fold of religion. And then, when the Imam says that through me, Allah keeps all calamities away from my Shias and my household, it means that the calamities and troubles that do come upon us are very few. Many are those from which Allah has protected us solely due to the blessings of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) and his grace. If we want to remain safe from every calamity and trouble in the world, we must draw closer to our Imam. The closer we get to our Imam, the more we are protected. While worldly calamities may still occur, the greatest calamity from which the Imam will keep us away is the calamity of faith—that a person's faith will not be corrupted. Their faith will remain firm. They will hold a steadfast belief in their Imam. And what is that belief? The belief whose most important part is to consider their Imam as the final Imam, after whom there is no other.

title: Qayaamat Mein Quran Kaise Madad Karega? (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture explores the intercessory role of the Holy Quran on the Day of Judgment based on a narration from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.). It explains how the Quran will appear in a beautiful form to testify for those who dedicated their lives to its recitation and practice. The speaker emphasizes that the level of one's devotion to the Quran in this world directly determines their elevated status and rank in Paradise.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. As-salamu 'alaykum... [Recitation]... As narrated, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) said: On the Day of Judgment, the Holy Quran will appear in a very beautiful form. When it passes among the Muslims, the Muslims will say, 'This person is always passing by them.' It will reach near the Prophets (a.s.), and the Prophets (a.s.) will say, 'This is one of us.' Passing by them, it will come to the angels who are close to Allah, and they too will say, 'This is one of us.' Then it will pass by them as well and stand in the presence of the Lord of Honor, the Almighty, and will call out: 'O my Lord! This person used to endure thirst for my sake and spent the whole night in my recitation, and that person did not endure thirst for my sake, nor did he spend the whole night in my recitation.' And that person did not endure thirst for my sake, nor did he spend the whole night in my recitation. Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala will say: 'Take them to their place in Paradise.' And then the Holy Quran will stand, and those people will also stand with it and follow it. The Holy Quran will say to them: 'Ascend and climb the ranks.' After this, the Imam (a.s.) said: 'Then that believer will continue to recite the verses of the Holy Quran and will ascend the ranks of Paradise until every one of those people reaches their place in Paradise.' After that, the Holy Quran will return from there. From this Hadith, it becomes clear that the more a person recites the Holy Quran, the higher their ranks in Paradise will be. Besides this, as we saw in this, the Holy Quran itself will intercede for us in the presence of Allah if we have recited the Holy Quran in the world. Meaning, whoever keeps the Quran with them in the world, the Quran will be with them on the Day of Judgment until it takes that person to their place in Paradise. We pray in the presence of the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability to recite the Holy Quran as much as possible and hastens the reappearance of our Master, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Amin, Ya Rabbal 'Alamin. We pray in the presence of the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability to recite the Holy Quran as much as possible and hastens the reappearance of our Master, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Amin, Ya Rabbal 'Alamin.

title: EP#11: Bibi Fatima (s.a.) Darwaaze Par Kyun Aayin?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the historical circumstances surrounding Bibi Fatima (s.a.) appearing at her door following the events after the Prophet's passing. It clarifies that she approached the door not to welcome the oppressors, but to confront them and complete the divine proof (Hujjat) against their rebellion. By speaking out, she ensured that no future generation could claim ignorance regarding the identity of those inside or the nature of the aggression committed against the Ahlulbayt.
content:
What reason did Janabe Zahra (s.a.) give for coming to the door? When Imam Ali (a.s.) refused to pledge allegiance to the oppressors after coming out of the house, it is found in the narrations that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) closed the door in the faces of those people. Meaning, firstly, the Bibi did not go to open the door, but to close it. The second time when those people came again, Janabe Fizza (s.a.) turned them away. Even then, those people did not listen and called Moula Ali (a.s.) outside for the pledge of allegiance. Then Bibi Zahra (s.a.) came and stood behind the door and said, 'O misguided and lying people, what do you want?' It was said to her, 'O Fatimah, what has happened to your husband that you have been sent to the door, and he himself is hiding behind the curtain?' Upon this, the Bibi said to that oppressor, 'Your rebellion, O wretched one, has forced me to come here, to complete the proof (Hujjat) upon you and every misguided and rebellious person.' Meaning, the Bibi came to the door and completed the proof upon those people in such a way that until the Day of Judgment, those oppressors and their supporters could not say that if they had known who was behind the door, they would never have set fire to it.

title: Zohair Ibn Qain Ki Imam Husain (a.s.) Se Mulaaqaat | #muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture explores the transformative encounter between Zuhayr ibn Qayn and Imam Husayn (a.s.) during the journey to Karbala. It highlights how a prophecy from Salman al-Farsi regarding the Imam's mission shifted Zuhayr's perspective from being an Uthmani to a devoted companion. The talk emphasizes the importance of sacrificing everything for the sake of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and finding joy in their service.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. May Allah increase our reward and yours for our grief over Husayn (a.s.). Dear viewers, we have often heard in gatherings regarding Janab Zuhayr ibn Qayn al-Bajali, how he was setting up his tent separately from Imam Husayn (a.s.), and then, after meeting the Imam, he immediately became a devotee of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and became ready to sacrifice his life for him. So, what was that matter due to which Janab Zuhayr, immediately after meeting Imam Husayn, became ready to sacrifice his life for him, whereas history tells us that he was previously an 'Uthmani'—meaning he did not even believe in the Imam's Imamate? But one meeting with the Infallible Imam has such an effect, a single glance of grace from the Infallible Imam, that Janab Zuhayr immediately became a lover of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and was ready to sacrifice his life. Not once, but a hundred times—when on the night of Ashura, Imam Husayn (a.s.) extinguished the lamp and told his companions that whoever wants to leave may go, Janab Zuhayr uttered these words: 'If I were to die a hundred times and be brought back to life a hundred times, I would still wish to sacrifice my life for you, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), in your defense.' So, Janab Zuhayr himself reveals the secret of what that matter was that made him join Imam Husayn immediately after the meeting. When Janab Zuhayr divorced his wife and, after paying her dowry, set her free, while saying goodbye to his friends, he said, 'I will tell you something because of which we can understand why Janab Zuhayr joined Imam Husayn (a.s.).' He says that when we were returning from a battle, a campaign, which we had gone to by sea, we met Janab Salman. In this battle, we had attained a great deal of spoils and a great victory. Janab Salman said at that time, 'O Zuhayr, are you happy because Allah gave you this victory and you received these spoils?' Zuhayr said, 'Yes.' Janab Salman said to him, 'Idha adraktum sayyida shababi ali Muhammadin alayhis-salam' (When you reach the Master of the Youth of the Family of Muhammad, peace be upon him—referring to Imam Husayn), 'Fakunu ashadda farahan bi-qitalikum ma'ahu' (Then be much happier to fight alongside him) than you are today with the spoils you have received. This should be a cause of great joy for you. This should be your greatest joy, compared to the spoils you have received today, which make you happy. It will be a much greater joy when you fight alongside Imam Husayn (a.s.) in his defense and protection. This will be a cause of great joy for you. And after meeting Imam Husayn, Janab Zuhayr remembered this—meaning Imam Husayn (a.s.) reminded Janab Zuhayr of this incident with Janab Salman, due to which he immediately joined Imam Husayn (a.s.) and sacrificed his life in his defense. So, dear viewers, this should be a great matter for us too, that we also dedicate our lives to the defense of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Our lives, our wealth, our children, and everything in our possession, we should sacrifice in the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Insha'Allah, and this should be our greatest joy. May the blessings of Allah be upon Muhammad and his pure, clean, and infallible family, and may the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies.

content:

Open this link; if it does not open, copy it, open the Google Chrome browser on your phone, tablet, or laptop, and paste the link there. Once the link opens, click on the Google icon you see and select the Gmail ID through which you want to participate in this quiz. [Recitation of Quranic verses and Hadith]. Some people are surprised, and some people ask, 'Is Imam Mahdi (a.s.) superior to the Prophets?' In the first volume of his book 'Aujaz al-Siyar' (page 222, Hadith 241), Muhammad ibn Sirin narrates from... Muhammad ibn Sirin narrates that Mahdi (a.s.) is superior to them, or rather, equal to them. And immediately after this, in Hadith number 242, he writes, 'Indeed, he, meaning Imam Mahdi (a.s.), is superior to the Prophets.' Readers, this same Muhammad ibn Sirin, in a Hadith narrated by Hafiz Sulaiman al-Qanduzi in 'Yanabi al-Mawadda' (page 150), states that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is superior to all Prophets except for Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Whoever believes in the 124,000 Prophets should also believe in the Imamate and Caliphate of the 12 Imams, and in this age, the Imamate and Caliphate of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). We are surprised by the objections of some people because it is a proven fact that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) being superior to the Prophets of the Children of Israel is not doubted by anyone, but... But when it comes to the successor of the Prophet, they find the superiority of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) surprising. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds to hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and grant us the ability to remain steadfast in his obedience. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. title: Imam Sadiq (a.s.) Ka Pasandeeda Amal: Umme Khalid (r.a.) Ka Mukammal Waqeah | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the story of Umme Khalid, a devoted student of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) who faced severe persecution for her love of Imam Ali (a.s.). The lecture contrasts the steadfastness of Abu Basir, who adheres strictly to Quranic and Hadith-based arguments for Tabarra, against those like Kasir Nawa who compromise their principles. The speaker emphasizes the importance of unwavering commitment to the Wilayat of the Imams and the proper application of Taqiyya.
content:
Now, which of these two do you like more? Do you like Abu Basir, or Kasir Nawa and his ashab, who are the 'patryun', the goats, who say both are good? This is also good, that is also good. They have decorated it with flowers, and thorns are also in the bouquets. This lady, Khalid, had the intention, who gave a great sacrifice in the path of Muhammad. Now look at what is written in the book, we will read it out to you. Not from ourselves. This Abu Basir, Abu Basir is a famous Sahabi, the student of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Among them, our, among them, they say that when Khalid, when the Imam was not doing it, Khalid had come. Now what is written in the book? 'Ilaihi gana Yusuf', these were the ones whose both hands were cut off by Yusuf, the ruler of Baghdad, the governor, the governor in Baghdad. And why were they cut off? In the love of Ali. In the love of Ali, this is the one who said, 'I am...'. Imam (a.s.) asked Abu Basir, 'Do you want to hear the words of Khalid? You talk about another matter, that this is among them, Khalid, Abu Basir's...' And talk about another matter, that this was among them, Khalid, Abu Basir's student, she was also a student, she used to attend classes. So keep this in mind. So the Imam asks Abu Basir, 'Do you want to hear the words of Khalid? Any name?' I said, 'Okay, my life be sacrificed for you.' 'Kalam lafat na', if it is so, then do one thing, sit here behind, sit there. There was proficiency in language, meaning, in the degree, the eloquence and rhetoric in the language of the people, 'fasahat' and 'balahat'. 'Fasad' is, then 'fulan' and 'fulan'. Then among them, Khalid asked the Imam about those who drank the right of Ali. The condition of the time was very bad, Mansur al-Dawaniqi was there, it was the era, he was the one who martyred them. The Imam told her to practice 'Taqiyya' at that time, and I, Khalid, was also towards this, 'Isla laki', I will tell Allah on the Day of Judgment that you ordered me to follow them. He was explaining 'Taqiyya' to her, but she was very intense in her 'rabs', women are emotional, anyway, very emotional. Emotional, anyway, she was very emotional. Imam, okay, no problem. The Imam explained 'Taqiyya' to her, but even on this, she is less. She said, 'Panna hath lagi man ka', but this one sitting behind you, he is... 'Bas ye alag tan fishesh da', oh, he was saying to me that 'do this'. So this is saying, 'What is it? Roz nawa vashab hu', and Kasir Nawa, who is the 'barat han bahu', with him, the other goats, these people say that I did not build on the Wilayat of Imam (a.s.). These people say that you accept the opinion of those who drank the right of Ali. You speak, now which of these two do you like more? Do you like Abu Basir, or Kasir Nawa and his ashab, who are the 'patryun', the goats, who say both are good? This is also good, that is also good. They have decorated it with flowers, and thorns are also in the bouquets. So which one do you like? Out of these two, which one do you like? Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, you are understanding, this woman is not one to believe in 'Taqiyya'. By God, Abu Basir and his ashab, in my view, Kasir Nawa and his ashab have no value in my eyes, but Abu Basir has, who is obedient to the command, because Abu Basir is the one who... Because Abu Basir is the one who, for his 'Tabarra', only presents arguments from those things that Allah has revealed, meaning, besides the Quran and Hadith, there is no other thing. And the Imam recited the last part of verses 44, 45, and 47 of Surah Al-Ma'idah, meaning, whoever does not judge by the Quran and Hadith, he is a tyrant, a disbeliever. And Abu Basir, the judgment he makes, he makes it from the Quran and Hadith, and Kasir Nawa and his ashab do not do it from the Quran and Hadith. The Imam is presenting this argument, meaning, he is bringing arguments for 'Tabarra' from the Quran and Hadith. Now, Khalid, whatever there was to hear, she heard it.

title: Jo Allah Ki Rehmat Chahta Hai, Wo Azadaari Kare | Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual significance of Azadari and gathering to remember the Ahlulbayt. The speaker references a narration from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) highlighting that those who revive the cause of the Imams are blessed with Allah's mercy. It concludes by noting the immense reward of forgiveness for those who shed tears in remembrance of the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
Whoever desires the mercy of Allah, let him perform Azadari. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said to Fazl ibn Yasar, 'Do you people sit and narrate Hadith among yourselves?' Fazl said, 'Yes, Mawla, my life be sacrificed for you.' Then the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Indeed, I like such gatherings. So, O Fazl, revive our Amr, meaning our Wilayat. Fa rahimallahu man ahya amrana. May Allah have mercy on the person who revives our Amr. O Fuzail, whoever remembers us, or our mention is made in front of him, and even a tear equal to the wing of a fly flows from his eye, Allah will forgive all his sins, even if his sins are more than the foam of the sea.'

title: Masaaib | Shahaadat -e- Ameerul Momineen Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) | 21 Maahe Ramazan 1443
excerpt: This lecture commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) on the 21st of Ramadan. The speaker reflects on the profound grief felt by the Ummah, describing Imam Ali as the father of the believers and a pillar of support for the needy. Through the historical account of Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i and the final moments of the Imam, the lecture emphasizes the immense tragedy and the deep sorrow experienced by his family and companions.
content:
La ilaha, la ilaha, la ilaha, la ilaha, la ilaha, la ilaha, la ilaha, la ilaha. La hawla wala quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azeem. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Creator of creation, the Provider of sustenance, the Creator of the morning, the Lord of Majesty, Honor, Grace, and Bounty. Then, blessings and peace, greetings and honor, be upon our master, our prophet, our intercessor, the beloved of our hearts, the physician of our souls, and our master and leader, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. And upon his pure, purified, infallible, oppressed, awaited, guided, and guiding family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. And may the peace of Allah, the Lord, hasten the relief of his noble presence, and may the curse of Allah be upon their enemies, the usurpers of their rights, the deniers of their virtues and merits, and all those who follow them. To proceed, Allah the Almighty has said: 'Indeed, we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return.' Yes, dear respected ones, mourners of the Commander of the Faithful, this is the night of resurrection that has appeared. This is the night of resurrection, this is also the night of martyrdom, this is also the night of tragedy, this is also the night of resurrection. Ask Zainab's heart, ask Umm Kulthum's heart what they are going through. Ask the hidden Imam of the Time what he is going through. Yes, dear ones, wearing these black clothes, with these eyes of ours, beating our heads and chests, we are saying to our Mawla, 'O Imam of our time, O our master and leader, today you have not just become an orphan, today not only has Zainab become an orphan, today not only has Umm Kulthum become an orphan.' The Prophet said, 'I and Ali are the fathers of this Ummah,' we have all become orphans. This is the night of the orphanhood of the universe. Do not ask us how great this tragedy is; oh, the one whose father dies, he is truly an orphan. Ashrafu mallahu, dear respected ones, Ali, who is Ali? That Ali who was the support of the orphans, that Ali who was the hope of the widows, that Ali who was the comfort of the needy. Yes, which Ali? The same Ali who is 'Asbarus Sabireen' (the most patient of the patient). Which Ali? The same Ali who has endured the most patience. Which Ali? The same Ali who is the first oppressed one. Yes, dear respected ones, the grief of Ali, the separation of Ali, the mourning of Ali, what is the grief of Ali? Someone go and ask the followers of Ali, ask the companions of Ali what the grief of Ali is, what the separation of Ali is. After the martyrdom of the Commander of the Faithful, your companion Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i reached the palace of the Pharaoh of Syria, reached the court, Muawiyah, the cursed one of the abyss, looked at him once and said, 'Ali did not do justice to you.' Listen, dear respected ones, Insha'Allah you will weep and offer condolences in the court of the Imam of the Time. Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i had three sons: Tariq, Turfa, Turaif. Once, that cursed one looked at Adi and said, 'Ali did not do justice to you. You had three sons, all three were killed at Siffin. Ali's sons survived, your sons were killed.' As soon as he heard this, a follower of Ali, Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, trembled and cried out, 'I did not do justice to Ali!' Listen, dear respected ones, they have come to offer condolences, they have come to weep. What did that cursed one say? 'Ali did not do justice to you.' He says, 'I did not do justice to Ali.' Once, he was surprised, and in surprise, he says, 'What are you saying? You did not do justice to Ali?' Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i says, 'Yes, I did not do justice to Ali, because Ali was killed, and I remained alive. Ali was killed, and I remained alive.' That cursed one looks at Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i and says, 'Adi, how was your Mawla? How was your Ali?' Now, consider this night as a lament or a eulogy, consider it the praise of the Mawla or the tragedies of the Mawla. I am conveying the meaning; Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i looked at him once and said, 'Why do you ask how my Mawla was? That Ali who used to worship at night, that Ali who used to fast during the days. Go and ask the orphans of Kufa how my Mawla was, go and ask those poor people how my Ali was.' In this way, he mentioned my Mawla. Once, that cursed one, in surprise, says, 'O Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, how are you bearing the grief of such an Ali, the separation of such an Ali?' Now, those who have come to weep, who have come to offer condolences, how are you bearing the grief of such an Ali, the separation of such an Ali? Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i says, 'In the grief of Ali, my state is like that mother in whose lap her young son gasps and breathes his last.' Ashrafu mallahu, Ashrafu mallahu, Ashrafu mallahu. That Ali, that Ali, alas! In what state has our Mawla spent today? What is the condition of our Mawla today? A strike has hit his head, a strike has hit his head. Sarkar-e-Anees has described that scene when the strike happened. He says, 'In prostration, the Lion of Truth was struck again, the pillars and walls of the mosque began to tremble, the prayer niche became soaked in blood, an earthquake descended upon the earth, Gabriel cried out from the heavens that calamity has struck, in prostration to the Truth, the Commander of the Arabs was martyred.' Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Ashrafu mallahu, Ashrafu mallahu. What kind of wound was on the head of the Commander of the Faithful? What kind of wound was on the head of the Commander of the Faithful? Listen, dear respected ones, I will narrate a tradition, the month of Ramadan is ongoing. You recite Dua-e-Abu Hamza al-Thumali, you recite it. It is narrated from Hazrat Abu Hamza al-Thumali—apparently, he was not present at that time, he narrates from Amr ibn Habib—he says that as soon as the news reached that a strike had hit Ali's head, we reached the house of the Commander of the Faithful. Now, when I entered the service of Ali, what did I see? What scene did I see? The Commander of the Faithful is on the bed, there is a wound on his head, there is a wound on his head, a bandage is applied to it. Ali's companions are standing by Ali's bed, Hassan is present, Hussain is present, Muhammad al-Hanafiyyah is present, Ali's companions are standing by Ali, Hujr is there, Sasa is there, Asbagh ibn Nubata is there, the Shurtatul Khamis (the elite guard) is present by the bed of the Commander of the Faithful. So he describes the scene, he says that there were tears in everyone's eyes, but everyone was suppressing their tears because of Ali. Lest the Commander of the Faithful be further distressed by our weeping. Everyone was keeping their tears under control. Suddenly someone said, 'Go and call the surgeon, go and call the surgeon.' The greatest surgeon of Kufa, Aseer ibn Amr, was called. 'Come and examine the head wound of the Commander of the Faithful.' He arrived, he said, 'Bring a sheep's lung vein, bring a sheep's lung vein.' Listen, dear respected ones, the scene, the tradition, I cannot even read it completely, I am just giving hints. As soon as the sheep's lung vein came, he opened the bandage from the Commander of the Faithful's head once, and after opening the bandage, he takes the vein and puts it into the wound of our Mawla's blessed head to examine the wound. Listen, dear respected ones, what does the sermon describe? That the wound was so deep that the vein went beyond half of the head. Once, people, everyone asks, 'Tell us, will our Mawla recover? Tell us, will our Mawla be alright? You tell us, will the Commander of the Faithful recover?' He looks at the vein once, looks at Ali once, looks at the vein, looks at Ali, he did not say anything, he looked at Ali and started weeping loudly. Ali, who was suppressing his tears, everyone was wailing, a resurrection took place in Ali's house, Hassan is weeping, Hussain is weeping, the surgeon is saying, 'Commander of the Faithful, make your will.' O Allah! I have been left all alone. Father! You have left me alone. The daughter of Ali and Fatima, the belief of Ali, you have left me alone. O Father! You have left me all alone. Allah! Masha'Allah. Ya Allah! Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka antas-sami'ul-alim.

title: Majlis 9 | Imam: Ilaahi Rahnuma | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological necessity of the Imam as a divine guide and the central role of the Ahlulbayt in human salvation. It connects the historical struggles of the Imams, particularly the occultation of the twelfth Imam, with the broader themes of justice, sacrifice, and the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge from the 'People of the Reminder' and highlights the spiritual link between the mission of Imam Hussain and the future reappearance of the Imam of the Time.
content:
O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; by the morning, Zainab will be separated from her brother. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; the sleeping nation will not be able to sleep again. Even if she wants to cry, she will not be able to; she will not be able to meet Asghar again. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; the children are terrified, the mothers are trembling. Let me pray for Ali Akbar to my heart's content; I still have to take away the afflictions of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; O night, scatter as far as you can. By tomorrow, the signs of the Prophet's beloved will be erased; this scene remains until the mourning of Ali Akbar. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; the thirst of every child is still remaining. There is some longing in the eyes and some hope remains, but my brother, my Abbas, is still with me. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; the ark of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) still remains. Shabbir's (Imam Hussain's) chest is there to put his daughter to sleep; Sakina is swinging the cradle of Ali Asghar. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated; who will listen to my cries tomorrow? The dagger will also reach my brother's throat; the tent will be gone, and this veil will not be on my head. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated. O night, let there be peace for a moment; my helpers will be surrounded by the ranks of the enemy. These moon-like faces will be covered in blood. O night, do not pass, for Zainab will be devastated. [Arabic prayers and salutations]. Sayyid al-Shuhada (the Master of Martyrs) says: 'Whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped, Allah will grant him more than his wishes and needs.' Whatever he desires and whatever his needs are, Allah will give him more than that. The points I have been presenting to you continuously are that Ma'rifat (gnosis/recognition) is very necessary for worship. When a person has Ma'rifat, only then do they truly recognize the Imam, and accordingly, they obey the Imam. They learn the correct method of worship; they learn the right way, how worship is performed, and how a person can attain Sa'adat (felicity). That is, what it means to become a dweller of Paradise, and how one can achieve success in both this world and the hereafter. Yesterday, I was submitting to you that the presence of the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda) on earth is very necessary, because if the Proof of Allah is not there, a person will never know the right path. And this 'Hujjat'—it is called Hujjat because through it, Allah completes His argument. By sending this Proof, Allah completes His argument so that people have no excuse left. So, yesterday I submitted to you why the Proof of Allah is necessary, and there are many proofs for this. In fact, Allama Majlisi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alaih), when he begins the discussion in 'Bihar al-Anwar' in the 'Kitab al-Imama', the first chapter he brings is 'Bab al-Ihtiyaaj ilal-Hujjat' (The Chapter on the Need for the Proof). He brings many hadiths and many proofs—the proofs that the Imams themselves presented. Allama Majlisi presents all these proofs, meaning he presents the hadiths. There is not enough time to go into full detail, but I will briefly present one or two hadiths for you, and you will see how it shows why such a guide is necessary, and if that guide is not there, a person will certainly be misguided and stray from the path. Look at this tradition where Imam Baqir (a.s.) says: [Salutations]. Look at the logic the Imam presents. He says: 'When one of you travels a few kilometers'—'Farasikh' is the plural of 'Farsakh', meaning a distance—'when you travel even a short distance, for example, going from one city to another, what happens? You seek a guide for yourself.' Because if a person goes anywhere in that city, that country, or anywhere in the world, they look for a guide who will tell them what is where, because they are not familiar with it. And no person would ever suggest 'trial and error' because, through trial and error, they might not even be able to see one city. And if a person is traveling, especially if the journey is very important, it is very necessary for them to have such a guide. This is the Imam's argument—see, someone who shows the path, who shows the method, where to go, how to go, and how to achieve more things in less time, or how to benefit more in less time. The Imam says: 'He seeks a guide for himself.' And you are even more ignorant of the paths of the heavens than you are of the paths of the earth. Now, listen to the Master's words: 'You are ignorant of the paths of the earth, but you are completely ignorant of the paths of the heavens; you know nothing about them.' Now, remember this sentence and let us go to that personality who is called 'Saluni' (Ask me), Ali ibn Abi Talib, standing on the pulpit... He says repeatedly, "Saluni qabla an tafqiduni." Ask me before you lose me. "Qabla an tafqiduni." Before you lose me, meaning before I depart from among you, I will no longer be in your midst, so then from whom will you ask? "Qabla an tafqiduni." And look at the sentence that follows. He says, "Fa-inni a'lamu bi-turuqis-sama-i min turuqil-arz." I am more familiar with the paths of the heavens than I am with the paths of the earth. Subhan Allah. Meaning, as for the paths of the earth, a human can still somehow manage to find some routes. Mawla says, "What are the paths of the earth? Ask me about the paths of the heavens. I will tell you those." And not just one heaven, ask me about the seven heavens, I will tell you. Ask me whatever you wish. But the Arabs were so ignorant, just think—if you look at them today, you can estimate how ignorant they must have been in that era. They were so ignorant that they would ask, "Well, tell us how many lice are on our camel?" How many grains are in the desert? How many stars are in the sky? What benefit is there in this? These are the questions they were asking Ali. If anyone did ask, it was those from other religions who had a little bit of intellect. This was absolutely not present among the Muslims, and it is not present even today. It was neither in that era nor is it today. So, those from other religions would come and ask, "Well Ali, tell us, where is Allah?" First, they went to the one sitting on the throne and asked him where Allah is. He said, "Allah is above." So the Jew immediately retorted, "If He is above, does that mean the earth is empty of Allah? Is He not on the earth?" Then the big leaders got furious. They said, "You have made the mosque impure, get out of here." And so on. Anyway, the famous hadith is that Janabe Salman brought them to the Mawla of the universe, because those people were leaving. They said, "So this, this is Islam? This is Islam?" Those people were mocking and laughing. Because there were 40 of them. They were all laughing, "This is Islam?" Just as the world laughs today, they were laughing then. So Janabe Salman was present there. He took them and introduced them to Ali (a.s.), or in another hadith, he brought Ali (a.s.) to them. There are different accounts, different narrations. Anyway, the Mawla of the universe asked, "What is my question?" They said, "Where is Allah?" He replied, "The question is wrong." Why is it wrong? He said, "He created space." He encompasses space. He can contain space. Therefore, asking 'where' is not correct for Him. So, "Aynal ayn"—He also created time, He created space. So, one cannot ask about Him in terms of time and space. He encompasses all space, He encompasses all time, He encompasses everything, therefore it is not correct to ask about Him. And in this way, they asked many questions and Mawla kept answering each one. Then they realized that something was wrong. So they asked, "You are giving all these answers, then who is this great man?" He said, "You got the answer to your question, didn't you?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Go and do your work." So Imam Baqir (a.s.) says that you are completely ignorant of the paths of the heavens. You might know the paths of the earth—meaning you might know something about them—but as for the heavens, the paths of the heavens mean the Hereafter, you know nothing about that. You know nothing about the Unseen. The Quran itself has said, "Yas'alunaka 'anir-ruh." O Prophet! They come to you and ask about the soul, tell them about the soul. "Qul," O Prophet! Tell them, "Ar-ruhu min amri rabbi." The soul is from the command of my Lord. "Wama utitum minal 'ilmi illa qalila." And you have not been given knowledge except a little. You have no knowledge at all; people have no knowledge. If you want knowledge, come to the door of the Ahlulbayt. They are the ones saying, "Come to us, we will tell you." Allah is saying in the Quran that you do not have knowledge. Allah says, "Fas'alu ahlad-dhikri in kuntum la ta'lamun." Go and ask the People of the Reminder, O Muslims! Why do you not have intellect? Why do you not use your intellect? Go and ask the People of the Reminder. When someone is sick, they go to a doctor. When there is a legal problem, they go to a lawyer. When there is an engineering issue, they go to an engineer. In every profession, a person goes to an expert. Similarly, in religious matters, go to your Imam, the Imams, go to the Ahlulbayt, and then if the Ahlulbayt have said that in matters, go to—meaning ask the Maraje, ask the scholars, ask the jurists, seek it from them, they will tell you. Go and read, read the narrations, read the hadiths. But you abandoned the door of the Ahlulbayt. You distanced yourselves from the Ahlulbayt. Rather, no, you are bent on enmity with the Ahlulbayt. It is the same even today. They mock, they ridicule. And that is why you see the consequences. So Mawla says, "Fatlubu li-nafsika dalila." Therefore, seek a proof for yourself, seek a guide for yourself. And who is that guide? That is the Hujjat of Allah. That is why the Mawla of the universe says in a famous, well-known hadith, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). He says, "Allahumma," the Mawla of the universe points towards the sky and says, "Allahumma la budda laka min hujjatin fi arzika." O Lord! It is necessary that Your proofs be on the earth. Your guides, whom You have appointed, must be on the earth. "Hujjatun ba'da hujjatin." It is necessary to have one guide after another. It is necessary to have a guide in every era. In the theological service, I had submitted that a Hujjat is one who is the axis of the universe. The Imam is the one who is the axis of the universe. The Imam is the one upon whose foundation existence stands. That is called an Imam. An Imam is not made just by appointing someone. The Imam is the axis of the universe. Therefore, it is necessary for the Imam, the Hujjat, to exist. That is why the narration I presented in the theological service, I present it to you again, "Al-hujjatu qablal khalqi wa ma'al khalqi wa ba'dal khalqi." The Hujjat, the Hujjat of Allah, is before the creation. The Hujjat of Allah is with the creation, with the creation, and the Hujjat of Allah is after the creation. In other words, all of creation is like a body, and the Hujjat is like the soul. The soul of the entire creation is the Hujjat of Allah. Through whom Allah creates the universe, creates the entire creation. So Mawla says, it is necessary to have one Hujjat after another in every era. These are the words of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Why? "Li-alla," look at one benefit, what is the necessity? "Li-alla yatafarraqa atba'u awliya'ika." So that the followers of Your Awliya, meaning the followers of the Imams, "la yatafarraqa," do not become scattered, do not become dispersed, do not go here and there. Meaning, they should remain with one banner, with one guide, with one leader. A leader who will be in every era, they will gather around that leader. And this is what the Quran also says, "Wa'tasimu bi-hablillahi jami'an wa la tafarraqu." Look, hold firmly to the rope of Allah so that you do not become divided. So that there is no division, meaning disunity, among you. So on what basis should there be unity among Muslims? It should be on the Hablullah al-Matin (the firm rope of Allah). Meaning, if Muslims want unity and oneness, if they want unity, then what is the only way for that unity? It is around Ali ibn Abi Talib and his progeny. There is no other way. If humans want to go on other paths, then let them go wherever they want, Allah has made everyone free in the world. But then there cannot be unity. Because truth and falsehood can never gather in one place. Where there is truth, there will be no falsehood. Where there is falsehood, there will be no truth. That is why Allah has not created two hearts in the existence of any human. "Ma ja'alallahu li-rajulin min qalbayni fi jawfihi." Allah has created only one heart. So, the one in whose heart there is love for Adam, there will be no love for Satan in his heart. The one in whose heart there is love for Qabil, there will be no love for Qabil in his heart. The one in whose heart there is love for Ibrahim, there cannot be love for Nimrod in his heart. The one in whose heart there is love for Musa, there cannot be love for Pharaoh in his heart. The one in whose heart, the one in whose heart there is love for the Messenger of Allah, there cannot be, there cannot be love for Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab. And the one in whose heart there is love for Ali ibn Abi Talib, then there can never be love for the enemies of the right of Wilayah. Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Li-alla yatafarraqa atba'u awliya'ika. So that the followers of Your Awliya do not wander here and there. Where the Hujjat of Allah is, everything is there. Zahirun ghayru muta'in. It is possible that he—meaning when he is manifest, it is possible that he is manifest, but he is not being obeyed. Now he took his honor in front of everyone. Now he said, 'Oh brother, this is a headache.' He wrote a letter, 'What kind of headache have you sent me?' So he said, 'Okay, fine, send him back to me.' Then Janab-e-Abu Dharr was sent back to Medina. Then he came to Medina. Then he criticized there too. So Ka'b al-Ahbar objected there. We said, we submitted to your service. Ka'b al-Ahbar became a Muslim in the ninth year of Hijri. In the ninth year of Hijri. Now, when Janab-e-Abu Dharr criticized something saying it was not right, Ka'b al-Ahbar said, 'What kind of un-Islamic things are you saying?' So Janab-e-Abu Dharr hit him on the head with that same staff and said, 'O son of a Jew, will you teach me Islam?' Wow! Wow! Wow! So now they thought, 'Brother, this has become a headache.' Now he should be sent somewhere else. So he was sent to Rabdha. And in Rabdha, Janab-e-Abu Dharr was in complete solitude, in a state of poverty. In a state of poverty, completely. To the extent that his wife, Umm-e-Dharr, was sitting and crying bitterly. Abu Dharr was breathing his last. So he asked, 'Why are you crying?' She said, 'You are in this condition, and we don't even have money for a shroud.' He said, 'Do not worry, I have heard from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that Abu Dharr, you will pass away in such a place where there will be no one, but a few believers will come, and they will arrange for your shroud and burial. So go and stand on the highway.' She said, 'But the highway is closed now.' Because all the pilgrims have left, now there is no one. He said, 'I am telling you, if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said it, it must be true. Go, stand there.' She went and stood there. She went once, twice, three times, many times. But Janab-e-Abu Dharr kept sending her, 'Go back.' Then one time she saw some people coming. And they were riding horses very fast. They asked her, 'O servant of Allah, what are you doing here? O lady, what are you doing?' She said, 'My husband is breathing his last in this state. A companion of the Prophet.' They asked, 'Which companion?' She said, 'Abu Dharr.' 'Abu Dharr, the companion of the Prophet?' They came, and there is a very detailed Hadith, let's finish it briefly. And they performed the shroud and burial, they arranged everything properly, and they buried Hazrat Abu Dharr with a proper shroud and funeral rites. This is how the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) make arrangements for their companions. But when it comes to the Ahlulbayt themselves, just think of Karbala. Just think of Karbala and remember Hussain. Everyone was martyred, no one was left. Once, the son of Zahra raised a cry for help: 'Hal min nasirin yansuruna?' (Is there any helper to help us?) 'Hal min mugithin yughithuna?' (Is there any protector to protect us?) 'Hal min dhabbin yadhubbu 'an harami Rasulillahi?' (Is there anyone who will defend the harem of the Prophet of Allah? Who will save the harem of the Prophet of Allah?) Hussain raised the cry for help, and suddenly there was an uproar in the tents. Hussain came to the door of the tent. 'Sister Zainab, what is this uproar?' She said, 'Brother, you raised a cry for help. Asghar threw himself out of the cradle.' He said, 'Sister, bring Asghar to me.' She said, 'Asghar does not go into anyone's lap. You go and see for yourself.' Now it is written in the Maqtal that Hussain came near the cradle, near the cradle. Now what the father said and what the son understood, no one knows. It is just written that as soon as Hussain uttered some words softly, Asghar leaped into his lap. Hussain took the child and started walking. Now, when he had gone a little distance and came near the door of the tent, what did he see? That the mother is standing there. 'Rabab, why here?' Rabab replied, 'My master, I see that whoever has gone since morning has not returned alive.' Hussain consoled her, 'Rabab, those who went until now, the enemy thought they came with the intention of fighting. Oh, six-month-old children don't fight, why would they kill him?' Hussain consoled her. The mother's heart calmed down. Hussain came, brought Asghar, stood on an elevation, and called out, 'Amma fikum muslim?' (Is there any Muslim among you?) 'Islam says to give water to the thirsty. My child has been thirsty for three days.' No one said anything. Then Hussain asked a second question, 'Oh, if you are not Muslims, then is there no parent among you? Look at the condition of my child.' Still, no one gave an answer. Now Hussain asked a third question, 'Oh, are you not seeing how my child is writhing?' 'Afala tarauna kayfa yatalazza?' (Are you not seeing how he is writhing?) 'Talazzi' is used when a fish is taken out of water; it writhes for a while as long as it has life, and when its life ends, in its final moments, it sometimes opens its mouth, sometimes closes it, opens it, closes it, and in this way, it breathes its last. This state is called 'talazzi'. The Imam says, 'Are you seeing the state of his writhing? How he is breathing his last?' Suddenly, the wretched ones started crying, turning their faces away. Ibn Sa'd felt that signs of revolution were appearing. He called out, 'Where is Hurmala? Where is Hurmala?' The cursed one came forward. He took out a three-headed arrow. A three-headed arrow was used by the Arabs when they hunted large animals; they used such arrows then. Oh, this six-month-old child! Hurmala aimed at Asghar's throat. Now, when the arrow hit, the child turned in the father's lap. The arrow also pierced Hussain's hands. Now, when Hussain looked down, Asghar was smiling. Asghar is smiling, 'Father, do not worry.' Now, what should Hussain do? How should he take the child to the tent? You will perform the A'mal of Ashura. Hussain takes him. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' He walks a little, then comes back. 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' Hussain performed this action seven times. Then, in the end, Hussain thought that now the child has left this world, so why should the mother be deprived of the final sight? Hussain put his cloak over the child's face, came to the door of the tent, and called out, 'Rabab!' As soon as Hussain called 'Rabab', it is written in the Maqtal that Rabab came from one side, and Sakina came from the other, but she was a child, she came running and reached first. 'Father, has my brother drunk water? Now my brother is not thirsty.' Sakina was still asking when Rabab arrived. Now, when Rabab arrived, Hussain removed the cloak, and what a scene the mother saw! A six-month-old child with a three-headed arrow pierced in his throat. Rabab recited a dirge: 'Ya bunayya amisanuka yunhar' (O my son, are children like you also slaughtered?) 'Fasaya'lamulladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, wal-'aqibatu lil-muttaqin.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten our revenge for the blood of Hussain. 'Aynat-talibu bidamil maqtuli bi-Karbala.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his followers and helpers. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Those who are away from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Protect the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. Protect the high scholars and the esteemed Maraje. Protect the holy shrines and the holy mausoleums. Protect those who are protecting them. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab. Protect those who are protecting that shrine. O Lord, grant us the honor of visiting Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Accept this small act of mourning of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.summary: The lecture explains why a divinely appointed Proof (Hujjat) is essential for humanity to navigate the path to salvation and true worship.
