chapters.title: The Necessity of the Hujjat
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the Hujjat (Proof) of Allah is the axis of the universe and a necessary guide in every era to prevent the scattering of believers.

chapters.title: Unity Through Wilayah
chapters.summary: True unity among Muslims is only possible through adherence to the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib and his progeny, as truth and falsehood cannot coexist.

chapters.title: The Occultation of the Imam
chapters.summary: The Imam remains the guide for humanity even during occultation, as the environment of the world is insecure and the Imam awaits the appointed time for his manifestation.

chapters.title: The Promised Government of Justice
chapters.summary: Every nation will be given a chance to rule, but the ultimate era of justice and perfection will only be established by Imam-e-Zamana in the end times.

chapters.title: The Concept of Hadith and Divine Knowledge
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that 'Hadith' refers to new knowledge or news, emphasizing that the chain of knowledge from the Ahlulbayt is continuous and essential for the world.

chapters.title: Wali al-Amr and the Night of Decree
chapters.summary: The lecture defines 'Wali al-Amr' based on the descent of divine commands on Laylat al-Qadr, linking it to the Quranic obligation to obey those in authority.

chapters.title: Historical Struggles and the Imamate
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques the historical failure of Muslims to follow the true leaders, citing the conflicts during Imam Ali's caliphate and the necessity of studying history.

chapters.title: The Birth of the Twelfth Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the difficult circumstances surrounding the life of Imam Hasan al-Askari and the miraculous, hidden birth of Imam al-Mahdi.

chapters.title: Imam Hasan al-Askari and the Tafsir
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) provided deep Quranic education to his followers, including a comprehensive Tafsir that was unfortunately lost over time.

chapters.title: The Significance of Imamat and Guidance
chapters.summary: The Quranic concept of being called with one's Imam on the Day of Judgment highlights the necessity of following a divinely appointed leader.

chapters.title: The Spirit of Sacrifice and Abu Dharr
chapters.summary: True adherence to the Ahlulbayt requires a spirit of sacrifice, as exemplified by the unwavering truthfulness and asceticism of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.

chapters.title: The Exile and Passing of Abu Dharr
chapters.summary: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari faces persecution for his truthfulness, is exiled to Rabdha, and passes away in solitude, eventually being buried by a group of believers as prophesied by the Prophet.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Ali Asghar
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain brings his thirsty infant son, Ali Asghar, to the battlefield to plead for water, only for the child to be brutally martyred by a three-headed arrow.

chapters.title: The Aftermath and Final Supplications
chapters.summary: The tragedy of Ali Asghar's death is revealed to his mother, Rabab, followed by concluding prayers for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi and the welfare of the believers.

content:
TSR presents. Ya Sahar. Ya Sahar. Oh, the hidden desire in the longing of my eyes. Oh, the comfort of my heart. Oh, the comfort of my heart. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa aynan, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. A'udhu billahis sami'il alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya Waliyyul Asr, ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahush sharif, adrikna wala tuhlikna. The war between truth (Haq) and falsehood (Batil) is very old. These two can never come together. As time passed, the conflict between truth and falsehood increased, and now the situation is such that it has become even more difficult to recognize the truth because falsehood is misleading people by changing its guise. Therefore, how do we recognize the truth in the age of Ghaybah (Occultation)? How can one determine what is truth and what is falsehood? Our today's episode of the Panah-e-Kainat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Mega Quiz is related to this, in which our brothers will discuss the phrase from the Khutbah-e-Ghadir, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has said about his final successor, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.): 'Wala haqqa illa ma'a' (And truth is only with him). Let us remind you once again, you might see a surprise question in today's episode quiz link. This surprise question can be asked at any time during the quiz, so watch the episode carefully and get a chance to be included in both the daily prize and mega prize lucky draws by giving correct answers to all questions. With this, we begin our third episode today. A'udhu billahis sami'il alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. Truth is the name of something that a person is always in search of, and every person claims that they are on the truth. If we look around us, we will find that every person, every group, every class claims that they are on the truth. So how can one identify who is on the truth and who is not? Let us knock at the door of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and ask him what the standard of truth is. He has made it very clear for us that if you want to find the truth, you must stay with your Imam. Because in every era, the recognition of truth is only through the Imam. A famous and well-known hadith that we hear in every gathering and every Majlis, in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Ali ma'al haqqi wal haqqu ma'a Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali). 'Wal haqqu yadurru haythu ma dara Ali' (And the truth turns wherever Ali turns). That is, if we want to be on the truth, we must stay with Imam Ali (a.s.). And this is a hadith that is not found only in Shia books, but is also found in the major and authentic books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun. There is a famous and well-known book of the Ahl-e-Tasannun named 'Al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn', whose author is Hakim al-Nishapuri. He has also recorded this hadith in his book in this way. And this hadith is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that he says: 'Rahimallahu Aliyan' (May Allah shower mercy upon Ali). 'Allahumma adir al-haqqa ma'ahu haythu dara' (O Allah, turn the truth wherever Ali turns). From this hadith, we learn that the truth is only and only with Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). In fact, we can say that the truth follows Ali (a.s.). Ali (a.s.) is the Imam and the truth is the follower (Ma'mum). Because Ali (a.s.) is the Hujjah (Proof) of Allah after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Imam over the people, the Wasi (successor) of the Messenger, and the successor of the Messenger. And the truth is not limited to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), but after him, the truth is with Imam Hasan (a.s.), the truth is with Imam Husayn (a.s.). Therefore, if we want to see, if the truth is with Imam Hasan (a.s.), then whoever comes against him is on falsehood. The truth... The truth is with Imam Husayn (a.s.). If Yazid comes against him, then he is on falsehood. And in this current era, this truth is with Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Therefore, if we want to be on the truth, if we want to find the truth, we must acknowledge the Imamate of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and hold fast to his hem. That is why when differences increase, the means to recognize the true religion is the truth. Religion is recognized by the truth, not by people. Let us take the help of a hadith to clarify this point, which is narrated from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli. Regarding Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, it is enough to say that there is a hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in which Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states: 'Irtadda al-nasu ba'dal Husayni (a.s.) illa thalathah' (After the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.), everyone became apostates except for three people). One name is Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, the second name is Yahya ibn Umm al-Tawil, and the third name is Zubayr ibn Mut'im. So Abu Khalid al-Kabuli narrates from Asbagh ibn Nubata, who himself is a very big name among the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and he narrates that Harith al-Hamadani enters the presence of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) with some people, and Harith al-Hamadani's walk was a bit unsteady, meaning he was a bit ill, he looked a bit sick, and he was repeatedly striking his staff on the ground as he walked. When Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) sees this condition, Imam Ali (a.s.) says: 'Fa-aqbala alayhi Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)' (Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) turned towards him). And he had a high status in the eyes of the Imam. And the Imam says: 'Kayfa tajidu ya Harith?' (How do you find yourself, O Harith?). Meaning, when Ali (a.s.) saw his condition, Imam Ali (a.s.) asked about his state, how he finds himself. Upon this, Harith al-Hamadani says: 'Nala al-dahru minni' (O Ali, O Amir al-Mu'minin, time has exhausted me, and the differences among your companions have made me restless). Some are those who exaggerate (Ghulu) regarding you, some are those who fall short (Taqsir), and some are those who are in doubt regarding your virtues and merits. When Harith al-Hamadani expressed his pain before Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Ali (a.s.) told Harith al-Hamadani: 'Ala inna khayra shi'ati' (Indeed, the best of my Shias are those who adopt the middle path). And then Ali (a.s.) explained that those who exaggerate will also return to them, and those who fall short will also return to them. Now, when Ali (a.s.) stated these things and presented them before Harith al-Hamadani, Harith al-Hamadani said: 'O Mawla, may my parents be sacrificed for you, I wish you would remove this veil from our hearts and grant us insight through your command.' Upon this, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) uttered a powerful sentence which is our main topic, as we stated that religion is recognized by the truth, not by people. Now that part is coming in this hadith where Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is saying: 'Inna dinallahi la yu'rafu bil-rijal' (Indeed, the religion of Allah is not recognized by men), 'bal bi-ayati al-haqq' (but by the signs of the truth). 'Fa'rif al-haqqa' (So recognize the truth, O Harith, recognize the truth), 'ta'rif ahlahu' (you will recognize its people). Respected brothers, this sentence seems to remove the veils from many of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)'s words, that the Imam (a.s.) is stating a rational principle that religion is not recognized by any personality, nor is it limited to specific people. The truth is not dependent on any human, tribe, or sect, but is understood by its proofs and signs. That is, religion should be understood not by people but by proofs. And if this is applied to the current era, today many people try to recognize Islam through personalities, and this is the biggest mistake, that Islam should be recognized by personalities. Because when they look at personalities, they find that someone is working for their own interests, someone is working for their own desires, and then they associate this with Islam. If we apply this to the present era, the true standard for recognizing the truth is the Imam of the Time (a.s.), his teachings, the Quran, and the traditions and commands of his ancestors, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). One must seek evidence in the light of intellect and recognize the truth through that, rather than recognizing the truth through any personality. Dear ones, the truth itself is the standard by which right and wrong are identified. A hadith is narrated from Jesus (peace be upon our Prophet and his family and him). It is an extremely valuable hadith. One should pay close attention to this hadith, for he says: « خذوا الحق من أهل الباطل » (Take the truth from the people of falsehood). If the truth is being stated by the tongue of a person of falsehood, take it. « ولا تأخذوا الباطل من أهل الحق » (But do not take falsehood from the people of truth). If a person of truth is stating something and it is false, do not take it from them. Meaning, if you find someone who is religious and speaks the truth, but they start saying something false, it is not the case that just because they always spoke the truth, you will now accept the falsehood as well; no. If someone is a person of falsehood but is stating the truth, take the truth from them, and if someone is a person of truth but is stating falsehood, Jesus (a.s.) says: do not take it from them. He further says, it is an excellent sentence, he says « كونوا نقاد الكلام » (Be critics of speech). Meaning, do not just accept any speech. Meaning, whoever states it, whatever speech comes before you, you are just accepting it. You see that, oh, there is a personality, a great personality, they stated it and you accepted it. No, « كونوا نقاد الكلام » (Be critics of every speech). Do not accept anything unless you accept it with criticism. After examining and investigating it thoroughly, only then should you accept that speech. He further says, « فكم من ضلالة زخرفت بآيات من كتاب الله » (For how many misguidances have been decorated with verses from the Book of God). He says that there are so many misguidances that have been decorated and presented using the verses of the Book of God. Misguidances and deviations have been decorated and presented using the verses of the Book of God. That is why it is necessary to « كونوا نقاد الكلام » (Be critics of speech). If someone decorates and presents something to you, their point, their perspective, and they bring a verse of the Quran and present it to you in a distorted way, and you accepted it, no, « كونوا نقاد الكلام ». He further gives an example of it. What kind of example? « كما زخرفت الدراهم من نحاس بالفضة » (Just as dirhams made of copper are decorated with silver). He says that just as a dirham, which is a copper dirham, when it is plated with silver, when it is washed with silver and made into a silver coin—meaning it is a copper coin, it is made into a silver coin by silver plating—and then it appears to people as a silver coin, but what is it in reality? It is copper. So, in that way, the verses of the Quran have also been presented in this manner. Jesus (a.s.) is saying, « النظر إلى ذلك سواء » (The look at that is the same), and people who look at it with their apparent eyes, it looks the same to them, they see it as a silver coin. But « والبصراء به الخبراء » (But the insightful ones are the experts), those who have deep insight, those who are experts, they are skilled in recognizing it; they understand well that it is silver-plated, it is not silver in reality. So, one should become such a person of insight. This is what the Prophet is saying. How will this happen? « كونوا نقاد الكلام » (Be critics of speech); do not accept every speech, accept every speech with criticism. Now, what points do we get from this hadith? Let us reflect on them a little. Now look, first of all, what is meant here by 'people of falsehood' from whom even the truth should be taken? The people of falsehood are those whose belief is not correct, whose belief is not right, there are some inconsistencies in their belief, their belief is not correct. But when they are making a statement, they are stating a truthful matter. So here, their statement will be accepted. But what is meant here in this hadith by 'people of truth'? By 'people of truth' is meant someone whose belief is correct, who is right on their religion, whose belief is absolutely correct, but the speech they are making now is false; their speech is not the truth. They are stating it from themselves, they learned it from somewhere, or they are trying to prove some wrong thing of theirs, so now their speech will not be accepted, even if they are a person of truth. Meaning, if anyone says anything and their statement is in accordance with the Quran and the traditions, i.e., the hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then it will be accepted. As long as it is the Quran and the traditions of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), it will be accepted. Now, it does not matter who it is, no matter how small or how great they are, if their statement... is not in accordance with the Quran and the hadith, then it is not acceptable. It will not be accepted. No matter how much their name appears among the people of truth, among the right-holders, no matter how much they have raised the banner of truth, but if their statement is not in accordance with the Quran and hadith, it is not acceptable. The next point from this hadith is that, now think, this is truly justice and this is truly fairness. Meaning, justice and fairness will only be established when people recognize the truth, and what is the means to recognize the truth? The Quran and the Ahlulbayt, and when Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) reappears, that is the justice and fairness he will establish. Meaning, wrong will be called wrong, truth will be called truth. There will be no adulteration between truth and falsehood. Neither will truth or falsehood be covered with gold plating. Meaning, the matter is wrong and it will not be covered with the plating of truth. Imam-e-Zamana will make everything very clear, meaning people will call wrong as wrong. Today, that is not the case. People need to understand this. No one knows which matter is truth and which is wrong. People are presenting their own perspectives decorated with verses of the Quran and hadiths, and people are getting misguided in it. But we should look at every matter and definitely see its evidence from the Quran and hadith, and 'be critics of speech'—accept every speech only with criticism. Hazrat Isa (a.s.) pointed to another important matter in this hadith, and that is that not everything that glitters is gold. Not everything that is shiny is gold. People will have to keep this in mind. Meaning, if a matter seems very good to you, you are hearing something from someone and it looks very beautiful, but it is not that just because it is beautiful, you accepted it. No. You will have to examine its beauty. How will you examine it? Through the Quran and hadith. Only then will that thing be truly shiny if it is in accordance with the Quran and hadith. Dear ones, in this era of occultation, we have to be very careful about this, that for everything we accept from anyone, we must make the Quran and the hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) the standard, and we must become 'critics of speech'—that we accept every speech only with criticism. And this matter is extremely important. The most important thing is that in this era of occultation, every moment, every second, every time, every day, every week, every month, every year, every century, every era, the truth is only and only with the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and in this current era of occultation, it is with Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). It is only with him. When the matter is about the Imam (a.s.) and the truth, there is a famous and complete Ziyarat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Its name is Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira. These phrases are found in it, that when a servant reads this Ziyarat in the shrine of any Imam. Actually, there is an emphasis on reading this Ziyarat in the shrine of every Imam. You can read this Ziyarat in the shrine of any Imam. There is a phrase in this Ziyarat in which the one who is appearing is announcing and acknowledging through this Ziyarat. What? That 'the truth is with you, and in you, and from you, and towards you, and you are its people and its source.' The truth is with you and it is in your lineage, and the truth is from you, and the truth will return to you. 'You are the people of truth and you are the source of truth.' 'Ma'din' means mine, source. That the truth is not only with the Imam, but the Imam is the mine of truth. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the mine of truth. The truth comes from there. So, whatever comes from there is the truth. It is necessary here that we pay attention to Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira and try to make this Ziyarat a part of our lives. Not only when you go for the Ziyarat of the holy shrines of the Infallible Imams (a.s.), you must read this Ziyarat at that time. But apart from this, in your daily days, especially try to recite Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira on Thursday nights. Through this, one should visit the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and be present in their court through this Ziyarat. Because it is very important. First of all, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) recorded this Ziyarat in his book 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', Volume 2, page 609. Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) himself is recording this Ziyarat in his book, and that too in that book, 'Kitab-e-Faqih', for which he himself is guaranteeing that this book is a proof between me and Allah. Meaning, Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) himself is guaranteeing his book and recording this Ziyarat in it. Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) himself has emphasized reading this Ziyarat, reciting it. The Imam emphasized three things. Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) himself, in a meeting he had with Allama Majlisi's (r.a.) father, Allama Muhammad Taqi Majlisi (r.a.). In that meeting, Imam-e-Zamana emphasized these three things, that these three things should never be abandoned. One, Namaz-e-Shab (Salatul Layl). Salatul Layl, Salatul Layl, Salatul Layl, he said three times. Then Ashura, Ashura, Ashura, Ziyarat-e-Ashura. Meaning, remain steadfast on this. Take care of it. And the third, Al-Jamia, Al-Jamia, Al-Jamia. This Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira. The whole story of this meeting, Allama Majlisi's (r.a.) father writes in his book 'Rawdat al-Muttaqin', he recorded this incident. The meeting that he had, the honor he received of the Ziyarat of the Hazrat. He mentioned this whole honor. He recorded it in that book. He says that 'I was in Samarra one day, and I saw their shrines, I visited the shrines of the two Imams Askari (Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) and Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.)), I visited the holy grave, the pure grave.' And in this state, I saw their graves that they were at the peak of height and beauty. What? Meaning, there was a peak of height. What is the Imam? The Imam's shrine at that time was such that there was a strange height there and a strange beauty, and the grave was decorated in such a way that he says that I saw there that on their graves, on both graves, a green-colored garment, a green-colored cloth was placed, and that cloth was not of this world. That cloth was from Paradise. Why? Because I had never seen anything like it in this world in my life. It was a cloth of Paradise that was placed on both their graves. And when I reached there, what do I see? I saw our Master and the Master of all creation, Sahib al-Asr wal-Zaman (a.s.). I saw that Imam-e-Zamana is present there. Near his father's grave, near his grandfather's grave. Imam-e-Zamana is present. Meaning, look, try to understand the status of Allama Majlisi's (r.a.) father, Allama Muhammad Taqi Majlisi, what his status is, that he is seeing the Imam and recognizing that this is Imam-e-Zamana. This success was granted to Allama Majlisi's father by Imam-e-Zamana. He says that he writes in his book that I saw that the Imam of the time is sitting there. Imam-e-Zamana is sitting, and how is he sitting? He is leaning against the grave and facing the door, the door of the shrine, he is facing it. And when I saw him, as soon as my eyes fell on the Imam, now this sentence, a powerful sentence he writes, that as soon as my eyes fell on the Imam, I started reciting this Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira. Meaning, there are the graves of two Imams, one living, apparent, one living Imam is in front, in front of the eyes, and reading his Ziyarat in front of his Imam of the time and addressing his Imam through this Ziyarat, may Allah grant this success to all of us. He says that I began Ziyarat-e-Jami'a, but not in an ordinary manner. He says it is obvious; when the Imam is in front of you and you have the opportunity to recite his Ziyarat, he says I began with 'bisawtil-murtafa', meaning I began reciting the Ziyarat in a loud voice. And how? Like a maddah (eulogist). I was reciting my Ziyarat like a maddah. This is something that often happens to us too, when the heart is truly attached to the Imam. For instance, when you go for Ziyarat to the dome of any Imam, especially when you go for the Ziyarat of Najaf-e-Ashraf, when a person sees the dome of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) for the first time, when his lover sees it, the state of love that arises at that moment—based on that love, a few verses flow from his tongue. He praises his Imam, wondering to which paradise Allah has sent him. That is how he begins to praise. Allama Majlisi, Allama Majlisi... The father of [Allama Majlisi] says that I began reciting this Ziyarat-e-Jami'a Kabira like a maddah. As soon as my gaze fell upon my Imam of the time, and then when I completed this Ziyarat, when the Ziyarat was finished, then 'qala salawatullah alayhim', the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.s.) himself said, 'What an excellent Ziyarat this is.' The Imam of the Time himself praised the Ziyarat. 'What an excellent Ziyarat.' I said, I submitted to the Imam, 'Mawlaya, ruhi fidak' (My Master, may my soul be sacrificed for you). 'Ziyarat-e-Jaddak' (The Ziyarat of your grandfather). And saying this, I pointed towards the holy grave of Imam al-Naqi (a.s.), that 'Master, this is the Ziyarat of your grandfather,' because this Ziyarat is narrated from Imam al-Naqi (a.s.); he had taught this Ziyarat. 'Master, this is the Ziyarat of your grandfather.' The Imam said, 'Na'am' (Yes). Then the Imam said, 'Udkhul' (Come in). Come inside. Just think, what is the value and status of Allama Majlisi's father in the eyes of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) that he is calling him to himself? He says that 'falammā dakhaltu' (when I entered), 'waqaftu qariban minal bab' (I stood near the door). Meaning, I did not have the courage [to go further]. The awe of the Imam was such that I did not have the courage to go near the Imam. I stood near the door. The Imam said, 'Taqaddam' (Come forward). He is calling me to himself. I said, 'Mawlaya' (O my Master), 'akhafu an asira kafiran bitarkil adab' (I fear that by not observing the proper etiquette, I might go astray from my religion). This is the etiquette of the Ziyarat of the Imam. This is the etiquette of visiting the shrines and holy places of the A'imma-e-Ma'sumin (a.s.). We should try to observe the etiquettes of Ziyarat while visiting the Imams. It is not that one should just come and go in any manner. No, it is very important to keep those etiquettes in mind. So he says, 'Master, I fear that by not observing the etiquette, I might be cast out of my religion.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'La ba's' (No problem, there is no issue). 'Idha kana bi-idhnina' (If it is with our permission, then there is no problem, come forward). When we have called you, what is the status and rank! The Imam himself is calling. When we have called, there is no problem. So he says, 'faqaddamtu qalilan' (I moved a little forward), 'wa kuntu kha'ifan, murtashian' (and I was afraid, trembling). I was still afraid because the awe of the Imam, the awe of the Imam of the Time, was such that it had overwhelmed me so much that I was nervous. And 'murtashian', meaning my hands were shaking. My hands and feet were trembling. The Imam said, 'Taqaddam, taqaddam' (Come forward, come forward). He called me to himself. 'Hatta sirtu qariban minhu' (Until I reached very close to him). And then as soon as I reached very close to the Imam, the Imam (a.s.) said to me, 'Ijlis' (Sit). Sit down. Now he says, 'Qultu akhafu mawlaya' (I said, I am afraid, Master). The Imam said, 'La takhaf' (Do not fear, sit). So when the Imam gave permission to sit, he says, 'Falammā jlastu julsatal 'abd' (When I sat, I sat like a slave). I sat, but how? Just as a slave sits before a high-ranking master. That is how I sat. Meaning, the position of Tashahhud that we have, that is called 'julsatal 'abd' (the sitting of a slave). In this state, Jibra'il (a.s.) used to come and sit before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) when he brought revelation. 'Julsatal 'abd'. Sitting like a slave before his master. I also sat in that manner. After this, the Imam of the Time said a strange sentence. The Imam said, 'Istarih' (Sit comfortably). Meaning, fold your legs and sit. Do not sit like this, fold your legs and sit comfortably. Why? 'Fa-innaka ta'ibta' (For you are tired). You are tired. 'Ji'ta mashiyan hafiyan' (You have come walking barefoot). Allahu Akbar. Only Allah knows how the Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) welcomes those pilgrims who come walking from Najaf to Karbala. The Imam of the Time says, 'Sit, sit comfortably, fold your legs and sit.' And then he made me sit near him, and after that, Allama Majlisi's father says that after that, so many things were discussed, so many things, and the Imam (a.s.) showed so much grace and kindness, and told me so many things that it is not possible for me to recount them, and I have forgotten many of them. So, in this Ziyarat-e-Jami'a Kabira, the fact that the Imam (a.s.) is the Truth is mentioned; this phrase makes it clear. Which phrase? The same phrase: 'Wal-haqqu ma'akum wa fikum wa minkum wa ilaykum' (The Truth is only with you, in you, from you, and towards you). You are the Truth, aren't you? 'Wa antum ahluhu wa ma'dinuhu' (You are its people and its mine). You are the mine of Truth, you are the source of Truth. Truth emerges from you, towards you, and from your place. You are the fountainhead of Truth, you are its source. Whatever proceeds from you, that is the Truth. The Imam of the Time (a.s.) is the Truth, and his reappearance is the Truth. Because this is the promise that Allah has made, and Allah's promise is the Truth. We have just seen about Ziyarat-e-Jami'a. Let us mention another Ziyarat before you, and this is a Ziyarat that is attributed to the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Although we can recite this Ziyarat at any time, and we should try to recite this Ziyarat regularly, but a special place to recite this Ziyarat is the Sardab of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). When we are blessed with the Ziyarat of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and we get the opportunity to go to Samarra, we should definitely recite this Ziyarat in the Sardab. And this is such an authentic Ziyarat that our scholars have mentioned it in their famous books of supplications. We also find the mention of this Ziyarat in 'Balad al-Amin'. It is also found in Shaykh al-Kaf'ami's 'Al-Misbah' and also in 'Bihar al-Anwar'. So this is a Ziyarat that our scholars have mentioned. The opening sentence of this Ziyarat is such that we greet the Imam by saying, 'Assalamu 'alal-haqqil-jadid' (Peace be upon the New Truth). Meaning, 'Haqq' (Truth) is one of the names of the Imam, and we are greeting the Imam with this very name. Meaning, if we say that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is the Truth, Ali is the Truth, then there would be nothing wrong with that. And after that, we say, 'Wal-'alimulladhi 'ilmuhu la yabid' (And the scholar whose knowledge never perishes/becomes obsolete). That the Imam is such a scholar whose knowledge never becomes old, never becomes worn out. If we look at worldly sciences, as time progresses, human sciences or what is called 'ulum-e-bashar' (human sciences) become old. A theory that was common until a few years ago is not found today, and as time goes on, it is possible that the theory present among us today may not remain tomorrow. But the knowledge of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) never becomes old. The 'Haqq-ul-Jadid' (New Truth), which is the name of this Ziyarat, has some meanings. First of all, it is the Truth. Meaning, this is not a false speech, this is absolutely true and it is the Truth. And 'Jadid' (New), which we also use in Urdu, is something that is new, that is absolutely fresh. It never becomes old, it never becomes worn out. The Holy Quran also has a name 'Hadith'. It is called 'Hadith' because it always remains new, always remains fresh. Therefore, no matter how many times we recite the Quran, we never feel that we have read this book many times. Every time we read the Quran, we find new meanings and new lessons. So in the same way, the knowledge of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) never becomes old. And the Imam is that Truth whose reappearance has no doubt. As it was said, this is Allah's promise, and Allah's promise will surely be fulfilled. In short, the Imam himself is the Truth and his knowledge never becomes old. Just as the Imam (a.s.) is the Truth, in the same way, the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.) is also the Truth. In the Holy Quran, there is verse number 53 of Surah Fussilat, in which Allah the Almighty says: 'Sanurihim ayatina fil-afaqi wa fi anfusihim hatta yatabayyana lahum annahul-haqq' (We will soon show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth). Soon We will show them Our signs, where will We show them? 'Afaq', meaning in this universe, in the horizons. And 'fi anfusihim', in their own souls, We will show them signs. 'Hatta', how will We show them? Until it becomes absolutely clear to them, 'hatta yatabayyana', it will become absolutely clear to them that 'annahul-haqq', that it is the Truth. Now, in this regard, there is a narration that when the explanation of this verse was sought from the A'imma-e-Ma'sumin (a.s.), when Imam Sadiq (a.s.) was asked about this verse, the Imam said that those signs that will be shown, meaning in the horizons, in this universe, and those that will be shown in the souls of humans, what are those signs? The Imam says, 'Khasfun wa maskhun wa qadhfun'. 'Khasf', 'Khasf' means the sinking of the earth, meaning the earth swallowing its inhabitants. Then 'Maskh', meaning the transformation of one thing into another, being transformed, like many transformed animals. And then the third, the Imam says, 'Qadhfun'. 'Qadhfun' means rain, a shower of stones. All these things, meaning Allah is saying through this verse that We will show them these signs. Then the narrator asked the Imam, 'Master, what is the meaning of the final sentence, 'hatta yatabayyana annahul-haqq' (until it becomes clear to them what the Truth is)?' The Imam says, 'Da' dhaka' (Leave that, do not search too much into that). Why? The Imam says further, 'Dhaka qiyamul-Mahdi, 'ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif' (That is the rising of the Mahdi, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance). That refers to the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). That is what is meant by 'the Truth'. Meaning, not only is the Imam the Truth, but his reappearance is also the Truth. This hadith is present in Kitab al-Kafi. There is another similar hadith in which Abu Basir asks Imam Sadiq (a.s.) about this verse. In that too, the Imam mentions 'Maskh' and says, 'Wa yurihim fil-afaqi intiqadul-afaqi 'alayhim' (And He will show them in the horizons the collapse of the horizons upon them). What will Allah the Almighty do? The signs He will show them, meaning these signs of the universe collapsing, meaning such changes will come within time. He will show the changes of time. That these changes of time will become completely manifest to the people. And then the Imam says, 'Wa yarawna qudratallahi 'azza wa jalla fi anfusihim wa fil-afaq' (And they will see the power of Allah the Almighty in their own souls and in the horizons). The power of Allah the Almighty will be shown to them. The power of Allah will be shown to them. Meaning, in the heavens, in the horizons, in the universe, and also within their own souls. A small disease, an invisible virus, it made the whole world sit in its home. This is a small example of Allah's power. That if Allah wills, He can make the whole world sit in their homes through something invisible. So, this is just a sign of Allah. And then, when Janab Abu Baseer asked the Imam further, meaning he asked the Imam, 'Hatta yatabbayana lahu annahul haq' (until it becomes clear to him that it is the truth), what is meant by this, Mawla? That it will become clear to them that it is the truth. The Imam says, this is the khuruj (emergence) of the Imam. It is the khuruj of Imam-e-Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), it is his zuhoor (reappearance). 'Wa huwal haqqu min indillahi azza wa jall' (And it is the truth from Allah Azza wa Jall). 'Yarahul khalqu' (The creation will see it), meaning the creation will see this truth. All creatures, la budda minhu (there is no doubt about it). This will definitely happen. Meaning, this truth will be so clear that it will be absolutely evident to everyone that the zuhoor has taken place. And whose zuhoor has taken place? Meaning, that zuhoor is also the truth, and the Imam whose zuhoor has taken place is also the truth. Both these things will happen. Dear respected ones, from the discussion so far, it is proven that if anyone moves away from the truth, they move closer to falsehood. Meaning, whatever is besides the truth is falsehood, and this point is further clarified, just as Allah Subhanu wa Ta'ala stated in the Holy Quran, Surah Yunus, verse number 32: 'Fadhalikumullahu rabbukumul haq' (For that is Allah, your true Lord). 'Famaadha ba'dal haqqi illad dalal' (Then what is there after the truth except misguidance?). Further, it is stated, 'Fa anna tusrafun' (Then how are you turned away?). Meaning, Allah has clarified in this verse, just as in the first sentence Allah said that I am your true Lord. That I am your true Lord, and immediately after that, He says, what is left now? What remains? Meaning, now we should ponder upon this. We have seen this verse, and after the verse, there are some things we should ponder upon, and one thing becomes very clear: if anything remains after the truth, it is falsehood. If you move away from the truth, you will be close to falsehood. If you abandon the truth, you have embraced falsehood. So, we must understand the truth and hold onto the mantle of the truth. Meaning, whoever moved away from the Imam—meaning, in the entire discussion we have had so far, it is that the Imam is the truth. He is the true Imam. So, whoever moves away from the Imam will be close to falsehood. They will go into falsehood; they have chosen falsehood. If someone moves away from the Imam—meaning, we must be very careful and hold onto the Imam's mantle firmly, so that under no circumstances do we become separated from it. If we move even slightly away from it, at that moment we are with falsehood, at that moment we are in misguidance. In every matter, it is necessary to see what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) say. Meaning, in every matter—understand this 'every matter'—whether it is a small matter or a big matter. Meaning, any of our statements, actions, work, even our decisions, if we are giving any order, it is necessary to see what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) say about this. And when it comes to religion, faith, and belief, one should especially see what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are saying. If we are not paying attention to this and are trying to do something based on our own opinion, then understand that it is falsehood. Just as their word should be preferred in every matter. Whether it is a small matter or a big one. Meaning, a small matter—you are making decisions for your home, some dispute or fight happened between two brothers, there you must see what the Imam says. Then you will know who the truth is with. Whether in the neighborhood or in the world, and when it comes to religion, there is no word other than the word of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If you have moved even an iota away from their word, you are towards falsehood. It is not that you will only prefer the word of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in one place. In the mosque. No, in the world, in every moment of your life, their word will be preferred. And understand one thing, we should also understand it very well, and we should tie this knot in our hearts very firmly, that no one's personal opinion has any value. No one's personal opinion in this world has any value. The only value is the word of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Everywhere, their word will be preferred. No one's personal opinion holds any standard, and if someone is making their standard based on someone's opinion, they are drowning themselves in falsehood. They are drowning themselves in the ocean of falsehood. And this point was stated very clearly by the fifth Imam in this hadith. Meaning, look, we have always been hearing, and even our children know this hadith, that Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) prayed, 'O Allah, turn the truth in the direction that Ali turns.' Wherever Ali goes, turn the truth in that direction. Now, the fifth Imam further clarified this, saying: 'Kullama lam yakhruj min hadhal bayt fahuwa batil' (Whatever does not come out of this house is falsehood). He says, look, 'kullama'—everything, every thing, whatever it is, whether it is a statement, an action, a thought, or an idea, take anything, but 'lam yakhruj min hadhal bayt' (did not come out of this house)—the fifth Imam pointed to his house—if anything has not come out of this house, 'fahuwa batil' (it is falsehood). It is falsehood. Here, the Imam finished every argument. Now, whenever you have to see where the truth is, look at what has come out of their house. That's it. Now, if we also want to be with the truth, we must also keep our heads bowed in submission at that very threshold, keep our heads bowed. At their door, at the threshold of their house, that is where the truth comes from. And we want the truth to be with us, for us to be with the truth, so we should remain at their threshold, hold onto their mantle. That is the truth; besides that, if you move away from there for even a moment, for even a second, you will be with falsehood. Viewers, the points our brother presented before you, that 'Kullama lam yakhruj min hadhal bayt' is, then it is falsehood. That whatever does not originate from the house of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), all those things are falsehood. Come, let us present to you the summary of all the points mentioned in this episode: that the truth is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the truth is Ali (a.s.), the truth is Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.). Now, using the Ziyarat as a support, I want to present the conclusion of this point to you, the Ziyarat known as Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin, and about this Ziyarat, it is found that the Imam (a.s.) says that whenever you want to present yourself in our presence, then present yourself through this Ziyarat. Now, in this Ziyarat too, the word 'Haq' (truth) is being used, that Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the truth, and their pleasure is the truth. It is stated in this Ziyarat that 'Falhaqqu ma radhaitumuhu' (So the truth is that with which you are pleased). Meaning, the thing with which the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are pleased, that is the truth. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the mirror of Allah's pleasure. This means the scale of truth cannot be our own thinking, the majority's opinion, or historical propaganda, but the scale of truth is the Thaqalain (the two weighty things). Every matter that conforms to the sayings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) or the Masumeen (a.s.) and with which the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are pleased, that will be the truth. In a hadith, it is stated, 'Fakadhaba man za'ama annahu ma'ana' (He lies who claims to be with us), then the Mawla says, 'Fahuwa muta'alliqun bi furu'i ghairina' (but is attached to the branches of others), he is a liar. Meaning, the things that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have stated, which are originating from their house, only and only those are the truth. Besides this, nothing can be the truth. After this, the next phrase of Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin: 'Wal batilu ma sakhittumuhu' (And falsehood is that with which you are displeased). Now, the meaning of this part is that the identification of falsehood will also be known from the stance of the Masumeen (a.s.), as to what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are pleased with and what they are displeased with. If the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have expressed displeasure with any action, any thought, or any attitude, or have declared it wrong, then certainly that attitude, that thought, that action within the religion of Islam will be declared falsehood, and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) act as a 'Faruq' (separator) between truth and falsehood. That the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had stated, 'Sayakunu mim ba'di fitnatun' (There will be a trial after me), and then you said, 'Fa idha kana dhalika' (So when that happens), then 'Falzamu Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)' (then hold firmly onto Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)), 'Fa innahu al-faruqu bainal haqqi wal batil' (because he is the Faruq who decides between truth and falsehood). After that, I want to present two more phrases of Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin to summarize this entire episode: 'Wal ma'rufu ma amartum bi' (And the Ma'ruf—good things—are those which you have commanded). The good thing is that which you are commanding. And then the next phrase of Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin: 'Wal munkaru ma nahaitum anhu' (And the Munkar—evil—is that which you have forbidden). Meaning, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the standard of good and evil; that which you have stated is a good thing, and that which you have forbidden is a bad thing. Come, viewers, we pray in the court of Khuda-e-Alam that He grants haste in the reappearance of our Imam, Hazrat-e-Hujjat (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), and grants us the recognition of the truth, and grants us the ability to learn the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and along with learning, grants us the ability to act upon it. Viewers, the link for the quiz will be closed as soon as the timer on your screen ends, and now it is time for Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin. You are requested to pay attention to the Ziyarat because immediately after the Ziyarat, our today's daily winners will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system, Insha'Allah. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Salamun ala Ale Yasin. Assalamu alaika ya da'iyallahi wa rabbani ayatihi. Assalamu alaika ya baballahi wa dayyana dinihi. Assalamu alaika ya khalifatallahi wa nasira haqqihi. Assalamu alaika ya hujjatallahi wa dalila iradatihi. Assalamu alaika ya taliya kitabillahi wa tarjumana hu. Assalamu alaika fi anai lailika wa atraafi naharika. Assalamu alaika ya baqiyyatallahi fi ardhihi. Assalamu alaika ya misaqallahi ladhi akhadhahu wa wakkadahu. Assalamu alaika ya wa'dallahi ladhi dhaminahu. Assalamu alaika ayyuhal alamul mansubu wal ilmul masbubu wal ghawsu war rahmatul wasi'atu wa'dan ghaira makdhub. Assalamu alaika hina taqumu. Assalamu alaika hina taq'udu. Assalamu alaika hina taqra'u wa tubayyinu. Assalamu alaika hina tusalli wa taqnutu. Assalamu alaika hina tarka'u wa tasjudu. Assalamu alaika hina tuhallilu wa tukabbiru. Assalamu alaika hina tahmadu wa tastaghfiru. Assalamu alaika hina tusbihu wa tumsi. Assalamu alaika fil laili idha yaghsha wannahari idha tajalla. Assalamu alaika ayyuhal imamul ma'mun. Peace be upon you, O the awaited leader. Peace be upon you with all-encompassing greetings. I bear witness, O my Master, that I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He is One, there is no partner for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger; there is no beloved except Him and his family. And I call you to witness, O my Master, that Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, is His proof, and al-Hasan is His proof, and al-Husayn is His proof, and Ali ibn al-Husayn is His proof, and Muhammad ibn Ali is His proof, and Jafar ibn Muhammad is His proof, and Musa ibn Jafar is His proof, and Ali ibn Musa is His proof, and Muhammad ibn Ali is His proof, and Ali ibn Muhammad is His proof, and al-Hasan ibn Ali is His proof. And I bear witness that you are the proof of Allah; you are the first and the last, and that your return is true, there is no doubt in it, on the day when a soul's faith will not benefit it if it had not believed before or earned good in its faith. And that death is true, and Munkar and Nakir are true, and I bear witness that the resurrection is true, and the rising is true, and the path (Sirat) is true, and the watchtower (Mirsad) is true, and the scale (Mizan) is true, and the gathering (Hashr) is true, and the reckoning (Hisab) is true, and Paradise and Hell are true, and the promise and the threat regarding them are true. O my Master, wretched is he who opposes you, and prosperous is he who obeys you. So bear witness to what I have testified to you, and I am a friend to you and free from your enemy. So the truth is what you are pleased with, and falsehood is what you are displeased with, and the good is what you have commanded, and the evil is what you have forbidden. So my soul is a believer in Allah, the One, with no partner, and in His Messenger, and in the Commander of the Faithful, and in you, O my Master. In your beginning and your end, and my support is prepared for you, and my love is sincere for you. Amen, Amen. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Guardian of the Age (Wali al-Asr), help us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. First of all, we offer our congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of the sanctuary of the universe, Imam Mahdi (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance). And we pray to the Lord of the Worlds to hasten the reappearance of our Imam. The goal and purpose of the TSR team is solely the propagation of the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them). By subscribing to our channel, watching the videos, liking them, sharing them, and spreading this message to others, you too can participate in this work. Additionally, if anyone wishes to join this great task through donations, they can do so via the displayed bank account details or by scanning the QR code. Abid from Hyderabad. Many, many congratulations to all you winners. Viewers, if someone's name did not appear in today's winners, there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series, and by giving the correct answers to the quizzes of all episodes, you can participate in the lucky draw for the mega prize, i.e., a pilgrimage to Iraq. We thank you all once again. God willing, we will meet you again the day after tomorrow, i.e., February 10, 2026, at 9:00 PM India time, with the fourth and final episode of this series. Until then, goodbye, may you be in the protection of Allah. I request prayers, Ya Ali (peace be upon him) help.

chapters.title: The Conflict Between Truth and Falsehood
chapters.summary: The lecture introduces the eternal struggle between truth and falsehood, emphasizing that in the age of occultation, recognizing the truth requires following the Imam of the Time.

chapters.title: Imam Ali as the Standard of Truth
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that truth is inseparable from Imam Ali (a.s.) and the subsequent Imams, establishing the Imam as the ultimate criterion for identifying the truth.

chapters.title: Recognizing Religion Through Truth, Not Personalities
chapters.summary: Using a narration from Imam Ali (a.s.) to Harith al-Hamadani, the lecture clarifies that religion is defined by the signs of truth rather than by individual personalities.

chapters.title: The Objective Standard of Truth
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by advising believers to evaluate truth based on evidence and teachings rather than the status of individuals, citing a tradition from Prophet Isa (a.s.).

chapters.title: Be Critics of Speech
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes the necessity of critically evaluating all claims and perspectives, warning that even falsehoods can be disguised with Quranic verses.

chapters.title: The Standard of Truth
chapters.summary: The only valid standard for accepting any statement is its alignment with the Quran and the traditions of the Ahlulbayt, regardless of who makes the claim.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira
chapters.summary: Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira is highlighted as a vital source of truth and a recommended practice, emphasized by Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) himself.

chapters.title: Allama Majlisi's Father and the Imam
chapters.summary: The father of Allama Majlisi recounts a miraculous encounter where he witnessed the Imam of the Time (a.s.) at the shrines in Samarra and was invited to sit in his presence.

chapters.title: Etiquette and Awe in the Imam's Presence
chapters.summary: The narrative highlights the profound awe and strict etiquette required when in the presence of the Imam, emphasizing the humility of a true believer.

chapters.title: The Imam as the Source of Truth
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the theological concept that the Imam is the embodiment of Truth and possesses eternal, ever-fresh knowledge.

chapters.title: Understanding 'Al-Haqq al-Jadid'
chapters.summary: An analysis of the Ziyarat attributed to the Imam, explaining the title 'New Truth' as a reflection of his eternal and unchanging divine knowledge.

chapters.title: The Reappearance of Imam Mahdi as Truth
chapters.summary: The lecture explains that the Quranic verse regarding signs in the horizons and souls refers to the inevitable reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the ultimate Truth.

chapters.title: Avoiding Falsehood by Following Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that anything outside the guidance of the Ahlulbayt is falsehood, urging believers to align every aspect of their lives with the Imams' teachings.

chapters.title: The House of Ahlulbayt as the Sole Standard
chapters.summary: The fifth Imam's teaching that anything not originating from the house of the Ahlulbayt is false serves as the definitive standard for identifying the truth.

chapters.title: Ahlulbayt as the Standard of Truth

chapters.title: Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin and Conclusion

title: Majlis 5 | Momin Ki Pehchaan | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the characteristics of a true believer (Momin) through the lens of the tragedy of Karbala and the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The discussion emphasizes the importance of 'Ma'ruf' (good deeds), the necessity of maintaining high moral character, and the spiritual dangers of boasting about charity. By reflecting on the loyalty of companions like Amr ibn Hamiq al-Khuza'i and the final moments of Imam Hussain, the speaker encourages followers to embody the values of the Ahlulbayt in their daily lives.
content:
Listen to the poverty of the stranger of Zahra, O mourners, listen to the poverty of the stranger of Zahra, O mourners. When my Master was left alone on the battlefield, the army of Sham surrounded him from all sides. Every one of them was thirsty for blood by the Euphrates, the lamp of Imamate was yet to be extinguished, alas, Shabbir had to be brought down from the saddle to the ground. Hearing this, someone struck his forehead with a stone, someone plunged the blade of a spear into his side. Someone came in front and struck with the sword of tyranny, it was difficult for the stranger of Zahra to steady himself on the saddle. Ali and Zahra were made to weep on the battlefield, alas, Husayn did not fall, he was made to fall. When the arrow struck, he remembered Asghar, he called out to Ghazi when the mace struck his head. When the spear struck, he cried out in agony to Akbar, when the crowd struck a slap, he said, 'Ya Zahra'. He remembered Ali while the blows were falling on his head, he remembered Hasan while blood was gushing from his mouth. When the Master fell face-first from the saddle to the ground, the arrows that were in his chest came out from his back. The blades of all the spears came out from his side, how could the Master find peace for even a moment now. The stirrup slipped from the feet of the son of Ali, all the ribs of the descendant of the Prophet were broken. This has been recorded, this has been recorded by the narrator as a scene of pain, that at the moment when the dagger was about to move on Husayn. The daughter of Husayn was standing in front of her aunt, the stranger said this to Shimr at that moment, weeping. My Sakina, my Sakina, may she not breathe her last, O tyrant, have mercy, leave my hair, O tyrant. The son of Batool was lying lifeless in the desert, did someone ask Shimr if Husayn is still alive? Going near, Shimr laughed and called out again, 'Look, the second Zahra has arrived on the battlefield'. Hearing this, Shimr rose up feeling distressed, Shabbir rose up at the mention of his sister. Saying this, he moved forward with a dagger in his hand, over there a corpse began to writhe by the river. Here, the daughter of Batool came out from the tents, what strange disrespect Shimr showed by coming there. The tyrant showed not even a little bit of courtesy, the tyrant kicked the Holy Quran. Strange... The oppressor was committing such tyranny; sometimes his hands were in the hair of Husayn (a.s.), sometimes he would grab the blessed beard, and sometimes he would laugh. The oppressor removed the hair and struck with the dagger at once. Husayn (a.s.) said, 'Look, Ali Akbar!' The wretched one placed his knee on our chest. When the blow was struck, the angels turned their faces away. When the blow was struck, the angels turned their faces away. What to speak of angels, even the prophets turned their faces away. When the prophets turned away, the messengers turned their faces away. When the messengers turned away, the saints turned their faces away. Hasan (a.s.) and Ali (a.s.) said, 'Now only God knows, Husayn knows, the throat knows, and Fatimah (s.a.) knows.' Now, what more can be described? When the blow was struck, not a single drop of blood came out. The wretched one, in his rage, began to call out, 'Husayn!' Tell me quickly, what kind of miracle is this? The oppressed one said, 'What do you know of a mother's love? She has placed her throat upon my throat.' Fatimah (s.a.) said, 'Husayn, mother, remove your throat; it is impossible for you to be wounded.' When the wretched one's dagger moved across the Shah's throat, when the wretched one's dagger moved across the Shah's throat, this voice would come: 'Subhana Rabbiyal A'la' (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High). The son's blood flowed, the head was in the Sayyid's lap, Husayn was slaughtered in Fatimah's lap. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the pious and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon... Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief. Blessings be upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, our Imam of the time, our guardian, our master, our leader, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our consoler, the fortified cave, and the helper of the distressed and the destitute. May my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in His glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'Take to forgiveness, and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant.' Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief, and curse their enemies. I had declared this verse as the heading for this series of five lectures. In this verse, God Almighty is commanding His Prophet: 'O Prophet, take to forgiveness'—meaning, making forgiveness your habit, your way, your method. Adopt this method, that you keep forgiving people and treat them with gentleness. Be very soft, stay in a very mild manner with people. 'And enjoin kindness'—and always command what is 'Urfi' (customary/good). 'Urfi' means 'Ma'ruf' (virtuous), and 'Ma'ruf' means goodness. 'And turn away from the ignorant'—and when the ignorant address you, turn your face away from them. Do not argue with them, do not engage in unnecessary disputes with them. Do not argue with them, do not have unnecessary discussions with them. As I had submitted in your service, present your viewpoint. Continuing this sequence, see that 'Ma'ruf'—as I mentioned in the first lecture—means that which the intellect accepts and which gives pleasure to people when performed. That is what is called 'Ma'ruf', that which people find good. And because all of Allah's commandments, all the laws, all the divine laws, are in accordance with human nature, according to human nature, therefore when a person performs them, they feel good. Now, there might be a question in brackets here, that people might say, 'Brother, in every religion, in every faith, whatever a person does, they feel it is good.' What is the reason for that? If we get time today, Insha'Allah, we will try to cover why that is not 'Ma'ruf' and why this is 'Ma'ruf'. Insha'Allah, we will try to cover it if Allah grants the ability. So, in any case, the most important instance, the most important example of 'Ma'ruf', is the Imamate and Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Indeed. And in the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, there is a very important thing, and that is Azadari (mourning). So, before moving forward, let me submit to you that just as the child read the Maqtal of the Sayyid-e-Shuhada just now, and the young children, men, these children and youth who recite Noha (lamentation), believe me, these young people who recite Noha after the Majlis are the best example of 'Ma'ruf'. This is the best example, and believe me, I tell you with 100% confidence that this is not possible unless there is a mother's prayer. Subhan Allah. Without a mother's prayer, this is not possible at all. And for a mother's prayer, the mother's purity is the most important thing. These children who recite Noha, the Maqtal that the child read just now, or the other children and youth who recite, this is a sign of purity of birth. Believe this, and it is possible that for many people this might not be understood right now, it is possible that people might think, 'Brother, why do you say such things?' But firstly, this is all written in the traditions, and secondly, it is possible that it is not understood now, but Insha'Allah, at the time of death and in Barzakh, it will be understood very soon. Insha'Allah. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief. So remember that the most important example of 'Ma'ruf' is the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt. Love for the Ahlulbayt, and when there is love for the Ahlulbayt, a person will automatically, naturally learn their teachings. When they learn their teachings, they will automatically try to act upon them. And the more familiar they are, the closer they are, the more their life will be refined. Their actions should be like that, their character should be like that. The character should be such that the Ahlulbayt say, 'This is ours.' See, this is a very important thing—character. The character should be such that the Ahlulbayt say, 'This is ours.' It should not be that the Ahlulbayt distance themselves. No, it should not be that the Ahlulbayt distance themselves, rather they should say, 'This is ours.' That is why a tradition is found from the Imam, where the Imam said, 'Be an ornament for us and do not be a cause of shame for us.' See, become an ornament for us so that people see you and say that the lovers of the Ahlulbayt are like this. 'And do not be a cause of shame for us.' It should not be that people see you and say, 'All these Shias are like this. They are not right, do not deal with them, do not transact with them, they are dishonest, they are thieves.' Or their character is bad, they are bad in their outlook. This is a very important thing. A man came to Imam Sadiq (a.s.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief. And he said, 'Because of you, we have to face a lot of trouble, because of you, there is a lot of difficulty.' The Imam asked, 'What difficulty is there because of us?' He said, 'Whenever someone meets us, they say, "Are you a Shia?"'—in that era, Shias were called Ja'fari—'"Are you a Ja'fari?"' He said, 'They say, "Ja'fariyun khabithun" (The Ja'faris are wicked).' This is a Hadith, and it is a tradition in Usul al-Kafi, yes. I am reading the tradition of Kafi for you. Now, obviously, as soon as he said that, the Imam lowered his head. The Imam then asked him, 'Is there defamation for you because of us? Is there defamation for you because of us?' Then the Imam defined a Shia in one sentence. Do you know who is called a Shia? Who is a Shia? In one sentence. The Imam says, in one sentence, that a Shia is one who, if someone goes into a population of 100,000, 100,000, and asks, 'Who is the best in this entire population?', then they say, 'So-and-so person is the one,' that is the Shia. Subhan Allah. Pointing towards him. If it is not like that, then he is not among our Shias. In every respect, his character should be like that. Therefore, this method was taught, which I selected for this discussion, and the teachings—as I submitted to you until yesterday—that is, make it a habit to keep doing good to people. Keep doing good to everyone, whoever you meet. Only if you are certain that they will use it for a forbidden act or in disobedience to Allah, if they will use that thing to disobey Allah, then do not help them there. If you know, if you are certain that they are going to disobey Allah. Now, sometimes it happens that people, for example, if there are examples in front of you, surely you are more experienced than us, but the Hadith I am telling you in your service, if it becomes certain that a person is going to commit a sin, then do not help them. Now look at the Hadith, the Imam says, 'Four things go to waste,' meaning there are four things that have no benefit, they are always wasted. Which four things? One is sowing seeds in barren land. In barren land, seeds—barren means there is barren land, right, in which it is certain that farming cannot be done. If someone farms in it, then understand that he is a madman. If someone farms, when it is certain, for example, in the desert, if someone goes and sows seeds, then what will you call him? You would say this is a madman, what is he doing? How can farming happen in the desert? Farming cannot happen in the desert. And the second Imam says, "والسراج في القمر" (and a lamp in the moonlight), and if someone brings a lamp in front of the moon when it is shining fully, then he is wasting that lamp. And the third thing, "والأكل على الشبع" (eating while full), when the stomach is full, then eating. This is a very important thing; if the stomach is full, then one should not eat anything. In fact, I am speaking to the youngsters, even from a health perspective, it is very correct that one should leave the food—wa alaikum assalam—at that moment when there is still some space left in the stomach. Do not eat until the stomach is completely full; rather, leave some space; it is also a good thing for health. So these are three things. What was the first thing? That is, sowing seeds in barren land; second, lighting a lamp in front of the moon; third, eating even when the stomach is full, this is also a waste; and the fourth thing, "المعروف إلى من ليس بأهله" (doing a favor to one who is not worthy of it), doing good to someone who is not deserving of it. This thing is going to be wasted. But as for the other people, look, we are emphasizing this again and again, because a Shia is an ambassador of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Every Shia, for their group, whether they are small, big, young, a youth, old, anyone, whether they are a businessman, a professional, in every respect, what is every person? An ambassador. They are an emissary, they are representing the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Therefore, what should their character be? The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) taught that. It should be such that they keep distributing 'Ma'roof' (good deeds). Now listen to the Hadith, what it is. The Hadith is strange. Ma'ruf is defined as actions that align with human nature and intellect, with the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt being the ultimate example.
Boasting about charity or reminding recipients of favors invalidates the spiritual reward of the deed.
Small acts of kindness, such as smiling or making space for others, are essential expressions of faith.
Loyalty to the Imam must be absolute and independent of worldly status or power.
The sacrifice at Karbala serves as an eternal reminder to prioritize the pleasure of Allah over worldly desires.
Consistent recitation of prayers like Dua-e-Joshan-e-Kabeer helps maintain spiritual focus throughout the year.
