title: EP20 | Hadees-e-Saqalain Ke Nataaij (Part 2) | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound theological implications of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, emphasizing the mandatory nature of following the Ahlulbayt alongside the Quran. The discussion addresses common misconceptions and distortions regarding the obedience owed to the Prophet's family, citing both classical Sunni scholarship and Quranic exegesis. By analyzing the concept of 'Tamassuk' and the 'Habl al-Mateen,' the lecture argues that true salvation and adherence to the straight path are inextricably linked to the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
Teacher presents [music] [praise] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma salli ala sayyidina Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. [Arabic recitation]... The results of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, I will try to present as many results as possible for your service so that the discussion can be completed as quickly as possible. So, look, the second result of Hadith al-Thaqalayn is that following the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is just like the Quran. Just as a Muslim follows the Quran, just as following the Quran is mandatory, in the same way, following the Ahlulbayt is mandatory. And this is the same result that the scholars of Ahl-e-Sunnah have derived from Hadith al-Thaqalayn. This is the result derived by Mawlawi Muhammad Mubeen in his book 'Waseelat al-Najat' regarding the narration of the Hadith... Mubeen, in his book 'Waseelat al-Najat', after narrating Hadith al-Thaqalayn, writes in its commentary that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said three times, 'Udhakkirukumullah fi Ahl-e-Bayti, Udhakkirukumullah fi Ahl-e-Bayti, Udhakkirukumullah fi Ahl-e-Bayti' (I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt, I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt, I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahlulbayt). I remind you of Allah—when I remind you of Allah, how do you treat my Ahlulbayt? So, by that, he meant to fear God. Who is saying this? This is Mulla Muhammad Mubeen, the author of 'Waseelat al-Najat'. We are not reading this from a Shia scholar's book. So he says that your intention should be to fear God and observe the rights of the Ahlulbayt. Observe the rights of the Ahlulbayt, observe their rights, and wear the garment of their obedience and love. Meaning, obey them and love them. How is obedience done? How is love done? Claiming is a different thing. Is celebrating Eid on the day of Ashura love? Is celebrating Eid on the day of Ashura love? Does the demand of love mean we celebrate Eid on the day of Ashura? On the day of Ashura, we wear new clothes, go to fairs, celebrate weddings on the day of Ashura—is this love for the Ahlulbayt? This is not just not love for the Ahlulbayt, but it is a declaration of war against the Ahlulbayt, and a declaration of war against the Ahlulbayt is a declaration of war against the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Prophet said, the Prophet said in very clear terms, 'Silmuka silmi wa harbuka harbi' (Your peace is my peace, and your war is my war). 'Lahmuka lahmi wa damuka dami' (Your flesh is my flesh, and your blood is my blood). And what is the Ummah doing? The day the Prophet's grandson was martyred, the Ummah holds fairs, celebrates, and wears new clothes. This is the state of the Ummah. Now, who is saying this? Look, this is Mawlawi Muhammad Mubeen saying this in 'Waseelat al-Najat'—the book's name is also 'Waseelat al-Najat'. So he says, obey and follow the Ahlulbayt with your limbs and body, meaning physically obey the Ahlulbayt, obey the Ahlulbayt, and from your heart... Obey the Ahlulbayt and love them from your heart. And loving them from the heart is as mandatory as loving the Quran is mandatory. Just as it is mandatory to comply with the commandments of the Quran—'Imtisal' (compliance/obedience)—it is mandatory to comply with the commandments of the Quran. Whatever the Quran's command is, it is mandatory to obey it. In the same way, it is mandatory to obey the Ahlulbayt. This was the second result. Now look at the third result: it is mandatory for the Ummah to follow the Ahlulbayt. It is mandatory to follow them because if the Ummah does not follow them, it will go astray. What did the Prophet say? 'Ma in tamassaktum bihi lan tadillu ba'di' (As long as you hold onto them, you will never go astray after me). Now look at what Mulla Ali Qari writes here. He writes in 'Al-Mirqat fi Sharh al-Mishkat' that Ibn Malik says that holding onto the Book of God means acting upon it, meaning obeying its commands and abstaining from its prohibitions. Meaning, the command of the Quran, one must obey it, and whatever the Quran has forbidden, one must abstain from it and stay away from it. And holding onto the Ahlulbayt means loving them and imitating and following their lifestyle. It is mandatory for the Ummah that the Ahlulbayt... It is mandatory for the Ummah to imitate the Ahlulbayt, to follow the Ahlulbayt, to follow the Ahlulbayt. Imitation should be done. Who is writing this? Mulla Ali Qari is writing this. Sayyid Jamaluddin has added to this—this is Mulla Ali Qari saying that Sayyid Jamaluddin has added to this—that when their lifestyle and guidance are not against the religion. Look at how they even distort things, that when their... if this sentence itself is wrong, how can their lifestyle be against the religion? This is what we want to present to you, how they want to take one aspect and create a corner that goes against the Ahlulbayt. When the Prophet is saying it is mandatory for you to hold onto them in every respect, then how can you say they will go against the religion? When the Ahlulbayt are 'Ulu al-Amr' (those in authority) and their obedience is 'Ita'at-e-Mutlaqah' (unconditional obedience), when their obedience is mandatory without any condition, then how can they go against the religion? But this shows that this is a distortion. Look, it is a distortion. They say Sayyid Jamaluddin added, 'when their lifestyle and guidance are not against the religion.' But I say that the meaning of the Prophet's statement is this—who is saying this? Mulla Ali Qari is refuting Jamaluddin, saying, 'I say that the meaning of the Prophet's statement is this...' I say that the meaning of the Prophet's statement is that their lifestyle and guidance will always be in accordance with Sharia and Tariqa. This is what Mulla Ali says, meaning he refutes Jamaluddin's point, saying Jamaluddin is wrong. Mulla Ali Qari is defending this, remember. Therefore, this addition—the condition Jamaluddin added—is not needed. It is not only useless but is an extremely wrong condition. It is a condition that is against the statements of Allah and the Prophet. So, the reference is 'Al-Mirqat fi Sharh al-Mishkat', Volume 11, page number 307, and commentary on Hadith 6152. This is Mulla Ali Qari's. So this was the third result. Now let's come to the fourth result: the word 'Thaqalayn' itself, the word 'Thaqalayn' is proof of following the Ahlulbayt. The word 'Thaqalayn' itself is proof of following the Ahlulbayt. The word 'Thaqalayn' is enough. If the Prophet had only said this much—listen carefully—if the Prophet had only said, 'Inni taraktu feekum ma in tamassaktum bihi lan tadillu ba'di, Kitaballah...' (I am leaving among you two weighty things, if you hold onto them you will never go astray after me, the Book of Allah...), that would have been enough for their Imamate. That would have been enough. That would have been enough for their Imamate. So this word 'Thaqal' (weighty/precious), this 'Thaqal' is enough. Now look at what it is—meaning this very concept, how many scholars of Ahl-e-Sunnah have accepted it, which I presented to you. Al-Azhari in 'Tahzeeb al-Lugha', Nawawi in 'Al-Minhaj', Ibn al-Athir in 'Jami al-Usul' and 'Al-Nihaya', Daylami in 'Firdaws al-Akhbar', Tibi in 'Al-Kashif', Sharh Jurjani in 'Hashiya bar Mishkat', Ibn Khalifa in 'Al-Ikmal', Sanusi in 'Al-Nasir', Dawlatabadi in 'Hidayat al-Sa'ada', Muhammad Tahir Patni, who was a very great scholar of Gujarat, in 'Majma al-Bihar', Ibn Hajar Makki in 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa', Sheikh Abdul Haq Dehlavi in 'Al-Lama'at', and others—a very long list. Everyone has said that 'Thaqalayn' means those whom the Prophet called 'Thaqal'. Why? Because why were they called 'Thaqal'? 'Thaqal' because their obedience is very difficult, holding onto them is very difficult. Holding onto the Quran is also very difficult... Very difficult. Holding onto the Quran is also very difficult, and holding onto the Ahlulbayt is also very difficult, that is why they were called 'Thaqalayn'. All these scholars whose names I just presented to you, all these scholars have stated these things. Everyone's view is that their obedience is mandatory. This is everyone's view, and this is a very long list; this was just a very brief summary presented to you. Therefore, remaining attached to the mantle of the Ahlulbayt and acting upon their commands is mandatory, and this is what is called Imamate, this is what is called Caliphate. And what is Imamate and Caliphate called? Is there anything else besides this? Now let's reach the fifth result. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) expressed the words of Hadith al-Thaqalayn in one place like this: the Prophet said, 'Inni taraktu feekum ma in tamassaktum bihi lan tadillu ba'di, Kitaballah...' (I am leaving among you something, if you hold onto it, you will never go astray after me, the Book of Allah...). 'Tamassuk' (holding onto)—this word is also used in the Quran. What word is used in the Quran? There is a verse of the Quran... What word is used in the Quran? There is a verse of the Quran: 'Wa man ya'tasim billahi faqad hudiya ila siratin mustaqeem' (And whoever holds fast to Allah, he is guided to the straight path). Now tell me, how can one hold fast to Allah? What is the method? Can anyone tell? Is there any Muslim, brother, who will tell how to hold fast to Allah? What is the meaning of holding fast to Allah? Holding fast to Allah means acting upon the Quran, following the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Allah did not come down—as they say Allah sits in the sky, so He came down and said, 'Hold onto me, grab me.' It is not like that, is it? So 'Tamassuk' is in the Quran, 'Ila siratin mustaqeem', and the same thing the Prophet is saying. This is the Prophet's command. The Prophet's obedience is mandatory. The Quran has taken the guarantee regarding the Prophet: 'Wa ma yantiqu 'anil hawa, in huwa illa wahyun yuha' (And he does not speak from his own desire; it is only revelation revealed). This Prophet does not speak from his own desire, so this is Allah's command. This Prophet is Allah's... This is the command of Allah. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is merely conveying the command of Allah that I am leaving among you such things that if you hold fast to them, you will never go astray: one is the Book of Allah and the other is my Itrah (progeny). Now, if this does not mean Imamate and Caliphate, then what does it mean? Can anyone tell me what else it could mean? Ibn Abi Shaybah, in his book Musannaf—who is Ibn Abi Shaybah? Ibn Abi Shaybah was a teacher of Bukhari, but because he narrated some things regarding the status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) that were difficult for some people to accept, he was not included in the Sihah (the six authentic books). And Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in Al-Muttafaq wal-Muftaraq has narrated this tradition in these very words. That is why Muhammad Bashani wrote in his book Miftah al-Najah that this Hadith al-Thaqalayn was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Khatib in Al-Muttafaq wal-Muftaraq in these words. Mirza Muhammad Badani writes that both these scholars, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Khatib, in their book Muttafaq, wrote: 'Inni tarikun feekum ma in tamassaktum bihi lan tadillu ba'dikum Kitab Allahi wa Itrati...' If you hold fast to them—and I have already told you the verse of the Quran regarding 'I'tasam' (holding fast). One verse was 'Wa'tasimu bihablillahi jamee'an' (Surah Al-Imran, 103). Hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not be divided. Now you can look up the Tafsir (exegesis); the Tafsir of the opponents and the Shia Tafsir both state that 'Habl al-Mateen' (the firm rope) is the Holy Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). 'Habl al-Mateen' is the Holy Quran and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). This 'Habl al-Mateen' is a subject in itself. It is a topic on its own. 'Wa'tasimu' is a command from Allah. The Quran says 'Wa'tasimu bihablillahi jamee'an'. The Quran is giving a command. So, I have presented these two verses for your consideration. This is the view of the scholars of Tafsir, and this is the best proof for the Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And this is the meaning of 'I'tasam'. Muhammad Jarir al-Tabari, Tha'labi, Wahidi, Baghawi, Muhammad ibn Umar Razi, who is called Fakhr Razi... Muhammad ibn Umar Razi, who is called Fakhr Razi, Fakhreddin Razi, Baghawi, Nishapuri, Suyuti—all these scholars, all of them, regarding 'Wa'tasimu' in Surah Al-Imran, verse 103, have explained the meaning of 'I'tasam' as 'Tamassuk' (holding fast). And 'Tamassuk' means to follow and adhere to. So, when the command of 'I'tasam' is related to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then what else could it mean? There can be no other meaning beyond this. Now let us come to the final conclusion. Before that, a poem or a Qasida that Shafi'i said—Imam Shafi'i, as they call him—he said it in the honor of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). I present that Qasida for your consideration so that you may see that while people expressed love for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in books, to what extent they actually followed and obeyed them is between them and Allah. See what it is. Shafi'i says: 'Lamma ra'aitu al-nasa qad dhahabu... fi buhoori al-dalalati wal-jahli' (When I saw that people had gone into their sects... they drowned in the seas of rebellion and ignorance). When I saw that people were following such sects—this sect, that sect, this sect, that sect—Shafi'i says: 'Rakibtu bismi Allahi fi sufuni al-najat' (I boarded the ships of salvation in the name of Allah). And who are these? 'Wa hum Ahlulbayt al-Mustafa' (And they are the Ahlulbayt of the Chosen One). 'Wa amsaktu habla Allahi wa huwa wilayatuhum' (And I held fast to the rope of Allah, and that is the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt). This is what Shafi'i says: 'Kama qad umirna bi-tamassuki bi-hablihi' (Just as we have been commanded to hold fast to His rope). That is why I did this, and this became the cause of my salvation. This is Shafi'i's poem. And what did you do? So, the conclusion he derived and the result he reached was exactly this. And in this way, the results... The scholars of the Sunnah have narrated this. Tirmidhi has narrated it in these very words in Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 'Inni tariktum feekum ma in tamassaktum bihi lan tadillu ba'di, Kitab Allahi wa Itrati' (I am leaving among you that which if you hold fast to, you will never go astray after me: the Book of Allah and my Itrah). Take them, adopt them, do not abandon them. But alas, the Ummah abandoned them. It was just lip service. But if you ask, 'Brother, tell me, who are the members of the Ahlulbayt?', they cannot even name them. They do not know. Those who are not familiar with the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) tradition and the Seerah of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.)—this is the tragedy of this Ummah. The rest, Insha'Allah, next time. And our final prayer is praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and may Allah bless Muhammad and his pure, oppressed, and infallible progeny. Respected viewers, as announced, after every fourth episode of this video series 'Itmam al-Hujjah', there will be a quiz in which a few questions related to the previous four episodes will be asked. The link to the quiz... The link to the quiz is available in the video description and comment section. This link will remain live for one week, meaning you have a full week to provide your answers. [Music] [Laughter] The winners will be selected, who will receive 1,000 Indian Rupees. The winners will be announced in our next episode, Insha'Allah. Therefore, you are requested to watch these videos carefully and try to provide the correct answers to the questions asked in the quiz. Along with this, share these videos as much as possible. Participate in the quiz in large numbers and join us in helping to convey this message of the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to others, so that you too can be included among those who propagate the Wilayat.

title: Majlis 1 | Khair Kya Hai? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the Quranic concept of 'Khair' (goodness) and its intrinsic link to the love and remembrance of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The discourse emphasizes the spiritual significance of Majlis-e-Aza, the necessity of foresight in daily life, and the importance of teaching wisdom to the next generation. By reflecting on the tragedy of Karbala and the steadfastness of the Ahlulbayt, the speaker encourages believers to seize opportunities for virtuous deeds and maintain a deep, intellectual connection with their faith.
content:
May it be destined to go to Karbala, and from there, may it not be destined to return. May it be destined to go to Karbala. Whenever the eyes find an excuse for love, whenever the eyes find an excuse for love, may the excuse of the grief of the Prophet's family be destined. May it be destined to go to Karbala. Oh, the prostration on the chest of Husayn was the last, oh, the prostration on the chest of Husayn was the last, may I not have to lift my head. May it be destined to go to Karbala. Oh, you beloved, how long will you wander from door to door, may it not be destined to show in the end. May it be destined to go to Karbala. As Umm al-Banin received by destiny, as Umm al-Banin received by destiny, now what, now what, now what, may such a household be destined for anyone. May it be destined to go to Karbala. On the Day of Judgment, this is the desire, that without shroud, without burial, on the Day of Judgment, this is the desire, that without shroud, without burial, may it be destined to be buried in the soil of Karbala. May it be destined to go to Karbala. What is this, that the King left the shrine of the Prophet, in a foreign land, may I not be destined for a shroud. May it be destined to go to Karbala. May it be destined to go to Karbala. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the people of piety and certainty, and blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abu al-Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. May Allah bless him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our guardian, our master, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our comforter, the fortified cave, and the relief of the distressed and the needy, may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Now then, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in His glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: "Fastabiqu al-khayrat" (So race to all that is good). Allah the Most High, the Great, has spoken the truth. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. The honor of reciting this noble verse has been attained. In the noble verse, God Almighty is saying: "Fastabiqu al-khayrat". This noble verse has appeared twice in the Quran. That is, this sentence, this phrase, has appeared twice. Once in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse number 148, and Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse number 48. Meaning Surah Al-Baqarah verse number 148 and Surah Al-Ma'idah 48, in both, Allah is saying "Fastabiqu al-khayrat". The meaning of "Fastabiqu" is that you compete, all of you compete in good deeds. We usually use the word 'Khairat' in Urdu for charity, but in Arabic, the word for charity is 'Waliyah'. In Arabic, 'Khairat' is the plural of 'Khair'. Compete with one another in goodness. Try to get ahead of one another. See, if someone is doing more, you try to do even more. If there should be a competition, it should be in good deeds. Of course, there should be no envy in this, that one tries to bring the other down or prays for the destruction of their blessings. That is called envy. That is not the subject. The meaning is "Fastabiqu al-khayrat", that is, try to get ahead of one another in good deeds. This is the command of the Holy Quran, and these very good deeds are what become the cause for a person to receive forgiveness from Allah. Allah forgives their sins, and if someone tries to get ahead as much as possible in good deeds, Allah seeks different excuses to forgive them. The Quran says: "Sari'u ila maghfiratin min rabbikum wa jannatin arduha al-samawatu wa al-ard" (And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth). That is, you all run with speed. Look, what was in the first verse? "Fastabiqu al-khayrat" (Compete). Now what is here? "Sari'u" (Hasten). In Arabic, 'Sur'at' means speed. 'Sur'at' means speed. Go with speed. "Sari'u ila maghfiratin min rabbikum" (Hasten to the forgiveness of your Lord). And towards what? "Jannatin" (To that Garden) whose width is the distance between the heavens and the earth, and Allah has prepared it for whom? Peace be upon you too. "U'iddat lil-muttaqin" (Prepared for the righteous). Allah has prepared this Garden for the people of piety. Those whose hearts have the fear of God. Now, let us discuss two words here, God willing, and then move forward. See, two things: first, what is 'Khair'? 'Khair' means every good thing, whatever... Everything that brings a human closer to Allah is called 'Khair' (goodness). Everything that makes a human worthy of Paradise—or rather, not worthy, but brings them near to Paradise—is Khair. No one can truly be 'worthy' of Paradise; only those upon whom Allah’s mercy descends can enter it. Otherwise, no one is eligible. So, Khair refers to everything that brings a person closer to Paradise, everything that becomes a cause for Allah’s forgiveness and mercy so that they may enter Paradise. That is called Khair. Now, the question arises: there are many things that are Khair, but is there a specific Khair that is the focus or the collection of all goodness, where all goodness meets? In other words, if this Khair did not exist, the rest would be useless. There must be a Khair that is the source, the fountainhead of all goodness. So, when we began searching through the Hadith—or rather, digging through them—we came across a Hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Now, reflect on the words of the Hadith: 'Man arada Allahu bihi al-khair' (Whomever Allah intends good for). Look at the word 'al-khair' in Arabic; those familiar with Arabic know that when 'al' (the definite article) is used, it means the entirety of goodness, everything. In Arabic terminology, this is called 'istighraq'—meaning all of it, every bit of goodness. When Allah intends all goodness for someone—complete goodness, with no exceptions—'qadhafa fi qalbihi hubbal Husayn wa hubba ziyaratihi' (He casts into his heart the love of Husayn and the love of his Ziyarat). Allah places the love of Husayn and the love of visiting Husayn into his heart. And 'wa man arada bihi ash-shar' (And whomever He intends evil for)—and what is the opposite of Khair? Shar. Shar means evil. Now, when Allah intends evil for someone, what does that mean? It means Allah leaves them to their own devices. Allah leaves them to their own state. 'La ubali bi-ayyi wadin halak'—the phrase in the Hadith is that Allah says, 'I do not care in which valley he perishes.' Where he goes and dies, where he is ruined—Allah says, 'I do not care about him at all.' 'Wa man arada bihi ash-shar qadhafa fi qalbihi bughdal Husayn wa bughda ziyaratihi' (And whomever He intends evil for, He casts into his heart the hatred of Husayn and the hatred of his Ziyarat). He develops hatred for Husayn and hatred for visiting Husayn. Therefore, consider these Majalis-e-Aza (mourning gatherings) as a great blessing. Those who participate in these Majalis, where the virtues or the sufferings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are recounted—the Majlis of Husayn—are given a special name in the traditions: 'Huddasul-Husayn' (those who narrate/remember Husayn). They remember Husayn constantly, and they love Imam Husayn so much that when they are told to enter Paradise, they will not go; they will sit outside Paradise and continue to remember Husayn. This is a narration from Kamil al-Ziyarat. Subhanallah. Even the Houris (maidens of Paradise) will come and say, 'Come, we are longing for you.' They will say, 'No, the pleasure we find in the remembrance of Husayn, we will not find in anything else.' Subhanallah. This is the remembrance of Husayn, and this is the love of Husayn. This Azadari, this chest-beating, this Zanjeer-zani, this Qama-zani—all these Sha'air-e-Hussaini (symbols of Husayn) are where all goodness is gathered. These are the places where all goodness converges, and one should strive to excel in this, to outdo one another. Do not act with even the slightest stinginess or hesitation, wondering 'what will happen' or 'what will become of this,' because who is the leader of this? It is the Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (the Master of Martyrs), and He is responsible for everything. If Allah grants the opportunity to discuss creation, it will become clear to you that the leaders of the entire universe are Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). Therefore, a person should never worry that if I spend, my wealth will be exhausted. If I do this, will it be finished? These thoughts are for those who believe that they earned this money, that it is their income, their skill, or their achievement. They do not know that Allah gives to whom He wills and takes away from whom He wills. 'Qulillāhumma mālikal-mulki tu'til-mulka man tashā'u wa tanzi'ul-mulka mimman tashā'u wa tu'izzu man tashā'u wa tudhillu man tashā'u, biyadikal-khair, innaka 'alā kulli shay'in qadīr' (Say, 'O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. It is not something you earned yourself; it is all His bestowal. 'Qulillāhumma' means 'Say, O Lord,' 'Mālikal-mulk' means 'Owner of the Kingdom'—meaning, who is the owner of all the possessions in the entire universe? Allah. 'Tu'til-mulka man tashā'u'—You give this kingdom to whom You will. 'Wa tanzi'ul-mulka mimman tashā'u'—And You take it away from whom You will. There is also a verse in the Quran: 'Inna rabbaka labil-mirsad' (Indeed, your Lord is in observation). If someone just says this much, all their sins are forgiven, and Paradise becomes mandatory for them. This is a tradition. Just saying this much. Do not be surprised. Why? Because Paradise was created from the light of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Paradise was created from the light of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Imam Hussain (a.s.) is the leader of the youth of Paradise. We mourn the grief of that same Hussain in this Muharram. I will quickly present a Hadith in your service. You know Sheikh Saduq (may Allah be pleased with him); he was a very great scholar of religion, the leader of the traditionists. He narrated this tradition. He says that Imam Reza (a.s.) said, the Imam says that this month of Muharram was such that even the infidels in the age of ignorance used to respect it. They used to respect it. They considered killing and fighting forbidden in it. "Yuharrimuna fiha al-qital" (They considered fighting forbidden in it), but "Fastuhillat fihi dima'una" (Our blood was considered lawful in it by this Ummah). Look, killing is one thing, and considering blood to be lawful is a worse thing. That 'we can kill them, there is no harm, there is no sin in it.' "Fastuhillat fiha dima'una," "Wa hutika fihi hurmatuna" (Our sanctity was violated in it), "Wa subiya fihi dharariyyuna wa nisa'una" (Our children and our women were taken as prisoners in it), "Wa udrimat al-niranu fi madaribina" (Fire was set to our tents), "Wa untuhiba ma fiha min thiqlina" (And whatever they could loot from it, they looted), "Wa lam tura li-Rasulillahi hurmatun fi amrina" (And the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah was not observed regarding us). "Inna yawma al-Hussaini aqraha jufunana" (Indeed, this day of Hussain is the day, this grief of Hussain is the grief, by which our eyelids become wounded from weeping). Our eyelids become wounded. Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) says in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, "Fa-la-andubanna 'alayka sabahan wa masa'an wa la-abkiyanna 'alayka badala al-dumu'i dama" (I will lament for you morning and evening, and I will weep for you blood instead of tears). The same thing Imam Reza (a.s.) says, that the eyes and eyelids became so wounded, "Wa asbala dumu'una" (And tears kept flowing from our eyes). Then he says there, "Fa-'ala mithli al-Hussaini fal-yabki al-bakun" (So for the likes of Hussain, let the weepers weep). "Thumma qala 'alayhi al-salam" (Then the Imam (a.s.) said), "Kana abi idha dakhala shahru al-muharram" (When the month of Muharram used to enter, my noble father, Imam Kazim (a.s.), would not be seen smiling), "La yura dahikan," "Wa kanati al-ka'abatu taghlibu 'alayhi" (And grief would completely overcome him). And grief would completely overcome him. Until the 10th of Muharram would come. The 10th of Muharram, the day of tragedy, the day of grief and weeping. And he would say, 'This is the day on which Hussain (a.s.) was killed.' Yes, these are the same days. These are the days of weeping and lamentation that have arrived now. Today it has begun. Imam Hussain (a.s.) has come into our homes. Hussain is our guest. On the 28th of Rajab, this caravan left from there, but before that, on the 22nd of Rajab, when the news of Muawiyah's death came, Imam Hussain (a.s.) was called to the court. He was called to the court. Imam Hussain (a.s.) was in the mosque at that time, and someone came and told him that he had been called to the court. Hussain came home and informed Janabe Zainab (s.a.) that 'Zainab, I have been called to the court.' Janabe Zainab (s.a.) was worried upon hearing this, 'Brother, courts are not held at such a late hour. Why have you been called at this late hour?' He said, 'Sister, I know why I have been called. Their ruler has passed away, and I also know what they will demand from me.' I know what they will ask of me. And what they will ask, I can never give them. Janabe Zainab (s.a.) understood. She said, 'Brother, if you are going to the court at this time, I will not let you go alone.' She called out, 'Brother Abbas, son Ali Akbar, go, take the young men of Bani Hashim with you, and go to the court with the Master.' Yes, it is written in the Maqtal that there were 30 young men of Bani Hashim who took Imam Hussain (a.s.) in their circle and walked towards the Dar al-Imarah (Governor's house). As soon as they reached the Dar al-Imarah, Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Now you all stay here. It is not appropriate for you to come inside. I will go alone. Yes, but if my voice is raised, then you all come inside without permission. You all come inside.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) went in. The news of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan's death was announced to him. Upon hearing the news, the Mawla said, 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' After that, Walid read Yazid's letter, in which it was written, 'Walid, take the oath of allegiance (Bay'ah) from Hussain.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'This is a matter of Bay'ah.' This cannot be decided in the darkness of the night like this. Call the Muslims tomorrow morning in the daylight. Let everyone gather. After that, it will be decided whose allegiance (bay'ah) will be taken and who will give it. Walid said, 'No, Hussain, you cannot leave like this.' Yazid insisted. Hussain said, 'No, this matter is not like that, and if you are insisting, then hear my decision: Misli la yubayi'u mislah—a person like me can never give allegiance to a person like Yazid.' And saying this, Hussain left. As soon as Hussain left, Marwan called out, 'Walid, stop Hussain right now! Take his allegiance. If he does not give it, then behead him at this very moment.' As soon as the son of Fatima heard this, he looked at Marwan once and said, 'Who will kill me? You or Walid? Hatta tuhaddiduni bil-qatli yabna zarqa—O son of a woman with a bad reputation, you threaten me with death?' As soon as Hussain's voice rose, the youth of Banu Hashim entered the court. In the lead was Hazrat Abul Fadl Abbas. With sword in hand, he asked, 'My Mawla, who said what? Who dared to do this?' Hussain said, 'Abbas, Abbas, this is not the place for war. Abbas, be patient.' Hussain stopped Abbas. He counseled Abbas to be patient. I would say, 'My Mawla, this counsel continued until the day of Ashura, and Abbas left this world with that same patience. Fala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin (So may the curse of Allah be upon the unjust people). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the troubles of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant those who are childless, righteous and virtuous children. Return those who are far from their homeland safely and soundly. O Lord, O Lord, destroy the enemies of Islam and the enemies of Shi'ism. O Lord, protect the scholars of the world and the great Maraji'. Protect the holy shrines (Atabat-e-Muqaddasat). Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Hussain in this world and the intercession of Hussain in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Quranic Command to Compete in Goodness
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the Quranic injunction 'Fastabiqu al-khayrat,' emphasizing the importance of competing in good deeds to attain Allah's forgiveness and Paradise.

chapters.title: Defining Khair and the Love of Imam Husayn
chapters.summary: The lecture defines 'Khair' as everything that brings a person closer to Allah, identifying the love of Imam Husayn as the ultimate source of all goodness.

chapters.title: The Virtue of Azadari and Divine Sovereignty
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the spiritual significance of mourning for Imam Husayn and reminds believers that all wealth and sovereignty belong to Allah.

chapters.title: The Divine Gift of Majlis-e-Aza
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the opportunity to participate in mourning for Imam Husayn is a divine gift, often opposed by Iblis through various objections.

chapters.title: Seeking Divine Breezes and Remembering the Imam
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the concept of 'divine breezes' and emphasizes the importance of constant remembrance of the Imam of the Time in all life situations.

chapters.title: Keeping the Cause of Ahlulbayt Alive
chapters.summary: The Imam emphasizes that the cause of the Ahlulbayt is preserved by learning and teaching their sciences and keeping their traditions alive.

chapters.title: The Significance of Marifat and Harith al-Hamdani
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights that rituals like prayer are incomplete without the recognition (marifat) of the Imam, illustrated by the story of the loyal companion Harith al-Hamdani.

chapters.title: Teaching Wisdom to Children
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the importance of teaching children wisdom, foresight, and sound judgment as advised by Amirul Momineen to Harith-e-Hamdani.

chapters.title: The Importance of Foresight
chapters.summary: The lecture defines 'hazm' (foresight) as the obligation to consider the consequences of actions before beginning them, contrasting this with the behavior of the foolish.

chapters.title: Defining Intellect and Foresight
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba defines intellect as the protection of divine trusts and foresight as the ability to recognize and seize opportunities.

chapters.title: Seizing Opportunities in Life
chapters.summary: Using a practical analogy, the speaker explains that a wise person remains vigilant and prepared to seize opportunities, whether for worldly or spiritual gain.

chapters.title: Seizing Opportunities for Good
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the importance of seizing every opportunity to serve Imam Hussain (a.s.), highlighting that even small acts of devotion are significant.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Muharram
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the sanctity of Muharram and the immense grief of the Imams over the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the suffering of his family.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Refusal of Allegiance
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the events leading to Karbala, specifically Imam Hussain's firm refusal to pledge allegiance to Yazid in the governor's court.

title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 7 | Ghaibat-e-Kubra (Major Occultation) and Taqleed – Part 1
excerpt: This lecture explores the transition from the Minor to the Major Occultation of the 12th Imam, emphasizing the necessity of divine guidance in the absence of direct access to the Imam. It highlights the critical role of scholars in preserving the faith of the 'orphans of Ale-Muhammad' against modern ideological deviations. The session further discusses the importance of Intizar al-Faraj, the practice of Tabarra with wisdom, and the necessity of verifying religious knowledge through the authentic traditions of the Ahlul-Bayt.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik aduwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. Astaghfirullahalladhi la ilaha illa huwal hayyul qayyum ar-rahmanur rahim dhul jalali wal ikram wa atubu ilayh. A'udhu billahis sami'il 'alimi minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Allahumma kun liwaliyyikal hujjati-bnil hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil liwaliyyikal faraj waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi wa la taj'alna min a'da'ihi wa waffiqna lima tuhibbu wa tarda wa la takilna ila anfusina tarfata 'aynin abada wa la tastabdil bina ghayrana bihaqqi Muhammadin wa alihi tahirin. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da-hum ajma'in. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, it is Allah's grace and the blessings of His Proof (Hujjah) that this Mahdism webinar presented by 'The Strong Rope' has now entered its seventh session. With your prayers, dear viewers, our six sessions have been very successful. Under the topic 'The Doctrine of Mahdism in the light of the Holy Quran and Hadith,' various titles have been presented, and the discussion yesterday reached the point that during the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra), Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) had four special deputies whom the Imam (a.s.) himself had selected, and for whom the term 'Safeer' (Ambassador) has been used in the narrations. The first Safeer, Hazrat Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri (r.a.), was the representative of the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth Imams. Then, regarding his son, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, the eleventh Imam (a.s.) himself, in front of a delegation from Yemen—a special delegation that had come to the Imam—had declared, pointing towards Muhammad ibn Uthman, that he would be the representative of my son, Mahdi. And in that same sitting, the eleventh Imam (a.s.) stated regarding Uthman ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Uthman, 'Fasma' lahu-ma' (Listen to them both) and 'wa ati'u-huma' (and obey them both), 'fa-innahuma ath-thiqatan al-ma'munan' (because they are both our trusted individuals and our trustees). You will find this incident in the first volume of Al-Kafi, page 329-330, Hadith number one. Then, after that, in 304 or 305 Hijri, when Janab Muhammad ibn Uthman (r.a.) passed away, by the command of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), Hussain ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti (r.a.) was selected as the third Safeer. An interesting incident was narrated here: Hussain ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti's personality was neither very prominent nor well-known among the people, and despite not being very prominent or well-known, he was made the third Safeer, whereas people thought that Ja'far ibn Ahmad would become the one, who was a well-known personality at that time. A lesson-filled point for all of us here was that when the second Safeer was in his final moments, Ja'far ibn Ahmad was standing at his head side, and Hussain ibn Ruh was at his feet. As soon as it became clear that Hussain ibn Ruh would be the third Safeer, in accordance with the demand of obeying the Imam's command, Ja'far ibn Ahmad moved from his place and went to the feet, and requested Hussain ibn Ruh to come to the head side. Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) himself described Hussain ibn Ruh as the refuge for the believers during their most difficult stages. Finally, Janab Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samari became the fourth and final special Safeer of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), and after his passing, there is no longer any special Safeer or special deputy of the Imam; rather, Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) himself clarified through a Tawqi' (signed letter) that if anyone claims to be a special Safeer or special deputy after Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samari, then it should be clear to us that that person is a liar. From here, let us move towards today's connected discussion because our discussion on the Minor Occultation has concluded. Therefore, our topic for today and tomorrow, which is connected to it, will be the Major Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Kubra) and Taqlid (emulation). And for the increase of our knowledge on this topic, we have with us from Muscat, the honorable Maulana Sheikh Nadir Sadiqi Sahib. Salam Alaikum, Agha. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. I hope you, your family, and all your relatives and loved ones are well. Alhamdulillah, I hope you all are also well, and we pray to Allah that all believers, especially, remain in safety and well-being. Ilahi Amin, Ilahi Amin. You are welcome to this Mahdism webinar, and viewers, before the honorable Maulana begins his statement, please listen to an important announcement for today: today you will be able to send your questions only through 'The Strong Rope's' WhatsApp number. The number is, let me clarify the number for you once again: +91 or [number removed], which is the code, and after that [number removed], [number removed], [number removed]. So, keep your questions coming, and after the speech, Insha'Allah, the honorable Maulana will answer them. Bar Muhammad wa Ale Muhammad Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. A'udhu billahi minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Alhamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin. Was-salatu was-salamu 'ala sayyidina wa mawlana Abil Qasim Muhammad. Wa 'ala ahli baytihi tayyibinal tahirin. Wa la'nud da'imu 'ala a'da'ihim ila qiyam yawmid din. Rabbish rahli sadri wa yassirli amri. Wahlul 'uqdatan min lisani yafqahu qawli. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim, Allahumma kun liwaliyyikal hujjati-bnil hasan. Salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi. Fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin. Waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna. Hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil liwaliyyikal faraj waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa atba'ihi. Amma ba'd, faqad qala Allahu subhanahu wa ta'ala fi kitabil karim, a'udhu billahi minash shaytanir rajim, bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Yawma nad'u kulla unasin bi-imamihim, faman utiya kitabahu biyaminihi fa-ula'ika yaqra'una kitabahum. Fa-ula'ika yaqra'una kitabahum wa la yuzlamuna fatila. And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala said in another place: A'udhu billahi minash shaytanir rajim, bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Faintaziru inni ma'akum minal muntazirin. The Major Occultation and our responsibilities in this regard, and specifically one responsibility that I have to point out to you in this brief discussion, is that we will obviously discuss one of the most important responsibilities—and only one responsibility—that in the time of Occultation, the teachings of the Infallible Imams (a.s.) according to their names, regarding referring to the scholars in the Occultation, which the Infallible Imams (a.s.) have stated in their noble Hadiths, we will discuss that as much as possible, Insha'Allah. The Major Occultation, which began in 329 Hijri and continues to this day, and it is not known when it will end, when its conclusion will be. I will just present one point for your consideration: in view of the current situation, various messages, videos, and audios [suggest] that these conditions are signs of the Imam's reappearance—may God make all these conditions a precursor to the Imam's reappearance. This should be our prayer morning and evening: Allahumma ajjil liwaliyyikal faraj. Allahumma ajjil liwaliyyikal faraj. Fa-inna fi dhalika farajun lakum (For in that is relief for you). In this era of occultation (Ghaybah), the most important worship and the most important responsibility—which the fourteen Masumeen (a.s.) from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) down to the 12th Imam have emphasized, with details provided in their respective places—is the 'Ta'jil al-Faraj' (hastening the relief) or 'Intizar al-Faraj' (waiting for the relief), which has been declared the most superior form of worship. Its philosophy is very clear. For now, I do not wish to discuss this philosophy, but this era of occultation—about which the Imams (a.s.) had informed their followers, and I will read some traditions today and perhaps some tomorrow—it is stated in the traditions of Ghaybah that 'Inna lil-Qa'imi ghaybatayn' (Indeed, the Qa'im will have two occultations). There will be a minor occultation and a major occultation, and the believers living in that era have been explicitly warned in the traditions. In this era of occultation that we are living in today, we must not close our eyes and fall asleep. I am not saying all the things that are commonly said. My children and youth should remember one thing: whatever we need to take regarding guidance, we must take it from the door of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.). This white beard, this turban, this cloak and robe—they have authenticity and credibility only when they are substantiated by the sayings of the Masum (a.s.) and the sayings of the Imam (a.s.). If I state my own philosophy, my own theory, or my own intellect and thoughts, then it has no authenticity, and God willing, we will read traditions in this regard. Therefore, in this era of occultation, the Imams (a.s.) have warned their followers, their lovers, and those who believe in their Wilayah: where should you take your religion from? Protecting your religion and protecting your faith is the first stage. We take this very lightly; we have taken it very easily that since we were born into a Shia family, there is no problem. Nowadays, just as it is easy to access knowledge, it is equally easy to be led astray. A video clip comes, a WhatsApp message arrives, or we see a video on Facebook, and our faith becomes shaky, and doubts arise in us. Doubts arise in our faith, regarding our faith. Where will we go? I always say one sentence. Today, there are insurance companies all over the world. Some insurance company insures your car, some insures your business, some insures your house, your wealth, your life, and various other things, but there is no such insurance company that insures my faith and yours. For this, if we want to insure our faith, we must follow the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). Follow the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). 'Qala al-Imamu Baqirun alayhis-salam, Qala al-Imamu Sadiq alayhis-salam'—this is authentic for us. You know well that I gave the example of two Imams because knowledge has generally come from these two Imams. I mean, imagine that in such a difficult era of occultation, the Imams (a.s.) have not left their followers and lovers without a refuge. Does human intellect accept this? No, intellect does not accept it. Our claim is that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left this world, he appointed the 'Nafs-e-Rasool' (the soul of the Prophet) as his successor without any gap, because the earth cannot remain empty of the Hujjah (Proof) of Allah. The process of human guidance must continue. I do not mean—God forbid, God forbid—that today's scholars are the Hujjah of Allah. No, if I get a chance, I will present this to you. There is a difference between being a Hujjah of Allah and being a 'Hujjah' (in a general sense). A scholar can be a Hujjatul-Islam, but the Hujjah of Allah is behind the veil of occultation. 'Ayna al-sababu al-muttasilu bayna al-ardi wal-sama' (Where is the link connected between the earth and the sky?)—where is that sentence from Dua-e-Nudba, where is that connection that joins the existence of the earth and the sky? He is behind the veil of occultation. This does not mean that he is not behind the veil. 'Yantafi'una fi ghaybatihi wa yastadi'una fi bilayi bi-wilayatihi' (They benefit from him in his occultation and seek light from his Wilayah)—this is a sentence from a Hadith. We are still benefiting from his Wilayah today. Now that this has come to mind, some youth ask: 'Maulana, how are we benefiting?' I say one sentence: Our job is to seek guidance, and their job is to provide guidance. He and his Lord know how they are to guide us. I do not know. But when the saying of Sadiq (a.s.) has come: 'Yastadi'una bi-nuri wilayatihi' (They will seek light from the light of his Wilayah)—that light will be taken, guidance will be taken. Regardless, this is a separate matter. But after this, it is not as if my responsibility has ended, no. In the first stage, just for you... let me recite a Hadith so that we keep our faith strong and firm. That religion which came to us correctly through the companions after our Imams, then the scholars, and then through our ancestors—we must keep it protected. The narrator, Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, is among the 'Ashab-e-Ijma' (the consensus companions). He says: 'I went to the service of the seventh Imam (a.s.). I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, are you the Qa'im bil-Haq?' Look, the waiting for the Qa'im (a.s.) has been there since the time of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his traditions. These questions were also asked to the sixth Imam and the fifth Imam. It was asked to the seventh Imam: 'Are you the one who is the Sahib al-Amr (Master of the Command)?' Look at the expression: 'Sahib al-Amr'. That is, the one in whose hands is the command of the true government, the command of the divine government of the Imam of the Time—he is the Sahib, he is the Imam of the time who has been awaited since the time of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). 'Are you the Qa'im bil-Haq?' The Imam says: 'I am the Qa'im bil-Haq, but the Qa'im who will purify the earth from the enemies of Allah and fill it with justice just as it has been filled with oppression, is the fifth from my progeny.' The seventh Imam says that the Qa'im (a.s.)—may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for the dust of his footsteps—is the one who will cleanse the earth of the enemies of Allah. He will fill the earth with justice and fairness just as it has been filled with tyranny and oppression. Who is he? He will be the fifth from my progeny. The seventh Imam says: 'Lahu ghaybatun yatulu amaduha khawfan 'ala nafsihi' (He will have an occultation that will be prolonged due to fear for his own life). That Allah the Almighty will grant him occultation so that his life remains protected. Note this point. 'Yartaddu fiha aqwam' (In it, nations will apostatize). This is a dangerous sentence. 'Yartaddu fiha aqwam'—in which a nation will become apostate. Who is being talked about? Are the disbelievers being talked about? Are the Jews being talked about? Are the Christians being talked about? Are non-believers being talked about? No. This is talking about the people of Wilayah. This is talking about those who accept the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) without any gap. It is not about anyone else. Remember one sentence, my children and youth: in the light of these traditions, I say one thing. The 'admit card' for the examination of this era of occultation—the admit card that is needed to enter the examination—what is the condition of that admit card? Wilayat-e-Ali ibn Abi Talib. This is not just any test; it is the test of the Shias. 'Yartaddu fiha aqwam' (In it, nations will apostatize). Allah-o-Akbar. Nations, groups will become apostates. 'Wa yathbutu fiha akharun' (And others will remain steadfast). One... a certain amount. Although it was stated in a narration—not this one, but another—it was stated: 'Kal-milhi fit-ta'am' (Like salt in food). This is the exact expression. 'Kal-milhi fit-ta'am'. When our Shias remain, how many will be left? Like salt in food. Pray for your faith morning and evening. This is not a game, not a joke. A WhatsApp message comes, and we don't even know where our faith has drifted. Where are we standing? After faith is lost, a human doesn't grow horns on their head for them to realize it. A person thinks, 'I am a follower of Ali. I am an Azadari (mourner). I pray Namaz-e-Shab, I recite the Quran.' These are not the criteria. Teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). See for yourself. I am reading this narration for your benefit. There must be at least 10-12 such narrations. Pay attention to which points the Imam has highlighted. 'Wa yathbutu fiha akharun' (And others will remain steadfast). One nation will remain steadfast. 'Thumma qala alayhis-salam' (Then he said, peace be upon him). My seventh Imam says: 'Tuba li-shi'atina' (Glad tidings for our Shias). Open 'Mafatih al-Jinan'. Look at the deeds of Sha'ban; the definition of 'Tuba' is given there. 'Tuba li-shi'atina'. Are we receiving such a great thing without trial, without an examination? Is this trial and examination such that we are sleeping and passing the test? 'Tuba li-shi'atina al-mutamassikina bi-hubbina' (Glad tidings for our Shias who hold fast to our love). Do not think that just because we are currently on the love of the Ale-Muhammad, that is enough. To say that if we were born into a Shia family, what a great achievement that is? A person should go and seek forgiveness (Istighfar). The Wilayat of Ale-Muhammad, the love of Ale-Muhammad, is not granted to everyone. 'Tuba li-shi'atina al-mutamassikina bi-hubbina' (Glad tidings for our Shias who hold fast to our love). Those who remain steadfast on our love. Those who remain steadfast on our love. The love of Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad—remember, the love of Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad cannot be complete without this; listen to this Hadith: 'Tuba li-shi'atina al-mutamassikina bi-hubbina fi ghaybatihi' (Glad tidings for our Shias who hold fast to our love during his occultation), 'Fi ghaybati qa'imina alayhis-salam' (In the occultation of our Qa'im, peace be upon him). Second: 'As-sabirina 'ala muwalatina' (Those who are patient upon our Wilayat). They should not say that we should also take this Hadith, or go to that place, or meet those people, or follow those people, or take Hadith from that book. This Hadith, this religion is only and only Ali and the family of Ali. 'As-sabirina fi muwalatina' (Those who are patient in our Wilayat). And the second issue is one that perhaps we see around us, that people cannot swallow this. 'Wal-bara'ati min a'da'ina' (And disassociation from our enemies). 'Wal-bara'ati min a'da'ina'. Disassociation from our enemies. And after that, look at the status. See, this status shows that there is something fishy. The status the Imam (a.s.) is describing—first, he said 'Tuba' at the beginning. After that, the rank the Imam (a.s.) is describing, let a person just imagine. Let a person imagine that this rank—for which of his companions did the Imams describe such a rank? 'Ula'ika minna wa nahnu minhum' (They are from us and we are from them). 'Ula'ika minna wa nahnu minhum'. This expression is familiar, isn't it? Should I use the original context of this expression, for whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) used these words? 'Husaynun minni wa ana minal-Husayn' (Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn). 'Hasanun minni wa ana minal-Hasan' (Hasan is from me and I am from Hasan). 'Aliyyun minni wa ana min 'Ali' (Ali is from me and I am from Ali). 'Fatimatu bid'atun minni' (Fatima is a part of me). These are the expressions that my seventh Imam says, that those who remain steadfast on these during the time of occultation: 'Ula'ika minna wa nahnu minhum' (They are from us and we are from them). Two relationships, two mutual connections. 'Qad radu bina a'immatan' (They are pleased with us as their Imams). They do not go here and there. Only at the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), no matter what calamity comes, no matter what trouble comes. They are pleased with us as their Imams. 'Wa radina bihim shi'atan' (And we are pleased with them as our Shias). 'Wa tuba lahum' (And glad tidings for them). After that, what does the Imam say? I mean, what else does a person need? 'Hum wallahi ma'ana fi darajatina yawmal-qiyamah' (By Allah, they will be with us in our rank on the Day of Judgment). The matter is finished. That on the Day of Judgment, they will not be in our neighborhood in Paradise; they will be of our same rank. Of our same rank. Did you notice this? What does this mean? And what did the Imam say in this? He said a simple thing: 'Al-mutamassikina bi-wilayatina wal-bara'ati min a'da'ina' (Holding fast to our Wilayat and disassociation from our enemies). No. This means that this test itself is a difficult test. This is one thing I wanted to present to you. Insha'Allah, we will connect this to tomorrow's discussion. Let us read one narration today. As much time as we have, let us read one or two narrations. And then, Insha'Allah, our discussion will be directly on 'Taqlid' (emulation) tomorrow. And if we find time at the end, we will recite more narrations for you. But the Imam has warned us. Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). 'Qala Muhammad bin Ali al-Jawad alayhimus-salam' (Our ninth Imam said): 'Man takaffala bi-aytami ali Muhammad' (Whoever takes responsibility for the orphans of Ale-Muhammad). Who are we today? If our father is alive, mother is alive—may Allah grant long life to those whose parents are alive; and may Allah forgive those whose parents and ancestors have passed away from this world and grant them a place in the neighborhood of the Masumeen (a.s.). But the Masum (a.s.) says, who is the orphan? 'Yatimani ali Muhammad' (The orphans of Ale-Muhammad). The orphans of Ale-Muhammad are those whose Imam is behind the veil of occultation. We are all orphans of Ale-Muhammad. 'Man takaffala bi-aytami ali Muhammad' (Whoever takes responsibility for the orphans of Ale-Muhammad). Which scholar, which jurist (Faqih), which Mujtahid, who knows the Hadith of the Masumeen (a.s.). The scholar who takes responsibility for the orphans of Ale-Muhammad—responsibility does not mean just giving them rations, giving them food. That is a separate responsibility. That is a different responsibility. But it is not talking about that guardian. It is not talking about the one who is helping them for worldly growth. It is talking about that scholar, that Marja, that scholar who knows the Hadith of the Masumeen (a.s.) and the religion of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who is nurturing the faith of the orphans of Ale-Muhammad. What does the Imam say? The Imam says: 'Man takaffala bi-aytami ali Muhammad' (Whoever takes responsibility for the Ale-Muhammad). Who are the orphans? 'Al-munqati'ina 'an imamihim' (Those who are cut off from their Imam). Whose apparent connection is cut off. Now, whether it is a believer from Kufa or Nishapur living in the time of the sixth Imam, or a believer of today's era. What are the conditions of today's era? And yesterday, in the time of the sixth Imam, at least if a believer wanted, he could go from Nishapur to Medina. But today... 'Al-munqati'ina' (The connection has been cut off). And that minor occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra) about which you observed in the discussion yesterday and the day before—at least there was a special deputy (Naib-e-Khas). So now, in the time of occultation, has the Imam left us? No. 'Man takaffala' (Whoever takes responsibility) for the orphans of Ale-Muhammad. Who are the orphans? 'Al-munqati'ina 'an imamihim' (Those whose apparent connection from their Imam has been cut off). 'Al-mutahayyirina' (The bewildered). 'Al-mutahayyirina fi jahlihim' (Those who are bewildered in their ignorance). Who are bewildered and troubled. Obviously, a human is ignorant, a human is troubled, and they should be. That ignorance will destroy a human, will lead them to destruction if we do not have the fear and dread of that ignorance. 'Al-mutahayyirina fi jahlihim al-usara'i fi aydi shayatinihim' (Those who are bewildered in their ignorance, who are prisoners in the hands of their devils). And after this, just observe. Observe. It was enough, the matter was understood, but no. This matter is very important. 'Wa fi aydi an-nawasibi min a'da'ina' (And in the hands of the Nasibis from among our enemies). And here, 'Nasibi' does not mean the Nasibi that no Shia goes to. Has any Shia ever gone to a Nasibi? Have you seen any Shia go to a Nasibi? Who is called a Nasibi? One who holds malice against Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad, who holds malice against Ali, who holds malice against Ale-Muhammad. Can you imagine any Shia going to a Nasibi? That Nasibi is not meant here. Here, the Nasibi meant is the one who distances the Shia orphans of Ale-Muhammad from the virtues (Faza'il) and sciences of Ale-Muhammad. The Imam says: 'Man takaffala' (Whoever takes responsibility) for such orphans of Ale-Muhammad, 'Fastanqadhahum minhum' (He rescues them from them). 'Istanqadha' means to pull someone out who is drowning. Here, if he pulls them out from the ocean of darkness and misguidance, 'Wa akhrajahum min hayratihim' (And brings them out of their bewilderment), corrects their doubts, corrects their beliefs, answers their questions, solves their problems—that scholar. Now, I will leave the text. That he rescues them from the wrath of devils, from the whispers of people's devils. It extracts them from doubts. It extracts them from the wrath of the Nasibis and their doubts. بِحُجَجِ رَبِّهِمْ (By the proofs of their Lord), through the verses of the Quran and traditions, it guides them. And the proof of their Imams—not through their own philosophy, not through their own intellect, but in the light of the proofs of the A'imma-e-Athar (a.s.). لَا يَفْضُلُونَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى عَلَى الْعِبَادِ بِأَفْضَلِ مَوَاقِعِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ فَضْلِ السَّمَاءِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ (They are not superior before Allah the Exalted over the servants by a position greater than the superiority of the sky over the earth). It is a strange sentence. The Imam says, the status and rank of such scholars who extract the orphans of Ale-Muhammad from the devils, the Nawasib, the Nasibis, and the misguided ones, is so great that the distance between them and an ordinary human is as much as the distance between the earth and the sky, or even more. The earth and the sky, rather بِأَفْضَلِ مَوَاقِعِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ فَضْلِ السَّمَاءِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ, this superiority of the sky over the earth in terms of height is their superiority. وَالْعَرْشِ وَالْكُرْسِيِّ وَالْحَجْبِ عَلَى السَّمَاءِ (And the Throne, the Chair, and the Veil over the sky). Not just the sky; after the sky, there is the Throne, the Chair, the curtain, the veil—one does not know, this sky is not just this sky. The Chair, the Throne—that is the station of such scholars. And their superiority over an ascetic person is just like the superiority of the shining full moon over an ordinary, hidden star. This is the comparison and contrast the Imam is stating. But the point worth noting is that مِنَ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَالنَّوَاصِبِ (from the devils and the Nawasib). Therefore, in this era of occultation, in this time of occultation, we must strengthen our faith and specifically turn to those scholars whom, God willing, we will discuss in detail tomorrow. That in this era of occultation, the Imams have provided means for our training. And it is our responsibility to know where to turn in the time of occultation? How to turn? And what are its details? God willing, we will bring this topic to a point tomorrow. For today, our discussion will end here. وَآخِرُ دَعْوَانَا أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَجِّلْ فَرَجَهُمْ (And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief). Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. This was indeed a very instructive discussion for us, and Alhamdulillah, we have received a few questions. Yes. The first question is, let us read the first question and then we will explain it in our own words. 'During these tough times, how can we be more attached to the teachings of Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.) so that we are not deviated by the views and opinions of anyone?' Meaning, in these difficult times we are going through, the era of the Major Occultation, how can we remain attached to the teachings of Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.) so that we do not go astray from the religion due to anyone's views, opinions, or thoughts? Look, I don't know what happened, my voice must have reached you, there is no need to repeat it. Yes. No, no. Well, look, when I have this kind of discussion, this question always comes up, and answering it is very difficult. Look, how? Now, if I tell you to stay connected to the sciences of Ale-Muhammad. Obviously, you cannot stay in touch with the Hawza Ilmiyya, Arabic books, Bihar al-Anwar, and the likes of Bihar al-Anwar. I will try to mention one or two things. First, our biggest flaw is that we do not study books. This is our problem. Today, our entire religion is social media and nothing else. WhatsApp, Facebook, Hadith, clips—correct, incorrect—I have submitted to you. Look, I know such a layman. By layman, I do not mean, God forbid, anything derogatory; by layman, I mean someone who is not in direct touch with the Hawza Ilmiyya. But he has enough consciousness to understand what the teachings of Ahl-e-Bayt are and what they are not. One has to dedicate their life for this. One thing. Second thing, always try. Keep a method. What method? That when a speaker is speaking, see if it is in the light of the Quranic verses and Hadith, or if it is his own philosophy. No matter how reputable the person may be. Even in the Hadith of the Ma'sum (a.s.), try. It is our responsibility, it is our responsibility to read the Hadith with justice. Read it with the Arabic, translate it correctly. This is our responsibility, but it is also your responsibility, the responsibility of the public, to see if what is being said is in the light of Hadith or if it is my philosophy. I say one sentence, remember this. Whether it is the Hawza Ilmiyya of Najaf or the Hawza Ilmiyya of Qom, even if I study there for 100 years, my words have no authenticity. My words have authenticity only and only when I say 'Qala al-Baqir' (The Imam said) and 'Qala Imam Sadiq' (a.s.). Therefore, make it a habit to keep your eyes open, keep your mind open, that what we are listening to is 'Qala Imam Sadiq'. Alhamdulillah, we have enough consciousness, having listened to Majalis for 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 years. We should have at least that much. Therefore, specifically regarding this, and so that I do not make the answer to your question too long, let me submit one sentence to you. Now, the Imam has stated a method. The Imam has given an answer within your question: if it is the time of occultation and different voices are rising from here and there, then the Imam gave a law. What law did he give? He gave this law: keep loving those whom you used to love. That is, Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad. The 14 Ma'sumeen. And keep enmity and hatred towards those whom you used to have enmity and hatred for, that is, the enemies of Ale-Muhammad. We should make this an amulet and tie it on our hands; these are two sentences of the Imam. The 14 Ma'sumeen, the Ahl-e-Bayt-e-Athar (a.s.). Now, the 14 Ma'sumeen, certainly the Ahl-e-Bayt-e-Athar (a.s.), Hazrat Abul Fazl Abbas (a.s.), Hazrat-e-Zainab-e-Kubra (s.a.), Hazrat-e-Ali Akbar—all of them are included. Ahl-e-Bayt-e-Athar (a.s.) whom you and your ancestors used to love, keep loving them, and have enmity and hatred towards their enemies. Whether I understand this or not, we should instill this within ourselves and dissolve it in water and feed it to our children so that they do not go to any other door. Otherwise, this is the only path to salvation: to remain connected to the sciences of Ale-Muhammad. These two sentences, I... Alhamdulillah, thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. And the point at which you ended the first answer, our second question is related to that. One is love, the other is enmity and hatred towards the enemies of Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.). The second question related to that is: 'During these days, let us read the first question. Anyone who does Tabarra is looked down upon or called by various names. In the light of the tradition of Imam Kazim (a.s.), what is our responsibility with regards to Tabarra?' Meaning, these days, if anyone is seen doing Tabarra, they are either called by various names or they are... They are looked at with a different perspective. In the light of the Hadith of Imam Kazim (a.s.) that you mentioned, 'Tuba li-Shi'atina' (Glad tidings to our Shia), what is our responsibility regarding Tabarra? Look, Tabarra is not like the ignorant. Look, the A'imma have given us teachings according to wisdom, consciousness, and intellect. My children and youth, remember, the era that is called today—I will discuss its details some other time—is called the era of 'Khudna' in the traditions. Khudna. What is the era of Khudna called? That is, when the Imam is in the veil of occultation. In simple words, it is the era of Taqiyya. Therefore, there should be no ignorant act due to which a Shia life or the Shia religion and Islam are harmed. This is not permissible. It is mentioned in the traditions that people came to the A'imma and said, 'Mawla, if we help you in the time of occultation or in such circumstances, what should we do?' The Hadith of the eleventh Imam. I am not reading that tradition, but I will state the concept for you. 'If you want to help us, sit quietly and curse our enemies.' It's okay. Let people say what they want. First of all, the matter should not reach people's ears. What is the need? On my Facebook, on my WhatsApp, on my status, no. Neither the status is reliable, nor Facebook is reliable, nor WhatsApp is reliable. What is reliable is my heart, my soul, my tongue, that's all. I will not become 'Wilayi' by status. I will become 'Wilayi' by my heart and my faith. People—first of all, people shouldn't even know. Now, if you are an unfortunate cleric like us, then it's fine. Now it is our compulsion that our faith becomes apparent. It's okay. Let people say, call us 'Malang', whatever they want to say. First of all, we should keep it hidden as much as possible. But you are also compelled that, for example, you are preaching among your relatives or preaching somewhere and your faith is becoming apparent, it's fine, let people say what they want to say. But in any case, this is the religion of Ale-Muhammad. It is the religion of Ale-Muhammad. Listen to one Hadith in this regard so that the matter becomes even stronger. A person came to the sixth Imam, if I am not mistaken, to the sixth Imam, and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, a person believes in your Wilayat very much. He believes in the Wilayat with a loud 'Nara-e-Haidari', but his Tabarra is a little weak.' The Imam said, 'He thinks he is our Shia?' He is not our Shia. Yes. Many times, Maulana Sahib, it has been seen that, as you said, the point is absolutely correct because obviously, it is the command of the A'imma. Therefore, there is no two opinions about it that it is obligatory for every person to obey them. But those who say many times that 'it is our own gathering, our own Majlis, a private gathering where there is no such danger.' Nowadays, it is seen that even in such gatherings, there is a ban on these things. Well, it is good that you got clarification on this. Look, the Almighty has given us intellect, and this intellect should be with the Shia of Amir al-Mu'minin. If the Majlis or gathering is 100 percent safe, and if this gathering or Majlis does not happen, then how will our children know? Who will tell our children about this religion? Therefore, this... look, its justification, deciding this, every person is responsible for themselves. They are responsible for themselves. If they are satisfied between themselves and Allah that my words will not reach the ears of a non-mahram, that it will not reach their ears, I am satisfied. It is permissible, and in fact, sometimes it is obligatory. However, I have mentioned that if there is any threat to a Shia, the Shia school of thought, or Islam, then there is accountability on the Day of Judgment. A person should take precautions, and it is essential to convey this to our children and the youth. In such a closed gathering—a very private one—this issue should be addressed first. Once this issue is addressed, then it is fine; there is no harm. Obviously, there is no harm. If the Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) had not mentioned this in the traditions, how would you and I have known? Alhamdulillah. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. Another question has come up: you mentioned Yunus ibn Abdurrahman, may Allah have mercy on him, who is a narrator of hadith. There was a point about the 'Ashab-e-Ijma' (the companions of consensus). So the question is: who are these Ashab-e-Ijma? Do such people exist today, and if they do, how can they be identified? If I remember and get the opportunity, Insha'Allah, I will explain this in detail tomorrow. The Ashab-e-Ijma are those of the fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth Imams. Zurara, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Abu Basir, Burayd ibn Ijli Hamadani, Safwan ibn Abi Umayr, Yunus ibn Abdurrahman—there are about 18 such people, only 18. Sheikh Tusi has called them the Ashab-e-Ijma. Now, this will be a separate topic. I might not be able to discuss it in great detail, but if I get the chance tomorrow, I will list the names that Sheikh Tusi has identified as the special companions of the Imam. Although this is not in a single tradition, they were so reliable, close, and trustworthy that Sheikh Tusi—look, you cannot remove Sheikh Tusi from Shi'ism. If you remove him from Shi'ism, the foundation of Shi'ism will collapse. Sheikh Tusi has given them the title of Ashab-e-Ijma. If I get the chance, Insha'Allah, we might discuss it tomorrow. Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah. You mentioned Sheikh Tusi, the Sheikh al-Ta'ifa. Our elders used to tell us that whenever you go to Najaf for Ziyarat, for the Ziyarat of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), first take permission from Sheikh Tusi before entering the shrine of Amir al-Mu'minin, and then go to the shrine. May Allah have mercy on him. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. We have reached the conclusion of today's session. We are very grateful that you spoke clearly and candidly on a topic that is very rare to see these days, especially on such a subject. We are truly grateful to you. We are also grateful to all the viewers who have stayed with us. Let us all pray together at the end that the Almighty hastens the reappearance of the Imam of our time. May He count us among his sincere servants and grant us the ability to pave the way for his radiant reappearance. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasani salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Rabbi salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Insha'Allah, tomorrow at the same time, i.e., 10:30 PM India time, we will continue this topic. Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah. The Major Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Kubra) and Taqlid. Until then, we take your leave. Khuda Hafiz, iltemas-e-dua.

True scholars serve as essential guardians who protect the faith of believers from the 'ocean of darkness' and modern misinformation.
Religious knowledge must be strictly verified against the Quran and the traditions of the 14 Masumeen rather than personal opinion.
The era of Ghaibat is a profound test of faith requiring steadfastness, patience, and adherence to the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt.
Tabarra and Taqiyya must be practiced with intellect and caution to ensure the safety and preservation of the Shia community.
True Wilayat is an internal state of heart and faith, distinct from superficial social media expressions.
