chapters.title: The Four Special Deputies of the Minor Occultation
chapters.summary: The lecture reviews the era of the Minor Occultation, highlighting the roles of the four appointed ambassadors (Safeers) who served as the direct link between the Imam and the believers.

chapters.title: Introduction to Major Occultation and Taqlid
chapters.summary: The session transitions to the Major Occultation, emphasizing the necessity of relying on the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt and qualified scholars to protect one's faith.

chapters.title: The Importance of Intizar al-Faraj
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the significance of 'Intizar al-Faraj' (waiting for the relief) as the most superior form of worship during the era of the Major Occultation.

chapters.title: Protecting Faith in the Modern Era
chapters.summary: The lecture warns against the ease of spreading misinformation and stresses that true guidance must be rooted strictly in the authentic traditions of the Infallible Imams.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Divine Guidance
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the earth cannot remain without a Hujjah (Proof) of Allah, and that believers continue to benefit from the Wilayah of the Imam even during his occultation.

chapters.title: The Trial of Occultation
chapters.summary: Using a narration from the seventh Imam, the speaker highlights the prolonged occultation of the Qa'im and the severe test of faith that will cause many to apostatize.

chapters.title: Steadfastness and the Status of True Shias
chapters.summary: The lecture details the high status of those who remain steadfast in their love and Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt during the occultation, promising them a rank alongside the Imams.

chapters.title: The Orphans of Ale-Muhammad
chapters.summary: The speaker defines the orphans of Ale-Muhammad as those cut off from their Imam during the occultation, emphasizing the role of scholars in guiding them.

chapters.title: The Role of Scholars in Occultation
chapters.summary: Scholars who rescue believers from ignorance and misguidance hold a high spiritual status, likened to the vast distance between the earth and the heavens.

chapters.title: Maintaining Faith in Modern Times
chapters.summary: The speaker advises believers to prioritize authentic Hadith over personal opinions and to remain steadfast in their love for the Ahl-e-Bayt to avoid deviation.

chapters.title: The Practice of Tabarra in the Era of Occultation
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the importance of performing Tabarra (disassociation from enemies of Ahl-e-Bayt) with wisdom and caution, emphasizing that it should not endanger the lives or reputation of Shias.

chapters.title: Guidelines for Private Gatherings and Ashab-e-Ijma
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that private, safe gatherings are appropriate for discussing Tabarra to educate the youth, and introduces the concept of Ashab-e-Ijma as highly reliable companions of the Imams.

title: EP05 | Intezaar, Alaamatein Aur Hamaari Zimmedaari | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2025 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance of 'Intizar' (waiting) for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time. It emphasizes that true waiting is an active state of moral preparation and firm belief rather than passive expectation or the forbidden practice of fixing a specific time. The session highlights the virtues of the 'Muntazir' (the expectant), the importance of Dua-e-Ahad for renewing one's allegiance, and the necessity of aligning one's life with the teachings of the Ahlulbayt.

Mega Quiz. Before starting this episode, we praise and glorify Allah, that infinite praise and glorification be for that pure and holy Essence of Unity, for that All-Knowing, All-Wise Creator of the universe, who blessed us with the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And this is the Wilayah without which no worship or deed is acceptable. And the final link of this Wilayah and Imamate is Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), for whom the Holy Prophet Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) himself stated that 'Afdalul-ibadati intizarul-faraj' (The best of worship is waiting for the Faraj/reappearance). And this is no ordinary wait; for this, Allah (s.w.t.) Himself stated in the Holy Quran: 'Faintaziru inni ma'akum minal-muntazirin' (So wait, I am also with you among those who wait). And the topic of today's episode is also this: waiting for the reappearance, about which the poet has beautifully said: 'Aankhein bichhi hui hain yameen-o-yasar mein, armaan chal rahe hain dile-beqarar mein. Ek main hi muntazir nahi, muntazir Imam-e-Mahshar ruka hua hai' Muntazir Imam-e-Mahshar ruka hua hai tere intezar mein. Subhan Allah, Mahshar ruka hua hai tere intezar mein. Come, gentlemen, along with this, we welcome our guests, respected Ahsan Jafri Sahab, respected Kazim Syed Sahab, and respected Gulzar Haider Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Ahsan Bhai, as far as we have seen in the traditions, waiting is one of the best forms of worship, but the question arises that if it holds such a high status, then knowing its importance is very important in itself. We want you to describe the importance of this important topic of waiting for our viewers once. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Salla Allahu alaika ya Wali-Allah. Regarding the importance of waiting, and especially before speaking about waiting for the reappearance of the Imam, it is also necessary to know one thing, and this is a common thing, a common observation for us that we see in daily life, that this waiting has many stages. The reappearance of the Imam is the wait itself, and its importance is something we will discuss, Insha'Allah. But first, generally, waiting itself is a commendable thing. Waiting itself is a commendable thing. Not only is it a commendable thing, but we have also waited many times in daily life, and people keep this thing with them. Waiting, and clearly, waiting along with patience. Because if we look at the example of daily life, for instance, parents raise their children, they have all their hopes, they make all their efforts, they work hard so that they can raise their children in the best possible way. And that wait for which they have worked hard, the end result or the outcome for which they have worked hard—because waiting does not mean just sitting with hands folded. If we are talking about waiting, it means that along with waiting, there will be efforts. So, the parents who make efforts, work so hard, and struggle for the upbringing of their children, in what hope, in what wait? That this child becomes successful in the world, even from a worldly perspective, that our child becomes successful. Now, when that boy is 20, 22, 25 years old and stands on his own feet, then the parents get the fruit of their hard work. Because there is a famous saying, right, that the fruit of patience is sweet. So, now after 20-25 years, they got the result of that thing. In these 20-25 years, what did they do? They worked hard in the wait for the result that was to be received after 25 years. Indeed, indeed. And they made efforts. Wow. Then they got the result. Wow. So, generally, waiting is a very important thing, and often this thing is praised, and people themselves practice it in their practical lives. But now, when this same waiting is done for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), efforts are made for his reappearance, struggle and hard work and true patience are practiced for his reappearance, then it has a different importance, and the end result of it, we cannot even imagine. Absolutely correct. Because the state of this waiting is different, and since its state is different, therefore its result is also different. Indeed, it is not like the result of ordinary life. Or generally, if seen, every person is waiting for something or the other in their own way. A laborer waits for his wages, the one who has been oppressed waits for justice, even those who deny this belief in Mahdaviyat are waiting for that Day of Judgment. But we are waiting for the 'Qiyamah Sughra' (minor judgment) before that Qiyamah. Ahsan Bhai, that verse is coming to mind, that line is coming to mind: 'Qiyamah se pehle qiyamah ka aalam, qiyamah nahi hai' Qiyamah se pehle qiyamah ka aalam, qiyamah nahi hai, toh phir aur kya hai? Are chupne wale zamane ko teri zaroorat nahi hai, toh phir aur kya hai? Wow, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. So now, if one wants to estimate the importance of this waiting for the Imam, there is a Hadith of Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) in which the Imam says: 'Man mata... if any of you passes away, leaves this world, but in what state? Wa huwa muntazirun li-hadhal-amr' (And he is waiting for this matter, i.e., this government, i.e., the government of Ahlulbayt (a.s.)). Waiting for this government, the 'Dawlat-e-Karima' (Noble State) as mentioned in the traditions. 'Dawlat-e-Karima' or a noble government, a government in which every person will be valued, indeed humanity will be valued. Regarding justice, the spread of justice worldwide. This is what has been said about this government, that when the Imam (a.s.) comes, he will fill this world with justice as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. And such justice, about which it is narrated that justice will enter people's homes just like sunlight. Subhan Allah. This is an unimaginable thing in today's date, how this work will be accomplished, but for the Imam, nothing is difficult. And this justice is such a thing, a natural thing, that every person waits for it. Whoever has been oppressed waits for justice. Whoever has been oppressed waits for justice. Absolutely. And this, not only we, but this universe has seen only a slight glimpse of this justice in the years 36 to 40 Hijri during the government of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). In the life of the world, those are the only four years about which it can be said that no one slept hungry under Ali's government. Indeed, indeed. Or if someone was oppressed, he did not fail to get justice, he was not denied justice, because the judgment of Ali (a.s.) is famous. Indeed, indeed. So the world has seen only a glimpse. When Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) comes, he will fill the entire universe with justice. This is that 'Dawlat-e-Karima'. If the Imam says that even if you leave this world while waiting for this great government, what will be the reward? The Imam says the example of that person, your example is such that 'wa huwa ka-man kana ma'al-Mahdi fi fustatatihi' (he is like one who lived with Imam Mahdi (a.s.) in his tent). Then after this, the piece of the tradition says, the sentence of the tradition says, that after that the Imam (a.s.) paused for a while, the Imam remained silent for a while, then the Imam said, 'No, not just this much, but he is like one who has fought with a sword alongside the Imam.' Then the Imam says, 'No, not just' No, not just this much, by God, he is like one who has attained martyrdom alongside the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). This is the importance of that great waiting. But what is the most important point in this Hadith? What does the Imam say in the beginning? 'Man mata minkum' (If any of you dies before this reappearance). This means the most important thing here in this Hadith is: 'Among you' (i.e., the belief you hold, the belief you have). We saw that the virtue of waiting is so great that we cannot even imagine that it is like attaining the rank of martyrdom alongside the Messenger of Allah. So, for a 'Muntazir' (one who waits), the question is, how is his status higher compared to other people? A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Salla Allahu alaika ya Wali-Allah. Viewers, as our brother Janab Atta Sahab asked this question, what is the virtue of the Muntazir, what is the importance, and as you have just what is the importance, and as you have just heard from Ahsan Bhai, that if any of you who holds this belief, the belief in Mahdaviyat, the belief in Imamate, passes away from this world, then all these virtues have been stated in the Hadiths of the Masumeen (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). A similar Hadith, Atta Bhai, we want to present to the viewers, which confirms this belief. Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) states to his companion Abu Khalid: 'Ya Aba Khalid, inna ahl-e-zamani ghaibatihi al-qa'ilina bi-imamatihi' (O Abu Khalid, surely those who, during the time of his occultation, believe in his Imamate). And then the Mawla says: 'wal-muntaziruna li-zuhurihi' (and are waiting for his reappearance). So, both points are here: they hold the belief in Imamate and are also Muntazir (waiters). Now, from here, the Mawla is stating his virtue and what will happen. Who are they? Who Mawla is stating what will happen, who are they? What is the virtue of those people? Immediately, the Mawla says: 'Afdalu min ahli kulli zaman' (They are superior to the people of every age). Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. That these two qualities, if found in a person, that he believes in the Imamate and is a Muntazir of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), then what is he? The Imam (a.s.) has declared them superior to the people of all ages. And then about them, the Mawla says: 'Allah tabaraka wa ta'ala atahum minal-afham wal-ma'rifah' (Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has given them understanding and recognition). And since this person, this group, these people believe in the Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and are Muntazir, Allah does not leave them just like that, but Allah gives them, and gives them from His best blessings, which includes: He gives them 'Aql' (intellect). He gives them 'Fahm' (understanding). And He does not just give intellect and understanding through which they can distinguish between truth and falsehood, but Allah gives them 'Ma'rifah' (recognition). Wow. And what is Ma'rifah? Ma'rifah is the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). My son, if you want to recognize the status of the Shia, then know how much they narrate hadith from us and how much they possess our Ma'rifat (gnosis). Allah grants Ma'rifat to those who are expectant (Muntazir) and who believe in the Imamate; meaning, they are immersed in the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This is a very important point. Following this, the next sentence in the hadith says that the Mawla states that for them, the occultation (Ghaybah) is as clear as if they are witnessing it, as if they are seeing the Imam. So, it is very important to understand this. When can a human witness something? A human can only witness when they are at a level of certainty where not even a shred of doubt or hesitation exists in their mind—whether 'is he my Mawla?', 'is he not my Mawla?', 'when will my Mawla come?', 'will it be soon or late?'. They are very calm because their eyes are fixed on the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and they are absolutely firm in their belief in their Imamate. For this reason, they witness it; they do not panic. Four lines of poetry come to mind: 'The opponents are skeptical, but you go and see that we are waiting. It is a different matter whether we exist in this era or not, but you will come, we have this trust.' Wow, wow, wow, certainly that all of us... Wow, wow, wow, certainly that all of us who are followers of Imamate and expectant (Muntazir) believe that my Mawla will definitely come. After this, the hadith continues, and Imam (a.s.) states: 'And Allah will place them in that era at a status equal to those who are fighting with swords in front of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' This was your question regarding what the virtue of the Muntazir (the expectant) is. Firstly, they are superior to all eras, and as Hassan Bhai just mentioned in the hadith he narrated, this same sentence appears: they will be seen fighting alongside the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.). Now, the one who is waiting, in this era of 'ghaybah' (occultation) when the Imam is not present, for the one who is waiting in 'ghaybah', for the 'muntazir' (the one who waits), it is necessary and essential that to fulfill that purpose—when the Imam reappears, to fulfill what he will present before him, that he will be a helper of the Imam—for that, a firm determination is needed. He should keep a firm determination that I will help the Imam, I can become a helper of the Imam. And along with that, his intention should be with sincerity. Intention—intention is very much—if you look at the traditions, there are many traditions that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Niyyatu al-mu'mini khayrun min 'amalihi' (The intention of a believer is better than his action). The intention is better than the action. So, if he keeps the intention with sincerity, and even if he is not able to perform the action, he still gets the reward for it. He still gets the reward for the action based on the intention. But the condition is that his intention should be with sincerity. And to clarify this, the sixth Imam, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), says in a tradition: 'Niyyat'—the Imam himself is saying this—'I wish I were in Karbala.' Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) was not present in Karbala. There is a tradition in which the Imam says, 'I do not consider myself separate from the martyrs of Karbala; I cannot keep myself separate from them, and I do not consider myself separate from them.' And I consider their reward less for myself—the martyrs of Karbala, the reward they have, the Imam says, 'I do not consider myself less than them even in that.' That is, even in the reward, why does he say that? Because if I were present on the day of Ashura (in Karbala), I would have helped them there. Yes, so this intention of theirs to help—even if they are not present in Karbala, they are not among the martyrs, but still, they will get the same thing that is theirs because the intention must be sincere. This is what he says, 'My intention that I would have been there, even if I am not, I do not consider myself less than their reward.' He further says... He says that in the same way, our Shias are also martyrs. Whoever is a Shia, if he dies, he is also a martyr. Why is he a martyr? Because even if he dies in his bed, yes, but their intention is for our 'nusrat' (help). It is for the help of the Ahlulbayt. Therefore, every Shia who dies is a martyr. Why? Because with this intention, we need to make the intention with sincerity that we will help the Imam. So, in this 'intezar', when we are waiting in this era of 'ghaybah', it is the first duty of the 'muntazir' that he should purify his intention for helping the Imam after his 'zuhur'. Yes, absolutely. And here I want to ask Kazim Bhai, there is a very famous and well-known hadith: 'Man mata wa lam ya'rif imama zamanihi mata maytatan jahiliyyah' (Whoever dies without knowing the Imam of his time, dies the death of ignorance). So, we want to know, how do we do the 'tajdid-e-bay'at' (renewal of allegiance) for our Imam? Very important point. Look, Bhai, and we also address the viewers; we are addressing them. We want to submit for their service that if one tries to understand 'bay'at' (allegiance) in simple words, 'bay'at' means the expression of the heart through the tongue. Indeed, what is in your heart, expressing those things through the tongue. And what does 'bay'at' to the Imam mean? That now we are preparing, we are doing 'bay'at'... Now we are preparing, we are doing 'bay'at'—we are doing 'bay'at' to Imam (a.s.). It means we are preparing ourselves that we will obey him, we will help him in every matter, we will obey him in every matter, we will help him in every matter. Okay, we will serve him, and not just serve like that, but serve with 'ma'rifat' (gnosis). Serve with 'ma'rifat'. And this 'tajdid-e-bay'at' that you mentioned, our viewers also know, but for the sake of remembrance, we want to present this before the viewers: in 'Dua-e-Ahad', we do this 'tajdid-e-bay'at' to the Imam of our time every morning. Regarding which it has been said that this 'Dua-e-Ahad' is emphasized to be recited after the Fajr prayer. So, why is it emphasized? So that every morning after the Fajr prayer, you do 'bay'at' at the hands of the Imam of your time. You renew—'tajdid' means to renew. It means you have to renew the 'bay'at' every morning. In which we say what sentence? What sentence do we present in the service of the Imam (a.s.)? 'Allahumma inni...' (O Allah, I am renewing...). That, O Sustainer, I am renewing, I am renewing my 'bay'at' from the beginning of my day today. I am renewing the 'bay'at' of the Imam (a.s.) from the beginning of my day today, 'wa ma 'ishtu...' and in all the days of my life, I will renew this 'bay'at' by reciting this 'Dua-e-Ahad'. And then we say, ''ahdan' (a firm promise), with a firm promise, with a covenant, we are doing this... With a firm promise, with a covenant, we are renewing this 'bay'at'. 'Wa 'aqdan' (and a firm knot). And then after that, we recite the 'bay'at' that you just mentioned. We tie the 'bay'at' of the Imam (a.s.) around our necks. Then after that, we recite, and then we confirm this that, 'Mawla, I will never turn away from this 'bay'at' and I will never slip.' That is, I will always, always remain firm on this 'bay'at' that I am doing at your hands in your service. And what is the issue with this 'bay'at' of 'abad' (eternity)? The 'bay'at' of 'abad'. Look, the 'bay'at' of the world ends with life. Where life ends, this 'bay'at' ends. But in this 'Dua-e-Ahad', the 'bay'at' we are doing, the 'tajdid' we are doing, this is the 'tajdid' of the 'bay'at' until eternity. If you look at the next phrase, we are also seen confirming it, in which we say to the Imam (a.s.), 'Mawla, even if we die...' We were talking about eternity, we were talking about eternity, that what are we saying? 'Allahumma...' regarding that same 'bay'at' which is until eternity. That, O Sustainer, if death intervenes between me and my Imam, my Mawla's 'zuhur', then what to do? 'Allati ja'alta 'ala 'ibadika...' (Which You have made obligatory upon Your servants). This death You have kept for Your servants. If this intervenes between me and my Imam... If this intervenes between me and my Imam, then what to do? O Sustainer, then take me out of my grave. You are expressing this love, the 'bay'at' you are doing, that 'Mawla, I will present my service in such a way, I will present my 'nusrat' in such a way that take me out of the grave.' Mawla, how to take me out? 'Nashiran kafani' (with my shroud wrapped), that I have wrapped my shroud on my body, wrapped my shroud, and take me out of my grave. And then what are you saying? 'Shahiran sayfi' (with my sword drawn), and in my hand is a drawn sword. And then you say, we say, 'Mujarridan qanati' (and I have raised my spear). That is, in one hand I have a drawn sword, and in the other hand I have a spear. That is, in this state, O my Sustainer, raise me. And then what do we say? 'Mulabbiyan da'wati...' (and when the caller calls, I will say Labbayk, Labbayk, Labbayk). And when the caller, the one who calls, calls out, I will be present in the service of the Imam saying Labbayk, Labbayk, Labbayk. This is the 'bay'at' until eternity. And here, Kazim Bhai, a sentence of a scholar comes to mind. Recently, in the month of Rajab, he passed away. May God grant him Paradise, may He have mercy on him. Regarding this sentence, he used to say that the one who prays for being raised even after death in 'Dua-e-Ahad', he is a believer who recited the dua and the believer... He is a believer who has recited the supplication, and for the believer, the door to his paradise is opened in his grave. Indeed, he is enjoying the blessings of Paradise. Yes, but the spirit of serving the Imam and assisting the Imam is so great that a person would leave Paradise to return to this world for that cause. SubhanAllah! Ahsan Bhai, in light of these verses of Dua-e-Ahad, would you like to provide some further clarification? Certainly, there is a very interesting incident; I request the viewers to listen to it carefully. A man, an elderly man, was in the final stages of his life. He was frail, holding a staff, and had become old. He comes to the presence of the fifth Imam, Hazrat Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), and stands at the door. He has taken the support of his staff. Inside, the Imam (a.s.) is sitting, and his companions are present. What does this man do? He greets everyone from the door in a loud voice. First of all, he offers his greetings to the Imam. The Imam returns the greeting, and then he greets everyone present in the gathering. He receives the response, asks for permission to enter, and then asks the Imam a question. What is the question? Look, he is an old man, reaching the final part of his life, but his question... reaching the final part of his life, but his question is strange and unique. What does he ask? He says, 'Mawla, I love you, and I love those who love you.' And by God, this love I have for you is not for any worldly gain. Will I get any worldly benefit because of loving you? No, it is not for that. It is purely sincere love for you. And then he continues, 'Mawla, I hold enmity towards your enemies, and I hold enmity towards the enemies of those who love you. But this enmity of mine is not because there is any personal problem between me and your enemy. No, the standard of friendship is you, and the standard of enmity is you.' And then he says, 'By God, I consider your lawful as lawful, your forbidden as forbidden, and I am waiting for your government. I am waiting for your government, Mawla. Is there anything for me, or what reward will I get in exchange for this action, for this state of mine? May my life be sacrificed for you.' When he presented this to the Imam, the Imam listened, and then the Imam said, 'Come here, come to me.' So the elderly man, still holding his staff... Come to me, so the elderly man, still holding his staff, reaches the presence of the Imam. And then Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'This very same question was asked by an elderly man to my father, the fourth Imam, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), and the answer my father gave, I am giving you the same answer.' And what was that answer? The answer was that my father said to him, 'If the state you are in, the state you have described, the belief you have stated—that the question is, what should one do to reach this state—if this is your belief: love for the sake of the Ahlulbayt, enmity towards their enemies for the sake of the Ahlulbayt, considering their lawful things as lawful, considering their forbidden things as forbidden, and waiting for their government, that is, waiting for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.)—if you are in this state, with this belief... my father said to that man, if you die in this state, if you die in this state, then you will be brought, you will be presented before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and before the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)...' you will be presented before your Imam of the time, you will be brought into the presence of the Imam of the time. That is, at the time of death, you will see all of them; you will be blessed with their visitation at the time of death. And in that state, what will your condition be? At that time, your heart will be completely at peace. You will feel coolness in your heart. At that time, at the time of death, there will be no hardship for you. You will have a peaceful death. Your heart will be completely cool, your eyes will find coolness, your eyes will find peace. Naturally, when he is witnessing everyone from the Messenger of Allah to his Imam of the time, the fourth Imam, what could be better for the coolness of a person's eyes? He is witnessing these sacred figures. And then you will be welcomed. How will you be welcomed? Even the Kiraman Katibin (the recording angels) will welcome you. And at what time will you be welcomed? The angels will come, the Kiraman Katibin will come, and they will welcome you when your soul reaches here,'—the Imam pointed with his hand to his throat—'when your soul is about to depart, all this will happen to you.' Naturally, for a human, this is the most difficult moment when the soul is about to depart, but at that time, he will be completely at ease. So this will be your state if, before the reappearance... this will be your state if, before the reappearance, before our government comes, your death occurs. Then the Imam says, 'But if you remain alive,'—this is a strange thing—'if you remain alive, then the Imam says, if you remain alive, then Allah will show you such things through which your eyes will find coolness in this world. And because of this waiting, because of this intention, because of this waiting, Allah will place you with us, at our rank on the Day of Judgment.' So, as soon as this elderly man heard this statement of the Imam (a.s.), he could not believe his ears at first. What is he hearing? Is it true that for a person like me, I have performed this action, but in return, I am receiving so many things? So he asked the Imam, 'Mawla, will I really be blessed with all this?' The Imam (a.s.) stated the entire reward for him again, stated it again. And then a piece of the narration is found, a sentence of the narration is found, that the man wept so loudly, he fainted right there. Now he had fainted and fallen there. So when he fainted, he was by the Imam's side. What did the Imam do? The son of Zahra, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), the son of Zahra, passed his blessed hand over his eyes, his... blessed hand over his eyes, wiped his tears, and then wiped his tears. So when the Imam's (a.s.) blessed hand touched his face, he regained consciousness. He regained consciousness again, and after that, what did he do? He requested the Imam, 'Mawla, give me your blessed hand; I want to kiss your hands.' So he took the Imam's hand, kissed it, took the Imam's hand and rubbed it against his chest, placed it on his chest. He rubbed the Imam's hand on his chest, and then he bade farewell to the Imam (a.s.) and walked out of that gathering. As he was going out, after he had gone out, the Imam (a.s.), Imam Baqir (a.s.), addressed the gathering and said, 'If any of you wants to see a person from the people of Paradise, then look at this man, this old man.' A heavenly person left carrying the glad tidings of Paradise. What had he done? Had he really helped the Imam of the time, assisted him, served him? No, his intention was sincere, that if I... and he was waiting for that government, for that Dawlat-e-Karima. Indeed, this is such a great, such an important belief, such a great deed, this waiting for the reappearance, because of which all these rewards are included for a person. And the narrator of this hadith, Hakam ibn Utaybah... and the narrator of this hadith, Hakam ibn Utaybah, says at the end that I have never seen such a gathering in my life. SubhanAllah, there was so much weeping. Yes, meaning we can say that a person will get Paradise when he waits for the Imam, for the Imam of his time. Yes, absolutely. Thank you very much to all of you for having a very important discussion on an important topic, and we hope that our viewers have benefited from this discussion. In the end, I would just like to say that Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) himself said, 'If I had lived in their time, I would have served them all my life, I would have spent my entire life in their service.' And perhaps that is why the Imam said, 'Wait for our reappearance morning and evening.' So we should wait for the Imam's reappearance. In the end, we pray in the court of Allah Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and counts us among his servants. Amen. With this, we take our leave of you. Thank you, Khuda Hafiz, Ya Ali Madad. Viewers, the quiz link will be closed as soon as the timer on your screen ends, and now it is time for Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin. I request you to be ready for the Ziyarat. be ready for the Ziyarat. The names of the winners will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system, Insha Allah. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. chapters.title: Introduction and Quiz Details
chapters.summary: The program introduces the final episode of the Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz and explains the rules for participating in the lucky draw for the Iraq Ziyarat.

chapters.title: The Concept of Waiting for the Imam
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the significance of 'Intezaar' (waiting) for Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), framing it as the highest form of worship.

chapters.title: Defining True Waiting and Its Virtue
chapters.summary: The discussion clarifies that waiting is not passive but involves active effort, comparing it to the patience and hard work parents invest in their children.

chapters.title: The Reward of the Muntazir
chapters.summary: The speakers cite traditions highlighting that one who dies while waiting for the Imam's government is rewarded as if they fought alongside the Prophet.

chapters.title: Virtues of Believing in the Imam of the Time
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the significance of maintaining belief in Imamate and awaiting the reappearance of the Imam during the occultation, citing a Hadith from Imam Zainul Abideen.

chapters.title: Virtues of the Muntazir
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights that those who believe in Imamate and await Imam Mahdi (a.s.) are considered superior to all other generations.

chapters.title: The Status and Certainty of the Muntazir
chapters.summary: The true Shia are those who possess deep gnosis of the Ahlulbayt and maintain unwavering certainty in the Imamate during the occultation.

chapters.title: Virtues and Sincerity of the Expectant
chapters.summary: Those who wait for the Imam are granted a status equivalent to those who fought alongside the Prophet, characterized by absolute sincerity.

chapters.title: The Role of the Muntazir as a Caller
chapters.summary: True Shia are defined by their active role in calling others to the religion of the Ahlulbayt, both openly and secretly.

chapters.title: The Spiritual Depth of Expectation
chapters.summary: Waiting for the Imam is a spiritual state of constant expectation where the believer remains connected to the Divine Proof despite the occultation.

chapters.title: The Duty of Expectation vs. Fixing Time
chapters.summary: The speakers emphasize that believers should focus on personal preparation for the Imam's reappearance rather than debating or attempting to predict the timing, which is solely in Allah's hands.

chapters.title: The Dangers of Haste and Checklists
chapters.summary: Creating checklists of signs and acting with impatience or haste is condemned in the narrations of the Imams, as it leads to disappointment and spiritual peril.

chapters.title: Cultivating a State of Readiness
chapters.summary: True salvation lies in being in a constant state of expectation, viewing the reappearance as near, and focusing on personal worthiness to meet the Imam at any moment.

chapters.title: Avoiding the Prohibition of Time-Fixing
chapters.summary: The speakers clarify that while specific days like Friday or Ramadan are associated with the Imam, one must avoid the error of fixing the time of reappearance, a practice explicitly condemned by the Imams.

chapters.title: The Dangers of Haste and Time-Fixing
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against fixing dates for the Imam's reappearance, explaining that such actions lead to misguidance and disappointment among the believers.

chapters.title: Understanding Signs and Divine Alteration (Bada)
chapters.summary: The lecture clarifies that signs of reappearance are not mandatory or fixed, as Allah retains the power of 'Bada' (divine change) over all events until the final execution.

chapters.title: The Seven Stages of Divine Decree
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines the seven stages of divine action, from Will to Execution, explaining why signs remain subject to change until Allah grants final permission.

chapters.title: The Purpose of Signs and Divine Promise
chapters.summary: The discussion explains that signs are provided to keep believers expectant and motivated, even though the reappearance itself is a promise that does not strictly depend on them.

chapters.title: The Nature of Zuhur and the 313
chapters.summary: The reappearance of the Imam is a divine promise not dependent on specific conditions, and the 313 companions will be gathered by Allah when the time is right.

chapters.title: Zuhur Compared to the Sun
chapters.summary: The Imam's reappearance is likened to the sun, signifying that it will be an undeniable, manifest event that leaves no room for doubt.

chapters.title: Preparation and Sincerity in Waiting
chapters.summary: A true waiter (muntazir) prepares by cultivating sincere intentions to help the Imam, which can earn the reward of action even if the opportunity does not arise.

chapters.title: Renewal of Allegiance (Tajdid-e-Bay'at)
chapters.summary: Reciting Dua-e-Ahad after Fajr serves as a daily renewal of one's covenant and allegiance to the Imam, extending beyond this life into eternity.

chapters.title: The Essence of Dua-e-Ahad
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the profound commitment in Dua-e-Ahad, where a believer expresses a readiness to be resurrected to serve the Imam.

chapters.title: The Reward of Sincere Waiting
chapters.summary: An elderly man visits Imam Baqir (a.s.) to confirm the spiritual status and rewards of those who sincerely love, obey, and await the Imam's reappearance.

chapters.title: Divine Glad Tidings for the Awaiter
chapters.summary: The Imam explains that those who maintain true faith and await the Imam will be blessed with the presence of the Ahlulbayt at the time of death.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by emphasizing the importance of waiting for the Imam and transitions into the recitation of Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin.

chapters.title: Recitation of Ziyarat-e-Aal-e-Yasin
chapters.summary: The speaker recites the Ziyarat-e-Aal-e-Yasin, invoking peace upon Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and affirming the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Conclusion of Mega Quiz 2025
chapters.summary: The final episode of the Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz concludes with instructions for participants and an announcement of the lucky draw winners.

title: Roza Muhaafiz Hai | Fasting is a Protection | Kalaam e Noor # 20
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of fasting in Islam, highlighting the Prophetic tradition that describes it as a protective shield. It emphasizes how the act of fasting serves as a barrier against the consequences of the Hellfire. The discourse encourages believers to view fasting not just as an obligation, but as a vital tool for spiritual preservation and salvation.
content:

title: Is the Hadith of "Death of Ignorance" not authentic? - Part 1 | Resp. Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi
excerpt: This lecture examines the authenticity and theological significance of the hadith stating that one who dies without recognizing the Imam of their time dies a death of ignorance. Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi provides an analysis of the hadith's chain of narration, confirming its reliability through both Shia and Sunni scholarly perspectives. The discussion addresses common criticisms and misconceptions, emphasizing the central role of Wilayah as a foundational pillar of the Islamic faith.
content:
So the question is about the prophetic hadith, the very famous report where the Holy Prophet has said, 'Man mata la ya'rifu imama zamanihi mata maytatan jahiliyyah' (Whoever dies not recognizing the Imam of his time, dies a death of ignorance), meaning as though he died in the pre-Islamic pagan era, in the era known as the Jahiliyyah. Now, there are two claims made here. The first is that the hadith is not authentic, and the second is that the Imams have never even said anything remotely close to that, right? The Imams would never say that believing in us or recognizing us is a condition of salvation. So let's address the first part here. The hadith is accepted by both Shia and Sunni scholars. That's important to note. Not many ahadith would tick this box, to be unanimously accepted, to have consensus among all Muslims as to the authenticity of the hadith. So, for example, you know, in Sunni sources, which are irrelevant to our discussion, but again, it's important to know that they've mentioned it and they acknowledge the authenticity of the hadith. You have the hadith being reported in Sunan al-Bayhaqi, Sahih Muslim, Musnad Abi Dawud, Sahih Ibn Hibban, Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, as well as other sources like al-Mu'jam al-Kabir and others. And as I said, it is important to note that while they have misrepresented the meaning of the hadith to be about giving an oath of allegiance to the Caliph, whoever that happens to be, that has created a problem for the Sunni side because they have struggled to reconcile between the obvious religious nature of the oath and their dysfunctional political framework. And so, they have reached the point where you have to give an oath of allegiance to whoever happens to be in charge, whoever is sitting on that throne. So that has created a problem for them. But despite all that, they do not deny the hadith itself. So the problem is in the interpretation of the hadith, not in its authenticity and credibility. As for Shia sources, the hadith's authenticity is undeniable, which proves beyond doubt that the claim about the report's lack of credibility is a blatant lie. And it is a testament to his lack of credibility, this person making this claim. If you do not want to call him an imposter, a liar, a deceiver, then at the very least, he is ignorant of the most obvious truths. Now, let us see why that is. As I said, the hadith is mentioned in Shia sources by the highest authorities and the most reliable and credible sources. I will mention a couple of those. The first is Sheikh al-Saduq ibn Babawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, in his book Kamal al-Din or Ikmal al-Din wa Itmam al-Ni'mah. He reports this version of the hadith, and there are multiple versions by the way, which only go to reinforce the credibility of it, meaning that the hadith is mentioned by Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) in one case, and then it is mentioned by Imam al-Rida (a.s.), and it is mentioned by Imam al-Baqir (a.s.). And so you have a multiplicity of chains all leading back to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Let me read the actual text here. So, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (r.a.) narrated to us, saying: Abu Ali ibn Hammam narrated to me, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri, may Allah sanctify his soul—meaning the second Na'ib (deputy) of the Imam, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri. He was the second emissary to Imam al-Zaman (a.s.), an incredibly reliable individual, it goes without saying. He said: I heard my father, meaning Uthman ibn Sa'id, the first emissary, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (a.s.) was asked. So Uthman ibn Sa'id is saying that I was in the presence of Imam al-Askari (a.s.) when he was asked this question. What was the question? About the report that has been narrated from his forefathers (a.s.). The hadith is this: 'The earth will not be devoid of a Hujjah (proof) of Allah over His creation until the Day of Judgment.' That the earth, the world, will not be devoid of a Hujjah, a proof of Allah, a representative of Allah, upon the creation, until the Day of Judgment. 'And whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time has died a death of ignorance.' The second part of the hadith is the one that we are discussing, that whoever dies not recognizing the Imam of his time has died a death of ignorance. So the Imam (a.s.) responded: 'This is true, just as daylight is true.' In other words, it is as true as anything can be recognized as such. This is true, just as daylight is true. Absolutely, yes, this is true. So it was said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, who is the Hujjah and the Imam after you?' He said, 'My son, Muhammad, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance and may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.' He pointed to his son, the Imam of the time, Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.), and he said he is the Hujjah and the Imam after me. He is the Imam and Hujjah after me. Then the Imam reiterates this point: 'Whoever dies without recognizing him has died a death of ignorance.' Then the Imam goes on to say that he will go into occultation, and those who are ignorant will be lost and perplexed, and the falsifiers will perish therein. And the rest of the hadith is irrelevant to our discussion. But the point is, this hadith is authentic and it mentions this portion that is in question. That is mentioned in Kamal al-Din as I mentioned; it is mentioned in Kifayat al-Athar, it is mentioned in Wasa'il al-Shia by al-Hurr al-'Amili, as well as other sources. Another version of the hadith which I want to mention as well is reported by Ibn Hamzah al-Tusi in his book al-Thaqib fi al-Manaqib. So let me read this actual text as well. From Muhammad ibn al-Ala al-Jurjani, who said: 'I performed Hajj and I met Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) while I was on the pilgrimage, circumambulating the House (Kaaba). I said to him, may I be ransomed for you, this hadith has been reported from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.): Whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time has died a death of ignorance. This hadith that has been attributed to the Holy Prophet, is it true that the Prophet said that whoever dies not recognizing the Imam of his time has died a death of ignorance?' He said, 'Yes.' The Imam, al-Rida (a.s.), said: 'Yes, it is true. My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), who reported from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' So just notice how this chain, the Imam (a.s.), is emphasizing and reiterating the fact that this hadith is authentic. Knowing that there are going to be deniers, knowing that there are going to be doubters, the Imam is saying this hadith is true. I heard it from my father who heard it from his father, going all the way back to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), who said: 'Whoever dies not knowing the Imam of his time has died a death of ignorance.' I said to him, this man al-Jurjani, then said to the Imam, 'May I be ransomed for you, and who is one who dies a death of ignorance?' What does that mean to die a death of ignorance? In case somebody tries to misrepresent the meaning of the hadith. In case somebody comes along and says, 'ignorance' means he does not know, but he is excused for not knowing, the Imam responded: 'He dies a death of polytheism, a death of disbelief.' We seek refuge in Allah. However, having mentioned these two ahadith, I want to mention a third one that was selected by al-Kulayni (r.a.) for his al-Kafi. This hadith, I chose it to be showcased because the chain in this hadith is so clear and unambiguous. It will destroy the argument that is made by this guy. So, this is in al-Kafi, volume number two, page number 19. Muhammad ibn Yahya—I want to mention the chain and then talk about it later—from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Sari, Abu al-Yasa, who said: 'I said to Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) (a.s.).' This person, Isa ibn al-Sari, says to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). So now, we have a hadith from Imam al-Hasan al-Askari, a hadith from Imam al-Rida, and now a hadith from the sixth Imam. He said, 'I told him, inform me of the pillars of Islam.' Look at how important this hadith is. He says, 'I told him, tell me the pillars of Islam, the pillars of the religion that no one is allowed to not believe in them.' In other words, these are the foundational tenets of the faith. These are the principles of the faith that no one can be excused for not believing in them. What are they? 'The pillars that no one is allowed to be negligent in knowing any of them, for whoever is negligent in knowing any of them, his religion is corrupted.' He then elaborates. He says, the foundations that are so critical that if anyone does not believe in them, their religion is corrupted. Their religion is invalidated. 'And Allah will not accept his actions' without these pillars, without these beliefs. 'And whoever knows them and acts upon them, his religion is sound for him.' And just to emphasize this point further, he says, whoever knows them and acts upon them, Allah will accept his religion from him, his religion will be accepted. 'His religion is sound for him and his deeds are accepted from him.' What are these pillars? What are these absolute fundamentals? Look at what the Imam says. He said: 'The testimony that there is no god but Allah.' The testimony that there is no god other than Allah. Number one. 'And belief that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah' (s.a.w.a.). Number two. 'And acknowledging what he brought from Allah.' 'And the right in wealth, which is Zakat,' to give in the way of Allah (s.w.t.). This is number three. 'And the Wilayah (authority) which Allah the Almighty has commanded, the Wilayah of the family of Muhammad.' May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. 'And the authority and the allegiance that Allah has commanded us to have. To whom? To the family of Muhammad, to the family of the Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'I said to him, is there any level of Wilayah that is superior to another, which is known for those who adhere to it?' The Imam responded with this verse in the Quran. He said, 'Yes, Allah the Almighty says: O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you,' in Surah al-Nisa. And the Messenger of Allah said: 'Whoever dies without knowing his Imam has died a death of ignorance.' The Imam then concluded by saying: 'And the world will not exist except with an Imam. And whoever dies, once again, the Imam doubles down, whoever dies not knowing his Imam has died a death of ignorance.' Now, what is interesting here is that the person making this claim about this hadith not being authentic, suddenly pivots to a subject that is completely irrelevant. He goes off on a tangent and mentions Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami al-Razi and talks about how this person was a prolific hadith narrator and how he was known as a liar and a ghali (extremist) and he was thrown out of the city of Qom by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari and so on and so forth and how he invented and concocted all of these ahadith. This is a side note which has no relevance to our discussion. I will have something to say about this inshallah in a different question. However, as far as this hadith is concerned, why do you even mention him? Because remember these ahadith that I shared with you, Sahl ibn Ziyad is not mentioned there. So what's the point here? Why do you even talk about this person? Even though I have things to share about him, and I am of the opinion that you can't so easily dismiss this individual as a liar, as a fabricator, right? But we'll leave that for another discussion. For now, why even talk about him? Because you are confusing the audience. You're making them think that this hadith of 'whoever dies not knowing the Imam of his time' has been narrated by Sahl ibn Ziyad, which is not the case, right? So, let's actually talk about this particular hadith which I mentioned has been reported in al-Kafi, right? No one who knows anything about Rijal and Isnad will cast any doubt on this hadith's authenticity. Why? Let's talk about the narrators of this hadith one by one. The first one was Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar, al-mukanna bi-Abi Ja'far al-Ash'ari al-Qummi. He was among the mashayikh of al-Kulayni, radhiallahu ta'ala 'anhu, and all scholars of Rijal have classified him as thiqah. He is reliable, he is trustworthy. That's the first one, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar. The second one is Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Ash'ari. He was a companion of Imam al-Rida (a.s.), Imam al-Jawad (a.s.), and Imam al-Hadi (a.s.). So three Imams, and not only that, but Shaykh al-Tusi says, 'He is the shaykh of the Qummiyin, their leader, and their faqih.' So he wasn't just a companion, he was also a faqih, and he was the leader of the Qummiyin. That's Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa. The third narrator of the hadith is Safwan, Safwan ibn Yahya al-Bajali. He was also a companion of Imam al-Rida and Imam al-Jawad (a.s.), but it wasn't just that, he was also one of the representatives of these two Imams, who was so close to them that Imam al-Jawad (a.s.) praised him in a manner that is absolutely incredible. Imam al-Jawad, when Safwan ibn Yahya al-Bajali passed away, he said in a hadith, 'Radhiallahu 'anhuma.' May Allah be pleased with them, meaning Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Sinan, another of the companions of Imam al-Jawad. The Imam said, 'May Allah be pleased with them, for I am pleased with them. They never disobeyed me.' Allahu Akbar. So the third narrator of this hadith is a person who's been praised by Imam al-Jawad as someone who never disobeyed him. We come to the fourth individual in this chain, who is 'Isa ibn al-Sari, who was also given the kunya of Abu al-Yasa'. He was among the companions of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), and scholars of Rijal also classify him as thiqah, meaning reliable. So, the entire chain of this particular hadith is composed of thiqat, bila munaza'. Thiqat, reliable individuals whose reliability and whose trustworthiness is not subject to any kind of debate. It's unanimous, everybody accepts it. And therein lies the problem. with these individuals who make claims as this person does about this hadith not being authentic. You see, he slaps a doctor title before his name, throws around some names, and obviously there's going to be people who fall for that deception and believe everything he says, oh because he's a doctor, because he must know what he's talking about, right? You have a degree in Arabic grammar or whatever it may be, just stick to that. That's my advice to you. The hadith says, 'Al-mar'u makhbu'un tahta lisanihi' (A person is hidden underneath his tongue). The moment an illiterate person speaks, they expose their ignorance. They expose the fact that they're illiterate. So be quiet for your own sake. For you to come out and make this bold claim that this hadith does not have an authentic chain shows how ignorant and foolish you are. He then goes on to say that the Imams never made themselves a condition of salvation. Rather, he says, all they said was that we are preservers of the sunnah. We can help explain the Quran. So basically, they were preservers of hadith, they were simply reporters. They were like journalists who report a hadith from one person to another, and they understood a little bit of Arabic, so they could explain the Quran. This and again, you know, I've said this before, I'll say it again. This is not Shia belief. You can call yourself an Ismaili if you want, you can call yourself a Sunni if you want, you can call yourself a Bahai if you want. You're not a Shia if you say this. The entire Shia faith is predicated on indisputable statements and facts, things like 'Allahumma wali man walahu wa 'adi man 'adahu wansur man nasarahu wakhdhul man khadhalahu.' To suggest that the Imams of the Ahlulbayt were normal people, they were scholars, they were good people, they were individuals who reported ahadith, they were teachers in the hawza, right? Belies the entire belief system in tashayyu. So you're not a Shia. Just call yourself whatever you are. Don't claim that you're a Shia and then spout these false beliefs that have been imported from the Sunni faith or whatever other religion that you happen to be influenced by. And that's the problem with these people. They're bending over backwards to impose their own neo-Salafi views on tashayyu, on Islam, right? And in doing so, they'll misrepresent the Quran and hadith and disfigure the texts beyond recognition. However, we've already established the fact that he's lying here by saying that there is no authentic chain for this hadith. He is lying. There's no question about it. I mentioned all of the chain in one particular hadith which does the job, right? He's a liar. The authenticity of this hadith and dozens like it cannot be questioned as we've demonstrated. And all of this highlights the central position of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) alongside the Quran, right? This is beyond question and that alone is enough to discredit these imposters and their entire agenda without the need to probe their other extremist views and deviant beliefs. What's worse, and I'll just mention this last point, is that when he's asked which qualified scholars follow the approach that he's advocating for, he mentions a few obscure names, individuals who are either on the extreme fringe or completely unknown within the hawza circles, and a couple who have been completely discredited and debunked for their heretical and deviant views and beliefs. All of which shows that you're either dealing with someone who's completely ignorant or lacks the most basic qualifications to address these issues and certainly cannot take up any position of religious guidance or teaching of any kind.

title: EP10 | Madine Mein Imam Ali (a.s.) Ke Qatl Ki Saazish | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture details a historical account of a conspiracy to assassinate Imam Ali (a.s.) during his time in Medina. It describes how a ruler and his advisor plotted to have Khalid ibn al-Walid kill the Imam during prayer. The plot was thwarted when the ruler changed his mind at the last moment, leading to a confrontation where Imam Ali (a.s.) demonstrated his strength and divine protection.
content:
The Mawla (a.s.) said, 'So, are you going to kill me?' He said, 'By God, yes, if he had not stopped me before finishing the Salam, I would have certainly killed you.' As we saw in the sixth episode of this series, after becoming the ruler, the Hakim of the time called his advisor and consulted him. The Hakim asked, 'Did you see how Ali argued with us today? By God, if he does this one more time, he will prove our affair, i.e., the Caliphate, to be false. What is your opinion?' 'My opinion is that you should give the order for his killing.' My opinion is that you should give the order for his killing. Upon this, the Hakim asked, 'But who can kill him?' The advisor said, 'Khalid ibn al-Walid.' Here, it is also important to know who Khalid ibn al-Walid was. He became a Muslim after the Conquest of Mecca, meaning he had only been in Islam for 3 years. People, in their zeal of devotion, call him 'Saifullah' (The Sword of Allah). But this sword did not even have the discernment of who should be killed. The famous historian Ibn Athir, citing Bukhari, writes that once Khalid ibn al-Walid ordered his soldiers to kill the prisoners of Banu Jadhimah. Now, do it. The Hakim said, 'Go to the mosque.' Now, do it. The Hakim said, 'Go to the mosque and stand near him. When I am about to finish the prayer, you stand up and strike his neck.' Asma bint Umays heard this conversation and said to her maid, 'Go to the house of Ali and Fatimah (a.s.), give them my Salam, and recite this verse of the Quran: 'Indeed, the chiefs of the tribe are consulting among themselves to kill you, so leave; indeed, I am for you among the sincere advisors.' He said, 'Tell her that Allah will stand between them and their intention.' He entered and began to pray. Khalid came to him with his sword. During the prayer, the Hakim regretted his decision and began to think that this could lead to a very big Fitna (strife) because he knew the power of Ali (a.s.). People began to think that perhaps the Hakim had forgotten the Tashahhud and Salam, which is why he was taking so long to finish the prayer. And in the state of prayer, he turned towards Khalid and said, 'Khalid, do not act upon what I ordered you.' The Mawla (a.s.) asked Khalid, 'What were you ordered to do?' He said, 'The Mawla (a.s.) said, 'So, are you going to kill me?' He said, 'By God, yes, if he had not stopped me before finishing the Salam, I would have certainly killed you.' The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) grabbed Khalid and threw him to the ground. The advisor said to the Hakim, 'By the Lord of the Kaaba, Ali will kill Khalid.' People gathered, and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) [was taken] to the graveyard. Before this, the oppressed Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin... Before this, may Allah hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), for the sake of the oppression (mazlumiyat) of Ameer-ul-Momineen (a.s.), so that the enemies of the Ahlulbayt may reach their deserved end. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Har Rozedaar Par Imam-e-Hasan (a.s.) Ka Ehsaan | Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz 2022
excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual significance of the Iftar supplication attributed to Imam Hasan (a.s.). It emphasizes that the blessings of sustenance and fasting are manifestations of the grace of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). The speaker encourages believers to prioritize praying for the reappearance of the Imam during the moment of Iftar when prayers are accepted by Allah.
content:
The supplication taught by Imam Hasan (a.s.), which even our children are familiar with, is a supplication we benefit from during the month of Ramadan. Not just us, but all the people of the earth seek forgiveness for their sins through it. The supplication at the time of Iftar reached us through Imam Hasan (a.s.) himself. The words of the tradition are such that: 'Indeed, for every fasting person at the time of Iftar, Allah has a prayer that is accepted.' When a fasting person takes their first morsel of Iftar, they should say, 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah). And what could be better than starting our Iftar in the name of Allah, remembering the Waliy (Imam), and praying for his reappearance? Indeed, the blessings and the food we are eating, the Iftar we are having, is all due to the blessings and grace of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). It is a gift from his bounty. All the sustenance reaching us is due to him. So, as you said, since every fasting person has an accepted prayer, why shouldn't one pray for his reappearance? One should pray for the reappearance, and after that, one may ask for their own needs. But first and foremost, at the time of Iftar, pray for the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.).

title: Habeeb -e- Khuda (s.a.w.a.) Ka Noor | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the metaphysical concept of the 'Noor' (light) of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) as the foundational essence of all existence. He explains that the universe was created for the sake of the Prophet and that his light serves as the source of all being. The lecture highlights the authority granted to the Prophet by Allah to distribute this light and notes the shared light between the Prophet and Imam Ali (a.s.), supported by historical scholarly works.
content:
Fana-fil-Ishq (annihilated in love), O Help! The passion of affection whose light has illuminated the gathering of existence. The essence of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is such that the universe was created for his sake. 'Lawlaaka' (Had you not been), I would not have created the universe. The entire universe was created for his sake, and the entire universe exists because of his existence. When his light is present, things exist; and if he wishes to withdraw his light, man would become 'ma'dum' (non-existent). He wouldn't die, he would become non-existent. There are two concepts: one is 'Wujud' (existence) and the other is 'Adam' (non-existence). When the light of existence is received, a thing exists, and when this light is withdrawn... in English, existence is called 'existence' and non-existence is called 'non-existence'. The first thing Allah created was the light of the Prophet. The first thing Allah created was your light, O Prophet. And because of this light, all things came into existence. This light of existence was given to things by the Prophet. So, all these galaxies you see, all the universe you see, is because of the Prophet's light. It is not just one or two things; look at the entire realm of possibility. The verse is a bit difficult, but I will recite it: 'Fana-fil-Ishq, O Help! The passion of affection whose light has illuminated the gathering of existence.' The light by which the entire universe came into existence. But Allah created this light, and Allah made the Prophet the owner of this light. He said, 'Hadha 'ata'una' (This is our gift). This is a verse of the Quran. You see, 'Hadha 'ata'una' means this is our gift, we have given this to you. Now, give it to whom you wish, and withhold it from whom you wish. You have full authority. Give it to whom you wish, and withhold it from whom you wish; you have full authority. There is no accounting for this. If anything exists, it should thank the Prophet. This is the light, and then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ali is from one light.' And then Allah divided this light into two parts, and the chain of division continued. It is a very strange and profound discussion that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have stated. Interestingly, do not think this is only in Shia books. Janab Mir Ahmad Husain Hindi (R.A.) wrote two volumes specifically on the 'Hadith-e-Noor'. And as I submitted to you, these are not small volumes; they are huge books. When summarized in Arabic, they became about 15-20 volumes, just on the Hadith-e-Noor. And he did not bring any Shia narrators in this Hadith-e-Noor; that is his brilliance. So, this is the light of the Prophet, this is the light of Ameer-ul-Momineen. If a person understands this greatness, this majesty... now look at the address, what is Allah saying to the Prophet? Now you have understood the essence of the Prophet. In other words, I will tell you in one line, I won't take much time: the first thing Allah created is... The first thing Allah created is the essence (mahiyat), meaning the essence of the Prophet. The Lord is the Creator.

title: Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Ziyaarat - Har Momin Ka Fareeza [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual obligation of performing the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) for every believer who acknowledges the Imamate. Drawing from the traditions of Imam al-Baqir and Imam Rida, the speaker explains that visiting the graves of the Imams is a way to fulfill the covenant made with them. The talk concludes with a prayer for the grace and opportunity to visit Karbala, highlighting the importance of sincere intention in achieving this spiritual goal.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Muhammad ibn Muslim narrates that Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) said: 'Order our Shias to visit the grave of Husayn (a.s.), for visiting it is obligatory upon every believer who acknowledges the Imamate of Husayn (a.s.) from Allah azza-wa-jalla.' And Imam Rida (a.s.) says, 'Every Imam has a covenant on the necks of his followers and Shias, and the best way to fulfill this covenant and keep the promise made to them is to visit their blessed graves. So, whoever goes to visit them out of a longing to meet them and confirms that desire by visiting, all the Imams (a.s.) will intercede for him on the Day of Judgment.' The point to ponder in these two hadiths is that the Ziyarat of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and the other Imams (a.s.) is the duty of every believer who considers themselves a follower of the creed of the Imamate of the Family of Muhammad (a.s.). Therefore, keep striving as much as possible for this Ziyarat. It is certain that going to Karbala requires means and capacity, and the grace of the Creator must be included, but this grace is based on our intention. Going to Karbala is a matter of destiny, but the unfortunate one is he who did not even intend it. Our prayer in the court of the Lord of the Worlds is that He grants us the grace to fulfill the promise and covenant made to our Imam through the Ziyarat of the Oppressed of Karbala, and removes all obstacles in the path of this Ziyarat. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This lecture addresses the significance and continuity of Azadari for Imam Husain (a.s.) as requested by Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). It highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) guarantee that mourning for the Ahlulbayt would be a perpetual tradition maintained by the Ummah across generations. The speaker emphasizes that the annual practice of mourning is not merely a ritual but a fulfillment of a divine promise that transcends time.
content:
O father, who will mourn for my child? Who will establish the Azadari (mourning) for my child? Establishing this Azadari was the desire of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O my daughter Fatima, the women of my Ummah will mourn for the women of my Ahlulbayt, and the men of my Ummah will mourn for the men of my Ahlulbayt.' And then, we are asked every year, 'Why do you mourn every year? The event happened 1400 years ago, it is over. How long will you mourn?' The answer was given by the Prophet. The Prophet took the guarantee. The Prophet said, 'And those (women) who will mourn for the women, and the men who will mourn for the men, they will renew this mourning (tajdid). They will keep doing it, generation after generation. It will remain in every era. Azadari will continue in every era. Fi kulli sanah (In every year), it will happen. This Azadari will continue every year.' This... This is not in our hands; this is the Prophet's guarantee, based on which we are performing Azadari.
