title: Majlis 5 | Dosti (Friendship) | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 2023 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound significance of friendship, gentleness, and faith within the context of Islamic teachings and the tragedy of Karbala. It emphasizes that true belief is rooted in the mercy of the Prophet and the guidance of the Imams, rather than worldly power. The discourse highlights the importance of cultivating kindness in family dynamics and concludes with a poignant reflection on the final moments of Imam Husayn and the enduring lessons of his sacrifice.
content:
[music] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim [music] Ya Hawala Wala Wa Huwa [praise] Om Amawat Waqt Kal Maula Hussain Om Amawat Waqt Kal Maula Hussain [music] These pass by like clouds, so take as much advantage of this opportunity as you can. Do as much work as you can on this, because this thing will not come again. Once it is gone, it is gone. What is this world? It is water. And it passes very quickly, that is why whatever is present, one must cover it. What should a person's personality be like? And the things through which he attains closeness to Allah, through which he becomes near to Allah, and through which his afterlife is built, one should strive for them. But what is the most important thing? It is that a person's faith (aqeedah) must be correct, his beliefs must be correct, and after that, the deeds. These two things are very important; after that, the other particulars come later. But these two things are very important. If these are not there, then there is nothing. And similarly, there is one thing in the Holy Quran that is emphasized a lot, and there are many traditions about it: that there should be softness in a person's temperament. Softness, which in Arabic is called 'Layyin', and 'Layyin' is called 'Qatl'—to tear something. To tear something, like everyone says 'half'—so to tear something, 'Khair', in which relationships are torn, in which kinship is torn. Islam emphasizes this a lot. Now look at a few verses and traditions that are present today; we will cover them, Insha'Allah. If Allah is there, then in Surah Al-Imran, verse 159, Allah says: 'It is from the mercy of Allah upon you that you are soft with them.' This is Allah's mercy upon you, O Prophet, that you are so soft with them. If your temperament were harsh in front of them, they would change their ways. They would change their ways, and people used to come to the Prophet, and such people with such temperaments used to come that there was no limit to it. If you just read history, you would be surprised at how he tolerated them. And then look at the next sentence: 'Fafu anhum'—O Prophet, forgive them. You forgive them. However, the Prophet used to seek forgiveness when people came and said... People used to come and say, which is the verse in Surah An-Nisa, that when they come to the Prophet and then seek a prayer of forgiveness from the Prophet, 'O our Lord, forgive us.' If they did that, 'Wastaghfara lahumur-Rasulu la-wajadullaha Tawwaban Rahima'—then they would find Allah as the Acceptor of repentance, the Most Merciful. But the condition is that they come to the Prophet and say we made a mistake. But they would not come. Even after consulting, once the decision is made, then trust in Allah. 'Innallaha yuhibbul-mutawakkilin'—Allah loves those who trust in Him. Those who trust in Allah's power, Allah loves them. These are the verses of Surah An-Nisa and Surah Al-Imran. And after that, in Surah [__], it is mentioned: 'Washaawirhum fil-amr'—look, who is being addressed? The Prophet is being addressed. You think, look, we are speaking, you are listening, but just think a little, who is the Prophet? The Prophet is the one for whose sake the universe was created. The universe was created [based on the hadith] 'Lawlaaka lamaa khalaqtul aflaak'—if it were not for you, I would not have created the universe. The entire universe was created because of his existence and his essence. When his light (Noor) is present, things exist, and if he were to withdraw his light, existence would vanish. When the light of existence is present, things exist, and when this light is withdrawn, existence—what they call 'existence'—ceases. Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The first thing Allah created was the light of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and based on this light, everything... It is your light, and based on this light, everything came into existence. Whatever was given to things, it was given by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). So, all these galaxies you see, all the universe you see, is because of the Prophet's light. SubhanAllah, SubhanAllah, SubhanAllah. Now, give this to whomever you wish, and withhold it from whomever you wish; you have full authority. There is no accounting for this. If anything exists, it should be grateful to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Interestingly, Ameer al-Mu'mineen (a.s.) actually wrote two volumes on the Hadith al-Noor. And as I mentioned, these are not small volumes, but massive books. When summarized in Arabic, they became about 15-20 volumes, just on the Hadith al-Noor. And he did not bring any weak narrations in this Hadith al-Noor. This is the light of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the light of Ameer al-Mu'mineen (a.s.). So, this is the light of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the light of Ameer al-Mu'mineen (a.s.). If a person understands this greatness, this majesty... look at what Allah is saying to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). This premise I have stated—look, they have no status. Yet, they were so arrogant. Our teacher used to say—may Allah have mercy on him—that when the soul of Pharaoh was inside his body, he used to say, 'I am your Lord, the Most High.' If his soul had been outside his body, who knows what he would have said? When the soul is outside the body, one gains tremendous power. I will explain this premise to you in just one line, as you get tired very quickly. Allah has entrusted honor and disgrace to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). 'O Messenger, now that it has been given to you, give honor to whom you wish, and give disgrace to whom you wish.' Authority is in your hands. 'Khair' here does not mean 'goodness'; 'Khair' means authority, choice, freedom. You can do whatever you wish. 'Kulla shayin qadeer'—you have power over all things. You are the master of all that is known; you can do anything. There is no problem for you. For Allah, there is no problem with anyone. If we could just understand these points, our lives would change. If one understands that Allah can do anything, a king of the Muslims once wrote a letter saying, 'All bow before me...' Write a letter to Sajjad (a.s.) and whatever answer he gives, you give the same. Otherwise, I will destroy you.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) wrote an answer to him: 'For Allah, there is a Law, a Tablet (Lawh). I am in that state where Allah looks 360 times every single moment. Allah looks at it every moment, and in every moment, He makes a pauper rich, a rich man a pauper, a king a slave, and a slave a king.' SubhanAllah, SubhanAllah. Upon seeing this, he immediately said, 'He has no status to write an answer; this is better.' They used to just lie around in corners. They didn't know anything; they just had power. Power can come to anyone. In real Islam, power has no value. This fake Islam that is prevalent today, this is wrong. We are with whoever becomes dominant, whoever wins, whoever has the majority—that is the slogan of today's Islam. Is this written in the books? The Islam that you read in the 'Ziyarat al-Kabira', that is Islam. The Islam you read in the 'Sahifa Sajjadiyya', that is Islam. The Islam you read in the 'Nahj al-Balagha', that is Islam. That is the religion you read in 'Al-Kafi'. That is the religion. That is why the words of the Imams are light; your words are light. The more one is familiar with them, the more their existence will be illuminated, and the further one is, the darker their existence will be. Therefore, keep reading the Hadith as much as possible. Anyway, the topic was the position of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). You have understood the position of the Messenger. Now, let's return to the topic. Allah says in the Quran regarding this same Messenger: 'And lower your wing to the believers.' Meaning, be completely humble before the believers. The Quran mentions lowering the wing three times. Standing in respect for your parents—think, should one stand or not? 'I am a king.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not commit any sin. I am a king.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did not commit any sin, but for a moment, he thought about standing in their respect. 'Lower your wings'—meaning, lower your shoulders. This is mentioned twice to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). 'Lower your wings to the believers who believe in you and believe in your Ahlulbayt; be completely humble before them.' Allahu Akbar. But Allah loves the believers so much that He commands the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—listen to this—'And those who follow you, those who follow Islam and also follow you, lower your wings before them.' This is a verse from Surah Al-Furqan, verse number 63. 'The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth with humility.' As has been the recurring topic in these five consecutive gatherings, the personality we should possess—the personality that should be useful in our family, our business, our jobs, and our society—must be effective everywhere. So, when we are at home, it starts from home; charity begins at home. With gentleness, with children, with protection, there should be friendship with children, friendship with the wife, friendship with brothers and sisters—friendship with everyone. What does friendship mean? Friendship is that which... how are two friends? No, our boy is sitting in front, that is why I am saying this, not saying it secretly. You will have to study, whether you have the capacity or not—no, if she says later, 'I don't want to do science,' okay, give her the freedom. Whatever she likes... Give her the freedom. Whatever she likes, there should be such good relations that she can come forward and say, 'Dad, I don't want to do science,' and 'Son, I won't become a doctor.' 'No, I don't want to be a doctor.' You won't force them at gunpoint. Oh, talk freely, talk absolutely freely. This freedom is a very important thing; it is very, very important. Oh, there is so much blessing in friendship. And the rude behavior, like some people enter the house and it feels like Hitler has arrived; everyone gets scared. Someone runs here, someone runs there. It is a curse, a curse. This spreads misery in the house. When a person has such a temperament, then in the house, see, children do exactly what they see their parents doing. Children never do what parents tell them to do. They do what they see their parents doing. When they see that our father is like this, our mother is like this, then they follow this. They follow this. So if they see that it is our father's habit, our mother's habit, our brother's habit, our sister's habit, then they do the same. That is why the atmosphere of the house—actually, we are talking about our personal matters here, what is our religion? Otherwise, we have seen some religious families where the father talks to the son, the son talks to the father, with such gentleness, talking so slowly. They are very religious, the whole family. A very great scholar passed away a few days ago, so we were at their house for the last year, both of us were there. We were at their house, and their... that scholar's son, their phone had come. Their phone had come. This became our color. The worst voice is the braying of a donkey; no one likes the voice of a donkey. Have you heard in any ghazal, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave the example of birds, the nightingale, or whatever it is? We know [praise] it sounds good. So, the Quran says that friendship is half of life. It is half of life. If a person maintains gentleness, 50% of their life becomes successful. Just by being gentle with people. And 'rifq' means friendship, that is, gentleness. What is the opposite of that? 'Rifq'... What is the opposite of that? 'Rifq'... Naini was a very great scholar. As many great Maraja of the time were, as many contemporaries as there were, his father's name was Sabit. His father's name was Sabit, and his grandfather's name was Harmala. This was the one who came to burn the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). That is why the grandfather did that. And he, and Farsi, his grandfather's name was... his father's name was Bakri, and son, a powerful Hadith reaches the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and he says that 'Inna fir-rifq'—in gentleness, in friendship, there is increase. In gentleness, in friendship, there is increase. That is, Allah will give more sustenance and blessings. And the one whom Allah deprives of this gentleness, He deprives him of all goodness. He deprives him; he is not among those whom Allah has mercy upon. He is deprived. He is the one who is... Allahu Akbar. If a person speaks with gentleness, then whatever his half is, whatever his goal is, he will achieve it. Then, the smile—you have a good smile. In almost every gathering, I say this point: the teachings of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) remain, and others take the benefit. The teachings of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) remain, and others take the benefit. Why? Because we are still stuck in 'this is one, two, four, five.' And when a debate comes, we argue a lot: 'Is the Hadith authentic or not? Is it wrong? Is it weak?' They keep pressing from there, they are 'Mustafid,' and they were brought only to compete with the Imam. So that a man who is at least a scholar, and all the debates are recorded, the 'Ihtijajat-e-Tabarsi' is recorded, and it can be recorded in the 'Bihar.' The references are being given to you here. In the two volumes, in the second volume, there is a debate. In 'Bihar al-Anwar,' in volume 10, there are the debates of the Imam, and in 'Tuhaf al-Uqul,' in one volume, you can give the chapter at the end; the last chapter is of the Imam's debates. And Alhamdulillah, it has been translated into English as well, Alhamdulillah, it has been translated into Urdu as well. And look at what he is saying. And after that, in the Hadith, he says that 'Inna Shaytan'... He says that 'Inna Shaytan'... give the salawat. It is that which is behind the back. I am telling the youth, read the Quran, read it, read the translation. Allah is commanding His great Prophet, Hazrat Musa (a.s.)—this is for today—that with Harun, go to Pharaoh, who has become rebellious, has become a tyrant, Pharaoh, and the rest who... Did Allah not know? Allah did know, but Allah wanted to inform you. This is their style, this is their way of speaking. So do not become a source of disgrace. It is stated: if you want to be humiliated, insulted, and mocked, then become rude. Those who obey Allah and His Messenger—'fa-ula'ika'... ...and the Messenger, they are in the company of Allah and His Messenger. What a wonderful company! Can you find a better company? He will be with the Messenger, he will be with the Siddiq, meaning the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). What an excellent company! So tell me, if there is a better company... ...so tell me, if there is a better company, then let us go there. If there is a better companionship available, then in this era, everyone should hold fast to the Imam of the Time (a.s.). And listen to this Hadith from Kamaluddin: how do we follow him? Just as... ...how do we follow him? Just as he proceeds, we proceed. If a person deliberately performs prostration before the Imam, his prayer will be void. Befriending his friends and being hostile to his enemies—this is what is coming. I love him. And on the Day of Judgment, they will have the most honor and respect. But the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) also knew what the Ummah would turn out to be. He knew everything beforehand. That is why it is narrated from Malik that when they were returning from Tabuk, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stopped... ...the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stopped the Muslims and said, 'O Muslims, what has happened to you? When I say love Ali (a.s.), your faces light up, you become very happy. But when I say love the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), it seems as if pomegranate seeds are bursting in your mouths. At the mention of love for the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), pomegranate seeds start bursting in your mouths; your faces turn red with anger. What has happened to you? It is the Day of Judgment. If any of you comes on the Day of Judgment with deeds like mountains, but the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is not with him, Allah will throw him into Hell face-down. He will throw him into Hell face-down.' It is stated that if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had ordered his Ummah... ...it is stated that if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had ordered his Ummah to oppress his family and his progeny, the Ummah could never have oppressed as much as they did when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Love my family and my progeny.' You know, in Kufa, there was a special group of the Mawla (a.s.) who always stayed with him for his defense. They were called 'Shurtat al-Khamis'. These were special individuals who defended the Mawla. There were always five people ahead who were with the Mawla. I was following the Mawla, and I saw that the Mawla went into the market and was asking the Kufans, 'Why are you doing all this wrongdoing? Is there any sign of my Imamate, any proof?' ...is there any sign of my Imamate, any proof? The Mawla turned and looked. 'You want proof? Yes.' He picked up a stone. He picked up the stone, the Mawla pressed his ring on it, and the seal of the Mawla appeared on the stone. He said, 'In this way, as the sign appears, you must keep accepting his Imamate.' The woman says the Mawla was saying this. I went to Imam Hasan (a.s.). He said, 'Father, for the sign of the stone, come here.' Then Imam Husayn (a.s.)... Imam Husayn (a.s.)... what was my age then? 103 years old. 113... I was of that age, and I was standing there. So I thought that perhaps now... ...and I was standing there, and I thought that perhaps now I am standing, I will pass away. Will I be able to bear the Imam for this long? And the Imam gestured. Father, he gestured with his finger. The miracle of the finger's gesture was so powerful that from 63 to 2163... 2163 years, the father of the believers was alive, and I had asked for the proof of Imamate from every Imam. These were the kinds of women who had immense Wilayah. And if there are such women, then such people are born in the house, such children are born who are ready to sacrifice their lives. And the entire event of Karbala is just this. Everything was looted, until Ali Asghar (a.s.) was also martyred. Now no one is left. Now Husayn... ...was martyred. Now no one is left. Now Husayn (a.s.) comes to my house. After coming, he says, 'My peace be upon you all, this is the last one.' As soon as she heard, she immediately said, 'Brother, what is this last peace you are saying?' [Music] Husayn [Praise] is... 'Do not say it like this. Where is he? Take me to Sayyid Sajjad (a.s.).' Zaynab (s.a.) was the arm of Imam Husayn (a.s.). She brought him to Sayyid Sajjad (a.s.). 'Son, Sayyid Sajjad, get up, see, Father has come.' And as soon as Zaynab (s.a.) spoke... Sayyid Sajjad (a.s.) could not even recognize him. Later, Imam Sajjad (a.s.) says, 'I did not recognize him because there were so many wounds on the Imam's body, so much blood, that the Imam's face had become unrecognizable.' He could not even recognize him. He was saying, 'Father, what has happened to your body?' The Imam asked about each one, 'What happened to them?' ...asked about each one, 'What happened to them?' 'They were martyred.' He asked about each one, 'They were martyred.' He asked, remembering, 'And my brother Ali Akbar?' 'Bring my sword, I will fight on behalf of my father.' 'Husayn, son, Sayyid Sajjad, Karbala is your park, this is Jihad. Rather, the markets of Kufa are the Jihad of your mother. Son, be patient. And son, when you return to Medina, give my peace to my Shias and say, 'Sayyid-e-Mazloom (a.s.) says, O my Shias, when you drink cold water, remember my thirst. And when you see any destitute or poor person, remember my helplessness and loneliness.'' Saying this, Husayn (a.s.) became... he came to bid farewell. Once, he looked outside the tent, once he looked at the place of the martyrs. He saw the companions lying in blood. Covered in blood, the martyrs. Now Husayn (a.s.) calls out. Husayn (a.s.), whose name he took, once a voice... O my brave ones, O my valiant ones, O my horsemen, O my masters, what has happened to you? Why are you silent? I am calling out to you, yet you do not answer my call. Hussein (a.s.) called out once, a strange sentence, 'Who is there among you who will take my reins? Who will be my horseman? Who will ride with me?' On the 28th of Rajab, Hussein (a.s.) had said that Abbas's day would come. Hussein (a.s.) came to the battlefield, attacked the army once, they collided like walls, then he returned and attacked again. 'Do not be surprised, just watch my battle.' Abbas (a.s.) returned. Now, as he thought of making a third attack, he stopped for a moment. Suddenly, a divine call came: 'Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul-mutma'innah, irji'i ila rabbiki radiyatan mardiyyah, fadkhuli fi 'ibadi wadkhuli jannati' (O soul that is at rest, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise). Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. Imam Hussein (a.s.) says, 'My father put the sword in the sheath, and as soon as he did, someone threw a stone, someone threw a spear, and there was a rain of arrows.' Hussein (a.s.) did not come to the land of Karbala, but rather to the arrows. And suddenly, a scene appeared—it is written in the Maqtal—that Shimr (may Allah curse him) was sitting on his chest and wanted to behead the Imam. Janabe Zainab (s.a.), searching for her brother, saw that scene—may Allah never show any sister such a sight—that he was cutting Hussein's throat. When Zainab (s.a.) looked, she saw, 'Are you watching my brother being slaughtered?' As soon as Zainab's voice reached Hussein's ears, Hussein (a.s.) signaled, 'Zainab, go back to the tent, I am still alive.' I am still alive. Zainab (s.a.) went to the tent. I had not yet finished when the land of Karbala began to shake. The sun was eclipsed, and the water began to surge. The wind began to blow. 'Son, Sajjad (a.s.), what is happening? Remove the curtain of the tent.' When he removed the curtain, what did he see? The head of Hussein (a.s.) was on the tip of a spear. 'Assalamu alayka ya Aba Abdillah, O Father, you were martyred and I remained alive. O Lord, accept our brief mourning.' Accept our brief mourning, place these tears in the presence of Fatimah (s.a.). Three times Surah Fatiha, for the family, for the ancestors, for all the deceased of the family, O Allah.

title: Tamaam Musalmaanon Se Chaar (4) Sawaal
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the critical importance of recognizing the Imam of one's time according to Islamic tradition. The speaker cites a hadith stating that dying without an allegiance to an Imam is equivalent to a death of ignorance. Four specific questions are posed to all Muslims to evaluate their understanding and connection to the divinely appointed leadership. The lecture challenges the audience to reflect on the identity and legitimacy of their Imam in the context of the twelve successors.
content:
On the Day of Judgment, every person will be raised with their Imam. They will be called with their Imam. The famous scholar of the first generation, Muslim bin Hajjaj Nishapuri, recorded this hadith in his book. In it, Abdullah ibn Umar said that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Whoever dies and there is no allegiance to anyone on his neck, his death is the death of ignorance.' And our question, our five questions to all Muslims: The first question is, who is the Imam of the time? The second question is, is he present in this era and at this time? The third question is, is he from the Bani Hashim? And the fourth and final question is, does he belong to those 12 Imams whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) mentioned in his hadith? If the answer to even one of these four questions is 'no', then that person's death will be the death of ignorance.
Every individual will be resurrected alongside their Imam on the Day of Judgment.

title: Muharram 1442 English Majlis #05: The Core of Islam | Sayed Mahdi Modarresi
excerpt: In this lecture, Sayed Mahdi Modarresi explores the fundamental essence of Islam as total submission to divine authority and the guidance of the Ahlulbayt. He critiques modern attempts to reinterpret religious texts through a Quran-centric approach, emphasizing that true faith requires obedience even when it defies personal rationalization. The discourse also highlights the critical role of parents in safeguarding their children's spiritual development against worldly influences and concludes with a poignant reflection on the grief of the Ahlulbayt following the tragedy of Karbala.

chapters.title: The Essence of Submission
chapters.summary: The ultimate goal of a believer is to reach the end of life with faith and complete submission to Allah, a state even the prophets prayed to achieve.

chapters.title: Obedience to Divine Authority
chapters.summary: True submission requires following the Imam's guidance even during times of extreme oppression, rather than acting on personal impulse or rationalization.

chapters.title: The Danger of Rejecting Hadith
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques those who dismiss authentic hadith to promote 'Quran-centricity,' arguing that the Quran requires the Prophet and his successors for proper interpretation.

chapters.title: The Essence of Religious Obedience
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that religious rituals like Hajj are defined by specific, non-negotiable commands from Allah, emphasizing that true faith requires submission rather than personal rationalization.

chapters.title: Submission vs. Rationalization
chapters.summary: Using the story of a woman seeking guidance from Imam al-Sadiq, the speaker illustrates the importance of prioritizing divine law over personal opinion or medical convenience.

chapters.title: Rejecting Modernist Reinterpretations
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques the tendency to discard or modernize religious laws like Hijab based on contemporary societal norms, arguing that divine commands remain valid regardless of human logic.

chapters.title: Parental Responsibility and Religious Values
chapters.summary: The speaker challenges the modern tendency to question religious traditions and emphasizes that parents are primarily responsible for instilling faith and values in their children.

chapters.title: The Metaphor of the Open Field
chapters.summary: Using the teachings of Imam Ali (AS), the speaker explains that a child's heart is like an unplanted field that requires deliberate cultivation of good values to prevent it from becoming a wasteland.

chapters.title: Prioritizing Religion Over Worldly Success
chapters.summary: The speaker critiques the community's tendency to prioritize secular education and career success over religious practice, urging parents to be as vigilant about their children's spiritual environment as they are about their academic one.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Imam Hussain and Umul Banin
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by contrasting the worldly nature of the masses with the ultimate sacrifice of Imam Hussain (AS) and the devotion of Umul Banin, who prioritized the mission of Islam above all else.

chapters.title: The Return to Medina
chapters.summary: Lady Zainab and the remaining family members return to Medina in a small, grieving caravan without Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: The Meeting of Grief
chapters.summary: Lady Zainab requests privacy to mourn, but is visited by a companion who shares in her profound sorrow and loss.

title: EP02 | Khalifa Kaun Banaaye? | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 💐
excerpt: This lecture, part of the 'Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi' mega quiz series, explores the theological foundations of leadership succession in Islam. The speakers argue that the appointment of an Imam is an exclusive divine prerogative, contrasting this with historical Sunni selection methods which they claim lack Quranic support. Through a critical analysis of historical events like Saqifah and the Prophet's teachings, the session emphasizes that true leadership is divinely ordained rather than democratically determined.

Let us begin today's episode with these lines: Every heart, every tongue said 'Ya Ali Madad'. Every heart, every tongue said 'Ya Ali Madad'. Every elder, every youth said 'Ya Ali Madad'. A child falling on the ground who was saved, spontaneously the mother said 'Ya Ali Madad'. Rahim, Qul wajata Hassan, Salwa Safi, Qul Sa, Was wa dali, wa na khasa tasahu, wa ha. Let us first tell you a few things about the 'Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi' mega quiz. There will be seven episodes, and in each episode, a discussion regarding Ghadir and the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) will be presented to you, the discussion... Which will be presented to you, and the questions of this quiz will be related to that discussion. In each episode, we will have seven lucky winners who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. The first prize is 5,000, the second two prizes are 3,000, and the third four prizes are 1,000. And finally, the mega prize of our 'Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi' mega quiz is the one that every lover of Ali (a.s.) desires in their heart—that they want to go to the threshold of their Mawla and bow their head in submission, that is, a pilgrimage to Iraq. Yes, viewers, the mega prize is a pilgrimage to Iraq, which will be announced in a special episode after this series ends. To be eligible for the mega prize of the Iraq pilgrimage, one must watch all these episodes, i.e., all seven episodes, and participate in the quiz of each episode. You must give correct answers to all the questions in at least five out of the seven episodes. And from all such individuals, the winner of our mega prize, i.e., the Iraq pilgrimage, will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. We hope that... We hope that you will stay with us throughout this series and keep participating in every quiz. The quiz link will be activated as soon as each episode starts, and the quiz link is present in the live chat and description of this video. The quiz link will remain active until the end of the episode. At the end of each episode, there will be Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, after which this link will be closed. We request you to listen to our episodes carefully and give correct answers to all the questions. Dear viewers, in the previous episode, we presented a detailed discussion on the topic of what the successor of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) should be like and what characteristics he should possess. In today's episode, we will discuss who is responsible for selecting the Caliph and successor of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and who has the right to decide who the Caliph and successor of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) should be. So, for this discussion, we will request our brothers to shed more light on this topic. In our gathering, Mr. Mohammad Abbas Patel and Mr. Sajjad Mehar Ali are present. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Wa Alaikum Assalam. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Wa Alaikum Assalam. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Sajjad Sahab, we would like to start today's discussion with you on the topic of Caliphate—whose responsibility is it to appoint the Caliph of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? So, we would like you to shed more light on this. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Before we answer this question in the light of the Quran, it is necessary that we understand the viewpoints of these two sects. As we know, the belief of the Shia brethren is that the right to appoint the successor, Caliph, and Imam of the Prophet belongs solely to the Lord of Majesty, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appoints his successor, Caliph, and Imam by the command of Allah. People have no role in this. People have no authority to interfere in this. Now, regarding the belief of the other sect, in his book 'Muqaddimah', a famous and well-known scholar of that sect presents the theory that it is obligatory upon the Ummah to select the successor of the Prophet, and he mentions four ways to select him in his book. They describe four methods of selection in their books. They are trying to say that it is the right of the Ummah—it is the right of the Ummah to select and appoint the successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Four different methods are mentioned: first is Ijma (consensus), second is Istikhlaf (nomination), third is Shura (consultation), and fourth is Ghalba (conquest). We will explain each one. Ijma means that the entire Ummah comes together to select the successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). That is Ijma, yes, consensus. As for the second, Istikhlaf, it means that the existing Caliph appoints his successor. The third is Shura, in which a committee is formed consisting of a few people who choose one person together. And the fourth and final one, Ghalba, is that through force or power, some king or ruler captures a country and brings the people under his control; even then, he can be appointed as Caliph. So, these four different methods are mentioned by Ibn Khaldun in his book 'Muqaddimah Ibn Khaldun'—meaning these four methods exist among the Ahl al-Sunnah. But if one reflects on this, these four methods are in conflict with each other. If one reflects, these four methods are in conflict with each other. So, how can one determine which method to use and when? That is a very good question, Gulzar Bhai. If we look at the background of how these four methods came into existence, we understand that in reality, these four methods are different from one another. And this is because these four methods were used. First, the Caliph was selected through these four methods, and then this became the criteria. Or in other words, if we say that these four methods were actually a way to advance the plan of Saqifah. Not only that, there is another point, Gulzar Bhai: these four methods cannot be proven from the Quran and Sunnah anywhere. And if anyone is calling this a divine Sunnah, they should know that there is a decisive verse in the Quran regarding the Sunnah of Allah, where Allah (t.a.) says: 'Wa lan tajida li-sunnati-llahi tabdila' (And you will never find any change in the Sunnah of Allah). And here we see that the method of appointing every Caliph is being changed at every level, or in every sequence, changes are being introduced. Exactly. For example, we see that the first Caliph was appointed through Saqifah, and when the time of the first Caliph... When the time of the first Caliph came to an end, he appointed the second Caliph as his successor. When the time of the second Caliph came to an end, he said, 'I have heard that after me, people will repeat the same thing as Saqifah.' So, the second Caliph's statement that the way we appointed the first Caliph at Saqifah was a 'falta'—'falta' meaning something that happens suddenly or unexpectedly—and then the second Caliph saying, 'May Allah protect us from its evil,' and if anyone tries to organize such a thing again, then whoever does it and whoever is appointed—in the sense of whoever organizes Saqifah or whoever is appointed at Saqifah—I will kill them both. All of this reference is present in Sahih Bukhari. Meaning, the second Caliph is admitting that the Caliph chosen at Saqifah was an evil, it was a 'falta,' a mistake. He even said, 'May Allah protect us from such evil'—meaning it was an evil, he himself is admitting it. Yes, if it were correct, it would have continued in the same way. Yes, meaning two Caliphs were chosen through two different methods, and then after that, one Caliph is also admitting that it was a mistake. And when it comes to the third round of the Caliphate, the second Caliph formed a Shura, a committee in which six people were appointed, and it was decided among those six people... It was decided among those six people that if these people do not come together and select one person within three days, then kill them all. Meaning, even those who are eligible for the Caliphate, if a decision cannot be reached, kill them all, and then it is up to the Ummah to choose whomever they want. Now, as for the fourth, Ghalba. The question is, why was this Ghalba introduced? It is simple: this Ghalba was not for any Caliph; it was introduced into Islam to justify the rule of Muawiyah bin Abu Sufyan, whereas its reference is neither from the Quran nor from the Hadith, and it is not proven by anything. And that is why, Sajjad Sahab, we see in their books that their prominent people had a slogan: 'No man ghalaba'—we will be with whoever becomes dominant. Yes, Abbas Bhai, all these points lead to only one aspect: that after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Ummah took the authority to choose the Caliph into its own hands, and in 30 years, Caliphs were chosen in four different ways. So, a question arises here, viewers: when the Muslim Ummah has four such excellent methods through which they can choose a Caliph, then in this era, which method will the Muslim Ummah... Then in this era, which method will the Muslim Ummah adopt to choose a Caliph for themselves? And the interesting thing, Gulzar Bhai, is that the Ahl al-Sunnah ask us to prove Imamate from the Quran. Our answer to them is: take one step back and first look for the method of choosing a Caliph in the Quran. Can the Ahl al-Sunnah prove any one of these four methods mentioned for selecting a Caliph through the Quran? Has the Almighty God, anywhere from 'Bismillah' to 'Wan-nas', declared any one of these four methods permissible for choosing a Caliph? Certainly, those who raise the slogan of 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us) will also not be able to prove anywhere in the Quran that these four methods were used by the Almighty God to appoint a Caliph. If the Muslim Ummah chose its own Caliph, we see the consequences—that they invented different methods for choosing a Caliph afterward. But is there any logical answer as to why people cannot choose their own Caliph? This very question was asked to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.): 'Can people choose their own Imam?' The Imam replied with a counter-question: 'Which... The Imam replied with a counter-question: 'Which Imam? A righteous Imam or a corrupt and mischief-making Imam?' Meaning, if humans choose, there is a possibility of both—either they choose a righteous Imam or they choose a corrupt one. The narrator said, 'A righteous Imam.' Then the Imam said, 'If we look at the Prophets whom Allah chose, gave them the Book, sent down revelation, and made them 'Ulul 'Azm' (possessors of determination), is it possible for them to make a mistake in choosing people?' The narrator said, 'It is not possible.' Then the Imam said, 'Then how did it happen that when Allah commanded Musa Kalimullah to bring 70 people from his nation, and the people whom Hazrat Musa selected were leaders, believers, and righteous? But when Hazrat Musa (a.s.) took them to Mount Tur, they said there that they would not believe in him. The only condition for believing was that we see Allah. Those whom Hazrat Musa considered righteous rejected the Prophethood of Hazrat Musa, and the condition was to see Allah, whereas they were 'Ulul 'Azm' Prophets. And then what happened? Then a... Then a lightning bolt came and destroyed everyone. The lightning struck and destroyed everyone. This incident is in Surah Al-A'raf, verse 155. If a Prophet who is a possessor of Sharia, an 'Ulul 'Azm', and a Kalimullah tries to select believers from his Ummah, and if a corrupt person turns out to be among those believers, then what is the status of the Ansar and Muhajirun to choose a Caliph for themselves? Yes, that is correct, Sajjad Sahab. Whoever they choose, there is no guarantee that they won't turn back. When will they turn back? So, do the Prophets (a.s.) not have the authority to choose their own successor? Gulzar Bhai, we see a stage in the light of the verses of the Quran where this same Hazrat Musa (a.s.), when he wants a vizier (minister) for himself, he makes a request in the court of the Almighty God that Allah should appoint a Caliph or a vizier for him. And we see this verse in the Quran: 'Waj'al li waziran min ahli, Haruna akhi' (And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother). If we reflect on this verse, we realize that even an 'Ulul 'Azm' Prophet, when he wants a vizier for himself... When he wants a vizier for himself, he does not choose directly. Rather, he makes a request in the court of the Almighty God: 'O Allah, appoint a vizier for me.' And then Allah accepts this request, and the answer is found in the Quran itself: 'Qala qad utita su'la ya Musa' (He said: You have been granted your request, O Musa). Meaning, here we see that the Prophet makes a request, and Allah accepts that request. Yes, it is not that the Prophet directly chose Hazrat Harun as his vizier. Meaning, Hazrat Musa wanted his brother Hazrat Harun to be his vizier, but he did not choose him; he is presenting a request before Allah to make him his vizier. And then Allah chooses, saying, 'Yes, I have made him.' Correct, correct. Yes, so this Ummah, which cannot even guarantee its two units of prayer—cannot guarantee whether its two units of prayer are correct or not, or whether they were accepted or not—then how is it possible for them to choose an Imam or Caliph for themselves? Yes, and whoever they choose, what is the guarantee for him? Yes, meaning Abbas Bhai, the responsibility of choosing a Caliph and successor, when it is not even with the Prophets... When it is not even with the Prophets, then whose responsibility is it? Gulzar Bhai, the question you have raised is a very important question, and every Muslim should seek the answer to this question. Undoubtedly, they have the Quran and Hadith through which they can seek the answer to this question. And all the conflicts that exist among Muslims would disappear if they found the correct answer to this question. Indeed, if we reflect on the verses of the Quran, in a very clear manner, wherever Allah has spoken about appointing a Caliph, He has reserved this responsibility for Himself. Nowhere in any verse of the Quran do we find that Allah told people to choose an Imam for themselves. Even when Allah is choosing the first Caliph for this earth, or the first Imam for the earth, at that time the Almighty God says: 'Inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifa' (I am going to appoint a Caliph on the earth). Here, He did not say, 'You all get together and...'—the word 'ja'ilun' is used. 'Ja'ilun' means to appoint or to select. So here, Allah Himself is saying, 'I am appointing a Caliph.' He is not saying, 'Brother, you all...' He is not saying, 'Brother, you all choose,' or 'Whoever gains power should become the Imam or Caliph,' or any of the other methods the Ahl al-Sunnah have mentioned for appointing an Imam. It is the opposite. Meaning, Allah has reserved this responsibility for Himself, not handed it over to the Ummah. And when Allah made Hazrat Adam (a.s.) the Caliph, we find later in the Quran that the angels presented their opinion. Yes, and what did the angels say? 'Will You place therein one who will cause corruption and shed blood, while we glorify You and sanctify You?' Sajjad Sahab, this verse also proves one thing—a point is proven—that the angels also have the right to express their opinion. They presented this request before Allah: 'Make us the Caliph.' But what did Allah say in response? 'Qala inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun' (He said: I know what you do not know). Meaning, here Allah did not say to the angels, 'Brother, you all get together and decide on a Caliph for yourselves.' Nor did Allah say to any Prophet in the Quran anywhere, 'Brother, you choose your own successor after you,' or 'Form a committee of Prophets or angels to decide.' Is it the angels who decide who will be the Caliph, or is it said—God forbid—that whoever gains dominance becomes the Caliph? For example, in a common worldly scenario, suppose we have set up a business or opened a shop. Now, whom will we appoint in that shop? The one we want, or the one the neighbor next door wants? Obviously, since it is my shop, I will appoint the one I desire. So, when the religion belongs to Allah, the Messenger belongs to Allah, the Book belongs to Allah, and Islam belongs to Allah, then it is obvious that only Allah has the right to select its representative. When the angels raised an objection, what did Allah say to them? 'Inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun' (I know what you do not know). So, if an innocent angel does not have the authority to interfere in Allah's work, then how is it possible for a common human to choose a Prophet or Caliph for themselves? Here, Allah's response is that He does not even want to inform them. That is, despite being innocent angels, let alone having the right to choose, Allah does not even want to tell them to think about it. 'I know what you do not know.' So, it becomes absolutely clear here that the selection of a Caliph is a divine act. The selection of a Caliph is a divine act, and humans or the Muslim Ummah have no authority in this. A very beautiful discussion is taking place here, and every point is being presented through Quranic verses. We would like to present some Quranic verses in which the word 'Imam' has been used. If we reflect on the Quran, there are 12 such verses where the word 'Imam' is used. There are 12 verses, and there are 12 Imams. Indeed, SubhanAllah. Only Allah knows the wisdom behind this. As Allah says, 'And We made them Imams who guide by Our command.' Here, the word is 'Ja'alna' (We made). Similarly, there are other verses in the Quran where Allah keeps the responsibility of selecting an Imam to Himself, or if a Prophet requests the appointment of an Imam, he prays to Allah. For example, in Surah Al-Furqan, verse 74: 'Waj'alna lil-muttaqina imama' (And make us an Imam for the righteous). Make us an Imam for the righteous. Here, in Surah Al-Qasas, verse 5, 'Wa nuridu an namunna...' and We make them heirs on the earth. Or Surah As-Sajdah, verse 24, which is similar to the verse Sajjad Sahab recited: 'And We made from among them leaders (Imams) who guide by Our command.' In all these places, Allah reserves the act of appointing an Imam for Himself, not asking the Ummah to choose an Imam for themselves, nor asking the Prophets, nor giving this authority to the angels, as we have seen. Yes, these are the Imams whose criteria are set by Allah. As for those Imams whom people appoint, they do not meet the criteria of these verses. However, we find one such verse in the Quran regarding self-proclaimed Imams whom people have declared as Imams. It is verse 41 of Surah Al-Qasas. It refers to those whom the people of Hell have declared as Imams. It is possible that these self-proclaimed Imams, or those whom people are making Imams, are the ones referred to in this verse, who are leading people toward Hell. And Gulzar Bhai, this same point is present in Sahih Bukhari. It is narrated from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that he said: 'You will surely follow the ways of those who came before you, inch by inch, hand by hand, to the extent that if they were to enter the hole of a lizard, you would also enter it.' The companions asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, do you mean the Jews and Christians?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'Who else could it be?' Just as the Children of Israel abandoned Harun (a.s.) and followed Samiri, exactly in accordance with the prophecy of the Messenger of Allah, this Ummah will also abandon the true successor of the Messenger of Allah, i.e., Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Indeed, Abbas Bhai, we thank you both from the bottom of our hearts for presenting this in a very logical manner in the light of the Holy Quran. In the light of the Holy Quran, the discussion you presented regarding whose responsibility it is to select the Caliph and successor of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, viewers, the verses of the Holy Quran we observed today made it seem as if Allah has discussed the subject of Caliphate and Imamate in detail in the Holy Quran. And the way we reflected on that Hadith at the end, that the Muslim Ummah will follow the nations that passed before them in exactly the same way—just as the nation of Musa (a.s.) abandoned Harun (a.s.) despite him being his Vizier—in the same way, this Ummah of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) abandoned Ali (a.s.) despite him being his Caliph and successor. Dear viewers, now we move towards Ziyarat Aminullah. Immediately after the Ziyarat ends, the seven lucky winners of today's episode will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. You are requested to submit your answers as soon as possible and focus on the Ziyarat. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Now the time has come for the announcement of today's episode winners, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. So let's see who are today's four third-prize winners who will receive 1000 Indian Rupees. And these are the four names who won today's third prize: Zeeshan Haider from Allahabad, Taskeen Fatima from Prayagraj, Syed Abbas from Mumbai, and Shagufta Gabrani from Thane. Congratulations to all of you. Now let's see who are the two lucky individuals who are entitled to the two second prizes, i.e., 2000 Indian Rupees. And their names are in front of you: Hariya Mohammad Ali Asgar Ali from Palitana and Zainab Umatia from Mumbai. Many congratulations to you as well. And now let's see who is today's first-prize winner who will receive a prize of 5000 Indian Rupees. And their name is in front of you: today's first-prize winner is Ali Zain from Varanasi, India. We congratulate all the winners of today's episode from the bottom of our hearts, and we will meet all of you again tomorrow at the same time, i.e., 9:30 PM India time. Sallallahu ala Muhammad wa alihi at-tahirin al-ma'sumin.

chapters.title: Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Quiz Overview
chapters.summary: The episode introduces a seven-part mega quiz series focused on the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.), offering cash prizes and a grand prize of a pilgrimage to Iraq.

chapters.title: Authority to Appoint the Caliph
chapters.summary: The discussion explores the fundamental difference between the Shia belief that Caliphate is divinely appointed versus the Sunni perspective of human selection.

chapters.title: Critique of Sunni Selection Methods
chapters.summary: The speakers analyze the four methods of selecting a Caliph—Ijma, Istikhlaf, Shura, and Ghalba—arguing that they lack Quranic basis and are contradictory.

chapters.title: Divine Authority in Appointing Successors
chapters.summary: The discussion explores why the selection of a Caliph is a divine prerogative rather than a human choice, citing the fallibility of human selection.

chapters.title: Prophetic Requests and Divine Appointment

chapters.title: Allah's Exclusive Right to Appoint Imams

title: Majlis-e-Aza (Urdu) for Esaal e Sawaab of Marhoom Haji Mohammed Taqi Shaikh Ibne Haji Fazal Husain
excerpt: This lecture serves as a Majlis-e-Aza dedicated to the remembrance of Marhoom Haji Mohammed Taqi Shaikh, focusing on the fundamental theological concept of Wilayah. The speaker emphasizes that the love and acceptance of Imam Ali (a.s.) is the essential criterion for the validity of all religious deeds and faith. By drawing parallels between the Prophet's mission and the sacrifice of Abbas ibn Ali, the discourse highlights the necessity of aligning one's loyalties with the Ahlulbayt to achieve spiritual completeness.
content:
I am... [Poetry/Latmiya recitation begins] ...now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... [Poetry continues] ...now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... [Poetry continues] ...on the watch of oppression, this stands... On the watch of oppression, this stands... how to give... [Poetry continues] ...how to give... [Poetry continues] ...now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... [Poetry continues] ...when he was lifted, he could not be brought... [Poetry continues] ...now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... Now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... [Poetry continues] ...Zainab said in the land of the poor... [Poetry continues] ...seeing me, they weep... [Poetry continues] ...now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... [Poetry continues] ...the support of the hands... [Poetry continues] ...now your remembrance is your right, the world has become... Why do you cry for me, Ramesh? You have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. And ping, how were you surrounded by horses? How were you surrounded by horses? Listen to this, O Majnun, as much as you cry for me, you have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. O machine, tell me, where is the truth? Where is the talk? Where is this face? Where is the talk? Where is this face? You cry for me, O you who cry for me. You have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. Where are the desires? As much as you cry for me, the desires that were there, as much as you cry for me, you have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. Hazrat, with a bloodied eye, Hazrat Mehal Kushav, With a bloodied eye, Hazrat Mehal Kushav, blood-stained, O Amir Takallum, why do you cry for me? O Amir, why do you cry for me? You have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. When the face was forced, and you cry for me, you have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. You have the right to cry for me. It has been an age since you cried for me. Alhamdullilah, Rabbil Alamin, this is... This is what was being given to the children. Wassalatu Wassalamu ala Ashrafil Anbiya, and the social media, I am currently in the path of the Ahlulbayt. O Prophet (s.a.w.a.), listen, O Allah, guide us to the right path. O Lord, cut off the ladder of the oppressors. O Lord, I am in your path. That he may come, that he may cover me. What should I do? The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyyun mawlahu.' (Whoever I am his master, then Ali is his master). The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyyun mawlahu.' Before starting, let us recite Surah Al-Fatiha for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), for Hasan and Husayn, and for all the martyrs. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that whoever denies the Imamate of Ali after me, he has denied my Imamate, and whoever denies my Imamate has denied the Prophethood of Allah. Whoever denies the Imamate of Ali has denied the Prophethood of Allah. Whoever denies the Prophethood of Allah has denied the Oneness of Allah. How important is the Wilayah of Ali? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) emphasized it in his final sermon. He said, 'Take care of Ali, take care of Ali.' Do not be negligent in this. And he is not saying this on his own; Allah is the one who has taken the responsibility for this. He does not say anything from his own desire; he only speaks what... He only speaks what has been revealed to him. He only speaks what is sent down from Allah. He does not speak otherwise. And in another verse, it is addressed, 'Wa law taqawwala alayna ba'dal aqawil.' (If he had made up any saying concerning Us, We would have seized him by the right hand and cut his life-vein). This is the status of the Prophet, that Allah is taking the guarantee for him. This is the status of the Prophet, that Allah is taking the guarantee for him. Allah is testifying that he is the one who never lies. He does not speak from his own desire; he only speaks what is revealed to him. And who is this Prophet? He is the one who lived among the disbelievers of Mecca for 40 years, and they gave him the titles of 'Sadiq' (Truthful) and 'Amin' (Trustworthy). That is why when he announced his Prophethood, he first took a confession from them. He asked them, 'If I tell you that an army is behind this mountain, will you believe me?' They all said, 'Yes, we believe you, you are Sadiq and Amin.' Then he gathered his close relatives and warned them, as per the verse 'Wa andhir ashiratakal aqrabin' (And warn your closest relatives). When they confessed, the Prophet said, 'I am the Messenger of Allah for you.' This was the first public announcement. He asked who would help him in this mission. No one answered, except for a 13-year-old boy who stood up repeatedly and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I will help you.' The Prophet then said, 'This is my brother, my successor, and my caliph among you.' This is my brother, this is my successor, this is my vizier after me, so listen to him and obey him. The whole sentence is not even read; just look at this much, understand this much, that this process of announcing Wilayah did not happen only at Ghadir. Those who object and say, 'Why did he do it at Ghadir? Why not in Mecca?' No, they do not even know that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not just announce it at Ghadir. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did it in Mecca, from the first day, from the age of 30, and until his last breath, he announced it in Mecca, he announced it in the journey, wherever he was sure, he would announce it. And he would announce the Wilayah of his brother and the extension of his Wilayah. Yes, he would say it, he would not care about anyone. So let's begin, this is how he would say it... If you love, then do it for the sake of Allah. If you hate, then do it for the sake of Allah. Meaning, not for your personal matters, not for the world, not for money, not for these things. And brother, do it for the sake of Allah. Meaning, all your emotions, all the feelings you have, the basis of those emotions should be in the path of Allah, for Allah. That if you are loving, then for Allah; if you are hating, if you are showing enmity, then for Allah. If you are befriending, then do it for Allah. If you are showing enmity, then do it for Allah, because this is the status of Wilayah of God. No one can reach the Wilayah of God, no one can attain the Wilayah of God, until they make all their emotions for Allah, until they make them for Allah. And this is the Wilayah, and whoever considers it a matter of love, no one can attain the fragrance of faith until they do this. No matter how much they pray, no matter how much they fast, even if they spend their whole life, until they do this—that they love for the sake of Allah, hate for the sake of Allah, befriend for the sake of Allah, show enmity for the sake of Allah—when they do all this, then they will have faith. Meaning, faith is not through prayer, faith is not through fasting, although prayer and fasting are the most important, they are in the religion, they are the most important, certainly they have their own importance. But if someone is performing these acts without the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.)... If someone is performing these acts without the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), then his prayer and fasting do not matter. If there is no Wilayah, then there is nothing, there is no benefit. Even if he prays, it is of no use. Today, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Today, you people make these people your friends, but they are for the world.' They look at the world, for the sake of the world, for the sake of wealth, for their own personal matters, for personal things, not for the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). For that, they do not love, they do not hate. And this will not bring any benefit, no benefit at all. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explained all these things, that in your hearts, for the companions... In your hearts, he explained to the companions well that look, if you want Allah to accept all your worship, and you want to be among the people of faith, there is only one way: love for the sake of Allah, hate for the sake of Allah, befriend for the sake of Allah, show enmity for the sake of Allah. Apart from this, nothing else. Your friendship, your enmity, your love, your hatred, should not be for personal reasons. If a person does it for personal reasons, it will not be of any use. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated these things, someone asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not know, but I might be hurt, and I might start hating...' 'O Messenger of Allah, how will I know that I am doing it for the sake of Allah?' How will I know that I am befriending for the sake of Allah and showing enmity for the sake of Allah? He said, 'Accept his words, follow his path. Befriend him, and who is the enemy of Allah, show enmity towards him.' Who is the enemy of Allah? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) pointed towards Ali Murtaza (a.s.) and said, 'O people, do you see him?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would make them acknowledge it every moment so that no one could say, 'We did not understand who you were talking about, we thought you were talking about someone else.' No, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made them acknowledge it. 'I have explained it clearly. Now look with your own eyes, do you see him?' Pointing towards him, he asked, 'Do you see him?' They said, 'Yes, we see him.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'This is Ali. His lover is the lover of Allah, so befriend him. Whoever loves Ali has loved Allah. So, love the lover of Ali, befriend him. And his enemy is the enemy of Allah, so show enmity towards him. There should be no softness in your heart for him, no kindness. He is an enemy, so what?' Anyway, friends, we are talking about this. If it is possible that those who object, those who object, say that this was for that time, but if there is a need, then the objectors have said that show enmity to the enemy... Show enmity to the enemy, befriend his friend, even if he is the killer of your father or your son. Befriend the friend of Ali, love the lover of Ali, even if he is the killer of your father or your son. If any person... in my grandfather's time, there was enmity for three or four generations. If someone killed a son, you can understand how enmity can be. Here, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave an extreme example, an extreme example, so that no one could say that this could be something else. That the killer of your father, the killer of your son... all these things can happen. It means that if there is a small quarrel, for some property, wealth, land, or money, for small things, then do not have such enmity that you stop loving the lover of Ali. Do not have enmity, but rather forgive him. Allah will understand, and Allah will elevate your status. Even if he has done you so much harm, this is a difficult stage, but it is the stage of Wilayah in which a person has to come to a point. That befriend the friend of Ali, even if he is the killer of your father or your son. And show enmity to the enemy of Ali, even if he is your father or your son. If he is an enemy of Ali, then show enmity towards him. If your father is an enemy, then show enmity towards him. There should not be even a speck of love in your heart for him, no softness, no kindness. This is the matter. Did it reach them or not? It reached them, but here, those who have enmity, those who have enmity, those who I mentioned, the talk is about them, there is enmity towards them. And this tradition is present in our authentic books, and it is the way of the followers of Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). It is the name of an open book for the followers of Ali (a.s.). Now look, what is the tradition? It talks about this. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Ali, you are the one who will be the leader after me. Whoever opposes Ali after me...' After me, those who opposed Ali—what does 'opposing Ali' mean? It means not accepting Ali as the Caliph, not accepting Ali as the leader, not accepting Ali as the one who holds the authority. Those who spent their efforts against Ali, praising them, supporting them, believing in them, and following them—that is what is called opposition. Was there anything else? For the world? What is the world? The world is a deception. And this is the world. If someone says, 'I divorce you three times, I divorce you three times,' it means 'Go away, I am not interested in you, look for someone else.' So, the matter here is not just about the world; it is about the status, the Wilayah, the status that Allah gave to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). So, whoever opposes that, they are opposing the truth. And whoever denies that, they are a Mushrik (polytheist), and whoever associates anyone else with Ali is a Mushrik, because they have associated someone with Ali, and they have abandoned the path of Allah to appoint someone else in place of Ali. These are the ones who present their own opinions in the path of Allah. Those who present their own opinions in the path of Allah, how can they be believers? They may pray as much as they want, they may fast as much as they want, but in the eyes of Allah, they are not believers. We consider those to be believers who love Ali, who are with Ali, who love what Allah loves. When the name of Ali (a.s.) is mentioned, tears come to the eyes. That is the sign of a believer. That is the sign of a believer, and those who hold malice against Ali are the hypocrites. The love of Ali is such a thing that even at the time of death, it is there. But people befriend others and follow them. And who are those people? Just like people in this room, you are in a gathering, right? It is written in history that a person came and sat down. Every day, the time of the meeting, and he showed no reaction. The second day, he came and sat, no reaction. The third day, he came and sat, no reaction. Then, when the Imam (a.s.) entered, as soon as he entered, he started crying. He started crying and said, 'He is the one, he is the one.' I asked, 'How did you know?' He said, 'As soon as he entered, looking at him, we started crying. Our heartbeats increased, tears started flowing from our eyes. By God, our hearts and our souls testified that this is indeed him.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Your faith is true, your faith is sincere.' These are not among those people, and Malik al-Ashtar is one of them. And Malik al-Ashtar, and his brother Ibrahim, all of these are those who are ready to sacrifice their lives. So, the one who opposes Ali is a hypocrite, and the one who follows in the footsteps of Ali reaches the destination. Look, it is not enough to just claim to be a follower of Ali; it is necessary to follow in the footsteps of Ali. Ali used to pray; you also pray. Ali used to prostrate; you also prostrate. Look, you cannot be exactly like Ali, but at least try to follow in his footsteps. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Whoever follows in the footsteps of Ali, Ali is the embodiment of worship, Ali is the embodiment of generosity, Ali is the embodiment of patience, Ali is the embodiment of truthfulness, Ali is the embodiment of bravery, Ali is the door of knowledge, Ali is the treasure of God.' Whoever follows in the footsteps of Ali will reach the destination, and whoever opposes Ali will... And whoever opposes Ali will be destroyed. Those who rejected Ali, they were destroyed, they were ruined. Ali is the light of Allah (Noorullah). If these cities shine, it is because of the light of Allah upon the servants of Allah. Ali is the sword of Allah (Saifullah) against the enemies. Ali is the heir of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Ali is the Kalima, Ali is the truth. And those who are with Ali, they are the ones. Ali is the leader of the believers (Amir al-Mu'minin). Ali is the leader of the believers, he is the guide, and Ali is the one whose... Ali is the guide, and those on whose foreheads the mark of prostration has appeared, and those who are the pure ones, they are the ones who follow him. Ali is the leader of the Muslims. Allah will not accept anyone's deeds unless they contain the love of Ali and the Wilayah of Ali. As long as there is no Wilayah of Ali, until then, no one's prayer, no one's worship, no one's devotion is accepted; everything is wasted. It is nothing but dust. Everything will be wasted; his life is wasted, his worship is wasted, his deeds are wasted, everything is wasted. Ali is the name of the light. And Ali is the one whose sons had such a character that they represented Ali in their conduct, in their morals, and in their bravery. This is that personality, that whenever the name of Abbas (a.s.) is mentioned—because the Quran says—Abbas is the one about whom it is said, and the scholars say, that whenever you face a great difficulty, then call upon him seven times. If there is a great trouble, 'Ya Kashifal-Karbi an wajhi al-Husayn, ikshif karbi bi haqqi akhika al-Husayn, Abbas.' O remover of distress from the face of Husayn, remove my distress for the sake of your brother Husayn ibn Ali. O Abbas, remove my calamity. I swear to you by your brother Husayn ibn Ali. This is that Abbas who was constantly waiting for permission to fight, but he did not get the permission. Once, in the battlefield, Husayn (a.s.) said, 'Go and bring water for the children.' Abbas went to bring water. The children were saying, 'Uncle is going to bring water, get ready, uncle is coming with water, now no one will remain thirsty.' Sakina (s.a.) was watching him. Abbas moved towards the Euphrates. He cleared the enemies. Such was the awe of Abbas that the enemies were in a state of panic. Such was the awe of Abbas that the enemies were in a state of panic. He started running. He came to the Euphrates, put the horse into the water, filled the water skin, took water in his palms, and said, 'O soul, you think I am thirsty? I am thirsty, but the water is in my hands. I can drink, but I will not drink. The children of my brother are thirsty, so I will not drink.' Abbas threw the water from his palms. Once he started moving back towards the camp, they attacked him. His hand was cut off. Then another attacked, and he covered the banner with his other hand. The water was flowing. Abbas was the hope of the children. Abbas was the hope of the children. Abbas turned the horse around. Abbas stood with his head bowed. As he stood with his head bowed, thinking, 'What will I say to the children? Now even the water is gone.' Then he was struck, and he fell from the horse onto the ground. When someone falls from a height to the ground, they use their hands for support, but his hands were gone. Abbas fell on his face. He called out, 'O brother, come to me!' Husayn (a.s.) heard such a voice, he held his back and recited a dirge, 'Al-aan, al-aan, now my back is broken, now my enemies are rejoicing.' The bond has broken now... [unclear/fragmented speech]... reaching the status of the one who is pure and elevated. O elders, this is brotherly... in a little while, Ali's lion gives... stop for a moment... that Hussain is the only one, there is no peace... your desire was... now the satanic acts will go, children should... now your brother is alone... O Allah, O Messenger of Allah... Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. O Lord, forgive us, have mercy on us, we are all according to His will. title: Imam e Waqt Ki Niyaabat Mein Ziyaarat Karna Imam Ali Naqi (A.S.) Ki Sunnat Hai | Wilaadat Mubaarak
excerpt: This lecture discusses the significance of performing Ziyarat on behalf of the Imam of the Time, citing the practice of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). It highlights a historical incident where Imam al-Naqi requested prayers at the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) despite his own elevated spiritual status. The speaker emphasizes that certain sacred places are specifically designated by Allah for the acceptance of supplications. The talk concludes by encouraging believers to pray for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) whenever they visit the holy shrine of Karbala.
content:
Performing Ziyarat on behalf of the Imam of the Time is the Sunnah of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari states that he visited Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) when the Imam was suffering from a fever. The Imam said, 'Send someone from among our followers to the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) so that he may pray to Allah for me.' Abu Hashim says, 'I left and met Ali ibn Bilal, and I informed him of what the Imam had said and requested him to go to Karbala.' Ali ibn Bilal replied, 'The Imam's command is binding, but I believe that the status of Imam al-Naqi (a.s.) is far greater than the shrine; in fact, his rank is equal to the Master of the Shrine, Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). His own prayer for himself is superior to my prayer for him in the sanctuary.' I reported this to Imam al-Naqi (a.s.). The Imam said to me, 'Tell him: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was superior to the Kaaba and the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad), yet he used to perform Tawaf of the Kaaba and kiss the Black Stone.' Then the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Inna lillahi ta'ala biqa'an yuhibbu an yud'a fiha' (Indeed, Allah has certain places where He loves to be supplicated), 'fayastajibu liman da'ahu' (so that He may answer the one who prays to Him), 'wal-ha'iru minha' (and the shrine of Imam al-Husayn is one of those places). Three points emerge from this Hadith: First, sending someone for Ziyarat on one's behalf is the Sunnah of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.). Second, it is proven that we can perform Ziyarat on behalf of our Imam of the Time. Third, since Karbala is the land where Allah answers prayers, whenever we are blessed with the opportunity to go to Karbala, our first prayer should be: 'Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyikal faraj' (O Allah, hasten the reappearance of your Wali). O Allah, for the sake of the land of Karbala, hasten the reappearance of our Imam. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Zaaireen-e-Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Ek Khaas Fazeelat | Arbaeen 2025
excerpt: This lecture highlights the unique spiritual status and rewards granted to the pilgrims (Zaaireen) of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Based on a narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), it explains that these pilgrims will be granted entry into Paradise forty years before the rest of humanity. The discourse emphasizes the immense virtue associated with performing Ziyarat, particularly in the context of the Day of Judgment.
content:
Whoever wants to enter Paradise 40 years before others, let him go for Ziyarat. Abdullah ibn Zurarah says, I heard Aba Abdullah Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) saying: 'Indeed, on the Day of Judgment, the pilgrims of Imam Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.) will have a special excellence over other people.' Abdullah ibn Zurarah asked, 'What is their excellence?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'They will enter Paradise 40 years before other people, while all other people will still be in the stages of reckoning and the Day of Judgment.'
