And Kazim brother, it is necessary to tell our viewers that this Hadith does not stop here, but continues further and goes up to Ali (a.s.) and the descendants of Ali (a.s.). Indeed. Just as in Hadith al-Thaqalayn, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made it clear that I am leaving behind two weighty things among you. One is the Book of Allah, and the other is my Itrat (progeny), and if the Book of Allah is present today, then the presence of the Itrat is a condition. Wow, wow, wow, wow, Subhan Allah. Indeed, a very powerful conclusion. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Sadiq al-Musaddaq—whose truthfulness Allah has guaranteed in the Quran—and in the light of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, holding fast to the Quran and Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is obligatory until the Day of Judgment, and this holding fast, this Wilayah, this loyalty leads a person to success in this world and the hereafter. Indeed, indeed, indeed. So we should remain loyal to our and your last Imam, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), in this era, we should stay connected to him, and keep his Wilayah alive in our hearts so that Allah fulfills His promise. On the Day of Judgment, as the sentences of the Hadith say, Allah says: 'You fulfill your promise regarding the Wilayah of Ali that We have given you; We will fulfill Our promise to give you Paradise.' So viewers, an excellent Hadith, a powerful Hadith was presented to us, through which we understood that from Prophet Adam (a.s.) to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and then from Ali (a.s.) to Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), in every era, the Hujjah of Allah informed all people about the loyalty to the coming Hujjah, and commanded the people of their time to remain loyal to the coming Hujjah. Meaning, it is obligatory upon the people of every era to hold fast to their Imam of the time, their Prophet of the time, or their Messenger of the time, the Hujjah of Allah, and remain loyal. So now the question arises, how should one be loyal? What is the way to be loyal? What should we do so that it is proven that we are loyal Shias of the Aale Muhammad (a.s.) and Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.)? We want to know from our brother about this, what we should do? What are the things we should perform so that we can write our names in the list of the loyal ones? Yes, Abul-Hasan brother. This is truly a matter of great pride for us, Alhamdulillah, that we are the only nation whose faith is alive. And no one else has an Imam present in this era, and we are the only ones who can act upon all those verses and all those Hadiths that we presented for the viewers. Although, I would like to say one thing here, that the Imam is truly the Imam of everyone. The issue is that people do not accept it. Because the Imam of the time is the Imam of every person, the Imam of the entire universe. Yes, you are absolutely right. And the misfortune is that people do not accept it. The Imam is for everyone, but the honor of loyalty is only attained by us. Yes, Alhamdulillah. Because they do not even know who the Imam is, so to whom should they be loyal? And Muslims should feel regret that who are these verses addressing? When these verses are present in the Holy Quran, then in today's era, towards whom is the Almighty Allah pointing regarding loyalty, that to whom should they perform loyalty? The reason for this is also that people have left the door of Aale Muhammad (a.s.), so they have the Quran, but obviously, if they ask the Quran to explain, no voice will come from the Quran. Indeed, indeed, indeed. It is the soul of the Quran. Indeed. So, Abul-Hasan brother, let us present to the viewers how we can be loyal to the Imam and how we can perform the Bay'ah (allegiance) to the Imam. In this regard, we want to present two points from the famous book 'Mikyal al-Makarim' by Ayatollah Sayyid Muhammad Taqi Musawi Isfahani, in which he has explained how you can be loyal to the Imam of your time and how you can perform Bay'ah to him. The first point he mentions is that a person should make an intention. This is the most important point because the foundation of all actions depends on the intention. So, the first point he brings in this book is that a person should first intend that he will obey his Imam. It is very important to make this intention because until a person makes an intention, he will never do it. So, a person should first intend that he will obey and remain steadfast on it. He will remain steadfast on the obedience of the Infallible Imams (a.s.) and will help and support the Imam with his life and wealth. This intention is necessary. It is not necessary that the Imam has appeared today. The Imam is in occultation, but this intention is necessary that I will obey the Imam, remain steadfast, and support the Imam with my life and wealth. This is very necessary, this is a very important point that Sayyid Muhammad Taqi Musawi Isfahani (may Allah have mercy on him) is bringing in this book. The second point he mentions in his book is to express all these things with the tongue. This is a very important matter because until you express these things with your tongue, your coming generations will not know. You have to tell them. You have to give this message to the people. You have to pass it on to your generations that you should obey your Imam, remain steadfast in his obedience, and protect and support him with your life and wealth. So, expressing it with the tongue is very necessary, and do not just express it with the tongue, but also prove your loyalty through the obedience of the Imam in this era of occultation. Meaning, it is not just to be stated with the tongue. One will have to come forward in the field of action and present proof of obedience to the Imam in the court of the Imam, saying, 'O Mawla, I am not just making this covenant with my tongue, I am not just doing your Bay'ah, but I am also ready to support and help you in the field of action.' Meaning, Wilayah is not something to be hidden in the heart. We have to acknowledge and express this Wilayah with our tongue and also with our actions. Yes, so let us tell our viewers one more point: the intention is related to the heart, and everyone did Bay'ah at the hand of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) at Ghadir-e-Khumm, but no one knew the state of anyone's heart. Later, everyone deviated, later everyone turned away from the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). But here, the matter will not be like that. The matter of Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) is the opposite of this, that the Imam knows the states of the hearts, and when he appears, one will receive reward and recompense according to the state of his heart and his intention. This is an important point, that we should make the intention to help and support the Imam, and that intention should not just be an intention, but we should express it and put it into practice. Yes. Abul-Hasan brother, it is also necessary to know how we should renew our covenant. Yes, and in this regard, the Infallible Imams (a.s.) have emphasized supplications to us. Alright? Like the famous and well-known Dua, Dua-e-Ahad. Yes, that if any believer—Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states—whoever recites this Dua for 40 days after the Fajr prayer will be among the helpers and supporters of our Mahdi, and if this person dies before the reappearance, he will be raised from his grave after the reappearance so that he can support and help Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). So, it means if someone is reciting this Dua-e-Ahad for 40 days, then he will be counted among the companions of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Alright? So, there is an important phrase in this Dua through which we renew our covenant. Right? Just as when you perform Bay'ah, you renew your covenant or Bay'ah with Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) daily after the Fajr prayer with these sentences, which we repeat again and again in this Dua. Whenever you recite it after every Fajr prayer, this repetition is happening with these sentences. Alright? And with these sentences, you are renewing your Bay'ah with Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). What are those sentences? 'Allahumma inni ujaddidu lahu fi sabihathi yawmi hadha wa ma ishtu min ayyami ahdan wa aqdan wa bay'atan lahu fi unuqi la ahulu 'anha wa la azulu abada.' With these sentences, you are renewing your Bay'ah with Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). Indeed. And besides this, a Dua that Allama Majlisi (may Allah have mercy on him) has mentioned in his book 'Bihar al-Anwar' is very powerful. Just this thing, this Dua is being brought by Allama Majlisi (may Allah have mercy on him), in which the sentences of the Dua are: 'Allahumma balligh Mawlaya Sahib al-Zaman salawatullahi alayh.' And Allama Majlisi says a powerful thing regarding this Dua, that 'I have seen in some old books'—Allama Majlisi is speaking about himself—'that after reciting this Dua, we should place our right hand on our left hand, as if we are performing Bay'ah on the hands of our Imam.' With this imagination, with this imagination, and when... this method of Bay'ah is the interpretation of that Bay'ah, Abul-Hasan brother, which was performed at Ghadir-e-Khumm at the hands of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), so it seems as if through this Dua, we are performing Bay'ah on the hands of our Imam of the time, that 'O Mawla, we will never leave your side,' and daily in Dua-e-Ahad, we also say the same thing, that 'O Mawla, the world may leave us, but we will not leave your side.' Indeed, we should truly pray, 'O Lord, by the sake of Imam al-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), grant us the ability to support and help the Imam of our time, and always grant us the ability to remain loyal and hold fast to him.' And Kazim brother, there is another way of loyalty, and that is to remain a slave of the Imam. Indeed, indeed, when the Imam is our master, then we are the slaves of the Imam. He is the Imam, we are the followers. He is the Mawla, and we are his followers. Yes, sir, and this is not something we made, it is the system of Allah. Yes, sir. Now, the point here is that whenever we get the honor of visiting Samarra, we should understand that we are not just going to the Zarih, but we are going to the house of our Imam, and in that Bay'ah, we have to enter in the capacity of a slave of the Imam. Meaning, one must go with the understanding that the Imam is present and we are presenting ourselves before him. Yes, and that is why we recite the 'Idhn' (permission) because when a slave enters the master's house, he must seek permission first. Indeed, without permission, a slave has no status to enter the master's house. We do not even have the worth to enter the house of the Imam (a.s.) without permission. That is true. Now, sometimes people say that if someone says this, it is 'Ghulu' (exaggeration). But this has no connection to 'Ghulu', because Allah has appointed them as a 'Hujjah' (proof) over us. Indeed, and Allah Himself has appointed them as our Wali and Mawla, as the Messenger of Allah said at Ghadir-e-Khumm. Therefore, in the light of Hadith-e-Thaqalayn, they are our Imam-e-Waqt (Imam of the time), the Imam-e-Barhaq (the true Imam), and it is our responsibility to live our lives as their slaves so that a slave can express his loyalty to his master and remain a loyal servant of his master. And sir, here we would also like to say that when we go to the shrines of the Ahl-e-Muhammad (a.s.), along with the 'Idhn', when we perform 'Sajdah-e-Tazeemi' (prostration of respect) there, this is also a way of saying, 'Master, we are slaves and you are the master,' which is why we perform Sajdah-e-Tazeemi there. That is correct. Indeed, indeed. And Abul Hasan brother, regarding the Sajdah-e-Tazeemi you mentioned, in that same context, there is a Hadith of Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) where he says that if Allah had not made our obedience and our Wilayah obligatory, and had not commanded us to love you, we would never have let you stand at our door, nor would we have given you permission to enter our houses. Indeed, by God, we never speak out of our own whims or opinions. We say nothing except what our Lord says, and His principles are preserved with us just as these people keep gold and silver preserved with them. Sir, you narrated a wonderful Hadith; it truly gladdened the heart and also made the viewers realize that as long as the spirit of slavery remains within a person, they will keep getting closer to the Ahl-e-Muhammad. The more we humble ourselves and present ourselves as slaves, the more exalted we will become before the Ahl-e-Muhammad (a.s.). And among our responsibilities, this is one: that we present ourselves as excellent slaves who remain completely loyal to their master, and we obey the commands of the Ahl-e-Muhammad (a.s.). Obeying the command means acquiring knowledge of the Holy Quran and the traditions, because this is the 'Thaqalayn' (two weighty things) that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) commanded us to hold onto in the Hadith-e-Thaqalayn. So, viewers, with this, our program ends here. We hope that through this program, we have conveyed a few points regarding the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) to you, and that you have also participated in the quiz related to this program and given the correct answers to all the questions. chapters.title: Introduction to Panah-e-Kainat Grand Quiz
chapters.summary: The Strong Rooh Team introduces a quiz event focused on the Occultation and loyalty to Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) to strengthen the faith of the youth.

chapters.title: Understanding the Concept of Ghaybat
chapters.summary: The speakers explain the concept of Ghaybat (occultation) through the traditions of the Infallible Imams and the parallels found in the lives of previous Prophets.

chapters.title: Historical Precedents of Occultation

chapters.title: The Benefit of the Hidden Imam
chapters.summary: The speakers address the common objection regarding the utility of a hidden Imam by explaining that the concept of Imamate is foundational to understanding the necessity of the Hujjat.

chapters.title: The Hadith of the Sun Behind Clouds
chapters.summary: Using the famous analogy provided by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the speakers explain how believers derive spiritual benefit and light from the hidden Imam just as one benefits from the sun behind clouds.

chapters.title: Responsibilities of the Believer
chapters.summary: The section concludes by emphasizing that the existence of the Imam sustains the universe, placing a profound responsibility of loyalty and adherence to Wilayah upon the believers.

chapters.title: Loyalty to the Imam in Occultation
chapters.summary: The speakers clarify that loyalty to Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is a current responsibility for all believers, not just a future obligation after his reappearance.

chapters.title: Quranic Foundations of Covenant and Loyalty
chapters.summary: An analysis of Quranic terms like Wafa, Ahad, Mithaq, and Bay'ah, explaining how they relate to the divine covenant of Wilayah.

chapters.title: The Significance of Wilayah and Imamate
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss traditions from Al-Kafi and other sources emphasizing that fulfilling the covenant of Wilayah is the most critical obligation for the Ummah.

chapters.title: Prophetic Traditions on Succession and Loyalty
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights how previous Prophets established succession and loyalty, leading to the Messenger of Allah's (s.a.w.a.) final instructions regarding his own successors.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Wilayah Across Generations
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the historical continuity of the covenant of Wilayah from Prophet Adam (a.s.) to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), emphasizing the obligation to remain loyal to the Hujjah of the time.

chapters.title: Practical Loyalty to the Imam of the Time

chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the spiritual duty of believers to approach the Imam of the Time as humble slaves, emphasizing the necessity of seeking permission and maintaining loyalty.

title: 1st Shawwal | 🌙 Eid al-Fitr Mubarak 🌙 | The Strong Rope (عليه السلام) team
excerpt: This lecture reflects on the spiritual significance of bidding farewell to the holy month of Ramadan as expressed by Imam Sajjad (a.s.). It emphasizes the sadness of the month's departure and the importance of viewing it as a bond of salvation. The talk concludes with a supplication to Allah, invoking the intercession of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) to grant believers a true and meaningful Eid celebration.
content:
Hazrat Imam Sajjad (a.s.), while bidding farewell to the blessed month of Ramadan, used to say: 'We bid farewell to it as one whose departure is heavy for us, whose leaving makes us sad and lonely. It was a rope of salvation, a bond of sanctity, and a fulfiller of rights... and we say, Peace be upon you, O greatest month of Allah. O God, O Lord, I beseech You by this passed great and blessed month, by Your final intercession, and by our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.), so that we may celebrate a true Eid with him.'

title: Ep#02 | Musalmaan Aur 12 Imam Ka Aqeeda
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological significance of the Twelve Imams within the context of Islamic tradition. The speaker examines authentic hadiths found in prominent Sunni sources, such as Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, which reference twelve Caliphs or leaders from Quraish. By analyzing these narrations, the lecture argues that these references align with the Shia Ithna Ashari belief in the twelve divinely appointed Imams. The presentation concludes that the concept of twelve successors is well-documented across Islamic scholarship.
content:
From the beginning... I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and blessings be upon the Prophet and his family. Respected viewers, peace be upon you. In the first episode, we saw that the status of the Caliphate is considered a fundamental pillar according to the Ahl-e-Sunnah, and whoever denies it is criticized. In today's episode, we will try to understand what the stance of Muslims is regarding the Twelve Imams. The book 'Muntakhab al-Athar' by Safi Golpaygani, page 145, cites authentic hadiths from the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah. If a person reflects on these hadiths regarding the number of Imams or Caliphs, it will become clear to him that the twelve Imams mentioned in these hadiths are only and only the Shia Ithna Ashari Imams, who possess the twelve Imams. It is noteworthy that this is not just about twelve people, but about twelve such successors because of whom the religion of Islam will remain mighty, the religion of Islam will get honor, and the group that did not make the number twelve a condition for the Imams and Caliphs of the Messenger... For those who did not make the number twelve a condition for the Imams and Caliphs of the Messenger, these hadiths have become a cause of only astonishment and trouble, and they do not even have a correct interpretation of these hadiths. This hadith is famous and is present in the books of both sects. The version of the hadith that we are going to present is present in Sunan Abi Dawud: 'Samitu Rasulallahi (s.a.w.a.) yaqulu la yazalud-dinu qaiman hatta takuna ithna ashara khalifa.' This religion will always remain established as long as there are twelve Caliphs. The interesting and noteworthy thing is that the topic under which this hadith is brought in Sunan Abi Dawud is titled 'Kitab al-Mahdi', and with a slight difference in words, this same hadith is present in the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah. For example, Muslim has written in his book, Sahih Muslim, 'Kulluhum min Quraish' (all of them will be from Quraish). This same hadith is present in... Hafiz Sulaiman Qanduzi says the twelve Caliphs are from the Bani Hashim. This hadith in Sahih Bukhari... In Sahih Bukhari, it is stated in this way: 'Yaqunu ithna ashara amiran, kulluhum min Quraish' (There will be twelve leaders in this Ummah, all of them from Quraish). This hadith 'Ithna ashara amiran min Quraish' (12 leaders from Quraish) has been narrated by Tabarani in his 'Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir'. It is worth mentioning that Tabarani in 'Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir' has narrated this hadith... with the words 'Ithna ashara khalifatan, kulluhum min Quraish' (12 Caliphs, all from Quraish). In this way, this type of hadith is narrated from various sources, the authentic interpretations of which are found in the books. After this, Abdullah bin Mas'ud is seen stating this same number. This is the total of 12. From Abdullah bin Mas'ud, whose title is like this: '12 Imams from Quraish, 12 Caliphs, leaders of Bani Israel'. And another narrator who is considered authentic by the Ahl-e-Sunnah, whose name is Anas bin Malik, from him 6 hadiths were narrated, and these 6 hadiths... From him, 6 hadiths were narrated, and these 6 hadiths with these titles: 12 individuals from Quraish, 12 Imams from Quraish, 12 Imams from Quraish, 12 Caliphs from us, 12 Imams, leaders of Bani Israel. In total, 70 hadiths, the majority of which are present in the authentic books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, such as Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, etc. These 12 Imams were sometimes referred to as Caliphs, sometimes as Amirs, Qayyum, Hakim, individuals, Wali, Imam, and all of them from Quraish or leaders of Bani Israel. From these hadiths, it can certainly be concluded that the mention of these 12 Imams is present in the authentic books of Muslims, and this is not a new thing for Muslims. May Allah bless Muhammad and his family... [Poetry/Chanting]... The medium of love, now there is no separation... [Music]...

title: Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.)  Ki Baddua Ka Anjaam
excerpt: This lecture recounts a historical event involving Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) and the Abbasid Caliph Mutawakkil. When forced to walk in a humiliating procession, the Imam compared his status to the she-camel of Prophet Salih, signaling divine retribution for his oppressors. A knowledgeable companion correctly interpreted this as a prophecy of Mutawakkil's imminent destruction, which occurred within three days. The lecture highlights the power of the Imam's supplication against those who exceed the limits of oppression.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. There was a follower of Imam al-Naqi (a.s.) named Zurafa. Zurafa worked as a guard inside the palace of Mutawakkil. Mutawakkil loved a special man of his named Fath ibn Khaqan very much and wanted to manifest his honor and status among the people. To fulfill this, Mutawakkil ordered all his nobles, ministers, and officials to walk in a procession on foot, and he forcibly compelled Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) to walk in this crowd as well. Zurafa saw that the Imam was drenched in sweat and exhausted from walking. He approached the Imam, took his hand, and said, 'Master, I am in great pain because of the hardship and trouble these oppressors are causing you.' Zurafa says that the Imam (a.s.) held my hand, stood up with my support, and said, 'O Zurafa, my rank and status before Allah is not less than the she-camel of Prophet Salih; in fact, it is greater.' Zurafa says I kept talking to the Imam until Mutawakkil reached his palace, dismounted, and went inside. Those who were with him also went to their homes, and the Imam (a.s.) also rode his mount and went to his house. Zurafa says my son had a teacher who was a lover of the Ahlulbayt, possessed knowledge and virtue, and understood the Imam's hints. It was my habit to sit with him during meals. During this time, when I narrated this incident to him and repeated the Imam's words, 'The she-camel of Prophet Salih is not of greater value before Allah than my status,' as soon as he heard this, he immediately stopped eating and said to me, 'By God, did you hear this sentence from the Imam yourself?' I said, 'Yes, I heard this sentence from the Imam myself.' He said, 'Be certain, Mutawakkil will not live in his kingdom for more than three days and he will be destroyed.' 'Set your affairs in order. Keep the things that need to be secured safe so that you do not face any trouble.' I asked, 'How are you so sure?' He said, 'Have you not read the story of Prophet Salih's she-camel in the Quran? "Tamatta'u fi darikum thalathata ayyamin dhalika wa'dun ghayru makdhub" (Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise that will not be belied). And the word of the Imam (a.s.) is never false.' Zurafa says, by God, the third day had not even passed when Muntasir, Bugha, and Wasi Turk, along with soldiers, attacked Mutawakkil's palace and killed Fath ibn Khaqan and Mutawakkil, and cut their bodies into so many pieces that it could not be identified whose piece was whose, and thus Allah ended his kingdom and blessings. After this, I went to the service of the Imam (a.s.) and narrated the whole incident to him. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'He spoke the truth.' When the oppression and suffering against me exceeded all limits, I turned to those treasures of my ancestors that I inherited, which are more powerful than any fortresses or weapons, and that is the curse of the oppressed against the oppressor. Then I prayed against him, and Allah destroyed him. We pray to Allah to keep our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.s.), in His protection and safety. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This lecture highlights specific titles attributed to Imam Ali (a.s.) by the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) as recorded in Sunni scholarly works. The speaker references Nuruddin Haythami's 'Majma' al-Zawa'id' to establish that Imam Ali was designated as the Siddiq-e-Akbar and Farooq-e-Ummah. The talk emphasizes the historical and spiritual significance of these titles and the Prophet's personal affection for the kunyat 'Abu Turab'.
content:
A very great scholar of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, Nuruddin Haythami, wrote a book called 'Majma' al-Zawa'id'. In it, he narrates a hadith that is present in both Shia and Sunni sources, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) held the hand of Mawla Ali (a.s.) and introduced him, saying: 'This is the one who was the first to believe in me, and this is the person who will be the first to shake hands with me on the Day of Judgment. And this is the Siddiq-e-Akbar, this is the Farooq-e-Ummah, this is the Amir al-Mu'minin.' Farooq means the one who will distinguish between truth and falsehood. So, the book I just mentioned, 'Majma' al-Zawa'id', in it, Mawla Ali's kunyat 'Abu Turab' is mentioned, where he states that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself called Mawla Ali 'Abu Turab', and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) liked this 'Abu Turab' very much, and Mawla Ali (a.s.) used to be happy when someone called him by the kunyat of Abu Turab.

title: Dua-e-Ahad Ka Sab Se Badaa Faayda | ⛅ IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound spiritual significance of reciting Dua-e-Ahad for forty consecutive days. The speaker explains that this prayer serves as a pledge of allegiance to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), ensuring that the reciter will be resurrected to support the Imam upon his reappearance. The talk emphasizes that this return will facilitate divine justice and revenge for the historical injustices faced by Imam al-Husayn and Hazrat Fatima Zahra.
content:
As a mourner, we should be committed to Dua-e-Ahad. Whoever recites this prayer after Fajr prayers for 40 days, even if they pass away from this world, when the Imam (a.s.) reappears, this person will be brought out of their grave. And this is a sentence from Dua-e-Ahad: 'Allahumma in hala bayni wa baynahul mawt' (O Lord, if death comes between me and the reappearance of the Imam), 'fa-akhrijni min qabri' (O Lord, bring me out of my grave), 'mu'taziran kafani' (wrapped in my shroud), 'shahiran sayfi' (with my sword in my hand), 'mujarridan qanati' (with my spear in my hands). This means this revenge is for Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), and another special revenge that will occur after the Imam's reappearance will be for the oppression inflicted upon the Princess of the Worlds, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), which will also happen after the reappearance. This will take place in that era when the enemies will be brought back to life. When they are brought back to life, only then will revenge be taken. Therefore, the return of those people is certain, and the revenge for all the atrocities they committed is also certain. He will receive the command for reappearance from the Lord one day, he will show the style of Haider one day, he will come with Zulfiqar one day, he will show everyone their place one day, he will show everyone their place one day; the heir of the Prophet is sitting in occultation, he will come and take the revenge for the blood.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 12 | Tafseer of Surah at-Tauheed (Surah # 112) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture provides a theological exploration of Surah al-Ikhlas, focusing on the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God). The speaker utilizes narrations from Imam Ali (a.s.) and Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) to clarify that God's unity is not numerical or categorical, but rather an indivisible, unique essence. The session emphasizes that Allah transcends human imagination, senses, and physical limitations.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the best of His creation, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and his pure and purified progeny. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the One, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is His servant and messenger. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, 'He is Allah, [who is] One.' Peace be upon you. Once again, I am here with a new clip. Before this, I had made statements regarding what one should do when entering their home, and how reciting Surah al-Ikhlas not only brings blessings to the home but also improves the relationship between the spouses and provides comfort in times of pain and suffering. Today, we will proceed with its translation and commentary. Today, we will proceed with its translation and commentary. First, I will present the meaning of 'Qul Huwallahu Ahad'—say, 'He is Allah, the One.' He has not begotten anyone, nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. Now, let us move to the commentary. Imam Ali (a.s.) said that the meaning of 'Allah' is a deity who is worshipped, and hearts are filled with love and awe for Him. Allah is the One who is hidden from the perception of eyes and is beyond the reach of human imagination. Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) states that 'Al-Ahad' and 'Al-Wahid' have the same meaning; He is a unique Being who has no equal or peer. His oneness is His unity and uniqueness. Therefore, it is mentioned that 'Wahid' is not a number, but rather the foundation of numbers; the sequence of numbers begins with it. It is the foundation of numbers. Based on this, 'Al-Ahad' means the Worshipped One, whose essence is beyond human comprehension and whose nature is beyond description. The meaning is that He is unique in His unity and transcends the attributes of created beings. This topic of Tawhid (monotheism) is quite vast. Once, in a battlefield, a man stood up and asked the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (a.s.), 'You say that God is One; what is the meaning of One?' Some people attacked him from all sides, saying, 'Do you not see this is a battlefield? Is this a place for such questions? Do you not see the Commander of the Faithful is busy solving problems?' But Imam Ali (a.s.) said, 'Leave him alone, for what he seeks, we seek from our enemies. He is asking about Tawhid, and we are inviting our opponents to the word of Tawhid.' Then, addressing the man, he said, 'O man, those who say God is one, there can be four meanings, two of which are correct for God and two are not. Among those that are not correct...' Among those that are not correct, one is that it is a numerical 'one'. This is not applicable to God, because saying He is one in a numerical sense implies the possibility of a second, even if it does not exist. However, it is an established fact that regarding the essence of Allah, the imagination of a second is impossible, because He who has no peer does not enter into the category of numbers. Do you not see that God condemned those who said, 'Allah is the third of three'? The second meaning that is not correct for God is that He is one in the sense of a species, for example, saying that a certain man is 'one of the people'—meaning there are many people and he is one of them. This is not correct for Allah because Allah is not a genus or a species, and God is far above any comparison or likeness. Now, as for the two meanings that are correct regarding God, the first is that it is said that God is One, meaning... It is said that God is One, meaning that in the universe, He has no likeness. Yes, our Lord is indeed like this. The second meaning is that our Lord is One, meaning His essence is indivisible; He cannot be divided, neither in reality, nor in imagination, nor in thought. Yes, the Almighty God is indeed like this. Thus, it is known that God is One and Unique; He is not 'one' in the sense of a numerical or species-based unity, but rather in the sense of the unity of His essence. He has no equal or peer. In this regard, I present a hadith for your benefit, which Mawla Ali (a.s.) stated regarding Tawhid: 'He is One, but not by number; He is Eternal, but not by the passage of time; He is standing, but not by the support of pillars; He is understood by hearts and minds, but not through the senses; He is known through His signs, and the seen world testifies to Him, but not by His physical presence.' No one can explain it more simply than the Master of the Faithful. No one can explain it more simply than the Master of the Faithful has explained Tawhid to us. There are other hadiths of Mawla Ali (a.s.) in which he has explained the Oneness of that Lord. Let me bring another hadith before you. He says, 'All praise is due to Allah, who existed before the earth, the heavens, and the throne. He will remain as He is. He cannot be known through senses, nor can His greatness be estimated through imagination. No one can compare Him to another. If someone asks about Him, it is not like asking about a human where the answer might change or be diverted. God is not like that. God's attention is towards everyone; He is not distracted. No one can diminish His giving or His blessings. He cannot be seen through eyes, nor can He be felt in a physical place. His description is not possible through any means. He does not act through any intermediary; He does whatever He wills. He cannot be perceived through the senses...' He cannot be perceived through the senses, nor can He be understood through human interaction. Dear viewers, these hadiths that I have presented to you are from the book 'Nahj al-Balagha', which contains the sermons and hadiths of the Commander of the Faithful. If you wish to see more hadiths, you can look at this book; you will find these hadiths regarding Tawhid there. So, dear viewers, we conclude our discussion here. God willing, the next discussion will be in the next clip. Until then, goodbye. And all praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

title: Jo Ziyaarat Par Nahin Jaa Sakey [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the feelings of disappointment experienced by believers who intend to visit the shrine of Imam Husayn (a.s.) but are unable to do so due to illness or other obstacles. The speaker cites a reliable hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) to explain that those who prepare for Ziyarat but cannot travel still receive immense spiritual rewards. By supporting the journey of others or serving pilgrims, one can remain connected to the blessings of Karbala and have their calamities removed.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon Muhammad and his pure progeny. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Many times it happens that a person is a believer, has all the means to go for Ziyarat, and has the intention to visit the shrine of the Prince (a.s.), but due to some preoccupation, illness, or some other reason, he cannot go. Should such a person be disappointed? No, do not be disappointed. Note this hadith, because even without going for Ziyarat, one can participate in the reward of those who go. In a reliable hadith, Safwan al-Jammal narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) about what reward one gets for praying near the holy grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Whoever prays two rak'ats of prayer there and then asks Allah for whatever he wishes, Allah will surely grant it.' Safwan asked again... Safwan asked again, 'What about the one who performs Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates and goes to their graves?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'If he performs Ghusl with the intention of Ziyarat, his sins will be washed away, and he will become as pure as the day he was born.' Then Safwan asked, 'What about the one who prepared to go for Ziyarat but could not go due to some reason?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'For every dirham he spent in this path, Allah will grant him the reward equivalent to the mountain of Uhud, and whatever he spent, He will return to him much more. The calamities that were to descend upon him will be removed, and his wealth will be protected.' If we reflect on this hadith, every person who cannot go for Ziyarat due to a valid reason can still participate in the reward by spending in this path, whether by helping with the arrangements for Ziyarat, serving other pilgrims in any way, or by sending someone else for Ziyarat who is not able to afford it. Or by sending someone else for Ziyarat who is not able to afford it. The effort should be that we remain connected to the Ziyarat of Hazrat Abdullah al-Husayn (a.s.) in some way. It is said that when the followers of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) are yearning to go to Karbala, and they cannot go for some reason, then by serving the pilgrims, they become the recipients of this hadith. Amen, O Lord of the worlds.

The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in any hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first; the only condition for the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear in today's winners or if an episode was missed, there is no need to be disappointed, because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the pilgrimage to Iraq, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all questions in 7 out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone did not become a daily winner, but has given correct answers in 7 out of 12 episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Iraq pilgrimage. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, al-Hujjah ibn al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali al-'Asr, help us, do not let us perish. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Regarding the glory, honor, status, and greatness of Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.), it is enough to say that the Lord of the Worlds made you the means for the advent of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and you were declared the trustee of this light. Who will fill the world with justice and fairness just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.) belonged to the lineage of the granddaughter of the Caesar of Rome on her father Joshua's side, and on her mother's side, she belonged to the lineage of Janabe Sham'un, the successor of Prophet Isa (a.s.). Historians have described the account of her arrival in the household of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in such a way that there was a slave trader named Bishr bin Sulayman in the lineage of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, a companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), who was also a companion of Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) and his neighbor in Samarra. He says that one day Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) summoned me through his slave Kafur and said, 'O Bishr, you are from the lineage of the Ansar, the blood of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari flows in your veins, so I have full trust in your love, friendship, and loyalty to us. I have summoned you for a special task, and that honor relates to the purchase of a slave girl, for which I want to send you.' 'Can you perform this task secretly?' I said, 'Master, my life be sacrificed for you, give me the command.' After this, the Imam (a.s.) handed me a letter written in the Roman language along with a bag of 200 gold coins and said, 'Take this and go to Baghdad. When you reach the western bank of the Euphrates River there, you will see some boats of slave traders, and there will be some slave girls for sale, around whom a crowd of Arab buyers, young leaders, and agents of the Banu Abbas will gather. Among those slave traders, a man named Umar bin Yazid will be present, in whose boat there will be a veiled slave girl, and she will not be ready to go with anyone. So much so that one of the agents of the Banu Abbas will say to Umar bin Yazid to sell this slave girl to me for 300 dinars. Hearing these words from his tongue, the slave girl will address him in Arabic and say, 'O man, even if you place the throne and crown of Solomon son of David at my feet, I still cannot incline towards you.' Upon this answer of the slave girl, Umar bin Yazid will be disappointed and will say to her that whenever a buyer turns towards you, you flatly refuse to go with him. Finally, what method should I adopt? In response, the slave girl replied, "O Umar bin Yazid, do not be anxious or hasty in this matter. The buyer I am waiting for will soon speak to you about me. O Bishr, at that time, give my letter to that slave trader and say that there is a letter from a Sayyid addressed to this slave girl. Give it to her so that if she reads it and agrees, I am the representative on his behalf for the purchase." Bishr says that when Umar bin Yazid, the slave trader, gave that letter to that noble lady and she read it, her eyes filled with tears. She told Umar bin Yazid that she was willing to go with this person. Finally, the deal was settled for the same amount of gold coins that the Imam (a.s.) had given, and after paying the price, I took this noble lady with me to my residence. I saw that she was extremely happy, pressing the letter to her eyes and kissing it. I asked her, why such attachment and devotion to the letter of a person you do not even know? In response, she said, "O Bishr, your gnostic insight is still incomplete. Listen to my story. My name is Malika. I am the daughter of Yeshua and the granddaughter of the Caesar of Rome. My mother's lineage traces back to Janabe Shamun (a.s.), the successor of Isa (a.s.). I want to inform you of a strange matter, which is that when I was 13 years old, my grandfather, the Caesar of Rome, wanted to marry me to his nephew. Consequently, he gathered 300 disciples of Isa, 300 scholars of the Christians, 700 dignitaries, and 4,000 army commanders. He had a throne brought that was set on 40 pillars, which he decorated with diamonds and jewels and placed on an elevation. He seated his nephew on that throne and ordered the priests to perform the wedding rituals. The rituals had just begun when an earthquake struck the royal palace. All the idols fell to the ground, all the pillars of the throne shattered, and the groom also fell from the throne and became unconscious. A state of fear and terror gripped all the priests. They said to the Caesar of Rome, "O King! Forgive us from performing these rituals." Saddened by this excuse from the Christian scholars, my grandfather said, "Re-erect the pillars, and this time bring the groom's brother to me so that I may marry this girl to him." Consequently, the preparations were made again, and when the Christian scholars opened the pages of the Gospel, the same incident occurred as before, and my grandfather left the place in grief. That same night, I saw in a dream that in the palace of the Caesar of Rome, where the throne was installed, Isa (a.s.) had set up a pulpit of light along with a group of his disciples. Meanwhile, the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.), his successor (a.s.), and other elders entered the palace. Isa (a.s.) stepped forward and kissed their hands. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "O Ruhullah! I have come to marry Malika, the daughter of your successor Shamun, to my son Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)." Isa (a.s.) and his disciples were made witnesses to this marriage. Isa (a.s.) looked towards Janabe Shamun and said, "It is a matter of honor for you to be connected to Muhammad al-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) through this relationship." Janabe Shamun said, "I have agreed." After this, all the gentlemen proceeded towards the pulpit. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited the marriage sermon and married me to his son, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Isa (a.s.) and his disciples were made witnesses to this marriage. After this, when I woke up, my whole body was trembling. I did not mention this dream to anyone. 14 days later, I saw in a dream that the daughter of the Prophet, Fatima Zahra (s.a.), and Maryam (s.a.) came with the houris of Paradise to inquire about my health, and Maryam (s.a.) said, "O Malika! This Sayyida is the grandmother of your husband." I held onto the hem of this Masuma (s.a.) and expressed my sorrow over Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) not coming. Upon this, she (s.a.) said, "Because you are still bound to the religion of Isa (a.s.), Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) cannot grace you with his presence. If you seek the pleasure of God, the approval of Maryam (s.a.) and Isa (a.s.), and a meeting with Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), then recite the Kalima-e-Tawhid on your tongue." I recited the Kalima-e-Tawhid, and she embraced me and said, "Now you will continue to have the vision of my son Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)." After this, I was blessed with the vision of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) in a dream. Bishr says that I asked, "How did you become included among the captives?" Bibi Narjis (s.a.) said that Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) ordered me one night that your grandfather would send an army to fight the Muslims on such and such a day. You should join the slave girls in their attire. I followed this order of the Imam and, having been captured by the Muslims, reached here, and now you see my condition, that I am moving towards my destination. Bishr says that I presented these noble ladies with great respect and honor to the service of Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) said to her, "From you, a son will be born who will fill the entire earth with justice and fairness, just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny." Bishr says that upon hearing this, the noble lady placed her forehead in prostration of gratitude. After this, Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) summoned his sister, Bibi Hakima Khatun (s.a.), and told her that this is the same lady about whom I often spoke to you. Hearing this, Hakima Khatun (s.a.) embraced Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.), and the Imam (a.s.) ordered her to acquaint these noble ladies with Islamic culture because she is the wife of Abu Muhammad (a.s.) and the mother of Mahdi-e-Akhiruzzaman (a.j.t.f.s.). Respected viewers! The incident that has just been presented to you, regarding how Janabe Narjis Khatun was brought from Rome to Baghdad and the slave through whom the Imam carried out this entire event, several objections are raised against this incident. One of these objections is that the incident of Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.) being brought to Samarra through a slave is false because no such war is mentioned in history in which a war took place between the Roman Empire and the Abbasids. Dear ones! Before answering this objection, there is an Arabic proverb that I want to present to you: "Adamu al-wijdan la yadullu 'ala 'adami al-wujud" (The lack of finding something does not indicate its non-existence). The era of Imam Hadi (a.s.) and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), which is from 828 AD to 874 AD, meaning if you study or even search on Google, you will find all these wars that took place between the Roman Empire and the Abbasids. Some of these are: the Battle of Anzen from 837 AD to 838 AD, and the Sack of Amorium in 838 AD. Among these, there are five wars that you can easily find in history. These wars occurred during the lives of the two Imams, i.e., the 10th and 11th Imams, which confirms the incident of Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.) being brought to Baghdad, and history has mentioned several naval battles between the Roman Empire and the Abbasid government. The Euphrates River extends to Turkey, and the Roman Empire's control extended to areas near or between the Euphrates River. All these things are proof that this narration is historically completely accurate. Another thing that should be remembered is that Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) was martyred in 868 AD, and this hadith occurred during the life of Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.), which says that Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.) was brought to Baghdad as a prisoner of war. So, respected viewers! To those who object, it will only be said that they have no interest in studying. They just want to object, and there are many reasons for that. The first is that they want to diminish the status of Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.), and a bigger reason is that through this, they want to deny the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). And the objection we have answered makes the whole incident clear. The purpose of narrating this incident in such detail was to describe the existence and the status and greatness of Janabe Narjis Khatun in terms of history and to give an answer to those who object, so that people can become familiar with the reality of this incident. In this way, it becomes our responsibility that if anyone objects to Janabe Narjis Khatun (s.a.) or any member of the Ahlulbayt family, it becomes our religious duty to give them a befitting reply. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. A'udhu billahi minash shaitanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Wasallallahu alaika ya waliyal asr adriknah wala tuhlikna. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum. Now the time has come for the announcement of our six lucky draw winners for today. They will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees. Their names are on your screen: Fahim Bano from Alipur, Ali Mehdi Jassani from Sangli, Mohammad Taqi Gabrani from Mumbai, Zahura Akhtar from Bargam, Syed Anees Hashmi from Alipur, Farzad Rizvi from Mumbai. Congratulations to all of you. Before you leave, let me remind you that the link for today's quiz will remain live until the end of the series. Among those who provide correct answers to all questions in at least seven out of the 12 episodes, the lucky draw winners for our mega prize—a pilgrimage to Iraq—will be announced. We are grateful to all of you for your encouragement. God willing, we will meet again tomorrow at this same time. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 1 | Tafseer of the verse بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
excerpt: This lecture provides an introductory exegesis of the phrase 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim' based on Shia traditions. It explores the spiritual significance of the phrase, its role as a shield against difficulties, and its connection to the 'Ism-e-Azam' (Greatest Name of Allah). The speaker also highlights the theological definitions of 'Allah', 'Rahman', and 'Rahim' as explained by the Imams, emphasizing the concept of turning to Allah in times of absolute despair.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin. Assalatu wassalamu ala ashrafil ambiya-i wal mursalin, wa ala alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin, wal la'natu ala a'daihim ajma'in. Amma ba'd. Respected believers, I have come before you to present the exegesis (tafsir) of 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim'. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim is a part of every Surah, and every Surah begins with it. It is also a fact that its rewards are immense. According to narrations, it is stated that in Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, there is the 'Ism-e-Azam' (The Greatest Name of Allah). Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) stated that whatever book Allah revealed from the heavens, its beginning was Bismillah. Whatever book was revealed from the heavens, its beginning was Bismillah. When Bismillah was revealed, it indicated that the previous Surah had ended and the next Surah had begun. It is also said that when you recite Bismillah, it will shield you from everything between the heavens and the earth; meaning, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim will protect you from every difficulty. In the book 'Tafsir', it is narrated from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that he said: 'My forefathers narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that the Prophet said: Whoever faces a difficulty due to some matter and becomes anxious because of it—which often happens, as one does not understand if they are in grief or facing a problem, and the matter becomes common—and they find no way out of that anxiety and are worried, then for such a person, it is best to recite Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim with sincerity and from the heart.' Recite Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim from the heart; they will definitely receive one of two things: either their need will be fulfilled in this world, or its reward will be stored for them with the Lord. And whatever is with Allah for the believers is better and more lasting. If a person loses something and wants it back, or if they are in need, what is with Allah is better and more lasting than what we have. Furthermore, in a long hadith from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), it is mentioned that after our shortcomings, if someone forgets to recite Bismillah at the beginning of a task—forgetting is common—then Allah tests them through some unpleasant incident, something they dislike, so that they may be turned towards Him and the mistake of omitting Bismillah can be rectified. The thing they dislike, which is burdensome for them, is used as a test so that they may be turned towards Allah and the mistake of omitting Bismillah can be rectified. Now, how beautiful is the exegesis of Bismillah? You stated that 'Allah' refers to the light and splendor of Allah, and 'Rahman' refers to the kingdom of Allah. And after that, 'Allah' is called the Worshipped One of everyone. 'Rahman' is the one who shows mercy to all creation, and 'Rahim' is the one who shows mercy only to the believers. The letter 'Alif' in the name 'Allah' points towards 'Ilaahi' (My God), which He has made obligatory upon the creatures through our Wilayah. The 'Lam' in 'Allah' points towards the obligation of our Wilayah upon the creatures, and the second 'Lam' in 'Allah' points towards the Wilayah of the opponents of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. It points towards the Wilayah of the opponents. 'Rahman' refers to the one who shows mercy to all the worlds, and 'Rahim' refers to the one who shows mercy to the believers. Someone asked Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) about the meaning of Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. He said: 'The word Allah is the greatest name of that Essence which is exclusive to Allah alone. No one else can be called by this name; meaning, besides Allah, no one else can be called by the name Allah.' We only say this is a matter of gnosis (irfan); no effect of this has been seen from any other being. And this name cannot be given to anyone else. Someone asked, 'Explain the exegesis of the word Allah.' He said: 'When all hopes are shattered and all means fail, in that state of despair, the one towards whom hearts turn for help is called Allah.' Just like this, a person came to Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) and complained to the Imam. He complained to the Imam, 'O Messenger of Allah, guide me regarding Allah, for the philosophers have confused me.' In response, the Imam said: 'O servant of Allah, have you ever traveled by ship?' He said, 'Yes, I have traveled by ship.' The Imam asked, 'Has it ever happened that the ship broke in the middle of the sea, and there was no other ship to save you, and swimming could not help you—meaning your swimming could not save you?' He said, 'Yes, it has happened.' The Imam asked, 'In that state, was there any hope or support in your heart that could save you from destruction?' He said, 'Yes.' Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'That is Allah, who provides salvation even where there is no salvation, and helps where there is no helper.' Respected believers, this is the exegesis of Bismillah. Besides this, there are many other narrations and traditions from different Imams and different Ma'sumin. There are narrations and traditions from different Imams and different Ma'sumin, which I am not mentioning due to the constraints of time. So, I will conclude my speech here. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin.
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim is the beginning of every revealed book and contains the Ism-e-Azam.
Reciting Bismillah with sincerity acts as a shield against worldly anxieties and difficulties.
Forgetting to say Bismillah before a task may lead to unpleasant incidents as a form of divine correction.
The name 'Allah' represents the one to whom hearts turn when all other hopes and means are exhausted.
Rahman signifies mercy to all creation, while Rahim signifies mercy specifically to the believers.
The Imams emphasize that true gnosis of Allah is found when one realizes He is the only helper in desperate situations.

title: Majlis 5 | Aamaal Ke Qubooliyat Ki Shart Wilaayat-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological necessity of Wilayah (allegiance to the Ahlulbayt) as the fundamental condition for the acceptance of all religious deeds. The speaker argues that acts of worship, such as prayer and fasting, remain incomplete and spiritually void without the recognition of the divinely appointed Imams. Furthermore, the discourse emphasizes the importance of religious honor, the rejection of disparaging historical narratives regarding the Prophets, and the necessity of Tabarra (disassociation from the enemies of the Ahlulbayt) in achieving salvation.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... [repeated]. In the service of the Shah, in the path of the Shah, I found stones, I found heat, I found thorns. I found stones, I found heat, I found thorns in the path. Then it happened that I found Haider-e-Karrar. How disgraced was the tongue in every gathering of truth, then again, I found Meesam-e-Tammar. The Ayat-e-Tatheer was very happy under the Kisa, as if it found the characters exactly as it had asked for. And we looked very far into Paradise, and found no one, only found the Azadars. And the poet has also said a critical verse: those who do Zikr-e-Ali without the envelope (sincerity/devotion), I only found a few such people in the world. Listen to the concluding verse of Musaddiq Lakhani: One day Musaddiq passed through the alley of Qambar, when the dust rose, he found the signs of Paradise. Then it happened that I found Haider-e-Karrar. May Allah have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. The best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. And the end is for the righteous and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Blessings be upon his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths. The Imam of our time, the master of our affairs, our owner, our master, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our consoler, the sufficient one for the Husseini, and the relief for the distressed and the helpless. May my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Amma Ba'd (As for what follows), Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala says in the Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'Allah has not made for any man two hearts in his breast' (Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 4). Allah has made only one heart, not two. And only one love can reside in it; no other love can enter. When one love enters, its opposite cannot. The discussion was on Wilayah and Bara'ah. Today, regarding Wilayah, I will present a few narrations as time permits. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. This narration is from Sheikh Saduq, where he narrates that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'The first thing a servant will be asked about when he stands before Allah (Jalla Jalaluhu) on the Day of Judgment is the obligatory prayers. Then about obligatory Zakat and Khums, then about obligatory fasting, then about obligatory Hajj, and then about our Wilayah, the Ahlulbayt.' See, the Imam stated this order: prayer, Khums/Zakat, fasting, Hajj, and then Wilayah. These are all obligations; we are not talking about recommended acts. Recommended acts are only for increasing reward. Only the obligatory acts will be questioned, and finally, the Imam said, 'And about our Wilayah.' If he affirms our Wilayah in this world and dies in that state, his prayers, fasting, Zakat, and Hajj will be accepted. If there is no Wilayah, none of his deeds will be accepted. So the subject is clear: Wilayah is the criterion through which all deeds are accepted. Allama Majlisi (r.a.) has a chapter in Bihar al-Anwar titled: 'Deeds are not accepted except through Wilayah.' Wilayah is the basic criterion. If that is not fulfilled, everything else is secondary. If there is no Wilayah, prayer is not prayer, fasting is not fasting, Hajj is not Hajj. Why? Because these are physical acts of worship. Prayer, fasting, Hajj, Zakat—these are all physical. The soul of all these acts of worship is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Without Wilayah, without this soul, these acts are dead. This is not just rhetoric; there is a secret behind it. Before moving forward, I must mention the scholars who have performed great services, like Sayyid Hashim Bahrani (r.a.), whose grave is in Bahrain. He wrote a book on Wilayah titled 'Nihayat al-Ikmal allati la tuqbalu al-a'malu illa biha' (The Peak of Perfection without which deeds are not accepted). He is the one who named it, not me. The book is voluminous. What is the secret? A narrator asked the Imam, 'What is common between us and others (the Ahl al-Ahwa - those who follow their own desires/opinions)?' If it were today, we might say, 'The God is one, the Quran is one, the Book is one.' But the Imam said, 'By God, there is nothing common between us and them, except that we both face the Qibla for prayer.' Except for facing the Kaaba. That is the only thing common. Why is there nothing else common? If we go into details, it will take too long. Briefly, their concept of Tawheed is different; they believe in a physical God, which is anthropomorphism (shirk), while the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) believe in absolute transcendence (Tanzih). There is no similarity, no division, no comparison. 'There is nothing like unto Him.' Imam Ali (a.s.) says in Dua al-Sabah that Allah is purified from being of the same genus as anything else. Allah is a Being with no similarity; this is Tawheed. Others believe in either Jabr (compulsion) or Tafwid (delegation), while we believe in 'a position between the two positions' (Amr bayn al-Amrayn). Those who believe in Jabr think Allah is a tyrant, and those who believe in Tafwid believe in Shirk—that Allah cannot interfere in our affairs. But the Ahlulbayt said, 'No compulsion and no delegation, but a position between the two.' Regarding Prophethood, there is a world of difference. We believe, in light of the narrations of Imam Ridha (a.s.), that the Prophet is only like humans in outward appearance, but in spiritual and divine status, there is no comparison. They claim that when the Prophet first went to the Cave of Hira for meditation, when Gabriel came, he was terrified. This is from Bukhari, I am just quoting. They say he was terrified, went home trembling to Lady Khadija, had a high fever, and was shivering. Lady Khadija said, 'Don't worry, let's take you to a soothsayer (Kahin).' They took him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal, a soothsayer of the Age of Ignorance. Waraqa looked and said, 'Oh, you are a Prophet.' So according to them, Waraqa had to confirm his Prophethood first. But our belief is that Prophets are Prophets from birth. At least you consider him superior to Prophet Isa (a.s.), don't you? 'Wastahaqqa dukhulan-nari man 'adaka'—whoever showed enmity towards you, Allah has made it obligatory upon him that he will go to Hell. Whoever showed enmity towards you. O Ali. Look, now we are talking about enmity. Now, what does enmity mean? Enmity, look, there are many ways of enmity. One enmity is that we keep enmity in our hearts. We don't show it. 'I like you, yes.' This is also enmity. One enmity is that we cannot do anything, but we speak with our tongues. We taunt, we criticize. It is actually enmity. It is not friendship. But we cannot do anything physically. That is why we speak with our tongues. One enmity is when one comes down into the battlefield. There is no enmity greater than that. This means that at the very least, whoever stepped onto the battlefield, they will definitely go to Hell. Nara-e-Haidari. Ya Ali. Before I begin the lecture, let me mention that the late Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi, the author of Abaqat al-Anwar, has brought all these traditions into Abaqat. He has included all these hadiths in Abaqat al-Anwar. His collection is truly magnificent, but unfortunately, it is a matter of regret that we did not value it. Even though he was from India, from Lucknow, we did not value him. And the Arabs had this book translated into Arabic. The Arabs. The Arabs had the hadith section of this book translated. The Quranic section has not even been printed yet, but the Arabs had the entire thing translated into Arabic. It has been printed in Arabic under the title 'Nafahat al-Azha'. It is clear, isn't it? But we did not value it. And this is how it usually happens. Often, it is just like this. Then the Prophet says: 'Ya Ali, by the One who sent me with Prophethood and made me the Chosen One over all creation, over all creation.' If a servant were to worship Allah for 1000 years, keep worshipping for 1000 years. Look, 1000 years is a very, very long time. How much do we worship? How much do we worship Allah? We haven't even finished two rak'ahs of prayer before we start waiting for the end. Here, 1000 years of worship means what? That he keeps praying all the time. He keeps praying at every moment and fasts all day long. That is what is called worship. If he keeps worshipping for 1000 years, then Allah will not accept it from him except through your Wilayah. Through your Wilayah, based on your Wilayah. If he brings Wilayah, and not just your Wilayah, but the Wilayah of the Imams from your progeny. And your Wilayah... now listen very carefully. Let's end the hadith now. And your Wilayah, O Ali, will not be accepted. O Ali, even if someone brings your Wilayah, even if they say 'Ali, Ali', their Wilayah will not be accepted until they perform Tabarra (disassociation) from your enemies. Nara-e-Haidari. Ya Ali. The enemies of the Ahlulbayt, may they be countless. And those who perform Tabarra against the enemies of the Imams from your progeny. And you are looking for 'patrons of knowledge'. What a foolish man, truly. Looking for patrons of knowledge among the Umayyads and Abbasids. Truly. I mean, we should all definitely raise our voices on this. It is incumbent upon everyone to speak on this. This pulpit, this Azadari pulpit, is saying that the Umayyads and Abbasids did great things. Look, don't just look at their evil. Strange. And the whole world is silent. Except for a few. Except for two or four individuals, that's it. And then the Prophet says: 'Jibra'il (a.s.) informed me of this.' Meaning, I am not saying this from myself. Allah is telling me through Jibra'il. 'So whoever wishes, let him believe, and whoever wishes, let him disbelieve.' Now, whoever wants to, let them believe; whoever wants to, let them commit kufr. Now, whoever wants to accept or not accept, it is in everyone's own choice. There is no problem. It is a choice. In this world, Allah has given everyone a choice. Every person is free. Okay. No problem. Anyway, because it has been quite late, I will stop here for you. Insha'Allah, the remaining hadiths will be presented to you tomorrow. That it is this very Wilayah and this very Bara'ah that was not understood, which was the reason Karbala happened. And when Imam Hussain (a.s.) decided that he would go to Karbala, you know that great companions were present there. Great companions. In Medina, in Mecca. I mean, before moving forward, let me present one thing to you. Often people say that the people of Kufa betrayed. The people of Kufa betrayed. The people of Kufa killed. Our question is, okay, the people of Kufa betrayed. They mean that the Shias killed. Okay. No problem. If you say so, then no problem. So if the people of Kufa did it, then what were the people of Medina doing? What were the people of Mecca doing? Did they not know that Imam Hussain (a.s.) was going to be martyred? Everyone knew. Everyone knew. But all these other great companions and Tabi'in who were advising Imam Hussain (a.s.) not to go. In fact, if possible, to pledge allegiance at the hands of Yazid so that there would be no conflict. Do not fight. They were all giving this advice. These are the same individuals. These are the same individuals who used to advise the Messenger of Allah, 'Do not do this, do not do that.' These are the same individuals who were advising Imam Hussain (a.s.), 'Do not do this.' And these people of Medina and these people of Mecca. These companions. These Tabi'in who were in that era. They stopped Imam Hussain (a.s.). Read the history. We are not saying this from ourselves. It is written in history. Except for a few people. And then when all the companions were martyred, one time Janabe Zainab brought her two sons to Imam Hussain (a.s.). You know that all night on the eve of Ashura, Janabe Zainab was sometimes combing the hair of one, sometimes combing the hair of the other, sometimes caressing one, sometimes caressing the other, and repeatedly saying, 'My son, look, tomorrow is the day of trial, do not leave your uncle, sacrifice yourselves for your uncle.' And she was encouraging them for martyrdom all night long. What a mother Zainab was, what a mother. All night long, and when the people were martyred, one after another, all were martyred, then Janabe Zainab brought the two boys and stood them before Imam Hussain (a.s.). Hussain asked, 'Sister, why have you come?' She said, 'You know, when everyone is being martyred, I want you to give them permission.' Hussain gave permission, the sister prepared them, Janabe Zainab prepared them, but while preparing them, she gave two pieces of advice: 'My sons, you are going, but keep two things in mind. One, fight in such a way that the wretched ones realize whose grandsons you are and whose nephew you are. And second, when you go to the battlefield, I know you are hungry and thirsty for three days, but do not turn towards the water, do not turn towards the river.' 'You know Sakina is thirsty, Asghar is thirsty, the children are thirsty, everyone has been thirsty for three days, do not turn towards it.' The children promised their mother. One brother took care of one, the other brother took care of the other, and they attacked, they attacked the Syrians in such a way that the armies began to run here and there. Once, Ibn Sa'd shouted, 'Hey, surround them and kill them, these are the children of Bani Hashim.' The wretched ones surrounded them, someone threw a stone, someone threw a spear, someone shot an arrow. Both children, one after another, fell from their horses to the ground, and called out, 'Uncle, come to our aid.' Hussain took his strong arm, took Hazrat Abbas with him, and went. By the time they reached, the souls of both brothers had departed. Hussain took the body of one, Abbas took the body of the other. Now they brought both bodies and placed them in the tent, while Janabe Zainab was on her prayer mat. I have read in the Maqtal that Janabe Zainab was on her prayer mat when Janabe Fizza came and said, 'Bibi, come, your children have arrived. Your children have arrived.' I have read that Janabe Zainab said, 'I did not ask them to come, why have they come?' Janabe Fizza said, 'Bibi, come and see that they have come in the shade.' Now when Zainab saw that on one side was the body of one, and on the other side the body of the other. If it were any other mother, she would have been devastated, but Zainab said, 'Well done, my lions, you did not shame me before my brother and my mother.' I have not seen anywhere that Janabe Zainab wept or mourned for her children. Not in Kufa, not in Sham, not even after returning to Karbala. But when Zainab reached Medina, and when Janabe Abdullah ibn Ja'far took Janabe Zainab inside the house, as soon as she entered, she entered the room where both their beds were laid out. Seeing the small beds, Zainab's heart broke. 'Woe to me, woe to Muhammad, O my lions, O my darlings, where will Zainab find you now?' 'And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned.' 'May the curse of Allah be upon the oppressive people.' O Lord, O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are troubled. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant those who are childless, righteous and pious children. Return those who are away from their homeland safely to their homes. O Lord, grant complete and immediate healing to those who are victims of this epidemic. Remove this epidemic from among us. Especially protect the lives, property, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haidar-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. Especially the Shias of Afghanistan, protect their lives, property, honor, and dignity. O Lord, protect the holy shrines and sacred places. Protect those who are protecting them. Protect the great scholars and the Maraje-e-Izam. Grant us the Ziyarat of Hussain in this world and the intercession of Hussain in the hereafter, the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: EP2 |  Tamaam Sahaaba Sitaaron Ki Tarha! - Haqeeqat Kya Hai? | GHADEER PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture critically examines the popular Hadith 'My companions are like stars' and challenges the notion of universal infallibility among the Prophet's companions. Through historical analysis and Quranic evidence, the speaker highlights instances of disobedience and moral failings among certain companions, arguing that true guidance is found in the Ahlulbayt. The session concludes by clarifying that the 'stars' metaphor applies only to those who remained steadfast in their faith, while others will be rejected at the Pond of Kawthar for their innovations.

Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are present in the discussion.
