The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all questions in any one episode. Meaning, even if someone is not among the daily winners, but has given all the correct answers in any one episode, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. Alhamdulillahil-ladhi ja'alana minal-mutamassikina bi-wilayati Ali ibni Abi Talib alayhima-salam. Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-hujjatibnil-hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma 'ajjil li-waliyyikal-faraja wal-'afiyata wan-nasra, waj'alna min khayri a'wanihi wa ansarihi wal-mustashhadina bayna yadayh. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. Assalamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh, respected viewers. The topic of our discussion is a Hadith that the Sunni brethren misuse and attempt to instill an incorrect interpretation of it into people's minds. This Hadith is used many times, repeatedly used by Sunni scholars, and is narrated from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Hadith is as follows: 'Ashabi kan-nujum, bi-ayyihim iqtadaytum ihtadaytum.' Translation: 'My companions are like stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided.' Firstly, the discussion regarding the chain of narration (sanad) of this Hadith is very technical, and we will set that aside and go directly to the discussion of the text (matn), Insha'Allah. If any viewers are interested in studying the discussion of the sanad, they should refer to the book 'Ashabi kan-Nujum' by Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Milani (hafizahullah). As far as the text of this Hadith is concerned, there are several objections. The two major objections that appear from the text of this Hadith are: the first objection or problem is that it presents all companions as a guided leader—a guide—a guided leader for the Ummah. How is it possible that every companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is a leader for the Ummah, a guide for the Ummah, when they themselves were in need of guidance? Each one of them was in need of guidance. So, how can a person who is himself in need of guidance lead others? The second objection, which is even more dangerous, is that this list of companions includes names of people who were perpetrators of major sins (gunah-e-kabira). There are people among them who were adulterers, people who committed murder, people who were attending gatherings with singing women, or people who were alcoholics. History has recorded these events. These events are recorded not only in our books but in all history books, and the names of those people are present. The names of those companions who were committing these acts are present. If we take the literal meaning of this Hadith—that every companion is like a star and whoever you follow you will be guided—then what will happen to these people? If someone follows these people, will they go towards Paradise, will they be guided towards the true Islam, or where will their guidance lead? Only Allah knows best, because among these companions are those who are adulterers, murderers, or alcoholics—and among the murderers are those who killed the family of Muhammad (a.s.) or conspired to kill the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself. History has recorded such companions as well. The list of companions includes people who were prepared to kill the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and were conspiring to kill him. So, if the Ummah follows such companions, where will it reach? Let them decide for themselves. These companions included in this list—will they lead to Paradise, will they guide towards true Islam, or will they lead their followers to Hell? Moving to the next stage of our discussion, we will try to understand through some Hadiths and Quranic verses the second objection we presented: that there were such people among the companions, and we will try to present some evidence for this. First of all, this list of companions included those who, upon hearing the news of the Prophet's death—even if it was false news—turned back on their heels and left Islam, and the Quran points towards this. Wa ma Muhammadun illa rasul, qad khalat min qablihir-rusul. Afa'in mata aw qutila inqalabtum 'ala a'qabikum? Wa man yanqalib 'ala 'aqibayhi falan yadurrallaha shay'a, wa sayajzillahu-shakirin. 'Wa ma Muhammadun illa rasul'—Allah says in Surah Al-Imran that Muhammad is only a messenger. Allah Himself declares that Muhammad is a messenger. 'Qad khalat'—messengers have passed before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels to your past? That is, will you turn back to disbelief? 'Wa man yanqalib 'ala 'aqibayhi falan yadurrallaha shay'a'—whoever leaves Islam and turns to disbelief does not harm Allah in the slightest. And Allah will soon reward the grateful (shakirin). As soon as the false news spread during the Battle of Uhud that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had been killed, people started leaving the battlefield and began joining the hypocrites. They started joining the army that had come against Islam. At that time, this verse was revealed. There were people among the companions whom Allah is warning in the Quran, asking if they would turn back to disbelief upon hearing the news of the Prophet's death or after he was killed. If a person considers such a companion their leader, their Imam, then where will that companion lead them? To Islam or out of Islam? The second question is, how is it possible that... The companions are correct, while the list of companions includes people who conspired to kill the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) after the Battle of Tabuk. And this Hadith is present in the books of the Sunnis. The Hadith from Urwah: 'An Urwah, qala: wa raja'a Rasulullahi (s.a.w.a.) qafilan min Tabuka ilal-Madinah.' When the Prophet's caravan was returning from Tabuk to Medina, and it was passing through a pass in the mountains—near a valley—'hatta idha kana bi-ba'dit-tariq makara bi-Rasulillahi (s.a.w.a.) nasun min ashabihi.' Until they reached a point on the road, some of his companions—those who are called companions or compared to stars—secretly joined in a conspiracy. They consulted among themselves to push the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) off a 'aqaba' (a hill or high mountain) on the way. Then the narrator, according to the meaning of Ibn Ishaq, narrated the whole Hadith about what happened. These are the people who are compared to stars. If this Hadith we are discussing today were correct in terms of its text, then the major objection would be: is following such people, who were involved in a conspiracy to kill the Prophet, the path we should take? Those who follow them will be counted among the killers of the Prophet. Or there were some people among the companions who were alcoholics. And this is not just one incident or limited to one Hadith; rather, there are mutawatir (frequently narrated) traditions and many incidents present in Sunni books where the names of those companions are given who used to drink alcohol, even being caught drinking after the prohibition of alcohol, and being caught reciting poems in praise of hypocrites while intoxicated. And when they were caught, they would immediately repent and recite the Kalima. Anyway, those who want more information on this topic should look at the book 'An-Nass wal-Ijtihad' by Sayyid Sharafuddin, which contains a detailed discussion. Anyway, let us move to this incident. We will try to present one incident here. Abu Ishaq narrates from Umar, and he from another Hakim, that when the verse of the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, the second Hakim said, 'O Allah, reveal a clear sign for us regarding the prohibition of alcohol.' Then this verse was revealed: 'Yas'alunaka 'anil-khamri wal-maysir, qul fihima ithmun kabir.' This was the first verse revealed after the prohibition of alcohol. When the second Hakim asked this question—according to their books, this is the incident—he was not satisfied with alcohol being forbidden, so he was praying that a clearer verse should come for us so that we stop drinking alcohol. This was an excuse to continue drinking. 'Yas'alunaka 'anil-khamr'—this verse was revealed in the second stage: 'They ask you, O Messenger (s.a.w.a.), about wine and gambling; say, in them is great sin.' Then the second Hakim was called, and this verse was read to him. He asked again, 'O Lord, reveal a clearer verse for us regarding the prohibition of alcohol.' Well, this is according to their books, and this incident is not just one that we are mentioning from their books; rather, this incident has been authenticated and declared 'Sahih' by their major scholars. For example, Al-Albani has authenticated this incident. Now, the second Hakim prayed again, 'O Lord, reveal a clearer verse than this for us regarding alcohol.' Meaning, time was being bought, and delays were being sought. In other words, the first two verses were not enough; in fact, the first three verses were not enough, so another verse was requested. It was so difficult for them to give up alcohol that they prayed again. Then another verse was revealed: 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu la taqrabus-salata wa antum sukara hatta ta'lamu ma taqulun'—'O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying.' It is written in the Hadith, and it is stated, that whenever the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) Muezzin would give the Adhan, he would also say along with the Adhan, 'Know that whoever is in a state of intoxication should not come for prayer.' The second Hakim was called again, and this verse was recited to him, that another verse had come regarding the prohibition of alcohol. He prayed to Allah again, 'O Lord, reveal a clearer verse than this regarding alcohol.' And finally, this verse was revealed: 'Fahal antum muntahun?'—'Will you not then desist?' After this verse was revealed, the second Hakim said, 'Now we have stopped.' Meaning, so many verses were revealed, and after that—they were so stubborn, so insistent on their sin, or it could be said that they loved drinking alcohol so much—that giving up alcohol was so difficult for them that after so many verses came, they finally made this announcement. Well, this announcement was not just that they were admitting it; they announced that now we will stop. But in reality, they did not stop drinking alcohol. The testimony for this is present in Sunan Ibn Dawud itself, that the second Hakim did not stop drinking alcohol until the verse of the prohibition of alcohol was revealed three times. Or it is found in other books that until the very end, they did not stop drinking wine, and at the time of death, on their deathbed, they requested 'nabidh' (a type of drink) and asked people for wine. Let us move on to the next major sin recorded in books regarding the companions. How, in the presence of the companions—that is, in the presence of the Sahaba—singing girls were singing, and these so-called 'stars' were present in that gathering and were actively participating in it. Amir ibn Sa'd says: 'I entered upon Qurzah ibn Ka'b and Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari'—meaning the names of two companions are mentioned here, Qurzah ibn Ka'b and Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari—'in a wedding gathering. I entered their presence at a wedding, and singing girls were singing in their presence.' I said, 'You are the companions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the people of Badr,'—about whom the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunnis) say that they are destined for Paradise; indeed, all the people of Badr are destined for Paradise, that is their belief—'is this happening in your presence? That is, singing girls are singing in your presence?' They both said, 'If you wish, stay with us'—meaning, enjoy this gathering with us—'and if you do not wish, then leave; get out of here. Because the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) granted us permission for amusement at weddings and for weeping at times of tragedy.' Meaning, if one were to follow these companions or these two companions, then the one following them also has permission to call singing girls to their gatherings. Let us move on to the next major sin present in the books. From Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.): 'He was delivering a sermon on Friday, and a caravan arrived from Syria. The people turned towards it.' The entire congregation—the Friday sermon was ongoing, and a caravan arrived from Syria. The caravans that used to come from Syria contained merchandise, meaning worldly goods, attractive things that people would go to buy; a market would be set up. So, as soon as the market was set up, while the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was delivering the sermon, these people disappeared. As soon as the caravan arrived from Syria, they left the sermon and the Friday prayer and went away. Who were they? These were the 'stars' who are supposed to be followed. If one takes the apparent meaning of that hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), '...and they dispersed towards it, until only twelve people remained.' Then this verse was revealed: 'And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse towards it and leave you standing.' If we were to follow these people among the companions today, then it would be correct for us to run away from Friday prayer towards trade. If we follow these people among the companions, then Friday prayer would be completely abolished. People would go to trade and towards amusement, leaving the Imam of Friday prayer alone. If these companions are to be followed, it is very clear that every companion cannot be followed. And among the companions, there are some whose grave crimes are recorded in books, in history books. These are major sins that even an ordinary person today would feel ashamed to commit, yet they are recorded in books regarding the companions. So how is it possible that all companions are like stars whose following is necessary and essential, and that by following any one of them, you will be guided? No, never. It is not possible; this is impossible. And among them were some from whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself declared disavowal. So, if the Prophet is declaring disavowal of someone, and that person is included in the list of companions and becomes a 'star' worthy of being followed, how is it possible to follow someone whom the Prophet has disavowed? This is rationally impossible. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) sent Khalid ibn Walid to the tribe of Jadhima to invite them to Islam. Khalid ibn Walid told them, 'Say: We have accepted Islam.' But these people started saying, 'Saba'na, saba'na' (we have changed our religion). Khalid ibn Walid insisted that they say 'Aslamna' (we have accepted Islam), but they kept saying 'Saba'na'. Eventually, Khalid ibn Walid started killing them one by one—meaning he started killing the people of that tribe and taking them prisoner—under the excuse that they were not accepting Islam. And then a day came when Khalid ibn Walid distributed these prisoners among those who had gone with him to Jadhima, and one day he ordered that all the prisoners be killed one by one. Now, some of these people started rebelling, saying, 'No, we cannot kill our prisoners; we will not kill them. We will go to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and present this matter to him.' And when this matter was presented to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he said, 'I am innocent of this act of Khalid ibn Walid.' O Allah! Be a witness that I am innocent of this act of Khalid ibn Walid. And today we see that those who consider such companions as stars are following them and ruining the name of Islam, defaming Islam by following this person. And this is the person whose act the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) disavowed. And in this list of stars, there are some people about whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had clearly prophesied that some people would come who would call people against the command of God. That is, they would make the lawful unlawful and the unlawful lawful. They would stop people from the good and lead them towards the evil. The narration is as follows: 'From Uthman ibn Affan, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) saying...' The narrator says I heard the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) saying: 'Soon after me, men will take charge of your affairs who will forbid you from what you used to know (as good).' Meaning, they will forbid you from the lawful. 'And they will forbid you from what you used to know.' They will forbid you from lawful things and lead you towards the unlawful, inviting you to it. 'So there is no obedience to one who disobeys Allah.' This is a hadith of the Prophet in clear words, present in the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, that there is no obedience to those who lead people towards the disobedience of Allah. So how do these stars become worthy of being followed? How can these stars, these luminaries who are involved in major sins, be obeyed? 'Do not put your souls into difficulty. For by the One in whose hand is my soul, Muawiyah is among them.' And the Prophet swears by the One in whose hand is my soul, that Muawiyah is among them. So this is a 'star' whom the Prophet himself is forbidding to follow. But if the apparent meaning of the hadith 'My companions are like stars' is taken, then it is necessary to obey him and follow him for guidance. That is, on one hand, the Prophet is forbidding his obedience, and on the other hand, there is a hadith being used to say 'follow whoever you want.' And this hadith is being applied in a general sense, applied to every companion. It becomes clear that this hadith cannot be taken at its apparent meaning and cannot be applied in a general sense. Rather, it is specified for a particular group. In the next part, God willing, we will see who that specific group is, but before that, one last narration. The last narration describes that some companions will be brought to the Hawd al-Kawthar, they will reach the Hawd al-Kawthar, and then they will be dragged away from there. 'Why have you come here?' And the hadith is authentic and present in reliable books. From Anas, from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.): 'Some people from my companions will be brought to me at the Hawd, until I recognize them, and then they will be taken away from me. I will say: My companions! Where are they being taken?' From the Hawd. 'Then it will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you.' So a voice will come, just one voice, saying: 'You do not know what deeds these people committed after you.' Meaning, there will indeed be some among the companions—the hadith is authentic and present in reliable books—who will be turned away from the Hawd al-Kawthar, from the Prophet's Hawd, while being told: 'You do not know what innovations they introduced into Islam, what innovations they initiated in Islam, and what deeds they committed after you.' So, are such people also included in those to be followed? Will such people also be declared stars who are worthy of being followed? Imam Rida (a.s.) was asked about the Prophet's saying regarding 'My companions are like stars' and another famous saying of the Prophet: 'Leave my companions for me.' Imam (a.s.) was asked about these two sayings. He (a.s.) said: 'This is true. It refers to those who did not change after the Prophet's martyrdom and did not alter anything.' And no change was found in them. Even after the Prophet's martyrdom, they remained on the same belief that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had stated during his lifetime. It was asked: 'And how do we know who they were that changed and in whom the change was found?' After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), regarding what they narrate from him (s.a.w.a.), he said: 'Some men from my companions will be driven away from my pond (Hawd) on the Day of Judgment.' The Imam (a.s.) said that regarding what they themselves narrate from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Prophet said: 'Some men from my companions will be driven away from my pond on the Day of Judgment, just as stray camels—those that are not part of the herd, the stray ones—are driven away from the water, as if to say, "You do not belong to this area, this water is not permissible for you." They will be dragged away. In the same way, some of the companions will be taken away. And I will say, "O Lord, my companions, my companions!"' And it will be said to me, 'You do not know what they innovated after you.' Then they will be taken to the left side. And I will say, "Away with them, may they be ruined!" So, do you understand that this is for those companions who did not change and did not alter? This hadith describes the condition of those companions who changed after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), those who turned back on their heels and left Islam after the Prophet's passing, after his martyrdom, and those who were completely transformed. So, on one hand, there is this validation from Imam Ridha (a.s.) that this hadith is authentic and cannot be denied. Therefore, there must be a group to whom this hadith applies. In reality, there is a group of stars whose guidance will lead a person to the truth. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: "Whatever you find in the Book of Allah (Azza wa Jall), it is obligatory for you to act upon it; you have no excuse to abandon it. And whatever you do not find in the Book of Allah (Azza wa Jall) but find a Sunnah of mine regarding it, you have no excuse to abandon my Sunnah." And whatever you do not find in my Sunnah, then whatever my companions say, you should follow it. For the likeness of my companions among you is like the stars; whichever one you follow, you will be guided. And whichever of the sayings of my companions you adopt, you will be guided. And the differences among my companions are a mercy for you.' It was then said, 'O Messenger of Allah'—this is the main part of the hadith—'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), who are your companions?' He (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'My Ahlulbayt.' Meaning, here, by 'companions' and 'stars,' it refers to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). There is no one else besides them. Therefore, if we want to be guided, a person must hold onto any of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and they will be guided. If one follows the sayings of any of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and acts upon them, they will be guided. Thus, this hadith becomes completely clear for us, and along with the hadith of Imam Ridha (a.s.), it is clarified where this hadith is truly applied. It also indicates that if one holds onto anyone else or follows the sayings of anyone else besides them, one cannot reach true guidance. And if one comes to their door, even the most difficult matters will become easy for them. The Imam (a.s.) explained in a very clear manner how to apply this hadith, and this is a tremendous guidance from the Imam that a person should hold onto the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), through which they will be guided. Meaning, when a person comes to the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and understands the hadith through their sayings, they will be guided. In truth, the real stars are only the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and the real stars are those upon whose door the star has descended. And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. The time has come for the announcement of the daily winners of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz 2026. Remember that the quiz link has not been closed and will remain live until the end of this series. The selection of daily winners will only be from those individuals who have given the correct answers to all questions before the timer ends in the episode. So, let us move towards the announcement of the 18 daily winners of today's episode, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. They will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees, and their names are on your screen. Farzeen Zahra from Bengaluru, Mahmood Hasan from Sirsi, Abbasi from Srinagar, Jamani Rozina Banu from Mahuva, Bintul Khadija from New Delhi, Maroof Haider from Bengaluru, Rizvi Hilal from New Delhi, Zaheer Abbas Jamani from Una, Sania Fatima from Gadada, Heena Yusuf Khan from Chennai, Fatima Meghani from Bhavnagar, Syed Mehdi Abbas from Jaipur, Sania Zahra from Alipur, Rukh Syed from Thane, Sayyeda Fatima from Bangkok Thailand, Syed Dayan from Bengaluru, Sayyeda Sumaiya Hashmi from Bengaluru, Shabi Zahra Zaidi from Meerut. Many congratulations to all you winners. If someone's name did not appear in today's winners, there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series, and remember, you can enter the lucky draw for the mega prize—a pilgrimage to Iraq—by answering all questions correctly in just one episode of this series. We thank you all once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time, 9:30 PM India time, in the next episode of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz, with another video on an important topic titled 'Moula Ali (a.s.)'s Protest Against the Shura.' Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

excerpt: The Kulle Iman Grand Quiz 2025 lecture explores the central theological importance of the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the 'Rope of Allah' (Hablullah). The session emphasizes that true guidance and unity within the Muslim Ummah are achieved only by adhering to both the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, as established in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. Beyond theological discourse, the lecture highlights the esoteric knowledge and divine authority of Imam Ali (a.s.), concluding with the announcement of winners for the educational quiz competition.
content:
Ali Ali Ali Ali Ali. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala abih, fi hadhihis-sa'ah wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'a wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa salla Allahu ala waliyul asr, wa ala alihi. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. On behalf of the TSR team, we are at your service... On behalf of the TSR team, we are at your service to offer congratulations on the blessed birth of Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and we welcome you all to this 'Kulle Iman' (a.s.) Grand Quiz. We begin our discussion with the praise of Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala. All praise is for that Allah whose praise cannot be reached by the speaker, whose blessings cannot be counted by those who try to count, whose right cannot be fulfilled by those who strive, who cannot be attained by high-flying ambitions, and whose depth cannot be reached by the depths of intellect and understanding. There are no descriptive words for Him, no time for His beginning to be counted, and no duration where He ends. He created the creation through His power, set the winds in motion with His mercy, and anchored the mountains on the trembling earth. The beginning of religion is His recognition (Ma'rifat), the perfection of recognition is His affirmation (Tasdeeq), the perfection of affirmation is Monotheism (Tawheed), and the perfection of Monotheism is sincerity and purity. Yes, respected viewers, this luminous word which contains the praise of Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala... which contains the praise of Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala, has been issued through that luminous essence (Noor-e-Aqdas) whom Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala declares as His Light in the Holy Quran. Allah Subhan wa Ta'ala says in Surah As-Saff, verse number 8: 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Yuriduna liyutfiu nurallahi bi-afwahihim, wallahu mutimmu nurihi wa law karihal kafirun' (They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it). Respected viewers, this Light of Allah, the noble name of this Light is Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Your blessed birth took place on the 13th of Rajab, 30 Aam-ul-Feel, inside the Kaaba. Regarding your birth in the Kaaba, I feel like reciting a couplet: 'Faraz-e-dar se Meesam bayan dete hain, rahega zikr-e-Ali hum zaban dete hain. Saf-e-bana-o-mohib-e-dar se Meesam, namaz-e-ishq-e-Ali ki azan dete hain. Ali ki jaye wiladat ki jab bhi baat chali, kaha Khuda ne hum apna makan dete hain.' Yes, respected viewers, on the occasion of this 13th of Rajab, the TSR team... On the occasion of this blessed day, the TSR team is here once again with the 'Kulle Iman' (a.s.) Grand Quiz. Before we start our discussion, let's take a look at the rules of the quiz. The quiz link is live and is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you haven't registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. You must answer all the questions correctly. From those who have answered all questions correctly, 18 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, who will be given these prizes [Music]. Yes, viewers, Alhamdulillah, this is the fourth round of the 'Kulle Iman' (a.s.) Grand Quiz. In the first round, we discussed the Amirul... In the first round, we discussed the arrival of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) in the Kaaba. In the second round, we mentioned the names and titles of Amirul Momineen (a.s.), and in the third round, which took place last year, we discussed 'Ali in the Quran'. So viewers, if you want to study traditions regarding the blessed birth of Ali (a.s.), or want to know about the names and titles of Ali (a.s.), or want to know where Ali (a.s.) is present in the Quran, you can visit our YouTube channel. In the fourth round of the Grand Quiz, we have brought a very important topic before you, titled 'The Strong Rope of Allah'. In this discussion, we will be joined by two of our brothers, Mr. Kazim Syed and Mr. Ahsan Jafri. So let us begin this discussion. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. Hasan Bhai, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. First of all, brother, on behalf of the TSR team, we want to offer congratulations to all the viewers on the blessed birth of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) with a Salawat: Allahumma salli ala Muhammad. Now, as the viewers are aware of today's topic, I have to present a few points regarding it. Our topic begins with the reference to Amirul Momineen (a.s.) being called 'Hablullah' (The Rope of Allah) in the Quran. Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala says in this verse of His Great Book: 'Wa'tasimu bi hablillahi jami'an wa la tafarraqu' (And hold fast, all of you together, to the Rope of Allah and do not be divided). We consider it very important to tell the viewers that Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala did not send the Holy Quran to the Muslim Ummah just as a book of recitation, but presented this book to the Muslim Ummah in the form of guidance. However, in our true religion, it is our belief, it is our faith... it is our faith that everything has certain conditions, and this guidance also has certain conditions. Indeed, if guidance were obtained only by recitation, then after the martyrdom of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), there would have been no division in the Muslim Ummah. But we see that immediately after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), division occurred in the Muslim Ummah. Therefore, we must know where we will obtain this guidance along with recitation. That Great Messenger told us that guidance will be found at the door of the one who is the door of 'Ilm' (Knowledge), the perfection of the Quran, and the one who is 'Rasikhun fil Ilm' (firm in knowledge). Therefore, especially we, the Shias of Ali (a.s.), should refer to the Thaqalayn (the two weighty things) in every matter of religion. We also find a Hadith of our Masumeen (a.s.) in this regard, where they say: 'Man akhadha dinahu min afwahir-rijal...' (Whoever takes his religion from the mouths of people, those very people will lead him astray). And then the Hadith continues, and in it, the Masumeen (a.s.) state: 'Man amila'... The Masumeen (a.s.) state: 'Man tamassaka bi kitabi-llahi wa sunnati nabiyyihi... (Whoever holds onto the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet...)'. If you hold onto your religion through the Quran and the authentic Sunnah, the mountains may move from their place, but the person who has taken their religion from the Thaqalayn (the two weighty things) will not be moved from their place. Regarding the verse we have chosen as our opening, we will look at it through the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to see what they have said about it. Indeed, let us clarify through a few narrations of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) who is being referred to by 'Hablullah' (the Rope of Allah). The first Hadith I want to present is from Imam Baqir (a.s.), who says regarding 'wa la tafarraqu' (and do not be divided): 'Indeed, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala knew that these people would fall into division and disagreement after their Prophet (s.a.w.a.). So, Allah forbade them from division just as He forbade those who came before them. And then, the Almighty God gave them a command here—did Allah give them a command?' Did Allah give them a command? What did He command? 'Wala' (allegiance) to the family of Muhammad (a.s.). Allah commanded them to be united upon the Wilayah of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) and then said, 'Do not be divided.' And look, if any person opens their eyes and recites the Quran in the light of intellect, it becomes clear that if Allah has recorded something in the Holy Quran, the Word of Allah is not in vain. Indeed, if Allah has declared in this verse not to divide, it means Allah knew well that people would split and division would occur. And Imam Baqir (a.s.) pointed to this very fact: Allah knew that people would split after the Prophet. Therefore, if one wants to stop from splitting, to save oneself from division, to stop oneself from being divided, and to be united, then the only path is the Wilayah of the family of Muhammad (a.s.). And look, as you have stated here, and as it is clearly mentioned in this Hadith, Allah knew that the Muslim Ummah would fall into division after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). That is why, through the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Allah repeatedly emphasized the Wilayah and Imamate of the Masumeen (a.s.). The repeated emphasis on the Wilayah and Imamate of the Masumeen (a.s.)... and I want to present another Hadith here for the viewers, narrated from Imam Kazim (a.s.): 'Allah has not emphasized anything to His servants as much as the acknowledgement of Imamate.' Meaning, if there is anything Allah has emphasized the most, it is the acknowledgement of Imamate. And then the Imam (a.s.) says, 'But alas, people were given so much emphasis regarding the acknowledgement of Imamate, yet alas, if there is anything people denied the most, it is the subject of Imamate.' And this is the reason for the division—that people denied the Imamate. Here, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala, the Masumeen (a.s.), and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) want to convey the message that if you do not want to be divided, the best option is to be united upon the Wilayah of the Masumeen (a.s.). Indeed, this is the only means through which the Muslim Ummah can find salvation, and this is the command being given in the Quran regarding this verse. Let us present the second Hadith to the viewers, Hassan Bhai, in which we will see who is meant by 'Hablullah'. This Hadith is also narrated from Imam Kazim (a.s.), in which he says regarding this verse... He says regarding this verse: 'Qala Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)'—that who is meant by this? Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). And then he says, 'Hablul Matin' (the firm rope). And this is that firm rope. Meaning, it is very clear. If one wants to take religion, if one wants to understand religion, we can say anything based on our own thoughts, our own illusions, our own whims—we can say anything, but the actual religion will be found in the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Indeed, that is correct. And just as there is a verse in the Quran, let us present a verse of the Quran to the believers: that most people have followed 'Zann' (conjecture/assumption). The Quran explicitly states that Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala is revealing: 'Inna yattabi'una illa al-zann' (They follow nothing but conjecture). Following conjecture and assumption, which is far from reality. And then Allah immediately says, 'Inna la yughni min al-haqqi shay'an' (Indeed, conjecture does not avail against the truth at all). So, these people—because if you look at the last four or five years, this verse has been interpreted in many different ways, and it is being presented to people in different ways as to who is meant by 'Hablullah'. But if we want to know who is actually meant by 'Hablullah'... If we want to know who is actually meant by 'Hablullah', we must seek the help of the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and then we will know. And you said it absolutely correctly that in the past few years, a lot of misunderstanding regarding this verse has been seen in society. It is true that it is insisted upon not to divide, but what is the condition stated for not dividing? That 'hold fast to the rope of Allah,' only then will there be no division. Indeed, indeed. If someone has not held onto the rope, they will definitely fall victim to division. So, if people are to be brought to one platform, the only means is the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Indeed, this is the only means through which people can be united; otherwise, there will be division. And this is the reality—true unity will only be this. Now, Hassan Bhai, let us present a Tafsir of the Ahl-e-Sunnah to the viewers as well, which Ibn Mardawayh has narrated in his Tafsir. He presents this narration in his Tafsir through 89 chains of transmission regarding this verse, and in it, he writes that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said regarding this verse: 'Inni mukhallifun fikum al-thaqalayn' (I am leaving among you two weighty things). And then he writes further that the Book of Allah... And then he writes further that the Book of Allah is one, and the other is my Itrah (progeny), my Ahlulbayt (a.s.). In the context of this very verse, he brings the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, meaning that 'Hablullah' refers to the Hadith al-Thaqalayn—the two weighty things. And then he further states the very sentence of the Hadith al-Thaqalayn: 'If you hold onto these two, you will never go astray.' Look, I wanted to present a very important point to the viewers here: 'In' is a conditional particle; if you do this, then that will happen. Just like the Quranic verse: 'In tansurullaha yansurkum' (If you help Allah, He will help you). So, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is saying in this Hadith that if you hold onto these two things—meaning the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—then you will 'lan tadillu abadan' (never go astray). Here, there is a negation of 'ever'; you will never go astray. Meaning, he is giving a guarantee. And if there were any other individual in the Muslim Ummah, the Messenger of Allah would surely have pointed towards them. Here, there were only two things that could be the means of salvation for the Muslim Ummah. Here is a very interesting incident, since you spoke about 'tamassuk' (holding fast) and in the verse... Since you spoke about 'tamassuk' and in the verse, there is a discussion about 'Hablullah', there is a very interesting incident connected to both. The incident is such that once the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was present in Masjid al-Nabawi, and the companions were present. This Hadith has been narrated in 'Ghayat al-Maram' and Sayyid Hashim Bahrani has also narrated this Hadith in 'Tafsir al-Burhan'. The Hadith is from the fourth Imam (a.s.), in which he said that the Prophet was sitting in Masjid al-Nabawi, and the companions were with him. Wow, they killed or drove away the enemies in front of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). SubhanAllah, subhanAllah. Then these people celebrated, the angels celebrated, meaning they were present there, watching the battle of Ali (a.s.). And in another Hadith, if you look, all these angels were also seen supporting Ali (a.s.) in the battle. And then Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari says, 'Whoever does not feel joy upon seeing Ali (a.s.)...' Here it is talking about not doing so, that if someone does not feel it, then what is he saying about him? '...then the curse of Allah is upon him.' Wow, wow, subhanAllah. If someone does not feel joy after seeing Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), then the curse of Allah is upon him. Now we cannot see Ali (a.s.) or the last descendant of Ali (a.s.), but when he is mentioned, our faces should light up. Indeed, indeed. If someone's face does not light up, then indeed the curse of Allah will be upon him. Absolutely correct. The curse of Allah is upon him. Absolutely correct, Kazim brother. And as you mentioned regarding the battles, that the angels often participated in the support of the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat) and not just support, but they registered their participation so that they could be included among those fighting alongside Ali (a.s.). In this regard, the Battle of Badr is a famous battle, the first battle of Islam. In that regard, there are narrations, and this is also coincidentally from Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari, that he says the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said—and Allama brought this Hadith in Bihar al-Anwar citing Tafsir al-Qummi—that the Prophet said, 'By the Being in whose control is my life, I never turned my attention to Ali in any battle except that I saw Jibra'il (a.s.) on the right side of Ali (a.s.) with an army of 70,000 angels.' Wow, this Jibra'il is on the right side, and if you look to the left, Mikal is there with another 70,000 angels. They are both fighting together. And these are on the right and left, who is in front? In front is the Angel of Death. In front is the Angel of Death. Oh, oh, oh. The Angel of Death is walking ahead of Ali (a.s.). Wow, wow. Yes, absolutely, as if it were said that the Angel of Death is subject to the command of Ali (a.s.)'s sword, that wherever the sword moves, the Angel of Death will continue to take the souls of all of them. The Prophet is saying, 'I always saw that even in battles, a cloud used to shade Ali.' And it would shade him until Ali (a.s.) achieved victory in the best way, until he achieved success. That cloud would keep shading him. This means this whole matter of the angels' support and help in battles kept happening. And regarding the participation in the Battle of Badr, specifically regarding the participation of Jibra'il, it is mentioned especially. And this is also what Ibn Abbas narrates, what is the narration? That in the Battle of Badr, because it was the first battle, the polytheists of Mecca, what was their intention? The killing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). They came with that intention. So, who incited those people to be ready to kill a Prophet of Allah, who is also the last Prophet, the most superior Prophet? Iblis. Iblis himself had come to participate in the Battle of Badr, or to oppose the Prophet, to oppose Ali (a.s.), to oppose the Muslims. Iblis himself came. Iblis himself had come to oppose the Muslims. And how did he come? In the form of Suraqa ibn Malik, taking the shape of Suraqa ibn Malik. And he was at the front of their army, the army of the enemies, at the front, to fight the Prophet. So what happened? Allah Almighty ordered Jibra'il (a.s.). Jibra'il (a.s.) came immediately, presented himself to the Prophet, and he did not come alone, he did not come alone. What did he bring with him? He brought an army of 1,000 angels. And Jibra'il (a.s.) stood on the right side of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). When Ali (a.s.) attacked, Jibra'il would also attack along with him. Wow. Then Iblis saw this whole scene. Iblis saw that Ali is attacking and Jibra'il is also attacking along with him, Jibra'il is also involved in the battle. So as soon as he saw Jibra'il (a.s.) and the army of 1,000 angels, the sentence of the narration is that he turned on his heels and ran away. He ran away in fear, fled from the battle. This means choosing to flee from the battle is the Sunnah of Iblis. Wow, wow, wow, wow. And then he himself says when... Wow, wow, and then he himself says when he was turning back, what does he say while leaving? When, obviously, he had come in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik, so when people must have seen him leaving, they must have stopped him and asked, 'Hey brother, where are you fleeing to? Where are you running?' So what did he say while leaving? 'I see what you do not see.' And then after this, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud says, 'By Allah, Iblis did not go from there, but why did he go? Why did he run? He ran only after seeing Ali (a.s.).' He ran after seeing Ali (a.s.) and he was afraid that Ali (a.s.) might catch Iblis, might arrest him, might expose his reality to the people, because he had come in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik. He was afraid that Ali might catch him and tell everyone that in reality, this is Iblis. So he got scared of this and fled. And he was the first one to flee from that battle, that very Iblis. And he went saying this, and Allah has included this in the Quran as a verse, that in Surah Al-Anfal, verse 48, Allah says, 'I see what you do not see.' Allah has recorded the sentences of Iblis in the Quran, 'And I fear Allah.' I see what you do not see, and I fear Allah. In what regard do I fear? Why do I fear? '...in the matter of fighting Ali.' Wow, wow. I am afraid, I fear Allah, that I might end up fighting Ali. Why? 'And Allah is severe in punishment and retribution.' For whom? For those who fight Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). So whoever fought Ali (a.s.) will have to face the punishment of Allah. In this way, in every battle—this is the Battle of Badr—as I said before, in the previous Hadith, we saw that in every battle, the army of angels would come to support and help Ali (a.s.). And these angels who benefited from the knowledge of Ali (a.s.), whose Wilayah is obligatory, whose support is obligatory, all these, if it is said, if we look, the angels are just fulfilling their duty by participating in those battles, supporting Ali (a.s.). So, indeed, viewers, you have observed what severe consequences there are for fighting Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Ali, whoever fights you has fought me, and whoever fights me has fought Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' Whoever fought me, fought Allah (Azza wa Jall). Therefore, viewers, in the history of Islam, whoever came to fight against Hazrat Ali (a.s.), in reality, they did not fight Ali (a.s.) but fought the Messenger of Allah and Allah Himself. O Allah, make my soul tranquil, satisfied with Your decree... chapters.summary: The TSR team welcomes viewers to the fourth annual Kulle Iman Grand Quiz, celebrating the birth of Imam Ali (a.s.) and outlining the competition rules.

chapters.title: Hablullah: The Rope of Allah

chapters.title: The Necessity of Wilayah for Unity
chapters.summary: Using narrations from Imam Baqir (a.s.) and Imam Kazim (a.s.), the speakers explain that holding onto the Wilayah of the family of Muhammad (a.s.) is the only way to prevent division in the Ummah.

title: The Lost Father | A Short Film About Remembering Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)
excerpt: This short film uses the narrative of a young boy separated from his father to illustrate the spiritual state of humanity awaiting Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). As the boy realizes his mistake in letting go of his father's hand, he experiences the fear and isolation of being lost. He eventually turns to the Imam for help, mirroring the believer's need to seek refuge in the Savior during times of distress. The film concludes with a heartfelt plea for the reappearance of the Imam to end the world's suffering.
content:
In the name of Allah, Most Gracious, Most Merciful Father! Hhmm... We will stand in the first line. Just right behind the Maulana. Sure my son, We called it صف (Row), Not line. Will you remember? Yes father. The first صف (Row). That is correct! Father! Where are we going? Our car is parked over there! Then why are we not going in the car? Walking to the mosque has more rewards Hence we shall walk to the mosque today Oh, Alright. Did you perform the ablution (Wazu)? Hold my hand. No. I haven't performed the ablution. Okay, not a problem You can perform it at the Mosque. Sure, I'll do it there. I hope you know the conditions of the ablution Mumma has taught them to you, isn't it? Yes, she did. Hhmm... Father! I want a packet of chips. Not now. Aren't we getting get for the Congregational Prayer? Don't you want to be in the first صف (Row)? Yes, I do (sadly) Father, the shop has the Hulk toy. No, No, we are getting late for the prayers Excuse me, sir, Would you please show the Hulk toy? That Hulk toy. Can't you do that later? Fine. Here it is! wow! Oh no! I'm sorry! Hey kid What are you doing? I didn't do that on purpose Catch the kid I didn't do that on purpose Father... Father! Where is he? Father... Father...Father Where is my father? Father! How will I get back home? Where is my father? Father... (sobbing) Father... Please come back! My father! I shouldn't have left my father's hand! It was a big mistake I shouldn't have done that O Allah! I accept my mistake I have understood. I won't repeat this ever! Just get me, my father, once O Allah, Send my father soon I'm very scared O, Allah! Please Allah, I am hungry, I want to go to my Mumma Please my lord I won't do it ever... I remember Mumma saying When in trouble... Remember the Imam (as) of our time May Allah hasten the reappearance of Imam Zaman (a.t.f.s) O Imam, Please send my father soon Please my Imam, Please send him soon. If it becomes dark... I don't know what I will do. I hope I will be safe until then. O, Allah! Baba! (Surood) The eyes are raining. (Surood) Without you, Hussain is distressed (Surood) Without you Hasan is heartbroken Come O Mahdi, Come O Mahdi, The flag-bearer of Ghadir The leader of all souls The avenger of Zahra's (s.a) sorrows Come O Mahdi, Come O Mahdi, Come, O son of Zahra (sa.) Come... Come

title: Lailatul Qadr Ki Ahmiyyat | Hazrat Moosa (a.s.) Ki Allah Se Guftugu | [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual significance of Lailatul Qadr through the dialogue between Prophet Musa (a.s.) and Allah. It outlines specific acts of worship—such as staying awake, showing mercy to the poor, seeking forgiveness, and performing prayer—that lead to divine closeness, mercy, and salvation. The talk concludes with a heartfelt supplication for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and the strength to serve his cause.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Prophet Musa (a.s.) prayed to Allah, 'O Lord, I want Your closeness.' The answer came, 'My closeness is for the one who stays awake on the Night of Qadr.' Then he asked, 'O Lord, I want Your mercy.' The answer came, 'My mercy is for the one who shows mercy to the poor on the Night of Qadr.' Then he asked, 'Is it for the one who recites Tasbih on the Night of Qadr?' Then he asked, 'O Lord, I want salvation from the fire of Hell.' The answer came, 'This is for the one who seeks forgiveness on the Night of Qadr.' Finally, he prayed, 'O Lord, I want Your pleasure.' In the answer, Allah said, 'My pleasure is for the one who prays two Rak'ats of prayer on the Night of Qadr.' Finally, we also pray in the court of God, that O God, give us... In the court of God, we pray that O God, grant us the ability on the Night of Qadr. In this Night of Qadr, decree the appearance of the Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the ability to be included in his helpers and to prepare ourselves for his arrival. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds.

Showing mercy to the poor on this night earns divine mercy.
Seeking forgiveness on Lailatul Qadr is the path to salvation from Hellfire.
Performing two Rak'ats of prayer on this night leads to the pleasure of Allah.

Believers should pray for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) during this blessed night.

title: Majlis 3 | Foresight (Door Andeshi) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the concept of foresight (Door Andeshi) through the lens of Shia theology and the tragedy of Karbala. He emphasizes the necessity of cultivating intellect through the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt, the importance of recognizing a divinely appointed Imam, and the role of contemplation in spiritual growth. The session also highlights the significance of historical awareness, parental responsibility in religious education, and the enduring legacy of Lady Zaynab in preserving the message of Imam Hussain.
content:
Zaynab became the interpreter of the biography of the Ahl al-Kisa, Zaynab became the commentator of the laws of the religion of Mustafa, Zaynab became the publisher of the message of the King of Karbala. In every martyr of duty, she explained the meaning of purity and sincerity, Abbas explained the meaning of the word loyalty with force. When the day ended, Zaynab became the manifestation of the word loyalty, Shabbir (Imam Husayn) was the guide of the people of submission and contentment, and in the river of blood, Shabbir was undoubtedly the captain. But in the river of fire, Zaynab was the captain. A veil came over the eyes of the oppressors, hair was disheveled in the rain of arrows, darkness spread, and the sun turned its eyes away, Zaynab was unveiled. And she gave a sermon in Kufa, she caused a rain of tears, and thus the gathering was held in the court of Sham. The truth is that Zaynab is the founder of the tradition of mourning. And Zaynab wore shackles, the heavens trembled, the sweat of honor appeared on the forehead of time, Zaynab became the conqueror of every stage of patience and contentment. With what cheerfulness she sacrificed both her sons, in this world, she was the beginning of maternal patience and steadfastness, Hajar was the beginning, Zaynab was the end, just as the glorious interpretation of the Prophet's branch. Just as Abbas was the desire of Ali, so too, in this beautiful earthly form, Zainab became the prayer of Zahra; Zainab became the interpreter of the character of the Ahl al-Aba. And Shabbir (Imam Hussain) was the guide for the people of submission and contentment; indeed, in the ocean of blood, Shabbir was the captain, but in the ocean of fire, Zainab was the captain. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; the best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome is for the righteous and those who possess certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the noblest of the prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Blessings be upon the infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance, especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, our Imam of the time, our guardian, our master, our beloved, our physician, our intimate companion, our comforter, the fortified cave, and the relief of the distressed and the desperate—may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. This matter will continue until the Day of Judgment, and therefore, think about your Imam, who your Imam is, and take everything from your Imam. Now, in this regard, look, our scholar Mir Hamid Hussain, may Allah be pleased with him, Mir Hamid Hussain wrote 'Abaqat al-Anwar'. He brought a very large discussion in the chapter of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, which is not our topic right now. We are just pointing it out. It has been translated into English and is also available on the website; you can see it. In it, in the third or fourth volume, besides that, in Hadith al-Safina—Hadith al-Safina is in one volume—he brought many discussions in which he proved that all the people who were with the Messenger of Allah, who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah, were so ignorant of the Ahlulbayt, fundamentally, they were not even aware of the basic rulings. They were so ignorant that when one person claimed—or rather sat down—that "I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah," after that, a man came and asked, "I am in a state of impurity (najasat), should I pray or not?" He said, "No, there is no need to pray. Why do you pray? You are in a state of impurity." So, Janab-e-Ammar was standing there. He said, "Brother, what kind of things are you saying? What are you saying? Do you remember that when you and I were traveling once, and we were in a state of impurity, then I performed Tayammum and you did not pray? You said, 'I will not pray.' So we came to the Messenger of Allah. We told the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah said, 'Yes, that is correct.' He said to Ammar, 'You did the right thing,' and to you, He said that you did the wrong thing. You should have performed Tayammum and prayed.' Now Ammar said this in front of everyone in the court. Now his reputation was gone. So, he had Ammar beaten so much, so much that Ammar—you can understand—was in a very bad state. He was in a miserable state. And that was their custom too. That is, the incidents are documented. Let me quickly present a small incident so that you know and become familiar with the value of the teachings of the Ahlulbayt of Prophethood. A small incident is present, and we are not saying this from a Shia book, yes. This is actually from the books of others. This incident is present that a person came and said, "Sir, what is the meaning of this verse?" The verse was: 'وَالذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْوًا'. This is a verse of the Quran, Surah Adh-Dhariyat. 'وَالذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْوًا'. What is the meaning of this verse? It is the first verse of Surah Adh-Dhariyat. He just had to ask the verse. He beat him so much, beat him so much that his condition became miserable. He went home, his wounds were dressed. Now they sent someone to ask if he was okay or not. So he said, "Yes, now I am fine." They said, "Call him." Then he was called. What was the question? He said, "Wadh-dhariyat-i dharwa." Then he had him beaten again. We are not telling any joke, yes brother. This is actually a historical document we are telling you. This is a historical document we are telling you. Then he beat him, had him beaten so much that he left. Then they sent someone to ask if he was okay or not. "Yes, I am fine." Then he was called. Then he asked, "What was the question?" He said, "Wadh-dhariyat-i dharwa. Wadh-dhariyat-i dharwa." Then he had him beaten. And after having him beaten, now he is not allowed to stay in Medina. It is not allowed to stay in Medina, and he was sent where? Basra. Who was the governor in Basra? Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. He told Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, "I am sending him to Basra, and this is 'extermination'—yes, 'extermination,' which is called 'tadipar' in Bombay language." Right? So, I have exiled him. Now everyone should boycott him. No one should entertain him. He said, 'Fine.' Abu Musa al-Ash'ari passed an order throughout Basra: 'No one will entertain him. Boycott him completely.' So, the poor man became distressed. He went and fell at the feet of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. He said, 'Please forgive me and ask the Caliph to forgive me. I will not ask any questions next time. I apologize, please.' So, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari wrote a letter saying that he is very remorseful. He is regretting it a lot. He says he will not do such a thing next time. So, he said, 'Fine, send him.' So, he was sent back to Medina. Then he was called to the court. What was the question? He said, 'There was no question.' He said, 'A favor.' Did you notice? I mean, reflect on this now. Look, what you have heard so far, there is nothing surprising in it. When we read it too, we were not surprised. Why were we not surprised? Because when someone leaves the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), this is the result. In fact, the result is even worse, which you see today in the condition of Muslims all over the world. This is the result of leaving the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). There is nothing surprising about this. What is surprising? The way the so-called scholars who came after that justified this. They justified the action and started saying that because he was asking about 'Ayat-e-Mutashabihat' (ambiguous verses), the Caliph got angry. That is why his hands and feet were broken. This is the justification. Have you seen in the history of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) or the history of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that someone's hands and feet were broken for asking a question? For asking a question? But when someone... this is a moment of reflection for Muslims. 'Lamha-e-Fikriya' means this is food for thought for them. Reflect on it a little. Look, if you leave the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)... that is why we emphasize bringing children to Majalis. Bring children to gatherings. Familiarize children with Shia culture. That this is a gathering, this is a Majlis, the etiquette of Majlis, the etiquette of gatherings, and take them to the mosque. Tell them everything so that the children understand what our religion is. People should not even know what our religion actually is. What is a Majlis called, what is a gathering called? Do not think there are no such people; there are many people who do not even know what religion actually is. They do not know what a Majlis is, what a gathering is, what a mosque is, and what the etiquette, the manners are. Take them to Ziyarat if possible so that they are familiar with the etiquette of Ziyarat. For example, we have seen young people go on Ziyarat; do you know what the etiquette of Ziyarat is? The basic etiquette, what is the basic etiquette of Ziyarat? When you go, I am talking about the young people, those who are old, well, that is a different matter. A young person should recite Ziyarat standing up, not sitting down. Unless it is written in the Ziyarat that 'yes, after this you may sit down.' Where it is written, sit there, and where it is not written, stand up; that is the etiquette of Ziyarat. You are going into the presence of the Imam. So teach children all these things so that they know. Tell the children, 'Brother, charity should be given.' Make children give charity with their own hands so that children understand what charity is. There was a very great scholar, the late Khunsari, a very great one. He wrote a book, 'Raudat al-Jannat'. In 'Raudat al-Jannat', he wrote the biographies of scholars. Life history, 'Sawan-e-Hayat' means life history, biographies of scholars. In it, one scholar, a very great scholar, and he was actually a minister basically. He was a minister in the government, the Buyid dynasty. So, the Buyid dynasty, like the Banu Abbas, Banu Umayya, Banu Marwan, Banu Fatima, similarly the Buyid dynasty which was in the time of Sheikh Saduq. So, he was a minister in it. His name was Ismail ibn Abbad al-Taliqani. I mean, Taliqan is a province in Iran, and it is now, for example, one part of it is in Iran, now the other one is... earlier it was very big, now it has become small because everything has expanded, right, small areas have been formed. Otherwise, some part has even gone into Russia now. A very large area, Taliqan, and very fertile land. If you study the books of Hadith, you will find narrators from Taliqan, narrators of traditions. Like Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taliqani, from whom Sheikh Saduq narrated many Hadiths. These mostly lived in Mashhad, I mean today's Mashhad, in that era its name was Marv. Very fertile, very productive, many scholars. So, this minister, Ismail ibn Abbad, was also a very great poet. And because he had a lot of influence, the opponents wrote a lot of nonsense about him, that he used to drink wine and this and that, and then many of our people, you know our people are very simple, right, whatever those people wrote, they copied it here. Whereas if you look, Shia books nowhere state that Ismail ibn Abbad had these habits. All this was written by others. The Shias who copied from those people later, you will find that in them. It is not in the original books anywhere. In the original books, there is only praise for Ismail ibn Abbad al-Taliqani. Anyway, this Ismail ibn Abbad al-Taliqani, his parents had taught him this habit, do you know? That when he was a child, they taught him to give charity, and it is also in the Hadith, 'Give charity through the hands of your children.' Giving charity yourself is a good thing, but teach children the culture, Islamic culture is this, so that they know that charity is given. Now it was his habit. Now when he even became a minister, obviously, there is a lot of tension, a lot of work, so to remember it himself, he told one of his servants, his attendant, 'Every day, put a gold coin and a silver coin under my pillow, one gold coin every day, daily, yes?' Obviously, he was a minister, a big man, so he could give a gold coin every day. Right? Now obviously we cannot give, that is fine. We say, 'Give 5 rupees, brother,' you can give 5 rupees, if you cannot give 5 rupees, you can give 1 rupee, give 1 rupee. Allah looks at the intention, not the amount. Allah looks at the intention. So, he was a minister, so he could keep it, so one gold coin, one silver coin. And it was his habit since childhood, this thing was never missed. One day when he woke up in the morning, there was no money. So, he asked the servant, 'Where did the money go? Did you not put it?' So, he said, 'Master, I forgot. I was busy with work at night, I forgot.' Now he was very remorseful, he regretted a lot, 'What should I do?' I mean, let me tell you, he was a scholar of the fourth century, Ismail ibn Abbad Taliqani, the minister. I mean, he passed away in 385 Hijri, meaning he was a contemporary of Sheikh Saduq, and the book that Sheikh Saduq wrote, 'Uyun Akhbar ar-Rida', was written at his request. 'Uyun Akhbar ar-Rida (a.s.), all the Hadiths of Imam Rida (a.s.) that were collected, were written at his request. If you read its preface, it is written in it. Similarly, Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi was a very great scholar in that same era. Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi. This Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi wrote a book, 'Tarikh-e-Madinat-e-Qum'. The history of the city of Qum. It was written at his request, 'What are the virtues of Qum?' There is the city of Qum, right, in Iran. What are its virtues? So, 'Tarikh-e-Madinat-e-Qum', he collected all the narrations in it. The late Qummi, at whose request? At his request. So, now you understand that he was a great personality. Now he did not give charity, the servant did not put it, so now he was very remorseful. Immediately, what did he do? He told the servant, 'Look, now it is not that... do one thing, all this furniture, all of it in the house, take it all and go and give it away. Do not keep anything. We will get new furniture, but take this away immediately.' So, the servant said, 'Fine,' but now to whom should he give so much furniture? The servant left. This was written by the late Khunsari, and let me tell you, the late Khunsari was not some small scholar, he was a Marja-e-Taqlid of his time, a great personality, 'Raudat al-Jannat' is his very famous book, and there are many things about him, the late Khunsari, I am not telling you, otherwise a lot of time will be spent on it. So, this is like this, I am not telling you any story, I am telling you from his book. So, now he did what, now the servant left, took the whole furniture, everything. Obviously, several vehicles must have been used for that. So, he left, must have given a contract to Packers and Movers. Now to whom should he give? He had not gone far when he saw a blind man coming, blind, and with him was a daughter, a girl. He asked, 'Brother, who are you?' And he was also crying. He said, 'What happened?' He said, 'I am a Sayyid, and this... I mean, this is my daughter. This is my daughter. Now I have no dowry for her. So, what should I do?' Remember, this which they gave, it was not charity. He said, 'Take everything, give it all away.' I mean, he did not say it is charity. Because charity is forbidden for the Sadaat (descendants of the Prophet). So, it is not charity. And let me tell you more about Ismail ibn Abbad Taliqani, that in the month of Ramadan, he used to set a table for Iftar every day. In which 1,000 people used to eat. 1,000 people used to break their fast every day. Anyway, so he said, 'Brother, who are you?' 'I am a Sayyid, I am blind, this is my daughter, and I have no money for her, I cannot buy dowry, I cannot get her married.' He said, 'All these things are yours, you take everything.' As soon as the Sayyid heard this, he fainted. He fainted, became unconscious. Then when he regained consciousness, anyway, he said, 'You take it, everything is done.' Sahib Ismail ibn Abbad, who was famous by the name of Sahib. So, Sahib was informed that 'Brother, such and such happened.' He asked, 'Brother, what happened?' So, the Sayyid told the whole story. So, he said, 'You do not take this.' Ismail ibn Abbad said, 'You do not take this. I will arrange a whole different dowry for you. This will be from your money, this is for you, this is not for you, leave this.' Is it clear? This is the result when children, when they are taught from childhood, 'Look, you this...' and one should always pray for the children, one does not know whose prayer might be answered, how, whose prayer Allah might accept, no one knows. Parents should always keep praying for their children, and what should they pray for? Not for the wealth of the world. Nothing will happen with the wealth of the world. Okay, in the world, it is not that one should not pray for that, but the main thing that parents should pray for is that their afterlife should be correct. The afterlife should not be ruined. Always remain attached to the hem of Allah, His Messenger, and the Imams. One does not know whose prayer might be answered when, how, where, when Allah guides someone, no one knows anything about anyone. If you read the event of Karbala, then in Karbala... Such people came to help Imam Husayn (a.s.) that you will be surprised to hear. You will be surprised. That there is a Christian. He is bringing his mother and his wife after getting married on the way. And a glance of grace from the Hujjat of Allah (the Proof of God) happens, a glance of kindness, and he not only becomes a Shia but sacrifices his life to be martyred. He joins the Imam. Now when the day of Ashura came, when the companions started being martyred one by one, the mother insisted, 'Go son, be sacrificed. Go son, give your life.' The mother insisted a lot, so the son came and stood before Imam Husayn (a.s.) with folded hands. That person's name was Wahab al-Kalbi. He stood before him with folded hands. 'O son of the Messenger, give me permission.' Imam Husayn (a.s.) is silent, 'How can I give him permission now?' He is the only support of his mother, and he has just brought his wife after taking her from her father's house. She has not even reached her husband's house yet. How can we give her permission? Imam Hussain (a.s.) was silent; Imam Hussain (a.s.) bowed his head. Suddenly, a voice came from behind the curtain, 'Maula, please grant permission, Maula.' Hussain (a.s.) granted permission. Now Wahab al-Kalbi came, he got ready. As he was about to leave, his wife was standing at the door, at the entrance of the tent. He said, 'What do you want? Why are you standing there?' She said, 'I want you to take me to Maula one last time; I want to place my request before Maula now.' Wahab al-Kalbi brought her to Maula. Maula asked, 'What do you want to say?' She said, 'Maula, you know that I have left my father's house, and now he is also going to be martyred. I have no one left in the world. Just grant me permission that after his martyrdom, I may stay in the tents with the ladies so that I remain safe. May my honor remain protected.' Hussain (a.s.) heard this and bowed his head. What could he say? Hussain (a.s.) could not say anything. Now Wahab al-Kalbi left. He had not gone far when he felt footsteps behind him. When he turned to look, he saw his wife following him. He said, 'O believer, why are you coming now? You had already bid me farewell.' She said, 'Wahab, when you left, I saw that Hussain (a.s.) sat on the ground and was reciting a dirge: Waa Ghurbata, Waa Ghurbata (Alas, the loneliness! Alas, the loneliness!). All the companions are being killed.' I would say, 'O wife of Wahab al-Kalbi, you saw such an easy scene and you were shaken? Ask the heart of Zainab (s.a.).' It is the afternoon of Ashura. What scene is Zainab (s.a.) witnessing? That Shimr is sitting on his chest. Zainab (s.a.) could do nothing. She called out, 'O son of Sa'd, do you see that my mother's son is being slaughtered?' Sayalamu-lladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, wal-'aqibatu lil-muttaqin (And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned, and the outcome is for the righteous). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and companions. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are troubled. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant children to those who are childless, righteous and virtuous offspring. Grant complete and swift recovery to those who are ill. Especially those who have requested prayers, grant them complete and swift recovery. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. O Lord, protect the great scholars and the esteemed Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Whoever protects them, You protect them. Grant us the blessing of visiting Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Accept this small act of mourning of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: EP05 | Fadak Ka Mutaaleba | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn | Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Fatimiyyah (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical event of Fadak, focusing on the demand made by Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) after the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It highlights the injustice faced by the Ahlulbayt when the Prophet's gift was seized and his document was disregarded by the government of the time. The speaker emphasizes the significance of the Princess's sermon at the Mosque and calls for believers to continue defending the rights of the Ahlulbayt today.
content:
The Bibi presented the document of her father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in which she was gifted [Fadak]. Those who recited the Kalima of the Messenger paid the reward of Risalat by tearing the document of the Messenger, and finally, the Ayat-e-Karima was revealed. So the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) made a promise and vow to God, and after his daughter, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), the government sent its soldiers... After that, the government sent its soldiers and seized these lands. When the news of this reached the Princess of the World, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), she took some of her maids and women of the tribe and went towards the Mosque. The Princess's immediate departure to the Mosque upon hearing this news is proof that she did not tolerate remaining silent when her right was usurped. Demanding it when it is snatched away is a sign of the righteous. Therefore, we should also continue to defend the right of the Princess of the World, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), as long as we live in this world. It is found in history that the Princess's style of walking was exactly like her father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). A curtain was used for her, she sat behind it, and began to speak in such a way that the people with her also started crying. She paused so that the noise of the crowd would stop and their cries would subside. Then she began her speech with the praise of Allah and blessings upon her father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Then it began, the sermon was short, the Princess gave a long and historical sermon... The sermon is famous by the name of Khutbah. In her demand, she presented Imam Ali (a.s.) and Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.) as witnesses, but the government rejected all their testimonies. Those people read a fabricated and forged verse of the Quran, which declares Hazrat Sulaiman (a.s.) as the heir of Hazrat Dawood (a.s.) and Hazrat Yahya (a.s.) as the heir of Hazrat Zakariya (a.s.). Those who claimed 'The Book of Allah is enough for us' did not even look at this verse of the Holy Quran. After this, the document of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in which she was gifted [Fadak]... those who recited the Kalima of the Messenger paid the reward of Risalat by tearing the document of the Messenger, and finally... When the best provider will be Allah, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) will be honored. The Day of Judgment will come, and at that hour, they will be among our people. And at that time, your regret will be of no benefit to you. He acted upon the Sunnah of the Princess (s.a.). O Allah, I beseech You by the right of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the right of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.).
