title: Kya Imam Ali (a.s.) Aise Logon Se Raazi Reh Sakte Hain? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual connection between the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his daughter, Janabe Zahra (s.a.). It highlights the prophetic tradition stating that angering Fatima (s.a.) is equivalent to angering the Prophet and Allah. The speaker questions how Imam Ali (a.s.) could maintain ties with those who caused grief to his wife, emphasizing the necessity of distancing oneself from those who oppose the Ahlulbayt.
content:
The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself stated, 'Fatimatu bid'atun minni, faman aghdhabaha aghdhabani' (Fatima is a part of me; whoever angers her, angers me). Now, Abul Hasan brother, tell me, if someone caused grief to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), who caused grief to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and even caused grief to Allah, then how can my Maula maintain good relations or good ties with those people? Absolutely correct. In this regard, a couplet by the master poet Manzoor Azmi Sahib comes to mind: 'Some people do not like my Maula. Now, Abul Hasan brother, please listen, and I request the audience to listen: Some people do not like my Maula, and for that reason, some people do not like me.'
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared that Fatima (s.a.) is a part of him.
Angering Fatima (s.a.) is equivalent to angering the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Allah.
Imam Ali (a.s.) cannot maintain positive relations with those who caused grief to Janabe Zahra (s.a.).
The grief of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is a matter of divine displeasure.
Loving the Maula necessitates distancing oneself from his enemies.
The bond between the Prophet and his daughter is central to Islamic faith.

title: Ep#19 | Ashaab e Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Kaise Honge?
excerpt: This lecture explores the essential qualities and ethical standards required for those who aspire to be among the companions of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Based on a tradition from Imam Ali (a.s.), the speaker details the specific oaths of conduct, such as honesty, justice, and humility, that the Imam will require from his followers. The talk emphasizes that preparing for the reappearance of the Imam involves both spiritual refinement and practical adherence to these moral commitments in our daily lives.
content:
It was issued from there at that time, water was polluted, and chili was mixed. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And peace be upon you, O son of the best of creation. May Allah grant us the benefit of the noble knowledge that we have received. Respected viewers, it is the heartfelt desire of all of us that we be counted among the close companions and followers of our Imam of the time. But as we know and observe in our daily lives, for every important position, a person must possess certain qualities. So, when we desire to be included among the companions of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), should we not cultivate certain qualities for this position? Especially when we see that the mission of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is the very mission for which we are all waiting. Let us try to understand in the light of traditions what the characteristics of the companions of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) are. Although there are many narrations on this subject, the narration we have chosen today is from our Mawla, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), in which he mentions Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) will surely appear, and what promises he will take from his companions, what oaths he will take—he has mentioned that. So, a little bit of detail—that is, the author of the book has mentioned this narration in his book and says that I narrate from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). He says that our Imam (a.s.) will take these promises from his companions. This taking of promises by Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) from his companions draws attention to the fact that if we desire to be included among the companions of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), we should also try to prepare ourselves to fulfill these promises. The Imam (a.s.) will say to his companions, 'I will support you only when you fulfill these promises.' What are these promises? Let us listen to them carefully. Imam (a.s.) will take a promise from them that they will never steal. They will never be greedy—they will not be like the people of today. And along with this, the Imam will also take from them that they will not shed blood unjustly, neither in secret nor openly. They will not shed blood, neither in secret nor openly. They will not attack anyone unjustly. They will not destroy any Muslim. Today, if we look at the conditions of our society, this is not considered a sin. To mock a believer, to insult them—people think it is a joke, that there is no harm in doing these things. But in the eyes of the Imam (a.s.), this is a very grave sin. Along with this, the Imam (a.s.) will also take a promise from them that they will never hoard gold, silver, wheat, or barley. That is, what we call 'hoarding' in English, which is a major problem in today's society, where greedy people hoard things to increase prices. But the Imam (a.s.) will not accept this behavior from his companions at all. And along with this, the Imam (a.s.) will bring their attention to an important promise: that they will never consume the property of an orphan. Today, if we look at the state of our society, this has become rampant. People think that since the orphan has no one behind them, they can consume the orphans' wealth without thinking. People forget that they are not consuming the orphan's wealth, but are entering the fire of Hell into their stomachs. This is the promise the Imam (a.s.) will take from his companions: that they will never consume the right of an orphan. Along with this, the Imam (a.s.) will also take a promise from them that they will only testify when they are absolutely certain, and if they are not certain, they will not testify. They will never destroy any mosque. They will never insult any Muslim. That is, it will not be acceptable to the Imam (a.s.) at all that any of his companions should insult any Muslim. And along with this, the Imam will also take an oath from them that they will not speak ill of any believer or worker. If we look at this, the Imam (a.s.) is showing us a way of action that we need to prepare for today. Along with this, the Imam (a.s.) will take from them that they will never drink alcohol, and they will never wear gold, silver, or silk, or clothes made from them. Along with this, the Imam will draw their attention to another oath: that they will never betray a trust. They will never betray a trust. Pausing here, I would like to present another point to all the viewers: trust is not only about things that are entrusted to someone. Betrayal of trust also happens in matters of secrets, where one believer tells a secret to another believer, and they go and reveal that secret to others. This is also a form of betrayal. Therefore, the Imam (a.s.) will take a promise from his companions that they will never betray a trust. They will never remain in the company of those who are corrupt. We do not like this either. And along with this, the Imam (a.s.) will take an oath that they will wear coarse or rough clothing—that is, what we call 'coarse clothes' in English, which are very rough—they will prefer such clothing for themselves. They will make the earth their pillow. They will always strive in the way of Allah. They will dislike filth. They will practice 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' (enjoining good) and 'Nahy an al-Munkar' (forbidding evil). Today, a major problem in our society is that sometimes, even knowing that our friend or relative will not mind our words, why do we hesitate to practice 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' and 'Nahy an al-Munkar'? We hesitate to invite people towards goodness and stop them from evil. So, the Imam (a.s.) will take this promise from his companions. Viewers, when the Imam (a.s.) has taken these promises from his companions, then we find a narration that the Imam (a.s.) will say to them, 'If you do all this—that is, if you fulfill these promises—then I also make these promises to you.' And the Imam (a.s.) will promise them a few things. What is this promise? If the Imam (a.s.) says to them, 'If you fulfill all these promises, firstly, I will never be far from you; I will always remain close to you.' And along with this, the Imam will promise them that whatever you wear, I will wear; whatever vehicle you use, I will use the same. Then the Imam (a.s.) gives a very important glad tiding: 'I will be satisfied even with your small deeds.' And along with this, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'If you fulfill these promises, I will fill this earth with justice just as it will be filled with oppression.' I will speak the truth that is its right, that is, the Imam (a.s.) today... It is his right, or not? The Imam (a.s.) today also has the right to speak the truth, to make such a promise. But at that time, when the Imam (a.s.) will say this, people will see the Imam (a.s.) worshipping and will understand what the right of worship is. The Imam (a.s.) will further say to them, 'I will fulfill these promises, and you also fulfill these promises.' Respected viewers, Alhamdulillah, Allah has given us a life of ease, but from these promises, one thing becomes very clear: if we want to be included among the companions of the Imam (a.s.), we will have to prepare for all these things. Both spiritually and practically, and in this era of mercy, as much as possible, we must try to perform these actions and strive to make our deeds such that our Imam (a.s.) keeps us among his companions. So, whatever is written in a person's destiny, they should accept the Wilayah of Imam Hassan (a.s.) and ask through their intercession. Apart from this, another Hadith is found, and this Lawh and Qalam thing is very interesting. We will discuss this a little. Another Hadith related to this light is found in another narration, that Allah (swt) created the sun and the moon from the light of Imam Hassan (a.s.). Dear viewers, the creation of the sun and the moon happened from the light of Imam Hassan (a.s.). If you look, you cannot imagine the world without the sun and the moon. Everything in this entire universe, in this whole world, benefits from the light of the sun. And after that, all things—trees, plants—everything that is growing... trees, plants—everything that is growing, this entire universe, is through the light of the sun and the moon. And they were created from a part of the light of Imam Hassan (a.s.). The sun and the moon are part of the manifestation of Imam Hassan (a.s.). The sun, which a person cannot look at with their naked eyes, that sunlight is just a part of the light of Imam Hassan (a.s.). This is about the sun and the moon being created from his light. And before that, regarding the Lawh and Qalam, there is a very interesting Hadith in the book of Ibn Razi, in which the narrator is Abdullah bin Mas'ud. He says: 'I went to the service of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and I asked the Prophet, "O Messenger of Allah, show me the Truth (Haq) so that I may be influenced by it, so that I may hold onto it." I want to attach myself to the Truth, to keep myself connected to the Truth.' And in the narration of Ibn Razi, Abdullah bin Mas'ud said, "O Messenger, show me." And we all know that Hadith where the Prophet said, "Allah is with the Truth, and the Truth is with Ali. O Allah, keep the Truth with Ali wherever Ali turns." So, Abdullah bin Mas'ud... So, Abdullah bin Mas'ud asked, "O Messenger of Allah, show me the Truth, I want to see it." The Prophet said, "Abdullah, wait, go to that room." And then Abdullah bin Mas'ud says, "I went into that room, and I saw Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) there. And I saw that Ali (a.s.) was in the state of prayer, in the state of Ruku, and in the state of Sujud. He was saying in his Ruku, 'O Allah, for the sake of Muhammad, Your servant, and for the sake of all the Prophets, forgive the sins of my Shia who have committed mistakes.'" Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was praying in his Ruku and Sujud. This is not the prayer of an ordinary person; this is the prayer of an Imam, who is praying for his Shia, "Forgive those among my Shia who have committed mistakes." As soon as Abdullah bin Mas'ud saw this, he came out of the room and went to the Prophet to tell him what he had seen. As soon as he reached the Prophet... Tell us what he saw when he reached the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and saw that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was becoming ill. Now, in the final moments, what was the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) praying in his prayer? 'Allahumma bi haqqi Ali ibn Abi Talib...' (O Allah, by the right of Ali ibn Abi Talib...). Now look, he was saying, 'O Lord, by the right of Ali ibn Abi Talib...' This was the intercession, the one who is Your servant—let no one think of Ali as anything else—O Prophet, what are you saying? 'O Lord, by the right of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the intercession of Ali ibn Abi Talib, this intercession is for those of my Ummah, those who believe in me, those who love me, those who are among the sinners, forgive them.' Now, when Abdullah ibn Mas'ud saw this, he looked inside the room and saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) invoking the intercession of Ali. He came outside and saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was still invoking the intercession of Ali. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud became angry. When he came out of the house, he thought, 'What is this? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is helping him, or is he helping the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)?' When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came out, he asked, 'What happened?' Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said, 'O Prophet of Allah, I do not understand. I see that you are invoking him, and he is invoking you. Who is superior between you and Ali?' Upon this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Abdullah, sit down in this world...' Sit down in this world, and sit. So when he sat down, he (the Prophet) held his hand, and then he narrated the luminous tradition regarding the creation of their light. He said, 'O Abdullah, Allah the Almighty created my light and Ali's light from the light of His own Majesty, 2,000 years before the creation of all creatures. At that time, when He created them, there was nothing there—no Allah's creation, no throne, no nothing. First, the light of the Prophet and Ali was created. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Then Allah took a part of my light and created the heavens and the earth from it, and that is why I am the weight of the heavens and the earth. title: Majlis 5 | Mukhtasar Tareekh-e-Azadaari | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the historical and theological significance of Azadari, tracing the efforts of the Ahlulbayt to preserve the true essence of Islam against Umayyad and Abbasid distortions. The discourse highlights the importance of historical awareness, the practice of Tabarra, and the moral responsibilities of believers in the face of oppression. Through the lens of Karbala, the lecture emphasizes the resilience of figures like Janabe Zaynab and the necessity of maintaining the tradition of mourning as a form of judicial inquiry into the truth.

To deprive those who have a right to this Bayt al-Mal of their right? By God, I swear by Allah," the Commander of the Faithful says, "No, even if only two people are left alive in the universe, I will not do this. I will never do this. I will distribute the wealth exactly as it is the right to distribute it." After that, the Commander of the Faithful—now this was a general matter—the Commander of the Faithful gave us advice. Pay attention to this. The point we were making was this sentence. The Commander of the Faithful remained silent for a very, very long time. The sentence of the Hadith is that the Commander of the Faithful—this is a narration in Al-Kafi. The Hadith I just taught you is a narration from Usul al-Kafi. This is a narration from Furu al-Kafi. The Commander of the Faithful remained silent for a long time. After remaining silent, the Commander of the Faithful said, "Whoever among you is given wealth by Allah, remember to keep yourself away from corruption. Keep away from corruption. Why? Because wealth should never be in 'Tabzir'. Tabzir means wastefulness. Meaning, unnecessary extravagance is called Tabzir. And it should not be in 'Israf' either. Israf also means a kind of extravagance, but there is a difference between the two. Both are used in the Quran. Both are used in the Quran. Never be extravagant. Do only as much as is necessary, that's it. Because if a person is extravagant, there is no end to it." So the Imam says, "If you are extravagant—meaning here, what is meant by extravagance? Spending money in places where people are not deserving of it. Just giving money for your own name and for your own show so that some title is attached to your name. So, for all those titles." He says that this might make your name big in society, but you will fall in the eyes of Allah. You will fall in the eyes of Allah. Because if any person ever keeps wealth in a place where it should not be spent, then the people of the world might praise him, they might laud him, but this cannot be anything other than false praise. And after that, the Imam says a sentence, and what could be a worse fate and worse wealth and what could be a worse thing than a person spending his wealth in this way? And then he says, "If Allah has given wealth to any of you, then use it for a few things." And what are those things? The first thing is to give to your relatives. فَالِصِلْ بِهِ الْقَرَابَةَ (Connect with it to your relatives). Whatever their need is, fulfill it. The second thing is to host the believers; meaning, be a host for the believers, show them hospitality. And free the prisoners. Help the travelers. These are the real tasks through which you will get honor in both this world and the hereafter. This is the way of the Ahl al-Bayt. This is a narration in the fourth volume of Al-Kafi. And after that, he says, 'Look, if someone comes to you for basic needs, basic needs—and the Imam is saying this for basic needs—like food, things like that.' He even mentioned it. He said, "Never send them back empty-handed. Never send them back empty-handed." This is a very important thing. لَا تُعَانِيوُا قَرْضَ الْخَمِيرِ وَاتِّبَاعِ الدَّارِ (Do not be stingy with the loan of leaven and the following of the house). Why? If you do this, it will increase the sustenance of your family. If you give to others, your family's [sustenance will increase]. And you will be elevated in the eyes of Allah. And then the final sentence the Imam says is that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, the Imam says that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "O Ali, there are three characters that you should always adopt, through which you will get elevation in this world and the hereafter. One, forgive the one who oppresses you. Meaning, in the relationships that happen in the world, forgive them. Two, the relative who severs ties with you, you maintain ties with them. Do not sever ties. If they sever ties with you, let them do it. You greet them from your side. If they don't, it doesn't matter. The third thing is this: when an ignorant person addresses you, then with your 'Hilm' (forbearance) and 'Burd-bari' (patience), deal with the ignorant person." And then he says, "O Ali, just this last sentence. O Ali, run quickly towards four things before four other things come. This is for all the youth. And he is saying this based on experience. The Hadith and the youth. Listen very carefully. Run quickly towards four things before four things come towards you. One, use your youth before old age comes. Use your youth in the path of Allah. Usually, what do people do? They use their youth in the disobedience of Allah and think they will do it when they get old. When will they perform Hajj? In old age. As if they brought a guarantee that they will live. Has anyone brought a guarantee? No one has. So, youth. Second thing, use your health before you get sick. No one knows when they will get sick. Use your health in the path of Allah. The strength that Allah has given, O youth, this strength is given by Allah. Use it. Use it for Namaz-e-Shab (night prayer). Use it for the service of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.), use it for the service of the Ahl al-Bayt. Use it for 'Ta'qibat' (post-prayer supplications), for supplications, for the Quran; use this strength. Later, when you become old, you will not be able to do it. You will think you will do it, but when you get sick, you won't be able to do anything. وَغِنَاكَ قَبْلَ فَقْرِكَ (And your wealth before your poverty). And the wealth you have, use it in the right way, otherwise you will become poor. Once poverty comes, once wealth slips out of your hands, then you will be able to do nothing but wring your hands. You will only say 'if only, if only'. If only it were like that. So whatever wealth you have today, use it in the path of Allah. Spend it. Do not sit on the money, spend it in the path of Allah. And the fourth thing, spend your life completely in the path of Allah before death comes to you. Once death comes, it's over. Then the story is over, then you can't do anything. And never rely on others that we are missing prayers, our children will complete them. No, no. Nowadays, it is very rare to find children who care about their parents' missed prayers. Meaning, the father's prayer is obligatory on the son, on the eldest son. It is obligatory on the eldest son, the father's prayer. The mother's prayer is not obligatory, yes. The father's prayer is obligatory, remember this. This is the Sharia issue we are telling you. The father's prayer is obligatory. And on the eldest son, not on other sons. You will rarely find individuals who care that our father's prayer is remaining, our father's fast is remaining, our father did not perform Hajj. Nowadays, such children are not even found in museums. They don't even care to do something in the father's name, something in the mother's name, to do some good deeds for them. So, do it yourself, don't wait for anyone. Leave this world having done everything yourself. Whatever is possible. And these are the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So far, we have mentioned the martyrdom of the companions; today, after the family of Aqeel, it is the turn of the family of Jafar. Jafar ibn Abi Talib is the brother of Amirul Momineen (a.s.). You know what Amirul Momineen (a.s.) used to always say? He would say that if Hamza, my uncle, and Jafar, my brother, were both alive, I would have fought for my caliphate. Amirul Momineen (a.s.) was so proud of Jafar ibn Abi Talib. And that is why he gave his daughter Zaynab to Jafar's son, Abdullah, to Janabe Abdullah. He married his daughter Janabe Zaynab to Janabe Abdullah. And they had sons, Janabe Awn and Janabe Muhammad. And it is the night of their martyrdom that we commemorate today. It is strange and remarkable that when all the companions were killed and the family of Aqeel was killed, Janabe Zaynab started telling her two children, 'Go and sacrifice yourselves for your uncle.' The children said, 'Mother, you go and ask the uncle yourself.' Janabe Zaynab took both children and stood before Hussain (a.s.). She stood silently. The Imam asked, 'Zaynab, what do you want to say?' She said, 'Brother, you know what I want to say, and I am sure you will not turn down my request. I trust you; you will not turn down my request. Brother, give these two permission so they can go and be martyred.' Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Zaynab, today is the day of martyrdom.' Hussain (a.s.) gave permission. As soon as he gave permission, the account in the Maqtal is strange; you too should pay attention: Janabe Zaynab brings both children into the tent and starts preparing them herself. And while preparing them, she keeps advising them, 'Son, look, be sacrificed, be sacrificed for your uncle. Son, look, I know you are hungry and thirsty for three days, but remember two things. Son, one is that you should fight in such a way that the enemy understands you are the grandsons of Ali ibn Abi Talib and the grandsons of Jafar ibn Abi Talib.' 'Why should you say that you belong to the Wali of God? Let the army cry out that they are the grandsons of Ali.' And the second thing to keep in mind, son, is that I know you are thirsty. You are children, you are not very old yet. You are thirsty, children, but look, do not even let the thought of water come to you. Do not turn towards the water, do not turn towards the Euphrates. Do not even let the thought of water come to you. Yes, children, Sakina is thirsty in the tent, Asghar is thirsty, the children are thirsty. She gave great advice. Zaynab gave advice. She sent the children off. Now, there is a strange phrase in the Maqtal: one brother attacked from one side, the other from the other, and they did it in such a way that the army of Sham began to run here and there. Then Ibn Sa'ad said, 'Hey, these are the children of Bani Hashim, surround them and kill them. Surround them and kill them.' So the wretched ones surrounded them, surrounded the children, and started killing them. They did it to such an extent that both children called out, 'Uncle, accept our final salaam.' Hussain (a.s.) arrived with the strength of his arm, Abul Fazl Abbas. By the time he arrived, both children had departed from this world. Hussain (a.s.) picked up the body of one, and Abbas picked up the body of the other. They brought them and placed them in the tent. Then Zaynab said, 'Lady, the princes have arrived. Come, the princes have arrived.' Zaynab was on her prayer mat. She asked, 'Why have you come? I did not ask you to come.' She said, 'Lady, come and see.' Now when Zaynab saw, she performed the prostration of gratitude. 'O Lord, thank You, taqabbal minni. O Lord, accept my sacrifice.' It is nowhere written that Zaynab shed tears for her beloved ones. On the 11th of Muharram, when Zaynab began to leave Karbala, even then she did not grieve for her children. She grieved for Hussain (a.s.). When she reached Kufa, even then she did not grieve for her children. She came to Sham, even then she did not. After that, when Zaynab was released and reached Medina, and Abdullah ibn Jafar did not even recognize Janabe Zaynab at first. Such mountains of tragedies had broken upon her. Zaynab had become completely aged. Abdullah could not recognize her. When he recognized her, he brought Zaynab into the house. 'Now, Lady, come.' He brought her. Now when Zaynab came, her eyes fell upon a cradle, upon two small beds. Zaynab's heart broke. 'O Awn, O Muhammad, O Hussain.' Wa sayalamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Alal la'natullahi alal qawmiz zalimin. O Lord, O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the privilege of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Accept this small act of mourning of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: Lamentation for Lady Sakina
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a poignant recitation depicting the suffering and loneliness of Lady Sakina in captivity.

chapters.title: Racing Towards Goodness
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the Quranic command to race towards goodness, identifying the Ahlulbayt as the ultimate source of all virtue.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Yazid and Historical Context
chapters.summary: The speaker contrasts the moral decay of Yazid with the noble mission of Imam Hussain to preserve Islam.

chapters.title: The Knowledge of Maytham al-Tammar
chapters.summary: An introduction to the companions of Imam Ali, specifically Maytham al-Tammar, and the reliability of the historical traditions narrated by Sheikh al-Saduq.

chapters.title: Prophecies of Maytham al-Tammar
chapters.summary: Maytham al-Tammar recounts Imam Ali's prophecies regarding the martyrdom of Imam Hussain and the cosmic mourning that follows.

chapters.title: Fabricated Traditions and the Distortion of History
chapters.summary: The lecture explains how enemies of the Ahlulbayt fabricated Hadiths to turn the day of Ashura into a day of celebration.

chapters.title: The Identity of Shi'ism and Tabarra
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that the true identity of a Shia is defined by Tabarra (disassociation from enemies) rather than just acknowledging virtues.

chapters.title: Majlis-e-Aza as a Court of Inquiry
chapters.summary: The Majlis is presented as a court of inquiry established by Janabe Zainab to investigate the historical roots of the tragedy of Karbala.

chapters.title: Fabrication of Ashura as a Day of Joy
chapters.summary: The Banu Umayya fabricated hadiths to frame Ashura as a day of celebration and fasting to counter the influence of Ghadir.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ziyarat Ashura
chapters.summary: Ziyarat Ashura is presented as a Hadith Qudsi that exposes the historical enmity of the Banu Umayya and the family of Ziyad toward the Ahl al-Bayt.

chapters.title: Historical Suppression and Preservation of Azadari
chapters.summary: For centuries, various ruling dynasties attempted to erase Azadari, while others like the Buyids and Fatimids helped re-establish and spread the remembrance of Imam Husayn.

chapters.title: The Value of Preserving the Cause
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that Azadari is not a guaranteed right but a legacy that must be actively protected and valued by the Shia community.

chapters.title: Defining Glory and the Caliphate of Ali
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan defines glory as bearing burdens and building virtues, while Imam Ali demonstrates these principles by refusing to compromise justice for political expediency.

chapters.title: Proper Use of Wealth and Social Responsibility
chapters.summary: The Imam warns against wastefulness and extravagance, emphasizing that wealth should be used to support relatives, host believers, and assist the needy.

chapters.title: Urgency in Worship and Moral Conduct
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the importance of acting during youth and health, urging believers to prioritize spiritual duties before old age and death arrive.

chapters.title: Religious Obligations and Personal Responsibility
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the religious duty of the eldest son to fulfill the missed prayers and fasts of the father, while encouraging everyone to perform good deeds for themselves.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Awn and Muhammad
chapters.summary: The lecture recounts the martyrdom of Janabe Zaynab's sons, Awn and Muhammad, highlighting her strength and dedication to the cause of Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: Janabe Zaynab's Resilience and Final Supplication
chapters.summary: Janabe Zaynab's reaction to the loss of her sons and her eventual return to Medina are described, followed by a concluding prayer for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time.

title: Majlis #5: Hawas (Carnal Desires) | Ahle Bait (a.s.): Daawate Husnaa | Muharram 1443
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual dangers of following carnal desires (Hawas) and the necessity of aligning one's intellect with the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. It emphasizes that the self can become a false god when driven by ego, and that true guidance is found only through divine revelation and the wisdom of the Imams. The session also covers the importance of digital accountability, the power of supplication, and the profound sacrifices made for the sake of Imam Hussain (a.s.).
content:
[Quranic recitation] [Quranic recitation and concluding remarks] It seems like scientific evidence... [unclear audio]... Assalamu Alaikum, Ghulam Rasool... [unclear audio]... the 356th Urs was concluded by the Chief Electoral Officer. It was concluded, or the journey until the final round... [unclear audio]... Assalamu Alaikum Ya Rasool Allah... [unclear audio]... [music]... [unclear audio]... love for him... [unclear audio]... [unclear audio]... I am speaking, I will appeal to the followers... [unclear audio]... I will subscribe to the Messenger of Allah... [unclear audio]... very beautiful... [unclear audio]... [music]... [unclear audio]... How should I take you away from the life of Sakina? How should I take you away from the life of Sakina? If you are wounded by arrows, you haven't slept yet. If you are wounded by arrows, you haven't slept yet. How can I sleep peacefully? Sakina, let the world see the wounds on my body. Let the world see the wounds on my body. If you are a trust of Baba, then keep your life safe. Keep your life safe... [music]... how should I give you life? Sakina, come with me to Medina, my sister. Come with me to Medina, my sister. If you are not with me, how will I explain to mother? How will I explain to mother, Sakina? How should I take you away from the life of Sakina? [music]... Where will you go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? Where will you go? Understand this today. Ask for the Kalima today, O traveler. Where will the followers of Muhammad go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? We do not befriend enemies. When the time comes, where will the martyrs go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? If you are not a Muslim, do not do this. Where will you go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? Come, mourn, beat your chest. Otherwise, where will the one who is restless go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? The one in whose prostrations Ali's Wilayah is not included, where will that person go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? They snatched away the garden of Zahra (s.a.). Where will the oppressors go? We have love for Islam, where will you go? This is my favorite poem in the entire speech. Which is my favorite city in this entire discourse? Where will the one who is not a follower go? Look at the field of Hashr (Resurrection), look at the greatness of the field of Hashr, look at the greatness of the field of Hashr, who will buy Paradise? Where will the one who is not innocent go? Even if one is not innocent, but is innocent in deeds, he will be granted Paradise. Where will the one who is not a follower go? Whatever eyes weep for the sake of the day, let them weep, let them weep for the sake of the day, let them weep, let them weep. Where will the one who is not a follower go? We have the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. And peace and blessings be upon the best of the prophets and messengers, our master and our prophet, Abul Qasim Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). May Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his pure progeny. And may Allah's peace be upon the chosen ones, the pure ones, the righteous ones, the guided ones, the leaders of the people, the ones who are the proof of Allah upon the creation, and the ones who are the light of Allah upon the earth. And the ones who are the guides of the people. May Allah's peace be upon them. The topic of today's discussion is what is the third thing that the human being follows? And what is the third thing that leads to destruction? The main topic is what is the third thing that leads to destruction? What is the third thing that is a garment of sins for a human being? And today, the third thing that was mentioned is the following of desires. The first thing is the following of the Imam, the one who is followed and whose path is followed. And if the third thing is the following of desires, then those who follow their own desires... Those who follow their own desires, they use themselves for their own desires. And those who follow their own desires, can Allah guide them? No, Allah cannot guide them, and they will have no helpers. There will be no one to help them. Those who follow their own desires, the self (nafs) is like a wild animal. If you leave the self uncontrolled, it will be like a wild animal that you cannot control. It will run here and there. If the self is left uncontrolled, it will lead the human being to the path of sins. As long as a human being is the rider of the self, the human being is the rider. If he does not control the self with wisdom, then this self will lead him to destruction. Therefore, the Quran says that these are the oppressors. Therefore, the Quran says that these people follow the oppressors, they use themselves for the desires of others. They do not tie their own selves. That is why in Arabic, it is called 'aqal' (to tie), the rope with which animals are tied. That is why it is called 'aqal'. This self, which is like an animal, needs to be tied so that it controls the human being. If a human being does not use this blessing of wisdom, then his end will be nothing but destruction. And this self leads to a level where Allah Himself calls this desire a god. Allah says in the Quran, Surah Al-Jathiya, verse 23: 'Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god?' What does it mean to take desire as a god? It means he has abandoned the obedience of God and started obeying his own self. If he follows his own desires, then despite that, Allah will lead him astray. Allah will lead him astray. And Allah will place a seal upon his ears and his heart. He will place a seal, so he will not hear any good words, nor will he understand anything with his heart. And Allah will place a veil over his eyes, so he will become blind. He will not see the truth. Why will he not see? Because he is following his own desires. That is why Allah will make his ears deaf and his heart sealed, and his eyes blind. He will not understand anything. Then Allah asks, 'Who will guide him after Allah?' If Allah has led him astray, it means Allah has left him to his own state. If Allah has left him to his own state, then he is astray. Allah has left him to his own state. Now, what does it matter to Allah? Allah has no sympathy for him. Are you not thinking? Don't you understand? This is the state of the one who follows his desires. The self is a god that is worshipped. When a human being listens to his own self and does not listen to Allah, then he is worshipping his own self, not Allah. And this is a general principle that applies everywhere. Therefore, you see in another hadith, 'Whoever listens to a speaker, he is worshipping that speaker.' If the speaker is speaking from Allah, then he is worshipping Allah. And if the speaker is speaking the words of Satan, then the listener is worshipping Satan. If the speaker is speaking the words of Satan, then the listener is worshipping Satan. From morning till night, how many things do we listen to? And what things do we give a place in our hearts? So, if the one who is speaking is speaking the words of Allah, then it is fine. If he is speaking the words of Allah, then he is worshipping Allah. But if we are listening to those who are not speaking the words of Allah, what is worse than the words of Allah? Is he speaking from the Quran or the Hadith? There are two things: either the Quran or the Hadith of the Prophet. If he is speaking from the Quran, then it is fine. 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Quran and my progeny.' In a better presentation, helping lives, finding the tiger—you have these positions, and if you hold them firmly, you will never be bad after me. It is a matter of life, and the speaker is quoting from Hadith. Now, you should observe: whenever you listen to a speaker, see if he is starting with Hadith or just stating his own opinions. If he is stating his own opinions, then he is from the 'Ahwa' (desires). The term 'Ahwa' was used in the time of Imam Hasan (a.s.), in the year 62, regarding those who abandoned the first path and followed others' innovations. Because the meaning of 'following others' is: whatever comes to mind, issue a fatwa; just issue a fatwa on any problem. This is what 'Ahwa' means. Remember this. After that, the term 'Ahwa' became a term for struggle and hard work. If it is for the sake of truth, it is for struggle, for effort, for pride, for difficulty. So, this 'Ahwa' is not found anywhere as a good thing. You will not find 'Ahwa' mentioned anywhere as a good thing. I said to them, 'I am with them.' Therefore, if this has happened, it is very dangerous. Listen carefully. This 'Ahwa'—from here, it has been entered into his book by Ibn Abi al-Hadid. It is not just a matter of the third century; it is about the companions of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). They are among those who wrote books, and their books are famous. So, in this book, he mentions a narration. A man came later and asked, 'What is the similarity between us and the Ahwa? How much is it?' How much is it? Today, the speaker says—excuse me—he used to say that Allah and the Quran are books, and there is no difference between them. We have seen the narrations; we have no complaints about them. [Praise] The only similarity is that they do not follow anything that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) brought. They do not follow anything that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) brought. We will avoid 'Istiqbal' (facing). One thing we have in common is that they also face the Kaaba to pray, and we also face the Kaaba to pray. That is the only similarity; nothing more. So, if Allah—may He not let me live, may He not let me live—is something that is ours, there is a difference of heaven and earth. He is the One (Tawhid); there is no image on Him, no... He is the One (Tawhid); there is no image on Him, no form, no body, and you cannot liken Him to anything or compare Him to anything. Not at all. After this, Allah is not a body that is not like other bodies. He does not have hair, He does not have curly hair, and He does not look good. Allah looks good—that is, the 'Tashbih' (anthropomorphism) of Allah is for the whole of humanity. Whatever comes to your mind, you remember it here with a meaning. Our Imams did not say this; they performed 'Tanzih' (declaring Allah free from imperfections). Even if you think about Allah and... Even if you think about Allah and imagine something about Allah, that is not Allah. The Imams say that it will return to you like yourself. It is not your Creator; it is not your Lord; it is not your Sustainer; it is not your God. This which is encompassing you is the One who cannot be contained in your eyes. And since this is a point, let me complete it: if Muslims were to reflect on the Quran in the light of Hadith, then Allah is far beyond what you can contain in your minds. The Quran says, 'Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la' [Praise the name of your Lord, the Most High]. Perform 'Tanzih'—that is, remove it from your mind. You cannot recognize the name of your Lord. Which essence of the Lord... The Lord—what is the Lord? The Imams say that if you hold onto something and say, 'This is Allah,' read it—my heart is saying this, the flood of the heart is flowing. The bird, no matter how high it flies, will return. It could not recognize the Creator. Because the 'Tamiz' (distinction) of the status of Ali (a.s.)—what is it? The 'Wali' cannot understand it. title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#08 - Darwaaze par Imam Ali (as) kyun nahin aaye?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common polemical objection regarding why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not intervene when Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.) went to the door during the attack on their home. The speaker clarifies that the attack was a premeditated, multi-stage event involving threats and the use of fire, rather than a single spontaneous incident. By citing historical sources and Quranic etiquette, the lecture argues that the attackers deliberately violated the sanctity of the Prophet's household. Ultimately, the speaker refutes the objection by highlighting that the presence of a household head does not negate the historical reality of the assault.

But this objection is being presented in such a way as if Imam (a.s.) was never present at the door. Is it correct to say such a thing? Absolutely not. If any person presents the matter in such a way that Ali (a.s.) never went to the door, then either they are accusing the Shias or they deliberately want to hide things. If we look at history, we find mention of not one, not two, but three attacks on the house of the Lady (s.a.w.a.). Where people gathered to take allegiance from Imam (a.s.), and the first time people gathered at the house of the Lady, and it was forced, that was... Gathered, and it was forced, that was, they were arrested. This is present in number 139. It is found that when all the Bani Hashim were arrested, they were told that just as others have pledged allegiance, you also pledge allegiance, otherwise, by God, swords will be drawn against you. Bani Hashim are being threatened in this way. This is the first incident when people went to the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.). After this, the second attack happened when Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) refused to pledge allegiance due to the commitment of compiling the Holy Quran. At that time, a tyrant said, 'Either you come out of the house, or we will burn this house with those inside it.' Someone said to that tyrant, 'But Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), is in this house.' But it had no effect on him, and he replied by saying that... It had no effect on him, and he replied by saying that I do not care about this. So this was the second occasion when people gathered at the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.). When these two attempts to take allegiance from Imam (a.s.) failed, then they received news, the slave who was there, he was told to go to their house and bring them out of the house to pledge allegiance. If they agree, then it is fine, otherwise, gather wood and fire and tell them that if they do not come out and pledge allegiance, the whole house will be burned down with the inhabitants. The mention of this incident is available in the book 'Al-Jamal' by Sheikh Mufid on page 117. Before I mention this attack, one thing that is worth noting here is, who was Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.)? Janabe Zahra (s.a.w.a.) was the bridge between the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Ummah. That Ummah, meaning you tell us from that perspective, the one in which the companions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) were present, from them this... The companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) were present, and it could be argued that this matter could have been handled without entering her house. However, if we look at the third attack, which Allama Majlisi describes in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 18, page 387, it is mentioned that the people not only entered the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) without permission, but they also brought fire. It is recorded that they knocked on the door of Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.) with great force, kicked it with such intensity, and when she remained steadfast in her house, a tyrant said, 'Now, neither Muhammad is among us, nor is there that revelation which used to come from Allah. If you wish, send them out, otherwise, I will burn you all.' Meaning, viewers, as we heard that there were three attacks, this proves two things. Firstly, this attack was premeditated; it can be called a pre-planned attack. Secondly, the tyrants knew who was in that house. Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was in that house, Imam Ali (a.s.) was there, and the Hasanain (a.s.) were there. Another point that becomes clear is that the tyrants did not respect the sanctity of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) household. If we look at the Holy Quran, Surah An-Nur, verse 27, it is clearly indicated: 'O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants. That is best for you; perhaps you will be reminded.' After this, verse 28 follows. After this, verse 28 follows, which states: 'And if you do not find anyone therein, do not enter them until permission has been given you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back.' This is the Quranic etiquette for all people. But here, I want to raise a question: did those who claim to be followers of the Book forget the Quran's teachings so quickly? Look, this house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.)—what kind of house was it? It was the house where even the Angel of Death would enter only after seeking permission. Should the Ummah not have respected this house? Especially when the Princess (s.a.) had told those tyrants to leave, should they not have obeyed her command and returned? Instead, we see they gathered fire and wood, burned the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), and... Burned the door of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and entered the house by force. These tyrants not only insulted the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) household but also showed no regard for the sanctity of Allah (s.w.t.), the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This incident is mentioned in the books of the other school of thought as well, which we have already presented in this series. However, a question still remains: what is the answer to the question raised about Imam Ali's (a.s.) silence? As I mentioned earlier, the goal of some is to prove that this incident never happened, and they want to use the bravery and courage of Imam Ali (a.s.) to support this claim. They raise the objection: 'How could someone as brave as Ali (a.s.) let this happen at his door?' But our question is, to decide... To decide that despite being in the house, his presence at the door is a question of his courage and bravery—this is a way people object, saying that if he were there, he would have fought. If we look at the life of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself, there were many times when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was present at home, but someone else opened the door. So, if someone wants to raise an objection against Ali (a.s.) for allowing this without his permission while he was present, they should first ask the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself: 'O Prophet, you were at home, so why did your wife go to the door?' The question arises here. To complete my point, I want to present an interesting incident to the viewers. This incident is found in the mother of books, Sahih Bukhari, Volume 6, page 349, where it is mentioned that the incident is incomplete. The incident is incomplete, but it goes like this: when Marwan was sent by Muawiyah to put pressure on Abdur Rahman, and he insisted that he should start the allegiance, Abdur Rahman said some things that made Marwan very angry, and he ordered his arrest. Abdur Rahman fled and took refuge in his sister's house, so they could not arrest him. They were looking for him, but he had taken refuge in his sister's house. When Marwan found out, he recited verse 16 of Surah Al-Ahqaf and said, 'What is the meaning of this, Abdur Rahman?' In the beginning of this verse, Allah says: 'But one who says to his parents, "Uff to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the dead]..."' Meaning, he is saying to his parents, 'Are you threatening me?' When I gave a fitting reply to Abdur Rahman that in our matter... That in our matter, there is nothing, and in the Quran, it is mine. Besides this, nothing remains in my favor in the Quran. Here the question is, those who raise this objection, our question to them is: either tell Abdur Rahman why he went to his sister's house to take refuge, or we will say that the other situation could be that in the eyes of the people, there was no such sanctity, so they did not enter Aisha's house without permission. That is why Abdur Rahman took refuge in the house of Aisha, who was his sister. And viewers, reflect on this: those who came to the house of the Princess of the Worlds, Janabe Zahra (s.a.), are they not worse than these people? These people knew who was inside, yet despite knowing everything, they besieged the Princess's house, set fire to it, and broke down the door to enter. Broke down the door and entered. I am grateful that you answered with such clarity. Despite this, if anyone in our audience still has objections to this topic, they can contact us via our WhatsApp or our social media handles. We will try to answer their questions with evidence, Insha'Allah. We will be back tomorrow with another episode of this series, 'Attacks on the House of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and Answers to Objections.' Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Ya Ali Madad, thank you.

title: Lecture 1: The Last Sermon Of Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) | Respected H. I. SAYED MAHDI MODARRESI
excerpt: This lecture by Sayed Mahdi Modarresi examines the final sermon and the profound loneliness of Imam Ali (a.s.) during his leadership. It highlights the importance of unwavering loyalty, drawing parallels between the historical companions of the Imam and the responsibilities of believers today. The discourse emphasizes that true faith requires standing against injustice and prioritizing service to the Imam over personal comfort or social approval.

title: EP19 | Hadees-e-Saqalain Ke Nataaij | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound theological implications of Hadith al-Thaqalayn, emphasizing the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt. The discussion highlights the necessity of following the Prophet's progeny as the authoritative repositories of divine knowledge and the 'speaking Quran.' Dr. Rizvi further addresses the contradiction between professing love for the Ahlulbayt and the historical actions taken against them, calling for a sincere commitment to their teachings and moral guidance.
content:
Presenting [Music] [Applause] Rahim Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. As you know, the discussion was about Hadith al-Thaqalayn, and we have discussed it in detail. Now, we reach the final discussion on Hadith al-Thaqalayn, and that is to state the conclusions of Hadith al-Thaqalayn in light of their references. In light of the references, the first conclusion that can be derived from Hadith al-Thaqalayn is that it is proof of following the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Look, the Prophet clearly said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: one is the Book of Allah, and the other is my Ahlulbayt. If you hold onto both, you will never go astray after me.' Before moving forward, let me mention one very important point: the Prophet said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Quran and the Ahlulbayt.' The Quran is the 'silent Quran,' and the Ahlulbayt are the 'speaking Quran.' Of course, when people interpret this Hadith, they say it refers to the traditions and teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). There is no doubt in that, but when the Prophet introduced them, he introduced the persons of the Ahlulbayt themselves. Remember, it is the persons themselves. Remember, they had the pledge of allegiance (Bay'ah) performed. The very essence of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) is a cause for the guidance of humanity; their very existence is the issue. Today, who is the person of the Ahl al-Bayt? The living Imam, Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.), who is the representative of the Ahl al-Bayt today, and until the reappearance, or as long as his government remains, he will be the representative. So, when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to hold fast (tamasuk), it means that not only are their teachings to be followed, but holding fast to their noble essence is also necessary and essential. Their noble essence is the 'Kahf al-Haseen' (the fortified refuge). Imam al-Zaman (a.j.t.f.) is the 'Sirat al-Mustaqeem' (the straight path); he is the refuge for those who are distressed and helpless. Imam al-Zaman is the guide (Hadi); Imam al-Zaman guides people. Their very existence is for the guidance of people, and their teachings are for the guidance of people. This is a very important and subtle point that you should try to understand—that holding fast to Imam al-Zaman himself is necessary and essential in today's era, and of course, holding fast to the other Imams who preceded him is also required. The previous Imams, and their teachings are also to be followed. Now, look, this is as clear as the bright day that following the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) and considering them as Imams is necessary and obligatory upon every Muslim, at least in the light of Hadith al-Thaqalayn. If anyone denies this, they are denying Hadith al-Thaqalayn. Denying Hadith al-Thaqalayn means denying the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and denying the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) means denying Allah. And obviously, whoever denies the Messenger of Allah and Allah is outside the fold of religion. Now, look at how the argument for Imamate is presented. You see here, al-Tayyibi, a great scholar whose interpretations we have already discussed—and if anyone wants more details, they are present in the first volume of 'Abaqat al-Anwar' regarding Hadith al-Thaqalayn, with full explanations. Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi (r.a.) and Miran Kirmani Musawi (r.a.) have explained the entire era in great detail. So, al-Tayyibi, in his book 'Al-Kashif Sharh al-Mishkat', where he explains Hadith al-Thaqalayn, writes that holding fast to the Quran means acting upon it. This is what he writes. See, remember his perspective; we are not reading this from a Shia book. Remember, we are not reading this from a Shia book. Holding fast to the Quran means acting upon it, obeying its commands, and refraining from what it forbids. Whatever the Quran has commanded, act upon it, and whatever the Quran has forbidden, abstain from it. This is the meaning of holding fast to the Quran. And then he writes further, and the meaning of holding fast to the 'Itrah' (the Prophet's progeny) is that they should be loved. He writes one thing: they should be loved. Why? Because the Quran commanded it, 'Qul la as'alukum...' (Surah al-Shura, verse 23). 'O Prophet, say: I do not ask of you any reward for this message, except love for my near kin (Qurba), for my family.' So, they should be loved. And secondly, guidance should be sought from them. The Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) are guides (Hadi); it is our job to seek guidance from them. 'Istihda' (seeking guidance) is our responsibility. And when they guide, 'Ihtida' (accepting guidance) is also our responsibility. It is our responsibility to accept their guidance. The Ahl al-Bayt are guides; guiding is their job. But in response to them, we have two responsibilities: one is 'Istihda', which is seeking guidance from them, and the second is that when they guide, we must accept their guidance, obey their words, and not argue or question them—not asking 'how is this' or 'why is that'—but rather, accept it. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself said, in the context of this Quranic verse, 'Innama anta mundhirun wa likulli qawmin hadin' (You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide). The Prophet said, 'I am the warner, and you, Ali, are the guide for every people.' And in another interpretation of this verse, it is stated that the Imams are the guides. Furthermore, al-Tayyibi writes that their 'Seerah' (biography/conduct) should be followed. When can a person follow the Seerah of the Itrah? Only when they are familiar with their Seerah, when they are familiar with their life history, and when they are familiar with their teachings. Instead, they celebrate the enemies of the Itrah, they glorify them, and they respect them. The Ummah did this to the enemies of the Itrah. This was the statement of al-Tayyibi. Now let us look at another great Sunni theologian, the author of 'Sharh al-Maqasid', Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani. In it, after mentioning Hadith al-Thaqalayn, he writes: 'Have you not seen that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has declared the Ahl al-Bayt as the peers and companions in this regard, that holding fast and attaching oneself to both of them is what saves one from going astray?' Meaning, he has placed the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt together, and this will save a person from misguidance. The meaning of holding fast to the Quran is nothing other than seeking its sciences, its truths, and guidance from it, and the same meaning applies to holding fast to the Itrah. This is what Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani writes in his book 'Sharh al-Maqasid', Volume 2, page 222. See, it is quite clear. On page 222, see, it is quite clear what Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani, the theologian, says. And as we have told you before, why he wrote this book and what his goal was—'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa' (The Burning Thunderbolts)—it was written so that his intention was to strike such a lightning bolt upon the Shias that they would be destroyed and annihilated. But if you study the book, it will be quite clear to you that he did nothing but praise the Ahl al-Bayt. Anyway, in 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa', he writes that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called the Quran and the Itrah—who are his family, descendants, and closest relatives—see, he is making it very clear who the Itrah are. The Ahl al-Bayt are the Prophet's family, the Prophet's descendants, and the Prophet's closest relatives, the 'Qurba', the same Qurba mentioned in Surah al-Shura. The Prophet has called both of them 'Thaqalayn' (the two weighty things). The Prophet has called both of them 'Thaqalayn'. This Ibn Hajar writes: Why were they called 'Thaqalayn'? Because every precious, invaluable, and protected thing is called 'Thaqal'. Anything that is valuable and which a person keeps safe is called 'Thaqal'. And both of these—the Quran and the Itrah—are just like that, because both of them are the mines of all 'Ilm al-Ladunni' (divine knowledge) and the repositories of secrets. They are the mines of divine knowledge—the knowledge that Allah has given—and the repositories, the treasury where all this knowledge resides. And they are the source of the laws of the Sharia. This is the source of the highest wisdom and the laws of the Sharia. For this reason, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) encouraged people to follow them, to hold fast to them, and to acquire knowledge from them. He encouraged people, motivated them, and advised them that you... He advised them and urged them that you should follow them and follow them only. See, these are all great Sunni scholars. In 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa', on page 151, he has written this quite clearly. Now let us look at another reference in this regard. Nur al-Din al-Samhudi, a great scholar of religion, in his book 'Jawahir al-Aqdayn', narrates Hadith al-Thaqalayn and then writes: 'Because each of the Quran and the Itrah is a mine of divine knowledge, secrets, and the source of the laws of the Sharia, and a treasury of truths.' Meaning, whatever knowledge Allah has given, this is its treasury. This is the meaning of the Prophet's saying, 'I am the city of knowledge...' This is the meaning. If you want to understand the Quran, understand it through Ali. Come to the door of Ali, come to the door of the Progeny of Ali. You see, the interpretations (Tafsir) that are from the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), study them, look at them, study them. Study them, so if anyone wants to know these truths, they should come to their door. That is why the Prophet called both of them 'Thaqalayn'. And according to some narrations, he encouraged people to follow his Ahl al-Bayt—this is what al-Samhudi is writing, al-Samhudi is a scholar of the 10th century—he says that according to some narrations, he encouraged people to follow his Ahl al-Bayt, to hold fast to them, and to acquire knowledge from them, and he commanded them to acquire knowledge from them. All this is being written by al-Samhudi. So, if this is not Imamate, then what is Imamate? Is there anything else to Imamate? But still, people say that Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt is not proven from Hadith al-Thaqalayn. If it is not proven from Hadith al-Thaqalayn, then from what is it proven? Al-Samhudi wrote this in 'Jawahir al-Aqdayn', page 243, Part 2, Section 4. And similarly, in the last conclusion, in the reference to the first conclusion, Mulla Ali Qari writes... In the reference, Mulla Ali Qari writes. Mulla Ali Qari is a very great scholar of religion; this is also his book, a very famous book, 'Sharh al-Shifa'. In it, he writes that holding fast to the Quran means acting upon all its commands and refraining from all its prohibitions. Meaning, what is the meaning of holding fast to the Quran? To act upon whatever command the Quran has given, and to abstain from whatever it has forbidden, to keep distance from it, to abstain from it. And the meaning of holding fast to the Prophet's Itrah is to love them and to follow their Seerah. This is what Mulla Ali Qari is saying. See, this is the statement of Mulla Ali Qari in 'Sharh al-Shifa'. He writes that what is the meaning of holding fast to the Ahl al-Bayt? One is to love them. This is what the Ummah did—how did the Ummah love them? Some were killed, some were put in prisons, some were driven from place to place. This was the love the Ummah showed, this was the reward for the message (Ajar al-Risalat) the Ummah gave. This was the Ummah's reward for the message, that they killed some of the Ahl al-Bayt, put some in prisons, drove some from place to place, and paraded them in public. And the worst thing they did was that those... And the worst thing they did was that those who committed these crimes were justified and defended, and they are still doing so today. If this is the demand of love, then what is enmity? What is enmity? If killing, putting in prison, wandering from door to door, and snatching the veil from the head of a lady is love, then what is enmity? The Quran and the Prophet said to love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and the Sunni scholars also understand this meaning, but what has the Ummah done in practice and what is it doing even today? Even today, some people are shamelessly, with great shamelessness, defending a cursed and filthy person like Yazid. Now, when can a person follow the Seerah? Only when they read the Seerah, then they will follow it, right? Seerah means their life. Read their life, meaning become familiar with their teachings, their commands, and most importantly, their... Become familiar with their teachings, their commands, their beliefs, and most importantly, their beliefs. What were their beliefs? The matters of their character, their commands—read all of that. This is what Mulla Ali Qari is saying, and Mulla Ali Qari, in Volume 2, page 82, and 'Fasl-o-man Takihi', and in that way, you may refer to it to see how he has described this matter. The rest, Insha'Allah, we will try to do in the next episode. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin, wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi...

title: Ep#03 | Aaj Musalmanon Ka Imam Kaun?
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of recognizing the Imam of one's time, citing Quranic verse 17:71 and the famous Hadith regarding the 'death of ignorance.' The speaker argues that every era must have a divinely appointed Imam from the Bani Hashim, specifically the Twelve Imams of the Ahlulbayt. The talk concludes by challenging listeners to identify their Imam to avoid dying in a state of disbelief or hypocrisy.
content:
Voice of Bahrain... Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. In the previous two episodes, we have seen that the recognition of the Imam, and especially the twelve Imams, is extremely important for all Muslims. Continuing with the same topic, let us turn to a verse of the Holy Quran. Surah Bani Israil, the 17th Surah of the Quran, Surah number 17, and its verse number is 71. It is very easy to remember the reference: 17:71. In this verse of Surah Bani Israil, God Almighty states: Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. 'Yawma nad'u kulla unasin bi-imamihim' (The day We will call all people with their Imam). In this verse, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala is announcing that on the Day of Judgment—the day of resurrection—Allah will gather every human being with their Imam. Gather every human being with their Imam, raised with their Imam, called with their Imam. Now, some people interpret this verse incorrectly and take 'Imam' to mean the Quran. They say that our Imam is the Quran. If the word 'Imam' was not intended, then 'Imamihim' would not have been used. The use of the word 'Imamihim' is proof that there will be an Imam in every era, and it is necessary for people to accept the Imamate of that Imam. If it were the Quran, the Quran is the same in every era; the Quran does not change. The Quran is for every era, but the word 'Imamihim' indicates that there will be some Imam in every era. Another point, and a very noteworthy point here, is that in this verse, God Almighty has announced that on the Day of Judgment, every human being will be called with their Imam. It is not said that the Imam will be called with his Ummah. Now, it is the responsibility of every human being to recognize who the Imam of their time is, with whom they will be raised on the Day of Judgment. Now, let us move towards a famous Hadith in which the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) states... The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) states: 'Man mata wa laysa fi unuqihi bay'atun li-imam-i zamanihi mata maytatan jahiliyyah' (Whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time, his death will be a death of ignorance). And a death of ignorance means a death of disbelief, a death of hypocrisy, a death of misguidance; meaning he will rise from this world as a disbeliever if he has not attained the recognition of the Imam of his time and has not recognized him. And all Muslims believe in this Hadith with slight variations in wording. The famous Sunni scholar Muslim bin Hajjaj al-Naysaburi has recorded this Hadith in his famous book and has narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, stating that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Whoever dies and there is no pledge of allegiance on his neck, his death will be a death of ignorance.' Regarding this Hadith, an interesting incident is found in history. It was the era of the Umayyad government. Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was on the throne of power. In Medina, his governor was Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, and you know who this Hajjaj was. This is the same Hajjaj ibn Yusuf... Who was this Hajjaj? This is the same Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi who used to drink wine while sitting on the roof of the Kaaba and used to say, 'Oh Muhammad, what a fool he made of everyone.' Strange, but this is the same Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi who is the killer of many Sahaba and many Tabi'in. This Hajjaj, one night, in a state of deep intoxication, in the middle of the night... now, who comes to this Hajjaj? Abdullah ibn Umar comes to this Hajjaj. What is his intention? To pledge allegiance. Why? Because this incident is found in Sahih Muslim, Volume 13, page 242, where this entire incident is described. Ibn Hajar Asqalani, the famous scholar, has recorded this incident in his book. Now, when the arrival of Abdullah ibn Umar is written here, it is written that he came for allegiance so that he could pledge allegiance to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan through Hajjaj. Actually, the noteworthy point here is this, but it is surprising that this same Abdullah... But it is surprising that this same Abdullah ibn Umar had refused to pledge allegiance to Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (a.s.), and today he came to pledge allegiance to someone like Hajjaj. Why? Because further on, the reason is given: 'Likay la yubita laylatan wa laysa fi unuqihi bay'ah' (So that he does not spend a night without having a pledge of allegiance on his neck). Because according to the Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), 'Whoever dies and there is no pledge of allegiance on his neck, his death will be a death of ignorance.' This was Abdullah ibn Umar's belief, and for this very intention, for this very reason, he came to pledge allegiance to someone like Hajjaj. He did not pledge allegiance to Ali (a.s.), but he came to pledge allegiance to Hajjaj. title: 8th Rabi ul-Awwal | Shahadat e Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture recounts the final moments and martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). It describes the prophetic instructions given to his slave, Abul Adhiya, regarding the timing of his passing. The narrative concludes with the funeral arrangements led by Imam Hussain (a.s.) and the burial of the Imam near his grandfather, the Prophet Muhammad.
content:
When the time of Imam Hasan's (a.s.) martyrdom was approaching, he gave some letters to his slave, Abul Adhiya, which were to be delivered to Medina. Imam Hussain (a.s.) said to Abul Adhiya, 'Your journey will take 15 days, and when you return, you will be welcomed by the sounds of mourning from my house.' When Abul Adhiya returned after 15 days, the martyrdom of Imam Hasan (a.s.) had already occurred. He states, 'I saw that he was kept in the room where the mosque is illuminated. After some time, Imam Hussain (a.s.) performed his funeral prayers and buried him beside the grave of his grandfather (the Prophet). May the curse of God be upon the killers of Imam Hasan (a.s.).'

title: Majlis #6 Khud Pasandi (Self Praise) | Ahle Bait (a.s.): Daawate Husnaa | Muharram 1443
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual dangers of 'Ujb' (self-conceit) and the destructive nature of ego, emphasizing how vanity and the desire for praise can corrupt one's intellect and worship. The speaker highlights the necessity of humility, the importance of purifying the soul, and the danger of dismissing minor sins or good deeds. The session concludes with a poignant reflection on the martyrdom of Qasim ibn Hasan and the resilience of the Ahlulbayt, illustrating the ultimate sacrifice and loyalty required in the path of faith.
