In Samarra, there were such great scholars; when he went to everyone's house, you know, when you... you became worried. 'If his family asks me where he used to stay, what answer will I give?' So he went to the Haram, and after going to the Haram, he complained to the Imam (a.s.) and said, 'This is your matter, my guest has gone missing. I don't know who has taken him or kidnapped him. I know he has been kidnapped, he has been taken away. Where will you go? When you appear, then... If you can understand this matter, then understand that if someone's responsibility is on your shoulders and...' If someone's responsibility is on your shoulders and if something happens to them, what a great reward it is. What to do? It is hard to understand. Today, for the sake of the 90, [the eyes] were crying and fell asleep. And the one who was laughing, on the other side, in the body... how did it happen? Then don't do it. He came with us, hmm, he took him with him. He became one of our own, one of our companions. And as for his family, don't worry about them, he is with us now. At that place, he took that young man with him. Now he has become one of us. And in this way, the elders... why did they sit with them for 24 hours at their homes? And in such large numbers, they arrived. Okay, this is the explanation of the word, and the others were... and whatever it is, it is his. Introduction, but he was 17-18 years old, and what was this? So, they knew a little bit about it. At his house, subscribe... and also in the seminary, he was just wearing a simple garment. And then, when he came, he was like... that Shirazi, his... but for the sake of hospitality, he was sitting here and went inside your house so that people could provide hospitality. Bring the items for hospitality. But when they came back, they saw he was not there. They asked, 'Where did he go?' 'Don't know, he left.' 'You people were rude, you should have known the teacher.' So, perhaps he was like that, wearing a shawl, in the middle of the night... he was there. You didn't... he was asking you some questions, 'What do you study here? What do you read?' 'This is very childish, we...' He asked this question, 'Good, tell me this.' We said, 'This is a very childish question, why are you asking us?' A childish question, why are you asking us? He didn't answer, he just smiled. Then after that, these two, 17-18 years old, started... this is 40-50 years ago. 'I and you, the law... you will be martyred.' And he said this and left. When these people narrated this incident to Ayatollah Shirazi, he held his head and realized who that person was. He was a man of God. He understood that his teacher was someone who didn't just sit in one place to give lectures; he used to move. He moved from one place to another so that his fame and popularity would not increase, that is why he kept moving. So, finally, he said, 'Allah keeps His Wali (saint) hidden among His servants.' Therefore, look, do not look at any servant of Allah in that way, do not consider any believer small. If someone comes to our gathering, who... If someone comes to our gathering—for instance, someone who is considered very virtuous or a prominent person—and we remove someone else to make room for them, we should know that this small act might displease the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). Imam Hussain (a.s.) could be displeased; the status of the Imam could be offended. You removed a person who was small in our eyes, but you do not know their status. You do not know if they were a friend of Allah. Just because they were poor or lacked wealth, you did not respect them. La'natullah (the curse of Allah) be upon those who arrange seating for someone based on their wealth. Therefore, never engage in such discrimination. Any person who comes to a Majlis is not our guest; they are the guest of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Therefore, serve them well. We are only a medium; our job is that of a servant. Can a servant decide who is worthy and who is not? If someone has arrived, you do not know who sent them, and it is possible that this person's arrival is a test for the gathering. We do not know, and in this way, there are many such instances. The first thing is to always remember that ultimate power and authority belong to Allah. We are nothing; our power is a loan. If He wills, He can make us helpless; He can paralyze us in a moment. He can make us blind, deaf, or mute in an instant. If one is proud of their knowledge, He can make them ignorant. There are not just one, but hundreds of examples of this. Therefore, always remember the power of the Creator so that a person always remains humble, no matter how much worldly wealth they may possess. No matter how much worldly wealth comes, always remain humble. The second thing is to always think about the reality of your deeds. What are they truly? We should constantly analyze our deeds. And remember, there are things from which no one can escape. Remember the day when your back will be broken; there is such a place. Apart from this, when people will see their book of deeds, they will say, 'What is this book? It has left nothing small or big, but it has recorded it.' And when the Quran says 'Ahsaaha' (recorded it), it means not just the major deeds, but it means to purify every single event and every single episode, just as... Purify every episode, just as He is purifying the finest details. Now, who should purify the soul? When a person does this, their soul becomes pure. But we do not pay attention to these things at all. We do not even understand; we just go and pray. That is fine, and it is not a small thing—prayer and fasting have their own place and importance—but the most important thing is that your inner self should be pure. If there is filth inside, then everything is useless. And that is why you see that there were many people who claimed to be with the Imam, but only 72 were fortunate enough to attain martyrdom with him. It is written that there were 24 generations mentioned—which Sahaba were there, which Tabi'un were there. The Sahaba saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and the Tabi'un saw the Sahaba who had seen the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). But besides that, they have mentioned many others. You can understand this, but how many were in Karbala? There were many who were called, and the Imam (a.s.) kept calling out, 'Will you come with me?' People would give excuses. Some were busy with their own affairs; one person said, 'I have this grain stored, I need to secure it, and then I will come to Karbala.' He went home to store the grain properly, and by the time he returned and reached near Karbala, the news had already arrived that... When he reached near Karbala, he received the news that Hussain (a.s.) had been martyred. While crying, Qasim remembered that when his father was leaving this world, he had tied a ta'wiz (amulet) on his arm and said, 'Son Qasim, when...' He had tied a ta'wiz on his arm and said, 'Son Qasim, when a very big calamity comes, when such a calamity comes that you look everywhere and see no way out, then open this and look at it. chapters.title: Understanding Ujb (Self-Conceit)
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces the concept of 'Ujb' or self-conceit, defining it as an ego-driven state where an individual craves praise and self-admiration.

chapters.title: The Dangers of Ego and Flattery
chapters.summary: The lecture warns against the destructive nature of self-praise and the trap of seeking validation from others, noting how it blinds a person's intellect.

chapters.title: Satan's Strategy of Self-Love
chapters.summary: The speaker explains how Satan exploits a person's desire for praise to destroy their good deeds and spiritual progress.

chapters.title: The Ruin of Intellect and Worship
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes that self-obsession ruins one's ability to distinguish between good and evil, ultimately hindering true worship of Allah.

chapters.title: The Danger of Self-Praise and Arrogance
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against the dangers of self-praise and seeking public validation, illustrating how pride can lead to spiritual downfall.

chapters.title: The Value of Knowledge and Humility
chapters.summary: Historical examples of scholars and believers demonstrate the importance of valuing knowledge and performing humble acts of service.

chapters.title: Repentance and Avoiding Small Sins
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that sincere regret is the atonement for sin and warns against justifying wrongdoing by comparing it to others.

chapters.title: Hidden Divine Pleasure and Displeasure
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that Allah hides His pleasure in small acts of obedience and His displeasure in minor sins or disliked acts.

chapters.title: Hidden Saints and Divine Wisdom
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that Allah hides His saints among ordinary servants, urging believers not to underestimate anyone or judge based on outward appearances.

chapters.title: Hospitality and Humility in Majlis
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that all attendees at a Majlis are guests of the Ahlulbayt, and discriminating based on wealth or status is a grave error.

chapters.title: Purification of the Soul
chapters.summary: True devotion requires internal purity and constant self-analysis, as external rituals alone are insufficient without a sincere and purified heart.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Qasim ibn Hasan
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the story of Qasim ibn Hasan, who found his father's final instruction to support Imam Hussain in Karbala, leading to his martyrdom.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Qasim ibn Hasan
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the emotional farewell and martyrdom of Qasim, highlighting the deep bond between him and Imam Hussain.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Final Instructions to Zainab
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain prepares his sister, Sayyida Zainab, for the trials and captivity she will face after his martyrdom.

It focuses on the assault on the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and the defense of the Wilayat of Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker highlights the martyrdom of Janabe Mohsin and the immense sacrifices made by the Ahlulbayt to uphold the truth.

title: Lecture 3: The Focal Point of Lailatul Qadr | Respected H. I. SAYED MAHDI MODARRESI
excerpt: This lecture by Sayed Mahdi Modarresi explores the profound spiritual significance of Lailatul Qadr, emphasizing that its true value lies in connecting one's life and worship to the Imam of the time. The speaker argues that religious rituals are incomplete without a deep, intellectual, and practical commitment to the Imam, who serves as the central axis of a believer's existence. By integrating the remembrance of the Imam into daily decisions and moral conduct, believers can transform their spiritual lives and achieve a balance between worldly responsibilities and the afterlife. The discourse also highlights the importance of loyalty, drawing lessons from the sacrifices of figures like Abbas ibn Ali and the suffering of Fatima Zahra.

Lailatul Qadr is a night of immense spiritual potential, equivalent to over 83 years of worship.
True spiritual vitality requires moving beyond rituals to develop a deep, intellectual connection with the Imam of the time.
The Imam should be the central focus of a believer's life, influencing daily decisions, career, and personal conduct.
Spiritual ignorance arises from failing to recognize the Imam, rendering religious practices less effective.
Living with the awareness of the Imam's presence encourages higher moral standards and sincere repentance.
Loyalty to the Imam, as demonstrated by historical figures like Abbas, transcends personal interests and tribal affiliations.
Believers are encouraged to actively engage with religious teachings and challenge deviations from the Quran and Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Significance of Lailatul Qadr
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the immense value of Lailatul Qadr, particularly the 23rd night of Ramadan, as a time when divine revelations descended and deeds are amplified beyond a thousand months.

chapters.title: Reviving the Night through Knowledge
chapters.summary: The concept of 'Ihya' (keeping the night alive) is explained not just as staying awake, but as engaging in scholarly pursuit and gaining true knowledge to properly value the night.

chapters.title: Critical Listening and Spiritual Vitality
chapters.summary: The speaker urges the audience to be critical listeners who challenge speakers on the pulpit, ensuring that the focus remains on the Quran and the Ahlulbayt rather than peripheral or misleading topics.

chapters.title: True Life through the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker defines true spiritual life as being connected to the Imam of the time, noting that living without this recognition is a life of ignorance (Jahiliyah).

chapters.title: The Necessity of Knowing the Imam
chapters.summary: Recognizing the Imam of the time is essential to avoid a life of ignorance and disbelief, as he is the vital source of spiritual life.

chapters.title: Connecting Beyond Rituals
chapters.summary: True connection with the Imam requires his presence to actively influence one's daily decisions, relationships, and life choices rather than just performing superficial rituals.

chapters.title: Integrating the Imam into Life Decisions
chapters.summary: Many believers treat the Imam's existence as a theoretical fact that has no impact on their marriage, career, or personal priorities, rendering their faith practically irrelevant.

chapters.title: Cultivating Remembrance of the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker encourages shifting community discourse away from trivial politics and gossip toward the constant remembrance and merits of the Imam of the time.

chapters.title: The Imam in Occultation
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the pain of waiting for a loved one, drawing a parallel to the believers' longing for the hidden Imam.

chapters.title: Living for the Imam
chapters.summary: True connection to the Imam involves prioritizing his remembrance over personal worldly desires, leading to a more meaningful life.

chapters.title: Balancing Dunya and Akhirah
chapters.summary: Aligning one's life with the Imam does not mean abandoning the world, but rather giving worldly actions purpose and moral direction.

chapters.title: Repentance Through the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that seeking forgiveness through the Imam is the proper spiritual path, as demonstrated by the Prophet and the Quran.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Abbas and Loyal Companions
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the unwavering loyalty of Abbas and other companions of Imam Hussain, highlighting their selfless devotion and desire to protect the Imam's family.

chapters.title: The Reward of Loyalty and Divine Connection
chapters.summary: The narrative explores the spiritual intimacy between the Imam and his followers, illustrating how the Imam honors those who sacrifice their lives for his cause.

chapters.title: The Suffering of Fatima Zahra
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the immense pain and historical injustices suffered by Fatima Zahra, emphasizing her role as a symbol of sacrifice on the Day of Judgment.

When something like the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is being revealed to the Prophet, who gave those who sat with the Prophet the right to deny this Wilayah? It is better for them that the message... It is better for them that the message which the Prophet is proclaiming to the people in the plain of Ghadir Khumm, and the Wilayah to which he is inviting people on behalf of Allah—to come and greet Ali by calling him Mawla, to come and greet Ali by calling him Amir al-Mu'minin, to come and accept the Wilayah of Ali—it is the people's responsibility to accept that Wilayah. Why? Because the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin) cannot be compared to anyone. Praise be to Allah, the Commander of the Faithful. In the end, we pray to Allah Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of the heir of the Commander of the Faithful, Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), so that when he comes, he brings the same Quran that the Master of the Universe collected in his time, and with that same Alawi style, he explains the interpretation and the Ta'wil (esoteric meaning) of that Quran to us. Just as it was revealed, he will clarify it for us all. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. Peace be upon you, O Trustee of Allah on His earth and His proof over His servants. Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Faithful. I bear witness that you strove for the sake of Allah as is His due, and followed the path of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), until Allah called you to Him. You are the clear proof of Allah over all His creation. May my soul be sacrificed for you... May my soul be sacrificed for you, in your love, in your obedience, in your friendship, in your devotion, in your following, in your guidance, in your piety, in your patience, in your truthfulness, in your morals, in your world, and in your hereafter. Indeed, our hearts are inclined towards you, and our souls are yearning for you, and our... And our souls are yearning for your invitation, for your hope, for your presence, for your existence, for your station, for your rank, for your protection, for your eternity, for your greatness, for your intercession, for your forgiveness, and for your... And for your creation, for your greatness, for your guidance, for your assistance, and for our request that you answer our prayers, and our needs, and our desires, and our friendship, by the right of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Fatimah (s.a.) and Hasan (a.s.) and Husayn (a.s.). You are our guardian and our master. We seek your intercession in our return and our... You are capable of all things. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, the master of the messengers, and upon his pure and purified family. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Wali of Allah. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Now the time has come for the announcement of the daily winners of the Ghadir Divine Scale Mega Quiz 2025. Remember that the quiz link has not been closed, and the link is open until Sunday, June 22nd, at 9:30 PM. is and the link will remain live until Sunday, June 22nd, at 9:30 PM. The daily winners will be selected only from those individuals who have answered all the questions correctly until the Ziyarat in the episode concludes. With this, let us move towards the announcement of today's daily winners, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. Let us see who those 18 winners are who will receive a prize of ₹1400 Indian Rupees, and their names are on your screen: Syeda Ashraf Nisa (Alipur), Kulsum Zahra (Bengaluru), Fatima Zahra (Azamgarh), Shabi Zahra Zaidi (Meerut), Shadab Hussain (Mumbai), Ata-e-Sakina (Bengaluru), Fatima Khizra (Bengaluru), Zainab Mohammad Raza Mukadam (Maharashtra), Kaleem Haider Abidi (Saharanpur), Bilqees Masani (Mumbra), Asma Rizvi (Mumbai), Syed Mohammad Ibrahim (Alipur), Ehsan Syed (Mumbai), Kausar Fatima Afzal Rajani (Mahua), Shahjan Fatima (Bengaluru), Mohammad Azeem (Moradabad), Mir Jafar Haider (Bangkok, Thailand), Seema (Kashmir). Many congratulations to all the winners. As mentioned, if your name has not appeared in any episode or if you have missed an episode, there is no need to be disappointed; this quiz link will remain live until Sunday, June 22nd, at 9:30 PM. For those in this series who have [answered] all the episodes' quizzes those who have answered all the questions in all the episodes' quizzes correctly will be included in the mega prize lucky draw, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq. We thank you all once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet again on Sunday, June 22nd, in our special episode at the same time, 9:30 PM India time, in which the winner of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz 2025 mega prize, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq lucky draw, will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. Insha'Allah, until then, Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali (a.s.) Madad.

chapters.title: Quiz Instructions and Program Overview
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the rules for the ongoing quiz, including how to register and the criteria for winning the mega prize of Ziyarat.

chapters.title: The Incident of Hasbuna Kitabullah
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates the historical event from Sahih Bukhari where the phrase 'the Book of Allah is sufficient' was used to prevent the Prophet from writing a final document.

chapters.title: Imamate and the Necessity of a Teacher
chapters.summary: The speaker connects the Ghadir declaration to the Prophet's role as a teacher of the Book, arguing that a successor must possess complete knowledge of the Quran.

chapters.title: The Status of the Quran After the Prophet
chapters.summary: The speaker challenges the claim that the Quran was sufficient during the Prophet's time by questioning if a compiled Mushaf even existed then.

chapters.title: Historical Evidence of Quranic Compilation
chapters.summary: Using Sahih Bukhari narrations, the speaker argues that the Quran was not compiled during the Prophet's life and highlights Zayd ibn Thabit's struggle to collect it later.

chapters.title: The Necessity of a Teacher for the Quran
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that the Quran alone is insufficient for religious practice, such as prayer, and requires a teacher, just as worldly education requires instructors.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Expert Quranic Interpretation
chapters.summary: Understanding the Quran requires deep knowledge of Arabic, grammar, and context, as it contains both clear and allegorical verses.

chapters.title: The Quranic Command to Consult Ahl al-Dhikr
chapters.summary: Surah an-Nahl verse 43 establishes that those without knowledge must consult the Ahl al-Dhikr, identified as the Ahl al-Bayt, to understand the Book.

chapters.title: The Necessity of a Qayyim for the Quran
chapters.summary: Mansur ibn Hazim argues that because various sects use the Quran to justify conflicting beliefs, the Quran requires a divinely appointed interpreter (Qayyim).

chapters.title: Ali ibn Abi Talib as the Ultimate Authority
chapters.summary: Only Imam Ali claimed comprehensive knowledge of the Quran, and Imams confirm the Quran is sufficient only when accompanied by its authorized interpreter.

chapters.title: The Exclusive Authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) designated Imam Ali (a.s.) as the sole interpreter of the Quranic verses at Ghadir Khumm.

chapters.title: The Significance of Wilayah and Ziyarat
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes the obligation to accept the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) and concludes with a Ziyarat prayer and the announcement of quiz winners.

title: EP06 | Ghadeer Par Eteraazat Kyun Huey? | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm, focusing on the divine appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the successor to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). It addresses common historical objections, such as the concentration of leadership within Banu Hashim and the age of the Imam, by providing Quranic and historical counter-arguments. The session emphasizes that the rejection of this appointment was rooted in resistance to justice and a misunderstanding of divine decree, while also promoting a community-wide quiz initiative to deepen the understanding of Wilayah.
content:
Subdi hai ye noor-e-Khuda, Paighambar-e-Haq, Ali. La ilaha illallah, Ali-un-Waliullah. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh, Ya Ali Madad. We are once again present to serve you with another episode of Ghadir, the Divine Covenant, and we welcome you all to this episode. Let us, dear viewers, begin today's episode with these lines: 'He will remain far from all difficulties, by God, whoever says from the heart, Ya Ali Madad. And this is the word of Truth, it is the duty of the angels, what are we? The Prophets have said, Ya Ali Madad.' Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi fi kulli waqtin wa dhalik [music] faha. Respected viewers, first of all, let us tell you a few things about the Ghadir, the Divine Covenant Mega Quiz. There will be seven episodes, and in each episode, a discussion regarding Ghadir and the Wilayat of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) will be presented to you, and the questions for this quiz will be related to this discussion. In every episode, we will have seven lucky winners who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system, in which the first prize is 5,000, the next two prizes are 3,000, and the next four prizes are 1,000 3,000, and the next four prizes are 1,000. And finally, our Ghadir, the Divine Covenant Mega Quiz's mega prize is the one that every lover of Ali (a.s.) desires in their heart, that they want to go to the threshold of their Mawla and bow their head in submission. That is, a pilgrimage to Iraq. Yes, viewers, the mega prize is a pilgrimage to Iraq, which will be announced in a special episode after this series ends. To be eligible for the mega prize of the Iraq pilgrimage, one must watch all these episodes, i.e., all seven episodes, and participate in the quiz of every episode, and you must give correct answers to all the questions in at least five out of the seven episodes. From among all such individuals, the winner of our mega prize, i.e., the Iraq pilgrimage, will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. We hope that you will stay with us throughout this series and keep participating in every quiz. The quiz link will be activated as soon as each episode begins, and the quiz link is present in the live chat and description of this video. At the end of every episode, there will be Ziyarat-e-Aminullah. As soon as the Ziyarat ends, the seven lucky winners of the episode will be announced through our computerized The seven lucky winners will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. We request you to listen to our episodes carefully and answer all the questions correctly. Respected viewers, the personality of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is that personality of Islamic history whose virtues and merits are beyond reach, let alone competing with even a particle of his excellence. Whether it is the beginning of Islam, Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira, or the very first battle, the Battle of Badr, or after that, the Battle of Uhud, Khandaq, or Khaybar, whether it is the field of martyrdom or the field of worship, or the field of knowledge, no one appears anywhere near Hazrat Ali (a.s.). So much so that the poet says, 'The pen says, every historian of the world, how does this miracle appear to me? I have been writing the virtues of Ali for centuries, yet it still appears fresh.' I have been writing the virtues of Ali for centuries, yet it still appears fresh. So much so that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) clearly declared in the field of Ghadir that Hazrat Ali (a.s.) will be my Mawla after me. That is, he enforced the Wilayat of Hazrat Ali (a.s.) for all Muslims. Despite this, people denied it. That is, so clear People denied it. That is, despite it being so clear, they denied it and even rejected the command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And they are seen looking for different excuses to justify this mistake. Some excuses are that the word 'Mawla' that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) used there does not mean Wilayat or authority, but friendship. And many such objections, about which we have discussed in our previous several episodes. Let us today also discuss some such objections or excuses that Muslims have brought from after Ghadir until today to justify their mistake. Let us take this discussion forward. To conduct this discussion, present in our gathering are Mr. Sajjad Mehar Ali Sahab and Mr. Abbas Patel Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Regarding our topic today, if we look at Islamic history, those who denied the Wilayat of Hazrat Ali (a.s.) tried to present various objections and baseless excuses. For example, they say that if the announcement of Ghadir was so important, then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should have made this announcement during Hajj or should have made it in the field of Arafat. Why did he make the announcement in Ghadir? Or besides this, other objections of theirs, that they compare this event with the event of Yemen, that they say that those who went to Yemen had complained to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) about Hazrat Ali (a.s.), and that is why the Messenger of Allah made this announcement there in Ghadir and made Hazrat Ali the friend of everyone. People present such objections, baseless objections. And by the grace of God, Alhamdulillah, we have already given detailed answers to all these objections in our previous series 'Eteraz-e-Ghadir'. Today also, we have some such points here, some such questions here, that after all, what is the reason that despite the announcement of the Wilayat and Imamate of Hazrat Ali (a.s.) being so clear, 'Azhar min ash-shams' (brighter than the sun), people denied it? After all, what is the reason for it? Mohammad Abbas Sahab, we would like you to start this discussion. Gulzar Bhai, there are many reasons, but we will try to discuss those reasons in this episode that we find in the books of Ahl-e-Tasannun, according to their statements. And the very first reason or cause that we find in their books, which we will discuss here today Which we will discuss here today, is that Prophethood and Imamate should not have been in the same family. This is a sentence from Tarikh-e-Tabari. Prophethood was in Banu Hashim, so Imamate and Caliphate should have been in some other family. Oh, so this means that if the Messenger and Prophet have come in the family of Banu Hashim, then now the Imamate and Caliphate, that is, the Caliph or Imam of that Prophet, will not be from that family. Whether the Messenger of Allah or God wants it or not. And Gulzar Bhai, Ibn Abbas pointed towards this very thing, saying that if the Quraish have chosen Caliphate and Imamate for themselves, then this is Allah's will, that is, this was not their own personal decision, but rather Allah had decided that the Caliphate and Imamate should be for Banu Hashim. And then Ibn Abbas further explained that God Almighty has described the dislike of some people in the Holy Quran like this: 'This is because they disliked what God Almighty revealed, so God also nullified their deeds.' That is, Gulzar Bhai, here 'Ahkam' (commands) means that Allah had decided that the Caliphate and Imamate would be for Amir al-Mu'minin, and the Messenger of Allah announced it at Ghadir What we are going to discuss here today is the claim that Prophethood (Nubuwwat) and Imamate should not have been in the same household. This is a statement from Tarikh al-Tabari: 'Since Prophethood was in Banu Hashim, Imamate and Caliphate should have been in another family.' This implies that if a Messenger and Prophet has already come from the Banu Hashim family, then the Imamate and Caliphate—that is, the successor or Imam of that Prophet—should not be from that same family, regardless of whether the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) or God wills it or not. Brother Gulzar, Ibn Abbas pointed towards this very issue, saying that if the Quraish chose the Caliphate and Imamate for themselves, it was Allah's will—meaning it was not their personal decision, but rather Allah had decreed that the Caliphate and Imamate should be for Banu Hashim. Ibn Abbas further explained that God Almighty described the aversion of some people in the Holy Quran in this way: 'This is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds vain.' Brother Gulzar, here 'Ahkam' (commandments) refers to the fact that Allah had decided that the Caliphate and Imamate would be for the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced at Ghadir. And that which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced in the plain of Ghadir. But this command of Allah was not pleasing to these people. And that is why these people were against this command. And Allah, on this basis, rendered their deeds void. Meaning, the objection is not against the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.). This objection is against Allah—that the commands Allah is giving, the commands He is revealing, are being rejected. Allah's command, Allah's command is being rejected. Yes, so Gulzar Bhai, this command that came, the announcement of Wilayah, this came from Allah. The revelation that came down was from Allah. This was not the personal decision of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Allah commanded that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) be declared the Imam and be declared the successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). So what right did the people have to place their own opinions before the command of Allah? And Ibn Abbas has pointed towards this very fact, that it was the will of the Almighty that Ali (a.s.) and his Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) be given preference over others. Allah had given this preference, so what business did the people have to offer their own opinions? Because their hearts, meaning their hearts are from the heart of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). These are the personalities from whose existence the Almighty has kept away impurity and evil, and has declared their hearts to be pure. Meaning, declared their hearts to be pure. Meaning, Abbas Bhai, if their objection is that there cannot be two positions in one family—meaning, in the family where there is Prophethood, there cannot be Caliphate and Imamate—then what will they do in the Hereafter? Where the Master of Kauthar is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the Distributor of Kauthar is Haider-e-Karrar Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and the leaders of the youth of Paradise are Hasanain Karimain (a.s.), and the leader of the women of Paradise is Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.)? So now, these people will not even try to go to Paradise? And Gulzar Bhai, such objections are not only baseless and absurd, but they are also against the Quran. Against the Quran, yes. Will you explain? The explanation is that when Janabe Musa (a.s.) wanted a vizier in the Quran, he prayed to Allah, 'Make Harun my vizier,' and Allah accepted his prayer. Indeed, if it were not possible within the same lineage, within the same line, then Allah would not have done it. Indeed, meaning whoever rejects this has effectively rejected the Quran, and whoever rejects the Quran is outside of Islam. Meaning, hearing these baseless and absurd objections, it seems that if it were up to these people, they would have chosen the Prophet themselves. Not just chosen, Gulzar Bhai, but they tried their best to choose the Prophet, and Allah rejected this choice of theirs. And in the Quran, it is... rejected this choice, and in the Quran, it is stated in this way, that the people of the Quranic era used to say that this Quran should have been revealed to some great person from Mecca or Taif. Why was it revealed to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? These people were trying their best that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should not even become a Prophet. That Prophethood should not come to the Banu Hashim. Meaning, this family-based bias was already in the minds of the people. Their mindset was such that even the first Messenger should be from such a family, and after that, they brought up the issue of the family again, saying that two positions cannot be in one family. And if one looks at it, this was the very thinking of those people—that a position should only go to the wealthy, the affluent, the rich, and no one else. In that era, the standard of the Arabs was only money, necessity, and nothing else. There was no concept of justice and fairness. But if there was animosity towards Maula-e-Kainat Ali (a.s.), it was only and only because the justice of Ali was not tolerable to the Arabs. The way he used to deal with matters—meaning, the justice of Ali became the cause of enmity towards Ali. Because Ali (a.s.) was the manifestation of justice and fairness. The Arabs could not tolerate the justice and fairness of Maula-e-Kainat. Therefore, there was no expediency in him becoming the Caliph. And Sajjad Sahab, meaning this... expediency, and Sajjad Sahab, meaning this same reason is what became the cause of the murder of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) due to his justice. Regarding this, a Christian named George Jordac writes that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was martyred in the Mihrab, martyred in the Mihrab of worship, because of the intensity of his justice. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was so fond of justice. If we take this objection, the Arabs did not like it, and the reason for that is also that they did not like the justice of Hazrat Ali (a.s.). So there was no expediency in it. It is an absolutely tyrannical objection if one looks at it. And indeed, Gulzar Bhai, people of this same mindset, who cannot tolerate the justice of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), are the same people who are engaged in enmity towards the last descendant of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and are rejecting him. Because when the Imam (a.t.f.s.) reappears, he will fill this world with justice and fairness. And those people whose temperament is such that they do not like justice and fairness, due to which they are rejecting the Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), how will these people be able to live in the era of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)? Perhaps that is why these people have also excluded the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) from their beliefs. excluded the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) from their beliefs. Yes. Now, the thing to see is that if people cannot tolerate the justice of a creation, then how will they tolerate the justice of the Lord of Majesty on the Day of Judgment? And Abbas Bhai, what you quoted, that the martyrdom of Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) happened because of his justice—regarding this, we see another point, and that is that the wretch who martyred Ali (a.s.) with a strike, Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) gave the command that if I survive, I will take revenge, and if I pass away, if I am martyred, then strike my killer with only one blow. This is the ultimate justice of Ali (a.s.). Only a Wali of Allah can implement such justice, or someone who, for himself—meaning, if someone strikes someone, if someone murders someone, even his relatives would not make such a decision as the one being murdered is making, that 'strike only one blow' because he struck me one blow. Truly, and Gulzar Bhai, these were the people of that era who recited the Kalima but could not tolerate the justice of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). And this justice of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), George Jordac, in his book 'The Voice of Human Justice: Imam Ali', 'The Voice of Human Justice: Imam Ali', records that the things and laws that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) implemented regarding human rights, it seems that the human rights laws implemented by the United Nations are less effective than the laws of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Viewers, if one considers this objection, it is so baseless and astonishing that one should weep or laugh at this objection. Their claim is that because of his justice, because he was the best at doing justice, for this reason, he was not chosen as Caliph, Imam, or Ruler. Meaning, this is exactly like saying that if someone is the best doctor, we will not get treated by him, or if someone is the best judge, we will not get a verdict from him. Truly, this is strange and astonishing. Abbas Bhai, another objection is found in the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah, that when Ibn Abbas objected to the second Caliph regarding the Wilayah of Hazrat Ali (a.s.), asking why he did not become the Caliph, the Caliph replied that it was because the nation considered him young. Meaning, here an objection was presented, an excuse was made, saying he was young. For this reason, he was not accepted as Caliph. We would like you to shed some light on this. shed some light on this. Gulzar Bhai, you used a very appropriate word, 'excuse,' because in reality, this was just an excuse they presented to usurp the Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). But in reality, their goal was not to let Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) reach the Caliphate. The goal was this, and they kept making excuses to prove their point. If we look at it, the age of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) at that time was 33 years, and a 33-year-old person is a full-grown adult; he is not a child or young. So they kept making excuses that he was young and a youth, and therefore we did not accept him. But their temperament was exactly such that they presented excuses to prove their points. As we see that during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded them to go in the Army of Usama, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded them to go in the Army of Usama—meaning Usama bin Zaid, who was a youth at that time, about 20 years old. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made him the commander of the army and commanded all the people to join Usama's army and leave Medina. Yes, but these hypocrites, at that... leave Medina. Yes, but these hypocrites, at that time, presented the same objection that Usama is young, and how can we go in his army, under his command? They were objecting in front of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). They were openly opposing the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) by presenting this objection. Meaning, it is possible that those who were objecting were all elderly in age, and therefore they were advancing their own candidacy before Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and presenting these excuses that 'we have more experience, we are elderly, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is young.' They were presenting these excuses, just as they openly rejected the command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and did not go in the Army of Usama, saying or making the excuse that 'he is young and we are elderly.' Meaning, this was their mindset from the beginning. Yes, meaning it could be that this was their mentality from that era. Yes, meaning it could be that this was the temperament of the Age of Ignorance that remained within them. And one more thing is found, which is the first announcement of Imamate, which we call 'Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira,' in which there is a verse of the Quran. Allah commanded, 'O Messenger, gather your relatives, tell them.' And when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced there, 'Who is it that will support me?' Everyone was sitting as elders, so the feast was empty, right? the feast was empty, right? 'Who is it that will support me?' Yes, everyone was sitting, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Who will support me in this task?' No one said anything. Only Ali (a.s.), a 13-year-old child, said, 'Ana ya Rasool Allah' (I am, O Messenger of Allah), 'I will help you. Whoever raises an eye towards you, I will pull out his eyes. Whoever speaks against you, I will pull out his tongue. I will support you, I will protect you.' A 13-year-old child—in this, there is no restriction of age. He said it, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) then said, 'Yes, you will be my successor after me, my Caliph, my Wasi, and the guide and leader of the Ummah.' chapters.title: Ghadir Mega Quiz Details
chapters.summary: The program introduces a seven-episode quiz series on the Wilayat of Imam Ali (a.s.) with prizes including a pilgrimage to Iraq.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ghadir and Objections
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the historical clarity of the Ghadir declaration and address common objections used to deny the Wilayat of Imam Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: Analyzing Historical Objections to Imamate
chapters.summary: The discussion examines the historical claim that Prophethood and Imamate should not reside in the same family, refuting it as an opposition to Divine command.

chapters.title: Baseless Objections Against Divine Leadership
chapters.summary: The speakers refute the argument that Prophethood and Imamate cannot coexist within the same family, highlighting the Quranic precedent of Prophet Musa and Harun.

chapters.title: Justice as the Root of Enmity
chapters.summary: The lecture explains that opposition to Imam Ali was primarily driven by his uncompromising commitment to justice, which the elite of that era could not tolerate.

chapters.title: Refuting the Age Excuse
chapters.summary: The speakers analyze the historical excuse that Imam Ali was too young for leadership, contrasting it with the Prophet's appointment of Usama bin Zaid and the divine appointment of Prophet Isa.

chapters.title: Refuting Objections to Divine Appointments
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the historical objection to Ali (a.s.)'s leadership based on age and explain that divine selection is not bound by human criteria.

chapters.title: Addressing the 'Allah's Will' Argument
chapters.summary: The speakers refute the claim that Ali (a.s.) did not become Caliph because Allah did not will it, clarifying the misuse of Jabriya ideology to justify human disobedience.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Quiz Winners Announcement
chapters.summary: The episode concludes with reflections on the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and the announcement of the winners for the Ghadir mega quiz.

title: Majlis #8 Jahannam Se Nejaat (Amnesty from Hell) | Ahle Bait (a.s.): Daawate Husnaa | Muharram 1443
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual and ethical teachings of the Ahlulbayt, emphasizing the importance of moderation, generosity, and consistent faith in daily life. It highlights the necessity of disassociating from falsehood while maintaining a deep, transformative connection to the tragedy of Karbala. Through the emotional narrative of the martyrdom of Ali Akbar and the suffering of Sakina, the speaker illustrates the profound sacrifices made by Imam Hussain and his family. The session concludes by reflecting on the Day of Judgment and the eternal rewards promised to those who remain steadfast in their love and devotion to the Imams.

title: EP03 | Quran Ke Mutaabiq Khalifa Kaun? | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the concept of Caliphate through the lens of the Quran, arguing that the appointment of a leader is a divine prerogative rather than a human selection. By analyzing Quranic criteria such as divine knowledge, infallibility, and moral uprightness, the speaker presents Imam Ali (a.s.) as the uniquely qualified successor to the Prophet. The session also contrasts the divine appointment of an Imam with historical caliphates, emphasizing the necessity of a leader who possesses superior knowledge and a history free from idol worship.
content:
PSR presents. [Music/Poetry in Persian/Arabic]. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And blessings be upon you, O Wali of the Age, help us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable viewers and listeners, peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. Ya Ali Madad. We are once again present before you with another episode of Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi, and we welcome you all to today's episode. So come, respected viewers, as per tradition, seeking help from Mushkil Kusha, let us begin today's episode: 'Remove sorrow and pain, let there be happiness all around, recite Ya Ali Madad and give it to the patient of grief. And he is far from Islam and unfortunate, who could not even say Ya Ali Madad once.' In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of Hassan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye. Until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. Respected viewers, first of all, let us tell you a few things about the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz. It will have seven episodes, and in each episode, a discussion regarding Ghadir and the Wilayah of Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) will be presented to you. The questions of this quiz will be related to this discussion. In each episode, there will be seven lucky winners who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. In which the first prize is 5,000, the second two prizes are 3,000, and the third four prizes are 1,000. And finally, the mega prize of our Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz is the one that every lover of Ali (a.s.) keeps in their heart, that they want to go to the threshold of their Mawla and bow their head in submission, that is, the Ziyarat of Iraq. Yes, viewers, the mega prize is for the Ziyarat of Iraq. Which will be announced in a special episode after this series ends. Eligible for the mega prize of Ziyarat of Iraq will be those who watch all these episodes, i.e., all seven episodes, and participate in the quiz of each episode, and you will have to give correct answers to all the questions in the quiz of at least five out of the seven episodes. And from among all such individuals, the winner of our mega prize, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. We hope that you will stay with us throughout this series and keep participating in every quiz. The quiz link will be activated as soon as each episode starts, and the quiz link is present in the live chat and description of this video. The quiz link will remain active until the end of the episode. At the end of each episode, there will be Ziyarat-e-Aminullah, after which this link will be closed. We request you to listen to our episodes carefully and give correct answers to all the questions. Respected viewers, the announcement of the Wilayah and Imamate of Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) made by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) at Ghadir-e-Khumm filled the hearts of the believers with such joy that it appears on their faces as soon as Ghadir is mentioned. And this announcement of Ghadir is such a powerful slap on the faces of the hypocrites that it will force them until the Day of Judgment to deny this event, this announcement, and raise objections to it. And we are also trying to answer such objections here, under which we have discussed in our previous two episodes the topics of what the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) should be like. So come, in today's episode, let us move forward with the same question: according to the Quran, who is the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? That those who were called Caliph in the Holy Quran, why did they get that status? And after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in whom were those qualities found? So come, viewers, to shed light on this topic, our brothers Janab Ahsan Jafri Sahab and Janab Shabiul Hassan Sahab are present in our gathering. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Peace be upon you too and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Shabiul Hassan Sahab, we would like to start this discussion with you, and in the previous two episodes, the questions we have discussed, such as what should the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) be like and who has the right to choose him? And indeed, today's topic seems like it is going to shed much more light on these two topics as well, on the topic of this Caliphate: the qualities of a Caliph mentioned in the Holy Quran, in whom are they found after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? We would like you to shed some light on this topic. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Gulzar Sahab, if we recite the Holy Quran with careful attention, we find the answer to your question in Surah Al-Baqarah, from verse 30 to 33. When Allah decided that He would send His Caliph, His Imam, to the earth, He first announced it to the angels. The Quranic verse, verse number 30, says: 'Wa idh qala rabbuka lil-mala'ikati inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifa.' If we look at it from here, when Allah expressed His intention to send His Caliph or Imam to the earth, the angels were the most concerned. Yes. They asked Allah a counter-question: 'Qalu ataj'alu fiha may-yufsidu fiha wa yasfikud-dima'a.' That, O Lord, will You make someone a Caliph who will spread bloodshed and corruption on earth? The angels are saying this to Allah. And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You. Then Allah says: 'Qala inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun.' I know what you do not know. That is, in this verse, one realizes that the Caliph must possess a special kind of knowledge for Allah to make him His Caliph on earth. If you look at the very next verse, in which Allah says to Hazrat Adam (a.s.): 'Wa 'allama Adamal-asma'a kullaha'—and Allah taught Adam the knowledge of all the names. 'Summa 'aradahum 'alal-mala'ikati'—and then before the angels, He presented these names. Then He said: 'Anbi'uni bi-asma'i ha'ula'i in kuntum sadiqin'—that if you are truthful in your claim, then tell me the names of these. That is, Allah taught Adam (a.s.) some names, the knowledge of all names, the knowledge of the Divine names, and then placed this challenge before the angels, because in the previous verse, the angels were saying that He would make someone a Caliph who would cause corruption, while we—meaning the angels—wanted to imply that You should make us the Caliph. So now, regarding their claim, Allah is challenging them Himself. 'Qalu subhanaka la 'ilma lana illa ma 'allamtana'—the angels said, when they did not realize that knowledge, they very humbly said to their Lord: O Lord, we know nothing except what You have taught us. 'Innaka antal-'alimul-hakim'—and You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. That is, the angels understood how far they could offer their opinion, how far they could think. But the people of Saqifah did not understand; they selected a Caliph themselves. And let me tell you one thing, Gulzar Bhai, that the way the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) addressed Allah, no one else possessed that knowledge. Indeed. Not even the angels knew how to address Allah. Indeed. Wow. Now, if you analyze these verses, it shows that Allah taught Hazrat Adam some names, granted him the knowledge of some names that are necessary to become a Caliph on earth or to become a representative of Allah. Indeed. Without that, you cannot claim that I am a Caliph. Just as the angels did before Allah, that will You make someone Your successor who will only cause corruption? Allah has answered that in this verse. Indeed. While the angels are infallible, while the angels are infallible. This makes it clear that the right to become a Caliph belongs only to the one who possesses Divine knowledge. Indeed. Indeed. And has the knowledge of all these names, and the knowledge of all these Divine names must be with him. Indeed. That is, Allah has stated this criterion. Allah has stated this criterion in this verse of the Quran, that it is necessary for him to have the knowledge of the Divine names. Indeed. Indeed. Look further. Allah says: 'Qala ya Adamu anbi'hum bi-asma'ihim'—to whom is He speaking? To Hazrat Adam. Adam (a.s.). Who is to be taught? The angels. Wow. Yes. The knowledge that Allah gave to Hazrat Adam, He told him to teach it to the angels. Wow, wow, wow. 'Falamma amba'ahum bi-asma'ihim'—Hazrat Adam gave that knowledge to the angels, made them recognize, introduced them to those names. To the infallible angels. Then Allah said: 'Qala alam aqul lakum inni a'lamu ghaybas-samawati wal-ardi wa a'lamu ma tubduna wa ma kuntum taktumun'—then Allah says to the angels: Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know everything that you reveal and what you conceal? I have knowledge of everything that is manifest and hidden. Gulzar Sahab, these three verses make it absolutely clear that the one who will be Allah's Caliph on earth is the one who teaches the angels. Wow, wow, subhanAllah, subhanAllah. Not that the angels teach him. Wow, wow, wow, subhanAllah, subhanAllah. While the angels are infallible, infallible, their creation is infallible. Yes. But our Caliph of the earth must be such that he is the teacher of even the infallible angels. Indeed. Indeed. Yes, Hassan Bhai, now in this verse that Shabihul Hassan Sahab explained, it became clear that according to the Quran, the Caliph will be the one who teaches the angels and who possesses the knowledge of the names. We would like you to also shed some light on this topic according to the Quran. Certainly. As Shabihul Hassan Sahab just explained, you were saying that this should be the first characteristic, and because this verse becomes so important also because Adam (a.s.) is the very first creation on Allah's earth. Indeed. And Allah is sending His Caliph to the earth for the first time. Yes. And He is sending him with these qualities. Yes. There is no one yet, there is no creation on earth that he will guide. But he is a Caliph. But Allah is appointing the Caliph beforehand. Indeed. So one is amazed at the intellects of those people that the most excellent Prophet, when he is leaving this world, will Allah leave the earth without a Caliph? Indeed. And even in today's age, without a Caliph. Yes. Even today, without a Caliph, the world is still standing. It is truly amazing to think about the intellects of those people. Allah did not leave the empty earth without a Caliph. He did not. Will He leave this populated earth without a Caliph? Indeed. Indeed. So now, another second characteristic here in the Holy Quran, because our topic is who is the Caliph according to the Holy Quran, according to the Holy Quran. So in this, besides Hazrat Adam (a.s.), we find the mention of Hazrat Dawood (a.s.). That for Hazrat Dawood (a.s.) too, Allah the Almighty has used the word 'Khalifa' in the Holy Quran. Yes. And this is Surah Sad, which is Surah number 38, the 38th Surah, its 26th verse. What does the verse say? Allah the Almighty says: 'Ya Dawudu inna ja'alnaka khalifatan fil-ardi'—O Dawood, We have appointed you as a Caliph on the earth. We have made you a Caliph on the earth. We have made it. 'Fahkum'—so now, what should you do? Hazrat Dawood (a.s.), now since He has made you a Caliph, so what should you do? The two important tasks that Allah has stated for a Caliph in this verse. The first task, now what should you do? 'Fahkum baynannasi bil-haqq'—you judge between people with truth, with justice and fairness. That is, you make just decisions. 'Wa la tattabi'il-hawa'—and look, do not follow desires. Why? Because if you followed desires, what will happen? 'Fayudilluka 'an sabilillah'—so it should not happen that you stray from the path of Allah. Allah is stating this quality for a Caliph, that the Caliph should be such that he does not follow desires, otherwise he will stray from the straight path, that is, the path of Allah. Yes. Why? And those who strayed from the path of Allah, what does the verse say further? 'Innalladhina yadhilluna 'an sabilillah'—those who stray from the path of Allah, 'lahum 'adhabun shadid'—so if people have selected such a Caliph, right, based on their ignorance, who himself will stray from the path of Allah, then not only will that Caliph be punished, but those who made him will also be punished. And why will there be punishment? 'Bima nasu yawmal-hisab'—because they forgot the Day of Judgment. They do not have the Day of Judgment in their minds. It is just politics. Yes. So this second verse, in which the Caliphate of Hazrat Dawood (a.s.) is mentioned, has two important responsibilities according to this verse. The first responsibility is to judge justly between people, to make decisions. He should be a judge. And the second is not to follow desires. Now, as far as the question of judgment is concerned, let us study history to see which of these two characteristics were found after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). As far as the question of judgment is concerned, the matter of making just decisions, let us see, the first thing is that for a judge, there should be some conditions. There are some conditions to become a judge. What are those conditions? Now, before you, I have a book from Oxford University Press, a book published there, 'Journal of Islamic Studies'. In it, for becoming a judge, according to the Hanbali school, yes, according to the Hanbalis, some conditions have been stated to become a judge. We are not even talking about the Shia perspective yet. Yes. According to the Hanbalis, what is the first condition to become a judge? They have stated three conditions in that book. The first condition they have kept is 'Kamal' (perfection). That is, there should be two types of perfection in him. One is 'Kamal al-Ahkam' and the second is 'Kamal al-Khilqat'. Both of these things. 'Kamal al-Ahkam' means what? That is, the issues of puberty, that he should be an adult, sane, a man, all these things come under 'Kamal al-Ahkam'. And 'Kamal al-Khilqat' means that he should be physically perfect. It is not that his eyes are bad, he hears less, the one who hears less himself, what decision will he make for others? Yes, yes, yes. Yes, so there should be no physical defect in him. So this was the first condition, perfection. The second condition, which is the second condition, is 'Adalat' (justice/integrity). And what does 'Adalat' mean? They write that the one who is a 'Fasiq' (sinner), a 'Fasiq' and 'Fajir', who openly commits sins, he is not 'Adil' (just/upright). Therefore, he cannot become a judge. Yes. So he cannot commit open sins, he cannot be a 'Fasiq', he must be 'Adil'. And the third thing that people write is 'Ijtihad'. For 'Ijtihad', that is, he has to deliver the decisions himself. Yes. He will deliver decisions by struggling himself. For 'Ijtihad', what is necessary? He must have complete knowledge of the Quran and Sunnah. He must have complete knowledge. He must have complete knowledge. In this, 'To be fully convergent with the Holy Quran means to be in possession of knowledge of 10 things'. They have talked about 10 things. That is, he must have complete knowledge of the Quran. Along with that, that judge must also have complete knowledge of Hadith, that is, the Sunnah. The discourse emphasizes that questioning the status granted to the Ahlulbayt by Allah is a sign of hypocrisy and a grave sin.
content:
Doubting the virtues of Maula is actually a very big sin. Regarding this, Janabe Jabir ibn Abdullah Ansari (r.a.) was asked to say something about doubt. So, he narrated a hadith before the people regarding this virtue and this doubt: 'No one doubts them except that they go out of the fold of religion.' Wow, wow, wow. 'And no one will doubt them except that they are a hypocrite.' Indeed, indeed. Meaning, the result of this is so dangerous—the virtues of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the authority that Allah has given them, if anyone doubts that, then it is as if they go out of the fold of religion. Indeed, indeed. So, this is such a dangerous thing, to doubt the virtues of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Indeed.
