title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 8 | Ghaibat-e-Kubra (Major Occultation) and Taqleed – Part 2
excerpt: This lecture explores the necessity and theological foundations of Taqlid (religious emulation) during the Major Occultation of the 12th Imam. It emphasizes that while the Imam is absent, believers are obligated to follow qualified jurists who derive rulings from the Quran and the traditions of the Ahlulbayt. The session clarifies that Taqlid is a rational and narratively supported framework designed to ensure religious practice remains aligned with divine law despite the lack of direct access to the Imam.
content:
Wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik aduwwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. Astaghfirullahalladhi la ilaha illa huwal hayyul qayyum ar-rahmanur-rahim dhul jalali wal ikram wa atubu ilayh. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasani salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba-ihi fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafiza wa qa'ida wa nasira wa dalila wa 'ayna hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyikal faraj wa aj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi wa la taj'alna min a'da-ihi wa waffiqna lima tuhibbu wa tarda wa la takilna ila anfusina tarfata 'aynin abada wa la tastabdil bina ghairana bihaqqi Muhammadin wa Aalihit-Tahirine. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da-ahum ajma'in. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. This Mahdawiyat webinar of Sha'ban-ul-Mu'azzam 1441 Hijri is now moving towards its final stages, and after today's session, there will be two more sessions, Insha'Allah. In today's eighth session, we will continue yesterday's topic, Insha'Allah, which is Ghaybat-e-Kubra and Taqlid. After the conclusion of Safarat-e-Khasa in Ghaybat-e-Sughra, the era of Ghaybat-e-Kubra began. The most important responsibility stated for us Shias is the protection of our religion and faith, and the only path for this is to remain connected to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Today, a person can easily go astray because everyone seems to be presenting their own perspective. Therefore, the importance of anyone's perspective will only be valid when it is stated in the light of the Hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The greatest responsibility lies with each one of us to connect ourselves more and more to the Hadiths. In this Ghaybat-e-Kubra, it is necessary to refer to those scholars who benefit people through the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the light of their Wilayat. Imam Kazim (a.s.) himself gave a message to the Shias during the Ghaybat through Yunus ibn Abdur-Rahman Ridwanullahi Ta'ala Alayh, who was among the Ashab-e-Ijma. In that message, the Imam mentioned the three most important responsibilities of the Shias, and in that Hadith, the Imam said: Tuba lishi'atinal mutamassikina bihubbina. The first responsibility the Imam stated is that there is 'Tuba' for these Shias of ours—meaning the Imam is giving the glad tidings of Paradise—but for which Shias? Those who remain steadfast in our love, 'fi ghaybati mahdina'—meaning the Imam used that special title of Imam-e-Zaman—so the first responsibility in the Ghaybat of Imam-e-Zaman is to remain steadfast in the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), 'al-thabitina ala mawalatina' (to remain steadfast on our Wilayat), 'wal bara'ati min a'da-ina' (and to dissociate from our enemies). If we do this, the Imam says that 'ulaika minna wa nahnu minhum' (they are from us and we are from them). They are pleased that we are their Imams, and we are also pleased that they are our Shias. And then the Imam took an oath—what is called Qasam-e-Shar'i—the Imam swore by God, saying: 'Wallahi hum wallahi ma'ana fi darajatina yawmal qiyamah' (By God, by God, they will be with us at our level on the Day of Judgment). You will find this Hadith in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 51, Chapter 7, on page 151; this is Hadith number 6. Furthermore, in a Hadith of Imam Jawad (a.s.), regarding those scholars who, in this era of Ghaybat, take care of the faith of the 'Yatiman-e-Aal-e-Muhammad' (a.s.)—those individuals who are far from their Imam—who provide for them, protect them from the attacks of enemies and Nasibis, connect them to their Imam, and keep them away from the whispers of Satan, Imam Jawad (a.s.) says that the virtue of such scholars over all other worshippers is like the virtue of the sky over the earth. And you will find this Hadith in Tafsir-e-Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) on page 344, Hadith number 224. Now, let us move on to today's discussion, in which the respected Maulana Sheikh Nadir Sadiqi Sahab will guide us on the topic of Taqlid, Insha'Allah. Assalamu Alaikum, Aqa. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. Alhamdulillah, the Momineen benefited greatly from your session yesterday, and the reason for that is that you did not use complex language, but rather simple and clear language. It is your love. The elegance of Urdu is there, what can we do? We are all ready to listen to you, Maulana Sahab, but I would like to make a special request to the viewers. As I mentioned yesterday, you can only send questions via The Strong Rope's WhatsApp number, which is +91 or [number removed], the code is [number removed]. [number removed]. However, while asking questions, please keep one thing in mind: your questions should be relevant to the topic and the discussion, and should not be about any specific individual. If your question includes the name of any personality, especially any Shia, we will not be able to include such questions. I apologize to the viewers for this; it is my responsibility to clarify this so that no viewer feels that we intentionally excluded their question. Therefore, keep these things in mind while asking questions. With that, let us move towards today's discussion. Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum wal'an A'da'ahum Ajma'in. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alamin. Assalatu was-salamu ala Sayyidina wa Mawlana Abil Qasim Muhammad, wa ala Ahlil-baytit-tayyibinat-tahirin, wa la'nud-da'imu ala a'da'ihim ila qiyam yawmid-din. Rabbi-shrah li sadri wa yassir li amri wahlul uqdatan min lisani yafqahu qawli. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-hujjatibnil-hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyina. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyikal-faraj waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa atba'ihi wa shi'atihi. Amma ba'd, faqad qala Allahu Subhanahu wa Ta'ala fi kitabil-karim, A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Yawma nad'u kulla unasin bi-imamihim, faman utiya kitabahu bi-yaminihi fa-ula'ika yaqra'una kitabahum wa la yuzlamuna fatila. Fatazaru inni ma'akum minal-muntazirin. Sadaq Allahul Aliyul Azim. Our discussion is about our responsibility in the era of Ghaybah (Occultation), and specifically about referring to those scholars, taking our religious issues to those scholars who 'ya'rifu halalana wa haramana, ya'rifu hadithana' (who know our lawful and unlawful, who know our hadith). Those who... Are knowledgeable of our lawful and unlawful. Who are knowledgeable of our hadiths. It is very strict. It is difficult. But regardless, the way we are in our worldly life, in worldly affairs, in the matter of earning every single penny, in the matter of living life, in the matter of eating and drinking, the amount of caution we exercise, the amount of time we give—if even a tenth of that—and it is a matter of regret that I am even using the term 'a tenth'—if we gave even a tenth of that time to religion, then this biggest problem that every Momin is worried about today... Why are they worried? I presented the hadith of the eleventh Imam to you: 'Man takaffala bi-aytami Ale Muhammad alayhimussalam' (Whoever takes responsibility for the orphans of the family of Muhammad). We do not entrust our worldly affairs to non-experts. But in the affairs of religion, whoever took the name of Allah and the Messenger, we entrusted our religion to them. For God's sake! If we exercised even a tenth of the caution we exercise in worldly matters in religious matters, then this situation would not have arisen today. I apologize. Do not trust what I say, because you do not know me. Look, Insha'Allah, today I will read a narration that I will connect to Taqlid (emulation). 'Ma'munana fid-dunya wal-akhirah' (Trustworthy in this world and the hereafter). When a narrator comes and asks the Imam, 'O Messenger of Allah, we cannot reach you at all times, so where should we go?' So the Imam stated two criteria: that he is 'thiqah' (reliable), trustworthy. 'Ma'mun', 'ma'mun' means he is in safety; you can take religion from him without fear or danger. You do not know me, you cannot take religion from me. These robes and turbans, with all due respect, are not a sign of being 'ma'mun', not a sign of safety, not a sign of being without danger. I am very sorry, I apologize. Every person, every scholar is worthy of respect. Respect is in its place, but in acquiring religion, as the Imams have stated, one must be 'ma'mun'. 'Ma'mun', safe from security. Having a good opinion (Husn-e-Zann) is a different matter; one must have a good opinion of every Momin. One must respect a scholar more, respect the one in these robes more. But this does not mean that I should entrust my religion to just anyone. Many Momineen might have seen me for the first time through this channel. That is fine, look at my words, listen to them, if it is logical, then every human's logic and every human's intellect can grasp it. It is in accordance with the hadith, go and check the hadith to see if I am speaking correctly or not. This is a 2+2=4 law. But we do not exercise this kind of caution in worldly affairs. I do not want to discuss this topic much. Therefore, I will present some narrations regarding religion. Taqlid, we directly apply it to Taqlid. The Imams of Ahlul-bayt (a.s.) had started giving the concept of Taqlid in their time. The concept of Taqlid, both from an intellectual perspective and from the perspective of narrations, is absolutely clear, like 2+2=4. First, I will present a small intellectual argument (Dalil-e-Aqli) for you. Look, the intellectual argument—this is also a big problem, that what do we even call an intellectual argument? We don't even know what an intellectual argument is. We take our temperament, our upbringing, our desires, and put them all into the intellectual argument. This is a detailed discussion in itself. But regardless, I am giving you an argument right now. If your noble intellect can understand this argument of mine, then it is fine, otherwise, we will go into the transmitted argument (Dalil-e-Naqli) which the narrations state. The first question, now I will ask a few questions, you keep answering them for yourselves. The first question: Are we obligated (mukallaf) like the rest of the Momineen or not? The time of the Messenger, the time of Amirul Momineen (a.s.), the time of the rest of the Imams (a.s.), and the Imam of the Time (a.s.) went into occultation. These companions of the Imams, the Momineen of that time, were they obligated to perform prayer, fasting, Hajj, Zakat, Khums, and all the religious rulings, or not? Was prayer obligatory for them or not? This is called being 'mukallaf'. Everyone will say, 'Of course, they were.' Well, when the companions of the Imams, the Momineen of that time, were obligated, we are also obligated today. Prayer is obligatory for us, fasting is obligatory for us, Hajj is obligatory for us, and all the same religion is obligatory for us that was obligatory for the companions and Momineen of the time of the Imams (a.s.). This is the first question and its answer. The second question: Is there anyone today upon whom revelation (Wahi) descends? Everyone's answer is clear. There is no such person upon whom revelation descends. The third question: Is there any person today who can claim that I am connected to the Imam of the Time (a.s.)? I take my questions, my thoughts, my religion, my Sharia from the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Who am I and who are you, with all due respect? Look, meeting the Imam of the Time is a separate discussion. Its denial cannot be made, this is a separate discussion. But legal Taqlid, is there any Momin today? A Faqih, a Marja, a Mujtahid does not say this, so how can we? I and you, with all due respect. Sometimes someone might have met him in their life—may God Almighty grant us all the opportunity to visit the Imam. May God Almighty grant us all the success to live in the wealth of the Imam's truth. May He place us among his helpers and supporters. But this is the appearance of Ghaybah, the era of Ghaybah. Today's Faqih—and I am saying this with a challenge, I will discuss this topic at some other time—I will just present one sentence for you: go and see, the books of Dars-e-Kharij of all the Fuqaha are present, no Faqih says that I asked this jurisprudential question to the Imam of the Time. One or two issues are found, and even their authenticity is a detailed discussion, that is a separate debate. So, the third question: no one among me or you has the Imam's WhatsApp number. Prayer, fasting, Hajj, Zakat, practicing religion—the first question. Gabriel and revelation do not descend, peace be upon him. Third, there is no connection with the Imam (a.s.) in jurisprudential matters. That is a separate thing, having unseen help. What is that? That is a separate debate. Then I have to pray, I have to fast, I have to perform Wudu, I have to perform Taharah, these are thousands of issues. Well, up to here it is proven to me that I have to pray, I have to fast. Now, which prayer should I perform? Should I perform the prayer of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) or should I perform the prayer that is in my intellect? One has to practice Sharia and Fiqh in the way that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) has... Imam Baqir (a.s.) explained the religion of the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in 55,000 narrations in Wasa'il al-Shia. 55,000 narrations, 30 volumes of Wasa'il al-Shia. According to the print of Mu'assasat Al al-Bayt, it is 30 volumes of Wasa'il al-Shia, approximately 55,000 narrations. 55,000 narrations. This Tawdih al-Masa'il of ours has about 2,500 to 3,000 rulings. 2,000, 2,500. Maximum 3,000. And Wasa'il al-Shia has approximately 55,000 narrations. Which prayer should I perform? Should I perform the prayer according to Wasa'il al-Shia, or according to what comes to my mind, what I desire, what suits my mood, or what I understand? If the prayer were according to my intellect, if the Sharia were according to my desire and my mood, then what was the need to send the Imams? Those companions like Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Abu Basir, and all the companions of the Imams (a.s.) were coming to the Imam, asking about every single thing, writing it down, inquiring, pressing for details, and cross-questioning. God forbid, one might say that the Imam had no other activity—God forbid, God forbid, God forbid. Right. So, the fourth question. Whose Sharia must I follow? That is known. That is clear. This is what it means. This is what it means. 'Innama waliyyukumullahu wa rasuluhu walladhina amanu...' Allah is your Wali, the Messenger is your Wali, Ali ibn Abi Talib (s.a.) is your Wali. Your Wali, meaning 'O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority (Ulil Amr).' Obey the masters of Wilayah. This is it. I just have to follow that Sharia. Right. Now tell me. Perhaps the answer to one question is possible for many—for students of religious seminaries and schools, this might not be new, but I say one sentence, and everyone is stunned by this question of mine. Who said Taqlid (emulation) is obligatory? No jurist (Faqih), no Marja, no Mujtahid says that Taqlid itself is obligatory. No. Now, I will clarify this point later, though my point must have become clear by now. Four questions. Right, now when I have to act upon the religion, act upon the Sharia of the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and not use my own intellect, then what will I do? Therefore, there are three paths before me. And this is the answer to that question. This is the answer to that question: Who said that Taqlid is exclusively obligatory? Taqlid is not exclusively obligatory. You can accept any one of the three options. And I will put Taqlid in the last place. The first option: become a Mujtahid yourself. Become a Mujtahid. By Mujtahid, I don't mean—if someone doesn't like the name of the Hawza Ilmiyya of Qom, or doesn't like the name of the Hawza Ilmiyya of Najaf—it is impossible without going there. But I have no concern with that. There are 500-600 Quranic verses that explain the jurisprudential rulings, the lawful and the unlawful. About 500-550 verses. Approximately 550. You don't do it. What is the difficulty? I have the Urdu translation of the Quran in my house, the English translation of the Quran, the Hindi translation of the Quran. No, you should not follow the translator. What is the verse of the Quran stating? Therefore, first of all, you must know Arabic. You must know the Arabic book. In this, you will not follow the translator? You need to know what the Divine Revelation is stating directly, what the words of the Divine Revelation are. No one said you must follow so-and-so. If you don't like the name 'Taqlid,' that's fine. Learn the Arabic language, learn the language of the Quran. I am not even saying the whole Quran. Just derive the command of God from those 550 jurisprudential verses. And the four books (Kutub al-Arba) which were compiled, and other books compiled by Sheikh Hurr al-Amili in the book Wasa'il al-Shia, approximately 55,000 narrations. Don't say, 'I have the translation of Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih, I have the translation of Istibsar, I have the translation of Tahdhib.' No, it is not about the translator. We must understand the words of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and the words of Imam Baqir (a.s.). What is the translator's interpretation? What do I know? The translator's understanding is his own. His understanding is not a proof (Hujjah) for me. Therefore, the first option is to become a Mujtahid. The second option: act upon the most difficult ruling among the fatwas of all the jurists from Sheikh Tusi to Sheikh Saduq and up to today. The third option—this sounds good, doesn't it? From Sheikh Saduq until today, all the most difficult rulings, because that is what precaution (Ihtiyat) means. Perhaps the fatwa of Sheikh Saduq is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Sheikh Tusi is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Sheikh Hurr al-Amili is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Allama Hilli is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Muhaqqiq Hilli is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Shahid al-Awwal is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Shahid al-Thani is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Sheikh Ansari is correct, perhaps the fatwa of the late Akhund Khumayni is correct, perhaps the fatwa of the late Khoei is correct, perhaps the fatwa of Agha Sistani is correct. They are not infallible. Therefore, practice precaution. Collect everyone's fatwas. We couldn't digest one Tawdih (book of rulings) until now, and the Maulana has made us read all the Tawdihs. Collect all the Tawdihs and follow the most difficult fatwa, because a difficult fatwa is what precaution is. The issue of 'clear appearance' is there. What remains as the third option? Which is a rational method. It is that the ignorant should refer to the learned. The ignorant should refer to the learned. If we talk technically, it is that the ignorant should refer to the ignorant. Intellect says so. Should the learned refer to the ignorant? Intellect does not accept that. Should the learned refer to the learned? No, these three options are wrong. Even the learned referring to the learned—why? The learned should refer to the Imam. That is why Taqlid of another Mujtahid is not permissible for a Mujtahid. The fourth option remains, which is that I am ignorant. I am ignorant of Ijtihad and deduction. I will refer to the learned; intellect says this. Tell me, can the Imam or God make a rule that every person should get up and leave the Hawza Ilmiyya of Qom, Najaf, and all their work? It is not possible. The Quranic verse 'Lawla nafara min kulli firqatin minhum ta'ifatun'—the Quran is saying that a group should go from every sect. A group should go. Why is the Quran saying this? It is written in the Quran. Because it is not reasonable. This world order, the system of life, cannot be disrupted, cannot be turned upside down. It cannot be that businesses close, offices close, all work stops, and every person becomes a Zurarah or a Muhammad ibn Muslim. Every person becomes a Sheikh Tusi or a Sheikh Mufid. Let us all together pray for the reappearance of the Imam (a.t.f.s.) that, O Lord, by the sake of Muhammad and Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time. Grant us all the Taufiq to be counted among his sincere servants. Wa Akhiru Da'wana Anil Hamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum wal An A'daahum Ajma'een. Iltimas-e-Dua.

chapters.title: Responsibilities During the Major Occultation
chapters.summary: The era of Ghaybat-e-Kubra requires Shias to protect their faith by adhering to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt and following qualified scholars.

chapters.title: Guidelines for Religious Inquiry
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines the protocol for asking questions during the webinar and emphasizes the necessity of caution when selecting religious authorities.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Caution in Religious Matters
chapters.summary: Believers are urged to apply the same level of scrutiny to religious guidance as they do to worldly affairs, ensuring they follow scholars who are truly trustworthy.

chapters.title: The Concept and Logic of Taqlid
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces the concept of Taqlid, explaining that it is rooted in the teachings of the Ahlulbayt and is intellectually verifiable.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Religious Obligation
chapters.summary: The speaker establishes that believers in the era of Ghaybah remain obligated to follow the Sharia, just as the companions of the Imams were.

chapters.title: The Rationality of Following Religious Authority
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that given the vast number of narrations and the complexity of jurisprudence, one cannot rely on personal opinion or mood to practice religion.

chapters.title: Three Paths for Religious Practice
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines three logical options for practicing religion: becoming a Mujtahid, practicing absolute precaution (Ihtiyat), or performing Taqlid.

chapters.title: The Authority of Jurists and Taqleed
chapters.summary: The Imam encouraged his companions to issue fatwas and directed followers to specific trusted jurists when they could not reach him personally.

chapters.title: The Four Pillars of Hadith Preservation
chapters.summary: The Imam praised four specific companions for reviving the teachings of the Ahlulbayt, establishing the foundation for religious derivation.

chapters.title: The Role of Istinbat and Protectors of Religion
chapters.summary: The lecture explains that without these key jurists, the traces of Prophethood would have been lost, and defines the importance of Istinbat.

chapters.title: The Continuity of Jurisprudence and Ijtihad
chapters.summary: The work of early companions is compared to later scholars, emphasizing that Mujtahids dedicate their lives to preserving the Imams' teachings.

chapters.title: Necessity of Taqlid in the Occultation
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that in the absence of the Infallible Imam, following non-infallible Fuqaha is the only viable option for believers to understand religious law.

chapters.title: Understanding Ijtihad and Disagreement
chapters.summary: Disagreement among Mujtahidin is presented as a natural consequence of human non-infallibility and the complexity of interpreting 1400-year-old traditions.

chapters.title: The Evolution of Religious Understanding
chapters.summary: The speaker compares the progression of human intellect and scientific understanding to the scholarly development in interpreting the traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt.

chapters.title: The Legitimacy of Fatwa and Authority
chapters.summary: Clarifying that the Imams condemned those who used analogy and personal opinion, while explicitly authorizing qualified narrators to issue rulings based on divine traditions.

chapters.title: The Nature of Taqlid and Accountability
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that Taqlid is a procedural necessity for ensuring religious acts align with divine law, serving as a safeguard for the believer on the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: Defining a Momin and Concluding Advice
chapters.summary: The speaker defines a Momin through four core beliefs and encourages utilizing current times to deepen one's knowledge of the teachings of the Ahlulbayt.

title: Muharram 1442 English Majlis #09: A Key Reason for Success & Failure  | Sayed Mahdi Modarresi
excerpt: In this lecture, Sayed Mahdi Modarresi explores the spiritual and practical foundations of success, emphasizing the critical role of filial piety and honoring one's parents. He argues that personal and societal struggles often stem from a disconnect from divine values, specifically the neglect of parental rights. By drawing parallels between the life of Ali al-Akbar and the importance of obedience, the speaker encourages listeners to prioritize their relationship with their parents as a primary gateway to receiving divine guidance and blessings.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#09 - Imam Ali (a.s.) Ne Inteqaam Kyun Nahin Liya?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common theological objection regarding why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not take physical revenge after the oppression against Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). The speaker clarifies that the lack of retaliation does not negate the historical reality of the incident, citing Imam Ali's own words in the Khutbah-e-Shaqshaqiyyah. The discussion emphasizes that the Imam's patience was a calculated sacrifice for the preservation of Islam and the Ummah, rather than a sign of weakness or lack of bravery.
content:
Do it, do it [Music]. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. After the praise of Allah and the salutations upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his family, in today's episode, we have a question that is often raised. The critics ask that when Hazrat Ali (a.s.) was present there—and the bravery of Ali (a.s.) is famous, he is the one who uprooted the gate of Khaybar, he is the leader of the brave—then how is it possible that the door of the house was burnt before his eyes, the face of the lady was injured, and such oppression was committed? Why did he not take revenge? To get the answer to this objection, we have with us our scholar, our Chaudhary... With us is our scholar, our Chaudhary Ajit Singh Rawat, Tanveer Sahab, Anil Bhai, Ram Naresh Kumar, Anuj Bhai. As you have seen, this is the objection that the opponents present before us regarding the Princess (s.a.w.a.), that when he was present, how did this happen, and why did the Imam (a.s.) not take revenge? What will our respected scholar present as his thoughts on this? Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Brother, this series of ours, in which, if there is any biggest objection, it is this: that when Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) was present at that time when this oppression was being committed against Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.w.a.), why did he not make arrangements? The right to take revenge, the right to take breath, Allah has given to the oppressed, but whether they use this right or not, that is their choice. We find many such incidents in history where someone was oppressed, someone was killed, but their heirs, their guardians, did not take revenge... But their heirs, their guardians, did not take revenge, but this does not prove that the incident did not happen. Here, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), the successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), was not just any person, but the Caliph of the Muslims, and he presented a shining example of high moral character. That after so much oppression, when he observed patience, it does not prove that Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.w.a.) was not present. Today, every Muslim, whether Shia or not, believes in this fact, accepts this fact that in the battle of Karbala, Imam Hussain (a.s.) was kept thirsty for three days, but his mother was... so does this mean we should say this is absolutely not... We should say this is absolutely not true, that if revenge was not taken, the incident did not happen. And secondly, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) himself, in one of his famous sermons which we know as the 'Khutbah-e-Shaqshaqiyyah', which is present in the world, in it he (a.s.) says: 'Fasabartu wa fi al-ayn qadha wa fi al-halq shaja'—that I observed patience while there was a thorn in my eye and a choking in my throat, and I was seeing my inheritance being looted. If this incident did not happen, then why these words of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.)? This proves that such an incident happened, and Amir al-Mu'minin observed it, and this patience was so heavy. The example he gave, that there was a thorn in my eye, this was not an easy matter. Was it for Amir al-Mu'minin... Was it not an easy matter for Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to observe patience? But keeping all these things in view, and as a true successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he presented a proof and observed patience. We all know Hazrat Musa (a.s.), who was martyred in the zeal and passion for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) took his martyrdom... it is not that we can say that Janab-e-Hamza was not martyred. History of Islam has a well-known battle, which we know by the name of the Battle of Tabuk, and when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was going, he was going there, so some people tried to assassinate him. So, after this incident, did the Messenger take revenge or not? This is our question. People raise this question, why didn't he kill them? Why not? The Messenger of Allah, in his Prophet's life, in many places and which... In his Prophet's life, in many places, and the famous battles, and the leaders and chiefs of the Muslims and non-Muslims took revenge from the people, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) took it. So much so that when these people came to the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah did not take revenge. People did, and it is not that for 1400 years these people remained for Islam, yet the Messenger did not take it. So all these are found in history, but all these were forgotten, and his martyrdom... what am I? By studying all the history, all the hadith, all the books, it is clear that Amir al-Mu'minin did not take revenge. Yes, this is not true. Apart from that, if... Yes, this is not correct. Besides, if Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) had to take action and seek justice, he would have gone there. Because our Caliphs were those people who did not want anyone to go to them. We find that people took their grievances to them, but that group was a gang of looters, so they were forgiven. We find that Bin Jahl committed adultery, and even though there were witnesses against him, he was still forgiven by the Caliph's order. Another instance is very famous: Khalid bin Walid attacked Malik bin Nuwayrah, forced himself upon his wife, and when he was brought to the court, no action was taken against him; rather, he was forgiven. So, what is the guarantee that if... So, what is the guarantee that if Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had taken his grievance to their court, he would have received his right? It was presented, but it was not received. So, we can say it like this, but these are some... please subscribe to the channel. And those oppressors will be punished for their deeds, Insha'Allah. Thank you very much, Sameer Bhai. You were young, you came yourself, you discussed this, and this is also a point. It is not necessary that what the Sunnis believe is the final word. I remembered the events of the city in this regard, that there was a will that the Caliphs did not let be fulfilled, a matter that they did not let be completed. A matter that they did not let be completed, and the Caliphate was taken away. While taking the Caliphate, he stood up and did not let an uproar happen. While taking the Caliphate, he stood up and did not let an uproar happen. These were some reasons. You mentioned that he was also seen saying that a bone was stuck in his throat, but he exercised patience for the sake of the Ummah. He endured this. These are the answers to the questions that are raised, like why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not take action. We end this episode here today, but I request you that if you are not satisfied with this answer, please send your questions to our WhatsApp number or our social media handles. Insha'Allah, we will try to answer them. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. [Music]

title: Majlis 3 |  Kufa Ki Mukhtasar Tareekh | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | #Muharram 2026 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the historical and spiritual significance of Kufa, tracing its evolution from the time of Imam Ali (a.s.) to the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in Wilayah, the virtues of patience and certainty, and the distinction between true followers and political opportunists. It concludes with a poignant reflection on the martyrdom of Ali Akbar (a.s.) and the enduring legacy of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
A'udhu billahi as-sami'il 'aleem min ash-shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Raheem. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'aliyyil 'azeem. Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, ni'mal mawla wa ni'man naseer. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen, wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqeen, wal yaqeen, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya-i wal mursaleen, habibi ilahil 'alameen, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aalihi al-ma'sumeen alladhina adhhaballahu 'anhumur rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum, sima baqiyatillahi fil aradeen, Imam-e-Zamanina wa wali amrina wa sahibina wa mawlana wa habibina wa tabibina wa anisina wa mu'nisina al-kahfil hasin wa ghiyathi mudtarril mustakeen, ruhi wa arwahul 'alamina lahu al-fida. Amma ba'd, faqad qala mawlana wa sayyidunal Husayn ibn Ali 'alayhimas salam: 'Wa'lamu anna al-ma'rufa maksabu hamdan wa mu'qibu ajran, falaw ra'aytum al-ma'rufa rajulan lara'aytumuhu hasanan jamilan yasurun nazireen wa yafuqul 'alameen.' Sadaqa mawlana al-Husayn ibn Ali 'alayhimas salam. Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sallallahu 'alayka ya Aba Abdillah, sallallahu 'alayka ya Aba Abdillah, sallallahu 'alayka ya Aba Abdillah. The Hadith... that has been selected for this discussion, for these five sessions, in this Hadith, Imam Husayn (a.s.) says: 'Wa'lamu anna al-ma'rufa maksabu hamdan wa mu'qibu ajran'—know that through Ma'ruf (good deeds), you will earn praise and commendation; people will praise you if you always keep doing good, 'wa mu'qibu ajran'—and Allah will also give you a reward. That is, your name will be good among people, and you will also receive a reward near Allah. 'Falaw ra'aytum al-ma'rufa rajulan'—if Ma'ruf were to come in the form of a human, if it were or would be, you would see that it would be extremely beautiful and handsome, which would bring joy to the onlookers, and it would have superiority over all the worlds; there could be nothing greater than this in all the worlds. And I have presented to you that what is meant by Ma'ruf is the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.); it is the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt. It is nothing other than the Wilayat of the Ahlulbayt. As I mentioned to you, the word Wilayat, understand it—you must hear it often, it is used frequently in Arabic. You must hear 'Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt'. If you read it as 'Wilayat', it means mastership. But if you look at Hadith books, it is not written as 'Wilayat', but 'Wilayat'. If you look at the Hadith books, when you read the diacritics (vowels), it is read as 'Wilayat'. The correct pronunciation is 'Wilayat', and 'Wilayat' means support, 'Wilayat' means helping. Supporting the Ahlulbayt is the real thing; not just considering them as masters—many people do that—but the real thing is 'Wilayat', meaning helping them, supporting them. Anyway, this is everything I presented to you, that Archangel Jibra'il came to the Prophet and said, 'I will give you such a gift from Allah that neither has He given to anyone before, nor will He ever give to anyone after you.' Meaning the best gift. And that was the Hadith in which he said, 'What is the first thing?' He said, 'Sabr (patience).' And 'What is better than patience?' He said, 'Rida (contentment).' And 'What is better than contentment?' He said, 'Zuhd (asceticism).' And 'What is better than asceticism?' He said, 'Ikhlas (sincerity).' And 'What is better than sincerity?' He said, 'Yaqeen (certainty).' And then he said, 'What is better than certainty?' He said, 'The perfection of all these things, when all these things gather at one stage, it is called Tawakkul (trust in Allah).' Look at the status of the Ahlulbayt. Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) himself says, 'By God, if there were no fear of God, Ali would have taught the son of Abu Sufyan what deceit means.' Subhan Allah. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Did you notice? So this Kufa entirely... After the martyrdom of Ali (a.s.), in 40 Hijri, for 10 years—or rather 20 years, because after 10 years was the martyrdom of Imam Hasan (a.s.)—Muawiya had rule over the entire Islamic world for 20 years. 20 years. 20 years. Now you can understand what 20 years means. There was tremendous propaganda there. You must understand what propaganda is, right? Those who understand, they understand. Tremendous propaganda. So much propaganda that 70,000 pulpits were set up to curse Ali (a.s.). And so much propaganda—a factory of hadiths was literally established. Many hadiths were fabricated. Such hadiths—the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ana Madinatul Ilm wa Aliyun Babuha' (I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate). So they said, 'Fabricate a hadith that so-and-so is the roof, so-and-so is the wall, so-and-so is...' I won't take many names, you understand the rest. Right? Whatever is necessary in a house. Recite a Salawat (Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum). Actually, those who fabricated the hadiths were also fools. They didn't understand that no matter what, people will enter through the door only. Subhan Allah. Did you notice? They didn't even think about what they were writing. But they fabricated the hadith. Well, they fabricated it, they were who they were. After that, people wrote in their books, 'Look, this is also among his virtues.' Just think, what has happened to the Muslims? Anyway, I don't want to go into details. Just understand that this happened—the Uthmani rule, meaning on one side the Uthmani trend, and on the other side, the lovers of Ali (a.s.). Now this became a whole thing—'No, no, brother, we must take revenge for the blood of Uthman, we must take revenge.' This became a slogan. They used to walk around carrying Uthman's shirt. You know, the blood-stained shirt. 'We will take revenge for this, we will take revenge for this, and we will take it from Ali, and from his children, and from his companions who killed him.' Now, so much propaganda was done, so much propaganda, that people completely—including Kufa—all of them adopted that ideology. Except for a few individuals. Even in Kufa, even in Kufa. Even in Kufa, if there were people who were truly lovers of Ali (a.s.), who were the actual Shias. Now, there were two types of Shias here. This is the point I wanted to present to you. There were two types of Shias. Remember this. And this is a very important point. This point is valid even today. Two types of Shias. One, political Shias. And two, Shias by belief. The political Shias were those who started following Ali (a.s.) because Ali's government had come. They followed because the slogan was 'Nahnu ma'a man ghalab' (We are with whoever is victorious). Whoever has the government, we are with them. So these were political Shias. How many were Shias by belief? Shias by belief were people like Habib ibn Mazahir, Maytham al-Tammar, Rashid al-Hujri, Mukhtar al-Thaqafi. These were the few who could be counted on fingers. These were the actual Shias. But they were very few. Hani ibn Urwa. Hani ibn Urwa. They were all there, but very few. Because the population of Kufa was large. So what happened? What was the result? That they planned this event of Karbala. So they planned it in such a way that it should happen where it is famous that Shias live—so that Hussain is killed there and the blame falls on the Shias. And that is why this was planned. 'Do one thing, tell the people of Kufa to invite Hussain.' This was a proper conspiracy. And those who wrote letters to Imam Hussain (a.s.) were all political Shias. 'You come, you come. We will support you.' And when Imam Hussain (a.s.) came to Karbala, it is obvious that he turned from Kufa to Karbala. He did not go to Kufa. Because Janab-e-Muslim (a.s.) had written a letter saying, 'Do not come here. Here, only tongues are with you, swords are against you. Everyone here is against you.' Janab-e-Muslim (a.s.) wrote. He was the ambassador of Imam Hussain (a.s.). He wrote. Imam Hussain (a.s.) understood. He went to Karbala. Now in Karbala, these were the same people who had written the letters, they were the ones who came to kill Imam Hussain (a.s.). What do you recite in Ziyarat-e-Ashura? That these people—there is a phrase in Ziyarat-e-Ashura, right? That they came wearing masks. Why did they come wearing masks? So that Hussain would not recognize them. But Imam Hussain (a.s.) recognized them. He was an Imam. They are not rulers of the world, they are not world leaders, they are not world rulers. They are the Hujjat-e-Khuda (Proof of God) from Allah who possesses knowledge of the unseen. They are not deans of some university. Did you notice? Hujjat-e-Khuda, whom Allah appoints. Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'You were the ones, right?' He addressed those who had called him by writing letters. You called me by writing letters. They became silent. There was no answer. Some of them who were ill-mannered behaved rudely with the companions of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and gave nonsensical answers, which I won't mention now. Anyway, these people did this. This brief background was presented to you, that if this event, the event of Karbala, had happened in Syria, if it had happened in Basra, then this thing would never have happened—that Shias killed him. But because Kufa was generally famous for Shias living there, this accusation was leveled. Otherwise, this is a very in-depth study. We have presented this to you in a few minutes, otherwise, it is an in-depth study. People in Kufa were against Ali (a.s.), and you see Ali (a.s.) has condemned them repeatedly in Nahjul Balagha. The condemnation in Nahjul Balagha is for the political Shias. Anyway, the martyr we have to mention today is the eldest son of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Whom we call Janab-e-Ali Akbar (a.s.). I will quickly present two points to you. You know that Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah has been issued by Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) as well. And in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah from Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), he instructs the companion that when you go for the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.), you must perform the Ziyarat of Janab-e-Ali Akbar (a.s.). After that, Sheikh al-Kulayni brings another tradition in Al-Kafi, from which you can understand the status of Janab-e-Ali Akbar (a.s.). I will read those sentences to you—these are the sentences of the Imam. Whose sentences are they? The sentences of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam says, 'Then after that, go to the grave of Ali ibn Hussain (a.s.) and say, "Assalamu alayka ya ibna Rasulillah" (Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah). "Wassalamu ala malaikatillahil muqarrabeen wa anbiya'ihil mursaleen" (And peace be upon the angels of Allah who are brought near and His sent Prophets). "Ya Mawlaya"'—whose words are these? Imam Sadiq (a.s.) is saying to Janab-e-Ali Akbar (a.s.), 'Ya Mawlaya' (O my Master)! 'Wa ibna Mawlaya' (And son of my Master)! 'Wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu alayka, sallallahu alayka wa ala ahli baytik' (And the mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, may Allah send blessings upon you and upon your Ahlulbayt). 'Wa itrati aba'ikal akhyaril abrar' (And peace be upon the progeny of your fathers, the chosen and the righteous). 'Alladhina adhhaballahu anhumur rijsa wa tahharahum tathira' (Those from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification). These are the ones—meaning Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and this is a tradition from Usul-e-Kafi, I am not saying this from myself. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) is linking Janab-e-Ali Akbar (a.s.) to the Ayat-e-Tat'hir (Verse of Purification). Did you notice? And that is why when all the martyrs were martyred, Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Taqaddam ya bunayya' (Go forward, O my son). Ali Akbar is ready, he is prepared to be martyred. But Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Son, first go to the tent and take permission from your mother, bid farewell to your aunt who has raised you with such care.' Ali Akbar came and first took permission from his mother. His mother said, 'Son, why do you take permission from me? Go and take permission from your aunt who has raised you with such care.' Ali Akbar came and stood before Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.). 'Aunt, please give me permission.' Before giving permission, Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.) said, 'Son, that is why I raised you for 18 years with such care.' She said, 'Aunt, if you do not give permission, then don't, but if there is a question on the Day of Judgment whether Ali Akbar was dearer or my Hussain?' That was all it took for Zainab (s.a.) to give permission. Now Ali Akbar left. Humayd ibn Muslim says that when Ali Akbar was leaving the tent, some lady was repeatedly holding Ali Akbar's garment. Ali Akbar was returning to the tent. If an elder stopped Ali Akbar, he would hold Ali Akbar's arm. But it is not strange that Sakina (s.a.) would repeatedly hold his garment and say, 'Ya Aliyyu irham ghurbatana' (O Ali Akbar, have mercy on our helplessness). Humayd ibn Muslim says Ali Akbar was leaving as if the funeral of a youth was leaving a house full of people. Ali Akbar left. Now Hussain, Hussain bid him farewell. He helped Ali Akbar mount, but once he looked towards the sky. After looking, he said, 'Allahumma ishhad ala ha'ula'il qawm' (O Allah, be a witness against this nation). 'Faqad baraza ilayhim ghulamun ashbahun nasi khalqan wa khuluqan wa mantiqan ila Rasulik' (For there has gone out to them a youth who is the most similar of people in creation, character, and speech to Your Messenger). In movement, in speech, in conduct, in character. When we were eager to see Your Messenger, we would look at Ali Akbar. He bid Ali Akbar farewell. Now Ali Akbar had not gone far when a sound was felt. He turned back and saw the old father with his hands on his waist. 'Ya Aliyyu, Ya Aliyyu'—'O Ali, O Ali,' father, you bid me farewell, you bid me farewell. He said, 'Son, if you had children, you would remember the grief of a young son, then you would understand what passes through a father's heart when a young son departs.' He bid Ali Akbar farewell. Ali Akbar went. He sent many wretches to hell. But Ali Akbar returned. Why did he return? How did he return? It is written in the Maqtal that it was a mother's heart; she could not bear it. A mother has a young son. She said, 'Fizza, stand by the door of the tent. Look, it is a matter of a young son. If my son falls into trouble, the color of my master's face will change.' Those who are parents understand the grief of children, they understand the trouble of children. Now Fizza came and stood at the door of the tent. After a while, the Lady (Zainab) came. The color of the master's face changed. She said, 'Give the master a little trouble.' Hussain came into the tent. 'Master, why has the color of your face changed?' She said, 'A famous wrestler of Arabia has come before my son. He is well-fed and quenched, and my child is hungry and thirsty for three days.' It was just a mother's heart. 'Master, what should I do?' He said, 'Pray. A mother's prayer is accepted for her child.' Umm-e-Laila formed a circle. The ladies formed a circle. Umm-e-Laila stood in the middle. "Ilahi bi-ghurbatil-Hussain, ya man radda Yusufa 'ala Ya'qub" (O Allah, by the loneliness of Hussain, O You who returned Yusuf to Ya'qub), O Sustainer, I beseech You by the helplessness of Hussain. O You who reunited Ya'qub with Yusuf, O You who returned Yusuf to Ya'qub, return my Ali Akbar to me. The mother's prayer had not even been completed when Ali Akbar came. But in what state did he come? In what condition did he come? That he was covered in wounds, drenched in blood, and what sentence did he say? It is a sentence from the Maqtal. You listen. I do not have the courage either. Ali Akbar began to say, "Ya abatal-'atashu qad qatalani" (O father, thirst has killed me). "Wa thiqlul-hadidi ajhadani" (And the weight of the iron armor has exhausted me). "Hal ila shurbatin minal-ma'i ataqawwa biha 'alal-a'da'" (Is there a sip of water so that I may gain strength against the enemies?). Hussain said, 'Son, you know that there is no water in the tents.' But "Hati lisanaka" (Bring your tongue), put your tongue in my mouth. Now, as soon as Ali Akbar placed his tongue in Hussain's blessed mouth, he pulled it back. He said, 'Father, there are thorns on your tongue.' Hussain gave him his ring. He said, 'Keep this, Ali Akbar. Now your grandfather will quench your thirst from the Pond of Kauthar.' Ali Akbar went. Even in that state, he sent 200 wretches to hell. Then, once, a wretch who had been aiming at Ali Akbar for a long time saw that Ali Akbar's chest was exposed. He struck such a spear that it pierced through Ali Akbar's chest. Ali Akbar fell to the ground. "Ya abata 'alaika minnis-salam" (O father, my final salaam to you). Hussain ran to him. He came and placed Ali Akbar's head on his lap. He pulled the spear from his chest. A fountain of blood erupted. Ali Akbar breathed his last. Hussain recited a dirge, "Ya bunayya 'alad-dunya ba'dakal-'afa'" (O son, after you, may the world be...), Enough! May there be dust upon the life of this world. It was like this, "Man hummud-dunya wa ghammuha" (Whoever is of the world's worries and griefs), son, you have been saved from the worries and griefs of the world, from the pain and trouble of the world. "Baqiya abuka faridan wahidan baynal-a'da'" (But your father remains alone and solitary among the enemies). Woe to Ali! Woe to the tragedy! "Wa saya'lamulladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun" (And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned). "'Ala la'natullahi 'alal-qawmiz-zalimin" (Upon the oppressors be the curse of Allah). O Sustainer! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. O Sustainer! Hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Allah, Amen. Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. O Allah, Amen. Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Allah, Amen. O Sustainer! Those who are in distress, remove their distresses. O Allah, Amen. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. O Allah, Amen. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. O Allah, Amen. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Allah, Amen. Those who are far from their homeland, return them safely to their homeland. O Allah, Amen. O Sustainer! Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. O Allah, Amen. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. O Allah, Amen. Protect the holy shrines. O Allah, Amen. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab. O Allah, Amen. Protect those who are protecting them. O Allah, Amen. Grant us the honor of the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the Hereafter. O Allah, Amen. Recite one Surah-e-Fatiha and three times Surah-e-Tawheed for the late Ghulam Ali ibn-e-Abdul Aziz Lakhani, the Lakhani family, Rupani family, Hamarvi family, Radha family, and Narsidani family, and for all the deceased men and women, one Surah-e-Fatiha and three times Surah-e-Qul-hu-Allah.

title: Ruku Mein Zakaat Kisne Di? | Shia Aur Ahle Tasannun Kitaabon Ka Muttafiq Aqeeda |
excerpt: This lecture discusses the Quranic verse 5:55, known as the Verse of Wilayah, which identifies the true guardians of the believers. The speaker explains that this verse was revealed to honor Hazrat Ali (a.s.) for giving his ring as charity while in the state of Ruku during prayer. The lecture highlights that both Shia and Sunni sources, such as Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur, confirm this historical event. It concludes by emphasizing the divine appointment of Ali (a.s.) as the successor to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his progeny. O Wali of the Age, help us and do not leave us. Allah (S.W.T.) announced the Wilayah of Hazrat Ali (a.s.) in the Holy Quran, Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 55. The Lord of Majesty says: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Verily, your Wali is only Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe, who establish prayer and give Zakat while they are in the state of Ruku.' Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) says in the interpretation of this verse: One day, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was offering prayers in the mosque when a beggar passed by him. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked the beggar, 'Has anyone given you anything?' The beggar replied, 'Yes, I passed by a person who was in the state of Ruku, and he gave me his ring.' And while saying this... He gave me his ring. And while saying this, he pointed towards Hazrat Ali (a.s.). Then this verse was revealed. Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'He, meaning Ali (a.s.), is your Wali after me.' In the Sunni book Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur, Ibn Abbas narrates that Hazrat Ali (a.s.) gave his ring in charity while in the state of Ruku. Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked the beggar, 'Who gave you this ring?' The beggar replied, 'The person who is in the state of Ruku.' After that, Allah (S.W.T.) revealed this verse. May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure progeny.
Surah Al-Ma'idah verse 55 identifies Allah, the Prophet, and those who give Zakat in Ruku as the believers' Wali.
Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) confirmed this verse refers to the incident where Hazrat Ali (a.s.) gave his ring to a beggar.
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) explicitly declared Ali (a.s.) as the Wali after him following this revelation.
Sunni scholar Ibn Abbas is cited as a narrator of this event in Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur.

The lecture emphasizes the consensus between Shia and Sunni historical accounts regarding this event.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 29 | Tafseer of Surah an-Nasr (110) - Part 3
excerpt: This lecture continues the tafseer of Surah an-Nasr by detailing the historical events leading up to the Conquest of Makkah. The speaker narrates the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) march with an army of 10,000 and the subsequent encounter with Abu Sufyan. The session highlights the Prophet's mercy in granting amnesty to his former enemies and the strategic surrender of Makkah.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the Prophet and the believers. I am here once again to continue the discussion. I was mentioning that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was preparing to leave... I mentioned that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was preparing to leave, he sent someone to bring Hatib. When he was brought, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked him why he did what he did. He replied, 'O Messenger of Allah, I believe in Allah and His Messenger; my faith has not changed. The truth is that my family is there, and I did this so that the people there would treat them well because of me.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) forgave him. Then, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) marched towards Makkah. It is narrated that when he set out for Makkah, it was the 10th of Ramadan, and he was fasting, as were the other Muslims. He reached a place called Kadid, near Usfan, where he broke his fast and then moved forward. He camped with an army of 10,000. People from the tribes also joined his army. The people of Makkah had no news of the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) arrival; they did not know what was happening. But when night fell, Abu Sufyan, Hakim bin Hizam, and Budayl bin Warqa went out of Makkah... Badal bin Warqa set out to find out if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was heading towards them. He met the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) at a certain place. Abu Sufyan and Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah also tried to reach the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to meet him. When they reached, they remembered Salman and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, your cousin and your brother's son want to meet you.' You (the Prophet) said, 'I have no need of them. They know what they did to me.' At that time, Abu Sufyan's young son was also with him. He said, 'Either you let me come to you, or I will take my child and go into the desert to die of hunger and thirst.' When this reached the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), he forgave him. He presented his mother in the form of a plea. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) struck his chest and said, 'You have troubled me everywhere and opposed me intensely.' Now, regarding the meeting of Abu Sufyan, it is narrated by Ibn Abbas that when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) reached Marr al-Zahran, Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib thought to himself, 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has left Medina, and now the people of Mecca are doomed.' If he enters Mecca with a sword, the people of Mecca will be destroyed forever. Abbas mounted the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) mount and went out, hoping to find a woodcutter or someone else to tell the people of Mecca to meet the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) at a certain place and seek amnesty. Abbas says, 'I was searching for someone with this intention when I heard the voices of Budayl bin Warqa and others who had gone out to get news of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). I heard Abu Sufyan saying, 'By God, I have never seen such fires as I see today.' These were the fires of the people of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) lit for battle. I recognized the voice and called out to him, 'O Abu Hanzala!' He replied, 'Who is this?' I said, 'It is I, Abbas.' Abu Sufyan asked, 'What has happened?' Abu Sufyan asked what had happened. He said, 'May my parents be sacrificed for you, what is the latest news?' I said, 'The fires you see are the fires of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). He has come with a massive army that you cannot withstand. He is with ten thousand Muslims.' Abu Sufyan asked, 'O Abbas, what is your advice for me? What can be done?' Abbas said, 'Get on the back of this mule behind me so I can take you to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and seek amnesty for you.' Abu Sufyan rode behind Abbas. We moved quickly toward the Islamic army. When we reached the fires of the Muslims, they recognized the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) uncle. Finally, we reached the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and I interceded for Abu Sufyan, and he accepted. At this moment, Abu Sufyan recited the Kalima of Islam. However, he did not recite it out of knowledge or love for Islam, but out of fear that they might be destroyed. He did not change his ways later; history is before you. Abbas says, 'I got up from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and I...' I got up from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and kept Abu Sufyan with me on the mountain peak. The Islamic army was passing by; one tribe would pass, and then another would follow. Abu Sufyan was watching, and I was telling him, 'This is such-and-such tribe.' In the meantime, the mount of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appeared, surrounded by the Muhajirun and Ansar, who were clad in iron armor such that only their eyes were visible. I asked him, 'Who is this?' I said, 'This is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' Abu Sufyan said, 'By God, your nephew's power and glory have increased greatly.' I said, 'This is not worldly rule; this is Prophethood.' I told Abu Sufyan, 'Now go to your people and warn them that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is coming toward them.' Abu Sufyan reached the place quickly and announced to the people of Mecca, 'O people of Mecca, be warned! Muhammad is coming toward you with a massive army. You have no power to resist him.' He then offered them a way out. He said, 'Whoever enters my house will be safe.' Abbas asked, 'How can so many people fit in your house?' He said, 'Then whoever enters the Masjid is also safe, and whoever locks his house door is also secure.' Respected listeners, this... Whoever locks his house door is also secure. Respected listeners, this is the story of Abu Sufyan. God willing, I will discuss more about this tomorrow. Until then, I take your leave. I have narrated what I have presented before you from Tafsir al-Qurtubi, Volume 9, pages 413-414. Anyone who wishes to check the references can do so. God willing, I will continue this tomorrow. Until then, I take your leave. Khuda Hafiz. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 19 | Tafseer of Surah al-Qadr (97) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual virtues and practical applications of Surah al-Qadr as taught by the Ahlulbayt. The speaker details specific traditions from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the use of the Surah for healing illnesses and seeking protection from the horrors of the Day of Judgment. The session concludes by highlighting the immense mercy bestowed upon worshippers during the Night of Decree, while emphasizing the critical importance of maintaining good character and avoiding major sins like disobedience to parents.
content:
Ma-sha-Allah, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil adheem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin. Assalatu wassalamu ala ashrafil ambiya-i wal mursalin, Abil Qasim Muhammad, wa ala alihi tayyibinal tahirin. Amma ba'd. Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, in the Holy Quran, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylatil qadr.' Assalamu Alaikum. Today, I am present before you to discuss the Tafsir of Surah al-Qadr, its benefits, and its virtues. The Tafsir of Surah al-Qadr, its benefits, and its virtues. Yesterday, we felt the atmosphere of the nights of Ramadan, in which I described the virtues of Laylat al-Qadr. What are those virtues? And in this Surah, I described some virtues. Let us take this matter further. First, I will present the translation before you: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter. Peace it is, until the emergence of dawn.' Respected viewers, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) has given a will to his followers: 'When you are afflicted with an illness, take a new clay pot, put water in it, and recite Surah al-Qadr 130 times over it.' Recite Surah al-Qadr 130 times over it. Then drink from that water, perform ablution, and pour the water over your body. When the water decreases, add more water to it. Do this for three days. God willing, you will get rid of this illness. Respected viewers, often we are worried about illnesses and ask one person or another for a cure. We ask for the method of Dua, we ask for the method of Quranic Surahs, asking, 'Tell us, what is the benefit of which Surah? We are ill, which Surah should we recite to get a cure? What deeds should we perform to get relief?' The meaning of 'Amal' (deed) is what the Masumeen (a.s.) have stated. I do not know any other deed. But the same deed that the Masumeen (a.s.) have told us—'Perform this deed, recite this Surah in this way, you will get these benefits'—therein lies the benefit. There is no benefit in following the words of any human. But often we are worried. For example, the current illness... since the Imam (a.s.) did not specify any particular illness... Did not specify that this will only work for a specific illness. To get rid of this illness, no matter what the illness is, even if it is a virus, if we perform this deed in our homes, God willing, I hope that since the Sadiq of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) said it, this will also provide relief from this virus and other illnesses. As for what others are saying, following it is also necessary. In the books of traditions, it is narrated from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) that the Night of Qadr is powerful. In it, the destiny of people is decided, and on the Night of Qadr, Allah sends down His angels. A caller calls out, 'Whoever visits the blessed grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) on this night, Allah will forgive all his sins.' May Allah grant us all the opportunity to visit the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) on the Night of Qadr. Imam (a.s.) said, 'Whoever visits the grave of his believing brother and recites Surah al-Qadr seven times over his grave, and while reciting, keeps his hand on the grave, Allah will, on the Day of Judgment...' May Allah protect such a person from the horrors of the Day of Judgment. The horrors of the Day of Judgment are such that every human being is terrified of them, but if we want salvation from them, then as the Imam (a.s.) has said, if one recites these supplications, the reciter will find relief, salvation from the horrors of the Day of Judgment, and those who are buried in the graves—whoever recites it for them—they will also benefit. This order has been given, and the Imam (a.s.) said that when the night of Qadr fully descends upon the earth, Allah commands Jibra'il (a.s.) to descend to the earth with the angels. They have a banner, and they place it on the back of the Kaaba. That banner has six hundred wings, and among them are two wings that never open except on the night of Qadr. When they open, they encompass the entire world. Allah sends the angels to be appointed over this Muslim Ummah, and these angels come to the worshippers when someone is in prayer, or in Ruku, or in Sujud, or in Zikr, or in Tasbih. They come when someone is in prayer, or in Ruku, or in Sujud, or in Zikr, or in Tasbih. The angels greet them all and pray along with them. And when they supplicate in the court of the Almighty, those same angels say 'Ameen'. Now think, respected viewers, if the angels say 'Ameen' to someone's prayer, will that prayer not reach the court of the Lord of Honor? It will certainly reach, and the Lord of Honor will surely answer their prayer. These angels say 'Ameen', and this sequence continues until dawn, that is, until sunrise. When dawn breaks, Jibra'il (a.s.) gives the call, saying, 'O angels, return, return.' At that time, the angels ask Jibra'il (a.s.), 'What reward has Allah given to these worshipping servants of His? These people have worshipped all night; we kept watching them praying, doing Ruku, doing Sujud, doing Qiyam, doing Zikr, reciting Tasbih, doing everything. Finally, what reward did Allah give to His servants for this whole night of worship?' Then Jibra'il (a.s.) says, 'Allah has cast a look of mercy and forgiveness upon His servants.' What will be the status of the servant upon whom Allah casts a look of mercy and forgiveness? What will be the status of the servant upon whom Allah casts a look of mercy and forgiveness, and whose sins He has forgiven? Who are those who have worshipped on the night of Qadr and Allah has forgiven their sins, cast a look of mercy upon them, and granted them forgiveness? Except for four types of people. The Imam (a.s.) said these four are: Number 1, the one who always drinks alcohol. Number 2, the one who disobeys their parents. No matter how much someone who disobeys their parents worships, they will get no benefit. No matter how many good deeds they do, they will get no benefit. No matter how much they pray at night, there is no benefit because disobedience to parents is a major sin. After that, the third one is the one who breaks ties, who ends relationships, who severs ties. And after that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was asked by the people, 'Who is the 'Shahin'?' He said, 'The one who tries to break people's relationships.' Allahu Akbar, respected viewers, now just ponder that such great virtues will be attained—meaning our sins will be forgiven, God's mercy and forgiveness will be upon us, and our sins will be wiped away—that is, if we... And our sins will be forgiven, that is, if we worship on the night of Qadr. But also remember, before worship, let us ponder: we don't drink alcohol, and surely no one drinks alcohol, but at least we can ponder whether we are disobedient to our parents. Before worshipping on that night, let us start with our parents. Ask them, 'Are you angry with us?' If they are angry, ask them to forgive us so that when we worship on that night, we may benefit from it, Insha'Allah. After that, the 'Fatih' (severer of ties) and 'Shahin' (slanderer/divider)—these are the things. In tomorrow's discussion, I will elaborate a bit more on the subject of disobedience to parents. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, respected viewers, stay away from these things.
