title: EP10 | Imam Ki Khususiyaat | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the essential characteristics required for an Imam, emphasizing the necessity of infallibility, supreme knowledge, bravery, and generosity. It examines how the absence of these divine qualities in historical leaders led to the adoption of fallible methods like Qiyas and Ra'y to compensate for their lack of understanding. The session further highlights the historical oppression of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the long-term consequences of rejecting divinely appointed leadership in favor of political authority.
content:
PSR presents. Ash-hadu anna Aliyan wali-ullah. This is being presented, witness the truth. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal-'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-hujjati-bnil-hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila, Allahummaj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi, wa khuddamihi wa atba'ihi, wa la taj'alna min a'da'ihi bihaqqi Muhammadin wa alihi-t-tahirin. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal-'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. The discussion was about what characteristics an Imam should possess, what his traits should be. That is, who is the person we can say is truly eligible for Imamate? A hadith of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) narrated in Bihar al-Anwar, volume 25, was the basis of this discussion, and I presented three characteristics to you. First, he must be infallible (Ma'sum). Second, he must be the most learned of people (A'lam al-nas), meaning there should be no one in the entire nation more learned than him, and his knowledge must be connected to divine knowledge (Ilm al-Ghayb). And third, he must be the bravest of people (Ashja' al-nas), so that people may seek refuge in him. People should come to him. The fourth quality, the fourth trait, is that he must be the most generous of people (Askh al-nas). He must be generous, open-handed, and benevolent. This is a very important trait. He cannot be a miser. Why? 'Wa in bakhila ahlul-ardi kulluhum'—if all the people of the world were to become misers, the Imam can never be a miser. 'Li-annahu in istawla-sh-shuhhu 'alayhi, shahha bima fi yadayhi min amwalil-muslimin.' If the Imam becomes a miser, then he will also act with stinginess regarding the public treasury (Bayt al-Mal) in his hands. He will try to save it instead of spending it on the people. He will not spend on things meant for the welfare, success, and well-being of the people. He will wonder why he should spend money. He will accumulate money, gather money, just like worldly people gather money; he would start doing the same. That is why it is necessary for the Imam to be generous. And what kind of generosity? He should be so generous that Surah al-Insan (Surah ad-Dahr) is revealed in his honor. That is what we call an Imam. And then, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) further clarifies these four qualities. He says that 'Ismah' (infallibility), meaning being infallible 'min jami'i-dh-dhunub' (from all sins), is necessary. Why? The Imam explains this: 'Wa bidhalika yatamayyazu 'anil-ma'mumin.' Because through this, he can be distinguished from his followers, 'alladhina hum ghayru ma'sumin' (who are not infallible), who keep committing sins morning and evening. They keep disobeying Allah morning and evening. 'Li-annahu law lam yakun ma'suman lam yu'man 'alayhi.' Because if the Imam is not infallible, 'lam yu'man 'alayhi'—there will be no trust in him, people cannot have faith. They cannot feel secure; they wouldn't know if what he is saying is right or wrong. Is he not making a slip? Is he not making a mistake? There will be no trust. 'An yadkhula fima yadkhulu-n-nasu fihi.' Meaning, he will not be safe—safe from what? That the Imam might also perform the same actions, enter into the same things that the common people are entering into. What do the common people do? 'Min mubiqati-dh-dhunubil-muhlikat.' That is, sins that ruin a person, destroy them. Meaning their afterlife is ruined, their worldly life is ruined. Then it is possible that the Imam might do the same thing. The Caliph might do the same thing. The one who is Allah's successor in the universe might do the same thing if he is not infallible. That is why his infallibility is necessary. Otherwise, if he followed his desires, it is possible that one decision would be enough for his destruction. For example, if he does not know, and based on his own desire or opinion, he makes a wrong decision. He has an innocent person killed. For instance, he sent a group saying, 'Go and bring Zakat from there.' Now, he sent the group, but did not check how much knowledge or virtue this group possesses, how much Islamic information they have, or whether they can control their desires or not. And they went there, and when those people were not giving Zakat, they demanded it. So when those people refused, saying, 'We do not recognize you,' what did he do? He killed them. The person he killed was named Malik ibn Nuwayra. He killed Malik ibn Nuwayra, and that very day, without waiting for the waiting period (Iddah), he married his wife. That very day. When people came here and reported that he had done this, many were angry. Even those around the Caliph at that time were angry. But he said, 'No, no, it's fine, it's okay, this happens.' Now, a man committing a sin like this—this is a cause for a person's destruction. How is it a cause for destruction? Look, there is a verse in the Quran: Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his reward is Hell. He has to go to Hell. That's it. The matter is closed. He killed intentionally. Was there any justification for the killing? No. And the second sin he committed after the killing was even greater than the first. And he did it. Now, when it was reported here, no action was taken against him. This means that the one who was in power at that time, who had sent him, is also pleased with this act. And when one is pleased with the act, it means he is a partner in that action. Because the famous and well-known tradition says: 'Ar-radi bi-fi'li qawmin ka-d-dakhili fihim.' Whoever is pleased with the act of a group is like one who has performed the act himself. Whoever is satisfied—if someone is satisfied with a killing, then according to Islamic law, he is also a partner in that killing. He is a partner in crime. That is why such destructive sins, 'wa-lladhdhat' (and desires)—like marrying immediately at that time—this was the result of desire. 'Wa law dakhala fi hadhihil-ashya'i'—and if the Imam himself does this, if the Caliph himself does this, then what will happen? 'La-htaja ila man yuqimu 'alayhil-hudud.' Then it is necessary that there should be someone who establishes the prescribed punishments (Hudud) upon this Imam and Caliph. Meaning, he should punish him. He should punish him. That is why, look, Islamic stories are very strange. Brother, you read them, you will find them very interesting. How these Caliphs were, they had become, well, they had all become [Caliphs]. So they received news that a certain person drinks alcohol in his house. So at night, obviously he used to drink at night, he would close the door and drink his alcohol. So at night, this Caliph climbed over the wall and went inside. And he caught him red-handed. And he said, 'I have caught you red-handed.' He said, 'Caliph, I have committed one sin, drinking alcohol. That is true, but you have committed a greater sin by climbing over the wall to come here. You have disobeyed the Quran. The Quran has forbidden this. This is a greater sin than that.' And that drunkard recited the verses of the Quran, which the Caliph had not even paid attention to. It is a very interesting thing, see. So he was like, 'Oh, I am sorry, sorry, sorry.' This Caliph... this is the state of the Muslims after the Prophet, just understand this. These are two small stories I have presented, one about not giving Zakat and the other this one. And there are numerous such examples, several examples. These are just two famous and well-known ones so that no one says, 'We didn't know about the Caliph.' No, it's very clear. Right? 'Man yuqimu 'alal-hudud.' Now, who should establish the Hudud on that Caliph? There should be someone to establish the Hudud, someone to punish him. 'Fa-yakunu hina'idhin imaman ma'muman.' So what will be the result? Now he is not an Imam, now he has become a follower (Ma'mum). Because there should be someone to establish the Hudud upon him. There should be someone to punish him, so the one who punishes him would become the Imam. 'Wa la yajuzu an yakuna imaman bi-hadhihi-s-sifah.' And it is not permissible for an Imam to possess such a quality. The Master of the Universe (a.s.) says this does not befit an Imam. And then he further clarifies why he should be the most learned. 'Wa amma wujubu kawnihi a'laman-nas.' And why is his being 'A'lam al-nas' (the most learned of people) mandatory? For if he were not the most learned, he would not be safe from overturning the laws and the boundaries. And this is why you find examples—history is full of them. A woman was brought—you can see it in history—she was insane, mentally unstable, and she was accused of adultery (zina). The Caliph immediately issued a fatwa that she should be stoned to death. He did not know the law; he was not familiar with Islamic law. Someone came to the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) and told him about this. The Master of the Universe immediately said, 'This is a wrong law, this is a wrong fatwa you have issued. This is an insane woman; this fatwa of stoning cannot be applied to her. She is not mukallaf (legally responsible). When she is not mukallaf, she has no religious responsibility. So, when there is no religious responsibility, how can she be punished?' Then the gentleman said, 'Oh, I was not aware, it did not cross my mind.' Oh, is it clear to you? So the Master (a.s.) says that it is possible that all these confused, 'wa takhtalifu alayhi al-qadaya wal-mushkilat'—and it is possible that if difficult judgments come before him, he might not understand them, 'fala yujibu anha'—he might not be able to answer them. He doesn't even know what it is. If a slightly confusing question comes, he doesn't know. 'Aw yujibu anha thumma yujibu bikhilafiha'—or he gives an answer and then gives the opposite answer. Which is not the actual truth, as the example just presented to you. Therefore, he must be the most learned of people (A'lam al-Nas). He must have knowledge of all things. The Master says, and then he says why he must be the bravest of people (Ashja' al-Nas)? 'Fabima qaddamnahu'—as we have mentioned before, 'li-annahu la yasihhu an yanhazima fayabu'a bighadabin min Allahi ta'ala'—it is not appropriate for him to be defeated and flee from the battlefield. Because when he flees from the battlefield, what will happen? The Master says the wrath of Allah will descend upon him. 'Wa hadhihi la yasihhu an takuna sifata al-imam'—and it is not appropriate for this to be a quality of an Imam. So, in this way, the Master of the Universe explicitly stated the qualities that an Imam must possess. After that, the Master further clarified, continuing this hadith—Imam Sadiq (a.s.)—it is a very long hadith. Then Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says regarding those who considered Qiyas (analogy) and Ra'y (personal opinion) as lawful—Qiyas and Ra'y meant conjecturing things on their own and making decisions based on their own opinions. What was the foundation of their entire religion? It was on Qiyas and Ra'y. So the Imam says, why did this happen? Because 'dhalika annahum lamma 'ajazu 'an iqamati al-ahkami 'ala ma anzala Allahu fi kitabihi wa 'adalu 'an akhdhiha min ahliha'—when they became incapable of stating the laws as Allah had revealed them in His Book, they could not understand them, and they turned away from taking them from those who were their rightful people. Those who were the true successors of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they did not go to them. Those whose obedience Allah had made obligatory, they did not go to them. Those from whom no mistake occurred, no slip occurred, no error occurred, who did not forget—they did not go to them. And they were well aware of how Allah revealed things and for whom He revealed them. So naturally, they became confused. When they became confused, but at the same time, they could not say to the Imam, 'Brother, look, I do not understand'—this is a sentence from the hadith. You translate it quickly because I do not understand. Because if the Imam says, if they do that, then their leadership will be lost. Their government will be lost. So what should they do? They had to do it. They had to make wrong decisions. They had to say all sorts of things. Now, I will tell you an incident for your service, which is recorded in a book. The incident is such that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who was a Umayyad Caliph, a king—Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. This was the king who stopped the cursing that was sent upon the Master of the Universe from the pulpits, from the year 40 Hijri—in fact, even before 40 Hijri, cursing was sent—until 110 Hijri. That is, for more than 83 years, cursing was sent upon the Master of the Universe from various pulpits. Who is this Master of the Universe? He is the successor of the Messenger of Allah, the son-in-law of the Messenger of Allah, the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, in whose honor the verse of Mubahila was revealed, in whose honor the verse of Tatheer was revealed. Insha'Allah, all these things that we will present to you, how he was the successor and deserving of the Caliphate. But anyway, even if they were nothing, at least, as the Muslims say, he was one of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. So, cursing was being sent upon him, and the entire Islamic world was silent. Muslims were silent. Cursing was sent upon the Master of the Universe during Friday prayers. Muslims were silent. No one said anything. In the entire Islamic world, cursing was sent upon Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.). Today you tell us, 'Do not do Tabarra, do not do this, do not do that.' Allama Amini says, 'Ali is our honor, Ali is our pride. How can we remain silent?' So, anyway, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz stopped this series of cursing which had been going on for more than 83 years. Okay? So, this incident of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz is recorded: 'I used to see that my father says, whenever my father used to send curses upon Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), he would have a strange state. His body would start trembling, he would shake.' He would start trembling. He would tremble. He would have a strange state. So one day I asked him, 'Father, when you send curses upon Ali ibn Abi Talib and speak ill of him and insult him, why does this state of yours happen?' So he replied—the answer was—'I have read so many virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib, so many, that if I were to start stating those virtues, if I were to tell people about these virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib, then not even two people would follow us. Not even two people would follow us. Therefore, whenever I curse, I insult...' I do the work, I use abusive language, then all those virtues that the Prophet stated in honor of Ali come to my mind. Allahu Akbar. Look at the oppression of Ali. This incident is properly present in the book, and its reference is present on your screen, you can see it. This is a scholar of the fourth century. He is narrating this incident. So this is the thing, that for the sake of government, they are ready to do anything. Whether you make a wrong decision or a right decision, it doesn't matter, it has to be done somehow. And after that, 'wa rakiba tariqata aslafihi'—they did the same thing that the proponents of Ra'y did. They did the same thing that their forefathers did. They saw that, 'Brother, they also make wrong decisions, we will also do it, it doesn't matter.' Who were their forefathers? The Master says, 'Man idda'a manzilata awliya'i Allah'—that their forefathers were the ones who claimed the status of the Awliya of Allah. So, 'lazimahum al-mu'jiz wa faddalu anna al-ra'ya wa al-qiyasa wajib'—now when they had no other choice, they claimed that Qiyas and Ra'y are obligatory. Qiyas, meaning conjecture, meaning doing guess work. Doing guess work in religion. And Ra'y, meaning personal opinion, presenting one's own opinion. It is obligatory. This became the religion. When people abandon the true Imam, then they follow this kind of religion. 'Mansus min Allah'—meaning that, 'Mansus min Allah'—what does it mean? That Imam who was appointed by Allah. When they abandon that Imam, then the result will be this. And if you want to see more clarification, then look at Nahj al-Balagha, read Sermon 131. Read it yourself, teach it to your children, and tell them what the Master of the Universe said. You listen carefully to the beginning of that sermon, 'Ayyuha al-nufusu al-mukhtalifatu wa al-qulubu al-mutashattitatu'—O you whose souls are different and whose hearts are scattered. So, Insha'Allah, you study this sermon yourself and see what the Master says. title: Kaamiyaabi Ke Raaz | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the three divine keys to success as outlined by Hazrat Ali (a.s.). By practicing moderation in speech, food, and sleep, a believer can maintain the activity and discipline required for worldly and spiritual progress. The lecture emphasizes that avoiding laziness and comfort-seeking is essential for personal growth and fulfilling one's potential.
content:
Hazrat Amir (a.s.) says, 'Idha aradallahu subhanahu salah 'abdihi' (When Allah, the Glorified, desires the righteousness of His servant), He wants goodness for them. That is, Allah wants this servant to progress, to be successful in this world and the hereafter. His success lies in this. When Allah wants a servant's success, what does He do? He puts three things into their heart. That is, three things descend into their heart. Allah inspires them. That is, the matter becomes clear to them. Now there is no need for anyone to explain, no need to accept it from others. They themselves understand that these three things are very good. What is the first thing? 'Qillatul kalam' (Speaking less), not talking too much. Just speaking as much as is necessary and not interfering in matters that do not concern us. 'Qillatul kalam' means speaking less, being brief, not talking excessively. The second thing is 'Qillatul ta'am' (Eating less). Allah inspires them to eat less. Just eat enough to be able to work. Because when a person's stomach is completely full, they become lazy. Then they feel sleepy, and then they become comfort-seeking. But one who eats less, just enough to stay active... Whether they eat three or four times a day, it doesn't matter, but they should eat a little. Just enough to remain 'fa'al' (active). 'He should be active.' Allah puts this thought into their heart that look, if you eat until you are completely full, then you cannot work. And the third thing is 'Qillatul manam' (Sleeping less). Sleep less. Because if a person is always craving to sleep more and more, and whenever you see them, they are overcome by sleep, then they can neither be successful in this world nor will they find success in the hereafter. They will be unsuccessful in the world, and if they sleep too much, they will be unsuccessful in the hereafter. Therefore, it is found in the Hadith that 'Innallaha yubghidhu kathratan nawmi wa kathratal faraghi' (Allah hates those who are very free and those who sleep too much). 'Kathratan nawmi' means those who sleep a lot. Whenever you see them, they are looking for sleep, looking for an opportunity to sleep. 'This is what to sleep.' Just rest. They do not want to come out of their comfort zone and are always free. They do not remain active, they do not remain 'fa'al'. A person should always look for activity for themselves, keep doing something so that they go one notch above their present level. That is, their two days should not be equal. So, this is a very important thing in a person's life.

content:
Ya Muhammad. On the night of the blessed birth of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), a voice came from the House of Kaaba: 'O progeny of Quraish! Surely a bearer of glad tidings has come to you, and a warner has come to you. He possesses great honor and great profit. He is the last of the Prophets (a.s.), and indeed we have found in the heavenly books that after them, the best of people will be their progeny. People will always remain safe from divine punishment as long as even one individual from their descendants remains in the world.'

title: Aaghaaz-e-Safar-e-Karbala | Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki J. Umme Salama (s.a.) Se Guftugu
excerpt: This lecture recounts the poignant conversation between Imam Hussain (a.s.) and Janabe Umm Salama (r.a.) as the Imam prepares to depart Medina for Iraq. Imam Hussain (a.s.) confirms his divine knowledge regarding his impending martyrdom in Karbala, including the specific location and the fate of his companions. Through a miraculous demonstration, he reveals the site of his future grave and tents to Umm Salama, who accepts the divine decree with great sorrow.
content:
When Imam Hussain (a.s.) intended to leave Medina, Umm al-Mu'minin Janabe Umm Salama (r.a.) came to him and said, 'O my son! Do not make me sorrowful by going towards Iraq, for I have heard your grandfather say that my son Hussain will be killed in the land of Iraq at a place called Karbala.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) replied, 'Grandmother, Ana wallahu a'lamu dhalik (I and Allah know that). By God, I know this well and it is certain that I will be killed and this will surely happen to me, and by God, I even have knowledge of the day when I will be killed. I also know who will kill me and I have knowledge of the place where I will be buried. I also know which of my Ahlulbayt, close friends, and Shias will be martyred. And O grandmother, if you wish, I can show you my grave right now.' Then the Imam (a.s.) pointed towards Karbala, and the earth sank in such a way that the Imam (a.s.) showed her his place of martyrdom, the mark of his grave, his army, and his tents. Hearing this, Bibi Umm Salama wept bitterly and entrusted this matter to Allah.

title: Anjuman-e-Gham Khwaraan -e-Karbala [Malwani]
excerpt: This brief lecture segment reflects on the profound grief and suffering experienced by Fatima Zahra, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, following his passing. It highlights the immense oppression she endured and the sorrow felt by the Prophet's grave itself. The narrative emphasizes the deep emotional and spiritual connection between the Prophet and his daughter during a time of great trial.
content:

title: Majlis 8 | Manzilat-e-Imam (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual status of the Imams (a.s.) and the necessity of recognizing them for true guidance. He emphasizes the significance of Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira, the concept of Wilayah, and the transformative power of Istighfar and mindfulness. The discourse culminates in a poignant reflection on the sacrifice of Ali Akbar (a.s.) at Karbala, highlighting his resemblance to the Prophet and the immense grief of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
Zainab received the corpses of her brothers. O Lord, may no poor person's head be broken. May the veils of sisters not be at odds with fate. O Lord, may the protector of every character be safe. All my young and old ones were killed. Eighteen lions slept in the lap of death. I have endured the grief of the martyrs of the day. I will never forget the grief of the two brothers for the rest of my life. One brother was lost in the siege of the army of Sham. One brother was lost in the siege of the army of Sham. And the other slept on the bank of the Euphrates. May no one be as troubled as I am. O Lord, may no brother be separated from any sister. Zainab wept and said over the corpse of Shabbir. O caravan of the era of captivity, wait a while. A lion is sleeping on the bank of the river Alqama. That young, brave, and valiant brother is mine. I will go to the river from Hussain's corpse. I will show Abbas's bound arms. When the sister of Hussain went towards Alqama. It is written that the darling of the door kept her head bowed. The brave one sensed the footsteps from afar. Crying out, he writhed in the grief of Ali. People, destroy my settlement. Pick me up and bury me in the grave of the stranger. O helplessness, call me into your lap. O honor, hide me somewhere in your lap. O earth, split open and hold me in your lap. O sky, take me into your lap. Why would I, unveiled, look at the Euphrates? The princesses are coming to the Euphrates with uncovered heads. When Zainab saw Alqama from afar. The tone of Ali's lion that the aggrieved one heard. She looked here and there many times with great longing. Abbas, the mirror of the mirror, cried out and gave a call. Tears of blood were writhing before her eyelashes. Two severed arms were writhing on the riverbank. The moment the daughter of Ali reached the riverbank. She called out to Abbas and fell upon the corpse. A stream of tears flowed from her eyes. Seeing this, the brave one felt great pain. Tears in his eyes, but lips sealed. Zainab's hands were tied behind her neck. When the grief-stricken sister rose after reciting Nad-e-Ali. She spoke, showing the rope soaked in blood. Abbas, my brother, my lion who breaks the ranks. The honor of the Panjetan has been looted and taken captive. The veil has been lost in the siege of the army of Sham. The sister of eighteen brothers has been imprisoned. You are the peace of Zahra's heart, my life. You are the desire of father Ali's heart. And you are the strength of the arms of the King of Martyrs. You are the guardian of the sisters' veils. When your arms were severed, you fell into the sleep of death. Oh Abbas, whose evil eye has struck you? When Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.) expresses her state to Moula Abbas (a.s.), the Moula replies: 'What should I say of my state, O Princess of the Alam (Standard)? The standard, which was dearer than life, has gone cold. Ever since my arms were severed at the Euphrates, I am suffering from a most intense grief.' What should I say? I am in great pain. A lady is standing bareheaded over my corpse. She is sorrowful, mourning, and helpless. She is calling out 'Ya Bunayya' (O my son) while weeping. Zainab (s.a.) cried out in agony, 'She is deeply grieved. O Abbas, know that she is my mother Fatima (s.a.).' Even in the grave, she does not sleep in peace. Fatima (s.a.) will weep, O Abbas, Fatima (s.a.) will weep for you until the Day of Judgment. Zainab's (s.a.) words were cut short by the tyrant's command. The army of Yazid moved away from the river to depart. The agony was contained within silent tears. Arif, saying this, Zainab (s.a.) clung to her brother: 'Let me at least mourn over the corpse of my devoted one, let me weep to my heart's content over the corpse of my brother.' O Lord, may no sister be separated from her brother. Salawat, Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. [Arabic Quranic and Hadith recitations...] The shadow of the Karim (generous one) that has been chosen for this ten-day Majlis, in that shadow, the Almighty God says: 'Fastabiqul khairat' (Hasten towards good deeds). I had submitted to you that 'Khair' (good) is the plural of 'Khairat', and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the essence of all goodness. 'Nahnu aslul kulli khair wa a'dauna aslul kulli shar' (We are the source of all goodness, and our enemies are the source of all evil). We are the fountainhead of every good, the root of every good, and our enemies are the root of every evil. I have been continuously submitting to you that the recognition (Ma'rifat) of this goodness is very necessary. That is, the recognition of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is essential. You must have heard the Hadith many times: 'Man mata wa lam ya'rif imama zamanihi mata maytatal jahiliyya' (Whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time dies the death of ignorance). And until there is recognition of the Ahlulbayt, success (Sa'adat) is impossible for a human being. Success, meaning entering Paradise, is impossible for him. This is the saying of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the Prophet said that 'whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time dies the death of ignorance.' So when someone asked Imam Sadiq (a.s.) what 'Jahiliyya' means, people usually translate it as ignorance. That is an incorrect translation. It is not the right translation. It is completely wrong. There is a difference between Jahiliyya and ignorance (Jahalat), and the Imam explained it. The Imam said that Jahiliyya means Kufr (disbelief), misguidance, and hypocrisy—three things. The Imam said Kufr, meaning 'maytata kufrin wa zalalin wa nifaqin.' That is, whoever dies without recognizing his Imam, dies the death of Kufr; he will not die upon Islam, he will die upon misguidance and the death of a hypocrite. Meaning, outwardly he might be a Muslim, outwardly he might recite the Kalima, but actually, he will not die as a Momin (believer), but rather as a hypocrite. So this is a very important matter. That is why the recognition of the Ahlulbayt is so necessary, and no matter how much we discuss it, it is not enough. See, Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.)—Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum—has done two great favors upon us. One great favor is by stating the Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira, and the second great favor is the Ziyarat-e-Ghadiriya, the Ziyarat of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) on the day of Ghadir, which is narrated from Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.). It is obligatory and necessary for all of us to recite these two Ziyarats. As far as Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira is concerned, this is the command of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) himself. When the Imam met that Baghdadi, he commanded him three things. One was Salat al-Layl (Night Prayer); he commanded him to be steadfast in the Night Prayer. One is the Night Prayer, two is Ziyarat-e-Ashura, and three is Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira. The Imam mentioned three things. The Night Prayer is, in any case, the best thing in terms of worship. That is to say, it is the crown of worship. The Night Prayer is the crown of worship, and if a person starts his morning with the Night Prayer and then performs the Morning Prayer, his day will go excellently. Divine assistance will come. 'Al-ilmu salatul layl.' He will have help and support from Allah. Ziyarat-e-Ashura is the best thing regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.), and the third, Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira, is the best thing for the recognition of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). It is the best Ziyarat, in which you actually understand the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) from their own words, their status, and their position. The Hadith I am about to present, because you know who the first Muhaddith (scholar of Hadith) was who recorded the Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira? Sheikh Saduq. Sheikh Saduq, may Allah have mercy on him. Sheikh, you know, Saduq was not his name; Saduq was his title. Saduq means one who speaks the truth very much. One who speaks the truth very much is called Saduq; it is a superlative in Arabic. Is it clear to you? His name was Muhammad ibn... Ali ibn Hussain ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may Allah have mercy on him. He himself was also Muhammad, a very great Sheikh Saduq, a very great Muhaddith. His title is Ra'is al-Muhaddithin (Chief of the Muhaddithin). And his father was also a very great Muhaddith, Ali ibn Hussain ibn Musa ibn Babawayh. So he recorded this Hadith in 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih'. This Ziyarat, Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira. 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih' is his book. You know, I am telling the children, what does 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih' mean? When you say 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', what does it mean? It means this book is sufficient for the one who does not have a Faqih (jurist) present. This book is sufficient for the one who does not have a Faqih present. So if he is all alone, for example, if a man is alone on an island and there is no one to guide him, he is somewhere alone and he only has 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih' with him, then it is sufficient for him. Sheikh Saduq wrote in his book and gave it that title. Is it clear? That for the one who does not have a Faqih present, this book is sufficient for him. Did you notice? And in the preface of this book, he writes that in this book, I have only recorded those Hadiths that I had 100% faith were authentic. There is no Hadith in this that I have even the slightest doubt about. This is his level of confidence. So Sheikh Saduq, he recorded this Hadith in his books 'Kamal al-Din' and 'Amali', which have sentences very similar to the sentences of this Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira. So I am presenting this narration to you; this narration is narrated from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). Recite Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum. We will read the sentences slowly, and you keep understanding the status of the Ahlulbayt, keep understanding their position. Because if we understand these things, then understand that they cannot be compared to anyone. That is, no human being, other than the Masumin (infallibles), can equal them. That is, we cannot even imagine it. And that is why I will read one sentence ahead—let me submit a sentence to you, then I will start reading the Hadith. That is why in our traditions, there is the last verse of Surah Al-Kahf. The last verse of Surah Al-Kahf: 'Wa man kana yarju liqa'a rabbihi' (So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord), 'falyamal 'amalan saliha' (let him do righteous work), 'wa la yushrik bi 'ibadati rabbihi ahada' (and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord). In the exegesis of this verse, it is present that 'falyamal 'amalan saliha'—he should do righteous work—means he should accept the Wilayah of Ali. Allahu Akbar, Subhan Allah. He should accept the Wilayah of Ali. 'Wa la yushrik bi 'ibadati rabbihi ahada'—and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord—means do not associate anyone else in the Wilayah of Ali. Wah-wah, Subhan Allah. In the Wilayah of Ali, there are only and only the 11 Masumeen after Ali (a.s.), the 11 Imams. Meaning a total of 14 Masumeen (a.s.). Apart from them, no one else can even be imagined. Janab-e-Umm Salama has a very high status. A very high status indeed. Recently, a very voluminous book has also been written regarding her. And Alhamdulillah, it has been translated as well, thanks to Allah, and editing is currently underway. InshaAllah, if you look, it will be published in English very soon. Ummul Momineen Umm Salama, Salamullah Alayha. But even she, when she sought permission from the Prophet to enter the Kisa (cloak), as in the Hadith-e-Kisa, the Prophet did not give her permission. He said, 'Anti 'ala khair' (You are upon goodness), but you are not worthy of this. Wah-wah, wah-wah. You are good, certainly you are very good, there is no issue with that. But you are not worthy of this Kisa. Meaning you are not at that level. You are not at that status that you should be here, not here. See, let me submit to your service, she is Ummul Momineen. And truly a defender of Ali (a.s.), one who defended the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and defended the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) with bravery. After the martyrdom of Rasulullah, Janab-e-Umm Salama defended it a lot. Truly, the reality is that she has a great position, a great status. I mean, for her status, it is enough that Imam Hussain (a.s.) used to call her 'Mother'. Now, did you notice? I mean, what could be a greater status than this? So, it is very important that we understand the position of the Ahlulbayt. Now look at this tradition, let me present it to your service; it is present in Kamaluddin as well, and in Amali, also by Sheikh Saduq, from which it is narrated that the fourth Imam, Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) says: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. He says, 'Nahnu Aimmatul Muslimeen' (We are the Imams of the Muslims). There is no other Imam. Apart from the 12, there is no 13th Imam. Wah-wah. There are only 12 Imams. Right? There is no 13th Imam. The Imam says, 'Nahnu Aimmatul Muslimeen.' We are the Imams of the Muslims, that's it. Apart from them, there is no one. Therefore, think very carefully before using words, what are we saying? What are we saying and what will be its effects? Because we will have to answer. Do not think that you will say anything and get away with it. Who will ask? Once you go into the grave, it will be asked there too, 'Man Imamuk?' (Who is your Imam?). Wah-wah, wah-wah. So there, just as it was asked to Janab-e-Fatima bint-e-Asad when she was in the grave, who is your Imam? The Prophet-e-Akram (s.a.w.a.) said: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. Say, 'Ibnuki, Ibnuki' (Your son, your son). So there are only 12 Imams, apart from them there is no Imam. It will be asked in the grave, and if you go there and take a third or fourth name, then understand that the work will start from there and will continue until the Day of Judgment. Then what will happen on the Day of Judgment, only Allah knows best. After that, he says, 'Wa Hujjatullah 'alal 'alameen' (And we are Allah's proof over all the worlds). 'Wa Sadatul Momineen' (And we are the masters of the believers). We are the only masters of the believers. 'Wa Qadatul Ghurril Muhajjaleen' (And we are the leaders of the Ghurril Muhajjaleen). We are the leaders. Qadat is the plural of Qa'id. Al-Ghurr-ul-Muhajjaleen. Who are the Ghurr? Ghurr is called the horse that has a white mark on its forehead, or sorry, a red, white sign. The whole horse is black, but on the forehead... so that is the believer who has a sign, one of prostration, that is its interpretation. The second is that one who is a Sayyid by birth, and Muhajjil is called one who is, meaning from both parents, has Sayyid lineage, meaning Najeeb-ut-Tarafain. His birth is from both sides. 'Wa Mawali al-Momineen' (And we are the Mawlas of all the believers). 'Nahnu Amanu Ahlil Ard' (We are the cause of safety for the people of the earth). Means cause of safety. Meaning as long as we are here, the people of the earth will not perish, the earth will remain. 'Kama annannujuma amanul-li-ahlis-sama' (Just as the stars are the cause of safety for the people of the heavens). 'Nahnu-lladhina bima bina yumsikullahu-ssama-a an taqa'a 'alal ardi illa bi-idhnihi' (We are the ones through whom Allah does not let the heavens fall on the earth except by His permission). Meaning He does not destroy it, does not end it. 'Wa bina yumsikul-arda an tamida bi-ahliha' (And through us, Allah does not bring an earthquake to the earth so that the earth would shake and perish). Why? Because Ali ibn Abi Talib is Abu Turab. Wah-wah. He is Abu Turab. That is why the Quran you read, 'Idha zulzilatil ardu zilzalaha, wa akhrajatil ardu athqalaha, wa qalal insanu ma laha.' Ala! 'Yawma'idhin tuhaddithu akhbaraha bi-anna rabbaka awha laha' (That day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it). On that day, Amirul Momineen (a.s.) will address it. This... meaning who is meant by 'the human' in this Surah? Ali ibn Abi Talib. Mawla, what will he say? Mawla, what is it doing? Ali (a.s.) will just touch the earth and the earthquake will stop. It is completely under the control of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). So the Imam says, 'Wa bina yunazzilul ghayth' (Through us, Allah sends down rain), through us Allah sends down mercy, through us Allah sends down blessings, and if we were not here, the earth would be annihilated with its people. If for even one moment there were no Imam of the time. 'Lawlal hujjatu lasakhatil ardu bi-ahliha' (If it were not for the Hujjah, the earth would have swallowed its people). Now if someone has such an Imam, then he can say that yes, this is our Imam. These are our Imams. Is it clear? Did you notice? So when will Imamate be proven? When all these characteristics are found. If these characteristics are not found, then how can he be an Imam? And then after that, the Imam says that 'Wa lam takhlil ardu mundhu khalaqallahu al-hujjata lillahi fiha zahirin mashhur' (The earth can never be empty of the Hujjah of Allah, whether this Hujjah is manifest or hidden). And until the Day of Judgment, until the Day of Judgment, one of these 12 Imams will always be alive. 'Wa lawla dhalika' (And if this Imam were not there, meaning the Masoom Imam), 'lam yu'badillahu' (Allah could not be worshipped). The worship of Allah is impossible. When the Imam said this, the narrator asked, 'But Mawla, if the Imam goes into occultation, then what is the benefit of such an Imam? Who goes into occultation?' So the Imam said, 'People will benefit from his occultation just as they benefit from the sun when it hides behind the clouds.' Recite one Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. So this is briefly what I submitted to your service, that it is very important that we recognize our Imams. Look at this tradition, all these sentences you read, all these sentences need a lot of explanation, a lot of detailed discussion, but anyway, now is not the time for it, so we will stop it here and then come to that Hadith which we are talking about. That the Prophet said: 'Thalathatun' (Three individuals are those), 'ma'sumuna min Iblisa wa junudihi' (who are protected from Iblis and his army). Three people are those who will always remain protected from Iblis and his army. Meaning Iblis will have no effect on them. Iblis and his devils, no matter how much they whisper, they cannot do anything. Who are these three people? How are they protected from the whispers of Iblis? The Imam said, what is the first thing? 'Adh-dhakiruna lillah' (Those who remember Allah). It is a command of the Quran: 'Wadhkurullaha dhikran kathiran wa sabbihu-hu bukratan wa asila' (And remember Allah much and glorify Him morning and evening). 'Wadhkurullaha dhikran kathiran wa sabbihu-hu bukratan wa asila' (And remember Allah much and glorify Him morning and evening). The Imam said in the context of this verse, will you listen to the Hadith? What a powerful Hadith! The Imam says that the most difficult duty that Allah has placed on the servants is the remembrance of Allah. The most difficult duty, meaning Dhikr means to remember. Remembering Allah is the most... the Imam says, 'Min ashaddil fara'id' (From the most difficult obligations), the most severe obligation, and what is that? Remembering Allah. Then the Imam says, 'La a'ni Subhanallahi walhamdu lillahi wala ilaha illallahu wallahu akbar' (I do not mean that you take a rosary and recite Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar, this is not it). Wa in kana min dhalika (Although that is also the remembrance of Allah). There is no denial of that, that is also Dhikr, that is also the remembrance of Allah, the memory of Allah. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, that is also it. No one is denying it, the Imam says it is not that it is not. But my intention is, I want to say that whenever any action comes before you, whenever anything comes before you, then see if Allah has allowed this thing or not allowed it. If Allah has allowed it, then do it, and if Allah has not allowed it, then abstain from it. This is the most difficult task. The Imam says the most difficult. To think about every action, whether this thing is allowed by Allah or not. Therefore, if something is coming in front of you to eat, someone has brought something to eat, then see if this food is allowed or not. Because a very great, elderly scholar, Mirza Mahdi Isfahani, Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh, he wrote a very powerful sentence in his book. He said that the food we eat becomes the cause of the transformation of our 'Teenat' (nature/essence). That Teenat, even if the Teenat is 'Illiyeen', is a good Teenat, but for example, if a person eats food, is eating forbidden food, impure food, it is impure, it is forbidden, what are they doing? He says this can become the cause of the transformation of the Teenat. The opposite is also true. The opposite is what? That if they are eating Tabarruk, from the tablecloth of Imam Hussain, from the tablecloth of Imam Reza (a.s.), different tablecloths, the tablecloths of the Imams, then this can become the cause of the transformation of the person's Teenat. The great teacher, a very great scholar, Khadimul Hujjat, used to say, the late Rahmatullah Alayh used to say that whenever someone gave him Tabarruk of a Majlis, meaning gave a message, rather this gift, gave a gift that this is a gift, then he would bring that gift and tell his family to cook food only with this. With the money of that gift. He used to say, cook food only with this. So his wife asked, 'Why? You insist so much to cook only with this.' He said, 'This is the Tabarruk (blessing) of the Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (Master of Martyrs), it is a gift. If I consume this, it will become a part of my flesh and skin, and I will be protected from the pressure of the grave (Fishar-e-Qabr). Because the earth does not have the power to exert pressure on the flesh and skin that has been formed by the remembrance of Hussain.' Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali! Ya Ali! Ya Ali! Ya Ali! So, this is a very important thing—that is, remembering Allah. The second thing is Al-bakuna min khashyatillah (those who weep out of fear of Allah). Weeping out of the fear of Allah—you should recite Dua-e-Kumayl. Understand the meaning of Dua-e-Kumayl, reflect upon it, weep, and cry. The words of Dua-e-Kumayl are strange. The words of Dua-e-Saba are strange. Recite Dua-e-Saba. Recite the supplications of the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.), recite the Munajat-e-Khamsa Ashara (the fifteen whispered prayers). Read them and weep while reading them. Look at the strange words in them. How the Mawla-e-Kainat (Master of the Universe) has expressed it: 'O Lord! Even if You were to cast me into Hell and leave me there speaking, after casting me into Hell, if You left me speaking, I would tell the people of Hell that I used to love You, yet You cast me into Hell.' And from there, I will cry out; from there, I will call upon You. Ya Waliyal-Mu'minin (O Guardian of the believers), Ya Aamalal-Arifin (O Hope of the gnostics), Ya Ghiyathal-Mustaghithin (O Succor of those who seek help), Ya Habib Qulubis-Sadiqin (O Beloved of the hearts of the truthful), wa ya Ilahal-Alamin (and O God of the worlds). I will call out from Hell. Look at the strange sentences of Dua-e-Kumayl. And what have you? That is why it is mentioned regarding the prayer of Imam Zain-ul-Abidin (a.s.) that when he used to go into prostration, he would not lift his head until he was completely drenched through his weeping. That was the Imam's prayer. Al-bakuna min khashyatillah. And the third thing, which I will emphasize greatly. That is, 'wal-mustaghfirina bil-ashar' (and those who seek forgiveness at the time of dawn). Seek forgiveness at the time of Sahar. Sahar, meaning the time before the morning prayer (Salat-ul-Subh). After performing Salat-ul-Layl (the night prayer), it is highly recommended—very highly—that you recite the Tasbih of Istighfar 100 times: 'Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh.' And what is recommended for us? It has come in the Hadith that when you seek forgiveness, you should remember each and every sin. Remember each and every sin. Look, we don't have that concept which people generally say, 'Forget the past.' The past is not something for us to forget. Remember each and every sin and keep seeking forgiveness. It is very important. And there are many benefits to this Istighfar. The nation of Prophet Nuh (a.s.) challenged Prophet Nuh. You know Prophet Nuh, you know Prophet Nuh is Abul-Bashar (the father of humanity), Abul-Bashar al-Thani, the second Abul-Bashar. The first Abul-Bashar was Prophet Adam (a.s.), he is the father of humanity, Prophet Adam. Who is the second Abul-Bashar, the second father of humanity? Prophet Nuh (a.s.). And where are both of them buried? With the Ruh-e-Islam (Spirit of Islam). The Father of the Earth, Abu Turab. Did you notice? Both are there. Both are there. Because where was Prophet Nuh sent to be brought? To Babil, Hilla. The nation of Prophet Nuh was in Hilla, whose old name was Babil, Babylon. And then after that, this nation was a very, very bad nation. They troubled him a lot. So much so that even Prophet Nuh's wife troubled him a lot. So much so that she also drowned. She also drowned—meaning she was destroyed, directly into Hell. It is a verse of the Quran, we are not saying it, brother. The Quran is saying about the Prophet's wife, that she went straight to Hell. Who? Prophet Nuh's wife. Directly, it is a verse of the Quran. Ughriqu nar (they were drowned and admitted to the Fire). Meaning, they were drowned and then entered directly into Hell. But Prophet Nuh was preaching to them, and what is most important? When Allah—meaning when Prophet Nuh said to Allah, 'O Lord, I am telling them.' Faqultu (I said to them), 'Istaghfiru Rabbakum' (Seek forgiveness from your Lord). What is the meaning of Istighfar? To seek Maghfirat (forgiveness). Maghfirat, pardon. 'O Lord, forgive me.' That is called Istighfar. Every morning, 'Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh.' This is the minimum, and in fact, it is in the traditions that if you just say 'Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh' three times after every prayer following the Tasbih, Allah will forgive all sins. You should read the Hadiths on Istighfar. You see how Karim (Generous) Allah is. How much Allah loves His servants. So here, Prophet Nuh said, 'Istaghfiru Rabbakum, innahu kana Ghaffara' (Seek forgiveness from your Lord, indeed He is the Great Forgiver). You just seek forgiveness from Allah; He is the One who forgives a lot. Very much Ghaffara. And then Prophet Nuh explains its benefits. If you seek forgiveness, what will happen? Look, the benefits have been stated: 'Yursilis-sama'a alaykum midrara' (He will send rain from the sky upon you in abundance). Meaning, if you keep seeking forgiveness, blessings will keep coming to you from the sky from Allah. Bounties will keep coming continuously. So many blessings will come that you cannot imagine. You cannot think of it. You will be among the chosen servants of Allah. Among the selected servants. This is a verse of the Quran, I am not saying it from myself, brother. 'Yursilis-sama'a alaykum midrara.' And after that, the Quran says, 'Wa yumdidkum bi-amwalin wa banin' (And He will assist you with wealth and children). And Allah will help you, provide aid. With what? With wealth and with children. He will give you wealth and children too. Just try seeking forgiveness. 'Yumdidkum bi-amwalin wa banin. Wa yaj'al lakum jannatin wa yaj'al lakum anhara' (And He will provide gardens for you and provide rivers for you). Allah will establish all these things for you. What else do you want? Prophet Nuh was repeatedly saying this to his nation. After that, he says, 'Ma lakum la tarjuna lillahi waqara' (What is the matter with you that you do not attribute greatness to Allah?). Oh, what has happened to you? Why don't you respect Allah, why don't you show respect to Allah? 'Ma lakum' (What is the matter with you). 'La tarjuna lillahi waqara. Wa qad khalaqakum atwara' (And He has created you in stages). And He has created you in so many stages, in so many ways. Don't you see in the heavens, don't you see in your own selves, don't you see in the universe, how many signs of His there are? Even after that, you do not respect Allah? Prophet Nuh is saying to his nation. Anyway, you should recite the entire Surah Nuh. You see how much importance it has. Right now, Istighfar is not our topic. I just mentioned it as a hint in brackets. That it has great importance. And then, specifically, I will tell you a secret. Which is in the traditions. In the light of Hadith, if we really want to be close to Allah, to be close to our Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), then the best way is to recite the Ziyarat of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada. Recite Ziyarat-e-Ashura, Ziyarat-e-Waritha, recite the Ziyarat of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada. If you can go for Ziyarat yourself, then what to say, it is 'Nur-un-ala-Nur' (light upon light). It is the best. But if someone cannot go, for any reason whatsoever, whatever the cause may be. Cannot go, is not in a position to, just say three times, 'Sallallahu alayka ya Aba Abdillah.' And while staying here, recite Ziyarat-e-Ashura, Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah. Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, you know we have two Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, not one. One Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah is from Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) which happened in 252 Hijri. Which the Imam taught. The eleventh Imam taught it. In 252 Hijri. And the other is Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah Muqaddasa which is from Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), which we generally recite. It is clear to you, right? So, you must recite this Ziyarat. Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, Ziyarat-e-Ashura, Ziyarat-e-Waritha. Become close to the Imam. There is no better way to be close to Allah and the Imam. It is the best way. The best way. Look, when you go for Ziyarat, these sentences—when you go for Ziyarat, what are the etiquette sentences of Ziyarat? That 'O Lord, I have come to such an Infallible (Masoom),' or in some places it is in the plural, 'I have come to such Infallibles.' That 'Yarauna maqami' (They see my station). They are aware of my position. They know what my position is. Meaning, a sinner, a lowly, bad servant has come to the service of the Imam. 'Yarauna maqami wa yasmauna kalami' (They see my station and they hear my speech). And they are also hearing my speech. They hear my speech and also reply to my Salam. Even though You have hidden their voice, their reply, from some people. What is the sentence of the Hadith? From some people—meaning from some people. From some people, You have hidden their voice. From whom have You hidden it? From those whose ears are accustomed to hearing Najis (impure), filthy, and dirty things all day long. For example, if they are accustomed to hearing lies, slander, and forbidden things all day, then what will they hear of the Imam's voice? Because this is a spiritual thing. Therefore, a person should try to train this. Train these ears. And it says that there are some people who do hear these replies. And there are such people. There are such people who actually go and go and say, 'O Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, I will keep coming to you and I will keep reciting your Ziyarat until I hear your reply.' And do you know where they often recite these sentences? Under the Qubba (dome), right? Under the dome. Because under the dome, this prayer is answered (Mustajab), Allah accepts it. So they keep saying, 'Until I hear your reply, I will keep saying it. I will keep remembering you, I will keep reciting this Ziyarat.' And then after that, the Imam says. And the time that has been given, when is the best time to do this Istighfar? Before the morning prayer. 100 times before the morning prayer. That is why waking up for Salat-ul-Layl is very important. And as I just submitted in your service, look. We have talked about religion, let's talk a little about the world. A man has just written a book, and we haven't introduced it anywhere yet, but I don't know what will happen, I even forget the name of that book. But whoever remembers it, please prompt me. He interviewed 1,000 successful people of the world according to him, 1,000, big people. Tim Ferriss is his name. And what has he written? 'Tools of the Titans', now I remember the name of the book, Ahsan. If you memorize the books of Hadith like this, then we wouldn't lose so much time, recite a Salawat on Muhammad. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. The name of the book is 'Tools of the Titans'. And in it, he interviewed 1,000 people. And these 1,000 who are in different fields, according to him, are successful people. We are not calling them successful according to the Quran and Hadith. According to him, he is an Englishman, he is a white man, so according to him, you understand, right? Anyone who is successful in any field. But anyway, the summary is that all the people who were successful from a worldly perspective, when he interviewed them, I am telling this only for the youth, did you know what was one common habit in all of them? They were all early risers. Meaning, they all used to wake up early in the morning. This was the secret to their success. By the time the rest of the world woke up, half of their day was already complete. Even our great scholars, such as Muhaddith-e-Nouri (may Allah be pleased with him), followed this. If Allah grants me the opportunity, I will present the full schedule of Muhaddith-e-Nouri to you. He used to arrive outside the shrine of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) before the person who opened the gates of the shrine even arrived. He would first recite all the initial Ziyarat. Then he would go inside, pray Namaz-e-Shab outside the shrine, then pray near the Zarih, followed by the morning prayers (Namaz-e-Subh) and other Ziyarat. Only then would he go home or to the place where he taught. In short, if we calculate according to Indian or Bombay time, by 11:00 AM, half of his day was already complete. From 11:00 AM until 12:00 or 12:30 PM, he would sleep, which we call 'Qailulah'. It is highly recommended (mustahab) in Hadith. He would sleep for an hour or an hour and a half. After waking up, he would pray Dhuhr and then begin his studies. Since there was no electricity in those days, they relied on oil lamps; by 5:00 or 6:00 PM, when it got dark, people would light lamps to work. In summary, the best time is 'As-Sahar'. In the month of Ramadan, we say 'Sehri'; the word 'Sehri' is derived from 'Sahar'. Wake up in the morning, brothers. Seek forgiveness at that time. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that if someone does this, Satan cannot overcome him; he will remain protected from the whispers of Satan. How strange! Finally, he mentions three types of people from whom Allah removes all punishment: 'Razi bi-qada-illah' (those who are content with the decree of Allah) will not face any punishment on the Day of Judgment. Whatever Allah has written in their destiny, they are content with it. They do not complain, asking 'why this' or 'why that'. They say, 'O Lord, I am grateful to You, my Master. I am grateful.' The second type is 'An-nasihu lil-muslimin' (those who are well-wishers of the Muslims). By Muslims, it means the Mu'minin (believers). When the term 'Muslim' is used in the Quran and Hadith, it has two meanings: a general meaning and a specific meaning. The general meaning is anyone who has recited the Kalima (La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah). But sometimes, the specific meaning of 'Muslim' is one who submits to the Ahlulbayt. The third type is 'Ad-dallu 'ala al-khayr' (those who guide others toward goodness). We have been discussing what 'Khayr' (goodness) is. Khayr is the Wilayah of the family of Muhammad. Khayr is Imam Hussain (a.s.). Whoever guides others toward Imam Hussain (a.s.), toward the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, will have the punishment removed from them on the Day of Judgment. It will be removed from them. Now, some people object, saying, 'Why do you mention the Ahlulbayt in everything? Mention others too.' This objection exists in history. The answer is very simple: these are the people whose mention has been commanded by Allah and His Messenger. Every Muslim has a duty of 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' (enjoining good) and 'Nahy anil-Munkar' (forbidding evil). Is there anyone who would deny this? No. Let me present a tradition narrated by Sheikh Mufid, which Allama Majlisi also recorded in 'Bihar al-Anwar', Volume 10, page 208. Please recite a Salawat, and I will narrate the Hadith. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) came to Iraq. Why did he come? For Ziyarat—the Ziyarat of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (Imam Hussain) and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). When he reached Karbala, the news spread that Sadiq-e-Ale Muhammad had arrived in Iraq. Naturally, the Imam is not an ordinary personality. So, his student came to him. Who was the student? Abu Hanifa. He said, 'Lawla as-sanatani la-halaka an-Nu'man' (If it were not for those two years of being a student of Imam Sadiq, Nu'man would have perished). Everyone used to claim, 'If it were not for Ali, I would have perished.' He said it 108 times. So, he came to the Imam and asked many questions. One of the questions was, 'Ju'iltu fidaka' (May my life be sacrificed for you). It was just lip service, of course. If you truly mean it, you would sacrifice your life, but he just said it. He asked, 'Ma al-amr bil-ma'ruf?' (What is enjoining good?). Usually, we teach children—and it is not wrong—that it means inviting people to goodness. Abu Hanifa, the teacher of the Hanafi school, was asking Imam Sadiq (a.s.) this question. And listen to what Sadiq-e-Ale Muhammad replied. He asked, 'What is Amr bil-Ma'ruf?' The Imam said, 'O Abu Hanifa! The Ma'ruf (good) known to the people of the heavens is the same as the Ma'ruf known to the people of the earth.' He asked, 'What is that?' The Imam replied, 'It is the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).' Haidari Ya Ali! Haidari Ya Ali! What is Ma'ruf? It is Amir al-Mu'minin. So, 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' means guiding everyone toward Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Whoever you talk to, say, 'Brother, come to Ali. Brother, follow Ali. Brother, follow the Ahlulbayt.' This is 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf'. If they go to them, everything else will be understood. Then he asked, 'What is Munkar (evil)?' if that is Ma'ruf. The Imam did not hesitate. He didn't worry, 'Oh, he won't come to our gathering or our class anymore.' Did you notice? The Imam did not hesitate, and I am quoting a Hadith for you. I am not speaking out of thin air. I gave you the reference: Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 10, page 208. It is also narrated in the book 'Al-Ihtijaj' by the late Tabarsi. You can go and check it, read it, and if you want to deny it, then deny it. What do we have to do? We have to answer those who deny it. The Imam clearly stated in Arabic: those who usurped Ali's right, those who sat in Ali's place, they are the Munkar. Did you notice? The Imam clearly said: those who oppressed Ali, snatched his position, usurped his authority, and forced people to follow them. They oppressed Ali. These people are the Munkar. Do not stop people from them? No, love them? 'They are also good, they are also good'? That is not our way. We have stated that Tashayyu (Shi'ism) means this. Anyway, he then asked, 'O Mawla, tell me, what is the meaning of this verse: 'Latusalunna yawma'idhin 'anin-na'im' (Then, on that day, you will be questioned about the blessings)?' The Imam asked him, 'You tell me, what is a blessing (na'im) according to you?' He said, 'The food we eat, the water we drink, a healthy body, and security.' The Imam said, 'Abu Hanifa, then you will not be able to escape on the Day of Judgment. You will have to answer for every single grain. It will be very difficult for you.' And in another Hadith, it is said that Allah is too generous to invite people as His guests in this world and then question them about the food they ate. Allah is more generous than that. No other person would do that. If someone invites you to their house to eat and then asks, 'How much did you eat? Why did you drink this much? Why did you do this?'—is that clear to you? The Imam said, 'Your standing on the Day of Judgment will not be long.' What is the meaning of 'Na'im'? The Imam said, 'Hubbuna Ahl al-Bayt' (Our love, the Ahlulbayt). You will be questioned about this. This Ahlulbayt, for whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said—it is a verse of the Quran, Surah Ash-Shura, verse 23: 'Qul la as'alukum 'alayhi ajran illal-mawaddata fil-qurba' (Say, O Prophet, I do not ask of you any reward for this except love for my near kin). But what did this Ummah do? They oppressed them as much as they possibly could. In Dua-e-Nudba, you recite: 'Faqutila man qutila wa subiya man subiya wa uqsiya man uqsiya' (Some of the Ahlulbayt were killed). Some were killed, some were taken prisoner, and some were driven away. What greater oppression could they commit? They could not have committed more. Today, we are mentioning that martyr of Karbala whom you mention in every Ziyarat: 'Wa 'ala Ali ibn al-Husayn' (Peace be upon Ali ibn al-Husayn). This is the martyr who, when all the companions were martyred and no one was left, the Imam said, 'Taqaddam ya bunayya' (Go forward, my son). Ali Akbar was waiting. Ali Akbar went, but the Imam said, 'Son Ali Akbar, first go to the tent and take permission.' Ali Akbar went to the tent and took permission. He first took permission from his mother, and she said, 'Why do you take permission from me? Go and take permission from your aunt Zainab, who prepared your armor.' When he took permission from Janabe Zainab, she said, 'Son, did I raise you for 18 years in luxury just so you could ask for permission to die?' He said, 'Aunt, if you do not give permission, then don't, but what if my grandmother (Fatima Zahra) asks me on the Day of Judgment?' Zaynab gave permission. Ali Akbar wanted to leave the tent. Hamid ibn Muslim says that every time Ali Akbar wanted to leave, someone would catch his garment and hold him back. Ali Akbar would go back. It felt as if a funeral of a young man was leaving a full house. Now, it is not written in the Maqtal who was holding Ali Akbar's garment. Yes, it is certain that if an elder had stopped Ali Akbar, they would have held his arm. But holding the garment means a little girl was holding her brother's garment and saying, 'Wa Akhah! O my brother! Have pity on our loneliness, on our helplessness.' Ali Akbar left. Husayn (a.s.) helped him mount the horse. After he mounted, he looked towards the sky and said, 'Allahumma ish-had ala ha-ulai qawm' (O Allah, be a witness against this nation). 'Qad baraza ilayhim ghulam' (A youth is going to fight them). 'Ashbahun-nasi khalqan wa khulqan wa mantiqan bi-Rasulika' (The one who resembles Your Messenger the most in appearance, character, and speech). When we longed to see Your Messenger, we would look at Ali Akbar. Ali Akbar was sent off. Ali Akbar went. He had not gone far when a sound was heard. When he turned back, he saw his father with his hand on his waist, saying, 'Ya Ali! Ya Ali!' 'O Father, you had already bid me farewell.' He said, 'Son, if you had children, you would know what the grief of separation from a young son is.' Ali Akbar went. It is written in the Maqtal that he sent more than 200 wretched enemies to Hell. Ali Akbar returned. Until now, whoever went to the battlefield did not return, except for Wahab al-Kalbi. But Ali Akbar returned, and how did he return? What was the reason Ali Akbar returned? It was his mother's prayer. It was a mother's heart that was anxious. She said, 'Fizza, stand at the door of the tent. Keep watching the master's face. If the color of the master's face changes, understand that my son is in great trouble, for it is a matter of a young son.' Fizza came to the tent door. After a while, she came running. 'Bibi, the color of the master's face has changed.' Go and trouble the master. Husayn (a.s.) came into the tent. She asked, 'What happened?' He said, 'Why has the color of your face changed?' He replied, 'A famous warrior has come before my Ali Akbar. He is a renowned fighter, and my son is hungry and thirsty for three days.' The mother's heart was torn. 'Master, what should I do?' He said, 'Pray. A mother's prayer is accepted for her son.' The ladies formed a circle. Umm Layla stood in the middle. 'Ilahi bi-ghurbati-Husayn' (O Allah, for the sake of Husayn's loneliness). 'Parwardigara, I beseech You by the helplessness of Husayn. O You who returned Yusuf to Yaqub, return my Ali Akbar to me.' The mother's prayer had not yet finished when Ali Akbar arrived. But in what state? In what state did he arrive? Covered in wounds and bathed in blood. He came and said, 'Ya Abbata! Ya Abbata! Al-atash qad qatalani' (O Father! O Father! Thirst is killing me). 'Wa siqalul-hadidi ajhadani' (And the heaviness of the iron armor is exhausting me). The weight of the sword is now felt very heavily; I cannot bear the burden. 'Fahal ila khurujin min sabil?' (Is there any way to get water?) Father, is there any possibility of water? If I could get a little water, I could fight the enemies. Husayn (a.s.) said, 'Son, you know there is not a drop of water in the tent, but bring your tongue into my mouth; perhaps you might get some relief, some hope.' As soon as Ali Akbar placed his tongue in Husayn's blessed mouth, he pulled it back. 'Father, your tongue is parched with thorns.' Husayn gave his ring to Ali Akbar, 'Son, keep this; now your grandfather will quench your thirst from the Hawd-e-Kawthar.' Ali Akbar went, and when he went, he continued to fight. Remember, this wretch took aim at Ali Akbar's chest and struck him with a spear such that Ali Akbar fell from his horse. Now listen to a sentence from the Maqtal; your heart will break. It is written in the Maqtal that as soon as Ali Akbar fell from the horse, 'Faqatta'uhu bi-suyufihim irban irban' (They began to cut his body into pieces with their swords). Ali Akbar called out, 'Ya Abbata!' Husayn (a.s.) came to Ali Akbar's corpse, saw the spear, and now Husayn is trying to remove the spear. The spear was removed, a fountain of blood erupted, but Ali Akbar's soul also departed. Husayn recited a dirge: 'Ala ad-dunya ba'dakal 'afa' (O son, may there be dust upon the life of this world after you). 'Istarahta min hammid-dunya wa ghammiha' (Son, you have found relief from the worries and sorrows of this world). 'Wa baqiya abuka wahidan faridan baynal a'da' (But your father remains alone and solitary among the enemies). Ali Akbar, now when the news of Ali Akbar's death spread, Hamid ibn Muslim says, 'Fa-ka-anni anzuru ila imra'atin' (It was as if I was looking at a woman). 'Kharajat musri'atan' (She came out running quickly). Her face was shining brighter than the sun. 'Tunadi bi-wayliha wa-thubur' (Calling out in her woe and destruction). Beating her face, 'Ya wayla! Ya sabura! Ya habiba! O my beloved! Ya samrad-e-pua! O piece of my heart! Ya nur-e-aina! O coolness of my eyes!' Hamid ibn Muslim says, I asked who it is? 'Qalu hiya Zaynab bintu Ali' (They said she is Zaynab, daughter of Ali). 'Wa sa'lamul-ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun' (And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned). 'Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz-zalimin' (The curse of Allah be upon the unjust people). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Age (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Age (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of Husayn's blood. Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are in distress, remove their distress. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. Those who are away from their homeland, return them safe and sound. O Lord! Protect the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world, their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the eminent Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zaynab. O Lord! Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the Hereafter. Accept our health, our mourning, and our Azadari. Matam-e-Husayn.

True Dhikr involves constant mindfulness of Allah's laws rather than mere verbal repetition.
Amr bil-Ma'ruf is defined as inviting others to the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.), while Munkar involves opposing the rights of the Ahlulbayt.
The 'Na'im' or blessings mentioned in the Quran refer specifically to the love and recognition of the Prophet's family.
The sacrifice of Ali Akbar (a.s.) serves as the ultimate example of devotion and moral perfection in the face of extreme brutality.

chapters.title: Zainab's Grief at the Euphrates
chapters.summary: Janab-e-Zainab mourns the martyrdom of Abbas and expresses her profound sorrow and helplessness to her brother.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Recognizing the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that true success and faith depend on the recognition of the Imam of the time, as defined by the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira
chapters.summary: An introduction to the importance of Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira and the scholarly contributions of Sheikh Saduq in preserving authentic traditions.

chapters.title: The Wilayah of the 14 Masumeen
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the righteous work mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf refers to accepting the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and the 14 Masumeen, emphasizing that no one else holds this status.

chapters.title: The Status and Necessity of the 12 Imams
chapters.summary: The lecture details the exclusive status of the 12 Imams as the Hujjah of Allah, explaining their role as the cause of safety for the earth and the heavens.

chapters.title: Protection from Iblis and True Remembrance
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses three individuals protected from Iblis, defining the true, difficult nature of 'Dhikr' (remembrance of Allah) as acting according to Allah's commands in every situation.

chapters.title: The Impact of Tabarruk on Human Nature
chapters.summary: The speaker explains how consuming Tabarruk from the Imams transforms one's essence (Teenat) and provides spiritual protection against the trials of the grave.

chapters.title: Weeping in Fear of Allah
chapters.summary: The importance of reciting supplications like Dua-e-Kumayl and the Munajat-e-Khamsa Ashara to cultivate a heart that weeps out of fear and love for Allah.

chapters.title: The Power of Istighfar and Seeking Forgiveness
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness at dawn (Sahar) and highlights the Quranic benefits of Istighfar, including abundance in wealth and children.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ziyarat
chapters.summary: Reciting Ziyarat of the Ahl-e-Bayt is presented as the best way to gain closeness to Allah and the Imam, with a focus on the spiritual etiquette of being heard by the Infallibles.

chapters.title: The Importance of Early Rising
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the spiritual and worldly benefits of waking up early, citing the habits of successful people and the practices of scholars like Muhaddith-e-Nouri.

chapters.title: Defining Goodness and Evil
chapters.summary: The lecture explains that true goodness (Ma'ruf) is the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt, while evil (Munkar) involves the usurpation of their rights.

chapters.title: The Meaning of Na'im and Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The Imam clarifies that the 'blessing' (Na'im) for which humanity will be questioned on Judgment Day is the love of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Ali Akbar
chapters.summary: The section concludes with the tragic departure of Ali Akbar to the battlefield and his final farewells to his family.

chapters.title: Departure of Ali Akbar to the Battlefield
chapters.summary: Ali Akbar bids farewell to his family, with Husayn (a.s.) describing his striking resemblance to the Prophet Muhammad.

chapters.title: The Mother's Prayer and Ali Akbar's Return
chapters.summary: Umm Layla prays for her son's safety, leading to a brief return of Ali Akbar to the tents before he faces his final battle.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Ali Akbar
chapters.summary: Ali Akbar suffers from extreme thirst and exhaustion, eventually falling in battle and being martyred, leaving Husayn (a.s.) in profound grief.

chapters.title: Zaynab's Lament and Final Supplications
chapters.summary: Zaynab (s.a.) rushes to the battlefield in despair, followed by a concluding prayer for the reappearance of the Imam of the Age.

title: Hazrat Abu Talib (peace be on him) - The Guardian of Islam  |  Sayed Mahdi Modarresi
excerpt: This lecture by Sayed Mahdi Modarresi explores the life, faith, and legacy of Hazrat Abu Talib, the uncle and guardian of the Prophet Muhammad. The speaker challenges historical misconceptions and Umayyad-era distortions that have cast doubt on Abu Talib's belief, arguing that his lifelong protection and sacrifice for the Prophet are definitive proofs of his true faith. By citing the testimonies of the Ahlulbayt and historical actions, the lecture establishes Abu Talib as a central figure whose status serves as a litmus test for spiritual integrity and loyalty to the Prophet's mission.
