chapters.title: The Virtue of Concealed Deeds
chapters.summary: True believers do not seek recognition for their good deeds, as fame is often associated with the worldly rather than the righteous.

chapters.title: The Unjust Accusations Against Abu Talib
chapters.summary: Despite his essential role in protecting the Prophet and Islam, Abu Talib is unfairly maligned by those influenced by Umayyad-era propaganda.

chapters.title: The Divine Lineage and Light
chapters.summary: Traditions from the Imams explain that the lights of the Prophet and Imam Ali were passed down through a pure, monotheistic lineage, including Abu Talib.

chapters.title: Faith as Measured by Action
chapters.summary: The Quran defines true faith through actions like providing shelter and aid, which serves as a definitive proof of Abu Talib's status as a believer.

chapters.title: The Logic of Abu Talib's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: The speaker argues that Abu Talib's willingness to sacrifice his own children to protect the Prophet is clear, logical evidence of his profound faith.

chapters.title: Historical Testimony on Abu Talib's Faith
chapters.summary: Ibn Abi al-Hadid and other scholars confirm that Abu Talib was a true believer who guarded the Prophet during the early days of Islam.

chapters.title: The Litmus Test of Faith
chapters.summary: The Imams of the Ahlulbayt declared that doubting the faith of Abu Talib is a serious matter, establishing his status as a litmus test for true belief.

chapters.title: Critique of Scholars and Historical Misconceptions
chapters.summary: The speaker challenges the claim that Abu Talib was a disbeliever, arguing that such views stem from biased scholarship and historical distortions by the Umayyads.

chapters.title: Refuting Misguided Views of Rumi and Ibn Arabi
chapters.summary: The speaker criticizes Jalaluddin Rumi and Ibn Arabi for their disparaging remarks about Abu Talib, warning followers of the Ahlulbayt against uncritically accepting their literature.

chapters.title: The High Status of Abu Talib and Practical Intercession
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the Ahlulbayt's practice of performing tawaf for Abu Talib and shares a tradition demonstrating his status as an intercessor for answered prayers.

chapters.title: Sacrifices of the Prophet's Family at Badr
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by honoring the sacrifices of the Prophet's family, specifically highlighting the martyrdom of Ubaydah ibn al-Harith at the Battle of Badr.

chapters.title: Abu Talib's Legacy of Sacrifice
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights how Abu Talib's spirit of devotion and sacrifice influenced the entire family of the Prophet, including Imam Ali and the martyrs of Karbala.

chapters.title: The Burial and Status of Abu Talib
chapters.summary: The Prophet's deep grief at the death of Abu Talib and the specific instructions given to Imam Ali for his burial underscore Abu Talib's profound importance.

chapters.title: The Intercession and Greatness of Abu Talib
chapters.summary: The Prophet promises an awe-inspiring intercession for Abu Talib, revealing that his true status and spiritual inheritance were far greater than many realized.

title: Muharram Mein Hansee Mazaak Se Parhez Kyun Zaroori Hai? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the importance of maintaining a respectful and somber demeanor during the month of Muharram. It emphasizes that the period commemorates the tragic martyrdom of Imam Hussain (AS) and his family at Karbala. The speaker advises believers to avoid laughter, excessive humor, and celebrations during these days to honor the grief of the Ahlulbayt. The talk serves as a reminder to align one's conduct with the sanctity of the mourning period.

chapters.title: Celebrating the Birth of the Prophet
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the joy of celebrating the birth of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the importance of following the path of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice and Legacy of Imam Hussain
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes how the mourning and sacrifice of Imam Hussain (a.s.) have kept the true religion alive throughout history.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Innovation, and Devotion
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the concept of loyalty to the Ahlulbayt, criticizing those who issue fatwas against traditional expressions of devotion like the Alam and Tazia.

chapters.title: Waiting for the Imam Mahdi

chapters.title: The Unparalleled Status of Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker reflects on the unique, incomparable status of the Ahlulbayt, comparing the tragedy of Imam Hussain (a.s.) to the sun and the stars.

chapters.title: Philosophy and Etiquette of Mourning

title: EP02 | Kya Nabi (s.a.w.a.) Shura Ke Zariye Faisle Liya Karte Thay? | 💐 GHADEER: PEI MEGA QUIZ 2025
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological nuances of the Quranic concept of Shura (consultation) in the context of the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) leadership. It clarifies that the Prophet's consultation with companions was a pedagogical and strategic tool rather than a necessity born of a lack of divine guidance. The discussion emphasizes the Shia doctrine of Infallibility, asserting that the appointment of a leader remains a divine prerogative that cannot be determined by human consensus.
content:
Hadi Siyas, Hadith Subh-e-Rabb-e-Aala, Hadi Noor-e-Khuda, Paighambar-e-Haq, Jo Ali, Ilahu Ali, Nash-e-Ali, Seema-e-Ali, Ek Sanad Hadith, Allahu Wali, Ka Hujjat-e-Hasan, Salwaka Alay, Wala Fi-d-Sa, Wa Fi Kull-e-Sa, Wali, Wa Hafiza, Wa Qada, Waha, Wa Daleela, Wa Na-Haqahu Aqa. Wahu [Praise]. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, subscribe now and do not forget to click the bell icon. The quiz link is live and is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered already, click on the quiz link and register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. The answers to all the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who have answered all the questions correctly, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. However, if your name did not appear among today's winners or if you missed an episode, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the Ziyarat of Iraq lucky draw winner, will be selected from those the Ziyarat of Iraq lucky draw winner will be selected from those who have answered all the questions correctly in all the episodes. That is, even if someone was not among the daily winners but has answered correctly in all episodes, all those people will be included in the mega prize Ziyarat of Iraq lucky draw. Some people, misusing this verse, say—they bring this verse as evidence—that this verse legitimizes Shura (consultation), and that determining or appointing a Caliph through Shura is present in the Quran. And they bring this verse as evidence that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was ordered to consult with the Sahaba. Now, the Prophet left the task of appointing a Caliph to the Sahaba. They should consult among themselves and decide who their Caliph will be. A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytanir rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim, wa sallallahu ala... So, dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. In Surah Al-Imran, verse 159, 'wa shawirhum fil-amr' (and consult them in the matter), here the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was ordered to consult with the Sahaba. ordered to consult with the Sahaba. Some individuals, some people, misusing this verse, say that this verse is proof for Shura. That is, the Shura that was chosen to appoint the Caliph. Although it was not even a Shura; it was not a complete Shura. When the first Caliph was chosen, some people claim that it was appointed based on Shura, and to legitimize that act, they use this verse. Let us see a brief and useful answer to this through the debate of Sheikh Mufid (al-rahma). Sheikh Mufid (al-rahma), who was born in 336 AH and died in 413 AH—that is, he was counted among the prominent Shia jurists, hadith scholars, and theologians of the 4th and 5th centuries. He has a book named 'Al-Fusul al-Mukhtara'. In this book, debates and discussions with the Ahl-e-Sunnah on various topics of Imamate, Risalah, and Shia beliefs are present. In this same book, one of your debates that took place at the house of Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Tahir, which took place with the Sunni jurist Al-Warsani, is narrated as follows. Al-Warsani says that 'Al-Madhhab'... is narrated as follows. Al-Warsani says, 'Al-Madhhab Rasul Allah (s.a.w.a.) kana ma'suman' (Is it not in your religion...)? The point worth noting here is that Al-Warsani also knew that Shia is a proper religion—that is, it is not a political movement as people are claiming today—and the best evidence for this is his saying in this debate, 'Alaysa madhhabik' (Is it not your religion?). That is, he knew that Shia is a religion; that is, the religion that Sheikh Mufid believes in is not a political movement but a religion. 'Al-Madhhab Rasul Allah (s.a.w.a.) kana ma'suman' (Is it not in your religion that the Messenger of Allah is infallible, protected from all sins, protected from all misguidance, protected from all forgetfulness, protected from all mistakes, and is completely perfect in his self? Independent of his subjects and his people? The Messenger of Allah). That is, this point is also worth noting that the belief in Infallibility (Ismah) is a proper ancient belief in the Shia religion, not what people are claiming nowadays—that the Imams are 'Ulama Abrar' (pious scholars) and are not infallible. No, this belief in Ismah is an ancient belief found in our religion. found in our religion, and this book was compiled in the 4th century. Sheikh Mufid (rahmatullahi alayh) said to him, 'Bala kadha' (Yes, it is certainly so, this is our belief). Now Al-Warsani turned back and said to Sheikh Mufid (al-rahma), 'Fama tasna'u bi-qawl Allah Jalla Jalaluhu' (Then what will you do with this saying of Allah Jalla Jalaluhu, i.e., Surah Al-Imran, verse 159, which says: 'wa shawirhum fil-amr, fa-idha azamta fa-tawakkal 'ala Allah' (and consult them in the matter, then when you have decided, rely upon Allah)?). He brought this verse before Sheikh Mufid as if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is needy, a beggar—na'udhu billah min dhalik—of the consultation of the Ummah. He actually used this word: 'Alaysa qad amara bi-istina'i ar-ra'y' (Did Allah not order you to take the opinion of the Sahaba and make them needy of their opinion—that is, make the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) needy of the Sahaba's opinion, na'udhu billah min dhalik)? needy of the Sahaba's opinion, na'udhu billah min dhalik. Now, when you are claiming this Infallibility, how will you answer the apparent meaning of this verse? That is, the apparent meaning of the verse, according to Al-Warsani, was against the Shia belief, against the Shia belief of Infallibility. Sheikh Mufid (rahmatullahi alayh) replies, saying that as for the reason, the wisdom behind why Allah ordered the Prophet to consult with the Sahaba, we will deal with that at the end. But as for the first part—did Allah make the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) needy of the Sahaba's opinion, na'udhu billah min dhalik—the answer to that is that this is your assumption and your conjecture, that you are thinking this way, whereas the verse is not like that. Sheikh Mufid (al-rahma) says in response to this: 'Inna Rasul Allah (s.a.w.a.) kana la yushawiru ashabahu li-faqr' (The Messenger of Allah, when he used to consult the Sahaba, it was not for the purpose that he was needy or that there was a need for their opinion and their consultation, and there was no need for him to consult them due to any necessity). It is not as you are assuming, as you are imagining. Rather, it has another as you are imagining. Rather, it has another reason and another wisdom, which I will explain to you at the end. 'Wa Rasul Allah (s.a.w.a.) kana ma'suman' (And the Messenger of Allah was infallible). Then he says that when we have known that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is infallible from every sin, whether major or minor, 'wa khata' ismatihi' (while your belief is this—that is, it is clear for the viewers that the Ahl-e-Sunnah do not believe that the Messenger of Allah is completely infallible in every sin. Among some sects of Ahl-e-Sunnah, this matter is like this. Their belief is that the Messenger of Allah cannot commit major sins but can commit minor ones, na'udhu billah min dhalik). And after that, when we have known that he is 'Akmal al-Khalq' (the most perfect of creation)—by the consensus of the Ummah, all the Ummah agrees that the Messenger of Allah is the most perfect of creation—he possesses the best opinion, that is, he has the best opinion, and he possesses the most abundant intellect. Whereas our belief, the belief of the Shias, is that the Messenger of Allah's status is of luminous intellect, and he is the most perfect in planning, at the highest level of perfection. And the 'Mawad' (affection) was between Allah and the Messenger. There is a connection between Allah and the Messenger, and between Allah and the Messenger of Allah. Angels used to come and go, bringing news of the unseen to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and they brought commands from Allah. The angels used to bring Allah's planning to the service of the Messenger of Allah. They would come and go; the angels were constantly moving. So, when a person is at such a station, such a person does not need anyone else's opinion. 'Lam yahtaj ila iqtibas ra'y' (he does not need to adopt an opinion)—meaning it is not correct to say that such a person should go to an imperfect person to seek their opinion or to take advice from them. That is, for the perfect one to go to an imperfect one to seek their opinion is not intellectually sound. Because no one in their Ummah was equal to them, and there is a consensus of the entire Ummah on this, knowing that all the followers, in terms of their attributes and virtues, are insignificant compared to the Messenger of Allah. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah does not need their opinion, and the Messenger of Allah, God forbid, is not dependent on their consultation. Because the perfect one is not a beggar of the imperfect one in matters where the perfect one is... In matters where the perfect one is in need, just as a scholar is not in need of an ignorant person regarding their knowledge—meaning a scholar has no dependency on an ignorant person to take knowledge from them. And then Sheikh Mufid (r.a.) explains in a very beautiful way here that the second part of the verse points towards this. The first part is 'wa shawirhum fil-amr' (and consult them in the matter), the wisdom of which Sheikh Mufid says I will explain at the end. In the command, the Messenger of Allah is being ordered to consult the companions in affairs. Then 'fa-idha azamta' (then when you have decided), Sheikh Mufid states that the 'azm' (determination) here is attributed to the person of the Messenger of Allah. 'Fa-idha azamta'—when you have made a decision, meaning the correct decision, the determination of it has been placed in your authority. 'Fatawakkal 'ala Allah' (then rely upon Allah and proceed). So, Mufid clearly states here that the command to consult was given, but it was not made mandatory to follow the consultation. The decision and the determination were kept in the authority of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). And that is why the word used in this verse of the Quran is 'fa-idha azamta' (when you have determined/decided). And as for the wisdom of the first part of the verse, 'wa shawirhum fil-amr', this is because... The wisdom of the part 'wa shawirhum fil-amr' (and consult them in the matter) is that the Prophet was commanded to consult, says Sheikh Mufid (al-rahma), so that the hearts of the companions would incline towards the Prophet and they would be taught how the Prophet makes decisions, and based on this, they could understand and be trained in the etiquette of Allah, 'li-ta'addub bi-adabillah' (so that they may be disciplined/trained in the etiquette of Allah). They were to be trained in how the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) makes decisions. This is not because there was any need, God forbid, for the Messenger of Allah to have the companions' advice. And another reason for this command to consult, which Sheikh Mufid explains here, is that not all of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) were believers; rather, among them were some who were 'mutalabbis' (deceptive), who wanted to deceive him, were waiting for an opportunity, were persistent in their opposition against the Prophet, and were hiding malice and hatred in their hearts regarding the Prophet, and were trying to... And were trying to ruin the Prophet's affairs and oppose him in the religion. But Allah did not directly reveal to the Messenger of Allah who these people were, nor did He state their names to the Messenger of Allah. Yes, there are many verses in the Quran that point towards these hypocrites. And then Sheikh Mufid (r.a.) mentions verses one after another: 'Wa mimman hawlakum minal-a'rabi munafiqun wa min ahlil-madinati maraddu 'alan-nifaq la ta'lamuhum nahnu na'lamuhum sanu'adhdhibuhum marratayn thumma yuradduna ila 'adhabin 'azim' (And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and [also] from the people of Madinah. They are persistent in hypocrisy; you do not know them, [but] We know them. We will punish them twice [in this world]; then they will be returned to a great punishment). Then another verse: 'Wa idha ma unzilat surah' (And whenever a surah is revealed), they look at one another [asking], 'Does anyone see you?' This shows that... This shows that these verses of the Surah being revealed regarding the hypocrites were fitting them so well that they felt someone was listening to them and watching them, and that is how the verses were being revealed. They would look at each other to see if anyone was watching, as these verses were about them. They were applying to them and fitting them perfectly. And then they turn away, so Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand. The third verse: 'Yahlifuna lakum li-tardaw 'anhum' (They swear to you so that you might be pleased with them). So even if you are pleased with them, Allah is not pleased with a defiantly disobedient people. 'Wa yahlifuna billahi innahum laminkum wa ma hum minkum wa lakinna hum qawmun yafraqun' (And they swear by Allah that they are among you, while they are not among you; but they are a people who are afraid). 'Wa idha ra'aytahum tu'jibuka ajsamuhum wa in yaqulu tasma' li-qawlihim' (And when you see them, their bodies please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech)... Their bodies please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech—meaning their outward appearance was like that of the believers, and they would meet the believers with great humility and talk so nicely that it seemed as if they were believers, but in reality, they were like dry logs propped up against a wall, thinking every shout is against them. They are truly enemies, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they being deluded? Then the next verse: 'Innal-munafiqina yukhadi'unallaha wa huwa khadi'uhum wa idha qamu ilas-salati qamu kusala yura'unan-nasa wa la yadhkurunallaha illa qalila' (Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves to] the people and not remembering Allah except a little). They want to deceive Allah, and Allah is the one who keeps them in deception. And when they rise for prayer, they do so lazily, acting to show people, and they remember Allah very little. Then the next verse: 'Wa la ya'tunassalata illa wa hum kusala wa la yunfiquna' (And they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy, and they do not spend)... And whatever they spend in the way of Allah, they spend with reluctance. These are the signs of the hypocrites mentioned in the Holy Quran, which Sheikh Mufid is bringing before them in the form of verses one after another. And observe, viewers, that it is not a matter of one or two verses. You will see that their preachers, wherever the companions are mentioned, cite only one verse and tell everyone about the status in which Allah remembered the companions in the Holy Quran. Although among the companions, there were some who held the rank of hypocrites, who were counted in the ranks of the hypocrites, and they are mentioned in the entire Surah Tawbah, Surah Munafiqun, and other Surahs like Anfal and Nisa. Sheikh Mufid is bringing this here one after another before the viewers: 'Wa law nashau la-araynakahum fa-la'araftahum bi-simahum wa la-ta'rifannahum fi lahnil-qawl' (And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark; but you will surely know them by the tone of their speech). Here, Allah has placed the identification of the hypocrites in the tone of their speech. This is a point worth noting. And for this reason, Allah commanded the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) to consult them so that the 'lahnil-qawl' (tone of speech) could be understood... Commanded to consult them so that the 'lahnil-qawl' could be understood. Their tone of speech could be understood, by which you could recognize who is a hypocrite and who is a believer among the companions. And a person's reality is hidden in their advice. The one who is a well-wisher will give you good advice. Conversely, your enemy will always try to give you advice that will destroy you. Through consultation, it will be known who is truly a hypocrite, and the 'lahnil-qawl' will be recognized. Allah is pointing towards this in this verse of the Quran, and Sheikh Mufid is saying: 'Did you not see that when these companions gave advice to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) at Badr, was their advice based on sincerity or hypocrisy?' And Allah admonished them and revealed their hypocrisy to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in this manner: 'Ma kana li-nabiyyin an yakuna lahu asra hatta yuthkhina fil-ard, turiduna 'aradal-dunya wallahu yuridu-l-akhirah, wallahu 'azizun hakim' (It is not for a prophet to have captives [of war] until he inflicts a major slaughter [upon the enemies] in the earth. You desire the commodities of this world, but Allah desires [for you] the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise). When the Prophet at Badr... When the Prophet at Badr took the polytheists of Makkah as captives, at that time, these hypocrites advised the Prophet to free these captives in exchange for ransom. You have already killed many. These hypocrites advised the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to free those who were taken captive after the Battle of Badr in exchange for ransom. And this advice of theirs was based on worldly desire and their hypocrisy. Although there was no sincerity in this advice, and Allah pointed to this: 'You desire the commodities of this world, while Allah desires the Hereafter.' So, viewers, when we have seen the true meaning of this verse and what is intended by it, when we have understood this well, let us draw your attention to the fact that some people, misusing this verse, bring it as evidence, saying that this verse legitimizes 'Shura' (consultation) and that determining or appointing a Caliph through Shura is present in the Quran... Determining or appointing a Caliph through Shura is present in the Quran. And they bring this verse as evidence that the Prophet was commanded to consult with the companions. Now, the Prophet left the task of appointing a Caliph to the companions. They should consult among themselves and decide who their Caliph will be. You can understand whether this is like using a verse to prove a predetermined goal. A verse has been fitted into a place to prove what they wanted to prove. That is, what they wanted to prove was already in their minds as their belief. Now they found a verse and fitted it to say that this verse proves our belief. Whereas that verse is pointing in a completely different direction, totally 180 degrees opposite. As far as appointing a Caliph is concerned, let us draw your attention to that Hadith. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), in the beginning of his Prophethood, was inviting tribes to Islam, when he invited the Banu Kilab, when the Prophet was inviting various tribes around Madinah to Islam, at that time he went to the Banu Kilab, and they said to the Prophet, 'Will you give us the command after you?' So the leaders of Banu Kilab... The leaders of the Banu Kilab tribe said, 'We will pledge allegiance to you on the condition that after you, the authority (amr) will come to us; it will be transferred to us, to our tribe.' Meaning, the Wilayah after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would be attained by a member of the Banu Kilab. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'Fal-amru lillah' (The authority belongs to Allah). The right to choose an Imam or a Caliph belongs solely to Allah. 'Fa-in sha'a ja'alahu feekum wa kana fee ghayrikum' (If He wills, it will be among you, and if He wills, it will be in others). Upon this, they left and did not pledge allegiance at the hands of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Any rational person can conclude from this Hadith that the right to choose the authority—the Wali and Caliph—belongs solely to Allah. Here, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is not even attributing this authority to himself, let alone leaving it in the hands of those companions who were deficient in intellect and in whose hearts hypocrisy and disease were found. Should Allah leave it in the hands of such people? They said, 'Shall we wield our swords in your wars and then you...' Shall we wield our swords in your wars and then you impose someone else over us?' They understood perfectly well from the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) statement that the Caliph and the Wali was not going to come from the Banu Kilab. He was to come from another tribe, and this authority was entrusted to someone else. Respected viewers, it is clear to us that the Caliphate is solely in the hands of Allah. Choosing a Caliph and choosing an Imam is His right. If anyone misuses the verse regarding consultation (shura) for this selection, it is nothing but clear misguidance. Peace be upon Muhammad and his pure, infallible progeny. Peace be upon you, O Trustee of Allah on His earth and His proof over His servants. Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Faithful. I bear witness that you strove in Jihad and... Then listening to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) until Allah granted him the choice, and he became the proof of Allah over all of creation. He was a soul of power, a manifestation of destiny, a call of love, a quality of the Awliya (saints), a beloved one in the heavens and the earth, a guide, a leader... A leader, a longing for the truth, a pious one, a reward, a chosen one of the Awliya, a possessor of noble character, a helper of the world, and we are those whose hearts are inclined towards Him, seeking Him, and seeking His path, and we are those who are satisfied with His decree, a caller who is answered, and a repentance that is accepted, and a structure that is... And a structure that is firm, and a presence that is manifest, and a presence that is manifest, and a presence that is manifest, and a servant who is miraculous, and a position that is elevated, and a protection that is preserved, and a descent that is divine, and a return that is towards the hearts of the seekers, forgiven, and He is the Creator of all things, so answer the prayer. Answer the prayer, O our Master, and our Mawla, and our Awliya, by the right of Muhammad, and Ali, and Fatima, and Hasan, and Husayn, for you are my Wali and my Imam, and my refuge, and my destination in my return and my [music]... You are the Truth, and You are the Protector, and You are the Helper, for You are capable of all things. Capable of all things, and may Allah bless Muhammad, the Master of the Messengers, and his pure and purified family. [music] I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Master of the Age. Remember that the quiz link has not been closed and will remain live until the end of this series. Daily winners will be selected only from those who have answered all questions correctly until the end of the Ziyarat in the episode. With that, let us move towards the announcement of today's daily winners, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. Let us see who those 18 winners are who will receive a prize of 1400 Indian Rupees. Their names are on your screen: Syed Ashraf (Mumbai), Mehrin Shafi (Srinagar), Mohammad Hussain (Kaushambi), Syed Baqar Ali Rizvi (Saharanpur), Jinan Zaidi (Mumbai), Sana Abbas (Lucknow), Sughra Ali (New Delhi), Gulrez Haider (Azamgarh), Zareen Fatima (Mumbai), Ruqaiya Zainab (Jaipur), Syeda Areez Ali (Alipur), Ghazi Rajani (Thaliya), Anjum Wasaya (Mahua), Syeda Fatima (Alipur), Ehsan Abbas Rizvi (Sarai Aqil), Ali Asghar Keshwani (Bhavnagar), Mir Shahzad Ali Asghar Keshwani (Bhavnagar), Mir Shahzad Mahdi (Bengaluru), Zainab Hashmi (Alipur). Many congratulations to all the winners. As mentioned, if your name has not appeared in any episode, there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series. Those who have answered all the quiz questions correctly in all episodes of this series will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize, i.e., a Ziyarat to Iraq. We thank you all once again. title: Maah-e-Ramazan Mein Badnaseeb Kaun? | Maah-e-Ramazan 2026
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual significance of the month of Ramadan as described in a profound tradition narrated through the Ahlulbayt. It emphasizes that Ramadan is a divine invitation to Allah's hospitality, where even simple acts like breathing and sleeping are considered worship. The speaker warns that the truly unfortunate person is the one who fails to attain Allah's forgiveness during this blessed period. The message serves as a call to approach the month with sincerity and a focus on fasting and Quranic recitation.
content:
Imam Rida (a.s.) narrated from his father Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.), who narrated from his father Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), who narrated from his father Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), who narrated from his father Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.), who narrated from his noble father Sayyidush-Shuhada Imam Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.), who narrated from his father Sayyidul Wasiyyin Amirul Momineen Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) that he said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) addressed us one day and said, 'Ayyuhannas' (O people), 'Innahu qad aqbala ilaykum shahrullahi' (Indeed, the month of Allah has approached you) with blessings, mercy, and forgiveness. This is a month that is superior to all months in the sight of Allah, its days are superior to all days, 'wa layalihi afdalul layali' (and its nights are superior to all nights), and its moments are superior to all moments. 'Huwa shahrun du'itum fihi ila diyafatillah' (It is a month in which you have been invited to the hospitality of Allah) and you have been counted among the honored people. 'Anfasukum fihi tasbihun' (Your breathing in this month is glorification), 'wa nawmukum fihi ibadatun' (and your sleep in it is worship), 'wa amalukum fihi maqbulun' (and your deeds in it will be accepted), 'wa du'aukum fihi mustajabun' (and your supplications in it will be answered). So ask your Lord, who is your Creator, with sincere intentions and pure hearts, for what? 'Ayyuwaffiqakum lisiyamihi' (That He grants you the success to fast in it), 'wa tilawati kitabihi' (and to recite His Book, the Holy Quran). 'Fa innash-shaqiyu' (For who is the wretched and unfortunate one?) 'Man hurima min ghufranillahi fi hadhash-shahril azim' (He who is deprived of Allah's forgiveness in this great month). This is so, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure and purified progeny.

title: Wilaadat e Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Aur Ahle Tasannun Ulama
excerpt: This lecture addresses common doubts regarding the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) by citing historical records from Sunni scholars. The speaker presents evidence from authoritative texts such as 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqah' and 'Wafayat al-A'yan' to confirm the Imam's lineage and birth date. By highlighting these scholarly admissions, the lecture aims to validate the Shia belief in the existence and occultation of the 12th Imam.
content:
So, let us present these references before you and state that these are the facts regarding the birth, which the opponents fill people's minds with doubts about. Let us examine these from their own books to see if your birth truly happened or will happen. I want to present the first reference before you. In 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqah', volume 2, page 601, they write: 'And Abu Muhammad, the son of Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), he did not appoint anyone as his caliph or successor after his son Abu al-Qasim al-Hujjah, and at that time, the age of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) was 5 years.' Let me present the second reference before you, which is from 'Al-Halaq al-Ashrafi' in his book 'Wafayat al-A'yan', volume 4, page 176. Regarding the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), he states—what does he write? 'Abu al-Qasim al-Musawi al-Najafi', and after that, he clearly writes the name of the Imam of Islam there as well, that Muhammad, son of Hasan al-Askari... That he also writes the name of Muhammad, son of Hasan al-Askari, in his book, and he is also writing the name of his father. And he also mentions the name of the Imam of Islam there, and after that, he mentions the name of the father of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), Ali al-Hadi, and then he also writes the name of the father of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), which is 'Amr al-Jawad'. Meaning, there is a lineage of Imamate that he has recorded in this book. And then he further writes that he will be the 12th Imam of the Imami sect, and then he writes, 'Al-Ma'ruf bil-Hujjah' (known as the Hujjah), and then he states that his birth took place on Friday, the middle of Sha'ban, 255 Hijri. And when your father departed from this mortal world, your blessed age was 5 years. Respected audience, not only this, but many such references have been recorded in their books regarding the birth of Mahdi (a.s.) by the scholars of the opponents themselves.

title: Aql aur Akhlaq | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the intrinsic relationship between intellect (Aql) and character (Akhlaq) through the teachings of Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker uses the metaphor of a tree to explain that while intellect remains hidden like roots, it serves as the foundation for the visible fruits of one's manners. By studying the traditions of the Ahlulbayt, believers can nourish their intellect and cultivate superior moral character.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The noble saying of the Master of the Pious, Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is: 'Al-adabu fil insani kashajaratin asluha aql' (Politeness in a human is like a tree whose roots are intellect). We cannot see the roots of a tree. What we see are only the branches, leaves, fruits, and flowers of the tree. Similarly, a person's intellect is not visible, but their manners and character testify to their intellect. Just as it is necessary for the roots to be strong to strengthen a tree, for which the roots need water and sunlight. Water and sunbeams are not delivered to the branches, leaves, fruits, and flowers directly. In the same way, the stronger and more robust a person's intellect is, the better and higher their manners and character will be. Therefore, if we want to improve our manners and character, we must study the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). O God, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) and grant us the good fortune to read and understand the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt-e-Athar (a.s.), through which we may remain attached to the teachings of the family of Muhammad. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: EP26 | Hadees-e-Ghadeer aur Ahle Tasannun Ulama  | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi provides a scholarly analysis of the Hadith-e-Ghadir from the perspective of Sunni academic sources. It systematically refutes historical objections and misinterpretations, demonstrating that the event is supported by mutawatir narrations and documented in canonical Sunni texts. The presentation emphasizes the significance of the Prophet's declaration of Ali ibn Abi Talib as the Mawla, arguing that the historical evidence confirms a formal appointment of authority rather than a mere statement of friendship.
content:
PSR presents. Ashhadu anna Aliyan Waliullah. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila.' O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse their enemies all together. By the status of Muhammad and the pure Progeny. In the series of 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' (Completion of Proof), there was a Hadith, a discussion about Hadith-e-Ghadir. And I submitted to your service that Fakhr-e-Razi objected to Hadith-e-Ghadir, and one of his objections is that he said the Shaykhayn, meaning Bukhari and Muslim, did not record it, to which I responded in the previous episode. Besides that, he says that Abu Dawud Sijistani also criticized it. This statement of his is also wrong. Abu Dawud Sijistani did not criticize Hadith-e-Ghadir anywhere. Not anywhere. His sentence is completely wrong, not correct at all. Rather, the other Sihah, the Sihah al-Sittah, because among the Ahl-e-Tasannun, the other authentic books which are called Sihah al-Sittah, besides Bukhari and Muslim, i.e., Ibn Majah, Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud Sijistani, and Nasa'i, so out of these four, at least Ibn Majah has recorded it, Tirmidhi has recorded it, and Nasa'i has recorded it. They have recorded Hadith-e-Ghadir in their Sunan. So, although briefly, but they have recorded it. So now we present two references from Sunan Ibn Majah to your service, and it is necessary to submit to your service that according to many scholars of Ahl-e-Tasannun, these Sihah al-Sittah are very authentic, the most authentic after the Quran, and whatever is present in them should be accepted. Ibn Hajar Asqalani and Ibn Hajar Makki have written this in their book 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa'. Anyway, let's look at Sunan Ibn Majah, I present two Hadiths to your service. One is Hadith number 116, the other is Hadith number 121. Hadith number 116, which is from Bara ibn Azib, and he says that he narrates the event of Hajjat al-Wida and says that the Prophet stopped everyone, then said, 'Alastu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim?' (Am I not more entitled to the believers than their own selves?) Meaning the Prophet first gave the order for 'Salat-e-Jami'ah', 'Fa-amara as-salata jami'ah fa-akhadha bi-yadi Ali' (Then he ordered the prayer to be gathered, then he took Ali's hand). Then, holding the hand of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), the Prophet asked, 'Alastu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim?' Am I not more entitled to the believers than their own selves? 'Qalu bala' (They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, yes, you are'). Then the Prophet asked again, 'Alastu awla bi-kulli mu'minin min nafsihi?' (Am I not more entitled to every believer than his own self?) 'Qalu bala' (They said, 'Yes, it is true, absolutely true'). No one denied it, no one said, 'No, O Messenger of Allah, it is not like that, no, we also have some authority.' Someone should have said something, brother. But because the Quran had already announced, 'An-Nabiyyu awla bil-mu'minina min anfusihim' (The Prophet is more entitled to the believers than their own selves). So the Prophet was giving the same affirmation again. 'Qala fahadha waliyyu man ana mawlahu' (He said, 'This is the Wali of whomever I am the Mawla of'). 'Fahadha waliyyu hadha ya'ni Ali' (This is the Wali, this means Ali). 'Fahadha waliyyu' (The Prophet held his hand and said this). 'Fahadha waliyyu man ana mawlahu' (Whomever I am the Mawla of, this is his Wali). See, no one left any room. After that, he said, 'Allahumma wali man walahu, Allahumma adi man adahu' (O Allah, be a friend to whoever befriends him, O Allah, be an enemy to whoever opposes him). This is exactly the sentence from Sunan Ibn Majah. 'Allahumma wali man walahu, Allahumma adi man adahu'. O Lord, whoever considers Ali his Mawla, You take him as Your slave, and whoever bears enmity towards Ali, You bear enmity towards him. See, it is completely clear, it is a tradition from Sunan Ibn Majah. After that, Hadith number 121 is also similar, that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says, who is this narrator Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas? 'Qadima Mu'awiya fi ba'di hajjatihi' (Mu'awiya came for Hajj). 'Fa-dakhala alayhi Sa'd' (Sa'd went to him, Sa'd went to meet him, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas). Look, remember, as we have mentioned in a previous episode, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is one of the 'Ashara Mubashara'—the ten people whom Allah gave the glad tidings of Paradise, according to their belief. Among them is this Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. I mentioned to you that Umar ibn Sa'd was also his son, who participated in the killing of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Umar ibn Sa'd is the son of this Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. But he is among the Ashara Mubashara, you must understand. So, this Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas went to meet whom? Muawiya. 'Fadhakaru Aliyan'—the topic of Ali (a.s.) came up. The mention of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) was such that whether one wanted to or not, it would come up. Some people would be happy, while others would turn pale. 'Fadhakaru Aliyan fanala minhu'—Muawiya started speaking ill. Muawiya started speaking ill of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). 'Faghadiba Sa'dun'—Sa'd, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, became angry at Muawiya. 'Are you speaking ill of Ali?' 'Yaqulu hadha lirajulin sami'tu Rasulillahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi yaqulu'—'You are speaking ill of a man about whom I heard the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say: 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa Aliyyun mawlahu'—'Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.' This Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. 'Wa sami'tuhu yaqulu'—and I heard him saying: 'Ya Aliyyu anta minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa'—in the hadith it does not say 'Ya Ali', it says: 'Anta minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiyya ba'di'—'You are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me.' 'Wa sami'tuhu yaqulu'—and I heard him say that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'La u'tiyannar-rayata al-yawma rajulan yuhibbullaha wa rasulahu'—'I will give the banner today to a man whom Allah loves and His Messenger loves.' Now you understand that the man about whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa Aliyyun mawlahu'—of whomsoever I am the Mawla, Ali is his Mawla; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ali, you are to me as Aaron was to Moses'; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that Allah and His Messenger love Ali. After that, if someone curses Ali and speaks ill of him, what should his position be in your view? So, judge this for yourself, decide for yourself. These are all in the books; I am quoting the narration from Sunan Ibn Majah. Now, let me present another reference for you. This was narrated by Hakim al-Nishapuri, and it is a narration of Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Abdullah was the son of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and it is enough to say about him that some people have said he had memorized more hadiths than even his father. This has also been written by people. You can see his virtues in the biographical books; Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, he had so many hadiths memorized. So, Hakim has narrated from him, and one narration is from Zayd ibn Arqam. Zayd ibn Arqam says that when we were returning from the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wida), we reached a place near the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—yes, we do not add 'Aali' (in their books), we reached a place called Ghadir Khumm. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) ordered that the thorns and whatever was there should be cleared, the ground should be cleaned, and everyone should gather under the trees. When the people gathered, a pulpit made of camel saddles was erected. Anyway, in that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) delivered this sermon: 'Ka'anni qad du'itu'—now look, this became a detailed sermon. What Bukhari did not narrate, what Ibn Majah did not narrate, Ahmad ibn Hanbal is narrating it. Is it clear to you? 'Ka'anni qad du'itu'—'It is as if I am being called, soon, soon I will be called,' and who? It is strange, meaning the Angel of Death will come and I will depart from this world. There are different phrases, there are many narrations, very many. 'Fa-ajibu'—I will say 'Labbayk' (I am here) to the call of the Angel of Death. 'Inni taraktu feekum al-thaqalayn'—'I am leaving among you two weighty things, one of them is greater than the other: the Book of Allah the Almighty and my Itrat (progeny). So look at how you treat them after me.' How do you treat them? We have discussed this in detail in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. 'Fa-innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida alayya al-hawd'—'Because these two will not separate until they return to me at the Pond (Hawd al-Kawthar).' Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said—in their view 'sallallahu alayhi wa sallam', but in our view 'sallallahu alayhi wa alihi wa sallam'. You must emphasize the 'Aali', you must emphasize it. Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Innallaha azza wa jalla mawlaya'—'Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, is my Mawla, and I am the Wali of every believer.' Then he took the hand of Ali (r.a.). Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Man kuntu waliyyahu fahadha waliyyuhu'—'Of whomsoever I am the Wali, this is his Wali.' We are repeating the sentence again. 'Man kuntu waliyyahu fahadha waliyyuhu.' So that there is no room for doubt, by holding his hand and saying 'Hadha' (this one), so that there is no room for doubt that we did not see who you were talking about. And showing it like this, 'Hadha waliyyuhu.' 'Allahumma wali man walahu wa adi man adahu.' And then after that, Ahmad ibn Hanbal says that he completed the hadith. Oh, you narrate any hadith. Yes. After narrating this hadith, Hakim says that this hadith meets all the conditions of the 'Shaykhayn' (Bukhari and Muslim). That is, all the conditions of Bukhari and Muslim. Well, do you know who Hakim al-Nishapuri is? His book is 'Al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn'. That is, I am narrating those hadiths that the Shaykhayn did not narrate. That is, those that Bukhari and Muslim did not narrate, I am narrating them. Is it clear? And he says that this hadith has not been narrated in full either. Ahmad ibn Hanbal did not narrate it in full, and what is the proof of this? That the full hadith was narrated by Salama ibn Kuhayl from Abu Tufayl, and that also meets the criteria of the Shaykhayn. He explained it in complete detail. In 'Al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn', page 118, hadith number 4576. 4576 is the hadith number. Now after that, let me present another hadith for you, and this is from Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Sahl al-Qabbani. This was also narrated by Hakim al-Nishapuri, I am presenting it to you only because Hakim al-Nishapuri calls him the 'Imam of the Era in Bukhara'. Who? Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Sahl al-Qabbani. He narrated the full hadith, meaning he narrated this tradition from Zayd ibn Arqam, exactly like the previous hadith, that we were returning from Ghadir Khumm, i.e., from the Farewell Pilgrimage, and when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) reached near Ghadir Khumm, he said that the ground should be cleared and everyone should gather there. After that, he delivered this sermon, and he said it in the sermon. It is the same as the previous hadith, exactly the same. And regarding the reliability of Abu Nasr al-Qabbani, it is enough that Hakim has taken many hadiths from him in his Mustadrak and has mentioned his name with great respect. And called him 'Imam of the Era in Bukhara'. Anyway, let me narrate one more hadith for you, the Hadith of Ghadir, so that there is no room left for it to be rejected in any way. And that is from Abu Awana al-Isfarayini. Shaykh Mahmud Shaykhani Qadri, the author of 'Al-Sirat al-Sawiy', writes that Abu Awana al-Isfarayini narrates the Hadith al-Thaqalayn in his book 'Al-Musnad al-Sahih', and how does he narrate the Hadith al-Thaqalayn? The one I presented to you today, it is the same Zayd ibn Arqam narration, that we were returning from the Farewell Pilgrimage, and after that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said this sentence, and at the end of it is the sentence: 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha waliyyuhu, Allahumma wali man walahu wa adi man adahu.' Abu Tufayl says that I asked Zayd ibn Arqam, 'Did you hear this hadith yourself from the Messenger of Allah?' Zayd said, 'There was no one in that field who did not see this scene with their own eyes and did not hear the words of the Messenger of Allah with their own ears.' And Hafiz Dhahabi has called this hadith 'Sahih' (authentic). So now, who is this Abu Awana? Sam'ani says—Sam'ani is a very great historian of the Ahl al-Tasawwuf who wrote the book 'Al-Ansab'. His book is famous by the name 'Al-Ansab'. In 'Al-Ansab', he writes under 'Isfarayini', Volume 1, page 235, that this Abu Awana Yaqub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Isfarayini was a very great Muhaddith (hadith scholar), and he traveled to different cities, i.e., he went to Iraq, Syria, Sham, Hijaz, Iran, Yemen to collect hadiths, and he collected his 'Al-Mustadrak al-Sahih' in this way. And pay attention to this sentence: the method he used to collect hadiths was like 'Sahih Muslim', 'bi-nahw-e ahsan'—in a better way. 'Bi-nahw-e ahsan', meaning even better than 'Sahih Muslim'. Who is writing this? Sam'ani is writing it in 'Al-Ansab'. 'Bi-nahw-e ahsan', and he was very pious, ascetic, religious, contented; many have written his praises. Similarly, Ibn Khallikan writes in 'Wafayat al-Ayan' that Abu Hafiz Abu Awana was a very great Hafiz whose memory was extraordinary. He had memorized narrations in the thousands and millions, and Abu Abdullah Hakim says that he was an expert in hadiths, a scholar, and was 'Thabit' (firm/reliable), meaning among the most reliable. He traveled to different cities to collect hadiths, and the same thing was written by Dhahabi in 'Tadhkirat al-Huffaz' and 'Al-Ibar', and by Yafi'i in 'Mirat al-Jinan'. Pay attention, Dhahabi also wrote the same thing. Remember the name Dhahabi. Okay? In both his books, 'Tadhkirat al-Huffaz' and 'Al-Ibar', and Yafi'i wrote it in 'Mirat al-Jinan'. Now after that, what did Fakhr al-Razi say? That the hadith is not 'Mutawatir' (mass-transmitted). The Hadith of Ghadir is not Mutawatir. Look, there is a couplet by the poet Mawlawi, Maulana Jalaluddin Rumi, the author of the Masnavi, he says—it is probably his, as far as my memory serves—'Dasht-e chashm baz wa gosh baz wa in ama'—his eyes are open and his ears are open, and yet he is blind. 'Hayrat-e mast chashm-bandi-e khuda'—I am amazed at how Allah blinds people. This is what the Mawlawi says. Now look, the Hadith of Ghadir has been narrated by 110 Companions. Remember, there are references available for every one of them. There is no time, otherwise, one... and if anyone wants a reference for any Companion, i.e., if they want the full list of the 110, that list can also be provided, and if you want, you can refer to the books. Allama Amini has prepared a list of 110 Companions in 'Al-Ghadir'. Al-Ghadir is available in English, Al-Ghadir is in Urdu, Al-Ghadir is in Persian, and Al-Ghadir is in Arabic. Whatever language one knows. Fakhr-e-Razi says it is not mutawatir (consecutive/widely transmitted), it is not mutawatir. Why? Why is it not mutawatir? It just isn't. The hadith is not mutawatir. There is no argument at all. Now, let me present a point for your consideration. Ibn Hazm al-Andalusi, a very prominent Salafi, a very big personality of the Zahiri school of thought, was from Spain. He brings a hadith and says that this hadith is mutawatir. Why is it mutawatir? Because eight companions (Sahaba) have narrated it. Eight companions have narrated it, so therefore it is mutawatir. Did you notice? He said one... 110 companions, and he said 8 companions make it mutawatir. Right? Now take another example. Ibn Hajar Makki writes in Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa, after quoting a hadith, that this hadith is mutawatir. Why is it mutawatir? It is written in Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa, isn't it? Why is it mutawatir? Because 4 companions have narrated it. Now tell me, if 4 narrate it, it is mutawatir; if 8 narrate it, it is mutawatir; sometimes they say if 1 narrates it, it is mutawatir. But 110 companions are announcing the Wilayah of Ali, announcing the Caliphate of Ali without any interval (bila-fasl), and that is not mutawatir? Here, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh) presents a very subtle, very delightful point, Masha'Allah. He says that as you have seen, if 4 companions narrate a hadith, it becomes like a verse of the Quran. That is their standard. So no one can doubt it. And some people say if 8 people narrate it, it is mutawatir, no one can doubt it. Right? So 4 or 8. What is the second standard? Or rather, what is the third standard they mention? That if in every era, scholars have narrated the hadith and accepted it, then that hadith is mutawatir. Now, look, pay attention to one thing. Whatever standard they are setting, there is no foundation for it. That the Prophet said, or that it is in the Quran, or the Prophet said—no, these are things being made up by them. Remember, this is what happens when people leave the 'Gate of the City of Knowledge' (Bab-e-Madinat-ul-Ilm) and go here and there, then this is what happens. Anyway, so if they say that scholars have narrated it, then it is fine. Actually, the entire list is very long regarding how many scholars in which century have narrated it. Allama Amini has recorded it in Al-Ghadir; there is a complete list. Besides that, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi, in that era—meaning he passed away in 1306 Hijri—well, his son was Arjumand, whose name was Nasir-ul-Millat, and he completed this volume of Al-Ghadir. Today, the Ghadir volumes that are printed are in 10 volumes. If more references were added to it, it would be even more. Anyway, Al-Ghadir is just a response to Fakhr-e-Razi and the author of Tuhfa. In other words, what is currently available is approximately 3,000 pages. In 10 volumes, each volume has 300 pages. So if there are 10 volumes, that makes 3,000 pages. The Muhaddith Dehlavi, Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlavi, who refuted it in Tuhfa, used a total of 10 pages for it. So for every page, he used 10 pages of Ghadir. For every page, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh) wrote 300 pages. And all are logical responses. Anyway, time is short, so I will quickly read the list for you of how many scholars—scholars of Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni), there is not a single Shia name in this. As Ibn Athir writes in Al-Nihaya, Muhammad ibn Idris Shafi'i, who passed away in 204 Hijri, narrated this hadith. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who is the Imam of the Hanbali school, passed away in 241 Hijri; he narrated the Hadith-e-Ghadir in his Musnad and also in his book Manaqib. Ibn Majah, the author of Sunan-e-Ibn Majah, who passed away in 273 Hijri, narrated it. Tirmidhi, who passed away in 279 Hijri, it is in Sahih Tirmidhi. Nasa'i in his Khasa'is, 303 Hijri. Abu Ya'la Musuli, who passed away in 307 Hijri, in his Musnad. Baghawi, who is called Muhyi-us-Sunnah. What title was given? Muhyi-us-Sunnah, the one who revives the Sunnah. Mr. Baghawi mentioned the Hadith-e-Ghadir in his Sunan. Dulabi in Al-Kuna wal-Asma, who passed away in 320 Hijri, did so. Al-Tahawi, a very great scholar, in his book Mushkil al-Athar, passed away in 321 Hijri, he narrated it. Hakim in his Musnad, Hakim passed away in 405 Hijri, he did so in his book Al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn. This list is very long. I have just quickly mentioned 10 names for you. 10 names for you. And this list does not end. Did you notice? The interesting thing about this is that if you look at the response of the scholars of Ahl-e-Tasannun, you will see that in every matter, they definitely take the support of Dhahabi. That Dhahabi in his book, for example, Tadhkirat al-Huffaz, or Dhahabi in the book Al-Ibar, or Dhahabi in the book Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, or Dhahabi in the book Mizan al-I'tidal, or Dhahabi in his book Siyar A'lam al-Nubala. All these books by Dhahabi are on Rijal (biographical evaluation) because he was a tremendous expert in Rijal. Well, because he was also a bit extremist. Extremist means he had some enmity towards Shias, some hatred, malice, stubbornness; he had enmity towards Shias. That is why there is a bit more respect for him among them. That is why there is a bit more respect. So Dhahabi, this very Dhahabi—that is why in everything, 'Dhahabi said, Dhahabi said, Dhahabi said, Dhahabi said.' Now Dhahabi says that the Hadith-e-Ghadir is authentic (mu'tabar), it is mutawatir. The Hadith-e-Ghadir is mutawatir. So why are you not taking the support of Dhahabi here? Take the support of Dhahabi. Anyway, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi, even after reaching this point, says that truly, the way these people have abandoned the support of Dhahabi here, it seems a verse of the Quran was revealed regarding them: 'Wa-alladhina la yu'minuna fi adhanihim waqrun wa-huwa 'alayhim 'ama' (And those who do not believe, it is as if they have become both deaf and blind). 'Ula'ika yunadawna min makanin ba'id' (They are those who are called from a far place). They are called from a far place because they neither hear nor see, nothing at all. And what have you? Now, as for the verses, the verse of Surah Al-Ma'idah which I mentioned to you earlier: 'Ya ayyuha al-rasulu balligh ma unzila ilayka min rabbika...' (O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord...). This is one. The second verse, Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse number 3: 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum...' (This day I have perfected for you your religion...). Three, the first verse of Surah Al-Ma'arij: 'Sa'ala sa'ilun bi-'adhabin waqi'in' (A questioner asked about a punishment bound to happen). And besides this, look, these are the three verses that are usually quoted. So look, let me submit to you that only these three verses were not revealed on the day of Ghadir; it is not just in honor of Ghadir, but there are 21 verses in honor of Ghadir. Although this is among Shia scholars. But at least the scholars of Ahl-e-Tasannun accept that these three verses are in honor of Ghadir, and if anyone wants to see, they are present in their books of Tafsir (exegesis), the books of Tafsir. If they want to see, they can refer to those books. Time is short, but still, if Allah grants the ability, I will try to mention just a few Tafsirs so that the matter becomes clear to people. So if you wish, you can refer to the books of Tafsir or other books. I will present a few examples for you. Al-Durr al-Manthur is the Tafsir of Suyuti, Jalaluddin Suyuti, Hafiz Jalaluddin Suyuti. There is the history of Khatib al-Baghdadi, and they have narrated this tradition from Abu Hurairah. Then there is the Manaqib of Ibn Maghazili, the Tarikh-e-Dimashq of Ibn Asakir; this Tarikh-e-Dimashq, Tarikh-o-Madinat-ul-Dimashq is in 80 volumes. In it, he has narrated the entire event. Then there is another Tafsir by Suyuti, Hafiz Jalaluddin Suyuti has another Tafsir, its name is Al-Itqan. Then there is Al-Manaqib of Khatib al-Khwarizmi, then Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah of Ibn Kathir, then Yanabi' al-Mawadda of Al-Qunduzi Hanafi, and Hafiz Nu'aym, Hafiz Abu Nu'aym's Nuzul al-Quran. In it, he has narrated the tradition from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. And in this way, the list is very long. Those who are interested and want to go into detail can refer to Al-Ghadir by Allama Amini or other books that are present; all references are available, you can see. So anyway, in summary, this event of Ghadir is one that no one can deny. Except for one who is prejudiced and whose heart is filled with hatred for the Ahl-e-Bayt. And this event, the Hadith-e-Ghadir—the event of Ghadir is where the Prophet announced the Caliphate without interval (bila-fasl) and Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (alayhis-salam). As I have already submitted to you that people argue over the word 'Mawla' that the Prophet only announced friendship, so you know that such arrangements are not made for friendship that... The entire caravan is stopped, one hundred thousand people are gathered, and then this announcement is made. This is not done for friendship. And what is friendship? The Quran has already said that the believers are brothers to one another. 'Innama al-mu'minuna ikhwah.' When they are brothers, then friendship is something less than that. So here, the talk is about being brothers, and the believers are brothers to one another. And the formula of brotherhood (sigha-e-ukhuwwat) had also been recited. The formula of brotherhood had been recited in Masjid-e-Nabawi. So then, when they had already become brothers, where would friendship come from? Therefore, all these arguments against Ghadir are very childish and they only point to a person's hatred for the Ahl-e-Bayt. Nothing more than that. So if a person is a seeker of truth, if he is searching for the truth, if he wants the truth and is not prejudiced, then he has no choice but to accept this truth. 'Aliyun ma'al-haqq wal-haqqu ma'a Ali.' Allahumma adir al-haqqa haythu ma dara. Wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi al-tayyibin al-tahirin, al-ma'sumin al-mazlumin, wal-la'natu al-da'imu ala a'da'ihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri faza'ilihim wa manaqibihim wa mukhalifi aqwalihim wa ahkamihim wa ma'arifihim.

title: Aashur Ke Din Duniyaawi Kaamon Se Parhez Karein | Imam Reza (a.s.) Ki Taqeed
excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual significance of Ashura as emphasized by Imam Reza (a.s.). It advises believers to abstain from worldly pursuits and focus on mourning and grief to honor the tragedy of Karbala. The discourse warns against treating the day as one of celebration, noting the severe spiritual consequences for those who do so.
content:
Hazrat Imam Rida (a.s.) stated: 'Whoever refrains from seeking their worldly needs on the day of Ashura, the Almighty will fulfill their worldly and hereafter needs. For whoever makes the day of Ashura a day of sorrow, grief, and weeping, Allah will make the Day of Judgment a day of joy and happiness for him. His eyes will find coolness in Paradise by looking at us. But whoever considers the day of Ashura a day of blessing and brings something new into their house, there will be no blessing in it, and on the Day of Judgment, he will be gathered with Yazid and Ubaidullah and will be in the lowest pit of Hell.'
Refraining from worldly tasks on Ashura leads to divine fulfillment of needs.
Mourning and weeping on Ashura brings joy on the Day of Judgment.
Those who grieve for Imam Hussain (a.s.) will find solace in Paradise.
Treating Ashura as a day of blessing or celebration is spiritually condemned.
Bringing new items into the home on Ashura is discouraged.
Those who celebrate Ashura will be gathered with the oppressors of the Ahlulbayt.
The day of Ashura is strictly for sorrow and remembrance of the tragedy.

title: Ep#16 | Zuhoor Ke Liye Sab Se Zyaada Kya Zaroori Hai?
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the vital importance of praying for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) as a primary responsibility for believers. Drawing from traditions in 'Al-Kafi' and 'Bihar al-Anwar', the speaker explains that prayer acts as both a weapon and a shield for the faithful. By citing the historical example of the Bani Israel, the lecture illustrates how collective, sincere prayer can accelerate divine intervention and hasten the Imam's return.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wa ahlik 'aduwwahum ajma'in. Respected audience, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. We are in the era of the Imam of the Time (a.s.), and in this era, we have responsibilities. Among these responsibilities, the most important one is to pray for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). May Allah hasten his reappearance. As the Imam of the Time (a.s.) himself has stated: 'Pray abundantly for my reappearance, for in it lies your own well-being.' And if a person loves someone and cannot do anything for them, they at least pray for them. It has come in traditions that prayer is the weapon of the believer. Sheikh Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni (r.a.) has included a specific chapter in his book 'Al-Kafi', volume 2, in which he narrates five hadiths. The name of that chapter is 'Bab al-Du'a Silah al-Mu'min'. In it, he narrates that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)... The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states: 'Prayer is the weapon of the believer, the pillar of religion, and the light of the heavens and the earth.' In the second hadith, this hadith is from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), where he states: 'Prayer is the shield of the believer.' On the battlefield, when a person fights, they use a weapon to attack the enemy in front of them and use a shield for their protection. Here, prayer has been compared to both—meaning, in one place it is called the weapon of the believer, and in another place, it is called a shield. And there is a narration from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) where he states: 'Should I not inform you of the weapon of the Prophets (a.s.)?' It was asked to the Imam (a.s.), 'What is the weapon of the Prophets (a.s.)?' The Imam (a.s.) replied: 'Prayer. Prayer is...' The Imam (a.s.) replied: 'Prayer is the weapon of the Prophets (a.s.).' A person uses a weapon for their protection, and they use it when they need it the most, and they rely on it completely. And why shouldn't a person rely on prayer? Because the Almighty states in the Holy Quran: 'Call upon Me, I will answer you.' A person takes the help of prayer for even their smallest needs, so the Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is not just a human; he is the greatest need of humanity. So why should we not take the help of this prayer and pray for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.)? Now, those who do not consider praying enough, according to them, nothing will happen just by praying, so we request those individuals to reflect on this tradition. This incident is from the time of Musa (a.s.), and this tradition has been recorded by Allama Majlisi (r.a.) in his book 'Bihar al-Anwar', and this is from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states that when the Bani Israel became old in their state, they cried out in the court of Allah for 40 days. Allah then revealed to Musa (a.s.) and Harun (a.s.) to go and save the Bani Israel from the evil of Pharaoh. Thus, 170 years were reduced from their punishment. Then Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'Your situation is similar. If you do this, Allah will grant you this, but if you do not do this, then this matter (the reappearance) will be delayed.' In this graph, you explained how Allah, due to the prayers of the Bani Israel, reduced 170 years from their punishment and saved them from the oppression of Pharaoh through Musa (a.s.). Similarly, if we pray from our hearts to Allah (s.w.t.), Allah will surely... Allah will surely hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). And finally, we all pray together in the court of Allah... that Allah hastens the reappearance of our Imam and includes us among his helpers. [Prayer/Dua]...
