title: Majlis 3 | Ahle Bait (a.s.) Haadi Hain | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the divine role of the Ahlulbayt as spiritual guides and the necessity of aligning one's character with their teachings. The discourse emphasizes that true faith requires both the recognition of Wilayah and the practical application of moral conduct, such as gentleness and avoiding unnecessary argumentation. The session culminates in a poignant reflection on the sacrifice of Ali Akbar at Karbala, illustrating the ultimate devotion to the Imam of the time.
content:
They draw the likeness of the Imam of the Age, they draw the likeness of the Imam of the Age, in imagination, they draw the picture of the soul, they draw the likeness of the Imam of the Age. They have bought land for the sake of shrines, they have bought land for the sake of shrines, on the earth, they draw the signs of the martyrs, they draw the signs of the martyrs. Sakina cries out, 'Help, O Father,' Sakina cries out, 'Help, O Father,' the oppressors are pulling my earrings, the oppressors are pulling my earrings. Akbar said, weeping, 'O pain, stop,' Akbar said, weeping, 'O pain, stop,' do not pull the father from the chest, do not pull the father from the chest. A'udhu billahi al-sami'i al-'alimi min al-shaytani al-rajim. Bismillah al-rahman al-rahim. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'aliyyi al-'azim. Hasbunallahu wa ni'ma al-wakil. Ni'ma al-mawla wa ni'ma al-nasir. Alhamdu lillahi rabbil 'alamin. Wal-'aqibatu li-ahlil taqwa wal-yaqin. Wa al-salatu wa al-salamu 'ala ashrafi al-anbiya'i wa al-mursalin, habibi ilahi al-'alamin, Abi al-Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Salla Allahu 'alayhi wa alihi al-ma'sumin alladhina adhhaba Allahu 'anhumu al-rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Siyyama baqiyyati Allahi fi al-aradinin, imami zamanina wa waliyyi amrina wa sahibina wa mawlana wa habibina wa tabibina wa anisina wa munisina al-kafiri hasinin wa ghiyathi mudtarri mustaghithi, ruhi wa arwahu al-'alamina lahu al-fida'. Amma ba'du, faqad qala Allahu tabaraka wa ta'ala fi kitabihi al-karim, wa qawluhu al-haqqu wa huwa asdaqu al-qa'ilin: 'Khudhi al-'afwa wa'mur bil-'urfi wa a'rid 'an al-jahilin.' Sadaqa Allahu al-'aliyyu al-'azim. Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. In this noble verse, Allah Ta'ala is commanding that O Prophet, make forgiveness and pardon your way, make it your habit, forgive the people. People, (a.s.), leave people's mistakes alone, meaning do not sit around dwelling on the mistakes of others, and treat people with great gentleness, very great gentleness. I have presented verses to you in your service before this, 'wa'mur bil-urfi' (and enjoin what is right), and always enjoin goodness, just enjoin goodness, keep doing good. 'Wa'mur bil-urfi' and it was submitted, 'urf' means 'ma'ruf'. 'Ma'ruf' means goodness, and I am repeating 'ma'ruf' again and again so that the matter is well preserved in your noble minds. 'Ma'ruf' means that thing which the intellect says is correct. The intellect says it is correct, and the intellect finds pleasure in doing that act. That is why an example was presented before you that the Imam said, 'Look, do not just look at prayer, fasting, or Hajj, look at all these things; when he speaks, does he speak the truth or not, and does he act with honesty and trustworthiness or not?' This itself is a very vast topic, so we do not need to go into the details of it right now, and the third thing is 'wa'rid 'anil-jahilin' (and turn away from the ignorant), meaning do not argue with the ignorant for no reason, do not talk to them, do not get entangled with them. Because no benefit is going to come from getting entangled with the ignorant. Even if you are right, still, no. That is why in our traditions, one thing is strictly forbidden; it is called 'mira' in the traditions. 'Mira' means arguing for no reason. It is strictly forbidden. Meaning, ethically, (a.s.), ethically it is haram; ethically, not religiously, but ethically, meaning the intellect strictly forbids it. You have to present your point, present your point, and after that, do not talk further. If someone says, as there is a saying in Arabic, 'in qulta fa-aqulu' (if you say this, then I will say that), if you say this, then I will say that, if you say this, then I will say that—this is called 'mira'. Arguing for no reason, remaining entangled for no reason, this is haram. What is the tradition in this, what is the hadith? That 'utrukil-mira wa law kunta muhiqqa' (abandon 'mira', meaning do not argue for no reason, even if you are on the truth). Even if you are right, one hundred percent right. You present your viewpoint; if the person in front understands, then good; if they do not understand, it does not matter. Brother, I have presented my point; if you want to accept it, then accept it; if you do not want to accept it, then do not. There is no benefit in arguing for no reason. So that is why it says 'wa'rid 'anil-jahilin'. And the verse of Surah Al-Furqan that was recited before you, that 'Ibadur-Rahman alladhina yamshuna 'alal-ardi hawna wa idha khatabahumul-jahiluna qalu salama' (The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace'). Meaning, the servants of Allah are those who walk on the earth with humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say 'Assalamu Alaikum'. Meaning, they do not clash with the ignorant, they do not argue with the ignorant. They have no concern with the ignorant. Now look, this strategy, actually these are three words of this verse, right? This is a strategy. If you reflect on this. Meaning, Allah is telling this to Rasulullah (s.a.w.a.). Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum. You are Rahmat-ul-lil-'Alamin (a mercy to the worlds). You have to do tabligh (preaching). Look, we will, Insha'Allah, present each point in your service. You see how the Prophet dealt with things and how he practically acted upon this verse. Because Rasulullah was not someone who only spoke with his tongue, no, but practically, and anyway, in our Islam, look at this too, this is also a matter of intellect, and every... Whoever accepts it, whether they are Hindu, Muslim, of any religion, of any faith. That every... look, there is a proverb in English too, right? They say, 'Practice what you preach'. And the Mawla's hadith is even more powerful than this. Because what can be said about them. Now look at the sentence, it says, 'Ad-da'i bila 'amalin kal-rami bila watarin' (The one who invites without action is like the archer without a bowstring). The one who gives an invitation without action is like someone who does archery without a bow. If someone throws an arrow like this, pulling and hitting, will anything happen from that? Similarly, if someone is doing tabligh without acting upon it themselves, it is just like... now people do not understand bows and arrows, so understand a gun, a pistol, right? Its bullet. So instead of a gun, if you pull and throw the bullet with your hand, nothing is going to happen. Nothing is going to happen. No matter how much you speak, it is evident, right? The Prophet showed everything by doing it practically, Insha'Allah, we will present it in your service. So this was what? This was a strategy that Allah gave through a verse, through verse number 199 of Surah Al-A'raf, Allah told the Prophet that you have to do these three things. And this has to be done in every stage of life. And you have to treat all people in this way. 'Khudh-il-'afwa' (Take to forgiveness), keep forgiving. Look at this, this is such a powerful thing. And generally, we are saying, apart from this Quranic verse, look, adopt this in your life. Do not think much at all. Whoever has done bad to you, whoever has done very bad, do not even mention them. Just look at this—we are talking about ourselves—that we should see how we can make ourselves better. That is it. What he did, what he is doing, who he is, it has no meaning. Rather, we will submit one more step in your service, that if someone is doing bad to you, then as much as he is working against you, work that much harder to make yourself better, so that as much as he is working on you, you work more on yourself so that he himself admits defeat in the end. He himself gives up. Therefore, keep constantly improving yourself. What strategy did Allah make for the Prophet, (a.s.), what strategy did He give? And this is why you must read Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah Kabirah. This is the emphasis of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) emphasized this a lot, he said, 'Al-Jami'ah, Al-Jami'ah, Al-Jami'ah', read Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah. We especially tell the youth, look, nowadays, Alhamdulillah, you have all the facilities. You have these apps that come, what do they call that English app, 'Divine Pearls'? Excellent, those children, Zahid Bhai's sons, both of them, the Azani brothers, what, Masha'Allah, may Allah increase their success. Right? Truly, youth should be like this, look, they did a great job. So you see, Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah is in 'Divine Pearls'. It is concise, not too long, if this... of course, it is a little long, but if you cannot read half of it at once, read it for five or ten minutes. You will see that slowly you will have a good command over it, and you must read its translation. Now look, we will present its opening words in your service, and we will emphasize one word a little more. That Ziyarat starts like this. Oh, one more thing, the first time this Ziyarat was recorded was by Sheikh Saduq in his book 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih'. Sheikh Saduq recorded it in 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', and you know that 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih' is among our Kutub-e-Arba (the Four Books), among our four books. Four books: one is Al-Kafi, the second is 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', the third is Al-Istibsar, and the fourth is Tahdhib al-Ahkam. These are the four important books. Out of them, this is one book, 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih'. Do you know what Sheikh Saduq writes at the beginning of this book? You should know this. Sheikh Saduq writes that I declare all the hadiths of this book, whatever hadith I have recorded, as a proof (hujjah) between me and Allah. That whatever hadith I have recorded, all are authentic. This entire guarantee is mine; if there is anything in it about which there is doubt, then on the Day of Judgment, he can catch my garment, he can question me. Sheikh Saduq is saying this with a full guarantee. 'Hujjah' means exactly this. My full guarantee, 100% my guarantee. Sheikh Saduq, right? Sheikh Saduq is not an ordinary man, yes. Do not take Sheikh Saduq lightly. Sheikh Saduq's title is 'Ra'is al-Muhaddithin' (Chief of the Hadith Scholars), the chief of the hadith scholars. He is a very great personality, a very great personality. Meaning, if we talk about him now, for that, a separate topic, meaning a separate gathering is needed, if we only talk about Sheikh Saduq. Anyway, he recorded this Ziyarat-e-Jami'ah in 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih'. Its opening sentences are like this, the beginning sentence: 'Assalamu 'alaikum ya Ahl-e-Bayt-in-Nubuwwah' (Peace be upon you, O family of Prophethood). 'Ahl-e-Bayt' means family. O family of Prophethood, 'wa mawdi' ar-risalah' (and the place of the Message). It is strange, every word is very strange, yes. 'Mawdi' ar-risalah', meaning that place where the Risalah (Message) is found. 'Mawdi'' means place. That place where the Risalah, meaning Allah's Messenger, is there, right? Allah's message is found there. 'Mawdi' ar-risalah', 'wa mukhtalaf al-mala'ikah' (and the place where angels frequent). And the Ahl-e-Bayt are those where angels come and go. Angels come and go. Meaning, the angels are the servants of the Ale-Muhammad. The angels are the servants of the Ale-Muhammad. Someone asked the Mawla-e-Kainat (Ali), 'Are the angels servants of the Ahl-e-Bayt?' The Imam said, 'They are the servants of our Shias, what are you talking about us?' Recite a Salawat on Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad. And do not consider this very difficult, it is a very... a great status of the Shias. The servants of the Shias, 'Mala'ikatu khuddamu shi'atina' (The angels are the servants of our Shias). You can take service from the angels. It is just that a person should have the capability of how to take work from servants. Recite a Salawat on Muhammad and Ale-Muhammad. We are that household, 'mahbat al-wahy' (the place where revelation descends), where revelation descends. 'Hubut-e-Wahy' happens. 'Hubut-e-Wahy' happens. And 'wa ma'dan ar-rahmah' (and the mine of mercy), we are those who are the treasure of Allah's mercy. They are the mines of Allah's mercy. 'Mines' meaning the source. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the mines of Allah's mercy. If you want Allah's mercy, come to the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This is how the discourse begins. Then a phrase comes: "wa-sāsat al-ʿibād" (the caretakers of the servants). This is the topic we are discussing. What is Ahlulbayt? "Sāsat al-ʿibād". 'Sāsa' in Arabic is the plural of 'sā'is'. You use this word in Urdu very frequently. It comes from 'siyāsat' (politics/governance). In Arabic, when we say 'siyāsat', it does not mean politics in the modern sense. In Arabic, 'siyāsat' means to organize all the affairs of the servants. We organize all the affairs of the servants. Ahlulbayt, for the servants of Allah—look, pay attention to the sentence, pay attention to the words. Ahlulbayt, because their knowledge—it is narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.), it is narrated from the Imam, the Imam says: 'By Allah, if our obedience were not obligatory upon you, if it were not a duty upon you, you would not even be worthy of us letting you stand at our door.' The Imam says this while swearing by Allah. If our obedience were not obligatory. And then, listen to what the Imam says next, listen to the words of the Imam. The Imam says: 'We do not say anything based on our own opinion' (lā naqūlu bi-raʾyinā). We do not say anything from our own hearts, meaning not out of desire. Rather, we only say what has been given to us as knowledge from Allah. No, this applies to all the Ahlulbayt, whose speech is only through Ilm-e-Ghayb (knowledge of the unseen), while the speech of other people is based on their own thoughts, their own conjectures. And that is why the difference is that Ilm-e-Ghayb is light (noor), and the words of others are darkness (zulmat). This is the difference between light and darkness. This is a very important point. The Imam says we only speak that which is true. So, the Imam organizes all things, in every way, "sāsat al-ʿibād", and this is solely based on Ilm-e-Ghayb, through Ilm-e-Ghayb. So the Imam says, what is the responsibility of the Imam? To guide the people. Remember, (a.s.) guide the people. In every situation, whether they have outward authority or not, it makes no difference. Look, I am presenting a very important sentence for your consideration. What happened after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? After the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, some people sat in the place of Ali (a.s.). They thought that since they got the government, they were now in power and everything was theirs. Now, I present two lines of Sibte Jafar for your consideration. Sibte Jafar says: 'You seated strangers on your throne, O deputy of Mustafa, manifestation of Majesty. You remained Ali, the Wali, and the Successor; what deficiency could ever come to your status?' Would any deficiency come to the status of Ali? What is this worldly government? What is its value in the eyes of Ali? The Master of the Universe himself says this in many places in Nahj al-Balagha, which is a separate topic, God willing. Yes. So, people thought that this government was everything. They sat there. And after that, what did they do? When 100-200 years passed, they even changed the definition of Imamate. We don't need to go into their definition of Imamate right now. We are just giving a hint. They created a definition of Imamate from their own side, and what was it? "Al-Imamatu"—what is Imamate? Imamate is the name of government. "Ar-riyāsah"—what is Imamate? It is leadership. "Caliphate of the Prophet in the affairs of religion and the world." In worldly affairs, "Innal-imāmata riyāsatun ʿāmmatun fī umūrid-dīni wad-dunyā"—Imamate means government, that's it. They thought that with this definition, they were perfectly correct. And after that, they added a little more. Now, when they said that, if someone becomes an Imam through power, you cannot remove him, even if he is a transgressor (fāsiq) and a sinner (fājir). Now, the children won't understand 'fāsiq' and 'fājir'. Because our children don't understand these things at all. So, we explain it in their language. Meaning, even if he is a drunkard, it's fine. Even if he is a debauched person, it's fine. Even if he is a hedonist, it's fine, but he is the Imam. This became their definition. Now they say, 'Brother, (a.s.).' How brother? What is it? No, he just came into power, so 'nahnu maʿa man ghalaba' (we are with whoever wins). I have presented this briefly for your consideration. But the Ahlulbayt are not like that. How are the Ahlulbayt? What is their aim? What is their purpose? It is to guide the people. In every situation, in every condition, to guide them. Whether the Ahlulbayt are in power or not. The only condition is: This is important. What is the condition? The condition is that you go to the door of the Ahlulbayt. Go to the door of the Ahlulbayt. That is why the Prophet said: "The likeness of the Imam is the likeness of the Kaaba." People go to the Kaaba; the Kaaba does not go to anyone, saying, 'I am coming to your house, you perform Hajj right there.' No, no. We have to go to the Kaaba. Similarly, we should go to the door of the Imam. When we go to the door of the Imam, we can benefit from the Imam. And understand what 'benefiting' means, because there are many people who say different things, so we will only present to you from the Hadith. Nothing but Hadith. If you have anything other than this, bring the Hadith to us. Look, we are only talking about the Quran and Hadith. Yes, brother. That person is saying this, that person is saying that—for us, it is no proof. Even if that person is very great, even if he is very great, he is not equal to the sandals of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). That is why a man came to the Imam and said, 'I cannot connect with you.' Connection means contact. 'I cannot meet you, and I have needs.' What should I do? How should I do it? What sentence did the Imam say? Look, I am telling all the children, remember this. Always stay connected to your Imam. Never forget your Imam. In every situation, whatever your condition may be. Listen to the sentence, listen to the words. He said: 'Just move your lips, for the answer will come to you.' Now, here, the answer does not mean that someone will come directly and speak; that is the answer. No. Allah will create a means. Allah will create a way, show a method through which the message reaches you. So, I presented this for your consideration. Now, before moving forward, let me mention one more very important point. Look, sometimes we have a tremendous spirit of propagation (tabligh) among some of our people, and it should be there, it is a good thing. But sometimes its direction changes a little. And some people become so much about prayer and fasting—what do you call it? They become angels; they become so attached to prayer that they are ready to sacrifice Wilayah for the sake of prayer. They are ready to sacrifice the love of Ahlulbayt. Now, I will tell you a small incident, and after that, I will present the proof for it from the Hadith. Look, sometimes we have some zakireen (speakers) among us—not all, but some—who say that if you are coming to the Majlis and, for example, not praying, your coming to the Majlis is useless. There is no benefit in coming to the Majlis. And they address the women, saying, 'If you are coming without hijab, your coming to the Majlis is useless.' You must have heard this. I don't know if you have heard it or not, but I have heard it, and I have heard it a lot. Allah says in the Quran regarding such things: "Yā ayyuhalladhīna āmanū idhā qīla lakum tafassaḥū"—this is a verse of the Quran, a verse of Surah Al-Mujadilah. "Idhā qīla lakum tafassaḥū fil-majālisi fafsaḥū yafsaḥillāhu lakum"—O you who believe, when you are told to make space in the Majlis, then make space; Allah will make space for you. This is a verse of the Quran, yes, a verse of Surah Al-Mujadilah. Recite one more Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. So, a companion came to Imam Sadiq (a.s.), and the Imam's tablecloth was spread, so the Imam told him to come and sit as well. So he sat down; there was no one else except him. But someone was poking him in the elbow. So he said, "Yabna Rasulillah" (O son of the Messenger of Allah), there is no one here, so who is poking me in the elbow? He said, 'These are the angels who struggle to sit at our tablecloth.' So, in the same way, to come to the gathering of Zahra (s.a.), Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. It is found in the narrations. It is in the narrations, and this is a Hadith narrated by Allama Majlisi in Bihar al-Anwar. Here is the story of Prophet Musa (a.s.) and Qarun. You know that Qarun was the cousin of Prophet Musa, upon whom the divine punishment descended. The divine punishment descended. So, when this punishment was descending upon Qarun—this narration is present in Bihar al-Anwar, yes—at that time, Qarun received the news—it was likely a Barzakhi punishment—Qarun received the news that Prophet Musa had passed away. Or Prophet Musa or Prophet Harun, I don't remember exactly, but one of the two, one of the two brothers. Or Prophet Musa or Prophet Harun passed away. So Qarun said, "Wa asafā ʿalā āli ʿImrān"—meaning "Wa asafā" is used in Arabic for mourning. Meaning, it is used to express sorrow. 'Alas, the sorrow that a son of the family of Imran—Imran was the name of Prophet Musa's father—has passed away.' Because Imran was the uncle of Qarun, and this Harun was his cousin. So, 'Alas, he has passed away.' 'Alas, he has passed away.' The sorrow he expressed—Allah liked this gesture of Qarun so much that Allah stopped Qarun's punishment for that duration. So the proof is, now compare Qarun and Prophet Musa and Imam Hussain (a.s.); can there be any comparison? Can there be any comparison? There can be no comparison. Meaning, where is Prophet Musa and where is Imam Hussain (a.s.)? And no matter how bad we are, we are not worse than Qarun. We are not worse than Qarun. So, if Allah can stop the punishment of Qarun, then if Allah forgives the sins of someone who weeps for Hussain, what is there to be surprised about? So, do not say such things. Do not say such things. Always look—meaning, never mix the beliefs (aqaid), the Wilayah, with any branch of religion (furu-e-deen). Meaning, beliefs, the roots of religion (usul-e-deen), and Wilayah have their own special place, and deeds have their own place. This does not mean that one should not perform deeds, yes. One should perform deeds, one should pray, one should fast. It is very important, and if someone intentionally does not pray, it is possible that his intentional abandonment of prayer, fasting, and obligations might take him outside of Wilayah. This is also possible. It is also possible that he becomes distant from the Ahlulbayt. And it is possible that he becomes an enemy of the Ahlulbayt; that is also possible. Therefore, all these acts of worship are very necessary. They are very essential, and that is why there is a very famous Hadith where the Imam says: "Man kāna lillāhi muṭīʿan fahuwa lanā waliyyun"—whoever obeys Allah is our friend, our lover. "Wa man kāna lillāhi ʿāṣiyan fahuwa lanā ʿaduwwun"—and whoever disobeys Allah is our enemy. Therefore, never consider prayer and fasting lightly. But as I presented to you yesterday, what is 'Ma'ruf' (the good)? Ma'ruf is to keep every thing in its place. Yesterday, I presented to you: what is the definition of justice (adl)? To keep every thing in its place. I would like to present an incident for your consideration, but since time is short, God willing, tomorrow I will tell this whole incident. This incident is a bit long, but it is very important for the children to know. This incident is called the Incident of Aqaba. If Allah grants the opportunity and life until tomorrow, then tomorrow I will present this event in your service, explaining when it occurred and what transpired in it. Insha'Allah, if Allah grants the opportunity. Today, in your service, I will first mention a martyr of Karbala whose name was Muslim ibn Awsaja. You know that Muslim ibn Awsaja was a very elderly man, very old, and yesterday I mentioned an old man. When this Muslim ibn Awsaja was martyred, his soul was departing. As his soul was departing, Habib ibn Mazahir came to him. And after coming, he asked, "Yā Muslimu hal laka min al-waṣiyyah?" (O Muslim, O Muslim ibn Awsaja, do you have any will?) So he said, while his soul was departing, he pointed towards Imam Hussain (a.s.) and said, "Uṣīka bi-hādhā" (I entrust you with him). Look, both of them—Muslim has just been martyred, and in a little while, Habib is also going to be martyred. But he is making a will not to forget the Imam. Do you want to know the faith of Muslim? When the night of Ashura came, Imam Hussain (a.s.) called all his companions and told everyone that whoever wants to leave should leave. To the extent that he addressed Muslim directly, and said, "Muslim, you are an old man, this is not your age anymore,"—we are speaking in our own words—"just go, let it be. Where will you fight now?" Listen to Muslim's reply. This should be our reply for the service of our Imam. For the service of our Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), this should be our reply. The Imam—meaning Muslim says, "Anaḥnu nukhallīka?" (Should I leave you alone? Abandon you?) "Wa bimā naʿtadhiru ilā Allāh?" (And what excuse will I present before Allah?) "Min adāʾi ḥaqqika" (When Allah asks me if I fulfilled the right of my Imam of the time or not?) In Dua-e-Nudba, you say exactly this, "Wa aʿinnā ʿalā taʾdiyati ḥuqūqihi ilayh" (Help us, O Lord, so that we may fulfill the rights of the Imam of the time). This is a sentence from Dua-e-Nudba. Recite Dua-e-Nudba every Friday. Recite Dua-e-Nudba. Muslim says this, Muslim ibn Awsaja, "Lā wa Allāh" (No, by God, by God, I will not leave you), "Ḥattā aksira fī ṣudūrihim rumḥī" (Until I thrust my spear into their chests). Look at the passion. "Wa aḍribahum bi-sayfī mā thabata qāʾimuhu fī yadī" (And I will fight them with my sword as long as its hilt remains in my hand). This is the strength to hold the sword, right? Until that time, I will keep fighting them with the sword. "Wa lā ufāriquka" (And I will not leave you for even a single moment). For a single moment. "Wa law lam yakun maʿī silāḥ" (And even if I have no spear, no sword, nothing) "uqātiluhum, uqātiluhum bihi" (with which I could fight), then "la-qadhaftuhum bi-l-ḥijārah" (I will fight them with stones). I will keep fighting with stones, "Thumma lam ufāriq ḥattā amūta maʿak" (Then I will not leave you until I die with you). Look, look at the passion. For a single moment. Come, do we talk to our Imam-e-Zamana like this? Do we talk to our Imam-e-Zamana like this? Think about it. So, this sentence was whose? Muslim ibn Awsaja. Now after that, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, "Wa kunta awwala man sharā nafsahu" (O Muslim, you were the first among the martyrs of Karbala who gave his life). "Wa awwala shahīdin min shuhadāʾi Allāhi qaḍā naḥbahu" (And you were the first martyr among the martyrs of Allah who fulfilled his vow). "Fa-fuzta wa rabbi-l-kaʿbah" (By the Lord of the Kaaba, Muslim, you have succeeded). Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, and after that says, "Shakara Allāhu istiqdāmaka wa muwāsātaka imāmaka" (May Allah reward you for how you stood by your Imam and were martyred in front of your Imam). May Allah shower mercy upon you, O Muslim ibn Awsaja. These are the sentences of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). This that I am reciting in your service, this is in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 98, this is the complete Ziyarat, the complete Ziyarat of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in which the Imam has taken the name of each martyr. By taking the names, it becomes known that the martyrs who were in Karbala, the Imam took the name of each one. So yesterday also I mentioned Anas in your service, Anas ibn Harith al-Kahili al-Asadi, and today it is Muslim ibn Awsaja. Now you think, I am presenting this in your service because when these companions of the Imam, who were outsiders, had this passion to be sacrificed for the Imam, then think about what passion must have been in the one who was the Imam's own son? Just understand that as soon as the Imam said, "Taqaddam yā bunayya ʿAliyyu-l-Akbar" (Ali Akbar, now you move forward, now go to fight). Ali Akbar immediately came forward, "Father, I am ready." He said, "Son, first go to the tent and take permission." Now Ali Akbar came to the tent, to take permission from his mother. The mother said, "Take permission from your aunt, who has raised you for 18 years." Now, as soon as he came to ask for permission from Zainab, Zainab looked at Ali Akbar from head to toe and said, "Son, did I raise you for 18 years just so that you would take permission for death?" Ali Akbar said, "Aunt, if you don't give permission, it's fine, but what if Grandmother asks on the Day of Judgment?" Zainab gave permission. Ali Akbar came, Hussain prepared Ali Akbar, adorned him. Before making him sit on the horse, he said, "Allāhumma-sh-had ʿalā hāʾulāʾi-l-qawm" (O Lord, be a witness against this nation). "Qad baraza ilayhim ghulāmun" (A youth is going to fight them), "Ashbahu-n-nāsi khalqan wa khuluqan wa manṭiqan ilā nabiyyika" (who resembled Your Prophet the most in appearance, character, and speech). Ali Akbar was the image of the Prophet. When we wanted to see Your Prophet, we would look at Ali Akbar. Hussain bid him farewell, Ali Akbar started to go, he hadn't gone far, a sound was felt. When Ali Akbar looked back, what did he see? That the father was standing with his hand on his waist, "Ya Ali, Ya Ali." "Father, you had bid me farewell, why are you coming now?" He said, "Son, if you had children..." Mourners, you must have surely seen some individuals who have lost their young sons. Surely you must have seen, they can bear the greatest calamities of the world, but bearing the grief of a young son is very difficult. Hussain bid him farewell, Ali Akbar went, he kept fighting, kept fighting, sent 120 wretches to Hell and came back, but how did he come back? It was a mother's heart. Once she said to Fizza, "Fizza, go to the door of the tent, see if the color of the Master's face has changed, then understand that my son is in great trouble." Fizza came and stood at the door of the tent, was watching Hussain, once a voice came, "Bibi." The color of the Master's face has changed. She said, "Give the Master a little trouble." Hussain came, how did he remember? She said, "Master, why has the color of your face changed?" He said, "What can I do? A famous wrestler has come to fight my son. He is satiated and quenched, and my son is hungry and thirsty for three days." Just hearing this, it was a mother's heart. She said, "Master, what should I do?" He said, "Pray. A mother's prayer is accepted for her son." Umm Layla made a circle. She said, "Ladies, I am praying, you say Amen. O You who reunited Yusuf with Yaqub, O Allah, I swear by the loneliness of Hussain, I swear by the helplessness of Hussain, call my Ali Akbar back." Ali Akbar came back, but in what condition? He was covered in wounds, blood-stained, bathed in blood. He came and started saying, started saying, "Yā abatī al-ʿatshu qad qatalanī" (Father, thirst is killing me). "Wa siqlu-l-ḥadīdi qad ajhadanī" (And the weight of the armor has exhausted me). Is there a sip of water available? Is there a little water, Father? Hussain said, "Son, you know that there is not a drop of water in the tent. But bring your tongue into my mouth." "Hāti lisānaka." As soon as Ali Akbar put his tongue in, he pulled it back. He said, "Father, there are thorns in your tongue." Now what happened, "Go son, now go. Now your noble grandfather will quench your thirst with the water of Kawthar." Ali Akbar went, kept fighting, kept fighting with great bravery, with great valor. Until once the wretches surrounded Ali Akbar. A wretch took aim at Ali Akbar's chest and pulled a spear and struck it in such a way that the spear pierced Ali Akbar's chest. Ali Akbar fell from the horse, came among the wretches. The wretches started to cut Ali Akbar's body into pieces. "Fa-qattaʿūhu bi-suyūfihim irban irbā." They started to cut Ali Akbar's body into pieces. Ali Akbar gave a call, "Father, my final farewell." Hussain ran, this is a sentence from the Maqtal. Hussain ran like a furious lion and went and pushed the wretches away. It was a matter of a young son. Hussain placed Ali Akbar's head on his lap. He pulled out the tip of the spear, a fountain of blood erupted. Hussain recited a dirge. "Yā bunayya, al-dunyā baʿdaka lafā." (O my son, may there be dust on the life of this world after you.) "Istaraḥta min hammi-d-dunyā wa ghammihā." (You have found relief from the worries and sorrows of this world.) "Baqiya abūka waḥīdan farīdan bayna-l-aʿdā." (Your father is left alone and solitary among the enemies.) "Wā ʿAliyā, Wā Ḥusaynā." "Sa-yaʿlamu-lladhīna ẓalamū ayya munqalabin yanqalibūn." "ʿAlā laʿnatu-llāhi ʿalā-l-qawmi-ẓ-ẓālimīn." O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Grant us the ability to fulfill the right of his service. Until the last moment, until the last breath, may we keep serving our Imam. O Lord, O Lord, wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Grant complete and immediate cure to those who are ill. Remove the troubles of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. And grant righteous and pious children to those who are childless. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab. Deliver them from the clutches of the enemies. O Lord, bless us in this world with the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and in the Hereafter with the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. By reciting one Surah Fatiha and three times Surah Tawheed, bestow the reward upon the souls of the late Ghulam Ali ibn Abdul Aziz Lakhani, the Lakhani family, Rupani family, Himani family, Lada family, Narsidani family, and all the deceased men and women.

title: Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) Ke Naam Ka Waseela | Dawood-e-Raqqi Ka Waaqeya
excerpt: This lecture recounts the story of Dawud-e-Raqqi, a companion of Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.), who was struggling with debt and fear of a sea voyage. Imam al-Sadiq provided spiritual guidance, assuring him of divine protection and the power of the Ahlulbayt's intercession. Upon following the Imam's advice, Dawud experienced a miraculous provision of gold, which he later returned to the Imam to verify. The lecture emphasizes the importance of trust in Allah, the significance of the Imam's status in the universe, and the necessity of gratitude.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. It is in the narrations that once Dawud-e-Raqqi, a famous companion of Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), comes to the service of the Imam. As soon as the Imam sees Dawud, he says, 'Dawud, what has happened? Your face looks changed, your complexion is pale, are you worried about something?' Dawud says, 'Yes, Master, there is a worry; I am drowned in a debt, because of which I am very ashamed, and I am thinking of paying off that debt, but to pay it, I will have to go to India, traveling by sea, and go to my such-and-such brother to pay off that debt there.' So we said, 'As you wish.' That is, there was a hint from the Imam (a.s.) not to delay in paying off that debt. Pay off that debt as soon as possible. On this, Dawud says, 'Yes, Master, but the problem is that I am afraid of the sea voyage. So, therefore, I am thinking whether to go or not.' On this, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'Innal ladhi yahfazu fil barri huwa hafizun laka fil bahri' (Indeed, the One who protects on land is the same One who will protect you in the sea). And after this, the Imam states a profound sentence: 'Ya Dawud, lawlas ismi wa ruhi' (O Dawud, if it were not for my name and my spirit), that is, if my existence were not in this universe, then neither would the sea flow, nor would water flow in it, nor would fruits grow on trees, nor would trees grow, nor would greenery grow on the earth. Nothing will happen. Meaning, it is the name of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) by which this universe operates. This universe is running by his name. And similarly, in this era, the Imam of every age, by his noble name, the existence of this universe is sustained. And so, it is as if Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) is giving this lesson to Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi, giving this instruction: 'Dawood, go, have trust in Allah. If there is to be trust, it should be in Allah. Regarding any task—if it is a righteous deed—firstly, do not delay in performing it, in executing it. Be quick, and if you are troubled by something, use the intercession of the name of us, the Ahlulbayt, in the court of Allah. Insha'Allah, Allah will protect you and grant you blessings in that task.' So, Dawood immediately says: 'Then I made the intention, and after traveling for 120 days, I reached my destination. It was a Friday, and I arrived there at the time of Zawal (midday). As soon as I reached that shore, what happened? I saw dark black clouds covering the sky. Meaning, the very thing that Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi feared was happening. But as the black clouds gathered, Dawood al-Raqqi says: ﴿وَإِذَا نُورٌ سَاطِعٌ مِنْ قَرْنِ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى جَدَدِ الْأَرْضِ﴾ 'From the edge of the sky to the earth, I saw a light shining, a light glowing.' And then, after that, a hidden voice came to my ears. A hidden call—what does a hidden call mean? Dawood says that no one was visible there, only the voice was coming.' The voice was heard, and that hidden voice called out to me and said: 'This is the time, this is the right time for your debt to be paid. O Dawood, ﴿فَارْفَعْ رَأْسَكَ﴾ lift your head. Why? Because you are safe and sound. You have reached your destination safely.' Meaning, the guarantee that Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) had given before the journey began, that guarantee had been fulfilled. And then Dawood says: 'I then lifted my head. As soon as I lifted my head, a second call came. A second call came, and now I was told that the red-colored mountain you see in front of you, go behind that mountain.' Dawood says: 'I went behind the mountain. As soon as I reached behind that mountain, there were large plates of red color, large tablets made of gold. There were gold tablets. And how were the gold tablets? One side was plain, the surface was smooth, and on the other side, a verse of the Holy Quran was written. And which verse? Surah Sad, verse number 39. In it, the Lord of Majesty declares: ﴿هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ 'This is our gift; so give or withhold, without account.' What does this mean? When Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi saw this inscription, this Quranic verse written, it meant that this entire thing was for him. This entire arrangement was for him so that his debt could be paid. But now, this is Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi. He is not an ordinary human being. What did Dawood al-Raqqi do? He took the gold, and when he wanted to count it to see what its value would be, he saw that this was priceless gold.' Meaning, Dawood al-Raqqi could not determine its value at that time. At that moment, Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi says: ﴿فَقُلْتُ﴾ 'I said to myself, ﴿لَا أُحْدِثُ فِيهَا حَتَّى آتِيَ الْمَدِينَةَ﴾.' These are Dawood al-Raqqi, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). He says, 'I will not mention this to anyone. I will not take this before anyone until I reach Medina.' Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi says: 'I returned to Medina. As soon as I arrived and entered Medina, I went to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) saw me and said: 'O Dawood, in reality, the gift we gave you was the light that was shining from the sky to the earth. And this gold in your hand is the grace of the Lord. This is additional, extra, given to you by Allah. ﴿وَلَكِنْ هُوَ لَكَ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا﴾ It is pure and clean for you to use, it is lawful for you. You can use it however you wish. There is no problem. ﴿مِنْ رَبٍّ كَرِيمٍ﴾ It is a gift for you from the Generous Lord. ﴿فَاحْمَدِ اللَّهَ﴾ Therefore, thank Allah, praise Allah.' Look at how Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) is teaching Janab-e-Dawood al-Raqqi that when something is gifted, even if it is gifted from our court, thank Allah. Praise and glorify Allah. ﴿هَذَا وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ الْمَعْصُومِينَ﴾

title: Allah Bhi Muntazir Hai | ⛅ IMAM MAHDI (A.T.F.S.): PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ
excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual significance of waiting for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as emphasized by Imam Ridha (a.s.). It underscores the virtue of patience and the divine promise that Allah is also among those who wait for the relief of the believers. The message serves as a reminder to maintain steadfastness and hope during times of despair, drawing inspiration from the endurance of previous generations.
content:
Imam Ridha (a.s.) says, 'How excellent it is to have patience while waiting for the reappearance (Zuhur). Have you not heard the saying of Allah Azza wa Jall: ﴿وَارْتَقِبُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُم رَقِيبٌ﴾ and the other verse of the Quran: ﴿فَانتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ الْمُنتَظِرِينَ﴾? So wait, surely I am also with you among those who wait. Therefore, it is obligatory upon you all to be patient, because surely after despair, there will be a reappearance, and those who passed before you were more patient than you.'
Imam Ridha (a.s.) emphasizes the excellence of patience while awaiting the reappearance.
The Quranic verse 'Wait, surely I am with you among those who wait' confirms divine companionship in the waiting process.

The Quranic verse 'Wait, surely I am with you among those who wait' confirms divine companionship in the waiting process.
Patience is considered an obligatory duty for the believers during the occultation.
Relief and reappearance are promised to follow periods of despair.
Believers are encouraged to look to the endurance of past generations as a model for their own patience.

title: Mohabbat Aur Nafrat Ka Me'yaar
excerpt: This lecture explores the fundamental criteria for faith in Shia Islam, centering on the concept of loving and hating for the sake of Allah. It emphasizes that a believer's actions, including generosity and withholding, must be aligned with their devotion to the Wilayat of Ale-Muhammad. Ultimately, the speaker highlights that true faith is defined by these divine-centered attachments and detachments.
content:
Imam (a.s.) says: 'Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, and gives for the sake of Allah, his faith is complete.' And then he says, 'The strongest bond of faith is that you love for the sake of Allah, hate for the sake of Allah, give for the sake of Allah, and deprive people for the sake of Allah.' Meaning, if you are not giving something to someone, say that I could give it, but I am not giving it because the Wilayat of Ale-Muhammad is not in your heart.
Faith is perfected when love and hate are directed solely for the sake of Allah.
The strongest bond of faith involves aligning all personal actions with divine pleasure.
Giving or withholding resources should be based on one's spiritual alignment.
The Wilayat of Ale-Muhammad is the central standard for evaluating relationships.
A believer must be conscious of their motivations in every social and material interaction.

title: Majlis 1 | Ma'refat Ka Me'yaar | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 1444
excerpt: This lecture, the first in the Khamsa-e-Majaalis series, explores the criteria for true religious knowledge and adherence to the Ahlulbayt. It emphasizes the necessity of sourcing guidance exclusively from the Imams, the critical importance of prayer, and the dangers of spreading unverified religious information. The session also reflects on the historical sacrifices of the Ahlulbayt, particularly the tragedy of Karbala and the enduring grief of Imam Sajjad, to illustrate the perpetual struggle between truth and falsehood.
content:
Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. In this state of exile, how can I let you go? In this desert of calamity, how can I let you go? In this moment of doomsday, how can I let you go? Oh son, you are asking for permission to go to war. You are asking your father for permission to die. Have you not thought about what will happen to this father's heart? You have taken my life, Akbar, have you not thought? I will die after being separated from you, have you not thought? You are asking me for the provisions of old age. You are asking your father for permission to die. Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. The heart weeps if the son is away from the eyes. How can your separation be acceptable, my son? You are my eyes, you are my light, my son. You are asking me for the light of my eyes. You are asking your father for permission to die. Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. The moment the beloved of God left the world, the grandson longed to see his grandfather. Oh son, that is why I had asked for you from the Creator. My prayer has been accepted, you are asking for it. You are asking your father for permission to die. Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. Shed your own blood for Islam on the battlefield. Take the spear on your chest with pride in the field. Mingle the image of the Prophet with the dust. Is this why you are asking for permission to die? You are asking your father for permission to die. Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. One day, your aunt had come and asked for you. Your aunt had raised you with affection for 18 years. Your aunt loved you even more than her own sons. You are asking for the favor that Zainab did. You are asking your father for permission to die. Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking your father for permission to die. May God have mercy on those who recite Al-Fatiha. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best disposer of affairs, the best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the righteous and the certain, and blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Blessings be upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Especially the remainder of Allah on the earths, the Imam of our time, our guardian, our master, our leader, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our confidant, the fortified cave, and the succor of the distressed and the helpless, may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. After that, our master Ja'far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'He is a liar who claims that he knows us while holding onto the rope of others.' May our master Ja'far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) be truthful. Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse their enemies. The hadith I have chosen for today's discussion and for the discussion of this gathering, in it Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse their enemies. 'He is a liar.' He is a liar, the one who assumes. In this hadith, the word is 'assumes,' and in another hadith, it is 'claims.' Two things, meaning the Imam is saying in both hadiths that he assumes—an assumption is not the truth—and a claim is not necessarily true. So in both places, the Imam said, 'He who claims, he who assumes,' meaning he only thinks that he knows us, or in the other hadith, that he is from our Shia, but he is holding onto the rope of others. He claims to be our Shia but is holding onto the rope of others. He is not holding onto our hem. Look, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) do not have formalities in their clear words. When they state something, they state it exactly as it is. Now, whether someone likes it or dislikes it. So, which hadith is the Imam interpreting? That hadith of the Prophet which the Prophet repeated many times in his life and which every Muslim should remember if they are a Muslim. That 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahlulbayt. If you hold onto them, you will never go astray after me.' Hold them firmly, you will never go astray. 'For they will never separate from each other until they return to me at the Pond (Hawd).' This is a narration of the Prophet, and not just once, the Prophet repeated this hadith many times. Now, some people have made changes to it and are repeating it in one source, in many traditions, again and again. Sunnah, Sunnah, only once, but there are many references for the Ahlulbayt, many references, and no one can deny this. Therefore, one must believe in the Ahlulbayt, and if one believes in the Ahlulbayt, then follow the correct Sunnah, which we will summarize today, Insha'Allah, in today's speech, in today's gathering, that only the Ahlulbayt can truly introduce the correct Sunnah, and no one else can do it besides them. Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Therefore, it is necessary that if you are to take a narration, take it from the Ahlulbayt, and one more thing is important in this, that we should study the narrations, read them, teach them to children, and create an environment where children are familiar with the teachings of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Now, unfortunately, the environment today—which is a matter of regret—is that the environment has become such that people are moving away from the Quran and Hadith. They are moving away from the Quran and narrations, and as much as they should hold onto them—what does 'holding onto' (tamassuk) mean? It is not explained in the hadith, but what does the Prophet mean by 'tamassuk'? If you hold onto them, how is 'tamassuk' explained in the narrations? It is like a man who is drowning. He is drowning. The current in the water is tremendous, a very powerful current. A powerful current indeed, and he is drowning in it. In such a situation, if a trunk or a log of wood comes before him, a trunk—that is, a wooden log—how will he hold onto that log? Will he just touch it from afar, or just touch it like this? Will he just kiss it from a distance? No. Rather, he will hold onto it with all his might because his life depends on this very log of wood. Similarly, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that if you want to save your afterlife, there is only one way, and that is to hold fast (tamassuk) to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). There is no other way, and hold onto them with all your might. There is no other way. And then, in very clear words, he said, 'Indeed, Hussain is the lamp of guidance and the ark of salvation.' Look, Hussain is the lamp of guidance, Hussain is the ark of salvation, the boat of salvation. Hold onto the hem of Hussain. If you leave Hussain, you will drown. 'The example of my Ahlulbayt is like the Ark of Nuh. Whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind is destroyed.' Therefore, boarding is very important, and what does boarding mean? See, people understand boarding, but what is the meaning, what is the concept? Let's give an example from the modern world so that everyone understands. We board an airplane. Nowadays, very few people board a boat. We board an airplane. As soon as you sit inside the plane, you quietly sit wherever you are told to sit. You don't say, 'No, I will sit here.' Brother, this is not your business class; if you have to sit in economy, you will sit in economy. You won't say, 'Why are they sitting in that big seat?' Because the air hostess will say, 'This is not a matter of your religion where you can do as you please. This is an airplane.' You cannot do here what you do in religion. You have to listen here. So, you sit in the seat you are assigned, even if it is a middle seat. Okay, you sat down. Now, if they say, 'Fasten your seatbelt,' will you say, 'I am already wearing a belt on my pants, what is the need to fasten a seatbelt?' If any person says at that moment, 'No, I will not do this, I will not do that,' then the pilot or the captain has every right to immediately turn the plane back, offload him, and he can even be arrested. This is the law. This is the law. This is what obedience is. Whatever the captain said, whatever instructions were received, they were followed. That is what boarding means. That is what the Ark of Salvation means. Therefore, when you read the hadith, read them very carefully. Look, I present one hadith for your service so that the children understand, and especially the elders who have children, they should arrange such an education for their children that is based on the traditions of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) and set a schedule for them. There is a famous hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam says that each one of you should, at the very least, at the very least, dedicate one day a week—the Imam says one day a week—at the very least, without exception, keep the whole day only for religious knowledge. Just take the religion, learn and teach the religion, and do no other work on that day. Of course, the word 'Jumu'ah' (Friday) was used in the hadith because Friday used to be a holiday. Now, well, Friday is not a holiday. If Sunday is your day off, then dedicate it to that. Any day, whatever day is your weekly off, however it is, but at the very least, this much is necessary, and read it very well. Now look at what the tradition says. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says—Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum wal an a'daahum—'Do you want to know the status of our Shia? Do you want to know which Shia has a higher level? Do you want to find out? Then see how well they narrate our traditions (riwayat) from us. See who understands the traditions.' Who narrates the traditions? How much mastery, how much command do they have over the traditions—that is, the teachings of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.)—how familiar are they with the books? And this should be our standard everywhere. It should be our standard everywhere. If you want to find out which person is at what level, see how familiar they are with the traditions, with the hadith. The more familiar they are, the higher their rank. And do not read hadith like a newspaper, yes, do not read it like a newspaper. No, the word the Imam used is 'yuhsinun', 'yuhsinun', meaning in a good way. That is why in another hadith, what does he say? In 'Ma'ani al-Akhbar' by Sheikh Saduq, there is a tradition that 'One hadith that you understand well is better than 1,000 hadith that you merely narrate.' Aha! Subhan Allah! Subhan Allah! Understand one hadith well, that's it. Wow! Wow! Meaning, read it, understand it, ponder over it, internalize it, act upon it. The whole process. Otherwise, our example will be the same as the example of the scholars of the Children of Israel, which the Quran describes in Surah Jumu'ah: 'The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah but did not uphold it is like that of a donkey.' Meaning, they used to read the Torah, but they neither tried to understand it nor acted upon it. That is why the Quran gave the example of a donkey, meaning the example of that donkey upon which books have been loaded. Wow! What a point. Meaning, if you load 'Usul al-Kafi' on a donkey, its character will not become good. Wow! Wow! That the donkey will say, 'No, now I have to make sounds properly, in a well-mannered way; the way I used to shout loudly, now I will shout softly.' The donkey will remain the same; there is no change going to happen to it. The Quran gave the example of a donkey: 'The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah but did not uphold it is like that of a donkey.' And in many places, the Quran has given such examples; there is no time now, otherwise, every single example is an example from the Quran. That, 'His example is like that of a dog; if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.' The Quran says this. Look, if we say this, they will say their language is very bad, they use this language while sitting on the pulpit. But Jibra'il brought that language from Allah! Hai! Hai! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! 'His example is like that of a dog; if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.' His example is the example of a dog. If you ride him, he will still do the same, and if you leave him to his state, he will still do the same. He is not going to improve. Or there are many such examples. The Quran says that their example is the example of animals, rather even worse than that. 'Bal hum adhallu sabeela', 'Ulaika kal-an'am'. They are like animals. Rather, no, they are worse than animals. These are the examples of the Quran. Therefore, read the traditions and understand them very well, contemplate, ponder, deliberate, reflect, and act upon them. This is a very important thing. 'Fa-inna'—after that, the Imam says a slightly dangerous sentence—'Fa-inna la na'udul-faqeeha minhum faqeeha', because we do not consider any of our Shia to be a 'Faqeeh'—Faqeeh, meaning one who is very deep in knowledge—we do not consider him a Faqeeh 'hatta yakuna muhaddatha', until he is 'Muhaddath'. Not 'Muhaddith'. 'Muhaddith' is one who narrates hadith. 'Muhaddath' is one with whom the angels converse. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! There is a slogan, Haidari! Ya Ali! A Faqeeh will not be a Faqeeh until then, we will not consider him so, the Imam says that we will not consider him a Faqeeh until the angels converse with him. What a point! Now the narrator got scared hearing this. The narrator got scared; naturally, since the Imam stated such a big thing, such a deep meaning, he immediately asked, 'Faqeeh lahu', someone asked, 'A-yakunul-mu'minu muhaddatha?' Can an ordinary believer be such that angels converse with him? Wow! Can Jibra'il come to him? Can a believer be like this? The Imam said, 'Yakunu mufahhaman wal-mufahhamu muhaddatha.' Hai! Hai! Wow! Wow! He will be 'Mufahham'. Mufahham, meaning one who is made to understand. Wow! Subhan Allah! Mufahham, meaning one who is given 'Fahm'. Understand, 'Fahm' means understanding. This is being translated into English for the youngsters so they understand. 'Fahm' means understanding, to understand something. So, he is made to understand so that he understands the matter. And when he understands the matter, how will he understand it? Because understanding is that light, that light from Allah, which Allah gives to some people; Allah does not give it to everyone. Therefore, the Imam said in another hadith, 'Istafhimillaha yufhimka.' Look, if you want understanding, then ask Allah that Allah may make you understand; Allah will make you understand. Wow! Subhan Allah! Granting 'Fahm' is Allah's work; it is not in the servant's control. A servant can read things, but making one understand is Allah's work, and especially if it is religious education, then only Allah will make one understand, and no one else can. Therefore, a believer should always pray, meaning read and pray to Allah that Allah may make him understand. So, this is a very important thing, to study the traditions, and this is the way to hold fast to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Otherwise, if we do not read the hadith, if we are not aware of their teachings, if we are not familiar with them, then how will we know what the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is pleased with and what they are not pleased with? Let me give a small example. For instance, there are many youngsters who are not aware of the importance of the Fajr prayer; that one should pray Fajr, one should pray Fajr on time, one should pray at the beginning of the time. Okay, they are not aware. So, they miss the Fajr prayer. They don't pray Fajr. Sometimes there are also some who leave the prayer altogether, thinking, 'Now it has become Qadha (missed), let it be.' Why is it like this? What is the reason? Because they are not familiar with the teachings. Because they are not familiar with the teachings. If they had read the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), they would never do such a thing. Because the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) said, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said in his will. Let us recite a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. Abu Basir was a lover of the Imam, he was blind. When he came to Medina, he had gone somewhere outside, when he returned, he received the news that the Imam of the time, Imam Sadiq (a.s.), had departed from this world. So he came to offer condolences to his sister, Umm-e-Hamida. And he came and said, 'Umm-e-Hamida, did my Mawla (a.s.) make any will?' She said, 'Yes, he did make a will.' And what was the will? So, among the wills, this was one of them: 'Convey my greetings to our Shia and say, 'Our intercession will never reach the one who takes the prayer lightly.'' Who takes the prayer lightly. And taking the prayer lightly is just this, that the Fajr prayer was missed and we are sleeping. We are sleeping, the time for prayer came and went, and we didn't even pray. Now we woke up late, now we thought, 'Let it be, leave it, let's not pray today.' Took it lightly. Prayed Dhuhr-Asr, prayed Maghrib-Isha, but the morning one was left. We won't pray. Is this the right thing? No, it is wrong. The Quran has sent a curse upon such people. There is a verse in Surah Ma'un. The Quran says, 'Wailul-likulli', 'Wailul-musalleen', 'Wailul-musalleen fawailul-musalleen'. 'Wail' is the name of a valley in Hell. Who is this valley of Hell for? For the ones who pray. It is for the worshippers. Which worshippers are these? The Quran says, "Alladhina hum 'an salatihim sahun" (Those who are neglectful of their prayers). These are the people who took their prayers lightly, were negligent, sometimes prayed and sometimes did not. They did not care about the prayer. They did not worry about the prayer. The Quran says, "Rijalun la tulhihim tijaratun wa la bay'un 'an dhikrillahi wa iqamis-salah" (Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and the establishment of prayer). Men are those, men are those, "la tulhihim tijaratun wa la bay'un 'an dhikrillahi" (whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah). Meaning, they do not get so busy in the world, in business, or in work that they forget the prayer, the remembrance, "'an dhikrillahi wa iqamis-salah" (from the remembrance of Allah and the establishment of prayer), "wa ita'iz-zakah" (and the giving of Zakat). The Quran is saying this; it is a verse of the Quran, look and reflect. This is a verse of the Quran. So, when will this happen? When you become familiar with the teachings of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.), when you understand how much emphasis the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) have placed on it. Meaning, just think and imagine that no one can describe the Day of Ashura. No one can describe the Day of Ashura. No one in the world has the power to praise Ashura, to describe Ashura. Please move forward a little so that those who have come behind can also find space. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the Ale Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum. It is a scene of Qiyamah (Judgment Day). Ashura is Qiyamah, Qiyamah. This is truly not just rhetoric, not just oratory. No, the reality is that Ashura is Qiyamah, Qiyamah. Ashura was Qiyamah. But on that Ashura, Abu Sumama al-Sa'idi comes and says, "Ya Ibn Rasulullah, qad hana waqtus-salah" (O son of the Messenger of Allah, the time for prayer has arrived). O son of the Messenger, the time for prayer has arrived. A fierce battle. In such a situation, Abu Sumama al-Sa'idi comes and says, "Maula, the time for prayer has arrived." The Imam said, "Dhakartas-salah" (You have remembered the prayer). "Ja'alakallahu minal-musallin" (May Allah count you among the worshippers). Now, until the Day of Judgment, whenever the Adhan is mentioned, the name of Abu Sumama al-Sa'idi is mentioned. Abu Sumama al-Sa'idi was telling the Imam on the day of Ashura that the time for prayer had arrived. Of course, the Imam knew that the time for prayer had arrived, but Allah wanted to bestow this virtue upon Abu Sumama. So, Allah gave this virtue to Abu Sumama. The Imam knew, the Imam was aware, the Imam was cognizant—or was the Imam not aware? But Abu Sumama attained this virtue, this honor. He came and submitted to the Imam, "Maula, the time for prayer has arrived." Therefore, it is very important that whatever teachings we take, we take them only from the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) and do not go to anyone else's door. Now look, this is also an important thing. Since the topic has come up, let me also share this Hadith with you. Nowadays, this has generally become a fashion, and this world of WhatsApp is a very dangerous world. Before shedding light on this, let me first tell you what the Seerah (tradition) was here. It is very important to understand this. Many people here might not be familiar with Hadith, might not be familiar with the world of Hadith. So, we tell them, for the youngsters, for the children. The others who know, they know. For those who don't know, we tell them that in the books of Hadith, it is written like this: 'An' (from), for example, 'An' this, 'An' that, 'An' that, 'An' that, 'An' that—meaning he narrated from him, he narrated from him, he narrated from him, he narrated from him, and he narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). This is how the chain goes. In terminology, this is also called 'Mu'al-an'an', Mu'al-an'an. But anyway, it is not necessary to know that. This is what is called a chain, this is called a 'Chain of Narrators'. What is it called? A 'Chain of Narrators'. This is the chain of narrators. So, the system we have—and Insha'Allah, if there is time, we will try to bring both Hadiths before you for comparison—is that the system we had was not such that when there is a chain, it is not that he heard from him, he heard from him, he heard from him. It is not like that among the Shias. Rather, with us, when there is 'An, An, An', it means he was his student, he was his student, he was his student, he was his student, and he heard from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). Subhan Allah. Meaning, the student had the right to sit in his teacher's lesson and then write down the Hadiths. This is our system, and it is a very solid system. Understand this here. He used to write down the Hadiths. It is a system from the beginning, yes. He used to write down the Hadiths, and after writing, what would he do? He would present them to the Imam—excuse me, meaning to his teacher. The teacher would read the Hadiths and see if he had written them correctly or not. Subhan Allah. And when it was written correctly, if there was any mistake, the Imam—the teacher—would correct it. And if it was written correctly, then it was fine, meaning the teacher would say, "Yes, it is correct." And when the whole book was finished, the teacher would certify it. Meaning, he would sign it and say, "He has the right to narrate these traditions." Subhan Allah. This used to happen in two ways. This is called 'Al-Qira'atu 'indal Mashayikh' (Reading before the scholars) or 'Al-Sama'atu 'anil Mashayikh' (Hearing from the scholars). There are two ways. Either read before the teacher after writing, or hear from the teacher. The teacher would read and he would listen, and he would check. This is our system. I mean, of course, technology has advanced a lot now, but in that era, it used to be like this. And it used to be like this from the beginning. So, that is why there was a complete system among us that he heard from him, he heard from him, he heard from him—or 'heard' means he attended his class, and then when he received the permission (Ijazah), he could narrate those Hadiths. Now, what has the current era become? Now, a statement comes from anywhere, and we forward it saying this is a Hadith. Now, that Hadith has neither a head nor a tail. No reference. For example, just yesterday someone sent me a Hadith. I am talking about yesterday. And Masha'Allah, a very educated man, very educated. And he sent a Hadith, this Hadith. At that very moment, Alhamdulillah, I was sitting at my laptop, and at that very moment I checked, there was no reference for it anywhere, and no such Hadith existed. So, I asked him, "Did you check the reference before sending this?" I am talking about yesterday. He said, "No, I didn't check the reference." I said, "Please check it, see if you find it anywhere, then let me know." So he looked and said, "No sir, I didn't find it." I said, "Then why did you forward it? You have even put it on your status. And how many people must you have forwarded it to? Now you are responsible for this. Meaning, you have attributed a lie to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.). And attributing a lie is such a big sin that it invalidates the fast. Therefore, never forward any such thing on WhatsApp unless you are absolutely sure that the sender is reliable, just, and unless he himself has checked it, until then, do not send it forward. Otherwise, a pile of such false Hadiths will accumulate among us. Now, a new fashion has emerged these days: 'Ghurar al-Hikam', just said it. Now go and find it. Not that, there is a reference in 'Ghurar al-Hikam', meaning there is a page number, a Hadith number. And did you see if it is in 'Ghurar al-Hikam' or not? No, they just put it, they said it. Translation, correct translation, wrong translation, whatever it is. Therefore, well, even up to that point, we still say, still yes, it is not correct. Pay attention to the words. Still, it is a blessing. Now it has become such that we have started propagating the words of the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Forwarding their videos, forwarding their words. title: J. Qasim (a.s.) Ki Ta'weez Mein Kya Likha Tha?
excerpt: This lecture discusses the poignant final will of Imam Hasan (a.s.) left for his son, Janabe Qasim (a.s.), regarding the events of Karbala. It details how Qasim utilized an amulet containing his father's instructions to seek permission to fight alongside his uncle, Imam Hussain (a.s.). The message emphasized the necessity of sacrificing one's life to defend the Imam and the religion of Allah against the enemies of the Prophet.
content:
The final will of Imam Hasan (a.s.) in Karbala: When Janabe Qasim (a.s.) did not get permission for battle and remembered the command regarding his father's amulet, he opened the amulet tied to his arm. It was written: 'O my son Qasim, I advise you that when you see your uncle Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala surrounded by enemies, do not refrain from fighting and confronting the enemies of Allah and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Do not hold back from sacrificing your life for them. And if he does not give you permission to fight, keep asking until he grants it, so that you may attain eternal martyrdom.'
Imam Hasan (a.s.) left a written will for his son Qasim (a.s.) in an amulet.
The amulet instructed Qasim to stand by Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Karbala.
Qasim was advised to confront the enemies of Allah and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).
The will explicitly commanded Qasim to sacrifice his life for his uncle.
Qasim was told to persist in asking for permission if Imam Hussain initially refused.
The ultimate goal mentioned in the letter was the attainment of eternal martyrdom.
