title: 10 Maah e Ramazan | Shahaadat e Umm al-Momineen Hazrat Khadijah (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound life, character, and spiritual stature of Lady Khadija (s.a.), the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights her immense contributions to the early Islamic community, specifically how her vast wealth and business acumen provided the foundational support for the spread of Islam. The discussion also covers her noble lineage, her titles such as 'Tahira' and 'Siddiqa', and the divine recognition she received, including greetings from Allah via Jibra'il and a shroud from Paradise.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah... [Recitation]... The martyrdom of the Lady of the Worlds, Janabe Khadija (s.a.), has been mentioned. And Janabe Khadija, who is the mother of the believers, and the mother of the infallible Imams (a.s.)... the verse in the Holy Quran where it is said: 'Did He not find you poor and enrich you?' 'Did He not find you poor and enrich you?' O My Beloved, did We not find you poor and make you rich and independent? Respected listeners, it is a place to think, whose daughter was she? Whose wealth is the Lord of the Worlds attributing to Himself? Whose wealth is it that the Lord of the Worlds is attributing to His own self? I believe that if I say something, it has no weight, but the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Islam did not stand on its own feet; Islam did not get stability, or if Islam got stability, it was either through Ali's sword or Khadija's wealth.' If Islam stood on its own feet, it was through Ali's sword or Khadija's wealth. Or let me say that in the mission of Prophethood, the status of Khadija's wealth is the same as the status of Ali's sword. The status of Janabe Khadija's wealth, respected listeners, is that she is 'Malikat-ul-Arab' (Queen of the Arabs). Understand this title of Janabe Khadija. There are many virtues, but if you understand this, you will understand the rest. She was called 'Malika' (Queen). What is the difference between 'Malika' and 'Mulk'? 'Malika' refers to those who possess authority, and 'Mulk' also refers to those who possess authority. But if Janabe Khadija were just called a 'Malika', it could be questioned that if she was a queen, there might have been a possibility of change in her authority or wealth. But she was called 'Malika' in a way that implies her authority yesterday is the same as her authority today. She was Malikat-ul-Arab in the world, and she will be Malikat-ul-Arab in the Hereafter. The word 'Malika' is an ocean of virtues. Regarding Janabe Khadija (s.a.), look at two words: 'Milk' and 'Mulk'. Both relate to authority, but there is a difference. For example, if I inherit something from my father, and my father passes away, the property is mine, but someone else is in possession of it. Here, the 'Milk' (ownership) is mine, but the authority is not. Where the thing is yours but the authority is not, the word used is 'Milk'. Where the thing is yours and the authority is also yours, the word used is 'Mulk'. When the Lord of the Worlds described His sovereignty and authority in the Quran, He did not use the word 'Milk' for Himself; He used 'Mulk'. The Lord of the Worlds is saying that the universe is Mine and the authority is also Mine. This is not 'Milk', it is 'Mulk'. The Lord of the Worlds did not use the word 'Milk' for His own Being, but said 'Tabarakalladhi biyadihi al-mulk' (Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion). This is to explain that the universe is His and the authority is His. Respected listeners, understand the difference between 'Milk' and 'Mulk'. Where the thing is yours but the authority is not, it is 'Milk'. Where the thing is yours and the authority is also yours, it is 'Mulk'. The Lord of the Worlds used 'Mulk' for His sovereignty. Janabe Khadija is not just 'Malika' of 'Milk', she is 'Malika' of 'Mulk'. She was not just a queen yesterday, she will be a queen until the Day of Judgment. Someone might say this is your personal opinion. What evidence do you have? Remember, Janabe Khadija has a very prominent personality in her family, whose name is Waraqa ibn Nawfal. First, understand that Janabe Khadija's family was not an ordinary family. Janabe Khadija belonged to the same lineage. After four generations, Janabe Khadija's lineage meets the Prophet of Islam's lineage. There was a difference of four generations, otherwise, the lineage is the same. Janabe Khadija's father is Khuwaylid, Khuwaylid's father is Asad, Asad's father is Abd al-Uzza. And Abd al-Uzza's father is... [lineage continues]... Janabe Khadija's family was a very dignified family. In her family, there was a prominent personality, Waraqa ibn Nawfal. Waraqa ibn Nawfal was the paternal cousin of Khadija (s.a.). He was one of the most learned men of his time, a great scholar of the heavenly books, and a profound expert in the scriptures of the past. In his family, and indeed among the youth of the Quraysh, he was considered a man of great wisdom. He understood that the time was approaching and that the final Prophet was soon to arrive; he was certain of this. He was well-versed in the signs of his arrival and held him in high esteem. He used to say to Khadija (s.a.), 'You are wealthy and possess great resources; how wonderful it would be if you were to marry him.' It was Waraqa who first suggested this to her. When she spoke to her cousin about her intention to send a message to the son of Abdullah, Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), she asked for his opinion on the matter. Listen to Waraqa's response, for this is why I said what I did. Listen to Waraqa's response, for this is why I said that the best of traders in the world would be the best of traders in the Hereafter. When Lady Khadija (s.a.) expressed her intention, Waraqa said, 'O my cousin, when the sun of his excellence shines upon you, do not forget me.' Waraqa was conveying a message that the sun that was about to rise—the sun of the Prophet of Islam and his household—was Lady Khadija (s.a.). It is evident what the perfections and virtues of this lady must have been, for she is the one whom the Infallible Imams (a.s.) have referred to as the center of their identity. How many times have the Imams introduced themselves through Lady Khadija (s.a.)? How exalted must this lady be! Consider that in the fourth month of the tragedy of Karbala, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) stood in the court of Yazid and declared, 'Do you recognize me? Those who know me, know me; those who do not, let them know. I am the son of Mecca and Mina, I am the son of Zamzam and Safa, I am the son of Muhammad al-Mustafa, I am the son of Ali al-Murtada.' In that same sermon, the Imam declared, 'I am the son of Khadija al-Kubra.' In this way, you see that the Imams have introduced themselves through Lady Khadija (s.a.). They considered it a source of pride; they considered it an honor to be associated with her. Consider how, in the Ziyarat of our Master, our Imam, our Leader, the Master of the Age (a.t.f.s.), the best way to remember him is through his lineage. In this era, when we remember the Imam through his genealogy, there comes a moment where we address him by his ancestors. We say, 'O son of Muhammad al-Mustafa, O son of Ali al-Murtada, O son of Khadija al-Kubra, O son of Fatima al-Zahra.' When we remember the Imam of the Age, we say, 'O son of Khadija al-Kubra.' Why do we call her 'al-Kubra'? And what does 'Khadija' mean? It refers to a woman who is very intelligent, very wise, and possesses great intellect. She is very intelligent and very wise—meaning one who is deeply connected to wisdom. That is why she is called 'al-Kubra.' Look at what the Divine chose; He chose one who was not just Khadija, but Khadija al-Kubra. I am reminded of a point: Lady Khadija (s.a.) was such a great business tycoon, such a great lady of wealth and status. If she were not wise, who would be? Our Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) stated—the essence of which is that he who makes trade a way of life strengthens his intellect. You see, there is a deep connection between trade and intellect. If she were not wise, who would be? Regardless, discussing her life is a vast subject. I want to touch upon aspects of her life, for it was not just about her wealth; it is about where she spent it. Consider that among those villages, there was one small one... Because among them was a small village, and from the perspective of truth, the center of the Arab world—the capital, the commercial hub of India, like Mumbai where the most trade and business happens—Mecca was the cultural and commercial center of all of Arabia. It was the place where the caravans gathered; it served as a central hub. In such a Mecca, Lady Khadija (s.a.) had her business. The scale of her trade was such that, as recorded in history, her trade caravans reached as far as Egypt in one direction and Syria in another, and even as far as India. The accounts of Lady Khadija's (s.a.) caravans state that 70,000 or 80,000 camels would travel in her trade caravans. Just think, this is no small matter. 80,000 camels cannot be gathered in one place, yet 80,000 camels traveled in Lady Khadija's (s.a.) trade caravans. Any wise businessman knows that anyone who is a trader... Any wise businessman knows that if I have 100 rupees, I will not invest all 100 rupees in business. I will keep some in surplus, I will keep some as a backup. I will invest 40 or 50 rupees and keep the rest for difficult times. That is, from the capital a person has, they only invest a portion and keep the rest safe as a surplus or backup. If 80,000 camels traveled in Lady Khadija's (s.a.) caravans, imagine how much wealth she must have had in reserve and surplus. And what happened to all this wealth? In those days, houses were usually one-story buildings. History records that Lady Khadija's (s.a.) house was a three-story building, and the upper part was blue, decorated with stars, the moon, and the sun, with curtains of silk. What was the purpose of such a large house? Lady Khadija (s.a.) would instruct her employees—listen, listen carefully—to go out into the deserts of Arabia... Go out into the deserts of Arabia and see if any father is burying his daughter alive. Tell him, 'Brother, do not bury your daughter alive. If you cannot afford to raise her, Khadija will raise her. If you cannot provide for her, Khadija will provide for her.' This was the extent of her generosity. Even before the declaration of Islam, before the proclamation of 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah,' just as the Prophet of Islam was known as 'Sadiq' (the Truthful) and 'Amin' (the Trustworthy), Lady Khadija (s.a.) was known as 'Tahira' (the Pure) and 'Siddiqa' (the Truthful). You see, for the 'Sadiq' and 'Amin,' the trade partner he chose was also a 'Siddiqa.' She was the lady whom everyone called 'Tahira.' And the wealth that Lady Khadija (s.a.) used—the way she used it was magnificent. When the Prophet of Islam migrated to Medina and established the Bait al-Mal (Public Treasury), whose money was it? The wealth that formed the first Islamic treasury was the wealth of Lady Khadija (s.a.). There is a fundamental difference between the wealth of Lady Khadija (s.a.) and other wealth. Later, when the caliphate reached the third stage, someone went to the third caliph and said, 'Our budget is limited; please open the treasury of Khadija again, start it again.' This means the treasury that was funded by the money of Khadija (s.a.). When the Prophet of Islam said, 'Islam did not stand on its own feet; Islam did not get this stability, whatever it received was through the sword of Ali and the wealth of Khadija.' The favors of Lady Khadija (s.a.) are countless. The first favor of Lady Khadija (s.a.) to the Prophet of Islam is that she sent him in her trade caravan to Syria. When, on the advice of Abu Talib (a.s.), the Prophet was sent to Syria, she did not keep him as an employee. Consider how great this is... She did not keep him as an employee. At that time, the Messenger of Allah did not have the capital to invest in Lady Khadija's (s.a.) caravan. Yet, despite this, Lady Khadija (s.a.) did not make the Messenger of Allah an employee; she made him a business partner. Consider how significant this is: she did not make the Messenger of Allah an employee, she made him a partner. This is a favor of Lady Khadija (s.a.). She gave a message to the world that remains relevant. As the world moves toward capitalism, and capitalism has become corrupted by cronyism, at such a time, this action of Lady Khadija (s.a.) should be noted. Even though the Messenger of Allah did not have the capital to invest in her trade, she did not make him an employee; she made him a partner. Lady Khadija (s.a.) gave a message to the world that the best trader is not one who just looks at the money, but one who looks at the capabilities. She looks at the capabilities. Regardless, Lady Khadija (s.a.) did not make the Messenger of Allah an employee; she made him a partner. This surprised the entire Islamic world. If Lady Khadija (s.a.) had made the Messenger of Allah an employee, then the Sunnah of trading would not have been established. By not making him an employee but a business partner, she made trade a Sunnah. This will remain a Sunnah until the end of time. Regardless, there was a great spirit in Lady Khadija (s.a.). When the Messenger of Allah returned from that trade journey with excellent profits, Lady Khadija's (s.a.) slave, Maysara, who had been instructed by her to observe everything that happened with Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) on the journey, returned. When he reported back, he said, 'In the last 40 years, there has never been such profit as there was in this trade caravan. The journey that used to take many days, we completed in a few days.' And when he returned with such profit, Maysara said to the Messenger of Allah, 'How good it would be if you went and told our mistress, our lady, about the profit.' And the Messenger of Allah... How much profit has been made, but there is hope for relief from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). This year, the sun itself was approaching the house of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.), towards that palace. As she looked at the majestic figure, she noticed that a cloud was shading you, and on one side there was an angel, and on the other side another angel. Janab-e-Khadija's eyes filled with tears, and it was after this that you sent a message, and the marriage of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) took place. It was also remembered that in all the marriages that happened after this, the daughter was brought to their house. Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) is the only wife, the only lady, who was not just brought to the house, but the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself went as a bridegroom to bring her. And when the marriage took place, for three days, the fragrance of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) remained. And I have even read in narrations that Allah (s.w.t.) ordered the angels to shower the mountains and the valleys of Mecca with musk and amber. For three days, the fragrance continuously spread throughout Mecca, and whoever was there was amazed, asking what this fragrance was. The answer would be that the marriage of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), has taken place with Khadija (a.s.). What can be said about Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.)? Who can understand the status of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.)? This is not a trivial matter; she is the mother of all the infallible ones. She is the mother of the one who takes the night of Qadr. What is the reason that I am talking about the status of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.)? To understand the status of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) through the light of her Ma'rifat (gnosis), I would like to quote the scholars of Irfan. Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) uttered a sentence about the history of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.), listen to it. Allama Muhammad Baqir Majlisi has written in his book that Imam Hasan (a.s.) used to say, 'Kuntu ana ashbahu-na bi-Khadijatul Kubra' (I am the one among all people who most resembles Khadijatul Kubra). Imam Hasan (a.s.) says that among all human beings, the one who most resembles Khadijatul Kubra is I, Hasan al-Mujtaba. And here, our scholars have a strange and profound sentence... This is a strange and profound sentence. 'Kuntu ana ashbahu-na...' This is the same 'Kuntu' that appears in the Quran. This is the same 'Kuntu' that appears in the 32nd verse. Meaning, when Allah (s.w.t.) created the form of Imam Hasan (a.s.), at that very moment, He gave Imam Hasan (a.s.) the greatest resemblance to Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). Allah! How great is this matter! If a person thinks about this, many paths of Ma'rifat will open up. Anyway, who knows Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.)? Who knows what the status of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) is? If we go somewhere, for example, and a peon greets us, we feel very proud, thinking, 'Oh, the peon greeted me, people know me here, I am someone important.' What does the world know about what Khadija (a.s.) did? When someone wanted to say something malicious about her, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said a sentence, the summary of which is that until Khadija (a.s.) passed away, until Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) died... Until Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) passed away, whenever Jibra'il (a.s.) brought revelation, the message was for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the greeting (Salam) was for Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). Meaning, whatever revelation Jibra'il (a.s.) brought, in every revelation, he would greet Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). What could be a greater status than the angels greeting her, and Allah (s.w.t.) sending His Salam through Jibra'il (a.s.) to the one who gave everything she had? She gave her wealth, everything, and sacrificed it for the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.). She sacrificed her entire wealth for the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.). She is the one for whose departure, for whose martyrdom, the mourning is being held today. And wherever you are sitting, please pray for Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). Ask Janab-e-Sayyeda (a.s.), the Khatima-e-Zamana, may Allah reward you for this. She gave everything for Islam. This year was a strange year for the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.); in this same year, the martyrdom of Abu Talib (a.s.) occurred, and the martyrdom of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) occurred. The Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) called this entire year 'Aam al-Huzn' (Year of Sorrow). It was a year of grief, a year of mourning. People say 'death of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.)', but I say it was the martyrdom of Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). If you look closely at this, it was a martyrdom... If you look closely, it was a martyrdom because the hardships, the troubles, the difficulties, and the calamities that were inflicted upon Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) in Shi'b Abi Talib—after those calamities, after those troubles, it was indeed a martyrdom. She passed away from this world in pain and suffering in Shi'b Abi Talib. And the state was such that when the time came—think, it must have been the 10th of Ramadan—when Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) was departing from this world, it was a strange scene in Shi'b Abi Talib. The narrations say that Janab-e-Sayyeda (a.s.) was only five years old at that time, and the shadow of her mother was being lifted from her head. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) came near Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) and saw that tears had come to her eyes. He said, 'Khadija, where you are going, there you will meet Maryam (a.s.), there you will meet Asiya (a.s.). Khadija, when you meet them, give them my Salam.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) came out after saying this. A five-year-old Janab-e-Sayyeda (a.s.)—her mother was departing from the world. It is the fate of this household that today she is being martyred, and Zahra (a.s.) is five years old. Tomorrow, Sayyeda (a.s.) will be martyred, and then she will be five years old. Janab-e-Sayyeda (a.s.) came near Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). The mother saw her daughter, tears came to her eyes, and addressing her daughter, she said, 'My darling, I feel shy before your father. Convey my message to your father that if a shroud is not found...' Convey my message to your father that if a shroud is not found, if there is difficulty in finding a shroud, then there is no need to worry. Khadija (a.s.) will give her own kurta (shirt) as a shroud. If a shroud is not found... Who is this lady? This is the lady who sacrificed all her wealth for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), sacrificed it for Islam, and today she has reached a day where she cannot even find a shroud. She said, 'My darling, go and tell your father that if a shroud is not found, it does not matter, there is no need to worry. I will give my kurta as a shroud.' Now, in the narrations, it is mentioned that when Janab-e-Sayyeda (a.s.) went, she would have received the kurta of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) as a shroud. But just look at the tragedy—there is a small child who is being given a burnt kurta as a shroud in Sham-e-Ghariban. Yes, the narrations say that when Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.) was departing from the world, Jibra'il (a.s.) descended from the sky. And after descending, he said, 'Allah (s.w.t.) sends His Salam and greetings. We are sending a shroud from Paradise for Khadija (a.s.). We are sending a shroud from Paradise for Khadija (a.s.).' Allah (s.w.t.) sent a shroud from Paradise for Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). He also sent a shroud from Paradise for Janab-e-Khadija (a.s.). I will fold my hands and say, 'Congratulations, you received a shroud from Paradise.' But in Karbala, there is a stranger who is being given Ghusl with his own blood, who is being buried in the sand, who is being given a shroud of dust, and who is being trampled by the hooves of horses. Allah!... ...
Islam was sustained by the sword of Imam Ali (a.s.) and the wealth of Lady Khadija (s.a.).
Lady Khadija was recognized for her purity and truthfulness long before the advent of Islam.
She transformed her business empire into a source of humanitarian aid, effectively creating the first Bait al-Mal.
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.w.) held her in such high esteem that her passing, alongside Abu Talib, was marked as the 'Year of Sorrow'.

title: Azadaar Ahlebait (a.s.) Ke Saath Hoga Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound spiritual rewards promised by Imam Rida (a.s.) for those who commemorate the tragedies of the Ahlulbayt. It emphasizes that weeping for their oppression and participating in gatherings that keep their cause alive ensures spiritual protection on the Day of Judgment. The message serves as a reminder of the eternal bond between the followers and the Imams, promising companionship in the afterlife for those who remain devoted.
content:
Imam Rida (a.s.) says: 'Whoever mentions our calamities and weeps over the oppression inflicted upon us, he will be with us in our rank on the Day of Judgment. And whoever hears the mention of our calamity and weeps or makes others weep, his eyes will not weep on the day when all eyes will be weeping. And whoever participates in a gathering where our cause is being kept alive, his heart will not die on the day when all hearts will die.'

title: Surah Al-Hamd Recitation Course  (With LIVE Demo) - Session # 5
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive guide to mastering the recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha through the application of Tajweed and Tartil. It emphasizes the spiritual significance of Quranic education and the technical necessity of correct articulation points (makharij) for Arabic letters. The session includes practical demonstrations, feedback on specific letters like 'Dhad', and guidance on maintaining consistent recitation standards for daily prayers.
content:
... May Allah reward all the participants present here. If He permits, we will feel the greatness of Surah Al-Hamd, and you will be able to recite it more correctly. When you recite, do it slowly and steadily, so that the listeners can learn and correct themselves. The Quran itself supports this; the Quranic method of recitation is 'Tartil'. Allah has described the interpretation of 'Tartil' as reading the Quran clearly and distinctly, not like reading prose quickly. The purpose is not just to finish it, and the reason is obvious. Although reciting the Holy Quran is an excellent act, its fundamental purpose is to contemplate its verses and understand its meanings. We should not lose sight of this fundamental purpose, but we should not use this as an excuse to neglect the recitation itself. Friends, let us begin the final program of this series by turning to the presence of the respected Maulana Azad and Abbas Khan Sahab, and request them to speak on a few points so that our knowledge and information may increase. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I hope you are well. By the grace of Allah, we are in this session. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Rasulillahi wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi wa sayyidina Muhammadin wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in. In Surah Al-Muzzammil, you must have seen how beautiful and full of qualities this book is. As beautiful and full of qualities as this book is, and as much light as it contains, it is filled with blessings from every corner. Because it is the enemy of all Satans, all evil, and all darkness, it is the enemy of all those who are spiritually and intellectually corrupt. In every era, people have tried to present a substitute or a rival to the Holy Quran and have tried to diminish its light. Everyone knows that just as our Imams have had enemies, the Holy Quran has also had enemies in every era. Keeping in mind the beauty and qualities of the Holy Quran, and considering the Arabic language and its grammar, the Lord of the Worlds has commanded that it be recited with care, pausing, and tranquility. There are three steps to recitation. I have mentioned this in the introduction several times: reciting slowly, that is, pronouncing every letter from its proper articulation point (makhraj), and... And by following the rules of Tajweed while reciting, this is called 'Tajweed'. After that, reading at a medium pace is called 'Tartil'. There is another name for it, which is 'Tadwir'. And there is another term called 'Tahqiq'. I have mentioned several times that 'Tahqiq' involves the rules of recitation. Keeping the meanings of the verses of the Holy Quran in mind, and looking at the seven 'Ahruf' (modes of recitation), one also looks at the beauty of the recitation. Combining both—the meanings and the beauty of the recitation—is very difficult and is a technical skill that not everyone possesses. We don't have to do that, but we must try to recite at a medium pace. I am not satisfied with the way many people recite the Quran today. There are not just one or two, but hundreds of such instances. It was said that based on these wise teachings and your life, we feel proud... And based on your life, we feel proud that we and you... not only have people praised you in many places, but they have also described your qualities. Among your thousands of countless qualities, one is that the words Imam Ali (a.s.) spoke, the sentences that came from his tongue, were measured. The words were few, but the meaning was like an ocean. The proof is before you. Since I want to move forward quickly, deviating slightly from our topic, we see in this world that if someone is an expert in language, they are a great personality, but their knowledge might be weak. If someone is an expert in knowledge, they might be weak in language. Very few people possess both. And if one looks at other qualities, then very few people are found. But in the land of Arabia, or rather in the entire universe, our Mawla is such a personality... He is such a personality, such a figure in our history, that his speech was matchless, the sentences from his tongue were matchless, and he was matchless on the battlefield. As you know, when he was asked how to recite, he replied by referring to the Quran. In Surah Al-Muzzammil, look, the questioners asked, and the Quran says: 'Wa rattilil-qur'ana tartila' (And recite the Quran with Tartil). What is the meaning of 'Tartil'? Imam Ali (a.s.) explained this meaning. If you look at the history and the narrations, you won't find this definition anywhere else. I am learning, and I am trying to teach. I am making a small effort, so I understand this. The Imam said: 'Tartil is to pronounce the letters correctly...' There is a sentence, and that is why those who were complete in knowledge... That is why those who were complete in knowledge, those who are fond of learning and want to understand and increase their knowledge, should read the books written on the definition of this sentence. You will see that we have to recite the Quran with Tartil. We ask the Mawla himself the meaning of Tartil. He was the greatest scholar of the Quran, who used to recite the Quran in a few moments. His interpretation was not just of someone who understood or heard the Quran, but he was the one who compiled the entire Quran. You collected all the verses of the Quran along with their 'Shane Nuzul' (reasons for revelation). It is a different matter that the court of that time did not accept it. So you said: 'Tartil is to pronounce the letters correctly...' All the articulation points, all the qualities of the letters, all the rules of Tajweed, all the rules of 'Waqf' (pausing) and 'Wasl' (connecting) are included in this. Tell me, our great scholars, our Imams, who have praised it so much—today, most of our community is unaware of it. But it is the grace of Allah that this movement of awakening has started, and... This movement of awakening has started, and it is by the grace of Allah that this work is being done with passion. Although I mentioned earlier that there is a lack in quantity—we haven't reached the masses—but in terms of quality, good work is being done. In India too, our friends have become such that they are competing at the national level. A day will come when this work will grow further. Then, according to the Mawla's command, we must recite the Quran with Tartil. According to the command, we must recite the Quran with Tartil, and the definition of Tartil is to pronounce the letters correctly and to observe the rules of Tajweed. To pronounce the letters correctly means to articulate every letter from its proper place and to observe the rules of 'Waqf' and 'Wasl' in the Quran. I will not go into detail as time will run out; this is enough. Now, you see, regarding learning and teaching the Quran, since this is the last session... Regarding learning and teaching the Holy Quran, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Khairukum man ta'allamal-qur'ana wa 'allamahu' (The best among you is he who learns the Quran and teaches it). He also said: 'Ashraful ummati hamalatul-qur'an' (The most noble of my Ummah are the bearers of the Quran). And finally, you are the ones who learn and teach it. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was asked about the fourth point, he said that those who recite the Quran, especially in this world, wherever they sit to teach someone, all the things present there pray for their forgiveness. And you know that the prayers we make in the Divine Court for ourselves, there is no guarantee whether they will be accepted or not. But some places have been mentioned where, if we pray for others, they are definitely accepted. One is that when we pray, we should try to pray for others. When you pray for others, the Most Gracious and Merciful Lord says that this person is not being selfish; he is praying for his brother or sister... He is praying for his brother or sister, so He says that the angels say, 'Pray for him too.' When the angels pray for the one who is praying, these angels are innocent, so how can their prayers for him not be accepted? Number two: when we pray for someone, before praying for ourselves, we should definitely send blessings (Salawat). Our prayers are often held back, so Allah says, 'I am in the position...' which Imam Sajjad (a.s.) described. He said that when a teacher teaches the Quran to someone, everything present in that place prays for the forgiveness of the teacher. '...wa innal-mala'ikata tastaghfiru li-mu'allimil-qur'an' (And the angels seek forgiveness for the teacher of the Quran). Everything prays for the teacher of the Quran, even the fish in the sea. So, we have to learn the Quran and teach it. And after that, how we should read and how we should teach, we are doing this entire program for that. For now, we have presented a small program before you on how to recite the blessed Surah Al-Hamd. When we recite correctly ourselves, only then can we teach others correctly. In all of this, we have presented the six verses of the first Surah of the Holy Quran, Surah Al-Hamd... Regarding the alarm (Surah Al-Fatiha) that I presented, we discussed the school of thought—not the symptoms—but rather the manual work involved in the recitation. I had asked you to study it. I am still repeating this: first, one must learn the articulation points (makharij) of the letters in the verses of this Surah. Then, one must learn the proper pronunciation. Once these two things are correct, we will move on to the recitation. The target and purpose of this program was that we should at least learn to recite Surah Al-Fatiha correctly. These five or six sessions were not for anything else; I only asked you to recite it every Monday and a few other small things. Our only goal is to learn to recite it correctly because people have little time, and in our society, the Quran has not been given its proper place. Or, we could say that we have not developed the capacity to give the Quran the importance it deserves. We still consider the Quran to be for others, or something to be read only on specific occasions—like when someone is born or when someone passes away. When something special happens, that is when we recite it. We have not given the Quran enough space in our lives. It should be that we are so accustomed to it that we feel restless without it—just like when we look at our mobile phones, we keep opening them and using them; we don't feel at ease otherwise. This means we are not yet so familiar with the Quran that we give it the importance it deserves. Our Imams (a.s.) and our elders gave it importance, so we should at least recite the Quran so that our prayers are not invalidated. I will try to show you how to recite it correctly, as I have taken this upon myself. Today, I will present to you how to recite it, or how to teach others quickly. Let me quickly recite it again as we studied: 'Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim, siratal-ladhina an'amta 'alayhim, ghayril-maghdubi 'alayhim wa lad-dallin.' And 'wa lad-dallin'. Now, this 'ghayri'—we haven't studied this yet. Let's look at it. In India, people in different regions pronounce it differently. I have seen here in Mumbai, and outside Mumbai, that Gujarati speakers—which is their language—have a specific way of speaking. One thing is that 'ghayn' is not 'ghayn'. In Hindi, Gujarati, or Sanskrit, what is the issue? Most people read it as 'kha'. 'Ghayril-maghdubi 'alayhim'—they read the small 'kaf' as a big 'kha'. This is 'ghayril-maghdubi'. And the sad thing is that even in many madrasas, most people teach these same things. People don't read it correctly, so the wrong pronunciation is spreading. We have hundreds of children who have learned it with great effort, saying 'Allahumma kullu...' instead of 'Allahumma qul...' In 'Allahumma qul...', the 'qaf' becomes silent. People often read 'qul' as 'kullu'. Our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) emphasized that whatever your mother tongue is, you must make an effort to correct your recitation or correct the letters of the Quran. The scholars have emphasized that you must recite the letters in prayer correctly. If you haven't learned it correctly, it's not the fault of the Gujarati speakers; they just need to follow the correct pronunciation I am teaching. Now, let's look at the 'ghayn'. They don't have the sound of 'ghayn'; they read it with an 'alif' or 'wa'. If someone who is not a Gujarati speaker is teaching Gujarati children or adults, it is their responsibility to point this out. Just as for hundreds of years everyone has been teaching children 'Alif, Be, Te, Se', we should teach children the Arabic names: 'Alif, Ba, Ta, Tha', so that the pronunciation is correct. The children's pronunciation—those who are teaching them don't even know it themselves. For example, in Surah Al-Fatiha, we have to say 'ghayn'. It comes from the throat. I have told you about the makharij (articulation points). The throat has three parts: the bottom, the middle, and the top. 'Ghayn' and 'kha' come from the top of the throat. And the 'ghayn' is the one with the dot. In Urdu, the sound of 'ghayn'—in Hindi or English, these two sounds are different. If you want to recite the Quran correctly, you have to produce this sound. And if you can't, we cannot say 'I can't do it'. Allah (s.w.t.) will accept the prayers of those whose recitation was correct in His sight, and their sacrifices and efforts in the path of Allah. And their efforts in the path of Allah and in establishing the truth—there are many things, and the Quran is their helper. If we don't do this, we can ask ourselves, 'How many people are there?' But in the second part, you should focus on this, practice it, and learn it. Every task in the world can be done if we want to. This is only a 10-minute task. Understand that every time you recite, if you open your mouth in front of a mirror and stick your tongue out, you will see a curve at the end of the tongue with a piece of flesh; that is where the 'ghayn' starts. From that same place, the letters 'ghayn' and 'kha' will emerge. When we are teaching someone Urdu, we say 'ghayn, ghayn, ghayn'. Even there, they don't pronounce it correctly. They say 'gain, gain'. In Urdu, it is 'gain, gain', but when we are teaching the Quran, we have to say 'ghayn'. In Surah Al-Fatiha, it is 'ghayril-maghdubi'. Before that, there is a 'ya' with a sukoon, and before that, a letter with a fatha. We have to say 'ghayri'. Those who say 'gayri'—I don't think that is correct according to Tajweed. We have to say 'ghayri'. 'Ghayn' is a heavy letter; among the 28 letters, the heavy ones are 'sad, dad, ta, za'—these are the heaviest. After that, there is 'ghayn', which we read heavily: 'ghayn, ghayn, ghayn'. Now, to practice 'ghayri'... To practice 'ghayri', we must focus on the path: 'Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim' (Guide us to the straight path). 'Siratal-ladhina an'amta 'alayhim' (The path of those upon whom You have bestowed Your favor). 'Ghayril-maghdubi 'alayhim' (Not of those who have earned Your wrath). 'Wa lad-dallin' (And not of those who have gone astray). This is the way. If we say 'ghayril-maghdubi', it means the path of those upon whom is Your wrath. In Urdu, we make some mistakes in reading. I have told you that I have studied the Arab recitation. Iranian brothers sometimes pronounce 'ghayn' as 'qaf', and sometimes 'qaf' as 'ghayn'. For example, the word 'al-ghad'—everyone says 'al-qad'... Everyone says 'al-qad'. People do this; they change the letters. This will not work. That is why I am saying that some people follow the Iranian scholars in their recitation, but that is not correct. The scholars are experts in their own right, and there is no doubt that they are the pride of our nation and our scholars, but one must learn the correct recitation. Try to understand what I am saying. I am being very clear so that it becomes obvious. If it is 'ghayri', the Iranian brothers say 'ghayri' as 'qayri'. It is rarely heard, but if they say 'ghayri' by mistake, that is a different matter. If we say 'ghayri', it means 'other than'. We must correct the pronunciation. The meaning is 'other than'. We must correct the pronunciation. And what we are doing here is to fulfill the command given to us. We can do it. 'Ghayril-maghdubi'. We should not say 'gayril'. That is 100% wrong. We should not say 'ghas'. If we say 'gayri', it is wrong according to Tajweed. The evidence is there. You didn't even realize that you had to say 'ghayri'. Every letter has a rule. If anyone remembers, 1400 years ago... About 563 years ago, the 'Babli' channel used to run on the street. For three years during Ramadan, our classes were live continuously, and many people, Masha'Allah, would sit with notebooks to take notes. When they replied, there were problems, and we were the ones who were blamed. We have been there for 21 years, and we had very detailed discussions about Tajweed for about an hour and a half to two hours. Today, we will summarize that in just 5 minutes. And I told you a day or two ago that out of all the things you learned, everything has faded away; only one thing remains: that if you look at the Sunnah and Tajweed, there is no difference in the rules. It is the same. On this basis, Alhamdulillah, I have taught Tajweed to Sunnis, Wahhabis, and Ahl-e-Hadith alike, and in the beginning, I learned it myself. When I was a child in my village, if I knew how to recite the Quran correctly, I could teach the Quran to any Muslim, whether they are from India, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, or anywhere else. There is no difference in the rules of Tajweed; the only difference is that in some areas, we call things by different names. There isn't much of a difference. There isn't much of a difference. Now, listen carefully, because this is the essence of the 59 days of Quranic study. If this is achieved, we will consider it a great accomplishment. I told you that out of the 28 letters, there are 8 letters that are read with a heavy sound. I said that out of those 8, there are 4 that are read with a slightly heavier sound, and the other 4 are a bit lighter. But I said that just as my mouth fills up, every letter should be read that way. And every 'Dhad'—which in Urdu they say is not 'Zwad'—well, I won't talk about that. The 'Dhad' is a bit difficult, and all the... It is a bit difficult, and in the attempt to make it sound better than the others, they ruined it and started reading it like a 'Dal'. But every letter has its own place, its own rule, its own quality, and its own characteristics. So, on the 'Dhad', we were not going towards the goal, just how it is read. We read 'Walad-dalleen', but we heard in our society that 'Walad-dalleen' is being read, and they read it very heavily. But in my opinion, both are wrong. So what is correct? The truth is that the sound comes from the middle, and how will the sound of 'Dal' come out? How will you do it? From here, the upper part... and in the second line, there are 16-32... if I show you my teeth, look at your teeth in the mirror; there are two big teeth at the top, and just below them are two... Just below them are two. These four are called 'Thanaya'. These four are called 'Thanaya'. And right next to them are two above and two below, which are the 'Ruba'iyat'. Out of these, 8 teeth are done: 4 'Thanaya' and 4 'Ruba'iyat'. Then there are the canines above, and below them are the ones called... so that makes 4+4=8. 4 'Thanaya', 4 'Ruba'iyat', 8, and 4 canines make 12. Now, the remaining 20 teeth are next to the canines. I am pointing to my right side; you don't know if it's right or left on the screen. Anyway, I am pointing to the teeth. So, 4 'Thanaya', 4 'Ruba'iyat', 4 'Aniyab', 4+4+4=12. After these 12 teeth, 20 teeth remain in both rows. These are called 'Adras'. I won't talk much about the lips. These 20 teeth are called 'Adras' or 'Athan'. One row is above, and the other row is behind it, and this is my right side... Behind it, and this is my right side. On the left side, there is one row above the teeth, and just below them is the second row. Together, these 20 teeth are called 'Adras'. Now, there are three parts to these. There are 3 groups. Now, the canine teeth I told you about, next to them are two above and two below; their name is 'Dawahik'. The ones that appear when a person smiles, near the canines. After that, there are 3 above on the right and 3 above on the left, and 6 below them. 6 and 6 make 12. These are called 'Tawahin'. They are the ones that grind; the ones at the back are the 'Tawahin'. We chew food with them. Any food we eat, we grind it with these to make it small and fine, so they are called 'Tawahin'. So, there are 12 teeth in total. 4 'Thanaya', 4 'Ruba'iyat', 4 'Aniyab', and 4 'Dawahik'. 16 and 12 make 28. The very last teeth, two above and two below, are called 'Nawajidh', which appear between the ages of 18 and 19... Between the ages of 18 and 19, when a child becomes mature, these appear, so they are called 'Nawajidh'. Now we have named the teeth. Now, these 20 teeth, after the canines, include the 'Dawahik' and 'Tawahin'. Among these, on the left side—my left—the edge of the tongue... the tongue has different parts. The left side, if you place this part of the tongue on the inner side of the upper large teeth, the sound will come out correctly. Because if you... if I give you my WhatsApp number, the second number, and you shouldn't do it, but if you talk to me, he said... the 'Dhad' is also present in the Quran, so this always takes more time... It is always there, so it cannot take much time. I placed it like this, so the edge, the left edge of the tongue, when you place it on the same side, on the left side, on the upper 'Adras' teeth that I mentioned—among the three types, the 'Dawahik' and 'Tawahin'—the inner part of them, if you place it there, the sound will come out correctly. Although we can place the edge of the tongue on any side, on any teeth, above or below, and produce it, but the exact way is to place the left edge of the tongue on the inner part of the large upper teeth on the left side. Then the sound of 'Dhad' will be perfectly correct. Okay, first I will read 'Walad-dalleen'. 'Walad-dalleen'. After the 'Dhad' comes the 'Dal'. Its sound is completely wrong, and in our Urdu language, we read 'Dhad' as 'Dal'. So there is no special benefit in this 'Makhraj'. Now, just like... in this, place the left edge of the tongue on the inner edge of the upper teeth on the left side, and the sound that comes out will be the sound of 'Dhad'. Not the sound of 'Dal'. title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#17 - Kya Ahle Bait (a.s.) Har Zulm Par Khaamosh Rahey?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common misconception that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) remained passive and silent in the face of oppression. The speakers provide historical examples, including Janabe Zahra (s.a.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), and Imam Hussain (a.s.), to demonstrate that they actively protested and defended their divinely appointed rights. By speaking out in public forums and courts, the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) ensured the truth of their Wilayah was clearly communicated to the Muslim community.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. We are presenting another episode of the series addressing the objections raised against the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Before we begin this episode, we first express our heartfelt gratitude to all of you for liking our previous episode so much and for letting us know through your comments and feedback how we can further improve our updates, what other topics we can discuss, and what other objections we can address. Thank you very much. Let us proceed with this episode. Today's topic is that it is often believed that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)—from Janabe Zahra (s.a.) to Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.)—only endured oppression and did nothing but observe patience. Is it really true that the Imams (a.s.) did nothing? To answer this, we have with us our brother, Kamil Deoji Sahab. Brother Kamil, peace be upon you. Peace be upon you too. As you heard the question, people say that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) only endured oppression and never took any action. Is this true? In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah send blessings upon our master, Mufaddal Saifuddin. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. The question you have raised is very important, not just because opponents raise it, but because nowadays, such questions are being raised by many. In our previous episode, we saw that regarding the attack on the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) began their protest and objection right from that moment. And not just there, but they also informed the people that our right was established by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). By looking at this, we will realize that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) clearly presented their stance to the people. It is not that they did nothing; rather, they took every possible step. We will see how they protested. Take the example of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), whose martyrdom we commemorate. When those who came to seize the caliphate arrived at her door, she stood behind the door and said, 'O people, you have left the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) behind and decided your own affairs, ignoring our rights.' It is truly a tragedy that the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was not even considered worthy of being consulted regarding the caliphate. She reminded them, 'Do you not know that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)?' She shattered their hopes for the caliphate, yet they persisted in their own path. She even warned them of the final outcome, saying that Allah is sufficient as a judge between you and us in this world and the hereafter. This was not just a statement of patience; it was a declaration that Allah would judge between them. Furthermore, Imam Hasan (a.s.) also took a stand. Furthermore, there is the incident of Imam Hasan (a.s.). When some people gathered, he testified to the truth of Imam Ali (a.s.) according to the decree of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Then Imam Hasan (a.s.) said, 'O people, you follow the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in many things, but there is one thing on which we differ, and that is the matter of Wilayah.' The Imam then said, 'We do not consider anyone other than the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) worthy of the caliphate, and Allah and His Messenger have made this clear in the Book and in their teachings.' He clearly told the people that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had appointed them. Similarly, there is the incident where Imam Hussain (a.s.) stood on the pulpit of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and asked someone to descend from his grandfather's pulpit. When asked if he did this on his own or if his father told him to, Imam Hussain (a.s.) replied that if his father had told him to, he would have obeyed, as he is the one to follow. He is the one to follow, as the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had designated the houses of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) as the ones to be honored, a fact brought by Jibril (a.s.). No one denied this, yet they acted against it. If someone acts against this, they have forgotten the Book of Allah. The Imam warned the people that if they did not accept this, they would face the consequences. He asked what they would do when they meet the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). If we look at these three, we find a common thread: the most important thing is that Janabe Zahra (s.a.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), and Imam Hussain (a.s.) did not do this in secret. They did not do this in a place where no one was present. They spoke in clear terms in front of the people, in the courts, and in the mosques. None of those people denied that they had usurped their rights. If they were truly on the path of truth, they should have refuted these claims. The fact that they did not is proof that what the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) stated was the absolute truth, and they were realizing their mistake. So, we have seen that the Imams (a.s.) presented their case to the people. Not only them, but the followers of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) also did the same in their lives. For example, there is the famous companion of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Abu Dharr (r.a.). It is well-known among all Muslims that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said about him that no one more truthful than Abu Dharr has walked on earth. He stood before the people and said, 'You know very well that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said that the truth remains with Ali (a.s.) and his progeny, and the incident of Imam Hussain (a.s.) will remain in history.' He asked the people, 'Did you not hear this?' They could not deny it. Thus, we can say that the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) presented the truth before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the people. The Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) clearly told the people that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had appointed them. Every Imam in his time told the people that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had designated them as the leaders. We have seen that when oppression was inflicted upon the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), they observed patience, but they also protested. From Janabe Zahra (s.a.) to Imam Hasan (a.s.), Imam Hussain (a.s.), and companions like Abu Dharr (r.a.), they all protested. With this, the episode concludes. Insha'Allah, we will return soon with a new episode. With which a bread trance and even after its place, until then a little [music]
