title: Mega Winner Announcement | Special Episode | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2025 🎁🎉
excerpt: This special episode of the Panaah-e-Kainaat Mega Quiz 2025 focuses on the spiritual significance of the Ahlulbayt as the divine light and the essential role of the Imam in guiding humanity. The lecture emphasizes the necessity of complete submission, the practice of daily spiritual renewal through Dua-e-Ahad, and the duty of believers to defend the faith intellectually and culturally. It concludes with the announcement of the Mega Quiz winner, highlighting the importance of maintaining a constant, active connection with the Imam of the Time.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Hujjat (proof), son of Al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, subscribe now and do not forget to click the bell icon. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Master, and the best Helper. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the righteous. And may Allah bless our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his purified progeny, from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance, and curse all their enemies. May Allah bless the Greatest Manifestation, the perfection of His ancient splendor, the Tree of Tur, the written Book, the Light upon Light, in the darkness of the night, the guide of guidance, the remover of blindness, the light of the eyes of creation, and Your door through which one is approached, our master and our leader, our Imam, our guide with the truth, and may the curse be upon their enemies, the worshippers of the worshippers and the eternal dwellers. Furthermore, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in His true Book, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'Yuriduna liyutfi'u nurallahi bi-afwahihim wallahu mutimmu nurihi wa law karihal kafirun' (They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it). Sadaqallahul Aliyul Azeem. The Almighty God, in this noble verse whose recitation has been honored, says in this verse: 'Yuriduna liyutfi'u nurallahi bi-afwahihim' (They intend, they want to extinguish the light of Allah by blowing with their mouths). 'Wallahu mutimmu nurihi' (But Allah will bring this light of His to the destination of perfection and completion). Even if the disbelievers dislike it. The Ayah-e-Karima (noble verse) that I have had the honor of reciting, in this verse, Allah promises that He will protect His light. What is this light? This light is the Imams of the Masumeen (a.s.) and in this current era, it is Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) and we are with him. Therefore, you see that in the book 'Al-Kafi', there is a narration where the Imam said to one of his special companions named Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, when Abu Khalid asked the Imam, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.), 'Sa'altu Aba Ja'far (a.s.) an qawlihi' (I asked Abu Ja'far (a.s.) about His saying), regarding this Ayah-e-Karima: 'Fa-aminu billahi wa rasulihi wan-nurilladhi anzalna' (So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down). Abu Khalid al-Kabuli asked about this Ayah-e-Karima. Fa-qala (he said) (a.s.), the Imam replied: 'Ya Aba Khalid! O Abu Khalid! An-nuru wallahi al-a'immatu aali Muhammadin 'alayhimus-salamu ila yawmil-qiyamah' (By Allah, this light is the Imams from the family of Muhammad (a.s.) until the Day of Judgment). Because they are one of the two weighty things (Thaqalayn). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had said exactly this: 'I am leaving among you two precious things, the Thaqalayn: the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahlulbayt.' One is the Book of Allah and the other is my progeny, my Ahlulbayt. And both will remain until the Day of Judgment; the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has promised this. 'Fa-innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayyal-hawd' (They will never separate until they return to me at the Pond). Therefore, the lineage of the Imams of the Masumeen (a.s.) will remain until the Day of Judgment. Then the Imam says: 'Hum wallahi' (By Allah, they are the Imams), 'Nurullahi alladhi anzala' (the light of Allah which He sent down). 'Wa hum wallahi nurullahi fis-samawati wal-ard' (And by Allah, they are the light of Allah in the heavens and the earth). Meaning they are the light of Allah, meaning it is through them that guidance occurs. It is through them that people become guided. If they were not there, people would not receive guidance, just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself prophesied: 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abada' (As long as you hold onto them, you will never go astray after me). You will never wander; you will always remain on the straight path, on the Sirat al-Mustaqim. Who is the Sirat al-Mustaqim? Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is the Sirat al-Mustaqim. On the Sirat al-Mustaqim, 'Walla ya Aba Khalid, ya Aba Khalid, lanurul-imami fi qulubil-mu'minin' (By Allah, O Abu Khalid, the light of the Imam in the hearts of the believers), 'Anwaru minash-shamsil-mudhi'ati bin-nahar' (is brighter than the sun shining in the day). The Imam's light in the hearts of the believers is so bright, so bright, that when the sun shines at its peak during the day with all its brilliance, the Imam's light in the hearts of the believers shines even brighter. Meaning, the sign of faith that is manifest in a believer is because of this light, because of this belief in Imamate, because of this guidance that Allah has destined for the believers. 'Wa hum wallahi yunawwiruna qulub al-mu'minin' (And by Allah, they are the ones who illuminate and brighten the hearts of the believers). 'Wa yahjubullahu nurahum amman yasha' (And Allah hides this light from whom He wills), He makes this light veiled, He hides this light, and they are deprived of this light. Allah does not destine this for everyone; Allah does not put this light in everyone's fate. Allah does not give it to everyone, but only to those for whom Allah has destined faith. This light is not for just anyone. 'Fatazlimu qulubuhum' (So their hearts become dark and gloomy), their souls become dark because they are deprived of this light. That light is the light of the Imam, in this age the light of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). 'Walla ya Aba Khalid' (By Allah, O Abu Khalid), 'La yuhibbuna 'abdun' (No servant loves us), 'Wa yatawallana' (nor accepts our Wilayah), 'Hatta yutahhirallahu qalbahu' (until Allah purifies his heart). Meaning, purity of heart and purity of soul is a sign of faith; it is a condition of faith. It is a condition that this light be illuminated, that this light be bright. If anyone wants to attain this light, they must purify their heart completely from all impurities, from all filth, from all dirt—whether it is material or spiritual—and after that, the Imam says, 'Wa la yutahhirallahu qalba 'abdin' (And Allah does not purify the heart of a servant), now the Imam is setting a condition for how the heart is purified, how the soul is purified. Allah does not purify a servant's soul 'Hatta yusallima lana' (until he submits to us). This is the very first condition: until he bows his head in submission before us, becomes completely submissive to our words, our actions, our commands, our Wilayah, and everything. Until he bows his head in complete submission, Allah will not purify his heart. This means that the level of submission and the degree of surrender will determine the level of light Allah grants him. The more the submission, the more the light; the more the surrender before the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the more this light will be attained, the more this illumination will be received. 'Wa yakuna salman lana' (And he is completely at peace with us), and he is completely submissive to us. 'Fa-idha kana silman lana' (And when he treats us with peace and reconciliation), and in every respect—meaning there should not be even a particle of crookedness, doubt, suspicion, or other heart diseases related to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in his heart—there should not be even a particle of doubt, not even a particle of enmity or stubbornness. 'Sallamahullahu min shadidil-hisab' (Allah will save him from the severe reckoning). If someone comes before Allah on the Day of Judgment in this state, Allah will protect him from the severe reckoning of the Day of Judgment. He will have no need to worry about the accounting. Allah will protect him, and on the Day of Judgment, in the stage of the 'Faza-e-Akbar' (the greatest fear)—meaning the greatest fear of the Day of Judgment (there are 50 stages of the Day of Judgment, 50 stations of the Ma'ad, and the most terrifying one is called 'Faza-e-Akbar' in the terminology of the Quran and narrations)—Allah will keep him in a state of peace and security in that station of Faza-e-Akbar. This is the stage where he will be completely safe, while others will be distressed. Others will be fearful and will want to receive light. Remember, one thing should be preserved in your noble minds: the only place to attain this light is this world. Apart from this world, if anyone thinks they can attain it in the Hereafter, they will not get it there. Whatever he attains in this world, that much share of light will remain in the Hereafter. The amount of Wilayah, love, and affection for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in his heart, that much light he will have, and that much his existence will be illuminated and bright on the Day of Judgment. And accordingly, he will walk with that light on the Day of Judgment. This is reflected in Surah Al-Hadid, that those who were completely devoid of the light of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in this world—they neither had the belief of Wilayah, nor did they believe in the Imamate of the Ahlulbayt, but rather believed in the Wilayah of others—they had abandoned the Ahlulbayt. They had forsaken the Ahlulbayt. They only called themselves Ahlulbayt by name, but they had nothing of their Imamate, their Wilayah, their Hadith, or their narrations. They were completely deprived; they had nothing. So, when they rise on the Day of Judgment without light—it is a verse of Surah Al-Hadid—they will say to the people of faith, 'Can we get some of your light?' They will be told, 'No, go back to the world now. Faltamisu nura (Seek light there).' Now there is no possibility of going back to the world, no way, no method, no path. There is no path to return to the world. Now this is the Day of Judgment. They will beg for light, they will beg for the charity of faith on the Day of Judgment, and from whom will they beg? From the possessors of faith, because they will see that the existence of the possessors of faith is completely bright and illuminated. Therefore, they will want to attain that light because the possessors of faith are walking in light, and these people without faith are walking in darkness, because one person will not be able to benefit from the light of another person on the Day of Judgment. Whoever has as much light will benefit from his own light. Therefore, Allah will protect them in the Faza-e-Akbar. So the question arises: how do we know how connected we are to our Imam-e-Zamana, how attached we are, how strong our relationship is with our Imam? Look, if we want to know how much we love our Imam, some signs are mentioned in the narrations. One sign is that when the Ahlulbayt are happy, we should be happy. We should be happy in their happiness. When they are sorrowful, we should be sorrowful. We should be sorrowful in their sorrow. Look, when it is their time of happiness, no matter how great our own sorrow may be, we should celebrate their happiness. Our sorrows, our troubles, our problems, our pain and suffering are nothing compared to the happiness of the Imam and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And likewise, when the Ahlulbayt are sorrowful, we should be sorrowful, even if we have some great happiness of our own. For example, during the days of mourning (Ayyam-e-Aza), one should not congratulate others. Many people say 'Mubarak, Mubarak.' No, congratulations are not given during the days of mourning. Wait, be patient. When the days of mourning are over, then offer congratulations or accept them. This is a sign of faith. This is 'Afrahuna li-farahina wa yahzanuna li-huznina' (They rejoice in our happiness and grieve in our sorrow). And pray as much as possible for the Imam. 'Akthiru ad-du'a bi-ta'jilil-faraj fa-inna dhalika farajukum' (Increase the prayer for the hastening of the Faraj, for that is your own relief). Meaning, in Usul al-Kafi, there is a narration that a man came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'I keep my Durood and Salawat, meaning my prayers, sometimes one-third for you.' Then after a while, he said, 'No, rather sometimes I keep half of my Durood and half of my prayers for you.' Meaning half for myself, half for you. He says, 'No, rather sometimes I pray only for you, meaning for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), and I don't pray any other prayer at all. Only for you, only for your sake.' Look how great a thing this is. He doesn't pray for himself. As soon as he said this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, saying that if you do this, then be certain that Allah will take care of all your troubles in this world and the Hereafter, in your religion and your world. Allah will make him needless of troubles, He will make you needless. Because you have prayed for our sake, we will take care of you. You have prayed for us, we will pray for you because He is Generous. And if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prays for someone, then the Prophet and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) are 'Mustajab-ud-Da'wah' (those whose prayers are answered). It is mandatory and necessary for their prayers to be answered. It is a duty that their prayers be answered. Whether our prayers are answered or not, there is always a question mark about that. But the prayer of the Prophet and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), if they pray for someone—and the most important thing is that at every moment, every instant, every second, one should be ready for the support, service, and defense of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Cultural defense in today's age. If someone is objecting to Imamate, if someone is saying absurd things, then defend, answer them. Of course, a cultural answer, a cultural defense according to today's age. Meaning, try to become like the 'Shurtat al-Khamis' of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had some companions who were called 'Shurtat al-Khamis'. Look, I will mention some narrations about the Shurtat al-Khamis very quickly because time is short. A person asked Asbagh ibn Nubata, who was called a 'Mawla', and was part of the Shurtat al-Khamis. That person asked Asbagh, 'Kayfa sammaytahumu Shurtat al-Khamis ya Asbagh?' (How did you give them this name, Shurtat al-Khamis, O Asbagh?). 'Fa-qala' (He said), Asbagh said, 'Inna daminna lahu az-zaba' (We guaranteed him our slaughter). We said that we are ready, meaning we have pledged ourselves. For what? To be slaughtered. We are ready to be slaughtered in your path. 'Wa damina lahu al-fath' (And he guaranteed us victory). He guaranteed us victory. 'You are ready to do this in my path, I guarantee you victory that you will certainly be successful.' And this same question was asked by Abu al-Jarud, meaning Ziyad ibn Mundhir, to Asbagh ibn Nubata. Because Asbagh was very close to the Mawla of the universe and loved him very much. Asbagh ibn Nubata loved him very much. So Ziyad ibn Mundhir, meaning Abu al-Jarud, asked, 'Ma kana manzilatu hadhar-rajuli fikum' (What was the status of this man among you?). Meaning, what was the question? What was the status of Amir al-Mu'minin in your view? What was their status in your view? Meaning, how much importance did you give them? How much importance? Look, this was the actual question of Abu al-Jarud to Asbagh, but we can ask this same question to ourselves today: how much importance does the Imam-e-Zamana have in our view? How much importance? 'Qala ma adri ma taqulu' (He said, I don't understand what you are saying). Asbagh said, 'I don't understand what you are saying.' Just this much: 'Illa anna suyufana kanat 'ala 'awatiqina' (Except that our swords were on our shoulders). 'Fa-man awma'a ilayna' (And whoever gestured towards us), and meaning, whoever looked at us even with a slightly crooked glance, 'Awma'a' refers to a gesture, 'Ima' refers to a sign. Meaning, if anyone even looked with a slightly evil intention at the Mawla of the universe, because these people used to surround the Mawla of the universe. If anyone looked with an evil eye, ﴿ضَرَبْنَا بِهَا﴾ we would immediately attack them and strike them with our swords. ﴿وَكَانَ يَقُولُ﴾ And the Master of the Universe (a.s.) used to say, he would say to us, ﴿تَشَرَّطُوا فَوَاللَّهِ مَا اشْتَرَطْتُكُمْ لِذَهَبٍ وَلَا فِضَّةٍ﴾ 'Pledge yourselves to me; I do not ask you for gold or silver. I do not want gold or silver. I only want one thing, and that is that you are prepared to sacrifice your lives.' ﴿إِنَّ قَوْمًا مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ تَشَاطَرَ تَشَارَطُوا بَيْنَهُمْ فَمَا مَاتَ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ حَتَّى كَانَ نَبِيَّ قَوْمِ نَبِيٍّ﴾ Meaning, the Master (a.s.) says that whoever among the Children of Israel accepted this condition became a prophet. The only difference is that you are not prophets. You are not prophets, but in terms of status and rank, you are very exalted. This is the 'Shurtat al-Khamis' (The Vanguard). That is why, when Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Hazmi was martyred in the Battle of Jamal, the custom of the Master of the Universe (a.s.) was that when the battle ended, he would go and inspect his companions to see who had been martyred. So when the Imam (a.s.) saw Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Hazmi on the day of the Battle of Jamal, the Master (a.s.) said, ﴿أَبْشِرْ يَا ابْنَ يَحْيَى﴾ 'Rejoice, O son of Yahya, for you shall have glad tidings.' ﴿فَإِنَّكَ وَأَبُوكَ فَإِنَّكَ وَأَبُوكَ مِنْ شُرْطَةِ الْخَمِيسِ حَقًّا﴾ 'Verily, you and your father were truly among the Shurtat al-Khamis.' Shurtat al-Khamis means those who were my defenders, those who were among my protectors. And this title was bestowed upon you by Allah, Shurtat al-Khamis. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) informed me of this, saying, 'O Ali! This title for those who will be your defenders was given by Allah: Shurtat al-Khamis for you.' ﴿سَمَّاكُمْ شُرْطَةَ الْخَمِيسِ عَلَى لِسَانِ نَبِيِّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ﴾ So this is the status of the Shurtat al-Khamis, and that is why, now look, this is the important thing here. A narration related to this. That if a person does not attach their heart to the Imam, does not draw near to the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.), and is not prepared to defend the Imam, then there is no other path for them except misguidance; there is no path other than Hell. Look, listen to the Hadith; this narration is found in Rijal al-Kashshi, that indeed Amr al-Hamdani says that the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) passed by us. Indeed, Ibn Amr al-Hamdani was also among the Shurtat al-Khamis. So he says that we, the lovers of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), were all sitting when the Master (a.s.) passed by us. He said (a.s.), 'Remain in this Shurta (vanguard).' Look, remain in this state, remain in this, meaning remain in the defense of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), in the defense of Ali (a.s.), in the defense of the Progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and in today's age, remain in the defense of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.). Do not leave it. Keep defending the Imam of the Time. Do not lag behind in the defense of the Imam of the Time. 'For by Allah, there is nothing after them except the vanguard of the Fire,' that is, by God, there is nothing after them except the people of Hell, that is all. The Master (a.s.) swears by God. Whoever abandons the path of defense has no other path except Hell. 'Except for those who perform deeds like their deeds.' Except for the person who performs the same actions that the Shurtat al-Khamis were performing. Meaning, among the other companions of the Imams who performed this task, those who did what the companions of Ali (a.s.) did, they will have the same rank as the defenders of Ali (a.s.)—that is, Paradise was for them, and they had the station that belongs to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And there are many narrations in this regard, many Hadiths that they will be with us in the highest Paradise, they will be with us in this station. And there were many such companions of the Imams (a.s.) and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), like Amr ibn al-Hamiq al-Khuza'i, Qambar; you can read their narrations, study the Hadiths. You will see that these were people who would not tolerate even an atom's worth of disrespect towards the status of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The martyrs of Karbala, the martyrs of the Master of Martyrs (a.s.), how they defended the Master of Martyrs (a.s.), sacrificing their lives—they even gave their lives—but when they were breathing their last, they would ask, 'Have we fulfilled the right of loyalty?' This is the Shurtat al-Khamis. These are the defenders. Meaning, these Shurtat al-Khamis are those who truly love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who do not look at day or night, do not look at heat or cold, do not sell their faith for the sake of expediency, and do not get scared by small things. They are not like that. Therefore, it is very necessary to be prepared for the defense of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Intellectual defense, cultural defense. If someone attacks the creed, answer them, answer them with the pen. But for that, 'Marifat' (gnosis/knowledge) is necessary. For that, knowledge is necessary. Until there is knowledge, until there is Marifat, how can a person defend? Can an ignorant person who is not educated at all, who knows nothing, who has absolutely no Marifat, can they defend? No, rather, if the situation changes even slightly, they will change. Therefore, try to be as the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) want you to be. Look at Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi; he was a resident of Ahwaz and loved the Imam very much, the 12th Imam. He had so much love in his heart for the Imam, such a longing for the Imam's vision, that he went on Hajj 20 times just to meet the Imam, because it is found in narrations that the Imam is present at the Hajj every year. The Imam always comes. He is at the Hajj every year. So Ali ibn Mahziyar performed Hajj for 20 years. In that era, performing Hajj was very difficult. It is not like today's era where it is very easy. It was very hard, very difficult. But Ali ibn Mahziyar went, and when he went on Hajj 20 times and did not meet the Imam, he became disappointed. He said, 'I will not go anymore. It seems the Master does not want to grant me a vision. I do not have the merit for a vision.' Ali ibn Mahziyar is now sleeping. The Hajj season drew near. He saw someone in a dream saying, 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, wake up and prepare for Hajj. This year your wish will be fulfilled. This year your desire will be fulfilled in Hajj.' The story is very long. In short, a person came and took him, and near Taif—Taif is a city near Medina and Mecca, a hill station—he took him near Taif, and there Ali ibn Mahziyar met the Imam. As soon as Ali ibn Mahziyar appeared, do you know what was said in that era? The Imam said, 'O Abul Hasan'—his name was Ali, so his kunya was Abul Hasan—'O Abul Hasan, we were waiting for you day and night.' The Imam says, 'We were waiting day and night for you to come, to come for a meeting.' 'What caused you to delay in meeting us?' Think about it, Ali ibn Mahziyar is going on Hajj 20 times to meet the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.), and the Imam is saying, 'Why such a delay in meeting?' 'I said: My Master, I did not find anyone to guide me until now.' O my Sayyid, my Master, I did not find anyone who would guide me, who would lead me, who would bring me to you. The Imam immediately turned and asked, 'Did you not find anyone to guide you?' Meaning, what are you saying? You didn't find anyone to guide you? Are you saying such a thing? 'Then he tapped the ground with his finger,' then the Imam began to write something on the ground with his finger, in that way. 'Then he said: May Allah hasten his noble reappearance,' then the Imam said, 'No, that was not the reason. That was not the reason. But you were busy accumulating wealth.' The reason was that you were busy accumulating wealth. 'And you were arrogant towards the weak believers.' And you were oppressing the weak believers. You were using oppression against them, you were oppressing them. 'And you severed the ties of kinship' that were between you and your relatives; you cut off your relations with them. You broke your ties with them. 'So what excuse do you have?' Now, after these three things, what excuse do you have? Meaning, you were busy accumulating wealth, you were oppressing the weak believers, and you were severing ties with your relatives. Now what excuse do you have? With what face could you come to us? 'So what excuse do you have?' Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi immediately realized his shortcomings, his sins. He said, 'Repentance, repentance, forgive me, forgive me.' 'Iqala' means forgive me, pardon me. Then he said, 'May Allah hasten his noble reappearance.' Then the Imam said, 'O son of Mahziyar! If it were not for the seeking of forgiveness by some of you for others, everyone on earth would have perished, except for the special Shias.' So everyone in the world is saved only because of this seeking of forgiveness. No one would have survived, except for the special Shias. And what is the sign of these special Shias? The Imam says, 'Those whose words resemble their deeds.' That there is no contradiction between their speech and their actions. What they preach, they practice. Look at this Hadith, this short Hadith which is in Dala'il al-Imamah, page number 297, page number 297, by Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari. Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Rustam al-Tabari was a Shia scholar, yes? In his book, 'Dala'il al-Imamah', the Imam explains the reasons why we are distant from the Imam. Or rather, why the Imam is veiled from us. This is the wrath of the Lord. When Allah is displeased with His servants, the Imam says, 'He distances us, the Ahlulbayt, from their proximity, from their neighborhood.' That is why we must strive to be as close to the Imam as possible. We must try to defend the Imam through 'Ma'rifat' (gnosis) and knowledge. Acquire knowledge, acquire Ma'rifat. Reach the highest levels of Ma'rifat and knowledge. Be close to the Imam through supplications. Recite Dua-e-Ahad daily. Never miss Dua-e-Ahad. And especially, I request the youth, the teenagers, and the children to memorize Dua-e-Ahad. Parents should ensure their children memorize Dua-e-Ahad. If someone recites Dua-e-Ahad consistently for 40 days, even if they pass away before the reappearance (Zuhur) of the Imam, when the Imam reappears, he will bring them out from their grave and count them among his companions. That is why a sentence in Dua-e-Ahad says, 'Allahummaj'alni min ansarihi wa a'wanihi.' O Lord! Count me among the helpers and supporters of the Imam-e-Zaman. 'Ansar' is derived from 'Nasir'. Nasir means a helper. And 'A'wan' means 'Mu'awin', meaning those who help the Imam-e-Zaman in his tasks. 'Wa dhabina 'anhu'—and those who defend the Imam. 'Dhab' means to defend. 'Wa dhabina 'anhu wal musari'ina ilayhi fi qada'i hawa'ijihi.' And count me among those who rush, meaning run quickly, to fulfill the needs of the Imam. 'Wal muhamina 'anhu'—and those who protect the Imam, support the Imam, and defend the Imam. In today's age, defending Wilayat. In today's age, defending Azadari. Even if it brings them personal infamy, they will defend Wilayat. They will defend the Princess (Sayyeda Zainab). They will defend the Azadari of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada. 'Wa sabiqina ila iradatihi'—and they will try to outdo one another to fulfill the Imam's will. 'Sabiqina' means to compete, to race, so that they reach before their peers to fulfill the Imam's will. And finally, 'Wal mustashhidina bayna yadayhi.' O Lord! Grant us the fortune that when our soul departs, it departs while we are in the company of the Imam. May we attain martyrdom with the Imam, may we attain martyrdom in the Imam's company. And that is why 'Allahumma inni ujaddidu lahu fi sabihati yawmi hadha wa ma ishtu min ayyami 'ahdan wa 'aqdan wa bay'atan.' Daily, I renew, I renew the oath of allegiance. I renew it. Daily, as long as I live, 'wa ma ishtu min ayyami'—as long as I live, 'ahdan wa 'aqdan wa bay'atan lahu fi 'unuqi'—the oath of allegiance to the Imam that is upon my neck, 'la ulu'nu wala azulu abada.' I will never remove this yoke of allegiance from my neck. This covenant is Dua-e-Ahad, which is why it is called Dua-e-Ahad. 'Ahad' means covenant, 'Ahad' means promise. So, memorize this dua. Ensure you recite Dua-e-Nudba every Friday. Wherever you live, ensure the recitation of Dua-e-Nudba. People should come, participate, and this is a sign of love. Otherwise, mere verbal love and expressing love only once a year is not enough; day and night, day and night, this is the expression of love. 'Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil 'alamin wa sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin wa la'natul da'ima 'ala a'daihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim wa munkiri fada'ilihim wa manaqibihim wa mukhalifi aqwalihim wa ahkamihim.' Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad. Yes, may He grant everyone the reward and merit of Ziyarat according to their intentions. And to whoever the winner is, we humbly request that whenever you go for Ziyarat, please go on behalf of all the members of the TSR team and everyone who participated in this quiz. So, viewers, the time has come that you all have been waiting for impatiently. That is, the announcement of the mega winner of the Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz 2025, which is being selected through our computerized lucky draw system. The winner will receive the prize that every lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) desires. That is, the prize of Ziyarat of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimiya, and Samarra—the Ziyarat of Iraq. So, let's see who that lucky person is, and their name is on your screen. Arzoo Fatima from Mumbra. Many congratulations to you for being the lucky one who has won the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. The TSR team is once again grateful to all you viewers. Do remember us in your prayers so that the Almighty grants us the ability to organize such quizzes. And if you have any feedback or suggestions regarding this series, please send them to our WhatsApp number [number removed]. If you also want to join us in spreading the message of Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt (a.s.), you just need to subscribe to our channel. Like our videos and share them with your contacts so that the message of Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt (a.s.) reaches as many people as possible. Furthermore, if anyone wants to join this noble cause through donations, they can donate via the provided bank account details or by scanning the QR code. Allah and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will grant the complete reward for this, Insha'Allah. We pray in the court of the Almighty that He hastens the reappearance of the Heir of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the Imam of our time, and grants us the ability to hold firmly onto the Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt (a.s.) until the very end. And may He count those who share our videos with others among those who propagate the Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ameen ya Rabbal Alameen. Insha'Allah, we will meet again in our upcoming quiz. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah. Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Ziyaarat During War & Fear [ENG SUBS] | #arbaeen #ziyarat #arbaeen2026
excerpt: This lecture discusses the spiritual significance and immense rewards of performing Ziyarat to the shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.) despite facing fear or danger. The speaker cites narrations from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir, emphasizing that the difficulty and fear endured during the pilgrimage are directly proportional to the divine rewards received. The talk concludes with a prayer for the safety of pilgrims and the hastening of the reappearance of Imam Mahdi.
content:
Haydar, Haydar, Haydar... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. It is the command of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.): 'Never abandon the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) due to fear. Because whoever abandons it will surely regret it and will wish that their grave were near the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Do you not want Allah to see you among those for whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Ali, Fatima, and all the Imams (a.s.) pray? Do you not want to be counted among those who return to the court of Allah in such a state that all their past sins have been forgiven, and your 70 years of sins have been pardoned? Do you not like to become like the person who rises from this world in such a state that no sin remains upon his head, and do you not want the Messenger of Allah to shake your hand on the Day of Judgment?' Furthermore, it is found in another Hadith that the eminent companion Muhammad ibn Muslim (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) asked me, 'Do you go for the Ziyarat of the holy grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.)?' I replied, 'Yes, but in a state of fear and terror.' Upon this, the Imam (a.s.) stated, 'The more difficult this Ziyarat is, the greater its reward will be in proportion to its fear. Whoever comes for this Ziyarat in a state of fear, Allah will transform his fear into security on the Day of Judgment. On the day when all humans will be present before the Lord of the Worlds, this person will be present with forgiveness. The angels will greet him, and the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) will come to visit him and pray in his favor, due to which that person will return with the bounty and grace of Allah. No evil will touch him, and he will be a follower of Divine pleasure.' If we reflect, both Hadiths have a very deep connection with the noble personality of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). On one hand, his shaking hands with them, and on the other hand, his coming to visit the pilgrim of his grandson and praying for him, itself tells us how dear the Ziyarat of Aba Abdillah al-Hussain (a.s.) is to the Prophet. This is our prayer in the court of the Lord of the Worlds: regardless of the circumstances, grant us the opportunity for this Ziyarat every year, and to make the path of this Ziyarat completely easy and to erase all kinds of fear, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. Heart and soul, our oppressed one, our oppressed one, our oppressed one.

title: EP24 | Ayat-e-Tatheer: Ahle Bait (a.s.) Ya Azwaaj? | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi provides a theological analysis of the Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tatheer) to clarify its specific application to the Ahl al-Bayt. By examining the linguistic and thematic context of Surah Al-Ahzab and Surah At-Tahrim, the speaker distinguishes between the instructions given to the Prophet's wives and the inherent purity attributed to the Ahl al-Bayt. The presentation emphasizes the necessity of objective Quranic study to understand the unique status of the Prophet's household.
content:
Presenting PSR. Ashhadu anna Aliyan Waliullah. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjah, son of al-Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him inhabit Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his supporters, his Shia, his servants, and his followers, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. The discussion reached the point that some people tried to apply this Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tatheer) to the wives, and at the top of the list is the name of Fazl ibn Ruzbahan al-Nishapuri, who said that contrary to the majority of exegetes, the majority of exegetes believe that this verse was revealed in honor of the wives and it also has relevance to the arrangement of the Quran. So, it was submitted to you, what is meant by this arrangement of the Quran? Look, there are two things: one is the revelation of the Quran and the other is the order, meaning the arrangement of the Quran, arranging the Quran. So, it is obvious that the Quran was revealed to the Prophet, but the Prophet did not arrange it, and this history is famous, everyone agrees on this, no one denies this. Anyway, so what Fazl ibn Ruzbahan said about the majority of exegetes, first of all, he did not bring any evidence. Meaning, he should have brought it—how many exegetes say this? How many exegetes? He should have brought a list, right? And he should have answered their arguments as well. Anyway, we see that this verse is the verse of infallibility (Ismah). It is the verse of the infallibility of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). It is announcing their purity, it is announcing their cleanliness. And wherever the mention of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) has occurred in the Holy Quran, there is nothing there except virtues and merits. But did Allah use the same tone for the wives? So let us study that too. Look, this is not our perspective, nor your perspective, from the Quran. These are the verses of the Quran, and no Muslim can ever deny them. Look at this verse, in the same Surah al-Ahzab in which this Verse of Purification is, in the same one in which these people thought that we would put this Verse of Purification here, so it would apply to the wives. Now, look at how the wives are mentioned, and in what tone, so that the matter becomes clear to everyone. This is verse number 28. Verse number 28. Allah says: 'Ya ayyuhan-Nabi' (O Prophet), 'Qul li-azwajika' (say to your wives), 'in kuntunna turidnal-hayatad-dunya wa zinataha' (if you desire the life of this world and its adornments, the luxuries of this place), 'fata'alayna umatti'kunna wa usarrihkunna sarahan jamila' (come, I will provide for you whatever worldly wealth you desire and then I will release you, I will let you go, finished. I will release you in a beautiful manner). I have nothing to do with you. This is a verse from Surah Al-Ahzab; you can check it. And after that, it says that if you desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, then Allah has prepared many good things for you, a great reward. For those among you who are 'muhsanat' (virtuous), for those among you who are good wives, Allah has prepared a great reward. Look, this is a Quranic verse. Now you have to decide, for the Quran says: 'Fa-innallaha a'adda lil-muhsanati minkunna' (Indeed, Allah has prepared for the virtuous among you), meaning for those who are good among the wives, there is a great reward. This implies that for those who are not good, there is not a great reward. Now, however you wish to interpret this, we are not interpreting it. After that is verse number 30, look at what it says: 'Ya nisa-an-Nabi' (O wives of the Prophet), 'man ya'ti minkunna bifahishatin mubayyina' (if any of you, O wives of the Prophet, were to commit a clear indecency), God forbid—we are saying 'God forbid', it is not in the Quran—if one commits a clear indecency, this is a Quranic verse. Look, not a single word is ours. Then what will happen? 'Yuda'af lahal-'adhabu di'fayn' (Allah will inflict double the punishment on such a wife, on the wife of the Prophet). He will subject her to double the punishment. 'Wa kana dhalika 'alallahi yasira' (And that is easy for Allah). And likewise, if she does good deeds, obeys Allah and His Messenger, performs worship, and does all good things, then for her, there is a double reward. Then after that, look at verse number 32: 'Ya nisa-an-Nabi, lastunna ka-ahadin minan-nisa' (O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women). 'Fala takhda'na bil-qawl' (Look, when you speak to men, do not speak in a soft tone). Otherwise, 'fayatma'alladhi fi qalbihi marad' (those in whose hearts is a disease will have dirty thoughts about you). A desire will be born in their minds. It is forbidden. Do not speak in a soft tone. This is being said to the wives of the Prophet. 'Wa qulna qawlan ma'rufa' (And speak honorable words, but not in a soft tone). And then after that is verse number 33, which is the very Verse of Purification (Ayat al-Tat'hir), the first part of which I presented to you: stay in your homes and do not display yourselves like the display of the times of ignorance (Jahiliyyah), meaning without veil, without hijab, adorned. Perform prayer and fasting, pay Zakat, and obey the Messenger of Allah. And then the tone of the Quran changes: 'Allah only intends to remove from you, O Ahl al-Bayt, all impurity and to purify you with a thorough purification.' Now tell me, how much difference is there between the two? Be fair, look, be fair. You will clearly see the difference. Study it, sit down and study. Reflect and ponder upon it. And if Allah is forbidding certain things and forbidding them very strictly, are there examples of this in history or not? This should be studied. In our opinion, it should be studied whether, regarding the things that were forbidden, anyone acted upon them or committed them or not? This is a matter worthy of study. Look, nothing is solved by working with prejudice and bias. That is one thing. Now another example—there are many examples, but we are keeping it very brief. Okay? Look, another example for you, this is the occasion of revelation (Sha'n-e-Nuzul) for verses 3 and 4 of Surah At-Tahrim. Surah At-Tahrim is Surah number 66. Verses 3 and 4. What is the background? The background is that the Prophet had a wife named Janabe Mariya al-Qibtiyya (peace be upon her). Umm al-Mu'minin, a very good woman, Janabe Mariya al-Qibtiyya. Qibtiyya means Egyptian; she was Egyptian. The King of Egypt had gifted her to the Prophet. That is why they call her Qibtiyya. Qibtiyya in English is called Coptic. Meaning Coptic, she was an Egyptian woman. But it is found in books of Hadith, the background of which I am presenting to you, that there were two wives of the Prophet who did not like the fact that the Prophet was spending time with Janabe Mariya. There were two wives. Now, they are mentioned; I will not take their names, you can see for yourselves. What those people did was put pressure on the Prophet: 'Why do you give her so much time? Why do you talk to her?' Because jealousy was born in their hearts. So they pressured the Prophet. And obviously... ...after that, Surah At-Tahrim was revealed. The first verse, the second verse of Surah At-Tahrim, all were revealed. Allah says, 'Ya ayyuhan-Nabi' (O Prophet), why are you forbidding for yourself what Allah has made lawful for you, Mariya? And why are you listening to these two wives of yours? Do not listen to them. Do not come under their pressure. I am saying this in my own words so that the children can understand. Now listen to the third verse. Anyway, we have little time, so we are coming directly to the third verse. Otherwise, read the whole Surah At-Tahrim, read the four or five verses. When the Prophet told these two wives of his that the verse had been revealed and this had happened, Allah had placed a condition: 'Brother, do not tell anyone. Look, I am telling you, do not tell anyone.' The Prophet said to both of them, 'Look, do not tell anyone.' He set a condition. Do not betray the trust. This is only for you, do not tell anyone. But the Quran says, 'Fa lamma nabba'at bihi' (But when she told it to others). She told others. 'Wa azharahullahu 'alayh' (And Allah made it known to the Prophet) that your wife had told it. 'Arafa ba'dahu wa a'rada 'an ba'd' (So the Prophet made some things known and ignored some). We are not going into other details right now, we are keeping it very brief, just to the translation and one Hadith, that's all. Otherwise, if we go into details, it would require a lot of time and you might get bored; it would become too much of a discussion. Therefore, very brief. Limit ourselves to the Quranic verse and one Hadith, Bukhari's Hadith, that's all. So, 'A'rada 'an ba'd, fa lamma nabba'a bihi' (He ignored some, and when he told her about it), when the Prophet told his wife that this is Allah's command, that Allah had revealed that you did this thing, even though I had forbidden you not to tell, then she turns and asks the Prophet, 'Man anba'aka hadha?' (Who told you this?). Now, can anyone ask the Prophet this? If someone believes in the Prophet's mission and prophethood, can they ask the Prophet who told him? Where did you get the news? This means there is a doubt about his prophethood. There is a doubt about the Prophet's prophethood. 'Man anba'aka hadha?' The Prophet immediately replied. This is a Quranic verse, we are reading the verse of Surah At-Tahrim. 'Nabba'ani al-'Alimul-Khabir' (The All-Knowing, the All-Aware God told me). Then in verse number four, 'In tatuba ilallahi faqad saghat qulubukuma' (If you both repent to Allah, then your hearts have already inclined), meaning your hearts are still inclined towards that, meaning all those things will happen. Okay? Meaning you are creating these problems for the Prophet in some way. 'Wa in tazahara 'alayh' (And if you support each other against him), look, if you have repented, then it is fine, but if you have done this against the Prophet, meaning pressured the Prophet and shown enmity towards the Prophet, 'fa innallaha huwa mawlahu' (then indeed Allah is his protector). The Prophet's Mawla is Allah. 'Wa Jibrilu wa salihul-mu'minina wal-mala'ikatu ba'da dhalika zahir' (And Jibril and the righteous among the believers and the angels, after that, are his supporters). And Jibril and after that the righteous believers, meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the angels, all are the Prophet's supporters. Allah is the Mawla, and Jibril and the righteous believers, meaning Amir al-Mu'minin, and the angels, all these are the Prophet's supporters. So you will not be able to stand before Allah, Jibril, the righteous believers, and the angels. These are absolutely clear Quranic verses, look. We are not saying anything from ourselves. Now look at the narration in the context of this verse. The Hadith is like this: 'An Ibn Abbas radiyallahu 'anhuma' (According to him). As it is, we are reading it out. 'Qala kuntu uridu an as'ala 'Umara' (It is written in it, 'radiyallahu 'anhu', I intended to ask Umar), 'anil-imaratayn' (about those two women), 'allataini tazaharata 'alan-Nabi' (sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam). 'Alayhi'—no, look, pay attention to the sentence of the Hadith. About those two women who 'tazahara' (supported each other/conspired) against the Prophet. What was the Quranic verse? What was the verse of Surah At-Tahrim? What was verse number four? 'In tatuba ilallahi' (Either repent). 'Wa in tazahara' (But if you 'tazahara'—conspired), but if you conspired against the Prophet, created problems for the Prophet, protested, demonstrated, caused the Prophet distress, then here, this Hadith of Ibn Abbas shows that they did not repent. They did not repent, they conspired. We are reading the Hadith, look. Not a single word from ourselves. 'Tazaharrata 'alan-Nabi' (They conspired against the Prophet). So I saw the opportunity was good to ask, 'Fa adraktuhu' (I reached near him), 'fa sa'altuhu' (and I asked him this question). 'Fa qala 'Umar, 'Umar, 'A'ishatu wa Hafsatu' (Who were they? Aisha and Hafsa). Now you see, you have seen the verses of Surah Al-Ahzab. You have seen these verses of Surah At-Tahrim. And there are many other verses that have come regarding the wives. The Ahl al-Bayt are at the status of 'Lahmuhu lahmi wa damuhu dami' (Their flesh is my flesh, their blood is my blood). This excellence is neither attained by the Sahaba nor by the wives. No one has it. So the Verse of Purification was revealed only and only in honor of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), not for anyone else. 'Wa akhiru da'wana anil-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin wa sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibin at-tahirin al-ma'sumin al-mazlumin wa la'natullahi da'im 'ala a'da'ihim wa qatalatihim wa ghasibi huquqihim munkiri faza'ilihim wa manaqibihim'. If you do not know the answer to any question, you can watch the video again to find it. From among all those who provide correct answers, 14 lucky winners will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system, who will receive a gift of ₹1000 Indian Rupees. The winners will be announced in our next episode, Insha'Allah. Therefore, you are requested to watch these videos carefully, try to provide correct answers to the questions asked in the quiz, and also share these videos as much as possible. Participate in the quiz in large numbers and join us in helping to convey this message of Wilayat-e-Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to others, so that you too may be included among those who propagate Wilayat.

title: Fatima (s.a.) Naam Ki Tafseer | SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2022
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance and interpretation of the name 'Fatima' (s.a.). The speaker references traditions from the Imams to explain that she is divinely protected from all evil. It further emphasizes her unparalleled status in the universe, noting that no one, from the time of Adam (a.s.) until the Day of Judgment, is her equal.
content:
It does not happen in this entire universe, and then it is not that there was no time, until the Day of Judgment, there would be no equal (kuf) to the Princess. Imam (a.s.) asks, Imam asks, 'Do you know what is the destiny of the name Fatima? Do you know what is the meaning of Fatima?' I said, 'My master, my leader, you are the leader, my right, you tell me, please explain.' Then after that, Imam (a.s.) explained the destiny of the word Fatima, explained its meaning. He says that the interpretation of this is that the Princess (s.a.) has been kept away by Allah from every evil. Indeed, indeed, all those who were included in the evil, whose salam was not replied to, who were not allowed to participate in her funeral. Not allowed to participate in her funeral, that all are evil according to this Hadith. And finally, the salam in this Hadith, Hazrat Imam Ali (a.s.) stated, 'If Ali (a.s.) were not there,' meaning if he were not there, then the world whose marriage happened with the Princess, would not exist in this entire universe. And then it is not that at that time, until the Day of Judgment, no one would come who would be equal to the Princess. Whether it is Hazrat Adam (a.s.) or anyone else, no one can equal the Princess in this virtue.
The name Fatima signifies being kept away from all evil by Allah.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 8 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) & The Holy Quran - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound connection between the Holy Quran and Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), emphasizing the necessity of divine leadership for true spiritual guidance. It examines the inseparable relationship between the Ahlulbayt and the Quran, highlighting the Imam's role as the ultimate interpreter of divine truth. The session further discusses the significance of the Imam's occultation, the importance of recognizing his authority, and the necessity of patience and spiritual preparation for his eventual global manifestation.
content:
We are recording a video. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. [Greetings and opening prayers]. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. [Recitation of prayers and greetings]. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. First of all, we apologize for the technical problems in yesterday's session. However, praise be to Allah, the video of the entire session from yesterday has been uploaded to our YouTube channel, 'The Strong', without any interruptions. You can watch the video there and benefit from it. Under the topic of our Quranic discussions, today, praise be to Allah, is our eighth session. So, let us begin this session with the recitation of the Holy Quran. For this, I request the respected Maulana Asad Abbas Khan Sahab to come forward. Peace be upon you. Are you all well? We pray for his health. [Recitation of the Holy Quran - Surah Al-Ikhlas] [Recitation of the Holy Quran - Surah Al-Ikhlas continued] O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Indeed, Allah, the Great and Exalted, has spoken the truth. Regarding the 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim', today's Hadith is a unique one, which gives us an idea of Allah's mercy and forgiveness. In the book 'Tafsir al-Burhan', volume 2, page 266, this tradition is present: The sixth Imam, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), says that whenever any of our Shia does not begin his work with 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim', Allah puts him through a trial or difficulty that he dislikes, which causes him distress, so that through this trial, Allah may warn the servant and he may repent. Then, the servant thanks Allah and praises Him, and in exchange for this praise and gratitude, Allah removes the disgrace that the servant had to face due to neglecting the 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim'. The disgrace that the servant had to face due to neglecting it, Allah removes it. My master, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), has spoken the truth. And indeed, Allah is the Most Merciful. Now, let us move towards today's discussion, which is the second part of yesterday's topic. Yesterday, we talked about the 'Thaqalayn' (the two weighty things). Both the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the strong ropes of Allah. If you remember yesterday's discussion, it was mentioned that the Imam is the one who invites towards the Quran, and the Quran invites towards the Imam. If anyone wants the true knowledge of the Holy Quran, they must obtain it from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and the Quran will only be understood in the light of the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). I request the respected Maulana Syed Naseer Abbas Rizvi Sahab to shed more light on the topic of the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). But before Maulana begins his speech, there is an important matter to share with you. An important matter to share with you is that today's eighth session of this Quranic series is dedicated to the late Maulana Syed Ghulam Hasnain Rizvi Sahab. He played a huge role in guiding many young people and making them religious and pious. Today was his 24th death anniversary. We dedicate today's session to him. And viewers, you are requested to keep sending your questions related to the topic to the 'The Strong' group's WhatsApp number: [number removed]. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. [Recitation of Quranic verses and prayers]. This blessed verse is one whose interpretation, according to the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), is that when we look at the verses, the Lord of the Worlds says in this verse that we have made them leaders. The Lord of the Worlds has made the Imams leaders, guiding by our command. Guiding by our command. In the guidance of a human, the command of Allah matters—who to follow and who not to follow. The Lord of the Worlds says that this is our command: that we have revealed to them the performance of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of Zakat. And they were worshippers of Us. When the Lord of the Worlds mentions the performance of good deeds, what are the greatest good deeds? First, establishing prayer, and after that, the greatest good deed is giving Zakat. If a human wants to do good deeds, he should first give Zakat. Prayer is the manifestation of servitude. When these two things are in a human's personal life, he will become a servant of Allah, and in social life, he will do social work. Then, servitude will be achieved. Prayer is a matter, and along with it, Zakat is also a matter. Both matters are mentioned here. Islam and politics are not separate from each other. What is the concept of politics here? That their job is to state the issues. What is meant by politics? Politics is honesty, and honesty is politics. If we want this Islam, if we want honesty, then both things—from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—we can take servitude from there. If you look within the Imamate, the Lord of the Worlds has... So, the appointment of a leader is not something that you should decide based on your own whims or what you find appealing—like someone with a long beard or a handsome appearance. Leadership quality is not found in every human being. It is not about who you like, but rather, it is a matter that Allah (s.w.t.) has kept in His own hands. He chooses whom He wills. Not everyone possesses leadership qualities; rather, it is a divine selection. The true leader is not just someone powerful, but one whom Allah (s.w.t.) has chosen to guide, according to His wisdom. Even if someone seems good to us, they may lack the necessary qualities. This is a matter of divine appointment, and there is no room for human interference in this; guidance is given by Him alone. Guidance is not merely about power; it is about following the divine path. If a person wants to live their life correctly, they cannot do so without the guidance of Allah (s.w.t.). He is the one who defines what constitutes good deeds. If these divine instructions are included in a person's life, then their actions become righteous. The most important aspect of this, as I mentioned in my introduction, is that prayer (Salat) and charity (Zakat) hold a special status. If we want to live a righteous life, we must first establish prayer and pay Zakat. This is the essence of this verse. If we reflect upon this verse, Surah Al-Anbiya, verse 73, Allah (s.w.t.) points towards this. In this verse, Allah (s.w.t.) indicates that He made them Imams, guiding by His command, and He revealed to them the performance of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of Zakat. They were our devoted servants. If we reflect on this verse, although it seems general, these two verses specifically refer to the Imams. This is because the Imamate was established for them. Regarding this, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) said that the Imam who is from the progeny of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) is the one whom Allah (s.w.t.) guides through Ruh al-Amin (Gabriel), telling him what to do and what not to do, what to emphasize, and what not to emphasize. This is according to divine will, and such actions can never be wrong. This is for the Muslims to understand that the Prophets and the Imams (a.s.) do not make mistakes. They are the ones to be followed. No human can claim to open the path of guidance on their own. The Imams, peace be upon them, are the ones who guide. For instance, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, when he met Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.)... when Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) came out of a room, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari saw my master, Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), and stood up. When he reached him, he said, 'O young man, come forward.' When he reached him, he said, 'O young man, come forward.' When the Imam stepped forward, he said, 'Now step back.' The Imam stepped back. He then said, 'By the Lord of the Kaaba, your gait, your posture, everything is exactly like the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' Then he asked, 'O young man, what is your name?' He replied, 'My name is Muhammad.' He asked, 'Whose son are you?' He replied, 'I am the son of Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib.' The Imam then embraced him, kissed his forehead, and kissed his hands. Even though he was a small child, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who was a companion of the Prophet, kissed the hands of the Imam. He kissed the hands of the child and said, 'O Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has sent you his greetings.' The Imam replied, 'Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, and peace be upon you, O Jabir.' He then said, 'Peace be upon you too, for you have conveyed the greetings of my noble grandfather to me, so you are also worthy of peace.' After this, Jabir returned to his family and told his father, 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) told me one day, "O Jabir, you will live until you meet my grandson, Muhammad al-Baqir. Convey my greetings to him, for he is my namesake, and he will be the one who splits knowledge open."' He is the trustee of this Ummah, he is infallible, he is an Imam, and he is the seventh Imam of this Ummah. He will fill the world with justice just as it will be filled with oppression. I want to say that for this very day, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke of him. If you reflect on this, you will realize that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was pointing towards the diseases and evils present in society. How to remove the diseases and evils in society, and what we should do in our personal lives. Corruption in society is the greatest challenge that Imam al-Zaman (a.s.) will face. When society becomes pure, the path to righteousness will naturally open. If a swimming pool is contaminated, we don't just treat the people; we clean the pool itself. Similarly, we must remove the root cause of the disease. If we work according to the Imam's guidance, the society will flourish. If we act with determination, we can eradicate corruption. We should be grateful that we are not in a time where we might have been tested in ways that would have made us falter. We should be grateful that we are in a time where we can prepare ourselves. There is corruption in society. In the West, they talk about corruption, but they only catch the small thieves. The big corrupt figures often go unnoticed. We point fingers at others, but we ourselves commit small thefts—stealing water, cutting corners in bills. We call a person who steals a rupee a thief, but we don't look at those who are sitting in power, filling their bellies with haram wealth. The one who steals ten rupees is called a thief, but the one who steals the wealth of the people while in government is not called a thief? That is corruption. If we, as followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), do not distinguish between these, then what is the difference between us and others? We must reflect on this. After this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) recited the verse about the appointment of the Imams. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) established the Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and he made it clear who the Imams are. There are many who have denied the Prophet's people. Just as all the media and programs become useless if one denies the Wilayah of the Prophet and the Imam, similarly, after performing the pilgrimage to the Imam of the Time (a.s.), if one denies Imam Mahdi (a.s.), everything becomes void. Now, you know that regarding him, we should subscribe to things; we are all on WhatsApp and Facebook. In Mumbai, in Lucknow, news reaches everywhere, and we get on social media even for the smallest pieces of news. How many of us are there who have even once thought about the Imam of the Time (a.s.)? Has it ever crossed our minds to say, 'Let's see what the Imam of the Time (a.s.) is doing today'? Although, if you look at social media, it is not that people have become indifferent; rather, people have become inclined towards the Imam of the Time (a.s.). You see how many videos are appearing on YouTube that are describing the conditions of the reappearance. Even the Ahl-e-Sunnat wal-Jamaat are presenting their analysis according to their traditions. Anyway, today there is a need for those who have no news of their Imam, who are asking if the Imam Mahdi has been born or not, to stop talking about the signs of Mahdi. And those who are 1000 percent certain about the Imam of the Time (a.s.), they should start focusing on their own character and their own deeds. I do not understand why we do not fulfill our responsibility. We should see what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said. When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was asked, 'Who is Mahdi?', he said, 'He is from my progeny, from the progeny of Fatimah.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'He will appear among you, and his name will be the same as yours.' His name will be the same as yours, and he will be known by your name. This is a clear statement. If we look at this Hadith, there is a question: the Imam of the Time (a.s.) who is not in front of our eyes, is his occultation (Ghaybah) a physical occultation or a spiritual one? These are two different things. What is physical occultation? What is spiritual occultation? Physical occultation means that the Imam of the Time (a.s.) is living among people, but people do not recognize him. A neighbor knows his neighbor, knows what position he holds, what work he does, and in which department he works. But here, people do not recognize him. But the question is, is his occultation spiritual, or is his occultation physical, like Janab-e-Khizr (a.s.) who appears before whomever he wishes? Or is his presence included within his occultation? Both sides have arguments. Some people say that the one who is not in front of our eyes is in a state of occultation. I have presented one thing before you: regarding the occultation of the Imam of the Time (a.s.), scholars have different views. Some people say his occultation is physical, and some people say his occultation is spiritual. It depends on the level of understanding a person reaches. But the purpose of telling you this is that even among the scholars, there is a difference of opinion, and this difference does not mean fighting or quarreling; it just means different perspectives. It does not mean fighting or quarreling; it just means different perspectives. They present their arguments. There is no room for conflict here. I will move forward with all these arguments and move towards what the Imam of the Time (a.s.) is doing, for whom the Lord of the Worlds has made such preparations. It is narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that he said, 'You are drowned in the ocean of the Imam's concern.' He is looking towards the earth and observing. He is in deep thought. I am looking at you, what are you thinking? You are drowned in deep thought, and I am thinking about my Imam, observing him. He is looking and... He is looking and observing. Are you thinking about your government, your relatives, and worldly affairs? The Imam is not like that. He is thinking about the world, that a day will come when the world and worldly people will incline towards him. He is thinking about that child who is coming, the eleventh Imam from my progeny, who will fill the earth with justice as it has been filled with oppression. He is the one for whom the people will be bewildered and wandering. They will be looking for their Imam. They will say, 'Where is he?' If people are bewildered, then the Imam of the Time (a.s.) has begun his occultation. Some will try, and the world will reach this conclusion. The world reached the conclusion that a great organization should be created so that the world could function under one system. But that organization is being misused. It is being used against the weak and the oppressed. Therefore, half the world is feeling the need for a government—what kind of government? A government of justice, where everyone is equal. No one should have veto power. If there is any veto power, it should only be in the hands of the infallible Imam (a.s.) whom the Lord of the Worlds has appointed. When he appears, some people will be guided, and some will go astray. Some will be happy, and some will be sad. The Imam will come and establish justice. He will remove the oppression of the oppressors. And people will be with those who have accepted the Wilayah of Hazrat Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Because you have accepted it, what will happen after that? He said, 'Allah will do what He wills.' What do you have to do with it? He is the One who does what He wills. He has His own limits and His own ends. He does what He wants. And why does our society bring this up? The meaning is that this statement is not for some people; it is not our concern. What is the matter? We will let the fruit ripen. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked a shepherd, 'Why are you doing this?' And he did not understand anything. The perfection of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) is that the Imam of the Time (a.s.)... He starts with people, he takes them as his students. [Music] He tests his students. Just like the Prophet Musa (a.s.) went to learn from a servant of Allah. This is a story from the Quran. Who is Musa (a.s.)? A great Prophet, a Prophet who spoke to Allah (Kalimullah). Whenever there was a problem, he would go to him. He went to learn from Khizr (a.s.). Musa (a.s.) is a Prophet, and he is going to become a student of Khizr (a.s.). Musa (a.s.) went to him and joined his hands, saying, 'Please accept me as your student. Keep me with you for a few days.' Khizr (a.s.) looked at him from head to toe. 'You are fine in your house, you are a Prophet among the Children of Israel, you are fine in your house, but you have come here as a student.' Here you have come as a student to us, to learn. Have you been sent by Allah, or have you come on your own? If you have come on your own, then we have some conditions. He looked at him from head to toe. A teacher is one who can sense the potential in a single glance. After looking at Musa (a.s.) from head to toe, Janab-e-Khizr (a.s.) said, 'The first condition for learning is patience. You have no patience at all. You will not be able to stay with me.' Now, the point is that the speaker wants to say that if we want to be successful in life, the first thing we need is to discipline our souls. Janab-e-Musa (a.s.), a great Prophet, was turned away from being a student of Janab-e-Khizr (a.s.). This was a lesson. This picture that was given, it could have been taken, but why the whole path above? Therefore, this means the path of success in a human's life, and the final path. If a human cannot do this in life, then the human cannot be [successful]. During the period of waiting for the Imam (a.s.), during the period of bail in the court, do it today. We are getting the blessings without those players twice. If you have started, you will get the notification of the comment, and after that, all these effects will have an impact on you. Whether the taste comes, the change, the killing, thousands of state assemblies will get it. So, on these signals, and the state of the world is that A.R. Rahman is included. The second thing is that Salam has been given, that is, friends, if we have to go to their wedding, then at least don't give anything, but take a heart big enough that for the sake of the rice, we are in the presence of the Lord of the Worlds. The Lord of the Worlds has bones, we have reports, it is said that the report is normal, China, Param, our Maduban. It is said that the report is normal, China, Param, our Maduban's forehead, may this blessed Ramadan be accepted for us, all the books and incidents. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. This structure is Rahim and Kohli, this is the office, surely this sound, I will give advice, this is the part of history, Haldi, exactly like the behavior, both of them, that avatar happened, that hungry... that Jim, the friends of Allah, Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, Rizwan Jal Bharat Mission. We are very grateful, and we are happy that when the questions of the believer come to us, if you allow, then it means that I can present that. I am present. title: EP09 | Imam Ali (a.s.) Ka Hamlaawaron Ko Jawaab | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture addresses historical misconceptions regarding the reaction of Imam Ali (a.s.) to the attack on the house of Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.). The speaker refutes the claim that Imam Ali (a.s.) remained silent or passive, explaining that his restraint was a deliberate act of patience based on a divine covenant with the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The talk emphasizes that Imam Ali (a.s.) physically confronted the attackers, proving his courage and authority while upholding his commitment to the Prophet's instructions.
content:
Move forward and caught that tyrant by his collar and threw him down, then his nose and his neck were injured. Well, he had to do it, does it suit a brave and courageous person like the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that someone attacks his house and he remains silent? Perhaps you have heard these sentences before; such things are only said by those people or those whose purpose is only and... Or those whose purpose is only and only to cover up the wrongdoings of their elders. By making such objections, they are making a failed attempt to erase some dark realities of Islamic history, in which, after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the right of Caliphate was snatched from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and an attack was made by setting fire to the house of Princess Fatima Zahra (s.a.). To refute these events, these objections are often raised: if these things are true, then why did Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) sit silently in the house? Why didn't he do anything? The first answer to this is that the misunderstanding of taking the patience of the Mawla as the silence of the Mawla, first of all, these people should remove this veil of negligence. The second thing is, when the house of the Mawla was attacked, he got up from his place, moved forward, and caught that tyrant by his collar and threw him down, then his... Caught that tyrant by his collar and threw him down, then his nose and his neck were injured. Well, he had to do it, the promise he made to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he caught that person and said, 'By the oath of the One who honored Muhammad with Prophethood, if the decision had not been made from Allah's side beforehand, if the Book had not been there, and if there had not been the promise that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had given me, then you would have known that you could never enter my house.' By calling the patience of the Mawla the silence of the Mawla, even today, injustice is being done to the Mawla. But by answering those who attacked his house, the Mawla proved that he was not helpless. For 14 centuries, the true lovers of the Mawla have been describing the oppression of the Mawla, and we will continue to mention this until the peace of the Sharia is achieved. From the Lord of the Worlds... May there be peace in the world. We pray to Allah (S.W.T.) that He grants peace to Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) and grants us the ability to distinguish between truth and falsehood. Ameen.

And from here begins the sequence of how the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat) introduced his 'Marifat-e-Nuraniya' (knowledge of his light). The answer is: why did you not recognize Him? We did not know the Messenger. Why did you not know? Yes, if the message did not reach someone, if the matter did not reach them at all, it did not reach them at all, then that is a different matter. You know that there will be different stages on the Day of Judgment. Meaning, when people are resurrected, when the Barzakh ends, when the world ends, people will be raised from their graves again. So, this being raised from the graves is called 'Ba'th', meaning to raise from the grave. This is the first position, the first stage of Qiyamah. And this stage, the first stage, is one of 50 such stages. Each stage lasts for a thousand years. One thousand years. So, this 'Ba'th'—meaning when one is raised from the grave—people will be so troubled and terrified upon seeing this Qiyamah that they will start running here and there. They will start running here and there. This is called 'Nashr'. This 'Nashr', this running here and there, will also last for a thousand years. A thousand years. Meaning, it is not a matter of a thousand days. It is not a matter of a thousand hours. It is a matter of a thousand years, and it is not even known if these are years of this world or years of the Hereafter. That is also unknown. It is just that it is a thousand years. For a thousand years, this 'Nashr' will continue in the same way, and in any case, the summary is that the angels will gather those people and bring them to one place, and then the accounting will take place. In this way, one stage after another will come, in which they will be questioned. One of these stages is 'A'raf'. A'raf—meaning this will be the place where the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be. A'raf means height. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be at a height, on an elevation, A'raf. 'Wa ya'rifuna kullan bisimahum' (And they will recognize everyone by their marks). The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will recognize everyone on the Day of Judgment by looking at their foreheads, to see who is a Momin and who is not. Everyone. So, those in A'raf who, for instance, truly did not know anything—the poor, innocent ones—it is said that the message did not reach them. For example, they were in some jungle, and no Prophet came, no Messenger came, no preacher came, no scholar came; no one went there because there was no one there. Alone in the jungle, just a few people, individuals living alone, knowing nothing.
