Sustenance is in the hands of Allah. Not in anyone else's hands. Sometimes we say, 'Actually, there was a problem, this problem happened.' Brother, there was no problem bigger than Karbala, right? There cannot be any problem bigger than Karbala, right? If in your view there can be, then tell me. There cannot be any problem bigger than Karbala. But in such circumstances, Abu Thumama al-Sa'idi comes forward and says, 'Ya Ibn Rasool Allah, hanna waqtu-s-salah' (O son of the Messenger of Allah, the time for prayer has arrived). Farfa'a al-Hussain... Hussain raised his head towards the sky to see that the time for prayer had arrived. So he addresses Abu Thumama and says, 'Dhakarta-s-salah, ja'alakallahu min al-musalleen' (You have remembered the prayer, may Allah count you among the worshippers). And what a prayer he prayed! That prayer which Hussain prayed, neither was such a prayer prayed before it in the world, nor after it, nor will it be prayed. That prayer which Hussain prayed. With what kind of companions! That ahead of Hussain were Sa'id and Zuhair. Zuhair ibn Qayn. InshaAllah, if Allah grants the opportunity, I will tell you about them. Who is Zuhair ibn Qayn? What were they, and then what did they become? Allah, whomsoever He grants the opportunity. Both of these are sentences from the Maqtal. That from head to toe—this is a sentence from the Maqtal. I am not doing any oratory, I am not saying anything like that. There is no exaggeration. It is written in the Maqtal. That there was no part of the body that did not have an arrow in it. But both were standing just like that. It was the Prophet's glad tiding. That 'O Hussain, your companions will be such that iron will not affect them.' The effect of Hadid (iron) will not be there. Meaning, the harm that will be, Hadid, iron, will not cause them harm. Meaning, they will be so drowned in your love, so immersed! They will be immersed in your love. They will not care about anything else in the world. Real life is this life. Real life is the life that is spent in the defense of the Ahlulbayt. Otherwise, animals also eat and drink. But real life is this. Zuhair ibn Qayn was an Uthmani. He was an Uthmani. But Allah granted him such an opportunity. Now, as soon as Hussain said, 'Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullah,' then the sentence of the Maqtal is that on one side Sa'id fell, on the other side Zuhair fell. Hussain went forward and placed Sa'id's head on his lap. So Sa'id's first sentence was, 'Hal wafaytu ya Ibn Rasool Allah?' (Have I fulfilled my promise, O son of the Messenger of Allah, or not?). You see, meaning, what was this status? Look at their level. How immersed they were. Similarly, another companion. Wahab al-Kalbi. He is a Christian. He is a Christian. But he meets the Imam during the journey. The attention of the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda) is upon him. As soon as the attention of the Proof of God is upon Wahab al-Kalbi, he immediately accepts faith. And what kind of faith! He has just been married. He just got married. And there is no one with him. One wife and one mother, that's it, and no one else in the world. Apart from these two, there is no one in the world. But he is ready to be sacrificed for Hussain. Look at the spirit, what it is. Look at the mother's spirit. The night of Ashura. Wahab al-Kalbi's mother. All night she tells Wahab al-Kalbi, 'If you are not martyred for the son of Fatima tomorrow, I will not forgive you.' All night she is instructing him. 'If for the son of Fatima...' Just in the morning, when the sequence of martyrdom begins... Then Wahab al-Kalbi comes and stands before the Imam, saying, 'Maula, grant me permission. Maula, grant me permission.' How could Hussain (a.s.) say 'go,' when he has just been married, he is a youth, and his wife will soon become a widow? How could Hussain (a.s.) grant permission? Hussain (a.s.) is silent. He is saying nothing. Suddenly, a voice comes from behind the curtain, 'Master, grant him permission. Master, I have nothing else besides this child. Master, accept this sacrifice.' Hussain (a.s.) granted permission. It is written in the Maqtal that Wahab went. He was brave, he was valiant. He went and fought a tremendous battle. He sent many wretched enemies to Hell. In this process, he himself became covered in wounds and was bathed in blood. After fighting, he returned and said to his mother, 'Ya Umma, hal radita anni?' (Mother, are you pleased with me or not?). The mother said, 'I did not send you to return alive. Go, go and fight again; you are not to come back alive.' Now, as Wahab was about to leave, his wife was standing at the tent. What does his wife want to say? From behind, the mother's voice came, 'Son, this is the time for martyrdom, not the time to converse with your wife.' Wahab asked, 'Wife, what do you want to say?' She began to say, 'You are leaving now. You will go, and now I have no one left in the world. I have left my father's house. Take me to the Maula once. Request the Maula that when I am left all alone and have no one, at least let me come into the tents with the noble ladies so that I may remain safe.' Wahab al-Kalbi takes his wife to Hussain (a.s.) and presents the request. As soon as Hussain (a.s.) heard this, he bowed his head. What could he say to her—that the noble ladies would not be safe on the evening of Ashura? Wahab left. As he got up and started walking again, he hadn't gone far when he felt a rustle. Just listen to the final sentences, offer condolences to Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). Just a rustle was felt, and when he turned back, his wife was coming. He said, 'Why are you coming to the battlefield? Don't you know that Jihad is not obligatory for women?' She said, 'Wahab, I just wanted to tell you that when you started to leave, I saw a scene that I could not bear.' He asked, 'What did you see?' She said, 'When you started to leave, Hussain (a.s.) sat down on the ground, the Maula sat on the ground and began to pick up dust and put it on his head, saying, "Wa Ghurbata, Wa Ghurbata."' I would say, O wife of Wahab, you saw that much and could not bear it. Ask Zainab's (s.a.) heart, on the night of the 10th, 'Jalasa ala sadri' (He sat on my chest). He is cutting the jugular vein, and Zainab (s.a.) could not understand anything. O Ibn-e-Sa'ad, you are watching, my master is being slaughtered. Wa Hussainah, Wa Mazlumah. 'Sayalamul-ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun.' 'Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz-zalimin.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain (a.s.). O Lord, count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the troubles of those who are distressed. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant children to those who are childless. Grant complete and swift recovery to those who are ill. Return those who are far from their homeland safely. Grant freedom to those who are in prisons this very night. O Lord, protect the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and Aale-Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and Aale-Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 1 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture provides a foundational overview of the laws and spiritual etiquette of fasting during the month of Ramadan. Maulana Noor Prakash Mehdi explains the requirements for Niyyah (intention) and Imsak (abstinence), emphasizing that fasting extends beyond physical hunger to include the purification of one's limbs and heart. The session concludes with practical advice for youth on maintaining spiritual growth through consistent prayer, supplication, and engagement with the Quran.
content:
Before beginning any speech, we present our praise to the Almighty, who has given us the opportunity to be present here this year as well. We have been given the opportunity to perform acts of worship in this month of Ramadan and to seek forgiveness for our sins. We congratulate all the believers on the arrival of this month. We are here with a program of questions and answers regarding the rulings of fasting in Ramadan. Although our scholars answer these questions in mosques and Imambargahs, due to the current situation, we have decided to bring this program to you so that you can present your questions to the scholars. Viewers are requested to send their questions to this WhatsApp number [number removed], and we will try our best to get the answers from the scholars. Today, we have a scholar with us who needs no introduction, Maulana Noor Prakash Mehdi Sahab. We welcome him to this program. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. (Maulana: Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh). I hope you and your family are safe during this pandemic. May Allah keep you safe. Maulana, the first question that often arises among the youth is regarding the 'niyyah' (intention) of fasting. Is it possible to make a single intention for the entire month of Ramadan? Secondly, if one has to make an intention every day and forgets to do so, what is the ruling in Sharia? And there are many among us who say that this blessed month of Ramadan consists of thirty fasts. Therefore, if it is an act of worship, can one intention suffice for the whole month? But I want to clarify one thing for you: you do not need to say it out loud. The intention is simply the resolve in your heart. You do not need to say it out loud; having the intention is enough. If a person resolves that 'I will fast today,' and two things are present—sincerity and the intention that this fast is solely for Allah—that is sufficient. The intention must be pure; there should be no show or hypocrisy. If you fast just to show others, your fast will not be valid. It is not for others, but for the sake of Allah. I want to add that if a person intends to fast, that is enough. Thank you, Maulana. Viewers, you have seen that there is no need to repeat the intention or say it out loud; just the resolve is enough. Maulana, the second question is about 'Imsak' (abstinence). What is it? Regarding 'Imsak', it means to restrain oneself. Some people think it is just about not eating or drinking, but it is about refraining from all things that break the fast. If you do not make the intention, your fast is not valid, but you must still refrain from things that break the fast. For example, if a person forgets to make the intention in Ramadan, they cannot fast, but they must still refrain from breaking the fast until sunset. They should not eat or drink anything until sunset. Similarly, if someone is traveling and reaches their destination, or if someone is sick, our scholars say that you should not openly eat or drink in front of others, even if you are not fasting, out of respect for the month. The final question, Maulana, is about which acts and prayers are recommended during this blessed month of Ramadan. Could you please shed some light on this for our viewers? There are many daily prayers for this month, both short and long. After breaking the fast, there are specific supplications and recitations. It is narrated from Imam Ali (a.s.) that one should be diligent in performing these recommended acts. After Maghrib, there is a specific prayer known as 'Dua-e-Iftitah'. It is said that everything is present in it [the month of Ramadan]. After Iftar, you can read whatever you want; there are supplications (duas) available, there are tasbihs available, and there are dhikr available. You are free to do as much as you wish. Another thing is, when you come to the time of Suhoor, our scholars have said that the sign of a Momin is that they perform acts of worship during the time of Suhoor. If a person wakes up at the time of Suhoor, even if it is difficult to eat, and I have said that even if you have two hours, how do you spend them? If your heart is inclined, then to fulfill that, you should subscribe to our channel... ...you should subscribe to our channel, and we have the Duas for every hour, the Duas for every day. Every day, a person is busy, but in our books, there are so many things. My dear brother, these books are in our homes. This book has been published; it is the daily routine for every man and woman. Every day, there is a supplication after the prayer. And this is not just a burden, my brother, take it easy. It is good, so you should read it if your heart desires. So, Dua and prayer in this blessed month are for every Momin... ...in this blessed month, for every Momin, so that there is no deficiency in their deeds. Now, regarding the youth: look, youth is a blessing. We have a very beautiful Hadith. It says that the youth is like a clean slate. When this youth comes into the presence of Allah, Allah loves them and likes them. Our scholars have determined three things: one is fasting, which has an effect on the soul. You think about it; the Imam says that fasting increases the piety (taqwa) of a person. This fast was created and ordained so that a person's piety could be tested. So, fasting is necessary. The youth should fast, and the rewards of this fast... ...and I do not want to go into the rewards of this fast, as there are many spiritual benefits. But keep the fast, and do not let it be just about hunger and thirst. You are hungry and thirsty, and Masha'Allah, you are busy with mobile phones, looking at things, or your hands are easily reaching out to criticize someone. A person should not be like a cat. If a cat is just looking for an opportunity, and as soon as it gets one, it pounces—that is not how a Momin should be. Even great Momins, when they get an opportunity, all their 'Momin-ness' is left behind. That is not the kind of fast it should be. That is why the categories of fasting mentioned are very important. Fasting is not just about being hungry and thirsty; when you are hungry and thirsty, your limbs... ...when you are hungry and thirsty, your limbs should also be fasting. The third category is even higher: when you are fasting, besides thinking about the greatness of God and the blessings of God, you should not think of anything else. You should be like this: if you are sitting with someone who is smoking, and you are not smoking, you are sitting with someone who is gambling, and you are leaving that gambling. Today, everyone says that the gambling you are sitting near is no less harmful than the one who is smoking; their lungs will be just as black as the one who is smoking. Similarly, if you think of anything other than God, your fast will be incomplete, even if you are not punished. But regardless, it is gone. That is why fasting is a shield; if you have protected yourself, it will purify your heart, and if your heart is purified, then you will be ready for Allah's... ...if your heart is purified, then you will be ready for Allah's reward. You must be ready for Allah's mercy. So, one thing is to keep this in mind. And the second thing is Dua. A person's value lies in their Dua. You can say that your share is in the Dua; speak up. Doing Dua is very good; the more one does Dua, the more success is destined in their life. The third thing is the Quran. If someone wants to be successful, there is no other way except to go to Allah. One thing is that we have to read the Quran. This is the way of humanity; Allah is giving a chance to the human to talk to Him through Dua and the Quran. The third thing I want to say is that the Quran is such a book; our scholars used to say that if you want to talk to Allah, read the book... ...if you want to talk to Allah, read the book, and if you want Allah to talk to you, then read the Quran. It was necessary for Allah to say this, meaning you have to take it inside you. It is not about hanging it around your neck, my brother; that is a burden. Rather, it is about taking it into the depths of your being. When you read the Quran, Allah is speaking to you. Take it into your being, just like when love enters the heart, your heart becomes illuminated. You will be close to Him in every way. So, in the same way, if we read the Quran, we will stay connected to Him. Imam Ali (a.s.) says that the Quran is a hidden treasure. If you read it, you will find it. As a person reads the Quran, it starts descending into the heart, and you will become better. Allah will open a path for you. That is why these three things are for every youth... ...that is why these three things are very important for every youth: constant Dua, fasting, and the Quran. I pray that Allah keeps me and you attached to these things. And in this blessed month, may we be among those who rise from His table. Thank you, Maulana Sahib, for adding so much to our knowledge. Viewers, you saw how the Maulana gave us advice regarding the month of Ramadan, about the Duas of Suhoor, and what we should do during the time of Suhoor. Then, regarding the youth, you mentioned many things about protecting oneself. This should be done continuously. You should do it as much as possible. This is from your side to us, and regarding your questions, we should recite the Quran more and more in this blessed month. We should keep reciting the Quran. We are very grateful to the Maulana for his presence and for increasing our knowledge. Maulana Sahib, we will be back with your answers, Insha'Allah. Those who have sent questions, we have understood them, and we request you to keep sending your questions to this WhatsApp number [number removed]. We keep appearing before you with this program of questions and answers regarding the deeds of Ramadan. Until then, Allah Hafiz.

title: Ep#18: Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.) Par Imam Ali (a.s.) Ka Marsiya
excerpt: This lecture reflects on the profound grief of Imam Ali (a.s.) following the burial of his wife, Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.). He addresses the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.w.) at his grave, expressing his immense sorrow and the weight of the tragedy that befell the Prophet's daughter. The discourse highlights the Imam's patience and his commitment to the divine decree despite the oppression faced by the Ahlulbayt.
content:
After burying Bibi Zahra (s.a.), Mawla (a.s.) said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, from me and from your daughter who is now coming to you and will soon meet you. My patience has diminished over the martyrdom of your beloved daughter, and my strength is failing me. The only consolation is that I have endured the shock of your separation. I laid you in the grave, and your soul departed in my arms. Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. Today, the trust has been taken back, and what was entrusted to me has been lifted. My grief will now remain forever, and my nights will be spent awake until Allah chooses for me the same home where you reside. Soon, your daughter will tell you how your Ummah united to oppress her. Ask her and inquire about her condition. All this happened when not much time had passed since your era, and your mention is still fresh. My peace be upon you both, the peace of one who is bidding farewell, who is neither tired nor weary. If I leave from here, it is not out of exhaustion, and if I stay here, it is not out of doubt regarding the promise Allah has made to those who are patient.'

title: Majlis 10 | Masaaib: Shahaadat-e-Imam Husain (a.s.) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2024
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi provides a poignant account of the final moments of Imam Hussain (a.s.) at the Battle of Karbala. It details the cruelty faced by the Imam, his final farewells to his family, and the immense suffering endured by the Ahlulbayt in the aftermath. The session emphasizes the spiritual significance of the sacrifice and the enduring legacy of the tragedy through mourning and remembrance.
content:
Hey nada, hey nada... Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aale Muhammad. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' When I mounted his chest, he began to move his lips. Your Maula, in his thirst, began to pray for me. Shabbir, it felt as if I had placed my ear to his lips and heard; he was remembering Ghazi. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' What a state of loneliness it was for the son of Zahra (s.a.); Sakina (s.a.) was watching this scene in my hands. I held the beard of the King, I kept making him cry, and I laughed. The bodies nearby also began to writhe when I slapped Hussain (a.s.). Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' I don't know what was in his eyes, Mir, no one would meet his gaze. I too could not look into his eyes, so I turned his face away. This was the reason why I slaughtered your Maula from the back of the neck. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' That river which flows there, your Maula fell from there near Ghazi. Umar Sa'ad told me, 'Kill him in the low ground.' I, Mukhtar, dragged him by his hair to the slaughterhouse. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' Yes, that moment was strange, Mukhtar, there was speed in my hands, the sword was becoming blunt, my dagger... I even struck him like that. His throat would not be cut by me; his mother had placed her hand there. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' There is a mound in Karbala where his sister was crying, standing there, begging everyone, saying, 'Do not run the knife.' She saw her brother's throat being cut from 70 steps away. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' She saw... When Zainab (s.a.) arrived, Shabbir, crying, said to me, 'Shimr, let her go to the tent, hide your dagger from her. Shimr, you tyrant, remove it from your chest, I swear to you by Muhammad.' Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' Mir Sajjad, hearing all his atrocities, the courtiers began to wail. Shimr the accursed said, 'O Mukhtar, shall I show you something...' If you grant permission, the dagger that was on the Garib-e-Zahra (s.a.) himself, he showed that dagger to everyone. Shimr used to say, 'Do not listen, Mukhtar, to how I killed Hussain.' And Hamd, Salam, and Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-e-Aale-Muhammad. Listen to the loneliness of Garib-e-Zahra (s.a.), O mourners. When my Maula was left alone in the Maqtal, the army of Sham surrounded him from all sides. Every one of them was thirsty for blood on the banks of the Euphrates. The lamp of Imamate had to be extinguished, and Shabbir had to be thrown from the saddle onto the ground. Hearing this, when someone struck this blow, someone drove the blade of a spear into his side. Someone came in front and swung a sword. It was difficult for Garib-e-Zahra (s.a.) to steady himself on the saddle. Ali (a.s.) and Zahra (s.a.) were made to cry on the battlefield. Alas, Hussain (a.s.) did not fall, he was made to fall. When the arrow struck, the King (Imam Hussain a.s.) remembered Asghar. When the mace struck his head, he called out to Ghazi (Abbas a.s.). When the spear struck, he cried out in agony for Akbar. When the slap struck, he called out, 'Ya Zahra!' He remembered Ali (a.s.) as the blow fell upon his head. He remembered Hasan (a.s.) as blood flowed from his mouth. The Imam fell from his saddle onto the ground face-first. The arrows that were in his chest came out from his back. The tips of all the spears emerged from his sides. How could the King find peace for even a moment now? The feet of the son of Ali slipped from the stirrups. All the ribs of the Prophet's grandson were broken. The narrator has recorded this scene of pain: at the moment the dagger was about to move upon Hussain. Hussain's daughter was standing in front of her aunt. At that moment, the oppressed Imam cried out to Shimr, 'My Sakina, my Sakina, do not let her die, O tyrant! Have mercy, leave my children alone, O tyrant!' It was read in the desert, it was read in the desert that the son of Batool (Fatima s.a.) was alone. Did anyone ask Shimr if Hussain was still alive? Approaching him, Shimr laughed and called out, 'Look, the second Zahra (Zainab s.a.) has arrived at the battlefield.' Hearing this, the grief-stricken King sat up. At the mention of his sister, Shabbir (Hussain a.s.) sat up. Saying this, he advanced with a dagger in his hand. On one side, a corpse began to writhe by the river, and on the other, the daughter of Batool emerged from the tents. Shimr committed a strange act of insolence. The tyrant showed not even a shred of decency. The tyrant kicked the Holy Quran. The oppressor was committing atrocities in a strange way; sometimes his hand was in Hussain's hair... Sometimes he grabbed the blessed beard, sometimes he laughed. Shimr removed the hair with the dagger at once. Hussain said, 'Look, O Ali Akbar, the accursed one has placed his knee upon our chest.' When the blow fell, the angels turned their faces away. What of angels? Even the prophets turned their faces away. When the prophets turned away, the messengers turned their faces away. When the messengers moved, the saints turned their faces away. Hasan and Ali said, 'Now only God knows, Hussain knows, the throat knows, and Fatima knows.' What more can be described beyond this? When the blow fell, not a single drop of blood came out. The accursed one, in rage, began to call out, 'Hussain, tell me quickly, what kind of miracle is this?' The oppressed Imam said, 'You do not know a mother's love. Zahra has placed her throat against my throat.' Hussain said, 'Mother, take your throat away, you are wounded, this cannot be.' When the accursed one's dagger moved upon the King's throat, the voice came, 'Subhana Rabbi al-A'la.' The blood of the head flowed into the lap of the Sayyid; the head of Hussain was severed in the lap of Fatima. Sakina would say, 'I saw the murder of my father.' She would say, 'I saw the funeral of my brother Ali Akbar.' Trapped in prison and enduring slaps, what did she not see at the age of four? Sakina would say this. When the travelers of Karbala passed from the battlefield, see how they descended thirsty at the riverbank. Zainab cried out, 'All my kin have died without me. Where should I search? Where have my loved ones gone?' The home built over years turned into a wasteland. The preparations for Zainab's imprisonment were made. The accursed ones entered the noble court. Shimr the accursed was in the middle, surrounded by spear-bearers. They kept stabbing the backs of the women with spears. They were looting the belongings and goods. Alas, they committed a new act of heartlessness. They left the daughters of the Prophet unveiled. It was the time of Asr when the Imam was beheaded. The enemies looted the family of the Prophet until evening. As evening fell, they set fire to the tents. That fire, that smoke, and the thirsty daughters of the Prophet. The breath of the small children was stifled in their chests. A river of tears flowed from their thirsty eyes. Sakina would scream, 'Call my uncle! Call my uncle to my wounds! Tell them the house is on fire, come and extinguish it. For God's sake, bring a water skin. Extinguish this fire, do not give me water, O wind, for the sake of the sacrifice.' The cradle is burning, the cradle of my little brother is burning. He is falling in the battlefield. He is falling in the battlefield, save Hussain. O Fatima, hide Hussain in your veil. O Fatima, hide Hussain in your veil. The oppressed one is helpless with spears in his sides; your broken ribs do not even let you rise. Take the name of Ali and lift Hussain up. O Fatima, hide Hussain in your veil. The desires that remained between the walls and the doors, the lullabies that were kept in the heart for Mohsin, sing those lullabies today and put Hussain to sleep. O Fatima, hide Hussain in your veil. Like the desires of the King's oppressed daughter, taking him in your lap like the third of Shaban, if possible, put Hussain to sleep for a while. O Fatima, hide Hussain in your veil. Haider (Ali a.s.) is writhing, the Prophet is restless. How are you hearing these cries again and again? There is an uproar on the earth, bring Hussain down. O Fatima, hide Hussain in your veil. The intentions of the Yazidi soldiers are not good. The feet of the King are slipping from the stirrups. Ghazi is not here; you yourself save Hussain. O Fatimah, hide Husain in your cloak. Zainab calls out, 'O restless mother, let the daughters of Haider bind his wounds together; call Husain into the tent for once.' O Fatimah, hide Husain in your cloak. Now, upon the hearts of the prostrating ones... Speak at the grave of Asghar, O mother, 'Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. Why have you made your bed here? Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar.' Alas, what kind of sleep is this? Rise, I am a sacrifice for you; your mother is weeping for you, your mother is weeping for you. How can this mother console her heart? Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. Weeping, little Sakina used to say, 'Brother, do not drink water alone, brother, do not drink water alone. We are also very thirsty, brother; come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar.' Where should this helpless one go with an uncovered head? From where should this mother bring water? From where should this mother bring water? The oppressors have blocked the riverbank; come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. What kind of sleep has come to you, my dear? Why do you not ask for water? Why do you not ask for water? Have you drunk the water of Kauthar yourself? Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. Speak at the grave of Asghar, O mother, 'Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar.' The earth has swallowed your face; it has taken you, my delicate one, from me; it has taken you, my delicate one, from me. Do not think that your mother will weep; come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. Ask for water from your uncle. Everyone is suffering from thirst in the tents, everyone is suffering from thirst in the tents. You too, after giving water to everyone, come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. Speak at the grave of Asghar, O mother, 'Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar.' O you who sleep in my lap, to whom have I entrusted you? To whom have I entrusted you? Where should this mother search for you? Where should this mother search for you? Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar. Speak at the grave of Asghar, O mother, 'Come home, for evening is falling, O Asghar.' The garment that mother gave, bring that, O Zainab. The garment that mother gave, bring that, O Zainab. With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. Today in the battlefield, only your words will remain. Soon I will have a meeting with mother. Soon I will have a meeting with mother. If there is any message, then tell me, O Zainab. With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. Your hands will be bound with ropes, sister. I keep thinking about my corpse. I keep thinking about my corpse. Tell me, how will you remove the arrows, O Zainab? Tell me, how will you remove the arrows, O Zainab? With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. You will recognize my corpse, sister. Tear the collar of my shirt, sister. Tear the collar of my shirt, sister. Make it such that no one loots it, O Zainab. With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. Have Sakina take off her jewelry in front of you. In a little while, the house of the oppressed will be looted. In a little while, the house of the oppressed will be looted. Hide this trust in some corner, O Zainab. With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. If Abbas were here, I would not have asked you to leave the tent. If Abbas were here, I would not have caused you pain. If Abbas were here, I would not have caused you pain. Become like Abbas and help me mount my horse, O Zainab. With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. Take care of this trust of the prison, O lady. Take her in your lap, let the oppressed one depart, O lady. Take her in your lap, let the oppressed one depart, O lady. My hem, my hem, release it from my daughter, O Zainab. My hem, release it from my daughter, O Zainab. With your own hands, put my shroud on me, O Zainab. Ever since Akbar left, the sight of my eyes has also gone. Bring and give me some keepsake of Ali Asghar. Bring and give me some keepsake of Ali Asghar. Oh, Bashir's kurta, place it against my eyes, Zainab. With your own hands, dress me in my shroud, Zainab. Shabbir left his home as if it were a funeral procession. Everyone was weeping, Takallum, standing on the banks of the tents. Everyone was weeping, Takallum. Standing at the door of the tent, when the King (Imam Hussain) said, when the King said, 'Give me permission to die, Zainab,' when the King said, 'Give me permission to die, Zainab, dress me in my shroud with your own hands, Zainab.' Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad-e-Aal-e-Muhammad. Curse be upon the oppressors, countless, total curse, countless, curse upon Hurmala, countless. Inna Lillahi wa Inna Ilayhi Raji'un. The afternoon of Ashura was no less than a doomsday. Hussain is standing all alone, calling out, 'Ya Abtal-as-Safa, wa ya Fursan-al-Hija' (O my lions, O my brave ones), 'Ma lakum, munadikum fala tujibuni' (What has happened to you? I am calling you, and you do not answer). Hussain is all alone, Hussain is without any helper or supporter. Once, Zainab came out of the tent and said, 'Brother, do not be anxious, Zainab is still alive, Zainab is here, do not feel lonely.' She said only this much, and Hussain said, 'Sister Zainab, then take me into the tent, take me into the tent.' They took him into the tent. And once at the door of the tent, Hussain first greeted everyone, and said, 'Ya Zainab, Ya Umm-e-Kulthum, Ya Ruqayya, Ya Fizza, Alaykunna minni salam' (My final peace be upon you). The ladies asked, 'Istaslamta lil mawt?' (Are you prepared for death?). Hussain said, 'Kaifa la yastaslamu lil mawt, man la mu'ina lahu wa la nasir' (How can one not be prepared for death who has no helper or supporter?). Zainab gave him support. Hussain came into the tent, came to Sayyid-us-Sajidin (Imam Sajjad). Zainab said, 'Son Sayyid-us-Sajidin, son, open your eyes, son, look, your father has come.' Sayyid-us-Sajidin tried to open his eyes, he also said, 'Mother, where is father? Where is father?' Sayyid-us-Sajidin could not recognize the Imam; so much blood had left Hussain's body that the color of his body had changed. Hussain said, 'Son Sayyid-e-Sajjad, I am your father.' Sayyid-e-Sajjad said, 'Father, has this happened to you? Father, all this blood?' Sayyid-e-Sajjad asked about each one, 'Father, is there no helper or supporter left?' He said, 'Son, everyone has been martyred, everyone has been killed.' He kept asking about each one, until he asked, 'O little one, brother Ali Akbar, what is the letter of martyrdom?' Then he asked, 'O little one, uncle Abbas, what is the letter of martyrdom?' Abbas was also killed. 'Son, now there is no one left in the curtains except me and you.' Sayyid-e-Sajjad said, 'Aunt, bring my sword, I will help my father.' Hussain said, 'No, my son, this is not the place or field for your Jihad. The field of your Jihad is the markets of Kufa and Sham. Son, be patient, that will be your true Jihad.' Hussain embraced Sayyid-e-Sajjad for the final farewell. Hussain was about to rise, and began to say to Sayyid-e-Sajjad, 'Son Sayyid-e-Sajjad, when you are released from captivity and go, give my greetings to my Shias, and say: Shiyati ma in sharabtum ma azb-e-furat-e-fukuruni (O my Shias, when you drink cool water, remember my thirst, and when there is a mention of any helpless and oppressed person, remember my helplessness).' Hussain remembered you at the final moment, he has sent his greetings to you. This Hussain, this oppressed Hussain, offer condolences to this oppressed Hussain today, offer condolences to the Imam of the Time, offer condolences to Janab-e-Zahra. Hussain rose. Now as Hussain began to walk, Zainab stopped him once again. She said, 'Brother, wait for a moment.' He said, 'What happened, Zainab?' She said, 'Brother, brother, when father was leaving this world, he said, Sister Zainab, when Hussain comes for the final farewell, then take a kiss of Hussain's throat on my behalf.' I asked, 'Father, why?' He said, 'A dagger will run across this throat.' When Hussain heard this, he said, 'Sister Zainab, move your gaze from the arms.' Hussain kissed his arms. Zainab asked, 'Brother, what is this?' He said, 'Sister, chains will be tied here. Sister, be patient.' Hussain's final farewell. After the final farewell, he came to the battlefield, looked at the corpses once, looked towards the Euphrates, and after looking, said, 'Ayyukum yuqaddimu jawani' (Who will bring my mount?). Remember the 28th of Rajab, when all the riders had left. Zainab Abbas, O Abbas! Step of youth, Abbas, bring my horse. Now Hussain is asking, 'O step of youth, who will bring my guide? Who will bring my mount?' It is not strange for Abbas, that the master was forced by death. Zainab came out, sister Zainab said, 'Brother, Zainab is still alive.' Zainab helped Hussain mount. Now Hussain came, it is found in the Maqtal (chronicle of martyrdom) that Hussain came, the first attack Hussain made was towards Qadisiyah. He did it in such a way that the armies began to collide with the walls of Qadisiyah. Now Hussain, when he returned, it is written in the Maqtal that the second attack Hussain made was towards the Euphrates, and it was such a severe attack that the armies began to flee here and there. Hussain reached the bank of the Euphrates. Hussain called out, 'Abbas! Abbas, rise and see my battle, Abbas!' Now when Hussain came for the third attack, he wanted to take a breath, to stop for a while. For once, for a single moment, Hussain stopped, when a voice came: 'Ya ayyatuhan-nafsul mutma'innatu irji'i ila rabbiki radiyatan mardiyyah' (O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing). O soul at peace, O soul at peace, return, return to your Lord. Your Lord is pleased with you and you are pleased with your Lord. Just as he heard this call, Hussain put his sword in the sheath. Now hear the remaining tragedies from the blessed tongue of Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). I do not have the courage to recite it. Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) says that as soon as Father put the sword in the sheath, one of the wretched ones threw a stone. From there, a rain of arrows followed. My father's body was covered in arrows. There were so many arrows that Father's body was not visible. Someone threw a stone, someone stabbed a spear. Hussain fell from the back of the horse onto the land of Karbala. No, rather he did not fall onto the land of Karbala, he fell onto the arrows. Now when he fell, Ibn-e-Sa'ad called out, 'Who is it that will separate Hussain's head from Hussain's body?' Bashim the accursed moved forward. The Imam of the Time says in Ziyarat-e-Nahiyah, 'Wa Shamrun fi jalisul...' Shamr is mounted on Hussain's chest. Zainab has now come, she is looking for Imam Hussain. Hussain was nowhere to be seen. The voice echoed in the atmosphere of Karbala, 'Ya Hussain! Ya Hussain!' The voice echoed, 'Ya Hussain!' Once Zainab came to the hill of Zainabiyah, which is called the hill of Zainabiyah today. This is the same height that Zainab climbed, and Zainab came and saw that scene which may Allah not show any sister. She saw that Shamr is mounted on the chest, the dagger is in his hand. Zainab could not do anything. She looked at the throat, she looked at the feet, there was no helper or supporter, no companion or sympathizer. Just once she called out, 'O Ibn-e-Sa'ad! O Ibn-e-Sa'ad, you are watching, my master is being slaughtered here.' As soon as Hussain heard the voice, he said, 'Zainab!' Go back to the tent, Hussain is still alive.' Zainab went back to the tent. She had not even stepped into the tent when the land of Karbala began to shake, black storms began to blow, the sun was eclipsed, the water of the Euphrates began to surge. Sister Zainab said, 'Son Sayyid-e-Sajjad, what is happening?' He said, 'Aunt, just remove the curtain of the tent once.' As soon as the curtain of the tent was removed, what did she see? Her father's head is raised on the tip of a spear. Sayyid-e-Sajjad calls out, 'Assalamu alayka ya Aba Abdillah, Assalamu alayka ya Ibn Rasulillah, Matam-e-Hussain.'

title: PROMO | GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 2025💐💐
excerpt: This promotional lecture highlights the significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm and the appointment of Imam Ali as the successor to the Prophet Muhammad. It recounts the historical narrative of Harith bin Nu'man al-Fihri, who challenged the divine appointment and faced immediate divine retribution. The speaker emphasizes the importance of Hadith al-Thaqalayn and the Prophet's declaration of Ali's authority over the believers.
content:
TSR presents. Nine is the Quran, the condition of faith, the successor of the Prophet. When this announcement was made, one individual named Harith bin Nu'man al-Fihri came to the Prophet's service. He said, 'If this message is from Allah, then let a punishment from Allah descend upon me right now; let a stone fall and destroy me.' His curse upon himself had not even been completed when a stone fell from the sky and destroyed Harith. You are mentioning this Hadith al-Thaqalayn here while telling people about its importance, saying, 'Ma-ashar-an-nas' (O people). In this same book, there is a debate of yours that took place at the house of Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Tahir, and 'Aktubu lakum kitaban la tadillu ba'dahu' (I will write for you a document after which you will never go astray). [Poetry in Persian/Arabic: The master of the garden, the master of the universe, those lost from the light of God. The master of the 'Lawlak' (Prophet) has not yet raised his voice, that whoever I am the Prophet of, Ali is his Master. Just as I am more entitled to the souls of all, Ali, my successor, is more entitled to them than their own souls.]
The declaration at Ghadir Khumm established Imam Ali as the successor to the Prophet.
Harith bin Nu'man al-Fihri challenged the divine nature of the announcement and was destroyed by a stone from the sky.
Hadith al-Thaqalayn is central to understanding the guidance provided by the Prophet.
The Prophet declared that whoever he is the master of, Ali is also his master.
The Prophet's authority over the souls of the believers is extended to Imam Ali as his successor.
The event of Ghadir serves as a foundational moment for the Shia faith and the concept of Wilayah.

title: Will of Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) - An Analysis | Wafaat Ya Shahaadat |Ek Guftugu: Part 4 #shia #sunni
excerpt: This lecture provides a critical analysis of the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) will, arguing that as the ultimate exemplar of Islamic law, he would not have neglected the mandatory duty of leaving a testament. The discussion explores historical accounts, including the 'Calamity of Thursday,' to contrast the Prophet's intent to provide guidance for the Ummah with the actions of companions who prevented it. By examining Shia traditions and historical records, the lecture asserts that the Prophet's true will explicitly designated Imam Ali (a.s.) as his successor and identifies the twelve Imams as the path to salvation.
content:
So, the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) who taught Muslims every single action in his life. How to cut nails, how to perform ghusl, applying kohl on Fridays—Muslims adopted all these things. But did this same Messenger (s.a.w.a.) not teach them about the will (wasiyyah)? There is no discourse without action. Now, the Quranic verse that has come, as you stated, is that Allah has made it mandatory to write a will. It was necessary for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to convey this message to the people. Now, when it has to be conveyed, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) must do it himself first. Brother, if you claim to be the successor of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), and if you say that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) did not leave a will, then who gave you the right to make a will? You consider it so important that you are going on a journey, yet you are writing a will, but you do not believe in the Messenger's (s.a.w.a.) will. And if, for example, a Muslim today says, 'No, we believe in the Messenger's (s.a.w.a.) will,' then bring it forth—where is the will? What will you find other than these three points, of which the third point is not even there? They forgot it; they forgot it. This shows how much importance you give to whom. You have recorded it in your books in that very manner. If the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had importance, then every minor detail of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would be present in your books, but that is... It would be present in your books, but it is not even visible itself. This is not the Messenger's (s.a.w.a.) will. Every wise person in the world understands that one of the most important stages of a human's life is in their will. So, through all these things, the hadiths you have narrated—those in the books of the Ahl-e-Sunnah and those in the books of the Shia—the conclusion is that when all these things are among the fundamental teachings of Islam, and a person should do these things before dying, then how is it possible that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) who conveyed these teachings to us would leave the world without a will? So, would the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) not make a will regarding these matters, knowing that after him, people would divide into sects and the majority of them would go astray? So, did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) not consider it necessary to make such a will for the people so that they could find a path of guidance and not go astray? From Prophet Adam (a.s.) to the last human to come into this world, if anyone's will is the most important, it cannot be more excellent than the Messenger's (s.a.w.a.). So, how much importance should Muslims have given to what the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) was leaving behind after him? A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim minash shaytanir rajim. A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'ala ka ya waliyyal 'asr. Wasiyyah is something that, outwardly, is just a document written on paper, but in terms of its importance, it has the power to both build and destroy families and nations. Every will has three aspects: First, whose will is it? Second, for whom is the will? And third, what is written in the will? The higher these three aspects are in their status, the more the importance of that will increases. And when the will belongs to the most excellent of all creation, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), then this is not an ordinary will, but the 'Wasiyyah al-Uzma' (the Great Will) of that Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). But was there really any will of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) or not? In the previous episode of this video series on the passing or martyrdom, we had a detailed discussion on the 'Waqi'at al-Qirtas' or 'Raziyat al-Khamis,' which is a blot on the history of Islam, in which we saw how the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was... Obstacles were placed in the way of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) when he wanted to have his will written, and insults were even hurled at the Prophet's status using inappropriate language. In this fourth and final episode of the series, let us see how, despite the opposition and the attempts to stop him, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had his will written in his final moments. Let us explore this through our discussion. It is a matter of regret and astonishment—and the more one is astonished, the more the regret grows—that in the major, so-called 'Sahih' books of the Muslims, there is virtually nothing to be found regarding the will of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And if there is anything, it consists of matters that would only be called advice for an ordinary person, not the will of the Messenger of Allah. Yet, in the Holy Quran, the concept of a will is mentioned at least four times, where the Quran has explained in complete detail how a will should be made. If we look at the command regarding the will in Surah Al-Baqarah, it is found in verse 180, in which Allah (t.b.t.) states: In which Allah (t.b.t.) states: 'Kutiba alaykum idha hadara ahadakum al-mawtu in taraka khayran al-wasiyyatu lil-walidayni wa al-aqrabina bil-ma'rufi haqqan 'ala al-muttaqin.' What is Allah (t.b.t.) stating in verse 180 of Surah Al-Baqarah? 'Kutiba alaykum'—it has been written for you, meaning it is obligatory upon you that when death approaches any one of you, and if he is leaving behind some wealth, he should make a will for his parents and relatives; this is a right upon the God-fearing (Muttaqin). And how does the verse begin? With the words 'Kutiba alaykum.' When the phrase 'Kutiba alaykum' is used, it means it has been written for you, meaning it is obligatory upon you—this reaches the level of being mandatory. Just as we find in the verse regarding fasting. Three verses later, in verse 183 of the same Surah Al-Baqarah, what do we find in the verse of fasting? 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu kutiba alaykum al-siyam'—fasting has been written for you, meaning fasting is obligatory. Now, the regret and astonishment I was speaking of is that the verse is from the Quran. It is in the Holy Quran. Muslims recite this verse. How can they not understand that the Prophet who brought this verse, the Prophet who is preaching this verse to us, could he go without... ...preaching this to us, could he go without making a will? It is impossible that the Prophet would preach this verse to us and not make a will himself. So, Hasan Bhai, the Quranic verse you mentioned clearly states that it is obligatory—making a will has been made obligatory for every Muslim. Allah Himself has given this command in the Holy Quran that you must make a will. So, should this not apply to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? If someone insists that this is not for the Messenger of Allah, that it is only for ordinary Muslims, then what should be done with the other verses of the Quran? For instance, in Surah As-Saff, Allah (s.w.t.) states in verses 2 and 3: 'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu lima taquluna ma la taf'alun'—O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Meaning, Allah is admonishing here, telling people that if you say something, you should only say what you have practiced yourself. There is no discourse without practice. Now, the Quranic verse that has come, as you stated, that Allah has made writing a will obligatory—it was necessary for the Messenger of Allah to convey this message to the people. And when it has to be conveyed, the Messenger of Allah must do it himself first. This is necessary for the Messenger of Allah. And look at the third verse, in which Allah (s.w.t.) states... ...in which Allah (s.w.t.) states that 'Kabura maqtan 'inda Allahi an taqulu ma la taf'alun'—it is a cause of great displeasure to Allah that you say what you do not do. Meaning, Allah becomes displeased, and we cannot even imagine that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) would do anything that would cause Allah's displeasure. And the character of the Messenger of Allah, the way he acts—he is such that in terms of action, Allah tells him, 'O Messenger, take some rest too.' In the field of action, the Messenger of Allah is such that if someone were to say that the Messenger of Allah was preaching something that was not necessary for him, and that he himself would not do it, then this is extremely foolish talk. Anyone who says such a thing does not know the Messenger of Allah and is trying to downgrade him. And even the principle of the world is: 'Practice what you preach.' Brother, whatever you are preaching, at least practice it. Any wise person, anyone who possesses even a little bit of intellect, will acknowledge that it is never good for a person to preach what he does not practice himself. And there are further verses in the Holy Quran regarding this. Allah (s.w.t.) states in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 44: ...in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 44, Allah states: 'Atamuruna al-nasa bil-birri wa tansawna anfusakum'—Do you command people to do good and forget yourselves? Meaning, when you command people to do good, when you talk about guidance, when you preach goodness, then remember yourselves first. You must perform that good deed first, then tell people, 'Yes, you do this, perform this action,' while forgetting yourself? This is what Allah is stating in the Holy Quran. Further, He says, 'Wa antum tatluna al-kitab, afala ta'qilun'—And you recite the Book of Allah, do you not have any intellect? Meaning, the same point: a wise person would never do this. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is the perfection of intellect. How can anyone expect from him that he would preach—because it is clear that he must preach, it is the command of the Quran, it is the duty of the Messenger of Allah to preach—and then not practice what he preaches? This does not apply to the Messenger of Allah; rather, the Messenger of Allah is the guide, the leader, and he has to implement the Sharia for the Muslims. Therefore, it becomes even more necessary for the Messenger of Allah to write a will. We do not consider anyone a Messenger who preaches to others but does not practice it himself. Indeed. And it is the custom of the world that if such... And it is a custom of this world that why should one follow someone who does not act upon what they preach to others? Correct. If we talk about traditions, there are many narrations in both Shia and Sunni books regarding the subject of 'Wasiyyah' (will/testament) that highlight its importance. Let us present a Hadith before you, and this Hadith is found in both Bukhari and Muslim. This Hadith is narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated: If a Muslim possesses wealth and intends to write a will, it is not appropriate for them to spend two nights without keeping their will secured. A written will should be with them; a written will should be with them, and they should not delay it for too long. After the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stated this, Ibn Umar says, 'Ma marrat alayya laylatun munthu sami'tu Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.)...' Now, these people do not send salutations upon the Prophet's family and limit it only to 'Sallam'. But the correct way to recite it is 'Sami'tu Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi)...' Sami'tu Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi) qala dhalika illa wa inna wasiyati... He says that ever since I heard this statement from the Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi), not a single night has passed for me without my written will being with me. This was the Sunni perspective; you mentioned a Hadith from Bukhari and Muslim. If we look at the corpus of Shia Hadith, there are hundreds of narrations. Hundreds—our scholars have compiled them, and this shows the difference. It shows the vast difference between Shia Hadith and non-Shia Hadith. Just take the topic of 'Wasiyyah'—and we are not even talking about all the books, just one book, 'Wasa'il al-Shia' by Sheikh al-Hurr al-Amili (r.a.). In volume 19 of Wasa'il al-Shia, he has brought 100 chapters regarding the will. And in those 100 chapters, there are 1,358 Hadiths—meaning approximately 1,400 Hadiths just on the subject of the will. The importance of the will, what things should be included in the will, what should not be written in the will, not to neglect the will—there are 100 such chapters containing about 1,350 to 1,400 narrations. Meaning, the number of chapters he has brought... Meaning, the number of chapters he has brought, perhaps even the total number of Hadiths among the others is not that many. It is not present among them. Correct. Now, let us look at some of these Hadiths regarding the importance of the will from our Shia sources. In the same Wasa'il al-Shia, volume 19, let us look at some Hadiths. The first Hadith is from the sixth Imam, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), in which the Imam says: 'Annahu la yanbaghi'—meaning it is not appropriate for any person 'yabita'—that he sleeps 'illa wa wasiyatuhu tahta ra'sihi'—unless his will is under his head. The practice of keeping the will under one's pillow while sleeping is derived from this very Hadith, that it is not permissible, it is not befitting, it is not appropriate for him to sleep without a will. And then in another narration within the same chapter, it is narrated from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi) that the Prophet said: 'Al-wasiyyatu haqqan 'ala kulli muslim'—a will is the right of every Muslim. Look closely at this Hadith; it is only a few words, but the Prophet called the will the right of a Muslim. Meaning, no one can stop a Muslim from making a will; if a Muslim wants to make a will, they cannot be stopped. The will is their right, and whoever tries to stop them from this right... Whoever tries to stop them from this right has deprived a Muslim of their right. So, this is about an ordinary Muslim. Think about what the fate will be of those who stopped the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) from writing or stating his will? It is like saying that performing Salah is a Muslim's right, fasting is a Muslim's right, and whoever stops a Muslim from doing this, what will be their fate? And as you mentioned, what will be the fate of the one who stopped the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) from his right? There was a detailed discussion on this in the incident of 'Raziya-tul-Khamis' (The Calamity of Thursday) which you brothers discussed earlier, covering in detail who stopped the Prophet from writing his will. Now, following this, in those same chapters, there is a Hadith specifically about a person who does not make a will and leaves this world without one. The narration is stated as: 'Man mata ghayra wasiyyah, mata maytatan jahiliyyah'—whoever leaves this world without a will, dies the death of Jahiliyyah (ignorance). Jahiliyyah means Kufr (disbelief) and Nifaq (hypocrisy)—the era before Islam. Meaning, their death is not upon Islam; it is a death of Kufr. It is a death of irreligion, and they left this world as a hypocrite. And following that, there is another Hadith from 'Manaqib Aali Abi Talib (a.s.)' that whoever dies... From 'Manaqib Aali Abi Talib (a.s.)' that whoever dies and does not make a will, their final act—the last act they did before leaving this world—was not making a will, so they depart this world in a state of disobedience. This is the consequence of not writing a will. And similarly, what is the reward for the one who does make a will? It is narrated from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Allama Majlisi has included it in 'Bihar al-Anwar', and Muhaddith Nuri has also included this Hadith in 'Mustadrak al-Wasa'il'. He says: 'Man mata 'ala wasiyyah hasanah, mata shahida'—whoever leaves this world having made a good will, dies as a martyr. Meaning, on one hand, the one who makes a will departs this world with the death of a martyr. The death of a martyr means they have been forgiven. They will be granted the status of a martyr. But on the other hand, the one who does not make a will dies the death of Kufr, Nifaq, and Jahiliyyah. Now, what is the conclusion from all these points? When these Hadiths—and we have seen these are the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) Hadiths—are narrated by Imam Sadiq (a.s.), the truthful one of the family of Muhammad, narrating from the Prophet... [clears throat] What is the conclusion? So, what is the conclusion from all these things, the Hadiths you mentioned that are in the books of the Sunnis and the Shias? The conclusion is that when all these things are among the fundamental teachings of Islam, and a person should do these things before dying, it is a fundamental teaching. So, how is it possible that the Prophet who brought these teachings to us would leave this world without a will? And one reason for the importance of the will is also revealed here. Like the Hadith you read, that a person should not sleep without keeping their will under their head. Perhaps it is because there is no guarantee of life. A person can die at any time. So, they should always keep their will with them. And conversely, where the will is so important, it is also mentioned in the Hadith that if a person does not write their will, what will be the consequence? We find a Hadith from the Imams (a.s.) in which they say: 'Man lam yuhsin wasiyyatahu 'inda mawtihi, kana dhalika naqsan fi 'aqlihi wa muruwwatihi'—whoever does not properly arrange or write their will at the time of their death, it is evidence of a deficiency in their intellect and their character. Wow! Meaning, that person does not even possess the intellect if they do not prepare their will. It is evidence of a lack of intellect that a person is about to leave the world and does not make a will. And as you said, when an ordinary person leaves the world, they don't even know when they are going to leave. But this is not the case with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). He knew very well, and before leaving—in his final days—he mentioned so many times that 'I will soon leave from among you, I will leave, I will leave.' So, how can it be that when he knew he was going to leave, he did not make a will? All these verses and narrations we mentioned prove the importance of the will and how mandatory it is to write it. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi), who is superior to every person, superior to every Prophet, who is the 'Uswah Hasanah' (excellent example) according to the Holy Quran, about whom the Quran praises him saying: 'Laqad kana lakum fi Rasoolillahi uswatun hasanah'—surely there is for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern of conduct. Meaning, look at the Prophet and do as he does. He is an ideal for you, a model of action. So, the Prophet who taught Muslims every single action in his life—how to cut nails, how to perform Ghusl, to apply Kohl on Fridays—Muslims adopted all these things. But did this same Prophet not teach them about the will? And if... And if he did, did the Muslims not take it from him, did they not learn a lesson from him? So, the question arises: what was the will of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi)? Because if he left this world without a will, then 'Na'udhubillah' (God forbid), the things we saw in the narrations would apply to the Prophet. This makes it absolutely clear that the Prophet did make his will. We cannot even keep this thought in any corner of our hearts or minds that the Prophet did not make a will. It is out of the question. The Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi) definitely and absolutely made a will. And in this regard, when we study the books of the Sunnis, in the incident of 'Raziya-tul-Khamis'—the Calamity of Thursday, about which we made a detailed video last year—it is narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi) made a will consisting of three points. Meaning, there were three points that his will consisted of. The first point was to expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula. Meaning, all the polytheists should be expelled from the Arabian Peninsula, which is called the Gulf, the Arabian Peninsula. The second was that if any delegation comes to meet people after the Prophet, they should meet them and treat them in the same way the Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi) used to treat them. And the third point of the will, he says that the Prophet did make a will, but... but I forgot. But I forgot. Now, compare this with that statement of the Prophet (s.a.w.a. wa aalihi): 'I'tuni bi kitabin aktubu lakum kitaban lan tadillu ba'dahu abadan'—bring me a pen and inkwell so that I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray. So, neither the expulsion of polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula, nor the treatment of delegations, nor this third thing that Ibn Abbas forgot—none of these are things that would serve as a source of eternal guidance for the Ummah and save them from going astray. The first point you mentioned, which is in their books—to expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula—if we consider this as the Prophet's will according to them, have the Muslims acted upon this today? And when it comes to guidance, the Prophet said, 'I will write something after which you will never go astray'—meaning a matter of guidance. So, was the Prophet not concerned about the guidance of this Ummah... So, was the Prophet not concerned about the guidance of this Ummah, that he left without saying or writing anything other than these few things, of which the third one, as you said, was half-hearted? Ibn Abbas said, 'I don't remember the third point.' But when we look at the people who came after them, if we look at history, if we look at the lives of those who called themselves the self-appointed successors of the Prophet, what do we see during the time of the first ruler? When the time for the first ruler to depart from this world arrived, what did he do? He called the third ruler and had a will [clears throat] written. He had a will written. We don't need to go into full detail, otherwise, we will deviate from the topic. Our topic is the Prophet's will, not the will of others. But anyway, when he had the will written, what do we find in history? He kept dictating, kept dictating, and while dictating, he fainted. He fainted. When he regained consciousness, he asked the third ruler, who was writing the will, 'What did you write next?' So he said, 'I have written that your successor will be such and such person.' Meaning, he wrote the name of the second ruler. So the first ruler said, 'Yes, yes, you wrote correctly.' Meaning, a will that he fainted while writing, the same person who until yesterday was on the Prophet's mind... They fainted. Those who until yesterday were accusing the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) mind, they themselves fainted while writing their own wills. Yes. And when it was seen that, brother, they didn't actually write the will themselves either. Someone else wrote it, and they only verified it. 'Yes, okay, you have written it correctly.' So, in this way, the government was transferred from the first to the second. Yes, and when the turn of the second came—well, the government that was transferred from the first to the second, people objected to the name of the second ruler that was written. They are making a will for a person to be the ruler after them, but the people are not satisfied with him. People even protested. What kind of protest did they make? They came to this gentleman and even said, 'You are leaving us under the command of a person who is extremely hot-tempered. He is harsh-hearted. He is extremely hot-tempered.' And they say—what do they say?—'His tone of speaking is so harsh, and you are leaving us under the command of such a person.' But despite that, no one listened to anything. Now, when the time came for the second ruler's final moments, what did he do? He also made a will, didn't he? What did he make a will about? He created an entire Shura committee, and that is a strange will. A strange committee was created, that six-person committee, in which the very people he is making a will to appoint as his successor, the order for their execution is also in that same... The order for the execution of those same people is in that same will, that if these people cannot choose a ruler, then execute them. Meaning, that was less of a will and more of an innovation (bid'ah). And if you, brother, if you are claiming that you are the successor of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.), and if you are saying that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) did not leave a will, then who gave you the right to make a will? So, for you, it has such importance that you are going through the throes of death, but you are writing a will. But you are not a believer in the Messenger's (s.a.w.a.) will. And if, for example, in today's date, any Muslim says, 'No, we believe in the Messenger's (s.a.w.a.) will,' then bring it. Where is the will? Where is it? That's true. Apart from these three points, what will you find? Out of which the third point doesn't even exist. They forgot. They forgot. When the Shura committee was fully formed by the second ruler before he left, what different conditions did he set? But before the Shura began, how should it start? What did he say about that? This is also part of his will, isn't it? That he called Janab-e-Miqdad. And what did he say after calling Janab-e-Miqdad? 'When you lower me into my grave, then...'—meaning, again, this six-person committee, then gather these people in one room so that they can choose a man to become the Caliph. Or, Sheikh, someone should say to you at this time... Someone should say to you at this time, 'You remembered to tell Janab-e-Miqdad to lower you into your grave first, and after that, do all this work.' You didn't think of these things during the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) time? At that time, you left the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) funeral and went to Saqifah. Meaning, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is also saying that I am among you for only a few more days. I will leave this world. After that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave a long sermon. He set the stage, saying I am coming for the last time, and a person in their final days says only things that are very important for people. He does not talk about trivial things. So the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave a long sermon and then said, 'Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, be an enemy to whoever is his enemy, and help whoever helps him, and abandon whoever abandons him.' Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla. And after that, the incident of the Thursday (Raziya-tul-Khamees), with which our discussion began, in that incident too, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told the people, 'Give me paper and pen so that I may write for you something after which you will never go astray.' If we summarize all these points, Alhamdulillah, in our books, the Prophet's complete will—the different wills he made in different styles, on different occasions, from Dawat-e-Dhul-Ashira to Hajjat-ul-Wida, from the beginning to Ghadir, and even in his final moments during the incident of Thursday—the Prophet was continuously pointing toward his actual, true will and his true Wasi. So, we find the will, but if someone wants to know briefly what the essence of the Prophet's entire life is, the most important will, it points toward what the Prophet intended: 'Bring it so that I may write something after which you will never go astray.' And this is the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. After which you will never go astray, and this is the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. We find this only in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahlulbayt. As long as you hold fast to both, you will never go astray after me. And these two things, the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, will never separate from each other until they meet me at the Pond of Kawthar.' These things that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is leaving as a will are the Quran and his Ahlulbayt. If a person holds onto these two, they will be saved from the misguidance until the Day of Judgment, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) wanted to save them from. But those who intended to prevent the Prophet from writing did not let him write. But it is Allah's will that the thing comes to be written, comes onto paper. So, those who did not want it left, and those who wanted it stayed, and after that, the task was accomplished. But it was Allah's will that the Prophet's will be written, so it was written. And therefore, Alhamdulillah, there is only one group today—from the martyrdom of the Prophet until today, and Insha'Allah until the Day of Judgment—that... Insha'Allah until the Day of Judgment, there is only one group that truly acts upon this will, by holding onto both the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This is the Prophet's true and final will. So, if anyone today wants to act upon the Prophet's true will, they must hold onto the last Imam among those twelve Imams whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) named in his will, who is Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Until a person holds onto him, they cannot be saved from misguidance. Until they hold onto him, they will not attain the Prophet's will. Holding onto the Prophet's will means holding onto Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). And that is why, by invoking the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), we pray to the Lord of the Worlds: O Lord, hasten the reappearance of our Imam (a.s.). Grant us the ability to act upon the true will of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and along with the reappearance of our last Imam, grant us the ability to be counted among his true servants. Finally, all praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance of worship, the necessity of Wilayah, and the profound lessons derived from the tragedy of Karbala. It emphasizes the importance of congregational prayer, the purification of the soul through Wudu, and the role of the Ahlulbayt as the foundation of faith. The discourse further highlights the virtues of patience, the dangers of greed, and the duty of parents to instill religious values in their children.

The greatness of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is such that even if one were to spend their entire life describing it, it would not be enough. The status of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is beyond human comprehension. When we speak of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), we are speaking of the one who is the mercy to the worlds. His character and his teachings are the guiding light for all of humanity, and his presence is a blessing for every soul. The love for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his family (a.s.) is the essence of faith. It is through this love that one finds the path to salvation and the closeness to Allah (s.w.t.). The life of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is a testament to patience, sacrifice, and devotion to the command of Allah. Every moment of his life serves as a lesson for those who seek the truth. In the face of adversity, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) remained steadfast, showing us that true strength lies in submission to the will of the Almighty and in upholding justice. The teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) emphasize the importance of compassion, kindness, and unity among the believers. He taught us to look beyond ourselves and serve humanity. May we always strive to follow the path laid down by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his purified progeny (a.s.), for in their footsteps lies the ultimate success in this world and the hereafter. In the history of Islam, there has never been a sacrifice like that of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The world has seen many events, but none compare to the tragedy of Karbala, where the truth stood firm against falsehood. Just as there is only one sun, there was only one Shabbir (Imam Hussain (a.s.)). Even when the stars were not visible, the light of his sacrifice shone brightly, teaching the world the meaning of standing for justice against tyranny. Thousands were taken, and in a single moment, everything was lost, as if the world were merely a toy. Yet, the legacy of Imam Hussain (a.s.) remains, a beacon of light that will never fade, guiding the hearts of the faithful forever. title: Jaan Nisaar e Wilayat - Hujr Ibn Adi (a.r.)
excerpt: This lecture recounts the unwavering loyalty of Hujr ibn Adi (a.r.) to Imam Ali (a.s.) during his final moments. Despite being offered safety for himself and his son in exchange for cursing the Imam, Hujr refused to compromise his faith. His steadfastness serves as a profound example of devotion and integrity in the face of martyrdom.
content:
It is that whenever Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was arrested, he was with these companions. They were arrested in Syria. Now they are taking them to Syria. The commander of the Syrian army said, 'There is still a chance, curse Ali, and I will save your life, your children, and your young son. Your young son's life will be saved, and your friends' lives will be saved.' But the one who is loyal to Ali (a.s.) will never be a traitor. The one who is loyal will never be a traitor. The one who is loyal... he was a descendant of Hatim Tai. What did he say? 'You do your work, let me do my work.' We are not people who will compromise. He addressed him like this. He addressed him like this: 'You do your work, we will do our work.' And then, when the time for martyrdom came, he did not say, 'Okay, kill my son first so that I can be satisfied that my faith does not waver.' This is the level of love.
