title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 25 | Tafseer of Surah al-Kawthar (108) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture continues the exegesis of Surah al-Kawthar, focusing on the spiritual significance of the Kawthar river and its connection to the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker narrates traditions regarding the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) Mi'raj, highlighting the divine appointment of Ali (a.s.) as his successor and the celestial celebration of his status. The session emphasizes that love and acceptance of Ali's (a.s.) leadership are essential conditions for the acceptance of one's religious deeds.
content:
Masha'Allah, La Hawla wa La Quwwata illa Billahil Aliyyil Adheem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin. Assalatu wassalamu ala Ashrafil Anbiya wal Mursalin, Muhammadin wa alihi at-tahirin. Amma ba'd. Respected ladies and gentlemen, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Once again, I am present in your presence with the explanation of Surah Al-Kawthar. Yesterday, the discussion was about Kawthar, about which it is said that it is a river in Paradise. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was asked about its qualities. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'This river that flows, its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey...' Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and softer than butter. And he described its specialty: its banks will be of saffron, its soil will be of musk. And he said to Mawla Ali (a.s.), 'This river will be for me, for you, and for your friends.' Meaning, whoever is a friend of Ali (a.s.) will be able to drink from this river. Whoever is not a friend of Ali (a.s.) and does not love Ali (a.s.) cannot even come near this river, let alone drink from it. Then I mentioned its depth is equal to 70,000 years. Now, let me present more narrations of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) before you. I am reading from Tafsir al-Safi, volume 9, page 700. It says that Ali (a.s.) is the one whom Allah gave me... Allah gave me a response... Allah gave me a response. Allah showed me the heavens and opened the doors of the heavens for me, until I could see them and they could see me. Tears filled his eyes. I asked him... I asked him the reason for his tears. He said, 'Ibn Abbas, the first thing Allah spoke to me about was this: O Muhammad, look towards the earth.' When I looked towards the earth, where I had been, the doors of the heavens had opened. I saw Ali (a.s.) looking up at me. This is how I spoke to Ali (a.s.) while I was above the heavens and he was on the earth. Ibn Abbas asked, 'What did Allah say to you?' He replied, 'Allah said, O Muhammad, I have made Ali (a.s.) your successor, vizier, and caliph. Now, when you go to the earth, tell Ali (a.s.), although he is hearing even now.' So I told Ali (a.s.) at that time when I went to the earth, and Ali (a.s.) replied, 'I have accepted this.' At that time, Allah commanded the angels to send blessings upon Ali (a.s.). Thus, all the angels sent blessings upon Ali (a.s.), and Ali (a.s.) replied to the angels' greetings. At that time, I saw that the angels were giving each other the good news of Ali's (a.s.) Wilayah. So when I passed by the angels, they congratulated me on Ali's (a.s.) Wilayah and said, 'We are the ones who believe in the night when He made you the true Prophet.' All the angels were given the good news of Ali's (a.s.)... The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'He who made me a Prophet of Truth, all the angels are happy with the Caliphate of Ali (a.s.). At that time, I saw the angels of the Arsh (Throne) also looking towards the earth. During that, Gabriel (a.s.) told me that the rest of the angels have already visited Imam Ali (a.s.), but the angels of the Arsh have just received permission now, so they are bowing their heads to visit Ali (a.s.).' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'When I returned to earth, I narrated my story to Ali (a.s.), and Ali (a.s.) narrated the entire story of my Mi'raj to me. Then I realized that wherever I stepped, Ali (a.s.) was watching over me. I asked him, "Give me some advice." The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, "I advise you to love Ali (a.s.). By Him in whose hand is my soul, who made me a Prophet of Truth, Allah will not accept anyone's deeds until they acknowledge the Wilayah and love of Ali (a.s.). By Him who made me a Prophet, those who have attributed children to God have committed a sin, but the enemies of Ali (a.s.) will be punished even more than them." Ibn Abbas says I asked the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), "Is there anyone who bears enmity towards Ali (a.s.)?" He said, "Yes, those people who have no connection with the religion." He said, "Yes, those people who have no connection with the religion. By Him who made me a Prophet of Truth, Allah has not created a Prophet better than me, and has not created a Wasi (successor) better than Ali (a.s.)." Ibn Abbas says I asked the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), "O Messenger of Allah, what is the complete fulfillment of worship according to your command?" When the time of his passing reached the station of Prophethood, he said, "O Ibn Abbas, remain as an opponent of Ali's (a.s.) opposition and do not support him." I asked, "Why don't you tell the people this?" He wept and remained silent for a long time. After remaining silent, he said, "If Allah wants to guide someone, He turns them towards Ali (a.s.). To leave them, to turn away from them, to consider them as one's own, to consider their enemy as an enemy, and to consider their friend as one's own friend." When someone asked in the presence of Muhammad ibn Abbas about the clear picture, he said, "It is the Holy Quran, it is the only proof." I said, "Allah the Almighty has given me five characteristics, and has given Ali (a.s.) five characteristics. He gave me the Kawthar, and gave Ali (a.s.) the same..." Now pay attention to this narration, what is the status of the Master of the Universe, what are the virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is describing. The virtues that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is describing regarding the Mi'raj, if the world still does not understand them, then it is their weakness, their deficiency. Whatever is said, it can be called the misfortune of those who do not understand. The virtues that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is describing with such clarity, and this narration that I have narrated, is recorded by the scholars of the Ahl al-Sunnah as well. There are many authentic books available. It is a matter of wonder because the virtues of Ali (a.s.) are not seen; there are at least one thousand verses in the Holy Quran revealed in the virtue of Ali (a.s.). Imagine how much more there is. I am concluding this discussion here, and Insha'Allah, I will present the further discussion before you. Insha'Allah, our interpretation of Surah al-Kawthar will be completed. Until tomorrow, I bid you farewell.

title: 1st Maah-e-Ramazan Ko Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer Padhne Ka Sawaab
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual rewards of reciting Dua-e-Joshan-e-Kabeer on the first night of Ramadan. The speaker explains that this supplication was inscribed on the Throne of Allah long before creation and grants the reciter the reward of Laylat al-Qadr. Furthermore, it promises the creation of 70,000 angels to pray for the reciter and ensures direct access to Allah's mercy on the Day of Judgment.
content:
When did Allah Almighty write this supplication on the pillar of the Arsh (Throne)? Fifty thousand years before creating the world. And whoever recites this supplication with a sincere intention, with purity of heart, when? At the beginning of the month of Ramadan, then what happens? Allah Almighty grants him the reward of Laylat al-Qadr. He receives the reward of Laylat al-Qadr. And Allah creates 70,000 angels for that person, who glorify Allah, who sanctify Him, and all that reward goes to the person who recites this supplication. Then after that, Allah says, 'O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), whoever recites this supplication, there will be no veil between him and Allah Almighty.' Allahu Akbar. What does 'no veil' mean? Now, whatever this person asks for, Allah will grant his supplication. And on the Day of Judgment, when the field of Resurrection is established and he is brought forth, all the people in that vast field, all the creation, will look at him and say, 'Who is this person? Who is surrounded by Ghilman (youths of Paradise), so many servants, so many angels—angels in front of him, angels behind him—and they are taking him?' Then a caller from the side of the Most Merciful will call out, 'O My servant, enter Paradise without any reckoning.'

title: Zuhoor-e-Imam Jald Ho Sakta hai Agar...
excerpt: This lecture discusses the concept of Bada (divine change) in the context of the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). By referencing the historical precedent of the Children of Israel, the speaker emphasizes that collective prayer and sincere lamentation can hasten the end of the occultation. The talk highlights that the timing of the Imam's return is not fixed and can be accelerated through the spiritual efforts of the Shia community.
content:
The famous Tawqi of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) in which the Imam himself commands: 'And pray a lot for the hastening of the Faraj (reappearance).' Or the statement of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in which he explained that the cause of the salvation of the Children of Israel was their collective weeping, lamenting, and praying to Allah for 40 consecutive days. That is, when the Children of Israel wept and lamented together for 40 days and prayed to Allah, Allah reduced the occultation of Hazrat Musa (a.s.) by 170 years. That is, the 400-year punishment that Allah had originally decreed for them, Allah reduced it by 170 years, and after 230 years, He granted Hazrat Musa (a.s.) his reappearance. Here, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'You and your example are the same. If you come together and weep and lament before Allah and pray for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman, then Allah can change this matter (Bada) and hasten his reappearance. And if you do not do so, the matter of reappearance will go to its limit.' The important point here is that this teaching and command of prayer points to the fact that there is room for Bada (change) in the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). [music]

title: Yazid Par La'nat - Imam Reza (a.s.) Ka Hukm [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture recounts a historical narration from Imam Reza (a.s.) regarding the atrocities committed by Yazid after the tragedy of Karbala. It describes how Yazid mocked the Ahlulbayt by playing chess and drinking wine over the noble head of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The speaker emphasizes the Imam's instruction for Shias to abstain from these acts and to remember the suffering of the Imam whenever they encounter such symbols of oppression.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Master of the Age, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. For the family of Imam Husayn (a.s.), the hardships of Kufa and Sham were far more difficult than the tragedies of Karbala. Fadl ibn Shadhan says that I heard Imam Rida (a.s.) saying that when the noble head of Imam Husayn (a.s.) was brought to Sham, on the orders of Yazid (may Allah's curse be upon him), the Imam's noble head was placed down and a tablecloth was spread over it. Then he and his companions began to eat and drink wine. When they finished, the accursed Yazid ordered that the noble head of the Imam be placed in a tray under his throne and a chessboard be spread over it. Then Yazid (may Allah's curse be upon him) sat there and began to play chess, and he was taking the names of Imam Husayn (a.s.), his noble father Imam Ali (a.s.), and his noble grandfather the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and mocking them, God forbid. Whenever he would defeat his companion in a game of chess, he would pick up the wine and drink it three times, and pour the remaining wine onto the tray placed under the ground. Then Imam Rida (a.s.) said, 'Therefore, whoever is our Shia should abstain from drinking wine and playing chess. And whoever sees wine and chess should remember Imam Husayn (a.s.) and curse Yazid and the family of Ziyad.' Allah the Almighty, in exchange for this act, erases all his sins, even if his sins were equal to the number of stars. From this Hadith of Imam Rida (a.s.), it is known that drinking wine, playing chess, and showing disrespect to the status of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) were the traits of Yazid ibn Muawiya (may Allah's curse be upon them both). Therefore, we pray in the court of the Lord of the Worlds: O God! For the sake of Imam Husayn (a.s.), grant us the ability to act upon this Hadith of Imam Rida (a.s.), that whenever we see wine or chess, we remember the oppression of Imam Husayn (a.s.) and curse Yazid and the family of Ziyad, and may this act of ours be a cause for the forgiveness of our sins. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Motasim Ka Hasad Imam Muhammad Taqi (a.s) Ki Shahadat Ka Sabab Banaa
excerpt: This lecture recounts the events leading to the martyrdom of Imam Muhammad Taqi (a.s.) at the hands of the Abbasid Caliph Mu'tasim. It details a legal debate in the Caliph's court where the Imam's superior knowledge regarding Islamic jurisprudence humiliated the court scholars. This incident fueled the jealousy of Qazi Ibn Abi Dawood, who incited Mu'tasim to view the Imam as a political threat. Consequently, the Caliph orchestrated the poisoning of the Imam, leading to his tragic martyrdom.
content:
Mu'tasim's jealousy became the cause of the martyrdom of Imam Muhammad Taqi (a.s.). Qazi Ibn Abi Dawood states that one day a thief confessed to his theft in Mu'tasim's court and requested the prescribed punishment, upon which Mu'tasim gathered the scholars, and Imam Muhammad Taqi (a.s.) was also present there. Mu'tasim asked those scholars, 'Where should the thief's hands be cut from?' Ibn Abi Dawood said, 'From the wrists,' and presented the verse of Tayammum as evidence, in which 'hand' means the wrist. Other scholars said the hand should be cut from the elbows because hands are washed up to the elbows in Wudu. Mu'tasim asked Imam Taqi (a.s.), 'What do you have to say about this?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'These people have said what they had to say. It is better if I am kept away from this.' Then Mu'tasim requested the Imam (a.s.), 'I swear you by Allah, please state it.' Upon this, the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Since you have sworn by Allah, then listen. These people have made a mistake in understanding the Sunnah of the Messenger. Only the fingers will be cut, and the rest of the hand will be left.' When Mu'tasim asked for evidence, the Imam (a.s.) said, 'It is the saying of the Messenger that prostration is on seven limbs: the forehead, two hands, two knees, and the toes of both feet. If the hand is cut from the wrist or elbow, then for prostration, the hand...' will not remain. Whereas Allah Ta'ala says, 'Wa al-masajidu lillah', meaning the limbs of prostration belong to Allah. And that which belongs to Allah cannot be severed. Mu'tasim was extremely surprised and ordered only the thief's fingers to be cut, not the rest of the hand. Ibn Abi Dawood said, 'This was a scene of Qiyamah for me, and I wish I were not alive.' Three days later, he went to Mu'tasim and said, 'It is my duty to advise the King, and I am certain that after this, my abode will be Hell.' He said to Mu'tasim, 'Yesterday, when you preferred the word of that person, you should have kept in mind that the scholars, jurists, your relatives, and the public in the court were listening carefully. In such a situation, you ignored the words of your scholars and accepted the decision of that person whose Imamate some people believe in, and often suspect that he is more entitled to the Caliphate than you.' Ibn Abi Dawood says, 'I saw the color of Mu'tasim's face changing, and he understood my point. He said to me, 'May Allah reward you with good for your good intentions.' Four days later, he invited Imam Taqi (a.s.) to his house. The Imam (a.s.) refused to come.' Mu'tasim said, 'I am only inviting you for a meal so that my house may be blessed.' Upon Mu'tasim's great insistence, Imam Taqi (a.s.) accepted his invitation. When the Imam (a.s.) ate the food, he realized that he had been poisoned. The Imam (a.s.) called for his mount and headed towards his house, saying, 'My leaving your house is better for you.' Then the effect of the poison began to take hold of the Imam's (a.s.) body, and for days and nights, the Imam (a.s.) suffered intense pain, and finally, he departed from this world. We pray to Allah Ta'ala to hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), so that revenge can be taken from all the killers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ameen Ya Rabbul Alameen. [Music]

title: Imam Hasan (a.s.) Ka Naam 'Hasan' Kyun Rakha Gaya? ! SIBT-E-AKBAR (a.s) GRAND QUIZ 2022
excerpt: This lecture explains the profound spiritual significance behind the name of Imam Hasan (a.s.). It highlights a tradition from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) stating that the Imam was named Hasan because the heavens and all earths are established through the grace of Allah associated with his name. The speaker emphasizes that this blessing extends beyond our world to all of Allah's creations.
content:
Ya Hasan. It is found in the traditions that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Summiyal Hasanu hasanan li-anna bi-ihsanillahi qamat-is-samawatu wal-ardun' (Imam Hasan was named Hasan because it is by the grace of Allah that the heavens and the earths are established). Meaning, the name of Imam Hasan (a.s.) is that grace of Allah due to which the earth and the heavens are established. As you stated in the Hadith, the word 'ardun' (earths) is used. Meaning, there are many earths. Meaning, all the earths that Allah has created—not just this world, but all the worlds that Allah has created—all those worlds, all those earths, are established by the blessing of the name of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.).
The name 'Hasan' is derived from the grace of Allah.

key_points: The name 'Hasan' is derived from the grace of Allah.
The heavens and earths are sustained by the blessing of Imam Hasan (a.s.).
The term 'ardun' implies the existence of multiple earths beyond our own.
Imam Hasan (a.s.) holds a central position in the stability of the universe.
The naming of the Imam was a divinely inspired act by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).

chapters.title: The Divine Significance of Imam Hasan's Name
chapters.summary: An exploration of the Prophetic tradition explaining why Imam Hasan (a.s.) was named Hasan and its cosmic implications.

title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 4 | Hazrat Narjis Khatoon & Birth of Imam Mahdi (علیہما السلام)
excerpt: This lecture explores the life and spiritual significance of Hazrat Narjis Khatoon, the mother of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), detailing her noble lineage and the divine orchestration of her marriage to Imam Hasan al-Askari. The session examines the historical context of the Imam's hidden birth, known as Khafiyul Mawlid, and emphasizes the importance of Ma'rifah and Adab in the lives of the Ahlulbayt. Furthermore, it addresses common historical objections and warns against speculative claims regarding signs of reappearance, urging believers to focus on genuine devotion and service to the Imam.
content:
La hawla wala quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azeem. A'udhu billahis sami'il alimi minash shaytanir rajeem. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Wa ajjil farajahum. Wa ahlik aduwwahum. Minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan. Salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba-ihi. Fi hadihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah. Waliyan wa hafiza. Wa qa'idan wa nasira. Wa dalilan wa ayna. Hatta tuskinahu arzaka taw'a. Wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyikal faraj. Waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi. Wala taj'alna min a'da-ihi. Wa waffiqna lima tuhibbu wa tarda. Wala takilna ila anfusina tarfata aynin abada. Wala tastabdil bina ghairana. Bihaqqi Muhammadin wa Aalihit Tahirin. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an aduwwahum ajma'in. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaykum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. I welcome all of you to this fourth session of the Mahdaviyat webinar. And I consider it necessary to say one important thing to all of you, that the support you have given so far and the encouragement you have provided, we are grateful to you from the bottom of our hearts for that. We are receiving a response and feedback much better than we expected, and we are getting the courage to implement your suggestions, and we are trying as much as possible. As some viewers and some audience members requested after the first session that if the summary of the discussion and debate that takes place during the session is presented, it would be beneficial for the Momineen. Therefore, we are now starting every session with a summary of the previous session. We hope that this is proving useful for you. We are grateful for your love and keep encouraging us with your support in this way. Criticism for the sake of reform is a good thing. Therefore, if you criticize us for any improvement and betterment, we will feel good. The summary of yesterday's discussion is something like this: that yesterday's topic was the second part of the characteristics of Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), in which these points came to light. First of all, when the discussion began, it started with how Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is the descendant of every Imam. That is, he is the ninth descendant of Imam Hussain (a.s.), the seventh descendant of Imam Baqir (a.s.), and similarly, the grandson of the tenth Imam and the son of the eleventh Imam, and there are numerous hadiths present in this regard. The second point discussed was briefly mentioning that he is the son of Janabe Narjis Khatoon (s.a.), who was a lady of high status and the daughter of the Caesar of Rome. This was mentioned briefly yesterday. Then the third point discussed was that Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is such that one of his characteristics is that it is found about him that he is 'Khafiyul Mawlid', meaning his birth will be hidden, just as the birth of Hazrat Musa (a.s.) was hidden. Then the next point discussed was that, according to the hadith of Amirul Momineen (a.s.), there will be a prolonged occultation (Ghaybah) for Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) in which people will be wandering here and there to find him and to seek guidance, and in which most people will go astray. Regarding his occultation, it was briefly mentioned that there were various kinds of misunderstandings among people about where Imam-e-Mahdi (a.s.) is. The book 'Kamaluddin wa Tamamun Ni'ma' was mentioned, in which Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) has discussed the occultation of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) in detail and has proven the Imam's occultation through the occultation of the Prophets. And then, according to the hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) is present at the Hajj every year. On the occasion of Hajj, the Imam is present in the House of Kaaba, and he sees people and recognizes them too, but people are unable to recognize him. Finally, regarding the Imam's house during the occultation, it was mentioned that even the name of the house where the Imam resides during the occultation is present in the hadiths, which is called 'Baytul Hamd'. We saw this hadith that the house whose name is Baytul Hamd, which is called Baytul Hamd. The name of the Imam's house is Baytul Hamd, and in that house, there is a lamp that has been burning since his birth and will continue to burn until his reappearance. Now let us move on to today's topic, and as you know, today, God willing, our topic is related to Hazrat Narjis Khatoon (s.a.) and the birth of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), and it is our good fortune that we have the honorable Maulana Syed Zulfiqar Mehdi Sahab Qibla present among us to shed more light on this topic. Assalamu Alaikum, Maulana Sahab. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. I hope you and your family are well, Maulana Sahab. Alhamdulillah, we are well. It is your kindness. How are you? Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, Maulana Sahab. It is your kindness that you joined us in this Mahdaviyat webinar, and we are confident that all our viewers will benefit from your speech. I request the viewers to recite a loud Salawat to welcome the Maulana. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. And finally, viewers, as always, the same request: you can send your questions via The Strong Row's WhatsApp number and through the question-and-answer chat box in Zoom. Recite Salawat for Muhammad and his family. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Bismillah, Maulana Sahab. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdulillahilladhi safa wa salamun ala ibadihilladhi nastafa Muhammadin wa alihi-tahirin. La siyyama al-Imamul Mubin Baqiyatullahi fil-ardhin al-Hujjatith-thani 'ashar. Al-Imamul Mahdi al-Muntazar salawatullahi wa salamun alayh. Before saying anything about the Bibi, I want to draw attention to a point. Then we will talk about our Princess and, I should say, our true and spiritual mother—just as the Imam is our guardian, the Proof of God, and the Master of Blessings, the greatness of his mother, his noble mother, is a source of pride for all of us. So, the point I want to point out first, and then start my discussion, is that Imamate is the name of a belief, and what we are going to talk about, the topic we want to present, we will mention it in front of you with reference to history. The belief in Imamate is a belief that... whose roots are found in the depths of the Quran and Hadith. And according to us Shias, it is 100% proven by the Quran and Hadith; there is no doubt, suspicion, or refutation in it. And one of the beliefs within that belief of Imamate is when we perform Ziyarat and say, 'Salam be upon you, O Imams, Kuntum talabish-shamikha wal-arhamil-mutahhara.' O my master, O my leader, O my Mawla, O my Imam, our peace be upon you. You are the ones who came into this world passing through pure loins, passing through high and great loins, and passing through pure wombs. So this is very clear, very evident that the one who is our Imam, his father is of very high status, and the mother is 'Tayyab-o-Tahir' (pure and clean). Now, whether it is mentioned in history or not, whether we have historical evidence or not, it makes no difference. When the Almighty God intends to bring an Imam into this world, God has the authority to choose the best vessel He wants, and through that, he comes into this world. Dear ones, I have seen five types of narrations about Bibi Narjis in books myself. But the one that is very famous and mentioned by Sheikh Saduq and Allama Majlisi—the role of Sheikh Saduq, the books of Sheikh Saduq, the greatness of Sheikh Saduq, the authenticity of his words, and on the other hand, the narration of Allama Majlisi—carries more weight because these people were very close to Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). So, those who were close did not write without reading or without research. Therefore, when we mention Bibi Narjis, we will generally quote from the books of Sheikh Saduq and Allama Majlisi. When we say that Bibi Narjis herself says that when Bashr ibn Sulayman went to Baghdad on behalf of Imam-e-Hadi (a.s.) to fetch her and handle the matter, the very sentence the Bibi said contains a point from which we can estimate when the Bibi was born. And from here the question will arise, in which city and where was she from? So, since the mention came up, let me mention here that there is an Eastern Rome and a Western Rome. There is a difference between the Eastern and the Western. The Eastern Rome, which was Alexandria or Istanbul, Turkey, and even Syria and some parts of Libya and Lebanon, was called 'Rumi Sharqi'. And the Western Rome was called the region of Italy and Spain, etc. The Bibi's connection is with Istanbul. And this was also called Rumi Sharqi. And the Bibi herself said that I was 13 years old when my grandfather, the Caesar of Rome, arranged my marriage to his brother's son, and then after that, the decorations... you were the granddaughter of the Emperor of Rome. Your father's name was Yeshua, and I have not seen the mention of your noble mother in the books. But it is said that she was also from the lineage of the disciples of Janabe Isa (a.s.). Now some people have mentioned Yeshua and some have mentioned different names. Anyway, I said earlier that it doesn't make much difference to us; for the recognition of the Bibi, it is enough to know that she was from a very great family on both her mother's and father's side. You were the granddaughter of the Emperor of Rome. On your mother's side, you were from the disciple of Janabe Isa, Yeshua or Yusuf—different names have been mentioned; perhaps in reading, it came as Yeshua with a 'seen', or with a 'sheen', or with a 'he', or with an 'alif'. So it can be read in many ways, how she was related to the disciples of Janabe Isa on her mother's side. Now some people have said that you were the cousin of Janabe Maryam, your father was a cousin. Anyway, so the Bibi said that my marriage was arranged at the age of 13. And it was decorated, and even the Bibi herself said that 300 nobles, 700 soldiers, and 4000 guests were invited, and the throne... in our time today, we can say that the wedding pavilion set up for the Bibi was studded with jewels, and when that grandson was brought and seated on the throne, and the priest started reading the Gospel, an earthquake occurred, and this pavilion was destroyed, and these priests lost their senses; they started trembling and shaking. They even told the Caesar of Rome that the sign we have seen makes us feel that Christianity is about to end, the name and trace of Christianity is about to be erased. The Bibi says that our grandfather said, 'Okay, if not this one, then get me married to his brother.' So it was done again in the same way, and the same incident happened again, so they all got scared, and our grandfather got up and went into the house and stopped talking to anyone. So, if you look at that, and on the other hand, I want to present a historical witness. The historian Masudi—who was Sunni, though some say Shia, but the Sunni historical accounts he wrote—mentions that a battle took place with the Romans. If you calculate, it was roughly between 45-46 AH and 53 AH. Right? This is the period when, if we look at history, this battle with Rome occurred. This is the era when the Lady (Bibi) came from there in disguise, under the pretext of treating the wounded, and placed herself among the slave girls by the command of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). When the Muslims were victorious, the Lady was taken captive along with those slave girls. When these slave girls were distributed, history records that they came into the possession of different people, and Umar ibn Yazid brought you to Baghdad. Right? He says this himself, I am the Imam's... Now, let us pause here and move to another aspect. It is said that on the night this incident occurred, when I went to sleep, I saw that in my house, on one side, Yeshua and Janab-e-Isa (Jesus) appeared, and on the other side, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) entered the house with his children following behind him into our palace. I want to point out a very subtle point here, and that point is that history says the Caesar of Rome had decorated a throne with 40 steps. It is said that the Lady says, 'Now, when Yeshua, Janab-e-Isa, and behind them the Prophet and his children all arrived...' Then Janab-e-Isa addressed Yeshua and said, 'This Prophet is the final Messenger, and he has brought a great honor for you, that he has come to ask for your daughter's hand, and this is an honor that has no substitute. It has come to you. Do you accept?' He said, 'Yes, yes, undoubtedly, I accept this great relationship.' And when the relationship was accepted, the Lady says, 'I saw that a pulpit was decorated, the height of which could not be seen even up to 40 steps.' It is said its height reached the heavens. Certainly, when the son of the Pride of the Universe is to be born from her womb, when a pulpit for the marriage contract is decorated for her, its height, greatness, spirituality, and essence cannot be measured by you or me; how great it must have been. Because it is said that one kept looking at its height until the end of the sky. The Prophet delivered the sermon, and it was answered, and this event vanished from my sight. When I woke up in the morning, I did not mention it to anyone, fearing that if I told them, I would be killed. I did not mention it to anyone. Now, I read in books that after 14 nights, four nights passed. The Lady says, 'I saw that Janab-e-Maryam (Mary) came to my house, and with her was a great lady whose majesty and awe left me stunned. Thousands of slave girls from heaven came with her. They visited our house, and Janab-e-Maryam addressed me and said, "Daughter, this is the mother of Abu Muhammad and your husband." Today, for whom there is a very beautiful sentence: "Daughter, you are her daughter-in-law. You are the daughter-in-law of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). This is your mother-in-law." As soon as she said this, grief filled my being, and I said in a complaining tone, "Lady, your son has married me, but he has not come to see me yet." The Lady looked at me and said, "Daughter, how can my son come to see you while you still remain in the religion of Christianity? You have not yet accepted the religion of Islam." Then the Lady said, "Daughter, accept the religion of Islam, and I will send my son to see you." It is said that after this, she recited the Shahadatain. 'Say, daughter: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah.' And after reciting the Kalima, she says, as soon as I recited it, she opened her arms, and I ran—although the narration does not explicitly say 'ran,' the tone suggests it was full of longing—and when she spread her arms, I ran and clung to her and embraced her. It is said that the way she embraced me, I felt a coolness in my being, and I expressed my complaint. The Lady said, "Daughter, today itself I will go and send my son to you." It is said that I saw this dream, and when morning came, there was a new freshness in my being. There was a new day in my being, a new blossoming, and that day I felt a different kind of joy. After that event, which is worth mentioning, I was becoming restless. So much so that my grandfather called every kind of physician, but I could not hide it. One day, my grandfather asked me, and I said to him, "I feel that if you stop torturing the Muslim prisoners, if you stop punishing them, perhaps Janab-e-Maryam and Isa will show us mercy." It is said that my grandfather stopped the oppression at my request, so I ate a little food the next day and showed some relief, and my grandfather was very happy and started treating them well. It is said that after that, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) would constantly come to see me. One day, when he came to visit me, I complained that you had not come to see me for so many days. The Imam gave the exact same answer that the Lady (Zahra) had given: "You remained in Christianity, that is why I did not come. Now that you have accepted Islam, I will come to see you every day until Allah provides the means for our public meeting." Then the Lady says that one day came when the Imam said, "The time has come for you to leave Rome and come to Samarra." And the Imam said to the Lady, "Look, tomorrow your grandfather is going to send an army to fight the Muslims. You, among the slave girls, wear such clothes and disguise yourself, mix yourself among them, and under the pretext that you are going to nurse the war-wounded, go with them. And it will happen that the Muslims will be victorious, and you will be taken captive." And then the Imam explained the whole situation, that you will be taken prisoner, and then when you are taken to that market, we will send our representative to you. Up to this point, the Lady says that she herself told this story to Bishr ibn Sulayman. Now listen from the other side, and then we will talk about some of the Lady's qualities. It is said that Bishr ibn Sulayman says it was night when the Imam's slave, Kafur, came to my door and knocked. After knocking, when I came out, I saw the Imam's slave was present. He said, "Imam Hadi (a.s.) has remembered you and has called for you now." I went there, went to the Imam's house, wore clothes, and went to the Imam's house. When I went to the Imam's house, I saw Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) there, and the tenth Imam, and in the narration, it is said that Janab-e-Hakima Khatoon was also present behind the curtain. I greeted the Imam and sat down. The Imam said, "O Bishr, you belong to the Ansar tribe. You have always been a lover of the Ahlulbayt and have always been loyal to the Ahlulbayt. We want to honor you with a great privilege. We want to bestow upon you a great honor because of the loyalty that has been found in your family until now." And then the Imam gave a purse of 220 dirhams—the color of the purse is also written as yellow. He gave it and wrote a letter in the Roman language. He sealed the letter and said, "Go to Baghdad, and on such and such a day, reach that bridge in Baghdad. When you reach that bridge, at that time, Umar ibn Yazid will bring the slave girls in a boat. You will see the people of Bani Abbas and some young men outside the bridge who have stood there to buy these slave girls. You search for Umar ibn Yazid among these sellers, and do not talk directly. First, observe the whole scene. See that he has a slave girl who is wearing two thick silk garments and is fully veiled, and she strictly forbids anyone who wants to see her, and she scolds them in her own language, saying, 'Stay away from me, do not come near me.' And you keep watching, keep watching until you see this scene, that the slave girl refuses whoever comes to buy her, saying, 'No, I will never accept being sold to you.' And at that time, you keep watching, keep watching until such a scene occurs, such a situation arises that she does not let anyone come near her and says, 'If anyone comes near me, I will give my life, your money will be wasted.'" At such a time, you go near her and... Say, 'You are saying that I will not agree to be sold to anyone until I know their character, their conduct, and their purity.' When you see this, you take this letter to her and say to the seller, 'Brother, look, I have brought a letter for her in the Roman language. The one who wrote this letter has written about his character, his conduct, and his nobility. Give it to them. If she wants to after reading this letter, then I will make the deal, and we will take her after the deal. And if she does not agree, then we will withdraw from this deal.' Umar ibn Yazid had been watching since morning that she was not agreeing at all. Once he said, 'You are right. Let's go.' When I said this, I went to the Lady with that letter and gave it to her. As soon as she took the letter and saw it, she started kissing it, until a stream of tears flowed from her eyes. When I saw this, she addressed Umar ibn Yazid and said, 'O Umar!' She said, 'Sell me to him, and apart from that, I will never accept being sold to anyone else. I would rather lose my life than accept such a thing. Now, you have no choice but to make a deal with him.' Umar ibn Yazid says that Bashar agreed to the amount the Imam had offered. I gave him the bag of money, took the lady, and left for Baghdad, to the place where I had arranged for my stay. I reached there with the lady, and she took out the letter, kissing it and pressing it to her eyes. I was astonished to see this scene. She kept kissing it. A girl who came as a captive from Rome, who had suffered so many hardships—history says she was 13 when she was married, and we have records that she married Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) at the age of 15, and at the age of 21, she departed from this world. Just think, at that age, when she saw such attachment, love, and affection for this letter, and she was expressing such restlessness, he asked, 'How do you know the owner of this letter? How do you know who he is? You haven't seen him yet, you haven't known him, and yet you are behaving like this with this letter.' The lady replied, 'How can you be one of the people of Wilayah? How can you be of Wilayah? Those who do not have an estimation of the greatness of the Imams, those who do not possess this true Wilayah, they cannot fathom what Wilayah is, what the reality of Wilayah is.' She said, 'You don't know, you don't understand, and how could you? Only those who have Ma'rifah (divine knowledge) can know. And if you want to know, I will tell you my story.' Bashar said, 'Yes, please tell me, I want to hear how you speak fluent Arabic while you belong to Rome, and where did you get such Ma'rifah regarding Imamate and Wilayah?' The lady said, 'What you are saying shows you cannot truly understand Wilayah and Imamate. The status of Imamate is very high. Now I will tell you my story.' She narrated the whole story of the marriage, then the meeting with Imam Hasan (a.s.), and then the whole incident of this letter from the tenth Imam, and said, 'Look, this is how I came out of that land of Kufr and Shirk under the banner of Tawheed.' After that, when she reached Samarra, Bashar ibn Sulayman says that he took her to the house of Imam Hadi (a.s.). The lady offered her Salam, and as soon as she did, the Imam replied and said—you should see the greatness of the lady here—as soon as she offered Salam, the Imam replied and said, 'If you wish, I can give you glad tidings, or if you wish, I can give you 10,000 dirhams.' The lady replied, 'I do not want 10,000 dirhams; I want you to give me the good news.' He said, 'God Almighty will grant you a son who will rule over the universe, and whose rule the world has never seen before.' Such a rule that the world has never seen until today. He will fill this world, which is filled with oppression, with justice and fairness, just as it has been filled with oppression and tyranny.' Then Imam Hadi (a.s.) said, 'Have you not seen how Allah has honored Islam and brought disgrace to Christianity?' Look at her Ma'rifah. What a beautiful sentence she said. She said, 'You know better than me. What can I tell you? How can I tell anything to a person who already has knowledge of all things?' You see what the lady's Ma'rifah regarding Imamate was. This is one thing, the second is Adab (etiquette). See, this is a great thing. I want to mention the Adab of the lady. The tenth Imam called his sister and Janabe Hakima Khatun and said to them, 'Sister, take her, take Narjis. Teach her the etiquettes of Islam. She is the one about whom he speaks, that she is the mother of our last Qaim, and she is the wife of our son Hasan al-Askari, from whom Allah will grant such a son.' The lady took her to her house. I want to mention two such things, so that one can realize what the lady's supreme quality was. In the Quran, Allah said about His Messenger—this sentence was also said by the Prophet, and it has come in his honor—the Prophet was saying, 'Ad-dabani Rabbi fa-ahsana ta'dibi' (My Lord taught me etiquette, and He taught me beautifully). And obviously, who can teach better etiquette than the One whom God teaches? He says, 'My etiquette is beautiful. I am a very well-mannered person.' So, Adab—I want to narrate another Hadith so you can estimate its greatness. History has written, there is a sentence in history, that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said to someone, 'If you were given two days of your life, if Allah told you that you have only two days left in your life, what would you do in those two days?' Now look, what does the Imam want to say to that narrator? The Imam said, 'If Allah informs you that two days of your life remain, what will you do in these two days?' He said, 'Mawla, you tell me.' So he said, 'I would tell you to spend one whole day learning Adab.' Do whatever you want for one day, but spend a whole day learning Adab. So you can estimate how much this Adab holds existence, how much value it has, that Allah says to His Messenger, and the Imam says, 'If Allah gives you two days of life, spend a whole day learning Adab.' Now, when she went there, Janabe Narjis herself says that when I went to their house—apparently, this is an incident after the marriage—when I went to the house of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and I met Narjis, the lady came forward and said, 'O our Princess, allow me to take off your shoes.' When Janabe Hakima Khatun saw this, she said, 'No, no, daughter, no. The truth is that I should take off your shoes. You are our Princess. You are the heir in this house...' ...who is going to be the leader of the universe. So in reality, I should have served you. You are my...' She said, 'No, you are an elder. Your respect holds a different status.' This is one incident; similarly, I want to mention another incident of Adab. You see, it is that on the night when Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) was born, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) had called his aunt. So she says that when I went to the house of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), when Janabe Narjis addressed me, she addressed me by saying, 'You are our Princess, Ya Sayyidati, I want to serve you. I want to serve you.' She says when Janabe Hakima heard this, she said, 'No, daughter. I have come to serve you, not to be served by you.' So you see the Adab—she is the mother of the Imam. She had come into that house, she was the granddaughter of the King of Rome, a princess. Despite that, when she came into the family of Ismah (infallibility), she had so much Adab that Janabe Hakima Khatun herself said in astonishment, 'No, daughter, you should not do this. I will serve you.' This is one point. Then, from that, I want to mention another quality before you, and let us talk about Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). I wanted to talk about a few objections. Perhaps time will be short, so I will leave that topic there. That in his Ziyarat, one finds a very strange sentence about Lady Narjis. And what is it? When we offer Salam, there is also a sentence of Salam in it: 'Our Salam be upon you, for you kept the secrets of Allah safe, and you nurtured your son very well.' It is said that Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) sent a message on the night of the 15th to Janabe Hakima Khatun, 'Mother, come to our house today. Because today, that child is coming into this world who is the Maw'ud al-Umam (the Promised One of the nations), whom Allah has promised to the whole world.' So the lady says I asked, 'From whom? From whom?' He said, 'From Narjis.' I said, 'Son, I do not see any signs of pregnancy.' He said, 'Aunt, stay. Do not be in a hurry.' The command of Allah is going to manifest today.' I saw a narration in 'Khisal' that Sheikh Saduq has recorded, that Janabe Hakima Khatun says I sat near the lady, near Lady Narjis, and saw she was sleeping peacefully. She was sleeping peacefully. She did not even turn, nor did I see any movement in her body. I kept watching carefully until it was almost morning, when suddenly I saw Janabe Narjis wake up with a start. When she woke up with a start, she says I embraced her, and when I embraced her, I said, 'Daughter, what is the matter?' She turned and said, 'Princess, I am feeling the signs of what the Imam had informed me about in my being.' She says just then, the voice of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) came, 'Aunt, recite Surah Inna Anzalna.' Although there are some other things in some narrations, I have seen this in the Tafsir 'Kashf al-Daqaiq', what is the virtue of Surah Inna Anzalna, it is mentioned there that he said, 'O Aunt, recite Surah Inna Anzalna.' She says I started reciting Surah Inna Anzalna. I was blowing on the lady after reciting Surah Inna Anzalna, when suddenly there was a distance between me and her. There was a veil, and then when the veil was removed, I saw a child who had his head on the ground, testifying, reciting Surah Inna Anzalna, and he greeted me, so I became frightened. This is found in that narration. The Imam came into this world, and when he came into this world, the Imam called out, 'Aunt, bring my child.' This is a brief incident. Now I want to know about one or two objections, and these objections are made by enemies today. The first objection is about the Imam's mother. They said, 'What war? When did the war happen? There was no war.' And that is why I said in the beginning, Masudi himself has said in history that there was a war between the Muslims and the Romans between 48 or 49 and 53. It is exactly the same time when the lady left her house and came here. Exactly that time. The second thing I want to say before you is that one objection is, 'Brother, she came as a captive, so why didn't the Romans demand her back later?' So let me mention in your presence that, look, what was brought from the Muslims—I said that there was an Eastern Rome and a Western Rome. The Eastern Roman Empire was devastated. The true Muslims devastated it. Now, those who were taken captive had no one to ask after them. Well, you should look at that too. Today, if any government remains, the demand is to exchange the prisoners. But when a government is finished, wiped out, and its traces are gone, then who will come and say, 'Return the prisoners'? So, this objection—my brother, an objection is raised where something still exists. When nothing remains, how can there be a demand? Certainly, there is no demand in that case. Another objection is about the name of the Lady (the mother of Imam Mahdi). What is the Lady's name? Narjis, Malika, Sawsan, Khamat, Saikal, or something else? In fact, in some places, it is even 'Muleka'. In some old books, 'Malika' or 'Malika'—whatever it may be—'Malika' or 'Muleka' has also appeared. And even the European historians have interpreted 'Muleka' in two ways. One interpretation is that she is the 'Sahib-e-Khat' (the one who possesses the letter). Now, you can translate this 'Khat-wali' as the one who received the Imam's letter, and thus a connection was established. That name, 'Muleka', was kept behind the veil of the unseen. One name that we understand from 'Malika' is 'Princess'. Today, European historians themselves have written that one meaning of 'Muleka' is the diminutive and feminine form, and just as 'Malik' was used for kings, 'Malika' or 'Muleka' was used for princesses. I have seen this in a narration by Fazl ibn Shadhan, where someone asked what the name of the Imam's noble mother would be, and Imam Rida (a.s.) gave five names. Just imagine. Now, why did he give five names? It is very clear. It is very logical. And what is that logical point? The logical point is that every person in the world, especially in the Islamic realm, knew that this is the Imam who will eradicate oppression and tyranny from the world. And one after another, hadiths were coming from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Hadiths were coming from the Imams: 'He will be my 12th successor.' Imam Husayn (a.s.) was saying, 'He will be my 8th.' The 10th Imam is saying, 'He will be the third after me.' Imam Hasan (a.s.) is saying, 'He will be my descendant.' Everyone knows this. So, why were they taking the 10th Imam to Samarra and keeping Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) in prison? What was the secret behind it? It was to keep them imprisoned in such a way that his existence would not be known outside. They wanted to extinguish the Light of God through their oppression. But Allah wanted to complete it. So, obviously, this could not be done by just one person. Unless this precaution was also taken regarding this mother. This was the arrangement of the Lord of the Worlds that the mother of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) came from Rome, and the Abbasid caliphs did not even get a hint of it. On the other hand, the Imams never called her by one name. Sometimes they called her Sawsan, sometimes Rehana, sometimes Narjis, sometimes Khamat, sometimes Saikal. What does this mean? So that those who are searching, who are plotting, their plots can be made unsuccessful. This was a brief history I have read before you. This history was about the noble mother of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and the birth of the Imam (a.s.). I have mentioned a few objections very briefly before you. And our final prayer is praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. I am ready to hear your objections. Please, if there is any objection or question, please state it. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. There are no objections, but there are some questions. Yes. Speak. Well, Alhamdulillah, there are two or three questions. And two of them are quite similar. Mr. Qasim Syed has asked via WhatsApp. Saif Haider Sahib has asked the same question via Zoom. 'Please throw some light on the family of Imam-e-Zamana, his wife, his children.' Are there any narrations regarding the marriage and children of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) himself? Look, we have only one narration, which is about the Green Island (Jazirat al-Khadra). Because it is a 'Khabar-e-Wahid' (solitary report), and I have seen it in one place. Now, as far as I remember, in the first or second volume of 'Qarib al-Ihsan', where he mentions the meeting with the Imam, he also mentions his government and his children. But to say with certainty—we read this sentence in some Ziyarat (pilgrimages) and some supplications. But for us to say with certainty who the Imam's wife is and who his children are—I said that Allama Majlisi has narrated a tradition. But since it is a solitary hadith, we cannot say with certainty, although that narration exists. Yes. Hear your second question. Besides this, the second question, Maulana Sahib, is this, and it has also come via WhatsApp: 'Are there any records of the life of Janabe Narjis Khatoon (s.a.) after the birth of Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)?' That is, after the birth of Imam-e-Zamana, regarding his mother's life—we have two narrations. One narration is that if the Imam was born in 255 AH, and I said in this speech that the Lady was married to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) at the age of 15, and she passed away/was martyred at the age of 21. Now think, the Imam was born in 255. The Imam was born in 255. And some history says that the Lady passed away during the lifetime of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Some say, no, the Lady passed away after the Imam's death. After the Imam's martyrdom, the Lady passed away. So, what we find in history is that after the Imam's birth, those tyrant kings, the Abbasid kings, put Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) back in prison. So, at that time, the Lady took all the responsibility upon herself, and you find a little bit in history that she—as I said in the Ziyarat, this sentence is found in the Ziyarat: 'You protected the secret of God.' Now, 'protecting the secret of God' means that the Imam is not there, the Imam is in prison, and the upbringing, guardianship, and nurturing of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) were kept secret by the Lady. She made arrangements in this way. The other one is a sentence from the same Ziyarat: 'Qad ahsanta al-kifalah' (You performed the guardianship in the best way). This shows that during the Imam's occultation, the Lady protected her child in this way. After that, I saw in a history that when the Imam was martyred, the Lady was taken prisoner and kept at the house of the Qadi al-Qudat (Chief Justice) at that time. Until the Lady passed away. This is as much as we have in history regarding the Lady's passing. So, regarding her life after the Imam's birth, we do not have details. If you ask, for example, if the Imam was born in 255, to tell the history of every month, every day, or every week, that history is not available to us. It is a matter of great regret, and perhaps the reason is that history—like today is the age of social media, it was not like that in that era. In that era, the kings themselves would have history written, and they would have it written as they wished. One reason why the history of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) could not come down to us in detail is that the enemies of the Ahlulbayt wrote the history. We have received most things through them. It has happened very rarely that when the Imams were asked later and the Imams clarified, a few things came out. Otherwise, you do not get the full history about the Lady. Thank you, Maulana Sahib. Since you also mentioned the Green Island, Maulana Sahib, there is a question related to this. 'What is the story behind the Bermuda Triangle, that is, Jazirat al-Khadra? What is the reality of this?' Look, only Allah knows the reality. If you want to obtain information, there is a book available in English by the name of 'Bermuda Triangles'. There is a book in Urdu by the name of 'Jazire Bermuda'. There is a book in Arabic. There is a book in Persian. So, you should read about it yourself. I said that since Allama Majlisi has mentioned a narration and has mentioned it in great detail, Allama Majlisi did it. Later, various things are said about it, but we do not have any authentic hadiths. Yes, we consider it a possibility; we do not deny it. But if you ask us if the Mawla is there, I will say no. The Imam will not be there. The reason is that in the occultation, wherever the Imam is, he will not be in one place. Okay? It is possible that his children are there. I am not saying that they are not. It is possible that his children are there, but I cannot say that the Imam is there. That is, Maulana Sahib, if only clarification is sought, then Allama Majlisi (r.a.) has certainly narrated this in Bihar al-Anwar. It is a 'Khabar-e-Wahid', it is a hadith. It cannot be denied at all. No, we are not denying it. I said it could be a possibility. But how can I say it with certainty? You also cannot say it with certainty. This 'Khabar-e-Wahid' only brings a conjecture. We can say a little above a possibility that the Mawla, obviously, the world is in his hands; wherever he wants to live, he is the master and authority. If he wants to be in Mumbai, then even if the whole world wants to find him while he is in Mumbai, they cannot find him. And this could be a place in Mumbai that is like Paradise. We cannot say. He is the master and authority. And what Allama Majlisi mentioned, that a man was called by the Imam and he went through them and saw this and that, it is present. Denying that is not denying the hadith, and Allama Majlisi was also a scholar who would not write without any research or investigation. That is true. There is room for one last question, Maulana Sahib. Please. The question is like this, it has come from two or three sources. Regarding Ahmad al-Yamani, 'Is Ahmad al-Yamani related to Imam-e-Zamana? How far is the claim of Ahmad al-Hasan right?' Look, among the signs found regarding Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), there is a mention of these Yemenis. There is a mention of the army of the Yamani. What our scholars have considered as a possibility is that this Yemen is the same Yemen that is Yemen today, that is the part. Okay? But that particular personality, that 'this is the Ahmad al-Yamani'—that I should raise my finger and say 'this is him'—no one has the right to interpret that. We can say about the signs that the reappearance (Zuhur) does not depend on the signs, my brother. Whether the signs exist or not, the reappearance of the Imam is certain. These signs existing—it is possible they happen, it is possible they do not. For example, we have this narration that even the definitive signs, as the Imam said, this is certain... It will be full. Someone asked the Mawla about it, 'Can there be a Bada (change in divine decree) in this?' He said, 'Yes, it can happen.' Okay? So my brothers, we are waiting for the Imam, we are not waiting for the signs. Yes, among the signs that have been mentioned, it is also mentioned that there will be many from the Mani, the Lashkar-e-Mani, and many companions of the Imam from Yemen. There will also be many helpers of the Imam. There is no doubt about that. They will be there. Insha'Allah, they will be there. Thank you, Maulana Sahab. Our time is up. We are wholeheartedly grateful to the honorable Maulana Sahab. May Allah keep you all safe and happy. Thank you very much. And may He grant you further ability to serve the Imam. Ilahi Ameen. Even if this service is small. At the very least, through this service, we can tell the Mawla that we are your loyal ones. We do think about you, even if it is just a little. And Insha'Allah, if a small service is accepted, then it is a matter of honor and pride. Insha'Allah, you pray for me, and I pray for you all. May Allah include you all among the servants of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), the helpers of Imam-e-Zaman, those who pave the way for the Imam, and include you all in the prayers of the Imam. Ilahi Ameen. And may He keep us all safe from these calamities and afflictions. Ilahi Ameen. Insha'Allah. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. We are grateful to Maulana Sahab. And all the viewers are also grateful to you for joining us. Tomorrow, Insha'Allah, our discussion, that is, the topic 'The Creed of Mahdaviyat in the Light of the Holy Quran and Hadith', will continue. Insha'Allah, tomorrow's topic will be related to the Imam's Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra), and I am extremely happy that tomorrow, Insha'Allah, the honorable Maulana Abu Talib Taba-Tabai Sahab will join us. So, I request all viewers to stay with us tomorrow at this same time, 10:30 PM India time, and subscribe to our channel. When the session ends and the videos are uploaded, you must watch them and circulate these videos among your friends and relatives. Let us all pray together at the end that the Almighty Allah hastens the luminous reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). May He count us among his sincere slaves and may the shadow of the true scholars (Ulama-e-Haq) always remain over our heads. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal an a'da'ahum ajma'in.

title: Ziyaarat-e-Imam Husain (a.s.): Mukammal Khair | Watch 👆 Full Video | Majlis 01 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the profound spiritual significance of Ziyarat-e-Imam Husain (a.s.) based on a Hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The lecture highlights that when Allah desires absolute goodness for a believer, He instills a deep love for Imam Husain and his Ziyarat within their heart. Consequently, attending Majalis-e-Aza is presented as a manifestation of this divine favor and a source of immense blessings.
content:
So, a Hadith came from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Now, pay attention to the words of the Hadith: 'Man aradallahu bihi al-khayr.' In Arabic, see, those who are familiar with Arabic know that when 'al' (the definite article) comes, it means 'all goodness,' everything—this is called 'istighraq' in Arabic terminology. Meaning, all the goodness—when Allah wants all goodness for someone, without any exception, when Allah wants such goodness for someone that nothing of goodness remains, 'qadhafi qalbihi hubba al-Husain wa ziyaratihi'—He places the love of Husain and the love of his Ziyarat in his heart. So, consider these Majalis-e-Aza as a great blessing.

title: Ahle Bait (a.s.) Azaadaari Kaise Karte Thay? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical practice of Azadari (mourning) for Imam Husayn (a.s.) as demonstrated by the Ahl al-Bayt. The speaker narrates a tradition involving Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) and the poet Jafar ibn Affan to illustrate the spiritual significance of reciting elegies. The talk emphasizes that weeping and organizing mourning gatherings are acts of devotion that lead to divine forgiveness and Paradise.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Master of the Age, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Zayd ibn Shaham states that a group of us from Kufa was present in the service of Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) when Jafar ibn Affan arrived. The Imam (a.s.) called Jafar to him and asked, 'O Jafar! We have heard that you recite elegies (marsiya) for our grandfather Imam Husayn (a.s.)?' Jafar said, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, yes, Mawla.' The Imam (a.s.) said to him, 'Recite.' So Jafar recited the elegy. Upon hearing the elegy, the Imam (a.s.) began to weep, and all those present there also began to weep, and the Imam (a.s.) wept so much that his cheeks and noble beard became wet with tears. Then the Imam (a.s.) said, 'O Jafar! By God, the closest angels of Allah were present here, listening to your elegy for Imam Husayn (a.s.). They also wept just as we are weeping, and those angels wept a great deal, and O Jafar!' Verily, Allah Almighty has made Paradise obligatory for you at this very moment and has forgiven you.' The Imam (a.s.) asked, 'O Jafar! Should I tell you more?' Jafar said, 'Certainly, my master.' Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Ma min ahadin qala fil-Husayni shi'ran fabaka wa-abka bihi illa awjaballahu lahul-jannata wa ghafara lahu' (There is no one who recites poetry for Husayn and weeps, or causes others to weep, but that Allah makes Paradise obligatory for him and forgives him). Whoever recites an elegy for Imam Husayn (a.s.) and weeps himself or becomes the cause of others weeping, the Lord of the Worlds makes Paradise obligatory for him and forgives his sins. From this Hadith, it becomes clear that arranging Azadari in homes, reciting elegies, and weeping was a method of Azadari for the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) that we inherited from them. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He grants us the ability to organize gatherings for Imam Husayn (a.s.), perform Azadari, and weep in our homes, Imambargahs, and mosques as much as possible. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Bait-e-Tat'heer Par Kitni Baar Hamla Hua? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture details the historical accounts of the three separate attacks on the house of Bibi Fatima (s.a.) following the demise of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The speaker references various historical texts to describe the pressure exerted upon Imam Ali (a.s.) to pledge allegiance and the tragic events that unfolded at the door of the Princess. The narrative emphasizes the disregard shown by the oppressors toward the sanctity of the Prophet's household.
content:
That regarding the matter of the Princess (Fatima s.a.), there is not one, not two, but three attacks that we find. Where people gathered at the house of the Princess to take allegiance from Ali (a.s.)... the first time when people gathered at the Princess's house and demanded forced allegiance from Ali (a.s.), and all the Banu Hashim were arrested. This incident is present in the book 'Masail' not just on page 139. It is found that when all the Banu Hashim were arrested, they were told that just as others have pledged allegiance, you should also pledge allegiance, otherwise, by God, swords will be drawn against you. After this, the second attack happened when Imam (a.s.) refused to pledge allegiance due to his preoccupation with compiling the Holy Quran. At that time, a tyrant said, 'See, if he comes out of the house, then put this house with those inside it on fire.' When someone said to that tyrant, 'But in this house, Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), is present, and her signs are present.' Her signs are present [Music]—but it had no effect on that tyrant, and in response, he said, 'I do not care.' When these two attempts to take allegiance from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) failed, then Qunfudh, who was a slave, was sent with this message: 'Go to their house and order them to come out and pledge allegiance. If they agree, then fine, otherwise gather wood and fire, and tell them that if they do not come out and pledge allegiance, the whole house will be burned with them inside.' This matter is mentioned in 'Tarikh-e-Tabari' and many books, and it is in his book 'Al-Jamal' on page 117. But if we look at the third and final attack, this incident is mentioned in the 53rd volume of 'Bihar al-Anwar' on page 18, and 'Hadiqah al-Shia' on page 30. It is mentioned that people not only entered the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), they also... it is found that at the door of Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.)... At the door of Zahra (s.a.), people knocked loudly, pushed it with extreme force, and it is mentioned that when Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.) remained standing in her house, the tyrant's sentences are heart-wrenching. This tyrant says, 'We have no love or relationship between us anymore.' When they brought Janabe Ali (a.s.), they said, 'If you want, send them out so they can pledge allegiance, otherwise, we will burn everyone.'
There were three distinct attempts to force Imam Ali (a.s.) to pledge allegiance.
The first attack involved the arrest of the Banu Hashim to coerce their submission.
The second attack involved a direct threat to burn the house while the Prophet's daughter was inside.
Historical sources like 'Bihar al-Anwar' and 'Tarikh-e-Tabari' document these events.
The tyrant explicitly disregarded the status of Bibi Fatima (s.a.) when ordering the fire.
The final assault involved the forceful entry and the tragic events at the door of the house.

title: Muharram 1442 Urdu Majlis #09: Hasad (Jealousy) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the spiritual dangers of Hasad (jealousy) and Takabbur (pride) within the context of Islamic ethics. The speaker emphasizes that these traits are destructive to faith and originate from a lack of self-recognition and trust in divine justice. By contrasting destructive envy with Ghibta (positive emulation), the lecture encourages believers to focus on their own spiritual growth and service to the Ahlulbayt. The discourse is framed by the tragic events of Karbala, using the sacrifices of the Prophet's family as a catalyst for reflection and spiritual purification.

Light the fire of jealousy, and when this happens among them, then 'Fasad' (corruption) and the second thing, 'Bagha' (rebellion/aggression), will happen. There should be a spirit of harming one another. There should be a spirit of harming one another. So what happens? They will be destroyed. This is not Allah's force, this is Iblis's. We also think that this blessing will not come to us by our wishing, it will not come by our wishing. It is a blessing given by Allah. It will not come by our wishing. Do one thing, complain about him in this department, do it there, so that he gets worried. He will be so worried that his mental balance will start to deteriorate, his health will get spoiled, he will go crazy. So keep complaining about him constantly. Stand two or four people against him, stand your own people so that they go against him. So Iblis constantly whispers. Anyway, he was clever. You all know that. After that, he has a test.
