So he gets new ideas, new ways to harm the person in front, the one who is called 'Mahsud' (the envied). So how to harm the envied? That is why in the Holy Quran it is said: 'Wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad' (And from the evil of the envier when he envies). Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. 'Qul a'udhu birabbil-falaq, min sharri ma khalaq, wa min sharri ghasiqin idha waqab, wa min sharrin-naffathati fil-'uqad, wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad.' It is in the Quran that when someone envies, then you seek refuge in Allah from... Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of that envier. It is such a dangerous thing. And when they do magic, make knots, and throw them in the well, then 'A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir rajim'. So it is more than that. That is why in the narrations it is found that Iblis... you know how much discussion there is about Shaitan. In Al-Kafi, in volume 2, from page 131 to 310, there is a long discussion about Iblis. You can check it. From page 131 to 136, there are constant hadiths about Iblis. He is such a dangerous enemy that you should keep seeking refuge from his evil. The Imams (a.s.) say that when you wake up in the morning, seek refuge from Iblis. When you leave the house, seek refuge from Iblis. When you go to the toilet, seek refuge from Iblis. When you ride a vehicle, seek refuge from Iblis. When you get off the vehicle, seek refuge from Iblis. This is a very dangerous thing. This jealousy, this is a very dangerous thing. That is why in the narrations we... This is a very dangerous thing. That is why in the narrations we talk about the 'evil eye'. This is superstition, consider this superstition, this is very dangerous. But there are narrations about superstition. In Al-Kafi, there is a whole chapter called 'Bab al-Ayn' (Chapter on the Evil Eye). This is the evil eye, and some people have such an eye that if they look at someone... it is present in the hadith. It is a narration that some people were such that when they looked at a camel with a jealous eye, it would go a little further and fall and die. It is a dangerous thing, and it exists even today. So do not envy people. Why? Because this is Iblis's trap, and we should not become one with him. Never envy anyone. Anyway, this work, this jealousy, takes a person out of the circle of faith. The hadith says: 'Al-hasadu ya'kulul-imana kama ta'kulun-naru al-hatab' (Jealousy eats faith just as fire eats wood). This hadith is from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). 'Al-hasadu ya'kulul-imana kama ta'kulun-naru al-hatab.' Be kind to those who are lower than you in rank. Never show pride in front of those who are lower than you. And after that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'And do not envy those who are above you.' Do not envy them. 'Al-hasadu ya'kulul-imana kama ta'kulun-naru al-hatab.' Jealousy eats faith just as fire eats wood. Why does it eat faith? Because for a believer, he sees a blessing, and he envies it. The fire of jealousy ignites in his heart, and the good deeds start burning. If the good deeds burn, then what should we do? We are worshipping, reading prayers, and we are suffering, we are doing patience, but actually, in our hearts, we have jealousy for our brother. Why is this person like this? Why is he like that? If someone has something, why is it given to him? Whoever Allah gives, whoever He gives, look... Whoever He gives, whoever He gives, look. There was a man, Muhammad bin Abi Bakr. There were two brothers in history. One was named Muhammad bin Abi Bakr and the other was Umar bin Abi Bakr. Muhammad was a very devoted follower of Imam Ali (a.s.). He loved him very much. And the incident that happened, remember the name, Muhammad bin Abi Bakr, and his brother, who was... anyway, jealousy was there. And the king, Muawiyah, was in our time, in the time of the Imam (a.s.). These two brothers, in the time of the Imam (a.s.), there was so much complaint. The king said, 'Go and bring him as a prisoner.' What did this brother do? Muhammad bin Abi Bakr, he took the whole troop and went to the house of the Imam (a.s.), started searching the house, unveiled the women, and leveled false accusations against the Imam (a.s.) which cannot be described. He unveiled the women and was bringing the Imam (a.s.) as a prisoner. And when he was looking, he had brought him from Medina, and now he was bringing him to the Levant. So when the troop stopped for a while to rest, this brother... When they stopped to rest, this person began to taunt the Imam. What taunt did he give? It is in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 50, page 66. He began to taunt him, saying, 'You claim that you have knowledge of the unseen, and you claim to know what is in the hearts of people. Do you really claim this?' The Imam replied to his taunt by asking, 'Tell me, if today I were to decide to give you knowledge of the unseen, could I give it to you? If Allah does not allow it, I cannot give it. But if Allah allows it, I can give it. Even if it is something as small as a deer, if Allah allows, I can give it. At the very least, you would acknowledge that we are more honorable in the sight of Allah than that deer, and that Allah loves us more than that. There is no doubt that you would acknowledge this.' He presented this logic and reasoning before him. This is something that completely destroys a person; it takes them outside the boundaries of religion and faith. If jealousy and envy take root, no matter how much a person prays, it will be of no use. If the fire of jealousy is burning in their heart, they will complain and plot against others. This is why the remedy for this is that whenever a believer feels jealousy towards someone, they should immediately remember Allah, because jealousy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood. Therefore, this is sufficient. Therefore, this is a sign of those who cannot tolerate seeing others succeed. They cannot bear anyone else's progress. They start finding faults in others. If someone has been blessed by Allah with wealth, they start thinking, 'Why did Allah give it to him? May Allah punish him.' This is why there is a tradition where the Imam says that jealousy is a disease that consumes one's faith. For example, if there is someone very powerful in front of you, and you... If there is someone very powerful in front of you, and you are jealous of them, wishing for their downfall—this happens in elections and in positions of power. People used to do this to Bahadur Shah Zafar. But the most dangerous thing is when those closest to you are jealous. Bahadur Shah Zafar had two sons-in-law who were very jealous. They hid his sons from the British and didn't tell anyone where they were hiding. Only they knew. They took money from the British and revealed where they were hiding. The British caught them, killed them, and brought their heads to Bahadur Shah Zafar as a 'gift'. When he uncovered the cloth, he saw his sons' heads, and the King recited a quatrain. The King recited a quatrain: 'The city has become empty of the noble ones; the low-born have become the leaders. Those who were once considered insignificant have now become great.' He spoke of the changing times and the depths of human betrayal, which cannot be fully described. This is the result of jealousy. If you see someone who has reached a high status, do not use such phrases. A believer is one who protects the honor and dignity of another believer. If someone is jealous, the Imam says that jealousy imprisons your soul. It restricts your soul so that it cannot fly. Your thoughts become small, your perspective becomes narrow. You will think about them in the morning, in the afternoon, and in the evening. You will be obsessed with what they ate, what they drank, and what they wore. Your entire existence will become confined. Free yourself from this, because this jealousy is the root of corruption. This jealousy is the root of corruption, and it causes evil and sins. Who can understand this? When there is jealousy, it leads to corruption. The Quran says in Surah An-Nisa, verse 54: 'Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?' We gave the family of Ibrahim the Book and Wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom. We gave them everything that a person could desire. We gave them everything. This was given by Allah. So, if we have jealousy in our hearts, we are essentially wishing for Allah's blessings to be destroyed. We are questioning why Allah gave them these things. This is very dangerous. Do not envy what Allah has given to others from His bounty. And do not cast your eyes longingly at what others have. Do not look at what others have, because you do not know how they acquired it. It might be through haram means, or it might be a test from Allah. That very thing might be the cause of their destruction. Do not look at their blessings; look at your own soul and do not put it in distress. Allah gave them what He gave them. You should pray that Allah gives you similar blessings. This is called 'Ghibta' (emulation), which is different from 'Hasad' (jealousy). There was a companion of the Imam who was a scholar from Khorasan. He had written 160 books. When he met the Imam, the Imam asked him about the people of Khorasan. He replied that they were doing well. The Imam then said, 'Tell the people of Khorasan that I envy them because they have a man like you among them.' In other words, having scholars like him is a blessing. How can we build ourselves today? How can we make ourselves such that Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) considers us his own? There is a story about this. It is said that there was a merchant in India who loved the Imam (a.t.f.s.) very much. He was very devoted, and every year he would go to the pilgrimage. He would take a lot of money with him, and when he reached the Imam's presence, he would give all that money to him. This story is mentioned in a very famous book. The book is about the people who were fortunate enough to meet the Imam (a.t.f.s.). The author of this book has recorded these accounts. So, what happened? The merchant was the host, and he became worried, 'Where has he gone?' He was not found anywhere. He was searching for him everywhere, and he was very distressed. He was distressed and was in India. When he could not find him anywhere, he became worried. He went to a scholar and said, 'I used to go to my Master, the Imam (a.t.f.s.), from India. I used to take gifts and offerings for him, but now I cannot find him. What should I do?' The scholar said, 'Do one thing. Ask the Imam (a.t.f.s.) himself. Go to the shrine of Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) and Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) in Samarra. Go and ask them; they will tell you what happened.' The merchant was worried, 'What if I go there and cry, and he is not there? What will I say? He was my host, and I have received so much from him.' He was reading this famous book while crying. Suddenly, a man came to him and said, 'My host, the Imam (a.t.f.s.), has sent me to you. He says that he was such a good man, and he had so much love for the Imam (a.t.f.s.) that we have kept him with us. You people of this world were not worthy of him being among you, so we have taken him with us.' You know that there are traditions about the companions of the Imam (a.t.f.s.). In every era, there are 30 people who are his companions, whom he calls 'Mawali' (my masters). He stays with them always and keeps teaching them. When he recites the Quran and explains its interpretation, these 30 people are present before him, whom he teaches. These 30 people are very close to the Imam (a.t.f.s.). Regarding these people, it is said that we are envious of them because such personalities are present among them. And that is why Allah says, 'Does he envy people for what Allah has given them out of His bounty?' The one who is jealous, the one who burns with envy, is angry at the blessings of others. And the one who is jealous of what I have distributed, of the share I have given to others, is trying to stop it. In the Quran, Allah says, 'Are they the ones who distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world.' Who are they to ask? Who are they to distribute? I swear by Allah, whatever I have distributed among My servants, whoever does this, whoever acts like this, he is not from Me, he is not among them, and he is not one of those who are jealous of others' blessings. He is not one of those who are jealous of others' blessings. If someone hears the news that such-and-such a person has faced a calamity, and they feel happy or smile, it means that Satan is residing in their heart. If there is jealousy in a person, he cannot be a believer. He cannot be a leader or a guide for the people. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) wants to say that the one who acts with jealousy can never be a leader of the people. A leader is one who is always ready to take responsibility. You can see who a leader is; if his team does well, he gives credit to the team, and if the team makes a mistake or suffers a loss, he takes the responsibility himself. And if a member of the team rises, he is happy. We will read about this later, Insha'Allah, Imam Ali (a.s.) says... You will read later, Imam Ali (a.s.) says that the levels of faith are like stairs. Just as there are stairs, the Imam (a.s.) says that there are levels of faith. So, what should one do? The one who is at the second level should help the one at the first level to come up. He should bring him up with love. He should not say, 'Let him stay there.' No, help him. If any of your employees or anyone is rising, or if someone is coming up in any field, help them rise. And then, do not think, 'This is not our group, this is not our person.' Because it happens that when we see someone at the second level of faith, and we see someone at the first level, we think of kicking them down so they cannot rise. If the second one kicks the first one down, the third one will kick the second one down. This is Allah's system. It may not happen immediately, but it will happen eventually. This is Allah's system. Therefore, it is narrated that you should never be friends with a jealous person. Do not befriend him. If you can change him, do so; otherwise, stay away from him. Why? Because he is dangerous. He will transfer the jealousy that is in his heart to you. He will ignite a fire in your heart. He will keep talking negatively about others. If you listen to him, that same jealousy will enter your heart. He will keep criticizing others. And we should try to be like the companions of the Imam (a.t.f.s.). The companions used to promote others because they were presenting them to the Imam (a.t.f.s.). They used to promote them. They would compete in doing good, but they were never jealous. And if someone is jealous, understand that he is outside the circle of religion and faith. There are many other things, but time is very short. Always pray, 'O Allah, if You have made me a follower, I am not a jealous person.' Always thank Allah, 'O Lord, thank You for making me a follower, for keeping me away from jealousy.' Every person whom Allah has blessed with a gift—someone has the gift of wealth, someone has the gift of knowledge, someone has the gift of status—everyone has been given some blessing by Allah. Whatever He has given, the requirement of that blessing is to be grateful. There are many other things, but always remember, there are many needy people. Keep giving charity, but first of all, give charity to the Imam (a.t.f.s.) because he is the most deserving. Give charity to the Imam (a.t.f.s.) first because he is the most deserving. He is the most needy of all. The Quran says about them that they are in need. Therefore, give charity to the Imam (a.t.f.s.) first. This will have two benefits. First, the love for the Imam (a.t.f.s.) in your heart will increase. Many people object, 'Why give charity to the Imam? Is he in need of our charity?' He is not in need of our charity; this is a sign of our love. We love our Imam, so we pray for his well-being. Otherwise, it is written, 'If you help Allah, Allah will help you.' Is Allah in need of your help? No, Allah is not in need of your help, but by helping, you become elevated. Similarly, by giving charity for the Imam (a.t.f.s.), love for him increases in your heart. So, give charity, at least once a month. Even if it is a small amount, give it. It doesn't matter if it's one, two, or five rupees. Give it. And for whom we give charity, his life changes. If he is not a follower, he becomes one. He becomes a blessed person. This Imam (a.t.f.s.), for whom you give charity, will surely bless you with spiritual blessings, even if you don't get worldly wealth. And keep this in mind, this is an experienced thing. So, definitely do this. And the greatest blessing for which you should always pray is that Allah keeps us on the path of the Imam (a.t.f.s.) until our last breath. We should keep him in our prayers. We should perform good deeds for him. Because the Imam (a.t.f.s.) prays for everyone. Allah gives him the power. Even if you perform many deeds, if your heart is not clean, it will not be effective. Either the speaker is not effective, or the listener is not ready. One of the two is the problem. The speaker is the one who is talking about the Imam (a.t.f.s.), and he has willed that when I die, this shroud should be kept in Muharram, in which I used to weep. Keep this handkerchief in Muharram, I used to weep with it; keep it with my shroud because it is my intercession. This handkerchief wiped the tears of the oppressed, and it will be the cause of my salvation. I have no other means of salvation. This is the only hope. When you understand that I have died, open it. When the great ones died, they were very great, and the chador, and the head of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—what can be said about them? Why is this crying important? This Karbala, this weeping, this mourning—as we see it, it is all becoming pink. I am sacrificing everything. The mothers are sacrificing their sons. All these youths were martyred. The Imam (a.s.) raised his voice in distress: 'Is there anyone to help us? Is there anyone to help the family of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)?' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Is there anyone who will help us? Is there anyone who will defend the harem of the Prophet?' Then a commotion broke out in the second stage. Someone came near the Imam and whispered something in Asghar's ear. I don't know what he said or what the child understood, but it is written that Asghar came into the lap of the Imam. Hussain (a.s.) started walking. Rubab was standing there. Hussain asked, 'Rubab, why are you standing?' She said, 'I am standing because whoever went to the battlefield since morning has not returned.' I have done everything for him so far, but a six-month-old child does not fight. Hussain brought the child and said, 'There is no one to give water to this child in Islam.' Someone asked, 'Is there any life left in him?' Look at the condition of my child. Someone replied, 'Hussain, the third question is, how is he breathing?' He said, 'When you take a fish out of water, it gasps for breath.' Then the matter came to the fore. Then the matter came to the fore. Hussain was the manifestation of the truth. The enemy pulled out a three-headed arrow. The archer shot the arrow. The child was thirsty. Hussain says that the child had already flown to the heavens. 'Do not be afraid, Hussain.' Hussain said, 'O Messenger of Allah, O Hussain, O Hussain.' The child has left the world. Why keep the mother deprived of the last glimpse? Hussain came and reached the other side first. 'O brother, he is not there.' Hussain recited a dirge: 'Are children like you also slaughtered?' Remove the troubles of the believers. Protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. May Allah grant them the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Lord of the Worlds, I asked the family of the Prophet (a.s.) one day, 'How did the days pass for you?' They started crying and said... They started crying and said, 'O Sham, O Sham.' They started sobbing and said, 'What is the matter? My martyrdom is my honor.' Is there any justice? My martyrdom is the cause of the salvation of the past and the future. My sisters' veils were snatched. What happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. How am I alive? I live moment by moment, I do not die. What these eyes have seen, what happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. Yes, in the beginning, I was in grief. The veils of the sisters were removed. What happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) cloak was torn, and stones were rained down. The face was covered in blood. What happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. The grief of the tragedy killed me. What happened to my family? The grief of the tragedy killed me. What happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. The killer was sitting on the chest. What happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry. Go to the streets of Sham, where the pain remains. What happened to my family? O Sham, O Sham, do not cry, do not cry.

title: EP12 | Aqeedah -e- Raj'at | ⛅  Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉 #ImamMahdiعج
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological concept of Raj'ah, the belief in the return of specific individuals, including the Imams and past oppressors, to this world prior to the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that this belief is a fundamental tenet of Shia Ithna Ashari faith, supported by Quranic verses and the interpretations of the Ahlul-Bayt. The session also serves as the conclusion to the 'Panaah-e-Kainaat' mega quiz, highlighting the spiritual significance of waiting for Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and the restoration of divine justice.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. The link for the quiz is now live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. You have to answer all the questions correctly. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer. There is no prize for answering first. The only condition for the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. Among all those who have answered all the questions correctly, the winners of today's episode will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system at the end of the program. But if your name is not among today's winners or if you missed an episode, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the pilgrimage to Iraq, will be selected from those who have answered all the questions correctly in seven out of the 12 episodes. If you have given correct answers in seven out of the ten episodes—meaning even if someone did not become a daily winner, but has given correct answers in seven out of the twelve episodes—then all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. A'udhu billahi sami'il 'alim minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal-Hujjatibni-Hasan, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis-sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma walli kullal-faraj, waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi, wa la taj'alna mimman yudda'u Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. For this final episode of the mega quiz regarding the sanctuary of the universe, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), the topic selected to be presented before you is such an important topic that it relates to... ...is such an important topic that it relates to our belief, and that topic is Raj'ah. First of all, if we want to enter into this topic, we must understand its meaning and concept. What is the literal meaning of Raj'ah? It comes from 'Raja', which means to turn back or return. So, Raj'ah is the belief in turning back or returning. This is the literal meaning. If we look at its terminological meaning, it is the belief that after the reappearance of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and before the Day of Judgment, the dead will be brought back to life. There will be some people who have departed from this world who will be raised again, brought back to life. The Day of Judgment has not arrived yet; before the Day of Judgment, some people will be brought back to life. This is called Raj'ah, meaning they will be brought back to the world, they will be turned back to the world again. This is its terminological meaning, and this terminological meaning, this concept of Raj'ah, we are not stating it from ourselves; this belief is actually a Quranic belief. There is evidence for it in the Holy Quran, and... ...there is evidence for it in the Holy Quran, and this belief is proven by the Holy Quran. Although there are many verses, for today's discussion, we have tried to select only two verses and some Hadith to present before you. The first verse that needs to be presented to you in this regard is verse number 243 of Surah Al-Baqarah, in which Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala states: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. 'Alam tara'—have you not seen, or do you not know about those who went out of their homes, 'min diyarihim'—they went out of their homes, 'wa hum ulufun'—and they were in the thousands, 'hazaral-mawt'—why did they go out? Out of fear of death. Out of fear of death, they went out. In the narrations, it is said, what was this fear of death? It is actually the incident of a tribe in Sham where for years, for many years, the plague had spread. So, the strong people of that time, the wealthy individuals, what did they do? They left the city, they went out of their homes just to escape death. Those who were weak, who were among the frail, the poor souls, they remained there, but those who could go out... ...those poor souls remained there, but those who could go out, they went out. So, out of fear of death, thousands of people went out of their homes, and after that, the verse continues, 'faqala lahumullahu mutu'—Allah said to them, 'Die,' or Allah gave them all death, and then 'thumma ahyahum'—after that, He brought them back to life. After that, they were brought back to life. This means that after giving them death in this very world, Allah brought them back to this world. This is called Raj'ah. This is proven by the Quran. This was the Raj'ah of those people who happened in the world, or this is a concept, a belief being stated that even after death, some people being brought back to the world is proven by this verse. Now, in this same regard, let us move towards another verse. The second verse is from Surah number 27, verse number 83. In it, the Lord of Majesty is stating: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. 'Yawma nahshuru min kulli ummatin fawjan'—look, this is a very interesting verse. Ponder over it. What is Allah stating? That 'wa yawma'—and a day will come when what will we do? That we will bring a group from every nation, we will raise them, 'nahshuru'—meaning we will gather them, we will bring a group from every nation... ...we will bring a group, 'mimman yukadhdhibu bi-ayatina'—and we will bring such a group that had denied Our verses, Our signs. We will specifically bring such people, 'fahum yuwza'un'—and after that, they will be divided into groups, or they will all be brought in separate groups. Now, ponder over this verse, that this 'min kulli ummatin fawjan'—the bringing of a group from every nation—is being talked about. In the context of the commentary of this verse, Janab Abu Basir narrates from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) that once, regarding this verse, Imam Baqir (a.s.) said to me, 'Qala Abu Ja'far (a.s.)'—Imam Baqir (a.s.) says to me, 'Yunkiru ahlul-Iraq ar-raj'ah?'—Do the people of Iraq deny Raj'ah? The Imam directly asked Abu Basir. Do the Iraqis deny Raj'ah? Abu Basir said, 'Na'am'—Yes, Master, these people deny it, that there is no such thing as Raj'ah in the world. Once a human has gone, they will not return to the world. This is their belief. The Master said a strange sentence. Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'Ama yaqra'ul-Quran?'—Do these people not read the Quran? A strange and amazing thing. The Imam (a.s.) could have answered in simple words, but the Imam chose these words... ...the Imam chose these words. Meaning, in a way, the Imam (a.s.) asking this question, 'Do they not read the Quran?', is telling us that these were the same people—meaning, in a way, the Imam (a.s.) is pointing towards those people—these were the same people who had said yesterday that 'the Quran is sufficient for us.' This was their claim, and today the Imam (a.s.) is asking about these same people, 'Do these people not read the Quran?' So, all the claims made yesterday that 'the Quran is sufficient for us'—all these claims are false. And well, someone here might say, 'No, there are many Huffaz there, there are many people who have read the Quran, memorized it.' So look, memorizing is of no use if the Quran is not understood and all its teachings are not followed, because one must have faith in it. The most important condition is that there must be faith for it. And that is why we need to teach our children and our youth the Tafsir (exegesis) of the Quran, teach them the Tafsir of the Quran. But that Tafsir which is based on the Hadith of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). The books of Hadith, that Tafsir should be of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), so that the more a person tries to understand the Quran in the light of the Hadith of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), then this will become the true manifestation of the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, that he has then become satisfied with the Quran and the Ahlul-Bayt... ...he has then become satisfied with the Quran and the Ahlul-Bayt. So, a person who turns towards the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) to understand the Quran has actually practiced the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. So, we should try as much as possible that our youth understand the Quran in the light of the narrations of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), and this Quranic understanding is more important, holds more significance compared to just memorizing the Quran. Memorizing is important, it's not that it shouldn't be memorized; memorizing has its own virtue, but at the same time, understanding the Quran is more necessary, and having faith in it is more necessary. So, the Imam (a.s.) asked about these people, 'Do they not read the Quran?' In the Quran, it is clearly written, and the Imam (a.s.) is clearly pointing towards this very verse. And the Imam says that these people do not read, look, it is clearly, clearly written in the Quran that on that day, we will bring a group, an army from every nation, from every nation, we will raise them. Now, let us move towards another commentary of this verse. A person came to Imam Ja'far Sadiq (a.s.) and says to the Imam, 'Mawla, inna...'—regarding this same verse, he says, 'Mawla, these 'amma'—meaning the common Muslims—they speculate about this verse, they speculate that this is about the Day of Judgment, that on that day Allah will raise a group from every nation'... ...that on that day Allah will raise a group from every nation—so they think, they speculate that the verse is about the Day of Judgment. So, on this, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'Faqala...'—look, the Imam (a.s.) criticized those who hold the belief that this verse is about the Day of Judgment, that it has no relation to Raj'ah. The Imam (a.s.)'s criticism is for those people. What criticism is the Imam making? The Imam says, 'Will Allah bring a group from every nation on the Day of Judgment and leave the rest? Will He not raise them?' Will they keep resting in their graves? Will they not be raised? This means the verse itself is saying, the raising of a group from every nation is proof that it is not about the Day of Judgment. This is about Raj'ah. The Imam says, 'La, la...'—No, 'innama dhalika fir-raj'ah'—this will happen when Raj'ah occurs. This is about Raj'ah. 'Wa ayatul-qiyamah'—and as far as the Day of Judgment is concerned, the verse related to the Day of Judgment is another verse, to which the Imam is pointing. And the Imam recited the verse of Surah Al-Kahf. The Imam recited verse number 47 of Surah Al-Kahf and says, 'As far as the Day of Judgment is concerned, then the other verse is what? 'Wa hasharnahum falam nughadir minhum ahada'—and We will gather them and will not leave even one of them. Not even one will be left; everyone will be raised, everyone will be gathered. Everyone will be raised, everyone will be gathered. The Imam says, 'This verse is about the Day of Judgment.' The Imam says, 'This verse is about the Day of Judgment.' That Surah Al-Baqarah verse or that Surah An-Nahl verse is not about the Day of Judgment; it is about Raj'ah, because in it, a group will be raised from every nation. Look, this is another point; this way of the Imam (a.s.) answering also proves that those who claimed 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us), those who abandoned the 'Quran-e-Natiq' (the Speaking Quran) and thought that the 'Quran-e-Samit' (the Silent Quran) is sufficient for our guidance, actually, due to abandoning the Quran-e-Natiq, they could not even understand the clear verses of the Quran. They could not understand the apparent verses then, they are not understanding them today, and they will not understand them in the future. These people will not understand. Why? Because they did not come to the door of the Ahlul-Bayt. They will understand this when they present themselves at the door of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). Until the Quran is understood in the light of the narrations of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), a human will not even be able to understand the apparent meaning of the Quran. To understand the apparent meaning of the Quran, the help of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) is required. So, now, as the Imam said, this verse is about Raj'ah, not about the Day of Judgment. On the Day of Judgment, everyone will be brought, everyone will be raised, not just one group. Meaning, this faith in Raj'ah is a Quranic belief. Now... ...this faith in Raj'ah is a Quranic belief. Now, let us move towards some Hadith which are necessary for us in our books, specifically for us to have faith in this Raj'ah. This is a specialty of the Shias, it is our specialty that our faith, our belief is in Raj'ah. In this regard, Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'Laysa minna man lam yu'min bi-karratina'—that person is not from us, he is not from us at all, who does not believe in our 'Karratina'. 'Karratina' means this is another name for Raj'ah. The concept of 'Karrat' is also this: to come again, to return again, to be brought back again. Whoever does not believe in this returning again is not from us. And second, 'wa lam yastahillu mut'atana'—or he who does not consider Mut'ah as Halal, considers Mut'ah as Haram, he is also not from us. Meaning, in the Shia religion, faith in Imamate is only acceptable when there is also faith in Raj'ah along with it. If a person does not have faith in Raj'ah, then he cannot be a Shia Ithna Ashari. This is how important, how significant this belief in Raj'ah is. How important and significant 'Aqeedah' (belief) is, can be found in another Hadith. Abu Sabbah says to Hazrat Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.), 'I asked Imam Baqir (a.s.)...' Actually, the style of asking the question in this Hadith is a bit different; it wasn't a direct question. Although the narrator didn't exactly ask the Imam a question, the narrator says, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, O Mawla, I feel hesitant to present the question I have before you. I feel hesitant to ask this because, in reality, the Masumeen (a.s.) had already explained everything so clearly regarding 'Raj'at' (the return) that there was no room for doubt. Therefore, asking the same question repeatedly...' The narrator says, 'I feel hesitant to ask you the same question again.' The narrator did not clarify or state what he wanted to ask; he only said, 'O Mawla, may my life be sacrificed for you, I feel hesitant to present the question I have brought before you.' The Imam (a.s.) immediately said to him—what did the Imam (a.s.) say to the narrator? 'Are you wanting to ask about Raj'at?' He said, 'Yes, Mawla.' This is how the Imam is—someone who reads the states of our hearts. Here, our belief... Reads the states of our hearts. Here, our belief is in such an Imam that we consider someone an Imam who possesses 'Ilm-e-Ghayb' (knowledge of the unseen) and is 'Masoom' (infallible). We do not consider just anyone an Imam, because if someone is not aware of the states of our hearts, how will he guide our hearts? Otherwise, look, if a person considers someone an Imam who is no different from us—who only believes in the apparent, who possesses only the same apparent knowledge that we possess—then there is no difference between the two. Then why would he be an Imam? Then tomorrow, anyone could rise and claim Imamate. Therefore, our belief in Imamate is that the Imam we accept, the Imam we submit to—and that too, the Imam whom Allah has selected—must be infallible and must possess 'Ilm-e-Ghayb'. The Imam (a.s.) read the state of his heart and immediately said, 'Do you want to ask about Raj'at?' The narrator said, 'Yes, Mawla.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Strange, this is our belief.' Look at the Imam's answer. The Imam says, 'Lakal Qudrat' (This is the power of Allah). This is the power of God. Raj'at, and no one has denied this belief except those who deny the power of God. Therefore, look, 'La Tunakho, Lakal Qudrat' (Do not deny it, this is the power of Allah). This is the power of Allah. Never deny it. This means the Imam (a.s.), through this answer, wants to tell us what Raj'at means—that people returning to life in this world after death. This 'Raj'at' (return)—meaning many people will return—there are two important things here. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'You are asking about Raj'at,' meaning you are asking about the return of many people. This Raj'at, in this Hadith, the Imam (a.s.) has described as a proof of the power of God. Meaning, having faith in this Raj'at, holding this belief in Raj'at, is a sign of a Momin (believer). In this regard, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states in another Hadith that whoever believes in seven things, he is a Momin. If he affirms these seven things, he is a Momin. If he denies even one of these seven things, he will be outside the fold of faith. What are these seven things? First, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Al-Bara'atu min al-Jibt wa al-Taghut' (Disavowal of Jibt and Taghut). 'Taghut' is plural. In another Hadith, it is explicitly stated as 'Al-Bara'atu min al-Jibt wa al-Taghut'. Disavowing and distancing oneself from all the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is the first thing, the first belief. Then, 'Wilayat' (guardianship) is the second. Affirming our Wilayat—first is 'Tabarra' (disavowal), then 'Tawalla' (allegiance). First, our... First is Tabarra, then Tawalla. First, disavow our enemies, then affirm our Wilayat. 'Wal-Imanu bi-Raj'at' (And faith in Raj'at). There must be faith in Raj'at. 'Wa hillu al-Mut'ah' (And consider Mut'ah lawful). 'Wa al-Jirri'—Jirri refers to the fish that is without scales. The fish without scales is not permissible for us to eat; it is not allowed. Only fish with scales can be eaten; that is what is lawful. So, eating fish without scales is Haram (forbidden). 'Wa al-Jirri Haram' (And Jirri is forbidden). One must have faith in this. 'Wa mash 'ala al-khuffayn' (And wiping over the socks/leather slippers) is Haram; it is not allowed. So, whoever believes in these things, whoever affirms these things, is a Momin. Sheikh Saduq has included this Hadith in his book 'Sifat al-Shia', and Sheikh Amili (may Allah be pleased with him) has also narrated this Hadith in 'Wasa'il al-Shia'. Whoever denies all these seven things will be outside the fold of faith. Meaning, Raj'at is 'Haq' (truth), it is 'Tammi' (certain), it must happen. Faith in this is necessary; otherwise, that person is not a Momin and will be outside of faith. In another Hadith, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says—it is a long Hadith—the important part related to Raj'at is where Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'By Allah, by God, no...' The Imam (a.s.) says, 'By Allah, by God, the days and nights will keep passing. Days will come, nights will come. This is not how this sequence will end, until Allah brings some dead back to life and gives death to some living.' This means that in this era of Raj'at, the dead will be brought back to life, and the living will also face death. And further, the Imam says, 'Wa yaruddu Allah al-Haqqa ila ahlihi' (And Allah will return the truth to its people). This means the truth will be returned to its people. And who are the people of the truth? Look, in that same famous Hadith that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with Ali.' Allah will turn the truth to where Ali turns. Therefore, Raj'at will be the era where the government of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be established, where the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be given their right. Raj'at will be that era. This era that is to come after the 'Zuhoor' (reappearance) is a necessary condition for Raj'at—the Zuhoor of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.). And then in the Hadith, the Imam (a.s.) further says that Allah will return the truth to its people. Allah will establish the religion with which He... Allah will establish the religion with which He is pleased. He will establish the religion that He has chosen and is pleased with. Which religion? The same Ghadiri religion, the same religion that He announced on the plains of Ghadir, the verse that was revealed: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you.' And this Islam, which was completed with the Wilayat of Ali, this Islam I have chosen for you. That same religion, that same Ghadiri religion, Allah will re-establish it. He will establish that religion in the era of Raj'at. And it will be the religion that Allah has chosen for Himself and His Prophet. Then after that, the Imam says, 'Abshiru' (Rejoice), 'Thumma abshiru' (Then rejoice), 'Thumma abshiru' (Then rejoice). Three times the Imam (a.s.) has given glad tidings. There is good news for you. If you truly believe in Raj'at, then when that era comes, it will be a cause of joy for you. Since you have faith in it, since you have this belief, that era is a cause of glad tidings for you. So rejoice, 'Falla al-Haqqa ila...' The truth is nothing, by God, the truth is nothing except that which is in your hands, or that which is your religion—the religion in your hands upon which you remain steadfast. That is the truth, that is the truth. This means Raj'at is certain, it is certainly going to happen. Raj'at... It is certain, Raj'at must happen. This era must come, and this is the truth towards which we—Alhamdulillah—in this entire series, after the video, you all recite Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin. Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin is recited, and you all participate in it. In Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin itself, there is an indication towards Raj'at. What is the phrase in Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin? 'I bear witness that Raj'at is the truth, there is no doubt or suspicion in it.' I bear witness. Along with this, if we turn towards Ziyarat-e-Jame'a al-Kabira, in Ziyarat-e-Jame'a al-Kabira as well, the belief in Raj'at is expressed. The person, through this phrase, is expressing his faith. What is that phrase? 'O Mawla, I affirm this, I acknowledge your Wilayat and the status and the station that you have. I acknowledge it, I affirm it. 'Mu'minun bi-iyabikum' (I have faith in your return). I am certain that you will return. 'Musaddiqun bi-raj'atikum' (I am confirming your Raj'at). Look, this confirmation is necessary. Confirmation means to declare that this is the truth. I am announcing this... This is the truth, I am announcing this, I am confirming this. I am confirming what? That your return will happen, you will return. This means the Masumeen (a.s.) will return in Raj'at. 'Muntazirun li-amrikum' (I am waiting for your government, for your command). I am waiting for you. 'Murtaqibun li-dawlatikum' (I am keeping my eyes fixed on your government). 'Murtaqib' is used for looking intently, which is also in the Quranic verse: 'Allah says, so keep watching, I am also watching with you.' In Ziyarat-e-Jame'a al-Kabira, the person is pointing towards that: 'Murtaqibun li-dawlatikum' (I am keeping my eyes fixed on your government). I am waiting for your government. This is Ziyarat-e-Jame'a al-Kabira, in which a person is expressing his belief. Now the question arises, who will come in Raj'at? In this regard, there are many narrations. Just briefly, one or two more Hadiths, and Insha'Allah, we will conclude our discussion. Now, who will return in Raj'at? In this regard, Janab Mufazzal ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) regarding that same verse of the Holy Quran, regarding the saying of Allah the Almighty: 'And the day We will gather from every nation a group...' In that regard, Janab Mufazzal narrates a Hadith from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that the Imam (a.s.) said... The Imam (a.s.) said, 'There will be no person among the Momineen who was killed in the world or who was martyred, except that he will return in Raj'at.' He will be brought back. All those who were martyred, all those among the Momineen who were martyred, will all return in Raj'at. Until they return in Raj'at and then depart from this world through their natural death. Because when they came into this world, when they were living their lives in that world, they did not get to experience a natural death; they were martyred. The enemies martyred them. Therefore, these Momineen will be given another chance; they will be brought back to life in Raj'at so that they can come, live their lives fully, and depart from the world through their natural death. All the Momineen who were martyred. And then the Imam (a.s.) further says, 'And no one will return in Raj'at except the one who is a staunch Momin, whose faith was complete in the world. Only he will be brought back.' And not only will this staunch Momin be brought back, 'And those who were completely enemies of the religion, the religion of Allah, the religion of Islam, they will also be brought back.' Meaning, the Momin will also be brought back, and the enemies of the religion will also be brought back. Both these groups will be brought back... These are all the people who will be brought back. Now, as the previous point has already been made, when we acknowledge the Masumeen (a.s.), when we recite their Ziyarat, especially when the discussion of Ziyarat-e-Jame'a al-Kabira came up, there was that phrase: 'I am waiting for your government and I have faith in your Raj'at, in your return.' So now, when the turn of the Masumeen (a.s.) comes, when the mention of the Masumeen (a.s.) comes—when they will return—what is the case in that regard? In that regard, there is a narration from Janab Mufazzal ibn Qays from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Janab Mufazzal ibn Qays narrates from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that the Imam (a.s.) said, 'The first one who will return to the world will be Al-Husayn (a.s.), the Master of Martyrs.' Hazrat Abdullah al-Husayn will come. Imam Husayn (a.s.) will come to the world first. Among the Masumeen (a.s.), Imam Husayn (a.s.) will be the first to return. In this Hadith, it is like this—in some Hadiths, it is mentioned that Amir al-Momineen (a.s.) will also come, and all the Imams will come. But the first one who will come is Imam Husayn (a.s.). And then, not only will he return, but an interesting thing in this Hadith is that the Imam further says that after that, Imam Husayn (a.s.) will rule over this world. Husain (a.s.) will rule over this world; the rule of Sayyid al-Shuhada (a.s.) will be in the world. That is to say, the first one to return will be Imam Husain (a.s.). And look, this very belief—the return of Imam Husain (a.s.)—is completely connected to our belief that he will take revenge on his killers. This revenge will only happen after the reappearance (Zuhur). That is why we recite, 'Talib bi-thar al-Maqtul bi-Karbala' (The seeker of the blood of the one killed in Karbala). We are calling out to Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) in this way: 'Where is the one who will take revenge for the blood of the one killed in Karbala?' Now, let us connect this to Ziyarat Ashura. In Ziyarat Ashura, this very point is indicated. What do we recite in Ziyarat Ashura? 'O Allah, I ask of You, I am making a request, Allahumma akrim maqami'—that You have honored my position, 'wa an yuballighani al-maqam al-mahmud lakum'—and that I am also honorable because I affirm your Wilayah. I am your follower, your lover; therefore, Allah has made me honorable. So, based on that honor, what do I pray? 'An yarzuqani talaba tharika ma'a Imam mansur'—I pray to Allah by His right that He grants me this sustenance, which sustenance? That I may take revenge for your blood... ...that I may take revenge for your blood, 'ma'a Imam mansur min ahl-i Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)'—along with the victorious Imam, the Imam of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). That victorious Imam, that Imam who will be helped and supported, that Imam is Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.). Here, 'Imam Mansur' refers to Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.). We recite this in Ziyarat Ashura, and Ziyarat Ashura is one of the proofs of Raj'ah (the return). It is a part of the belief in Raj'ah that we should be able to take revenge. This should be the desire of every mourner. A true mourner, based on this, should pray for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) at every moment, every second. As much as possible, every mourner who feels this pain—that the revenge for the blood of Imam Husain (a.s.) has not yet been fully taken—should, as a true mourner, pray as much as possible for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), because this will only be possible after the reappearance. After the reappearance, this will happen. Therefore, pray for the reappearance as much as possible, and... ...and as a true mourner, we should be committed to Dua-e-Ahad. In Dua-e-Ahad, there is also an indication of this belief in Raj'ah. Or the person, as is famous about Dua-e-Ahad, you all know that there is an emphasis on reciting it for 40 days after the morning prayer. What is the special thing in that emphasis, what is the reward of this Dua-e-Ahad? The special thing is that for whoever recites this Dua for 40 days, even if he passes away from this world, when Imam (a.s.) reappears, this person—because he used to recite Dua-e-Ahad—will be brought out from his grave. He will be raised again. And this is a sentence from Dua-e-Ahad itself: 'Allahumma in hal bayni wa baynahu al-mawt'—O Lord, if death comes between me and the reappearance of the Imam, if the veil of death comes, if death arrives—meaning if I leave this world and the Imam reappears after I am gone—then what to do? 'Allahumma inna al-mawt haq'—O Lord, this death is the truth, no one denies this, death is bound to happen—'wa lakin in kharaja qabli'—but if death comes before the reappearance, then O Lord, what should I do? 'Fa-akhrijni min qabri'—O Lord, bring me out of my grave... ...O Lord, bring me out of my grave, 'mu'taziran kafani'—wrapped in my shroud, 'shahiran sayfani'—my sword in my hand, 'mujarridan qanati'—my spear in my hand, 'mulabbiyan da'wat al-da'i'—responding to the call of the caller. This is the sentence of Dua-e-Ahad. This revenge for Imam Husain (a.s.), and another special revenge that will happen after the reappearance of the Imam, is the revenge for the oppression inflicted upon Princess Fatima Zahra (s.a.). That will also happen after the reappearance. That is to say, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) will take revenge for all the injustices. This will happen in that era when the enemies will be brought back to life. Only when they are brought back to life can revenge be taken. Therefore, the return of those people is also certain. Those who committed injustices, the revenge for all those injustices will be taken after the reappearance. One day, he will show his Haidari style; one day, he will come carrying the Zulfiqar. One day, he will show everyone their true status. The heir of the Prophet is sitting in occultation; one day, he will come and take the revenge. O Lord, O God, by the intercession of the injustices inflicted upon Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.)... ...O God, by the intercession of the injustices inflicted upon Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), hasten the reappearance of our Imam of the time (a.j.t.f.). Grant us the success to be included among his helpers and supporters, and after his reappearance, grant us the success to take revenge on Your enemies and the enemies of all the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) along with him. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds. And our final prayer is praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his pure and infallible family. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. [Music] Peace... ...[Music]... ...[Music]... I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Wali of the believers. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Before we announce today's winners, we would like to tell you that this was the last episode of the Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.) Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz 2024, and there will be no episode of this series tomorrow. However, you have been given a one-day opportunity so that those who have given correct answers to all the questions in 7 out of 12 episodes of this series, or if their quizzes were not completed, they can still attempt these quizzes, the links for which will be live until Sunday, March 3rd, at 9:00 PM... ...the links for which will be live until Sunday, March 3rd, at 9:00 PM, and after that, they can be eligible for the mega prize, the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq, which will be conducted on the same day, i.e., Sunday, March 3rd, at 9:30 PM through our computerized lucky draw system, Insha Allah. Now let's see who our daily lucky draw winners are today, who will receive the Indian Hajj prize, and their names are on your screen: Rida Zahra from Srinagar, Syed Mohammad Hanafi from Alipur, Mahboob Khwaja from Bhut, Sarfaraz Madina from Mumbai, Sayyeda Kazma Farhad from Jaipur. Many congratulations to all the winners. We would like to thank you all once again. Insha Allah, we will meet you again on Sunday, March 3rd, at 9:30 PM, where the announcement of the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq will be made. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Iltemas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali.

chapters.title: Mega Quiz Guidelines and Procedures
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the rules for the ongoing quiz, including how to participate and the requirements for winning the mega prize of a Ziyarat pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Defining the Concept of Raj'ah
chapters.summary: The lecture defines Raj'ah as the belief that certain individuals will return to life in this world after the reappearance of Imam Mahdi but before the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: Quranic Evidence for Raj'ah
chapters.summary: The speaker provides Quranic verses, specifically Surah Al-Baqarah 243 and Surah An-Naml 83, to demonstrate that the concept of returning to life is supported by the Holy Quran.

chapters.title: Understanding Quran via Ahlul-Bayt
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that understanding the Quran through the teachings of the Ahlul-Bayt is essential for true faith, rather than relying on literal memorization alone.

chapters.title: Raj'ah vs. The Day of Judgment
chapters.summary: The Imam clarifies that specific Quranic verses referring to the raising of a group from every nation describe the event of Raj'ah, distinct from the universal gathering on the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Belief in Raj'ah
chapters.summary: Faith in Raj'ah is presented as an essential component of Shia identity and Imamate, with narrations stating that those who deny it are not considered true followers.

chapters.title: Imamate, Ilm-e-Ghayb, and Seven Essential Beliefs
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the Imam's knowledge of the unseen and outlines seven core beliefs, including Raj'ah and Tabarra, that define a true Momin.

chapters.title: The Era of Truth and Justice
chapters.summary: Raj'ah is described as the era where the truth will be returned to the Ahlulbayt and their government will be established following the reappearance of Imam Mahdi.

chapters.title: The Certainty of Raj'at
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that Raj'at (the return) is a fundamental truth of the Ghadiri religion and is explicitly affirmed in Ziyarat-e-Ale Yasin and Ziyarat-e-Jame'a al-Kabira.

chapters.title: Who Returns in Raj'at
chapters.summary: Narrations indicate that martyrs and staunch believers, as well as the enemies of Islam, will return during the era of Raj'at.

chapters.title: The Return of Imam Husayn (a.s.)
chapters.summary: Imam Husayn (a.s.) will be the first among the Masumeen to return and rule, fulfilling the prayers of believers seeking justice for his martyrdom.

title: Muharram 1442 Urdu Majlis #10: Amal (Action) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this Majlis, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the essential relationship between faith, Wilayah, and practical action in the life of a believer. He emphasizes that love for the Ahlulbayt must manifest through consistent good deeds, spiritual vigilance, and a commitment to acquiring knowledge. By drawing lessons from the tragedy of Karbala and the teachings of the Imams, the lecture encourages listeners to cultivate piety, patience, and kindness in their daily lives while preparing for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time.

title: Raziallah Kaun Aur Ghazeballah Kaun | From SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual status of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) and the direct correlation between her pleasure or anger and that of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and Allah. The speaker highlights a tradition narrated to Salman al-Farsi, emphasizing that devotion to Fatimah provides essential salvation during critical moments like death, the grave, and the Day of Judgment. Furthermore, the lecture warns against the severe consequences of oppressing her, her progeny, or her followers, noting that such actions invite the wrath of Allah.
content:
What does the Prophet say to Salman? 'Ya Salman, man ahabba Fatimata ibnati fahuwa fil-jannati ma'i' (O Salman, whoever has devotion to my daughter Fatimah, he will be with me in Paradise). The Prophet further says, 'Wa man abghadaha fahuwa fin-nar' (But whoever angers my daughter, he will burn in the fire of Hell). Then the Prophet says, 'Ya Salman, hubbu Fatimata yanfa'u fi mi'ati mawtin' (O Salman, devotion to Fatimah will be useful in 100 places). Among which, the easiest, the lightest places that the Prophet mentioned, what are they? 'Aysaru tilkal-mawatini' (The lightest of those occasions). Which are the easiest occasions? Death, the grave, the scale (mizan), the gathering (mahshar), the path (sirat), and the reckoning (muhasaba). Well, these are all things... these are the lightest places. If these are light, then what will the severe places be? I don't know. Now, after that, the Prophet's sentence is amazing. The Prophet says, now look, pay attention to this. The Prophet says, 'Faman radiyat 'anhu ibnati Fatimatu radiytu 'anhu' (Whoever my daughter Fatimah is pleased with, I am pleased with him). Wow! 'Wa man radiytu 'anhu radiyallahu 'anhu' (And whoever I am pleased with, Allah is pleased with him). Wow! Wow! Wow! Here, the talk is about pleasure. Along with pleasure, there is also anger. Yes. Meaning, Allah is not leaving any aspect, any corner empty. Neither is Allah leaving it empty, nor the Prophet. The Prophet says, 'Wa man ghadibat 'alayhi Fatimatu ghadibtu 'alayhi' (Whoever Fatimah is angry with, I am angry with him). 'Wa man ghadibtu 'alayhi ghadiballahu 'alayhi' (And whoever I am angry with, Allah is angry with him). Meaning, the opposite of 'Radiallahu' (Allah is pleased) will be 'Ghadabullah' (Allah's anger). Then the Prophet says, 'Ya Salman, waylun liman yazlimuha' (Woe to those who oppress her). 'Wayl' means Hell. Curses be upon those people. One of the pits of Hell, meaning one of the valleys of Hell, is named 'Wayl'. The lowest valley. It is also mentioned in the Quran. That this is 'Wayl'. These people will be in the lowest level of Hell. Which people? Those who oppressed my daughter. 'Wa yazlimu dhurriyyataha' (And oppress her progeny). Not just oppressed my daughter, but also oppressed her progeny, her family, her children, her sons. Oppressed her daughters. 'Wa shi'ataha' (And her Shias). This means whoever oppresses the Shias in the name of the Princess. Why? Because they defend the rights of the Princess. They defend the Wilayat. They raise their voices for it. They come forward for their rights. And because of this, some people find this unpleasant, and therefore they oppose them and cause harm to those Shias, then all of them will come under the scope of 'Ghadiballahu 'alayhim'.
Loving Lady Fatimah is a source of salvation in 100 critical moments, including death and the grave.
The pleasure of Fatimah is the criterion for the pleasure of the Prophet and Allah.
The anger of Fatimah is the criterion for the anger of the Prophet and Allah.
Oppressing Lady Fatimah or her progeny leads to the lowest level of Hell.
Oppressing the Shias for defending the Wilayat of Fatimah incurs divine wrath.
The term 'Wayl' refers to a specific, severe valley in Hell reserved for oppressors.

title: Eesaal-e-Sawaab Majlis-e-Azaa Baraaye Marhoom Nazar Abbas Ibn Gulam Abbas Talajawala
excerpt: This lecture serves as a memorial service (Majlis-e-Azaa) dedicated to the late Nazar Abbas, focusing on the Islamic perspective regarding death, grief, and divine decree. It draws profound parallels between the personal loss of a loved one and the universal tragedy of Karbala to provide comfort and spiritual guidance. The discourse emphasizes the importance of patience (Sabr), the acceptance of Allah's will, and the belief that trials are opportunities for spiritual purification rather than mere punishment.

I want to point out that whenever any difficulty, calamity, or trial befalls a human being according to the Quran, the reaction of humans is found to be of different types. So, look, the Quran says that whenever a trial comes, there is a way to remember, a way to complain, and what will be the result? And it is possible that our reaction will be: 'Why me? Why did this happen to me?' But if you ponder, you will find a path in your life and mine, for such situations, as the Quran and Hadith state... Regarding the spiritual contracts and the hadith that is valid—whether it is from Medina or some other issue, the exact location is unknown, but it is from Medina or perhaps picked up on the way—these types of issues remained. And he said, 'May it be so.' Well, tell me, what are you saying? Did you not speak? Are you praying while fasting? To remember in this way is wrong; you are wasting your energy. It was asked, 'Is there any human being in the world who has come and will not go through a test?' For example, if we are working for someone and they are sitting in front of us, then this world... Sitting in front of us, this world... when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) went with a marriage proposal, the family of the house he visited wrote that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) brought a proposal and all this, so they were happy. It is natural to be happy. In that same joy, the father said a sentence in praise of his daughter: 'My daughter has great qualities, she is amazing, she is very virtuous, she is very pious.' He said that sentence, and to this day, she has never been ill. As soon as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) heard the praise of his daughter—that she never gets sick—think, if it were you or me, what would our reaction be? 'Oh, how healthy she is, that's very good.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) reacted completely contrary to our reaction. He said, 'Get up, let's go.' He asked, 'Is there no flaw in such a girl? Never being ill, never facing any trouble—this is not for a human being.' Today, when such trouble comes to us, because we are not among those... Because we are not among those whose faith is very strong, whose faith I could talk about for a long time... My point is that the first person, in the eyes of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), is the one who, when trouble comes, screams and shouts. If the world did not have trouble, a human being could not be good. Why did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) descend from the heavens, and why is this necessary? It is because through it, one remembers God. The waiting for the family of Muhammad (a.s.) is for this reason. You said that if you want to react, do it this way. Instead, pray, 'O Allah, remove the pain from the world.' You have... Remove the pain from the world. Have you ever seen anyone who, today, we can do the whole society... if you put someone in trouble, do you say, 'May Allah keep you happy, may Allah make you smile, may Allah give you this'? No, this is wrong. Never pray like this. Do you pray that 'May Allah put you in trouble'? Our prayer should be, 'O Allah, do not put us in such trouble that we cannot bear it.' When a person does this, everything will happen. I am with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the family of Muhammad (a.s.). Someone has been struck by grief, and their tears do not stop, their restlessness is on their face, their pain does not decrease. No matter how much comfort others give, it does not go away. The command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is with us, that you bring the command of Allah. Look, it is a very big matter. Today, we have similar situations before us—someone's father, someone's son... Truly, the situation—whether it is someone's father, son, mother, or sister—going through this pain is unbearable. It is not easy for a human being to see someone suffering or to watch someone struggling for breath. It is easy to say from the outside, but if you adopt this divine perspective, you will find patience. Look at the Prophet (s.a.w.a.); when he was brought to a place, he suddenly saw a pigeon's nest. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked the person who brought the pigeon, 'Where did you bring this from? How many eggs does this pigeon lay every year? How many chicks hatch, and how many grow up? Their life is very short, yet is there any deficiency in how she raises them? No.' Then he asked, 'What is the reason that when we humans catch her chicks and press them, she does not leave her home? She does not go away, does she?' She does not leave, does she? What were you looking at? You took her chicks and hid them, yet she is still there. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Is your value less than this pigeon, that when trouble comes, your reaction is to this extent?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explained this to him with that example, and his tears were wiped away. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Indeed, the God who gave is the one who is calling back, so I have no right to complain.' This is the first point: how a person reacts when someone is taken. The second point I have read is that the children of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—why does He give glad tidings to those in trouble? Because if He puts them through any pain or trouble in this world, He never does it without purpose. He never puts them in trouble; rather, He uses all His power. If Allah has put me in this trouble, I will face it with courage and fight it. I want to say that there is no doubt that he spent a large part of his life serving his parents without any greed. He dedicated a large part of his life to his parents. His own children told me, 'Baba, even when he is on oxygen, he says, look, so-and-so helps me, I feel proud to serve them.' Even in that state, his heart is filled with how he can help others. So, on one hand, Allah gave you a father who was capable and a believer. He was capable, a believer, and he raised you with proper upbringing. He got you married, and after that, he spent a part of his life for his Lord. Now, the Lord of the Worlds has called him back to Himself. If He has called him, I am pained, and you are pained too, but if He has called him, it was not our decision. Who am I or you to decide? If it was His trust and He called him back, who am I to say he shouldn't have gone, or it wasn't the right time, or he should have lived longer? There is no one better to decide than Allah. Know this, 'Inna Hu absaru bi-ibadihi'—Allah is the best judge for His servants. It is a matter of faith. I have heard that once a month, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) would smile towards the sky. The Prophet's lips would smile; he never laughed out loud, but he would smile. He would smile among the people and look towards the sky. When Prophet Musa (a.s.) asked, 'Why are you smiling?', the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'I am seeing the descent of the angels.' They were descending. These angels who were descending were specifically for the patient ones. They go wherever they are—in the mosque, at home, anywhere. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I see the angels descending and saying, O Lord, this is your servant...' So what happens? All the angels came to record his deeds. And you didn't even get to see them; he is lying there. Now look, what a beautiful phrase: 'We have kept him in our custody.' We have kept him in our custody, so whatever good deeds he used to do in health, keep writing them in his record. Do not say that there is no one better than Allah. When he is writhing in pain, when his voice groans with pain, he is struggling. So, the angels say, 'O our Lord, as long as this servant is lying on the bed in this state, keep writing all the deeds he used to do during his health in his record.' Keep writing them in his record. Why? Because he is in My custody. Now, the question arises—this is where the confusion happens—'Why did such a big trouble come?' I have already explained that these people will be among those who are patient. Now look, how beautiful it is. Do not consider this a punishment; consider it a mercy. What is the reality of Allah's mercy? He gives a reason for mercy so that he remembers Allah and His blessings. When he goes through this, our hearts become soft. He did not reduce his status; rather, He forgave his sins. He did not just do that; He forgave his sins. And after that, I will tell you a story of Muhammad Raza. When he went to meet Imam Muhammad Taqi (a.s.), he said, 'When someone is given a trial, what should he do?' If someone is given a trial, he should be patient. Just think, what is the status of martyrdom and what is the status of illness? To be patient. If Allah has given you a trial and you have been patient, what is it? Suddenly, this started happening to me. For a long time, I started thinking about what to do. Starting from there, what should I think? Then, suddenly, pain started in my leg. The pain increased, the leg swelled up. It turned into an abscess, and pus started coming out. He says he was bedridden for ten months. When I was caught in this trouble, I remembered why the Imam (a.s.) had said that. It means the Imam (a.s.) had a hundred percent idea of my situation. That is why the Imam (a.s.) had already told me, 'O Muhammad, if you are patient, you will be a martyr. If you are not, you will go, but your status will not be the same.' To please Him, this is not just a matter of our family, but our deeds. Our deeds are to ask for forgiveness for our sins from the Almighty. And this pain, in this state, I accept it. So, the first thing is patience. The second quality of a special servant is that he is not just patient—patience is easy—but after that, he is pleased with the decree. He is not worried; he is not restless. He says, 'He considered me worthy of this.' So what did He do? He made you a believer. This is why Allah is pleased with them. I am pleased with You, O Allah, and if You are pleased, then I am also pleased. Your servant is before Your command. And look at this sentence, it is certain that 'I am leaving the people in the hands of Allah,' so that I may offer my children. I am giving them away. Just think, how great a matter this must have been for a father. It is a tragedy for me, and it would be a tragedy for you too, but just think, a father like Husayn (a.s.) and a son like Ali Akbar (a.s.). But look at both the father and the son, imagine the scene. What kind of son is he, who does not want any power other than his father's? He raised his voice for the truth, he raised his voice here. He raised his voice here, to the point that he is sacrificing himself. And on the other side, he says, 'Once he goes, there is no one left.' Now the time of separation between brother and sister has come. 'Brother, why is this happening? Can you not let me go? Can I not entrust you to Allah? I will not let you go.' She called him into her room, held both his arms, and said, 'I will not let you go to the battlefield, because since the morning, whoever has gone, Zainab (s.a.) has had this peace, Zainab (s.a.) has had this comfort that my brother... I have sacrificed Akbar (a.s.)...' Brother, brother, but the oppressors... he turned his face towards the sky, raised his hands, and said, 'Meet your sister with your fingers.' He pointed towards the sky and said... [inaudible]... before going to the battlefield, some precautions were taken. He is coming before Husayn (a.s.). You are being told, but this [praise] image, is it possible to see Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)? He will keep departing, this... [inaudible]... He was following behind... who recognizes him? From which place are you? Seeing him laughing, he cried out, 'O mother, my brother Akbar (a.s.) has answered.' Papa, one Akbar (a.s.) was Husayn (a.s.)... [praise]... a man has given martyrdom in his house, but O light of my eyes, you have to do this work which no one has done before. He looked up. Which no one has done before, he must have looked up. Tomorrow will be the day, there will be... there will be... and tomorrow, when you... O Allah, we are the progeny of the Prophet... O Allah, forgive his sins, forgive his sins. O Allah, grant him the company of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Grant the children of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) patience. O Allah, for the sake of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), grant us the intercession... O Allah, forgive all of us before the day of judgment, shower Your mercy upon us. Forgive us, shower Your blessings and mercy upon us. Those who are ill, grant them health. Those who have passed away from this world, forgive them. O Allah, protect the believers. Wherever they are, protect their lives. O Allah, wherever the believers are, protect them from the evil of the oppressors. Those who are fighting for their rights, O Lord, help them. O Allah, make me among the followers of the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and in this world, grant me the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and in the hereafter, grant me their intercession... O Allah, grant the soul of Abbas (a.s.) peace... O my brother, all around... O Allah, grant them patience... Say that this land is standing... where are you? If you find any check... tell me... tell me what is the matter... [music]... I am near you... tell me... O my brother... [inaudible]... calling out... [inaudible]... Here... [inaudible]... they said... [inaudible]... even then they will open... [inaudible]... stand on the path... [inaudible]... Take away the book... [inaudible]...

title: Ziyaarat Par Kharch Karne Ka Sawaab [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses the immense spiritual and material rewards of performing Ziyarat to the holy grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.). Drawing from a Hadith by Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.), the speaker highlights that expenses incurred during this journey are not losses but investments that guarantee divine protection for one's family and wealth. The talk encourages believers to overcome their anxieties regarding finances and family safety by placing their trust in Allah.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Master of the Age, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Husayn, and upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, and upon the children of Husayn, and upon the companions of Husayn. Aban ibn Taghlib states that I heard Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) saying, 'Whoever goes for the Ziyarat of the holy grave of Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (a.s.), he has connected himself to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and to us. Backbiting such a person is forbidden, and his flesh is forbidden upon the fire of Hell. For every dirham he spent on this Ziyarat, Allah will grant him ten thousand cities, which will be recorded in a preserved book. Now Allah will busy Himself in fulfilling his needs, and whatever that person left behind, all of that will also be protected. That person will not make any supplication to Allah but that Allah will certainly grant his supplications, whether immediately or after a slight delay.' May our lives be sacrificed for Imam Sadiq (a.s.), for it often happens that whenever someone intends to go for Ziyarat, they are very worried about two things, and the solution to both things has been stated by Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in this Hadith. One is the expense, and the other is the family. Those who possess wealth are often anxious that they might spend more than necessary, while those who save every penny to go on this Ziyarat worry about their families, wondering if they will remain safe after they leave. Sadiq-e-Aale Muhammad, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), has guaranteed both these matters in this Hadith. On one hand, for spending one dirham, Allah (s.w.t.) will grant ten thousand cities—not cities that perish in this world, but ten thousand cities recorded in a preserved book, meaning they will remain forever in Paradise. On the other hand, the guarantee has been given that whatever they leave behind will also be protected. Therefore, never be in a dilemma that spending on Ziyarat will diminish your wealth or that something will happen to your family in your absence. Relying on Allah, entrust your affairs to Him and try as much as possible to visit Hazrat Aba Abdillahil Hussain (a.s.). It is our prayer to the Almighty that He grants every lover of Imam Hussain (a.s.) the opportunity to perform this Ziyarat. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
