In the book 'Bihar al-Anwar', volume 33, page 154, a tradition is recorded in which Hazrat Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) narrates from his father Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), who narrates from his father Imam Hussain (a.s.), who narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself has stated: 'Al-Mahdi (a.s.) is from my progeny. There will be a test and a trial for them, during which the people will go astray. When he comes, he will bring the inheritance of the Prophets (a.s.) with him, and he will fill this earth with justice and equity just as it was filled with oppression and tyranny.' It is clear from this hadith that there will be a trial for Imam Mahdi (a.s.) in which people will go astray, meaning it will be difficult for people in that era. The second point mentioned in this hadith is that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will bring the inheritance of the Prophets (a.s.). The inheritance of the Prophets means all those relics and items through which the Prophets (a.s.) used to present proof of the reality of their prophethood, such as the ring of Hazrat Sulaiman (a.s.), the staff of Hazrat Musa (a.s.) the ring of Hazrat Musa (a.s.), the Ark of the Children of Israel which is called the 'Tabut-e-Sakina'. Therefore, whoever wishes to see those relics of the Prophets (a.s.) should pray for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as much as possible, for he is the heir to the relics of the Prophets (a.s.). In the end, we pray to the Almighty, while invoking the intercession of the Masumeen (a.s.), that the Lord of the Worlds may grant all the followers of Islam the reward for their efforts in this world and hasten the reappearance of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) so that he may come and the purpose of the Prophets (a.s.) may be fulfilled. title: Fadak aur Hum | Watch EP3 of The #Fadak #Podcast | #DoNotMiss
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological significance of the dispute over Fadak, framing it as a challenge to the legitimacy of the early Islamic government. The speaker argues that the demand for Fadak by Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) was fundamentally a defense of Wilayat and Imamate rather than a mere property dispute. The discourse critiques the historical narrative that attempts to reconcile conflicting parties in this event and emphasizes the ultimate accountability for these actions on the Day of Judgment.
content:
And the Imam wanted to explain that these boundaries were actually the boundaries of the Islamic government at that time. Yes. So, in reality, the Imam wanted to say that the position you are sitting on is a usurped position. And the Imam came and demanded not just Fadak, but the Wilayat and Imamate. Whoever—and here is the sentence—whoever snatched Fadak started an innovation (bid'ah) in the Prophetic law. Right? Because Hazrat Zahra (s.a.) presented many verses of the Quran as evidence that the Prophets have an inheritance. But we do not understand this stance of the Muslims: that the one who snatches the right is 'Rightly Guided', the one who returns the right is 'Rightly Guided', and the one whose right was snatched is also 'Rightly Guided'. One thing is certain: these protests have had an effect on every tyrant of every era, but this will end somewhere, and it is certain that this will be decided on the Day of Judgment. So, the question arises: where does an ordinary Muslim find themselves standing on this issue on the Day of Resurrection?

title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#18 - Bait E Tatheer Par Hamla - Duaon Aur Ziyaaraton Mein
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and spiritual significance of the tragedy of Lady Zahra (s.a.), focusing on the attack on her house and its profound impact on the Ahlulbayt. content:

Peace be upon the oppressed, peace be upon the one whose house was attacked, peace be upon Hazrat Zahra (s.a.). Every person who knows about the tragedies of Imam Hussain (a.s.) becomes immersed in his grief. Some people mourn from the first of Muharram until the end, while others mourn until Arbaeen, and we mourn this grief for about two and a quarter months. Meaning, from the moment the moon of Muharram is sighted, until... from the moment the moon of Muharram is sighted, until the end of Rabi al-Awwal. And we find a lot of material about this grief. We find all the tragedies of Imam Hussain (a.s.) in many supplications, poems, and elegies. So, the objection is that if, as we saw in the previous episode, the attack on the house of the Lady (s.a.) was a very big crime and the root of all tragedies, because the oppressors wanted to take allegiance from Ali (a.s.), and because of that allegiance, people came to Imam Ali (a.s.), his house was set on fire, and injustice was done to Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), and all the tragedies happened because of this. So, if we find the mourning for Imam Hussain (a.s.) so much, then was the attack on the house of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) and the tragedies that happened to her also such a big crime? Is it also mentioned in the elegies, poems, and supplications? To answer this, we have with us Janab Aakash Patel Sahab. Abbas Bhai, Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam. Please answer this, as people say that we claim that the attack on the house of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) was... The world should know that the burning of the door of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) and the attack on the house was a very big crime against the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and this grief should come out of the house. Pointing towards it, do not take it lightly, and that which was done, and that child who was... and was broken, pointing towards the attack, in this time, which was brought into the light, in 52453, this verse is present, and we see that in the supplication too, there is a mention of this attack, of this oppression. Now when... Let's go, it's getting very late. And if he says that I asked what happened, how did it come here? When he was brought to the judge, the judge asked, 'What is your crime?' This woman said, 'I was walking, my foot stumbled, and I... the one who was doing it... I had not even... for this, he did not... this... it becomes different, that I am very wrong with you, you... these friends, accept the problems from our side.' Not only that, they were giving... as a pension. This woman refused to take it. Now, this... and the woman was in great need of money, this... that none of them do... you become a trouble, and then how he provides the path for them, he works with ease, he is the seven... He works with ease, he is the seven... silver, golden, and put in his jail, and now... taking his friends, his companions, and he... this is also from my side, I have... the reward of the supplication, here you get to see that if anyone remembers the problems that happened to Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) and cries, and points towards those who oppressed them, then the Imam of the time comes to his aid. And if, God forbid, a big accident, if upon our greed, if any trouble comes upon us, then our Imam comes to save us. Friends, if we look, then all these problems, after hearing all these narrations, perhaps there will be no such person whose heart will not cry out for Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) and if after hearing this incident, these oppressions, after hearing from their own ears or reading with their own eyes, if someone does not understand, and from his heart, a curse for the oppressors of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) does not come out, then finally his... If this state of distress does not end, it eventually affects his mind. He has found the door of the people well. The departure of Muhsin (a.s.) from this world before even arriving in it. title: EP02 | Saqifa Ke Baad Masjid-un-Nabawi (s.a.w.a.) Mein Kya Hua | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture discusses the events immediately following the passing of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the gathering at Saqifa. It recounts an encounter witnessed by Janabe Salman al-Muhammadi involving a mysterious figure, identified by Imam Ali (a.s.) as Iblis, who celebrated the transition of leadership. The talk highlights the betrayal of the covenant of Wilayah and the subsequent warnings issued by Janabe Salman to the people of Medina regarding their abandonment of Imam Ali (a.s.).
content:
The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) asked Janabe Salman, 'Salman, do you know who that was?' Janabe Salman replied, 'No, but his words caused me great pain. It was as if he was happy about the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'That was Iblis, may Allah curse him.' When the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (a.s.), was busy with the funeral of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Janabe Salman al-Muhammadi (r.a.) came to him and informed him that the people had accomplished their task—meaning they had chosen their leader, and at that moment, that leader was on the pulpit of the Messenger. The people were not satisfied with helping him with just one hand, but all those people were... helping him with their right and left hands, meaning both hands. I saw a man leaning on a staff, with a deep scar between his eyes, saying to the leader, 'All praise is due to Allah who did not give me death and did not take me from this world until I saw you in this position. Extend your hand so I may help you.' The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) asked Janabe Salman, 'Salman, do you know who that was?' Janabe Salman replied, 'No, but his words caused me great pain. He was happy about the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). May Allah curse him.' Three days after this incident, Janabe Salman addressed the people of Medina and said, 'You have adopted the tradition of the Children of Israel. You have abandoned Ali (a.s.). Despite knowing everything about the virtues of Ali (a.s.), you have handed over this Wilayah to someone other than him. Since you have broken the covenant with Ali (a.s.), therefore, now upon you...' the punishment will fall. Do not expect anything from anyone. We will continue to talk to you on this subject, and we will not come to save you in times of trouble. We pray in the court of the Almighty that our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.)... [Music] [Laughter]

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 18 | Tafseer of Surah al-Qadr (97) - Part 1
excerpt: This lecture provides an introductory tafseer of Surah al-Qadr, emphasizing its significance in the Quran and the immense spiritual rewards associated with its recitation. The speaker highlights the Night of Qadr as a pivotal time for divine decree, forgiveness, and spiritual renewal. Drawing on traditions from the Imams, the session encourages believers to prepare diligently for this night to seek relief from worldly troubles and divine mercy.
content:
Masha'Allah. Allah is the Greatest. La ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar, wa lillahil hamd. All praise is due to Allah, and peace and blessings be upon the best of His creation, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his pure progeny. I am present in your service tonight to present the recitation and interpretation of Surah Al-Qadr. I have already discussed... I have already discussed Surah Al-Qadr. In the previous nights, Surah Al-Kafirun was mentioned, in which the Lord of the Worlds answered the question of the disbelievers that they had posed to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Lord of the Worlds answered it with emphasis. Respected viewers, Surah Al-Qadr is recited frequently, and almost all believers know that this Surah mentions the revelation of the Quran. It is emphasized in the traditions that one should recite it at least 1,000 times during the night of Qadr, as the reward is immense. Many of you might remember it. So, let us begin. In this Surah, Allah has given the message that He alone has revealed the Quran, no one else. 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylatil qadr'—indeed, We have revealed it. This Quran is not the speech of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.); it is My speech. It is this Surah in which Allah has stated that the Quran was revealed on the holy night of Ramadan. It was revealed on the holy night of Ramadan. The name of this Surah is Al-Qadr, and Qadr means destiny. It is indeed a night of greatness and majesty, in which the events, sustenance, and conditions of the entire year are decided and written by Allah. Regarding this night, it is said that the worship on this night is better than the worship of a thousand months. On this night, the angels and the Spirit descend with every command, and this peace and security remain until the break of dawn. 'Salamun hiya hatta matla'il fajr'—it remains until the dawn. This is the writing of the command. If we reflect on the virtues of reciting this Surah, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) said: 'Whoever recites Surah Al-Qadr in a loud voice, it is as if he has drawn his sword in the way of Allah, and whoever recites it silently...' recites it silently, it is like the example of a person who has fought in the way of Allah and is drenched in his own blood. That is, whoever recited it loudly, he has taken up the sword in the way of God, and whoever recited it silently, he gets the reward that one gets when one is drenched in blood while fighting in the way of God. And whoever recites this Surah 10 times, Allah forgives a thousand of his sins. This is an offer—if we call it an offer, it is not wrong. But we usually understand worldly offers and think about how to cash them in, while there is a lot of fraud in worldly offers. Companies say one thing and mean another, yet humans still get trapped in worldly offers. How many offers has God given? That if you do such-and-such work, you will get such-and-such reward. If you do such-and-such work, so many good deeds will be written for you. If you do such-and-such work, so many of your sins will be erased. If you recite such-and-such Surah, you will get such-and-such reward. 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim'—if you recite it in such a way, your sustenance will increase, your status will increase. But God's offers are not liked by every human. But God's offers are not liked by every human. There are only a few people who are motivated to take these offers and benefit from them. But look at how people are running towards worldly offers, and they are the ones who are in profit who are trying to cash in on the offers of the Almighty. Therefore, respected viewers, I request you to cash in on these offers. The night of Qadr has so many virtues: the name of the one who goes for Hajj is written, healing from death, life, and illness, and all the rewards of the year are kept in the house. But there are many people who keep crying—meaning they cry all year long that 'I am sick, I am not getting better, my sustenance is not increasing, I am not getting relief from pain, I am not getting relief from trouble, I am not finding peace.' They complain about all these things, but as soon as the night of Qadr comes, and it is said, 'Go and improve your destiny tonight, go and have your sustenance written well tonight,' they sleep peacefully. Respected viewers, this is an opportunity the Lord of the Worlds grants. Let us not let these moments pass. Let us try to perform these acts, as the reward is great and sins are forgiven. Besides that, there is another tradition regarding it. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'Whoever recites Surah Al-Qadr in his obligatory prayers, a caller calls out to him: 'Your past sins have been forgiven.' Now think about this: in ordinary days, if you recited Surah Al-Qadr in your obligatory prayers, the caller calls out that your past sins have been forgiven. So, if you go to the night of Qadr and recite Surah Al-Qadr in your prayers, how many sins will be forgiven? How many rewards will you get? What benefits will we get? Think about it. It is said that the caller calls out to the one who recites it in his obligatory prayers, 'Your past sins have been forgiven.' Now, start your life anew, just as a child who has just come into the world starts a new life. There are no sins in his record of deeds. He is like a person who has no sins left in his record. The Almighty has forgiven and erased those sins. Now it is up to the human how he spends the rest of his life. Therefore, this... How one spends their life, therefore, the recitation of this [Surah] has great rewards. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that whoever recites Surah al-Qadr will receive a reward equal to the person who fasts the entire month of Ramadan and spends the night of Qadr in the worship of Allah. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. [The speaker mentions] that even the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has said that whoever recites this Surah will receive a reward equal to the person who fasts the month of Ramadan and spends the night in the worship of Allah. This is the question, respected viewers: what is the importance of this Surah? What is the reward for its recitation? The Night of Qadr is coming, Insha'Allah, stay awake and utilize it. The Masumeen (a.s.) used to utilize it. Some of them would not even let their children sleep during the day, saying, 'Sleep during the day so that you can stay awake at night.' And at night, they would eat very little—they would say 'eat little' so that sleep would not overcome them, and they could stay awake to worship the Lord of the Worlds. Now think, if she [referring to Lady Fatima (s.a.w.a.)], for whom the universe was created, used to make such preparations for the Night of Qadr... ...if she used to make such preparations for the Night of Qadr, then we should also make preparations. We need it, we need forgiveness, we are sinners. She is not a sinner; she is the means for our sins to be forgiven, she is the means for the acceptance of our deeds. They used to make such preparations, and by making such preparations, they would attain [their status]. She used to tell us, 'Look, these nights have such greatness and virtues.' When we are making such preparations, you should also make them. Therefore, I request and hope that we all will stay awake on the Night of Qadr and pray. The entire world of humanity is troubled; the whole world is troubled by the Coronavirus. We will all pray on the Night of Qadr, and surely, through our collective prayers, the world will get relief from this Coronavirus too, Insha'Allah. We will continue this tomorrow. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Ziyaarat Ko Tark Karne Ke Nuqsaanaat | Arbaeen 2025
excerpt: This lecture highlights the spiritual and worldly consequences of abandoning the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Citing a narration from Imam Baqir (a.s.), the speaker explains that neglecting this pilgrimage can lead to a reduction in one's lifespan and sustenance. The talk emphasizes that this warning specifically applies to those who intentionally neglect the Ziyarat despite having the means to perform it. Ultimately, the lecture encourages believers to prioritize the Ziyarat to gain the intercession and testimony of the Ahlulbayt before Allah.
content:
Abandoning the Ziyarat (pilgrimage) decreases one's lifespan and sustenance. Mansur ibn Hazim says: We heard Imam Baqir (a.s.) saying, 'Whoever does not come for the Ziyarat of the grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.) for a year, Allah decreases one year from that person's lifespan. And if I were to say that there are people among you who will die 30 years before their appointed time of death, I would be telling the truth. And this is because you abandon the Ziyarat of Hussain (a.s.). Therefore, never abandon his Ziyarat. Allah will increase your lifespan and sustenance. And if you abandon his Ziyarat, Allah will decrease your lifespan and sustenance. Therefore, try to compete with one another in performing his Ziyarat, and never abandon it. Because Imam Hussain (a.s.) himself will testify to your Ziyarat in the presence of Allah, His Messenger (s.a.w.a.), Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). It is clear that in this Hadith, the Imam's (a.s.) intent is the intentional abandonment of Ziyarat. That is, this is for those who, despite having all the means available, do not give importance to the Ziyarat.

title: Shahadat e Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.) aur Imam Hasan (a.s.) - Baraahe Raast Najaf e Ashraf se
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical and spiritual implications of the succession crisis following the passing of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker emphasizes the Prophet's explicit directives regarding Imam Ali (a.s.) and highlights the hypocrisy of those who conspired against the Ahlulbayt. The talk concludes with condolences offered from Najaf al-Ashraf for the martyrdom of the Prophet and the Imams, while praying for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The issue of the Caliphate after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was a subject that divided the Muslims forever. The Muslims, who appeared united during the Prophet's lifetime—who were supposedly six [referring to a specific context]—opposed the Messenger on this issue in a way that they themselves did not realize that they were no longer believers but had become hypocrites. As it is stated in the 9th verse of Surah al-Baqarah: 'They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves, and they perceive it not.' In their greed for the Caliphate, they forgot that they were opposing the Truth, because the famous and well-known Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), which all Muslims accept, is: 'He is with Ali, and Ali is with the Truth.' O Lord, wherever Ali is... ...and wherever Ali is, O Lord, turn the Truth towards where Ali is. From this Hadith, it becomes clear that whoever, whenever, wherever, and in whatever manner opposed Ali (a.s.), they could not be on the Truth. If those people had only acted upon the will of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they would have known for themselves that opposing Ali (a.s.) is disobedience to God. In his final moments, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) willed to Ali (a.s.) while many people were present around him: 'By God, O Ali, most of these people will turn back after me; they will conspire against one another. And when you witness this, know that I will not be among you.' And by saying this, the Prophet condemned the will, saying: 'Ali is from my wives and my household; whoever separates from you has surely disobeyed me, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. I express my hatred towards those people, and you too should express your hatred towards them.' Ali (a.s.) said, 'Indeed, I have done so.' The Prophet said, 'O God, be a witness. Ali, these people will surely become rulers after me; they will commit crimes, and for this, in the darkness of the night...' ...they will commit crimes, and for this, they will conspire in the darkness of the night. And whoever conspires for this government in the darkness of the night, I express my hatred towards them. And it is for these people that this verse was revealed: '...they plot in the darkness of the night against what you are saying, and Allah records their plots made in the night.' So, it was under this conspiracy that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his household had to face the oppression of the entire Muslim community, about which the Master of the Martyrs, al-Mustafa (a.s.), stated in his famous Hadith: 'There is none among us who has not been martyred by the sword or by poison.' Today, in Najaf al-Ashraf, at the shrine of Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), we present our salutations on behalf of all of you and on behalf of everyone who receives this video, to the presence of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and we offer our condolences on the occasion of the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the Master of the Martyrs (a.s.). Finally... ...we offer our condolences. Finally, we pray that the Lord of the Worlds may hasten the reappearance of the last successor of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the ability to remain steadfast until our last breath, and grant us the guidance to remain attached to Ali (a.s.). Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

The Hadith 'Ali is with the Truth and the Truth is with Ali' serves as the ultimate criterion for faith.

The speaker emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in the love and obedience of Imam Ali (a.s.).

Ultimately, the lecture highlights the role of the Imams as the ultimate source of divine knowledge and invites further inquiry into how faith and reason coexist.

excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the concept of Shujaa’at (bravery) within the context of faith, emphasizing that true courage is rooted in sincerity and devotion to the Ahlulbayt. The speaker highlights the importance of time management and personality development, arguing that a believer's strength is tested by their consistency in private and public life. By reflecting on historical figures like Janabe Fizza and the sacrifice of Ali Akbar, the lecture illustrates that bravery is an act of spiritual resilience rather than physical force. Ultimately, it calls for a commitment to the principles of Wilayah and Bara'ah as the foundational pillars of a courageous life.
content:
Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking for permission to go to the battlefield. Akbar, do you know... [music]... do you know you are asking for permission to go to the battlefield? In this state of loneliness, how can I let you go? In this difficult time, how can I let you go? This moment is like the Day of Judgment, how can I let you go? You are asking for permission to go to the battlefield, Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? Akbar, do you know what you are asking for? You are asking for permission to go to the battlefield. You did not think, my dear Akbar, you are asking for permission to go to the battlefield. You are asking for permission to go to the battlefield. You are asking for permission to go to the battlefield. You are asking for permission to go to the battlefield [music]... Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un... Allah [music]... Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam [music]... [music] [praise] Allah Khwaja [music] uses every second. He uses every second because whether it is any person, whether they are a professional, a businessman, someone employed, or a student, anyone—a wise person is one who values their time. And a fool is one who does not value their time and wastes it on worldly, useless things. Like many youngsters are wasting time on video games and other worldly things as people do. So, their lives are just passing by, and their personalities are not developing at all. Whereas those who want to continue, they want their personalities to develop, to become strong personalities. That is why you see, those individuals were better because we are very far from them, so we do not recognize them, even from a worldly perspective, those who work very hard... even from a worldly perspective, those who work very hard and value their time, they do not waste it. But a fool never understands; they do not understand that the asset I have is only time. And no one knows when it will go, when it will be snatched away; no one knows. As you know, what is 'Akhir-uz-Zaman'? It is sudden death, the death of the youth. And today, you see every day some news comes that a young person died. So many, let's go, this one died, how did he die? These are all excuses. Allah ordains these things in this way. So, these personalities, personality development, and such personalities that are in front of the Imam of the time... and such personalities that are kept in front of the Imam of the time, we give examples. Generally, you may have heard, it is possible, when the event of Karbala happened, if we exclude the Bani Hashim and count the 72 who were martyred in Karbala, 18 were from Bani Hashim. Subtract 18 from 72, how many are left? 54 left. Now we ask you a question: in Makkah and Madinah, what was the total population? In Makkah and Madinah alone, there were 1 million people. There was a population of 1 million. Out of that 1 million, 54 people... From this, you can estimate how many people were ready. If you look at it in terms of percentage, it is 0.0054—put three zeros there. And that is why they asked the Imam, 'Mawla, when will your government be established?' The companions of our Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) will have specific characteristics. The Imam began to describe these traits: they will worship all night, roam like lions during the day, and eat whatever food they find—even if it is coarse food, as mentioned in the hadith, they will eat it. They will wear very simple clothes and sleep on stones; they will sleep on horse saddles. And Muslims will also be involved in administration. What is the reason for this? The reason is that the personality required is not there, the people required are not there. You will find many people like us who only talk. You can make them talk as much as you want—and Alhamdulillah, you are very ahead in this—they will talk so much. The topic we were discussing was 'Ikhlas' (sincerity). Only two or three points were left; let me finish them quickly, then we will move to a new topic. What is the reality of Ikhlas? What is the reality of sincerity? The first thing is that it is in the traditions that the Mawla says, 'Inna li kulli haqiqatin haqiqah' (Indeed, for everything there is a reality), and no servant can reach the reality of Ikhlas. This is the first sincerity; it is the reality of sincerity. It has an opposite. If you do more good deeds, there will be more opposition, and more people will criticize you. But if you are on the path of religion, you should never care about any criticism. No matter how many people are against you, no problem. Just try to stay on the truth. If you deviate from the truth, then there is a problem. They did not care about anyone; they did not care what anyone was saying. It was just about whether it was right or wrong; they would do the work and not care about anyone. Those who praise... the second thing is that a person's outward and inward should be the same. But before saying this, there was a companion of the eighth Imam, Abdur Rahman, who was very famous. He had a powerful personality. Just read his life history. One day he was sitting with the Imam, and his fellow villagers, people from Basra, his tribe, and his friends came to meet the Imam. He did not recognize them. He said, 'Sit here, go behind the curtain, and stay silent, completely silent.' They went behind. Then his villagers and tribesmen came and started talking. He said, 'Okay, okay, no problem, it's fine, we will talk.' As it happens, he explained to them, 'Yes, we will say this.' Now, when they left, Rajab came crying, 'Mawla, I am such a staunch Shia, and I look after you people so much, and these people said so many things and left, and you didn't say anything to them? I am such a strong Shia, I do this, I do that.' He thought, 'How much will I bow down until the bone of my forehead breaks?' And in private, when no one is watching, he commits as many sins as possible because no one is seeing. But he forgets that Allah is watching. As the Mawla was saying, 'Avoid disobeying Allah and committing sins in solitude, in private, because the One who is the Witness is also the Judge. He does not need any judge, and His way of taking testimony is very strange, as stated in the Quran.' The Quran says that Allah says—He gives the power of speech after a year. The same Allah has given us... The same Allah has given us the power of speech. He called us, 'Why do you say what you do not practice? Why do you do such things?' O servants of Allah, this is a very bad thing. You say things that you do not act upon. Or in another verse, in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 44, it is stated—please recite a Salawat. Are you foolish? Do you not understand? You are doing such things. The difference between hypocrisy and sincerity in a person is a lack of intellect. The Imam says, 'La ilaha illallah'—there is no difference in sincerity except for a lack of intellect. Why is this deficiency there? The Imam explains the reason: it is because he is keeping expectations from people, whereas he is not keeping expectations from Allah, who is the Giver of judgment. Who is the one who gives the reward? Allah. He is not doing it for Him. And the people, who are beggars themselves, who cannot do anything themselves... but before moving forward, look at this service, one thing repeatedly: in all these things, a person should not forget their faith, meaning Wilayah and Bara'ah. These are the two things that are the center. A question was asked: 'Is the number of angels greater, or the number of humans?' The Imam replied, 'By God, the number of angels in the heavens is greater than the particles of the earth. There is no place to put a foot in the sky, but everywhere there is an angel who is glorifying Allah.' They worship Allah in a way that no one can estimate. All the angels, but every one of these angels thinks that the path to being closest to Allah is one path, and what is that? Through the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and for those who love us... For those who love us, to befriend them, to express devotion to them—these are two things. And the third thing is that they keep sending curses upon our enemies. This is a very important thing. You will see in the Tafsir of Imam Hasan (a.s.), if you have read it—it was in 120 volumes, then it was lost in history; only one volume remains. In those 120 volumes, there were two characteristics of every Tafsir: first, almost every hadith had a connection to Wilayah and Bara'ah, especially Bara'ah. And second, under every verse, Imam Hasan (a.s.) narrated traditions from all the Masumeen (a.s.). And the Imam trained his students in this. History, history is telling you everything. We are not talking in the air. Under the umbrella of history, we Shias have often made Taqiyyah an excuse to abandon courage, bravery, and valor, and have become cowardly. Therefore, in personality development, a very important thing is that a believer is one who is brave. And that is why, you see, the best history we have passed through—look at Sheikh Mufid, look at the mention of the pen in this service—one percent of the population, those people used to look for insults, where did they run away? Those people used to look for excuses, asking where they ran off to, why they were reading this immediately. Brother, listen to a dream, they would immediately make one up and start a debate. 'Oh brother, I must have seen a dream, let's joke about it a little.' If anyone wants the source for this, they should refer to the book of Sheikh Murtaza Ansari regarding 'Risalat-e-Shadi'. You all know he was a jurist of the 13th century, and his title was 'Khatam-ul-Fuqaha' (Seal of the Jurists). No greater jurist has been born since his martyrdom and his passing until now. Ask any jurist, any Marja, any person who is learned, about him—he was so close to the Imam that when his students started interrupting him repeatedly, then Sheikh Murtaza Ansari... When a person's religion is in danger—if it were just about saving one's life, it wouldn't be for saving one's life, but for saving the religion. That is why it was said, 'Inna kum...' your religion is the top priority. Save the religion first. If it were just about saving one's life, why would so many companions give their lives? Did they not know the innocence? Did they not understand the 'Taqiyya' (dissimulation) of the Imam? Did they not understand the Imam's strategy? The women were afraid, those who were close to the courage, the people who were there, they were not afraid. Like Janabe Fizza, the daughter of the King, when the tyrant was shouting, I have heard that she said, 'May the government forgive you,' this is what she replied. The woman is with her and says, 'If anyone says that someone is superior to Ali (a.s.), he is lying. Ali (a.s.) is superior to Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Dawud,' and she started naming all the prophets. '...if you don't prove it right now, I will behead you. You prove to me that Ali (a.s.) is superior.' So Janabe Fizza started reading... but no one was ready to come, no one was ready to help, everyone was sitting at home. She used to go from house to house saying... Everyone was sitting at home, she used to go from house to house saying, 'What is this? Be on the side of truth, talk about Ali (a.s.).' Now you people say, 'We sat down, break the conversation a little, sit down, you are being biased.' Now, if someone does this publicly, the news of their words will reach others, right? So people told him, 'Sir, you are sitting here and this woman is doing this work, you are sitting here and she is doing all this there, talking about you.' 'Alright, call her.' She was called. Just... we are reading the whole Hadith, very well, speaking very quickly. 'Call her.' Allah... the Majlis in Bihar al-Anwar has recorded this Hadith. We will also give you the reference. It is Hadith number 13, and they didn't bring it from their own pockets; they quoted it from the book of Qutb al-Din al-Rawandi. 'Al-Fara'ij' is very famous. There were three scholars: Sadr al-Din, al-Rawandi, and the one whose nickname was Qutb al-Din, meaning the favorite of the religion. They quoted from his book. Allah has given you the reference, whoever wants it... I have given you the reference, whoever wants it should check. Volume 41, page 199, Hadith number 13. 'Tell me, do you know? Tell me, if it were permissible for women in Islam...' If it were permissible for women in Islam to teach men, then I would teach you. If you don't tell me today, I will kill you right now. You will have to accept my authority, you will have to.' In any matter, you see, in the mouth of every bird... In the mouth of every bird is a pomegranate seed, and it is putting it into the grave. As soon as they saw Maula-e-Kainat (Ali a.s.), the birds started speaking in their own language, which is the sentence of the Hadith, 'Raf-raf...' and whatever they said, they started answering in their language and said, 'I am doing it, Insha'Allah, wait, wait.' And then he stood at the grave and raised his hands towards the sky, 'O You who bring the dead to life!' And it is written in history that he lived until 41 Hijri. So this bravery... and who is the narrator of this whole Hadith? Janabe Salman was sitting near the King. Now when people came and said... Now when people came and said, 'Long live the King, wow, subhanAllah [praise]... talk about it,' then people kept saying, 'What about Khaybar?' Talk about it, then people kept saying, 'What about Khaybar and Khandaq?' People said it so much, it was said so much that often our Zakireen stopped reciting Khaybar and Khandaq. And you know what the result of that was? That women stopped giving birth to brave children. That is why our Zakireen always used to recite Khaybar and Khandaq so that children and youth would get courage. Never look at the numbers, that our numbers are small and theirs are large. That is a different topic, Insha'Allah, if Allah gives the opportunity, then that is a topic—the minority and majority one. Will not bow before the tyrant. Yes, then the ideology and I will fight it... And I will fight it, two... remain silent and tolerate a life of humiliation, be humiliated before the tyrant, and then... it has been rightly said, here... there are many incidents. All the Imam Hussain (a.s.) ones are not read. So today, the third thing is 'Talab' (seeking/demand), meaning when he shows his bravery, he tells for whom he is showing his bravery. Not for his own ego, not for his own self. That is why they used to come to the battlefield, someone would introduce themselves, 'If you don't recognize me, then recognize me,' they used to recite their 'Rajaz' (battle poetry), introduce themselves in hand-to-hand combat, just as you have heard that Maula-e-Kainat also used to... Otherwise, if Ali (a.s.) had kept striking, the very earth would have been severed. Who was standing before him in the battlefield? A man. He said, 'I am Uthman, are you some brave warrior?' Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)—yes, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)—and within a fraction of a second, he struck and severed both his legs. When both his legs were cut off, he saw him and began to plead, 'Ya Ali, forgive me, I will not do it again.' He began to plead, 'Ya Ali, forgive me, I will not do it again.' He turned his face away and walked back. So, the brave ones who were sitting inside, trembling, said, 'Ali, we are present here.' The brave ones who were sitting inside, who were not coming out, said, 'If you are brave, give me your sword. What is your advantage? It is your sword. While fighting, give me your sword.' Maula (a.s.) picked up his sword and threw it. They have a habit that when someone asks us for something... They have a habit that when someone asks us for something, they do not send them back empty-handed. Someone is fighting on the road, a car driver is fighting with another over a road rage incident—that is called hooliganism. Bravery is what happened when the circumstances were... The circumstances were such that I had no other option. My eyes were filled with thorns, and there was a bone stuck in my throat. I remained patient. What policy to adopt? Where? It was exactly like the Imamate of Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Imam Hasan (a.s.)... It was the Imamate of Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Imam Hasan (a.s.) did it and kept me with him. That is why as long as Muawiyah is alive, that peace treaty will remain in its place. It will remain in its place, and the Imam was among the people in this Medina. But when in 60 Hijri, they destroyed it... They destroyed it. These people destroyed it. Someone asked Imam Sajjad (a.s.) who is meant by 'Ali' in the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Imam Sajjad (a.s.) replied, 'It refers to Janabe Ali Akbar (a.s.).' Look, for any father, the hardest thing is to see his son go through various hardships; he will not be able to bear it, especially if he is a young man. He will not be able to bear it. How is the blood of a young man? But Janabe Ali Akbar (a.s.) could not bear it. Until, when everyone was martyred, he asked for permission from his mother. Laila looked at Ali Akbar from head to toe and said, 'Son, was it for this that I raised you?' Son, was it for this that I raised you? He said, 'Mother, if you do not say so, I will not go. But if my grandmother asks me on the Day of Judgment, who will answer?' She said, 'Go son, you have my permission.' Ali Akbar (a.s.) left. Maqtal says that I was watching that as soon as Ali Akbar (a.s.) wanted to leave, someone would hold his hem. Some lady would hold his hem. Ali Akbar (a.s.) would go back. There was an uproar. It is a big deal that a young man's funeral is leaving from a house. From a full house, Ali Akbar (a.s.) wants to leave, he goes back. Now, a very dangerous sentence here: if an elder had stopped him, they would have held his arm, but holding the hem means that 'O Ali Akbar, you are leaving, but keep us in mind.' Ali Akbar (a.s.) went. Now, when he was about to go, Hussain (a.s.) asked and prayed, 'Allahumma ishhad ala ha'ulail qawm' (O Allah, be a witness against this nation). O Lord, there is no one else. O Lord, a young man is going to fight against them who, in his creation, in his character, in his speech, in his gait, resembled Your Messenger the most. Whenever we longed to see Your Prophet, we would look at Ali Akbar (a.s.). Whenever we longed to see Ali Akbar (a.s.). Now, look at the beautiful, handsome young man who is going. Now, as he departed, he went a little distance and felt a sound. When he turned back, he saw his father with his hand on his grave. He said, 'Father, you had already bid me farewell.' 'Son, if you had children, you would know what it means to bid farewell to a young son.' Ali Akbar (a.s.) went. Ali Akbar (a.s.) went and fought, sent 200 soldiers to hell, and returned. Ali Akbar (a.s.) returned from the other side, and how did he return? Umm Laila was there, a mother's heart was fluttering. She said, 'Fizza, go and stand at the gate of the tent. See, if the color of the master's face changes, then tell me.' Fizza saw that the color of the master's face had changed. When the color of the master's face changes, then Hussain (a.s.) came. How did he remember? He said, 'Why is the color of your face changing?' He said, 'A wrestler has come to fight my son, and my son is hungry and thirsty for three days.' So, it was a mother's heart. Then what did the ladies do? The ladies formed a circle and said, 'I pray, so that along with Amin, my Ali Akbar, who resembles Yusuf, may return.' Now here... My Ali Akbar (a.s.) returned. But in what condition did he come? He was covered in blood from wounds, blood was flowing. And once, the narrator says a sentence that will break your heart: 'O father, these are the sweet melodies of the thirsty.' Now he cannot even lift his sword. [Music] 'Is there any water?' Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Son, this is not your time. It is the status of the thirsty. Give me your tongue.' As soon as Ali Akbar (a.s.) gave his tongue, Hussain (a.s.) put it in his mouth. 'Father, your tongue is drier than mine, there are thorns in your tongue.' 'Go son, your grandfather will quench your thirst from the Kauthar.' Ali Akbar (a.s.) went, fighting, and once a wretched man struck such a spear that Ali Akbar (a.s.) fell from his horse. Maqtal says they surrounded Ali Akbar (a.s.) and after surrounding him, they started to tear Ali Akbar (a.s.) into pieces with their swords. Father, my last salaam to you. Hussain (a.s.) came like Ali Akbar (a.s.). Now, when he came, he wanted to pull out the spearhead. The spearhead was stuck. 'Ya Ali, Ya Ali.' He pulled it out, and a fountain of blood erupted. Ali Akbar (a.s.) passed away from this world. He recited a dirge, 'O my Ali Akbar, the world after you is ruined.' [Music] 'O my dream, such a tragedy in the world, we are here, Ali Akbar, you have left us in this world of grief.' The same painful grief, your father is lying in the midst of the enemies. [Music] May He remove the worries of those who are worried. May He grant us the intercession of the Ahlulbayt. May He grant what He grants, may Allah grant what He provides, may He protect those who are working, and may He protect us. May He honor us in this world with the Ziyarat of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and say it three times [Music].

title: Anjuman-e-Yaadgaar-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) [Bandra]
excerpt: This brief lecture segment focuses on a heartfelt supplication addressed to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The speaker expresses a deep longing for spiritual proximity to Sayyeda Zahra (s.a.). It reflects on the historical and emotional connection between the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.w.) and his daughter, Lady Fatima (s.a.).
content:

A prayer for spiritual closeness to the Ahlulbayt.

title: Is Dua Iftitaah Unreliable & Too Negative? | Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi
excerpt: Sayed Mahdi al-Modarresi addresses contemporary criticisms labeling Dua Iftitaah as overly negative or unreliable. He argues that these critiques often stem from a misunderstanding of the prophetic tradition of expressing grief and complaining to Allah, which serves as a vital psychological and spiritual tool. The lecture emphasizes the authenticity of Shia supplications, the importance of scholarly transmission, and the necessity of spiritual filtration in preparing for the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi.

content:

title: Kya Quran Kaafi Hai? Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) Ka Jawaab | From KULL-E-IMAAN (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 2023 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture explores the necessity of an authoritative interpreter for the Holy Quran, referencing a profound dialogue involving Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.). The Imam clarifies that while the Quran is sufficient, it requires a divinely appointed commentator to be fully understood. He explains that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) entrusted this interpretive knowledge to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and directed the Ummah to seek guidance from him.
content:
The narrator then asked the Imam, the questioner asked exactly this: Is the Quran not enough? The Mawla, Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.), says, "Bala" (Yes), indeed it is enough, "In wujida lahu mufassiran" (if a commentator for it is present). Subhan Allah. Meaning, if someone to interpret the Quran is present, someone to explain the Quran, then the Quran is enough. Then he asked again, did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) not explain the interpretation of the Quran? Because often people say that yes, the Quran is enough because the Messenger of Allah explained the entire Quran. To this, Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) says, "Bala" (Yes), indeed the Prophet explained the interpretation of the Quran, "Fassarahu li-rajulin" (but only to one man). Subhan Allah. He explained the interpretation of the Quran to only one man, and what did he do for the rest of the Ummah? "Wa fassara lil-ummati sha'na dhalikar-rajul" (and for the rest of the Ummah, he explained the virtue and status of that one man). Indeed. So that when people need the interpretation of the Quran, they should go to that one man, and who is he? "Wa huwa Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)."
The Quran is sufficient for guidance only if an authorized interpreter is present.
Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) confirmed that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) taught the Quran's interpretation to one specific person.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explained the status and virtue of this individual to the rest of the Ummah.
The designated interpreter of the Quran is Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).
The Ummah is directed to seek the true meaning of the Quran through the Ahlulbayt.
The Prophet's teaching ensured that the Ummah would know where to turn for divine guidance.

title: EP#7: Eid-e-Ghadeer Kaise Manayein
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound religious and historical significance of Eid-e-Ghadir, emphasizing its status as one of the most important celebrations in Islam. It details various recommended acts of worship, including fasting, reciting Salawat, and performing Ziyarat of Imam Ali (a.s.) to strengthen one's connection with the Ahlulbayt. The session also highlights social traditions such as the bond of brotherhood, feeding believers, and dressing up to honor the day's spiritual importance.
content:
May Allah grant us the light of God... O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I wholeheartedly wish you all a very happy Eid, and I pray that the one who solves difficulties, Ali (a.s.), may God write him as the minister, and may He write the oppressor as the one who is oppressed. May the Mahdi be with us, may the Ziyarat of Ali be before us. O Lord, write such a destiny for me. O Lord, write such a destiny for me. I beseech You by the sake of this blessed day, by the sake of Zahra (s.a.), in the joy of this Eid. By the sake of this joy of Eid, our greatest joy is the reappearance (Zuhur) of Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.), and by his intercession, may He remove all our sorrows and griefs. May He also fulfill the needs of every lover of Ali, every Momin. May He keep us all safe from all calamities and trials on this blessed day. So let us all together offer our congratulations for this blessed day to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Imams (a.s.), and all the Prophets (a.s.) with a beautiful Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Now, before we start our episode, let me remind you that the names of the winners of our past episodes are available on all our social media channels, i.e., Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. You can go and see them there. Also, the top scorer playlist is there, which includes all those people who participated in the quizzes of all episodes, gave correct answers to all questions, and answered as quickly as possible. There is a list of all those people, and you can see their names in that list. And with this, let us start our episode, and the topic for today is: Let us start the episode, and the topic for today is: How should we celebrate Eid-e-Ghadir? The question is how we should celebrate it. We celebrate many things; we celebrated Eid-ul-Adha, we celebrated Eid-ul-Fitr, and for many years we have been celebrating all these things. So how should we celebrate Eid-e-Ghadir? Is it just about wearing new clothes or eating good food? All that happens, but we want to turn towards the traditions (Riwayat) and see if the Masumeen (a.s.) have mentioned any specific acts or special deeds for the day of Ghadir that we should perform. For more on this, we have our brother Abbas Naqvi with us. Brother Abbas, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I offer you congratulations on this blessed day. You are very welcome. As you mentioned, how should we celebrate it? What should we do? Please tell us some things that have been pointed towards in the traditions. As for the things pointed towards in the traditions, the scholars have mentioned them in books. Along with that, there are some subtle points that we get in the light of traditions. Insha'Allah, we will try to point our viewers towards that. Let me say that the elders know these things better, but this is an effort from our side for our young friends to try and convey this. Brother Abbas, first of all, the tradition we would like to mention, Sheikh Muhammad bin Yaqub al-Kulayni has mentioned it in his famous book 'Al-Kafi'. The chain of narrators reaches Imam Sadiq (a.s.). The person who asked this question to the Imam was Hassan bin Rashid. He asked the Imam, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, is there any other Eid for Muslims besides these two Eids, i.e., Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha? Is there any other Eid for Muslims?' Is there any other Eid for Muslims? In response, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'Yes, there is another Eid, and it is greater and more honorable than them.' I asked, 'Which day is that, which is more honorable and greater?' Imam Sadiq (a.s.) replied, 'It is the day when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appointed Ali (a.s.) as a leader for all people, introducing him to the people.' I asked, 'May my life be sacrificed for you, what should one do if they reach that day?' Imam Sadiq (a.s.) mentioned three acts in response that we should do. In response, three acts were mentioned that we should do. First, as much as possible, send abundant Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And the third thing that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) emphasized is to express Tabarra (disassociation) from those who oppressed the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). In this Hadith, we saw that the Imam is telling us that on the day of Ghadir, we should do three things: first, we should fast; second, as much as possible, we should send Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad; and third, we should express Tabarra from those who oppressed the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). So let us see what else we find that we should do on the day of Ghadir, and it has been emphasized. It has been emphasized, and let me say that in this same tradition, the Imam further mentions that this was the day when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded his companions to congratulate him. The Imam says that fasting on this day is equivalent to the reward of 360 months of fasting. So, we should try as much as possible to observe this fast. The second tradition that has been mentioned is by Allama Majlisi in his book 'Bihar al-Anwar', narrated from Imam Reza (a.s.). This is a very old Hadith in which the acts have been collected, and the virtues and greatness of the day of Ghadir have been described. Imam Reza (a.s.) has also mentioned many other virtues and some specific acts for this day. Some acts for this day. So, Insha'Allah, we have tried to collect these acts. In the light of this Hadith, the first thing we find is that the name itself tells us, 'Yawm-e-Tahniyat' (Day of Congratulations). The Imam (a.s.) mentions that on this day, we should send abundant Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The second thing the Imam emphasized is that this is a day of 'Tawbah' (repentance). On this day, you should repent from major sins and keep yourself away from sins. So, one should recite more Salawat and also stay away from sins. The third name the Imam gives for this day is 'Yawm-e-Ibadat' (Day of Worship). This means that a Shia should try to engage himself in worship as much as possible. Along with this, there is another thing that has been emphasized, which is... It is the day of Ghadir, and what a day it is! It is the day when we are required to provide Iftar for those who are fasting. Imam (a.s.) describes the reward for this, stating that if we provide Iftar for those fasting, the reward is immense. The Imam (a.s.) says that whoever provides Iftar for a Momin (believer), it is as if he has fed ten lakh prophets, ten lakh truthful ones (Siddiqin), and ten lakh martyrs. The Imam (a.s.) repeated this, emphasizing that providing Iftar for even one fasting person is equivalent to providing Iftar for ten lakh people. This is the magnitude of the reward, and we should encourage others to do the same. We should encourage others to do the same. Imam (a.s.) says that when a Momin meets his brother Momin on this day, he should say: 'Alhamdulillahil-ladhi ja'alana minal-mutamassikina bi-wilayati Amiril-Mu'minin wa A'immatina (a.s.)' (All praise is to Allah who kept us attached to the Wilayat and Imamate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and our Imams (a.s.)). This is how we should greet each other. Furthermore, Imam (a.s.) says that this is a day of smiling; when we meet a Momin, we should look at them with a smile and happiness. Imam (a.s.) says that whoever meets his believing brother with a smile, Allah will look at him with mercy on the Day of Judgment. And for him, He will fulfill a thousand needs and build a palace of pearls for him in Paradise. This shows the great importance of the day of Ghadir and how much we should value it. Imam (a.s.) guides us on how to celebrate this day. Celebration involves dressing up. Usually, people do this, but sometimes we forget. The Imam (a.s.) says this is a day to adorn oneself. Imam (a.s.) says... Imam (a.s.) says that whoever adorns himself on this day, Allah will forgive all his sins, whether small or large. Just as we prepare for Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha, we should prepare even more for this day. If we do this, Allah will forgive all our sins. Not only that, Imam (a.s.) further says that if someone adorns himself, Allah sends angels to him. The task of these angels is to write good deeds for him or to increase his status, and they continue to do this until the following year. But if you cannot do this, then at least prepare for tomorrow. Prepare yourself, and in this way, pass this tradition on to the coming generations so that children also realize that this is the greatest Eid. The greatest thing is that this Eid belongs to the followers of Islam, the followers of Ali (a.s.). When they go out prepared, the world will know that this is the day of the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.). Then the Imam (a.s.) mentions the invitation of a Momin. Imam (a.s.) says that whoever invites a Momin to a meal on this day, it is as if he has invited all the Prophets and Siddiqin. Meeting a Momin on this day is like meeting the Prophets. Whoever meets a Momin, Allah will illuminate his grave and make his face radiant. 70,000 angels will visit him in his grave and give him the glad tidings of Paradise. This is why we should try to meet as many Momineen as possible. If we meet them with a smile, we get all these rewards. Let us see what else we should do on the day of Ghadir. It becomes a very important duty for us to visit Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and there are many traditions regarding this. Regarding the visit, the Imam (a.s.) says that it is part of the Ziyarat that wherever you are, you should go to the Ziyarat of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). If we get the opportunity, we should try to be present there on this day. But if we cannot be present, we should at least perform the Ziyarat from where we are. There are two types of Ziyarat mentioned for this day, and besides these, there is the very famous Ziyarat Aminullah that we can recite. We should remain mindful of this. Also, there are specific prayers that should be recited on this day. This day of Ghadir was a great day because it was on this day that Prophet Musa (a.s.) triumphed over the magicians. Allah saved Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) from the fire of Namrud. On this day, Prophet Musa (a.s.) appointed his successor, Prophet Isa (a.s.) appointed his successor, and Prophet Sulaiman (a.s.) appointed his successor. On this day, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) as his successor and vicegerent. It is also mentioned that this is the day when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) established the bond of brotherhood between the believers. Therefore, it is highly recommended that believers hold each other's hands and say: 'I consider you my brother for the sake of Allah, I befriend you for the sake of Allah, I speak to you for the sake of Allah, and I promise Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, His prophets, and the infallible Imams (a.s.)...' And I promise the infallible Imams (a.s.) that if I am among the people of Paradise, I will not enter it until you are with me. This is the bond of brotherhood. In response, the other brother should say: 'I accept.' This is something we should try to do on the day of Ghadir. Finally, the day of Ghadir remains incomplete without the remembrance of the Imam of our time. We should present ourselves in the court of the Imam of our time, and the best way to do this, which has been emphasized, is the recitation of the Ziyarat of the Imam. We should present ourselves in the court of the Imam (a.s.) through this. He is our leader, our hope, and our vision. The best of the ladies, Sayyeda Fatima (s.a.), is our intercessor. In this chaotic environment, we should not be left to ourselves. May Allah grant us the ability to remain attached to the mantle of the Imams (a.s.) and to lead our lives according to their guidance. It is very good that you have told our viewers about these deeds. We are sure that you all perform these deeds, and perhaps even more. We wanted to cover these deeds in this episode so that the children and youth are aware of them. We will try our best to perform these deeds this year, Insha'Allah, and we pray that Allah grants us the ability to perform these deeds. We pray that Allah (Azza wa Jal) grants us the ability to perform these deeds and fulfill all our duties, and grants us the ability to pray for the reappearance of the Imam of our time (a.t.f.s.) everywhere. Come, before we go, there is a special news and an important announcement for you. This announcement is special and important because we have been told that if this announcement is not made, then nothing happens in this episode. It is very important for you, because if you do not hear this announcement, you will miss out on a lot. Since tomorrow is Friday, a blessed day, the announcement made on this day is special, and the opportunity we have received is special. So we thought, why not try to do something special? The special thing is that in the quiz that will be presented to you tomorrow, every person who participates in this quiz and answers all the questions correctly will have a chance to go to Iran. Yes, one lucky winner among them, who will be selected through our computerized lucky draw, will get a pilgrimage to Iran. We hope that all of you will definitely participate in this. All of you must participate in this, and those who are listening to us, it is necessary for them to convey this news to others. If someone has not seen this video yet, please do not miss this episode at all, because this is a special episode. I have brought a special matter for you, so do watch it. And those who are not present, who are not watching this video, convey this news to your family members, relatives, and friends so that they can also watch this special episode tomorrow and participate in it so that everyone can get a chance to go to Iraq. So let us end this episode with this, but before ending, let me remind you once again that the link for this episode's quiz will be attached with this episode. So click on that link immediately and participate in today's episode quiz. Until then, goodbye, may Allah help us.

title: EP03 | Bait-e-Tatheer Par Hamle Ki Pehli Dhamki | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical challenges faced by Imam Ali (a.s.) following the passing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), specifically focusing on his commitment to compiling the Holy Quran. The speaker highlights the pressure Imam Ali faced from those who sought to interfere with his work and his steadfast refusal to compromise his mission. The talk emphasizes the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt as the ultimate source of guidance for believers.
content:
The first attempt was when Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) brought the Holy Quran to the mosque to be compiled so that it could be better understood. He was told that if he did not do it the way they wanted, they would draw their swords against him. When the Master of the Universe, Imam Ali (a.s.), was asked to explain, he flatly refused and said, 'I am busy, and I have vowed that except for prayer, I will not put my cloak on my shoulders until the compilation and collection of the Holy Quran is complete.' I wonder what kind of Muslims they were who wanted to trade their faith for the faith of the Imam and their hatred for the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) for their own souls. But at that time, the protection of the Holy Quran was the most important thing. That is why when the Master of the Universe (a.s.) refused to discuss the chosen Caliph in Saqifah, they prepared for a second attack. O Allah, we pray in Your court that we may remain attached to Your Prophet's progeny until the last moment, that is, the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). That is, the Quran and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the ability to remain attached to whom is guidance, and the final successor and the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
