title: Muharram 1442 Urdu Majlis #05: Sakhaawat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound Islamic concept of Sakhawat (generosity) as a fundamental pillar of faith and a defining trait of the Ahlulbayt. He emphasizes that true generosity is rooted in absolute certainty in Allah's provision and manifests as selflessness, whether through wealth or the ultimate sacrifice of life. The discourse highlights how the companions of Imam Husayn and the Ahlulbayt exemplified this virtue, contrasting it with the spiritual dangers of stinginess and hoarding. Ultimately, the lecture serves as a guide for believers to align their spending and personal conduct with the ethics of divine stewardship.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and salute him with a worthy salutation. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Abi Talib. Peace be upon you, O Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.). Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Husayn ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Husayn. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ja'far ibn Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Musa ibn Ja'far. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Musa. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Hujjat ibn al-Hasan (a.t.f.s.). Peace be upon you, O Husayn ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Abi Talib. Peace be upon you, O Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.). Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Husayn ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Husayn. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ja'far ibn Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Musa ibn Ja'far. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Musa. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Hujjat ibn al-Hasan (a.t.f.s.). Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Abi Talib. Peace be upon you, O Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.). Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Husayn ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Husayn. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ja'far ibn Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Musa ibn Ja'far. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Musa. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Muhammad. Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali. Peace be upon you, O Hujjat ibn al-Hasan (a.t.f.s.). Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance. 500 yards rose and the house was destroyed. Mother, one solid root of life, this house of love, this will be the house of Shabbir (a.s.). After the prayer, there is sorrow, tears, and the saints and peers. Who will ask? The heart is full of pain. Junayd Jamshed, the auspicious time, where the house is destroyed. At least in this, there is no peace for a dying person. Yes, choose if the whole world is destroyed. Like this, the house of love, after the father, Harikishan, from where it comes, I am for you, in my reference, from the special evening, I am coming. Well, the common man is not like this. My memory, the house of the master, is destroyed. The house is destroyed. The house of the master is destroyed. Keep your heart in a shadow like this. Today also, waiting, break your heart. I will handle it. In this world, someone else is sitting in the palace. It will come, the word, even then, in the flesh, after that, everything will be destroyed. The house of love, this is it. In front of you, [music] the most unique, obvious, the master, I am meeting you, the father of the topic has already happened. I am meeting you, the father of the topic has already happened. A smile on the face, be careful. This is it, everything will be destroyed. The house of love, this is it. The bodies are like, as if they are suffering, taking life. I am in despair, looking at the side, and on one side, this is it. When it rises, the Nawab's village, after that, everything will be destroyed. After that, the house of love, after the pain, keep your idol, keep your face, new. After the pain, keep your idol, keep your face, new. How will you write the last statement of sorrows? Everything will be destroyed. The house of love, the father of Shabbir. I said, yes, look here, here, move. Whatever happens, we will follow the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Following behind, saying this, he will go. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. Some time, take your father's old age with you. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. If you fall like this, the world will change. Who will we lean on when the mother dies? We will save you, we will save you, take your father with you, Ali Akbar. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. If the mother is sick and you are going, you are taking my life with you. How will I read this, how will I read this, this true golden... How will I read this, this true golden, Ali Akbar. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. My heart will go, my name will be destroyed. Do not go far away in your heart, my son. Now I cannot even walk, Ali Akbar. Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. If you had felt the pain like me, if you had been in my place, if you had been someone else's, if you had been someone's son, Ali Akbar. [Music] Turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar. And no more youth, no more home... And no more youth, no more home. When you go, the condition is that Ali's pocket is empty. Like Ali Akbar, turn around and look at me, Ali Akbar... And yes, the number one, the most wise. Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds. Peace be upon the children, the children of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Peace be upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his family. May Allah curse the oppressors, and may He punish them. May Allah's peace be upon the Imam of the Time. And he is the one who will take revenge. And he is my voice, he is my voice. Peace be upon the Master, Syed-e-Sajjad, Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.). Peace be upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Rawat Syed Hussain, may peace be upon him, was the one who was present... why? Because what are the qualities and characteristics that should be in a Shia? As the martyr Shahzada said about his companions, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said with anger, 'O Hussain, you will be martyred in this land, and with you, your group...' These are such issues that even if iron were to be placed upon them, it would have no effect. Is this the quality of Hussain's companions? What should be the qualities of a companion? These are the qualities that should show that yes, these are the Shias of Ahlulbayt, these are the lovers of the family of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). One quality that has been highly emphasized, and One quality that has been highly emphasized, and we cannot say this, but when it is mentioned... and that quality is 'Sakhawat' (generosity), and in contrast to this is 'Bukhul' (stinginess). There is a narration that a stingy person cannot be a lover of the Ahlulbayt. If he is a lover, then this quality will be found in him. So, when someone asked about all the qualities of a Shia, the first quality the Imam (a.s.) mentioned was, 'They are very generous with their brothers.' This is a constant, continuous giving. It is not just being generous; it is not about what is in front of them, but rather, as I told you about the companions, look at what the Imam (a.s.) says... And the Imam (a.s.) says that generosity is the morality of the Prophets. It is the trait of the Prophets. It is the trait that is the pillar of faith. If there is no generosity, if there is no 'Sakhawat', then the building of faith cannot stand. No one can be a believer unless they have this quality. And the second thing he mentioned is that he will never be stingy. And he explains the reason: when the Imam (a.s.) used to give something, he would give it in such a way, he would speak in such a way, that a person would naturally accept it from the bottom of their heart. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'The generous person is close to Allah.' This is because he has 100% certainty in Allah, in the Day of Judgment, in Allah's promise, in Allah's sustenance, and in Allah's support. He has 100% certainty that the Provider is Allah. He has 100% certainty that if he gives, the return will come. Just as if you know that if you invest in this company, you will get a return, if you put money into this business, you will get a profit—there is no chance of it failing. So, he is generous because he has certainty that the return will come from Allah. There is no chance it will be lost. Therefore, he is generous; he will not let anyone go empty-handed. No one will go empty-handed from his door, even if it is his enemy. This is the 'Yaqeen' (certainty) of the generous. Generosity is the trait of those with great intentions. Generosity is the trait of those with great intentions; it is not the work of small-minded people. A stingy person will never be generous; he will always think that if I give this, my money will be finished, my wealth will be gone. He does not understand that the One who gave it is Allah. He does not know that the Provider is Allah. This is our Imam's (a.s.) statement: 'Generosity is a ray of the sun of certainty.' It is a ray of certainty. And the one who has certainty in Allah, how can he be stingy? If you find a similar sentence, let me know. No one can say such a sentence. Look at the Imam's (a.s.) statement: 'And the one who has the recognition (Ma'rifat) of where he is spending, he will never think about why he gave it.' It will not even cross his mind. He has certainty; he has the Ma'rifat of the purpose. He gave it in the way of Allah, and it is in the way of Allah. That is why those people were sacrificing themselves for the Imam (a.s.). What sacrifices were they making? They were sacrificing their lives, their... They were sacrificing their lives, their children. There can be no greater sacrifice than this. And when it comes to one's own life, that is the greatest sacrifice, and then their children. They were ready to sacrifice everything. The reason was... and we are not talking about the companions of the past, we are talking about the companions of the Imam (a.s.). When the commander of the army of Sham arrested the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), including those whose graves are in Syria, he said, 'Now there is still a chance, curse Ali (a.s.) and accept the leadership of the Umayyads, and you will be saved. Your life will be saved, your children's lives will be saved, your young son's life will be saved.' So, what did the companion answer? And look at the character of the one who has 'Royal Blood' (noble lineage)—only he will be generous. The one who is base will never be generous. Only he will be generous. The one who is base will never be generous. Look at his companions, like Hatim Tai's companions. What did he say? 'You do your work, and let me do mine.' If it were us, we might have compromised. He addressed him like this: 'You do your work, and we will do ours.' And then, when it came to martyrdom, he did not say, 'Okay, kill my son first so that I don't have to see him die.' These companions were completely drowned in the love of the Imam (a.s.). They were not ordinary people of that time. This is one example; I will give you another example. Those who were in the love of the Imam (a.s.), they were noble. When the Imam (a.s.) gave them the responsibility of distributing money, they were the ones who held the money... They were the ones who held the money, so the register was with them. The ruler ordered them to be whipped, but it made no difference. They fulfilled their duty completely. They were whipped, but they did not betray the trust. This is the state of a minister of the Imam (a.s.). The biggest test for any wealthy person is that they might lose their wealth. But they were ready to sacrifice everything. They did not waver for even a second. They did not hesitate for a second. Everything was gone, and when a friend came, he said, 'These are your two dirhams that I was keeping for you.' And when a friend came, he said, 'These are your two dirhams that I was keeping for you.' He said, 'I don't need them now, keep them.' And he saw that the companion was in such a state that he needed them as much as he needed them today. And this is not the only example; there are many examples in history. Like the one known as Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari. You have heard the names of the companions so that you can recognize them. Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari was a man of great status. He was often put in jail. He was put in jail, why? Because he was a Shia. But he never stepped back. Going to jail was acceptable to him, but he never stepped back from the Wilayah. Therefore, the Imam (a.s.) says that a Shia is close to the people, he is generous, and he is far from the world. He says that a Shia is close to the people, he is generous, and he is far from the world. He is close to Allah because Allah likes him. Why is he close to the people? Because he likes to give. You yourself tell me, you yourself decide, do you like a generous person or a stingy person? No wise person would say they like a stingy person. Everyone likes a generous person. That is why in the narrations, it is said that in every age, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Allah has chosen Islam for you.' Allah has selected Islam for you as a religion. So, when you are a Muslim, be the best Muslim. How can you be the best Muslim? Look, when the word 'Islam' is used, it has two meanings. Remember this, I tell the children this so that if they ever read the hadiths in the future, it should be clear to them that... If it is read, it should be clear to them that it is submerged in people. This word 'Muslim' comes in two meanings: one is its product meaning, and the other is not in its waves. What is the broader meaning? Whether the one who recites the Shahada is an uneducated Muslim, or whether it is MLA Arif Aqueel or not, how should it be awarded? The significance is that he is a Muslim, he is not a non-Muslim, he is a Muslim. I am giving the meaning, its product meaning is one, and another meaning is that a Muslim is one who has completely submitted to Allah, His Messenger, and the path of Allah. 'Al-Islam' is the name of submission, and 'Iman' is the name of belief. Therefore, a Muslim is one who is completely submissive. If there is any doubt anywhere, then anyway, this is for watching. This is the word 'Islam' in the Quran, 'Islam' is not just a word, it is heard in the Quran, '...wa la tamutunna illa wa antum muslimun' (and do not die except as Muslims). So, Islam is the name of your submission to Allah, He has... Your heart is with Allah, He has made you a Muslim, so fulfill your duty. There are two ways for this: one is the way of submission, and the second is good character. Allah has named your Islam, so be a Muslim in whom generosity is found, and in whom good character is found. This is the definition of a Muslim, this is the definition of a Shia, this is the definition of a follower. What a generous person is, understand that too. What is meant by 'Sakhi' (generous)? What is its root? How should it be? It is called... its root in Arabic is from 'Sakhawat', 'Sakhawat' means, just like in grammar 'Faa'il' (doer), it means a person who gives what he has, and becomes ten times greater by giving it. I have given it for the sake of Allah, this is what is called 'Sakhi'. There is no worry in it, that I gave it and it is gone. No, just as the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) teach, only that person will be a Muslim in whom generosity is found, and in whom generosity is not found, he will not be a Muslim. He cannot be, he cannot be a Shia. This is the second point. This cannot be shared, this is another time, this will never be evening, and in the opinion of Ali, and in the opinion of heart disease, never think, never have courage, never think. And yes, you should always be careful, it remains very low, you have to do everything. Now, hundreds of stories, not just one, hundreds of people have decided that, look, the example is clear, the example is everywhere. These 15-20 years, they spent in His (a.s.) path. A time came when their financial condition became so bad that they had nothing left to spend. So how to do it? There are many such examples that they wept, first they sought, first they helped the needy. So never... in the path of the Imam, never stop. Why spend on this? Why spend on that? This is foolishness. They do not understand what this thing is. If they had thought a little, they would never talk like this. Leave the first point for a while, let it go. You just read the hadiths in which there is a reward for feeding others. Feeding a believer has so much reward that... The reward for feeding is so much that... you will be surprised that there are still some people, and there were people in the past as well, about whom we have heard that, as you know, the great people like Zulfiqar, they used to eat outside. The dining spread (dastarkhwan) would be laid out, and the food would be served. How many people would eat? We have seen with our own eyes that the dining spread was so large, and after the food was served, anyone walking on the road would come and sit, eat, and leave. We even saw that the host was not even greeting them, not even saying goodbye, not even knowing them. They would come, sit at the dining spread, eat, and leave. We had heard about them, then we saw it ourselves, we witnessed it. It was a wonder; people would come, eat, and leave. There is so much reward and so much blessing in this that no one can imagine. This is just about feeding people. Now, if this spending is in the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then how much does the reward increase? I mean, those personalities for whom the universe was created, Allah created the whole world for the sake of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If... If we spend for them, and everything is theirs—we have nothing, everything is theirs—then whatever we have received, it is not our own. So, if we spend in their path, and listen to this, this is a very important sentence: if anyone wants the reward, they can give it. There is no spending better than the spending that is done in the path of Imam Hussain (a.s.). In this, one should never be stingy, never. People say, 'Why? Build hospitals, build schools.' Yes, build hospitals, build schools, these are other things, but not from the budget of Imam Hussain (a.s.), use your own budget. I have said this many times, but this is very important. Never let anything become an obstacle in the path of Imam Hussain (a.s.), otherwise, neither the school will be built nor anything else will happen. And even if a school is built, remember this, if a school or college is built, other people will also benefit from it and go their own way; it will not provide any benefit to the Imam's cause. Salawat ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. If someone in the world... If someone wants to become a leader in this world, what is the way? One must be generous (sakhi). Without generosity, one can never lead people, nor can one ever become a leader. To be a leader, to lead, being generous is essential. Give as much as you can from whatever you have. That is why it is said, 'Man jada, sada.' You will not find such a philosophy or such a concept in the entire world, in any other school of thought. You won't find these two words. 'Man jada, sada'—whoever gives, becomes a leader. That is the concept given by the Ma'sum (a.s.). Whoever gives will have the same spirit, and only they will become a leader. And one who cannot be generous to people can never be a leader. And why? Because these are the qualities—these two things—that matter. Now look, these things being said are not easily understood by you or me. These are words of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), but we must accept them because they are the truth. Listen to how strange this is. They say, 'As-sakha wal-shaja'—two things: generosity and bravery. Generosity, meaning bravery—these are both natural instincts that the Almighty places in the hearts of those He loves. He does not give them to everyone. Generosity and bravery, and then He tests them with these two. He gives them, and then He tests them. These are natural instincts that the Almighty places in the hearts of those He loves. He does not give them to everyone. Generosity and bravery, and then He tests them with these two. Now, let me give you an example. This is about the grandson of Hatim Tai. You know the story of Hatim Tai—how many doors did he have? Seventy doors. Or seven—let's say seventy, whatever it is. He had people stationed at every door to keep giving to those who came to ask. How much would he give? When they left, they would leave as wealthy people. Whether he had seventy doors or seven, it is a lot. Anyway, someone said that he had seventy doors, and he would give so much from every door that it was amazing. This is about the grandson of Hatim Tai, Adi bin Hatim. Hatim's grandson, Adi, was... Hatim's grandson, Adi, was... when he saw that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had sent a letter, and he had to go to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), his mother said, 'I will go.' It was not easy. Hatim was comfortable here, and you are listening, but young men, imagine going into the enemy's camp, to that great personality, and going to meet him. And he gave him so much, he had already read about it, I won't repeat it. This is a bit correct. Then he asked, 'Who is this for? Who is this from?' The great King, the Hakim, the brave one, and then after that, he said to his mother, 'I will go.' He got up and said, 'I am going to the mosque to see him.' He said, 'I am going to the mosque to see him.' His mother said, 'I will not stop you.' He went to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was sitting there. When he saw him, he stood up and welcomed him. This is generosity and bravery. What is it? 'Man jada, sada'—everything is given. He had kept his promise. He broke his idols and came. And when he accepted Islam, he gave his life for the sake of Islam. Now look at what our Ma'sum (a.s.) says. Within these two words, look at the leadership training. Look at the training of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If you want to learn leadership, there is a book called 'Ghurar al-Hikam,' which contains 10,760 hadith from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (a.s.). A scholar collected them. Unfortunately, we don't know much about it. We know the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), but this book is a famous book, also known as 'Ghurar.' Thank God, it has been translated into English. Now, look at the leadership training: 'As-sakha wal-shaja'... Among them was bravery. The bravest of people is the one who is the most generous, the one who gives the most. Look at the connection. Look at the connection. I submitted that 'sakhi' (generous) is one who is ready to give to people, who is ready to earn and give. Now, how did he become the bravest? How did the most generous person become the bravest? Because he is ready to the extent that he is even ready to give his life. If you are ready to give your life, then why talk about money? One who is ready to give his life, will he be afraid? Why would he be afraid? If he is killed, so be it. A man was very brave; he was trapped in Mumbai, went to Baroda, stood on the terrace and was speaking. This is what 'bakhil' (miser) is—'bakhil' means a goat's kid. This is a goat's kid, and 'dal'—you understand, it's a small heart. If one is generous, his heart is big; it is not small. We went to Germany; there was nothing to eat at home, yet he still gave. It is said that if a human gives a small amount, or three drops, or whatever is left, and gives it to the children, or feeds the guest, or the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Take it away, whoever is ready to take it for the sake of health, for water, for the children,' then just give it to the children, extinguish the lamp, let the children go, let the guest rise. This is peace, and therefore, when they were in the battlefield, they were ready to give their lives for Islam. Today, those same values and the same teachings are being applied. Why? Because you have praised the hands many times before, and once again, your definition has been given. You are the mother, and the Brahmin teachings are what you have, which is how Allah is worshipped and Paradise is attained. Giving in the way of Allah is not about increasing or decreasing; it is about the path of Allah. The next generous person will be the one who is wise. A fool thinks that money will run out, but a wise person knows that money will not run out because you know that the Giver is the same, and by spending in His way, money never decreases; it never ends. And people are like this in the world. So now look at what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Generosity is intelligence.' This is leadership training. Generosity and intelligence—this is what wisdom and cleverness are. The one who is wise, the one who is clever, keeps giving; he never worries. The one who is wise, and the one who is a fool, is the one who is stingy; he will never give. He thinks it will run out because he thinks that this wealth is something that ends. Then, when it ends, what will happen? Then who will give me? But the Giver is not limited. Now look at what the Hadith says. Read the Hadith carefully. The Imam (a.s.) says that your wealth, if you do not spend it, will consume you. And what is the need for a common man? It is not a thing that remains; this world is meant to pass away. So, if you do not spend it today, you will leave, and someone else will spend it. And what is the command? 'Eat your wealth before it eats you.' Now, he gives an example: we deposited money in a bank so that it would be safe. Very good. Now, our children, our offspring—there are two possibilities: either they spent that money well, or they spent that money in a bad way. This is the difference. If they spent it in a good way, the reward goes to you. And if they spent it in a bad way, the burden is on our heads. So, why leave money for your children? The wise thing is to spend it now, do not keep it. And the children—your wealth is also your children's wealth. So, the guarantee for your children is not to leave them behind. And it further says, 'Do not kill your children for fear of poverty.' We provided for you, and We will provide for them. Do not think that you are earning for them; their provision is also Ours, and yours is also Ours. Therefore, it should never be in your mind that wealth is for the future. If you have money, if you have wealth, spend it in the way of Allah, and spend it in the way of Allah when you are alive. And that is why Allah forbade Prophet Musa (a.s.) from killing Samiri. Do you know who Samiri was? He was the one who set up the golden calf. And he said, 'This is your god, and Musa's god.' He prepared a calf, and he created a sound in it. It made the Bani Israel go astray, and they started worshipping it. And how did he create the sound? He was a great scholar of the time, he knew many things. So, when he saw this—and these are the verses of the Quran—Samiri says, 'I took a handful of dust from the footprint of the Messenger (Jibra'il).' I took it, and I understood that this is the footprint of Jibra'il, so there must be blessings in it. Yes, these are the verses of the Quran. And I took it and put it into the calf. That calf, that golden calf, he had prepared it himself with his own hands and with gold. As soon as he put it in, the effect was that the calf began to speak; a sound was produced in it. To this day, Muslims have not been able to understand this. To this day, Muslims have not been able to understand that if the footprint of Jibra'il or his trace has so much effect, then when people go to the doorstep of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to pay their respects, if we consider their soil to be a source of blessing, then what is there to be surprised about? Listen, this is the point. These were the facts, and we should use them properly. But this Samiri, what he did was create discord and division among the Bani Israel. But Allah said to Prophet Musa (a.s.), 'Do not kill him.' Why? Allah said, 'He is a companion.' This religion does not tolerate the killing of any companion. Allah knows who it is that committed shirk. So, this is in the Bani Israel. Anyway, in this, there is a lesson that one should not put money into haram deeds, even if it is a little. If you spend haram money on good deeds, even if you give 10,000 or 10 lakhs, it is not an issue, but spending even 10 rupees of haram money is not permissible. It is a waste, and you will have to give an account for it. The Imams (a.s.) say: You will have to give an account for it. The Imams (a.s.) say that a generous person is never a spendthrift. A spendthrift is not a generous person; he is a waster. The Quran says, 'The spendthrifts are the brothers of the devils.' This is what they do. Any thing that Islam has not allowed to be spent on—any thing, even if it is a small thing of 10 rupees—it is not allowed to spend on it, and you will have to answer for it. And you will be stopped: 'How did you spend it? On what did you spend it?' This is haram. It is a sin. Therefore, the question is that even a little bit is not allowed. So, this is very important. This is the lesson of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Two people came to the door of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to see how they used to act. Now, read the Salawat on Muhammad and his family. After the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), it was the time of the third Caliph. You know, they give big amounts. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was sitting outside the mosque. The third Caliph was sitting on a chair. So, the ruler—you know, he wouldn't sit alone. A person came and asked for some money and said, 'I need your help.' He gave him 5 dirhams. Now, if we calculate today's value, it would be around 400 or 500 rupees. He said, 'This won't solve my problem.' He said, 'I don't have any other way. Go to those people sitting in the mosque; you will find it there.' You will find it there. Who was sitting there? In the Hadith, it is mentioned that Imam Hasan (a.s.) and Imam Hussain (a.s.) and Janab-e-Abbas (a.s.) were sitting there. This beggar saw that he needed help. Now look at the training of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). They say, 'It is not permissible to spread your hands before others.' This is the training that is happening. It is not permissible to spread your hands before others unless there are three conditions. If these three reasons are not there, then never spread your hands before anyone. One: either you have to pay blood money to save someone's life. You know what blood money is, right? If someone kills someone, then the one who is the killer has to pay the victim's family. This is called blood money. Or, if you are in deep debt and are very troubled because of the debt. And the third is... And the third is such poverty and such need that it breaks you. So, the Imams (a.s.) have mentioned these three reasons: blood money, or if there is a debt that keeps you awake at night, or such poverty that it breaks you. Until these three conditions are met, do not spread your hands before anyone. Look at how Islam is emphasizing being generous on one hand, and on the other hand, it says that begging is haram. Begging is not permissible unless it is a necessity. So, think, what is this thing? The one who is asking, his need must be one of these three. But he cannot tell. He is one of these three. It's okay, no problem. The Bani Israel did not count. Imam Hasan (a.s.) gave him 50 dinars. Today, that would be 25,000. And then after that, Imam Hussain (a.s.) gave him 49,000, and then Janab-e-Abbas (a.s.). He gave him 49,000, then you gave him ginger and more. This year, I am coming for 147 days. What is online currency? What is rubber? Do you know what it means to give? If it were a gold coin, then that is what it is called—a gold coin. Now, just do the calculation yourself. So, this matter is that he gave so much, he gave 5,958 from his own pocket so that he could go. Now, as he was leaving, the old man was sitting at the door of the mosque, and he was watching from afar. He called out, 'What happened?' He said, 'I came to you, and you only gave me five dirhams. But when I went to him, he didn't just give me money; he asked me questions about my problems, gave me guidance, taught me, and told me when to ask for money and when not to. And after that, they all gave me such amounts.' When he heard this, the Hakim said, 'These are the people whom Allah has chosen.' These are the people whom Allah has chosen. It is written in their share that all the goodness and virtue of this world belong to them. All the blessings belong to them. And that is why you see that Imam Ridha (a.s.) is in Mashhad, and the Imam of the time is in Medina. What is this? Eight years, nine years... these are all jewels. The Imam of the time is in Medina. Imam Ridha (a.s.) wrote a letter to his son and wrote, 'I have received news that your servants take you out through the back door, while the front door, the big door... in the old days, houses had a big door and a small door at the back. This was especially for when someone came, so no one would know. If you look at the old houses, it is better.' He said, 'It is better to look at the old houses.' So, I heard that your servants take you out through the back door so that the beggars sitting at the front door do not ask you for anything. All of Iran is in Medina, but the Imam is so concerned. And this is the training the Imams are giving us—that we should not cut off the beggars by looking at them, or avoid them. For example, someone posted on their WhatsApp status that their condition is very bad and asked for help. So, I told the Imam, 'I will give you my bank details, you help them.' He said, 'No, son, I don't need money. I posted it so that they wouldn't ask.' There are many such WhatsApp statuses. The Imam is a bit... he knows that if the person asking is coming, they will ask directly. These are all techniques. But this is not the Imam's way. The Imam wrote in a letter, and it is narrated: 'I swear to you by the right that I have over you, I swear by this right that you must go through the front door, not the back door.' You must go through the front door, not the back door. And when you take out money, take out good money so that you can give it to the one who is asking. Do not keep it hidden, saying, 'There is no money,' and then give it later. There is a saying in Mumbai, 'The shopkeeper is giving the father's share.' It shouldn't be like that—that you are showing others, 'Oh, give it to him.' No, you give it yourself; that is generosity. The Imam said, 'Take this money out.' And look at the sentence—it is a lesson for everyone, especially for relatives. Especially in this world, relatives are beloved. If your uncle asks, at least listen to him. This is why it is said, and you all get tired, so I am not saying it. Give at least five dinars to your uncle if he asks. Minimum five dinars, and give as much as you want beyond that. At least five dinars, and if your aunt asks, 25 dinars at least... If your aunt asks, give at least 25 dinars, and more as you wish. At least 25. Now, why 50 for the uncle and 25 for the aunt? Because the share of a man is double that of a woman. Some people object to this, saying it is wrong. No, it is not wrong. Why? Because women get from both sides—from their parents and from their husbands—and their needs are also less, while men have many responsibilities. Islam is very systematic and logical. The Imam said, 'This should be your minimum.' The Imam wrote this letter, and the Imam believes that when you spend, Allah will increase your status. This is for us—the Imam wants Allah to increase our status. Spend in the way of Allah, and never fear poverty. The miser is the one who is always afraid. That is why the Imam said in the letter to his son, 'It is enough for a person's evil that he thinks ill of his Lord.' It is enough for a person's evil that he thinks ill of his Lord. Leave the other things aside. When he is in such a state, he will be very stingy regarding his sins. So, the Imam said, 'Beware of stinginess.' What is stinginess? It is a disease. It is the inheritance of his heirs. When the heir gets it, it becomes a bank system. And there is a great lesson in that too. You might know, there are many cases where a man dies, and no heir comes forward. It happens many times that no heir comes, and there is so much money in his house. In the old days, they used to hide notes, wandering off the path. In the old days, they would put them in pots—you know what a pot is—and they would bury them deep inside, in a dark room, so no one would know. And then, two years later, when they took it out, termites had eaten it. All the notes were eaten by termites. So, he lost in this world and in the hereafter. That is a clear loss. Can this person be satisfied? So, in the way of the Ahlulbayt, in the way of Imam Hussain (a.s.), whatever we spend... Whatever we spend in the way of Hussain (a.s.), whatever we do... and this is the lesson of Karbala. You see how Zainab (s.a.) gave her life, how she cleaned her tears. You mention the Ahlulbayt in your lectures. The children of Zainab (s.a.) were martyred. Now whose turn is it? Zainab (s.a.) is preparing her children, Aun and Muhammad. She is spending the whole night giving them advice: 'Son, sacrifice your lives for your uncle.' Now, when the time for martyrdom came, they were small—Aun and Muhammad, 10 and 8 years old. They were very small. And when Zainab (s.a.) brought both sons and stood before Imam Hussain (a.s.), who would recognize them? Who would recognize them from Hussain (a.s.)? What do you want to say, sister? I want... What do you want to say, sister? I want... Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Today, you are offering a sacrifice. Come, I have given permission.' After doing this, after preparing them, when they were ready to fight, Imam Hussain (a.s.) asked them questions, and after asking them, he sent them to the battlefield. Both brothers went; one attacked the right flank, and the other attacked the left flank. They kept attacking like this. They were not just children of Bani Hashim; they were the students of Zainab (s.a.). As they fought, the enemies said, 'Surround them! These are the sons of Bani Hashim.' But before leaving, Zainab (s.a.) had given them some advice: 'Children, I know you are thirsty for three days. I know it. But no matter how thirsty you are, do not even think about water, because in the tents, the children are thirsty, Sakina is thirsty, Asghar is thirsty. Do not even think about water. And secondly, children, fight in such a way that the enemies realize whose children you are.' The enemies should realize whose children you are. Mir Anis says, 'Say that they are the lions of the Wali of God; the army cried out that they are the lions of Ali (a.s.).' They fought just as they had seen their uncle fight. The enemies realized that these are the children of Bani Hashim. So, they surrounded them and martyred them. Both children passed away at that moment. Zainab (s.a.) called out, 'Brother Hussain, come!' Hussain (a.s.) went. He picked up one body, then the other, and brought them to the tent. Zainab (s.a.) saw that her children had come. Zainab (s.a.) was sitting on the prayer mat. Why did she come? I didn't tell them to come back. She asked, 'In what condition are they?' And when she saw them, she didn't cry for her children. She thanked Allah for accepting her sacrifice. I have never seen Zainab (s.a.) cry for Aun and Muhammad. She did not cry for Aun and Muhammad. She saw them and thanked Allah. When she returned, she sat in the sun. Zainab (s.a.) was following the command of Allah. Zainab (s.a.) had broken her share of patience. She had broken it. Zainab (s.a.) stepped forward, but she did not go to Aun and Muhammad. But once she reached their heads, she turned around... May Allah remove the troubles of those who are worried, and may He protect those who are oppressed. O Lord, you have the greatest share in this world, and you are the source of intercession. [Music] [Music]

title: Majlis 6 | Sakhaawat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound concept of 'Sakhaawat' (generosity) within the context of the tragedy of Karbala and the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The discourse emphasizes that true generosity is a hallmark of faith and a spiritual shield, transcending worldly loss through the promise of divine support. By examining the lives of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions, the lecture highlights the importance of competing in good deeds, the reality of the hereafter, and the eternal test of Wilayah.
content:
O Qatil-e-Shahe Zahra, my Hussain, my Hussain. O Qatil-e-Shahe Zahra, my Hussain, my Hussain. You did not even find a shroud, my Hussain, my Hussain. My poor one, my hungry one, my thirsty one. My poor one, my hungry one, my thirsty one. My martyr of longing, my Hussain, my Hussain. I have come from Paradise to mourn you, my son. I have come from Paradise to mourn you, my son. Give me consolation by rising, my Hussain, my Hussain. The settlement of Shaam is inhabited, Medina is desolate. The settlement of Shaam is inhabited, Medina is desolate. My shrine is empty, my Hussain, my Hussain. O Qatil-e-Shahe Zahra, my Hussain, my Hussain. You did not even find a shroud, my Hussain, my Hussain. Recite Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the final outcome is for the people of piety and certainty. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, our beloved, the God of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance, and curse their enemies. May Allah send blessings upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance, and curse their enemies. Especially, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, the Imam of our time, the Guardian of our affairs, our Master, our Mawla, our beloved, our healer, our companion, our confidant, the fortified cave, and the relief for the distressed and the helpless, may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Now then, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in His glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'So race to [all that is] good.' Allah the Almighty and Great has spoken the truth. May Allah bless you, O Aba Abdillah. May Allah bless you, O Aba Abdillah. May Allah bless you, O Aba Abdillah. Recite Salawat. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance, and curse their enemies. The verse of the Quran that has been made the title of this ten-day series of gatherings (Majalis), in that verse, the Almighty Allah says: 'Fastabiqul khayrat' (So race to all that is good). You all try to excel one another in good deeds, compete with one another, try to move forward as much as possible. And I submitted to you that who is the source of this goodness, all this goodness? It is the personality of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (the Master of Martyrs). It is the sacred personality of Imam Hussain (a.s.). This is the personality that is the source of all goodness. Source of all goodness. This is the personality of Hussain. As much as possible, everyone should try to excel one another in this path. Whether it is through wealth, money, or speech, spend however you can. Remember, a person should never think about what will happen, what will be the result? For example, will the money run out, or will this happen, or that happen? No. Never even let such thoughts enter your mind. Because this is against Allah's promise. Allah has promised in the Holy Quran: 'Inna lanansuru rusulana walladhina amanu fil-hayatid-dunya wa yawma yaqumul-ashhad' (Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of the world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand). Meaning, Allah says 'Inna' (Indeed), Allah is saying with emphasis, He is emphasizing, surely We will help. 'Lanansuru' (We will surely help), whom will He help? 'Rusulana' (Our messengers), He will help His messengers, 'Walladhina amanu' (and those who believe), and He will help the people of faith. Surely, We will help. Always, be sure, meaning do not even have any doubt in your mind. That if someone becomes of Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, then Sayyid-ush-Shuhada becomes theirs. Remember this. Rather, what we can do, they do much more for us and will continue to do so. Therefore, a person should never be afraid. This is Allah's promise: 'Inna lanansuru rusulana walladhina amanu fil-hayatid-dunya' (Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of the world). Meaning, it is not just about the reward of the Hereafter. In this world, The best of the life of the world and the day when the witnesses will stand. 'Ashhad', witnesses, the witnesses will be raised. Meaning, on the Day of Judgment. There will be help in this world, there will be help in the Hereafter, and there are many such verses in the Quran. If you study the Holy Quran, this verse we just read is verse number 51 of Surah Ghafir. There are many such verses; verse number 47 of Surah Rum. Allah Ta'ala promises, 'Wa kana haqqan alayna nasrul-muminin' (And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers). It is incumbent upon Us to help the believers. Allah says, 'Haqqan alayna'. Meaning, it is on our neck, Allah is saying that it is incumbent upon us that we help the believers. The condition is that there must be faith. The condition is that there must be faith. In both verses, the condition is faith. And there are other verses, 'Wa kadhalika nunjil-muminin' (And thus We save the believers). Allah says, We save them. It is Allah's promise. If there is faith, then do not be afraid of anything else. What can the people of the world do? Look, read the stories of the Quran, then study the traditions. Keep reading. Look, you will definitely find something in it. Let me present a small example for you, from the Quran, from the Holy Quran. When Hazrat Musa came to Pharaoh, Pharaoh said that brothers, call the magicians. To make it very brief, I am not telling the whole detailed story. Pharaoh said, call the magicians. The magicians came. Pharaoh said, brothers, we have to defeat Musa. The magicians asked, will we get any reward or not? He said, what reward do you want? They said, we want to become close to you. Look, is there 'Qurbat ilallah' (closeness to Allah) or not? What did the magicians say? We want to become close to you. Usually, the concern of the people of the world is to become close to some big man. If they become close to him, then they will get this position, that money, that wealth, that status, that honor. These worldly things will be obtained. Just keep sticking with him. Is it clear to you? They said exactly that. Pharaoh said, okay. Give, you will become close. No problem. But as soon as they came and stood in front of Hazrat Musa for the competition, now look, the glance of grace of the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda) fell. The glance of kindness of the Proof of God fell upon the magicians. This is a very important thing. Because we only understand apparent things; our intellects cannot grasp more than that. Our intellects are very limited. Very limited, they cannot understand beyond that. So, this is what is called 'Momin-e-Mumtahan' (the tested believer). So Allah takes the test. When the test of the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) was taken, everyone failed except for a very small minority that passed. And that is the same minority that passes in this world. That is the same minority that says 'Ali-yun-Wali-Ullah' in this world. That is the same minority that affirms the Wilayah of Ali in this world. They go for Ziyarat to Ali and say, 'Assalamu alaika ya awwalal mazlumeen' (Peace be upon you, O first of the oppressed). They curse the enemies of Ali. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Recite another Salawat for Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. So, this generosity has many benefits. One benefit is that it is proof of a person being wise and intelligent. A person who just sits on their wealth—for example, a man who kept hoarding money, and then termites ate it. There were notes in that era, so it ate all the notes. Or you have seen many announcements like the one on November 8th; such announcements cause losses for many people. Whatever happens, look, let me present one thing to you: Allah extracts money through various excuses. Understand this much. If a person does not give willingly in the way of Allah, then what can I say? Then Allah knows many ways. Income tax, GST, hospitals, lawyers—Allah has created this world with many such ways. He will extract that money in different ways. If the same money were spent in the way of Allah, then neither this issue nor that problem would have arisen; nothing would have happened. Allah Himself protects it because Allah has promised. What can I say? And people spend on all these things like madmen. Why? Because when one does not spend in the way of Allah, Allah knows how to fix them. And the only thing that saves them from loss is that. And you see, there is plenty of wealth, but it turns out they get diabetes, so they cannot even eat. This problem arises, they cannot eat that either. That problem arises, they cannot eat that either. And they end up in the hospital. As Akbar Allahabadi says, 'Became so civilized, never saw the face of home, spent life in hotels, died in the hospital.' What can I say? This is life. Allah knows how to fix them. And then it happens that in the end, they say, 'I find no pleasure in living anymore.' You must understand that this generosity, regarding this, Hazrat Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) presents a Hadith for you: 'Usturu ma'akum bis-sakha' (Hide your faults with generosity). Look, hide your faults with generosity. If you are generous, people will not see your faults. Otherwise, they will look at every single one of your faults. 'Fa-innahu sitrul uyub' (For it is a veil for faults). Generosity is a veil for faults. Subhan Allah. You will only get these words from the door of the Ahlulbayt. Indeed, indeed. Amir-ul-Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Nara-e-Haidari, Ya Ali. Did you notice? Now, I will present a Hadith here that the late Dailami has recorded in 'Irshad al-Qulub', that the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. There is no time now, so today I will present only one phrase of this Hadith to you, and the rest, Insha'Allah, tomorrow if Allah gives life and the opportunity. Both conditions are necessary. There must be life and there must be the opportunity, if it is Allah's pleasure. The Prophet says, 'Thalathatun...' look at the first phrase of the Hadith, just the first one, 'Thalathatun yastaghfiru lahumus-samawatu wal-ardu wal-mala'ikatu wal-lailu wan-nahar' (There are three types of people for whom the heavens, the earth, the angels, the night, and the day all seek forgiveness). They seek forgiveness from Allah for them. O Lord, forgive them, pardon their sins. Look, you understand the meaning, right? The heavens, you understood, right? All the heavens, all the earths—meaning there are seven layers of earth too—the day, the night, and the angels. And what are the angels? They are infallible (Masoom). Therefore, the prayer of the angels is 100% answered. Indeed. Because they are infallible, and an infallible person's prayer is always answered. The prayer of an infallible is 100% accepted. Indeed. Allah accepts the prayer of the angels. So they seek forgiveness. Who are these three individuals? The Prophet says, one, 'Al-Ulama' (The scholars). The scholars. Those who are Ahlulbayt, or the first instance of scholars are the Ahlulbayt themselves. The Ahlulbayt themselves are scholars. Meaning, there is a tradition, a Hadith that says, 'Nahnu al-Ulama' (We are the scholars). The Imam says, 'We Ahlulbayt are the scholars.' Two, 'Wal-muta'allimun' (And those who learn). And those who learn the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt. Those who learn the Hadith of the Ahlulbayt, for them, all these seek forgiveness, all keep asking for pardon. Muta'allimun. And third, the Prophet says, 'Wal-asqiya' (And the generous ones). And those who are generous individuals. For them, all these seek forgiveness. Whoever is generous, Allah forgives all his sins. And just one sentence of Maula-e-Kainat, and we will end this discussion here today, Insha'Allah tomorrow. Maula says, 'Man ayqana bil-khalaf, jada bil-atiyya' (He who is certain of the return/reward, is generous in giving). Subhan Allah. He who is certain that Allah... exists. He who has faith that Imam Hussain (a.s.) exists. He who has faith that Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) exists. And he who knows that He is Kareem (Generous). Do you recite in the Dua or not? You recite the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain and Imam-e-Zaman, right? What sentence do you recite on Friday? 'Anta Kareemun min awladil kiram' (You are generous, from the children of the generous). You are Kareem. What does Kareem mean? Who is called Kareem? One who rewards goodness with goodness. Kareem 'min awladil kiram', and all your ancestors are Kareem. If anyone spends even a penny for the Ahlulbayt, remember, they have never done it for the Ahlulbayt, they have done it for themselves. Because the Ahlulbayt do not keep anyone's debt and return it multiplied many times over. They give it back many times over. This is the Ahlulbayt. Why not? Allah has kept a great reward for Imam Hussain (a.s.). Do you know? It is found in traditions. Look, all the Imams, they all did everything for the sake of Allah. But regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.), some strange words are found in some Hadiths. That Allah has kept some special things for him. Which are not for everyone. One of them is that whoever stands under his dome, meaning under the 'Qubba', and prays, their prayer will be answered. Allah will never reject their prayer. And his 'Turbat' (soil), the 'Khak-e-Shifa', Allah has placed healing in it. Look, all the Imams are infallible, everyone has their own station. But this specialty, this is only for Sayyidush Shuhada (the Master of Martyrs). It is not for everyone. This is not for other Imams either. So if someone says we went from Mashhad, we brought this soil from Mashhad and we can eat it—no, that is not it. That is not it. Ask any Faqih (jurist), do not ask us. You ask any Marja-e-Deen. You ask them, see what answer they give. This is only for Imam Hussain, that's it. Because the sacrifice that Imam Hussain gave, the way he gave it, Allah loves this thing. Allah chose him. Who are we to talk about this? You just imagine, that's all. It is the night of Ashura. Imam Hussain (a.s.) is sitting with his companions. First, Sayyidush Shuhada told everyone that whoever wants to leave, should leave. Whoever wants to go, should go. But no one left. He said, 'I even give you a guarantee of Paradise. Go. Go, there is a guarantee of Paradise.' Even then, no one moved. No one moved from their place. Sayyidush Shuhada then extinguished the lamp. Thinking that perhaps you are shy because you do not want to go in front of me in the light. That is why I am extinguishing the lamp so that whoever wants to leave, should leave. You know, when Sayyidush Shuhada lit the lamp again, what did he see? All these companions were sitting in their places, with swords placed on their necks. 'Maula, you are talking about one life. If we get 70 lives in this path, we would sacrifice them for you.' After that, Hussain began to count the 'Mazhar-e-Shahadat' (manifestations of martyrdom). He began to recite the 'Mazhar-e-Shahadat'. He started taking the name of each martyr. He took the name of each martyr. He took everyone's name among the companions. After that, he started taking the names of everyone in his Ahlulbayt. He took the names of the martyrs of Bani Hashim. He took everyone's name. But there was a child, 13 years old, whose name Hussain did not take. When that child saw that my name is not in the 'Mazhar-e-Shahadat', he went to a corner and started crying, started weeping. And while crying, suddenly he remembered that when his father was leaving this world, he had tied this amulet on his arm and said, 'Son Qasim, when a very big trouble comes, open this amulet, the solution to your trouble will be in it.' Qasim thought, what could be a bigger trouble than this? What could be a bigger trouble than this? Qasim immediately opened the amulet. Now when he opened it and looked, it was written in it, 'Bunayya Qasim, adrik ammakal Hussain' (Son Qasim, go to the aid of your uncle Hussain). As soon as the child, as soon as the child read this writing, a smile appeared on his face. A strange child, seeing the message of death in Karbala, is smiling. He came smiling and handed a scroll to the Master of Martyrs (a.s.). He asked, 'Son, what is this?' He replied, 'It is a message from my father.' As soon as Hussain (a.s.) read his brother's scroll, Imam Hussain (a.s.) said after reading it, 'Son Qasim, this is not just your brother's scroll, but you have brought a message from your own father.' Qasim said, 'Uncle, it is my father's command.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Qasim, Qasim, I did not include your name in the list of martyrs, otherwise your name was Qasim, and it was not just your name, but your brother Ali Asghar's name was also there.' So, while the honorable child of Bani Hashim was happy on one hand to hear that his name was in the list of martyrs, on the other hand, as soon as he heard Ali Asghar's name, he was distressed and asked Imam Hussain (a.s.) a question, 'Ya Amma, hal yasiluna ilal khiyam?' (Oh Uncle, will these wretches enter the tents? Will these wretches enter the tents?) Hussain (a.s.) explained, 'No son, I myself, I myself will take Ali Asghar, and Ali Asghar will be martyred on the battlefield. I will say, oh honorable one of Bani Hashim.' Just hearing this made him distressed. Oh, ask Sayyid-e-Sajjad (a.s.) who is witnessing the scene himself. The day of Ashura arrived. One by one, the martyrs were martyred. After the Noon prayer, when it was the turn of Bani Hashim, everyone was martyred. Now Qasim came and stood in front, 'Uncle, please give me permission.' My Master, how could he give permission? The Master was just watching. 'Uncle, please give me permission.' Now let me present a sentence from the Maqtal to you. This is enough to make you weep, enough for lamentation. It is written in the Maqtal that when the Imam was not giving permission, Qasim took both of Imam Hussain's (a.s.) hands and started rubbing his eyes against them. 'Master, give me permission, Uncle, give me permission, Master, give me permission.' Hussain said, 'Go Qasim, today is the day of martyrdom.' Hussain prepared Qasim. Hussain himself adorned him. After adorning Qasim, Imam Hussain embraced him once. Both uncle and nephew wept so much, so much that they fainted. Mourners, when someone cries, when someone faints, water is sprinkled on them to bring them back to consciousness. But alas, Zainab's (s.a.) helplessness, where would Zainab get water from? She sprinkled tears. When he regained consciousness, 'Brother, now let Qasim go, do not stop Qasim now.' Hussain mounted Qasim. But before leaving, he tore his garment. He said, 'Uncle, what is this?' He said, 'This is the sign of orphans.' Now that Qasim went, he fought and sent many wretches to Hell, until one wretch struck such a blow that Qasim could not steady himself on the horse. Now that he fell, as he was falling, the wretches started trampling Qasim's body with their horses. Horses from here, horses from there. Qasim's, Qasim's... Oh! Now he is being torn to pieces. No voice. Ya Abbas! Uncle! Come to my aid. When Hussain reached there, Qasim had already departed from this world. 'Sayalamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, wa la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin.' O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord! Remove the troubles of those who are distressed. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant the blessing of righteous children to those who are childless. Grant complete and swift healing to those who are ill. Return those who are far from their homeland safely. Protect the life, wealth, honor, and dignity of the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar wherever they are in the world. O Lord! Protect the high scholars and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. O Lord! Grant us the pilgrimage of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Accept this humble mourning of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: Shahaadat-e-Fatima Zahra (s.a.) Aur Paighambar (s.a.w.a.) Ki Peshangoi [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture discusses a profound hadith narrated by Ibn Abbas regarding the status and future suffering of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) describes her as the leader of all women and a piece of his own soul, while also foretelling the calamities, oppression, and martyrdom she would face after his passing. The discourse emphasizes the deep sorrow of the Prophet and the spiritual connection between the followers of Fatima and the anticipation of the Imam of the Time.
content:
It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said in a profound hadith regarding his daughter, Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), that she is the leader of all women of the worlds from the beginning to the end. She is a piece of me, the light of my eyes, and the comfort of my heart. She is the soul that is within my body; in fact, she is a human in the form of a houri. When she stands in her prayer niche before her Lord, her light shines for the angels of the heavens just as the stars of the sky shine for the inhabitants of the earth. Then Allah (s.w.t.) says to His angels, 'O My angels, look at My maidservant Fatima, who is the leader of all My maidservants, standing for My worship, trembling in awe of Me, and having come for My worship from the depths of her heart. I make you all witnesses...' ...that I will surely keep her followers safe from the fire of Hell. After this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) described the calamities of his daughter, saying, 'Whenever I see her, I am reminded of what will be done to her after me. I see that wicked people will enter her house, disrespect her, usurp her right, and seize her inheritance. Her ribs will be broken, and her child will be martyred in her womb. She will be calling out, "O Muhammad!" but no one will answer her. She will be crying out for help, but no one will assist her. After me, she will always be sorrowful, distressed, and weeping. Sometimes she will be saddened by the fact that the revelation has ceased from her house, and sometimes she will remember my departure. Whenever it is night, she will feel a sense of loneliness because when I used to wake up at night to recite the Quran in Tahajjud, she will no longer hear that voice of mine.' She will see herself in a state where she is not being respected, whereas in her father's lifetime, she was honored. At such a time, Allah (s.w.t.) will send His angels to comfort her, just as He comforted Maryam bint Imran (s.a.). They will say to her, 'O Fatima, innallaha istafaki wa tahharaki wa istafaki ala nisa'il alamin' (Indeed, Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds). 'O Fatima, worship your Lord, prostrate, and bow down with those who bow.' When my daughter becomes afflicted with illness, Allah (s.w.t.) will send Maryam bint Imran (s.a.) to her, who will nurse her and take care of her during her illness. After this, my daughter Fatima will pray, 'O my Lord, I am tired of life, and I am fed up with the world and its people. So, unite me with my father.' Then Allah (s.w.t.) will unite her with me, and she will be the first of my household to meet me. She will come to me in a state where she will be grieving, distressed, sorrowful, her rights will have been usurped, and she will have been killed. Then I will say, 'O Allah, curse those who oppressed her, punish those who usurped her rights, humiliate those who tried to disgrace her, and cast into Hell forever those who struck her side until her child was martyred.' And the angels will say 'Ameen' to this. I wonder what must have passed through the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) when he was narrating the calamities of the daughter whom he himself had raised and called a piece of himself. The realization of this pain can only be felt by those who are waiting for the reappearance of the Imam of the Time. We can only pray: O Allah, keep us steadfast on the path of Fatima (s.a.) and grant us the intercession of Fatima (s.a.) on the Day of Judgment. Ameen, O Lord of the worlds. [Music]

Respected viewers, peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. All praise is due to Allah for His purity, for that Exalted God who kept us all attached to the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the Imams (a.s.) from his progeny. Respected listeners, as much as we thank Allah... No matter how much we thank Allah (S.W.T.) and how many prostrations of gratitude we offer in His presence, it is insufficient, for He has blessed us with countless bounties that even human intellect cannot count. The Holy Quran itself declares: 'Wa in ta'uddu ni'matallahi la tuhsuha'—if you try to count the bounties of Allah, you will not be able to count them. Among these infinite bounties, the greatest one with which Allah (S.W.T.) has blessed us is the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Its importance is such that without this Wilayah, a person cannot even attain the honor of having their worship accepted in the Divine presence. Describing its significance, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Ali (a.s.): 'O Ali, lawla anta ma khalaqallahu nar'—if all creatures had gathered upon your Wilayah, Allah would not have created the Fire. excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical evidence for the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as documented in Sunni Islamic literature. The speaker emphasizes that the concept of divine guidance through Imamate is a continuous chain, and that the birth of the 12th Imam is acknowledged by prominent Sunni scholars. By citing works like 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa' and 'Wafayat al-A'yan', the lecture aims to refute claims that the Imam has not yet been born.

All praise is due to that Almighty who brought this universe into existence. After bringing the universe into existence, He provided all those resources through which humans could live their lives. But His most special grace and mercy upon humans remained in the form of guidance, that after creating humans, He never left them alone. Rather, through one after another, through various guides, He kept guiding them. Sometimes in the form of Prophet Nuh (a.s.), sometimes in the form of Prophet Adam (a.s.), sometimes in the form of Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.), sometimes in the form of Prophet Musa (a.s.), and sometimes in the form of Prophet Isa (a.s.), He kept guiding humans. And when this chain of guidance reached the personality of Prophet Mohammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.), it was completed, and He, through His perfect mercy, continued this chain of guidance in the form of Imamate and In the form of Imamate and Wilayah, so that the world would never be empty of divine and heavenly guides. So viewers, the birth of the last individual of this chain, Hazrat Mahdi-e-Muntazar (a.t.f.s.), took place on 15th Shaban, which all of us have been celebrating separately until now. But a large group of Muslims has been continuously denying that your birth has not happened yet. Therefore, viewers, we should celebrate the birth of Hazrat as much as possible through our words and actions to give the world a message about the existence of Hazrat. I want to present this first reference before you, and this is not a small book, but Ibn Hajar al-Makki, who is a very big scholar in the matter of religion, he writes in his book 'As-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa', Volume 2, page number 601, there he writes that '...he did not leave anyone as his Caliph and successor after Abul Qasim al-Hujjah', and at that time the blessed age of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) was 5 years. He also mentions the name of the Imam's mother there, and then he writes the name of the father of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), which is Ali al-Hadi, and then he also writes the name of the father of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), which is Imam Jawad (a.s.). It is a lineage of the Imams that he has recorded in his book. And then he writes that he will be the 12th Imam of the Imamiya sect, and then he writes 'al-Ma'ruf bil-Hujjah', meaning he will be known by the title of 'al-Hujjah'. And after that, he states that his birth took place on a Friday in the year 255 Hijri. It took place on a Friday in the year 255 Hijri. And when your father departed from this transient world, your blessed age at that time was 5 years. Respected viewers, it is not just this; there are many such books of Ahl-e-Sunnat that have published the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). It is not that the opponents have not recorded it. Rather, the opponents, due to their sectarian compulsions, despite all these proofs, have continued to deny the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). excerpt: This lecture discusses the spiritual significance of the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) in relation to the respite granted to Satan. It highlights historical Islamic sources that suggest the end of Satan's influence coincides with the arrival of the Imam. The session also includes instructions for participants to register for an educational quiz regarding these theological concepts.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. To participate in this quiz, first, you need to register on the website quiz.al-hujjat.com. The registration link is provided in the comments and description of this video. Open this link, and if it does not open, copy the link and paste it into the Google Chrome browser on your phone, tablet, or laptop. Once the link opens, click on the Google icon and select your Gmail ID through which you want to participate in the quiz. As soon as you select your Gmail ID, your registration will be completed. On the registration page, you will see your token number and your details. At the end of that same page, there will be an 'Edit Profile' button; click on it and edit your details, especially your name, WhatsApp number, and area details. It is very important for these details to be correct because... It is very important because the winners of the quiz will be contacted through these details. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's blessings be upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny. In the race for progress, Satan has misled both small and great people. But when we look at the history, we find that until the appointed time... Until the appointed time, the question arises: who has Allah granted respite to? The famous scholar Sulaiman Qunduzi, in his book 'Yanabi al-Mawaddah', has recorded that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'The day when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will appear is the day when the respite granted to Satan until the appointed time will end.' The one who tried to mislead humanity until the appointed time will be eliminated by the blessed hands of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). Our prayer is that Imam Mahdi (a.s.)... May Allah hasten his reappearance. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Today's quiz questions are: According to which verse of the Holy Quran was Satan granted respite until the appointed time? To answer, click on the quiz link provided in the description and comments of this video and get a chance to win various prizes by answering these questions correctly as soon as possible.

title: Shab-e-Qadr Mein Ye Dua Mat Bhooliyega
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound significance of Laylatul Qadr, specifically linking it to the decree of Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker emphasizes the importance of reciting the specific supplication for Imam al-Mahdi (ajtf) during this holy night. By connecting the destiny of the heavens and earth to the Wilayah, the lecture encourages believers to dedicate their prayers to the reappearance of the Hujjah.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Mufazzal ibn Umar (r.a.) says that he mentioned "Inna Anzalnahu fi Laylatil Qadr" in the presence of Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) said: How clear and bright is its virtue over all other months. Mufazzal (r.a.) says, I asked, how so? The Imam (a.s.) stated, because the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was revealed in this night. I asked, the Night of Qadr that occurs in the month of Ramadan? The Imam (a.s.) said, yes, this is the Laylatul Qadr in which the destiny of the earth and the heavens is decided, and the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is decreed. Meaning, the decision of how much Wilayah will be in whose heart is made on this night. In another tradition, Muhammad ibn Isa narrates from the Imams (a.s.) that he said: On the night of the 23rd of Ramadan, while in prostration, or standing, or sitting—in fact, in every state throughout the month of Ramadan, and indeed throughout your life whenever possible—after praising Allah (Azza wa Jall) and sending blessings upon the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.), say: [Dua text: O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjah son of Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him dwell on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time.] O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten his reappearance, and destroy his enemies from among the Jinn and mankind, from the first to the last. O Allah, in this very Night of Qadr, decree the reappearance of Mahdi (ajtf), and grant us, our families, and our progeny the opportunity to live our lives upon the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and let our end be upon this Wilayah, and grant us the opportunity to recite both these supplications on the Night of Qadr. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen.

The destiny of the heavens and the earth is decided on the Night of Qadr.

title: Muharram Khushi Ka Mahina Ya Gham Ka? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the emotional and spiritual significance of the month of Muharram in the context of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Citing a narration from Imam Riza (a.s.), the speaker highlights the atrocities committed against the Prophet's family, including the violation of their sanctity and the looting of their tents. The lecture concludes by challenging the audience to choose between celebrating during this period or mourning the tragedy as a demonstration of humanity and love for the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.).
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon Ali ibn al-Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain, and upon the companions of Hussain. Hazrat Imam-e-Riza (a.s.) stated: Muharram was a month in which even the people of the age of ignorance considered fighting to be forbidden. But in this very month, the shedding of our blood was considered lawful. In this month, our sanctity was violated. Our children and the ladies of the household were taken as prisoners. Our tents were set on fire and burned, and whatever belongings we had in those tents were looted, and regarding our affairs, no regard was shown for the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). From this statement of Imam-e-Riza (a.s.), one can estimate how mercilessly and cruelly Yazid ibn Muawiyah (la'natullah alaih) had Imam-e-Hussain (a.s.) killed, and his soldiers, who called themselves the Ummah of the Prophet, were the ones who killed the son of the Prophet. Now you must decide: in the month when the son of the Prophet was killed, will you support Yazid by celebrating, smiling, and congratulating each other, or will you mourn the great martyrdom of Imam-e-Hussain (a.s.) as a requirement of humanity and to express your sympathy with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Peace be upon those who follow the guidance.
