title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 10 | Tafseer of Surah at-Tauheed (Surah # 112) - Introduction
excerpt: This lecture provides an introduction to the spiritual significance and merits of Surah al-Ikhlas (often referred to as Surah at-Tawheed). The speaker highlights traditions from the Ahlulbayt regarding the immense rewards of reciting this Surah, including protection, forgiveness, and the intercession of angels. The session emphasizes the importance of consistent recitation in daily life to achieve spiritual purification and closeness to Allah.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the best of His creation, Muhammad, and his pure progeny. Peace be upon the messengers. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family. [Music] Peace be upon you, O believers. Peace be upon you. I am present here with the recitation of Surah At-Tawbah. It contains the majesty and greatness of the Lord of the Worlds. It is a brief Surah. Allah has described His own greatness and independence. He is independent of all His creation; His creation needs Him, but He does not need the creation. I will recite the Surah. It is in the Holy Quran that Hazrat... It is in the Holy Quran that Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) used to say that whoever prays the daily prayers and does not recite Surah At-Tawbah in any of them, they are not among the believers. It is stated in the traditions that whoever recites Surah At-Tawbah, it is as if they have recited one-third of the Holy Quran. Allah will grant such a person rewards equal to the number of those who believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Day of Judgment. Even up to this point, the recitation of this Surah... O believers, look at the greatness of the recitation of this Surah. In a hadith, the Commander of the Faithful, Hazrat Ali (a.s.), says, 'On the night of the Battle of Badr, I saw Hazrat Khizr (a.s.) in my dream, and I asked him to tell me something through which I could gain victory over the enemies.' In truth, the Commander of the Faithful does not need anything, but how did he say this? Ali (a.s.) has given help to the help of Allah. Certainly, Ali (a.s.) is telling us, 'Look, if any difficulty arises and there is a mission...' If any difficulty arises and there is a mission, and you want to achieve success, how can you achieve it? The Mawla says, 'I saw Khizr (a.s.) and I asked him to tell me something through which I could gain victory over the enemies.' He said to me, 'Recite: Ya Man La Huwa Illa Huwa.' When morning came, I told the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) about my dream, and he said, 'O Ali, you have been taught the Greatest Name of Allah.' He says that on the day of Badr, this prayer was on my tongue: 'Ya Man La Huwa Illa Huwa, Ya Man La Ya'lamu Ma Huwa Illa Huwa.' Then Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'And when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) prayed the funeral prayer for Sa'd, he said that 70,000 angels, among whom was Jibra'il (a.s.), participated in his funeral prayer.' Sa'd was a very great companion; he had a very high status with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). But despite this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave him a hard time, prayed the funeral prayer, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the mother of Sa'd said, 'Congratulations to you on Paradise.' Then he... Then he asked, 'The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) forbade it, so how did you say Paradise? He is still being questioned.' So the companions asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, you prayed the funeral prayer, you gave him a hard time, he was a companion, you were with him, yet you are saying that he is being questioned?' He said, 'Yes, because Sa'd's behavior with his wife was not good.' Now, this is a separate issue, but since it came up, it is very important that how our behavior is in our home. It should be good. It should not be that because of it, we face questioning. Our spouse may not say anything, but the Lord is watching us. So, 70,000 angels, including Jibra'il (a.s.), prayed the funeral prayer. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, 'I asked about the reason for this participation, why the angels prayed, what deed Sa'd had done that caused so many angels, including the leader of the angels, to participate in the funeral prayer?' They said, 'Sa'd used to recite Surah At-Tawbah while sitting, walking, or standing. That is, whenever he sat, he would recite Surah At-Tawbah...' Whether sitting or standing, if they washed their hands, they would recite Surah Al-Tawhid. If they were doing any work, they would recite Surah Al-Tawhid. The Lord of the Worlds granted such a status to the person who recites it that 70,000 angels are appointed for them. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says that whoever recites Surah Al-Tawhid has recited one-third of the Quran, one-third of the Torah, and one-third of the Injeel. Now, think about it: if reciting it once is equivalent to one-third of these holy books, then imagine the reward. Amir al-Mu'minin Hazrat Ali (a.s.) says that when a person goes to their bed and recites Surah Al-Tawhid, Allah sends 70,000 angels to protect them throughout the night. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says that whoever passes by a graveyard and recites Surah Al-Tawhid 11 times, then to such a person... ...they receive a reward equal to the number of those buried there. That is, in the graveyard where they recited it 11 times, however many are buried—whether a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand—the reciter receives a reward equal to the number of all those buried. This is a very authentic Hadith. Amir al-Mu'minin Hazrat Ali (a.s.) says that whoever wishes to depart from this world purified of sins, as pure as gold, and to be raised on the Day of Judgment without any blemish, they should recite Surah Al-Tawhid 12 times after every obligatory prayer. After that, there is a supplication. Dear viewers, Insha'Allah, in the next clip, I will present that supplication before you so that we may follow the path of salvation. Regarding the number of times to recite Surah Al-Tawhid, it is not specified as a very large number; it is 100 times, 200 times, 70 times, or even 11, 3, 6, 9, or 12 times. If you recite it this many times, you get this benefit. If you start reciting it while sitting and standing, the benefits are even greater. ...the benefits are even greater. You have seen how the Imams (a.s.) have guided us. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that He counts us among those who recite Surah Al-Tawhid. Walhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen.

title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#13 - Kya Imam Ali (a.s.) Ne Khalifa e Awwal Ki Bay'at Ki? Part 1/2
excerpt: This lecture examines the historical controversy surrounding whether Imam Ali (a.s.) voluntarily pledged allegiance to the first Caliph. The speaker analyzes the concept of 'ijma' (consensus) and the term 'faltah' to argue that the initial election lacked universal agreement and legitimacy. By referencing historical sources like Sahih Bukhari, the lecture highlights that Imam Ali and several prominent companions withheld their support for six months. Ultimately, the discussion distinguishes between voluntary allegiance and forced submission, asserting that the pressure applied to Imam Ali was a political necessity for the opposition rather than a genuine endorsement.
content:
Peace be upon you all. We are present before you with another episode of the series regarding the objections raised against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Today, the objection and the issue we need to discuss is the root cause of all the oppressions inflicted upon Janabe Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). The burning of her house, the burning of her door, the martyrdom of Janabe Mohsin (a.s.), the breaking of her ribs, and the usurping of the rights of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—the root cause of all these tragedies was nothing but one issue. Yes, that was the issue that led to all these events. The reason why all these things have happened, all these issues are legislative, so the question arises that after enduring all these issues, the things that have been written in the books of history under the authority of the first Caliph, such hadiths are found where they state that Ali (a.s.) sat with his hand in the hand of the first Caliph. So let us see if this really happened. To answer this, we have with us Brother Syed Zaki. Assalamu Alaikum. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah. Brother, as you have just heard this question, people say that Ali (a.s.) sat with his hand in the hand of the first Caliph. So we would like you to tell the viewers what truth is hidden in this, as this is a very important issue. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Assalamu ala Fatimatuz Zahra wa abiha wa ummiha wa ba'liha wa baniha wa sirril mustawda'i fiha. Now, Roshan Bhai, this issue of allegiance (bay'ah) is so important that it should be understood that this is the root of all the differences among Muslims, and if the Muslims understand this issue of allegiance... And if the Muslims understand this issue of allegiance, then all the conflicts and disputes will be resolved. And as far as the objection is concerned, whether Ali (a.s.) gave allegiance or not, we will try to present the answer to this in two parts, Insha'Allah, because we do not want any aspect of this answer to remain unclear or for the viewers not to receive the answer. Therefore, we will try to present the answer in two episodes. In the first part, today, we will try to answer the question of whether Ali (a.s.) gave allegiance or not, and the second part will be presented to you tomorrow, Insha'Allah, and in that, we will try to analyze why, if Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance, he did not. In these two episodes, Insha'Allah, we will try to answer this. Let us turn to the first part and see whether Ali (a.s.) gave allegiance or not. The first group of people are witnesses to the fact that there was a consensus (ijma) of the Ummah on the caliphate of the first Caliph, even that Ali (a.s.) also gave his allegiance. Although this is completely wrong, they believe that there was a consensus of the people on the caliphate of the first Caliph. If you look at this consensus... If you look at this consensus, it is most important to understand what 'ijma' actually means. This matter arose from the word 'ijma', which means the gathering of all people on one matter, or people agreeing on one thing. This is called ijma. The first group, to prove the caliphate of the first Caliph, says that he was chosen from among the people by this ijma, meaning all Muslims, as many Muslims as there were, all people chose him. This is their claim. But this is not true. If you look at the definition of ijma, if even one Muslim is left out, then it is not an ijma. It should be like that. But was it like that? Let's see. In Sahih Bukhari, Book 86, Hadith 6830, the statement of the second Caliph is found, and what is written there? He says, '...wa la yughtarran imru'un an yaqula innamat bay'atu Abi Bakrin kanat faltatan...' (Let no one be deceived by saying that the allegiance to Abu Bakr was a 'faltah'). This was exactly like that, that this allegiance was a 'faltah'. And look here, the word 'faltah' is used. Look here, the word 'faltah' is used. It means something that happens suddenly, it is unexpected. It was not in any consultation, no one expected it, no one thought about it, and suddenly something happened. No one had any expectation, and suddenly that thing happened; that is called 'faltah'. So, one thing becomes clear: whose sentence is this? This is Bukhari, 6830. Look, whose sentence is this? '...innamat bay'atu Abi Bakrin kanat faltatan...' If anyone thinks that all people were in agreement on the allegiance of the first Caliph, then this is wrong in itself. Those people were deceived because the word used is 'faltah', so no one should be deceived that there was any consultation. Furthermore, in the same hadith, the next sentence is found, and what is it? '...fa-man baya'a rajulan 'an ghayri mashwaratin min al-muslimin fa-la yubaya'u huwa wa la alladhi baya'a...' (Whoever gives allegiance to a man without consultation from the Muslims, then neither he nor the one to whom allegiance is given should be followed). How strange it is that if allegiance is given without the consultation of the Muslims, then both the one who gave the allegiance and... If allegiance is given without the consultation of the Muslims, then both the one who gave the allegiance and the one to whom it was given, both should be killed. This is the command given. If they say that this is not referring to such a person, they are saying that there was no ijma. On the other hand, if it was done without the consultation of the Muslims, without permission, then according to this hadith, it should be rejected. And then, after this, it is proven that not all people gave allegiance at that time. The sentence that follows in the same hadith states that after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Ansar opposed us. The Ansar refused to acknowledge us, and then Ali (a.s.), Zubayr, and whoever was with them, they also opposed us. And who gave allegiance? Only the Muhajirun who were with us. The rest of the Ansar were against us. So, here we can see who the culprits are. This is our evidence; this is the point. Who are these people? They were with us, and they carried out this task. So, it is clear that they gathered with the Ansar, and with them, with the Ansar... They gathered with the Ansar, and with them, it was not with the consensus of the Muslims. And Sahih Bukhari Hadith 6830 makes it absolutely clear that without the consultation of the Muslims, was Ali (a.s.) considered a Muslim? Understand this. If it is said that allegiance was given without the consultation of the Muslims, then this allegiance has no status at all. Absolutely. And the narration of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), as it is with Ali (a.s.) and the companions of Ali (a.s.)... so here it is absolutely clear and understandable that what is this? And if we look at the sentences of this same hadith, that whoever gave allegiance and this was done without the consultation of the Muslims, then both should be killed. It is strange. And are we not Muslims? Are those who were with Ali (a.s.) not Muslims? We are not included in the Muslims? Those who were with him are not Muslims? So, whatever happens in the gathering, whatever happens with the Ansar, then who will it be? And besides this, not only this, but there is a very long list of the companions of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), a large list of those who did not give allegiance. People who did not give allegiance, and this is not a small or insignificant personality. These are the noble companions and great figures. For example, Janab Salman Farsi (r.a.), he did not give allegiance. Janab Abu Dharr, where he did not give allegiance. Janab Miqdad, for whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that the sky has not shaded anyone, nor has the earth carried anyone, who is more truthful than Abu Dharr. And the one whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is giving the certificate of truthfulness and being 'Siddiq', that Abu Dharr, he also did not give allegiance. Besides them, Janab Ammar, about whom it is found that he did not give allegiance anywhere. History is sitting in front of me. When we sit in history, such great companions also did not give allegiance. Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance. Zubayr did not give allegiance. The daughter of the Prophet, Fatimatuz Zahra (s.a.), she did not give allegiance. The leaders of the youth of Paradise, Imam Hasan and Imam Husain (a.s.), they did not give allegiance. And it is not found about any of the Banu Hashim that anyone gave allegiance. And without Banu Hashim, what is the allegiance? This is true, and even this, if we take Sahih Bukhari and study the hadith, it is written in it itself... Study the hadith, it is written in it itself that after the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), for 6 months, Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance to anyone. This is in front of you, from Sahih Bukhari Hadith. For 6 months, Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance to anyone. And this is actually the position that we, the Imamiyyah Shias, have been saying for a long time, that Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance to anyone. And similarly, in their book 'Al-Sunan al-Kubra', on page 56, volume 6, they write this. They write that '...wa kana ijma'u al-ummah 'ala bay'ati Abi Bakr...' (The consensus of the Ummah was on the allegiance of Abu Bakr). They say that Ali (a.s.) gave allegiance. But here, the word 'ijma' has been used, but the way it has been used, it is very important to understand. They say that the ijma of the Muslims was on this, that Ali (a.s.) gave allegiance. So, the people are confused about the fact that Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance at that time. Now, the scholars have different opinions about this. Some say that the situation was such that... there are different aspects. One aspect is that he did not give allegiance for three days. This is a very small group that believes he did not give allegiance for three days. And besides that, the majority of the scholars believe that Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance until Janab Fatimah (s.a.) was in this world. And after the martyrdom of the Lady, they say that he gave allegiance. And then a group also believes that Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance for 40 days. These are the different narrations in which he did not give allegiance. And on this, the scholars say, and they take the view that as far as the ijma is concerned, the scholars have agreed on this, that Ali (a.s.) did not give allegiance to anyone for 6 months. This is the official view. So, we have seen that some people bring some such hadiths from our books, from where they try to prove that Ali (a.s.) actually sat with his hand in the hand of the first Caliph. So, we will answer them. Now, people who raise such objections, perhaps they have not studied the history of Islam. Because if they had studied history, they would never have dared to call a 'bay'at-e-ijbari' (forced allegiance) a 'bay'at-e-ikhtiyari' (voluntary allegiance). To call a forced allegiance a voluntary one, they would not have the audacity. In this history, it is absolutely our claim that the allegiance they are talking about, where he sat with his hand in the hand, that is 'bay'at-e-ijbari'. It is a forced allegiance. What is 'bay'at-e-ikhtiyari'? First of all, see what 'bay'at-e-ikhtiyari' means. 'Bay'at-e-ikhtiyari' is when a person, by his own choice, by his own will, gives his hand to someone. That becomes 'bay'at-e-ikhtiyari'. And 'bay'at-e-ijbari' is when two people, or someone, forces another person, and allegiance is taken by force, then it is called 'bay'at-e-ijbari'. And this 'bay'at-e-ijbari' has no status in Islam. Absolutely. We, from this, absolutely reject that if someone takes something from someone by force, and then in the whole city, they say that the person in front gave it by his own choice, then this is a deceptive sentence. If a person has even a little bit of intellect, he will understand this. So, this is 'bay'at-e-ijbari'. Absolutely, taking allegiance from someone by force, and Ali (a.s.) giving allegiance by choice, this is not only in our books but also in the books of the Sunnis. We are bringing narrations from our Shia books, where it is mentioned that this allegiance was 'bay'at-e-ijbari'. Not 'bay'at-e-ikhtiyari', where he sat with his hand in the hand of someone by his own choice. It is not the case that he placed his hand on someone else's hand at all. And in the books of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it is mentioned—and Sheikh Al-Mufid, in his book 'Al-Jamal', in the first volume, on page 30, has recorded these narrations. He writes and narrates that they forcibly brought Ali (a.s.) out, and there, they brought him before the people. After that, they imposed this law. Ali (a.s.) said, 'If I do not do this, what will you do? What will happen?' After that, the strange threat that those people used—the people who say 'La ilaha illallah'—was, 'We swear by God, besides whom there is no god, that we will strike off your head.' This means that those who today raise slogans of 'Nara-e-Takbeer, Allahu Akbar' and enter people's homes and cut throats, this is the same tradition. This is exactly how it was in the context of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.), the slogan of 'Nara-e-Takbeer' was used alongside the killing of Hussain (a.s.). Indeed. The killing of Hussain (a.s.) and the slogan of 'Nara-e-Takbeer'. Indeed, those who cut throats today while raising these slogans, this is not the tradition of the Muslims. It is not. The followers of those people will reach this. This is a forced allegiance. They are trying to extract a statement from Ali (a.s.) by force. They are threatening him. They are threatening the Master of the Believers (a.s.), saying that if you do not pledge allegiance, we will strike off your head. Will you pledge allegiance? Absolutely not. This is not from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And in this regard, in the book 'Bihar al-Anwar', volume 28, page 227, we find this narration. The narrator of the hadith is someone who is a reliable narrator, and this is a famous hadith. This is also a famous narration that they have narrated from their grandfather, Zayd bin Arqam. He was present there, and he was among those who came to the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) with wood, carrying fire and wood. Those who went there, they have narrated this. This is to be noted, and then they call it... This is the field, keep this in mind. And I saw that in the life of Ali (a.s.), there are two things. The first day was when the martyrdom of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) occurred, and the second day was when all these things happened. And that is the work of the devil. I was sitting there, and I saw that the Caliph was sitting on the right side. I sent a message to all the people there to come and sit. At that time, a person said to the others, 'Listen, nothing will be achieved until Ali pledges allegiance to you.' This means that the voice was being raised, 'Call him, call him.' They said, 'He will come to you, and you should also talk to him, because these people who are gathered here, after this, what will happen?' They stopped them. Does this mean that he is saying that all these people who are gathered here are all legitimate? Yes, he is... All these people who are gathered here are all legitimate? Yes, he is calling all of them legitimate. Look, all the people who were pledging allegiance at that time, all of them were standing there with the group, based on whose allegiance it is being said that the allegiance was taken, and through that, the Caliphate was proven. The whole thing is being presented to the people so that it can be proven that it was necessary for Ali (a.s.) to pledge allegiance. Those people actually wanted Ali (a.s.) to pledge allegiance so that their actions, which they wanted to justify and make legal according to the Sharia, could be validated. They wanted to put a stamp on it. Those people knew very well that if Ali (a.s.) pledged allegiance, then no Muslim in the universe would deny it, and no one would have any objection. Indeed. And as far as this forced allegiance is concerned, it is also found in 'Bihar al-Anwar', volume 28, page 245, in the 45th hadith... In the 45th hadith, it is mentioned that they narrate from their sources, and the narrator of this hadith is Zayd bin Arqam. He says that they said to Ali (a.s.), 'Pledge allegiance.' Ali (a.s.) stood up, and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were there. He said to them, 'If I do not do it, then?' They gave the same threat, 'We swear by God, we will strike off your head.' Ali (a.s.) asked them three times, and all three times they said, 'We swear by God, we will strike off your head.' And after that, the narration continues, saying that they took Ali (a.s.)'s hand, and Ali (a.s.) had kept his fist closed. They intentionally forced Ali (a.s.)'s hand, but in what state? Ali (a.s.)'s fist remained closed. And then what did they do? They placed their hand over it and said, 'This is allegiance,' and then they were satisfied with this. They were satisfied with this. This is a matter of forced allegiance. On this, they will be satisfied. This is what is called forced allegiance, in which the person's heart is not involved, nor is his consent involved. Absolutely correct. So, this is also in their books, and they admit that it was only a forced allegiance and never a voluntary one. And whatever happened, it was not with his consent. Thank you very much for explaining this to us in such a simple and clear way. We learned that Ali (a.s.) never pledged allegiance to anyone, and we also learned why the allegiance of Ali (a.s.) was important for them. They knew that if they got the allegiance of Ali (a.s.), then all the Muslims would easily pledge allegiance. And if Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance, then they would get tired of explaining to people who the true successor is and who the owner of the right is. With this, this episode ends. Insha'Allah, in the next episode, we will see that if Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance, then why didn't he? What was the reason? Insha'Allah, in the next episode, once again... Insha'Allah, in the next episode, we will meet again. Until then, goodbye, and my regards to all.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 9 | Importance of Reciting Holy Quran with Tajweed & Arabic Accent
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual and practical necessity of reciting the Holy Quran with correct Tajweed and authentic Arabic pronunciation. It highlights the role of the Ahlulbayt in interpreting the Quran and stresses that learning proper recitation is a fundamental obligation for every believer. The session addresses common challenges, such as the limitations of transliteration, and encourages students to seek qualified teachers to preserve the integrity of the Quranic text.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief. [Music] O Allah, guide us to the truth and keep us firm on the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). In the light of the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), under the topic of 'Ma'rifat-e-Quran' (Knowledge of the Quran), the series we started, today, Alhamdulillah, is its new session, in which I welcome you all. The month of Ramadan is passing; we are all trying to do as much as possible. Let us start this session with the recitation of some verses. For this, once again... ... We will create... [music]... 169... Indeed, Allah the Almighty has said. Moving towards the next segment, regarding the Bismillah, the Hadith I have chosen for today is from the book 'Sirhan-e-Jila', Hadith number 253. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has stated that when a Muslim or a teacher says to a child, 'Say Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim,' and then when that child says 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim,' Allah writes salvation from the fire of Hell for that child, for their parents, and for that teacher. It is a great... It is a great... it is a great... for that child, it is a great... salvation from the fire of Hell is written for them. Surely, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has spoken the truth. Dear viewers, our topic today is Tafsir and the importance of the recitation of the Holy Quran in the Arabic language. Today's session is a bit different, and the reason is that we are enlightened by the daily recitation of the Quran. We will discuss this topic further, Insha'Allah. Through 'Nawa-e-Adab', many students have received Quranic education under the supervision of the respected Maulana Asad Abbas Khan Sahab. Without further delay, I request Maulana to enlighten us on this topic in the light of the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). I request all of you to keep sending your questions related to this topic to the WhatsApp number shown on the screen. My WhatsApp number is [number removed]... My WhatsApp number is [number removed]... keep the series of questions going. Wa Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. Salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil aliyyil adheem. Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. As-salamu ala Rasulil Kareem wa Aalihi at-tahireen. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. As-salamu alaykum. As I mentioned in the recitation, I referred to the blessed Surah. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has stated... The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has stated, and you all know that 'Sab'ul Mathani' is one of the names of the blessed Surah Al-Fatiha. The importance, greatness, and blessings of Surah Al-Fatiha, which Allah has mentioned in the Quran, are unique. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told you that it was revealed to you as 'Sab'ul Mathani'. And the blessed Surah Al-Fatiha, the Quran, and the book that was revealed to the great master—the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his purified progeny (a.s.)—how can a human like us estimate the greatness and majesty of this book and revelation? Understanding the greatness and majesty of this book is not just difficult, but impossible, if the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were not there... If the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were not there, then how could we understand? To explain this, Ayatollah (r.a.) states in his Tafsir that our attitude and responsibility should be that we should adopt such humility and respect before the blessed and glorious heavenly book that we consider ourselves lowly and weak before it. He further states that just as a student stands before his teacher with his ears attentive and in a very polite and civilized manner, with his head bowed, we should present ourselves before the Quran as if our teacher is standing in front of us, and every fiber of our being should be filled with awe and respect. This is how we should show respect, my dear viewers. As you have seen in the lectures and Tafsir, and as you are aware, the style of speaking and the chain of transmission are things you have observed. In my opinion, my speaking was not necessary, but I present a few things before you. I apologize for the delay. Those who know me, know me; for those who don't, I am just a humble servant. It is not arrogance, but by the grace of Allah, in 1999, during my time in the seminaries, an examination was held. Alhamdulillah, I stood first among 460 students in Quranic studies, after which I got the opportunity to stay in Delhi for 5 years and conduct Quranic camps in different cities across India. And Alhamdulillah, today this work is happening in Mumbai. I am grateful to Allah for giving me this opportunity. To have had the chance to sit before 120-130 students... To have had the chance to sit before them and verify the Quranic studies, and in the last 20 years, 6 to 7 thousand people from all walks of life, including non-Muslims, have shown interest in learning the Quran. This has been a success. There was a time when the number of people working on Quranic studies in India and Pakistan was very small. Although the work has seemingly decreased, Alhamdulillah, there are great names in the field of Tafsir and Quranic sciences. You all know them. But today, Alhamdulillah, in India alone, we have 38 Huffaz-e-Quran. I have worked with them, and about 12 of our students are performing at the international level, and 12 are at the national level, and about 6-7 are international reciters. Alhamdulillah, this work is progressing well. May Allah accept these efforts and keep them in His presence. But the greatness of any book is estimated either by the personality of the author... Is estimated either by the personality of the author. If the author is very famous, people buy the book because it is written by so-and-so. And if an ordinary person writes it, but the contents are excellent and well-referenced, people buy it and accept it based on that. The book we are discussing today, whose Tafsir you are listening to, its author is the Ruler of the worlds, the Creator of the universe, in whose power the entire creation lies. Therefore, it is impossible to describe the Author. And the medium was the one who is a mercy for all of humanity, a role model, rather, the leader of all Prophets, about whom Allah said in the Quran that he does not speak until he receives revelation. And the medium to bring this book to this world, to this earth, was the one whose name is written as 'Amin', who was trustworthy. Whatever Surahs, verses, and Quran Allah revealed, he did not take them without the Prophet's command... He did not take them without the Prophet's command and handed them over. And it was revealed in a place that is the most blessed and best place on earth, which is the Holy Kaaba and Makkah al-Mukarramah, which the Quran refers to as 'Balad al-Amin'. Therefore, there is no room for any doubt or suspicion regarding the content, greatness, truthfulness, and authenticity of this book. I would like to say one more thing: if you go deep into the Tafsir, you will find that Allah has sent about 400 small and large scriptures from the sky, and out of these 400, He has specified four books: Torah, Zabur, Injeel, and Quran. And among these four, the one He has given the most importance and made a source of many blessings, we know it is the Holy Quran. If we changed any letter or changed the pronunciation, you know that some things happen by mistake, which is a matter for the next scholar. But if we can learn and do not learn, then in my opinion, it is a matter of negligence. And the first question is, if someone is a new... And the first question is, if someone is a new Muslim and has not memorized the Surah yet, and has not learned the Arabic, and the time for prayer arrives, what is the solution? So, the solution is that if they have understood that they have to pray, then for now, whatever is possible for them, they should pray. Insha'Allah, it will be accepted. If they ask later, it will be better. If the congregation is happening, it is very good. What is better than that? If they want to read, they can stand and say 'Subhanallah, Subhanallah'. If they don't know anything about what the prayer is and what the rules are, then after that, they will learn and it will be fine. I have seen people do this. Okay, the next question is, and you hinted at this during the session, in how much time can a person learn to read Arabic correctly? In how much time? Usually, Tajweed is practical, and the one listening to it is the one teaching it. The point is that if you have taught someone, you have taught them. title: GIRYA E ZAHRA (سلام الله عليها) - Bait E Tatheer Par Hamla - E'teraazaat ke Jawaabaat
excerpt: This lecture discusses the martyrdom of Syeda Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) and the significance of the Ayyam-e-Fatimiyah period. The speaker highlights that her passing was a result of oppression rather than natural causes, emphasizing the historical link between the events in Medina and the tragedy of Karbala. The lecture calls upon followers to observe these days through mourning and awareness to honor the Ahlulbayt. Additionally, it introduces a new program series dedicated to addressing common historical questions and skepticism surrounding these events.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. 13th of Jamadi-ul-Awwal and 3rd of Jamadi-us-Sani are two dates that are extremely painful and sorrowful for the world of Islam. This is because, according to various narrations, these dates mark the martyrdom of the only daughter of the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the piece of his heart, Syeda Siddiqa Tahira Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). Yes, you heard it right: martyrdom. The term 'death' is used for a passing that occurs due to natural causes, but a passing that occurs due to poisoning, oppression, or being wounded is called martyrdom. People usually take care of their leaders and guides, but alas for those Muslims who, until yesterday, claimed to love their Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his family, and upon them... upon Hussain ibn Ali... And upon them, upon Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.), the leader of the youth of Paradise, Imam Hasan and Imam Hussain, whose mother is the source of humanity's pride. This can be gauged from the fact that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had declared, 'Fatimah is a part of me; whoever hurts her has hurt me.' Regarding this, she (s.a.) said, 'O Father, after you, such calamities befell me that if they had fallen upon bright days, they would have turned into dark nights.' It is because of these calamities that the martyrdom of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) is remembered. From the 13th of Jamadi-ul-Awwal to the 3rd of Jamadi-us-Sani, the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) remember these days as 'Ayyam-e-Fatimiyah' so that, just as the oppression that Yazid committed against Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions in Karbala... Just as the oppression committed against Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions in Karbala was brought before the world, in the same way, the world should not remain unaware of the oppression that occurred in Medina and Shaam before Karbala. The oppression in Medina and Shaam laid the foundation for the oppression in Karbala. In this regard, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'There is no day of greater calamity for us than Ashura, except for the day when the house of Ali and Fatimah was attacked, in which the daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was injured, and the grandson of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was martyred while still in the womb.' That is a day of greater calamity for us because that day laid the foundation for Ashura. It is the responsibility of the followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to raise awareness about this aspect of Islamic history, to organize gatherings where, like the months of Muharram and Safar, we wear black clothes during these days, refrain from celebrating, and organize Majlis, Matam, and processions so that the oppression inflicted upon these important figures... So that the oppression inflicted upon these important figures is known to the people and the entire Islamic world becomes familiar with the sufferings of Fatimah Zahra (s.a.). If we become the cause of guidance for even one person through these efforts, then on the Day of Judgment, our intercession will be... [Transliteration: Hazrat-e-Shuaib-la-Fatimah-Zahra-salamullah-alaiha-aakhri-ichha-anusar-isi-muneshwar-singh-the-strong-room-alaihis-salam-ki-team]. Now, we are presenting our new program to you. From the 13th of Jamadi-ul-Awwal to the 3rd of Jamadi-us-Sani, in 8:30 shows across India, titled 'Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) - The Jewel of the Prophet's Heart,' we will answer questions related to this event that are often raised by skeptics. Please subscribe to our YouTube channel for the program and press the bell icon for notifications. We pray to the Lord of the Worlds to grant us the ability to mourn for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and to keep us among their true followers.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 20 | Tafseer of Surah al-Qadr (97) - Part 3
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual significance of honoring parents in Islam, drawing from Tafsir-ul-Safi and various narrations. The speaker emphasizes that obedience to parents is a mandatory duty that holds a status second only to God and the Prophet. Through historical anecdotes, the talk illustrates the impossibility of fully repaying a mother's labor and highlights how kindness toward parents serves as a key to increasing one's sustenance and spiritual success.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the best of His creation, Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and his pure progeny. I am once again present before you with the explanation of Surah Al-Adiyat. Before this, you might recall the narrations I mentioned earlier, and today I will continue with that. Let me tell you the name of this book: 'Tafsir-ul-Safi'. In 'Tafsir-ul-Safi', on page 330, you can see and study this. I am discussing pages 329-330. The narrations I mentioned previously must be in your minds. These narrations mention four types of people: one who drinks alcohol, one who is disobedient to parents, one who is a persistent sinner, and one who severs ties of kinship. These are major sins. No deed will benefit a person until they are obedient to their parents. Being obedient to parents is mandatory, for which the Lord of the Worlds has said: 'Do not even raise your voice before your parents; keep your head bowed.' Because the status of parents is very high. If we draw a conclusion from the narrations and Hadith, it is that after God and the Prophet, the highest status belongs to the parents. It is also said in narrations that you cannot repay the debt of a mother's labor, not even for a single moment. You cannot repay the father either. A mother carries the child for nine months, feeds the child with her own blood, stays awake at night, and if the bed is wet, she sleeps on the wet side herself and keeps the child on the dry side. But besides that, the pain of childbirth, staying hungry herself to feed the children, sacrificing her own desires to nurture the children's desires—this is what parents do. It is sad when many young people become disobedient to their parents. It is very painful, not just for me—what does it matter if I am hurt? It is God who is hurt. It is the Creator who is hurt. Think about what we are doing to our parents, how much of their right we are fulfilling. We clash with our parents. But look at the companion who came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my mother is very old. A time came when she could not eat or drink anything. I would soften the bread with my own mouth and then feed her. After that, a time came when she needed liquid, and I didn't have milk ready. I prayed to the Lord of the Worlds, and God gave me the ability, and I would provide milk for my mother. I didn't like anything for myself; my parents were everything to me. I would arrange milk and feed her. How did I feed her? O Prophet of Allah, you know.' The Prophet stood up, embraced him, kissed his forehead, and said, 'You have fulfilled the right.' The man asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, have I built a place in Paradise? Have I fulfilled the mother's right?' The Prophet said, 'Beware.' So think, you could not fulfill the right... So think, you could not fulfill the right. And that person who is saying, 'I have bathed my parents with my own hands, dressed them, fed them, softened the food by chewing it, lifted them from one place to another, laid them down, and served them,' even after doing all this, he asks, 'O Messenger of Allah, I don't even feel any pain; I don't frown, I don't sigh, I don't complain. Should I be ashamed or not? My parents should be comfortable.' Did he fulfill the right? No, he did not fulfill the right. Today, we don't even try. And look, there is another point. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'In the Bani Israel, there was a man who wore a woolen garment and prayed for a thousand years...' He did not descend for a thousand months; he remained engaged in the path of Allah. Hearing this, the Sahaba expressed their desire, wishing that such a reward could also be theirs. So, Surah Al-Qadr is better than the worship of a thousand months. In fact, some narrations state that obeying the parents is equivalent to Jihad. Is it not a great matter? Yes, this is a significant question. And since the topic of parents and Hadith has come up, let me mention that people often face difficulties and worries regarding their livelihood. A person came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I am very worried about my livelihood.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'Be kind to your parents; God will increase your sustenance through them.' If our parents are no longer with us, go to their graves. If our parents are no longer with us, go to their graves, recite Fatiha, and do good deeds; God will increase your sustenance. The man said, 'I do not even know where their graves are, as in those days people traveled and often passed away on the road and were buried there.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'It does not matter. Go to the desert or the forest, mark a spot as their grave, and imagine that it is your parents' grave. Sit there, recite Surah Fatiha for them, do good deeds for them, and then pray to the Lord of the Worlds. The Lord of the Worlds will remove your difficulties and increase your sustenance through them.' He did exactly that. A few days later, he returned to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'Did your sustenance increase?' He replied, 'O Messenger of Allah, I did exactly as you said. I went to the desert, marked the spot, and imagined it was my parents' grave. I did good deeds there, recited Fatiha, and did what I could. Allah has increased our sustenance.' Alhamdulillah, I have enough now. These matters regarding parents are very important. ...we will continue tomorrow. Until then, I bid you farewell. Khuda Hafiz. Walhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen.

The reasons for the delay in the answering of prayers and the mention of the most important blessings of Allah are at the beginning of this supplication. title: Imam Reza (a.s.) - Har Zabaan Ke Maalik | Wilaadat Ba'saadat-e-Imam Raza (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture discusses the miraculous ability of Imam Reza (a.s.) to communicate with people in their native languages and dialects. It highlights a narration by Abu Salt al-Harawi, where the Imam explains that as the Hujjah (Proof) of Allah, he must possess the knowledge of all languages to guide creation. The talk concludes with a prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and for believers to be granted spiritual wisdom.
content:
Abu Salt al-Harawi narrates that Imam Reza (a.s.) used to speak to people in their own languages. By God, he was the most eloquent among them and had the most knowledge of various languages and dialects. One day I asked him, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, I am amazed at how you know so many different languages, and that too with their distinct dialects.' Imam Reza (a.s.) replied, 'O Abu Salt, I am Allah's proof (Hujjah) over His creation, and Allah does not appoint anyone as His proof over His creation who does not know their language. Has the saying of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) not reached you that we have been granted 'Fasl al-Khitab' (the decisive speech)? Is 'Fasl al-Khitab' anything other than the knowledge of languages?' We pray to the Lord of the Worlds that, like Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and Imam Reza (a.s.), He makes us heirs to this 'Fasl al-Khitab' and hastens the reappearance of our Imam, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grants us the opportunity to hear the eloquent speech from his blessed tongue. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

chapters.title: The Sorrow of Separation

chapters.title: Submission and Following Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes the necessity of complete submission to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt rather than relying on personal opinions in matters of religion.

chapters.title: The Status of the Believer

chapters.title: The Importance of Identifying Evil

chapters.title: Inheritance and Loyalty to Imam Hussain (a.s.)

chapters.summary: The speaker argues that many modern societal conflicts have no connection to true religion and warns against the naivety of being misled by political actors.

chapters.title: The True Followers of the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The lecture concludes by discussing the rarity of true disciples (Hawari) of the Imams and the historical resilience of the Shia community.

chapters.title: The Nature of Hypocrisy and Loyalty
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical patterns of bravery and betrayal, highlighting how hypocrites conspired against the Prophet and how true believers like Hudhaifa remained loyal.

chapters.title: The Status of Nasibis and the Love of Ali

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Karbala and Ali Akbar
