chapters.title: Closing Supplications and Blessings
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes the session with prayers for the audience's well-being and the intercession of the Prophet and his progeny.

title: Majlis 2 | Aql aur Aaqil | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound relationship between intellect (Aql) and the spiritual path of the believer, using the martyrdom of Hur ibn Yazid al-Riyahi as a primary example of divine guidance. The discourse defines true intellect as a tether that controls base desires and emphasizes the necessity of aligning one's words with righteous deeds. Through Quranic insights and the teachings of the Ahlulbayt, the lecture highlights the importance of humility, reflective speech, and preparation for the afterlife while avoiding worldly distractions.
content:
The face of the King is like a sun to a speck of dust, from which even the moon seeks the light of the King's body. The fervor of the King is the amulet for the arm of David. The horses of the King make the fairies lose their senses. In the garden of the world, the spring breeze has arrived; the ride of Solomon has appeared in the Qaf. He called out, 'You speak the truth, without a doubt.' The mantle of Hazrat-e-Shabbir covered my flaws. Neither my mantle nor my pocket is empty of the wealth of faith. Praise be to God, the unseen caller gives the call. Having received the grace, I have come to wield the sword; I went from here a beggar, I have returned from there wealthy. Hearing this speech, he called out to the noble leader, 'Yes, let us move towards the supporter of the King of Faith with spears and arrows.' Taking weapons, the large crowd of the army advanced. Reciting the Fatiha, the brave men drew their swords. Hur's face turned red, the army of tyranny turned pale and yellow. With the flame of the sword, the lightning flashed in the dust. The night passed, with the roar of a lion. The bones of Rustam trembled under the earth. The ranks of the army were overturned as they gathered. Even the horses shone with fear from the lightning of the sword. The time for battle had not yet come, but hearts were broken. The banners fell, the standards slipped from hands. Hashim was stirred as the sword of Huzaifa moved. Lightning moved towards the battlefield to rain fire. By what miracle did he take the path of victory? If it stopped, it stopped; if it moved, it moved. The wounds of the chests burst open like collars. Oh, what was the pace that thousands of throats were cut? It did not stop for stone, nor did it stop for iron. It blew away heads and necks from the shoulders. Its hard blow did not rise from any armor. It moved wherever the opposing wind came with a whistle. Showing the fervor of a storm, it became pure. Oh, in the river of blood, the crop of the body drowned. Advancing, Abbas would say, 'What courage!' The beloved of the King would call out, 'Praise be to God!' He would say, 'Son of Hassan, bravo!' Hur-e-Ghazi, bravo! The King would say 'Masha-Allah' at every strike. The Ghazi, who received the reward for his bravery, would bow down in submission with a smile. Alas, in bowing, the wretches found an opportunity. Leaving the front, the whole army came from behind. Millions of arrows there, and loneliness here. Oh, he took a spear blow while turning the horse. He came into the clutches of death, it did not take long. A mace struck his head, a sword struck his shoulder. His chest became like a flower, the arrows of the enemies flew. The lion placed his head on the saddle, bowing down. Ali Akbar said this to the Hazrat, shouting, 'Oh, if it is ordered, I will go and take care of the mother.' The journey from the saddle to non-existence falls to the dust; now the brave Hur falls from the horse. The King began to weep as soon as he heard this, he got news of the mother, his blessed beard became wet with tears. He said to Ali Akbar, 'You wait for now, my beloved, we will go to his aid, oh light of my eyes.' To whom should I say at this time, the grief that is upon me? I will lift the mother's corpse, for it is my right. Hazrat-e-Abbas requested, 'The slave is going,' in a state of emotion, the King said, 'No, oh flower-faced one.' Hur, of good end, was killed for my love; how can a friend be one who does not come to help in bad times? When a difficult hour comes upon him, we will come to help, and what is a corpse, we will go as guests to the grave. Saying these words, Hazrat-e-Shabbir went to the battlefield, and Hur-e-Ba-Tauqir fell to the dust from his horse. Seeing the King coming, the godless ones fled. The Imam of both worlds reached the corpse at the final hour. He saw the garden of the guest's life being ruined, he saw the wounded one rubbing his heels on the dust. Falling beside the corpse, the Master called out, 'Alas, oh my helper and supporter. Did a mace strike you, my back is broken. You fell from the horse and did not give me news. In the separation of a friend, which friend has found peace? Oh, open your eyes, oh, Hussain, the brother, has come.' Habib ibn Mazahir said, 'You are restless, oh brave Hur, come to your senses, see the sight of the beloved of Zahra. The journey is ahead, this is not the time for negligence. If your breath has stopped, make a will with a gesture, see the sight of the light of God.' Hur saw the face of the Master with half-closed eyes, he saw the pillow of Shabbir's knee under his head. Smiling, he looked towards the higher world. The King asked, 'Oh brave Hur, what did you see?' He requested, 'The beauty of the face of the Houris is visible, from the throne to the earth, light is visible.' 'Turn my corpse towards the Qibla, oh Qibla of faith, recite Yasin, for this is the final breath. The journey is ahead, oh King sitting on the throne, take it, my dear life is leaving my body. Now even speech cannot be made with the tongue. Oh, blow something, Master, I am feeling sleepy.' Saying this, he stretched out in Shabbir's lap, sweat appeared on his forehead, yellowness covered his face. The King said, 'Why have you left us, brother?' The brave Hur passed away, then no sound came. The bird of the soul took flight towards Tuba, the pupils remained turned towards the King. The bird of the soul took flight towards Tuba, the pupils remained turned towards the King. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Blessings be upon him and his purified family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our guardian, our master, our companion, our intimate friend, the fortified cave, and the relief for the distressed and the desperate—may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has said in His glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'So race to [all that is] good.' Allah, the Almighty, has spoken the truth. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The noble verse I have chosen for these ten nights of gatherings is a short verse. I have two words—two points—regarding this noble verse. As I mentioned to you yesterday, it is verse 148 of Surah Al-Baqarah and verse 48 of Surah Al-Ma'idah. In this noble verse, the Almighty Allah says: 'Fastabiqul-khayrat' (So race to all that is good). Compete with one another for goodness. And the collection, the source, or rather, it should be said that all goodness—whatever goodness exists—Allah has gathered it all into one being, who is known as Husayn ibn Ali. And this is a statement from the Imam himself. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Whoever Allah desires good for, He casts into his heart the love of Husayn and the love of his Ziyarat.' That for whom Allah desires good, He places the love of Husayn and the love of visiting Husayn in his heart. 'Wa man arada bihi al-sharr' (And whoever He desires for him evil)... ...He casts into his heart the hatred of Husayn and the hatred of his Ziyarat. Allah places the hatred of Husayn, the hatred of Husayn, and the hatred of visiting Husayn in his heart. I mentioned all of this to you yesterday with some details. Today, while moving the topic forward, let us repeat the sentence of the hadith so that the matter is refreshed in your minds. The Master of the Faithful (a.s.) said to Harith al-Hamdani, to Harith al-Yamani, the Imam said: 'O Harith, teach these wisdoms to your children.' Look, teach your children these wisdoms. The entire hadith, which I presented to you and whose details we will discuss today—we will start from today—teach your children, 'Allimu hadhihil-hikam' (Teach these wisdoms), 'fa innaha ziyadatun fil-aql wal-hazm wal-ra'y' (for it increases their intellect, their foresight, and their judgment). Because it will increase their intellect, their foresight, and their opinion—meaning the selection of ideas, the selection of decision-making, knowing which decision to make where—it will help in all these things if you teach your children this. In which the first question the Imam asked Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) was: 'O my son, what is intellect?' 'O my son, what is intellect?' Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) replied... See, actually, I will give you the answer first, then explain it a little. The Imam said: 'Hifzu qalbika ma istawda'tahu' (Guard your heart with what has been entrusted to you), or you can put other diacritics on it, 'istawda'tahu'—meaning remember those things that have been deposited with you, that have been entrusted to you, the teachings that have been given to you, remember them. Now look, peace be upon you. This topic of intellect is very vast, very... ...vast, and for this, the lessons—the discussions that happen about intellect—can last for years, even two years, just the discussion of intellect. And our great scholars, like Sheikh Kulayni, like the author of Al-Mahasin (the late Barqi), like Allama Majlisi, and all the great scholars, when they discussed intellect in their books, they brought this discussion of intellect first. It is given so much importance and is in such detail. Peace be upon you. So, we cannot fully explain these details here. We will just give a few points and then repeat them—meaning we won't be able to go into much detail. We will just point to them, and the rest is for you to ponder and study as much as you can; it will never be enough. So, look, first of all, let's start with the Holy Quran. In the Holy Quran, the root of the word 'aql' (intellect)—'ya'qilun', 'ta'qilun', 'aqaltu', 'aqilu'—this word 'aql' and what is derived from it, has appeared 49 times in the Quran. Meaning, Allah has emphasized it so much, 49 times! Besides this, Allah has used different words for 'ta'aqqul' (using the intellect). For example, He said 'Ulin-nuha'. 'Nuha'—meaning Allah has used 'intellect'—'Ulin-nuha' means 'possessors of intellect'. This verse has appeared twice in Surah Taha, at the end of Surah Taha, Surah number 20. If you read the Quran, 'Ulin-nuha'. 'Nuha'—what is it made from? First, let me tell you the meaning of 'aql' so that the matter becomes clear to you. What is 'aql' made from? It is made from 'iqal'. 'Iqal' refers to a peg, a stake, the stake to which an animal is tied; that is called 'iqal'. So, for which animal did Allah give man intellect to tie? What was this animal? It is written in the traditions: 'Inna al-nafsa mithlu akhbath al-dawabb' (The human soul is like the most wicked of beasts). This human soul is like an uncontrolled animal. 'Law lam tuqal harat' (If it is not tied, it will become uncontrollable). The human soul, because the human soul constantly commands man towards sins. This is also a verse of the Quran, a verse of Surah Yusuf: 'Inna al-nafsa la-ammaratun bil-su'' (Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil). It constantly commands, it is 'la-ammaratun bil-su''—very much a commander towards sin. If man is left to his own devices without intellect, without teachings, he will drown so much in sins, he will drown so much in sins... ...that we see those who are far from the Quran and Hadith—apparently, look, it is a 'civilized world', look, apparently, what is called the 'civilized world'. And an Epstein file has shown how civilized they are. Meaning, those who cut up children and eat them—you can judge from this alone. This is the 'nafs-e-ammara' (the soul that commands evil), and not just cutting and eating, but even worse than that. Meaning, we have heard from many people that they said, 'Brother, when we read just a few things from these Epstein files, we vomited.' Just by reading it. These people practically carried out those things, and no sane person can listen to what these people did. So, this is what happens if man's soul is left to its own devices; it is like an uncontrollable animal. So the Imam says that the soul is like that, and Allah placed the intellect for this reason. This intellect—that is why it is called that. Now, look at the subtlety of the Quran, its eloquence, its rhetoric, its eloquence. Look at how Allah has used different words. For intellect, 'Ulin-nuha', possessors of intellect, the possessors of intellect—what has He called them? 'Ulin-nuha'. 'Nuha' is made from 'nahya'. 'Nahya' means to stop. 'Nahya' means to stop. This intellect stops man from going towards sin. From not going towards sin. Did you notice? 'Ulin-nuha', this has appeared twice in the Quran. Besides this, it has appeared many times in the Quran as 'Ulul-albab'. 'Ulul-albab', possessors of intellect are called 'Ulul-albab'. 'Albab' is made from 'lubb'. 'Lubb' means—'lubb-e-lubab' is also used in Urdu—meaning the essence of something is called 'lubb-e-lubab'. Or one says, 'Look, the essence of my speech is this.' The essence of my speech is this. The summary is this, the gist is this. Man's humanity depends on his intellect. If there is no intellect in man, he will not be a human; he will be worse than an animal. Which you can observe in the world now. Now the question is, first of all, what is intellect? So, look, the discussion of intellect in our traditions is that 'Awwalu ma khalaqallahu al-aql' (The first thing Allah created was the intellect). This intellect is a light. It comes in the tradition: 'Inna Allaha jalla thana'uhu khalaqal-aql' (Indeed, Allah, may His praise be exalted, created the intellect), 'wa huwa awwalu khalqin khalaqahu' (and it was the first creation He created), 'min al-ruhaniyyin 'an yamini al-'arshi min nurihi' (from the spiritual beings on the right of the Throne, from His light). Meaning, this is important, which I wanted to present to you, that Allah created it from His own light—meaning directly, Allah created it directly. Meaning there was no intermediary in between. The rest of the other things, they were created indirectly—the things that Allah created, through these things. But Allah created the intellect directly. It is such an important thing. And then, this intellect is the greatest blessing that Allah gives to anyone. Now, before saying one point here—meaning before moving forward—I should present to you, we were actually not able to decide when to say this. Whether to say it at the beginning of the majlis or at the end of the majlis, meaning until the discussion of the majlis ends. Because our very dear Maulana Askari Khan Sahab's statement, we repeat it; if we say it as our own, it would be 'duzdi-e-ilmi' (intellectual theft). Therefore, we quote him, that he says our listeners who come to the majlis are also like the verses of the Quran; they come slowly. It is clear, isn't it? They don't come all at once. So, it is not understood when to say such an important thing. But anyway, so I will say it now, then Insha'Allah we will see if someone understands it, then good, otherwise no problem. Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Look, those who are already born, they are born. Those whose children are born, they are born. Now, the thing I am going to say is for those who are not married yet. And in the future, it is possible that they might become parents. In the future, for those for whom it is possible to become parents, they should pray a lot to Allah that our children become possessors of intellect. Pray a lot. A narrator asked the Imam a question, and it was a very strange and unique question; it is a hadith in Usul al-Kafi. The narrator asked the Imam, 'Master, when I talk to people, I meet three types of people. One is the one whom I just start speaking to, and he picks up the point. I start speaking, and he picks up the point.' This is a tradition from Kafi. 'And the second is the one who, until I tell him the whole thing, he does not understand the matter. When I tell the whole thing, he understands the matter completely, when I tell the whole thing.' And the third is the one to whom I tell the whole thing, and even after that, he says, 'A'id 'alayya' (Repeat it for me). Meaning, speak again, I did not understand the whole thing. So these are three types of people. First, the one who, when you just start speaking, picks up the whole point of what you are trying to say—one. Two, the one who, when you tell him the whole thing, understands it. Third, the one who, even after telling him the whole thing, does not understand it, and he says, 'A'id 'alayya', please repeat. I could not follow, please repeat. Like we often say. The Imam said that this has to do with intellect. It depends on when Allah gives the intellect. If Allah gives that child, who is still in the 'sulb-e-pidar' (loins of the father)—meaning he has not yet gone into the 'rahm-e-madar' (womb of the mother), he is in the 'sulb-e-pidar', 'sulb-e-pidar' means loins of the father, his transfer has not happened yet—at that time when the angels come and grant him the light of intellect, then he is the one who is so incredibly intelligent that he just—meaning the person in front starts speaking, and he understands what he is about to say. The second is the one who, when this drop (nutfa) goes into the 'batn-e-madar' (womb of the mother), after that, approximately, as it is in the hadith, at that time when the angels come and grant him the light of intellect, then he is the one who understands the whole thing when you say the whole thing. When the drop has already been transferred into the womb of the mother, that is when it is. And the third thing, which is the third one, who does not understand the matter, this is the one to whom Allah gives intellect, but after being born into the world. After a good amount of time, Allah gives him intellect, then he starts to understand things a little bit, so that is why his—what we don't call in our language—'tubelight'. It lights up slowly, that 'Yes, will you please repeat? I did not understand the matter.' So this intellect, this is such an important thing. This is Allah's greatest, greatest blessing. Hazrat-e-Amir, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) says, O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. He says the most excellent thing, the best thing that Allah grants to His creatures, is intellect. The best thing, 'Afdalu hazzir-rajuli 'aqluhu' (The best portion of a man is his intellect). Allah does not grant anything better than intellect. The best thing. If He gives it to someone, then what is it for him? In the hadith, the Master says, 'In zalla a'azzahu' (If he slips, it honors him). If he is humiliated, through intellect he gets honor. 'Wa in saqata rafa'ahu' (And if he falls, it raises him). If he remains low, if he is from the lower class of society, through intellect Allah raises him. Wa in zalla arshadahu. If he remains misguided, Allah guides him through intellect. If he remains misguided, Allah guides him through intellect. Wa in takallama saddadahu. And when he speaks, he speaks the truth. If he is a person of intellect. This is light (Noor). Allah does not give it equally to everyone. And based on that, Allah also holds them accountable. We will cover the subject very quickly because time is short, and insha'Allah, there is a different topic every day, so we will try as much as possible. So this is a gift from Allah. See, basically, what is this intellect? It is light. And this light is the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad. This is the station of light (Maqam-e-Noorani). This is the station of light. Therefore, if someone wants this intellect and wants to increase it, then there is only one path for that, which the Prophet stated: "Inni tarikun feekumuth-thaqalayn, Kitaballahi wa itrati Ahli Bayti, ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abada." I am leaving behind two precious things among you. This is value, precious. The Quran and the Ahlulbayt. That is why regarding the teachings of the Ahlulbayt, it is said in Ziyarat Jami'ah al-Kabirah, "Kalamukum Noor" (Your speech is light). This light, this light, is intellect. So you see, how will one know who has intellect and who does not? Meaning, we also need to, for ourselves and for others, first decide about ourselves whether we are intellectual or not. There are many narrations on this; we will not read all the hadiths, just two or three, on how to recognize who is an intellectual, a wise person. Who is one, and who is not? The Ahlulbayt have explained everything. Look, look at the hadith: "Al-aqilu man wada'athu al-tajaribu." The very first sign of intellect, of a wise person, is that they learn from experience. They gain experience. Experience teaches them. Because it is found in narrations that a believer will never be stung from the same hole twice. He will not be stung from the same hole twice. Once he has had the experience, he will not be deceived a second time. He remembers it. That is why many people who are wise write down their experiences. And they keep looking at those experiences repeatedly so that they remain in control. Meaning, so that it refreshes, so that it doesn't happen that the same thing happens again, and there is a problem again. So, one should write those things down so that in the future, one is not deceived. Now it has happened, it happened once. Now it should not happen a second time. After that, he says in another hadith, "Al-aqilu man saddaqa aqwalahu af'aluhu" or "aqwalahu af'alan," it can be read both ways. An intellectual is one whose words and deeds have compatibility. Walaikum Assalam. His words and his actions are the same. Meaning, what he says, he acts upon. Or conversely, what he acts upon, he says. Otherwise, if he only preaches and it turns out that in the field of action he is zero, he does not act upon anything himself. First, let's talk about ourselves, not others. The Quran says, "Ata'muruna al-nasa bil-birri wa tansawna anfusakum wa antum tatluna al-kitaba afala ta'qilun?" You command people to do good and forget yourselves while you recite the Book. Do you not have intellect? "Ata'muruna al-nasa bil-birri" - you tell people to do good, do good. And you forget yourselves, "wa tansawna anfusakum wa antum tatluna al-kitaba" while you keep reciting the Quran. "Afala ta'qilun?" Do you not have intellect? Do you not use your intellect? Meaning, whose intellect is the Quran questioning? Those who only preach and do not practice. Or perhaps it is the verse of Surah Hujurat or Surah Saff, "Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu lima taquluna ma la taf'alun? Kabura maqtan 'indallahi an taqulu ma la taf'alun." O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Why do you say such things? "Kabura maqtan 'indallahi an taqulu ma la taf'alun." Allah hates it, hates it, that you say things that you do not act upon yourself. You must have heard many incidents on this topic, that many, meaning in the time of the Prophet, a man came and said my son eats too much honey, forbid him. The Prophet called him after three days. He called him after three days. So people said that the Prophet could have said that to him earlier. The Prophet said to the son, do not eat honey. That man said, you could have said this earlier. The Prophet said, three days ago I was eating it myself. That is why I did not say it. I was eating it myself, so how could I tell him not to eat it? For three days I did not eat honey. That is why I called him after three days. So look, this has an effect. When a person acts, his words have an effect. Otherwise, his words have no effect. Like there are many professional speakers, professionals. Like there was a scientist, he spent more than 30 years researching the harms of tobacco, how harmful tobacco is. And then, to present his research, he called a press conference. And while he was addressing the press conference, he was smoking cigarettes. So there is no benefit in that. If he does not act himself. I mean, people of this world are like that, no problem. But in religion, this should not be the case. That is why our jurists, if you look, our Maraja-e-Kiram like Ayatollah Khoei, Ayatollah Sistani, their books, their treatises, "Minhaj al-Salihin," you will see that they have discussed this topic in detail. Under the section of "Al-amr bil-ma'ruf wa al-nahy 'an al-munkar" (Enjoining good and forbidding evil), they have discussed this topic. And they have discussed whether it is allowed for a person to preach something he is not acting upon or not? This is an issue among them. At least in obligatory matters (Wajib), it is not allowed for both. If the person himself is not acting, in obligatory matters. Regarding recommended matters (Mustahabbat), jurists have different views. Now you understand Wajib and Mustahab, right? Wajib is something like Wajib prayer. And Mustahab means that which is not Wajib but is recommended. This is fine, for example, like Namaz-e-Shab is Mustahab, not Wajib. Reciting Tasbih is not Wajib, it is Mustahab. So if we tell someone to recite Tasbih, we don't recite it ourselves. But we tell someone. Some jurists say no, it is better that one acts upon it first and then says it. But most jurists say that they can say it. Because not everyone does every task, but they can speak. Anyway, this is a very important thing. This is a sign of intellect, that words and deeds, meaning a person's speech and a person's action, both should be the same. And if they are not the same, then this is a sign of a hypocrite. He is a hypocrite. Especially, you must have seen that some show more humility and devotion to people, but keep something else in their hearts. So the Imam says, "Ma zada khushu' al-jasadi 'ala ma fi al-qalbi fahuwa 'indana nifaq." If a person has more inclination in the heart, sorry, there is no inclination in the heart, and he is only bowing outwardly. What love is he showing? Then he is a hypocrite. "Fahuwa 'indana nifaq" (In our view, this is hypocrisy). A believer is one whose heart is what is apparent. What is apparent is absolutely clear. Now look, all the companions of the Imams (a.s.) used to be like this. You look at the story of each companion. They all used to speak openly. Meaning, they used to have very clear conversations. There was no such thing among them that, for example, there was any shopkeeping (deception). The companions of the Imams who were close to the Imams, none of them were shopkeepers. If they were shopkeepers, they wouldn't let the Imam come close. Recite a Salawat on Muhammad and Aali Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa aali Muhammad. The third sign of intellect is that an intellectual person is always practical. And the ignorant one keeps building castles in the air. He only makes plans, we will do this, we will do that. An intellectual speaks less, works more. The Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), says, he says, "Al-aqilu ya'tamidu 'ala 'amalihi." Actually, this is the eloquence and rhetoric of Arabic, the peak of eloquence of Amir al-Mu'minin. Amazing. "Al-aqilu ya'tamidu 'ala 'amalihi wa al-jahilu ya'tamidu 'ala amalihi." The first 'amal' with 'ayn', the second 'amal' with 'alif' (hope). An intellectual is one who relies on his actions. His trust, his reliance is on his actions. He does the work, then he tells, yes, I have done this work. And the ignorant one, the Mawla says, the ignorant one, he builds castles in the air. We will do this, we will do that. There are many people who, every time they get a little excited, they say we will do this, we will do that, and then it's over. Nothing else besides that. This is a sign of being ignorant. So an intellectual always does what? He is practical. He speaks less, He works more. People recognize him by his work, not by his words. Anyone can talk. Anyone can plan, we will do this, we will do that. Now you see, just now in service, all these sayings were from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Now a hadith of the Prophet has also come, in which he has fully explained what the sign of an intellectual is. We will try to cover it very quickly, as much as possible, as much as we are enabled. The first thing, the Prophet says, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Very important. See, actually the sentences are small, but it is a whole treasure, an ocean. He says, the first sign of an intellectual is that he is very patient in front of an ignorant person, meaning he tolerates the behavior of that ignorant person very much. When an ignorant person interacts with him, the ignorant person, he tolerates him a lot. Meaning, when an ignorant person shows ignorance, he does not respond to ignorance with ignorance. He responds to ignorance with intellect. See, the Quran has also pointed towards this, it is in Surah Rahman. Surah, excuse me, not Surah Rahman, Surah Furqan. Surah number 25 of the Quran. The Quran says, Ibad al-Rahman (The servants of the Most Merciful), Allah's servants are those, Ibad al-Rahman. Alladhina yamshuna 'ala al-ardi hawna (Those who walk on the earth in humility). When they walk on the earth, they walk very gently. Meaning, there is no noise or clamor. There is an interpretation for this in Usul al-Kafi, we are not stating it right now. Alladhina yamshuna 'ala al-ardi hawna wa idha khatabahumu al-jahiluna qalu salama (And when the ignorant address them, they say peace). And when an ignorant person comes and argues with them, he says, Assalamu Alaikum. Meaning, I don't even want to argue with you. He knows that arguing with this ignorant person will result in nothing but ruining his own intellect. So, absolutely. Here, let me present an example for you, so that the matter becomes completely clear. See, when an ignorant person cannot do anything, what does he do? He uses foul language. When someone uses foul language, see, it is very common among us, it is common. People think they are doing something very good. They are doing something very good, they use foul language. No, let me present a hadith for you, then I will tell you the incident. It is a very famous hadith, that the Imam says that "Inna Allaha harrama al-jannata 'ala kulli fahhashin badhi'in bi-al-haya'i" (Allah has forbidden Paradise to every person who uses foul language). Someone who has no control over their tongue and is shameless. Meaning, anywhere, in any gathering, they start swearing. Swearing in front of anyone. We are not saying they should swear in front of some and not others, that is not the point. They just sit anywhere and start swearing. 'Badi'un bil-haya'i la yubali ma qala wa la ma qila lahu'—they do not care what they are saying or what people are saying about them. They have no concern at all. 'La yubali ma qala wa la ma qila lahu'. Strange people. Well, nowadays, I address the youth, because the elders, well, they know more than us, they don't need to be told. What happens with the youth is that when four friends meet, it often happens that out of those four, let's say, three are irreligious. Only one is religious. So, I am talking about friends. Yes. So when four friends meet, three are mostly irreligious, they have no connection with religion. Only one has religion. So these three friends, they swear, they do these things, I mean, their home education is like that, their upbringing is like that. And if we go deeper into the Hadith, and present it to you, sometimes I am even afraid to speak. It is found in traditions that if you see someone swearing a lot, understand that Satan was a partner in his birth. Shirk and Satan, in the Hadith. Shirk and Satan, Satan was a partner in his birth. Because Satan, there is a verse in Surah Bani Israil, Satan had asked Allah, 'Give me permission to be a partner in the birth of humans.' Allah said, 'Okay, granted.' Satan had asked for about 12-13 things. Allah gave him everything. He said, 'I worshipped You for so many years, so I should get some reward for it, shouldn't I?' Allah said, 'Okay, ask.' But whatever it is, it will all be worldly things, nothing of the Hereafter. You will not get anything of the Hereafter, you will get everything of the world. He kept asking, and Allah kept giving. If Allah gives the opportunity in some other gathering, I will tell you what Satan asked for and what Allah gave. One of those things was to be a partner in their birth. The Imam says that if you want to recognize whether Satan is a partner in someone's birth or not, what is the way to do it? How will you know? If he swears. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Meaning, there is some fault, there is a problem somewhere. Look, a defective piece is a defective piece. Now, what the root of it is, only Allah knows best. Anyway, so as I was presenting to you, a man came and started swearing at Qambar. Look, this is an incident in Kufa. Qambar is the servant and slave of Maula (Ali). And he is a young man, Qambar is a very strong, powerful man. He is not ordinary. A powerful man. And this man comes and swears at Qambar. As soon as he did, Qambar stood up, and as it happens with our attitude, if he gives two abuses, we give four. Qambar also thought, 'Let me fix him now.' As soon as Qambar stood up to swear back, the Imam stopped him, 'Qambar, sit down. Qambar, sit down.' Qambar sat down, it was the order of the Maula, he sat down. The Maula said, 'Qambar, the biggest punishment for such a person is that you remain silent. Remain silent, do not answer him at all. There can be no greater punishment for him than this.' It is the saying of the Maula. People of the world are swearing, they are swearing. And nowadays, online swearing is common, right? This is it. Okay, no problem. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. 'Wa yatajawazu 'amman zalam'—the Prophet says, and if someone snatches his right or oppresses him, he ignores it, he overlooks it. 'Okay, no problem, I have taken it here, I will take it from him in the Hereafter. You have taken it in this world, you have snatched it in this world, no problem, I will take it in the Hereafter.' 'Wa yatawada'u liman huwa dunahu'—the Prophet says, and he is completely humble before those who are lower than him in status or rank. This is a very difficult thing, yes. Those who are lower in rank, in any respect. For example, a boss, he should be humble before his juniors. Look, if he is humble before his boss, what is the big deal? He has to be. But if he is humble before his juniors. And think, take the example from the Quran here. The Quran says, Allah commands the Prophet, 'Wakhfid janahaka lil-mu'minin'—O Prophet, who is the Prophet? The Prophet is the source of creation. 'Awwalo ma khalaq Allah', he is the first creation of Allah. He is the purpose of the universe, the target of the universe, for whom Allah created the entire universe, that is the essence of the Prophet. Is it clear to you? The Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, the greatest among the Ulul 'Azm. The entire universe, there is no one greater than him. I mean, so great that we cannot even think, we cannot even imagine. But Allah commands that Prophet, 'Wakhfid janahaka lil-mu'minin'—when the believers come before you, lower your shoulders. Meaning, present yourself before them with complete humility. It is strange. With complete humility, 'Wakhfid janahaka lil-mu'minin'. Of course, in another verse, it is explained a bit more, 'Wakhfid janahaka limanittaba'aka minal-mu'minin'—be humble before those believers who follow you. Be completely humble before them. So look here, 'Yatawada'u liman dunahu', the one who is a junior, who is lower than him, he should not say, 'I am a senior.' That is why Islam provided training, look, what is the method of Islamic training? Greet the younger ones, so that they learn to greet. Yes. We say later, 'Oh, do you know that so-and-so person is very rude, that child is very rude.' A person asks, 'Why is he rude?' We said, 'He did not greet us.' He did not greet you? Well, you should have greeted him, right? 'Oh, how can I? I am a senior.' This senior-junior thing is itself Satanic. This is itself Satanic. 'I am older, he should greet me. He didn't, so I didn't.' This is not the culture, not the Islamic culture. That is why what is found in the traditions? The one who is riding—in those days there were no cars, meaning the rider—should greet the one who is walking. The one who is walking on foot. The rider should greet the one walking on foot. Look at the training of Islam. After that, he says, and with those who are senior to you, compete with them to get ahead in good deeds. Get ahead of them in good deeds. This is a sign of intellect. A sign of intellect. Meaning, the one who is above him, who is his senior, he should try that if he is doing 10 good deeds, then he should do 12. If he does 12, then he should do 14. One should try. 'Fi talabul mazhar'. And after that, this next point is very important. 'Idha arada ayyatakallama tadabbara'—when he intends to speak, to have a conversation, he reflects. He thinks. He thinks before speaking. The Maula of the universe says that until you speak, your words are in your possession, under your control. And as soon as you speak, you come under the control of your words. And he says, 'Al-mar'u makhbu'un tahta lisanihi'—man is hidden under his tongue. You will know him by his words. Insha'Allah, if there is time, we will explain it a bit. So whenever you have to say something, think first. Think, stop and speak. There should be no haste, no haste in speaking. 'Fa-in kana khayran takallama fa-ghanim'—if it is a good thing, then he will speak and consider it a gain. Meaning, he will benefit from it. 'Wa-in kana sharran sakata fa-salim'—and if the matter is bad, then he will remain silent. He will remain silent. And in this way, he will remain safe. Meaning, always think before speaking. And always keep this in mind. What is the principle in it? That if someone says this to me, how will I feel? If this same thing, I am in his place and he is in mine. If he says this to me, how will he feel? So how will I feel? If he says that to me. This is very important. So he says that if it is a bad thing, backbiting, why backbite, brother? So don't, don't engage in useless talk, sitting around with nothing to do. So you are bringing up someone's matter, anyone's, this third-person talk. Firstly, whenever you sit, avoid talking about other humans as much as possible. You should either discuss work or discuss concepts, that 'this is the work, this is the concept.' Meaning, discuss work, talk should be about work. How to make work better? Talking about humans, because when it comes to talking about humans, mostly, mostly it will happen, more often than not, that there will be backbiting in it. There will be some evil about him. There will be something. Sometimes even lies will be added. Because, anyway, it is a tongue, it is like an animal, so it doesn't stay under human control. Once it starts running, like a horse, an unbridled horse. Once it starts running, it doesn't stay under anyone's control. So the Prophet says that if it is a bad thing, remain silent. 'Wa-in 'aradat lahu fitnatun ista'sama billah'—when a trial comes, when there is a trial from all sides, he clings to Allah. He holds onto Allah firmly. The Quran says, 'Wa'tasimu bi-hablillahi jami'an wa la tafarraqu'—look, hold onto the rope of Allah firmly. And do not divide among yourselves. Hold onto the rope of Allah firmly. The Ahlulbayt are the rope of Allah. And how did you know about the Ahlulbayt? Through their teachings. Through their teachings, about which I spoke to you yesterday, I don't want to repeat it now. But the closer you get to the teachings, the safer you will remain. 'Wa-amsaka yaddahu wa lisanahu'—and when there is a trial from all sides, there should be control over the tongue and control over the hands. Meaning, what you are saying, what you are writing. Or who you are shaking hands with, that is also important. Because the hand is a very dangerous thing. Who are you shaking hands with? Are you not shaking hands with the wrong person? Is it not that he is an enemy of religion, and we have shaken hands with him? This is a very dangerous thing. But anyway, look, there is a trial, that is why the very first Hadith of Nahjul Balagha, what is it? This is it, right? The 'Kalimat-e-Qisar', the third part of Nahjul Balagha, which are the short sayings. You know, I am saying for the children, that Nahjul Balagha is in three parts. The first part is what? Sermons, speeches of Ali (a.s.). The second part is what? Letters. And the third part is what? 'Kalimat-e-Qisar', meaning short sayings, short statements, small statements. The very first statement of it is this, 'Fi al-fitnati kun ka-ibnil labun'—when there is a trial from all sides, the Prophet is also talking about trial, then become like the young camel whose milk cannot be milked, and no one can ride on it. No one can ride it. And no one can milk it. No one can benefit from it. And no one can force any burden on it, 'No, you have to do this.' When a person thinks, 'What is the use of taking work from this?', then it is of no use. Meaning, this huge sentence itself, what we just read to you, is just one sentence. But the commentators of Nahjul Balagha have written many pages on it. Many pages. For just one sentence, how many meanings it has. Just one sentence. So here the Prophet says to cling to Allah. Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says to become such that no one can even take advantage of you. "Wa idha ra'a fadilatan intahaza biha" - When he sees a virtue, as I mentioned to you yesterday, 'fadhilat' means any opportunity he gets, he takes advantage of it. He uses that virtue, that opportunity. A Momin is one who does not let an opportunity slip away. If he gets an opportunity to do a good deed, he immediately uses it. He does not look right or left. Whatever strength or power he has, he uses it. "Wala yabdu minhul-hirsu" - And he is never greedy. He is never greedy for the world. If he has greed, what is it for? It is for the Hereafter. If he is greedy, it is for the Hereafter. He is not greedy for the world at all. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says these are the 10 conditions that must be found in everyone. If you want to recognize a wise person, recognize him by this. Just one last sentence for your service: Hazrat-e-Amir Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) says that a wise person is one who is always awake from 'ghaflah' (negligence). Meaning, he does not fall into the sleep of negligence. Negligence, or 'ghaflah', is a vast subject in itself. There are hundreds of hadiths on this topic. It requires a separate discussion; there is no time for it here. I will just give a hint, as I hinted a little yesterday, and again today. For example, those things in the world that distance a human from Allah are called negligence. Everything that distances a human from Allah. In the Quran, they have been given different names. One is called 'lahw', 'lahw' meaning vain things, useless things. That is called 'lahw'. The second name given to it is 'la'ib', 'la'ib' meaning play and sport. Play and sport. This is the work of Satan. Satan keeps a human so engrossed in it that the human drowns in it completely. He gets so lost in it that he forgets Allah. So, Alhamdulillah, the World Cup is going on. Children stay awake late at night to watch the match. For the World Cup, Alhamdulillah. If you ask these same children to wake up for Namaz-e-Shab, then for that, if... Even if you have to call the fire brigade to spray water, they might not wake up quickly. Satan is so completely dominant over the children that they don't see anything else. Yes, but they will wake up for that. How is Satan dominant? Satan is dominant and overwhelming in this way. The word the Quran used is 'la'ib'. The Quran has many verses in this regard, though it is not our topic to read all those verses now. For example, 'la hiyatun qulubuhum' and 'wa la'ibun wa la'ibun', it is a Quranic verse. In praise of the Ahlulbayt, the Quran says in Surah Nur, 'Rijalun' (men) - the Ahlulbayt are those men, 'la tulhihim tijaratun wa la bay'un an dhikrillahi wa iqamis salati wa itayiz zakah'. These are those men. These are those men whom trade and buying-selling do not distance from the remembrance of Allah. They are not distanced from the remembrance of Allah. And no worldly power can stop them from praying and giving Zakat; they are infallible. So, in any case, we should look at this. The Mawla says, this is the saying of Hazrat-e-Amir, and he says, 'wa ta'ahhaba lirihlati', he prepares for his journey. He has to travel now, a long journey. Who knows how long the Barzakh is? After death—everyone has to die, and nowadays, as you know, after COVID, so many young people are dying. Some are 30, some 35, some 40, some 45; you see how many people are dying. There is no guarantee for anyone. And once they die, the Barzakh begins. No one knows how long the Barzakh will last. No one knows when the Day of Judgment will be. God forbid, if one goes to Hell in the Barzakh, the Imam says, 'In this Day of Judgment, we will intercede for you, but for the Barzakh, you will have to make arrangements yourself.' The Imam says, 'We only fear for you regarding the Barzakh, that is all. We will take you to Paradise, Insha'Allah. But the Barzakh is a dangerous thing.' There is a narration, 'Akhafu alaykumul Barzakh' (I fear the Barzakh for you). The Imam, the Infallible Imam, fears it. Did you notice? After that, the Imam says, 'wa amma', this is the sign of a wise person, 'wa amma aradda iqamati'. And the place that is his permanent home, he cultivates it; he works for it from here. Where he has to live forever. 'Hum fiha khalidun' is the Quranic term. He has to live there forever. For the eternal abode, the home where he must live forever, there is no preparation. So remember that the best preparation, the best thing—look, what are our provisions and what are our deeds? If there is anything, it is this 'Gham-e-Hussain' (Grief of Hussain). If a person holds onto this grief, does not leave this grief, and remains busy in the grief of Hussain throughout his life, which is the ultimate good—the entirety of goodness is the grief of Hussain, the remembrance of Hussain—then this is the thing that can become the cause of a person's salvation. And that is why you see that when Hussain left Medina, he told the people of Medina, 'Inni lam akhruj ashran wala batran wala mufsidan wala zaliman.' Not out of arrogance, not out of vanity. Neither to spread oppression nor to spread corruption. 'Bal innama kharajtu li talabil islahi fi ummati jaddi Rasulillahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi.' I am leaving so that I can reform the Ummah of my grandfather. I want to reform them. 'Uridu an amura bil ma'rufi wa anha anil munkari wa asira bi sirati abi Ali ibn Abi Talib.' My intention is to enjoin good, forbid evil, and follow the path of my noble father, Ali ibn Abi Talib. On the 28th of Rajab, Hussain left Medina. Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Kufi narrates that by chance, I reached Medina on the same day Hussain was leaving. He was leaving Medina that very day. I saw that sadness had spread everywhere. People were disappointed. I asked, 'What is this sadness?' People asked, 'Are you a stranger?' I said, 'I am a resident of Kufa.' So the people said, 'The life of Medina, the soul of Medina, Hussain ibn Ali is leaving Medina.' Muhammad ibn Sinan says that I thought, 'Let me also see how the people of Medina bid farewell to Hussain ibn Ali.' When I reached near the house of nobility, I saw that there was a huge crowd there. A huge crowd, people were coming to see how Hussain was leaving Medina. Just a little while later, two youths came out of the house. They pushed the crowd back and said, 'Move back, move back! The ladies are coming out, the ladies are about to mount, everyone move back! The daughters of the Prophet are about to mount.' They pushed the crowd back, and one by one, the camels came, and one by one, the ladies mounted. He said that I saw another lady come out, and when she mounted, I saw a 13-year-old boy helping her mount. Very young. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the orphan of Hasan, Qasim, and he is helping his mother, Umm Farwa, mount.' Not much time had passed when another noble lady emerged. And when she did, another youth stepped forward and helped her mount. I said, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the son of Hussain, the likeness of the Prophet, Ali Akbar, helping his mother, Umm Laila, mount.' A little while later, another noble lady emerged, and a sturdy, strong youth stepped forward and helped her mount. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the younger daughter of Ali, Umm Kulthum, and the one helping her is Abbas, the Moon of the Bani Hashim.' By now, as all the ladies were mounting, they were mounting the litters, Hussain was sitting on a chair, and Hussain was overseeing. Suddenly, Muhammad ibn Sinan says that as one lady emerged, Hussain stood up from his chair. The youths of Bani Hashim ran. Someone held the sandals, someone held the arm, someone removed the curtain of the litter, and helped the lady mount. I asked, 'Who is this?' They said, 'This is the elder daughter of Ali, this is Zainab.' Now, when all the ladies had mounted, Hussain said, 'Ya Abbas, qaddim jawadi.' 'Abbas, now bring my mount, bring my horse.' Abbas stepped forward and helped Hussain mount. I will ask, 'Mawla, there was such great arrangement here.' I will ask the Princess, 'Princess Zainab, oh, there was such great arrangement here, what will happen on the 11th of Muharram?' And I will ask Imam Hussain, 'Mawla, oh, this is the 28th of Rajab, but on the afternoon of Ashura, when Hussain comes after his final farewell, he looks to the right, he looks to the left, there is no one. He says, 'Ayyukum yuqaddimu jawadi?' 'Who among you will help me mount?' No one will come from the banks of the Euphrates, but yes, Zainab will come out. 'Brother, do not worry, Zainab is still alive, Zainab will help you mount.' Zainab helped him mount... He mounted. But when it was time to fall from the horse, Fatima is standing with her hands outstretched. 'Come, my son,' the mother has come to the battlefield to welcome Hussain. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdu lillahi rabbil 'alamin, wa saya'lamulladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, 'ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are troubled. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant children to those who are childless, righteous and pious children. Return those who are far from their homeland safely. Grant complete and immediate healing to those who are sick. Especially those who have requested prayers, grant them complete and immediate healing. O Lord, protect the great scholars and the Maraje-e-Izam. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. O Lord, protect the holy shrines. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the Hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Hur ibn Yazid al-Riyahi
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with a poetic account of the bravery and eventual martyrdom of Hur ibn Yazid al-Riyahi on the battlefield of Karbala.

chapters.title: Imam Hussain's Final Moments with Hur
chapters.summary: Imam Hussain arrives at the side of the dying Hur, who finds peace and spiritual vision in the presence of the Imam before passing away.

chapters.title: Racing Towards Goodness and the Love of Hussain
chapters.summary: The speaker transitions to a theological discussion on the Quranic command to race toward goodness, identifying the love of Imam Hussain as the ultimate source of all good.

chapters.title: The Definition of Intellect in Islamic Tradition
chapters.summary: The speaker explores the definition of intellect (Aql) as taught by the Imams, emphasizing the importance of guarding one's heart with divine knowledge.

chapters.title: The Quranic Emphasis on Intellect
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the importance of intellect (Aql) in Islamic scholarship and its frequent mention in the Quran, noting its role as a divine gift.

chapters.title: Defining Aql and the Nafs
chapters.summary: Intellect is described as a tether for the human soul, which is naturally prone to evil, and acts as a barrier against sinful behavior.

chapters.title: The Divine Origin and Levels of Intellect
chapters.summary: Intellect is a direct creation of divine light, and its varying levels of capacity in individuals are determined by the timing of its bestowal.

chapters.title: The Excellence of Intellect
chapters.summary: Intellect is considered the greatest blessing from Allah, providing honor, guidance, and truthfulness to those who possess it.

chapters.title: Defining the Intellect and Learning from Experience
chapters.summary: The lecturer defines intellect as a light derived from the Quran and Ahlulbayt, emphasizing that a wise person learns from experience to avoid repeating mistakes.

chapters.title: Alignment of Words and Deeds
chapters.summary: A core sign of an intellectual is the consistency between their speech and actions, as hypocrisy is condemned in both religious and social contexts.

chapters.title: Practicality vs. Empty Hopes
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights that an intellectual relies on concrete actions rather than empty plans, contrasting the wise with those who only build castles in the air.

chapters.title: Patience and Response to Ignorance
chapters.summary: True intellect is demonstrated by maintaining patience and composure when dealing with ignorant behavior, choosing peace over engaging in futile arguments.

chapters.title: Controlling the Tongue and Responding to Abuse
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the importance of controlling one's speech and avoiding vulgarity, citing the example of Qambar, who was instructed by Imam Ali to remain silent in the face of verbal abuse.

chapters.title: Humility and Social Conduct
chapters.summary: This section explores the necessity of humility toward those of lower status and the importance of greeting others regardless of social rank, framing this as a core Islamic value.

chapters.title: Reflective Speech and Avoiding Backbiting
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes the need to think before speaking, noting that silence is a safeguard against sin, especially regarding backbiting and idle gossip about others.

chapters.title: Holding Fast to Allah During Trials
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes by advising believers to cling to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt and maintain control over their words and actions when facing trials and temptations.

chapters.title: Characteristics of a Wise Person
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the traits of a wise person, emphasizing the avoidance of negligence (ghaflah) and the importance of seizing opportunities for good deeds.

chapters.title: Negligence and Worldly Distractions
chapters.summary: The lecture warns against becoming engrossed in vain worldly activities that distance a believer from Allah, contrasting this with the steadfastness of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Preparing for the Eternal Journey
chapters.summary: The speaker highlights the necessity of preparing for the Barzakh and the afterlife, suggesting that holding onto the grief of Imam Hussain is a path to salvation.

chapters.title: The Departure of Imam Hussain from Medina
chapters.summary: The speaker narrates the emotional departure of Imam Hussain from Medina, detailing the respect shown by the Bani Hashim youths to the ladies of the Prophet's household.

chapters.title: The Final Moments and Closing Supplications
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the tragic final moments of Imam Hussain and concludes the session with collective prayers for the reappearance of the Imam and the well-being of the community.

title: Kaun Se A'maal Jannat Mein Sab Se Zyada Kaam Aayenge?  [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture recounts a narration from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) regarding a dream about his uncle Hamza and cousin Jafar in Paradise. They reveal that three specific deeds are the most beneficial for attaining rewards in the afterlife. The speaker emphasizes the spiritual significance of these actions for every believer.
content:
It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Last night in a dream, I saw my uncle Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib and my cousin Jafar ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Before them was a tray containing berries. They ate from it for a while, then the berries were replaced by grapes. After eating for a while longer, the grapes were replaced by fresh dates. I approached them and asked, "Which of your deeds are most beneficial? What actions did you perform that have brought these heavenly fruits before you, and how are you enjoying the blessings of Paradise in this manner? What are the most beneficial deeds in Paradise?" They both replied, "Our parents are sacrificed for our deeds. We found three deeds to be the most beneficial in Paradise." The first one they mentioned was sending blessings (Salawat) upon the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' The first was sending blessings (Salawat) upon the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). The second, they said, was giving water to the thirsty. And the third was the love for Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). These are the three most beneficial and rewarding deeds for a person in Paradise: sending Salawat upon the Messenger, giving water to the thirsty, and the love of Ali (a.s.).

title: Ask anything from your Imam
excerpt: This lecture recounts a miraculous event involving Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and his companion, Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari. While imprisoned, Abu Hashim received a divine promise of release from the Imam, which manifested exactly as predicted. The story highlights the Imam's omniscience and his compassionate nature, encouraging believers to approach the Ahlulbayt with their needs without hesitation or shame.
content:
Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) once freed one of his Shia followers from prison and helped him. Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari states: 'I complained to Imam Abu Muhammad Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) about the hardships of imprisonment and the severity of the chains. In response, I received a letter from the Imam (a.s.) stating: "You will perform your Dhuhr prayer at your home today." It happened exactly as the Imam (a.s.) had written; I was released from prison at the time of Dhuhr and prayed at home. However, while I was in prison for several days, the thought had crossed my mind to ask the Imam (a.s.) for some financial help in my letter, but I felt ashamed and did not write it. As soon as I reached home, the Imam (a.s.) sent me 100 dinars with a letter saying: "When you are in need of something, do not be ashamed; ask. Whatever you desire, you shall receive."
Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) demonstrated his divine knowledge by predicting Abu Hashim's release.
Abu Hashim was released from prison exactly at the time of Dhuhr prayer as promised.
The Imam provided financial assistance to Abu Hashim even though he had not explicitly asked for it.

The relationship between the Imam and his followers is one of profound care and spiritual connection.
