title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#7 | Truth is the Criterion, Not Personalities  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi emphasizes that truth, rather than personalities, must be the ultimate criterion for spiritual recognition and guidance. He explores the central role of the Ahlulbayt as the 'Ark of Salvation' and the 'Gate of Repentance,' urging believers to prioritize divine truth over historical figures or charismatic leaders. The discussion highlights the necessity of absolute submission to the Imam's guidance and warns against the dangers of personality worship and historical inconsistency.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. This program is about the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The fragrance of this recognition is, Alhamdulillah, for the sake of understanding the true Islam. This is our seventh episode. In the previous episode, we discussed a young companion of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) who, despite his young age, defended the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and supported their Wilayah. Dear viewers, let us continue this journey of learning about the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and move forward to this seventh episode. As the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), said: 'Do not recognize the truth by people; rather, recognize the truth first, and then you will recognize its people.' It is our responsibility to recognize what the truth is. Wherever the truth is, we must be with it. According to the words of the Mawla, personalities should be recognized by the truth, not the other way around. Recognition should be through the truth; the truth does not need personalities to be recognized. This is the subject of our seventh episode: 'The Criterion is the Truth, not Personalities.' I invite the respected Dr. Samir to share his knowledge on this topic. I request everyone to recite a loud Salawat: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Whoever wants to follow my religion, whoever wants to walk on my path, and whoever wants to follow my Sunnah, must follow the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' This is the criterion. One must be careful about what they follow, as the religion should not be based on anything else. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the gate of repentance (Bab al-Hittah). Before talking about the gate of repentance, let us look at the historical context. There was a person who was famous for fabricating hadiths against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). He used to invent so many lies that he was eventually punished and placed in a location where his feet were shackled. Sometimes, such people would say things that, if followed, would lead one astray. As you have heard, the translation is clear: the example given is that anyone who follows the Messenger must follow the Imams of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), for these twelve Imams are superior to all. The second point is that their example is like the 'Gate of Repentance' (Bab al-Hittah). The word 'Hittah' comes from the root meaning to fall or to descend. It refers to the gate of the village mentioned in the Quran where one must enter while prostrating. Enter the gate while prostrating and say 'Hittah' (forgiveness), and We will forgive your sins and increase the reward for the righteous. Allah says that if they enter the gate in a state of prostration, saying 'Hittah', He will forgive their sins. This is the significance of the gate of repentance. But the judge, in a state of... Allah, Allah, Allah. At this door, the image, the name, the name that was inscribed was Muhammad and Allah. The late Yashindu Puja, etc., were all connected. And Allah commanded the Children of Israel to prostrate. In the interval of these names, in their respect, prostrate. So, prostrate to Allah, but I prostrate... why is there any objection? Why do you ask why we prostrate when we go to the shrines? Yes, and why do we prostrate in the shrines? We are not prostrating to the shrine; the prostration is for Allah. If we are placing our foreheads on the ground, we are doing it for Allah, but in respect of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Because if the name of Allah is alive, it is alive because of the Ahlulbayt, because of their sacrifices, their hard work, and this is why we place our foreheads [on the ground] when we go to the shrines, like when we go to the shrine of Imam Hussain (a.s.), when we go to the shrine of the Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.), to any... When we go to the shrine of the Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.), to any, to the shrine of any of the Ma'sumeen (a.s.), when we prostrate at their shrines, this prostration is not a prostration of worship. It is a prostration of respect. The Imam (a.s.) says that Allah commanded you to prostrate, 'wa-idkhulu al-baba sujjadan' (and enter the gate prostrating). And when you do this, you are confirming what your Prophets had told you earlier, that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his Ahlulbayt (a.s.) would be the ones to be respected, and they would be the ones to be followed. Now, its confirmation, its renewal is happening. See, this is the guidance, and this is the greatness. And their Wilayah is being mentioned. 'Wa-id qulna' (and when We said), that covenant which was taken from the Children of Israel, 'wa-id qulna udkhulu hadhihi al-qaryata' (and when We said, 'Enter this city'). This matter was for Muhammad and Ali (a.s.) and their Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And Allah says, 'wa-qulu hittatun' (and say, 'Relieve us of our burdens'). This is a part of it. 'Qulu inna sujjadan' (say, 'We are prostrating'). This is our prostration for Allah, but the respect is for them. For example, Muhammad and Ali (a.s.), this respect is... For example, Muhammad and Ali (a.s.), this respect is for Muhammad and Ali (a.s.), the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And what we are saying, 'wa-sanazidu al-muhsinin' (and We will increase [the reward of] the doers of good), this is for our sins to fall away. With this, our sins will be wiped away. I tell you, all your sins will be wiped away. So, the result is that we are in the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and all our sins will be wiped away. But as we mention the name of Muhammad and Ali (a.s.), and we do this... now some have started doing this, they say, 'What is this, just by taking the name?' So, for you, we are in it. If you feel bad, then it is a bit... Allah, we will keep you... 'nafir lakum khatayakum' (We will forgive your sins). From this tree, it was removed... 'Nafir lakum khatayakum' (We will forgive your sins). From this tree, it was removed. 'Wa-sanazidu al-muhsinin' (and We will increase [the reward of] the doers of good). Whatever your sins are, whatever sins you have committed, we will wipe them all away. 'Wa-sanazidu al-muhsinin' (and We will increase [the reward of] the doers of good). And those who were like you, who had not done good deeds, they used to do this and that... so we will increase their reward. 'Wa-id qulna' (and when We said)... 'fa-baddala alladhina zalamu' (but those who did wrong changed [the words]). Who did the wrong? Those who opposed the Wilayah. Allah says, 'This is how the Children of Israel's story goes.' But it happens that... they will not do it. They will not do it. And then after that... They did what they did, and they changed it. They changed the strategy. They were told to do something, but they did not do it. I had to go, what should I say? 'Faqulu hittatun' (say, 'Relieve us of our burdens'), and they did not do it like that. 'Wa-sujjadan' (and prostrating), they did not do it like that either. And what they were told to say, they did not say. 'Faqulu' (say), but they... look, instead of prostrating, they sat down and dragged themselves inside, saying, 'We are prostrating.' This is what the worst people of the time will do, who did this and that. And it is a sign of their humiliation. 'La-naghfiru lakum khatayakum' (We will forgive your sins). These people, we like them more. We will do this, and we will... this is all present in the Quran. Now look here... This is all present in the Quran. Now look here, if you look at this picture, look at this... 'udkhulu al-baba sujjadan' (enter the gate prostrating). Allah, Allah, Allah. Before the door of Allah, you prostrate and say 'hittatun' (relieve us of our burdens). 'Hittatun' (relieve us of our burdens). Is the wood superior, or is the one who is honored superior? The one who is the habit of Allah, who is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) of Allah, the first of Allah... so prostrating before a wooden door, and they will be taken along with them. If they are... and if they say Muhammad and Ali (a.s.), then will you... and they do it, but they do it... but this is a claim of love, but it is not the love that is required. So, this is the story of the whole Quran. Keep this Hadith in your mind, this... Keep this Hadith in your mind, keep this way in your mind. So, this Hadith, which is present with its explanation in our Sheikh Saduq's [books], and on the other side, when you come to its interpretation, the result will be different. The discussion is different. This is the Hadith that he climbed, and after climbing, he stood at the door of the Kaaba, and after that, he turned his back, his back, and after that, he said, 'Whoever knows me, knows me! And whoever does not know me, I am Abu Dharr! I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say: The example of my Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in this Ummah is like the Ark of Nuh (a.s.). Whoever boards this ship will be saved, whoever...' Whoever boards this ship will be saved. Whoever held onto the hem, whoever accepted the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), whoever accepted the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), he will be the only one to be saved. 'Wa-man takhallafa 'anha' (and whoever stays behind from it), whoever left the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and held onto the hem of others, he will be drowned. He will be destroyed. Whoever left the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be destroyed. So, do not say, 'I hold onto the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and I love others too, it's all good.' No, it is not like that. This is a clear Hadith. Abu Dharr (r.a.) says this, and keep the Hadith in mind. It is not yet... it is time. So, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, and Abu Dharr says, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say: Give my Ahlulbayt (a.s.) the same importance among you that the head has to the body. And give them the status that the eyes have to the face.' In reality, who is given more importance, the head or the eyes? 'Fa-innahu la yahdi al-jasadu illa bi-ra'sin' (because the body cannot walk on the right path if it does not have a head). If there is no head, how will the body walk? The body cannot walk without a head. If you separate the head from the body, the first thing is that there will be no life in that body. The first thing is that there will be no life in the body. So, the Ummah from which the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is separated, that Ummah will be dead, it will not be alive, it will be a corpse. The second thing is... And when the head is separated from the body, that body will be pulled by one rope after another, by the help of others. It will not walk by itself. It will only be pulled. And when it is pulled, it will be said, 'If this body is here, it is lifeless.' Similarly, the Ummah without the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be pulled like this, like a body without a head, it is pulled. And the third thing is, and the most important thing is, here the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said that if the head is not with the body... He said that if the head is not with the body, then the body will not be able to walk, there will be no life in it. Where will the guidance come from? And after that, he says, 'Wa-la yahdi al-jasadu illa bi-ra'sin' (and the body cannot be guided except with a head). And if there is a head, but if there are no eyes, then the person will be blind. Whoever is blind will not be able to walk, he will need help, someone to lead him. So, even if there is a head, but if there are no eyes, that Ummah will be a blind Ummah. There will be no one to show them the way, there will be no one to guide them. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the eyes. That is why, 'Innama anta mundhirun wa-likulli qawmin hadin' (You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide). The Prophet is only a warner, and for every nation, there is a guide, an Imam, a guide. The Imam guides. Who will be without a guide? They will not go anywhere. Remember this. Now, in this Hadith, why did Abu Dharr say, 'I am Abu Dharr, whoever recognized me, recognized me, and whoever did not recognize me, I am Abu Dharr, the companion of the Messenger'? Because the Prophet had said, 'Man 'arafani faqad 'arafa Allah, wa-man ankarani faqad ankara Allah' (Whoever recognizes me, recognizes Allah, and whoever denies me, denies Allah). There is no one more truthful than Abu Dharr (r.a.) in the entire universe, except for the Infallible Imams (a.s.). No one has walked on the earth or been shaded by the sky who is more truthful than Abu Dharr. And this is why it is said: 'Be with the truthful ones.' The Quran says: 'O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful ones.' Remember, you may do whatever you want in your worldly life, but you must hold onto the love of the truthful ones. This is why when Muawiyah built a very large palace, he invited all the companions, the Tabi'in, the scholars, and the reciters, and they all gathered there, eating and enjoying everything. They were all enjoying themselves, and suddenly, Abu Dharr (r.a.) entered. When the people saw him, some might have been happy, but the faces of the others turned pale. When a truthful person enters a gathering, the liars are always afraid that he might speak the truth. Muawiyah thought the best way to handle this was to welcome him, so he said, 'Welcome, O Abu Dharr! How do you like our palace?' Abu Dharr looked at it and asked, 'Did you build this palace with your own money, or with public money from the Bayt al-Mal? If you say you built it with your own money, you did not need such a massive palace; someone else would have needed it. And if you built it with public money, then it is forbidden (haram), and you have betrayed the trust.' In front of everyone, Abu Dharr challenged him. He felt insulted in front of the whole gathering. Muawiyah was a king, so he immediately sent a message to Medina, asking, 'Who have you sent to me? Take him away from here.' He was then sent to Syria, and when he became a problem there, he was sent back to Medina. He said, 'I will not keep him.' This was Abu Dharr. This Hadith clearly explains what the truth is. It is like the Ark of Nuh (a.s.); whoever held onto it was saved, and whoever strayed was destroyed. There is no doubt about this; it is only and only about the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (a.s.). But there was a major problem among the Muslims, and it still exists today. There was a major problem, and it still exists today. It has become a problem for us as well. But generally, the problem with the Muslims throughout history was that they abandoned the Truth and started worshipping personalities. This is why, when the Quran was raised on spears, these Muslims—whose faith was superficial—started attacking Ali (a.s.). They said, 'Stop the war! We are Muslims, and they are Muslims. We are all Muslims.' These people thought they understood Islam better than Ali (a.s.). And this is what happened in history; those who abandoned Ali (a.s.) were the ones who thought they understood Islam better than him. When the Mawla said, 'Do not be deceived, the Quran has not reached their throats; they do not understand the Quran,' they were not ready to listen. They were the Kharijites who were used to martyr the Commander of the Faithful. Think about this: those who were used—the name of Ibn Muljam and others came up—they and their companions, may Allah's curse be upon them, were the ones who martyred the Mawla. But those who sent them were the ones sitting in Syria. Remember this; this is a very powerful historical fact. There is research on this, but Muslims do not understand the reality, so they are deceived. There is a book called 'Sulh al-Hasan' by Radi Aal-e-Yasin. This book is a powerful work on Wilayah, and the narrator for the author was... I heard this from the narrator, and I took this book to Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was there, and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) was there. He says, 'I took this book to the Imam, and I saw that he was sitting with Umm Salama (s.a.), who was truly a believer and a noble lady.' This Umm Salama was the one who was married to someone else before the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and after he passed away... After he passed away, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) married her. She was also sitting there. She was one of those raised in the house of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself raised her. This is important. He says, 'I asked, what do you say about this book?' The Imam said, 'Whatever the narrator said is true; may Allah's mercy be upon him.' The Imam confirms it easily because it contains the presence of Allah and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). One should think about this: if this book is true, then who is actually being honored? It is the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Allah (s.w.t.). Whoever honors the Infallible honors the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and whoever honors the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) honors Allah (s.w.t.). Therefore, they should realize that we cannot easily dismiss these Hadiths. The Imam said, 'What he said is true; this book is correct.' Now, listen to this very important point. I said, 'O Imam, there are some things in this book that make my heart feel constricted; I feel depressed. It feels like the entire Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is doomed, that everyone—all the companions, all the Tabi'in—except for those who held onto the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), will be destroyed. Reading this makes my heart heavy.' The Imam replied, 'O brother of the family of...' The Imam, while referring to his family, said, 'Have you not heard the Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? My Ahlulbayt are like the Ark of Nuh (a.s.); whoever boards it will be saved, and whoever stays behind will be drowned and destroyed. And have you not heard the Hadith where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'The example of my Ahlulbayt among you is like the Gate of Repentance of the Children of Israel; whoever enters it will be forgiven'? Entering the gate means accepting Wilayah. Prostrating means submission. It is nothing but that. Whoever does this will be saved.' Whoever does this will be saved. So, someone asked, 'Have you heard this?' He said, 'I heard it from Abu Dharr (r.a.) when he was holding the handle of the door of the Kaaba, calling out that he heard it from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).' We asked, 'And from whom did you hear it?' He said, 'I heard it from Hasan al-Basri.' Hasan al-Basri was someone who saw the time of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) in his youth, but he ran away to the jungles when the Mawla needed help. When the Mawla was teaching, he would take notes like a student. He would write down what the Mawla said, but then he would attribute it to himself and teach it to others. He was deceiving the Ummah. This channel, this content, this city, this Ummah is included. This resident is included, who was in Bani Israel. This is the content of that age. The only difference is that the content of that time said, 'Do not touch the red chili, do not touch the sexual organs.' The account that was created for worship in Bani Israel, they have left it and come to the symptoms. Allah is saying, and this says, 'Do not fight, do not fight,' and this is running away from the wild roots. Allah will repair its doubts in this way. Some people will feel bad that some people arrange for others' speeches, but our point is that Hasan al-Basri is ready. And in fact, you know, this Hasan al-Basri, this is the one who was the biggest scholar of his time, the biggest scholar of Sindh. He did not even consider the next one. So someone asked him, 'How did you become such a great scholar from Hasan al-Basri?' So he said, 'What should I do? I used to go to his class, and sometimes he would talk about the mind, sometimes about free will, sometimes he was this, sometimes he was that. He had no permanent stance. So I got confused listening to him, so I said, 'Forget it, I don't want to stay there.' And leaving Sindh, I became a complete Sindhi.' This is present in the books of the scholars, it is present in the books regarding Hasan al-Basri. This is something special for you, it will be surprising. It will be surprising for you, but it is very important that people keep recognizing. Similarly, look, people are grateful. One is a 'Fasiq' (sinner), one is a 'Jahil' (ignorant). 'Jahil' is one who has not reached your level of knowledge, meaning he does not know things, he cannot understand. He does not know, he has not heard, the matter has not reached him. This is not a university bill, he does not know. But 'Fasiq' is one who knows the truth but denies it, knowing it. Hasan al-Basri, whom we heard, who was a 'Mudassir' (one who changes his colors), and these people are very dangerous. Until yesterday, he was one thing, then another, then a third. Their stance keeps changing regularly. They keep changing their fans, their books. These people are very dangerous because they have no firm foundation. In today's time, there are many such people. Yesterday they said something else, today they say something else. Yesterday they were with someone, today they say something else. In this way, you will find these people even today, and they are all over the world. It was about avoiding the state, and this Hasan al-Basri was saying to the ruler, 'I will write your praises,' but he used to help the Banu Marwan. The Banu Marwan, who were oppressive rulers. That is why in history we find the sentence that 'the sword of Hajjaj would be today.' If we look, the sword of Hajjaj is... If we look, the sword of Hajjaj is the sword of Hajjaj, and the tongue of Hasan al-Basri. The Umayyad rule was established, the Marwan rule was established, the Marwan rule that was established is because of the sword of Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, because of the massacre he committed, and because of the tongue of Hasan al-Basri, because of his power and support, he used to say all these things. Then he said, 'In the bracket, he heard something amazing.' Then he asked, 'From whom did you hear it?' He said, 'I heard it from Sahih, I heard it from so-and-so, I heard it from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.' When we heard it from Abu Dharr, and this was an Arab family, and when we heard it from Abu Dharr, and this was all completed, then the two elders who were sitting there, they said, 'By God, we have also heard both these hadiths. We have heard them from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).' And we have heard this hadith from Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as well, and from Miqdad, and from Salman. And they added references, and the two elders who were sitting there, Humay ibn Sa... The two elders who were sitting there, Humay ibn Sa and Abu Tufayl Amir, confirmed the hadith. Then after that, Salman also confirmed it. Then he turned towards me and said, 'Look at me.' And besides this, I have heard this hadith directly from the words of those who are the most virtuous, meaning Abu Dharr, Salman, Miqdad, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). I heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that my Ahlulbayt are like the Ark of Nuh, and the example of my Ahlulbayt is like the Ark. chapters.title: Truth as the Criterion for Recognition
chapters.summary: The lecture emphasizes that truth must be the standard for identifying individuals, rather than using personalities to define the truth.

chapters.title: The Ahlulbayt as the Gate of Repentance
chapters.summary: The speaker explains the concept of 'Bab al-Hittah' (Gate of Repentance) and its connection to following the Ahlulbayt as a means of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Prostration and Respect for the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that prostration at the shrines of the Ma'sumeen is an act of respect for Allah's chosen ones, not an act of worship toward the shrines themselves.

chapters.title: The Ahlulbayt as the Ark of Salvation
chapters.summary: Using the analogy of the Ark of Nuh and the human body, the speaker highlights that the Ahlulbayt are essential for the spiritual life and salvation of the Ummah.

chapters.title: The Ummah and the Need for Guidance
chapters.summary: The speaker compares the Ummah without the Ahlulbayt to a headless body, emphasizing that true guidance requires the eyes of the Imams.

chapters.title: Abu Dharr and the Truth
chapters.summary: Abu Dharr is highlighted as a paragon of truth who fearlessly challenged the corruption of Muawiyah, serving as a model for standing by the truthful.

chapters.title: The Danger of Personality Worship
chapters.summary: The lecture warns against the historical tendency of Muslims to abandon the objective truth of Ali ibn Abi Talib in favor of superficial personality worship.

chapters.title: The Ark of Salvation
chapters.summary: The Imam confirms the necessity of Wilayah, comparing the Ahlulbayt to the Ark of Nuh and the Gate of Repentance for the salvation of the Ummah.

chapters.title: Dangers of Inconsistent Personalities
chapters.summary: The speaker warns against individuals who change their stances and allegiances, citing historical figures like Hasan al-Basri as examples of those who supported oppressive rulers.

chapters.title: The Ark of Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) emphasizes the importance of the Hadith of the Ark of Nuh, comparing the Ahlulbayt to the salvation provided by the Ark.

chapters.title: The Devotion of Shurtat al-Khamis
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the unwavering loyalty and absolute obedience of the Shurtat al-Khamis, who served Imam Ali (a.s.) without questioning his commands.

chapters.title: Truth Over Personalities
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes that personalities are only significant if they uphold the truth, urging followers to emulate the steadfastness of the companions of the Imam.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 5 | Apparent Etiquette of reciting the Holy Quran
excerpt: This webinar session explores the essential etiquette, or Adab, required when engaging with the Holy Quran. It emphasizes that proper conduct and spiritual preparation are vital for a meaningful connection with the divine text, covering both physical requirements like Wudu and the importance of respectful posture. The lecture also addresses practical questions regarding digital versus physical copies of the Quran and highlights the significance of reciting with sincerity and beauty.

Therefore, saying that we should stop reciting the Quran during travel is not something I would recommend. You should continue to recite while maintaining as much etiquette as possible. The second question is: is it necessary to perform wudu for a mobile phone, and if the mobile... Is it necessary to perform wudu for a mobile phone, and what if the mobile screen is touched? There is a difference between the two. One is reciting the Quran from the screen, and the other is touching the screen while reciting. Touching the screen is not considered touching the Quran itself, so you can do it. The last question is: if one has made the intention of reciting the Quran, can one perform other tasks simultaneously? Yes, if you have made the intention, you should focus on the recitation. Regarding the intention, it is said that you should use one thing for the sake of prayer. If someone is performing an act in that manner, they can do it. We have reached the end of today's session, Alhamdulillah. But as is the custom, after every session, we have our quiz series. The winners of yesterday's quiz—meaning the ten people who answered all the questions of Session 4 correctly first—are: Chashma Wala Patel, Saif Ali, EMS Mehroli, Sadaf Fatma, Sakina Fatma, Allah, and Mohammad Jawad. These are the people who answered all questions correctly first. There are other individuals who also answered correctly, and their names will be updated on the social media handles of 'The Strong Rock'. You can see the names of the other winners of yesterday's quiz on those platforms. Tomorrow, Insha'Allah, I consider it necessary to mention two things regarding the quiz. I request you to listen carefully: the quiz series will continue throughout the entire duration of the sessions. After every session, a quiz related to that specific session will be sent the next day. The quiz consists of brief questions—five to seven short questions—related to the previous session. It will be announced every day. Even if your name is not announced in a particular session—for instance, if you answered all questions correctly but your name was not called—it does not mean you cannot win a prize. As we announced earlier, after the completion of all ten quizzes, those who have answered correctly the most times across all ten quizzes will be eligible for the prize, Insha'Allah. So, even if your name is not called here, if you have answered the questions correctly, you will definitely be among those eligible for the prize. Finally, thanking everyone, we hope that tomorrow, Insha'Allah, you will join us again. The second part of this topic, regarding the etiquette of recitation, was discussed today. Tomorrow, Insha'Allah, we will discuss the inner and spiritual etiquettes of the Quran with Janab Baqir Sahab. We conclude with: 'Audhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim, Alhamdulillahir-Rabbil-Alamin, Astaghfirullahal-Azim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, Muhammad...' Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, Muhammad... [Recitation of Quranic verses]. Thank you very much. We will meet at 10:30 PM India time.

title: EP09 | Marefat-e-Imam (a.s.) Ki Zaroorat | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of recognizing the Imam of the time, emphasizing that such recognition is a fundamental obligation for every believer. It details the critical attributes of an Imam, including divine appointment, absolute infallibility (Ma'sum), and superior knowledge, which are essential for guiding the community. The session warns that failing to recognize the Imam leads to a state of spiritual ignorance, or Jahiliyyah, and underscores the Imam's role as the ultimate representative of God on earth.
content:
TSR presents. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace and blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, assist us and do not let us perish. Greetings, viewers. Before we begin today's episode, let us see who the winners are of our second quiz of 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' (from episode 5 to episode 8), which are being announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Their names are on your screen: Syed Afsar Hussain from Jamshedpur, Syed Hasan from Bangalore, Syed Najma from Mumbai, Gulrez Azmi from Azamgarh, Rameez Fatima from Bangalore, Syeda Miqdad Zahra from Alipur, Dr. Shafi from Bangalore, Syed Moattar Fatima from Bangalore, Nazi Zahra from Bangalore, Syeda Kazima Farhat from Jaipur, Abbas Haider from Bangalore, Zeeshan Hussain from Budgam, Tazkira Bano from Alipur, Arzoo Sarwar from Alipur. Congratulations to all of you. Now, let us move on to our new episode today. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjah, son of Al-Hassan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers and supporters, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his purified family. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten his reappearance, and curse all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The discussion was about the importance of the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam, and the point had reached the connection between the recognition of Allah and the recognition of the Imam, which we discussed in the previous episode. Continuing that sequence, today, Insha'Allah, we will talk about the first thing: that keeping the importance of this knowledge in mind, we must understand that this is a matter for which no excuse is acceptable. If someone finds out once and realizes who the true Imam is—we are not yet on the topic of who the true Imam is, we are only having general discussions on Imamate—after finishing these general discussions, we will discuss whom the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed as his successor. So, once it becomes clear to us that the Prophet appointed a certain person as his successor, then following him and obeying him becomes obligatory for all of us, and then no excuse will be accepted for him. If we think of presenting any excuse for it, it will not be accepted. This is a very important thing to keep in mind. Now, look at this narration which I am presenting to you; it is from Al-Kafi, from the noble book Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 186, Kitab al-Hujjah. Bashir Attar is the narrator, and he says: I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: 'Nahnu qawmun faradallahu ta'atana' (We are a people whose obedience Allah has made obligatory). And you are those who must follow the one whose ignorance is not an excuse; no excuse will be accepted that 'we did not know.' Once the truth is clear, the matter is illuminated, and the evidence is before you, everyone should try. As I gave an example in the previous episode, if we go to live in a country, it is necessary for us to be aware of the laws of that country. It is not possible for us to go there, break the law, and then say we did not know. People would say, 'Brother, you should have known; you have come to live in this country, so it is obligatory upon you.' Similarly, when we are living in the kingdom of Allah, we must know who is the successor of God in this kingdom, who is not, and what characteristics that successor should have. We will recognize him—those details will come later—and that is why the importance of the recognition of the Imam is such that there are many famous narrations regarding it. You have heard many times: 'Man mata wa lam ya'rif imama zamanihi mata maytatan jahiliyyah' (Whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time dies the death of Jahiliyyah). Look, ignorance (Jahal) is one thing, and Jahiliyyah is another. Often people translate it as 'death of ignorance,' but no, ignorance is different. Jahiliyyah means he died the death of disbelief, hypocrisy, and misguidance. That is, he did not die upon Islam; he did not die a Muslim. It is possible for a Muslim to be ignorant, and there is not that much blame or evil in that. But Jahiliyyah means he is not even a Muslim. If his death was not upon Islam, then that is a different matter. So here, in 'Kamal al-Din', which is the book of Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), and this book was also written by Sheikh Saduq at the behest of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), there is a narration that Imam Hassan al-Askari (a.s.) narrates from his forefathers: 'Annal arda la takhlu min hujjatillahi 'ala khalqihi' (The earth can never be devoid of the Hujjah of Allah over His creation). The existence of a Hujjah, a representative of God—about whom we have already stated that after sending this representative, no excuse remains—the earth will never be devoid of such a representative. 'Wa anna man mata wa lam ya'rif imama zamanihi mata maytatan jahiliyyah' (And whoever dies without recognizing the Imam of his time dies the death of Jahiliyyah). That is, he died the death of disbelief, hypocrisy, and misguidance. Therefore, it is very important to recognize who is the representative of Allah on this face of the earth today. Who is it that teaches us the religion, who is the protector of the religion? The recognition of that person holds such importance. Otherwise, the recognition of any ruler or leader does not have such importance. And then the Imam said: 'Inna hadha haqqun kama annannahara haqqun' (This truth is as true as the day is true). Just as the day shines and no one can deny the day, in the same way, no one can deny this reality that the recognition of the Imam of the time is obligatory and everyone must recognize him, and in fact, our Imams are our delegation that is taking us to Allah. Meaning, this narration is very famous: 'Inna a'immatakum wafdukum' (Your Imams are your delegation). Where? 'Ilallah' (To Allah). In the previous episode, I mentioned the Quranic verse: 'Yawma nad'u kulla unasin bi-imamihim' (The day We will call every group of people with their Imam). We are moving forward under someone's guidance. These are our delegation, they are guiding us, they are leading us. So we have to see under whose guidance we are moving forward. 'Fanzuru man tufiduna fi dinikum wa san'atikum' (So look at whom you are following in your religion and your affairs). Just look at whose guidance, whose leadership, whose direction you are following to go to Allah. Taking your religion, taking your prayers—meaning taking your religion and your worship—to whom are you going? That is, under whose guidance are you going to Allah? You are going before that Being who is your Creator. The Hadith is saying exactly this. And you have to present your religion. And presenting this religion is not a game, not a sport, not amusement. Our entire hereafter depends on this. Paradise and Hell depend on this. Therefore, it is necessary that we see whom we are following, whom we are obeying. Now we come to an important topic: that Imam who has such importance, such emphasis, and about whom all these things have been said—that this is the recognition of the Imam, the recognition of Allah, the recognition of the Imam. And the Imam is the one who takes our delegation to Allah, and the Imam is the one for whom no excuse is accepted. His recognition is compulsory, and whoever does not recognize the Imam dies the death of Jahiliyyah. When there are so many things, it is also mentioned in the narrations what the qualities of this Imam are. What attributes should he have? So here, let us first read the attributes mentioned among the Shia. Insha'Allah, if granted the opportunity, we will also discuss what attributes are mentioned by others, by other Muslims, so that we can get an idea of whose view is closer to the religion, closer to the hereafter, closer to Allah, so that the matter becomes clear. So here is a very important Hadith I present to you, in which Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says in a narration: 'Qala Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.): Wal-imamu al-mustahaqqu lil-imamatih' (The Imam who is deserving of Imamate—deserving, meaning eligible). Meaning, the one who is entitled to be called an Imam. لَهُ عَلَامَاتٌ (He has signs). There are certain signs for him. There are certain sciences, certain symbols, and certain characteristics for him. There are certain attributes in him. Obviously, one cannot just make anyone an Imam. As I mentioned, the fate of the hereafter depends on this. So, who should it be? Who is that Imam? What characteristics should he possess? It is very important for us to look at these characteristics, and this is very crucial. So, the Mawla says: فَمِنْهَا أَنْ يُعْلَمَ أَنَّهُ مَعْصُوْمٌ (Among them is that it should be known that he is infallible). The first thing. This should be known, يُعْلَمَ (it should be known). Among these attributes, among these signs, what is the first thing? It should be known that he must be infallible. He should be infallible. And then the Mawla explains it: مَعْصُوْمٌ مِنَ الذُّنُوْبِ (He must be infallible from sins). He must be infallible from sins. كُلِّهَا (All of them). صَغِيْرِهَا وَكَبِيْرِهَا (Small or big). No small sin, no big sin. No sin at all. The Imam is one who is infallible. Because he is the interpreter of the Quran, he is the explainer of the Quran. In fact, he is also the messenger of the Quran. Just as when the verse of Surah Tawbah was revealed, the Prophet sent Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) for this very reason later on. Which, God willing, will be explained. It is not the purpose to state it right now. So, those who were sent earlier were stopped. As soon as those who were sent earlier saw the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali), they asked, 'O Ali, has any news come?' He said, 'Yes, the Prophet has told me that either—meaning Jibril said to the Prophet—either you yourself convey it, you yourself deliver it, or the one who is from you should deliver it. The Nafs-e-Rasool (Soul of the Prophet).' And the announcement of Nafs-e-Rasool had already been made before this in Mubahila as well. God willing, those details later, not now. So, Ma'sum min al-dhunub kulliha sagiriha wa kabiha. Infallible from every sin, small or big. لَا يَزِلُّ فِي الْفُتْيَا وَلَا يُخْطِئُ فِي الْجَوَابِ (He does not slip in giving fatwa, and he does not err in answering). Meaning, he must be infallible. Look, this hadith is very important. Even in giving a fatwa, he must be infallible. In that, 'la yazillu' means he should not slip. Meaning, it is not that he gave a wrong answer. Or said, 'Oh sorry, I don't know. I am not aware. Oh, I forgot.' He is the Imam, who is appointed by Allah, which we are emphasizing repeatedly, that he is Mansus min Allah, meaning he has a divine appointment. So, he does not slip. He does not say, 'I did not know, I am sorry. I was not aware.' La yazillu fil-futya wa la yukhti fil-jawab. And he does not make a mistake in answering. That, 'Oh, the answer was like this, oh I made a mistake. Oh, I should have done this, I did not.' No. Why? Because the Imam is one whose connection is with the knowledge of the unseen (Ilm-e-Ghayb). He is connected to Allah, that Imam. He is not an Imam of the worldly people, not appointed like the worldly people appoint. So, the Master of the Universe, Hazrat Amir (a.s.), says: 'He does not err in answering, and he does not commit sahw (inadvertent error), and he does not forget (la yansa).' Nisyan (forgetfulness) is not found in him. Forgetfulness is not found. 'Wa la yalhu bishay'in min amrid-dunya' (And he is not distracted by anything of worldly affairs). And it is not that some worldly thing makes him negligent of his goal, his purpose. Meaning, he does not get so entangled in amusement, or other things, or business, that he forgets Allah, forgets the hereafter, forgets his duties, forgets prayer, all these things. The Imam should not be like that. So, clearly, the Mawla first explained that he must be infallible from all sins, and from sahw and nisyan, from forgetfulness, and it is not that there is a loss of memory, and it is not that he is so busy in play and other things, so busy in worldly things that he forgets the religion. All this is against this status. So, the Mawla explains that he must be infallible. This is the first thing. What should be his second attribute? The second: أَنْ يَكُوْنَ أَعْلَمَ النَّاسِ بِحَلَالِ اللهِ وَحَرَامِهِ (He must be the most knowledgeable of people regarding the lawful and unlawful of Allah). He must be A'lam-un-Nas. Most knowledgeable of the people. He must be aware of all lawful and unlawful things. The Imam should not be one who is dependent on someone else, that 'we will ask him and tell you, call him, call him quickly, we are not understanding this right now.' Or he is giving a fatwa based on his own qiyas (conjecture), based on guesswork, or his own opinion, or his own desires. That whatever he understood, he gave a fatwa. It is not like that. Rather, his connection is with the knowledge of the unseen. Therefore, whatever fatwa he gives, that fatwa must be in accordance with the Quran. It must be in accordance with the traditions and the Sunnah. Meaning, it must be in accordance with the Sunnah of the Prophet. He should be familiar with the Sunnah of the Prophet, familiar with the Quran, familiar with the interpretation of the Quran, familiar with the ta'wil (esoteric meaning) of the Quran, familiar with all the muhkamat (clear verses) and mutashabihat (allegorical verses) of the Quran, familiar with the nasikh (abrogating) and mansukh (abrogated) verses. He should be familiar with everything. Familiar means he should be aware of it. He should have the knowledge of it. Otherwise, what kind of an Imam is he? Who doesn't even know. And even after being told, and here I would like to mention one more thing for your service, that this Imam should be an Imam who is not... Dependent on someone else to go and take information from another religion, to go and take information from another sect. No, the Shari'at-e-Baiza an-Naqiya (the pure and clear Islamic law) should be enough for him. The Quran and Sunnah should be enough for him. If a person is such that he is dependent on someone else, goes and studies with someone else, goes and receives this training from someone else, while the Prophet is there, the Quran is there, the religion is there, then what kind of an Imam is he? What kind of successor of the Messenger of Allah is he? Who himself does not trust the teachings of the Messenger of Allah. So, this became the second thing. The second attribute is this. The third attribute, the Mawla says, 'Wa th-thalith yajibu an-yakuna ashja' an-nas' (And the third, it is necessary that he be the bravest of people). It is necessary that the Imam be the one who is the bravest, Ashja' an-nas. 'Li-annahu fi'atul-mu'minin allati yarji'una ilayha' (Because he is the group of the believers, the fi'a, the group). He is the leader of the believers, the guide of the believers, to whom those people return, in whom they take refuge. The Imam is the one, people look up to him. He should be brave and courageous. 'Allati yarji'una ilayha in-inhazama minaz-za'f, inhazaman-nasu li-inhizamih' (To whom they return; if he is defeated due to weakness, the people are defeated by his defeat). If he goes into battle and suffers defeat, or flees from the battle, as soon as he saw the enemies, he ran away. If someone's Imam or Caliph is such a brave person, then the whole nation will be like that. Everyone will be like that. Now, you keep looking in history, who was it that was at the forefront in every battle? I don't have to mention anyone's name right now. I don't have to take anyone's name right now. Just keep reading history yourself. See who was given the flag, then they went, then they ran back, saying, 'Oh brother, a big wrestler has come in front, so what should we do?' Then they sent another, then they went, then they ran back. They said, 'Oh brother, he is a very big wrestler.' To the extent that the Mawla, to the extent that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had to say that tomorrow I will give the flag to such a man... The Prophet used the word 'man'. Now the explanation of this is in your hands. We will not explain it. The Prophet said that 'la-u'tiyanna' (I will certainly give), God willing, the Hadith of the flag will come, I don't have to state it right now. That 'la-u'tiyannar-rayata ghadan' (I will certainly give the flag tomorrow) to whom? 'Rajul' (a man). God willing, its explanation will come. And anyway, fleeing from the battlefield is a major sin (Gunah-e-Kabira). If you look at the list of major sins, the first is Shirk, the second is despairing of Allah's mercy, the third is considering oneself safe from Allah's plan, and the fourth is that a person—this list of major sins that is in the traditions—the fourth is that a person flees from the battlefield. This is a major sin, and this is in every constitution of the world. Meaning, fleeing from the battlefield is considered a very big sin. This is unacceptable, and no excuse is accepted for this. God willing, its details some other time, and God willing, the fourth attribute and the rest, God willing, in the next episode. Wa akhiru da'wana anil-hamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin, wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibina at-tahirin al-ma'sumin, wa la'nut-da'imu ala a'daihim wa qatalatihim wa qasibi huquqihim wa munkiri faza'ilihim wa manaqibihim.

title: Hum Apne Imam Se Kitne Qareeb Hain? | Dr Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the indicators of a believer's spiritual connection to Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). He emphasizes that a true bond is reflected in the alignment of one's emotional state with the joys and sorrows of the Ahlul-Bayt. By prioritizing the Imam's happiness over personal struggles, a believer demonstrates the depth of their faith and devotion.
content:
How do we know how connected and attached we are to our Imam-e-Zamana, how strong our bond is with our Imam? Look, if we want to know how much we love our Imam, some signs are mentioned in the traditions. One sign is that when the Ahlul-Bayt are happy, we are happy. We are happy in their happiness. When they are sorrowful, we are sorrowful. Look, when it is their happiness, no matter how great our own sorrow may be, we should celebrate their happiness. Our grief, our sorrow, our trouble, our pain is nothing compared to the happiness of the Imam and the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). And likewise, when the Ahlul-Bayt are sorrowful, we should be sorrowful, even if we have a great joy of our own. This is a sign of faith: "They rejoice at our happiness and grieve at our grief."
The strength of a believer's bond with the Imam is measured by emotional resonance.
A sign of faith is rejoicing when the Ahlul-Bayt are happy.
True believers grieve when the Ahlul-Bayt are sorrowful.
Personal sorrows should be set aside to celebrate the happiness of the Imam.
Personal joys should be secondary to the grief of the Ahlul-Bayt.
Aligning one's emotional state with the Ahlul-Bayt is a core tenet of faith.

title: SIBT E AKBAR (a.s.) GRAND QUIZ | Presentation and Live Quiz on Hazrat Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive overview of the life, virtues, and divine authority of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) through a series of presentations and an interactive quiz. It explores his status as the 'Speaking Quran,' his possession of Wilayat-e-Takwini and Ilm-e-Ghayb, and his strategic patience in the face of political adversity. The session emphasizes the necessity of loving the Ahl al-Bayt as a fundamental aspect of faith and highlights the broader Islamic concept of worship as a lifestyle aligned with divine guidance.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. From Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, who said: I heard Fatimah (a.s.) say: 'My father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), came to visit me one day and said: "Peace be upon you, O Fatimah." I replied: "And upon you be peace." He said: "I feel a weakness in my body." I said to him: "I seek refuge in Allah, O my father, from your weakness." He then said: "O Fatimah, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it." I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it, and I began to look at him. His face was shining like the full moon in its perfection and completion. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' It was only an hour later when my son, al-Hasan (a.s.), arrived and said: "Peace be upon you, O mother." I replied: "And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart." He said: "O mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)." I said: "Yes, your grandfather is under the cloak." Al-Hasan approached the cloak and said: "Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah. Do you permit me to enter under the cloak with you?" He replied: "And upon you be peace, O my son and master of my pond (Hawd), I have granted you permission." So he entered with him under the cloak. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. It was only an hour later when my son, al-Husayn (a.s.), arrived and said: "Peace be upon you, O mother." I replied: "And upon you be peace, O my son and coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart." He said to me: "O mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)." I said: "Yes, your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak." Al-Husayn approached the cloak and said: "Peace be upon you, O grandfather. Peace be upon you, O one whom Allah has chosen. Do you permit me to be with you both under the cloak?" He replied: "And upon you be peace, O my son and intercessor of my nation, I have granted you permission." He entered with them under the cloak. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. After that, Abu al-Hasan, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), arrived and said: "Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah." I replied: "And upon you be peace, O Abu al-Hasan and O Commander of the Faithful." He said: "O Fatimah, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)." I said: "Yes, he is here with your two sons under the cloak." Ali approached the cloak and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Do you permit me to be with you under the cloak?" He replied to him: "And upon you be peace, O my brother, my successor, my caliph, and the bearer of my banner." "I have granted you permission." So Ali entered under the cloak. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Then I approached the cloak and said: "Peace be upon you, O my father, O Messenger of Allah. Do you permit me to be with you under the cloak?" He replied: "And upon you be peace, O my daughter and part of me, I have granted you permission." So I entered under the cloak. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. When we were all gathered under the cloak, my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), took the edges of the cloak and raised his right hand toward the sky and said: "O Allah, these are the people of my house (Ahl al-Bayt), my elite, and my close ones." "Their flesh is my flesh, and their blood is my blood. What hurts them hurts me, and what saddens them saddens me. I am at war with those who war against them, at peace with those who are at peace with them, an enemy to those who show enmity toward them, and a lover of those who love them. They are from me and I am from them. So bestow Your blessings, Your benedictions, Your mercy, Your forgiveness, and Your pleasure upon me and upon them. And remove impurity from them and purify them with a thorough purification." O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, said: "O My angels and O inhabitants of My heavens, I have not created the established sky, nor the spread-out earth, nor the shining moon, nor the luminous sun, nor the rotating celestial sphere..." "...nor the flowing sea, nor the sailing ship, except for the love of these five who are under the cloak." O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The trustworthy Gabriel asked: "O my Lord, who is under the cloak?" The Almighty and Majestic replied: "They are the people of the house of Prophethood and the mine of Messengership. They are Fatimah, her father, her husband, and her sons." Fatimah, her father, her husband, and her sons. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family. Gabriel said: "O my Lord, do You permit me to descend to the earth to be the sixth with them?" Allah said: "Yes, I have granted you permission." So the trustworthy Gabriel descended and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. The Most High, the Exalted, sends you greetings and honors you with salutations and reverence, and says to you: 'By My Might and Majesty, I have not created an established sky, nor a spread-out earth, nor a shining moon, nor a luminous sun, nor a rotating celestial sphere, nor a flowing sea, nor a sailing ship, except for your sake and your love. And He has permitted me to enter with you, so do you permit me, O Messenger of Allah?'" The Messenger of Allah replied: "And upon you be peace. Indeed, Allah wishes to remove impurity from you, O Ahl al-Bayt, and purify you with a thorough purification." O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Ali said to my father: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me, what is the merit of this gathering of ours under the cloak in the sight of Allah?" The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied: "By the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me for the Message as a confidant, our story is not mentioned in any gathering of the people of the earth, in which there is a group of our Shia and lovers, but that mercy descends upon them, the angels surround them, and they seek forgiveness for them until they disperse." Ali (a.s.) said: "Then, by the Lord of the Kaaba, we have succeeded, and our Shia have succeeded." My father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), said: "O Ali, by the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet and chose me for the Message as a confidant, our story is not mentioned in any gathering of the people of the earth, in which there is a group of our Shia and lovers, and among them is one who is distressed, but Allah relieves his distress; nor one who is sorrowful, but Allah removes his sorrow; nor one who has a need, but Allah fulfills his need." Ali (a.s.) said: "Then, by the Lord of the Kaaba, we have succeeded and attained felicity, and likewise our Shia have succeeded and attained felicity in this world and the hereafter." And may Allah bless our master and Prophet Muhammad and his pure family. O Allah, send blessings upon... Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. TSR presents: Ya Hasan, Ya Hasan. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of al-Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten his reappearance. Honorable viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. All praise is for that Lord whose throne of power and majesty has always existed and will always exist. Blessings and peace be upon those chosen, Mustafa, Murtada, and Mujtaba servants of Allah, from whom blessings received such honor that even the One without partners is seen sending blessings upon them. Honorable viewers, from the 17th of Rabi' al-Awwal to the 13th of Rajab, from the 13th of Rajab to the 3rd of Sha'ban, from the 3rd of Sha'ban to the 15th of Sha'ban, and from the 15th of Sha'ban to the 15th of Ramadan, we have been celebrating the festivals of our 14 Infallibles, declaring that those whose birth is worth mentioning, whose birth is worth taking pride in, and whose birth is worth remembering, are the only ones entitled to be called the true successors of the Greatest Messenger, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Our first Muhammad came on the 17th of Rabi' al-Awwal, toppling the 14 towers of the false kings of the Caesar's palace, cooling the fire temples of Persia, and bringing the lamp of guidance to the infidel society of the Arabian Peninsula. He came to illuminate it. Our second Muhammad came, creating a door in the wall of the Holy Kaaba, sleeping on the bed of Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) on the night of migration, crushing the arguments of the deceivers, and sending the impure offspring of wandering mothers to Hell. And the one for whose birth we have gathered here, our Muhammad, who came into this world as the second condition of 'La ilaha illallah' regarding Imamate, came spreading smiles on the lips of the Infallible of the two worlds, making the blessed mouth of the Messenger his first nourishment, interpreting the prayer of Ibrahim, saving Muhammad Mustafa from the taunts of being childless until the Day of Judgment, awakening the destiny of the Preserved Tablet, and exposing the hypocrisy of the Pharaoh of Syria. The command of the Lord of Majesty is being recited in Surah al-Baqarah, where the Almighty God says: 'The month of Ramadan is that in which the Quran was revealed.' O month of Ramadan, congratulations to you, for you are the month in which two Qurans were revealed: one the Speaking Quran and one the Silent Quran. Come, let us present today's program, which has been named after the Grandson, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), in relation to the Speaking Quran, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). This is our third round, which we are bringing before you regarding Imam Hasan (a.s.). Regarding the life [of the Imam], viewers, let us inform you that the quiz link is available in the video description and the live chat and has become active. This link will remain live until the end of the program, and a countdown timer will appear on your screen in the last 10 minutes. When you click this link, you will see the questions, but do not be in a hurry to provide answers because the prizes in the lucky draw are for giving correct answers, not for giving them quickly. All the correct answers will be provided during this conversation, so listen to this discussion carefully and then attempt the answers. Viewers, our brothers Mr. Abbas Patel and Mr. Ahsan Jafri are also present here with us, who have joined us to discuss this topic further. Let us begin our program with some basic information about Imam Hasan (a.s.). Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Walaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. How are you, Ahsan Bhai? Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah. Many congratulations to you on the occasion of the blessed birth of this Sibt-e-Paighambar (a.s.). We also extend our heartfelt congratulations to all our viewers. Many congratulations to you too on the birth of Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.). Since our children also watch this program, let us begin by presenting some information about Imam Hasan (a.s.) to our viewers so that the children watching this program can also benefit from it. Your name was Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Your noble father's name was Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Your noble mother's name was Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), and your birth took place on the 15th of Ramadan, 2 AH. Your martyrdom occurred on the 28th of Safar, 50 AH, due to the poison given by your wife, Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath. Your Kunniyat is Abu Muhammad, and Imam Hasan (a.s.) has many titles, a few of which we would like to present to our viewers: one is 'Mujtaba', another is 'Sibt-e-Nabi', 'Sibt-e-Akbar'—the name after which this program is titled—and besides these, 'Sayyid-e-Shabab-e-Ahl-e-Jannah'. All these titles are found in the traditions regarding the Imam (a.s.). Kazim Bhai, you were speaking about the name of Imam Hasan (a.s.). Let us tell the viewers what the power of the name 'Hasan' is and what the importance of this name is in our lives. It is found in a tradition that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Summiyal Hasanu Hasanan li anna bi ihsanillahi qamatissamawatu wal ardhun' (Hasan was named Hasan because it is by the grace/ihsan of Allah that the heavens and the earths are established). This means that the name of Imam Hasan (a.s.) is that grace of Allah due to which the heavens and the earth are established. And Abbas Bhai, an interesting point here is, as you stated the Hadith, the word 'Ardhun' is used, meaning there are many earths. That is, not just this world, but all the worlds that Allah has created, all those earths are established by the blessing of the name of Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.). Wow! Indeed, this is the blessing of the name. And let us tell the viewers that the prayer taught by Imam Hasan (a.s.), which even our children are familiar with—the prayer we use during the month of Ramadan—is not just used by us, but all the people of the earth use it to seek forgiveness for their sins. The prayer at the time of Iftar has reached us through Imam Hasan (a.s.) himself. The sentences of the tradition are as follows: 'Anna likulli sa'imin inda futurihi da'watan mustajabah' (For every fasting person, Allah has kept a prayer that is answered at the time of Iftar). 'Fa idha kana awwalu luqmatin' (And when that fasting person takes their first morsel of Iftar), 'Faqul Bismillah' (Start with the name of Allah), 'Allahumma ya wasi'al maghfirah ighfirli' (O Allah, O the One of vast forgiveness, forgive me). Our every child recites this prayer, and whoever recites this prayer at the time of Iftar, Allah will forgive their sins, grant them forgiveness, and Allah has also kept a prayer that is answered for them. What could be better than starting our Iftar with the name of Allah, remembering that Wali-un-Ni'mah (the guardian of blessings), and praying for his reappearance? Indeed, indeed, because truly, the blessings and the food we are eating, the Iftar we are having, and all the food we are consuming is a blessing and a charity from the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). It is because of him that all this food reaches us. So why, when Allah has said, as you mentioned, that one prayer of every fasting person will definitely be answered, should a person not pray for the reappearance? One should definitely pray for the reappearance, and after that, one should ask for their personal prayers, but the very first prayer at the time of Iftar should be for the reappearance of Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.). Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. This prayer taught by Imam Hasan (a.s.) is being used by all the people of the earth—all the Shias found across the entire earth are benefiting from it. So viewers, you saw here that the prayer we have been reciting continuously—some people might not know this, but let us tell you that this prayer is attributed to Imam Hasan (a.s.). This is a prayer taught by Imam Hasan (a.s.), and you saw through this Hadith that the whole world—all the people in the world—are benefiting from this prayer, and through this prayer of yours, people are attaining forgiveness. So, Abbas Bhai, this was about the world. A Hadith comes to mind regarding the power of the Imam (a.s.), that the power of the Imam (a.s.) is not just over this world but over the worlds, and that Hadith is as follows. This is narrated in 'Manaqib-e-Aal-e-Abi Talib (a.s.)' by Ibn Shahr-e-Ashob. In this book, he brings a Hadith narrated from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in which Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that Imam Hasan (a.s.) is saying—listen to what he is saying: 'Inna lillahi madinatayni ihdahuma bil mashriqi wal ukhra bil maghrib' (Indeed, Allah the Almighty has created two cities, one in the East and the other in the West). Now, what has Allah placed between these two cities? Imam Hasan (a.s.) says: 'Alayhima surun min hadid' (Allah has placed a wall of iron between those cities). And not just this, Imam Hasan (a.s.) further says: 'Wa 'ala kulli madinatin alfu alfi bab' (Allah the Almighty has created 1 million gates in them). And what is in those gates? Listen: 'Likulli babin misra'ani min dhahab' (When a person enters through that gate, they will find two cities inside, and both cities are made of gold). Wow! Both cities, Abbas Bhai, Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.) says that both cities are made of gold. This is not about this world. This is about those two worlds that Allah has created in the East and the West. After this, the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Wa fihima sab'una alfa lughatin' (Allah has created 70,000 different languages used in those cities). Wow! 70,000 different languages that people speak there. And the person using a language inside there, it is not necessary that their companion knows that language. Meaning, every person there is using a different language, and the Imam further says: 'Wa ana 'arifun bijami'il lughati wa ma fihima wa ma baynahuma' (And I know all the languages used between these cities and what is in them and what is between them). Wow, wow, wow, SubhanAllah. The Imam is saying that he knows those 70,000 languages. And then, Kazim Bhai, here is a point to consider: this is not about this world. Those two separate worlds that Allah has created in the East and the West have 70,000 languages. Indeed, no human has the capacity, the power, or the strength to speak all the languages of this world today. Indeed, they could speak those languages, but Imam Hasan (a.s.) is saying that there are 70,000 languages there, and as you said, every person's language is different from the other. And Imam Hasan (a.s.) has knowledge of all those languages. He has knowledge. Indeed, and after that, the amazing sentence Imam Hasan (a.s.) says is: 'Wa ma 'alayhima hujjatan' (And there is no proof/authority over them), and then he says: 'ghayri' (except me). Wow! And Imam Hasan (a.s.) says: 'Wa ghayril Husaini akhi' (And except for my brother, the Sultan of Karbala, Imam Hussain Abi Abdillah al-Hussain (a.s.), who is also Allah's proof over those lands). Wow, wow, SubhanAllah. And as you mentioned, Kazim Bhai, about this 'Hujjat' (proof), that Imam Hasan (a.s.) is the Hujjat and what his authority is, in this regard, and in the same book you cited, 'Manaqib-e-Aal-e-Abi Talib (a.s.)', Ibn Shahr-e-Ashob (r.a.) brings a Hadith in which, as you said, Imam Hasan (a.s.) is the Hujjat, and Imam Hasan (a.s.) himself is stating about his being the Hujjat and his authority. The incident is that once Amirul Momineen Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)—Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad—called his son, Imam Hasan (a.s.), and said to gather the people and deliver a sermon. Indeed, this is the claim of 'Saluni' (ask me). He wants, it is his desire, to hear his son's sermon. So the Mawla said to Imam Hasan (a.s.), 'O son, gather everyone and deliver a sermon.' Now, what happened after that? Imam Hasan (a.s.) gathered everyone and then the Imam went up to the pulpit and then the Imam began the sermon. He says, 'Ayyuhan-nas, O people! Innallaha (Indeed, Allah) ikhtarana linafsihi (Allah has chosen us for Himself, He has selected us for Himself). Warta-dhana lidinihi (And He is pleased with us for His religion). Meaning, whether someone acts upon Allah's religion or not, it makes no difference to Allah. It is enough for Allah that He created the Ahl-e-Bait (a.s.) who are acting perfectly upon His religion. Wastafana 'ala khalqihi (Allah has chosen us over His creation). Meaning, He selected us, He made us the Hujjat. Imam Hasan (a.s.) is saying here in this sermon that if there is any Hujjat of Allah over His creation, then it is us.' And then after that, the Imam (a.s.) says—this Hujjat, meaning He made us the Hujjat, He selected us, He chose us—and then what did He do? Wa anzala 'alayna (And He revealed upon us). Look, it is the blessed month of Ramadan, the nights of the revelation of the Holy Quran are coming. In the Night of Qadr, the Quran that was revealed, Imam Hasan (a.s.) says, 'Wa anzala 'alayna kitabahu wa wahyahu' (Allah chose us and then revealed His Book and His revelation upon us). Meaning, this is exclusively specific to the fact that the revelation of the Holy Quran is specific only to the personality of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). Imam Hasan (a.s.) is pointing towards this. Indeed, indeed, and 'Kulluna Muhammad' (we are all Muhammad), as Kazim Bhai said in the beginning, Imam Hasan (a.s.) is himself stating his authority, what authority Allah has given them. And then after that, Imam Hasan (a.s.) says an amazing sentence, and this sentence is very important for all those people who nowadays try to diminish the status and rank of the Ahl-e-Bait (a.s.). Imam Hasan (a.s.) has given this message for them. The Imam says, 'Waillahi (By God!), la yanqusuna ahadun min haqqina shay-an (No person diminishes anything from our right) illan-taqasahullahu min haqqihi (except that Allah diminishes from his right, from that person's right). In what? Fi 'ajili dunyahu wa akhiratihi (In his worldly life and in his share of the hereafter). Allah will diminish it. If someone has made a reduction, just one reduction, if someone reduces even one thing, if they reduce one of their rights. Here, it is not just about usurping the entire right.' Meaning, whoever does not love their own soul, they become a 'Muqassir' (one who falls short). They become a Muqassir, indeed. He will face loss not only in this world—his share in this world will diminish—but he will also face loss in the hereafter, and loss in the hereafter is the greatest loss. Indeed, indeed. And then, after that, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'wa la yakuna 'alayna dawlatun'—there will be no government for us, but what? But that 'illa kanat lana al-'aqibatu'—but when our government comes, the end will be upon our government. Wow! This is an allusion to the Master of the Age (Hujjat). Indeed, indeed. He is pointing towards the government of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). That 'dawlah' (government) which we also allude to in Dua-e-Iftitah, where we recite, 'Allahumma inna narghabu ilayka fi dawlatin karimah'—O Allah, we desire from You a noble government—grant us that noble government. Imam Hasan (a.s.) pointed towards that government, and after that, Imam Hasan (a.s.) pointed towards a verse of the Quran and said, 'wa la ta'lamunna naba'ahu ba'da hin'—very soon, in the near future, those people will know when the government of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) arrives. And then, after the Imam delivered this sermon and stated his authorities, when he descended from the pulpit, the Master of the Universe, Imam Hasan (a.s.), approached him and kissed his forehead. Masha'Allah. Subhan'Allah. And this is a matter of authority. As for the excellence of Imam Hasan (a.s.), this was one excellence that the Imam stated himself, and he even stated that if anyone diminishes or falls short in this excellence, they will have to suffer the consequences. What does this mean? What is the message for us? That as long as we live, we should continue to proclaim the rights of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Indeed. And in that proclamation of truth, there should not be even an iota of negligence or deficiency. So, this was the eloquence and rhetoric of Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.) with which he delivered the sermon. Now, an important point that often creates doubt or suspicion in people's minds—or rather, is intentionally created—is that our Imams (a.s.), even though their rights were usurped, remained silent. They did not take any action. They never raised their voices in such a way. You are absolutely right. Although this is a huge misunderstanding. The Imams certainly practiced patience (sabr), but that patience cannot be called silence. Wow! Patience is different, silence is different. So, viewers, Ahsan Bhai is presenting a very important point here: the Imams certainly practiced patience, but they were not silent regarding their rights. Indeed, and wherever there was an opportunity for the Imams to state their rights or their excellences, they did so. For example, there is an incident where the ruler of Sham insulted the status of Imam Hasan-e-Mujtaba (a.s.). And how did he insult him? The ruler of Sham said to Imam Hasan (a.s.), 'Ana khayrun minka ya Hasan'—O Hasan! I am better than you, I am superior to you. Now, this was an insult to the status of the Imam (a.s.), that a mere mortal would express his false superiority and status before a being of light. Right? Because where is the grandson of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and where is the progeny of Abu Sufyan? He is insulting Imam Hasan (a.s.) in this manner.
