Those people who are seen calling themselves like the Prophet, who consider the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) to be humans like themselves, let them bring proof that Janabe Jibra'il used to descend into their houses too? Wow. That I am, I am from those Ahl al-Bayt to whom Jibra'il used to come, and not only come, but Jibra'il's ascension (Mi'raj) would start from there, when he would go from there towards the heavens. And then I am the one, "Ana min ahli bayti alladhīna iftarada Allāhu mawaddatahum wa-walāyatahum," I am from those Ahl al-Bayt whose Wilayah, whose Mawaddah (affection) and love, Allah has made obligatory, made mandatory in His Holy Quran. When Allah, then the Imam (a.s.) recited that Verse of Mawaddah from Surah Ash-Shura. "Fīmā anzala ʿalā Muḥammadin ṣallā Llāhu ʿalayhi wa-ālihi," regarding which Allah revealed this verse upon His Prophet, His Beloved, "Qul lā asʾalukum ʿalayhi ajran illā al-mawaddata fī al-qurbā," that I do not ask you for any reward for the message, except that you show affection, show love to my close relatives, to my Ahl al-Bayt. "Wa-man yaqtarif ḥasanatan," the rest of the verse, that whoever earns a good deed, this is very special, this is a very important sentence. Whoever earns a good deed. Then Imam Hasan (a.s.) says at the end, and earning a good deed means what? To have Mawaddah. Our Mawaddah. Wow! What excellent interpretations of the Holy Quran are being stated by the Speaking Quran, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.). So viewers, "Qul lā asʾalukum ʿalayhi ajran illā al-mawaddata fī al-qurbā." Regarding this, in whose honor this verse was revealed, what reward did the Muslim Ummah give? That on one side, people gather to seek retribution for the blood of the Caliph of the time, and on the other side, you see that when Amir al-Mu'minin is martyred, then among them, these very people of the Muslim Ummah, and especially those who had initiated the Battle of Jamal, those who had arranged the armies, the same people are seen performing the prostration of gratitude (Sajdah-e-Shukr) upon the martyrdom of Imam Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). This is truly oppression. This reward, was the Messenger of Allah asking for a reward for his deeds or for the preaching he did, the hardships he endured in the way of Allah, the reward the Muslims gave for that was the prostration of gratitude upon the martyrdom of Amir al-Mu'minin. And after that, what a scene it must have been, with what heart Imam Hasan (a.s.) must have delivered the first sermon after the martyrdom of his father, that Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.) has to introduce Amir al-Mu'minin, that Ali whose virtues were stated by the blessed tongue of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) countless times. From Asir to Ghadir, the Messenger of Allah introduced Amir al-Mu'minin. The same Amir al-Mu'minin is being introduced here by Imam Hasan in his first sermon. And after that, Imam Hasan told of the aspect of the Mawla's asceticism, that at the time of his martyrdom, he left behind only a small amount of wealth. Look at all the Caliphs who passed among the opponents, let the Muslim Ummah look at their wealth, how much wealth they left behind. Here, the justice and the fairness-loving nature of the Imam (a.s.) is presented before the people. Yes viewers, this is truly the oppression of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) that they were forgotten. Come viewers, here we bring this program of ours towards its conclusion, and we thank all the viewers from the bottom of our hearts for listening to the entire program. And as you might be seeing on your screen, the timer, the 10-minute timer, must have reached its final stage now. So viewers, here we invite you to get ready for Dua-e-Iftitah. Immediately after Dua-e-Iftitah, which you are waiting for impatiently, we will reach the stage where we will select the lucky draw winners for this quiz and presentation regarding the Sibte Akbar (a.s.) that was placed before you. And if you have given the correct answers, then through our computerized system, we will select them and make the announcement here, Insha'Allah. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. [Arabic text of Dua-e-Iftitah] He has no prophet to resemble Him, nor any helper to assist Him. He has subdued the mighty with His might, and the great have humbled themselves before His greatness; thus, He attains by His power whatever He wills. Praise be to Allah, who answers me when I call upon Him, covers every fault of mine while I disobey Him, and magnifies His grace upon me, yet I do not reward Him. How many pleasant gifts has He given me, how many terrifying calamities has He spared me from, and how many delightful joys has He shown me! So I praise Him, thanking Him, and remember Him, glorifying Him. Praise be to Allah, whose veil is not torn, whose door is not locked, who does not turn away the one who asks Him, and does not disappoint the one who hopes in Him. Praise be to Allah, who gives security to the fearful, saves the righteous, raises the oppressed, humbles the arrogant, destroys kings, and replaces them with others. Praise be to Allah, the crusher of tyrants, the destroyer of oppressors, the pursuer of fugitives, the punisher of the unjust, the helper of those who cry for help, the place of needs for those who ask, and the reliance of the believers. Praise be to Allah, from whose awe the sky and its inhabitants tremble, the earth and its dwellers shake, and the seas and those who swim in their depths surge. Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. Praise be to Allah, who creates and is not created, provides and is not provided for, feeds and is not fed, causes the living to die and brings the dead to life, and He is the Ever-Living who does not die. In His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your messenger, Your trustee, Your chosen one, Your beloved, the best of Your creation, the keeper of Your secret, and the conveyor of Your messages—with the best, most beautiful, most perfect, purest, most flourishing, most pleasant, most holy, most exalted, and most abundant blessings, benedictions, mercy, kindness, and peace that You have ever bestowed upon any of Your servants, prophets, messengers, chosen ones, and those honored by You among Your creation. O Allah, and send blessings upon Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, the successor of the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, Your servant, Your vicegerent, the brother of Your Messenger, Your proof over Your creation, Your greatest sign, and the Great News. And send blessings upon the truthful, the pure, Fatimah, the leader of the women of the worlds. And send blessings upon the two grandsons of mercy and the two Imams of guidance, Hasan and Husayn, the leaders of the youth of Paradise. And send blessings upon the Imams of the Muslims: Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and the Successor, the Guide, the Guided—the proofs over Your servants and Your trustees in Your lands—with abundant and everlasting blessings. O Allah, send blessings upon the guardian of Your command, the Upholder, the Expected, and the Justice awaited. Encompass him with Your near-stationed angels and support him with the Holy Spirit, O Lord of the Worlds. O Allah, make him the caller to Your Book and the upholder of Your religion. Appoint him as Your successor on earth just as You appointed those before him. Establish for him his religion which You have chosen for him, and replace his fear with security, that he may worship You and not associate anything with You. O Allah, honor him and honor through him, help him and seek victory through him, and grant him a mighty victory. Open for him an easy opening, and grant him from Your presence a supporting authority. O Allah, manifest through him Your religion and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, so that nothing of the truth remains hidden for fear of any of Your creation. O Allah, we yearn toward You for a noble state in which You honor Islam and its people, humiliate hypocrisy and its people, and make us among those who call to Your obedience and lead to Your path, and grant us through it the honor of this world and the hereafter. O Allah, whatever truth You have made known to us, help us to bear it, and whatever we have fallen short of, help us to reach it. O Allah, gather our scattered affairs through him, mend our rift, bridge our gap, increase our small numbers, and strengthen our weakness. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the master of the prophets and messengers, the Seal of the Prophets, Abul-Qasim Muhammad, and upon his pure, holy, infallible, and oppressed progeny, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. To proceed: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has said in His glorious Book, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful: 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.' Send salutations upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Respected listeners, believers, brothers in faith, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has sent man into this world for a specific purpose. And that purpose of the creation of humanity is the worship and servitude of Allah. As Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has stated in this noble verse, that He created the jinn and mankind only and solely for His worship. Now the question arises: does worship only mean prayer, fasting, Hajj, and Zakat? Or is the scope of worship much wider than that? In the religion of Islam, the concept of worship is very broad. Every act that is performed for the pleasure of Allah is worship. If a person lives their life according to the commands of Allah in every sphere—whether it be trade, politics, society, or family life—then every moment of it is counted as worship. It is narrated from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that he said: 'Worship is not just the name of prayer and fasting, but reflecting upon the creation of Allah is also worship.' Therefore, we should shape our lives in such a way that our every action becomes a cause for Allah's pleasure. We should keep the commands of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) before us at every step of our lives. We pray to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, to grant us the ability to perform true servitude to Him and give us the strength to walk on the straight path. And our final prayer is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

excerpt: This special episode celebrates the conclusion of the Ghadeer: Paymaan-e-Ilaahi Mega Quiz 2024, focusing on the theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khum. content:
Haydar, Haydar, Haydar... TSR presents... [Poetic/Devotional recitation in Persian/Urdu mix]. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your guardian, the Proof, son of al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour... And in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him dwell on Your earth in obedience, and cause him to enjoy it for a long time. [Poetic/Devotional recitation]. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, subscribe now and do not forget to press the bell icon. [Poetic/Devotional recitation]. The Messenger (s.a.w.a.) went to Mi'raj 120 times. The Messenger, the secret of Yazdan, Haider, the comfort of Fatima's heart, he bound the covenant of unity. Hadith: The story of the mercy of Ridwan, 'Illallah', meaning they bring the 'Illat' (cause) of Wudu, Adhan, and Salah. Hadith: The light of God is the Prophet, the Hadith of the heart, if you know it, it is beautiful. Hadith: 'La ilaha illallah', the Hadith of the imprint of Ali on the chest of the masses. Hadith: A living testimony. Then Gabriel (a.s.) said, 'Qad qamatis-salah, qad qamatis-salah'. This is the fourth heaven, the fourth heaven. We do not have a caller as high as the Khwaja-e-Lulak (the Prophet). Whoever has me as their master, Ali is their master. Just as I am more entitled to the believers than their own selves, Ali is my successor, and he is more entitled to them than their own selves. Ali, Ali, and Ali is the knower. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) crossed that river until he reached a station which was the station of veils (Hijabat). Then he was Ali, the Zamzam, Ali the Safa and Marwa, and Ali the Mas'a. Ali is the Adhan and the Iqamah, Ali is the Ruku and Sujud, Ali is the Qiyam and Qu'ud, and Ali is the Salam and Dua. Ali is the Sirat (Path), Ali is the Mahshar (Gathering), Ali is the Mizan (Scale), Ali is Paradise. Until the eighth day, Allah revealed another verse, which is the famous verse, the Verse of 'Bali' (Yes). In that, the one who is always on the path of error is the one who is the successor of the Messenger in Khaybar, not the one who fled from Jihad in battle. Someone who traded the Imamate for salted meat, not someone who, out of ignorance, was a fool. One 'Wahid' (Unique), meaning one warning, after one 'Wahid' is a 'Hadi' (Guide). The successor of the Prophet is not the one who seeks his own comfort. Someone who breaks idols while on the shoulders of the Prophet, for the protection of the Caliphate, is more entitled than anyone else. My witness to the Caliphate is that very existence of Ali, who is the sun. Gabriel (a.s.)—meaning the first time someone addressed Ali (a.s.) with the title of Amir al-Mu'minin, it was Gabriel (a.s.). Truth and reality revolve around him. Ali is justice and fairness, moving in his footsteps. If all creation were to separate from him, God is witness that the path of all creation is error. The reward is only the reward that comes with the love of Ali. Either change it or replace them. Meaning, the one you have made Imam, the Amir al-Mu'minin, either bring someone else as Imam instead of him or change his status, his position. Do not make him Imam over me. Ali is as if... whoever separates you from Ali, your refuge in the sun of the Day of Judgment is gone. Ali is my blood, my flesh, and the soul of the Prophet. Ali. The first collection of verses is from Surah Al-Baqarah, verses 8 to 16. Moving towards Surah Yunus, there is the 15th verse in which it is commanded. Besides that, Surah An-Nahl, verses 91 and 92. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) joined these two fingers of his and said, 'Ka-usbu'ayya hatayn jama'a bayna sabbabatay' (Like these two fingers of mine, he joined the two index fingers) and said that it is like these two fingers. And this entire Surah was revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wida), and then the Prophet gathered the people at Masjid al-Khif and began to advise them. And those who had malice against the Amir al-Mu'minin in their hearts, they had firmly decided that they would rebel against the Amir al-Mu'minin and would not let the Imamate reach Ali (a.s.). As soon as the Prophet's eyes close, we will not let this Imamate reach Ali (a.s.). Meaning, we will not let this Imamate reach its rightful place. The Amir al-Mu'minin called out, meaning he invoked Allah through the medium, and these mountains began to respond, 'Summa nadathu al-jibal' (Then the mountains called out to him), 'Ya Ali, Ya Wasiyyar-Rasul Rabbil-Alamin' (O Ali, O Successor of the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds). Meaning, what authority the Amir al-Mu'minin has! Yes, whoever he wants, however he changes them, this is Wilayat-e-Takwini (Creative Guardianship). And meaning, before this, it had turned into silver. The silver said, the sentence mentioned above, that 'Spend us however you wish, we are present when you command.' You state that, 'Masalul-mu'minina fi qubul-wilayat-e-Amir al-Mu'minin fi yawmi Ghadir Khum' (The example of the believer who accepted the Wilayat of Amir al-Mu'minin on the day of Ghadir Khum)... that believer who accepts Ghadir, the Mawla is now giving an example here. 'Kamathalil-mala'ikati fi sujudihim li-Adam' (Like the example of the angels in their prostration to Adam). Iblis says here, 'Okay,' and swears by the honor and majesty of Allah, 'O Allah, I swear by Your honor that I will make sin and disobedience so adorned and decorated for the companions of Ali, those who love him, that I will present it to them and declare them Your enemy.' Meaning, I will call them towards sin, I will present it so beautifully to these believers that they will commit that sin, and O Lord of the Worlds, when they commit this disobedience to You, I will declare them Your enemy. It is narrated that he states, 'Qala Abu Ja'far (a.s.) ya Zurara'—Zurara ibn A'yun, who holds the status of being among the special companions of the Imam (a.s.). He is addressing him, Imam Baqir (a.s.) is stating, 'O Zurara, inna-ma samada laka wa li-ashabika fa-ammal-akhirina faqad fazza minhum' (O Zurara, the target of Iblis is only you and your companions, meaning you Shias). So when all these devils reach their leader and say that the announcement was made at Ghadir and they are throwing dust (in despair), at that time Iblis says—now listen to what Iblis says. Iblis says, 'Do not worry, I am sure about those people who are around this person'—by this person, he means the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—'that among those who are around this person, there are some who have promised me in this regard that they will not deceive me, okay, and they will keep supporting me.' Addressing the Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) directly, he states, 'Law anna 'abdan 'abada-llah' (If a servant were to worship Allah), 'mithlama qama Nuhun fi qawmihi' (as much as Noah (a.s.) stood among his people). Meaning, do you understand how much action he is performing? He worshipped for nine hundred and fifty years, gave gold equal to Mount Uhud in charity, performed a thousand Hajj pilgrimages—and you know the value of one Hajj. He is not talking about an ordinary worshipper. Then, look at what the Messenger of Allah is saying here, 'Summa qutila bayna Safa wal-Marwa mazluman' (Then he is killed between Safa and Marwa, and he is killed in a state of oppression). It means there are so many virtues of his, and this is being stated by the Seal of the Prophets, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) himself. He performs so many deeds, and then my Mawla states a strange and unique sentence: "Summa lam yuwālika ya Ali"—that O Ali, if he does not possess your love, your Wilayah, "lam yashumma rāyhatal jannati wa lam yadkhul"—that Allah will not let him even smell the fragrance of Paradise, let alone enter it. "As-sirātul ladhī qāla Iblīs"—the path that Iblis was mentioning or referring to, the one he had claimed to God, the path he was pointing towards—then the Imam recites that verse: "La-aq'udanna lahum sirātakal mustaqīm"—that I will sit on Your path and mislead Your servants. What is meant by this? The Imam says, "Huwa Aliyun alayhis-salam." Subhan Allah. The Mawla states: "Inna Iblīsa ranna arba'a rannāt"—that Iblis has shrieked four times in his life so far. What were those occasions? "Yawma lu'ina"—the day he was cursed, the first occasion. The second occasion: "Wa yawma uhbita ilal-ard"—when he was thrown to the earth, cast out in humiliation. When he refused to prostrate to Adam (a.s.) and was driven away, that was the moment of his despair. The third occasion: "Wa yawma bu'itha an-nabīyu sallallāhu alayhi wa ālih"—when the Almighty God commissioned Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.). That was the moment his spine was broken. Yes, a Prophet had arrived who would propagate divine messages throughout the entire universe. And this Prophet would put an end to all his schemes and all his agents. Right? His successors and his commands will do this, the successors who are to come will do this. The fourth occasion: "Wa yawma al-Ghadīr." [Poetry in Persian]. The sermon that our scholars have narrated in full, they narrated the hadith on the authority of Imam Baqir (a.s.), the entire sermon was narrated, and it was recorded by Sheikh Tabarsi (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Ihtijaj'. [Poetry in Persian]. "Wa lā nahya 'an munkar"—and there can be no forbidding of evil "illā ma'a imāmin ma'sūm"—except with the guidance of an infallible Imam. [Poetry in Persian]. The Prophet says that after this, you all should say: "Nubāyi'uka"—we all pledge allegiance to you "'alā dhālik"—on this matter, we pledge our allegiance "bi-qulūbinā"—with our hearts, "bi-anfusinā"—with our souls, "bi-alsinatinā"—with our tongues, "wa aydīnā"—and with our hands. Look, all things have come back again. Everything has come. "'Alā dhālik"—on all these things, meaning on what you have stated. And on this, on all these things, "'alā dhālika nahyā wa namūt"—we will live on this, we will spend our lives on this, and we will die on this. "Wa nub'athu"—and we will be resurrected on this on the Day of Judgment. Meaning, on this belief, the belief in the Imamate of Ali and the progeny of Ali, we will live, we will die, and we will rise. This is the belief. "Lā nughayyiru wa lā nubaddilu"—we will not change this, nor will we bring any alteration. The Prophet stated these sentences in front of everyone, told them all to repeat these sentences. This verbal affirmation is still going on. "Wa lā nashukku wa lā nartābu"—we will not keep any room for doubt or suspicion in this. Yes, indeed, there will be no room for doubt or suspicion; we will not be afflicted by doubt or suspicion. "Wa lā narji'u 'an 'ahdin"—we will not turn back from this covenant. The promise we are making to you here, we will fulfill it. "Wa lā nanquḍu al-mīthāq"—we will not break this, we will not break this promise, this divine pact. "Wa nuṭī'u Allāha"—we will obey Allah "wa 'Aliyan Amīral-Mu'minīn"—and we will obey Ali, who is the Commander of the Faithful. "Wa wuldahu al-a'imma"—and his children, the infallible Imams, the twelve Imams, all "alladhīna dhakartahum min dhurriyyatika"—whom you have just mentioned, who will be from your progeny, we believe in them all and will obey them. All these sentences are being repeated by the Messenger of Allah, he is stating them. The Messenger of Allah is saying them first, and everyone is being asked to repeat them. [Poetry in Persian]. Therefore, Allah has commanded me that first, I should take a verbal affirmation from you. Meaning, look at the style of the pledge. [Poetry in Persian]. If all creation... and regarding Ali, the Prophet says: "Ma'āshira an-nās, ḥujjū al-bayta bi-kamāl ad-dīn"—go for Hajj with a complete religion. [Poetry in Persian]. Both say that O people, the virtues of Ali near Allah (azzawajal) are so many, and the virtues that He has revealed in the Quran regarding the Mawla of the universe, Ali, are so numerous that I cannot even count all those virtues for you while standing here in this one place. Subhan Allah. I cannot even count them for you. Just the virtues that Allah has revealed in the Quran regarding Ali. Therefore, "Faman anba'akum bihā"—now whoever tells you about them "wa 'arrafahā"—whoever introduces them, "fa-ṣaddiqūhu"—believe him. [Poetry in Persian]. "Alladhī yaghzī bil-ḥaqq"—he who will judge with the truth. The judgment that Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf) will make, it will be the truth. May Allah grant us that day, Insha'Allah, may He hasten the reappearance of the Imam. May He grant reward. And whoever is the winner, it is our humble request to them that whenever they go for Ziyarat, they should go for Ziyarat on behalf of all the members of the TSR team and all the people who participated in this quiz. That is, the announcement of the mega winner of the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi 2024 Mega Quiz, whose selection is being made through our computerized lucky draw system. The one who is going to receive the prize that every lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) desires. Which is the Ziyarat of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimiya, and Samarra, i.e., the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. If you also wish to join us in spreading the message of Wilayat-e-Ahlebait (a.s.), please subscribe to our channel, like the videos, and keep the notification bell on so that every video of ours reaches you first. We pray in the court of the Almighty God that He hastens the reappearance of the Heir of Ahlebait (a.s.), the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.), and grants us the strength to hold firmly onto the Wilayat-e-Ahlebait (a.s.) until the very end. And whoever shares our videos with others, may He include them in the reward of Tabligh-e-Wilayat-e-Ahlebait (a.s.). Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen. Insha'Allah, we will meet again in our upcoming quiz. title: Namaz Se Maula Ali (a.s.) Ki Mohabbat | Promo | Kull-e-Imaan (a.s.) Grand Quiz 2026 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound devotion of Imam Ali (a.s.) to prayer, emphasizing his commitment to Salat al-Layl and his mindfulness of obligatory prayers even during the intensity of battle. The speaker reflects on how the Imam's connection to divine light is inseparable from his worship. The talk concludes by encouraging believers to maintain the remembrance of Imam Ali (a.s.) as a form of worship while awaiting the eventual meeting with the Imam of the Time (a.s.).
content:
Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) says, 'I have never abandoned the Night Prayer (Salat al-Layl) since I heard from the blessed tongue of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that the Night Prayer is light.' Subhan Allah. The Night Prayer itself is light. We have often heard that performing the Night Prayer makes a person's face radiant and Allah blesses them with other bounties. But the fact that the Night Prayer itself is light is a profound matter. And when the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) themselves are light, how could they abandon this light? Light is never separated from light. During the heat of battle, what was the Master of the Universe doing? He was looking at the sun to see how far it had progressed. On one hand, he was fighting, and on the other, his gaze was on the sun. Ibn Abbas asked the Master, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, what are you doing?' The Master replied, 'I am waiting for the zawal (noon) so that we can pray.' Allahu Akbar. This is the Master of the Universe; even in the midst of such a fierce battle, he was mindful of prayer. To see the Master of the Universe, one must leave this world. We do not have that option; that meeting will happen when Allah wills. However, the son of the Master of the Universe, the Imam of the Time (a.s.), when he wills, a meeting can occur. Since we do not have that option, if the world passes, let it pass, but the remembrance of Ali (a.s.) should not pass. Indeed, for us, the remembrance of Ali (a.s.) is worship.

title: Bibi Fatima (s.a.) Ki Baddua | Watch EP2 of The #Fadak #Podcast | #DoNotMiss
excerpt: This lecture discusses the historical and theological significance of the Sermon of Fadak delivered by Bibi Fatima (s.a.). The speaker addresses the misinterpretation of inheritance hadiths used to justify the seizure of Fadak, arguing that such claims are intellectually dishonest. The talk emphasizes that supporting the oppressed is incomplete without defending the rights of Bibi Fatima, as her curse carries eternal consequences for those who wronged her.
content:
It is clearly written that the Prophets leave behind neither dirhams nor dinars. Their inheritance is not dirhams or dinars. So, what is the answer to this? Presenting a half-truth or a single hadith without understanding it, as an objection, is proof that the enemy is faltering and has no answer. It is like a person drowning in the sea who doesn't know how to swim; they have no choice but to flail their arms. They are just flailing. Since they don't know how to swim, the result will be that they will drown, and they have drowned. Do you know why the condition of Muslims today is as it is? Because in that very Sermon of Fadak, which Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) delivered, she cursed those oppressors. In what words did she curse them? The Princess said, 'What is left for you people? In what state will you remain? There is nothing for you but disgrace and shame.' Many people today, and in every era, talk about supporting the oppressed. Indeed, it is a good thing for a person to support the oppressed. But if a person has supported every oppressed person in the world, the Princess... If one does not defend the rights of Salamullah Alayha, on the Day of Judgment, they will find themselves standing in the list of those very oppressors. The litmus test for supporting the oppressed is the defense of the rights of the Princess (Fatima Zahra s.a.). If one does not defend this, then even if they defend every oppressed person in the world, they will gain nothing on the Day of Judgment. On the Day of Judgment, the wrath of Allah will come.
Prophets do not leave worldly wealth as inheritance in the sense claimed by those who seized Fadak.

It addresses the skepticism regarding the long lifespan of the Imam by citing the Quranic account of the sleepers of the cave. The speaker explains that these individuals are destined to awaken upon the arrival of Imam Mahdi to testify to his mission and greet him.
content:

It is a rule that this is our lesson. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. If any person raises an objection against Imam Mahdi (a.s.) regarding how it is possible for someone to remain alive for approximately 1200 years, then our question to such people is: have they not recited the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf) in the Holy Quran, and their claim of remaining alive until today... ...the answer given by Allah to those who claim they remained alive until today in the Quran. Along with the Quran, the famous 7th-century scholar, Ibn Kathir, in his book 'Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah', Volume 2, page 234, in the context of the interpretation of the verses of Surah Al-Kahf, researched that the resting place of the People of the Cave was designated, and they will remain there until the time of the reappearance of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.). When the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) begins, he will greet the People of the Cave, and Allah Azza wa Jall, for his sake, will grant them life again—that is, they will wake up from their deep sleep of centuries and will testify to the construction of the mosque. This testimony is mentioned in the Holy Quran in Surah Al-Kahf... ...the testimony is mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf, verse 21, which says: 'We will build a mosque over them.' That is, the People of the Cave will rise again only to answer the greeting of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). We pray to Khuda-e-Wand-e-Alam that we are among those who greet Hazrat Imam (a.s.) and prove to be his helpers. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. excerpt: This lecture discusses the theological necessity of believing in the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) within Islam. Citing narrations from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the speaker emphasizes that denying the Imam is equivalent to rejecting the entire Sharia. The talk further explains that belief must be established before the Imam's reappearance to be spiritually valid, referencing Quranic verses regarding the signs of Allah.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. To participate in this entire video series and the mega quiz, the first step is that you have to register for the quiz at account.dawngroup.com. The registration link is given in the comments and description of this video. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. ... Various scholars in their books, citing the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.), have narrated hadith regarding the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) in the end times. But we see people denying the existence and reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). First, Sheikh Ibrahim Hamwini in his book 'Fara'id al-Simtayn', Volume 2, page 334-336... ...page 334-336, 585, records that the famous companion of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Jabir bin Abdullah Ansari (r.a.), narrated from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that whoever denies the reappearance of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has denied everything that was revealed to Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). From this hadith, a few things become clear: that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), who explained to us the laws of prayer, fasting, Hajj, Zakat, and other aspects of Sharia, according to this very hadith of his, whoever denies Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is like one who has denied the Sharia. Waiting for the reappearance of Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is equivalent to believing in his existence. The reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is one of the fundamental Islamic beliefs, which is proven by the verses of the Holy Quran and authentic, reliable narrations. Therefore, if a person denies this belief, then in the light of this Prophetic hadith, he is outside the fold of Islam. And it is also necessary that the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.s.) should be before his reappearance. Once he has reappeared, then... Once it has happened, there will be no benefit in believing in them. Ali bin Ibrahim inquired from Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) regarding verse 158 of Surah Al-An'am of the Holy Quran: 'Are they waiting for the angels to come to them, or for your Lord to come, or for some of the signs of your Lord to come? On the day when some of the signs of your Lord will come, belief will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned any good through its belief.' Imam (a.s.) stated: 'Here, the signs refer to the Imams from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and the later signs refer to Imam Mahdi (a.s.). So, the person who did not believe in them before the reappearance will not benefit from believing at the time when he (Imam Mahdi) will act with the sword, even if he already held a belief in the Imams (a.s.). That is, if a person believes in the Imamate of the 11 Imams, but does not believe in the Imamate of Mahdi (a.s.), then his belief in the Imamate...' ...is not valid. And it is also important that the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.s.) must be held before his reappearance, not after, because after the reappearance, when Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will strike the enemies of Ali (a.s.), believing at that time will not be of any use to a person. We pray to Allah (s.w.t.) to hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), keep us steadfast on the belief in his existence and reappearance, and count us among his helpers and followers. title: Allah Ne Imam Reza (a.s.) Ka Naam Reza Kyun Rakha? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture clarifies the divine origin of the title 'Al-Riza' given to the eighth Imam, Ali ibn Musa al-Riza (a.s.). Imam Muhammad al-Taqi (a.s.) explains that the name was not chosen by the Caliph Ma'mun, but was divinely ordained because the Imam was pleasing to Allah and His Messenger. Furthermore, the title is unique among the Imams because both his friends and his enemies were satisfied with his character and conduct.
content:
Riza, Riza, Riza... I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrates that I asked Imam Muhammad-e-Taqi (a.s.) that a group among your opponents assumes that Ma'mun named your father 'Riza' because he was pleased with his appointment as successor. Imam Taqi (a.s.) replied: "They lie. By Allah, they have committed a great sin. Rather, Allah (Tabarak wa Ta'ala) named him 'Riza' because he was pleasing to Allah (Azza wa Jall) in His heavens, and he was pleasing to His Messenger (s.a.w.a.) and the Imams (a.s.) after him on His earth." I then asked, "Was not every one of your past ancestors pleasing to Allah, His Messenger (s.a.w.a.), and the Imams (a.s.)?" The Imam (a.s.) replied, "Indeed they were." I then asked, "Then why was the name 'Riza' given only to your noble father among all of them?" The Imam (a.s.) replied, "That is because his enemies and opponents were pleased with him just as his friends and those who agreed with him were pleased with him, whereas this was not the case for any of his ancestors." Therefore, among all of them, only my father's name was kept 'Riza'. O Lord, by the intercession of Imam-e-Riza (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of his heir and our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Mahdi (ajtf), and grant us the ability to become worthy so that we may be pleasing to our Imam of the time, and he may be pleased with us. Ameen, Ya Rabbal Alameen. Riza, Riza, Riza... O Allah, I have stood at a door from the doors of the houses of Your Prophet, may Your blessings be upon him and his family. May I enter, O Messenger of Allah? May I enter, O Hujjah of Allah?
The name 'Riza' was given by Allah, not by the Caliph Ma'mun.
Imam al-Riza was pleasing to Allah, the Prophet, and the preceding Imams.
The title signifies that the Imam was a source of satisfaction for both friends and enemies.
No other Imam shared this specific title because their circumstances of opposition differed.
The lecture emphasizes the importance of seeking the pleasure of the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (ajtf).

title: EP02 | Hadees-e-Manzelat Par E'teraazaat Aur Unke Jawaabaat | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ💐
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive analysis of Hadith-e-Manzilat, exploring its historical context, authenticity, and theological significance in establishing the Imamate of Imam Ali (a.s.). By drawing parallels between the relationship of Musa (a.s.) and Harun (a.s.) with that of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.), the session addresses common objections and highlights the necessity of divine succession. The discussion culminates in the broader context of Ghadir Khumm, framing the appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.) as a central pillar of Islamic faith and divine guidance.
content:
Haider, Haider, Haider... [repeated] TSR presents: The importance of Hadith-e-Manzilat and the response to objections against it. One of the most famous Hadiths found in both renowned Shia and Sunni books is the Hadith-e-Manzilat. All Muslims agree that in this Hadith, the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) said to Hazrat Amirul Momineen Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.): 'O Ali, your status (manzilat) in relation to me is the same as the status of Hazrat Haroon (a.s.) to Hazrat Musa (a.s.).' Except that there is no prophet after me. Sunni brethren, in their highly authentic and, according to them, 'Sahih' books, do record this Hadith-e-Manzilat as a virtue of Mawla Ali (a.s.), but they do not accept it as proof of Imam Ali's (a.s.) Imamate and Caliphate; rather, they seek various excuses to escape this reality. On the other hand, the Shia Ithna Ashari consider this Hadith-e-Manzilat as one of the greatest proofs of Imam Ali's (a.s.) Imamate and Caliphate-e-Bila Fasl (immediate succession). In other words, there is unity among Muslims in accepting the Hadith, but there is disagreement regarding the conclusion derived from it. Through this video, our brothers, Mr. Syed Kazim Sahab and Mr. Tanveer Devji Sahab, will discuss the Hadith-e-Manzilat from various perspectives. They will derive the correct conclusion, present it before you, and also attempt to answer the objections raised against it, Insha'Allah. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. A'udhu billahis sami'il alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu. Respected viewers, we offer our congratulations and greetings on the occasion of Eid-e-Ghadir and Eid-e-Mubahila. As you know, our topic today is the Hadith-e-Manzilat, and we have a few points to present regarding it. Before we proceed to this topic, we must mention that the biggest controversial and disputed issue from the martyrdom of the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) until today concerns his vicegerency (wisayat), his caliphate, and his succession. We have observed and witnessed repeatedly that if blood has been shed over any issue, it is the issue of Imamate and Caliphate, and it continues to flow to this day. We also want to present the stance of the opponents on this topic: Did the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) appoint his successor or not? Their stance is that he did not appoint anyone, nor did he present any 'nass' (explicit text), nor did he provide any procedure for how to select a caliph after him. Respected brothers, these three claims are not logical—that he made no appointment, presented no 'nass', or provided no procedure. Our question to the opponents is: The Messenger of God knew he was going to leave this world, and after Hajjatul Wida, he was continuously saying that he would soon depart from this world. God knew when His Prophet was to return to Him, and God also knew that the greatest conflict in this Ummah would be regarding Imamate. God also knew that the most blood shed in this Ummah would be over the issue of Imamate, and that disagreement would be visible in everything in this Ummah. From Tawheed to even the way the five daily prayers are performed, disagreement is clearly visible in this Ummah, as we observe. So the question is: Why did God and His Messenger not arrange for this system? And respected viewers, the Messenger of God also said that after him, this Ummah would split into 73 sects, and only one would be saved. He also said that there would be no prophet after him. And since these programs are being held regarding Ghadir, in the field of Ghadir, God also said through His Beloved: 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum wa atmamtu alaykum ni'mati wa radhitu lakumul-Islama dina' (Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion). So, respected brothers, this is our question to all Muslims and the entire Ummah: When God and His Messenger announced that the religion was perfected, it is clearly evident why He did not appoint the one regarding whom the most conflict is found in the Ummah. Now, we want to state our position: What is our perspective? Our perspective is that the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) did make arrangements, and he did not just make arrangements at the time of Ghadir, but from the beginning to Ghadir, the Messenger of God continuously gave the message to the Ummah regarding who his successor would be after him. Respected brothers, this Hadith-e-Manzilat is also in that regard, as it is a proclamation by the Messenger of God, and the Messenger of God has explicitly appointed Amirul Momineen as his successor, his caliph, in his Ummah. So, respected brothers, we will present a few points before you regarding the Hadith-e-Manzilat and clearly demonstrate to the Ummah and all viewers how this Hadith-e-Manzilat is an explicit 'nass' regarding the Wilayat and Imamate of Amirul Momineen (a.s.) and the vicegerency of the Messenger of God. The topics are as follows: The background of Hadith-e-Manzilat, the narrators of Hadith-e-Manzilat, Hadith-e-Manzilat in Sunni books, and then the importance of Hadith-e-Manzilat. According to the Shia perspective. After that, why did the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) compare Amirul Momineen (a.s.) specifically to Hazrat Haroon (a.s.), the similarity between the Children of Israel and the Muslims, and then the answers to the objections raised by the opponents regarding this Hadith. These are the few points we are going to discuss. Respected viewers, we offer our congratulations on the greatest Eid, Eid-e-Ghadir. And Kazim Bhai, you have presented a very good introduction to this Hadith. As our first discussion is about the background of the Hadith-e-Manzilat, the words spoken by the Messenger of God are found on two occasions. The first occasion is when the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, and he established brotherhood among the Muslims. It is found in the Hadith: 'Lamma hajar an-Nabi (s.a.w.a.) wa akha baynal Muhajireen wal Ansar' (When the Prophet migrated, he established brotherhood between the Muhajireen and the Ansar). This was a time when the enemies of Islam were trying to create discord among the Muslims. That is why the Messenger of God established brotherhood among the Muslims and foiled their plans. And it is found that 'Akha bayna Abi Bakrin wa Umar wa bayna Uthmana wa Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf wa bayna Talhata wa Zubayr wa bayna Salman wa Abi Dharr wa baynal Miqdadi wa Ammar' (He made Abu Bakr the brother of Umar, Uthman the brother of Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Talha the brother of Zubayr, Salman the brother of Abu Dharr, and Miqdad the brother of Ammar). The Messenger of God made some companions brothers of each other, and Muslims brothers of Muslims. Like he made Janab-e-Salman the brother of Janab-e-Abu Dharr, and Janab-e-Miqdad the brother of Janab-e-Ammar. But at that time, he did not make Amirul Momineen (a.s.) the brother of anyone. Amirul Momineen was very saddened by this and went to the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'May my parents be sacrificed for you, why did you not make me the brother of anyone?' This was a question Amirul Momineen (a.s.) formally presented to the Messenger of God because everyone had been made a brother to someone else; only Amirul Momineen (a.s.) was left. Yes. In one Hadith, this sentence is also found that Amirul Momineen (a.s.) was left. So when the Messenger of God heard this, he (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Ali, I have reserved you for myself.' Wow! And are you not pleased that you are my brother and I am your brother? Wow! Meaning, if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made anyone his brother, he made Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) his own brother. Wow! And here, Tanveer Bhai, the Muslim Ummah is calling the Messenger of Allah their brother. Indeed. But no one can become the brother of the Messenger of Allah except Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). And no one can become the brother of Amir al-Mu'minin except the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). This means even the Sahaba did not attain the honor of becoming the brother of the Messenger of Allah. Even those Sahaba whom Muslims hold in high regard are not worthy of becoming the brother of the Messenger of Allah. It is astonishing to the intellect of Muslims that they call the Messenger of Allah their brother, while this is explicitly stated—meaning it is a clear-cut hadith—that the Messenger of Allah made Amir al-Mu'minin his brother. Yes. And the matter does not stop there. The Messenger of Allah did not just limit Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to being his brother, just as he made other companions brothers to one another. Beyond that, he said, "Wa anta wasiyi wa waziri wa khalifati." Wow! Wow! Wow! Meaning, you are my successor, my vizier, and my caliph after me. This means from the very initial stages of Islam, the Messenger of Allah was declaring the Wilayah and the successorship of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Indeed, and we cannot find clearer words than this in a hadith. He called him Wasi, he called him Wazir, he called him Khalifa. Correct. And then he said, "Taqdi dayni," that you are the one who will pay my debts, fulfill my promises, and perform my ghusl, and these are tasks that no one can perform except you. Wow! And then, coming to our topic, the Messenger of Allah says, "Wa anta minni bi-manzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiya ba'di." Wow! Wow! That O Ali, your status in my sight is the same as Harun's was to Musa (a.s.), except that there will be no prophet after me. When Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) heard this, he smiled. So, dear viewers, the points that emerge from this hadith are that the Messenger of Allah chose only and only Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to be his brother. And it is not limited to him just being the brother of the Messenger of Allah, but he is his successor, his vizier, and his caliph. Indeed. And he compared him to Harun (a.s.), that just as the status of Harun (a.s.) was with Musa (a.s.), the same is the status of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, indeed, indeed. So, Tanveer Bhai, this was the first stage when the Messenger of Allah presented the Hadith al-Manzilah regarding Amir al-Mu'minin to the Muslim Ummah from his blessed mind. Now, dear viewers, the second stage that I want to present to you is that of the Battle of Tabuk, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was leaving Medina for the Battle of Tabuk, and it was a very long journey from Medina. The hypocrites who were in Medina knew that it was a very long journey. So, they planned that when the Messenger of Allah would depart from Medina towards Tabuk, in the meantime, we would capture the center of Islam and take everything into our own hands. So, this was their plan, this was their intention. Now, when this plan of theirs reached the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that the hypocrites of Medina were planning in this way, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appointed Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) in his place, although Amir al-Mu'minin was Asadullah (the Lion of Allah). Although Amir al-Mu'minin was a warrior, and it was never seen in previous battles that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not take Amir al-Mu'minin with him. Whether it was the Battle of Badr or all other battles, the participation of Amir al-Mu'minin is clearly present in the history of Islam. This was the first stage, and from this, the importance of the matter becomes clear to people, as to how much the hypocrites were planning and intending to capture the center of Islam and take all the affairs of Islam into their own hands. When the Messenger of Allah learned of their plan and intention, he installed Amir al-Mu'minin in his place, made him his successor, made him his caliph, and thwarted their plans and intentions, and he departed from there. When the hypocrites saw that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was present among them and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had appointed him as his successor in his place, they planned among themselves that now we will not be successful in our goal. So, they spread a rumor and started presenting false things among the people of Medina that it seems the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is angry with Amir al-Mu'minin and that is why he did not take him to the battle. When this news reached Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) became saddened upon hearing this and immediately departed from there. The Messenger of Allah had already left for the battle, and he reached the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and told him about the situation in Medina, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, after you left, people are saying things about me in Medina that you are angry with me and that is why you are leaving me behind in Medina." The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) comforted Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and this was the second occasion when he mentioned the Hadith al-Manzilah, saying, "O Ali, anta minni bi-manzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiya ba'di." O Ali, your status with me is the same as Harun (a.s.) had with Musa (a.s.). So, this was the second occasion when the Hadith al-Manzilah... was presented to the Muslim Ummah, and it is a point worth reflecting upon that this occasion was in the 9th year of Hijrah, and his martyrdom occurred in the 11th year of Hijrah. Two years before his martyrdom, the Messenger of Allah made such a major decision and appointed Amir al-Mu'minin before leaving. Kazim Bhai, you made a very important point here that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not take Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to this battle, even though Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) was the one through whom Islam had won every battle. Indeed. Meaning, leaving him in Medina was a greater task than taking him to the battle. Indeed. And this was such a major task that the survival of the entire Islam depended on it. This was not a matter of one or two days that the Messenger of Allah appointed someone as his successor just to lead the prayer, while some people even bring up this incident to claim that someone became the successor of the Messenger of Allah just by leading one prayer, even though that matter is not proven. Wow, wow. Wow, wow. So, this was a much greater stage than that, where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) as his successor in Medina. Come, Kazim Bhai, let us now look at the narrators of this hadith. According to the Ahl al-Sunnah, when one wants to know if a hadith is authentic or not, its chain of narration (sanad) is examined, and it is seen who has narrated this hadith. The Hadith al-Manzilah is such a hadith that it has been narrated by 25 companions of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and among them are such prominent companions who are considered very authentic by the Ahl al-Sunnah. Like Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Sa'd ibn Malik, Asma bint Umays, Abdullah ibn Umar, and many other such names. But among these names, the one that stands out the most is a very authentic name according to them, which is Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. This is because this hadith has been narrated from him in at least 10 different wordings. Let me present an example to you; the name of the book is Al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, whose author Al-Zuhri has brought an entire chapter in which he discusses this hadith. In it, he has stated three different hadiths with different wordings, and all of them are from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, where he narrates this Hadith al-Manzilah. For example, in one hadith, it is found that Sa'd ibn Malik asks Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, "I want to ask you about a hadith, but I am hesitant." So, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said, "O son of my brother, do not be hesitant, ask me, and whatever I know, I will answer you." Then Sa'd ibn Malik asks him about the Battle of Tabuk, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas narrates this entire hadith where the Messenger of Allah compared Imam Ali (a.s.) to Harun (a.s.). Similarly, in another book, Al-Isti'ab, the author Ibn Abd al-Barr writes that the Hadith al-Manzilah is among the most authentic and correct hadiths, and after that, he writes that the chain of narration of this hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is the most authentic chain. Meaning, through the references of these two books, we prove that the narrators of this hadith are very authentic, and there is no Muslim who can doubt the authenticity of this hadith. So, Tanveer Bhai, Masha Allah, you spoke about the narrators, that the most authentic narrators of the opposition have narrated this hadith, and that too in the early days of Islam. Come, let us also present to the viewers the references from the books. In our books, from Sulaym ibn Qays to all other books, this hadith is found. But let us tell you regarding the opposition that we have been seeing the Hadith al-Manzilah in 50 of their books, and not just minor books, but even in their Sihah al-Sittah (the six authentic books), the Hadith al-Manzilah is found. For example, let us present to you that in Sahih Bukhari, this hadith is narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, in which he narrates from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that he said: "Ama tarda an takuna minni bi-manzilati Haruna min Musa." O Ali, are you not pleased that your status with me is the same as Harun's was to Musa (a.s.)? In the same way, if you look at the second book, which is a very famous and well-known book among the opposition, Sahih Muslim, this hadith is also found there from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: "Amara Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan Sa'dan faqala ma mana'aka an tasubba Aba al-Turab." Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan said to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, "What is it that stops you from expressing disavowal of Abu Turab?" Now, to this, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, "Whenever I remember three virtues of Ali, I wish that if only I had one of those three virtues." Now, listen, viewers, what these three virtues are. Regarding the first virtue, he talks about the Battle of Tabuk, that in the Battle of Tabuk, O Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, do you not remember that the Messenger of Allah said regarding Amir al-Mu'minin: "Ama tarda an takuna minni bi-manzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nubuwwata ba'di." This is the first thing that we are repeatedly presenting to you regarding the Hadith al-Manzilah. This is the first thing he is wishing for, that if only I were in that place and the Messenger of Allah had stated this regarding me. The second thing he says to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan is that the second virtue that the Messenger of Allah presented to the world regarding Ali (a.s.) was in the field of Khaybar, which was: "Today I will give the banner to a man who will be a man, and Allah and His Messenger love him, and he loves Allah and His Messenger." This is the second position, this is the second virtue of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Regarding the third virtue, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says, 'Do you not remember the event of Mubahila, where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) declared Ali (a.s.) to be his own self (nafs), and then recited this prayer: Allahumma ha'ula'i ahli (O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt)?' So, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is presenting these three virtues to Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan regarding Ali (a.s.). Kazim bhai, looking at this hadith, one cannot understand whether to talk about the virtue of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) or his oppression. On one side, a companion is talking about abusing the Caliph of the Muslims, Amir al-Mu'minin, and on the other side, a companion wishes to attain even one of the countless virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). This was truly a strange phase for Amir al-Mu'minin to face such people. And Kazim bhai, one feels like laughing at those people who, upon seeing this hadith, do not understand that the one ordering the abuse is also 'Radiyallahu' (may Allah be pleased with him), the one listening and denying is also 'Radiyallahu', and the one being spoken about is also 'Radiyallahu'. Truly, it is incomprehensible whether Allah is pleased with this religion or not. Indeed. And you mentioned that there are 50 such books in existence where this hadith has been recorded. Among us, there is a famous and well-known book called 'Shabahat-e-Peshawar' (Peshawar Nights). It has also been translated into English. This book is a collection of a debate that took place about 100 years ago, authored by Sayyid Muhammad al-Musawi Shirazi. He had this debate with opponents, and in this debate, he proved the doctrine of Imamate from various aspects, one of which is the Hadith al-Manzila. In that debate, he himself cited references from 30 books. Masha'Allah. This book is available on the internet and everywhere. Our request to the Momineen is to search for this book and, especially on the occasion of Ghadir, to study it. And Kazim, Brother, when the topic of Peshawar Nights and Shia ideologies came up, we have numerous books where the Hadith al-Manzila is found. Whether it is Kitab al-Sulaym, Al-Kafi, or other books. Whether it is in terms of the text (matn), the chain of narration (sanad), or authenticity (sehat), the Hadith al-Manzila is authentic to us in every way. Even in our supplications, the Hadith al-Manzila is mentioned. In Dua-e-Nudba, which we recite every Friday, the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin that are counted include the Hadith al-Manzila. Yes, indeed. But here, an important point to share with the viewers is that a book was written called 'Tuhfa-e-Ithna Ashariya', written by Dehlavi, and the reason for writing this book was to create doubts among the Shias. One of the things the Maulvi brings up is that all these hadiths of virtues according to the Shias are fabricated. Maulvi Dehlavi wrote a very interesting point in his book: that in that era, the religion of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) was being propagated so much that a Shia child was being found in every opponent's house. So, he wrote this book regarding that as well, to create doubts in people's hearts. And truly, this is absolutely correct because it is evident from the fact that as soon as he wrote this book, our scholars gave very detailed responses to it. Among these responses, the name that comes to the forefront is 'Abaqat al-Anwar', whose author is Sayyid Hamid Hussain Musawi al-Hindi (may Allah elevate his status). He wrote an entire volume just in response to the chapter on Hadith al-Manzila. Meaning, the matter that Dehlavi stated in a few pages, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi brought an entire volume in response. And let us also tell the viewers that regarding the response to Maulvi Dehlavi's book 'Tuhfa', 53 books were written in that era. 53 books—this shows how much religious zeal the scholars of that time had; if opponents wanted to create any objection or doubt in people's hearts, our scholars would immediately bring the responses into book form and into the public eye. Now, a question arises here, Kazim bhai: why did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) compare Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) specifically to Harun (a.s.)? So let's see why he did that. If we read the Quran, the first verse that comes before us is verse number 142 of Surah al-A'raf. This is the verse that is highly emphasized to be recited in the first 10 days of the month of Dhu al-Hijjah through a two-rak'ah prayer. In it, Allah Almighty states that He made a promise of 30 days with Musa (a.s.) and extended it by 10 days so that he could fulfill his promise. And then Hazrat Musa (a.s.) said to his brother Harun, 'I am making you my caliph (successor) over the people so that you may reform them and not follow the path of the wrongdoers.' So this event bears a complete resemblance to the event of Tabuk, where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was going away from his nation, his homeland, and his city for some time, and he appointed his successor behind him. Just like when Hazrat Musa (a.s.) was going to Mount Tur, he appointed his brother Harun as his successor for his nation and his people. Indeed. The word used here in the Quran is 'ukhlufni', meaning 'be my caliph'. This word 'caliph' is very important here. A caliph is someone who is the successor of another after them. Wow. Meaning, when Hazrat Musa (a.s.) was not present at that time and place, Hazrat Harun (a.s.) was his successor. Similarly, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was not present, Hazrat Imam Ali (a.s.) is his successor. Now, whether it is for that limited time or when the Messenger of Allah departs from this world, Amir al-Mu'minin is his successor forever. Tanveer bhai, the point you presented here, you spoke about the resemblance, how Amir al-Mu'minin resembles Harun (a.s.). Now, the opponents try to put a kind of doubt into the minds of the Momineen that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is not the successor in a general sense. He was only a successor for a limited time, for the war, the Ghazwa of Tabuk, or the period of Tabuk. While the point coming here is, okay, he will reform the Ummah, so according to the opponents, the Messenger of Allah did not appoint anyone, did not designate anyone, so who will reform the Ummah? So the person whom the Messenger of Allah is leaving behind in his life, in his lifetime, for the reform of the Ummah, because there is a resemblance. Here, the talk of reform is coming, so just as Harun (a.s.) has a task of reform, similarly, Amir al-Mu'minin also has the task of reform here. So if for a small time, for a small period, the task of reforming the Ummah is the responsibility of Amir al-Mu'minin, given to him by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), then how is it possible that when the Messenger of Allah departs from this transient world, he would leave the Muslim Ummah to its own devices? Similarly, another verse is found in the Quran in Surah Taha, in which Allah is commanding Hazrat Musa and Hazrat Harun (a.s.) to go to Pharaoh because he has rebelled. When Hazrat Musa (a.s.) wants to go to Pharaoh, before that, he makes a prayer to Allah in which he says: 'Qala rabbi ishrah li sadri wa yassir li amri wahlul uqdatan min lisani yafqahu qawli waj'al li waziran min ahli'. This is an important verse. 'Waj'al li waziran min ahli Haruna akhi'. Meaning, where Hazrat Musa (a.s.) is making other prayers to Allah, he is also making this prayer: 'Appoint for me a minister (wazir) from my family.' Wow. And who should that be? 'Harun, who is my brother.' Wow. In this verse, we see two things. First, he has placed a request to make Harun (a.s.) his minister. So here, the word that has come openly is that he prayed for Harun (a.s.) to be appointed as his minister. Now, there is no need for a detailed discussion on what a minister is. Okay? So, first, he chose Harun (a.s.) as his minister, and second, he prayed to Allah to appoint him. Indeed. Meaning, if a successor (wasi) of a prophet is to be appointed, it can only be done by Allah. It is 'Mansus min Allah' (appointed by Allah). It is 'Mansus min Allah'. The Ummah does not have the right to gather and appoint its own caliph. This right belongs only to Allah, that whoever He chooses, He declares him the successor of the prophet. So this is the 'Sunnat-e-Ilahiya' (Divine Tradition). This is the 'Sunnat-e-Ilahiya'. So if we look at both these verses, the word 'caliph' also appeared, and the word 'minister' also appeared, which was used for Harun (a.s.). Now let us connect this to our topic, which is our discussion on Hadith al-Manzila, that Imam Ali (a.s.) has the same status as Harun (a.s.). So if Harun (a.s.) is the caliph of Musa (a.s.), his brother, and his minister, then Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is also the caliph, brother, and minister of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). There is no doubt about this. Indeed. And here, another objection that opponents put among our youth is that Harun (a.s.) passed away during the lifetime of Musa (a.s.). So his death happened first, whereas if you look here, the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is happening first, and after that, Amir al-Mu'minin was alive after him. So they try to put doubts into people's minds with such objections. Whereas this should be clear from the name of the hadith, 'Hadith al-Manzila'. Nowhere is it being said here, life and death are not being discussed, there is no mention of it here. Here, the status (manzila) The status is being discussed, just as you presented in the verse: 'Waj'al li waziran min ahli', that 'O Lord, appoint him as my minister who is from my family.' So if Hazrat Musa (a.s.) is praying for Hazrat Harun (a.s.) to make him his minister, then in the same way, Amir al-Mu'minin is also the minister. So here, the word 'manzila' is being presented by the Messenger of Allah to the Muslim Ummah regarding the status. So if Harun (a.s.) is a minister, then Amir al-Mu'minin is also a minister. If Harun (a.s.) is a caliph, then Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is also a caliph. So there is no room for this here, and one more thing: if Hazrat Musa (a.s.) made Harun (a.s.) his caliph, his minister, his successor during his lifetime, then where does the Muslim Ummah derive the conclusion that if Harun (a.s.) were alive, he would not be the caliph? If Harun (a.s.) were alive after Hazrat Musa (a.s.), he would definitely be his successor. He would definitely be his successor. When he is his successor during his lifetime, when he is his caliph during his lifetime, then he would definitely be the same successor and the same caliph after he left. So here, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is presenting the status before the Muslim Ummah. You are creating a doubt in people's minds about coercion, that he passed away and left this world before. And if you look at the subsequent verse in that same sequence, it is stated in the Quran: 'wa ashrikhu fi amri' (and appoint for me a minister from my family, Aaron, my brother). Meaning, you have to understand here what the affairs of the Prophets are. The affairs of the Prophets are reformation, as you stated in the first verse. And what is reformation? Reformation is the main task of the Prophets, to resolve the differences among the Ummah, because the greatest difference is Imamate, and there is disagreement in every matter. Today, apart from the Qibla and the Kaaba, there is disagreement in every matter. So, just as Prophet Aaron (a.s.) was appointed for reformation by Prophet Moses (a.s.), in the same way, if Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) had been there, the reformation of this Ummah would have been perfect. When the discussion is about similarity, a hadith is found in Sahih Bukhari where the Muslim Ummah is compared to the Children of Israel. So let us see in what things this similarity is found. Whatever things were in the Children of Israel will be in the Muslim Ummah. In the Children of Israel, the Prophet was Moses (a.s.). In the Muslim Ummah, it is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). In the Children of Israel, the successor of Moses (a.s.) was Aaron (a.s.). In the Muslim Ummah, that Wasi, that Caliph, that Vizier is Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). When Prophet Moses (a.s.) went to Mount Tur, he appointed a successor. Wow. When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) went to the Battle of Tabuk, he appointed a successor. Meaning, whatever was happening in the Children of Israel would also happen in the Muslim Ummah. Now the question arises that there was a person in the Children of Israel named Samiri who misled the people. Wow. And there was a golden calf through which he misled them. Wow. Now our question to the Muslim Ummah is, is there any Samiri in this Ummah, and who is that golden calf through which people will be misled? Discussion on this, Insha'Allah, another day. Now, Tamir Bhai, what you said about the similarity you mentioned, you want to present it to the viewers, that this incident is happening in the 9th year of Hijri. The Verse of Wilayah is being revealed, in which it is being declared: 'Innama waliyyukumullahu wa rasuluhu walladhina amanu alladhina yuqimunas-salata wa yu'tunaz-zakata wa hum raki'un'. Now, there is a need to reflect on the stage before this; what is the incident before the revelation of this verse? That when Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) gave the ring. After that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) prayed in Masjid-e-Nabawi: 'Waj'al li waziran min ahli' (And appoint for me a minister from my family). And after that, you immediately prayed that, O Lord, just as You chose Aaron (a.s.) for Moses (a.s.) as his minister, in the same way, appoint Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) from my family as my minister. So, it is worth noting here that when Allah does not reject the prayer of Moses (a.s.), then how would He reject the prayer of the Pride of Moses? This is an incident of 9 Hijri, which is according to the Verse of Wilayah, and this is a clear-cut 'nass' (explicit text) regarding the Wilayah, Imamate, and Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). Similarly, if you look, other major events also took place in 9 Hijri. The Battle of Tabuk itself, which we mentioned in the beginning, and this Hadith al-Manzilat are events of 9 Hijri. So these are two major events in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is clearly announcing the 'nass' of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), announcing his Wilayah, his Caliphate, and his Vizierate. The third major event, the third major event is Surah Bara'at, when you gave Surah Bara'at to a person and said to go and recite it in Mecca. Right. Gabriel (a.s.) comes from Allah to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and says, 'O my Beloved, either you recite these verses or someone like you can recite them.' Meaning, here it is clear-cut, this matter is clear before the Muslim Ummah; it is not a hidden matter. A clear-cut message is coming out from this that 'or someone like the Messenger'. So, someone like the Messenger means that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) is just like the Messenger. Meaning, whatever tasks the Messenger has to perform, only Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) can perform them. Indeed, indeed. And the fourth major event that occurs in 9 Hijri is that of Mubahila, in which the message is also very clear here for the Muslim Ummah, that the 'Nafs' (Self) of the Messenger is being announced: 'O Messenger, bring the one who is your Nafs.' And here, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) chose Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and took him to the field of Mubahila. So, on one side is the Nafs of the Messenger, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.); on one side, he is like Aaron (a.s.) as he was for Moses (a.s.). On one side, you see in Surah Bara'at that either you recite or someone like you goes. After that, you see the Verse of Wilayah, and remember that prayer too, which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) prayed before this Verse of Wilayah. So these are major events from which a clear-cut message is going that if there is anyone after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he should be like the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And who was like the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). So these are the major events that took place in 9 Hijri. Now, when you go from 9 Hijri to 10 Hijri, in that, finally, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced his succession. In the field of Ghadir, and you raised Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) among a gathering of 124,000 and declared: 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyyun mawlah' (Of whomsoever I am the Mawla, this Ali is his Mawla). So, this means we can say that all these events were preliminaries for Ghadir, where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was declaring Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) as his successor on every occasion, and in 10 Hijri, at the time of Ghadir, he openly announced his Wilayah before the people. Indeed, indeed. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) compared Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) to Aaron (a.s.). So, among all these similarities, one similarity that is very important is that when Prophet Moses (a.s.) went to Mount Tur and chose Aaron (a.s.) as his successor, it was a test for the people whether they would follow their Prophet and accept his successor, his minister, his Caliph as their Imam or not. If they accepted, they would be on the right path. When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) departed from this world, he also appointed a successor by the command of Allah. Now, it is the test of this Ummah whether they accept this successor, this Caliph, this minister as their Imam. If they follow the Messenger, then they are Muslims in the true sense, because the Quran is saying in clear words: 'Ahasiban-nasu an yutraku an yaqulu amanna wa hum la yuftanun' (Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and they will not be tested?). So, there is no test greater than Wilayah. Therefore, our prayer is that Allah makes us successful in this test and keeps us firm and constant on the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and the Wilayah of our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. With this, this episode of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz ends here. We hope that you all have given the answers to all the questions by now. If not, there is still time. A countdown timer has started for you. As long as this timer runs, the quiz link will remain live. As soon as the countdown timer ends, the quiz link will also be closed. Therefore, submit your answers before the quiz link closes. Let us all turn our attention towards the Ziyarat of Aminullah. Immediately after this, we will announce the winners of today's episode through our computerized lucky draw system. A'udhu billahi-sami'il-'alim minash-shaytanir-la'inir-rajim. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Wa salla-llahu 'alayka ya waliyyal-'asr adrikna wa la tuhlikna. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Come, gentlemen, now let us see who are the eight lucky winners of our today's episode, who are being selected through our computerized lucky draw system. First, we have our five third-prize lucky winners who will be awarded a prize of ₹1000 Indian Rupees. Their names are on your screen: Syed Mohammad Baqir from Mumbra, Aliya Sugra from Meerut, Shahr Bano Mehndi from Mumbai, Syeda Nazreen Bano from Jaipur, and Panjwani Shaukat Ali from Mota Kutavade. Now, let us move to our second-prize winners, two individuals who will receive a prize of ₹2500 Indian Rupees. They have also been selected through our computerized lucky draw system. Their names are on your screen: Rahil Fatima from Alipur, and Kaneez Fatima from Islamabad. Many congratulations to you all. Now, let us see who the lucky one is who... is going to receive our first prize, that is, a prize of ₹5,000 Indian Rupees. So, their name is on your screen: Syeda Mahvi Fatima from Bangalore. Many congratulations to you. We heartfully congratulate today's episode winners. And now it is time to say goodbye. We will meet all of you again tomorrow at 9:30 PM sharp, India time. Until then, please remember us in your prayers. Khuda Hafiz, Ya Ali Madad.
Hadith-e-Manzilat establishes Imam Ali's (a.s.) status as equivalent to Harun's (a.s.) relationship with Musa (a.s.).
The hadith is widely authenticated in over 50 Sunni sources, including Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) decision to leave Imam Ali (a.s.) in Medina during the Battle of Tabuk was a strategic leadership appointment, not an exclusion.
Divine succession is argued to be a necessity for the Ummah, mirroring the leadership patterns found in the history of the Children of Israel.
The concept of 'Wazir' and 'Caliph' for the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is presented as a divine appointment (Mansus min Allah) rather than a communal choice.
Historical events like Mubahila, Surah Bara'at, and Ghadir Khumm serve as cumulative evidence for the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.).
