chapters.title: Introduction to Hadith-e-Manzilat
chapters.summary: The lecture introduces Hadith-e-Manzilat as a pivotal tradition accepted by all Muslims, though interpreted differently regarding Imam Ali's (a.s.) succession.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Divine Succession
chapters.summary: The speakers argue that it is illogical to suggest the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) left no instructions for leadership, given the importance of Imamate and the perfection of religion.

chapters.title: Historical Context and Brotherhood
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the occasion of brotherhood in Madinah, where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared Imam Ali (a.s.) as his exclusive brother, successor, and caliph.

chapters.title: The Context of Hadith al-Manzilah at Tabuk
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the strategic importance of the Battle of Tabuk, where the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed Imam Ali (a.s.) as his successor in Medina to thwart the plans of hypocrites.

chapters.title: Authenticity and Narrators of Hadith al-Manzilah
chapters.summary: The lecture examines the chain of narration for Hadith al-Manzilah, highlighting its transmission by prominent companions like Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and its inclusion in major Sunni texts.

chapters.title: Hadith al-Manzilah in Sunni Sources
chapters.summary: The speakers analyze the presence of the hadith in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, specifically focusing on Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's defense of Imam Ali (a.s.) against Mu'awiyah.

chapters.title: Resources for Further Study
chapters.summary: The speakers recommend 'Peshawar Nights' as a vital resource for understanding the doctrine of Imamate and the historical evidence supporting the status of Imam Ali (a.s.).

chapters.title: Authenticity of Hadith al-Manzila
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the authenticity of Hadith al-Manzila in Shia tradition and address historical attempts by opponents to cast doubt on its validity.

chapters.title: Quranic Parallels: Musa and Harun
chapters.summary: The lecture draws parallels between the relationship of Prophet Musa and Harun and that of the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali, focusing on the roles of caliph and minister.

chapters.title: Addressing Objections on Status
chapters.summary: The speakers refute common objections regarding the timing of Harun's death, emphasizing that Hadith al-Manzila defines the eternal status and authority of Imam Ali.

chapters.title: Events of 9 Hijri and Imam Ali's Status
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights key events in 9 Hijri, such as the Battle of Tabuk, the Verse of Wilayah, Surah Bara'at, and Mubahila, as evidence of Imam Ali's (a.s.) unique status as the Prophet's successor.

chapters.title: Ghadir as the Culmination of Divine Succession
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the events of 9 Hijri served as preparation for the final declaration of Imam Ali's (a.s.) Wilayah at Ghadir Khumm in 10 Hijri, establishing it as a divine test for the Ummah.

chapters.title: Quiz Winners Announcement
chapters.summary: The session concludes with the announcement of the lucky draw winners for the Ghadir Mega Quiz.

title: EP04 | Imam Mahdi (a.s.) Ki Wilaadat Ahle Tasannun Kitaabon Mein | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 🎁🎉
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical documentation of the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) within Sunni Islamic literature, bridging the gap between different theological perspectives. The speaker cites prominent Sunni scholars and historians, such as Ibn Khallikan, Ali ibn al-Athir, and Sibt ibn al-Jawzi, to provide evidence that the birth of the 12th Imam is acknowledged in classical Sunni texts. Additionally, the session serves as an episode of the 'Panah-e-Kainat' series, which includes a quiz competition aimed at encouraging deeper study of Islamic history.
content:
[Music] Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. The quiz link is now live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on that same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. The only condition for the quiz prize is that all the answers must be correct. Among all those who have given the correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But if your name did not appear in today's winners or if you missed an episode, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from those who have given correct answers to all questions in seven out of 12 episodes. That is, even if someone did not become a daily winner but has given correct answers in seven out of 12... ...episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. Allahumma Kulla Waliyyil Hasan, Salawatuka Alayhi wa Ala Abaihi... [Music] Audhubillahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Audhubillahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Sallallahu ala Ya Wadikna wa la tana. Dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. If we look at the beliefs of the two major sects of the Islamic world, i.e., Shia and Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni), we see that there are many beliefs between them that are common. But if we go into the depth of these beliefs, we realize that they are common only in name, but in reality, there are differences in these beliefs. All Muslims, whether Shia or Ahl-e-Tasannun, believe in the oneness of Allah. They profess the unity of Allah. But if we study the books of both these sects and look at the attributes of Allah described, we will realize that there is a huge difference between them. For example, it is very common among the Ahl-e-Tasannun that Allah can be seen, and their great scholars are unanimous on this. But if we look at the Shia books and the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)... ...and study them, it is very clear to us that Allah will not be seen either in this world or on the Day of Judgment. Similarly, if we talk about Prophethood, the belief we have regarding Prophethood and the attributes we describe for our Prophet, and the attributes that the Ahl-e-Tasannun describe, there is a huge difference. If we take the early period of the preaching of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) or his preaching life or the last moments of his life, the things that the Ahl-e-Tasannun have said about the Messenger of Allah on these occasions or the belief they hold about him, and the belief that the Shias hold, these two cannot come together on one person. That is, they are not common. There is a lot of difference between them. Similarly, it is common in both sects that after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), there are his successors, his Caliphs. But how are these Caliphs and Imams selected and what are their attributes? In... ...both of these, there is a difference. So, in summary, these beliefs are common only in name, but if one goes into their depth, there is a lot of difference. Similarly, an important belief that is found in both sects is the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Both sects believe that from the progeny of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), Imam Mahdi (a.s.), will come and fill this world with justice and fairness. But a major difference that is found between these two sects is whether Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been born or not. And our topic today is exactly this, where we will present some references from the books of Ahl-e-Tasannun, which will make it clear that the birth of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) has been mentioned in their books as well. Before we discuss our actual topic, let us look at the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.s.) from their books. Here, we are presenting only a few references from their famous books. But if these references are studied, many such books will be found where Imam... ...Mahdi (a.s.) is mentioned. One of their famous and well-known books, which is called Sunan Ibn Majah, and which is also counted among the Sihah al-Sittah (the six authentic books). In this book, a hadith is found from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) where he says: 'Al-Mahdi is from the progeny of Fatimah,' that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will be from the progeny of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). Similarly, another reference from this same book where the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says that Mahdi is from us, that is, from the Ahlulbayt, and he will reform the affairs of this world in one night. That is, these hadiths show that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been mentioned in the books of Ahl-e-Tasannun as well. We request our viewers to go to their famous website, which is www.shamela.ws, and just type the word 'Mahdi', and you will find many different narrations from their authentic books regarding Imam Mahdi (a.s.). Now, let us come to our actual topic, where we will see where in the books of Ahl-e-Tasannun... ...the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been mentioned. The first book we will mention is called 'Al-Wafi bi al-Wafayat', and its author is Salahuddin Safadi. This book is a collection of 14,000 personalities and this book was written in the 8th century. And this book has been written according to the alphabetical order and this book is in the Arabic language. Its manuscript is found in many different libraries and the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been mentioned in this book. Let us see how Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been mentioned here. Here, he writes 'Al-Hujjat al-Muntazar' and then he takes the name of the Imam. That is, Mim, Ha, Mim, Dal, son of Hasan al-Askari, and after that, he takes the name of every Imam. That is, al-Askari, son of Ali al-Hadi, son of Muhammad al-Jawad, son of Ali al-Rida, son of Musa al-Kazim, and in this way, he takes it up to Imam Ali (a.s.) and then he says Ali ibn Abi Talib (r.a.), meaning Allah [is pleased with] all these... Radhiyallahu Anhu, meaning may Allah be pleased with these personalities. And then they say that this person, i.e., Hujjat al-Muntadhar, is the 12th Imam of the Shias, and the Shias know him as the Muntadhar (the Awaited One) and the Mahdi. His birth took place in the Sardab of Samarra in the year 255 Hijri. In clear words, it is found in this book that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has already occurred. After this, they further say that he is the one whom the Shias are waiting for. Meaning, Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is in Ghaybah (occultation) and the Shias are waiting for his reappearance. This book does not just tell us that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been born, but his father's name is also mentioned. And his ancestors, i.e., our Imams (a.s.), are also mentioned, explaining from whose lineage Imam Mahdi (a.s.) descends. The final point they mentioned is that Imam Mahdi (a.s.) will go into Ghaybah and the Shias will wait for his reappearance. The second book we need to mention is titled Wafayat al-A'yan wa Anba' Abna'. Its name is Wafayat al-A'yan wa Anba' Abna' al-Zaman, which is famous as Wafayat al-A'yan. It is an important book by Ibn Khallikan, written in Arabic between 654 and 671 Hijri. It is found in Arabic. In this book, the author has described the life stories of nearly 850 scholars, rulers, ministers, and famous individuals. This book is also arranged in alphabetical order. It is based on information, history, documents, and stories. In this book, the dates of birth and other details of these personalities are also mentioned. Detailed accounts of the lives of the Companions of the Prophet, the Tabi'in, and the Caliphs are not included in this book because it was famous before their era, and they are mentioned only in a few words. Regarding Imam Mahdi (a.s.), he writes: Abul Qasim Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Askari ibn al-Hadi. Ibn al-Hasan al-Askari ibn al-Hadi ibn Muhammad al-Jawad is the 12th Imam of the Shias, and he is famous by the name Al-Hujjah. His birth took place on Friday, the 15th of Sha'ban, 255 Hijri. When his father was martyred, he was 5 years old. This is another book where the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is mentioned. And it does not stop there; the father of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) is also mentioned, as is his martyrdom. It is also stated in clear words that when the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) occurred, Imam Mahdi (a.s.) was 5 years old. All these things prove that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has already occurred. The third book we need to mention is Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh, whose author is Ali ibn al-Athir. This is a book of Islamic history. It was completed around 628 Hijri and is one of the important books of Islamic history. It is found in several volumes, and each volume is organized by year. Each volume is organized by year. That is, the events that happened in the year 200 Hijri, the events that happened in the year 205 Hijri—in this way, the book is arranged by different years. When it comes to the year 260 Hijri, the author writes that in this year, i.e., 260 Hijri, Abu Muhammad al-Alawi al-Askari passed away. He was the 11th Imam of the Imami sect, and he is the father of... (the author has mentioned the name of the Imam of the Time (a.s.)) whom the Shias consider their 12th Imam, and his birth took place in the Sardab of Samarra. This is another reference where the author is stating that Imam Askari (a.s.) had a son named Imam Mahdi (a.s.), who is the 12th Imam of the Shias, and his birth took place in the Sardab of Samarra. He has stated everything in detail. So, this is the third book in which it is stated that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has occurred. There are many such books and many references that can be given where we can see from the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah... where we can prove from the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has occurred. The fourth book we need to mention is Tadhkirat al-Khawas, whose author is Sibt ibn al-Jawzi, who passed away in 654 Hijri. This book is based on the virtues of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the 12 Imams. In this book, regarding Imam Mahdi (a.s.), he writes that he is the son of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), and the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) took place in 260 Hijri. He has only mentioned this much regarding the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) in this book. If we read this book further, other attributes of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) are found, but regarding his birth, he has written only this one sentence. But to prove the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), this one sentence is enough. Because he says that the martyrdom of Imam Askari (a.s.) occurred in the year 260 Hijri and he had a son named Mahdi. So, if the martyrdom of Imam Askari (a.s.) occurred in 260 Hijri and he also has a son named Mahdi, then it is absolutely clear that his birth has occurred. He has not mentioned the date in this book. He has not mentioned the date in this book, but this fact can be proven from this sentence. So, viewers, in this video, we have presented four references before you where it is proven from the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has occurred. As mentioned, there are numerous such books where the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has been written about. We will put other references in the description for you. We request you to study these books as well so that it becomes absolutely clear that not only in Shia books but also in the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah, it is found that the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) has occurred. Wa Akhiru Da'wana Anil Hamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, wa sallallahu ala... Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Now the time has come that you all were eagerly waiting for. That is, the announcement of the daily lucky draw winners of the Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Panah-e-Kainat Mega Quiz, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. They will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees. Sayyid Yashab Hussain from Zadpur, Sayyid Qaim Raza Zaidi from Sultanpur, Fateh Ali Fatimi from Bengaluru, Marziya Rizvi from Mumbai, Maryam Zahra from Jamshedpur, Wajiha Kamran Sayyid from Pune Junnar. Many, many congratulations to all the winners. If someone's name did not appear in today's winners, there is no need to be disappointed. there is no need to be disappointed. This quiz link will remain live until the end of the series. And those who have given all the correct answers in the quizzes of seven out of twelve episodes will be included in the mega prize, i.e., the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq. We thank all of you once again. Insha'Allah, we will meet you again tomorrow at this same time with another new video. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 5 | Ghaibat-e-Sughra and the 4 Special Deputies (r.a.) - Part 1
excerpt: This lecture explores the foundational concepts of Mahdaviyyat, focusing on the birth of Imam Mahdi (a.s.) and the critical transition into the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra). It details the divinely appointed role of the four special deputies (Nawwab-e-Arba), specifically highlighting the life and service of Uthman ibn Sa'id. The session emphasizes the necessity of maintaining a spiritual connection with the Imam and distinguishes between the unique authority of the deputies and the role of modern religious scholars.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik aduwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwaleena wal akhireen. Astaghfirullahalladhi la ilaha illa huwal hayyul qayyum ar-rahmanur-raheem dhul jalali wal ikram wa atubu ilayh. Audhu billahis samee'il aleemi minash shaitanir rajeem. Bismillahir-rahmanir-raheem. Allahumma kun li waliyyikal hujjatibnil hasan salawatuka alayhi wa ala aaba-ihi fee hadhihis sa'ati wa fee kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafiza wa qa'idan wa nasira wa daleelan wa 'ayna hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu feeha taweela. Allahumma ajjil waliyyikal faraj waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi wa la taj'alna min a'da-ihi wa waffiqna lima tuhibbu wa tarda wa la takilna ila anfusina tarfata 'aynin abada wa la tastabdil bina ghayrana bihaqqi Muhammadin wa aalihi tahireen. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da-hum ajma'een. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Viewers, this Mahdaviyat webinar is progressing through its stages, and it is only because of your prayers and support that we are able to present various topics related to Hazrat Wali-e-Asr Hujjatibnil Hasanil Askari (a.t.f.s.) to you. This belief in Mahdaviyat and faith in Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.) is so important that the secret to the success of the efforts of all Prophets and Successors lies in the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.s.). The truthfulness of any belief can only be proven when its roots are in the Holy Quran. The eminent scholar Syed Hashim Bahrani (r.a.) has mentioned approximately 120 verses in his book 'Al-Mahajja' that relate to Imam Mahdi (a.s.). Alhamdulillah, this book has also been translated into Urdu and English. As lovers of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), we should keep trying to connect ourselves with the luminous sayings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) through such books. And why not, for only the Quran can truly praise another Quran. A poet has beautifully said: 'How the Quran recites the Quran, I wish to see this scene if the veil of the unseen is lifted.' How the Quran recites the Quran, I wish to see this scene if the veil of the unseen is lifted. And I think, why the formality of an 'Areeza' (petition), I wish to descend into the river myself this time. Dear brothers and sisters, our discussion yesterday was about Imam-e-Zaman (a.t.f.s.)'s noble mother, Bibi Narjis Khatoon (s.a.), and the birth of the Imam (a.s.). To summarize it: firstly, Bibi Narjis (s.a.) belonged to a very noble family. On her father's side, she was the granddaughter of the Caesar of Rome, and on her mother's side, she was from the lineage of the disciples of Hazrat Isa (a.s.), Janab-e-Yeshua. The Bibi's marriage was arranged at the age of 13, but by the command of God, an earthquake occurred, the wedding arrangements were destroyed, and the priest there told the Caesar of Rome that it seems as if Christianity is coming to an end. Then Janab-e-Narjis Khatoon saw a dream in which she saw Hazrat Isa (a.s.), Janab-e-Yeshua, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Janab-e-Maryam (s.a.), and the Princess of the Worlds, Siddiqa-e-Tahira Fatima Zahra (s.a.) visiting her house, and they ordered her to travel from Rome to Baghdad so that God's plan could be implemented. There was a war between Rome and the Muslims, and the Bibi included herself among the slave girls, through which she reached Baghdad. Imam Hadi (a.s.) ordered Bishr ibn Sulaiman—or as written in some books, Bashar ibn Sulaiman—to go to Baghdad and bring Bibi Narjis (s.a.) to Samarra. The Bibi reached Samarra, where her marriage (aqd) took place with Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). Then came the time for the birth of the personality who was to save this universe from oppression and tyranny. The 11th Imam's aunt, Janab-e-Hakima Khatoon (s.a.), was present there, and at the time of Fajr, the sound of Surah Inna Anzalna was echoing. After the recitation of Surah Inna Anzalna, a light appeared between Janab-e-Hakima and Bibi Narjis, and when that light vanished, the Imam of the Time was prostrating before God. Now, let us move to today's discussion, which is about the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra) and the Four Deputies (Nawab-e-Arba). As I promised yesterday, Alhamdulillah, we have with us a scholar who has served the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in such a way, and continues to do so, that whenever he speaks, it feels as if he is picking pearls from the ocean of the teachings of Aale Muhammad (a.s.) and handing them to us. With great respect and honor, I welcome Janab Maulana Syed Abu Talib Tabatabai Sahab to this Mahdaviyat webinar. Assalamu Alaikum, Aqa. Wa Alaikum Assalam, how are you? Are you well? Alhamdulillah, I hope Aqa that you and your entire family and loved ones are well. Thank you very much, Jazakallah. Despite all your busy schedule, you joined this webinar; this itself is proof of how important the service of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is to you. Thank you, viewers. Gentlemen, once again, I request that during the lecture, you continue to send your questions via the Strong Rope WhatsApp number, which is [number removed], or through the Q&A or chat option in Zoom. Alhamdulillah, we have received many questions, but keeping the time and topic in mind, only those questions have been presented to the speaker so far. So, Insha'Allah, this process will continue today as well. Let us begin today's session. Recite Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, who made praise a key to His remembrance, a cause for the increase of His grace, and a guide to His signs and greatness. And blessings and peace be upon His servant, the trustee of His revelation, the seal of His messengers, our master and leader, Abul Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad, and upon his pure and purified household, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them completely. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad, and curse all their enemies. Amma ba'd (Furthermore), Allah the Wise has said in the Glorious Book, I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: 'O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful.' This verse, which is the topic before you, the ladies and gentlemen, and first of all, thanks to God that in these circumstances, the entire current... By taking advantage of the system, it was organized in this way, and how can one thank God enough for this? The Lord of the Worlds knows this. There is a slight disturbance in our connection; I do not know if my voice is reaching you or not. It is reaching us, Maulana Sahib. There is a slight disturbance, but it is audible. Hmm, okay, good. Correct. So, in any case, while praying for more and more success for all of you, I will move forward. And that is, the verse I recited before you is from Surah Al-i-Imran, verse 200. In it, 'wa sabiru wa rabitu wattaqullaha la'allakum tuflihun.' I do not want to go into any complex discussion of Tafsir or Ta'wil here. Listen to the translation of the verse: 'Isbiru' (be patient). 'Wa sabiru' (encourage one another to be patient). 'Wa rabitu' (maintain the bond/station). I will present the translation in an easy way. 'Isbiru' (be patient). 'Wa sabiru' (practice patience together). 'Wa rabitu' (practice Murabita). 'Wattaqullaha' (adopt Taqwa/fear God). 'La'allakum tuflihun' (the hope is that you will find success). This means that after 'Isbiru, wa sabiru, wa rabitu,' the command for Taqwa is being given. Therefore, all these three commands must have a connection with Taqwa. Now, without wasting any time, without getting caught up in linguistic debates and all these hassles, so that we can get to our topic as soon as possible. What is the narration from the sixth Imam and the fifth Imam? That 'Isbiru' means be patient. 'Sabiru' means practice patience together. On what? On the Lord of the Worlds. 'Rabitu' means practice Murabita. Pay a little attention to the word. 'Rabitu' comes from 'Rabt' (connection). R-B-T. When we say, what is the connection (rabt) of this matter with that? What is your connection with him? It is used in Urdu as well. When it is used in Arabic, for those who have sat in an airplane, when it comes to fastening the safety belt or the seat belt in a motor car, it is written there: 'Irbitul hizam.' Connect/fasten your precautionary belt, which is your seat belt. Keep this meaning in your mind. What linguistics says about 'Rabt,' about 'Murabita,' which is the word used in the verse, is 'Saddus sughur' (fill the gaps). The soldier who is standing on the border and defending our country, where is he stationed? At the most sensitive place. The places that are clearly visible do not need as much military presence. Therefore, the soldier, the person of the forces, the 'Jundi' as they say in Arabic, who stands at a place to stop the enemy's army from entering, is called a 'Murabit'. He is doing 'Murabita'. The same word used in the verse, 'Rabitu'. Now, pay close attention. What does linguistics say? What does the Arab say? Regardless of whether he is a Muslim, an Arab, a non-Muslim, a Christian, a Jew, a Sunni, a Shia, a Deobandi, or a Barelvi. Look at the linguistics. 'Rabitu'. Where does the Arab use it? He calls that soldier who does not let the enemy's soldier enter. Now, what did the Imam say? The Imam said, 'Rabitu' means 'Al-muqamu ma'a imamikum' (stand with your Imam). Stay in connection with your Imam. Keep a relationship with your Imam. That is, if you have a connection with the Imam of your time, then just as that soldier who is standing at a sensitive place, who is standing near a cliff, or standing in a valley, or standing near a mountain bridge, or standing in the mountain ranges or forests—this is a dangerous place from where the enemy can come because this place is not very clear, the vision is not clear—so he stops the enemy from coming. Similarly, if you keep a connection with your Imam, then what will stop the gaps from appearing in your being, in your faith, in your belief, in your world, and in your hereafter? The connection you have with your Imam. The relationship you have with the Imam. 'La'allakum tuflihun.' The hope is that you will be successful. From here, this point was understood that the sixth and fifth Imams have stated this. Regarding this verse, without wasting time, this matter became clear. Connecting this verse with the words of both Imams (peace be upon them), the fifth and sixth Imams, that what is meant by 'Rabitu' is to maintain a relationship with the Imam of the time. When this point came up, the topic is so vast that I don't know how I will discuss it fully, but in any case, Insha'Allah, I will speak quickly so that I can cover the whole matter. We come here and see that, Alhamdulillah, the people listening are an educated gathering, educated people, conscious. In one word, the world of management today, actuarial sciences, risk management, and disaster management—things you know better than me, we learn from you—all these things are being taught at the Masters and PhD levels, and large institutions have been built that teach risk management, disaster management, actuarial sciences, and all this. If we take all these sciences that are taught in today's universities, and my topic, which is Imamate and the 'Nawab-e-Arba' (the four deputies), if we summarize it in one sentence. There is one word, Maulana. God sent the messengers, God sent the Imams, God sent... well, what should I do? It is written here that the audio is not clear, so should I keep going, keep speaking? I don't have anything to do with this, okay. I want it to be very good. Okay. A single, we say, don't we, a single-line agenda, Maulana. We sit in meetings, we sit, we say a single-line agenda so that we can move forward with great focus. So, what does a single-line agenda mean here? Why were Imams sent? Why were messengers sent? Why did the 'Nawab-e-Arba' come? Maraje-e-Taqlid, Mujtahid, 'Usul-e-Kafi' was written, and Sheikh Saduq, Sheikh Kulayni, Sheikh... there is a long list we have, of our greatest scholars. Summarize this in one line. What was all this happening? In the 1400-year history and before that, from Adam to Isa, and from Isa to Khatam-un-Nabiyyin (peace be upon him and his family), what was happening? This was 'Ehtiyaj' (need), requirement, need, necessity. The Lord of the Worlds wanted to fulfill your needs, your requirements, your needs, your necessities. Now, I don't know if I should say bring it to completion. 'Sadd-e-sughur' (fill the gaps), 'Qaza-e-hajat' (fulfill needs). Should I use these words? He wanted to take it towards accomplishment. Fulfilling necessities. The entire universe revolves around this. We came into the world, we need guidance in the world. We need the grave, we need the hereafter, we have to walk on the 'Pul-e-Sirat'. For all these things, the Lord of the Worlds sent whom? The Prophets and the Imams. Now, okay. Okay, okay. Well, correct, sorry. Thank you very much. Well, now I would like to look here. The first question is, and I will speak very briefly so that our discussion does not spread out. And I request that when my time is up, please tell me so that I can stop it. A question that young children, boys and girls, ask is: why did the 12th Imam go into occultation (Ghaybah)? And why has God kept the 12th Imam? Brother, the Lord of the Worlds has already said in the Quran that this is His will. 'Inna iddata shuhuri indallahi ithna 'ashara shahran.' In the sight of God, the months are only 12. When? 'Fi kitabillah.' God has written it in a written form with Him. Where are these 12 months? 'Yawma khalaqas-samawati wal-ard.' When He created the heavens and the earth, from that time He had decided that the months are 12. 'Dhalikad-dinul qayyim.' This is the religion of the Lord, believing in the 12 months, that this is the religion that is firm, established, strongly, nicely placed, well-rooted, it has very deep roots. Now, tell me, is believing in the 12 months such an important matter that the Lord will command to believe in the 12 months? There is a narration from the sixth and fifth Imams that the year is the Messenger of God, and the months are us. That is, the 12 Imams are the months. Therefore, the Quran does not mean the months by believing in these 12 Imams. Now, the point is, why did the Imam of the Time go into occultation? So, for the children, the college and university boys and girls who are sitting, I should tell them that when the head of the house wants to go on a journey for 2 or 3 months, he knows that he has a journey ahead. Whatever the reasons may be, he knows that he has to go on a journey after 3 months for 10 years. So, what will he do? He will check the house's electrical system. He will leave enough things in the refrigerator so that the children do not have trouble. He will arrange for a car, pay the university and college fees. All the necessities—this head of the house will be absent from the house for 10 years, will go away—so he will leave these needs fulfilled so that the children have food, drink, medical, education, house rent, utility bills... Okay. He will leave all the safety measures in place. If this occultation had happened to Imam Zainul Abideen (peace be upon him), then look, look at the history of all the Imams. During this time, you were given the sermons of Maula-e-Kainat. You received the teachings of Janab-e-Sayyeda. You received the Hadith of the sixth and fifth Imams. You were told about 'Ziyarat-e-Jamia Kabira'. You were taught 'Ziyarat-e-Ashura'. You were given the entire Hadith of more than 50 chapters of your Fiqh. That is, you were made self-sufficient, that O our followers, O our Shias, even if your 12th Imam disappears from your sight, disappears, is not seen, is not in contact, physically, then we are leaving you self-sufficient. Whatever there is, we are giving it to you. So, first of all, understand this. I will return to that point again, that one line, if we look at a single-line agenda, 'Ehtiyaj', fulfilling the need. How the Imam fulfilled the need, and the preparation for the Major Occultation (Ghaybah-e-Kubra) and Minor Occultation (Ghaybah-e-Sughra) had started from the time of Imam Hasan Askari and Imam Ali Naqi (peace be upon them). Therefore, 'need' is the best word, that the need had to be fulfilled. The conditions of the need had to be fulfilled. This matter ends here. Now we come to another point. Some people say that it was a political move, that if it couldn't happen for the government, then this should happen, if that couldn't happen, then this should happen. Sir, this was not a political move. It was just meant to be done in this way. When we take 'political' in its traditional meaning, what does it mean? It means that you come onto the floor, you come into the National Assembly, the Provincial Assembly, form a party there, then make alliances, gather them, raise them, make deals—so many ministers for you, so many for us. Imamate is not the name of any such sharing. 'If you do this, we will do that; we will step back this much, you come forward that much.' No, sir, absolutely not. Imamate is the existence of God Almighty that is visible, which is leading us to the Lord of the Worlds—the Imam of the Time. Therefore, remove from your minds that this was a traditional political move like worldly politics. It was not that. Rather, if we look precisely, the Imam of the Time, Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.), is preparing his followers for the Major Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Kubra) during the Minor Occultation (Ghaybat-e-Sughra). That is one point finished. I am giving an indication so that if I get the opportunity again, we can refine this and talk about it further. Keep this in your mind. The next question that arises is: among all the Nawwab-e-Arba (the Four Deputies), there is no Imamzada (descendant of an Imam). How can this be? Was no Imamzada capable of becoming a deputy, a Naib, or a special deputy (Naib-e-Khas)? They absolutely were. But the Taqiyya (dissimulation) that forced the Imam to carry out this task—if this word is not correct, I am saying it for the sake of explanation—was that if any of the Sadat (descendants of the Prophet) or the family of Bibi Fatima (s.a.) or the family of Hashim had been made one of the Nawwab-e-Arba, they were already under focus; they were already being oppressed. Since they were from the Sadat, they would not have been able to fulfill the responsibility, because the Imam did not want to perform a miracle. That is one point. Let me tell you another thing: we are building the equations, the preface, and the foundation here so that we can then know about the personalities of the Nawwab-e-Arba. Regarding these Nawwab-e-Arba, another point arises: that the scholars of today are not like that. Were Agha Boroujerdi not like that? Were Mohsin al-Hakim not like that? Were Agha Khoei not like that? Sheikh Ansari—why did they not become among the Nawwab-e-Arba, why did they not become a Naib-e-Khas? When we talk about the Nawwab-e-Arba or the Sufara-e-Khas, these are the special ambassadors, the special deputies of the Imam, whom the Imam of the Time (a.s.) himself appointed through his letters. That is why this question arises. Look, this is outside our jurisdiction. It is outside our authority to decide whether they were like that or not. If they were not, why were they not appointed? This is a method of the Imam. Therefore, when the Major Occultation began, there were four deputies. Who was the first? Uthman ibn Sa'id. Then who was the second? Muhammad ibn Uthman. The third was Husayn ibn Ruh, and the fourth was Ali ibn Muhammad. After these four, there is no longer a Naib-e-Khas. What does it mean that there is no Naib-e-Khas? Understand this: if we were living in the era of Uthman ibn Sa'id, and an order came from him, it would be as if that order came from the Imam of the Time. It is not the fatwa of Uthman ibn Sa'id. You can oppose a Marja-e-Taqlid; you can say, 'My Marja says I should pray, but I am not praying.' You become a fasiq (transgressor), you become a sinner, your testimony is rejected. But if you oppose Uthman ibn Sa'id, your belief in Imamate is corrupted. Therefore, our scholars have written that it is a necessity of the religion that the Sufara-e-Arba, meaning the Nawwab-e-Khas, are only these four, who were appointed by the Imam's own will and his blessed Tawqi (signed letter). What does this mean? No matter how great a Marja-e-Taqlid Sheikh Ansari becomes, no matter how great a scholar Sheikh Tusi becomes, since they are not among the Nawwab-e-Arba, not among the special deputies whom the Imam appointed through his letters by his own will, opposing them is a sin—even a major sin—but we might become fasiq, yet we do not exit the fold of the religion. Every Marja-e-Taqlid today has a proof (hujjat). I follow one Marja, you follow the one in Mashhad, he follows the one in Tehran, he follows the one in Qom, he follows the one in Karbala, and he follows the one in Najaf. Everyone is moving with their own proof. No one has the right today to say, 'I am directly connected to the Imam, and what I am saying is the Imam's word, so obey me.' That chain ended with the Nawwab-e-Arba. Keep this in your mind as well. Now we come to the Nawwab-e-Arba. There is another important point I want to present to you. Look, there is the Imam's will and the Imam's power. Maulana, is the speed of the Imam correct? Did the Imam not have the power to help us without the Nawwab-e-Arba? Does the Imam not have the power to come to every Shia's house in the morning and leave a letter saying, 'Do this work today'? There are two things. I am answering this. The Imam having power is one thing, and what the Imam has been ordered by God is another. In the event of Karbala, did the Imam have the power or not to make water gush from the earth with a gesture? He had the power. Did the Imam do it? He did not. Why not? The Will of God, the testament of the Messenger of God, the testament of the Panjtan (the Five), the way the Master of Martyrs (a.s.) had to proceed. So, our respected listeners—our brothers, sisters, mothers, and daughters—should not mix these two things. When we talk about the Nawwab-e-Arba, we are not just talking about the Imam's power. We are talking about the procedure, the process, and the chain of jurisdiction that the Imam left for us. Otherwise, tomorrow someone might say in Egypt, 'O Malik al-Ashtar, why did Ali send you? Salman al-Farsi, why did Ali send you? O so-and-so, why did Hasan al-Mujtaba send Hudhayfah al-Yamani? O Abu Dharr, why did the Messenger of God send you? Does the Messenger of God not have the power to come to our village and preach?' It is not about the power and strength of the Messenger of God, the Lady of the Worlds, the Panjtan, or the 12 Imams. It is about that chain, that link, that process and procedure which the Imam ordered us to follow. Okay? Let this be clear. Now understand one more thing. The Imam of the Time, the Infallible Imam, sometimes deals with two things, sometimes three. What does he deal with? The Will of God, the Knowledge of the Unseen (Ilm-e-Ghayb), and the trial of his servants. Let me clarify with an example. What is the Will of God? That Husayn remained thirsty. Husayn is also bearing this with complete happiness—'Allahumma lakal-hamd, hamd-e-shakireen' (O Allah, all praise is Yours, the praise of the grateful), the Ziyarat-e-Ashura is before you. Imam Husayn is bearing it with great happiness. And what is 'Samad-wa-Ta'atan' (patience and obedience)? That Husayn ibn Ali and his children remained thirsty and were martyred while thirsty. This is the Will of God, the command of God—to be patient. What is the Imam's Knowledge of the Unseen? What is the Imam's power? That if the Imam gestures, water would gush out. But how is the Imam taking the test of God's will and his servants? By keeping the children thirsty. 'Abbas, go dig a well. Abbas, go bring water. Habib ibn Mazahir, go bring water. O my companions, go fight, go to the Euphrates and bring water.' 'Maula, you know that you have the power.' So the Maula might answer, 'My having power is one thing, and I want to see if my companions hold this belief...' ...that Maula Husayn has the power to turn the course of the river, but despite that, the Maula is sending us. How obedient are my companions and how submissive are they to my command? Abbas, Abul-Fadl Abbas, Maula Abbas did not turn back and say, 'Brother, you have the power, just gesture and water will gush out from the tents. You are ordering me to dig a well?' No. The Will of God is one thing, Abbas's test is another. Have you understood this? Now we come to the Nawwab-e-Arba. What does the Imam want to do? The Imam wants to say that after me, in my Minor Occultation, there will be four, one after another, my deputies. How long is the period of the Minor Occultation? Excuse me, how long is the period of the Minor Occultation? The period of the Minor Occultation is approximately 69 years and some months. People have even calculated the days. You can say approximately 69.5 years. Okay, who was the first ambassador of the Imam of the Time (a.s.)? He was Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, Abu Amr al-Asadi. This was his name: Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, Abu Amr al-Asadi. He remained the deputy of Imam Hasan al-Askari and Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) himself. Therefore, this means that Uthman ibn Sa'id is no ordinary personality. If we keep a Marja-e-Taqlid for so many years, in 10-20 years there might be a disagreement somewhere, and we might not be able to follow the rulings of that Marja. But he remained the deputy of Imam al-Hadi. He remained the deputy of Imam Hasan al-Askari and then the deputy of the Imam of the Time—meaning he was the deputy of three Imams. In fact, there is a narration that when the Imam of the Time was born and our 12th Maula arrived in the world, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) ordered Uthman ibn Sa'id to buy 10,000 ritls of bread, 10,000 ritls of meat, and distribute it among the Banu Hashim. In our time, in today's time, Uthman ibn Sa'id was present at the Aqiqah of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). You see, this is a very strange virtue. He is the deputy of three Imams. He had two sons, Muhammad and Ahmad. Muhammad became the deputy, he came into his father's place after his father, but Ahmad did not become a deputy. Okay. Now look at his personality. And they were in Baghdad. And a strange oppression was that Sheikh Tusi wrote in his book that in our time, people think that this is the son of the lady who—let's say in our language—breastfed Imam Husayn, that Uthman ibn Sa'id is from her offspring. And Sheikh Tusi wrote that in our time, when we went to the grave to recite Fatiha, to perform Ziyarat of Uthman ibn Sa'id—because the time of Sheikh Tusi is 30-40 years after the passing of... ...Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id. There is a very small gap, even less than that, between Uthman ibn Sa'id and the era of Sheikh Tusi's Marjaiyat. Sheikh Tusi went to the grave to recite Fatiha, for Ziyarat, and he said that people there make vows and pray, saying he was a very righteous man and the son of the lady who breastfed Imam Husayn. Surely this is not so. This chain, these were the deputies. Meaning Sheikh Tusi wrote that until this time, this matter was not well-known, and the common people did not know. Sheikh Tusi, however, had gone. So, Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, Abu Amr al-Asadi. There is a very interesting incident regarding his Kunya (patronymic) that Imam al-Hadi (a.s.) told him to change his Kunya. A very subtle and interesting reason for this has been stated in the narration. I said, what did the Imam say? He was the deputy of the 10th Imam. Now look at what the Imam said. And I will make a request here that if we want to be close to our Imam of the Time, we must have great control over our tongues. You pray for me that I control my tongue, and I will pray for you. The tongue is a very important thing, and using the tongue correctly is among the qualities of the Prophets and the Saints. What is Imam al-Hadi (a.s.), the 10th Imam, saying about Uthman ibn Sa'id? He is saying, 'Fama qalahu lakum anni famaqalahu lakum fa-inni yaquluhu' (So listen, whatever Uthman ibn Sa'id says to you, understand that he is saying it on my behalf). 'Wa ma addahu ilaykum fa-inni yu'addihu' (And whatever he conveys to you from me, understand that he is conveying it on my behalf). Meaning, it is impossible that Uthman ibn Sa'id would say that Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) said this and be attributing a lie to me. This is a very great guarantee. Meaning, there is 'Ismat-e-Lisani' (infallibility of the tongue) for Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id. This is a strange robe of honor he received, a medal and a badge, a reward that Uthman ibn Sa'id received. Then, when Imam al-Hadi Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) was martyred in 254 AH, from 254 to 260—that is, 6 years—he was the deputy of whom? He was the deputy of Imam Hasan al-Askari, Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id. What did Imam al-Askari (a.s.) say about him? He said, 'Thiqatul-madi wa thiqati fil-mahya wal-mamat' (He was the trusted one of the past, and he is my trusted one in life and in death). He said he was the trusted one of the one who passed from among us—meaning my noble father Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) himself is saying this, Imam Hasan al-Askari. This is what Imam Hasan al-Askari is saying, that the one who passed from among us, meaning my father Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.), he was his trusted one, he was trustworthy, and there was a lot of reliance on him. And 'wa thiqati', he is my trusted deputy, my trusted student, my trusted companion. In what way? "Fī al-maḥyā wa al-mamāt" (In life and in death). Regarding whom was this said? It was said regarding Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id. And I mentioned that the 'aqiqa of the Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) was performed through him, and meat and bread were distributed among the Banu Hashim. Similarly, in a gathering where more than 40 believers were present, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) praised Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id. And when Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id passed away, look at the words used. The words were, the letter that the Imam-e-Zamana wrote, or the 'Tawqi' (signed decree) that was issued by the representative, was this. The Imam-e-Zamana is saying, according to this narration, to Uthman ibn Sa'id's son—to whom? To Muhammad ibn Uthman. He said, "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" (Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we shall return), "Tasliman li-amrihi wa ridan bi-qada'ihi" (Submitting to His command and being pleased with His decree). You all know the meaning of this verse; it means to be submissive in the face of God's command and to remain pleased with His decisions. "'Asha abuka sa'idan wa mata hamidan" (Your father lived happily and died while being praised). O Muhammad ibn Uthman, your father Uthman ibn Sa'id, the life he lived, he lived a very fortunate life, and when death came to him, it was in a state where he is being praised. These are the words of the Imam-e-Zamana. "Fa-rahimahu Allah" (May God's mercy descend upon Uthman ibn Sa'id, your father), "Wa alhaqahu bi-awliya'ihi wa mawalihi 'alayhimu al-salam" (And may God join your father, your father Uthman, with the Imams-e-Masumin, and with those whom he considered his Mawla, and join him with the Masumin). "Falam yazal mujtahidan fi amrihim" (He remained diligent in their affairs). Because, please pay close attention, I need to extract a meaning from this sentence to tell you. These are the words of the Imam-e-Zamana according to this narration, he is saying to your father—to whom is the Imam-e-Zamana speaking? To Muhammad. Which Muhammad? Janab-e-Uthman's son. O Muhammad ibn Uthman, your father Uthman, as long as he lived, he kept striving intensely. 'Mujtahid' does not mean what we use today. 'Mujtahid' in the hadith of the Imams means 'Ijtihad', that is, to struggle, to exert one's final efforts. As long as your father lived, he was 'mujtahidan', he tried his best, he put in every ounce of his strength. In what? "Fi amrihim" (In the affairs of the Imams). That is, in things that the Imams liked. Now someone might ask, what is the 'Amr' (affair) of the Imams? I will tell you briefly. The 'Amr' of the Imams is that whatever the Imams liked, the way they liked it, the things they emphasized, you should also emphasize them, you should also follow them. This is the 'Amr' of the Imams, and keep striving for it. The Imam-e-Zamana is saying this; there can be no greater testimony, witness, evidence, or proof than this. "Falam yazal mujtahidan fi amrihim" (As long as your father lived, in the affairs of the Imams, in the affairs of Imamate, he exerted all his strength). "Sa'iyan fima yuqarribuhu ila Allah" (And he lived in a state where he kept striving, making efforts in things that would bring him closer to God). And he kept striving for things that would bring your father closer to the Imams. "Naddara Allahu wajhahu wa aqala 'athratahu" (May God brighten his face and forgive his slips). The last two prayers. "Naddara Allahu wajhahu" is a verse from the Quran: "Wujuhun yawma'idhin nadirah" (Some faces that day will be radiant). There will be faces on the Day of Judgment that will have signs of joy on them, faces that will not have anxiety, faces that will be blooming, faces that will be like a blooming flower, faces that will have freshness and a pleasant effect, they will be delightful, they will be beaming, they will be happy. You see someone and say, 'What is the matter, brother? There are signs of great joy on your face.' The Imam is saying, "Naddara Allahu wajhahu" (May God keep your father's face just as fresh, radiant, and beaming). "Wa aqala 'athratahu" (And for your father, after all, Uthman... ibn Sa'id was not infallible, he was not infallible, he was fallible. He said, "Aqala 'athratahu" (And whatever mistakes your father made, any stumbling of any kind, any ignorance, may God draw a line through it, erase it, purify it, delete it, eliminate it). What did the Imam say in the second letter? "Ruzi'ta wa ruzi'na" (You have been afflicted and we have been afflicted). O Muhammad ibn Uthman, your father Uthman who died, passed away, death came to him from the world, he departed, he was our representative. You, you too have been afflicted with a tragedy, and we too have been afflicted with a tragedy. The Imam is saying, "Wa awhashaka firaquhu" (His separation has caused you anxiety), "Wa awhashana" (And we are also troubled because of his separation). "Fasarrahu Allahu fi munqalabihi" (May God keep your father happy in whatever state he is in the Barzakh, in his grave, in every state). "Kana min kamali sa'adatihi" (It was among his greatest fortunes). Your father's greatest good fortune was—we say things like 'The best of luck' or 'All the best', these are phrases we use nowadays—your father's perfection of good fortune was, "An razaqahu Allahu ta'ala waladan mithlaka" (That God granted your father a son like you), "Yakhlufuhu min ba'dihi" (Who can fill his place after him). Therefore, the Imam then said that O Muhammad, after Uthman, now you will be our representative. Now, from here, my point—the things that were being received, they ended. I intended to say two things here; one was the 'Nawab-e-Arba' (the four special representatives), what were their personalities? We tried to some extent to seek blessings from the personality of the first representative. People say, 'Shed some light.' What light can we shed? We will take light from them. So we took some light from them. One was their personality, our first representative, the first representative of the Mawla, may our pure peace be upon them, upon their parents, and may God the Almighty elevate their ranks, elevate them so much that the Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.) is pleased with them. The second point is now the method of propagation and connection, how they interacted with the believers, how they stayed in touch. Please pay close attention to this now. The most important issue today for us is not prayer; it is a personal issue. The most important issue when we come to the level of interaction is not our Azadari (mourning). The most important issue is not our fasting, not our Nazr-o-Niyaz (vows/offerings). The most important issue—you all know this. The most important issue is how we live in society. Are we living in society in such a way that because of our bad deeds and bad character, Azadari is brought into question? Are Azadars like this? Then the Azadari will also be like that. That is, the Alam of Mawla Abbas, the Zarih of Mohsin-e-Zuljanah, the Taboot of the martyrs of Karbala, we take all these things out, and take them out plenty, take them out to your heart's content, and take them out with the intention of seeking closeness to God, you will get reward. You take out the Mehndi of Hazrat-e-Qasim, you do everything, do it excellently. Do it with strictly halal earnings. Create memories, spread the mention of the martyrs of Karbala. But there is one small thing that is a very important thing, what is it? It is that one of our friends told a very good thing. He said, if you bring Zam-Zam water and put one drop of impurity in it, you cannot drink it now. If you bring Zam-Zam water in a dirty container, a stained container, an ugly container, people will not like to drink it. Therefore, what is the way to serve Zam-Zam? It is blessed water. Therefore, you give it in a very good container. Turbat-e-Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (soil of Karbala), it is soil that is a great honor for us to have in someone's house. So we wrap it in very good cloth, wrap it in a plastic bag, in velvet cloth, green, keep it in some box, a small case, and give it. We don't just take it out of a tissue box, wrap it in tissue, and say, 'Here, take this, I have brought you the soil of healing.' We don't do that. Therefore, when we are living in society, we have to see what the method of propagation is. What is the method of connection? The Imam's, which the Nawab-e-Arba had, should be ours. What do we do? We do, we start from where? We, first of all, do we have to propagate or not? Who said we have to propagate? That is, if we become a good Muslim, we become a good Shia, as the Imams have told us. The Imams said, 'Return the trust.' The dagger with which Mawla Ali was killed, if it is with me, I return it. The dagger with which my Baba Hussain was killed, I return it. If there is a Hindu, his check is due. Why are you holding it, brother? Return his check to him. Whatever you said, follow through with it. That is, among people, this should be, whose check is it? 'Man, that was such an issue, he is a friend of mine, you mean...' If we use this kind of language, then I am speaking in their language. This check, the one who does Majlis and Matam there, who does Zanjeer, who does Qama, I don't know what his religion is now, but he also carries the Taboot and also the Alam. He is good, I am worried. If he has written a check, it will not bounce. If we did it this way, this was the method of propagation, the method of connection of whom? Janab-e-Hussain ibn Ruh. And what is the second thing? That all—please pay close attention. To hide. To hide what? That is, what does it mean? To hide the secrets of the Ahl-e-Bayt. I said before, the Nawab-e-Arba, these four representatives who were made, you tell me when my time is up. Okay. Alright. So, what is the method of propagation in this? The method of propagation is that, brother, 'Be a good human being.' The Imam is the pinnacle of humanity. Imam Hussain is the one who gave water to Shimr in the Battle of Siffin, and Shimr is the one who did not give water to Hussain ibn Ali in the Battle of Karbala. So you see these two, how the characters are appearing. And now our method of propagation. What did I say? 'Taqiyya' (dissimulation). Hiding your secrets. In front of everyone, every matter, brother, you become a good person. Who said that you have to prove to everyone that this is how the Mawla-e-Kainat was, what is the status of Bibi Sayyeda? Until your presentation is good, the matter will not move forward. Therefore, remember, the method of the Nawab-e-Arba, people say, 'It was a political move and they bring it as an institution.' In such a way that it was a political move and the Imam wanted to do a political act. No. The Imam first of all wanted to make people accustomed to the Ghaybat-e-Kubra (Major Occultation), that there should be four representatives, representatives should remain, after that the Ghaybat-e-Kubra will begin. And the method the Imam used, it was that the Nawab-e-Arba used to sell oil, Janab-e-Uthman ibn Sa'id. So when they sold this oil, the barrels of oil that went or the water skins that went, they used to keep these messages inside them and send them. Therefore, what does this mean? This means that believers should make themselves a good human being, which were the teachings of the Imams, but the special teachings, share them with your friends. That all—your own, 'Jihadun fi sabilillah' (Jihad in the way of God), to protect our secrets, to protect our secret things is Jihad in the way of God. So what was their method of propagation? Their method of propagation was that first of all, they were an excellent Muslim, an excellent Momin, an excellent Shia. The tongue at this stage that the Imam-e-Zamana is testifying. The character at this stage that the Imam is saying that your father kept making continuous efforts. What is their method of propagation? Remember, the religion of Tashayyu says, 'Tell your people first what they need.' Give your people what they need. Before fixing ourselves, we want to fix the world. It cannot happen like that. Therefore, what I said at the very beginning of the speech, precaution, needs, necessities, what is that? In today's era, how will that issue be solved? I end my speech. It is in such a way that the sixth Imam said that, 'Shi'atuna khuliqu min fadili tinatina' (Our Shias are created from the remainder of our clay), our Shias are made from our remaining, remaining 'tina' (clay), the clay from which we were created, our Shias are made from that clay. The apparent creation is from clay, the inner creation is light. Now, let there not be a debate here that the Maulana said the Imams are made of clay and the Imams are made of light. The Imams are absolutely made of light, but the Imam wants to explain that the 'tina' that was ours, the essence that was ours, from what remained of it, our Shias are made. Therefore, there is our luminosity in our Shias, this is a hint towards this. I am definitely not saying that the Imams are made of clay, not made of light. No, the Imams have a luminous creation, there is no argument in this. 'Shi'atuna khuliqu min fadili tinatina' (Our Shias are made from our remaining clay). 'Yahzanuna li-huznina wa yafrahuna li-farahina' (They grieve for our grief and rejoice for our joy). Whatever makes us happy, makes them happy. Whatever makes us sad, makes them sad. Therefore, the Imam said, listen very carefully, that India, Pakistan, wherever this voice is going, he said that look, 'Fa-idha aradana ahadun minhum' (So whenever any of you, from our Shias, wants to do any good to us), 'Falyaqsidu-hum' (then do that good to our Shias). 'Fa-innahumu alladhina yasilu minhum ilayna' (Because the good you do to our Shias, it will reach us). Today you know the situation, there has been a lockdown. Such a big India, such a big Pakistan, the whole world is spread out. So the first thing is to take care of the believers and as much as possible, do that work openly. The Imam said, 'Mujtahidan' (exert all your strength) in fulfilling the needs of the Shias. Apart from this, your next-door neighbor, there is someone, a Hindu, a Sikh, an atheist, no problem. If hungry, give food in his house so that it is known that the followers of Ali ibn Abi Talib love humanity. Tell me, in the guise you are living, in the place where you are living, its protocols Look at this and look at all things. Now, look at this sentence here: what the Imam said about his deputy, that our deputy, Uthman ibn Sa'id, was a constant mujtahid (striver), he put in a lot of effort. Therefore, the Lord of the Worlds—because this was the status of Janab Uthman ibn Sa'id, being at the forefront of obedience—we have also been deeply saddened by his death, we are also distressed. Why are we distressed? The Imam does not need anyone. Remember, the Imam does not need anyone. That is, the Imam does not need anyone. The Imam himself is receiving all the divine lights. Why would the Imam be distressed by someone's death? We are distressed because what will happen to our Shias now? He was such a personality among the Shias. Therefore, if a person lives in a society where the believers reside and serves them in this way, fulfills their needs—widows, orphans, the poor, the destitute, education, health, shelter, food—in such a way that he protects the honor and dignity of Shia women so they do not have to leave their homes; if someone is creating employment for them so that a woman does not have to step out of the house, believe me, even if he skips his Night Prayer (Salat al-Layl) to do this work, he will get more reward than the Night Prayer. I am saying this in the light of tradition. Therefore, what was the most important thing? The most important thing was that the Imam of the Time (a.s.) is saying about his deputy that our deputy, Uthman ibn Sa'id, put in efforts his whole life, the work that we assigned—and regarding the work assigned, I read to you the hadith of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) that support our Shias in whatever way possible, the kind of lawful support that is appropriate. As I gave you examples of food, health, and all other things. So yes, it is our prayer that the Imam of the Time (a.s.) accepts these broken words, and thank you all very much. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin wa sallallahu ala sayyidina Muhammadin wa alihi baytihit tayyibeenat tahireen. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa ajjil farajahum. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. We have received some questions. Jazakallah. The first question is from Janab Zaheer Abbas Sahib via Zoom. Why is the word 'Naib' (deputy) used, while Naib means a successor? That is, Naib-e-Khas, Naib-e-Aam. So why is the word Naib used? Look, there can be no successor to Imamate. Remember, and this meaning of Naib as a successor is something we have derived from our own traditions. One point is this. Another point is that when we say Naib means a successor, if the Imam is placing someone in his position, the Infallible Imam is placing them for tasks that a non-Infallible person can perform. When we say—look, we have no issue with the word, our issue is with the essence. If someone believes that Uthman ibn Sa'id sat in the place of the Imam of the Time (a.s.), then it is as if he became like the Imam of the Time himself. If, for example, there is a person who has 20 years of medical practice experience, and someone else has 8 years, Imamate is not like that. An Imam is either an Imam or he is not. Right? And those people who participate in this Majlis, in the traditions, a special name has been given to them: 'Huddajul Hussain'. Huddajul Hussain are those who keep mentioning Hussain. Those who keep remembering Hussain, it is in the traditions. And they love Imam Hussain (a.s.) to such an extent that when they are told to go to Paradise, they will not even go to Paradise; they will sit outside Paradise and mention Hussain. This is a tradition from Kamil al-Ziyarat. So much so that even the Houris will come and say, 'Come, we are longing for you.' They will say no, they will say, 'The pleasure we are getting in the mention of Hussain, we will not get in anything else.' This is the mention of Hussain and this is the love of Hussain. This Azadari, this chest-beating, this Zanjeer-zani, this Qama-zani, all these Sha'air-e-Hussaini, these are all things where the collection of all goodness resides. Where all goodness comes and gathers. And in this, as much as possible, a person should try to excel, to excel over one another. No one should act with even the slightest stinginess or miserliness, thinking 'what will happen, what will not happen.' Because who is its Sayyid-us-Sardar (Master of Leaders)? It is the Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (Master of Martyrs).
