Because in the Holy Quran, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala has repeatedly declared that the authority to appoint a Caliph lies with Allah Himself. If you take the mention of Hazrat Adam (a.s.), in it, Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala has said, 'Inni ja'ilun fil ardi khalifa' (Indeed, I am going to place a successor on earth). When it comes to the Caliphate of Hazrat Dawood (a.s.), Allah says regarding Hazrat Dawood (a.s.), 'Ya Dawood inna ja'alnaka khalifatan fil ard' (O Dawood, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth). When we read the story of Hazrat Ibrahim (a.s.), what is the noble declaration of the Lord of the Worlds in it? 'Inni ja'iluka lin nasi imama' (Indeed, I will make you an Imam for the people). That is, Allah has never given the right to appoint a Caliph even to any Prophet or Messenger. Appointing a Caliph is solely the work of Allah. It is not the Prophet's job to appoint a Caliph, only to announce the Caliph. The Prophet will tell who the Caliph is, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced in the plain of Ghadir-e-Khumm, in the open field, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyun mawla' (Whoever I am his master, this Ali is his master). By pointing towards the Mawla, he announced it. That is, the Ali (a.s.) whom Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala made the Caliph, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced that same Ali (a.s.) as the Caliph. So here, the selection is Allah's, and conveying the message is the Prophet's responsibility. Now, the question here is to those who keep raising the banner of Tawheed and say 'ask from Allah, ask from Allah, ask everything from Allah'—why did they not ask Allah for the Caliph? And they refused to accept the one whom Allah sent as the Caliph. So now, what did the second ruler do at the time of his passing, in his final moments? He selected some people, he selected them in such a way that they could sit together, consult each other, and then select the next ruler. Although this action, i.e., making a Caliph by mutual consultation, is against the Quran. Is this not interference? On one hand, they are saying 'ask from Allah, ask from Allah, ask from Allah'—well, why didn't you ask Allah for the Caliph? And you refused to accept the one whom Allah made the Caliph. So now, what did the second ruler do at the time of his passing, in his final moments? He selected some people, he selected them in such a way that they could sit together, consult each other, and then select the next ruler. Although this action, i.e., making a Caliph by mutual consultation, is against the Quran. In the beginning, the second ruler had expressed the wish that 'I wish Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah was alive, I would have made him the Caliph.' Or Salim, who was the slave of Abu Hudhayfah, I would have made him the Caliph because I had heard from the Prophet's tongue, the noble tongue, that Allah loves him very much. That Salim, who was the slave of Abu Hudhayfah. Both had passed away, so it was not possible to make either of them the Caliph. Our question is, O Sheikh, you understood Salim, the slave of Abu Hudhayfah, about whom you say that the Prophet said Allah loves him very much, so why did you not remember this Hadith of the Prophet at that time? That at the time of the Battle of Khaybar, the Prophet had made an announcement, in whose honor had he made the announcement? Regarding whom, in whose context, did the Prophet announce, 'La u'tiyannar rayata ghadan rajulan karraran ghayra farrarin yuhibbullaha wa rasulahu wa yuhibbuhullahu wa rasuluhu' (I will surely give the banner tomorrow to a man who is a Karrar, not a Farrar, who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him). That tomorrow, I will give the flag to a man who will be a Karrar, not a Farrar, he will not flee, he will be one who loves Allah and the Messenger, and Allah and the Messenger will be loving him. So, what was your opinion about that person? Why did you not remember that Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) at that time to make him the Caliph? But regardless, what did the second ruler do? He formed a committee of six people. Who were those six people? First, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), second, Uthman ibn Affan, Abdur Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, and Talha ibn Ubaydullah. That is, these were the six people who were selected, and why was it done? We will come to that too. These six people were selected so that they could consult each other and appoint, select, choose a Caliph after him. Well, what is known about these six people? Why were they selected? Because these six were the individuals who, according to the Ahl-e-Sunnah—not our traditions, not Shia traditions, but according to the Ahl-e-Sunnah—all six of these individuals were included in the 'Ashara-e-Mubashara' (the ten promised Paradise). That is, those Ashara-e-Mubashara about whom the Ahl-e-Sunnah believe that the Prophet had guaranteed Paradise for them, that all of them are people who will go to Paradise. So, out of those ten, these six were selected for the Shura to decide together who would become the Caliph. Now, let us come to how the functioning of this Shura was determined? What were its rules? What were its laws? Were those six people supposed to do it together? The second ruler had also determined this and had already told them what those six people would do together, and had given some other instructions to some other people about what they should do. So, first, the second ruler called Abu Talha al-Ansari and told Abu Talha to gather 50 people, 'khamsina rajulan minal ansar', and keep all these six people in one room, and you stand outside with 50 people. This order was issued to Abu Talha al-Ansari. Now after that, the second order was issued, the second instruction was given, the second command was given to Janab-e-Miqdad. It was said to Janab-e-Miqdad, 'Idha wada'tumuni fi hufrati' (When you bury me), then what to do? Then gather these six people again, this group of six people, in one room so that they, these six people, can together select one person to become the Caliph. Now, pause here and reflect on just one thing. What order was given to Janab-e-Miqdad? 'When you have done my funeral rites, that is, when my burial is done, when you have lowered me into my grave, then do this work.' I will say, O Sheikh, why didn't you use this principle at the time of the Prophet's martyrdom? There, all the moths of the candle of Prophethood left the Prophet's funeral and gathered at Saqifah, saying that choosing a Caliph was more important at that time. So why is that haste not being shown now? Why is it being waited for that 'no, first the funeral should be done, then the Caliph should be chosen'? Where did all those moths of the candle of Prophethood go now? That is, at that time, they left the Prophet's funeral. This was the importance of the Prophet in your life, that leaving the Prophet's funeral is fine? But here, 'when my funeral is done, then do this work'. Have the bonds of loyalty been broken or joined? They have turned towards the threshold of the trial of love. And if this is the taste of loyalty, then shame on such loyalty; the moths have flown away from the candle. Was this loyalty? Anyway, the order given was that when you bury me, gather these people in a room so that they can meet among themselves, and they should be given a time of 3 days. Within these 3 days, they must choose one among themselves as the Caliph. Now, after this, the most interesting order, the most interesting law of this entire Shura committee that was given and announced, was this—and this was good. On the other hand, what was the order given to Abu Talha al-Ansari? 'You take 50 men and remain gathered outside. Now, what should you do? If five people gather in one place and one refuses, then what to do? Fashdukh ra'sahu bis-sayf (smash his head with the sword). That one person who has refused, behead him. Wa in-ittafaqa arba'atun wa aba ithnani fadribu ru'usahuma (And if four gather in one place and two refuse, then behead those two). And wa in radiya thalathatun rajulan (And if three people agree on a man), meaning three on one side, three on the other, fahakkimu Abdullah ibn Umar (then appoint Abdullah ibn Umar, my son, as a judge). My son will make the decision. And if the final decision is made—that if even after my son Abdullah ibn Umar's decision, they are not satisfied, meaning a decision cannot be reached—then what should you look for? Fakunu ma'a alladhina fihim Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (Then be with the group in which Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf is). That group, those three people who are choosing the Caliph together, accept him as the Caliph.' Side with them. Waqtulu al-baqina (And kill the remaining three). I mean, have you noticed what kind of order this is? On one side, these are the six individuals being selected to become Caliph. Meaning, all of them are considered worthy of becoming Caliph. On the other side, it is being said that if they do not agree, behead them. Why was the selection made? Because the Prophet had given them the glad tidings of Paradise, according to the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni view), meaning all of them are people of Paradise. An order is being given to behead the people of Paradise, and is this act in accordance with the Quran? Because what has the Holy Quran said? Look at Surah An-Nisa, verse number 93. In it, what does Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala command? That wa man yaqtul mu'minan muta'ammidan (And whoever kills a believer intentionally), if someone kills a believer intentionally, fajaza'uhu jahannamu (his recompense is Hell), his reward is Hell, khalidan fiha (abiding eternally therein), he will remain there forever, ghadiballahu 'alayhi (Allah is angry with him), Allah is wrathful upon him, wa la'anahu (and He has cursed him), and Allah sends His curse upon him, wa a'adda lahu 'adhaban 'azima (and has prepared for him a great punishment). I mean, this order to kill—meaning the Caliph is ordering the killing of those who are not satisfied with the Caliphate after him—is he paving the way to Hell for himself? This decision is beyond understanding. This is how this Shura was formed. As soon as this decision was made, when these six people gathered—meaning Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.)—at that time, Mawla met his uncle Abbas. So, what did Mawla do? Mawla said to Abbas, 'Adhalat anna' (This matter has slipped from our hands). Meaning, now the Caliphate is not going to come into our hands. So Abbas asked, 'Wa ma 'ilmuka?' (And how do you know this?). So, what did Mawla say? Mawla said, 'Look at how this entire Shura, this entire conspiracy, has been orchestrated.' Meaning, what was said? 'Kunu ma'al aksar' (Be with the majority), meaning always stay where there are more people. 'Wa fa-in radiya rajulani rajulan wa rajulani rajulan' (And if two people are on one side and two on the other), meaning if a group of three and three is formed, 'fakunu ma'al ladhina fihim Abdur-Rahman' (then be with the group where Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf is), the decision of that group will be accepted. And as far as Sa'd is concerned, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is the cousin of Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, so he will never oppose him. And Abdur-Rahman is the brother-in-law of Uthman; Abdur-Rahman is the brother-in-law of the third ruler, because the third ruler's step-sister was married to Abdur-Rahman. So, the collusion of these three people was immediately understood. Mawla immediately understood that this matter was not going to come into our hands. So then Mawla said to Abbas, his uncle, 'Falo kanal akharan' (Even if the other two decide in my favor), even if they support me, it will not be of any benefit. This is written in the famous book of Ahl-e-Tasannun, Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh by Ibn al-Athir, Volume 2, page 461. We are not giving evidence from our own books; this is a book of the Ahl-e-Tasannun. So, Mawla had already given the verdict, he had already understood and announced the decision that this was going to happen, and it happened exactly as Mawla had said. The Shura, the beginning of the Shura The council started. First of all, what did Talha do? Talha's vote went in favor of the third ruler. Zubayr voted in favor of Ali (a.s.). Now, since Sa'd was the cousin of Abdur-Rahman, he voted in favor of Abdur-Rahman. Abdur-Rahman played a clever trick here. Abdur-Rahman said, 'I am removing myself from this election, from this selection of the Caliphate.' Meaning, I do not want the Caliphate. So now, what did Abdur-Rahman do? Abdur-Rahman said to Mawla-e-Kainat, 'Ashhidukum' (I call you as witnesses). Now look, the decision was in Abdur-Rahman's hands. So, whoever Abdur-Rahman sides with will become the Caliph. So, what did Abdur-Rahman do first? He came to Mawla and said, 'Ashhidukum, I bear witness, I make you a witness, annani qad akhrajtu nafsi min al-khilafah (that I have removed myself from this Caliphate). And I will choose one of you two.' Both remained silent. Who? Ali (a.s.) and the third ruler who was about to be chosen. Both were silent. Now Abdur-Rahman said to Ali (a.s.), 'Ubayi'uka 'ala kitabillahi wa sunnati rasulillahi sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi wa sirati ash-shaykhayn' (I will pledge allegiance to you on the condition of the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, and the conduct of the two Shaykhs). I am ready to give my vote, to make a decision in your favor, on these conditions. What? That you will decide according to the Book of God, you will follow the Sunnah of the Messenger, and you will follow the conduct of the two Shaykhs. Now the question arises here: was the conduct of the two Shaykhs different from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger? If it was not different, then what was the need to mention it separately? And if it was different, then what was the need for Ali (a.s.) to follow it? So, obviously, since he was the true successor of the Messenger, the heir to the Book of God, and the protector of the Book of God, Ali (a.s.) refused this. He said, 'No, if I act, I will act according to the Book of Allah, I will act according to the Sunnah of the Messenger, and I will act according to my own Ijtihad.' Why shouldn't Ali (a.s.) act according to his own Ijtihad? Because 'Aliyun ma'al haqqi wal-haqqu ma'a Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali), and there is no error in Ali's Ijtihad. Ali knows very well. So Ali (a.s.) flatly refused, saying, 'No, your condition is not acceptable. I will act according to the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Messenger; I am not going to act according to the conduct of the two Shaykhs.' So when Ali (a.s.) refused, what did Abdur-Rahman do? He gave the same offer to the third ruler. He accepted it immediately. He came back to Ali (a.s.) and asked, 'Will you accept those conditions?' Ali (a.s.) said, 'No, I am not ready to accept.' So finally, what did he do? Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf went to the third ruler, placed his hand on his hand, pledged allegiance, and said, 'As-salamu 'alayka ya Amir al-Mu'minin' (Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Faithful). By saying this, he pledged allegiance to the third ruler, and the third ruler was selected to become the Caliph. At that time, Mawla-e-Kainat said to Abdur-Rahman—in fact, not just Abdur-Rahman, but to both Abdur-Rahman and the third ruler. Addressing Abdur-Rahman specifically, Mawla says, 'Wallahi' (By God), 'ma fa'altaha illa li-annaka rajawta minhu' (I know very well why you did this. Because you hope from him exactly what the one before you hoped from the one before him). Meaning, that one should leave and appoint the other. Meaning, you also did this out of greed for the Caliphate. Although you are not going to get this Caliphate. Then Ali (a.s.) cursed Abdur-Rahman, saying, 'Daqqallahu baynakuma' (May Allah cause a rift between you two). Meaning, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf and the third ruler, since they were relatives, brothers-in-law. So Mawla-e-Kainat cursed both of them, 'Daqqallahu baynakuma 'itru Manshim' (May Allah break you like the perfume of Manshim). 'Itru Manshim' is a different idiom. This is a specific phrase. What was 'Itru Manshim'? There was a woman from Hamdan who used to wear perfume or fragrance, and when people felt her fragrance, they were so influenced that they would end up fighting among themselves. Meaning, war. It is written that war, 'ishtaddatil harbu' (the war intensified), a severe war would break out between them. And then since then, this became an example for evil. If someone wanted to attribute evil to someone, or attribute a fight, this 'Itru Manshim' idiom was used. Now, this narration is found, it is written by Ibn al-Athir, in Sharh Nahj al-Balagha by Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili. On page 120 of its first volume, this entire phrase is written. Now, what was the result of this curse of Mawla Ali? It is said that 'fafasada ba'da dhalika bayna Uthmana wa Abdur-Rahman' (After that, there was so much discord between Uthman and Abdur-Rahman) that they stopped talking to each other until Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf passed away. Meaning, this is how the matter ended there in the Shura. Now Ali (a.s.) saw that this Caliphate was out of his hands, because he already knew. He had already told his uncle Abbas that this Caliphate was not going to be attained. Now begins the protest of Ali (a.s.). Those who say that Ali (a.s.) was satisfied, and that he participated in the Shura because he wanted to support their actions and them—so here Ali (a.s.) presented his protest, a historical protest. Shia, Ahl-e-Tasannun, all books, all historians have written it. It is written in our Shia books, it is written in the books of the Ahl-e-Tasannun, and great people have written it. For example, Ibn al-Maghazili al-Shafi'i has written in his book 'Manaqib Ali ibn Abi Talib'. There, Ibn al-Maghazili has mentioned the protest that Mawla-e-Kainat made at that time. Why does a person protest? Does a person protest in agreement or in disagreement? A person protests only when there is a disagreement with something. Otherwise, in the world, no person ever protests for something they are satisfied with. Protest is the name of expressing dissatisfaction. Mawla did this at that time. Ibn al-Maghazili al-Shafi'i has recorded 29 sentences of Mawla in his book. And here, our scholars have recorded 100 sentences—meaning 100 virtues that Mawla stated at that time. Ibn al-Maghazili brought 29, in our books 100 virtues have been stated. 100 virtues are recorded. At that time, Mawla protested in front of all the individuals present there, and one after another, one after another, he started stating his virtues, his excellences. And by stating these virtues, Mawla took testimony from everyone: 'Do you all, all the individuals here, believe in these virtues or not?' When they all said, 'No, all these virtues belong only to you,' then Mawla took this entire confession from them at that time. And now let's see what that protest was. As I submitted to you, when those people, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, gave his decision and the Caliphate once again slipped from Mawla's hands. Meaning, obviously, the Caliphate, the throne of Caliphate—Mawla did not need it. Mawla was not dependent on people's decisions. Allah has made him the Caliph. Ali loses nothing if people do not accept him. And even if all the people together oppose Ali (a.s.), no harm will come to Ali. The loss was only the people's. Once again, people made the wrong decision. And now what happened? Now began the protest of Ali (a.s.). The Lion of God started to roar. Now, one after another, the Lion of God, Mawla-e-Kainat (a.s.), is stating his virtues, counting his virtues. He says, 'I ask you in the name of Allah, all of you, is there anyone among you who acknowledged the oneness of Allah before me?' Everyone said, 'Allahumma la' (No, by God, no). You are the one who acknowledged the oneness first. 'Is there anyone among you, other than me, whose brother is Ja'far-e-Tayyar and whose uncle is Hamza, Asadullahi wa Asadu Rasulihi (The Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger), who is the Sayyidush-Shuhada (a.s.)? I mean, is there anyone? If anyone has such kinship?' Everyone said, 'No.' 'Is there anyone among you, other than me, whose wife is Fatima Salam-ullah 'alayha, Sayyidatu Nisa'i Ahlil Jannah (The leader of the women of the people of Paradise)? Is there anyone?' Everyone said no. Is there anyone else besides me whose sons are the leaders of the youth of Paradise? Now, Mawla Ali (a.s.) reminded them of Ghadir. And how did he remind them of Ghadir? Mawla said, "فَأَنْشُدُكُمْ بِاللهِ" (I adjure you by Allah), I ask you by Allah, "هَلْ فِيكُمْ أَحَدٌ قَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ" (Is there anyone among you to whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said...) although the word 'Aale' (family) is not written there, we are saying it. Is there anyone among you about whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declared, "مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلَاهُ فَعَلِيٌّ مَوْلَاهُ اللَّهُمَّ وَالِ مَنْ وَالَاهُ وَعَادِ مَنْ عَادَاهُ" (Of whomsoever I am Mawla, Ali is his Mawla. O Allah, befriend those who befriend him and be the enemy of those who are his enemy)? O Lord, accept him as Your friend, accept him as Your servant, who accepts Ali as his master. And become the enemy of the one who shows enmity towards Ali. "لِيُبَلِّغَ الشَّاهِدُ مِنْكُمُ الْغَائِبَ" (Let those present convey this to those absent). It is incumbent upon every person present, it is a duty upon every person present, to convey this message to those who are absent. Is there anyone besides me in whose favor this was stated? Everyone said, 'Allahumma la' (O Allah, no). No, by God, no. Now after this, Ibn Ali Salam, he keeps stating these facts, he keeps stating them. Who was given the support of the bird with the Messenger? Who received the standard (Alam) at Khaybar? Who did the angels greet? For whom did Zulfiqar descend from the heavens? For whom did the sun turn back? Who delivered Surah Tawbah? Oh, for whom did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say that your status in relation to me is like that of Harun to Musa? For whom did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say, "لَا يُحِبُّكَ إِلَّا مُؤْمِنٌ وَلَا يُبْغِضُكَ إِلَّا كَافِرٌ" (None shall love you except a believer, and none shall hate you except a disbeliever)? If anyone bears malice towards you, it is only because they are an enemy of the religion. Whose house door remained open in the mosque? Only mine. Is there anyone else besides me for whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that the truth is with Ali, and Ali is with the truth? The truth will go wherever Ali goes. For whom else did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) declare the Hadith al-Thaqalayn besides me? Who saved the Prophet's life by sleeping in his bed? Who went to face Amr ibn Abd-e-Wud when he was challenging the Muslim Ummah? And finally, Mawla says, according to this Hadith, for whom was Ayah al-Tat-hir revealed? These are all virtues; this is not our book. This is a book of the Ahl al-Sunnah, the book of Ibn al-Maghazili. He is a Shafi'i scholar. He has recorded all of this in his book. Despite all this, whatever Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf did, he did. He stopped Mawla from ascending the throne of the Caliphate, then stopped him again. And he handed over the government to the third ruler. Here, Sheikh Tabrizi brings a narration, and Allama Majlisi has also copied it in Bihar al-Anwar. That Mawla is stating, when I presented all my virtues before those people, I stated everything, they even acknowledged them. But in the end, what did those people do? The sentence of the narration Mawla says, "فَـتَغَامَزُوا بَيْنَهُمْ وَتَشَاوَرُوا" (They began to wink at each other and consult among themselves). They kept winking and saying what? "وَقَالُوا قَدْ عَرَفْنَا فَضْلَهُ" (And they said, we know his virtue), we know it very well. "وَعَلِمْنَا أَنَّهُ أَحَقُّ النَّاسِ بِهَذَا" (And we know that he is the most deserving of people for this), we know very well that Ali is the most deserving among the people for this Caliphate. "وَلَكِنَّهُ رَجُلٌ" (But he is a man...), but why are we not making Ali the Caliph? Why are we not agreeing to Ali's Caliphate? Why? Because Ali is such a person that "لَا يُفَضِّلُ أَحَدًا عَلَى أَحَدٍ" (He does not prefer one over another). He establishes equality among people. That is, a ruler who establishes equality among people, people do not like. Today, people yearn for equality. That there should be no rich or poor, no big or small. People yearn for this, people yearn for such a government. But here, they were getting such a leader, such a ruler, such a Caliph right in front of them, but the people refused. And then those people said, "فَإِنْ وَلَّيْتُمُوهَا إِيَّاهُ" (If you entrust it to him), if you entrust the Caliphate to him, to Ali (a.s.), then what will happen? "جَعَلَكُمْ وَجَمِيعَ النَّاسِ فِيهِمْ شَرَعًا سَوَاءً" (He will make you and all the people equal in it). He will bring everyone to one platform, he will consider everyone the same. You will not get a chance for partiality and favoritism. You will not be able to have your way. So, therefore, "وَلَكِنْ وَلَّوْهَا" (But entrust it to...), you do one thing, give it to the one whom Abd al-Rahman has decided. Follow that decision. Why? Because the one in whose favor Abd al-Rahman has decided, he will do exactly as you wish. And saying all this, "فَـدَفَعُوهَا إِلَيْهِ" (They pushed it away from him), they kept the Caliphate away from Mawla. And Mawla remained patient. Look, the protest, I have mentioned this in your service before. The protest is proof that Mawla was not silent. Neither was Mawla silent, nor was Mawla satisfied. And Mawla himself expressed this in Nahj al-Balagha, in Sermon number 74. The Imam says, "لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ أَنِّي أَحَقُّ النَّاسِ بِهَا مِنْ غَيْرِي" (You all know that I am more deserving of it than anyone else). "وَوَاللَّهِ لَأُسَلِّمَنَّ مَا سَلِمَتْ مَا سَلِمَتْ أُمُورُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ" (And by Allah, I will submit as long as the affairs of the Muslims are safe). Fine, I will be patient. As long as the affairs of the Muslims are safe and sound and no injustice is done to anyone other than me, I will be patient. That is, Mawla was ready to bear the loss of his own rights and the injustice done to himself. As long as other Muslims were not oppressed and remained safe and sound. But eventually, how long could they remain safe and sound? Then what happened? Ali (a.s.) was left alone again. He was stopped from the government and Caliphate for the third time. But Ali (a.s.) proved this by protesting. He is neither satisfied with the Shura nor satisfied with the Caliph appointed by the Shura. So the question arises, when Mawla was not satisfied with the Shura, and knew very well what the result was going to be, then why did Mawla participate in the Shura at all? The answer was given by Mawla himself. And this answer is also presented before you from the book of Ahl al-Sunnah, Sharh Nahj al-Balagha, from the book of Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili. When this whole incident was about to happen, Mawla had already stated what was going to happen, and what happened, happened. Ibn Abbas asked Mawla that when you knew very well what was going to happen and the Caliphate would go into the hands of so-and-so, then why did you participate in the Shura? Why should you have gone to the Shura? Now the sentence of the narration is, Ibn Abi al-Hadid al-Mu'tazili writes that "فَـقَالَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِذَلِكَ" (Ali (a.s.) said, I know that), I knew very well what was going to happen. "وَلَكِنِّي أَدْخُلُ مَعَهُمْ فِي الشُّورَى" (But I will enter the Shura with them). Why? Because the second ruler considered me worthy of the Caliphate. The second ruler considered me worthy of the Caliphate, that is why he included me in that Shura among those six people. But before this, some time before this, what had that second ruler said? That I have heard this Hadith of the Messenger that Prophethood and Imamate cannot be gathered in one house. So, therefore, I entered the Shura, I entered the Shura so that I could bring the lie of that second ruler before everyone. So that it becomes clear to all of you that the second ruler's words are different and his actions are different. Yesterday he said one thing, today he did something else. So, by participating in the Shura, the Mawla of the Universe not only opposed the Shura, but also opposed the one who had set up the Shura, and declared his displeasure and disagreement with him as well. title: EP#14: Inteqaam Nahin To Haadesa Nahin – Ek Ajeeb E’teraaz
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common skeptical argument that the absence of physical retaliation by Imam Ali (a.s.) implies that the burning of Bibi Zahra's (s.a.) house never occurred. The speaker refutes this logic by providing historical precedents where prophets and Imams chose patience over revenge despite clear instances of oppression. By citing examples like Prophet Adam (a.s.), the martyrdom of Janabe Hamza, and the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) treatment of his enemies, the lecture demonstrates that lack of revenge does not equate to the non-existence of an event. Ultimately, the speaker emphasizes that patience in the face of injustice does not absolve the oppressors of their crimes.
content:
Four such events where oppression took place but revenge was not taken. If the door of Bibi Zahra's (s.a.) house was burnt, why did Imam Ali (a.s.) not take revenge for such a major tragedy? Is not taking revenge proof that no such event occurred? In response, we present four examples. Qabil killed Habil; did Prophet Adam (a.s.) take revenge for the blood of his son Habil? No. In the Battle of Uhud, Janabe Hamza was martyred; did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) take revenge for the martyrdom of his uncle? No. Abu Sufyan plotted countless conspiracies against the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and fought many wars against him, but history is witness that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) never took revenge for this, neither before the conquest of Makkah nor after the conquest of Makkah. While returning from the Battle of Tabuk, a life-threatening attack was made on the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) saw the attackers, recognized them, and even told Janabe Hudhayfah the names of those hypocrites, but he never took revenge on those hypocrites. In all these events, revenge was not taken, but no Muslim has the audacity to deny them. Similarly, if Maula Ali (a.s.) did not take revenge and observed patience, then by denying this event, the oppression of the oppressors cannot be covered up. The oppression of the oppressors cannot be covered up.

title: Bughz-e-Fatima (s.a.) Ka Anjaam | From SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024
excerpt: This lecture discusses the severe spiritual consequences of harboring hatred or oppressing Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.). The speaker references a tradition from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) warning against those who usurp her rights. It emphasizes her status, specifically the granting of Maqam-e-Mahmood, which allows her to intercede for her followers on the Day of Judgment.
content:
Narrating from Abi Abdullah (a.s.) or Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'My grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), said: "He is cursed, he is cursed, he is cursed—the person who oppresses my daughter Fatima after me." And it is a matter upon which all Muslims agree that whoever oppresses Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is cursed.' Then the narration continues, 'And whoever usurps her right.' Now, is this some hidden matter? Who usurped the right of Janabe Zahra (s.a.)? Muslims should go and read the history of Islam to see what happened or who those individuals were who usurped the right of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). After that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, "O Fatima, I give you glad tidings of the Maqam-e-Mahmood." He is giving glad tidings to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) that, "O Fatima, this is the glad tiding for you, that Allah has given you the Maqam-e-Mahmood." What is the Maqam-e-Mahmood? It is the station of intercession that Allah has given to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), that you will intercede for your followers and for your Shias." You will intercede for your Shias, and Allah will accept your intercession. 'O Fatima, even if all the Prophets whom Allah has sent, and all the angels—and which angels? The Muqarrabun (near) angels—if all these Prophets and all the Muqarrabun angels try to intercede for any of those who bear hatred towards you, or for those who usurped your right, Allah will never grant that person freedom from Hell.' Even if all the Prophets and all the Muqarrabun angels try to intercede for that person. [Music]

excerpt: This lecture highlights the elevated spiritual status of Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.) through the historical account of a 190-year-old monk named Masram. The speaker details how the monk, who had spent his life in worship, prayed to Allah to meet one of His Awliya. Allah directed Hazrat Abu Talib to visit the monk, who immediately recognized his spiritual greatness upon their meeting. The narrative emphasizes the profound sanctity of the father of Imam Ali (a.s.).
content:
How high is the status, how blessed is the personality of Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.). In this regard, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) narrated a very interesting incident, and this incident is also related to Ali (a.s.). Among them, there used to be a very famous monk; he was 190 years old. He was famous, that monk, his name was Masram. For 190 years, he had worshipped Allah. [Music] That monk had a prayer to Allah: 'O Lord, show me the sight of one of Your Awliya (friends), let me meet one of Your Awliya.' And then Allah revealed to Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) to go and meet that monk. Now, we are not discussing the personality of Ali (a.s.), we are discussing the father of Ali (a.s.). We are discussing the father of Ali (a.s.). We are not discussing the personality of Ali (a.s.) itself. First, one should understand the personality of Abu Talib (a.s.), the one from whose lineage Allah brought forth Ali (a.s.). When Allah revealed to Abu Talib (a.s.) to go and meet that monk, the monk Masram immediately stood up from his place, kissed his forehead, [Music] and asked him a question. [Music] He had not yet introduced himself. A person living in the mountains of 'Kahma'—as soon as he heard the greeting, he immediately said, 'In our land, the air is... where are you from? Which region?' So Janabe Abu Talib (a.s.) said, 'From Makkah.' 'Oh, in Makkah, who are you related to?' He said, 'I am from my [Music] tribe.' As soon as the monk heard the name, he immediately stood up from his place, stood up again—where he had greeted him before, he stood up again and... Where he had greeted him before, he stood up again and went to him, for he whose prayer was... [Music]

title: EP08 | Madine Mein Hua Sab Se Badaa Zulm | Bayn-ash-Shahadatayn | Ayyaam-e-Azaa-e-Fatimiyyah (s.a)
excerpt: This lecture recounts the tragic events surrounding the attack on the house of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.) in Medina. It details the historical account of the oppressors threatening to burn the house to force a pledge of allegiance from Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker highlights the physical assault on Lady Fatima (s.a.), which resulted in the martyrdom of her unborn son, Janabe Mohsin (a.s.). The talk concludes with a reflection on the promise of justice through the eventual reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).
content:
Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'When our Mahdi comes, he will burn those oppressors with the same wood that they had gathered to burn Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Hussain (a.s.), because that wood is present with us as an inheritance.' After failed attempts to forcefully extract a pledge of allegiance, the oppressors sent orders to the oppressors to go to their house and order them to come out and give the pledge. 'If they agree, then it is fine, otherwise gather wood and fire and tell them that if they do not come out and give the pledge...' Tell them that if they do not come out and give the pledge, the entire house will be burned down with the inhabitants inside. Seeing the oppressors coming towards the house, the Princess Fatima Zahra (s.a.) thought to close the door, thinking they would not enter the house without her permission. But they knocked on the door forcefully, pushed it with strength, and started to force their way in. When the Lady remained firm in her place, they were told, 'Be silent, Fatima! Neither Muhammad is among us now, nor are those angels who used to bring messages of revelation from Allah in the air, and Ali is like an ordinary Muslim. Now, if you wish, send him out for the pledge, otherwise, you will all be burned.' The Lady began to cry and prayed, 'O Allah, we complain to You that Your Prophet, Your Messenger, and Your chosen one are not among us. This Ummah has turned away from us and snatched away the right that You granted us.' The Princess was still making this plea when those oppressors set fire to the door and... Those oppressors set fire to the door, and—may Allah curse them—attacked the door. Then an oppressor struck the Lady's arm with a whip in such a way that a black mark appeared on her arm. But that oppressor did not stop there; he kicked the door, which fell onto the stomach of the Lady (s.a.). This was the oppression due to which her 6-month-old son, Janabe Mohsin ibn Ali (a.s.), was martyred in her womb. The Lady cried out to her father, saying, 'O Father, O Messenger of Allah, your daughter Fatima is being belied, she is being beaten, and the child in her womb has been destroyed.' This was the great oppression that took place at the house of the daughter of the Master of the Universe and the Prophet of Mercy. Those who recited the Kalima of the Prophet attacked with such beastly hearts that neither their hands trembled nor their feet. Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'When our Mahdi comes, he will burn those oppressors...' When our Mahdi comes, he will burn those oppressors with the same wood that they had gathered to burn Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Hussain (a.s.), because that wood is present with us as an inheritance. O Allah, for the sake of the broken rib of the Lady, hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and grant us the ability to take revenge from the oppressors along with him. Ameen, Ya Rabb-ul-Alameen. I don't know [Music] [Laughter]

title: Khilqat-e-Noor-e-Fatima (s.a) | From SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024
excerpt: This lecture explores the metaphysical origin of Lady Fatima (s.a.), highlighting that her light was created before the heavens and the earth. It details a narration from the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) regarding a divine gift from Paradise in the form of an apple. Upon consuming this fruit, the Prophet witnessed the radiant light of the 'Mansoura,' identifying her as Fatima (s.a.) on earth.
content:
The Imam states that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, "The light of Fatima (s.a.) was created before the creation of the earth and the heavens." The light of the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.) was created before the creation of the earth and the heavens. When Allah (s.w.t.) created Prophet Adam (a.s.) and brought me out from his loins, and Allah (s.w.t.) willed to bring her—the Princess of the Worlds (s.a.)—out from my loins, Allah placed her in Paradise in the form of an apple. Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) further states that Jibra'il (a.s.) brought this apple to me and said, "O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), indeed Allah has sent this apple to you as a gift from Paradise." Allah is saying, consume it. He says that when I split it open, I saw a light emanating from it that left me astonished. Then Jibra'il (a.s.) said to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), "O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), consume it and do not worry, for that is the light of the 'Mansoura' (the helped one) in the heavens, and she is Fatima (s.a.) on this earth."
The light of Fatima (s.a.) predates the creation of the heavens and the earth.

The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was instructed to consume the apple, which contained the light of the 'Mansoura'.
The title 'Mansoura' refers to the one helped in the heavens, known as Fatima (s.a.) on earth.

title: #10: Ziyaarat-e-Arbaeen Ka Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Se Rabt | Sharh -e- Ziyaarat -e- Arbaeen [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound spiritual connection between the Ziyarat-e-Arba'een and the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The speaker highlights how Imam Mahdi is the ultimate avenger of Imam Hussain's blood, as evidenced by historical accounts of his prayers at the Kaaba. The session emphasizes that mourning for Imam Hussain should naturally lead to a deep, restless longing and prayer for the reappearance of the Imam of our time.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us. Someone asked the second special deputy of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) among the four deputies, namely Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri (r.a.), "Have you seen the Sahib al-Amr (a.t.f.s.)?" He replied, "My last meeting with him was at Baytullah al-Haram, near the Kaaba, when he was reciting this prayer: 'O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me.'" In another hadith, it is found that Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) was holding the covering of the Kaaba and saying: "O Allah, take revenge from Your enemies." We read a similar phrase in the Ziyarat-e-Arba'een of Imam Hussain (a.s.). A pilgrim says this to Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Ziyarat-e-Arba'een: "I bear witness that Allah (s.w.t.) will fulfill the promise He made to you." He will destroy those who abandoned you, and He will punish those who killed you. That is, after Ziyarat-e-Ashura and Dua-e-Nudba, it is clear in Ziyarat-e-Arba'een as well that there is a special connection between Imam Hussain (a.s.) and Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) is not only the heir of Imam Hussain (a.s.), but he is also the avenger of the blood of Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). From these two hadiths and this phrase of Ziyarat-e-Arba'een, it is clear how important it is for those who mourn the great martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) to pray for the earliest reappearance of the avenger of the blood of Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.). When Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) himself has been so restless for about 1200 years for the revenge of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and is praying for his reappearance, then imagine with what intensity and longing we, as lovers, mourners, and pilgrims of Imam Hussain (a.s.), should pray for the reappearance of our Imam of the time. O Allah, by the intercession of the oppression of Imam Hussain (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the avenger of the blood of Hussain, our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). Grant us the opportunity to pray for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) while holding the blessed Zarih of Imam Hussain (a.s.) in his shrine, and grant us the opportunity to take revenge on his enemies alongside him after his reappearance. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Holy Quran Webinar | Session # 1 | Excellence & Importance of The Holy Quran - Part 1
excerpt: This webinar session explores the profound significance and divine nature of the Holy Quran, emphasizing its role as the ultimate criterion for truth. The lecture highlights the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahlulbayt, arguing that true understanding of the scripture is rooted in the teachings of the Prophet's household. Participants are encouraged to view life as a journey of preparation for the afterlife, utilizing the Quran and the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt as essential guides for salvation.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, make this gathering a means of understanding the Quran and a source of guidance for us. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I hope all of you are safe in your homes. May Allah keep all believers and Muslims safe. May He accept our worship during the month of Shaban and the month of Ramadan, and grant us the ability to benefit from the blessings of this holy month. After the success of the previous webinar, we received requests from viewers to organize similar programs because this is a unique initiative where a single topic is discussed from various perspectives, followed by a Q&A session. By the grace of Allah and the prayers of the believers, we are here with another webinar series. When this webinar was being planned and the topic was chosen, we thought that since the month of Ramadan is the spring of the Holy Quran, why not discuss the Holy Quran? And since we are followers of the school of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), why not try to attain the recognition of the Quran through the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)? As mentioned in Al-Kafi, Volume 8, page 312, Sheikh Muhammad bin Yaqub (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.): Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) says: 'Innama ya'rifu al-Qur'ana man khutiba bihi' (The true knowledge of the Quran is only with those who were addressed by it). The true recognition of the Quran is only with them. That is why the title of this webinar is 'The Knowledge of the Quran in the Teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)'. I welcome all the viewers to this series. In this series, there will be a discussion on a specific topic under this title every day. You can also participate by sending your questions. In every session, the speakers will address your questions related to the topic, and God willing, they will provide answers. You can send your questions to the Dostan Group WhatsApp number [number removed]. Since this webinar is related to the Holy Quran and the month of Ramadan is the spring of the Quran, this webinar will begin with the recitation of some verses of the Holy Quran. For this, we are happy to have a renowned personality among us who... is known worldwide for his expertise in the recitation of the Quran. The students trained by you are known as Qaris all over the world, and you yourself are invited as a judge in competitions worldwide. Those who have heard of the 'Nawa Academy' will know that I am referring to Maulana Asad Abbas Khan Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum. Thank you for joining us and for reciting the Holy Quran for us. May Allah reward you for this noble deed. [Recitation of the Holy Quran] [Recitation of the Holy Quran] Indeed, Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. We are grateful to Maulana Masood and the viewers. God willing, we will continue to benefit from Maulana Masood's recitation of the Holy Quran in every session of this webinar. Another routine of this webinar will be that after the recitation and before the speech begins, a brief Hadith related to the interpretation of 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' will be presented for the viewers. Let us begin with Bismillah. In Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn, Volume 1, page 233, Hadith number 256, it is narrated that someone asked Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s.) about the interpretation of 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'. Imam (a.s.) replied: 'Ba' stands for Baha'ullah (the splendor of Allah), 'Sin' stands for Sana'ullah (the glory of Allah), and 'Mim' stands for Mulkullah (the kingdom of Allah). 'Allah' is the One who possesses divinity and lordship over all creation. 'Al-Rahman' is the One who is merciful to all His creation, and 'Al-Rahim' is the One whose mercy is specifically for the believers. And that is the word of my Master. Along with this, the topic of today's webinar is very important. To shed more light on it, we have Dr. Sabih Zaidi Sahab with us. Assalamu Alaikum, Sir. Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I hope you and all your viewers are well. I welcome you to this webinar, and viewers, I request you to keep sending your questions related to the topic to the Dostan Group WhatsApp number. God willing, the answers to those questions will be given after the speech. Let us begin this webinar with the remembrance of the Imam of our time (a.s.) and through the intercession of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allah the Almighty has stated in the Holy Quran that the month of Ramadan is the month in which We revealed the Quran. It is a guidance for the people and contains clear proofs, signs, miracles, and is the criterion (Furqan) to distinguish between truth and falsehood. Verse 185 of Surah Al-Baqarah confirms this. As we all know, the Holy Quran was revealed in this holy month. It is a miracle that will remain until the Day of Judgment. If anyone has any doubt about Islam or the truthfulness of the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.), let them bring a book like the Quran, bring verses like these, and see the depth of its meanings and wisdom contained wisdom. It is present, and it is present, and you have challenged people at least three times to bring a book like it if you have any doubts. You have been asked to bring something like it, to bring it in three different places, to bring it in fourteen years. The enemies of Islam have attacked Islam according to their own stations and tried to defame Islam in different ways, using every kind of method, but there was no one who stood up and said, 'I have brought something better than the Quran, challenge the Quran.' This concept, this idea, this work, this last, this Quran—if there is something better than the Quran, then you should have brought it. So, the Surah was... Bring your claim, bring your proof, and bring something better than it. If you read this, there is nothing better than it. And what is better than the Quran? And what is better than the action of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? And what is better than this miracle? And in the discussion of the Quran, the discussion of the Day of Judgment, you will not find anything better than it. Better is far away; you won't even find anything close to it. See, in one statement, he claimed that he could bring it, and he made a claim that he challenged it. And Rahman Malik said that he made it like the Quran, in two places, 'Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alamin', he made a claim in place of the Quran. He is the master of Rahman Malik. When he wrote the commentary, he gave a proper answer to it, saying that if you accept this challenge and do not do this kind of act, your honor is ruined. Your honor is ruined by making this claim. This is not how it is done. This is just taking the words of the Quran and changing them. If you want to bring something, bring something that is better than the Quran's status. If there is something better than 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim', then bring it. If there is something better than 'Alhamdulillah', then bring it. But in any case, in the Holy Quran, it happens that in Surah Al-Furqan, verse 33, it says: 'And they do not bring you a parable, but We bring you the truth.' That We come with the truth, We bring the truth, We bring the Quran. Now, the commentary is mentioned here. The best commentary is mentioned, and everything is mentioned. Now, without going into details, it is enough that 'Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with Ali.' Wherever Ali is, turn the truth towards him. The Quran, Ali, the truth—Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with Ali. Both are together; they will never be separated. So, we should always try to know about the importance and the virtues of the Holy Quran. This is the Quran, this is the Quran, this is the Quran. In Surah Al-Ankabut, verse 49, it says: 'Nay, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.' These are clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. What is this? These are the verses of the Quran in the chests of those who have been given knowledge—that Allah has given them. Apart from them, no one else can claim this. This is the commentary of the Quran, and no one will deny that they can speak about this. And all people have been given this, that they should ask and learn. If you do not know, ask me, ask questions. And that is why, when their knowledge becomes a book, these people go to the Kaaba. These people go to the Kaaba. It does not come to anyone else. In Islam, when a commission is formed, an example is set. So, we should do our duty, which is to understand what the Quran is. And on the other side, I address those who claim that we love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If we are truly Shias, then we should hold fast to this Quran, about which the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) have emphasized, about which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) has emphasized. It is our responsibility to fulfill this duty, to acquire its knowledge, to know about it, and to read the Quran. And to gain information about it. So, I said that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Allah will not punish the heart that contains the Quran.' The day on which there is the Quran in the heart, Allah will not punish it. This is present in our traditions. It has been mentioned in volume 66. Now, let us not delay. The Quran is something that we should read, memorize, read its commentary, and try to understand its meanings and contents. Before moving forward, let me mention that there is a book written by Marhum Bahrani, 'Majma al-Bahrain'. He was a great scholar of his time. And this 'Majma al-Bahrain', this book, is the meeting of two seas. What are these two seas? The Quran and Hadith. By this, it is meant that the words in the Quran and Hadith whose meanings are difficult to understand, he has explained their meanings in six volumes, and in fact, even more volumes now. A lot of work has been done on it. This book is printed. Now, its name is Majma... This book is printed. Now, its name is Majma al-Bahrain. Let me tell you about him, who he is. Marhum Bahrani (r.a.) was the teacher of Allama Majlisi, he was the teacher of Sayyid Hashim Bahrani. He was one of the great scholars. Because he was a great scholar, but he had such great students who were famous scholars of their time. They must have sat at his feet to learn. So, as it begins, the introduction of Marhum Bahrani, in it, immediately, after the praise of Allah and blessings upon Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his family, he immediately wrote about the Quran, that acquiring the knowledge of the Quran and knowing about it is essential for the Arabic language. Why? Because the correctness of his book and the basis of its being... The basis of its being depends on how much he knows the Quran. That is why it is very necessary to learn Arabic. And if he doesn't learn, if he reads Arabic, reads traditions, reads Hadith, then the matter will be understood by him, he will understand the truth. If today, Alhamdulillah, many of our sources, our references, are being translated into Urdu and English, there is no doubt that these are good things. But if one reads the original directly, it is something else. So, here the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that Allah will not punish the heart that contains the Quran. So, think about how important it is. It cannot be punished; Allah will not punish it. Therefore, Imam Ali (a.s.) says: 'The best among you is the one who learns the Quran and teaches it to others.' This is also present in our traditions. And if you want, you can refer to it. Now, here in the traditions, he mentions something... Here in the traditions, he mentions something. The tradition is from Al-Kafi, and in it, there might be some Arabic words, some text that is necessary to read because the meaning of that word is the concept itself. Therefore, it is necessary to understand that once, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave a sermon. In that sermon, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'O people, you are in a house of preparation.' What should we do? Then he answered it. So, whatever you are taking, you are in a journey. You are traveling. This life is a journey, and this traveling is very fast. This journey is very fast. And you have seen that the day and night, and the sun and the moon, have made everything new old. And everything that is far... And the state of things that were far away has now been brought near. I have seen you, and now look, this might be something that the youth might not understand quickly, but those who are a bit older—forty, fifty, seventy-two—can understand this more quickly. If you ask me why the old things, the childhood memories, seem like they are happening now, it is because time is passing quickly. What was new has become old; what was far has become near. And this sun, this moon, and you—all of these are bringing everything that was promised. What has been promised? The promise of death, the promise of the resurrection, the promise of the Day of Judgment—everything must be faced. This is not a joke. Have you seen anyone who has lived in this world forever? No one has. Everyone has to go. He says, 'Whatever has been promised is coming very quickly.' Look, it is coming very quickly. Until now, it seems so immense to us, as if it belongs to someone else, or as if it is something else. But those who kept moving forward know that everyone has to go. And in the end, in this tension, in this claim, he is saying that everyone should keep in mind that they have to answer before Allah. Every single thing must be answered. No one should think that nothing will happen to them. Certainly, Wilayah—that is, the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—will save us, it will save us with great difficulty, but it should not be that we claim Wilayah while our actions, our behavior, and our character are like those whom the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) used to condemn. Anyway, coming back to the Hadith, he said, 'Prepare yourselves, get ready for a journey from which you must pass.' Prepare yourselves, get ready for a journey from which you must pass. It is a very long journey, but no one knows when the Day of Judgment will come. No one knows when Qiyamah will arrive. Every person thinks, 'I died a thousand years ago,' and they think their deeds were not good, and they are in a state of anxiety. This thought might be in your mind, it might be in the state of Qiyamah, because Qiyamah is a day that will be very long. But we can be saved. In fact, a few moments of suffering can feel like a long time. If someone is in pain, suffering, or worried, and you ask them, then even a few moments feel like a long time. So, if one has to burn for thousands of years, and if there is no Wilayah in it, and Qiyamah is there, then you can understand what the condition will be. Therefore, prepare yourselves, get ready for the journey, and the best thing for that is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Prepare yourselves, get ready for the journey, and the best thing for that is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). But this Wilayah means that your life should not be wasted; it should be spent in obedience. Try to make your deeds such that they please them (the Ahlulbayt), that they remove their displeasure, so that we can be theirs, and they can say, 'Yes, this is ours.' As the Imam (a.s.) himself said, and this is a matter of the past, the story is very old. Now, when I reached this number, I remembered that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that after his martyrdom, people would turn back. When this happened, Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad (r.a.) remained. I am telling you that slowly, people started returning, the number of 16 or 17 people who were there at that time, as mentioned in the narrations... ...as mentioned in the narrations, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) stood up and asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the house you mentioned, the house that is the cause of the delay?' He said, 'This is the house that will reach you, the house that will bring you to the destination, and it is the one that will cut off all ties.' You will be surrounded by trials. How? He says, like a dark night, a pitch-black night when the moonlight is dim and there is nothing to see. At that time, you are surrounded on all sides. We are walking on a path where there is absolutely no light, and that path is also very bad. There are many deep pits, or we are walking on a narrow bridge, and there is a fear of falling down. Along with that, there are man-eating beasts... ...along with that, there are man-eating beasts. If you are traveling on such a path, what will you do? What should you do at that time? He says, 'In such circumstances, hold fast to the Quran. Hold it firmly.' Remember, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said many times, 'I am leaving two things among you: one is the Book of Allah, and the other is my Ahlulbayt.' Here, he emphasizes that without the Ahlulbayt, the Quran cannot be understood. If anyone says that, he will be a liar, because without them, he will not understand the Quran. Because the Quran and the Ahlulbayt are such that when they intercede for someone before Allah, their intercession will be accepted. Whether it is good or bad, the person will say, 'O Lord, he used to recite me, he used to recite me all year round, and especially in the month of Ramadan, he used to recite me more.' So, at that time, he will take care of the Quran more because it is that month. But who is the one complaining? The one whose complaint will be registered, whose complaint will be accepted. It will not be like that. He will say, 'He abandoned me. He used to keep me in his house, but I was in such a high place that it took effort for him to take me down.' And then he would keep it just to show off. So, if someone is going on a journey, this complaint will be registered. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Whoever makes the Quran his guide, his leader, and his companion, he will be led to Paradise.' Whoever makes the Quran his guide, his leader, and his companion, he will be led to Paradise. And whoever puts the Quran behind him, abandons it, or ignores it, it will drive him, it will drag him, and take him to the Fire. The Quran is the proof, it is the guide that leads to the best path. There is no path better than this, as it is mentioned in another verse: 'Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.' That is, the Quran guides towards the Imam, and the Imam guides towards the Quran. Both are connected to each other. Therefore, they will not be separated from each other until they come to me at the Fountain (of Kawthar). They will not be separated from each other until they come to me at the Fountain. And he pointed with his fingers, joining them together, saying, 'The Quran and the Ahlulbayt are like this.' These two fingers are exactly equal. One leads to the Imam, and the Quran contains the details of all things, the explanations, the signs. And look, this is the word of Allah, it is not a joke. There are things in the Quran that are not hidden, and there are things that are hidden. And who has the knowledge of the hidden? Only the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). One should turn to them; they will explain, they will make one understand one thing. Just as the Quran has seven levels, and for everyone, there are seven meanings, and for every year, seven meanings emerge. Remember, this is being told to show that it has infinite meanings. That is why the Imam (a.s.) said that if he had people who could understand, he would have shown them the religion, the Sharia, and everything from the Quran. But for me, it is such that I have to go to the pulpit and say, 'Ask me before you lose me.' So where would I get such people? He says that the Quran has an outward appearance, and its inward is very deep. Its outward is very beautiful, very beautiful. It is very beautiful, very beautiful. It is very deep in its meaning, its concepts, its beliefs, its love, its ideas, and its purpose. In every aspect, it is like an ocean of ancient narratives. It is truly beautiful. All the things that the Quran says, with its eloquence and rhetoric, with the weight of its words, it is top-class. No one can compete with it. If we discuss these things, Insha'Allah, we will try to provide examples if Allah grants us the ability. The Imam (a.s.) says that the Quran has an outer meaning and an inner meaning. It has levels, and for every level, there are many sub-levels. For everyone, it is a miracle, and its strange and wonderful things never grow old. Its strange and wonderful things never grow old. And no matter how many times you recite it, you find a new meaning, a new insight. This is very important; you should keep reading it. Tafsir al-Ayyashi is available; it is a treasure. It is a lamp of guidance. If anyone needs guidance, then the Quran is there. We are from the Quran, we are from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If someone says, 'We have read the Quran a little bit, now what? Should we not read it anymore?' Please, never think like that. It has a depth, no matter how much you have read. Read the Quran. If you don't know how to learn it, then this blessed month of Ramadan is the best month. It is the month of Allah, the month in which the Quran was revealed, in which the lamps of guidance are present, and the signs of truth are present. Look at the depth of the Quran. Tafsir al-Ayyashi is a book that tells us how to attain Ma'rifah (divine knowledge). It explains how, through the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), a person can attain Ma'rifah from Allah. This tradition is present in Tafsir al-Ayyashi. Remember, some people say that this Tafsir is not reliable. You go and read the books of Rijal and see what the scholars have written about Ayyashi. Muhammad bin Mas'ud al-Ayyashi was a great scholar. He was not born a Shia, but when he started seeking knowledge and truth, he realized that the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) was the true path, so he accepted it. He accepted the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and then dedicated his life to the service of the religion in a way that no one else could. His father was very wealthy; according to today's calculations, he had about 300 crore rupees. He spent his entire inheritance on the teachings of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.). When I went to meet Muhammad bin Mas'ud al-Ayyashi, I saw that his house was divided into three parts. The first part was where Ayyashi would sit and explain religious issues to people. The second part was where people would write down traditions (Hadith), and the third part was where the traditions were checked, proofread, and corrected. This was his contribution. Unfortunately, his entire Tafsir was destroyed. During the time of the Abbasids, when there was a major attack on the Shias, Tusi had to leave Baghdad. Anyway, that is a different topic, but you should read this Tafsir. It has been translated into English, and if not, those who can should get it translated and spread it among the people. Insha'Allah, we will talk about this tomorrow. Walhamdulillahirabbil Alameen. Thank you very much. We have some questions. The first question is: 'Are the words of the Quran kept hidden, and if Allah wanted to hide them, why reveal them at all?' What is the question? My answer is clear. Everyone understands that the capacity for understanding varies. Even the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—let alone the Quran—when he used to speak, he would look at the capacity, the intellect, and the background of the people. It is narrated that the Prophets (a.s.) were commanded to speak to people according to their intellect. In the traditions, there is a discussion that when the Imams (a.s.) spoke, they would give different answers to the same question to different people. Why? Because their capacities were different. If he gave one answer to one, he wouldn't understand, and if he gave it to another, he wouldn't understand. So, he gave different answers according to their capacity. That is why Allah says the Quran is for the people, but we might not understand it. Many things were kept hidden so that people would ask the Imams (a.s.). It was asked, 'Why is the Quran hidden from us?' The Imams (a.s.) said, 'It is our responsibility to explain it.' We do not take knowledge from anyone else. The Imams (a.s.) have the knowledge so that they can answer. Allah has given everything to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and the Imams (a.s.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) never spoke from his own intellect. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) never spoke from the depths of his own intellect. Because no one could understand the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) knowledge except Ali (a.s.). Whatever he gave, he gave to Ali (a.s.), and then to the Imams (a.s.). Apart from them, no one else had access to it. And the other people, he never spoke to them like that. If you look at the verses of the Quran, Allah mentions two types of people: those who listen and those who understand or memorize the Quran. Some people say that when you finish reciting, you see... Surah Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), verse 16. It says, 'Among them are those who listen to you, but when they leave, they ask those who were given knowledge, "What did he say just now?"' These are the people whose hearts Allah has sealed because they followed their own desires. The second question is: 'What is the translation of Alif-Lam-Mim according to Hadith?' This is a separate topic, and we will discuss it. It is among the 'Muqatta'at' (abbreviated letters), and Insha'Allah, the Tafsir will explain it. There is a tradition about it. The question is: 'Does the person who recites the Quran not get punished? What about the person who does not recite it? Will they be free from punishment?' Let me correct this. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'We have no status of our own.' There is a tradition in Al-Kafi that says if someone wants to reach the Quran, they should say, 'Allahumma inni abra'u ilayka min... (O Allah, I disassociate myself from...)' and follow the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.). My belief regarding everything is exactly what the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have stated. Whether it is what they have kept hidden, or what they have revealed, or what has reached us, or what has not reached us—my belief regarding everything is exactly what the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) have stated. This is the first point. The second point is that the question arises, and as for the narrations, our narrations are absolutely correct and are also present in the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah. The condition for the acceptance of deeds is the Wilayah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). If one does not have Wilayah, then even if one prays or fasts for thousands of years, it will be of no use. When asked about this, the Imam (a.s.) replied that if this is the case, why do people talk about other things today? Why do they talk about other things today? If you go to many Western countries, America, or Australia, you will find university professors in various departments who know more than Muslims. They have memorized the entire Quran and keep its exegesis with them. They study it more than us. So, if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has said that from the recitation of the Quran to everything else, it is tied to the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), then these two conditions are very important. This second generation is very important. But along with this, I repeat to all the brothers and sisters who have asked questions, and to others as well, that Ramadan is the month of Wilayah and also the month of the Quran. As much as possible... As much as possible, because as we are followers of them, and as we are followers of this school of thought, it has been said that if you hold onto the rope of Allah, it refers to the Quran, and it has also been said that it refers to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). It is said, 'Hold firmly to the rope of Allah,' and the Quran is also called the rope of Allah, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is also called the rope of Allah. Both are called the rope. So, how can both be the rope? This question will only be asked by someone who has not seen a rope properly. When a rope is strong and good, how is it made? If there are separate strands, how are they intertwined? The more they are intertwined, the stronger the rope becomes, and the more you can rely on it. It is called Hablullah (the rope of Allah) and also Urwat al-Wuthqa (the firmest handle). And the firmest handle is that which you can rely upon; it is the most reliable. If one is reading the Quran but does not have this, then it is of no use. If one is reading it without this, then it is of no use. Thank you very much for the insightful points you have made regarding the excellence and importance of the Holy Quran. We pray that Allah grants us the ability to learn more of the Holy Quran and understand it in the light of the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). As we conclude, I would like to inform all the viewers that regarding the discussion of every session, a quiz will be presented to you tomorrow, Insha'Allah. In this way, a quiz will be presented to you every day. Those who give the most correct answers will be given a gift after the completion of the entire series, Insha'Allah. We have reached the end of today's session. Insha'Allah, we will meet again tomorrow at the same time, 10:30 PM India time. We will be back tomorrow with the same topic, in the light of the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) regarding the knowledge of the Holy Quran. Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alamin. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad...

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#10 | Waqeah e Ghadeer - Ahle Tasannun ki Kitabon mein | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture, part of the 'Shameem-e-Ma'refat' series, explores the historical and theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi provides evidence from Sunni scholarly sources to authenticate the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) declaration of Ali (a.s.) as his successor. The discussion emphasizes the consensus regarding the term 'Mawla' and encourages viewers to utilize historical documentation to deepen their understanding of Wilayah.
content:
But a little bit of the path... [Arabic recitation]... The day, the occasion, the event that I wait for the most throughout the year, today that occasion is arriving. Today that occasion is arriving, the occasion in which the religion was completed, the occasion in which faith was perfected, the occasion in which blessings were fulfilled, and the occasion from which the authority of Islam was established. This event is remembered in the memory of that promise when, after completing the Hajj, when all the pilgrims were returning to their homes, in the plain of Khumm, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) called back those pilgrims who had gone ahead, waited for those who were left behind, and in a place where the heat of the sun was intense, in the scorching sand of the desert, he stood before the pilgrims and delivered that sermon. And that sermon, in that heat, was described in two ways: some people were burnt by the sun in the desert... Some people were burnt by the sun in the desert, and some were in the shade. Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) was the shade for some, and for others, it was a test. But those who were the followers of the truth, they accepted it. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyun mawlahu' (Of whomsoever I am the master, this Ali is his master). So, surely this was unpleasant for some people. The state of their lives was beautifully described in these four lines: 'When the sun was scorching, the servant of the Lord... how could one go away from the shade? The shade of Abu Haydar, whose habit was to solve difficulties, the shade of Abu Haydar, whose habit was... I will not ask today.' title: Qayamat Mein Bibi Fatima (s.a) Ke Shiyon Ka Maqaam | From SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2024
excerpt: This lecture describes the profound status of the Shias of Bibi Fatima (s.a.) on the Day of Judgment. It explains how these believers will be granted the unique honor of interceding for those who showed them kindness or support for the sake of the Princess of the Worlds. The narrative highlights the deep spiritual connection between the followers of Fatima (s.a.) and the acts of charity performed in her name.
content:
When these lovers, when these Shias are granted intercession, and when they are permitted to enter Paradise, they will refuse to go in. They will stand at the gates of Paradise and wait. Allah will then ask them, 'Why are you not entering? You have already been granted intercession.' These Shias will then say, 'O Lord, we wish for our status to be revealed before everyone, just as the status of the Princess (Fatima (a.s.)) was revealed. We want people to recognize our worth.' Allah will then say, 'Go back. Return to the plains of Mahshar (the Gathering). Look for those who loved you for the sake of the Princess, who loved you because of the Princess, and for the sake of the Princess. See who fed you in the name of the Princess, who gave you clothing in the name of the Princess, who quenched your thirst in the name of the Princess, and who averted any calamity or trouble from you in the name of the Princess. Go and find anyone you know who did this, and take them with you into Paradise.' So these Shias will go and intercede for such people, for the sake of Fatima (a.s.).
