title: Inhedaam-e-Jannatul Baqi Ki Asl Wajha Kya Hai? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and ideological motivations behind the destruction of the Jannat al-Baqi cemetery by the Al-Saud government. The speaker argues that the demolition was driven by deep-seated envy and hatred toward the Ahlul-Bayt, rather than genuine theological concerns regarding innovation. By highlighting the sacred figures buried there and the Prophet's own reverence for the site, the lecture calls for the eventual restoration of these shrines under the leadership of Imam Mahdi.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not destroy us. Malice, enmity, and hatred towards the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) is an incurable disease, as a result of which a person loses both their intellect in this world and Paradise in the hereafter, and the reason for this is only one: envy. But those who envy forget that the status and position attained by the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) is what Allah has bestowed upon them. In the Holy Quran, Allah (s.w.t.) says: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Ibrahim the Scripture and wisdom and conferred upon them a great kingdom." Since all these virtues and merits are bestowed by Allah (s.w.t.), when the envious could not snatch the status of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) from them, they chose the path of oppression. Sometimes they usurped their rights, broke the allegiance pledged to them, waged war against them, martyred them with poison or swords, and sometimes killed their followers. It reached the point that when the oppressors saw that despite all efforts, the status, dignity, and glory of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) remained the same, they started taking revenge on their graves. The destruction of the Jannat al-Baqi cemetery is the result of that same envy and hatred that existed in the hearts of those with extremist and terrorist ideologies towards the Ahlul-Bayt of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.). A Muslim cannot even imagine that the Al-Saud government, which oversees the Haramain Sharifain for Muslims worldwide, had such hatred for the Progeny of the Messenger that they demolished the shrines and domes built over the graves of the children of the Messenger. Jannat al-Baqi is not an ordinary cemetery. Who is buried there? Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba (a.s.), who, besides being the grandson of the Messenger, is also the leader of the youth of Paradise. Imam Ali ibn Hussain Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.), who is the nephew of Imam Hasan (a.s.) and the son of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Then Imam Zayn al-Abidin's (a.s.) son, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.), and his son, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), at whose service the Imams of the four schools of thought of the Ahl al-Sunnah sat with reverence. According to some narrations, the grave of the daughter of the Messenger, the Princess of the Worlds, Hazrat Siddiqa-e-Tahira Fatima Zahra (s.a.), is also in Baqi. Besides them, the noble mother of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Hazrat Fatima bint Asad (s.a.), the brother of the Master of the Universe, Aqil ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), Bibi Umm al-Banin (s.a.), Bibi Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib, Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and the famous companion of the Messenger, Uthman ibn Maz'un, whom the Prophet himself buried there. The Prophet's son, Janab-e-Ibrahim, who is buried near Uthman ibn Maz'un, and Asad ibn Zurara, who was the first among the people of Medina to embrace faith. Furthermore, as far as the excellence of Baqi is concerned, this narration from the famous Sunni book Sahih Muslim is sufficient, in which Aisha bint Abi Bakr states that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) used to go to Baqi in the last part of the night and say: 'Assalamu alaykum dara qawmin mu'minin, wa atakum ma tu'aduna ghadan mu'ajjalun, wa inna in sha' Allahu bikum lahiqun. Allahummaghfir li-ahli Baqi' al-Gharqad' (Peace be upon you, O abode of the believing people. What you were promised has come to you; your time had arrived, and soon, God willing, we will join you. O Allah, forgive the inhabitants of Baqi al-Gharqad). The tyrannical government of Al-Saud completely ignored the fact that the very land of Baqi which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) used to greet and for whose buried believers he used to seek forgiveness, they razed the graves of the Household of Prophethood and demolished the shrines built there. The Al-Saud government justified this act, which shamed humanity, by claiming that visiting graves is an innovation (bid'ah). However, their hatred for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) misled them to such an extent that along with this visit of the Prophet, they also forgot the clear verses of the Book of Allah, in which the justification for building a mosque at the resting place of the People of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf) and making the Station of Ibrahim (Maqam-e-Ibrahim) a place of prayer exists in the Holy Quran itself. During the circumambulation of the Kaaba, they see no harm in offering prayers at Hijr-e-Ismail, where the graves of the Prophets (a.s.) are located. Yes, but the only thing that causes them pain is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and their graves. O Allah! By the sake of the desolation of Jannat al-Baqi, for the return of the splendor of that graveyard and for the revenge of the demolition of Jannat al-Baqi, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the opportunity to rebuild the shrines of Jannat al-Baqi along with him. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds.

title: Dua-e-Iftetaah: Importance & Dua with English & Urdu Translation | Shaikh Maitham al-Najafi
excerpt: This lecture explores the spiritual significance and structure of Dua-e-Iftitah, a prominent supplication recited during the nights of Ramadan. Shaikh Maitham al-Najafi explains that the prayer was narrated by the second deputy of Imam Mahdi and serves as a profound tool for recognizing Allah's attributes and mercy. The talk breaks down the supplication into its three core components: praise of God, salutations upon the Prophet and the Ahlulbayt, and a heartfelt plea for the reappearance of the Imam to establish justice.
content:
A'udhu billahis-sami'il-'alim minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Sallallahu alayka ya waliyal-asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Among the famous supplications recited in the nights of the blessed month of Ramadan is Dua-e-Iftitah. This supplication was narrated by Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri (r.a.), who was the second ambassador and special deputy of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.), upon the command of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.), that recite this supplication every night of the blessed month of Ramadan, because the angels listen to the supplications of this month and seek forgiveness for the one who recites it. This supplication contains the highest themes of the recognition of the Lord of the Worlds. His praise and glorification, His attributes, especially His complete mercy when He acts with pardon and forgiveness, and His punishment when He takes severe account and revenge. The reasons for the delay in the fulfillment of needs and the statement of the most important blessings of Allah Almighty are at the beginning of this supplication. The second part of the supplication is that in which special blessings and salutations are upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.), and their names and titles are mentioned. Then there is the prayer for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.) and the expression of the desire for the establishment of the Islamic government, at which time Islam and the people of Islam will gain honor, and hypocrisy and the hypocrites will be humiliated and disgraced. And since we are among those who invite people towards that government, it is our responsibility to invite others towards the obedience of Allah Almighty and guide them towards the path of God. The third and final part of the Dua is one in which there is a complaint in the court of Allah (Azza-wa-Jall), in which there is a complaint regarding the absence of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) among us, the occultation of our Mawla Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajuhush-sharif), the large number of enemies, our scarcity, severe tribulations, and the oppression of enemies against us. However, along with all these things, there is also a prayer to Allah (Ta'ala) for victory and success through the reappearance (Zuhur) of the Imam (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajuhush-sharif). This Dua is called Dua-e-Iftitah because it begins in this manner: [Arabic text omitted] He has given me, and He has sufficed me against great terrors, and He has shown me delightful joys. So I praise Him, thanking Him, and I remember Him, glorifying Him. All praise is due to Allah, whose veil is not torn, whose door is not locked, who does not turn away the one who asks Him, and who does not disappoint the one who hopes in Him. All praise is due to Allah, who gives security to the fearful, saves the righteous, raises the oppressed, humbles the arrogant, destroys kings, and replaces them with others. And all praise is due to Allah, the crusher of tyrants, the destroyer of oppressors, the one who overtakes the fugitives, the punisher of the unjust, the helper of those who cry for help, the place of needs for those who ask, and the reliance of the believers. All praise is due to Allah, from whose fear the heavens and their inhabitants tremble, the earth and its dwellers shake, and the seas and those who swim in their depths surge. All praise is due to Allah, who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. All praise is due to Allah, who creates and is not created, who provides and is not provided for, who feeds and is not fed, who causes the living to die and gives life to the dead, and He is the Living who does not die; in His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your messenger, Your trustee, Your chosen one, Your beloved, the best of Your creation, the guardian of Your secret, and the conveyor of Your messages—with the best, most beautiful, most complete, purest, most growing, most pleasant, cleanest, most exalted, and most abundant blessings, benedictions, mercy, affection, and peace that You have ever bestowed upon any of Your servants, prophets, messengers, chosen ones, and those who are honored by You among Your creation. O Allah, and send blessings upon Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, and the successor... of the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, Your servant, Your guardian, the brother of Your Messenger, Your proof over Your creation, Your greatest sign, and the Great News. And send blessings upon the truthful and pure Fatima, the leader of the women of the worlds. And send blessings upon the two grandsons of mercy and the two Imams of guidance, Hasan and Husayn, the leaders of the youth of the people of Paradise. And send blessings upon the Imams of the Muslims: Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hasan ibn Ali, and the Successor, the Guide, the Mahdi—Your proofs over Your servants and Your trustees in Your lands, with a continuous and abundant blessing. O Allah, and send blessings upon the guardian of Your affair, the Awaited Qaim, the hoped-for Justice, and surround him with Your close angels, and support him with the Holy Spirit, O Lord of the Worlds. O Allah, make him the caller to Your Book and the upholder of Your religion. Appoint him as Your successor on earth, just as You appointed those before him. Establish for him his religion which You have chosen for him, and replace his fear with security, so that he may worship You and not associate anything with You. O Allah, honor him and honor through him, help him and help through him, and grant him a mighty victory, and open for him an easy opening, and grant him from Yourself a supporting authority. O Allah, manifest through him Your religion and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, so that nothing of the truth remains hidden for fear of any of Your creation. O Allah, we desire from You a noble state in which You honor... Islam and its people, and humiliate hypocrisy and its people, and make us therein among those who call to Your obedience and lead to Your path, and grant us through it the honor of this world and the hereafter. O Allah, whatever truth You have made known to us, help us to bear it, and whatever we have fallen short of, help us to attain it. O Allah, gather through him our scattered affairs, mend through him our rift, heal through him our split, increase through him our small numbers, honor through him our humiliation, enrich through him our poor, settle through him our debts, patch through him our poverty, close through him our gaps, ease through him our difficulties, whiten through him our faces, release through him our captives, fulfill through him our requests, accomplish through him our promises, answer through him our prayers, grant us through him our desires, and let us reach through him the hopes of this world and the hereafter, and give us through him more than our desires, O Best of those who are asked and Most Generous of those who give. Heal through him our chests, remove through him the rage of our hearts, and guide us through him to the truth in which there is disagreement, by Your permission; indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path. And help us through him against Your enemy and our enemy, O God of Truth. Amen. O Allah, we complain to You about the loss of our Prophet (Your blessings be upon him and his family), the occultation of our guardian, the multitude of our enemies, the scarcity of our numbers, the severity of the trials upon us, and the turning of time against us. So send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and help us against that with a victory from You that You hasten, a distress that You remove, a victory that You strengthen, an authority of truth that You manifest, a mercy from You that covers us, and a wellness from You... that You clothe us with, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

title: Mazloomiyyat e Ali (a.s.) | Majlis#02 | Maulana Meesam Zaidi Sahab | Majaalis e Azaa e Ali (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture by Maulana Meesam Zaidi explores the historical and spiritual significance of the oppression (Mazloomiyyat) of Imam Ali (a.s.). The speaker discusses the events surrounding the attack on the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) and the forced allegiance demanded from Imam Ali (a.s.). The discourse emphasizes the Imam's patience and divine appointment as the Commander of the Faithful, while drawing parallels to the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
Today, everyone has emerged from their homes, and no one is left behind. Everyone has come out for the sake of the mourning of the Master of Martyrs (Imam Hussain (a.s.)). Some have come out for the sake of Allah, and some have come out for the sake of the mourning. Have you heard of the explosions in the mosques? Yes, I have heard. It is not a small matter; this is a message for you, that this has emerged from the hearts of those who have left their homes for the sake of Allah. It has emerged from the hearts of those who have left their homes for the sake of Allah. Tell those who are in the mourning gatherings to weep with all their hearts. Tell them to weep, for this has emerged from the hearts of those who have left their homes for the sake of Allah. Be warned, O you who are oppressed and burdened, be warned of the cries that are rising. Be warned of the cries that are rising. The Princess has left her home for the sake of Allah. And we are here, and we are here, remembering the moments of the tragedy. This is a message for those who have left their homes for the sake of Allah. And remembering Shabbir (Imam Hussain (a.s.)), they cannot restrain themselves. It is not just that, but the tragedy itself is so immense. The tragedy is so immense that even the children were affected. When the veil was removed, it was as if the Princess had left her home for the sake of Allah. When the veil was removed, the broken heart was revealed. It was as if the Princess had left her home for the sake of Allah. In the evening, when they were guests in the land of Sham... In the evening, when they were guests in the land of Sham, they were in a state of grief. When the veil was removed, it was as if the Princess had left her home for the sake of Allah. Everyone has emerged from their homes for the sake of the mourning of the Master of Martyrs. They are seeking the intercession of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and his family. We praise Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and we send blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his purified progeny. O Master, O Master of the two worlds, when the heart remembers Hussain (a.s.), it is the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) who is remembered. O Master, we seek your intercession. We seek the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.). I have read this tradition of the Prophet of Islam, in which the Prophet of Islam said that you (Ali) are the master in this world and the hereafter. Therefore, to say that the oppressed were oppressed, and to say that those who were wronged... That the Master of the Universe (Ali (a.s.)) was indeed oppressed, and injustice was certainly done to him. When the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) was attacked, and a rope was tied around his neck—such injustice was done before the eyes of the world. And the second point is that if this had happened, if the rope had been tied, then the first thing mentioned would have been this. The first thing cited would have been the fact that they tied a rope around the neck of Ali (a.s.). Some people say that they went and drew their swords, so why is this not mentioned first? It is not that it is not mentioned; it is a very big issue. I want to convey this to my children, that history does not even acknowledge that someone came and tied a rope around the neck of Ali (a.s.), or that Ali (a.s.) was taken to the open court. Rather, they claim in their books that the caliphs were chosen and the people pledged allegiance. They claim that the Prophet's place was taken, and it was announced that it was done, and all the Muslims accepted it. This is what they claim, but not everyone accepted it. Everyone subscribed, but this time subscribe in a way that points towards the opposition of the government. It is said that for one—meaning the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat)—it cannot be applied to anyone else. But others were called, and the leaders of the villages and neighborhoods were summoned. He closed the door of his house, and the people came and opened the door, and... The people came and opened the door and said to the one who arrived that there could be no greater lie than being told that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) is calling you, for the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) has made no one his successor other than me. Mawla Ali (a.s.) replied... The Messenger (s.a.w.a.) was told, and another was sent, and he was told to go to the door of Ali (a.s.) and after going there, call Ali (a.s.) and say, 'O Ali, come to the mosque, the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin) is calling you.' These words, 'The Commander of the Faithful is calling you,' were spoken. Mawla Ali (a.s.) opened the door of the house, and upon opening it, he said, 'How can it be said to me that the Commander is calling me?' He said, 'If he called you, then the one who made him the Commander is the one who...' He told those two to go and say, 'Have you forgotten so quickly? Have you forgotten so soon? I was giving this water.' The Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) took his four companions at that time, and after arriving, he told his companions to call him the Commander of the Faithful. They did so, but both of them asked the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.), 'Did Allah (s.w.t.) make you the Commander?' He replied, 'Ali is the Commander of the Faithful from that time when there was a covenant between the hearts...' Between the hearts, a covenant was made. And they ask us, 'Since when is he the Commander?' Our answer is that since Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has been the Messenger of Allah, since then Ali (a.s.) has been the Commander. And God willing, as long as Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) remains the Messenger, Ali (a.s.) will remain the Commander. So, you two have... [inaudible]... they had no other choice but to call a third person... It is said that fire was set to the door of Mawla Ali's (a.s.) house, and the burning door was pushed down. And the people who were inside were... [inaudible]... they are saying that he is at home. It will definitely be said, it will not be said otherwise. And perhaps at this time, for those who say today... [inaudible]... what does it mean to be in someone's house? Being in the house means... What does it mean to be in the house? There was no need to... [inaudible]... there was a need for... if he had intended, the enemies of Ali (a.s.) would have been annihilated. But the Master of the Universe (a.s.) demonstrated his patience here. He demonstrated patience. Mawla Ali (a.s.) reached the court, and when he arrived, Mawla (a.s.) said... [inaudible]... and he said, 'I am the one who will cast stones, I am the one who will tell you...' I am the one who will tell you. He used to describe it himself... [inaudible]... if you do this, then you will be... [inaudible]... you should listen to me, otherwise we will make you thin/weak. So that the world may understand that... [inaudible]... That Kashmir... [inaudible]... my mother, Fatima bint Asad, raised the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) just as a mother raises her son. And the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) [honored] Fatima bint Asad like a mother. Now here, my... [inaudible]... someone asked, 'Why did you accept the help?' [Laughter]... How do you accept it? Because they were older, younger, so how do you treat the illness? If they were younger, how would you treat the illness? Those who are young in age... [inaudible]... we do not do that. Just as... [inaudible]... at that time, someone martyred Mawla Ali (a.s.), and the enemies of the people... [inaudible]... they departed from this world in 40 AH, but this was not the first attempt; the effort was to incite the people who were coming... The effort was to incite the people who were coming, saying, 'Attack him.' So this culprit did not come on his own; he was not alone. He had been sent, and to help him, two... [inaudible]... the situation is that Mawla Ali (a.s.) would remain in the mosque, and he would show softness in his demeanor, and he would keep saying... The wounds were being dressed, but when you look towards the battlefield of Karbala, how they were... and it is very possible that this light was extinguished, it was set upon... The light was extinguished, tears came to his eyes... and the handkerchief is soaked in blood, and the wounds were dressed. At least Husayn (a.s.) had arrived here, and when he bandaged the wounds, Husayn (a.s.) was... He had bandaged the wounds... Husayn (a.s.) writhes in pain... at the same place from where he left for his village... on the cheeks, slaps were continuously rained down... The trees are swaying, the labor is in vain, O Muslim... like a cradle, they are swaying in the cradle... That the others are swaying in the cradle... O Muslim, for the trees, why did he say that...? O Muslim, from the trees... they say the name of Muslim... the trees... Quickly... [praise]... in the cradle, they are swaying... In the cradle, they are swaying... O Muslim, why do you take the trees...?

title: Shahaadat-e-Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) | Majlis-e-Azaa | Maulana Yusuf Ahmad Mashhadi Sahab
excerpt: This lecture by Maulana Yusuf Ahmad Mashhadi explores the profound spiritual status, virtues, and tragic martyrdom of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.). It emphasizes the importance of Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Fatimiyah as a vital practice for maintaining Shia identity and preparing for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The discourse highlights her role as the 'Uswatun Hasanah' (perfect model) and the necessity of linking Wilayah with the practice of Bara'ah (disassociation from enemies).
content:
That surely, I asked, so there is a house and an Azakhana (mourning room) is also present here. So every person has at least a small Azakhana in their house. Whether it is in the form of an Alam (standard) or a Taziya, if one builds a house, they will designate that place in their home. I recite a few verses: 'The tyranny of the beloved is not a share of the oppressors. The tyranny of the beloved is not a share of the oppressors. Every tear of mine is a share of Sayyeda (s.a.). Every tear of mine is a share of Sayyeda (s.a.).' So where the replica of the Zarih of Hussain (a.s.) is kept, that is not my house anymore, it is a part of Karbala. That is not my house anymore, it is a part of Karbala. That is not my house anymore, it is a part of Karbala. 'The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. I say Allah Allah, so Allah. The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. But He will let the mourner of the King (Hussain) pass upon seeing him.' The lovers of the Mawla are sitting here. If it is the truth, then speak up. I recite a verse: 'The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him.' We go to His house in the remembrance of God, the cry of Ali (a.s.) comes upon seeing the wall. The cry of Ali (a.s.) comes upon seeing the wall, the Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. 'Why should I tell you the price of love, O Ridwan? I will place a bid upon seeing the buyer.' The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him, the Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him, the Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. 'The mother says, may God increase your status, the mother says, may God increase your status, upon seeing me ill in the grief of Hussain (a.s.).' The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. And I recite a verse if you like it. The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. 'O preacher, perform Matam (mourning) with these hands too. O preacher, perform Matam with these hands too, it is a pity to see them useless.' The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. And in the love of Ali (a.s.), people, do not become Nusayris; Ali (a.s.) feels hatred upon seeing this love. Ali (a.s.) feels hatred upon seeing this love. The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. 'This arrow of Hurmala itself says to Hurmala, the arrow of Hurmala itself laughs at your defeat, O speechless one.' The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. Every nation says we are better than the Kalima-reciters, upon seeing the grave of the daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) demolished. The Lord will surely stop the sinner upon seeing him. Come, let me tell you the scene after the martyrdom. That surely, when my Mawla buried the Princess, my Mawla would sometimes erase the mark of the grave, then make another mark. I will recite three or four lines for the sake of reward so that I may also participate in the Hadith. You also try so that tears may flow from your eyes. Whenever we need, we remember Mawla Mushkil Kusha (the remover of difficulties) in times of difficulty. I will tell you the difficulty of Mushkil Kusha. Sitting alone, alas, at the grave of Zahra (s.a.), erasing the marks, Haider (a.s.) was saying, 'Griefs have troubled me so much while Ali was present, griefs have troubled me so much while Ali was present. Alas, Zahra died in agony, Zahra died in agony, while Ali was present.' My Mawla was carrying forward his words on the will of the Messenger of God, what difficulties Bibi Zahra (s.a.) endured. 'Griefs have troubled me so much while Ali was present. Alas, the oppressor knocked down the door and broke the ribs, alas, the hand placed on the side, broke the fingers.' Alas, the door of Batool (s.a.) was burned, the door of Batool was burned, while Ali was present. And this happened in just these four shrouds. Alas, the hair turned white and the back became bent. Alas, Zahra became weak, Zahra became weak, while Ali was present. Alas, when she spoke, her face would turn pale. Alas, when she breathed, there was pain in her chest. She spent some time like this, she spent some time like this, while Ali was present. Alas, Batool would not turn in her sleep. Alas, I saw this, she would walk with a staff. She was living even like this, she was living even like this, while Ali was present. Griefs have troubled me so much, while Ali was present. Alas, this was such a grief that I could never forget. Alas, Zahra called me and I could not come. Alas, Fizza came to help, Fizza came to help, while Ali was present. Grief has tormented us so much, even with Ali present. Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. La hawla wala quwwata illa billahil aliyyil azeem. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Creator of servants, the spreader of lands, the mover of valleys, and the one who brings about salvation. There is no beginning to His primacy, nor is there an end to His eternity. He is the First, and He has always been, and the Remaining without a limit. Foreheads bow to Him, and His unity is the cure. Blessings and peace, greetings and honor be upon the unlettered Prophet, the Meccan, the Medinan, the Qurayshi, the Hashimi, the Muttalibi. The Hijazi, the Arab, the supported Messenger, the glorified Prophet, the chosen, the most noble, Abul Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. And upon his pure, clean, infallible, oppressed, chosen, and selected family. And may the eternal and lasting curse be upon their enemies, their killers, those who usurped their rights, and those who denied their virtues, their sufferings, their bravery, their purity, their generosity, and their Wilayah. And all those who were negligent in their rights, from now until the Day of Judgment. After this, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. If goodness were a person, it would be Fatimah. Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Please recite a loud Salawat for the hastening of the reappearance of the Imam of the Age. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. Gentlemen, it is apparently one o'clock at night. And one o'clock only strikes when it has already passed twelve. But Alhamdulillah, the sanctity of the Twelve Infallibles, the Twelve Imams, and the Fourteen Infallibles in our community never strikes twelve. And this is certainly the grace of the Twelve Imams and the favor of the Fourteen Infallibles. Regardless, these are moments of great worship that you are sitting in the remembrance of the Princess of Islam. And in my view, you are performing an act of worship superior to Namaz-e-Shab at this moment. Subhan Allah. In this silence of the night, in this darkness of the night, and surely it is an honor that Allah chose us to sit on the carpet of the Princess. Otherwise, it is a fact and a clear matter that not everyone is granted the opportunity to participate in the mourning of Fatimah. You might say, 'Qibla, how can you say that not everyone is granted this opportunity?' No, this is a completely necessary and clear matter that not everyone has the right to participate in the mourning of the Lady (s.a.). You ask how? Then the will of the Lady (s.a.) is a witness to this. The Lady (s.a.) herself willed that, 'Look, so-and-so and I don't know how many such individuals, they are not allowed to come to my funeral.' 'O Ali, only those should come to my funeral who are worthy of it.' This means that the Princess herself wants that not everyone should come to my funeral. Not everyone should come to my mourning. If this sentence is rephrased, it means that this sentence of the Princess is telling us until the Day of Judgment that the Princess is leaving after deciding that only people with a Salman-like temperament have the right to participate in my mourning. Subhan Allah. Pay attention, this is a clear narration; the names are present there, 'O Ali, these individuals should not come to my funeral.' This means that the Princess is telling us before leaving that not everyone has the right to participate in our mourning. Now, if we are participating, then surely there is some good deed of someone, or some action of someone, because of which we received this opportunity. And a question that is asked very often today is, 'Sir, previously, the Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Fatimiyah (days of mourning for Fatimah) were not celebrated so well and on this scale.' It is possible that this question has come before you too, that 'Brother, in our time and in the time of our ancestors, Majlis of Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Fatimiyah were not held at this level, in this style, and on such a large scale.' So look, this is not the place to ask this question. If this question is arising in anyone's mind that 'Sir, it was not there in our time,' then why are so many Majlis being held in this time, why is the night vigil being held in the name of Janab-e-Sayyeda or in the name of the Princess, then this is not the place to ask this question, but rather a place to express gratitude. Wah wah wah wah. That Allah gave our generation the opportunity to mourn the Infallible of the World. Wah wah wah. And also listen to this, saying this sentence that 'Sir, it did not happen in our time, now I don't know what all is starting to happen,' then nothing is happening yet. Ah ha ha ha wah wah wah wah. No, pay attention, I am stating a sentence, nothing is happening yet, wait for the reappearance of the Imam. Wah wah wah. The day the offspring of Zahra (s.a.) comes from behind the veil, then who will you go to say that 'this did not happen in our time, that did not happen in our time, that did not happen in our time'? You just feel this sentence, that when he comes. Ay Haidari. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. Let us also recite one Salawat together loudly. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Please pay attention, today it is said, 'Sir, this did not happen in our time, now look, these new things are coming and in new ways.' It is coming. You haven't seen anything yet. The time is yet to be seen when the one who is to come will come and tell how the Ayyam (days) are to be celebrated. Or he will come and tell how the religion is to be practiced and what is the religion, and what is Fiqh-e-Akbar, and what is Fiqh-e-Asghar. Pay attention. So, therefore, if we call these days our good fortune, our luck, it would not be an understatement that we have been given this opportunity to recognize the truth through these days. Pay attention, and what is today, what is the benefit, sir, of these days? What is the benefit? What is the benefit? So look, the benefit of many things is not seen immediately in one moment. And it is possible that you may not even see the benefit. Brother, the greatest benefit of the universe is Imamate, which is not visible at this time but it exists. So there are many benefits that exist but you are not seeing them. So, therefore, do not even talk about this, that 'Sir, what is the benefit? What is the benefit?' People used to ask the same about Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Hussain, that 'Sir, mourning is happening in Muharram, what is its benefit?' Its benefit is that we reach the Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Fatimiyah. The benefit of Aza-e-Hussain is that we reach the Ayyam-e-Aza-e-Fatimiyah, and InshaAllah, its benefit will be that we will reach the reappearance of the Imam. Pay attention, this will surely be the blessing of these very days that we will reach the reappearance of the Imam. We will witness the reappearance of the Imam, this is truly the blessing of these very days. And what can I say at this moment in the greatness of that Princess, and what tongue can I open in the greatness of the Princess? This is truly the misfortune of people like us that when we want to recite a Majlis about the Princess or want to open our tongues, we open our tongues on such topics that are our own self-made topics. Talk is happening on the piety of the Princess, talk is happening on the hijab of the Princess, on the prayers of the Princess... Oh, learn from the Imams what the Imams have said about the Princess. We have only seen in the cluster of narrations and in the diwan of narrations that when someone asked about the Princess, the Imams were seen saying, 'Wa ma adraka ma laylatul qadr' (And what will make you know what the Night of Power is). When someone asked about the Princess, the Imam said, 'Fatamatin-nasi an qadri ma'rifatiha' (People have been kept away from the extent of her recognition). When someone asked about the Princess, he said, 'Fatamatin anish-shar, ay quti'at anish-shar' (She has been cut off from evil). Meaning, that personality is boundless, in the concept of whose name eight-eight narrations exist. You just feel, have you ever thought that there used to be one question, 'Maula, why is the name of the Lady Fatimah?' Every Imam is seen giving a new answer. You just feel, brother, when the question is one, then the answer should also have been one, but when asked to the fifth Imam, he said that people were kept helpless from her recognition, that is why Fatimah is called Fatimah. When asked to the sixth Imam, he said, 'Evil has been kept away from her.' 'Fatamatin sharra anna' (Evil has been kept away from us). Let me also say the sentence of Hazrat Ali's oratory, 'Evil has been kept away from her.' Now there is no need to look for evil here and there; whoever is away from Fatimah is the evil. What did you hear? 'Fatamatin sharra' (Evil has been kept away from her). Or when asked to the Imam, 'Maula, why is Fatimah called Fatimah?' He said, 'Fatamatin shi'ataha anin-nar' (Fatimah is called Fatimah because she will save her Shias from the Fire). Are you feeling it? Eight such narrations exist, and every person, every narrator's question to the Imam used to be, 'Maula, why is Fatimah called Fatimah?' And in response to every question, the Imam would give a new cause, a new point, a new reason, 'Why Maula, why?' I feel that the Infallibles used to wait that someone would ask about my grandmother and I would pour out the rivers of virtues. Did you pay attention? Absolutely this, Ya Ali, Ya Ali, Ya Ali. I would pour out the rivers of virtues. You just feel that when the Imams spoke about Fatimah, what did they speak? 'Limadha summiyat Zahra, Zahra, ya Ibna Rasulillah?' (Why is Zahra called Zahra, O Son of the Messenger of Allah?) Tell us, Imam of the time, why Zahra is Zahra. He said, 'Idha qamat fi mihrabiha' (Whenever the Princess would stand in her prayer niche), 'Zahara nuruha li ahlis-sama' (Her light would shine for the people of the heavens), 'Kama yazharu nurul kawakibi li ahlil-ard' (Just as the light of the stars appears for the people of the earth). Oh, you didn't feel the subtlety of the Hadith? The Imam is saying, 'Idha qamat fi mihrabiha' (Whenever the Princess would stand in her prayer niche), 'Zahara nuruha' (Her light would shine for the people of the heavens). First, you find out how far the sky is. You are not paying attention. Brother, the distance of the sky cannot be estimated by looking at a star. The star is very close, and the Imam is saying it used to shine for the people of the heavens. Brother, you see, there is the earth, above the earth is the atmosphere, above the atmosphere is the vacuum, above the vacuum is the flight, above the flight then the beginning of the celestial layers starts, then there is the first heaven, then the second heaven, then the third heaven, then the fourth heaven, then the sixth heaven, then the seventh heaven, and between these, I don't know how many lights there are; there is the light of the sun, there is the light of the moon, there is the light of the stars. Oh, what did you hear? There is the light of the sun, there is the light of the moon, there is the light of the stars, and the Maula is saying that when the Lady would stand in the prayer niche, she would shine for the people of the heavens just as a star shines for the people of the earth. Brother, we see the star because the light of the sun is not shining in the sky at that time. Pay attention. At that time, the light of the sun is not shining, and when the light of the sun shines, we do not see the stars. But the Imam is saying that the light of the Princess used to shine for the people of the heavens just as a star shines, and the people of the heavens live at that height. This means, let me say, that when Zahra came into the prayer niche and the light of Zahra started to rise, the light of Zahra started to shine, it rose so high, it started to shine so much, there was so much subtlety, so much luminosity that in front of that light, first the light of the sun faded, then the light of the moon faded, then the light of the sky faded. Reflect on this, Ya Ali, Ya Ali, Ya Ali. I mean, at whatever height the light of the Princess (s.a.) shines. Just feel this, brother; the comparison was made with the stars because the light of the stars shines for us when no other light is shining, but for them, there is no concept of night or day, because they are far above even the stars. So let me say that those in the heavens have to look towards the earth to see such radiance. No, I am saying another sentence of etiquette if you can grasp it. Just as we call our heights the 'sky', in the same way, the sky of the inhabitants of the heavens is called the house of Zahra (s.a.). Did you pay attention? In the same way, the sky of the inhabitants of the heavens is called the house of Zahra (s.a.). It was said, 'Zahra's light shines just as the light of the stars appears to the people of the earth.' It was said that this is how the Lady's light shone. Now think, what is it? How can I describe the greatness of the Lady's light? I have even seen in traditions that the people of Paradise will be sitting in Paradise one day. They will be sitting in great peace, with great contentment, and in a very tranquil manner, when suddenly a light will rise in Paradise. A light will shine. Now, the people of Paradise will start talking among themselves, 'What is this light?' Because this light is being seen in Paradise for the first time. So someone will say, 'It seems like the sun has risen today.' Then some people among them will say, 'No, did you not read the Quran in the world? The Quran said that there is no concept of the sun in Paradise.' Because, brother, the sun is a thing of this world; what is the need for the sun in Paradise? The best time in Paradise is between the dawn and the sunrise. This is present in the traditions of the Imams, that the time of Paradise is that very time. So those people say that there is no concept of the sun in Paradise. Then some people will say—listen, I want to say a sentence of etiquette—then some people will say, 'It seems God has manifested.' I don't know why, when I often see traditions regarding Janabe Sayyeda (s.a.), I don't know why people have doubts about divinity regarding the light of Sayyeda. Brother, reflect. I am talking about two or three traditions. You, MashaAllah, are all familiar with traditions. Read the tradition of Janabe Adam (a.s.); this was the first time Adam (a.s.) saw the light of Fatima (s.a.), and he said, 'Jibraeel, is this not God?' And when the angels themselves saw the light of Zahra (s.a.) on the back of the earth, on the heavens, they started thinking, 'Could this be God?' They were repeatedly told, 'This is not God, this is not God, this is not God.' Now I understand why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Lawla Aliyyun lam yakun li-Fatimata kufwun'—if Ali (a.s.) were not there, there would be no equal to Fatima (s.a.). In this matter too, Zahra (s.a.) appeared equal to Ali (a.s.). What did you hear? In this matter too, Zahra (s.a.) appeared equal to Ali (a.s.). The only difference seen was that the people of the earth were seen calling Ali (a.s.) God, and the people of the heavens were seen calling Zahra (s.a.) God. Did you reflect on this? May you remain safe. Ya Ali, Ya Ali. It was repeatedly explained, 'No, no, this is not God, no, no, this is not God.' So, as soon as the people of Paradise say, 'Has God manifested?', then the voice of Jibraeel will rise, 'Do not be worried, this is not the light of God.' It was asked, 'Then whose light is it?' It was said, 'Actually, in Paradise, Ali (a.s.) has made a joke with his wife Zahra (s.a.).' He has made a joke, and in return for that joke, Zahra (s.a.) has smiled. What are you hearing? And by Zahra (s.a.) smiling, Zahra's two teeth have become visible. This is the light of those two teeth that is illuminating the entire Paradise. Hay hay hay. Perhaps you have not reflected on this tradition; perhaps you are not reaching the subtlety of this tradition. Qibla, this is not about the world. This is about Paradise. Well, tell me, how luminous is Paradise itself? Brother, 'Khuliqa min noor-il-Hussein'—Paradise was created from the light of Hussein (a.s.). This is also a tradition; what can I do? You should state the saying of the Masoom (a.s.) himself, 'Khuliqa min noor-il-Hussein'—Paradise was created from a part of the light of Hussein (a.s.). So, obviously, Paradise must also be luminous. Now let me say that which covers the light of the entire Paradise is called the light of Fatima (s.a.). That before which the light of Paradise appears dim is called the light of Fatima (s.a.). Well, one more thing was learned: when the Princess (s.a.) smiles, the atmosphere becomes luminous. Brother, are you reflecting or not? When the Princess (s.a.) smiles, the atmosphere becomes luminous. Now I am remembering a sentence of the 'Khateeb-e-Inqilab' (Orator of Revolution); I am reciting it in his name. He used to say that when the Princess (s.a.) smiles, the atmosphere becomes luminous. Now do you understand why the atmosphere becomes so luminous on the 9th of Rabi-ul-Awwal? When the Princess (s.a.) smiles. Recite Salawat on the being of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. Did you pay attention? This is the light of Fatima (s.a.). Whenever the Imam (a.s.) was asked about Sayyeda (s.a.), the Imam (a.s.) kept flowing rivers of traditions. Subhan Allah. Strike the hands of Fatima (s.a.).' That cursed one drew his scabbard. Allahu Akbar. He drew his scabbard and started striking the arms of the Princess (s.a.). That cursed one kept striking the arms of the Princess (s.a.) continuously with his scabbard. But in the defense of the Imamate, the Princess (s.a.) did not let go of that waist belt. In the end, that belt broke, a piece came into her hand. People took Ali (a.s.) away, Zahra (s.a.) kept weeping. 'Leave Abul Hasan (a.s.), leave Ali (a.s.).' Here the ribs are broken, there the arm is wounded. That is why Master Hasan (a.s.) used to see that my mother is sitting at night groaning. Leaning against the wall. 'O Mother, can't you sleep? O Mother, don't you sleep?' She would say, 'Son, how can I sleep? On one side the arm is wounded, on the other side the ribs are broken. If I turn this way, it hurts; if I turn that way, it hurts.' O son, Fatima (s.a.) is spending her life sitting. She is reciting the rosary with one hand. Allahumma Ajjil Waliyyikal Faraj. Allahumma Ajjil Waliyyikal Faraj. Allahumma Ajjil Waliyyikal Faraj. Allahummal'an qatili Fatimatuz-Zahra. Allahummal'an qatili Fatimatuz-Zahra Salamullah Alayha. Allahummal'an qatili Fatimatuz-Zahra. Matam-e-Sayyeda.
