title: SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ 2025 | 14-Dec-2025 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture, presented as the fifth annual Shahzaadi-e-Kaunain Grand Quiz, explores the profound divine knowledge and spiritual virtues of Janabe Fatima (s.a.). The session delves into the etymological significance of her names, her status as a repository of divine wisdom, and the historical and theological importance of the Ahlulbayt. Participants are encouraged to study and propagate these teachings, emphasizing that the pursuit of knowledge is a path to spiritual enlightenment and divine favor.
content:
Presenting the third [segment]. Who can understand the greatness of the Princess (s.a.)? [music] I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon the Master of the Era, reach us and help us. How can your perfections be described, O Fatima (s.a.)? Your blessings are beyond count, O Fatima (s.a.). The bride is the beloved of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), the groom is the beloved of God, your wedding procession ascended to the heavens, O Fatima (s.a.). How can I call those beggars rich who consumed your gardens, O Fatima (s.a.)? It is not possible for me to say 'Radi Allah' (May Allah be pleased with them) to those against whom you have been complaining, O Fatima (s.a.). They pray with their faces turned, yet they turn their faces away from you, those who do not send Salawat upon Fatima (s.a.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. On behalf of the TSR team, we present congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of Janabe Fatima (s.a.), and to all of you... We welcome you to the Shahzadi Konain Grand Quiz. Let us offer our congratulations on this auspicious occasion in the presence of the Masumeen (a.s.) and in the presence of Ummul Momineen Janabe Khadija (s.a.) through a Salawat. Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum. Before we begin our discussion, let us look at the rules of this quiz, which are on your screen. A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. The rules for the Shahzadi Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz: The quiz link is now live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just need to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize, which is that all answers must be correct. Among all those who have provided correct answers to all questions, the winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, and they will be awarded these prizes. Respected viewers, as you all know, this is the fifth edition of the Shahzadi Konain Grand Quiz. Let us take a look at what we have discussed about Janabe Fatima (s.a.) in the previous editions. In the first edition, we discussed the topic of Tasbih-e-Zahra (s.a.). In the second edition, we discussed Janabe Fatima's (s.a.) pleasure and anger, her status in the hereafter, and how her intercession will be attained. In the third edition, we discussed the nature of Hazrat Fatima's (s.a.) light in this world and people's astonishment at her light. In the fourth edition, which took place last year, we discussed the luminous creation of Janabe Fatima (s.a.) and the angels seeking to serve her from Allah. And this year, which is the fifth edition of the Shahzadi Konain (s.a.) Grand Quiz, we have brought an interesting topic for you titled 'Knowledge and Virtue of Janabe Fatima (s.a.)'. Respected viewers, our sixth Imam, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) (Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum), states: 'Li-Fatimata (s.a.) tis'atu asma'in indallah'. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) states that Janabe Fatima (s.a.) has nine names near Allah, and those nine names are: Fatima, Siddiqa, Mubaraka, Tahira, Zakia, Radhia, Mardhia, Muhaddatha, and Zahra (s.a.). Today, we will discuss the knowledge of that Lady whose father is the City of Knowledge and whose husband is the Gate to that City of Knowledge. So, what would be the status of that Lady's knowledge herself? With us are our brothers, Janab Ali Abbas Sahab and Janab Abbas Nahid Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. So, respected viewers, let us begin this discussion with Ali Abbas Bhai. Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, wa sallallahu ala ka ya waliyyal asr. Yes, Qamar Abbas Bhai, when we generally talk about an ordinary human being, the first thing that comes to mind is their name. Now, if the first thing for the recognition of an ordinary human is their name, then we are talking about that luminous personality who is the reason for the creation of the universe. So, let us begin our discussion with this special name of Shahzadi Fatima Zahra (s.a.), 'Fatima (s.a.)'. Traditions clarify that her name, Fatima (s.a.), is a divine command and is connected to knowledge. Here, Imam Baqir (a.s.) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) named his daughter Fatima (s.a.) by the command of Allah, and then the Lord of the Worlds stated: 'Inni fatamtuki bil-ilm' (Indeed, I have separated/distinguished you from others through knowledge). Then Imam Baqir (a.s.) further said: 'Wallahi laqad fatamaha billahi bil-ilm fil-misaq' (By Allah, she was indeed made independent/distinguished through knowledge in the realm of the Covenant). So, indeed Ali Bhai, the one whose daughter is 'Alima Ghayr Mu'allama' (learned without being taught), if Allah keeps her independent of people through knowledge, then there is no reason to be surprised. Qamar Abbas Bhai, Ali Abbas Bhai just used the word 'Fatama' and mentioned it. And if we want to understand this Hadith better, we need to pay a little more attention to this word 'Fatama'. And here, I would like to take the support of the statement of that servant of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) who spent his entire life in the propagation of the sciences of the Ahlulbayt. I am referring to Allama Muhammad Baqir Majlisi (R.A.), who compiled his encyclopedia, that is, the collection 'Bihar al-Anwar', and in the first two volumes, he compiled this encyclopedia or collection, containing 93,000 traditions and Hadith from the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And here, it is important to pay attention to the fact that those Muhaddithin (traditionists) and Fuqaha (jurists) who spend their entire lives trying to understand the traditions of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.), are blessed by the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) with such special favors that through them, they become aware of the sciences of the sayings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). They also understand their hints. Therefore, here we will take support from the statement of Allama Majlisi (R.A.) which is present in the context of this Hadith. Allama Majlisi has stated several points in the context of this Hadith, out of which we will pay attention to two important points, Insha'Allah. The first point is what Allama Majlisi says: this sentence 'Fatamtuki bil-ilm' (I have made you self-sufficient through knowledge). This sentence has several depths that Allama Majlisi explains here, and he says 'Fatamtuki bil-ilm'—now if we look at its literal meaning, 'I have separated you through knowledge'. And in its explanation, Allama Majlisi states: 'Qala jahla sababa bil-ilm' (I have removed ignorance from you due to knowledge). So, Abbas Bhai, does this mean that the light of knowledge was such that there was no room for the darkness of ignorance? Indeed, indeed. And Allama Majlisi (R.A.) further states that not only was she learned from the beginning of creation, but Allah made her such that she would remove ignorance from people. That is, her creation was so pure and clean. Alhamdulillah, Abbas Bhai, so truly, the Lady who possesses divine knowledge, it is impossible that she would not know what the laws of inheritance are that Allah has determined. And the personality who possesses divine knowledge, will people come and teach her whether she will get the inheritance or not? So, Ali Abbas Bhai, tell us, many virtuous women have passed in history. So, was this knowledge specific to Janabe Fatima (s.a.), or did Allah grant this virtue to other virtuous women who have passed? Yes, Qamar Abbas Bhai, Allah has blessed past women with many bounties. But when it comes to knowledge, it is specifically attributed to Shahzadi Zahra (s.a.). Let us see what Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says in the traditions. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states in a long tradition that Allah has attributed 10 virtues to 10 women: Repentance to Janabe Hawwa, who is the wife of Janabe Adam (a.s.); Beauty and grace to Janabe Sarah who is the wife of Ibrahim (a.s.); Honor and respect to Janabe Asiya, who is the wife of Pharaoh; Wisdom to Zulekha, who is the wife of Yusuf (a.s.); Intellect to Bilqis, who was a queen and the wife of Sulaiman (a.s.); Patience to Barkhana, who is the mother of Janabe Musa (a.s.); Purity to Maryam (a.s.), who is the mother of Janabe Isa (a.s.); Pleasure to Ummul Momineen Janabe Khadija (s.a.) (Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa Ajjil Farajahum); and Knowledge to 'Li-Fatimata zawjatil-Murtada (a.s.)' (Knowledge is attributed only and only to Janabe Fatima Zahra, who is the wife of Ali al-Murtada (a.s.)). Subhan Allah, Ali Bhai, Subhan Allah. Masha'Allah. So, viewers, we have seen that the knowledge which is specifically attributed to Janabe Fatima (s.a.), and on the other hand, we also see that Janabe Fatima's (s.a.) husband is Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) (Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad). So, is it now correct to say that the knowledge of Janabe Fatima (s.a.) and Janabe Amirul Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) is at the same level? Is it equal? Indeed, traditions confirm this equality and the depth of knowledge. And if we look at the interpretation of the verses of the Holy Quran itself, this matter is quite clear. For example, in Surah Rahman, the Lord of Might states: 'Marajal-bahrayni yaltaqiyan' (He released the two seas, meeting side by side). Explaining this, Sadiq-e-Ale-Muhammad, Hazrat Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.), states: 'Aliyyun wa Fatimatu bahraynil-ilm' (Ali and Fatima are the two deep seas of knowledge). They are two deep seas of knowledge. And he further says: 'Yakhruju minhuma al-lu'lu'u wal-marjan' (From them emerge pearls and coral). Who are the pearls and coral? Hasanain (a.s.), that is, Imam Hasan and Imam Hussain (a.s.). And here, it is also necessary that we understand what the knowledge of Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) is called. Only then will we understand that if Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is equal to his knowledge, then to what extent is Janabe Zahra's (s.a.) knowledge? Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) is the personality who claimed 'Saluni' (Ask me). And Maula-e-Kainat himself, while describing his knowledge, says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) taught me a thousand doors. How many doors? A thousand doors. And these doors were related to what? Related to the forbidden and the lawful. Whatever is, and whatever will be lawful and forbidden until the Day of Judgment. And you say that from each of these doors, a thousand more doors open. That is, the Messenger of Allah taught a thousand doors, and from each door, a thousand more open. That is, how many total doors are we talking about? We are talking about a million doors here. And Maula-e-Kainat says that I have known—that is, I have attained the knowledge of 'Ilm-e-Manaya' (the knowledge of death). That is, who will die when. The knowledge of that is with Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.). 'Ilm-e-Balaya' (the knowledge of trials) has come—that is, how and when Allah will test whom, Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) is aware of this. And 'Faslul-Khitab' (the decisive word) for him—that is, the word... Ultimately, it is about them. This is the excellence of the knowledge of the Master of the Universe (a.s.), Abbas Bhai—the knowledge of death, the knowledge of calamities, knowing things before they happen. Yes, so this is the knowledge of the Unseen (Ilm-e-Ghayb), right? Indeed. So, did Allah bestow this knowledge upon Lady Fatima (s.a.w.a.)? Indeed, this knowledge was also bestowed upon Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.). Yes. And if we look for this, the mention of it is present in the traditions. But we will take the help of one incident here. A very interesting incident, InshaAllah, we will try to prove our point with its help. If you look at the incident, before entering it, one important thing is necessary to state for the viewers: this entire incident is 'Maslahi' (for the sake of education). We call it 'Maslahi', meaning where the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) had knowledge of all things, but for the sake of those to whom this news is reaching—for their education and training—the Family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) stated those things. Yes, and especially the incident that is about to be mentioned, the thing that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) taught us is: what is the meaning of showing reverence to Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.)? How should one show reverence to the Princess of the Two Worlds (s.a.w.a.)? Meaning, what right does she have over us? So, two important things are emerging here. Meaning, the knowledge of the Unseen of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and the reverence of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.)—both these things are obtained from this incident. Who is the narrator of this incident? Salman-e-Mohammadi (may Allah have mercy on him). From whom does he narrate? From Ammar (r.a.). And what kind of incident? As we said, it is very interesting. What kind of incident? 'Ajayib' (wondrous). Meaning, Ammar himself says to Salman, 'Ubbika Ajaba'—I will tell you a strange thing. And saying this, Ammar narrates the whole incident. What is this incident? He says that I saw the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) go to the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.). Yes. Then Ammar also went there and says that when Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) saw the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), she called out to him. She said, 'Come near me so that I may tell you everything that has happened'—meaning 'bima kana'—'and what is going to happen'—meaning 'bima yakun'—'and what will not have happened until the Day of Judgment.' SubhanAllah. Meaning, until the Day of Judgment is established. This sentence proves the knowledge of the Unseen of the Princess (s.a.w.a.). And after this, if you look, Ammar narrates that when the Princess of the Two Worlds (s.a.w.a.) had stated these things to the Master of the Universe (a.s.), I saw the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) coming out walking backwards. See, there is a very important point here for all of us. Meaning, as we said, how is the reverence of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) to be shown? We learn that. The Master of the Universe (a.s.) is not turning his back to Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.), but is coming out walking backwards. SubhanAllah. And Ammar says that then I also came out with him. Ammar also adopted the same method, came out the same way. Until, he says, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) reached the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). So when the Messenger of Allah saw the Master of the Faithful (a.s.), he said, 'Come near.' So the Master went to the Messenger of Allah, sat down, became a companion, and sat in the gathering of the Messenger of Allah. Now, when the Master of the Universe (a.s.) sat down, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to him, 'O Ali, will you tell, or should I tell?' This is a proof of the Messenger of Allah's (s.a.w.a.) knowledge of the Unseen. Indeed. So he says, 'Will you tell, or should I tell?' Now, how should the reverence of the Messenger of Allah be shown? The Master of the Universe is teaching this. Yes. So what does he say? 'O Messenger of Allah, it is better if it is stated by you.' Yes, this was the etiquette. So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'It is as if I am seeing you, that you went to the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and she said this and this to you, and you came back out.' Yes. So when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated this, the Master of the Universe—as we said this incident is 'Maslahi'—what were the Master's words after this? 'Nooru Fatimata Nooruna'—the light of Fatima is from our light. So the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked the Commander of the Faithful, 'Awala ta'lam?'—Do you not have knowledge of this? This is the same 'Maslahi' sentence. The Master of the Universe had the knowledge, but who is being taught here? Whose training is being done? The one to whom this news reaches, their training is being done. Therefore, it was necessary to state this. Then the Master of the Universe (a.s.) performed a prostration of gratitude. And Ammar says that after this—meaning after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—the Master of the Universe (a.s.) went back to the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.). Meaning he came out from there and then went to the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.). Then he went into the house of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.). So Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) said to him—this sentence that Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) is about to say, from that again the knowledge of the Unseen of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) is known. She says, 'It is as if you were in the presence of my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and whatever I told you, you told him.' In response, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) said, 'Indeed, O Fatima (s.a.w.a.), it is so.' Lady Zahra said to the Master of the Universe (a.s.) at that time, 'O Abul Hasan (a.s.), know that Allah Almighty created my light.' Understand the greatness of the creation of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.). The Princess (s.a.w.a.) says that Allah Almighty created my light, and it kept glorifying Allah Jalla Jalaluhu. SubhanAllah. SubhanAllah. Then Allah Almighty placed this light in a tree of Paradise, and that tree became illuminated. When the light of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) settled in it, that tree of Paradise became illuminated. When my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), came to Paradise—Allah's peace and blessings—when he went to Paradise, Allah inspired him. At that time, what did Allah command him? That you pluck the fruit of that tree and consume it. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did exactly that. Then Allah Almighty placed my light in the blessed loins of my father. SubhanAllah. And then transferred it into the womb of my mother, Lady Khadija (s.a.w.a.). SubhanAllah. And then my arrival into the world took place. Meaning, Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) is mentioning the greatness and purity of her light. She further says, 'And I am from that same light. I know what has happened, what is going to happen, and what will not happen until the Day of Judgment.' SubhanAllah. Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) has knowledge of all these things. And in the end, she says, 'O Abul Hasan, the believer sees with the light of Allah.' This incident tells us many things: that Allah bestowed the knowledge of the Unseen upon all the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). How should their reverence be shown? And along with this, what is the greatness of the light of Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) that was created? We saw a glimpse of it in this brief tradition. So, respected viewers, you see that when a believer sees with the light of Allah, what will be the status and rank of that being by believing in whom people become believers? SubhanAllah. So, respected viewers, now it is time for a break, and at the time of the break, the summary of the discussion so far will be shown on your screens. So, InshaAllah, we will meet after the break. So, respected viewers, in this grand quiz, once again we welcome you, and let us take this discussion forward. The miracles and excellences that Allah Almighty bestowed upon Lady Fatima (s.a.w.a.) and the other Imams (a.s.), people should have valued them, understood their status and rank. But what did people do? People envied them. Allah Almighty says in the Holy Quran, 'Am yahsudunan-nasa 'ala ma atahumullahu min fadlih'—Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? Yes, exactly. And this is what happened in history. From the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), the opponents of the Imams (a.s.) envied them. And we find this in history, even in the house of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), there were individuals who used to envy the excellences and virtues of the Princess (s.a.w.a.). We find this incident that Lady Zahra (s.a.w.a.) was cooking food for Hasanain (a.s.), and the pot was on the fire, and the Princess (s.a.w.a.) was stirring it with her blessed fingers. And this incident was seen by a woman living in the house of the Messenger. Okay, and as soon as she saw that, she got scared and went to her father. And when she went to her father and narrated this incident, her father said to that woman, his daughter, 'O my daughter, keep this incident hidden. Indeed, this is a great deed.' Then when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) heard the incident, the Messenger of Allah came to the pulpit, and after praising and glorifying Allah, he said, 'I swear by the Being who sent me as a Messenger and chose me for Prophethood, Allah has made the fire forbidden upon Fatima (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, the fire of Hell is forbidden upon her descendants and her Shias. Indeed, in her descendants are those who will be accompanied by the fire, the sun, the moon, the stars, and the mountains. SubhanAllah. And they will perform Jihad with their swords, and the Prophets (a.s.) will fulfill their covenants. And Abbas Bhai, the earth will hand over all its treasures to them, and the blessings of the sky will descend upon them. May failure be upon the person who doubts the excellences of Fatima (s.a.w.a.). Indeed, may Allah curse the one who bears enmity towards her husband and does not accept the Imamate of her sons.' Abbas Bhai, here I want to draw attention to one thing. Allah is cursing those people who do not accept the Imamate of her sons—meaning the Princess's sons. Meaning, whoever in today's era denies the Imamate, Wilayat, and Occultation of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), the curse of Allah is upon that person. Indeed, indeed. Here, the use of the word 'Al-Wail' points to the fact that the fire of Hell is mandatory for such a person. And on the Day of Judgment, Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and her Shias will have unique and special positions and ranks. When the Princess (s.a.w.a.) is called, she will come. When she intercedes, her intercession will be accepted, even if it is unpleasant to someone. SubhanAllah, Ali Abbas Bhai, MashaAllah. Respected viewers, I would like to add one thing here: usually, what does a person get angry about, get annoyed about, or fight about? If we look at what is the foundation of a fight, what is the root of a fight, then in reality, we will know that the root of a fight is ignorance. The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), says, 'An-nasu a'da'u ma jahilu'—People are enemies of what they do not know. So, respected viewers, now To not accept, meaning in this current era, whoever denies the Imamate, Wilayah, and the Occultation (Ghaybah) of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), the curse of Allah is upon that person. Indeed, indeed, the use of the word 'al-wayl' here indicates that the fire of Hell is mandatory for such a person. And on the Day of Judgment, there are unique and special stations and ranks for Princess Fatima Zahra (s.a.) and her Shia. When the Princess (s.a.) is called, she will arrive. When she intercedes, her intercession will be accepted, even if it is displeasing to some. Subhan Allah, Ali Abbas brother, Mashallah. Respected viewers, I would like to add one point here: usually, what makes a person angry, upset, or leads to a quarrel? If we look at what the foundation of a quarrel is, what the root of a conflict is, then in reality, we will find that the root of the quarrel is ignorance. Yes, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)—Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad—states: 'An-nasu a'da'u ma jahalu' (People are enemies of what they do not know). So, respected viewers, now... When we realized that when we do not know something, we become its enemy. Then, when people did not understand the Wilayah, the knowledge, and the status of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), Janabe Fatimah (s.a.), and the other Imams (a.s.), they became their enemies. So, respected viewers, just as we mentioned at the beginning of our program, the knowledge of Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) was divine. Yes, and through that knowledge, Allah kept Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) independent of all creation. So, Abbas Nad Bhai, tell us, was this knowledge that Allah bestowed limited to Janabe Fatimah (s.a.), or did people also benefit from this knowledge? Indeed, Abbas Bhai, you have brought our attention to a very profound point. The personality of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is not only one that was kept far from ignorance, but it is the personality through whom Allah kept people far from ignorance. And we find many such narrations and hadiths here, using an incident from the Tafsir of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) as a reference. To clarify this for the viewers, it is found that one day a woman came to the presence of Janabe Siddiqa Tahira Fatimatuz Zahra (s.a.). Why did she come? Because her mother had some questions regarding prayer. So, she appeared in the service of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and said, 'My mother is very old, and she had some questions. So, she requested me to present these questions to you and bring back the answers.' Upon saying this, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) told her, 'Ask the question.' So, that woman presented the first question. Janabe Zahra (s.a.) answered it. That is, she removed her from ignorance. She removed her ignorance. After that, the woman presented the second question. She answered that too. The third, the fourth, until that woman asked Janabe Zahra (s.a.) 10 questions one after another, and Janabe Zahra (s.a.) answered all the questions. And you see, the interesting thing we find in this incident—which we usually hear in narrations and incidents that are often narrated—is that people went to the service of the Imams (a.s.) or the service of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). What is special about this incident is that here, The woman asking the questions is coming directly to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) to ask. So, this incident is, in that respect, a unique incident in itself. A rare incident. And let us see what happens in this incident. That is, when Janabe Zahra (s.a.) answers 10 questions, the woman herself starts feeling embarrassed that I have asked Janabe Zahra (s.a.) 10 questions. At that time, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) encouraged her; she did not discourage her, but rather encouraged her, saying, 'No, ask whatever questions you want to ask, do not feel embarrassed.' The woman began to say, 'No, I do not want to trouble you.' Janabe Zahra (s.a.) asked, 'No, there is no such thing.' And then, the example that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) gives her shows us the importance of answering people's questions under the shadow of the knowledge of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.). Because the source, the actual origin of all knowledge, is the Ale Muhammad (a.s.). And the center, the source, the origin of the knowledge of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) is Allah. Anyway, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) asks her, 'If a person is told to carry a heavy load to the roof, and in return, he will be given 100,000 dinars,' Then would he have any trouble carrying that load to the roof? So, that woman replied, 'No, he would carry it; he would have no trouble.' Now, listen to what Janabe Zahra (s.a.) says. Janabe Zahra (s.a.) says, 'I will be given a reward for every answer that is greater than if pearls were to fill the space from the earth to the Arsh.' That is, for every question—if pearls were to fill the space from the earth to the Arsh—Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is saying that a reward and recompense greater than that would be given for each question. So, we should understand the importance of this duty. And Janabe Zahra (s.a.) says, 'Then why would I have any trouble with this?' That is, when my Lord has kept so much reward for me. After this, the stage to which this narration is drawing our attention is the importance of scholars in the era, and the status and position that Allah (s.w.t.) has bestowed upon them. Who is stating this? Janabe Siddiqa Tahira (s.a.) herself. What does she state? 'I heard from my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.),' That when our Shia scholars are gathered—that is, when they are questioned, when they are assembled on the Day of Resurrection—they will be gathered. When they are assembled on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will drape them in luminous garments of honor in proportion to their knowledge and their hard work and struggle in guiding the servants of Allah. Luminous garments of honor will be bestowed upon them. So much so that one scholar will be dressed in 1 million such luminous garments. 1 million such luminous garments will be worn. And a caller will proclaim at that time, 'O you who took care of the orphans of Ale Muhammad!' You see with what honor Allah is bestowing upon them. With what respect and reverence they are being called in the gathering. 'O you who took care of the orphans of Ale Muhammad, these are your students.' Just now, the talk was about those teachers. The students they trained, whom they gave knowledge—the talk was about those students—that these are your students, those orphans whom You taught the knowledge of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) while they were far from their Imams (a.s.). Now, just as you gave them knowledge in the world, in the same way, dress them in luminous garments.' At that time, the scholar will dress his students in these luminous garments based on the knowledge they acquired. So much so that some of these students will be dressed in 100,000 garments. 100,000 garments. Similarly, the students will also dress their own students in garments. That is, this chain will continue. Then Allah (s.w.t.) will command that now these scholars who took care of the orphans of Ale Muhammad (a.s.) should be dressed in luminous garments again so that their reward is completed, or rather, increased. So, you saw how the cycle turned and reached the teachers again, and this chain will continue in this way until what was given to the earlier scholars is completed, and its reward is also increased. And in this way, this chain will continue to the students of the students. Well, the talk is about garments. A garment is made of threads. Now, understand the virtue of that thread. Janabe Zahra (s.a.) draws our attention to that as well. She says, 'O servant of Allah, one thread of these luminous garments is 10 million times better than all the things upon which the sun rises.' That is, wherever the sun's light falls, on everything—that is, it is 10 million times better than the entire universe—is one thread from which this garment is made. Because Janabe Zahra (s.a.) also states the reason for this: because everything in the world has deficiency, and hardship is involved in it. That is, this incident draws our attention to many points. The first important point to which this incident draws our attention is that here, questions are being asked to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and she is answering. That is, she is removing people from ignorance. She is removing people's ignorance. Secondly, things about the knowledge of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) draw our attention to the fact that her knowledge was bestowed by Allah. And besides this, this incident also draws our attention to the virtue of answering people's questions in the light of the knowledge of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) And it encourages our youth. Look, where Allah (s.w.t.) has blessed the scholars, He told the scholars, 'You bless your students,' and told the students, 'You bless your students,' and this chain continued. That is, this should create a passion in us that we spend our entire lives in 'Ihya Amr Ahlulbayt (a.s.)'—that is, in the promotion of the sayings and hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), in teaching, in spreading their teachings. Acquire the teachings of the Imams (a.s.) and strive to see how it can be conveyed to other Shias in a better way and with full responsibility. And if we look, this is also our duty. Look, where Allah (s.w.t.) commands the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that you are a reminder—that is, you keep reminding people—in the same way, the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) have also entrusted us with an important responsibility. What is it? That you make people aware of the Beauty of our speech. Because the Imam says that if people become aware of the beauty of our speech, they will automatically start following us. So, it is important for us now that we first acquire the correct knowledge of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) ourselves. Strive for it, and after acquiring the correct knowledge, convey it to the people so that people become familiar with the knowledge of the Ale Muhammad (a.s.) and follow them. This is our responsibility. So, respected viewers, what did we state in this program? Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) is the center of knowledge. Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) is equal to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in knowledge. Janabe Fatimah (s.a.) removes ignorance. We are very grateful to our brothers who, in the light of verses and narrations, stated the status and position of Janabe Fatimah (s.a.). So, respected viewers, let us conclude this program. And if you have not yet Submitted the answers to this quiz, then as soon as this timer running on your screen ends, the quiz link will be closed. So, submit your answers quickly. Let us move towards the Ziyarat, and immediately after the Ziyarat, today's lucky winners will be selected through our computerized lucky draw system. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad. Ziyarat of Fatimatuz Zahra (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad... Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Beloved of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Friend of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Chosen One of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Safi of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Amin of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the best of the Prophets of Allah and His Messengers and His angels. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the best of creation. Peace be upon you, O mistress of the women of the first and the last. Peace be upon you, O mistress of the women of the worlds and the last of the Messengers. Peace be upon you, O mother of Hasan and Husayn, the masters of the youth of Paradise. Peace be upon you, O truthful one, the martyr. Peace be upon you, O oppressed one. Peace be upon you, O the one whose right was usurped. Peace be upon you, O the one who was oppressed. Peace be upon you, O the one who was martyred. Peace be upon you, O Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, and may the mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you. I bear witness that you were upon a clear proof from your Lord, and whoever pleases you has pleased the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Whoever hurts you has hurt the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and whoever shows enmity towards you has shown enmity towards the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and whoever connects with you has connected with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and whoever cuts ties with you has cut ties with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). And you are a part of him and his soul which is between his two sides. I call Allah as a witness, and His angels as witnesses, that I am a friend to those who befriend you and an enemy to those who show enmity towards you. May Allah bless Muhammad and his pure progeny. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you. Peace be upon you all, dear viewers, and the mercy of Allah. First of all, once again, we offer our congratulations on the occasion of the birth of the Princess of the Two Worlds, Lady Zahra (s.a.). Now the time has arrived that you all have been waiting for—the announcement of the lucky draw winners of the Princess of the Two Worlds Grand Quiz 2025. But before announcing the names of the winners, we are grateful to all of you who participated in this quiz and encouraged us. So now, let us proceed to the announcement of the lucky draw winners of today's Grand Quiz, which is being conducted through our computerized lucky draw system. title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#16 - Imam Ali (a.s.) Ne Qiyaam Kyun Nahin Kiya?
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and theological reasons behind Imam Ali's (a.s.) decision to remain patient rather than rising against the political leadership of his time. It clarifies that his restraint was not due to a lack of courage, but rather strict adherence to the Prophet Muhammad's (s.a.w.a.) specific instructions regarding the necessity of having sufficient loyal supporters. The discussion emphasizes that the Imam actively sought aid from the Muhajireen and Ansar, and his actions were guided by divine wisdom and the preservation of the faith.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May the blessings of Allah be upon you. Peace be upon you all, and the mercy of Allah. This is another episode of the 'Jawab' series regarding Lady Zahra (s.a.). We hope you are all well. Now, the time has come to seek the blessings of Lady Zahra (s.a.) and pray that Allah removes all our difficulties and keeps us safe from all calamities and diseases. Let us proceed with this episode. Today's question is one that is often raised by opponents: Why did the Imam, whose Imamate and Wilayat were announced by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) from Ghadir to the end, not rise up for his right immediately after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Why did he not rise up? The one whose bravery is discussed more in the heavens than on earth, the one for whom Allah Almighty sent down Zulfiqar from the heavens, the one who defeated the enemies of Islam in battles like Badr, Khaybar, and Khandaq—why did the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), not draw his sword for his right? This is the question. To answer this, we have with us our brother, Janab... [Name]. As you have heard the question, we want you to explain through history and verses what the answer should be. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. First of all, a million thanks to Allah who gave us the opportunity to love those whom He Himself loves. Thanks to the Almighty who commanded us to hate those whom... Thanks to the Almighty who commanded us to hate those whom we have always been taught to view through the lens of the Infallibles. Our path is either the Quran or the commands of Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his successors. Why should we look elsewhere when we have the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.)? Let us go to the Commander of the Faithful himself to seek the answer to this objection. Why did you not rise up? I would like to quickly mention a Hadith... I would like to quickly mention a Hadith in which the Imam (a.s.) explained why he did not rise up against the opponents after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). A person came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and asked, 'O Ali, if you had called the people, they would have been ready.' The person was implying that it was a shortcoming on the Imam's part. The Imam (a.s.) stood up and said, 'I did call you to Jihad, but you were not ready.' He then said, 'I advised you, but you did not accept it.' He then said... You believe here that the skin... I am asking, I gave you an invitation, but you and your people did not listen to my words, and then it does not happen. After that, we present these situations, the situations of that era, one after another, what situations kept arising. And after that, when the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) is giving the sermon, a person was also present there. He asks the Commander of the Faithful in a sarcastic tone, 'What stopped you, O Ali, from drawing your sword?' He is asking the Commander of the Faithful this question in a sarcastic tone. We stop here, and if we say in the context, he says, 'O son of so-and-so, you have asked a question, so listen to its answer too.' Then we believe here, and what does he say? 'It was not cowardice that stopped me from drawing my sword.' Then he further says, 'Nor was I feeling any fear in meeting my Lord,' meaning I was not afraid of martyrdom. Here he wants to show his bravery. Why would my alarm start fearing death? Is it not the greatest proof in people's minds that when my Master was seen sleeping with peace on his deathbed? Is this not proof that the Commander of the Faithful was not afraid of death? Is it not true that the Commander of the Faithful was not afraid of death? Then, has the world forgotten how my Master used to crush the opponents and how he used to mix them into the dust like a stormy wind that displaces things? Has the world forgotten that when my Master waved his sword in the air, no man remained to put a shroud on the corpses of the widows of the enemies? The incidents of the bravery or the virtues of the Commander of the Faithful are endless, which cannot be described here. Now, after that, the Imam (a.s.) attacked there, which is why it is asked why you did not take action. At that time, what was the reason you did not take action? He says, 'But I was stopped by the command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.),' the command of Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) stopped me. Then he further says, 'And he had taken a promise from me.' The Messenger had taken a promise, so not coming here was not a matter of cowardice. And we will give an example of this if you have an example before you, and after this, if you want, in this, the Messenger... After this, if you want, in this, the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) gave the reason, because the Messenger of Allah is now beginning to tell why the Messenger of Allah said, 'If you find helpers (Ansar), then you do Jihad, but if you do not find helpers, then do not do Jihad.' Now the Messenger wants to tell that if people come to help you, then you do Jihad. Further, he says, 'And if you do not find helpers, then what to do? Then you save your hand and save your life.' And until you find helpers, you should hold onto the Book of Allah and the Sunnah. Here, the Messenger of Allah wants to say that if you find helpers, then you should do it, but if you do not find helpers, then do not do this work. The world saw that through this tradition... The world saw that through this tradition, it is understood that the reason for not taking action by Ali (a.s.) is that the promise he made to the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) was that if you find helpers, if you find supporters, then you should do Jihad, otherwise do not. And the Imam did exactly that. So here, this example is found that just as Ali (a.s.) followed the command of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) in that place, despite his bravery and being a warrior, the world knows that his bravery is such that even if he did not have a single helper or a single companion, he could still defeat the entire universe alone. He has the support of Allah; Allah has given him everything. There is no example of his bravery, but what is seen here is that in the same way, just as we see the commands of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) in the life of the Imam, we should also follow the commands of our time. We should follow the hadiths, traditions, and instructions that we receive from the Imams (a.s.) regarding what we should do and what we should not do. We should follow them exactly. We should not think about what our benefit or loss will be. And after that, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.)... The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) pointed to one thing: what mountains of oppression would be broken upon me? And after that, he tried to bring you here, just as it is in our books, rather it is impossible, it is also found in their books, such as Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Ibn Majah, Musnad Ahmad bin Hanbal. This hadith is found in these books too, and the words are slightly different, such as 'O Ali, you are to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me.' This hadith was stated by the Messenger of Allah, and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) quoted this hadith himself and then said that the Messenger also stated that Musa (a.s.) had given this advice to Harun (a.s.). What advice? 'O Harun, if you find helpers, if you find supporters, then you should stand up, but O Harun, if you do not find helpers, then you should remain patient.' He wanted to say here that just as Janab Harun (a.s.) remained patient, in the same way, I did not take action, rather I also remained patient. So, if you look at the history, there is a striking similarity between Janab Harun (a.s.) and Ali (a.s.). It is not that the Imam (a.s.) did not go to the people... He did not go to the people for kingship. The Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) went to the people so that people could not say, 'If Ali had come to us, we would have helped Ali.' So the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) did not go alone, but took the princes, the sons of the Prophet, Hasan and Husayn (a.s.), and knocked on the doors of the Muhajireen, the doors of the people of Badr, the doors of the people of Medina. And you reminded them of the oath of Ghadir, that the Messenger of Allah had chosen you, that 'Whoever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.' You did not help me in my house. And this is a one-day incident; for three consecutive days, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) kept going to people's doors, and people kept promising the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) that 'O Ali, we will come.' And the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) said, 'Come in the morning with your heads shaved.' So, look at the situation of all three days; on all three days, hardly three or four people came to help the Imam (a.s.). It is absolutely clear that the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) needed supporters, needed Ansar, through whom he could work. And he himself had promised, and the advice of the Messenger was that 'Do not take action until you have supporters.' And Allah... in the narrations of the Imam (a.s.), it is mentioned that 'All people turned back except three,' that all people died... All people died except three. The names of those three are also mentioned in that tradition, that except for those three people, all the people who were present in the Ummah, all of them became apostates. And in the traditions, this is found that the people remained with only faith, while all the rest of the people of Medina, all the people of Islam who were in that era, all of them became apostates. After this, the Imam (a.s.) again mentioned his bravery and said, 'O son of so-and-so, did you find me weak on the day of the battle?' Then after that, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) also mentioned Siffin, that we sent 50,000 people to Hell there, and then said, 'How did you find me there? Did you not find me brave?' Then he did not just mention Siffin, but the Imam (a.s.) also asked about Nahrawan, 'Did you find me weak in Nahrawan?' And repeatedly in the sermon, the Imam (a.s.) kept saying that if only I had found people, found helpers, then surely I would have done this work. Look here, what sentences the Imam (a.s.) said about his bravery... Look at what sentences the Imam (a.s.) said about his bravery. The Imam (a.s.) says that on that day, there was no one among the companions of Ali (a.s.) whose face was not shining, and everyone's face was shining, so they were happy. And their hearts were happy. All the people sitting there, when the Imam (a.s.) was describing the bravery, all his followers were happy, but the reason is why he did not take action. Now look, this is the first tradition before you, and in the same way, there is a second tradition, which is famous by the name of 'Khutbah al-Wasiyyah,' and this is not any small book; it is present in our very great book 'Al-Kafi,' which was written by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), who was the teacher of Sheikh Saduq (r.a.). In this sermon, if you look, the Imam (a.s.) has explained why he did not take action. And the Imam (a.s.) says, swearing by God, 'I swear by God, if I had as many people as Talut had, or as many people as the people of Badr had, then I would have surely raised my sword against you and would have made you submit.' The Imam (a.s.) comes out of the mosque and goes towards an open land where 30 people are present in the crowd, and the Imam (a.s.) sees... And the Imam (a.s.) sees with big eyes and says, 'If only I had found even this many people who were obedient to Allah and His Messenger, then surely my sword would have...' So here, if you look at both traditions, the Imam (a.s.) is presenting the reason for people not coming and not helping. The half-finished things we have seen so far prove that Ali (a.s.) did not take action only because he did not have helpers, supporters, or Ansar present. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had told him that until you have these Ansar, until you have these with you, do not take action and remain patient. And the Imam did exactly that. He said exactly what the Messenger said. And I would like to say one thing: it is not understood from the books or arguments of Ali (a.s.) that Ali (a.s.) is the result of patience, and whether people believe it or not, it does not matter, but it is our belief that his patience is such that until we die and until our last breath, we will... Until our last breath, we will keep showing the path of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). What a beautiful thing the poet said, 'Where the tongue-cutters live, in that era, the one who cuts the tongue, may the poem of the Master reach there.' So this is our prayer that may the Almighty soon grant us the day when the sole heir of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), in the era of the Master, and the one who will save the followers of Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) from the darkness until the Day of Judgment, and when he appears, Allah will manifest His power and might through him, and he will come as the wrath of Allah, and he will take revenge for the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), Janab Zahra (s.a.), and their children. Thank you very much, sir, that you explained to our viewers in a very easy answer and in an easy way why Ali (a.s.) did not take action. We are sure and we hope that this answer must have reached our viewers, and in the end, we would like to say that when we cannot fully understand the actions of a human being with our limited intellect, then how is it possible that the... If we find it, how is it possible that we can fully understand the actions and points of an infallible Imam, who is the companion of the Infallible? Therefore, to say why the Imam (a.s.) did this or why he did not do that is not a correct way to approach the situation. Rather, trying to prove the words and actions of an infallible Imam as right or wrong based on our own intellect is nothing but our own limited reasoning. I would also like to say that the enemy constantly tries to create doubts about the Imamate, Wilayah, and the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.) in the hearts of the Shias through such objections, and tries to place a question mark. In the end, we pray to Allah (s.w.t.) that the Wilayah of the Imam (a.s.) remains in our hearts as long as we breathe. As long as we are alive, let us keep saying 'Ya Ali, Ya Ali', and when we depart from this world, whether we have anything in our travel provisions or not, may the love of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his Progeny (a.s.) definitely be with us.
Imam Ali's (a.s.) restraint was a strategic decision based on the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) direct command.
The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) instructed the Imam to only initiate action if he possessed a sufficient number of loyal supporters.
Imam Ali (a.s.) drew a parallel between his situation and that of Prophet Harun (a.s.), who was also commanded to exercise patience without support.
The Imam personally sought support from the companions for three days, but the lack of response prevented him from taking military action.
Doubts regarding the Imam's actions often stem from limited human understanding and are sometimes used to undermine the concept of Wilayah.
The Imam's historical military record in battles like Siffin and Nahrawan serves as definitive proof of his unmatched bravery and leadership.

chapters.title: Why Imam Ali (a.s.) Did Not Rise
chapters.summary: The lecture addresses the common objection regarding why Imam Ali (a.s.) did not immediately claim his right to leadership after the Prophet's passing.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Command and Promise
chapters.summary: Imam Ali (a.s.) explains that his restraint was not due to cowardice or fear of death, but adherence to the Prophet's specific instructions and a binding promise.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Supporters
chapters.summary: The Imam clarifies that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded him to act only if he found sufficient helpers, drawing a parallel to the patience of Prophet Harun (a.s.).

chapters.title: The Imam's Efforts to Seek Support
chapters.summary: Imam Ali (a.s.) recounts his efforts to remind the people of the Ghadir oath, noting that despite his attempts, he lacked the necessary support to act.

chapters.title: Reasons for Imam Ali's Patience
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that Imam Ali (a.s.) refrained from military action due to a lack of loyal supporters, citing traditions from Al-Kafi.

chapters.title: The Role of Faith and Infallibility
chapters.summary: The discussion emphasizes that human intellect is insufficient to judge the actions of an infallible Imam, warning against doubts sown by enemies.

excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm, emphasizing the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the cornerstone of faith. It highlights the historical courage of scholars like Shaykh al-Mufid in defending these beliefs and underscores the necessity of both Wilayah and Tabarra for a complete spiritual life. The session concludes with the announcement of the 'Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi' Mega Quiz winner, who was awarded a Ziyarat tour of Iraq.

The hadith of the white morning, we all are darkness, the hadith of the guidance of Subhan-e-Rabbi-al-A'la, the hadith of the gift of the light of God, without a prophet, the hadith of the eternal and beautiful memory, the hadith of the guidance of La ilaha illallah, the hadith of the imprint of the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.), in our chests, the hadith of a living testimony, a pure reality, the hadith of the lamp of God for all the lost ones. The presence of the master of 'Lawlak', the loud call, that whoever, my prophet is, Ali (a.s.) is the master, since I am for everyone, without soul and without 'la ya', Ali (a.s.) is enough for me, more than the soul and better than him, Ali, Ali, and Ali is the world and Ali is the world, Ali, Ali, and Ali is the guardian and Ali is the exalted, Ali is the Hajj and Ali is the Kaaba and Ali is the Zamzam, Ali is Safa and Ali is Marwa and Ali is the place of effort, Ali is the Adhan and Iqamah, Ali is the Ruku and Sujud, Ali is the Qiyam and the distance and Ali is the greeting and prayer, Ali is the Sirat and Ali is the Mahshar and Ali is the Mizan, Ali is Paradise and Ali is Kawthar and Ali is Tuba, Ali, according to the saying of the Prophet, is the door to the city of knowledge, from the door, the one who is the path of error, always error, like the door of Khaybar, the successor of the Messenger, not the one who fled from Jihad, where is the truth, someone who said 'Saluni' (ask me) is the Imamate, not someone who, due to his own ignorance, says, someone who is the successor of the Prophet in the place of the Prophet, not the one who asks for his own life, someone who breaks on the shoulder of the Prophet, for the sake of preserving the Caliphate from everyone, my witness to the Caliphate is the very existence of Ali (a.s.), that the sun is a witness to the confirmation of the sun, that the sun is a witness to the confirmation of the sun.
