And may Allah send blessings upon you, O Wali of the Age, help us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and dear viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu, Ya Ali Madad. Ghadir, the divine covenant, the mega quiz, bringing this special episode, we are present in your service, and we welcome you all to this episode. Dear viewers, today's episode is special because in today's episode of our Ghadir, the divine covenant, mega quiz, the mega winner will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. But viewers, before this announcement, a short speech will be presented before you, which you have to listen to, and immediately after that speech, our mega-winner will be announced. This speech will be delivered by the respected Dr. Shabib Rizvi Sahab. So come, viewers, let us begin this episode with these four lines: 'He filled the heart with new enthusiasm and smiled, he filled the heart with new enthusiasm and smiled, what a miracle it was to say Ya Ali Madad, there is no difficulty that has no solution, there is no difficulty that has no solution, if one says it from the heart, Ya Ali Madad.' So come, viewers, before you, the respected Dr. Shabib Rizvi Sahab. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hassan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his supporters, his Shia, his servants, and his followers, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his purified family. Furthermore, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has said in His glorious Book, and His word is the truth and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, and Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.' Khuda-e-Muta'al (God Almighty) is stating in the Holy Quran: 'O Messenger, balligh (convey), you convey that which has been revealed to you from your Lord.' Whatever has been revealed, convey it. 'And if you do not do this, then you have not conveyed His message.' As if you have not performed any task of the Risalat (Prophethood). 'And Allah will protect you from the people.' Allah will save you from the people. 'Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.' Indeed, Allah never guides those who choose disbelief. This is verse number 67 of Surah Al-Ma'idah, a very famous and well-known verse, which was revealed on the occasion of Ghadir-e-Khumm, when Allah commanded the Prophet to convey this message—the message of the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). There is another similar verse, which is verse number 39 of Surah Al-Ahzab, verse number 39, in which the truth is stated: 'Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and do not fear anyone except Allah, and sufficient is Allah as an Accountant.' Those who convey the messages of Allah, who convey the Risalat of Allah, and they fear Him, and they do not fear anyone else, they do not fear anyone, and sufficient is Allah as an Accountant, Allah is sufficient for all accounting. So you noticed, if you look at these two verses, what becomes clear is that the message of Ghadir, the message of Wilayah, is a message that we must convey to the people, and we must convey it with boldness, without any fear. The first thing is, if you have pondered over the verse, that Allah has taken the guarantee that Allah will protect him; no one can harm him, and even if something happens, His religion will remain protected. Even if the world goes away, His religion will remain protected with Wilayah. It will never, ever be harmed; His religion will not be harmed. He does not fear anyone except Allah; he only fears the Being of Truth. And these are the masters of Irfan (gnosis) who possess the knowledge of Ghadir, about whom the Quran says: 'Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.' Only the Ulama, meaning the Urfa (gnostics), meaning the masters of Irfan who possess the knowledge of Ghadir, who possess the knowledge of Wilayah. Of course, the first instance of this is Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.) himself, as is found in the traditions, that this refers to Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.). So, whoever moves forward with the message of Ghadir should never, ever, in any way, be afraid. Allah is with him, the Messenger of Allah is with him, and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are with him. When all these personalities are with him, these individuals are with him, then what is there to fear? Then what is the fear? And that is why we see that the Imams (a.s.) whenever they found an opportunity, they spoke of Ghadir, they conveyed the message of Ghadir, because it was the Prophet's command. In the sermon of Ghadir, the Prophet said, 'Let those who are present convey it to those who are absent.' It is obligatory upon whoever is present here to convey this message of Ghadir to those who are absent, who are not present here. And here, one more thing is very important to say, and this is a very significant point. Usually, people are a bit negligent about this, and that is that there should be no discrimination of religion or sect in this message of Wilayah; there is no discrimination of school of thought. This message should be conveyed to everyone, it should be conveyed to everyone that we have a Wali, we have a Mawla, we have a Wali who is called Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and then there are 11 Imams from his progeny, because this belief is a natural belief that is in accordance with the nature of every human being. People will automatically be attracted to it, they will be attracted to this belief, they will be attracted to the Imam. So our Imams (a.s.) continuously tried to keep conveying this message. A similar sermon-like hadith is from Imam Reza (a.s.), which we present to you, that a sermon of Imam Reza (a.s.)—the sermon is very long, but we present only a few brief sentences of that sermon to you, to show how the Imams (a.s.) used to convey it. The Imam gave this sermon, the eighth Imam gave this sermon on the day of Ghadir. And remember, keep this in mind, in what circumstances did the Imam give this sermon? You yourself know better in what circumstances the Imam was surrounded, and giving this sermon in those circumstances is no less than a miracle or a great achievement. It is a very great task. The Imam gave this sermon, and let us tell you about the authenticity of this sermon so that no one can point a finger at it, wondering where it is coming from. This sermon is by Janab-e-Sayyid Ibn Tawus, who was a very great Marja-e-Taqlid of the seventh century, a very great, a personality of great stature. Books have been written about him, Sayyid Ibn Tawus, who passed away in 664 Hijri, Janab-e-Sayyid Radi al-Din Ibn Tawus. So his book 'Iqbal al-A'mal', 'Iqbal al-A'mal' is the book that we usually refer to for supplications and deeds, and we keep studying it, and Sheikh Abbas-e-Qummi (r.a.) himself used it in 'Mafatih al-Jinan'. Now, just listen to a few sentences from this sermon, then Insha'Allah we will benefit from these sentences. Imam Reza (a.s.) says: 'When the Day of Judgment comes, four days will be led to Allah like a bride,' or 'Four days will be led to Allah like a bride is led to her husband's house.' Just as a bride is led, in that way, these four days will be led on the Day of Judgment. Meaning, just as angels lead a bride, in that way, the angels will lead them with great care, and with great glorification and praise. And which are these days? The narrator asked, 'What are these days?' He said, 'Eid al-Adha is one, Eid al-Fitr is two, the day of Friday is three, and the day of Ghadir is four.' And then the Imam says, 'Indeed, the day of Ghadir among Adha, Fitr, and Friday is like the moon among the stars.' The day of Ghadir will be like the moon among the stars, shining. 'And it is the day when Ibrahim the Friend (Khalil) was saved from the fire.' This was the day when Ibrahim was saved from the fire. And on that day, he fasted; Hazrat Ibrahim fasted on that day to express gratitude to Allah. 'And it is the day when Allah perfected the religion through the establishment of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) of Ali as the Commander of the Faithful and a sign.' This is the day, this is the day when Allah perfected His religion. How? That through the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he made Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) a sign and a guide for the people. 'And He made his virtue clear.' This sentence is very important. 'Abana' means He made it completely clear. He made the virtue of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) completely clear. Now after Ghadir, no one can say that this one is first, that one is second, or third and fourth. That debate cannot happen. Now either you accept or you reject, either you believe or you do not believe, either you bring this Islam or you choose disbelief, either you become a believer or you become a hypocrite. Now only two options remain, nothing else. 'And He made his virtue clear,' He clearly stated who is superior and who is inferior. Yes, when a veil falls on the intellect, then a person writes in his book: 'All praise is due to Allah who gave preference to the inferior over the superior.' Who gave preference to the inferior, meaning an inferior person over a superior one. This does not make sense to the intellect, how? I mean, the example is quite clear: there are two children in a class, two children got good ranks, one first rank and one second rank. For example. So you give the first prize to the second-rank holder and the second prize to the first-rank holder. Don't say, 'Oh, that is Allah's praise, all praise to Allah, Allah did it.' Allah did not do it, you did it. So do not blame Allah, do not put the crown of your actions on Allah. You say we performed this task. 'And his vicegerency'—the announcement of the vicegerency of Amir al-Mu'minin was made on this day. 'And it is truly the day of perfection.' This is the day of perfection. 'And the day of the humiliation of Satan.' This is the day when Satan's nose was rubbed in the dust. You know that rubbing the nose can also be an idiom. It is true, it is an idiom, some people say, 'No, this is an idiom.' Yes, it can be an idiom, okay. An idiom, meaning what does rubbing the nose mean? To be humiliated, to be disgraced. So now, if you want to identify who is on the side of the Merciful and who is on the side of Satan, then look at who celebrates on the day of Ghadir and whose faces are downcast. So whoever celebrates is on the side of the Merciful, and whose faces are downcast, understand that they are on the side of Satan. 'Whoever fits the hat,' now whoever it is, it is upon him. 'And the day when the deeds of the Shia are accepted.' This is the day when the deeds of the Shia are accepted. 'And the lovers of the family of Muhammad,' and all those who are lovers of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), their deeds are accepted. 'And it is the day when Allah perfected the religion.' And this is the day when those who are anti-Ghadir, who are the opponents, the Imam says, 'What the opponents did, Allah will make it scattered dust on the Day of Judgment.' Allah will give their deeds into their hands on the Day of Judgment, and this day of Ghadir is the day of judgment. Ghadir is the standard, Ghadir is the foundation, Ghadir is the balance, Ghadir is the proof. Whoever is on this side, his deeds are accepted; whoever is on that side, they will become the proof of that verse of the Quran. The Quran says: 'And We will turn to what they have done of deeds and make them scattered dust.' And then what will we do? That whatever deeds they have performed, we will blow them away like dust. In their hands. All those deeds will come and they will see that everything has flown away. They are of no use, of no value, nothing at all. And this day, this is the day of Ghadir. The day when Jibra'il (Gabriel) will give the command. That a chair of Allah's honor (Kursi-e-Karamat) be installed and placed. It should be placed in front of the Bayt al-Ma'mur in the fourth heaven. Just as the Kaaba is in this world, there is a Bayt al-Ma'mur in the fourth heaven. It should be placed in front of it, opposite to it, and after that, Jibra'il will ascend. Jibra'il will preside over this chair of honor. That is, Hazrat Jibra'il (a.s.) will be seated on the chair. And the angels from all the heavens will gather around Jibra'il. Just imagine the scene, the celebration, the joy, the happiness. Everyone from all the heavens will gather, and they will all be doing one thing, and what will that be? They will be sending blessings upon Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his family. They will all be praising the Messenger of Allah. And after praising the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), what will they do? They will seek forgiveness for the Shia of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), the Imams (a.s.), and their lovers from the progeny of Adam. From the progeny of Adam until the Seal of Prophets, and in fact until the Day of Judgment, all the Shia—those who are the Shia of Ali (a.s.) and the Shia of the Imams (a.s.) after Ali—the angels will seek forgiveness for them. And remember that angels are those whose prayers are answered. Their prayers are never rejected. It is one thing for us to seek forgiveness, and another for the angels to seek it. We do not know if our prayers will be accepted or not, but the prayers of the angels will certainly be accepted because they are infallible (ma'sum) and therefore their prayers are answered. And then it is stated: 'And the example of the believers in their acceptance of the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) on the day of Ghadir Khumm.' Those who accept the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) on the day of Ghadir Khumm, the example of those believers is like the example of the angels in their prostration. It is like those angels who prostrated before Adam. They prostrated before Adam when Allah commanded them. 'Wa id qulna' (And when We said) - these are the opening verses of Surah Al-Baqarah. 'Wa id qulna lil-mala'ikatisjudu li-Adama fasajadu' (And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated), so they all prostrated except Iblis. Except for Iblis. So here the Imam says that whoever accepts the Wilayah of Ali, his example will be like those angels who prostrated before Adam, and whoever does not accept the Wilayah of Ali, his example is like the example of Iblis. The sermon is very long, and there is no time. It requires not one but many such lectures for that, and for its explanation, this was just a brief hint towards the sermon so that people may refer to it and benefit from it as much as possible and tell their children. So, this Ghadir, this message of Ghadir, requires courage to convey. This is not the work of cowards. This is not the work of those who get nervous. Those who get scared in a little situation, in a little problem, thinking 'what will happen?' and get afraid. This is not the work of cowards. Being a Ghadiri is the work of the brave. And from the beginning of Islam until today, whoever has carried the Wilayah of Ali, they definitely possessed this quality: they were brave and never feared anything. Today, I am presenting to you an example of such a scholar, a truly magnificent personality. A very famous personality in history. Someone in whose heart there was no such thing as fear. And that was Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nu'man al-Ukbari, known as Shaykh al-Mufid (r.a.). He was famous by the name Shaykh al-Mufid. He was a scholar of the fourth century. He passed away in 413 AH. A great scholar, highly educated, and for his excellence and virtue, it is enough to say that he was the teacher of great scholars like Sayyid al-Murtada and Shaykh al-Ta'ifa, i.e., Shaykh al-Tusi. He was a student of a traditionist like Shaykh al-Saduq. He was his student. A great personality, Shaykh al-Mufid. Today, I present to you an incident: why was he called 'Mufid'? There are two different narrations for this. I will present one famous narration to you, and who has recorded this narration? The late Qadi Nurullah Shushtari. The late Qadi Nurullah Shushtari—though in Persian they say 'Shushtari', the pronunciation is 'Shushtari'. In Arabic, they say 'Tustari', in Urdu, they say 'Shushtari'. Qadi Nurullah Shushtari, you know, the famous personality known as Shahid-e-Salis (the third martyr). He wrote the book 'Majalis al-Mu'minin'. In it, he recorded this incident, and it is worth noting. It is a very interesting incident. Especially for the youth, this is a direct address; listen to this incident carefully. Look, this is what courage and bravery are. First, understand the background. What was the background? Shaykh al-Mufid was from Ukbara. Ukbara was a suburb of Baghdad. A suburb. Not Baghdad proper, but one of its suburbs. In all of Baghdad, the total Shia population was only 1%. And the opponents were dominant. Naturally, where the population is only 1%, what would the situation be? They would live in fear, they would be suppressed. But this is not the case with Shaykh al-Mufid. Shaykh al-Mufid lived with great courage and regularly held debates. So much so that even the great scholars of the opponents were afraid to debate Shaykh al-Mufid. And as you know, the immediate accusation leveled against him was that he possessed 'magic of speech', that he had the magic of rhetoric, so do not talk to him. He will convince you. This has been going on since that time. So, regarding Shaykh al-Mufid, Dr. Wahid Akhtar, a very great professor at Aligarh Muslim University, wrote that seeing Shaykh al-Mufid, the great scholars would change their path. That Shaykh al-Mufid is coming from the front. Such a personality. Such a personality was Shaykh al-Mufid. So, among such opponents was a great scholar, a very famous one, Qadi Abd al-Jabbar. Qadi Abd al-Jabbar al-Mu'tazili, he wrote a book, the name of the book was 'Al-Mughni'. 'Al-Mughni'. In that era, just think, the book was written in the fourth century. In 20 volumes. And the 20th volume was entirely against the Shia, against the concept of Imamate. So, think about how much love he had. He had so much love that he wrote the entire 20th volume against the Shia. When that book came into the public eye, Shaykh al-Mufid reached his lecture circle. Look, if it were someone like us, he would think ten times, 'Oh my God, such a great scholar, how can I go, what will happen, how to do it?' And if we discussed it with friends, they would say, 'Brother, don't go, otherwise this will happen, you will get beaten up,' and all these worldly things. But Shaykh al-Mufid went there. And after arriving, people were sitting in a circle, his students, and great scholars were also present there. Naturally, Qadi Abd al-Jabbar was a great personality. A great personality. So people were sitting in a circle. Shaykh al-Mufid went there and sat at the back. He was teaching. When he finished teaching, Shaykh al-Mufid said, 'Master, if you allow, may I ask a question?' He did not recognize Shaykh al-Mufid by his face, but he had heard about him, that there is some young man among the Shia who debates very powerfully and possesses great knowledge and virtue. He had heard of him, he had heard of him. He said, 'Shaykh Mufid, may I ask you a question?' He said, 'Ask.' He said, 'This Hadith, "Man kuntu mawlahu fahadha Aliyun mawla" (Of whomsoever I am master, this Ali is his master), which the Messenger of Allah said at Ghadir Khumm, is it authentic? Is it correct? Is it right?' He said, 'Yes, yes, it is certainly correct, the Hadith is authentic, and all scholars have accepted it.' 'Second question. So, what does "Mawla" mean here?' He said, 'Mawla means Awla (most worthy). That is, the one who holds the top priority, the number one, that one. Awla.' Shaykh Mufid said, 'After that, whoever is there, will it be after him?' He said, 'Yes.' 'So this was said about Ali?' 'Yes.' 'So now this means no one can compete with Ali?' He said, 'Yes, that is correct, no one can compete with Ali.' Then he said, 'Then how did it happen in history? As you know, history is a toy for those who seek the world. History is nothing but a plaything for those who seek the world.' So Shaykh Mufid said, 'How did it happen that in history, Ali was pushed back and others were put forward?' He immediately understood that this is some Shia youth. He said, 'Son, look, it is not like that.' Naturally, the long-bearded and the poor young Shaykh Mufid... so he said, 'Son, it is not like that. The Hadith you are quoting is a narration (Riwayat). This is a narration. And what happened in history is based on deduction (Dirayat). And when there is a conflict between narration and deduction, deduction is preferred over narration. Deduction is accepted, and the narration is set aside. Therefore, what happened was correct. What happened was correct. The Hadith is also correct in its place, but accept what happened in history.' He said, 'Okay Master, if you are saying it, then it must be correct.' Then Shaykh Mufid said, 'Master, one more question.' He said, 'Ask.' He said, 'Is this Hadith authentic that the Prophet, the Noble Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), "Harbuka harbi wa silmuka silmi" (Your war is my war and your peace is my peace). Is this correct, authentic?' He said, 'Yes, absolutely correct. It is authentic.' 'Second question: Whoever fights the Prophet, does he remain within the fold of Islam or does he go outside the fold of Islam?' He said, 'Certainly, he goes outside the fold of Islam.' He said, 'So those who came to fight Ali (a.s.) in the Battle of Jamal, X, Y, Z, Z, Z. It is clear, right? So did these Muslims die, or did they die outside the fold of Islam?' He said, 'No son, it is not like that. It is found in narrations that those people repented, and they died in a state of repentance, so they died as Muslims.' He said, 'Just now you said that what happened in history is deduction, and if a narration comes in conflict with it, the narration is set aside. So here, the narration you are speaking of, let us set the narration aside and accept the deduction of what happened. This means that whoever came against Ali died outside the fold of Islam.' Now he had no answer, he became silent. He started looking at Shaykh Mufid and said, 'My book, what is your name?' Sheikh Mufid said, "Ana Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nu'man," I am Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nu'man at-Talla'ukbari. He said, 'Come here.' He called him close, sat him on his own seat, on his own chair, and said, "Anta Mufid haqqan, anta Mufid haqqan, anta Mufid haqqan" (You are truly Mufid, you are truly Mufid, you are truly Mufid). Truly you are Mufid, truly you are a scholar. As soon as he said this, the people present there, his supporters and students, began to cry out, 'What are you doing, Master? You are seating a Rafidi in your own place and saying, "Anta Mufid haqqan," you are truly Mufid, you are truly Mufid, you are truly Mufid. What are you doing?' Qadi Abdul Jabbar said, 'Silence. If anyone has an objection to my words or my actions, then Sheikh Mufid is here. If any of you have the courage, then question him.' It is written that a silence fell, everyone in the gathering became quiet, and shortly after, the gathering was dismissed. And what else? These were individuals in whom the spirit of Wilayah was so intense that no one could estimate it. Meaning, these people were drowned in the Wilayah and love of the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.); they were submerged. Apart from this, they saw nothing else; for them, the only goal and purpose of life was the support (nusrat) of the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.). There was nothing else. Read the books of Sheikh Mufid, read 'Al-Fusul al-Mukhtara'. We request the youth to read 'Al-Fusul al-Mukhtara', what an amazing book it is. It is a short book, mostly. It is in one volume. Read this book. Wilayah is a very important thing, a very significant thing. But Wilayah has a condition, and we are presenting this in your service because nowadays many people say, 'No, teach love for the Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.), love them, love.' No. Look, along with love (hubb), hatred and disgust (bughz) against evil is also necessary. I mean, is there anyone in the world who would say that we love terror or terrorists? Is there anyone who would say that? Surely everyone would say no, no. Whoever spreads terror in the world, whoever spreads panic in the world, the world hates them. The world hates them and condemns them. And if someone says, 'No, we condemn evil but we don't say anything. We consider it bad in our hearts.' Will anyone accept this? For example, if a man comes and kills an innocent person. We are giving an example, look. He kills an innocent person, snatches his belongings, and starts walking away, and we are standing there. Someone asked us, 'He killed in front of you, you didn't say anything?' We said, 'We condemned it very much in our hearts.' And when we go home, we speak very harshly against him, only in our hearts. People will say, 'What kind of person are you? You should have condemned it there, you should have condemned it in public so that the world knows that this is the terrorist who is spreading terror.' And it is necessary to take a stand against him. In Islam, in the school of Tashayyu, that is why Tabarra is obligatory, so that the world knows who we are expressing Tabarra against. The one who usurped the right of Muhammad and Aal-e-Muhammad (a.s.). The root of everything is there, and all other things have emerged from there. There is this narration, "Nahnu aslu kulli khair" (We are the root of all good), of all good. So listen to the Hadith: The Imam says, rather the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, "Ya Ali! Inna Wilayataka la tuqbalu illa bil-bara'ati min ada'ika wa ada'il-a'immati min wuldik" (O Ali! Your Wilayah will not be accepted until people express Bara'ah [disavowal] from your enemies and from the enemies of the Imams who will come from your progeny). This is a very important thing. Meaning, we have to carry both these things together. Otherwise, the Prophet says, "La tuqbal," your Wilayah will not be accepted. So if you... So whenever you have to set a standard, see if he is expressing Wilayah, is he expressing Bara'ah or not? Is he mentioning the enemies or not? Those who usurped the rights of Ali and Fatimah, is he mentioning them or not? The Prophet says it will not be accepted. Now, some people among us become so 'pious' that their piety is frightening. So pious, 'you shouldn't do all this,' and 'this is a bad thing.' Now look, I present a narration in your service which is present in Rijal al-Kashshi. The page number is 528 and the entry number in Rijal al-Kashshi is 1012. In this narration, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'Man ta'assama...' Look, it is necessary to mention in your service that this Rijal al-Kashshi book that we have today, this was also compiled by Sheikh al-Tusi. Because the Rijal al-Kashshi that was compiled by Kashshi, Janab Muhammad ibn Umar al-Kashshi, he was a Mustabsir (one who converted to the truth). He became a Shia later. After that, he wrote this book. By the name of Rijal. The name of the book was 'Ma'rifat al-Rijal'. But when the enemy cannot win, what do they do? Either they set the house on fire or they set the books on fire. This has been the habit of the enemy. They hatch conspiracies, conspiracies are hatched. Somehow, they want to suppress the truth. So Janab Kashshi's book was also burned in libraries. But anyway, whatever was available, Sheikh al-Tusi collected it. Sheikh al-Tusi (r.a.), whose title is Sheikh al-Ta'ifa, as I just mentioned in your service. Meaning the Sheikh of the Shias. Sheikh al-Tusi, and he named the book 'Ikhtiyar Ma'rifat al-Rijal'. Meaning not the complete knowledge, but a selected part of it. 'Ikhtiyar Ma'rifat al-Rijal'. From that, this is entry number 1012. It is a Hadith of the Prophet. 'Man ta'assama ayyal'ana man la'anahu Allah fa'alayhil la'natullah.' Whoever hesitates or considers it bad to send La'nat (curse) on the one whom Allah has cursed, then the one who is hesitating, the one who is afraid, the one who is not sending it, upon him is also the La'nat of Allah. Look, I told you the Hadith with the reference. Now it is up to you, whether you accept the Hadith or reject the Hadith, that is your choice. Our job is only to deliver the message. The message has been delivered, whether you accept it or not is your job. Therefore, this week, this 'Week of Wilayah' that has passed, from Ghadir to Mubahila, the seven days that we have celebrated, in this, our pledge and covenant should be very firm, very solid, that we will accept the Wilayah of Ali and along with it, we will also know the condemnation of his enemies, we will also have knowledge of them so that we can express Bara'ah from the enemies just as we express the Wilayah of Ali. This is the complete concept of Wilayah and Ghadir, which, if Allah gives us the ability, we will all act upon together and convey this message to the world that this is Ali. This is Ali. Let us end the matter. With a small, very small, brief story, just two-three lines, not more. There is a very great Islamic scholar, actually he became a scholar. He passed away just a few days ago. He was not even a Shia. He wrote 25 volumes on Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.). 25 volumes. Remember, he was not a Shia. When someone asked him that this is not even your field and you have done so much study and research. He said that I saw in a dream that Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.) is very wounded and the Prophet is supporting him. And the Prophet is saying to me, 'Do you see Ali is so wounded? Make some arrangements for his treatment.' I could not understand. I went and studied the books. As I kept studying, I saw that Ali is truly the oppressed of humanity, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). So let us try to convey this message of Ghadir and provide some relief to the wounded heart of Ali (a.s.) from our side. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. Without purifying the heart from hypocrisy, without performing Tabarra, one will not get Paradise. Respected viewers, this was Dr. Sharif Rizvi Sahab, who was enlightening our hearts through his very comprehensive and radiant speech. And as we were listening in this speech, truly Wilayah is not acceptable if there is no Tabarra. If Bara'ah is not expressed from the enemies of Ahlulbayt, and also that the importance of the message of Ghadir is what the Imams (a.s.) themselves taught us, that we should convey this message to the people. Convey this message to the whole world, and truly our episode was also a small attempt from our side to convey the message of Ghadir to the people. And the way you have supported us in this series, you were also walking in the path of Ahlulbayt in the same way. What a beautiful thing this poet says for such people, for such Momineen: 'Do not consider me humble, O seekers of lust. Do not consider me humble, O seekers of lust. If self-centeredness is not found in my temperament. Oh, I am a drop, but I am a servant of that place. I am a drop, but I am a servant of that place. Where the oceans do not get employment. I am a drop, but I am a servant of that place. Where the oceans do not get employment.' So come, respected viewers, let us start our today's special episode in which the announcement of the mega winner of our Ghadir Payam-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz is going to happen through our computerized lucky draw system. But before that, let us repeat the names of the winners who have become lucky winners in our last seven episodes. So viewers, the names of all those winners are on your screen. 'Waqalal insanu ma laha' (And man says, 'What is the matter with it?'). By the oath of the verses of the Quran, you are the one who completes the incomplete. The Quran is the word of God in praise of Ali. Every verse is reciting your name. The beauty of the Quran, the surging ocean, the scale of deeds, like the sun of faith, the gravity of the command, you are the master and the exalted, O Hazrat-e-Ainullah, you are the witness of all conditions. The path of the Quran is Haider, the condition of faith is Haider, the successor of the Prophet, the chest of the secrets, Haider. O comfort of Fatima's heart, we have made a covenant with you. Ghadir is the morning of white light amidst all darkness, Ghadir is the verse of 'Subhana Rabbi al-A'la', Ghadir is the gift of the light of God without a prophet, Ghadir is the reason for the creation of the wise and the beautiful. Ghadir is the verse of 'La ilaha illallah', Ghadir is the imprint of the Wilayat of Ali on our chests, Ghadir is a living document of a true reality, Ghadir is the guide of God for all the lost ones. Still, the call of the master of 'Lawla ka' (Had it not been for you) is loud, that whoever considers the Prophet as his master, Ali is his master. Just as I am the master of all by the soul and authority, Ali is my successor, from his soul to his soul. Ali, Ali, and Ali is the scholar and Ali is the world, Ali is the guardian and Ali is the ruler and Ali is the exalted. Ali is the Hajj and Ali is the Kaaba and Ali is the Zamzam, Ali is Safa and Ali is Marwa and Ali is the struggle. Ali is the Adhan and Iqamah, Ali is the Ruku and Sujud, Ali is the Qiyam and Qu'ud and Ali is the Salam and Dua. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may the blessings of Allah be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, the time has come for the announcement of the Mega Winner of the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz, which will be done through our computerized lucky draw system. The one who is going to receive the prize that every lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) keeps in their heart. Which is the Ziyarat of Najaf, Karbala, Kadhimiya, and Samarra, meaning the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. So viewers, let's see who is the Mega Winner of this year's Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz, who is going to receive the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. Their name is here on your screen. Zeenat Poonawala, from Mumbai. Many, many congratulations to you. You are the Mega Winner of the Ghadir Paiman-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz, who is receiving the prize of Ziyarat of Iraq. We, the PSR team, are grateful to all you viewers for encouraging us by watching the videos and participating in the quiz throughout this series. If you have any feedback, suggestions, or advice regarding this video series, please send it to our WhatsApp number [number removed], repeating again, [number removed]. If you also want to join us in spreading this message of the Wilayat of Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then subscribe to our channel, press the bell icon, and watch our upcoming videos, and do like, comment, and share. May Allah (s.w.t.) grant us all the strength to hold firmly to the Wilayat of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) until the very end. Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Teen Logon Se Dosti Na Karo | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #YouTubeShorts
excerpt: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the advice of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) regarding the selection of friends. The lecture highlights three types of individuals a Muslim should avoid befriending: those who commit open sins, the foolish, and habitual liars. The speaker emphasizes that one's social circle significantly shapes their personality and encourages maintaining a small, handpicked group of virtuous friends.
content:
The Mawla says, look at what a strange sentence this is. Mawla Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, he says, 'La yanbaghi lil-mar'il-muslimi an yuwakhi al-fajira wal-ahmaqa wal-kadhdhab' (It does not befit a Muslim person to befriend three types of people). One who is a sinner, committing sins openly, stay away from him. Two, the fool (ahmaq). A fool is someone who wants to benefit you but ends up causing you harm. There are many arguments for this, for which there is no time right now. And third, one who lies. If you find out once that this person lies a lot, stay away from him. Bad friends who take you away from your goal, maintain distance from them. Always keep your friends handpicked, always. Keep them few but keep them good. There should be handpicked friends. All these things mold a person's personality.
A Muslim should be selective about their friendships.
Avoid befriending those who commit sins openly.
Avoid the 'fool' who intends to help but causes harm.
Stay away from habitual liars.
Friends have a profound impact on an individual's personality.
It is better to have a few handpicked, good friends than many acquaintances.
Social circles should be curated to align with one's goals.
