title: Majlis 3 | Haqeeqi Tauheed Kya Hai? | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | Muharram 1444
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound concept of 'Haqeeqi Tauheed' (True Monotheism) as the essential foundation of faith, emphasizing the necessity of seeking knowledge from the Ahlulbayt. The speaker discusses the intellectual and spiritual requirements for understanding Allah, warning against anthropomorphic concepts and mental illusions. The discourse bridges these theological insights with the historical tragedies of Karbala, specifically focusing on the martyrdom of Ali Akbar as a testament to absolute reliance on the Creator.
content:
Ask Sajjad about the going of Kulsum and the noble ladies to Syria. Ask Sajjad about the going of the bare-headed mothers and sisters to the court. Ask Sajjad about how the noble ladies used to hide behind each other out of modesty, and the pointing of swords at those ladies. Ask Sajjad about the scene in the court where everyone, small and large, was sitting, and the Sadat were standing, and the head being placed on the tray and shown to Zainab. Ask Sajjad about when the daughter of Shabbir passed away in the prison, it was a time of calamity, and lifting that small corpse with bound hands. Ask Sajjad about the one rope around the necks of twelve captives, everyone was standing silently, and the arrival of Zainab and Kulsum bound in ropes. Ask Sajjad about when Sajjad used to see the hair of Sakina, he would cry out, 'Alas, alas', and ask him about the marks of the rope on that small neck. And when the Sayyid Sajjad fell to the ground, and the Day of Judgment was enacted, ask Sajjad about lifting them with the tip of the spear. Ask Sajjad about the going of the bare-headed mothers and sisters to the court. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Master and the best Helper. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and the end is for those who have piety and certainty, and blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, our beloved of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Blessings be upon his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, the Imam of our time, our guardian, and our master. O our master, our beloved, our healer, our companion, the one who guides the confused, the helper of the distressed, may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be sacrificed for him. To proceed: Our master and leader, Ja'far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (a.s.) said: 'He lies who claims that he knows us while holding onto the handle of others.' Our master and leader Ja'far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) spoke the truth. Salawat. He asked the Imam, 'From whom should we take the teachings of our religion?' The Imam replied, 'The one who has spent his life in our traditions, whose beard has turned white in the field of Hadith.' Now, if you go to someone who cannot even read an Arabic text correctly, then obviously, what will he do? What will he teach? What will he read? Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an adahum. A sentence came to my mind; there was a very great scholar, Sayyid Murtaza Naw-Nahri (may Allah have mercy on him). He was very great; he passed away about 125 years ago. You must have seen the Dua-e-Mashlool, right? How many pages is Dua-e-Mashlool in Mafatih? It would be at most three or four pages, not more than that. He wrote an explanation and commentary on Dua-e-Mashlool in 850 pages. 850 pages, and he wrote it in Arabic. An Indian Maulana wrote its commentary in Arabic, and he spent 34 pages discussing just the word 'Allah'. What are the various meanings of the word 'Allah'? 34 pages. When he finishes the book, he writes at the end, saying he wants to share something with a heavy heart. He says, we are also speaking, right? That is his pain. You can read it; we have it, we even have a copy of it. He says that today's era is so chaotic that a person who cannot even read an Arabic text, let alone write it—this is what he says, he wrote it—let alone writing, someone who cannot even read an Arabic text, the title 'Shamsul Ulama' (Sun of the Scholars) is written before their name. He wrote this, we are not saying it. No one is accusing us, brother. He wrote it, we are just quoting it. So, just recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. So, the point was that whenever you want to pass a comment on any topic or present your perspective, first go and read all the Hadith on that topic. See what the family of Muhammad (a.s.) has said. Now, in that same connection, I present one more Hadith, two more Hadith for your service, and then if time permits, I will narrate a third Hadith related to it. Yes, look, the first Hadith is narrated from Amali-e-Saduq. In Amali-e-Saduq, this tradition exists that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said to Muhammad ibn Muslim. Now, do you know who Muhammad ibn Muslim was? Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi (may Allah be pleased with him) was such a companion of the Imam that the Imam gave him 30,000 Hadith and said, 'Muhammad, this is only for you, do not tell anyone.' Just imagine what his level must have been. So, this is one Hadith that the Imam said to Muhammad: 'Man hafiza min shi'atina arba'ina hadithan ba'athahu Allahu azza wa jalla yawmal qiyamati 'aliman faqihan wa lam yu'adhdhibhu.' If any of our Shias memorizes 40 Hadith, Allah (Azza wa Jalla) will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment as a scholar and a jurist (Faqih) and will not subject him to punishment. 40 Hadith, if he memorizes them. This is one tradition, you have heard it, Alhamdulillah, and understood it, Alhamdulillah. Now listen to the second Hadith. The second Hadith is from Khisal-e-Saduq, this is also a book by Sheikh Saduq, Al-Khisal. The specialty of this book is that Sheikh Saduq has collected all the Hadith that contain a number. Look at how our scholars were, MashaAllah. So, in it, he narrates a Hadith from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.)—Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wa ahlik a'da'ahum—said: 'Man hafiza min ummati arba'ina hadithan minas sunnati.' Whoever from my Ummah memorizes 40 Hadith from the Sunnah, if he memorizes them, 'Kuntu lahu shafi'an yawmal qiyamati.' On the Day of Judgment, I will be his intercessor, I will intercede for him. So, these are two Hadith. Now, let's take a small break here. What is called a 'rider' in legal language. That someone like an ignorant person like us, he memorized 40 small Hadith, like 'As-salatu amudud din, in qubilat qubila ma siwaha wa in ruddat rudda ma siwaha' (Prayer is the pillar of religion; if it is accepted, everything else is accepted, and if it is rejected, everything else is rejected). One, or rather, he doesn't even consider this a bad thing, and he says, 'Now I have become a Faqih, an Alim, now Allah will not punish me,' and he is roaming around happily. When does this happen? When we are 'Neem Hakim' (half-baked scholars). That is why it is said that on any topic, read all the Hadith, then make a decision. Now look, the Hadith I am going to present for your service, see what that Hadith is. This Hadith is also in Khisal-e-Saduq, and it says that Imam Hussain (a.s.) said that the Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) made a will to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.): 'Ya Ali! Man hafiza min ummati arba'ina hadithan, yatlubu bizalika wajhallah.' O Ali! If someone from my Ummah memorizes 40 Hadith, the first condition is here: 'Yatlubu bizalika wajhallah.' His intention is only for the sake of Allah. It is for the pleasure of Allah and nothing else. It is not to show off to the world, not for hypocrisy, not to earn money. 'Yatlubu wajhallah' and what is the second condition? 'Wa daral akhirah' and he seeks the hereafter. 'Hasharahullahu yawmal qiyamah.' Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment. With whom? 'Ma'an nabiyyina was siddiqina wash shuhada'i was salihin wa hasuna ula'ika rafiqa.' This is verse number 69 of Surah An-Nisa that the Prophet is quoting in this Hadith. This means, what does he say here? If someone memorizes them, Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment with whom? With the Prophets, the Truthful (Siddiqin), the Martyrs (Shuhada), and the Righteous (Salihin), and what an excellent company this is. This is a Quranic verse, verse number 69 of Surah An-Nisa. What is it? 'Ula'ikal lazina...' Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. 'Wa may yuti'illaha war rasul, fa ula'ika ma'al lazina an'amallahu 'alaihim.' That those whom Allah has blessed with His bounties. They will be with them, and who will these people be? 'Minan nabiyyina was siddiqina wash shuhada'i was salihin wa hasuna ula'ika rafiqa.' And what an excellent company, can there be a better company than this? There are Prophets, Siddiqin, Shuhada, Salihin, excellent people. Who is better than this? Is it possible? All the Masumin (infallibles) are present there. All the angels are engaged in their service. Everyone is standing with folded hands. And we somehow reach them and in that gathering, we too, with permission, yes? Because it is not the world. In this world, a person finds paths here and there and reaches, but not there. There, angels are standing at every turn. Therefore, anyway, through some intercession, through some request, reaching there—what could be a better company than this? What could be a better gathering than this? But the matter does not stop here. The matter does not stop here. That is why I requested your service, the trouble I gave you, the trouble I am giving you for the third day today, it was for this part of the Hadith. That when the Prophet said this Hadith, look, until now we have read two Hadith before you. In both Hadith, the narrators heard it. But here, who was the Prophet addressing? Who was the addressee? That addressee, who? That addressee, the City of Knowledge and that addressee, the Gate of the City of Knowledge. So, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) would not just listen like that. The Commander of the Faithful asked in return. He asked, 'Ya Rasulullah! Akhbirni ma hazil ahadith.' Tell me, what are these Hadith that if someone memorizes 40? Now the Prophet starts explaining, what are these 40 Hadith? That we requested, if some ignorant person among us hears this, then after understanding 40 Hadith, starts considering himself an Alim and a Faqih? No. Now the Prophet is explaining, and in reality, the Commander of the Faithful knows. This was asked by the Mawla for our understanding. Obviously, so that tomorrow no argument remains against anyone. Tomorrow, one should not say that we did not know. That is why the Mawla asked, 'What are these 40 Hadith?' So the Prophet says, these are 40 subjects. These are 40 topics. This is not one Hadith, or if someone read 'Khairul Iman' and started considering himself a Faqih and an Alim? No. Now look, the Prophet says, the very first subject the Prophet says is: 'An tu'mina billahi wahdahu la sharika lahu wa ta'budahu wa la ta'bud ghayrah.' So have faith in that Allah, besides whom there is no other god. In that God, besides whom there is no other god, and He has no partner, and worship only Him, and do not worship anyone else besides Him. Now, look, in the terminology of Hadith, this is called 'Hadith-e-Jumli'. What does 'Hadith-e-Jumli' mean? It means there are three types of Hadith, three types of words. This has been mentioned in both the Quran and the traditions. One is 'Jami-e-Jumli', meaning extremely brief, like 'Allah'. You just said 'Allah'. This is just... but I had to explain so that the children might understand a little bit. If they don't understand, it doesn't matter, but at least something will go into their minds. Insha'Allah, 5 or 10 years from now, when they grow up a bit, they will understand more. Insha'Allah. But always keeping the standard of the Majlis very low by saying that 'no one understands' is why the standard keeps falling. And when the standard of listening also falls, then one should not complain about anyone. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the speakers, the responsibility of the Zakireen, to gradually keep raising the standard. That is why it is in the Quran and Hadith that there is a 'Jami-e-Jumli'. Meaning, extremely brief, extremely brief. The Prophet just said 'Allah, Allah'. In this, the entire Tawheed (monotheism) was contained. In the single word 'Allah', the entire Tawheed was contained. And the second is 'La ilaha illallah'. This is called 'Jumli', meaning brief. But not 'Jami-e-Jumli'; 'Jami-e-Jumli' means extremely comprehensive and brief. And 'Jumal' and 'Jumli' mean brief, meaning slightly spread out. And after that, the third is 'Tafseeli'. 'Tafseeli' means detailed. So there are three types of knowledge, which are mentioned in the Quran and Hadith. 'Tafseeli'. And the Quran says, 'Fassalna-hu ala ilm' (And We have detailed it with knowledge). The Quran is claiming that our knowledge is detailed. Now, it is a matter of surprise that the Quran, in which it is not even written how many Rak'ats are in the Fajr prayer, claims that its knowledge is detailed. So we objected, 'O Lord! You are saying that the knowledge in it is detailed, and it doesn't even have the two Rak'ats of Fajr. What kind of claim is this?' Then the voice will come, 'O ignorant one! You have not read the verses of the Quran. We have written that if you want to understand the Quran, go to the door of those to whom We have given knowledge.' Ya Ali! To whose door should you go? The entire verse is in the Quran, it is a verse of Surah Al-e-Imran. 'Huwal ladhi anzala alaikal kitab' (It is He who has sent down to you the Book). 'Hunna ummul kitab wa ukharu mutashabihat' (Some of it is the Mother of the Book, and others are ambiguous). 'Fa ammal ladhina fi qulubihim zaighun fa yattabi-una ma tashaba min-hu ibtigha-al fitnati wa ibtigha-a ta'wili-hi wa ma ya'lamu ta'wi-la-hu illallahu war-rasikhuna fil ilm' (As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that which is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation. And no one knows its interpretation except Allah and those who are firm in knowledge). Allah is saying in the Quran, 'We have sent down the Quran to you. It has two types of verses. One is completely clear and one is ambiguous.' If you want to understand the ambiguous and unclear verses, then go to the door of those who are 'Rasikhuna fil ilm' (firm in knowledge). We have given them the knowledge. So this is 'Tafseeli' (detailed) knowledge. Now here, the Prophet, in this brief Hadith, has only hinted that 'Ali! Tawheed is the most important thing. If you understood Tawheed, then you understood everything. If you didn't understand Tawheed... Then you understood nothing. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. But now what happened? This is the tragedy of the Ummah, meaning the Shias. I am not talking about others. That we ourselves have become distant from the house of the Ahlulbayt. We ourselves have become distant from Nahjul Balagha. If we read Nahjul Balagha, the first sermon of Nahjul Balagha. Look, now we will tell you some sentences that might not be understood by some people. But it is the saying of the Masoom, it is the saying of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. We will try to explain, we will try to speak. If it is understood, then good; if it is not understood, then pray, Insha'Allah, may Allah make you understand too. The Imam says, look, what is the sentence? The first sermon of Nahjul Balagha. 'Awwaluddin ma'rifatuhu' (The beginning of religion is His recognition). If you want to enter religion, enter with the recognition of Allah. 'Awwaluddin', meaning entering. 'Awwaluddin'. To enter religion. Meaning, if someone does not have Tawheed, then they have not entered religion at all. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. 'Awwaluddin ma'rifatuhu'. And perfection, now what is Ma'rifat? Ma'rifat means to know Him, to recognize Him. 'Wa kamalu ma'rifatihi' (And the perfection of His recognition), 'at-tasdiqu bihi' (is to believe in Him). The perfection of Ma'rifat is the peak of Ma'rifat, that you testify to Allah. You say, 'Yes, Allah exists.' Meaning, even if 1000 battered generations come before you and say, 1000 atheists come and tell you that there is no God, you should say, 'What kind of things are you saying?' You are denying the One who is more manifest than our own existence. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. More manifest than our existence, His existence is more manifest. You are denying Him? 'At-tasdiqu bihi'. This is the perfection of Ma'rifat. Testify to Him. No matter how many whispers of the devils there are, there should never be even an atom's worth of doubt in your heart about Allah. Indeed. Look, it's a small issue. The issue is small. Yes, come here, brother. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Recite one more Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. What does 'Tasdiq' mean? Tasdiq means to have faith, correct faith. Meaning, to tie a knot so firm that no matter how many whispers there are, no matter how many whispers there are. Now, how are the whispers? Let me present that to you as well. I am telling the children, the elders understand more now. I am telling the children, the youth. How are the whispers? For example, some great trouble, some great calamity comes. For example, someone's young son passed away. The young son died. Now the faith is weak. 'Now, Allah, what did Allah gain by taking our young son?' Look, the faith, meaning there is wavering in the faith. Faith, a little trouble came. We have even seen people who had a loss in business, and in that, they said, 'What happiness did Allah get from this?' We said, 'The same happiness that He got by giving you profit.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. There are strange people. Small things, small problems. There are small problems, and they immediately point fingers at Allah. What is this? Why did He do this? Why did He do that? Alayhis salam rahmatullah. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. So what is the end of Ma'rifat? What is the perfection of Ma'rifat? That 'Tasdiq', what does 'Tasdiq' mean? Faith. Faith should be so strong that the world might turn upside down, but on Tawheed, on Allah's oneness, meaning on the faith in Allah that Allah exists, there should not be even the slightest wavering. That is why, that is why Sayyid al-Shuhada says in a Hadith, it is the Hadith of Sayyid al-Shuhada that, 'Innal mu'mina ashaddu min zubari al-hadid' (The believer is stronger than pieces of iron). The believer is stronger than iron, more powerful than iron. 'Innal hadida idha udkhila fin-nari taghayyara' (If iron is put into fire, it melts). Iron melts. But 'Innal mu'mina idha qutila thumma nushira thumma qutila lam yataghayyar qalbuhu' (But if a believer is killed, then resurrected, then killed, his heart will not change). There will be no change in his faith. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Imam, Hay! Haidari! Ya Ali! This is Tasdiq. Mawla-e-Kainat is standing on the pulpit of the sermon and giving this sermon. You see Mawla-e-Kainat. Now, believe me, the majority of the audience, they were not understanding anything of what Ali ibn Abi Talib was saying. The majority of them were like that. Some just sat there for the sake of reward, and some just sat to object to Ali (a.s.). Their purpose was just to object to Ali and they would repeatedly interrupt Mawla-e-Kainat. That is why the Khutbah Shaqshaqiyyah, which was mentioned in the Majlis the day before yesterday, that sermon, the Maulana, the Maulana stopped it in the middle. He didn't read it. Then he was interrupted in the middle. So such people used to come, they used to trouble Mawla a lot. Do not think, I told you yesterday as well, do not think that his life was like a velvet rope. No, no, many troubles. Anyway, so here he says, 'Wa kamalut tasdiq' (And the perfection of His testimony), 'Tawhiduhu' (is to affirm His oneness). That Allah is one. Now look, it is so easy to say. But even in this, what happens? That if a person asks for a prayer from Allah, these are the practical things we are telling you, which we see in daily life, observe, experience, people come and state their problems, so from that, the matter is understood, brother, we are presenting it to you. That a prayer was asked from Allah, asked from the Imams (a.s.), the prayer was not answered. We kept asking for 40 days. We are telling you, we kept asking for 40 days. Then when it was not accepted, then we went there with them. You understand where we went, right? In this way, the faith started to shake. Tawheed means this, Tawheed means this, that in every state, consider Allah as one. Now, what does considering Allah as one mean? Now, let me present a Hadith to you, Imam Baqir (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. He says, 'Law wajadtu li-ilmi' (If I found for my knowledge), Imam Baqir (a.s.) says, 'if I found 'hamalatan' (carriers), those who could carry the knowledge, those who could bear the knowledge, 'hamalatan', those who could carry the knowledge, then for them, I would have explained the entire religion, the entire Sharia, all things, every single thing, only, only through Surah Tawheed.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Only if there were those who could acquire knowledge. Just one Surah, meaning the word in the Hadith is 'minas samad'. Now, it is possible that the Imam's intent is 'Samad', meaning the word 'Samad', or it is possible it is Surah Tawheed. Qul huwallahu ahad, Allahus samad, lam yalid wa lam yulad, wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad. The Imam says, the entire Sharia is present in this, the entire religion is present in this, all the commandments are present in this, everything is present in this. But there is no one to listen. Then after that, the Imam says a strange sentence. He says, 'And how will I find them? Why would I find them? Such people who could bear knowledge, when my grandfather Amir al-Mu'minin did not find them.' Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. To the extent that, the Imam says, the Imam's sentences are, that the Imam says that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) went to the pulpit, took a cold sigh, and after taking a cold sigh, said, 'Saluni, saluni, qabla an tafqiduni' (Ask me, ask me, before you lose me). But you know, do you know what these Arabs used to ask? 'How much milk is in the stomach of our camel? How many stars are in the sky? How many grains of sand are in the desert?' Not even one proper question. What must have been passing through the heart of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)? And then, the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali (a.s.)) once again took the hand of Janabe Kumayl and led him into the desert, near the Wadi-us-Salaam in Kufa—you know Wadi-us-Salaam is in Najaf. After reaching near the graveyard, the Master of the Universe let out a deep sigh, a cry. 'Ah, O Kumayl! O Kumayl! This heart is overflowing with knowledge, it is full, but there is no one to receive it. There is no one to receive it. Inna hadhihil quloobu aw'iyatun fakhayruha aw'aha. The best heart, the best vessel, is the one that has the most capacity. O Kumayl! I see people coming for knowledge, but their only purpose is to attain the world.' And it is a very detailed hadith, a very long hadith. Just as a summary: Tawheed is that a human should not have even an atom's worth of doubt about Allah at any stage—that why doesn't Allah help us? If Allah is One, then why is this not happening? If it is like this, then why is that? Or, for example, if Allah existed, then why did Saddam—someone objected—why didn't He save them from Abbas (a.s.)? Why didn't Allah save them? Is this even a question? This is being said just for the children. Look, if such questions ever come to your mind, remove them immediately. Because it is a whisper of Satan, yes? Indeed. If the world were to be run in this manner, then Allah would have first told Satan at the beginning to prostrate, and Satan would have had to do it. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! There is no option; he would have had to do it. Go on. But Allah gave him an option in His court. 'If you want to do it, do it; if you don't want to, don't.' He said, 'I will not.' Then he said, 'What about the years I spent worshipping You?' Allah said, 'Fine, I have granted you respite until the reappearance of the Imam-e-Zamana.' He granted him respite until that time. He said, 'No, that is not enough. I want more powers.' 'What powers?' 'This power, that power, that power.' He even said, 'Give me enough power so that I can enter people's veins, nerves, and blood.' 'Give me this power, and through it, I can sit upon their hearts and whisper against You.' Against You. The Quran says: La-aq'udanna lahum siratakal mustaqeem (I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path), Wala-ughwiyannahum ajma'een (And I will mislead them all), Illa 'ibadaka minhumul mukhliseen (Except for those of Your servants whom You have purified). Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! So it is known that there are some servants over whom Satan has no power. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Now, if you want to find out, look at yourself. One Khutbah-giver is saying, 'Saluni, saluni' (Ask me, ask me), and the other is saying, 'A Satan is overpowering me,' who keeps misleading. Nara-e-Haydari, Ya Ali! Wow! Wow! Wow! So he keeps misleading. 'If I am on the right path, then you follow me. If I do wrong, you set me straight.' Now, one who is himself in need of being set straight, will he lead and guide the Ummah? The Quran itself asked the question beforehand. The Quran asked the question for the Muslims long ago. But the Muslim has always been foolish and will always remain foolish. Wow! SubhanAllah. Why are you telling me right now that they will always remain foolish? Because the Princess (Fatima (s.a.)) said so, in the court: 'Today you are treating me like this, you will be humiliated and disgraced until the Day of Judgment.' So, will the Princess's word be wrong? So the Quran asked the question beforehand: Afaman yahdee ilal haqqi ahaqqu an yuttaba'a amman la yahdee illa an yuhda (Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not guide unless he is guided?). The Quran is asking the human intellect. Do you have intellect? The Quran is asking, 'Do you have intellect?' Then tell me, between two people, whom will you follow? One who doesn't even know the path unless someone tells him, or one who shows the path to others? Wow! SubhanAllah. This is the Quran's question. The Quran is asking the human intellect. But man—that is, the Muslim—does not understand this obvious point. Here, the Master of the Universe says: Kamalut tasdeeqi bihi tawheeduhu wa kamalu tawheedihi al-ikhlasu lahu. And the perfection of Tawheed is to purify Allah from everything, to make Him transcendent, to purify Him. That is, do not bring any thought about Allah into your mind. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! No thought should come into the mind about Allah. That Allah is like this, like that, what must He look like? What must Allah look like? Will He be a bit sturdy, fat, tall, what kind of clothes would He wear? So the Muslims thought, 'Yes, the question is correct.' I had presented the hadith about the Jew in the service (of the Imam) earlier, about what answer he got in the mosque. He said, 'What did the Master of the Universe answer?' I don't need to repeat that hadith. But now I am bringing you to another hadith. To the second hadith, that the Muslims thought we must have something somewhere. When it is asked, 'How does Allah look?', the Muslims split into two groups. One is called Mujassama, the other is called Mushabba. Mujassama are those who believe in a body for Allah like our body. Just as we have a body, Allah has a body. That is, hands, feet, nose, ears, eyes, all the same. Allah is exactly like that. But now, since it is Allah, Allah should be a bit bigger. So they increased His height a bit. And made Him a bit stronger. Made the hair golden. And green-colored clothes and golden shoes and everything—like, it's good. Good. They described Allah like that, okay? These are called Mujassama. And the second group is those who are called Mushabba. Mushabba, meaning they make a tashbih (comparison). They say Allah exists, He is something like us, but exactly how, we don't know. But He is like that. Now look here, come back to the door of the Ahlulbayt. Wow! Wow! Wow! Now we will read three hadiths very quickly. Maybe you will understand. Okay, if you don't understand, it doesn't matter. Now the first hadith of the Master of the Universe is continuing. What is the perfection of Tawheed? That you purify Allah from every kind of thought. And what is the perfection of Ikhlas (sincerity)? The perfection of Ikhlas, meaning purity—the perfection of purifying Allah is that whatever thought of an attribute comes into your mind, remove it from your mind. Wow! Wow! If any idea is coming into your mind. The Master says: Nafyus sifati 'anhu (Negate the attributes from Him), Lishahadati kulli sifatin annaha ghayru mawsoofin wa lishahadati kulli mawsoofin annahu ghayru sifatin (Because every attribute testifies that it is not like the described, and every described testifies that it is not like the attribute). Because there are two things. One is the attribute, one is the described. Attribute refers to the description. For example, if you say about someone that he is fat. For example, and say about someone that he is thin. This being thin and being fat is an attribute. And the one about whom it is being said is the described. So, are this attribute and the described both the same? No. The reason for that is that if tomorrow he becomes thin or fat, you will not say that he is no longer there. He was fat, we will consider him fat. Whether you stay like that. And similarly, the opposite is also the same. Or for example, if a man is brave and a man is a coward. It is possible that the brave one becomes a coward tomorrow, and it is possible that the coward becomes brave tomorrow. So these two things are both separate things. Therefore, the Imam says that purify Allah from every attribute that comes into your mind. Now look, I bring another hadith of balagha (eloquence) so that the matter becomes completely clear. It is a small hadith. Someone asked the Master, 'What is Tawheed?' So in one sentence, the Master said—not one sentence, one word—'At-Tawheed, alla tatawahhamahu' (Tawheed is that you do not imagine Him). Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! SubhanAllah. What is he saying? And what a miracle this sentence is. It is that thing, any thought coming into your mind, because if once you have formed a thought about God, about your Lord, and some people have accepted that thought, then there is no limit to it. Yes. You didn't understand the point. Yes. Now I take you to the other side. Listen very carefully. Recite one more Salawat. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. So this is also about balagha, the seekers of Tawheed. Just now they asked about Tawheed in Islam. 'At-Tawheed, alla tatawahhamahu.' The Master said in one sentence, in one word, Tawheed is that you do not have any illusion about Allah. Illusion, meaning whatever comes into your brain, whatever comes into your mind, purify Allah from it. About the essence of Allah, yes, about the essence of Allah, whatever comes, why? If this door opens, then every person will say, 'Our Lord is like this.' Every person will say. And then an image of the Lord will be formed. And then if an image is formed, there will be no limit to it. You will make an image, we will make an image, he will make an image, everyone will make an image. Then as many images, so many Lords. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! This is not God. This is not God. Just one hadith of Imam Baqir (a.s.), just that. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. 'Kullama mayyaztumoohu bi-awhamikum fee adaqqi ma'anihi' (Whatever you are preparing in your minds, in its most subtle meaning)—that is, O Imam, you are trying to say that this is not about common people. It is about Farabi, it is about Aristotle, it is about Abu Ali Sina, it is about Khwaja Nasir, such great people—if even they think about the greatest God in their minds, 'Kullama mayyaztumoohu'—bringing a very powerful image of God into the mind. Think, keep thinking for a long time and an image... 'mayyaztumoohu bi-awhamikum fee adaqqi ma'anihi' (in its most subtle meaning). Everyone paid attention to the first sentence, right? Everyone paid attention? What you prepared in your mind, what you made in your mind, and made with great effort, put a lot of strength into thinking, 'How would Allah be?' Think, 'He would be like this, a little of this, a little of that, mix this.' That is, an assorted Allah. Think, very powerful. After all the thinking, the Imam says—only the Masoom (infallible) can say this. Ali and the progeny of Ali can say this. Indeed, indeed. It is not in anyone else's capacity. 'Makhlooq' (Created). Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Whatever you think is created. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! 'Masnoo'un lakum' (Manufactured by you). Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! And now it is not God. It is not your God. It is a manufactured thing. It is your creation, it is your product, your Creator is someone else. This is a thing made by you, it is not your God. 'Masnoo'un, makhlooqun, mardoodun ilaykum' (Manufactured, created, returned to you). And this is going to turn back to you itself. It has no connection with Allah at all. Wow! Wow! Wow! And then the Imam gives a simile, an example. And the example of such a thinker is like an ant, which thinks that 'since I have two antennae, and based on these antennae I do all the work,' because the ant does the same work based on the antennae, right? The Imam says that the ant thinks that 'this antenna is the cause of perfection,' so Allah must have big antennae. Wow! Wow! Allah must have such great antennas, through which He can perform great deeds. Did you notice? And the Muslims did the same. If we are like this, then Allah must be like that. If you come to the door of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), then the Mawla says, 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad'. So, this is a very dry topic. A very dry topic indeed. But it is very important. As we said in the beginning, 'Awwal al-din ma'rifatuhu' (The beginning of religion is His recognition). Human, this is what the Mawla of the universe is saying from the pulpit of Kufa, that if you want to enter the religion, you must enter with His recognition. 'Awwal al-din ma'rifatuhu'. Now the word is Allah, Allah. Has anyone understood Allah until today? What does Allah mean? Allah. Now, there are three or four meanings of Allah in the hadiths. Right now, I cannot explain each meaning here, there is no time. Just finish it quickly. One meaning of Allah is that when all hopes from every source in the world are cut off, then refuge is taken in Allah. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! When a person becomes disappointed with everyone. As long as there is hope that the doctor will cure, no, the doctor has said, there is nothing to worry about. The doctor said the medicines are working. Oh, got sick again. Health deteriorated again. Now the doctor said, 'Sorry, I cannot do anything more, I did as much as I could.' Now even the medicines are not working. Now they go to Allah. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) say, before reaching that stage, go to Allah at the first stage. Wow! Wow! Wow! Go to the doctor, but if you go at the first stage, your faith will be strengthened. Do not place your faith in the doctor. The doctor gives medicine. The doctor's work is not healing. Healing is in the hands of Allah. Indeed, indeed. So, this is Allah, the Imam says, these are not our words, do not think we are saying this. The Imam says that when all sources, all resources, are disconnected, when everything is cut off, then the Being in whom refuge is taken is called Allah. That is why when a narrator asked the Imam, 'Is there an Allah?' The Imam said, 'Yes, there is.' 'Is there any proof?' He said, 'Yes, there is. Have you ever boarded a ship?' He said, 'Yes, I have. I have boarded a ship.' Has it ever happened that the ship got stuck in a storm and you thought there is no one here to save you? He said, 'Yes, that has happened too.' At that time, your hope must have been attached to only one Being. That only one Being can save and no one else can save. He said, 'Yes, that happened too.' That is what is called Allah. Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! Wow! That is what is called Allah. This is Tawheed (Monotheism). And of course, the discussion of Tawheed is very vast and it is a very broad topic. But because this hadith is very long and trying to cover this hadith in two days, I mean, this is the main hadith. Insha'Allah, I have less time, so I will end this discussion here. Just this, the important thing is that Allah kept the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) for this reason, the Quran announced, the Quran announced that 'Laqad kana lakum fi rasulillahi uswatun hasanah' (Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent pattern of conduct). 'Laqad kana lakum fi rasulillahi uswatun hasanah'. In the Messenger of Allah, there is an excellent role model for you. You follow the Messenger of Allah. Well, the life of the Messenger of Allah that was among the Muslims was 23 years. It was 23 years. Now what after that? After that, the Messenger of Allah announced his Ahlulbayt. The Messenger of Allah announced, 'After me, my Ahlulbayt.' And then each individual of the Ahlulbayt set such examples that should be recorded in the golden pages of history, every single thing. And that is why if anyone wants to see Tawheed, they should see it in the field of Karbala. In the field of Karbala. On the night of Ashura, on the night of Ashura, martyrdom, when the battle was to be fought, just in one night, he said, 'Worship Allah. Worship Allah.' One man said, it will happen in the universe. Tawheed alive. And in such circumstances, in such circumstances, in the martyrdom of the martyrs, he called upon Allah, he did not call his companions, he did not call his children, he did not call anyone. And he kept remembering, all the time. So much so that even in such a difficult atmosphere, Hazrat Ali Akbar stood up and gave the Adhan. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. This is a very big thing. Oh, that Ali Akbar who is the likeness of the Messenger of Allah. You think, the youth, and Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'Tada' qulubuna ya bunayya, son, now you have come, now you go.' Ali Akbar was waiting impatiently. Ali Akbar was waiting for this moment, when the father would say and when I would go. So Ali Akbar said, 'Yes father, I am ready to go.' But Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Go and meet Zainab once.' Now Ali Akbar went, went to Zainab, but the mother said, 'Go, let me see Akbar again.' The one who raised him, Ali Akbar came and after coming said, 'Bibi Amma, give me permission.' Zainab looked at Ali Akbar from head to toe and started saying, 'Son, did I raise you for this, did I raise you for 18 years, so that I would give you permission to die?' He said, 'Bibi Amma, if you don't give, it doesn't matter, but if the Prophet goes and asks what happened to my Hussain, brother Ali Akbar?' Then he saw death as death. Zainab said, 'Go son, I have given permission.' Now as soon as Ali Akbar wanted to depart, Humaid bin Muslim, who is the historian of Karbala, says, 'I was watching that as Ali Akbar wanted to leave, someone would catch his garment and pull him back, the curtain of walking would rise, fall, rise, fall, someone was holding the garment.' Ali Akbar asked, 'Bibi, why did you let me go, why, why are you holding my garment?' So she said, 'Ya Ali Akbar, irham gurbatana' (O Ali Akbar, have mercy on our loneliness). Ali Akbar, have mercy on our helplessness. Ali Akbar said, 'Oh, my father is also watching.' Now, who was holding the garment in the battlefield, it is not written who was holding it, but it is just that if an elder was holding it, they would hold the arm, but holding the garment means it was some child who was sitting holding the garment, 'Brother, don't leave us alone.' Humaid bin Muslim says, when Ali Akbar left, I did not see the funeral of any such youth. Ali Akbar came from a full house, Hussain prepared him, Hussain prepared him and mounted him on the horse and after that, looking towards the sky, prayed, 'Allahumma ishhad ala ha'ula'il qawm' (O Allah, bear witness against this nation). 'Qatala ala Ali ghulam' (A youth has gone against them). A slave, a youth has gone against them, for whom the throne would not remain. 'Khalqan wa khuluqan wa mantiqan rasulillah' (In creation, in character, in speech, in conduct, he was the Messenger of Allah). Whenever we were eager to see your Messenger, we would look at Ali Akbar. We would look at Ali Akbar. Ali Akbar left, Hussain said, 'Son, keep looking back as you go.' Now Ali Akbar went some distance, then felt a sound, when he turned back, the whole father was standing with his hand on his waist, 'Ya Ali, Ya Ali, Ya Ali.' Father, you gave me permission, now why are you coming? He said, 'Son, if you had children, you would know what it means to bid farewell to a young son.' Ali Akbar went and fought, and while fighting, sent at least 200 wretched ones to Hell. Ali Akbar was covered in wounds and came back, until now no one had come back, except in the event of Karbala, except just, and there were other Ali Akbars, and how did they come? They came because it was a mother's heart, a mother's soul, a young son had gone, she was restless, she said, 'Fizza, stand at the door of the tent, and see if the color of the Master's face is changing.' Now Fizza came and stood at the door of the tent, once she came back, 'Bibi, the color of the Master's face has changed.' She said, 'Give the Master a little Ahmad.' So now when Hussain came, she said, 'Master, why has the color of your face changed?' He said, 'Because a famous wrestler has come before my son, he is a lion, and my child is hungry and thirsty for three days.' Just a mother's heart, she was restless, 'Master, what should I do?' He said, 'Pray, a mother's prayer is accepted for the child.' Umm Layla said to the ladies, 'Make a circle.' They made a circle, Umm Layla stood up, 'O You who reunited Yaqub with Yusuf.' The mother's prayer was not even finished when Ali Akbar came back and started saying, 'What a strange news Ali Akbar brought, O father, al-atash, qatala Ali, thirst is killing me.' Just the blood that is hadith, the blood of the Prophet, and the heaviness of the bitterness and it is very dear. 'Hal ilana min sabil' (Is there any way). Hussain said, 'Son, give me your hand, taste a little, the thirst will be quenched.' Ali Akbar put his tongue in Hussain's mouth, he pulled it back, said, 'Father, your tongue is full of thorns.' Hussain bid farewell, Ali Akbar went, then while fighting, now let the oppressed one of the battlefield present his service, just listen and the Majlis is over, give condolences to the Princess, give condolences to the Princess. Ali Akbar went, from the army of Sham, once a wretched one, a tyrant, struck such a spear that it hit Ali Akbar's chest, now the sentence of the Maqtal is, 'A'tanaqa al-faras' (He embraced the horse). So A'tanaqa al-faras, Ali Akbar put his arms around the horse's neck, A'tanaqa al-faras, then after that the horse took him among the enemies, went among the enemies, 'Faqatta'uhu' (They cut him into pieces). Ali Akbar called out, 'Ya abata' (O father). Father, final farewell. Hussain walked, reciting a dirge, but before Hussain, Humaid bin Muslim says, 'This one lady, outside the tent, and in the shadow of the tent, Ya Zahra, Ya Fatima.' O piece of my tent, O light of my eyes, Zainab-e-Kubra and Zainab threw herself on Ali Akbar. I asked who is this? He said, 'This is Ali's daughter Zainab.' Hussain sent Zainab back to the tent, sat near Ali Akbar, pulled the spear out of the chest, the tip of the spear remained, and Eve raised her head and said, 'Father, Ali Akbar has departed.' Hussain raised the spear, 'Ya bunayya, ad-dunya ba'daka nafa' (O my son, after you, may this world be ruined). 'Jaza'ka bin huma ad-dunya wa gham-e-ha' (You have been saved from the sorrows and griefs of the world), so now the rest, son, is the same, your father is left alone among the wretched. O Allah, hayya al-salam, ya al-mun, ala al-adw, ala al-qawm-e-zalimin. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us all among the helpers of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Remove the troubles of those who are troubled. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. O Lord, grant Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) safety. Those who are away from their homeland, return them safe and sound. Wherever the Shias are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the high-ranking scholars and the esteemed Maraje. Protect the Atabat-e-Muqaddasa (holy shrines). May Allah grant us the opportunity for Ziyarat in this world and bless us with the intercession of Muhammad and the progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Recite one Surah Al-Fatiha and three times Surah Al-Ikhlas and gift the reward to the souls of the late Ghulam Ali Ibn Abdul Aziz Dakhani, the Lakhani family, and all the deceased of the Ruhani family. Bismillah.

title: Kis Baat Ki Nidaamat? I Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture addresses historical inquiries and scholarly investigations regarding the events surrounding the birth of a significant figure in Islamic history. The speaker analyzes the specific detail of the Imam locking the door from the inside, questioning the implications of this action. The discussion aims to clarify misconceptions and explore the mystery surrounding these reported events.
content:
That this incident... and this incident which the people are talking about, the scholars have investigated it, in which the first thing that has been mentioned is this: that when the Imam (a.s.) went inside, he locked the door from the inside. If the birth was to happen, why lock the door from the inside? This objection points towards the fact that what should have happened here did not happen, or it is a great mystery that it did not happen, otherwise, why this objection?

title: Noor-e-Sayyedul Mursaleen (s.a.w.a) Ki Khilqat | 17th Rabiul Awwal | Roz-e-Wilaadat Baa Sa'aadat
excerpt: This lecture explores the metaphysical origins of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) based on a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.). It details how Allah created the Light (Noor) of the Prophet 424,000 years before all other creations, including the heavens, earth, and previous prophets. The talk describes the Prophet's Light passing through twelve distinct spiritual veils, each for a specific duration, while reciting unique glorifications of Allah. Finally, it traces the journey of this Light through the Tablet, the Throne, and the lineage of the prophets until its manifestation in the loins of Abdullah ibn Abdul-Muttalib.
content:
And before the creation of all the Prophets, He created [him], and how long before? He created this Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) 424,000 years earlier. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And blessings of Allah be upon you, O Waliy-al-Asr, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance, assist us and grant us success. O my respected ones, this narration describes the reality of the Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and the precedence of that Light. This narration is reported from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), in which he states regarding the creation of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) that, 'Innallaha tabaraka wa ta'ala khalaqa nura Muhammadin s.a.w.a.' (Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, created the Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)) before He created the heavens, the earth, the Throne (Arsh), and the Footstool (Kursi). He created it before the Tablet (Lawh) and the Pen (Qalam), before Paradise and Hell. And before He created Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Musa, Isa, Dawud, and Sulayman (a.s.), He created the Light of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) before the creation of all these Prophets, and how long before? He created this Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) 424,000 years earlier. After that, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states, 'Wa khalaqa azza wa jalla ma'ahu ithna ashara hijaban' (And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, created twelve veils along with the Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)). And what are those veils? The Veil of Power, the Veil of Greatness, the Veil of Grace, the Veil of Mercy, the Veil of Happiness, the Veil of Honor, the Veil of Status, the Veil of Guidance, the Veil of Prophethood, the Veil of Exaltation, the Veil of Awe, and the Veil of Intercession. And then Allah kept this Light of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) in each veil for a fixed period. In the Veil of Power, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, kept this Light of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) for 12,000 years, and during those 12,000 years, this Light of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) was reciting this glorification: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High). And then Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that after 12,000 years, Allah kept this Light of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Greatness, and for 11,000 years in the Veil of Greatness, the Light of the Messenger of Allah was reciting the glorification and praise of 'Subhana 'Alim-as-Sirr' (Glory be to the Knower of the Unseen). And then after that, Allah kept the Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Grace for 10,000 years, and for 10,000 years, the Light of Hazrat Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was reciting 'Subhana man huwa qayimun la yalhu' (Glory be to Him who is Ever-Standing and does not neglect). And then after that, in the Veil of Mercy, Allah kept the Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) for 9,000 years, and for 9,000 years, the Light of Hazrat Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was reciting the glorification and praise of 'Subhana ar-Rafi'-il-A'la' (Glory be to the Exalted, the Most High). After that, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, kept this Light of the Messenger of Allah in the Veil of Happiness for 8,000 years, and for those 8,000 years, what was this Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) reciting? 'Subhana man huwa da'imun la yashu' (Glory be to Him who is Everlasting and does not err). And then when this period of 8,000 years was completed, after that, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, kept this Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Honor, and the Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was in the Veil of Honor for 7,000 years, and for 7,000 years, his Light was reciting the glorification and praise of 'Subhana man huwa ghaniyyun la yaftaqir' (Glory be to Him who is Self-Sufficient and does not need). And when this period was completed, then Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, placed the Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Status, and for 6,000 years, the Light of the Messenger of Allah was declaring, was reciting the glorification and praise of 'Subhana al-'Alim-il-Karim' (Glory be to the All-Knowing, the Generous). And when this period of 6,000 years ended, after that, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, placed the Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Guidance, and his Light remained in the Veil of Guidance for 5,000 years, and his Light was seen reciting, 'Subhana Dhil-'Arshil-'Azim' (Glory be to the Lord of the Great Throne). And then after that, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, placed the Light of Hazrat Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Prophethood, and his Light remained in this Veil of Prophethood for 4,000 years, and for 4,000 years, his Light was continuously reciting this: 'Subhana Rabbil-'Izzati 'amma yasifun' (Glory be to the Lord of Might, above what they describe). And after that, Allah kept this Light of Greatness of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Exaltation for 3,000 years, and what was his Light reciting during this time? 'Subhana Dhil-Mulki wal-Malakut' (Glory be to the Possessor of the Kingdom and the Dominion). And when this period ended, after that, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, placed this Light of His beloved Prophet in the Veil of Awe, and kept this Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) in the Veil of Awe for 2,000 years, and his Light was seen reciting, 'Subhanallahi wa bi-hamdihi' (Glory be to Allah and by His praise). And then after that, when this period ended, in which veil was this Light transferred? It reached the final stage, that veil which is called the Veil of Intercession, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, kept the Light of His beloved in this Veil of Intercession for 1,000 years, and for this 1,000 years, the Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was seen saying, 'Subhana Rabbiyal-'Azimi wa bi-hamdihi' (Glory be to my Lord, the Great, and by His praise). Just, respected sir, after that, these sentences are found in the narration: 'Summa azhara ismahu 'alal-lawh' (Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, manifested his name on the Tablet), and it remained shining on the Tablet for 4,000 years. When it passed from the stage of the veil, it reached the Tablet; this Light remained shining on the Tablet for 4,000 years. And then it has come in the narration, 'Summa azharahu 'alal-'Arsh' (Then Allah manifested this Light of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) on the Throne), and his Light remained written on its pillar on the Throne for 7,000 years. And then here, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says, and until Allah placed it in the loins of Hazrat Adam (a.s.). 'Summa naqalahu min sulbi Adama 'alayhis-salam ila sulbi Nuhin 'alayhis-salam' (Then He transferred it from the loins of Adam (a.s.) to the loins of Nuh (a.s.)), then after that, the sentences of the narration are, 'Summa min sulbin ila sulbin' (Then from loins to loins), that this Light kept transferring from one loin to another, 'Hatta akhrajahullahu azza wa jalla min sulbi Abdillahi ibni Abdul-Muttalib' (Until Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, brought it out from the loins of Abdullah ibn Abdul-Muttalib), and until this Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) emerged from the loins of Hazrat Abdullah ibn Abdul-Muttalib (a.s.). Now, O respected sir, here I want to say this sentence to you that this is one narration; I do not know how many such narrations exist in our books regarding the creation of Hazrat Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his Light. Now, after hearing this Hadith, even after that, if someone is seen saying that the Prophet is like us, then what can be done about him? Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali-e-Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum.
The Light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) was created 424,000 years before any other creation.
The Light passed through twelve spiritual veils, including Power, Greatness, Mercy, and Intercession.
Each veil had a specific duration, ranging from 1,000 to 12,000 years.
The Light recited unique glorifications (tasbih) while residing in each of the twelve veils.
The Light was manifested on the Tablet (Lawh) for 4,000 years and the Throne (Arsh) for 7,000 years.
The Light was transferred through the loins of the prophets, starting from Adam (a.s.) to Abdullah ibn Abdul-Muttalib.
The lecture emphasizes the unique, non-ordinary status of the Prophet's creation compared to humanity.
