title: 🎁🎉 ANWAAR-E-REZA (A.S.) GRAND QUIZ 🎁🎉 | Sunday, 3-May-2026 | Imam Reza (a.s.) Ki Wilaayat Ki Ehmiyat
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive exploration of the life, teachings, and divine status of Imam Reza (a.s.), centered around the significance of his Wilayah. Through the analysis of the Hadith-e-Silsilatuz Zahab and historical accounts of his interactions with the Abbasid Caliph Ma'mun, the session emphasizes that Imamate is a divinely appointed position independent of political authority. The lecture also addresses the dangers of sects like the Waqifiyya and underscores the necessity of recognizing the Imam of one's time for the validity of faith.
content:
Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasani, salawatuka alayhi wa ala abaihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. A'udhu billahis sami'il alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu alayka ya waliyal asr, adriknā wa la tuhliknā. Respected and honorable listeners and viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. On behalf of the TSR team, we extend our congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of Imamul Murtaza, Sayyidul Murtaza, the eighth of the Imams of guidance, Abul Hasan, Imam Ali Ibn Musa ar-Riza (a.s.). And most importantly, we offer congratulations on this joyous occasion to the Masumeen (a.s.) through a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'dahum ajma'in. Regarding Imam Ali Ibn Musa ar-Riza (a.s.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to Amirul Momineen Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s.): 'Wa man ahabba an yalqallaha dahikan mustabshiran falyatawalla Aliyya bna Musar-Rida alayhimus salam' (And whoever wishes to meet Allah while laughing and rejoicing, it is incumbent upon him to accept the Wilayah of Imam Ali Ibn Musa ar-Riza (a.s.)). Dear brothers, on the occasion of this auspicious birth, the TSR team is here with the 'Anware Riza Grand Quiz'. In this program, we will discuss the Wilayah and Imamate of Imam Riza (a.s.). Before starting this program, let us look at some of the rules of this quiz. The quiz link is now live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just need to watch the discussion carefully and provide the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program. Therefore, do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all answers must be correct. Among all those who have answered all questions correctly, 18 winners will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system, who will be given these prizes. Respected viewers, along with the quiz rules, let us also inform you that there is a surprise question among today's quiz questions, which will be shown on the screen at any time during this entire discussion. So, listen to this discussion carefully so that you do not miss that question. Let us begin our discussion today. A'udhu billahis sami'il alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Sallallahu alayka ya waliyal asr, adriknā wa la tuhliknā. The hadith through which we want to start this discussion regarding the importance of the Wilayah and Imamate of Imam Riza (a.s.) is the famous hadith known as 'Hadith-e-Silsilatuz Zahab'. 'Silsila' in Arabic means a chain. And 'Zahab' means gold. So, Silsilatuz Zahab means the 'Hadith of the Golden Chain'. It is called Silsilatuz Zahab because all the narrators in the chain of this hadith are not ordinary people; rather, all the narrators are Masumeen (a.s.). They are all Imams, and the hadith reaches from all the Imams to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and from there to Jibra'il (a.s.), and from there to Allah. This is a Hadith-e-Qudsi. That is why it is called Hadith-e-Silsilatuz Zahab. The chain starts from Imam Riza (a.s.) and reaches up to Allah. It is narrated that when Imam Riza (a.s.) passed through Nishapur—when Ma'mun had called him, his journey started from Medina. When the Imam reached Nishapur, it is found in the narrations that 'Ijtama'a ilayhi as-habul hadith' (many scholars of hadith gathered around him). They were those who did not believe in the Imamate of Imam Riza (a.s.). They were not Shias; they were opponents of the Shias. They were called 'As-habul Hadith' (scholars of hadith). They were experts in the hadiths of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). They were memorizers of hadith. So, they requested Imam Riza (a.s.), saying, 'Ya Ibn Rasulullah, O son of the Prophet, tarhalu 'anna wa la tuhaddithuna bi-hadith? (Will you leave us like this without narrating a hadith from which we can benefit?)' The Imam was sitting in his litter (ammari). He brought his head out of the litter, and then the Imam began to narrate the Hadith-e-Silsilatuz Zahab. The chain of which starts from Imam Riza (a.s.) and goes back to Allah, as I mentioned. The Imam said: 'Sami'tu abi Musa Ibn Ja'far alayhimus salam' (I heard from my noble father Imam Musa Kazim (a.s.)). He heard from his father, Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq (a.s.). He heard from his father, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.). He heard from his father, Imam Sayyidus Sajjad, i.e., Ali Ibn al-Husayn (a.s.), the fourth Imam. He heard from his father, Imam Husayn Ibn Ali (a.s.). He heard from his father, Amirul Momineen (a.s.), Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). He said that he heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and he said that he heard from Jibra'il (a.s.) that he heard from Allah Azza wa Jall. What does Allah say? Allah Azza wa Jall says: 'La ilaha illallah hisni' (The word 'La ilaha illallah', i.e., the belief in Tawhid, is My fortress, My strong and fortified castle). 'Faman dakhala hisni amina min 'adhabi' (Whoever enters My fortress will be safe from My punishment). This is the belief in Tawhid, the most important fundamental belief. Whoever becomes a believer in this Tawhid, he remains safe from Allah's punishment. Imam Riza (a.s.) narrated this hadith about Tawhid to those who had requested it. But then, after saying this much, the Imam remained silent for a moment. The Imam's caravan was about to move forward. When the caravan had moved a little further, the Imam called out to us again. The Imam stopped his caravan and addressed us—the same scholars of hadith who were not Shias and who had made the request. The Imam said: 'Bi-shurutiha, wa ana min shurutiha' (But there are conditions for this belief in 'La ilaha illallah', and I am one of its conditions). The Imam wanted to convey that whoever does not believe in the Imamate of Imam Riza (a.s.), his belief in Tawhid will not be accepted. And that is why it is called Silsilatuz Zahab. As I mentioned, Ahmad Ibn Hanbal, who is considered one of the great scholars of the Ahl-e-Sunnat and an Imam of the Hanbali school, stated in 'Manaqib-e-Ale Abi Talib' by Ibn Shahr Ashub Mazandarani, that if this chain—which starts from Imam Riza (a.s.) and goes up to the Messenger of Allah and then to Jibra'il and then to Allah—if this chain were to be recited over a madman, his madness would vanish and he would be cured. Now he will no longer be a fool. Meaning, this chain of narration that begins with Imam Reza (a.s.) is so blessed. The most important thing here is what the Imam said: the belief in Tawheed (monotheism) will be accepted, but with what condition? With the condition of my Imamate and my Wilayah. Meaning, Imam Reza (a.s.) made it clear that no one will enter the fortress until—that is, one cannot enter the fortress of Tawheed unless they acknowledge my Imamate. If we look at this, merely declaring with the tongue that we are believers in 'La ilaha illallah' will not save a person from the punishment of Allah. This belief is not proven by mere verbal declaration. A person should not just say Tawheed with their tongue or declare 'La ilaha illallah', but they must acknowledge the Imamate of Imam Reza (a.s.) in their heart. The verses of the Holy Quran also point towards this, indicating that the decision of Paradise and Hell will not be based on what a person says with their tongue, but rather, what will the decision of Paradise and Hell be based on? It will be based on what is in a person's heart, what their true belief is. There is verse number 225 of Surah Al-Baqarah, in which Allah Tabarak wa Ta'ala states: 'La yu'akhidukumullahu bil-laghwi fi aymanikum.' Meaning, Allah will not hold you accountable for what you declare with your tongue; your reckoning will not be based on that. 'Wa lakin yu'akhidukum bima kasabat qulubukum'—but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned. The things that reside within your heart, what your heart has earned—that is, what your true belief is—Allah will judge based on that; the decision of Paradise and Hell will be based on that. 'Wallahu Ghafurun Halim'—and Allah is indeed Ghafur (Forgiving) and Halim (Forbearing). Meaning, verbal declaration has no importance unless that belief is in the heart. Respected viewers, the incident of the Hadith-e-Silsilat al-Dhahab that we heard is just a small link in the long journey the Imam undertook from Medina to Merv. When Ma'mun's rule became stable, he ordered Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Reza (a.s.) to leave Medina and come to Merv. The Imam presented several excuses and kept delaying it, but Ma'mun kept calling the Imam repeatedly, until the Imam was forced to depart from there. Ma'mun also gave a specific order that when the Imam was brought to Merv, he should not be brought via the route of Kufa and Qom, but rather through the route of Basra, Ahwaz, and Fars. The reason for this was that he did not want the people of Kufa and Qom to be influenced by the Imam and become his followers. Therefore, he specifically ordered that the Imam be brought to Merv via a long, different route. When the Imam (a.s.) reached Merv, Ma'mun first offered him the Caliphate. The Imam refused it. After that, Ma'mun offered the Imam (a.s.) the succession (Wilayat al-Ahd) and insisted upon it greatly. The Imam accepted it, but said that I have a few conditions upon which I will accept this position. Among those conditions were that the Imam said: 'I will not give any orders, nor will I stop anyone from doing anything. I will not pass any judgments, nor will I change any system.' Ma'mun accepted all these conditions, and based on this, he took the oath of allegiance from the people. When all these things were done, he minted coins in the name of the Imam, and the Imam's name began to be mentioned from the pulpits. Now, in the meantime, the day of Eid arrives. Ma'mun requests the Imam to lead the people in prayer so that the people may be assured that you are holding this position. The Imam initially refused and reminded him of the conditions that I will not interfere in this government in any way. But after much insistence from Ma'mun, the Imam accepted that 'Alright, I will lead the prayer.' But the Imam said, 'If you want me to lead the prayer, I will lead it exactly as my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), used to lead it.' Ma'mun accepted this. When the Imam (a.s.) left his house to lead the prayer, he was barefoot. He was wearing very simple clothes and his sleeves were rolled up. The Imam had a staff in his hand and was heading towards the mosque with great sincerity, and was raising a voice that contained the Takbir of Allah. The Imam was raising the call: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, 'ala ma hadana.' When the people saw this scene, they were deeply moved. The whole city echoed with weeping and wailing, and not just the common people, but even Ma'mun's commanders, upon seeing the Imam, got down from their mounts. And just as the Imam was barefoot, these commanders also took off their shoes. The atmosphere had become very luminous and spiritual. Seeing this, Ma'mun's advisors said to Ma'mun, 'O Ma'mun, stop the Imam from reaching the mosque, stop him from leading the prayer. Because if he reaches the prayer mat in this state, the people will become his complete followers and will start disobeying you.' Upon this, Ma'mun stopped the Imam and sent a message for him to return. The Imam (a.s.) put on his shoes and returned. So, in this whole incident, Ma'mun tried his best to keep the Imam (a.s.) away from the people. Just as we see that he gave the specific order that the Imam be brought via a different route instead of the route of Qom and Kufa so that people could not meet the Imam, people could not be influenced by the Imam, and people could not converse with the Imam so that they would not be influenced by him. But this was Allah's way, that this same Ma'mun ordered the Imam to lead the prayer, and when the Imam leaves his house, seeing that majesty of the Imam, seeing that spirituality of the Imam, seeing the son of the Messenger, the people become so influenced that they engage in weeping and wailing, and Ma'mun begins to fear that his government might come to an end. This is what Imamate is, this is what Wilayah is. This is the status given by Allah, not a position of some sultan that people can control. Rather, Allah Himself manifests His Wilayah, His Imamate, and His Light to the people through His Proof (Hujjah). Pausing here, a thought comes to mind: how fortunate were those people who prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). How fortunate were those people who saw Imam Reza (a.s.) on the day of Eid and got the opportunity to pray behind the Imam. We also, by invoking the intercession of Imam Reza (a.s.), pray to Allah to give us that opportunity, to give us that grace so that we too may pray behind our Imam of the Time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). The journey of Imam Reza (a.s.) that you were just listening to, in reality, that journey was prophesied beforehand, and that prophecy was revealed through a miracle—a miracle that manifested through Imam Reza (a.s.) himself. In this regard, two separate but similar incidents are found. Let's try to present these incidents to you quickly. The first incident is that Abu Habib al-Nibazi states: 'I was once in Jufa. I was in Jufa, I was sleeping, resting there, when I saw the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in a dream.' I saw the Messenger, I went to the Messenger, and the Messenger said to me—what does the Prophet say? 'He said to me, O so-and-so, I am very pleased with the good treatment you show towards my children in this world. I feel great joy, I feel great happiness.' So I submitted to the service of the Messenger, 'If I were to leave them, then with whom would I do good?' Meaning, O Prophet of Allah, if I do not do good to your children, then with whom shall I do it? Then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Certainly, you will receive its reward from me in the hereafter.' And then, near the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), there was a tray containing some dates, some fresh dates. So I requested the Prophet to grant me some of those dates. The Prophet extended a handful, took a few dates in his hand, and gave them to me. When I counted those dates, they were 18 in total. The meaning of the Prophet giving me 18 dates—I interpreted this dream in such a way, since I was seeing a dream, what did this mean? That now 18 years of my life are left in this world. This was the interpretation of that dream. And then I forgot this incident. Then one day, what happened? I saw a large crowd of people. People were gathered in large numbers. I asked those people, 'What is the matter?' The people said, 'Ali ibn Musa al-Reza (a.s.) has arrived.' I saw Imam Reza (a.s.) sitting in the same place where I had seen the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the dream. And in front of the Imam, there was a similar tray, and it also had some fresh dates in it. They were kept there. The Imam took a handful of dates from it into his hand and gave them to me. He handed them to me, and when I counted those dates, they also turned out to be 18 dates. Now what did I do? I submitted to the Imam, 'My Mawla, give me a little more, give me a few more dates.' Upon this, Imam Reza (a.s.) replied, and this incident is the miracle about which I had mentioned to you, that the Imam's journey was prophesied beforehand through a dream. When he said, 'Mawla, give me some more dates,' the Imam said, 'If my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), had given you more than this, I would have given you more too.' This meant that this was the interpretation of that dream, that the 18 dates the Prophet gave, the son of the Prophet gave exactly the same number of dates. This is one incident. The second incident, as Tanveer Bhai was just narrating to you, was that the journey of the Imam (a.s.) from Medina to Merv was via the route of Basra. Now, this is the incident of Basra. The incident of Basra is that there is a man named Ibn-e-Ulwan. Ibn-e-Ulwan says, 'I also saw in a dream that it was as if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had come to Basra.' The Prophet himself had come to Basra. And I am saying, 'The Prophet has come, he has come to Basra, so where is he? At whose house is he staying?' So I was told, 'He is at the house of such-and-such person.' So I immediately went to that person's house. I found the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) there, sitting, and his companions were also sitting with him, and in front of him was a similar tray containing some fresh dates. Faqabaza bi-yadihi kaffan min rutbin. Meaning, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) also did what? He took a handful of dates in his palm and gave them to me, bestowed them upon me, and then I counted those dates and they were 18 dates. And then what happened after that, fa-summa intahaitu, then I woke up from my dream. Fa-tawazza'tu, I performed wudu, wa-sallaitu, I offered prayers, wa-jitu ilal-hayat, and then I went to the same house where I had seen in the dream that the Messenger had come. Fa-araftul-makan, now I recognized the place well, meaning I saw that house, I saw that place, I remembered it, I kept it in my mind as to which house this was where the Prophet had visited. I saw that house. Now fa-ba'da zalik, meaning after that, some days passed, after that I heard one day what happened, sami'tunnas, I heard people saying that qad ja'a Ali ibn-e-Musa Riza (a.s.). That Imam Riza (a.s.) has arrived at the same place. I asked, where is he? So people said, at the house of such-and-such person. Meaning this was the same house that I had seen in the dream and after waking up from the dream, where I had gone and verified that house that yes, this is the same house. So at that very house, Imam Riza (a.s.) had arrived. Fa-mazaitu, I went there, wa-fa-wajadtuhu fil-mauzil-lazi ra'aitu-nnabi sallallahu alaihi wa-alihi. At the same place where I had seen the Prophet sitting in the dream, Imam Riza (a.s.) was also seated there, and in front of him, exactly in the same way, a tray was kept which contained fresh dates. Imam Riza (a.s.) took a handful of dates, handed them to me, and then I counted, they were the same 18 dates. I also asked the same question to Imam Riza (a.s.) that, 'Mawla, please give a little more, if I could get some more dates.' So the Imam said the same thing, that if my grandfather had given you more than this, I would have given you too. And then after that, or a few days later, meaning Imam (a.s.) stayed in Basra for a few days. This narration shows that the Imam stayed in Basra for a few days during that journey. Summa ba'asa ilayya ba'ada ayyamin, meaning after a few days, Imam Riza (a.s.) called for me and yatlubu minni rida'an, a special cloak, there was a special cloak that the Imam requested, bring a special cloak. Wa-zakara tu-lahu wa-arzahu, the Imam (a.s.) did what regarding that cloak, meaning he described its dimensions completely, that it is a cloak of this kind, this long, this wide, the Imam described the whole thing to me. Fa-qultu laisa haza indi. I said, 'No, I do not have such a cloak.' Then the Imam said, 'Go to your house and in such-and-such chest, this kind of cloak is kept which your wife had brought.' So then I remembered, fa-zakartu, now I remembered that thing and then I went, looked, and in that very chest, right there in that same chest, in the exact same place, that cloak was also kept just as Imam Riza (a.s.) had said. Meaning the summary is that the purpose of Mamun in taking the Imamate and Wilayah of Imam Riza (a.s.) towards this second path, through which the Wilayah of the Imam (a.s.) could not be revealed to the people, this Imamate and Wilayah is not, as Tanveer Bhai also submitted before you, a worldly position that some king made him a successor or his minister, so people would know its importance. This is a divine position. This Imamate is a thing bestowed by Allah. Therefore, the one who is the true Imam, his actions, his miracles, his knowledge of the unseen, his power that Allah has bestowed upon him, through that, his light will keep spreading. Wherever the Imam goes, the light of his Imamate will also spread there. Imamate is a divine position. Allah gives this position, this status to His chosen servants. And no matter how much people try, they can neither diminish this position nor can they erase it. Although they think that they will overcome it with their few efforts and will diminish this position. Allah Ta'ala Himself says in the Holy Quran: 'Yuriduna liyutfi'u nurallahi bi-afwahihim wallahu mutimmu nurihi wa-lau karihal-kafirun' (They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it). One incident is found where Mamun held a debate between Imam Riza (a.s.) and a person, so that his assumption was that perhaps that person could defeat the Imam in this debate and the Imam's position would be diminished. We find many such incidents in history where rulers tried many times to diminish the Imam's position, to reduce the Imam's position. But they always had to face defeat. One such debate was held between Imam Riza (a.s.) and a person named Yahya ibn al-Dahhak al-Samarqandi. When Mamun called Imam Riza (a.s.) and Yahya was sitting in front, the Imam said to Yahya, 'O Yahya, ask what you want to ask.' Yahya replied, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, you ask me so that it may be an honor for me to answer you.' The Imam said, 'Alright.' The Imam said, 'O Yahya, what do you say about a person who claims to be truthful and calls the truthful ones liars? Can he himself be truthful or is he a liar?' Look, the question was very simple: what should be said about a person who claims to be truthful and calls the truthful ones liars? Is that person truthful or a liar? Yahya kept thinking for a while but he did not get an answer. Mamun said, 'Yahya, why don't you answer?' Yahya said, 'The Imam has left me speechless.' Then Mamun said to the Imam, 'What is this matter that this Yahya is unable to answer and has confessed his helplessness?' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'If Yahya says that he verified the truthful ones, then Imamate cannot be for a person who confesses his own weakness. Whereas we know about a person who goes to the pulpit of the Messenger and said that I have been made a ruler over you, while there are people present here who are better than me. Whereas it is a very common thing that the one who is the leader of the people, who is the Imam of the people, who is the Caliph of the people, who is the guide of the people, he must be better than the people. And if Yahya says that he verified the truthful ones, then Imamate is not for a person who said that a devil overcomes my head. Whereas this matter is quite clearly evident that the devil has no authority over the Imam.' Rather, the devil himself says that when he said that I will lead all people astray, after that the devil himself says that there will be some sincere servants, some chosen servants whom I will not be able to lead astray. So Imam is not the name of a person upon whom the devil overcomes. And after that, the Imam (a.s.) says that if Yahya says that he verified the truthful ones, then Imamate is not for a person about whom his companion himself said that the Imamate of such-and-such happened suddenly, happened by chance, and Allah saved from his evil, so then whoever does this, you kill him. Hearing this, Mamun shouted at them and all the people dispersed. After that, Mamun said to the people of Banu Abbas who were sitting there, who were among his relatives, 'Did I not tell you not to debate with them, not to argue with them, because their knowledge, meaning the knowledge of Imam Riza (a.s.), is from the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' From this narration, it becomes quite clear that Imamate is a divine position. Imamate is a luminous position and it is not for everyone. It is such a position in which no kind of weakness, ignorance, or deficiency is found, and the devil has no effect on the Imam (a.s.). The Imam is always superior, the Imam is always perfect, the Imam is always on the truth, and he never confesses his incompetence. Rather, the Imam is the one who invites people towards himself by saying that we are the representatives of Allah, we are the proof sent by Allah, we will guide you towards Allah. Imamate can only be attained by one who is perfect, who is infallible, who is on the truth, who has been sent by Allah, whom Allah has chosen, and this position is only and only for the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and his progeny, meaning the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The discussion that has taken place so far, in it we have seen the importance of the Imamate of Imam Riza (a.s.), a few incidents related to it, the debate that was seen, the debate regarding the Imamate, meaning the debate regarding the position of Imamate itself, we have seen that. Now let us move towards an incident in which we try to see what was the fate of the one who denied the Wilayah of Imam Riza (a.s.). As you know, the Wilayah of Imam Riza (a.s.), the beginning of his Imamate, was a period that was a very difficult period for the Shias. In the narrations, very harsh words have been used for the period after the martyrdom of Imam Kazim (a.s.). Harsh means here that the circumstances were very difficult. The term 'fitnatun amya' used in the narration, 'fitnatun amya' means a blinding sedition. Meaning, a person will not understand anything, will not see anything, whether what is right or wrong, he will not see any right path. It was a period full of severe trials. And why was it? See, the martyrdom of Imam Kazim (a.s.) took place in Baghdad. At that time, Imam Riza (a.s.) was not present there with him. In that era, such a sedition arose which was known as the 'Fitna-e-Waqifiyya'. This Waqifiyya was a group. Waqifiyya is called those who stopped. 'Waqf' or 'Waqfa' means to stop, to pause. Those people who stopped at the Wilayah of Imam Kazim (a.s.), stopped at his Imamate, did not move forward from there. Meaning, they stopped at the seventh Imam, those people, they stood still. They did not believe in the Imamate of the eighth Imam, meaning Imam Riza (a.s.), and refused to accept it. The followers of Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) used to come to him. They would deposit Khums money with him. He would collect religious dues from the people and was responsible for delivering them to Imam al-Kazim (a.s.). This was Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini. He held religious funds, including Khums money, which he was supposed to deliver to the Imam. It is recorded in traditions that when the martyrdom of Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) occurred, this Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini had 30,000 dinars—a dinar refers to a gold coin—of religious funds in his possession. That is, he had 30,000 dinars of Khums money. Now, greed for those 30,000 dinars entered his heart. What did he do out of greed for those 30,000 dinars? If he had accepted the Imamate and Wilayah of Imam al-Rida (a.s.), what would he have had to do? He would have had to hand over all 30,000 dinars to Imam al-Rida (a.s.). He thought the only way to keep this money for himself was to deny the Wilayah of Imam al-Rida (a.s.). He denied the Imam's Wilayah and Imamate and kept all the Khums money for himself. This was Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini, and he was the leader of the Waqifi sect. This sect later vanished. Today, thank God, this sect does not exist, and this belief does not exist. When this Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini passed away, when he departed from this world, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) was in Marw. That is, he was in Marw, a province of Khorasan. There, he summoned one of his companions, Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha. Imam (a.s.) spoke to Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha—this is Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha's own account. He narrates: 'My master, Rida (a.s.), called me to Marw and said, "O Hasan, what happened to Ali ibn Abi Hamza al-Bata'ini today?" O Hasan, Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini passed away today. His death occurred today. That is, where is the Imam? The Imam is in Marw. Where is Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini? He is in Iraq. They are in different countries, but what does the Imam (a.s.) say? "Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini passed away today. And he was placed in his grave at this very hour." That is, he has been buried at this very moment. And Munkar and Nakir have entered his grave. "And the angel of the grave entered upon him and began questioning him." Munkar and Nakir are questioning him. They asked him, "Who is your Lord?" So Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini said, "Allah." He answered them that Allah is my Lord. Then they asked, "Who is your Prophet?" He said, "Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)." Then the question was asked, "Who is your Wali?" He said, "Ali ibn Abi Talib." "Who is your Imam? Who is your Wali?" Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini is answering the angels in the grave. "Ali ibn Abi Talib is my Imam, my Wali." Then who after him? He said, "Imam al-Hasan (a.s.)." After him? He said, "Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)." Then who? He said, "Ali ibn al-Husayn," meaning Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.). Then who is your Wali? The angels kept asking, and he kept answering. He said, "Muhammad ibn Ali," meaning Imam al-Baqir (a.s.). He said, "Then who?" He said, "Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)." After him who? He said, "Musa ibn Ja'far," meaning Imam al-Kazim (a.s.). Then Munkar and Nakir asked him, "Then who?" After Imam al-Kazim (a.s.), who is your Wali? The phrase in the tradition is, "He began to stutter." His tongue began to stumble, he began to stammer, unable to answer who his Imam is after Imam al-Kazim (a.s.). "He was rebuked," the tradition says, "and they asked him, 'Then who?'" The angels insisted and asked him again, "After Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Kazim (a.s.), who is your Imam?" The tradition says, "He fell silent." The Imam says, "He fell silent," he became quiet. He is unable to give any answer at all. Because he had denied the Wilayah of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) in the world, he cannot utter his name in the grave. His tongue is stumbling. He is stammering, unable to say anything. Those angels said, "Did Musa ibn Ja'far command you to remain silent? Is this what he commanded you? Did he tell you there is no Imam after him?" The meaning of the tradition is that the angels' questioning implies this. But he could not say anything, he could not answer. After that, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) says that those angels, Munkar and Nakir, struck him with such a rod of fire that his entire grave became filled with fire. That is, his grave was filled with fire, and how long will this last? How long will this fire remain in his grave? How long is this punishment for him? "Until the Day of Judgment." He will face this same punishment until the Day of Judgment. This punishment will be upon him inside the grave because he refused to accept the Imamate of his Imam of the time, Imam al-Rida (a.s.). Now, Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha says that Imam al-Rida (a.s.) narrated this entire event to me. He narrated it, and then I left from the presence of my master, I mean Imam al-Rida (a.s.), I went out from there. And I recorded that day, but I did one thing. I noted down the day and date when Imam al-Rida (a.s.) narrated this event to me regarding when Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini passed away. I noted down that day. A few days passed, and some letters arrived from the people of Kufa, and in those letters, the news of Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini's death was given, stating that on such and such a day, Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini passed away. I took their letters and checked them against the date Imam al-Rida (a.s.) had stated. And that he was placed in his grave at that very hour—regarding all the things they had written, that is, the date written in the Kufan letters about when Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini passed away, it was exactly the same date I had noted down that day. That is, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) had described in complete detail what the fate of his opponent would be in the grave, what the fate of one who denies the Imamate would be in the grave. In other words, if one were to say that by denying the Wilayah and Imamate of Imam al-Rida (a.s.)—even though such a person had reached the father correctly and had acknowledged the Imamate of his father—because he denied the Imam of his own time, Imam al-Rida (a.s.), all the service he had rendered to his father became void, and he too became deserving of Hell. This means that Allah is not pleased just by using the title 'Radi Allahu' (May Allah be pleased with him). Unless a person is pleased with the Wilayah of Imam al-Rida (a.s.), unless a person is pleased with his Imamate and accepts it, Allah will not be pleased with that person. This is the importance of the recognition of the Imam of the time, of knowing the Imam of the time. Therefore, we pray to the Almighty God that He grants us the success to attain the recognition of our Imam of the time, Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.s.), until our last breath. Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. We are grateful to the brothers who presented a very Wilayah-filled and knowledge-filled discussion regarding Imam al-Rida (a.s.). Some of its important points were: Hadith al-Silsilat al-Dhahab, in which one of the important conditions for safety from punishment is the Wilayah of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) himself. After that, we saw the journey of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) from Medina to Khorasan. Then, how the knowledge and status of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) are part of the Divine system. After that, a debate of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) regarding Imamate, and finally, the story of Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata'ini, who had denied the Wilayah of the Imam (a.s.), and we saw what punishment he received in the grave. And dear ones, the discussion regarding the Wilayah of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) is such a deep ocean that it is impossible to encompass it in words. But if it is to be stated briefly, an excellent means for this is this Salawat upon Imam al-Rida (a.s.). Let us conclude our discussion today with this Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, alladhi irtadaytahu wa radita bihi man shi'ta min khalqik. O Lord, send blessings upon Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, whom You have chosen and through whom You are pleased with whomever You wish among Your creation. Allahumma wa kama ja'altahu hujjatan ala khalqik, wa qa'iman bi-amrik, wa nasiran li-dinik, wa shahidan ala ibadik. O Allah, just as You made him a proof (Hujjah) over Your creation, one who establishes Your command, a helper and supporter of Your religion, And appointed him a witness over Your servants. Wa kama nasaha lahum fi sirri wa alaniyah, wa da'a ila sabilika bil-hikmati wa maw'izatil hasanah. And just as he advised them in secret and in public, and invited them to Your path with wisdom and beautiful preaching. Fa salli alayhi afdala ma sallayta ala ahadin min awliya'ika wa khiyaratika min khalqik, innaka jawadun karim. Then send upon him the best blessings You have sent upon any of Your Awliya and Your chosen ones from Your creation. Indeed, You are generous and noble. With this, we conclude our discussion, and dear viewers, the timer on your screen—as soon as this timer stops, the quiz link will be closed. And now, let us move towards the Ziyarat, and immediately after the Ziyarat, our lucky draw winners will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad. [Arabic text of Ziyarat omitted for brevity as per instructions to translate segments]. I seek refuge in Allah, by the honor of the pure ancestors and the chosen righteous descendants, if not for the distance that has separated me from you, the distance that has separated me from your abode, I would have fulfilled some of your obligatory rights by visiting your shrine. Peace be upon you, O protectors of the religion, children of the Prophet, masters of the creatures, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their relief. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and may Allah bless you, O Wali of the Age, help us and do not destroy us. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. First of all, once again, we offer our congratulations to all of you on the occasion of the birth of Imam Rida (a.s.). We are very grateful to you for participating in this grand quiz related to the luminous words and the luminous life of Anwar-e-Raza (a.s.), i.e., Imam Reza (a.s.). We hope you all enjoyed today's discussion and that this conversation regarding the recognition (Ma'rifat) and Wilayah of Imam Reza (a.s.) has proven beneficial, Insha'Allah. Now the time has come to announce the lucky draw winners of the Anwar-e-Raza (a.s.) Grand Quiz 2026. So, let us proceed towards the announcement of today's grand quiz lucky draw winners, which is being done through our computerized lucky draw system. First, the names of our 12 fourth-prize winners are appearing on our screen, who will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees, and those names are here on your screen. Nargis Abdul Lalani from Mahuva. Tasneem Fatima from Bengaluru. Mehdi Raza Haryani from Mahuva. Mehdi Haryani from Thane. Kumail Khund from Palitana. Many congratulations to all you winners. Now let's see our three third-prize winners who will receive a prize of 3000 Indian Rupees, and those names are here on your screen: Mehrin Mase from France, Zeenat Poonawala from Mumbai. Grand Quiz 2026, who will receive a prize of 7000 Indian Rupees, and their name is here on your screen: Sakina Hashmi from Bengaluru. Many congratulations to you and all our winners. We thank all of you once again. We pray in the court of the Almighty that the Heir of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the Imam of our time, hastens his reappearance and grants us the ability to hold firmly onto the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) until the very end. And whoever shares our videos with others, may they also be counted among those who propagate the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Ameen Ya Rabbal Alameen. Insha'Allah, we will meet again in our upcoming quiz. Until then, Khuda Hafiz. Iltimas-e-Dua, Ya Ali Madad.

title: Maut Ko Yaad Karna | Remembering Death | Kalaam e Noor # 12
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound Islamic teaching that remembering death is a mark of true wisdom. By reflecting on the inevitability of the afterlife, a believer can better prioritize their spiritual goals and moral conduct in this world. The session emphasizes that constant awareness of mortality serves as a catalyst for piety and detachment from worldly distractions.
content:
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'The wisest of people is the one who remembers death the most.'
The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) identified the remembrance of death as the hallmark of the wisest individuals.
Reflecting on mortality helps believers maintain a balanced perspective on worldly life.
Constant awareness of death encourages a focus on eternal success over temporary pleasures.
Remembering the end of life acts as a spiritual deterrent against sins and negligence.
True wisdom in Islam is measured by one's preparedness for the afterlife.

title: Benefits of Reciting Dua e Ahad
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual significance of daily supplications dedicated to the Imam of the Time (aj). The speaker highlights the importance of adding 'wa ajjil farajahum' to Salawat and details the profound benefits of reciting Dua-e-Ahad for forty consecutive days. The talk concludes by explaining the powerful request within the Dua to be resurrected to serve as a helper for Imam Mahdi upon his reappearance.
content:
Various supplications have been introduced. One is simply this: when you send Salawat, 'Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad', then in every Salawat, add 'wa ajjil farajahum'. Yes, 'wa ajjil farajahum'. And hasten the relief (faraj) of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, hasten their reappearance, their coming. 'Wa lan ada-ahum' (and curse their enemies). So whenever you send Salawat, make sure to keep these two phrases, these two sentences in mind. Do not be shy about it. These are very powerful supplications and phrases. Understand their importance, understand their significance. Then, apart from that, there is the Dua-e-Ahad, which should be recited every morning. It is found in the traditions that whoever recites Dua-e-Ahad continuously for 40 days will not leave this world without having the Ziyarat (vision) of the Imam. And if he dies before the reappearance (Zuhur), he will be raised from his grave after the reappearance so that he may be counted among the helpers and supporters of the Imam, among his assistants. His name will be among the helpers because he used to remember his Imam every day, every morning. And one of the phrases of this Dua is exactly this: 'Allahumma in hala bayni wa baynahul mawt' - O Allah, if death stands between me and him, if death comes, yes, if I die, if I die before his reappearance. 'Allahumma in hala bayni wa baynahul mawt' - what kind of death? 'Alladhi ja'altahu 'ala 'ibadika hatman maqdiyya' - the death that You have decreed as inevitable and mandatory for Your servants. Everyone has to die. Everyone has to die; no one is going to live in this world forever. 'Fa-akhrijni min qabri mu'taziran kafani shahiran sayfi mujarradan qanati' - raise me from my grave, raise me from the grave. 'Mu'taziran kafani' - wearing my shroud, in that same state with the shroud. 'Shahiran sayfi' - and in my hand should be his sword, a naked sword. 'Shahiran mujarradan qanati' - and along with it a spear, a ready spear. 'Mujarradan qanati mulabbiyan da'watal da'i fil hadiri wal badi' - and when my Imam calls me, I should say 'Labbayk' (I am here) to his invitation, wherever I am, whether I am in the cities or in the wilderness, wherever I am or wherever my Imam calls me, I should immediately say 'Labbayk' to his voice. 'Labbayk ya Sahib al-Zaman, Labbayk ya Sahib al-Zaman, Labbayk ya Mahdi'. This spirit of 'Labbayk' should be there.
Always include 'wa ajjil farajahum' when reciting Salawat.
Reciting Dua-e-Ahad for 40 consecutive mornings ensures a vision of the Imam.
Those who recite Dua-e-Ahad will be resurrected to assist the Imam if they die before his reappearance.
The Dua expresses a sincere desire to be among the active supporters of the Imam.
The phrase 'Labbayk' signifies a constant state of readiness to answer the Imam's call.
Death is inevitable, but the spiritual connection to the Imam transcends the grave.
The supplication asks to be raised from the grave ready for battle in the service of the Imam.

title: EP07 | Har Ek Ko Uske Imam Ke Saath Bulaaya Jaayega | ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological concept of the Imam as a divinely appointed guide and the ultimate connection between humanity and Allah. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, individuals will be resurrected alongside the leader they followed, highlighting the critical importance of discerning true, infallible leadership from false guidance. The session further outlines the necessity of infallibility in an Imam and provides a methodology for believers to identify the true path through objective study and innate spiritual recognition.
content:
Haydar, Haydar... [repeated]. I bear witness that Ali is the Wali of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their relief and curse all their enemies. O Allah, be for Your guardian, the Proof, son of al-Hasan—may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers—in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and enjoy him therein for a long time. Now then, Allah (Tabarak wa Ta'ala) has said in the Glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: “The day We will call every people with their Imam.” Allah (Tabarak wa Ta'ala) says in the Quran-e-Majeed that on the Day of Judgment, We will call every nation, every group of people, with their Imam. Before beginning the discussion, as I requested, if you have any questions regarding Imamate or these lectures, please do ask. Whether you send them in written form to these mobile numbers, or via audio or video. So, anyway, this is the question before you now. And the question is, as I said in the previous lecture, regarding the Quranic verse: “You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.” In the context of this verse, the Prophet said, “I am the warner, and you, O Ali, are the guide.” So if only Ali is the guide, then what about the other 11 Imams? See, this is a good question; the listener has asked well. But this was one tradition in the context of this verse. This was one tradition; there are others as well. For instance, in Al-Kafi, there is a tradition where a narrator asked Imam Sadiq (a.s.), Fudayl ibn Yasar asked about this verse: “And for every people there is a guide.” The Imam replied, “Every Imam is a guide for the generation in which he lives.” Every Imam—meaning the remaining 11 Imams, a total of 12 Imams—is a guide for the generation in which he is living. This tradition exists, and similarly, there are subsequent traditions where Imam Baqir (a.s.) said in the context of this verse that the Messenger of Allah is the warner, and among us, the Ahlulbayt, there is an Imam in every era who guides people to what the Messenger of Allah brought. What the Messenger of Allah brought—among all things—is the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). And then, one guide after another, “Then the guides after him,” one after another. That is, Ali (a.s.), then the successors (Awsia), the successors of the Prophet, all one after another. So this is not just for Ali (a.s.) but for all the Masumin, meaning the 12 Imams (a.s.). So, Insha'Allah, this answer is clear. That was just one Hadith read, but it was a good question, and you should ask more questions like this, Insha'Allah. This will encourage us that yes, people are listening and asking questions. Anyway, “A good question is half the answer.” So, the verse I recited before you, “The day We will call every people with their Imam,” Allah is saying this. This is a verse from Surah Bani Isra'il, verse number 71. Surah number 17, verse number 71. Meaning, on the Day of Judgment, We will resurrect everyone, every individual, with their Imam. That is, the one whom they considered their Imam in this world. Now, look at the tradition in this context, and reflect on it. Imam Ja'far Sadiq (a.s.) says, “When the Day of Judgment comes...” (the Hadith is long, so I am shortening it). “Then a call will come from Allah (Jalla Jalaluhu).” Allah (Jalla Jalaluhu) will make a call on the Day of Judgment. “Beware! Whoever followed an Imam in the worldly life, let him follow him to wherever he leads him.” So, whoever followed an Imam in the world, he should now—on the Day of Judgment—follow his Imam wherever he leads him. Now, if that Imam is not appointed by Allah (Mansus min Allah)—meaning Allah did not appoint him, he is an Imam created by people—then no one knows whether he is of the people of Paradise or the people of Hell. And what his end will be? Everyone knows what the end will be. So the Quran then recites two verses that when it is said, “Go,” people will follow whom? The hellish Imams whom they followed in the world. That is, if they follow any Imam other than these 12 Imams, any other leader, they will follow him into Hell. The Imam derives this from these verses. “At that time, those who were followed will disown those who followed them.” Now, reflect on the verse: those who were followed will express their disavowal, meaning they will say, “Go, run away.” Meaning, those who were Imams in this world, who were calling themselves the successors of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in this world, they will say, 'Run away from here, run away from us.' Tabarra'a minalladhina-ttaba'u. From whom will they say to go away? They will express disassociation (Bara'ah), they will perform Tabarra from whom? They will say it to those who were following them, who were adhering to them. Wa ra'awul-'adhab. And they will see the punishment. Wa taqatta'at bihimul-asbab. And all means will be severed for them. So, when those who were here, who were sitting on high positions, when they see this situation on the Day of Judgment, they will tell their followers, 'Run away, because of you we are in even more trouble.' So the Quran gives their answer in another verse. The Quran says, Wa qala-lladhina-ttaba'u. Now those who were following them will say, Law anna lana karratan. If only we could be returned—meaning they are wishing in the Hereafter to return to the world, but they will not be brought back, they will not be brought back. If we were brought back to the world, fanatabarra'a minhum kama tabarra'u minna, then we would also express disassociation from them just as they are expressing disassociation from us today. These are verses of the Quran, yes. They are expressing disassociation, they are distancing themselves from us. We would also do the same to them if we were returned. So brother, do not wait for the Hereafter, perform Tabarra now. Understand who is from Allah and who is not from Allah. Whom did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) make his successor, and whom did he not? Kadhalika yurihimullahu a'malahum hasaratin 'alayhim. And in this way, Allah will show them their deeds, which will be a cause of regret and remorse for them. They will regret, those people will repent. Wa ma hum bi-kharijina minan-nar. But now they will not be taken out of Hell. They will not be taken out of Hell; they have to remain in Hell forever. Look, a person should be very cautious. This is a matter of religion. You see whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed in his lifetime; Insha'Allah, we will discuss the details of that. Right now, we are discussing general Imamate. Insha'Allah, when the discussion proceeds... If Allah grants the ability, when the discussion reaches the stage of who the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) appointed as his successor after him, then the matter will be completely clear. Just stay connected. So, Imam Hussain (a.s.) was asked, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me about the saying of Allah Azza wa Jalla: "The day We will call every people with their Imam."' O Son of the Messenger, please explain this verse, that on the Day of Judgment, everyone will be called with their Imam. So, Sayyid al-Shuhada Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'Imamun da'a ila hudan fa-ajabu-hu ilayh.' There will be one group whose Imam will be the one whom Allah has appointed—meaning from the twelve Imams. And of course, the Prophets who came before, who were on the truth, meaning the Prophets whom Allah sent and their successors. 'Fa-ajabu-hu ilayh,' so their nation, those who are following them, they will say 'Labbayk' to their invitation. They will follow them, they will adhere to them. So on one side, there will be these people, and on the other side, there will be another group. Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, 'Wa imamun da'a ila dalatin,' and the Imam who is inviting people towards misguidance in this world, who is claiming falsely that I am the successor of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) while the Messenger of Allah did not make him so. He has been made or became so through different ways. 'Fa-ajabu-ha,' so now when they see, 'Okay, these are our Imams, let's follow them.' Now what will be the result? 'Ha'ula'i fil-jannati wa ha'ula'i fin-nar.' Those who followed the true Imam will go to Paradise with their Imam, and those who followed the false Imam will go to Hell with them. 'Wa huwa qawluhu Azza wa Jalla,' and Imam Hussain (a.s.) takes support from this noble verse, 'Fariqun fil-jannati wa fariqun fis-sa'ir.' This is a verse from Surah Ash-Shura, that one group will go to Paradise and one group will go to Hell. So it is absolutely clear, absolutely clear that they will be called. And in this regard, the son of Sayyid al-Shuhada, Zain al-Abidin, Sayyid al-Sajidin Imam Zain al-Abidin (a.s.) says, 'Allahumma innaka ayyatta...' Pay attention to this Hadith; this is a supplication from Sahifa-e-Sajjadiyya which is recited on the day of Arafah. 'O Allah, You have supported Your religion in every era.' You have assisted Your religion, You have helped Your religion. 'Fi kulli awanin,' meaning in every era. Meaning, no era has passed from Prophet Adam (a.s.) until the Day of Judgment when Allah does not support His religion. Remember this, Allah always supports His religion. 'Fi kulli awanin bi-imamin,' through whom does He support it? Through an Imam. He supports it through an Imam, assists it, supports the religion. 'Aqamtahu 'ala man li-'ibadik,' You established this Imam for Your servants. 'Wa manaran fi biladik,' and this Imam is a lighthouse, a minaret in Your lands. Meaning, a place of light. This is that light towards which people, meaning the believers, turn. 'Ba'da an wasalta hablahu bi-hablika,' when You connected his rope with Your rope. The rope of Allah and the rope of the Imam became one. Meaning, this is one rope, a connection, a union. Both, this is a strong connection. That is why it is called the strong rope, which is called 'Strong Rope' in English. The Imam is this very strong rope; the Imam is this very strong rope. 'Wa ja'altahu-dh-dhari'ata ila ridwanik,' and You made this Imam a means, a medium for Your pleasure and Your satisfaction, for Your Ridwan. This is also taken from the Quranic verse, 'Ridwanum minallahi akbar,' the pleasure of Allah, the pleasure of Allah is the greatest thing. 'Wa-ftaradta ta'atahu,' and You made the obedience of this Imam obligatory. This is the proof of Infallibility (Ismah), Insha'Allah, the discussion on that will come. It is the proof of Ismah. Meaning, the Imam should be such that people follow him with the certainty that this Imam cannot make a mistake. He can never be the leader and Imam of the people who goes in his first sermon and says, 'A devil has overcome me. Therefore, if I do right, follow me, and if I do wrong, then correct me.' The one who is in need of the nation's correction cannot be the Imam of the nation. He becomes the one being led (Ma'mum), he cannot be the Imam. 'Wa hazzarta ma'siyatahu,' and You warned people never to disobey this Imam. In every situation, there must be obedience to the Imam. In every situation. But the Muslim Ummah did not act upon the advice of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). They did not act upon the injunctions of the Quran. Sayyid al-Sajidin (a.s.) says, 'Wa amarta bi-imtisali awamirihi,' and You commanded that they should obey his commands. When he commands something, obey it. 'Wal-intiha'i 'inda nahyihi,' and when the Imam forbids something, then stop, abstain, avoid it, keep away from it. When the Imam stops or prohibits something, then stop from it. 'Wa alla yat-qaddamahu mutaqaddimun,' and that no person should try to go ahead of the Imam. Do not try to advance yourself before the Imam, do not try to bring your turn first. 'Wa la yata-akhkhara 'anhu muta-akhkhirun,' and no one should stay behind. Look, in both cases, meaning if someone goes ahead or stays behind, in both cases there is destruction. In both cases, a person will be annihilated. Why? 'Fahuwa 'ismatulladhina,' the Imam is the sanctuary in which people take refuge. The Imam is a sanctuary. Meaning, all creation takes refuge in the Imam. 'Wa kahful-mu'minin,' the Imam is a refuge, a shelter, a sanctuary for the believers. 'Wa urwatul-mutamassikin,' and those who hold fast to the rope of Allah, the Imam is that rope. The 'Mutamassikin' are those who perform 'Tamassuk'. We have already mentioned the meaning of the word 'Tamassuk' in your presence, that what does 'Tamassuk' mean? To hold firmly. As if the basis of salvation depends on this. Meaning, salvation is only in this, that a person holds the Imam firmly. 'Wa baha'ul-'alamin,' and the Imam is the cause of splendor and light for the entire universe. The Imam is that light that has illuminated the assembly of existence. The one who illuminates the entire universe is the Imam. This is the Imam. This is the importance of the Imam. Therefore, it is the responsibility of all of us that we should choose our Imam with great caution in our religion and not follow someone's words, but rather study ourselves. Establish your belief on this study so that the matter is completely clear as to who is on the truth and who is on falsehood. Who are those holy personalities whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appointed after him? And there is an easy way for this. A very easy way. Look, I will state a very easy way in your presence on how to distinguish between truth and falsehood. How can a person understand, because it is generally a very difficult task, right? Generally, how can a person understand? Because if you tell them, there are many objections to it. They say, 'Oh, we saw our parents doing this work. Oh, the majority is doing this. Oh, society is doing this.' So look, do not look at anyone. You only look at yourself and look at your God. That's it. And how to know that? Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) says in a sermon in Nahj al-Balagha, 'Look, you cannot attain the recognition of guidance until you understand the right path and guidance, you cannot recognize it until you recognize those who have abandoned guidance.' What does this mean? It means that if you want to know who is on the truth and who is on falsehood, then on any subject—whether it is Tawheed (Monotheism), Adl (Justice), Nubuwwah (Prophethood), Imamah, or Ma'ad (Resurrection)—look at what the Aimma-e-Masumeen (a.s.) from the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) have said. Read their teachings and then compare them with others who have not held fast (tamussuk) to the progeny of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Look at them, and you will know immediately. Just ensure there is no bias, no prejudice, no bigotry. With justice—complete justice—pray to Allah, saying, 'O Lord, I am going to read these two groups of traditions; guide me. Lead me.' Just pray to Allah and then start reading the hadith. Take any one subject—we are not saying you must read all subjects—compare the two, and you will see who is right and who is wrong. And after that, if any question comes to your mind, then ask. That is why there is a very famous tradition: 'I'rifu Allaha billah' (Recognize Allah through Allah), 'wa ar-rasula bir-risalah' (and recognize the Messenger through his message). Recognize the Messenger. For instance, if someone comes and claims to be a Messenger—see, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is the last Prophet, that is our belief—but suppose tomorrow someone stands up and claims to be a Messenger or a Prophet, how do you know if he is right or wrong? You will recognize him through his message, through his teachings. You will immediately see whether his teachings are in accordance with your fitrah (innate nature) or not. Just read and then compare. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin, wa sallallahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi at-tayyibina at-tahirin.
