title: EP01 | Hujjat-e-Khuda Ki Zaroorat |  ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of Imamate and the concept of Itmam-e-Hujjat, or the completion of divine proof. It addresses historical controversies surrounding the Prophet Muhammad's succession, refuting claims that he left no formal successor. By analyzing foundational traditions like Hadith-e-Saqalain, the lecture establishes the divine appointment of the Ahlul-Bayt as the essential guides for the Muslim Ummah. The series aims to provide clear, evidence-based arguments to ensure the truth is conveyed, leaving no room for ignorance regarding the path of the Imams.
content:
TSR presents. Ashhadu anna Aliyan Waliullah. This is the bond that is at the threshold of the Throne of God. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Sallallahu alaika ya Wali-al-Asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. On the 28th of Safar, 11 Hijri, when the first and most superior creation of Allah, Hazrat-e-Rasoolullah (s.a.w.a.), after 23 years of propagation, after showing the servants of God the path of servitude to God, after turning man living in the darkness of ignorance into a human through guidance, bid farewell to this transient world, his shroud had not even turned dusty when the Muslim Ummah became so divided and such differences emerged that from that day until today, and until the Day of Judgment, Muslims were divided into various sects. The single topic that created an irreparable rift among Muslims was the issue of the succession of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), his Caliphate, and the Imamate of the Ummah after him. On one side are the Sunni brethren, who believe that the Prophet, who struggled greatly, endured hardships and difficulties to convey the true religion of Allah to the people, left the world without appointing a successor or Caliph, without showing the Ummah the path to avoid misguidance, and without entrusting his followers, companions, and his Ummah to any Imam until the Day of Judgment, leaving the Ummah to wander alone. On the other side, we, the Shia-e-Imamiya, believe in the doctrine of the 12 Imams after the Prophet, whose introduction was given by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) himself during his lifetime, and which is based on numerous verses of the Holy Quran and authentic, reliable, and continuous (Mutawatir) Hadiths of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Those 12 Imams whose names were stated by the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) during his lifetime, and it was also stated that all 12 Imams would be from the Ahlulbayt of the Prophet. Among whom the first would be Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and the last would be Hazrat-e-Imam-e-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). After completing the first and last Hajj of his apparent life, when the verse of 'Tabligh' was revealed by the command of God at the plain of Ghadir-e-Khumm, by announcing the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) in front of a gathering of 125,000 pilgrims, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made it clear that Ali (a.s.) becoming the Caliph and Imam after him is the choice of Allah. And after this announcement, by revealing the third verse of Surah Al-Ma'idah, Allah Almighty made it clear that today I have perfected the religion and completed My blessings. Meaning, the becoming of Amir-ul-Momineen Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) as the Caliph and Imam after the Prophet was not just a choice of the Hujjat (Proof), but an 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' (Completion of Proof) from Allah the Almighty. And that is why the TSR team has come before you with its new video series, titled 'Itmam-e-Hujjat'. Meaning, the proof after which there is no need for any debate, any argument, or any discussion. In this series, we will try to see in the light of the verses of the Holy Quran and the Hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) what the Shia perspective is on this doctrine of Imamate. Why do we, the Shia-e-Ithna-Ashari, consider this doctrine so important? So that for all those who are deniers of this Imamate of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), these verses and Hadiths may be an 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' for them, after which no further proof is needed. So, let us begin our first episode today, titled 'The Need for the Proof of God (Hujjat-e-Khuda)', on which the orator of the Ahlulbayt, Dr. Shabib Rizvi, will speak further. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the God-fearing and the certain, and blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul-Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-wa-ali-Muhammad-wa-ajjil-farajahum. Sallallahu alaihi wa alihil-ma'sumeen, alladhina adhhaba-llahu anhumur-rijsa wa tahharahum tathira, Allahumma salli. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hassan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You settle him on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. Allahumma ja'alna min ansarihi wa-awanih. Rabbi salli ala Muhammad-wa-ali-Muhammad-wa-ajjil-farajahum-wal'an-aada-hum ajma'een. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said: 'I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahlulbayt. If you hold onto them both, you will never go astray after me. They will not separate from each other until they return to me at the Pond (Hawd).' This is a very famous and well-known Hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), which is called Hadith-e-Saqalain, and this Hadith is Mutawatir (continuous) in both sects, i.e., among the Sunnis and the Shias, it has been narrated with Tawatir, both in the general and specific sources. And in this famous Hadith, the Prophet says that I am leaving behind two weighty things among you. 'Saqal' means weighty/precious. And what are these two things? 'Kitabullah' - one is the Book of Allah, i.e., the Holy Quran, 'wa Ahl-e-Bayti' - and my Ahlulbayt. 'Ma in tamassaktum bihima' - if you hold onto these two firmly, 'lan tadillu ba'di abada' - then you will never go astray after me, never go astray after me. 'Fa innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida alayyal-hawd' - because these two will not separate from each other until they come to me at the Hawd-e-Kawthar, until they arrive at me. It is a famous and well-known Hadith and it is Mutawatir. There is so much Tawatir in this that about 24 companions narrated it. Now look, we are mentioning the names of a few companions, we are presenting them in your service, very quickly, this is not our topic, this is just being presented as an introduction. We are taking 10 names so that everyone is satisfied according to their taste, so that no one says we didn't mention their person, so according to every taste, Zayd ibn Arqam, we are giving one example, it is narrated by Zayd ibn Arqam and it is in how many books, it is in Sunan an-Nasa'i, in Tabarani's Mu'jam al-Kabir, in Sunan at-Tirmidhi, in Al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn by Hakim al-Nishapuri, in Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal and many other books. It is narrated only by Zayd ibn Arqam. Then it is from Zayd ibn Thabit, in Musnad Ahmad and Mu'jam al-Kabir, and then after that, it is from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Master of the Universe himself, Amir-ul-Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), from Abu Dharr al-Ghiffari, from Abu Hurairah, from Abdullah ibn Hantaf, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, so many companions, we are just taking the names of 10 companions in your service, look, these are the names of the companions. Meaning, at least here you should show respect to the Sahaba; if the Sahaba narrated it, then the Hadith must be authentic. So, this Hadith is authentic, and not only is it authentic, but it is also Mutawatir (widely transmitted). It possesses Tawatir, specifically Tawatir-e-Ma'nawi, meaning in terms of its meaning and conceptual consecutiveness, and it also possesses Tawatir in terms of its chain of narration (Sanad). All scholars have recorded it, and InshaAllah, when we discuss this in detail, we will present it to you. If anyone wants to check, they can refer to the book 'Istijdaab-o-Irtiqa-al-Ghurf' by Shamsuddin al-Sakhawi. He has recorded everything on page 23. And 'Al-Isaba' by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, volume 7, from page 245 to 274, he has discussed only the Hadith al-Thaqalayn. So, this was the first point I wanted to present to you, and the second point is that this series is titled 'Itmam-e-Hujjat' (Completion of the Argument). That is, to complete the argument, to perfect the proof, so that after this—meaning after listening to this entire series—no one can say, 'I didn't know what the truth was, I didn't know what the reality was.' And that is why, in our Usul al-Kafi, there is a narration in 'Babul-Istid'af' that a Mustad'af (oppressed/weakened person) is only the one who is not familiar with the differences among people. A Mustad'af is someone who is not aware of the differences among people, meaning he does not know why there is a difference among people and what the reason for this difference is; he is unaware. But if he knows, and he has come to know what is truth and what is falsehood, then... For him, there is no excuse (Hujjat); meaning on the Day of Judgment, he cannot present any argument before Allah, he cannot present any excuse that 'I did not know.' As it is stated in Surah An-Nisa, verse 165: 'Rusulan mubashireena wa mundhireen' (Messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners). We sent messengers, Allah says, we sent messengers. Why did we send them? 'Li-alla yakuna linnasi 'ala Allahi hujjatun ba'da al-rusul' (So that there would be no argument for the people against Allah after the messengers), so that after the coming of the messengers, no argument remains against the people, so that no one can say, 'We did not know.' And the Quran has also clarified this in Surah Taha, verse 134, where Allah Almighty says: 'Wa law anna ahlaknahum bi-'adhabin min qablihi' (And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it [the messenger]), if we had destroyed them without explaining, without sending prophets, without sending messengers, if we had sent a punishment upon them, they would have said: 'Rabbana lawla arsalta ilayna rasulan' (Our Lord, why did You not send a messenger to us), 'fanattabi'a ayatika' (so that we could follow Your verses), we would have followed Your verses, Your signs, we would have followed them, 'min qabli an nadhilla wa nakhza' (before we were humiliated and disgraced). Meaning, before this humiliation and disgrace, they will face humiliation and disgrace on the Day of Judgment. Those who know what the truth is and yet do not follow the truth, they will be humiliated and disgraced on the Day of Judgment. These are the words of the Quran: 'Min qabli an nadhilla wa nakhza' (Before we are humiliated and disgraced). This is a Quranic verse regarding the completion of the argument. Similarly, if you take the support of a Hadith, then the Master of the Universe, Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), says in the first sermon of Nahj al-Balagha: 'Faba'atha fihim rusulahu' (So He sent His messengers among them), 'wa watara ilayhim anbiya'ahu' (and sent His prophets to them one after another), 'liyastadduhum mithaqa fitratihi' (so that they might demand from them the fulfillment of the covenant of His nature), the covenant that was taken from them when He created them, so that they might demand the fulfillment of that covenant. Means to seek the fulfillment of the covenant. To demand that fulfillment, that 'you made this promise, now fulfill it.' 'Liyastadduhum mithaqa fitratihi', 'wa yudhakkiruhum mansiyya ni'matihi' (and remind them of His forgotten blessings). InshaAllah, the details of this will come later. 'Mansiyya ni'matihi', the blessings they forgot. 'Wa yahtajju 'alayhim bil-tabligh' (And complete the argument against them by conveying the message). 'Wa yahtajju 'alayhim bil-tabligh'. Now the argument is complete; now no one can say, 'We didn't know, we weren't aware.' 'Wa yuthiru lahum dafa'in al-'uqul' (And bring forth for them the treasures of intellect), and bring out the treasures of intellect that exist within their being, so that they can use their intellects. InshaAllah, the details of this another time. So, this was a brief thing that I have presented to you as an introduction, so obviously, all the details are not here yet, InshaAllah they will come. As an introduction. Here, I would like to add one more thing: the first thing I want to present to you today is that the Shia religion, meaning the faith, is not something separate from Islam. Shia and Islam are the same thing. There is nothing separate. The Shia sect is not a historical sect that came into existence based on history. Rather, this Shia faith is the religion of Islam, the Shia religion is the religion of Islam, which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) introduced during his time. And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to the Master of the Universe, 'O Ali! You and your Shia are the successful ones.' And many times, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) linked this term to Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.) and stated that this sect, those who will be Ali's companions, who will walk on Ali's path, they are the ones who will be successful; no one else will be successful besides them. So, it is not the case that the Shia religion came into existence for some other reason. For example, some people say, they write in their books—there are many details in it—that Abdullah ibn Saba created the Shia religion. Abdullah ibn Saba came to Medina 20 years after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). He came to Medina 20 years after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and after coming to Medina, he saw—he was a Jew, that's how they wrote it—he was a Jew, and he saw, he talked to people about what is truth and what is falsehood, and he saw that what Ali was saying was correct, and what the others were saying was not correct, so he created a Shia religion, and then he did what? He gave fame to the Shia religion. This sentence is important. He gave fame to the Shia religion, which was not famous before him. This is what those people have written. Although we do not accept this explanation, this justification. But still, if we just, for the sake of argument—meaning, for the sake of argument—if we accept it, the sentence is that he only gave it fame. He did not create the religion. He only said that this religion of Ali is correct, it is true. He gave it fame. Therefore, attributing it to Abdullah ibn Saba and doing this is all a lie. And no Shia ever, in any way, believes in Abdullah ibn Saba. Abdullah ibn Saba is neither counted among the Imams, nor is he counted among the Sahaba, nor is he counted among the scholars. If you ask any child, any Shia child, he doesn't even know who Abdullah ibn Saba is. Who is Abdullah ibn Saba? But anyway, the enemies made him so famous that 'this is the one' and 'this was started by Abdullah ibn Saba.' So this religion is 'Inna ad-dina 'inda Allahi al-Islam' (Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam). There is no other religion besides Islam, and this is our belief. And this is our belief that there is no other religion besides Islam, and we believe in the same Islam that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) brought. The same Islam whose teachings the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) gave to Hazrat-e-Amir (a.s.), and after giving all the teachings, he also announced, 'Ana madinatu al-'ilmi wa 'Aliyyun babuha' (I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate). And this is a Mutawatir Hadith. This itself is a subject. 'Ana madinatu al-'ilmi'—this Hadith is a subject, a topic. InshaAllah, of this series of lectures. So, people put a roof on it, put doors, walls—meaning they put a roof, built walls, did this, did that, and did all these things. InshaAllah, the details will come later, but just briefly, the Prophet announced, 'Faman arada al-madinata wal-hikmata falyatiha min babiha' (Whoever wants the city and wisdom, let him come through its gate). People built roofs and this and that, they made windows, they made everything, they made walls, they made compound walls that 'this is the compound wall,' 'this is the roof,' 'this is that,' but the Prophet never said that if someone wants knowledge and wisdom, they should jump over the compound wall. That they should jump through the wall, through the window. He never said that. So, this was given to the Master of the Universe, and the Master of the Universe was taught this. The second important point in this is that it is the belief of all Muslims, and especially the Shias, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was the last Prophet, and there was no other prophet after him. And InshaAllah, when the Hadith al-Manzila is discussed, it is in that: 'Ama tarda an takuna minni bimanzilati Haruna min Musa illa annahu la nabiya ba'di' (Are you not pleased that you are to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me). The Prophet said this, and this is the belief of all Shias, and it is a verse of the Quran. Which is the Quranic verse in which the end of prophethood was announced: 'Ma kana Muhammadun (s.a.w.a.) aba ahadin min rijalikum' (Muhammad is not the father of any of your men), 'wa lakin rasulallahi wa khatam an-nabiyyin' (but he is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets). 'Wa khatam an-nabiyyin', he is only the Messenger of Allah and the last prophet. And we will take this 'Khatam' in every meaning that has been taken in the language, that now no prophet will come after him. This is the belief of every Shia. And the belief of the Shias is that if someone does not have this belief of 'Khatamiyat' (finality), the belief in the end of prophethood, then he is outside the fold of Islam. He is not a Muslim. If someone believes that a prophet came after the Messenger of Allah, a messenger came after the Messenger of Allah, a religion came after Islam, then such a person is not a Muslim, he is outside the fold of Islam. This is the belief of the Muslims, the Shias, and this is the religion. So, the Hadith, the noble Hadith that I recited to you, the Hadith al-Thaqalayn: 'Inni tarikun fikum al-thaqalayn, kitaballahi wa 'itrati ahli bayti, ma in tamassaktum bihima lan tadillu ba'di abada, fa-innahuma lan yaftariqa hatta yarida 'alayya al-hawd' (I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt. If you hold fast to them, you will never go astray after me, and they will never separate from each other until they return to me at the Pond [of Kawthar]). So now, if every Muslim holds the belief that after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), there is no other prophet, and if a person or a Muslim believes that the Quran is to remain until the Day of Judgment, then that same Muslim must also believe that there will be some member of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) who will be with this Quran until the Day of Judgment. And he is the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda). If the Quran remains—and Insha'Allah, as we will see in detail, if the Quran remains and will certainly remain—then it is necessary and mandatory, in light of this hadith, for one member of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) to remain. This is the belief of all Muslims. So, if this is the belief of all Muslims, then the question arises: where did the differences come from? The question is, when all Muslims believe in Hadith al-Thaqalayn, when all Muslims believe in the finality of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), when everyone believes that he was the last Messenger, and everyone believes that Islam is the religion and there is no other religion besides Islam—when all this is believed, and that the Thaqalayn (the Quran and Ahlul-Bayt) will be together until the Day of Judgment, then where did these differences come from? This is a matter worth pondering. And if this is the position of the Shias, it means the Shia school of thought has existed since the time of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). To this day, there is no historical event or incident where 'Tashayyu' (Shi'ism) came into existence later. The idea that the Shia sect was formed only when some people sided with Ali (a.s.) is wrong. These are all false justifications. If no one had been with Ali (a.s.)—understand this, if no one had been with him—if he were alone with his family, with Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) and the Hasanayn (a.s.), and no one else, it would still be the same religion, and there would be no other religion besides it. If all people had gone to the other side and claimed to be Muslims, they would not be Muslims, and only Ali (a.s.) and those with him would be Muslims; there would be no other Muslims besides them. That is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Aliyun ma'al-haqqi wal-haqqu ma'a Ali. Allahumma adir-il-haqqa haythuma dara.' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali. O Allah, turn the truth wherever Ali turns.) If you want to recognize the truth, look at where Ali is. It is a very simple matter. Ali is the standard of truth. Ali is the standard of truth. This is a very important point. So, where did the difference arise? The difference arose because the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did so many times—and the verses of the Quran are present, which Insha'Allah will be our topic—we will discuss the verses of the Quran in light of the traditions, if Allah grants us the ability. And all these things that we will present to you, we will try our best to present them in light of the books written by the scholars of India on this topic, the topic of Imamate. Especially the book 'Abaqat al-Anwar'. Insha'Allah, we will discuss all topics in its light, but first, it is necessary to present an introductory discussion. It is necessary to mention the name of the book and the scholar, Mir Hamid Hussain Hindi Kinturi Nishapuri (r.a.), who wrote 'Abaqat al-Anwar', and what its background was. All those details will come, Insha'Allah, but it is necessary to state this so that there is no intellectual dishonesty. That is, we are not presenting these points from ourselves; no. The points that will be presented, Insha'Allah, will be from the books of the scholars of India, especially 'Abaqat al-Anwar'. And other books as well, Insha'Allah, such as the book written by his honorable father, Sayyid Muhammad Quli (r.a.), as well as the works of Maulana Ghufran Ma'ab, Sayyid Dildar Ali Naqvi (r.a.), and the books written by their sons. We will take references from them to present to you, so that the reality becomes clear and it is also evident to the Shia youth how our scholars used to defend Tashayyu. So that is one thing. Now the question is, why did these differences arise? They arose because after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—even during the life of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), when he wanted to write the final document—the announcement had been made many times. The announcement had been made many times, but when he was stopped from writing that final document, it was then naturally announced that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had not appointed anyone, had not designated anyone, and had no successor. Propaganda was spread that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had not appointed anyone at all. Many arguments were created about this, and many things were presented claiming that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) left no will, that he did not leave a 'will' for the Muslims. So when they are told, 'Brother, if the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint a will, then how could the Messenger, who emphasized the importance of a will in so many hadiths, leave without a will?' The importance of a will is stated so clearly in the Quran. So how could the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) leave without a will? This is the question that arises. So what do they bring as an answer? They bring many 'mawiza' (exhortations) and pieces of advice. 'Look, I advise you...' That 'advice' is not in the sense that you are describing. Rather, what is it? It is advice and exhortation. Advice and exhortation are different things; a will is a different thing. So this is just a deception. It is just a deception to bring up 'I advise you' and show it as a will. In Arabic, one meaning of 'wasiyyah' is just to give advice and exhortation. That is, to advise, to admonish. Like, 'Look, don't lie, look, don't do this, look, don't backbite.' Is this a will? If this were a will, everyone would say, 'Yes, my father made a will: look, don't lie.' So we would distribute property based on lying? This is not a will. Rather, in a will, it is formally written that 'so much goes to this person, so much goes to that person.' Therefore, it is very clear that the problem started there. So they say the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint anyone. Okay. So what should be done? They say it is mandatory for the Ummah—now look at this, ponder over this—it is mandatory for the Ummah to appoint an Imam for itself. It is mandatory for the Ummah. All the theologians have written this, yes? Ibn Taymiyyah also wrote it. And Imam al-Mutakallimin Qushji wrote this, Qushji, he wrote it, and others whom we will mention, Insha'Allah, they all wrote it. Insha'Allah, the details will come now, or in the next episode, the details will come. So, the existence of an Imam is necessary. If the existence of an Imam—that is, it is mandatory for the Ummah to appoint an Imam—it means one... It is necessary for there to be an Imam. Whether the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appointed him or not. The matter is clear, right? If you say the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint anyone, okay, no problem, you say it doesn't matter. If the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not appoint anyone and you say, 'No, but it is mandatory for the Ummah to appoint an Imam,' then it means that the existence of an Imam is necessary. Now, whether Allah and His Messenger appoint him, or the Ummah appoints him. Now, it is the decision of a wise person whether to accept the Imam appointed by Allah and His Messenger or to accept an Imam appointed by some sinners or some non-infallible people. That decision is in the hands of the people; they can accept whoever they want. It is the responsibility of the people, the people have the choice, okay, it is in the world. So, we will start with how the need for an Imam arises. First, briefly, why it is necessary according to the Ahl-e-Tasannun (Sunni school), what the reason is, and then the series will begin from the Shia books. Insha'Allah, wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin.

title: Imam Ali (a.s.) Ki Wasiyyat | Will Of Imam Ali (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture highlights the profound final advice of Imam Ali (a.s.) as narrated by Imam Musa al-Kazim (a.s.). It emphasizes the fundamental necessity of maintaining Taqwa and holding firmly to the rope of Allah to ensure spiritual unity. The message serves as a timeless reminder for the Ahlulbayt and all believers to remain steadfast in their faith until death.
content:
Imam Kazim (a.s.) says that the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) wrote in his will: 'I advise you, all my Ahlulbayt, my children, and whoever this writing reaches, to adopt Taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah, who is your Lord, and take care that you do not die except while you are Muslims. And you all must hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not be divided. The fasting ones are for the Day of Judgment.'

excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological significance of the Khutba-e-Ghadir, focusing on the Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the definitive criterion for faith and salvation. It highlights the distinction between the party of Allah and the followers of falsehood, emphasizing that allegiance to the Ahlulbayt is essential for spiritual success in both this world and the Hereafter. The session concludes with administrative details regarding the Ghadir Mega Quiz 2026, including winner announcements and participation incentives for the upcoming series.

If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, subscribe now and don't forget to click the bell icon. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. A'udhu billahis sami'il alim minash shaitanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Allahumma kulli waliyyikal hujjati-bnil Hasan, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba-ihi fi hadihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Rabbi salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Nazreen, Assalamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. We want to offer our congratulations to all our viewers on the coronation of the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), which took place at Ghadir-e-Khumm at the hands of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), with these Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Nazreen, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stood on the pulpit and delivered a sermon in which he (s.a.w.a.) did not just designate the Imamate, but established such a criterion, such a standard, that he (s.a.w.a.) prayed, 'Allahumma wali man walahu wa adi man adahu'—'O Allah! Befriend the one who befriends him (Ali a.s.) and be the enemy of the one who is an enemy to him (Ali a.s.).' Nazreen, this prayer actually became a means of distinguishing between a believer and a hypocrite until the Day of Judgment. Come, Nazreen, we want to present to you other sentences of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) from the Sermon of Ghadir regarding this topic, and the title of this topic is: 'The Mention of the Lovers and Enemies of Imam Ali (a.s.) in the Sermon of Ghadir.' Dear brothers and sisters, respected viewers, this topic in the Sermon of Ghadir is a line drawn between truth and falsehood that will remain until the Day of Judgment. Nazreen, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stood in the field of Ghadir and presented the essence of all the explanations of the religion before the entire Muslim Ummah. Let us begin our talk with that sentence from the sermon in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) states, 'Ma shar-an-nas, ana siratullahil mustaqim'—'O people! I am that straight path of Allah, which He has commanded you to follow.' Nazreen, but the matter did not end there. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) called his own self the 'Sirat-e-Mustaqim' (Straight Path) and then immediately stated the continuity of that path, and then he declared, 'Summa Aliyyun min ba'di'—'Then after me, Ali (a.s.) is that straight path.' "Summa waladi min sulbihi" then from his sulb, meaning from the sulb of Ali (a.s.) is my progeny, and then you (s.a.w.a.) said, "A'immatun yahduna ilal haq" that they will be such Imams, such leaders, who will guide towards the truth. This means that the Sirat-e-Mustaqeem (Straight Path) maintains a face until the Day of Judgment so that no wanderer can say that I did not find the path. Viewers, after this, I want to present a hadith before you which Allama Majlisi (r.a.) brings in Bihar al-Anwar, and it is narrated from Mufaddal ibn Umar in which Mufaddal ibn Umar asks Imam Sadiq (a.s.) a question, "Sa'altu Aba Abdillah (a.s.) anis Sirat" - you ask a question regarding the Sirat. The Mawla says, "Huwat tariqu ila ma'rifatillah-i azza wa jall" - what is that Sirat? It is the path to the recognition of Allah (azza wa jall), and then the Mawla says, "Wa huma siratani, siratun fid-dunya wa siratun fil-akhirah" - and then after that, the Mawla says that there is not one Sirat, there are two, two paths. One Sirat is in this world and one Sirat is the Sirat of the Hereafter. After that, "Wa ammas-siratul-lazi fid-dunya" - as for the Sirat that is in this world, the Mawla says, "Fahuwal Imamul muftarazu ta'atuhu" - that Sirat of the world, the Mawla says, who is that Sirat of the world? It is the Imam, and who is that Imam whose obedience Allah (t.w.t.) has made obligatory upon the entire Muslim Ummah? And then after that, Imam Sadiq (a.s.) states, "Man arafahu fid-dunya waqtada bihuda-hu" - that whoever recognized that Imam in this world and followed his guidance, "Marra alas-siratil-lazi huwa jisru jahannama fil-akhirah" - he will easily cross that Sirat in the Hereafter which will be the bridge over Hell. And after this, the last sentence of this hadith which the Imam (a.s.) states is, "Wa man lam ya'rifhu fid-dunya" - that whoever did not recognize that Imam, whoever did not know that Imam, his foot will slip from the Sirat in the Hereafter, "Zallat" and then "Fataradda fi nari jahannama" and he will fall into the fire of Hell. Now viewers, after the discussion on the Sirat, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) comes to Surah al-Hamd and says, "Summa qara'a (s.a.w.a.) ila akhiraha" - then he recited the entire Surah al-Hamd and then he declared, "Fi nazalat wa fihim nazalat" - that this Surah was revealed about me and about the Infallible Imams (a.s.), and then he stated, "Wa lahum 'ammat wa iyyahum khassat" - it is general for them and it is specific for them. Meaning, it is general for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and it has been specified for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). "Ulaika awliya-ullah" - right? These are the people who are the servants of Allah, the Awliya. "La khawfun alaihim wa la hum yahzanun" - that upon them there will be no fear, nor will they grieve. So here, after the discussion of the Sirat, the Messenger of Allah ends the discussion of Surah al-Hamd, and if you look at the verses of Surah al-Hamd, in reality, the verses of Surah al-Hamd are that point of unity, the connection point of the Khutbah of Ghadir, from where the separation begins. That if you look at every path in the world, viewers, it definitely leads somewhere, but not every path leads to the destination. Every day in every prayer, we ask only one question to the Creator of the universe, "Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim" (Guide us to the straight path), but the question is, whose path is that? What is its address? What is the address towards which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was pointing, that I am that Sirat, I am the master of the Sirat, my Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the masters of the Sirat. Right? We are... for us, Surah al-Hamd, in which the mention of "Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim" is being made, this is specific for us. Now from here, We move to the next sentence of the Khutbah of Allah, where the Messenger of Allah, having identified the Sirat and attributed Surah al-Hamd to himself, now starts drawing the line between friend and foe, and immediately says, 'Ala' (Beware), that O people, know that "Inna hizballahi humul muflihun al-ghalibun" - that indeed, only the party of Allah is successful and victorious. Meaning, whoever walks on the Sirat of Surah al-Hamd is included in the party of Allah, and whoever is included in the party of Allah, Allah has given two guarantees for him. What is the first guarantee? Which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, that 'Al-Muflihun' - they are successful, successful in this world and in the Hereafter. And what is the second guarantee? 'Al-Ghalibun' - they will always be victorious, even if they are few in number, even if they are very small in appearance. Right, even after that, they will be victorious. Now from here, a great question, because if you look at the second hadith of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), in the Prophetic hadith we find that regarding the party of Allah, I want to present a hadith before you. You (s.a.w.a.) stated that the Ummah of Prophet Musa (a.s.) was divided into 71 sects, 71 parts, out of which only one group was successful, they were the 'Najin', they were successful. And then after that, the Ummah of Prophet Isa (a.s.) was divided into 72 sects, and out of them, 71 sects will go to Hell. And here, you do not remain silent, but rather warn your Ummah regarding that danger, that it is not just the Ummah of Prophet Musa (a.s.) that turned into sects, the Ummah of Prophet Isa (a.s.) that turned into sects, but this Ummah, the Ummah of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), this Ummah will also turn into sects. You point towards that, "Wa inna ummati sataftariqu ba'di" - that surely this Ummah of mine will also turn into sects, and into how many sects? "Ala thalathin wa sab'ina firqah" - into 73 sects, 73 divisions. "Firqatun minha najiyah" - right, out of which only one sect will be 'Najiyah', will be successful, will be successful. Meaning 72 will go to Hell, will go into the fire of Hell. Meaning the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is telling something very important, that this Ummah should be very careful, that this Ummah will be divided into 73 parts, and out of that, 72 parts of the Ummah will not be on the path of truth. So now, who is that one? Regarding that, this Ummah will have to find out who that one is. So this is not a trivial number, 72 people will go, the number 72 is seen going to Hell. Now the decision is in the hands of the Muslim Ummah, that the announcement was made by the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in the field of Ghadir, and it was told who that group will be, who that group will be, that group will be the lovers of Hazrat Ali (a.s.), who will follow them, who will follow them, who will obey them, and whoever abandons Ali (a.s.), surely he will be misguided and he will be thrown into the fire of Hell. Now here, the tone of the Khutbah of Ghadir will appear to be extremely strict, now we will present before you a few things regarding the enemies of Ali (a.s.) from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). What did he state? That whoever is the enemy of Ali (a.s.), the Messenger did not associate him with any tribe or lineage, but called him "Ikhwanush-shayatin" (brothers of the devils), and what will be their end? They are "Zukhruful qawl" (ornamented speech), meaning they fabricate beautiful words to make falsehood appear as truth so that they can misguide people. Let us see what those sentences are. That you stated, "Ala inna a'da'a Aliyyin" - beware, know that indeed, the enemy of Ali is the same. Who is he? "Hum ahlush-shiqaq" - who are the people of 'shiqaq', meaning those who create division, those who oppose. "Al-'adun" - and what is meant by 'adun'? Those who cross the limits. "Wa ikhwanush-shayatin" - which we were mentioning before you, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated that those who are enemies of Ali (a.s.) are brothers of whom? They will be brothers of the devils. "Alladhina yuhi ba'duhum ila ba'din" - who whisper to one another to deceive, "Zukhrufal qawli ghurura" - right? Meaning, they inject deceptive, falsehood-adorned words. Viewers, when the line of enmity was drawn, the question arises, who is a Momin (believer)? Because on the other side, the Messenger of Allah described that group as being 'Ikhwanush-shayatin', brothers of the devils. So, is just reciting the Kalima enough? Are prayer and fasting the only proof of faith? No, will he be called a Momin? The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) gave such an answer in Ghadir that it shakes the foundation of our faith. We are going to present the next sentence of Ghadir, of the Khutbah of Ghadir, that you stated, "Ala inna awliya'ahum" - that know, be warned, be aware, indeed those who are the 'Mawali' (friends/followers) of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), "Humul mu'minuna alladhina dhakarahumullahu fi kitabihi" - they are the Momineen whom Allah (t.w.t.) has mentioned in His Book. "Faqala azza wa jall: La tajidu qawman yu'minuna billahi wal-yawmil akhir" - that you will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment. How will you not find them? "Yuwadduna man haddallaha wa rasulahu ila akhiril ayah" - that they love those who oppose Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.). Meaning, from this sentence, it is absolutely clear that being neutral is against faith. This sentence of Ghadir teaches us that being neutral is against faith, and whoever is an enemy of Allah and the Messenger, meaning whoever is an enemy of Ali (a.s.), one who loves him can never be a Momin. Even if he performs a million prostrations, because Allah has clearly said, "La tajidu qawman" - meaning you cannot find such a person that he loves Ali and also loves the enemy of Ali. Meaning, both loves cannot coexist in one heart. Now come, viewers, to the verse of Surah al-Mujadila, that you will not find that one who... right, loves the enemies of Allah and His Messenger and Ali (a.s.), right, who believes in Allah, believes in the Messenger, and believes in Ali (a.s.). Regarding that, I have to present a hadith before you, that the narrator says, how should we recognize who is the friend of Allah so that we can become his slave, and who is the enemy of Allah so that we can be enemies with him? Now here, when he puts this question before the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he asks, he inquires, at that time what does the Messenger of Allah do? "Fa-ashara lahu Rasulullahi (s.a.w.a.) ila Aliyyin (a.s.)" - that the Messenger of Allah pointed towards Ali (a.s.) in front of that person and what did he say? "Faqala" - he said, "Atara hadha?" - do you see him? He said, "Bala ya Rasulallah" - yes, I see him, O Messenger of Allah. Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, "Waliyyu hadha waliyyullah" - that know, his 'Wali' (friend/master), meaning his slave, is the slave of Allah, and then after that he said, "Fawalihi" - right, that then you befriend the one who considers Ali (a.s.) his Imam, who considers himself a slave of Ali (a.s.), you befriend him. And then the next sentence the Messenger of Allah states, "Wa 'aduwwuhu hadha 'aduwwullah" - and his enemy is the enemy of Allah. "Fa-'adihi" - then you be enemies with those who are enemies of Ali (a.s.). And then after that, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not stop here, but rather stated that matter which is very difficult to bear. You said, "Wali waliyya hadha" - right, befriend his slave, his slave, and then stated, "Wa law annahu qatilu abika wa waladika" - even if he is the killer of your father or your child. Meaning, if he is a lover of Ali (a.s.), then love him, even if he is the killer of your father. Even if he is the killer of your son. And then after that, he said, "Wa 'adi 'aduwwa hadha" - and be enemies with his enemies, "Wa law annahu abuka aw waladuka" - even if he is your father or your son. You see at what status the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is presenting the love of Ali (a.s.) before the Muslim Ummah, that if someone holds his Wilayah, even if he has killed your father, still you love him, and if he is your father and hates Ali (a.s.), bears enmity towards him, then what should you do with your father? Be enemies with him. Now viewers, we move to the next sentence in which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) He described the attributes of the Momineen, that is, the attributes of the lovers of Ali (a.s.), and he declared, "Ala inna awliya-ahum"—be warned, indeed those who are the followers, lovers, and devotees of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are "alladhina wasafahumullahu azza wa jalla," the very ones whose attributes Allah (t.w.t.) has described. And what did He describe? "Faqala alladhina amanu," that those who believe—meaning the followers of Ali (a.s.), his lovers, his devotees—are the ones who believe. This is the first attribute. Then what is the second attribute being described? "Wa lam yalbisu imanahum bi-zulmin," and they have not mixed or blended their faith with injustice or shirk. "Ulaika lahumul amnu wa hum muhtadun," for them is security, and they are the guided ones. Viewers, let us see what Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said regarding this verse, where the mixing of faith with injustice is mentioned. The Mawla said regarding this verse, "Wa alladhina amanu wa lam yalbisu imanahum bi-zulmin," that those who believed and did not mix their faith with injustice, "Qala bima ja'a bi-Muhammadin (s.a.w.a.) min al-wilayati," that they believed in that Wilayah. Meaning, what is meant by the faith being spoken of here? It means that the Wilayah which the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) presented to the world, those people accepted that Wilayah and believed in it. And then, with what did they not mix it? "Wa lam yakhlituha bi-wilayati fulanin wa fulanin," and they did not mix the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) with the Wilayah of so-and-so and so-and-so. Now, let us move to the next phrase. The Messenger of Allah states that Allah will grant Paradise to the lovers and devotees of Ali (a.s.). This phrase is: "Ala, know that inna awliya-ahumulladhina yadkhulunal jannata aminin," indeed the followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), their lovers, and their adherents are the ones who will enter Paradise in safety. "Wa tatalaqquhumul mala'ikatu bit-taslim," and the angels will welcome them with greetings. "An tibtum," and they will say, "You are happy, you have become pure." "Fadkhuluha khalidin," and enter this Paradise to dwell therein forever. So, this phrase shows us that the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) will be admitted into Paradise in the hereafter, the angels will welcome them, and now I must present a hadith to you because this phrase mentions that pure people will go to Paradise—the lovers of the Ale-Muhammad (a.s.) will be pure people. Now let us see, what about those who do not hold love for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) or who harbor hatred (bughz) for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)? Are they pure, or something else? Imam Reza (a.s.) narrates from his forefathers that once Imam Ali (a.s.) was resting near the Kaaba when a stooped man, meaning a very elderly person, came there. His condition was such that his eyes and eyebrows were drooping over his eyes due to the intensity of old age. He had a staff in his hand, a red cap on his head, and a shirt made of hair on his body. After arriving, he approached the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) while the Messenger of Allah was sitting, leaning against the Kaaba. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray for my forgiveness." As soon as he made this request to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), what did the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say? "Khaba sa'yuka ya shaykh wa zalla amaluk," O old man, your efforts have failed and your deeds will be wasted. When he heard these words from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he turned back and started to leave. In the meantime, the Messenger of Allah said to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), "Ali, O Abul Hasan, do you know who this old man is?" Imam Ali (a.s.) said, "The Messenger knows best, you know best, O Messenger of Allah, you know better." The Messenger of Allah stated, "He is none other than Iblis." As soon as Ali (a.s.) heard that this was Iblis, Imam Ali (a.s.) went after him very quickly, caught him from behind, threw him to the ground, sat on his chest, and began to choke him. When Ali (a.s.) began to choke him, he said—Iblis said—"La taf'al ya Abul Hasan," O Abul Hasan, do not do this. "Fa-inni minal muntazirina ila yawmil waqtil ma'lum. Wallahi ya Ali inni la uhibbuka jiddan," I am among those who are granted respite until the appointed day. By God, O Ali, I truly love you. Look, the Shaytan is saying about Ali (a.s.) that "O Ali, I love you." "Wa ma abghazaka ahadun," and whoever has hated you, O Ali, whoever has held enmity toward you—now Iblis explains about him, what he does to the one who hates you or what happens to him—"illa shariktu abahu fi ummihi," Iblis says, "I become a partner in his birth." And then, when Ali (a.s.) heard this from Iblis, Ali (a.s.) smiled and let him go. So here it became very clear that those who enter Paradise will be the pure and clean ones who are lovers of Ali (a.s.), and those who go to Hell will be those who harbor hatred for Ali (a.s.); they will be the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Now let us see the next phrase that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is stating; what is he saying in it? He also stated this sentence regarding the lovers of Ali (a.s.): "Ala," be warned, "inna awliya-ahumulladhina," those who are the followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), what are they? "Qalallahu azza wa jalla," Allah (t.w.t.) says about them, "yadkhulunal jannata," that He will admit them into Paradise, they will enter. But the most important part is the sentence that comes after this: "bi-ghayri hisab," that He will admit them without any reckoning. This is a very interesting point, that they will go to Paradise, but they will not go with reckoning; Allah will admit them into Paradise without reckoning. Regarding this, we have many hadiths that Allah will send the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to Paradise without reckoning. Let us present a hadith from Bihar: the Mawla says, "Ala wa man ahabba Aliyan," the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is stating, "Know, be warned, that whoever loves Ali, istaghfarat lahul mala'ikatu," the angels seek forgiveness for him, "wa futihat lahu abwabul jannati," the doors of Paradise will be opened for him, "yadkhulu min ayyi babin sha'a bi-ghayri hisab," he will enter through whichever door of Paradise he wishes, without reckoning. So we find many such traditions where it is stated that whoever loves the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), befriends them, and expresses his affection for them, Allah will admit him into Paradise without reckoning. Now, after the talk about the friends of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), let us move to what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said in the sermon of Ghadir about the enemies of Ali (a.s.): "Ala inna a'da-ahumulladhina yaslawna sa'ira," be warned, indeed the one who is an enemy of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), an adversary, what is for him? The blazing fire; "Sa'ir" means the blazing fire into which he will be thrown. Meaning, for the lovers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Allah has prepared Paradise, and for their enemies—those who harbor hatred for them, especially those who harbor hatred for Ali (a.s.) and his children—He has prepared the blazing fire. And if you look at other hadiths, the Hell that Allah has created, He created it because of the hatred for Ali (a.s.). If the world had not hated Ali (a.s.), Allah would not have created Hell at all. It is stated in a hadith, "Ya Ali law ijtama'atil khala'iqu ala wilayatik," O Ali, if people had gathered upon your Wilayah, "la khalaqallahunnaar," Allah would not have created the Fire. Meaning, those who are going to Hell are none other than those individuals who express hatred for the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), keep hatred in their hearts, and commit many evil deeds against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Listen to what the Messenger of Allah is saying in the next phrase: "Ala inna a'da-ahumulladhina yasma'una lijahannama shaheeqa," that their enemies, the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), will hear the terrifying sound of Hell. "Shaheeq" refers to the sound. When they go to Hell, a terrifying sound will come from there. "Wa hiya tafooru," while it will be boiling, "wa laha zafeer," and in it, there will be very dangerous things... The sound of striking; "Zafeer"—very dangerous sounds will come from within it. "Kullama dakhalat ummatun," whenever a group, an Ummah, is admitted into it, what will happen? "La'anat ukhtaha," meaning they will curse the group that came before them. And he states, "Ala inna a'da'ahumulladhina qalallahu azza wa jalla," so be warned. Indeed, the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are the ones about whom Allah (t.w.t.) is saying this. What is He saying? "Kullama ulqiya fiha fawjun," whenever a group is thrown into that Hell, what will happen? "Sa'alahum khazanatuha," the keeper of Hell will ask them. What will they ask? "Alam ya'tikum nadhir?" Did no warner come to you? What will they say? "Qalu bala," they will not say that no warner came. They will say, they will confess, that yes, a warner did come. "Qad ja'ana nadhir," yes, a warner did come to us. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) quotes that verse of the Quran, "Ila qawlihi fasuqan li-ashabis sa'ir," so away with the companions of the Blaze. What is the purpose behind the mention of this verse in the Sermon of Ghadir in these verses of Surah Mulk? That the declaration of the Wilayah of Mawla Ali (a.s.) is such a "Hujjat-e-Tamma," a final proof, that after it, no one will be able to say that they were not told. Because they themselves are confessing, "Bala," that a warner did come, but even after that, we denied. Meaning, this is called "Juhood." "Al-inkar ba'dal ma'rifa," that we knew, yet even after that, we denied Ali (a.s.). Now, viewers, we have been seeing continuously how the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), through his statements one after another, is warning those people that the enemies of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the enemies of Ali (a.s.), will be subjected to such a painful punishment by Allah. Now, in contrast, the next phrase that is coming is that the fear of Allah will be found in the friends of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). He states, "Ala," know, be aware. "Inna awliya'ahumulladhina yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghayb," that indeed, O slaves of the Masumin (a.s.), their followers will be those who fear their Lord without seeing Him, will be fearful, and "lahum maghfiratun wa ajrun kabir," for them is forgiveness and a great reward. Now, if you look, we have many traditions regarding the fear of Allah. Right? Our scholars have dedicated entire chapters to the fear of Allah. But I will present just one sentence from Dua-e-Saba before you regarding the fear of Allah: "Man dha ya'rifu qadrak," who is it that knows Your power and Your status, "fala yakhafuk," yet does not fear You? Then the sentence of the supplication is, "Wa man dha ya'lamu ma anta," and who is it that knows what You are, "fala yahabuk," yet does not feel awe of You? So, such sentences are found abundantly in our supplications regarding the fear of Allah, that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) presented this teaching and training to their lovers, that a person who loves the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) should have the fear of Allah within him. So now, let us see what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is saying in the final phrase: "Ma'shar an-nas," O people, "shattan ma baynas sa'iri wal jannah," there is a huge difference between the fire of Hell and Paradise. And then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says, "Fa'aduwwuna man dhammahullahu," so our enemy is the one whom Allah has condemned, and not just condemned, "wa la'anahu," and cursed him. And then, this is what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated regarding the condemnation and cursing of the enemies. Now, here he is stating something regarding his lovers or the followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). What is it? How will Allah treat them? What will Allah do with them? "Wa waliyuna man madaḥahullāh" (And our friend is the one whom Allah has praised, whose virtues He has extolled, and whose praises He has sung). "Wa aḥabbahu" (And not only did He praise him, but Allah loves him). Ghadir has made it clear that there are only two groups in the world. One group is the one whom God is praising on the Throne; they are the lovers of Ali (a.s.), his devotees, his followers. And the other group is the one upon whom God has sent curses; they are the enemies of Ali (a.s.), those who hold malice against him. Now, we have to make this decision. On one side, there is the coolness of Paradise and entry without reckoning, entry without account, and on the other side, there is 'Sa'ir', which refers to the blazing fire. So, there is no middle path between these two. It is either Paradise or Hell; there is no middle ground. Now the world has to decide whether to be worthy of God's praise—that is, by expressing love and affection for Ali (a.s.)—or to become worthy of God's curse by holding malice against Ali (a.s.) and being his enemy. So the decision is in your hands as to which group you want to join. Viewers, regarding this last point, one or two more hadiths, and then I will conclude. Here, the Mawla says, and the Mawla says it under oath, "Wallāhi" (By Allah), "Law ḍarabtu khayshūmal-mu'mini bisayfī hādhā" (By Allah, if I were to strike the nose of a believer with this sword of mine), "ʿalā an yubghiḍanī mā abghaḍanī" (so that he might hate me, he would never hate me). He would never bear enmity towards me. Think about the level at which a lover of Ali (a.s.) loves Ali (a.s.), that even if Ali (a.s.) were to strike him, he would still not hold malice against Ali (a.s.). And conversely, what does the Mawla say? "Wa law ṣababtud-dunyā bi-mā fī raḥāhā ʿalal-kāfir" (And if I were to gather the whole world and all its blessings and bestow them upon a disbeliever), "mā aḥabbanī" (he would not love me). Meaning, on one side, his friend, even if the Mawla were to strike him, he would not bear enmity towards the Mawla; and on the other side, those who hate the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), even if the whole world were given to them, even if Ali (a.s.) were to give it to them, they would still not express love for Ali (a.s.). And then the Mawla says, "Wa dhālika annahu quḍiya fa-qaḍā ʿalā lisānin-nabiyyil-ummī" (And this is because it has been decreed and decided upon the tongue of the Unlettered Prophet, Muhammad-e-Mustafa (s.a.w.a.)). What is the decision? That you used to state, or you stated, "Annahu lā yubghiḍuka mu'min" (That O Ali, no believer will hate you), "wa lā yuḥibbuka kāfir" (and no disbeliever will love you). Meaning, the Messenger of God (s.a.w.a.) has stated the principle that whoever is a believer, O Ali, will not hold malice against you, and whoever is an enemy of God, an enemy of the religion, cannot love you. Now, viewers, we have reached our final stage, and as it has become very clear that no one will hate Ali (a.s.) unless they are a disbeliever, and no one will love Ali (a.s.) unless they are a believer. So, for us, our red line, our standard, is Ali (a.s.). Right? Whoever loves Ali (a.s.), right? "Innī silmun liman sālamakum wa ḥarbun liman ḥārabakum" (I am at peace with those who are at peace with you, and at war with those who are at war with you). We will love everyone who loves Ali (a.s.), and we declare war against everyone who has fought Ali (a.s.) or intended to fight him. Let us conclude your efforts with a couplet, for what a poet beautifully says: that some people do not like my Mawla. Regarding 'Tabarra' (disassociation), what is our attitude towards those who hate Ali (a.s.)? That some people do not like my Mawla. Some people do not like my Mawla, and some people I do not like because of that. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Master of the Age, help us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullah. title: Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ki Wilaadat Baa Sa'aadat Ka Poora Waaqe'ah  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi details the miraculous birth of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as narrated by Janabe Hakima Khatoon. It highlights the divine protection surrounding the birth, comparing the hidden pregnancy of Janabe Narjis to that of the mother of Prophet Musa (a.s.). The talk concludes by emphasizing the significance of the 15th of Shaban and the connection between the awaited Savior and the tragedy of Karbala.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. May Allah (s.w.t.) keep the book... First of all, in this blessed month, we congratulate you all... In this month, we congratulate you all on the birth of that great personality, the Master of the Universe, the 12th Imam, the Mahdi (a.s.). May Allah (s.w.t.) keep his reappearance blessed. Since this is the end, let us study that hadith, which is very old, in which the news of the birth of the 12th Imam (a.s.), born from the womb of Janabe Narjis Khatoon, was given by Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.). This is present in the book 'Kamaluddin', Volume 2, Chapter 42. It is present there in detail, and similarly in 'Bihar al-Anwar', in the first volume, this narration is present in the first chapter. In the first chapter, this narration is present: 'Say, the truth has come, and falsehood has vanished; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to perish.' There is no doubt that falsehood was meant to perish. So, let us hear the news of this blessed arrival and birth from the blessed lips of the lady herself. Janabe Narjis Khatoon says that just as I used to serve the mother of the 10th Imam, after her passing, I used to serve the mother of the 11th Imam. One day, I went to the house of the Imam, and I said, 'I swear by you, I will not leave, and I will not be satisfied unless you let me serve you. Serving you is an honor for me.' Just as I said this, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) looked at me and said, 'May Allah keep you in His protection...' May Allah keep you in His protection. Yes, on that night, I was at the house of the Imam. When I decided to leave, I called my maid to bring my cloak. As I was about to leave, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) said, 'O aunt, stay with us tonight. Tonight is the night the promised one, whose arrival Allah has promised, is to be born. He is the one who will fill the world with justice just as it has been filled with oppression.' I had looked at her (Narjis) carefully, but there were no signs of pregnancy. So I asked the Imam, 'From whom will this son be born?' Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) said, 'From Narjis, and no one else.' I went to Narjis and looked closely, but I saw no signs of pregnancy. I returned to the Imam and told him that there were no signs of pregnancy in her. He smiled and said, 'O aunt, when this night ends and the morning of the birth arrives, the signs of pregnancy will become apparent in Narjis, because the example of Narjis is like the example of the mother of Musa (a.s.), in whom the signs of pregnancy were not visible, and because of which Pharaoh did not know, and he killed all the pregnant women...' And the mother of Musa (a.s.) is the sign, in whom the signs of pregnancy were not visible, and the Pharaoh did not know, and he killed thousands of children. The example of Narjis is like the mother of Musa (a.s.). And Janabe Hakima Khatoon says that I prayed the Maghrib and Isha prayers at the house of the Imam, and then food was brought for me and Janabe Narjis. We ate, and then we slept in the same room. I fell asleep for a little while, and in the middle of the night, I woke up for the night prayer (Tahajjud). I started praying, but I was thinking about what the Imam had said regarding the birth, but until then, that event had not yet occurred. I used to wake up before my usual time to perform my prayers. I had finished my prayers and was reciting the supplications when suddenly, I felt a sense of unease. I went out of the room and looked towards the sky. I felt that the time was very near, but I had no scientific proof of it. Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) had told me about the promise of Allah regarding the birth of the Imam, and at that very moment, a slight doubt entered my heart. Suddenly, I heard the Imam's voice saying, 'Do not doubt, for what I have said is about to happen, and you will witness it, Insha'Allah.' I felt very ashamed because of my doubt and turned back towards my room. As I reached near my room, I saw that Janab-e-Nargis had finished her prayers and was coming out in a state of great haste. I said, 'May my parents be sacrificed for you, what are you feeling?' Janab-e-Nargis replied, 'O aunt, I am feeling a kind of sign.' I said, 'Insha'Allah, everything will be fine, do not worry.' I embraced Nargis and began to recite the name of God. The Imam called out, 'O aunt, recite Surah al-Qadr.' I began reciting Surah al-Qadr while holding Nargis in my arms and asked her, 'My daughter, how are you?' Janab-e-Nargis replied, 'O aunt, the news that Mawla Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) gave you has become manifest.' I continued reciting Surah al-Qadr, but I was surprised that... But I was surprised that along with my recitation, someone else was also reciting Surah al-Qadr. I looked and saw that the newborn was reciting it from inside. He greeted me, and I followed the Imam's instructions. Then the Imam called out, 'Do not be surprised by the work of God, for God grants us wisdom in our childhood, opens our tongues with wisdom, and when we grow up, He appoints us as His proof on the entire earth.' Before he could finish his words, the newborn disappeared from my sight. A veil was drawn between me and them, and I could no longer see them. I began to cry out and ran towards Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). The Imam said, 'O aunt, go back, you will find Nargis there.' Go back, you will find Nargis there. I returned, and it had not been long when the veil between us was removed. What did I see? A light, a light that shone from Nargis, so bright that my eyes were dazzled. After that, I saw that the one who was born to Janab-e-Nargis was in prostration. His forehead was on the ground, his face was on his palms, and his index fingers were raised towards the sky. He was testifying to the oneness of Allah, saying: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He is one, He has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.' And he continued, 'And Ali is the Commander of the Faithful, and Hasan, and Husayn...' He kept mentioning the names of the Imams until he reached his own name. Janab-e-Hakima says that after this, I saw the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.) praying in the presence of Allah: 'O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me, complete my task for me, make my steps firm, and through me, fill the earth with justice and fairness.' This was the entire Hadith, or rather, the summary of the Hadith. This was the summary of the Hadith that I presented to you, explaining how the birth of the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.) took place, and Janab-e-Fatimah Khatoon herself testified to it. As you know, people ask, 'What is the proof?' The proof is that the one who was present at the time of birth is the witness, and Janab-e-Hakima Khatoon was that witness—the daughter of an Imam, the granddaughter of an Imam, and the aunt of an Imam. In a way, she was the grandmother of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). After the testimony of such a personality, there is no room for doubt. Thus, the morning came, and the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.) arrived in this world on the 15th of Shaban, 255 AH. Great scholars have mentioned the birth of the Imam in their books. So, saying this, 'O Allah, forgive the oppressed and the oppressed ones, and hasten the relief of the oppressed...' and in Karbala, this is special because the one who will take revenge for the blood of God has arrived. They are saying, 'Congratulations, O Husayn, the one who will take your revenge has arrived.' Alas, if only we were in Karbala today, we would have offered these congratulations to you ourselves in Karbala. But circumstances have forced us, and we could not be present in Karbala today. Therefore, as it is said, if a person is not present in Karbala, they should go to a high place in their house, look left and right, look towards the sky, and greet Imam Husayn (a.s.) in this way: 'Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah...' Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah...

title: Kya Taqiyyah Hamara Deen Nahin? [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture addresses the nuanced concept of Taqiyyah (dissimulation) in Shia Islam, clarifying when it is permissible and when it is forbidden. The speaker emphasizes that while Taqiyyah is allowed for self-preservation, it must never be used as an excuse to abandon one's duties or fail to support the Ahlulbayt. Citing the words of Imam Reza (a.s.), the talk highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be Shias but neglect their responsibilities to the faith and their fellow believers.
content:
If one can save their life by practicing Taqiyya (dissimulation), then it is fine. But if, despite the hardship, one's life is at stake, then Taqiyya should not be practiced. By God, if we call you for our help, you will refuse by saying that your life is dearer to you than your parents. And Imam Reza (a.s.) refused to meet some of his followers, saying, 'You call yourselves Shias of Ali (a.s.), but in many things, you oppose him. You are negligent in fulfilling your duties, you do not show consideration for your fellow believers, you practice Taqiyya where it should not be practiced, and you do not practice it where it is required.' According to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), when it comes to helping and supporting the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), Taqiyya is not permissible.
Taqiyyah is permissible for self-preservation but not for avoiding religious duties.
Using Taqiyyah to avoid helping the Ahlulbayt is strictly forbidden.
Imam Reza (a.s.) criticized followers who misused Taqiyyah to justify their negligence.
True Shia identity requires balancing caution with the courage to support the truth.
One must distinguish between situations requiring protection and those requiring sacrifice.
Neglecting fellow believers while claiming to follow Ali (a.s.) is a contradiction of faith.
