Using Taqiyyah to avoid helping the Ahlulbayt is strictly forbidden.
Imam Reza (a.s.) criticized followers who misused Taqiyyah to justify their negligence.
True Shia identity requires balancing caution with the courage to support the truth.
One must distinguish between situations requiring protection and those requiring sacrifice.
Neglecting fellow believers while claiming to follow Ali (a.s.) is a contradiction of faith.

chapters.title: The Proper Application of Taqiyyah
chapters.summary: The lecture defines the boundaries of Taqiyyah, explaining that it is not a tool for negligence but a measure for survival.

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#4 | Who are the Twelve Imams (peace be on them)? | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological and historical foundations of the Twelve Imams within the Shia tradition, emphasizing the concept of divine appointment. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the significance of Wilayah, the historical deviations following the Prophet's passing, and the critical role of authentic Hadith in preserving Islamic truth. The session also addresses the legitimacy of the Imams as successors to the Prophet and the importance of disassociating from those who oppressed the Ahlulbayt.
content:
Nasreen-e-Kiram, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Following the fragrance of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), the journey of recognition that we have embarked upon has reached its fourth stage today. Yes, viewers, regarding the recognition of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), our program... Regarding our program 'Shame-e-Marifat' (The Fragrance of Gnosis), this is the fourth episode. I welcome all the gentlemen present. In the third episode, it was made clear that Allah (SWT) has not emphasized anything as much as Imamate, and people have not denied anything as much as they have denied Imamate. In that episode, it was also established that Allah has declared that appointing a Caliph is solely Allah's prerogative, and whoever denies the Caliph and Imam appointed by Allah is like the accursed Iblis. This selection of the Caliph is solely Allah's responsibility, and our topic today is connected to this, where we will see, InshaAllah, whom Allah has made an Imam and a Caliph. Yes, in today's fourth episode, our topic is 'Who is our Imam?' To shed light on this, I request the respected Dr. Syed Ali to please come forward and initiate the discussion for the benefit of the viewers and the program. Muhammad Salle... Initiate the discussion, Muhammad, peace be upon Muhammad and his family. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. [Recitation of Arabic prayers and salutations]. Through the respected Maulana Syed... this is present in almost all books of Tafsir and Hadith, such as Tafsir al-Safi, it is present in Al-Kafi, it is present in Wasa'il, and it is present in Burhan and Tafsir al-Nur al-Thaqalayn, and other such books. It is present in all of them. And in this Hadith, it is stated... [The speaker mentions a Hadith regarding three types of people whom Allah will not speak to or purify on the Day of Judgment]. The meaning of 'Tazkiyah' (purification) here: one meaning is to praise someone, but the Quran says 'do not purify yourselves' (la tuzakku anfusakum). Allah knows best who is righteous. The second meaning is whether Allah will accept their deeds or not. It says, 'Allah will not accept their deeds, and for them is a painful punishment.' These are the three things: first, Allah will not speak to them (they will be deprived of Allah's mercy); second, Allah will not purify them; and third, there is a painful punishment for them. Who are these three types of people? This is a matter of Wilayah and Imamate. The Hadith says, 'Whoever claims to be an Imam from Allah while the Imamate is not his right...' While the Imamate is not his right, yet he claims it, it means he is claiming something that is not from Allah. An Imam is one about whom there is a 'Nass' (explicit designation), about whom there is a text, and about whom the Messenger has spoken in Hadiths. That is called an Imam. No one else should claim, 'I am an Imam.' The second type of person is the one who denies the Imam appointed by Allah. In Arabic, the word for denial is 'Juhud', which means to deny while knowing the truth. You know, and yet you deny; this is called 'Juhud'. So, whoever denies while knowing—for example, knowing that Ali (a.s.) is the successor of the Messenger... And the Messenger of Allah repeatedly announced the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), from the Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira to Ghadir-e-Khum and the final sermon in the mosque. If someone still says, 'We do not accept it,' then they will be deserving of these three punishments: 1. Allah will not speak to them, 2. Allah will not accept any of their deeds, and 3. There will be a painful punishment for them, no matter how much they worship. Because without Wilayah, no deed is acceptable. As mentioned in the previous session, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O people, the foundation of the religion is this.' Therefore, if they deny it, their deeds are not acceptable. And who is the third person? The one who assumes that these two—the one claiming Imamate falsely and the one denying the true Imam—are Muslims. If someone considers both of these as Muslims, they will receive the same punishment as the others. The one who is denying the Wilayah is rejecting the truth, and the one who is claiming Imamate falsely is a liar. The third person who considers them both Muslims will also face these three consequences. If one knows who the true Imam is, they should not abandon the Imam under any circumstances. And if one knows that this person is the true Imam and the other is wrong, they should raise their voice against them. They should raise their voice against them; this is very important. The problem is that when voices are not raised against falsehood, and everyone says, 'What is the need? Let it be,' then the disease spreads everywhere. The rule is that the truth must be upheld. We should follow the truth and gather around it. If we don't, this disease will spread. This is not just a minor illness; we are talking about the Hereafter, about Paradise and Hell. We must practice 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' (enjoining good) and 'Nahy an al-Munkar' (forbidding evil). We should not remain silent. Then the question arises: Did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) appoint a successor or not? This is a big question that we have been discussing for the past two or three weeks. We have been discussing this for two or three weeks, and InshaAllah, we will continue. Let me present a narration from Sunan Abi Dawud, which is also present in Sahih Bukhari with slight variations, and in Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and in other books. It is a very authentic narration. The Hadith is the narration of the twelve successors. Memorize this Hadith well so that this message reaches people. The Hadith is: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'This religion will remain strong and powerful as long as there are twelve Caliphs.' Now, look at the narration in Sunan Abi Dawud: what happened when the Prophet said this? The people started shouting 'Allahu Akbar' and making noise. The people started shouting 'Allahu Akbar' and making noise. Allah says, 'Lower your voices in the presence of the Prophet.' When the Prophet is speaking, be silent. At least show that much respect. The Quran says, 'When the Quran is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent, so that you may receive mercy.' If this is the command regarding the Quran, then the one upon whom the Quran was revealed deserves even more respect. But what was the state of the people? As soon as the Prophet spoke, they started shouting and making noise. Now you decide, who was making that noise? They must be making noise, they must be making their noise, those whose interests are not being served, those who do not like this talk of the Prophet, those who are wondering which 12 successors he is talking about, or perhaps there are other criminals who do not like this. Therefore, there is no suggestion, no peaceful gathering, even if they keep quiet... Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar! They have used this [phrase] to the point that at least they say Allahu Akbar, but they use Allahu Akbar to cut the throats of the innocent. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar! Shouting is not the way; the truth and falsehood are not decided by shouting. Do not forget to share, the hadith is present, Hadith number 4280, Sahih Bukhari, Hadith number 4280. Be alert, wake up! When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says something, when people start making noise and creating a ruckus, then these people... some people say, 'What was this? Why did he say this?' His companions were close to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'What happened?' His companions said, 'This is what he said.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Leave them alone...' He said, 'Leave them alone.' This is in the books, this is in the books, or perhaps there was some discussion. Regarding this noise-making, another hadith is found. You should know, and it is present in Sahih Bukhari, in other books as well. And that hadith is that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Bring me a pen and paper so that I may write something for you, after which you will never go astray, which will be the cause of your guidance,' bring me a pen and paper... some people were there—I will not take names, you should go and read it so that your investigation continues—some people said something. I will not repeat the sentence, but the sentence was such that it is disrespectful to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Such insolence, such bad manners, that this is the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)—he is delirious, he is talking nonsense! They keep saying he is delirious... He is delirious, he is talking nonsense. The one who is the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), what is the verdict about him? You know what he said? 'Inna ha-rajul'—this man, this man, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is not delirious, nothing—'Inna ha-rajul yahjur'—this man has lost his mind, he is talking nonsense. 'Ma shaanuhu, ahajr?'—has he lost his mind? Look at who he is talking about! He is talking about the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). And people have done so much, and they even try to justify it. They justify it! This justification... this is the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and this is the insult. And there can be no justification for this. For a man to say such things about the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), whether he remains within the fold of Islam or not, the Muslims have to decide. This is present in Sahih Bukhari, in it, it is decided... It is present in Bukhari, it is present in Musnad Ahmad, besides that, it is present in Dalail al-Nubuwwah. It is present in the Sahih of Muslim as well. Then after that, it is present in the Sunan of Tirmidhi, and in many references, this is present. The religion will remain as long as there are 12 Caliphs, 12 Amirs, 12 successors—different words have been used. And along with that, another condition was set. He said, 'La yazalu hadha al-din'—this religion will remain until the Day of Judgment. So look here, two things: one, the religion will not be erased; second, there will be 12 Caliphs, 12 Imams, 12 successors. Both things are mentioned together. This means that this chain of 12 will continue until the Day of Judgment. And interestingly, let me tell you that this is the same hadith that those people used at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah who usurped the right of Wilayah of Ali (a.s.)... They usurped the right of Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). In Saqifah Bani Sa'idah, they used this. The Ansar stood up. The Ansar said, 'We, the Ansar, helped the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), so we should be the ones [in charge].' So the Ansar were declared fools by saying, 'Listen, the three of us... this is the tribe of Quraish, and the Caliphate must be from Quraish.' So, 'We are Quraish, and you are not, so we should be the Amirs.' So they said, 'We will be the Amirs, and you just stay with us.' This is their advice, 'Give us your allegiance, let us be the Caliphs.' This hadith was used there at Saqifah Bani Sa'idah. You know the incident of Saqifah Bani Sa'idah—I request the children and the youth to read history. The money of all these people is available; you read it. Saqifah Bani Sa'idah, what happened there? The Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) funeral was lying there, and to bury the body, no new Muslim from Mecca... To bury the body, no new Muslim from Mecca... in Medina, there was a population of 500,000 Muslims. Today, if someone dies there, at least two or three hundred people stand for the funeral prayer. Here, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), who brought Islam, at his funeral, there were only a maximum of 12 people. The rest were busy deciding who would be the Caliph. And here, too, the Muslims have a justification for this. The justification is that the issue of the Caliphate was so important, the subject was so important, that leaving the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) shroud and burial, they went to... this is written in the books, we are not making anything up. It is explicitly written: 'Importance of the issue of the Caliphate of the Messenger.' Leaving the Messenger, this... Leaving the Messenger, this... someone's father... and they have to use this. They were already in control. And a sentence from history is found that they were giving the news of the Caliphate to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Suddenly, loud voices of Takbir were raised. He asked his companions, 'What is this sound? Why is this Takbir being raised?' The answer was given, 'They are busy with their own affairs.' Allahu Akbar, and what else? So in Saqifah Bani Sa'idah, when the Ansar, who were a large tribe, said they wanted to be the ones, they were silenced in this way. So let's see how historians justified these 12 Imams. Where did they bring them from? It became a bone in their throat. First, tell us the names, what are they? Then, how did they justify it? That the first ones were the Rightly Guided Caliphs, there are four Caliphs... And in this, the fourth Caliph, he is talking about them, not himself. If we... let's assume for 10-15 minutes, just for the sake of argument, that these are our leaders, but anyway, after that, what you are mentioning, this is present in the books, and it is present in the Sahih of Muslim, and after that, the fifth, sixth, seventh... where is the eighth? Where is the ninth? Where is the tenth? Where is the eleventh? Where is the twelfth? Why did this chain stop here? If you go further, there would be 12. It's very simple. And the other thing is, leave the incident aside, I don't want to go into the details of that, otherwise, there will be many problems. If Yazid is the Messenger of Allah's successor, then on such an Islam... If he is the Messenger of Allah's successor, then on such an Islam... what was written about him in history, this is not even being discussed. This is a fact that he used to play with monkeys and dogs. It is present in the books that he was... this is very important. In the year 63 Hijri, he was the one who martyred the grandson of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Imam Hussain (a.s.). In the year 63 Hijri, he attacked Medina. And how did he attack? How did he plunder Medina? It is a stain that his soldiers misbehaved with the girls and women of Medina, because of which 100,000 illegitimate children were born. That is a large number, or if you say 10,000, it is still a large number of illegitimate children born, and... And Yazid's soldiers... while the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) hadith is what? You know the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) hadith: 'Whoever frightens the people of Medina, Allah will frighten him on the Day of Judgment.' And during the time of Yazid, regarding what he did, there can be no comparison. If Allah frightens someone, you can understand what his condition will be, what his state will be. Now you know what his condition will be. 'Man akhafa ahl al-Madinah, akhafahu Allah yawm al-Qiyamah.' He, Yazid, you say he is the Messenger of Allah's successor? This is 62 Hijri. In 63 Hijri, this same Yazid sent his army, and his army attacked the Kaaba. They rained fireballs on the Kaaba. Oh Muslims, oh people, this has nothing to do with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), there is no book, no discussion. So it doesn't matter to the Muslims, if someone says something bad about the Kaaba, will your conscience accept this? Tell me, will your conscience accept that you either stop talking to someone or you speak ill of them, and if a traitor is a Muslim, will the public ever accept them? And here, his name is being written as the successor of the Messenger. Now look at the state of this, this is a transition, and after that, you normally consider your Marwadi, others... if you are told about the deeds of the Banu Umayya, you will be astonished. Just look at their history, their actions. What were they? They would lie around drunk. So, if they drank alcohol, let them handle the prayers; instead of two rak'ahs, they would lead four. Instead of two, they would lead four rak'ahs, and in the state of intoxication, they would perform the prayer. And if the people asked, they would say, 'If your hearts are not satisfied, we will add more.' This was the state of the Banu Umayya, and they are called the successors of the Messenger. Allahu Akbar. And after that, the second list... well, in the first list, there was one more thing. Did you notice that in this list, Ali... Did you notice that in this list, after Ali (a.s.), there is no name of Imam Hasan (a.s.) or Imam Husain (a.s.)? You have noticed this, right? Look, these are the ones who are drunkards and gamblers, and their names are included. That is, the ones about whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Sayyid al-Shabab Ahl al-Jannah' (the leaders of the youth of Paradise), and these are the 300 hadith—that Hasan and Husain are the leaders of the youth of Paradise—their names are not there. Then, on this... this is the Islam found with them, and with these drunkards, you see, they are honored. This is the religion; the destruction you see today is because of this. Now look at the second list. This was the first list of the robbers, and the second list... now in this, the first four... they did a great favor by including the fifth one, but look at the enmity. This was... let's move on. Then after that, this is what was said, now such... Then after that, this is what was said, now such a list was prepared... now you look at it at home. Then it became a big problem for Jalaluddin Suyuti. So what did he do? He said there will be two Mahdis—two awaited Mahdis who are expected. And what did you notice? They will come, two will come. Now look, this is a strange situation; he turned one into two. Initially, they were not ready to accept one Mahdi, and now look, they are adjusting it to two. So they will adjust it like this. That is why a couplet of Zauq comes to mind, which Zauq said: 'The eyes of the heart are open, and the eyes of the head are also open, yet they are blind.' And despite that, I am surprised at how Allah blinds people. Everything is in front of them, and there is a reference to it—in Al-Suyuti, page 19, and in the history, page... and you will see that this... And you will see that this... if you have not subscribed yet, then until it reaches your account, it means... that when this chain broke, it was broken, or the chain is wrong, or the chain you created is wrong. And then, your chain only goes up to the third or fourth generation. So you see what needs to be done. That is why we request you to look at the narrations once. Although in their books, they have... and look at this, look at this way, look at this... they have not included this hadith. This hadith was named... and Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I have heard that you...' Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I have heard that you people claim that you will answer my questions, so I will accept Islam.' The condition is that the answer should be as it is written in the Torah; the answer should be as it is in the Torah. I heard... he had to answer our questions. He asked questions, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) answered the ten questions. He said, 'Absolutely correct, this is the answer.' And on the other side, I have another question: 'Tell me the names of your successors.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) started counting the names. 'Hasan, Husain...' When he reached here, he said, 'In the Torah, it is exactly like this: in place of Ali, it is Yusha, and his two sons, Shabbar and Shabbir.' These two sons are written exactly like this in the Torah. After that, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) continued and told the names of the rest. These are the great scholars of the Ahlulbayt who included this in their books, that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) told the names, and that Jewish scholar accepted Islam at the hands of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). He accepted Islam at the hands of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and I accept Islam. Look, this is completely simple... And I accept Islam. Look, this is completely simple, a very simple thing. That if we believe, then it is absolutely clear. Now we move forward here. An explanation of a hadith... what is it? It is not a hadith, but a biography that has been described. Our... you know, Sheikh Saduq's book... first, let me tell you about Sheikh Saduq, so that the enemies, the ones who are... for them, it becomes clear that we are talking about Sheikh Saduq. He was very truthful. What was his name? Muhammad ibn Ali... he was Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, Sheikh Saduq, al-Qummi. And... when the chain of the minor occultation ended, Sheikh Saduq was in the period of the major occultation... He was in the period of the major occultation, and he saw the time of the minor occultation. In front of him, there were... his students were there, and after that, Sheikh Saduq became a scholar and a leader. In fact, in our tradition, he is called 'Saduq' (the truthful). And his title is 'Ra'is al-Muhaddithin' (the leader of the traditionists). This means that all the traditions were under his authority, that is his position. This is Sheikh Saduq. The specialty of Sheikh Saduq was that he would not talk about anything except hadith. Whatever he wrote, he wrote only based on hadith. He would show the miracle of hadith, and he had great contemporaries. All the great scholars were in front of him, and they all acknowledged him. And these great elders, all of them... look, nowadays some people have come into our society, and I doubt whether they are Shia or not. Their appearance is more Shia than the Shias, they are properly dressed as Shias, but they deny the infallibility of the Imams (a.s.), they deny the hadith, they deny the infallibility of the Prophets (a.s.), they even deny the infallibility of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), they deny the infallibility of the Infallibles, and they say, 'How can he make a mistake?' They completely deny the narrations and say, 'Our approach is the Quran only.' This is their slogan. Remember this slogan... This is their slogan. Remember this slogan, keep it well in mind. These are their words—even if they change a little, understand that these are the same people—that our approach, our methodology, is the Quranic methodology. And today they start... now if there is any such thing, then these are the people who deny all hadith, who remember the great scholars with bad words, even to the extent that they use bad words for Sheikh Saduq. They claim bad things about Allama Majlisi, they insult him, and all this is present in the evidence. The evidence is present. In such matters, these are their chats, their chats are present. If anyone wants, we can present the evidence for it. So, about these 'Quran-only' people, they have used words like 'ignorant' and such for Sheikh Saduq. Allama Hilli, who did this work, gave them a life, and today the Shiaism that exists, Allama Majlisi has a huge hand in it, along with Allama Hilli. Allama Majlisi and a huge hand... those who know history and events well, otherwise, it was not Shiaism. It was not... but these two are our scholars... But these two are our scholars. Allama Hilli (r.a.) and Allama Majlisi (r.a.) had a huge contribution. Anyway, these are... so we are telling you that Allama Majlisi and others, all of them have acknowledged the authority of Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), they have trusted his narrations. They are great scholars, they have a huge position. And his book is 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', which is one of our four books. So he wrote the book here. Now remember, and this book, all these... if you ask any scholar, they will tell you that this is a book of hadith. But these people will do a lot of research in it, they will discuss the hadith a lot, but they will discuss... you will read it line by line. The book's name is 'Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih', and it has been translated into English as 'Shi'a Creed'. Asaf Ali Fyzee translated it. 'Shi'a Creed' is Sheikh Saduq's book, 'Risalat al-I'tiqadat'... Sheikh Saduq's book, 'Risalat al-I'tiqadat', and then he starts: 'Our belief, our belief about these oppressors.' About these oppressors who have usurped the rights of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.)... 'The oppressor, the one who usurped, he is not just the one who did it, but also the one who helped him, and not just the one who helped, but the one who remained silent and kept watching the show.' This is all on them, this is all on them, because he who is pleased with the action of a people is like one who participated in it. On one side, our Shia belief is about these oppressors: 'La'natullah alayhim' (the curse of Allah be upon them). I will tell you, if anyone asks for the proof of this, for its evidence, there were hundreds of narrations. It is not just from one place, it is from the narrations... 'La'natullah alayhim' (the curse of Allah be upon them). And this is a great event, and this is 'Bara'at' (disassociation) and it is on them... and these are wedding instruments, and it is obligatory upon them. Now, there are many justifications for this, let's move forward from this and subscribe. They did not subscribe in this way; they did not subscribe—what is this? This is a war, but we do not know about them. It is strange that they are reading it, but we do not know who they are. Just like I don't know, why have you become so naive that you—you have seen many books. With great diligence, in 80-80 volumes, history, lessons, programs—therefore, volumes, volumes, they have written the most, and you do not know the volumes of the Messenger (s.a.w.a.)? That when the claim was formally presented in the court, you rejected it, that when the Princess (s.a.) entered the court, and the veil that the Princess (s.a.) was wearing, you tore it into pieces, so how will you understand the matter? It will not be understood. That is why all this will keep happening. And these were the same people who, after that, what is there to say? That when they refused to express their condolences, they sent their goons. They are using foul language, and this is nothing but hooliganism. History is witness that they set fire to the house of Syeda Zahra (s.a.), and shouted from outside, 'Set fire to the house, hand over Ali (a.s.) to us.' And the Princess (s.a.) called out from inside, 'Will you set fire to the house in which Ali (a.s.), Fatima (s.a.), Hasan (a.s.), and Hussain (a.s.) are?' They called out again, 'We do not care who is inside, I am the daughter of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), we do not care about that either.' And they set fire, and they set fire to the door, and Zahra (s.a.) was behind the door, and in this way, they kicked the door so that... in this way, they kicked the door so that the door fell upon the Princess (s.a.). The burning door crushed the Princess (s.a.) between the door and the wall. She cried out, 'Father, come to help!' The incident is the same, and some even say that the Princess (s.a.) complained to the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) at that time, 'Father, what has been done to me?' 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' The looters have arrived. You came here, what happened there? There, the gathering... Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)—through the statements, for the sake of the eyes, for all of us, it was completely closed, that the Holy Quran and... subscribe from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), absolutely, this is the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) direction is this, and the names of the Twelve Imams (a.s.) are mentioned in the Quran explicitly. We are very grateful to you and to all the viewers, we are grateful for joining us in this program, for participating with us. Respected viewers, along with this, I would like to thank you once again. The grand quiz that was held last week regarding the life of the helper of Islam, Hazrat Abu Talib (a.s.), his biography, you participated in it, we are deeply grateful to you for this. Those who were the winners of the quiz, all those people who gave the correct answers to all the questions, you can see their names on our social media sites. And respected viewers, in this series, as we move along, our discussion is starting from this Thursday regarding the Twelve Imams (a.s.), whose leader is Hazrat Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), Amir-ul-Momineen Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). It is a request to present a few couplets in the court of Maula (a.s.), in the praise of the family of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). present a few couplets in the praise of the family of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). It is written from eternity, 'Zikr-e-Asman-e-Un-Waliyon', the family of Ali (a.s.)... if all the promises of the world become false, it should not happen that the hand of God is between them. Those who raised the name of Ali (a.s.), those who raised the name of Ali (a.s.)... the tablet of Ali's (a.s.) name is correct on the Kaaba, on the door of Ali (a.s.) is written the status of those... the height of Ali (a.s.) reached the stars, searching for the height... Along with this, we also invite you for next week. We will be waiting for all the viewers. Keep participating in this program with your questions. Remember us in your prayers. Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa Muhammadin... (recitation of prayers).

chapters.title: The Divine Appointment of Imamate
chapters.summary: The lecture establishes that Imamate is a divine prerogative and that rejecting the divinely appointed Imam is equivalent to the rebellion of Iblis.

chapters.title: Consequences of Rejecting Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the severe spiritual consequences for those who falsely claim Imamate, those who deny the true Imam, and those who consider both groups as legitimate Muslims.

chapters.title: The Hadith of the Twelve Successors
chapters.summary: The speaker references authentic historical narrations regarding the twelve successors of the Prophet and highlights the disrespect shown by some companions when these truths were proclaimed.

chapters.title: The Incident of Saqifah Bani Sa'idah
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the historical events at Saqifah, where the leadership was decided while the Prophet's funeral was still pending.

chapters.title: Critique of Caliphate Successions and Yazid
chapters.summary: The lecture challenges the legitimacy of historical caliphs, particularly criticizing the actions and character of Yazid.

chapters.title: The Twelve Imams and Prophetic Hadith
chapters.summary: The speaker addresses attempts by scholars to reconcile historical inconsistencies regarding the twelve successors and references a hadith about the Prophet naming the Imams.

chapters.title: The Authority of Sheikh Saduq
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces Sheikh Saduq and his role in documenting the history and traditions of the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Sheikh Saduq and the Quran-Only Movement
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces Sheikh Saduq as a foundational scholar of Hadith and warns against modern groups who reject traditions and the infallibility of the Imams.

chapters.title: The Importance of Hadith and Shia Beliefs
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the scholarly contributions of Allama Hilli and Allama Majlisi, while emphasizing the importance of disassociation (Bara'at) from those who oppressed the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: The Tragedy of Syeda Zahra (s.a.)
chapters.summary: The speaker recounts the historical events surrounding the attack on the house of Syeda Zahra (s.a.) and the suffering she endured.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Future Discussions
chapters.summary: The session concludes with a mention of the Twelve Imams, a thank you to quiz participants, and a transition to future topics regarding the Ahlulbayt.

title: SHAHZAADI-E-KAUNAIN (s.a.) GRAND QUIZ | 25-Jan-2022 🇮🇳 9.00 pm IST 🇬🇧 15.30 GMT
excerpt: This lecture provides a comprehensive overview of the virtues, spiritual significance, and historical origins of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.). It explores the divine status of the Ahlul-Bayt, the profound meaning behind her names, and the immense spiritual benefits of the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra. The session emphasizes the importance of this specific dhikr as a means of seeking nearness to Allah and highlights the sanctity of the soil of Karbala in spiritual practice.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance and our relief through them. Bless them all. From Fatimatuz Zahra (a.s.), daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). She said, I heard Fatima (a.s.) saying, 'My father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), came to me on one of the days. He said, Peace be upon you, O Fatima. I said, And upon you be peace. He said, I find weakness in my body. I said to him, I seek refuge for you in Allah, O my father, from weakness. He said, O Fatima, bring me the Yemeni cloak and cover me with it.' So I brought him the Yemeni cloak and covered him with it, and I began to look at him, and his face was shining as if it were the full moon on the night of its perfection and completion. It was not long before my son, Hasan (a.s.), approached and said, Peace be upon you, O mother. I said, And upon you be peace, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart. He said, O mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). I said, Yes, your grandfather is under the cloak. So Hasan approached the cloak and said, Peace be upon you, O grandfather, O Messenger of Allah, do you give me permission to enter with you under the cloak? He said, 'And peace be upon you, O my son and O owner of my pond (Hawd), I have given you permission.' So he entered with him under the cloak. It was but an hour, when my son Al-Husayn (a.s.) approached and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Mother.' I said, 'And peace be upon you, O coolness of my eyes and fruit of my heart.' He said, 'O Mother, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' I said, 'Yes, your grandfather and your brother are under the cloak.' So Al-Husayn approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O my grandfather, O Messenger of Allah, do you give me permission to enter with you under the cloak?' He said, 'And peace be upon you, O my son and O intercessor of my nation, I have given you permission.' So he entered with them under the cloak. After that, Abul-Hasan Ali ibn Abi Talib approached and said, 'Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah.' I said, 'And peace be upon you, O Abul-Hasan and O Commander of the Faithful.' He said, 'O Fatimah, I smell a pleasant scent from you, as if it is the scent of my brother and cousin, the Messenger of Allah.' I said, 'Yes, he is here with your two sons under the cloak.' So Ali (a.s.) approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, do you give me permission to be with you under the cloak?' He said, 'And peace be upon you, O my brother, my successor, my caliph, and the bearer of my standard, I have given you permission.' So Ali entered under the cloak. Then I approached the cloak and said, 'Peace be upon you, O my father, O Messenger of Allah, do you give me permission to be with you under the cloak?' He said, 'And peace be upon you, O my daughter and O part of me, I have given you permission.' So I entered under the cloak. When we were all gathered under the cloak, my father, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), took the two ends of the cloak and gestured with his right hand toward the sky and said, 'O Allah, these are my Ahlul-Bayt, my elite, and my close ones. Their flesh is my flesh and their blood is my blood. What hurts them hurts me, and what saddens them saddens me. I am at war with those who war against them, at peace with those who are at peace with them, an enemy to those who show enmity toward them, and a lover of those who love them. They are from me and I am from them. So bestow Your blessings, Your benedictions, Your mercy, Your forgiveness, and Your pleasure upon me and upon them, and remove impurity from them and purify them with a thorough purification.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, 'O My angels and O inhabitants of My heavens, I have not created the established sky, nor the spread-out earth, nor the shining moon, nor the luminous sun, nor the rotating planets, nor the flowing seas, nor the sailing ships, except for the love of these five.' I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah bless you, O Wali al-Asr, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance, assist us. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the noblest of the prophets and messengers, and upon his pure and purified family, and the curse of Allah be upon all their enemies. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Proof, son of Al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience, and allow him to enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and hasten their reappearance. Zahra is your domain, as is Paradise and Fadak. These mountains, these trees, this water, and the heavens too. From the side of the Jewel (Ali), even the angels are in servitude. O Lady, even the salt is included in your dowry. The world is settled only on your lands; for centuries, the world has only been eating your salt. Honorable viewers, we, on behalf of 'The Strong Rope', welcome you all to this grand quiz and offer our congratulations on this great day, the day on which our Princess of the two worlds, Lady Zahra (s.a.), was born. And we also offer our gift of greetings to the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), especially to the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). In today's special program, we have with us Mr. Abbas Patel and Mr. Ahsan Jafri. We welcome you both to this program as well. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. And peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. And we offer our congratulations to you both on this great day. Congratulations to you too, and truly, what a blessed date it is, the day the Princess of the two worlds (s.a.) arrived in this world. And truly, the personality of the Princess is so blessed that regarding the Princess herself, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) states: 'Li-Fatimata 'alayhas-salamu tis'atu asma'in 'indallahi 'azza wa jall'—meaning, with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Lady Fatimah Zahra (s.a.) has nine names. And what are those nine names? Fatimah, Siddiqah, Al-Mubarakah, At-Tahirah, Az-Zakiyah, Ar-Radiyah, Al-Mardiyah, Al-Muhaddathah, and Zahra. These nine names of the Princess (s.a.), the Imam (a.s.) states, are names that Allah has chosen for the Princess at the 'Maqam-e-Indiyat' (the station of nearness to Allah). Among these is the name 'Al-Mubarakah'. And what a joyous occasion this is, and we truly offer our congratulations to all the viewers on this joyous occasion. And there is another interesting thing in this Hadith; it is a fascinating point that the Imam (a.s.) did not just stop after stating these nine names, but the Imam (a.s.) asks the narrator. The Imam asks: 'Atadri ayyu shay'in tafsiru Fatimah?'—meaning, do you know what the interpretation of the name Fatimah is? What is the meaning of Fatimah? The narrator said, "Tell me," and the narrator says that I said, "Akhbirni ya Sayyidi" (Inform me, O my master), O my master, O my leader and chief, O my lord, please tell me, please explain it to me. After that, the Imam (a.s.) explained the interpretation of the word Fatima, the meaning of the name Fatima. The Imam says that the interpretation of this name is, "Qala alayhis-salam futimat minash-shar" (He, peace be upon him, said: She has been separated from evil), meaning the interpretation of the name Fatima, the meaning of Fatima is that she—meaning the Princess, peace be upon her—has been kept away by Allah from all evil. That is, Ahsan Bhai, all those people whom Janabe Zahra (s.a.) distanced herself from, even if it were regarding her own funeral, all those people are counted among the evil. Indeed, indeed, all of them will be included in the evil. Whoever the Princess (s.a.) is distant from, it is because Allah has kept evil away from the Princess. So, whoever the Princess (s.a.) expressed her disassociation from, whose greeting she did not return, whom she did not allow to participate in her funeral, whoever she maintained distance from, all of them are evil according to this Hadith. And in the end, the Imam (a.s.) states in this Hadith that, "Lawla anna Amir al-Mu'minin alayhis-salam" (If it were not for Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him), that if Amir al-Mu'minin, Hazrat Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) were not there, meaning if he were not there, "tazawwaja-ha" (to marry her), "lama kana laha kufuwan" (there would have been no match for her), then there would be no equal to the Princess, no match for her in this entire universe. And it is not just for that time, no, "ila yawmil qiyama" (until the Day of Judgment), there would be no match for the Princess until the Day of Judgment. "Ala wajhil arz" (on the face of the earth), and the most interesting thing, there would be no match, no one would come until the Day of Judgment who would be equal to the Princess. "Adam faman dunahu" (Adam and those below him), whether it is Hazrat Adam (a.s.) or anyone else. Meaning, no one can equal the Master of the Universe in this virtue. So here, Ahsan Bhai, Abbas Bhai, I am reminded of a sentence by Allama Irfan Haider Abidi Shaheed, which he recited in one of his majalis, that if Hazrat Adam (a.s.) cannot compete with Imam Ali (a.s.), cannot compete with Janabe Zahra (s.a.), then how could the sinful progeny of Adam compete with them? Wah, wah, wah, indeed, indeed. And in this connection, four verses of Janab Fanoos Barwani Sahib come to mind, please listen: Who is the equal of the Lion of God except Batool? Who is the equal of the Lion of God except Batool? Whose status is this in both worlds except Batool? One is the King of Men and one is the source of purity, La fata illa Ali, La tahira illa Batool. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. Indeed, you mentioned the names of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), one of them is 'Mubaraka' (The Blessed One), and one proof of her being Mubaraka is the Tasbih attributed to her name, which contains the remembrance of the Divine; it is so blessed that when a child is taught prayer, they are also urged to recite the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) along with it. Indeed. And this Tasbih of Janabe Zahra holds such importance for us that in our mosques after every prayer, and in the shrines of the Infallible Imams (a.s.), after every prayer, it is emphasized that this Tasbih should be recited. And our topic today, the subject of our discussion, is the Tasbih of Zahra (s.a.)—what that Tasbih is, how it should be recited, and what its importance is. So let us first see what the story behind this Tasbih is. Tanveer Bhai, although this Tasbih brings a wave of blessings into the lives of the believers, and as Ahsan Bhai mentioned, the name of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is Mubaraka, and we benefit from many of its blessings in our lives. But we are not attentive to those blessings. If one wants to understand how the blessing of this Tasbih was in the life of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) herself, let us turn to its story. How did this Tasbih come about? And why did the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) teach this Tasbih to Janabe Zahra (s.a.)? The incident is narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), who says that when Janabe Zahra (s.a.) used to be busy with household chores, she had to endure so much hardship that, for example, when she would fill the water skin, it was so heavy that her hand would get injured from carrying it. Or when Janabe Zahra (s.a.) would operate the hand mill, her hands would often bleed due to the exertion. Or, for example, when Janabe Zahra (s.a.) was busy cleaning the house, the dust and dirt would affect her clothes. Or when she would light the stove—in that era, we didn't have a gas system like we do today—she had to blow to ignite the fire, and the smoke from that would affect her clothes. Amir al-Mu'minin could not bear to see this condition of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) consulted with Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and suggested that why don't you go to your father and request a maidservant? Following the suggestion of Amir al-Mu'minin, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) left the house and went towards the mosque. There, she saw that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was conversing with some companions. The sentences of the Hadith are as follows: "Fa'atat-in-Nabiyya salla-llahu alayhi wa alihi fawajadat indahu khuddasan" (She went to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and found him with some people). Janabe Zahra (s.a.) went to the mosque and saw that the Messenger of Allah was talking to people. "Fastahayt" (She felt shy), meaning the Princess felt shy to present this service or request in front of those people, in front of the Messenger of Allah. And because they were non-mahram (strangers) to the Princess, and she did not consider it appropriate to reveal her voice in front of non-mahrams, she turned back and returned home. Abbas Bhai, it is very important to pause here and say that this was indeed the way of the household of Ale Muhammad (a.s.), their method was that the women of their house, even their voices, would never reach the ears of a non-mahram. This is a lesson for us too, that we should also try to ensure that the voices of the women of our house do not reach non-mahrams. And one more thing, although this is an occasion of happiness and not a place for lamentation, one thing definitely shakes the mind. If we look at the action of the Princess, as you just described, Abbas Bhai, that the Princess felt shy that her voice might reach the ears of those non-mahrams, and that is why she returned home. Those very people, those who claimed to recite the Kalima of the Prophet, who knows what atrocities they must have committed against the Princess, that after the martyrdom of the Prophet, the same Princess who was feeling shy yesterday was forced to protest to claim her right and had to come to the court. May God's curse be upon those who caused pain to the Princess. Indeed. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came to the Princess's house the next day because he saw that the Princess had come to the mosque and left without speaking. So, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked Janabe Zahra, "What was the reason for coming to the mosque yesterday, daughter?" Before the Princess could explain, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) explained the whole situation, how Janabe Zahra (s.a.) has to endure various hardships to perform household chores, and the suggestion that Amir al-Mu'minin had made, for which Janabe Zahra had gone to the service of the Messenger of Allah. Now, after hearing this whole story, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said to Amir al-Mu'minin and Janabe Zahra, the sentences of the Hadith are: "Qala salla-llahu alayhi wa alihi afla u'allimukuma ma huwa khayrul lakuma minal khadim?" (Shall I not teach you both something that will be better for you than this servant?) "Iza akhaztuma manamakuma" (When you go to your sleep), meaning the Messenger of Allah said that whenever you go to sleep, before sleeping, recite this Tasbih—which we know as the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra—he taught this Tasbih, and certainly, the teaching of this Tasbih that the Messenger of Allah gave to Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and Amir al-Mu'minin, because of it and its reason, Because of which so many blessings came into the life of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) that they cannot be counted. Meaning, if you pay attention to the fact that Janabe Zahra is asking the Messenger of Allah for a maidservant, and the Messenger of Allah in return is teaching Janabe Zahra a Tasbih. Meaning, whenever you go to sleep, recite this Tasbih before it, which we know as the Tasbih of Zahra. So, surely there were blessings in this Tasbih because of which her household chores became easy. And indeed, perhaps it is the blessing of this Tasbih that a queen like Janabe Fizza, a companion like Janabe Salman, and angels like Janabe Jibra'il and Mika'il used to come to her door to serve her. Indeed, wah. Correct. And as far as the method of reciting this Tasbih is concerned, another similar incident is found which is narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) himself. And Amir al-Mu'minin says that some non-Arab kings had presented servants and maidservants to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) as gifts. And when these servants were present with the Messenger of Allah, at that time Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) suggested to Janabe Zahra that you should request a maidservant from your father so that your household chores might become easier. So Janabe Zahra (s.a.) came to the Messenger of Allah and requested him, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to Janabe Zahra, "Daughter, shall I give you a gift that is better than this maidservant and better than everything that exists in this world?" And then the Messenger of Allah taught this Tasbih to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), in which he said that first recite Allah-o-Akbar 34 times, then Alhamdulillah 33 times, and then Subhan Allah 33 times, and then end this Tasbih with La ilaha illallah. So this is a method that the Messenger of Allah described regarding the performance of this Tasbih. Meaning, after completing the entire Tasbih, it is necessary to say La ilaha illallah once at the end. Yes. Once, meaning end this Tasbih with La ilaha illallah. Because the Messenger of Allah taught this Tasbih to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), that is why this Tasbih was attributed to the name of Janabe Zahra and it was called the Tasbih of Zahra (s.a.). Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. Furthermore, when a companion came to Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) and asked about the method of this Tasbih, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) actually recited the Tasbih and showed him, and the narrator says that I counted that first Imam Sadiq (a.s.) recited Allah-o-Akbar 34 times, after that Alhamdulillah until the count reached 67, and then Imam Sadiq (a.s.) started the recitation of Subhan Allah until the count reached 100. Meaning the entire Tasbih consists of 100 recitations. 100, meaning it consists of statements. And the Imam (a.s.) actually recited this Tasbih and showed it. Meaning, if these Hadiths and incidents are looked at, then this is also the saying of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), meaning the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) told the method of reciting this Tasbih, and Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) himself recited this Tasbih and showed how it should be recited. Meaning, for us who believe in the Imams (a.s.) and the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), through their actions and their sayings, it is absolutely clear to us how this Tasbih should be recited. Correct. Meaning, on one side there was the saying of the Messenger of Allah and on the other side the action of an Infallible Imam. Both are proof for us on how this Tasbih will be recited. Dear viewers, now we move towards a very important topic: Is the mention of the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) found in the Holy Quran or not? Meaning, Tanveer Bhai, we have seen the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah, meaning the Sunnah, now we are moving towards the Quran. Yes, so that those who say that we need proof for everything from the Quran, for them too, it is proven that its mention is in the Quran. In the Quran, Surah Al-Ahzab, which is the 33rd Surah, verse number 41, Allah (S.W.T.) states: 'Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū udhkurū Allāha dhikran kathīrā' (O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance). Now, our question to those who demand proof from the Quran for everything and hold the belief of 'Hasbuna Kitabullah' (The Book of Allah is sufficient for us) is: what is the meaning of this verse? Does it mean that a person should sit with prayer beads and just keep saying 'Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah'? What does it mean? And Allah, whose remembrance no human can fully perform—if we cannot count the blessings Allah has given us, we cannot perform the complete praise and glorification of Allah, not even in a small measure. So, when Allah says in this verse to perform 'Dhikr-e-Kathir' (much remembrance), what does it mean? We are followers of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and we are followers of Hadith-e-Saqalain. If we read a verse of the Quran, we seek its interpretation in the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Tanveer Bhai, you made a very good point that the blessings Allah has given are unlimited, infinite; there is no limit or end to them. As you just said, it does not mean that a person should sit with prayer beads and keep saying 'Allah-Allah' all day. No one can fulfill the right of Allah's praise. Indeed. Despite that, Allah commands in the Quran to perform 'Dhikr-e-Kathir'. Indeed. So, if the One whose praise and glorification cannot be fully fulfilled is saying to perform 'Dhikr-e-Kathir', then its interpretation must be very interesting and worth seeing. Yes, absolutely. For the interpretation of this verse, we will take the support of our sixth Imam, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.). One of his famous companions named Zurarah narrates that Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said that the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is that 'Dhikr-e-Kathir'. Meaning, the 'Dhikr-e-Kathir' mentioned here is nothing but the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). And after reading this hadith, the Imam (a.s.) recited this verse: 'Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū udhkurū Allāha dhikran kathīrā'. Wow, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. Apart from this, we also find another verse which is very famous, verse number 152 of Surah Baqarah, in which Allah (S.W.T.) states: 'Fadhkurūnī adhkurkum' (Remember Me, and I will remember you). Everyone remembers Allah, but for Allah to remember a human is a matter of great honor. In the context of this verse, another famous companion of our sixth Imam, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), named Muhammad ibn Muslim, who belongs to the tribe of Janabe Mukhtar-e-Thaqafi, narrates. Oh, Tanveer Bhai, so this is the same tribe of Bani Thaqif to which Janabe Mukhtar belonged? Yes, this hadith is narrated by Janabe Muhammad ibn Muslim, who was a prominent and famous companion of Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Yes. So, Muhammad ibn Muslim says—it is narrated from him—that in the context of this verse, he says that the Tasbih of Fatima Zahra (s.a.) is the remembrance of Allah, and this is the remembrance that when a person performs it, they will be included in the context of this verse and will become the manifestation of this verse, that they remember Allah and Allah remembers them. So, if we want to remember Allah and for Allah to remember us, we should recite the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) regularly. Subhan Allah, so the 'Dhikr-e-Kathir' found in the Quran points towards the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). Indeed. And those who are giving their own opinions in the interpretation of the Quran, where will they get this explanation from? Yes, it has been stated by the Imams (a.s.). Indeed. And from this, the importance of this Tasbih can also be estimated; on one hand, a person performs this Tasbih—what is this Tasbih? This Tasbih is attributed to Janabe Zahra (s.a.), but it is the praise and glorification of Allah. Yes. So when they, in this... Through this Tasbih, they perform the praise and glorification of Allah, then Allah will remember them. So, what can be estimated about the status of the one whom Allah remembers? Ahsan Bhai, what you said, that the remembrance of Janabe Zahra is the remembrance of Allah, reminds me of a couplet by the martyr Mohsin Naqvi. Wow! 'Jahan-e-insaniyat mein tawheed ka muqaddas khayal-e-Zahra. Sharaf mein wahdat, ada imamat, jabeen nabuwat, jamal-e-Zahra. Wow! Subhan Allah! Woh jis pe nazan dil-e-musawwir, woh naqsh-e-husn-e-kamal-e-Zahra. Khuda-e-be-misl ki khudai mein tha abad be-misal-e-Zahra.' Wow! Wow! Wow! 'Yeh shamma-e-irfan-e-Yazdi hai, markaz-e-aal-e-Mustafa hai. Hasan se Mahdi talak imamat ki yeh ibtida hai.' Hai! Hai! Subhan Allah! Wow! Wow! Allahumma Salli Ala Muhammad-o-Aal-e-Muhammad. And regarding the importance of this Tasbih, the fifth Imam, Hazrat Imam Muhammad-e-Baqir (a.s.), states: 'Ma ubidallahu bishayin min al-tahmid' (Allah is not worshipped with anything of praise) — meaning if a servant performs the praise and glorification of Allah, no servant can perform the praise of Allah through which Allah is worshipped — 'Afdal min tasbih Fatima alayha al-salam' (better than the Tasbih of Fatima (s.a.)). Subhan Allah! Which is better than the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). Meaning, there is no better way to worship Allah than this Tasbih. Wow! And the Imam further says, 'Wa law kana shayun afdalu minhu' (And if there were anything better than this Tasbih), 'Lanahalahu Rasulullahi sallallahu alayhi wa alihi Fatima alayha al-salam' (then the Prophet would have given that thing to his daughter). Meaning, the Prophet giving this Tasbih to his daughter is proof in itself that this Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is the most beloved thing to the Prophet and to Allah. Indeed. And there is so much emphasis on this Tasbih that it is recommended, a confirmed recommendation, to recite this Tasbih after every prayer. It is found in the traditions that the sixth Imam says that if a person, immediately after prayer, 'Man sabbaha tasbih Fatima alayha al-salam qabla an yathniya rijlahu' (whoever recites the Tasbih of Fatima (s.a.) before moving their legs) — meaning before moving their legs, while they have just finished the Tashahhud and Salam — 'min salat al-faridah' (after the obligatory prayer), and look, the importance is also estimated by the fact that what is the reward after the obligatory prayer? 'Ghafara Allahu lahu' (Allah will forgive them). It is the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). If a person is reciting it after the obligatory prayer while remaining in their place without moving, Allah will forgive all their sins. 'Wa yabda'u bil-takbir' (And start with Takbir), and the Tasbih that starts with 'Allahu Akbar', Takbir. Meaning, this Tasbih, and often, many times, it happens that when people have this—we have this in our homes ourselves. Every Shia home, there wouldn't be a Shia home that has a prayer mat and a Sajdagah (turbah) but not prayer beads. You will definitely find these prayer beads on the prayer mat along with the Sajdagah in every Shia home, in the home of every lover of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). This itself shows how dear this Tasbih is to us. And while reciting this Tasbih, many times it happens that if a person is not using prayer beads—because we also recite Tasbih on our fingers—many times a person gets into doubt, forgetting the count, 'How many times did I recite it?' So, its importance is also estimated by the fact that the Imam says, the sixth Imam says, 'Idha shakakta fi tasbih Fatima alayha al-salam' (If you have doubt regarding the Tasbih of Fatima Zahra (s.a.)), 'Fa'id' (then recite it again). Meaning, it's not that you continue from where you left off. The Imam said no, recite it again. This itself shows its importance. Meaning, a person should recite this Tasbih with full attention. Yes, here one must recite this Tasbih with full attention. And we ourselves see, as is the custom in our homes, and it should be, that every child is taught this Tasbih, it is emphasized, children are trained, and this is the command of our Imams (a.s.). The Imam said, the Imam said to his companion, 'Ya Aba Harun' (O Abu Harun), 'Inna na'muru sibyanana' (We, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), ourselves command our children) 'bi-tasbih Fatima alayha al-salam' (to recite the Tasbih of Fatima (s.a.)), 'Kama na'muruhum bil-salah' (just as we command them to pray). Meaning, the Tasbih is as important to the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) as prayer is. Wow! Then the Imam says, 'Falzamhu' (So be regular with it). Meaning, recite this Tasbih without fail. 'Fa-innahu lam yalzamhu 'abdun fashaqiya' (For no servant has been regular with it and become wretched). Allahu Akbar. If a person is not regular with this Tasbih, they will become wretched. I have to provide a narration regarding the reward of this Tasbih. What is the reward for the one who recites this Tasbih? Again, this narration is from Janab Muhammad ibn Muslim, who narrates from Ibn Saqfi and Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) that: ﴿مَنْ سَبَّحَ تَسْبِيحَ الزَّهْرَاءِ ثُمَّ اسْتَغْفَرَ غُفِرَ لَهُ﴾ (Whoever recites the Tasbih of Al-Zahra and then seeks forgiveness from Allah, Allah will forgive him). Wonderful! And this Tasbih is equal to 100 on the tongue. That is, ﴿وَهِيَ مِائَةٌ بِاللِّسَانِ﴾, we recite 100 beads of this Tasbih on the tongue. Yes. But in the Mizan (scale), its effect is equal to 1000. Wow. ﴿وَأَلْفٌ فِي الْمِيزَانِ وَتَطْرُدُ الشَّيْطَانَ﴾ (And 1000 in the Mizan, and it drives away Satan). Whoever Janab Zahra (s.a.) has driven away, we can include everyone in this category. Indeed, indeed. ﴿وَتَطْرُدُ الشَّيْطَانَ﴾, the effect of this Tasbih is that Satan runs away. ﴿وَتُرْضِي الرَّحْمَنَ﴾ (And it pleases the Most Merciful), and Allah is pleased with the one who recites this Tasbih. What can one say! It is truly a point worth noting, a point worth reflecting upon, that what you stated at the end, the last part of this Hadith, ﴿وَتُرْضِي الرَّحْمَنَ﴾, means this is the Tasbih that pleases Allah. On one side is the noble personality of Janab Sayyida (s.a.) herself, who pleases Allah. Subhan Allah. And on the other side is her Tasbih, which pleases Allah. Masha Allah. So, on both sides, if a person truly wants to please their Lord, then the Tasbih of Janab Zahra (s.a.) and devotion, love, and affection towards her is essential. Indeed, indeed. And there is another interesting thing about this Tasbih: when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) taught this Tasbih to Janab Zahra (s.a.) in the beginning, as you mentioned, how was this Tasbih made at that time? Janab Zahra (s.a.) initially wove this Tasbih with woolen threads and made the beads, and it was a 34-bead Tasbih in the beginning. That is, initially, it was a 34-bead Tasbih which Janab Zahra (s.a.) used to recite. When the martyrdom of Hazrat Hamza (a.s.) occurred, Janab Zahra (s.a.) used to go to his blessed grave, take the soil from that grave, and weave a Tasbih from it. Beads of the Tasbih were made from it, and not only Janab Zahra (s.a.) but all the people of Medina at that time used to do the same—they used to recite the Tasbih made from the soil of Hazrat Hamza's (a.s.) grave. This continued until that time. Until when? Until 61 AH. And after that, when the martyrdom of the Master of Martyrs, Imam Hussain ibn Ali (a.s.), occurred, this practice was established, and it became a Sunnah that after that, this Tasbih was made from the soil of the holy grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.). And that is why even today, the Tasbih beads that have the most blessings are those made from the soil of the holy grave of Imam Hussain (a.s.). That is, the pious predecessors had this practice of using a Tasbih made from soil—a Tasbih made from soil, and that too from the soil of a grave. From the soil of a grave. So, for those who run away from graves, or those who have an allergy to seeking intercession (Tawassul) from graves, this is a very good example that the Tasbih was made from soil—from the soil of a grave. You said a very good thing: those who run away from these graves and do not take blessings from them, the pious predecessors—those who were in the era of Islam—used to try to attain closeness to Allah through the soil of that grave. Subhan Allah. So, whoever keeps people away from graves, especially the graves of the friends of Allah (Awliya-Allah), is actually keeping people away from Allah. Indeed. And the blessings of this Tasbih made from Khak-e-Shifa (healing soil) are something else, something strange. Because regarding it, the sixth Imam, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), says: ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ سُبْحَةً مِنْ تُرْبَةِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ﴾ (Whoever takes a Tasbih made from the soil of Hussain (a.s.)), if a person recites Tasbih with it, they will get the reward of the Tasbih, but if they only possess the Tasbih made from Khak-e-Shifa and have not yet recited it, have not done Tilawat or Zikr, but just kept it with them, ﴿وَإِلَّا سَبَّحَتْ فِي كَفِّهِ﴾ (otherwise, it recites Tasbih in their palm by itself). This is the blessing of the Tasbih made from Khak-e-Shifa. And then the Imam says, ﴿وَإِذَا حَرَّكَهَا﴾ (And if he moves it), if he is just turning the Tasbih, the person who has the Tasbih of Khak-e-Shifa in their hand, just turning it, ﴿وَهُوَ سَاهٍ﴾ (while he is heedless), even though he is not doing Zikr, just turning it, not paying attention to the Tasbih, ﴿كُتِبَ لَهُ تَسْبِيحَةً﴾ (the reward of a Tasbih is written for him). Even though he has not recited the Tasbih yet. But if he is turning the Tasbih and also ﴿وَإِذَا حَرَّكَهَا وَهُوَ ذَاكِرُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى﴾ (and if he moves it while remembering Allah Almighty), if he is moving the beads of this Tasbih and also doing Zikr of Allah, meaning he is reciting the Tasbih, ﴿كُتِبَ لَهُ أَرْبَعِينَ تَسْبِيحَةً﴾ (the reward of 40 Tasbihs will be written for him). This is the blessing of the Tasbih made from this Khak-e-Shifa. That is, on one side is the blessing of the Tasbih of Janab Zahra (s.a.), and on top of that is the blessing of this Turbat (soil). The blessing of the Turbat. As you viewers are seeing on your screen, a timer is running. As soon as this timer reaches zero, who is this Princess? Do not forget to submit that link, that quiz. And let us finally see that if there is a mention of Janab Zahra (s.a.) and there is no mention of Imam Mahdi (a.s.), how is that possible? A story is found where a companion of the Imam, his name was Imeri, wrote a letter to our Imam of the time, Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and in that letter, he asked some questions regarding the Tasbih of Janab Zahra (s.a.), which we are presenting before you. His first question was: Can a Tasbih be made from the Turbat of Imam Hussain (a.s.), and what is its virtue? So, in response to that letter, the Imam wrote that there is nothing better than the Tasbih made from the Turbat of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Wonderful! And if that person recites its Tasbih and if he ever forgets, he will still definitely get the reward of reciting that Tasbih. That is, we should try to regularly recite the Tasbih made from the Turbat of Imam Hussain (a.s.), and God forbid, if we ever forget, we will definitely get its reward. The second question this companion asks the Imam (a.s.) is: Can a person recite Tasbih with their left hand? So the Imam replied: Indeed yes, he can recite it, there is no fault in that. And the last question he asks the Imam (a.s.) through this letter is: If a person, while reciting that Tasbih, forgets where he reached or how much he has recited, what should he do? So the Imam (a.s.) replied that he should recite that Tasbih again. Just like Tanveer Bhai, Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.) also told us the importance of the Turbat. Indeed. And besides this, there is also this Tawqi (signed letter) of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) in which the Imam gave a verdict that the Tasbih made from the Turbat—that is, made from the soil of Karbala—there is nothing better than that. Yes. So if there is any wise person, they will certainly take advantage of this Tasbih. Indeed. It is not that other things are not available on which we can do Tasbih or perform Sajdah. For example, wood; we can perform Sajdah on wood, or other things, or a mat if it is made of wood, we can perform Sajdah on it, there is no fault in that. But if we use Khak-e-Shifa, use the Turbat of Imam Hussain (a.s.), then the reward is doubled, tripled, and in fact, we saw it increases 40 times, and even if we just keep it with us, even if we are not doing Tasbih, we will continue to get benefits from it. Indeed. No wise person will leave this practice. By saying that, 'Brother, it is not available,' or making small excuses, one would not like to leave such a great benefit. Absolutely correct. And finally, the third question—the way Imam-e-Sadiq (a.s.) also said in the previous Hadith, the Imam also instructed the same thing, that if you forget, start again. Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) Allah Ta'ala Farajahu Sharif is also giving the same command that if a person forgets while reciting, he does not remember if he is reciting 'Allahu Akbar', where he has reached, how many times he has recited, how many times he has recited 'Allahu Akbar', if he has forgotten, then the Imam is saying to start again. And this is a strange connection between our Imams (a.s.) and the noble personality of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), that as you said, it is not appropriate and it is not possible that there is a mention of Janab Zahra (s.a.) and there is no mention of the Imams along with it, especially the mention of Imam-e-Zamana. Because this is such a link between Prophethood and Imamate, Janab Zahra (s.a.), especially regarding the discussion that took place about this Tasbih, I remember a couplet of the late master of poets, late Ahsan Danpuri Sahab, this couplet: 'Allah re qadro-qeemat-e-Tasbih-e-Fatima, Allah re qadro-qeemat-e-Tasbih-e-Fatima, halqe mein iske jo bhi hai dana Imam hai' (Oh, the value and worth of the Tasbih of Fatima, oh, the value and worth of the Tasbih of Fatima, whatever bead is in its circle is an Imam). Viewers, with this, we move towards the conclusion of this Princess of the Two Worlds Grand Quiz, and with this, the link for this quiz is being closed. We hope that you all have answered all its questions. We request you to stay with us. Now, God willing, the Ziyarat will be recited, and immediately after that, the names of the lucky winners will be chosen and announced through our computerized system. Therefore, it is requested of you all to pay attention to the Ziyarat. [Ziyarat text follows...] And upon Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, may Your curse be upon them forever and ever. This is a day on which the family of Ziyad and the family of Marwan rejoiced at their killing of al-Husayn, blessings of Allah be upon him. O Allah, double the curse and the painful punishment upon them from You. O Allah, I seek nearness to You on this day, in this station, and throughout the days of my life through disavowal of them, cursing them, and through allegiance to Your Prophet and the family of Your Prophet, peace be upon him and them. O Allah, curse the first oppressor who oppressed the right of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and the last one who followed him in that. O Allah, curse the group that fought al-Husayn and supported, pledged allegiance to, and followed one another in killing him. O Allah, curse them all. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah, and upon the souls that descended into your courtyard. Upon you from me is the peace of Allah forever, as long as I remain and as long as the night and day remain. May Allah not make this the last time I visit you. Peace be upon al-Husayn, upon Ali ibn al-Husayn, upon the children of al-Husayn, and upon the companions of al-Husayn. O Allah, single out the first oppressor with a curse from me, and begin with him first, then curse the second, the third, and the fourth. O Allah, curse Yazid as the fifth, and curse Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad, the son of Marjanah, Umar ibn Sa'd, Shimr, and the family of Abu Sufyan, the family of Ziyad, and the family of Marwan until the Day of Judgment. O Allah, to You belongs the praise, the praise of those who are grateful to You for their affliction. Praise be to Allah for the greatness of my calamity. O Allah, grant me the intercession of al-Husayn on the day of arrival, and establish for me a firm footing with You alongside al-Husayn and the companions of al-Husayn who sacrificed their lives for al-Husayn, peace be upon him. Allah, the Lord of Majesty, has stated in the Holy Quran: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow—and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.' O believers! Fear Allah, and every person should see what they have sent ahead for tomorrow (the Hereafter). And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is well-acquainted with what you do. My respected brothers and elders, in this noble verse, Allah, the Lord of Majesty, has addressed the believers and commanded them to adopt Taqwa (God-consciousness). Taqwa means to refrain from disobeying Allah and to obey Him. And then Allah said that every person should reflect on what they have prepared for tomorrow, meaning the Day of Judgment. We prepare a lot in this world, but have we prepared anything for the Hereafter? Have we taken stock of our deeds? Have we repented for our sins? May Allah, the Lord of Majesty, grant us the ability to prepare for our Hereafter and to save ourselves from the punishment of Allah. Ameen.
