chapters.title: The Hadith of the Cloak
chapters.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) gathers his family—Fatima, Ali, Hasan, and Husayn—under a cloak, declaring them his purified Ahlul-Bayt.

chapters.title: Celebration of Lady Zahra's Birth
chapters.summary: The speakers introduce a grand quiz program celebrating the birth of Lady Fatima Zahra (s.a.) and honor her status.

chapters.title: The Nine Names and Meaning of Fatima
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the nine names of Lady Fatima (s.a.) and explains that her name signifies her total separation from evil.

chapters.title: The Unmatched Status of Fatima and Ali
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the unique spiritual status of Lady Fatima (s.a.) and Imam Ali (a.s.), noting that no one in creation is their equal.

chapters.title: Origin of the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra
chapters.summary: The Tasbih of Janabe Zahra originated when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) offered it as a spiritual gift to his daughter to ease the hardships of her household duties.

chapters.title: Method and Significance of the Tasbih
chapters.summary: The correct method of reciting the Tasbih involves 34 Allah-o-Akbar, 33 Alhamdulillah, 33 Subhan Allah, and ending with La ilaha illallah, as taught by the Prophet and demonstrated by Imam Sadiq.

chapters.title: Quranic Basis for Dhikr
chapters.summary: The lecture explores the Quranic foundation of 'Dhikr-e-Kathir' (much remembrance) in Surah Al-Ahzab, emphasizing that the Ahlulbayt provide the necessary interpretation for such commands.

chapters.title: Tasbih of Janabe Zahra as Dhikr-e-Kathir
chapters.summary: The speakers explain that the Quranic command for 'Dhikr-e-Kathir' refers to the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), as confirmed by Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.).

chapters.title: Superiority and Importance of the Tasbih
chapters.summary: Imam Muhammad-e-Baqir (a.s.) emphasizes that no form of worship is superior to the Tasbih of Janabe Zahra (s.a.), highlighting its status as the most beloved praise of Allah.

chapters.title: Guidelines and Spiritual Rewards of the Tasbih
chapters.summary: The lecture details the etiquette of reciting the Tasbih after obligatory prayers, its power to forgive sins, and the importance of maintaining focus and regularity.

chapters.title: Spiritual Effects and Historical Origins
chapters.summary: The session concludes by discussing the immense spiritual rewards of the Tasbih, including pleasing Allah and repelling Satan, and its historical origin using soil from the grave of Hazrat Hamza (a.s.).

chapters.title: Virtues of Tasbih from Khak-e-Shifa
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the historical practice of using prayer beads made from the soil of Imam Hussain's (a.s.) grave and the immense spiritual rewards associated with them.

chapters.title: Guidance from Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) on Tasbih
chapters.summary: The speaker shares a historical letter from Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) regarding the use of Turbat for Tasbih, including protocols for recitation and handling mistakes.

chapters.title: Ziyarat Ashura and Spiritual Reflection
chapters.summary: The session concludes with the recitation of Ziyarat Ashura, followed by a brief sermon on the importance of Taqwa and preparing for the Hereafter.

title: Majlis 4 | Haq aur Baatil | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2026
excerpt: In this lecture, Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual status of Imam Hussain (a.s.) as the 'Ark of Salvation' and the 'Lamp of Guidance.' The discourse contrasts the path of truth, represented by the Ahlul-Bayt, against the path of falsehood and Satanic influence, emphasizing the necessity of following the Proof of God. The session also addresses the historical suppression of the tragedy of Karbala and highlights the unwavering devotion of figures like Habib ibn Mazahir, ultimately calling for a year-round commitment to the values of the Ahlul-Bayt.
content:
Mother Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? What kind of people are these, asking us for prayers? O prisoners, pray that this day does not come upon us. While taking prayers from us, they are also hurting our hearts. Have we reached Sham? Mother Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Of all the heads on the spears, whose head is that? It belongs to your servant, and it falls into the dust. This is the head of Abbas, his expression reveals it. Have we reached Sham? Mother Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Mother Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Children are clinging to their mothers' laps. Mothers' hands are tied with ropes in such a way. The children who are falling are dying. Have we reached Sham? Mother Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Mother Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? The son of Mushkil Kusha (the remover of difficulties) is weeping on the spear. I am the Haram, for my name has reached the lips. The slave-girls are making me weep even more. Has the evening arrived? O Amma Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? O Amma Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Sajjad's heart is being torn apart. Every wound of his is weeping in this grief. They are making me weep by mentioning Zainab's name. Has the evening arrived? O Amma Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Rihan, a clamor of weeping has erupted among the prisoners. The daughter of Zahra (s.a.) is mourning, sobbing until tomorrow. Sajjad (a.s.) is reciting a noha (elegy). Has the evening arrived? O Amma Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? What kind of time is this, they are hurting our hearts too. Has the evening arrived? O Amma Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? O Amma Fizza, tell me, why are stones being thrown? Amma Fizza, Amma Fizza, Amma Fizza, Amma Fizza, Amma Fizza, Amma Fizza. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; the best Protector and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for those who possess piety and certainty. And peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Peace be upon him and his infallible family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Especially the Remnant of Allah on the earths, the Imam of our time, our guardian, our master, our leader, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our consoler, the fortified cave, and the succor of the distressed and the helpless—may my soul and the souls of all the worlds be his ransom. To proceed: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has said in His glorious Book, and His word is the truth, and He is the most truthful of speakers: 'So race to all that is good' (Fastabiqul-khayrat). Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O Aba Abdillah. Blessings of Allah. These are the two paths. This, and besides that, besides that, listen. In Surah Al-Ahzab, verse number 4, Allah says, 'Ma ja'alallahu li-rajulin min qalbayni fi jawfihi' (Allah has not made for a man two hearts in his interior). Allah does not make two hearts in any human, He does not make two hearts. Only one heart. In the commentary of this verse, the Imam (a.s.) says, the one in whose heart there is the love of Adam (a.s.), there cannot be the love of Iblis in his heart. The one in whose heart there is the love of Ibrahim (a.s.), there cannot be the love of Nimrod in his heart. The one in whose heart there is the love of Musa (a.s.), there cannot be the love of Pharaoh in his heart. It is a tradition, brother, yes, it is a tradition. The one in whose heart there is the love of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), there cannot be the love of Abu Jahl in his heart. The one in whose heart there is the love of Ali (a.s.), there cannot be the love of anyone else in his heart. Ya Ali. Ya Ali. 'Ma ja'alallahu li-rajulin min qalbayni fi jawfihi.' There is only one path. Look at the Quran, how many verses of the Quran should I present to you? The Quran says, 'Fa-ma dha ba'dal-haqqi illad-dalal' (And what can be beyond truth except error?). The path of truth is only one. Whatever is after the truth is all error. Truth is only truth. Truth, truth. Whatever is after that is error. There is nothing but error. Nothing. Whoever held onto the hem of truth found salvation. Whoever left the truth went astray. Now people, Muslims, started looking for the truth. Where will the truth be found? The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) prayed and told us where the truth is. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) announced, 'Aliyun ma'al-haqqi wal-haqqu ma'a Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali). After that, if the matter ended here, the matter would remain incomplete. The matter would not be complete. If it were only this much, the matter would remain incomplete, that truth is with Ali, Ali is with the truth. No. The Prophet raised his hands towards the sky and said, 'Allahumma adi ril haqqa haisu ma dara' (O Allah, let the truth turn wherever Ali turns). Let the truth turn wherever Ali turns. Jazak Allah. Now people only need to find Ali. If you want to know where the truth is, look to Ali. Now, whoever removed Ali—the matter is absolutely clear. It is completely bright. There is no need for much debate on this. I have already narrated the incident in my previous service. That man's name was Sabigh Tamimi. And I mentioned the reference, look, we are not speaking from Shia books. It is explicitly in Sunan al-Darimi, Volume 1, page number 54, 55. Tafsir al-Qurtubi is a very famous commentary, Volume 4, page number 15. Tafsir Ibn Kathir—Ibn Kathir has brought it in his commentary, Volume 4, page 248. And this was the same incident I mentioned in the previous service: that when he asked a question, he was beaten so severely, so severely—and this is what used to happen. Whoever asked a question, they would beat him. We said, look, it is not surprising that he asked a question and was beaten. No. Those who justify it are worse than them. Those who make excuses. What is it? He was asking about the 'mutashabihat' (ambiguous verses). If he was asking about the mutashabihat—mutashabihat means things that are not clear are called mutashabih. So, two types of verses are mentioned in the Quran. Two types of verses are mentioned in the Quran: 'Huwal ladhi anzala alaykal kitaba minhu ayatun muhkamatun hunna ummul kitabi wa ukharu mutashabihat' (It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses [that are] precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific). Allah is the Being who revealed the Book to you. Allah revealed the Book to you. 'Huwal ladhi anzala alaykal kitaba'. In it, some verses are 'muhkamat' (precise), which are absolutely clear and these are the 'ummul kitab' (mother of the Book). This is the mother of the Book. 'Wa ukharu mutashabihat' and the remaining verses are mutashabihat, ambiguous. 'Fa-ammalladhina fi qulubihim zaighun' (As for those in whose hearts is deviation [from truth]). But those who have a disease in their hearts, those who are sick—meaning, sick in their hearts, meaning sick in faith. 'Fa-yattabi'una ma tashaba minhu ibtigha'al fitnati wa ibtigha'a ta'wilihi' (they will follow that of it which is unspecific, seeking discord and an attempt [to see] its interpretation). So they look for its interpretation. Those who are sick in their hearts—what is their purpose? Only discord. 'Ibtigha'al fitna', they seek discord. 'Ibtigha'a ta'wilihi', they seek its interpretation. So they quote just that much part and say, 'Look, because he was seeking discord, that is why he was punished. That is why he was beaten.' Oh brother, read the whole Quran. What does the Quran say after that? What does the Quran say? 'Wa ma ya'lamu ta'wilahu illallahu war-rasikhuna fil 'ilm' (But no one knows its [true] interpretation except Allah and those who are firm in knowledge). And the interpretation of these mutashabihat, no one knows its interpretation except Allah and those who are 'rasikhun fil 'ilm' (firm in knowledge). Those whom Allah has fully irrigated with knowledge. They are completely immersed in knowledge. Go to them, ask them. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ali Muhammad. So these were all the issues I presented to you. We could not reach the main topic. But anyway, the hadith, the topic—that hadith, meaning... We repeat it in front of you so that the topic remains fresh, and let me present two more hadiths for you quickly, and then, God willing, we will move the topic forward tomorrow. That the Master of the Universe said to his companion, Harith Hamdani, 'Ya Harith, 'Allimu hadira hikami awladikum' (O Harith, teach these wisdoms to your children). O Harith, teach these wisdoms to your children. Teach them. 'Fa-inna ziyadatan fil 'aqli wal-hazmi war-ra'yi' (For it increases their intellect, prudence, and judgment). This will increase their intellect, their 'hazm'—meaning foresight—and their 'ra'y'—meaning their decision-making process. Tell children all these things. The Master of the Universe is saying this. So we were discussing 'hazm' yesterday, asking what 'hazm' is. 'Hazm' does not mean the digestion of food, brother. 'Hazm' means foresight. So, regarding that, we discussed two hadiths: that one who is 'hazim'—meaning one who is farsighted—one of his signs is that no matter how many calamities he is surrounded by, no matter how many troubles or difficulties come, his faith never wavers, he is never terrified. 'La yarhashu indal bala'il hazimu' (The farsighted person does not tremble at the time of calamity). 'Hazim'—meaning one who is farsighted. No matter how many troubles he is surrounded by, no matter how many calamities he is surrounded by, he knows who is the one giving the trouble. Allah has placed him in this trouble. He knows that if Allah has given this trouble—meaning even if a tyrant has oppressed him—Allah has permitted it, for instance, Allah has left the tyrant alone. So it is fine, it does not matter. He is enduring it, why? Because he knows that Allah will only give him a test according to his capacity to endure. Allah never tests anyone beyond that. Therefore, because he knows this, and secondly, he knows that Allah will give a tremendous reward for this. It is present in the traditions that if people who endure calamities and troubles in this world, when people see their reward in the Hereafter—the reward that Allah will give them—then seeing that reward, people will wish, 'If only we had faced more trouble and endured it.' This is the reward. And after that, in one hadith, it says that the farsighted person is one 'man jada bima fi yadihi' (who is generous with what is in his hands). Meaning, the farsighted person, whose vision is far, is one who is very generous with whatever wealth or power he has; he gives to people, he spends. Spending—meaning he is open-handed. A believer can never be a miser. A narrator asked the Imam, 'Can a believer ever be a miser?' The Imam said, 'No, he can never be stingy.' His hands are always open, he keeps giving to people, keeps distributing. A believer is open-handed. 'Wa lam yu'akhkhir 'amala yawmin ila ghadin' (And he does not delay the work of today for tomorrow). And his next sign is that whatever work he can perform today, he performs it today; he does not leave it for tomorrow. This is his characteristic. Any work—do not do this, this is called 'taswib'. 'Taswib' means delaying things. If you can do it today, the Imam said exactly this, that if you can do it today, then do it today. If you have the power, the possibility, if you can do it today, then do it today; if you can do it now, then do it now. But anyway, this is a tragedy, it is a tragedy among us that we have adopted so much laziness and lethargy in our lives that we delay everything, saying 'we will do it later, we will do it later,' until life passes by. And has anyone seen 'later'? Has anyone seen 'later'? Has anyone seen when 'later' will come? Anyway, so when Allah gave the opportunity to come to this 'farsh-e-aza' (mourning assembly). Allah gave the opportunity for us to weep for Imam Hussain. Allah gave the opportunity to mourn for Imam Hussain (a.s.), to perform Zanjeer Zani, to perform Qama Zani for the Imam, to participate in processions, to say 'Ya Hussain'. Come on, saying 'Ya Hussain', 'Ya Hussain' itself is a very great blessing. Understand this, do not take it lightly. When Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) will reappear, when he will reappear, his slogan will be 'Ya latharatil Hussain'. This will be the slogan of Imam-e-Zamana. Meaning, even when the Imam will emerge, will reappear, he will reappear taking the name of Imam Hussain. 'Ya latharatil Hussain'. Meaning, it will also be written on his banner. The banner of Imam-e-Zamana will have this written on it: 'Ya latharatil Hussain'. 'Tharat' means revenge, retribution. Imam Hussain (a.s.), 'Ayna talibu bidamil maqtuli bi Karbala' (Where is the seeker of the blood of the one killed in Karbala?), 'Ayna talibu bi zuhuril anbiya'i wa abna'il anbiya'i' (Where is the seeker of the blood of the prophets and the children of the prophets?). Where is the one who will take revenge for the blood of the martyrs of Karbala? 'Ya latharatil Hussain'. So if you have received this opportunity, then look, do not do anything that would cause this opportunity to be lost. Many people are engaged in trying to stop this work somehow. Okay? God willing, we will present more details about this in your service some other time. Because coming to the threshold of Hussain is not everyone's cup of tea. And if someone comes, understand this much: he has not come, he has been called. When Hussain calls, people come. When permission is granted, they come. And similarly, in Karbala, Hussain wrote a letter to one of his childhood friends. Habib is sitting in Kufa, eating food, sitting at the tablecloth with his wife, when someone knocked. He said, 'Who?' He said, 'Ana baridul Hussain' (I am the messenger of Hussain). As soon as he heard the name of Hussain, Habib was restless. He came, took the letter from the messenger, took the letter, touched it to his eyes, placed it on his head, and then started opening the letter. He saw it was written: 'Min al-Hussain ibni Ali ilar-rajulil faqih Habib ibni Mazahir al-Asadi' (From Hussain ibn Ali to the man of jurisprudence, the scholar, the understanding, Habib ibn Mazahir al-Asadi). This letter is from Hussain ibn Ali to that man of jurisprudence, scholar, understanding, Habib ibn Mazahir—the one whom Hussain calls a 'faqih' (jurist) is a faqih. Habib ibn Mazahir, 'Habib, if you are not aware of our situation, then know that we are surrounded by enemies. Enemies have surrounded us from all sides. You know what our relationship is with the Messenger of Allah. Habib, if possible, come to our aid.' The weight of the letter was such that Habib could not stand, he sat down. His wife asked, 'What happened? Whose letter is it?' He said, 'It is a letter from my master, my Mawla, Hussain ibn Ali.' She said, 'What is written?' He said, 'He has called me for help, the enemies have surrounded the son of the Messenger.' She said, 'What is your intention?' He said, 'You know that the situation is such and such, how can I help Hussain?' How is it possible for me to help Hussain? As soon as his wife heard this, she said, 'Habib, then you sit at home, I will go to help the son of Fatima.' Hearing this, Habib said, 'O believer, my Mawla calls and I do not go? I only wanted to test your heart, I wanted to know your faith.' Just by saying this, Habib called his servant and started saying, 'Take my mount and go and stand at such and such a place, we have to go for the help of our Imam, our Mawla.' And he instructed the servant not to tell anyone. The servant left with the horse. Habib left a little later, as it is written in the Maqtal, that Habib, through the streets of Kufa, changing streets so that... Habib reached the place where the slave was waiting, changing alleys so as not to be seen by anyone. But what a strange scene Habib witnessed. Habib saw that tears were flowing from the eyes of the animals. The horse was weeping, and the slave was consoling it, saying, 'O loyal one, do not be afraid. Even if my master does not come, I will take you to serve the son of Fatima.' Habib slapped them all. 'O son of Fatima, O descendant of the Prophet, the time has come upon you that even animals are being cared for, and a slave is ready for your service.' Habib mounted the horse. After mounting, he said to the slave, 'Go, I have set you free in the way of Allah.' The slave said, 'Habib, this is not fair. You have accepted my service all this time, and now that the opportunity to serve the son of Fatima has arrived, you are casting me aside.' I will also go with you. Habib took the slave and headed towards Karbala. When they reached near Karbala, as soon as Imam Hussain (a.s.) saw them, he said to his loved ones, 'Go, rise, and move forward. My childhood friend Habib is coming. Welcome him.' He told all his loved ones, and they went and welcomed him. A wave of joy spread. The news reached the tent. Sani-e-Zahra (Zainab (s.a.)) asked, 'Fizza, ever since we left home, we have only been receiving news of enemies. Who has arrived now? Why is there such a wave of joy?' Fizza came to the door of the tent. After a while, she returned and said, 'Bibi, the master's childhood friend, Habib ibn Mazahir, has arrived.' As soon as Zainab (s.a.) heard this, she said, 'Fizza, go back. Give our greetings to Habib. Tell him, Habib, you have done a great deed. You have come to help the Imam at such a time.' As soon as Fizza delivered the message, Habib slapped his own face. He sat down on the soil of Karbala. He threw away his turban. He put the dust of Karbala on his head. 'Alas, has this time come upon the leaders? Has this time come upon the daughters of Ali and Fatima that they are sending greetings to slaves?' I would say, 'Habib, this is just the beginning of the calamities.' When Zainab is sending greetings, the ultimate calamity will be when Hussain says to Sayyid al-Sajjad (a.s.), 'O Sayyid al-Sajjad, when you are released from captivity and go to Medina, give our greetings to our Shias and say: O my Shias, when you remember my thirst, whenever you drink cold water, remember my thirst, and whenever the mention of a helpless one comes, remember my helplessness.' 'Fasaya'lamu alladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Ala la'natullahi 'alal qawmiz zalimin.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Hasten the reappearance of the Avenger of the blood of Hussain. Count us among his followers and helpers. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant children to those who are childless, righteous and virtuous offspring. Grant complete and swift healing to those who are ill. Return those who are far from their homeland safe and sound. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Destroy the enemies of the religion. O Lord, protect the high scholars and the great Maraje. Protect the holy shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. Accept this small act of mourning of ours. Matam-e-Hussain.

title: EP#9: Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ki Beti Se Zyaada Azwaaj Ka Ehteraam?
excerpt: This lecture examines the double standards regarding the sanctity of households in early Islamic history. The speaker highlights an incident from Sahih Bukhari where Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Bakr sought refuge in Aisha's home, which was respected by the authorities of the time. The lecture contrasts this with the historical account of the forced entry into the house of Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), arguing that such actions contradict the Prophet's teachings and demonstrate a lack of true respect for the Ahlul-Bayt.
content:
The Muslims respected Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.) more than anyone else. When Muawiya sent Marwan as the governor of Hijaz and ordered him to take the oath of allegiance for Yazid, at that time, Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said some things that angered Marwan, and he ordered the arrest of Abdur Rahman. Hearing this, Abdur Rahman took refuge in the house of his sister, Aisha bint Abi Bakr, and Marwan's men could not arrest him. That is, Abdur Rahman taking refuge in the house of his sister, Aisha bint Abi Bakr, is proof that he also knew very well that those people would not enter the house of Aisha bint Abi Bakr by force without permission because, in their view, she was respectable. This Hadith from Sahih Bukhari proves the claim false that those people loved the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) very much. What kind of love is this that Aisha bint Abi Bakr was respected, but Hazrat Fatima Zahra (s.a.), for whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said that 'Fatima is a piece of me, whoever hurts her hurts me,' people entered her house by force? Is this not an insult to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)?
Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Bakr sought refuge in Aisha's house to avoid arrest by Marwan.
The authorities respected the sanctity of Aisha's home, preventing them from entering by force.

Historical accounts show that the house of Fatima (s.a.) was entered by force, unlike the houses of other prominent figures.
The contrast in treatment suggests a lack of genuine reverence for the Ahlul-Bayt among those in power.

title: Girya e Zahra (s.a.) |  Ep#06 - Kya Kitaab e Sulaim Ibn Qais Ghair Mo'tabar Hai? Part 2/2
excerpt: This lecture addresses objections regarding the authenticity of the book 'Kitab Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali' by focusing on the character of Aban ibn Abi Ayyash. The speakers argue that accusations against Aban being a liar are biased and emerged primarily after he became a follower of the Ahlulbayt. By citing historical sources and scholarly perspectives, the lecture defends the reliability of the book and the integrity of its transmitter.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa sallallahu ala ya Bal-e-Sira... Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Respected viewers, we are present before you with another episode of the answers to the objections regarding the attack on the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.). In this series, our effort is to narrate the reality of the attack on the house of Janabe Zahra (s.a.) and in that connection, try to give answers to the objections of the opponents. In the previous episode, we saw how the opponents objected to the book 'Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali', and in this matter, in the light of the narrations of the Imams (a.s.) and the opinions of the scholars and the researchers, we proved that the book 'Sulaym ibn Qays' is an authentic book, and not only that, but it is an original book of Islamic history. Today, in this episode, we will try to give an answer to another objection regarding the book 'Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali'. The opponents... try to give an answer to the opponents. The objection of the opponents is that according to the Shia, Janabe Aban ibn Abi Ayyash is a liar and a fabricator. To answer this objection, today we have with us Janab Mohammad Abbas Patel Sahab. Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. Abbas Bhai, as you know what today's objection is, but before starting further on this, can you tell us what is the connection of the author of this book, Janabe Sulaym, with Janabe Aban ibn Abi Ayyash? In the previous episode, we saw that when Hajjaj ibn Yusuf intended to kill Janabe Sulaym ibn Qays, Janabe Sulaym left Iraq and reached a place called 'Nawbandajan', which is in today's Iran, Persia. There he met Aban ibn Abi Ayyash. And as far as their connection with the book of Sulaym is concerned, when the time of the death of Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali was near, he handed over this book to Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, and Aban read this book in front of Imam Sajjad (a.s.) and got it verified, and from this Imam (a.s.), this book reached... reached this Imam (a.s.). That is, Abbas Bhai, this means that if Janabe Aban ibn Abi Ayyash is declared a liar, then the book 'Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali' can be declared a fabrication. Therefore, it becomes even more important to answer this objection. If I use the perspective of the scholars for the next one or two, if this is declared unreliable based on Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, then this method will be wrong. If this method is to be used, then we can also bring the narrations of the scholars of the opponents regarding Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, which can prove that he was a very reliable narrator in their view. For example, in 'Tahdhib al-Tahdhib' of Ibn Hajar, it is narrated from Malik ibn Dinar that he says that Aban ibn Abi Ayyash was one of the best reciters, he was among the reciters of the Quran. So, during the 2nd century, this scene in the society, the way the reciters of the Quran were, this scene is found by those who used to recite the Quran, they used to give the Quran in the city and were the best people to understand the Quran. Or in another place in the same book, it is found that... and always Aban was known by the name of the best reciter... and always Aban was known by the name of the best reciter. In this same book, it is mentioned that he saw Aban ibn Abi Ayyash writing Hadith in the darkness of the night, and he is the personality who used to take the Hadith from the people before others. According to your book, if these narrations are used as an argument and presented before them, then in your view, it is very important that the perspective of all the scholars and the personality of Aban ibn Abi Ayyash... You said what you said very correctly, but my question is, is there any scholar who has declared Aban a liar? On the contrary, it is found—liar is a far cry, but rather, it is found that, for example, here, Janabe Aban has been praised, he has been declared a 'Zahid' (ascetic) and 'Aabid' (worshipper). For example, in the book 'A'yan al-Shia', Mohsin al-Amin says that Aban ibn Abu Ismail ibn Abi Ayyash al-Basri was a Zahid, pious, and trustworthy, his name is... Regarding the book and peace, his name is also mentioned; where has it been said? In this, may Allah have mercy on him, subscribe to the channel. It is known that this status is a very high status. If we turn towards the book of Allama Sheikh Mohsin Jani, it shows that he has accepted the authenticity of the narrations of Janab Aban. Because our scholars, for example, as they remain on the page, are confirming this matter of ours. As far as the matter is concerned, he has not at all declared him a liar, nor as in the Russian [text], Allama has mentioned him twice in his result, once on page 126, where he is a Tabi'i and Sharif. Keep in mind that the word 'Sahih' has been used correctly here, not saying 'Jafiya' or 'Wajah'. It has been used correctly, not saying 'Jafiya' or 'Wajah' or 'Dho-kar-baans' or 'Majboor'. And the second time in this same book, the second author on page number 164, has called Aban a Basri and a Tabi'i; he did not use the word 'Sahih' here. So this shows that the word 'Sahih' which the second author used here for the first time, is in the background, and it is towards this that Sayyid Aban points out that the word 'Sahih' used by the second author is in reality a 'Tashih' (correction) and 'Tashih-writing' (copying) which was written by mistake; it is not in reality, but 'Saghir' (small) which became 'Tashih' after the copy. So far, according to what we have seen, some scholars of the first Tabaqat have praised Janab Aban, and the majority of Shia scholars have described Janab Aban as a companion of the Imam. So, what is the reality of Janab Aban? What is his truth? To understand this reality, one must reflect on history and search through books. If we reflect on history, we find that Aban was originally a follower of the Ahlulbayt. And when he met Janab Sulaym bin Qays al-Hilali, and Sulaym explained the oppression that was inflicted upon the Ahlulbayt after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), he became enlightened. And when Aban became a Shia, after that, the scholars of the Ahlulbayt began to confirm Aban and started criticizing him. In the book of Rijal, as long as he was according to their Tabaqat, he was being praised, but when he became a Shia, his criticism began. And our scholar Mulla Tahriri in 'Kitab-e-Kabir' clarified this matter that under the guise of giving a different picture, they started criticizing Aban, and that thing is in our books. If we place that discussion before you, then some have praised him. From the narrations, it is known that at that time, as soon as he became a Rafidi, Ahmad bin Hanbal and Shu'bah etc., started severe criticism of him and expressed their hatred against him. It reached the point that Shu'bah said regarding Aban that I consider it better to drink the urine of a donkey than to narrate the traditions of Aban. I consider it better to drink the urine of a donkey than to narrate these. Despite this, Shu'bah narrated many Hadith from him. Thank you very much, brother, for answering the objections raised regarding the book of Sulaym bin Qays al-Hilali and Janab Aban. After seeing all these things, Abbas brother, this conclusion can be drawn that as long as Janab Aban was of the first Tabaqat, he was praised. As long as they read his Hadith and narrated his Hadith, he was praised, but as soon as he became a Shia, his criticism started, and from then on, the accusation of being a liar and a fabricator was leveled against him. So viewers, we have seen from the narrations that no one can raise a question on the authenticity of the book of Sulaym bin Qays al-Hilali, and undoubtedly, the oppression that happened to Janab Zahra (s.a.) is a failed attempt to justify that oppression. Despite this, if anyone has any questions on this topic, they can contact us on our social media handles. We will try to answer their questions with evidence, Insha'Allah. We will be present again tomorrow with the next episode of this series, i.e., the answer to the objections regarding the oppression of Janab Zahra (s.a.). With the answers to the objections, give us permission. Thanks for the support, i.e., help. [Music]

title: EP#8: Ghadeer Mein Munaafiqeen Aur Inkaar-E-Wilaayat Ka Anjaam
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological significance of the event of Ghadir and the divine appointment of Imam Ali (a.s.) as the successor to Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). It emphasizes that the Wilayah of Ali is the essential foundation of the Islamic faith and that its rejection constitutes a grave spiritual transgression. The speaker discusses the dangers of hypocrisy, the necessity of disassociating from those who oppose this divine authority, and the eternal consequences for those who deny this core tenet of Islam.
content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. We welcome you all to the eighth episode of this program. First of all, we offer our heartfelt congratulations to all of you on the occasion of Eid. I repeat what I presented before you yesterday, which is that today's episode is a very special episode. If the person participating in the quiz related to this episode answers all the questions correctly, they might get the opportunity for the Ziyarat of Imam Reza (a.s.), the Ziyarat of Iran. Yes, all those who answer the quiz of today's episode correctly, one of them will get the Ziyarat of Iran through our computerized lucky draw system, Insha'Allah. And along with this, I would like to inform you that for this eighth episode, you can participate in the quiz of this last episode until the 22nd, which is our free episode day. Until that day, you can participate in the quiz of this eighth episode. That is, from today until the 22nd, whoever participates in the quiz of this eighth episode and answers all the questions correctly, the names of all such people will be collected, and a lucky draw will be taken out through the computer system, and whoever's name comes up will get the Ziyarat of Iran, Insha'Allah. So, with this, let's start today's episode. Today's topic is 'The Hypocrites in the Ummah and the Consequences of Denying Wilayah'. And to address you on this special topic, the respected Dr. Sami is present. This was it, so apart from this, Allah... [Music] ...Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and upon your family. O Allah, be a friend to whoever befriends him, and be an enemy to whoever is his enemy, and help whoever helps him, and abandon whoever abandons him. And whoever abandons Ali, abandon him. You, O Allah, abandon the one whom You abandon; that person becomes destroyed, he becomes ruined. Because this is a matter that should remain in the mind, that the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) has said this, in which the Messenger (s.a.w.a.) has clearly stated about the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). About the status of Ali (a.s.) and in the Ummah, the life of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and about this, he will be in his place. The Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is a matter that is the foundation of the religion, which the religion is based on. And about his enemies, the hypocrites, this is a serious matter, about which the discussion today is that about them, in the Ummah, the entire history is full of this, because this is only about the hypocrites, and after that, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) and the status of the Imams, and after that, another description of it, and then after that... After that, another image of his, and then after that, the lawful and the unlawful, and side matters, and our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has shed light on this as well. And this religion, having suppressed all these things, now he has said, now we move towards those verses in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) spoke about those people. And this, pay attention now, what this means is that at that time, the number of people in the crowd, the number of those sitting there, a good number of them were hypocrites. And that is why our Prophet (s.a.w.a.) also said, meaning those people who were hypocrites or those who were deniers, they were all sitting in front, and they were listening very carefully to what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was saying and what he was about to say. Look, we said 120,000, meaning all these things, all these people were there, and a good number of them were sitting, listening, and believing. Listening and believing in whom? In Allah and His Messenger (s.a.w.a.). 'Wa aminu bima anzaltu musaddiqan lima ma'akum' (Believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you). And believe in that which has been revealed before, lest We efface your faces and turn them towards their backs, or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers. And Allah's command is always executed. And then we move towards the next part, which is that Allah is saying that whoever does not believe in the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and does not believe in Allah, We will efface their faces, turn them towards their backs, and curse them just as We cursed the people of the Sabbath. Now, what is 'Ashab al-Sabt' (the people of the Sabbath)? It refers to those who were forbidden from catching fish on Saturday. Forbidden from catching fish on Saturday, but they did not listen to the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) words and started catching fish through various tricks. So much so that Allah's curse fell upon them, and what was the result? Allah said, 'Kunu qiradatan khasi'in' (Be you apes, despised). So, here, the Almighty is saying that whoever does not believe in the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), their end will also be the same—that it will be said, 'Be you apes.' So, you will become apes. We will all see the end of this, Insha'Allah. Before moving forward, it is necessary to clarify a few things. Whatever I am presenting here, these are all from very authentic books, from the books of the Ahlul-Sunnah scholars, from the great scholars of the Ahlul-Sunnah, from the book 'Yanabi al-Mawaddah'. It is from this book that I am presenting this. Then he says that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Wallahi ma ana bi-hadha' (By God, I am not like this). 'Ayyuhal-nas, inna li kulli nabiyyin wasiyan' (O people, every Prophet has a successor). I swear by God, the verses of the Quran I am reading, I have no doubt, but my companions are a group, every group is my companions. 'Wa inni la-a'rifuhum bi-asma'ihim wa ansabihim' (And I know them by their names and their lineages). I know them all. 'Amma an-tuwaffi' (As for now), I have ordered to ignore them, to leave them to their hypocrisy and their state. But 'wa inna li-Aliyyin' (and for Ali), the son of Abu Talib, I have been ordered to do this: to see what the state of their hearts is, how much they love him, and how much they hate him, so that they may test their own hearts. I will not say anything. I will not say anything. 'Nur Allah' (The light of Allah). And after that, this is the truth, and after that, the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is that for which one should stand up. It has been decided that they will give the right of Allah, and if the right of Allah is not fulfilled, then he who denies this will be a loser. And we will take our rights from the people. Today, it is fine, do whatever you want, but on the Day of Judgment, when Allah Almighty will be present, it will surely happen. Then after that, He will take the account. O people, pay attention, to distract you, they have made these things. Allah has made us, He has made us... I am sure that those who are not ready to accept the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), they try to lower the status of Ali (a.s.). No one had it, only Ali (a.s.) had it. Others had nothing. And our ancestors were human beings, and they knew them, and they were good people, but they did not talk about it. They have come to their own selves, and they are doing this in the name of Islam, that we are bringing an Islamic revolution. They are not bringing Islam, but they are spreading corruption. Imam Sadiq (a.s.) said, 'There is nothing between you and your enemies except a 'mithl' (a likeness/standard).' What is a 'mithl'? Look, the Quran uses the word 'mithl' in various places. In this context, it means that if a wall is not straight, it will collapse, because if the foundation is weak, the whole building can fall. Therefore, it is essential for the building to be straight and correct. So the Imam said, 'What you call a 'mithl' is the one who opposes you...' The one who opposes you, opposes your Wilayah, and turns away from the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) to follow someone else—this is what you call a 'mithl'. Whether it is day or night, show your disassociation (Bara'ah). Even if they are Fatimi or Sayyid, if they are acting against the Wilayah, if they are opposing the Wilayah, then do not befriend them, do not shake their hands, do not hold them in your heart, and keep your distance from them. Let us begin. We are moving forward, and we are quoting from the books. It is a great tradition, and keep this in mind: Imam Sadiq (a.s.) says that my father narrated that Allah (s.w.t.) made Ali (a.s.) a sign (Alam) for all of creation. 'Alam' means a banner, a mountain, a place where people gather. Allah made Ali (a.s.) the sign for all of creation. There is no other sign, no other banner, no other mountain besides Ali (a.s.). If people are to gather, they should gather around Ali (a.s.). If they are to gather, they should gather upon the Wilayah of Allah. That is why the traditions state... The traditions state that Allah says, 'If people had gathered upon the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), I would not have created Hell.' I only create Hell because of this. If you are upon the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), it means you accept his Wilayah and Caliphate, and you do not leave him for others. I am talking about those who accept Ali (a.s.) as the first Caliph. Otherwise, just saying 'Ali, Ali' is not enough for salvation. Whoever follows Ali (a.s.) is a believer, and whoever denies him is a disbeliever, outside the fold of Islam. Whoever denies the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and prefers others over him is a polytheist (Mushrik). Why? Because they have associated others with him; they have placed others on the same level as Ali (a.s.). In fact, some people considered others greater and started saying that those who say Ali (a.s.) is the leader are wrong. Whoever prefers the inferior over the superior is doing a great injustice. On this occasion of Ghadir, we should spread this message as much as possible. Ghadir is not just for one day; it is a message for the whole year. And Islam will remain only because of the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.).

title: Imsaak Kise Kehte Hai?  |  Maah e Mubarak e Ramazan Ke Ahkaam
excerpt: This lecture explains the concept of Imsaak, or restraint, during the holy month of Ramadan. It clarifies the necessity of making a proper intention for fasting and discusses the rulings for those who may have forgotten or are unable to fast. The speaker also draws a parallel between the physical act of fasting and the spiritual discipline required in daily life, emphasizing patience during hardships.
content:
Here, people say that one should restrain oneself. Some people have defined the fast, saying that one must avoid things that break the fast. But one must also stay away from things that invalidate the intention. For example, if a person forgets to make the intention for the fast during Ramadan, or doesn't even know that such a thing as 'intention' exists, and before noon they realize they should have made the intention... for the fast to be valid, the intention is necessary. If they have already done something that breaks the fast, they cannot fast. But the point is to be cautious and not do anything that would invalidate the fast, like eating or drinking. Do not eat or drink, and avoid other things. This is what our scholars say. If you are traveling and you eat or drink on the way, and then reach home, our scholars say you should refrain from eating and drinking for the rest of the day. Similarly, our life is like a fast. Even if you are in trouble, sick, or facing difficulties, our Imams say you should not show your frustration to people.
Imsaak refers to the act of restraining oneself from things that invalidate a fast.
A valid intention is a mandatory requirement for the validity of a fast in Ramadan.
If one forgets to make an intention before dawn, they may still make it before noon provided they have not committed any acts that break the fast.
Travelers who break their fast during a journey should continue to refrain from eating and drinking once they return home.
Fasting serves as a metaphor for life, teaching believers to maintain composure and patience during sickness or difficulty.
One should avoid displaying frustration or complaining to others during times of hardship.

title: Aqeedah e Muntazar (a.t.f.s.)  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi  |  Urdu Taqreer
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the theological foundations of the belief in Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) within Shia Islam. It provides historical evidence for the Imam's birth, citing both Shia and Sunni sources, and discusses the divine wisdom behind his occultation. The discourse emphasizes the spiritual connection between the Imam and his followers, highlighting the necessity of unity and moral preparation for his eventual reappearance.
content:

You can watch all our transmissions through Jadoo TV, Roku TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Apple TV. Today is the day of the birth of Hazrat Bibi Sayyida-tun-Nisa al-Alamin, Salamullahi alayha, Bibi Fatima Zahra (s.a.). So, on behalf of the Imam Hussain (a.s.) team, we extend our congratulations to Hazrat Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) and all the lovers of the Ahlulbayt. It is natural that the Imam (a.s.) says that to be happy in our happiness and to be sad in our days of grief is a sign of our followers. Why should one celebrate their own festival? To make one's life a role model, the one who is the role model is Bibi (s.a.), whose command will be received; naturally, one has to act upon that command. title: EP#12: Imam Ali (a.s.) Ne Talwaar Kyun Nahin Uthaayi?
excerpt: This lecture explains the historical and theological reasons why Imam Ali (a.s.) refrained from using his sword to claim his right to the Caliphate. It highlights that his restraint was not due to a lack of courage, but rather strict adherence to the specific instructions and covenant given to him by the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The speaker emphasizes that Imam Ali's obedience to the Prophet's command to wait for sufficient support serves as the ultimate proof of his legitimacy as the true successor.
content:
Maula Ali (a.s.) did not raise his sword because of the will of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.). When Ash'ath ibn Qays al-Kindi did not stop him, he said: 'I am the one who knows very well that what is with Allah is better for me than this whole world and everything in it. Only the command of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and the promise he took from me stopped me from doing this, i.e., raising the sword. He told me that if you find helpers and supporters, then do Jihad with them, and if you do not find helpers, then hold back your hand and protect your life until you find helpers and supporters to establish the religion, the Book of Allah, and my Sunnah.' This is the real reason that stopped Ali (a.s.) from raising his sword. By this action, Ali (a.s.) proved that the true Caliph and successor of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is the one who completely obeys the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).

content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Before reading the Prophet's (s.a.w.a.) name, if you haven't clicked, then click. To participate in this entire video series, first, you need to register at account.dawngroup.com. The registration link is provided in the comments and description of this video. Open this link, and if it doesn't open, copy it, open the Google Chrome browser on your phone, tablet, or laptop, and paste the link there. Once the link opens, click on the Google icon visible and select the Gmail ID through which you want to participate in this quiz. As soon as you select your Gmail ID, your registration will be complete. On the registration page, you will see your token number and your details. On the same page, there will be an 'Edit Profile' button at the end; click on it and edit your details, especially your name, WhatsApp number, and area details. It is very important for these details to be correct because through these details, it is very important because through these details, the winners of the quiz will be contacted. [Recitation of Quranic verses] I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's blessings be upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). In the first section of the seventh and eighth centuries, in our book 'Fara'id al-Simtayn', on page 321 of volume two, we have included a chapter whose title is 'The Hadith of Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) regarding the mention of the 12 Imams, the last of whom will be Imam Mahdi (a.s.).' In this regard, in Hadith number 572, he has... In Hadith number 572, he has narrated from al-Juwayni al-Shafi'i that Imam Ali (a.s.) said: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) said, 'O Ali, I will meet you at the Hawd al-Kawthar. O Ali, you will be the distributor of Kawthar, Hasan will be the protector, and Husayn will be the provider. Ali will grant abundance, Muhammad ibn Ali will be the helper, Ja'far will lead the people forward, Musa will count the friends and enemies and end the oppression. Ali will be the helper of the oppressed, Muhammad ibn Ali will determine their ranks in Paradise. Ali will arrange the marriages of the followers of Muhammad with full sincerity. The lights of Paradise will emerge from them, from whom all the people of Paradise will receive light, and they will be the Mahdi who will intercede for the people on the Day of Judgment, where Allah has not given permission to anyone except whom He wills and is pleased with.' Except for whom He wills and is pleased with. The last part of this Hadith points towards the 26th verse of Surah al-Jinn, in which the Almighty Allah says: '...and how many angels are there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after Allah has permitted it to whom He wills and approves.' This is a Quranic truth, and whoever denies this result actually denies the apparent Quran. And when the progeny of Muhammad (a.s.) can intercede, are they superior to the angels? Meaning, the only person entitled to receive intercession on the Day of Judgment will be the one who has faith in the 12 Imams. Therefore, whoever hopes for intercession must have faith in the 12 Imams, and especially in this era, must accept the Imamate and Wilayah of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). May the Almighty Allah hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.). May the Almighty Allah hasten the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and grant us the opportunity to remain steadfast on the Wilayah and Imamate until the last moment, and grant us his intercession in the Hereafter. Amen, O Lord of the worlds. [Recitation of Quranic verses]. The first question: Which Imam has been described as the light of the people of Paradise? And the second question: In which verse of the Holy Quran is the intercession of the angels mentioned? To answer, click on the link provided in the description and comments of this video, and by giving the correct answers to these questions as soon as possible, you have a chance to win in this quiz.
