title: Shabaan - Noor (a.t.f.s.) Ka Intezaar | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual significance of waiting for the reappearance of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) during the period of occultation. It emphasizes that 'Intizar' (waiting) is not a passive state but an active form of worship requiring faith, piety, and adherence to the teachings of the Ahlulbayt. The discourse highlights the necessity of maintaining hope, avoiding despair, and cultivating deep Ma'rifah to remain steadfast in the face of contemporary challenges.
content:
What is reappearance (Zuhur)? It is the name for the descent of Divine Mercy. It is the name for the arrival of Divine Mercy. When the whole world will be filled with the mercy of Allah, when the whole world will be filled with the mercy of Allah, and all the difficulties and troubles of the world will be removed. The reappearance of the Imam will be the Golden Era of Re-appearance. 'A'udhu billahis sami'il 'alimi minash shaytanir rajim. A'udhu billahil qawiyyi minash shaytanir rajim. Wa a'udhu bi Muhammadinir radiyyi min sharri ma quddira wa ma qudiya. Wa a'udhu bi alihi tayyibinat tahirina min sharril jinni wannasi ajma'in. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Allahumma kun liwaliyyikal hujjati bnil hasani salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawilan. Rabbi salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammadin wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Amma ba'du faqad qala mawlana wa sayyiduna amirul mu'minina 'Aliyyu bnu Abi Talibin 'alayhimas salatu was salam. Intazirul faraja wa la tay'asu min rawhillahi fa'inna ahabbal a'mali ilallahi intizarul faraj. Sadaqa mawlana amirul mu'minina 'Aliyyu bnu Abi Talib.' The Master of the Universe, Amirul Momineen (a.s.) says, 'Intizarul faraj', wait for the relief, wait for the reappearance, wait for salvation. 'Fa'inna ahabbal a'mali ilallah', because the best deed near Allah is to wait for the reappearance. One drop of knowledge from the ocean of knowledge of Imam-e-Zamana, Imam-e-Mahdi, Hazrat-e-Baqiyatullah, Hujjat ibn al-Hasan al-Askari (may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him, and may Allah hasten his noble reappearance, and may we be with him) is that Imam-e-Zamana is the proof of Allah on earth, the eye of Allah among His creatures, the light of Allah's guidance, the ark of salvation, the fountain of life. Or if said in one word, Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) is the greatest blessing of Allah. The greatest blessing of Allah, which is beyond our description and our imagination. That is, we can neither define it nor imagine it. He is beyond our definition and imagination. Therefore, regarding this greatest blessing, which is currently in occultation, we have many responsibilities, and one of the important responsibilities is to wait for the reappearance. So that he may arrive and fill the world with justice and fairness just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. Firstly, there are many points regarding waiting, although all points cannot be covered in this small speech, so I will present a few points for your service. The first point is, why is waiting necessary? One reason why waiting is necessary is that waiting is a condition for the acceptance of all deeds. Waiting is a condition for the acceptance of deeds. How? The reason is that for the acceptance of any deed, the condition is that it must be according to the will of Allah, according to the religion of Allah. If that thing is not according to the will of Allah, not according to the command of Allah, then that thing will not be acceptable in the court of Allah. Therefore, only that worship will be accepted which Allah has commanded. If Allah has not commanded it, then that thing will not be acceptable. That is why when Iblis the accursed (may Allah's curse be upon him) refused to prostrate to Hazrat Adam (a.s.), Iblis argued with Allah, saying, 'O Lord, do not ask me to prostrate to Adam, otherwise I will worship You in such a way that no close angel or sent prophet has ever worshipped You.' Allah replied, 'Uridu an a'budaka min haythu uridu wa la min haythu turidu', I want My worship to be as I wish, not as you wish. Therefore, if our deeds are according to the religion of Allah, they will attain the honor of acceptance. If they are not according to the religion, then no matter how many prostrations we make, no matter how many prayers we offer, no matter how many acts of worship we perform, it has no importance near Allah, because Allah wants His worship to be as Allah wishes. That is why the Master of the Universe, Amirul Momineen (a.s.) says, 'Ayyuhannas dinakum dinakum', O people, guard your religion, guard your religion, 'dinakum dinakum, tamassaku bihi', look, hold fast to the religion, 'tamassaku bihi', tamassuk means to hold fast, 'tamassaku bihi, wa la yuzilannakum wa la yaruddannakum ahadun anhu', look, let no one remove you from your religion, let no one turn you away from your religion, let no one make you an apostate. Be careful, because there are many 'qati-ut-tariq' (highway robbers) sitting, as they say in Arabic, who are ready to loot your religion, who are ready to ruin your religion. Therefore, always look at what the Hadith is saying, what the Quran is saying, what the Thaqalayn are saying, pay attention to that. Here the Master is saying, let no one snatch your religion from you, let no one deviate you from your religion, let no one turn you back, 'li'annas sayyi'ata fihi khayrun minal hasanati fi ghayrih', because if you commit a sin while remaining within the religion, it is better than a good deed performed without religion. Did you notice the sentence? What is the Master of the Universe saying? A sin with religion is better than a good deed with irreligion. Strange! Now if many people hear this, they will say, 'Is this a thing to say? That you are saying a sin with religion is better?' This is the saying of the Master. But the Master does not state anything without evidence. The specialty of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is that whenever they say something, there will definitely be a rational argument in it. So the Master says, listen to the evidence, excellent evidence, it is amazing evidence, 'li'annas sayyi'ata fihi tughfar', 'li'annas sayyi'ata' means because a sin 'fihi' means 'fiddin' (in religion), if there is a sin with religion, then 'tughfar' (it is forgiven), so there is a possibility of its forgiveness. There is a possibility of its forgiveness that Allah may forgive it. 'Wa lakin wal hasanata fi ghayrih', but if one does any amount of good deeds without religion, 'la tuqbal', it will not be accepted, because in the Quran, the word 'Iman' (faith) always comes before 'Amal-e-Saleh' (righteous deeds), 'Alladhina amanu wa 'amilus salihati'. Faith, the correct belief, is the standard for acceptance. If the faith is not correct, if the belief is not correct, then no matter what a person does. If a person is seen not believing in Allah, no matter how many good deeds he keeps doing, yes, in this world Allah might give him a reward, Allah might give him a reward in this world, but the matter will be limited to this world; in the hereafter, there will be nothing for him. For the hereafter, there must be only and only the correct belief. Now let's move towards the second Hadith, which is a very important Hadith and we all should know it. A person named Abu al-Jarud came to the service of Imam Baqir (a.s.), came to the service of the fifth Imam, and he submitted, 'Ya Rasulullah', O descendant of the Prophet, 'al ta'rifu mawaddati lakum', do you know that I love you, 'wa inqita'i ilaykum', and I am fully devoted to you, 'wa muwalati iyakum', and I accept your Wilayah, I believe in your Wilayah. Qala, faqala alayhissalam, "Na'am", the Imam said, "Yes, I know, I know." Qala, Abu al-Jarud requested, "Fa-inni as'aluka mas'alatan", I have come to ask you a question today, "Tujibuni fiha", please answer it for me, "Fa-inni makshuf al-basar", now my eyesight is also is... let's say, this person has become very blind, I cannot see you. Qalil al-mashy, I cannot even walk. Wala astati'u ziyaratakum, and I cannot come for your Ziyarat, I cannot come to meet you kullahu hinan, whenever I want. Every moment, meeting you—well, youth was a different matter. There is a lesson in this too, that look, consider youth a blessing; do as many good deeds as you can in your youth. Otherwise, a time will come when old age arrives, and then many things that one can usually do in youth, one will not be able to do in old age. No matter how much a person says that I will do this later, no one has seen the 'later'. So here, Abu al-Jarud says—whose name was Munzir of Ziyarat—he said that I cannot come for your Ziyarat repeatedly, I have become old, have become blind, and cannot walk. The Imam said, ask what you want to ask. Qultu, I, Abu al-Jarud, requested: Akhbirni bi-dīnik, tell me about your religion, alladhi tadinullaha 'azza wa jalla bihi, through which you have faith in Allah, upon which you hold belief in Allah. Anta wa ahlu baytik, not just you, but you and your Ahl al-Bayt. Li-adinallaha 'azza wa jalla bihi, so that I too may believe in the religion of Allah according to your religion. Qala alayhissalam, the Imam said, "In kunta aksarta al-khutba", if you have stated the matter in very few words, "faqad a'zamta al-mas'alata", but your question is very great. Wallahi la-u'tiyannaka dini wa dina aba'i, by God, I will give you my religion and the religion of my forefathers, alladhi tadinullaha 'azza wa jalla bihi, upon which we hold belief in Allah, the Almighty. And what is that religion? Pay attention to it. A few things, very important. The first thing: Shahadatu an la ilaha illallah, to bear witness that there is no god but Allah. Wa anna Muhammadan rasulullah sallallahu alayhi wa alihi, and second, that Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is the Messenger of Allah. Wal-iqraru bima ja'a bihi min indillah, and to acknowledge, accept, and believe in everything that the Messenger of Allah has brought from Allah. Wal-walayatu li-waliyyina, and to accept the Wilayah of our Wali. To accept the Wilayah. Wal-bara'atu min aduwwina, and to express disassociation (Bara'ah) from our enemies. Wa tasliman li-amrina, and to completely submit to our command, total submission. Wa intizaran, and then the Imam mentioned that special name for whom one stands up, standing with humility, and to wait for our Mahdi. Wal-ijtihada, and along with these beliefs, a Shia is one who strives hard, wal-ijtihad, works very hard. Wal-wara', and to abstain from forbidden things, wal-wara'. And 'Wara' means al-wuquf 'inda al-shubuhat, meaning to stop even where there is doubt. This is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 22, Hadith number 1. So you noticed how the Imam explained what an important pillar of religion is: waiting for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf). And in this waiting, there should also be struggle, and one should distance oneself from the forbidden. Now we come to a topic related to this: what are the factors that create the spirit of waiting in a person? Waiting, what are those factors? See, this is a very important point that should be considered: what are the factors that create the spirit of waiting? Meaning, why does this spirit not arise in us? If it is not in us, then why not? That is what we need to consider. The first thing—these four factors—is that a person must have certainty that the thing or the person they are waiting for is going to come. Meaning, there must be certainty that he will come. This is the first thing. The thing about which there is no certainty, one does not wait for it. Or the waiting is very weak—'I don't know if he will come or not. If he comes, we'll see.' So there must be certainty that he will come. This is the first thing. What is the second thing? He will come, and he will come soon. He will come shortly. He will come soon. That is why in the traditions we find a strange phrase: "Tabaqqa amra sahibika laylaka wa naharak." Wait for your master, your leader, day and night. You don't know when the reappearance might happen. So if someone asks, 'Brother, what about the signs?', signs have only been mentioned; it is not necessary that there be signs. That is why we have been commanded to wait for the reappearance, not for the signs. Allah can surpass any sign, lillahil bada'. Allah can surpass any sign. Yamhullahu ma yasha'u wa yuthbitu wa 'indahu ummul kitab. Allah erases whatever He wills and writes something else in its place, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. This is a verse from Surah Ar-Ra'd, verse number 39, I believe. Yamhullahu ma yasha'u wa yuthbitu wa 'indahu ummul kitab. Whatever He wills, Allah erases. Bada' (change in divine decree) can happen; Allah has the authority. Therefore, we have to wait for the reappearance because the reappearance is Allah's promise; there can be no Bada' in that. Bada' can happen in the timing of the reappearance, but not in the reappearance itself; it cannot change. There will be no change in the reappearance. It can happen in the timing of the reappearance. If Allah has written the reappearance for 400 years from now, He can do it today. Allah has the authority; Allah can do it. So if there is certainty that the reappearance is near, then the waiting will be more intense. For example, if you are waiting for someone, if you know he is coming in 3 months, then for the first month or two, you will be very relaxed. But as those hours draw near, the intensity of your waiting will increase. The intensity will increase. Now you will wait; now there is one day left, one day left, one day left—just saying 'one day less, one day less', now he is coming, he is coming next week, now more preparation—is all the preparation done or not? As the days of the arrival of the one who is coming draw near, the intensity of waiting increases. So just understand that if there is certainty that the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana will be soon, soon, and can happen at any time—"Tabaqqa amra sahibika laylaka wa naharak"—then a person will always be prepared. The third thing is that the person should love the thing or the person they are waiting for. If they do not like him, they will not like waiting for him either. What kind of personality is he waiting for? He is waiting for that personality who will fill the world with justice and fairness and end oppression and tyranny. If we ourselves are oppressors and tyrants, then how will we wait for the one who is going to end oppression and tyranny? If we ourselves are oppressors, how can we wait for the one who is going to behead us? We will not wait for him. Therefore, make yourself such that when the one who is coming arrives, he says, 'Yes, you are among our lovers, come, join our army, come, be with us.' And not only this, but the fourth thing is that when someone mentions the awaited one, one should also have love for the one who is mentioning him, and always keep looking to see who is mentioning the awaited one. The one who is being waited for, if he is being mentioned, one should love that too. Therefore, it is necessary that there be love for Imam-e-Zamana (ajtf) in our hearts. Love him as much as possible. Meaning, a person should practice Wara', meaning Wara'-e-Taqwa, distancing from sins, keeping Allah in mind. Meaning, distance yourself from sins, act upon obligations, abstain from forbidden things, try to act upon recommended acts, try to abstain from disliked acts, and reflect on ethics. Adorn yourself with such ethics that are pleasing to Imam-e-Zamana. And other things like this. The second thing is: never despair of Allah's mercy. Look, what happens is that when we get tired after waiting for a long time, we say, 'Oh, I don't know if he will come or not, I don't know when he will come.' Meaning, this happens when we start thinking, 'I don't know when he will come.' We start thinking, 'Will he come or not? Will he come in our lifetime or not?' This is all despair. And despair—despair of Allah's mercy is the second greatest sin after Shirk. What is Akbar al-Kaba'ir? Shirk. After that, what is it? Despair of Allah's mercy. That is why there is a verse in Surah Yusuf where Prophet Yaqub (a.s.) said to his sons, "Ya baniyya idhhabu fatahassasu min Yusufa wa akhihi wa la tay'asu min rawhillahi innahu la yay'asu min rawhillahi illal-qawmul kafirun." Look, do not despair of Allah's mercy. No one despairs of Allah's mercy except those who do not have faith in Allah. They do not have faith in Allah at all. That is why they do not have faith in Allah's mercy. That is why Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) says to one of his companions, "Amr, oh Amr, Akbar al-Kaba'ir al-shirku billah." Oh Amr, among the major sins, the greatest sin is to associate a partner with Allah. It is the greatest sin. "Wa ba'dahu", and after that, "al-ya'su min rawhillah", despair of Allah's mercy. And then the Imam, quoting this verse, the verse of Surah Yusuf. What a great thing the Master of the Universe said in four words. Look, what a strange sentence it is. The Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), says, "A'zamu al-bala'i inqita'u al-raja'." The greatest calamity, the greatest catastrophe is not to have hope in Allah. "Inqita'u al-raja'", not to have hope in Allah, to despair of Allah's mercy. There is no greater calamity than this. Meaning, what is the Master trying to say? That no matter how great a calamity in the world may be, in any case, that calamity is going to pass, it is going to go away, it is temporary. Allah can remove that calamity immediately. But if, but if a person becomes hopeless of Allah's mercy, then the punishment for that is something they will have to suffer forever. That is, they will have to remain in Hell forever because of this sin, that they became hopeless of Allah's mercy. Therefore, one should always have hope in Allah's mercy. The Imam says, 'Kun'—the narrator says, 'Sami'tu Aba Abdillah (a.s.)'—I heard from Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that the Imam said, 'Qul liman la tarju arja minka lima tarju'—in English, the translation sounds very good: 'Expect the unexpected more than the expected.' Meaning, the thing you do not expect, the thing you are not even expecting, expect that more than the thing you are expecting. The Imam says this. That is why waiting is the greatest form of worship; there is no worship greater than this. And that is why, in the hadith which I made the heading of this discourse, the Mawla says, 'Intaziru al-faraj'—wait for the relief, wait for the Faraj, that is, wait for the reappearance, wait for salvation. 'Fa inna ahabba al-a'mali ila Allah'—because the most beloved deed to Allah is what? 'Intizar al-faraj'—that is the waiting for the reappearance. There is no better deed than this. There is no better work than this; Allah loves it the most. Why? What is the reason? But what is the powerful argument in it? Consider why waiting for the reappearance has been called the best and most beloved deed. Because what does Faraj and relief mean? What does salvation mean? The waiting for the reappearance—meaning in this, a person expects, hopes that Divine Mercy will descend. Reappearance. What is the reappearance? It is the name of the descent of Divine Mercy. It is the name of the arrival of Divine Mercy, the descent of Divine Mercy. When the whole world will be filled with Allah's mercy, the whole world will be filled with Allah's mercy, and all the world's difficulties and troubles will be removed. The reappearance of the Imam will be the Golden Era of Reappearance. There will be tremendous blessings in the whole world, there will be peace, there will be security, there will be safety. No one will oppress anyone even to the slightest degree. No one will have the courage to do anything wrong. No one will have the courage, because they know this is the government where witnesses, the waiting for witnesses will not be required. Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) will see it immediately. Therefore, when someone waits, they are not just waiting for themselves, but they are waiting for the entire universe. They are not just waiting for themselves, but they are waiting for the minerals, they are waiting for the plants, they are waiting for the animals, they are waiting for the humans, the angels are waiting. Allah says, 'Fa-ntaziru inni ma'akum mina al-muntazirin'—you also wait, and I am among those who wait with you. Meaning everyone is waiting for the reappearance, everyone is waiting so that Divine Mercy may descend. That is why it has been said, 'Afdalu 'ibadati al-mu'mini intizaru al-faraj'—the best worship of a believer is waiting for the reappearance. The believer's, yes? What is the best worship of a believer? It is waiting for the reappearance. But now, how will one know who is a believer and who is not? Although this is a very detailed topic, a very detailed discussion, but I will present just one or two hadiths for your service, that the narrator asked the Imam, 'Bi-ayyi shay'in yu'lamu al-mu'minu bi-annahu mu'min'—how should a believer know that he is a believer? The Imam said, 'One, bat-taslimi lillah'—they will submit to whatever destiny Allah has decreed, they will submit. 'Wa al-rida fima warada 'alayhi min sururin aw sakhatin'—and whatever Allah has destined for them, whether it is something good that makes them happy, or something bad that He has destined, for instance, if He sends down some calamity, they will be content even with that. They will not complain in the court of Allah, 'O Lord, why did You do this?' So, whatever calamity Allah sends down, the greatest sign of faith is this: 'Al-rida bi-qada'i bi-qadari Allah'—to be content with Allah's decree and destiny, to be content with destiny, whatever Allah has destined. Not to complain against that Allah. In a Hadith-e-Qudsi, Allah says, 'Man lam yarda bi-qadari wa qada'i'—whoever is not content with My decree and destiny, 'falyaltamis ilahan ghayri'—let him go and seek another god, let him go and find someone else. That is why it is necessary. So, this occultation (Ghaybah) is a very difficult period. The occultation is very difficult. The occultation is a manifestation of Allah's wrath. Allah wants to show that I am angry with the servants. That is why He took His Proof (Hujjah) away from among the people. Because people did not value the Divine Proof that was there before, the Divine clues, the Imams. That is why Allah took this Proof away from them. That is why it is found in the traditions, Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rukhaji, who is a companion of the ninth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rukhaji, he says that 'Kataba ilayya Abu Ja'far (a.s.)'—Imam-e-Jawad (a.s.), the ninth Imam, wrote me a letter, in which he said, 'Idha ghadiba Allahu tabaraka wa ta'ala 'ala khalqihi'—when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is angry with His creation, is wrathful upon His creation, 'nahhana 'an jiwarihim'—He removes us from their neighborhood. He removes us from their vicinity, He distances us from them. This tradition is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, Page 343, and Hadith number 31. So, the event of the occultation is a very great calamity, a trouble. And we should wait for the Imam, Imam-e-Zamana, in this occultation, and keep waiting day and night. The very first condition of waiting is that there must be faith in the Imam. That indeed, Imam-e-Zamana exists. There are many people who verbally acknowledge that we have faith in Imam-e-Zamana, but actually, in their hearts, there is a doubt whether the Imam exists or not. In reality, there remains a doubt in their hearts. That is why the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ya Ali! A'zamu al-nasi imanan'—O Ali! The people who will bring faith in the most strange and wonderful way, 'wa a'zamuhum yaqinan'—and whose certainty will be the most firm and the greatest, 'qawmun'—they will be the people 'yakununa fi akhiri al-zaman'—who will be in the end times, they will be the people. Meaning the Shias of the end times. 'Lam yalqaun-nabi'—they will not meet their Prophet. Their Prophet will not be among them. 'Wa hujjiba 'alayhimul hujjah'—and Allah's Proof, that is, their Imam, will be hidden from them. Despite that, they have brought faith. On what basis? 'Wa amanu bi-sawadin 'ala bayazin'—they will bring faith only through books. They will read and bring faith, that's it. That is why the fundamental condition of waiting is that there must be faith. So, let us conclude our discussion with a hadith of the fourth Imam, Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.), in which Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.) says, 'Ya Abu Khalid! Inna ahla zamani ghaybatihi al-qa'ilina bi-imamatihi, al-muntazirina li-zuhurihi afdalul ahli kulli zaman'—O Abu Khalid! O Abu Khalid al-Kabuli! The people of the time of his occultation, 'in ahla zamani ghaybatihi'—those who will be in the time of his occultation, 'al-qa'ilina bi-imamatihi'—who will be believers in his Imamate. Who will be believers, will have faith in the Imamate. 'Al-muntazirina li-zuhurihi'—who will wait for his reappearance, 'afdalul ahli kulli zaman'—they will be better than the people of all times. They will be the most excellent. Why? The Imam explains, 'Li-annallaha ta'ala a'tahum minal 'uquli wa al-afhami wa al-ma'rifah'—because Allah the Exalted has given them three things. One, He has given them intellect, second, He has given them understanding, and intellect, meaning through which they can distinguish between good and bad. And between good and evil, between the original and the fake, they can distinguish, they can differentiate. 'Li-annallaha ta'ala a'tahum minal 'uquli wa al-afhami wa al-ma'rifah'—and they have the recognition (Ma'rifah) of their Imam. 'Ma sarat bihil ghaybatu 'indahum bi-manzilati al-mushahadah'—and the result of which is that for them, there is no difference between occultation and witnessing, whether their Imam is hidden from them physically, bodily, or the Imam is physically present. 'Ula'ika al-mu'minuna haqqan'—these are the ones who are true believers. 'Wa shi'atuna sidqan'—and our true Shias. 'Wa du'atu ila dini-llahi sirran wa jahran'—these are the people who invite people to Allah's religion, secretly as well, openly as well, in both ways they invite people. So, let us try in this month of Shaban that as much as possible, we convey the message of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) to the people. Tell people that this is our Imam. Introduce people, tell people that O people! This is our master, this is our lord, this is our master. If you have any work, if you want anything, then ask your Imam. Do not go here and there. It is our responsibility that whether we hold a small celebration or a big celebration, if you cannot hold a big celebration, hold a small celebration, do it in your homes. Do it in your neighborhood, wherever you are, hold a celebration. And introduce Imam-e-Zamana, make people aware of Imam-e-Zamana. If you need any scholarly material, if you need any kind of cooperation, then the Strong Room team is ready to cooperate with you in any way. If you need scholarly material, if you need any banner or anything else, then the Imam—this Strong Room team will fully cooperate with you. It is our, your, everyone's responsibility to spread this message as much as possible. So that we can please our Imam. So that when Imam-e-Zamana comes, we can say, 'Mawla! We did this much for you, we did this little bit.' That is why, just to conclude this, I present a hadith of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) in your service, which has been narrated in Ghaybat-e-Nu'mani. Janab-e-Nu'mani has narrated this hadith in his book Al-Ghaybah on page 320, Hadith number 10, 'Li-yu'iddanna ahadukum li-khuruji al-Mahdi'—each one of you should prepare yourself for the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana, meaning he gave a specific name for whom it is necessary to stand up, that you prepare yourself for his reappearance. 'Wa law sahman'—even if it is with one arrow. A small thing. That is why we should prepare ourselves. And what is the best weapon of a believer? Dua (supplication). We should try to recite Dua-e-Nudba every Friday after the morning prayer. Recite Dua-e-Ahad daily after the morning prayer. At least recite this dua, Dua-e-Ahad. And the youth should memorize Dua-e-Ahad. And in every prayer's Qunut, definitely recite 'Allahumma kulla waliyyika al-hujjati-bni al-Hasan'. Prepare yourself in this way, so that, meaning prepare yourself mentally. If a person is mentally prepared, then the rest of the things will follow automatically. 'Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdu lillahi rabbil 'alamin.'

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 28 | Tafseer of Surah an-Nasr (110) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture details the historical events surrounding the conquest of Makkah, focusing on Abu Sufyan's failed attempt to seek protection from the Prophet and his companions. The speaker highlights the incident involving Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who attempted to leak the Prophet's military plans, and the Prophet's subsequent decision to forgive him. The session concludes with a moral lesson on the importance of forgiveness, character, and avoiding backbiting in accordance with the teachings of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the High, the Great. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. Blessings and peace be upon the best of creation, the Prophet Muhammad, and his pure and purified progeny. Do not forget to subscribe. Respected viewers, peace be upon you. Once again, I am present with the blessings of the Ahlulbayt to present the series. Our discussion yesterday was about the event of Abu Sufyan and the events of other individuals that I had narrated. As I said yesterday, I will narrate to you the arrival of Abu Sufyan in Medina. I will narrate the arrival of Abu Sufyan in Medina and his reaching his daughter, Umm Habibah. And when he wanted to sit on the bed of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in Umm Habibah's house, that lady folded the bed. Abu Sufyan said, 'My daughter, did you not consider this bed worthy of me, or did you not consider me worthy of this bed? What is the matter?' And Lady Umm Habibah said, 'O father, this is the bed of the Messenger of Allah. You are an idolater and impure. I do not like for you to sit on the bed of the Messenger of Allah, so I folded it.' Abu Sufyan said, 'Daughter, you have been living away from me, that is why you are not doing this work for me.' Abu Sufyan came to the Messenger of Allah and presented his matter to the Messenger of Allah, but he gave him no answer. Then he came to Abu Bakr and Umar; they also gave him no answer. Then he came to Ali (a.s.). At that time, Lady Fatimah (s.a.) was sitting there, and Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (a.s.) were sitting there, who were children and were playing with each other. He said, 'I have said to you that my relations with you are pleasant and in kinship. You are also dear to me. I have come to you with a need; it should not be that I return empty-handed. You recommend me to the Messenger of Allah.' The Imam said, 'O Abu Sufyan, the Messenger of Allah has already decided on the matter. By God, we do not have the audacity to say anything in front of him.' Abu Sufyan turned towards Lady Fatimah (s.a.) and said, 'O daughter of the Prophet, can you not do this work for me, that you tell your son to grant me protection among everyone and thus become the leader of the Arabs forever?' Lady Fatimah (s.a.) said, 'By God, my child has not yet reached the age where he can grant you protection among all people. No one can grant protection to anyone against the will of the Messenger of Allah.' Abu Sufyan said, 'I am caught in a very difficult situation. Give me advice on what I should do now.' Imam Ali (a.s.) said, 'I do not see any such strategy in my understanding that can get you out of this. Yes, you are the leader of your tribe; stand in the public gathering and give yourself under the protection of everyone, and return to your homeland.' Abu Sufyan said, 'Will this really be useful for me?' You said, 'This will also be of no benefit to you, but there is no other strategy besides this.' There is no other strategy besides this. Abu Sufyan stood in the mosque and said in front of everyone, 'O people, I give myself under the protection of everyone.' Saying this, he mounted his horse and left. When he returned to Makkah and met the Quraysh, they asked him, 'What have you done?' He replied, 'I met Muhammad and spoke to him; he gave me no answer. Abu Bakr and Umar also gave me no answer. Then I met Ali; he gave me this advice that I should stand in the public gathering and say that I am under the protection of all of you. I went in front of them and did this.' The Quraysh said, 'Did Muhammad accept it and give you permission?' Abu Sufyan said, 'No.' The Quraysh said, 'Then Ali has made a mockery of you. What benefit can we get from this?' Abu Sufyan said, 'Nothing else could be done by me.' Now the Messenger of Allah ordered preparations for the journey towards Makkah. He told his family to prepare for the journey, ordered the people to prepare, and said to his companions, 'Until we reach Makkah, the Meccans should not know about us.' On this occasion, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who used to be a spy... Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who used to be a spy, his spying was for the sake of the Quraysh. Now that the preparations of the Messenger of Islam were complete, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote to the Quraysh that the Messenger of Allah is coming towards you. He gave that letter to a woman who belonged to Medina. Her name is mentioned as Sarah. She had hidden it in her hair. This woman left for Makkah. Revelation came to the Messenger of Allah that Hatib has given a letter to a woman and she has left for Makkah. You called Ali and Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and told them the news of the revelation and ordered them to go and catch that woman. They went with great speed and caught her on the way. They searched her belongings, but nothing was found. Ali (a.s.) said, 'We have been told a lie, otherwise we are not liars, and we have been told a lie by the one who said it, he is truthful.' Therefore, either you give it yourself, or you will be killed. That woman took that letter out of her hair and handed it over to these gentlemen. They brought the letter back to Medina and handed it over to the Messenger of Allah. You called Hatib and asked him about it. He was brought before the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and when asked why he did this, he replied, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have faith in Allah and His Messenger; there has been no change in my faith. The truth is that my family is there, and I did this so that they might treat them well because of me.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) forgave him immediately, saying, 'We have forgiven you.' Respected audience, it is worth noting how the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) forgave him despite the gravity of the situation. What usually happens? If someone makes a mistake, people do not forgive them; they hold a grudge in their hearts. It becomes a heavy burden, and instead of letting it go, they start telling others about it. They ignore all the virtues of that person and focus only on their flaws, spreading them among everyone, saying, 'Look, this person has this flaw.' The state of human temperament has become such that if they dislike one thing about someone, they wish the worst for them, no matter how good they are. Conversely, if they like one thing about someone, they consider them good, no matter how many flaws they have. This is not the temperament of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). The temperament of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is to appreciate the good and, regarding the bad, not to engage in backbiting or spreading rumors, but to practice Amr bil-Ma'ruf (enjoining good). Do not engage in backbiting; you were instructed to practice Amr bil-Ma'ruf. If someone has wronged you, forgive that mistake. If you forgive their mistake, they will feel remorse for their own error and think, 'I committed evil against this person, yet they forgave me.' Consequently, not only will they stop, but others will also refrain from such actions because they will see that the person they intended to harm treats them with such kindness and good character. Therefore, dear audience, we must present the best of character and adopt the path of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Our welfare in both this world and the hereafter lies in that. We will find success in this world and the hereafter. But if we do not do this, the world might seem better to us, but the hereafter will become difficult. If we want both worlds to be better, we must forgive the servants of Allah and cover people's faults. If someone asks for forgiveness, forgive them so that Allah (s.w.t.) may forgive us. I conclude my speech here and take your leave. Khuda Hafiz, and Alhamdulillah Rabbil Alameen.

title: EP#6: Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ka Ghar Jalaaya Gaya | Musibat-e-Batool (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture examines historical accounts regarding the events surrounding the house of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) following the passing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The speaker references Sunni historical sources, such as Tarikh al-Tabari and the works of Ibn Abi Shaybah, to discuss the threats made against those refusing to pledge allegiance. The lecture argues that the historical context and the refusal of Imam Ali (a.s.) to pledge allegiance for six months support the conclusion that the house was indeed attacked.
content:
[Music] Was burning the house of Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) just a threat? In the famous Sunni book 'Tarikh al-Tabari', it is mentioned that Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the house of Imam Ali (a.s.) when Talha and Zubayr were inside. Umar said, 'By Allah, either I will set this house on fire, or you all must come out to pledge allegiance.' Furthermore, Ibn Abi Shaybah, who was a teacher of Bukhari, also wrote in his book that after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), when people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr, Ali (a.s.) and Zubayr were in the house of Fatima (s.a.) and did not pledge allegiance. When this was reported to Umar ibn al-Khattab, he went there and said to Fatima (s.a.), 'By Allah, nothing will stop me from ordering that those who have gathered in your house be burned inside.' Now, if someone says this was just a threat and it doesn't prove the house was burned, then for them, there is this narration in Sahih Bukhari which states that after the passing of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) lived for six months, and during this time, Imam Ali (a.s.) did not pledge allegiance to anyone. That is, if the allegiance had happened, the house would not have been burned. But since the allegiance did not happen, the only conclusion is that the house of the Prophet's daughter was attacked and the door was burned; otherwise, the oath sworn by Allah would be proven false.

Sahih Bukhari confirms that Hazrat Fatima (s.a.) lived for six months after the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) without Imam Ali (a.s.) pledging allegiance.

The narrative emphasizes the sanctity of the Prophet's daughter and the gravity of these historical events.
