title: Majlis 2 |  Sabr (Patience) | Khamsa-e-Majaalis | #Muharram 2026 | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi explores the profound spiritual concept of Sabr (patience) within the context of the Ahlulbayt's teachings. It bridges practical jurisprudential guidance, such as the importance of lawful sustenance and correct Wudu, with the deeper theological necessity of Tawakkul and steadfast faith. The discourse culminates in the tragic and heroic example of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.), illustrating how true patience manifests as absolute obedience and sacrifice in the face of extreme adversity.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Almighty. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Protector, and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the Lord of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. Blessings be upon his pure family, from whom Allah has removed all impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our Master, our Owner, our Beloved, our Physician, our intimate companion, our confidant, the fortified cave, and the succor for the distressed and the desperate—may my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our Master and Leader, Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), has said: 'Know that a good deed (Ma'ruf) earns praise and brings a reward. If you were to see a good deed as a person, you would see it as beautiful and handsome, pleasing to the beholders and surpassing all the worlds.' Truthful is our Master and Leader, Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), may the blessings of Allah be upon him. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The hadith I have chosen for these five gatherings is one in which the Master of Martyrs says: 'Know that Ma'ruf...' I had submitted to you what is meant by Ma'ruf. 'Ma'ruf earns praise'—from this, you will earn praise, meaning commendation. 'Maksub' comes from 'kasb' (earning). 'And brings a reward'—and its result and conclusion will be a reward, meaning Allah will grant a reward. If a person continuously performs good deeds, 'If you were to see a good deed as a person,' if Allah had given a human form to this Ma'ruf, He would have made it extremely beautiful and handsome. 'You would see it as beautiful and handsome, pleasing to the beholders and surpassing all the worlds,' such that those who see it would be delighted and happy, and this Ma'ruf would surpass all the worlds, the entire universe. I had briefly submitted to you in this gathering about this, that the general translation we use for Ma'ruf is 'goodness' or 'virtue.' As we say, 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf' (enjoining the good) and 'Nahy anil-Munkar' (forbidding the evil). And I submitted to you, what is written in Ziyarat Ashura? 'The Ma'ruf is what you have commanded, and the Munkar is what you have forbidden.' Ma'ruf is everything that you (the Ahlulbayt) have commanded. Meaning, whatever you command will be good. Whatever the Ahlulbayt command is good, and whatever they forbid is wrong; it is not correct. All the teachings of the Ahlulbayt are like this, and these teachings surpass the entire universe. Now, let us move to the hadith that Allah gave to the Prophet as a gift, saying that no gift better than this has been given to anyone before or after him. It contained several things, the first of which was 'Tawakkul' (trust in Allah). I had submitted a few points about Tawakkul. Today, I will complete two hadiths, and then we will move to the second thing. Just two hadiths quickly, as I mentioned, this topic of Tawakkul—relying on the essence of Allah—is very vast. But there are two things: one is the etiquette of Tawakkul. Etiquette means manners. These are very brief, small hadiths. Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) says—O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The first thing is: 'Do not abandon seeking sustenance from its lawful source.' Look, the first principle is that in Tawakkul, when you are seeking sustenance and relying on Allah, you must never choose a forbidden (Haram) path. Therefore, it is obligatory—obligatory for everyone, whether they are in a profession, business, or any job—to first go and ask about the jurisprudential ruling regarding it. Ask, 'Can we do this work or not? Is it not Haram?' For example, serving alcohol to someone—we don't drink it, we just serve it. Is it allowed? No, it is not allowed. If someone opens a liquor business and then says, 'Allah is the Provider (Razzaq), Allah will give,' this is not Tawakkul; this is deceiving oneself. This is Haram earnings. That is why the Master of the Universe (Ali a.s.) has a very powerful and beautiful hadith: 'Jurisprudence (Fiqh) first, then trade.' Fiqh first, then trade. Look, first learn the Fiqh, meaning understand the rulings well, then start the business. Fiqh first, then trade. It should not be that you are eating Haram earnings and then taking out a portion, saying, 'If we take out this much, the rest will become pure.' It does not become pure like that. It does not become pure in our school of thought. Yes, some people... yes, it happens, but in our traditions, it is clearly not allowed; it is absolutely not religiously permissible. Now, since the topic of Sharia has come up, there were one or two questions. Actually, look, the jurisprudential questions, I tell the youngsters, please read them in the Tawdih al-Masa'il (Book of Practical Laws). The answers to all questions are in the Tawdih al-Masa'il. For example, the Tawdih al-Masa'il of Sistani, or whichever Marja' you follow, read that Tawdih al-Masa'il. And if it is not in there, or you cannot find it for any reason, then ask your local prayer leader or the Maulana; that would be better. Okay? When we say 'ask questions,' we mean only regarding what we are speaking about. Otherwise, we never do a Q&A session. Okay? Or, for example, asking about anything—that is not it either. Okay? These two things. But anyway, since you asked, I will answer. One is, if the place of 'Masah' (wiping) is wet, can you perform Masah or not? No, you cannot. Whether that moisture is due to sweat, or you just came out of a bath, or you got wet from rainwater—for any reason—whether it is Masah of the head or Masah of the feet, you cannot perform Masah. Dry it, then perform Masah. They asked, 'What if the hand is wet and you perform Wudu over it?' Yes, you can do that. If the face and hands are wet, you can perform Wudu over them; there is no harm in that, no problem. But for Masah, it is a condition that the head... and the feet must be dry; Masah will be performed on that. If you perform Masah on a wet head or wet feet, the Wudu becomes void. So, repeat it. And if you prayed with that Wudu, then you must repeat the prayer—first perform Wudu again, then pray. And if the time for the prayer has passed, then its Qada (make-up) is obligatory if you remember. So, its Qada is obligatory. Okay? That was the ruling. The second was, if after performing Wudu, can one wipe it with a handkerchief or tissue paper? Wa alaykum as-salam. Yes, you can wipe it; there is no harm in that. For example, if you want to wipe your face after Wudu, you can, but it is 'Makruh' (disliked). It is just that in the traditions, this is called 'Tamandul.' 'Tamandul' comes from 'Mindil,' meaning tissue paper or handkerchief. A small handkerchief is called 'Mindil' or 'Mindila' in Arabic, and wiping the face with it is called 'Tamandul' in Arabic. So, 'Tamandul' is Makruh in the traditions; it has been forbidden. But it is not Haram. It does not make the Wudu void. There is no harm in it. Recite a Salawat for Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. So, this was an important thing: 'Do not abandon seeking sustenance from its lawful source, for it will help you in your religion.' Look, always earn through lawful means because Allah has already decreed the sustenance for everyone. But the method is left to the servant—whether it will be through lawful or unlawful means. Allah has given that option because the world is a test. Therefore, it is an option. It is the servant's choice: lawful means or unlawful means. The same thing—the sustenance will be exactly what it is. Remember this. Yes, how one can increase sustenance is a different matter. That is a different discussion. If a person wants to know how to increase sustenance, there are ways in the traditions, but that is not our topic right now. But the main thing is that a person should use lawful means. The Imam says this will help you in your religion. This will help you in your religion because if Haram food enters, its effects are very bad. Hazrat Mirza Mahdi Isfahani (may Allah be pleased with him) was a very great scholar who passed away in 1365 AH, which is about 83 years ago from today. He was a very great scholar, a very powerful scholar. He wrote a point in his book. Of course, he used to speak in the light of traditions. He used to say that what happens by eating Haram and wrong food? He says it affects the 'Tinah' (nature/clay). The clay from which a human is created is affected. The clay that was from 'Illiyin' (the highest heaven) can turn into 'Sijjin' (the lowest hell) if he does that. Meaning, it changes—a mixture. Meaning, no one knows what his end will be. His fate is not known to anyone. But he says it is a reason. It is a reason that causes a person's nature to spoil. Nature spoiled means his hereafter is spoiled. Meaning, he is a dweller of Hell. Meaning, the term he used—that the reason for a 'Sa'id' (blessed/person of Paradise) becoming a 'Shaqi' (wretched/person of Hell) can be this food. And this is the same thing the Master of Martyrs said on the day of Ashura to the people: 'You are not listening to me because your bellies are filled with Haram.' Because your bellies are filled with Haram, that is why you are not listening to me. So, this is a very important thing. Anyway, this is also a different topic. We will not go into this right now. After that, what is the second thing? 'And tie your mount, and then rely on Allah.' It is not that you left the mount, and someone took it, and then you say, 'We rely on Allah.' The Imam says it is not like that. Meaning, take all necessary precautions, do whatever needs to be done, and then rely on Allah. The second hadith clarifies this sentence. Wa alaykum as-salam. Yes. It clarifies it completely. And then, because this is a very big misconception about Tawakkul, and that is that people usually do not work, they sit at home and say, 'We are relying on Allah.' They don't work hard. 'Relying on Allah.' No, this is not Tawakkul. Allah does not like this at all. Now, look, we will not use our own words; we will use the words that Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) used. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and hasten their reappearance. The words he used, we will use. It is in the tradition that some healthy, strong people—look, that is why it was clarified in the hadith so that if someone is sick or a patient and cannot work, that is a different matter. But the hadith says, 'For a group of healthy people.' 'Asiha' is the plural of 'Sahih' (healthy). Healthy people were sitting in a corner of the mosque. 'Jalisina fi zawiyatil masjid.' Sitting in a corner of the mosque. So, the Master (Ali a.s.) asked them, 'Who are you?' 'We are the ones who rely on Allah (Mutawakkilun).' Relying on Allah. They don't do any work. 'Relying on Allah.' The Master's sentence—what did he use? Look, we are reading the hadith; we are not speaking from ourselves. He said, 'No, rather you are 'Muta'akkilun' (freeloaders).' Not Mutawakkilun, but Muta'akkilun. Meaning, freeloaders. Meaning, if they get food for free, they eat it. Then the Master asked, 'If you say you are Mutawakkilun, if you rely on Allah, then what has this Tawakkul of yours brought you to? What is the meaning of this? What do you mean by Tawakkul? What do you want to say?' So they replied, 'If we find, we eat. And if we don't find, we are patient.' Which is our next topic, patience. 'If we don't find, we are patient.' The Master of the Universe said, 'This is what a dog does in our view.' The Master says, 'In the view of us Ahlulbayt, this is what a dog does. If it finds, it eats. If it doesn't find, it is patient.' This is what a dog does, the Master says. Look, we are telling you this because the Master was very strict with his Shias in these matters. He would not tolerate these things. Then they said, 'So what should we do?' The Imam said, 'Do as we do.' So they asked, 'How do you do it?' The Imam (peace be upon him) said, 'When we find, we spend it in the way of Allah. And if we don't find, we thank Allah.' We thank Allah. If we find, we spend it in the way of Allah. If I tell you the hadiths in this regard, this is a very interesting topic. Wherever it is written in the Quran, 'Establish prayer and give Zakat,' you see, it is written in many places in the Quran, 'Establish prayer and give Zakat.' So, the Imam says in this regard—it is a tradition in Usul al-Kafi, Volume 3—that the Imam says what is meant by this is not the obligatory prayer and obligatory Zakat. Obligatory prayer and obligatory Zakat only keep you away from Hell. This... when it is said in the Quran, 'Establish prayer and give Zakat,' it means that the prayer you perform should be 'Nafila' (supererogatory) so that your ranks are elevated. Besides the obligatory, perform Nafila. And give Zakat, give as much as possible, give as much as you can. So that through this, you become close to Allah. So, these are the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (peace be upon them). Anyway, this is the teaching of the Master of the Universe regarding Tawakkul. Now, the Prophet asked Gabriel, 'What is the second thing?' So Gabriel said, 'Patience (Sabr).' So he asked, 'What is patience? What is its interpretation?' The Prophet asked. So he said, 'To be patient in times of hardship just as one is patient in times of ease.' Just as one is patient when times are good—everyone has good times—one should be patient in bad times as well. Now, let us give you an example of this. A small example that happens in your daily life so that the matter becomes clear. Let us give a small example. Meaning, what happens? Look, if someone has, for example, 100 rupees in his pocket. And out of that 100, he misplaces 10 rupees somewhere. Now he has 90. 100 is extra, yes. So 90—he has no work for it, but he has 90 rupees. So he is fine; he doesn't get that worried about where the 10 rupees went. This is called 'Sarra' (ease). Meaning, there is comfort; there is no problem. If someone has, for example, two or four lakh rupees, if two thousand or five thousand go here or there, he doesn't feel much pain. But if someone is 'hand to mouth' and he only has those 100 rupees, that is all he has, then understand that if those 100 rupees are gone, what will his condition be? What will his state be? Here, the role of patience is very great. And here, the role of sacrifice is very great. Here, sacrifice, where patience and sacrifice... Look, what is found in the traditions about the Master of Martyrs? That on the day of Ashura, as his calamities were increasing, the color of his face—his face was becoming more radiant. And where it is difficult to be patient, where patience was difficult, he was thanking Allah. This is a very difficult stage, very difficult. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) says, 'If we don't find, we thank.' And here, the spirit of 'Isar' (selflessness/sacrifice)—look, we say this again and again, that look, it is very easy to say all this, but it is very difficult to act upon it. And we condemn ourselves first in all these things; we don't talk about others. And remember, in the gathering or anywhere, we never say any point keeping others in mind. So, some people are asking us, 'Brother, are you saying this by looking at someone?' No, brother, not at all. Because I have to face Allah and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), yes. So, I never say anything by looking at anyone. Allah and the Prophet are witnesses, Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.) is a witness. Whatever is said is always what is written in the Hadith. So, this spirit of sacrifice is very important. There was a man whose financial condition was very poor. This narration is brought by Allama Majlisi in Bihar-ul-Anwar, Volume 23, and it is that the Prophet-e-Akram (s.a.w.a.) and Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.)—Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad—there is a Hadith, right? That 'Muhammadun wa Aliyun abawa hazihil ummah' (Muhammad and Ali are the two fathers of this Ummah). The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Ali (a.s.) are the two fathers of this Ummah. And what is in the narration? That give them preference, give preference to their relatives, meaning the Ahlulbayt, over your own blood relatives. This is the Hadith. So, this person was a lover of the Ahlulbayt. Now, one day he really had no money. There was starvation in his house. So, he went and did labor. He worked and got one dirham. One dirham. In that one dirham, he—you know what a dirham is, right? What is a dirham called? A dirham is a silver coin, a silver coin. So, with that dirham, he went and bought curry and bread for his family, for his wife and children. Now, he was bringing it so that his wife and children could eat. I am being very brief, speaking quickly. He saw some Sadat (descendants of the Prophet). Sadat. And their condition was very bad. So, he asked, 'What happened?' They said, 'We haven't eaten for so many days, we are hungry.' He said, 'Okay, do one thing, you take this bread and curry. You eat it.' They took it and ate it. Now, he started going home. On the way, he started thinking, 'What will I say at home now? What answer will I give?' Anyway, the story is very long. I will tell you in one short line: he was just thinking this when he met a man who said, 'Brother, are you so-and-so?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'A caravan from Egypt is looking for you.' He said, 'Oh? Really?' So he went to them and said, 'Yes, tell me, were you asking for me?' He said, 'Does your cousin live in Egypt?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'He has passed away, and before dying, he gave this note.' A note, meaning what we call a 'hundi' or a promissory note. He gave this promissory note and said, 'Go and give this to so-and-so.' And collect this much money from there. He took it and went and received a large sum. After that, he brought it home and gave it to his family; they were very happy to have food and drink. After that, he went to sleep. When he slept, he saw the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.) in his dream. And they said to him, 'You have done a great deed. You have done a great deed by preferring our relatives over your own relatives, over your own wife and children. Now we want to make you so happy that there is no limit to it.' Your cousin had many properties in Egypt. We are getting all that wealth transferred to you as well. And they appeared in the dream of the ruler of Egypt and said, 'Sell all the properties of the one who died, and give it to his cousin who is there in Medina.' This is the entire Hadith; I am not saying this from myself. This is the saying of the sixth Imam (a.s.). The whole incident I am telling is the saying of the sixth Imam. Allama Majlisi has recorded it in Bihar-ul-Anwar, Volume 23. Right? And then both of them came in his dream and told him. He sold all the properties, and whatever the amount was, he gave it to a money changer, who sent the promissory note there, collected it, and the bottom line was that he became the richest man in Medina. He became the wealthiest man. This is because he gave preference. So, this generosity and this quality are very important, very great things. That is why it is said that just as in ease, one should be patient in hardship. In every situation. 'Wafil faqati kama yasbiru fil ghina' (And be patient in poverty just as one is patient in wealth). How does one show patience in wealth? In the same way, one should show patience in poverty. And then, when one is sick, one should be patient. Just as one is patient when healthy. Meaning, every sentence that Allah is saying, because it is a Hadith-e-Qudsi. Because when a man is healthy, what is the proportion of his patience? He doesn't have to do anything; there is no need for patience, right? So, in the same way, when he is in trouble, he should be patient. Not even a particle's worth of worry. Why? Remember, this is the decree of the Lord. This is destiny from Allah, it is ordained. Nothing will happen except what Allah wills. Except what Allah wills. And then the Imam says, 'Fala yashku halahu indal makhluqe bima yusibuhu minal bala' (And do not complain about his condition to any creature regarding the calamities that befall him). Usually, what is our habit? If we get a little sick, we meet someone and tell them we are sick; we meet someone else and tell them we are sick, whatever it is. If there is any other trouble, we keep telling everyone about this trouble. Allah dislikes this very much. Very much. Allah took away Prophethood from the lineage of a Prophet because of this. Because he was telling others. That is why Hazrat Yaqub (a.s.) said, 'Innama ashku bassi wa huzni ilallah' (I only complain of my suffering and grief to Allah). It is a verse in the Quran, in Surah Yusuf, 'Innama ashku bassi wa huzni ilallah.' I will complain about all my troubles, sorrows, and grief only to Allah. And you can try this. See, I am just telling you the concept, the main one. The concepts of the Quran and Hadith. Or it is a very simple, very simple thing. Do not complain to anyone, no matter what the trouble is, only to Allah. And I would like to submit in your service, what is the best time to talk to Allah and Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.)? The time before the Morning Prayer (Salat-ul-Subh). A little before the Morning Prayer. Just pray two rakats of Salat-ul-Shaf, one rakat of Salat-ul-Witr, that's it. Do Istighfar with the tasbih, meaning 100 times, 'Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh.' Sit on the prayer mat and after that, converse with Allah. Just 2 minutes, not more, converse with your Imam. And after that, see how your life changes. Do not complain to anyone else. Live as if nothing happened. Let me add one thing in brackets: first of all, no one is interested in listening to us. Our problems, mostly it is like that. You can be sure of this, yes. Now see, I have also become a senior citizen. So, whatever I am saying, I am saying from experience. Nobody is interested in listening. No one is interested in hearing our problems and issues. And even those who listen, you just understand that if we take a very optimistic ratio, 80% are just having fun. And 20% will be genuinely sympathetic to you, understand that. This is very optimistic. Otherwise, 80% are just having fun. They met. You stated your problems there, and they will go and tell 10 people, 'Oh, they met. Look, they were acting very smart, see? And look at their condition! See this? See that trouble? See that problem?' That is why Islam has forbidden it. Never tell anyone, don't tell anyone, not anyone. We have had scholars in the past; read their stories, read the stories of the scholars. It is explicitly mentioned that scholars never told anyone, not even in their own homes. They wouldn't even tell their wives, they were that reserved. You read their stories. So, in ethics, what is of great importance is patience, patience and gratitude. Meaning, the root of 'sabr' has appeared 103 times in the Quran. The root of sabr has been used 103 times in the Holy Quran, understand that. 103 times. 'Sabirun' has appeared, 'Sabirin', 'Sabirin' has appeared 14 times, just 'Sabirin'. 'Sabirun' has appeared, 'Sabr' has appeared, 'Nasbiru' has appeared, and it has also appeared in a slightly negative meaning, negative, right? 'Fama asbarahum alan nar' (How patient they will be for the fire). Allah asks, what thing will make them patient for Hell, for the fire of Hell? This is its negative connotation. Meaning, what thing? 'Fama asbarahum alan nar'—they cannot bear the troubles of this world, how will they bear the fire of Hell? There is Dua-e-Kumayl, right? Read it, you should read Dua-e-Kumayl. It is a powerful supplication, and read it with the meaning. Read it with its translation. You see, Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) says that I cannot bear the difficulties of this world. How will I be able to bear the difficulties of the Hereafter? Whereas the duration of the difficulties of this world is very short. And the punishment of the Hereafter is infinite. It is going to last forever. So, look at the words of Maula-e-Kainat in Dua-e-Kumayl. And what is the most important thing? To be patient on faith (Aqeedah). Being patient on worldly things is one thing, but being patient on faith, when difficulties come in your faith, the troubles that come with it, being patient on that is a very difficult task. Even the best ones break in that. There was a time, it was the time after the tragedy of Karbala. Banu Umayya and Banu Marwan, Banu Umayya and Banu Marwan—la'natullahi alayhima—both of them were great tyrants and their hearts were filled with hatred for Ali (a.s.). Banu Umayya and Banu Marwan. I mean, you know about Banu Umayya. It was up to Muawiya, then Yazid, and then Yazid's son, he left the government after a few days, Muawiya was his name, Yazid's son, he left the government. So when he left and there was no child of Banu Umayya left, Marwan jumped and sat on the throne. Marwan, do you know Marwan? This is the same Marwan who, when we read about the departure of Imam Hussain (a.s.), we read that when Walid said to pledge allegiance, Imam Hussain (a.s.) refused. So Marwan said, 'Walid, if he leaves now, you will not find him until rivers of blood flow.' This was the same Marwan. So what did Imam Hussain (a.s.) call him? 'Atuhaddiduni bil qatli ya ibnaz Zarqa?' (Do you threaten me with death, O son of Zarqa?). Do you know whose title Zarqa was? Zarqa was the title of Marwan's grandmother. Marwan's grandmother. Her name was Maria bint Muhib. Maria bint Muhib. This was Marwan's grandmother. In the age of ignorance, she used to do bad businesses. She used to do bad work. The one who used to put up the flag, she was that woman. Marwan was her offspring. Now you understand. What kind of people must they be who came to kill Imam Hussain (a.s.), you understand, right? We will try to do this too, InshaAllah. Time is short, but if not today, then tomorrow, InshaAllah, I will tell the youth a little history; understand history. InshaAllah, within the last year, I have done a lot of research on this topic and have written a 40-page essay. So, for a magazine, I wrote a 40-45 page essay. I will tell you the summary of it, what it is, when people say that Shias killed Imam Hussain (a.s.). So, understanding that history is very important. So, this Marwan, then his son Abdul Malik ibn Marwan. How was he, do you know? He used to pray in the Kaaba all the time. And if he wasn't praying, he would be reading the Quran, that's it. So people used to say, 'What a great personality, look at the father and look at the son.' And as soon as Marwan died, people said, 'Brother, you come and sit on the throne.' He closed the Quran and said, 'Hadha firaqu bayni wa baynak, hadha firaqu bayni wa baynak' (This is the separation between me and you). Now we will meet on the Day of Judgment. Meaning, all these days, what he was doing was just to show that he is very pious. Now when he became the ruler, he said, 'It's done, brother, the work of the Quran is over.' And just like many people in the world do, that once they get that thing, then goodbye. It happens, right? There are many people in the world who are crazy about the throne and crown, who are crazy about some position. They are prepared to do anything for that position. They will wear the outward garb of religion. People say, 'Look how pious he is,' but never be deceived by this. Never be deceived. Never be fooled by outward appearances. I am telling the youth this. We have seen many such people who wear the cloak of religion, and there is no one more 'pious' than them, but later it turns out that it was only to attain worldly gains, nothing else. Once the world was attained, it was over. Then nothing remained. Anyway, this is very difficult, and this Marwan ibn al-Hakam and his entire lineage—meaning his lineage, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, who martyred two Imams—just think about it. And these people made Hajjaj ibn Yusuf the governor. And as for the religion they were talking about... Ali, at that time, taking the name of Ali was a crime. If someone's name was Ali, they would kill him. The name Ali. This is a very important matter. What does the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) say? Listen to this sentence; it is a hadith. This hadith is from Shahid-e-Thani. You know Shahid-e-Awwal was Muhammad ibn Makki (r.a.). Shahid-e-Thani was Sheikh Zayn al-Din al-Amili, from Jabal Amil. He was a great scholar of the 10th century who wrote 'Sharh al-Lum'ah' while in prison. He was a very great scholar, and his 'Sharh al-Lum'ah' is still taught in the Hawzas today. He was a great scholar of the 10th century who was martyred. He is famous as Shahid-e-Thani, Sheikh Zayn al-Din al-Amili, from Jabal Amil. You know Jabal Amil, right? It is the same place where Israel is bombing today, saying they want this entire area. That is the same Jabal Amil. The one they claim is their territory—the 'Greater Israel' project—it is the same Jabal Amil mentioned in our hadiths. The Imam (a.s.) said that if someone wants to be our Shia, they must possess these characteristics. He mentioned many characteristics. When the narrator asked, 'How can such characteristics be found in Shias? Are such Shias even found in the world?' The Imam said, 'Yes, they are found in Jabal Amil.' The Imam said, 'Qala ala ru'us al-jibal wa atraf al-mudun' (They are on the mountain peaks and the outskirts of the cities). Jabal Amil and its surrounding cities, meaning Lebanon—what is now Lebanon. Why? You know why? These are the areas where Janabe Abu Dharr (r.a.) had preached. And it was Janabe Abu Dharr who made them Shias. In the history of Shi'ism, especially in the last 300-400 years since Iran became Shia, the contribution of Iranian scholars has been very great. Otherwise, throughout history, there have been no scholars as great as those who came from Jabal Amil. Although, in terms of numbers, they were not even 10% of today's Shia population. Not even 10%. I am giving a very high estimate; 10% is a lot. The Shia population in the world is very large. So, this is a very small number—not 10%, in my opinion, it should be 1%. Right? This is a very small, the entire population of Lebanon, you know, is very small. Anyway, so now look at what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'Min aqalli ma utitum al-yaqinu wa azimatu al-sabri' (The least of what you have been given is certainty and firm patience). Certainty—having certainty in the essence of Allah—and secondly, patience. 'Azimatu al-sabri' (firm patience). That is, unwavering patience. A person should not falter. Is it clear? This is what was submitted for your service. This matter of the name 'Ali'—a man came to Hajjaj and said, 'Hajjaj, forgive me.' Forgive me. Why forgive? He said, 'My family has done a great injustice to me.' What injustice? 'They named me Ali.' Forgive me. Do you know what Hajjaj said? Hajjaj started laughing. These are the exact words, and I am not quoting from a Shia book. I am not quoting from a Shia book; I am quoting from the books of the Ahl al-Sunnah. Hajjaj laughed and said that he has become so greedy for the world, so greedy for land, that he is even ready to change his name. And he said, 'Fine, do one thing, write some land in his name.' And obviously, what was his practice? First, curse Ali, and then take a piece of land and become a landlord. This was Hajjaj's practice. He came, and his name was Ali—his family had named him Ali. He cursed Ali (a.s.) just to get some worldly land. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that there should be no such wavering, that as soon as circumstances get difficult, we start changing everything. 'Wa man utiya hazzan minhuma' (And whoever is given a share of these two), 'lam yubali'—now listen to this sentence, it is a very important sentence I am presenting to you. It is the Prophet's sentence, not ours. 'Lam yubali ma fatahu min qiyami al-layli wa siyami al-nahari' (He should not even care what he has missed in terms of night prayers and fasting during the day). It is strange. If there is patience and certainty, the Prophet says he should not even care. 'Lam yubali' means 'la ubali'—should not even care—about which night prayer was missed or which fast. So, the reference I gave you is from the book 'Maskin al-Fu'ad' by Shahid-e-Thani, page 41. I gave the reference so you can be assured that I am reading a hadith, not talking about random things. Right? 'Wa la an tasbiru ala misli ma antum alayhi' (And be patient upon the creed you are on). Be patient upon it. This means that hardships will come, difficulties will come, problems will come. Right now, we don't understand these things. Why? Because we are in great comfort, Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, until now. In India, we are living in great comfort, very easily. There is no trouble. Otherwise, there was a time in this same India where entire families of Sadaat practiced Taqiyya and later left Shi'ism. They didn't even know where to practice Taqiyya and where not to. They practiced Taqiyya and left the religion. If you look at their names even today, they all sound the same—Jafri, Rizvi, Kazmi, Abidi, and all of them. You would be surprised by their names. They themselves used to say that our ancestors were all Shias, but they all practiced Taqiyya. Anyway, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'Wa la an tasbiru ala misli ma antum alayhi ahabbu ilayya min an yu'afini kullu minkum misla al-amali jami'ikum' (And your patience upon the creed you are on is dearer to me than if every one of you brought the deeds of all of you combined). Meaning, if you only bring these two things to me—certainty and patience—if you bring these two, then even if your deeds are small, it is acceptable to me. Right? Equal to whose deeds? The Prophet says that for those who do not have this—this certainty and patience—even if all the people of the world combined their deeds, they could not equal your deeds. If there is certainty and patience—look, I mentioned in yesterday's Majlis that these are things we can train for. It's not that we cannot train. We can train for patience, and we can train for certainty. We can train, we can train our children, we can give them education, upbringing, training. There is nothing in the world that, if it couldn't be trained, the Prophet wouldn't have narrated these traditions. Every person would say, 'Brother, what can I do? I am not like that, I cannot bear it. I am made this way.' No, no, this will not be an excuse. Train yourself, there is no problem. After that, the Prophet says another sentence: 'Wa lakin akhafu an taftaha alaykum al-dunya ba'di' (But I fear for you that the world will be opened up for you after me). That is what I just mentioned to you—that the love of the world will enter your hearts. That the love of the world will enter your hearts. What does 'the world' mean? This property, that property, this thing, that thing, this wealth, that wealth. This is the world, what else is it? What do we call the world? This is what we call the world, right? If the love of all these things enters, then what will you do? You will start hating one another. 'Fa yunkiru ba'dukum ba'dan' (And some of you will reject others). You will start hating one another—those who were very close until yesterday become enemies today. Why? Because they thought, 'If we take this property, they will stop us. They will create difficulties.' Therefore, it is better to remove them from the path. Remove their names from the documents. This happens, it happens in many places, you might know. People do all sorts of things for the love of the world. Even though, look, none of us thinks that we are going to live forever. None of us. But we are not at the level of certainty. These are not my words; these are the words of the Master of the Universe (Imam Ali). He says there is nothing more certain than death. But people—this is the Master of the Universe's statement—but people behave as if they are never going to die. Every one of us, meaning we think that you all will die except us. Everyone has to go, everyone—look, when I say everyone has to go, it means everyone has to go. I don't have to go. That is why all the things we do, we do for that reason. If there were certainty that one does not have to go, and that there is a stage after the grave, the difficulties would start right here. I am not saying this; the Quran is saying it. In Surah Qaf, Surah Qaf, Chapter 50, Verse 22: 'Laqad kunta fi ghaflatin min hadha' (You were in heedlessness of this). You were in heedlessness in the world, right? 'Fa kashafna anka ghita'aka' (So We have removed your veil from you), 'fa basaruka al-yawma hadid' (and your sight today is sharp). That is, he will start seeing the Barzakh. He will see the grave, the Barzakh. He is still in this world. The children are reciting Surah Yasin so that he dies quickly. I mean, they don't say 'die,' they say 'may his difficulty be eased.' The children say it. 'May his difficulty be eased.' Why? Because if his difficulty is eased, we will then divide the property. And this is what happens—go and read the 'Khutbah al-Gharra' of Nahj al-Balagha. Nahj al-Balagha, Khutbah al-Gharra, it is Sermon number 81 in Nahj al-Balagha. Go and read it. Go and see what the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) says. It is a very great sermon. 'Gharra' means brilliant, beautiful sermon. Go and see what the Commander (a.s.) says. And this is what happens. The Quran says, as soon as he dies and starts to leave, it is all over. It all starts from there. Now, look, here the creed is very important. It is very important. The creed must be absolutely solid. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says that because of this love of the world, your creed will be lost. Because of this love of the world. It is also in the traditions. There are many hadiths, not just one or two. Not just one or two. In this love of the world. And let me tell you one more thing. Look, a person can be anything throughout their life, but what their end will be, no one knows. Do you know? Ibn Muljam used to live in Kufa, do you know that? Do you know he was a follower of Ali (a.s.)? Ibn Muljam, may the curse of Allah be upon him. One day he came and said, 'Ya Ali, wallahi inni uhibbuka' (O Ali, by God, I love you). He said, 'Kadhabta' (You are lying). Now tell me, I am not saying this myself. He was a Shia. He was a Shia. Then he said, 'Wallahi inni uhibbuka' (By God, I love you). Then the Mawla said, 'Kadhabta' (You are lying). Three times he said it, and all three times the Mawla said, 'You are lying.' He said, 'Ya Ali, you are a strange man. I am saying I love you. Ibn Muljam.' And you are denying it. The Master of the Universe (a.s.) said, 'If you were a lover of ours, where were you in the Realm of Particles (Alam-e-Zarr)? When all the souls were divided there, the souls of the believers were on one side, and the souls of the rest were on the other. "Innal arwaha junudun mujannada" (Verily, souls are like gathered troops), so I did not see your soul there. Your soul was not there.' Meaning, even he did not know. What is written on the forehead, only the Ahl al-Bayt know. Subhan Allah. Subhan Allah. What a matter. O Ali. Ya Ali. Only the Ahl al-Bayt know, no one else. Shimr, la'natullah alayh. Countless. Shimr. Umar-e-Sa'ad, who was this Shimr? He was also the same. He was from the Banu Kilab. He was a relative of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.). And that is why he sent a letter of amnesty, saying that I will grant you amnesty. I will get you amnesty from Yazid. Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) initially refused to meet him, saying, 'I do not want your amnesty.' But upon the insistence of Imam Hussain (a.s.), he said, 'No Abbas, go and talk to him.' So Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) went and spoke. He said, 'No.' He began to say, 'Only for you.' Hazrat Abbas (a.s.), in any case, as written in the Maqtal, drove him away. And the bitterness that occurred between the two, the entire conversation is present in the Maqtal. So it is not written on anyone's forehead. So what is the standard for being a Shia? Only the Ahl al-Bayt know that the end should be on Shi'ism. On Shi'ism. Therefore, a person should always pray. Always pray. Insha'Allah, if I remember tomorrow, I will also present this prayer in your service and tell you which prayer is recited so that our end may be upon this. It is a very important prayer. So the martyr we are mentioning today is this same Hazrat Abbas (a.s.). This Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) who was the embodiment of patience. That is, patience personified. This is that Hazrat Abbas (a.s.). You see, in the Battle of Siffin, when the Master of the Universe (a.s.) sent Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) to fight, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) put a veil on Hazrat Abbas's face so that people would not recognize him. So the way Maula Abbas (a.s.) fought, everyone started running here and there. They started saying, 'Ali himself has come to the battlefield.' At that time, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) had not come to the battlefield. 'Ali has come.' And when Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) returned, the Master of the Universe (a.s.) praised him, even though he was only 18 years old at that time. He was not more than 16 or 18. For such a brave person to be patient, to repeatedly seek permission from Imam Hussain (a.s.), he would say, 'No Abbas, you are the standard-bearer of my army.' Once, when Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) insisted a lot, he said, 'Go Abbas, bring water.' He called out at the door of the tent, 'Sakina.' Janab-e-Sakina came running, 'Uncle, how did you remember me?' He said, 'The Master has ordered me to bring water, bring your water skin so that I can bring water.' Janab-e-Sakina went and took her water skin. It is written in the Maqtal that as soon as Sakina started walking with the water skin, small children asked, 'Bibi, where is this water skin going?' Janab-e-Sakina said, 'My uncle is going to bring water, Father has ordered it. Children, now be satisfied, now my uncle will bring water. Now my uncle will bring water, children, be satisfied. Now you have peace that uncle will bring water.' Today, when Sakina walked and gave the water skin, Abbas departed, pushed back the armies, put the horse into the Euphrates, then got off the horse, wetted the water skin, filled the water skin with water, then took water in his palm and started saying, 'O wretched ones, do not consider me helpless and destitute. I can drink water, but I am not drinking because the children in the tents are thirsty, my niece Sakina is thirsty, that is why I am not drinking water.' Saying this, Abbas threw the water, then took the water skin, the water skin in one hand and the standard in the other, Abbas mounted the horse. Now that he went, there was only one aim, one target, one purpose, that somehow the water skin should reach the tent, reach the tent. Now Abbas is running fast, galloping the horse, when suddenly a wretch struck from behind such that his right hand was severed. Abbas recited Rajaz, but kept holding the water skin. Another wretch struck such that the left hand was severed. Abbas quickly held the water skin with his teeth, but the precaution was, the bravery's precaution was, that the water skin should remain in the teeth, but the moisture should not reach the tongue. Abbas is running fast, galloping the horse towards the tent, that the arrow of oppression now struck, it hit the water skin. The water of the water skin started flowing. Abbas bowed his head, 'What will I do now by going towards the tent?' That a wretch struck a mace on his head, on Hazrat Abbas's head, from behind, Abbas fell onto the land of Karbala. Mourners, mourners, in the world when someone falls from a height, naturally their hand comes forward first. Abbas could not bring his hands, he fell face down on the land of Karbala. He came to the land of Karbala, called out, 'Master, my final salaam.' As soon as Hussain heard the final salaam, he held his waist, recited a dirge, 'Al-aan inkasara zahri' (Now my back is broken). Now my back is broken. Hussain's back is broken, the back of Imamate is Abbas, the back of Ismat is Abbas, with the death of Abbas, Hussain's back is broken. 'Al-aan inkasara zahri wa qallat heelati' (Now my back is broken and my stratagem is diminished). 'Abbas, now I cannot see anything, Abbas, now I cannot see anything.' 'Wa shamata bi aduwi' (And my enemy is gloating over me). Abbas, the enemy is taunting, your standard-bearer has been killed. Abbas, the enemy is taunting. While reciting this dirge, Hussain reached the bank of the Euphrates, lifted Abbas, placed his head on his knees, there was some conversation between the brothers, Abbas made some wills, one will was, 'Master, do not take my corpse to the tent.' I am very ashamed. Very ashamed. Abbas closed his eyes, Hussain recited a dirge, 'Al-yawma namat ayunul Abbas' (Today the eyes of Abbas have slept). Now those eyes will sleep that used to stay awake out of fear of you, used to stay awake out of your awe, now the Sayyidas will stay awake, now the Bibis will stay awake. Hussain left Abbas's corpse on the bank of the Euphrates. 'Wa saya'lamul ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun, ala la'natullahi alal qawmiz zalimin.' O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.). Count us among his helpers and supporters. Those who are troubled, remove their troubles. Those who are in debt, pay off their debts. Those who are childless, grant them righteous and virtuous children. Those who are ill, grant them complete and swift recovery. O Lord! O Lord! Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. Protect the great scholars and the high-ranking Maraji. Protect the holy shrines. Those who are protecting them, protect them. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab (s.a.). O Lord! Grant us the honor of Ziyarat of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in this world and the intercession of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad in the hereafter. By reciting one Surah-e-Fatiha and three times Surah-e-Tawhid, bestow the reward upon the souls of the late Ghulam Ali ibn-e-Abdul Aziz Lakhani, the deceased of the Lakhani family, the deceased of the Rupani family, the deceased of the Himani family, the deceased of the Zada family, and the deceased of the Narsidani family.

title: Jaanasheen-e-Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ko Har Cheez Ka Ilm Hona Chaahiye!
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity for the Prophet's successor to possess comprehensive knowledge of both good and evil. Using a historical debate between Ali ibn Maytham al-Tammar and the Mu'tazili scholar Abul Hudhayl, the speaker argues that if Iblis possesses such knowledge to lead people astray, the Imam must possess even greater knowledge to guide them toward virtue. The discourse emphasizes that true leadership requires an intellectual and spiritual capacity that surpasses the forces of evil.
content:
Do you not know that Iblis prevents all good things, all virtue, and commands all evil? So Abul Hudhayl said, 'Na'am' (Yes), that is correct. 'Afayajuzu' - so is it appropriate that 'an ya'mura bish-sharri kullihi' - that he commands all evil 'wa la ya'rifuhu' - but he does not know about the evils? 'Wa yanha 'anil khayri kullihi wa la ya'rifuhu' - and he forbids all good, prevents it, but does not know about the good? He has no knowledge of what good is? That the Prophet and the Prophet's successor, both, whoever claims to be the successor of the Prophet, must have more knowledge than Iblis. Certainly. Only then will he save people from the attacks of Iblis. Now, in this regard, an interesting incident is found; this is a very interesting incident. This incident is of Abul Hasan Ali ibn Maytham al-Tammar, the son of Janab Maytham al-Tammar, and a person named Abul Hudhayl, who was a Mu'tazili. As we all know about Shaykh al-Mufid, he is the personality that when he departed from the world, when he said goodbye to the world, Imam-e-Zaman (a.j.t.f.) recited an elegy for him. And this elegy is still written today on the grave of Shaykh al-Mufid in Kadhimiya, right outside the Zarih of Imam al-Kadhim (a.s.). So Shaykh al-Mufid (r.a.) narrates this incident in his book 'Al-Fusul al-Mukhtara' that Abul Hasan Ali ibn Maytham al-Tammar once asked Abul Hudhayl al-Mu'tazili, and then Ali ibn Maytham asked again, a second question. 'Afayajuzu' - so is it appropriate? Is it permissible? 'Is it possible?' Is it possible that 'an ya'mura bish-sharri kullihi' - that he commands all evil 'wa la ya'rifuhu' - but he does not know about the evils? 'Wa yanha 'anil khayri kullihi wa la ya'rifuhu' - he has knowledge of both all good and all evil. He knows both things. So Abul Hudhayl said, 'Ajal' (Yes), certainly. He knows. He is so knowledgeable, he knows its good and he knows its evil. If he doesn't know, how will he stop people from good, from virtues? So then, as soon as he said, 'Yes, certainly', Iblis has that knowledge... [he is referring to] that Imam of yours whom you followed after the Prophet, whom you considered an Imam, right?
Iblis possesses knowledge of all good and evil to effectively command evil and forbid good.

title: EP#6 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) Ki Itaa'at Allah (s.w.t.) aur Rasool (s.a.w.a.) Ki Itaa'at Hai
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological status of Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) as the divinely appointed successor to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). By citing traditions from both Sunni and Shia sources, the speaker establishes that obedience to the Imam is equivalent to obedience to the Prophet and, ultimately, to Allah. title: Darwaaza Nahin Tha - Yeh Kaisa E'teraaz? | Girya-e-Zahra (s.a.)
excerpt: This lecture addresses the controversial claim that the house of Bibi Fatima (s.a.) had no door, an argument often used to deny the historical tragedy of the attack on her home. The speaker explains that critics intentionally misinterpret metaphorical language in Hadith to exonerate historical figures. By analyzing the context of the Hadith found in Al-Kafi, the speaker clarifies that the phrasing refers to the selflessness and accessibility of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) rather than a literal lack of physical shelter.
content:
Now, you know why this is done? It is because if it is proven in any way that there was no door at the house of Fatima (s.a.), then if there was no door, there was no attack. If there was no attack, then the tragedy of Fatima (s.a.) becomes a lie, and the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.) will be easily denied, and the killers of the martyrs will be exonerated. That is why it is very important to get to the bottom of this. And these objections are just like if someone says, 'My stomach is growling with hunger,' does it mean mice have actually entered the human body and started running? If someone says, 'My heart has come to my throat due to thirst,' does the heart actually come to the throat? These idioms are used to express the intensity of hunger and thirst. Now, the hadith of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) that the opponents use to object—and they use our own sources—is that they have taken a small part of the hadith and intentionally omitted the rest, because if the full hadith were taken, the truth of the Shia would be... How do the protectors of the religion of the Shias create [arguments] by taking the entire Hadith? But if we compare this Hadith with the objections raised by the critics, then first of all, let us see where this Hadith is recorded. In the book 'Al-Kafi' by Sheikh Al-Kulayni, Volume 2, page 373, this Hadith is written. Imam Ali (a.s.) says: 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not leave behind for us any houses, no doors, nothing except some palm leaves.' And for this reason, the other party says: 'Now, let a human tell another human, if there is no door, no roof, and the place of shelter is only palm leaves, can it be called a house or not?' This means the meaning of this Hadith is something else. Let us find out what Imam Ali (a.s.) actually expressed through these sentences. What is the meaning? And for this, we do not need to look anywhere else. The same Hadith from which the critics have brought the text, if we look at that same Hadith, if we look at that chapter, the answer will come out by itself. The name of that chapter is 'Imtihan al-Anbiya' (The Trial of the Prophets) or... or 'Imtihan al-Anbiya' (The Trial of the Prophets) or 'Hadir al-Anbiya'. This chapter... the name of this chapter is: 'The trial of Allah (Azza wa Jall), the trial that Allah took of the Prophets (a.s.) in seven places, and after them, in seven places after the Prophets (a.s.) left the world.' And in these seven places, He took the trial. We are mentioning those trials in this Hadith, that how many hardships the Prophets (a.s.) faced. How many hardships... this idiom has been used by the Imams (a.s.) because if you look at the sentence just before this one in the Hadith, it is stated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was very concerned for those people who were new Muslims, regarding their hardships, mercy, and guidance. That is why this idiom has been used. 'Not having a house' does not mean they were not worried about weather changes. They used to endure all those hardships. 'No door' also has a meaning. It means that for the people who used to come to the Imam (a.s.), for those who used to come with grievances, for those who used to tell their problems, for them... for those who used to come with grievances, for them, the doors of the Muslims were always open. This means that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is saying that we, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), used to help other Muslims without caring about our own comfort. This is the meaning of this idiom and this sentence that has been used.
Denying the door of Fatima (s.a.) is a tactic to undermine the historical reality of the attack on her house.
