These are the three roots, and whoever possesses them falls outside the circle of faith. Now, there is another discussion here. You know that in religious texts, we have discussed the qualities of faith (iman) and the roots of disbelief. We discussed the importance of 'ma'rifat' (gnosis/knowledge), which is our foundation. However, it often happens that a person possesses 'ma'rifat', they are a scholar, they know what is right and what is wrong, but they have certain flaws and moral diseases. These moral diseases take them outside the circle of faith. This is why we are discussing ethics after discussing faith. Let me tell you that one of the greatest scholars in our history, in the 6th or 7th century, Kulayni (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Kafi', which is the most important book, discusses ethics in the second volume. The entire book is named 'Kitab al-Iman wa al-Kufr' (The Book of Faith and Disbelief). The discussion within it is about ethics. The name of the book itself is 'Kitab al-Iman wa al-Kufr', and the discussion is about how ethics can take a person out of faith and towards disbelief, and vice versa—how it can lead one from disbelief to faith. When certain qualities like humanity are found in a person, they lead them towards faith. In the same way, the greatest scholar, Allama Majlisi (r.a.), in his book 'Bihar al-Anwar', which has 110 volumes, discussed ethics in the seventh volume. He has discussed ethics in seven volumes. You know that each volume is 300 pages; he has discussed more than 2,000 hadiths. Actually, it is even more than that because there are other topics. We are only talking about faith and disbelief. Besides that, there are other books like 'Kitab al-Malahi' which is two volumes, 'Kitab al-Sira' which is also two volumes. If you add these six volumes, it makes 12-16 volumes. He has written about 3,500 pages on ethics. He states that the roots of disbelief are three: greed, arrogance, and jealousy. We will discuss greed. We will discuss greed: what is greed? What does the Quran say about greed? Let's go to Surah Ma'arij, verses 19, 20, 21, 22, and 23. It says: 'Innal-insana khuliqa halu'a' (Indeed, mankind was created anxious). In Surah 17, there are five verses, you can check them. The Quran says: 'Innal-insana khuliqa halu'a'—meaning Allah created man, and He created him well, but then man, due to his own self (nafs), becomes anxious. 'Halu'a' means restless, greedy, and impatient. 'Idha massahu ash-sharru jazu'a' (When evil touches him, he is impatient). He has no patience. If any trouble or calamity comes, he lacks patience. He becomes restless. This is the human being. Allah did not create him like this; man becomes like this by listening to his own nafs. Otherwise, Allah says: 'Except for those who are patient and advise each other to be patient.' Patience is also a work. Advise each other to be patient. Patience is also a work. A person who remains calm and relaxed can solve many problems. But when he is restless and impatient, he doesn't just fail to solve problems, he creates them. 'Wa idha massahu al-khayru manu'a' (And when good touches him, he is stingy). He doesn't give to others; he wants to keep it for himself. There is a condition. Why? While a believer is very generous. We discussed 'Sadaqah' earlier. 'Illal-musallin' (Except for those who pray). We translate this as 'except those who pray', which is correct, but that is not the only interpretation. There is another interpretation: 'Except for those who send blessings (Salawat)'. Except for those who send Salawat. You know that sending Salawat is a part of prayer. You are doing 'Tabarra' (disassociation) and 'Tawalla' (association). The incentive for this is 'Tabarra'. In religion, 'Tabarra' is more important than 'Tawalla'. How? You can see that in the foundation of Islam, the first thing was 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah). The greatest foundation of Islam was presented, and in everything, this 'Tabarra' is present. Inshallah, we will discuss this later. But 'Tabarra' and 'Tawalla' are actually part of the religion. If you keep them in the general sense, they are part of the religion. How is 'Tabarra' and 'Tawalla' more important than prayer? If someone does not have 'Tawalla', then even if they pray, it is of no use. And even if someone prays so much that they become bent over and their condition deteriorates, but they do not have 'Tawalla' for Ali (a.s.), then their worship will not be accepted. This is why people pray... There is no compromise on this. Regarding the definition of greed: what does a greedy person do? They have a desire for the world, a wish to attain worldly things. You see how worldly people are; they want to attain this and that. There are two things to consider here. First, it is not that we say you should become a Sufi and sit idle. Do your work, give your family a good life; that is one thing. The second thing is that perhaps Allah has blessed someone with worldly wealth, which is fine. But it is Allah's decision. However, a person should not have such a desire that they want to attain everything. Trust in Allah. Whatever Allah has destined, it will come. Do not worry about the world. Greed is when you don't know what will happen tomorrow and you sit in anxiety. Greed is the root of all evil. Greed is the root of all evil. What is this greed? The Imam says: 'Talab al-qalil bi-idha'at al-kathir' (Seeking a little by wasting a lot). He wastes his afterlife to seek a little bit of this world. He is so engrossed that from morning till night, he is busy, and some even remain like that until the very end. They are chasing the world. And you will see many politicians; no matter how much they have, their hunger is never satisfied. That is why the Imam says, 'Send Salawat'. The Imam says: 'Al-rajulu yashibu wa yashubbu ma'ahu ithnan' (A man grows old, but two things grow young within him): 'Hirsuhu' (his greed) and 'Amaluhu' (his hope). His greed and his hope grow young as he grows old. The greed he didn't have in his youth, he will have more of in his old age. The desire for the world that he didn't have in his youth, he will have more of in his old age. Now, in old age, he becomes even greedier. The Imam says: 'Seeking a little by wasting a lot'—he ruins his afterlife to gain a little bit of the world. His afterlife is lost. And what is the greatest matter of this greed? As I mentioned before, the Imam says: 'The roots of disbelief are three qualities.' One is stinginess (bukhl), which we have already discussed. The second is cowardice (jubn). If you remember, generosity (sakhawat) and courage (shuja'at) go together. Similarly, greed and cowardice go together. Whoever is greedy will definitely be a coward. How? That is... He must be a coward. How would he think of a short ball? Now look, there are many people who are worldly, who sleep on the world, they are always afraid. They have so much fear in their hearts that if they do this, they will lose, if they do that, they will lose. That is why they get nervous. So Mawla (a.s.) says these three things, and what is the root of all three? It is a lack of trust in Allah. Not being positive about Allah. People do not know this. Allah is the Provider, Allah is the Sustainer. Remember, in any matter, no one except Allah can cause you harm or benefit. Did the people of the world promise you your sustenance (rizq)? No, they did not. Allah promised it. So, can the people of the world give you any benefit? Remember, I told you, do not just sit at home and do nothing. Allah does not reach those who do not strive. Go out, search for Allah's bounties, do research, go to the shop, go to the market, go to your business, go to your office, work, Allah... Go to your office, work. Allah hates those who are idle. Allah hates those who think too much and remain too free. He hates those who are lazier than the lazy ones. What is this? No, keep working. There should be hard work. Those who work day and night, in this, one finds success. Those who worship Allah all night and work like lions during the day—look, there are such people. These are the ones who stay awake all night and sleep all day, and what are they doing? Playing carrom, playing cards. These are all things that waste time. And gambling is not permissible. Gambling, cards, all these are not permissible. Now, someone might say, 'I am playing for my own amusement.' No, it is not permissible. Play, play, play, but it is not permissible. This gambling is not permissible. It means that thing is not in Islam. Allah Ta'ala says, 'Worship Allah at night, keep doing it, and roam like lions during the day.' Strive, struggle. A believer is full of energy. Here, look, if you want to reach a position, to reach leadership, then today, especially in your era, this is not an era of instruction. Even those you call employees, they are not ready to be instructed quickly. Today is the era of inspiration. Inspire people. If you work hard, those who follow you will also work hard. And if we do not work hard ourselves, then how will the others follow? Therefore, inspiration is very important. A believer should be an inspiration for others. People should see, 'Look, how hard this believer works.' There are some believers who are famous for their hard work—it is not appropriate to take names, but there are some believers who work very hard. There is a group of people who work very hard, but our authority, especially in general... But our authority, especially among Muslims, what happens is that if we get a little bit of success, then our habits start to deteriorate. A little bit of property comes, and habits start to deteriorate. That is why Akbar Allahabadi said—Akbar Allahabadi says, 'O God, protect the Muslims.' Akbar, we are afraid of their habits. Allah, protect us. We are just afraid that when these people get some wealth, what will they do? If they get two pennies, what will be their state? Habits deteriorate, and you all know what the conditions of the world are. So, this is a very important thing. Therefore, he says, greed is such a thing that it puts a person in trouble and pain, always. Spiritually, always. Now, these worries, why don't they get peace? It means that in this world, they remain crazy, mad, and put themselves in trouble. They will come to the grave, and for this world... They will come to the grave, and for this world, and after that, when they leave, they have achieved nothing from the world. So, as soon as they left this world, then in the grave, everywhere, there is only pain. Nothing else. And why is this such a great pain? Because a person, to achieve this world, lowers himself. Now look, the person who is like this, it was the same before; people used to go to the courts of kings and say things to please the kings, they would laugh, they would be empty, just so the king would be pleased. Even today, you see that those who are in power, everyone wants to please them. What have we done? The world is like this. So, Mawla (a.s.) says, this greed reduces a person's honor, lowers their value, and makes them fall. It is a burden. Greed does not increase one's sustenance; sustenance is only what Allah has destined. If it is meant to be, it will come; otherwise, it will not. It is not that someone else has done it, but it is possible that this sustenance might decrease. This is one of the sins, and he says, and greed... He says, and greed is the root of all sins. Greed makes one hungry. They say, 'Who is this?' Many things come into this, and there are very big sins. And this greed, that is why the greedy person's example is like a silkworm. The silkworm, the more it collects, the more it wraps itself, wraps itself, wraps itself. The more it wraps, the more difficult it becomes for it to get out. The more a person is crazy after the world, the more difficult it becomes for him to get out of the world. How to get out? To the point that it reaches a stage where the weight becomes so much on it, so much load, that it dies of its own weight. What an example! Look, and the worldly people are saving... Look, and the worldly people are saving, aren't they? That one cannot run after the world. Money is kept, but it becomes a disease of the world. He gets diabetes, he gets hypertension, this happens, that happens. Then it turns out that he is taking medicine for this, medicine for that. He is living on medicine, and there is no joy in life. But look at these people who were content in the world, they were at peace. Anyway, so here, look, to the point that they die of their own weight. 'Oh, he died.' Now what happens? After that, what happens? They take the silk, and what do they do? They put it in boiling water. In boiling water. They put it in boiling water, so understand that they take out the silk. They take out the silk and put it in boiling water. They take the silk and leave the worm in the water. Look, this is exactly what happens. The state of the world is the same. After he is gone, what happened? The worldly people took him... After he is gone, what happened? The worldly people took him and laid him down. Then this is his boiling water. They laid him down, he is laid down. Even before he is buried, they start discussing, 'Who will get what?' 'This is yours, this is ours, this is yours, this is ours.' And they will not leave anything. They are taking out the silk, how to get more benefit from it. The one who remained behind, the one who earned, what happened? He is gone. That is why Mawla (a.s.) says, look, what is this worldly struggle? Don't worry too much about your children, because if the children worship Allah, then Allah takes care of His servants. And if the children rebel against Allah and are sinners, then why are you worried about Allah's sustenance? Therefore, many people think, 'For the sake of the children, I am doing this.' So Allah is the Provider, He will provide. Otherwise, you are not the provider. Therefore, he says, 'Look, never become a prisoner of greed. Never become a prisoner of greed.' It should not be that this greed... Never become a prisoner of greed. It should not be that this greed makes you so busy in this world and in the grave that you cannot think about the Hereafter. Why are you neglecting the Hereafter? Especially for the youth, I am saying, look, if you love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), if you have faith, then understand this, that today, this is youth. This youth is a blessing. And those who have passed this age, they will understand this well. That the things they could have done in their youth, they cannot do now. The question arises, what will be your age? So, youth is a blessing. So, use your youth completely for the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And there is a consequence of this, this greed. It takes away a person's modesty, it makes them shameless. A person just wants business from a party, so to achieve that business, he is ready to do anything. Worldly people do it, right? Then there is no shame in the religion. Even if he has to insult himself, he keeps smiling, keeps laughing. If a person is insulting him, then why does he give him an order? If he does a little bit, he won't give an order. Why? He understands that this is a... Why? He understands that this is a... He doesn't understand anything. He fights after my speech, but here, it's okay, a person gives it. There is no one to meet, whoever is ready to commit a sin, and there are some people whom you and I cannot even imagine. They go, and they are... but they speak very quickly. They just pray that you are seeing... a reminder, they are successful because they have heard from their fathers, from sixteen generations. They have heard from their ancestors, and this whole chain goes up to the Imam (a.s.). Even today, our... one day he was sitting in the mosque with the Imam (a.s.), and he was guiding them about the rights of the people. So, an old man, a very old man who was tired and exhausted from the journey, had come after a long journey. He was asked, 'Where is the Imam (a.s.)? Where is the Imam (a.s.)?' He was sitting there. Where is the evening? The first one happened, they are sitting there. Assalamu Alaikum, Amir al-Mu'minin, we have answered him. In the evening gathering, in the evening assembly, I have come seriously. Just look, we are reading very fast, right? I have come seriously, and it is very good, very old, very long, two or three pages have been presented. This has been very enriching for every youngster. Listen, friend, I have come seriously. I am old, I have heard a lot about your knowledge. It is very necessary, I have heard so much that I cannot store it. I have heard so much that I cannot contain it in my mind. And I am afraid that, O Amir al-Mu'minin, you will be martyred. What is he hoping for? I am afraid, O Amir al-Mu'minin, that people are so jealous of you that you will be martyred. So, give me the knowledge that Allah has given you, teach me what Allah has taught you. Teach me. How can I teach you? You will not understand. Allah has gathered everything. If a few people gather and study, it is an ocean of knowledge. The world is a destroyed thing. What Allah has taught me, it was 13,000 youths. Allah has taught me, it was 13,000 youths. Security, whatever it is, and some are thinking about Naxalism, I have emphasized it. Or, he who has two days that are equal is in loss. Meaning, every day you must improve. You should be better than the previous day. Every day, read two hadiths, read four or five hadiths. Hadith and Quranic verses, hadith should be a little bit, not too much, but do it. If it is equal, then it is a loss. It is a loss. If the good deeds are less, and the bad deeds remain the same, then you are equal. Whoever thinks only about the world will always be very beneficial, so when he leaves the world, he will only regret why he is leaving the world. He will regret. Or, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Whoever's second day is less than the first day, he has not increased anything.' He has not increased anything, he has just gone lower. Meaning, he has committed sins. In our daily life, in our Shia path, in everything, we have wasted our time in useless things. So, you are in loss, rather, you have been deprived of mercy. You have been deprived, not 'marhoom' (deceased), but 'mehroom' (deprived). The mercy has gone. And whoever does not prepare for his hereafter while his world is correct and sound, when his world is good, when the world is strong, if he does not prepare for the hereafter at that time, then he will be destroyed. Both this world and the hereafter are failures. And the person who does not look at his own defects, his desires will overpower him. When he does not look at his defects, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'Do not be pleased with yourself for something, and do not want that thing for people.' The thing you want for yourself, want that for people. And what you want to do for yourself, do that for people. He explained it completely. And then he turned towards goodness and began to say, 'O people of the world, do you not see the people of the world? Do you not see that they sit in the morning and evening, and their conditions keep changing? Their condition keeps changing, but there is no change in them. They are the same. They are running after the world, and the world is running after them. It is coming after them. It is a little bit, it is very little. When his time comes, it will take him away.' When the Imam (a.s.) said this, they did not even recognize him. They do not recognize him. Recognize the truth and recognize the falsehood. You, for Zaid, go to a mosque. The mosque is on one side. The mosque is on one side. The brothers of the city, both brothers, the lovers of the Imam (a.s.), what is the condition? After that, what is the condition? O Amir al-Mu'minin, I asked, 'Who is the most powerful and overwhelming king?' Who is the strongest king? When a person's desires are overpowered, they fall very quickly. And then the question came, 'What is the thing that humiliates a person the most?' What is that thing? He said, 'Greed for the world.' This greed for the world, and this hadith is very old. Time has passed, we will stop it here. And InshaAllah, we will stop a little bit of the hadith and move on to other topics. I will give a speech on this, but this greed for the world is the thing that makes a person not care about what is haram and what is halal. A man does not care what is haram. He does not care about Allah. Ask anyone, why are they not caring? Therefore, on the day of Ashura, he was constantly advising the people. Standing in his city, in the sermon, he was asking and advising them, but those people were not affected. Why would they be affected? They do not know. Why is my advice, my words, my speech not affecting you? Your stomachs are filled with haram. There is haram in them. Your stomachs are filled with haram, that is why my voice and advice will have no effect on you. Therefore, if someone gives advice and talks, and there is no effect, it means either we have eaten haram, or God forbid, we were fed haram in childhood. Somewhere or other, there is haram. And that is why you see, these were such people, these world-worshippers, their conscience had died. They stopped the water. The children were writhing with thirst. The sounds of the chess game were raised. The sounds of the chess game were raised. Once, in front of Imam Hussain (a.s.), Janab Abbas-e-Ali (a.s.) came. 'Abbas, go and bring water for the children.' But before that, it is very important to understand the condition of Janab Abbas. But Janab Abbas had four brothers who were in Karbala. There were four brothers. You know that when the turn of the sons of Ali (a.s.) came, Janab Abbas used to prepare one of his brothers and send him. One brother was martyred, he sent the second one. He was martyred, he sent the third one. A strange courage, he sent all his brothers. He sent all his brothers, while it should have been that when death is near and the enemy is in front, then he should have gone and been martyred first. But if Hazrat Abbas asked, 'Maula, why did you do this?' The Imam (a.s.) would say, 'You do not know that if I had died first, my back would have been broken. So who would have picked up the bodies of my brothers? Who would have brought their bodies?' Abbas used to send them, rather he used to bring the bodies of his brothers. He used to bring the bodies. Now, when the thirsty children were in the tent, the Maula sent him. 'Abbas, go and bring water.' When the voice of Sakina reached, how did she remember Janab Abbas? She remembered him like this. The Maula has ordered to go and bring water, so I am going to bring water for the children. I am bringing water. When Sakina went and ran and brought a small water skin, as she was bringing the water skin, the children said, 'Where are you taking it?' 'My uncle is going to bring water.' 'Children, my uncle will bring water. My uncle, when he makes a promise, he fulfills it. My uncle will bring water.' Janab Sakina went. Abbas went, pushing through the soldiers, tearing through the army, and reached the bank of the Euphrates. He put his horse into the river. He got off the horse, took water in his palms. Understand my condition. I can drink water, but my children are thirsty. My niece Sakina is thirsty. That is why I am drinking. Saying this, he threw the water away. After that... Saying this, he threw the water away. After that, he mounted. He filled the water skin and mounted. Abbas started moving. The army started surrounding him. A person attacked from behind, and Abbas's arm was severed. Then another person attacked, and he caught the water skin with his other hand. Then another person attacked, and the other arm was severed. He held the water skin with his teeth, giving it strength. 'O my master, my status, your oppression is such that I am meeting the water skin.' And they fired arrows at the water skin. The water from the water skin was lost. Now what should I do? As he fell from the horse, he fell in such a way that usually a person puts his hands forward, but my Maula Abbas fell on his face. The water skin was attacked. He fell on his face. The water skin was attacked. 'Maula, accept my salaam.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) came out towards the river, reciting a dirge. He was holding his back. 'Now my back is broken. Now I cannot see anything.' 'O Abbas, what happened to your Alam (flag)?' He reached the bank, lifted his head, and put it on his lap. 'Brother, brother.' There was some talk. Abbas had a will, 'Take my body away.' 'I am very ashamed.' He departed from the world. Imam Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Brother, you are mine.' Greetings, brothers. Greetings. May you sleep... [unclear]... I am keeping watch over these devilish acts. O world, [unclear]... according to the teachings, those who are troubled... [unclear]... wherever they are in the world, may Allah protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. [unclear]... may Allah protect them... [unclear]... Now, [unclear]... breaking the heads of the enemies... [unclear]... the soul of the family... understand this, how to protect your generations... [unclear]... How to protect your generations... [unclear]... when the money reached the prison, mourning, mourning... [unclear]... if you are with me, even if my head is severed for this cause, then I will remain... [unclear]... I am here, [unclear]... I am being watched at home... I am being watched at home... [unclear]... this is the last day in my house... [unclear]... The chain continues, I remain...

title: Majlis 5 | Maqaam-e-Imaamat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi | #Muharram 2025
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound concept of Maqaam-e-Imaamat, emphasizing that the recognition of the Imam is the essential foundation for all religious worship and spiritual validity. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi discusses the historical distortion of Imamate, the central role of Wilayah in the lives of the Ahlulbayt's companions, and the sacrifices made by figures like Abbas (a.s.), Maytham al-Tammar, and the sons of Lady Zainab (s.a.). The discourse highlights the responsibility of parents in religious upbringing and the necessity of aligning one's life with the virtues of the Ahlulbayt to attain true salvation.
content:
When Mir Anis's dirge says that the journey of the night of the sun... Some verses from it are about Muhammad, which I present. The Master of the elite and the common had already attached the weapons there. The world of the Master of all creation was ready there. The Sayyidas were all around with their heads uncovered, crying while holding the pole of the standard, the sister of the Imam. Swords in the waist, shoulders... the sons of Zainab stood under the standard. Necks, garments, the garden of the cloak. ... The majesty of the Lion of the Almighty, the appearance on their stature, famous and renowned. Eyes rubbed on the standard, kissing, started circling the flag, swaying. Sometimes they looked at the standard, sometimes at the life of the world. The slogan was sometimes that we are sacrifices for the Master of the Ummah. Both brothers would sometimes consult each other, sometimes ask the mother slowly, those dignified ones. 'What is the sign of Ali-e-Wali, mother, who will get the standard of the grandfather?' Some consultation, the King of good character. 'We are also ready, you should keep this in mind.' Out of respect, they submitted, 'We do not have the audacity, there is also a fear that you might be saddened. We are slaves of the Master and sacrifices of life, we are seekers of honor, hopeful for the name.' All the soldiers of the Prophet's army were matchless, but the Prophet gave the standard to our ancestor. In Khaybar, I have seen a massive army, yet Ali (a.s.) held the standard at the time of trial. There is no lack of strength; they are hungry and thirsty, and we are their grandsons, their descendants. Zainab (s.a.) then said, 'What business is it of yours? What concern is it of mine? The Imam is the master of his own affairs. Do not speak disrespectfully; I will be angry if anyone mentions the standard with their tongue. Go, just stand aside, with folded hands. Why have you come here leaving Ali Akbar (a.s.) behind? Move, step back, do not stand near the standard, lest the King of the heavens sees you. You are here, and you have come to my senses, enough. This request is unacceptable.' You will start crying if I say something harsh or kind; what else can I call this stubbornness but childishness? A short life and a desire for a glorious position; alright, find some way to grow taller. May your mother be sacrificed, if you need proof of courage, yes, among your peers, you have no equal. It is necessary to think, to ponder, to look ahead and behind; why should a human not desire what is possible? This standard will be raised by these tiny hands, among the shortest in stature, the youngest in age. The steps of the Prophet's grandson follow one another; this is the only duty, this is the position, this is the grandeur. If you seek permission, that is my task; oh, may your mother be sacrificed, today there is honor in dying. Then what is it to you? If your elders were the pride of the age, it is not appropriate to boast of secondary virtues. True merit is that which one reveals themselves; show today what you can do on the battlefield. Why do you say, 'Oh! We are the sons of the Wali of God,' the army itself proclaims that we are the grandsons of Ali (a.s.). What a price the standard had to be prepared; this was a gift from the Prophet of heavenly status. In difficult battles, they achieved success through it; when they pulled it, Rome and Syria would tremble. When they were displaced, they gave fruits like the trees of the garden; when it remained, God gave wings of jewels in return. When the army suffered defeat for three days, the Prophet of God then bestowed the standard upon Ali (a.s.). When he killed Marhab and advanced, that Lion of God, the entire army of the fort fled, closing the gates. He uprooted it and it fell as if from a hard rock, just as one might pluck a leaf from a tree. For three days, the son of Mushkil-Kusha (the remover of difficulties) has been in the siege; the garden of my mother is being trampled in the wilderness. Did you not ask why you have let your hair loose? I am being looted and you are thinking of positions. You are not my sympathizers, nor lovers of the Imam; it has become clear to me that you are seekers of fame. Folding their hands, they said with tearful eyes, 'Control your anger, O sister of the Imam. By God, there is no chance that anyone will take the name of the standard now; it will be revealed when these loyal slaves fight. We will sleep in the treasure of martyrs after routing the army; then you will realize our worth when we are no more.' Saying this, they moved away, and the mother's heart swelled as she said, 'My dear ones, you give me news of your own death; wait a moment, let me take your afflictions.' 'Why should I be sacrificed? Did the mother's advice seem bad, children? What is this you said, that a dagger has pierced my heart?' Coming to Zainab (s.a.), the King of the Age said, 'Why? Have you heard the words of both sons, sister? Lions of lions, wise and fierce, and breakers of all. Zainab (s.a.), both these flower-bodied ones are unique in this era. To look at them, they are elders in all, they have the ways of elders, their expressions are different, and their intentions are different. At the age of nine or ten, this courage and enthusiasm; has anyone seen such children? Such spirited ones. May fortune favor them, who would dare to face them? In whose lap were they raised, on whose milk were they nourished? Undoubtedly, they are the inheritors of Janab-e-Amir (a.s.), but what can I do, both are of tender age. Now, whoever you say, give them the standard of the army.' 'For the request is the advice of the King of heavenly grandeur, ever since Zahra-e-Ba-Karam (s.a.) passed away, from that day we consider you in the place of a mother. You are the master, whether someone is an elder or a younger, whoever you say, they are entrusted to God.' The sister said, 'You also take someone's name; towards whom is the attention of the Sultan of the elite and the common? And after you, there is your word; if you ask me, O King of heavenly status, in majesty, in stature, in glory, there is no equal; there is no one better than Abbas Namdar (a.s.).' A lover, a slave, a servant of the faith, a self-sacrificer, a son, a brother, the ornament of the side, a practitioner of loyalty. A provider of comfort, obedient, prominent and famous, fierce, a memorial of the father, the pride of the age. Everything is there; he is lion-hearted, brave, virtuous, matchless, one in hundreds, one in thousands. With eyes full of tears, the King of the Age said, 'This is the one.' It is also Ali's (a.s.) will, sister, you call him, where is that breaker of all? Akbar (a.s.) went to his uncle after hearing this, saying, 'The King of the jealous is waiting, come, the aunt has remembered you, O master.' Abbas (a.s.) came, folding his hands, 'King, go to the sister,' said the refuge of the needy. Zainab (s.a.) came there with the standard, weeping bitterly, the King of the heavenly court said, taking the standard, 'Their happiness is that which is the pleasure of the Panjtan (a.s.). Take the standard, brother, this is a gift from the sister.' Placing his hand on the standard, he bowed, and rubbed his face on the feet of his sister with pride. Zainab (s.a.) took his afflictions and said, 'I am sacrificed, Abbas, be careful with the earnings of Fatima (s.a.). If a peaceful situation arises today, then leave tomorrow; oh, take your brother away from these calamities.' I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the High, the Great. Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs, the best Master and the best Helper. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and the end is for the pious and the certain. And blessings and peace be upon the most noble of prophets and messengers, the beloved of the God of the worlds, Abul Qasim Muhammad. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the infallible ones from whom Allah has removed impurity and purified them with a thorough purification. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, especially the Remnant of Allah on earth, our Imam of the time, our guardian, our master, our beloved, our physician, our companion, our intimate, the fortified cave, and the relief of the distressed and the helpless. May my soul and the souls of the worlds be sacrificed for him. Furthermore, our master and leader, Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), has said: 'Whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped, Allah grants him more than his wishes and his needs.' Our master Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) spoke the truth. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The Hadith I have chosen for this gathering, in it the Master of Martyrs says: 'Whoever worships Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped, Allah grants him more than his wishes and his needs.' What is the condition? That he worships as He truly deserves. And worship is impossible without Ma'rifat (recognition). Worship cannot happen without Ma'rifat. If it happens without Ma'rifat, nothing will come of it; the result is zero. Therefore, Ma'rifat is very necessary. The Master of Martyrs himself says that Ma'rifat is very necessary here. And what is Ma'rifat? Here, it is the Ma'rifat of the Imam of the time. For this, it is very necessary that we recognize our Imam of the time and the station of Imamate itself. It is very necessary to recognize the station of Imamate. See what happened after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Immediately after his martyrdom, everything changed. Everyone reached the stage of 'turning back on their heels.' They became inverted; people deviated from the straight path. The result was that the definition of everything changed. For example, what became the definition of Imamate? Generally, the definition of Imamate became: 'Imamate is the general leadership in religion and worldly affairs, as a successor to the Messenger of Allah.' Imamate is the name of government; it became the name of general leadership. Now, slowly, this government kept changing. To give it a religious color, they added 'religion and world' and 'successor to the Messenger of Allah.' Who is the Imam? The successor of the Messenger of Allah, but the one who has the government is the Imam. Now, the focus of Imamate shifted to government. Whoever has the government is the Imam. Slowly, 'religion' was removed from this definition, only 'world' remained. And then, in the end, they started saying, 'We are with whoever wins.' Whoever has the government is the Imam. Now, many other things were added to it; that whoever becomes the Imam, even if he is a transgressor or a sinner, it is fine. If he does whatever he wants, it is fine. There is no problem, as long as he is not outside of Islam, not outside of religion. Even if he is ignorant, it is fine. There is no problem. If an ignorant person becomes an Imam, there is no problem. What will he do? What should he do? He should just take the help of a scholar so that the scholar can issue a fatwa. In this way, the definition of Imamate kept changing, and in the end, it was found that the real Imamate remained nothing; only government remained, which is also called monarchy. Government—just that a man becomes the owner, becomes the king, becomes the ruler. That is everything. Then whether religion remains or not. That is why you look at the history of Islam—rather, one should not say Islam, but the history of Muslims. It is not a very old matter. If you go back just a little, you see that it had not even been 40 or 50 years since the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah. It had barely been 50 years, and who was made the Caliph, the Caliph of the Muslims, the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah? Yazid ibn Muawiyah (may Allah's curse be upon him). They made him that, and they went and said, 'This is the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, the successor of the Messenger of Allah.' Now, who was this Yazid? You know, he was a drunkard. He was one who played with monkeys and dogs. He was one who did not distinguish between marriage and fornication. That is, he had no distinction between what is lawful and what is forbidden. He did not know anything. He was just a debauched person. He had nothing to do with anything else in the world. Now, for him, they fabricated Hadiths, saying that the Messenger of Allah had prophesied that he is among the people of Paradise. Why? Because he went into the army. All the Hadiths were fabricated in his favor so that somehow they could call him a dweller of Paradise. That's it. This whole effort was made. But what is in history cannot be denied by anyone. The reality that exists cannot be denied by anyone; all these things were found in him. Now, if nothing else worked, they started saying he looked very handsome. Does Imamate have a connection to that? He was a great poet. Does Imamate have a connection to that? If this is Imamate, then we should search for the Imam by seeing who looks the most handsome, who is a great poet, and make him the Imam. But all these things were created only so that the real Imamate could be hidden from the people. But while this was happening on one side, on the other side, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were continuing their work of guidance, that is, the guidance and leadership of the people. The Ahlulbayt (a.s.) did not step back from the responsibility they had. Now you see, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are formally defining the Imam and telling what Imamate is. Look carefully, see the difference between the two. There, government and monarchy became Imamate. Now, hear what Imam Reza (a.s.) says about the definition of Imamate. Send Salawat. He says: 'Indeed, Imamate is the foundation of the growing Islam and its lofty branch.' What is Imamate? It is the foundation of religion, of Islam. 'Foundation of Islam,' 'growing'—that which grows is called 'Nami.' That is, through Imamate, Islam grows and becomes great. If there is no Imamate, then growth will not be found in Islam. See, 'growth' means development. That which does not have growth is called dead. If there is no true Imamate in Islam, then this Islam will be dead; it will not be a living Islam. And that is what happened in history. The Imam says that this Imamate is the foundation of Islam and it is that 'growing' foundation and its 'lofty branch.' And what is this Imamate? It is the branch of Islam that is very high. That is, among the branches of the religion of Islam—prayer, fasting, Hajj, Zakat, Khums, Jihad, and all the things that are among the secondary branches of Islam—what is the highest? The most exalted and most important thing is Imamate. How? Because if Imamate is not understood, if you do not follow the correct Imam, the true Imam who is 'Mansus min Allah' (appointed by Allah) and whom the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) introduced, then neither prayer, nor fasting, nor Hajj, nor Khums, nor Jihad—nothing will be understood. And that is why you see that because this was missing in Islam, because people did not follow the true Imam, so many changes occurred in Islam that the true Islam that existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) no longer remains. If this were the true Islam, there would not be so many sects among Muslims. This division of Muslims into so many sects—as I mentioned in the service of the Hadith that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said there would be 73 sects after me. There were 71 sects among the Jews, 72 sects among the Christians, and 73 sects among the Muslims. So why did all these sects form? The reason was that they abandoned the true Imam. When they abandoned the true Imam, everyone went their own way. Now every person is introducing things according to their own understanding. Everyone is talking according to their own perspective. Different prayers, different fasts, different everything, Hajj is different. There are great details to this, but that is not the topic right now. But you see, that is why it is found in the traditions that the Imam (a.s.) says: 'Buniyal Islamu ala khamsatin ashya' (Islam is built upon five things). Islam is built upon five things: 'As-salati waz-zakati wal-hajji was-sawmi wal-wilayah'. Here, when the Imam (a.s.) is explaining, he is introducing Islam in terms of the branches of religion (Furu-e-Deen), not in terms of the roots of religion (Usul-e-Deen). Look, Wilayah and Imamate is something that is in both the roots of religion and the branches of religion. And this is a very important thing, remember. Meaning, Imamate and Wilayah are that. Imamate is in the roots of religion because through the Imam, true Monotheism (Tawhid) is known. Through the Imam, true Justice (Adl) is known, through the Imam, true Prophethood (Nubuwwah) is known, through the Imam, true Imamate is known, and through the Imam, true Resurrection (Qiyamah) is known, provided that people follow the true Imam. If you follow the true Imam, and if you do not follow the true Imam, then neither will Tawhid be correct, nor Adl, nor Nubuwwah, nor Imamate, nor Ma'ad, nor Qiyamah—nothing will be correct. And similarly, in the branches of religion, if there is no true Imam, then neither prayer, nor fasting, nor Hajj, nor Khums—Khums won't even exist—nor Zakat, nor Hajj, nor Jihad will be correct; nothing. Nothing at all. Neither Amr-bil-Ma'ruf (enjoining good) will be correct, nor Nahy-anil-Munkar (forbidding evil), nor Tawalla (loving the Ahlulbayt), nor Tabarra (disassociating from their enemies); nothing will be correct. That is why they say, what do they say in Tawalla and Tabarra, in Amr-bil-Ma'ruf and Nahy-anil-Munkar? They say that if some Fasiq (sinner) and Fajir (wicked person)—who is a Fasiq? Someone who is a drunkard, a gambler—if even he becomes an Imam, it is not right to remove him. Now just do Amr-bil-Ma'ruf to him. For example, 'Imam Sahib, please do not drink alcohol. Imam Sahib, please do not gamble.' This has become their definition of Imamate. But the definition of Imam that the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) gave is: the Imam says that the foundation of Islam is on five things: prayer, fasting, Hajj, Zakat, and the fifth thing is Wilayah. So now Zurarah, Zurarah is among the very special companions of the Imam. Zurarah ibn A'yan. Look, recognize these companions; because of them, true Islam, true Shi'ism has reached us today, and these are not our words. These are the words of the Imams themselves. The Imam (a.s.) says that if these four companions were not there, 'La-darasat atharun-nubuwwah' (the traces of Prophethood would have been erased). If these four companions were not there—and among them is Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Burayd al-Ijli, and Abu Basir. If these four companions were not there, the traces of Prophethood would have been erased. Through whom have these traces of Prophethood reached us? Through these people. And Zurarah especially, look, this Zurarah is strange and extraordinary; there were many brothers. There were many brothers, six or seven brothers. And none of them were Shia, we know. None of them were Shia at first. They had a sister, Umm al-Aswad. Look at this sister, Umm al-Aswad; women have such an important role in Islam. If a woman wants, she can change the entire family. Umm al-Aswad had such a great character, such a great role, that Umm al-Aswad made the whole family Shia. Not just Shia, how? I will present that to you as well. This Umm al-Aswad used to go to the lessons of Abu Khalid al-Kabuli. Abu Khalid al-Kabuli was a student of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.). This Abu Khalid was a companion of the Imam, he was a companion of the fourth Imam, he was a resident of Kabul, Afghanistan, and he used to regularly come to the Imam's lessons. He was among the most excellent students, very excellent. About him, Insha'Allah, if time permits, I will tell you his stories; his stories are very amazing, Abu Khalid's. So this Abu Khalid used to regularly—now what he did was, he started teaching what he learned from the Imam. That was also a very brave act because the situation at that time was very bad. But Abu Khalid, anyway, was a Pathan man, he was not afraid of anyone. So he used to teach, he was brave, he was courageous, he used to teach. Now Umm al-Aswad used to come to that lesson. When she started coming to the lesson, she automatically started saying... This is the truth. And she became a Shia, she became 'Mustabsirah' (one with insight). Allah granted her insight, she became a Shia. Now when she became a Shia, she came home and said to her brothers, especially to Zurarah. She said to Zurarah, 'Zurarah, come, let's go and see what that man says.' Because Zurarah was previously a Jahmi. Jahmiyyah was a sect, a sect among the Muslims. Zurarah used to follow it. So Zurarah said, 'No, no, I will not go there.' The sister insisted, 'Come at least.' When she insisted, he went. When he went, after some questions and answers with Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, Zurarah became a Shia. When Zurarah became a Shia, his brother Humran became one. When Humran became one, then Ubaydullah became one. When Ubaydullah became one, then Bukayr became one. One after another, the brothers kept becoming Shia, among whom six brothers turned out to be Faqih (jurists). Subhan Allah. How Faqih? How Faqih? Think about what status. It is found in the Hadith that when it will be announced on the Day of Judgment, 'Where are the Hawari (special companions) of Imam al-Baqir and Imam as-Sadiq (a.s.)?' Hawari means very special friends. So among them, the first two names are Zurarah and Humran, the two brothers. Now look at the status, look at what it is. And Humran, about Humran, the Imam (a.s.) said, 'At-turu-turu-Humran' (Humran is the standard). The standard is Humran. If you want to see if your belief is correct, present your belief before Humran. If your belief is like Humran's belief, then you are a true Shia. If it is not, then you are not a true Shia. What a status! Shaykh Saduq brought an entire chapter in 'Ma'ani al-Akhbar', page number 200, 212, 'At-turu-turu-Humran'. This is the name of the chapter Shaykh Saduq kept. 'Bab At-turu-turu-Bab At-turu-At-turu-Humran' or 'Bab At-turu-turu-Humran'. 'Turu' means standard, criterion. This Shaykh Saduq brought an entire chapter, now look. And in it, he says, 'Humran is the standard, the criterion of religion, of belief.' The Imam said, 'I [present my belief] before Humran.' And all this happened because of a woman. And that is why, in brackets, I present this to you, that if you want to understand Karbala in its reality, in its truth, then you must understand the role of the women in Karbala. You must understand its importance, read about it. You see what role the women played in Karbala and how, because of them, Karbala remained alive. We will not go into the details of that right now, this is just in brackets. So you see, now Zurarah asked the Imam (a.s.), 'Wa ayyu shayin min dhalika afdal?' (And which of these is the most excellent?). Now when you are saying that these five things are the foundation, the five foundations of religion, then what is the most excellent among them? The best? The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Al-Wilayatu afdal' (Wilayah is the most excellent). Wilayah is more excellent than what? Than prayer. Than what? Than fasting, than Hajj. What is more excellent than all these things? Imamate and Wilayah. Now you won't ask, brother, what is more important? Wow! Wow! Wow! Recite a Salawat upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. But still, there are some people among us who, even after that, ask that no, no, this does not mean this, that does not mean that. Zurarah is asking a very clear question: what is the most excellent? The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Al-Wilayatu afdal.' The Imam also presents evidence for that, gives a reason. Why? 'Li-annaha miftahuhunna' (Because Wilayah is the key to all of them). Because Wilayah is the key, the 'Kalid', the key to all these acts of worship. All acts of worship are known through it, through Imamate. 'Wal-Wali' (meaning the Imam) 'huwa dalilu alayhinna' (he is the guide to them). The Imam guides, the Imam shows how these acts of worship should be performed correctly. Look, we keep reading a Hadith repeatedly so that the point is clear to everyone. A companion of Imam as-Sadiq (a.s.), Allahumma Salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad, came and asked the Imam, 'What is the similarity and what is the difference between us and the opponents?' It was a very simple question of his. What is the similarity and what is the difference between us and other Muslims? The Imam (a.s.) replied that there is no similarity, except that we only face the same Qibla, that's all. 'Istiqbal-ul-Kaaba', nothing else. What is the evidence? The evidence is very simple. Tawhid was changed. Adl was removed from the roots of religion. Nubuwwah, if we talk about that, that is a whole separate chapter. Meaning, how they presented Nubuwwah. If I give just one example, the matter will become clear to you. In the beginning of Nubuwwah, how did they define the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? Gabriel came, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) got scared seeing Gabriel with the revelation. He got afraid, started running here and there. Gabriel said, 'Do not be afraid, I am a messenger. I am the Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) did not even understand. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) came back home, covered himself with a blanket and lay down, started shivering, got a fever. Janab-e-Khadija (s.a.) asked, 'What happened?' He didn't know, meaning he saw something in the Cave of Hira. 'Let's go to my cousin, let's go to Waraqa ibn Nawfal.' They went to Waraqa ibn Nawfal. Who was Waraqa? Was Waraqa a Muslim? No. Waraqa, at that time Islam had not even come, so how could Waraqa be a Muslim? They took him to Waraqa. Waraqa saw, who was Waraqa? Do you know? He was a 'Najumi' (astrologer). You know what an astrologer is, right? He was an astrologer. He saw and said, 'Oh! He has become a Prophet.' He saw and said, 'He has become a Prophet, now he is a Prophet.' So now, if Waraqa understood Nubuwwah better, then he is better suited to be a Prophet than the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself. You saw how they introduced Nubuwwah? This is one example, there are hundreds of such examples. There are hundreds of examples. So, the Imam says, that is why you see, let me present another hadith for your service. And this hadith is very important. It is very important; make it a principle of your life. This narration is from Imam Sadiq (a.s.). Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. The Imam says, "Nahnu aslu kulli khair" (We are the root of all goodness). We are the root of all goodness. What goodness? "Wa min furu'ina" (And among our branches is...). What is among our branches? "Kullu bir" (All righteousness). Whatever good deeds there are, they are all our branches, the branches of Imamate. And what is among our branches? "Wa minal birri at-tawhid" (And among righteousness is Tawhid), meaning true Tawhid, yes. Prayer, fasting, morality, meaning controlling anger, 'afw al-musi' (forgiving the sinners and offenders), having mercy on the poor, taking care of neighbors, and acknowledging the virtue of those who possess virtue. Those who are truly the people of virtue, acknowledging them. Meaning, whatever good deed you can imagine, whether it is in the principles of religion (Usul al-Din), the branches of religion (Furu' al-Din), or in morality, in everything, whatever good deed there is, its root is the Ahl al-Bayt. After that, the Imam says, "Wa aduwwuna aslu kulli sharr" (And our enemy is the root of all evil). All the evils you see, their root is our enemy. And all the ugly and indecent things, meaning all evils and indecencies, they all originate from our enemies. And what is among them? He says: lying, stinginess, backbiting, severing ties of kinship (qat' al-rahm), and consuming usury (riba), consuming the orphan's wealth, the orphan's wealth, in an unjust manner. Consuming the orphan's wealth in an unjust manner is forbidden. "Man akala min amwalina shay'an fa-innama ya'kulu fi batnihi naran wa sa-yasla sa'ira." The Imam says, the interpretation of this verse, what is the verse? "Alladhina ya'kuluna amwalal yatama zulman, innama ya'kuluna fi butunihim naran wa sa-yaslawna sa'ira." This is a verse of the Quran. Those who consume the orphan's wealth, the orphan's wealth, in an unjust manner. This is a Quranic verse, yes brother. "Alladhina ya'kuluna amwalal yatama zulman, innama ya'kuluna fi butunihim naran wa sa-yaslawna sa'ira." Consuming it unjustly, meaning in an unlawful way, meaning they have no right to consume it. Meaning, if someone has a right, we will clarify it a little now. There is a right, but we will explain how. "Zulman innama ya'kuluna fi butunihim naran" (They are only consuming fire into their bellies), and they will soon be thrown into that fire. Why? Because the Imam of the Time (a.j.t.f.) himself says in this Tawqi', while explaining this noble verse, the Imam says: "Man akala min amwalina zulman innama ya'kulu fi batnihi naran wa sa-yasla sa'ira." Whoever consumes anything from our wealth, if anyone consumes even a little bit of our wealth, he is doing what? "Innama ya'kulu fi batnihi naran" (He is only consuming fire into his belly), and he will soon be thrown into the fire. The Imam says, our wealth, what is the Imam's wealth? It is the Sahm-e-Imam (the Imam's share). It is the Sahm-e-Imam. Now, what is the right in this? The right is for someone who is distributing the Sahm-e-Imam, dividing it, distributing the Sahm-e-Imam, reaching it to the people, collecting it, coming and going, doing all of that. So, the effort he is making and the time he is giving, he can take a wage for that effort and time. He can take that much, saying I can take this much. And if someone is working full-time, then how much right does he have to take? What is in the narrations, which the jurists (Fuqaha) have also explicitly stated, is that he can take as much as is sufficient for an ordinary person—if we say in today's time, as much as is enough to run a middle-class family's household, he can take that much. Not more than that. Now, for the rest, you should ask the jurists, the scholars, the Fuqaha, and the Maraje' about what its further interpretation or explanation is; we do not know more than what we have read in the hadiths and the fatwas of the jurists, which we are telling you. You should look into it, read it with peace of mind. And if you need more details, then ask the jurists and Maraje', they will tell you more details about it. So, consuming the orphan's wealth is a very evil thing. A very evil thing. So here, and after that, what is it? "Wa ta'addud hudud allati amarallahu" (And transgressing the limits that Allah has commanded), meaning committing sins, generally sins. Transgressing the limits means crossing Allah's boundaries. This is taken from the second verse of Surah At-Talaq. In Surah At-Talaq, Allah says: "Wa man yata'adda hududallahi faqad zalama nafsah." Whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. He has committed a sin, committed an unlawful act. Well, this sin can happen in two ways. Doing something is a sin, and not doing something is also a sin. For example, if drinking alcohol is a sin, then if someone did it, it is a sin. Okay? Not doing something is also a sin. For example, if a young person is not praying, then this is a sin. This 'tark-e-wajib' (abandoning an obligatory act) is haram, 'tark-e-wajib' is a sin. This is 'ithm', a sin. He will be punished for it. Allah will punish him for it. See, usually, we don't wake the children up in the morning, saying he is sleeping now, he must be tired, don't wake him up. That's why we let them sleep, we don't say anything, he is sleeping, he is sleeping. Well, we also mentioned that, well, in another gathering, not here. That, meaning a young person gets more sleep, especially the youth, children, so that's why there is a proverb in English, 'sleep like a baby'. The younger one is in age, the better he sleeps. That's why they don't pray the morning prayer mostly. There will be very few, rare, who are punctual for the morning prayer. Rare. We are talking about children, we are talking about the youth. So what do we do? We say, 'Oh, he is sleeping, let him sleep.' Don't disturb him, he is sleeping, he is tired, he was studying at night. We just ask you one question: if God forbid, may Allah not let it happen, if there is a fire in your house and it starts in the same room where the child is sleeping. Will you say he is tired, let him sleep? Will you say let him sleep? No. Your attention will first go towards him, how to save him and bring him out. Let him be saved, even if we burn, it's fine. But our child should be saved. So this is that fire which is not the one that burns more, and there is a possibility that he might be saved and the fire might be extinguished. For that, we are so worried. So think about that fire which will be an eternal fire, which will never end, rather about which the Quran says: "Fattaqunnarallati waqudunnasu wal-hijarah." The Quran says, fear that fire whose fuel, whose fuel is humans and stones. Humans are its fuel, the fuel of that fire is humans, the Quran is saying. "Fattaqunnarallati..." We are leaving it and not even advising the children. We ourselves don't care, and we don't advise the children, we don't explain to the children, let it be, let it be. No, no. You insist. See, it is emphasized in the hadith that when a child turns 7 years old, command him to pray. 7 years old. This is in the hadith. And if someone says he hasn't reached puberty yet, no, no, puberty is a different matter at 15 years old. Here we are talking about upbringing. When the child is 7 years old, command him, and when he is 10 years old, and if he doesn't pray, then hit him. 'Hit him' doesn't mean too much, but take a stick and make a little noise so that he doesn't start hating religion. No, no, not like that. It means a little bit so that he knows that yes, it has importance near his parents. It has importance. So it is very necessary. Similarly, fasting is the same, other acts of worship are the same. Hajj, we ignore Hajj very easily. Even those who are capable (Sahib-e-Istita'at) do not go for Hajj. Hajj is obligatory. And it is in the narrations that if someone who is capable can perform Hajj but does not do it, then if he dies, he will die the death of a Jew or a Christian, but he will not die as a Muslim. This is in the narrations. And there is so much emphasis. Of course, this is the first level of capability. But if you go a little deeper, then the Imam of the Imams (a.s.) explicitly emphasizes it so much, gives so much stress, saying that even if you have to take a loan to go, then go. Even if you have to take a loan. Why? You are performing a very important act of worship. So the Imam says here that a person must avoid sins. After that, he says, "Wa rukubul fawahish" (And avoid indecencies), and avoid 'fawahish'. Meaning 'fawahish', meaning indecencies, evil deeds that are dirty, whether apparent or hidden. Meaning, apparently or secretly, whatever it is. And avoid adultery, and theft, and "wa kullu ma wusifa minal qabih" (and everything that has been described as ugly in Islam), and it has been called ugly, avoid it, maintain distance from it. It has been said to maintain distance from it. After that, now when the Imam divided both things, that what is good and what is evil. After that, the Imam says a sentence. He says, "Wa kadhaba man za'ama annahu ma'ana wa huwa muta'alliqun bi furu'i ghairina." (And he is a liar who claims or assumes that he is with us, but he is attached to the branches of others.) He is a liar, that person who makes this claim or assumes, he assumes that he is one of us, he is our lover, he is our Shia, but his actions are like our enemies. He commits unlawful acts, commits sins, and claims that we are lovers of the Ahl al-Bayt. What kind of lover is he? He cannot be a lover. So the Imam says, and similarly, there is another hadith similar to this, meaning in the context of this verse, the Imam says that Allah has forbidden all 'fawahish', meaning 'fawahish', meaning evil things, indecencies, Allah has forbidden them. So what is apparent from this? What are the evil deeds? And what is the hidden meaning? They are the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt. Allah has forbidden even going near the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt. Those who are near the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt. That, meaning, or those who usurped the right of the Ahl al-Bayt, listening to their words. Anyway, there are details about that, Insha'Allah, we will present them to you some other time. Now, that is why see, what is the Imamate of Islam? It is the perfection of Islam. Islam becomes complete with Imamate. Meaning, before moving forward, now let us mention a person in your service who was completely immersed in the love of Ali and the Wilayat of Ali. Completely immersed in Wilayat. And who was that? It was Janab-e-Maytham al-Tammar, who is also called Maytham al-Tammar. What was the real name, Maytham al-Nahrawani? Because he was from Nahrawan, he was Iraqi, and 'Tammar' because he used to set up a date stall. That's why they also called him 'Tammar'. They say Maytham says that one day Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) called me and started saying to me, "O Maytham! What will be your condition at that time when the wretch of the Banu Umayya" (meaning the Imam used a specific word for him, we are using a very mild word) "the wretch of the Banu Umayya, Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, will tell you to curse Ali, to speak ill of Ali?" So Maytham said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin! By God, I can never do this work. I will never do it." The Master of the Universe asked a second question, "Do you know what the outcome is? Do you know the outcome?" He said, "What will happen, Mawla?" He said, "They will kill you and they will also hang you on the gallows." Listen to Maytham's answer, it is a beautiful answer. He said, "I will bear this little trouble. I will bear this little trouble." The Mawla says, "Then if you bear this, you will be with me in Paradise." (Idhan takuna ma'i fi darajati) You will be with me in Paradise. What follows after that? (وَكَانَ مِيثَمٌ يَمُرُّ بِعَرِيفِ قَوْمِهِ) Maytham used to go to the leader of his tribe—'Areef' means leader—and say, "O so-and-so! (كَأَنِّي بِكَ) I can see you." Now look, he is repeating the same thing from that day. The one we discussed that day, whose was it? It was Rushayd al-Hajari. Now, the Mawla had told Maytham so much, but look at the level he was at, saying, "I see that the wretched one from Banu Umayya is calling you and telling you and me to bring Maytham to him, and you take me to that wretched one, and that wretched one from Banu Umayya hangs me on the gallows." After that, Maytham went to Amr ibn Huraith and said to him, "I will be killed very soon, and I will become your neighbor." So Amr said, "I wish it were so." Then Maytham went to that tree, because the Mawla had said that the date palm tree outside Amr ibn Huraith's house is where you will be hanged. You will be hanged on that tree. Now, Maytham would pass by that tree repeatedly and water it, tending to it so that the tree would not dry up. Do you see his faith? Maytham would tend to it. Now, what happened? The time came. The time came when Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad—may Allah's curse be upon him—this wretched man became the governor of Kufa, and he summoned Maytham. He had previously called that 'Areef', the tribal leader, and said, "I want Maytham." He replied, "Maytham has gone to Mecca." He said, "Summon him, bring him by any means." So he sent a message to Maytham. Maytham came. He went a long way to meet Maytham and brought him, and stood Maytham before Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad—may Allah's curse be upon him—saying, "This is Maytham." Then a detailed conversation took place between Maytham and Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad. Let me briefly present it to you. He asked, "Are you Maytham?" Maytham said, very proudly, "Yes, I am Maytham." Look, some people nowadays start speaking Arabic a bit too much, so they pronounce it 'Maysam'. 'Maysam' is the wrong pronunciation, yes. 'Maytham' is the correct pronunciation. The correct pronunciation is indeed 'Maytham'. But those people start saying 'Maitham', 'Maitham'—it is not 'Maitham', it is 'Maytham'. 'Maytham'—meaning what we read in Arabic, 'Maytham', not 'Maysam'. Anyway, this was originally a Persian word that was Arabized. So, this Maytham, he said, "Are you Maytham?" He said, "Yes, I am Maytham." He said, "Curse Abu Turab. Curse Abu Turab." Maytham said, "Which Abu Turab? I do not know any Abu Turab." So he said, "You don't know Abu Turab? Curse Ali ibn Abi Talib." Maytham said, "And if I do not?" "Then I will kill you." Maytham said, "My Mawla used to say that Maytham, you will be killed, and you will be hanged on the tree outside Amr ibn Huraith's house, and after being hanged for three days, on the fourth day, blood will start flowing from your nose, meaning your death will come. You will remain hanging on the gallows for three days, and on the fourth day, death will come to you." Allahu Akbar. Do you understand what it means to be on the gallows for three days? To remain on the gallows for three days—just stand like that for a little while, and if a person is just left hanging like that, in a little while, the person will get tired and distressed. We are talking about a short time. At most, half an hour, an hour, two hours; a person cannot hang for longer than that if both hands are tied. Here, Maytham is hanging for three days. On the fourth day, blood started flowing from his nose. Ibn Ziyad the accursed said that the same should be done to him. After that, when Maytham was being taken away, Maytham said, "O people of Kufa!" Look at this sentence I was presenting to you; look at the status and rank of those who are drowned in the love of Ali. "O people of Kufa! I am being taken to be killed, this will happen, whatever it is—not the details, in short—I have been killed. If you want to know anything about the future, ask me, I will tell you. I will tell you." Meaning, the tribulations, the creation, whatever it is, all the tribulations that will happen until the Day of Judgment, Maytham says, "I can tell you about all the tribulations that are to happen until the Day of Judgment." When a lover of Ali possesses such knowledge, then what can you say about the Ahlulbayt? And then people started asking questions. So you know what he did to Maytham? Ibn Ziyad ordered that Maytham's mouth be tied with those thick ropes so that he could not speak. The thick ropes—there is a specific word for it in Arabic. They were tied with those ropes, so Maytham's entire mouth was tied with those ropes, and then Maytham was hanged. And it is written in the hadith that he was the first person in Islam, Maytham was the first person whose mouth was tied with ropes in this manner. After that, it became a common practice of Banu Umayya, and after Banu Umayya, the Banu Marwan did this work, that whoever spoke too much, they would tie their mouths with these ropes. And after Banu Marwan, the Banu Abbas also started it, and all these rulers of the so-called 'Golden Period' of Islam, they all did this work, which these people call the 'Golden Period'. This is their 'Golden Period'. So, Maytham with ropes in his mouth, thick ropes in his mouth—this is very severe; a person would die right then. This was the case of Karbala. This was the case. Maytham was telling what was going to happen, and this same Ibn Ziyad—look, the Ahlulbayt do not do anything by deceit. What the Ahlulbayt do, they do openly. Even when Janabe Muslim had the chance to kill Ibn Ziyad in the house of Hani ibn Urwa, he had the chance to kill him in the house of Hani ibn Urwa, but he did not kill him because the Ahlulbayt do not do anything by deceit. Remember, this is the principle of the Ahlulbayt. But anyway, then what he did to Muslim, You know that. And this is what happened in Karbala, then when on the day of Ashura, one by one they kept being martyred. The sequence of martyrdom started from the morning. Until when the Banu Hashim, the children of Aqeel, had given their martyrdom, then it was the turn of the children of Abdullah ibn Ja'far. When it was the turn of the children of Abdullah ibn Ja'far, Janabe Zainab said to her sons, "Go sons, go take permission from your uncle and go be martyred." Go sacrifice yourselves for your uncle. Janabe Zainab was instructing her children, saying, "Go son, go." The children were saying, "Mother, you come yourself, you get us permission from our uncle." Zainab took the hands of both children, Awn and Muhammad, and brought them and stood silently before Hussain. Now, who would know Zainab better than Hussain? He asked, "Sister Zainab, why have you come?" She said, "Brother, you know why I have come." And I know that you will not reject my request. Brother, now give these children permission. Now the family of Muslim has also been martyred, now let my children be martyred, now let them be sacrificed. Hussain gave permission. It is written in the Maqtal that Zainab brought both children to the tent and Zainab herself prepared them. And Zainab was preparing them and explaining, "Look sons, you are going, you are going for martyrdom, for sacrifice, you are going to fight, but keep two things in mind. Keep two things very much in mind. One, fight in such a way that people themselves say that these are the grandsons of Ja'far-e-Tayyar and the great-grandsons of Haider-e-Karrar." That Mir Anees says, "Why do you say they are the sons of God's Wali, the army should cry out that they are the grandsons of Ali." She instructed them well, explained well. The one explaining, "Son, look, the second thing is that I know you have been hungry and thirsty for three days, but do not turn towards water because the children in the tent are thirsty. Ali Asghar is thirsty, Sakina is thirsty, everyone in the tent is thirsty. Do not even let the thought of water come to your mind." Now listen to the sentences of the Maqtal, I leave them to you. And it is written in the Maqtal that one brother attacked the right flank, the other brother attacked the left flank. One brother sent some horsemen to Hell and some who were on foot to Hell. The other brother also sent horsemen and foot soldiers to Hell in the same way. When both brothers were attacking the right and left flanks like this, Ibn Sa'd, Umar ibn Sa'd said, "Surround them and kill them. These are the children of Banu Hashim, not the children of the grocers and merchants of Kufa. Surround them and attack." When the attack happened, first one brother fell from the horse, then the other brother fell from the horse. They called out, "Uncle, goodbye." Hussain went, took his strength, Abbas, with him. When they reached the Maqtal, both children had departed from this world. Hussain picked up the body of one, Abbas picked up the body of the other. They brought them and placed them in the tent. And when they placed the bodies in the tent, Fizza came and said, "Lady, come see, the princes have arrived." When Zainab was on her prayer mat, she said, "I did not tell them to come back. Why have they returned?" Fizza joined her hands in respect and said, "Lady, just look at the condition in which they have arrived." Now when Zainab came and saw, she saw the scene that Allah should not show any mother. On one side the body of Awn, on the other side the body of Muhammad. Zainab performed a prostration of gratitude. "O Lord, accept this small sacrifice of mine." It is not found anywhere that Zainab mourned for Awn and Muhammad. Whenever Zainab mourned, she mourned for Hussain. She mourned for the family of Hussain. The 11th of Muharram came, Zainab did not mourn for Awn and Muhammad. She reached Kufa, she did not mourn for Awn and Muhammad. She went from Kufa to Sham, she did not mourn for Awn and Muhammad. She came back from Sham to Karbala, she did not mourn for Awn and Muhammad. Then, when she returned from Karbala to Medina, Zainab (a.s.) sat outside her house. Zainab (a.s.) had been shattered by the tragedy of Karbala. Abdullah ibn Ja'far could not recognize her. He said, "Bibi, why are you sitting outside like this? Why are you sitting outside? Please go inside your house." Zainab (a.s.) lifted her veil for a moment. "Oh Abdullah, even you did not recognize me?" Seeing the condition of Zainab (a.s.), Abdullah began to weep loudly. He held Zainab's (a.s.) arm and brought her into the house. The Zainab (a.s.) who had been patient until now, the moment she entered the house and saw the small beds of Aun and Muhammad, the mother's heart broke. She remembered her children. "Waa Auna, Waa Muhammada, Waa Sayyida." Sayalamul-ladhina zalamu ayya munqalabin yanqalibun. Ala la'natullahi 'alaz-zalimin. O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). O Lord, hasten the reappearance of Hazrat Baqiyatullah al-A'zam, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance. Count us among his followers and helpers. O Lord, remove the difficulties of those who are in distress. Pay off the debts of those who are in debt. Grant those who are childless, righteous and virtuous children. Grant those who are ill, a complete and swift recovery. Return those who are far from their homelands safely and soundly. Wherever the Shias of Haider-e-Karrar are in the world, protect their lives, wealth, honor, and dignity. O Lord, protect the great scholars and the esteemed Maraje. Protect the sacred shrines. Protect those who are protecting them. Especially protect the shrine of Janab-e-Zainab (a.s.). Protect those who are protecting it. O Lord, grant us the honor of the Ziyarat of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in this world, and the intercession of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in the hereafter. Matam-e-Hussain.

chapters.title: The Sons of Zainab and the Standard
chapters.summary: The sons of Zainab (s.a.) express their desire to carry the standard of the Imam, leading to a poignant exchange about merit, sacrifice, and the true nature of service.

chapters.title: The Selection of Abbas (a.s.)
chapters.summary: Imam Husayn (a.s.) and Lady Zainab (s.a.) discuss the qualities of the youth and ultimately entrust the standard to Abbas (a.s.) due to his unmatched loyalty and stature.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Ma'rifat in Worship
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces a Hadith from Imam Husayn (a.s.) emphasizing that true worship requires Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Imam of the time.

chapters.title: Distortion of the Concept of Imamate
chapters.summary: The speaker explains how the definition of Imamate was corrupted from divine leadership into mere political monarchy, leading to the acceptance of corrupt rulers.

chapters.title: Ahlulbayt's Definition of True Imamate
chapters.summary: The Ahlulbayt countered political distortions by defining Imamate as the essential, growing foundation of Islam, without which religious practices are incomplete.

chapters.title: Wilayah as the Core of Religious Practice
chapters.summary: Imamate and Wilayah are presented as the central pillars that validate all other aspects of faith, including the roots and branches of religion.

chapters.title: The Role of Companions and Family in Preserving Islam

chapters.summary: The speaker recounts how the family of Zurarah became Shia through the influence of his sister and the guidance of Imam al-Baqir and Imam as-Sadiq, highlighting their status as special companions.

chapters.title: Wilayah as the Foundation of Religion
