title: The Heroics of Hisham ibn Hakam (may Allah have mercy on him)  |  Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi (ENG SUBS)
excerpt: This lecture explores the life and intellectual prowess of Hisham ibn Hakam, a prominent companion of Imam Jafar al-Sadiq. Originally a follower of the Jahmiyyah sect, Hisham converted to Shi'ism after meeting the Imam and subsequently became a formidable defender of the faith. The talk highlights his youthful brilliance in theological debates and how he was frequently chosen by the Imam to represent the school of Ahlulbayt against opponents.
content:
Hisham was a Jehmia. He was not a Shia. Jehmia was a different sect. Those who followed Jehm ibn Safwan were called Jehmia. Their beliefs were completely different. Hisham's uncle told him, "which path are you treading on... ...come with me, I will introduce you to a man." Hisham asked: "Who is this man?" His uncle replied: "Jafar bin Mohammad (peace be upon him)." Hisham came to meet Imam Jafar Sadiq (peace be upon him). In his first session, he converted to Shiaism. And what a personality Hisham ibn Hakam became! How can we understand Hisham! Once Hisham asked Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) a question. The question was related to Tauheed. Hisham asked: "Master, what is the meaning of Allah?" Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) replied in a single sentence. Then Imam (peace be upon him) asked: "Did you understand, O Hisham?" Hisham replied: "O Son of the Prophet (peace be upon him), please explain further." Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) explained a bit further (another line) Then Imam (peace be upon him) said: "O Hisham, this is enough for you..." ...these couple of words/lines are enough for you... ...to defeat our enemies and completely dominate them. Hisham says, "from the time I got up from this session... Look at how a youth should be trained ...till the rest of my life, nobody could defeat me... ...in the discussion of Tauheed." How old was Hisham? He didn't even have a beard. He was 16/17 years old. He was so young! Nobody could defeat him in debates And whenever anyone used to come to debate with Imam (peace be upon him) Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) used to say: "CALL HISHAM!" Then Imam (peace be upon him) used to say "First debate him (Hisham), then we will debate." Imagine the lofty position of Hisham ibn Hakam. Once a Syrian came to Makkah to debate Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) during Hajj. The Syrian said to the Imam (peace be upon him): "I'm here to debate you." Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructed his slave (Yunus) to call a debater. So Yunus went and called several debaters one after another, but Imam (peace be upon him) refused all of them Many of them who were refused were as old as 90 years. such as Qais ibn Maasir, he was 90 years old And Qais ibn Maasir wasn't any ordinary debater He was taught the art of debate by Imam Zainal Abideen (peace be upon him). But Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) refused Qais ibn Maasir as well. Then Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked: "Then who?" Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) replied: "Bring Hisham!" Then Hisham was summoned. and Hisham debated the Syrian. It is a two page debate in Al Kafi & Behaar al Anwaar. Hisham defeated him & made him convert to Shiaism, on the spot.

title: Girya e Zahra (sa) |  Ep#11 - Kya Imam Ali(as) Ke Qaatilaane H. Zahra(sa) Se Achche Taalluqaat The?
excerpt: This lecture addresses the common misconception that Imam Ali (a.s.) maintained friendly relations with the individuals who oppressed Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). The speakers provide historical evidence, including the Imam's refusal to attend their funerals and the refusal of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) to return their greetings. By citing authentic Sunni sources like Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the lecture demonstrates that Imam Ali (a.s.) openly regarded these figures as untrustworthy and tyrannical, refuting claims of a harmonious relationship.
content:
Do it. [Music]... In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Peace and blessings be upon the Prophet and his family. Peace be upon you all. Welcome to this new episode of the series. Today, we will discuss an objection that is raised not only by opponents but sometimes even by our own people, who say strange things. The objection is: 'Did Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) have good relations with the enemies of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.w.a.)?' We will see if this is true, if there is any reality to it, and if not, what evidence we have. To answer this, we have our brother Qasim with us. Peace be upon you. Are you well? All praise is to Allah, prayers to you. As you heard, people, especially opponents, ask this question... Opponents, especially, raise this objection that Ali (a.s.) had very good relations with the enemies of Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and used to help them. They also say that if Ali (a.s.) himself had good relations, then why do you speak ill of them? We want you to tell us if this was really the case, and if not, please provide evidence. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Brother, the first thing to present before you—and all scholars will accept this, even if opponents might deny it due to their sectarian compulsions—is that this is our belief, our faith, that the Masumeen (a.s.) are the manifestation of the mercy of Allah. Just as the Creator of the universe feeding the Pharaoh is a manifestation of His being the Lord of the Worlds, similarly, the Masumeen (a.s.) helping their enemies and saving them from difficulties is a manifestation of something else entirely. And we do not just believe in Ali; we believe in Ali because of that noble character, the likes of which cannot be presented. Amir al-Mu'minin helping his enemies is a manifestation of his being a 'Mushkil Kusha' (Solver of difficulties). Now, let's come to the actual point regarding the enemies of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) and Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.w.a.). Those who killed Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.w.a.) and committed atrocities against her—there is no room for improvement there. However, this enmity is clear in the books of both sects. And this is only done to hide the truth, as opponents spread such things so that ignorant and simple-minded Muslims can be misled. I will present a very famous historical fact before you: those with whom it is claimed Ali had good relations, they all died in the neighborhood of Ali in Medina, during Ali's lifetime, but Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) did not attend a single one of their funerals. Not participating in the funeral is a result of the fact that those who did not participate in the funeral of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) took special care not to participate in the funerals of all those individuals. Another point that emerges from this is regarding those people to whom Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) did not return the greeting of peace (Salam). As it has been beautifully said, 'The one to whom Zahra (s.a.) did not return the Salam, that person cannot be a Muslim.' Following that same path, Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) did not participate in the funerals of those individuals. Finally, the most important point to present before you is that, let alone participating in the funeral, it was such that when they died, their corpse remained in the streets of Medina for three days, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) did not give permission for them to be buried. And when the people of Banu Umayya came to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) with a request, saying, 'Mawla, give permission to bury him,' Mawla gave permission, but with one condition: that he should not be buried in the cemetery of the Muslims. So, where should he be buried? If you... So, where should he be buried? If you... if you know, do you know where this is found? It is good. Meaning, this proves that these people were not Muslims at all. Absolutely, Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) not returning the Salam, and Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) not participating in their funeral, proves that they were not Muslims. Now, we request all innocent Muslims to open the eyes of their hearts, remove the layers of negligence from their hearts, and with the eyes of reality, descend into the depths of history to seek the truth: were the relations of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) really good with these people? Absolutely not. These are the things that have been presented to you from the perspective of history. Let us also present some traditions before you, and not from our books, but from the books of the opponents. They are present in their books as well. Absolutely, if you look at these sources... absolutely, and those too, not just small books, but from major, authentic books, I am going to present those things before you which will make it absolutely clear that the relations of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) were not good with these people. The first tradition I have to present before you is from Sahih Muslim, and its author, Muslim bin al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi, writes this. Through this book, he narrates the tradition that Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, who was the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and addressing Imam Ali (a.s.), is saying... Addressing Imam Ali (a.s.), he is saying, and the interesting thing is that not only were these two people present there, but there is a long list of others who were also present, such as Uthman bin Affan was also present, Abdur Rahman was also present, and others were also present. Now, listen to what he says: 'When the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) departed from this world, you both took over the reins of the Caliphate, and you considered him (the first Caliph) a liar, a sinner, a treacherous person, and a deceiver. And when he died and I came in his place, you both considered me the same.' And I give the reference for this: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad, Chapter 15, Hadith number 1756, page number 840. On page 840, this is recorded. Similarly, the second thing I will present before you from Sahih Bukhari, in which Muhammad bin Ismail is the narrator, he narrates a Hadith from Aisha bint Abu Bakr, in which Aisha says, regarding Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), that Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) considered Umar a tyrant and an ignorant person. Imam Ali (a.s.) used to avoid meeting Umar and did not feel comfortable in the presence of others. I will also give you the reference for this: this tradition is recorded in Sahih Bukhari, Book number 64, Hadith number 278. And one last tradition I will present before you, and this is not a small book; it is a very popular book among the Ahlul-Sunnah, 'Tarikh al-Tabari'. In this book, regarding the Battle of Siffin, when they were going, when they were moving towards Siffin, the first Caliph said to Abbas, what did he say? Now listen to this: 'Regarding your cousin (Ali), I have complaints.' By cousin, he means... Complaints; by cousin, he means us. Yes. I had requested him to follow this path, but he flatly refused. Your cousin is always restless in our presence.' So, these traditions are present in very few books. Now tell me, is there any human who considers another human a liar, a conspirator, a sinner, a traitor, a tyrant, an ignorant person? So, how can these be good relations? All these things are understood, and it is being spread in history and among all Muslims that Amir al-Mu'minin's (a.s.) relations with these people were good. With those people who did what they did to Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.)? The result is the same. So, these are not just our books; I have presented these traditions to you from their books. So, surely... I hope... One last thing I will say to conclude my talk: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated, 'Fatima is a part of me; whoever hurts her, hurts me.' Whoever hurts Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), hurts the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and even hurts Allah. So, how can my Mawla maintain good relations with those people? Whoever hurts her, hurts me. Whoever hurts Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), hurts the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and even hurts Allah. So, how can my Mawla maintain good relations with those people? Absolutely correct. In this regard, a couplet by a poet comes to mind: 'Some people do not like my Mawla.' I also request the viewers to listen: 'Some people do not like my Mawla, some people do not like me because of him.' Thank you very much for presenting the answer to this question in such a good way and in such a good style. We saw how this idea, that the enemies of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) had very good relations with Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), is completely wrong. Ali (a.s.) did not have good relations with them at all. We saw that neither did Ali (a.s.) participate in their funerals, nor did Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.) return their Salam. And along with this, we saw those traditions from their own books, such as Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, in which such words were used that a person who has good relations with someone would never use for them. We saw those traditions in which such words were used that a person who has good relations with someone would never use for them. So, with this, the episode ends here. Insha'Allah, we will be back soon with the next episode. And on this topic, if you have any objections in your mind, then send them to our social media handles. Insha'Allah, the answers will be given from here. Wa al-hamdulillah rabbil alamin.

title: Shahaadat-e-Husain (a.s.) Par Farishton Mein Kohraam | #Muharram2026
excerpt: This lecture discusses a narration from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) regarding the reaction of the angels to the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (a.s.). It highlights the divine promise of retribution for the killers of the Imam, which will be fulfilled through the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.). The talk explains the significance of the title 'Qaim' as it relates to the Imam's state of worship and his future role in seeking justice.
content:
Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) says: 'When my grandfather Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred, at that time the angels lamented and cried, pleading in the court of Allah, 'O our Lord and our Master, will You ignore the one who killed Your chosen servant, the son of Your chosen servant, and the best of Your creation?' Then Allah (azza wa jall) revealed to them, 'O My angels, be at peace and rest. I swear by My honor and majesty, I will surely take revenge on them, even if it is after a period of time.' Then Allah (azza wa jall) lifted the veil from the light of the Imams (a.s.) who were to come from the progeny of Imam Hussain (a.s.) before the angels. The angels saw those lights and were happy. One of those lights was in a state of standing (Qiyam). At that time, Allah (azza wa jall) said, 'This Qaim (the one who was in the state of standing) is the light of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.).' So Allah says, 'Through this Qaim, i.e., Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), I will take revenge on them, i.e., the killers of Imam Hussain (a.s.).' From this Hadith, it is clear that when the angels saw the light of Imam-e-Zaman (a.s.), he was in a state of standing for worship, meaning he was standing, and Allah remembered him by the name 'Qaim' because of that specific state. Apart from this, Allah Ta'ala is swearing by His honor and majesty, promising that the revenge for the blood of Imam Hussain (a.s.) will be taken in any case, no matter how much time it takes. This is something that is inevitable and necessary. Let us pray in the court of the Almighty: 'Ya Rabbal Hussain, bihaqqil Hussain, ishfi sadral Hussain, bi-zuhuril Hujja. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum wa lana da'a-mashfa.'

The title 'Qaim' signifies the Imam's readiness and standing for the cause of Allah.

title: Mahdaviyyat Webinar | Session # 6 | Ghaibat-e-Sughra and the 4 Special Deputies (r.a.) - Part 2
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical and spiritual significance of the four special deputies (Nawwab-e-Arba) during the Minor Occultation (Ghaibat-e-Sughra) of the 12th Imam. It emphasizes that serving the Ahlulbayt is a privilege for the believer rather than a necessity for the Imams, who are divinely supported. The session clarifies the distinction between the divinely appointed special deputies and the general authority of jurists, while providing practical guidance on maintaining spiritual connection with the Imam through piety, charity, and obedience.
content:
Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum, wa ahlik aduwwahum minal jinni wal insi minal awwalina wal akhirin. Astaghfirullaha alladhi la ilaha illa huwal hayyul qayyum, ar-rahmanur rahim, dhul jalali wal ikram, wa atubu ilayh. A'udhu billahi as-sami'il 'alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasani, salawatuka 'alayhi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma ajjil li-waliyyikal faraj, waj'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi wa shi'atihi wa khuddamihi, wa la taj'alna min a'da'ih. La'anallahu Muhammadan wa alahut tahirin. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad, wa ajjil farajahum, wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I welcome you all to this sixth session of the webinar. As I mentioned to you yesterday, our session today will continue yesterday's discussion, titled 'The Minor Occultation and the Four Deputies'. And with us today, once again, is the honorable Maulana Syed Abu Talib Tabatabai. Alhamdulillah, he will enlighten us by drawing from the biographies of the Four Deputies, helping us understand the secrets of becoming closer to our Imam of the Time, Hazrat Yusuf-e-Zahra, Hujjat ibn al-Hasan al-Askari, may Allah hasten his noble reappearance. Since there was such an interesting discussion on the topic yesterday, I do not want to stand between you viewers and the honorable Maulana. Therefore, I will make the requests that I usually make later, right now: please continue sending your questions via the PSR WhatsApp number [number removed], and through the Q&A and chat in Zoom. Keeping with our routine, I will briefly present a summary of yesterday's discussion for you. The discussion began with the last verse of Surah Al-e-Imran, in which the Lord of the Worlds says: "O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful." In the context of this verse, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) says: "Remain in contact with your awaited Imam." This contact provided the link to the topic of the Four Deputies, where the discussion began regarding the four special deputies during the time of the Imam's Minor Occultation. The first special deputy was Abu Amr, Janab Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Umari (r.a.), about whom the Imam of the Time himself wrote a condolence letter to his son upon the passing of Uthman ibn Sa'id, in which the Imam said: "Your father lived a blessed life and died in a praiseworthy manner; may Allah have mercy on him and join him with his friends and masters (peace be upon them)." That is, your father lived a life of felicity, and his death was also praiseworthy, meaning worthy of praise and commendation, and may Allah have mercy on him, for he has gone to meet his friends and his Master. "He was always striving," he was always struggling, working hard, "in their affairs, striving for what would bring him closer to Allah (Azza wa Jall) and to them; may Allah brighten his face and forgive his slips." That is, he was always striving, struggling on this path; the only goal was to attain closeness to Allah and the friends of Allah. Through this letter, the Imam (a.s.) selected Muhammad ibn Uthman Sa'id al-Umari as his second deputy and said: "And it is among the perfections of his felicity that Allah (Azza wa Jall) blessed your father with a son like you, who will succeed him after him and stand in his place by His command." That is, after Uthman ibn Sa'id, his son, Muhammad ibn Uthman Sa'id al-Umari, became the second special deputy of the Imam. You can find this letter in Sheikh Saduq's (r.a.) book 'Kamal al-Din', Volume 2, page 510. Now, we request the honorable Maulana Syed Abu Talib Tabatabai to continue his discussion. Assalamu Alaikum, Agha. Walaikum Assalam. Our viewers, Alhamdulillah, I hope you are also well. Alhamdulillah, thank you very much. Agha, our viewers liked yesterday's session very much, but I have one request for you first, and that is if you could repeat the answer to yesterday's last question, it would be a favor, and those believers who could not hear the answer clearly yesterday will also benefit from your answer. Yes, yes. First, I will begin. A'udhu billahi as-sami'il 'alim minash shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir rahmanir rahim. Wa salli ala sayyidina Muhammadin wa ali baytihit tayyibinat tahirin, wal la'nud da'imu 'ala a'da'ihim ajma'in. The verse from yesterday must surely be in your minds. Well, the question from yesterday was—now look, I ask for your permission, the talk will be a bit long because I cannot just say it in two or four sentences and move on, and my intention here, the purpose, is that the matter is clearly understood by all of you. All 35-40 of our participants, I want to make the matter clear in their minds. I hope my voice is reaching you, because the tasbih in front of our Mr. Jafari has stopped. Yes, yes, Maulana Sahib, your voice is coming through perfectly. Alhamdulillah. Well, look, yesterday the talk was rushed. First of all, why should we give charity on behalf of the Imam? I will strengthen the question further, given that it is through the Imam's charity that calamities are removed from us. If I may say, I will take it in ascending order, going from bottom to top, okay? We are in need of our parents' prayers. No one doubts this. Our parents pray, and as a result of our parents' prayers, many of our difficulties are eased. So then, when you go for Ziyarat, why do you pray Namaz on behalf of your parents as a proxy? Why do you give charity on behalf of your parents? When you go for Ziyarat, why do you pray for your parents as a proxy, and why do you pray two rak'ats of Namaz at the head of the grave? You yourself are in need of your parents' prayers, we ourselves are in need of our parents' prayers, so when we go there, why do we pray for our parents? This will make the matter clear. Similarly, we perform acts on behalf of all the Imams, we perform acts on behalf of Janab-e-Sayyida (s.a.), we offer them as gifts in their presence, and likewise, the series of Azadari—there is no shortage of those who weep for Imam Hussain (a.s.). From the Messenger of Allah to Hazrat Adam (a.s.), and from the close angels and the Cherubim of the Throne down to Hazrat Adam and below, down to Hazrat Isa (a.s.) and the Messenger of God, all of them weep over the tragedies of Imam Hussain (a.s.). So then, what need does God have for our weeping? Such emphasis has been placed on it. So keep all these things in your mind. Now, what is the essence of this? It is not necessary that if someone holding a superior designation, a high office, or a high status provides us with benefits, then the law says we cannot provide any benefit to them from our own selves. That is the first point. From here arises the question: Maulana, can we provide a benefit to the Imam of the Time? Is this possible? God forbid, how can this be? My question to you: if we were in the time of Janab-e-Sayyida (s.a.), and we were living in the neighborhood of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), living in the house next door, in the neighborhood of the Master of the Universe, would we cook good food in our house and take it to the house of the Master of the Universe or not? We would say to the Master of the Universe, "O Son of the Messenger of Allah, Imam Hassan, Imam Hussain, or Janab-e-Amir al-Mu'minin, or Amir al-Mu'minin, do you have any work? Tell us." I am talking very simply—washing dishes in the house. The Mawla would say, "May God have mercy on you, do this work in our house, grind the flour, soothe Hassan and Hussain." If our women went to Janab-e-Zainab (a.s.), would we be providing a benefit to the family of Prophethood or not? Question. Mawla, should just the angels come for their service? So what is our need for them? I mean, should I and you go, what is the need? If Abu Dharr, Salman, Ammar, and Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari go into the house and perform the service of Janab-e-Amir like servants, then they could call the angels. They can call the angels, but they were not sent to be Imams for the angels. Although they are the Imams of the angels too. They are the means for the angels, they are the proof for the angels. But they were sent into the world for our guidance. It is as if we want to prove that, "O Son of the Messenger of Allah, O Amir al-Mu'minin, O Princess of the Two Worlds, the difficulty that has fallen upon you, we are with you." Pay attention to this word. We are with you. This is proof of being together, this is proof of companionship. This is, in a way, proof that our hearts, minds, and souls are present with these personalities. Whenever they face any worldly suffering, we want to be the first to step forward. "Fastabiqul-khayrat"—what? "Fastabiqul-khayrat," race towards good deeds. Janab-e-Amir can call the angels, Janab-e-Amir can take service from the Malaika, but we have been commanded, "Fastabiqul-khayrat," race towards good deeds, towards righteous acts. Why go? Because this is for you; you have to set your own Heaven and Hell right. Therefore, do not get caught up in this confusion, this mess, and this debate that they can call Gabriel for their help, they can call Azrael or Michael for their help. So call them, why should I go to sweep the house of the Master of the Universe (Mawla-e-Kainat)? Why should I go to cook food for Ali ibn Abi Talib? Why should I bring Janabe Zainab into my house? Why should I tell the women of my house that, 'Brother, take care of Janabe Zainab, this four-year-old girl is ours, a princess.' So, our test is how you helped the Ahlulbayt in this difficult time, in this hard and difficult time. The help you are providing to the Ahlulbayt here is not because the Ahlulbayt are needy, but so that you can provide proof of your faith in the Messenger of Allah through your love for the Ahlulbayt. That they had a connection with the Messenger of Allah. How much is my faith that I see, ignore, and walk away, and give no importance, or do I prioritize the needs of the Ahlulbayt over my own needs? What does this mean? When we perform all these things in the service of the Ahlulbayt—prayer, fasting, gifts, pilgrimage, supplication, vows—what are all these? Let us move towards the verse of the Quran. Brother, offer sacrifices. God has commanded in the Quran to slaughter animals. As we have commanded. Then what did He say? That your "lan yanala Allah"—in the court of the Lord of the Worlds—"lan yanala Allahu luhumuha wa la dima'uha"—the blood and meat of these animals do not reach God, "wa lakin yanalahu al-taqwa minkum"—your piety reaches God. O Lord, what need do You have for us to slaughter camels, cows, bulls, goats, sheep, rams, and lambs? You are so Merciful and Generous. God wants to know if you slaughter these animals and distribute them, feed people, and fill their stomachs or not? Do you follow the command of God or not? Therefore, remember that all the Infallible Imams (Aimma-e-Masumin) do not need us; we need them. Even if we feel that this need is Imam Hussain's, in reality, that need is ours. That is, in Karbala—I will go back to Karbala because, Alhamdulillah, our believers are mourners here, and the audience of the subcontinent can understand the matter very well through examples of mourning (Azadari). The incident of Abdullah ibn Afif al-Azdi is before you, that he said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, Mawla Hussain, take this sword of mine, it is a thousand-dirham sword. Take the horse, it is an excellent horse. Whenever I have fled on it, no one could catch me.' So, what did Imam Hussain say? 'Brother, keep your sword and your horse with you. If you can walk with us for support, then come.' Well, does the Mawla need helpers (Ansar)? Apparently, it seems the Mawla needs them. But in reality, this is the grace of Mawla Hussain upon that person, that we are inviting you to come with us so that you can attain those ranks of Paradise and, by saying "Assalamu alaykum ya ansara dinillah," your pilgrimage can be performed, and you can be buried near our feet. Mawla Hussain does not need anything. Now, I think the example has become clear. Now let us move towards the Imam of the Time (Imam-e-Zamana). There are two things. One is the soul of the Imam, and the other is the body of the Imam. We cannot harm the soul of the Imam. What does that mean? It means I cannot do something with the Imam that—na'udhubillah, may God protect us—would affect the soul of the Imam, and the Imam would forget something. Suppose the Imam forgets something from his mind. The Imam's senses are not in their place. I cannot do this with the soul of the Imam. But this can be done with the body of the Imam, as it was done. Wounds were inflicted on the body of the Imam. Deep wounds were inflicted, there was no strength to walk, there was the thirst of drought, Mawla Hussain was unable to walk. So, we want to prove that, O Lord of the Worlds, if You want to test us and You put the Imam of the time in some difficulty, it is not because—na'udhubillah—the Imam of the time has committed any sin. In Usul al-Kafi, Kitab al-Hujjah, there is a tradition that the sixth Imam said that the hardships that God gave to the Infallibles were not because they had committed any sin, not because they had made any mistake, or committed any disobedience, but because there are some ranks that God wanted to give them. Now, that is a long discussion about ranks, and I apologize again that the talk is getting long, but what can I do? Listen to this carefully. Therefore, O Lord of the Worlds, do not give any physical pain to the Imam of our time, so that the Imam of our time does not even have any physical pain. We are giving charity (Sadaqah) for him. Why should there be no physical pain? First thing, O Lord, do not test us by seeing the Imam's body in pain. That is, O Lord, may no physical pain reach the Imam. One is proof of love, and the other is what? The other is that we do not want to be tested in this regard. That is, this is the most difficult stage, that our Imam is suffering from any physical pain. We give charity for this reason. Okay? And this charity returns to us. Well, yesterday I gave the example of Salawat. The seventh Imam was asked, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the philosophy of Salawat? What is the meaning of Salawat?' So the seventh Imam said, 'The meaning of Salawat is that you are still adhering to the same covenant that you made on the Day of Alast.' "Alastu bi-rabbikum"—everyone said, "Bala." Am I not your Lord? Everyone said, "Yes, O Lord, You are our Lord." That is, now it is a strange thing. There, the oneness of God (Tawhid) was acknowledged on the Day of Alast. A request is being made to God to send blessings (Durood) upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. The seventh Imam is saying that this is the confirmation, verification, extension, and renewal of the covenant you made on that Day of Alast. Strange thing. That is, what does it mean? If you are committed to Tawhid, if you believe in Tawhid, then along with it, Muhammad and the family of Muhammad are not separate from Tawhid. This is one point. Well. Now, let me clarify one more thing from here. Can the Lord of the Worlds take the Imam away from among us or not? He can take him away. The Lord of the Worlds—can some cursed, some corrupt, some devil mislead him and he strikes the Imam with a sword, gives him poison? It is possible, absolutely possible. It has happened, there are incidents. All our Imams left the world like this. Listen to the hadith of the sixth Imam, which Sheikh Saduq narrated from the sixth Imam in "Ilal al-Sharai". What does the sixth Imam say in "Ilal al-Sharai", in the tradition of Sheikh Saduq, "Idha kariha Allahu tabaraka wa ta'ala li-qawmin naza'ana min bayni azhurihim"—when God Almighty finds our presence unpleasant for some people, and when God does not like that, O Jafar ibn Muhammad, O Muhammad al-Baqir, O Hussain ibn Ali, O Musa al-Kazim, O Ali al-Rida, I do not like that you stay among these people any longer. Now come to us. So God takes us away from there. That is, whether it is the Imam's martyrdom or his occultation, both can be the case. That when God does not like that Imam Hussain stays any longer among these wretches, among these unfortunate people who do not value Hussain ibn Ali, then God says, "Hussain, now come to us. We do not like that you stay with these people." The second meaning, when God sees the Hujjah (Imam Mahdi) that, 'O people, we gave you 12 Imams, you did not value them. Now, O Hujjah ibn al-Hasan, O Aba Saleh, O Mahdi of the End Times, now disappear from their sight. Now do not come within their reach. Except for "aw haliyyun min al-nas"—some rare individual, he will meet you, you will have permission for that, and you may meet him.' That is, what does it mean? That is, there are two things. When we give charity, we say, 'O Lord, protect the life of our Imam.' Why? Why protect our life, O Lord, why protect our Imam, O Lord? Because some of our Imams were martyred by the sword, some were martyred by poison. Why were they martyred? Because, O Lord, there were unfortunate and wretched people among whom our Imam was living, and You did not like it, You took them away. So, O Lord, we are giving charity so that no wretch, no unfortunate person, no cursed person can move towards our Imam with evil intentions. A question can arise here. Maulana, the Imam of the Time has to reappear, the Imam has to manifest. So then this is not like the other Imams who will be martyred. He has to live a long life and then after the reappearance, the government and the Raj'ah (return) and all the Imams have to return and war and all those things. So it is correct, if it were in the time of Imam Jafar al-Sadiq, we would have... Mawla, O Lord, remove every danger from the Imam, from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq. The Imam of the Time has no danger at all. Yes, see, this word, the matter that I talked about today, the Imam's body is in danger, the Imam's body is in danger. As the late Sheikh Abdul Hussain Amini used to say, give charity on the night of Ashura on behalf of the Imam of the Time, because the night of Ashura is a time of severe grief and pain for the Imam of the Time. When you give charity, your Imam's heart finds peace. When you recite Durood upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, Allahumma salli ala Muhammad-e-Aal-e-Muhammad, then the Imam's heart finds peace. What does it mean? That is, 'Mawla, we are with you. The message of Wilayah that your father gave, our heart, our soul is with you.' This thing gives peace to the Imam that those who believe in the Wilayah of my father Ali al-Murtaza are with me and my father's message has not gone to waste. If it had gone to waste, the Imam would have been sad, the Imam would have been regretful. We want to prove by doing all this grace that, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, O Aba Saleh, O Hujjah ibn al-Hasan, even at this time, in this era, there are some whose hearts are connected to your heart, who prioritize your physical pain over their own physical pain,' or suppose some worthless and incompetent people who, anyway, take out charity, there will be reward, our difficulties will be removed, and there are many such elderly people, such personalities who prioritize the Imam's pain over their own pain. So this is about connecting with the heart, that we prove our connection. One point, second answer. It is the Sunnah of the Imams that they have prayed for the physical health of the Imam of the Time. The prayer we recite, in the days of occultation, it is in Mafatih al-Jinan, this is after Ziyarat-e-Aal-e-Yasin, go and see it. Where does it start? 'Allahumma idfa' an waliyyika'—O Lord, remove from Your Wali, the Imam of the Time, what? Hardships, troubles, difficulties, calamities, all kinds of sorrows, pains, and grief, and then this sentence, 'Allahumma ihfazhu min bayni yadayhi wa min khalfihi wa 'an yaminihi wa 'an shamalihi'—O Lord, protect the Imam of the Time from the right, left, front, back, may no one strike him, may no pain reach him from the front, from above, from below, protect the Imam. 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyika al-Hujjah ibn al-Hasan'—what do we recite? 'Salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi'—you remember this whole prayer. 'Qaidan wa hafiza'—there, O Lord, protect the Imam of the Time. That is, what does it mean? Let me clarify this now. O Lord, may no pain reach the Imam's heart. How can no pain reach? How does pain reach the Imam's heart? That is, na'udhubillah, if the Imam of the Time has two barley loaves today, will the Imam be worried that, 'Since when have I—astaghfirullah rabbi wa atubu—na'udhubillah—not had good food, I don't have velvet and silk bedding, I don't have a good ride?' Where is the Imam's pain? Pay close attention. What was our discussion? May evils be removed from the Imam. The Imam has no evil, no pain. If any injustice is done to any believer, to any follower of Wilayah, to any servant of God, then the Imam feels pain from this. If injustice stops to some extent because we give charity for the Imam. Giving charity for the Imam returns to us. One thing, second thing, even if injustice happens somewhere, may this not reach the Imam's heart as grief and pain. What is the example of this? The example of this is that there is an elderly mother, grandmother, maternal grandmother, father, elderly person in someone's house, and God forbid, God forbid, their hand is fractured, their health is bad, they had an accident, there is blood on the bandage, so what does he do? He says, 'Brother, put a sheet over this, grandmother is coming to see, maternal grandmother is coming, aunt is coming, the eldest uncle is coming, see that there is no bandage and blood, it will hurt their heart, and look, stay calm, don't let them see.' So we say, 'O Lord, remove every kind of pain, every kind of suffering from the heart of Hazrat-e-Hujjah through this charity,' and our prayer is that remove it in this way. I hope that to some extent this matter has become clear, I think, what is the philosophy of giving charity, and I will say one last thing that giving charity for Hazrat-e-Hujjah is exactly like that bank account that we sometimes deposit 10, 20, 50 rupees, and at the end of every month we have 10, 15, 20, 25 thousand rupees deposited in the account, and we keep doing this for years, and then suddenly when we need it, we go and see that 8-10 lakh rupees are deposited in that account. We have to get a child married, send children to university, some other difficulty arose, so it is as if by taking out charity for Hazrat-e-Hujjah, we are in a way making ourselves worthy in the court of Hazrat-e-Hujjah. What does it mean, making ourselves worthy? That is, 'Mawla, I was also there, I used to take out charity on your behalf, please remember me too.' That's it, there is no other talk beyond this. Okay? If this matter is clear, then let's move to today's topic, and from there I don't know that now we have to Bismillah, Bismillah. Okay. Now, the deputies we were talking about earlier, they were Uthman ibn Said, and I said that the incident of Janabe Uthman ibn Said is very strange and a very interesting incident. This is happening like this, okay, okay. When this started spinning, it means there is a problem, we have to stop. I said the incident is very interesting, go and see in the books how the Imam changed the name of Janabe Uthman ibn Said, and now it is the turn of Muhammad ibn Uthman, who is the son of Uthman ibn Said. That is a very strange thing, in one house, the father also became a deputy, and since when? Imam Ali Naqi, Imam Hasan Askari, and Imam-e-Zamana. The deputy and representative (Safir) of these three Imams. Well, one more thing, yesterday a question was asked, why do we call them deputy (Naib)? So I had answered it. We say this in Urdu, but look, the word that has come to us in the traditions in Arabic, the word 'Sufara' has come very much, Sufara, Safir. What is the meaning of 'Safeer'? A king sits in the center; what is a 'Safeer' to him in front of the people? A king is not a 'Safeer', and a king does not become a 'Safeer'. Therefore, keep this term 'Safeer' in your mind. Now, today we come to Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said. Regarding Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said, it is said that when a delegation from Yemen came to meet—with whom? To meet Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)—the Imam said, 'Wash-hadu alayya' (Bear witness for me), O people of Yemen, bear witness. Who is saying this? Imam al-Askari. 'Inna Uthman ibn Said wakeeli, wa Safeeri' (Indeed, Uthman ibn Said is my deputy, my Safeer), 'wa anna ibnahu Muhammad wakeelo ibni Mahdikum' (and his son Muhammad is the deputy of my son, your Mahdi, to you people). So, this matter was decided and made clear by Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) at that time, and he informed the delegation that came from Yemen. We do not know how many people were in this Yemeni delegation; surely they must have been the elite of the elite, because this was not announced publicly. Furthermore, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) gave a statement regarding Muhammad ibn Uthman and Uthman ibn Said, saying, 'Fasma' lahum wa ati'uhuma' (Listen to them and obey them), 'wa innahumassiqtan al-mamoonan' (and they are the most trustworthy and are completely safe and secure in every respect). Now, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said passed away in 304 or 305 Hijri, and he served as the Safeer or Naib (deputy) for approximately 40 years. Who? Janab-e-Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said. Besides this, he also wrote a book on Fiqh called 'Kitab-ul-Ashriba', in which he discussed drinks and beverages—what is permissible and what is not. This book was passed down until the last deputy, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samari, but after that, we do not find this book. It seems as though it was lost, or perhaps it is in some library; we do not know. Now, look, we believe—and I am saying this for our youth—that, 'Who was this Maulana?' He was the deputy of the Imam. Amazing. This is a very interesting matter; it means you have a connection with the Imam, and whatever you said reached the Imam. You had no problems at all with the Imam. Sir, the biggest problems were faced by these four Nawwab-e-Arba (the four deputies) and the four Safeers. The closer you are to Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.), the more problems will come into your life because your faith will increase accordingly. When faith increases, Ma'rifat (gnosis) increases, and responsibilities increase. You cannot see your neighbor—be it a Hindu, Sikh, Christian, or atheist—sleeping hungry. You cannot see a dog thirsty on the street because the specialty of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) is to help the creation of God, to provide for the needs of the creation of God. How could it be that if Uthman ibn Said or Muhammad ibn Uthman are close to Imam-e-Zamana, they would not help the creation of God? Therefore, when the chain of helping begins, if you want to understand help, go and ask the person working in the fire brigade station, ask a doctor, ask a policeman, ask people like taxi drivers; whenever a call comes, you have to go—the night is not yours, the day is not yours. So, we are talking about ordinary people—doctors, taxi drivers, people working at fire stations—we are talking about those who help people in specific aspects. Now, when we come to Hazrat-e-Hujjat, whose eyes are upon the entire universe, who is the trustee of the Lord's will, and then his closest person and companion... Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said or Husayn ibn Ruh, these people—if they were given all the authorities by Hazrat-e-Hujjat, it was not as if they were distributing sweets, giving whatever they wanted by the handful. Rather, it is written in the history of the narrations that they had dug a grave in their house, and every day they would descend into that grave to recite the Quran. There was a wooden board on which some verses were written, and he said, 'Keep this board on which the verses are written on top of my grave.' This is a very strange thing. See, descending into the grave—meaning they had the fear of God—but when a person descends into the grave, a greater state of fear of God is created, and one weeps more. The way he used to recite the Quran, and then two months before [his death], it intensified; he had dug his grave, and two months before, he would descend into it to worship and recite the Quran. Pay close attention. What I want to tell you is that you cannot have a connection with faith until you are concerned about your afterlife. What is the afterlife? It is another matter that at some point, the hand of the Imam's power might reach a person drowned in sin and vice, and lift him to the heavens. That is a different matter; someone might become Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi, someone might become Zuhayr ibn Qayn—this is a different thing. We are not talking about exceptional cases, but the routine, the process, and the procedure—look at how pious these people were that the Imam is guaranteeing their tongues, guaranteeing their actions. Until purity comes, until there is purity in the ears, until there is purity in the eyes and the tongue, until a person does not eat Halal sustenance, the problem cannot be solved. Let me tell you a small incident. I went to a place—a city in Pakistan, I might even name it here—Bahawalpur, a city in our Southern Punjab. It is a small city, not a big one, but a very clean, beautiful, and lovely city. We went to an Imambargah, and the characteristics told about that Imambargah were surprising. They said that great Zakirs come here and request, 'Let us recite for ten minutes, five minutes,' and there is such weeping and lamentation here, and a strange atmosphere is created. This is very strange, that great Zakirs who wouldn't even look at anyone—there are good Zakirs, and there are Zakirs who are very arrogant—anyway, may God guide us all. They must have their own justification for it, I don't know, but the organizers of the Majlis say this. I asked, and they said, 'Maulana, we collected money, and the person who runs this Imambargah has a small shop.' So what happened? When the money was collected, it was Halal money, and a scholar ordered us to pay Khums on this money. Khums was paid, and then the Imambargah was built with that money. So, see, when the Imam's right is paid in everything—in your home, in your wealth, in your earnings, in your worship, the rights regarding your wife, the rights regarding your children, the rights of parents—when everyone is given their due right, only then does a person come into the 'good book' of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) in today's terminology. Although we are all, Insha'Allah, in the Imam's good book because we mourn his suffering, believe in his Wilayah, and hate his enemies, but how does one get that extraordinary, uncommon status? By descending into the grave to pray, reciting the Quran, Tahajjud, staying awake at night, Halal earnings, and all the limbs and senses—the five senses—all are pure. Until the five senses are pure, this soul, this spirit of yours, cannot be pure. It is impossible that I look at things that displease the Imam and my heart becomes a pure and clean soul. It is impossible that I listen to things or my tongue utters things that the Imam has forbidden—which makes the Imam angry, furious, and wrathful—and then I say, 'Husayn ibn Ruh, these people were amazing.' And how were they? Was it easy for them? Did they just say, 'Maula, solve this,' and it was solved? No. There is no such system. They were obedient to the Imam's command, and if they reached that level, they reached it through obedience. There is no condition of a turban here. Believe me, you gentlemen, Maulana, you are like this, and Masha'Allah, you have a turban and are a scholar, but this turban has no status. The real thing is whether you are at the stage the Imam demanded of you or not. It is not mentioned in any narration that those wearing turbans will go straight to Paradise. It is mentioned in the narrations that whoever spreads our knowledge, whoever speaks our words, whoever performs the obligatory duties, whoever avoids the forbidden, whose character is such—he will have the right to intercession. Therefore, these are all worldly titles. This turban, this cloak, this robe, and 'he is a Zakir', and 'he is this', and the Sherwani and the cap—what is the real truth? Wilayah, Tawalli, and Tabarri, and after that, the obligatory duties and the forbidden things, and beyond that, the journey continues toward the character of the Ahlulbayt. When a guest comes to your house, what do you do? If someone is sick, do you go to visit them or not? How do you walk on the street? How do you talk? To what extent does your tongue utter inappropriate words? You know all these things. Therefore, what is the lesson from the lives of these Nawwab-e-Arba, the four ambassadors, the Safeers of the Imam? Achieve purity so that you may be connected to them. I am not talking about people like them; that office is finished, it is over. Therefore, when the Imam said afterwards, 'What are you doing, Qibla?' He had dug a grave and started reciting the Quran excessively. Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said said, 'Qad umirtu an ajma'a amri famā taba'da shay'un' (I have been commanded to wrap up my affairs, for nothing remains). He lived for two months after saying this. Meaning, the Imam is telling us, 'Look, wrap up your affairs.' What does this mean? It means, 'Stop paying Khums now.' Whatever Khums was there, send it to its place, make all the wills, fulfill the work of people that is your responsibility, set it aside, line up things, clear them, do all this. Meaning, the Imam is telling his most special, special, special person—his ambassador, his Safeer—to wrap up his affairs. So, how can it be that we don't know about our Qada (missed) prayers, don't know about our Qada fasts, and it's just going on like this? It cannot be like this. It cannot be like this, according to what I know and the narrations. Otherwise, if we talk about the power of Hazrat-e-Hujjat, then as the poet said: 'If Pharaoh were to hold the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib with both hands, Moses son of Imran would rise from the grave with two palms.' If that is the sequence, I am not talking about that; I am talking about what we have been taught and commanded. Therefore, such was Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Said, and he passed away in 304 or 305 Hijri. Now I don't know how much time we have. 10:10, okay, fine. Before that, whatever. Okay. Now we come to whom? The third Safeer, the third ambassador of the Imam. Who was he? Husayn ibn Ruh ibn Abi Bahr al-Nawbakhti. His Kuniyat was Abul Qasim, and he is very famous; the 'Areeza' (petition) we write, we write it to him. Now, regarding him, it is a very strange matter that when Muhammad ibn Uthman—we are talking about whom? The third Safeer, the third deputy, or the third helper, the third special deputy of the Maula. Husayn ibn Ruh ibn Abi Bahr al-Nawbakhti. In his case, an incident is found that a person brought 400 Dinars, 400 gold coins, in whose time? In the time of Muhammad ibn Uthman. Who is Husayn? Whose name is Husayn? Abul Qasim is Husayn, the third Safeer. The third Safeer had not yet become the Safeer; it was the time of the second Safeer, meaning Muhammad ibn Uthman. A person brought 400 Dinars. When he brought 400 Dinars, it was the time of the second Safeer, Muhammad ibn Uthman. He said, 'Go and give this to Husayn ibn Ruh.' Okay? And he made him a deputy, saying, 'Give it to him.' Meaning, the signal was received beforehand. A slight hint—well, he wasn't told on what basis, he just said, 'Go and give it to him.' And when it was asked, 'Why are you giving this to him? You are the deputy, has the deputyship changed?' It's a question, right? 'Qibla, you are the deputy, Janab Muhammad ibn Uthman, you are the deputy and you are the Safeer of Hazrat-e-Hujjat, so why are you sending money to Husayn ibn Ruh?' He said, 'I am sending this based on the command of the Hazrat.' So, this is one thing you should pay attention to. Now, after that, a big issue is that when—it is a strange thing, let me tell you here—that Janab Husayn ibn Ruh, who had all the protocols and all the occasions, the anniversaries—you understand, it happens in any country that on January 25th or August 14th or August 15th, there are big occasions in the country where the army is coming, the army is parading, a guard of honor is being given, delegations, in the presidency—these happen everywhere. So, in the same way, on the occasions that used to happen, Janab Husayn ibn Ruh was not such a prominent personality. But despite that, he became the third Safeer. Everyone thought that Ja'far ibn Ahmad would become this, or Janab Ahmad, who was the father of Janab Ja'far. But Husayn ibn Ruh was made the one. Well, this itself is a matter of discussion—how did the change happen so suddenly? The change happened for us, otherwise, the Imam knew. A very strange incident happened when Janab Muhammad... Ibn Uthman, meaning the second Safir (deputy). The time of his passing approached, and he was in the state of death throes (sakarat). Janab Husayn ibn Ruh, who is the third Safir, was standing at the foot of the bed, and Janab Jafar ibn Ahmad was standing at the head of the bed. Whose? Muhammad ibn Uthman's. To clarify, the second Safir of the Mawla is breathing his last, passing away, in the state of sakarat. Janab Jafar ibn Ahmad is standing at the head, and who is standing at the feet? Husayn ibn Ruh. He opened his eyes once; Janab Muhammad ibn Uthman regained consciousness. Look at this; Janab Muhammad ibn Uthman is a humble servant of the Messenger of Allah and the Imam of the Time. Right? His state is such that even before death, his senses are fully intact. So, tell me, regarding those who accuse the Messenger of Allah—na'udhu billahi min dhalik (we seek refuge in Allah from that)—of delirium, what should be said about them? May the Almighty Lord truly curse those who level such false accusations against the Messenger of Allah. So, he opened his eyes once, Husayn ibn Ruh, he regained consciousness. What happened? It is not specifically described in the narration, but I am saying he opened his eyes. He said, 'Look, after me,' he stated the sentence, 'wa-safiru baynakum wa-bayna sahib al-amr' (and the deputy between you and the Master of the Command) is who? Muhammad ibn Uthman opened his eyes and said to Janab Jafar ibn Ahmad, 'After today, after me, the deputy between you and your Imam will be Husayn ibn Ruh.' Pay close attention. Meaning, all his life, people kept thinking that Jafar ibn Ahmad would become the third deputy and the third Safir. But the second deputy, Muhammad ibn Uthman, announced this decision at the time of his death: that after me, the one who will be the Safir between you and your Imam, the Imam's deputy, will be Husayn ibn Ruh. As soon as Jafar ibn Ahmad heard this—Husayn ibn Ruh was standing at the head, Muhammad ibn Uthman was at the head—he left the head of the bed, came to the foot, and gestured to Husayn ibn Ruh to come to the head. This is submission (ta'abbud). A whole lifetime—my knowledge of jurisprudence, principles, theology, philosophy, the hadiths of the Ahlulbayt, exegesis, discipleship—I have been with you for 30-40 years, and all these things... if I were to present the example of an ordinary person like me, na'udhu billahi min dhalik, one would get angry, one would feel hurt. We did all this work our whole lives, studying and working, from Baghdad to Basra, Basra to Kufa, here and there, the rights of the Shia, Zakat, Khums, feeding people, Majlis, mourning, Azadari—and in the final moments, he is dismissed? What was special about them? Look at the submission. He didn't even say, 'Yes, okay, Qibla, you said it, we will accept it.' Instead, he said, 'No, my place is not at the head.' Whose head is this? This is not the head of the Imam of the Time; this is the head of Muhammad ibn Uthman, a servant of the Imam. He said, 'No, my place...' he proved it with his actions. 'My place is not at the head; I will come to the blessed feet.' And Janab Jafar ibn Ahmad moved away from Muhammad ibn Uthman's head, moved away from the head, came to the foot, and said to Janab Husayn ibn Ruh, 'You come to the head.' Meaning, when the second Safir is leaving the world, the third Safir should stand at his head. And he said this sentence: 'wa-safiru baynakum wa-bayna sahib al-amr' (and the deputy between you and the Master of the Command). Look, Husayn ibn Ruh is the deputy between the Master of the Command and you after me. 'Farji'u ilayhi fi amri umurikum' (Therefore, refer to him in all your affairs). I command you to refer to him; whenever anyone comes, go to him for all your matters. And he said, 'Wa-'awwilu 'alayhi fi muhimmatikum' (And rely on him in your most important matters). Pay close attention. There are two things: 'umurikum' and 'muhimmatikum'. What are 'umur'? Any matter that arises—should I write an Istikhara, should I marry my daughter or not, should I buy a house there or not, a problem of prayer, a problem of fasting, if you don't understand a verse of the Quran, then what should you do? Come to Husayn ibn Ruh. Who is saying this? The second Safir about the third Safir. That is one thing. 'Farji'u ilayhi fi amri umurikum wa-'awwilu 'alayhi fi muhimmatikum'. 'Awwilu' means 'ta'wil', reliance. Meaning, lean on him, trust him, put your burden on him. We lean on a wall, we lean on a cushion, we use a cushion, there is a seat, we sit on it comfortably. 'Muhimmatikum' means your most important, most critical, and most dangerous matters—in those, what should you do? Don't just ask him; 'awwilu 'alayhi'—this is your place of reliance, trust him. In important matters, act according to what he says. It's not just 'act,' it's 'this is your place of reliance, you trust him.' It is not just that; just as we trust the Imam, the command is being given: trust Husayn ibn Ruh. There is always a point here. Now, let me say one thing here, which is that, look, this is perhaps the reason why in our petitions (ariza) we mention his name, 'wa-'awwilu 'alayhi fi muhimmatikum'. Now, look, this is a very strange method. Husayn ibn Ruh was made a deputy, a Safir, while he was not famous. He was among the special companions, in a circle; it's not that, na'udhu billahi, until yesterday he didn't know Wilayah or anything, and now he was suddenly brought in—no, that's not it. He was among the believers, among the people of faith, and among the companions, from that group. But I said that for Jafar ibn Ahmad, it was considered possible that he would become the third Safir. Who became it? Husayn ibn Ruh. What is the reason for this? The reason is that the Imam saw the sincerity; the Imam saw that the level required is within Husayn ibn Ruh. So, what should we do now? Should we draw a line through everyone else? Should we say, 'Discard this completely, the rest were all useless people'? No, that gaze of the Imam, which sees with precision, that gaze is so high. Let me use a sentence: in some places, precision is detected by a computer, not by the naked eye. For me, this color is red, and that is also red, but the computer says, 'Sir, in this shade of red and that shade of red, there are 150 more shades of red.' So, we don't have the right; we have the right to follow according to our eyes, as far as the proof (hujjah) is needed for us, but the Imam appointed them. Now, here is the same point: we say, 'Sir, these are the special deputies, and today these Maraji'—what is the difference between these four and these Maraji'?' As mentioned yesterday, these were special, they were by the Imam's command, but the Maraji' we have today are based on your discretion. You have to distinguish, you have to identify, you have to go and investigate, you have to go and search who is better, who is the most learned—if this word is correct to say—meaning, the most learned hidden within, who has the most knowledge? Your Marja-e-Taqlid depends on your discretion. If I find it correct, if his justice seems correct, if his knowledge, his piety seems correct, and I see all those conditions and credentials in my Marja-e-Taqlid, then I will consider him my Marja-e-Taqlid; if I don't see them, I won't. There are very great Maraji-e-Taqlid, sir, in Qom, Najaf, Mashhad, Karbala. Sir, for me, this person is not just; for me, his jurisprudence does not meet the complete conditions; in my view, this person is not a Mujtahid. You can try your hardest; the Imam has given me this system that in the Major Occultation, after these four deputies, after these four Safirs, we will not appoint; we will tell the conditions, but choosing, selection, election is your job. Therefore, there is a difference as vast as the earth and the sky. These four personalities were appointed by the Imam. If I say, 'I don't like Husayn ibn Ruh, I used to live in his neighborhood, he used to do this, he didn't come out for congregational prayer, and I saw that he used to pray like this, like that'—Sir, keep your intellect aside; you don't have the right to make even a tiny decision about Husayn ibn Ruh once he has been appointed by the Hujjah. But my Marja-e-Taqlid is someone else, my friend's Marja-e-Taqlid is someone else; his fatwas have no status for me, and my Marja-e-fatwa has no status for him. And every person should look to their own Marja' in every jurisprudential issue. In the Major Occultation, it is against the foundation and the basis of the creed of Shi'ism to say that any one Marja-e-Taqlid is the best, the most correct. Here, look at any Marja-e-Taqlid; wherever your Marja-e-Taqlid is, whoever it is, the first condition he writes is the initial condition: that in your view, he must be just, in your view, he must have jurisprudence. Therefore, any Marja' of today—we respect all our Maraji', our leaders, we kiss their hands, and we will not tolerate any insult towards them, all our scholars, Maraji', Fuqaha, Muhaddithin, we absolutely respect them. But if someone says that these are the same [as the four deputies], where from? Show me a document from the Hujjah, show me a letter from the Hujjah, show me any statement of the Hujjah, then we will accept it. And we will not accept this, because after Ali ibn Muhammad, the fourth Safir, the Imam said, 'After this, whoever claims deputyship,' it is in that letter, 'deny him, and he is a liar, he is slandering, he is fabricating, he is saying something wrong.' Therefore, the special deputyship and special embassy that the Imam appointed—what does it mean? My young sons and daughters, listen carefully, meaning these four personalities... ...I do not have the right to make a decision about. Just like Malik al-Ashtar, whom the Mawla of the Universe sent. We don't like Malik. You have no right to say that. Because Ali ibn Abi Talib sent him, so in the same way, the Hujjah sent these four to you. Therefore, bringing today's Maraji-e-Taqlid, whether it is Sheikh Tusi, Sheikh Mufid, Sayyid al-Isfahani, Agha Hakim, Agha Borujerdi, anyone, to the level of these four deputies is a violation of the creed of Shi'ism. Therefore, this was their specialty. But respect all Maraji'. Do not speak ill of any Mujtahid. Every Mujtahid gives his own fatwa. Whether you like his fatwa or not. My talk has reached this point, and I think we have time. Akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin wa sallallahu ala sayyidina Muhammadin wa ali baytihit tayyibina wa tahirin. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. The questions have reached you, Maulana Sahib. Okay. Look, Nusrat, it is asked that 'wa ja'alna min ansarihi wa a'wanihi'. What is the meaning of Nusrat? It also means to help. What is the meaning of 'Awn'? It also means to help. So what is the difference between the two? Perhaps the difference between these two can be stated—I am saying 'perhaps'—that for Nusrat, you do not need to be physically present. Apologies, for Nusrat, you should do all those things that can help someone. But 'Awn' means that you come along with him. Meaning, in 'Awn', when it is said 'a'wanihi', physical presence, physical attachment might be required. And for Nusrat, physical attachment is not required. Meaning what? Meaning we are currently doing Nusrat of the Imam of the Time if we help in his work. But we are not his 'Awn', his helpers. Right? Therefore, when will we be 'Awn'? When the Hujjah reappears and we work according to his command. What is coming to my mind right now, and I have no doubt about it—if I am wrong, then any friend can provide me a reference where something to the contrary is written—but what is in my mind is that for Nusrat, your physical attachment is not necessary. But for 'Awn', your physical attachment, physical presence, your apparent existence must be there. Right? And... Okay. And there is another question in this: the question is, can we become the Ansar and A'wan of the Imam of the Time before the reappearance while we are involved in our worldly activities and engaged in our personal lives? Absolutely, we can. This is a wrong concept that I want to remove, eliminate, and discard: that when a believer wakes up in the morning, if he is working in a field in UP, Sindh, Punjab, Bihar, or Bengal, using a shovel, he is helping the Imam if he is doing it with the intention of Halal sustenance. Therefore, the work we do in worldly life and separating the Imam from it is impossible for a believer. We have a narration in Bihar al-Anwar: 'Man ishtara mithqalan min al-lahm' (Whoever buys a mithqal of meat for his family), 'fa-ka'annama a'taq nasamatan min waladi Isma'il' (it is as if he bought and freed a person from the progeny of Ishmael). On Friday, take fruits and flowers for your wife and children when you return after praying, so that the children wait for Friday. Feed them good food on Friday. Maulana, Friday is for seeking help from the Imam of the Time, recite Ziyarat-e-Ale-Yasin. The same Imam has commanded that children should look forward to Friday. So, when we are drowning in our worldly life, if we are drowning in terms of sin and transgression, then we are moving away from the Imam. But if we are going because, Maulana, 'Yabna Rasulullah', so that our hands are not stretched out, our family is not embarrassed, our house is big, relatives can come and stay comfortably, we can hold Majlis, we have more money so that we can feed the hungry, we can help the believers—then, sir, this matter might not be digestible to many, but I am saying if you become so busy helping the believers that you cannot pray Namaz-e-Shab on time and have to pray it as Qada, then do this work. You should perform Namaz-e-Shab even if you have to do it as Qaza, but do not abandon it. The responsibility of fulfilling the needs of the Momineen is immense. Regarding Ghaibat (Occultation), this is a very good question that has come up. How can you be connected to the Imam during the Ghaibat-e-Kubra? One way is through Wajibats (obligatory acts), Muharramat (prohibited acts), and supplications. If someone wants an easy method—if I don't have the courage to open Mafatih (al-Jinan) or the courage to recite the Quran—then I will tell them a concise prescription. It is based on traditions. If someone asks, I can present not just one, but ten traditions before them. If you don't have the courage to open Mafatih, that's fine; keep reciting Salawat in abundance. If you have the courage to recite Salawat, gift it to the Imam. 'Qadwalna Inna Sallallahu'. The second task is to dedicate your life to the Momineen. Help with food, shelter, clothing, health, and support for orphan children; you will receive more reward than someone who reads Mafatih-ul-Jinan. Do not doubt this. Helping the hearts of those who have the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Sahib-e-Wila, those in whose hearts the love of the Panjtan resides, is a very great reward. So, this is how we can do this work. We can be included among the Ansar (helpers) of the Imam, no matter what work we are doing. It is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) to engage in trade. It is the Sunnah of Imam Baqir (a.s.), Imam Hasan (a.s.), Imam Hussain (a.s.), Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.), and Imam Musa-e-Kazim (a.s.) to engage in farming, planting gardens, planting date palms, and grapevines; this is the Sunnah. Why is it a Sunnah? So that my hand does not need to be stretched out before anyone. So that I have money, I can help the Momineen, and I can solve their problems. Regarding some special Tawqi'at (signed letters) that came through the first Naib (deputy). Look, there are some special Tawqi'at written that came through the first Naib. There is a significant number of them that we find, which were answers to questions asked through them. All of this is in my mind right now, but go and look in the A'mal of Rajab in Mafatih. The supplications in the A'mal of Rajab, 'Allahumma ya dhal-minani as-sabigha wal-ala'il wazi'a war-rahmatil wasi'a wal-qudratil jami'a wan-ni'matil jasima'—wherever this supplication is, look there; it was issued through Hussain ibn Ruh. And look in the A'mal of Shaban, there too, supplications came through Janab-e-Hussain ibn Ruh from Hazrat-e-Hujjat (a.s.). Regarding the term 'Naib-e-Aam' (General Deputy) used for the jurists—has the term 'Naib-e-Aam' appeared in the Hadith? I am relying on my memory right now, and it does not come to my mind that the term 'Naib-e-Aam' has appeared in the Hadith in this way. No, it is not in my mind. But if it hasn't appeared, it doesn't matter, because we are not focusing on the word. If the Imam has given the Faqih (jurist) the authority that you can issue a divorce, you can take care of the property of orphans, you look after widows, it is your responsibility, you take care of the person who has become insane and has money, you collect Khums, you distribute Zakat in this way—this can happen with the permission of the Faqih. Regarding judges, decisions of lawsuits, and Hudud (penalties), the Faqih will implement them, so this falls under the 'Ni'mat-e-Aam' (General Authority). The word might not have appeared, but the function has appeared, which is what we denote when we use the term 'Ni'mat-e-Aam' and refer to that reality, that jurisdiction, and authority. It is the same as what has come in the traditions. The word hasn't appeared, but the tasks that a Faqih can perform have appeared in the traditions. Is my point clear? Is it clear up to here? Yes, yes, Maulana Sahib. Maulana Sahib, this last question—the Hadith presented for the legitimacy of Taqlid, the Hadith 'Fa-innahu Hujjati Alaykum' (for he is my proof upon you), can this be applied to this? To what can it be applied? The question is about the 'Naib-e-Aam'. Yes, yes, yes, absolutely, absolutely, Marhaba. Yes, it can be applied to that. Absolutely. Regarding the traditions we have about Qaza (judiciary), that when one of our Faqihs who possesses the knowledge of our Fiqh gives a ruling, then accept his ruling. It is as if we have given the ruling. And when our narrators, who are trustworthy (Muwathaq), present a tradition, it is not befitting for you, you should not doubt it, and you should not impose your own opinions according to our words. Follow what our trustworthy ones have told you. So, all these things can be derived from it. Alhamdulillah. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. Jazakumullah. We apologize to the viewers that there was a slight delay in starting today. But Alhamdulillah, the topic was, in any case, a bit short on time for Maulana Sahib because, in reality, this topic is so vast in itself that justice could not be done to it in two sessions. Nevertheless, it is also our shortcoming that we forced you to discuss this topic in only two sessions. Thank you very much, it was very good that two sessions remained. Obviously, the talk happened, the Imam's name was mentioned, and if I have two more minutes, I will speak for two more minutes. Bismillah, Bismillah, yes, yes, Maulana Sahib. Look, one painful matter is that our poets are involved in this—the poets of Ahlulbayt, the Maddahs, the Qasida reciters, the Noha reciters—that in the subcontinent, all the dervishes, Sufis, and elders who are buried, we respect them, and we do not insult them at all; we remember them with good names, as they were lovers of the Ahlulbayt and they served and spread Islam. But look, no matter how many electric bulbs are lit in your house, they cannot equal the sun. Therefore, no elder can be equal to the dust of the feet of Hazrat-e-Hujjat ibn al-Hasan (a.s.). Therefore, I cannot make a request to all my Noha reciters because I am not addressing them, but I am addressing my listeners, the 30, 40, 50 people—that the evening of such-and-such Sufi elder is being celebrated, Qasidas are being recited in the evening of such-and-such, in the gathering of 3rd Shaban, in the gathering of 15th Shaban, Qasidas after Qasidas are being recited in their names. They were Sufi elders, lovers of Ahlulbayt, they are on our heads and eyes. And if it is not being said, how many people know about Fazl ibn Shadhan? How many people know about Ali ibn Mahziyar? Or who knows about Ali ibn Yaqtin? Or who knows about Ibn Ammar al-Sababi? Or similarly, say Muhammad ibn Uthman, Uthman ibn Sa'id, who knows about them? I mean, those people about whom we have 'Nass' (explicit text), we don't even mention them. Who knows about Sheikh-e-Mufid? Take Bilal-e-Habashi. Who knows about the companions of the Imams? How much have we discussed them? So all these come. Hazrat-e-Hujjat does not like it, he gets angry, Hazrat-e-Hujjat's heart is hurt that you take the names of random people. No matter how much respect they have, I said, even if a 100-watt, 1000-watt bulb is lit in my house, it cannot be equal to the sun. So we should revive these personalities, revive their names, and discuss them, and tell the scholars. And this talk that has entered into the religions, Qasidas, and Nohas—someone is talking about Pakistan, someone about India, someone about this, someone about that, some Sufi elder, some dervish—all are respectable in their place, but Hazrat-e-Hujjat, the Sahib-e-Asr-e-waz-Zaman, and his special deputies, they have their own status. They should be revived. Fazl ibn Shadhan, Ali ibn Mahziyar, all these, Ali ibn Yaqtin, the names of these companions should be alive among us, and we should know who these people were. So this is the right of Hazrat-e-Hujjat, and Hazrat-e-Hujjat can be angry with us if we show more negligence than this. Thank you very much, Maulana Sahib. This is truly a tragedy today, in a way, that those who are deserving of being mentioned, it is a matter of regret that they are not being discussed much in our society today. For example, you mentioned Fazl ibn Shadhan, about whom, as you yourself said, the 'Nass' exists that the Imam says, 'I envy the people of Khorasan because individuals like Fazl ibn Shadhan are present among them.' Maulana Sahib, thank you very much for being with us. I truly have no words to thank you. No, no, of course, of course. We request all the viewers to recite a loud Salawat for the health and safety of Maulana Sahib. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. And finally, while seeking permission from you all, since Maulana Sahib had already mentioned the poets and the talk of 'Nusrat' (help) also came up in the conversation, so please listen to a few lines by Mir Takallum Sahib: 'We will never let the city of the heart become Kufa.' 'We will never let the city of the heart become Kufa. O son of Zahra, we will not let you be alone. We write letters and call you, but it is a promise, we will not let what has happened happen again. And now, may the Lord take away the Mukassir (the one who diminishes the status) and the Nusayri (the extremist). Now, may the Lord take away the Mukassir and the Nusayri. We will never let them become the 313.' One small request of mine is that for the health and safety you prayed for me at the end, thank you very much. But I think we should recite 'Allahumma kun li-waliyyika', you remember Hazrat-e-Hujjat, with his noble name, we end with that. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasani, salawatuka alayhi wa ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'atin, waliyyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'aynan, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum. Jazakumullah Khair. Thank you, Maulana Sahib, thank you very much. Iltimas-e-Dua (request for prayers), remember us in your prayers. You also remember, absolutely, absolutely. Request for prayers from all viewers, tomorrow InshaAllah we will meet again at 10:30 PM India time. Wa akhiru da'wana anil hamdulillahi rabbil alamin. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad wa ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in.

True followers must exhibit complete submission to the Imam's decisions, prioritizing spiritual preparation and awareness of the afterlife.
