chapters.title: Review of the Four Deputies
chapters.summary: A summary of the previous session regarding the role of the Four Deputies during the Minor Occultation, specifically focusing on the transition from Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Umari to his son Muhammad.

chapters.title: The Philosophy of Serving the Ahlulbayt
chapters.summary: An explanation of why believers perform acts of service, charity, and worship on behalf of the Imams, clarifying that it is for the believer's spiritual growth rather than the Imam's need.

chapters.title: The Nature of Need and Service to the Imam
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that the Imams do not need human assistance; rather, serving them is a grace that allows believers to attain spiritual ranks and proximity to the Ahlulbayt.

chapters.title: Physical Hardships and the Imam's Status
chapters.summary: Hardships faced by the Infallibles are not due to sins but are a means to elevate their spiritual status, and believers pray for the Imam's protection to avoid the pain of seeing him suffer.

chapters.title: Charity, Salawat, and the Covenant of Alast
chapters.summary: Giving charity for the Imam and reciting Salawat serves as a renewal of the primordial covenant of Tawhid and a way to demonstrate loyalty to the Imam during his occultation.

chapters.title: Occultation and Divine Protection
chapters.summary: The occultation is described as a divine response to a society that fails to value the Imam, and believers pray for his safety to ensure no harm reaches him from the wicked.

chapters.title: Philosophy of Charity for the Imam
chapters.summary: Giving charity for the Imam serves as a spiritual connection and a way to seek the Imam's protection and favor.

chapters.title: The Role of the Special Deputies
chapters.summary: The lecture introduces the concept of 'Safeer' (deputy) and discusses the appointment of Muhammad ibn Uthman by Imam al-Askari.

chapters.title: Responsibilities and Piety of the Deputies
chapters.summary: The deputies faced immense responsibilities and maintained deep piety, serving as models for those seeking a connection with the Imam.

chapters.title: Purity and Halal Sustenance
chapters.summary: Spiritual connection with the Imam requires personal purity, Halal earnings, and fulfilling the rights of others, including Khums.

chapters.title: Achieving Spiritual Purity and Obedience
chapters.summary: The speaker emphasizes that true status with the Imam is achieved through the purification of the senses, obedience to divine commands, and sincere character rather than external titles or religious attire.

chapters.title: Preparing for the End and the Third Deputy
chapters.summary: The lecture discusses the importance of settling worldly affairs and fulfilling obligations, as demonstrated by the second deputy, Muhammad ibn Uthman, before introducing the third deputy, Husayn ibn Ruh.

chapters.title: The Succession of Husayn ibn Ruh
chapters.summary: This section details the transition of the deputyship from Muhammad ibn Uthman to Husayn ibn Ruh, highlighting the divine selection process and the profound submission of those who were bypassed.

chapters.title: The Final Announcement and Exemplary Submission
chapters.summary: Muhammad ibn Uthman announces Husayn ibn Ruh as his successor during his final moments, prompting a remarkable display of humility and obedience from Jafar ibn Ahmad.

chapters.title: The Appointment of Husayn ibn Ruh
chapters.summary: The second special deputy, Muhammad ibn Uthman, officially designates Husayn ibn Ruh as his successor, instructing the community to rely on him for all religious and critical affairs.

chapters.title: Distinction Between Special Deputies and Maraji
chapters.summary: The speaker clarifies that the four special deputies were divinely appointed by the Imam, whereas modern-day Maraji are selected based on individual discretion and scholarly qualifications.

chapters.title: Defining Ansar and A'wan of the Imam
chapters.summary: The lecture explains the difference between 'Nusrat' (general assistance) and 'Awn' (physical support/companionship) and emphasizes that daily Halal work can contribute to the Imam's cause.

chapters.title: Connecting with the Imam during Ghaibat
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines practical ways to maintain a connection with Imam Mahdi (a.s.) through obligatory acts, reciting Salawat, and serving the Momineen.

chapters.title: Authority of the Faqih and General Deputies
chapters.summary: The discussion clarifies the role of the Faqih as a general deputy and the legitimacy of Taqlid based on traditions regarding the Imam's authority.

chapters.title: Prioritizing the Companions of the Imams
chapters.summary: The speaker urges the community to shift focus from local Sufi figures to the historical companions of the Imams who have explicit recognition in traditions.

title: Mega Winner Announcement | Special Episode | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2026 🎁🎉
excerpt: This special episode of the Panaah-e-Kainaat Mega Quiz 2026 focuses on the theological significance of recognizing the Twelfth Imam, exploring his various titles and the duties of believers during his occultation. The lecture emphasizes the necessity of spiritual preparation, the importance of specific supplications like Dua-e-Ahad, and the Imam's future role in establishing global justice. The session concludes with the announcement of the Mega Quiz winner, who is tasked with performing a pilgrimage on behalf of the community.
content:
TSR presents. O, O you desire hidden in the longing of my gaze. O, O comfort of my heart. O, comfort of my heart. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, then subscribe now and don't forget to click the bell icon. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and peace and blessings be upon the noblest of prophets and messengers, and upon his pure and purified family, and may the eternal curse be upon their enemies, their killers, those who usurped their rights, and those who denied their virtues and merits. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your Wali, the Hujjat ibn al-Hasan, may Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside in Your earth willingly and let him enjoy it for a long time. O Allah, make us among his helpers, his assistants, his Shias, his servants, and his followers, and do not make us among his enemies, by the right of Muhammad and his pure family. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The topic of today's discussion is the names and titles of Imam-e-Zamana, Hazrat-e-Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif). Well, names—names, meaning the plural of 'Ism' (name). The names and titles of the Imam. So when we talk about a name or a title, the question is, why is this important? The reason is that the first reason is that the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam is obligatory. Allama Majlisi (Rizwanullah Ta'ala Alayh) has brought an entire chapter on this topic in Bihar al-Anwar. If you just read the name of that chapter, you will get an idea of how important this is. In Bihar, Volume 23, page 76, and Chapter 4, Allama Majlisi narrates from it: 'Bab Wujub Ma'rifatil Imam' (The chapter on the obligation of recognizing the Imam). Meaning, it is obligatory to attain the recognition of the Imam. 'Wa annahu la yu'dharun-nasu bi tarkil wilayati' (And people will not be excused for abandoning the Wilayah). Meaning, there is no excuse acceptable before Allah regarding this. 'Wa man mata la ya'rifu imamahu aw shakka fihi mata mitatan jahiliyyatin wa kufrin wa nifaqin' (And whoever dies without recognizing his Imam, or doubts him, dies the death of Jahiliyyah, Kufr, and Nifaq). And whoever dies and has not recognized his Imam, has not affirmed the Imam, or has doubted the Imam, then he will die the death of Jahiliyyah (ignorance), Kufr (disbelief), and Nifaq (hypocrisy). And in this connection, Allama Majlisi has cited 40 hadiths. 40 hadiths, 40 traditions, 40 hadiths. Therefore, since it is Wajib (obligatory), the recognition (Ma'rifat) of the Imam is Wajib; it is Wajib to know the Imam. So, what is the way to know the Imam? The most fundamental thing, the very first thing in this regard, is that we can recognize the Imam through his names and his titles (Alqab). It is not within the capacity of an ordinary human, not within the capacity of an ordinary mortal, to understand the reality of the Imam or Imamate. This is our belief that it is beyond the capacity of an ordinary mortal because Allah has created them, their creation, in a different way, in a different manner. And their creation at the Noorani level, especially the level of their creation in the A'la Illiyyin, is beyond the understanding of an ordinary mortal. And this hadith of Imam Reza (a.s.) confirms this, which is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page number 198, hadith number 1. This narration is from Imam Reza (a.s.), where the Imam says: 'Hal ya'rifuna qadral Imamati wa mahallaha minal ummah?' Have they recognized the Imam, the Imamate? Have they known the value of Imamate? Or what is the status and position of Imamate in comparison to the Ummah? Do they know? 'Fayajuzu fiha ikhtiyaruhum'—that they have deemed it permissible for themselves to choose the Imam for themselves? Do they even understand what Imamate is? Do they even know what the reality of the Imam is? Who is the Imam? Then he says, 'Innal Imamata ajallu qadran wa a'zamu sha'nan wa a'la makanan wa amna'u janiban wa ab'adu ghauran'—meaning, the Imam says to consider this from five aspects. The Imam says that Imamate is more exalted in its value, more magnificent in its status, higher and superior in its position, more secure and protected in its aspect, and deeper in its depth than that people could reach it with their intellects. Or reach it through their opinions, or reach the Imam through their own theories, or appoint an Imam by their own choice, by their own selection. Therefore, when something is beyond human intellect, what is the way to it? The way is exactly the same as how a human cannot recognize Allah. It is impossible for a human to attain the Ma'rifat of Allah unless Allah introduces Himself, unless He provides His own introduction. When Allah provides His introduction, when He makes Himself known, then the human recognizes Allah. And the way Allah has kept for His recognition, what is it? Through His names. Through His Asma and Sifat (Names and Attributes). The narration is present in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page number 113, hadith number 2. The Imam says, 'Wa lakinna hu'—meaning, and Allah. What did Allah do? 'Ikhtara linafsihi asma'an.' Allah Himself chose names for Himself. Now look here, the sentence before this in the hadith was that Allah was not in need of designating names for Himself, of creating names. Meaning, creating names. But Allah chose names for Himself. 'Wa lakinna hu ikhtara linafsihi asma'an.' Why? 'Li ghayrihi.' For others. Allah did not do it for Himself, but for others—meaning for the creation, Allah chose these names. 'Yad'uhu biha'—so that they may call upon Him through them. The way to call upon Allah is the same Asma and Sifat that Allah has chosen for Himself. 'Li annahu iza lam yud'a bismihi lam yu'raf.' Because if Allah is not called upon by these names, if one does not pray using the names through which Allah has made Himself known or which Allah has chosen for Himself, then the Ma'rifat of Allah cannot be attained. If someone wants to attain the true Ma'rifat of Allah, the only way is this method of Asma and Sifat through which they call upon Allah. So, in the same way, if a person wants to attain the true Ma'rifat of the Imam, the way is that they should be aware of the Imam's Asma, Alqab (titles), and Kuniyat (agnomens)—what the Imam's Kuniyat is, what the Imam's Asma are, what the Imam's Alqab are. And even in the narrations, it is stated what their reasons (illat) are. Therefore, Allama Majlisi, may Allah be pleased with him, in Bihar al-Anwar, Volume 51, from page 28 to 31, brings a chapter: 'Bab Asma'ihi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif) wa Alqab'. And so on. Meaning their Asma, which is the plural of Ism (name). And their Alqab, which is the plural of Laqab (title). Meaning their titles. 'Wa Kunahu'—and their Kuniyat. Kuniyat means agnomens, for example, where it is attributed to their son, like the Imam's Kuniyat, Abul Qasim. Insha'Allah, we will see that. 'Wa illaha'—and what are the reasons for them? Why these names came, and what is the reason? So, let us present a few hadiths for your service so that the matter becomes clear. In this same chapter, hadith number four, which Allama Majlisi cites, he cites it from Kamaluddin. Kamaluddin is a book by Sheikh Saduq, and the full name of the book is 'Kamaluddin wa Tamam al-Ni'ma'. And this book, which Sheikh Saduq wrote, was written at the behest of Imam-e-Zamana (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif). Now, from that hadith, Allama Majlisi cites this narration. It is hadith number four of the same chapter that I just mentioned to you. The hadith is such that the narrator says: 'Sami'tu Aba Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Reza (a.s.) yaqul.' I heard Imam-e-Jawad (a.s.), meaning the ninth Imam, say: 'Innal Imama ba'di ibni Ali. After me, my son Ali will be the Imam. Amruhu amri. His command will be my command. Wa qawluhu qawli. And his word will be my word. Wa ta'atuhu ta'ati. And his obedience will be my obedience. Wal Imamatu ba'dahu fi ibnil Hasan.' And the Imamate after him will be in his son Hasan, meaning Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.). 'Amruhu amr-e-abihi'—and the command of Imam Hasan will be just as the command of his father Imam Ali Naqi (a.s.) was, it will be the same. 'Wa qawluhu qawl-e-abihi'—and his word, meaning Hasan's word, will be the word of his father Ali Naqi. 'Wa ta'atuhu ta'at-e-abihi'—and his obedience will be like the obedience of his father. Then he became silent. After saying this, Imam-e-Jawad (a.s.) became silent. So I said to him—the narrator says I said, the narrator's name is Saqr ibn Dulf. Saqr says I said: 'Ya Ibna Rasulillah, O son of the Messenger of Allah, famanil Imam ba'd al-Hasan?' Meaning, who is the Imam after Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)? Fabaqa (a.s.). Imam-e-Jawad (a.s.) began to weep. Fabaqa buka'an shadida. He began to weep intensely. Summa qala (a.s.), then the Imam said: 'Inna min ba'dil Hasan ibnahu.' After Hasan, it will be his son. And he took the specific name for which it is Mustahab—it is Mustahab, not Wajib—that when a person takes this name, they should stand facing the Qibla: 'Al-Qa'im bil-Haq'. Meaning, he who will rise with the truth. 'Al-Muntazar'. Meaning, he for whom people will wait. Now here, the Imam introduced two names. He introduced two names: one, Al-Qa'im bil-Haq, and the second, Al-Muntazar. Fa qultu lahu, I said—the narrator says I said: 'Ya Ibna Rasulillah, wa lima summiyal Qa'im?' Why is he called the Qa'im? What is the reason this name was given? Because this word 'Qa'im' is an attribute of all the Imams. It is not just for the twelfth Imam. But it has been used more specifically for him. So why was he given this name? Qala (a.s.), the Imam says: 'Li annahu yaqumu ba'da mawt-e-zikri.' Allahu Akbar. Because he will rise when his remembrance has died. 'Ba'da mawt-e-zikri.' When people have forgotten him. People will have erased him from their memories. No one will be attentive towards the Imam. 'Ba'da mawt-e-zikri.' 'Wa irtidad-e-aksaril qa'ilina bi-imamati.' And most of those individuals who claim that we believe in his Imamate will also deviate from this belief of theirs, will turn back, will become apostates. Meaning, most people will forget his remembrance, will become apostates from his Imamate. That is why the Imam is weeping. And that is why it is said he is 'Wahid' (lonely), and 'Tarid'. Tarid means one who is not welcomed by people. Rather, in Arabic, its literal meaning is one whose door is closed in his face. One who is told 'You are not welcome'. This is what Maula-e-Kainat (a.s.) has said. In the hadith of Maula-e-Kainat, Imam-e-Zamana is Tarid, Sharid, and Wahid. These are among the names of the Imams. People will forget to such an extent. This is a different matter that he is a generous Imam who says: 'Inna ghayru muhmilina li-mura'atikum wa la nasina li-zikrikum.' We do not neglect your care, and we do not forget your remembrance. 'Inna ghayru muhmilina li-mura'atikum.' We do not falter in your guardianship, in your protection, and we do not forget you. 'Wa la nasina li-zikrikum.' We do not forget your remembrance. But people will forget the Imam's remembrance, look. This is the difference between the Imam and others. The Imam says: 'We will not forget you. We will not falter in your guardianship, we will not falter in your protection.' If we had forgotten you, if we had faltered in your protection, then 'la-nazalat bikumul bala'u wa istalamatkumul a'da'—calamities would have broken upon you and the enemies would have uprooted you and thrown you away. But the Imam is a generous Imam. That is why the Imam does not forget, although we forget. And if those who do remember, when is their remembrance? For example, once a year, and sometimes just as a formality. Therefore, try to remember your Imam as much as possible, day and night. No day should pass that you do not remember your Imam. Be regular with Dua-e-Ahad, read Dua-e-Ahad yourself every morning after the morning prayer, and teach your children to memorize Dua-e-Ahad and explain its contents to them, explain its meanings to the children so that they understand what the meaning of this prayer is. Then the narrator asked: 'Fa qultu lahu wa lima summiyal Muntazar?' I then asked why the twelfth Imam is called the Muntazar? Qala (a.s.), Imam-e-Jawad (a.s.) replied: 'Li anna lahu ghaybatan.' Because for him there will be an occultation. 'Taqsiru ayyamuha.' Whose days will be very many. 'Wa yatulu amaduha'—and its duration will be long. “Fa yantaziru khurujahu al-mukhlisun.” So those who are the people of sincerity, the sincere individuals, will wait for his reappearance. They will wait for his reappearance. “Wa yankiruhu al-murtabun.” And the murtab—murtab is derived from rayb, meaning those who doubt will deny him. There is a difference between shakk (doubt) and rayb. Shakk is one aspect, but when the word rayb is used, like in the Quran, “La rayba feehi” (there is no doubt in it), rayb means accusation or suspicion. Rayb means to doubt, and it also means that a person might deny something. It has a vast meaning compared to shakk. Therefore, the Imam did not use the word shakk, but used rayb—al-murtabun. “Wa yastahzi’u bi-zikrihi al-jahidun.” Al-jahidun means the deniers. Those who deny will mock his remembrance. They will mock, saying, “How can someone be hidden for such a long time? How can someone have such a long lifespan?” “Wa yaksuru fihal waqqatun.” And what will happen in that era? The waqqatun will be many. Waqqatun means those who fix the time of the reappearance. Meaning, there are many individuals who say, “Yes, the reappearance will happen next year, so many signs have been fulfilled, the Imam will come now.” They fix the time. There is a strict prohibition against this in the traditions. “Kazaba al-waqqatun” (the time-fixers lie) is in the tradition. Those who fix the time are lying because Allah has not decreed the time of the reappearance. So, when Allah has not decreed it, how can a human fix the time? When Allah has not decreed it—because nowhere in any hadith is it said that Allah has decreed and fixed the time. And after that, he says, “Wa yahliku fihal musta’jilun.” And the musta’jilun—meaning those who are in a hurry, those who are impatient regarding the Imam’s affair, —they will perish in the reappearance. What does impatience mean? It means those who lack patience, who say, “Oh, the Imam hasn’t come, when will he come, we don’t know when it will happen, and so much oppression and tyranny have filled the world, so many people are being killed here, this is happening, that is happening, when will the Imam come?” These are the musta’jilun. Allah knows best when to manifest His proof. No one knows better than Allah. Allah knows when the time of reappearance is the best time. Therefore, the Imam says, “Yahliku fiha al-musta’jilun wa yanju fiha al-musallimun” (The impatient ones will perish in it, and the submissive ones will be saved). And only those who submit will find salvation in it. Only those who submit—meaning to submit before the command of Allah. Meaning to say, “O Lord! Pray, pray. O Lord! Hasten the reappearance of the Imam of the Time.” Pray, do it abundantly, day and night. “Akthiru al-du’a bi-ta’jil al-faraj fa-inna dhalika farajukum” (Increase your prayers for the hastening of the relief, for that is your relief). Do it as much as possible because your salvation and ease lie in it. Do it as much as possible. That is correct for oneself, but at the same time, we should not be among the jahidun (deniers), nor among the murtabun (those who doubt), nor should we be among the waqqatun (those who fix the time), nor should we be among the musta’jilun (those who are impatient), but rather we should act with patience and endurance. When Allah determines the appointed time, at that moment. We just have to prepare, to remain ready. When the Hazrat arrives, we should be ready at that time. This was hadith number four. In hadith number five, another name has been introduced. This hadith is from Ghaybat al-Shaykh al-Tusi. Ghaybat al-Shaykh al-Tusi is one of the ancient books written during the occultation. The most ancient book on the subject of occultation was by Fazl ibn Shadhan, “Isbat al-Ghaybah,” and after that is Ghaybat al-Nu’mani, whose author passed away in 336 AH, and Shaykh al-Tusi passed away in 430 AH. Thus, Ghaybat al-Shaykh al-Tusi is one of the ancient books. It is famous by the name “Al-Ghaybah.” Shaykh al-Tusi is its author. He narrates from Shaykh al-Kulayni, who is the writer of Al-Kafi. Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates that “Qala Abu Abdillah alayhis salam” (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) said) that “Hina wulida al-hujjah” (When the Hujjah was born), “Za’ama al-zalama annahum yaqtulunani li-yaqta’u hadha al-nasl” (The oppressors thought that they would kill me to cut off this lineage). But it is not so. “Fa kayfa ra’aw qudrata Allah” (And how they saw the power of Allah). Now, when the Hujjah is born, they will see what the power of Allah is. “Wa sammahu al-mu’ammal.” Now, by what name has the Imam been introduced here? “Al-Mu’ammal.” What does Mu’ammal mean? It is derived from amal (hope). Amal means hope, and Mu’ammal means the one in whom hope is placed. So, one of the names of the Imam is “Al-Mu’ammal,” the one in whom hope is placed. And that is why when we recite in Dua-e-Nudba, one of the names of the Imam of the Time is “Ayna al-mu’ammal li-ihya’ al-kitab wa hududihi” (Where is the one hoped for to revive the Book and its boundaries?). Where is the one who is hoped for, that when he arrives, he will revive the Book, meaning the Quran, and revive its boundaries? Because people will have forgotten the true Quran. People will have stopped acting upon the true Quran. People will not be paying attention to the Quran. The boundaries of the Quran will be mocked. The boundaries and laws within the Quran will all be mocked. The Quran itself will be mocked because the actions of the Muslims will be such that people will turn away from the Quran, people will defame the Quran. When the Imam of the Time (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance) arrives, he will revive the Quran again. “Li-ihya’ al-kitab” (To revive the Book). Ihya means to bring to life, to give life. This is a sentence from Dua-e-Nudba, and that is why one should make arrangements for Dua-e-Nudba every Friday morning after the morning prayer. In your mosque, in your Imambargah, in your area, in the local mosque, teach your children the dua, so they learn to recite Dua-e-Nudba, so they become familiar with the meanings of Dua-e-Nudba. Look, Dua-e-Nudba itself is a treasure of the recognition of the Imam. It is a treasure of the recognition of the Imam. Now, after that, hadith number six, which Allama Majlisi narrates, it is also from Ghaybat al-Shaykh al-Tusi, where the narrator says, “Qultu li-Abi Abdillah alayhis salam” (I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)) that “Al-Mahdi wa al-Qa’im wahid?” (Are the Mahdi and the Qa’im one and the same?). “Faqala alayhis salam na’am” (The Imam replied, “Yes”). “Faqultu li-ayyi shay’in summiya al-Mahdi” (I asked, “Why was he given the title of Mahdi?”). “Qala alayhis salam” (The Imam replied), “Li-annahu yuhda ila kulli amrin khafiyy” (Because he is guided to every hidden matter). Meaning all hidden, concealed matters will be manifest to the Imam. And that is why the Imam’s conduct will be that he will be “ma’mur bil-batin” (commanded by the inner/hidden). All other Imams, all the infallible ones, from the Messenger of Allah to the 11th Imam, were “ma’mur bil-zahir” (commanded by the outer/apparent). What does “ma’mur bil-zahir” mean? It means they were commanded to deal with people based on the apparent, not the inner. Meaning, the way of the world was such that the Messenger of Allah knew that this person sitting in front of me is a hypocrite. But when he spoke to him, he spoke in a normal way. Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) knew that this is my killer. But he gave him respite. And similarly, all the Imams were aware of the unseen. But when they dealt with people, they dealt with them in a normal way. But when the Imam of the Time (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance) reappears, he will be “ma’mur bil-batin.” Meaning, not based on the apparent; at that time, no hypocrite will be able to hide his hypocrisy. If someone goes before the Imam and tries to show that I am very pious and God-fearing and my faith is true, but in reality, there is crookedness in his heart, the Imam will deal with him according to his heart. Not according to his tongue. Therefore, “yuhda ila kulli amrin khafiyy” (he is guided to every hidden matter). And “wa summiya al-Qa’im” (and he is called the Qa’im) because of this—there are two reasons. The first reason has already passed in the previous hadith. Now, in this hadith, along with that reason, another reason is stated: “Li-annahu yaqumu bi-amrin ‘azim” (Because he will rise with a great affair). A great affair, and what is that affair? It will be a global government. There will be a government in the whole world, and he will fill the whole world with justice and fairness just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. There will be justice and fairness in every corner. Not even an atom’s worth of oppression will occur, even to an ant. That if an ant is carrying a grain in its mouth, no one will be able to snatch that grain from its mouth. Today, you know what the situation is. People, one country occupies another country, one man occupies another’s house, one land occupies another, and everyone oppresses everyone, kills anyone, everything. Then after that, in hadith number seven, Allama Majlisi narrates this hadith from Shaykh al-Mufid’s book “Al-Irshad.” Shaykh al-Mufid, who was the teacher of Shaykh al-Tusi and passed away in 413 AH, and was a student of Shaykh al-Saduq. So, Shaykh al-Mufid wrote the book “Kitab al-Irshad.” In it, he narrates the tradition that Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) says, “Idha qama al-Qa’im (may Allah hasten his noble reappearance), da’a al-nasa ila al-islami jadidan” (When the Qa’im rises, he will invite people to Islam anew). He will invite people to Islam again. When the Imam of the Time reappears, he will say to the Muslims, “Bring Islam.” He will say to the Muslims, “Bring Islam.” “Annata ila al-islami jadidan. Wa hadahum ila amrin qad dasara wa jalla ‘anhu al-jumhur.” And he will guide people to that affair which has been erased. People will have erased the command of Allah. The Imam will bring it back. And these are matters in which the majority—except for a few individuals—the majority will have been misguided from it. “Jalla ‘anhu al-jumhur” (The majority will have turned away from it). Jumhur means the majority. A large majority will have been misguided from it. “Wa innama summiya al-Qa’im Mahdiyan” (And he is called Mahdi because he will be guided to an affair from which people are misguided). Because he will be guided to that affair. Here is another reason why he is called Mahdi: that he will be guided to that affair from which most people will be misguided. Meaning, they will be misguided from true Islam. They will not be aware of true Islam. “Wa summiya al-Qa’im li-qiyamihi bil-haqq” (And he is called the Qa’im because his rising will be with the truth). Therefore, when the Imam arrives, he will introduce people to the Quran, the essence of the Quran—meaning the true teachings of the Quran and the true teachings of the religion and the Sunnah of the Messenger, the Sunnah which is the true Sunnah. And people will have to listen. It will not be like the times of other Imams, where people oppressed the Imams (a.s.), killed them, martyred them, and kept them in prisons. Instead, the circumstances will now be transformed and changed. Now, if someone does not listen, they will have no other option but to be under the dagger of the Imam of the Time, under the sword of the Imam of the Time. That is why in Dua-e-Nudba, we find: 'Ayna Muhyi Ma'alim-id-din wa ahlihi' (Where is the one who will revive the landmarks of religion and the people of religion?). The people of religion will be revived at that time. Even if they have died, they will be raised from their graves, as you recite in Dua-e-Ahad: 'Allahumma in hala bayni wa baynahumul mawt' (O Allah, if death stands between me and him), 'Alladhi ja'altahu 'ala 'ibadika hatman maqziya' (which You have decreed as an inevitable fate for Your servants), 'Fa-akhrijni min qabri mu'taziran kafani' (then bring me out of my grave, wearing my shroud), 'Shahiran sayfi mujarradan qanati' (with my sword drawn and my spear unsheathed). A bare sword, a bare spear. 'Mujarradan qanati, mulabbiyan da'watad-da'i fil-haziri wal-badi' (With my spear unsheathed, responding to the caller's invitation, whether present or in the desert). And when the Imam of the Time calls me, I will respond to his invitation, I will answer. Labbayk ya Sahib-az-Zaman, Labbayk. Labbayk ya Mahdi. Whether in the city or in the wilderness, anywhere. Therefore, a human being must always be ready and prepared. After that, there is another narration, let me finish quickly because time is running out. The narration says that 'Sammallahul Mahdiya al-Mansur' (Allah has named the Mahdi as al-Mansur). Look, here the Imam says that Allah named the Imam of the Time as 'al-Mansur'. This means that the names of the other Imams (a.s.) were also from Allah; Allah used to name them. 'Sammallahul Mahdiya al-Mansur'. And the Imam also gives a comparison, just as Allah named the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) Ahmad, Muhammad, and Mahmud, in the same way, Allah named the Imam of the Time as al-Mansur. And just as Allah named Isa (a.s.) as al-Masih. Why al-Mansur? Meaning the one who has been granted victory. The one whom Allah helps. He is al-Mansur, he will be helped. Allah will help him. He will grant him victory. That is why we recite in Dua-e-Nudba: 'Aynal-Mansuru 'ala man i'tada 'alayhi wa-iftara' (Where is the one who will be helped against those who transgressed against him and fabricated lies?). Allah will help him. Allah will grant him victory. Against whom? 'Man i'tada 'alayhi wa-iftara'. Those who cross the limits against the Imam of the Time, who transgress, commit sins, and rebel. Allah will help the Imam against them. 'Wa-iftara' (and those who) make accusations against the Imam, attributing false things to the Imam. And finally, a title that is very famous, Baqiyatullah. This is taken from a verse of the Quran, Surah Hud, verse 86: 'Baqiyatullahi khayrul-lakum in kuntum mu'minin' (That which remains from Allah is better for you, if you are believers). Now, the word 'Baqiya' is usually translated as 'the remainder of Allah', as I have translated it, because it is usually translated this way everywhere. But there was a very great scholar who passed away, whose name is the late Fakhruddin al-Turayhi, who was also the teacher of Allama Majlisi, the teacher of Sheikh al-Amili, the teacher of Sayyid Hashim Bahrani, and was a great litterateur. He was a great scholar. He had mastery over Arabic grammar. He wrote a book, Majma' al-Bahrayn. The name of the book is Majma' al-Bahrayn. 'Bahrayn' means the two seas: the Quran and the Hadith. Who are the two seas? The Quran and the Hadith. In the light of both, he explained the words. So, when he explains this verse, specifically this word 'Baqiya', he says: 'Wal-Baqiyatu ar-rahma' (And Baqiya means the mercy of the Lord). Not 'the remainder'. Baqiya means the mercy of the Lord. 'The remainder' could be a literal meaning, but it has a hidden meaning, what is it? The mercy of the Lord. And he says: 'Wa-minhu hadithun wasafa 'alayhis-salam' (And the proof for this is the hadith that describes him (a.s.)): 'Antum Baqiyatullahi fi 'ibadihi' (O Ahlul-Bayt, you are the Baqiyatullah among His servants). O Rahamatullah (Mercy of Allah). You are the mercy of Allah, 'Allati mannallahu biha 'ala 'ibadihi' (through whom Allah has bestowed favor upon His servants). Meaning, the Ahlul-Bayt are that mercy of Allah through whom Allah has favored His servants. And another proof of this is that this is a title of the Imam of the Time. A person came and said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), 'Assalamu 'alayka ya Amir al-Mu'minin'. Can I address you with this title? So the Imam, the sixth Imam, forbade it, saying that the title 'Amir al-Mu'minin' belongs only and exclusively to Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Neither was it a title for anyone before him, nor for anyone after him. So he asked, 'Then how should we address the Mahdi?' The Imam replied, 'Address him by saying: Assalamu 'alayka ya Baqiyatullah' (Peace be upon you, O Mercy of Allah). 'Ayna Baqiyatullah'. That is why there is a sentence in Dua-e-Nudba: 'Ayna Baqiyatullahi allati la takhlu minal-'itratil-hadiya' (Where is the Baqiyatullah of Allah, from whom the guided progeny is never empty?). It is never empty of this mercy. So these were a few names that I presented to you. Now, when you recite Dua-e-Nudba and other supplications, look at how many names have been introduced. Understand their meanings and address the Imam by those very names. So that you do not make up any names on your own, do not invent any names on your own. Just as the Imams themselves have introduced themselves, remember the Imams in that same way. Not in any other way. And this 'Baqiyatullah' is the same name that when the Imam of the Time arrives, he will lean against the wall of the Kaaba and say: 'Baqiyatullahi khayrul-lakum in kuntum mu'minin. Wa-ana Baqiyatullah' (That which remains from Allah is better for you, if you are believers. And I am the Baqiyatullah). That which remains from Allah is better for you if you are people of faith. And I am that very remainder of Allah, meaning I am the mercy of Allah that Allah has now sent to you. So let us all pray together that O Lord, keep us alive until the time when the Imam reappears and the Imam gives this call: 'Ana Baqiyatullah', and we respond to his call, to this voice of his, by saying: 'Labbayk ya Baqiyatullah, Labbayk'. First of all, we once again offer our congratulations to all of you on the auspicious birth of the Shelter of the Universe, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (ajjalallahu ta'ala farajahu sharif), and we pray to the Lord of the Worlds to hasten the reappearance of our Imam, grant us all the ability to remain steadfast on his Wilayah, and grant us the ability to convey the message of the Wilayah of Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) to the entire world. title: Watch 👆 Full Video | Imam Zameen Ka Rabb | EP04 | PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ 2026
excerpt: This lecture explores the Quranic verse regarding the earth shining with the light of its Lord, interpreting 'Rabb' as the Imam of the time. It explains that the Imam acts as the nurturer and sustainer of the earth, whose divine light will illuminate the world upon his reappearance. The discourse highlights that the light of the Imam will surpass the brightness of the sun and moon, rendering them unnecessary for humanity.
content:
‘And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord.’ What is the interpretation of this? Janab-e-Mufazzal asks Imam Sadiq (a.s.) regarding this verse, ‘What is meant by the earth shining with the light of its Lord?’ The Imam says, ‘Rabb al-Ard’ (Lord of the Earth). The Imam of the earth is the Lord of the earth. The one who is the Imam of the earth, the Imam says, is the ‘Rabb’ (Lord/Nurturer). He is the one who nurtures this earth. This verse of the Holy Quran—here, ‘Rabb’ does not mean the ‘Ma’bud’ (Worshipped One/God). ‘Rabb’ here means the one who is responsible for the entire upbringing of the earth, the one by whose command the earth flourishes, and the one by whose light the earth will shine, is the Imam of the earth. Janab-e-Mufazzal asks, ‘When the Imam (a.s.) comes, when the Imam of the earth comes’—pointing towards Hazrat Hujjat (a.s.)—‘what will happen then?’ The Imam says, ‘People will become independent of the light of the sun, and the light of the moon will also not be needed. The light of the Imam will be enough for them.’ The light of the sun and moon will fade when the light of the Imam shines across the whole world, the whole universe, when the reappearance of the Imam (a.s.) takes place. After that, the Imam says, people will become independent of the light of the sun.
The term 'Rabb' in the context of the earth refers to the Imam of the time.
The Imam is the nurturer and sustainer responsible for the flourishing of the earth.

The light of the Imam will be so profound that the sun and moon will no longer be needed.

Humanity will become independent of celestial light sources during the era of the Imam.

content:
TSR presents. Ya Karim, Ya Karim, Be Ahle Bait, Ya Karim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Received his name from God, his kunniyat from the Holy Prophet. And this is the honor of the Quran, this is the respect of the Haram. And one is the light of the Prophet's eyes, the second is the Imam. And like the grandfather, the Prophet; like the father, the Commander of Hunayn. Like the grandfather, the Prophet; like the father, the Commander of Hunayn. Like the mother, Fatima; like the strength of the arm, Hussain. Wow, wow, wow. Like the mother, Fatima; like the strength of the arm, Hussain. Unlimited praise and glorification for that pure and holy personality, for that All-Knowing, Wise, Merciful, and Generous Creator of the universe, who kept us all attached to the Wilayat of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and his pure and holy progeny, who are the guides and leaders of God's creation after him. And one link in this chain of infallibility and purity, for whose auspicious birth we are all gathered here today. And the Strong Rope, i.e., the TSR team, is once again present before you with the Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz. So come, first of all, let us offer congratulations for this blessed and auspicious birth in the court of the Ahlulbayt, especially in the service of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), through a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad, ajjal farajahum wa sahhil makhrajahum. And we also offer congratulations to all of you for this auspicious birth and welcome you all to this Sibt-e-Akbar (a.s.) Grand Quiz. So viewers, before this quiz begins, we would like you to be aware of its rules. So, here are the rules of this quiz on your screen. Audhu billahis sami'il alimi minash shaitanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Wa salli Allahu alayka ya Waliyyal Asr adrikna. The quiz link is live and is available in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then, on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first; the only condition for the quiz prize is that all answers must be correct. Viewers, before starting today's discussion about Imam Hasan (a.s.), we will present a brief biography of the Imam (a.s.), especially for children, as this program is on the occasion of his auspicious birth, which is the episode of today, and the joys of which the entire humanity is celebrating. His name is Imam Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). His noble father's name is Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). His noble mother's name is Siddiqa Tahira Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.). His date of birth is 15th of the blessed month of Ramadan, 3 Hijri. His date of martyrdom is 28th Safar, 50 Hijri, and he was martyred by the poison of deceit, which was given by his wife, Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath. Your kunniyat is Abu Muhammad, and your famous titles are Mujtaba, Sibt-e-Nabi, Sibt-e-Akbar, and Sayyid-e-Shabab-e-Ahlul Jannah. Let us start today's discussion with the name of Imam Hasan (a.s.), i.e., how his name was given after his birth. There is a narration here from Janabe Asma bint Umays, who says that when Imam Hasan (a.s.) was born, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) came there. And after coming, he said to Asma bint Umays, 'Ya Asma, hati ibni' (O Asma, bring my son to me). Here, there is a point to ponder: the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is addressing Imam Hasan (a.s.) as his son. If we turn our minds towards the event of Mubahila, the first interpretation of 'abna'ana wa abna'akum' (our sons and your sons) is Imam Hasan (a.s.), as the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) took Imam Hasan (a.s.) for Mubahila. So here, at the time of birth, the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is announcing that he should not be remembered as my grandson, but as my son. And after that, he ordered Janabe Asma to bring him wrapped in a white cloth. And when Janabe Asma bint Umays brought Imam Hasan (a.s.) to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) properly wrapped in a white cloth, the words of the narration are that he recited Adhan in his right ear and Iqamah in his left ear. excerpt: This lecture challenges the concept of 'Adalat-e-Sahaba' (the absolute righteousness of all companions) by referencing a specific historical event. The speaker cites a Hadith from Hudhayfah regarding a conspiracy by certain companions to assassinate the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) at Aqaba after the Battle of Tabuk. The discourse questions the theological validity of following individuals who allegedly plotted against the Prophet, highlighting a contradiction in mainstream narratives.
content:
How is it possible that every companion (Sahabi) is righteous, when in the list of companions, there are also people who conspired to kill the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) after the Battle of Tabuk? And this is present in the books of Ahl-e-Sunnah as a proper Hadith. The Hadith is from Hudhayfah, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was returning from Tabuk, and when the caravan of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was coming to Medina, it was passing through a mountain pass (Aqaba).' That is, he was passing near a valley. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was moving, and the people were with him, until when he reached a certain place on the path, some of his companions—who are called Sahaba or compared to stars—secretly joined a conspiracy. They consulted among themselves to push the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) from the Aqaba, a hill or a high mountain, on the way. Then the narrator, according to the meaning of Ibn Ishaq, narrated the whole Hadith as to what happened. That is, these are the people who are compared to stars. And if this Hadith, which we are discussing today, if this Hadith were authentic in terms of its chain of narration (sanad), as the apparent meaning of this Hadith suggests, then a very big problem arises: is it incumbent upon us to follow such people who were involved in the conspiracy to kill the Prophet? involved in the conspiracy to kill the Prophet? Those who follow them, where will they go? [Music] Every

title: Shameem -e- Ma'refat | Ep.#6 | Hisham ibn Hakam -Defender of Wilayat | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological and practical significance of Wilayah and Bara'ah within the Shia tradition, focusing on the life and intellectual contributions of Hisham ibn Hakam. Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi examines how Hisham served as a model for defending the faith through logic, knowledge, and unwavering devotion to the Ahlulbayt. The discourse emphasizes the necessity of an infallible Imam as a source of certainty and divine guidance, while encouraging believers to cultivate intellectual bravery and spiritual commitment.
content:
that the signs of the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.)... in the previous, i.e., the fifth episode of 'Ma'rifat', we listened to some points from Shahid (r.a.) regarding the issue of Wilayah, in which he mentioned that Sheikh... mentioned that Sheikh Saduq (r.a.), in his famous book 'Al-I'tiqadat', described the belief of Wilayah in the light of the teachings of the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.) in such a way that he wrote in his book that whoever usurped the right of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), all those people are oppressors, and in the view of the followers of God and the Prophet, and according to the Quran and Hadith, these people are cursed and are oppressors; the curse of Allah be upon them. From this, it also became clear that the belief in Wilayah, the belief in the Wilayah of the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.), is not complete until it includes 'Bara'ah' (disassociation) from their enemies. Until a person believes in the principle of Bara'ah along with Wilayah, their faith is incomplete. And it was mentioned that the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'The one who claims our Wilayah and our love but does not disassociate from our enemies is a liar.' is a liar. Today's episode is about a person who defended the Wilayah, who defended the Wilayah from a very young age, and defended the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.). Yes, dear viewers, my reference is to Janab-e-Kumayl ibn Ziyad (r.a.), who was a student of the sixth Imam, Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.), whom the Imam had taught the supplication of Kumayl. And his words, the words of Janab-e-Kumayl, are very famous. How he defended the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.) through his words and his actions. And to get more information in this regard, I am obliged to invite our guest to provide us with information on this topic, and I request all of you to welcome him with a loud Salawat. Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, peace be upon... Rizwan Mirza Muhammad Muhammad, peace be upon... O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, guide us... our master, Al-Hajj... the upcoming Sharad Pawar, Maulana Al-Hajj... is that the night... for the devotees. In this regard, the chain of narration... this Hadith... this Hadith... in his book 'Majma' al-Zawa'id'... and the Hadith is narrated from 'Amr ibn Thabit. Who is 'Amr ibn Thabit? This is also interesting, listen. 'Amr ibn Thabit is the one who was... and 'Amr ibn Thabit... and 'Amr ibn Thabit was among those who went to the house of Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.) to threaten her. He was an enemy of the Ahl-e-Bayt (a.s.). And then the son of 'Amr, the father of 'Amr, his name was... and he was in the battlefield. This was the one who was... and the son of 'Amr ibn Thabit was this person. He was the son of Hakam bin Sabit. This person, Hisham, was a young man of great determination who loved Ali (a.s.) immensely during his lifetime. This has been narrated from Hisham, who loved Ali (a.s.) and the family of Ali (a.s.) very much. He asked his father, and the Imam (a.s.) said: 'Whoever loves us with their heart, helps us with their hands, and supports us with their tongue, then he is with us.' So, three conditions have been set: first, to love with the heart; second, to help with the tongue; and third, to help with the hands. If someone does this, then the Almighty will place him in our station, in our rank, and he will be with us because he loves us, helps us with his tongue, and helps us with his hands. And after that, it was finished, and whoever loves with the heart... It was finished, and whoever loves with the heart and helps us, but if he helps with his hands... and whoever loves us with the heart but helps with his hands... some only love. And those who love with the heart and tongue, but the highest will be those who love with the heart, help with the hands, help with the tongue, support us, and confirm us. They will be with us in our chambers in Paradise. This is the station of the one who loves the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) immensely and is always ready for their defense. So, our topic today is the defense of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) because this... Our topic today is the defense of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) because this is a very, very vast topic. There are many things, many events, and many people involved in it. And because it is not possible to cover all these people, this Hisham, who loved the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) so much and was always ready for them, was ready to do anything for them. Therefore, Hisham bin Hakam is a name we often mention, but even for the youth and children, it is necessary to start learning. For this, it is very important that a person has knowledge so that they can defend. So, this is the second condition: a person must possess knowledge and have a smile/pleasant demeanor to start and defend. So, there is religious knowledge and the second is to do something. There is religious knowledge, and the second is to be filled with the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). To love so much, to love so much that if anyone speaks against the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), they are immediately ready for defense. Before doing this work, I will give you a small example today. This is a very famous magazine, and they had this spirit, this great love. The opponents had a magazine, and in that magazine, an author wrote an article against the Shia. And it was going on, and he had 300... Against it, and it was going on, and he had 300 Shia scholars... from that, a magazine was published from Lucknow, which was published monthly, which used to answer them. It started in 1956 and continued until 1993, every month, answering them. So, if we talk about defense, then today... Hisham bin Hakam, regarding the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), there are two events, and he is very hot-headed. He told the important points. These two events are present in Usul al-Kafi, and the English translation of Usul al-Kafi is available; you can refer to it. So, these events are not just stories; Hisham has done something. And he tells you that in the presence of... And he tells you that in the presence of Imam Sadiq (a.s.), he was sitting with some of his companions. Who were among his companions? Humran bin A'yan. He was also a great personality, a very great personality about whom the Imam said: 'You are the helper of Humran.' If anyone wants to see if their faith is correct or wrong, they should look at Humran. Humran was the brother of Zurarah, and along with him was Muhammad bin Nu'man, who is famous by the name of Mu'min al-Taq. Then after that, Hisham bin Salim al-Jawaliqi was present, and Abul Khattab was present. And among all of them was a young man whose name was Hisham bin Hakam. Now, this whole report is about this young man whose name was Hisham. He had this spirit in his heart: 'I don't know, you have not defended the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' Hisham says: 'I cannot answer in front of you. You are present, and I feel that my tongue gets tied in front of you.' The Imam said: 'Hisham, when we say something, act upon it. When it happens, act upon it.' And it was enough. Hisham starts narrating that I heard that Amr bin Ubayd and his... the event started, but then he started his journey, whose name was... and he was the founder of the Mu'tazila. And Hisham says that I heard that Amr bin Ubayd was sitting in the mosque of Basra, properly teaching his followers, and he was training them. Now, let me tell you a point here that is necessary. In that era, Basra was the stronghold of the opponents. Many people there were almost all of them, in that era, not today—today we have many lovers of Ahlulbayt (a.s.)—but in that era, they were almost all against them and were very, very strict. They were very dirty in their behavior, and very... In that era, they were almost all against them, and they were very strict. They were very dirty in their behavior, and very... He was sitting in the Jamia Masjid of Basra, teaching his followers. I got this news. Now, this point, Hisham says that as soon as I got the news, I immediately went to Basra. So, Hisham says, 'I went there, and I sat quietly.' This is not my purpose. From this, it is clear that Hisham should have gone immediately. But Hisham says, and Hisham went, and he says, and look at Hisham's courage, look at his bravery: in the gathering of the enemies, in the Jamia Masjid itself, look at the courage. This is bravery. Hisham went there and says: 'I saw that a circle of people...' I saw that a circle of people had formed, and he was sitting on a seat. Those who were sitting in the first row were the most important people; the less important people were standing far away. And he was sitting on a high seat and teaching. Hisham says that I pushed through the crowd and went and sat in the front. And I saw that this Amr bin Ubayd was sitting on his seat in the form of a leader, and one of his cloaks was draped over his shoulders, and another cloak was over that. He was showing his face, and people were asking him questions, and he was answering. When it reached a level, the thought came to his mind: 'Ask him whatever you want to ask, don't hesitate, I will answer your questions.' Just like in the time of the Imam, he used to say 'Saluni' (ask me), these people were also saying: 'Ask whatever you want to ask, ask, ask,' and people were asking, and he was answering. Ask whatever you want to ask, and people were asking, and he was answering. Hisham says, 'I went and sat exactly where the method was, and I sat on my knees.' And Hisham, who was a young man at that time, had to see the Imam. So he says, 'I sat on my knees.' When people asked questions, I said, 'O scholar, O teacher, I am a stranger here. If you allow me, may I ask you a question?' He said, 'Ask.' Hisham said, 'Do you have eyes?' He said, 'Young man, what kind of question is this? You are asking about something that you see with your own eyes.' I said, 'Even though I have eyes, I am still asking if you have them or not.' Hisham said, 'My question is of this nature. This is a ridiculous question, but you answer.' 'Okay, young man, ask, even if your question is ridiculous.' 'Then answer, do you have eyes?' 'Yes, I have eyes.' 'What do you do with them?' 'I see the colors, I see the people, I see the reports.' 'Do you have a tongue?' 'Yes, I have a tongue.' 'What do you do with it?' 'I speak, especially when I can...' How can I distinguish? What do I do with this? I hear the sound, I hear the maximum volume, I recognize the sound, whose sound it is. You can see, you can hear, you can smell, you can taste, and you can touch. All these senses are working equally. Where are you getting confused? You said that you distinguish, you differentiate for your own senses. So, your senses, your five senses—do you need an Imam for them? Where is the need? It is not needed. But you said that your senses are all working, you can see, hear, and do everything. So then what is the need? He said, 'When there is any doubt regarding my five senses, I use my intellect to remove that doubt.' So, I remove this doubt through my intellect. When something needs to be analyzed, I analyze it through my intellect and remove my doubt, replacing the doubt with certainty. I become certain that this thing is correct and this thing is wrong. I have to use my intellect. For example, if two sounds are coming, and if the ear is unable to distinguish whose sound it is, then through the intellect, I reach a conclusion that this sound is from so-and-so and the other is not. Besides this, in other matters, he took it further. This means you are saying that even though the senses are present and working, it is impossible to attain certainty without an Imam? It is impossible to attain certainty without an Imam? It is necessary in the same way. An Imam is appointed. Allah has not left the body and the senses without an Imam. And you say that Allah has left the entire universe without an Imam? Someone who answers people's questions, Someone who removes people's doubts, someone who converts people's doubts into certainty—Allah has kept an Imam for you, but has not kept an Imam for the universe? As soon as Imam (a.s.) said this, Hisham became silent. He did not say anything for a long time. After that, what did he say? Hisham says, 'He turned towards me and started saying, "So, you are Hisham?"' Now, there was a bit of danger here. It was possible that he might say, 'He is the one who came to the mosque and humiliated me, kill him right now.' But Imam (a.s.) did not stop. He asked about his friends and his companions. He asked, 'Where are they?' At such a young age, Imam (a.s.) had so much dignity that everyone recognized Hisham. His debates are famous. Today, who is a youth whose debate skills are discussed? And he is a disbeliever... Skills are discussed, and he is a disbeliever, yet he is afraid of his skills. Tell me, what answer do you have? He said, 'We are the people...' He hugged him and made him sit on his seat. To say this, 'You are my teacher,' and for a youth to be compared to him, this was a very big thing. Hisham and his opponent got up from his seat and made Hisham sit. And Hisham says that as long as I remained seated, he was silent. Completely silent. As long as I did not get up from that seat. When I got up from that seat, after that, then I left from there. When Hisham narrated this, Imam (a.s.) started smiling. And Imam (a.s.) asked, 'Hisham, tell me, from whom did you learn these debate skills? From whom did you learn?' Hisham said, 'Whatever I have learned, I have learned from you. Whatever I have proven, I have proven through your teachings.' Imam (a.s.) said, 'By God, this which you have done...' By God, this which you have done, this is exactly how it is present in the Sahifa and the books. Exactly like this. So, this entire debate is present in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 169, and the chapter name is 'Bab al-Istita'a'. This was the debate. Now look at another one, let's move quickly because time is short. And he has narrated from his teacher Ali bin Ibrahim, and he from his master, and he from the Imams (a.s.), who say, 'I was always with the Imam during the Hajj season.' During Hajj, the Imam (a.s.) used to go to Mecca, and in Mecca, near the well of Safa, they used to build a small tent and live in it. So he says, 'I was with the Imam, and in one season, and today also to a large extent this was the case, and those people who were followers...' It had become a whole stronghold. So, the Imam came, and the opponents and the scholars, they are all gathered. I am narrating from the book. They gathered to debate with the Imam. The Imam said, 'I am ready for the debate, but I will only accept what is from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and what is from the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.).' When the Imam's character was like this, they were rude. They asked the Imam, 'Look, Imam, tell me...' The Imam said, 'First of all, this is not the way to ask. A questioner has come, the question must be answered. He asked me, "Tell me, this that you are talking about, is it from your side or is it from the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)?" Both are the same, both are knowledge combined, I have made this knowledge.' The Imam asked him, 'Does this mean that you have become a partner of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? You have become a partner of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)?' He said, 'No, it is not like that.' I asked, 'Then if it is not like that, then is the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) angry with you, or did he give you news that you should be like this?' 'There is nothing like that.' 'So, are you the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) or a partner of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)? Or are you infallible, that you cannot make mistakes?' 'So, what have you brought?' The Imam turned towards his companions and said to them, 'I have already defeated him before starting the debate.' He was defeated. 'If you know how to debate, then I tell you to be patient.' He says, 'That day I was very regretful...' He says that that day I was very regretful that why did I not learn how to debate? Why did I learn? But I... my life, you forbade me from debating. And you say that people say, 'This can be interpreted this way, this cannot be interpreted, this can be understood, this cannot be understood.' Do not debate. We said that those people whom I criticized, whom I debated, these were the people who, leaving our knowledge or leaving the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), speak from their own opinions. They make their own arguments themselves. Leaving the arguments of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), leaving their hadiths, they make their own arguments. Learn the knowledge and become a Muslim. And those who debate with me, bring them to me, to defeat them. So they went, and they brought the scholars, and they were defeated by the Imam. They were defeated by the Imam, and they brought the best debaters. Why? Because they had learned the method of debating from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). And today, this was the time of Imam (a.s.), and there were old people too. They all brought them, and from here, we move forward. He says, 'Look, how many followers were there!' They learned how to debate from Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s.). They must have seen the time of the Imams (a.s.), but despite that, you know that their son, Abu Hisham, went astray. He went astray, and he was with such a great... he became a child, leaving the Shia path, leaving the right path, and became a Waqifi. That is why we should always pray for ourselves, always after every prayer, during every prayer, whenever possible, pray for our own guidance and for our children, constantly pray... And constantly pray for your children, 'O Allah, keep us and our offspring on the right path.' And as much as possible, try to instill the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) in their hearts. Let the love of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) sink into their hearts so that they always... when we talk, they love the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). And when... this was what happened. So many years passed, and just a few days later, it started that the Imam (a.s.) was staying... one time, look, Hisham was not among these people. Hisham was... the Imam (a.s.) took him out, and the Kufa... the Imam (a.s.) was happy. By God, the Imam (a.s.) was happy. Seeing this happiness, we thought that this is the one who was... they were angry, and in the matters where people used to create problems... And in the parts where people used to cause problems, now we have returned to this. The era of the Imam (a.s.) has arrived, which is why so much is happening. But as soon as they became indifferent, we saw that this is the work. And Yunus says this was the answer to the question, that his beard had also just started to grow. He was barely 16, 17, or 18 years old, just a little bit. And among all those who were sitting there, he was the youngest companion of the Imam (a.s.). Look, this is the ready-made chosen one. Now, this second debate begins. Although it is a bit long, but because of the time, we are spending it. So, we first have the misguided Shami. So, he debated him, defeated that image, and defeated him in such a way that the whole assembly was amazed. Then the Imam (a.s.) said, 'Now you debate.' So, the Imam (a.s.) debated Muhammad bin Jafar and defeated him. The Imam (a.s.) said, '10 years, 10 years, 10 years.' You listen, debate him. He debated, but both of them debated in such a way that neither his victory nor his defeat was clear. Both of them became like that. Then the Imam (a.s.) said to the Shami, 'Thanks.' Then the Imam (a.s.) said to the Shami, 'Thanks.' You debate him. So, when he started debating, the Shami's condition became so deep, his condition became so bad, debating with the companions of the Imam (a.s.), that the Imam (a.s.) and his companions started laughing at his condition. And the state he was put in during the debate made the Imam (a.s.) laugh. The Imam (a.s.) said to the Shami, 'O Shami, you have met these people until now. Now debate this boy.' And he pointed towards the Imam (a.s.), calling him a boy. 'Debate this child.' The Shami was a child at that time. Now look at the position. The claim of the Imam (a.s.) is that this is the spirit, that we are the ones who answer every question, we are the ones who defend our Ahlulbayt (a.s.), but for that, it is necessary, for that, these qualities are necessary. That this child, this Shami, while his condition is so bad, he had already been defeated, he had already received it. After that, he said to the Imam (a.s.), 'Child, you... tell me about the Imamate of this man, this man...' with a very bad, wrong, and rude manner, he said, 'This man...' And with a rude manner, he said, 'Tell me about the Imamate of this man, prove his Imamate.' This is the level of his manners. When the Imam (a.s.) heard this, he started trembling with anger. Look, today the condition is, what should we debate? If there is any disrespect towards the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), then we have our love, our prejudice, our emotions, and these feelings of ours should be met with silence. Okay, what to do? Let it be, he is not doing it, we should take silence like the Imam (a.s.). How can he stop? The Imam (a.s.) came forward. 'O Shami, you tell me, does your Lord have more mercy on His creatures, or do the creatures have more mercy on themselves?' He said, 'My Lord has more mercy than the creatures have on themselves.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Then how does Allah show His mercy and grace upon His servants?' The Shami said, 'Allah has appointed a guide for them.' 'Go on, speak.' 'This guide, if they go astray, and if there is a disagreement among them, then this guide, this leader, this Imam, he unites them.' This guide, this leader, this Imam, he unites them. Their disputes, their crookedness, he straightens it and tells them what their responsibility is towards their Lord. The Shami asked, 'Who is this guide, this leader? Who is he?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.).' 'Who is after the Messenger?' He said, 'The Book and the Sunnah.' 'We are the Book and the Sunnah.' The Shami said, 'If the Book and the Sunnah are enough, then why did you come here from Syria? To resolve our differences? We have the Book and the Sunnah, and both of us are using the Quran and the Sunnah, and our differences have not been resolved. Both of us are using the Quran.' This is the argument he is bringing from the Quran. Now the Shami is stuck, he has no answer. The Imam (a.s.) asked, 'Why are you not answering? Why are you silent?' He said, 'What answer should I give? If I say, then I am wrong. If I say that the Book and the Sunnah resolve our differences, then I am cutting my own argument. The Quran itself has many meanings, people can do their own interpretation.' Now the Imam (a.s.) said, 'And if I say...' Now the Imam (a.s.) said, 'And if I say that both of us are right, then I am wrong, because the Book and the Sunnah are not benefiting us. Both are right, and both of their interpretations are right, then what is the benefit of the Quran? That both are on the wrong path.' When there is a disagreement on something, when there is a defeat, it is always between truth and falsehood, or falsehood and falsehood. It is not that this is not decided. The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Answer me. Always when we see, the truth-seeker sees.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'The same question you asked the Shami, why don't you ask the Shami?' He said, 'Okay, tell me, does your Lord have more mercy on His creatures, or do the creatures have more mercy on themselves?' The Shami said, 'The Lord has more mercy on His creatures than they have on themselves.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'Has He appointed anyone as a guide who will guide them, who will straighten their crookedness, and who will tell them what is truth and what is falsehood? Has He appointed anyone like that?' The Shami said... Has He appointed anyone like that? The Shami said, 'In the time of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), and in today's time...' The Shami thought, 'In today's time, who is it?' The Shami said, 'This Imam, this leader, these are the ones who come, they are the ones who give news of the heavens and the earth.' And this is the knowledge that has been given. This Shami, in this hadith, is acknowledging the Imam (a.s.). Those who today have created some such people who deny the Imam's knowledge of the unseen, the Shami said, 'They will give you news.' Now, as soon as the Shami was stuck, what is the argument? The Shami said, 'Ask them whatever you want to ask, they will answer.' The Imam (a.s.) said, 'You have finished all my arguments, you have finished all the evidence. Now I have no option left.' The Imam (a.s.) started answering the questions before he could even ask. 'O Shami, I give you news of when your journey started...' I give you news of when your journey started, how it happened, where you stopped, where you stayed, what you did during the whole journey.' And the Imam (a.s.) gave all the details, small details of his whole journey. When the Imam (a.s.) explained everything, the Shami said, 'Indeed, you have spoken the truth, and I now support your Imamate and guidance. I accept Islam.' The Imam (a.s.) said to him, 'No, why are you doing this? I have faith in Allah, and I accept Islam because you were already a Muslim, and accepting Islam only means inheritance and marriage, but based on faith, a person goes to Paradise.' That is, the Imam (a.s.) explained that based on faith, a person's status is correct. Here, as soon as the Imam (a.s.) said this, the Shami immediately recited the Kalima and, by reciting the Kalima, acknowledged the Imamate of the Imam (a.s.). Now, from this, it is known, from this it is known that until now, if someone asks a question, okay, in that time the Imam (a.s.) gave the answer. In today's time, the Imam (a.s.) is not present, the Imam (a.s.) is in occultation, so what should we do? How should we do it? So the answer is that the Imam (a.s.) himself can see this. One aspect is that he is the Imam (a.s.) of his time, and for every era, there is an Imam (a.s.). It is necessary that there is an Imam (a.s.) in every era. Who is he? So you should search. He is alive, the Quran confirms that he is the guide. It is the Imam's (a.s.) job to guide. The Imam (a.s.) will show the way, will show the path. Just like he met hundreds and thousands of people, he didn't meet them, but the Imam's (a.s.) job is to guide. And he says, 'Okay, you search for the Imam (a.s.).' He says, 'Okay, you search for the Imam (a.s.). You will talk about your intellect.' And you see, it is like this, but the problem is that we are not familiar with our Imam (a.s.) until we are familiar with our Imam (a.s.), then what will we tell others? This whole debate of the Shami is present in Al-Kafi, after this, the 20th volume, after the 11th century, in the 110.4 tradition, the incident of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is present. And we should, as much as possible, help the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). I will not say from my side, they don't need our help, but this is better for us, for our hereafter, this will improve our hereafter, this will build the hereafter of our children. We should do this, and become like those who left the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who left the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) alone, in the way that this... In the way that this... 'Is there anyone who will help me? Is there anyone who will help the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)?' We also know that we have the ability, we have the capacity, still, whatever little we have, we will try to create it. Create it, gain knowledge, and defend the Wilayah so that we can do a little bit for you. Do it. May Allah help us. Peace be upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. And today, Ali (a.s.) has made this matter completely clear for us that the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.)... It has been stated that there is no age limit for defending the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). If a person has courage, a pure intention, and sincerity within them, they can defend it. On such an occasion, they will receive support from the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), and may Allah grant the ability to do so. The truth is that the reality of this will only be attained by a person after death. So, let us recite a few couplets regarding the defense of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.): 'Those who speak of Hussain (a.s.) of Karbala, those who speak of the successor of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), they speak with the tongue of Ali (a.s.). Whoever opens their mouth in the world in defense of Ali (a.s.), Ali (a.s.) speaks on their behalf in the hereafter.' And Insha'Allah, whoever defends the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), the angels will surely speak on their behalf. It is my prayer to Allah (s.w.t.) that He grants us the opportunity to live our lives under the shadow of the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). May He grant us the opportunity to live under the shadow of their Wilayah and keep us steadfast upon their Wilayah until our last breath. And after death, may He grant us their intercession. Dear listeners, in the end, let me make an announcement: tomorrow, Sunday, our other program which started last week—which is related to Religion and Science—will be presented by Janab Hujjat al-Islam Maulana Syed Aftab Haider Sahab. I request you to watch this program tomorrow, Sunday, at 9:30 PM India time. This program is related to Religion and Science, and if you have any questions regarding special diseases or other topics, please send them to our WhatsApp number: [number removed], either via voice message or text message. Remember us in your prayers. Let us conclude this program with the Ziyarat of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim, Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad... Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa Aali Muhammad. With this, we take your leave. We will meet again next week. Until then, Allah Hafiz.
