title: Majlis-e-Aza (Urdu) for Esaal e Sawaab of Marhoom Dr. Nazim Habib Merchant
excerpt: This lecture, delivered as a Majlis-e-Aza for the Esaal-e-Sawaab of Dr. Nazim Habib Merchant, explores the profound Islamic virtues of Ithar (altruism) and Ihsan (benevolence). The speaker emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the needs of others over oneself, drawing inspiration from the selfless sacrifices of the Ahl al-Bayt. By highlighting historical examples such as Imam Ali’s actions at Laylat al-Mabit and the sacrifice of Ali Akbar, the lecture encourages listeners to practice compassion, maintain the dignity of those they assist, and view their wealth as a divine trust.
content:
Insha'Allah, we will proceed with the recitation... [Music] ...May Allah grant us the strength to follow the path of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). [Music] ...[Music]... [Music] ...[Music]... Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. I request prayers for the late Dr. Nazim Habib Merchant, who passed away. He was a doctor who served patients, and for those who were in need and could not afford treatment, he provided it for free. Today's topic for this session, which has been chosen, is 'Ithar' (Selflessness). Dr. Nazim Habib Merchant... The topic chosen for this session is 'Ithar'. The Arabic word 'Ithar' means to prioritize others. If we translate it, it means helping others, erasing the pain of others, even if one has to endure hardship or suffering oneself. This is called 'Ithar'. It means trying to reduce the troubles of others. We should try to comfort whoever comes into contact with us. This is the word 'Ithar'. Now, look at the status of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). What is the 'Maqam' (status) of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.)? 'Maqam' refers to the heights, the elevated status. And if someone reaches that, it is called... And if someone reaches that, it is 'Maqam al-Ithar'. It is when one prioritizes others, where greed is not found, where stinginess is not found, where selfishness is not found. That is why it is said that the sign of a Momin (believer) is that they put themselves in hardship so that others may find comfort. They cause pain to their own body so that others may find rest. This is the sign of a Momin. So, regarding the late person for whom this gathering is held, many people have spoken about his qualities. Mashallah, there are many, but I have chosen this topic because this spirit should increase in our community—the spirit of 'Ithar', the spirit of sacrifice, the spirit of selflessness. My Mawla (a.s.) used these words, 'Al-Ithar...', why does he say this? Because 'Ithar' is the manifestation of the best character. The manifestation of 'Ithar' is for the good of others. Whoever we interact with, we should think about how to comfort them and how to remove their pain. If we are in this chapter, we should try to remove their pain. We should not cause them trouble or distress, but rather remove their suffering, even if we have to endure pain in the process. This is 'Ithar'. My Mawla (a.s.) says, 'Al-Ithar is the best of human qualities.' It is the highest level of faith. This spirit of 'Ithar' is what Allah has placed in the hearts of the believers; they always want to bring comfort to people, and they possess this... Regarding providing comfort to people and the concept of 'Ihsan' (benevolence), you will find many traditions that tell people to be benevolent to others, to do good to others, so that others may be relieved of their distress. Being benevolent does not mean that if you have done a favor to someone a month ago, you keep reminding them of it. That is not Ihsan. Ihsan means that a person should, as much as possible, provide the other person with what they are in need of, in the way they need it. And during this, one should seek the pleasure of Allah (SWT). May your character be made more beautiful, and may you continue to do good to people. Allah (SWT) is doing Ihsan to you, so you should continue to do Ihsan to your fellow humans. Before moving forward, it is important to mention that for this Ihsan, there is no distinction of religion, sect, caste, or skin color. Whoever is a human being, continue to do Ihsan to them. Whatever is the creation of Allah, do Ihsan to them. Whatever is the creation of Allah, do Ihsan to them. This feeling is very important. You must have heard the name of Janab-e-Malik-e-Ashtar. He was such a powerful personality that even enemies feared him. He was a commander-in-chief, a very powerful army commander. But this same Malik-e-Ashtar is walking on the road, and a dog is sleeping there. He is placing his feet very slowly so that the dog's sleep is not disturbed. Look at the character of a follower of Ali (a.s.). Even a dog's sleep should not be disturbed. Malik-e-Ashtar, a commander-in-chief, is worried about a dog's sleep. If a believer causes pain to an animal, then he is not a true follower of the Commander of the Faithful. If a believer causes pain to an animal, he is not a true follower of the Commander of the Faithful. If the matter concerns a believer, the responsibility increases even more. You see, this is present in our famous books, including our Tafsir. It is narrated that a person came to the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I am hungry.' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) sent him to the houses of his wives to see if he could find anything. He went and asked, but they replied, 'We have nothing here except water.' Then he sat with the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) again, and the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'Who will take this man in and feed him? Who will remove his hunger? This is the guest of Allah.' Who will remove his hunger? This is the guest of Allah. Ali (a.s.) said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I will take him. I will take care of him and remove his hunger.' He took him to his house. He asked his wife, 'Do we have anything to eat?' She replied, 'We have only enough for the children.' Ali (a.s.) said, 'Put the children to sleep. We will give preference to our guest.' Look at how they gave preference to their guest. We will give preference to our guest. Look at how they did it. O Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Put the children to sleep, extinguish the lamp.' And in that darkness, they gave the food that was meant for the children to the hungry guest. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was pleased. They are ready to stay hungry themselves but will feed others. 'And whoever saves his soul from stinginess and selfishness, they are the successful ones.' These are the people who achieve success. Even if they do not get worldly wealth, in the hereafter, Allah has written for them a reward that no one can estimate. This is the story of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.). This entire event is detailed in the books of the great scholars. They have narrated this in the Tafsir of the verse, 'They give preference to others over themselves.' When there was a little food in the house of Zahra (s.a.), she prepared it. She prepared it and placed it before her family and children. Just as the food was placed, a beggar came and called out, 'May Allah have mercy on you, O Ahlulbayt. I am hungry, give me some of the food you have.' They stood up and gave him the food. Then a second person came and called out, 'May Allah have mercy on you, I am hungry.' They gave him the remaining food. Then a third person came, an orphan, and called out, 'May Allah have mercy on you, I am hungry.' They gave him the rest of the food. Nothing was left for them. This spirit of sacrifice, this spirit of 'Ithar' (altruism). No one tasted it. You can imagine, usually, when something is made at home, even if people are a little hungry, they might control themselves, but it is difficult to control children. But these were the children of Ali (a.s.) and Fatimah (s.a.). In some narrations, it is mentioned that the children cried. They were Hassan and Hussain (a.s.). Remember this, who is the narrator of this tradition? Remember this, who is the narrator of this tradition? The narrator is Abu Hurairah. And Abu Hurairah was known to be someone who loved them very much. He narrated this to show the greatness of the Ahlulbayt. After narrating this, he says, 'O family of the Prophet, you have sacrificed your own needs for others.' This verse was revealed for this act of sacrifice, which is the highest level of Ihsan. The issue of revealing this on this verse, the death of this verse, therefore, it is necessary that they should be... this is a very important feeling, this is the time, surely the angels... just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) slept, so Allah, from this field, before the angels, did this. This is fine; a human being, his life... he gave one human being to another, and from someone, it is necessary that you give your life for another. One, two, nothing... now, now, the claim of Saudi Arabia... cannot do it. Allah, Allah, the Messenger, or the Messenger of Allah, but others should become the highest so that this... But others should become the highest so that this... did not know that they were going to be... we are ready to sleep, but they were prepared when they were there, then there it was looted and Allah's faith is necessary, it is called, actually, Allah... Allah is with us because nothing will happen to us. That you... Inna Allah ma'ana, Allah is with us because Allah is with us and at this time, you are our means, nothing will happen to you. You are our means, nothing will happen to you. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) asked, 'Will I sleep here?' He asked back, 'O Messenger of Allah, if I sleep, will your life be saved? Is your life...?' I said, 'My life... I will sleep, you sleep, my life...' 'I will sleep, I will be alive until morning, you take my place, you take it.' This is... he did not ask this question, you... look at this sacrifice, this is called sacrifice, this is called the spirit of sacrifice, this is called... Then he slept in the place of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and what is called, he slept, he did not just lie down, he slept, and he slept with such sleep as never before and never after. This is what Allah referred to, the sacrifice, before the angels, first Allah asked, 'If...' Before the angels, first Allah asked, 'If one of you gives your life and the other is ready to give his life...' Now look, who is the first man? For Allah, the angels, the greatest angels of Allah, and who is Allah... Allah asked the angels, 'Who among you is ready to sacrifice his life for the other?' Both were selected... so that they talk about things like this... Look at Muhammad, look at Ali, how Ali, when Muhammad is, is ready to sacrifice his life. Just this matter, or immediately the verse was revealed, 'Wa min an-nasi man yashri nafsahu...' The verse was revealed, 'Wa min an-nasi man yashri nafsahu...' and among the people are some who are ready to sell, ready to give their lives, to attain the pleasure of Allah, and are ready to take... then it doesn't matter, there are other destinations. And the pleasure was bought, Allah always bought it, Allah's pleasure was always bought. Ali's life became Allah's life, and Ali became Allah's. That is why... that is why... this is... Allah, Allah, Allah... Allah's... so they are all ready. Allah's... so they are all ready, but where... when the matter comes, there, immediately select... so this is the juice, and these were all... Allah, where He made the Baitullah, all these things, He turned them towards Himself. So if Allah and the Messenger have seen, this has been taken, and Allah deals with the servants, and if you become a servant... this is the spirit of sacrifice, and what Allah has given... Now here, in the center, two or three hadiths, let's open them quickly, then move towards the prayers. This, look at the habit, two people, to fulfill this need, in this regard, it is formally stated in the traditions that if someone fulfills the need of a Momin, if a Momin comes with his need, and if the one he is coming to can fulfill his need, then what is its reward? See its reward, see its result, what is it? This is narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). Narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), this is the question, the wealth is present, this is... he said, Malikana said, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) say: 'Man qada li-akhihi al-mu'mini hajah...' whoever fulfills the need of his Momin brother, it is as if he has worshipped Allah for his whole life. This is... worshipped Allah... if he fulfills the need, if someone comes with a need, he should be present, this... if you want to fulfill it, 'Get this work done,' then there, in his form, and then after that, the other... this is... whoever fulfills the need of his brother, O Momin, if your need... if you have... he says, '...yada'u Allah... or Allah fulfills his need...' Allah fulfills his need. Or Allah fulfills his need, Allah's arrival... He will fulfill one hundred thousand of his needs, out of which the very first need will be Paradise. Paradise is the basic need. A human being works hard his whole life to go to Paradise. The Imam has given such a simple formula that help people, people... fulfill their needs, fulfill the needs of the Momineen. You should look at your relatives first, the closest relatives, then after that, other family members, even if they are not very close, then far, then after that, within his society, the Momineen, the Momineen who are there, then others, this is how it is, one has to look at all this, take care of this. It should not be that our brother is present in our house and we do social work in society. They are very good, or they cannot take care of their own house, they take care of their own benefit, and go and participate in the whole world, only... but when we have done such a big job, and after that, if someone... this is... 27, this is... look, they are giving... this is... I don't know to what extent... They are giving... this is... I don't know to what extent this is correct, we cannot issue a fatwa on this, that we say, issue a fatwa, then... where the matter is... so ask your Marja, is this correct or not? We can... but the intellect, the Aql, tells you that brother, if you are doing a favor to someone, then it should not be that he feels it, and he should not feel bad. That is why a tradition is found, where the Imam (a.s.) was simple, and he said, 'I am a traveler and my money is finished. If you give me some money, then as soon as I reach my homeland, I will return the money to you.' The Imam went inside, brought some money from inside, and after that, the Imam did not come in front of him. We heard from behind the curtain, 'O so-and-so, take the money, he has come, the Imam is... he has come in front of him, on that, the Imam gave the money. The Momin took it and left. Someone asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, you did not come in front of him?' The Imam said, 'I saw shame in his eyes, he was asking, so my conscience was not allowing me to make him embarrassed, to make him feel ashamed that I am taking money from him.' This is... Allah does not want, and we do not do any such favor, we don't even go... We don't do any such favor, we don't even go... in the whole world, it should be, we have so much, and if you want, and if you can do it, and they believe that the Imam... this is... so fulfill the needs of your brothers, O Allah, brother has become, fulfill the needs of the brothers, do not do a favor, and as much as is possible for you, keep doing favors to them, keep doing good behavior to them, this is the end of your Imam, and if you did not do this, if any Momin is coming to you, your brother is coming to you, and you can fulfill his need, whether you do something or through others, if you can do it, then do it, do it, Allah... For the sake of Ar-Rahman (The Most Gracious), where no one will help except Allah, keep helping your brothers as much as you can. This is why our Imam (a.s.) teaches us that one should be kind to their brothers. There should be a sense of realization that whatever we possess is from Allah, and Allah is testing us. Allah is the greatest provider, so this blessing you have received is a great favor from Him. Do not become arrogant because of these blessings. If it is going to the factory, then it is because it is coming from Allah. Alhamdulillah, one should express gratitude to Allah. Imam Hussain (a.s.) says, do not get tired of these blessings. This Momin (believer) who is bringing your own [needs] to you, Allah is sending His blessings to you through him. When you help them, Allah is showing mercy upon you. Allah will increase your wealth. You should keep giving, and see how much blessing there will be. Always treat your brothers with kindness and have mercy on them. Never be harsh, never be arrogant. Forgive them, pardon them. If you follow these two things, you will come to us, you will be at our door, you will be with us. And as you know, the spirit of sacrifice is the greatest thing. What is greater than a person giving their own life? But where does it happen? There is another sacrifice, and that is the sacrifice of one's young son. And that sacrifice was in Karbala. Imam Hussain (a.s.) gave that sacrifice, the likes of which history has no other example. It was Ashura, when Allah is the only One, and Hussain (a.s.) sacrificed everyone in the way of Allah. He sacrificed everyone in the way of Allah, until... come forward, come forward. Hussain (a.s.) prepared Akbar. Imam Hussain (a.s.) prepared Ali Akbar. Peace be upon Hussain (a.s.). Son, the time for your departure has come. No one is left now. The time has come, no one is left. Ali Akbar was happy. Imam Hussain (a.s.) prepared Ali Akbar, he made all the arrangements. It is not possible to describe it all. In short, when he prepared Ali Akbar and was helping him mount the horse, he looked towards the sky once and said, 'O Allah, bear witness that a youth is going to fight who, in his character, in his morals, in his personality, and in his face, resembled the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) the most.' He resembled the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) the most. When he would see Ali Akbar, he would see the Messenger of Allah. Imam Hussain (a.s.) asked, 'Ali Akbar, as you go towards the battlefield...' He felt a tug, he turned back and saw Ali Akbar holding his father's hand. 'Father, bid me farewell.' Hussain (a.s.) said, 'Son, if you had a father, you would know what the farewell of a young son means.' Ali Akbar went. Now, the situation was such that whoever went to the battlefield did not return alive, except for Ghazi (Abbas), who had returned to his mother. But Akbar... and why did it happen? It is a matter of the heart. If the color of your face changes, my heart stops. The color changed. 'O Hussain, what happened? Why has the color of your face changed? My father, I am going to fight, and I am three days hungry and thirsty...' I am three days hungry and thirsty. He was suffering. 'What should I do? If I had water, I would give it to you.' But Hussain (a.s.) was helpless. And what is this? He put his tongue in his mouth. The child became silent. 'Father, the dryness of the tongue is gone, the heaviness of the sword is gone, I have found water.' Hussain, O Hussain, there is no danger to my soul. Hussain, O Hussain, there is no danger to my soul. Now, as Akbar put his mouth to Hussain's, 'Father, you are young, you are thirsty, go son, now you will be served by your grandfather, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), you will be served by Ali al-Murtaza.' Ali Akbar went and kept fighting. The historian says that they surrounded Ali Akbar. One person struck him with a spear. The spear pierced him. Ali Akbar fell. Now, as he fell from the horse, the historian says, at this moment, 'Father, come to me, come to me!' They started cutting Ali Akbar into pieces with their swords. Hussain (a.s.) heard the voice. [Music] Hussain (a.s.) went to Ali Akbar, holding his back. He came to Ali Akbar, placed Ali Akbar's head on his lap, and pulled out the spear. A fountain of blood erupted. A fountain of blood erupted. Akbar, O Hussain, O Allah, this world is temporary, son. Your life was always meant to be from this world... and your status is high. The enemies have done this. O Allah, keep the believers safe. O Allah, remove the difficulties of those who are in trouble. Grant health to those who are ill. This disease that has spread, protect us all from it. Protect us all from it. By the mercy of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). One prayer... O Lord, O Lord of the worlds, for those who are in this world, and for those who have passed away...
Ithar is defined as the noble act of prioritizing the comfort and needs of others above one's own.
True Ihsan requires unconditional benevolence that extends to all living beings, including animals.
The Ahl al-Bayt serve as the ultimate moral exemplars for self-sacrifice and devotion to Allah.
Fulfilling the needs of a believer is described as being equivalent to a lifetime of worship.
Charity should be performed with discretion to preserve the dignity of the recipient.

excerpt: This lecture explores the profound connection between Imam Ali (a.s.) and the concept of truth, emphasizing the prophetic tradition that truth always follows him. The speaker highlights a teaching from the Fifth Imam (a.s.) asserting that any ideology or action not originating from the Ahlulbayt is inherently false. The talk concludes by urging believers to remain steadfast at the threshold of the Prophet's household to ensure they remain aligned with the truth.
content:
Meaning, look, you keep hearing this constantly, and even our children here remember this Hadith: 'Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with Ali.' And the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) prayed, 'O Allah, turn the truth in the direction that Ali turns; wherever Ali goes, turn the truth in that direction.' Now, how did the Fifth Imam (a.s.) further clarify this? The Imam says, 'Kullu ma lam yakhruj min hadha al-bayt fahuwa batil' (Everything that has not emerged from this house is falsehood). The Imam says that look, every single thing—whether it is a statement, an action, a thought, or an ideology—anything at all, if it has not emerged from this house—the Fifth Imam pointed to his house—then it is falsehood. The Imam has concluded every matter here. Now, whenever you want to see where the truth lies, just see what has emerged from their house. That is all. Now, if we also want to be with the truth, we must keep our heads bowed in submission at that very threshold; we must keep our heads lowered at their door, at the threshold of their house. Truth comes from there, and if we want the truth to be with us and for us to be with the truth, then we must remain at their threshold. We must hold onto their hem. That is the only truth. Apart from that, even if you separate yourself from there for a single moment, for a single instant, then you are with falsehood. [Music] Rashida.

title: Imam Hasan Askari (a.s.) ka aakhri waqt kaisa tha? | 8th Rabi ul-Awwal | Shahadat
excerpt: This lecture details the final moments of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) on the 8th of Rabi al-Awwal, 260 Hijri. It describes his physical state due to the effects of poison, his performance of Wudu and Fajr prayer while bedridden, and the presence of his son, Imam-e-Zamana (ajf). The account highlights the solemnity of his passing and his subsequent burial within his own home.
content:
What was the final moment of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) like? It is narrated by Muhammad ibn Husayn ibn Abbas. The martyrdom of Abu Muhammad, Hazrat Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), occurred on Friday at the time of Fajr prayer. That night, he had written and sent many letters to Medina with his own hand. And this was the date of 8th Rabi al-Awwal, 260 Hijri. At that time, only his maid Saqil and his servant Aqib were with him. And besides those two, there was someone present whom only Allah knows—that is, his son, Imam-e-Zamana (ajlallahu ta'ala farajah al-sharif). This shows how necessary it was to keep the personality of Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.) in occultation at that time. It is stated that the Imam (a.s.) asked for water that had been boiled with mastic. It was a type of perfume or something used in treatment. We brought that water and presented it to the Imam (a.s.). He (a.s.) said, 'I have to pray. Help me perform Wudu.' I brought some items to the Imam (a.s.) and spread a handkerchief on his lap. The Imam (a.s.) took water from Saqil and washed his face and both arms once, and performed Masah of his head and both feet. The Imam (a.s.) offered Fajr prayer on his bed. Then he picked up the cup to drink water, but the cup began to strike against his blessed teeth because there was a tremor in his hands—that is, his hands were shaking. That is, the Imam (a.s.) The effect of the poison given to the Imam (a.s.) was so deep that the Imam (a.s.) was not even able to get up to perform Wudu himself. He offered prayer on the bed, and his hands had become so weak that they were trembling. Then, as soon as the maid Saqil took the cup from his hand, the martyrdom of the Imam (a.s.) occurred. May Allah's blessings be upon him, and then the Imam (a.s.) was buried in his own house.

excerpt: This lecture explores the profound theological significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm and its role in the perfection of the Islamic faith. content:
We hope that you all are well, and we pray that Allah keeps us all safe from all calamities and diseases, and also grants us the ability to firmly hold onto the strong rope of Allah, the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Before we begin this episode, we hope that you participated in yesterday's special episode of Ghadir. If not, you can click on the link to this eighth episode now, or tomorrow, or whenever you wish, to provide the correct answers to all the questions. By clicking on the link, you can provide the correct answers to all their questions because we will be waiting for your answers until our final episode. And the winner of the Ziyarat of this series will be declared with all the dignity of the Imam (a.s.) upon the conclusion of our series. So let us begin the new episode of 'Ahamiyat-e-Ghadir' (The Importance of Ghadir). Yes, what is the importance of Ghadir? How valuable is Ghadir? Let us see what the traditions and Quranic verses tell us about Ghadir. To answer this, our brother Syed Qasim is with us. Peace be upon you. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. First of all, I would like to offer congratulations to all the viewers on the occasion of Eid-e-Ghadir. With Salawat, Allahumma Salli 'ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad, I would like to start today's discussion by placing my feet on the chest of the enemies of Ghadir. The importance of Ghadir is not understood by eyes, but by insights. It is not understood by eyes, but by insights. Like the cities of the world, the journey of breaths may end, but the journey of the rights and virtues of Ghadir and Sahib-e-Ghadir can never end. Regarding the importance, there are countless traditions from the Masumeen (a.s.). If you believe, then there is reward; if you do not believe, then there are countless curses, because we do not show any leniency regarding the name of Ali (a.s.). There is no compromise on our family and our belief. It is a big deal that some people do not like it. Some people do not like me because I am a lover of Ali (a.s.). So, Hassan bhai, let me present a tradition from Imam Reza (a.s.) regarding the importance of Ghadir before you and the viewers. It is a very old tradition, and I would like to present a part of it, in which Imam Reza (a.s.) is saying, 'I swear by Allah, if people knew the reality of the virtues of this day—the reality of the virtues of the day of Ghadir—' If they knew the reality of the virtues of the day of Ghadir, then what would happen? The angels would shake hands with them ten times a day. It is not just once in a lifetime; the tradition says the angels visit the believer ten times a day because they are familiar with the reality of Ghadir and shake hands with them. So, the virtue of Ghadir is great here, and it is not just about traditions; the virtue of Ghadir is found in the Quran as well. If we look towards the Quran, the importance and virtue of Ghadir appear through the verses of the Quran. As we see in the verse of 'Baligh', if this had not been conveyed, then where else could we highlight the importance of Ghadir? Allah (swt) is saying to His beloved Messenger, 'O Messenger, all your tasks are on one side, and the message of Ghadir is on the other.' This verse itself points towards the importance of Ghadir, that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—how many tasks of his life were on one side— How many tasks of his life were on one side, and the message of Ghadir on the other? Let us look at that verse again. It is being revealed with majesty, and the verse is 'Ya ayyuhar-rasulu balligh ma unzila ilayka mir-rabbik...'. Here, Allah (swt) is addressing His Messenger, His beloved, regarding his designation. He is not calling him 'Ya Muzzammil' or 'Ya Muddathir', but 'Ya Ayyuhar-Rasul'. The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) cannot be distinguished here because, in the Quran, among all the titles, the one most pointed towards the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is that Muhammad is nothing but a Messenger. But still, Allah (swt) called His Messenger by different names on different occasions. Sometimes He called him Taha, sometimes Muzzammil, sometimes Muddathir, sometimes Sirajan Munira, and sometimes the name of the Messenger of Allah was given. But here, Allah (swt) is calling His beloved Messenger by his designation to convey the message. By calling him by his designation, He is commanding him to convey the message to the Ummah. And after that, if you look at the sentence, He immediately said, 'Balligh' (Convey). Convey what? The Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). He is commanding the conveyance. So, if the Ummah had continued to convey this message to the world after the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)—just as the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) conveyed the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) in the field of Ghadir—then the amount of disagreement we see among the Ummah today would not be there. And we see that along with the command, Allah is also saying that if you do not convey this, you have not conveyed anything. That is, the message is nothing but the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). If emphasis was placed on anything, it was for the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). And the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) is also found in this regard: 'Law ijtama'an-nasu 'ala hubbi 'Aliyyin la-ma khalaqallahu jahannam' (If all people had gathered on the love of Ali, Allah would not have created Hell). Allah would not have created Hell. From here, it becomes clear that if all people had understood the message of Ghadir, if they had understood the importance of Ghadir, then no one would have gone to Hell. From here, we understand the importance of Ghadir. At the same time, this is the reason why if you have everything—fasting, prayer, Hajj, Zakat—but you do not have the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), then your destination is nothing but Hell. Friends, it is a matter of great surprise and great regret that the Ummah researches the smallest of things. They research small things, but the thing about which it is said, 'If you did not do this, you did nothing,' for 1400 years, the Ummah has not been able to research what that thing was, about which Allah is telling His Messenger, 'If you do not convey this, you have conveyed nothing.' This clearly shows the importance of Ghadir. The importance of Ghadir is becoming clear, how much importance Ghadir holds in Islam. Now, let me present the second verse, when the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) among the people with his pure tongue, saying 'Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha 'Aliyyun mawlahu', after that this verse comes, Jibra'il (a.s.) brings it— Jibra'il (a.s.) brings it, and what is that verse? The verse of 'Ikmal'. 'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum wa atmamtu 'alaykum ni'mati wa radhitu lakumul-islama dina'. 'Today I have perfected your religion for you, and completed My favor upon you, and I have chosen Islam as your religion.' If we look at this verse in three aspects: in the first part, there is talk of the religion being perfected—'Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum'—that today the religion is being perfected. In the second part, the second part of this verse, there is talk of the favor being completed—'wa atmamtu 'alaykum ni'mati'—that today I have completed the favors. And in the final part, the final part of this verse, it is saying that today I am pleased that Islam is the religion. Now, we want to ask the Ummah: they are very proud of their prayers, very proud of their fasts, very proud of their Hajj, that they will get them salvation. If they do not consider the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) as part of the religion, then how will those acts of the Ummah be accepted, which were performed before this announcement? Before this announcement of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) in the valley of Khumm, if you pay attention, the court of Allah was established. It was not just about distributing Zakat or charity; this year, it was everything. The Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) was not just any ordinary Wilayah. This announcement was so important that before this, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had conveyed all the commands of Allah to the people, but this announcement is saying that if you do not convey this, if you do not announce the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), then you have not performed any duty at all. We can see in the Quran that until the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is included in the religion, the religion is not worthy of being called a religion. The religion of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) is not complete until the announcement of the Imamate and Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is made. Secondly, until the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is included, the greatest blessing that Allah has bestowed upon us is not complete, and that is nothing but the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Along with this, we also saw that Allah is not pleased until our tongues, our hearts, and our souls are in agreement. Yes, this meaning is with the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Regarding the time, it is not just this, but regarding the last verse of Surah al-Takathur, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) asked the people, 'Will you be questioned about the blessings?' By Allah, it is not about food and water; people will be asked about the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). The Quran has completed the blessings, and on the other hand, it is emphasizing the blessings. If you are asking what this blessing of Islam is, it will be questioned. It is not about food and drink; rather, it is about the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Let us listen to the verse 83 of Surah al-Nahl regarding this. Regarding verse 83 of Surah al-Nahl, let me present a Hadith before you. In verse 83 of Surah al-Nahl, it is clearly stated: 'They recognize the blessing of Allah, and then they deny it.' It was asked to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), 'What is this blessing that people recognize and then deny?' He replied, 'It is us.' Meaning, they knew about the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). People recognized the blessing of Allah, and that blessing was the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and then they denied it. Similarly, if you look at the famous Hadith of Imam al-Baqir (a.s.), where the Imam (a.s.) explained the foundation of Islam based on five things, saying that Islam is built upon five pillars. It is built upon five pillars. In the final part of that Hadith, if you look, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'And the call was made for Wilayah just as it was made for other things.' And if you look at the end of that Hadith, it says, 'People took all other things but abandoned the Wilayah.' If you look at that verse, you will see that most people became disbelievers regarding the Wilayah. In this Hadith, you see that most people abandoned the Wilayah. And in the same way, the Imam (a.s.) says, 'I am the religion that was denied.' And not only this, but there is a series of Hadith where the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) expressed his attributes: 'I am the Dhikr (remembrance) of Allah that was denied; I am the path (Sabil) that people deviated from; I am the blessing (Ni'mah) that was denied; I am the Quran that people abandoned; I am the religion (Deen) that was rejected; and I am the path (Sirat) that people will fall into Hell for rejecting.' Here, the Imam (a.s.) has... Here, the Imam (a.s.) has expressed his attributes: I am the truth, I am the path, I am the faith, I am the religion, I am the Sirat. 'Today I have perfected your religion for you'—and this perfection was through the Wilayah, in which the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is found. And here the Imam (a.s.) says, 'I am the religion that was denied,' meaning the true religion was denied. People forgot the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Here you can see how people denied the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). But I would also like to say that if the entire universe together denies Ali (a.s.), it does not harm Ali (a.s.) in the slightest. And if the entire universe together accepts him, it does not add anything to Ali (a.s.). If we accept Ali (a.s.), it is for our own benefit; it is for our own Paradise. There is a Hadith that I must present before you, which Imam al-Rida (a.s.) narrated, which is a very powerful Hadith. The Imam (a.s.) says, 'The example of one who acknowledges the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) is like the angels who prostrated before Adam (a.s.).' And the Imam (a.s.) does not stop there; he continues, 'And the example of those who denied the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) is like Iblis (Satan).' This shows that becoming a believer and a Muslim is one thing, but denying the Wilayah makes one like Iblis. From these Hadith, we understand that if you do not understand the importance of Wilayah, then the person who does this is with that Satan. As I mentioned, just as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, this is a Hadith from the book of Allamah Majlisi. It says, 'O Ali, if someone worships Allah for as long as the people of Nuh (a.s.) lived—not 12 years, but for as many years as the people of Nuh lived—and not only that, but if he spends gold equal to the mountain of Uhud in the way of Allah—not silver, but gold equal to the mountain of Uhud—and performs a thousand Hajj...' And performs a thousand Hajj in his lifetime, and not just that, but is killed between Safa and Marwa while in a state of oppression—meaning he is martyred—then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'O Ali, if he does not have your Wilayah, if your Wilayah is not in his heart, then he will not even smell the fragrance of Paradise, let alone enter it.' This shows that even if a person spends his entire life in worship, spends gold equal to the mountain of Uhud, performs a thousand Hajj, and is martyred between Safa and Marwa, if he does not have the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) in his heart, he will not even smell the fragrance of Paradise. We can see that there are so many traditions and verses that explain the importance of the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). So, what are our responsibilities? The most important responsibility that I see, which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) mentioned, is that it is obligatory upon every person present to convey this to those who are absent. It is the duty of every human being to convey this to their children, their family, and their friends. To their children, their family, their friends, and to all those they can reach. As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, if you do not convey this, then you have not performed your duty. A person may perform all other acts, but if they do not convey this, they have failed. We should keep mentioning this to our coming generations and to everyone we meet. Our team's effort is to convey the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) to the whole world through these videos. If you are watching our videos, you should watch them yourself and also share them with those who are not watching. Tell them that the Wilayah of Ahlulbayt (a.s.) is being discussed here. The second thing I want to present is about the perfection of religion. As we discussed, there is a Hadith from the Imams (a.s.) that says religion is perfected not just by Wilayah, but by disavowal (Bara'ah) from our enemies. If we are to receive guidance from the Bara'ah (disassociation) of our enemies, then we must perform both tasks: along with Wilayah, we must perform Bara'ah from the enemies of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) and all the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). If someone claims that they hold Wilayah but tries to deceive us by saying they love the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) very much, understand that as long as they do not perform Bara'ah from the enemies of Ali (a.s.), the enemies of Janab-e-Zahra (s.a.), and all the enemies of the Aal-e-Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), they do not possess the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.). Wherever the mention of your killers arises, it compels us to mourn. So, dear viewers, just as we make arrangements for the Azadari of Abdullah al-Husayn (a.s.) in the coming days, we should also make arrangements for Ghadir. We should celebrate this entire month as the 'Month of Wilayah', and making the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) known to all is our great responsibility, because if people do not remember Ghadir... Because if people do not remember Ghadir, then Karbala would not have happened. So, just as we make arrangements for the Azadari of Abdullah al-Husayn (a.s.), we should make arrangements for Ghadir. As the poet beautifully said: 'He saw the chest of Akbar and saved Wilayah; ask Husayn (a.s.) the price of Ghadir.' It is not enough to just express grief—everyone reaches the mourning—rather, we should also express joy. Beyond our other programs, we should celebrate this Ghadir-e-Akbar with much greater fervor. I am very grateful to you for explaining the importance of Ghadir through so many narrations and verses in such simple language. So, dear viewers, if we were to summarize the essence of all these narrations and verses in one sentence, it is enough to say that there is nothing more important to Allah than the Ghadir or the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and likewise, the most important task in our lives should be to convey the Ghadir and the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) to all people. Conveying the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) to all people should be our priority. So, let us end this episode here, but before we finish, let me remind you that the quiz for this episode will go live. I request you to participate in this quiz and try to answer all the questions correctly. We will be back soon with the next episode; until then, goodbye.

title: Kareem-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.) Ka Karam | Imam Hasan (a.s.) Aur Ek Zaeefa Ka Waaqeya
excerpt: This lecture recounts the profound generosity of Imam Hasan (a.s.), Imam Husayn (a.s.), and Abdullah ibn Ja'far toward an elderly woman who hosted them during their Hajj journey. Despite having only one goat, the woman sacrificed it to feed the travelers, who later rewarded her kindness with immense wealth. The story illustrates the unparalleled character of the Ahl al-Bayt and their habit of reciprocating small acts of service with extraordinary abundance.
content:
Imam Hasan (a.s.), Imam Husayn (a.s.), and Janab-e-Abdullah ibn Ja'far were on the Hajj pilgrimage. While they were traveling, their provisions ran out. Due to the lack of provisions, they were overcome by hunger and thirst. On the way, they saw some worn-out tents, and an old woman was present there. They asked this woman for water and expressed their intense thirst. The woman pointed towards a water skin, and they quenched their thirst. After that, they expressed their hunger. The woman said, 'I have nothing except this goat. One of you should go and slaughter this goat so that I can cook it for you.' As the woman requested, the goat was slaughtered, and she cooked it for them. After being satisfied, they thanked the woman and said, 'When we return to Medina after Hajj, you should come to Medina, and we wish to show our generosity to you,' because that woman had done a favor to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Because that woman had done a favor to the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), these generous individuals wanted to repay her kindness. It is a very interesting story of how they repaid this favor or how they rewarded this woman. When these generous individuals left, her husband arrived. He saw that the only asset they had in that house—that goat—the woman had spent it for the sake of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). Her husband scolded her and was angry, and since they had nothing else in that desert—just a worn-out tent and a goat—their condition was deteriorating, and they were facing hardship. So, the woman decided to go to Medina to meet the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.). When she reached Medina, Imam Hasan (a.s.) recognized her, and Imam Hasan (a.s.) gave her 1,000 goats and 1,000 dinars in exchange for one goat. Imam Hasan (a.s.) returned 1,000 goats and gave her 1,000 dinars; her tent wasn't even big enough to hold these goats. If it were you or me, we would think that if one person has given, that is enough. But the generosity of Imam Hasan (a.s.) does not end there. He wrote a letter and sent it through a messenger to Imam Husayn (a.s.), asking him to reward this woman. When this woman reached Imam Husayn (a.s.), he also gave her 1,000 goats and 1,000 dinars. So, in exchange for one goat, she received 2,000 goats and 2,000 dinars. Imam Husayn (a.s.) did the same as Imam Hasan (a.s.). Imam Husayn (a.s.) sent the messenger to Janab-e-Abdullah ibn Ja'far, and he also gave her 1,000 goats and 1,000 dinars. This is the generosity of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.): if a person, even though they had nothing, sacrificed their only possession in the path of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.), in return for this sacrifice, the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) rewarded her so much that she could barely manage it. It is the height of generosity; for the people of the world, it is the limit, but for them, it is nothing extraordinary.
The Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) were traveling for Hajj when they encountered an elderly woman in the desert.
The woman sacrificed her only possession, a goat, to feed the hungry travelers.
Imam Hasan (a.s.) rewarded her with 1,000 goats and 1,000 dinars upon her arrival in Medina.
Imam Husayn (a.s.) and Abdullah ibn Ja'far also provided equal rewards, multiplying her initial sacrifice.
The total reward for one goat was 3,000 goats and 3,000 dinars.
The story highlights the extreme generosity and appreciation of the Ahl al-Bayt for those who serve them.
True generosity, as demonstrated by the Imams, goes far beyond the initial value of the favor received.

title: 🕋 JASHN E AAMAD E MURTAZA (a.s.)  |  Mahdiyyah Imambargah  |  Taqreer: Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi, delivered at Mahdiyyah Imambargah, celebrates the miraculous birth of Imam Ali (a.s.) inside the Kaaba and explores his profound spiritual status. The discourse emphasizes that the love and Wilayah of Imam Ali (a.s.) are the essential foundations of true faith and divine guidance. Dr. Rizvi highlights the importance of unwavering commitment to these principles, warning against compromising core beliefs for worldly convenience. The session concludes with a call for believers to maintain a 'Qalb-e-Saleem' and remain steadfast in their devotion to the Ahlulbayt.
content:
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and upon Fatimah al-Zahra (s.a.), the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). O Allah, send blessings upon Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), the Commander of the Faithful, and upon the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you. O Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you. Peace be upon you all. I welcome the honorable guests and the scholars who have arrived. I extend my congratulations to all of you on this auspicious occasion. If you have accepted these congratulations, then please recite Salawat. I do not say this because I am someone important, but because it is a duty. I request the brothers in the back to please come forward and fill the empty spaces. As you move forward, please recite Salawat. This gathering is very beautiful and honorable. It is very beautiful and honorable. The scholars who have arrived include Dr. Chauraha Faizabadi, Janab Mashhoor Danapuri, Professor Gramin Mohammadi, and Janab Syed Ali Abbas Rizvi Banarasi. They will all present their tributes. Without taking much of your time, as per our tradition, we begin our programs with the recitation of Naat-e-Pak. I request the two doctors to please take their seats. I will present four lines. I searched the world, but found nothing like Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). I searched the world, but found nothing like Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). Furthermore, when Fatima bint-e-Asad (s.a.) entered the Kaaba, it was a great miracle. I will present four lines for you. Peace be upon you, and Eid Mubarak. It is a matter of the heart; I need your support. Whatever decision is made, it should be just. Whatever the situation, the one who is the master is the one who decides. I was so restless that I could not wait. You are watching this on WhatsApp. It is a wonderful program. After the recitation, we will proceed with the scholarly discussion. When the child was born, the Kaaba was illuminated. It is said that the walls of the Kaaba split open. The one who is the master of the universe has arrived. The one who is the commander of the faithful has arrived. On the occasion of the birth of Imam Ali (a.s.), I extend my congratulations to you all. A thought came to my mind: are you afraid of the lions? Ali (a.s.) is the one who resides within the walls of the Kaaba. Who can question your bravery? Even the word 'Shahadat' (martyrdom) feels honored by your name. Your majesty and glory are unmatched. You are the lion of Allah. It is your choice whose name you take, but if you want to be purified, say 'Ali'. Everyone has said that your destiny will be brightened by saying 'Ali'. The walls of the Kaaba testify that whoever accepts Ali (a.s.) will have their prayers accepted. Your life will be free from darkness if you follow Ali (a.s.). The remembrance of Ali (a.s.) is the worship of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). The remembrance of Ali (a.s.) is the worship of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). By God, you will attain honor if you remember Ali (a.s.). In the life of Ali (a.s.), there is guidance. If you follow his path, you will find the truth. The followers of the Imam are gathered here today to celebrate. The followers of the Imam are gathered here today. He made the Kaaba his home and brought Haider (a.s.) into the world. He showed us how to live with dignity. Even when the door was closed, the remembrance of Ali (a.s.) continued. He invited us to his presence. The path of Ali (a.s.) is the path of truth. The path of Ali (a.s.) is the path of truth. Today, we are gathered here to celebrate this auspicious occasion. The scholars are present, and we are grateful for their presence. Gratitude to God. Today, the atmosphere is filled with divine light. I request the audience to move forward and fill the gaps so that the program can proceed in the traditional manner. May Allah bless you all. Here it means that a man who rides once, does not ride the second time, and looks at the Mustahab and runs away. Or it means that it takes a big heart to attack the Bid'ah. That is also in the Hadith. Every 'Ibtila' (trial) is for the Ma'sum (infallible), it is... In the Hadith, every 'Ibtila' is for the Ma'sum, it is... the name of the companion, I have brought it, he cannot do it, he cannot bear it. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is the one who is the closest, he can bear it. My Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is the guide, he can bear it. The one who is 'Mumtaz' (distinguished), whose test has been taken, only he can bear it. When the companion heard this, he got scared, 'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) cannot bear it, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) cannot bear it, then who can bear it?' 'Whom We wish.' [Praise]... This is our gift, which we will give. If he does not want to give it, he prays, he does anything, he keeps doing the right thing, he dies, these people of the world... Anyway, only Allah knows what his final destination will be. [Praise]... Just this, that you see, when the mention of Wilayah is made, when the mention of Reliance is made, then how is the face? And more than that, when the enemy of Ali (a.s.) is mentioned, the heart is happy. [Praise]... The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says, 'No one can force it, except the one whose heart Allah has illuminated.' That chest, that chest which Allah has illuminated, that heart which Allah has illuminated, that liver which Allah has kept safe. The words are 'Sudur', 'Qulub', 'Af'idah'... but the words used are 'Qalb-e-Saleem'. What is this? It is taken from the Quran: 'Illa man atallaha bi qalbin saleem' (Except he who comes to Allah with a sound heart). That... Comes with a Qalb-e-Saleem. That Qalb-e-Saleem... when asked, 'What is Qalb-e-Saleem?', it is that heart in which there is not even an atom's weight of doubt about the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.)... [Praise]... And the second big thing is, how is this possible? How is it possible? Very little... and this claim, this thing, is that... do not say this. They will not be able to solve it. The one who cannot bear it, let him sit, do not be too persistent. And if in the previous times, this matter... and the friends, they are experts because Allah had taken our covenant in the realm of 'Alam-e-Dharr'. Whoever fulfilled the covenant there, whoever showed loyalty there, then in this world, His grace was upon him. And whoever showed you... and our... And whoever showed you... and did not fulfill our right, then he will die hungry in Hell. Send a Salawat upon Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) and his family. [Praise]... This is the second thing, which is from the tongue of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Send a Salawat upon Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)... When the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'I have been given the pride of all the Prophets, and I have been preferred over all the Prophets, and Allah has honored me through the Holy Quran, and through Ali (a.s.), Allah has honored me.' So, 'I have been honored.' And Ali (a.s.) is the leader... 'If you do not recognize Allah, then you are a stranger.' Ali (a.s.) is the one whom Allah has praised. He (the Prophet) praised me, saying that Allah has bestowed upon me such a blessing without me even asking. He said, 'O Muhammad, how should I express gratitude for this?' I asked, 'O Prophet of Allah, how should I express my gratitude?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was teaching us, for although he knew, he was explaining it for our benefit. He asked, 'How should I express my gratitude for the Islam that Allah has bestowed upon us?' The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) replied, 'O Muhammad, listen carefully, and listen quickly, for this is the way to express gratitude for the blessing of Islam.' The way to express gratitude for this blessing is to treat your brother—this brother of yours—with kindness. As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was asked, 'What is the best way to express gratitude?'—obviously, if they hadn't asked, no one would have known. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) was showing us the way. Allah replied, 'O Muhammad, tell them to spread this, spread this among the people.' This is the gratitude for the blessing of Wilayah, the blessing of Allah. Tell all the people to be united. Even if they are in their homes, they should be united. This is the command of my Lord. My servants should express gratitude for this blessing. We are currently in a state where we have enmity with our own people and are seeking friendship with strangers. That is why I have been saying for 12 or 14 years that these are our principles. When people asked, 'How will this happen? Will they be hostile toward our principles?' I said, 'For the sake of friendship with the people, Allah is giving you the path. O people, O nation, O followers of the path, you must improve yourselves.' You must all realize that Allah, the Almighty, wants love—love for Him and Him alone. We should love for the sake of Allah. And if we hate anyone, it should only be based on Wilayah. This is the standard: Wilayah is the standard for hatred, and Wilayah is the standard for love. If you oppose anyone, it should only be for the sake of Wilayah. And you must declare that you are with the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) and oppose those who oppose the Wilayah. There should be no compromise on this, whether it is a businessman or anyone else. There should be no compromise on this. Whether it is a businessman or anyone else, that is fine, but when it comes to principles, when it comes to Wilayah, there is no compromise. I was telling you about history; I have already told you that in history, in Baghdad, they were only one percent. History shows they were only one percent, but they had such courage and such a leader that they had no fear. They were only one percent, but they held the entire area. Whenever there was a big occasion, they would put up a banner and write on it: 'La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah, Aliyun Waliullah, Wasiyyu Rasulillah, wa Khalifatuhu bila fasl.' Look, they were only one percent, but they were not afraid. They were not afraid of what people would say or what would happen to them. We are answering those who say, 'Why do you do this? They will remove the phrase 'Khalifatuhu bila fasl' (the successor without interval).' We have no objection to that; it is the truth. But the people there, the moderate ones, said, 'You don't understand. If you do this, such and such will happen, and so many people will be killed.' We are facing the same problem today. They are saying, 'You are sitting here and talking, while people are being killed there.' But listen to what the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said: 'In Paradise, there is a station for the followers of Ali (a.s.) where even the common people will reach, but the great scholars...' Even the common people will reach there, but the great scholars... for the followers of Ali (a.s.), there is a station. Some will reach there, but the great scholars... you understand, you understand. Everyone will be happy. Even the common people will reach there. So, when the pressure is high, the youth said, 'Okay, we will reach there.' This is history, the history of the year 440 AH, the history of Baghdad, the time of Sheikh Tusi. Sheikh Tusi had to leave; he was forced to leave. This is history, and we should not compromise on it. Let's leave it here and tell you a short story so that things become clear for you to make decisions. To make things clear for you to make decisions: There was a rooster that used to crow in the morning. The neighbors didn't like it and said, 'Don't crow, it disturbs our sleep.' The rooster said, 'Okay, I won't crow.' Then, after a few days, they demanded, 'Make a sound like a hen.' The rooster said, 'Okay, I will make a sound like a hen.' Then their demands increased, and they said, 'Stop all your sounds, and if you don't, we will kill you.' The rooster thought, 'If I had been martyred for the sake of Allah, I would have been a martyr.' But he compromised, and he was killed anyway. This is the same history, the same 'Khalifatuhu bila fasl'. This is the same history. You should also remove that. They say, 'Life is precious, Allah and the Messenger are there, let it go.' Then they showed them everything, and after that, they attacked, and everything was destroyed, except for the books. Even Sheikh Tusi had to leave. This is history. When you read it, you will understand. I am telling you briefly. When you read the details, you will see. So, this is the entire situation. Never compromise on principles. If someone says, 'This is this, that is that,' listen, but Wilayah is the red line. You can say anything else, but Wilayah is the red line. You cannot cross it. Everything else is fine, we are ready to do whatever you want, but this is enough. This is how it happened. Now come to the point. We ask Allah to grant us the grace to follow the Wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and his infallible progeny. May Allah hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), grant him a long life, and may He fulfill the needs of all those who are in distress, those who are far from their homes, and all the believers.

title: Ahkaam | Session # 6 | Laws & Etiquette of Fasting
excerpt: This lecture addresses common practical questions regarding the laws and etiquette of fasting during the month of Ramadan. Maulana Zulfiqar Ali provides guidance on medical procedures like root canals, grooming, and the rules surrounding the obligatory prostration (Sajdah) during Quran recitation. The session emphasizes the importance of caution to ensure that nothing is swallowed during these activities to maintain the validity of the fast.
content:
Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. Today, in this program, we welcome all our viewers. First of all, congratulations on the arrival of the blessed month of Ramadan. The month of Ramadan is a blessed month from Allah. It is a month of reception, a month in which the gates of heaven and mercy are opened, and the gates of hell are closed. In this month, there is a night in which worship is better than a thousand months. So, friends, in this month, Allah has bestowed blessings and rewards. We should certainly spend every moment of this month in the worship of Allah and in seeking closeness to Him. May Allah grant us the ability to make the most of this month. Now, we proceed to the questions you have asked, which will be answered by the respected Maulana Zulfiqar Ali Sahab. Let us once again turn to him with your questions. Peace be upon you, Maulana. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you. How are you? I am well, thank you. How are you? May Allah keep you safe. Tell me, are you well? May Allah keep you safe. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The first question is: Can dental treatments like a root canal be performed while fasting? If the treatment is necessary, and I say it is necessary because you should not suffer, then you may undergo the treatment. If you proceed with the treatment while being careful that the doctor does not put too much water or liquid in your mouth, and you ensure it does not go down your throat, you may do it. However, if I were to do it, I would ensure nothing goes down. But if you cannot guarantee that, then you should not do it. Especially if you are undergoing treatment... Especially if you are undergoing treatment, a root canal will definitely cause some bleeding. One thing is that, and the other is that you must be sure that nothing will go down your throat. If you are sure, you can proceed. But if you are afraid, you should not do it, as it might weaken your fast. So, if these two conditions are met—that you are sure no blood will be swallowed and nothing will go down your throat—then you may proceed, and your fast will not be invalidated. Now, what if we were sure in the first instance that nothing would go down, but during the root canal, something did go down? In that situation, what should be done? If it went down, and you were sure with certainty... You were sure with certainty. Let us present the next question to you: Is it permissible to trim one's beard or groom one's face while fasting? Is there any problem with that? No, there is no problem with that. You can do it; it does not affect the fast. Thank you very much. The next question we have received is regarding the recitation of the Quran. During the recitation of the Quran, if a verse of Sajdah (prostration) is recited, should the prostration be performed? And what are the conditions for it? What happens during it? The verses of the obligatory Sajdah in the Quran are four: Surah Najm, Surah Al-Alaq, Surah As-Sajdah, and Surah Fussilat. Secondly, regarding the conditions you asked about, listen carefully. First, one must have the intention of the obligatory Sajdah because one has recited the Quran. The intention is necessary. Second, when you perform the Sajdah, you should place your forehead on the ground. Third, the place where you place your forehead must be a place where one can perform Sajdah. And the fourth condition is that the place where you place your forehead must be level with where your knees and toes are placed. These are the four conditions. Now, after that, some scholars say that besides the forehead, other parts of the body should also be in the position of Sajdah. It is also a rule that when performing the Sajdah, you must place your forehead on the ground. Your knees and toes must also be in the position of Sajdah. Now, what should be recited? You should recite the Zikr of Sajdah, such as 'Subhanallah' or 'Astaghfirullah' or 'Subhana Rabbi al-A'la wa bi hamdihi'. If you do not remember this prayer, then you can recite 'La ilaha illallah'. This is what you should recite. And one thing, although you did not ask about age... Although you did not ask about age, I will tell you that for the Sajdah of recitation, it is not necessary to have Wudu, nor is it necessary to face the Qibla. And should one perform the Sajdah immediately? Yes, one should perform it immediately. Another thing is that it is not necessary to cover one's private parts or for a woman to cover her hair or body for this Sajdah. It is also not necessary that the forehead be placed on the earth; it can be on anything else. If you are unable to perform it, you can do it later. You can do it later. You cannot say that my condition is missed. It is not necessary to do it immediately. If you are traveling on a train or in Mumbai, and you hear the verse, and you are not listening but reading, and the verse is recited, then in a state of necessity, you should perform the Sajdah. Thank you very much, Maulana. The fourth question that has come to us is: Can one brush their teeth before the fast? Can one brush their teeth before the fast, and at what time can it be done? Brushing is allowed. When you are brushing, as the child said, if you are going to the doctor, then you should be careful. If you are working with caution, I will use toothpaste or a brush, but I will ensure that nothing goes down my throat. If you are sure, you can do it. But after brushing, when you rinse... After brushing, if some toothpaste remains and mixes with your saliva, it is not a major issue; it is a very small amount. However, children in big cities often eat the toothpaste instead of brushing. This is not correct. You should not use the excuse of brushing to swallow the substances present in the toothpaste. We are very grateful to the respected guest and would like to inform you that to ask questions, you can reach us on our WhatsApp number. We are very thankful that you are continuously answering all the questions in our program. In response to the questions, we now bid farewell to our guest. In the next episode, we will cover the remaining material.
Root canals are permissible if necessary, provided no blood or liquid is swallowed.
Trimming a beard or grooming does not invalidate a fast.
There are four specific verses in the Quran that require an obligatory Sajdah.
The Sajdah of recitation does not require Wudu, facing the Qibla, or specific clothing.
Brushing teeth is allowed, but one must be extremely careful not to swallow toothpaste or water.
The Sajdah of recitation should be performed as soon as possible, though it can be delayed if necessary.
