title: EP03 | Quran Ka Mufassir Kaun Hai? |  ITMAAM-E-HUJJAT
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of a divine interpreter for the Quran, emphasizing that the text requires a 'Qayyim'—an infallible leader—to serve as its true proof. It argues that while the Quran provides the foundation, the Ahlulbayt possess the inherent, divine knowledge required to interpret it correctly. By contrasting the limitations of human intellect with the unique status of Imam Ali, the session establishes the concept of Itmaam-e-Hujjat, asserting that the earth is never devoid of a divinely appointed guide.
content:
Haidar, Haidar... [repeated]... Ashhadu anna Aliyan Waliullah. A'udhu billahi as-sami'il alim min ash-shaytanir rajim. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alamin, wal 'aqibatu lil muttaqin, wal yaqin, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala ashrafil anbiya'i wal mursalin, habibi ilahil 'alamin, Abil Qasim Muhammad. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum. Sallallahu 'alaihi wa alihi al-ma'sumin alladhina adhhaba Allahu 'anhumur rijsa wa tahharahum tathira. Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. Allahumma kun li-waliyyikal Hujjatibnil Hasan, salawatuka 'alaihi wa 'ala aba'ihi, fi hadhihis sa'ati wa fi kulli sa'ah, waliyan wa hafizan wa qa'idan wa nasiran wa dalilan wa 'ayna, hatta tuskinahu ardaka taw'an wa tumatti'ahu fiha tawila. Rabbi salli 'ala Muhammadin wa ali Muhammad wa 'ajjil farajahum wal'an a'da'ahum ajma'in. Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. The discussion had reached the point that once the existence of Allah is proven—it is in the traditions, in the traditions of Al-Kafi—there are 'Sufara' (plural of Safir) for Him, who bring messages from Allah, telling people and the creatures what is in their benefit, what is in their harm, what is in their survival, and what is in their destruction. That is, survival means eternal success and prosperity, and destruction means annihilation and remaining in Hell forever. So, when all these things were proven, then 'fathabata al-amiruna wan-nahuna 'anil hakim al-'alim' (it was proven that there must be those who command and forbid on behalf of the Wise, the All-Knowing). So it was proven that there must be individuals from Allah who bring His commands and prohibitions—what to do and what not to do—from that Allah who is Hakim (Wise) and 'Alim (All-Knowing), to implement these things among His people, and to explain things on His behalf, the Majestic and Exalted. Ta'bir means to convey. It is like a bridge, the connection between Allah and the creatures. And who are these people? They are the Prophets (a.s.) and His 'Safwah' (chosen ones), His selected individuals from among His creatures. They are the Hukama (the wise). They are the possessors of wisdom. They are the people of knowledge. Allah has taught them. They are not ignorant like the people of the world who say, 'We do not know, we are not aware.' No, that is why the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'Ana madinatul 'ilmi wa 'Aliyyun babuha, faman aradal madinata wal hikmata falyatiha min babiha' (I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate; so whoever desires the city and wisdom, let them come through its gate). Ali ibn Abi Talib is the gate. And then it says, 'mu'addabina bil hikmah' (disciplined by wisdom). Allah disciplined them; Allah taught them manners through wisdom. He taught them manners through knowledge and wisdom. 'Mab'uthina biha' (sent with it). They were sent with wisdom, just as you read in the Holy Quran in Surah Al-Jumu'ah: 'Huwalladhi ba'atha fil ummiyyina rasulan minhum yatlu 'alayhim ayatihi wa yuzakkihim wa yu'allimuhumul kitaba wal hikmah' (He it is Who raised among the inhabitants of Mecca a Messenger from among themselves, who recites to them His communications and purifies them, and teaches them the Book and the Wisdom). The Book and the Wisdom—this means the Book is one thing and the Wisdom is another. The Book is what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) brought, and the Wisdom is its interpretation, its explanation, which is the teachings of the Progeny of Muhammad (a.s.). That is wisdom. 'Wa yu'allimuhumul kitaba wal hikmah'. So, 'mu'addabina bil hikmah, mab'uthina biha, mu'ayyadina min 'indil hakim al-'alim bil hikmah' (disciplined by wisdom, sent with it, supported by the Wise, the All-Knowing with wisdom). Look at how much emphasis is being placed. That they were supported by Allah. Allah supported them. Supported with what? With wisdom. When He sent them into the world—for example, today when you send a teacher to a school to teach, you ensure that the teacher is familiar with all the subjects they are going to teach. They must know what they are teaching. For instance, they must have a degree in the subject they are teaching. And then you check if they know it. Therefore, it is necessary that the teacher who is going to teach should be familiar with it themselves. Have you ever seen a teacher in the world who goes and says, 'I don't know, you teach me so that I can then see, learn from you, and then teach you'? Is there any such teacher? But the Muslims did not even make that a condition. That having knowledge is not necessary. It is not necessary; what is the problem? They can call some scholar and ask for a fatwa. This is not just about fatwas. This is about wisdom, about explanation, about the exegesis of the Quran. So, if the greatest man himself does not know, then what would the other scholar whom he calls know? If he knows, then he is more deserving to sit on this chair than the former. So, anyway, the debate of 'afdal' (superior) and 'mafdul' (inferior) comes up again. Who is superior and who is inferior? If this Caliph, this Imam, if he himself does not know what is right and what is wrong, what this means and what that concept is, and he is dependent on someone else to come and explain it to him, then it means the one who is explaining is more deserving to sit here. Anyway, 'thumma thabata dhalika fi kulli dahrin wa zaman' (then it is proven that in every age and time), 'mimma atat bihir rusulu wal anbiya' (from what the Messengers and Prophets brought), 'minad dala'ili wal barahin' (from the proofs and arguments). So that through them—and who taught these arguments? Who gave these proofs? Allah taught them and sent them. Now, the one whom Allah has taught, who can teach him? Can anyone teach him? The one whom Allah has taught? So it is known that the Prophet, the Messenger, and the Imam is the one whom Allah teaches. And this is also in the Quran. There is a verse of the Quran, the verse of Surah An-Najm, right? In Surah An-Najm: 'Wa ma yantiqu 'anil hawa. In huwa illa wahyun yuha. 'allamahu shadidul quwa' (Nor does he speak out of desire. It is naught but revelation that is revealed. The Lord of Mighty Power has taught him). This Prophet does not speak from his own self. 'Wa ma yantiqu 'anil hawa'. Whatever he speaks, 'In huwa illa wahyun yuha' (it is naught but revelation that is revealed). And who taught him this revelation? 'Allamahu shadidul quwa' (The Lord of Mighty Power has taught him). Very powerful. 'Shadidul quwa' means you should not try to wrestle with God. Do not present your own opinion against the Prophet. Because the Prophet is not speaking from himself; he is speaking on behalf of Allah. Now, if someone has doubts about the Prophet's decision, then it is not against the Prophet, it is against Allah. That is why it is announced in Surah Al-Ahzab: 'Wa ma kana li-mu'minin wa la mu'minatin idha qada Allahu wa rasuluhu amran an yakuna lahumul khiyaratu min amrihim' (And it behooves not a believing man and a believing woman that they should have any choice in their matter when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter). No believing man or woman, no one, has the permission. It is not possible for them that when Allah and His Messenger have made a decision, they should interfere in it or present their own opinion. That is, interfering in the Messenger's decision is like wrestling with Allah. Will you argue with Allah, saying, 'O Lord, Your perspective is this, but my perspective is like this'? Now let's see whose perspective is correct. And whoever holds such a belief, the divine punishment descends upon him. As it happened in the event of Ghadir. Harith bin Nu'man did not ask then, did he? That this appointment of Ali, is this appointment from you or from Allah? If it is from Allah, then let the punishment descend right now. So the punishment descended upon him at that very moment. 'Sa'ala sa'ilun bi-'adhabin waqi'' (One demanding, demanded the chastisement which must befall). It is a verse of Surah Al-Ma'arij. The punishment descended immediately. Why? He was wrestling with Allah. So Allah said, 'Okay, this is the result, look.' So the Imam says, 'Likay la takhlu ardullahi min hujjatin' (So that the earth of Allah may never be devoid of a Hujjah). That is why Allah sent the Prophets and Messengers with proofs and arguments, and their successors came so that the earth is never empty of the Hujjah of Allah. There must always be a Hujjah of Allah on earth. 'Yakunu ma'ahu 'ilmun' (He must possess knowledge). And it is necessary that the Hujjah possesses knowledge. That is, the Hujjah of Allah cannot be ignorant. The Hujjah of Allah cannot be ignorant. 'Yadillu 'ala sidqi maqatihi' (And this knowledge should point to the truthfulness of his words). This is truly the Hujjah of Allah. This is truly the Hujjah of Allah. Now, look, there is no time, but because the topic came up, I will give an example very quickly. What happened after the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.)? After the martyrdom of the Messenger of Allah, some people from other religions came, people of other faiths, and they came and asked, 'Who is the successor of the Messenger of Allah?' This is an event that took place after the martyrdom. Right? Not many days had passed. For instance, not even a month or two would have passed. And you know what happened after that. So, who is the successor (Janashin) of the brother of Ruhullah? It was said that so-and-so is the successor, he is the one who adorns the pulpit (Mimbar Afroz). Come, ask him whatever you want to ask. So, the first question the Jew asked was, 'Ayn Allah?' (Where is Allah?). The answer given was, 'Allah is in the heavens.' Then the Jew's second question was, 'Does this mean the earth is devoid of the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda)? Does it mean Allah is not on the earth? Does it mean Allah is not in the earth?' The people sitting there got furious. 'What insolence is this? Get out of here. You have made the mosque impure.' They didn't know the answer, did they? Now, there are different narrations here; that someone took him to Hazrat Ali (a.s.), or he reached there somehow, Salman took him, and Hazrat Ali was sitting there. Regardless, whoever it was, when he came to Hazrat Ali, he said, 'Brother, what is the question?' He said, 'The question is, where is Allah?' Hazrat Amir (a.s.) replied, 'Aynal-ayn fala aynal-lahu wa kayfal-kayf fala kayfa lahu.' Where did He create? Therefore, 'where' (ayn) is not appropriate for Him, and 'how' (kayf) is what He created, so 'how' is not appropriate for Him. He is the Creator of both, just as He is the Creator of a house; He encompasses the entire house. When He created the world, He encompasses the entire world; He encompasses the world. Therefore, 'where' and 'how' are not appropriate questions for Allah. And in this way, he said, 'I have more questions.' He said, 'Yes, bring them, how many questions are there? Bring them.' He had written down many questions. He started asking all the questions, and he (Ali a.s.) answered them all. It is clear, isn't it? 'Ma yadillu ala sidqi maqalihi huwa jawaz-e-adalatihi.' And this is the permission for his justice, the justification of his justice. This is the proof, the evidence of his justice. That he is just (Adil). Because he has come with the truth. That is why it is found in the narrations: 'Arifullah billah' (Know Allah through Allah), 'Wa rasul bir-risala' (Know the Messenger through his message), 'Wa ulil amr bil adli wal ehsan' (And know the Ulil Amr through justice and benevolence). The Ulil Amr who will be the Wali-e-Amr from Allah will never commit injustice. The Imam will truly be just. So, this is one hadith which is in Al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 168. Kitab al-Hujjah, it is the first hadith. Now we come to the second hadith here, and this second hadith is narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim. Mansur ibn Hazim says that I presented myself in the service of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) and I submitted to him how I debated with other Muslims regarding the Proof of Allah (Hujjat-e-Khuda). With other Muslims who were not Shia, how I did it. Listen to that, it is a very interesting debate. He says I said to the Muslims, 'Wa qultu linnasi' (And I said to the people), that do you believe that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) was the Proof of Allah over all creatures? Was the Messenger of Allah the Proof of Allah or not? So they said, 'Qalu bala' (They said yes). Yes, he was. So I asked them, 'Fa-hina maza rasulullahi salla-llahu alayhi wa alihi man kana hujjat ala khalqi' (So when the Messenger of Allah passed away, who is the Proof of Allah over the creation?). So, what was the answer given by the Muslims? 'Al-Quran.' Very proudly. 'Al-Quran, the Quran is the Proof of Allah.' So Mansur says, 'Fa-nazartu fil-quran' (So I looked into the Quran). So when I looked into the Quran, what happened? 'Fa-idha huwa yukhasimu bihi al-murji'u wal-qadariyyu wal-zindiq' (I saw that all the sects and groups of Muslims are presenting arguments from the Quran itself). Even the Zindiq (heretic) who does not believe in God is also bringing evidence from the Quran. The one who does not believe in God, meaning to defeat the Muslims, the Zindiq is also using the Quran. And what else? Zindiq, Zindiq is called the one who does not believe in God, who does not believe in the Day of Judgment, he is called a Zindiq. 'Wa zindiqulladhi la yu'minu bihi' (And the Zindiq who does not believe in it). The one who does not believe in the Quran, he uses the Quran, and his argument is so powerful that 'hatta yaghlibur-rijala bi-khusumati' (that he defeats others through his arguments). People lose to him, this Zindiq. 'Fa-araftu' (So I understood). So from this, we understood one thing: 'Annal-qurana la yakunu hujjatan illa bi-qayyimin' (That the Quran cannot be a Proof unless it has a Qayyim). Now, what is meant by Qayyim? So now you look up the dictionary to see what the translation of Qayyim is, what has been told in the dictionary. So Lisan al-Arab is a very big dictionary written by Ibn Manzur, it is very famous, which everyone accepts. Famous in the whole world, famous in the Arab world. Lisan al-Arab, the language of the Arabs. So in the word 'Qayyim', he explained: 'Al-Qayyimu ay al-mustaqim' (The Qayyim means the upright). The one who is perfectly upright, 'la zaygha fihi' (in whom there is no crookedness). In whom there is no crookedness. 'Wala mayla anil haqqi' (And he never deviates from the truth). And he will always remain on the truth. He is called Qayyim. And what is the second definition written? 'Wal-qayyimu as-sayyid' (And the Qayyim is the master/leader). Qayyim is the one who is a Sayyid. 'Wa sa-isul amr' (And the manager of affairs), and manages all affairs very well. He is called Qayyim. So Mansur ibn Hazim says that this Hujjah, meaning this proof of the Quran, cannot be established until there is someone to establish it who has no crookedness, no crookedness in him, and who always remains on the truth. And we have not seen in history that there has been anyone who has no crookedness and is always on the truth, except for one personality who is called Ali ibn Abi Talib. And about whom I submitted to your service in the previous episode, that the Prophet put a seal on it: 'Aliyun ma'al haqqi wal haqqi ma'a Ali' (Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali). 'Aliyun ma'al haqqi wal haqqi ma'a Ali.' Ali is with the truth and the truth is with Ali. Meaning these two will never be separated from each other. Perfectly straight, and Ali is the Sayyid. Ali is the Sayyid, look, the one from Lisan al-Arab is writing this. He was not a Shia. Ibn Manzur was not a Shia. He is saying who the Qayyim should be, the one who is a Sayyid. Sa-isul amr, manages all affairs, affairs very well. Manages them excellently. Who can be better than Ali ibn Abi Talib? Did you notice? So, 'la yakunu hujjatan illa bi-qayyimin' (It cannot be a proof except with a Qayyim). 'Fa-ma kana fihi min shay'in kana haqqan' (So whatever was in it, it was the truth). Now if you read the Quran with Ali's interpretation, then whatever is in the Quran will be correct. Now there will be nothing wrong in the Quran. 'Fa-qultu lahum' (So I asked them). So who is the Qayyim of the Quran today? Who is the Sayyid of the Quran? Who is the Mustaqim (upright one) of the Quran who can explain the Quran well? Who is the Sa-isul amr (manager of affairs) of the Quran? So they answered, listen to the answer, it is very interesting, very delightful. They answered, 'Faqalu' (Some people said), Ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. One. 'Qad kana ya'lam' (He knew), he knew the whole Quran, he was an exegete of the Quran, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Some people said Umar ya'lam (Umar knew), he also knew the Quran, Umar also knew the Quran. Some people said, he also knew, brother. And some people said Hudhayfah, ya'lam (Hudhayfah knew), Hudhayfah also knew the Quran. So Mansur ibn Hazim asked, 'Were these three, kulluhum' (all of them), did they know the whole Quran? Were they aware of the entire Quran? So they said, 'They didn't know the whole thing.' 'Qalu la' (They said no), no, they didn't know the whole thing. Because the evidence for that exists, doesn't it? The evidence for that exists, Insha'Allah when the discussion of the Imam's knowledge comes, we will discuss it Insha'Allah Ta'ala. 'Qalu la' (They said no). 'Falam yajid ahadan' (So I did not find anyone) about whom it could be said 'innahu ya'rifu dhalika kullahu' (that he knows all of that), that he knows the whole Quran. I could not find anyone. I did not find anyone about whom it could be said that he knows the whole Quran 'illa Aliyan' (except Ali). Except Ali. 'Wa idha kana shay'un baynal qawm' (And when there was something among the people), and the ones you named, when some questions came before them, the first one, meaning Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, would say, 'Hadha la adri' (I don't know this). The second one, meaning Umar, he would say, 'Hadha la adri' (I don't know this). The third one, Hudhayfah, 'Hadha la adri' (I don't know this). I don't know this. Examples of 'I don't know' are found for everyone, I don't know, I don't know. They didn't know the whole Quran. When those three would fail, then Amir al-Mu'minin would say, 'Hadha adri' (I know this). 'Hadha ana adri' (I know this), ask me, don't you? Meaning Ali is the one who says, 'Saluni qabla an tafqiduni' (Ask me before you lose me). That is why I testified, 'Fa ashhadu anna Aliyan alayhis-salam kana qayyimal-quran' (So I bear witness that Ali ibn Abi Talib was the Qayyim of the Quran). The Sayyid of the Quran, the translator of the Quran is Ali ibn Abi Talib. That is why I testified. 'Wa kana ta'atuhu muftarada' (And that is why his obedience is obligatory). Obedience to Ali is obligatory. 'Wa kanal-hujjatu alannasi ba'da rasulillahi salla-llahu alayhi wa alihi' (And that is why after the Messenger of Allah, if there is any Proof, it is Ali ibn Abi Talib). 'Wa anna ma fil-qurani fahuwa haqqun' (And whatever Ali has said about the Quran, that is the truth). That is the truth, nothing else is the truth. Mansur ibn Hazim presented this entire debate before Imam Sadiq (a.s.). When the Imam heard the entire debate, the Imam said, 'Rahimakallah' (May Allah shower His mercy upon you). 'Wa salla-llahu ala Muhammadin wa alihi tayyibin tahirin ma'sumin'.

title: EP01 | Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s): Allah Ki Baaqi Rehne Waali Hujjat | ⛅ PANAAH-E-KAINAAT MEGA QUIZ  2026
excerpt: This lecture explores the theological necessity of the Imam of the Time (a.t.f.s.) as the living Proof (Hujjah) of Allah, essential for the stability and existence of the universe. It delves into the concept of 'Baqiyatullah,' the significance of Surah Al-Qadr in proving the ongoing presence of the Imam, and the vital importance of Ma'rifat (recognition) of the Imam for true worship. The session also addresses the divine trial of occultation, the virtues of patient waiting (Intizar), and the spiritual status of believers who maintain their faith during the Imam's absence.

TSR presents. Oh, oh, the hidden desire in the longing of my gaze, oh, oh, the comfort of my heart, oh, the comfort of my heart. If you have not subscribed to our channel yet, subscribe now and do not forget to click the bell icon. The quiz link is live, which is present in the live chat and comment section of this video. If you have not registered yet, click on the quiz link to register. Then on the same quiz link, you will see questions related to this discussion. All the answers to the questions are present in the discussion. You just have to watch the discussion carefully and give the correct answers to the quiz questions. The quiz link will remain live until the end of the program, so do not be in a hurry to answer the questions. There is no prize for answering first. There is only one condition for the quiz prize: all the answers to the questions must be correct. Among all those who have given correct answers to all the questions, the winners of today's episode will be selected at the end of the program through our computerized lucky draw system. But those whose names did not appear in today's winners or if any episode was missed, there is no need to be disappointed because the quiz link will remain live until the end of this series. The mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw winner for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will be selected from among those who have given correct answers to all questions in all episodes. That is, even if someone is not among the daily winners, but has given correct answers in all episodes, all those people will be included in the lucky draw for the mega prize of the Ziyarat of Iraq. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, be for Your representative, the Proof, son of Al-Hasan, Your blessings be upon him and his forefathers, in this hour and in every hour, a guardian, a protector, a leader, a helper, a guide, and an eye, until You make him reside on Your earth in obedience and let him enjoy it for a long time. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may peace be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us and do not destroy us. How can it be proven that today there is a proof (Hujjah) of Allah remaining on this earth and that he is alive? Is there evidence for this in the Holy Quran? In the Khutbah of Ghadir, the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) uttered some sentences regarding Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.), and this series is based on four of those sentences. This series of the 'Panah-e-Kainat Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.)' mega quiz and the first episode of today's series is based on this sentence of the Khutbah of Ghadir: 'Alanahu al-baqi Hujjat'—that is, O people, know that he is the remaining Proof of Allah. And keep one thing in mind: along with the episode, there will be a surprise question in the quiz that can be asked at any time during the episode. So, watch the episode carefully and get a chance to be included in the lucky draw for both the daily prize and the mega prize by giving correct answers to all the questions. So, let us start the episode with this. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Momineen, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. First of all, we present our congratulations to all the viewers on the auspicious birth of Hazrat-e-Hujjah. As it was presented before you, our topic today is 'Alanahu al-baqi Hujjat'—the remaining Proof of Allah, which was a part of a Hadith from the Khutbah of Ghadir. And the topic we have to present before you is that the earth cannot remain empty without the Proof of God. So, by presenting just one sentence on the word 'Hujjah' and explaining it, let us start our talk: Hujjah refers to that divine proof through which the Almighty God removes the misguidance of polytheism and sedition so clearly that no excuse for denial remains. That is, if we present a small and brief summary of Hujjah before you, it means 'between truth and falsehood'—that the work of the Hujjah is to decide between falsehood and truth, what is falsehood and what is truth. So, let us present the first Hadith before you: the earth cannot remain without the Proof of God. We are presenting this Hadith of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) before you, and this Hadith is from the book Al-Kafi, in which the Imam (a.s.) says that if the Imam were to be removed even for a single moment, 'that the Imam is removed from the earth for an hour'—if he were removed even for a moment, 'the earth would destroy its inhabitants, just as the sea waves destroy those who live within it.' Now, dear brothers, the analogy given here in the Hadith—that just as the waves of the sea destroy the things living within it—we want to draw your attention to this by giving you a hint: when does the sea remain in a stable state and how does it reach an unstable state from its stable state? The ocean is essentially maintained by the balance of stable forces. These stable forces include gravity, wind stress (which is the pressure of the wind), and tidal forces—the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun—through which the ocean remains stable. When these stable forces change, the ocean shifts from a stable state to an unstable one. Similarly, this analogy is given that if the Imam is a force on this earth, then if he were removed even for a single moment, the balance of this entire earth would be disrupted. In this regard, it is not just this one hadith of Imam Baqir (a.s.) that we have presented to you; rather, in the greatest and most authentic book of the Shia school of thought, known as Al-Kafi, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) has brought forth approximately 13 hadiths and dedicated a chapter titled 'Annal-arda la takhlu min al-hujja' (The earth is never devoid of a Hujjah), meaning the earth is never empty of Allah's Hujjah. In this entire chapter, Sheikh Kulayni (r.a.) has presented 13 hadiths, which clearly reveal that this earth cannot remain empty without the Hujjah of Allah. If you look, in the same way, in Mafatih al-Jinan, within Dua-e-Adila, this sentence appears: 'Wa bi-baqa'ihi baqiyat al-dunya' (And by his remaining, the world remains). 'Wa bi-yumnihi ruziqa al-wara' (And by his blessing, the creation receives sustenance). 'Wa bi-wujudihi thabatat al-ardu wa al-sama' (And by his existence, the earth and the heavens are established). So, if you study all these hadiths—whether you look at Al-Kafi or the two things we presented, the hadith of Imam Baqir (a.s.) and these sentences from Dua-e-Adila—it becomes clear that the Hujjah of Allah plays a massive role on this earth; if the Hujjah of Allah were removed from this earth, this earth would perish and be destroyed. Similarly, let us present another hadith to you, which is also found in Usul al-Kafi, Volume 1, page 179. It is narrated from Imam Baqir (a.s.) that he said: 'Wallahi ma taraka Allahu ardan mundhu qabada Adam (a.s.)'—I swear by Allah, the Imam (a.s.) is swearing by Allah, and after swearing by Allah, the Imam (a.s.) says that since the passing of Adam (a.s.), Allah has never left the earth such that 'Illa wa fiha imamu yuhtada bihi ila Allah' (except that there is an Imam in it through whom guidance is obtained towards Allah). And he is His Hujjah over His servants. 'Wa la tabqa al-ardu bighayri imami hujjatin lillahi 'ala 'ibadihi' (And the earth cannot remain without an Imam who is a Hujjah of Allah over His servants). It cannot remain. This means it is clear from this hadith that from the creation of Adam (a.s.) until today, there has never been a time when Allah has not kept His Hujjah on this earth. Similarly, the second chapter that Sheikh Kulayni presented in his book Al-Kafi also has a similar theme, titled: 'Annahu law lam yabqa fi al-ardi illa rajulani la-kana ahaduhuma al-hujja' (If only two men remained on earth, one of them would be the Hujjah). This means if the entire world were to perish and only two of Allah's creations remained on this earth, one of them would be the Hujjah of Allah. We have such strong hadiths that the presence of the Imam in this world is essential for the very existence of this world. Now, one final point to conclude this topic: Imam Baqir (a.s.) states: 'Inna al-hujjata la taqumu lillahi 'azza wa jalla 'ala khalqihi' (Indeed, the Hujjah of Allah does not stand over His creation) 'Illa bi-imamin hayyin ya'rifunahu' (except with a living Imam whom they recognize and know). So, it is clearly mentioned in this hadith that Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) is conveying a message to his followers that the Imam will be alive. Why? Because as long as the Imam exists, this world exists. And if there is no Imam, then as we have presented to you—the hadith that if this Imam were removed for even a moment, this world would perish, be destroyed, and the existence of this world would end. And this living Imam is none other than the final Hujjah of Allah, our Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). He is the one whom Allah has honored in the Holy Quran with the title 'Baqiyatullah'. In Surah Hud, verse 86, Allah the Almighty says: 'Baqiyatullahi khayrun lakum in kuntum mu'minin wa ma ana 'alaykum bi-hafiz' (That which remains from Allah is better for you if you are believers, and I am not a guardian over you). In the context of this verse, we find a hadith from our sixth Imam, Imam Sadiq (a.s.). A person comes to the service of the Imam and asks him a question, addressing the Imam by a specific title, asking: 'When we meet Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), can we address him with the title 'Amir al-Mu'minin' or not?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'No. Allah has reserved this title for Imam Ali (a.s.), and this title has not been given to anyone before him or after him.' And if anyone claims to be Amir al-Mu'minin, he is a disbeliever. That is, apart from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), no one else is entitled to this title. Then the person asks, 'When we meet Imam-e-Zamana (a.s.), when we meet your final Hujjah, how should we greet him?' The Imam (a.s.) replied, 'Greet him by saying: 'Assalamu 'alayka ya Baqiyatullah' (Peace be upon you, O Baqiyatullah).' In the Holy Quran, there is a famous Surah, on everyone's tongue, even the smallest child remembers this Surah, which is called Surah Inna Anzalna, Surah Qadr. What is this Surah? Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim. 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylatil qadr' (Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree). Allah says that He revealed this Quran-e-Majeed in Laylatul Qadr, the Night of Decree. Laylatul Qadr means the night of destinies. 'Wa ma adraka ma laylatul qadr' (And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is?). What happens in it? The Surah continues. 'Tanazzalul malaikatu' (The angels descend). It is not in the past tense. The form of the past tense is not used; it is in the present tense. The angels descend. When does Laylatul Qadr come? In the blessed month of Ramadan. Everyone knows this. Meaning, no one can deny that this Night of Decree comes in the blessed month of Ramadan. And what happens in this night? The Quran says that in this night, the angels descend. 'Tanazzalul malaikatu war-ruh' (The angels and the Spirit descend). And Hazrat Ruh al-Qudus (a.s.) descends. With whom do they descend? They descend with all affairs, with all tasks. Regarding this Surah, Dawood ibn Farqad was a famous companion of the sixth Imam, Hazrat Imam Jafar-e-Sadiq (a.s.). He asked the Imam a question regarding this very Surah. The Imam says: 'Nazala fiha ma yakunu minas-sanati ilas-sanah' (There descends in it what will be from one year to the next). From this year until the coming year, meaning from one Laylatul Qadr until the next coming Laylatul Qadr, the angels descend with all the affairs of the entire year. And what happens in it? 'Min mawtin wa mawludin' (Regarding death and birth). Whose death will occur, that is decided in his destiny. Who will be born, that is decided in his destiny. Then Dawood, Dawood ibn Farqad asks, he asks the Imam, 'Qultu lahu ila man?' (I said to him, to whom?). O Mawla, to whom do these angels descend? This hadith is narrated from Imam Sajjad (a.s.), in which he states: ‘Nahnu aimmatul muslimeen’ (We are the Imams of the Muslims). The first sentence. In the second sentence, the Mawla says: ‘Wa hujajul-lahi alal-alamin’ (And we are the proof/hujjah of Allah for the people of the worlds). And then the Mawla says: ‘Wa qadatul-ghurril-muhajjaleen’ (And we are the leaders of the pure and radiant ones). Now, let me explain a little about ‘ghurril-muhajjaleen’. ‘Ghur’ refers to a horse that is black but has a white forehead, and this confirms the purity of the horse's father's lineage. If a horse has a white forehead and is entirely black, it confirms the purity of its father's lineage. And ‘muhajjil’ refers to that same horse having four white legs. What does this confirm? It is a sign of the purity of the horse's mother. It means it is pure from the mother's side as well—a horse that has a white forehead, is entirely black, and has four white legs. So, this is a confirmation of the horse's purity from both the mother's and father's sides. And the Mawla is saying here: ‘Wa qadatul-ghurril-muhajjaleen’ (We are the leaders of the pure and radiant ones). And then the Mawla says: ‘Wa mawali-mu'minin’ (And we are the guardians/mawali of the believers). ‘Wa nahnu aman...’ then after that, the Mawla says: ‘Wa nahnu amanu ahlil-ard’ (And we are the security/aman for the people of the earth). And then the Mawla makes a comparison: ‘Kama annannujuma amanun li-ahlis-sama’ (Just as the stars are a security for the people of the sky). So, the stars are a security for the people of the sky; let me present two or three points to clarify this. Every star has its own gravitational field and holds the bodies, planets, or asteroids around it in place. For example, the sun is also a star. If this sun did not exist, the planets would move out of their orbits and the entire solar system would collapse. Point number two: these same stars are used for navigation; they are reference points for navigation, and whether it is the sea, land, or sky, these stars serve the purpose of navigation everywhere. So, just as these stars are guides for the sky, in the same way, the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) are guides from Allah on this earth, and their presence saves this earth from destruction and is the cause of peace and security for this earth. Then the Imam (a.s.) says further: ‘Wa nahnu alladhina bina yumsikullahu-ssama-a an taqa'a alal-ardi illa bi-idhnihi’ (And we are the ones through whom Allah prevents the sky from falling onto the earth, except by His permission). So, the sky falling onto the earth—this is due to whom? If the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were not there, this cosmic balance would not be maintained. Meaning, the sky would fall onto the earth. Now, how would it fall? We cannot explain that in great detail, but here the Imam is giving a clear-cut indication that the sky remaining in its place is due to the blessed existence of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). After that, the Imam (a.s.) says: ‘Wa bina yumsikul-arda an tamida bi-ahliha’ (And through us, He keeps the earth from shaking with its inhabitants). This means it is not just physical earthquakes; if the Imam (a.s.) were not present, it would not just be physical earthquakes, but rather fitna (strife), corruption, immorality, or the complete collapse of ethics in this society would occur. If the Imam (a.s.) were not there, the world would be filled with all these things along with the earth itself. If Allah did not send down rain, the existence of this entire world would not be possible. The existence of the entire world is based on this water, and this water rains down from the heavens because of the Infallible Imams (a.s.). Then the Imam (a.s.) says: ‘Wa bina yanshurur-rahmah’ (And through us, He spreads mercy). And after that, the Imam (a.s.) says that through us, Allah spreads mercy upon the face of the earth. And if we reflect on Dua-e-Nudba, we find a similar sentence in Dua-e-Nudba where the Imam (a.s.) is pointed to: ‘Aynas-sababul-muttasil’ (Where is the connection/means that joins) ‘baynal-ardi was-sama’ (the people of the earth to the sky). Meaning, blessings are coming from Allah Almighty from the sky for the people of this earth, and the means of those blessings, the cause of those blessings, is the presence of the Imam of the Time (a.s.) in this age. After that, Imam Sajjad (a.s.) says: ‘Wa yukhriju barakatil-ard’ (And He brings out the blessings of the earth). And all the blessings we are receiving from this earth are due to our existence. Meaning, because of the existence of the Imam (a.s.), we are receiving all the things we get from the earth. Then the Imam (a.s.) says: ‘Wa lawla ma fil-ardi minna lasakhat bi-ahliha’ (And if there were no one from us on the earth, it would sink with its inhabitants). And then he states: ‘Wa lam takhlul-ardu mundhu khalaqallahu Adama min hujjatin lillahi fiha’ (And since Allah created Adam, the earth has never been empty of Allah’s Hujjah/Proof). And then he says: ‘Zahirun mashhurun aw ghaibun mastur’ (Whether that Hujjah is manifest and known, or that Hujjah is hidden and veiled). And after that, the Imam (a.s.) says: ‘Wa la takhlu ila an taqumas-sa’atu min hujjatin lillahi fiha’ (And until the Hour of Resurrection, the earth will not be empty of a Hujjah of Allah). And after that, the Imam (a.s.) states: ‘Wa lawla dhalika lam yu’badillahu’ (And if it were not so, Allah would not be worshipped). So, dear ones, this is a very important point: if true worship of the Almighty God is taking place on the face of this earth, it is because of the existence of the Imam of the Time (a.s.); otherwise, these acts of worship would have been impossible. After that, the hadith takes a different turn, and the narrator, Sulaiman, asks the Imam (a.s.): ‘Mawla, fakayfa yantafi’un-nasu bil-hujjatil-ghaibil-mastur?’ (Mawla, as you said that the Hujjah is either hidden or manifest, if the Hujjah is hidden, how will people benefit from that Hujjah?) Now here, the Imam (a.s.) explains: ‘Qala kama yantafi’una bish-shamsi idha satarahas-sahab’ (He said: Just as people benefit from the sun when it is hidden behind the clouds). So, dear ones, we have seen through this hadith that the secret of this world's survival is the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). If the Ahlulbayt (a.s.) were to be removed from this world for even a single moment, or if their attention—let alone their existence—were to be removed from this world for even a single moment, this world would perish. And all the blessings that are descending from Allah in this world, whether in the form of rain, or the blessings coming out of this earth, or all the bounties that come to a human's imagination, the source of all those bounties in this age is only and only the Imam of the Time (a.s.). This means that just as the sun exists, the Imam is also present and is among us. We have discussed this topic in detail in last year's episode of Panah-e-Kainat. And in this same connection, our twelfth Imam's second special ambassador, Muhammad bin Uthman al-Amri (r.a.), says when he was asked about the Imam of the Time (a.s.): ‘Wallahi inna sahibahadhal-amri la ya’dhurul-mawsima kulla sanah’ (By Allah, indeed the Imam of the Time (a.s.), who is the master of this affair, is present every year at the time of Hajj). ‘Yarannasa wa ya’rifuhum’ (He sees the people and recognizes them). ‘Wa yarawnahu wa la ya’rifunahu’ (And the people also see him but do not recognize him). This is the difference between the Imam and other people: the Imam recognizes all people, but people certainly see the Imam but do not recognize him. And on this very topic, another statement is found from the second special ambassador. He was asked about the Imam of the Time (a.s.), and the person asking was Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari. He asks him: Have you met the Imam (a.s.), meaning the twelfth Imam? He says: Yes. And the last time I met him, it was in the House of Kaaba, it was in the Baitullah-al-Haram. And at that time, the Imam (a.s.) was praying this supplication: ‘Allahumma anjiz li ma wa’adtani’ (O Allah, fulfill for me what You have promised me). And after that, Muhammad ibn Uthman says that I saw him holding the cover of the Kaaba, and he was standing towards the Mustajar, and he was praying this: ‘Allahummantaqim bi min a’daika’ (O Allah, take revenge on my enemies through me). ‘Wa yarawnahu wa la ya’rifunahu’ (People see him but do not recognize him). This is what is called Ghaybah (Occultation). Meaning, Ghaybah can be a veil for the eyes, but the remembrance of our Imam, his mention, can never be erased from our hearts. In this connection, a narration is found from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, and this narration has been recorded by Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) in his book ‘Kamaluddin’. He comes once to the service of Imam Kazim (a.s.) and asks the Imam. The sentence of the narration is: ‘Sa’altu sayyidi Musa bna Ja’farin alayhimas-salam’ (I asked my Sayyid, my master, Imam Kazim (a.s.)) regarding this verse, the noble verse which is verse number 20 of Surah Luqman. What is the verse? The part of the verse is: ‘Wa asbagha alaykum ni’amahu zahiratan wa batinah’ (And He has bestowed upon you His blessings, manifest and hidden). What did Allah do? He perfected His blessings upon you all. Which blessings? Both the apparent blessings and the hidden blessings. Allah perfected this blessing. This is a verse of the Quran. Regarding this verse, they asked Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) what the meaning of this verse is. The Imam said: 'An-ni'matu az-zahiratu al-imamu az-zahir' (The apparent blessing is the apparent Imam). The Imam who is before the eyes of the people, whom people can see, recognize, meet, and ask about their problems and issues, and all such things. 'Wal-batinatu' (And what is the meaning of the hidden blessing?) 'Al-imamu al-gha'ib' (The Imam who will be in occultation, the Imam who will be hidden). As soon as Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi heard this, he immediately asked the Imam: 'Wa yakunu fil-a'immati man yaghib' (Will any of the Imams go into occultation?) Look, this was very difficult for those people at that time, for the companions of the Imams (a.s.), to bear the thought that their Imam would not be before the eyes of the people. We were born in this era of occultation, Alhamdulillah, due to the blessings of our parents, the nobility of our mother, because of which we are steadfast in this Shia belief. May the Almighty grant us the ability to remain steadfast in this belief until our last breath. We stepped into the world during this era of occultation, so we are accustomed to it, in a way, that we are living in this time of occultation; therefore, we have the capacity to understand the concept of occultation to some extent because we are seeing it, meaning we are witnessing this era of occultation. But at that time, when the eleven Imams were present, it was not an era of occultation. There, the Imam was apparent before everyone. Therefore, it was very heavy and difficult for those people to accept that a time could come when their Imam would not be present before them. That is why Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi is asking if any of the Imams will be hidden. Will anyone go into occultation? The Imam says, 'Na'am' (Yes). Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) says, 'Yes'. 'Yaghibu 'an absarin-nasi shakhsuhu' (His person will be hidden from the eyes of the people). There is a difference between the personality being in occultation and the person being in occultation. The personality being in occultation means, as mentioned in the hadith presented to you earlier, that people see him but do not recognize him. They are not aware of the personality, that the one we are seeing is the Imam of the Time. Otherwise, during the Hajj season, at the time of Hajj, there are millions of people. Hundreds of thousands of people go for Hajj. It is in the narrations that people see the Imam, but they do not recognize that this is the Imam of the Time, this is Imam Mahdi (ajtf). This is called the personality being in occultation. Physically, the Imam is not in occultation; people are seeing him, meetings are happening, but when they see him, they do not recognize at that moment that this is the Imam. But this does not mean that they should not remember their Imam. Because further on, Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) says that although his personality will be hidden from the eyes of the people, 'Wa la yaghibu 'an qulubil-mu'minina dhikruhu' (But his remembrance will never be erased from the hearts of the believers). The hearts of the believers will always remain restless. His remembrance will always remain fresh in the hearts of the believers. A believer will never forget the remembrance of his Imam. He will always keep remembering his Imam. This is Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) prophesying that this will be the level of faith of the believer of the end times, that he does not need to see his Imam to remember him. Why? Because he has never forgotten the remembrance of his Imam from his heart. His Imam always resides in his heart, in his entire being. At every moment, he remembers his Imam. And who will that Imam be? Then Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) says, clarifying: 'Wa huwath-thani 'ashara minna' (He will be the twelfth from among us). And then the Imam mentions some characteristics regarding the Imam of the Time, what Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) is stating: 'Yusahhillu-llahu lahu kulla 'asir' (Allah will make every difficulty easy for him). Now, how will Allah help the Imam of the Time? Regarding this, Imam al-Kazim (a.s.) is shedding light on this reality, clarifying that Allah will make every difficulty easy for him. 'Wa yudhillu lahu kulla sa'b' (And He will humble every difficult thing for him). Every thing that appears tough, every thing that appears difficult, or in a way, every harsh person, every harsh tyrant and oppressive king, Allah will humble him before the Imam of the Time, will force him to kneel. This is our twelfth. 'Wa yuzhiru lahu kunuzal-ard' (Allah will reveal the treasures of the earth for him). All the treasures that Allah has placed inside the earth will be revealed when our twelfth comes. Now, it is possible that someone might get worried hearing this, how can it be that treasures from inside the earth... today people are bent on looting wherever there are treasures on earth. Wherever someone gets news that there is a treasure there, that there is something truly precious there, like oil, etc., people want to occupy that land. But after the Imam comes, the earth itself will bring out all its treasures. Allah will make it happen. People might be surprised how it is possible for the earth to bring out all the treasures itself? So what is there to be surprised about in this? The same God, the same Allah who placed the treasures inside the earth, He will bring those treasures out. How can anyone doubt the power of Allah? If there is truly faith in Allah. Then the Imam says: 'Wa yuqarribu lahu kulla ba'id' (And every distance will become near for him). Meaning, no distance will remain a distance for the Imam. And He will destroy through him every stubborn tyrant. Every oppressive and tyrannical person in this world, Allah will destroy him through the Imam. And He will destroy at his hands every rebellious devil. Every rejected devil and all the agents of the devil roaming on this earth, who are misleading people, Allah will destroy them at the hands of the Imam of the Time (a.s.). This is the son of the princess of the bondmaids, meaning Lady Narjis Khatun (s.a.), he will be her son. He is the one whose birth will be hidden from the people. His birth will be in a hidden state, people will not know. But it will not be permissible for them to name him. That is why we have been forbidden in history, in narrations, in hadiths, not to call him by his name. Although it is quite clear in the hadiths that his name is the same as the name of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). But still, in a way, it is against etiquette to call someone who is greater than oneself, someone who is elder, by their name. And there are other reasons as well due to which we have been forbidden not to take his name. If you want to remember him, remember him through his titles. And this will continue until Allah (azza wa jall) commands his reappearance. And then when he reappears, he will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it will be filled with oppression and tyranny. Indeed, waiting for the Imam of the Time (ajtf) with recognition has such importance that the faith of that believer, its value, its price, is clarified in this narration where this is narrated from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, who was asking the Fourth Imam (a.s.) about the Imams to come after him, and when it came to the last Imam, Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) stated that he would have a long occultation. And regarding that occultation, when the Imam mentions it further, the Imam says: 'Ya Aba Khalid, inna ahla zamani ghaibatihi wal-qa'ilina bi-imamatihi wal-muntazirina li-zuhurihi afdalu min ahli kulli zaman' (O Abu Khalid, indeed the people of the time of his occultation, who believe in his Imamate and wait for his reappearance, are superior to the people of every time). Meaning, all the eras that have passed, from Adam (a.s.) until today, the people living in this era of occultation who believe in the Imam's Imamate and wait for his reappearance will be superior to the people of all those eras. Then the Imam further states: 'Li-annallaha tabaraka wa ta'ala atahum minal-'uquli wal-afhami wal-ma'rifa' (Because Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will grant them such intellect, understanding, and recognition). And Allah will grant them such intellect, such understanding, and such recognition that the Imam states: 'Ma sarat bihil-ghaibatu 'indahum bi-manzilatil-mushahada' (That the occultation for them will be like witnessing). Meaning, for them, the occultation will be like witnessing. Even while in occultation, the Imam will be for them as if they are seeing the Imam. Then the Imam further states: Now, here the Imam is telling their status, that these believers of the era of occultation, who have faith in the Imam, are steadfast in the belief of his Imamate, and are waiting for his reappearance, what is their status? The Imam further states: 'Wa ja'a lahum fi dhalikal-zamani bi-manzilatil-mujahidina baina yadai rasulillahi sallallahu 'alaihi wa alihi bis-saif' (And their status in that time will be like those who participated in battle alongside the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) with the sword). Alongside the Messenger of Allah, meaning look, those who fought alongside the Messenger of Allah, like the Battle of Badr, the Battle of Uhud, those who fought, that status will be attained by the people living in this era of occultation. Just because they have faith in the occultation, have belief in the Imamate of the Imam of the Time, and are waiting for his reappearance. Then Imam Zayn al-Abidin (a.s.) further states: 'Ula'ikal-mukhlisuna haqqan' (They are the truly sincere ones). And they will be the ones who are truly sincere. Those who are truly sincere will be them. Then he says: 'Wa shi'atuna sidqan' (And they are our true Shia). They are the true Shia of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). Further, he states: 'Wa du'atu ila dinillahi sirran wa jahran' (And they will invite people to the religion of Allah secretly and openly). And they will invite people to the religion of God. Further, the Imam states: And Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) states that 'Intizarul-faraji min a'zamil-faraj' (Waiting for the reappearance is the greatest relief/success). Meaning, the believer who wants to go towards success, meaning whoever wants to go towards success, the Imam is saying that waiting for the reappearance is the greatest success. If anyone wants to be successful in this era of occultation, in their religion and in the world, wants to be successful in the hereafter, the Imam is saying that the one who is waiting for the reappearance, this is the greatest success. In this era of occultation (Ghaybah), there is no greater success than waiting for the reappearance (Zuhur). The greatest success is the wait for the Zuhur. So, respected audience, let us pray in the court of the Almighty that the Lord of the Worlds grants us the ability to remain steadfast on the Wilayah of our remaining Proof, the Imam of our time, Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.). May He make his remembrance so strong in our hearts that it never fades, and may He grant us the ability to pray for his reappearance as much as possible. Ameen, O Lord of the Worlds. chapters.title: Quiz Instructions and Program Overview
chapters.summary: The host explains the rules for the mega quiz, including how to participate, the criteria for winning daily and mega prizes, and the importance of watching the lecture carefully.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Allah's Hujjah
chapters.summary: The lecture defines 'Hujjah' as the divine proof that distinguishes truth from falsehood and explains why the earth cannot exist without a living Imam.

chapters.title: The Role of the Imam in World Stability
chapters.summary: Using narrations from Al-Kafi and Dua-e-Adila, the speaker illustrates that the existence of the universe is dependent upon the presence of the living Imam.

chapters.title: Imam Mahdi as Baqiyatullah
chapters.summary: The speaker identifies Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) as the 'Baqiyatullah' mentioned in the Quran and explains the proper way to greet the Imam.

chapters.title: The Title Baqiyatullah
chapters.summary: The speaker explains that 'Baqiyatullah' is a beloved title for Imam Mahdi (a.j.t.f.s.) and recounts the historical meeting where the young Imam introduced himself to Ahmad ibn Ishaq.

chapters.title: Surah Qadr as Proof of Imamate
chapters.summary: The lecture presents Surah Al-Qadr as a definitive Quranic proof for the existence of a living Imam, as angels continue to descend to the 'Sahib al-Amr' with the affairs of the year.

chapters.title: Surah Qadr and the Imam of the Time
chapters.summary: The Imam of the time is the recipient of all divine decrees on Laylatul Qadr, making recognition of him essential for believers.

chapters.title: The Necessity of Recognizing the Imam
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) confirms that the earth is never without a divine Proof and emphasizes the danger of dying without recognizing the Imam.

chapters.title: The Trial of Occultation
chapters.summary: Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) describes the trials of the occultation, warning against bewilderment, falsehood, and setting specific times for the reappearance.

chapters.title: Worship Through Recognition
chapters.summary: True worship of Allah is contingent upon the recognition of the Imam, as explained by Imam Husain (a.s.).

chapters.title: The Necessity of Knowing the Imam
chapters.summary: True recognition of Allah is attained through the recognition of the Imam of the time, whose obedience is obligatory.

chapters.title: Perseverance and Readiness for the Awaited Imam
chapters.summary: Believers are instructed to remain patient in their duties and maintain a constant state of readiness for the support of the Awaited Imam.

chapters.title: The Ahlulbayt as the Security of the Earth
chapters.summary: The Imams serve as the spiritual security for the world, acting as the vital link between the heavens and the earth.

chapters.title: The Perpetual Presence of Allah's Hujjah
chapters.summary: The earth is never devoid of a Hujjah of Allah, whether manifest or hidden, which is the fundamental reason for the existence of worship.

chapters.title: The Imam as the Sun Behind Clouds
chapters.summary: The Imam of the Time is the source of all worldly blessings, acting like the sun hidden behind clouds, sustaining existence through his presence.

chapters.title: The Nature of Occultation
chapters.summary: The Imam is present among people during Hajj and elsewhere, but while they see him, they do not recognize him; this is the reality of his occultation.

chapters.title: Manifest and Hidden Blessings
chapters.summary: Imam al-Kazim explains that the 'hidden blessing' in the Quran refers to the Imam in occultation, whose physical presence is veiled but whose remembrance remains in believers' hearts.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Imam's Divine Mission
chapters.summary: The twelfth Imam will be empowered by Allah to overcome all difficulties, reveal earth's treasures, and destroy tyranny and rebellion upon his reappearance.

chapters.title: Superiority of Believers in Occultation
chapters.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin explains that those who maintain faith and wait for the Imam during the occultation are superior to believers of all previous eras.

title: Fadak Ki Zameen Kaise Haasil Hui? | Watch EP 1 of #The_Fadak_Podcast
excerpt: This lecture explores the historical acquisition of Fadak and its status as the exclusive property of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.a.). The speaker explains that Fadak was acquired peacefully without military conflict, categorizing it as 'Fay' rather than spoils of war. The discussion highlights the political significance of Fadak, suggesting that control over this land was central to the legitimacy and financial stability of the early Islamic government.
content:
Some people say that when Khaybar was conquered, some people remained in that fort. It wasn't that Khaybar was just one fort; Khaybar consisted of various forts. According to historical accounts, there were about five forts, three of which were captured through battle. The remaining two were not taken by charging horses or camels, nor was there any struggle involved. They were taken under the decree of 'Fay'. We will discuss this inshallah. As Tabari has recorded, Khaybar became spoils of war for the Muslims, and Fadak became the exclusive property of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.). Why are we using the word 'exclusive' for those two forts? Because no battle took place there. This land of Khaybar was acquired peacefully and came into the Prophet's possession. The very first thing done upon assuming the position of Caliphate was to break the financial backbone of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), which was the means by which their affairs were being run. If you observe closely, this implies that this land was not just a piece of land or a financial matter for which protests were being held and attempts were being made to seize it. Rather, the entire foundation of the government rested on this land. Whoever was the rightful owner of this land would be the one in charge of the government.

Fadak is classified as 'Fay', meaning it was the exclusive property of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.).

The financial status of Fadak was vital to the economic support of the Ahlulbayt.
The seizure of Fadak was a calculated effort to break the financial independence of the Prophet's family.
Control over Fadak was intrinsically linked to the authority and foundation of the early Caliphate.

title: Azadaari Par E'teraaz? Kyun? | #Muharram 2026 | #YaHusain (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture addresses the frequent objections and fatwas raised against Azadari (mourning for Imam Hussain) during Muharram. By citing a narration from Imam Ali (a.s.) to Janabe Zainab (s.a.), the speaker explains that these doubts are part of a deliberate strategy by Iblis to lead humanity astray. The talk emphasizes that holding onto the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt is the only way to remain protected from these satanic deceptions. Ultimately, the speaker encourages believers to remain steadfast in their mourning rituals despite external criticism.
content:
A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim. Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Assalamu alal-Husain wa ala Ali ibnil-Husain wa ala awladil-Husain wa ala as-habil-Husain. As soon as Muharram begins and the days of mourning (Ayyam-e-Aza) arrive, the market of fatwas becomes heated. Various fatwas are issued regarding Azadari. 'Why is there an Alam? This coffin is an innovation (bid'ah). This weeping is an innovation. What will be achieved by these processions?' All sorts of objections, doubts, and suspicions are raised by the enemies of Azadari against the mourning. Do you know why this happens? Listen to the Hadith. The narrator's name is Zaidah. Zaidah narrates from Imam Sayyid-us-Sajjad (a.s.), and the fourth Imam (a.s.) says that this Hadith was narrated to me by my aunt, Janabe Zainab (s.a.), and Janabe Zainab (s.a.) narrated it from Janabe Umm-e-Ayman, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) narrated this entire Hadith to Janabe Umm-e-Ayman, which contains the entire event of Karbala as described by the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Janabe Zainab (s.a.) verified this entire event and this entire Hadith with her father, Ali Murtaza Amir-ul-Momineen (a.s.). When? Even at the last moments of the Mawla, when Ibn Muljim (la'natullah alaih) struck him with the blow that led to the Mawla's martyrdom. So, before his martyrdom, Janabe Zainab (s.a.) had inquired from the Mawla about this Hadith, that 'Father, Janabe Umm-e-Ayman told us such a Hadith in which the entire event of Karbala occurred, and the conditions after Karbala were all described by Janabe Umm-e-Ayman to Janabe Zainab (s.a.).' Now the Mawla says to Janabe Zainab (s.a.): 'O my daughter, the Hadith is exactly as Umm-e-Ayman told you.' Just as Janabe Umm-e-Ayman narrated to you, the Hadith is exactly like that. Meaning, that event will happen. The event of Karbala will happen, and then the Imam says: 'It is as if I see you, my daughters, and my family members; I see that you will be taken as prisoners in this city of Kufa, and attempts will be made to insult you.' You will live in fear that people might capture you or attack you. So when all this happens, 'Fasbirn' (be patient), my daughter. By the One who split the seed and created the soul—the Mawla swears by Allah—the Mawla says that on that day, when this event happens, when the entire event of Karbala and what happened to the Ahl-e-Haram afterwards occurs, the Mawla says that on that day, there will be no Wali of Allah left on the face of this earth except you, your followers, and your Shias. Apart from you, there will be no Wali of Allah on earth. And the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has informed us of this, what? That Iblis, the Shaitan (la'natullah alaih), will be flying with joy on that day. He will be roaming the entire earth with his devils and his demons. He will wander the whole earth, he will roam with his other devils and demons—the demons being Iblis's agents, his henchmen—and he will circle the entire earth and say to them, meaning to the other devils: 'O community of devils, we have taken revenge from the progeny of Adam.' Today we have taken revenge from the progeny of Adam. Meaning, by killing Imam Hussain (a.s.), by martyring him, Iblis is saying that we have taken revenge from the progeny of Adam. Now you understand when you read in Ziyarat-e-Waritha who Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (a.s.) is? We salute the Mawla: 'Assalamu alaika ya waritha Adama safwatillah.' Imam Hussain (a.s.) was the heir of Adam (a.s.) whom they killed. Meaning, Iblis was being represented in Karbala by Yazid and Yazid's army, and Adam (a.s.) was being represented by Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions, the martyrs of Karbala. And then Shaitan says, Iblis says to his agents: 'And we have reached the limit of their destruction, and we have made them heirs to evil.' Meaning, all those wicked ones who were involved in Karbala, we have brought them to the limit of destruction. Except for whom? 'Except those who have held fast to this group,' meaning those who have held onto the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), who have firmly grasped their hem. Only those we will not be able to bring to destruction because these people have held onto the hem of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.). So now, what should you do? Iblis is saying to the other devils: 'Make this your occupation.' Now you become busy. Busy with what? 'By casting doubts among the people regarding them.' Incite people, force them to be hostile towards them. 'And incite them against them and their followers.' Now you understand where those fatwas come from? Where do all those doubts and suspicions come from? This is all the work of Iblis. Therefore, as soon as Muharram arrives, as soon as the days of mourning arrive, as soon as you see that objections are increasing, new objections are coming, understand that this is the work of Iblis. So we must be alert against his attacks, that if anything stops us from Azadari, understand that it is the work of Iblis. And in this way, Iblis says, 'Mislead these people so that misguidance and disbelief become firmly established among the entire creation.' So that they all become misguided. Keep working on them like this. 'And let no one be saved.' And remember, no one should be saved. Meaning, Iblis will come after every mourner, he will come in different guises, he will bring all kinds of objections. But it is our responsibility to save ourselves from his attacks. And then the Mawla says, he says to his daughter Janabe Zainab: 'And Iblis made his assumption come true.' He quotes the Quranic verse that Iblis made his assumption come true, even though he is the biggest liar, 'wa huwa kazubun.' Even though he was a liar, the assumption he had, the expectation he had from people that they would go astray, they did go astray. Meaning, people made Iblis successful. They fell victim to Iblis's doubts and his various attacks. And then the Imam says what? 'Indeed, no good deed will benefit anyone who holds enmity towards you.' And the Mawla is saying to his daughter: 'And no sin will harm anyone who has love and devotion for you, except for major sins.' And what are the major sins? We must be alert about those too. Major sins are called those sins in narrations for which Allah has promised Hell. So we should abstain from all those things and abstain from major sins. So if we abstain from them and have the Wilayah of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), and their love is in our hearts, then that love will help in forgiving other sins and in our intercession. And finally, Zaidah, who is the original narrator of the Hadith, says that after this, when the fourth Imam narrated this entire narration to me, the fourth Imam (a.s.) said: 'After this, O Zaidah, hold onto this.' Hold onto this Hadith firmly. Meaning, tie a knot. Understand this attack of Iblis well. The Imam says: 'Hold onto it.' Grasp this Hadith well, hold it. 'Even if you ride a camel and drive it, and drive it so much that it travels for a year, if you travel on that camel for a year, it would be a small thing.' Compared to this Hadith, that is a very small thing. Meaning, the effort and struggle you put in for a year while sitting on a camel, traveling from here to there, the struggle you will make is a very small thing compared to this. Meaning, the most important thing in these days of mourning is to save yourself from these attacks of Shaitan, to protect yourself. And for protection, we cannot protect ourselves on our own. We protect ourselves with 'A'udhu billahi minash-shaitanir-rajim.' We place ourselves under the protection of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.), who is the protector of the universe, who is the heir of this mourning, who is the heir of Sarkar-e-Aba Abdillah (a.s.). We place ourselves under his protection: 'Mawla, O Sahib-e-Zaman, grant us the opportunity in these days of mourning to shed tears for your grandfather and to establish the mourning of your grandfather. And if anyone tries to distance us from this mourning, we can save ourselves from his tricks and his traps.' Wal-hamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin.

title: E'teraazaate Ghadeer Ep#01 - Eid-e-Ghadeer Manaana Bid'at Hai Ya Sunnat?
excerpt: This lecture series, 'Address-e-Ghadir', addresses common objections regarding the celebration of Eid-e-Ghadir in Islam. The speakers argue that while Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha are established, Ghadir holds a superior status because it marks the perfection of religion and the announcement of Imam Ali's (a.s.) Wilayat. By referencing historical traditions and the Quranic verse of Al-Akmal, the lecture asserts that celebrating Ghadir is a sunnah supported by early Islamic history and the Prophet's own declarations.
content:
Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. Congratulations to all of you on this Eid-e-Ghadir. Let us all together offer congratulations to all the Imams (a.s.) and especially to Syeda Zahra (s.a.) with a Salawat. Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad. We are here once again on behalf of the team with a new series titled 'Address-e-Ghadir'. As you all know, we discuss various objections regarding Ghadir in each meeting so that we can address the misconceptions about Ali (a.s.). So that we can reduce or erase these misconceptions about Ali (a.s.). Through this series, our effort will be to provide you with the arguments and present their answers through the Quran and narrations. Let us move towards our first objection, which is that Muslims have always had two Eids: Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha. This third Eid, which is celebrated as Eid-e-Ghadir, is an innovation (bid'ah) and has no Islamic status. This is the objection. Let's see what the answer is. To answer this, our brother Tajammul is with us. Congratulations to you. Please tell us, is this objection valid, or is there an Islamic basis for this? I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. First of all, I offer my congratulations on this Eid-e-Ghadir. Regarding the question, I would like to say that the purpose of this discussion is to clarify things for those who are watching this program and might have doubts. What kind of objection is this that it is considered necessary to force this? They say these names are not mentioned in the mosque. It is strange that a person celebrates every small joy in their life, but when the greatest joy comes, they refuse to name it. These people celebrate all the small joys that exist within Islam, but they turn away from the greatest joy of Islam. Perhaps this is what is coming between us. The reason we celebrate this Eid is that Muslims celebrate after the month of Ramadan. Fasting in Ramadan is completed, and as a sign of gratitude, they celebrate this, which the Ummah knows as Eid-ul-Fitr. When Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) was ready to sacrifice his son, in memory of that, Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Adha. The Ummah knows this Eid by this name. Although in the month of Ramadan, the religion was not perfected, and the blessings were not completed, yet the Muslim Ummah celebrates after the month of Ramadan. On the other hand, in Eid-ul-Adha, the Hajj is completed, but the religion was not perfected, and no such verse came to any companion's ears that 'Today I have perfected for you...' The religion was not perfected, and no such verse came to any companion's ears that 'Today I have perfected for you...'. If you look at both these Eids, neither is the religion perfected in them, nor is the blessing completed, nor is there any verse from Allah saying 'Today I am pleased with you.' As for the day of Eid-e-Ghadir, if you look at it, the fasting of Ramadan is encompassed in it, and the Hajj is encompassed in it. The entire religion of Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) is encompassed in this day. Today, the religion is being perfected. The religion that had been ongoing for thousands of years, despite all the debates, is being perfected today. Allah is also pleased, the blessing is being completed, and the guidance has been received because today, the announcement of the Wilayat of Ali (a.s.) is being made, in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.)'s... When it was said to write 'Man Kunto Mawla', it was as if God was revealing this verse in the sanctuary. This is an extremely vital and important point. After this announcement, the verse of Al-Akmal (Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 3) was revealed, which says: 'Today, I have perfected your religion for you.' It is a powerful statement regarding this day, where Allah (s.w.t.) says: 'Today, I have perfected your religion, completed My favors upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.' As the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had been conveying the message from the beginning, when this announcement was made on that day, the revelation of this verse at this specific moment signifies that this was the very verse that followed 'Man Kunto Mawla'. It was expected that as soon as the words 'Man Kunto Mawla' were spoken, this Hadith or this announcement would make it clear that on this day, the religion was perfected. You know that the Eid you are celebrating is one that you celebrate after the completion of the Sharia, fulfilling it completely. But today, the entire day shows how Allah Himself, through the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), declared this day to be so important. It also shows that the happiness of the believers is our happiness, and perhaps this is what is called 'completeness'. Regarding this, I want to present to you the testament of this day, which is recorded in the book of a scholar in Damascus, in volume 42. In volume 42, page 234, he narrates a tradition where he says that one should fast on the 18th of Dhu al-Hijjah. He further mentions that Allah will reward the one who fasts on this day with the reward of sixty years of fasting. He speaks about the day when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) presented Ali (a.s.) before the people in the field of Ghadir. He then mentions that the second Caliph of the Muslims congratulated Ali (a.s.) by saying, 'Congratulations to you, O Ali, you have become the master of all believing men and women.' And here, the second Caliph of the Muslims is offering congratulations and celebrating the joy of this day. However, the Muslim Ummah, due to this very history of the second Caliph, perhaps cannot accept this reality. If people hide this truth, they are playing with their own faith and are not following the Quran of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) or the desire of the Messenger of Allah. Now, apart from this, I want to share one last tradition regarding this, in which Ameer al-Mu'minin Ali (a.s.) is mentioned. A scholar brings this Hadith in his book, where he writes that we should celebrate this day in our cities, and he says this quite clearly. Regarding this, it is said that on one hand, where we have the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), and further it is said that the day the announcement of the name was made, on that very day, it was also said that all people—and it is clear from this that those who remembered this day—you will be familiar with a very big name from your books, and number 65 is one that we mention, in which you describe the virtues of this day. title: Qabron Par Masjid Banaana: Ashaab e Kahf Ka Waaqeah
excerpt: This lecture discusses the Quranic narrative of the People of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf) to address the theological debate surrounding the construction of mosques over the graves of righteous individuals. The speaker argues that building places of worship at these sites is a way to honor monotheism and the sacrifices of holy figures rather than an act of polytheism. The talk concludes by connecting this historical precedent to the historical oppression regarding the hidden grave of Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.).
content:
We have received the opportunity. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May Allah's peace and blessings be upon the Prophet (s.a.w.a.). Every Muslim is aware of the incident of the People of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf). This incident is about those individuals who were living in the land of a tyrant and oppressive king who was forcing people to worship him. However, despite the threats to their faith, they did not let go of the truth. They went far away from the city and took refuge in a cave. Allah sealed the cave, cast sleep upon them, and they remained asleep in that cave for a long period. After about 300 years had passed, when people learned of this incident, they debated how to best commemorate them, and it was suggested that a structure should be built. One group suggested that a large structure should be built at this location so that it... A large structure should be built so that this building always reminds them of them. They said, 'Build a structure over them.' Another group believed that a mosque should be built at this place so that it becomes a center for the worship of Allah, because these were the people who waited for the worship of Allah, left the city of the disbelievers, and thus maintained monotheism (Tawheed). Everyone accepted their suggestion. They said, 'We will surely build a mosque over them.' Those who prevailed in this matter said, 'We will surely build a mosque here.' Thus, building mosques and places of worship over the graves of Allah's righteous servants and gathering there for prayer and supplication is indeed Tawheed, which is proven by the Quran. The Prophets and the Masumeen (a.s.) have kept the reality of Tawheed pure and intact throughout their lives. Not only this, they spent their entire lives spreading the message of Tawheed and... Spent their entire lives erasing polytheism and disbelief, to the extent that they even accepted martyrdom for this cause. Building structures like mosques over the graves of Allah's close servants is in no way polytheism; rather, it is a means of appreciating the sacrifices of those personalities. The reality is that keeping the holy shrines of those individuals occupied, and preventing people from praying and seeking supplication in their vicinity, is a form of oppression. Everyone is aware of the high status of Janabe Fatima Zahra (s.a.) and her sacrifices for the religion of Allah. Unfortunately, her blessed grave has also been kept hidden by the enemies of Islam, and to this day, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) is a victim of this oppression. We pray to Allah to hasten the reappearance of Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) so that he may reveal the grave of the Masooma (s.a.). Amen, O Lord of the Worlds. [Music]
