title: Hum Azaa Se Hain | Muharram 2024 | #muharram #Azadar #Husain (a.s.) #محرم
excerpt: This lecture emphasizes the spiritual significance of Muharram and the practice of Azadari as a means to connect with Imam Hussain (a.s.). The speaker encourages believers to deepen their devotion through daily Ziyarat, reading about the tragedy of Karbala, and actively participating in mourning rituals. It concludes by highlighting the importance of offering condolences to Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.) and praying for his reappearance as the ultimate heir of the blood of Hussain.
content:
A'udhu billahis-sami'il-alimi minash-shaitanir-rajim, Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim. Wa sallallahu alaika ya waliyyal-asr, adrikna wala tuhlikna. Assalamu alal-Husain wa ala Ali ibnil-Husain wa ala awladil-Husain wa ala as-habil-Husain. Hazrat Imam-e-Raza (a.s.) says that whenever the month of Muharram began, my father, Imam Musa ibne Jafar (a.s.), was never seen smiling. Intense grief would overwhelm him, until ten days passed in this manner. And when the day of Ashura arrived, it would be a day of intense grief and weeping for him, and he would say that this is the day on which Imam Hussain (a.s.) was martyred. Another month of Muharram, the month of mourning, has arrived. Thanks to Allah that He has granted us the opportunity to weep and perform Azadari for the oppressed of Karbala, Sarkar-e-Sayyid-ush-Shuhada Hazrat-e-Aba Abdillahil-Husain (a.s.) and the martyrs of Karbala. It is certain that the cause of our Azadari is the Mawaddat and love for Hazrat-e-Imam Hussain (a.s.) that resides in our hearts. Based on this Mawaddat and love, we weep over his tragedy, perform Matam, and bring out the Alam, Taboot, and Tazia, and also offer our condolences. And why shouldn't they be, for the Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) himself stated: 'There is a heat in the hearts of the believers for Hussain (a.s.) that will never cool.' This is the same heat that we have inherited from our ancestors in the form of Azadari. Therefore, it is our request to all Azadars that just as our elders used to perform Azadari, we too should observe these rituals with complete devotion. Through this Azadari, we should strive to draw closer to the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). This Aza is our identity, our strength, and our survival, because Aza is not from us; we are from Aza. Let us pay attention to a few things that can help us in observing Azadari and strengthening our bond with Hazrat Aba Abdillah al-Hussain (a.s.). Converse with Imam Hussain (a.s.). Dedicate a portion of your day or night to converse with Imam Hussain (a.s.) and promise him that for his sake, you will begin a good deed or, as much as possible, abstain from sins. We can forsake lies, immodesty, and countless other sins solely for the sake of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Recite the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) daily, whether it is Ziyarat-e-Warisa or Ziyarat-e-Ashura. Especially during the first ten days, when you recite the Ziyarat, reflect upon its words, meanings, and concepts, which describe the status and station of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Read a book related to the tragedy of Karbala. After consulting with a religious scholar, choose a book regarding Karbala and read it during the days of Aza. Especially books that describe the biography of Imam Hussain (a.s.), his status, his suffering, the events of Karbala and the subsequent events in Kufa and Sham, and the traditions of our Infallible Imams (a.s.) regarding Azadari. These books will be a cause for increasing our Ma'rifat (gnosis) regarding Imam Hussain (a.s.) and his companions. Expressing grief is essential. We should express our mourning and Azadari for Imam Hussain (a.s.) with our entire being so that others living in our society also know that we are in mourning. Wear black clothes, place the Alam of Hazrat Abbas (a.s.) on your homes, put up black sheets and curtains, and let the sounds of Nauhas and Marsiyas come from your homes so that it is known that this house and the people living in it are in a state of mourning. Spread the message of Karbala. During these days of grief, especially the first ten days, try to talk to people as much as possible about Karbala, Imam Hussain (a.s.), his oppression, and his revolution. Try to convey this message to your family members, friends, and other members of society. Attend the Majalis of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Attend Majalis daily; go yourself and take your family members, especially children, to the Farsh-e-Aza. It is better to attend as many Majalis as possible. Despite all your engagements, try to attend at least two Majalis a day for the sake of Imam Hussain (a.s.). Always keep in mind that Satan will try to create obstacles in this path. Therefore, we must remain vigilant against his attacks. Participate in the tasks of Azadari. Participate in any way you can in establishing the Azadari of Imam Hussain (a.s.). For example, arranging Nazr-o-Niyaz, setting up Sabeels in the name of Imam Hussain (a.s.), serving water to people, or inviting Anjumans to your home or Imambargah for Matam and Nauha-khwani. If, due to some compulsion, believers in any area are facing obstacles in establishing Azadari, help them in any way possible so that they too can participate in this Aza. Finally, the most important and necessary point, and I request special attention to this. If an elder passes away in a house, their family is offered condolences (Pursa). Therefore, when we observe the Aza of Sayyidush-Shuhada Imam Hussain (a.s.), offer Pursa to his heir and the Imam of our time, Hazrat Baqiyatullah al-Azam Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and do not forget to pray for his glorious reappearance. When there are tears of grief for Hussain in your eyes, pray for the reappearance of the Imam of your time with those same tearful and grieving eyes. Because he is the true heir of this Aza and the avenger of the blood of Hussain. If we want to gauge the pain and suffering our Imam is in, reflect on how he remembered Imam Hussain (a.s.) in Ziyarat-e-Nahiya, where Imam-e-Zamana (a.t.f.s.) says: 'Fa la-andubannaka sabahan wa masa'an wa la-abkiyanna 'alayka badalad-dumu'i dama' (So I will lament for you morning and evening, and I will weep for you blood instead of tears).' O Allah, for the sake of the oppression of Imam Hussain (a.s.), hasten the reappearance of the Imam of our time, Hazrat Imam Mahdi (a.t.f.s.), and grant us the Taufiq to observe the Azadari of Sarkar Aba Abdillah al-Hussain (a.s.) this year and every year. Because, Allah (s.w.t.) has stated in the Holy Quran: 'Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim. Wa ma khalaqtul jinna wal insa illa liya'budun.' Allah (s.w.t.) has created humans and jinn only for His worship.

title: 8 Rabi ul-Awwal 1442 | Majlis e Aza | Shahadat e Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) | Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi
excerpt: This lecture by Dr. Shabeeb Rizvi commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), exploring his life, spiritual stature, and the challenges faced during his confinement in Samarra. The discourse highlights the Imam's divine dignity in the face of Abbasid oppression and his crucial role in preparing the Shia community for the period of occultation. Furthermore, the session emphasizes the moral responsibility of believers to support one another's faith and provides reflections on the sacrifices of the Ahlulbayt.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the Master of the Prophets, our Master and Prophet, Abul Qasim Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), and upon his pure and purified progeny. Imam... [Music] ...and upon his progeny. ...the disbelievers... [Recitation of Quranic verses] ... ...like they return home in the evening. The martyrdom of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), and as you know, he was one of those Imams who was very young, and he was martyred at a very young age. The answer to the birth of the Imam (a.s.) is... The answer to the birth of the Imam (a.s.) is in 232 AH, and he was born in Samarra in 232 AH, and his martyrdom also took place in Samarra. Why are you called 'Askari'? The reason is that 'Askar' means an army camp in Urdu. Where there is an army, where there is a cantonment area, it is called 'Urdu' in Urdu, and 'Askar' in Arabic. Because Imam Askari (a.s.) was kept in a military camp in Samarra by the rulers of that time, he became known as 'Askari'. Therefore, both of these... As you know, Imam Ali al-Naqi (a.s.) was in the village, and his mother, Salil, was from there. Regarding the Imam (a.s.), peace be upon him, he was a source of guidance. He was a light that illuminates itself so that it may illuminate others. So that it may illuminate others, and many people used to seek him for their physical and spiritual needs. He acted according to the pleasure of Allah, and the pleasure of Allah means that which is in accordance with His will. As for his appointment, the greatest authority and the greatest appointment is from Allah, and these people know that those appointed by Allah are the true guides. It is said that you are the ones from whom the light of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) shines. Through them, the treasures of knowledge are opened, and they are the ones who invite others to the path of Allah. They are the ones who reach the destination through their guidance, and through them, the mercy of Allah descends upon the people. The perfections of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) are within them. They possess the patience of Musa (a.s.), the perfections of Isa (a.s.), and the endurance of Ayyub (a.s.). In their time, there were enemies who killed and burned them, yet they remained steadfast in their mission, even as their blood was shed. Their blood was shed, and this continued constantly. There are so few people who know the extent of their perfections, to the point that even their enemies, upon seeing their greatness, are forced to bow their heads in respect. This was the case with the representative of the Abbasid Caliph, who was a governor. This governor, despite being an enemy, could not help but admire his dignity, his calmness, his patience, and his generosity. He was like a full moon; everyone respected him, and even the Bani Hashim treated him with great reverence, more so than they did for others who were older or held positions of power. I was standing near my father when he arrived. I saw that my father used to stand at the door to welcome him. Then, he called out, 'O Abu Muhammad!' I was astonished. I wondered, how could he address him so informally in front of my father? No one dared to call him by his name in my father's presence. No one had the courage to address him so casually in front of my father, who was a governor. But when my father saw him, his appearance was so handsome and his presence so majestic that my father stood up from his place. He stood up, even though he was a man of high status and had many enemies. He walked towards him slowly. I had never seen my father treat anyone from the Bani Hashim or any commander with such respect. As Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) approached, my father embraced him, kissed his forehead and chest, held his hand, and seated him in his own place. However, the others did not receive such treatment. When he left, my father instructed his servants to honor the Caliph's representative. Later, I gathered the courage to ask my father, 'Who was that man whom you honored so greatly?' Until that time, who was he that you gave so much to? Such pressure, such respect—it was for my and the other states. And he is famous by the name of Amino-ur-Rehman. He remained silent for a while, and then he started saying, 'No, if the mind and the opposition are removed, then there is no one.' He said that he is not interested in his own position, his own status, or his own opposition, but rather in his worship, his character, and his other virtues. And this, even from his childhood, hearing his father's words, just as my... Hearing his father's words, just as I was astonished and became perplexed, I became restless. And as I pondered over these things, I wondered, 'What kind of things is he saying?' But along with that, a desire arose in me to investigate. When I started doing this, I asked him questions again, and again, and again. And whoever I was talking to, even today, that person was praising him without any reason, honoring him, respecting him, talking about his father's greatness, and talking about the good things of his character. And he was saying that there is no one like him, and in the world, there is no one greater than him. Every person was honoring him, and I was seeing that whoever I talked to, whether... Whether it was an enemy or a friend, every person was saying good things about him, and only and only praising him, helping him, and honoring him. This is a very strange thing. The Abbasids, who were always trying to humiliate him and disgrace him so that they could prove that they were the rightful heirs to the Imamate and Caliphate, built a very large palace. They kept many wild animals and beautiful things there, and they had prepared everything for him. They had invited the people and prepared the animals so that when the Imam (a.s.) would try to speak, these animals would make noise, they would make so much sound that the Imam... They would make so much sound that the Imam would not be able to speak, would not be able to speak. And the Abbasid's effort was to somehow humiliate the Imam. And when they would not be able to humiliate the Imam, they would laugh, mock, and make fun of the Imam. The Imam (a.s.) was called to that palace. When the Imam arrived, the Abbasid thought that just as his plan and his scheme were, it would happen. But as soon as the Imam said, 'Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim,' there was complete silence. The animals became silent, and then when the Imam started to speak, and after the Imam finished his speech, the Imam got up and left. Now, the Imam's... peace be upon him... Peace be upon him. They knew that his life was very short, and they knew that the Imam (a.s.) was going to be the one who would go into occultation, and the government, even up to that point, had to live like the oppressed. Because of the fear of the Abbasids, he had to live in hiding. Therefore, they have to do this; this character changes life. How much patience the Imam (a.s.) had, and Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) is the only one who got the opportunity to perform Hajj physically. So, if anyone gets the chance, then he... if... If he is in the company of our Imam, once the Imam (a.s.) continuously sent messages to his Shias, saying, 'Look, the era of the occultation of the Imam of the Age will begin, and you will have to wait for the reappearance of the Imam of the Age.' And in the cities, and I am also coming, the Imam (a.s.) says that the Shias should submit this entire report, wait for the reappearance. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said, 'My Ummah, and in this era of occultation, my Shias will remain in trouble and anxiety until my son...' That my son is the one about whom the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) gave the glad tidings, gave the good news. The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said that this is my son. So, he told all the Shias that the occultation of the Imam of the Age is certain because this earth belongs to Allah, and Allah gives the inheritance of the earth to whomever He wants among His servants. And for your guidance, the oppressors and... Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon you. The Imam (a.s.) ended the matter right there, and there was a will, and this was the will that the Imam (a.s.) met with the Imam of the Age. Met him. So, when they met, the Imam of the Age (a.t.f.s.) said to him, 'My noble ancestors have accepted from me that I am in distant lands so that I may be hidden from the people and safe from the conspiracies of the misguided and their accusations.' And after that, the Imam (a.s.) said, following his father's will, 'Allah will bring back those whose hearts are filled with your love, just as birds return to their nests in the evening.' Now look, a bird, no matter where it stays all day, returns to its nest in the evening. Whoever loves our Imam, no matter how much he goes here and there, in the evening, he returns to his Imam. And this... Returns to his Imam. This might be in the eyes of the world, but in the sight of Allah, it will be a great status. And this will be the person who, in the world, will be considered to have no status, from Mecca, that people will think they have no status, and they will be in the middle, and they start their work, they remember their Imam day and night. The Imam (a.s.) continuously told his Shias that all this, all this, and you will have to face all these troubles. And the second thing that the Imam (a.s.) emphasized a lot was that in the era of the occultation, one should try to help the orphans, the weak. And strengthen their faith, so this work is done. In the traditions of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), whoever takes care of the orphans of the family of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.), whoever takes care of them, those Ahlulbayt (a.s.) who are away from their Imam, whose Imam is in occultation, he is like an orphan. So, the Imam (a.s.) says that this is because he is away from his Imam, he can be away from his Imam, and he is wandering in the darkness of the occultation. So, this person who comes out and removes his doubts, who removes the doubts, and helps him, then I give him a reward like a police officer, and those Nasibis who continuously spread propaganda, he saves them from those Nasibis, and he also strengthens him so that he can face the Nasibis. is that he can compete with the seeds. This existing door that is present, all this, and this caretaker, meaning the intellectual and spiritual caretaker, this caretaker of the people, our department that takes care of our affairs, the virtue of the one who fulfills these needs, who fulfills the needs of the orphans, who fulfills their physical needs, his virtue is like the virtue of the sun over the stars. The stars are small stars in the sky, which do not even have much light; they are called 'nayshar' (dim stars). The importance that the sun has over these stars, in the same way, this virtue of the orphan (caretaker) has over the one who only fulfills material needs. How great is the responsibility of the educated, so they should fulfill it, everyone... The responsibility of the educated is that they should fulfill it. Everyone, as much as they can do things. Now look, this picture... this picture is of 120 Jalal-ud-din, it is written in the books. This picture, but not immediately, later. And all these people in this school, they should subscribe and tell their friends. There were two young men who were workers in that class, and other people also used to come to that class, but out of them, two individuals, they started this. The reason for it was that there was something present there... that was misleading, it was inciting that 'this is like this, that is like this'. So, the one who was the ruler, he used to talk about his matters, therefore he left that side and this family, they are the ones who kept their belongings. And those who had kept their belongings or were in the inns, as they were called in those days, the travelers' lodges—both of them returned and presented themselves to the Imam (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) said, 'We are cautious, and our intention is to let you stay; you people go back. Now, your responsibility is over. The man who was constantly complaining is finished; his end has come. And now the vizier, the ruler, the governor, has stopped oppressing the Shia. You go, and if you want—or rather, if you have come from such a great distance—then both of you go and leave these two sons here.' When they were informed that your words were true, they said, 'I will leave these two sons with you.' I will tell you the rest of the story, which will make the whole picture clear. A week later, they departed, leaving their two sons in Samarra, and after traveling a short distance, they received news of how the one who was constantly complaining had been killed and had fallen. He continued to write, and how he was struck down, and as he fell—subscribe to the young boys, subscribe—and along with them, revise the peace, so that they would perform the idol immersion of the ice statue. Subscribe to the 274 Puri, and subscribe to the address in this way. These boys wrote this for years, and how it was written, you can write as long as you have the strength to write. As long as you have the courage to write, you will continue to increase, and the mother continued to increase it daily, O brother. O brother, it is a matter worthy of mention. The kings of the time were watching all this, and they were beginning to understand that when these people come near, they want to entice the people so that they do not feel the burden. Both decided that Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)—it was decided that Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) should be poisoned. It is found that poison was mixed and given to him. It is said that in front of the eyes, the Imam's breath began to fade slowly, and the Imam departed from this world. The picture of the Imam's martyrdom was clear; General Raheel Sharif properly—subscribe and you subscribe, someone... You subscribed, and someone did not subscribe to the corpse, but my Mawla Hussain (a.s.) was martyred in such a way, and the scene was being watched by the eyes, and a voice asked when the speed of the movement was slow. You people, give the status of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) and along with it the status of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The Imam of the time sends salutations, I click on the mosque, and I shed blood instead of tears. So you are the one whose head was separated from the body. Ah, now we must remove the veil. When the cover was removed, what do we see? Oh father, peace be upon you. You have come back. May Allah remove the troubles of those who are worried daily. Wherever they are appointed, subscribe to them.

title: Best Way To Follow Ahle Bait (a.s.) | Akhlaaq-e-Ahle Bait (a.s.)
excerpt: This lecture explores the methodology for following the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) by focusing on the revival of their teachings. Citing a tradition from Imam Ali ar-Rida (a.s.), the speaker emphasizes that the primary duty of a believer is to learn the knowledge of the Imams and propagate it to others. By sharing the beautiful and profound speech of the Ahlul-Bayt, believers can naturally attract hearts toward the path of the Imams.
content:
Bismillah-hir-Rahman-nir-Rahim. Wa sallallahu 'alayka ya Waliyyul Asr, adriknā wa la tuhliknā. Allama Majlisi (r.a.) narrates from Sheikh Saduq (r.a.) in his book 'Ma'ani al-Akhbar' through Aba Salt al-Harawi that Aba Salt heard our and your eighth Imam, Abul Hassan Ali ibn Musa ar-Rida (a.s.), saying: 'May Allah have mercy on the servant who revives our affairs.' Aba Salt asked the Imam, 'Mawla, how are your affairs revived?' The Mawla replied, 'Learn our knowledge and teach it to the people.' Then Imam (a.s.) said: 'Fa inna-n-nasa law 'alimu mahasina kalamina la-ttaba'una' (If people knew the beauty of our speech, they would surely follow us). Therefore, if we want people to become obedient to the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), it is necessary for us to first learn the speech of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), i.e., the Hadith of Ale-Muhammad (a.s.), reflect upon it, contemplate it, and convey it to the people without fearing the blame of any critic. The more we convey these words to people, the more their hearts will incline towards the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.). Wa sallallahu 'ala Muhammadin wa alihi-tayyibina-t-tahirin-al-ma'sumin.

title: #1 - Ziyaarat-e-Arbaeen Mein Imam Husain (a.s.) Ki Ma’refat | Sharh-e-Ziyaarat-e-Arbaeen [ENG SUBS]
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of performing Ziyarat-e-Arbaeen with true recognition (Ma'refat) of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The speaker emphasizes that the key to attaining divine forgiveness and Paradise is understanding the status of the Imam as described in the Ziyarat texts. By analyzing the opening salutations of Ziyarat Arbaeen, the lecture highlights the titles of Wali, Habib, Safiy, and Amin, which establish the Imam's unique proximity to Allah. Ultimately, the session encourages believers to internalize these divine attributes to deepen their spiritual connection during pilgrimage.
content:
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon you, O Ali, and upon the children of Ali. Peace be upon Hussain, and upon the children of Hussain. Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) stated: 'Man ata qabra Hussain (a.s.) arifan bi haqqihi falahu al-jannah' (Whoever comes to the grave of Hussain (a.s.) with the recognition of his right, for him is Paradise). It is clear from the words of Imam Sadiq (a.s.) that if we want the Almighty Allah to forgive all our past and future sins, it is our responsibility to go for his Ziyarat with the recognition of Imam Hussain (a.s.). The best way to attain the recognition of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is through the Ziyarat texts themselves, which were uttered by the tongues of the Masumeen (a.s.). Therefore, let us try to recognize the status and great rank of Imam Hussain (a.s.) through the Ziyarat of Arbaeen so that we can perform his Ziyarat with recognition and through this, attain the forgiveness of Allah. so that through this, Allah's forgiveness and mercy may encompass us. The opening phrases of Ziyarat Arbaeen are: 'Assalamu ala wali-Allah, Assalamu ala habib-Allah, Assalamu ala safiy-Allah, Assalamu ala amini-Allah.' Peace be upon the Wali (friend/guardian) of Allah and His beloved. Peace be upon the friend of Allah and His confidant. Peace be upon the chosen servant of Allah and the son of His chosen servant. 'Salam' is a form of prayer and an excellent way of greeting. Here, the first station of the recognition of Imam Hussain (a.s.) is that he is also the Wali of Allah, just as in verse 55 of Surah Al-Ma'idah, the leader of the believers is called a Wali. And he is also His beloved, meaning the Lord of the Worlds has a special attachment to Imam Hussain (a.s.). Similarly, friend... a special attachment to Imam Hussain (a.s.). Similarly, the terms 'friend' and 'confidant' are used for one who holds a special proximity. Allah granted Prophet Ibrahim (a.s.) the status of His Khalil, meaning friend, in the Holy Quran, and in these phrases, the same station is described for Imam Hussain (a.s.). Likewise, 'Safiy-Allah' means the chosen one of Allah, and the word 'Mustafa' is also derived from this word 'Safiy'. One of the names of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) is Mustafa. In verse 33 of Surah Aal-e-Imran, the family of Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim, and the family of Imran (a.s.) are described as the chosen ones of Allah. In this phrase of Ziyarat Arbaeen, the same status is granted to Imam Hussain (a.s.). Therefore, whenever we go for the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) and stand before his blessed grave to offer him Salam, it should be in our minds that we are offering Salam to that noble personality who is the chosen one of Allah, His friend, His beloved, and His confidant. May the Lord of the Worlds grant us this recognition... His confidant. May the Lord of the Worlds grant us the opportunity to perform the Ziyarat of Imam Hussain (a.s.) with this recognition. Ameen, Ya Rabb.

Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says, 'In the world of Barzakh, on the day of Jumu'ah, the souls of the deceased come and stand, and while weeping and lamenting, they say: O my relatives, O my family, O my children, O my loved ones, have mercy on us, even if it is through something small, Allah will have mercy on you.' We must remember this point. We should not forget in our prayers to say, 'Have mercy on us and our group,' because we are in an era where the past is forgotten. We are in such a state that we are stingy in praying for those who have passed away. Do not be stingy in praying for us so that Allah may have mercy on us, before you also come to be like us. Before you also come to be like us. This is a thought: today, just as you have wealth, tomorrow we could have had the same. O servants of Allah, listen to our words carefully and do not forget us, because tomorrow you will also know that what is in your hands today, that time of wealth, used to be with us too. But we did not spend it in the way of Allah, and we were not deserving. Therefore, now it has become a burden for us and has proven beneficial for others. Have mercy on us, even if it is through a small deed. Imam (a.s.) says that after this, they will say, 'Very soon you will also weep for yourselves, but your weeping will not benefit you, just as we are weeping, but now our weeping is not benefiting us.' Before you also come to be like us, because my Mawla, the leader of the believers, in the team of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.)... in the team of Muhammad (s.a.w.a.) has verified the truth.

title: Tafseer Noor al-Saqalain | Session # 7 | Tafseer of Surah al-Faatiha (Surah # 1) - Part 7
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound meaning of 'Sirat al-Mustaqim' (the Straight Path) in Surah al-Fatiha through the lens of Shia tradition. The speaker emphasizes that the path is intrinsically linked to the recognition and Wilayah of the Imams, particularly Imam Ali (a.s.). By following their guidance in this world, believers prepare themselves to traverse the bridge of the Hereafter, ensuring their salvation.
content:
And Allah is the Truth, the Great. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. Peace and blessings be upon the best of His creation, our Prophet Muhammad and his pure progeny. Peace be upon you all. Once again, I am here with the explanation of Surah Al-Fatiha. The explanation I gave previously will be available in the recordings, and those who have not seen it can watch the third clip. Our discussion was regarding 'Sirat al-Mustaqim' (the straight path). When Prophet Muhammad Mustafa (s.a.w.a.) was asked, he said, 'Allah has favored me by guiding me to it.' Surah Al-Fatiha and 'Sirat al-Mustaqim' refer to the path of those upon whom Allah has bestowed His favors. refers to the path of those upon whom Allah has bestowed His favors. There is also a Hadith from Imam Ridha (a.s.) that 'Sirat al-Mustaqim' refers to the path that leads a servant to the guidance of the religion and increases his certainty and knowledge of Allah. It means: O Lord, keep us firm on the path You are guiding us to. Keep us firm on the straight path, the path that leads to Him. Keep us firm on that path and do not let us deviate. In many commentaries, the meaning of 'Sirat' is the Book of Allah, and the same meaning is narrated from the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) and Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.). It is the Book of Allah, but it is not just that. When Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) was asked about 'Sirat al-Mustaqim', he said, 'It refers to the path of the Imam and the recognition of the Imam.' In this book, Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) also said in one place, 'We are that Sirat al-Mustaqim.' I swear by Allah, we are the Sirat al-Mustaqim. Meaning, the Imam is the Sirat al-Mustaqim; the path of the Imam is the Sirat al-Mustaqim. If we are attached to them, their Wilayah, and are acting upon the path shown by them, then we are walking on the Sirat al-Mustaqim. But if anyone leaves even one Imam, they have deviated from the Sirat al-Mustaqim and will wander away from the path of Allah. This is a matter to be known. Another Hadith from Imam Jafar Sadiq (a.s.) says that 'Sirat al-Mustaqim' refers to the Commander of the Faithful (Ali) and his recognition. The proof for this is that Allah said, 'And indeed, he is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.' In our tradition, the Mother of the Book is Surah Al-Fatiha, and in Surah Al-Fatiha, 'Sirat al-Mustaqim' refers to the Commander of the Faithful. Ponder that the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), is the path. Whoever is attached to Ali will be able to walk on the straight path; whoever distances themselves from Ali will deviate from that straight path, and whoever deviates from the straight path, their destination is Hell. Another narration from Imam Jafar Sadiq... Regarding another narration, when the police officer asked about the 'Sirat' (Path) according to Islam, you (the Imam) replied: 'By this, the path of the Hereafter is meant, and the paths are two: one is the path of this world, and one is the path of the Hereafter.' One might think, 'What if someone gets confused, as you previously said this refers to the Imams?' You explained that through the Imams, you are referring to the path of God, so both statements are correct and not contradictory. There is a need to reflect on this. The reflection needed is that the recognition (Ma'rifat) of God cannot be attained unless one is connected to Ali (a.s.), connected to the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and connected to the Imams after him. Without that, one cannot attain the recognition of God. Our recognition of God is tied to following their path. You state that in this world, the path of truth is the Imam, whose authority is from God. Whoever attains the recognition of this Imam in this world and follows his guidance will be on that path, and on the Day of Judgment, he will be on the Sirat (the bridge). Who will be on it? The one who followed the Imam and the Imam's authority will be on it, because only the one who follows the Imam finds the right path. Only the one who follows the Imam finds the right path. And if he does not attain the recognition of the Imam in this world, then on the Day of Judgment, the Sirat will collapse under him, and he will be thrown into Hell. So, it becomes clear that if we want to enter the recognition of God, we must follow the Imam. If we follow the Imam, we will surely cross the Sirat, and if we do not follow the Imam, we cannot cross it because the recognition of God will not be attained. There is a famous narration in 'Tafsir-e-Ayyashi' where Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) said regarding the Sirat: 'Its width will be like a thousand years, its descent will be a thousand years, and its flat part will be equal to a distance of a thousand years.' Now, reflect on this. In another narration, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) was asked about the path, and he said: 'It is thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword.' Some people will cross it with the speed of lightning, some will cross it like galloping horses, some will cross it on foot, some will cross it on their hands, feet, and bellies, and some will cross it while being scorched and burnt. The fire will burn a part of their bodies and... The fire will burn a part of their bodies and leave them on it. These are different levels of deeds that the Imam (a.s.) has described. It may be that whoever has the status, whoever has attained the recognition, and whoever has followed and obeyed more, will have a different experience. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) says in another hadith: 'The Straight Path (Sirat al-Mustaqim) is Amir al-Mu'minin (Ali).' The conclusion is that the Straight Path is Ali (a.s.). Apart from him, no one can attain the Straight Path. It is mentioned in the commentary of 'Tafsir-e-Ayyashi' that while interpreting 'Ihdinas Sirat al-Mustaqim', he said: 'The Sirat is of two types. O God, continue the series of Your grace through which we became worthy of Your obedience. Grant us Your grace so that we may continue to obey You in our lives.' The Sirat al-Mustaqim is two-fold: one is the Sirat al-Mustaqim that is in this world, which is free from excess and deficiency and is perfectly straight, and... Free from deficiency and is perfectly straight, and does not incline even a bit to either side. And the Sirat al-Mustaqim of the Hereafter is the complete path of the Imam that leads them to Paradise, and it is as such that it does not lead to the other side, which is Hell. Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil 'alamin.

title: Unka Naqeeb Kaun Aur Hamara Khateeb Kaun? | Maulana Meesam Zaidi Sahab Ka Aham Paighaam
excerpt: Maulana Meesam Zaidi discusses a historical narration found in the works of Nasir al-Din al-Albani regarding the Prophet's daughter and the implications of his teachings. The lecture highlights the lack of courage among some scholars to publicly acknowledge historical truths that contradict their established narratives. The speaker emphasizes the importance of speaking the truth, even when it is controversial or risks offending others.
content:
There is a book written by Nasir al-Din al-Albani, and many of our scholars and speakers keep referring to that book. In one of his books, he wrote—I have seen it in his own book—that when the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) migrated from Mecca to Medina, the Prophet's eldest daughter, whose name is Zaynab... some people hold the view that he had four daughters. In our Shia school of thought, the accepted view is that these daughters—Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, and Ruqayyah—were not the daughters of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), but were the daughters of Khadija's sister, Hala. And he writes that when Islam... Were not the daughters of the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), but were the daughters of Khadija's sister, Hala. And he writes that when Islam... [music]... has no connection to the daughter of the Prophet. But I read in the book that the Prophet's eldest daughter, Zaynab, set out from Mecca to Medina on a camel. When the Quraish found out that one of the Prophet's daughters was migrating from Mecca to Medina, they surrounded her and started to harass her. He writes that there was a daughter of the Prophet named Zaynab, and she was successful in her migration, which is why she was able to go from Mecca to Medina. In this way, she went from Mecca to Medina. The Prophet of Islam (s.a.w.a.) had permitted it, which proves that the Prophet of Islam... [inaudible]... He says that the Prophet addressed all the people and stated the remaining part, and then said: 'Look, if any of you ever gain power over your enemies, do not seek the excuse of my permission to kill them.' So the Prophet explained that if someone gains power over an enemy, they should not look for an excuse to get his permission, because if the Prophet's permission is there, then it will be done. Nasir al-Din al-Albani says: 'When I read this narration, I went to my teacher, whose name was... some say it was this, some say it was that... in the field of Hadith, Nasir al-Din al-Albani says: 'I called my teacher, Nasir al-Din al-Albani, to my house and placed the book in front of him and said, 'Read this narration.' He read the narration. I asked him, 'Tell me, what conclusion did you draw after reaching this narration? What did you find?'' What did you find? Nasir al-Din al-Albani said to me: 'It is clear that after reading this narration, only one conclusion can be drawn: if the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) had permitted it at that time, then when the Prophet's martyred daughter had the door pushed upon her... if the Prophet had permitted it then, it would have been necessary for the one who pushed the door to be killed.' Nasir al-Din al-Albani says: 'I said to my teacher, Nasir al-Din al-Albani, 'With your permission, may I state this issue to people by mentioning your name?'' Nasir al-Din al-Albani said: 'I have stated it to you, but I do not give you permission. Because it is a matter of my status, it is a matter of my honor. If you state it in front of someone, I will confirm it, otherwise, I will categorically deny it.' These words are understandable... there is no courage to say it... there is no courage to say it. In front of you, we roam all over India and hold gatherings, but often at such places, it happens that if we have to go with the truth, people will be offended, this will happen, that will happen, they will get angry, they will not... They will get angry, they will not... the mirror of history will be shattered. You speak of deep statements and results, and in your statements, you should speak the truth. You keep it to yourself. I am taking only one sentence from this. If you don't speak, then who will? Nasir al-Din al-Albani is not a Shia, but even then, those who are anti-Shia, who give fatwas against those who pushed the door on the martyred daughter of the Prophet, they do not have the courage to say it. They do not have the courage. If we follow the path of truth, then their... [inaudible]... on the enemies of the city... [inaudible]... meaning...

chapters.title: The Quranic Status of Knowledge
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the Quranic distinction between the learned and the ignorant, emphasizing that Allah elevates the status of believers who possess knowledge.

chapters.title: Obligation and Excellence of Knowledge

title: Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer Ka Sawaab Likhte Likhte Farishte Thak Jaate Hain
excerpt: This lecture highlights the immense spiritual rewards associated with reciting Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer, particularly during the month of Ramadan. The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explains that reciting this supplication even once grants the believer protection from Hellfire and secures their entry into Paradise. Furthermore, the recitation leads to divine guardianship, where angels are appointed to protect the believer from sin and calamity throughout their life.
content:
The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.a.) says: 'O Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.), which servant who recites this supplication keeps his angels busy writing his good deeds and erasing his sins?' Then the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) says: 'O my believers, there is no one from my Ummah who recites this supplication in the month of Ramadan, even if it is three times or even just once, but Allah declares Hellfire forbidden upon that servant's body. Paradise is made obligatory for him. He has a great status near Allah. And then another reward is obtained: whoever recites this supplication, Allah appoints two angels for him who protect him from committing sins, praise and glorify Allah, protect that servant from all calamities, open one of the doors of Paradise for him, and close the doors of Hell for him. And this continues as long as he is alive. And when the time of his death arrives, he remains in the protection of Allah. Ajirna minan-nar ya Rabb, ya Rabb.'
Reciting Dua-e-Jaushan-e-Kabeer in Ramadan forbids Hellfire upon the believer.
Paradise becomes obligatory for those who recite this supplication.

The supplication provides lifelong protection from committing sins.
Reciters are shielded from worldly calamities and dangers.
Divine protection continues for the believer until the moment of death.
The recitation opens the doors of Paradise and closes the doors of Hell.

title: EP04 | Bay'at-e-Ghadeer | 💐 GHADEER: PAYMAAN-E-ILAAHI MEGA QUIZ 2024💐
excerpt: This lecture explores the profound significance of the event of Ghadir Khumm, focusing on the divine command for the pledge of allegiance (Bay'ah) to Imam Ali (a.s.). It details the authenticity of the Ghadir sermon, the necessity of Wilayah for the completion of faith, and the eternal nature of the Imamate chain. The session emphasizes the duty of believers to uphold this covenant, recognize the Ahlul-Bayt, and propagate the message of Ghadir as a core component of religious practice.
content:

I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. And may Allah's blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, reach us and do not destroy us. Respected and honorable listeners and dear viewers, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Praise be to Allah who made us among those who hold fast to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams from his progeny. Infinite praise to that Great and Exalted God who kept us all attached to the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), and the Imams (a.s.) from his progeny, and along with this, granted the ability, the fortune, and the honor that today, once again, in the fourth episode of Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi, we are present in your service while discussing his Wilayah. Respected dear ones, if we reflect on the history of Islam, how the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) announced the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) in his 23 years of propagation. From the invitation of Dawat-e-Zul-Ashira to the event of Tabuk and other places, the Messenger of Allah announced the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). So much so that in the field of Ghadir, among 125,000 pilgrims, he clearly announced the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). But the event of Ghadir is also special because here, not only was the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) announced, but the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) ordered the people to pledge allegiance (Bay'ah) to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), and in the long sermon which is famous as Khutbah-e-Ghadir, he gave statements regarding the Bay'ah. And today, in our discussion, a few things will be presented regarding Ghadir and the Bay'ah of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) in it—what is the consequence if someone breaks the Bay'ah, and what is the reward and status of the one who remains steadfast on the Bay'ah. So come, for today's discussion, our dear brother Mr. Ahsan Jafri is present with us in our gathering. Ahsan Bhai, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Gulzar Bhai, first of all, I offer congratulations to you and all our viewers on the occasion of Eid-e-Ghadir, and I also offer heartfelt congratulations to all of you regarding the upcoming Eid-e-Mubahila. Gulzar Bhai, what is this topic of Bay'ah-e-Ghadir, especially what is the mention of Bay'ah found in the Khutbah-e-Ghadir that we are focusing on? The Prophet of Allah (s.a.w.a.) in his long Khutbah-e-Ghadir paid special attention to the fact that all the Muslims present there, the gathering of 125,000 pilgrims, should pledge allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.). Such a lengthy sermon was delivered, and after that, special emphasis was placed on everyone pledging allegiance (Bay'ah) to Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.) there. Yes. Ahsan Bhai, before you discuss the Bay'ah, we would like you to clarify for the viewers how strong the chain of narration (isnad) of this Sermon of Ghadir is, and what is the perspective of the opponents regarding this Sermon of Ghadir? Certainly. Although the Sunni scholars have filled their books with the Hadith of Ghadir—'Man Kunto Mawlahu Fahadha Aliyun Mawla'—the Hadith of Ghadir, the announcement of the Mawla's Wilayah, the verse revealed at Ghadir known as the 'Ayat al-Tabligh', the 'Ayat al-Ikmal' (Al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum), and the verse 'Sa'ala sa'ilun bi-'adhabin waqi'—their books are full of these, and it is clearly written there that this Hadith of Ghadir, in which the Wilayah of the Master of the Universe was announced, is a Mutawatir (consecutive/widely transmitted) Hadith. So, this is the statement of the opponents? Yes, it is absolutely proven from their books that this is a Mutawatir Hadith. Yes. Now, there are many scholars who have recorded this Hadith of Ghadir in their books. Among them, I will mention just a few to move the discussion forward because there is a specific point I want to present to our viewers. If we study their books, in Sunan al-Tirmidhi, through the chain of Zayd ibn Arqam, Hadith number 3713 is mentioned. It is mentioned in Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah. It is mentioned in Tabarani's Mu'jam al-Kabir. Hakim al-Nishapuri has mentioned it in Al-Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn. It is in Durr al-Manthur, in Tafsir Ibn Kathir, in Tafsir al-Alusi, in Tafsir al-Kabir by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, and it is present in Al-Isti'ab fi Ma'rifat al-Ashab, volume 1, page 338. In Muruj al-Dhahab, yes, volume 1, page 346; in Tarikh Madinat Dimashq by Ibn Asakir, it is in volume 42, pages 234 to 237; it is mentioned there. Majma' al-Zawa'id by Haythami also contains it in volume 9, Hadith number 14614. Besides this, it is in Tarikh al-Khulafa and Tarikh Baghdad as well. So, these 10-15 references are just the obvious ones. Meaning, the Hadith of Ghadir is present in all these authentic books of theirs. Now, the interesting point here, and this is our question to their scholars as well, is that when you have admitted that the Hadith of Ghadir is a Mutawatir Hadith—yes, you acknowledge the event of Ghadir, whether you accept it or not, but you have written it in your books. It is written. The event of Ghadir is recorded in the books. The verses of Ghadir are recorded in the books. The Hadith of Ghadir is recorded in the books. But despite stating all these things regarding Ghadir, the complete Sermon of Ghadir is not found in their books. So, the complete Sermon of Ghadir is not there? It is not found. Now, if any person of intellect sees all these hadiths, verses, and commentaries regarding Ghadir, wouldn't the question arise in their mind that when such a lengthy sermon was delivered there, and special arrangements were made to keep the people there and make this announcement, why is that sermon not in their books? Yes. But Alhamdulillah, in our books, our scholars have recorded the complete Sermon of Ghadir. First of all, it is necessary to note that people have recorded that a lengthy sermon was delivered. Everything—that the Bay'ah was taken, the sermon was delivered, the announcement of the Mawla's Wilayah was made, the 'Man Kunto Mawla' hadith was there—everything is present. Everything is present, but the entire long sermon is not there. The sermon is not there. No. And this is our question: why did you draw a veil over that sermon? Yes. There is something that is being hidden. Indeed. But our scholars have properly recorded that entire sermon. The first scholar among us who recorded this sermon completely, narrated the hadith from Imam Baqir (a.s.), and the entire sermon was recorded, and it was recorded by Sheikh Tabarsi (r.a.) in his book 'Al-Ihtijaj'. Besides this, Sheikh Radi al-Din Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Mutahhar al-Hilli, who was the elder brother of Allamah Hilli—about 13 years older than him—also recorded this sermon in his book 'Al-'Adad al-Qawiyyah'. Sayyid Ibn Tawus (r.a.) recorded it in his book 'Al-Yaqin'. Allamah Majlisi (r.a.) has narrated it in his book 'Bihar al-Anwar', volume 37, citing the book 'Al-Ihtijaj'. So, all these scholars... well, a special feature of the book 'Al-Ihtijaj' is that Sheikh Tabarsi has recorded the various debates (Ihtijajat) of the Ma'sumin (a.s.) in it. When he wrote this book, his main goal and purpose was only to record the debates of the 14 Ma'sumin (a.s.). Yes. Yes. Therefore, in many instances, there are many hadiths—or many debates—in that book where the chain of narration (sanad) is not found because that was not his purpose. His purpose was only to record the debates of the Ma'sumin (a.s.). But the special feature of the Sermon of Ghadir in the book 'Al-Ihtijaj' is that Sheikh Tabarsi has narrated it with a complete chain of narration. And in that chain, there are narrators—well, this is not the time, but Insha'Allah, if there is ever a need to discuss the chain of the Hadith of Ghadir, a detailed discussion can be held. But it is enough to say that the Sermon of Ghadir we have is with a complete chain of narration, and there are narrators in the chain whom the scholars of Rijal have called 'thiqah' (trustworthy), who can be relied upon. So, this complete sermon, if one analyzes it—and several analyses of this sermon have been done—if seen cursorily, 10 different sections are found in this sermon, in which the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) has discussed various topics. In the last three sections of the sermon, there is a discussion regarding the Bay'ah. Yes. In which the first is a small section containing about three sentences and then a verse of the Quran. In it, while encouraging people to pledge allegiance to Ali (a.s.), the Prophet says: 'Ma'ashar al-nas' (O people!), 'Qad bayyantu lakum' (I have explained everything to you), because the detailed sermon was delivered before this. Yes. 'Wa afhamtukum' (And I have made you understand everything). 'Wa hadha Aliyun' (And this is Ali), 'Yufhimukum ba'adi' (He will explain to you after me). Meaning, if anyone is to explain to you after the Prophet, it will be Ali. So, the Prophet is starting this section by saying that if you need to understand anything about the religion after me, you have to go to Ali. Subhan Allah. Then he says, and points to this, that now I have reached the final part of my sermon. 'Ad'ukum' (I invite you all), I am calling out to you. For what? That come, all of you come and place your hand on my hand and pledge allegiance to Ali. Because there was a method of Bay'ah, right? Yes, yes. That the one taking the Bay'ah has his hand below, and the one pledging has his hand above, and the Bay'ah was done by placing hand on hand. And what is Bay'ah? It is a contract. Meaning, a person is completely handing himself over to the one he is pledging to. So, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) commanded the people to come and completely hand themselves over to Ali. And then he said, 'Iqrar' (affirmation), meaning affirm the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.), and then first come and pledge allegiance at my hand, and after me, pledge allegiance at the hand of Ali. Meaning, the Prophet's Bay'ah happened first, and after that, the Bay'ah of Ali (a.s.) was taken. Yes. And then he says, 'Ala inni qad baya'tullah' (Beware, I have pledged to Allah), why am I taking this Bay'ah from you? Because I have pledged to Allah, 'Wa Aliyun qad baya'ani' (And Ali has pledged to me), 'Wa ana akhidhukum bil-bay'ati lahu' (And I am taking your pledge for him). Why am I taking it for Ali?
