That is, Ahsan Bhai, those who hold Wilayah, those who are 'Mowlais', if they hear these sentences of the sermon, their hearts would be filled with joy; they would want to repeat them too. They would want to repeat them. That is, on the day of Ghadir, people should, even if they don't read the whole sermon, definitely read this part of the sermon that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) had them read there. And especially this: 'Ala dhalika nahya wa namutu wa nub'athu' (Upon this we live, we die, and we are resurrected). That upon this, upon this belief, upon this allegiance, we should live, upon this we should die, and upon this we should be raised. Subhan Allah. And then the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) said to them all, not just this—meaning, not just the allegiance of Ali and the Imams, no, it's not like that—by name, 'Ba'dal Hasani wal Husaini' (After Hasan and Husain). Because Imam Hasan and Imam Husain (a.s.) were present there. So everyone was told that after Ali, Hasan, and after them Husain, their allegiance must be taken. Allegiance too. That is, by name, the allegiance of Imam Hasan and Imam Husain (a.s.) was taken. 'Alladhina qad 'arraf-tukum makanahuma minni wa mahallaha 'indi' (Those whose position from me and whose status with me I have already introduced to you). That is, these Hasan and Husain are those whose position and status with me is what I have told you repeatedly, even before this. And their status, what their value and status is with Allah, I have told you all these things. So I have fulfilled this, meaning I have conveyed this message, in favor of these two, regarding these two, what is the decision regarding Hasan and Husain (a.s.)? The grandson of the Prophet, the youth of the people of Paradise. Both of them are the leaders of the youth of Paradise. 'Wa innahuma al-imaman' (and both of them are Imams), they will be Imams after their father. After their father, Ali (a.s.). 'Wa ana abuhuma qablah' (and I am their father before him). Ah. That is why we call everyone the child of the Messenger, the child of the Messenger. Indeed. Why? Because the lineage of the Messenger is continuing. So, the need is for the Messenger, the need is for the Wali. And after that, you all say this: 'Faqulu' (so say), you all say, 'Ata'na Allah bidhalik' (we have obeyed Allah regarding this message). 'Wa iyyak' (and we have obeyed you), 'wa Aliyan' (and we have obeyed Ali), 'wa al-Hasan wa al-Husayn' (and we have obeyed Hasan and Husayn), 'wa al-aimmat alayhimussalam' (and we have also obeyed the Imams). We have obeyed, meaning we will obey, we will obey until the Day of Judgment. 'Dhakarta ahdan wa mithaqan makhudhan li-Amir al-Mu'minin alayhissalam' (you have mentioned a covenant and a pledge taken for Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.)). And the covenant you mentioned, the pledge, the promise and the covenant you have taken from us, the allegiance you have taken in favor of Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.). 'Min qulubina wa anfusina wa alsinatina' (from our hearts, our souls, and our tongues). The same point is coming again; with our hearts, our souls, and our tongues, we are affirming, we are pledging obedience. 'Wa musafaqat adina' (and we will pledge by shaking hands). Yes. We will pledge by shaking hands. 'Man adrakahuma bi-yad' (whoever reaches them with their hand), we will pledge by placing our hands not just on Ali's hand, but also on the hands of Hasan and Husayn. Meaning, this is the process of allegiance that was formally established there. Yes. That first, pledge allegiance to the Prophet, then place your hand on Ali's hand, then Hasan, then Husayn (a.s.). Pledge your allegiance by placing your hands on all of theirs. And then further say: 'Wa aqirru bihima bil-lisan' (and acknowledge them with your tongue), and it is the responsibility of every person to acknowledge the Wilayah of these two, meaning Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (a.s.), with their tongue. And say: 'La nabghi bidhalika badalan wa la nara min anfusina anhu hiwala' (we will never seek any substitute for this, and we will not see any turning away from it in ourselves). We will never look for any other path besides them. Ah. Subhan Allah. We will not go to anyone else, we will only come to them. We will not bring any substitute for them. Meaning, we will not seat anyone else in their place, never. You all promise this. The Prophet is taking a promise from everyone. 'Nahnu nu'addi dhalika 'anka 'anka ad-dani wal-qasi min awladina wa ahlina' (we will fulfill this on behalf of our near and distant ones, our children, and our families). We will fulfill this, we will be loyal to it, and not only will we do it, but we will command our children and our families, whether they are close relatives or distant relatives, that they all must stand firm on this allegiance. No path has been left out. Absolutely not, absolutely not. No excuse remains for anyone after Ghadir. Yes. And this is the same thing that Janabe Zahra (s.a.) said later, when people broke the allegiance made at Ghadir, Janabe Zahra (s.a.) said that after Ghadir, no excuse remains for anyone. Indeed. 'Al al-a'lan' (publicly), it is not that the allegiance is being taken in the darkness of the night, meaning in silence. No, it is all happening in the light of day. Meaning, if a person reflects on the event of Ghadir and reads the sermon carefully, they will understand that sentence of Janabe Zahra (s.a.)—what she is saying, that there is no excuse left. No excuse left, absolutely. And then the Prophet says further, you all say this and make them witnesses. Now, not only have you pledged allegiance—do pledge the allegiance—but now bring your witnesses for this allegiance as well. Because for every matter, a witness is needed, right? Yes. That we have done this, so who will you make your witness? So say, 'Ashhadna Allah' (we have made Allah our witness). Subhan Allah. And 'wa kafa billahi shahida' (and Allah is sufficient as a witness). This is also a witness. It is the last verse of Surah Ar-Ra'd. 'Wa anta 'alayna bihi shahid' (and you are a witness over us regarding this), we make you our witness too at this moment for this act. Subhan Allah, make Him a witness too. They are making the Prophet a witness. 'Wa kullu man ata' (and everyone who obeys), and every person who obeys this message, who obeys Allah, they are also witnesses. They are also witnesses. 'Mimman zahara wa statar' (from those who are manifest and those who are hidden), whether they are obeying openly or secretly, we are making them witnesses too. 'Wa mala'ikat Allah' (and the angels of Allah), we are making the angels of Allah witnesses. And 'wa junudahu wa 'abidahu' (and His armies and His servants), meaning all the armies, the divine armies, they are also witnesses. And the servants of Allah, 'wa 'abidahu', all the servants of Allah, we are making them all witnesses. 'Wallahu akbaru min kulli shahid' (and Allah is greater than every witness), and Allah is the best witness anyway. The greatest witness is Allah. We are making all of them witnesses to this act of ours. Then the Prophet says, 'Ma'ashiran-nas, ma taqulun' (O people, what you have said), so now know that 'fa-innallaha ya'lamu kulla sawt' (Allah knows every voice). Hmm. Allah knows the voice of everyone. 'Wa khafiyat kulla nafs' (and what is hidden in every soul), Allah also knows what is hidden inside the heart of everyone. He knows that too. Indeed. So here, the Prophet is warning the hypocrites, even if there were hypocrites present there who were only affirming with their tongues and not intending it in their hearts, the Prophet is alerting them. Yes. That look, what you have affirmed with your tongue, Allah knows that too, and what is in your heart, Allah knows that too. 'Faman ihtada' (so whoever is guided), and that is why the Quranic verse was recited. It is verse number 41 of Surah Az-Zumar. 'Faman ihtada' (so whoever is guided), it is better for their own self. 'Wa man dalla fa-innama yadillu 'alayha' (and whoever goes astray, then they go astray to their own detriment). They are astray. They have gone astray themselves. And 'wa man baya' fa-innama yubayi'ullah' (and whoever pledges allegiance, they are in reality pledging allegiance to Allah). Subhan Allah. 'Yadullahi fawqa aydihim' (the hand of Allah is above their hands). Subhan Allah. Meaning, the help of Allah will always be with those who remain loyal to this allegiance. Whoever remains loyal to this allegiance, the greatest reward for them in this world and the hereafter is that the help of Allah will be with them. Indeed. Those who are living with the support of this Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) do not need to worry. Then the Prophet says, 'Ma'ashiran-nas, fattaqullah' (O people, fear Allah). Look, you have pledged allegiance, right? Now keep fearing Allah regarding this allegiance. 'Wa bay'u Aliyan Amir al-Mu'minin' (and pledge allegiance to Ali, the Commander of the Faithful). 'Salawatullahi 'alayh' (may the blessings of Allah be upon him). 'Wal-Hasan wal-Husayn wal-aimmat alayhimussalam' (and to Hasan and Husayn and the Imams (a.s.)). Now pledge allegiance to all of them. Now, the individual pledges that happened, now come one by one, pledge allegiance to Ali, pledge allegiance to Hasan, pledge allegiance to Husayn, pledge allegiance to all the Imams. Those Imams who are not even present there in the field of Ghadir at that time, but pledge allegiance to them too. Because the chain is not going to be broken. Yes. The chain will continue until the Day of Judgment. 'Kalimatan tayyibatan baqiyah' (a lasting good word), which Allah has termed in the Quran as the lasting good word. Then after this, there is a strange and amazing sentence. Here the Prophet is warning. We are reaching the end of the speech. He says, 'Yuhlikullahu man ghadar' (Allah will destroy whoever betrays). Ah. He will destroy, there is destruction for them. Even if it may seem that there is no apparent destruction for them in this world, but on the Day of Judgment, they will surely be destroyed. Because they have betrayed this allegiance. 'Wa yarhamu man wafa' (and He will have mercy on whoever is loyal), and whoever is loyal, Allah will have mercy on them. 'Faman naqasa fa-innama yanqusu 'ala nafs' (so whoever breaks the allegiance, they only harm themselves), the same verse the Prophet quoted again. So whoever breaks the allegiance, they will harm themselves. It will be their own loss. Now just the last two-three sentences. We have reached the very conclusion of that sermon. He says, 'Ma'ashiran-nas' (O people), say what I have said to you. 'Wa sallimu 'ala Aliyan bi-imaratil-mu'minin' (and greet Ali by calling him the Commander of the Faithful). Subhan Allah. Meaning, it is only the right of Ali (a.s.) that he should be greeted by calling him the Commander of the Faithful. That is why, when you go to Najaf, Insha'Allah, may Allah give everyone the opportunity for Ziyarat. Insha'Allah. When you see the dome of the Mawla from afar for the first time, then standing from afar, you must say, 'Assalamu 'alayka ya Amir al-Mu'minin'. Because it is only the right of Ali (a.s.) that he should be greeted by calling him the Commander of the Faithful. And if anyone has tried to use this title, which is specific for the Commander of the Faithful, for themselves, they have done a forbidden act. Indeed. Or if anyone has called someone else by this title, by this name, they have also done a wrong act. Well, there can be two types of people who call this. One is someone who calls out in a mocking way, so if someone calls out in a mocking way and the person in front is happy with this title for themselves, yes. Then they are ignorant. They have done a forbidden act. It is not that this person will be a sinner because they are saying it mockingly, to see, to test whether they are happy with this title or not. Yes. And if someone intentionally uses the word 'Amir al-Mu'minin' for themselves—'I am the commander of the Muslims'—if anyone other than Ali (a.s.) calls themselves the commander of the Muslims, it is forbidden. It is not permissible for them. This is breaking the allegiance of Ghadir. Yes, indeed. Because there, only Ali (a.s.) was greeted by calling him the Commander of the Faithful. No one else has the right. And then, regarding everyone, it is also that when someone called the sixth Imam 'Amir al-Mu'minin', the Imam became angry. He became angry, to the extent that it is not permissible to use the word 'Amir al-Mu'minin' even for any of our Imams. Hazrat Ali (a.s.). Indeed, indeed. Then the Prophet quotes the verse, may the blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, saying that you all say, 'Sami'na wa ata'na, ghufranaka' (we hear and we obey, we seek Your forgiveness), the verse of Surah Al-Baqarah. 'Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir' (our Lord, and to You is the return). We heard, we obeyed. O Lord, we only seek Your forgiveness. And we will return to You. To You is the return. 'Wa qulu' (and you all say). Now that you have reached this stage, that you have pledged allegiance, then say: 'Alhamdulillahilladhi hadana lihadha wa ma kunna linahtadiya lawla an hadanallah' (All praise is due to Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us). All praise to that Lord of the Worlds who guided us, and if He had not guided us, then how would we have found guidance? How would we have found guidance? You know this verse, it is verse number 43 of Surah Al-A'raf. Its interpretation is very interesting. Abu Basir asked Imam Sadiq (a.s.) about this verse: 'Mawla, what is the meaning of this verse? That all praise to Allah who guided us to this, to this thing.' So the Imam says that on the Day of Judgment, the Day of Resurrection, the Prophet (s.a.w.a.), Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), and all the Infallible Imams (a.s.) will be brought and they will be installed. Meaning, they will be placed in front of the people. Meaning, they will be present before the people. People will be seeing them. Yes. Okay? 'Yunsabuna lin-nas' (they will be installed for the people). They will all be present there in front of all the people. The Prophet, the Master of the Universe, and all the Infallible Imams (a.s.). Everyone will be seeing them. But those who are the Shia, those who are their Shia, the Imam says, 'Fa-idha ra'athu shiatuhum' (when their Shia see them), on the Day of Judgment, that 'Oh, these were the ones whose Wilayah we lived our lives with'. Yes, yes. So when the Shia see them, at that time they will say, 'Alhamdulillahilladhi hadana lihadha wa ma kunna linahtadiya lawla an hadanallah'. That all praise to Allah that on the Day of Judgment, He showed us their Ziyarat. Those with whose Wilayah we were living our lives. Meaning, 'lawla an hadanallah' (if Allah had not guided us), meaning Allah guided us in the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams from his children (a.s.). Allah guided us, the Wilayah of Ali (a.s.) and his children that He gave us, this is the real guidance. This is the real guidance. And then the Prophet says that O people, the virtues of Ali near Allah Azza wa Jall are so many, and the virtues of the Master of the Universe, Ali, that He has revealed in the Quran, they are so many that I cannot even count all those virtues for you here, standing in this one place. Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah. I cannot even count them for you. Only the virtues that Allah has revealed in the Quran regarding Ali. Therefore, 'faman anba'akum biha' (so whoever tells you about them), and 'wa 'arrafaha' (and praises them), 'fasaddiquhu' (believe them). Believe them. Believe them. Meaning, whoever is narrating the virtues of the Master of the Universe, that is the truth. This was stated in the Sermon of Ghadir. This is the Sermon of Ghadir. This is the Sermon of Ghadir. Now people say that they keep saying 'Ali-Ali', 'Ali-Ali', 'Ali-Ali'. Now it is the command of the Prophet. Yes. The Prophet said that, meaning justice, it is not even a matter of justice. I cannot do justice by standing in one place and counting and narrating all the virtues of Ali before you. Therefore, now whoever you hear the virtues of Ali from, then believe those virtues, that yes, believe them. It is your responsibility that you believe them. Do not doubt the virtues of Ali. So now, the more 'Ali-Ali' there is, the more it is the responsibility of a person that the demand of this allegiance is that we believe it. The command of the Messenger of Allah is also being fulfilled. Indeed. Indeed. And the demand of the allegiance is also being fulfilled. The demand of the allegiance is being fulfilled. The demand of the allegiance is that we keep saying 'Ali-Ali' throughout our lives. It should be 'Ali-Ali'. It should be. Absolutely, and correctly. There should be no reduction or obstacle in this. Absolutely not. It cannot come. And whatever happens, just believe. Our job is that when virtues are narrated, we believe them. This is our job. Now, meaning there is no room left by the Prophet to be caught in even the slightest doubt. It is not the right of any human being that when the virtues of the Master of the Universe are being narrated or the virtues of the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.) are being narrated, they should be caught in doubt, that 'how is this?'. They cannot say that. It is not permissible for them. If anyone says 'how is this?', you tell them that 'yes, it is just like this'. Because our Mawla was just like this. So whoever doubts, they should doubt themselves there. Meaning, how is my faith and my Wilayah (allegiance) regarding his faith that I am doubting? Yes. One should doubt oneself. If someone says 'how is this?', we should say 'brother, how are you? What kind of Wilayah is this that you are doubting this Wilayah? Doubting the virtues (Fadhail)? Yes. 'Ma'asharan-nas man yuti'allaha wa rasulahu'—whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, 'wa Aliyan wal-aimatalladhina dhakartuhum'—and obeys Ali and the Imams (a.s.) whom I have mentioned to you, 'faqad faza fawzan adhima'—he has truly achieved a great success. He has attained a great success. Now, whoever among you comes first, whoever takes the lead in this pledge (Bay'ah) and whoever takes the lead in this belief of Wilayah, and whoever is the first to greet Ali as Amir al-Mu'minin, 'ula'ikal fa'izun'—they are the successful ones. Yes, SubhanAllah. Whoever comes forward first is the successful one. 'Fi jannatin-na'im'—and he will be in Paradise, in the bounties of Paradise, meaning he will remain in the gardens of Paradise. Then the final sentence, the final sentence, the sermon ends. 'Ma'asharan-nas, qulu ma yardhallahu ankum'—O people, say those things that will make Allah pleased with you. Good. Always say things that please Allah. 'Fa'in takfuru'—if you deny, and 'wa antum, antum wa man fil-ardhi jami'a'—what about you? Even if all the people on earth were to become deniers, if everyone were to deny, 'falan tadhurrullaha shay'a'—they would not harm Allah even by an atom's weight. No harm at all. Allah will suffer no harm. Ali will suffer no harm, the Prophet will suffer no harm if someone breaks this pledge. The loss is their own. In the end, the Prophet prays, 'Allahummaghfir lil-mu'minin'—O Lord, forgive the believers. Yes. Meaning those who are believers, who have faith in Ali, even though no one among us is infallible. Those who fulfill the requirements of the pledge. Those who are fulfilling the requirements of the pledge, even if they have slipped or committed sins. The Messenger of Allah prays for them. The Prophet's prayer is for them. And the Prophet is 'Mustajab-ud-Da'wat' (one whose prayers are answered). Indeed. If someone says, let them say it regarding their own sustenance, that Allah will not accept the Prophet's prayer. Meaning, if someone wants to include themselves in the Messenger of Allah's prayer, they must fulfill the requirements of the pledge. Indeed. Indeed. And meaning, 'wa 'atib 'alal-kafirin'—and punish the disbelievers. Those who are enemies of the religion, those who are enemies of the religion, punish them with severe torment. 'Atib', 'atib' means the mention of severe torment has been made. Punish them with severe torment. 'Walhamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin'. JazakAllah, SubhanAllah. I am grateful to you, Ahsan Bhai, that you have explained in a very well-reasoned manner what the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) stated regarding the pledge of Ghadir in the Sermon of Ghadir, for the viewers. And we truly hope that the viewers have also benefited from this and have been delighted by the things that have been mentioned, especially the final sentences of the Sermon of Ghadir, which the Prophet asked the people to repeat. We should also repeat these sentences of the final part of the Sermon of Ghadir on the day of Ghadir. Truly, for those who hold Wilayah, who love the Ahlul-Bayt (a.s.), these are words that gladden the heart. And Gulzar Bhai, although it is a natural thing, we all feel that although we were not physically present at Ghadir. Yes. But whenever we read this sermon, whenever we read or hear things regarding Wilayah, it feels as if, although we were not physically at Ghadir, we were certainly there in our hearts. Indeed, indeed. And also that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) made arrangements such that all those who were present at Ghadir were ordered to convey this message to those who were absent, who were not present. Meaning, this arrangement was made until the Day of Judgment that the message of Ghadir should continue to reach people. To convey this message to whoever is absent, and this program of ours, 'Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi', the program running by the TSR (The Strong Rooh) team, this is also an effort to convey the message of Ghadir to people, and this message will continue to reach people until the Day of Judgment because the Messenger of Allah ordered it. 1400 years ago, 1400 years later, our sitting here and trying to defend Wilayah regarding Ghadir, and participating in this propagation of Wilayah, is proof that we were present at Ghadir in our hearts. Truly, and a poet has also expressed this concept in a couplet: 'There is a distance of centuries between me and them. This is the message that has been reaching us for 1400 years, that there is a distance of centuries between me and them, but I know that I was at Ghadir.' Wah, wah, wah. 'There is a distance of centuries between me and them, but I know that I was at Ghadir.' And many things have been mentioned here regarding the virtues (Fadhail) that there should be no doubt or suspicion, and the Prophet says that if I were to start mentioning the virtues of Ali that are in the Quran, I would not be able to mention them all before you. There is not enough time for that either. And the virtues that the Prophet has mentioned, who can count them? A poet has also said this, and there is a Hadith of the Prophet himself that if all the trees were to become pens and all the oceans were to become ink, they could not count the virtues of Ali. The poet says: 'The pen says, what kind of miracle of every historian in the world is this that I see? I have been writing the virtues of Ali for centuries, yet the page still appears blank.' Wah! Wah! Wah! I have been writing the virtues of Ali for centuries. And respected viewers, it is the decree of the Almighty God, it is His will that we were not present in the field of Ghadir, and the desire in our hearts to pledge allegiance by placing our hands in the hands of our Imam could not be fulfilled. So we pray to the Almighty God that He hastens the reappearance of the Heir of Ghadir so that we may fulfill that desire by pledging allegiance at his hands in the House of Kaaba. And God forbid, if we depart from this world before his reappearance, there is no need to be disappointed. If the Dua-e-Ahad is recited continuously every day, the Almighty God will raise us from our graves after the reappearance, saying, 'Go, the time has come that you can pledge allegiance at the hands of your Imam.' So viewers, with this, we conclude our episode for today. Before the timer currently on your screen ends, submit your answers if you want to be included in today's lucky draw winners. So let us proceed towards Ziyarat-e-Aminullah. As soon as Ziyarat-e-Aminullah ends, our 18 lucky winners for today will be announced through our computerized lucky draw system, InshaAllah. So we bid you farewell. Request for prayers (Iltimas-e-Dua). Khuda Hafiz. Ya Ali Madad. I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may blessings be upon you, O Wali al-Asr, help us and do not let us perish. Respected viewers, Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi. Before we announce today's winners, we would like to tell you that this was the final episode of the Ghadir Paimana-e-Ilahi Mega Quiz 2024, and there will be no episode of this series tomorrow. But you have been given one day's time so that if those whose correct answers for these episodes' questions were not completed, they can still attempt these quizzes. The link for which will remain live until Sunday, June 30th, at 9:00 PM, and after that, they can be eligible for the mega prize, i.e., the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq, which will be conducted on the same day, i.e., Sunday, June 30th, at 9:30 PM through our computerized lucky draw system, InshaAllah. Now let us see who those 18 winners are who will receive a prize of 1000 Indian Rupees, and their names are on your screen: Rizvi Zainab from Mumbai, Gulrez Azmi from Azamgarh, Marziya Rizvi from Mumbai, Mir Musahib Raza from Alipur, Syed Arif Ali from Mumbai, Syed Yashab Hussain from Zaidpur, Shabi Haider from Alipur, Syeda Tameez Zahra from Kolkata, Zeeshan Haider from Azamgarh, Fatima Halifa Syeda from Alipur, Syeda Fehmi Zahra from Qom, Ehsan Syed from Mumbai, Askari Hussain from Zaidpur, Zari Hussain from Bengaluru, Samira Hariani from Mumbai, Younas Hassan from New Delhi, Sohail Abbas from Mumbai, and Fabia from Bengaluru. Many, many congratulations to all the winners. We thank all of you once again. InshaAllah, we will meet you again on Sunday, June 30th, at 9:30 PM, where the announcement of the mega prize winner, i.e., the lucky draw for the Ziyarat of Iraq, will take place. Until then, Khuda Hafiz, Iltimas-e-Dua, Fi Amanillah, Ya Ali Madad.

Wilayah is presented as the essential foundation of religion, without which acts of worship like Hajj are considered incomplete.

Believers are obligated to maintain this covenant through their hearts, tongues, and actions, and to pass this commitment to future generations.
The title 'Amir al-Mu'minin' is exclusively reserved for Imam Ali (a.s.) by divine decree.
Daily recitation of Dua-e-Ahad serves as a modern-day renewal of the pledge of allegiance to the Imam of the Time.

chapters.title: Ghadir Quiz and Program Overview
chapters.summary: The host explains the rules for the Ghadir mega quiz, including registration, the importance of accuracy, and the selection process for the Iraq Ziyarat grand prize.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ghadir and Bay'ah
chapters.summary: The discussion introduces the historical importance of the Ghadir event, focusing on the Prophet's command for the public to pledge allegiance (Bay'ah) to Imam Ali.

chapters.title: Authenticity and Documentation of Ghadir Sermon
chapters.summary: The speakers analyze the Mutawatir status of the Ghadir Hadith in Sunni literature and contrast the omission of the full sermon in those texts with its preservation in Shia scholarship.

chapters.title: Preservation of the Ghadir Sermon
chapters.summary: The segment highlights key Shia scholars like Sheikh Tabarsi who preserved the complete text of the Khutbah-e-Ghadir with a reliable chain of narration.

chapters.title: The Divine Command of Bay'ah
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) explains that the pledge of allegiance to Ali (a.s.) is a direct command from Allah, not a personal choice.

chapters.title: The Eternal Covenant of Ghadir
chapters.summary: The Prophet emphasizes that the Bay'ah is a binding covenant with Allah, and breaking it leads to self-harm, applicable to all generations until the Day of Judgment.

chapters.title: Perfection of Religion through Wilayah
chapters.summary: The Prophet links the perfection of religion and the validity of Hajj to the acceptance of Wilayah, urging believers to understand its central importance.

chapters.title: Ali as the Source of Guidance
chapters.summary: The Prophet designates Imam Ali as the ultimate authority for answering questions and resolving uncertainties after his passing.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Imamate
chapters.summary: The Prophet formalizes the pledge of allegiance to Ali and the continuous chain of infallible Imams leading to the Mahdi.

chapters.title: The Duty of Propagating Wilayah
chapters.summary: The Prophet defines the propagation of Wilayah as the highest form of Amr bil-Ma'ruf and commands its transmission to future generations.

chapters.title: The Significance of Ghadir and Imamate
chapters.summary: The lecture highlights the Prophet's focus on the Imam of the Time during the Ghadir sermon and emphasizes the Quranic basis for the continuous chain of Imamate.

chapters.title: Taqwa, Accountability, and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses the necessity of combining Taqwa and self-accountability with the Wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin, noting that deeds hold no value without this allegiance.

chapters.title: The Process of Bay'at-e-Ghadir
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) established a systematic process for taking the oath of allegiance, requiring verbal affirmation and commitment from the hearts, tongues, and hands of the believers.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Ghadir
chapters.summary: The Prophet (s.a.w.a.) leads the congregation in a formal verbal affirmation of allegiance to Imam Ali and his descendants, emphasizing that this covenant is to be upheld throughout their lives and into the afterlife.

chapters.title: Allegiance to Hasan and Husain
chapters.summary: The Prophet explicitly includes Imam Hasan and Imam Husain in the pledge of allegiance, confirming their status as Imams and the continuation of the divine lineage.

chapters.title: Formalizing the Pledge and Witnessing
chapters.summary: The congregation is instructed to physically and verbally confirm their obedience to the Prophet, Ali, and the Imams, while calling upon Allah, the angels, and all creation as witnesses to this binding pact.

chapters.title: Divine Knowledge and Responsibility
chapters.summary: The Prophet warns that Allah is aware of both the spoken words and the hidden intentions of the heart, reminding the people that guidance or misguidance ultimately rests upon their own souls.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Allegiance and Its Consequences
chapters.summary: The Prophet emphasizes that pledging allegiance to Ali (a.s.) and the Imams is equivalent to pledging to Allah, warning that betrayal leads to destruction while loyalty brings divine mercy.

chapters.title: The Exclusive Title of Amir al-Mu'minin
chapters.summary: The Prophet declares that the title 'Commander of the Faithful' is exclusively for Ali (a.s.), and using it for anyone else is a violation of the Ghadir covenant.

chapters.title: Gratitude for Divine Guidance and Wilayah
chapters.summary: The lecture explains the Quranic verse regarding gratitude for guidance, noting that on the Day of Judgment, the Shia will recognize the Imams as the source of their salvation.

chapters.title: Believing in the Virtues of Ali (a.s.)
chapters.summary: The Prophet commands the believers to accept and affirm all narrated virtues of Ali (a.s.) without doubt, as true success lies in obeying Allah, His Messenger, and the Imams.

chapters.title: The Significance of the Ghadir Pledge
chapters.summary: The speakers discuss the Prophet's prayer for believers who uphold the pledge of Ghadir and the divine punishment for those who oppose the religion.

chapters.title: Spiritual Presence at Ghadir
chapters.summary: The participants reflect on how believers today maintain a spiritual connection to Ghadir by propagating the message of Wilayah as commanded by the Prophet.

chapters.title: Allegiance to the Imam and Conclusion
chapters.summary: The discussion emphasizes the importance of Dua-e-Ahad for those awaiting the Imam and concludes the quiz series with the announcement of winners.
